description: This is our version of aligot, a dish Jordon learnt to make in the Auvergne. Traditionally it uses a cheese called Tome fraîche but the best substitutes available here are a mix of Lancashire and mozzarella.
keywords: Aligot with Crispy Chicken Thighs recipe
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Place the potatoes into a large pan and cover with cold water. Bring up to a boil and cook until tender, about 15 to 20 mins.
While the potatoes cook, prepare the chicken. Place the thighs skin-side down in a cold frying pan and place over a medium heat.
After about 6 or 7 mins, once the skin is golden brown, flip the thighs over and place the pan into the oven for 10 mins.
Check the chicken is cooked through, place onto a tray and then turn off the oven and allow it to keep warm. Set the frying pan aside.
Meanwhile, grate the cheeses. Once the potatoes are tender, drain and use a tea towel to rub off the skins.
If you have a potato ricer, that’s the best way to get a smooth mash. If not, just mash them really well with a masher.
Put the potatoes back into the pan and place over a low heat. Add the milk and crème fraîche and grate in the garlic.
Now add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring well. Once all of the cheese is added, keep mixing hard until the cheese is all melted and the mix is smooth.
It will become very stringy when you lift out the spoon. Taste, add salt and pepper if needed.
Finally, make the gravy by placing the pan you cooked the chicken in over a medium heat. Add 2 tbsp of flour and cook out until lightly golden.
Add the vinegar, let it evaporate then pour in the stock a little at a time, whisking constantly. Simmer for a minute, then turn off the heat.
Plate up a few big spoons of the mash, followed by a couple of chicken thighs and finally pour over the gravy. Great with a crunchy green salad.

name: All The Veg Chow Mein
description: Giving the classic noodle stir-fry a healthy upgrade packed with colour, crunch and loads of veg. It's the perfect speedy midweek meal.
instructions: Cook the noodles following pack instructions. Drain well and rinse under cold running water to stop them sticking.
Finely chop the onion, carrot, courgette and red pepper.
Heat the sesame oil and a splash of sunflower oil in a large frying pan or wok set over a medium-high heat. Add all the chopped veg and stir-fry for 6-7 mins until soft and starting to caramelise.
Peel and finely chop the ginger and garlic, then add to the pan. Fry for 1 min until fragrant.
Add the beansprouts, cooked noodles and soy sauce to the pan. Toss everything together for a couple of mins until the noodles are glossy and evenly coated.
Serve up! Kids Plate: Dish out the noodles as is.Adults Plate: Top with coriander, a drizzle of crispy chilli oil and a fried egg if you fancy. Add an extra splash of soy sauce to taste.

name: All-the-Veg Fried Rice
description: A quick and healthy dinner for all the family. This fried rice is packed with veg, great for kids and even better with a crispy fried egg and spoonful of crispy chilli oil on top for grown-ups.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings 
Finely chop the onion, carrot, courgette, red pepper and cabbage.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add all the chopped vegetables and stir-fry for 6-7 mins, tossing regularly, until completely soft.
Peel and finely chop the ginger and garlic, then add them to the pan. Fry for 1 min until fragrant.
Add the cooked rice and frozen peas. Stir-fry for 1 min to heat through, then push everything to one side of the pan.
Crack the eggs into the empty space and leave to set for 30 seconds. Use a spoon or spatula to gently scramble the eggs, then fold them through the rice and veg.
Splash in the soy sauce, stir well and season to taste.

If making the crispy chilli egg, set a small saucepan on a medium heat. 
Add a drizzle of chilli oil and crack in the egg. Fry until cooked to your desired done-ness, we like a runny yolk!

Serve up! 
Kids Plate: Dish up the rice as is. 
Parents Plate: Top adult portions with a crispy fried egg, chopped coriander and a spoonful of extra crispy chilli oil if you want more heat.

name: Almond Croissant Baked Oats
description: Basically an almond croissant in the form of baked oats, with some raspberries folded in for a bit of tang. It's fudgy, high in protein and ridiculously good.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Line a deep baking tray (we used a 20cm x 20cm tray) with parchment.
To a bowl, add the almond butter, ¾ of the maple syrup, ½ the almond extract and a pinch of flaky salt. Mix until combined then set aside.

In a separate bowl, mash the banana with a fork until smooth. Add the remaining maple syrup and almond extract along with the oats, protein powder, almond milk, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and a pinch of flaky salt. Stir to combine then fold through the raspberries.

Pour ½ the banana oat mix into the prepared baking tray then drizzle over ½ the almond butter mix, then top with the rest of the oat mixture and repeat with the almond butter mix before scattering over the flaked almonds.
Slide the tray into the oven to bake for 45 mins. Keep an eye on it – if the top is getting too dark, cover with tin foil and continue to bake.

Remove from the oven and let it cool completely so it sets, before dusting with icing sugar and cutting into pieces. Serve it up in bowls with a dollop of yoghurt and some berry coulis or extra berries, if you like.

name: Almond-Crusted Salmon, Broccoli & Edamame Traybake
description: Nutty, punchy, and packed with green goodness. This easy salmon traybake is weeknight gold – ready in under 20 mins with hardly any washing up.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with foil.
Cut the broccoli into small florets. Tip the broccoli and edamame onto the tray, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Toss everything together to coat.
Season the salmon fillets with salt and pepper, then spread a teaspoon of Dijon mustard over each fillet.
Finely chop the almonds and parsley, finely grate the lemon zest and toss it all together, then press onto the mustard-topped salmon.
Nestle the salmon into the tray with the veg and bake for 10–12 mins, until the salmon is opaque throughout and the broccoli is starting to char. Cut the lemon into wedges for serving
To serve, swirl the remaining dijon through the yoghurt and spoon onto plates.

name: Aloo Paratha Toastie
description: The most flavourful, double carb toastie. Filled with potato, cheese, spices and pure bliss. Dunk the toastie into your favourite chutney for a 360° experience of deliciousness.
instructions: With a fork, stab the potatoes all over. Place them onto a plate and microwave at 800W for 6 mins, turn the potato and keep microwaving for 3 min intervals until cooked through and soft.
Meanwhile, trim and finely chop the chilli and coriander. Add both into a bowl with the garam masala and cumin seeds.

Once the potatoes are soft, halve and scoop out the flesh into the spices. Lightly mash, leaving some bits in and let cool down slightly. Once cooled down a little, stir through both cheeses. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Butter the bread on both sides. Share the potato mixture onto 4 slices of bread and top with a slice of bread.
Place a frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, add the sandwiches in and cook on both sides until golden and the cheese has melted, 5-7 mins – if it’s browning too quickly, turn the heat down.
Slice the toasties in half and serve with your favourite dip or chutney.

name: Aloo Pie with Curry Channa
description: You are going to love this recipe from Sheliza Thomson (@thedoubleskitchen). Aloo pie with curry channa is essentially a potato pie with curried chickpeas. It’s all the things  you’d want in a snack – crunchy, spicy, zingy, sweet, savoury and most of all moreish. It totally hits the spot!
keywords: Aloo Pie with Curry Channa  recipe
instructions: For the dough, mix the flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl. You can either use a mixer for speed or you can hand mix it. Make a well in the middle and add half the water, mix, then add the remaining water. You want the consistency of a very soft dough with a slightly tacky surface. Place into an oiled bowl and cover with cling film overnight, or leave in a warm place for 2 hours until doubled in size.

Peel and chop potatoes into small pieces, then soak in cold water for at least 10 mins to get rid of the starch. Meanwhile, place a saucepan filled with water over a medium heat and bring to the boil. Once bubbling, add a pinch of salt and the potatoes. Boil for at least 10-15 mins until the potatoes are cooked all the way through.
Meanwhile, start on the channa. Finely dice the white onion and ⅔ of the garlic cloves, then finely chop the saw leaf. Set aside.

Dice the scotch bonnet. Add a shot of vegetable oil to a new pot, then the scotch bonnet. Fry over a medium heat for 1 min, then add the chopped onion, garlic and chopped saw leaf. Fry over a medium heat for 2 mins. Add the curry powder and turmeric, then dry-fry for 30 seconds. Add ⅕ of the water and stir quickly to create a paste. Lower the heat slightly and leave to cook down for 2 mins.

Once the paste has thickened, add the chickpeas. Stir and cook for 5 mins. Add the remaining water (just enough to cover the chickpeas), put the lid on and bring to the boil. Lower the heat and cook for about 30 mins.
Meanwhile, the potatoes should be ready. Drain and leave to cool on a tray or in a bowl. Grate the rest of the garlic for the pie filling, then set aside.

Lightly flour a clean surface and turn out the dough. Split the dough into 10 pieces and roll into small balls. Place on an oiled tray, spaced apart, then cover. Leave to rest for a minimum of 20 mins.
In a small frying pan, dry-roast the cumin and transfer to a bowl. Keep the pan aside. Shred the potatoes into a mixing bowl using a ricer or grater.

Using the same pan you fried the cumin in, heat a shot of oil over a medium heat, then add the grated garlic. Stir with a fork to break up any clumps, then add a pinch of salt and mix. Once the garlic starts to brown, turn off the heat immediately and add the garlic to the grated potato bowl. Add the roasted cumin and a dollop of pepper sauce, then mix well.
Check the channa for salt and softness, adjusting the seasoning if necessary. Add the remaining chopped saw leaf, stir and cook for 5-10 mins, then turn off the heat.
Fill a wok or wide frying pan halfway with the Crisp ‘n’ Dry, then turn the heat to medium-high.

While the oil is heating up, fill the pies with the potato mixture. Lightly oil your hands, take one dough ball, then flatten it in your palm to the length of your hand. Add 1-1.5 tbsp of the potato mixture into the centre of the dough, then gently pull one side of the dough to the other and pinch the edges so that the filling is totally encased. Lay back onto the oiled tray and gently flatten a little. Repeat until all dough balls have been filled.
Check to see if the Crisp ‘n’ Dry is hot enough by adding a small piece of dough to it – the dough shouldn’t brown too quickly. If it does, lower the heat. You want it to rise up quickly in the oil.

Gently flatten each pie, starting from the centre and working outwards to spread the potato mix inside evenly. It should be approximately 1 inch thick. Deep-fry each pie for 3-4 mins, turning occasionally until golden brown. Use tongs to take out and drain well. You may need to oil your hands at regular intervals, so the dough doesn’t stick when flattening. You should be able to fry two pies at a time.

Once all the pies have been fried, leave them on a cooling rack for 10 mins. To serve, cut open each pie down one side, fill with channa and drizzle tamarind and pepper sauce on top. Get a napkin and enjoy!

name: Amaretti Cookies
description: These almond and lemon biscuits are crunchy on the outside, soft and chewy in the middle, and absolutely bursting with flavour.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C. Line a large baking tray with baking paper. Sift the icing sugar into a small bowl and set aside.
In a separate mixing bowl, mix together the caster sugar, salt and ground almonds. Zest in the lemons and mix thoroughly.

Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise) Then, in another mixing bowl, use an electric whisk to beat the egg whites and honey together until thick and glossy with stiff peaks forming.
Use a spoon or spatula to gently fold the egg whites into the ground almond mix. Use a spoon or your hands to portion out the dough into roughly 25g pieces and roll them into balls.
Coat the cookies in some icing sugar and place them on the prepared baking tray.
Gently press an almond into the centre of each cookie then slide the tray into the oven to bake for 15-20 mins, until cracked on the surface. Let them cool down fully before serving.

name: Amatriciana N'Casciata
description: A delicious, rich pasta dish. Covered in a layer of charred grilled aubergines. An Italian classic. Such a showstopper.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F
Cut your aubergine into long thin slices. Grill each slice on a griddle pan until charred and soft. If you don't have a griddle, use a frying pan with NO OIL. Set aubergine slices to one side.
Pasta sauce time. Cut up your bacon into chunks. Add to a pan with no oil. Cook on a medium heat until nice and crispy.
Add two chopped garlic cloves and a teaspoon of crushed chillies. Cook for 30 seconds and pour in tins of chopped tomatoes. Mix everything in and reduce the sauce down.
While the sauce is reducing, get your pasta on. When the pasta is al dente (not completely cooked) drain it and add to the sauce. Mix it all together and remove from the heat.
Take an oven proof dish (preferably metal). It has to be quite deep.
Line it with your aubergines. First line the bottom, making sure all the pieces of aubergine overlap. Place them around the edges until all sides are covered.
Spoon in a layer of pasta so it comes up to about a third. Spoon in your ricotta, smoothing it out. Grate over a layer of Parmesan and then add the rest of the pasta.
Place the remaining aubergine slices over the top so it is covered. Grate over some Parmesan and cover with tin foil. Bake in the oven for 20 minutes.
Remove the dish from the oven and remove the tin foil. Place it back in the oven for 4 minutes so the Parmesan melts.
Place a plate on top of the dish, flip it and ease the tin off the pasta cake. Slice it up and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: American Pancakes
description: Who can resist a fluffy American pancake? For these beauties you make your own buttermilk which literally involves whisking milk and lemon juice together. It really takes them to the next level.
instructions: Melt the butter in a small pot over a low heat and leave to cool slightly.
Measure the milk into a jug, squeeze in the lemon juice and whisk with a fork. Set aside for 5 mins to curdle (boom, you’ve made buttermilk).

Measure the flour, baking powder, caster sugar and a pinch of salt into a bowl. Whisk together then make a well in the centre. Crack in the egg, pour in the melted butter and buttermilk then whisk everything together until a smooth pancake batter.
Melt a smidge of butter in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat, swirling the pan so that it coats the base. Spoon in some of the batter to make 3 pancakes, around 6cm in diameter each.

Cook for 2-3 mins on this first side until bubbles appear on the top of each pancake and the underside is deeply golden and releases from the pan easily. Flip and cook for a further 1-2 mins on the second side.
Repeat with the remaining batter. Serve the pancakes with whatever toppings you like (I love berries and maple syrup with some more butter but you do you).

name: Ancho Chicken Burrito Bowl
description: All your burrito faves – chicken, avo, cheddar, zingy salsa – in one banger of a bowl. The best part? You get to use up your leftovers from the Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake.
instructions: Make the Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake.
Cut the leftover chicken into bite-sized pieces. If you prefer, warm the beans and veg in a saucepan or the microwave.
Slice the lettuce. Grate the cheddar. Peel and slice the avocado. Cut the lime into wedges.
Assemble the bowl with lettuce, the leftover chicken, beans and veg, cheddar, avocado and salsa. Finish with a big squeeze of lime juice.

name: Ancho Chicken Fajita Wraps
description: Leftovers from our Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake, crunchy lettuce, zingy onion and guac – all wrapped up. The easiest dinner win.
instructions: Make the Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake.
Peel and finely slice the red onion. Squeeze over the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt. Massage with your hands and set aside to quick-pickle.
Slice the chicken. Warm the tortilla wraps over a hob flame or in a dry frying pan.
Separate the lettuce leaves. Build each wrap with chicken, beans, lettuce, guacamole and pickled onion. Finish with a squeeze of lime juice.

name: Ancho Chicken with Herby Lime Rice & Charred Corn
description: A zingy Tex-Mex bowl with buttery charred corn, herby lime rice and leftovers from our Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake. Simple, fresh and mega satisfying.
instructions: Make the Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake.
Warm the chicken and beans in a saucepan or the microwave. Slice the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Heat the rice following pack instructions. Finely chop most of the coriander and stir it through the rice along with the zest of the lime.
Heat the grill to high. Place the corn on a tray and slide under the grill for 10–15 mins, turning halfway, until nicely charred. Once cooked, rub with a pat of butter.
Cut the lime into wedges. Serve the chicken and beans with the herby rice, corn on the cob and a spoonful of tomato salsa. Garnish with the remaining coriander and a lime wedge.

name: Ancho Chilli Chicken & Tomato Soup
description: Stretch out your Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake batch with this delicious and warming soup. It's a bowl of comfort with a little kick - plus there's pasta involved.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake batch recipe.
Shred the chicken from the traybake. Thinly slice the garlic and red chilli. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stalks.

Set a large saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the tomato purée, coriander stalks, garlic and half the chilli. Cook, stirring, for a couple of minutes until softened and the tomato purée has darkened.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to the boil. Tip in the pasta and cook following pack instructions until al dente.

Five minutes before the pasta is done, stir the shredded chicken into the pan and cook for the remainder of the time. Taste and season with salt and pepper, adding a splash of water if you prefer a runnier soup.
Ladle the soup into bowls, top with a dollop of soured cream, and scatter over the coriander leaves and remaining chilli.

name: Ancho Chilli Chicken Brothy Rice
description: Smoky, zesty, and full of beans, this speedy chipotle chicken broth hits all the comfort buttons.
keywords: brothy chipotle chicken with beans and rice
instructions: Before you begin, make the Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake batch recipe.
Separate the chicken and peppers from the beans in the traybake. Shred the chicken, thinly slice the garlic, and pick the coriander leaves, thinly slicing the stems.
Set a saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the tomato purée, garlic, and coriander stems. Cook for a couple of minutes until softened and the purée has darkened.
Stir in the chipotle paste, chicken stock, shredded chicken, and peppers. Leave on the heat until piping hot, then reduce to low. Season to taste with salt, black pepper, and a squeeze of lime juice.
Stir the beans through the cooked rice and reheat until steaming.
Share the rice between bowls, ladle over the broth, and top with the shredded chicken and peppers. Finish with the coriander leaves and serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Ancho Chilli Chicken Stew
description: Using up your leftovers from the Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake, this stew is super comforting and gets on the table in under 20 mins!
instructions: Make the Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake.

Slice the leftover chicken. Tip the chicken and beans into a saucepan with the chopped tomatoes. Cover and bring to the boil over a medium heat. Let it simmer until bubbling and piping hot. 
Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Roughly chop the coriander. Drain the jalapeños.
Serve the stew in bowls and top with a dollop of soured cream, coriander and jalapeños.

name: Ancho Chilli Chicken Traybake
description: Big Tex-Mex energy all in one tray. Juicy chicken, smoky peppers and beans ready to roll into wraps or bowls all week. This is the ultimate batch recipe.
keywords: ancho chilli chicken traybake batch recipe
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C.
Add the chicken thighs to a bowl with the ancho chilli paste and half the olive oil, season with salt and pepper.

Slice the peppers, removing the seeds. Cut the onions into wedges. Tip both onto a large baking tray with the remaining olive oil, the cumin, oregano, smoked paprika, cayenne and garlic granules. Season with salt and pepper and toss to coat.
Place the chicken thighs on top of the veg. Spoon over any leftover marinade from the bowl.
Roast for 30 mins until the chicken is cooked through. Remove the chicken from the tray and return the peppers to the oven for another 10 mins until slightly charred.
Once the peppers are softened and slightly blackened, remove the tray from the oven. Drain and rinse the black beans, then mix them through the peppers on the tray.

Serve with rice, wraps, or salad this traybake works with just about anything!If you're making this as batch, transfer the cooked chicken to a separate container. Store the beans and peppers in another, ready to upgrade more meals throughout the week.

name: Ancho Mushroom and Cheese Tacos by Tommi Miers
description: Thomasina Miers' tacos will rock your world. Caramelised mushrooms and crispy, grilled cheese... is doesn't really get more delicious.
instructions: Start with the salsa. Take your chillies and de-seed them. Add the de-seeded chillies to a frying pan and cook on a medium-high heat for 20 seconds each side. Once toasted, add to a jug and pour boiling water over the top to rehydrate them.

Peel and chop your garlic. Add about 1cm of oil to your pan and place on a medium heat. Once it begins to heat, add your garlic and turn the heat down as low as possible so that it doesn’t burn. Cook for around 20 minutes (depending on the heat of your hob), whilst adding your thyme and a pinch of salt to the pan. Once this is done, pour the water out of your chillies and replace it for the garlic oil. Take a hand blender and gently blitz it.
Time to get on with your mushrooms. Halve them and add to a lightly oiled pan. Add 3 tbsp of your salsa and mix together until fully covered. Cook until nice and caramelised.
Finely chop your cabbage and squeeze the juice of the lime over the top along with a pinch of salt and a grinding of pepper. Toss together.

To grill your cheese, add 50g to a dry frying pan in an oblong shape and repeat for the rest of your tacos. As they begin to melt, use your wooden spoon to create a cigar shape and set aside for later.

Finally, heat your tortilla wraps in a frying pan. It’s assembly time. Take your tortilla and add a spoonful of your mushrooms, a small handful of your cabbage, some crumbled grilled cheese and a dollop of your extra salsa. Chop up your parsley and sprinkle over the top. Repeat for the rest of your MOB and tuck in!

name: Anchovy & Fennel Bucatini
description: Sweet, silky fennel meets salty anchovies, juicy currants and crunchy pine nuts. It’s grown-up pasta that still feels dead easy and deeply satisfying.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Spread the pine nuts over a baking tray and toast for about 5 mins until golden, keeping a close eye on them as they burn fast. Set aside.
Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.

Halve the fennel, remove the core and finely slice it. Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a good glug of olive oil and the oil from the anchovy tin. Add the fennel with a pinch of salt and cook for about 15 mins, stirring often, until soft, sweet and silky.
Roughly chop most of the dill, saving a few fronds to go on top at the end.
When the fennel is cooked, drop the bucatini in the boiling water for 2 mins less than the pack instructions.
While the pasta cooks, finely slice the garlic. Add it to the fennel along with the fennel seeds and anchovies. Cook for a couple of minutes, breaking up the anchovies as they melt into the pan.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for a few minutes until reduced by about half. Stir through the currants, the juice of half the lemon and the chopped dill.
Transfer the pasta straight into the sauce with a splash of pasta water. Add most of the pine nuts and toss everything together until glossy and well combined.
Taste and season generously with salt and black pepper. Divide between bowls and finish with the remaining pine nuts and dill. Serve with the remaining lemon half, cut into wedges, for squeezing.

name: Anchovy & Lamb Ragu
description: Lamb and anchovies are just a match made in heaven. This ragu is left to bubble away on the stove so the salty anchovies completely melt into the sauce leaving behind a deep umami flavour - it's bound to convert any anchovy hater!
instructions: Finely dice the onion, carrots and celery. Finely slice the garlic.

Place a large lidded saucepan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the lamb mince with a good pinch of salt and cook for 6-8 mins, breaking it up with your spoon, until browned and slightly crisp at the edges. Remove the lamb from the pan with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the fat behind.

Turn the heat down to medium. Add the onion, carrot and celery to the pan with another small drizzle of olive oil if needed. Cook for 8-10 mins until soft and starting to caramelise. Stir in the garlic and cook for a couple of minutes more.

Add the entire can of anchovies, oil and all. Cook for 2-3 mins, stirring and breaking them up with the back of your spoon until they melt into the veg. Stir through the tomato purée and cook for 3-4 mins until darkened and slightly sticky on the bottom of the pan. Add the rosemary sprig.
Pour in the red wine and let it bubble away for 2-3 mins until reduced by about half, scraping up any bits from the bottom.
Add the chopped tomatoes and the lamb stock. Return the browned lamb mince to the pan.. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a low-medium heat.

Cover with the lid slightly ajar and simmer gently for 30 mins, stirring occasionally, until thick, rich and glossy. If it thickens too much, add a splash of water. Taste and season well with salt and plenty of black pepper.

Meanwhile, cook the pasta following pack instructions in a large saucepan of well-salted boiling water. Use tongs or a slotted spoon to move the pasta from the water into the sauce, add a big splash of the pasta water and stir together.
Spoon into bowls, cover with grated parmesan and serve scattered with basil leaves.

name: Anchovy Butter Spaghetti
description: Heavy on the anchovies and bursting with umami, this simple spaghetti recipe punches well above its weight class.
instructions: Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil.
Whisk the egg yolk in a bowl with a big crack of black pepper. Finely grate the Parmesan and add to the egg mixture. Set aside. Finely chop the parsley and set aside.
Drop the pasta into the boiling water and set a timer for 1 min less than pack instructions.

Meanwhile, place a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the butter and, once melted and frothy, add all the anchovies, along with the oil from the tins. 
Sizzle for 2 mins, using a spatula or wooden spoon to break the anchovies up into a paste. Use a microplane or garlic crusher to grate or crush the garlic straight into the pan. Sizzle for 1 min, then remove from the heat and wait for the pasta timer to go off.

If moved off the heat, place the frying pan back over the heat. Use tongs to transfer the cooked pasta to the pan and toss with the sauce. Add a ladle of pasta water and keep tossing until the pasta is silky, then remove from the heat.

Add the egg and Parmesan mix and toss well, adding a splash of water if you need to loosen further. The sauce should be clinging to the pasta. Add the parsley and slowly squeeze in the juice of the lemon until it's seasoned to your liking. Toss further, then tip onto plates and finish with an extra grating of Parmesan and a crack of black pepper.

name: Anchovy Nam Prik Roasted Mushrooms
description: Thai food is incredible. We've taken inspiration from Nam Prik – a sour, salty, sweet, spicy condiment usually made with shrimp paste to dress these roasted mushrooms. We’ve switched it around a little and loaded it with anchovies to give it a fishy but not too fishy savoury punch.
keywords: Anchovy Nam Prik Roasted Mushrooms recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Tear the mushrooms into 1-2cm small chunks and place onto a baking tray. Drizzle with oil and season generously with salt. Roast for 20-25 mins, until golden.
Trim and finely mince the red chilli and garlic. Thinly slice the spring onions, pick the mint leaves.
Add the anchovy fillets into a large bowl and mash into a paste. Stir through the minced chilli and garlic, season with lime juice, sugar and fish sauce.
Finely slice the cabbage, and toss the veggies and herbs into the sauce.
Serve on a bed of hot rice.

name: Anchovy Pan Con Tomate
description: Salty, juicy anchovies match up perfectly with our take on this Spanish classic. Finished with chopped chives and a drizzle of olive oil. Bon app.
instructions: Split the ciabatta in half to make a top and bottom. Then cut each in half again to make four equal-sized pieces. Rub with a generous amount of olive oil. Preheat a griddle pan over a high heat. Press the ciabatta, cut-side down, onto the grill and cook for 3-4 mins on each side until good and toasted, even a little charred.

Meanwhile, split the tomatoes in half and, using a box grater, coarsely grate the tomatoes into a bowl. Press the cut-side of the tomato against the grater and go to work. You should be left with just the skin.
Season with the sherry vinegar (you might not need all of it), plenty of salt and black pepper.
Remove the anchovies from the tin and finely cut the chives.
Spread the 4 slices of ciabatta onto a board and top with a generous amount of the tomatoes and 2-3 anchovies. Finish with chopped chives and get stuck in.

name: Anchovy Pizza Recipe
description: These frying pan pizzas are super impressive but super easy. The salted anchovy fillets are a wonderful topping that make for bright briny bursts – don’t forget to brush the crust with the salty oil they come in! If you want to get a real taste of Italian pizza from the comfort of your own home, this is the closest you’re going to get.
instructions: Measure the warm water into a jug and spoon in the yeast. Mix briefly to dissolve.
Tip the flour into a large bowl, then pour in the yeasted water. Mix with clean hands until you have a rough dough.
Add the salt into the dough and mix again until you have a smooth dough.
Shape into a rough ball, cover and leave to prove until doubled in size (roughly 2 hrs).

Tip the dough out onto a lightly floured work surface and divide into four balls. Put onto a floured tray, leaving an 8cm gap around each ball. Cover again and leave to prove for another 2 hrs until soft and pillowy.
Tip the plum tomatoes into a bowl, add a pinch of sugar and plenty of salt and pepper. Use clean hands to crush into a pulp.
Drain the anchovies from their oil, keeping it for later.
Heat your grill to high and get a large ovenproof frying pan set over a high heat.
Flour the work surface and gently stretch a ball of dough out to roughly the same size as your frying pan. Carefully lift into the pan.

Spoon over 4 Tbsp of the tomato mixture, spreading with the back of your spoon, but leaving a gap around the edge of 3cm for a crust. Tear over some of the mozzarella, then drape over as many anchovy fillets as you like. Sprinkle with a pinch of chilli flakes, if you like.
Cook the pizza for 2-3 mins, using a spatula to have a peek at the base, until it is crisp and beginning to char. Put the pizza under the grill for 1-2 mins until risen, golden and bubbling.
Move the pizza onto a chopping board, scatter with basil leaves and brush the crust with the anchovy oil. Repeat with the remaining dough and toppings.

name: Anchovy and Caper Carbonara
description: A new take on the classic carbonara. We've subbed anchovies in for the bacon and it works an absolute treat. Deeply savoury. The ultimate pescatarian pasta.
instructions: Take two bowls and separate your British Lion egg yolks from the egg whites. (Set egg whites aside and use for meringues or cocktails. Visit eggrecipes.co.uk for inspiration!)
Season your yolks with salt, a generous amount of pepper (around 4 pinches), lemon zest and grated parmesan (saving some for the garnish). Whisk together and set aside.

Chop your anchovies finely and add them, along with the anchovy oil saved from the tin and chilli flakes, to a pan over a medium heat. Cook until the anchovies dissolve and you get a thick brown paste which holds the ﬂavour.
Once you get this paste, slice the garlic and add into the pan with the capers and a glug of olive oil.
Bring some water to the boil in a saucepan, add a pinch of salt and your linguine.
Once the pasta has been cooking for 5 minutes, remove around 200ml of pasta water and add 5 tbsp of it into the anchovy pan, letting it bubble down.
Keep an eye on your linguine and once it is al dente, drain and add to the anchovy pan along with your eggy mix and a further 3 tbsp of pasta water. Mix this all together.
When the linguine is nice and silky, remove from the heat - if the sauce looks too thick add a bit more water.
Finely chop up the parsley and toss this though the linguine (saving some for garnish). Serve up with a scatter of parsley, a grating of parmesan and a twist of black pepper. Enjoy!

name: Anchovy, Greens & Mozzarella Butter Beans
description: This beany, garlicky, cheesy one pot couldn’t be simpler and its packed full of greens for when you want an injection of comfort and health. If you want to be boujie, use some fancy jars of butter beans along with all their liquid instead.
instructions: Wash, halve and finely slice the leek.
Pour the oil from the anchovy tin into your largest ovenproof high sided frying pan over a medium heat. Add the leek, with a pinch of salt. Cook for 6-8 mins, stirring occasionally until soft.
Meanwhile cut the broccoli florets off the stalks, slicing the stalks into bite sized pieces. Finely slice the cabbage.
Add the broccoli stalks to the pan. Cook for a further 2-3 mins, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic cloves. Add to the pan, along with the anchovies and chilli flakes, and a splash of more olive oil. Cook, stirring until the anchovies have melted.
Add the sliced cabbage and florets to the pan. Pour in the white wine, leave to bubble away for a couple of minutes.

Drain two tins of butter beans and add them to the pan. Add the final tin of butter beans along with its liquid. Simmer for 8-10 mins, stirring occasionally until the cabbage has wilted and the broccoli is tender.
Heat your grill to high. Grate the Parmesan.

Stir ½ the Parmesan into the beans until melted then season to taste – I like loads of black pepper. Scatter over the mozzarella and remaining Parmesan. Drizzle with a little more olive oil then slide under the grill for a few minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling golden brown.
Sprinkle over some more chilli flakes to serve.

name: Antipasti Dense Bean Salad
description: All your antipasti faves tossed into a punchy bean salad that only gets better sat in the fridge.
instructions: Drain and rinse the butter beans. Drain the artichokes and roughly chop them. Drain and chop the pickled peppers. Drain and chop the sundried tomatoes. Drain the mozzarella. Dice the salami. Zest the lemon and set aside.
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Add the green beans and cook for 1 min, then drain and cool under cold water. Drain again and set aside.
Grab a large mixing bowl. Squeeze in the lemon juice and finely grate in the garlic. Add the olive oil, balsamic vinegar and honey, then whisk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Add the butter beans, artichokes, pickled peppers, mozzarella, sundried tomatoes, salami and green beans to the bowl. Add in the lemon zest. Give everything a good mix, taste and adjust seasoning. If making ahead, share between Tupperware containers and chill until needed.
The salad will last for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Antipasti Pasta Salad
description: Relying almost fully on dried goods like pasta, jars, tins and condiments, this is a delicious, hearty and healthy pasta salad that’s full of flavour.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook your pasta according to package instructions. Drain, drizzle a little olive oil over it to help prevent sticking, and pour it into a large bowl.
Meanwhile, make the dressing. Add all of the dressing ingredients to a small bowl with plenty of salt and pepper.

Next, prep your ingredients. Lightly toast the pine nuts. Finely slice the red peppers and thinly slice the artichokes lengthways. Chop the preserved lemon and pickled chillies. Finely chop the dill including the stems. Drain and rinse the beans. Weigh out the capers.

Add all of the prepped ingredients and the dressing to the bowl with the pasta and toss well. Add the zest and juice of the lemon, then taste and adjust the seasonings to your taste. Add more caper brine or lemon juice for acidity, or more mustard or salt and pepper if you like.

Finish with the vegan mayonnaise and chilli flakes if using and stir well to combine. This salad is great warm or at room temperature. Store in the fridge for a couple of days and let it come up to room temperature before serving.

name: Apple & Blueberry Quaker Oats With Almond Butter & Banana
description: Creamy Apple and Blueberry Quaker Oats rippled with blueberry compote, topped with banana, almond butter, fresh blueberries and almonds for the ultimate bowl of oats!
keywords: Apple & Blueberry Quaker Oats With Almond Butter and Banana
Apple & Blueberry Quaker Oats With Almond Butter and Banana recipe
instructions: For the blueberry compote, add 100g blueberries, the zest and juice of a lemon and maple syrup to a saucepan. Simmer on medium heat for 5 mins until jammy.
In a separate pan add your Apple & Blueberry Quaker Oats sachets along with the milk, simmer for 2 mins or until the milk is absorbed, stirring occasionally.
Slice the bananas and roughly chop almonds.

Distribute the Quaker Oats between bowls, swirl through a tbsp of the blueberry compote, top with the sliced banana, a drizzle of almond butter, finish with a scattering of roughly chopped almonds and the remaining fresh blueberries.

name: Apple & Rosemary Olive Oil Cake
description: Brown sugar, warming spices, apples and rosemary give this cake a lovely depth of flavour. Enjoy it with coffee during the day or warmed up with ice cream for dessert.
keywords: Apple and rosemary olive oil cake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease and line a 20cm round cake tin.
For the batter, peel, core and very finely dice the apples. Finely chop the fresh rosemary. Set aside.
In a mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, spices and baking powder until evenly incorporated. Set aside.

In a separate mixing bowl, use an electric whisk to beat the butter and sugar together for about 4 mins until light and fluffy. Beat the eggs in a separate mug then add to the butter and sugar mix and beat to combine.

Add the oil to the butter and sugar mix and beat until fully incorporated. Use a spoon or spatula to fold in the diced apple and chopped rosemary. Use a spoon or spatula to gently fold in the flour mix until fully combined.

Transfer the cake batter into the prepared cake tin and level the edges. For the topping, lay the slices of apple on top. Coat the surface of the cake with a thin layer of brown sugar. Dip the sprigs of rosemary into cold water, dust with brown sugar, then press on to the top of the cake.
Bake for 35-40 mins, or until firm in the centre and a cocktail stick inserted comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tin for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely, or serve warm.

name: Apple Crumble Overnight Oats
description: These delicious and indulgent overnights are super healthy, packed full of protein and perfect for meal prep.
instructions: For the oats, dice or grate the apple, then add ½ the apple to a clean mixing bowl along with the remaining oats ingredients. Whisk together until well combined. Divide the mixture between containers, about 130g per container. Make sure your butter is fridge-cold.

For the yoghurt topping, add the yoghurt to a clean mixing bowl with the remaining topping ingredients. Whisk vigorously for about 2 mins until the mixture becomes shinny and slightly aerated. Add the remaining grated/diced apple and mix through. Gently spoon the mixture over the oats, about 100g per container. I spoon the yoghurt around the edge of the container first before adding to the middle to maintain a visual line between the oats and the topping, but that’s just aesthetic.

For the crumble, add all the ingredients into a clean bowl. Using your fingers, mix the ingredients together until you have no lumps of butter and a nice crumbly texture. Sprinkle over the top of each container.
Cover and place in the fridge overnight. The oats will keep for 3 days.

name: Apple Crumble with Vanilla Custard
description: A classic apple crumble with an oaty crumble topping, served with warm homemade custard. A cosy, comforting pud for the colder months.
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C fan and line a baking tray with baking paper.  Ensure your butter is very cold. Cut the cold butter into cubes.

To make the oaty crumble topping, put all the ingredients and a pinch of sea salt into a bowl and rub together with your fingers to form breadcrumbs. Spread the mixture on the lined baking tray and put into the freezer for 10 mins (this will firm up the butter that you’ve softened with your hands). Remove and set aside.

Meanwhile, core, peel and slice the apples into 3cm thick chunks. Add the apple, cinnamon and sugar to a heavy-bottomed pan and cook gently over a medium heat until the fruit begins to soften and starts releasing its juice – approximately 7-10 mins, depending on the ripeness of your fruit. Spoon into a 30 x 20cm pie dish.

Allow the fruit to cool just slightly, then sprinkle the oaty crumble mix evenly over the top of the fruit (break up the crumble with your hands if necessary). Get it in the oven to bake for 25-30 mins or until the topping is golden.
Meanwhile, make the custard. Whisk the egg yolks and sugar together in a heatproof bowl.

Heat the cream in a pan with the vanilla pod and a pinch of sea salt until hot but not boiling. You’ll know it’s hot when it starts to steam. Pour the hot cream over the egg yolks slowly and evenly, whisking continuously as you go. Get someone to help you here if possible – they can pour while you whisk.

Place the bowl over a pan of simmering water to make a double boiler (also known as a bain marie), and heat, whisking continuously with a large balloon whisk, until it thickens. The custard is ready when the bubbles disappear. Another good test is to drag your wooden spoon through the middle of the custard – if it is ready the spoon will leave a mark that takes a moment to disappear. It should take about 8 mins to get to this stage.
Remove the vanilla pod, split it lengthways and scrape the seeds into the custard. If necessary, sieve the custard through a fine mesh to eliminate any lumps, then pour into a jug.

If the crumble has finished cooking, serve up a generous portion into each bowl and pour over the warm custard. If it’s still a way off, keep the custard warm by standing the jug in a pan of hot water and covering the top (of the custard, not the jug) with clingfilm to prevent a skin forming.

name: Apple Green Goddess With Herby Dressing
description: Zingy and creamy green goddess salad. The perfect nutritious lunch to make ahead when you want something fresh, filling, and full of flavour.
instructions: Add the herbs, crème fraîche, peeled garlic, olive oil, Dijon and ½ the lime to a blender, then season with salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth, then taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Slice the apple into matchsticks, then the sugar snaps into 2cm pieces on a diagonal.
Cook the edamame in boiling water for 7 mins then drain.
Using a veg peeler, finely shred the green cabbage and peel, pit and slice the avocado.
Squeeze the rest of the lime juice into a bowl with the cabbage, seasoning with salt. Massage until it just starts to soften. Then add the edamame, sugar snaps, drained beans and apple mixing well.
Box up the slaw. If eating immediately, drizzle with the dressing. If not, box the dressing up for later.

name: Apple Maple Pecan Crumble Pie
description: This stacked apple pie is a great dessert to whip out at your next dinner party. It tastes as impressive as it looks.
keywords: Apple Maple Pecan Crumble Pie recipe
instructions: To make the pastry, cut the butter into 2cm cubes, and place in the fridge to keep cold. Add flour, ½ tsp salt and sugar into a large mixing bowl. Mix together until evenly combined.

Using your hands, toss the cubes of cold butter into the flour mixture. Quickly break and smash the pieces of butter in the flour into smaller chunks (it’s ok if they are not all the same size). Add 100ml of ice cold water into the mixture. Stir with a fork until a shaggy dough forms. Add a tsp more of water at a time if it's too dry.

Gather the dough into a mound. Using your hand, squeeze it together to form large clumps, place them onto a clean work surface. If you have some dry floury areas, leave it in the bowl and stir a few teaspoons of ice cold water until you can squeeze the dough together. The texture should not be sticky, it should still be a little dry.

Split the dough into 3 chunks, then flatten on top of each other, this is key to getting flakey pastry. Flatten and shape into a thick disc. Wrap in cling film and refrigerate the dough for at least 1 hour.

While the pastry rests, bake the apples. Preheat the oven to 180°C. Peel, core and slice your apples into 1cm thick slices and toss with the sugar, spices and a pinch of salt. Lay out over a couple of baking trays and slide into the oven for 20 mins.
Pour off any excess juice into a pan and reduce to a syrup.
Roll out the pastry and use it to line a 23cm springform pan. Leave plenty of overhang over the sides of the tin.
Line the pastry case with foil and pour in 1kg of rice or dried beans. Slide into the oven for 30 mins, then remove the foil and weight and bake for another 30 mins.

Pull out the oven and stack the apples in the baked case. Press them down and make sure there are no air pockets. Drizzle any of the reduced apple juice over the top and top with the Raise Maple Pecan.
Bake for another 30 mins. Pull out the oven and trim any excess pastry from the rim of the tin. Pop out the tin, slice and serve with crème fraîche, custard or ice cream.

name: Apple Sauce
description: This classic homemade apple sauce is so easy to make, and is much more delicious than the shop-bought stuff. Serve it with roast pork for the perfect Sunday lunch.
instructions: Peel the apples. Coarsely grate the peeled apples into a saucepan.
Add the lemon juice, sugar and butter into the grated apples. Mix to combine then set the pan over a medium-high heat.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then turn the heat down to medium, place a lid on and cook for 15-20 mins, stirring occasionally, until the apples have softened completely.

Once softened, remove the lid. If your apple sauce is too loose for your liking, turn the heat up to medium-high and keep cooking the apple sauce for another 5-10 mins, with the lid off, until thickened.
Taste and season with more sugar, if desired. Serve with roast pork.

name: Apple, Basil & Gin Pitcher
description: A ridiculously refreshing pitcher. Basil gives a lovely herbal edge to this fragrant gin and lemon drink.
instructions: Add your caster sugar and water to a small saucepan set over a low heat. Gently heat until your sugar has dissolved, then leave to cool to room temperature.
Add your basil leaves to a jug, then bash with the base of a wooden spoon to bruise the leaves and release their oils.

Tip in the gin and some of the sugar syrup at a ratio of 2:1 gin to sugar syrup. Add the juice of the lemons and your apple juice then fill with ice. Mix well with a long spoon so all the ingredients are combined and cold.
Rub the edge of your serving glasses with the lemon skins and then dip into the Maldon Flaky Sea Salt.
Pour your drink into your prepared glasses, then top with a leaf of basil. Enjoy responsibly.

name: Apple, Pecan & Pearl Barley Stuffing
description: This stuffing is so good you could even serve it as a veggie Christmas dinner main with all the trimmings. It’s made using the leftover veggies from our veggie gravy recipe, giving it loads of extra flavour with little extra work.
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C fan.
Set a large pan of boiling water over a medium heat. Add the pearl barley and garlic clove and boil for 15-20 mins until tender, then drain and remove the garlic clove.

Toss the pearly barley in the olive oil in a large mixing bowl. Roughly chop the pecans and parsley and add them to the barley. Coarsely grate in the apple. Add the strained vegetables from the gravy including the dried mushrooms. Cut the bread into small 1cm cubes then add to the stuffing mixture. Mix really well to combine then season well to taste with salt and plenty of black pepper.

Rub a large baking dish (approx 22 x 16cm) with olive oil. Transfer the mixture to the dish then lay the sage leaves on top and drizzle over a little olive oil. Slide in the oven to bake for around 30 mins until firm to touch, lightly golden brown and piping hot throughout.

name: Apricot and Pistachio Spiced Cookies
description: The perfect cookie consistency - part squidgy, part crisp. Made using rolled oats, crunchy pistachios and sweet apricots. How cookies should be done.
instructions: Set oven to 175°C/347°F and line two baking trays with greaseproof paper.
Blitz 75g of the oats until you get a flour consistency and set to the side in a mixing bowl.
Add in the flour, spices (cinnamon, ginger, allspice) and baking powder.
In a separate large bowl beat the softened butter and sugars together. Then add your egg and whisk together.
Add the sugar mixture, remaining oats and tbsp of water to the flour combination.
Roughly chop the pistachios (chopping extra to garnish your cookie dough). Finely dice the apricots and add both ingredients to your cookie mixture.
Roll the dough into walnut size balls and place on a baking tray, leaving space in between and lightly flatten each ball down.
Sprinkle a generous amount of salt and your extra pistachio crumbs on each portion.
Cook for 13 minutes, turning your tray around halfway through.
Once ready, leave to cool on a rack.

name: Aromatic Chicken Stew With Fennel, Olives & Filo
description: A quick and simple chicken stew topped with a crunchy filo layer. Think of this like a light and bright, Mediterranean-style take on a chicken pie.
instructions: Before you begin, make the No-Fuss Roast Chicken.
Preheat the oven to 190°C.

Roughly chop the fennel bulb and onion. Preheat a medium-sized, oven-proof frying pan over a medium heat. Add a good glug of oil and tip in the chopped veggies. Add a pinch of salt and cook for 4-5 mins until starting to soften. Add the cumin and turmeric and cook for a minute. Slice the garlic clove and tip into the pan. Cook for 2-3 mins together before adding the chicken stock and the jar of chickpeas, liquid and all. Bring to a boil and reduce by about a third.

Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and stir through the stew with the olives. Roughly chop half of the parsley (stalks and all!) and add to the stew. Have a taste and adjust the seasoning, adding a little lemon juice if you’d like.
Lay the sheets of filo out and brush with olive oil. Scrunch them into little bundles and sit on top of your stew. Slide into the oven for 18-20 mins or until the pastry is golden and crisp.

Combine the leaves from the remaining parsley in a bowl with thinly sliced red onion and the juice of the lemon. Toss with a little olive oil and salt. Serve the crispy filo stew on warm plates with a big handful of parsley salad.

name: Arrabbiata Beans With Crispy Garlic
description: A super simple bean-y dish: Arrabiata-style beans zhuzhed up with some scotch bonnet, fresh thyme, and garnished with garlic crisps. It’s hearty, comforting, and full of goodness.
keywords: Arrabiata Beans With Crispy Garlic recipe
instructions: Peel all the cloves of garlic. Thinly slice the scotch bonnet, pick the basil leaves, discarding the stalks.

Using a mandoline slicer or a sharp knife, thinly slice the cloves, as evenly as possible. Add your garlic into a pan with your olive oil, place on medium-low heat and cook, stirring constantly until golden, 10-15 mins. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the garlic onto a kitchen paper-lined plate.

Add the scotch bonnet and thyme stalks into the hot garlic oil and cook until fragrant. Pour in the plum tomatoes and crush to break them down. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer until the sauce has thickened, 15-20 mins.

Meanwhile, drain the butter beans, reserving the bean liquid. Once the tomato sauce has thickened, stir through the beans, adding some bean liquid to thin out the sauce to your desired consistency. Cook until piping hot, taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Stir through half the basil leaves before serving. Spoon into bowls and finely grate over some Pecorino. Top with garlic crisps and some remaining basil leaves. Enjoy with crusty bread.

name: Arroz Con Pollo
description: Arroz con pollo is a delicious Peruvian dish from Erik Ramirez, the chef and owner of Llama Inn.
instructions: Combine the chicken, beer, salt, black pepper, cumin, MSG and white wine vinegar in a large bowl. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 4 hrs.
For the aji verde, first remove the seeds from the jalapeños then put them in a blender with the coriander, vegetable oil, water, garlic cloves, salt and MSG. Blitz until smooth and set aside.

For the salsa criolla, first julienne the red onion, de-seed and julienne the habaneros as thinly as possible and chop the coriander. Tip it all into a bowl with the lime juice, olive oil, salt and pepper. Mix well and set aside.

Remove the chicken from the marinade and pat dry with paper towels, making sure to reserve the marinade. Heat some oil in a large dutch oven (casserole dish) over a high heat. Sear the chicken pieces until browned on all sides. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside. Don't wash your dish.

Chop the Spanish onions and mince the garlic. Add the aji amarillo purée to the same casserole dish, alongside the chopped onions and minced garlic. Sauté until the onions are translucent and aromatic.

Meanwhile, blend the coriander and 200ml water together, then pour it all into the casserole dish once the onions are cooked. Add the reserved chicken marinade and bring the liquid to a simmer. Return the seared chicken pieces to the dish, cover and braise over a low heat for 30 mins until the chicken is cooked through and tender. Adjust the seasoning with salt, pepper and cumin as desired.

Remove the cooked chicken and set aside. Add all the chicken fat and drippings to the pot, alongside the rice and choclo. Stir well to combine. Cover the pan and cook over a low heat for 15 mins until the rice is cooked and has absorbed the flavours of the liquid.

Add the chicken back to the dish (don’t stir), cover and cook for another 10 mins over a low heat. Remove from the heat and let it rest. Serve each person rice, a piece of chicken, salsa criolla and a little of the aji verde. Enjoy.

name: Artichoke & Fennel Tagliatelle
description: So cheap, so easy, so veggie. The fennel and the artichoke work together beautifully.
instructions: Cut your fennel into thin slices. Add a splash of olive oil to a pan and add the fennel. Cook over a low to medium heat until very soft and tender. This will take about 15 minutes.

Add grated courgette and stir it around. Once it is beginning to brown, add your artichokes and sliced garlic cloves. Mix them around. After about 30 seconds, add a heaped tablespoon of mascarpone. Stir it in.
Get your pasta cooking.
Add about 150ml of the starchy pasta water to the sauce and beat it in. Add the juice and zest of a lemon. Grate in a generous amount of pepper, add some salt and mix everything in.
Once the pasta is cooked, add it to the sauce. Fold everything in and serve it up. Garnish with fennel fronds and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Artichoke & Lemon Butter Beans
description: These butter beans with artichokes and lemon pack in the prebiotics to feed you and your gut microbes.
instructions: Finely chop the shallot and crush the garlic. Add a splash of oil to a large pan, then tip in the onions and garlic. Gently sauté until golden, then add the drained artichoke hearts and butter beans with their liquid.
If using, toss in the rosemary or any other herbs and simmer for 5 mins or until the liquid becomes a thick sauce.
Taste and adjust the seasoning before turning off the heat and squeezing over the lemon juice.
Serve with your favourite toast and an extra drizzle of olive oil.

name: Artichoke & Pine Nut Pasta
description: Transform a jar of artichokes into a glossy, vegan bowl of pasta. At least 4 people in the Mob office have said this has major vongole vibes. Thoughts? B x
keywords: Artichoke and pine nut pasta recipes
instructions: Set a small frying over a medium heat and toast the pine nuts for 7-9 mins, until golden brown.
Bring a large pan of water to a rolling boil and season generously with salt. Drop in your spaghetti and cook according to the pack instructions.

Now you can get on with the rest of the prep. Roughly chop the artichokes and finely chop the garlic, chilli and rosemary. Then roughly chop the mint, and set aside for later. Finally, zest and juice the lemon.

Add the chopped garlic, chilli and rosemary to a large saucepan with plenty of good olive oil and set it over a medium-low heat. Cook for 4-5 mins until starting to sizzle and the room is filled with the smell of toasting rosemary, garlic and chilli.
Add the chopped artichokes and stir together, frying for another 2-3 mins, until the artichokes are starting to break down a little.

Transfer the cooked spaghetti straight into the artichoke sauce and toss to combine until you have a creamy, emulsified, glossy sauce that coats the pasta. Add in a handful of pine nuts, plenty of black pepper, roughly chopped mint, lemon zest and juice.
Give it another toss, divide between warm plates and top with extra pine nuts and lemon zest. Now get stuck in.

name: Artichoke Fatteh
description: Fatteh comes in all shapes and sizes but this one is a wintery vibe with crispy artichokes, creamy chickpeas and a little fresh mint and chilli to finish.
instructions: Drain the chickpeas and add to a pan along with a litre of cold water and a tsp of salt. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 mins until the chickpeas are soft but not falling apart.
Meanwhile, heat 100ml of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Separate the layers of the pittas and cut into roughly 2cm squares.
Fry in the hot oil until golden and crispy. Remove from the pan onto a plate lined with kitchen paper and sprinkle generously with sea salt and 1 tsp of sumac. Set side.

Wipe the pan clean. Drain and quarter the artichokes (they might come quartered already). Heat a glug of olive oil in the pan over a medium-high heat and fry the artichokes cut side down until golden brown,
Remove from the pan and set aside. Toast the pine nuts along with a splash of olive oil in the same pan until golden brown. Add the remaining sumac and chilli and take off the heat.
Mix the yoghurt with the juice of the lemon, the tahini, 4 tbsp of cold water and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
To assemble, place a layer of the crispy bread onto a large bowl or plate, top with a few spoons of the tahini yoghurt, a few spoons of the chickpeas and a few pieces of artichoke.
Repeat in layers and finish by pouring the pine nuts and olive oil over the top.
Finely chop the mint and sprinkle over.

name: Asparagus & Lemon Gnocchi
description: A fresh zesty dish to get you ready for spring. Gnocchi doesn't get much better than this.
instructions: Fill a large saucepan with water and bring to the boil. Meanwhile, mince the garlic and dice the chilli. Chop up your mint and basil. Heat a glug of oil in a large frying pan and add the chilli, half the garlic, and breadcrumbs. Keep them moving and let them turn a lovely golden brown colour before setting aside on kitchen paper to soak up excess oil.
Meanwhile, dice the shallot as finely as possible. Trim the asparagus tips off (leave them whole) and cut the stalks into 1-2cm rounds.
Heat a splash of oil in a large frying pan and fry the shallot and asparagus with a pinch of salt for 5 mins, then add the other half of the minced garlic and cook for 1 min.
Tip the gnocchi into the boiling water and cook following pack instructions.

Pour the white wine into the pan with the asparagus. Let it bubble for a moment, then stir through the nutritional yeast. Add the drained gnocchi along with some gnocchi cooking water and stir well. Squeeze in the lemon, stirring constantly, and then serve on a plate topped with chopped mint, chopped basil, breadcrumbs and Parmesan.

name: Asparagus & Pea Caprese
description:
Bright, fresh and beautifully assembled. Tender asparagus two ways - blanched spears and a vibrant pesto, piled with torn mozzarella. This one's perfect for a when it starts to get a little warmer.

In Partnership with Aldi #ad
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Add the pine nuts to a baking tray and pop in the oven for 4-7 mins, or until golden, then remove and leave to cool. You'll need a handful for garnish and the rest are for the pesto.
Meanwhile, snap the woody ends off all the asparagus and discard. Finely dice the shallot, peel the garlic, grate the Parmesan and zest all the lemons, then set aside.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the asparagus to the pan and reduce to a simmer. Cook for 4 mins, then lift out three-quarters of the spears with tongs and plunge into ice water to stop the cooking. Remove and drain on kitchen paper. Cook the remaining asparagus for a further 3 mins until nice and soft so it blends easily in the pesto, then scoop out with a slotted spoon and pop on kitchen paper, leaving to steam dry. (Keep your saucepan on a low heat, you'll use the water again to cook your peas later on).

Make the shallot dressing. Squeeze the juice of the lemon into a bowl and add the finely diced shallot. Drizzle in the olive oil, season with salt and black pepper and whisk to emulsify. Toss the blanched asparagus spears (the softer cooked asparagus is for your pesto) in the dressing and set aside.

Make the asparagus pesto. Add the remaining soft-cooked asparagus to a blender with the peeled garlic, most of the toasted pine nuts, the Parmesan, olive oil, the lemon zest and juice of the lemon. Blitz until smooth, then taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Back to your large saucepan, turn up the heat until the water is boiling. Add the frozen peas and cook for 2-3 mins until bright green, then drain.
To serve, divide the dressed asparagus spears between plates, then tear over the mozzarella, spoonfuls of the asparagus pesto, the peas, basil leaves and the remaining pine nuts. Dig in.

name: Asparagus Fries With Lemon Aioli
description: A beautiful asparagus dish that's best enjoyed when they're in season. The crispy coating of these goes great with the simple zesty homemade aioli.
keywords: Asparagus Fries With Lemon Aioli recipe
instructions: Start by making the aioli, the easiest way to do this is using a stick blender and a tall, narrow container. Add the egg yolks and mustard to the container, then grate in the garlic, the zest of half the lemon and all of its juice, add a generous few twists of pepper, a tsp of salt and finally pour over the sunflower oil.
Put the stick blender against the bottom of the container and then slowly lift it up as you blend until the whole mix is creamy and emulsified.
Trim the woody ends from your asparagus and set aside. Place a large frying pan over a medium heat and add enough oil to cover the pan about 0.5cm deep.
Make the batter by whisking the flour and cold sparkling water in a mixing bowl with a big pinch of salt (you don’t need to whisk until totally smooth).
Swirl the asparagus in the batter and coat well all over, then carefully lay it straight into the hot oil. It should sizzle nicely. Drizzle a little extra batter over for a more crunchy coating.

Cook for about 2 mins, then flip and cook the other side for another minute or so until the batter is golden and crunchy. They will stick together but that's okay, just use a fork or spatula to gently separate the spears.
Remove from the oil onto a wire rack or a plate lined with kitchen paper and sprinkle with flaky salt. Repeat until all of the asparagus is cooked.
Plate up with a generous dollop of the aioli and a few twists of black pepper.

name: Asparagus and Pea Minestrone
description: A fresh, green take on the classic Minestrone. Packed full of veggie, nuts and beans. One of the healthiest spoonfuls you'll ever have. Make this veggie by simply swapping out the parmesan for a veggie alternative.
instructions: Toast the nuts in a dry frying pan until golden. Set aside.
Cut the asparagus into small pieces and slice the green leaves. Finely chop 2/3 of the garlic. Cut the parmesan rind off the parmesan and cut into small chunks.

Get a large saucepan on a medium heat. Drizzle in a glug of olive oil. Add the garlic and chilli flakes, fry for 1 minute stirring, then add the stock (dissolved in 1.5 litres of boiling water). Add the parmesan rind. Drain the beans, tip into the pan with the pasta. If using spaghetti break up into smaller lengths with your hands. Season and leave to simmer for around 6 minutes.

Pesto time. Put the toasted nuts, remaining garlic clove, and fresh herbs into a mini food processor. Blitz and then pour in enough olive oil to make a drizzlable pesto. Grate in half the parmesan and lemon zest. Season to taste.
Back to the soup. Drop in the asparagus, cook for 1 minute then add the green leaves and frozen peas. Cook for 2 minutes (check the pasta is cooked).
Season the minestrone with lemon juice, salt and pepper. Spoon into four bowls, swirl through the pesto and grate over the remaining parmesan.

name: Asparagus, Burrata & Basil Salad
description: This springtime recipe is all about the produce. Make sure to use in-season asparagus and quality burrata to get the best possible eating experience.
instructions: Heat your grill to full power. Roughly chop the olives, capers, basil and sun-dried tomatoes and transfer to a bowl. Add a few scrapes of lemon zest, all of the lemon’s juice, salt, olive oil and mix well to make a dressing.
Trim the woody ends from the asparagus and then lay them onto a grill pan lined with baking paper. Drizzle with olive oil and salt.
Place the asparagus on a high rack right under the grill and cook for about 2 mins on each side until nicely browned.
Remove the asparagus from the tray and replace it with the sourdough, get that back under the grill until nicely toasted on both sides. Remove and cut into chunky croutons.
Halve the cooked asparagus, add to a big mixing bowl with the rocket and croutons and add a splash of the dressing you made earlier. Mix well.

Lay everything over a big plate, tear over the burrata and dot it around. Add a pinch of salt to the burrata and then spoon the rest of the dressing over everything. I like to finish with an extra little squeeze of lemon. Enjoy!

name: Aubergine & Caper Pasta
description: We all love pasta, and this one is made even speedier by using our batch-cooked aubergine sauce. Pack it full of fridge staples for a nutritious weeknight dinner.
instructions: Make the Aubergine Alla Norma batch recipe.
Get the Aubergine Alla Norma base into a large saucepan and bring to a simmer. Boil the pasta in salted water, according to package instructions - then drain, saving some pasta water.
Roughly chop the olives. Add the olives, capers, and pasta into the sauce along with a good slosh of pasta water, then mix vigorously until glossy.
Serve up and top with torn basil, a drizzle of your best olive oil, and grated parmesan.

name: Aubergine & Chickpea Zaalouk
description: A delicious spiced aubergine and chickpea stew inspired by Moroccan zaalouk. Perfect mopped up with crusty bread.
instructions: Mince the garlic and dice the aubergines and tomatoes. Finely chop the fresh coriander. Heat the olive oil and garlic in a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Once warm, add the aubergines and ½ ladle of water. Let the aubergines cook for 5 mins with the lid on.

Add the tomatoes, spices and tomato purée, and let it simmer with the lid on for 15 minutes. If it’s too dry, add another ladle of water. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Simmer for another 5-8 mins with the lid off. Once the aubergines are very soft and all the water from the tomatoes has evaporated, turn off the heat.
Stir through the coriander and the chickpeas. Leave to sit for 5 mins.
Divide between bowls and serve with crusty bread.

name: Aubergine & Curried Sesame Noodle Salad
description: A silky, spicy, tahini noodle salad with roasted aubergine & a punchy curry dressing. Perfect cold from the fridge for a scrummy make-ahead lunch.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.
Trim and dice the aubergines into 2cm chunks. Spread out on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season well. Roast for 20–25 mins until golden and creamy inside.
Meanwhile, cook the rice noodles following pack instructions. Once soft, run them under cold water in a sieve to chill them down, then toss with the chilli oil until coated.
Pick the coriander leaves and set aside. Save the stems for the dressing.

Chuck the tahini, coriander stems, ice cubes, curry powder, maple syrup and juice of the limes into a blender. Blitz until smooth. Taste, season with salt, and add more maple if you want it sweeter. The dressing should be runny, it’ll thicken slightly as it rests.
To box up, pour the dressing into the base of your containers. Pile the chilli noodles on top, followed by the roasted aubergine, and finish with the coriander leaves.
Chill until needed. Shake well before serving.

name: Aubergine & Hummus Bowl with Cheat’s Amba Sauce
description: We've taken the sandwich and turned it into a healthy vegetable bowl. The homemade amba sauce delivers the sweet heat.
keywords: Sabich Bowl with Cheat’s Amba Sauce
Sabich Bowl with Cheat’s Amba Sauce recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the aubergine into 2cm slices. Halve the tomatoes. Transfer the aubergine and tomatoes to a baking tray and drizzle with the remaining olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper, then roast for 20 mins. Remove the veg from the oven to cool slightly.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. Toast the chilli flakes, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds and mustard seeds in a dry pan over a medium heat until fragrant. Transfer to a spice grinder or a pestle and mortar, then finely grind. Tip into a blender with the mango flesh, peeled garlic, half of the lemon juice, two-thirds of the olive oil, vinegar, salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth and season with salt. Set aside.
Bring a pan of water to the boil. Once boiling, drop in the eggs. Reduce to a simmer and cook for 7 mins, then remove the eggs and cool under cold water. Peel and halve, then set aside.
Roughly chop the parsley including the stalks. Once the veg has cooled, toss through the chopped parsley and the remaining lemon juice.
To serve, swoosh the hummus in a serving bowl, then top with the aubergine salad, chopped egg and a big drizzle of the cheat’s amba sauce. Scoop-up with pitta bread, if you like.

name: Aubergine & Mascarpone Gnocchi Traybake
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad. 

A one tray dinner of dreams. This creamy number is a perfect midweek dinner, and could even be meal prepped for the week.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Cut your aubergine into 3cm chunks. Finely chop your rosemary.
Tip your aubergines into a large baking tray with your cherry tomatoes and gnocchi. Add a good glug of olive oil, your chopped rosemary, chilli flakes and salt, then give it a good mix.
Roast in the oven for 45 mins, tossing every so often so that everything cooks evenly. The gnocchi should be crispy and the aubergines super soft.
Add your mascarpone, lemon zest and juice and parmesan to a bowl. Give everything a really good mix, loosening with the water to make it saucy.
Remove your baking tray from the oven. Remove the vines from your tomatoes, then pour in your mascarpone mixture. Mix to combine.
Sprinkle with basil, a little more parmesan and chilli flakes, then serve.

name: Aubergine & Tomato Traybake Curry
description: A beautiful, mild curry that involves minimal cooking time and maximum flavour. Packed with coconut milk, spices and all the veg.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/400°F.
Cut your aubergines into batons.

Toss them into a large roasting tray along with your cherry tomatoes. Grate in your garlic and ginger, then add the coriander, cumin, turmeric and chilli powder. Drizzle with veg oil and salt. Give it a good toss to coat. Roast for 35 mins.
Remove your tray from the oven. Add your chickpeas, chopped tomatoes and coconut milk and stir to combine. Return to the oven for another 25 mins, by which time your sauce should be nice and thick.
Finely slice your green chillies and chop your coriander.
Season the curry to taste, then sprinkle with green chillies and coriander. Serve either over rice or with flatbreads.

name: Aubergine Alla Norma
description: Making a great big batch of saucy aubergines is a great way to see in the week. This one is great as it is, or you can turn it into a chickpea bake, a pasta sauce, or a coconutty curry. Enjoy.
instructions: Heat the grill to medium-high and dice the aubergine into 2cm pieces. Put the aubergine onto a tray and whack under the grill for 10 mins, then flip and grill for another 5-10 mins until charred and soft. Remove from the grill and season with salt and pepper.

Slice the garlic and finely chop the basil stalks. Heat a shot of oil in a large pan over a low-medium heat and add the garlic, chilli flakes and basil stalks, frying gently for 3 mins until just golden. Tip in the roasted aubergine and canned tomatoes, squashing the tomatoes down a bit. Simmer for 20-25 mins.
Tear the basil leaves and mix through the sauce along with the red wine vinegar, seasoning with salt and pepper. Cool and decant into an airtight container and store in the fridge or freezer.

name: Aubergine Alla Norma Shakshuka
description: A speedy veggie shakshuka made with spicy aubergine, soft eggs and sweet roasted peppers. Perfect with warm bread for dunking.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Aubergine Alla Norma batch recipe.
Drain the roasted red pepper and slice it into strips. Roughly chop the parsley.

Tip the Aubergine Alla Norma batch base into a wide frying pan with the harissa and sliced pepper. Set over a medium heat and cook until bubbling. Add a splash of water if the sauce is looking too thick.

Use the back of a spoon to make four small wells in the sauce, then crack an egg into each one. Cover with a lid or foil and simmer gently for 5–7 mins, until the whites are just set and the yolks are still runny (or to your liking).
Season the eggs with a pinch of salt and a crack of black pepper. Drizzle with olive oil and scatter over the chopped parsley.
Serve straight from the pan with warm toasted sourdough on the side for dipping, if you fancy.

name: Aubergine And Lentil Shepherd's Pie
description: A very loose interpretation of a shepherd's pie using aubergines and lentils, with harissa as the base and sweet potatoes for the top.
instructions: Scrub the sweet potatoes clean. Peeling is optional, I prefer to leave the skin on as it’s full of nutrients and gives a nice texture to the mash. Chop into large pieces (about 4cm chunks) and boil for 15-18 mins until soft enough to squash easily with a fork. Drain and allow to steam dry in a colander.

To make the mash, tip the sweet potatoes back into the pot or into another large bowl and add 2 tbsp oil from the sun-dried tomatoes into the potatoes and mash with a fork or potato masher. I like quite a chunky texture but you can get them as smooth as you like. Season very well with plenty of salt and pepper.
Finely chop the onions, dice the aubergines into very small cubes and mince the garlic cloves. Finely slice the sun-dried tomatoes. Finely chop the parsley and walnuts. Set everything aside.

To make the filling, heat a good drizzle of olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan or pot over a medium heat. Fry the aubergines with salt and pepper, for 10-15 mins until golden and softened and starting to brown.

Add the onion, garlic and a little more salt and pepper to the frying pan with the aubergines. Cook for a further 7 mins until softened. You may need to add a splash of oil or water. Add the tinned tomatoes, balsamic vinegar, sun-dried tomatoes and 2-3 tbsp of harissa. 
Fill the tomato tin with water one and a half times and add to the pot. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer, add the lentils and cook for 18-25 mins with the lid on. (If you don’t have a lid, cover with some parchment paper.) 
The amount of time will depend on the type of lentils you use. Green lentils will take about 18 mins, while smaller, black or puy lentils can take up to 25 mins. Keep checking, stirring and adding more water if needed until the lentils are done.
Add the chopped parsley and walnuts, if using, and stir. Taste and season well.

Pour the aubergine filling into a medium-sized baking dish and spoon over the potatoes. Drizzle with a little olive oil if you like and bake until the top starts to turn crisp and golden. Pop it under the grill for 5 mins to crisp up the top.

name: Aubergine Dal With Mango Chutney Yoghurt
description: A simple, vegetarian dal recipe that's got plenty of protein and fibre. This is a healthy weeknight dinner if we've ever seen one.
keywords: Aubergine Dal With Mango Chutney Yoghurt
Aubergine Dal With Mango Chutney Yoghurt recipe
