instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the aubergine into 2cm chunks, tip onto a roasting tray, drizzle with olive oil and season well with salt. Slide into the oven and cook for 25-30 mins, until charred and softened.

Peel the garlic and ginger and use a fine grater to grate, or finely chop. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add 2 tbsp olive oil and the garlic and ginger and fry for 2 mins, then add the spices. Stir well, then add the lentils, along with the coconut milk. Add water, turn the heat up and cook for 10 mins, until reduced. Stir the aubergine in. Add the juice of the lime, taste and season.
Top with the yoghurt, swirl through the mango chutney and top with coriander leaves to serve.

name: Aubergine Hummus Bowl
description: Aubergines are incredible when they're cooked down until they're charred and fudgy. We've paired them with homemade hummus here for the ultimate combo.
instructions: Cut the aubergine up into large chunks. Place a large frying pan over a high heat. Add the aubergine to the pan with a big pinch of salt, dry fry for 10- 15 mins, until blackened on all sides.

Meanwhile, make the hummus. Drain the tin of chickpeas and add to a high speed blender with roasted red peppers, the tahini and harissa and juice of half the lemons. Add a drizzle of olive oil and an ice cube if you have one. Season generously and blend until smooth. Set aside in the fridge to firm up.

Finely shred the cabbage and finely slice the red onion. Pull the mint and parsley leaves from the stem and add to a bowl. Add the juice of a lemon and a tbsp of olive oil and toss well. Season and set aside.
Add the ras el hanout and chickpeas to the aubergine, then add another drizzle of olive oil and the honey, toss well. The aubergine should be collapsed and sticky.
To serve, add a big dollop of hummus to a bowl, pile on the aubergine and salad. Scatter with sesame seeds and serve with flatbreads or toast.

name: Aubergine Involtini
description: Aubergine Involtini is one of those classic Italian comfort dishes. It's rich, hearty, cheesy, and an instant crowdpleaser.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Cut the aubergines into thin slices, lengthways, about 1cm thick. Preheat a griddle pan over a high heat. Rub the aubergine slices with oil and salt and griddle for 2 mins a side, you’re after some lovely bar marks and tender aubergine.
Grate one of the garlic cloves into a bowl and tip in the ricotta. Season with salt and black pepper, tear in half of the mozzarella and add the zest of the lemon.

Lay out your aubergines and top each with a scoop of garlicky ricotta. Chunk up the peppers and add a slice to each aubergine. Now top with a couple of basil leaves each and carefully roll up. Set aside.

Slice the remaining garlic and fry half off in plenty of olive oil in a small saucepan. Add in your chopped tomatoes. Season with salt and cook for 5 mins. Tip into a roasting tray and sit the little aubergine rolls in the sauce. Top with the remaining mozzarella cheese and slide into the oven for 30 mins.

While the involtini are baking, make the garlic ciabatta. Tip the remaining garlic into a small pan and cover with olive oil. Set over a low heat and allow to sizzle for 2-3 mins, then remove from the heat. Finely chop the parsley and add to the garlicky oil along with the pesto.
Split the ciabatta in half and cover with pesto garlic parsley oil. Bake for the last 10 mins with the involtini.
Serve the involtini straight from the tray with garlic ciabatta for dipping.

name: Aubergine Lentil Parmigiana
description: If you’re looking for comforting dishes that still support your health goals, look no further. This aubergine parmigiana packs in plenty of fibre and plant protein, thanks to the addition of hearty and satisfying lentils in the sauce. Using canned lentils and tomatoes helps to speed up the cooking process, making this work for a speedy midweek meal. Studies also show that canned tomatoes have higher levels of beneficial phytonutrient lycopene.
instructions: Slice your aubergine lengthways into 1cm-thick slices. Salt generously on both sides and place onto a tea towel or kitchen paper, then set aside for at least 15 mins.
Meanwhile, finely dice the onion, garlic and chilli and heat the oven to 190°C.

Squeeze the aubergine slices between two tea towels or pieces of kitchen paper to remove any moisture, then place onto a lined tray with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Roast for around 20 mins, turning halfway.

While the aubergine is cooking, make your lentil ragu. Add 2 tbsp oil to a pan set over a medium heat, followed by the finely diced onion. Cook for 5 mins until the onion becomes translucent and slightly golden. Next, add the garlic and chilli. Continue to cook for a minute or so before adding the tomato purée.

Allow the tomato purée to brown for a couple of minutes, then throw in the tomatoes along with half a can of water and the drained lentils. Add the bunch of basil and a generous pinch of salt, then cover and leave to simmer for 15 mins until the sauce thickens. Check the seasoning and add more salt and pepper as needed.

Layer the aubergine slices and the lentil ragu in an ovenproof dish, starting with a layer of ragu on the bottom until you have no more aubergine left. Then top it all off with a final layer of mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake the dish for 30-45 mins until the cheese is bubbling and beginning to brown. Enjoy!

name: Aubergine Parmigiana
description: Everyone loves an aubergine parmigiana, right? We've written up a recipe here to show you how to get one of these cheesy behemoths on the dinner table.
instructions: Heat a splash of olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium/low heat. Finely dice the onions and add to the pan with a big pinch of salt and fry for around 10 mins, or until totally softened.

Slice your garlic as finely as you can, (you can also grate it or crush it if you don't fancy slicing), and add to the pan with the oregano leaves. Cook for a couple more mins. Add the tomato paste and cook it out in the pan for 2 mins. Turn the heat up, then pour in the red wine, bubble away for 2-3 mins, until the wine has reduced by half. Add the tomatoes, bring to the boil, then turn right down to a low simmer, add the pinch of sugar, and leave to bubble away for the VERY LEAST an hour, stirring regularly. (If you can leave for a couple of hours, you'll thank yourself for it).

Meanwhile, heat the grill as high as possible. Grab your largest baking sheet and cover it with foil. Chop the aubergines into chunks. I do this by taking off the tops, quartering lengthways, then slicing the long quarters a few times horizontally into 2-3cm chunks. Tip the chunks out onto the baking sheet – they need to be in an even layer so spread them out over a second tray if you need to- don't worry if it looks like too much, they'll shrink as they cook!

Season the aubergines generously with salt, (don't be tempted to add oil) then slide under the grill to cook for 45 - 50 mins, until really charred and totally collapsed. Tip into a large baking dish, roasting tray, or an ovenproof frying pan if you've halved the recipe!

Turn the oven to 180°C fan. Taste the tomato sauce, add the red wine vinegar and season to taste, adding a little more sugar and salt as it needs. Smush the tomatoes down a little to make a smoother sauce. Pour the tomato sauce over the top of the grilled aubergine chunks, no need for layering here! You might need to use a spoon to make sure the sauce gets all the way to the bottom. Drain the mozzarella balls, pat dry, then tear and use to cover the aubergine and tomato sauce. Finely grate the parmesan over the top. Bake for 30 mins, then allow to sit for 10 mins before serving.

name: Aubergine Parmigiana Bean Salad & Parmesan Dressing
description: A hearty and flavour-packed dish inspired by aubergine parmigiana, featuring roasted aubergine, creamy butter beans, crispy breadcrumbs, and a tangy parmesan dressing. Perfect for meal prep or a comforting dinner.
keywords: Aubergine 'Parmigiana' Beans with Parmesan Dressing recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan.
Cut the aubergines into 2cm slices and cut the tomatoes into irregular pieces.
Place the tomatoes in a sieve over a bowl, season with salt, and set aside to drain.
Toss the aubergine slices with olive oil, salt, and black pepper, then spread onto a baking tray. Roast for 35 mins, flipping for the final 10 mins, until soft and charred.
Heat ½ tbsp olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the breadcrumbs and toast until golden. Remove from heat, then stir in the lemon zest and season with salt and black pepper.
In a bowl, whisk together the yoghurt, honey, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and grated parmesan. Season with salt and black pepper. For a smoother consistency, blend the dressing until fully combined.
Add the butter beans to a bowl along with the roasted aubergine and drained tomatoes. Toss to combine. If using, mix in the rocket.

To serve, divide into boxes or plates, drizzle with the parmesan dressing, and sprinkle with crispy breadcrumbs. Garnish with fresh basil and extra parmesan. If packing for meal prep, store the breadcrumbs separately and add just before serving.

name: Aubergine Parmigiana Jacket Potato
description: The mash-up you didn’t know you needed. Crispy jacket potatoes stuffed with layers of rich, melty aubergine parmigiana goodness. Feels like big time comfort food, but it’s a little bit nourishing too.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

Rub the potatoes in olive oil, salt and pepper then wrap them individually in tin foil and pop them on a baking tray. Slide into the top shelf of the oven for 1 hr then take off the foil and cook for another 15 mins until crisp.
Dice the aubergine and add to another baking tray. Toss with a glug of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Slide into the oven, below the potatoes, to roast for 25 mins under tender.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large pan set over a medium heat until foamy and nutty. Add the flour and cook it out for a couple of minutes. Gradually add in the milk whilst whisking constantly until you have a smooth sauce. Add the bay leaf and grate in the nutmeg, if using, then simmer for a few minutes until thickened. Grate in half of the Parmesan and tear in the mozzarella, then give it a good stir and season with salt and pepper to taste.

Finely mince the garlic and basil stalks – reserving the leaves for later. Heat a shot of olive oil in a new pan set over a medium heat then add the garlic and basil stalks. Cook for a couple of minutes then tip in the canned tomatoes and season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer then tear the basil leaves (save a few for garnish) and stir them through the sauce. Remove from the heat.

Remove the baked potatoes from the oven. Heat the grill. Cut a cross into each potato and push the skin outward to open it up. Add a pat of butter, if you like, then season with salt and pepper and use a fork to mash the potato until smooth.
Top each potato with a handful of roasted aubergine, then spoon over the tomato sauce. Add a layer of the cheese sauce then grate over the rest of the Parmesan.
Slide the potatoes under the grill and cook until bubbling and golden. Serve with a few extra basil leaves and a crack of black pepper.

name: Aubergine Parmigiana Orzo
description: Imagine aubergine parm and a silky bowl of pasta had a baby. This is she. Tomatoey orzotto topped with crispy basil crumbs. Incredible.
instructions: Heat your oven to 170°C.
Thinly slice your bread, then drizzle it with a little olive oil. Bake in the oven for 15 mins until crisp.
Break your bread into a food processor or blender and add your basil leaves. Pulse until you have crispy green breadcrumbs. Set aside until later.
Finely dice your onion. Finely mince your garlic and dice your aubergine into 2cm chunks. Halve your cherry tomatoes.
Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large sauté pan. Add your onions and cook over a medium heat for 15 mins until totally soft.
Add your aubergine chunks and turn up the heat. Fry for another 10 mins until they are tender, stirring frequently so that all the chunks cook evenly.

Add your garlic, chilli flakes and tomato purée, then cook for another 2 mins. Tip in your cherry tomatoes and turn down the heat a little. Cook down for 5 mins, smooshing them with your wooden spoon to create a sauce.
Get a pan of water on to boil. Add a good handful of salt, then tip in your orzo. Cook for 6 mins until tender.
Add a mugful of pasta water to your aubergine pan, then drain your orzo. Tip the orzo in with the sauce and give it a good mix. Grate in your parmesan, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon your orzo into bowls and top with a drizzle of olive oil, some mozzarella (if you fancy it), a grating of parmesan and a sprinkle of your basil breadcrumbs. Serve and enjoy!

name: Aubergine Parmigiana Salad
description: You love aubergine parmigiana, right? Well, you're going to love this aubergine parmigiana salad. It's a whopper of a salad. And it's lighter than it sounds.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Slice the aubergines in half lengthways, then slice each half into 3 long wedges and put them all on a baking sheet. Sprinkle with salt. Wrap the garlic bulb in foil and snuggle onto the same tray. Roast for 45 mins, until the aubergine is charred and collapsing.

Meanwhile, blitz the sourdough to the size of chunky breadcrumbs. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium high heat, add the breadcrumbs and fry, stirring, for 6-8 mins, until golden. Finely grate the parmesan over the breadcrumbs for the last minute and toss well, coating and letting the parmesan melt. Tip into a bowl.
Meanwhile, whisk 3 tbsp olive oil with the oregano and a pinch of salt and pepper. Add the charred aubergine wedges to the oil and toss.

To make the dressing, grate the plum tomatoes, discarding the skin. Add the grated tomato to a blender along with 3 tbsp olive oil, the mustard and lemon juice, plus seasoning. Squeeze the roasted garlic flesh from the bulb and into the blender, then blitz until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Drain and slice the mozzarella and slice the beef tomatoes. Season both with salt. Place the aubergine and sliced tomatoes onto a big platter, then snuggle the mozzarella around it. Season with salt, then drizzle over the tomato dressing. Scatter the parmesan breadcrumbs on top and finish with basil, an extra drizzle of olive oil and a crack of black pepper.

name: Aubergine Parmigiana Sub
description: What’s better than an aubergine parm? An aubergine parm that’s been lovingly wedged in a soft sub roll. This aubergine parmigiana sub is the bee's knees.
instructions: Trim the ends off the aubergines then cut lengthways into 1cm-long strips. Season with salt and leave for 20 minutes whilst you make the sauce.

Finely chop the onion and garlic cloves. Get a small saucepan overa medium heat. Drizzle in a good glug of olive oil. Scrape in the onion along with a pinch of salt and fry, stirring occasionally, until completely soft. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and fry, stirring for 30 seconds, then tip in the plum tomatoes. Use the back of your spoon to break up the tomatoes, add the sugar then lower the heat and leave the sauce to simmer away.

Spoon the flour out onto a plate. Lightly coat half the aubergineslices in the flour – this will help make them jammy and soft withoutabsorbing too much oil. Get a large non-stick frying pan over a medium–high heat, drizzle in a good amount of oil then place half the floured aubergine slices in the pan. Fry for 6–8 mins, turning halfway, until golden and soft. Transfer to a plate then repeat with the remaining aubergine.

Preheat your grill to high. Slice the rolls three-quarters of the waythrough the centre, opening them up slightly so you can fit in the most amount of filling. Season your sauce with salt and black pepper and stir through most of the basil leaves.

Assembly time. Thinly spread sauce over the bottom of each sub.Layer up the aubergine, more sauce and mozzarella, tearing the cheese in as you go, making sure to finish with a layer of mozzarella. Finely grate over the Parmesan. Season with black pepper then slide under the hot grill until golden and bubbling. Tear over the remaining basil leaves and drizzle with a little more oil to serve.

name: Aubergine Tikka Masala
description: Aubergine gets lovely and smokey on the griddle pan and so works an absolute charm in this dish. A great veggie version of the classic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Cut aubergines into strips and salt them. Leave for 10 minutes and then pat dry (this removes excess moisture).
Place the aubergine strips into a bowl. Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin. Season with salt and pepper and mix everything together.

Heat a griddle pan. Once very hot, add your aubergines in batches. Cook on a high heat for 4 minutes on each side until charred. Place the char-grilled aubergine in the oven for 12 minutes so they can cook through.
Time to get on with the curry sauce. Slice up your onions. Add to a large pan with a good drizzle of olive oil. Cook on a medium heat until the onions are lovely and caramelised.
Add a finely chopped garlic clove and a chopped knob of ginger. Mix them in. Add half a tsp of turmeric, and a tsp each of chilli powder, ground coriander and cumin. Mix everything together.
Add a heaped tbsp of tomato purée. Give it all a good stir and pour in the passata.
Add your coconut cream into the curry. Stir it through and bring the sauce to the boil. Once it is bubbling, turn it down, and let it simmer and thicken for 2 minutes.
Add your aubergine and stir. Add 300ml of water and bring to a simmer. Bring it to a medium heat and cover for 15 minutes.
Get your rice on (follow pack instructions).
Serve the aubergine tikka masala over a bed of steaming rice. Garnish with some chopped coriander. Enjoy!

name: Aubergine With Coconut Satay Sauce
description: This vegan recipe combines a rich and fragrant satay sauce with fudgy baked aubergines. It's as good as that sounds.
keywords: Aubergine With Coconut Satay Sauce recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C

Cut the aubergines in half and then slice in half again, keeping the stems intact. If they are large enough, cut each half into quarters, still keeping the stem intact. Drizzle with plenty of olive oil and season with salt and pepper, rubbing into all of the nooks.
Place the aubergines slices on a lined baking dish, cut-side down, and roast for 30 mins.
Cook the rice according to package instructions. Drain the chickpeas and stir them through the rice.

Meanwhile, make the satay sauce. Finely chop the shallot and mince the ginger and garlic. Add the shallots to a pan with a good drizzle of olive oil and fry for 3-4 mins, stirring often, until softened. Add the ginger, garlic, curry powder, chilli flakes (if using) and cook for 2 more mins.
Then add the coconut milk, soy sauce, peanut butter, and agave. Simmer for about 10 mins on medium heat until it’s thickened and fragrant.

After the aubergines have been cooking for 30 mins, remove them from the oven and drizzle over the peanut sauce, saving a few tablespoons to the side. Return to the oven for another 10 mins until golden.
Finely slice the chilli and roughly chop the peanuts. Serve the aubergines over the chickpeas and rice and drizzle with the reserved peanut sauce and any of your chosen toppings.

name: Avocado & Jalapeño Crema
description: A creamy, tangy, and slightly spicy avocado sauce that’s perfect for tacos, grilled meats, or as a dip. Packed with fresh flavours and ready in minutes.
instructions: Deseed and chop the jalapeños. Add the Greek yoghurt, jalapeños, avocado, half of the coriander, and lime juice to a blender.
Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
Season with salt to taste.
Garnish with extra coriander and serve.

name: Avocado, Kale & Feta Salad
description: The crunchiness of the raw kale is softened by a creamy spiced lemon and avocado dressing. Salty feta and toasted seeds take this kale salad to the next level.
instructions:
Cut one avocado in half, remove the pit and scoop out the flesh
into a mini food processor. Cut the lemons in half and squeeze all
the juice into the food processor. Add the ground coriander,
a generous pinch of salt, some black pepper, a glug of extra virgin
olive oil and chilli flakes to taste. Blitz to a dressing.
Tip the dressing into a large serving bowl. Add the bag of kale.
Use your hands to massage the dressing into the kale. Set aside.
Halve, pit, peel and slice the remaining avocado. Pile on top of the
salad. Do not mix.
Get a dry frying pan over a medium heat and add the mixed
seeds. Let the seeds toast while you deseed and roughly chop
the yellow peppers and chop the radishes. Tip the veg and
toasted seeds into the salad.
Crumble over the feta and give everything a toss to combine.
Adjust the seasoning to taste, then serve the salad at the table for
people to help themselves.

name: BBQ Chicken Pitta
description: Intensely crispy chicken skin in a soft pitta with a lemony slaw, tangy dressing and pickled onions.
instructions: Preheat the grill to high. Place the chicken into a bowl and sprinkle on the smoked paprika, ½ tsp salt, a good grinding of black pepper and a big glug of olive oil. Mix well so it's evenly coated and stained red.

Line a baking tray with foil. Place the chicken onto the tray, making sure to pour all of the marinade on top. Slide onto the middle rack of the grill and cook for 10-15 mins, or until cooked through. If the chicken is charring too quickly, turn the grill down a notch.
Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion. Add them in a bowl with the juice of 1/2 the lemon, season with salt and scrunch the onions with your hands to quick pickle.
Finely slice your white cabbage and combine in a bowl with half the soured cream, the juice of the remaining lemon, season with salt and pepper.
For the sauce, combine the remaining soured cream with the hot sauce. Mix well and season with salt and pepper.
Roughly chop the chicken and pick the leaves of the parsley. Combine the parsley with the pickled onions.
Toast the pitta and stuff with the cabbage, chicken, pickled red onion mix and the sour cream hot sauce and enjoy!

name: BBQ Chicken Quesadillas
description: Spicy shredded chicken. Loads of Bull’s-Eye Smokey Chipotle BBQ Sauce. Beautiful melted cheese. So quick to make. An absolute winner.
instructions: Get your chicken thighs in a bowl. Add your smoked paprika, cumin and cayenne pepper along with a glug of olive oil, salt and pepper. Give it a good mix so your chicken is evenly coated in the spices.

Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add your chicken and cook for 4 mins on each side - they should be caramelised on the outside and lovely and tender in the middle when the time is up. Remove from the pan and leave to cool a little.
Grate your red leicester and mozzarella. Finely slice your spring onions.
Finely shred your chicken with 2 forks. Pop the chicken in a bowl then add your Bull’s-Eye Smokey Chipotle BBQ Sauce and sliced spring onions.
Wipe out your chicken pan to clean it, then add a tortilla to the pan on a low heat. Add a handful of mozzarella, red leicester, some chicken mixture and then more cheese. Top with a second tortilla.
Cook on both sides until golden brown and then slice into quarters. Serve and enjoy!

name: BBQ Chilli Cheeseburger
description: Chilli cheese burgers blow most other burgers out the park. Sweet with Bull’s-Eye Original BBQ Sauce, spicy, cheesy and savoury. All the good stuff.
instructions: Finely chop your chillies and roughly chop your coriander. Add them to a food processor along with your pickled jalapeños, lime juice and a pinch of salt. Blitz to a smooth paste.
Add your beef mince to a bowl and season with salt and pepper, lightly tossing the mince so the seasoning is combined but not overworking it.
Grate your red leicester cheese.
Heat a frying pan on a high heat. Fry your streaky bacon until crisp. Toast your burger buns.

Take an eighth of the beef mixture and shape it into a loose ball. Place it in the pan and press it down with your spatula. Place a piece of baking parchment on top, then compress the patties with a heavy cast iron pan. Fry for 2 mins.
Flip over your patties and brush them with Bull’s-Eye Original BBQ Sauce. Top with a handful of Red Leicester, then place a lid on the pan and let the cheese melt.

Assembly time. Place some Bull’s-Eye Original BBQ Sauce on the base of your burger, then top with two patties and a slice of bacon. Spread your chilli chutney on the lid of the buns, then pop on top of the burgers. Serve!

name: BBQ Lamb Chops & Burnt Aubergines
description: Lamb chops are the perfect meat for the barbecue. Grilling these lamb chops and coating them in fresh herbs is an essential summer move.
keywords: BBQ Lamb Chops & Burnt Aubergines recipe
instructions: Pile coals over to one side of your BBQ to create a hot, direct cooking side, and a warm, indirect cooking side. Add the aubergines to the hot side and cover with a lid. Cook for 9-10 mins, turning regularly, until thoroughly charred and burnt. Once completely tender, transfer to a bowl and cover with a lid or plate and allow to steam for 10 mins.

While the aubergines steam, marinade the lamb. Chuck the chops into a bowl with the paprika and a good pinch of salt. Finely grate in the garlic cloves and add the fish sauce. Finely chop the rosemary and get that into the bowl, too.

Once steamed, peel the burnt skins from the aubergines and tip the flesh into a bowl. Add the tahini and yoghurt and mash the aubergine through. Add the juice of a lemon and season with salt and black pepper. Aim for a chunky, creamy, dippable texture. Set aside.

Quarter the red onions and rub with oil and salt. Grill on the cut sides until thoroughly charred and burnt. Pull over to the indirect side to rest. Grill the lamb chops over the direct heat for 3-4 mins a side. Place on the indirect side to rest for 5-6 mins.

Separate the grilled onions into petals and toss with a little lemon juice. Finely chop the parsley and stir through the aubergine. Spread the burnt aubergine over one side of a plate and top with burnt onion petals and a little aleppo pepper.
Pile the grilled chops onto the other side and serve.

name: BBQ Spatchcock Chicken Flatbreads
description: Don’t be put off by spatchcocking the chicken or making the flatbreads. Both are so simple and it's definitely worth the effort.
instructions: Heat the BBQ until hot or heat an oven to 220°C/200°C Fan.

Chicken time. Lay the chicken on your chopping board breast side down then, using a pair of scissors, cut either side of the back bone to remove it. Once the bone is removed, turn the chicken breast side up, and using your hands apply some weight to the chicken to flatten it.

Next - marinade. Crush the garlic cloves into a bowl, spoon in the paprika/chilli flakes, cumin, 1 tsp of dried oregano and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Zest and juice in the lemon then pour in a good glug of olive oil and mix.

Pour the marinade over the chicken, getting into all the crevices. Place the chicken breast side up on the BBQ, or on a tray in the oven. If roasting in the oven, cook for 40-45 minutes until cooked through. For BBQ, cook on the bone side for 40 minutes, checking occasionally. Move the chicken around the BBQ to make sure it is cooking evenly, then flip and finish breast side down for 10-15 minutes.

Flatbread time. Mix together the flour, yoghurt and salt with 2 tbsp water, using your hands to bring the dough together. If the dough is looking a little dry, add the remaining tbsp of water. Knead for a minute until there are no visible dry bits then put back in the bowl. Cover with a clean tea towel and leave to rest until your chicken is cooked.

On to the Greek salad. Roughly chop the tomatoes, cucumber and other salad veggies. Pour in the red wine vinegar, 1 tsp of oregano and a good glug of olive oil and add your olives. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Once the chicken is done, transfer to a plate, cover loosely with foil and let rest.
Flour your surface. Cut the dough into 8 pieces. Roll each into a rough ball with your hands. Then, using a rolling pin, roll into oval flatbreads 1/2 cm thick.

Get a large griddle hot, or cook on your BBQ. In batches, cook the flatbreads for 2 minutes on each side. Once golden, wrap inside a clean tea towel, sprinkle with a little water and pile on top of each other to keep them light and soft.
Tear the mint into the Greek salad and crumble in the feta. Bring the chicken, a big knife for carving, flatbreads, salad and yoghurt outside for ultimate summer roast vibes.

name: BBQ'd Courgettes with Yoghurt & Brown Butter
description: Chargrilled courgettes served with a beautiful browned butter yoghurt. It's the ultimate vegetarian barbecue recipe.
keywords: BBQ'd Courgettes with Yoghurt & Brown Butter
BBQ'd Courgettes with Yoghurt & Brown Butter recipe
instructions: Pile coals over to one side of your BBQ to create a hot, direct cooking side, and a warm, indirect cooking side.

Cut the courgettes into chunks, rolling the courgette around as you cut to create irregular shapes. Toss with oil and salt and pile onto the hot side of the grill. Leave to cook, untouched, for 5-6 mins or until one side is really well charred. Toss straight into a bowl.

Roughly chop the mint and add to the same bowl, along with the vinegar. Thinly slice the onion and add to the bowl. Toss everything together and top with a bowl to allow the courgettes to steam and soak in that vinegar.

Meanwhile, spread the yoghurt over the base of a plate and set a pan over the heat of the BBQ. Add the butter to the pan and let it melt, bubble and start to brown. Add the chilli flakes and a couple of smashed garlic cloves. Allow to infuse into the butter.
Pile the warm courgettes and onions onto the plate, then top with the hot chilli butter. Serve with flatbreads on the side and lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: BLT Chicken Salad
description: It’s a BLT in salad form. Juicy chicken, crispy bacon and a tomato dressing that brings everything together. High protein meal prep done right.
instructions: Butterfly the chicken breasts and season them generously with salt and pepper.
Add the bacon to a frying pan and place over a medium heat. Cook for 4–5 mins, until crispy and golden on both sides. Transfer to a plate, keeping the fat in the pan.
Add the chicken breasts to the same pan. Cook for 10–15 mins, flipping occasionally, until golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves and discard the stems. Chop the tomatoes (for the salad) into bite-sized chunks. Remove any tough kale stalks and add the leaves to a large bowl. Season with salt and massage for a couple of minutes until soft and wilted.

Make the dressing. Halve the tomato and coarsely grate the cut side into a bowl, discarding the skins. Crumble in half of the cooked bacon. Stir through the olive oil and season with salt, black pepper and a splash of sherry vinegar, to taste.
Add the parsley, chopped tomatoes, quinoa and tomato dressing to the bowl of kale. Toss everything together until well combined.

Slice the cooked chicken breasts. Share the salad between Tupperware containers and top with the chicken. Finish with the remaining crumbled bacon and a generous crack of black pepper. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

Slice the cooked chicken breasts. Share the salad between plates and top with the chicken. Finish with the remaining crumbled bacon and a generous crack of black pepper.

name: BLT Toastie
description: A BLT is the GOAT sandwich. Add cheese? Sure. We've levelled up your grilled cheese with juicy tomatoes and crispy bacon. Lettuce on the side.
instructions: Lay the bacon in an even layer in a large, cold frying pan. Set the pan over a medium heat and allow the bacon fat to render and the rashers to crisp. This should take between 10-11 mins.
Remove the crispy bacon from the pan, leaving the residual fat, this is what we'll use to cook our toasties.
Thickly slice the tomatoes and season generously with salt and black pepper. Separate the lettuce into leaves and coarsely grate the cheddar cheese.
To build your sandwiches, start with a slice of sourdough, top with mayo, black pepper, cheese, bacon, a couple of thick slices of tomato, more cheese and crown with a mayo'd lid.
Cook the sandwiches over a medium heat in the bacon fat, turning regularly, for 10-12 mins until fully melted and warm all the way through.
Dress the lettuce with olive oil, salt and lemon and serve on the side of your warm, gooey BLT toasties for a hit of fresh crunch.
Get stuck in.

name: Baba Ganoush Pasta Salad
description: Check out our baba ganoush recipe to make your own. This is great to use any leftovers. Smokey aubergine, kalamata olives and juicy, sweet pomegranate seeds.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.
Place the garlic bulb onto a tray and place in the oven for 30 minutes.

As the garlic is cooking, char the aubergines on a gas stove. As the aubergines begin to cook, the skin will start to blacken. Once the skin is completely charred and black, remove the aubergines and place them in a bowl of ice cold water.
As the aubergines cool, the skin will become loose, allowing you to peel away the charred skin easily from the aubergine, leaving only the middle.
Get the pasta on.

Chop the ends off the peeled aubergines and place them in a bowl. Remove the garlic bulb from the oven. Take one clove of garlic at a time and squeeze the inside of each clove from its skin (this should be easy because they are cooked). Once you have squeezed each clove, combine the aubergine and the garlic with a fork, mashing it up.

Add tahini, the juice of a lemon, a large glug of olive oil and a sprinkling of pepper before mixing again. Roughly chop up the basil and sprinkle on top. Give your Baba Ganoush a final mix before setting aside.

Once your pasta is cooked, drain, setting a little pasta water aside. Combine the pasta with the Baba Ganoush mixture, stirring well. In a separate pan, lightly toast the pine nuts and add this to the mixture along with the kalamata olives and two thirds of the pomegranate seeds.

Roughly chop up the mint, adding two thirds to the pasta mixture along with the remaining pasta water and a sprinkling of salt and pepper in order to loosen the sauce slightly, giving it a silky consistency.
Serve by sprinkling the remaining mint and pomegranate seeds over the top of each bowl.

name: Baby Potato Salad With Harissa Butter & Chives
description: This is it, the summery potato salad you all need. Tossed in a spicy harissa butter, lots of lemon, tomatoes (health!), and some fancy chives on top. Lovely.
keywords: Baby Potato Salad With Harissa Butter & Chives
instructions: Add the potatoes to a large pan and cover with cold water. Add salt like you would with pasta and bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. After 15 mins, the potatoes should be cooked through.
Meanwhile, peel and finely slice the red onion into rings. Add to a small bowl along with the zest and juice of a lemon and a pinch of salt.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and set aside.
Once the potatoes are cooked, drain and transfer to a large bowl. Cube in the butter, add the harissa and mix well until the butter melts.
Add the onions and lemon juice along with the cherry tomatoes, a pinch of salt and some black pepper. Toss again and then transfer to a platter.
Finely chop the chives and sprinkle over the top.

name: Bacon & Broccoli Pasta
description: Crispy bacon, tender broccoli and pasta all tossed together with a lemony basil whipped ricotta. A dinner the kids’ll devour plus the adults get fancy bits too.
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsBring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the pasta and cook following pack instructions. Cut the broccoli into small florets and add to the pan for the final 2 mins of cooking. Drain, reserving a mugful of the pasta water.
Finely chop the bacon. Add to a cold frying pan with a drizzle of oil and set over a medium heat. Cook for 4–6 mins until golden and crisp.

Meanwhile, make the whipped ricotta for the adults. Pick most of the basil leaves (save a few small ones for garnish) and add to a small food processor with the ricotta. Grate in the zest of the lemon, season with black pepper and add a drizzle of olive oil. Blitz until smooth and creamy.
Tip the pasta and broccoli into the pan with the bacon. Grate in the Parmesan and toss everything together, loosening with splashes of reserved pasta water until you’ve got a silky sauce.

Serve up!Kids Plate: Spoon the pasta onto plates and serve with extra grated cheese on top.Parents Plate: Dish up the pasta, then add a dollop of whipped basil ricotta. Finish with the reserved basil leaves, a crack of black pepper and lemon wedges on the side.

name: Bacon Fried Egg with Spicy Pineapple Salad
description: Crispy bacon, jammy fried eggs and a punchy pineapple salad with bird's-eye chilli and lime. Fresh, fiery and on the table in 20 mins.
keywords: Bacon Fried Egg with Spicy Pineapple Salad
Bacon Fried Egg with Spicy Pineapple Salad recipe
instructions: Chop the bacon rashers into 2cm chunks and place into a large frying pan. Turn the heat to medium and leave to render and crisp for 4-6 mins.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the pineapple, cucumber, chillies and shallot, and roughly chop the coriander. Add the shallot and chilli to a bowl with the juice of the limes, season with salt and stir in the pineapple.
Place the cucumber into a sieve, toss with a pinch of salt and set aside over a bowl to draw out any excess moisture.
Once the bacon is starting to brown, crack the eggs on top and fry to your liking.

Reheat the rice according to packet instructions and share between plates. Toss the cucumber and coriander into the pineapple salad and taste, seasoning with salt and a pinch of sugar if needed to balance. Top the rice with a bacon fried egg and serve the salad alongside.

name: Bacon Mac & Cheese
description: Crispy smoked bacon with a Mac was always going to work. With the creamiest cheesy sauce. Topped off with breadcrumbs for that crispy finish. A certified 10/10.
instructions: Preheat your grill to 180°C/356°F.

Chop your bacon up into small pieces and place them in a frying pan. Cook until crispy and golden. Chop up your spring onions and tear off a handful of fresh rosemary, saving some for later, and add this to the pan. Stir through for a few minutes and then transfer to a bowl to use later.

Add 2 tbsp of olive oil to the frying pan with your flour. Whisk until the olive oil and flour have combined and then add a splash of milk. Whisk, and then keep adding milk and whisking until you have a creamy consistency.
Get your macaroni on.

While the pasta cooks, it’s time for cheese! Go back to your frying pan of creamy goodness and sprinkle in cheddar and parmesan and tear in the mozzarella. Give the sauce a good mix until all the cheese has melted.
Add the macaroni to the cheesy sauce, give it a stir and then whack in the bacon mixture. Season with a good pinch of salt, black pepper and stir.
Sprinkle the mac with your breadcrumbs, grate some more parmesan over the top, tear in the saved rosemary and crack pepper over to finish.
Place the pan under a hot grill for 8 minutes, or until the breadcrumbs are crispy and golden-brown on top. Plate up and enjoy this bad boy!

name: Bacon, Brie & Blueberry French Toastie
description: A French toast recipe filled with oozy brie, salty bacon and tangy blueberry chutney. A beautiful little Christmas brunch solution.
instructions: Put the blueberries into a small saucepan with the red wine vinegar, then gently heat until the blueberries are bursting – give them a bit of a squish to make a loose jam.
Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the bacon. Cook until deeply golden, around 5 mins, then remove and drain on kitchen paper.

Whisk the eggs and milk, then season with salt and pepper, then slice the brie. Wipe out the bacon pan and add the butter, melting over a medium heat. Briefly dip one piece of bread into the egg mixture and then add into the buttery pan, lay on slices of the brie, top with the bacon and a spoonful of jammy blueberries. Repeat with another piece of bread, then when the bottom piece is golden, carefully flip and cook.
Cut in half and serve immediately topped with maple syrup and icing sugar.

name: Bacony Gnocchi Bake
description: It doesn't get more comforting than this one. Salty smoked bacon, soft gnocchi, fresh basil, sweet tomatoes and delicious melted mozzarella & parmesan. Sublime.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C/400°F. Add smoked bacon lardons to a large deep frying pan and cook until crispy on a medium-low heat.
Add your cherry tomatoes and cook until they start to burst. Chop your garlic and add it to the pan. Stir in your basil leaves.
Once they have wilted, mix everything together. Season with salt and pepper. Bubble down until the sauce is thick and rich.
Once the sauce has thickened remove from the heat, fold in the spinach to wilt (this may need to be done in batches) then fold the gnocchi into the sauce.
Pour the gnocchi into a baking dish and flatten it out. Tear two balls of mozzarella over the top. Cover the whole dish with grated Parmesan, season with pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.
Bake in the oven 15 minutes or until the cheese is golden and bubbling. Enjoy!

name: Bacony Packet Noodles
description: Taking your packet noodles to the next level by ditching the flavour sachet that comes with them and creating your own sauce. Bacon and chilli oil. Go on...
instructions: Spoon your peanut butter into a bowl and mix together with your soy sauce, chilli oil, rice vinegar and 2 tbsp of water until you get a thick, creamy, rich sauce. Then set aside.
Chop your bacon into chunks and fry in a non-stick pan until crispy.
Meanwhile, finely chop your spring onion (setting aside a handful for garnish) and ginger. Add to the pan along with your five-spice for an aromatic kick, then stir together.
In another pan bring your noodles to the boil. Simmer for about 3 minutes then add to your bacony pan. Set some of the noodle water aside.
Next, take your peanut sauce and toss it through the noodles until they are evenly coated - add a splash of the noodle water to loosen it.
Plate up and garnish with a sprinkle of spring onion and a tsp chilli oil then you’re ready to dig in.

name: Baharat Chicken Bowl with Grated Feta
description: Juicy baharat-marinated chicken skewers with zingy salad, cooling tzatziki and grated feta. Your meal prep lunch just got a serious upgrade.
instructions: Pop the feta into the freezer. This helps it grate more easily later.

Zest the lemons (reserve half for the tzatziki) and juice ¼ of the lemon into a bowl. Whisk together ¼ of the yoghurt with the baharat, lemon zest and juice. Season with salt. Cut the chicken into chunks, then toss in the marinade. Ideally chill overnight, or for at least 20 mins.
If you’re using bamboo skewers, soak them in water.

Peel and finely slice the red onion. Squeeze over the remaining lemon juice and season with salt and pepper. Scrunch together with your hands to help quick-pickle the onion. Cut the remaining lemon half into wedges for serving.

Cut the cucumber in half lengthwise and use a spoon to scoop out the seeds. Coarsely grate one-third of the cucumber and squeeze out the excess liquid. Chop most of the dill. Stir the grated cucumber, chopped dill and remaining lemon zest and yoghurt together to make a quick tzatziki. Season with salt and pepper.
Shred the lettuce. Chop the tomatoes and remaining cucumber into bite-sized chunks. Roughly chop the rest of the dill. Toss everything together with a drizzle of olive oil and season to taste.
Heat a grill pan on high. Thread the chicken onto skewers and grill for about 2 mins per side until lightly charred and cooked through.

Dish out the salad and top with pickled onions and a little drizzle of olive oil. Add the chicken skewers. Grate over the frozen feta and dollop on the tzatziki. Serve with lemon wedges and a pinch more baharat, if you fancy.

name: Baharat Chicken Bowl with Grated Feta
description: Juicy baharat-marinated chicken skewers with zingy salad, cooling tzatziki and grated feta. Weeknight dinner levelled up.

name: Baja Fish Tacos by Breddos Tacos
description: Nud is the founder of Breddos (arguably the best tacos in London). These are his fish tacos. The way he preps the fish should be followed to the letter. Enjoy.
instructions: Start by making your mango salsa. Dice your mango into small chunks, finely chop your jalapeños and mint then mix together in a bowl. Squeeze in your lime and add a pinch of salt, pepper, sugar and a drizzle of olive oil. Set aside.
Now for the chipotle mayo, it’s super easy! Just mix together your mayo, sriracha, and chipotle then set aside.
Quarter your cabbage and slice it into thin strips. Set aside.
On to the wet fish batter. Into a bowl, add 150g plain flour, baking powder, salt, pepper, beer, and vodka. Whisk well to create a smooth batter.

Frying time. Add the remaining flour (100g) to a bowl. Chop your fish into 8 strips and dip each chunk into the flour, shake off any excess then dip it straight into the wet fish batter, making sure it is thoroughly coated.
Heat your rapeseed oil to 180°C/ 356°F. Then, carefully massage the fish into the oil and repeat for all fish chunks. Leave to fry for about 5 minutes until golden and crunchy.
Once your fish is ready, place it on some kitchen roll to cool down. Meanwhile, warm up your tortillas by placing them in a dry pan over low heat until slightly browned.

Time to assemble! Take a tortilla, place some red cabbage on the bottom, followed your chipotle mayonnaise, then the fried fish and a tsp of the mango salsa. Top with a couple of coriander leaves, a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt. Tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Baked Aubergine Meatballs
description:
These veggie meatballs are packed with aubergine and fragrant herbs, then baked with lots of cheese 
and a jammy tomato sauce. I think you might like it. Soph x
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Finely slice your onion. Dice your aubergines into small chunks. Finely chop your garlic and parsley.
Heat a saute pan over a medium heat with a little olive oil. Add your sliced onion and cook until softened, about 10 mins.
Drain your lentils, then tip them onto a baking tray. Bake for 15 mins until they have dried out slightly.

Add your aubergine chunks to the same pan as your onions with a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Fry for 5 mins until totally soft and tender. Tip in half of your garlic and cook for another 2 mins. Allow your aubergines and lentils to cool slightly.

Add your bread to the food processor and whizz to crumbs, then remove 25g to save until later. Tip the aubergines and lentils into your food processor, along with your onions, parmesan, all but a tbsp of your parsley and salt and pepper. Whizz to a paste, then season to taste.
Roll your mixture into 12 equal sized balls.
Place them on a parchment lined baking tray, then drizzle with a little olive oil.
Bake for 40 mins until crisp.

Meanwhile, make your tomato sauce. Heat a little olive oil in a saute pan over medium heat. Add your remaining garlic and chilli flakes, and cook for 1 min. Tip in your tinned tomatoes and add a sprig of basil. Simmer for 25 mins until reduced.
Whizz up with a stick blender if you like it smoother, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Heat your grill to high.
Mix your remaining 25g of breadcrumbs with chopped parsley.
Pour your sauce into a baking dish. Add your meatballs, then tears over your mozzarella. Grate over a little parmesan and sprinkle on your breadcrumbs, then grill for 5 mins.
Top with basil leaves, then serve!

name: Baked Beetroot Soup With Spicy Seeds
description: Beetroot are baked until tender and whizzed up with onions, garlic and warming spices, topped with crunchy spicy seeds.
keywords: Baked Beetroot Soup With Spicy Seeds
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place the beetroots into a roasting dish, pour over 200ml of water and cover tightly with tin foil. Bake until tender, about 1/1.5 hours.
Meanwhile, finely slice the onions and add to a large saucepan over a medium heat with a splash of olive oil. Cook until soft, about 7 mins.
Mince the garlic and add along with 1 tbsp of the ras el hanout and the chilli (if using) and cook for another 2 mins. Set aside.
In a small pan, toast the seeds until golden, add the remaining ras el hanout and take off the heat. Mix well and set aside.
Once the beetroots are ready, remove them from the oven and slip their skins off. Roughly chop and add to a blender along with the onion mix and vegetable stock. Whizz until smooth.
Transfer the mix back to the saucepan, heat until piping, then taste and add salt.
Pour into bowls and swirl in a spoon of yoghurt. Finely chop the parsley and sprinkle over, top with the seeds and enjoy.

name: Baked Camembert With Spicy Pickle Dressing & Croissant Croutons
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This is a perfect twist on a classic. We’ve swapped out crusty bread for flaky baked croissants, cheers Aldi.
keywords: Baked Camebert With Spicy Pickle Dressing & Croissant Croutons
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Remove the cheese from the plastic wrapper and pop into a cheese baking dish or back into the wooden box. Score the top in a criss cross pattern and season with salt and pepper.
Cut the croissants into bite-sized chunks and place onto a baking tray. Toss with oil, salt and black pepper. Throw on a few sprigs of rosemary and two smashed garlic cloves.
Pop the cheese and the tray of croissant pieces into the oven and bake for 20 mins, turning the croissants halfway through cooking.

While they’re ticking along, make your herby, pickly, spicy dressing. Pick a handful of rosemary leaves and finely chop them, you don’t want any stem here so get ‘em out of there. Finely chop the red chilli, keeping the seeds if you like it hot. Tip the whole lot into heatproof bowl.
Heat 4-5 tbsp of olive oil until just under smoking point. Pour over the chilli and rosemary and leave to infuse for 5 mins.

Finely chop the gherkins and add to the oil, rosemary and chilli with a big pinch of salt and black pepper. Add a splash of gherkin liquor and have a taste. You want this to be tangy, the cheese is super rich and this is your cut through element.
Once the croissant pieces are crunchy and golden, and the cheese is like liquid gold, pull them out the oven.
Pop the cheese onto a sharing board and surround with croissant dippers. Cover the cheese with the pickle dressing and get dipping.

name: Baked Cheesecake With Roasted Cherries
description: This baked cheesecake recipe guarantees a velvety texture by cooking it in a water bath at a low temperature. Using egg yolks adds richness, while the spare egg whites you don't use can be frozen for meringues. The recipe involves preparing a smooth mixture of cream cheese, sour cream, and caster sugar, which is then poured into a springform pan lined with digestive biscuits or graham cracker crust. After baking, the cheesecake should be cooled and refrigerated to set, enhancing its flavour and creamy consistency. This oven-baked dessert keeps well in the fridge for up to five days, making it a convenient and delicious choice for sweet desserts. Whether you’re a fan of New York cheesecake or just enjoy a good baked cheesecake, this recipe is a must-try for any baking enthusiast. Serve it with fruit coulis or whipped cream for an extra touch of indulgence.
keywords: Baked Cheesecake Recipe With Roasted Cherries
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C. Invert the base of a 20cm springform round cake tin so that the flat side is facing upwards. Lightly grease the tin and line the base and sides with baking parchment, then wrap foil around the whole sides of the tin. Find a deep roasting tin that fits the cake tin in easily.

Melt the butter for the biscuit base then crush the biscuits into fine crumbs. The easiest way to do this is in a food processor. If not, use a Ziploc bag, some elbow grease and a rolling pin. Once crushed, mix with the melted butter. Tip into the tin and pat into an even base layer, then put into the fridge to chill while you make the filling.

For the filling, whisk together the sugar, flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the soft cheese, vanilla and lemon juice and whisk until smooth – you don’t want any lumps. Add the egg yolks one at a time, whisking in between each addition. Then finally, whisk in the soured cream.

Boil the kettle. Pour the cheesecake filling on top of the biscuit base, then transfer the unbaked cheesecake to the roasting tin. Pour the boiling water into the roasting tin so that it comes up at least halfway up the sides of the cake tin.

Carefully transfer to the centre of the oven and bake for 1 hr-1 hr 10 mins until the cheesecake is set around the edges and has the slightest jiggle in the centre. Once baked, leave to cool in the water bath for around 2 hrs, then put into the fridge to chill for at least 3 hrs, or preferably overnight.

For the roasted cherries, heat the oven to 220°C. De-stone and halve the cherries, then transfer them to a roasting tray with the caster sugar and lemon juice. Roast for 5-8 mins until the cherries are beginning to collapse and char in places and have released their own banging syrup. Leave to cool.
Unmould the cheesecake, then cut into fat slices and serve with the roasted cherries. Unreal.

name: Baked Chicken & Leek Orzo
description: Creamy, cheesy baked orzo with golden chicken and melty leeks. A warm hug of a dish, and did we mention it freezes like a dream?
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsHeat the oven to 180°C.
Finely slice the leeks and garlic. Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized chunks.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the chicken, season well with salt and black pepper, and fry for 5–6 mins until golden on the outside. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Add the leeks and garlic to the same pan and fry for 8–10 mins until soft and golden. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 min, stirring constantly.

Tip the orzo into a deep roasting tin or ovenproof casserole dish. Add in the cooked chicken and leek mixture, pour over the stock and stir well to combine. Cover tightly with a lid or foil and bake for 25 mins.
Remove from the oven, stir through the double cream and most of the parmesan. Scatter the rest of the cheese on top, then return to the oven uncovered for 10 mins until golden and bubbling.
Leave to cool for 5 mins before serving. Or, if freezing, divide into containers once cool, cover and freeze for another day.

name: Baked Chicken Legs with Leeks & Butter Beans
description: This braised chicken leg stew is a really comforting and delicious one-pot wonder.
keywords: Chicken & Butter Beans with Leek Gremolata
instructions: Season the chicken all over with salt. Place a shallow, heavy bottom casserole dish over a medium high heat, add a generous drizzle of olive oil and brown off the chicken legs for 6 or 7 mins until golden on all sides. Remove the chicken and set aside, leaving the oil and chicken fat in the pan.

Wash the leeks and remove the root and the tough outer layers. Finely slice the leeks, separating the darker greens from the whites/lighter greens. Set aside the darker greens for later. Peel the garlic.

Set the casserole dish over a medium heat and add the finely sliced leek whites/light greens and garlic cloves with a big pinch of salt. Cook for about 5 mins until soft and fragrant. Add the paprika and rosemary sprigs and cook for another minute then pour in the wine and leave it to reduce by half.

Tip in the tinned tomatoes and a very generous pinch of salt, then return the chicken to the pan. Bring the tomatoes to a simmer, place a lid on and reduce the heat to low and cook gently for 45 mins.

Meanwhile, make the gremolata. Trim and discard the first inch or so from the reserved dark green leek tops then finely mince the rest and add to a small bowl. Peel a couple of strips of lemon zest (if there’s a lot of pith on the back, carefully use the tip of a knife to remove it). Finely dice the lemon peel and add to the minced leeks along with the chopped almonds and a pinch of salt. Mix to combine and set aside.
When the cooking time is up for the tomatoes, add the drained butter beans and spinach, replace the lid and cook for another 5 mins until the spinach has wilted, then give everything a gentle stir.
Plate up, top with the gremolata and finish with a big squeeze of lemon juice.

name: Baked Chicken Legs with Mustardy Lentils
description: A classic dish that never gets old. Crispy chicken legs slow-roasted in the oven with chicken stock and creamy mustard lentils. You need this one in your repertoire.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken legs, skin side down, and cook for 5-10 mins on each side until nicely browned. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery stick (this is your soffritto). Get the soffritto in the chicken pan along with the bacon lardons. Cook for about 10-15 mins until softened then deglaze with the wine.
Add the lentils, chicken stock, fresh thyme and bay leaf to the pan and give it a stir then top with the chicken legs. Cover and bake with the lid on for 50 mins.
Remove the chicken to a plate. Stir the spinach, mustard, crème fraîche and black pepper through the lentils.
To serve, divide the lentils between plates and top with the chicken legs. Serve with a simple side salad and a vinaigrette dressing, if you like.

name: Baked Chicken, Peperonata & Parmesan Mash
description: Simple, colourful and hearty with a nice mix of flavours and textures. The chicken and peperonata all happens in one tray and goes on a bed of creamy parm mash.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°c.
Core and slice the peppers into roughly 1cm thick strips. Add to a large baking dish along with 4 tbsp of olive oil, the garlic (unpeeled) and a big pinch of salt.
Toss well and roast for about 20 mins. Remove and stir in the tomatoes, olives and half of the vinegar.
Rub the chicken all over with a drizzle of olive oil and a generous pinch of salt, then arrange on top of the peppers and tomatoes.
Return to the oven and roast for another 25 mins until the chicken is cooked through and the peppers are tomatoes are soft and saucy.
While the chicken cooks, make the mash. Peel and quarter the potatoes and add to a large pan. Cover with water and bring to the boil.
Simmer for about 15 mins until the potatoes are soft through. Drain and allow to steam dry for a couple of minutes.
Grate in the parmesan, cube and add the butter, a teaspoon of salt and black pepper. Mash well until mostly smooth, then add the milk and mix vigorously. Taste and add salt and pepper in needed.
Remove the tray from the oven. Set the chicken to one side to rest for a few mins, meanwhile add the basil and remaining vinegar to the peppers and mix well.
Plate up the mash, top with a spoon of the peperonata and then the chicken. Drizzle over some of the roasting juices from the pan and enjoy.

name: Baked Cumin Cod With Labneh Chickpeas
description: We love cumin, we love cod, and we certainly love labneh chickpeas. Have a go at this lovely cod dish.
instructions: Line a sieve with a piece of kitchen paper or J cloth and set over a bowl. Tip in the yoghurt and chill for 2 hrs.

When ready to eat, heat the oven to 180°C. Season the cod with salt and pepper. Add to a bowl with the cumin and grate in the garlic. Toss with a little olive oil and add to a lined tray. Slide into the oven for 8-10 mins or until just cooked.
Tip the chickpeas, liquid and all, into a pan and set over a medium heat. Once warm, drain and toss with the hung yoghurt.
Finely dice the red onion and cover with lemon juice. Finely dice the cucumber and herbs and get those into the bowl, too. Add a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the warm labneh chickpeas onto a plate, top with a cod fillet and finish with the cucumber salsa and a wedge of lemon.

name: Baked Double Cheese Gnocchi
description: The ultimate winter warmer, fluffy potato gnocchi baked in a rich double cheese sauce, perfect.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Place a large saucepan over a medium heat, add the butter and when it begins to foam, add the flour and whisk well. Cook for about a minute until lightly golden.
Now slowly pour in the milk, whisking constantly until smooth. Finely chop and add the sage and grate in the parmesan and gruyere.
Mix until the cheese has melted and then add the nutmeg and grind in a generous amount of black pepper. Taste and add salt as needed.
Now, if you’re using the soft fresh gnocchi from the fridge in the supermarket you can go ahead and add it straight into the creamy sauce. If using dried, cook it first, drain and add.
Give it all a good stir and then pour into a baking dish and bake in the oven for about 20 mins until bubbling and golden brown.
Serve hot, great with a little green salad on the side.

name: Baked Egg Stuffed Croissants
description: Baked eggs as you’ve never seen them before. Stuffed inside insanely delicious Pret All-Butter Croissants with spicy harissa tomatoes.
instructions: Cook your croissants according to packet instructions.
Slice your onion and grate your garlic. Finely chop your parsley.
Heat a little oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Tip your red onion into the pan and fry for 10 mins until it has gone totally soft and is starting to caramelise.

Add your grated garlic, cumin and cinnamon, then cook out for 2 mins. Throw in your tbsp of harissa paste and then tip your cans of tomatoes into the pan. Break them up with the back of your spoon. Simmer for 10 mins until they're getting nice and thick and jammy.
Hollow out your croissants, reserving the middle. Cut the middle parts into rough cubes.
Heat your oven to 190°C.
Drizzle the cubes with oil, dried oregano and salt. Bake in the oven for 10 mins.

Fill your hollowed out croissants with the tomato mix. Make a well in the middle and crack in an egg. Bake for 10-15 mins and keep an eye on them - they're ready when your whites are just set and your yolks still gooey.
Sprinkle your croissants with your chopped parsley and a crumbling of feta. Serve up with your croissant croutons.

name: Baked Lemon Custard Brûlée
description: Caramel and lemon is an underrated combination – the tang of the ultra-smooth custard plays so well with the bitterness of the caramel. The custard can be made in advance and brûlée’d when you’re ready to serve.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 120°C fan. Arrange the ramekins in a large baking dish with high sides for the water bath.
Heat together the lemon peels, double cream and half the sugar until simmering. Remove from the heat and leave for 30 minutes to infuse.

Whisk together the eggs and the remaining sugar very well, followed by the infused double cream and the lemon juice. Pass through a fine sieve. Use a spoon to remove any bubbles or foam from the top of the mixture. This can be a painstaking process but it’s important!
Divide the lemon custard among the ramekins, about 150g per ramekin. Boil the kettle, then pour the boiling water carefully into the baking dish until it reaches halfway up the sides of the ramekins.

Bake until there is around 2–3cm of good wobble in the centre of your custards. You don’t want to overbake them as this leads to potential cracks later down the line, so just watch out for that. I start checking after 20 mins and then every 5–10 mins after that. Remember it’s better to underbake than overbake in this case!
Remove from the oven and carefully transfer each ramekin onto a cooling rack. Allow to cool for 1 hour before transferring to the fridge for at least 2 hours or overnight.

Just before serving, sprinkle the top of the custard with a thin, even layer of caster or demerara sugar. Caramelise the sugar using a blow torch. You can do several layers if you prefer a thicker crust.

Allow the caramelised crust to cool and harden for 5 mins before serving. If you don’t have a blow torch, preheat the grill to high, then place the custard dishes on a baking sheet and grill for 1–2 mins until the sugar caramelises and turns golden brown. Cool and harden as above.

name: Baked Paprika Cod With Peas & Spicy Chorizo Dressing
description: The mild, comforting flavour of cod is the perfect vessel for a spicy chorizo dressing in this fancy-ish weeknight dinner.
keywords: Baked Paprika Cod With Peas & Spicy Chorizo Dressing
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Pat the cod fillets dry with a bit of kitchen paper and pop them onto a tray lined with parchment. Sprinkle them with salt and the smoked paprika. Grate over half of the garlic cloves and add a good splash of olive oil. Roll the fish around in the spices and garlic. Set aside.
Pour boiling water from the kettle over the pea. Finely dice the remaining garlic cloves and the shallots. Cut the chorizo into 1cm cubes. Now slide the cod into the oven for 10-11 mins.

While the cod is cooking, finish the garnish. Preheat a small frying pan over a medium heat. Tip in the chorizo and cook for 5-6 mins until rendered and crispy. Add the diced shallots and half the diced garlic and cook for 2 mins. Add the sherry vinegar and defrosted peas. Finely cut the chives and add half to the dressing.
Mix the yoghurt with the remaining diced garlic, the zest from the lemon and some salt. Cut the lemon into wedges for later.
Heat the grains according to the package instructions. Pull the cooked fish out of the oven.
Divide the grains between warm bowls. Top with a piece of cod, some garlic yoghurt and dress with lashings of the spicy chorizo and pea dressing. Finish with chives and a lemon wedge.

name: Baked Pesto Penne
description: This easy baked pesto pasta uses Gluten Free Penne for a perfect weeknight dinner. On the table in under half an hour.
instructions: Boil the pasta in plenty of salted water until slightly more al dente than you would normally have.
Meanwhile, blitz the almonds in a food processor until they resemble breadcrumbs. Then add the basil, a pinch of salt and a big glug of olive oil and blitz again.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium heat, then add the flour and cook until golden. Pour in the milk bit by bit, stirring all the while.
Once all of the milk has been added, grate in 150g of the parmesan cheese, stir until melted and then stir in the pesto too.
Drain the cooked pasta into a large bowl and pour in the pesto béchamel mix. Stir well until the pasta is creamy and well coated.
Pour into an oven dish and sprinkle over the breadcrumbs, grate over the remaining parmesan and break up the mozzarella and dot around the top.
Bake in the oven at 180°C for 15 mins until golden.

name: Baked Potato Gnocchi With Sage Brown Butter & Lemon
description: Making homemade gnocchi using a baked potato is dead easy. Here, we've teamed that gnocchi up with a drinkable sage brown butter and lemon sauce.
keywords: Baked Potato Gnocchi With Sage Brown Butter & Lemon
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Rub the potato with a little olive and salt and pop into the oven for 75-90 mins or until very tender. Pull out the oven and let it cool enough to handle. Slice in half and scoop out the flesh. Mash using a ricer or with a fork in a bowl, be as thorough as you can!

Tip the mash out onto a clean surface and spread out a little. Sprinkle over the flour and season with a big pinch of salt. Start rubbing the flour through the potato with the tips of your fingers as if you’re making pastry. Once combined, add the egg yolk (you can freeze your egg whites for meringue) and briefly knead the mixture into a homogenous dough. Let rest for 15 mins.

Divide the dough in half, dust the surface with flour and roll each half of the dough out into a long sausage shape about 2cm thick. Cut the ropes into little pillows approximately 4 cm long and set aside.
Bring a medium pot of water to a boil and season with salt. Set a medium frying pan over a medium heat.

Drop the gnocchi into the water and cook for 2-3 mins until they float to the surface. Meanwhile, add a couple of glugs of oil to the frying pan. Transfer the gnocchi to the hot pan and cook for 1-2 mins on each side until golden brown and caramelised.

Now drop the butter into the frying pan and allow to foam and sizzle. Chuck in the sage leaves and let them crackle and fry for 30 seconds. Toss to coat the gnocchi and finish with big squeeze of lemon and Parmesan.
Tip onto a plate and get stuck in.

name: Baked Prawn Saganaki Orzo
description: Sweet prawns and salty feta are the stars of this saganaki-inspired orzo recipe. A summer comfort classic.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic.

Get a large, shallow casserole dish over a medium heat with lots of olive oil, then add the onion. Cook for 10 mins, or until softened. Add the garlic, chilli flakes and cinnamon, then cook for 1 min. Tip in the chopped tomatoes, oregano, water and a big pinch of salt. Bring to the boil. Once the pan is simmering, add the orzo and give everything a stir. Transfer the dish to the oven and cook for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, remove the middle section of shell from the prawns, leaving the heads and tails intact. Devein each one by cutting an incision along the back and removing the trail.

After the cooking time is complete, remove the dish from the oven and give everything a good stir. Add the prawns and mix again. Crumble the feta over the surface, add a drizzle of olive oil, then bake for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, pick the dill leaves.
To serve, remove the dish from the oven and sprinkle chilli flakes and dill on top. Zest over the lemon, then serve with lemon wedges on the side.

name: Baked Sausage Cassoulet
description: A delicious twist on the classic French dish. Traditionally made with salted pork and confit duck legs, our version uses garlicky Toulouse sausages (but any will do) and salty bacon lardons for a rich, savoury flavour. It's perfect for a cosy evening when you fancy a bowl of comfort.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Put a large, deep roasting tin into the oven to heat for 5 mins. Chuck the sausages and lardons into the tin, pour in 1 tbsp oil and roast for 10 mins, tossing halfway until starting to brown.

Turn the heat down to 180°C. Peel and finely chop the onion, carrots and celery. Scrape into the roasting tin with the garlic cloves in their skins, three-quarters of the thyme sprigs and the bay leaves. Drizzle with 1 tbsp oil, season with salt and pepper and roast in the oven for 10 mins.

Pour in the white wine, both tins of beans and their liquid and the can of chopped tomatoes. Put back into the oven for 20 mins until reduced and thickened slightly. Remove from the oven, squeeze out the flesh from the roasted garlic skins and pop them back in the sauce.
Meanwhile, combine the mozzarella and breadcrumbs in a bowl. Strip the remaining thyme leaves from their stalks and add them to the bowl, too.
Scatter the cheesy breadcrumbs over the top of the dish, drizzle with a little oil and bake for a final 15 mins until golden and bubbling.
Serve with a baguette for scooping-up and a bright, fresh green salad to compliment.

name: Baked Spinach and Ricotta Tortelloni
description: You could almost think of this as a super easy weeknight lasagna. Start to finish in just over half an hour, and a guaranteed crowd pleaser.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C/400°F.
Gently crush your two cloves of garlic, then peel them.
Start by making a simple tomato sauce. In a saucepan, warm 3 tbsp of olive oil over a medium heat and add your garlic.
After a few minutes they should be lightly golden brown. Strip the leaves from the basil and add to the oil (be careful, it might spit!) along with the chilli flakes.
Stir and cook for 1 min, then add the tomato passata and 1 tsp salt. Leave to simmer for about 15 mins.
Set a large pan of salted water on to boil. Once boiling, add the tortelloni and cook for just 1 min. Drain and set aside.
Drain and dice up the mozzarella into roughly 1cm cubes.
After 15 mins, once the sauce has reduced and thickened a little, taste it for seasoning - it might need more salt.
Now, mix the tortellini into the sauce along with two-thirds of the diced mozzarella. Pour the mixture into an ovenproof dish. Top with the remaining mozzarella and a generous sprinkling of parmesan.
Bake in the oven for 15 mins until the cheese is golden brown and bubbling. Let it rest for 5 mins before serving. Enjoy!

name: Baked Sweet Potato With Mushrooms & Soy-Lime Tahini Drizzle
description: A tangy soy-lime drizzle is the perfect topping for a baked sweet potato. That's a fact.
keywords: Baked Sweet Potato With Mushrooms & Soy-Lime Tahini Drizzle
Baked Sweet Potato With Mushrooms & Soy-Lime Tahini Drizzle  recipe
ingredients: Black And White Sesame Seed (to serve)
instructions: To make this a speedy recipe, you can cook the sweet potatoes in the microwave. Wash the sweet potatoes and poke them all over with a fork. Wrap the potatoes in wet kitchen paper and place in a microwave-safe bowl or plate. Microwave the sweet potatoes for 10-12 mins, until a knife pierces through very easily. Keep cooking and checking at 5 min intervals.

Meanwhile, make the filling. Tear or cut the mushrooms into bite-sized pieces. Add a little drizzle of olive oil to a large frying pan, then add the mushrooms and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, over a medium heat for about 8 mins.
Drain the chickpeas and add these to the pan, along with the spinach. Add a drizzle of soy sauce if you like and cook for 5 mins until the spinach has wilted and the mushrooms are caramelised.
To make the soy tahini drizzle, juice the lime into a small bowl. Add the remaining ingredients and whisk together until smooth.

To serve, slice the sweet potatoes open and mash them down slightly with a fork. Season with salt and pepper before loading with the mushroom chickpea filling. Drizzle over plenty of tahini sauce and top with your chosen toppings.

name: Baked Sweet Potato with Lamb Bolognese
description: A simple sweet potato topped with a rich and warming lamb bolognese.
keywords: Baked Sweet Potato with Lamb Bolognese
Baked Sweet Potato with Lamb Bolognese recipe
instructions: Peel the onions and lob them into a food processor along with the carrot, celery, garlic and rosemary. Whizz into a fine chop and set aside.

Preheat a large dutch oven or cast iron over a medium-high heat. Add a few glugs of olive oil and start to brown off the lamb mince. Working in batches, crumble in some mince, add a pinch of salt and cook, stirring very occasionally for 6-7 mins or until super crispy. Whip it out and repeat with the remaining lamb mince.

Once the lamb is browned, leave the lamb fat and olive oil behind and tip in the veggies. Add a pinch of salt and cook for 7-8 mins. Add the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes and stock. Add the lamb mince back to the pan, bring to a boil, and then reduce the heat to low. Cook for 1-2 hours, stirring occasionally.
When the lamb has had an hour or so, preheat the oven to 200°C. Rub the sweet potatoes with oil and salt, prick with a fork and slide into the oven for the last hour of the lamb’s cooking time.
When the lamb has finished cooking, season with salt and pepper.
Split open the baked sweet potatoes and fill with ragù, finish with crumbled feta and mint leaves.

name: Baked Sweet Potato with Spicy Pork Ragù
description: Another banging recipe made using leftovers from our Spicy Pork Ragù. If you're a sweet potato fan then you're in for a treat.
keywords: baked sweet potato with spicy ragu
instructions: Make the Spicy Pork Ragú batch recipe.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Rub your sweet potatoes with oil and salt and slide into the oven for 60 mins or until baked and tender all the way through. You can also pop them in the microwave for 5-6 minutes to give them a head start before finishing in the oven for 15 mins with the same oil and salt.
Warm up the ragù and finely chop the chillies and coriander.
Split open the sweet potatoes and stuff with ragu. Top with chillies and coriander. Serve with half a lime for squeezing.

name: Baked Tuna Egg Mayo on Japanese Rice with Teriyaki Sauce
description: Tuna mayo but make it baked, golden and bubbling. Layered over sticky Japanese rice and finished with a drizzle of glossy teriyaki sauce. So wrong, it’s right.
keywords: Baked Tuna Egg Mayo on Japanese Rice with Teriyaki Sauce
Baked Tuna Egg Mayo on Japanese Rice with Teriyaki Sauce recipe
instructions: Boil the eggs. Bring a saucepan of water to a boil. Carefully lower in the eggs and cook for 6 mins. While they cook, prep a bowl of cold water. Once done, transfer the eggs to the cold water and let them sit for 5 mins. Peel and cut into quarters.

Prep the tuna mix. Thinly slice the spring onion. Finely mince the brown onion. Drain the tuna and add to a mixing bowl along with the spring onion, brown onion, Japanese mayo, sriracha, soy sauce, and black pepper. Mix gently to combine, keeping some tuna in chunks.
Fold the egg quarters into the tuna mixture gently to avoid breaking them up too much.
Spoon the cooked rice into a small-medium ovenproof dish and spread evenly. Top with the tuna egg mayo mix and smooth out.
Turn your grill to high. Place the dish on the middle shelf and cook for 10 mins, or until golden, slightly crispy and bubbling on top.
Peel and grate the ginger. Add to a small pan with the soy sauce, mirin, sake (if using), and sugar. Stir to combine and bring to a boil. Let it bubble for 1 minute, then remove from the heat.
Remove the bake from the oven. Drizzle over the teriyaki sauce. Finely chop the chives and sprinkle on top along with the toasted sesame seeds. Serve hot.

name: Baklava Cheesecake Pots
description: An easy, baklava-inspired dessert that's perfect for your next dinner party. Prep them ahead of time for minimal faff.
instructions:
Take your cream cheese out of the fridge as it needs to be at room temperature.
Heat the oven to 180°C and get your pastry and cut into circles the same size as
your serving glasses. Then line a tray with greaseproof paper, dust with half of
the icing sugar and add the pastry, pricking them with a fork. Dust with the
remaining icing sugar and cover with greaseproof paper, then add a tray on top
to prevent the pastry from rising. Slide into the oven and bake for 25 mins.
Remove from the oven and set aside to cool­.

Chop your chocolate into small pieces and set up a ban marie, alternatively you
can melt in the microwave in 30 second bursts, then set aside to cool. In a large
bowl mix the cream cheese with a wooden spoon, then in another bowl lightly
whip the double cream until thickened but not in stiff peaks.

When the
chocolate has been cooling for 10-15 mins, pour into the cream cheese and mix
to combine, then fold in the whipped cream in 2 batches. Zest in the peel of an
orange, then squeeze in the juice of half. Add the vanilla extract and a squeeze of
