lemon and fold to combine. Fill into glasses and set aside in the fridge for at
least half an hour­

Tip the pistachios onto a tray and slide into the oven for 10 minutes. Heat the
honey and cinnamon in a saucepan and set aside to cool slightly. Crumble the
pastry over the cheesecake bases and add the pistachios. Drizzle over the
Cinnamon honey and get stuck in.

name: Balsamic & Fennel Italian Eggs
description: These eggs are meal-prep friendly and bursting with garlicky flavour and balanced by a mellow heat and a sharp hit of balsamic. Toasting the fennel seeds in olive oil brings a game-changing depth.
instructions: Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Gently lower in the eggs and boil for 6 mins. Cool in iced water and peel once chilled.
Toast the fennel seeds in a dry pan, then grind in a pestle and mortar. Add the garlic and smash together.
Finely chop the chives, slice the chilli and zest the lemon.
In a bowl mix together the lemon zest, red chilli, chives, crushed fennel and garlic, oregano, balsamic vinegar, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Place the peeled eggs in a clean jar or container. Pour over the marinade and top up with a little extra olive oil to fully cover.
Chill for at least 4 hrs, ideally overnight. The oil will separate, totally normal. You’ll end up with half the egg deeply brown and vinegared. Really delicious.
Serve halved with a spoonful of marinade, crusty bread and something salty.

name: Balsamic Carrots With Orange Tahini Yogurt
description: Elevate your roasted carrots with a balsamic glaze and crispy lentils, on a whipped orange and tahini.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200C.

Cook the lentils for 25-30 mins. 
Lay the cooked lentils on a large baking tray and sprinkle a pinch of cumin, salt and pepper and a drizzle of olive oil over them. Give them a mix to make sure they are evenly coated and bake for 25 mins, tossing halfway. They should be very crispy and crunchy.
If using large carrots, slice them lengthways and then again to create large sticks.
Lay the carrots on a large lined baking tray. Toss them with a good drizzle of olive oil and salt and pepper. Cook for 20 mins.

Mix together the balsamic vinegar, 1 tbsp of olive oil and maple syrup. After the carrots have been roasting for 20 mins, drizzle this mixture over the carrots and mix well. Add a few thyme sprigs over the top and return to the oven for another 15-20 mins, until the carrots are tender and caramelised.
Meanwhile, mix the tahini and yoghurt with the juice of half of the orange and a pinch of cumin. Season with salt and taste. Add more orange juice if you prefer more acidity.
While the carrots are cooking, toast the pecans or your chosen nuts. Lay them on a small baking tray and toast for 8 mins, or until fragrant and toasted.
To serve, lay the whipped yogurt on a large plate. Pile up the lentils, then carrots, pecans and fresh herbs. Finish with plenty of orange zest.

name: Balsamic Glazed Plant-Based Meatballs
description: Vegan meatballs. So easy to make. The lemon zest works so nicely to lift the dish. Freshened with basil. You'll be making them again and again.
instructions: Break off small pieces of your mince until you have around 18 pieces. Roll them up into small balls. Sprinkle a generous amount of salt and pepper over the top. Move them around with your hands to make sure each ball is coated.
Get your pasta on.
Drizzle some olive oil into a pan and add your meatless meatballs. Stir them around until they begin to brown.
Chop up the garlic cloves and basil.
Add the garlic to the pan along with the chilli flakes. After 30 seconds, add the balsamic glaze and mix everything together.
Pour the passata into the pan and grate the zest of 1 lemon over the top. Add your chopped basil to the sauce and give everything a good stir.
Once your pasta is cooked, take it out of the saucepan and mix it into the tomato sauce and stir everything together. Serve it up and tuck into this delicious meat-free dish.

name: Balsamic Tomato Macaroni with Olive Pangrattato
description: This dish is unbelievably tasty and couldn't be simpler to make. The tomatoes, shallots and garlic melt together in olive oil to make the creamy, rich sauce. The olive pangrattato makes it extra special.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.

Peel the shallots and garlic, cut the shallots into eights and leave the garlic whole. Add these to a small casserole dish or a roasting tin – a dish into which everything will fit snugly so that not too much liquid escapes.

Add the tomatoes, olive oil and a sprinkle of salt, and shake to coat. Cover with a lid (or cover tightly with foil) and bake for 40 mins, until everything is very soft. The garlic should melt when pushed to with a fork, and the shallots should be completely softened. Everything should be swimming in a pool of garlicky tomato juice.

Meanwhile, make the pangrattato. Mince the garlic and finely chop the olives. Whizz the bread into breadcrumbs in a food processor, then tip into a bowl. Add the minced garlic and olive oil, and crumble together with your fingers. Set aside.

Heat a large, dry frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the chopped olives and fry for 3-4 mins, stirring often, until they start to get crispy. Add the breadcrumbs and cook for 3-4 mins until golden and fragrant. Taste before you season as the olives can be salty. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Cook your pasta in a large saucepan of salted boiling water until al dente (1 minute less than the packet instructions). Drain and set aside, drizzling with a little olive oil to prevent from sticking.
When the tomatoes are ready, remove about a third of them and set aside. Blend the remaining, juice and all, with a stick blender or in a stand blender, until smooth or almost smooth.
Stir the cooked pasta into the sauce. Add the balsamic vinegar and season well with salt and pepper. To serve, ladle the pasta into bowls and top with the olive pangrattato.

name: Balsamic Veggies & Hummus Bowls
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A simple veggie-packed hummus bowl recipe that's perfect for a hearty lunch or light and breezy dinner.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Trim and chop the aubergine into 2cm chunks. Peel and wedge the onion. Add both onto a baking tray, drizzle with the balsamic vinegar and olive oil. Toss together and roast for 20-25 mins.

Meanwhile, pick the basil leaves, discarding the stems, and roughy chop the peppers into bite-size chunks. Using a peeler, peel shavings of Parmesan. Add all the dressing ingredients together and whisk or shake in a jar to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Share the dip between bowls, toss the basil and Parm through the veggies and finish with a drizzle of dressing. Enjoy with ciabatta.

name: Balsamic-Glazed Meatballs
description: These pork meatballs are a homage to my dad's old Italian restaurant, Cibo. They're easy to make, and the glaze brings the perfect sweetness to the dish. Ben x
instructions: Finely slice your garlic.
Squeeze the meat out of sausages and make small balls. Add to a frying pan on a medium heat.
Once the meatballs start to brown, add the chilli flakes and the garlic. Before the garlic starts browning, add the balsamic vinegar and allow it to reduce.
As it starts to caramelise, add your tomatoes and leave the sauce to simmer.
Start cooking the pasta, following the instructions on the packet.
Once the sauce is reduced, season with salt and pepper, tear in some basil and add a splash of pasta water.

At this point, drain your pasta and add it to the saucepan. Toss everything together, and then serve on warm plates, with mozzarella torn over the top. Finish with parmesan, more basil and pepper. Enjoy.

name: Banana Bread
description: The secret to the perfect banana bread? Using 4 whole over-ripe bananas. That, plus toasting the slices in a pan and topping them with a big pat of butter.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160C/140C fan. Line a 2lb loaf tin.
Melt the butter in the microwave or in a pan over a low heat, then set aside to cool to room temp.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk the melted butter with the sugar, vanilla, eggs, and yogurt.

Mix the self-raising flour with the bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt. Tip into the wet mix. Mash the bananas, leaving a few chunkier bits and then stir into the cake mix. Tip into the tin and bake for 1 hour, until a skewer comes out clean when it slides in. If it still looks wet, bake for 10 mins further.
Either serve the slices, warm, with a pat of cold butter OR…

To serve, heat a large frying pan over a medium high heat, slice the banana bread into chunky slices. Lie a square of baking paper on each side of the slice and then lie in the frying pan, toast until golden, then flip over and repeat on the other side- move to a plate and slide away the paper. Finish with a pat of cold butter that will melt when it hits the surface.

name: Banana Ice Cream
description:
Trust us when we say that this healthy ‘ice cream’ is going to blow your mind – and that’s not just because it’s
made by blitzing up frozen bananas.
instructions: The day before you want to eat this, peel and slice the bananas. Put into an airtight container or freezer bag and pop into the freezer until frozen solid.
When ready to eat, preheat the oven to 160°C.
Tip the hazelnuts onto a baking tray. Toast in the oven for 6–8 mins until golden, then leave to cool slightly.

Sauce time. Once the hazelnuts are cooled, tip most of them into a food processor. Blitz until very finely chopped and beginning to clump together – almost at a nut butter stage. Snap the chocolate into a heatproof bowl and melt, either in the microwave in 30-sec bursts or over a pan of barely simmering water. Once melted, scrape into the processor. Add the maple syrup, 3 tbsp of water and a big pinch of sea salt. Blitz again to a chocolate sauce; if you prefer it looser, stir in a splash more water. Scrape into a bowl.
Clean the food processor, then tip in the frozen bananas. Blitz until you the texture of ice cream – trust us, be patient, this really works. If your processor is small, do this in two batches.
Roughly chop the remaining hazelnuts.
Divide the banana ‘ice cream’ between four bowls. Spoon over the chocolate sauce and served topped with the chopped hazelnuts.

name: Banana Pancakes
description: Minimal ingredients. Maximum flavour. A staple pancake topping — bananas. These Banana Pancakes take just minutes to prepare, and the pay off is outrageous.
instructions: Mash up the bananas in the bowl and add in the eggs and flour. Whisk until combined, don't worry if it's not totally smooth.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat, brush over some vegetable oil, and a ladle of pancake batter.
Cook on a low/medium heat for 3 mins on either side.
Serve on a plate with your favourite toppings, our favourite is maple syrup and butter.

name: Bangers & Mash Traybake
description: This dish isn't as chaotic as it sounds. We've taken everything you love about bangers and mash and turned into a summery traybake. The gravy mayo? Genius.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Tip the potatoes into a large pan of cold salted water, bring to the boil and cook for 10-15 mins until totally soft. Drain and set aside to steam. Meanwhile, slice the courgettes into 2cm rounds.

Tip the potatoes onto your largest baking sheet ​​– you may have to spread them across two trays. Use the bottom of a glass or the back of a spatula to gently break the potatoes a little. Add the sausages and courgette slices to the trays, drizzle everything with a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 30-40 mins, tossing gently halfway, until the potatoes are crispy and the sausages are golden and cooked through.
For the gravy mayo, put the gravy granules in a small bowl and add 1 tbsp boiling water to create a paste.

Tip the egg yolk into another bowl and add the mustard and a squeeze of lemon juice. Whisk together, then add a small splash of the vegetable oil. Whisk well, then add the rest of the vegetable oil very slowly, whisking with each edition until it emulsifies to form a thick mayo. Whisk in the gravy paste, taste and season well, adding a little more lemon juice if necessary.

Tip the peas into a bowl and cover in boiling water. Drain immediately and rinse in cold water, then return to the bowl. Use a potato masher to roughly crush the peas – you can also do this in a mini chopper.
Roughly chop the mint and add most of it to the peas. Add the juice of the lemon half and 2 tbsp olive oil.

Tip the sausages, potatoes and courgettes onto a platter. Scatter with the herby peas, drizzle over a little of the gravy mayo and finish with the reserved herbs and a crack of black pepper. Serve the remaining gravy mayo on the side.

name: Banoffee Overnight Oats
description: Creamy, caramelly oats layered with bananas & a lush peanut-date sauce. Tastes like dessert, but it’s breakfast.
instructions: First soak the dates in boiling water for 30 mins, then drain them.
Blend the dates with the oat milk, vanilla, maple syrup, peanut butter and a pinch of salt until smooth. Add a splash of water if needed to loosen the mix.
Combine the oats, flax seeds, Greek yoghurt, and oat milk in a bowl. Mix well, then cover and set aside to soak.
Slice the bananas.

Grab some glasses or jars and start layering up. Spoon a little of the oat mixture into the bottom of your glasses, followed by a spoonful of the toffee sauce and a few banana slices. Repeat the layers in each glass until everything is used up. 
Top each with a dollop of Greek yoghurt (if using) and a scattering of granola. Pop in the fridge overnight, ready for tomorrow's breakfast.

name: Banoffee Pie
description: You can’t beat a classic banoffee pie recipe. Make sure to stir the condensed milk mixture constantly when making the caramel layer so that it doesn’t catch whilst cooking. This is a delicious dessert that can be eaten all year round, especially in summer.
instructions: Get a medium saucepan over a low-medium heat, tip in two-thirds of the butter and let it melt. Get out a 20cm springform cake tin and flip the base upside down so that the flat side is facing up in the tin (this will help you get the pie out more easily later).

Use a food processor to blitz the digestive biscuits (or put in a ziplock bag and crush with a rolling pin) until they resemble fine breadcrumbs then tip them into the melted butter and stir together until all the crumbs are coated.

Scrape the buttery biscuit crumbs into the cake tin and use your fingers to evenly push them across the base and up the sides of the tin to create your pie shell. You might like to use the bottom of a glass or mug to help push down and create a compact, even crust. Transfer to the fridge to chill for at least 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, make your caramel. Wipe out the pan you’ve just used then measure in the remaining butter and the brown sugar. Put over a low heat and leave to melt, stirring occasionally until combined. Pour in the condensed milk then turn up the heat to medium. Stirring constantly, bring to the boil then cook for 2-3 minutes until everything is smooth and combined. You don’t want to boil for much longer than 3 minutes otherwise it will start to become much thicker and toffee-like. You’ll need to keep stirring the whole time to make sure the caramel doesn’t catch on the bottom –a silicone spatula works well for this!
Pour the hot caramel into the chilled biscuit base, sprinkle over some sea salt then return to the fridge for at least an 4-5 hours until set, or preferably overnight.
Once your caramel is set and you’re ready to assemble the rest of the pie, whisk the double cream with the vanilla extract until it’s just holding its shape. Slice the bananas into 1cm rounds.

Lay the sliced bananas on top of the set caramel then top with the cream and crumble over the flake, or grate over the chocolate. The banoffee pie is now ready to serve or will keep in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Banoffee Pie
description: Creamy, caramelly banoffee pudding with a shortcrust pastry base. A classic for a reason.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan. Grease a 23cm round tart tin with butter.

Use a rolling pin to roll out the pastry to 5mm thick, then use it to line your prepared tart tin and pop it in the fridge to chill for around 30 mins. Add a layer of baking paper and weigh it down with baking beans. Pop it on a baking tray then slide into the oven to bake for 15–20 mins until starting to turn golden.

Remove the tray from the oven and remove the baking beans and paper. Use a fork to prick the base of the pastry then return to the oven to bake for another 10 mins, or until browning and starting to crisp.

Make the egg wash by whisking together the yolk and milk in a mug. Remove the pastry from the oven and brush all over with a thin layer of egg wash then return to the oven to bake for another 2 mins. Remove from the oven and place the dish on a wire rack to cool completely.

Meanwhile, peel and slice the bananas into 1-2cm coins. In a mixing bowl, use an electric whisk to whip the double cream with the espresso powder and vanilla extract until thick and creamy with stiff peaks forming. You can do this by hand, but it will take longer.
Spread the dulce de leche into the cooled tart case, followed by the chopped bananas, the whipped cream and the pecan halves. Sprinkle with the ground cinnamon and serve immediately!

name: Bao Buns
description: Here's the insider info on how to make the fluffiest, softest bao buns in town. Make them solo or bring in the crew and make an afternoon of it.
instructions: Tip the yeast into a bowl and add 240ml warm water. Whisk well and set aside for 10 mins.
Tip the flour, baking powder and sugar into a large mixing bowl. Slowly add water mix and then oil. Add salt and mix together, then tip onto a clean surface and knead for 10 mins.
Add dough to a bowl and add a small layer of oil to top of dough – I like to use sesame oil but any oil will do. Cover with cling film.
Leave to prove for 40-60 mins or until the dough has doubled in size, then remove the dough on a well-floured table top and lightly knead till the dough is smooth
Get some scales and weigh out chunks of dough into 55g balls, shaping them into smooth balls (the smoother the better).
Place them on a tabletop or baking sheet a couple inches apart, cover lightly with cling film and let them prove for another 20-30 mins, until puffed up.
Take each ball and with a rolling pin roll them into an oval shape, trying to get them about 1cm thick, then brush lightly with oil, I use sesame.
Carefully fold in half and place inside your steamers. Repeat this process until they’re all done, put the steamer lid on and let them sit for another 30-40 mins.

Get a pan big enough to sit the steamers on and bring the temperature up to a rolling boil. Once the water has come up to temp, add the steamers on top and let them steam for 10-12 minutes until the buns are fluffy.

name: Barbecued Fish Burgers
description: Change it up with the BBQ fish burgers. Charred & smokey, on top of a toasted brioche bun. Whammy.
instructions: Defrost cod fillets.
Finely chop your cod and prawns into small chunks. Throw them into a bowl.
Add the finely sliced shallots, the zest of a lemon, a handful of chopped parsley and 1 grated clove of garlic. Season with salt, pepper and olive oil, and mix it all together.
Divide the fish mix into 4 patties. Place them on a board, cover with cling film and refrigerate for 1 hour. This will firm up the patties.
While the burgers are chilling, make your mayo.

Squeeze half a bottle of mayo into a bowl. Grate in a clove of garlic, squeeze in the juice of a lemon and add a handful of chopped coriander. Season with salt and pepper and mix it all together. Keep in the fridge until you serve.
Barbecue time. Fire up the BBQ, and when it is at a medium to high heat, place your patties on the grill. Grill for 7 minutes on the first side, and flip them as they begin to char.

After flipping, close the lid for 7 more minutes, which will make them nice and smoky. Timings may vary here based on the heat of the BBQ, so just keep checking them and remove them when they are cooked through.
Cut your brioche buns in half and toast them on the barbie.

Assemble time. Smother the bottom half of the bun in mayo. Place the burger on top, spoon on some more mayo, add any leftover parsley leaves and then top with the bun. Pick it up, take a bite and enjoy!

name: Barraquito
description: In need of a tasty morning pick-me-up? How about a morning pick-me-up that straps jetpacks to your feet? The Barraquito is an excellent coffee cocktail.
instructions: First, get your milk on the stove onto a low heat and whisk it for 30 secs using an electric whisk (if you have one) or manual whisk until its foamy and creamy.
Using the back of a spoon, you're going to want to really slowly pour in the following ingredients in this order: the condensed milk, Liquor 43, shot of espresso and then your foamed milk.
Dust a little cinnamon on top and then garnish with a small twist of lemon rind.
Push the lemon rind down and stir until all the layers are combined. Enjoy.

name: Basil Chicken Skewers with Mango Salad
description: A lovely summer BBQ recipe. Tender chicken skewers marinated in a few key ingredients served with a fresh mint mango salad that'll make your mouth water. Xien x
keywords: Basil chicken skewers with mango salad
instructions: Soak your skewers in water (this prevents them from burning).
Slice your chicken into rough 3cm chunks and add all the sauces, a glug of oil and chilli flakes. Grate in the garlic and add chopped basil. Season with salt and leave to marinate in the fridge.

Peel your mango and slice it into 1cm slices before slicing it once again into even thinner slices and adding to a big bowl. Halve your tomatoes and get them into the same bowl. Chop up your basil and mint and add them to your mango salad.
Add your garlic and peanuts to a pestle and mortar and bash them up. Mix fish sauce, palm sugar and lime juice together. Get this all into your salad, season with a pinch of salt and toss together.
Skewer assembly time – thread 5 chicken pieces onto each skewer.
On medium heat, grill the skewers on an oiled pan, brush with the reserving marinade and cook until golden and the juices run clear on each side (should take about 12 mins).
Serve the skewers with the mango salad and enjoy!

name: Basil Shortbread
description: We've given classic shortbread a makeover by adding fresh herbs to the biscuit dough. Buttery, crumbly, sweet and just a tiny bit savoury. Yes please.
instructions: Line two baking trays with baking parchment.  Ensure your butter is very cold. Cut the butter into cubes. Very finely chop the basil leaves.

Sift the flour, sugars, salt and basil together in a large bowl and mix to combine. Add the cold butter and use your fingertips and thumbs to rub the flour mix into the butter until it resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolk and vanilla and use your hands to gently bring the mixture together into a dough, being careful not to overwork it.

Using a rolling pin, roll the dough out on a floured surface to approximately 1cm thick. Use an 8cm cookie cutter (or 6cm if you prefer mini shortbreads) to cut the dough into circles. Place them on the prepared baking tray and refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours, but preferably overnight.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan.

Slide the tray into the oven and bake for approximately 12 mins, or until the edges are just starting to brown. Remove from the oven, cool on the tray for a couple of mins, then transfer to a wire rack. Dust the tops with more sugar and leave to cool completely.

name: Basil Tortelloni
description: Plump tortelloni and an extremely simple sauce. Keep the tortelloni al dente for the best eating experience. A new mid-week staple.
instructions: Place a pot of water on to boil. Season with salt. Finely grate the parmesan.
Add the butter into a saucepan on medium heat, let it melt fully and cook, stirring, until it turns brown and smells nutty, 2-3 mins.

Meanwhile, place ⅓ of your basil leaves into a food processor with 50ml of olive oil. Pulse until a green oil appears, it should still be a little chunky, not completely smooth. Season well with salt and pepper.
Drop the tortelloni into the boiling water for 2 mins.

Once the pasta is cooked, remove the pan from the heat. Add the pasta to the buttery sauce along with the basil oil and a few ladles of the cooking water. Add the parmesan and half of the basil leaves and toss well until it coats the pasta. Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Tip onto your plates and garnish with the remaining fresh basil leaves, plus a little extra parmesan cheese.

name: Batch Prep Roasted Vegetables
description: Cook up a big batch of roasted vegetables and you'll never be far away from a quick and easy dinner. Perfect for a Sunday afternoon.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C. You will need multiple trays, and may have to do this in batches. Add all of the tomatoes into a large baking dish and drizzle with 4 tbsp olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper. Dice the aubergines into 2 cm pieces and add to the tray, drizzling with olive oil, salt and pepper.

Grab another tray, rub the sweet potatoes in olive oil, salt and pepper. Remove the tops of the garlic bulbs and wrap individually in tin foil. Add them to the sweet potato tray. Put everything in the oven, with the cherry tomatoes on the higher shelf.

Roast for 35-40 mins, then remove from the oven. Decant the cherry tomatoes, garlic and aubergine into separate air tight containers. Check how the sweet potatoes are getting on, they may need cooking for 20 mins longer!

name: Bean & Cheese Brekkie Quesadilla
description: Crispy, cheesy, beany heaven. These freezer-friendly quesadillas are ideal for when you want max comfort with zero faff. Make a big batch now and thank yourself later.
instructions: Finely dice the onion and finely grate the garlic.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the onion and cook for 6–7 mins until soft and translucent. Stir through the garlic and mixed herbs, then cook for about 30 seconds until the garlic smells mellow.
Add the beans – liquid and all – along with half the salsa. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 10–15 mins until it thickens slightly.
Use a masher to mash about half the beans in the pan. This helps the mix hold together. Season with salt and pepper, then let it cool slightly.

Lay 1 slice of cheese onto the tortillas, spoon the beans onto one half. Fold in half, stack the uncooked quesadillas on top of each other.
If making ahead, stack into a sandwich bag or box and freeze. 
If cooking straight away, toast the quesadillas in a dry frying pan over a medium heat until golden and the cheese is gooey.

If cooking from frozen, heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan over a low-medium heat. Add the frozen quesadillas, cover with a lid, and cook gently until defrosted. Remove the lid, turn up the heat slightly and cook until crisp and golden.
Serve with hot sauce and remaining salsa.

name: Bean & Lentil Salad with Whipped Sesame Tofu
description: A high-protein salad inspired by the dense bean salads you see everywhere right now, but this one comes with a whipped sesame tofu that's so good you'll want to eat it every day.
keywords: Bean & Lentil Salad with Whipped Sesame Tofu
Bean & Lentil Salad with Whipped Sesame Tofu recipe
instructions: Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil. Drop in the frozen bean medley and edamame and cook for 2-3 mins until defrosted and heated through. Drain and set aside.

Drain the chickpeas and add to a large bowl along with the quinoa, lentils, bean medley and edamame. Zest the lemon half over the top, then squeeze over the juice. Drizzle over the sesame oil and add the soy sauce. Toss everything together.

Drain the white beans and add to a blender with the remaining dressing ingredients, apart from the lemon. Blend until completely smooth. Taste and squeeze in lemon juice a little at a time, along with more soy sauce if needed, until the seasoning is right.
Spoon the dressing onto plates and top with the salad. This keeps well in the fridge for 2-3 days.

name: Bean Chilli-Stuffed Jacket Potato with Lime Pickled Onions & Avocado
description: Everyone loves a jacket potato, so we’ve stuffed this with our ultimate veggie chilli for a midweek crowd-pleaser.
keywords: Bean Chilli-Stuffed Jacket Potato with Lime Pickled Onions & Avocado
instructions: Make the Veggie Chilli Sin Carne.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Prick the potatoes with a fork and rub with olive oil, salt and pepper. Pop onto a baking tray and get into the oven for 1 hr - 1 hr 30 mins, until a knife goes through.
Finely slice the red onion and transfer to a bowl with a pinch of salt and the juice of the lime. Scrunch the onion a little with your hands and set aside.

Get the leftover Veggie Chilli Sin Carne into a saucepan and heat through until piping hot. Dice the avocado. Get the potatoes out of the oven, cut with a cross and squish to open. Add the butter and mash it in before topping with the chilli, feta, avocado and limey onions.

name: Beans Alla Norma
description: Beans are a magical food. They’re packed with dietary fibre and plant protein, plus studies show that the rhyme is true – they really are good for your heart!
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Roughly dice the aubergine and roast in the oven for 30 mins until soft.

Meanwhile, chop the garlic and most of the basil (reserve a few leaves for garnish). Set a frying pan over a medium heat, then add 2 tbsp oil and the garlic. Fry for a minute or two until it begins to turn translucent. Add the chopped tomatoes and basil, then cook for 20 mins. Season to taste.
Stir the roasted aubergine into the sauce along with the drained beans and cook for a further 5 mins.
Serve with 2 tablespoons of ricotta on each serving, parmesan shavings and the remaining basil leaves. Tuck in!

name: Beany Chicken Traybake with Sweetcorn & Jalapeño Salsa
description: Charred curried chicken thighs, a silky blitzed tomato sauce and creamy beans, all from one tray. The sweet-sharp corn salsa on top does a lot of the heavy lifting. In Partnership with Aldi #ad
keywords: Chicken & Bean Traybake with Sweetcorn & Jalapeño Salsa
Chicken & Bean Traybake with Sweetcorn & Jalapeño Salsa recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Add most of the Greek yoghurt to a large baking tray along with the curry powder, the jalapeño brine and a good pinch of salt. Grate in the garlic, then give it a really good mix.

Cut one and a half of the red onions into wedges, then tip into the tray with the cherry tomatoes and toss well. Arrange the chicken thighs on top, drizzle with olive oil and season the skin with a big pinch of salt. Bake for 40 mins, until the chicken is tender and lightly charred on top.
While that cooks, heat a large frying pan over a high heat. Drain the sweetcorn, tip it into the pan and fry for a few minutes, until lightly charred, then leave to cool.

Finely dice the remaining half onion and add it to the cooled corn along with the pickled jalapeños and the juice of half the lime. Give it a mix and season to taste with salt, then set aside to serve.
Squeeze the juice of the remaining lime half into the rest of the yoghurt and set aside to serve.

Get the chicken out of the oven, then lift out the thighs and set aside. Tip everything from the tray into a blender, don't worry, it'll look a little split but it'll all come together. Blitz until smooth, then taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Drain the beans and tip them into the empty tray, top with the chicken, then pour the sauce all over the top. Slide back into the oven and cook for 10 more mins.
Spoon the beans and chicken into bowls, then top with a spoonful of the yoghurt and the corn salsa. Sprinkle with the coriander leaves and serve.

name: Beany Chilli Soup with Toasted Seeds & Wholegrain Rice
description: We’ve repurposed the batch-cooked ultimate veg chilli and turned it into a soup with wholegrain rice and toasted seeds. Proper nourishing!
keywords: Beany Chilli Soup with Toasted Seeds & Wholegrain Rice
instructions: Make the Veggie Chilli Sin Carne.

Heat the oven to 160°C. 
Put the seeds onto a baking tray and pop in the oven for 12-15 mins until golden. Get the leftover Veggie Chilli Sin Carne into a saucepan along with the stock, then simmer it away until piping hot.
Finely slice the jalapeño. Heat the rice following pack instructions, then serve up in bowls. Ladle in the soup and top with soured cream, jalapeños, and toasted seeds.

name: Beany, Corn & Cheese Chilli Enchiladas
description: Cheesy corn-stuffed tortillas baked in using our rich Veggie Chilli Sin Carne leftover. It's like a hug in enchilada form.
instructions: Make the Veggie Chilli Sin Carne.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan.

Grate the cheddar and pick the coriander leaves. Finely chop half the leaves and stems, and add to a bowl. Stir in the sweetcorn, ricotta and half of the grated cheddar. Season with salt and black pepper.

Divide the cheesy corn mixture between the tortillas, roll them up tightly and place seam-side down into a small ovenproof baking dish. Spoon the leftover Veggie Chilli Sin Carne over the top of the tortillas and scatter over the remaining cheddar.
Bake for 20 mins until bubbling and golden.
Share the enchiladas onto plates. Top with the remaining coriander leaves and serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Beeble Paloma
description: A refreshing summery cocktail recipe made with Beeble Honey Tequila. It's a little bit sweet, a little sharp, and a lot of delicious.
instructions: Zest the lime and mix with the sugar, then squeeze the lime for the juice.
Rub the lime husk around the rim to wet it and dip in the sugar zest mix.
Fill the glass with ice.
In a shaker go in with your tequila, grapefruit juice, sugar syrup and lime juice then add some ice and shake. Double strain into your rimmed glass then add a slice of grapefruit for garnish. Enjoy!

name: Beef & Ale Slice Pie
description: We worked to perfect our beef pie recipe, and it's sublime. Thick, unctuous filling. Perfectly tender meat. Salty, crusty pastry. Serve with English mustard.
instructions: Chop the onion, carrot and celery into same sized pieces.
Season the steak generously with salt and pepper and toss in the plain flour so that each piece is evenly coated.
Pour a splash of oil into a large saucepan/casserole dish. Get it on a high heat and fry the steak in batches until evenly browned. Set aside on a plate.
Turn down the heat. Don’t worry about the pan bottom being brown, this is all flavour! Tip in the onion, carrot and celery. Cook until softened (5 minutes or so), stirring as you go.

Pour in the ale and stock. Stir in the thyme and brown sauce. Put the steak back in the pan. Simmer gently on a low heat, uncovered, for 2 1/2 hours, until you have a very thick pie filling. If the gravy is too thin, remove the meat and bubble the sauce down. Leave to cool - you can do this the day before if you want.
Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.
Pie time. Unravel your first sheet of shortcrust pastry with its paper onto a baking tray. Spread mustard over the pastry and spoon in your filling, keeping a 2cm border free around the edge.
Smooth the filling down and brush the border with beaten egg. Place your second shortcrust pastry sheet on top (roll it out first to make sure it fits with enough overlap).
Press the two sheets of pastry together around the edge, and cut off any messy bits. Press the edges with a fork to create a seal.
Score the top with a cutlery knife. Don’t press the knife in too far as you don’t want to cut the pastry open. Bake in the oven for 30 mins until deep golden brown.
Slice and serve with a dollop of brown sauce or mustard, or both if you are a maverick! Tuck in!

name: Beef & Black Bean Nachos
description: Beefy, cheesy, crunchy, and a bit spicy. These loaded nachos are the midweek hero you didn’t know you needed. Built in one pan and done in minutes.
instructions: Brush any dirt off the mushrooms and finely chop.
Set a large nonstick oven-safe frying pan over a medium heat. Add the mushrooms and cook dry for 8-10 mins, stirring now and then, until golden and softened.

Add the beef mince, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Cook for 1-2 mins until browned all over. Stir through the taco seasoning, then tip in the black beans — juice and all. Add half a jar of water and let the mixture simmer, stirring occasionally for 15 to mins until the beef is tender, adding a splash more water if it starts to look dry.
Meanwhile, peel the onion, thinly slice and add to a bowl. Pour over a little juice from the pickled jalapeños, add a pinch of salt and scrunch it all together to soften. Set aside.

Shred the lettuce and fill bowls. Add the tortilla chips then spoon over the beef. Top with the cheddar, pickled onions, jalapeños, dollops of yoghurt and coriander leaves. Serve straight from the pan with green Tabasco on the side.

name: Beef & Guinness Stew With Chilli Cheddar Dumplings
description: A big, brash beef stew that we've topped with spicy cheesy dumplings. This is a proper winter warmer.
keywords: Beef & Guinness Stew With Chilli Cheddar Dumplings
instructions: Heat the oven to 150°C. Tip the beef chunks all into a bowl and season with plenty of salt and pepper. Add the flour and toss to thoroughly coat all the pieces of beef. Ensure your butter is very cold.

Heat a large lidded casserole dish over a medium heat and add a shot of olive oil. Working in batches, sear the beef until deep golden-brown in colour. This will take 10-15 mins. Once browned, set aside, leaving any beef fat or residual olive oil in the pan.

While the beef is browning, chop the carrots, celery and shallots into chunks. Add them and the whole garlic cloves to the pan, then fry for 4-5 mins. Deglaze with the Guinness and add the beef stock.
Add the mustard and bring to a simmer. Pop the beef back in and add the rosemary, thyme and bay leaves. Slide the casserole, with the lid on, into the oven for 2 hours.

While that's cooking away, you can get on with the dumplings. First, tip the self-raising flour into a bowl, season with lots of salt and pepper, then add the Aleppo pepper and dried thyme. Grate in the butter and the cheese and toss through the dry ingredients until coated. Break the gratings down into smaller chunks, leaving a few larger pieces intact. Gradually add the milk while mixing constantly to bring the ingredients together to form a dough. Set aside.
After 2 hours remove the stew from the oven and stir in the cavolo nero, place the lid on and slide back into the oven whilst you finish off the dumplings.

Now back to the dumplings. Lightly flour a surface and roll out the dough to 2cm thick. Punch out circles with a pint glass or circular cutter of your choice and use them to top the pie. Re-roll any offcuts and cut until you’ve used up all the dough. Arrange the dumplings on the top of the pie and sprinkle over extra cheddar and black pepper.
Slide back into the oven for 25 mins, with the lid off, until golden-brown. Reheat your peas in the microwave with a little water. Then serve up altogether with a big dollop of mustard!

name: Beef & Mushroom Orzo
description: Beefy, mushroomy, cheesy orzo magic. A creamy, one-pan, weeknight comfort that delivers way more than it should.
instructions: Thinly slice the mushrooms and garlic. Pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the stems.
Place a frying pan with high sides over a medium-high heat (no oil). Once hot, add the mushrooms, season with salt and cook, stirring, until browned, 10-15 mins. Tip onto a plate.
Pour the olive oil into the empty pan. Once hot, add the beef mince, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 5–8 mins, until browned all over.
Add the orzo, parsley stems, garlic and plenty of black pepper to the pan. Cook for a couple of minutes until the garlic is fragrant.
Pour in the beef stock, Worcestershire sauce and water. Stir to combine, then cook the orzo until al dente, following pack instructions. Add a splash of water if it starts to look dry.
Meanwhile, grate the Parmesan.
Once the orzo is cooked, stir through the mushrooms and three-quarters of the Parmesan. Taste and season with more salt, pepper and an extra splash of Worcestershire sauce, if needed.
Share between bowls and top with the remaining Parmesan, a crack of black pepper and parsley leaves.

name: Beef & Udon Noodle Stir-Fry
description: Quick, punchy and full of sizzle. This speedy beef stir-fry hits all the right notes. Plus, it's ready in minutes.
instructions: Thinly slice the steak and season with a little salt and plenty of black pepper. Thinly slice the chilli and cut the spring onions into four pieces each. Peel and thinly slice the garlic. Peel the ginger and cut into matchsticks.
Place a wok or large deep frying pan over a medium-high heat with the sunflower oil. Once hot, add the steak and cook for 1-2 mins per side until just browned, then move it to one side of the pan.
Add the spring onions to the empty side of the pan and stir-fry for 1 min until fragrant. Add the chilli, garlic and ginger and toss for 1 min.
Chuck in the stir-fry veg and toss everything together. Cook for 2 mins until the veg starts to soften.

Cook the noodles according to packet instructions and add them in tossing again. Pour in the soy sauce, honey and the juice of half the lime. Stir-fry for another 1-2 mins until everything is piping hot.
Divide between bowls and top with the coriander, if using.

name: Beef Barbacoa Taco
description: This smokey beef barbacoa is exceptionally good for tacos. Make sure you really char your tomatoes and onions to bring that depth of flavour.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C/320°F.

Cut 1 red onion into wedges and peel the garlic cloves. Place in a dry frying pan along with the tomatoes. Fry on a very high heat until blackened. Don’t be scared about them charring - this is what makes the unreal smoky flavour later.
Tip the red onion, garlic and tomatoes into a food processor. Add the cumin seeds, paprika, oregano, chipotle paste and olive oil. Blitz together to make the barbacoa sauce.
Cut the brisket into chunky pieces and season generously with sea salt and pepper.

Pour a drizzle of oil into a casserole dish and fry the beef in batches until evenly browned on all sides. Return all the beef to the pan, pour in the chicken stock and scrape in the barbacoa sauce. Give everything a good mix and bring to the boil.
Put a lid on and transfer to the oven. Roast for 2 hours, remove the lid and continue to cook the meat for 1 1/2 hours until the meat is completely falling apart.

Thinly slice the remaining red onion and pour over the juice of the lime. Add a good pinch of salt and scrunch the onions with your hands - this will encourage them to soften. Leave for 10 minutes to pickle.
Shred the beef into its sauce & season to taste. Serve with the pickled onions, tortillas and whatever else you like.

name: Beef Birria
description: A fuss-free slow-cooked birria with tender beef and a rich broth. This dish from Guadalajara is a Mexican broth made using dried chilies and lots of different spices. In my family, we make birria using beef, because it’s easier to find and quicker to cook than goat. We cook birria for special occasions and we love having the leftovers for breakfast.
ingredients: Leftover Beans de la Olla (to serve)
instructions: Cut the bone-in beef shin and beef chuck into big 6-8cm chunks, separating the bone marrow from the shin meat.
Heat the grill to high. Get all the beef chunks, bone marrow and short ribs on a baking tray.
Slide the tray under the grill to cook for 8 mins until the meat is nicely browned, turning the beef and marrow over halfway through.
Transfer the meat to a large cast iron pot and set aside while you prep the adobo (sauce).

Remove the seeds and stem from the dried chilies. Add the chillies to a small bowl, cover with boiling water and set aside for 5 mins to rehydrate. Halve the tomatoes and onions. Peel the garlic cloves.

Get the tomatoes, onion and garlic in a blender and add all the spices, vinegar and ½ the salt. Add the soaked chilies and a splash of their water then blend until smooth (add more water if it feels too thick).
Pass the adobo through a sieve and pour it over the meat. Stir through ¾ of the water.

Set the pot over a high heat and bring the liquid to a boil then pop the lid on, reduce the heat to low and cook for about 2 hours, adding the remaining salt and water halfway through. The cooking time will vary depending on your hob so make sure the meat is tender and falling apart easily before you turn off the heat. Once cooked, season to taste with more salt if needed.
Before serving, transfer the pieces of meat to a bowl or plate and use two forks to shred it.

To serve, portion out some meat into bowls and ladle over some broth. Serve with warmed beans from the pot, if you like, and garnish with finely chopped fresh coriander, diced onion, spicy salsa and lime wedges on the side and warm rolled up corn tortillas.

name: Beef Chilli Con Carne
description: Student dinners don't get easier than this. Make a big batch of this beefy chilli con carne and you'll be able to make a load of easy meals throughout the week.
keywords: Batch: Beef Chilli Con Carne recipe
instructions: Finely dice the onion and red peppers. Crush the garlic.
Add a drizzle of olive oil into a large lidded saucepan on medium heat. Once hot, fry the mince in batches, making sure it doesn’t stew. Once browned, remove from the pan and set aside.
Add another glug of oil into the pan. Then, add the onion and pepper. Stir-fry over until softened, 7 mins, then add the garlic and fry until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato purée, chilli powder, paprika and ground cumin. Cook for 2 mins stirring all the time.

Add the tinned tomatoes and drained kidney beans. Mix well, then return the mince to the pan and pour in the beef stock. The mince should all be covered. If not, add a splash of water. Season with salt and pepper. At this point, taste the chilli – if you want more spice, add a wee bit more chilli powder.

Simmer the chilli until thickened to your liking, or bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer, place a lid on and leave to cook gently for up to 1 hr 30 mins, depending on how much time you have. Simmering for a longer time will mean a thicker, richer end result, but it’s still delicious eaten straight away if you don’t have the time or are too hungry.
Stir the sweetcorn through until defrosted before serving. Optional: if batch cooking for the week, transfer to Tupperware containers.

name: Beef Chow Mein
description: It doesn't get better than this. This easy beef chow mein recipe is ideal for when you want to spend a Friday night in.
instructions: Slice an onion. Peel your carrot and thinly slice. Chop your spring onions at an angle (about 3cm lengthways). Finely slice your garlic. Prep your mangetout and give it a wash.
Pop the noodles in a heatproof bowl and cover with boiling water until the noodles are cooked. This should take around 18 mins.
Cut your steak into three pieces then thinly slice across the line to shorten the fibre of the meat. Add to a bowl and mix the rest of the ingredients for the beef together until evenly coated.
Blanch your beansprouts in a pot of boiling water for just a few mins.
Coat your wok with 3 tbsp of oil then pour most of it away. Fry the beef slices on high heat for two mins, then add your garlic, carrot, onion and mangetout.
Fry for a few mins then add your cooked noodles, beansprouts and fry for another 2 mins, making sure to toss the noodles well.
Mix your sauce in a separate bowl and then slowly add it to the noodles and mix well.
Add your spring onions to your noodles and plate up!

name: Beef Shin Chilli
description: Take your chilli to new levels by using slow-cooked beef shin instead of mince. Melt-in-the-mouth and beautifully spiced. You'll never look back.
instructions: Heat your oven to 150°C.
Chop your beef shin into large pieces about 3 inches big.
Finely slice your onions, dice your red pepper and grate your garlic.

Heat a small glug of oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add half of your beef shin and season generously with salt and pepper. Fry until browned on all sides, which should take a few mins. Remove from the pan and repeat with your remaining meat. Set aside.

In a large casserole dish, heat a good glug of olive oil over a medium heat. Add your onion and cook out for 10 mins until soft. Tip in your red pepper and fry for another 5 mins until it is all soft and just starting to caramelise.

Pop your garlic in the pan and cook out for a minute. Add your cumin, coriander, paprika, chipotle puree and tomato purée to the pan and cook out for 2 mins until your spices are fragrant and your tomato purée has darkened in colour.
Add your beef back into the pan and pour your wine over the top. Allow it to bubble and reduce away, then tip in your plum tomatoes and beef stock.
Once simmering, pop a lid on the casserole and pop it in the oven. Cook for 3 and a half hours.
Remove your casserole from the oven and take off the lid. Pour in your drained tin of black beans and give it a good stir. Pop the lid back on and cook for another 30 mins.
Shred up your meat a little with two forks, then give the dish a final seasoning check. Reheat the rice.
Serve up over fluffy rice with a dollop of sour cream and a sprinkle of coriander, then tuck in.

name: Beef Stew And Dumplings
description: Discover the ultimate comfort food with our savoury beef stew and dumplings recipe. It’s the perfect dinner for cold evenings and a pretty foolproof recipe that you can leave on a nice simmer all afternoon.
instructions: Heat the oven to 140°C.
Cut the beef shin into 5cm pieces, or get the butcher to do this for you. Scrape into a bowl.
Halve the onion and cut into chunky dice, then peel the carrots and cut them into similar-sized pieces. Do the same with the celery.
Scatter the beef pieces with the flour and plenty of salt and pepper, then toss to coat really well.
Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large lidded casserole pan set over a medium-high heat. Lay in some of the beef pieces, leaving a little gap around each so they can fry properly.
Cook for 2 mins on each side until golden and crisp, then remove into a clean bowl. Repeat with the remaining beef pieces, adding a little more oil as you go, if needed.
Add in another drizzle of oil and add the onion, carrot, celery, and bay leaves along with a good pinch of salt.
Put on the lid and cook for 6-8 mins, stirring regularly until the onions have softened slightly.
Squeeze in the tomato purée, spoon in the Marmite, and cook for a minute before pouring in the beef stock and adding the beef back to the pan along with any resting juices from the bowl.

Bring to the boil, then put on the lid and pop it into the oven for 2 hrs. After 2 hrs, remove the lid and cook for another 30 mins, until the beef is meltingly tender and the gravy has thickened slightly.
For the dumplings, tip the flour, baking powder and suet into a bowl with a pinch of salt and pour in the water. Mix briefly to form a dough.
Tip the dough out onto a well-floured work surface, divide it into 8 pieces and shape into rough scone shapes.
Coarsely grate the cheddar.
Once the beef has been cooking for 2 hrs 30 mins as described above, nestle the dumplings into the top of the stew.
Add a pinch of cheddar on top of each, then pop back into the oven for 30-40 mins, until the cheese and dumplings are lightly golden.
Scatter with the parsley to serve.

name: Beef Stroganoff
description: A classic beef stroganoff recipe. This family favourite will have everyone happy at the dinner table. Rich, luxurious, and the right level of hearty.
instructions:
Prep your ingredients to marinade in the fridge. 
First, chop up your mushrooms. Finely slice your onion.
Put the beef slices into a nice large bowl. Now, flood the bowl with Worcestershire sauce, the curry powder and the English mustard, this may bite your nostrils a bit.

Give it a good stir – use your hands to get everything really coated well. This should not be overly wet, it should coat the beef nicely. Cover with foil or clingfilm and stick it in the fridge. Marinate this overnight if you can. It does make for a richer, deeper flavour, but if you can’t be arsed, leave it in the fridge for, at the very minimum, 2 hours.

Make sure you take the beef out of the fridge at least an hour before you use it. Then, in a big, deep frying pan, add a couple of tbsp of oil and a half of your butter and fry the beef strips in batches.
Once the pieces are brown and your kitchen smells lovely, put the fried steak back into the bowl and leave to one side to rest a bit.
In a large frying pan, melt a big knob of butter and add a nice hit of extra virgin olive oil. Let them heat up. The butter will foam and start to colour.
Add the onions and cook them until they are translucent, starting to brown and catch on the bottom of the pan.
Turn up the heat slightly and add the flour to the onions. Turn the temperature down a bit and then, bit by bit, add the tomato purée and stock.
Scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon to get all the bits off. Adjust the heat so the liquid is gently rolling.

Now, take the bowl with the beef in and tip the lot into the oniony liquid. Give it a stir and now we wait. I’m not sure how long this is going to take. We want the liquid to reduce down until it’s a rich, thick gravy. The beef should be not quite fall-apart-tender but really, really close. We’re almost finished.

Melt a large knob of butter in a frying pan. Add all the mushrooms. Fry until golden brown. Stir in the parsley. You can do this at any point during the cooking process and leave them in a bowl until you’re ready to use them.
Once the beef is tender, and the gravy is rich and spicy and complex, stir in the cooked mushrooms.
At this point I’ll stir in a tablespoon of soured cream, a big mill of black pepper and I’ll taste it to see if it needs salt. If yes, salt. That’s it.
We’ve always served it with white rice.

name: Beef Wellington
description: This beef wellington recipe is the be all and end all of beef wellington recipe. Follow the steps here and you'll know how to make beef wellington the proper way. The only way.
keywords: what to serve with beef wellington
how long to cook beef wellington
instructions: Start by preparing the beef. Make sure the fillet is fridge-cold before seasoning generously with salt and pepper. Preheat a frying pan until it is screaming hot. Add a shot of oil and sear the beef on all sides. Pull out of the pan and brush with the English mustard. Pop back on a tray and into the fridge.

Remove the leaves from the stems of the chard and cook for 1 min in boiling salted water. Transfer to ice water to stop the cooking process – this will also make sure the leaves stay bright green. Remove the leaves from the ice bath and squeeze out the excess moisture. Set aside.
To make the duxelle, finely chop the shallots, grate the garlic and pick the leaves from the thyme stems. Tip the mushrooms into a food processor and blitz until finely chopped.

Grab a large frying pan and add a splash of olive oil and the butter. Tip in the shallots and garlic and cook over a low heat until just translucent. Add the mushrooms and thyme and crank up the heat. Cook with a pinch of salt for 10-15 mins, stirring regularly, until the mixture is very dry. Now add the cognac and flambé. Cook until the cognac has evaporated, then tip into a bowl and set aside in the fridge.

Time to assemble. Lay out a sheet or two of cling film and spread the chard leaves out in an even layer. Add the beef fillet and wrap in the chard leaves, using the cling film to help you. Roll tightly and put in the fridge for 20 mins.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Now lay out some more cling film and cover it with the sliced parma ham. Add an even rectangle of duxelle (about 1cm thick). Unwrap your beef fillet and lay it on top of the duxelle. Wrap the duxelle and ham up and around the beef and wrap that with the cling film. Twist to tighten and pop back into the fridge for 20 mins.

Lay out the pastry sheets and pop the (unwrapped) beef on top. Crack the egg yolks into a small bowl (disgarding the whites) then beat together. Egg-wash the pastry and wrap everything up, sealing the beef inside. Pop this back into the fridge for 30 mins.
Egg-wash the wellington and sprinkle with loads of flaky salt. Bake for 35-50 mins until a deep golden-brown and the beef has an internal temp of 40°C. Rest for 1 hr before slicing and serving.

name: Beef, Black Bean and Cashew Pappardelle
description: We're giving pappardelle the noodle treatment and tossing that pasta in a black bean sauce with tender Ocado beef and crunchy Chikas Black Pepper Cashews.
instructions: Marinate the steak in 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 clove grated garlic, and 1 tbsp rice wine vinegar and allow to marinate until you are ready to cook.
Mince the remaining garlic, ginger and red chilli. Chop up the spring onions. Slice the onion and chop up the tenderstem broccoli.
Mix together the black bean sauce, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice wine vinegar and 200ml water. In a small cup, combine the cornflour with 2 tbsp of water.
Bring a pan of water to a boil. Add your pappardelle and bicarbonate of soda, then cook for a couple of mins less than the packet instructions
Add a large glug of cold oil to a hot wok and fry the beef for 2-3 mins until golden on the outside but still pink on the inside. Remove and set aside.

Add another glug of oil and fry the spring onion whites until charred for 3 mins. Then add in the ginger, garlic, red chilli and onions and cook for 4 mins until darkened. Then toss in the broccoli and cook for 3 mins.
Pour in the sauce and bring it to a bubble. Add the cornflour slurry and allow the sauce to bubble and thicken for 2 mins.
Add in the cooked pappardelle and toss together until the pasta is well-coated and glossy.
Finally, add in the beef, black pepper cashews, and spring onion greens. Toss it all together and serve.

name: Beef, Cheddar & Onion Pie
description: A hearty beef pie recipe that's set to be a new family favourite. The secret ingredient? Love. And cheddar. Lots of cheddar.
keywords: beef and cheddar and onion pie recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Remove the pastry from the fridge about 30 mins before using. Roll the pastry out and cut it into a circle around 1cm bigger than the pan or dish you’ll be cooking the pie in. Return to the fridge until you’re ready to use it.
Peel and finely slice the onion and garlic, peel and finely dice the carrot and then slice the celery.

Heat ⅓ of your olive oil in a frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add half the beef and fry until deeply caramelised. Remove from the pan and set aside, then repeat with another ⅓ of olive oil and the rest of the beef, then remove from the pan.

Add the last ⅓ of olive oil to the same pan and add the onion, carrot, garlic and celery along with a pinch of salt. Cook over a medium heat for 10 mins, then add the cooked beef and the flour. Cook for 3-4 mins, then add the Worcestershire sauce and stock. Taste and season with salt and pepper, then simmer for 5-10 mins until slightly thickened. Grate the cheese then mix it through the beef mixture until melted. If using a pie dish, transfer the mix into it, but if not, keep it in the ovenproof frying pan.

Get the pastry out of the fridge and score with a cross-hatch pattern. Cut a small hole or cross in the middle to let the steam escape, then drape the pastry over the pie filling, sticking the pastry to the edge of the dish to seal. Brush with beaten egg and pop in the oven for 20-25 mins until crisp and golden.
Serve with mash and greens!

name: Beefy Chilli Jacket Potato
description: Golden jacket potatoes loaded with rich beef chilli, melty cheese and sharp pickled onions. It’s a classic for a reason.
instructions: Make the Beef Chilli Con Carne.
Heat the oven to 200°C.

Scrub the potatoes, prick them all over with a fork, then rub with a little olive oil and salt. Place directly onto the oven rack and bake for 1 hr until crisp on the outside and fluffy in the middle.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the red onion and place it into a bowl. Squeeze over the lime juice and season with salt. Set aside to pickle.
Warm the leftover beef chilli in a saucepan set over a low heat, stirring occasionally until piping hot. Add a splash of water if it’s thickened in the fridge.
Grate the cheddar.

Once the potatoes are cooked, cut a deep cross into the tops and squeeze them open. Fluff the insides with a fork, then spoon over the hot beef chilli. Top with soured cream, grated cheddar and a big spoonful of pickled red onions.
Bake for 20 mins until the cheese is melted, golden and everything is bubbling.
Spoon onto plates and serve with the pickled red onions and a wedge of lime.

name: Beer Braised Pork Belly Tacos
description: The zingy salsa cuts through the rich pork like a dream. You've gotta try this one MOB.
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C. Place pork belly slices on a tray. Add 1⁄4 of a red onion and half the garlic cloves. Add cumin and smoked paprika. Season with salt and pepper. Pour 400ml of beer over the top and then add enough water to cover the pork. Cover the tray with tin foil and cook for 4 hours.

In the meantime, make your salsa. Chop the mango into cubes, and quarter the cherry tomatoes. Chop the coriander and the spring onions, red chilli and add to a bowl. Juice over the lime and add a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt. Mix together and pop in the fridge to chill.

After 4 hours, remove the pork from the oven. Remove the tin foil. Break up the pork with a fork. Place it back in the oven at 180°C for 20 minutes until most of the liquid has evaporated and you have your dark, sticky pork.

Black bean time. Splash some olive oil into a pan and fry two chopped garlic cloves. After 20 seconds, add your black beans but keep the water in the tin for later. Coat the beans in the garlic and oil. Mash them up. Add the water from the tin and reduce until you have a black bean mush.
Once everything is ready, heat up your mini tortillas, add a dollop of black beans, your pork and then the salsa.

name: Beer-Battered Vegan Fish Tacos With Chipotle Mayo & Slaw
description: Crispy beer-battered heart of palm and artichoke patties, piled into warm tortillas with a zingy lime slaw, crunchy peanuts and a spicy lime mayo. Vegan tacos that genuinely deliver on texture.
keywords: Beer-Battered Vegan Fish Tacos With Chipotle Mayo & Slaw
Beer-Battered Vegan Fish Tacos With Chipotle Mayo & Slaw recipe
instructions: First, make the slaw. Finely slice the red cabbage and red onion and place in a large bowl. Zest the lime over the top, then squeeze in the juice. Add a good pinch of salt, toss everything together and set aside to marinate.

Drain the heart of palm and add it to a large bowl. Use a fork or potato masher to mash it until you have a chunky texture. Drain the artichoke tin and squeeze out as much excess water as you can from each one. Tear the artichoke petals into the bowl and mash the sturdier base of them into the artichokes into the heart of palm. Add the Old Bay seasoning and a good amount of salt and pepper and mix well to combine. You can use your hands here too, you are looking for everything to be evenly combined and a chunky texture with the artichoke petals still intact and flaky. Add the smaller amount of breadcrumbs and mix gently. You should be able to squeeze a ball of the mix in your hands without it being too wet or falling apart. If not, add more breadcrumbs.
Shape the mixture into oblongs, you should get around 7-8. Lay them on a flat surface and transfer to the fridge to firm up.
Make the mayo by mixing all the ingredients together in a small bowl. Taste and adjust the spice or acidity if needed, then refrigerate until needed.
Finely slice the chilli and roughly chop the peanuts. Pick the coriander leaves.
In a large bowl, mix together the flour, fine sea salt, paprika, garlic powder and black pepper. Slowly pour in the lager and whisk to a smooth batter.
Lightly toast the tortillas and keep warm under a plate.

Heat a medium frying pan over a medium heat and add enough vegetable oil to come halfway up the patties. Test the oil is hot enough by dropping in a dot of batter, if it sizzles immediately, you're good to go. Take care not to let the oil get too hot. Set a plate lined with kitchen towel nearby. Dredge the patties in the batter and gently lower into the oil. Fry on one side for about 2 mins, then flip and fry for another minute or so until golden and crisp, then transfer to the kitchen towel. Repeat with the remaining patties, making sure not to overcrowd the pan.Air fryer option: Spray the basket generously with oil spray and air fry at 200°C for 12 mins, flipping them halfway through and spraying again. They won't be quite as crispy, but still great.
To serve, layer the crispy patties into the tortillas and top with the slaw, a spoonful of spicy lime mayo, sliced chilli, peanuts and coriander.

name: Beer-Battered Vegetable Fritters
description: These fritters are a great way to use up whatever leftover veggies you've got in the fridge. Serve them hot and salty with a cold beer.
instructions: Prepare your veg. Roughly chop your carrots and courgette into matchsticks. Halve your onion then finely slice it. Roughly chop your spring onion into thirds (you can leave the roots on). Finely chop your chilli. Place the veggies in a large bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil to 180°C in a deep saucepan set over a medium heat (if you don’t have a thermometer, pop the end of a wooden spoon in the oil; it’s ready when small bubbles form around it).
In a separate bowl, mix together the cornflour and plain flour then whisk in the beer. The batter should be thin and pourable but thick enough to cling to the vegetables.
Grab small bundles of vegetables from the bowl, dip them into the beer batter, and then straight into the oil. Leave them to fry for 2 mins until the batter is light brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and season with salt whilst hot.
To serve, transfer to a plate with some soy sauce and mayonnaise for dipping.

name: Beetroot & Feta Pesto
description: A tangy, bright Barbie-looking pesto that's going to add a pop of colour and flavour to your dinner table.
instructions: Add the beetroot, toasted walnuts and feta to a blender. Peel the garlic clove and add it in then squeeze in the juice of the lemon and season generously with salt and pepper.
Add ⅓ of the olive oil and begin to blend, then continue to add olive oil until you get to a thick pesto consistency.

name: Beetroot & Yoghurt Dip
description: A rich and creamy dip that gets its colour from our homemade beetroot and feta pesto.
instructions: Season the yoghurt with salt and pepper and spread onto a large platter. Spoon the pesto on top and then swirl into the yoghurt.
Drizzle with olive oil, scatter with dill and the toasted walnuts. Finish with a crack of black pepper. Serve with bread for swooping through.

name: Beetroot & Za'atar Marinated Eggs
description: These eggs are a flavour bomb! The flavours of earthy beetroot and zesty za'atar all wrapped up in a tangy marinade will jazz up any bougie brunch spread. Plus they're also great for meal prepping - so you can snack on them all week.
instructions: Prep your the ingredients for the marinade. Zest the lemon, thinly slice the cooked beetroot, smash the garlic cloves and half the red chills lengthways. Set aside them all aside.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Gently lower in the eggs and simmer for 6 mins. Transfer to a bowl of iced water to cool. Once cool, peel the eggs.
In a bowl, combine the beetroot, garlic, lemon zest, chilli, za’atar, honey, red wine vinegar, water and salt. Mix well.
Place the peeled eggs into a clean container. Pour over the beetroot marinade, ensuring the eggs are fully submerged. Cover with a piece of kitchen paper to keep the eggs submerged.

Place the lid on the container and refrigerate for at least 3 hrs, preferably overnight, to allow the flavours to develop and the eggs to take on a vibrant hue. 
These eggs will last for up to 4 days in the fridge, the flavour gets stronger each day.
When ready to serve, halve the eggs and drizzle with a little olive oil. Season with black pepper and, if using, crumble over some feta.

name: Beetroot Chickpea Soup
description: An earthy, sweet and creamy beetroot soup that’s packed with protective antioxidants. Combined with the fibre and plant protein from the chickpeas, you’ve got yourself a super bowl.
instructions: Heat the oven to 175°C and line a tray with baking paper.

Wash and scrub the beets (no need to peel), then roughly chop them into quarters. Add to a bowl and toss with a glug of olive oil and salt. Roast in the oven for 45 mins, turning once halfway through.

Heat another glug of olive oil in a large pan set over a low-medium heat. Peel and slice the shallots, then sauté them for about 5 mins until soft and fragrant. Stir in the roasted beets, then cover with broth and simmer for 10-15 mins, until the beets are very soft.

Transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until smooth. Allow to cool for a few mins, then blend in half a cup of the crème fraîche. Transfer the soup back to the pot, drain the chickpeas (reserve the liquid for another recipe), and stir them into the soup.
Divide the soup across four bowls and serve with the remaining crème fraîche, a few stalks of dill, and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Beetroot Hummus with Crispy Tarka
description: This pink, colourful number is as delicious as it looks. It’s the perfect balance of savoury, sweet, rich and spicy. We have no doubt you’ll love it!
instructions: Drain the chickpeas and drain and quarter the beetroot.
Place the chickpeas, beetroot, 1 garlic clove, tahini and ground cumin in a food processor with the juice of half a lemon, 50ml olive oil and 50ml cold water.
Season well with salt and pepper and blitz until smooth, adding more water or olive oil, if necessary.
Thinly slice the shallot, red chilli and remaining garlic clove, finely chop the ginger, and roughly chop the fresh coriander.
Heat the ghee in a saucepan that is at least 6 inches tall. This is to minimise splattering later.
Carefully add the curry leaves - they will pop and sizzle - then add the shallots and cumin seeds and cook until golden.
Add the red chilli, garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Turn the heat off and stir in the fresh coriander. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the spiced ghee over the hummus then serve with warm flatbreads. Enjoy!

name: Beetroot Risotto with Feta & Pumpkin Seeds
description: Add some sunshine to your day with this vivid pink risotto made from pre-cooked beetroot for minimal cooking. Half of the beetroot is blitzed into the sauce whilst the other half is chopped for some pleasing texture. A seriously banging dinner.
instructions: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a large, deep, high-sided frying pan set over a medium heat until starting to pop. Tip into a small bowl and set aside until later.
Finely chop the onion. Scrape into the same frying pan. Add a splash of olive oil along with a pinch of salt, cook set over a medium heat, stirring occasionally for 8-10 mins until soft.

Add the risotto rice, stir so that every grain gets coated in the onion oil, and toast in the pan for a minute. Pour in the white wine. Cook, stirring until the white wine has bubbled away, then add a ladleful of hot stock.
Stir the rice regularly once the stock has been added, cooking until the liquid has been absorbed, then add a ladleful more.
Keep cooking the risotto in this way for around 20-25 mins until the rice is tender, with a slight bite, and is a creamy, soupy consistency.

Meanwhile, cut half the beetroot into bite-sized pieces around 2cm big and put the remaining beetroot into a powerful blender (a smoothie maker or stick blender works well here) with 100ml of the stock, the vinegar and some seasoning. Blitz until completely smooth.
Once the rice is cooked, add the cut-up beetroot, along with the beetroot sauce.
Finely grate in all the Parmesan. Stir until all the cheese has melted, then season to taste (you’ll be topping with feta so go easy on the salt).
Spoon the risotto into bowls, crumble over the feta, drizzle with a little olive oil, then top with the toasted pumpkin seeds and za’atar, if using. Unreal.

name: Beetroot, Walnut & Poppy Seed Chicken Salad
description: The dressing is really what steals the show - tangy, bright and perfectly complements the caraway chicken. This is exactly the right dish to eat to nourish yourself after a hard day at work.
keywords: Walnut & Poppy Seed Chicken Salad recipe
instructions: Coarsely crush the caraway seeds. Butterfly the chicken breasts, then season on both sides with salt, pepper and the crushed caraway seeds.
Pick the dill fronds and thinly slice any soft stems. Discard any tough stems from the kale, then massage the leaves with a drizzle of olive oil until softened. Chop the beetroot into 2-3cm chunks.
Into a large bowl, add the yoghurt, mustard, creamed horseradish and poppy seeds. Grate in the zest of the lemon and squeeze in the juice, then season with salt.
Gently crush the walnuts. Place a frying pan over a medium heat and, once hot, add the walnuts and toast for 3-4 mins, until golden. Transfer into the dressing.
Into the now empty frying pan, add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken breasts and cook for 10-15 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through.
Share the chicken onto plates. Toss the dill, kale and beetroot into the dressing. Top the chicken with the salad and finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Ben's Crispy Rosemary Potatoes
description: My dad used to make me and my brothers these potatoes when we were growing up. It is the easiest way to make crispy potatoes. These are a staple dish. Ben x
instructions: Pre-heat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Chop your potatoes into small chunks. Separate your cloves of garlic from the bulb and peel them all.
Tip your potatoes and garlic into a large roasting tray. Pick the leaves off the rosemary and scatter these in too. Drizzle with a good glug of olive oil and a sprinkle of salt and pepper.
Roast for 25 mins, then take them out of the oven and give them a flip. Return them to the oven for another 25 mins until perfectly golden and crispy.
Finish them with a generous sprinkle of salt and enjoy!

name: Ben's Flatbreads
description: Once you get the hang of these, you’re on your way. Crispy, chewy, pillowy flatbreads, every time. B x
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the water, yeast and sugar and stir to combine.
Add the flour and salt and use your hand to mix the ingredients together and form a shaggy dough.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 mins until smooth and springy.
Divide the dough into 6 pieces, form into little balls and place into a tray dusted with semolina.
Now chuck them in the fridge and forget about them for a day or two.
When you’re ready for a flatbread, place a large frying pan over a medium heat.
Add a glug of oil, pull out a flatbread and stretch it out in a little more semolina.
Chuck it into the pan and cook on one side until crispy and puffed. Give it a flip and cook until lightly charred.
That’s it, good to go. Stuff them full of grilled chicken, hummus, baked feta – whatever you want. The dough balls will sit happily in your fridge, ready to go for up to 5 days.

name: Ben's Michelada
description: The Michelada. Mexico's answer to the Bloody Mary, and my god are they good. Spicy, tangy and delicious. They have healed me more times than I can remember. B x
instructions: Start by cutting a wedge of lime and rubbing it around the rim of your glass.
Now roll the rim of your glass in the chilli salt to coat.
Add the tomato juice to the glass with a big squeeze of lime, plus a few dashes each of Worcestershire and your favourite hot sauce. You can adjust to your taste.
Add your ice and give it a stir.
Now top off with ice cold beer and a slice of lime to garnish.
Get stuck in.

name: Ben's Summer Tomato Pasta
description: No dish makes tomatoes sing quite like this. Flavoured simply with herbs, chilli and garlic, this pasta is best when topped with gooey buffalo mozzarella.
instructions: Score a cross on the top of each tomato.
Place all your tomatoes in a large bowl and pour boiling water over them. Leave to sit for 10 mins, then drain and set aside to cool.
Once they're cool enough to handle, peel off the skin of each tomato. Cut the core out of each one.
Finely slice your garlic and chillies. Finely chop your chives.
Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large sauté pan. Add your garlic and cook gently for a minute.
Tip in your tomatoes and mash them up with a potato masher to purée them. Simmer for about 40 mins on a gentle heat until thick.
Add all but a handful of your sliced chilli, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil. Pour in your rigatoni and cook until al dente.
Tear your basil leaves into the tomato sauce. Add your rigatoni, along with a splash of your pasta water, then mix to combine. Add more pasta water where necessary to make a glossy sauce.
Spoon your pasta into bowls and tear over that beautiful buffalo mozzarella. Sprinkle with your remaining chilli, some more torn basil, your chopped chives, and some olive oil. Serve up and enjoy.

name: Bengali Lamb Curry
description: Also known as kosha mangsho, this is the quintessential Bengali meat curry. Mustard oil balanced with cooling yoghurt gives this curry a flavour like no other. Enjoy it with rice, luchis or rotis. I used some leftover egg roll dough to make myself a paratha to dip into it.
instructions: Bash the green chilli and pop into a large bowl. Add the rest of the marinade ingredients and thoroughly mix. Tip in the meat. Allow to marinate for 1 hr or ideally overnight.

Add a glug of mustard oil to a frying pan with high sides (ideally one with a lid, which you’ll need later). Set the pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cloves, cardamom, black peppercorns and dried red chillies. Cook for 30-45 seconds until fragrant, stirring constantly. Stir through the ginger and garlic paste. Add the fried onions with a splash of water and cook until they’ve softened.

Add the marinated meat to the pan and fry for 4-5 mins until browned. Add the ground coriander, cumin and garam masala, then mix well. Stir through the yoghurt and water, then season with salt and sugar. Bring the mixture to the boil, place a lid on top, turn the heat down to low and simmer for 45 mins-1 hr until the meat is tender (stir occasionally, so the bottom doesn’t catch).
Meanwhile, chop the coriander and green chillies.
Before serving, taste and season with salt and more sugar, if needed. Garnish with the coriander and green chillies.

name: Ben’s Amatriciana
description: A classic and ridiculously simple pasta dish. Smoky bacon combined with delicious Napolina tomatoes and pasta makes the perfect midweek meal.
instructions: First, finely dice your onion and chop your bacon.
