Pour a large glug of olive oil into your pan and add in your onions. Season with salt. Cook on a medium heat for 5 mins until translucent and very soft, but not brown.
Add in your bacon, then cook for 5 mins until lightly browned and crispy.
Deglaze your pan with the white wine and scrape down the bottom. Cook this for 3 mins until the wine has reduced.
Add in your plum tomatoes and allow this to bubble down for 15 mins.
Get a pan of water boiling and heavily season with salt. Add in the spaghetti and cook for 4 mins. Add a cup of pasta water into the tomato sauce.
Add the chilli flakes into the tomato sauce and give it a good mix. Season with salt and pepper. If you like it spicier, add more chilli flakes.

Cook your spaghetti according to the minimum time given in the packet instructions, ensuring it is al dente. Add it straight into the saucepot. Give it a good mix so the pasta is well coated in the sauce.
Serve this up in your bowls using your tongs to twirl the pasta. Serve with a healthy grating of pecorino cheese and enjoy.

name: Berry Pink Power Smoothie
description: Packed with berries, banana and a hit of lime, this is the smoothie that’ll put a spring in your step. Creamy, punchy and full of goodness.
instructions: Add the strawberries, 50g of the raspberries, cherries, banana, almond milk, yoghurt and protein powder to a blender. Grate in the zest of the lime and then squeeze in the juice.
Blitz until smooth. Pour into a glass.
Crush the remaining 25g frozen raspberries with the back of a spoon, then spoon over the top. Serve straight away – cold, creamy and berry-packed.

name: Berry Pink Power Smoothie Bowl
description: Thick, fruity and protein-packed. This one’s for smoothie bowl lovers who like theirs with a spoon and stacked with toppings.
instructions: Chuck the frozen strawberries, raspberries, cherries and banana into a blender with the almond milk, yoghurt, protein powder, lime juice and chia seeds.

Start blending on a low speed. Use a tamper to push the mixture down towards the blades – it’ll take a minute to get going. Don’t add more liquid unless you absolutely have to. If it really won’t budge, splash in 10ml more almond milk at a time.
Scoop your thick smoothie into a bowl, then top with whatever you fancy – sliced fruit, coconut flakes, granola, seeds or a drizzle of almond butter.

name: Berry Swiss Meringue Buttercream
description: A classic silky smooth raspberry buttercream made using egg whites. Perfect for sandwiching between cakes.
instructions: Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise). Add the sugar and egg whites to a heatproof mixing bowl. Cut the butter into cubes and set aside.

Fill a large saucepan ¼ of the way with water and set it over a medium-high heat until simmering. Place the bowl, with the sugar and eggs, on top of the saucepan (the bottom of the bowl shouldn’t touch the water) and whisk constantly until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is hot and no longer grainy to the touch (rub it between your fingers to check).
Transfer the mixture to a stand mixer and beat on the highest speed, until the bowl is completely cool to the touch and you have stiff peaks.

Switch to the paddle attachment (to avoid air bubbles) and add all the soft, cubed butter all at once. It's very important that the butter is soft and the same temperature as the meringue, otherwise you risk the mixture splitting. Leave the mixer on a medium speed until the mixture comes together (it may look split to start with, but don't worry it will come together), then turn down to low until you have a smooth buttercream. Add the berry coulis and whip until incorporated.
If the mixture looks split, don't worry; put the whole bowl in the fridge for 10-15 mins then whip again.

name: Best Ever Cheesy Seedy Scones
description: Are these the best cheese scones you'll ever eat? Why, yes, they are. Thanks for asking. You won't regret getting stuck into this easy scone recipe.
instructions: Dice your butter and put in the freezer for 15 mins, then grate the cheese and finely chop the chives. To a large bowl add flour, salt, black pepper (30 turns on a grinder) and baking powder, bicarb and sugar. Mix well. Get your butter out of the freezer and, using a butter knife, chop into the flour until you have pea-sized pieces — you can also use your hands but you need to work quickly! Make a well in the mixture and add three-quarters of your cheddar cheese along with your chives, mustard powder and buttermilk, folding with a spatula until combined.

Tip out onto a clean surface and form the dough into a circle. Lightly flour the surface and roll the dough into a rectangle about 36 x 18 cm. Fold the top ⅓ of the dough down into the middle, then fold the bottom ⅓ up to cover it, like folding a pamphlet. Turn the dough 90° and using a rolling pin, roll back out into a rectangle around 36 x 18 cm. Repeat. Cut the dough into 6 equal pieces, pop onto a tray, and cover with cling film before putting back into the fridge for 20 mins. Take the cream cheese out of the fridge and bring to room temp.

In the meantime, heat the oven to 220°C. Once the dough has chilled, transfer to a lined baking tray and brush with milk. Sprinkle with the cheese and your chosen seeds or spice mix (the recipe for the everything bagel seasoning is here) and bake for 25-30 mins until golden and cooked through.

Whilst the scones are cooking, finely chop the spring onions and chives. Mix the onions into the cream cheese and save the chives for serving. When the scones are cool enough to handle, spread with cream cheese and sprinkle with chives.

name: Best-Ever Potato Salad
description: Our ultimate potato salad with cornichons and capers for double briney goodness, celery for crunch and boiled eggs. Perfect for a picnic or BBQ.
instructions: Halve any large new potatoes. Put them in a large saucepan of cold salted water and bring to the boil over a medium-high heat. Once boiling, cook for 10 mins until completely tender.
If using eggs, put into a second saucepan of boiling water and cook for 9 mins then drain and rinse to cool under cold water, peel and roughly chop.

Roughly chop the capers and scrape them into a large salad bowl. Finely slice the cornichons, celery, spring onions (both green and white parts) and chives. Keep a handful of the chives back then add everything else to the bowl along with the egg, if using. Measure in the soured cream, mayo and mustard, stir together then season with apple cider vinegar, salt and lots of black pepper to taste.

Once the potatoes are cooked, drain and leave for 5 mins to steam dry then tip into the potato salad base. Give the warm potatoes a good toss so they get thoroughly coated in the dressing. Top with the remaining chives and dig in. Banging.

name: Biang Biang Noodles
description: These noodles are from Shaanxi in China, and although they take some time you will be rewarded with beautifully silky fresh noodles.
instructions: In a large bowl combine the flour, room temperature water and salt with a wooden spoon. Once it starts to form a dough, knead for 5 minutes until smooth. This is a very dry dough, don’t be tempted to add any more water, it should all come together with a bit of elbow grease.

Divide the dough into quarters, and then quarters again. Roll each piece into a small sausage and coat generously with vegetable oil. Place the oily sausages into an oily tray, cover with cling film and allow to rest for a minimum of an hour and a half.
Finely chop the spring onions.
After the dough has rested, start boiling a large pot of water—you’ll need to get the noodles in the pan as soon as they are made.
Start heating the 50ml oil in over medium heat.
Take a log, flatten and roll into a rectangle using a rolling pin. Press in a chopstick to make an indent (this is where you will rip your noodles).

Hold either end of the rectangle, and gently pull whilst you slap the centre onto your work surface. Continue gently pulling and slapping (which creates the signature bang noise). Keep going until you have a long thin noodle.
Rip along the centre and take this to your boiling water—boil for 30 seconds to 1 minute until it floats to the top.
Continue until you have a bowl of noodles—toss them in a teaspoon of sesame oil to prevent sticking!
Blanch the pak choi in the same noodle water for 30 seconds.
Take out 4 small bowls and start prepping the toppings.

In each bowl, on top of the noodles, grate in a clove of garlic and 1 cm of ginger. Add in each; 1 tablespoon chopped spring onion, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 teaspoon chilli powder and 1 tablespoon dark Chinese vinegar - add the greens to the side of the bowl.
Pour a few tablespoons of your (now smoking hot) oil onto the noodles—aiming for the garlic and chilli powder.
Quickly mix up the noodles and eat immediately!

name: Big Boy Bhaji Burger
description: These bhaji burgers are the one. The fresh homemade coconut raita is delicious!
instructions: Grab a bowl. Add finely sliced red onions, cumin seeds, garam masala and ground coriander. Add tsp grated ginger, a tbsp of chopped coriander stalks, baking powder, gram flour, salt, and 6 tbsp of water. Mix everything together until it resembles a chunky oniony batter.

Make your raita. Grab a bowl. Add coconut yogurt, a large handful of grated cucumber (squeeze gratings to get rid of excess water), a handful of chopped mint and coriander, salt and pepper. Mix everything together.
Heat some vegetable oil in a pan. Add a tablespoon of your bhaji batter. Flatten it out and fry for 3 minutes on each side until golden brown. Cook 2 bhajis per burger.
Cut your bap in half and whack it under the grill to toast it.
Assemble time. Add a big dollop of raita to the bap. Add a bhaji. More raita and another bhaji. Top with a big dollop of mango chutney and the remaining mint leaves.

name: Big Daddy Dhansak
description: The cardamom really brings the fragrance to this Indian classic. Lentils never tasted so good...
instructions: Finely chop your onion, a large knob of ginger, green chillies and garlic cloves. Dice your chicken thighs into bite-size pieces.
Place a large frying pan on the heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil. Add your chopped onion. Add garam masala and bashed cardamom pods. Mix together.
Add your ginger, green chillies and garlic. Cook for a further 2 minutes, making sure everything is coated in the spices. Add your chicken thighs.
Cook the meat on a medium to high heat until it starts to brown. Add red split lentils. Mix together.

Add two tins of chopped tomatoes and crumble in a chicken stock cube. Fill each tin ¾ of the way with water and add that too. Season with salt and pepper, stir, and cover. Leave on a low heat for 35 minutes.
Remove the lid and give the curry a good mix to prevent lentils from sticking. Add a large handful of chopped coriander and remove the curry from the heat.
Add 2 big tablespoons of plain yoghurt and fold it through the curry. Serve whilst hot with extra coriander leaves scattered on top. Enjoy!

name: Big Fat Greek-ish Salad
description: Watermelon salad meets Greek salad – the best of both worlds in one dish. Super fresh and the perfect salad for summer.
instructions: Cook the quinoa according to packaging instructions, let it cool down.
Peel and finely dice the shallots. Add them into a large mixing bowl with juice of the limes and 3 tbsp of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, mix together and let the shallots pickle.
Place a small frying pan on medium heat, add the sunflower seeds and cook, stirring until toasted, 3-5 mins. Tip into the shallot dressing.

Meanwhile, strip the cavolo nero leaves off, discard the stalks. Trim and chop the watermelon into slices, then chop into cubes, discarding the rind. Trim, halve, scoop the seeds out and chop the cucumber into 1cm half moons. Chop the tomatoes into 3cm chunks.
Add the cavolo nero into the dressing, toss and massage together until wilted. Add the rest of the veg into the dressing with the quinoa. Pick the mint leaves and add into the salad, toss together.
Share the salad between plates and crumble feta over. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Big Fat Miso Tofu Noodles
description: A silky tofu-miso broth poured over bouncy noodles, jammy eggs and crunchy greens. Big flavours. Barely any effort.
instructions: Cut the tenderstem broccoli in half lengthways.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil, then gently lower in the eggs and cook for 7 mins. Drain and cool under running water. Once cool enough to handle, peel and set aside.
Bring another pan of salted water to the boil. Add the noodles, broccoli and edamame, then cook following the noodle pack instructions. Drain and set aside.
Add the silken tofu and water to a blender and blitz until smooth. Pour into a saucepan set over a medium heat, then stir in the stock cube until fully dissolved.

Place the miso into a small sieve and dip it into the hot tofu broth. Use the back of a spoon to stir and dissolve the miso into the soup. Season with soy sauce, rice vinegar, salt and black pepper to taste.
Thinly slice the spring onions.

To serve, divide the noodles and edamame between bowls, then ladle over the hot miso broth. Halve the eggs and pop them on top. Finish with a scattering of spring onion, sesame seeds and a pinch of shichimi togarashi or chilli flakes, if using.

name: Big Fat Tomato & Ginger Salad
description: This tart and lip-puckering salad is a main all by itself. Make sure to use fresh, quality tomatoes – it'll make all the difference.
instructions: Bring a small pot of water to the boil and carefully lower in the eggs one by one. Set a timer for 7 mins. When the timer bleeps, pull out the eggs and dunk them into cold water. Carefully crack the shells all over and peel the eggs. Roll them in the sesame seeds and then sit them back into the egg box for ease and crack on with the rest of the recipe.

Cook the microwave rice and leave to cool. Very finely dice the onion and cut the tomatoes into random chunks, all shapes and sizes. Toss into a big bowl and season generously with salt and pepper. Add the ginger brine and plenty of olive oil. Leave to hang out for 7-8 mins.

Pick the basil leaves, chunk-up the cucumber and thinly slice the celery and mangetout on the diagonal. Toss through the marinated tomatoes and taste. Adjust the seasoning and add a splash more ginger brine or olive oil if you need to.

Mix the microwave rice through the salad and spread out onto a large sharing platter. Halve the eggs you prepared earlier, and place them on top of the salad and drizzle over the chilli oil and pickled ginger. Sprinkle over the peanuts to finish.

name: Big Green Noodles
description: These easy noodles are going to become a regular in your household. Just you wait.  They're healthy, delicious, and beyond easy to make.
instructions: Heat a splash of neutral oil in a large frying pan and fry the curry paste for 2 mins before transferring to a food processor with the coconut milk, spinach and half the coriander. Blitz until smooth and season generously with lime juice, salt and pepper. Set aside.

Get a big saucepan of salted water onto the boil. Chop your broccoli into 2cm pieces, then chuck into the boiling water and cook for 1 min before adding the noodles. Cook for a further 2-3 mins until the noodles are al dente. Drain, saving some of the cooking water.

Put the noodles and broccoli back into the frying pan with a splash of the cooking water, then pour over the green sauce. Mix well to heat through. Pile into bowls, then top with chilli oil, sesame seeds and more coriander, if you like.

name: Big Lentil Salad Bowl
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A high-protein salad bowl that's packed with fibre. The fudgy aubergines? Unbeatable.
keywords: Big Lentil Salad Bowl With Aubergine Dip
Big Lentil Salad Bowl With Aubergine Dip recipe
ingredients: 250g Worldwide Foods Good Grains French Inspired Lentils
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Trim and chop the aubergine into 2cm chunks. Transfer to a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, season and toss well. Bake for 20-25 mins until softened and golden.
Meanwhile, bring a saucepan full of water to the boil. Once boiling, gently drop the eggs in, turn the heat down slightly to a gentle simmer and cook for 7 mins until jammy.
Add all the dressing ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. Set aside.

Reheat the lentil and quinoa pouches, then tip both into a large bowl. Pick the parsley leaves and finely chop the stems, then add to the bowl along with the olives. Tip in the cooked aubergine and half the dressing. Toss to combine.
Add a dollop of hummus to four serving bowls. Spread it out, then top with the salad and a jammy egg. Finish with a drizzle of dressing.

name: Bimini's Spiced Chickpea Burger
description: A recipe you'll want to return to time and time again. This vegan spiced chickpea burger was made for us by cultural icon Bimini.
instructions: Finely chop the onions. Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add a splash of oil. Add the onion and fry for 5 mins until soft.
Finely slice the garlic, add to the pan with the tomato purée and cook for another 2 mins.
Remove from the heat and set aside.

Drain the chickpeas and add half of them to a food processor along with a tbsp of olive oil, the curry powder, 3 tbsp of the flour, breadcrumbs, 2 tsp of salt, the juice of half a lemon and a handful of the parsley. Pulse until it looks like chunky hummus.
Add the remaining chickpeas to a bowl, mash gently with a fork so that they’re just slightly broken up. Add the contents of the food processor and the onions to the same bowl and mix to combine.
Form the mixture into 4 large patties, they should be about 4cm tall. Dust a baking tray with the remaining 2 tbsp of flour and place the patties onto the tray. Chill in the fridge for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl mix the mayonnaise and sriracha together and set aside.
Half the burger buns and toast them. Roughly chop the remaining parsley and mint. Slice the pickles. Spread both sides of the buns with the sriracha mayo.

When ready to cook, heat a cm of neutral oil in a large frying pan over a medium high heat. Once the oil starts to shimmer, add the patties and cook for about 3 or 4 mins on each side until golden. Don’t move them too soon as you want to form a nice crust on each side.

Remove the patties from the pan and add to the bottom half of the bun. Top with a few slices of pickle, a sprinkle of the chopped herbs and an extra drizzle of sriracha, if you like. Pop the top of the bun on and you’re good to go. Enjoy!

name: Birria Tacos
description: This birria tacos recipe is a show stopper at any get together. Tender, fall-apart beef short ribs are slow-cooked in a rich, flavourful broth infused with guajillo peppers, chipotle chillies, and adobo sauce. These tacos are guaranteed to hit the spot.
instructions: Roughly chop the white onion, garlic and the tomatoes for the sauce. Remove the seeds and stems from the dried chillies.
Heat a glug of oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan. Add the beef and sear for 2 mins on every side until nicely browned. Remove the meat to a plate and set aside.

Add the onions to the pot and sauté in the beef fat for 5 mins (add a splash more oil if needed). Add in the garlic, bay leaves, cumin, peppercorns, oregano and your dried chillies. Sauté for 3 mins until fragrant and the spices are toasted.
Add the tomatoes and the stock. Bring to a boil and cook for 30 mins. Blend everything in a blender.
Return the meat to the pan and top it up with more water if needed so that all the meat is submerged. Simmer with the lid on for a minimum of 4 hours, up to 24 hours.
For the salsa, dice up the tomatoes, red onion and chop up the coriander. Mix it in a bowl with a squeeze of lime and salt.
Shred the mozzarella and slice up the remaining limes into wedges.
Take the meat out of the stew and roughly shred it, place it into another saucepan with a few ladles of sauce to keep it warm. Generously season the broth and meat with salt.

Heat a frying pan and dip a corn tortilla into the broth and place it onto the hot pan. Sprinkle a layer of meat and then a layer of shredded cheese. Close the taco and cook gently to melt the cheese and crisp up the shell. Repeat for all the tacos and enjoy with a squeeze of lime, fresh salsa and dipped in the gorgeous broth.

name: Biscoff Baked Oats
description: If you have a sweet tooth, these Biscoff baked oats are for you. It’s essentially cake for breakfast, although who says you can only have it for breakfast!? Plus it’s high in fibre and protein, so will help you to stay fuller for longer and energised throughout the day.
instructions: Heat the oven to 175°C. Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolk (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise). Measure 1 tablespoon of egg white per serving.
Combine the oats, banana, egg whites, milk, protein powder, baking powder, cinnamon and a pinch of salt in a blender, then blend until smooth.
Spray a baking dish with oil spray or rub with coconut oil, then pour in the mixture.
Melt a third of the Biscoff spread for 10-15 seconds in the microwave and pour it in the dish. Swirl it around into the batter with a skewer, toothpick or the tip of a knife.

Add another third of the biscoff spread (not melted) into the centre of the mixture, smoothing the oats over the top so it’s in the middle of the mixture. Bake for 15-20 mins, or until you can insert the skewer and have it come out clean.
Melt the remaining Biscoff spread and drizzle on top, followed by half a Lotus biscuit.

name: Biscoff Espresso Martini
description: An unholy marriage between the best spread and James Bond’s second-favourite cocktail is what creates this unhinged beverage: the Biscoff Espresso Martini.
instructions: Crush up the Biscoff biscuits in a pestle and mortar.
Gently spread a small amount of the Biscoff spread around the rim of your glass and rub it in the biscuit crumbs.
In a cocktail shaker, add the ice, vodka, Frangelico, Kahlúa, espresso, and the Biscoff spread.
Shake for a minute and a half or until a frost forms on the shaker.
Double-strain the mix into your Biscoff-rimmed glass.

name: Black Bean Aubergine Dal
description: You won't believe how much flavour is imparted into this black bean aubergine dal in just half an hour.
instructions: Cut the aubergines into medium-sized chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Get a large, deep frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the aubergine chunks and cook, stirring regularly, for 5 mins until the aubergine is beginning to char and soften in places.
Add ½ oil and keep cooking the aubergine for a further 5 mins, stirring regularly, until the aubergine is mostly softened.
Finely grate the ginger and garlic.

Add the grated ginger and garlic to the softened aubergines along with the curry powder, ½ of the cumin seeds and ½ of the coriander seeds. Cook, stirring for 2 mins then tip in the black beans along with their liquid as well as the coconut milk.
Simmer the black bean dal for 10 mins until the aubergine is fully cooked and the beans are nice and tender.

Meanwhile, get a second frying pan super hot. Once hot, add in the whole cherry tomatoes and cook for 4-5 minutes until blackened in places and beginning to burst. At this point add the remaining oil, remaining ½ of cumin seeds and ½ of coriander seeds. Toast for a minute then remove from the heat and season.
Roughly mash half the dal in the saucepan with a potato masher, then stir the dal well. Season to taste.
Divide the dal between bowls. Top with a spoonful of yoghurt, the charred tomatoes, and coriander. Serve with rice or naan, if you like.

name: Black Bean Curry with Juicy Lamb Meatballs & Coconut Sambal
description: Dal makhani-inspired black beans simmered until thick and deeply spiced, with juicy lamb meatballs and a spicy, toasted coconut sambal. A banging high protein weeknight meal.
keywords: Curried Black Beans with Lamb Meatballs & Coconut Sambal
Curried Black Beans with Lamb Meatballs & Coconut Sambal recipe
instructions: Add the breadcrumbs and the water to a large bowl and mix until combined. Add the lamb mince and season with salt and black pepper. Mix with your hands until smooth, then roll into golf ball-sized balls. Finely mince the garlic and grate the ginger.Top Tip: Rolling meatballs is easier when the meat mixture is a little bit cold. Start with fridge-temperature mince and wet your hands with a bit of water as you go.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large, deep frying pan over a medium heat. Add the meatballs and fry for 6–8 mins, turning regularly, until golden brown all over. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

In the same pan, add the cumin seeds, garlic and ginger. Fry for 1 min until fragrant, then add the tomato purée and fry for another 2 mins, stirring, until it starts to darken. Add the garam masala, chilli powder and the black beans along with all their liquid. Rinse one of the cans with water and add to the pan. Season with salt and cook for 15 mins, stirring frequently and adding a splash of water if it starts to dry out.

Meanwhile, make the sambal. Add the shallot, chillies and garlic to a food processor and blitz until finely minced. Set a small frying pan over a medium heat, add the coconut and toast for 2–3 mins, stirring often, until golden brown. Set aside. Add the vegetable oil to the pan and fry the minced mixture for 2–3 mins until it loses its rawness. Add the toasted coconut back in, season with salt and a generous pinch of sugar and mix to combine. Set aside.
Stir the yoghurt into the beans and turn the heat down to low. Nestle the meatballs back in, cover and cook for a further 10 mins until the meatballs are cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
To serve, spoon into bowls, finish with a dollop of yoghurt and scatter over the coconut sambal. Squeeze over the lime and serve with the naan.

name: Black Bean Makhani Dal
description: Dal makhani is the Godfather of all dals. This opulent dish from Sarah Woods is rich and decadent and bows to no other.
instructions: First cook the brown lentils – you’ll need a large lidded saucepan. Brown lentils don’t often need a soak and will cook in under 30 mins. Read the packet instructions, and cook until tender (please don’t overcook them into a mush). You need three to four times the volume of water to lentils. Bring to a rapid boil, then reduce to a simmer. Skim off any scum, and don’t allow the pan to go dry. Remove from the heat, and set aside.

Toast the coriander seeds in a dry frying pan and transfer to a pestle and mortar. Lightly grind – they’ll still have some texture – and set aside. Add your cardamom seeds to the mortar, with a pinch of salt to act as an abrasive, and grind to a powder.

Now make the tarka, the foundation of every curry. In a large sauté pan or similar, activate your whole spices – cumin seeds, cassia bark, cloves, dried chilli and star anise – in 3 or 4 tablespoons of oil on a medium to high heat. Dice the onion, finely grate the ginger and garlic and mince the chilli.

When the fragrant aromas waft up, tip in the onions, the crushed coriander and powdered cardamom, and reduce the heat to medium. Give these at least 10 mins or so to allow the onions to soften and become translucent.

Next add the ginger, garlic and chilli, cook for a couple of mins, then add the salt and garam masala. Toast for 30 seconds, then drop in half of the butter (this will prevent the masala from catching). Once melted, add the tomato purée and give everything a good mix. We want a few mins to cook the purée out. Add 1/3 of the water to help it on its way.

Add the passata and bring to the boil, then simmer for a few mins. When you see the tell-tale sign of the oil separating on the surface, it’s time to taste and make your adjustments. Though it will taste salty at this point, you are likely to need more salt when the lentils and beans have been added.

Stir all your cooked lentils and beans through the tarka. You’ll need to add the rest of water too. Ensure everything is mixed well, then bring to the boil and immediately reduce to a simmer. Taste again now, you’ll probably need more salt. Add the methi (dried fenugreek), the rest of the butter, yoghurt and cream. You may want to hold some of the cream back for a decorative swirl just before serving. Allow to simmer for a little longer and for all of the flavours to develop – say another 10 mins or so.
Pair with whichever bread takes your fancy, or with rice. We like to serve it with black cardamom rice, charred aloo gobi, yoghurt and a crunchy slaw.

name: Black Bean Soup
description: Hearty and creamy black bean soup with a smoky chipotle kick. The perfect nutritious weeknight dinner when you’re craving comfort.
instructions: Peel and finely dice the onion. Finely slice the garlic. Place a saucepan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the onion, garlic and chipotle paste, then cook for 3-4 mins until softened and translucent. Stir through the tomato purée and cook, stirring, for 2-3 mins until darkened.

Pour in the stock and black beans (with their liquid). Using a masher, mash half of the beans. Let the soup simmer for 15-20 mins, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Taste and season with salt if needed.
Meanwhile, slice the radishes into thin matchsticks. Thinly slice the jalapeño.
Share the soup between bowls, then top with the radishes, tomato salsa, soured cream and jalapeño.

name: Black Bean Stew With Nutty Sprinkle
description: A rich, nutty, spicy black bean dish inspired by Mole Poblano, served with tangy feta drizzle. To scoop up with tortilla crisps.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the onions, then mince the garlic. Add the raisins into a bowl and cover with boiling water. Add half of the onions into a bowl and squeeze over the juice of ⅔ of the limes, season with salt.

Place a frying pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the remaining onion and stir-fry for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the garlic, oregano and cinnamon, cook for 1 min until fragrant. Pour the black beans and their liquid from the cans into the mixture with the water. Stir, bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to low. Simmer for 10-15 mins until creamy, stirring occasionally.

Meanwhile, roughly chop the almonds. Place a small frying pan over a medium heat, add the sesame seeds and almonds, toast for 2-4 mins until golden. Transfer the almonds and sesame seeds to a bowl, then drain the raisins and add them in, too. Zest ¼ of a lime into the seeds and toss to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir the dark chocolate and chipotle paste into the black beans and simmer on low for 2-3 mins. Taste and season with salt and pepper, adding a splash of water if needed.

Discard the cinnamon stick, then share the black bean stew between bowls. Top with Feta, the nutty sprinkle and pickled red onions. Serve with a wedge of lime and scoop the mole up with tortilla crisps.

name: Black Bean and Chorizo Toastie
description: This smoky toastie is packed with crisp chorizo, spicy black beans and lots of cheese. It’s kind of like a quesadilla, but without the wrap, and it’s delicious!
instructions: Finely chop the chorizo, onion, garlic and red chilli.

Get the chorizo in a pan with a splash of olive oil and set over a medium heat. Cook until some of the fat has rendered out and the chorizo is beginning to crisp, then add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the garlic, red chilli, smoked paprika and ground cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Drain the black beans and add them to the pan with 300ml water. Season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid has evaporated.
Finely chop the fresh coriander and add it to the pan. Stir to combine and adjust the salt level to your liking. Leave to cool.
Meanwhile, grate the Cheddar.
Spread the chorizo beans onto 4 of the sourdough slices. Top with the grated Cheddar and the other 4 slices of sourdough. Spread the outside with mayonnaise
Cook over a medium/medium-low heat for 4 mins on each side, or until golden brown on the outside and melty in the middle, then plate up and serve hot - enjoy!

name: Black Beans de la Olla
description: Black Beans de la Olla, or Beans from the Pot. There is nothing more Mexican than cooking beans from scratch. I think every family in Mexico has a day for doing this – in my family it’s every Monday. They are called “de la olla” because, traditionally, the beans are cooked in a clay pot. As a child, this was one of my favourite dishes. My mum used to cook them early in the morning and she would serve them in a bowl with a bit of the juice, garnished with coriander, onion, queso fresco and spicy salsa or fresh serranos. Then she would freeze the leftover beans and use them throughout the week to make fried beans.
keywords: Black Beans de la Olla Recipe
instructions: Pour the beans into a large bowl and remove the broken ones. Cover with cold water (not the water specified in the ingredients list – just enough to cover the beans) and set aside to soak for 2 hrs.

Once soaked, drain the beans and transfer them to a large pan. Pour over the cold water (the water listed in the ingredients list) and add the epazote leaves, onion and garlic. Set the pan over a medium-high heat and bring the water to a boil, then lower the heat to low, cover with lid and simmer for one hour until the beans are soft.
While the beans have almost finished cooking, prep your garnishes of choice. Dice some fresh coriander, avocado and/or onion. Crumble some queso fresco. Get some spicy salsa at the ready.
When the beans are done, add the salt and cook for a final 5 mins. To serve, ladle up a portion of beans with some of their broth. Top with the garnishes!

name: Black Garlic & Feta Orzo
description: You’ve seen it all over TikTok, and in true MOB-style, we've made our version with orzo and spiked it with black garlic for an extra allium punch.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C.
Drop your baby plum tomatoes into a large baking tray so they are all lying flat and pop your block of feta on top.
In a bowl combine your black garlic paste, oregano, chilli flakes, red wine vinegar, a pinch of salt, few cracks of black pepper and olive oil.
Pour your olive oil sauce over the feta and tomatoes and bake in the oven for 40 mins.
Cook your orzo for 6 mins in boiling, salted water. Drain, reserving some of the cooking water.
Mash up the tomatoes and feta with a fork to form a creamy sauce. Pour on your cooked orzo and mix well, add some pasta water to loosen the sauce if needed, mixing well until glossy.
Serve the orzo in bowls. Tear over your basil leaves and sprinkle with pine nuts.

name: Black Olive Pesto Linguine
description: A cross between a tapenade and a pesto, this black olive pesto is briny and super savoury. We've served it with linguine here but you can use it for all sorts of delicious dishes: pastas, salads, sandwiches, the possibilities are endless!
instructions: Cook the linguine in salted boiling water following packet instructions.

Add the sun-dried black olives and toasted pine nuts to a blender. Peel the garlic clove and roughly slice the Parmesan, then add in. Add juice of your lemon and season generously with salt and pepper. Add the squid ink, if using.
Add ⅓ of olive oil and begin to blend, then continue to add olive oil until you get to a thick pesto consistency.
Drain the cooked linguine, reserving a cup of the cooking pasta, and return the linguine to the pan. Stir through the pesto, add a splash of cooking water and mix until thoroughly combined.
Divide the pasta between bowls and top with some fresh parsley and extra Parmesan, if you like.

name: Black Pepper Chicken & Lentil Rice
description: Inspired by the Palestinian dish Musakhan, which I first discovered at Akub, one of my fave restaurants in London. The simple flavours and that bright tang of sumac made it incredibly comforting, but somehow still light. This is my quick take on it: sumac and cracked black pepper grilled chicken, glazed with honey. Hopefully it brings a bit of brightness to your table too.
keywords: Tangy Black Pepper Chicken & Lentil Rice
Tangy Black Pepper Chicken & Lentil Rice recipe
ingredients: 1 x 250g Pouchx 250g Pouch Cooked Puy Lentils
instructions: Heat the oven grill to high. Chop the aubergine and chicken thighs into 2-3cm chunks and thinly slice the red onion.
Add the chicken and aubergine to a large bowl with a generous amount of salt, the sumac, the black pepper and the olive oil, tossing to coat.

Scatter the red onion over a baking tray and cover with the chicken and aubergine. Slide under the grill for 10-15 mins, until golden and cooked through. If it's charring too quickly, bring the tray down a level. Every grill is different, so check at 7 mins and keep an eye on it.
Once cooked, drizzle the honey over the chicken, toss together and slide back under the grill for 2-5 mins, until glazed and sticky.
Meanwhile, thinly slice most of the parsley and add to a bowl. Coarsely grate the cucumber on top, then stir the skyr through. Season with salt, black pepper and the zest and juice of the lemon.
Heat the rice and lentils according to the packet instructions, toss together, then fluff with a fork.

Divide the rice and lentils between boxes or plates and top with the chicken and aubergine and a dollop of the herby skyr. Scatter over the remaining parsley and divide the remaining lemon into wedges to serve.

name: Black Pepper Tofu
description: The butter & the pepper is a combo made in heaven. Warms you all the way down to your toes
instructions: Chop tofu into cubes then coat in cornflour.
Add vegetable oil to a wok over a medium-high heat. Fry the tofu until golden and set aside to drain on kitchen paper.
Get your rice on (follow pack instructions).
Clean your wok. Place on heat and add the rest of your oil. Add 1/2 the butter followed by the chopped garlic and ginger. Fry until softened.

Crush your peppercorns in a pestle and mortar, or grind the correct amount using your pepper mill. Add to the wok along with the sugar. Mix together. Once the sugar has dissolved, add your soy sauce and stir again.
Finely slice the red chilli, add to the wok and mix, then add the tofu back in. Add the remaining butter and melt, mix well to coat.
Serve the tofu on top of a mound of steaming rice, garnish with chopped spring onions and sesame seeds.

name: Black Rice with Crunchy Greens & Miso Dressing
description: This satisfying dish is delicious when it's hot and cold, so do your future self a favour and make some extra for lunch.
instructions: Put the rice in a pan with plenty of water and bring to the boil. Once boiling, simmer for 18 mins and turn off the heat. Then drain the rice in a colander, put the colander over the saucepan and cover with a tea towel to steam until you are ready to serve.

To make the dressing, add your cashews, ginger, rapeseed oil, 4 tbsp of lemon juice, miso, maple syrup and 100ml of water into a blender and blend until smooth. Taste and adjust the amount of lemon, miso and salt to your taste.

Finely slice the chilli, spring onions, and radishes and set them aside. Now you're going to want to finely slice the cabbage and place it in a small bowl with a good squeeze of lemon and some salt. Massage the cabbage until it starts to wilt. Set aside.

Add some water into a frying pan, just enough to cover the bottom of the pan. Add the mangetout and green beans and cover with a lid. Steam for about 2-3 mins until the greens are slightly cooked but still very crunchy and bright.

Cut the tofu into small cubes and heat some vegetable oil in a frying pan. Stir fry the tofu until it starts to crisp up, then add a splash of soy sauce and the sesame seeds and fry for a minute or two more.
To serve, layer the rice with the radish, sliced cabbage, peas and greens. Top with tofu and plenty of sauce, then finish with spring onions and chilli.

name: Black Tahini Fudge
description: This spooky black tahini fudge is an easy and fun treat for Halloween. You’ll need a high-speed food processor for this recipe.
ingredients: Black And White Sesame Seed (to serve)
instructions: Soak the cashews in boiling water and set aside.
Toast the black sesame seeds on medium heat in a dry pan until they start to pop. They should turn to dust if you rub them between your fingers, if not, toast them for a little longer.
While they are still hot, add the sesame seeds and sunflower oil to the food processor and blend for 7-10 mins. Scrape down the sides often. Keep blending until you have a smooth paste.

Melt the coconut oil on the hob or in the microwave. 
Drain the cashews and add these to the food processor along with the vanilla extract, salt, maple syrup and coconut oil. 
Blend for 5-7 mins or until smooth. Add a little water if needed.

Take a small cake tin or tupperware and line it with baking paper on the bottom. Add the tahini mixture to the tin and smooth out the top as best you can. Running a wet spatula along the top helps to get it smooth.
Cover and freeze the mixture for at least 3 hours.
Remove and allow to thaw for 10 mins to get the block out or pop it into a bigger tray with boiling water for a few seconds – this will loosen the sides enough to get it out.
Cut into squares and serve immediately or keep in the freezer until ready.
This fudge might start to melt slightly if left out for too long, so these are best served straight from the freezer.
Keep in a sealed container in the freezer for up to a month.

name: Black Velvet Cocktail Recipe
description: If you've never heard of a Black Velvet, it's a classic cocktail made from the simple yet intriguing combination of sparkling wine and stout beer. Traditionally, these two ingredients create a rich, velvety drink that's both refreshing and darkly indulgent. This version takes things up a notch by adding Kahlúa, the iconic coffee liqueur, for an extra layer of depth and sweetness. The addition of Kahlúa brings subtle coffee and caramel notes that blend perfectly with the stout's roasted flavours and the crisp, bubbly finish of sparkling wine. Whether you're a fan of rich stouts, love the sophistication of sparkling wine, or crave a hint of coffee in your cocktails, this twist on the Black Velvet is sure to impress. Perfect for special occasions or a cozy night in, this cocktail offers a deliciously bold and balanced flavour profile that’s as indulgent as it is easy to make.
instructions: Grab a tall, chilled glass and pour in your stout.
Add the Kahlúa and top up with sparkling wine.
If you like it a little sweeter, add a drop more Kahlúa.

name: Blackberry, Pear & Pine Nut Crumble
description: This might just be the perfect dessert for the colder months. Who doesn’t love a crumble?
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan and line a baking tray with baking paper.  Ensure your butter is very cold. Cut the cold butter into cubes.

To make the oaty crumble topping, put all the ingredients and a pinch of sea salt into a bowl and rub together with your fingers to form breadcrumbs. Spread the mixture on the lined baking tray and put into the freezer for 10 mins (this will firm up the butter that you’ve softened with your hands). Remove and set aside.

Meanwhile, core, peel and slice the pears lengthways into 1.5cm thick slices. Add the sliced pears and the sugar to a heavy-bottomed pan and cook gently over a medium heat until the fruit begins to soften and starts releasing its juice – approximately 7 mins, depending on the ripeness of your fruit. Add the blackberries and bring to the boil. Spoon into a 30 x 20cm pie dish.

Allow the fruit to cool just slightly, then sprinkle the oaty crumble mix evenly over the top of the fruit (break up the crumble with your hands if necessary). 
Then scatter over the pine nuts.
Bake for 20-25 mins, or until the pine nuts are starting to turn a light golden brown. Serve hot with custard, ice cream, double cream or yoghurt.

name: Blackcurrant & Lemon Friands
description: These gluten-free almond friands are chewy, moist and oh-so light. Delicious eaten fresh from the oven.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan assisted/gas mark 6. Grease a 12-hole cupcake or muffin tray with butter or oil spray (a silicone tray is best).
Melt the butter in a small saucepan over a low heat then leave to cool and set aside.
Sift the flour and icing sugar into a bowl and whisk together, then whisk in the salt and ground almonds, and zest in the lemons.

Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise, or dressing). In a separate bowl, use an electric whisk to beat the egg whites until thick and glossy with stiff peaks forming. Using a spoon, very gently fold the egg whites into the flour and icing sugar mix, then lightly stir in the melted butter. It should come together into a batter.

Spoon the mixture evenly into your prepared cupcake or muffin tray and press a few of the berries into each one. Scatter all over with the flaked almonds and bake for 15–20 mins, or until a cocktail stick inserted into the centre comes out clean (avoid skewering the fruit, as this may result in the stick coming out clean before it’s baked properly).
Allow to cool in the tin for 10 mins before transferring on to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Blackened Cod & Chickpea Smacked Cucumber Salad
description: A punchy, protein-packed salad topped with charred miso-glazed cod. Full of crunch, zing & savoury flavour. This one's going to become a regular fixture on the dinner table.
instructions: Mix the white miso and honey together in a small bowl, then rub it all over the cod fillets. Leave to marinate in the fridge for at least 30 mins — ideally up to 5 hours.

Trim the cucumber and cut it into quarters, widthways. Use a rolling pin or something heavy to smack the cucumber until it splits, then chop into rough 2cm chunks. Thinly slice the celery. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems.
Once the cod has marinated, remove it from the fridge and let it come to room temperature. Heat the grill to high.

Line a baking tray with foil, place the cod fillets on top and slide under the grill for 6–10 mins until cooked through and starting to char. If the marinade is catching too quickly, move the tray down a shelf or lower the grill temperature slightly.
While the cod is grilling, stir all the dressing ingredients together in a bowl.
Once the fish is cooked, toss the chickpeas, cucumber, celery, coriander and quinoa into the dressing and mix well. Share the salad between plates and top with the blackened cod.

name: Blackened Cod Tacos With Jalapeño Crema
description: These quick fish tacos are unbelievably easy to make, and even easier to eat. High protein, low effort.
keywords: Blackened Cod Tacos With Jalapeño Crema
Blackened Cod Tacos With Jalapeño Crema recipe
instructions: Add the taco seasoning, brown sugar and a big pinch of salt to a mixing bowl. Pour in the olive oil and stir to combine. Pat the cod dry and coat it in the marinade.

To cook, place a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the cod and fry for 3 mins on each side until blackened and flaky. Alternatively, air-fry at max temp for 6–8 mins until cooked through.

Meanwhile, make the crema. Roughly chop the coriander and add it to a blender with a third of the yoghurt, pickled jalapeños, lime juice and a pinch of salt. Blend until smooth. Add the remaining yoghurt and gently pulse to incorporate.
Finely shred the cabbage.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 10–20 seconds on each side until soft and golden.
To serve, fill the tortillas with shredded cabbage, chunks of blackened cod and a good drizzle of jalapeño crema. Serve with lime wedges.

name: Blackened Cod with Herby Miso Soba Noodles
description: This herby miso soup with sticky blackened cod is high in protein, quick to make and big in flavour. Perfect when you want a simple and nourishing meal.
keywords: Blackened Cod with Herby Miso Soba
instructions: For the miso marinade, heat a small pan over a medium heat. Add the miso, tamari and honey with a little splash of water and mix to combine. Bring to the boil then reduce to a simmer for about 5 mins until thick and dark. Remove from the heat and leave to cool.
Add the fish to a baking dish and pour over the miso marinade. Cover and leave in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Cook the soba noodles (and edamame if using from frozen) following pack instructions. Finely chop the spring onions, coriander and chives.
Heat the grill to the highest setting. Place the fish on a baking tray and grill on the highest shelf for 6 mins until cooked through and starting to caramelise.

Meanwhile, heat a splash of sesame oil in a saucepan over a medium heat and grate in the ginger. Cook for a minute then add the water. Put a small sieve over the saucepan so the bottom is submerged in the water. Add the miso to the sieve and use a spoon to press the miso through to the water below. This will emulsify the miso and flavour the broth.
Add the edamame beans, spring onions and herbs to the broth and squeeze in the juice of ½ your limes.
To serve, divide the broth between bowls and top with the noodles and cod. Sprinkle over the sesame seeds and finish with an extra squeeze of lime.

name: Blackened Leeks & Nutty Chipotle Salsa
description: Soft, charred leeks on creamy ricotta, served with smoky, nutty salsa inspired by salsa macha.
keywords: Blackened Leeks & Nutty Chipotle Salsa recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Finely chop the pumpkin seeds and peanuts. Add into a frying pan with the sesame seeds and the oil. Place over medium heat and cook for 2-4 mins until the nuts and seeds have toasted. Stir through the chipotle and oregano, then remove from the heat. Transfer to a bowl and allow to cool. Taste and season with lime juice and salt, then set aside.

Trim and peel the first few tough layers off the leeks. Char the leeks on a gas hob or under the grill. As the leeks begin to cook, the skin will start to blacken. Once the skin is charred, peel some of the char off then place the leeks onto a baking tray lined with foil, then roast in the oven for 20-25 mins until softened.
Finely mince the parsley, stalks and all. Stir through the ricotta and season with salt and pepper. Cut the leeks into thirds and peel the burnt layers off.
Spoon the ricotta onto a sharing platter or plate, place the leeks on top and drizzle over the nutty salsa.

name: Blackened Salmon With Smashed Cucumber Salad
description: We love salmon and we love cucumbers. Put them together and you get this fresh, flavourful dinner recipe.
keywords: Blackened Salmon With Smashed Cuke Salad
instructions: Check the salmon for any scales, and score the skin in 2-3 cm intervals. Season the salmon all over with salt and set aside for 30 mins in the fridge.

While the salmon is salting, Cook off your rice according to the package instructions. Keep warm on the side. Grab your cucumbers and bash with a rolling pin or small saucepan into smallish chunks. Season with salt and set aside for 15 mins.

Finely grate the garlic into a large bowl and add 1 tbsp of soy, 1 tbsp of sherry vinegar and the chilli oil. Finely slice the spring onions, chuck the white part into the bowl with the dressing. Get the edamame beans in there too.

Pull the salmon out of the fridge and pat dry with kitchen paper. Preheat a large frying pan over a high heat. Add a few tbsp of oil and carefully lay the salmon, skin side down, into the pan. Cook for 3-5 mins until the skin is very crispy and starting to char, flip over and cook for another 1-2 mins, turn off the heat and let the residual heat keep cooking the fish. Tip in the remaining soy and sherry vinegar to deglaze, removing the fish after it’s cooking time. Turn on the heat again and reduce the sauce for 1-2 minutes until thickened and sticky.
Transfer the salmon to a warm serving plate and pour over the soy and vinegar mixture from the pan. Sprinkle with the green tops of the spring onions
Drain any liquid from the cucumbers and toss through the green bean mix and serve alongside the salmon and warm brown rice. Garnish with fresh mint and a squeeze of lime juice.

name: Blistered Courgettes
description: Beautifully blistered coins of courgette that pair great with lean protein and high-fibre grains.
keywords: Blistered Courgettes with Minty Bulgur recipe
instructions: Cut the courgettes into 3-4cm-thick coins.

Preheat a large frying pan and add a good amount of olive oil, enough to almost cover the base of the pan. Season the courgettes with salt and add to the pan, cut-side down. Cook over a high heat for 4-5 mins or until blistered and heavily charred. Carefully flip and cook on the other cut side for 2-3 mins. Remove from the heat and allow the courgettes to sit for 5 mins in the pan, letting the residual heat cook the courgettes through.
Serve the courgette coins with your favourite grain or carbohydrate.

name: Blistered Courgettes with Minty Bulgur
description: Beautifully blistered coins of courgette on a bed of fresh and minty bulgur wheat. It's exactly what you want to be eating when the sun is shining.
keywords: Blistered Courgettes with Minty Bulgur recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the red onion and chilli and toss into a bowl. Hit them with a good pinch of salt and the juice of a lemon. Scrunch the juice and salt into the veggies and then set aside for 10-15 mins to macerate.

Cut the courgettes into 3-4cm-thick coins and finely grate the garlic. Set both aside. Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Rinse the bulgur wheat a few times with cold water before draining and adding to the boiling water. Cook for 10-12 mins or until just tender. Drain in a sieve and allow to steam for 6-7 mins before adding to a bowl.

Preheat a large frying pan and add a good amount of olive oil, enough to almost cover the base of the pan. Season the courgettes with salt and add to the pan, cut-side down. Cook over a high heat for 4-5 mins or until blistered and heavily charred. Carefully flip and cook on the other cut side for 2-3 mins. Remove from the heat and allow the courgettes to sit for 5 mins in the pan, letting the residual heat cook the courgettes through.

Finely chop all of the parsley and mint and chuck into the warm bulgur wheat with the juice of the other lemon and plenty of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and add the blistered courgettes. Toss together.
Mix the yoghurt with the finely grated garlic clove. Season with salt.
Tip a big pile of the bulgur salad onto a plate and add a handful of the macerated onions and chillies. Finish with a dollop of garlic yoghurt and serve.

name: Blood Orange Campari Spritz
description: Our take on the classic Campari spritz. Bitter, sweet, a little boozy. It's a summer stunner featuring blood orange soda.
instructions: Fill a wine glass with ice cubes.
Squeeze the juice from one of your oranges. Cut the other into rounds.
Pour your campari over your ice, followed by your blood orange juice.
Pour in your blood orange soda, then finish with a slice of blood orange. Serve and enjoy.

name: Blood Orange Shandy
description: This refreshing shandy is zhuzhed up with a twist of blood orange. A great drink for every season.
instructions: Pour your ingredients into a cocktail shaker.
Pour your lager into a glass.
Shake your cocktail shaker vigorously and double-strain it into the glass with your lager.
Garnish with a sprig of mint.

name: Bloody Mary Chicken Salad
description: Whenever I look at the ingredients in a Bloody Mary, I know I like them all, but when I take a sip, I just can’t get on board. So, instead, I’ve made a salad, inspired by the ingredients you find in the iconic cocktail, to make a version that I love and hopefully, whether you're a Bloody Mary lover, or not, you will too.
instructions: Butterfly the chicken breasts. Add the vodka and Worcestershire sauce to a bowl, finely grate in the garlic and season with salt and pepper. Toss the chicken through and leave to marinate for 5 mins while you get everything else ready.
Thinly slice the celery. Halve or chop the tomatoes into 2-3cm chunks and roughly chop the coriander, discarding the tough stems.
Mash the anchovies into a bowl, squeeze in the juice of the lemon, then stir the mayonnaise and mustard through. Season with salt and pepper.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Once hot, cook the chicken for 7-10 mins in batches, turning halfway, or until golden and cooked through. Leave to rest for 2-3 mins, before slicing.

Toss the tomatoes, celery and coriander through the dressing. Share between boxes or onto plates, top with the chicken and finish with the hot sauce. If your making this ahead, it's best to keep the dressing separate and serve when eating.

name: Blooming Onion
description: Double-dipped, deep-fried and delicious. This Blooming Onion has all the qualities of the perfect sharing starter.
instructions: Peel your brown onion and cut off the top and bottom. Using a large knife, slice down the centre of the onion, three quarters of the way down. Be careful not to cut all the way through. Turn the onion 90 degrees and slice again. Repeat the process until you have at least 16 little sections. You should now be able to open up the onion like a flower.
To make the dredge, combine the ingredients in a mixing bowl and whisk to combine. Season with a little salt.
Pour the milk into another bowl. Dust your prepped onion in the dredge, then pass through the milk, and then back into the flour again. Make sure all the sections are thoroughly coated.
Preheat a pot of vegetable oil to 150°C and carefully fry the dredged onion until golden brown and cooked through, this will take 10-12 mins. While still hot, season with five-spice and salt.
To make the ranch dip, add all ingredients to a mixing bowl and whisk until combined. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Serve the fried onion with the ranch and sweet chilli sauce on the side for dipping. Get stuck in.

name: Blue Cheese Ranch Dressing
description: Sometimes ranch is all you want on a salad. This creamy dressing is packed with blue cheese for a proper tang and finished with fresh chives. Yum.
instructions: Finely chop the chives and set aside.

Add the blue cheese, mayonnaise, buttermilk, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder and lemon juice to a high-speed blender. Blitz until completely smooth, then taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Stir through the chopped chives and you're done!

name: Blue Cheese Turnovers
description: We've made these rich and tangy blue cheese turnovers using just six ingredients. A great one for snacking on during the weekend.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Tip the walnuts onto a tray and roast for 10 mins, then remove from the oven and drizzle with half of the honey. Add a pinch of salt and set aside to cool.
Cut the pears in half, then use a sharp knife to cut away the core. Slice half the pears. Finely chop the rest of the pears and set aside in a bowl.

Roll out the puff pastry sheet and cut into 6 squares. Take each square and lie a slice of prosciutto from one of the corners to the opposite corner. Top with a few slices of the pear, followed by the blue cheese. Fold the other two corners of the square over the filling to form a turnover shape. Place on a baking sheet and repeat with the rest of the puff squares. Drizzle with a little honey and bake for 15-20 mins, until golden.
Meanwhile, make the pear salsa. Add olive oil to the finely chopped pears, a drizzle of honey and a big pinch of salt and pepper.
Roughly chop the honey walnuts.
Serve the turnovers, topped with the pear salsa and chopped walnuts.

name: Blue Cheese and Leek Cannelloni
description: Gizzi Erskine makes an incredible cannelloni using Castello Danish Blue. Loaded up with leeks and spinach, this dish is an absolute belter.
instructions: Separate your cloves from the bulb of garlic. Peel and finely chop them.
Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a heavy-based casserole over a medium-low heat. Gently fry the garlic for 5 mins until softened and lightly golden, but don't let it burn.
Quarter your tomatoes, then pour them into the pan. Season well, then add the vinegar and cook slowly on a low heat for an hour, so the sauce has reduced to a deep, concentrated flavour.
Blitz the sauce with a stick blender until it is perfectly smooth. Tear up the basil leaves and stir through.
For the béchamel, warm the milk, bay leaf and a generous grating of nutmeg in a saucepan. Remove from the heat and leave it to infuse for 10 mins.

In a separate saucepan, melt the butter. Whisk in the flour, then cook out for 2 mins. Slowly add the milk bit by bit, whisking as you go to achieve a smooth consistency. Continue whisking until the milk is all combined and the sauce looks glossy.
Bring the béchamel to the boil slowly to thicken it, scraping the base of the pan with a wooden spoon to avoid scorching.
Tear up the mozzarella and add this to the béchamel. Beat with a wooden spoon until the mozzarella is completely melted. Season to taste with salt and pepper and a little bit more grated nutmeg.
Now make the filling. Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a pan set over a medium heat. Wilt the spinach for 2 mins. Remove from the pan and squeeze out any water from the spinach in a sieve over the sink.
Roughly chop your spinach and slice your leeks.
Melt the butter in the same pan and add the leeks. Sweat for 5 mins until softened.
Mix the crème fraîche and Castello Danish Blue together in a bowl, then add your spinach, leeks, nutmeg, salt and pepper until well combined. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Transfer the spinach mixture into a piping bag, squeezing the mixture towards the nozzle so it is nicely compact and ready to pipe.
Preheat the oven to 200°C/400°F.
Pipe the filling into each cannelloni. Repeat until all the pasta and filling is used up.
Take a medium-size ceramic baking dish, (approx. 26cm), pour in half the tomato sauce, and then neatly arrange the filled cannelloni on top, packing them in tightly.
Press them down a little into the sauce so the cannelloni are partially submerged in the tomato sauce. Pour the rest of the tomato sauce on top, followed by the béchamel.
Grate over the Parmesan. Place in the hot oven for 30 mins until the cheese is delicious and bubbling.
Leave to stand for 5 mins before serving with a green salad and crusty bread.

name: Blueberry & Almond Smoothie
description: Nutty, creamy and bursting with berries. This smoothie’s got serious flavour and plenty of protein to back it up.
instructions: Chuck the blueberries, blackberries, banana, milk, protein powder, almond butter and chia seeds into a blender.
Blend until smooth. If it’s looking a bit too thick, loosen with a splash of cold water.
Pour into a glass and sip away.

name: Blueberry & Almond Smoothie Bowl
description: Thick, nutty and loaded with berries. This smoothie bowl is super speedy and perfect for anyone who likes their breakfast with a spoon and a crunchy topping.
instructions: Chuck the blueberries, blackberries, banana, milk, yoghurt, protein powder, almond butter, the juice of the lime and chia seeds into a blender.
Start blending on a low speed. Use a tamper to push everything down – it’ll be thick. Add 10ml more milk at a time only if it really won’t blend.
Scoop into a bowl and load up with your favourite toppings – fresh berries, granola, almonds, seeds or another drizzle of almond butter.

name: Blueberry & Rosemary Mocktail
description: Made with a super simple syrup flavoured with rosemary, complete with muddled blueberries, this mocktail is delicious as it is or spiked with a measure of gin.
instructions: In a medium pot, add the sugar, water and rosemary. Bring to the boil and simmer for 3 mins, then turn off the heat and set aside to infuse for another 10 mins.
Meanwhile, warm the blueberries gently in a pan on the stove or in the microwave until they burst and start to release their juices.
Crush the ice, if you like (I used a small food processor). Cut the lime into wedges.
To make one drink, add 2 tbsp of blueberries to a small glass followed by 2 tbsp of rosemary syrup and some ice. Top up with sparkling water and garnish with a wedge of lime.

name: Blueberry Basil Froyo
description: Frozen yoghurt is a summer fave and this delicious recipe is perfect to enjoy in the sunshine. Check out the other flavour combos on the website.
instructions: Save a few blueberries to the side and put them into the molds.
Blend the blueberries, yogurt and basil and a squeeze of agave if you like, until smooth. Pour into the molds and freeze for 3-4 hours.
Optional also to drizzle the finished ones with a little tahini and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

name: Blueberry Crunch Overnight Oats
description: Breakfast is the most important meal of the day. Make the most of that meal with these delicious blueberry-packed overnight oats.
instructions: Roughly chop the nuts and place them into a dry frying pan. Place onto medium heat and toast, stirring often, until golden, 5-8 mins. Tip half into a bowl and stir the honey and the rest of the topping ingredients through. Store in an airtight container at room temperature.
In the empty pan, make the base: Tip in the frozen blueberries and honey on medium heat and stir until the blueberries have defrosted. Remove from the heat and let it cool down.

Add the oats and remaining frozen blueberries into the bowl with the nuts. Coarsely grate the apple into the mixture and stir through the lemon zest, milk, and yoghurt. Season with as much honey as you’d like, and a pinch of salt
Share the blueberry coulis into jars and ladle the oat mixture on top. Cover and refrigerate overnight so the oats can soften. Once ready to eat, serve the blueberry pots with the toasted nuts.

name: Blueberry Pancakes
description: Blueberry Pancakes. A classic. A dream. We've used buttermilk for a thick batter that yields incredibly fluffy pancakes. Drizzle with syrup and you're golden.
instructions: Sift your flour into a mixing bowl and add your sugar, baking powder and bicarbonate of soda. Whisk to combine.

Make a well in the middle of your dry mix and add your milk, buttermilk and eggs. Whisk the mixture until just combined. Do not overbeat the mixture, or you will have chewy pancakes. A few lumps are okay. Add your blueberries and gently stir to combine.

Heat a non-stick frying pan on a medium-high heat. Add a ladle of pancake batter and fry for 2 mins or until the top has started bubbling and firming up. Flip and cook for 2 mins on the other side. Keep warm and repeat with your remaining pancakes.
Serve in a stack with maple syrup.

name: Bolognese On Toast
description: A recipe that's perfect when you can't be bothered to cook a spag bol. Bolognese on toast. Don't knock it 'til you try it.
instructions: Get a large saucepan over a medium heat and drizzle in some olive oil. Add the beef mince and fry until well browned, remove from the pan and set aside.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onions. Add to the pan along with a further drizzle of olive oil and fry for 8–10 mins until soft. Grate the garlic directly into the pan, then add the oregano and tomato paste and stir well.

Pour in the red wine. Once it has bubbled away by half, stir in the browned beef mince, then pour in the stock and milk. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to a low simmer, cover and cook for 1 ½ hours, adding a splash of water if it looks like it’s catching at all.
Season to taste, then set aside.
Toast the slices of toast. Serve the bolognese piled on top of the toast, covered in Parmesan and scattered in basil.

name: Bolognese Ragú
description: This bolognese ragù is rich, meaty and worth every minute. Red wine and pancetta give it a deep, savoury kick that clings perfectly to pasta. It's a winner.
instructions: Add the pancetta to a large, heavy-based pan with a drizzle of olive oil. Set it over a low-medium heat and cook gently until the fat is released and the pancetta starts to crisp.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, carrot and celery. Peel the garlic and finely chop. Add everything to the pan along with a pinch of salt, the bay leaves and rosemary. Fry for 8-10 mins until the veg is soft and the pancetta is browned.

Tip the contents of the pan into a bowl and set aside. Return the pan to the heat, turn it up high and add the beef mince with a big pinch of salt. Break the mince up with the back of your spoon and fry until browned. Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 3-5 mins until darkened.
Pour in the red wine and let it bubble away until reduced by half. Stir in the Worcestershire sauce, then add one-third of the stock. Bring to the boil and bubble until reduced by half again.
Add the chopped tomatoes. Return the cooked pancetta and veg to the pan, pour in the milk and remaining stock, add the salt and bring to a simmer. Simmer for 20-25 mins until thickened.
If you're prepping ahead, let the ragù cool to room temperature and chill overnight.

name: Bolognese Tortelloni With Grated Tomato & Burrata
description: We've dressed up La Famiglia Rana Bolognese Tortelloni with a freshly grated tomato and a creamy ball of burrata. Bliss.
keywords: Bolognese Tortelloni With Grated Tomato & Burrata
instructions: Grate the whole tomato on the largest side of a box grater into a wide bowl, then season generously with salt and add the extra virgin olive oil and sherry vinegar. Give this a try – it should taste like summer! Stir through the capers and finely grate in the garlic clove. Finely chop the parsley and add to the sauce.

Bring a large pot of water to the boil, then tip in the La Famiglia Rana Bolognese Tortellini to cook for just 2 mins before draining. Add the fresh tomato sauce to the pasta and give it a toss so it’s all coated.
Divide between two bowls and serve with large pieces of torn burrata or mozzarella, an extra drizzle of olive oil and a little more salt and pepper to finish.

name: Bombay Cauliflower & Turmeric Rice with Tamarind Yoghurt
description: Golden spiced cauliflower, fluffy turmeric rice and tangy tamarind yoghurt. Fresh, filling and perfect for lunchboxes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan.

Cut the cauliflower into bite-sized florets and tip into a large roasting tin. Toss with half of the turmeric, plus all of the cumin and coriander with a drizzle of olive oil and a big pinch of salt. Roast for 25–30 mins until golden and tender.
Meanwhile, peel and finely slice the garlic.
Place a medium saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry the garlic for 1 min, then stir through the rice and remaining turmeric until coated. Season rice with salt and pepper.
Pour in the stock, bring to the boil, then cover with a lid. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 10–12 mins until the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is fluffy.
While the rice and cauliflower cook, mix the yoghurt, tamarind paste and honey in a small bowl until smooth.
Slice the cucumber into thin half-moons and roughly chop the coriander.
Pack the rice into lunchboxes, top with the roasted cauliflower, spoon over the tamarind yoghurt and finish with cucumber and coriander.

name: Bombay Mix Aubergine Nuggets with Tikka Chickpeas
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad

Crispy, smoky aubergine nuggets coated in crushed Bombay mix? Say less. Served over a rich tikka-spiced chickpea sauce with a zingy cabbage and coriander slaw, this dish is packed with texture, spice, and affordable ingredients we got from Aldi.
keywords: Bombay Mix Aubergine Nuggets with Tikka Chickpeas
Bombay Mix Aubergine Nuggets with Tikka Chickpeas recipe
instructions: Blitz the Bombay mix in a food processor until it becomes a fine crumb. Tip onto a plate and season with salt. On a second plate, season the flour with salt and pepper. On a third, crack in the eggs, season, and whisk well.

Finely slice the cabbage and chop the coriander (reserving a few leaves for garnish, if you like). Mix in a bowl with the juice of ½ a lemon and a pinch of salt. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges for serving. Finely slice the green chilli.

Poke holes in the aubergines with a fork. Char them over an open flame, turning every few minutes, until the skin is blackened and the flesh is soft—this takes around 10–15 mins. Place in a bowl, cover with cling film, and set aside to steam for 10 mins.

Peel and grate the garlic. Heat a splash of oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the tikka paste with the garlic for 2 mins until fragrant. Add the tomatoes, breaking them up with a spoon, then stir in the chickpeas. Season and simmer for 10 mins, stirring occasionally.

Once cool, peel off and discard the aubergine skin. Place the flesh on a board and gently flatten with a fork. Season well. Dredge each aubergine in the flour, then dip into the egg, letting the excess drip off, and finally press into the Bombay mix crumbs until well coated.

Heat 1cm of oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Test the heat with a wooden chopstick—if bubbles form around the tip, you're good to go. Carefully add the aubergine and cook for a few mins per side, spooning over oil as you go, until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper. Keep warm in a low oven if frying in batches.
Spoon the chickpea sauce onto plates. Top with the crispy aubergine nuggets, cabbage slaw, sliced green chilli, and a wedge of lemon. Finish with a few coriander leaves, if you fancy.

name: Bombay Roast Potatoes
description: These are packed full of flavour. Tender and crispy potatoes baked with a spicy coating. Switch up your Sunday roast with these bad boys.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Add a large glug of oil to a baking dish and pop it into the oven to warm up.

Peel and chop up your potatoes and pop them into a large pan. Pour over cold water enough to cover and heavily season with salt and the turmeric. Bring to a boil and cook until just fork-tender, 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel the garlic and ginger, and slice the chillis.

Drain the potatoes and coat with flour, chilli powder, garam masala, coriander powder, cumin powder and a teaspoon of salt. Grate in the garlic and ginger, then add in the chilli. Shake to rustle them up to make them fluffy.
Add the cumin and black mustard seeds to the hot oil. Stir to mix evenly then pour in the potatoes.
Roast in the oven for 40 minutes, tossing occasionally to evenly roast.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the coriander and half the lemon/s.
When crispy and roasted, pull out the potatoes and squeeze on the juice from your lemon/s and sprinkle the coriander.

name: Boursin & Gnocchi Traybake
description: An easy gnocchi traybake that has a secret ingredient: Boursin cheese. It's garlicky goodness.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C fan.

Tip the gnocchi into a large tray. Slice the broccoli into 3cm- 5cm lengths and add to the tray. Snuggle the Boursin in. Drizzle with olive oil and season well. Slide into the oven and bake for 15-20 mins.

Remove from the oven and stir to combine. Add the spinach along with a big splash of boiling water. Keep string, adding enough boiling water to wilt the spinach. Add the juice of the lemon and then finely grate most of the Parmesan into the tray and stir to make a silky cheesy sauce.
Spoon into bowls, finely grate the remaining Parmesan over the top, then finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Braised Aubergine Lentils With Pesto Yoghurt
description: Fudgy aubergines? Plump lentils? Pesto yoghurt? This recipe has got it all. A healthy midweek dinner.
keywords: Braised Aubergine Lentils With Pesto Yoghurt
Braised Aubergine Lentils With Pesto Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Cut the top off the garlic bulb then drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and wrap in tin foil.
Finely dice the onion and add to a baking tray along with the tomatoes, lentils, thyme and stock. Mix well and season with salt and pepper then cover with tin foil.
Pop the tray and the wrapped garlic bulb in the oven for 30 mins.

Meanwhile, quarter the aubergine lengthways. Heat oil in a pan over a high heat and fry the aubergine until golden on each side. Remove from the pan and drain on kitchen paper, then season with salt and pepper.

Remove the roasted garlic bulb and cooked lentils from the oven, removing the tin foil from the tray. Let the garlic cool slightly then squeeze out the flesh, mash it up with a fork and mix it through the lentils.
Top the lentils with the aubergine, nestling them in. Return the tray to the oven for 20-25 mins.
Mix the yoghurt with the pesto. Divide the lentils and aubergines between bowls and top with the pesto yoghurt and toasted almonds.

name: Braised Chicken & Herby Couscous
description: This recipe can be made using a third of your batch-cooked turmeric braised chicken. Plus, it's delicious.
instructions: Make the Turmeric Braised Chicken.

Finely mince the coriander (stalks and all). Tip the couscous into a large heatproof bowl with a big pinch of salt. Pour over the boiling water, stir once, then cover with a plate and leave to steam for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, warm the Turmeric Braised Chicken in a saucepan set over a low heat, stirring occasionally, until piping hot. Add a splash of water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Fluff the couscous with a fork, then stir through the coriander, lemon zest and a drizzle of olive oil. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Spoon the couscous into bowls, top with the warm turmeric chicken and finish with a dollop of yoghurt.

name: Braised Chicken Cacciatore with Cheesy Polenta
description: Creamy, cheesy polenta is the perfect partner for a rich and saucy chicken cacciatore.
keywords: Braised Chicken Cacciatore with Cheesy Polenta
Braised Chicken Cacciatore with Cheesy Polenta recipe
instructions: Start by preheating your oven to 160°C.

Split the chicken legs into thighs and drumsticks by slicing through the joint that connects the two. Season with salt and pepper. Preheat a large braising pot or frying pan over a medium heat. Add plenty of olive oil and star browning off the chicken in batches. Start skin side down and cook over medium heat (nothing crazy) for 6-7 mins until the fat has renderred and the skin has crisped. Repeat with the remaining chicken.

Whilst the chicken is cooking, roughly chop the celery, fennel and shallots and finely chop the garlic. Once all the chicken is browned off, remove from the pan, leaving behind all that chicken fat and olive oil. Chuck in the celery, shallots and fennel with a pinch of salt and cook for 9-10 mins. Add the garlic, herbs and spices for 2 mins before cranking up the heat and dumping in the white wine. Deglaze the pan with the wine and reduce by half.
Deglaze the pan with the wine and reduce by half.

Tip in the tomatoes and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer and nestle in the chicken pieces. You want a little of the chicken skin sticking out the liquid, like alligators in the swamp. Scatter over the olives and then slide into the oven, uncovered, for an hour.

Whilst the chicken is braising, make the polenta. Add the water to a pot along with the milk and bring to a bare simmer. Whisk in the polenta and cook, stirring regularly, for 30-40 mins. Once cooked, season with salt and whisk in the butter and grated cheese. I like to add some grated nutmeg, too.
