Once the chicken has had an hour or so, crank up the heat for the last few minutes to really get some colour on the skin. Divide the polenta between warm bowls and spoon over some of the tomato sauce and a couple of pieces of chicken. Top with extra Parm and chopped parsley.

name: Braised Chicken Flatbread
description: Here's another quick and easy recipe you can make with your batch-cooked turmeric braised chicken.
instructions: Make the Turmeric Braised Chicken.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Finely dice the tomatoes and red onion, then combine in a bowl. Add a pinch of salt and give it a mix.
Shred the chicken off the bone, then get it back in the sauce. Cook it on the hob over a medium heat for 5 mins, or until it is hot and the sauce has thickened up.

Heat the flatbreads in the oven for 5 mins. Spoon the yoghurt over the flatbreads, then spoon over the chicken. Sprinkle over the tomato and onion mixture, then finish with a little coriander. Serve them up.

name: Braised Chickpeas With Chorizo & Cavolo Nero
description: A warming recipe that's perfect during the autumn and ideal for using up seasonal veg like cavolo nero. You'll be making this one again.
keywords: Braised Chickpeas With Chorizo & Cavolo Nero
Braised Chickpeas With Chorizo & Cavolo Nero recipe
instructions: Grab a large saucepan and set it over a medium heat to preheat.

Dice the onions and finely slice the garlic and chilli. Add the onion to the pan with a shot of olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Cook for 3-4 mins then add the garlic, chilli and bay leaves. Cook for another min or two.

Halve the potatoes and strip the leaves from the cavolo nero stalks. Add them to the pan and cover with chicken stock. Add the chickpeas and bring the whole lot to the boil. Add a lid and let it bubble away for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, cut the chorizo into 1cm-thick coins and add to a small pan with a shot of olive oil. Set over a medium-low heat and let crisp up, drawing out all the bright red fat.
Remove the lid from the stew, season with salt and lemon juice and finish with chopped dill.
Spoon into bowls and top with the chorizo.

name: Braised Courgettes with White Beans, Goat's Cheese & Pistou
description: Courgettes are cooked down with olive oil, garlic, red onions, white beans and basil. Topped with goats’ cheese, croutons and pistou, then finished under the grill.
instructions: Heat your grill. Finely slice the courgettes into roughly ½cm-thick rounds. Finely slice the red onion and ⅔ of the garlic cloves.

Add everything to a large, shallow saucepan or casserole and place over a medium heat with ⅓ of the olive oil and 1 tsp salt. Cook for 10 mins until the courgettes have softened (you want them to still hold their shape).

While the courgettes cook, make the pistou. In a pestle and mortar, crush the remaining garlic clove with a pinch of salt into a paste. Add the basil leaves a handful at a time until everything is blended to a rough paste. You could also do this in a small blender. Stir through another ⅓ of the olive oil and the zest and juice of half of your lemon. Set aside.
Add the jar of beans and its liquid to the courgettes and cook for 3 mins. Remove from the heat, squeeze in the remaining lemon, stir through and taste for seasoning.

Tear the baguette into 5cm chunks. Transfer to a bowl with the rest of the olive oil and a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Space the baguette chunks evenly across the top of the courgette and beans, slightly submerging them.
Dot tablespoons of the goats’ cheese in the remaining spaces, then sprinkle over some finely sliced chilli, if you like. Place under the grill for 3-4 mins until the baguette is golden and toasty.
Drizzle over the pistou and serve with extra chunks of bread, for mopping.

name: Braised Green Herby Chicken
description: Inspired by Tunisian pkaila, this high-protein herby chicken stew features tender thighs braised in a deep green herby sauce. Bold, comforting...It's everything you've ever wanted.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put all the spinach into a bowl and microwave for 5 mins until defrosted. Squeeze the liquid out into a separate bowl and discard it.

Season the chicken thighs with salt and heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Put the chicken thighs into the pan, skin-side down, and cook for 8-10 mins until the skin is deep golden brown. Transfer to a baking tray.
Peel and thinly slice the onions, then tip them into the empty chicken pan with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 7-10 mins until starting to soften.

Meanwhile, pour the chicken stock into a blender with the dill, coriander (stalks and all), half the spinach and three-quarters of the harissa. Blitz until smooth. Add this mixture to the onions, bring to the boil, stir through the remaining spinach and a splash of water if you'd like to loosen it, then pour everything over the chicken. Cook in the oven for 25-30 mins.
Once cooked, drizzle over the yoghurt and remaining harissa.

name: Braised Lentils with Fennel, Sausage and Salsa Verde
description: This is one of my favourite things to eat when the weather turns cold. Saucy braised lentils with a couple of juicy sausages and a zingy salsa verde. Jordon x
keywords: easy dinner party sausage and lentils recipes
instructions: First up, we’re going to cook the soffritto. Put a saucepan over a medium-low heat before adding 4 tbsp olive oil. Finely dice the onion and add it to the pan.
Whilst the onion cooks gently for a few minutes, dice the carrot and fennel, then add them to the pan with a good pinch of salt. Cook this mix for another 5 mins until soft and lightly golden.
Add the tomato purée, mince the garlic and add, then cook for another few minutes. Rinse the lentils, then add to the pan and stir well. Allow to cook for another minute until well coated in oil.
Add the stock, bring it up to a simmer and then allow it to cook for about 25/30 mins until the lentils are tender but still have a little bite.
Meanwhile, fry the sausages until golden brown, then keep warm.
To make the green sauce, finely chop all the herbs and the capers, then mix in a bowl with the mustard, 50ml of olive oil, the juice of half a lemon and a pinch of salt.
Once the lentils are cooked, add the juice of the other half of the lemon, stir, then plate up. Pop two sausages on top and a generous spoon of salsa verde.

name: Braised Pork Belly
description: The rich and unctuous wobble of pork belly is why we love it. This recipe brings the best out of this cut of meat.
instructions: Pour water into your wok and bring to a boil.
While you’re waiting for the water to boil, smash your ginger and star anise. Roughly chop your ginger and add these to your wok along with a teaspoon of salt.
Separate the white part of the spring onions from the greens, and smash the whites while leaving the greens aside. Add the whites to your wok along with sugar and give it a stir.
Prepare a large bowl of ice water.

Now add the pork belly to your wok and blanch for 3-5 mins on medium heat. Use a strainer to skim the foam from the top of the water until the water is clear, then discard. Once it’s done, add all of the pork belly to your ice water.
Now for the sauce, chop your ginger into a few pieces then smash your ginger. Smash your garlic and remove the skin. Roughly chop your shallot.
Chop your pork belly into 3cm pieces.

Using a clean wok, on medium heat, pour in 3 tbsp of vegetable oil and add your ginger, garlic and shallot. Give it a stir then add your palm sugar and bash to break it into smaller pieces. When the sugar starts to melt and becomes sticky, add your pork belly and give it a good mix so everything’s evenly coated.

Add the remaining sauces and seasonings to your wok. Cover with a lid and leave to braise on low heat for 45 mins on low heat. If the pork is tender but the sauce hasn’t reduced, remove the lid and bring to a boil until the glaze is sticky.
When the pork is cooked, evenly pour over a tbsp of shaoxing wine. Garnish with spring onions and serve with steamed rice – enjoy!

name: Braised Soy Sauce Chicken Udon Soup Noodles
description: A rich, comforting bowl of broth-soaked udon noodles, tender soy-braised chicken and zingy toppings. Big flavour. Minimal faff.
keywords: Braised Soy Sauce Chicken Udon Soup Noodles
Braised Soy Sauce Chicken Udon Soup Noodles recipe
instructions: Sear the chicken. Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a saucepan over high heat. Add the chicken thighs and sear for 2 mins per side until golden. Remove from the pan and reduce the heat to medium.

Prep and braise. Peel and thinly slice the onion and add it to the pan. Pour in the soy sauce, mirin, sake (if using), and cold water. Stir gently and cook for 3–5 mins until the onion softens and takes on the soy colour.
Return the chicken to the pan and pour in the dashi or chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-high heat and cook for 10 mins. Once cooked, remove the chicken and turn the heat to low.
Make the toppings. While the chicken cooks, slice the spring onions into thin strips and submerge them in a bowl of ice water. Zest the lime and grate the ginger.
Shred and mix. Shred the chicken and combine it in a bowl with the lime zest, sesame oil, sesame seeds, grated ginger, and drained spring onions. Mix to coat.
Cook the noodles. Bring the broth back to a boil. Add the frozen udon noodles and cook according to packet instructions.

Divide the noodles between two bowls. Ladle the broth over until the noodles are submerged. Top with a generous pile of shredded chicken and garnish with a wedge of lime and a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi, if using.

name: Braised Tomato-y Chickpeas With Salmon
description: Salmon poached in spiced tomato-y chickpeas, topped with dill and a big dollop of yoghurt — proper feel-good food.
keywords: Braised Tomato-y Chickpeas With Salmon recipe
instructions: Finely slice the garlic cloves. Pat the salmon dry with kitchen paper and season well on both sides with salt and black pepper.

Place a medium lidded saucepan over a medium heat and add the olive oil, cumin and garlic. Cook for 2–3 mins until the garlic is fragrant and starting to soften. Stir in the harissa paste and cook for another minute.

Pour in the passata and chickpeas. Bring to a gentle simmer, then carefully place the salmon on top. Turn the heat down to low, pop the lid on and simmer gently for 6 mins until the salmon is just cooked through.
Lift the salmon out and set aside. Squeeze in the juice of half the lemon and stir through half of the dill.
Divide the tomato-y chickpeas between bowls and top with the salmon. Finish with the rest of the dill, a generous dollop of yoghurt and a lemon wedge on the side.

name: Bramble
description: You need to make this classic drink – the blackberry Bramble cocktail. It's one of our fave gin cocktails. It’s so nice that’ll be yours, too, soon.
instructions: Gently heat your sugar and water until the sugar is fully dissolved, do not bring to boil.
Juice your lemon and slice a wheel for garnish.
Get a tea towel and fill it with ice. Wrap it up tight and bang it repeatedly against a table top to get crushed ice.
Fill your shaker with ice, then go in with the lemon juice, gin and sugar syrup.
Pour crushed ice into a glass and then single strain your cocktail onto it.
Pour the crème de mûre on top and garnish with lemon wheel and blackberry. Enjoy.

name: Brazilian Lemonade
description: It's creamy, it's citrussy, and it's sort of like drinking a key lime pie. This lemony cocktail is perfect for a sunny day. Just one of the many delicious cocktail recipes on the Mob website.
instructions: Add the water and your limes, whole, into a blender.
Blend them up until there are no big chunks, then strain through a sieve.
Return the liquid to the blender then add the sugar, rum, and condensed milk.
Serve over ice and garnish with a lime wheel and some mint. Enjoy!

name: Bread Sauce
description: Bread sauce is one of the most underrated aspects of a Christmas dinner. This bread sauce recipe is the bread sauce recipe to end all bread sauce recipes. It's seriously that good.
instructions: Smash the garlic clove and pick the leaves from the thyme stalks. Set both aside. Put the milk and butter into a saucepan and bring to a bare simmer. Roughly chop the onion and add to the pan with the cloves, black peppercorns, smashed garlic clove, thyme and bay leaves. Let the mixture simmer for 15 mins, then remove from the heat and allow to sit for 30 mins.

Once steeped, pass the mixture through a sieve and return the infused milk back to the pan. Add the breadcrumbs and bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 mins, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and black pepper and serve.

name: Breaded Lamb Chops With Caponata
description: Juicy lamb chops coated in a crunchy panko breadcrumb on a bed of tangy caponata. That's dinner, all right.
keywords: Breaded Lamb Chops With Caponata recipe
instructions: Start by dicing the aubergine, peppers, courgette, celery and red onions into a small-ish dice. You want everything roughly the same size! Preheat a pan over a medium-high heat and add a good glug of olive oil. Tip in the aubergines and season with salt. Cook for 5-6 mins or until nicely browned. Remove from the pan.

Add a shot more oil and tip in the other veggies (leaving the aubergine out for now). Season with salt and pepper and cook for 9-10 mins to sweat and soften. Finely grate in the garlic cloves and add the rosemary leaves. Tip the aubergines back in and cook everything together for 4-5 mins.

Add the passata, black olives, capers, vinegar and sugar. Simmer together for a further 9-10 mins before adding the nuts, raisins and folding through the rocket. Season to taste and keep warm while you prepare the lamb.
Season the chops generously with salt and pepper on both sides. Set up three separate bowls, one with the beaten eggs, one with seasoned flour and the third with the breadcrumbs.
Pass the chops through the flour, then coat with egg, before tossing in the breadcrumbs. I like to keep the bone clean of breadcrumbs, but don’t sweat it if you get a few on there!

Preheat a pan over a medium heat and add a generous layer of olive oil. Once hot, lay in the lamb chops, working in batches if necessary, and cook for 3-4 mins a side or until beautifully golden brown. Make sure your pan doesn’t get too hot, you want the chops to slowly brown in the oil. Remove from the pan, season with salt and pepper and rest for 5 mins or so before serving.
Serve a generous few spoons of warm caponata on warm plates, top with a couple of chops and serve with a wedge of lemon.

name: Breakfast Noodles
description: Picture a fry-up on top of a bowl of instant noodles, and you’ll get an idea of what this is all about. A cup of tea is optional, but highly recommended. Xien x
instructions: Thinly slice your mushrooms, chop your tomato in half and thinly slice your spring onion.
Cook your noodles according to packet instructions. Add the seasonings from the packet and soy sauce. Give it a good mix.
Meanwhile, fry your bacon until crispy then set aside. Now, fry up your egg with the tomato and mushrooms in the same pan and set them aside, too.
Pour the noodles into your favourite bowl with the tomato, egg, bacon, mushrooms and spring onion. Tuck in.

name: Breakfast Tacos
description: These protein packed breakfast tacos are an excellent way to start the day. Perfect for a post-run breakfast full of protein for recovery.
instructions: Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add a glug of olive oil. Drain the black beans and add to the pan with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 3 mins.
Add the cumin and paprika and cook for another 2 mins.
While the beans are frying, dice up the tomato and finely chop the coriander. Add both to a small bowl along with the chilli powder and lime juice, mix well and set aside.
Once the beans are ready, grab four tacos and divide the beans equally between them.
Rinse out the pan, add the butter and a splash of olive oil and place over a medium heat.
Finely chop the spring onions, add to the pan and sizzle for a couple of mins.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt and pour into the pan. Keep them moving and adjust the heat as necessary until you have just set, soft scrambled eggs.
Spoon the eggs over the beans, then top with the tomato salsa and a few shakes of hot sauce (if you like). Add a spoonful of the sour cream, fold up and tuck in.

name: Brick Chicken
description: This dish is all in the technique. Flattening the chicken with a brick gives you the most crispy, golden skin, while also keeping the meat perfectly tender.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.

Salsa verde time. Grab a bowl. Add a large handful of finely chopped parsley and tarragon leaves (remove the stalks), anchovies, shallots and roughly chopped capers. Stir together with red wine vinegar, 6 tbsps of olive oil, a crack of pepper and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Whack your baby potatoes onto a baking tray, drizzle over a large glug of olive oil and season generously. Massage together and roast for 50 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare your bricks. Wrap up 2 bricks in foil, making sure that the whole brick is covered.
Debone the chicken and cut away any excess fatty pieces. When all the chicken is ready, add into a bowl with a glug of olive oil, salt and pepper. Massage together.

Heat up a non-stick frying pan without any oil and flatten the chicken thighs into the pan skin-side down. Place your foiled bricks on top of the chicken and leave for about 10 minutes. Remove the brick and flip the chicken. The skin side will have become golden and crispy. Leave for a couple more minutes then remove from the pan once cooked through.
Serve up your crispy chicken with salty potatoes and a drizzle of your salsa verde dressing.

name: Brick Chicken & Charred Runner Bean Salad
description: Here, we've taken a classic dish — Pollo al Mattone — and matched it up with charred runner beans, a caper butter sauce and creamy ricotta.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Using kitchen scissors, cut along each side of the chicken spine, from the neck to the tail, and remove. Flip the chicken over and press down onto the breasts to flatten. Pat the chicken dry, then drizzle over 4 tbsp of olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper, set aside.

Wrap up 2 bricks in foil or the bottom of a heavy ovenproof frying pan or a heavy tray. Drizzle another ovenproof frying pan with 2 tbsp of olive oil, place the chicken, skin-side down and place on medium-high heat. Cook until golden, 8-10 mins. Then, place the weight on top and transfer to the oven. Roast for 20-25 mins, then flip, breast-side up, place the weight on top and return to the oven for 15 mins, until fully cooked through.

Meanwhile, trim, peel and thinly slice the shallots. Heat a griddle pan over a high heat until smoking hot. Trim and chop the runner beans into 5cm long pieces and drizzle with olive oil. Grill in batches, turning once or twice, until charred in spots, 3-5 minutes.

In an empty bowl, add the shallots, mustard, apple cider vinegar, honey and 50ml of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, mix. Once the beans have charred, add them into the mustard dressing and toss together.
Once the chicken is cooked, transfer it to a clean plate to rest, skin-side up. Peel and thinly slice the garlic, pick the oregano leaves and halve the lemon.

Place the chicken frying pan onto medium-high heat. Once hot, melt the butter. Add the garlic, capers and oregano, fry for 1 min. Pour the wine in and simmer until reduced by ¾. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Remove from the heat and vigorously stir the cold butter through.
Carve the chicken. Spread the ricotta onto a large serving platter or plate and top with the runner bean salad and chicken. Finish by spooning over the caper butter sauce.

name: Brick Chicken with Autumn Slaw
description: Want golden crispy chicken skin and extra juicy meat? Whack a brick on top of your chicken as it cooks. We’ve paired this 'Chicken Under a Brick' with an autumnal slaw of pears, hazelnuts and raw beetroot.
instructions: Grab a brick from the garden and give it a good wash with some hot soapy water then dry and set aside. (Alternatively, just use your heaviest pan.)

To make the slaw, thinly slice the cabbage, peel and thinly slice the beetroot, core and thinly slice the pear, thinly slice the red onion and roughly chop the parsley. Mix all the ingredients in a bowl with the juice of the lemon, then roughly chop the hazelnuts and stir in.
Combine the dressing ingredients and stir into the slaw, then season to taste with salt and pepper. Set aside for the flavours to come together.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper and olive oil in a bowl. Thinly slice the lemon.

Using a pair of scissors, cut a piece of greaseproof paper to fit a large frying pan or skillet. Heat the large frying pan or skillet until very hot, then add the chicken skin side down. Scatter over the lemon slices and sprigs of rosemary.
Top with the greaseproof paper then weigh down the chicken with the brick (or a heavy frying pan).

Leave to cook for about 12-15 mins until the chicken skin is deep golden brown and crisp and the chicken is cooked through. Remove the brick and parchment, flip the chicken over in the pan and cook for another minute more.
Remove from the heat and allow to rest for a couple of minutes.
Cut the chicken into slices, then top with the chicken juices and caramelised lemon slices. Serve with the slaw and hot sauce on the side, if you like.

name: Brioche Bread & Butter Pudding
description: Bread and butter pudding is an absolute British classic. It’s a great way to use up leftover custard and brioche or any other loaf. It works best with stale bread – too fresh and you end up with a soggy mess.
instructions: Start by making the custard. Stir the egg yolks and sugar together in a heatproof bowl. Heat the cream in a pan with the salt and vanilla pod until hot but not boiling. You’ll know it’s hot when it starts to steam. Pour the hot cream over the egg yolks slowly and evenly, whisking continuously as you go. Get someone to help you here if possible – they can pour while you whisk.

Remove the vanilla pod, split it lengthways and scrape the seeds into the custard. If necessary sieve the custard through a fine mesh to eliminate any lumps, then pour into a jug. Cover the top (of the custard, not the jug) with clingfilm to prevent a skin forming then set aside.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Grease a 20cm square pie dish. Cut the leftover brioche into slices. Melt the butter in a pot over a low heat.

Pack the brioche slices tightly into your prepared pie dish. Dot the raisins throughout and brush the brioche all over with the melted butter. Pour in the custard and bake for 20 mins, or until the custard is starting to set.

name: British Stir-Fried Morning Glory
description: You can use any dark greens to enjoy one of our fave Thai veggie dishes: morning glory. Best served simply with rice, fried eggs, fresh chilli, lime and crushed peanuts.
instructions: Cook the jasmine rice first, as this dish comes together very quickly.
Bring a small pot of salted water to the boil and set aside. Smash all the garlic cloves, remove the peel and smash more so they are broken into flat, irregular chunks. Set aside.

If using large dark leafy greens, slice into large chunks and remove any tough stems. Remove the rough stems from the tops of the green beans, as they are bad to eat! Cut them in half if preferred, for neater eating.
Combine all the sauce ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.

For the fried eggs, set a small frying pan over a high heat and add 1-2 tbsp oil, or just enough to cover the base of the pan, then carefully crack all the eggs into the same pan to fry together. Turn the heat to medium and cook to your liking. Season the yolks with a pinch of salt and set aside, off the heat.

Boil the green beans for 4 mins, then drain and set aside. Pour a glug of vegetable oil into a large saucepan, or just enough to cover the entire base of the pan, then add all the smashed garlic cloves. Turn the heat to medium-high and cook for 2-3 mins, or until the garlic is lightly golden. Quickly and carefully add all the green beans to the garlic oil – it may splatter, so stay at arm's length. Toss well and add all the sauce, then cook for 1 min over a high heat, allowing the sauce to caramelise around the beans.

Add all the remaining dark leafy greens and cook for another minute over a high heat. Taste for doneness, then turn off the heat if it is cooked with a slight bite (don’t overcook the greens, or they will lose their vibrant colour). Squeeze in half a lime and toss everything together well. Add chilli powder now if you like a bit of spice.
Serve in shallow pasta plates, making sure to pour over all the sauce and garlic chunks. Top with crushed peanuts, sliced fresh chilli and lime wedges. Eat with the fried eggs and rice.

name: Broccoli & Saint Agur Soup with Blue Cheese Croutons
description: Tie me up and call me Richard. This is the homemade soup to end all homemade soups. Try these blue cheese croutons & you'll never go back.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F
Roughly chop your leeks, potatoes, onion and broccoli.

Add a large knob of butter to a deep saucepan. Add the broccoli stalks, the potatoes, the leeks and onion. Fry for 8 minutes until beginning to soften and then add your broccoli heads. Mix everything together and pour in 800ml of vegetable stock.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook on a medium heat for 15 minutes or until the vegetables are soft.

In the meantime, get on with your croutons. Cut discs out of your baguette and spread 100g of the Saint Agur on the bread. Line up your croutons on a baking tray and place in the oven for 30 minutes or until crisp and golden.
Back to the soup. Once the vegetables are cooked through, remove the lid. Crumble in the rest of your Saint Agur and season with salt and pepper. Blitz with a hand blender until smooth.
Serve the soup in bowls with the crispy croutons and any leftover cheese on top. Enjoy!

name: Broccoli Caesar Salad
description: Roasted broccoli with all the caesar salad-y bits. We've used the broccoli stalk to make a quick pickle to reduce waste and bring an extra layer of flavour.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Cover the cashews with boiling water and set aside to soften.
Place the broccoli on its head, florets facing the chopping board and stalk facing upwards. Slice off the florets, and move them to the side, so you end up with just the stalk.
Slice the tough skin off of the stalk and cut it into a rectangle as best you can. Cut it into thin strips, then lay a few of these strips on top of each other to cut them into thin batons.
Place the batons in a bowl with ½ tsp table salt and massage the salt into the broccoli stem until they start to soften. Set aside while you get on with the rest.
Chop the broccoli florets into equal-sized pieces and lay on a baking tray.

Drain the chickpeas and place them on the tray with the broccoli and season with the cumin, coriander and paprika, olive oil and salt and pepper. Roast for 10 mins, toss and roast for another 10, until the chickpeas are golden brown and the broccoli is cooked through and starting to char on the outside.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Add the softened cashews, oat milk, Dijon mustard, nutritional yeast, ½ tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1½ tsp capers plus 1 tsp of caper brine and blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper and taste.

Roughly chop the lettuce and spread over a large platter, drizzle with a little olive oil and season lightly with salt. Scatter over the broccoli and chickpeas and pickled stem, then drizzle over the sauce.
Scatter broken crisps over the top, if using. This salad doesn't keep well, so assemble it right before serving.

name: Broccoli Cheddar Soup With Cheddar Sesame Cracker
description: Silky smooth, broccoli soup with a tangy punch of mature cheddar. Add the spinach right at the end to keep it vibrant.
keywords: Broccoli Cheddar Soup With Cheddar Sesame Cracker
instructions: Thinly slice the onions and garlic. Preheat a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil, then your onions and garlic. Sweat with a pinch of salt for 6-7 mins.
Peel and chunk up the potato and roughly chop the broccoli. Add the potato to the pan and cook for 5 mins. Now add the broccoli, stock and cream. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10-12 mins.
Meanwhile, coarsely grate the cheddar. Preheat a non-stick pan over medium heat, then add a handful of cheddar. Cook for a couple of mins until lacy and caramelised.

Sprinkle your cheddar crisp with black sesame seeds and Aleppo pepper. Flip, then cook for 2 mins on the other side. Transfer to a rack and allow to cool. Repeat with 3/4 of the cheddar, saving the remaining 1/4 until later.
Add the spinach to the soup, and cook for another minute until just wilted. Transfer to a blender along with the remaining cheese and blend until smooth.
Season your soup with salt and black pepper to taste, then divide between bowls and top with the cheddar crisps. Enjoy.

name: Broccoli Cheese Pie
description: It's pie weather. This cheesy, veggie-friendly pie is loaded with broccoli and a mountain of cheddar. It's just the thing to get you through the evening.
instructions: Preheat an oven to 190°C.

Start by making the cheese sauce. Add the butter to a saucepan, set over a medium heat and allow to melt before adding the flour. Cook the butter and flour together for a minute or so then start to slowly add in the milk bit by bit, whisking constantly.
Once you have added all the milk, allow it to bubble away for a couple of minutes before adding the cheese and mustard and stirring through. Season with salt and pepper and allow to cool.
Next prepare the vegetables, cut the leek lengthways and roughly chop, discarding the tough ends. Take the broccoli and cut into bite-sized florets.

In a separate large saucepan add a small knob of butter with a splash of olive oil and set over a medium heat. Add the leek and cook for 5 mins before adding the broccoli and cooking for 10 mins. Stir the peas through and take off the heat.

Season with salt and pepper, pour over the cheese sauce and transfer to a pie dish to cool. Roll out the puff pastry so it will fit over the pie dish. Whisk the egg and brush it over the edge of a pie dish then place on the pastry lid.

With a fork dusted with flour press down the edges on the pastry then cut off any excess. Decorate the pie with any extra pastry then brush all over with the egg wash and sprinkle with a little flaky salt. Place in a preheated oven for 30 mins.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool slightly before digging in.

name: Broccoli Fritti
description: You want a bit of sun and an icy cold beer for this one. If you're not into 'nduja, swap it for harissa, roasted chilli paste or your favourite hot sauce. B x
instructions: Fill a large pot just under halfway with vegetable oil and set over a medium heat, bring to 180°C.
Trim any woody ends from the broccoli and halve any large stalks lengthways.
Whisk together the rice and plain flours along with the baking powder and caster sugar. Gradually whisk in the sparkling water until you have a loose batter that's the texture of double cream.
Lightly dust the broccoli with rice flour, dunk briefly in the batter and carefully lower into the oil.
Fry for 2-3 mins until golden brown and crunchy. Carefully transfer to a lined baking tray or rack and season with salt. Repeat with the remaining broccoli.
Meanwhile, grate the garlic into a bowl and beat in the 'nduja with a big squeeze of lemon juice. Stir in the mayo and season with salt.
Serve the hot, crispy broccoli with lemon wedges and plenty of 'nduja aioli.

name: Broccoli Pesto Pasta with Whipped Lemon Tofu
description: This broccoli pesto is made using the whole broccoli, tip to tip. The lemony whipped tofu adds creaminess and extra nutrition.
instructions: Using a food processor, a knife or a pestle and mortar, pulse the basil and pine nuts with a pinch of salt until just pulverised. You want to keep some of the pine nuts chunky.
Using the largest side of a box grater, grate the whole broccoli, stem and florets, leaving only the very tough end. Grate the garlic on the smallest side.
Cook the broccoli and garlic in a large pan with half th olive oil and a pinch of salt, on medium high, for about 8 mins until it’s starting to char.
Add the basil and pine nuts to the pan and cook for another 2-3 mins.

Meanwhile, cook your pasta as per package instructions. Drain and keep a cup of pasta water. Stir the pasta gently through the broccoli pesto in the pan. Add a splash of pasta water and plenty of olive oil.

To make the whipped lemon tofu, add the tofu, juice of the lemons, the remaining olive oil, miso, nutritional yeast, garlic powder and water to a blender. Blend until smooth and season to taste with salt and pepper. You may need to add more water to loosen it up depending on the brand of tofu you are using.

To serve, spoon a generous amount of the whipped tofu onto the bottom of a plate, then layer over the pasta and finish with some lemon zest, plenty of black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Add a few basil leaves and a handful of pine nuts to finish, if you like.

name: Broccoli Salsa Macha Rice
description: Sophie Godwin brings the MOB her ridiculously tasty broccoli dish. Topped with salsa macha - a nutty Mexican condiment that makes everything taste good. Unreal.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C/428°F.

Cut each broccoli into four wedges, leaving the stem attached. Place the broccoli cut side down on your largest roasting tray, drizzle with a good glug of olive oil and season with the cumin, salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 25-30 minutes until completely tender and a little charred.

Thinly slice the red onion and scrape into a bowl. Squeeze in the juice of 1 1/2 limes, then season with salt. Use your hands to scrunch the onion into the lime juice - this will help it quick pickle.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions. Keep warm.

Salsa macha time. Thinly slice the garlic cloves. Chop the peanuts. Set aside. Remove the stems from the ancho chillies roughly chop, then blitz the chillies in the food processor until very finely chopped - this will take a good couple of minutes.

Get a small frying pan over a medium heat. Pour in enough olive oil to cover the base of the pan by 1cm. Once simmering, add the garlic cloves, peanuts and mixed seeds. Fry, stirring for a minute until the garlic is very lightly golden and seeds are starting to pop. Stir in the ancho chillies and chilli flakes, take off the heat and leave to cool.

Meanwhile de-stone the avocados and scoop it into the food processor (no need to wash it out first - the chilli residue just adds extra flavour). Squeeze in the remaining lime juice, add 4 tablespoons of water. Blitz to a spoonable consistency, season to taste.
Come back to the cooled salsa macha. Season with a big pinch of sugar and salt.

Assembly time. Divide the cooked rice between four bowls. Spoon over the avocado then top each with two broccoli wedges, drizzle over the salsa macha. Scatter over the quick pickled red onions and tear over the coriander leaves to serve.

name: Broccoli With Red Pepper Sauce & Caper Salsa
description: Broccoli is such a versatile veg, but layering it up with all of these flavours and textures really brings it to life. Double up both of the sauces if you like as they will keep in the fridge for five days and will be a great addition to sandwiches, salads or other roasted veggies.
keywords: Broccoli With Red Pepper Sauce & Caper Salsa
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Cut the broccoli into four quarters. Drizzle with olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Roast for 20-25 mins until tender and starting to crisp at the edges.
Roast the sunflower seeds for the red pepper dip in the oven for 5-8 mins until golden.

To make the red pepper dip, blend all of the ingredients together (setting aside a quarter of the sunflower seeds for garnish) in a food processor or blender. I prefer this with a little texture, rather than totally smooth.

Zest the lemon and set it aside. Toast your cumin seeds and coriander seeds until they’re aromatic. To make the gremolata, finely chop the herbs and add them to a bowl along with all of the other ingredients.
To serve, layer up the red pepper sauce, broccoli, gremolata, lemon zest, toasted sunflower seeds and a drizzle of tahini.

name: Broccoli and Tikka Salmon Traybake
description: Spiced salmon served with all the charred veggies. So much flavour packed into a tray using lovely Ocado ingredients. Your new midweek staple. Enjoy. Sophie x
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C/374°F.
Add your cumin seeds, coriander seeds, fennel seeds and your cardamom pods into a dry frying pan and toast over a medium heat for 2 mins until fragrant.

Pour your spices into a pestle and mortar and crush them into a fine powder, discarding the shells of the cardamom pods. If you don’t have a pestle and mortar, you can pour your spices onto a large chopping board and gently crush them with the base of a heavy pan.

Pop 100g of your yoghurt into a large bowl and grate in your garlic and ginger. Add all but 1 tbsp of your toasted spice mix, along with 1 tsp of your chilli powder, your turmeric and your tomato purée. Sprinkle in a generous pinch of salt, then mix.
Add your salmon into the bowl and toss to coat, then leave to marinate for at least 30 mins, preferably a couple of hours.

Meanwhile, halve your potatoes and toss them in a large roasting tray. Drizzle with vegetable oil, plus your remaining toasted spice mix, chilli powder and a large pinch of salt. Pop in the oven to roast for 25 mins, tossing every so often so that they cook evenly.
Put your spring onions and tomatoes into the potato tray along with your broccoli. Toss so that they are coated in the oil and spices, then roast for 15 mins more.
Place your salmon fillets on top of the traybake. Bake for 5 mins.
Heat your grill to high. Pop your traybake under the grill and cook for 2 mins until the top of the salmon is starting to char.
Mix your remaining yoghurt with the juice of your lime. Roughly chop your coriander and slice your red chilli.
Drizzle your traybake with your lime yoghurt, coriander, and chopped chillies. Serve.

name: Broccoli and Walnut Rigatoni
description: Who knew that smooshing up broccoli with walnuts and bread creating such a beautiful sauce? Tossed with Napolini Rigatoni, this is a stunning mid-week meal.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil.
Cut your bread into cubes and add them to a bowl. Pour over your milk and leave the bread to soak.
Cut your broccoli head into florets, cutting any extra stalk into similar sized pieces. Finely chop your garlic.
Pop the broccoli into your boiling water pan and cook the broccoli for 4 mins until tender. Lift out of the pan with a slotted spoon and pop them in a bowl of iced water.
Toast your walnuts in a dry frying pan. Roughly chop 25g of them and set them aside.
Pop your remaining walnuts into a blender along with your milk-soaked bread, your bunch of basil, most of your parmesan and 4 tbsp of Napolina Extra Virgin Olive Oil. Blend to a smooth sauce.
Pour your Napolina Rigatoni into your broccoli water and cook for 7 mins, or until al dente.

Meanwhile, heat a glug of olive oil in a large frying pan. Add your garlic and chilli flakes and gently fry for 2 mins over a low heat. Add your broccoli and mash it up a little with your spoon to create a sauce.

Pour your walnut cream into the broccoli pan along with a ladle of pasta water and a pinch of nutmeg. Mix to combine, then tip in your rigatoni and stir until you have a sauce that clings to the pasta - add more pasta water if necessary.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then spoon into bowls and sprinkle with chopped walnuts and a little more parmesan. Serve and enjoy!

name: Broccoli, Anchovy & Chickpea Orecchiette
description: A quick and easy pasta with all the best things: anchovies, garlic, lemon and chilli. We’ve swapped half the pasta for chickpeas to up the protein and keep you feeling fuller longer.
instructions: Break the broccoli into florets and roughly chop the stems. Steam or boil them for about 5 mins until soft then drain, reserving a splash of the cooking liquid.
Meanwhile, finely chop the shallot, garlic, red chilli and fresh parsley and set aside.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the shallots and cook for 5 mins until softened then add the anchovies and break them down with the back of a spoon. Next add in the chilli and garlic and cook for a further minute.
Add the cooked broccoli to the pan with a little of its cooking liquid and break it down with a spoon until it becomes saucy.
Cook your pasta of choice following pack instructions then drain and reserve a cup of the cooking water.
Add the pasta, a splash of its cooking liquid and the chickpeas to the pan and give everything a good mix. Cook for a further minute until the pasta is coated in the sauce.
Sprinkle in the fresh parsley and squeeze over the lemon juice. Taste and add seasoning as needed. Enjoy!

name: Broccoli, Chilli and Lemon Pasta
description: This pasta is made with ‘twice-cooked’ broccoli (ripassate in Italian) it’s quickly boiled and then fried with olive oil, garlic and chilli for a simple dinner.
instructions: Bring a large pan of well salted water to the boil. Roughly chop the entire head of broccoli and add to the water.
Cook for about 5 mins until soft. Meanwhile, add a splash of olive oil to a large pan over a medium heat. Finely chop the garlic, add and cook for 3 mins until just starting to turn gold.
Add the chilli and then scoop out the broccoli and add along with half a mug of the cooking water.
Break up the broccoli with a spoon and let it simmer gently while you cook the pasta in the same pan you cooked the broccoli in.

Once the pasta is al dente, add to the pan with the broccoli along with some more cooking water, toss well, season with salt and lemon juice to taste. Then plate up and serve with an extra sprinkle of chilli.

name: Broccoli, Kale & Coconut Stir Fry
description: A simple stir fry recipe that tastes a bit like getting clobbered in the face with a coconut. In a good way, of course.
instructions: Trim the Tenderstem if needed and remove the stems of the kale. Heat half of the coconut milk in a large pan or wok over a medium heat, cooking it whilst stirring and scraping the golden solids from the bottom of the pan. It will start to smell really coconutty and sweet, this will take about 10 mins.

Peel, slice and finely chop the ginger into matchsticks, then finely slice the chilli and garlic. Add to the pan and cook for 30 seconds, followed by the Tenderstem. Cook whilst stirring for a minute or two, then add in the kale, mixing well to wilt.
Add in the rice and lime juice along with the remaining coconut milk. Cook until it’s reduced and the veg is al dente. Add in the lime juice and fish sauce, then adjust seasoning with more if needed.
Scatter with roughly chopped coriander and get stuck in.

name: Brothy Caramelised Onion Chicken with Rice
description: Inspired by Senegalese chicken yassa – we've made it into a brothy caramelised onion soup base, reminiscent of French onion soup with a zingy kick you find in yassa. It’s the perfect weeknight meal to make.
keywords: Brothy Caramelised Onion Chicken with Rice
Brothy Caramelised Onion Chicken with Rice recipe
instructions: Add the chicken into a bowl and finely grate over the garlic. Add the mustard and juice of the lemon, season with salt and plenty of black pepper and thoroughly mix together. Set aside.

Trim and thinly slice the onions. Add a drizzle of oil to a saucepan set over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the onions along with a good pinch of salt. Cook the onions, stirring occasionally until they have softened and caramelised. After about 15-20 mins they should be golden. Add a splash of water if the onions are catching on the bottom of the pan.
Meanwhile, mince the garlic. Prick a few holes into the scotch bonnet or, if you like spice, finely mince. Pick half the parsley leaves and thinly slice the rest (stems included).

Stir the chopped parsley, garlic, mustard and scotch bonnet through the onions and pour in the vinegar. Cook it out, making sure to scrape the bottom of the pan to lift any caramelised bits. Add the bay leaves and pour in the chicken stock, bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to a gentle simmer.
Meanwhile, place a frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, fry the marinated chicken for 10-15 mins until cooked through and golden on both sides.
Share the cooked rice between bowls. Taste and season the broth with lemon juice, salt and pepper before ladeling into the bowls. Top with sliced chicken and a scattering of parsley.

name: Brothy Chickpeas with Chorizo & Cavolo Nero
description: A warming recipe that's perfect during the autumn and ideal for using up seasonal veg like cavolo nero. You'll be making this one again.
keywords: Braised Chickpeas With Chorizo & Cavolo Nero
Braised Chickpeas With Chorizo & Cavolo Nero recipe
instructions: Grab a large saucepan and set it over a medium heat to preheat.

Dice the onions and finely slice the garlic and chilli. Add the onion to the pan with a shot of olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Cook for 3-4 mins then add the garlic, chilli and bay leaves. Cook for another min or two.

Halve the potatoes and strip the leaves from the cavolo nero stalks. Add them to the pan and cover with chicken stock. Add the chickpeas and bring the whole lot to the boil. Add a lid and let it bubble away for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, cut the chorizo into 1cm-thick coins and add to a small pan with a shot of olive oil. Set over a medium-low heat and let crisp up, drawing out all the bright red fat.
Remove the lid from the stew, season with salt and lemon jucie and finish with chopped dill.
Spoon into meal-prep containers and top with the chorizo. Keep in the fridge for 3 days until ready to eat and reheat.

name: Brothy Chorizo, Beans & Feta
description: Spicy, smoky, brothy beans with kale and salty feta. A one-pan wonder that’s actually ready in 15 mins and tastes like it took all day.
instructions: Add the chorizo to a large saucepan and set over a medium heat. Let it cook for a couple of minutes until it starts to leach its oil.
Stir in the onion, garlic purée and fennel seeds. Cook for 4–5 mins until the onion is soft and translucent.
Pour in the black beans and their liquid, followed by the chicken stock. Whack up the heat and bring to the boil.
Once boiling, add the kale and simmer for 3–4 mins until wilted. Taste the broth and season with salt, black pepper and lemon juice.
Ladle the brothy beans into bowls. Finish with some lemon zest and a scattering of crumbled feta.

name: Brothy Harissa Chickpeas with Melty Cheese
description: High in fibre, naturally filling, and genuinely on the table in 15 minutes. These chickpeas are simmered with squash in a brothy harissa base, finished with melty cheese and fresh basil.  Perfect with buttery toast for dunking.
instructions: Add the butternut squash, chickpeas (with their liquid), harissa paste, vegetable stock and garlic purée to a medium sized saucepan. Season with salt, then place over a high heat and bring to the boil.
Turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 7–10 mins until the squash is tender. Meanwhile, toast the bread and spread the butter over one side of each slice.
Ladle the brothy chickpeas into bowls and top with the cheese and torn basil. Serve with the buttered toast on the side.

name: Brothy Kale Noodle Soup
description: A light, easy and nutritious cavolo nero and noodle soup. Perfect for when you need a bowl of goodness on your table in less than 15 minutes.
instructions: Remove and discard the tough stems of the cavolo nero, then chop the leaves into slices and place in a steamer basket or sieve.
Heat up the stock in a small pot.

Bring a medium pot of salted water to the boil, then reduce to a simmer. Add the soba noodles into the pot, rest the sieve or steamer basket with the kale on top, then cover with a lid. Cook the noodles following packet instructions, then drain and place the noodles and the cavolo nero into a bowl.
Pour the hot stock over the noodles and cavolo nero. Finely chop the chives and sprinkle them on top, followed by a splash of tamari and the black sesame seeds.

name: Brothy Miso Beans on Garlic Toast
description: This is beans on toast but upgraded. Packed full of creaminess, umami, crunch and a double whammy of garlic in the garlic toast and the crispy topping. This is a delicious, healthy, protein packed meal for any time of the day.
keywords: Brothy Miso Beans on Garlic Toast
Brothy Miso Beans on Garlic Toast recipe
instructions: Empty the tin of beans, with the liquid, into a saucepan and turn the heat up to medium-high. Cook for 5 mins, stirring every so often; it should be simmering gently. Then add the miso and nutritional yeast and stir well until they have both completely dissolved.

Taste the beans and if they are not very tender and melting in your mouth, continue to cook them. You can add more water if needed, to keep it brothy and loose. Keep cooking them until they are very soft. Season to taste with plenty of salt and pepper and stir through a good drizzle of olive oil which will make them rich and creamy.
Toast the bread, then rub a garlic clove onto each one. Rub the clove all over the bread, until it has dissolved into it.

To serve, put the garlic toast into a large plate or shallow bowl, then ladle over the brothy beans. Drizzle over some olive oil and harissa, then finish with a squeeze of lemon, if using, the crispy fried shallots, more black pepper and fresh herbs.
Any leftover beans can be stored in the fridge but add some water to heat them up again.

name: Brothy Orzo & Meatballs
description: A fast way to use up leftovers from our Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake. This herby, garlicky orzo broth is super comforting, and the meatballs and chickpeas make it packed with protein.
instructions: Make the Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake.
Pick the herb leaves and discard the stems. Thinly slice the red chilli.

Pour the stock into a large saucepan and bring to the boil. Once boiling, tip in the orzo and cook for 2 mins less than the packet instructions, the orzo will keep cooking in the broth. If you want it looser, just add more stock or a splash of water.
Stir in the lamb meatball traybake mix and half the herbs. Let everything simmer until piping hot and the orzo is tender. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Ladle into bowls and finish with the remaining herbs, the sliced chilli and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Brothy Pasta & Greens
description: A warming, brothy pasta that comes together in the time it takes to boil the pasta. Ginger-spiked chicken stock, ditalini, chickpeas and wilted watercress, comforting but light, with barely any washing up.
instructions: Finely grate the ginger and add it to a saucepan with a drizzle of olive oil. Place over a medium heat and leave to sizzle for 2-3 mins until fragrant.
Pour in the stock and bring to the boil, then stir in the ditalini and cook according to packet instructions. Meanwhile, use scissors to snip any large watercress stems.
Once the pasta is cooked, stir in the watercress and chickpeas and cook for a minute until wilted. Taste and season the broth with salt and pepper. Pour into a bowl and drizzle over the hot sauce.

name: Brothy Red Curry Noodles
description: This spicy red broth hits all the right notes. Rich, punchy, packed with prawns, and slurpably satisfying.
instructions: Add the rice noodles to a heatproof bowl and cover with boiling water. Let them sit for 4 mins until softened, then drain and rinse under cold water. Set aside.
Dice the tofu into bite-sized cubes. Halve any large mushrooms and trim the broccoli into bite-sized florets.
Add a third of the coconut milk to a large, heavy-bottomed saucepan set over a medium heat. Let it cook for 4–5 mins until the fat begins to separate from the milk.
Stir in the red curry paste and cook for 4–5 mins, stirring regularly, until fragrant. Add the sugar and cook for another 2 mins. Stir through half of the fish sauce.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk along with water. Bring to a simmer.
Add the mushrooms and tofu and cook for 2 mins. Add the broccoli and prawns and simmer for a final 3 mins until the prawns are cooked through.
Squeeze in half of the lime and season the broth with the remaining fish sauce. Taste and adjust with more salt or lime juice, if needed.
Divide the noodles between two bowls and ladle over the brothy curry. Finish with lime wedges and a handful of chopped coriander.

name: Brothy Roast Squash & Pasta With Greens
description: Think of this recipe as a wintery minestrone, but less soupy and topped with green pesto for a low effort zhuzh. It’s warming, easy and packed full of vitamins to keep you healthy over the colder months.
keywords: Brothy Roast Squash & Pasta With Greens
Brothy Roast Squash & Pasta With Greens recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel and dice the butternut squash into 1cm cubes. Tip onto a baking tray, drizzle over half the olive oil, season with salt and pepper and roast for 20-25 mins.

Finely chop the rosemary, slice the garlic and remove the kale leaves from their stems (discard the stems). Heat the remaining olive oil in a pan set over a medium heat and fry the garlic for 2 mins until turning golden, then add the rosemary and cook for 1 min. Add the tomato purée and cook for 1 min, then add the stock and pasta. Give it a stir, bring to the boil and reduce to a simmer. Cook the pasta for 2 mins less than the pack instructions, until the pasta is al dente.
When the pasta is cooked, add the kale leaves and squash cubes and mix until wilted. Spoon into bowls and top with pesto and black pepper.

name: Brothy Roast Tomatoes, Fennel & Giant Couscous
description: This recipe doesn't require a lot of prep and it's extremely comforting. A great one to use as a blueprint for whatever you have on hand.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the fennel into wedges and reserve the fronds. Add to a roasting tray with the cherry tomatoes and drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper, then cook for 20-25 mins, until all the veg is tender and a little charred.

Peel and finely slice the garlic. Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a large pot and cook the garlic over a medium heat until softened and slightly golden. Add the couscous and toast for 2 mins until it starts to smell nutty, then pour in the vegetable stock. Cook according to package instructions, and then finely chop the dill.

When everything is ready, serve the brothy couscous in bowls and top with the roasted tomato and fennel, making sure to get all the juices in there too. Top with chopped dill, fennel fronds, black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Brothy Slow-Cooked Coconut Chicken & Rice
description: Transform leftovers from our Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken into a golden, soupy rice bowl with fresh coriander, zingy lime and crispy onion on top. It’s pure comfort.
instructions: Make the Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken batch recipe.
Tip the chicken and coconut broth into a saucepan with the chicken stock. Set over a medium heat and warm through until piping hot.

Lift out the chicken pieces, if you’re using the breast, slice it up. If you’ve got leg meat, shred it with two forks. Taste the broth and season with salt, black pepper and a good squeeze of lime juice, if it needs it.
Reheat the rice and divide between bowls. Ladle over the hot broth, then top with the sliced or shredded chicken. Garnish with coriander leaves, crispy onions and serve with lime wedges on the side.

name: Brothy Smoky Pepper Prawns with Saffron Rice
description: A vibrant, nourishing and incredibly comforting bowl. The flavours of paella in a quick, soupy rice.
keywords: Brothy Smoky Pepper Prawns With Saffron Rice
instructions: Place the saffron and ice into a small bowl and set aside. The ice will melt and the saffron will bloom.

Meanwhile, peel, trim and finely grate the garlic directly into a saucepan. Pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the stalks. Add the stalks to the pan with the garlic, along with a drizzle of olive oil.

Get the saucepan over a medium-high heat. Cook for 2-3 mins, stirring until the parsley stalks have softened. Add the tomato purée and smoked paprika and fry off for 3-4 mins until the tomato purée has darkened.

Pour the stock into the saucepan and bring it up to a gentle simmer. Once simmering, decrease the heat to low, add the prawns and leave them to poach for 2-3 mins until cooked through (skim any foam out and discard). Add ½ the saffron water and season to taste with salt and lemon juice.
Pour the remaining saffron water over the cooked rice and reheat. Make sure to stir the rice thoroughly after reheating.

Divide the rice between bowls and ladle in the broth. Top with the poached prawns and parsley leaves. Drizzle over some olive oil and serve with any remaining lemon, and some chopped red chilli if you like.

name: Brothy Sumac Chicken & Giant Couscous
description: Transform your batch of Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake into this fragrant, soupy broth with giant couscous, warm cumin butter and cooling yoghurt. A perfect warming bowl of goodness.
keywords: zingy brothy chicken giant couscous recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake.

Shred the chicken from the Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake. Add it to a large saucepan with the chicken stock and set over a medium-high heat. Once boiling, tip in the giant couscous and cook according to the packet instructions.

Meanwhile, place a small frying pan over a medium heat with the ghee or butter. Once melted, add the cumin seeds and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant. Remove from the heat, stir through the smoked paprika and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Once the giant couscous is cooked, stir the roasted vegetables from the traybake through the soup, topping up with water if needed. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Ladle the soup into bowls, then top with a dollop of Greek yoghurt, a drizzle of the cumin butter and a few parsley leaves.

name: Brothy Tom Yum with Pork & Shiitake Cabbage Rolls
description: Inspired by the classic Thai soup, these pork and shiitake mince parcels are simmered in a fragrant, spicy, tangy tom yum broth. A proper bowl of nourishment that Chloe's seriously perfected.
keywords: Tom Yum Brothy Cabbage Rolls recipe
instructions: Trim the lemongrass and cut into 3cm chunks. Remove and discard the mushroom stalks. Roughly chop the shallot and celery. Pick the coriander leaves and keep the stems. Separate the cabbage leaves and trim any bulky stems.

If you have a food processor, add the lemongrass, coriander stems, shallot, shiitake mushrooms, celery and half the coriander leaves and blitz until finely minced. Add the pork mince, fish sauce and breadcrumbs, then blitz again until uniform and thoroughly mixed. If you don't have a food processor, finely mince all the filling ingredients by hand and stir through the mince with the fish sauce and breadcrumbs.
Fill and boil a kettle. Place the cabbage leaves in a large bowl, pour over the boiling water and leave to sit for 2-3 mins, until pliable. Drain and pat dry.

Lay a blanched cabbage leaf flat and place 2-3 tbsp of the mince mixture at the widest end. Roll it up like a burrito, tucking the sides in as you go. Repeat until all the mince is used up, you should end up with around three rolls per person.

Set a large, deep frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the curry paste and tomato purée and stir-fry for 2-3 mins, until dark red and fragrant. Add the lime leaves, pour in a third of the stock and stir together. Nestle the cabbage rolls seam-side down into the sauce, then pour over the remaining stock. Bring to the boil, put a lid on, turn the heat down to low and simmer for 15-20 mins, until the mince is fully cooked through.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice according to packet instructions. Once the rolls are cooked, taste the broth and season with fish sauce and a squeeze of lime, it should be a little tangy.
Divide the rice between bowls, top with the cabbage rolls and ladle over the broth. Finish with a scattering of coriander leaves and serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Brothy White Bean Chilli on Toast
description: Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli ladled over thick golden toast and finished with grated halloumi and fresh coriander. A seriously good lunch from last night's batch.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli batch recipe.
Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems, keeping them separate.
Add a drizzle of olive oil to a frying pan and place over a medium heat. Once hot, add the bread and toast on both sides for 2-4 mins, until golden brown.
Meanwhile, add your leftover Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli and the coriander stems to a saucepan over a medium heat. Cook for 4-6 mins, until piping hot.
Place the toast onto plates, ladle over the brothy beans and finely grate over the halloumi. Finish with a scattering of coriander leaves.

name: Brothy White Bean Chilli with Feta Drizzle
description: An effortless way to transform leftovers from your Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli batch into a warming Mexican soup.
keywords: Brothy White Bean Chilli with Feta Drizzle
Brothy White Bean Chilli with Feta Drizzle recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli batch recipe.
Tip the leftover Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli into a saucepan with the stock and reheat over a medium heat for 4-6 mins until piping hot. Taste and season with salt if needed.

Meanwhile, crumble the feta into a heatproof bowl. Pour the olive oil into a small saucepan and add the pumpkin seeds. Place over a medium heat and cook for 2-3 mins until the seeds are toasted. Remove from the heat, stir through the chipotle paste and pour over the crumbled feta.
Divide the brothy chilli between bowls and squeeze over the lime. Drizzle over the feta mixture and serve with the tortilla crisps alongside.

name: Brown Butter & Almond Salmon with Orange Salad
description: Charred, crisp-skinned salmon topped with toasty brown butter almonds, served alongside a zingy fennely orange, chicory and grain salad. Ideal for summer weeknight evening when you fancy something fresh and light but don't want to spend ages cooking.
keywords: Brown Butter & Almond Salmon with Orange Salad
Brown Butter & Almond Salmon with Orange Salad recipe
instructions: Start by making the salad dressing. Lightly crush the fennel seeds using a pestle and mortar or the flat of a knife, then add to a bowl with the Dijon mustard, white wine vinegar and extra virgin olive oil, mixing to combine.

Cut the top and bottom off each orange, then slice away the peel and pith following the curve. Cut between the membranes to release segments. Break off the leaves from the chicory and add to a bowl with the spelt and dill.

Season the salmon fillets with salt and black pepper. Heat a large frying pan over a high heat and add a splash of olive oil. Add the salmon, skin-side down, pressing down firmly with a spatula for 30 seconds so the skin makes full contact with the pan.

Cook for 4-5 mins without moving, until the skin is deeply charred and crisp, then flip and cook for a further 2 mins on each side, until golden, keeping the flesh slightly pink in the centre (or to your liking).
Remove the salmon from the pan and turn down the heat low. Add the butter and flaked almonds, stirring so the almonds toast in the butter for 1 min. Take off the heat and pour over the salmon.
Toss the salad with the dressing, then serve alongside the salmon and almonds.

name: Brown Butter & Green Bean Linguine
description: This is a version of ‘scraps pasta’ from Kitty Coles's cookbook, 'It Takes 15 Minutes', and we love it. You can swap the green beans for a thinly-sliced or peeled courgette, if you like. We love linguine for this, but any pasta type will do. We've used snapped lasagne sheets when the cupboards are really running dry.
keywords: Brown Butter & Green Bean Linguine recipe
instructions: Start by making the breadcrumbs, if not using shop-bought panko. Blitz the stale bread in a food processor. Add a splash of olive oil to a medium frying pan set over a medium heat, then tip in the breadcrumbs and a pinch of salt. Stir often for 2-3 mins until they start to crisp up, then add the almonds and continue to gently fry until everything is golden (add more olive oil, if necessary). Tip the breadcrumbs onto a plate lined with kitchen paper to cool.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta following pack instructions. Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley and zest the lemon. Set aside.
Peel and finely slice the garlic.

Get a medium frying pan over a medium heat, add the butter and let it melt. Carry on cooking the butter, whisking occasionally, until it turns from golden and foamy to a caramel brown colour and smells nutty. Add a splash of olive oil, the garlic and capers and cook for 1 min. Add the chili flakes, lemon zest and juice, caper brine, finely chopped parsley and salt and pepper. Allow to bubble for a minute then turn the heat to low.
When the pasta has 2 mins left, add the green beans to cook them. Drain everything, reserving a mug of pasta water (very important!).
Add the pasta, green beans and a splash of pasta water to the pan with the capers and brown butter, then give it a mix. Now grate in the Parmesan and mix again, adding more pasta water if needed.
Divide between two plates and top with the breadcrumbs and extra Parmesan, if you like.

name: Brown Butter Beef Kofta Barley Bowls
description: A high-protein, high-fibre grain bowl that ticks a lot of boxes. One for the gym heads out there.
keywords: Brown Butter Beef Kofta Barley Bowls
instructions: Rinse the pearl barley. Place a saucepan on medium-high heat. Tip the barley and water in, let it come to the boil. Place a lid on, decrease the heat to low and cook for 40 mins, adding more water if needed.
Pick the parsley leaves, thinly slice the stalks.

Add the beef mince into a bowl. Trim and finely grate half the onions, three-quarters of the cloves of garlic onto it, and stir the parsley stalks, oregano, pul biber, and half the sumac through, season generously with salt, and mix. Portion the mince out evenly and shape into thick sausages. Gently press down to flatten them slightly.
Thinly slice the onion, toss with the sumac and season with salt. Set aside. Before serving, toss the parsley leaves through.
Finely grate the remaining garlic into a bowl and stir through the yoghurt. Season with salt.

Place a frying pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the koftas and cook until golden brown, 5-8 mins. Add the butter and cook until browned and nutty, then add the tomatoes and stir through until just starting to soften.
Share the barley between bowls, top with the koftas and onion salad. Finish with a drizzle of garlic yoghurt.

name: Brown Butter Blondies
description: These blondies are squidgy, gooey and nutty in flavour. Add whatever mix-ins you like, be it white chocolate, nuts, raspberries or a combination of them all.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C/140°C Fan. Grease a 20cm brownie tin or small roasting tin with the butter foil then line the base with baking paper.

Get a large saucepan over a low to medium heat. Dump in the block of butter and let it melt. Once the butter has completely melted start whisking. Within a couple of minutes the butter will have changed from pale yellow to a nutty brown and you will be able to smell it. As soon as it smells nutty take the pan off the heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes. Brown butter done.
Roughly chop any mix-ins you’re using then come back to your butter.

Whisk in the brown sugar until smooth then crack in the eggs, add the vanilla extract, milk and a big pinch of salt. Whisk to combine then add your flour, whisk again. Finally stir through 3/4 of your mix-ins.

Pour the blondie batter into your tin then drop in the remaining mix-ins. Bake in the centre of your oven for 35-40 minutes until the outside is cooked but the centre still has a good wobble - this blondie is so buttery and gooey that the centre will deflate a little once cool. That’s the best bit.
Leave to cool completely in the tin then cut into squares. Will keep for up to 5 days in a container out of the fridge.

name: Brown Butter Miso Udon
description: Love brown butter? Love miso? Love a jammy egg? Then this quick and easy dish is the one for you. Xien x
keywords: Brown butter red miso udon recipes
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to boil then add your udon and cook according to packet instructions. Drain your udon, keeping the noodle water.
Pop your eggs into another pot of boiling water and cook for 6 ½ mins to get perfect jammy eggs. Once boiled, pop them into an ice-cold water bath to stop them from cooking.
Mince your garlic and finely slice your shallot.

On medium-low heat, melt the butter in a pan, continuously stirring and when it starts to smell nutty, add the garlic and shallot. Lower the heat then add your miso paste. Loosen the mix up with a splash of noodle water.
Then add your udon to the sauce and season well with salt and pepper. Squeeze in half a lemon. Stir your noodles gently you get a thick, glossy sauce and give it a good shake in the pan.
Peel your eggs.
Grate over parmesan and lemon zest. Serve with your perfect jammy eggs and nori, and tuck in.

name: Brown Butter Old Fashioned
description: A sweet and buttery cocktail that's made using homemade brown butter whiskey. A perfect wintery treat.
instructions: Using a peeler, get a twist of orange to use for garnish.
In a glass, add your sugar and then bitters, using a spoon to mix until the sugar is incorporated and slightly dissolved.
Then add a small amount of your whiskey and mix further.
Add your large ice cube and then the rest of the whiskey.
Stir for 2-3 mins allowing the sugar to dissolve slowly and the ice the melt.
Express the oils of the orange twist over your drink and then wipe the rim of the glass with it, finally placing it in the drink itself.
Enjoy.

name: Brown Butter Spaghetti
description: This is the simplest, sexiest pasta dish. I make it every week. The combo of cheese, butter and pasta water creates the silkiest sauce. Sophie x
instructions: Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Season with a pinch of salt, then once it comes to a boil again tip in your spaghetti. Cook for a couple of minutes less than the packet specifies, until al dente.
Meanwhile, grate your parmesan and pecorino.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add your butter. Once it melts, grind in a generous amount of black pepper and keep cooking for a few minutes longer until you can see the white flecks (the milk solids) turn golden and your kitchen smells like a digestive biscuit.
Turn down the heat to a simmer, then add a ladle of your pasta cooking water to the pan and allow it to bubble up and simmer until it becomes a homogenous mixture.

Remove your spaghetti from it’s pan with tongs and drop it into the melted butter mixture. Add another ladle of pasta water and let it continue cooking for a minute until perfectly tender, tossing around to get it all coated in the brown butter. Sprinkle both your cheeses on top and let them totally melt before tossing your pasta around the pan with your tongs until you have a smooth, creamy, homogenous sauce that coats each length of pasta. Add more pasta water if necessary.
Serve up immediately whilst still hot and glossy, and enjoy.

name: Brown Butter Squash Pasta
description: A sweet and nutty pasta dish that's perfect for the autumn. Caramelising your squash is the key to this dish.
instructions: Start by peeling and dicing the squash. You want to try and dice as small as you can. Don’t spend forever doing it, just get them pretty small. We’re cooking these through completely in a pan, no oven roasting, so the smaller you cut them, the quicker they’ll cook.
Finely dice the onion and chop the garlic cloves and chilli. Pick the sage leaves from the stems and roughly chop.

Bring a pan of water to a boil and season heavily with salt. Grab a large, lidded saucepan and set over a medium heat. Add the butter plus a couple of tablespoons of olive oil. Tip in the squash, add a pinch of salt, give ‘em a stir and add the lid. Cook, stirring now and then, for 10-12 mins, until the squash is tender and starting to caramelise. Add the onion and cook for 3-4 mins.
Drop your spaghetti into the boiling water and set a timer for 8 mins. We want the pasta to be pretty al dente when it lands in the sauce pan, we’ll cook it in the sauce for a good few minutes.
Add the garlic, chilli and sage to the squash pan and keep on cooking for those 8 mins over a medium heat. Everything should be looking nicely caramelised and roasted.

Transfer the cooked pasta to the sauce with a couple of big ladles of water. Start tossing and turning the pasta through the sauce, the squash and butter will begin to come together to make a sauce. Keep adding pasta water as needed until you have a delicious, rich sauce. Finish with grated Parmesan and lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper and divide between warm plates. Add extra sage and grated Parm.

name: Brown Butter Squash Tortelloni
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A really easy butternut squash pasta sauce that’s packed full of flavour. Simple, affordable and delicious.
instructions: Start by peeling and dicing the squash. You want to try and dice as small as you can. We’re cooking these through completely in the pan, no oven roasting, so the smaller you cut them, the quicker they’ll cook. Thinly slice the garlic cloves and red chilli.

Grab a large lidded frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Add plenty of olive oil and the butter before tipping in the squash. Pop the lid on the pan and cook the squash for 15-20 mins, stirring now and then, until it steams in its own liquid and starts to caramelise a little.
Remove the lid and add the sliced garlic and chilli. Sweat with the cooked squash for a couple of mins before adding a splash of water and using a fork to squish some of the squash into a sauce.
Meanwhile, bring a pot of water to a boil, season generously and cook the tortelloni following packet instructions.
Finely chop the parsley and tip into a bowl with the zest and juice of the lemons. Mix with a little olive oil.

Transfer the cooked tortelloni to the sauce and toss together. To serve, divide between bowls and top with a few spoons of the gremolata parsley dressing, a drizzle of olive oil, a little black pepper and some grated Parmesan.

name: Brown Butter Whiskey
description: Homemade brown butter whiskey. You'll feel like an absolute pro pulling this out at your next festive dinner party.
instructions: Pour out around 150ml of whiskey from the bottle.
Melt all the butter and heat making sure to stir regularly until it foams up.
At this point turn down the heat, keep stirring and watch for light brown specks to form. It should have a very nutty aroma at this point.
It’s easy to cook the butter so be sure to take it off the heat and pour into a bowl to stop it cooking.
Using a funnel, pour in all the butter into the whiskey and shake vigorously.
Leave to stand for 2 hours shaking every half hour.
Place in the freezer overnight.
Remove from the freezer and using a skewer gently break up the butter in the bottle.
Using a coffee filter or cheesecloth, filter the whiskey into a clean bottle. Do this twice to ensure a pure and clean whiskey.
If you like, return the other 150ml of whiskey to the bottle now – this will, however, dilute the flavour slightly. Label with date and flavour.

name: Brown Sugar Boba Milk Tea
description: Making homemade boba tea isn't as hard as you think. This sweet drink makes for a fun weekend project.
instructions: Mix your water and dark brown sugar in a saucepan until dissolved, bring to a boil then immediately remove from heat.
Add 3-4 tbsp of the tapioca flour then mix to combine.
Return to the heat and whisk for 3 mins until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat and add the rest of the tapioca flour – this doesn’t have to be fully incorporated right away.
Pour the mixture onto a tapioca-floured work surface and start working the dough with your hands.

If your dough is too wet, add more tapioca. If it's too hard, add some more water. You are looking for a texture that keeps its shape when rolled into a ball. You don’t want it to be crumbling in your hands but you don’t want it to be turning into goo either.
Roll out your dough into a log and cut it into four equal parts.

Take one of your logs and roll it out further. Now take a pea-sized lump off and roll it in the palm of your hand into a small ball, each pearl must be small enough to fit up your straw so be careful you don’t make them too big.
When all your pearls are rolled out, weigh them and then boil them in a saucepan of boiling water. The amount of water you need should be 6-7 times the weight of the pearls.
Boil for 35-40 mins until the pearls and soft and gooey. Don’t worry if your water has become very viscous, this is totally normal.
Take the pearls out with a slotted spoon and submerge in ice cold water to clean off any excess tapioca water solution.
Make some black tea and leave it to brew and cool down for 5 mins.
Get some brown sugar and add it to a pan with an equal weight of water.
Bring this to a boil and let it reduce until you are left with a thick sugar syrup.
Using a milk frother, or just a spoon if you don’t have one, decorate the inside of your glass with the sugar syrup and add an extra spoon of it to the glass.
Add as many of the tapioca pearls as your heart desires.
Add your tea and milk with some ice.
Put your lid on and enjoy! Make sure you have a thick straw.

name: Brownie Chunk Ice Cream
description: Indulgent vanilla ice cream with soft, fudgy brownie pieces. A match made in heaven.
keywords: Brownie Chunk Ice Cream Recipe recipe
instructions: Pour the milk into a pan, add the vanilla pod and bring slowly up to scalding point – do not let it reach the boil. Cover the surface with clingfilm to prevent a skin forming, then leave to cool and infuse with the vanilla for approximately 1 hour. Once cool, carefully remove the vanilla pod from the pan and scrape out the seeds into the milk.
Tip a bag of ice cubes into the sink and place a large wide metal bowl on top, to chill the bowl. Alternatively, place a metal bowl in the freezer.
In a bowl, beat together the egg yolks and sugar until thick and fluffy – approximately 4 mins. Pour in the vanilla milk and stir until you get a thin custard.

Pour the mixture into a clean heavy-bottomed pan, place over a medium heat and stir continuously with a wooden spoon as you slowly bring it nearly to the boil.
