When the custard has thickened and the foam bubbles on the surface have disappeared, remove it from the heat, whisk it for a couple of mins with a large balloon whisk (this will help it to cool quicker), then pour into your cold, dry metal bowl.
Leave it to cool for approximately 10 mins, stirring occasionally to prevent a skin forming.

If churning in an ice cream maker: turn on your ice cream maker and roughly chop the brownies. Once the mixture has cooled, stir in the cream, churn in the ice cream maker for 15 mins. Stir through the brownie pieces, then churn for another 15-20 mins. Transfer to an ice cream container and place in the freezer to set completely.

If churning by hand: once the mixture is cool, put it into the fridge for 1-2 hours. Remove, stir in the cream and transfer to an ice cream container. Pop it in the freezer for half an hour (meanwhile, roughly chop the brownies) then give it a churn with a spoon and stir through the brownies pieces. Return to the freezer to set completely.

name: Bruce Bogtrotter Cake
description:
This might be the chocolate cake to end all chocolate cakes. Think Bruce Bogtrotter on steroids. Tuck in. Imagine sinking your fork into layers of rich, chocolaty sponges, baked to perfection with cocoa and unsalted butter, creating a fudge-like texture that's every chocoholic’s dream. A touch of bicarb soda keeps the cake airy, while a generous coating of cream and chocolate icing ensures each bite melts in your mouth. The crust adds a satisfying contrast to the moist interior, and for a twist, serve with a side of custard or a fruit mocktail.

Perfect for any home cook, this cake is a showstopper at gatherings, outshining even the most festive Christmas cake or decadent baked Alaska. Whether you’re a fan of street food or fine restaurant cuisines, this baked masterpiece will have you coming back for more, making it the ultimate chocolaty indulgence.
instructions: For the ganache, finely chop the dark chocolate and transfer to a large bowl. Put the cream and sugar in a saucepan and gently heat until almost simmering and the sugar has dissolved – don’t let it boil! Remove from the heat and cool for a couple of minutes, then pour the mixture over the chocolate. Let it stand for 3-4 mins before mixing gently from the centre with a spatula. Gradually move the spatula outwards to incorporate the chocolate. Pour the ganache into two deep baking trays, cover with cling film and refrigerate overnight.

Heat the oven to 180°C. Lightly butter and line 3 x 20cm loose-bottomed cake tins. Tip the flour, bicarbonate of soda, both sugars, a pinch of salt and the cocoa powder into a large mixing bowl. If there are any hard lumps of sugar, break them up using your fingers.

Whisk the eggs, vanilla extract and soured cream together in another large bowl. Set aside. Finely chop the chocolate and dice the butter, then add both to a saucepan and melt over a medium heat, stirring continuously, until totally combined. Set aside. Put the coffee granules into a jug and top up with the boiling water.

Pour the soured cream mix into the dry ingredients along with the coffee and melted chocolate. Fold together using a large metal spoon until combined – do not over-mix. Divide half of the mixture between the lined cake tins and pop into the oven for 15 mins. You can check if they’re cooked by poking each cake through the centre with a skewer – if it comes out clean, the cake is ready! If not, return the cakes to the oven for a couple of minutes.

Set the cooked cakes aside to cool, then turn them out onto a cooling rack. Clean the cake tins and repeat the process with the remaining cake mixture. Once the last three cakes are out of the oven and cool, you can remove the baking paper.

When you are ready to assemble, coat a sponge layer with a 1cm-thick layer of ganache, smoothing out with a spatula, then top with another sponge. Repeat, coating each additional sponge with the same 1cm-thick layer of ganache, until all of the sponges are stacked. Spread the outside of the cake with a thin layer of ganache and let it air-dry for a couple of hours, or preferably overnight – this will help set the cake so you don’t get crumbs in the icing. Cover with the remaining ganache then use a hot offset spatula or blowtorch to smooth everything out and make it shiny.

For the topping, finely chop the chocolate and set aside. Heat the double cream with the sugar in a small saucepan – don’t let it boil! Stir until the sugar is dissolved, then pour over the chocolate. Let it stand for 3-4 mins, then stir from the middle to slowly incorporate the chocolate. Let it cool and thicken, then pour over the top of the cake, spreading out with a spatula, encouraging it to drip down the sides. Let it set.
Heat a knife before cutting to make the ganache extra shiny inside.

name: Brussels Sprout Pad Thai
description: A naughty little alternative to your traditional Pad Thai with charred Brussels and caramelised smoked tofu. Ohhhhhh the textures.
instructions: Trim the bases off the brussel sprouts and cut them in half. Cut the tofu into roughly 1cm squares. Cut the lime into four wedges. Finely chop the garlic cloves.
For the sauce, mix together the tamarind, soy, chilli oil and soft brown sugar. Set aside.
Soak the rice noodles in a large bowl full of hot water for 10 minutes.

While the noodles are soaking, get a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Pour in some vegetable oil. Add the sprouts. Stir fry for about 4 minutes until beginning to soften and lightly colour then scrape in the garlic. Cook for 1 minute more.

Scrape the brussels and garlic to one side of the pan. Pour in a splash more oil and add the tofu. Fry for 3 minutes until beginning to crisp then turn the heat to the lowest whilst you drain the noodles.

Get the pan back on the heat, tip in the drained noodles along with a splash of water. Give everything a good mix, fry for 2 minutes then pour in the sauce. Cook for a further 2 minutes until the noodles are soft enough to eat then add the beansprouts and most of the peanuts to the pan.
Give everything one last toss then dish the Pad Thai into bowls. Top with the remaining peanuts, a squeeze of lime and some torn coriander. You’re ready to plate up and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Brussels Sprout Pakoras
description: I think I've developed the crispiest pakora about... using Brussels sprouts. Serve them with a sweet, tangy cranberry chutney. They are so good MOB. Seema x
instructions: Chop up your Brussels sprouts in half and then slice thinly and slice your onions. Roughly chop the coriander, finely chop the chilli and grate the ginger. Finally, crush the cumin seeds and black pepper.

In a bowl combine turmeric, chilli powder, coriander, chilli, ginger, cumin, black pepper, gram flour and water with 1 tsp of salt. Mix well and then add the onions and Brussels sprouts. This should create a thick batter.
Heat up a wok about halfway of oil.
Using a spoon, drop in small balls of the batter and fry for 2 minutes on either side until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.

For the chutney, roughly chop the mint and peel the ginger. In a bowl mix the cranberry sauce, honey and water. Grate in the ginger, add the mint and squeeze in the lemon juice. Mix well and enjoy with your crispy pakoras.

name: Buffalo Aubergines & Ranch Orzotto
description: Sticky, spicy buffalo-glazed aubergines on top of a herby, creamy orzotto that eats like risotto but cooks in a fraction of the time.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Trim the aubergines and chop into 3cm batons. Transfer to a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and black pepper, toss and bake for 20-25 mins until softened and golden.

Meanwhile, add the orzo, onion granules and water to a medium saucepan and grate in the garlic. Season with salt and black pepper and bring to the boil. Lower the heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is al dente, check your pack for timings.
Reserve a couple of dill fronds and thinly slice a few chives, setting both aside for garnish. Finely mince the rest of the herbs, stalks and all.
Before serving, stir the herbs through the orzo along with the crème fraîche and Parmesan. Taste and season with salt and black pepper, adding a splash of water if it's too thick.

Once the aubergines are softened and golden, remove from the oven and add the butter and buffalo hot sauce. Stir together until the butter melts, if needed, pop the tray back in the oven for a couple of minutes to help it along.
Divide the orzotto between bowls, top with the aubergines and pour over any sauce. Finish with the reserved herbs.

name: Buffalo Chicken Quinoa Salad
description: This is our healthier take on everyone's favourite buffalo chicken. We’ve taken the flavours and made it into a quinoa bowl that you can wolf down post gym. We’ve used sour cream as the sauce here, feel free to swap out for Greek yoghurt if you prefer instead.
instructions: Chop three-quarters of your chives and mix into the soured cream. Season to taste. Slice the courgettes into diagonal slices. Set aside.
Rinse the quinoa then cook according to packet instructions then drain, tip into a bowl.
Meanwhile, season the chicken with salt and pepper.

Get your largest non-stick pan with a lid over a medium high heat. Drizzle in a good splash of olive oil. Add the chicken thighs and brown for 2-3 mins on each side until golden. Pour 100ml of water into the pan, put a lid on the pan and simmer the chicken for 6-8 minutes until cooked through.
Meanwhile, pour a drizzle of olive oil into a second large frying pan, fry the courgettes in batches for 2 minutes on each side until golden and charred.
Come back to the chicken, add 2 tbsp of hot sauce to the pan, shred the chicken with 2 forks then transfer to a bowl.

Finely slice the garlic cloves, put a frying pan back over a medium heat, add a good splash of olive oil and the garlic. Cook for a minute or so, stirring until the garlic is lightly golden. Take the pan off the heat and stir through the remaining hot sauce and vinegar.
Roughly chop herbs of your choice and stir through the quinoa.
Build up your quinoa bowls, with piles of chicken, courgette then spoon over the dressing and the sour cream and chive. Top with more chives and toasted seeds of your choice, to serve.

name: Buffalo Chicken, Celery & Blue Cheese Grain Bowl
description: All the best bits of buffalo wings served up in a punchy grain bowl. Spicy chicken, cooling yoghurt, tangy blue cheese, and crunchy celery.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Add the chicken thighs to a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle over the smoked paprika, garlic granules, brown sugar, salt and pepper. Drizzle with a bit more oil and spread into an even layer, skin-side up. Roast for 45 mins until cooked through and golden crisp.
Drizzle your hot sauce (we used Frank's Red Hot Sauce) over the cooked chicken and return to the oven for 5 more mins. Set aside to rest while you prep everything else.

Finely dice the celery and add to a large bowl. Crumble the blue cheese into bite-sized chunks and add to the bowl. Heat the grain pouches according to pack instructions, then tip the grains into the same bowl.
Add the natural yoghurt, apple cider vinegar and garlic granules. Season with salt and pepper, then mix well. Tear in most of the dill and gently fold through.
Divide the grain salad between containers or bowls and top each with 2 buffalo chicken thighs. Finish with the remaining dill and a little extra drizzle of hot sauce, if you like.

name: Buffalo Wing Traybake & Celery Blue Cheese Slaw
description: This one has it all. Succulent chicken wings, juicy celery sticks, creamy blue cheese, and tangy buffalo sauce. It's pretty simple to make and your tastebuds will love you for it.
keywords: roasted wing traybake celery blue cheese slaw
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Tip the chicken wings into a large oven tray. Halve the potatoes and get them into the tray, too. Drizzle the lot with olive oil and season with plenty of salt and pepper. Toss to coat and slide into the oven for 45 mins. Toss and turn the wings and potatoes a few times during the cook.
While the wings are roasting, whip up the salad. Add the yoghurt to a large mixing bowl and crumble in the blue cheese. Add the juice of a lemon, plenty of black pepper, and mix to combine.
Finely slice the hispi cabbage and celery. Core and thinly slice the apple. Add all three to the bowl and toss in the yoghurt and blue cheese dressing. Finely chop and add the dill to the salad.
Whip the tray out of the oven and pour over the buffalo-style hot sauce sauce. Toss to coat then return to the oven for 4-5 mins to warm through.
Divide the salad between plates and serve the traybake in the middle of the table, family-style.
Get stuck in.

name: Burning Inferno Spicy Margarita
description: This spicy margarita-like drink is going to change your life. Or, at the very least, your cocktail of choice when 5 o'clock rolls around.
instructions: Finely slice your jalapeño and juice a lime, saving a slice for garnish.
In a pan add your water and sugar and gently heat until the sugar is dissolved. Then add ½ of your jalapeño and simmer on a low heat for 3 mins.
Fill a cocktail shaker half way with ice, then add your vodka, lime juice, 25ml of your jalapeño-infused sugar syrup, triple sec and Tabasco.
Shake for 5-7 seconds until all the ingredients are combined.
Double strain into a glass filled with large ice cubes.
Garnish with remaining jalapeño and lime slice. Enjoy.

name: Burnt Aubergine Halloumi Flatbreads
description: Burnt aubergine yoghurt + sticky halloumi coated in honey and hot sauce + zingy tomato salsa = a very good speedy meal. Get into it. Sophie x
instructions:
Slice your onion in half. Finely slice one half, then pop it in a bowl. Squeeze over the juice of ½a lemon, then leave it to pickle.
Move onto your tomato salsa. Heat your grill to high, then pop half your tomatoes on a bakingtray and grill for 10 mins until they are blackened.
Finely chop your remaining onion half and your tomatoes. Add them to a bowl, and squeezeover your remaining lemon juice half.
Turn the flame of your gas hob on to a medium heat. Put your aubergine directly onto the flame,
and cook for a few mins on each side, turning carefully with tongs to ensure it cooks evenly. The
skin will flake off the the flesh will be totally soft when it is ready. Set aside to cool.
Once your grilled tomatoes have cooled slightly, bash them to a paste in a pestle and mortar.
Add your bowl of chopped tomatoes and onion to the mix, then season to taste with salt.
Once your aubergine is cool enough to handle, peel off the skin. Pop the flesh in a sieve set
over a bowl for the excess liquid to drain out.
Finely chop a big handful of your mint, then pop this in a bowl with your yoghurt. Add the zest
and juice of 1 lemon, then tip in your aubergine. Season to taste with salt.
Cut your halloumi into chunky slices. Combine your honey and hot sauce in a bowl.
Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a little olive oil, then get your halloumi in the
pan. Cook for a few mins on each side until it is deeply golden.
Turn the heat right down. Drizzle your honey hot sauce mixture over the halloumi in the pan to
coat it.
Heat your tortillas directly over your gas hob flame for 10 seconds on each side to warm up.
Spread your aubergine yoghurt on your flatbreads, then top with your sticky halloumi and your tomato salsa. Top with a few more mint leaves and your pickled onions, then serve.

name: Burnt Aubergine with Red Pepper Salsa
description: Completely vegan with deliciously sharp flavours. It's an incredible one, Mob.
keywords: burnt aubergine with red pepper salsa
instructions: Add pine nuts to a pan with a small pinch of salt and pepper. Toast these until browned.
Into a bowl, add the freshly toasted pine nuts, roasted peppers, capers, red chillies, red wine vinegar and 7 tbsp of olive oil. Then season generously with salt and pepper
Take your coriander seeds and roughly grind them in a mortar and pestle. Then add to your red pepper salsa and mix.
Once mixed together, set in the fridge. You want it to be nice and cool before serving.
Next, take your aubergines and place them over an open flame on the hob with a pair of tongs. Turn them regularly until they are charred and collapsed.
Once the aubergines are cooked, lay them on a plate and cover with another plate for 10 mins. This will make it easier to peel off the skin.
After 10 mins, remove the skin from the aubergines (don't worry if there are little bits still left on) and add them to your serving plate.
Slice the aubergines down the middle, and spoon in your pepper mix. Pour on some of the juices and top with fresh basil. Tuck in.

name: Burnt Aubergines With Braised Butter Beans & Hot Pepper Sauce
description: If you can find a better way to cook an aubergine, we're all ears. Something magical happens when they’re burnt. The flavour is unparalleled. Sit them on a sea of creamy, rich beans and top with a sharp hot pepper salsa verde, and you’re off.
keywords: Burnt Aubergines With Braised Butter Beans & Hot Pepper Sauce
instructions: Split the chilli in half lengthways and finely chop the shallot, fennel, garlic and rosemary.
In a large frying pan, sweat the halved chilli and the shallots and fennel in plenty of olive oil for 10-12 mins.
Add the garlic and rosemary and cook for a further 3-4 mins. Add the butterbeans and the liquid from the jar, season and bring to a simmer. Turn down the heat and let it bubble away for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, char your aubergines over the flame of a gas hob, on a barbecue or under a hot grill until collapsing and thoroughly burnt. Add them to a bowl and cover to steam for 5-6 mins.
Peel the blackened skin off of the aubergines and keep warm in the covered bowl.
Once your beans have bubbled away, they should have thickened up a little. Roughly chop the roasted pepper and add to the beans with the sherry vinegar.
Now finely chop the herbs and hot peppers and add to a small mixing bowl, season with salt and add plenty of oil and the pickling liquor. Mix to a beautiful salsa.
Warm a serving plate and add the beans to the base, top with the burnt aubergines and finish with plenty of the hot pepper salsa. Get stuck in.

name: Burnt Chilli Smash Burger
description: Smash burgers are the best burgers, right? And the best chillies are burnt chillies, yes? Throw in some crispy shallots and hot sauce onions and you've won. B x
instructions: Divide the mince into 8 roughly equal balls. Pop each ball onto a square of parchment paper and onto a tray in the fridge.
Char your chillies thoroughly on a gas hob or under a hot grill, chuck in a bowl and cover to steam through for 5 mins. Peel the skin off of the chillies, deseed and roughly chop. Set aside.

Thinly slice the shallots lengthways, and toss with the cornflour to coat. Fill a small saucepan halfway with vegetable oil and set over a medium heat. Once the oil reaches 120°C, add the shallots and stir to separate. Cook until golden brown and crispy, drain and season with salt.

Thinly slice the onions and add to a medium saucepan with a shot of oil and a pinch of salt. Cook over a medium heat until sweated down and caramelised, this should take about 25 mins. Add the hot sauce to deglaze and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the chilli paste and mayo with a pinch of salt and a few cracks of pepper.

Time to cook. Grab your beef balls from the fridge and get a large cast iron pan over a high heat. Preheat until smoking hot, add a shot of oil and add two of the burger balls with the parchment paper on top. Using a spatula, smash them down into the pan, season with salt and cook for 2 mins.
Toast the buns.

Flip the burgers over, top with the cheese, add a splash of water and cover the pan to steam and melt the cheese. Top with a spoon of hot sauce, onions, and a spoon of burnt chillies. Repeat with the remaining burgers.
To build, start with a dollop of chilli mayo, plenty of pickles, and then the beef patties. Top with a handful of crispy shallots and crown with more chilli mayo and the lid. Get stuck in.

name: Burnt Corn & Gochujang Fried Rice
description: Don’t throw away your leftover rice. Make this instead. Salty, sweet and most importantly spicy, it’ll become a staple.
keywords: Burnt Corn & Gochujang Fried Rice recipe
instructions: If using leftover rice, skip this first step. Start by washing the rice in a saucepan with cold water. Rinse and pour out, repeating three times, until the water is clear. Put the rice back in the saucepan and add cold water. Let it sit for 20 mins.
Bring the rice saucepan to the boil and, once boiling, reduce the heat to the lowest setting. Let the rice cook on low heat for 11 mins, then turn off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 mins.

Finely dice the garlic, shallot and spring onion, then set aside. Slice the bacon into 1cm pieces. Heat a dry frying pan over a high heat for around 3 mins. Add the corn on the cob, turning every minute, until it’s nicely charred and almost burnt. This should take around 5 mins.

Remove the corn and, using a brush or the back of a spoon, paint on the mayonnaise. Sprinkle on the chilli flakes and one-third of the minced spring onion. Hold the corn upright and run the knife down in between the kernels and the cob. The kernels should stay stuck together and you should have big clusters of corn.
Heat a frying pan over a high heat, add a glug of oil and fry the egg until the edges turn brown. Season with salt and set aside.
Heat a wok or large frying pan over a high heat for 2 mins. Add the butter, garlic, shallots and bacon, then gently stir-fry for 3 mins. Add the kimchi and stir-fry for 2 mins.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the rice, gochujang, sesame oil, 1 tsp salt, sugar and soy sauce. Bash the rice with a spatula to separate the grains and stir for around 3 mins until everything is combined. Add the sesame seeds, one-third of the diced spring onion and, using your hands, crush the seaweed into flakes straight into the rice.
Plate up the rice. Add the chunks of burnt corn on top and the crispy fried egg. Garnish with the remaining spring onion and enjoy.

name: Burnt Honey Teriyaki Udon
description: A twist on classic teriyaki sauce, I’ve changed it up and burnt some honey for extra flavour. The whole lot is finished with some cold butter for richness.
instructions: Trim and thinly slice the spring onions.

Into a frying pan on medium heat, add the honey and cook until it turns a dark amber colour, 2-4 mins. Then take it off the heat and add the rice vinegar, soy sauce, and chilli flakes. Place it back on the heat and cook until sticky and slightly thickened, 3-4 mins.
Cook the udon according to the packaging instructions.
Whisk the cold butter into the burnt honey teriyaki. Then toss the udon into the sauce until glossy and coated. Taste and season with more soy or rice vinegar if needed.
Share the udon into bowls. Garnish with spring onions.

name: Burnt Tomato Salsa
description: A fresh and vibrant salsa that's perfect for the summer. It'll give you a bit of an arm workout but it's so, so worth it.
instructions: Preheat your grill to the highest setting.

Cover all your veg in olive oil on a baking tray before popping them under the grill for 15-20 mins until very charred (every grill is different, so keep an eye on them every couple of minutes). Another option is to char them using a blowtorch or the flame of the hob instead, but make sure to be very careful if doing so.

Roughly chop the charred veg and place the garlic, red chillies, 1 tsp flaky sea salt into a mortar and pestle. Bash them together to form a fine paste. After you've made this chilli and garlic paste, add in the peppers and tomatoes and continue bashing until you form a chunky salsa. This could take up to 10 mins.
Serve with some tortilla chips and enjoy.

name: Burrata & Cucumber Salad With Green Chilli Oil
description: Burrata anything and you can count us in. Especially if it's topped with a heaping spoonful of delicious green chilli oil. Yes, please.
instructions: Cut the cucumbers into irregular-shaped pieces, then toss with salt and set aside.

Finely slice the spring onions. Dress the cucumbers with the juice and zest of a lime, and then add around two of the chopped spring onions, saving some for garnish. Add 2 tbsp of the green chilli oil and tip onto a platter.
Add the ball of burrata, breaking it open as you do. Spoon over the green chilli oil, top with the coriander and remaining sliced spring onion. Scatter with sesame seeds to serve.

name: Burrata, Fennel & Courgette Salad
description: A fresh and flavourful salad that goes great with an ice cold Birrificio Angelo Poretti beer. The aniseed flavour of the fennel balances well with the chilli.
instructions: Heat the grill or a barbecue to high. Finely chop the chilli, deseeding if you like, and grate in the garlic. Squeeze over half the lemon juice and set aside for 20-30 mins to lightly pickle, stirring occasionally, while you get on with the rest of the salad.

Toss two-thirds of the courgettes with a little olive oil and season with salt. Spread onto a baking tray and grill, or place on the BBQ, turning occasionally, until charred and softened all over. Remove and leave to cool.
Meanwhile, tear the burrata into chunks and leave to come to room temperature. Shave the fennel as thinly as you can on a mandolin or with a sharp knife. Pick the mint leaves.
Once the chilli and garlic have pickled, stir through the olive oil and season with salt.
Thinly slice the remaining raw courgettes into rounds and toss through the dressing, along with the charred courgettes, the fennel and most of the mint.
To serve, spread the burrata over a plate and season with salt. Spoon over the courgette salad and scatter with the remaining mint. Serve with grilled bread and a wedge of lemon.

name: Burst Soy Butter Tomatoes with Eggs & Rice
description: Sweet, jammy tomatoes in buttery soy sauce piled onto warm rice, finished with sesame-crusted fried eggs. Big flavour, low effort, proper joy.
keywords: Soy Butter Burst Tomatoes & Eggs on Rice recipe
Soy Butter Burst Tomatoes & Eggs on Rice
instructions: Peel the ginger and finely mince. If using, pick the coriander leaves, discarding the stems and thinly slice the spring onions. Add the herbs into a bowl of ice cold water to crisp.

Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the ginger, fry for 30 secs until fragrant, then tip the tomatoes in. Cook for 4-5 mins, until they’re about to burst. Next, pour in the soy sauce, water and bring to the boil, stirring until it gets all emulsified and glossy. Then remove from the heat.
Reheat the rice. Divide between bowls and top with the soy butter tomatoes.

Place the empty pan back onto medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the sesame seeds and crack the eggs in. Cook, basting the eggs with the hot oil, until they are done to your liking.
Top the tomatoes with a sesame fried egg and some crisp herbs and the spring onions.

name: Burst Tomato & Bacon Spaghetti
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This is a fun take on a classic amatriciana pasta recipe that makes good use of fresh cherry tomatoes. The ideal date night recipe.
instructions: This one’s all about multitasking. Get your pasta water on to boil and drop the pasta straight in with a big handful of salt. Set a timer for 10 mins.

Add the lardons into a pan with a shot of olive oil. Set over a medium heat and begin to cook and render the fat. Once crispy, whip the bacon out, leaving the fat behind. Thinly slice the garlic and drop that into the hot fat.
Sizzle for one min before adding the tomatoes. Pop a lid on and cook over a medium-high heat for 4-5 mins until the tomatoes start to pop and burst, releasing their juice into the pan.

Add the pesto and bacon to the sauce and remove from the heat. Transfer the cooked pasta to the pan with a few splashes of pasta water and toss through the sauce. Finish with basil leaves and Parmesan cheese.

name: Burst Tomato & Chicken Pasta
description: Juicy, burst cherry tomatoes, crispy chicken, and a cheesy twist of cottage cheese bring all the sauce to this simple, satisfying pasta dish.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.
Slice the cherry tomatoes in half. Chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Peel and finely slice the garlic. Grate the Parmesan and roughly chop the basil.

Set a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add the olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken along with a big pinch of salt and a good grind of black pepper. Cook for 8–10 mins until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside for later.

Lower the heat slightly and add the garlic to the pan. Cook for 1–2 mins until softened and fragrant. Tip in the cherry tomatoes and cook for 5–6 mins, stirring occasionally, until they burst and release their juices. Add a ladle of pasta water to help them along.
Cook the spaghetti following pack instructions until al dente. Use tongs to transfer the pasta straight into the pan with the tomatoes, along with a splash of the pasta water.

Return the chicken to the pan. Toss everything together for 1–2 mins until coated and glossy, adding more pasta water if needed to loosen. Stir through the grated Parmesan and chopped basil until the sauce is glossy and emulsified.
Divide the pasta between two bowls and finish each one with a generous dollop of cottage cheese.

name: Butter Bean Caponata
description: A hearty Sicilian veggie stew with aubergines, tomatoes, queen butter beans and tangy olives and capers.
instructions: Finely chop the onion, celery and tomatoes. Rinse the capers. Drizzle the diced aubergine with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Cook in the air fryer on roast function at 190°C for 15 mins or until tender and slightly browned.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a medium pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and celery and fry gently for 5 mins, stirring often.
Add the diced tomatoes, olives and capers to the pan. Simmer over a medium heat for 15 mins, stirring occasionally. Add a splash of water if it’s too dry.
In a small bowl, combine the vinegar and sugar and add it to the pan. Season and add more vinegar or sugar depending on how acidic or sweet you like it.

When the aubergines are finished roasting in the air fryer, add them to the pan along with the butter beans, and tear in the fresh basil leaves. Stir to combine and leave for five mins to heat through. Remove from the heat and leave to sit for another 5 mins.
Divide between bowls and serve with toasted sourdough, if you like.

name: Butter Bean Carbonara
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad.

Ordinarily, I’d say that substituting pasta for beans is criminal but in this case, it really works! The garlicky asparagus gives it a lovely, springy twist.
instructions: Trim the asparagus spears and thinly slice the garlic cloves.

Separate the egg yolks from the whites. Place the egg yolks and parmesan in a bowl and mash into a thick paste. Strain a tin’s worth of bean water into the mixture, season with a pinch of salt and mix until smooth.

Place the pancetta in a large saucepan or frying pan with a splash of olive oil. Heat the pan over
a medium heat and cook the pancetta until the fat renders out and it begins to crisp.
Add a generous amount of freshly-ground black pepper and toast for 1 minute.
Add the beans, bean water included, and season with salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid has evaporated.
Meanwhile, heat a splash of olive oil in another large frying pan. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, then add the asparagus spears and toss to coat in the garlicky oil.
Season the asparagus with salt and pepper and add 200ml water. Bring to a boil over high heat and cook, stirring occasionally, until the water has evaporated.

Once the beans are soft and most of the liquid has evaporated, take the pan off the heat and stir in the egg-parmesan mixture. Keep stirring until the beans are nicely coated in the thick, cheesy sauce.
Finely chop the parsley.
To serve, plate up the butter bean carbonara, place the garlicky asparagus on top and finish it all with a sprinkle of fresh parsley, some black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Butter Bean Curry with Garlicky Greens
description: A speedy, comforting korma-style curry loaded with leafy greens and soft butter beans, perfect for scooping up with warm naan.
instructions: Place a saucepan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the butter and let it melt. Stir in the onion and cumin seeds, and cook for 3–4 mins until the onion is soft and fragrant.
Add the korma paste, tomato purée and garlic purée. Cook for 2–3 mins until the paste darkens and smells toasty.

Tip in the butter beans and their liquid, along with the kale. Bring to the boil and cook, stirring now and then, until the kale has wilted, add a splash of water, if needed. Stir the spinach through and cook until wilted. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Share the curry between bowls, top with the crispy onions and a big dollop of yoghurt. Serve with the naans on the side.

name: Butter Bean Shakshuka
description: We’ve given shakshuka a gut-health makeover with the addition of beans, providing extra fibre to feed your gut microbes and extra plant protein to keep you feeling full.
instructions: Thinly slice your onion and pepper. Mince your garlic and red chilli.

Gently fry your onions in olive oil for around 5 mins until they begin to caramelise then add in the sliced red peppers and continue cooking for another 5 mins before adding the garlic and ⅔ of the chilli.

Once the garlic begins to get some colour, sprinkle in your spices and drained butter beans before stirring in the tinned tomatoes, the water (via the tomato tin to pick up any last bits) and a generous pinch of sea salt.
Leave the sauce to gently simmer for 10-15 mins until the sauce becomes thick then taste to check the seasoning.
Use a wooden spoon to make small wells in the sauce then crack your eggs in. Cover with a lid and cook for about 5-7 mins until the egg whites are set and the yolks are still runny.
Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley and pop some bread in the toaster.
Divide the shakshuka between bowls and top with the parsley, remaining red chilli and a drizzle of tahini, if you like. Dip your toast in and enjoy!

name: Butter Beans with Smashed Peas, Lemon & Parmesan
description: This nutritious and delicious recipe was created for us by Tim Spector. It's packed with fibre and protein and specially designed to improve your gut health.
instructions: Add the majority of the frozen peas and edamame beans (leaving a handful of each for later) to a blender or pestle and mortar and pulse or smash until pulpy.
Trim and slice the Tenderstem broccoli, and roughly chop the basil.

Now, heat a large frying pan over a high heat. Add a shot of oil and let that get nice and hot. Add the Tenderstem broccoli and cook for 2-3 mins, until bright green. Add the butter beans, along with the water from the cans. Stir in the kale, smashed pea mix, and crème fraîche. Toss everything together to create a beautifully green sauce. Then scatter over the remaining peas and edamame beans.
Season with salt and black pepper. Add lemon zest, a good grating of Parmesan, and your chopped basil.

Keep tossing everything together until glossy and gorgeous. Add the juice of half of the lemon, taste and adjust the seasoning if you need to. Divide between warm plates, top with more Parmesan and black pepper and get stuck in.

name: Butter Beer
description: This is the ultimate winter warmer with a coffee kick and crushed gingerbread garnish. Creamy rich and spiced, you’ll have to treat yourself to one of these.
instructions: Crush some gingerbread up in a pestle and mortar.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, then add the brown sugar until it’s all dissolved followed by the icing sugar.
Let this mixture cool a little, then add to a blender with the ice cream, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Blend until smooth.
Put two roughly tbsp of this mixture into each glass along with an even split of your Kahlúa, then top the lot off with hot water.
Mix this up until the butter mixture has melted, then top with a head of squirty cream and your crushed gingerbread.

name: Butter Halloumi Curry
description: Enriching the curry with butter is a brilliant way of adding creaminess and richness. The salty nuggets of halloumi in the sauce make it a winning meal.
instructions: Finely slice your onions. Finely chop your garlic and ginger.

Add a good glug of vegetable oil to your saute pan. Add your onions and cook for 15 mins over a medium heat, until they are fully softened and have just begun to caramelize. Add your garlic, ginger and tomato puree, then cook for 2 mins.
Tip in your bay leaf, chilli powder and garam masala, then add your water and your cream. Bring to a gentle simmer and simmer for 5 mins.
Meanwhile, cut your halloumi into large chunks.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Add your halloumi and cook for 5 mins until each piece is golden on all sides.
Dig out the bay leaf from your sauce and pour it into a blender, then blitz until you have a smooth consistency.
Warm up your roti in a hot frying pan.
Pour the sauce back into the pan, then tip in your fenugreek leaves (if using) and your halloumi. Add your butter, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Finish your curry with an extra drizzle of cream and some coriander leaves. Serve with roti.

name: Butter Masala Soup with Paneer Croutons
description: We’ve topped this creamy, curried tomato soup with crispy paneer and spiced butter. It’s a hug in a bowl to keep you warm this autumn.
instructions: Cut your paneer into 3cm chunks then add to a bowl. Toss with the salt, a glug of vegetable oil and ¼ of the chilli powder. Set aside to marinate.
Peel and finely slice your onions.

Heat a large saucepan over a medium heat, and add a generous glug of vegetable oil. Tip your onions into the pan, along with a big pinch of salt, then cook them for 20 mins, until they have softened and taken on a bit of colour.
Finely chop your garlic and ginger, then add to your onions. Cook them out for 2 mins.

Strain your tinned plum tomatoes from their juices, then add them to the pan. Add your garam masala and ⅔ of the remaining chilli powder, then pour in the water. Bring it up to a boil, then simmer it for 10 mins.

Transfer the contents of your pan to a blender along with your fenugreek leaves, ½ the butter and ¾ of the double cream, and whizz it up to a smooth sauce. Pour it back into the pan then season to taste with salt. Keep the soup warm.

Add your remaining butter to a small saucepan, along with your cumin seeds, nigella seeds and your remaining chilli powder. Cook it over a low heat, until the butter has melted and the spices are sizzling. Switch off the heat, and keep the butter warm.
Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Pan fry the paneer for a couple of mins on each side, until they are golden.
To serve, spoon your soup into bowls, and finish each one with a drizzle of the remaining cream, a few cubes of paneer, a spoonful of spiced butter and a few coriander leaves.

name: Butter-Poached Leeks with Parmesan Foam & Crispy Shallots
description: We've used a whipped cream dispenser to create Parmesan foam in this impressive side dish. If you prefer, just skip the foam and serve the Parmesan cream as a sauce instead.
keywords: butter-poached leeks with parmesan foam and crispy shallots
instructions: Trim, clean and cut the leeks in half lengthwise. Thinly slice the shallots. Grate the Parmesan.
Melt the butter in a large pan and add the leeks. Cook on a low heat for about 15 mins, basting occasionally, until tender.

Meanwhile, make the Parmesan foam. Warm the double cream in a saucepan and whisk in the grated Parmesan until melted. Season with salt and pepper. Strain the mixture and pour it into a whipped cream dispenser. Screw on the charger and shake vigorously. Set aside (don’t let it get cold).
Toss the shallot slices in flour, shaking off the excess. Fry in hot vegetable oil until crispy and golden. Drain on paper towels and season with salt.
To serve, plate the butter-poached leeks, spray over the Parmesan foam, and garnish with the crispy shallots.

name: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
description: Everyone loves fried chicken. This buttermilk fried chicken recipe is the best way to make crispy, golden fried chicken at home.
instructions: Begin by breaking down the chicken. Remove both of the legs by slicing the skin between the leg and the breast and pulling the leg away from the body. Pop out the joint and cut along the body of the chicken to remove the leg. Now cut each into a drum and a thigh by slicing through the joint that connects the two pieces. Now remove the spine from the crown by cutting through the ribs below each breast towards the top of the chicken. Split the crown in half through the breast plate and then cut each breast into 3, bone-in, chunks of breast, one with the wing attached.
Combine the buttermilk with the Frank’s Red Hot and the pickle brine from the jar. Mix well and season generously with salt. Tip in the chicken pieces and brine for 3-4 hours.
Combine the plain flour, cornflour, paprika, mustard powder, allspice and white pepper. Mix well and set aside.
When you’re ready to fry, preheat a half-full pot of vegetable oil to 170°C.

Fish out a couple of pieces of chicken from the buttermilk brine and transfer them to the dry mix. Add a few drops of the buttermilk brine and now scrunch that dry mix into the chicken. This’ll give you an amazing craggy texture. Repeat with the remaining chicken.

Carefully drop 2 or 3 pieces of chicken into the hot oil and fry for 8-9 mins, moving now and then, until golden brown and cooked through. Use a thermometer to check the internal temperature of each piece, you want to hit at least 70°C before pulling them out! Keep the pieces warm in a low oven (120°C) while you fry the rest of the chicken.
Serve the fried chicken with lemon wedges, loads of shichimi togarashi and plenty of pickles on the side. A bit of coleslaw wouldn’t go amiss, either.

name: Butternut Mac & Cheese
description: Roasted butternut works unbelievably well in a mac and cheese, we love it.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Peel your butternut squash and cut it into roughly 3cm pieces. Place on a baking tray. Drizzle with 1/4 of the olive oil, season with salt and pepper and roast for 25 minutes.
When the squash is ready, take 2/3 of it and add to a blender. Pour the milk into the blender and blitz until smooth.
Place a large saucepan on the heat. Add the rest of the olive oil along with the flour. Whisk it together until the flour is absorbed by the oil and bubbling.
Start gradually adding your blended butternut mix, whisking constantly. Once mixed in, add dijon mustard.
Get your macaroni cooking in a separate pan.
Finely grate cheddar and Parmesan. Heat grill to high.
Add chopped sage leaves and a small handful of chopped rosemary to the butternut squash sauce. Mix them in. Add the remaining roasted butternut.
Drain your macaroni and add it to the butternut squash pan. Mix well and add the cheese, saving a little to sprinkle over before putting it in the oven.
Once it has melted, remove the pan from the heat. Pour the macaroni into a baking dish. Sprinkle your leftover cheese on top.
Place under the grill for 5 minutes or until golden. Keep an eye on it, you don’t want the cheese to burn. Let stand for a few minutes then tuck in!

name: Butternut Squash & Marmite Gnocchi Traybake
description: This cheesy butternut squash gnocchi bake will give your fave mac and cheese recipe a real run for its money. Easy, cheesy goodness.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Tip the squash cubes into a large roasting tray, drizzle with 1/3 of the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and toss well. Snuggle the unpeeled garlic cloves into the tray, then roast for 30 mins, until the cubes are soft.

Squeeze the flesh from the garlic cloves into a blender with half of the squash cubes. Tip the gnocchi into the tray with the remaining squash cubes and slide back into the oven and bake for 20 mins further.
Meanwhile, add the cream cheese to the blender and grate the Parmesan in. Add the boiling water, the marmite and juice of ½ a lemon. Season with salt and pepper and blend to a creamy sauce.

Add 2/3 of the olive oil to a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Line a plate with a sheet of kitchen paper. Add the sage leaves to the hot oil and cook for 2 mins, until dark green and crisp, then remove with a slotted spoon onto the lined plate. Add the chilli flakes to the pan of oil and set aside.
Remove the bake from the oven, cover with the squash sauce and mix, adding a little more water to loosen it if necessary. Scatter with the crispy sage leaves and chilli oil to serve.

name: Butternut Squash Autumn Pie
description: The ultimate autumnal pie. The crunchiest topping. The lemon zest really cuts through the rich filling. Perfect.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Peel squash and sweet potato. Cut into cubes. Add to a roasting tray.
Season with salt and pepper and add a drizzle of olive oil. Place in the oven for 50 minutes or until cooked through.
Finely chop onion and garlic cloves. Add a splash of olive oil to a frying pan and chuck the onion and garlic in. Fry until the onions are soft.
Add your spinach and wilt it down. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the spinach mix from the frying pan and into a sieve. Squeeze the spinach with a wooden spoon to get rid of excess moisture. Add the spinach to a mixing bowl.

Remove your potato and squash from the oven. Mash it up. Add to the mixing bowl. Add your feta, ricotta, 4 eggs and the zest of a lemon. Season with salt, pepper and olive oil. Mix everything together.

Pie time. Line your pie dish with olive oil. Add a layer of filo pastry. Brush with olive oil. Repeat with 4 more layers of filo. Fill the pie with your filling. Fold the edges of the pastry over the top. Add 3-4 crumpled sheets of filo on the top. Brush with egg yolk.
Place the pie in the oven for 55 minutes. Remove when golden brown. Serve up the pie and tuck in!

name: Butternut Squash Chilli
description: The homemade pittas chips are the perfect tool for scooping up your delicious rich butternut chilli.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. Cut the butternut squash into wedges, leaving the skin on. Slice the red onions and finely chop the garlic cloves.
Put the squash on a roasting tray and drizzle with oil. Rub with 1 tbsp of harissa and 1 tsp of ground cumin. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 40 minutes until soft.
Meanwhile, put a pan on a medium heat. Add a splash of oil with the onions. Fry until soft, adding a splash of water (if needed) to stop them from catching.
Add half the garlic, 1 tbsp of harissa and 1 tsp of ground cumin. Fry for 1 minute.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes. Fill up one of the tins with water and pour that in too.

Drain the chickpeas and kidney beans, tip them into the tomato sauce and bring to the boil. Season with salt and pepper. Leave to bubble away. You want to reduce the sauce to a nice, thick consistency.

Cut the pitta bread into strips using scissors. Toss with the remaining chopped garlic and a good drizzle of oil and some salt. Spread out onto a baking tray. Roast in the oven underneath the squash until crisp. This should take around 10 minutes.
Stir the cooked squash into the chilli. Top with a spoonful of yoghurt swirled with harissa and chopped coriander. Place the garlic pitta crisps on the side. Enjoy!

name: Butternut Squash Curry With Coconut Rings
description: This recipe uses the whole butternut squash: coconut and sesame squash rings, creamy curry sauce, crispy skins and crunchy seeds for a warm and comforting meal.
instructions: Peel the squash and set the skin aside.
Slice the butternut squash into 1cm rounds and keep the rounds with the seeds in them to one side.
Cut the remaining squash into small cubes.
Dice the onion and grate or finely chop the ginger.
Add the olive oil to a saucepan and turn up to medium heat. Add the onion and fry for 2 mins, then add the ginger and curry powder and season well.

Add the cubed squash to the saucepan and fry for 2-3 mins, stirring often. Add 250ml water (or more if needed, just enough to cover the squash) and cover. Cook for 20 mins or until softened. Add the tofu and peanut butter and blend until smooth. Season to taste.
Cook the rice as per packet instructions.

Take the squash rings and remove the seeds with a spoon (see video for a visual on this). Set the seeds aside. 
Air fry the squash rings for 8 mins at 190°C or roast in the oven at 180°C for 10 mins until fork tender.

In one bowl, add the white sesame seeds and coconut. In another, add the milk or ‘flax egg’ (see notes). In another bowl, add the flour. Coat each ring in flour, then milk/flax and finally the sesame seed mix.

Shallow fry each ring in neutral oil for around 2 mins on each side, until golden brown. 
Alternatively, air fry again for 4 mins at 190°C.
Season the squash skins and drizzle with a little olive oil. Roast in the oven for 15-18 mins at 180°C or until golden brown. Alternatively, air fry for 8 mins at 180°C.

To roast the seeds, separate them from the flesh and give them a rinse. Season and drizzle with a little oil if you like. Roast in the oven at 180°C for 15-20 mins or until crispy. Alternatively, air fry for 15 mins at 180°C.
Serve the curry with rice and the squash rings and sprinkle over the skins and seeds.

name: Butternut Squash Pancakes
description: Great if you've ever got some leftover butternut squash kicking about. Topped with crispy smoked bacon & parmesan, this is the savoury brunch of your dreams.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Chop the butternut squash and place on a tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 50 minutes.

Once the butternut squash is soft, remove from the oven. Add to a mixing bowl and mash it up. Sieve in self-raising flour. Mix it together with a fork. Add whole milk, bit by bit. It will be a bit lumpy, don’t worry.

Crack in two eggs, add 60g of grated Parmesan and 1 ½ tsp of chopped rosemary. Season with salt and pepper and mix together. It should be a nice and thick consistency. If you need to, add a bit more flour.
Get your bacon frying in a pan. Once it is cooked, remove from the pan and keep the fat in there!
Add two ladles of your pancake batter to the pan. Cook for 4 minutes on each side.
Stack up your pancakes, add the bacon, squeeze on some honey, sprinkle on some Parmesan and get stuck in! Enjoy!

name: Butternut Squash Rigatoni
description: The creamiest pasta of your dreams using the mighty butternut squash two ways. Blended into a thick sauce and roasted for a crispy finish. Scrummy.
instructions: Preheat your oven 210°C/410°F.

Peel and dice your butternut. Take one half and place on a baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt and a grinding of pepper. Mix everything together and place into the oven for 40 minutes.
Boil some water in a saucepan and place a colander inside the saucepan and add your remaining squash to the colander. Cover and steam for 10 minutes.
Get your pasta cooking.
Dice your shallots and garlic and add to an oiled frying pan. Stir until the shallots begin to go translucent.
Blending time. Add your steamed squash to a blender, followed by your shallot mix, milk, salt and pepper. Blend until smooth.

Add the blended squash to a frying pan followed by your parmesan (save a handful for garnish at the end). Mix together. Stir in your cooked pasta, making sure the blended butternut coats the rigatoni.
Serve with your roasted butternut squash and remaining parmesan. Chop up your parsley and sprinkle over the top along with a drizzle of olive oil. Tuck into this delicious dish. Enjoy!

name: Butternut Squash Sandwich
description: These sandwiches are the perfect mix of crispy, tangy and buttery. Filled with a creamy mayo made with Pret Chipotle Ketchup and pickled avocado, a dream.
instructions: Heat up the sugar with 100ml of water, vinegar, chilli flakes and cumin seeds. When the sugar has dissolved, take it off the heat and allow it to cool down.
Halve your avocados and peel the skins. Slice them into thick chunks.
Pop the avocado slices into a container and pour over the now-cooled pickling liquid. Close the lid and pop that into the fridge until you’re ready to use it.

Shred the cabbage and massage with ½ tsp salt to soften it slightly. Finely chop the coriander and spring onions and add them to the cabbage along with 1 tbsp mayo. Mix well and season with salt and pepper.
For the chipotle sauce, combine the Pret Chipotle Ketchup with the remaining mayo and set it aside.
In a small bowl, combine the ground cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and 1 tsp of salt. This is your seasoning mix.
Peel the butternut squash and slice it into thick medallions.
Boil the squash in boiling water for 4 mins until slightly tender.
Place the cooked squash onto a chopping board and sprinkle with the paprika seasoning.
Put your plain flour, eggs and panko breadcrumbs into three separate bowls for each ingredient. Combine the flour with any remaining seasoning.
Heat up a large pan with enough oil to deep fry the squash.
Dip the squash into the flour, then the eggs and finally the breadcrumbs.
Deep fry the squash for 5-6 mins until golden brown and crispy.
Cut the crusts off the bread and toast them on one side with a glug of oil in a frying pan until golden.

Lay the toast onto a chopping board with the untoasted-side up. Spread a spoonful of the slaw on one slice of toast, then place the butternut squash on top of that followed by a few slices of your avocados. Spread a generous spoonful of the chipotle mayo on the other slice of toast and sandwich them together.
Cut your sandwich down the middle and plate up them with the cut-side up. Repeat with the remaining bread and tuck in.

name: Butternut Squash Soup with Croissant Croutons
description: We’ve given this cosy seasonal classic an upgrade with crunchy, flaky, buttery croissant croutons.
keywords: Butternut Squash Soup with Croissant Croutons Recipe
Butternut Squash Soup with Croissant Croutons
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan and line a baking tray with baking paper.

Peel and roughly chop the onion and garlic. Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat then add in the onion and garlic and sauté for about 5 mins until fragrant and translucent. Stir in the miso paste and continue cooking until it’s nicely incorporated.
Carefully peel, deseed and chop the squash. Add it to the pot, season with a pinch of salt and pepper and continue sautéing for 5 mins.
Pour in ½ the stock and bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 20-30 mins until the squash is soft.

Meanwhile, prepare your croutons. Slice the croissant into 1cm thick slices. Finely grate the Parmesan into a bowl then sprinkle a little over each slice. Drizzle the croutons with a little olive oil.
Bake in the oven for about 10 mins until golden and crunchy.

To finish off the soup, transfer the soup from the pot to a high-speed blender and blitz until smooth. Add more of the remaining stock if necessary until you reach your desired consistency. Season with salt and black pepper to taste then divide between bowls. Serve topped with a few croissant croutons and a sprinkling of dried flowers, if using.

name: Butternut Squash Soup with Garlic Bread
description: The key to this dish? Ginger. It brings a subtle heat that cuts the richness of the soup. Served with crunchy homemade garlic bread for dipping. Perfection.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Halve and peel your butternut squash, scoop out the seeds and cut it into cubes. Place the cubes on a baking tray and season with a few cracks of black pepper, a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Toss the butternut squash to season on all sides and whack the tray in the oven for 50 minutes.

Finely dice your carrots and onion. Finely chop the garlic and ginger. Pour a large drizzle of olive oil into a frying pan on medium-high heat. Add your carrots and onion and sauté for 10 minutes, until the carrots have softened and the onions are translucent. Add the chopped ginger and give it all a stir.

Squash time! Add the roasted butternut squash to your pan and stir to combine (leave the oven on for your garlic bread). Pour in the vegetable stock and season with a few cracks of pepper. Leave to simmer for 15 minutes. Blitz the soup in the pan with a stick blender until silky smooth, or your desired consistency.

Now for the garlic bread. Slice your ciabatta in half down the middle and place on a baking tray. Finely chop a large handful of parsley, leaving a third for later. In a bowl, mix together 3 tbsp of olive oil, the chopped garlic, two thirds of the parsley, a pinch of salt, and a few grinds of pepper. Give it a mix and spread over the ciabatta. Pop in the oven for 20 minutes.
Serve the soup with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of parsley, a crack of black pepper and your garlic bread. Dig in and enjoy!

name: Butternut Squash with Chilli Con Carne by Harlequins
description: A healthy, protein-packed butternut squash chilli. Spiced, sweetened with honey and bulked out with delicious kidney beans and softened veggies.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C/392°F.
Slice the butternut squash longways in half before drizzling with olive oil and seasoning with a pinch of salt and pepper. Wrap the squash in tin foil and place in the oven for 40 minutes.

Finely chop your onions, chillies, garlic and peppers. Add a splash of olive oil to a frying pan on medium-high heat and sauté the onions for 10 minutes or until translucent. Add the chillies, garlic and peppers to the pan and cook for another 10 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beef mince, cumin, cinnamon and paprika to the frying pan. Give it a stir and cook until the meat has browned. Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.

Once the chilli has reduced to a nice, thick consistency, add the juice of both lime and pour in the kidney beans. Simmer for another 5 minutes. Chop your coriander and add a handful to the chilli along with your honey.
Grate your cheddar. Serve the chilli in the squash half and top with a handful of cheese and a pinch of fresh coriander. Dig in!

name: Butternut Squash, Goat Cheese and Onion Pie
description: This pie makes great use of seasonal butternut squash as well as sweet caramelised onions and creamy goat's cheese. A true winter warmer.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.

Peel and dice the butternut squash into roughly 3cm pieces. Cut the top off the garlic bulb and wrap in tin foil. Place both the squash on a lined baking tray then drizzle with oil, salt and pepper. Add the garlic and slide into the oven for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, finely slice your onions. Melt the butter in a large, oven proof saucepan over a medium low heat, add the onions and thyme leaves, then cook for about 20 mins until soft and sticky. If you don't have an oven proof saucepan, do this in a frying pan and transfer to a baking dish later in the recipe.

Once the squash has cooked, remove from the oven and add to the saucepan with the onions, then squeeze in the roasted garlic and water. Tip in the beans along with their juice along with the goat cheese. mix gently until combined - taste and season with salt and pepper.
Measure and cut a circle of puff pastry using the saucepan/baking dish as a guide.
If using a baking dish, pour the content of the saucepan into the dish and top with the circle of puff pastry. If using an oven safe pan just pop the pastry over the filling. Brush with a beaten egg.
Place the dish in the oven to cook for 30 mins, until the pastry is golden brown. Remove and allow to rest for 10 mins before serving alongside a vinaigrette dressed salad.

name: Butternut and Halloumi Koftes
description: These veggie koftes are loaded up with all the sweetness of squash and saltiness of halloumi. These wraps are one of the best things to make with a squash.
instructions: The night before you intend to eat, pop your chickpeas in a bowl and cover them with water. Leave to soak for at least 10 hours.
Heat your oven to 200°C.
Cut your squash in half lengthways. Roast it in the oven for 45 mins until caramelised and tender.
Pickle your chillies. Add your apple cider vinegar, 200ml water, sugar and a pinch of salt to a heatproof jug, then heat in a microwave until steaming.
Finely slice your green chillies, then pop them in a bowl. Pour your hot cider vinegar mix over the top, then leave them to pickle.
Make your kofte. Roughly chop your chillies and parsley. Grate your halloumi.

Add your chickpeas to a food processor and pulse to break up slightly. Add the flesh from your butternut squash, chillies, fresh parsley, breadcrumbs, ground cumin, ground coriander, sumac and ½ tsp of salt. Blitz until it comes together in a paste.
Add your halloumi and mix to combine.
Roll your mixture into balls, then pop in the fridge to chill for 15 mins.
Make your chopped salad. Finely dice your red onion. Dice your tomatoes and cucumber.

Add your red onion to a bowl along with your lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Scrunch up with your hands to lightly pickle. Add your diced tomato, cucumber, a small handful of chopped parsley and your sumac.
Heat a generous glug of olive in a large frying pan. Once hot, add your kofte and fry for a few mins on each side until deeply golden and crisp.
Add your butter to a heatproof dish and grate in your garlic. Microwave until the butter is just melted.
Warm your naan in the oven for a few mins.

Assembly time. Brush your naan with garlic butter, then dollop on a little yoghurt. Sprinkle with your chopped salad, then add a few kofte on top. Scatter with pickled chillies and a pinch of sumac, then serve.

name: Buttery Pistachio Chicken
description: The most tender pistachio & herb butter chicken. The sumac brings the kick. A great dinner option.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Add the pistachios into a food processor and pulse until coarsely ground. Then, add the butter, garlic, 1/2 the lemon zest, 1/2 the lemon juice, sumac, salt and pepper. Blitz until thoroughly mixed.

Season your chicken legs. Use your hand to loosen the skin away from the leg, then push the pistachio butter under the skin, creating an even layer between the flesh and the skin of the chicken leg. Rub any left over butter on the outside of each portion of chicken.
On medium heat in a non-stick frying pan, add in the chicken and brown each leg, skin side down for 4-7 minutes, then flip and cook on the other side for 3-5 mins.
Transfer the chicken legs onto a baking tray and pour the juices from the frying pan over the chicken. Cook the chicken in the oven for 35-40 minutes.

Meanwhile, wash your rice until the water runs clear. Add into a saucepan with the water, a drizzle of olive oil, pinch of salt and the garlic cloves. Turn the heat up to high, and bring the rice to a boil. Once boiling place a lid on, and turn the heat down to low. Cook for 15 minutes, until cooked. Then turn the heat off and leave it to steam, covered, for another 10 minutes. Reserve some coriander leaves for garnish and finely mince the rest. Fluff the rice and toss the minced coriander through before serving.
Share the coriander and garlic rice between plates and top with a chicken leg and the juices. Serve with a wedge of lemon and any remaining coriander

name: Buttery Three-Chilli Linguine
description: Very buttery, silky smooth and a little bit spicy. This simple vegetarian-friendly pasta recipe has got it all.
instructions: Get a large pot of water on to boil. Grab a frying pan and set over a medium heat.

Finely dice the shallots, thinly slice the garlic cloves and finely slice the chillies. Chuck the butter into the pan and let it sizzle and foam. Add the shallots with a pinch of salt and cook for 3-4 mins. Slide in the garlic, chillies and aleppo. Sizzle for 3 mins then add the tomato puree and lower the heat.
Drop your pasta into the boiling water and cook for 8-9 mins. Cook the tomato purée for 5-6 mins then add a splash of pasta water to slow things down while the pasta finishes cooking.

Finely chop the parsley, stalks ‘n all, and grate the parm. Transfer the cooked pasta to the sauce and toss together with the most of parsley and half of the parmesan. Finish with a little lemon zest and juice and season to taste.
Divide between warm bowls and top with torn burrata, extra parm, more lemon zest and the remaining parsley.

name: Buttery Tomatoes on Cheese on Toast
description: This is such a great brunch option and a nice way to use any tomatoes lying around in your fridge! Cheesy buttery brunch, whats not to love?
keywords: Buttery Tomatoes on Cheese on Toast
instructions: Start by buttering one side of each slice of your bread and setting them aside. Get a large pan up to a medium heat and then toast the bread, butter side-down, until deep golden brown. Do this in batches to avoid overcrowding the pan.
Grate the cheese, then mix and load onto the untoasted side of the bread, season with black pepper and set aside ready for grilling.
Halve the tomatoes and set aside.

Next, take the same pan you toasted the bread in and heat up 2 tbsp of olive oil. Mince your garlic before adding it to the pan and gently frying. After a minute or so, add the chilli powder and cook for a further 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and toss to coat in the chilli powder and garlic.
Season with salt and pepper and allow to cook for 10 mins.
At this point, turn on your grill and allow it to come up to temperature.
Once the tomatoes have cooked down, reduce the pan to a low heat. Cube the cold butter and start to add a little at a time, whisking gently to emulsify.
Once you have used all the butter, stir through a handful of chopped parsley and take off the heat. Check the seasoning and adjust if necessary.
Place the bread under the grill for a couple of minutes to allow the cheese to melt then serve with the buttery tomatoes on top.
For an extra kick, finish the dish with a sprinkling of chilli flakes. Enjoy!

name: Cacao Almond Bliss Balls
description: Naturally sweet, nutty and rich with cacao these little bliss balls are perfect for a mid-afternoon pick-me-up or a post-gym snack.
instructions: Blitz the almonds in a food processor until they resemble coarse flour – not a paste.
Add the dates, raisins, cacao powder, almond butter, vanilla and salt. Blend again until the mixture forms a sticky dough.
If the dough feels too dry, add a little water or coconut oil, one teaspoon at a time, until it comes together.
Scoop out the mixture and roll into bite-sized balls using your hands. You should get around 12-14 depending on how big you make them.

Pop the balls into the fridge to chill for 20–30 mins until firm. Once set, transfer them to a Tupperware lined with baking paper – add another sheet between layers if you’re stacking them. Keep in the fridge for up to a week or freeze for up to 3 months.

name: Cacio E Pepe Toastie
description: A bit of black pepper in a cheese toastie recipe already gives it a little extra excitement, but, assemble it inside out, and you form a zingy pepe cheese crisp. Stuff it with melty mozz and it goes bonkers.
instructions: Put the cracked black pepper into a pan set over a medium heat. Cook for 2-4 mins, stirring until fragrant and toasted – it should smell citrusy. Remove from the heat and let the pan cool down.

Meanwhile, finely grate the cheddar and Parmesan. Add both cheeses to the cooled pan and toss, evenly dispersing the pepper. Put the bread slices into the pan, on top of the cheese mixture. Cook over a medium heat for 2-3 mins, until the cheese has turned crisp and is golden-brown in colour.

Butter the outside of both slices of bread, then flip the cheese crisp so that it’s bread-side down. Scatter the mozzarella over one bread slice, then sandwich the two slices of bread together so that the mozzarella is in the middle.
Set the frying pan over a medium heat and cook the toastie for 3-5 mins until both sides are golden and the cheese has melted.

name: Cacio e Pepe
description: The simplest and oldest of all the Roman pastas. Some people add olive oil or butter. I do not.
instructions: Add the water and salt to a saucepan and bring to a boil over a medium-high heat. Add the pasta and cook following packet instructions until al dente.
Meanwhile, gently toast the peppercorns for a minute in a small dry frying pan set over a medium heat (skip this step if you prefer a milder pepper flavour).
Use a pepper mill (or spice grinder or pestle and mortar) to grind the pepper into a mixing bowl. Grate in the cheese.

When the pasta has boiled for about 5 mins, take a tbsp of the boiling water, add to the cheese and mix vigorously into a paste (it will be thick and dry), then add another tbsp and keep mixing. Keep adding water and mixing until you have something nice and smooth, the texture of cream cheese.
Warm your serving bowls by soaking them in a washing up bowl of very hot water, then dry with a tea towel just before serving.

Drain the pasta, reserving a small bowl of the cooking water. Place the drained pasta back into the saucepan, then add the cheese paste and a splash of the cooking water and mix well, adding more cooking water a little at a time until you have a rich, smooth, creamy sauce.
Plate in the warm bowls (this is particularly important with cacio e pepe, otherwise the sauce will go cold and claggy very quickly). Finish with a little more pepper, if you like.

name: Cacio e Pepe Cheesy Leeks
description: Spiked with a ton of black pepper, and packed with all 3 of the major cheese players, these are the only leeks you need to bother with this Christmas.
instructions: Finely slice the leeks then put them in a large bowl. Cover with cold water, use your hands to clean them, then drain. Grate the cheddar and set it aside.

Grab a small frying pan and place over a high heat. Add the peppercorns and toast for a minute, then tip from the pan into a pestle and morter, or into a mini chopper or spice grinder. Crush or blitz until you have chunky black pepper.

Add a big glug of olive oil to a large non-stick frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the sliced leeks along with a big pinch of salt and cook, stirring regularly, for 10-15 mins until softened. Meanwhile, peel and finely slice the garlic. Once the leeks are soft, add the garlic and cook for a couple of minutes, then tip the whole mixture into a bowl and set aside. Turn the heat down to low-medium and add the butter to the pan.

Once melted, add the plain flour and whisk well to combine, then cook for 1-2 mins. Add a big splash of milk and whisk well. Continue to slowly add the milk, big splash at a time, whisking to combine each time. Add all the milk until you have a smooth sauce – it should be about the consistency of single cream. Turn the grill to high.

Bubble the sauce away for a minute, then add half the mozzarella and cheddar and the Dijon mustard. Finely grate the parmesan into the mix along with the black pepper and a big pinch of salt. Stir the leeks back into the pan. Remove the pan from the heat and, if your pan is oven-proof, leave the leeks in there. If not, tip the contents of the pan into an ovenproof pan or bowl.
Top with the remaining cheddar and mozzarella, then slide under the grill for 10-15 mins until golden and bubbling.

name: Cacio e Pepe Gnocchi
description: Robert Chambers from the exquisite restaurant Luca shows us the perfect way to make gnocchi with a luscious cacio e pepe sauce.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Bake your potatoes in a thick layer of salt for 40-50 mins until soft all the way through. You will know when you can slice it easily with a knife.
Meanwhile, separate one egg with the whites and yolks in separate bowls.

Once your potatoes are cooked, rub off the salt with a clean tea towel. Scoop the insides out with a spoon and pass them through a sieve. Put the potato flesh in a bowl and add in 80g parmesan cheese, flour, 1 whole egg, 1 egg yolk and a heaped tbsp of sea salt.

Mix very gently to combine, being careful not to overwork the mixture. Tip the dough onto a work surface and roll it into 2cm thick logs. Cut each log into small cubes, and roll them into balls. Push them off a gnocchi board or a fork to form ridges on the surface.

Bring a pot of unsalted water to a boil, and pop the gnocchi into the water. Bring the water back up to a boil, then reduce the heat. Cook until the gnocchi float to the top and then cook for a further 30 seconds and remove from the water.

Meanwhile, in a dry pan toast 1 tsp cracked black pepper for 30 secs on a low heat. Add in the butter and, once the butter has melted, add 3 tbsp of the gnocchi cooking water. Turn the heat up and let the mixture emulsify.
Turn the heat off and add in the cooked gnocchi. Grate in 10g parmesan cheese and toss together to melt the cheese – this will emulsify the sauce further.
Finish with a touch more pepper and a light coating of grated parmesan. Tuck in and enjoy.

name: Cacio e Pepe Potato Noodles
description: If you love gnocchi, these potato noodles are just for you. Extra chewy and plump, they’re a fun and different way of enjoying rich, creamy and zingy cacio e pepe.
keywords: Cacio e Pepe Potato Noodles recipe
instructions: Peel and chop the potatoes into 2cm chunks. Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, drop the potatoes in and cook for 10-15 mins until fork tender. Drain the potatoes through a fine mesh sieve, reserving 100ml of the cooking water. Ensure your butter is very cold.

Place the sieve with potatoes on top of a bowl. Working quickly, push the potatoes through to create a fine mash (or use a ricer for quicker results). Mix through the potato starch and three-quarters of the hot potato water, until a smooth dough forms. If it looks a bit dry, add more of the potato water until smooth.
Bring another pan of water to the boil. Divide the dough into 16 even pieces, then roll each one into a long, 1cm-thick log. Cover the noodles with wet kitchen paper.
Once the water comes to a boil, drop the noodles in and cook for 5 mins. Place the noodles into a bowl of ice water, reserving 400ml of the cooking liquid.

Coarsely grind the peppercorns, then add them to a dry frying pan set over a medium heat and toast until fragrant. Add 200ml reserved noodle water and let reduce by half. Add the noodles with the cold butter and toss until emulsified. Remove from the heat and toss the parmesan in little by little (leaving some for garnish) until a creamy sauce forms. Add a splash of noodle water to loosen, if needed. Taste and season with salt before serving.
Toss the cooked noodles through the sauce, then share between bowls and sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan.

name: Cacio e Pepe Scissor-Cut Noodles
description: This is a fantastic hack for creating a dish with the feeling of homemade pasta when in fact it takes less than 20 minutes. I had the idea when I was seeing Chinese scissor-cut noodles along with a German technique for making spätzle. You use this with an Italian pasta dough and then combined with an Italian sauce it will feel like fresh homemade pasta with no fuss. It's one of my proudest creations and now you can see it all over the internet!
instructions: Combine the plain flour with the egg and a pinch of salt and knead for 15 mins to form a soft dough. Cover with a cling film and rest for 5 (and up to 30) mins.
Bring a pot of boiling salted water to the boil.
Meanwhile, grate the pecorino cheese.

Using a pair of clean kitchen scissors, snip very small thin pieces of the dough ball directly into the water. Allow to boil for 2-3 mins, until floating, then drain, reserving some of the pasta water.

Warm a pan over a low heat and grind in the black pepper. Toast for 1 min, then ladle in some reserved pasta water (about 150ml per portion). Add the cooked pasta and then sprinkle over the grated cheese. Allow to sit for 30 seconds without stirring until the cheese melts, then toss the sauce and pasta together so the sauce coats the pasta.
Plate up with extra black pepper and cheese and enjoy.

name: Cacio e Pepe Spinach Toast
description: There is no easier way to eat your greens than by drowning them in Parmesan. The perfect side for you, Mob. Seema x
instructions: Roughly chop the garlic and grind the black pepper.
Add the garlic, black pepper, chilli flakes and butter to a pan and cook for 5 mins on low-medium heat until the garlic is lightly toasted.
Add in 2 tbsp of water and all the spinach. Allow the spinach to wilt down for 5 mins and then continue cooking to draw out most of the water. This should take around 10 mins.
Grate in the Parmesan and add a big pinch of salt.
Stir this together until creamy and serve with more Parmesan and black pepper. Meanwhile, toast your bread and make your crispy garlic eggs.

Thinly slice the garlic and fry in a generous glug of olive oil in a frying pan set over a medium heat, until starting to crisp. Crack in the eggs and spoon over the crispy garlic oil as they cook, until the whites are set.
Once your bread is toasted, heap your cheesy spinach mixture evenly onto every slice. Top with the eggs and more Parmesan.

name: Caesar-Style Broccoli Salad
description: Inspired by one of the most famous salads – the Caesar – we’ve added tenderstem for some extra veg and simplified the dressing so it's quick and easy to make.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely slice the bottom third of the Tenderstem broccoli stems and set aside. Put the top two-thirds onto a large baking sheet or roasting tin, drizzle with a little olive oil, season and roast for 15-20 mins, until charred in places.

Meanwhile, tear or cut the flatbreads into rough triangles, add to a large baking sheet. Drizzle with 2 tbsp olive oil, sprinkle with the oregano, season with salt and toss together before baking for 15 mins until golden and crisp. Set aside to cool down.

Make the dressing by whisking the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon zest and the juice of half the lemon together into a bowl. Finely grate 30g of Parmesan into the dressing, mix together, taste, and season well. Add a splash of water to loosen it a little, if needed.
Trim the romaine and separate the leaves, add them into a large bowl. If your romaine lettuce is particularly large, you can either shred it or roughly chop it.

Tip the croutons into the bowl, then use a peeler to shave most of the 50g of parmesan directly into the bowl. Add the finely sliced broccoli stems and the dressing. Give everything a toss, taste and season with a little extra lemon juice if needed! Tip into bowls or a platter, top with the charred broccoli, then finish with an extra shaving of parmesan and a fresh crack of black pepper. Serve the remaining lemon wedge on the side.

name: Cajun Cheesy Corn
description: Inspired by a popular Korean banchan: corn cheese! We’ve given it a twist by adding cajun seasoning. It's a ripper.
instructions: Set the grill to high. Slice the corn kernels off the cob. Trim and finely chop the bell pepper. Finely chop the chives.
Melt the butter in a small ovenproof frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the corn and pepper, then cook for 3-4 mins until softened.
