Remove from the heat, stir in the cajun seasoning, mayo, sugar, half the chives and half the cheese. Mix well, then scatter the remaining cheese on top.
Grill until the cheese is bubbly and golden, 3-6 mins. Sprinkle with the remaining chives.

name: Cajun Lentil Burritos
description: Lentils and kidney beans belong in a burrito. Loaded with spicy rice, vegan mayo and creamy avocado, this one is a hit.
ingredients: 2x 250g Packet Cajun-Style Lentils & Red Kidney Beans
instructions: Finely chop the jalapeños, coriander and parsley. Save a tbsp of coriander for later. Add this to a small bowl and grate in the garlic. Mix in ½ tsp salt, juice of a lime and add in 100ml extra virgin olive oil.
Wash your rice 3 times until the water runs almost clear. Pop this in a pan with 500ml of water, ground cumin and ½ tsp salt. Bring this to a simmer and cook for 10 mins until fully cooked.
Once the rice is cooked, stir through the juice of a lime and the saved coriander.
Finely chop the onion and tomato. Chop the avocado in half, remove the pit and peel the skin. Thinly slice the avocado and shred the lettuce.
Mash the avocado with some salt, pepper and olive oil. Stir in the onion and tomatoes. Cook your lentil and bean pouch in the microwave according to package instructions.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Lightly warm up your tortillas so that they soften. Add a spoon of mayonnaise on the bottom then top it with coriander rice, a spoonful of the cajun style lentils, the salsa verde, avocado and lettuce.
Wrap in tin foil, slice in half diagonally and serve hot.

name: Cajun Tofu with Limey Edamame Smash
description: An easy, speedy dinner with lots of punchy flavours and extra protein. Instead of making a guac with avocado we are using edamame beans and we love it.
keywords: Crispy Cajun Tofu with Limey Edamame Smash
Crispy Cajun Tofu with Limey Edamame Smash recipe
instructions: Break the tofu into chunky pieces, then toss with the olive oil, Cajun seasoning, salt and black pepper. Pop into the air fryer at 200°C for 15 mins, until crisp. No air fryer? Fry in a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat for 8-10 mins, turning, until crisp on all sides. Meanwhile, bring a pan of water to the boil, add the edamame and cook for 3 mins, then cool in cold water and drain.

Drain and rinse the black beans. Jarred beans are best here, but canned are fine too. Cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Finely chop the coriander. Add the rice, beans and coriander to a bowl with the smoked paprika, the juice of half the limes, salt and black pepper.

Grate the garlic. Add to a food processor with the cooked edamame, the tahini and the juice of the remaining limes. Season with salt and black pepper, then blitz until you have a coarse, hummus-like texture.
Serve up the beany rice topped with the Cajun tofu and a scoop of edamame smash.

name: Cajun-Spiced Chicken Meatball & Butternut Chilli
description: Warming and smoky chicken meatball chilli loaded with beans, squash and big Cajun flavour. Topped with yoghurt and fresh coriander for the win.
instructions: Mix the chicken mince with half of the Cajun seasoning, then shape into small balls.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken meatballs and fry for about 5 mins until browned on all sides.

Add the sofrito mix and season generously, stirring, for 2 mins. Finely slice the garlic and chuck it in with the chopped butternut squash. Cook for 1 min, then stir through the Cajun seasoning and cook for another minute until fragrant.

Pour in the plum tomatoes, squashing them with the back of a spoon. Fill one of the empty cans with water, swirl and tip into the pan. Add the beans — liquid and all — then bring everything to a simmer.
Turn the heat down and cook for 30 mins until thickened and the squash is soft. Stir through the balsamic and season to taste with salt and black pepper. Grate the cheddar and pick the coriander.
To serve, ladle the chilli into bowls and top with a dollop of Greek yoghurt, fresh coriander leaves and a little extra Cajun seasoning.

name: Cannellini Bean & Leek Miso Soup
description: Quick, easy and nourishing vegan miso soup, packed with protein. One of my go-to store cupboard recipes, quicker than boiling pasta. A drizzle of chilli oil and squeeze of lemon finish off this dish perfectly, any day of the year
keywords: Cannellini Bean & Leek Miso Soup recipe
instructions: Drain the beans. Peel the potato and dice into thumb-sized cubes. Finely dice the white onion. Slice the leeks into coins about 1cm in width. Finely slice the dill sprigs.
Set a lidded saucepan over a medium heat and add the olive oil. Add the onions, leeks and potato, then stir for 2-3 mins until softened. Add the beans and stir for a further minute.

Add the stock, then put the lid on. Turn the heat up to high and bring to the boil (this will take around 3 mins), then reduce the heat to low-medium and cook for 10 mins or until the potato is fork-tender. Turn the heat off, stir in the miso paste. Add the chopped dill and stir.
Serve in a deep bowl, drizzle with your favourite chilli oil and garnish with a wedge of lemon.

name: Cannellini Beans with Sage and Roasted Tomatoes
description: This vegan recipe is all about rich roasted tomatoes and creamy cannellini beans. Comfort food personified.
keywords: Creamy Cannellini Beans with Sage and Roasted Tomatoes recipes
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Put the cherry tomatoes onto a roasting tray, drizzle generously with olive oil. Sprinkle with sea salt and oregano.
Place into the oven and roast for 20 mins until they have collapsed and taken on some colour.
While the tomatoes are roasting, make the beans. Finely slice the onion and add to a large saucepan over a medium heat with a generous glug of olive oil and a good pinch of salt.
Finely chop the sage and finely slice the garlic. After 5 mins, once the onion is soft, add the garlic and sage and cook for another 2 mins.
Drain and add the cannellini beans and then pour in the oat milk. Season with 2 tsp of salt, add the zest of half a lemon and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook the beans for 10 mins, stirring well to help them become thick and creamy. When ready, squeeze in the juice of half the lemon, taste again and add salt as needed.
Plate up the beans, top with a handful of the roasted tomatoes, a sprinkle of parsley, a good drizzle of olive oil and some black pepper.

name: Caponata Lasagne
description: Caponata and lasagne are two of my favourite things. So I thought I’d combine them … and it works really well!
instructions: Heat the oven to 230°C. Dice the aubergines into 2cm pieces. Arrange the aubergine over two large baking trays, drizzle with the sunflower oil and toss to coat (don’t worry about them being totally glossed). Roast for around 20 mins, so they dry out and brown a bit.

Meanwhile, finely dice the onion and dice the celery and peppers into 1cm-2cm pieces. Finely slice the garlic and roughly chop the anchovies. Halve the cherry tomatoes and quarter the vine tomatoes. Tear the basil leaves.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large saucepan. Add the onion, celery and peppers and a big pinch of salt. Sauté for 10 mins until softened and glossy. Add the oregano, garlic, anchovies and their oil, and the capers. Mix and set aside off the heat.

Once the aubergines are done, remove them and reduce the oven temperature to 160°C. Spoon the celery mix over the base of a large roasting tin. Spread the aubergine on top in one layer, then top with all the tomatoes in one layer. Season the tomatoes with loads of salt, then the vinegar and sugar.

Return to the oven and bake for 1 hr – the tomatoes will dry out, soften and intensify. Sprinkle the pine nuts on top, add the torn basil and a glug of olive oil, then gently mix the vegetables (ideally not squashing them too much). Set aside for the flavours to mingle for at least 1 hr, but preferably overnight.

On the day of eating, make the white sauce. Melt the butter in a medium-sized saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 30-60 seconds with a spatula until the combination (a ‘roux’) is slack, light golden in colour and smells only slightly nutty. Add a splash of milk and stir with a spatula until the liquid is completely incorporated. Repeat three or four times, then begin to increase the amount of milk you’re adding and use a whisk instead of a spatula, each time ensuring there are no lumps before adding more milk. Once all the milk is in, add the white pepper, nutmeg and half the Parmesan, then gently cook over a low heat for 10 mins, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.

Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and spread 2-3 tea towels over your kitchen surface. Cook one-third of the pasta sheets for 3-4 mins until they’re floppy. Pick them out with tongs or a slotted spoon and lay over the tea towels. Repeat when needed, as you assemble the lasagne.

Heat the oven to 200°C and assemble the lasagne. We’re aiming for four layers of pasta. First, empty half the canned tomatoes over the base of a 2-2.5L ovenproof dish. Top with pasta sheets, trimming to fit as necessary. Spoon and spread half the caponata over the pasta, then top with more pasta. Add the remaining canned tomatoes, plus a couple of ladles of white sauce. Then more pasta, the remaining caponata, a final layer of pasta, then the remaining white sauce. Finish with the remaining Parmesan.
Bake in the oven for 35-40 mins until bronzed and bubbling. Allow to rest and cool for 15 mins before serving.

name: Caponata Parmigiana
description: We combined our favourite tangy tomato sauce with the parmigiana, and it works perfectly. The caponata cuts through the rich cheesy layers perfectly.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Slice up your aubergines. Salt the slices and leave for 15 minutes. This will draw out the moisture.
Dab with tissue. Coat the aubergine slices in flour.
Pour some oil into a frying pan. Add the sliced aubergines to the pan and fry until slightly browned on each side. Remove and set aside.

Add some more oil to a pan and add the diced onions. Add parsley stalks, capers, red wine vinegar and Kalamata olives. Stir everything together and once the vinegar has dissolved, add tins of tomatoes. Break them up and bubble on a high heat until you have a very thick sauce.
Add a handful of chopped parsley, season with salt and pepper and remove from the heat.

Get a baking dish. Spoon in a layer of your sauce. Top with a layer of aubergines. Add a layer of sliced mozzarella, followed by a layer of grated parmesan and then top with another layer of your tomato sauce. Top this with a final layer of aubergine. Add mozzarella and Parmesan on top. Drizzle over some olive oil and season with pepper.
Place dish in to the oven for 40-45 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Remove from the oven and leave to sit for 30 minutes. This will give it time to set. Then slice it up and tuck in!

name: Caprese Butter Bean Bake
description: A gorgeous butter bean bake inspired by the flavours of a caprese salad. A hugely satisfying vegetarian weeknight dinner.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic. Blend the tinned tomatoes until smooth and season with salt. Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and fry garlic for 2 mins, then add in the tomatoes and drained butter beans. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 mins, then stir through the crème fraîche, a handful of torn basil and sherry vinegar. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Grate your Parmesan.
Once the beans are done, transfer to an ovenproof dish and top with torn mozzarella, grated Parm, and the rest of the basil leaves. Slide under the grill until bubbling and golden.
Allow to cool slightly and serve with a simple salad.

name: Caprese Gnocchi Bake
description: All the elements of a caprese salad, in a bake. The fresh cherry tomato sauce is key. Ridiculously cheap. It will become a household regular, guaranteed.
instructions: Prepare the tomatoes. Cut the stem out of any big vine tomatoes and cut into chunks. Mix together with the cherry tomatoes.

Get your oil in an oven safe frying pan over a medium heat. If you don't have one, a regular frying pan will be fine! Just transfer the food to a baking dish a few steps down. Slice your garlic and add into the pan along with the chilli flakes, cook for a couple of minutes.
Add in the tomatoes, cook until they begin to break up and bubble down into a fresh tomato sauce. Add in the basil.
Add the gnocchi to a bowl and cover with boiling water. Leave for 5 minutes, then drain, reserving some of the gnocchi water. Heat the grill to high.

Drain the gnocchi and add into the tomato sauce with a slosh of the gnocchi water. Stir together and bubble down in the pan for a couple of minutes until you have a nice thick gnocchi sauce. Season with salt and pepper and tear in the basil.
Pour the gnocchi into a baking dish if you aren't already using an oven safe pan. Tear up the mozzarella and scatter over the top.
Place under the grill for 7-8 minutes until the cheese is golden and bubbling. Remove, serve up and scatter with more basil if you like.

name: Caprese Meatball Subs
description: You can't beat a good meatball sub. We've packed this one with with mozzarella and fresh pesto for a fragrant edge.
instructions: Finely dice one of the onions and thinly slice the other.
Toast the fennel seeds and chilli flakes in a dry pan over a medium-low heat, then coarsely grind them and tip into a large mixing bowl. Remove the sausage meat from the casings and add to the bowl.

Tip in the finely diced onion, finely grate in one of the garlic cloves and mix everything together. It’s easiest with your hands, so get stuck in. Now, roll the mixture into 20 golf ball-sized balls and put on a baking tray.
Mix the mayo and the pesto together and grate in the remaining garlic clove. Set aside.
Slice the tomatoes into rounds and put on a plate. Season generously with salt and pepper, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar and olive oil. Let them hang out for 15-20 mins.

While the tomatoes are marinating, cook the meatballs. Set a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add a splash of oil and cook for 8-10 mins, rolling them around the pan until crispy, golden and cooked through. Add a splash of water and 1 tbsp vinegar to deglaze the pan.

Split the baguettes in half, spread some pesto aioli over each side and layer on the tomatoes. Tear over the mozzarella and divide the meatballs between the sarnies. Finish with basil, olive oil, sliced onion and extra salt and pepper.
Get stuck in.

name: Caprese Ravioli
description: We've filled this gorgeous homemade ravioli with burrata and mozzarella. This delivers all the flavours of a caprese salad, with extra carbs. You're welcome.
instructions: To make the pasta dough, pour the flour out onto a clean work surface and create a well in the centre. Add the eggs and, using a fork, beat the eggs together. Slowly incorporate the flour into the centre of the well until you have a thick paste. Bring the walls of flour into the paste and knead until you have a smooth, springy dough. Wrap in cling film, or cover with an upturned bowl and rest for 30 mins.

Roll out the rested pasta using a pasta roller or a stand mixer attachment. Pass one-third of the dough through the widest setting, and keep working your way down until you have landed on the second thinnest setting. Cut the pasta sheets into 7x7cm squares and cover with a damp towel. Repeat until all the pasta is rolled out.

For the filling, coarsely grate the mozzarella into a bowl then add the burrata and mix to combine. To make the ravs, take a square of pasta and spoon 3 tsp of the burrata mix into the middle. Lightly brush the border of the pasta with water and carefully lower another square over the top, covering the cheese.

Carefully press your way around the filling, removing as much air as you can from the ravioli. Once it is mostly sealed, scoop up off the bench and press firmly around the edges to make sure the pasta is very sealed. You can trim the rav into any shape you like now, a fluted cutter is nice, cut into a heart, a star or leave as a square, up to you. Pop onto a semolina lined tray and repeat with the remaining ingredients, make a couple of extra if you can just in case any burst!

Now, make the speedy tomato sauce. Thinly slice the garlic cloves and add to a cold saucepan with 4 tbsp of olive oil. Set over a low heat and allow to slowly warm up, infusing the oil with the garlic flavour. Once the garlic smell is filling the room, tip in the tomatoes and season with salt. Cook for 3-4 mins until the raw taste has gone. We don’t want to cook this sauce too long, we want it to be bright and fresh.
Cook the ravioli in salted, boiling water for 1-2 mins and transfer to the tomato sauce. Toss gently to coat and divide between plates. Top with extra Parmesan, basil leaves and a drizzle of pesto.

name: Caprese Soba Noodle Salad
description: A riff on a caprese pulled towards Japan. Silken tofu in place of mozzarella, sesame oil and soy instead of olive oil. Basil stays, because it belongs here just as much. The tomatoes do most of the work, marinating until they give up their juices for the dressing, and it all comes together in minutes.
instructions: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat, shaking occasionally, for 2-3 mins until golden and fragrant. Tip onto a plate and set aside.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and toss with the sesame oil, soy sauce and rice wine vinegar. Leave to marinate while you prepare everything else - the longer they sit, the better.
Cook the soba noodles according to the packet instructions, about 4-5 mins. Drain and rinse well under cold running water to stop them cooking and keep them springy.

Once the noodles have cooled, divide between containers. Spoon over the marinated tomatoes and their juices, then break the silken tofu over the top. Scatter generously with the basil and toasted sesame seeds, and drizzle over any remaining marinade from the bowl. Pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Caprese Soba Noodle Salad
description: A riff on a caprese pulled towards Japan. Silken tofu in place of mozzarella, sesame oil and soy instead of olive oil. Basil stays, because it belongs here just as much. The tomatoes do most of the work, marinating until they give up their juices for the dressing, and it all comes together in minutes.
instructions: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat, shaking occasionally, for 2-3 mins until golden and fragrant. Tip onto a plate and set aside.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and toss with the sesame oil, soy sauce and rice wine vinegar. Leave to marinate while you prepare everything else - the longer they sit, the better.
Cook the soba noodles according to the packet instructions, about 4-5 mins. Drain and rinse well under cold running water to stop them cooking and keep them springy.

Divide the noodles between two bowls. Spoon over the marinated tomatoes and their juices, then break the silken tofu over the top. Scatter generously with the basil and toasted sesame seeds, and drizzle over any remaining marinade from the bowl. Best eaten straight away.

name: Caramelised Aubergines & Coconut Cucumber Salad
description: Beat the midday slump with this delish rice bowl. Packed with jammy soy-glazed aubergines and a cooling cucumber salad - it's a proper lunch upgrade.
keywords: Lunch Box: Caramelised Aubergines and Coconut Cucumber Salad recipe
Lunch Box: Caramelised Aubergines and Coconut Cucumber Salad
Caramelised Aubergines and Coconut Cucumber Salad recipe
instructions: Slice the aubergines into 3cm chunks. Bash the ginger and garlic. Thinly slice the cucumber, add to a strainer and toss with a good pinch of salt. Thinly slice the chilli. Pick the coriander leaves and discard the stems.
Set a large frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, add the coconut and toast, stirring for 2-4 mins, until nicely golden. Transfer onto a plate and set aside.
Return the pan over high heat with a generous glug of olive oil. Once hot, chuck in the aubergines and cook for 5–7 mins, until golden.

Pour in the coconut water and soy sauce, then drop in the garlic and ginger. Bring to the boil, turn the heat down to medium and let it simmer for 10–15 mins until the aubergines are softened and jammy.

Mix the cornflour with the water until smooth, then pour into the aubergines. Stir together and let it come back to the boil. Cook for 2–4 mins until thickened. Season with salt and pepper. Add a splash more water if it’s too thick.

Taste the cucumber. If they’re too salty, rinse under cold water and drain well. Toss with the juice of the lime, most of the desiccated coconut (saving a sprinkle for the garnish) and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with again, if needed.

Reheat the rice according to pack instructions and divide between your lunch boxes. Remove the ginger from the aubergines, then spoon over the rice and add the cucumber salad. Finish with a sprinkle of toasted coconut, chilli and coriander. 
Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch - they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Caramelised Banana & Coconut Overnight Oats
description: Proper creamy coconut oats layered with sticky caramelised banana and crunchy toasted coconut. Perfect brekkie vibes all week long.
keywords: Caramelised Banana & Coconut Overnight Oats recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
For the oats, whisk the yoghurt, water, oats and chia and poppy seeds together, season with as much maple syrup and salt as you like.Cover and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hrs, or overnight.

For the topping, add the coconut and sunflower seeds onto a baking tray. Once the oven is hot, slide in and bake for 7-10 mins until toasted and golden. Once ready, remove from the oven and drizzle over the maple syrup and season with salt, mixing together. Slide it back into the oven for 3-5 mins.Let it cool fully before transferring into a jar or Tupperware container.

For the banana, peel and slice into 1cm slices. 
Set a frying pan over medium heat and add in the coconut oil. Once hot, add the banana, fry on one side for 5-7 mins until caramelised, then tip in the remaining maple syrup and stir together. 
Season with a touch of salt and remove from the heat.
Once the oats have thickened, spoon into jars or containers, top with the bananas and sprinkle over the toasted coconut sprinkle. Dig in!

name: Caramelised Banana Split & Spiced Rum Fudge
description: A kitsch and decadent banana split that's as delicious as it is nostalgic. Grilling your bananas is the move to make.
keywords: Caramelised Banana Split & Spiced Rum Fudge
instructions: To make the ice cream: add the demerara sugar, ½ tsp of salt and coconut cream into a saucepan. Cook until the sugar has dissolved. Transfer to a bowl and whisk in the rest of the ingredients until fully incorporated. Chill the mixture and churn according to ice cream maker instructions.

For the rum fudge sauce: chop the chocolate into small chunks. Add the golden syrup, cinnamon, caster sugar, cocoa powder and 250ml of water into a saucepan. Place over medium-high heat and whisk until the sugar has dissolved. Bring the mixture to a boil, then turn the heat down to medium and simmer until reduced by half. Then, stir through the spiced rum, ½ tsp of salt and chocolate chunks, until melted. Continue cooking until thickened and glossy, 3-5 mins (do not bring the mixture to a boil, if its too hot, turn the heat down lower). Reheat the fudge sauce before serving, if needed.

For the grilled bananas: if you don’t have a blowtorch, preheat the grill to high. Add the sugar onto a plate. Peel and halve the bananas lengthwise. Dip the cut side of the bananas into the sugar and place onto a baking tray. Blowtorch or grill the sugar until caramelised.
For each portion, use two caramelised bananas, two or three scoops of ice cream and top with warm rum fudge sauce, toasted coconut flakes, sprinkles and a maraschino cherry.

name: Caramelised Brussels Sprouts with Butter Beans & 'Nduja
description: These Brussels sprouts take on a beautiful colour when they're cooked down with spicy ‘nduja and creamy butter beans.
keywords: Caramelised brussel sprouts with butter beans and 'nduja recipe
instructions: Trim and quarter the sprouts. Place a large frying pan over a high heat and add a good drizzle of olive oil. Add the sprouts and cook for 3 or 4 mins until golden.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the 'nduja, slice and add the garlic, cook for another 2 mins.
Drain and add the butter beans and then tomatoes. Add 2 tsp of salt, then simmer for 15 mins, breaking up the tomatoes a bit with a spoon as they cook.
Once the sauce has thickened down, add the zest and juice of half a lemon. Taste and season.
Plate up, top with chopped parsley and a good drizzle of olive oil.

name: Caramelised Carrot Porridge
description: Inspired by the Indian dessert Gajar Ka Halwa, this spiced porridge is loaded with sweet caramelised carrot, golden raisins and a swirl of almond butter. Comforting, fragrant and great for making ahead.
instructions: Peel and grate the carrots on the large holes of a box grater. Set a large saucepan over a medium-high heat and add the grated carrot and roughly a third of the milk. Cook, stirring continuously, for 25-30 mins until all of the milk has evaporated. (It might look a bit curdled towards the end — don't worry about it.)
Add the honey and a generous pinch of salt. Keep stirring for a couple of minutes until most of the remaining moisture has evaporated.
Add the oats, most of the golden raisins (saving some for serving), the ground cardamom, ground cinnamon and the remaining milk. Cook, stirring, for about 7 mins until the porridge has thickened.

Divide the porridge between bowls or containers. Roughly chop the almonds and scatter over eacg, then finish with a spoonful of almond butter, the reserved golden raisins and a drizzle of maple syrup.

name: Caramelised Coconut Chicken Pie
description: Creamy, fragrant coconut chicken bubbling away under golden puff pastry. It’s rich, cosy and packed with warming spice. We've served ours with peas, but feel free to add your favourite pie side!
instructions: Using scissors, cut the chicken into 2-3cm chunks. Thinly slice the leeks, chilli, garlic, lemongrass, and ginger.
Add ⅓ of the coconut milk into a pan over medium heat. Let it cook, stirring occasionally, until the fat has separated. Stir the dessicated coconut through and cook, stirring until toasted.

Add the chicken and leek, then cook for 5-7 mins until the leek has softened. Stir the chilli, garlic, ginger and lemongrass through and cook for 2-3 mins until fragrant. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat the oven to 220°C.

Once the aromats are fragrant, add the lime leaves, ground spices, star anise and stock cube. Pour in the remaining coconut milk and the water. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer for 10-15 mins until creamy and thickened. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Tip the chicken mixture into a baking tray (unless your pan is ovenproof). Lay the puff pastry over the top, trimming if needed. Brush with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and black pepper. Cut a small hole in the centre to let the steam escape, then bake for 20-25 mins until the pastry is puffed and golden.
Remove from the oven and serve. We added peas on the side, but any veg will work a treat here.

name: Caramelised Coconut Chicken With Zingy Herby Mango Salad
description: Fragrant coconut cream and a fresh mango side salad take this simple chicken recipe to the next level.
keywords: Caramelised Coconut Chicken With Zingy Herby Mango Salad
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stalks.

Add the coconut cream into a bowl with the soy sauce, honey and cornflour. Finely grate the garlic in, add the coriander stems and season with half the fish sauce and black pepper, mix together, then stir the chicken in.

Place onto an oiled baking tray, roast until cooked through,15-20 mins. Switch the grill onto high and grill until starting to char, basting every couple of minutes. Flip and continue cooking until charred in places on both sides.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the shallot and add to a bowl. Peel and slice the mango into long and thin matchsticks. Thinly slice the chillies and halve the tomatoes.
Add the chilli into a small bowl with the lime juice. Add the remaining half of fish sauce. Season to taste with sugar and add more fish sauce if needed.
Into another bowl, add the mango, shallot, and tomatoes, spoon over the chilli dressing, reserving some on the side.
Before serving, toss the coriander leaves into the salad. Share the rice between bowls, top with the chicken and mango salad. Drizzle over the zingy chilli sauce and any chicken sauce.

name: Caramelised Coconut Curry Prawn Stir Fry
description: Caramelising the coconut milk is a technique usually found in Thai cooking, where split coconut milk fries out the curry paste for extra aroma and depth. Here it's let loose with aromatics you'd find in South Asian curries, the result is a rich, fragrant prawn stir-fry that's ready in 35 minutes.
keywords: Caramelised Coconut Curry Prawn Stir-Fry recipe
instructions: Add the jasmine rice to a medium saucepan and wash it three or four times until the water runs clear. Pour in the measured water and place over a high heat. Bring to the boil, then pop on a tight-fitting lid, turn the heat right down to low and steam for 12 mins, do not lift the lid. Once done, remove from the heat, fluff with a fork, replace the lid and leave until ready to serve.
Meanwhile, core and discard the seeds from the peppers and chop into 2-3cm chunks. Gently bash the garlic cloves and ginger with the flat of a knife, discarding the garlic skins.

Pour half the coconut milk into a wok or large frying pan over a high heat and bring to the boil, letting it bubble until it splits and the fat separates, about 3-4 mins. Add the garlic and ginger and leave to infuse for 3-4 mins.

Stir in the curry leaves (careful, they'll spit) and the peppers. Turn the heat down to medium and stir-fry for 5-7 mins until the peppers are starting to soften, adding a splash more coconut milk if the mixture is browning too quickly.

Stir in the prawns, curry powder and crispy onions. Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and bring to the boil. Cook for 3-4 mins until the prawns are cooked through and opaque. Season with salt, black pepper and a good squeeze of lime juice.
Divide the rice between bowls, top with the prawns and sauce, and serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Caramelised Courgettes on Whipped Tofu with Harissa Pomegranate Drizzle
description: Whipped tofu is the perfect base for coins of caramelised courgettes. Douse them in a harissa pomegranate drizzle for a dead easy vegan dinner.
keywords: Caramelised Courgettes on Whipped Tofu recipe
instructions: Use a mandoline or very sharp knife to thinly slice the courgettes. Finely grate the garlic. Place the courgettes into a deep frying pan with a good drizzle of olive oil and plenty of salt and pepper. Add the grated garlic and cook over a low-medium heat for about 10-15 mins until very soft. Stir through the za’atar.
Meanwhile, make the whipped tofu. Squeeze the lemon juice into a blender, add the remaining ingredients and blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Whisk all of the harissa drizzle ingredients together in a small bowl. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Lightly toast the pine nuts.

To serve, spread the whipped tofu onto a platter, pile up the courgettes and drizzle over the harissa pomegranate sauce. Finish with an extra drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper and the toasted nuts.

name: Caramelised Lemongrass Chicken Bowl
description: Charred and fragrant lemongrass chicken thighs with rice and a fresh rainbow salad.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place the chicken into a bowl. Add the lemongrass, ginger, red chilli, garlic, sugar, soy, balsamic vinegar, and water into a blender. Blend until smooth. Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed, and pour over the chicken. Toss together.

Transfer the marinated chicken onto an oiled baking tray, pouring over all of the marinade. Slide into the oven for 20-25 mins, until cooked through. Check half way through and add a splash of water if the marinade is caramelising too quickly.

For the rainbow salad, use a peeler to shred the red cabbage and slice the carrots into thin matchsticks. Pick the mint leaves, discarding the stems, then combine the veg and herbs with the juice of a lime. Season to taste with salt and some sugar. Crush your peanuts.
Reheat the rice and serve onto plates. Slice the chicken and place on top with some rainbow salad. Finish with a sprinkling of crushed peanuts.

name: Caramelised Onion & Anchovy Tortilla
description: If you can manage it, save some tortilla for the next day and stuff the leftovers into a sandwich with heaps of aioli. You won’t regret it. B x
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high (190°C).
Crack your eggs into a large bowl, season with salt and whisk with a fork. Set aside.
Thinly slice your onions and get them into a pan with plenty of olive oil. Cook down with a pinch of salt for 9-10 mins until caramelised.
Meanwhile, peel and slice your potatoes as thin as you can. Chuck them into the pan with the onions and add a shed load of olive oil, approx 100ml (trust me).
Cover and cook, stirring regularly for 7-8 mins until the potatoes are just tender. Now drain off the excess oil (save this for later!) and mix the onions and potatoes into the eggs.
Slice up the peppers and roughly chop the anchovies and get them into the bowl with the eggs. Mix everything together and season with salt, pepper and a generous pinch of sweet smoked paprika.
Now grab a 24cm non-stick frying pan (trust me, you want it non-stick). Add a splash of the leftover olive oil and preheat over medium-low.
Dump the egg mixture into the pan (you should hear a gentle sizzle) and shake to distribute the potatoes, peppers and anchovies throughout the pan.
Now turn down the heat and cook for 10-12 mins until the sides begin to set. Pop it under the grill for 4-5 minutes.
Now, grab a large plate or lid and flip the tortilla out. Slide it back into the pan and cook for another 3-4 mins. Turn the tortilla out onto a chopping board and cut into wedges.
Now top with aioli, extra paprika and sliced spring onions. Serve with a green salad if you fancy it.

name: Caramelised Onion & Lemon Linguine
description: Whole lemons slow roasted in the oven, jammy caramelised onions and a garlicky cream sauce all tossed through linguine. Don't be put off by the time the oven does all the work.
keywords: Traybake Caramelised Onion & Lemon Linguine recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Peel and finely slice the onions and lay them across the base of a medium roasting tray. Thinly slice one lemon and lay it over the onions. Cut the top off the bulb of garlic, drizzle with a little olive oil, wrap tightly in foil and nestle into the tray. Dot the butter over the onions, drizzle with a tbsp of olive oil and season well with salt and black pepper. Cover the whole tray tightly with foil and bake for 50 mins.

After 40 mins, bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the linguine and cook for 2 mins less than the packet instructions. Finely chop most of the parsley, saving a few leaves to serve.

Remove the tray from the oven. Unwrap the garlic and squeeze all the roasted cloves out into the tray. Pour in the cream and squeeze in the juice of the remaining half lemon. Use tongs to transfer the linguine straight into the tray, then tip in a splash of the pasta water. Finely grate in most of the Parmesan and add the chopped parsley. Toss everything together well, adding a little more pasta water if needed to loosen. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Divide between bowls and finish with the reserved parsley leaves and the remaining Parmesan grated over the top.

name: Caramelised Onion Bubble & Squeak With Harissa Mayo
description: Bubble and Squeak's a blank canvas, you can chuck in whatever you fancy. We've gone for spicy harissa mayo. It's killer. B x
instructions: Thinly slice your red onions and toss them into a pan with a shot of oil. Set over a medium heat. Season with salt and add the cumin seeds. Cook for 10 mins until softened and caramelised.
Remove the core from the hispi cabbage and thinly slice the leaves. Add to the pan with the thyme and cook for 3 mins until wilted.
Roughly chop your parsley.
Add the leftover mash, most of the parsley and the zest from the lemon and fold everything together. Taste and add salt and pepper to taste.

Now preheat a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Add a splash of oil and a quarter of the mix. Form into a patty and cook for 4 mins on each side until crispy. Transfer to a low oven to keep warm and repeat with the rest of the mix.
Mix together the vegan mayo and harissa with a squeeze of lemon juice. Season to taste.
Serve topped with the remaining parsley and a big dollop of harissa mayo.
Get stuck in.

name: Caramelised Onion Linguine
description: Caramelised onions cooked unbelievably slowly until rich and jammy. Pasta water is key in creating the silky sauce. You're going to love this dish. Ben x
instructions: Prep your ingredients. Half your onions then finely chop to get half onions slices. Finely chop your garlic and your parsley.
Add most of your butter to a large frying pan. Allow to melt then add your onion.
This part is key: you have to cook your onions on a low to medium heat for about 30-40 minutes until rich and caramelised.

Add your garlic to the frying pan with the rest of your butter and fry for a minute until fragrant. Add your white wine to the frying pan and allow to bubble off. Grate your parmesan and pecorino while you wait.

Once the wine has evaporated, add your parmesan and pecorino, a massive grinding of black pepper and a big pinch of salt. Mix together with a wooden spatula until you have an onion cheese paste and turn off the heat.

Get a saucepan on the heat and add only enough water to just cover your pasta. Season generously with salt and add your linguine. Make sure everything is ready to go- once your pasta is cooked you have to move quickly.

After 4 minutes, remove a big mug of pasta water from the saucepan, add to your onions and get your heat back on. Mix together and keep adding pasta water until you have a thick, creamy caramelised onion sauce.

After 9 minutes your pasta will be al dente. Drain your pasta, reserving your pasta water. Add your pasta and a splash more pasta water to the sauce. Over a low heat with a pair of tongs, toss your pasta through the sauce. It will look split to begin with but stick with it.
Keep adding pasta water to the frying pan and tossing through until you have a rich, silky pasta dish. Squeeze in the juice of half a lemon and add a large handful of chopped parsley.
Plate up and serve with a grating more of parmesan, a sprinkling of parsley and black pepper. Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Caramelised Onion Pasta With Cheesy Breadcrumbs
description: Learn how to cook the jammiest caramelised onions and turn them into the base for this silky and decadent pasta dish inspired by the classic French onion soup.
keywords: Caramelised Onion Pasta with Gruyère & Thyme Breadcrumbs
instructions: Peel and thinly slice all of the onions. If you have a mandoline, now is the time to use it. If not, a sharp knife will do the job nicely. Strip the leaves off the thyme stalks. Peel and thinly slice the garlic. Grate the Gruyère. Zest half of the lemon.

Place a large saucepan with a drizzle of oil over medium heat, add half of the butter and let it melt. Stir the onions and 15g of thyme leaves along with a good pinch of salt. Cook the onions, stirring occasionally until they have softened and lost a lot of liquid. After about 25-30 mins they should be golden and very soft. Add a splash of the beef stock if the onions are catching on the bottom of the pan.

Meanwhile, heat a small frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Add the breadcrumbs, the remaining thyme leaves and plenty of fresh cracked black pepper, cook until golden brown. Transfer to a bowl, season with salt and let cool down.
Once the onions are caramelised, reserve ¼ on the side. Add the garlic into the saucepan and cook for 2 mins.
Stir in the white wine and let it fully evaporate. Add the remaining beef stock and let it reduce until the onions are jammy and the stock has reduced by ⅔, around 10-15 mins.
Meanwhile, cook your pasta in boiling salted water for 1 min under al dente. Once your pasta is done, add it to the caramelised onions, making sure to reserve the pasta water.
Toss the pasta into the sauce, with the remaining butter. Use the pasta water to thin the sauce out. Season with salt and plenty of pepper.
Remove the pasta from the heat and vigorously stir through half of the cheese until emulsified. Squeeze in some lemon juice. Taste and season with salt and more freshly cracked pepper, if desired.
Stir the lemon zest and remaining cheese into the breadcrumbs. Serve the pasta with some of the reserved caramelised onion and Gruyère and thyme breadcrumbs on top. Enjoy!

name: Caramelised Onion and Blue Cheese Pie
description: Nothing hits the spot like cheesy, garlicky potatoes in a crispy puff pastry pie crust. It is the best thing to curl up on the sofa with.
keywords: Potato and caramelised onion pie recipe
instructions: Thinly slice your onions and put them in a large pot with a large glug of oil. Cook on medium-low heat for 45 mins, stirring regularly until they are deep golden brown and caramelised.
Meanwhile, chop up your potatoes into small cubes - don’t bother peeling them and mince the garlic. Finally, crumble up the gorgonzola into irregular pieces.
Roll out your puff pastry so it fits the size of your pie tin.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Mix the stock cube with 450ml boiling water.

Once the onions are caramelised, add in the garlic and cook for 1 min until fragrant. Pour in the vegetable stock, thyme, and potatoes, then bring to a boil. Finish with the double cream and season generously with salt and pepper.
Stir in the gorgonzola and pour the mixture into the pie tin.
Brush the top of the pie crust with a beaten egg and pop this in the oven for 30 mins, or until the pastry is golden and puffed.
Allow to cool for 15 mins, then serve with a pile of greens.

name: Caramelised Onion, Anchovy & Olive Spaghetti
description: The sexiest spaghetti packed with all the savoury flavours of a pissaladière tart. Deeply caramelised onions, anchovies and olives. A simple, phenomenal dish.
instructions: Thinly slice your onions. Grate your garlic. Chop your parsley. Halve your kalamata olives.

Heat a good glug of olive oil in a large sauté pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add your onions and cook for 30 mins until totally soft and caramelised. Deglaze with water occasionally if they look like they’re sticking.
When your onions are nearly cooked, get a large pot of water on to boil. Season generously with salt. Add your spaghetti and cook until al dente.
Add your garlic and anchovies to the onions and cook for 2 mins until the anchovies have broken down and the garlic is fragrant. Add your olives and stir briefly.

Pour in your pasta water, using tongs, trasnfer the pasta into the onion pan. Grate in your parmesan and add your butter, then mix until you have a smooth sauce that coats each length of pasta. Add more Pasta Water if needed. Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Serve into bowls and top with parsley leaves.

name: Caramelised Onion, Ham & Cheese Empanadas
description: Homemade empanadas make any occasion better. We've stuffed these flaky pastry pockets with gentle caramelised onions, ham, and cheese. Yum.
instructions:
Peel and thinly slice the onions and garlic. If you have a mandoline, now is the time to use
it. If not, a sharp knife will do the job nicely. Strip the leaves off the thyme stalks.

Place a medium saucepan over medium heat with 3 tbsps of olive oil. Once hot, add the
onions, garlic and thyme leaves along with a good pinch of salt. Cook the onions, stirring
occasionally, until they have softened and lost a lot of liquid. After about 25-30 mins they
should be golden and very soft. Add a splash of the water if the onions are catching on the
bottom of the pan.

Meanwhile, chop the ham into 1cm pieces and grate the cheddar. Unroll the puff , Grab
yourself either a cookie cutter, bowl, or empty round container with a diameter of about
12cm. Cut the pastry into 12cm discs.

Once the onions have caramelised, transfer them into a bowl and let cool down a little.
Then, add the ham, cheddar and mozzarella cheese. Season with a generous crack of black
pepper.

Add 2 tbsp of ham and cheese mixture into the centre of the puff pastry circle, fold the
pastry in half to form a semicircle and seal the edges well. Place the empanadas onto a
lined baking sheet in the fridge for 30 mins.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Halve the tomatoes and add onto a baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt
and pepper, roast until softened, 10-15 mins. Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley and
coriander. Trim the chilli and finely slice.

Add the tomatoes into a medium bowl. Mash until they break apart and form a chunky
salsa consistency. Add the chilli, herbs, vinegar and 45ml of olive oil. Season with salt and
pepper. Cover and place in the fridge to cool down.

Crack the egg into a small bowl and whisk together. Brush the empanadas with egg wash
and bake for 25-30 mins, until golden brown and flakey. Serve with the herby salsa.

name: Caramelised Paneer & Coconut Lentil Salad
description: I love a light but creamy dressing for salads, this zingy, herby coconut one is the perfect summer sauce. Tossed through hearty lentils, caramelised paneer and roasted aubergine, it only gets better as it sits in the fridge.
keywords: Caramelised Paneer & Coconut Lentil Salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Chop the aubergines into 2-3cm chunks. Coat a large baking tray with a drizzle of oil, then spread out the aubergine and cherry tomatoes. Season with salt and roast for 20-30 mins, until softened and beginning to caramelise.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Pour the coconut milk into a frying pan over a high heat and boil for 3-4 mins, until reduced by half. Pour into a blender with the hemp seeds and the coriander for the dressing and leave to cool slightly, then blend until smooth. Squeeze in the juice of all the limes, add the honey and season with salt. Loosen with a splash of water if needed.

Place the frying pan back over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Slice the paneer in half widthways, then cut into triangles. Once the oil is hot, add the paneer and cook for 5-8 mins, turning once, until golden brown on both sides. Remove from the heat and toss with the mango chutney to coat.
Reheat the lentils, then toss with the dressing, paneer and roasted veg. Roughly chop the remaining coriander and toss through. Share between boxes, leave to cool and pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Caramelised Paneer & Coconut Lentil Salad
description: I love a light but creamy dressing for salads, this zingy, herby coconut one is the perfect summer sauce - this one is for the hemp seed lovers! Tossed through hearty lentils, caramelised paneer and roasted aubergine, it only gets better as it sits in the fridge.
keywords: Caramelised Paneer & Coconut Lentil Salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Chop the aubergines into 2-3cm chunks. Coat a large baking tray with a drizzle of oil, then spread out the aubergine and cherry tomatoes. Season with salt and roast for 20-30 mins, until softened and beginning to caramelise.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Pour the coconut milk into a frying pan over a high heat and boil for 3-4 mins, until reduced by half. Pour into a blender with the hemp seeds and the coriander for the dressing and leave to cool slightly, then blend until smooth. Squeeze in the juice of all the limes, add the honey and season with salt. Loosen with a splash of water if needed.

Place the frying pan back over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Slice the paneer in half widthways, then cut into triangles. Once the oil is hot, add the paneer and cook for 5-8 mins, turning once, until golden brown on both sides. Remove from the heat and toss with the mango chutney to coat.
Reheat the lentils, then toss with the dressing, paneer and roasted veg. Roughly chop the remaining coriander and toss through. Share between plates or boxes.

name: Caramelised Parsnips with Honey, Sage & Hazelnut Dust
description: These sticky, honey-roasted parsnips are a beautiful combination of sweet and savoury. Perfect as a side for Christmas, Thanksgiving or any big old feast.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C / 375°F. Peel the parsnips and cut them into long wedges. Finely chop the sage and crush the hazelnuts.
In a large ovenproof skillet, melt the butter over a medium heat. Add the parsnips and cook until golden. Drizzle with honey, add sage, and toss to coat.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast for 15-20 minutes, until the parsnips are tender and caramelised.
Sprinkle the caramelised parsnips with hazelnut dust and serve warm.

name: Caramelised Soy Chicken in Garlic Ginger Broth with Rice
description: Sticky, caramelised kecap manis-glazed chicken thighs in a fragrant garlic and ginger broth, finished with a punchy sesame spring onion oil. It's one of those dinners that really earns its place in the weekly rotation.
keywords: Caramelised Soy Chicken in Garlic Ginger Broth with Rice
instructions: Bash the ginger and garlic, then transfer to a saucepan with the stock and place over a medium heat. Trim the spring onions, then thinly slice the green parts and halve the whites lengthways. Add the spring onion whites to the stock. Let the stock simmer away until hot while you make the rest of the recipe.
Put the chicken thighs into a bowl with the kecap manis, then season with salt and white pepper. Set aside to marinate.

Add the neutral oil to a frying pan with the spring onion greens and place over a high heat. Once the spring onions have wilted, tip them into a bowl. Stir through the sesame oil and toasted sesame seeds. Set aside.

Return the frying pan to a medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 7-8 mins until golden brown, caramelised and charring in spots. Pour water into the leftover marinade and pour over the chicken. Cook until reduced to a thick sauce.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice the cucumber and season with salt before serving. Reheat the cooked rice.Taste your broth, season generously with salt and pepper if needed.
Share the rice between bowls. Ladle over the stock and top with the sliced chicken and cucumber. Drizzle with sambal/chilli sauce and the sesame spring onion oil.

name: Carbonara Ravioli
description: Everything you love about a carbonara, wrapped up in a gorgeous little pasta package. This carbonara ravioli is a flex, in the most delicious way possible.
instructions: To make the pasta dough, pour the flour out onto a clean work surface and create a well in the centre. Crack the eggs in, beating together with a fork. Slowly incorporate the flour into the centre of the well until you have a thick paste. Bring the walls of flour into the paste and knead until you have a smooth, springy dough. Wrap in cling film, or cover with an upturned bowl and rest for 30 mins.

Set a small pan over a medium heat. Chuck in the peppercorns and toast for 2-3 mins, or until fragrant. Transfer to a pestle and mortar or spice grinder and coarsely crush. Tip the ricotta into a bowl and grate in the pecorino. Beat together, season with salt, lots of the pepper and add to a piping bag. If you don’t have a piping bag, chuck it into a sandwich bag and snip off the corner. Pop the bag into the fridge.

Roll out the rested pasta using a pasta roller or a stand mixer attachment. Pass one-third of the dough through the widest setting, and keep working your way down until you have landed on the second thinnest setting. Cut the pasta sheets into 10x10 cm squares and cover with a damp towel. Repeat until all the pasta is rolled out.

To make the ravs take a square of pasta and pipe a thick ring of ricotta just bigger than the egg yolk into the centre. Separate the egg yolks from the whites (you can freeze these for later) and plop an egg yolk into the middle and pipe some extra ricotta around the edge so the cheese comes all the way up the sides. Season the yolk, lightly brush the border of the pasta with water and carefully lower another square over the top, covering the yolk and cheese.

Carefully press your way around the filling, removing as much air as you can from the ravioli. Once it is mostly sealed, scoop up off the bench and press firmly around the edges to make sure the pasta is very sealed. You can trim the rav into any shape you like now, a fluted cutter is nice, cut into a heart, a star or leave as a square, up to you. Pop onto a semolina lined tray and repeat with the remaining ingredients, make a couple of extra if you can just in case any pop!

Bring a pan of water to a rolling boil and season with salt. Add the guanciale/pancetta to a pan and set over a medium heat. Cook slowly until the fat has completely rendered and the guanciale/pancetta is crisp. Drop four ravs into the water, cooking for 2-2.5 mins, you don’t want the yolk to overcook. Scoop the crispy guanciale/pancetta out of the pan and leave the fat. Lower the heat and drop in the butter. Add plenty of pepper and, once melted, add in a little cooking water and swirl around vigorously to emulsify. Cook gently until the butter is glossy and coating the pasta beautifully.
Divide between warm plates, top with crispy guanciale/pancetta, a mountain of pecorino and extra black pepper. Get stuck in.

name: Carbonara Salad
description: All the flavours of a carbonara in crisp and refreshing salad form. Fried spaghetti croutons are going to change your life. Or, at the very least, your dinner.
instructions: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Add the spaghetti and cook according to packet instructions. Drain and rinse well with cold water to wash away the starch, then spread out on a baking sheet and put into the fridge, uncovered, to cool.

Meanwhile, add the pancetta to a pan over a medium heat. Add 3 tbsp of olive oil, the gently sizzle until golden brown. Pass through a sieve over a jug, reserving the bacon-y oil. Set the oil aside in the fridge to cool.

Tip vegetable into a deep saucepan until it comes half way up the sides, place over a high heat and heat to 180°C. Toss the pasta in a little flour and add a handful to the pan of oil, cook for 3-4 mins until crisp, then remove and set aside to drain on kitchen paper. Repeat with the rest of the spaghetti.
Pull the leaves from the gem lettuce and add to a large bowl. Add the parsley. Set aside in the fridge. Use a peeler to peel some Parmesan into the bowl.

To make the dressing, add the egg yolk to the base of a small bowl. Add a little squeeze of the lemon, drizzle a little of the pancetta oil into the mix and whisk well, once it starts to thicken together, start to drizzle in the rest of the oil, very slowly, it should come together into a thick mayo dressing. Add the rest of the lemon juice, then finely grate in the Parmesan. Season well with salt and pepper, then drizzle most of it over the salad.
Crunch in the crispy spaghetti along with the pancetta chunks. Toss well then pile onto a platter. Top with extra dressing and parmesan and a crack of black pepper.

name: Cardamom Granola
description: Alex is the master of breakfast, and this is her ultimate granola. Spiced. Crunchy. It is the ultimate little breakfast dish. Great for meal-prep.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Make sure your hazelnuts do not have the skins on. If you can’t find any without, simply pop them on a baking tray and into the oven for 10 minutes. When they are ready, rub them between your hands and the skins should drop off.
Finely chop your nuts (hazelnuts and almonds).
Take a deep baking tray and mix the dry ingredients together. Oats first, followed by nuts, then seeds. We use pumpkin and sunflower seeds but you can choose whichever you prefer.

Now for the spices - cinnamon and cardamom. Crush your cardamon to remove the seeds from the pods, then place the seeds into the baking tray along with the cinnamon. You can crack open your cardamon using your fingers or a pestle and mortar, then gently pulling it apart and catching the seeds.
Toss and stir this all together.
Add your olive oil, maple syrup and a good pinch of sea salt. Mix together, then you’re ready to bake.
Roast your granola for 15-20 minutes, stirring halfway through, until nice and golden brown.
Add your coconut flakes and mix together.
Time to serve up! Pair with a dollop of yoghurt and drizzle of honey, a splash of milk, or with porridge and apple puree. Enjoy.

name: Caribbean Coconut Turmeric Rice
description: Pair this Grenadian coconut turmeric rice with our Caribbean king prawn curry. It will transport you to sunnier days. A banging recipe from Michelle Trusselle (@chefmichelletrusselle).
instructions: Thinly slice the peppers, onion and garlic.

Heat the coconut oil in a lidded pan and, when hot, add the peppers and onion. Sauté until the vegetables are soft. Add the garlic and cook for 2 mins. Stir through the rice, turmeric and herbs. Season with salt, add the stock and bring to the boil.

Place the lid on, reduce the heat to medium and cook for a further 10 mins before turning down to the lowest setting for a further 5 mins. Turn off the heat, remove the lid to let out some of the steam and place the lid back on. Leave to sit for 5 mins before fluffing the rice with a fork.
Serve with our Caribbean prawn curry.

name: Caribbean King Prawn Curry
description: The heat levels in this simple Grenadian prawn curry are just right. It will transport you to sunnier days. A banging recipe from Michelle Trusselle (@chefmichelletrusselle).
instructions: Make the green seasoning by washing the spring onions and herbs, then roughly chopping all the ingredients (except the lime). Transfer everything to a blender and add the oil. Blitz to form a rough paste – if it’s too thick, add a little water. Squeeze in the lime juice to finish. Set aside.

Check the prawns and remove any veins that are still intact. Finely dice the peppers. Add both to a bowl with the green seasoning, curry powder and a pinch of salt. Leave to marinate at room temperature for at least 20 mins.
For the curry, dice the onion, slice the chilli, mince the garlic, slice the peppers, halve the cherry tomatoes and slice the spring onions. Set aside.

Heat the coconut oil in a frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the diced onion and fry until slightly brown. Add the scotch bonnet and garlic and continue to fry before adding the spring onions. Reduce the heat to medium.

Mix the curry powder with the water. Add the curry mixture to the pan with the thyme and allow to reduce by half while stirring. Add the tomatoes and peppers, then cook for about 5 mins before adding the coconut milk. Bring to the boil then reduce to a simmer.
Add the prawns to the curry and cook until they turn from grey to pink. Stir in 1 tbsp green seasoning to finish.
Serve with our coconut turmeric rice, some fresh coriander leaves and a lime wedge.

name: Carne en su Jugo
description: This ‘meat in its juices’ is a delicious and easy recipe from the state of Jalisco that’s going to blow your mind. A quick and hearty meal for a cold day.
instructions: Start by making the salsa verde: peel the onion and garlic cloves and add them to a saucepan along with the fresh tomatillos and fresh jalapeños. Cover them with water. Bring to a boil over a medium heat then lower the heat and simmer for 10 mins. Meanwhile, roughly chop the coriander.

Strain the vegetables from the water (don’t discard the water yet) and transfer them to a blender, adding the coriander, salt and pinch of caster sugar. Blend until smooth. If the salsa is too thick, add a splash of water until it’s the desired consistency. Set aside.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and garlic. Dice the bacon rashers and cut the bavette steak into thin strips.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep-frying pan set over a low-medium heat. Add the onion and fry for 2 mins, before adding the garlic and cooking for another minute.
Add the bacon and fry for 3-5 mins until the bacon is cooked and just slightly crispy (don’t overcook it). Throw in the bavette strips and fry for 3 mins until they’re just cooked.
Add in the pinto beans, their bean juice and the salsa verde. Lower the heat and cook for about 10 mins. Season with salt to taste.
To prep the garnish, finely chop the onion and coriander.
To serve, divide the beans between bowls and top with the chopped onion and coriander, with warm corn tortillas on the side.

name: Carrot & Almond Rice Salad With Hot Sauce Yoghurt
description: A vegetarian weeknight dinner with a difference. Plump raisins add a subtle sweetness to this dish while hot sauce yoghurt brings the heat.
keywords: Carrot & Almond Rice Salad With Hot Sauce Yoghurt
Carrot & Almond Rice Salad With Hot Sauce Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the carrots lengthways and add to a large roasting tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season well, then slide into the oven for 30 mins, until softened.

Meanwhile, make the rice. Cook the rice according to packet instructions, then add to a bowl. Roughly chop the parsley and mint and add to the bowl. Roughly chop the almonds and add most of them to rice.

Tip the raisins into a small saucepan, add the lemon juice, ras el hanout and 2 tbsp olive oil, place over a low heat and gently warm for 5 mins, until the raisins are plump, then tip the mix into the rice. Season well with salt and pepper.
Mix the yoghurt and the hot sauce, season well.
Tip the rice into bowls or onto a platter, top with the carrots, drizzle in the hot sauce yoghurt and scatter with the remaining toasted almonds. Finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Carrot & Coriander Soup
description: A simple and delicious carrot and coriander soup recipe that'll give any other carrot and coriander soup a run for its money. The secret is roasting your veg until it's nice and caramelised.
keywords: mary berry carrot and coriander soup
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Chop up your carrots into halves and your onions into quarters.
In a large baking tray, combine the chopped carrots and onions. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Roast the vegetables in the preheated oven for 30 mins or until they are golden and tender. Slice your ginger into thin discs.
Remove the tray from the oven and scatter your ginger over the top of the roasted vegetables before drizzling your honey. Add the Harissa paste and stir well. Roast for an additional 15 mins.
When they’re done, transfer the roasted vegetables to a large pot. Deglaze the baking tray with a bit of stock, scraping up any flavourful bits, and add it to the pot along with the remaining stock.
Bring the mixture to a simmer over medium heat. Add the fresh coriander, saving some for a garnish, and use a blender to blitz the soup until smooth. Add in a squeeze of lemon juice for brightness.
While the soup simmers, warm the mini baguette in the oven. Once warmed through, slice it open and spread butter on the cut sides.
Serve the roasted carrot and coriander soup in bowls, topped with crumbled feta, a drizzle of harissa, and a sprinkle of fresh coriander. Enjoy with the buttered mini baguette.

name: Carrot & Courgette Cake
description: This rich, moist carrot and courgette cake is packed with seeds, zests, nuts and spices, and there’s no gluten in sight.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease two 23cm round cake tins with olive oil. Grind the hazelnuts in a food processor until they resemble breadcrumbs, then set aside. Make sure your butter is at room temperature.

Peel, trim and grate the carrots and courgettes. Use kitchen paper to soak up any excess moisture from the grated vegetables, then transfer them to a bowl along with the desiccated coconut. Add the sultanas and orange juice and set aside to soak.

In a separate mixing bowl, use an electric whisk to beat together the eggs and sugar for 5-7 mins until light and airy. Slowly add the olive oil in a steady stream, beating just enough to incorporate completely.
Fold in the ground hazelnuts, orange zest and spices. Finally fold in the soaked carrots and courgette mix, and the seeds.

Divide the mixture evenly between the two prepared cake tins and level out to the edges. Bake for 30–40 mins, or until the top has risen and a cocktail stick inserted into the centre comes out crumby but clean. Remove from the oven and allow to cool in the tins for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely.

Meanwhile, make the cream cheese frosting. Beat the butter alone for 4–5 mins, then add the drained cream cheese and beat for another 2 mins. Sift in the icing sugar and add the vanilla and beat for another 2 mins, until smooth and evenly incorporated.
When cool, spread the base layer with cream cheese frosting, sandwich together and spread more frosting on the top. Sprinkle with more sunflower and pumpkin seeds.

name: Carrot Cake
description: Whipped tahini frosting teamed with a classic carrot cake sponge — what a dream. Here's a carrot cake recipe worth getting behind. Thank us later.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Line two 20cm cake tins.
Whisk the oil, dark brown sugar, honey and eggs together. Set aside for 10 mins.
Whisk the flour, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon and ground ginger together. Add a pinch of salt.
Whisk the flour mix into the oil mixture, along with grated carrots (it’ll be very stiff). Use a spatula to fold the grated carrots into the mixture and stir well — you’ll feel the mixture loosen.
Divide the mixture between the cake tins and bake for 30-35 mins.

Make the honey caramel. Add the honey, brown sugar and butter to a shallow pan over a medium-high heat. Cook down until the sugar is melted and the mixture is thick and dark. Add the double cream and whisk in. Set aside to cool completely.
Remove the cakes from the oven, allow to cool in the tin for 5 mins, then tip onto a wire rack to cool completely.

Make the buttercream. Add the butter to a bowl with the icing sugar and mix with an electric whisk until very fluffy. Add the cream cheese and whisk a little further until thick and creamy. Add the tahini and mix to combine.

Place one of the cake layers on a plate. Add half of the buttercream, then drizzle with the honey caramel. Top with the other cake layer. Top with the remaining buttercream. You can cover the sides if you like.
Finish with a drizzle of honey caramel and scatter with sesame seeds. Slice and serve.

name: Carrot Cake Bircher Muesli
description: Carrot cake for breakfast? You bet. We've thrown all the flavours of your favourite cake into this healthy, high-fibre bircher muesli recipe. Tuck in.
instructions: Finely chop the walnuts and pecans, finely zest the orange, and coarsely grate the carrots. Add them into a bowl with the chia seeds, oats and hemp seeds.
In a jug, whisk together the water and yoghurt until smooth, then stir in the juice of the orange. Season with a pinch of salt and honey to taste.

Pour the liquid mixture into the dry ingredients and mix well. Divide between jars or containers, cover, and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight, until the oats and chia have soaked up the liquid.

To make the seed topping, toast the mixed seeds and sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 3–4 mins, or until golden and popping. Remove from the heat and stir in the mixed spice, a touch of salt, and honey. Spread onto a plate to cool, then store in an airtight container at room temperature.
When ready to serve, top each portion of muesli with a dollop of Greek yoghurt and a generous sprinkle of spiced seed crunch.

name: Carrot Gnocchi
description: A sweet and delicious homemade carrot gnocchi.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Peel the carrots, cut off the ends, then wrap in foil and place into a roasting tray. Prick the potatoes, then add them to the tray. Slide into the oven and bake for 1 hr until a knife slides through the potato without resistance and the carrots are soft enough to mash.

Remove from the oven and open the foil, discarding any water. Place the carrots into a bowl. Slice the potatoes in half then leave to steam for 1 min until cool enough to handle. Tip the pine nuts into the tray, if using, and slide back into the oven for 8 mins.

Scrape the potato flesh from the skins and add to the bowl with the carrots. Tip the mix into a metal sieve, then use a spoon to press through onto a clean surface – it will take a bit of time and elbow grease. Sieve the flour over the top, then use a knife to chop through until you have a crumbly mess. Bring together with your hands (you may need to flour them) and knead a little, then split into four pieces.

Using a little more flour to dust your hands and your surface, roll each piece into a 20cm log. Then use a knife to cut into 2cm-long pillows and set aside on a lightly floured tray or plate. Repeat with the rest of the pieces.

Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Working in batches, add the gnocchi to the boiling water and boil for about 1 min, until they float. Remove with a slotted spoon onto a plate and repeat with the rest of the gnocchi. Once done, don’t throw away the water.
Heat a knob of the butter in a large non-stick frying pan over a high heat and fry the gnocchi for a few minutes until crisp, then set aside on a baking sheet or plate.

Add the remaining butter to the frying pan and turn the heat down, then cook for a few mins until it starts to brown and smells a little like digestive biscuits! Add a ladle of the gnocchi water and toss to make a silky sauce. Using a fine grater, grate the Parmesan into the pan and toss or whisk some more – the sauce should be all combined. Add the gnocchi to the pan and keep tossing, adding salt and pepper and some lemon juice. Tip onto plates and top with the chopped pine nuts, plus more grated Parmesan.

name: Casarecce con Salsiccia
description: Rich, tomatoey, sausage pasta topped with parmesan. Fennel seeds are key here. This dish was a favourite at Ben's Dad's Italian restaurant, Cibo. Give it a go.
instructions: Tear up the sausage meat into bite-sized pieces and add them into a pan with a drizzle of olive oil and cook for 5 minutes until they begin to brown then remove.

Chop your cloves of garlic and add to the pan along with your fennel seeds, chilli flakes, a little drizzle of olive oil and season of salt. Fry on a low heat for about a minute (do not let the garlic brown).
When the garlic looks translucent add your wine, deglaze the bottom of the pan and bubble down. Then, re-add the sausage meat.
Get your pasta on.

At this point open your tin of tomatoes, hold a sieve over the frying pan and pour the tomatoes through. Smoosh the tomatoes through the sieve with a wooden spoon - we do this because we want the sauce nice and fine, but not as fine as passata. Season with salt.
Bubble the tomatoes down until you get a thick sauce.
Once the pasta has been cooking for 5 mins, add a splash of pasta water to your pan and bubble down so the sauce is smooth and silky.
When your pasta is ready, chuck it into the pan (reserving some pasta water) and toss it through your sauce. If your pasta still needs loosening, add a splash more pasta water.
Serve into your bowls and add a grating of parmesan or pecorino on top to finish. Enjoy!

name: Cashew Chicken
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This Chinese takeaway classic is tender, juicy and really easy to make at home. Perfect served with fluffy rice. One for your midweek rotation.
instructions: Start by marinating the chicken. Chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces and get it in a medium mixing bowl. Add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, salt and white pepper.

In a mug, combine the cornstarch and a splash of water (don't use the water in the ingredients list yet – save that for later) to make a slurry. Add to the chicken, mix to combine and leave to marinate for at least 20 mins.

Meanwhile, roughly chop the onion, red pepper and baby corn, thinly slice the carrot and spring onions, and mince the garlic. Don't combine the veggies yet; keep them separate on the chopping board as you'll use them at different times.

Wash your rice three times until the water runs clear. Drain, then transfer to a saucepan and add enough water to reach just below your first knuckle. Bring to the boil over a medium-high heat, then turn the heat to low, cover with a lid and cook for 12 mins.
Add the vegetable oil to a clean wok set over a medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 4 mins (reserve the marinade for later) then remove and set aside.

Set the wok over a medium heat, add the minced garlic and white onion and stir fry for a minute. Add the carrot, pepper and corn and stir fry for 3 mins then add the par-cooked chicken and the reserved marinade. Bring to a boil then add the water (the water listed in the ingredients list). Cook, stirring, for another few minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Add the white wine, pouring it in from the edge of the wok into the sauce. Add the thinly sliced spring onions and the cashews and stir fry for 30 seconds. Serve with rice and enjoy.

name: Cashew Green Chicken
description: This chicken recipe is as green as it's good – the homemade sauce adds a nice herbal zing to the dish. It's one of our favourite healthy chicken recipes.
keywords: Cashew Green Chicken. Cashew Green Chicken recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Chuck the cashews, coriander, mint, chillies and chicken stock into a blender and whizz until bright green and smooth. Season the chicken thighs with salt and preheat a large frying pan over a medium heat.

Add the chicken thighs, skin-side down, to the pan and begin to render the fat. Cook for 8-10 mins, barely touching the chicken until the skin is a deep golden brown and starting to become very crispy. Keep going until the skin is gorgeously golden and almost shiny like glass.

Once you’re happy with the skin, remove the chicken and add to a baking dish, skin-side up, leaving behind the chicken fat. Finely slice the red onion and tip three-quarters of it into the pan. Add a pinch of salt and cook for 3-4 mins. Now add the ginger paste and spices. Cook for 4-5 mins until fragrant. Now pour in the cashew mixture, and bring to a boil. Pour over the chicken in the roasting dish and slide into the oven for 25-30 mins.
Heat or cook the rice according to the pack instructions.
Pull the chicken out of the oven and serve with the rice, remaining onions and fresh lime wedges.

name: Cauliflower & Broccoli Cheese
description: The thing cauliflower cheese is missing is chorizo, which imparts a delicious, smokey flavour to the cheesy white sauce. This will become a household staple. In fact, cauliflower & broccoli cheese is undeniably a cult classic; if it makes you think of school dinners, think again. This recipe is jam-packed with a rich, cheesy sauce, plenty of chorizo, hefty amounts of broccoli, and just a hint of rosemary. It’s really, really tasty, so give it a go for dinner tonight and let us know what you think.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Crumble your chorizo into a pan and fry on a medium heat until crispy.
Add the sliced garlic cloves and fry for 30 more seconds. Remove the garlic and chorizo from the pan, leaving the oil.

Add a splash of olive oil to the pan along with plain flour. Beat it together with a whisk and once it has formed a roux (once it has combined) start adding your milk. Add it bit by bit, beating it in. Once you’ve added it all, you should have a nice thick white sauce.
Add almost all of your grated cheddar and grated Parmesan, reserving a little, some salt and a lot of pepper. Mix it in. Once melted, re-add your chorizo and garlic. Stir it in.
Break your cauliflower and broccoli into florets, add to the sauce and give it a good stir.
Once everything is evenly coated, top the dish with the remaining grated cheddar, Parmesan, a handful of rosemary leaves and a large handful of breadcrumbs.
Place in the oven for 50 minutes until nice and golden. Serve it up with a simple side salad and enjoy!

name: Cauliflower & Cashew Macaroni Bake
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

If I didn’t tell you this was vegan, you wouldn’t have a clue. Such a great way to transform a handful of ingredients into a dead healthy weeknight banger.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Chunk up the cauliflower and dice the carrots. Toss with salt and a dash of oil and spread out onto a tray.
Roast the cauliflower and carrots at 220°C until tender, this will take roughly 25 mins. Roast the garlic in foil with salt and olive oil for 25 mins until tender.
Drop the oven temp to 200°C.

Briefly toast the cashews in the oven. Once toasted, transfer to a blender jug and pour over 750ml of warm oat milk. Add the roasted cauliflower and carrots. Squeeze one of the roasted garlic bulbs out of its skin and add it in there as well. Blend until super smooth.
Season the creamy sauce with salt and pepper and set aside.
Squeeze the second roasted garlic out of its skin into a pan. Toast the breadcrumbs in some of the garlicky oil. Finely chop the thyme, rosemary and parsley and toss through the breadcrumbs.

Cook the pasta for a couple of minutes less than the pack instructs. Stir through the sauce with a big splash of pasta water. You want it a bit wetter than you think. Pour into a dish and top with the herby breadcrumbs.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until bubbling and golden. Serve with a fresh, zingy green salad.

name: Cauliflower & Cashew Stir-Fry
description: A vegetarian cauliflower and cashew stir-fry that ticks all the boxes.
instructions: Trim the base of the cauliflower, keeping any small, tender leaves. Cut into roughly 4cm florets, then cut the stem into 2cm cubes. Trim the top off the pepper, remove the seeds and cut into long, 2cm-wide strips. Cut two-thirds of the spring onions into 4cm pieces and very thinly slice the remaining spring onion. Peel and finely chop the garlic, then peel and finely chop the ginger, too.

Heat the sesame oil in a large frying pan or wok set over a medium-high heat. Add the cashews and fry for 2-3 mins until turning golden and smelling amazing. Use a slotted spoon to scoop out onto a small plate.

Tip the cauliflower florets, leaves and stem into the pan along with the pepper pieces and fry for 6-8 mins, stirring regularly, until caramelised and charred. Add the spring onion pieces to the pan along with the garlic, ginger and chilli flakes, then fry for 2 mins while stirring.

Spoon the hoisin, rice vinegar and soy sauce into the pan along with the water and cook for 10 mins until the cauliflower is cooked through and the sauce is clinging to everything. Add a splash of water if too thick. Meanwhile, cook the noodles following packet instructions.
