Tip the cashews back into the stir-fry pan, toss well and season with a little salt and black pepper.
To serve, divide the noodles between bowls and top with the stir-fry. Scatter over the thinly sliced spring onion.

name: Cauliflower & Chestnut Soup
description: A festive, wintery soup with roasted cauliflower and chestnuts and an umami-packed miso broth. It’s light, nourishing and incredibly cosy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 175°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Remove the cauliflower leaves and roughly chop the cauliflower head. Arrange on the baking sheet in a single layer, drizzle with olive oil, and bake for about 45 mins until golden.
Finely slice the dark green ends of the leek (reserve the rest for another recipe). In a medium bowl, toss with a pinch of salt and a bit of olive oil.
When the cauliflower has 10 mins left in the oven, add the leek ends to the baking tray (keeping them separate to the cauliflower) and roast for the final 10 mins or until crispy.

Peel and chop the shallots and garlic cloves. Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pot set over a medium heat and sauté the chopped shallots for about 5 mins until translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another 3 mins.
Add in the chestnuts (save for a few to use as a topping), roasted cauliflower and miso paste, stirring frequently as you do. Cook for 5 mins, or until the miso paste is slightly caramelised.
Pour in enough vegetable stock to cover the vegetables and simmer for 10-15 mins, until the vegetables are soft.
Blitz the soup in a high-speed blender or with a hand-held mixer until smooth. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Serve the soup hot, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil, a few sliced chestnuts, and a spoonful of crispy leek ends.

name: Cauliflower & Chickpea Curry with Sesame Fried Eggs
description: Chickpeas are always a good idea. We've topped this creamy cauli and chickpea curry with crispy-fried eggs with golden runny yolks. Beautiful.
instructions: Reheat the leftover Cauliflower, Chickpea & Peanut Curry in a saucepan over a medium heat, stirring occasionally until piping hot.
Finely slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish. Heat the oil in a small frying pan over a medium-high heat and carefully crack in the eggs.
Sprinkle the sesame seeds over the eggs and baste the eggs with the hot oil until cooked to your liking and crispy around the edges.
To serve, divide the curry between bowls. Top with the crispy eggs and spring onions. Serve with naan, if you like.

name: Cauliflower & Sesame Eggs With Herby Coriander Salsa
description: A killer combination of jammy eggs and a homemade herby coriander salsa. This slaps.
keywords: Cauliflower & Sesame Eggs With Herby Coriander Salsa
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Roughly chop the cauliflower into florets and add to a large roasting tin. Drain and rinse the chickpeas and add to the tray. Drizzle with olive oil and add the ground coriander. Toss well until everything is well coated. Add the garlic bulb to the side. Roast for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, blitz half of the coriander and mint with the edamame beans. Add the juice of a lemon and 3 tbsp olive oil, loosen with a little water if it’s particularly thick. Set aside.
Bring a pan of water to the boil, add the eggs and cook for 6 mins, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Remove the veg from the oven, squeeze the garlic from the casing into the tin, then add the juice of a lemon. Roughly chop the remaining herbs and toss through. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Toast the sesame seeds in a small dry pan over a medium heat for 2 mins until their nutty aromas release. Tip most of the cooled toasted sesame seeds onto a plate (reserving a scattering for serving). Peel the eggs and roll in the sesame seeds, then cut in half.

Spoon the herby veg onto plates, top each with 3 sesame egg halves plus and drizzle with the coriander and mint salsa over the top. Finish with a scattering of the remaining toasted sesame seeds to finish.

name: Cauliflower 65
description: A super simple, one-tray roast cauliflower inspired by the famous Chicken 65. We’ve used a show-stopping whole cauliflower and roasted it in the oven instead of deep-frying. The result is dynamite.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Thinly slice the green chillies for the marinade and transfer to a bowl. Add the remaining marinade ingredients, season with salt and mix well.

Trim the cauliflower, then rub the marinade all over. Place onto an oiled baking tray, transfer to the oven and roast for 30-35 mins until tender. Crank the oven temperature up to 200°C and roast for another 5 mins to get some colour onto the cauliflower.

Meanwhile, add a glug of oil to a small frying pan and place over a medium-high heat. Once hot, drop the curry leaves in and fry until darkened (they’ll splutter, so be careful). Transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper.
Once the cauliflower is cooked, plate up and drizzle over the pan juices. Finish with a scattering of crispy curry leaves.

name: Cauliflower And Tahini Soup
description: A spiced tahini and roasted cauliflower soup. filled with roasted garlic and topped with lots of crunchy parsley, chilli and sesame seeds.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Roughly chop your head of cauliflower into small pieces before dicing your potatoes into equally-small pieces. Next, slice one bulb of garlic in half.

Divide your potato and cauliflower pieces into two trays with the bulb of garlic and pour over a big glug of olive oil. Sprinkle with 2 tsp ground cumin, 2 tsp sumac, 2 tsp smoked paprika, and 1 tsp salt. Massage that well into the veg with your hands and pop those trays into the oven for 40 mins until the cauliflower is crispy.
Pick out a handful of the prettiest cauliflower florets and crispiest potato cubes, save these for garnish

Dice the onion and roughly chop 3 cloves of garlic. Sauté them in a glug of oil for 5 mins until the onion turns translucent. Add in 1 tsp smoked paprika and 1 tsp ground cumin and toast for 30 seconds. Now it's time to add in your roasted veg. Place your crispy potatoes and cauliflower into the pan, squeezing out the soft flesh of the roasted garlic cloves as you go, and pour in the vegetable stock. Bring this to a simmer and then blend with a hand blender until smooth. Add in 3 tbsp of tahini and season liberally with salt. Adjust the thickness with water.
Finely slice the remaining garlic, chilli and parsley.

Add a big glug of extra virgin olive oil to a frying pan. Fry the cumin seeds for 1 min until they start to pop. Add in the chilli, garlic, sesame seeds and then fry that off for 2 mins until the garlic is lightly golden. Add in the finely sliced parsley and cook for 30 seconds until the parsley is crispy. Season with salt and pepper.

Ladle your soup into bowls and top with your crispy chilli, garlic and parsley. Next, you're going to want to layer on your reserved roasted cauliflower florets and crispy potatoes along a drizzle of tahini and a sprinkling of sumac. Enjoy hot.

name: Cauliflower Cheese Beans with Preserved Lemon Salsa
description: My slightly elevated, slightly healthier twist on a cauliflower cheese, with extra protein from the butter beans and a little bit of something special with the preserved lemon salsa. If you want unadulterated comfort, you can always skip the salsa.
keywords: Cauliflower Cheese Beans with Preserved Lemon Salsa
Cauliflower Cheese Beans with Preserved Lemon Salsa recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the cauliflower into florets then transfer to a baking tray and toss with olive oil, salt and pepper. Slide into the oven and roast for 15 mins until charred, then remove and set aside. Drain and rinse the butter beans and reduce the oven temperature to 190°C.

Meanwhile, start making a béchamel sauce by melting the butter in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Once the butter is foaming, add the flour and cook it out for 2 mins until it smells nutty. Gradually pour in the milk, whisking as you go, until fully incorporated. Bring the mixture to the boil then reduce to a simmer, add the bay leaf and mustard and let it bubble away for a couple of minutes. Remove the pan from the heat, season the mixture with salt and pepper and remove the bay leaf.

Transfer the cauliflower and beans to an ovenproof dish and pour over the béchamel sauce. Scatter with crumbled feta then slide into the oven to bake for 25 mins until bubbling, then remove and let stand for 5-10 mins.

Meanwhile, for the salsa, finely chop the parsley and deseed and finely chop the red chilli. Halve the preserved lemons and scoop out and discard the middles, then finely dice the skin. Grate the garlic. Add the parsley, chilli, preserved lemon and garlic to a bowl along with the olive oil, sherry vinegar and preserved lemon brine. Whisk well to emulsify then taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
To serve, spoon the cauliflower beans onto plates and drizzle over the salsa. Serve with some salad leaves, if you like.

name: Cauliflower Cheese Croquettes
description: I'm not going to lie to you, these are some of the most moreish nibbles I’ve ever made. The crispy outside gives way to an absolutely filthy cheese and cauliflower molten middles. Give them a go.
instructions: Chop your cauliflower into florets. Boil or steam for 5 mins until totally tender. Allow to cool slightly, then chop into small pieces.
Grate your cheddar.
Add half of your cheddar to a hot frying pan and fry until golden and crisp. Pour off the oil, then leave to cool.
Once cool, finely chop your golden cheesy crust into pieces.
Add your butter into a saucepan on a medium heat.
Once melted, tip in your flour and cook out for 5 mins. Gradually add your milk, whisking until you have a smooth sauce.

Bring your mixture to a boil, then simmer for 5 mins until thickened. Add the remaining cheddar, the crispy chopped cheddar, cauliflower, nutmeg, and mustard, then stir to combine. Season to taste with salt and lots of pepper.
Pour into a wide dish to set in the fridge for 1 hour.
Pour your flour, eggs and breadcrumbs into a bowl each.
Roll your mixture into ping-pong-sized balls, then dip them in your flour, eggs and breadcrumbs respectively.
Heat a generous glug of oil in a small saucepan. Once hot, add your croquettes a few at a time and fry for 5 mins until crisp and golden. Keep warm and repeat with your remaining croquettes.

name: Cauliflower Cheese Gnocchi Traybake
description: Cauliflower, cheese, gnocchi, and traybake are four of our favourite words. This creamy midweek dinner will have everyone very fed and happy.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C. Chop your cauliflower into florets and roughly chop the leaves and stems if they are looking good. Add the cauliflower to a baking tray and drizzle with half of the olive oil, salt and pepper. Put in the oven to roast for 10 mins. After 10 mins, add the gnocchi and give everything a toss, then return to the oven for another 10 mins.

While everything is roasting, melt butter in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add your flour, then mix to a paste and cook for another 2 mins. Gradually pour in your milk in small increments, whisking constantly so you have a smooth paste before pouring the rest in. Once all the milk has been added, bring your mixture to a boil and let it simmer for 2 mins until thickened. Remove your sauce from the heat. Add your mustard and the cheddar and mozzarella, stirring until melted. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Preheat a grill to medium. Tip your cauliflower into a baking dish, pour over the cheese sauce and grate over the Parmesan. Grill until golden and bubbly, then remove from the oven before scattering with parsley.

name: Cauliflower Leaf Pesto
description: Don't chuck your cauliflower leaves MOB. Get them nice and charred in a frying pan, then blitz them into a zero-waste pesto with capers, parmesan and lemon.
instructions: Cut your leaves off your cauliflower and finely dice them. Grate your garlic.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add your cauliflower leaves to the pan and fry for a few minutes until the stems are tender and the leaves are starting to char. Add your garlic and cook for another minute.
Tip your cauliflower mixture into a bowl to cool.
Toast your walnuts in a pan for a few minutes until golden and fragrant.

Add your cauliflower leaves and walnuts to the bowl of a food processor. Add the zest of your lemon, your capers, parsley, parmesan and a pinch of salt and pepper. Pulse until the cauliflower and walnuts have broken down into a fine mixture.
Squeeze your lemon juice and put the lid on. Run the machine, gradually pouring in olive oil until you have a loose paste.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then serve as you would any pesto. Toss it through pasta, spread it on toast or eat it with roasted vegetables.

name: Cauliflower Manchurian
description: This is a take on an Indo-Chinese dish. It's spicy, sticky, sweet and creates a really unique melody of flavours that we know you will love.
instructions: Heat oven to 180c. Chop up the cauliflower into bite sized florets. If the leaves are nice, cut them into bite sized pieces too.

In a large bowl, combine the cauliflower with 1/3 of the oil, half the light soy sauce, the garlic powder, chilli powder, garam masala.Toss well and then pop onto a baking tray. Slide into the oven and cook for 15-20 minutes.

For the sauce, finely chop the spring onion, separating the whites and greens. Bash the Sichuan peppercorns in a pestle and mortar. Add in the garlic and ginger, then bash to form a paste. Slice up the green pepper and chop the onion into large pieces.
In a bowl, combine the rest of the light soy sauce with the dark soy, ketchup, sriracha, rice vinegar and water. In a small cup, combine 1 tsp cornflour with 2 tbsp water.

In a large pan or wok, heat the rest of the oil. Fry the spring onions, garlic paste, tomato purée and crispy chilli oil for 2 mins until fragrant. Add in the green pepper and onion, cook for a further 3 mins. Mix the water with the cornflour.
Pour in your sauce and cook on a low heat for 3 mins. Add in the cornflour slurry and heat again until the sauce is bubbling and thickened.
Toss in the roasted cauliflower, mix gently so that the sauce coats the veggies. Top with the spring onion greens and serve with rice, if you like.

name: Cauliflower Parmigiana
description: You've all heard of an aubergine parmigiana, but how about a cauliflower parmigiana? This rich and cheesy recipe is one of the best.
instructions: Finely slice the garlic. Heat a medium-sized sauté pan over a medium heat with a generous amount of olive oil. Tip in the garlic, fennel seeds and chilli flakes, then cook over a low heat for a couple of minutes until the garlic is fragrant, but not taking on colour.
Tip the tomatoes into the pan, then bring to a simmer. Cook the sauce gently for 30 mins.

Meanwhile, heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the cauliflowers into four large steaks, then rub them with olive oil and salt. Arrange on a baking tray and roast for 35 mins, flipping them over at 25 mins and sprinkling with half the Parmesan.
When the sauce has finished cooking, blitz it with a stick blender, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Once the cauliflower is done, spoon the sauce on top of each steak. Grate over the remaining Parmesan, then tear over the mozzarella. Sprinkle with oregano, then bake for 15 mins.
Twist over some black pepper and a little olive oil, then serve it up with salad.

name: Cauliflower Pittas with Cauliflower Leaf Slaw
description: These cauliflower stuffed pitas taste as good as they look. If tahini and cauliflower are right up your street, this recipe is proof that vegans have more fun. Enjoy.
keywords: Cauliflower Pittas with Cauliflower Leaf Slaw
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut off the cauliflower leaves and set them aside. Chop the cauliflower into bite-sized pieces. Drain the chickpeas and put them on a large baking tray lined with baking parchment along with the cauliflower. Ensure the chickpeas and cauliflower are not too crowded – use two trays, if necessary.
Add the olive oil, salt, a few twists of black pepper and all of the spices to the tray and toss to cover the chickpeas and cauliflower well. Roast for 25 mins, tossing once.

For the slaw, discard any brown or damaged cauliflower leaves and slice the rest very finely, stalks and all. Finely slice the red onion and add to a large bowl along with the cauliflower leaves. Squeeze over the lemon juice and add a good sprinkle of salt. Add the tahini and sesame seeds and toss well to combine, then set aside to soften.

For the herby drizzle, finely slice the jalapeño and garlic and transfer to a small food processor. Roughly chop the fresh herbs, including any fine stems, and add to the food processor. Pulse until finely chopped and then transfer to a small bowl. Add a pinch of salt, the lemon juice and a little zest, salt and pepper, and olive oil. Add more olive oil if needed to achieve a drizzling consistency. Add the chili flakes if using and stir.

To make the garlic tahini sauce, mince the garlic and add to a small bowl with the tahini and water. Whisk, then add the lemon juice and keep whisking to combine into a smooth sauce. Season with a pinch of salt.
To serve, warm the pitas and spread some tahini sauce on one side, pile in the cauliflower and green sauce, and finish with more tahini.

name: Cauliflower Tikka Gyros
description: Chargrilled, spicy cauliflower works perfectly as the main item inside a warm gyros. Cooled by a lovely, minty tzatziki.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.

Break the cauliflower into florets, cut into strips and place in a bowl. Add turmeric, chilli powder, ground coriander, cinnamon and about 1/5 of your yoghurt. Season with salt and pepper and mix everything together.
Heat a griddle pan. Once very hot, add your cauliflower in batches. Cook on a high heat for 3 minutes on each side, until charred.
Place the char-grilled cauliflower into the oven for 10 minutes so they can cook through.
Slice up the red onions. Squeeze the juice of a lemon over the top and season with salt. Leave for 10 minutes to pickle.
For your raita, add your grated cucumber, the rest of your yoghurt, a handful of chopped mint, a handful of chopped coriander, salt, pepper and olive oil. Mix everything together.
Take your pitta bread, cut it open and place the cauliflower tikka in the pocket and drizzle some raita over the top. Add your pickled onions, some chopped tomatoes, more raita and tuck in.

name: Cauliflower With Harissa Tahini And Lentils
description: This one's a super satisfying, protein packed meal. Great for meal prep, just keep the tahini sauce separate until ready to serve.
instructions: Rinse the lentils well.

Add the water to a pot with the lentils and bring to a boil. Simmer for 15 mins, covered. 
Add the rice and stock cube and cook for another 12-15 mins or until cooked. Drizzle with plenty of olive oil, salt and pepper and mix well.

Chop the cauliflower into small pieces, including the stem. Drizzle with oil, salt and pepper and za’atar, if using. Air fry at 190°C for 10 mins or roast in the oven at 180°C for 25 mins until golden and crispy.
Slice the very tough, large stems off of the cauliflower leaves and toss in a little oil and season. Air fry for 3 mins at 180°C or roast with the florets for 8-10 mins or until crispy.

To make the tahini sauce, whisk together the tahini with 120-150ml cold water. It will congeal but don’t worry – keep whisking and adding water until it turns into a creamy consistency. Add the harissa and season with salt and pepper.
To serve, lay the lentils and rice on a plate and top with the cauliflower and a good drizzle of tahini sauce. Feel free to scatter some pomegranate seeds on top as well, if you like.
For meal prep, keep the lentils and rice with the cauliflower, and keep the tahini sauce separate until ready to serve.

name: Cauliflower and Charred Lemon Curry
description: Packed with veggies and perfect for a midweek dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Roughly chop the cauliflower into 4-5cm florets, saving the smaller leaves. Tip the florets onto a roasting tray and drizzle with olive oil and season well. Slide into the oven and roast for 15-20 mins, until a little charred, adding the leaves for the last 5 mins.

Place a large saucepan over a high heat. Once the pan is hot, slice the lemon in half add it to the pan, cut-side down. Char for 2-3 mins, until blackened, before removing them and setting them aside.
Halve the new potatoes. Peel and finely grate, or finely chop, the garlic and ginger.

Add 2 tbsp of neutral oil to the base of the pan. Add the garlic and ginger and sizzle for a minute, then add the spices and cook for a minute further. Add the coconut milk, then refill the empty tin of coconut milk with water and add to the pan with the stock cube. Bring to the boil.
Add the potatoes, turn to a simmer, and cook for 20- 30 mins, until cooked through. Taste and season well.
Add your cauliflower back in and then stir through the spinach and the juice of 1 of the charred lemons halves.
Top with the yoghurt and coriander, finely slice the red chilli and scatter on top. Cut the remaining charred lemon halves into wedges and serve on the side.

name: Cauliflower, Chickpea & Peanut Curry
description: Packed with all the good stuff, this vegetarian curry is a batch cooking base that just keeps on giving.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Pod and roughly crush the cardamom seeds. Cut the cauliflower into florets and tip them onto a baking tray. Drizzle with oil and scatter over the cumin, cardamom seeds, salt and pepper. Put in the oven for 15 mins until charred.

Peel and finely slice the onion, then peel and grate the garlic and ginger. Heat a shot of oil in a large pan over a low-medium heat and add the onions and a pinch of salt, sweating down for around 15 mins until deeply golden. Grate in the garlic and ginger, then add the spices. Cook for a couple of minutes, then tip in the cauliflower, drained chickpeas, coconut milk, peanut butter and vegetable stock. Gently simmer for 5 mins until thickened, then season with lime juice, salt and pepper.

Serve with rice and enjoy. 
Optional: if you're batch cooking the curry, portion it out into Tupperware containers.

name: Cauliflower, Mushroom & Walnut Bolognese
description: A rich and luxurious veggie-packed bolognese. You won't miss the meat in this beauty.
instructions: Heat oven to 230°C. Grab your food processor if you have one – it will be your best friend here! If you don't, no panic. Simply finely chopping will do the job. It will slightly increase your prep time but I promise, it’s worth it.

Add the mushrooms to the processor and pulse until coarse. Break the cauliflower into florets and, working in batches, repeat the process until the cauliflower starts to resemble grains of rice. Then do the same with the walnuts.

Add cauliflower and mushrooms to 2 lined baking trays and drizzle with most of the olive oil. Season with salt and lots of pepper, then roast for 20 mins. Add the walnuts, give it a good mix, and cook for 15 more, flipping the trays to make sure it's all golden. You want everything to be golden and starting to catch - then it’s done.

Blitz celery, onion and garlic in the processor, no need to clean it out. Heat the remaining oil over a medium heat and cook it all in a pan for 10 mins along with the thyme. Add tomato purée and miso, and cook for 2 mins, then add the cauliflower, mushrooms, and walnuts and water. Simmer for 20 mins until thickened. Then mix through the cream.

Get your salted pasta water on to boil, then add in the pasta, cooking to package instructions. Grate your parmesan. Add the Parmesan to the ragù and transfer the pasta directly from its pot along with a good slosh of pasta water. Mix vigorously to emulsify until its really glossy. Garnish with more thyme and a little more Parm if you like.

name: Cavatelli With Sardine Pepper Ragù
description: An easy, sardine-y recipe that's perfect when you want to cook something delicious for when you're on your tod. Making your own pasta is a doddle, too.
instructions: Get started by making the pasta dough, tip the semolina onto your work surface and use a bowl to create a well in the middle of the semolina. Fill the semolina volcano with 45 ml of warm water. Using a fork, begin mixing the semolina into the water gradually until you have a thick paste.

Now, using your hands, incorporate the rest of the semolina to form a shaggy dough. Knead for 5 minutes until the surface is smooth and elastic. Form into a ball and rest the dough under an upturned bowl for 15 mins. Your dough is now ready to roll.
While your dough is resting, finely chop the shallot and garlic clove and roughly chop the pepper.

Cut your dough into 8 pieces. Roll each piece into a rope around 1cm thick. Line up the ropes and cut into 2cm pieces. Pop each piece onto a fork and using your thumb, press into the middle of each piece and roll away from you, creating a curl in the middle of the pasta and ridges on the outside from the tines of the fork. Repeat with the remaining pieces of dough. Toss with a little extra semolina and set aside.

To make the sauce, set a frying pan over a medium heat, add 1 tbsp of olive oil and let it preheat. Add the shallots and cook with a pinch of salt for 2-3 mins. Add the garlic and the chili from the sardine tin. Cook for 1 min then tip in the peppers and tomatoes. Cook over a medium heat at a simmer for 5-6 mins. Season with salt and pepper.

Bring a small pan of water to a boil and season with salt. Drop in the cavatelli for 2-3 mins. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the cooked pasta to the sauce with a splash of pasta water. Toss together and tip in the sardines, capers, sultanas and basil. Cook together for 3 mins.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and tip into a bowl, top with crunchy breadcrumbs and get stuck in.

name: Caviar d’Aubergine With Roast Chicken, Parsley & Pepper Salad
description: Smoky aubergine dip with Provençal herbs and garlic, served with gloriously golden roast chicken thighs and a fresh parsley salad. This the dinner that dreams are made of.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the chicken legs onto a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Season generously with mixed herbs, salt and pepper. Roast for 45-50 mins until golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, char the aubergines over a gas hob flame or under the grill. As the aubergines begin to cook, the skin will start to blacken. Once the skin is completely charred and black, remove the aubergines and put them into a bowl. Cover. As they cool, the skin will loosen, allowing you to peel the charred skin easily from the aubergine.

Peel the garlic and pick the thyme leaves, discarding the stalks. Blitz the aubergine flesh in a blender with the thyme leaves, garlic and 45ml olive oil. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Put in the fridge to cool.

Drain and thinly slice the roasted peppers, then set aside. Trim, peel and thinly slice the red onion, pick the parsley leaves and finely chop the stalks. Put the onion and herbs into a bowl of ice water to keep crisp. Before serving, drain the herb mixture and toss through the peppers, rocket, balsamic vinegar and the remaining oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Share the chicken between plates and serve with the aubergine caviar and salad.

name: Cavolo Nero & Wild Mushroom Risotto
description: We’ve added some extra greens to this risotto by throwing in cavolo nero – high in fibre and calcium – and finished it with garlicky mushrooms and Parmesan.
instructions:
Melt the butter in a large high-sided frying pan over a low-
medium heat. Finely dice and add the onion and cook for about
10 mins until soft but not brown. Thinly slice and add 2 of the
garlic cloves and cook for another 2 mins.
Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Strip the cavolo
nero from its stalks, roughly chop the leaves and boil for 5 mins.
Drain and blitz in a blender until smooth, adding water to blend.
Once the onions are cooked, add the rice and cook for about a
minute, stirring, until the rice is turning translucent at the edges.
Pour in the wine, turn the heat up to medium and let it bubble
away until almost completely evaporated.
Now begin adding stock, a ladleful at a time, stirring as you go
and only adding more stock once each ladle has been absorbed.
Once all of the stock has been absorbed, the rice should be rich and
creamy and almost cooked through but still with a little bite.
Spoon in the cavolo nero purée and finely grate in half the
Parmesan. Cook for another minute, then turn the heat to super
low, cover and keep warm while you cook the mushrooms.
Thinly slice the mushrooms, then heat the olive oil in a large pan
over a high heat. Add the mushrooms and fry with a pinch of salt
until browned.
Once the mushrooms have some colour, finely chop the
remaining 2 garlic cloves and parsley (stalks and all). Add to the
mushroom pan and cook for another minute or so. Turn off the
heat, squeeze in the juice of the lemon and toss.
Warm the cream in a small pan but turn off the heat when it
starts to steam. Grate in the remaining Parmesan, grind in about
a teaspoon of black pepper and stir until the Parmesan has melted
and the mix is thick and creamy.
Plate up the risotto and top with the garlicky mushrooms and a
drizzle of the Parmesan cream.

name: Cavolo Nero & Za’atar Orzo With Marinated Feta
description: This is our take on the super vivid green pasta using cavolo nero or black Italian kale. Full of iron and vitamins, it makes a great change from pesto and we’ve added some marinated feta and za’atar for a flavour hit. Save the stalks and finely slice to use in a minestrone.
keywords: Cavolo Nero & Za’atar Orzo With Marinated Feta
Cavolo Nero & Za’atar Orzo With Marinated Feta recipe
instructions: Get a large saucepan of salted water to boil.
Meanwhile, break the feta into bite-sized pieces in a small bowl. Zest in the lemon, spoon over za’atar and drizzle with a good glug of extra virgin olive oil. Toss, leave in the fridge to marinate.
Very finely slice the red onion, scrape into a bowl, squeeze in half the lemon juice and season with salt. Use your hands to scrunch the onion into the lemon juice and set aside to quick pickle.
Strip the cavolo nero leaves from the stalks. Add the leaves and the unpeeled garlic to the pan of boiling water, cook for 6 mins.

Bring the pan of water back to the boil, drop in the orzo and cook for 7 mins. Drain the chickpeas, add to the orzo and cook for another 2-3 mins until the pasta is cooked. Drain, saving a mugful of pasta water.

Using tongs, add the leaves to a blender, squeeze the garlic from its skins into the blender too. Add a good splash of pasta water, pour in a good glug of extra virgin olive oil. Add the remaining za’atar, blitz to a smooth vivid green sauce. Season to taste.
Tip the pasta and chickpeas back into the saucepan, stir in the green sauce, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen if needed. Season to taste, squeezing over the remaining lemon juice.
Top with the marinated feta and quick pickled onions and a little more za’atar to serve.

name: Cavolo Nero Pesto Beans
description: Beans and greens. We’ve served this classic pasta sauce with nutritious cannellini beans to up the amount of gut-loving fibre and plant protein. Delicious and good for you too.
instructions: Cut the stems off the cavolo nero. Blanch them in a large pot of boiling water for 30 seconds then drain and blitz in a blender until smooth.
Meanwhile, finely dice your shallot and garlic then add to a large pan with a splash of olive oil set over a medium heat. Fry for about 5 mins until lightly golden.
Pour in the beans with their liquid and simmer for around 5 mins, until most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir the blended cavolo nero through the beans and leave to simmer for 5 mins until the sauce has thickened.
Grate the Parmesan into the beans then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Divide between bowls and top with a sprinkling of chilli flakes, some extra grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Cavolo Nero Rigatoni
description: This simple recipe makes great use of my favourite winter vegetable, cavolo nero, which is a black kale from Tuscany that you can find just about everywhere.
instructions: Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil.
Wash and strip the leaves from the cavolo nero, peel the garlic and add both to the pan. Cook for about 5 mins, then remove, keeping the water.
Place the cavolo nero and garlic into a blender and pulse until mushy but not completely smooth.
Cook the rigatoni in the cavolo cooking water until al dente.

While the pasta cooks, place a large frying pan over a medium-low heat and add 100ml of olive oil. Finely chop the chilli (remove the seeds for less heat) and add to the frying pan, sizzle gently for a minute then turn off the heat.
In a small frying pan, add a splash of olive oil and fry the breadcrumbs until crisp and golden. Just before they're done, add the oregano, then set aside.
Drain the pasta and add to the pan with the oil and chilli. Add the blended cavolo nero and a splash of the pasta water and mix well to emulsify.
Plate up and top with the herby breadcrumbs.

name: Celeriac Mash Recipe
description: Celeriac makes a nice change from your regular old mashed potatoes – it has a richer, deeper flavour with a bit of nuttiness. If you’ve never had mashed celeriac before, you’re in for a treat with this simple buttery recipe.
instructions: Top and tail the celeriac, then use a large knife to trim off all of the skin, without taking off too much flesh. Dice into 2cm cubes and tip into a saucepan.
Pour in enough cold water to completely submerge the celeriac and season generously with salt.
Set over a high heat and bring to the boil. Once simmering, turn the heat down to medium-high and cook for 15 mins, until the celeriac is very soft.

Meanwhile, pour the double cream into a small saucepan. Put the garlic clove, still in its skin, onto the chopping board and use the flat side of a large knife to bash it against the chopping board. Add this to the cream along with the thyme sprigs and black peppercorns.
Set the small saucepan over a medium heat and bring up to a simmer. Once simmering, remove from the heat and leave to infuse.
Drain the celeriac really well through a fine sieve, then tip into a bowl or back into the dry pan.

Use a potato masher to crush and mash until roughly smooth, or you can use a stick blender to whizz until smooth - or if you want it really smooth, tip into a blender and whizz to a super smooth purée.
Put the fine sieve over the bowl and pour in the double cream, catching all the infusion bits.
Add cubes of the butter and keep mashing and mixing until combined and smooth.
Season really well with salt and pepper and serve.

name: Celeriac Purée with Black Truffle & Crispy Pancetta
description: Creamy celeriac with salty pancetta and truffle. A seriously indulgent side dish for special occasions.
instructions: Peel and cube the celeriac and potatoes.
In a large pot set over a high heat, combine the celeriac, potatoes, and stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer until tender (about 20 mins).
Drain the vegetables and return them to the pot. Add butter and cream, and use an immersion blender to purée until smooth. Season with salt and white pepper, then stir in the truffle oil.
Dice the pancetta. In a small pan, cook the diced pancetta over medium heat until crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Spoon the celeriac purée onto a serving plate, top with crispy pancetta, and garnish with shaved black truffle (if using – feel free to skip this).

name: Celeriac Remoulade with Roasted Chicken Thighs
description: You can’t beat a classic celeriac remoulade; creamy, tangy with salty pops from capers and cornichons. Use the sharpest knife you have for cutting the celeriac into even matchsticks. The remoulade makes enough for leftovers, which will keep happily in the fridge for up to 3 days, and makes an excellent addition to ham sarnies.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Season the chicken thighs all over with salt, pepper and the smoked paprika then drizzle over a splash of olive oil. Put onto a roasting tray and into the oven for 40-45 mins until the skin is crisp and puffed up and the chicken is super tender.

Meanwhile, peel the celeriac then, using a sharp knife, cut into thin slices. Cut each slice into matchsticks (this will take a while - be patient as the better you chop the celeriac the nicer the remoulade texture will be).
Spoon the crème fraîche, mayonnaise and mustard into a large salad bowl. Add the matchstick celeriac, toss to coat.
Chop all the herbs (stalks and all). Slice the cornichons. Add everything to the celeriac, along with the capers. Toss together, season with salt, pepper and lemon juice to taste.
Serve the celeriac remoulade alongside the roasted chicken thighs. Unreal.

name: Celeriac Soup with Crispy Sage & Hazelnuts
description: Celeriac is one of our favourite vegetables to make into soup. Once cooked it goes super soft, so it whizzes into the smoothest of soups — so satisfying and cosy! The crispy sage and toasted hazelnuts (as well as the double cream) make the soup seem even creamier.
instructions: Top and tail the celeriac, then use a large knife to trim off all of the skin, without taking off too much flesh. Dice into 2cm cubes. Halve and finely chop the onion, then finely chop the garlic.

Melt half of the butter in a large lidded saucepan set over a medium heat and scrape in the diced celeriac and onion. Add a big pinch of salt and put on the lid. Cook for 10 mins, stirring every now and again. You want the onion to soften but not take on any colour.
Add the garlic and cook for another 2 mins.
Pour in the chicken stock and add the bay leaves. Bring up to the boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 15 mins with the lid on, until the celeriac cubes are really tender.
Pour in the double cream and use a stick blender to whizz until velvety smooth. Season with salt and black pepper and keep warm.
Toast the hazelnuts in a frying pan for 2-3 mins until lightly golden and smelling amazing. Tip out of the pan and roughly chop.

Melt the remaining butter in the same frying pan with the vegetable oil set over a medium-high heat and add the sage leaves. Fry for 1-2 mins until crisp, then remove from the heat and tip in the toasted hazelnuts.
Spoon the soup between bowls and top with some of the crispy sage and buttery hazelnuts. Finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Chaat-Inspired Charred Cauliflower Salad
description: Chaat is love. Chaat is life. We've been inspired by one of our favourite savoury snacks in this gorgeous charred cauliflower recipe.
instructions: Pop the potatoes into a large pan and cover with cold water. Season generously and set over a medium heat and bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-12 mins until just tender. Put the potatoes into a bowl and coat with oil and salt.
Trim away any really chunky leaves from the cauliflower and trim the base. Mix the garam masala with 3 tbsp olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Pour over the cauliflower and massage in.

Set the Weber Lumin to steam and steam the cauliflower whole for 4-5 mins to begin the cooking process. Remove the cauliflower and set the grill to medium-high. Put the cauliflower back into the machine and grill, turning now and then, for 35-45 mins until thoroughly charred. Tip the oiled potatoes into the grill halfway through the cauliflower cooking time. Cook until crispy.

To make the coriander sauce, roughly chop the green chilli (seeds left in if you like it hot!) and coriander, stalks and all, and chuck it all into a blender with 1 ½ tbsp of the yoghurt, the juice of 1½ lemons, a good pinch of salt and the sugar. Blend to a smooth green sauce. Season to taste and set aside.
Take the cauliflower and potatoes off the grill. Break the potatoes into chunks and roughly cut the cauliflower. Dress with the remaining lemon juice.

Grab a platter and spread the remaining yoghurt over the bottom, then add a little olive oil and half of the coriander sauce. Now spread over the cauliflower and potatoes. Top with Bombay mix, the remaining coriander sauce, lashings of mango chutney and chilli pickle and finally the pomegranate seeds. Get stuck in.

name: Chana Masala with Raita
description: A comforting, protein-packed curry that’s as easy as it is flavourful. The rich, spiced chickpeas pair perfectly with a cooling mint and cucumber raita. Plus, a jammy egg on top to take things up a notch.
instructions: Peel and roughly chop the onion, garlic, and ginger. Remove the stems from the chillies. Blitz everything together in a blender until smooth to make a paste.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the paste and cook for 10 mins, stirring occasionally, until fragrant and slightly darkened.

Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then add them to the pan along with the chopped tomatoes. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 mins until thickened. Stir through the garam masala and season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, bring a pan of water to the boil and cook the eggs for 8 mins. Once done, cool them under cold water, peel, and halve.

For the raita, finely chop the mint. Halve the cucumber, scoop out the seeds, and grate or finely dice the flesh. Mix together the yoghurt, cucumber, mint, and the juice and zest of half a lemon. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the chana masala in bowls with the raita on the side. Top each portion with a halved egg and scatter over some fresh coriander, if using.

name: Char Siu Chicken & Rice
description: Sticky oven-baked Chinese BBQ chicken, served with garlicky chicken rice. A quick and simple dinner that really hits the spot.
instructions: Into a mixing bowl, add the chicken and all the ingredients for the marinade. Mix to coat the chicken thoroughly. Set aside to marinate for at least 30 mins or up to overnight.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with tin foil.
Place the marinated chicken on the tray, skin side up. Slide the tray into the oven to bake for 30 mins. Set aside the leftover marinade.

Meanwhile, start on the rice. Halve and finely slice the shallot. Mince the fresh ginger and garlic. Heat the vegetable oil in a medium saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the shallot and fry for 5-10 mins until golden brown and almost burnt. Add the ginger and garlic and fry for another 45 seconds.

Tip the rice into the pan and toast for 45 seconds. Add the chicken stock, fish sauce and a pinch of salt. Put the lid on, turn the heat to high and bring to a boil. Once boiling, turn the heat to low and cook for 18 mins, then turn the heat off and set the pan aside with the lid on until needed.

Get all the ingredients for the sauce – except the cornstarch and water – into a saucepan. Stir through the leftover marinade. Bring to a boil over a high heat then turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 1-2 mins.

In a mug or small bowl, make a cornstarch slurry by mixing the cornstarch and water together. Turn the heat down to the lowest setting and slowly pour the slurry into the pan whilst stirring. It should have the consistency of a gravy; if too thin, add more slurry. Set aside.
For the garnish, cut the spring onion into thirds and then slice into thin matchsticks. Roughly chop the fresh coriander. Add both to a bowl of icy water to curl and crisp.
Remove the chicken from the oven and leave to rest for 5 mins, then slice into 1cm strips.
To serve, add a generous amount of rice to a plate, followed by the sliced chicken. Ladle the sauce over the top. Add some of the spring onion and coriander to the side.

name: Chargrilled Asparagus Carbonara
description: A tasty twist on the traditional carbonara.
instructions: Slice your asparagus in half, down the long side of the stalk. Grill the asparagus until charred on both sides.
Get your pasta on.
Separate the yolks from the eggs and put them in a separate bowl. Add salt, pepper, Parmesan and the zest of a whole lemon to your egg yolks. Mix until combined.
Dice your bacon and fry in olive oil until cooked.
Chop the thyme finely and slice the garlic into thin discs. Add the grilled asparagus with the thyme and garlic followed by a cup of pasta water.

Turn the heat off under the sauce pan. Drain the linguine (but save the pasta water) and add to the pan, followed by the egg mix. Toss the contents of your pan with tongs to make sure everything is mixed evenly and the creamy sauce is smooth. Stir in another cup of pasta water for extra creaminess. Dish up and get stuck in!

name: Chargrilled Chicken & Garlicky Broccoli Rice
description: Smoky chargrilled chicken meets a garlicky broccoli-studded rice. This is a high-protein  meal prep recipe that's actually exciting.
keywords: chargrilled chicken and garlicky broccoli rice
instructions: Finely chop the garlic. Chop the broccoli into small florets, smaller than you would usually.
Add half the olive oil to a large saucepan with a lid and set over a medium heat. Chuck in the garlic and cook for a couple of minutes until fragrant.
Tip in the rice and pour in the chicken stock. Bring to the boil, then cover with the lid, reduce the heat to low and cook for 4 mins.

After 4 mins, scatter the broccoli over the top. Give everything a quick stir, replace the lid and cook for another 8 mins. Turn off the heat and leave the rice to steam for 10 mins while you crack on with the chicken.

Place one of the chicken breasts between two sheets of baking paper and bash it with a rolling pin until about 1cm thick. Repeat with the rest of the chicken. Add the flattened chicken to a bowl with the remaining olive oil, ground cumin, a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Toss to coat.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 3-4 mins on each side until well charred and cooked through. Transfer to a piece of foil, squeeze over the juice of the lemon and loosely seal to keep warm.
Finely chop the dill and stir it through the rice. Taste and season with more salt and pepper if needed.

Slice the chicken and serve it over the rice in Tupperware containers with a generous dollop of cottage cheese. Grate over a little lemon zest if you fancy. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chargrilled Chicken & Garlicky Broccoli Rice
description: Smoky chargrilled chicken meets a garlicky broccoli-studded rice. This is a high-protein that's actually exciting.
keywords: chargrilled chicken and garlicky broccoli rice

name: Chargrilled Chicken With Spiced Cauliflower Rice & Tahini Drizzle
description: Upping your daily protein intake just got a whole lot tastier. The tahini drizzle in this recipe is extremely addictive stuff.
keywords: Chargrilled Chicken With Spiced Rice & Tahini Drizzle
instructions: Place one of the chicken breasts between two sheets of baking paper and bash, with a rolling pin, until around 1 cm thick. Repeat with the rest of the chicken breasts, then add to a bowl with a drizzle of olive oil and the ground coriander. Season with salt and pepper and toss well.

Tip the tahini into a bowl and add the juice of half of the lemon, don’t worry- it’ll seize up! Add water, 1 tbsp at a time until it loosens to a drizzle-able consistency. Season well with salt and pepper and set aside.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat, once really hot, add 2 of the chicken breasts and cook for 3-4 mins on each side, until well charred, then set aside to rest. Repeat with the rest of the chicken, setting it aside.

Turn the cauliflower upside down and use a knife to cut off down the sides, to turn the cauliflower into a chunky crumbly consistency. Alternatively, you can whack it in a blender and blitz until it’s the consistency of rice.

Tip the cauliflower into the pan used for the chicken, season well with salt and pepper and cook for 3-4 mins, until softened. Finely slice the garlic. Add the quinoa along with the miso paste and garlic and sizzle for a minute longer. Roughly chop most of the coriander, saving some leaves to serve, and stir the chopped coriander through the rice along with the juice of a lemon. Taste and season well, then share between plates.
Slice the chicken, then place on top of the cauliflower rice. Drizzle with a little of the tahini dressing and top with coriander. Serve with the remaining lemon half, cut into wedges.

name: Chargrilled Courgette & Bulgur Wheat Salad
description: A fresh and zingy salad studded with cannellini beans and all sorts of delicious vegetables. Vegan salads don't get much better than this.
instructions: Toast the bulgur wheat in a hot pan with a drizzle of olive oil on medium heat for 2-3 mins until it smells fragrant and toasted. Add water and crumble in the stock cube. Bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer, cover and cook for 8 mins, or until the water has evaporated and the grains are soft and fluffy. Drain the beans and add them to the bulghur.

Meanwhile, chop the top and tail off the courgettes and slice them thinly lengthways, about 0.5cm thick. Drizzle them with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place on a hot griddle pan and cook for about 4-5 mins on each side until charred.
To make the dressing, whisk all of the dressing ingredients together and season well with salt and pepper. Roughly chop the herbs.
To serve, pile up the bulgur and top with the dressing. Finish with the flaked almonds and herbs and plenty of pepper.

name: Charred Asparagus Risotto
description: Zesty and creamy risotto topped with charred asparagus. Simple and easy meal with zing.
instructions: Heat the grill to its highest setting. Peel and dice the onion as finely as possible. Add 1 tbsp olive oil into a deep frying pan over a medium-high heat, add the onion with a big pinch of salt and fry until softened and translucent- around 10 mins.

Finely slice the garlic and add to the pan along with the fennel seeds and toast for 2 mins. Add the risotto rice and stir well to coat the rice, 1 min. Pour the wine in and bubble away until the wine has been totally absorbed.
Add the stock, one big splash at a time, stirring and letting it absorb fully before adding more.
Meanwhile, tip the asparagus onto a baking tray, drizzle with 1 tbsp of olive oil, season well and slide under the grill. Grill for 10-15 mins, until charred.

Finely grate the parmesan into the risotto, reserving a little for the top. Add the juice and zest of one of the lemons, if it looks a little dry, add a splash of water or more stock! Taste and season generously. Spoon into bowls, top with the charred asparagus, and finish with the reserved grated parmesan, zest of the remaining lemon and a scattering of parsley. Slice the zested lemon into wedges and serve on the side.

name: Charred Aubergine Dhansak
description: Dhansak is a popular Indian curry usually made with goat or mutton. We’ve created an untraditional vegan riff on it, using aubergine instead.
instructions:
Cut the aubergines into roughly 3cm (1in) cubes while you get a large, high-sided frying pan over a high heat. Add half the aubergine to the pan and dry-fry for about 4 minutes, turning halfway, until the aubergine is beginning to collapse and is a little charred. Tip into a bowl and repeat with the remaining aubergine.
Finely chop the onion, ginger and garlic. Put the pan back over
a medium heat, melt in the coconut oil and add the onion. Cook,
stirring occasionally, until soft, then add the garlic and ginger and
cook for 1 minute more.
Spoon in the chilli powder, ground coriander, turmeric and
fenugreek or cumin seeds.
Give everything a good stir until smelling amazing, then tip in
the plum tomatoes, along with 1 ½ tins of water. Stir in the lentils,
bring the curry to a simmer and cook for 15 mins. Add the
aubergine to the curry, cover and cook for 15–20 mins more
until the aubergine and lentils are cooked through.
Herby yoghurt time. Put most of the coriander (stalks and all)
and mint leaves into a blender or food processor along with the
coconut yoghurt and 1 tsp of the garam masala. Blitz until
smooth-ish, season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Come back to the curry: stir though the remaining 2 tsp of garam masala and season to taste – you may want to add some of
the remaining lemon juice here.
Spoon the yoghurt over the curry and tear over the remaining
herbs. Serve with rice or naan – your choice.

name: Charred Bavette with Smoked Tomato Salad
description: The bavette is an underrated cut of meat. We’ve charred it and paired it with a smoky tomato salad. Your barbecues just got a hell of a lot better.
keywords: Charred Bavette With Smoked Tomato Salad
instructions: Preheat the air fryer to 230°C.
Season the steak with salt and pepper and rub it with a little olive oil. Coarsely grind the fennel seeds and sprinkle over the steaks with the chilli flakes. Set aside.
Make the dressing by peeling the charred skin from the chillies, finely chop and add to a bowl with the sherry vinegar, honey and olive oil. Mix to combine then season well.
Now, cook the steaks on the Ninja grill until they hit 47°C for a perfect medium. Remove the steak off the grill and rest for 5-6 mins.

While the steaks rest, toss the tomatoes with some olive oil and salt and add to the grill. If smoking, add some pellets to the smoke box and use the smoke function to grill and smoke the tomatoes for 10 mins, otherwise just grill as normal.

Peel the charred skin from the shallots and roughly chop up the flesh. Tip into a bowl with the smoky tomatoes, roughly chopped roasted peppers, rocket and freshly picked basil leaves. Toss with half of the dressing and salt and pepper. Tip onto a platter.
Carve the steaks against the grain and serve over top of the salad. Top with the remaining dressing, more basil leaves and shaved Parm.

name: Charred Broccoli & Crispy Chickpea Salad
description: This salad has got it all. Charred broccoli, a nutty tahini dressing, and loads of crispy chickpeas we've zhuzhed up in the air fryer.
instructions: Preheat the grill function on your Satisfry Air & Grill to 260°C, trim the end of the broccoli and peel the outer layer of the stem. Slice the broccoli into florets, and finely dice the stem. Toss the broccoli florets and stems in some oil and grill until charred, 7-10 mins.
Drain the chickpeas, dry them and add into a bowl with 2 tbsp of oil. Season with salt and toss together.

Meanwhile into a bowl, add the toasted sesame, tahini, mirin, light soy sauce and sugar. Stir together until mixed (the tahini will seize, it’s ok). Stir 1 tsp of water at a time into the sauce until it turns back to being creamy. Taste and season with salt if it needs it.

Once the broccoli has charred, transfer to a plate. Change to the air fryer function and preheat to 220°C. Once hot, add the chickpeas in and cook until crisp 10-15 mins. Then toss through the Chinese 5-spice.

Thinly slice the spring onions. Add them into a heat-safe bowl with the chilli flakes. Heat 50ml of oil until piping hot, and pour over the spring onions. Let cool down and stir through the zest of ½ a lime and season with lime juice and salt.

Toss the broccoli, stems and crispy chickpeas in with the chilli oil. Spoon onto a sharing plate and drizzle over the creamy sesame dressing, as well as a sprinkle of pul biber to garnish. Serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Charred Broccoli & Peanut Salad
description: Charred broccoli drizzled in a nutty, satay-inspired dressing and served over a zesty rice salad, perfect for a midweek meal. Oh, and it’s vegan!
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200ºC. Take both broccoli heads and cut them into quarters, through the stem, to create 4 large wedges from each head. If your broccoli has a long stem, trim it off and set aside. Rub the cut-side of the broccoli wedges with olive oil, season with salt and lay, cut-side down, on the tray. Slide into the oven and bake for 25 mins, turning the wedges halfway through so the other cut-side is flat on the tray.
Make the dressing by mixing the peanut butter, coconut milk, soy and maple syrup together in a bowl. Add the juice of the lime and season well, set aside.

Cook the rice pouches according to packet instructions and tip into a large mixing bowl. Finely slice any chunks of broccoli stem and add to the rice. Roughly chop most of the herbs, reserving a few for the top, and add to the bowl along with the zest and juice of 2 limes and 2 tbsp of olive oil. Roughly chop the peanuts and add 3/4 to the rice mix. Season with salt and pepper and toss, then tip into bowls.

To serve, top each of the bowls with 2 charred broccoli wedges and drizzle with the peanut dressing. Finely slice the red chilli and scatter on top. Finish with the reserved herb leaves and peanuts. Serve the remaining lime, cut into wedges, on the side for squeezing over at the table.

name: Charred Broccoli and Spiced Labneh
description: Labneh is a middle-eastern style yoghurt cheese. It’s thick and creamy and is a great combo with the crunchy broccoli. So simple. The tastiest side dish.
instructions: Start by making the Labneh. Line a measuring jug with a cheesecloth and spoon the greek yoghurt into the cloth. Pick up the edges of the cloth and tie at the top. Then leave the cloth in the measuring jug and place in the fridge for a day to allow the yoghurt to thicken. The Labneh can be left in the cheesecloth to drain for 24 to 48 hours. The longer the yoghurt is left the thicker the consistency.
Once the Labneh is ready, it’s time to prepare the broccoli. Cut the broccoli into small, bite size florets.
Get a non-stick frying pan with a tbsp of oil on a high heat and fry the broccoli until nicely charred.
While the broccoli is cooking, untie the cheesecloth and spoon the Labneh into a bowl. Add a squeeze of lemon, a tbsp of cayenne pepper, salt and pepper. Mix together and set aside.
Roughly chop the toasted hazelnuts.

Serve the charred broccoli on a large platter and dollop over the spiced Labneh. Chop your dill and finish off each dish with a scattering of the dill, 1/2 tbsp of cayenne pepper and the chopped hazelnuts. Enjoy!

name: Charred Cabbage & Brothy Beets with Rice
description: A nourishing rice bowl with a beetroot miso mushroom broth, topped with crispy hispi cabbage. This one is full of plant-based goodness.
keywords: charred cabbage and brothy beets with rice
instructions: Coarsely grate the onion and beets into a saucepan. Add a drizzle of olive oil then set the pan over a medium heat. Cook the beet mixture for 3-5 mins.
Meanwhile, thinly slice garlic and chop the cabbage into 3cm chunks.

Add the garlic, bay leaf and tomato purée and cook for 3-4 mins until the garlic is fragrant and the tomato paste has darkened. Pour the vegetable stock and vinegar in and let it come to the boil then turn the heat down to a gentle simmer to keep the broth hot until ready to serve. Taste and season with salt, pepper and a dash more of vinegar, if needed.
Set a frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the cabbage and cook for 6-10 mins until starting to char then remove from the heat and stir the butter through. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, reheat the cooked rice. Pick and roughly chop the dill fronds and finely slice the stalks. Fold through the rice. Dissolve the miso in the broth.
Share the rice between bowls and ladle over the broth. Top with the cabbage and a dollop of soured cream.

name: Charred Cabbage & Giant Couscous
description: Cabbage really doesn’t get the love it deserves. It’s one of the most affordable and versatile veggies out there. Here I’ve charred it and served it with some giant couscous and herby tahini sauce. It’s a great, cheap vegetarian dinner.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Slice the cabbage into eight wedges through the stem. Trim and thinly slice the leek and garlic. Tip the giant couscous into a sieve and rinse.

Drizzle some olive oil over the wedges, then season with salt. Heat a frying pan over a high heat and place the cabbage, cut-side down. Char the cut sides, then transfer the wedges to a baking dish, cover with foil and and roast for 10-15 mins until tender.

Meanwhile, add a drizzle of oil to a saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Stir-fry the leeks for 6-7 mins until softened, then stir through the garlic, tomato purée and Lebanese 7-spice. Cook for 2-4 mins until the tomato purée darkens. Pour the water in and bring to the boil. Once boiling, tip in the giant couscous and cook, stirring frequently, following pack instructions (top with more water if the water is evaporating too quickly).

Meanwhile, pick half the mint leaves and add them to a blender with the Greek yoghurt, tahini and juice of the lemon. Blend, then season with salt and stir through 1 tbsp cold water at a time until smooth and creamy. (If you don’t have a blender, finely mince the mint and stir the ingredients together instead).
Spoon the couscous onto plates, top with the charred cabbage and drizzle with mint tahini sauce. Scatter the remaining mint leaves on top and serve with a wedge of lemon.

name: Charred Cabbage & Sesame Chicken with Brothy Rice
description: Smoky, charred cabbage meets juicy sesame chicken in this comforting, umami-packed brothy rice bowl. Tastes like a hug in a bowl.
instructions: Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens. Chop the cabbage into 2–3cm chunks. Thinly slice the chilli, if using.

Pour the chicken stock into a saucepan and add the chicken breasts, spring onion whites and half the sesame oil. Season with salt and pepper, then place over a high heat. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid and turn the heat down to low. Poach the chicken for 10–15 mins or until cooked through.
Meanwhile, heat a frying pan over a high heat (no oil needed). Add the cabbage, season with salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until it starts to wilt and char in spots. Set aside.
Shred the chicken. In a small bowl, stir a splash of the hot broth into the miso to make a loose paste, then pour it back into the stock. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, if needed.
Toss the shredded chicken with the sesame seeds, chilli and ½ of the remaining sesame oil. Taste and season again if needed.
Reheat the rice and divide between bowls. Ladle the broth over the top, then spoon on the chicken and cabbage. Finish with a sprinkle of spring onion greens and a drizzle of the remaining sesame oil.

name: Charred Cabbage With Whipped Sesame Tofu
description: Turn the humble cabbage into a delicious dish that’s high in protein and jam packed full of flavours and textures. Serve with a side of rice for a complete meal
keywords: Charred Cabbage With Whipped Sesame Tofu
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Cut the cabbage into four wedges and drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper and rub it all over the wedges.

Place on a baking sheet and roast for 15 mins. Remove from the oven, cover with silver foil and turn the oven down to 200°C. Return the covered cabbage to the oven and cook for another 10-15 mins, until soft enough to poke a toothpick easily through the thickest part.

Meanwhile, make the sesame whipped tofu. Add the sesame oil, salt, miso, tahini, rice wine vinegar and well-drained silken tofu to a blender. Blend until smooth and pop in the fridge to set a little until you need it.
Finely chop the chives and add to a bowl with the sesame seeds and a little salt and pepper.
To serve, spread the whipped tofu onto a large plate and layer over the cabbage. Top with more whipped tofu, crispy chilli oil, and sesame chives.

name: Charred Cauliflower with Peanut Sauce
description: A hearty vegan-friendly recipe that proves vegetable can be the centrepiece of a meal. You won't find a better cauliflower recipe.
keywords: Charred Cauliflower with Peanut Sauce  recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely slice the onions, then get them into a medium-sized saucepan with a good drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt. Cook them over a medium heat for 40 mins until they are caramelised.
Trim the leaves off the cauliflowers, then cut the cauliflower into quarters to give you big wedges. Arrange the wedges on a baking tray.

Mix the turmeric and curry powder in a bowl, then spoon a teaspoon or two of the spice mix over the cauli wedges, along with a big pinch of salt and some oil. Rub the wedges all over so that they are coated.
Roast the cauliflower for 40 mins, turning them halfway through cooking.
Meanwhile, peel and finely chop the garlic, finely slice half the chilli and finely dice the other half. Cut the tomatoes into small chunks.

Heat a sauté pan over a low heat with a good splash of oil. Add the garlic and chilli and cook for 2 mins until fragrant, then add the remaining spice mix and tomatoes to the pan. Cook for 10 mins until the mixture is thickened and dark.
Add the coconut milk, peanut butter and soy sauce to the pan, then simmer for 5 mins until it has thickened. Squeeze in the lime juice, then season with salt.
Spoon the coconut sauce onto plates, then top with the roasted cauliflower wedges. Top with the caramelised onions, remaining sliced chilli and coriander leaves. Serve.

name: Charred Corn & Fried Egg Som Tam Noodles
description: You've guessed it - another recipe inspired by my recent trip to Thailand! Som Tam is normally a dish made with green papaya, but on my travels I found an amazing version with corn instead. I've made it into a noodle dish so it's a bit more substantial and added egg for extra protein.
keywords: Charred Corn Som Tam Noodles with Prawns
Charred Corn Som Tam Noodles with Prawns recipe
instructions: Heat the grill to its highest setting. Place the corn on the cob on a baking tray and slide under the grill, turning regularly, until charred all over, around 10-12 mins. Remove and leave until cool enough to handle, then use a sharp knife to cut the kernels off the cob.
Finely chop the bird's-eye chillies. Squeeze the juice of the limes into a large bowl, then add the fish sauce, sugar and chilli. Stir until the sugar has dissolved.

Cook the rice noodles according to the packet instructions, then drain. Trim the green beans and chop into bitesize pieces. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Roughly chop the coriander. Roughly crush the peanuts.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Crack in the eggs and fry for 3-4 mins until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny. Boiling also works great here too.

Add the noodles, green beans, corn, cherry tomatoes and coriander to the dressing and toss everything together. Divide between containers and top with the egg and and pop in the fridge until needed. When you're ready to eat give the noodles a a good mix (the dressing may collect at the bottom) and scatter over the crushed peanuts fresh.

name: Charred Corn & Tomato Pasta
description:
Charred corn, blistered tomatoes with a gentle chilli heat, tossed through a creamy, cheesy mascarpone sauce - a super comforting weeknight pasta. Make it veggie by swapping the Parmesan for a vegetarian hard cheese alternative.

In Partnership with Aldi #ad
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Slice the chillis and finely chop the garlic. Add the corn to a baking tray, drizzle with 1½ tbsp of the oil and season with salt and pepper, then give it a good rub with your hands. Slide under the grill and cook for around 15 mins, turning a couple of times, until charred.
Add the tomatoes and chillis to the tray, drizzle with ½ tbsp of the oil, then slide back under the grill for 5 mins until charred.

Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the pasta and cook according to the packet instructions until al dente, reserving some of the cooking water before draining. Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and fry the garlic for 1-2 mins, until it's about to turn golden, then remove from the heat.

Once the corn is cool enough to handle, remove the kernels from the cob using a sharp knife. Add around three-quarters of the kernels to a blender with the mascarpone and fried garlic, then season with salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.

Pour the sweetcorn sauce back into the pan and gently heat through, then remove from the heat and add the pasta and grated parmesan. Mix well until the cheese has melted, then gently stir through the charred tomatoes and chillis, adding a splash more pasta water if needed. Divide between bowls, then top with the reserved charred corn, torn basil and a little more parmesan, if you like.

name: Charred Corn Gnocchi with Crispy Chorizo
description: An unlikely combo of ingredients that makes for a tasty and beautiful meal. It’s creamy, smoky, spicy and a little bit sweet - the perfect balance of flavours.
instructions: Drain the sweetcorn and thinly slice the garlic.
Brush a cast iron skillet with oil and set over a high heat.
Add the sweetcorn and cook, stirring occasionally, until charred in places.
Turn the heat down to low, add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, then transfer to a blender.
Grate the parmesan.
Add the parmesan, double cream, whole milk, smoked paprika, cayenne pepper to the corn and season generously with salt and pepper. Blitz until nice and smooth and set aside.
Finely chop the chorizo. Add it to a pan with a little bit of olive oil and set over a medium heat.
Cook until some of the fat has rendered out and the chorizo is nice and crisp.
Meanwhile, cook your gnocchi in plenty of salted boiling water according to the package instructions.

Drain the gnocchi, reserving some of the cooking water. Add the charred corn sauce and cook over a low heat until the sauce nicely coats the gnocchi, adding some of the gnocchi cooking water as needed.
Squeeze in the lemon juice and stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper, to taste.
Plate up the gnocchi, top with the crispy chorizo and basil leaves, then tuck in and enjoy.

name: Charred Corn, Chorizo and Creamy Blue Cheese Salad
description: The perfect salad to go alongside your BBQ.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Place your cobs of corn in a baking dish, cover in olive oil, salt and pepper and bake for 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, break apart the chorizo sausage into a non-stick pan and stir until cooked. Remove the chorizo, place in a bowl and set aside. Leave the chorizo fat in the pan.
Chop your spring onions into evenly sized pieces and cook in the leftover chorizo fat. Add the chorizo back into the pan and give it a good stir.
Slice your sweet peppers into rings and slice up the lettuce. Roughly chop the almonds. Remove the corn from the oven and use a knife to slice the corn off the cob.
Add all of your ingredients into a large bowl. Break your Saint Agur into chunks, finely chop your parsley and scatter both into the salad bowl.

Dressing time. In a jar, mix 6 tablespoons of olive oil with red wine vinegar, salt and pepper. Shake well with the lid on to ensure the dressing is fully mixed. Drizzle this all over your salad bowl.
With tongs, toss the salad, making sure all the ingredients are combined. Dish up with extra Saint Agur and get stuck in.

name: Charred Courgette Gnocchi with Herby Yoghurt & Chilli Butter
description: Crispy pan-fried gnocchi and charred courgette on a bed of cool, minty yogurt, finished with a chilli butter and almonds. A fresh and comforting weeknight stunner.
keywords: Charred Courgette & Gnocchi on Herby Yogurt
Charred Courgette & Gnocchi on Herby Yogurt recipe
instructions: Finely chop most of the mint, reserving a few leaves for serving. Grate the cucumber and garlic into a medium bowl. Add the yogurt, the juice of half the lemon and the chopped mint, season with salt and mix to combine.

Cut the courgettes into large irregular chunks. Heat a large frying pan over a high heat and a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the courgettes and cook undisturbed for 3-4 mins, until charred on one side. Flip and cook until another side is charred. Season with salt and remove from the pan.

Add the remaining olive oil to the pan. Add the gnocchi and fry undisturbed until one side is golden brown, then shake the pan and cook for another 4-5 mins. Season with salt and black pepper, then add the courgettes back in to heat through.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small saucepan over a medium heat. Add the chilli powder and cook for a minute, until fragrant.

Roughly chop the almonds. Spoon the herby yogurt onto each plate and spread into a thin layer. Pile on the gnocchi and courgette, then scatter over the almonds. Drizzle over the chilli butter, top with the reserved mint leaves and squeeze over the juice of the remaining lemon.You can swap the almonds for any nut you've got; walnuts, pistachios and pine nuts all work great.

name: Charred Courgette Skewers With Mint Oil
description: A super fresh and plant-based addition to your barbecue. These skewers are incredibly moreish.
keywords: Charred Courgette Skewers With Mint Oil
instructions: Cut the tofu into small cubes and place them in a bowl. Squeeze over the juice of one lemon, add the nutritional yeast, 1 tbsp of olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Toss to coat and set aside to marinate, tossing again once or twice to make sure the pieces are evenly coated.
Peel the courgettes into ribbons. When you get to the seeded core, stop peeling and cut the core into cubes. Thread the cubes onto a skewer.
Fold the courgette ribbons into concertina-style folds and skewer one at a time. Alternate with tofu, artichoke, courgette cubes, and sun-dried tomatoes, if using.
Repeat until you have used all of your ingredients. Any leftover ingredients can be tossed with some lemon, olive oil, and mint to make a salad.
Drizzle a little olive oil over the skewers and onto a hot griddle pan. Place the skewers onto the pan and grill for 1-2 mins on each side until charred.
To make the mint oil, layer the mint leaves one on top of the other and roll them tightly, then finely slice them. Add them to a small bowl with 60ml olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Lightly toast the pine nuts.
To serve, layer the skewers onto a platter and season well with salt and plenty of black pepper. Drizzle over the mint oil, then sprinkle the pine nuts and pomegranate seeds.

name: Charred Curried Corn with Feta
description: A nod to elotes, but by no means traditional. Juicy charred corn. Curried feta mayo. All topped with crispy garlic and spices. A summer BBQ beauty.
instructions: Finely chop ¾ of the coriander and 1 of the cloves of garlic, then combine with 100g of the feta, the mayonnaise, sour cream and curry powder in a large bowl. Mix well until creamy.
Finely slice the remaining 2 cloves of garlic and set aside.
Heat a griddle pan over a high heat. Grill the corn on all sides until it has some good colour and char and is cooked through.
Slather all over with the cheese mix and pop onto a plate. Squeeze over the lime, sprinkle with the remaining coriander and crumble over the rest of the feta.
Heat 3 tbsp of neutral oil in a small saucepan over a medium heat. Add the sliced garlic and fry for 2 mins until just turning brown.
Add the cumin and mustard seeds and fry for another 30 seconds. Add the chilli powder and remove from the heat, pour over the corn and serve hot.
Season to taste with a pinch of salt and finish with another dash of chilli powder, if you like.

name: Charred Feta & Beetroot Salad
description: Baked feta is a game-changer that'll elevate any dish. When heated, the feta transforms into a gooey, rich delight that perfectly complements the earthiness of roasted beetroot.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Drain your beetroot and place them on a parchment lined baking tray. Sprinkle with salt, then bake for 40 mins until charring on the outside.
Finely slice your garlic and chillies. Finely chop your coriander. Cut one of your limes into wedges.

Heat a frying pan on a low heat with a little olive oil. Add your garlic and chillies and fry for a few mins until the oil has turned red and the garlic is just starting to turn golden. Tip into a bowl to cool.
Once cool, zest in 2 limes and add their juice. Add 3 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper, then whisk to combine.
Toast your pumpkin seeds in a dry frying pan until just starting to go golden and release their oils. Sprinkle with salt.
Cut the feta into triangles and transfer to a baking tray. Drizzle with oil and bake for 10 mins or until golden
Warm the grains according to package directions. Once your beetroot are cool enough to handle, quarter them. Toss them with half your dressing, the grains and your coriander.
Assembly time. Spoon the salad into bowls and top with the feta triangles. Sprinkle it with your pumpkin seeds and your remaining dressing. Serve with lime wedges and enjoy!

name: Charred Greens & Beans Salad with Spice Paste Dressing
description: Fresh greens. Fresh herbs. Fresh flavours. This plate of blackened greens and butter beans is fierce and uses up any curry paste you have lying around in the cupboards.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the curry paste, lime juice, 4 tbsp olive oil and grated garlic together, season with salt and pepper. Pick the mint and dill — no need to chop.

Blanch the tenderstem for 3 mins in boiling water then drain and refresh in iced water. Finely slice the radish and finely slice the sugar snaps on the diagonal. Roughly chop the romaine. Trim the spring onions and remove the woody ends on the asparagus. Put all of your prepped veg into the bowl.
Heat a grill pan over a medium heat. Drizzle the asparagus and spring onions with oil and season with salt and pepper, then fry in the grill pan for 5 mins until charred and tender.
Pop into the bowl with the rest of the veg and drained beans, then give it a good toss to coat with the dressing. Serve on a platter and tuck in.

name: Charred Halloumi & Tomato Traybake Curry
description: Spiced halloumi and blistered cherry tomatoes in a smoky, tangy coconut and tamarind curry sauce. With the rice cooked straight in the curry all in one tray, this dish makes for a super easy weeknight winner.
keywords: Charred Halloumi & Tomato Traybake Curry recipe
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Toast the cumin and coriander seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2-3 mins, until fragrant. Tip into a pestle and mortar and grind to a rough powder, then mix in the ground turmeric. Cut the halloumi into chunky cubes and toss with the spice mix.

Tip the cherry tomatoes into a large baking tray, top with the spiced halloumi and drizzle with olive oil. Slide under the grill for 4-5 mins, until the halloumi is beginning to char and the tomatoes are starting to blister and burst.

Remove the tray from the grill. Turn the grill off and heat the oven to 200°C fan. Scoop half the cherry tomatoes into a blender, squeeze in the juice of the lime, pour in the coconut milk, then spoon in the tamarind paste and fish sauce (you can substitute for soy sauce to keep it veggie). Add a good grind of salt and pepper, then blitz until completely smooth.

Tip the rice straight into the tray (no need to microwave, it will cook in the sauce) and mix well, then pour over the sauce. Transfer to the oven for 20 mins, until bubbling and the curry sauce has thickened.
Pick the coriander leaves and scatter over the curry, spoon over the crispy chilli oil and serve straight from the tray.
