name: Charred Hispi Cabbage And Romesco Chickpea Sandwich
description: This sandwich is full of textures, layers and flavours: lightly crushed chickpeas in creamy Romesco sauce, charred hispi cabbage and roasted red peppers.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Cut the cabbage into quarters, drizzle with plenty of olive oil, salt and pepper. Cover with foil and bake for 20 mins. Remove the foil and roast for another 15 mins or until charred and cooked through. You should be able to slide a knife through with no resistance.
Roughly chop the cabbage into chunks and set aside to cool.

Meanwhile, make the romesco sauce. Add 2 large red bell peppers, the sunflower seeds, lemon juice, sherry vinegar, smoked paprika, salt and 75ml olive oil to a blender. Blend until smooth and season with salt and pepper to taste.

Drain the chickpeas and add them to a bowl or wide plate. Add most of the romesco sauce to them and mash with a fork too get a chunky texture, keeping about half of the chickpeas whole. Taste and season again as the chickpeas may need extra seasoning.
To build, layer the chickpeas, two or three slices of red pepper from the jar, the cabbage and finally the leaves between two slices of sourdough bread. Enjoy!

name: Charred Hispi Cabbage Noodle Bowl With Green Curry Dressing
description: Vibrant. Garlicky. Spicy. This noodle bowl is an absolute breeze to make. Say hello to the latest addition to your weekly rotation of meals.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.

Cut the hispi cabbage into 8 wedges through the stem and drizzle with olive oil, then season with salt and pepper. Heat a large frying pan over a high heat and place the cabbage, cut-side down. Fry the cabbage for about 10 mins, turning over halfway when it’s nicely charred. Then, transfer the cabbage to a baking dish, cover with foil and put in the oven to continue cooking for 5-10 mins, or until tender.

Meanwhile, pick the mint, discard the stalks. Pick the coriander leaves and keep the stalks. Add the coriander stalks and most of the mint and coriander leaves (keeping some for garnish) into a blender. Add in the curry paste, lime juice and ½ a tbsp of olive oil and blitz until smooth, taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper. If you don't have a blender, finely chop the herbs and mix with the other ingredients. Set aside.

Cook the noodles according to packet instructions. Drain and rinse in cold water. Tip the sesame seeds into a dry pan and place over a medium heat, toast for around 2 mins, until golden. Finely slice the garlic.

Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and add the green beans. Fry until they start to char, then, remove from the pan and set aside. Add the garlic and fry for 2-3 mins before adding the ground coriander, then turn the heat off. Tip the noodles into the pan and pour over the dressing. Mix well and adjust the seasoning.
To serve, plate up the noodles and green beans, then top with the charred hispi. Garnish with the toasted sesame seeds and reserved herbs.

name: Charred Hispi Cabbage with Honey Vinegar and Herby Yoghurt
description: This makes a great side for a piece of roasted lamb or some grilled veggies. Jordon x
instructions: Start by removing the outer leaves of the cabbage and giving it a rinse, then slice into quarters.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat and add a splash of olive oil. Place the cabbages with the outer side down and cook for about 5 mins, moving around a little as they cook.
Season the cabbages all over with salt and pepper, then flip on to the cut side. You’ll want to cook each cut side for about 3 or 4 mins until it has a lovely golden brown colour.
While the cabbages cook, mix the honey, white wine vinegar, zest and juice of the lime in a small bowl.
Finely chop both chillies and all of the herbs. Mix the chillies into the honey vinegar and the herbs into the yoghurt.
Once the cabbage is cooked, remove from the pan and drizzle all over with the honey vinegar while still warm.
Spread 2 tablespoons of yoghurt on each plate, top with a wedge of the hispi cabbage and enjoy.

name: Charred Leeks, Butter Beans & Pickled Chilli Sauce
description: Comforting leeks and beans with some pickled chilli, lemon, white wine and crispy capers for a little pizzazz. This is a vegan recipe you're going to love.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.

Drain and rinse half of the beans. Remove the dark green tops of the leeks, keeping the root on. Cut the leeks in half lengthwise, then rinse each leek half under cold, running water, gently fanning layers open while being careful to keep leek halves intact to wash away any sand or grit. Peel and thinly slice the garlic cloves. Drain and pat the capers dry.

Pour the vegetable stock into an ovenproof dish and place the leeks cut-side down into the dish. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and bake for 20 mins. Halfway through, turn the leeks so that they are cut-side up.

Meanwhile, trim and finely mince the chilli – use a food processor if you have one to make this easier. Add the chilli, apple cider vinegar, hot water, sugar, 2 tbsp olive oil and ½ tsp salt into a heatproof bowl. Stir together until the sugar and salt are dissolved. Leave to pickle.
Zest the lemon. Roughly chop the parsley and smoked almonds.

Add 3 tbsp of olive oil into a large saucepan, add the sliced garlic and place on medium heat. Cook until it starts to go golden, add the fennel seeds and cook until fragrant, 1 min. Pour the white wine in and let reduce by half. Add all the beans with ½ a jar of bean liquid to the pan, stir together until piping hot and creamy and then remove from the heat. If you want your beans to be creamier, add a spoonful of beans with a few tablespoons of water into a blender and blend until a smooth paste forms, it should be the texture of thick double cream. Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Add a splash of water or more bean liquid if it needs to loosen, and stir the parsley through.
In a small pan, on medium-high heat, add 1 tbsp of olive oil. Once hot, add the capers and let cook until crispy, 2-3 mins.
Once the leeks are soft, turn your grill on to high, drizzle the leeks with some olive oil and grill them until brown and starting to char, 6-12 mins.

Serve the leeks on the beans. Garnish with lemon zest. Pour over the crispy capers and their oil and as much pickled chilli sauce as you want. Finish with the smoked almonds and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Charred Lemon & Leek Risotto with Shimeji Mushrooms
description: A simple vegan risotto recipe that's bright and zesty and unbelievably creamy (even though it contains zero cream, obviously).
keywords: Charred Lemon & Leek Risotto with Shimeji Mushrooms
instructions: Slice the leek into about 1cm rounds and wash well. Whisk the stock cube through the boiling water. Mince half of your garlic cloves. Slice ¾ of your lemon into very thin slices, as thin as you can get them. Remove the pips. Set everything aside.

Melt half of your vegan butter in a large pan or deep frying pan. Add the lemon slices in a single layer and cook over a low-medium heat for 2-3 mins on each side until charred but not crispy. Remove the charred lemons and set aside. Leave all of the charred bits in the pan – this is the big flavour.
Add a splash of olive oil to the same pan, plus the leeks and a good pinch of salt. Sauté the leeks with the minced garlic over a medium heat for about 10-15 mins until softened.
When the leek is caramelised and softened, melt the other half of your vegan butter, then add the rice and fry for 2-3 mins until toasted. Add the wine and cook until evaporated.

Add the stock, little by little, stirring and waiting until it’s all been absorbed before adding more. Keep adding until you have used up all of the stock and the rice is almost cooked through and still has a nice bite to it. It will take about 20 mins.

While the risotto is simmering, cook the mushrooms. Grate the rest of the garlic cloves and set aside. Slice off the brown end of the block of mushrooms, trying to keep the stalks intact. Slice the block down the middle so you end up with two blocks. Lots will fall apart, but don't worry – as long as some are still grouped together. Heat a good drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan. Place the mushrooms into the hot oil and season well with salt and pepper and spread the minced garlic over the exposed sides. Press them down with a spatula and let them cook on one side for about 3-4 mins until charred. Then carefully flip them over and cook the other side until charred. Set aside once cooked

Warm the milk, whisk through the miso paste and soy sauce and add this mixture to the risotto pan. Cook for about 5 mins, stirring all the time, until cooked to your liking and still very creamy. Add plenty of pepper and taste for salt as the miso will provide some saltiness.
Add a final knob of butter to melt through, if you like, plus the juice of the remaining half lemon. Add a splash or two of oat milk if it thickens too much and you would like it creamier.
Reserve about one-third of the charred lemon slices for topping and finely chop the rest. Add the finely chopped lemons to the risotto and stir through.

To serve, plate up the risotto and top with the charred lemon slices and mushrooms. Finish with some lemon zest, a good squeeze of lemon, a sprinkle of nutritional yeast, and plenty of pepper. Add a drizzle of olive oil, if you like.

name: Charred Lemon Chicken
description: Juicy charred chicken dressed in a lemony sauce on a bed of creamy cheesy potatoes. This will impress anyone you've got over for dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Peel the potatoes and cut into quarters. Add to a large pan of salted cold water. Peel the garlic cloves and add to the pan with the potatoes. Put on a lid and set over a high heat. Once boiling, remove the lid and simmer for 12-15 mins until the potatoes are very tender.
Meanwhile, make the chicken. Slice the lemon into 1cm slices, then season the chicken breasts really well and drizzle with a little oil.
Heat an ovenproof frying pan over a high heat. Add the lemon slices to the dry pan and fry for 2 mins until the underside is nicely charred. Transfer to a plate.

Turn the heat down to medium-high and add the chicken breasts, skin-side down, then put another frying pan on top to weigh them down. Fry for 4-5 mins until the skin is really crisp, then remove the top pan and turn them over. Add the butter and capers. Continue frying and basting the chicken breast, skin-side up, with the buttery capers for 2 mins.

Pour in the white wine and bubble for 2 mins, then lower the heat to a gentle simmer, pour in the cream and stir vigorously to combine. Lay the charred lemon slices on top. Put the pan into the oven for 10 mins until the chicken is cooked through, juicy and the sauce a little reduced.

Meanwhile, drain the potatoes through a colander, shaking off all the excess water, then tip them back into the pan and mash everything really well. Put the pan back over a very low heat, then grate in the cheese, add the double cream and butter and mash everything together really well until smooth. Season well with lots of black pepper.
Divide the aligot potatoes between two shallow bowls. Spoon over the sauce and top with the chicken and charred lemon slices. Finish with a sprinkling of roughly chopped parsley.

name: Charred Lime Yoghurt and Quorn Makes Amazing Kebab Lettuce Wraps
description: Crispy Quorn Makes Amazing Turkish Style Kebab, with a tangy charred lime yoghurt and herby quinoa served in crisp lettuce leaves
instructions: Wash your quinoa in cold water. Put it into a saucepan with 300ml water, your smoked paprika and a pinch of salt." Bring it to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10-15 mins until all the water has been absorbed. Pop on a lid and allow it to steam for 5 mins. Fluff it up with a fork.
Slice your limes in half and finely chop the jalapeno, coriander and parsley. Dice up your jarred red peppers. Peel apart the leaves of the baby gem lettuce.

Heat a saucepan to a medium heat and drizzle in olive oil. Pop on your limes, cut side down and let them char for 2 mins or until the limes have darkened and caramelised. Put them aside to cool slightly.
In a bowl, mix the yoghurt, coriander and jalapeño. Squeeze in the juice and flesh of the charred limes, give it a good mix and season to taste.
Stir the chopped parsley into the quinoa
Using the same saucepan as the limes, pour a glug of oil and pan-fry the Quorn Makes Amazing kebabs. Cook for 3 mins until browned and crispy.
To build the wrap, pile the quinoa on to a baby gem leaf, add the crispy Quorn Turkish Style Kebab, top with the lime and jalapeno yoghurt and the diced peppers.

name: Charred Onion and Fennel Broth with Fregola, Chickpeas and Feta
description: Onions and fennel are charred in a hot pan, then simmered in chicken stock with garlic, aromatics, fregola and chickpeas. Once cooked, the soup is finished with lots of soft green herbs, lemon and feta for a hearty but fresh dish.
instructions: Trim and peel the onions but leave the root on and cut each one into 8 wedges.
Add a splash of olive oil to a large saucepan over a medium-high heat and add the onion wedges in a single layer. Cook until very golden/slightly charred on each side.
Roughly chop and add the fennel, fennel seeds and garlic cloves. Cook for a few minutes until starting to soften, then pour in the chicken stock and bay leaves.

Bring to a simmer, then add the fregola and cook for about 10 mins. Drain and add the chickpeas and the parsley, basil and mint all roughly chopped (you can keep a pinch of the herbs aside for garnish). Cook for another 2 mins.
Taste and season with salt, squeeze in the lemon juice and then spoon into bowls. Top with the remaining herbs, crumble over the feta and finish with a drizzle of olive oil and grind of black pepper.

name: Charred Peach Panzanella
description: A more summery salad never existed. Adding beautiful Ocado charred peaches and a punchy olive tapenade to this Italian classic takes it up a notch.
instructions: Heat your oven to 150°C.
Tear your stale ciabatta into bite sized pieces. Pop them on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and salt, then bake for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, chop your tomatoes into large chunks and pop them in a colander set over a large bowl. Season them with salt and leave to sit for 15 mins.
Slice your peaches into 3cm pieces.
Heat a griddle pan over a high heat. Add your peaches and cook for a couple of minutes on each side until you have nice char lines.
Lift your sieve off the bowl - you should be left with a bowl of tomato juices. Add the juice of ½ lemon, 4 tbsp olive oil and pepper, then whisk to combine.
Tip your ciabatta, tomatoes and peaches back into the large bowl and toss to combine. Leave to sit for 30 mins.
Add your olives to a blender along with your basil and the zest and juice of your remaining ½ lemon. Add a pinch of salt and a little olive oil, then blend until you have a smooth sauce.
Spoon your panzanella into bowls and spoon your tapenade over the top. Serve and enjoy.

name: Charred Pepper & Halloumi Pasta
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad. 

Pasta. Chunky charred red pepper and tomato sauce. Golden halloumi bits. What’s not to love?
keywords: Charred pepper and halloumi pasta recipes
instructions: Using a pair of tongs, place the bell peppers over an open flame on the hob. Cook, turning often, until charred all over. If you don’t have a gas stove, you can char your bell peppers under the grill in the oven.
Transfer the peppers to a bowl, cover with cling film and leave for 10 mins. The steam created will make it easier to peel the skins off.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, mince the garlic, halve the cherry tomatoes and dice the halloumi into 1 cm cubes.
Peel the peppers and slice into thin strips.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the halloumi cubes until golden all over then transfer to a plate.
Cook the pasta in plenty of salted water until it’s al dente.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, around 5 mins.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 min then add the cherry tomatoes and 150ml water. Season generously with salt and pepper and cook for 5 mins, or until the tomatoes begin to break down.
Stir in the sliced bell peppers and season again with salt and pepper. Add the apple cider vinegar and sugar and cook for a further 5 mins.
Roughly chop the basil.
Remove the sauce from the heat and stir in the fresh basil. Taste and adjust the salt level to your liking.

Drain the pasta, reserving a few ladlefuls of the pasta cooking water. Add the pasta to the sauce with the halloumi cubes and a ladleful or two of the pasta cooking water and toss until the sauce nicely coats the pasta. Divide between bowls, serve and enjoy!

name: Charred Sea Bass With Fregola Salad
description: A fresh recipe where we've combined a vibrant green and red salsa. A nice healthy dinner that'll wow just about anyone.
keywords: Charred Sea Bass With Fregola Salad
instructions: Make the tomato marinade. Add the paprika, garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, and diced tomato into a blender or food processor with a tbsp of olive oil. Blend until it forms a paste. Rub the paste over the white flesh of the sea bass and set aside in the fridge for 10-15 mins.

Make the salsa verde by blitzing the herbs, anchovies, Dijon and juice of the lemon to make a thick and chunky paste. Add enough olive oil to make it drizzle-able consistency, then season well and set aside.

Rinse the giant fregola in a sieve until the water runs clear, then tip into a saucepan. Cover with boiling water, season with salt and place over a high heat. Bring to the boil and cook according to packet instructions. Drain and rinse with cold water, then tip into a bowl. Add the juice of the lemon and the capers. Roughly chop the soft herbs and toss them through, then finely dice the tomato and onion, add to the mix and season well. Add 1-2 tbsp olive oil.

Preheat the grill to high. Slide the marinated fish under the grill, flesh side up and cook for 3-4 mins. The marinade will char a little and the flesh beneath will cook through. To check if the flesh is cooked, you can pop a skewer in, if it passes through the fish with no resistance, you’re all good!
Spoon the fregola onto plates, top with the sea bass, drizzle with salsa verde. Scatter with a few extra herb leaves and top with a crack of black pepper. Slice lemon wedges and serve with the fish.

name: Cheat's Burrata Toast
description: Who knew that gooey bit of burrata was so easy to make at home? Only two ingredients to make the tastiest thing to eat on toast.
instructions: Tear your mozzarella into pieces, then pop it into a bowl. Add your crème fraîche and a good pinch of salt, then give it all a mix.
Cover the bowl with cling film and pop it in the fridge for a couple of hours.
Cut your figs into quarters.
Toast your bread in a frying pan with olive oil until the slices are crispy.
Spoon your cheat’s burrata onto your toast. Top with slices of prosciutto, figs, a drizzle of honey and a crack of black pepper.

name: Cheat's Cinnamon Swirls
description: The fluffy, sticky and sweet cinnamon swirls you all know and love, just easier. Puff pastry is the key. Drizzled with icing sugar and chopped pecans. Sublime.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C/392°F. Line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the butter with the sugar, cinnamon and a big pinch of salt until completely incorporated - you need the butter to be soft before you start (not melted).

Unravel the roll of puff pastry and turn it so that the longest edge is facing you. Using a spatula or wooden spoon, carefully spread 3/4 of the cinnamon butter across the puff pastry in a thin layer, getting it into all the corners. Rolling away from you, roll the pastry into a sausage then cut into 10-12 rolls depending on how big you want them.

Place the cinnamon rolls with the swirl facing up onto the lined baking tray, leaving 2-3cm between each so they will spread and just touch when baked. Squash down slightly on the top of each one with your hand - this will encourage the swirl to stay. Melt the remaining cinnamon butter in the microwave then brush all over the cinnamon rolls - this will ensure they get golden and sticky. Bake in the oven for 25 minutes until cooked through.

Leave to cool slightly. Meanwhile, toast the nuts and roughly chop. Mix the icing sugar with a splash of water to make a thick drizzlable icing. Drizzle the icing over the cooled buns and top with the toasted nuts. Keep in an airtight container for 3-4 days. BOOM.

name: Cheat's Custard Tarts
description: Delicate custard ‘tarts’ made with two halves of soft St Pierre brioche burger buns. Perfect for brunch or tea!
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Whisk together the yoghurt, maple syrup, egg and vanilla.
Flip the buns and using a teaspoon press down the insides to make an indent.
Pour the custard mixture into the buns and bake for 8 mins.
Take the buns out and decorate with fresh fruit.
Mix the jam with a tablespoon of water and brush that over the fruit until it looks all glossy.
Cut in half and enjoy.

name: Cheat's Dan Dan Noodles
description: Dan dan noodles are one of our most loved takeouts, and this dish manages to pack that epic flavour punch within a fraction of the time and ingredients. Easy.
instructions:
Get a large frying pan or wok over a high heat. Drizzle in a splash
of neutral oil and then squeeze the sausages out of their skins
straight into the pan. Add the five-spice powder and some salt
and black pepper. Leave to fry for 5 mins, stirring occasionally
to break up the meat, until crisp.
Meanwhile, slice the white stalks of the pak choi and separate the
leaves but keep them whole. Finely slice the spring onions. Set
both aside.
Dan dan sauce time. Use a fork to mix together the tahini,
dark soy sauce and as much chilli oil as you can handle with
2 tablespoons of hot water in a small bowl.
Back to the sausage meat, add the noodles and pak choi stalks
to the pan. Stir-fry, tossing everything together using tongs, for
1 minute, then pour in the Dan Dan sauce along with the pak choi leaves. Stir-fry for a further minute, then top the noodles with the
sliced spring onions and divide between four bowls to serve.

name: Cheat's Jian Bing
description: I love jian bing (also known as Chinese-style crêpes), but they’re not the easiest to make in a home kitchen. So here’s a cheat’s/inspired version of this iconic Chinese street food breakfast using frozen paratha and Mama Yu’s Chilli Oil. This idea was inspired by the one and only J. Kenji López-Alt.
instructions: Add the frozen paratha to a frying pan set over a medium heat and cook following pack instructions until it's golden brown and crispy. Remove and set aside.
Meanwhile, whisk the egg and finely chop the spring onion. Add the spring onions to the bowl of whisked egg.
Add a splash of vegetable oil to the now-empty pan along with the egg mixture. Fry for 30 seconds on each side.
While the egg is frying, spread the hoisin and sriracha onto one side of the cooked paratha.
When both sides of the egg are cooked, place the paratha directly onto the omelette, sauce-side down, until it sticks, then remove and set aside.
Slice the tomato and tear the lettuce leaf into small pieces. Finely chop the coriander.
Crush the peanuts.
Top the paratha with the tomato, lettuce, crushed peanuts, coriander, sesame seeds and chilli oil. Enjoy!

name: Cheat's Lahmacun
description: A juicy lahmacun recipe made easy using ready-made flatbreads, cutting the total time by more than half.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 220°C. 
Trim and peel the onions. Thinly slice one and roughly chop the other. Wash the thinly sliced onion under cold water to remove any harsh taste. Set aside. Pick ¾ of the parsley leaves, saving the stalks.

Peel the garlic, deseed and trim the pepper, then roughly chop. Add the roughly chopped onion, pepper and garlic into a food processor with the remaining whole parsley and the extra stalks. Pulse until minced, then transfer to a sieve set over a bowl. Squeeze as much liquid out of the veggies as possible. Discard the liquid, then add the veggies into the bowl with the lamb mince, tomato paste, pul biber and ½ tsp salt. Using your hands, thoroughly mix the ingredients together.

Evenly share the lamb mixture onto the khobez or wraps and spread into an even layer to the edges. Place the lahmacun in the oven and bake for 3-4 mins until fully cooked through. Transfer the lahmacuns to a plate, stack them and cover.

Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice the pickled chillies. Transfer to a bowl and toss with the thinly sliced onions, parsley leaves, sumac, a drizzle of olive oil and a splash of pickled chilli brine. Wedge the lemons.
Top each lahmacun with the spicy sumac onion salad. Squeeze over some lemon juice, roll up and eat as a wrap.

name: Cheat's Summer Veg Pilaf
description: The tastiest way to use up all your leftover veg is to grill them until nice and charred, toss with rice and spices and turn them into a easy cheat's pilaf.
instructions: Finely slice your onions. Halve your radishes and grate your garlic. Slice your courgettes into rounds.
Toss your courgettes in a bowl. Squeeze over the juice of half a lemon, a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Mix to combine.

Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a glug of olive oil, then tip in your cumin seeds. Cook for a minute until fragrant, then tip in your sliced onions. Fry for 20 mins until they are totally soft and caramelised.
Meanwhile, heat a griddle pan over a medium heat. Add your courgette slices and grill for a few minutes on each side until you have deep char lines.
Add your garlic, ground cinnamon and turmeric, to your onions, then cook out for another minute.
Tip in your radishes and peas, then fry for 3 mins until just tender.

Add your cooked rice to your pan and cook for a few mins until piping hot, stirring to prevent it from sticking. Tip in your courgettes and mix to combine. Add the juice of a lemon, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Combine your mayonnaise with the zest and juice of your remaining lemon in a bowl. Add a little water to make it a drizzle-able consistency.
Roughly chop your pistachios and mint.
Spoon your pilaf onto a serving plat. Drizzle your mayo over your pilaf, then sprinkle over your pistachios, mint and pickled chillies. Serve and enjoy.

name: Cheat’s Green Egg Piadina
description: Vibrant green egg piadine stuffed with melted cheddar & served with a fresh tomato, mozzarella & basil salad. Quick, fun, and full of flavour.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the shallot. Add to a bowl with the sherry vinegar, olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cut the tomatoes into wedges, reserving a few for the kids’ plates. Toss the rest into the bowl with the onions, then pick over the basil leaves and tear in the mozzarella. Toss to combine — this is your tomato & mozzarella salad.
Grate the cheddar. Add the spinach and eggs to a blender and blitz until smooth and bright green. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat a large nonstick frying pan (26–28cm) over a medium heat. Melt a third of the butter, then pour in a third of the spinach mixture, swirling to coat. Immediately place a piadina flatbread on top. Cook for 1½–2 mins until the egg is mostly set, then flip so the flatbread is egg-side up. Scatter over some cheese, and let cook for 30 secs more. Fold in half and slide out of the pan. Repeat with the remaining mixture.
Serve up! Kids Plate: Cut a piadina into wedges and serve with the reserved tomato slices.Parents Plate: Serve the piadina alongside the tomato & mozzarella salad.

name: Cheat’s Miso Ginger Ramen
description: Lean pork medallions are marinated in soy sauce, ginger, garlic and miso, then pan-fried and sliced in this simple ramen recipe. It's good. Very good.
instructions: Mince the garlic and ginger. Mix miso with soy sauce, add the ginger and garlic and give it a good mix. Marinate the pork with this mix and leave in the fridge.

Mix the chicken powder with boiling water to make your stock, add to a large pot. Bash your spring onions, garlic and ginger, and add to your pot, along with miso, soy sauce and chilli oil. You can also add some dashi, if you'd like. Give it a good stir then let it simmer for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, add oil to a pan and fry the pork steaks for 4 mins on each side until they’re cooked.

While your pork is cooking, blanch your pak choi in a pot of boiling water for just a few minutes, then set aside and carefully add your eggs in, cook them for just 5 mins (so they’re a bit jammy inside).

Cook your noodles in a separate pot of boiling water according to packet instructions or pop them into a deep bowl of boiling water and cover with a lid before draining out the water. This takes a little longer to cook but saves you from washing up another pot.
Slice your spring onion greens and pork into 1cm strips.

Add your noodles to a deep bowl, along with a few ladles of your broth, top with your pork strips, jammy egg, pak choi, spring onion greens and add a drizzle of chilli oil and sesame seeds and you’re done!

name: Cheat’s One-Pot Aubergine Lasagne with Ricotta & Parmesan
description: Think lasagne, but lazier. One pan, no layer, just creamy, saucy, cheesy comfort made from your Aubergine Alla Norma batch leftovers.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Aubergine Alla Norma batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 200°C.
Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Blanch the lasagne sheets for 1 min, then remove with tongs and set aside on a plate, make sure they’re not touching or they’ll stick. Save the water.
Tip the Aubergine Alla Norma leftovers into a deep ovenproof frying pan along with the tinned cherry tomatoes. Place over a medium heat and bring to a bubble.

Tear the lasagne sheets in half and stir through the sauce with a splash of the blanching water to loosen. The sauce should be a bit thinner than usual, the pasta will soak a lot of it up. Taste and season well with salt and black pepper.
Dice the mozzarella. Dot the ricotta and mozzarella evenly over the top, then grate over the parmesan. Drizzle with a little olive oil.
Transfer to the oven and bake for 35–40 mins until golden and bubbling. Garnish with basil, if using.

name: Cheat’s Sourdough Tin Loaf
description: A no-nonsense sandwich loaf which is soft, airy, and great for everyday baking. Recipe by MOB Contributor Thomas Colson.
instructions: The night before you make your dough, take your starter out the fridge and feed it.
The next day, mix together the water and flour in a medium mixing bowl and combine until all the flour is absorbed. You should have a loose, shaggy dough. Leave for one hour.
Add the salt and starter to your dough and mix with wet hands until it's combined.

Transfer the dough to an oiled medium mixing bowl. Cover with a tea towel and let the dough rise in a warm place until it has doubled in size. This usually takes around 12 hours, but can take as little as four.
Now transfer your dough to an oiled 26 x 14cm loaf tin taking care not to knock too much of the air out of the dough, and leave to rise for one hour.
Preheat the oven to 200°C / 392°F. Bake for 15 minutes.
Turn the oven down to 180°C / 356°F. Bake for a further 30 minutes.
Remove your bread from the oven, transfer it to a wire rack, and leave it to cool for one hour. Enjoy!

name: Cheddar & Chutney Sausage Rolls
description: Cheddar & onion chutney work wonders in the sausage roll - keeping the inside really lovely and moist (sorry).
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/365°F.
Grate the cheese. Squeeze the sausages out of their skins into a bowl.
Mix the grated cheese, thyme leaves and mustard into the sausage meat. Add some seasoning.
Warm the chutney slightly so it spreads more easily.
Unravel the sheet of puff pastry and cut in half length-ways. Spread red onion chutney over each rectangle.
Divide the sausage mixture into two equal parts. Lay out the mixture along the length of each pastry strip in a cylindrical shape - you want there to be a 1cm border.
Brush the top of the sausage meat and borders with beaten egg yolk. Tightly roll the pastry over the sausage to encase it. Cut into 12 sausage rolls and chill for 15 minutes.
Brush the remaining egg over the sausage rolls and sprinkle over the sesame seeds. Bake for 30 minutes until cooked through and a deep golden brown.

name: Cheese & Broccoli Pasta
description: This cheese and broccoli pasta is like the beloved Pasta 'N Sauce from the packet, but infinitely better! A one-pot wonder, it comes together in less than 30 minutes, making it perfect for busy weeknights. It's a meal the whole family will love!
instructions: Get your biggest pan on a medium-low heat and warm olive oil. Finely chop the garlic then fry for 3 mins until just golden. Add the vegetable stock, milk, butter, onion powder, pasta and then mix the cornflour with water and add in as well. Season with salt and pepper then bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 mins.

While that's cooking, chop the broccoli. Then grate the Parmesan and finely chop the parsley. Add the broccoli to the pasta and continue cooking for another 10 mins – by this point the broccoli and the pasta should be tender, and the sauce thickened. Add in Parmesan and parsley, then give it a good mix – if it's looking too thick just loosen with a splash of milk.
Plate up, top with a bit more parsley and Parm if you like, and that's it!

name: Cheese & Onion Lasagne
description: An easy, cheesy lasagne that’s definitely not for anyone sensitive to dairy. A million times tastier than a packet of cheese and onion crisps.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the onions. Melt the butter in a heavy-based pot over a medium heat and add the onions, thyme and bay leaves. Gently cook for around 30 mins, stirring so the onions don’t catch, until lightly golden and smelling sweet. In the meantime, drain and cut the pickled onions in half. Add the pickled onions, Worcestershire sauce and the stock to the pan, simmering for another 5 mins until reduced and thickened.

Heat oven to 200°C. For the béchamel, grate the cheeses, finely chop the chives and melt the butter in a large pot over a medium heat. Add the flour and cook out whilst stirring for around 4 mins, until golden and smelling biscuity. Gradually add the milk, mixing well after each addition to ensure there are no lumps. Continue adding the milk whilst whisking until it's all incorporated, then add in the mustard and most of the cheese, saving some for the top. Mix well and simmer for a couple of minutes before adding most of the chives and seasoning with salt and pepper.

Add a ladle of the cheese sauce to a baking dish around 20cm x 30cm, then layer with lasagne sheets. Top with some of the onion ragù, then more of the béchamel. Repeat with the lasagne sheets, ragù and béchamel until you’ve used up all the ingredients, ending on a layer of sauce. Top with the remaining cheeses and chives, then pop into the oven for 45 mins, until a knife can be pushed through with no resistance. If it needs longer, cover with tin foil and pop back in the oven for 10-15 mins. When cooked, remove from the oven and set aside to cool for 15 mins before cutting and serving.

name: Cheese Scones
description: These double cheese scones with feta, Cheddar cheese and spinach are unbelievably moreish. Make extra and pop them in the freezer for a rainy day.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C. Line a baking tray with baking parchment. Crumble the feta and grate the Cheddar cheese into a bowl and mix to combine. Ensure your butter is very cold.
Combine the flour, sugar, baking powder and baking soda with a pinch of salt and black pepper in a large mixing bowl. Mix to evenly combine.
Cut the cold butter into cubes and add it to the flour mix. Rub the butter into flour until the mixture resembles rough breadcrumbs.
Add the egg, sour cream and spinach and mix to combine evenly, then add ½ the cheese mix. With a spoon, very gently mix everything together, just enough to combine.
Use your hands to gently bring the dough together and pat it into a cube shape. Return to the bowl and leave to rest for 5 mins.

Use a rolling pin to roll out the dough to 2cm thickness and sprinkle over ½ the remaining cheese mix and a pinch of sea salt. Now do a book fold; this means folding the dough inwards as if closing a book twice. Fold each end of the dough to the centre then fold again to create four layers. Turn the dough by 90° and repeat the process, adding the remaining cheese mix but no more salt.
Use a rolling pin to roll the dough out to 3.5cm thickness. Use a knife to cut the pastry into triangles, with sides roughly 3.5cm in length. Transfer the scones to the lined baking tray.
Slide the tray into the oven and bake for 25 mins until golden on top, browned across the bottom and baked through.

name: Cheese and Bacon BBQ Chicken
description: What Willy Cook joins us in the studio to make the naughtiest bacon-wrapped, cheese-stuffed chicken. Glazed with beautiful Bull’s-Eye NY Steakhouse BBQ Sauce.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/354°F.
Finely chop your chives, saving about half for your mash later. Grate your cheddar. Mix chives and sour cream with cheddar in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper.

Slice down the thick part of each chicken breast to create a pocket to stuff in your cheesy mixture. Spoon in the filling. Smother in your first layer of Bull’s-Eye NY Steakhouse BBQ sauce and set aside.

Create a wrapping station with your bacon. Lay out around 6 strips horizontally and then 2 strips vertically. Place your BBQ chicken piece onto the bacon and fold the first horizontal bacon over. Then, fold the vertically placed bacon over the chicken lengthways. Press tightly so all the chicken is covered with bacon. Repeat for each breast.

Add a little oil to the pan and pan-fry over medium heat until everything is crispy. Turn carefully so things don't fall out everywhere. This should take around 5 mins. Once golden and crispy, coat the bacon chicken breast in Bull’s-Eye NY Steakhouse BBQ sauce as a glaze. Then pop it into the oven for 10-15 mins.

Meanwhile, peel and slice the potatoes. Pop those peeled spuds into a pan of cold water, bring it to a boil and cook for 10-15 mins until tender. Once cooked, drain the potatoes and cover them to steam them for a min.
Add the potatoes to a bowl with the remaining chives, milk and 50g butter. Mash until smooth and season with salt and pepper.

Finely dice the shallot and add it to the chicken pan with the remaining butter. Soften the shallot for 5 mins before adding the brown sugar and 300ml Bull’s-Eye NY Steakhouse BBQ sauce. Stir in and then add chicken stock. Bring to a bubble and cook for 10 mins until thick and sticky.
Serve up your chicken with your mash and BBQ gravy and enjoy.

name: Cheeseboard Cheesecake
description: A savoury Basque cheesecake where we’ve used a creamy blue and Parmesan to amp up the flavours. This is a proper showstopper. Inauthentically delicious.
instructions: Heat the oven to 250°C. Line a 20cm cake tin with two sheets of crumpled baking paper, making sure there’s an overhang of 3cm all the way round.

Finely chop the chives and finely grate the Parmesan, then set aside. Put the cream cheese into a large bowl and beat until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time, beating in each one entirely. Add the cream, parmesan, chives, fine salt and pepper, then mix to combine. Crumble in the gorgonzola and sieve in the cornflour. Fold in and mix well to combine.

Pour the mixture into the lined cake tin and transfer to the oven. Bake for 17-20 mins until dark on the top but very, very wobbly in the middle. It will sink and firm up as it cools! Cover and leave overnight before slicing and serving with crackers, warm bread and chutney.

name: Cheeseburger Smacos with Dill Pickle Burger Sauce
description: Everyone loves a cheeseburger and everyone loves a smaco (our smashed tacos), so we combined them and topped them off with a VERY dill pickley burger sauce. We loved them and know you will too.
keywords: Cheeseburger Smacos with Dill Pickle Burger Sauce
Cheeseburger Smacos with Dill Pickle Burger Sauce recipe
instructions: Finely chop the cornichons and dill. Add both to a bowl with the ketchup, mayo, pickle brine, mustard, garlic powder and vinegar. Season with salt and pepper, mixing well.
Finely slice the iceberg, then peel and slice the onion as finely as possible - use a mandoline if you have one - you're looking for it to be almost see through.
Get the beef into a bowl with the onion and season with salt and pepper, then mix and squish together using your hands. Finely slice the tomatoes.

Spread the beef mix onto the tortillas. Place a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and give it a light spray of oil, then pop the tortillas in, beef side down, working in batches. Cook for 4-6 mins, until nicely golden, then flip, top with the cheese, add a tbsp of water and clap a lid on. Cook for another 1-2 mins, until the cheese has melted and the water has evaporated.
Serve the tacos topped with slices of tomato, the iceberg and the burger sauce.

name: Cheesy & Saucy Aubergine Jacket Potato
description: A crispy jacket stuffed with gooey cheese and our jammy Aubergine Alla Norma. Healthy comfort food at its best.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Aubergine Alla Norma batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 180°C.

Rub the potatoes all over with olive oil, then season with salt and black pepper. Wrap each one in foil and place onto a baking tray. Roast for 1 hr, then remove the foil and bake for another 15–20 mins until crisp on the outside and fluffy in the middle.
Meanwhile, reheat the Aubergine Alla Norma in a saucepan over a medium heat until piping hot.
Cut a cross in the top of each potato and push the sides out to open them up. Drizzle the insides with a little olive oil, then sprinkle in the grated mozzarella and cheddar.
Spoon over the hot Aubergine Alla Norma, grate over the Parmesan and finish with a scattering of basil leaves.

name: Cheesy 'Nduja & Celeriac Steaks
description: These spicy celeriac steaks make an excellent midweek dinner. The sharp salsa on top really makes it pop.
keywords: simple and delicious celeriac steak recipes
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Peel your celeriac and cut it into inch wide slices.
Place your slices on a baking tray and season liberally with salt and pepper. Drizzle with olive oil, then roast for 30 mins.
Finely dice your peppers. Finely chop your capers and parsley. Add to a bowl, then add your sherry vinegar and 3 tbsp olive oil and mix to combine. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Top the steaks with ‘nduja and grated cheese, then bake for 5 mins to melt the cheese. Once they're golden brown, take the cheesy steaks out and drape them with your salsa.

name: Cheesy Air Fryer Potato Skins
description: The best thing about potato skins is the ability to customise them and get a different mouthful with every skin. Air fryers make them extra crunchy too.
keywords: Cheesy Air Fryer Potato Skins recipe
instructions: Heat the air fryer to 170°C. Pierce your potatoes all over with a fork. Rub oil all over the spuds and then sprinkle them with salt.
Pop the potatoes into the air-fryer basket and cook for 20 mins, then up the temperature to 200°C for a further 15 mins, until the flesh is tender.
Remove the potatoes from the basket and cut each one in half. Scoop out the flesh into a bowl, reserving the skins, and set aside.

Separate out one quarter of the flesh into a different bowl (serve this as mashed potatoes on the side!) and mix it with the butter and almost all of the cheese (leave enough for sprinkling just before cooking). Season with salt and pepper. Then spoon equal amounts of the cheesy potato back into the skins.
Sprinkle the potato skins with pancetta and the remaining cheese and return them to the air fryer.
Cook for 10 mins, until the pancetta is cooked and the skins are crispy. Remove and garnish with the spring onion.

name: Cheesy Bacony Potatoes
description: Herby, cheesy, bacony stuffed potatoes. The most important element of this dish is the tarragon - really brings the edge.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Add the potatoes to a tray. Drizzle with olive oil. Add salt and pepper. Place in the oven for 1 hour.
Add your pancetta to a frying pan. Cook until crispy.
Remove the potatoes from the oven, making sure they are soft in the centre. Halve the potatoes. Carefully spoon out the insides of each potato, keeping the skins intact.
Add the potato flesh to the bacon pan. Mix it in.
Finely chop a large handful of tarragon, parsley and chives. Add your herbs to the pan. Mix everything in.
Add 150g of grated cheese to the pan. Season with salt and pepper, mix everything together and remove pan from the heat.
Refill potato skins with the herby stuffing. Grate some extra cheddar on top, drizzle over some olive oil and place your skins under the grill for 12 minutes or until golden and bubbling.
Serve with a grating of cheddar, some leftover chopped herbs and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Bolognese Loaded Jacket Potato
description: Crispy jacket spuds stuffed with our rich Bolognese Ragú batch recipe and molten cheese. A proper comfort dinner that basically makes itself.
keywords: Cheesy Bolognese Loaded Jacket Potato recipe
instructions: Make the Bolognese Ragú.
Heat the oven to 200°C.

Scrub the potatoes, prick them all over with a fork, then rub with a little olive oil and salt. Place straight onto the oven rack and bake for 1 hr until crisp on the outside and fluffy in the middle.
Tear the mozzarella into chunks. Reheat the Bolognese ragù leftovers in a saucepan until piping hot.
Once the potatoes are ready, cut a deep cross into each one and squeeze them open. Fluff the insides with a fork, then spoon over the ragù. Top with mozzarella and a generous grating of pecorino.
If you want the cheese extra gooey, pop them under the grill for a couple of mins until bubbling.

name: Cheesy Bolognese Ragú on Garlic Toast
description: Thick sourdough toast slathered in garlic and butter, piled high with ragù and smothered in cheese. It’s giving lasagne vibes, but quicker. And a perfect way to use up leftovers from our Bolognese Ragú batch.
keywords: Cheesy Bolognese Ragú on Garlic Toast recipe
Cheesy Bolognese Ragú on Garlic Toast
instructions: Make the Bolognese Ragú.
Toast the sourdough slices until golden, then rub one side of each slice with the garlic clove. Spread over the butter while the toast is still warm.
Reheat the Bolognese ragù in a saucepan until piping hot. Add a splash of water if it needs loosening.
Spoon the ragù over the garlic toasts. Tear the mozzarella and scatter it on top. Finely grate the Parmesan over everything and finish with a few basil leaves.

name: Cheesy Brussels Sprout Tart
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad. 

Here's an indulgent tart that we've paired with a shaved brussels sprout salad and lots of crispy bacon-y bits. It's rich, it's wonderful, and it's festive.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Unroll the pastry and place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Score a 3cm border and prick the middle with a fork. Beat your egg with a pinch of salt and brush around the border.
Now bake the pastry for 20 mins until lightly golden. If the centre has puffed, push it back down with the back of a fork.
In a medium mixing bowl, mix the crème fraîche with a finely grated clove of garlic. Grate the comté and the parmesan and add to the mixture with an egg. Mix thoroughly.
Spread the mix over the pastry and pop back in the oven for 20 mins until golden and bubbling.
Meanwhile, add the pancetta to a frying pan and set over a medium heat. Cook until the fat has rendered and the pancetta is crispy.
Finely slice the sprouts and add to a large bowl. Roughly chop the parsley.
Scoop the crispy pancetta out the pan and pour the fat into a small bowl. Add the honey, mustard and apple cider vinegar to the fat and whisk together.
Pour the dressing over the salad, add the crispy pancetta and add the parsley.
Pull the tart out of the oven and pile on the sprout salad. Chop it up and get stuck in.

name: Cheesy Butternut Squash Gratin
description: This easy gratin uses peak season Ocado Own Range butternut squash to make a delicious weeknight dinner.
keywords: easy and cheesy squash gratin recipes
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.

Wash and finely slice your leek, roughly chop the sage. Place a
saucepan over medium heat and add 2 tbsp of olive oil. Add the
leeks and sage and sweat down for 5 mins until soft and golden.

While the leeks cook, wash and slice your Ocado Own Range
butternut squash into roughly half centimetre thick slices and
set aside. Grate the cheddar and also set aside.

Drain both tins of butter beans and add to the leeks along with
the mustard and cream, mix well and season with salt and
pepper.

In a large oven dish, spread a layer of squash, followed by half of
the butter bean mix and roughly a third of the grated cheddar.

Repeat with a second layer of squash, butter beans and cheddar,
then a final layer of squash and the remaining cheddar.

Place into the oven for 40 mins until the squash is tender and
the cheese is golden brown.
Allow to rest for 5 mins before serving.

name: Cheesy Chicken Tikka Arayes
description: Crispy, cheesy pittas stuffed with spiced chicken tikka mince, this one's going to be a proper family favourite. Plus it's just as good the next day. Don't skip the coriander yoghurt, it takes them to the next level.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and pop a baking tray in there to warm up. Finely slice the spring onions. Finely chop the chilli, removing the seeds if you don't like it spicy. Grate one clove of garlic and zest half the lemon directly into a large bowl with the chicken mince. Add the tikka paste, chilli and spring onions, season with salt and black pepper and mix well to combine.

Grate the Cheddar. Gently warm the pitta breads until they puff up,  a microwave or toaster works, just don't let them go crispy, you just need them to be warm and pliable. Cut each pitta in half and open up to make a pocket. Stuff with the mince mixture and plenty of Cheddar in layers, making sure the last layer is mince, all the way to the top. Repeat until you've used up all your pitta, cheese and mince.

Remove the hot baking tray from the oven and line with baking paper. Arrange the stuffed pittas meat-side down and slide back into the oven. Cook for 10-15 mins, until cooked through, this will depend on the size of your pittas, so keep checking.

Meanwhile, squeeze the juice of the lemon into a blender with the Greek yoghurt, coriander and the remaining clove of garlic. Season with salt and black pepper and blitz until smooth. Pour into a dish and scatter over the pomegranate seeds, if using.
Serve the arayes with the coriander yoghurt and get stuck in, they're also great as leftovers for lunch.

name: Cheesy Chilli Quesadillas
description: There's nothing better than a gooey cheesy quesadilla filled with spicy beef chilli. Perfect Friday night food.
instructions: Make the Beef Chilli Con Carne.
Set a saucepan on a medium heat and add the leftover Beef Chilli Con Carne, stirring until warmed through.
Place a frying pan on medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Using some kitchen paper, rub it around the pan so it is all evenly covered.

Place a tortilla into the pan. Grate over a large handful of cheddar and dollop a large spoonful of the chilli mix over the cheese. Top with more grated cheddar and place another tortilla on top. Cook on both sides until golden and the cheese has melted, 5-7 mins.
Repeat this three more times with your remaining chilli and tortillas, carve up your quesadillas and serve with a wedge of lime. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Chipotle Chicken Tacos
description: These easy cheesy chipotle chicken tacos are filling, spicy, and perfect for dinner tonight.
instructions: Season the chicken thighs well with salt and pepper and drizzle over the olive oil. Get a large frying pan (that has a lid) over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken thighs and fry for 2-3 mins on each side until evenly golden. Stir the chipotle paste into the pan, pour in the cherry tomatoes, stir and stick on a lid. Turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, cut or peel the cabbage into long thin shreds using a sharp knife or peeler. Toss in a bowl with some salt, pepper and the juice of ½ a lime.

Halve and finely chop the avocados, then transfer to a bowl. Finely slice the spring onions (both green and white parts), then finely chop most of the coriander (stalks and all) and pickled jalapeños. Add these to the bowl with the avocado and squeeze over the juice of 1½ limes. Season to taste. Cut the remaining lime into wedges to serve.
Come back to the chicken, which will now be cooked. Using two forks, shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces in the sauce, season to taste, then turn the heat to low to keep warm.

Grate the cheese. Get a second large, non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Sprinkle two small piles of the cheese, using roughly one-quarter of it, into the pan. As they begin to melt, place two of the tortillas on top and fry until the cheese has melted onto the tortillas and the underside is golden and crisp. Use tongs to flip the tortillas onto their un-cheesy side and cook for 20 seconds, then transfer to a plate. Repeat with the remaining tortillas and cheese.

Eating time! We like to bring everything to the table for everyone to help themselves, layering up the chipotle chicken, cabbage and avocado salsa inside the cheese-crusted tacos and serving with the lime wedges, more coriander and pickled jalapeños, if you like.

name: Cheesy Chipotle Garlic Bread
description: This cheesy chipotle garlic bread is about as comforting as it gets. It’s absolutely delicious and so easy to make. Treat yourself and whip some up tonight.
instructions: Heat your oven to 220°C / fan 200°C.
Mince the garlic cloves. Place in a bowl with the butter, chipotle paste and smoked paprika. Season with salt and pepper and mix to combine.
Grate the mozzarella and slice the baguette in half lengthways.
Spread the butter on each half of the baguette and top with the mozzarella.
Roast for 10-15 mins, or until nice and golden.
Finely chop the fresh coriander.
Slice into quarters, top with fresh coriander and serve hot - enjoy!

name: Cheesy Chorizo Brekkie Burritos
description: All your brunch dreams, wrapped up. These chorizo-loaded breakfast burritos are cheesy, eggy and golden, with crispy spuds and melty goodness in every bite. Make ahead and enjoy all week.
instructions: Start by cutting the potatoes into matchsticks and pop them into a bowl of ice-cold water. Set aside while you prep everything else. Drain and change the water twice to get rid of the starch.
Meanwhile, set a frying pan over a medium heat and add the chorizo. Fry for 8–10 mins until they are nicely caramelised and the oil’s released. Scoop out and set aside.
Pop the spinach into a colander and pour over a kettle of boiling water. Once wilted and cool enough to handle, squeeze out the excess water.
Grate the cheddar.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Pat the potatoes dry with kitchen paper and add them to the pan. Season with salt, pepper and the oregano. Cook until golden and tender – you’ll need to do this in batches to avoid overcrowding. Add the remaining oil in thirds as you go.

Crack the eggs into a bowl, season with salt and pepper, then whisk. Melt the butter in a large non-stick pan over a low heat. Pour in the eggs and gently stir until halfway cooked. Dollop in the soft cheese and fold gently with a spatula until creamy and just set – don’t overdo it. They'll keep cooking as you assemble.

Now you can assemble. Lay out the tortilla wraps on a chopping board. Start with a layer of crispy potatoes, then grated cheddar, spinach, scrambled eggs and finally chorizo. Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly into burritos.

To seal, heat a dry frying pan over a medium heat. Pop the burritos in seam-side down and cook for 1–2 mins until sealed. Alternatively, chuck them in the air fryer at 200°C for 5 mins. Once ready, wrap each burrito in a layer of baking paper followed by foil. Stash in the freezer for later.To reheat: Remove the foil, wrap the burrito in damp kitchen paper and microwave for 2 mins. Finish in the air fryer for 7–8 mins at 180°C (or in the oven for 10 mins at 160°C) until piping hot throughout.

name: Cheesy Chorizo High Protein Flatbreads
description: These fluffy flatbreads give the ultimate cheese pull. Plus with high protein dough and chorizo they're a perfect way to boost your protein while still feeling indulgent.
instructions: Finely chop the chorizo, onion, garlic and red chilli.

Add the chorizo to a frying pan with a splash of olive oil and set over a medium heat. Cook until some of the fat has rendered out and the chorizo is beginning to crisp, around 3 mins, then add the onion and cook until softened, for 10 mins.
Add the garlic, red chilli, smoked paprika and ground cumin and cook for 1 minute. Tip into a bowl.
Drain the black beans then add them to the bowl, add the cheese. Finely chop the fresh coriander, then add. Stir to combine and adjust the salt level to your liking. Set aside.

Now make the dough. Add the white bread flour, wholemeal bread flour, Greek yoghurt, baking powder and salt to a large bowl. Mix with a spoon until it forms a dough, then transfer to a lightly floured surface and knead for a minute until it comes together. (Or, if using a stand mixer, add all of the ingredients to the bowl and mix with a dough hook for a minute.)
Cut the dough into equal pieces (if you're making the recipe to serve 6, cut it into 6 pieces and so on). Flour the surface again, then roll each piece into a ball.

Flatten each ball so it makes a 15 - 20cm disk, then add a big handful of filling to the middle, leaving a large rim, then fold the outsides over the filling to seal them inside the flatbread. Flatten into a chunky disk.

Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium head. Add a small splash of olive oil. Add the flatbreads, one at a time, and cook for 5 mins on each side, until the bread is gold and puffed up. Set aside and repeat with the rest. Slice and serve immediately, or wrap and freezer to eat later.

name: Cheesy Corn One-Pot Pasta
description: A creamy, oozy one-pot pasta for when you want a big bowl of comfort food with a little bit of goodness. It’s the perfect combo of sweet, savoury, salty and spicy.
instructions: Add ¾ of the sweetcorn (with its liquid) to a blender along with milk, stock, cornflour and turmeric. Blitz until smooth. If it's too bitty, pass it through a fine sieve and discard the bits, then set aside. Trim and thinly slice the spring onion, separating the whites from greens.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Stir fry the lardons until crispy, then use a slotted spoon to transfer to a plate and set aside until it's time to serve. Add the spring onion whites and ½ the spring onion greens into the pan and cook for 2-3 mins until softened. Set aside the remaining spring onion greens for garnish.

Add the pasta to the saucepan and pour over the blended corn milk. Mix to combine and season with salt and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to medium and leave to simmer, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is cooked to al dente (normally around 10 mins but follow the packet instructions).
Meanwhile, grate the Cheddar cheese.
Once the pasta has cooked, stir through the cheeses, the remaining corn and the pickled jalapeño slices. Taste and season to taste with some pickle brine, salt and pepper, if needed.
Spoon into bowls and garnish with the lardons and remaining spring onion greens.

name: Cheesy Curried Chips
description: We've all stumbled into a kebab shop and come out with a portion of cheesy chips or curry chips before. This is our spiced-up take on that student classic.
instructions: Cook the chips following pack instructions. Meanwhile, trim, peel and finely slice one of the onions, put into a small bowl with half the vinegar, then season with salt and a pinch of sugar. Mix together and set aside.
Trim, peel and finely grate the second onion into another bowl – it should resemble pulp. Peel the garlic cloves, then finely grate both into the onion pulp.
Put the butter into a medium saucepan and place over a medium heat. Once fully melted, add the onion, garlic and ginger mixture. Cook, stirring, for 4-5 mins until thickened.
In a small bowl, combine the cornflour and 2 tbsp cold water to make a slurry, stirring until there are no clumps.

Add the curry powder and ground turmeric to the thickened onion mixture and cook for 30 secs. Stir through the remaining vinegar and let it completely evaporate before pouring the stock and cornflour slurry in. Whisk constantly until the curry sauce comes to a boil. Remove from the heat and season.
Grate the cheese and sprinkle it over the chips, drizzle over the curry sauce and top with the pickled onions and coriander leaves.

name: Cheesy Dough Balls With Roasted Garlic & Herb Dip
description: Our take on Pizza Express's classic (and addictive) dough balls. We've nailed this fakeaway recipe, if we do say so ourselves.
keywords: Cheesy Dough Balls With Roasted Garlic & Herb Dip
instructions: Start with the dough balls. Add the sugar, olive oil and yeast to the warm water, then set aside for 10-15 mins ​​– it should go frothy.

Put the flour and salt into a large mixing bowl, make a well in the middle and pour in the yeast mixture, slowly mixing with your hands until combined. Tip the dough onto your work surface, then knead with your hands for about 10 mins until it feels supple and soft – press the dough with your finger and it should bounce back. Put the dough into a lightly oiled bowl and cover with clingfilm. Leave to prove in a warm place for 1 hr or until doubled in size.

Dice the mozzarella into pieces around 1cm x 1cm. For the dip, finely chop the chives and parsley. Mix the mayo, greek yogurt and white wine vinegar with the juice and zest of a lemon, a grated garlic clove and the herbs. Mix well and season with salt and pepper, then cover and set aside in the fridge.

When the dough has proved, knock back into the bowl and weigh out into 25g pieces. Flatten each one out with your thumbs and fill with cheese. Seal the cheese in by pinching the edges together and rolling the seam on the tabletop. Transfer to a lightly oiled baking tray, spaced apart, and cover with lightly oiled cling film. Set aside in a warm place to prove for another 30 mins.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. For the garlic butter, melt the butter in a small pan, then add the oregano, a grated garlic clove and salt.

Brush some of the butter over the dough balls and bake in the oven for 12-15 mins. Once golden, remove the dough balls from the oven, brush with the remaining herb butter and grate over the parmesan, if using. Serve with the dip.

name: Cheesy Fish Finger Pie
description: Grilled fish fingers in a cheddar and parsley béchamel with peas, topped with a chive-y garlic mash and baked until bubbling and golden. Serve this fish finger pie with greens for an easy, crowd-pleasing dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 230°C. Put the fish fingers on a baking tray and cook in the oven for 12-15 mins, turning halfway. Meanwhile, get a large pan of salted water onto the boil and peel the potatoes. Once peeled, cut into quarters and carefully tip into the boiling water. Cook for 15 mins until just falling apart, then drain and leave to steam-dry. When the fish fingers are cooked, turn the grill to high.

Finely chop the parsley, grate the cheese and grate the garlic. Set aside. For the sauce, melt the butter in a pan set over a medium heat. Once melted, add the flour and cook for 1-2 mins until it starts to smell nutty, then gradually add the milk (reserving a splash later for the mash), stirring after each addition. Once all of the milk has been added, stir through the mustard and bring to a simmer. Cook for 2 mins, then add most of the grated cheese and half of the parsley. Pour boiling water over the peas, leave for 2 mins before draining, then add to the sauce. Season with salt and pepper.

Blitz the spring onions, remaining parsley and grated garlic together until smooth. Mash the potatoes, then add a splash of milk, a knob of butter and the blitzed greens. Mix well and season with salt and pepper.

Lay the fish fingers in the bottom of a baking dish, then top with the cheesy sauce. Spoon over the mashed potato and sprinkle with the reserved cheese. Pop under the grill for 5-10 mins until golden and bubbling.

name: Cheesy Garlic Bread
description: The most indulgent and cheesiest garlic bread around. Cross-hatching the top means all the crevices are filled with cheesy, garlicky goodness
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Slice the ciabatta in half and then score the inside with a cross-hatch pattern.
Grate the cheddar cheese.
Blitz the garlic, butter, parsley, 3 tbsp of olive oil, salt and pepper in a food processor.
Scoop out a tablespoon of garlic butter in a small bowl and microwave for 30 secs until melted.
Add ¾ of the cheddar and cream cheese to the food processor and blitz with the remaining garlic butter.
Spread the cheesy garlic butter on the ciabatta.
Push the remaining cheddar and cream cheese into the crevices of your ciabatta along with some torn-up chunks of mozzarella cheese.
Drizzle on the melted garlic butter and pop in the oven for 20 mins or until the cheese has melted and golden.
Slice into sticks and serve hot.

name: Cheesy Greens Stuffed Pittas
description: Crispy, golden pittas crammed with gooey halloumi, salty feta, herby spinach and dried mint, served alongside a punchy artichoke and tomato salad. Easy to whip up on a weeknight and perfect for lunches the next day.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Defrost the spinach in the microwave, then drain and squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible. Add to a large bowl.
Finely chop the dill and parsley, stalks and all. Grate the halloumi and crumble in the feta, then add the herbs and dried mint and toss everything together.
Halve the pitta breads and stuff each half with the herby cheese mixture, pressing it in evenly. Brush both sides with olive oil. Place on a baking tray and bake for 10-15 mins.

Meanwhile, chop the vine tomatoes into bite-sized chunks, thinly slice the red onion and drain the artichoke hearts. Sprinkle a little salt over the tomatoes. Squeeze the lemon juice into a bowl, add the olive oil and dried oregano and season to taste with salt and black pepper. Toss the tomatoes, red onion and artichoke hearts through the dressing.
Divide the salad between plates and serve alongside the stuffed pittas.If you're prepping ahead, wrap the pittas in foil and keep in the fridge or freezer. Reheat in the airfryer or until piping hot.

name: Cheesy Kimchi Noodles
description: These noods are gonna become your new dinner time saviour, trust me. They’re a mix of all your favourite things and perfect for a quick pick-me-up. Xien x
instructions: Mince your garlic and slice your spring onions. Set aside separately.
Grate your cheddar and also set aside.
Cook your instant noodles according to packet instructions. Drain using a sieve, saving the noodle-cooking water. Rinse the noodles with cold water.
Pour a glug of vegetable oil into a pan and add in the kimchi, minced garlic and spring onions. Give it a good stir.
Add in your cooked noodles with your Gochujang, kewpie mayo and 4 tbsp of the reserved noodle-cooking water. Give it a good mix then add in grated cheddar and sugar and give it another mix.
Fry your egg in a separate pan until it's golden and crispy around the edges.
Plate up your noodles with a sprinkle of sesame seeds, spring onions and a drizzle of chilli oil. Enjoy.

name: Cheesy Kimchi Potato Skins
description: These stuffed potato skins are packed with cheddar cheese and kimchi. The kimchi adds a sharp spiciness that cuts through the richness.
instructions: Wash the potatoes, pat dry and pierce all over with a fork. Place on a microwavable plate and microwave for 15-20 mins, turning over once halfway through. If the potatoes aren’t fork tender by then, continue microwaving in 1 minute increments. Leave to rest for 10 mins.
Heat your oven to 220°C.
Drain and finely chop the kimchi, grate the cheese and thinly slice the spring onions.
Split the potatoes in half and scoop out the flesh into a large mixing bowl.
Lightly oil a baking tray and arrange the potato skins on a single layer. Drizzle with oil and roast for 10 mins, or until crisp.
Meanwhile, add the kimchi, cheese, spring onions and mayonnaise into the mixing bowl with your potato flesh. Season with salt and pepper, to taste, and mix well to combine.
Stuff the potato skins with the cheesy, kimchi mixture.
Return to the oven and bake for 15 to 20 mins, or until browned.
Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley. Top the golden potato skins with the chopped parsley then serve and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Leek & Pancetta Pasta Bake
description: Is it a pasta bake, is it a mac and cheese? Creamy, cheesy sauce with sweet leeks and salty pancetta – whatever it is, it’s delicious. Make it with lacto-free cheese and milk if that's your vibe. B x
keywords: cheesy leek and pancetta pasta bake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Cut the leeks into rounds, finely chop the parsley and finely grate the garlic clove.
Combine the breadcrumbs, parsley and garlic in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and a glug of oil. Stir vigorously to distribute the oil and garlic.
Add the pancetta to a saucepan with a glug of oil, cook over a medium heat for 5 mins until the fat has started to render and the pancetta is starting to crisp.
Remove from the pan and add the leeks, sweat with a pinch of salt for 5 mins until soft but still bright green. Remove from the pan.
Now, add 50ml of olive oil and the flour to the pan. Cook out for 2 mins then slowly add the milk, whisking constantly. Bring to a boil then lower the heat.
Coarsely grate the Cheddar cheese and whisk into the sauce.
Season with salt, pepper and freshly grated nutmeg.

Cook your pasta for 8 mins until just al dente. Drain, reserving a mugful of pasta water. Combine the cooked pasta with the sauce, sweated leeks and pancetta and stir together, adding pasta water until you have a loose sauce.
Pour the lot into a baking dish and top with the garlicky breadcrumbs.
Bang it in the oven for 30 mins until golden and bubbling.
Serve up and get stuck in.

name: Cheesy Leek Lasagne Soup
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A twist on the viral lasagne soup, this one is packed full of sweet leeks and topped with crispy crunchy breadcrumbs. It’s creamy, cheesy and very comforting.
instructions: Halve, wash and thinly slice the leeks. Peel and thinly slice the garlic cloves.

Heat the butter in a deep lidded frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the leeks, garlic and a big pinch of salt. Pop the lid on and cook for 15 mins, stirring every now and again, until the leeks are really soft.

Scatter in the plain flour and cook for a few mins, then pour in the chicken stock. Bring to a simmer and then break in the lasagne sheets. Simmer gently for 15 mins, with the lid on, or until the pasta is cooked.
Finely grate the cheddar cheese and add ¾ of it to the soup, along with the mustard and ⅔ the crème fraîche. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Scatter in the breadcrumbs and cook for 3-4 mins, tossing and stirring all the time, until evenly browned and caramelised. Add in the chilli flakes and zest in the lemon.
Spoon the soup into bowls and top with the crispy breadcrumbs. Scatter over a little more cheese, add an extra dollop of crème fraîche and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: Cheesy Leek Soup With Crispy Gnocchi
description: A cheesy leek soup with crispy gnocchi and a dollop of mustard – rich, comforting and extremely easy.
keywords: Cheesy Leek Soup With Crispy Gnocchi
Cheesy Leek Soup With Crispy Gnocchi recipe
instructions: Remove the outer layer from the leeks, then half and slice into ½cm-thick pieces. Put into a colander and rinse well under cold water. Set aside. Peel and dice the potato into 2cm pieces. Finely slice the garlic.

Melt a glug of oil and the butter in a large, lidded saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the leeks and the garlic. Cook until just turning golden, then cover with the stock. Add the potato cubes, cover and simmer for 15 mins.

When the veg is tender, remove about ¼ of it from the pan, then purée this with a stick blender (or in a Nutribullet) before adding back to the pan. Stir through the soured cream, Dijon mustard and cheddar. Mix well to combine and season to taste with salt and pepper.

Finely chop the chives and halve the gnocchi pieces. Heat the butter in a saucepan and tip in the gnocchi. Add a splash of oil, then fry until golden on all sides. Serve the soup in bowls topped with the gnocchi, chives, more cheddar and wholegrain mustard, if you like.

name: Cheesy Lentils & Fridge-raid Greens
description: A cosy, comforting vegan dinner using the leftover greens in your fridge. It's packed with plant-based protein too.
instructions: Cover the cashews in boiling water and leave to soak for 10 mins then drain and set aside. Slice the leeks in half lengthwise and finely chop into half moons. Mince the garlic.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large sauté pan over a medium heat. Crumble in the tempeh using your hands, add a pinch of salt and fry for 5 mins. Add the tamari and continue to cook on a medium heat until the liquid has been absorbed and the tempeh is looking golden and a little crispy. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Wipe the pan out, then heat a glug of olive oil over a medium heat. Add the chopped leeks and a pinch of salt and fry for 7-8 mins. Add the garlic and fry for another 2-3 mins more, then add the smoked paprika, cumin and coriander. Continue frying for another minute.
Add the lentils and stock and stir. Bring the mixture to a boil then reduce to a simmer, cover with a lid and cook for 20-25 mins until the lentils are soft.
Meanwhile, in a blender, whizz up all the ingredients for the creamy cheesy sauce, including the juice of your lemon. Add a splash of water if needed so it’s a pourable consistency. Season to taste.

Roughly chop and wash your greens. Heat a dry frying pan over a high heat, add the greens and cook until starting to wilt and turning bright green. Add the oil, crushed garlic, salt and pepper. Fry 3-4 mins more, then turn off the heat and squeeze over the lemon. Set aside until ready to serve.
Once the lentils are cooked, add the creamy cheesy sauce to the pan, stir well, and season to taste. Divide into bowls and serve with the fried tempeh and greens on top.

name: Cheesy Marmite Mushroom Pie
description: A beautiful, wintery, rib-sticking, mushroom and ale pie. Pie is proper Sunday food and nothing else hits the spot like it.
instructions: For the pastry, take the puff out of the fridge 30 mins before starting and finely chop the chives. Roll out of the packet onto a lightly floured surface and drizzle with Marmite. Scatter over the cheese and the chives, then fold the two short ends of the pastry into the middle, then fold everything in half, like a book. Then fold the whole thing in half again before wrapping in cling film and popping back in the fridge for 30 minutes. This pastry isn't suitable for making the day before because of the added elements, so don’t be tempted to try it!

Start by tearing or chopping the mushrooms into equal-sized pieces. Heat a good glug of oil over high heat in a large, ovenproof frying pan and add the mushrooms, cooking until deeply golden – you will need to do this in batches so as not to overcrowd the pan. Once cooked, remove from the pan and set aside. Halve and finely slice the onion, then finely chop the garlic.

Reduce the heat to medium, and add more oil to the pan, before frying the onion, garlic and thyme for around 5 mins. Add the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins, then pour in the stout. Simmer for 5 mins, then add the mushrooms back into the pan with the stock. Simmer for 15-20 mins until thickened, then stir in the Marmite. Give it a taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.

Heat the oven to 180°C. When your elements are ready to assemble, roll the pastry on a lightly floured surface, as big as the frying pan the filling is in. Brush the edges of the pan with a bit of the liquid from the filling then drape the pastry over the top, pressing the edges to the pan to seal. Cut a little cross in the middle to let the steam out and brush with a beaten egg. Transfer to the oven and cook for 25 mins, until golden and bubbling. Serve with mash and greens.

name: Cheesy Okonomiyaki Pancake
description: This Japanese savoury pancake is the dream brunch dish – crispy, caramelised and soft inside, so quick and easy, you gotta try this one! We stuffed ours with mozzarella, but add anything you like. Especially a golden fried egg on top.
instructions: Combine the wet batter ingredients in a small bowl, stir until thick and paste-like, almost like thick greek yoghurt, set aside in the fridge. Slice the cheddar and mozzarella and grate the Parmesan. Cheese is optional if you want to keep this dairy-free!

Very finely slice the cabbage, shiitake mushrooms, and spring onions, (reserving the green part for garnish later). Into a large bowl, add minced ginger, eggs, sesame oil, soy sauce and salt, whisk vigorously for 1 minute, or until the eggs get slightly frothy and small bubbles appear. Fold the cabbage, mushrooms and spring onion whites until combined, then mix in the prepared wet batter. If the vegetables aren’t coated in the batter, add a tablespoon of water into the batter until coated - make sure to not add too much water, the batter shouldn’t be loose.

Heat a 6-inch frying pan over medium heat and add 1 tbsp neutral oil and swirl around the pan, making sure to get all the edges of the pan. Add 1/4 of the batter, and use a spatula to spread across the pan, but do not flatten the pancake, keep it airy! Turn the heat to low, add a few slices of cheddar and mozzarella, lightly pressing them into the batter, then cover the cheese with a little bit more batter. Place a lid on and cook for 2 mins, or until the bottom of the pancake looks golden brown (keep the bowl of remaining batter in the fridge).

Slide the pancake onto a large plate, with the raw side facing up, then flip the pan over the plate, and flip back into the pan. Drizzle a tsp of oil around the edge of the pan and cook for 4 mins without a lid, or until golden brown. In the meantime, fry your eggs in another pan and set aside. Flip the pancake again, and cook on medium heat for just 1 minute to crisp up the other side. (eat this pancake now or cook the second pancake.)
In the same pan, add another drizzle of oil and fry the remaining eggs to serve on top of your pancake.
