Pop up the onto pancake a plate, crispy side up. To garnish the okonomiyaki, sprinkle over a thin layer of grated Parmesan and drizzle HP sauce in long lines across the pancake, then repeat with the mayo. Top with the fried egg, spring onion, toasted sesame seeds.

name: Cheesy Pea Fritters
description: Crispy, cheesy fritters made with frozen peas and pantry staples. Great for kids and jazzed up with a spicy yoghurt dip for a grown-ups.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Boil the peas in a saucepan for 1–2 mins until tender. Drain and rinse under cold water to cool.
Roughly mash the peas with a fork or masher. You want them partly squished, but still chunky for texture.
Thinly slice the spring onions. Grate the cheddar.

Crack the eggs into a large mixing bowl. Add the flour, baking powder, mashed peas, spring onions and grated cheddar. Season with a little salt and black pepper. Stir everything together until fully combined.

Place a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Spoon in heaped tablespoons of the mixture, pressing them slightly to form small rounds. Fry for 2–3 mins per side until golden brown and set. Do this in batches if needed.
For the adults, mix the Greek yoghurt with a pinch of salt and the hot sauce to taste. Dress the rocket with a squeeze of lemon juice.

Serve up! 
Kids Plate: Dish up the fritters warm with the plain yoghurt and your kids favourite veg, we've gone for cherry tomatoes. 
Parents Plate: Serve with the rocket salad and spicy yoghurt dip and an extra wedge of lemon.

name: Cheesy Pesto Dough Balls
description: Growing herbs at home is a great way to reduce your use of plastic. These cheesy dough balls from Liam Charles show what you can do with a fresh bunch of basil.
keywords: IKEA cheesy pesto dough balls recipes
instructions:
Warm the milk in a saucepan, then remove from the heat. Add in your sugar and butter, and keep
stirring until butter has melted. Allow the mixture to cool until it’s lukewarm.

Sift the flour and 1 tsp of salt into a large bowl. Stir in the yeast and fresh basil, fresh oregano,
and then make a well in the centre. Beat your eggs together in a bowl and then pour your beaten
eggs into that well along with your milk mixture. Give it a quick mix to form a soft pillowy dough.

Knead the dough by hand for 15 mins until it has become elastic; the dough should be super soft
and sticky.

Pop the bowl in a lightly oiled bowl, cover it with cling film, and allow it to double in size. This will
take an hour or so.

Meanwhile, make your pesto. Blitz up the pine nuts, basil, parmesan and garlic in a food processor.
Slowly drizzle in the olive oil whilst blending and then season with salt and pepper.
Chop up the mozzarella into 18 large chunks and grate the cheddar.

Knock back the dough and divide it into 18 equal-sized pieces – you will need to weigh these on
scales.
Flatten each piece of dough and place a dollop of pesto and a big cube of mozzarella in the middle.
Pinch the edges together to close up the mozzarella and roll into a ball.

Grease a baking dish with butter. Arrange your rolls inside the dish seam-side down, then sprinkle
with your grated cheddar. Cover and leave to rise for an hour.
Heat your oven to 200°C.
Bake for 25 mins until puffed and golden.

For the garlic butter, finely chop the chives and parsley. Melt the butter in a microwave and grate in
three cloves of garlic. Season with salt.
Once the dough balls are out of the oven, brush liberally with the garlic butter and serve hot.

name: Cheesy Potato & Fennel Salad
description: An easy one-pot potato salad recipe where Wensleydale and fennel get along like a house on fire. This is a boiled dinner done right.
instructions: Fill a pot with heavily salted water and get it on a good roiling boil.
Halve your potatoes. Roughly chop your fennel, you want it to be chunky. Zest half of your lemons and chop the zest into little bite-sized pieces.
Add the fennel, potatoes, and lemon zest to the pan of boiling water and boil for 12 minutes. While your potatoes are cooking, finely chop the mint and parsley.
Once the potatoes are cooked, drain the mixture and add the potatoes, fennel, and lemon zest back to the pan.

Add in your butter and your chopped mint and parsley – reserving a bit for serving later. Roughly crumble in three-quarters of your Wensleydale with your hands into the pot. Add a big glug of olive oil into the pan with plenty of salt and pepper.
Mix everything in the pot until the butter has melted and then whack the lid back and let it sit for 5 mins so the cheese gets all nice and melted.
Serve onto plates and top with a bit more fresh parsley and mint and grate over the remaining Wensleydale and a good drizzle of olive oil.

name: Cheesy Potato Chaat Wrap
description: Inspired by some of the flavours found in potato chaat. I love biting into the wrap and getting chunks of half melted cheddar, some crispy onion and even better, when you dip it into the tangy tamarind sauce. It’s delish.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Chop the potatoes into 1-2cm chunks and toss with a drizzle of olive oil and the garam masala. Scatter onto a baking tray lined with baking paper, season with salt and pepper, then slide into the oven and bake for 20-25 mins, until golden and crispy.

Meanwhile, defrost the peas and chop the Cheddar into 1-2cm cubes. Once the potatoes are done, tip them into a large bowl with the peas, Cheddar and crispy onions. Add the coriander chutney and toss everything together. Taste and season with salt, pepper or a little more chutney if needed. Set aside.
Make the dressing by stirring the tamarind purée and honey together, then squeeze in the juice of the lime and add a pinch of salt. Stir to combine.
Divide the potato mixture between the tortillas and wrap tightly, tucking the sides in as you go.
Place a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the wraps and toast for a few mins on each side, until golden and the cheese inside starts to melt.

Wrap in foil to keep warm and serve immediately with the tamarind dressing on the side for dipping. If you're prepping ahead, skip the toasting step and keep the untoasted wraps in the fridge or freezer. Toast before serving.

name: Cheesy Potato Naan Toastie
description: If you haven’t turned your naan into a toastie before, you are missing out. This one is packed with a beautiful potato curry and lots of cheddar.
keywords: Deli Kitchen Cheesy Potato Naan Toastie
instructions: Finely slice your red onions. Finely mince your garlic and ginger. Finely chop your green chillies. Dice your aubergine into 2cm cubes.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a saute pan. Add your aubergine and fry for 5 mins until golden. Remove your aubergine from the pan.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in the same saute pan. Add your cumin seeds and toast for 1 min. Add your red onion and cook over a medium heat for 25 mins until totally softened and caramelised.
Peel your potatoes, then chop them into 2cm chunks. Put these in a small saucepan with a large pinch of salt, then fill the pan with cold water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 mins.
Add your garlic, ginger, chillies, garam masala, and tomato puree to the onion pan. Cook out for 2 mins, then tip in your spinach. Cook for 2 mins until wilted.
Once your potatoes are tender, drain them in a colander. Once they have dried off, tip them into the spinach mix along with your aubergines. Stir to combine, then season to taste with salt.
Grab your Deli Kitchen Garlic and Coriander Naans, and cut them in half.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Add your naan herby side down, then sprinkle ¼ of your cheddar on top. Add ½ of your potato mix, the sprinkle with another ¼ of your cheese. Add your other half of naan garlic side up, then pop a piece of baking parchment on top.
Pop a heavy pan on top to press it, then cook for 3 mins. Once your cheese has melted, carefully flip your naan and repeat the pressing with the other side. Cook for another 3 mins.
Repeat with the rest of your mixture.
Cut each naan sandwich in half, then serve.

name: Cheesy Potato Pasta
description: This big cheesy double carb winter warmer is a take on the Neapolitan dish pasta e patate con la provola.
instructions: Add the pancetta and a splash of olive oil to a large frying pan and place over a medium heat. Cook for about 5 mins until the fat is rendering and it’s starting to turn crispy.
Dice the onion and add to the pan with the pancetta. Cube the potatoes and add those along with a good splash of water.
Mince the garlic, and after a few mins add this in along with your rosemary. As the water evaporates, top it up so that the texture stays thick and soupy. Cook until the potatoes are soft.
Meanwhile, cook your pasta in a large pan of boiling salted water until al dente.
Drain the pasta (reserving a mug of the cooking water) and add to the pan with the potatoes and pancetta.

Dice the scamorza, add along with half a mug of pasta water and the Parmesan and mix gently for about a minute until melted. Add more water as necessary to make a thick soupy consistency. Remove the sprig of rosemary.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Cheesy Pull-Apart Garlic Gnocchi
description: Our twist on pull-apart garlic bread, with crispy garlic and mozzarella filled gnocchi and all the melted cheese.
ingredients: 2Pack La Famiglia Rana Garlic & Mozzarella Filled Pan Fry Gnocchi
instructions: Heat your grill to medium-high.
Peel and finely dice your shallot and peel your garlic. Separate the basil leaves from the stalks.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a small saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the chopped shallot and peeled garlic with a pinch of salt. Cook for 3-4 mins or until softened.

Add in the tomato purée and chilli flakes to the saucepan along with the basil stalks and the water. Stir to combine, then cook for another 3-4 mins. Season with black pepper and remove the garlic and basil stalks (this is your cheat’s marinara).

Heat a drizzle of olive oil (or a knob of butter if you prefer) in a wide non-stick frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the gnocchi and pan-fry for 4-5 mins or until golden and crispy all over. Remove from the heat.

Cover the base of a small oven-safe dish with a layer of the gnocchi then sprinkle over a layer of grated mozzarella. Repeat with another layer of gnocchi and a final layer of cheese. Stick it under the grill for 3-4 or until the cheese has melted.

Remove the dish from the oven and let it cool slightly before sprinkling over the torn basil leaves and an extra pinch of chilli, if you like. Serve with a bowl of the marinara sauce for dipping. Go for a pull and get stuck in!

name: Cheesy Ratatouille & Pesto Jacket Potato
description: Crispy baked spuds loaded with leftover ratatouille, gooey melted cheddar and a sprinkle of fresh chives. The perfect fuss-free comfort food for when you want something cosy without the effort.
keywords: Cheesy Ratatouille & Pesto Jacket Potato recipe
instructions: Make the Ratatouille.
Heat the oven to 180°C.
Heat the ratatouille in a small pan or in the microwave.
Poke the potato with a fork all over, then rub with olive oil, salt and pepper. Pop into the oven for 1 hour until soft and fluffy in the middle and crisp on the outside.

When the potatoes are cooked, remove them from the oven once they're cool enough to handle. Then, cut a cross in the middle and gently smash them open. Heat the ratatouille in a small pan or the microwave, then spoon it into the middle of the potato. Grate over the cheese and pop back into the oven until melted. If you want a crispier crust on the cheese, slide it under a heated grill.
Finely chop the chives and scatter over the bubbling potato.

name: Cheesy Sausage & Pepper Traybake
description: This is the kind of traybake you put in the oven and forget about. Golden sausages, crisp-edged gnocchi, sweet peppers and melted cheese come together in one pan for a low-effort, high-reward dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C. Core, deseed and chop the peppers into chunks. Tip them into a large roasting tray along with the gnocchi.

Sprinkle over the herbes de provence, a generous pinch of salt and black pepper, then drizzle with the olive oil. Give everything a good mix. Halve the chipolatas and scatter them over the tray. Roast in the oven for 20 mins, or until the sausages are starting to colour and the gnocchi are crispy on the edges.
Meanwhile, finely grate the parmesan and set aside.

Once the tray’s been in for 20 mins, remove it from the oven and nestle in the mozzarella balls and sprinkle over two-thirds of the parmesan. Return to the oven for another 5 mins, or until the sausages are golden and cooked through.
Spoon onto plates and top with the remaining parmesan.

name: Cheesy Sausage, Chips & Beans Pie
description: A mash-up of all your favourite school dinners. This cheesy sausage, chips and beans pie will deliver serious nostalgia. Your next family favourite.
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C. Spread a single layer of chips onto a baking tray and pop it into the top of the oven. Bake for 25 mins whilst you get on with the rest of the prep.

Chop the sausages into 2cm pieces. Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and fry the sausages for around 10 mins whilst turning, until golden all over, then remove from the pan and into an ovenproof dish.

Finely slice the onions and garlic, then pick the thyme leaves. Add 2 tbsp oil to and the onions to a frying pan and cook for around 5 mins. Next, add in the garlic and thyme and cook for 2 mins before adding the tomato purée. Cook that off for 1 min until darkened in colour, then add the brown sugar and smoked paprika.
Drain your beans and add them to the pan along with the passata and water. Simmer gently for about 5 mins.
Pour the beans into the ovenproof dish along with the sausages and give it a good mix. Top with the crispy chips and scatter with cheese, then pop back in the oven until golden.

name: Cheesy Scrambled Egg & Pesto Pittas
description: This one is a bit like cheesy, eggy bread… and it's so easy. Definitely going to be your new favourite.
keywords: Cheesy Scrambled Egg & Pesto Pittas recipe
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Toast the pitta and pop onto a baking tray. Whisk the eggs in a bowl and set aside.
Tear the mozzarella and scatter it over the pitta bread. Slide the pitta under the grill and cook until golden and bubbling. The pitta will puff-up and go a bit squidgy – exactly what we are after.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a pan set over a low-medium heat. Tip in the eggs and season with salt and pepper. Gently fold the eggs to make silky ribbons, cooking to your preference, then remove from the heat.
Pop the cheesy pitta onto plates, then top with the pesto. Spoon over the egg and grate over the Parmesan. Finish with basil leaves on top, if you like.

name: Cheesy Spinach & Artichoke Pasta Bake
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

An outrageously cheesy green pasta inspired by spinach artichoke dip. It’s comforting with just a hint of goodness, and quick and easy to make.
instructions: Add the spinach, parsley, cornflour, peeled garlic cloves, onion granules and milk to a blender and blitz until smooth.

Set a large saucepan over a high heat. Pour in the blended milk mixture, vegetable stock and pasta. Stir together and season with salt and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to medium and leave to simmer, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is cooked to al dente (normally around 10 mins but follow the packet instructions). Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, drain the artichokes and chop any large ones into bite sized chunks. Heat the grill to high.
Once the pasta is cooked, stir through the artichokes, grated Cheddar and ½ the grated mozzarella. If you want it saucier, stir through a splash of water.
Tip the pasta into an ovenproof dish, scatter the remaining mozzarella over the top and season with freshly cracked black pepper. Slide under the grill for 2-5 mins until golden.
Leave it to cool for a couple of minutes before tucking in (warning: it's HOT!).

name: Cheesy Sprout Gratin
description: This one is naughty but nice, yes it has 3 types of cheese but it’s also packed with winter veggies.
keywords: Brussels sprout and cheddar gratin recipe
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C fan. Thinly slice the onion.
Heat ½ the butter in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Tip in the onion and add a pinch of salt, then cook for about 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until soft.
Meanwhile, quarter the sprouts and cut the broccoli into 2 inch pieces.
Add the sprouts and broccoli to the onions and season generously with salt and pepper. Add the water, stir, cover with a lid and cook for 3 or 4 mins until the veg starts to soften a little.

Remove the lid, pour in the cream and mustard and grate in ½ the cheese. Stir and cook gently for a couple of minutes until the cheese has melted. Taste and season if needed then pour the mix into an oven dish.
Into a small bowl, grate the remaining cheese and add the breadcrumbs and a pinch of salt. Mix to combine then sprinkle the breadcrumb mix evenly over the top of the gratin.
Add the rest of the butter in little dots around the top. Bake for 25 mins until golden.
Leave to rest for 5 mins before serving.

name: Cheesy Stuffed Peppers with Charred Corn
description: Easy, cheesy stuffed peppers with sweet and caramelised corn. Veggie BBQ doesn't get better than this. Pair with an Inch's Cider for the ultimate flavour combo.
keywords: Cheesy Stuffed Peppers with Charred Corn
instructions: Preheat the grill to high.
Rub the peppers with olive oil and salt, place on a tray and slide under the grill to char and cook, turning regularly, for 7-8 mins or until tender. Remove and allow to cool.

Meanwhile, tip the corn, liquid and all, into a small saucepan and set over a medium heat. Add the crème fraîche and a pinch of salt and bring to a boil. Reduce the liquid by half then tip into a blender with the jalapenos and a splash of brine. Blend until smooth.

Cut the corn from the cob and add to a cold pan. Add a splash of olive oil and saute over a medium heat with the rosemary sprig and a pinch of salt for 3-4 mins. Finely slice the green chillies and chuck in the pan too. Now add the butter and allow it to caramelise and turn nut brown. Slide the whole pan under the grill to char the corn. Once grilled and gnarly, set aside to keep warm.

Mash the feta and add the zest of one lime. Split the peppers open on one side lengthway and fill with the feta mixture. Drizzle with oil, salt and pepper and slide under the grill, cheese side up for 4-5 mins until caramelised.

To serve, warm the jalapeño corn sauce and tip onto a platter. Top with the feta stuffed peppers and scatter over the brown butter green chilli corn. Serve with lime for squeezing and torn coriander over top.

name: Cheesy Veggie Muffins
description: These golden veggie muffins are cheesy, fluffy and packed with hidden greens. Perfect for lunchboxes, picky eaters or on-the-go snacking.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases or lightly oil the holes.
Tip the frozen spinach into a heatproof bowl and cover with boiling water. Leave to defrost fully, then drain and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Finely slice the spring onions and coarsely grate the cheese.

Add the drained spinach, peas, sweetcorn and spring onions to a large bowl. Stir in the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt. Crack in the eggs, pour in the milk and melted butter, and mix to combine. Fold through three-quarters of the grated cheese.
Divide the mixture evenly between the muffin cases and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 20-25 mins until golden and cooked through. Let them cool slightly before eating.

name: Cheesy White Bean Quesadillas & Dipping Broth
description: Crispy quesadillas stuffed with smoky mashed white beans and melted cheese, served with a warm bowl of broth for dipping. A brilliant way to use up your Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli batch.
keywords: White Bean Quesadillas & Dipping Broth recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli batch recipe.
Place a sieve over a saucepan and pour in the Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli leftovers to separate the solids from the broth. Set the pan over a low heat to keep the broth warm.
Tip the solids from the drained batch into a bowl and mash until a rough paste forms, you want some texture, not completely smooth. You can also blitz in a food processor if you prefer.
Spread a dollop of the bean mixture over one half of each tortilla, top with the cheese and fold in half.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add a drizzle of olive oil and cook the each quesadilla for 4-6 mins, turning halfway, until golden on both sides and the cheese is melted.
Serve the quesadillas with the warm broth alongside for dipping.

name: Chermoula Cod Rolls With Harissa Yoghurt
description: This sandwich is packed with bold, brash flavours. We've taken a herby sauce originally from North Africa, and paired it with beautifully with grilled fish.
instructions: Combine the paprika and turmeric in a bowl with a good pinch of salt and the tbsp of olive oil. Give it a mix.
Cut the cod loin into eight evenly-sized pieces, then add to the bowl and toss with your hands to get it totally coated in the mixture. Pop it into the fridge to marinate for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, make the chermoula. Toast the cumin seeds in a small dry frying pan for 2 mins over a medium heat until fragrant. Roughly chop the green chilli.

Tip the cumin seeds into a blender along with all of your parsley and coriander (stalks and all), the olive oil and 2 tbsp of water. Squeeze in the juice from the lemon, then whizz to a smooth consistency. Season to taste with salt.
Spoon the yoghurt and harissa into a bowl, then mix to combine.
Preheat the grill to high and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Arrange the cod pieces on the lined tray, then place under the grill for 5 mins. Carefully flip them over, then grill for another 2 mins. The fish will be visibly flaky when it is cooked.
Halve the ciabatta rolls, then toast them over a medium-high heat in a dry frying pan until crisp.
Spread the base of each roll with the harissa mayo, then place two pieces of fish on top. Spoon over some chermoula, then top with the lid of your bun. Serve and enjoy.

name: Cherry & Almond Jam Roly-Poly
description: This recipe is edible nostalgia – it tastes like a cherry bakewell tart and a jam roly-poly had a delicious baby. Desserts don't get much better than this.
instructions: Put the flour, sugar, vanilla extract, almond extract, suet, ground almonds, baking powder and a pinch of salt into a bowl and combine with a knife. Slowly pour in the water, mixing until it comes together. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead with your hands until combined. Flatten into a square and wrap in cling film, then transfer to the fridge for at least 30 mins.

Heat the oven to 160°C. Fill the kettle and boil. Pour the boiling water into a deep roasting tray and place on the bottom shelf of the oven. Cut out four large pieces of tin foil, slightly overlapping two, then repeat with the other two on top. Cut a piece of greaseproof paper the same length of the foil, then grease with butter and place on top of the foil, greased-side up.

When the dough is chilled, lightly dust a surface with flour. Unwrap the dough and roll out until it’s around 50cm x 35cm. Using a spoon, gently spread the cherry compote over the dough leaving a 2cm border around one of the short edges and both of the long edges. Brush the exposed edges with milk, and gently roll up from the short side nearest to you (where the compote goes right to the edge), pressing the edges together gently to seal in the compote.

Carefully transfer the roly-poly to the middle of the greaseproof paper, seam-side down, and brush with a beaten egg. Sprinkle with sugar and toasted flaked almonds, then wrap in the paper, creating a seam over the top and securing the ends using the tin foil. It doesn't have to be too tight, as the dough will expand as it cooks. Move the roly-poly onto a baking tray and pop it in the oven on the top shelf for 1 hr 30 mins.
When cooked, remove from the oven and allow to sit for 5 mins before slicing and serving with custard.

name: Cherry & Almond Tart
description: It doesn't get much more classic than this. Ben Lippett's easy cherry and almond tart recipe is perfect for when cherries are in season. A pud to remember.
instructions: Add the butter and sugar to a bowl and beat for 6-7 mins until light and fluffy. Incorporate the eggs one by one, making sure the last egg is fully incorporated before adding the next. You should have a smooth, light batter. If it looks a bit split, add a tbsp of the flour before adding the next egg, don’t sweat it!
Fold in the almond extract and salt. Sift over the almonds and flour and beat into the mixture. Pop into the fridge for 30 mins or so.

Preheat the oven to 180°C. Roll out your pastry until it’s roughly the thickness of a £1 coin. Pop your 23cm tin in the centre of the pastry and cut a large circle around, leaving plenty of extra space around the tin, this creates the walls of your tart. Lift the pastry into the tart case and nudge it into the corners. If it breaks at all, don’t worry, just patch it up with some excess.

Leave plenty of overhanging pastry on the sides of the tart and line with baking paper. Fill the lined tart with rice or dried beans and slide into the oven for 15-20 mins. Remove the paper and beans and bake for a further 10 mins at 170°C.

While the pastry is blind baking, remove the stalks and stones from the cherries. I like to put the frangipane into a piping bag to fill the tart, it makes things a little easier but is absolutely not essential.

Allow the pastry to cool a little before you fill it. If you’re using the jam, spread it over the base of the tart. Top with the frangipane and then stud the top with plenty of cherries. Make the tart as full as you can.

Slide back into the oven for 35-40 mins or until golden brown and a skewer inserted comes out clean. Allow to cool before trimming the excess pastry from the rim of the tart and popping out of the tin. Serve with creme fraiche and a dusting of icing sugar.

name: Cherry & Mixed Seed Madeira Cake
description: A light madeira sponge cake with fresh cherries and whipped cream. Perfect with a cuppa.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease and line two 18cm round cake tins with butter. Slice the pitted cherries into 3 pieces each.
Use an electric whisk to beat the butter and sugar together for 4 mins until thick and creamy. Add the eggs, one at a time, and beat until just incorporated.

Sieve the flour into the butter and sugar mixture then fold it in with a spoon or spatula. Add the milk slowly, gently mixing as you do – you may not need all the milk, you only need enough to ensure that the mixture falls slowly from the spoon. Fold in the seeds and cherries.

Divide the mixture between the two prepared cake tins and level out to the edges. Bake for 30–35 mins, or until a cocktail stick inserted into the centre comes out clean. Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tins for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely.

For the whipped cream, pour the cold double cream into a chilled bowl large enough to hold at least double the volume of cream you’re whipping. Use an electric whisk to whip the cream on a medium speed until it's starting to thicken and you see the first sign of stiff peaks forming. Add the sugar then reduce the speed to low-medium just until you have very soft speaks – watch carefully as it will happen quickly.
Spread the base layer with the jam and spread or pipe the whipped cream on top. Sandwich the two halves of the cake together.
Sift in the icing sugar with enough lemon juice to give it a pouring consistency, then pour over the top of the cake. Decorate with toasted almonds.

name: Cherry Bakewell Overnight Oats
description: Bakewell, but for breakfast. Creamy oats layered with sweet syrupy cherries, crunchy toasted almonds and a dreamy almond butter topping. Need we say more?
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Place the flaked almonds on an oven tray, roast for 10 minutes or until golden.
Chuck the oats into a bowl with the yoghurt, milk, vanilla extract, half the almond extract and the protein powder, if using. Mix well to combine, then set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the almond butter, the remaining almond extract, two-thirds of the maple syrup and a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Tip the frozen cherries into a small saucepan with the rest of the maple syrup. Set over a low-medium heat and cook until the cherries have defrosted and are starting to release their juices. Roughly mash with a potato masher, leaving a few chunky bits.
Spoon the cherry mixture into the bottom of your containers. Top with the oats, then drizzle over the almond butter mixture. Finish with a scattering of toasted flaked almonds.
Cover and place in the fridge overnight.

name: Cherry Chocolate Froyo
description: Who doesn't love a cherry chocolate combo? This froyo is perfect to share with friends on a summers day. Check out the other flavour combos on the website.
instructions: Deseed and roughly chop the cherries.
Blend the cherries and chocolate with the yogurt and a squeeze of agave if you like, until smooth.
You can also keep some cherries and chocolate pieces to put directly into the molds for some extra texture. Pour into molds and freeze for 3-4 hours.
Optional also to drizzle the finished ones with melted chocolate and chopped pistachios.

name: Cherry Labneh With Basil Oil And Pistachios
description: An ode to cherry season. This dip sits between sweet and savoury and can be served as part of a mezze or with a drizzle of agave to make a light dessert.
instructions: Add the yoghurt and the cream cheese to a bowl and whisk well until completely smooth. Add the lemon juice and salt and mix through well.

This next step is optional, but if you are after a thick labneh, straining it overnight will make it thicker and creamier. However, it’s already delicious as it is just mixed together as above. 
Place a j-cloth or cheesecloth over a strainer and place the strainer over a bowl to catch the liquid. Add the yoghurt carefully into the cloth and tie it up with an elastic band. Place a bowl over the top with a weight on it (a can works well), to help press the liquid out. Leave in the fridge to drain for a day. You should see some liquid in the bowl beneath.

To make the basil oil, boil a pot of water and have another bowl of ice water ready. Blanch the basil for 10 seconds and then strain it and quickly dunk it into the ice water to stop it cooking further. You can also prepare the basil oil in advance, it keeps well for up to 3 days.
Drain and squeeze as much water out of the basil as possible. In a high speed blender, blend the basil with 75ml olive oil for 4-5 mins until it is completely smooth, with no bits of basil. Strain over a j-cloth or cheesecloth for at least an hour, with a bowl below to catch the oil. This is your basil oil, it should be a bright, clear, fragrant oil. If it has turned out too dark, you may have boiled it for a little too long which cooks the delicate leaves.

When the labneh is ready, prepare the cherries by cutting them in half, around the pip. Pop the pips out by pushing them out from the back of the cherry. Add the cherry halves to a bowl and drizzle the pomegranate molasses and a squeeze of lemon juice over them.
Chop your pistachios.

To serve, lay a thick layer of labneh on a plate, spoon over the cherries and some of their juices, then finish with a drizzle of basil oil and some basil leaves and pistachios. Serve with crusty, toasted ciabatta.

name: Cherry Lemonade
description: Run to the shops and buy these four ingredients. Cherries. Lemons. Sugar. Sparkling water. They're all you'll need to whip up this summer sipper. Go get it! B x
instructions: Wash and pit your cherries.
Add the cherries to a blender, saving a few for later, with the lemon juice and sugar.
Blend to a sharp, sweet, tangy purée.
Fill a large jug with ice and pour over your purée.
Top off with the sparkling water and chuck in a few lemon wedges and extra cherries.
Pour into glasses and serve.

name: Cherry Tomato & Cottage Cheese Pasta Salad
description: A fresh, filling pasta salad with juicy chicken, creamy cottage cheese, and a hit of basil. Perfect straight from the fridge.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the fusilli following pack instructions. Drain, rinse under cold water and set aside to cool. You can do this ahead of time as well.

Halve the cherry tomatoes and finely slice the courgette. Grate the Parmesan. Toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 mins until golden. Tear the basil leaves. Shred or dice the cooked chicken.

Tip the cooled pasta into a large mixing bowl. Add the cherry tomatoes, sundried tomato paste, cottage cheese, chicken, courgette and most of the basil. Season generously with salt and black pepper, then toss everything together until well combined.
Divide between bowls or containers. Finish with the toasted pine nuts, a scattering of Parmesan and the rest of the basil.

name: Cherry Tomato Gnocchi With Herby Pesto
description: The pesto is a game changer - as soon as it hits the hot gnocchi the herby oils intensify, working wonders with the rich tomato sauce.
instructions: Lightly toast the walnuts in a frying pan. Once toasted, add them to a blender, followed by the basil, chives, mint, olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper and a dash of red wine vinegar. Blend until smooth.
Add your cherry tomatoes to a frying pan with a drizzle of olive oil. As the tomatoes soften, roughly crush them with a spoon.
Add gnocchi to a pan of salted boiling water.
Grate the garlic into the tomatoey pan, add your chilli flakes, your red wine vinegar and pepper.
Take a ladle of gnocchi water and add it to the pan and mix. Add your gnocchi and stir thoroughly. Pour some of your pesto over the top of the gnocchi and tuck in!

name: Cherry Tomato Risotto Recipe
description: Tomato risotto is a delicious and comforting dish that combines the creaminess of classic risotto with the vibrant flavour of tomatoes. This tomato risotto recipe is perfect for those who love rich, savoury meals with a hint of tanginess. To make this dish, start by sautéing onions and garlic in olive oil until soft, then stir in Arborio rice to toast slightly before deglazing with white wine. Slowly add vegetable or chicken broth, stirring regularly, allowing the rice to absorb the liquid. The star of this tomato risotto recipe is the addition of ripe tomatoes or tomato sauce, which gives the dish its signature flavour and beautiful colour. Fresh basil, Parmesan cheese, and a touch of butter are added toward the end for extra creaminess and depth. This tomato risotto recipe is perfect for a cozy dinner, and it pairs well with a crisp salad or roasted vegetables for a complete meal.
instructions: Heat a splash of olive oil in a pan on a high heat and add in the cherry tomatoes. You want the tomatoes to char and become squidgy but not so much that they disintegrate. It is important to remove the tomatoes from the pan before they completely disintegrate. Set aside.
Finely chop the onion. Heat a glug of oil and a tbsp of butter and fry the onion until soft and translucent.
Thinly chop your rosemary and garlic. Add into the pan along with your tomato purée and chilli flakes and stir together.
Toss through your rice until nicely coated and toast for about 2 minutes.

Dissolve the chicken stock in boiling water and pour a glug into the risotto. Once the rice has soaked this up, add more bit by bit. This is a process of beating and adding until all the stock is absorbed. By the end, your rice should be thick and creamy. This process will take about 30 minutes.

When this is done, re-add the majority of your cooked tomatoes (saving some for garnish). Grate 4/5 of the parmesan, chop your basil and add in 2/3 of the butter, salt and pepper. Stir it all through.
Once combined and perfectly cooked, turn off the heat, put the lid on and let it sit for a couple of minutes. Then, serve up and garnish with tomatoes and the leftover parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Chewy Apple, Oat & Almond Bars
description: Sweet, sticky spiced oat bars made with almond butter and grated apple. A proper tasty snack or brekkie bite with zero fuss.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a square 20cm x 20cm baking tin with baking paper.
Gently melt the coconut oil in a small saucepan or in the microwave, then set aside to cool slightly.
Grate the apples, leaving the skin on and in a separate bowl, stir together with the almond butter, melted coconut oil and date syrup until smooth.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix and stir everything together until you’ve got a thick, sticky mixture.
Press the mixture firmly into a lined tin, smoothing it out evenly.

Bake for 25–30 minutes, or until golden at the edges and firm in the center. Cool completely in the tin before removing from the tin and slicing into bars. Wrap in baking paper and chill or freeze until needed (these last for a week in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer).

name: Chicago Deep Dish Pizza
description: Cheesy, saucy, and just the right amount of greasy. This homemade Chicago deep-dish pizza recipe is surprisingly easy to make at home. With its thick, buttery crust, loaded with layers of gooey mozzarella cheese, and topped with a rich, tangy tomato sauce, this pizza is a true comfort food classic.
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the yeast and honey into 220ml of warm water and set aside. Tip the flour and salt into another bowl, dice the cold butter and add to the flour mixture. Using your fingertips, rub the butter into the flour until it has the texture of fine breadcrumbs.

Tip the yeast mixture into the butter and flour and mix to a shaggy dough. Tip out onto a work surface and knead briefly until you have a smooth dough. Form into a ball and add to an oiled bowl, cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size. Alternatively, pop the dough into the fridge for 12-24 hours.

While the dough is rising, make the sauce. Finely dice the onion and finely grate the garlic. Grab a medium saucepan and set over a medium heat. Add a shot of oil and add the onion with a big pinch of salt.

Cook for 5-6 mins until translucent and softened. Add the garlic and dried oregano and cook for a further 2-3 mins. Add the sugar, tomatoes and a whole bunch of basil. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 mins. Allow the basil leaves to break down and mix through the sauce, fishing out the stems at the end. Set the sauce aside.
Preheat the oven to 210°C.

Grab a round tin or cast iron pan that is roughly 25cm by 5cm. Turn the dough out onto a lightly oiled surface. Roll out until it is a circle measuring roughly 35cm across. Transfer to the pan and work into the corners and up the sides of the pan.

Layer the bottom of the dough with the sliced mozzarella so it is completely covered. Remove the meat from the sausage casings and pinch small amounts, dotting over the mozzarella, again, making sure there is an equal amount of meat over the pizza. Now ladle over your tomato sauce, covering the sausage.
Top the sauce with the pepperoni, be generous. Cover the whole lot with grated Parmesan and a shed load of black pepper. Drizzle with olive oil and slide into the oven for 35-40 mins.
Once baked, remove from the oven and allow to rest for 10 mins before slicing and serving.

name: Chicago-Style Hot Dogs
description: What's special about Chicago hot dogs? Everything. Dressed with mustard, relish, and pickle spear, these loaded hot dogs are the ultimate summer barbecue flex.
instructions: Pile coals over to one side of your BBQ to create a hot, direct cooking side, and a warm, indirect cooking side.

Score the hot dogs a few times so they stay nice and straight while on the grill. Lightly oil and then place onto the hot bars over the direct heat. Roll over, crisping up the skin, until nice and brown, before moving over to the indirect side. Pop the lid on the BBQ and cook and smoke for 8-10 mins.
Grab the hot dog buns and brush with a little water, then pop on top of the hot dogs under the lid of the BBQ. Allow to warm up for a couple of minutes.
Cut the tomatoes in half and then into slices. Season well with salt and black pepper and add a little oil. Cut the onion into chunky dice.

Once nice and warm, pull the buns off the grill and split in half lengthways. Slather the inside of each bun with mayo and top with a hot dog. Tuck in a couple of slices of tomato and top with relish and a zigzag of mustard. Finish with diced onions and a pickle spear.

name: Chicken & Bacon Chopped Salad
description: It's time for another chopped salad. This protein-heavy, veg-filled salad can easily be whipped up on a weeknight. We think you might like it.
instructions: Boil the broccoli in a pot of salted boiling water for 3-4 mins until it’s just about cooked. Then remove it and allow it to cool.

Preheat your oven to 180°C. Season your chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place your breasts onto a baking tray and get them in the oven for 25 mins. Allow them to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm. Add the bacon in for the last 10 mins until crispy.
Heat up your quinoa according to the package instructions.
Add lettuce, broccoli, chicken, and bacon to a board and chop it all up.
Add it all to a bowl with the quinoa.
Make the dressing with oil, lemon juice, mustard, and honey. Mix it all up until emulsified and coat the salad.
Give it a good toss and serve on plates.

name: Chicken & Bacon Mashed Potato Pie
description: Cheesy, hearty, warming. This chicken and bacon mashed potato pie is exactly the sort of dish you'd want to come home to after a long day at school. Nostalgia done right.
keywords: Chicken & Bacon Mashed Potato Pie recipe
instructions: Dice the chicken into 2cm pieces. Finely slice the garlic, then halve and finely slice the leeks before popping them into a colander and giving them a good rinse. Peel and finely dice the carrots. Pick the leaves from the thyme stems.

Add a shot of oil to a pan set over a medium heat, then add the chicken. Brown on all sides before removing the chicken from the pan. Set aside. Add the bacon and fry until golden and crisp. Add the carrots, leeks, thyme and garlic, then fry for 5 mins until the leeks are soft.

Add the flour and cook for 2-3 mins. Pour in the stock and simmer away for a couple of minutes until thickened. Return the chicken to the pan, then mix through 5 tbsp of the crème fraîche. Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning. Set aside while you prepare the mash.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel and cut the potatoes into quarters, put them into a large saucepan and cover with cold, salted water. Bring to the boil and cook for 10-15 mins until the potatoes are tender. Meanwhile, grate the cheddar. Drain the potatoes and steam-dry for a couple of minutes, before mashing until smooth.

Transfer the mashed potato back to the same saucepan and put over a low heat. Add the butter and melt through, then stir through 2 tbsp crème fraîche and your Dijon mustard. Mix until combined, then season generously with salt and pepper.

Now your filling and mash are ready, it’s time to assemble! All you need to do is fill a deep casserole dish with the filling and then scoop the mash on top using an ice-cream scoop – if you don’t have one, use a spoon and smooth-out instead (the ice-cream scoop is just very reminiscent of school dinners!). Scatter over the cheese, then transfer the pie to the oven and bake for 25-30 mins until golden.

name: Chicken & Basil Stir Fry
description: Inspired by my favourite Thai dish, Pad Kra Pao, this is as good as meal prep gets. Ready in under 30 minutes and the flavour gets better the longer you leave it. Plus there’s barely any chopping - only the broccoli, but that’s easy.
keywords: Meal Prep: Chicken & Basil Stir Fry
Meal Prep: Chicken & Basil Stir Fry recipe
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions.
Make the sauce: Add all the ingredients to a food processor and blend until smooth (don’t worry too much, some texture is nice). Set aside. Taste and add more fish sauce if you want it saltier.

Stir-fry time: Place a large pan or wok over a high heat and add the vegetable oil. Once hot add the chicken mince and cook it for 3 mins, breaking it up into small pieces with a wooden spoon as you go. Add the sauce and cook for another 2-3 mins.

Chop the broccoli up into bite-sized pieces. Add the broccoli to the pan and cook for 3-4 mins or until tender. Add the basil leaves and toss through to wilt. Taste and season with fish sauce, if needed
For the eggs, either boil them for 7 mins then peel and store them in the fridge until serving, or fry them fresh each time you eat a portion. Nothing beats a crispy fried egg.
To store the portions, divide the rice evenly between containers and top with the chicken mince. Keep in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat in the microwave for 3 mins or until piping hot.
To serve, transfer the reheated rice and chicken to a plate and finish with an egg, a lime wedge and some sriracha, if you like.

name: Chicken & Broccoli Chopped Salad
description: This super classic chopped salad recipe is great for a light dinner or a filling lunch. The homemade dressing is the key.
instructions: Boil the broccoli in a pot of salted boiling water for 3-4 mins until it’s just about cooked. Remove the broccoli and allow it to cool.

Preheat your oven to 180°C. Season your chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place your chicken breasts onto a baking tray and get them in the oven for 25 mins. Allow them to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm.
Heat up your quinoa according to package instructions.
Squeeze the juice from your limes and combine with the rest of the dressing ingredients in a bowl.

Chop up the coriander, the cooked broccoli, and chicken into even-sized pieces. Combine your broccoli, coriander, chicken, and quinoa in a bowl before topping with the dressing and tossing vigorously. Serve and enjoy.

name: Chicken & Cauliflower Fried Rice Bowl
description: A spicy, punchy fakeaway-style fried rice bowl made with cauliflower rice, chicken mince, and edamame. High protein, low faff.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the ginger into matchsticks. Peel and finely chop the garlic.

Heat half of the sesame oil in a large nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken mince and cook for about 4 mins, breaking it up with a wooden spoon until no longer pink. Add half the soy sauce and half the gochujang, stir to coat, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining sesame oil to the pan. Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 min until fragrant.

Tip in the frozen red peppers and edamame and stir-fry for 2–3 mins until heated through. Push everything to one side of the pan and spritz a little olive oil spray onto the empty space. Crack in the eggs and scramble them with a spoon, then fold through the veg.

Add the cooked chicken back to the pan along with the frozen cauliflower rice, remaining gochujang and soy sauce. Stir everything together and cook for 2–3 mins until piping hot. Season to taste. Pick the coriander leaves.
Spoon the rice into bowls, scatter over the coriander and serve with lime wedges.

name: Chicken & Cherry Tomato Barley Salad
description: A healthy, high-protein salad which is big on flavour and low on faff. Make a big batch for the ultimate weekday lunch.
keywords: Chicken & Cherry Tomato Barley Salad  recipe
instructions: Rinse the pearl barley under cold water. Tip into a saucepan with water and a good pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and cook for around 40 mins, or until tender. Add a splash more water if needed. Drain off any excess water and fluff with a fork.

Add the chicken to a bowl. Finely grate in the garlic, add the Dijon mustard and lemon juice. Season well with salt and plenty of black pepper. Mix to coat. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken for 10–15 mins, turning occasionally, until golden and cooked through. Set aside to rest, then slice.

Peel and finely slice the shallots into rings. Tip into a bowl with the vinegar and let sit for 5 mins to lightly pickle. Roughly chop the tomatoes and add them to the bowl. Thinly slice the courgette and pit the cherries, then add both to the salad. Season well with salt and pepper, tear in the dill, and drizzle with a little olive oil. Let the salad sit for at least 30 mins to develop flavour.

Make the green chilli dressing. Crack open the cardamom pods and remove the seeds. Toast the cardamom seeds, cumin seeds, and coriander seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2–3 mins, until fragrant. Transfer to a blender and pulse until roughly broken down. Add the trimmed chillies, garlic, and fresh coriander. Blend while gradually pouring in the olive oil to emulsify. Squeeze in the lemon juice, season with salt and pepper, and blend again until smooth.
Divide the barley between containers. Top with sliced chicken and a generous spoonful of the tomato and cherry salad. Drizzle with the green chilli dressing or serve it on the side.

name: Chicken & Chickpea Korma With Chunky Peanut Chutney
description: Chicken thighs and chickpeas cooked in a rich and creamy korma sauce served up with rice, a drizzle of yoghurt and an easy, no-blitz, chunky chutney. This chicken chickpea korma is elite.
keywords: Chicken & Chickpea Korma With Chunky Peanut Chutney
Chicken & Chickpea Korma With Chunky Peanut Chutney recipe
instructions: Dice the chicken into pieces and finely chop the coriander stalks. Add to a bowl with the korma pots, coriander stalks and a big pinch of salt, then cover and marinade for at least 4 hours but preferably overnight.

Finely slice the onion. Heat oil in a pot and fry the onion over a medium heat until translucent, around 7 mins. Add the chicken and fry for 5 mins, then add in the water and drained chickpeas. Cover with a lid and cook for 15 mins until the chicken is cooked through.

Toast the cumin seeds in a small pan over a low heat until fragrant and roughly chop the peanuts and finely chop most of the coriander. Add cumin seeds, peanuts and coriander to a bowl along with the zest and juice of a lemon, grated garlic and olive oil. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Back to the curry – stir in the yoghurt and the remainder of the fresh coriander. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, then plate up and drizzle with the chunky peanut chutney.

name: Chicken & Chorizo Baked Rice
description: Juicy chicken, smoky chorizo and sweet roasted tomatoes all baked in one pot of fluffy rice. Big flavour, low effort and perfect for feeding a hungry crowd.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Heat the oven to 180°C.
Cut the chorizo into chunks and the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Finely slice the onions, peppers and garlic.

Set a large ovenproof frying pan or casserole dish over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry the chorizo for 2-3 mins until it starts to release its oil, then add the chicken and cook for another 5-6 mins until browned.
Stir in the onions, peppers and garlic. Cook for 8-10 mins until soft and golden. Season well with salt and pepper.

Rinse the rice under cold water until it runs clear. Stir the rice into the pan, then pour in the chicken stock and scatter over the cherry tomatoes. Bring everything to the boil, then cover tightly with a lid or foil and transfer to the oven. Bake for 45 mins until the rice is tender and the stock has been absorbed.
Meanwhile, zest and juice lemon half the lemons. Mix the yoghurt with the lemon zest, juice, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt.

Fluff up the rice with a fork and serve up!
Kids Plate: Dish out with a dollop of the paprika yoghurt on the side.
Parents Plate: Dish out with a dollop of the paprika yoghurt and a handful of chopped parsley on top and a lemon wedge.

name: Chicken & Chorizo Giant Couscous
description: An easy one-pan high-protein meal. Giant couscous adds a lovely bit of texture to this delicious prep-friendly meal.
instructions: Rub the chicken thighs with olive oil, ½ the smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Heat a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Once hot, sear the chicken for 8–10 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan, cover, and let rest.

Meanwhile, peel and finely chop the garlic and onion. Dice the chorizo and finely chop the parsley stalks (reserve the leaves). Add a splash of oil to a large sauté pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, garlic, chorizo, parsley stalks, and remaining paprika for 5 mins until softened and fragrant. Stir in the tomato purée and cook for another 1–2 mins to thicken.

Slice the roasted red peppers and add them to the pan. Tip in the giant couscous and pour over the chicken stock. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 10–12 mins, stirring occasionally, until the couscous is just tender. Stir in the peas and cook for 2 more mins.

Finely chop the parsley leaves and stir through with a big squeeze of lemon juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Slice the rested chicken and lay it over the couscous. Serve with extra parsley, lemon wedges, and a dollop of yoghurt if you like.

name: Chicken & Chorizo Giant Couscous with Herb Salad
description: Here's a lovely couscous dish that you can make with your batch-cooked Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo recipe. It's really, really delicious.
keywords: chicken chorizo air fryer recipe uk
instructions: Make the Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo.
Start by cooking the couscous in boiling, salted water for 6 mins. Drain and rinse in cold water. Warm the batch through until piping hot if you like, or you can serve this one cold.

Whichever you decide, mix the Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo (saving the chicken either for the top or shredding it up) through the drained couscous along with the spinach. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Pick the herbs and finely slice the red onion. Mix together in a bowl.
Serve the couscous topped with the chicken (if eating whole) and the herb salad. Finish with a drizzle of oil and a sprinkling of sumac.

name: Chicken & Chorizo Quesadillas
description: Everyone loves a quesadilla. This is a simple student-friendly recipe that's affordable and filling.
instructions: Finely slice your chicken. Peel and roughly chop your chorizo and place in a bowl with the chicken.
Add the herbs and spices and season with salt and pepper and set aside.
Roughly dice your peppers, finely slice your red onion and mince the garlic.
Place a frying pan on a high heat and fry the chicken and chorizo in veg oil for 5 mins.
Then add your peppers, onions and garlic and fry for a few mins.
Remove the contents into a bowl and place the pan back on the heat.
Drizzle some more veg oil in the pan and add your tortilla.
Sprinkle a layer of cheese across the bottom on the tortilla and then add some of the chicken and chorizo mixture. Finally top with some extra cheese before putting another tortilla on top.

Once the bottom tortilla is golden brown use a spatula to flip it to get some colour on the other side. The cheese on either side of the quesadilla will act as glue holding everything together so it doesn’t spill out the sides.
Once golden on both sides. Cut the quesadilla into quarters and serve with some tomato salsa, sour cream and guacamole. Enjoy!

name: Chicken & Coconut Chickpeas
description: This one's a proper weeknight banger. Crispy and juicy chicken on a creamy, lightly-spiced coconut curry base finished with lime for that extra zing. It's high in fibre and protein and gets on the table in under 30 mins - plus the leftovers are even better the next day.
instructions: Slice the cucumber on an angle, then add to a bowl with the juice of one of the limes and a pinch of salt. Toss and set aside.

Drizzle a little olive oil over the chicken and season with salt and pepper. Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat and add the chicken. Cook for about 5-7 mins on each side, pressing the chicken down with the back of a spoon to get it crispy. While it’s cooking, peel the garlic and ginger and drain the chickpeas. Once cooked through, remove the chicken from the pan and set aside on a plate to rest.

Add a splash of olive oil to the pan, turn the heat down to medium and grate the garlic and ginger directly into the pan. Add the turmeric, then stir to cook for a minute. Add the chickpeas along with the coconut milk, season with salt and pepper and simmer for 10-15 mins until thickened to your liking. (If you've got the larger jarred chickpeas you may need less time as these are softer, whereas canned have a slightly more bite so will need the full cooking time to soften). Before serving, taste and season with fish sauce, if needed. Add the zest and juice of half the limes, cutting the other half into two wedges to serve.

Slice the chicken, then spoon the chickpeas into the bowl and top with the sliced chicken and cucumber salad. Drizzle a little of the cucumber liquid over the top, this really brings the extra zing to cut through the curry. Scatter with coriander leaves and top with a pinch of chilli flakes. Serve with a lime wedge on the side of each bowl.

name: Chicken & Cottage Cheese Meatballs with Butter Beans
description: Garlicky chicken meatballs on buttery beans with lemon, Parmesan, and a bit of chilli. Deliciously high protein. Perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Peel and finely grate the garlic. Pick the parsley leaves and finely chop them.

Chuck half the grated garlic and one-third of the chopped parsley into a mixing bowl with the chicken mince and cottage cheese. Grate over the zest of half the lemon and finely grate in half the Parmesan. Season well with salt and black pepper.
Shape into golfball-sized meatballs with wet hands and place them onto a foil-lined baking tray.
Grill the meatballs for about 15 mins, until golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, in a pan, add olive oil with the remaining garlic. Cook for 1 minute, until the garlic is sizzling then dump the butter beans (liquid and all) in. Bring to a gentle simmer. Fold through the spinach to wilt. Tip any juices from the chicken into the beans and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Grate over the remaining lemon zest and squeeze in the juice from a quarter of the lemon. Cut the rest into wedges for serving.

Spoon the beans into Tupperware containers and top with the meatballs. Sprinkle over the remaining chopped parsley, garlic, and chilli flakes then grate over the remaining Parmesan. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch - they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken & Cottage Cheese Meatballs with Butter Beans
description: Garlicky chicken meatballs on buttery beans with lemon, Parmesan, and a bit of chilli. Deliciously high protein.
instructions: Heat the grill to high and place the oven rack in the top 1/3 of the oven. Peel and finely grate the garlic. Pick the parsley leaves and finely chop them.

Chuck half of the grated garlic and one-third of the chopped parsley into a mixing bowl with the chicken mince and cottage cheese. Grate over the zest of half the lemon and finely grate in half the Parmesan. Season well with salt and black pepper.
Shape into golfball-sized meatballs with wet hands and place them onto a foil-lined baking tray and drizzle the olive oil.
Grill the meatballs for about 15 mins, until golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, in a pan, add olive oil with the remaining garlic. Cook for 1 minute, until the garlic is sizzling then dump the butter beans (liquid and all) in. Bring to a gentle simmer. Fold through the spinach to wilt. Tip any juices from the chicken into the beans and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Grate over the remaining lemon zest and squeeze in the juice from a quarter of the lemon. Cut the rest into wedges for serving.
Spoon the beans into bowls and top with the meatballs. Sprinkle over the remaining chopped parsley, garlic and chilli flakes then grate over the remaining Parmesan

name: Chicken & Egg Fried Rice
description: Sticky, crispy rice, juicy chicken, fluffy eggs, and that wok-charred magic. A healthy take on the ultimate fakeaway.
instructions: Mix all the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
Chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces, peel and finely mince the garlic. Trim and slice the spring onions, keeping the whites and greens separate. Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat.
Heat a large wok or frying pan over a high heat with the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the chicken and stir-fry for 4–6 mins until golden and cooked through. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

In the same pan, add the garlic and the whites of the spring onions. Cook for 1–2 mins until softened and fragrant. Push everything to one side of the pan and pour in the beaten eggs. Let them set slightly, then break them apart and stir through.
Add the day-old rice to the pan. Spread it out evenly and leave it for 1–2 mins to catch some colour, then toss well to break up any clumps.
Return the chicken to the pan and pour in the rest of the sauce directly onto the hot surface. Toss everything together until evenly coated and the rice is piping hot.
Stir through the frozen peas and beansprouts and cook for 1–2 mins until just heated through.
Divide the fried rice between bowls and top with and a handful of the sliced green spring onions.

name: Chicken & Garlic Rice Traybake with Herby Slaw
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A gorgeous and garlicky chicken traybake recipe that's incredibly easy to make. Made using affordable ingredients from Aldi. Yum.
keywords: Chicken & Garlic Rice Traybake with Herby Slaw
Chicken & Garlic Rice Traybake with Herby Slaw recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to fan 180°C. Bash the garlic, trim and thinly slice the ginger and spring onions. Wash the rice until the water runs clear.
Add the soy sauce, honey, 5-spice and bashed garlic into a bowl. Mix the chicken thighs through until coated.

Place an oven-proof frying pan over medium heat with a drizzle of oil (if you don’t have one you can transfer the dish into a baking tray before roasting). Once hot, add the chicken, and sear on one side (keep the chicken marinade). Transfer to a plate.

Add the spring onions whites and ¾ of the greens along with the ginger into the empty pan. Stir-fry until softened and fragrant, 1-2 mins. Tip the rice in with the chicken stock. Let it come to a boil, place a lid on and turn the heat down to low for 10 mins.

Uncover, place the chicken thighs on top, seared side up, and drizzle over the marinade. Place the lid back on, and transfer into the oven for 10 mins. Then, remove the lid and leave it in the oven for another 8-12 minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked and starting to char in places. If your chicken thighs are large, they may need longer.

Meanwhile, trim and finely slice the sugar snap peas, slice the carrots into thin matchsticks, pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems. Toss them all together with the sesame seeds. Right before serving, drizzle over some olive oil.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove the pan from the oven. Transfer the chicken to a board and let the rice rest for 5-10 mins before fluffing.
Once your chicken and rice are rested, slice the chicken. Share the rice in boxes or bowls. Add the chicken on top. Serve with the slaw and dress it with a wedge of lime.

name: Chicken & Garlic Rice with Crunchy Slaw
description: A gorgeous and garlicky chicken recipe that's incredibly easy to whip up and meal prep for the week.
keywords: Chicken & Garlic Rice Traybake with Herby Slaw
Chicken & Garlic Rice Traybake with Herby Slaw recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to fan 180°C. Bash the garlic, trim and thinly slice the ginger and spring onions. Wash the rice until the water runs clear.
Add the soy sauce, honey, 5-spice and bashed garlic into a bowl. Mix the chicken thighs through until coated.

Place an oven-proof frying pan over medium heat with a drizzle of oil (if you don’t have one you can transfer the dish into a baking tray before roasting). Once hot, add the chicken, and sear on one side (keep the chicken marinade). Transfer to a plate.

Add the spring onions whites and ¾ of the greens along with the ginger into the empty pan. Stir-fry until softened and fragrant, 1-2 mins. Tip the rice in with the chicken stock. Let it come to a boil, place a lid on and turn the heat down to low for 10 mins.

Uncover, place the chicken thighs on top, seared side up, and drizzle over the marinade. Place the lid back on, and transfer into the oven for 10 mins. Then, remove the lid and leave it in the oven for another 7-10 minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked and starting to char in places.
Meanwhile, trim and finely slice the sugar snap peas and slice the carrots into thin matchsticks. Toss them all together with the sesame seeds. Right before serving, drizzle over some olive oil.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove the pan from the oven. Transfer the chicken to a board and let the rice rest for 5-10 mins before fluffing.

Once your chicken and rice are rested, slice the chicken. Divide the rice between Tupperware containers. Add the chicken on top, along with the slaw and nestle in a wedge of lime. Garnish with the remaining spring onions and box up. Stash in the fridge ready for later - these keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken & Giant Couscous Soup
description: This hearty chicken soup with giant couscous (regular couscous’ bigger, chewier brother) is comforting and filling – perfect for when life screams for a warm, wholesome bowl of goodness pronto.
instructions: Heat a glug of olive oil in a large, deep pan over a medium heat. Season both sides of the chicken breasts with salt and pepper, then pan fry for 5 mins on each side until golden.
Pour in the chicken stock and simmer for 10 mins until the chicken is cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and shred using two forks. Set aside.
Meanwhile, peel and slice the carrots, slice the celery stalks and leeks (both the green and white parts), mince the garlic and shred the kale. Set aside.
In a separate large pan, heat a glug of olive oil over a medium heat. Add the leek, carrots and celery, and sauté for about 5 mins until the vegetables begin to soften.
Add the garlic and sauté for another minute, then pour in the stock, add the bay leaves and bring to the boil.
Once the soup is boiling, add the pearl couscous, then reduce to a simmer, cover and cook for 10–12 mins, or until the couscous is cooked through.
Stir in the shredded kale and cook until wilted, about 3 mins, followed by the shredded chicken.
Squeeze in the juice of the lemon for a burst of fresh flavour, then taste and adjust the seasoning with more salt and pepper, if needed.
Divide the soup between bowls and serve hot with a few more turns of freshly ground black pepper.

name: Chicken & Ginger Creamy Rice
description: If a congee and a risotto had a baby, it’d look a little bit like this. Every spoonful is packed with flavour.
instructions: Peel and finely grate or chop the garlic and ginger. Slice the spring onions. Add a tbsp of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium high heat, add the garlic, ginger and most of the spring onions and sizzle for a minute, then tip in the rice and stir to coat.

Add the rice wine, then add a large splash of the stock, stir until it absorbs, then add the rest, stirring constantly. Bring to the boil, remove from the heat, lower the chicken thighs into the pan, making sure the thighs are submerged. Turn the heat down to low, cover with a lid and leave for 20 mins, until the thighs are perfectly poached- if they need a little longer let them cook a little longer. Remove the thighs onto a plate and use two forks to shred.

Check the rice, it should be the consistency of a loose risotto. If it’s not, or the rice is still firm, simmer until the rice is cooked through, adding more water if necessary. Stir in the butter along with the shredded chicken. taste and season generously with salt. Add the lime juice.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with a drizzle of soy sauce and chili oil, then finish with the remaining sliced spring onion and toasted sesame seeds. Pure comfort.

name: Chicken & Greens in Brothy Rice
description: Tender chicken thighs with cavolo nero and fluffy rice in a fragrant broth. A cosy aromatic bowl that’s as comforting as it is nourishing.
keywords: Chicken & Greens in Brothy Rice Recipe
instructions: Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Bash the ginger with the back of a large knife then add to the pan along with the star anise and Sichuan peppercorns. Cook, stirring, for about 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the stir through ½ the crispy shallots.

Add the chicken thighs to the pan and pour over the stock. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer then pop a lid on and turn the heat down to low. Gently poach the chicken for 10-20 mins (depending on the thickness of the thighs) until cooked through.
Meanwhile, remove the cavolo nero stems and tear the greens into bite-sized chunks. Set aside.
When the chicken is cooked through, remove it from the stock and place on a chopping board. Allow it to cool slightly before shredding.
Add the cavolo nero greens to the stock, turn the heat up to medium-high and cook for 2-4 mins until wilted. Remove from the heat and taste and season the stock with salt, sugar and white pepper.
In the meantime, reheat your cooked rice.
Share the rice between bowls and ladle over the fragrant broth. Top with the greens and shredded chicken. Finish with a scattering of the remaining crispy shallots and sambal or chilli oil.

name: Chicken & Harissa Meatball Flatbreads
description: Spicy, juicy meatballs on a swirl of harissa yoghurt, topped with a lemony cucumber salad and scooped up with warm flatbread.
instructions: Finely slice the cucumber and toss it with a good pinch of salt in a colander. Leave to sit for 10 mins to draw out some of the water, then give it a squeeze to remove any excess moisture.
Chuck the chicken mince into a bowl with half the harissa. Season well with salt and pepper. Shape the mixture into 10 meatballs about the size of walnuts.
Heat a large nonstick frying pan over a medium heat and give it a spritz of olive oil. Add the meatballs and fry for 8–10 mins, turning regularly, until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer the cucumber to a bowl. Zest over the lemon and squeeze in the juice. Pick in the dill leaves, season with black pepper and toss to combine.
Finely slice the remaining red pepper, discarding any seeds, and toss it through the cucumber salad.
Dollop the yoghurt onto serving plates and ripple through the remaining harissa. Pile the meatballs on top, then spoon over the cucumber salad.
Toast the flatbread, cut into triangles and serve on the side for scooping.

name: Chicken & Herb Salad with Steamed Rice
description: A fresh, zesty chicken salad packed with herbs and a punchy Thai-inspired dressing. The crispy chicken skin and toasted rice powder take it to the next level. Serve with fragrant jasmine rice for a satisfying meal.
keywords: Chicken & Herb Salad with Steamed Rice
Chicken & Herb Salad with Steamed Rice recipe
instructions: Set aside ⅒ of the rice for the toasted rice powder (if using). Cook the remaining rice following packet instructions.

Season the chicken thighs with salt and black pepper on both sides. Place them skin-side down in a cold frying pan, then set over a medium heat. Cook for 5-7 mins until the fat has rendered and the skin is golden and crisp. Flip and cook for another 2-3 mins or until cooked through. Set aside to rest for at least 3 mins.
For the salad, pick and roughly chop the mint and coriander leaves. Thinly slice the banana shallot and spring onion. Julienne the cucumber into thin matchsticks.

To make the toasted rice powder (if using), add the reserved raw jasmine rice to a dry frying pan and toast over a high heat for 2 mins, moving the pan constantly to prevent burning. Once lightly golden, transfer to a pestle and mortar or spice grinder and grind into a coarse powder.

For the dressing, mix the fish sauce, palm sugar and chilli flakes together in a bowl. Squeeze in the juice of ⅔ of the lime, setting aside the remaining lime for garnish. Stir well until the sugar dissolves.

Slice the rested chicken into 1cm strips. Add to a large bowl along with the mint, coriander, banana shallot, spring onion, cucumber and toasted rice powder, if using. Pour over the dressing and toss well.
Cut the remaining lime into wedges and serve up with the chicken, rice and fresh herb salad.

name: Chicken & Herby Pepper Couscous
description: This one's made with leftovers from out Roast Chicken & Peppers batch, with a simple salad with giant couscous and fresh veggies. Healthy, high-protein, and a clever use of leftover chicken.
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken & Peppers.
Cook the couscous according to package instructions.
Finely mince the parsley. Zest the lemon into the yoghurt, season with salt and stir together.
Stir through the parsley, and veggies from the roast chicken into the couscous. Juice the lemon in and toss together with some of the roast juices. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Reheat the chicken in the microwave until hot. If you don’t have a microwave tip the chicken onto a baking tray and roast at 220°C until hot, 5-10 mins.
Share the lemon yoghurt between plates, top with the chicken and serve with the couscous.

name: Chicken & Pancetta Tortelloni With Red Romesco & Oregano
description: A homemade red romesco sauce and La Famiglia Rana Chicken & Pancetta Tortelloni make a dream team in this speedy recipe. It's about texture as much as taste
ingredients: 250g La Famiglia Rana Chicken & Pancetta Tortelloni
instructions: Start by peeling and finely dicing the onion and the garlic.

In a medium frying pan, add the peeled and finely diced onion with 1 tbsp of olive oil and fry on a medium heat for 5-8 mins until soft and a little caramelised. Add the finely chopped garlic and fry for a further minute until just cooked and fragrant.

Drain the jarred peppers and add them to a high speed blender with the caramelised onions and garlic, fresh oregano, tomato purée, the remaining 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil and salt and pepper and blitz until you have a smooth sauce.

Bring a large pot of water to the boil, then add in the La Famiglia Rana Chicken & Pancetta Tortellini to cook for just 2 mins before draining. Add the romesco into the pan with the cooked pasta and give it a toss so it is all coated.
Portion into bowls and serve with the herbs and the Parmesan and a little more salt and pepper to finish.

name: Chicken & Parmesan 'Caesar' Wrap
description: Everybody’s favourite salad in wrap form… you’re welcome! This tastes sensational and makes the perfect high-protein lunch.
instructions: Slice the chicken into thin strips, transfer to a bowl and add both the chargrilled chicken seasoning and the garlic Italian seasoning.
Roughly chop the lettuce. Finely grate the Parmesan.

Spray a non-stick frying pan with the oil over a high heat, then add the chicken strips. Leave to turn nice and golden on one side, then flip. Meanwhile, combine all the caesar dressing ingredients in a bowl and set aside.

Toss the salad into the dressing. Heat the wrap for 10-15 seconds in the microwave to make it more flexible. Layer the chicken into the centre of the wrap, followed by the lettuce, parmesan and cheese mix.
Fold either side in, flattening the mixture down a bit, then flip the wrap over the filling, tuck it under and roll it up.

Give the frying pan you used for the chicken a quick wipe (no need to clean properly), then add some more oil spray to the pan. Pop the wrap on top for a few minutes over a medium heat until it starts to go crispy.
Once golden and crispy, wrap in foil and enjoy!

name: Chicken & Pineapple Chopped Salad
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This hybrid recipe is a tasty combination of our chipotle pineapple traybake with our chicken and broccoli chopped salad.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Add the broccoli and cook for 3-4 mins until bright green but still with a little bite. Remove and set aside to cool.
Place the chicken breasts onto a baking tray, season generously with salt and pepper and cook in the oven for 25 mins. Allow them to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm.
While the chicken is cooking, heat up the rice following pack instructions. Set aside.
For the dressing, squeeze the lime juice into a bowl or jar and add the oil, chilli paste and honey. Season with salt and whisk together until thickened.

Put the lettuce, broccoli, chicken and coriander onto a board and chop it all up. Add the avocado and chop again. Tip everything into a large bowl, then add the rice and pineapple chunks and the dressing. Give it a good toss and serve on plates with a wedge of lime.

name: Chicken & Red Rice Burrito Bowl
description: This one has everything: perfectly cooked chicken, a satisfying rice base and fresh zingy veggie toppings. Enjoy it hot for dinner then eat the leftovers hot or cold for lunch the next day.
keywords: Chicken & Red Rice Burrito Bowl recipe
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions. Slice the chicken thighs into quarters lengthways. Peel and finely slice two of the onions, and finely dice the remaining one.

Add the chicken and the sliced onions to a large bowl with the chipotle paste, garlic powder, oregano, ground cumin and olive oil. Season well with salt and mix to combine. Spread evenly on an oven tray, then slide under the grill on the top shelf for 15-20 mins, turning halfway, until cooked through.

Finely shred the cabbage. Slice the avocado. Roughly chop the coriander and mix with the diced onion in a small bowl. Quarter the cherry tomatoes and toss with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt.

If batch cooking, transfer the different components (chicken, rice, onion-coriander mix, cabbage slaw and seasoned tomatoes) to separate containers and store in the fridge. Enjoy cold or reheat the chicken and rice until piping hot before serving.

To serve, spoon the rice into bowls, then top with chicken and the cabbage slaw. Then sprinkle over the onion-coriander mix. Finish with the tomatoes, crumble over the feta, and serve with lime wedges, sliced avo and hot sauce.

name: Chicken & Rice Salad with Sticky Honey & Gochujang Dressing
description: Shredded roast chicken, fluffy rice and crunchy veg tossed in our fave Sticky Honey Gochujang Dressing. Big, bold flavours and perfect for make-ahead lunches.
keywords: chicken and rice salad with sticky honey & gochujang dressing
easy lunch to take to work
