instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add the chicken breasts to a baking tray, drizzle with the olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Roast for 20 minutes, until cooked through, then remove and leave to cool slightly before shredding into bite-sized pieces.

Bring a pan of well-salted water to the boil. Halve the tenderstem broccoli and cook for 4 minutes, until just tender. Drain and leave to steam dry and cool. Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Halve the cucumber lengthways and cut into chunky, irregular pieces. Roughly crush the peanuts. Pick the coriander and mint leaves.

Now for the dressing. Peel and finely grate in the garlic into a bowl, then add the honey, gochujang, rice vinegar, sesame oil, soy sauce, water and sesame seeds. Whisk until everything's smooth and glossy.

Add the chicken, rice, broccoli, cucumber, herbs and peanuts to a large bowl. Pour over the dressing and toss everything together until well coated. Taste and season with a little salt if needed, then serve.

name: Chicken & Rice with Peanut Curry Sauce
description: A rich and flavourful chicken and rice dish with a creamy peanut curry sauce. Balanced with fresh lime, crispy onions, and cavolo nero, this meal is perfect for prepping ahead.
keywords: Chicken & Rice with Peanut Curry Sauce
Chicken & Rice with Peanut Curry Sauce recipe
instructions: In a bowl, mix the chicken thighs with half the garlic (peeled and bashed) and the kecap manis. Season with salt and black pepper, then set aside to marinate.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan with high sides over medium heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken and fry for 10-12 mins, turning occasionally, until cooked through and slightly charred. If your sauce is reducing too much turn the heat down to low. Transfer to a plate to rest.
Strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stems.
In the same pan, add the cavolo nero leaves and cook until wilted. Transfer to the chicken plate.
Add the remaining bashed garlic, red Thai curry paste, tomato purée, and peanut butter to the empty pan. Cook, stirring, for 2-3 mins until the mixture darkens in colour.
Pour in the coconut milk and cook, stirring, until the sauce thickens. Remove from heat and season with salt, lime juice, and a touch of sugar if needed.
Reheat the rice and divide it into serving boxes. Slice the chicken thighs and place them on top with the cavolo nero. Pour over the peanut curry sauce.
Garnish with crispy onions and fresh coriander. Box up and refrigerate until needed. Reheat before serving.

name: Chicken & Ricotta Meatballs With Green Spaghetti
description: Soft and fluffy chicken meatballs in a bright green tangle of spaghetti. This ain't your mama's spaghetti and meatballs recipe. It's Sophie Wyburd's – so, it's a lot better.
keywords: Chicken & Ricotta Meatballs With Green Spaghetti
Chicken & Ricotta Meatballs With Green Spaghetti recipe
instructions: Chop the chicken thigh fillets into pieces, then transfer to a food processor. Zest in the lemon, then add half of the ricotta, a pinch of salt, and 15 twists of black pepper. Pulse until you have a smooth paste. Grate in a third of the Parmesan, add the breadcrumbs, then finely chop the parsley and add that, too. Give it a stir so it’s all combined.
Roll the mixture into even-sized balls. Pop on a baking tray and transfer to the fridge. Chill for 15 mins to firm up.

Meanwhile, give your food processor a good clean, then add the watercress, basil, sunflower seeds, peeled garlic clove and remaining 50g Parmesan. Whizz to form a smooth green paste, then drizzle in the olive oil so that you have a smooth sauce. Squeeze in the juice from the zested ½ lemon and add the remaining ricotta, pulse the machine briefly, then season with salt.
Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Season it with salt as though it were a soup you were about to eat.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large sauté pan over a medium heat. Add the chilled meatballs to the pan and cook for about 10 mins, turning them frequently so that they cook evenly and take on some colour.
Meanwhile, add the spaghetti to the pan of boiling water. Cook the pasta for a couple of minutes less than pack instructions, or until it is just al dente.

Once cooked, transfer the spaghetti directly into the meatball pan using tongs, along with a ladleful of the pasta cooking water. Add the pesto to the pan and give it a good toss, so each strand of spaghetti is coated in the green sauce. Add as much pasta water as you need to get the sauce glossy. Adjust the seasoning if needed.
Divide the spaghetti and meatballs between plates. Serve sprinkled with extra Parmesan.

name: Chicken & Roasted Mushroom Hummus
description: This hearty chicken grain bowl with roasted mushroom hummus and fresh herbs is as delicious as it is healthy. It’s perfect for meal prep: eat it hot and fresh for dinner, then serve it cold as a shredded chicken salad for lunch the next day.
keywords: Chicken & Roasted Mushroom Hummus Bowl Recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Make sure your butter is in the fridge.
Slice the mushrooms into 1cm thick slices and place them onto one half of a baking tray with a drizzle of oil. Season with salt and pepper.

Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then place them skin side down into a frying pan. Set the pan over a medium-high heat and cook for 10-15 mins until the skin turns golden brown. Transfer the thighs, skin side up, to the empty part of the mushroom tray (keep the pan, don't wash it). Slide into the oven to roast for 20-25 mins, until golden brown and the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, pick the mint, dill and parsley leaves. Discard the mint stems and thinly slice the dill and parsley stalks. Add the leaves and stalks into a bowl of ice water.

Once the mushrooms are roasted, get them into a food processor with the hummus and miso and blitz together until smooth and incorporated. Or, use a sharp knife to finely mince the mushrooms by hand then transfer to a bowl and stir through the hummus and miso. Add a splash of water if it's too thick.

Tip all the juices from the chicken and mushroom tray into the empty frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Bring the juices to the boil then turn the heat down and stir through the cold butter. Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper, if needed. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of water.
Drain and dry the herbs then toss them with a drizzle of olive oil.

Reheat the grains and serve them up along one side of each plate. Spread a dollop of mushroom hummus over the other side of the plate then top with the chicken thighs and herb salad. Finish with a wedge of lemon.

name: Chicken & Sweetcorn Egg Drop Soup
description: Chicken and sweetcorn soup is an absolute classic. Adding a wispy egg to this chicken and sweetcorn soup recipe gives it a lovely velvety texture. You're going to love it.
keywords: Chicken & Sweetcorn Egg Drop Soup recipe
instructions: Wash your chicken by soaking it in a large bowl of cold salty water – the amount of salt needed is the same as you'd use when seasoning pasta water. Set aside until needed.

Roughly dice half of your corn into a rough mince then set aside. Slice the ginger into three pieces and cut the spring onion green tops off and remove any roots. Finely slice all the spring greens for garnishing, then set aside.

Put 1 tbsp oil, the ginger and just the spring onion whites into a large saucepan. Cook for 2-3 mins or until lightly charred. Add the chicken stock, soy sauce, turmeric, white pepper, honey, the minced and remaining sweetcorn and the chicken, skin-side down. Bring to the boil for 1 min and use a spoon to remove the scum on the surface. Reduce to the lowest heat then simmer for 15 mins, with a lid on.
Whisk the eggs and turmeric with a pinch of salt in a small jug and set aside. Combine the cornstarch slurry ingredients in a small cup and set aside.
Remove the chicken from the pan and rest on a plate loosely covered. Discard the spring onion and ginger.

Bring the soup to the boil and stir the cornstarch slurry well before pouring it into the soup. Allow to boil for 2 mins to thicken, then reduce to the lowest heat and immediately drizzle in the whisked egg in circular motions. Use a spatula to gently swirl the soup, and cook for 2 mins.
Add a tsp of sesame oil and squeeze in half a lemon.
Slice the chicken and pour any resting juices back into the soup. Serve the soup into bowls, then add the chicken and pile the spring onion into the centre. Finish with chilli oil and a lemon wedge.

name: Chicken & Tomato Grain Bowl
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

High in fibre, protein, and vitamins, this chicken and tomato grain bowl is the ultimate summer recipe.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Place a frying pan over high heat. Once hot, add the corn and cook until the corn starts to char. Transfer to a board, let it cool then slice the kernels off.

Return the pan to medium-high with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the chicken, skin-side down and cook until golden brown, 5-7 mins. Transfer to a tray, skin side up and roast for 15-20 mins, until fully cooked.
Chop the tomatoes into chunky 2cm pieces, add into a bowl with the corn, basil, anchovies, a sprinkle of salt and the balsamic, mix, set aside.
Reheat the quinoa.
Share the quinoa between bowls. Toss the basil leaves through the tomato salad. Top the quinoa and add the chicken thighs.

name: Chicken 61
description: This Chicken 61 recipe from Chapati Club is their take on the classic Chicken 65 recipe. It's a saucy, complex, and tender chicken curry.
instructions: Peel the garlic and ginger and finely chop or blitz in a food processor. Put aside.
Dice your chicken breast. Dice your onion.
Heat a large saucepan, add oil. When the oil has heated up, add cloves, mustard seeds, and cumin seeds.
Add the diced onion, ginger and garlic and mix well. Cook until it all softens and the base is golden brown.
Add the tomatoes and heat through for 1 minute. Lid on.
Add the chilli powder, ground turmeric, garam masala, ground cumin, ground coriander and a pinch of salt. Mix and heat through on a low heat with the lid on for 10 mins.
Add the chicken. Mix well and leave on a low heat with the lid on for around 15 mins, until the chicken is tender.
Remove from heat, garnish with the chopped coriander. Serve with rice or chapatis.

name: Chicken Adobo
description: Tender, juicy chicken thighs in a soy, garlic and black pepper marinade, served with steamed rice and zingy papaya pickles. This low-effort Filipino chicken adobo takes chicken and rice to another level.
instructions: Mince your garlic and add to your bowl of chicken along with the rice wine vinegar, light soy sauce, black peppercorns and bay leaves. Mix well and set aside to marinate in the fridge for at least 30 mins.

Meanwhile, prep the pickles. In a small pan, heat the vinegar, sugar, salt and black peppercorns over a medium heat. Let it simmer until the sugar dissolves then remove from the hob and set aside to cool. Thinly slice the papaya, carrot and red pepper and place in a jar.

On medium-high heat, add the vegetable oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Remove as much excess marinating liquid as possible from the chicken and set it aside for later. Place the chicken thighs skin-side down in the pan and fry for 3 mins on each side until golden brown.

Add the remaining marinating liquid to the pan with the chicken, including the bay leaves and black peppercorns. Add the water and sugar and mix to combine. Bring to a boil then turn the heat down to low and cook for 25 mins, flipping the chicken halfway through.
Meanwhile, add the cooled pickling liquid to the jar with the papaya, carrot and red pepper and set aside.

Wash your rice three times until the water runs clear then transfer to a medium saucepan and add enough water to reach just below your first knuckle. Bring to the boil over a medium-high heat then turn the heat down to low, cover with a lid and cook for 12 mins.
Thinly slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the chicken thighs and adobo sauce. Serve with the pickles, sliced spring onions and some crispy chilli oil if you like.

name: Chicken And Chorizo Paella Recipe
description: A Spanish holiday classic, packed full of crispy chicken and chorizo pieces and tender, glossy saffron-yellow rice. This chicken and chorizo paella recipe is one of a kind. Brimming with the rich tastes of Spanish cuisine, this simple recipe combines succulent chicken and smoky chorizo, creating a hearty and satisfying meal. The traditional sofrito base, featuring garlic and red peppers, infuses the dish with depth and warmth. Saffron and paprika add a beautiful golden hue and aromatic essence. This chicken and chorizo paella can be easily prepared in a large paella pan or a sturdy skillet, making it perfect for family dinners or gatherings. Garnished with fresh lemon wedges and paired with a crisp salad, this dish will transport you to the sunny streets of Spain. Whether you're a seasoned cook or new to Spanish recipes, this paella is a killer addition to your culinary repertoire.
instructions: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and season really well with salt and black pepper. Run a knife down the chorizo ring on a clean chopping board, then peel and discard the papery skin. Cut into 2cm chunks. Finely chop the onion, then finely chop the garlic cloves. Deseed and chop the peppers into 2cm pieces.

Put a splash of olive oil into a large (30cm), lidded deep frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the chorizo pieces and fry for 3-4 mins until the chorizo is crisp and has rendered some of its fat into the pan. Use a slotted spoon to scoop the chorizo out onto a plate.
Turn the heat to high and add the chicken pieces to the same pan. Fry for 5-6 mins, stirring occasionally, until caramelised. Scoop out onto the chorizo plate.

Turn the heat down to medium and scrape in the onion and pepper pieces along with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, for 8-10 mins until the onion has softened. Add the garlic, paprika and saffron and cook for 2 mins while stirring.

Tip the rice into the pan and mix really well so all the grains are coated in the lovely oil. Add the chorizo and chicken pieces, then pour in the chicken stock. Bring to the boil, season with salt and pepper and reduce the heat to low-medium. Put on the lid and simmer for 20 mins.

Add the peas to the pan and gently stir – most of the water should have been absorbed by now. Turn the heat to medium, leave the lid off and cook for a final 5 mins. There is no need to stir. The peas will defrost and the bottom should start to get a little crisp.
To serve, scatter over the parsley leaves and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing over.

name: Chicken Bhuna
description: Forget the takeaway. This chicken bhuna recipe is all you need for a filling, fiery weeknight dinner.
instructions: Grate a large thumb of ginger. Finely chop your cloves of garlic, green chillies and brown onions.
Fry the garlic, green chillies and ginger in a pan for 1 minute. Add your chopped onions and fry on a medium heat until soft.
Add your cumin, ground coriander, garam masala and turmeric. Then, add your diced chicken thighs.
Once the meat has browned add the tins of chopped or plum tomatoes. Fill the empty tins halfway with water and pour that into the curry.
Turn the curry onto a medium heat, and let it bubble away for 15 minutes, or until it is thick and the chicken is cooked through.
Serve on steaming hot basmati rice. Enjoy!

name: Chicken Burrito Bowls
description: Juicy taco-spiced chicken, beans and rice, topped with salsa, lettuce, tortilla chips and chipotle yoghurt. A proper family dinner winner.
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsChop the tomatoes. Set aside a portion for the kids. For the adults, pick and chop most of the coriander (save a few leaves for garnish) and toss with the remaining tomatoes, the juice of half the lime and half of the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, this is your salsa.
In a bowl, mix three-quarters of the yoghurt with the juice of the remaining half lime. Ripple through the chipotle paste to make your chipotle yoghurt. Then shred your lettuce and set aside.

Slice the chicken into 1cm-thick strips and toss with the taco seasoning. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry the chicken for 4 mins, stirring occasionally, then turn the heat down, cover and cook for another 5 mins, stirring a couple of times, until cooked through. Remove to a plate to rest.
In the same pan, add the beans (liquid and all) and cook until bubbling. Reheat your rice according to pack instructions.

Serve up!Kids Plate: Serve the rice and chicken with a side of black beans, chopped tomatoes, tortilla chips and a dollop of plain yoghurt.Parents Plate: Fill bowls with rice, chicken, black beans and salsa. Add tortilla chips and shredded lettuce, then drizzle with chipotle yoghurt. Garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Chicken Cacciatore Pasta
description: One thing we always think when we eat a Cacciatore - how do we mop up the sauce? This dish solves that - the pasta soaks up all the tomatoey juices. Divine.
instructions: Add your flour onto a plate with a pinch of salt. Turn the chicken thighs in the flour, ensuring both sides are fully covered. Shake off any excess flour and set aside for frying.
Heat 3 tbsp of olive oil in a large frying pan on medium-high heat. Add the chicken to the pan skin side down. Fry the chicken pieces on both sides for about 10 minutes, until golden brown.

While the chicken cooks, dice the onion, carrots, and celery. Cut the peppers into large chunks and slice the garlic. Once the chicken has been fried on both sides, remove from the pan, set aside and season with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Add all of the chopped vegetables to the pan, used to cook the chicken, with a drizzle of olive oil. Sauté the vegetables for 5 minutes or until they have slightly softened, and then re-add the chicken thighs.

Add two large sprigs of rosemary to the pan with the wine and chopped tomatoes. Stir to combine the vegetables and chicken with the sauce. Add the olives with a big pinch of salt and pepper and stir. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Get your penne pasta on. Salt the water and cook according to pack instructions.
Chop up your parsley and add to the pan, saving a small amount for garnish. Mix together.
Once the pasta is done, add it to your chicken and mix thoroughly.
Serve it up with a sprinkling of parsley and tuck into this delicious dish. Enjoy!

name: Chicken Caesar Chopped Salad
description: A simple chopped salad inspired by the greatest salad of all time – the chicken caesar.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Put the two chicken breasts on a tray and drizzle with a little olive oil. Season well and slide into the oven and bake for 20 mins, until cooked through. Set aside until cool.
Tear the bread into chunky croutons, whack on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Slide into the oven for 15 mins.
Bring a pan of salted water to the boil, drop in the Tenderstem broccoli and cook for 2 mins, then remove and set aside on a plate to cool.

Add the romaine lettuce halves to a board with the cooked chicken, Tenderstem broccoli and parmesan cheese. Chop together, then slide into a large bowl. Combine the dressing ingredients, then add the croutons and capers and drizzle with the dressing. Toss well then tip onto plates. Top with an extra grating of parmesan cheese.

name: Chicken Caesar Pasta Salad
description: All the flavours of a chicken Caesar salad, but in the form of a pasta salad. You're going to love this one. It's creamy, filling, and extremely moreish.
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Heat a splash of oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the chicken thighs for about 6-8 mins per side, or until fully cooked and golden brown. Remove from the skillet and let them rest for a few minutes before shredding. Set aside in the fridge to cool completely.
Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the spirali pasta according to the package instructions, then drain and rinse with cold water to cool it down quickly, tip into a large bowl.
Slice the cucumber into thin rounds or half-moons. Chop the parsley. Slice the spring onions. Slice the gem lettuces into 3cm wide strips.

Make the dressing. In a blender or food processor, combine the mayonnaise, tin of anchovies (with oil), Parmesan, Dijon mustard, and the juice of the lemon. Blend until smooth. If the dressing is too thick, you can add a bit of water or more lemon juice to loosen a little, season well with salt and pepper.

In a large bowl, combine the cooked pasta, sliced chicken, cucumber, chopped parsley, spring onions, and chopped gem lettuces. Use a peeler to shave in the Parmesan, saving a little to grate over the top.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss everything together until well combined. Spoon the salad into bowls, and grate extra Parmesan over the top.

name: Chicken Caesar Sandwich
description: Crispy smokey bacon and delicious, golden, tender rosemary-ey chicken thighs. The freshest Dijon + L&Ps + mayo + Parmesan + cornichon sauce. A straight 10/10.
instructions: Debone the chicken, tear away any excess fat (but keep the skin on), and place the thighs into a bowl. Grate the garlic and add in along with 4 tbsp Worcester sauce, 1 level tbsp mustard, salt, pepper, and rub altogether. Cover and leave to marinate for 30 minutes.

Sauce time. Thinly chop your cornichons and finely grate the parmesan. Add into a bowl with the mayo, 1 1/2 tbsp Worcester sauce, 1 1/2 tbsp mustard, salt, and pepper. Mix, squeeze in the juice of half a lemon and keep in the fridge until serving time.
Get a non-stick pan on a medium heat. Add in your bacon and fry. Cooking on a medium heat will allow the fat to render out.

Once crispy, move the bacon to the edge of the pan and place the marinated chicken thighs into the middle, skin side down. Fry for 4-5 minutes until the skin is nice and golden and then turn. Fry for another 3 minutes and set aside.
Finely chop the rosemary and add it into the pan. Fry for a couple of minutes then remove the chicken and bacon from the heat and cover until serving. Leave the juices in the pan.
Slice the ciabatta rolls in half and place face down in the pan with the leftover meat juices on a high heat. Fry for 2-3 minutes until golden brown.
Whilst the ciabatta is toasting, slice the remaining veg - lettuce and tomato.

Time to layer up. Spread the caesar sauce on the bottom bun, add a few lettuce leaves, a slice of tomato, 3 rashers of bacon, and 2 chicken thighs. Spread another layer of caesar sauce on the top bun and place the lid on. Take a bite and enjoy!

name: Chicken Caesar Toast
description: Let’s be honest here, the croutons are the best part of a chicken caesar salad. So we've made a massive one, and whacked the salad on top.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C, tip the chicken thighs into a roasting tin, cover with foil and roast for 30-40 mins, until cooked through.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Finely chop or blitz the anchovies then add to a bowl with the dijon and juice of half a lemon. Stir in the mayonnaise, and finely grate the parmesan into the bowl. Season well with salt and pepper, adding more lemon juice to taste. Loosen with a little water if it feels particularly thick.

Make the giant croutons. Slice the sourdough into chunky slices. Finely slice the garlic cloves. Add 2-3 tbsp of olive oil to a frying pan over a medium heat, add the sliced garlic and fry for around 3 mins, until crisp, remove the crispy garlic with a spoon, trying to avoid taking too much oil with it! Add the slices of bread, two at a time and fry for 2-3 mins on each side, until golden and crisp, set aside on a plate or cooling rack.
Shred the romaine and add it to a large bowl.

Once the chicken is cooked, remove from the oven and set aside to cool, then shred and add the bowl of lettuce along with the capers. Drizzle half the dressing into the bowl of lettuce and chicken and toss well. Add a giant crouton onto each plate, then top with the salad. Finish with a scattering of extra parmesan, and a crack of black pepper. Zest the lemon over the top, then slice into wedges to serve on the side. Finish each with a few slices of crispy garlic and a drizzle of the dressing on top.

name: Chicken Chasseur
description: This saucy classic of French cuisine is packed full of flavour and couldn’t be easier to make. We’ve opted for skin-on chicken breasts for this version of the dish, but you can make it with chicken legs or thighs, too.
instructions: Thickly slice the mushrooms then scrape into a bowl. Halve and finely chop the onion, then peel and finely chop the garlic. Peel and cut the potatoes into quarters, put them into a large saucepan and cover with cold, salted water. Bring to the boil for later on.
Season the chicken breasts really well with salt and pepper all over. Pour a splash of olive oil into a large, deep frying pan and set over a medium-high heat.
Once hot, lay the chicken into the pan, skin-side down. Fry for 3-4 mins until golden and crisp, then remove from the pan onto a plate.
Pour a glug of oil into the pan and add the mushroom slices. Fry for 5-6 mins until all of the water has evaporated and the mushrooms are caramelising.

Reduce the heat to medium and scrape in the onion along with a pinch of salt. Strip all of the leaves from the thyme sprigs and add to the pan, too. Cook, stirring, for 7-8 mins until the onion has softened.
Add in the garlic and cook for a couple of minutes, stirring every now and again. Pour in the white wine and bubble for a few minutes before pouring in the chopped tomatoes and chicken stock.
Bring up to the boil, reduce to a simmer and cook gently for 20 mins.

Add your peeled potatoes to the pot of boiling water and cook for 10-15 mins until the potatoes are tender. Drain the potatoes and steam-dry for a couple of minutes, before mashing until smooth. Add the butter and mash, pour the milk in slowly until you have your preferred consistency.
Put the chicken into the pan, skin-side up, and simmer for 12 mins until the sauce has thickened and the chicken is cooked through.
Scatter with the parsley leaves and serve with mash.

name: Chicken Chimichurri Traybake
description: This dish is really easy to make. While the chicken and peas are roasting, get on with prepping the spicy chimichurri. After that, you’re basically done. Easy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Take ¼ of your lemons and cut it into slices. Trim and halve the radishes. Finely slice the garlic. Finely chop the parsley (stalks and leaves).

Add a glug of olive oil into a large oven-proof frying pan off the heat. Lay the chicken skin-side down and season with salt. Place over a medium-high heat and fry until the skin turns golden, 4-5 mins. Remove from the heat. Transfer the chicken onto a plate.

Add the lemon slices, garlic, and radishes into the chicken pan, stirring to coat in the chicken fat, then nestle the chicken thighs back in, skin-side up. Drizzle with some more olive oil, season with salt and roast in the oven for 20-25 mins, until fully cooked.

For the chimichurri, trim and finely chop the chilli. Pick the mint leaves and finely chop. Add the chilli, mint and ½ the parsley into a bowl with the juice of the remaining lemons and the olive oil (the full amount listed in the ingredients list). Season with salt, pepper, and some sugar if needed. Set aside.
Lift the chicken out and set aside on a plate. Remove the slices of lemon. Stir in the frozen peas and cooked brown rice and roast for another 3-5 mins, until piping hot.
Stir the remaining parsley through the rice and spoon onto plates, top each with two thighs, then drizzle the chimmichurri all over.

name: Chicken Chow Mein
description:
If you think you can only get a great chow mein at your local Chinese takeout, think again. This homemade chicken chow mein bangs, bringing all the savoury goodness of Cantonese cooking right to your kitchen. Inspired by the flavours of traditional chǎomiàn (炒面), this dish is ridiculously simple to make, using classic stir-frying techniques to give the noodles that authentic wok hei taste. Stir-fried chicken thighs, fresh green onions, crunchy water chestnuts, and bamboo shoots come together for a dish that rivals any dim sum restaurant.

You can customize your chow mein by adding bok choy or tofu for a veggie twist, or spice it up with a little chili sauce. Serve it as part of a larger Chinese meal, perhaps alongside dim sum or sweet and sour pork, for a real restaurant experience at home. With just a few steps, you'll master one of the most beloved Chinese dishes around.
instructions: Make your Chow Mein Sauce. Grab a bowl. Add 1 tbsp of cornflour and soy sauce. Mix them together until the cornflour is fully absorbed. Add the oyster sauce, vinegar and sugar. Mix everything together until you have a nice smooth sauce. Set aside.
Prep your veg - chop your mangetout, peppers and spring onions into matchsticks, and slice your garlic finely.
Cook your egg noodles. Once ready, drain and leave in a bowl of cold water, ready for the wok.
Dice up your chicken breasts into bite-size strips.
Crack your eggs into a bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Beat everything together. Add 8 tablespoons of cornflour into another bowl. Dip the chicken in the egg and then in the flour.
Add the chicken to a wok with a splash of vegetable oil. Once all the chicken is cooked, set it aside. Remove the wok from the heat, wipe it down and place it back on the cooker.
Chow Mein cooking time. This is a quick process so you want everything prepared and ready by your wok.

Get the wok on a high heat. Add a splash of oil followed by your pepper, mangetout, carrots and spring onions. Fry for 4 minutes until they start to char and then add your garlic. Mix it in, add your chicken and your sauce. Toss everything together and cook for 2 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
At this point, add your noodles. Toss everything together. Serve the Chow Mein in a bowl. Top with some sliced spring onions and a small splash of soy sauce. Enjoy.

name: Chicken Curry Gyros
description: A bit of a mash up, but these Indian flavours work beautifully in a warm pitta. The cooling salsa over the sizzling chicken. Mmmmmmmmm.
instructions: Place your chicken thighs in a bowl. Add hot chilli powder, ground coriander, garam masala and 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Add yogurt. Season with salt and pepper. Mix in thoroughly. Leave to marinate for 25 minutes.

Meanwhile, make your green sauce. Get a blender and add a garlic clove, the juice of a lime, a small bunch of fresh mint, a large bunch of fresh coriander and a large green chilli. Whizz it up with a bit of water until smooth.
Finely chop your red onion and add to a bowl. Squeeze the juice of one lemon over the top. Add a generous pinch of sea salt. This will lightly pickle the onions.
Roughly chop some tomatoes and half a cucumber. Add to a bowl with salt and some leftover mint and coriander.
Pan fry the marinated chicken until cooked through.
Warm your pittas.
Once the chicken is cooked remove from the heat. Open your pittas and stuff with the chicken, the green sauce, the salad and some extra yogurt on top. Enjoy!

name: Chicken Curry Pie
description: It’s one of the nation's favourite meals... but in a pie! We've made a coconutty chicken curry and wrapped it with a super-easy, crispy rough puff pastry.
instructions: Dice your butter into small cubes and put them in the freezer for 15 mins.

Then add your flour, cold butter, salt, sugar and nigella seeds to a processor and pulse until you form a coarse crumb. Chuck into a bowl and add the water gradually, mixing in with a spatula until combined into a shaggy dough. Using your hands pack together as quickly as possible, tip out onto a work surface and form into a large square, around 2cm thick.
Cut into 4 equal-sized pieces and stack them on top of each other. Press down to seal them together and then roll them out into a rough circle.
Wrap in cling film and put in the fridge for at least 1 hour, but preferably overnight.
Heat oven to 200°C. Peel your garlic then roughly chop the ginger, coriander stems, green chilli. Peel and chop the onion too, then add all of these aromats into blender and blitz.
Heat 2 tbsp of oil in a frying pan over a medium heat, tip in the curry paste and fry until all of the moisture has evaporated. Next, add the curry powder and cook for a further 30 seconds.
Pour in your chicken stock and coconut cream. Add the chicken thighs and make sure they are submerged in the liquid - Pop a lid on and simmer for 20 mins.
In the meantime, remove the woody ends and cut the asparagus in 2cm pieces. Roughly chop the coriander leaves.

When the chicken is cooked through, remove it from the sauce and using 2 forks shred it into chunky pieces. Make a slurry with the cornflour by mixing with 4 tbsp of cold water, and add to the sauce whilst stirring. Cook over a low heat until thickened, around 3 mins. Add the asparagus, peas, coriander and shredded chicken back into the curry sauce and mix well. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Remove from the heat to cool a little.
Back to the pastry – lightly dust your surface with flour and roll out your chilled dough into a disk about 1 cm-thick. Whisk an egg.

If your frying pan isn't already ovenproof, pour your pie filling out into an ovenproof pan or dish. Brush the edges of the pan or dish with some of the whisked egg – this will help the lid stick. Drape the pastry over the filling, trim any excess and crimp to seal using your thumb and forefingers. If this is a bit too tricky, use a fork instead. Using a sharp knife, score a cross-hatch pattern on top before cutting a small ‘x’ in the middle to let steam out. Brush liberally with half of your egg wash and pop in the oven for 20 mins. Make sure you save some egg wash for the final step.

After 20 mins, bring your pie back out and repeat the egg wash – this will give the pastry a deeply golden colour. Put back in the oven and cook for another 20-25 mins. Once cooked, allow it to stand for 15 mins before digging in.

name: Chicken Curry Traybake
description: Think of this creamy, rich and flavourful curry as a perfect curry base: incredible to eat as is but also super easy to customise by adding extra ingredients (lemongrass, lime leaves, cinnamon bark, etc.). It’s easy to make and doesn’t require hours in the kitchen, and it can be made as meal prep, for a midweek dinner or even a weekend show stopper.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Season the chicken thighs on both sides with salt and pepper and place into an ovenproof frying pan, skin side down. Set over a medium heat and cook the chicken on one side for 7-10 mins, undisturbed, until the skin turns golden brown.
Meanwhile, add all the curry sauce ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth. Peel the potatoes (optional) and chop into 5cm chunks, then transfer to a baking tray.
Once the chicken is golden, transfer them to the baking tray, nestling them on top of the potatoes and flipping them over so they’re skin side up.

Pour the curry sauce into the pan you used to cook the chicken and set it over a medium heat. Bring the mixture up to the boil then pour it into the chicken tray, over the chicken and potatoes. Slide into the oven to roast for 30-35 mins until cooked through.
Cook the rice following packet instructions. Remove the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and roughly chop.

A couple minutes before the chicken is cooked, heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan set over a medium-high heat and drop in the garlic. Cook until fragrant, then drop the greens in with a splash of water. Cover immediately with a lid and leave to cook for 2-4 mins until wilted. Remove the lid and let the water evaporate. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls. Spoon in the chicken curry and serve with a side of garlicky greens.

name: Chicken Enchiladas With Charred Corn Salsa
description: A simple recipe for chicken enchiladas that's perfect for sharing with your loved ones. Or your enemies. The choice is up to you.
keywords: Chicken Enchiladas With Charred Corn Salsa
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toast the coriander seeds and cumin seeds in a dry pan, then crush them to a powder using a pestle and mortar.
Add the chicken, crushed coriander, crushed cumin and half the smoked paprika to a bowl with a big pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Give it all a good mix.
Finely slice three-quarters of the red onions, setting aside the rest for later. Add to a roasting dish, then nestle the chicken on top. Bake for 45 mins.

Now, it’s time to make your enchilada sauce. Start by finely slicing the garlic. Melt the butter in a medium-sized saucepan, then add the tomato pureé and garlic. Cook for 2 mins, then tip in the flour and cook for 2 mins.

Add the chipotle paste and cayenne pepper to the pan with the remaining smoked paprika. Gradually pour in the chicken stock, whisking all the time until smooth before each addition. Let the mixture come to a boil, then turn down the heat and simmer for 2 mins until thickened. Season to taste with salt.
Once your chicken is done, shred it and remove the bones. Reduce any juices in the tray so that they coat the back of a spoon.

Divide the chicken between the tortillas, placing the meat in the centre of each tortilla. Roll them up like a pancake, then nestle them all into a baking dish. Pour the sauce on top, focusing on a line down the middle. You want the tortilla ends to poke out a little.
Grate the cheddar and sprinkle it on top, then cover the dish with foil and bake in the oven for 15 mins.
Finely dice the remaining red onion and green chilli, then add both to a little bowl. Squeeze over the lime, add a good pinch of salt, then give it a mix.

Pat the sweetcorn dry. Heat a large frying pan over a high heat, then add a drizzle of olive oil. Get your sweetcorn in there, then pan-fry it for 5 mins or until lightly charred. Let it cool down for a bit.
Remove the foil from the enchiladas and bake for another 10 mins.
Add the sweetcorn to your pickled onion mixture and give it a good mix.
Once your enchiladas are done, dollop over the soured cream and sprinkle over the sweetcorn salsa and some coriander leaves. Serve it up.

name: Chicken Francese
description: Juicy chicken in a bright and zesty sauce. This chicken francese recipe is an Italian classic.
instructions: Start by halving the cherry tomatoes, finely slicing the garlic and parsley and picking the basil leaves from the stalk. Add everything to a bowl and set aside. Make sure your butter is fridge-cold.
Slice the chicken breasts widthways into slices about 1.5cm thick and sprinkle them generously with salt.
Set up two plates and add the flour to one and the eggs to the other. Grate the Parmesan onto the eggs and stir well to combine.
Get a large frying pan over a medium heat and add in your olive oil.
Dust the chicken slices in flour, then into the egg mix and coat well. Transfer straight into the hot oil. Depending on the size of your pan you might need to do this in two batches.
Fry the chicken for about 3 mins and then once golden, flip and cook for another minute. Remove onto a tray.
Drain off all but a splash of the oil and add tomatoes, garlic, basil, and parsley and fry for 1 min, then add the wine and let it bubble away until reduced by ¾, then turn the heat down low.
Cut one of the lemons into 5 thin rounds and add them to the pan, then place the chicken back in and squeeze in the juice of the other lemon, along with a splash of water.

Add the cold butter in 4 or 5 chunks and swirl the pan over a low heat so that the butter emulsifies into the sauce and becomes creamy. It should be just bubbling very gently. Plate up the chicken and spoon the sauce and tomatoes over.

name: Chicken Greek Salad Traybake
description: This dish sees juicy, roasted chicken legs teamed up with olives, feta, pitta and tomatoes for a Greek-inspired take on a throw-together traybake.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Slap the chicken legs into a roasting tray and hit them with a good whack of olive oil, a pinch of salt and a crack of black pepper. Toss to coat.

Smash the garlic cloves and lob them in. Peel and cut the onions into wedges through the root, and add to the tray. Tear the pitta bread into chunks and add to the tray. Toss with a little more oil and seasoning and slide the whole lot into the oven for 35-40 mins.

While the chicken roasts, chunk up the cucumber and tomatoes and sprinkle them with salt. Let them hang out in a colander. Crumble the feta into large chunks, finely chop the parsley and take the pits out of the olives. Tip the whole lot into a big bowl with the salted veggies and toss with the vinegar, oregano and a load of olive oil.
Pull the chicken out of the oven and tip the marinated salad over top, let the pitta soak up all the juices. Serve warm.

name: Chicken Gyros Smashed Tacos
description:
All the flavours of the classic Greek staple but in smashed taco form. Crispy chicken mince-topped tortillas with a zesty tomato salad and cooling tzatziki, packed with punchy flavour.

In Partnership with Aldi #ad
instructions: Preheat the oven or air fryer according to the French fry packet instructions.
Add the chicken mince to a bowl and season generously with salt and pepper. Finely grate in the garlic and half the lemon zest, then stir through the oregano.
Portion the mince onto the tortillas and spread it from edge to edge, then set aside.

Chop the tomatoes into 2-3cm chunks, mince the olives, thinly slice the red onion and pick the parsley leaves, thinly slicing any soft stems. Add the onion to a bowl with the lemon juice, season with salt and set aside to pickle.

Set a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the tortillas mince-side down and cook for 3-4 mins, or until cooked through. Flip, transfer to a plate and cover, then continue until all the tortillas are cooked.
Meanwhile, cook the fries according to the packet instructions.
Once ready, share the tacos between plates. Toss the olives, tomatoes, parsley stems and three-quarters of the leaves together, then season with more salt and pepper, if needed.
Top the tacos with a dollop of tzatziki, some fries and the tomato salad, then cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Chicken Jalapeño Caesar High Protein Smash
description: A perfect Caesar base ideal for meal prep. Chicken, cottage cheese and Greek yoghurt make the base, anchovies and jalapeños bring the heat, and it all piles beautifully onto toasted sourdough. Yum.
instructions: Finely chop the chicken breast into small pieces so it mixes easily, then add to a large bowl along with the cottage cheese and yoghurt.

Finely chop the anchovy fillets and jalapeños and halve the cherry tomatoes. Grate the garlic and finely grate the Parmesan. Add to the bowl along with the Dijon, Worcestershire sauce, juice of the lemon and tear in the basil leaves. If you're using it, finely dice a little red onion and add that in too.
Mix everything together until creamy but still chunky. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper and stir until thick and scoopable.
Toast the sourdough, then pile the mixture generously on top and serve. Any leftovers will keep in the fridge for up to three days.

name: Chicken Jalapeño Caesar Smash Salad
description: Chicken Caesar but not as you know it. This one's loaded with punchy jalapeños that bring the heat, cottage cheese and greek yoghurt for an extra hit of protein. It's a winner.
instructions: Finely chop the chicken breast into small pieces so it mixes easily, then add to a large bowl along with the cottage cheese and yoghurt.

Finely chop the anchovy fillets and jalapeños and then halve the cherry tomatoes. Grate the garlic and finely grate the Parmesan. Add to the bowl along with the Dijon, Worcestershire sauce, juice of the lemon and tear in the basil leaves. If you're using it, finely dice a little red onion and add that in too.
Mix everything together until creamy but still chunky. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper and stir until thick and scoopable.
Add the chicken mix to a bowl with the salad leaves, fold everything together to combine and divide between bowls. Add a sprinkle of pine nuts and grate over some parmesan to finish.

name: Chicken Karaage
description: If you've never tried Japanese fried chicken, this is your chance. This chicken kaarage is juicy, crispy, and packed with umami flavouring. Tuck in.
instructions: Finely mince the ginger. Combine all the marinade ingredients into a large bowl.

Cut the chicken thighs into ¼ piece squares by slices in half then half again, to make 4 pieces with each thigh. Make sure to keep the skin on for extra crispy texture. Then transfer the chicken to the marinade. Mix well and cover, leave in the fridge for 30 mins to overnight.
Meanwhile, combine all the sesame dip ingredients in a bowl with finely sliced chives or spring onions. Then slice the lemons into wedges for garnish.
For the sesame salt, grind the toasted sesame seeds with the salt and set aside.
For the slaw: Finely shred all the cabbage using a mandoline. If you don’t have a mandoline, thinly slice the cabbage. Wash the cabbage in cold tap water and drain, then set aside.
Add the potato starch and all purpose flour to a medium-sized mixing bowl and mix well. Now remove the chicken from the fridge and mix in a whole egg, making sure to coat all the chicken.
Add the marinated chicken into the bowl of flour and evenly coat. Then, place it into your palm to lightly cup it into a ball shape. Repeat with all the pieces, set aside.

Pour the neutral oil into a medium sized pot, making sure the oil is filled ⅓ of the way up the pot. Heat the oil to 160°C for the first fry. Fry the chicken in batches, cooking them for 2 mins on each side and then flip. The chicken should be a pale golden. Remove the chicken using a spider and place onto a plate lined with kitchen paper. Repeat until all the chicken is cooked.

For the second fry: Increase the oil heat to 170°C and fry the chicken for a second time for 1-2 mins, until golden brown. Using the spider, transfer the chicken to a wire rack and sprinkle over the sesame sea salt.

Dress the cabbage with sesame oil, and salt. Massage a few spoons of the sesame dip over the cabbage. Eat with the fresh, hot Japanese-fried chicken, and the sesame dipping sauce. Serve with a slice of lemon.

name: Chicken Katsu Toast
description: If you love katsu curry, you’re gonna love it reimagined… on toast.
instructions: Lay the chicken breast between two sheets of baking paper and use a rolling pin to bash until around 1.5cm-2cm thick. Drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper.

Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a high heat. Add the bashed chicken breast and leave for 4- 5 mins, then flip over and cook for 3-4 mins further until cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside on a plate to rest.
Meanwhile, toast the toast. Tip the curry paste into a sauce pan over a medium heat and warm up. Alternatively you can heat it in a covered bowl in the microwave.

Slice the chicken breast, then slide your knife under the sliced breast and lay on the toast. Drizzle with the katsu curry sauce, then finish with the toasted sesame seeds, coriander leaves and a squeeze of lime juice to serve.

name: Chicken Kebabs with Tahini Sauce
description: Cook Mob’s perfect chicken kebab recipe: juicy marinated chicken, vibrant veggies, and a flavourful grill. This easy to make Middle Eastern-inspired grilled chicken recipe is perfect for the summer.
instructions: Dice the chicken into bite-sized pieces and tip into a bowl. Sprinkle in the cumin seeds, dried mint and 1 tbsp olive oil and season really well with salt and cracked black pepper. Mix well then leave to marinate for at least 1 hour, but overnight would be great.

Make the tahini sauce by adding the tahini to a large bowl, half and squeeze in the juice of the lemon, peel and finely grate in the garlic and add a pinch of salt and pepper. Spoon in 1-2 tbsp of cold water and whisk to a smooth, drizzle-able sauce. It will thicken slightly as it sits, so bear this in mind.
Heat your BBQ or a griddle pan over a high heat. Carefully thread the chicken pieces onto 4 metal skewers and put onto a plate.
Lay the skewers straight onto the BBQ or into the griddle pan and cook for 4-5 minutes on each side until charred and cooked through.
Serve the chicken stuffed into pitta halves with sliced tomatoes, red onion, lettuce and crumbled feta,a good spoon of the tahini sauce and an extra sprinkle of dried mint.

name: Chicken Korma with Naan Croutons
description:
Creamy, comforting chicken korma meets crispy, cumin-spiced naan croutons. Perfect for dunking, scooping or scattering over a big bowl of saucy joy.

In partnership with Patak's #ad
instructions: Very thinly slice the red onion and chuck it into a bowl. Squeeze in the juice of the lime and give it a good scrunch with your hands to quick-pickle. Set aside.

Season the chicken breasts on both sides with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp of the sunflower oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a high heat. Add the chicken and cook until the underside is super golden – about 6 mins. Transfer to a plate, golden side up.

Cut the naans into chunky crouton-sized pieces. Add them to a bowl with the cumin seeds and remaining 1 tbsp sunflower oil. Toss well to coat. Return the pan to a medium-high heat and fry the croutons in two batches for a few mins until golden and crisp. Scoop out and set aside.

Tip the korma paste pots into the same pan along with the coconut milk. Bring everything to the boil, then reduce to a simmer. Nestle the chicken back into the sauce, golden side up, and let it bubble away for 12–15 mins, until cooked through. Transfer the chicken to a plate.
Stir the spinach into the sauce until wilted. Add the chicken back in and warm through.
Serve with steamed rice, those crunchy naan croutons, a handful of coriander and your quick-pickled onion.

name: Chicken Kyiv Pasta
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Air fryer crispy chicken combined with garlicky spaghetti. This low-effort recipe has all the flavours of a chicken kyiv. Plus, twenty cloves of garlic. Yes, twenty.
instructions: Lay a chicken breast between two sheets of baking parchment or cling film. Bash with a rolling pin until about 3mm thick. Repeat with the second breast.
Tip the flour onto a tray and season with salt and pepper. Crack the eggs onto another tray, whisk, and season. On a third tray, mix the panko and seeds with salt and pepper.
Dip each chicken breast into the flour, then the egg, then the seeded breadcrumb mix, pressing to coat fully.
Place the chicken in your air fryer basket and drizzle with olive oil. Air-fry at 200°C for 6–8 mins per side, or until golden and cooked through. The internal temp should read 74°C.
While the chicken cooks, bash the garlic cloves with a rolling pin — no need to peel, the skins will be easier to remove after this.
Place a wide, deep pan over low heat and coat the base with olive oil. Add the garlic cloves and cook gently for 10 mins, stirring occasionally.
Pour in the spaghetti and chicken stock. Simmer for 12 mins, or until the stock is absorbed and the spaghetti is cooked al dente.
Stir in the butter, lemon zest, and chopped parsley. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Plate up the garlicky pasta with your crispy chicken on top and a wedge of lemon on the side.

name: Chicken Legs With Burnt Courgette & Tomato Salad
description: Marinated, grilled chicken legs served with a beautiful salad of burnt courgettes, juicy summer tomatoes, cucumbers and red onion. Clean, summer cooking.
keywords: Chicken Legs With Burnt Courgette & Tomato Salad
instructions: Light up your BBQ and once very hot, add the coriander seeds and 1 tbsp of black peppercorns to a small frying pan and toast over the fire until fragrant. Tip into a pestle and mortar and coarsely grind. Add the paprika and pul biber and mix together.
Generously season the chicken legs with fine salt and add to a bowl. Tip in the spice mix, finely grated garlic and 4 tbsp of olive oil. Cover and leave to marinate for 15-20 mins.
Meanwhile, toss the whole courgette with oil and salt and chuck onto the BBQ while it’s still ripping hot. Grill for roughly 10-11 mins until blackened all over and tender. Pull off the grill.

Roughly chop the tomatoes and cucumber, finely chop the onion and pick the herbs from the stems. Add the tomatoes and cucumbers to a large mixing bowl and season generously with salt and pepper. Add the sherry vinegar and a good glug of olive oil. Set aside.

Once the grill has cooled off a little, add the chicken legs, skin side down and cook for roughly 7-8 mins or, until the skin is charred and gnarly. Flip over the chicken and cook flesh side down for another 11-12 mins until cooked through. You can turn as you go if the skin needs a bit more love.
Finish the salad by roughly chopping the courgettes and stirring through the marinated tomatoes and cucumbers. Add most of the whole herbs, crumble in the feta and check the seasoning.

Pull the chicken off the grill and add a little olive oil and lemon juice. Allow to rest for 5-6 mins. Serve the chicken to share with any resting juices, extra lemon wedges and the remaining herbs. Serve the salad on the side.

name: Chicken Massaman Curry
description: A classic Thai chicken and potato curry. Mildly spicy and full of flavour with lemongrass, coconut milk and peanut butter. It’s rich, creamy and super satisfying.
instructions: Bash the lemongrass and remove the bottom stems and outer husks. Set aside the core and stems/husks, keeping them separate. Halve the chilli.

For the curry, bring ¼ of the coconut milk to a boil in a large lidded pan set over a medium heat. Simmer for about 5 mins, stirring occasionally, to allow the water to evaporate, leaving just a shiny oily surface.

Add the curry paste and mix well. Let the mixture simmer for about 4 mins, stirring frequently, until it has thickened and the coconut oil has separated from the paste, then add the star anise and cinnamon stick and cook for another minute. If the paste sticks to the bottom of the pot, deglaze with a bit more coconut milk.

Add the palm sugar, tamarind paste, fish sauce, and peanut butter with a pinch of salt and mix well. Then add ⅘ of the remaining coconut milk (set the rest aside for garnish later) and the chilli. Mix well and scrape the bottom to make sure no curry paste is stuck. Add the chicken thighs and bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Partially cover the pan with a lid and let the mixture simmer gently for 35 mins, stirring halfway through.

Meanwhile make the rice. Wash the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Transfer to a rice cooker along with the coconut milk, water, salt and ½ the lemongrass stems/husks. Place over high heat, bring to the boil, then cover with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 12 mins, then remove from the heat and let steam, covered, for another 10.
Meanwhile, cut the potatoes into 3cm chunks. Halve the tofu puffs and quarter the onion. When the chicken cooking time is up, remove the chicken to a large bowl and set aside to cool.

Add the potato, tofu puffs, onions, water (if needed) and remaining lemongrass husks/stems to the curry and mix to combine. Simmer for another 15 mins with the lid on. The potatoes should just be fork tender; do not overcook it or it will thicken the curry sauce.
Meanwhile, finely slice the lime leaves and reserved lemongrass core, pick the coriander leaves.

When the potato has finished cooking, debone the cooled chicken, break it into large chunks, and return it to the pot. Gently mix and adjust the seasoning if needed with any extra fish sauce, sugar or tamarind paste. Turn off the heat, and leave to rest, with the lid on, for 15 mins.
Divide the rice between bowls and ladle over the curry. Top with the coriander leaves, lime leaves, sliced lemongrass and a drizzle of leftover coconut milk.

name: Chicken Meatball Korma
description: Creamy, nutty and mild enough for the littlest eaters, this healthy chicken meatball korma is the ultimate family fakeaway. Big comfort, low effort.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings 
Make the meatballs. Peel and finely grate the garlic and fresh ginger. Add to a mixing bowl with the chicken mince, curry powder, breadcrumbs, yoghurt and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix well until combined.
Wet your hands and roll the mixture into 16 small meatballs. Set aside.
Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of sunflower oil. Once hot, add the meatballs and cook for 5–6 mins, turning until golden all over. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Peel and finely dice the onion. Peel and finely slice the second garlic clove. Grate the remaining 20g of ginger.
In the same pan, add another drizzle of oil and cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 4–5 mins until soft. Stir in the curry powder and turmeric, then sprinkle in the flour and cook for 1 min.

Pour in the chicken stock and stir through the ground almonds. Mix well to form a smooth sauce, then return the meatballs to the pan. Simmer gently for 15 mins until the sauce has thickened and the meatballs are cooked through.
Turn off the heat and stir in the yoghurt. Taste and season with salt if needed.
For the adults, prep the garnish. Slice the red chilli, pick the leaves of the coriander and slice the lime into wedges.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Spoon the curry over bowls of rice, with a dollop of yoghurt.
Parents Plate: Top the curry and rice with coriander, lime wedges sliced red chilli and lime pickle or your favourite chutney.

name: Chicken Meatball Parm Orzo
description: Juicy chicken meatballs, saucy orzo & melty mozzarella — all in one pan. Proper comfort food, and quick enough for a weeknight.
instructions: Tip the chicken mince into a mixing bowl. Add 2 Tbsp breadcrumbs, the Italian seasoning, a generous pinch of salt and plenty of black pepper. Mix until just combined, then shape into meatballs. Chill on a plate in the fridge for 10 mins to help them firm up.
Finely chop the onion and thinly slice the garlic.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large, deep ovenproof frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the meatballs and fry for 5 mins, turning regularly, until browned all over. Scoop them onto a plate and turn the heat down to medium.
Get the garlic bread in the oven and bake it following the pack instructions.

Chuck the onion and garlic into the pan and cook for 6–8 mins until soft and golden. Stir through the tomato purée and orzo and cook for 1 min. Pour in the passata and water, season with salt and pepper, and bring it all to a simmer.
Nestle the meatballs back into the pan. Let everything bubble away for around 12 mins, or until the orzo is cooked through and the sauce is thickened.
Once the garlic bread’s out, heat the grill to high. Scatter over the remaining 3 Tbsp breadcrumbs and all the mozzarella, then whack it under the grill for 2–3 mins until golden and bubbling.
Tear over the basil, finish with a pinch of chilli flakes and serve with big chunks of garlic bread on the side.

name: Chicken Meatballs with Herby Freekeh & Greens
description: A punchy, high-protein dinner that hits all the right notes. Spicy chicken meatballs, nutty freekeh, lemony greens, and a cooling jalapeño yoghurt dressing come together for the ultimate meal prep-friendly meal.
keywords: Chicken Meatball Lunchbox with Herby Freekeh and Green Veg
Chicken Meatball Lunchbox with Herby Freekeh and Green Veg recipe
instructions: Pour the water into a saucepan and bring to the boil. While it heats, finely chop the parsley and the lemon. Stir in freekeh, cover, reduce the heat to low-medium, and simmer for 10–15 mins until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork, then stir through the parsley and lemon zest. Set aside to cool slightly.

Make the meatballs: Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan and fry 3 tbsp red curry paste for 3 mins until fragrant. Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander stalks and zest a lime. In a large bowl, combine chicken mince, the coriander stalks, lime zest, fish sauce, eggs, breadcrumbs, the fried curry paste, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix until sticky. Wet your hands and form into 12 meatballs (about 60–70g each).
Cook the meatballs: Wipe out the frying pan, add more oil, and fry the meatballs over medium heat for 10–15 mins, turning to brown evenly, until golden and cooked through.

Trim green beans and chop broccoli into small florets. Bring a pan of salted water to a rolling boil and blanch the veg for 3–4 mins until just tender. Drain and shock in iced water to keep their colour and crunch, then dry thoroughly.

In a large bowl, add pesto, grate in Parmesan, zest and juice a lemon, and drizzle in a few glugs of olive oil. Season well with salt and pepper. Add the drained greens and toasted almonds. Toss to coat.

Make the Jalapeño Yoghurt Dressing: Deseed and roughly chop the jalapeños. Add to a blender with Greek yoghurt, avocado, roughly chop fresh coriander, and the juice of the limes. Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides. Season with salt to taste.
Divide the freekeh between your lunchboxes. Top with chicken meatballs and the dressed greens. Serve with a generous spoonful of the yoghurt dressing or pack it on the side for drizzling later.

name: Chicken Milanese Spaghetti
description: There is something about crunchy breaded chicken and tomato pasta that just works. A great pairing.
instructions: Chop some garlic. Add a splash of olive oil to a pan. Add the garlic and oregano.
Add the chopped tomatoes and basil. Let it simmer.
Place your chicken breasts onto a surface and cover with cling film.
With a rolling pin, tenderise each breast (by rolling them out/bashing them) until flat.
Into separate bowls add flour, whisked eggs and crushed croutons.
Cover your chicken breasts in flour, followed by the whisked eggs, finishing with the croutons.
Get your spaghetti on.
Add a generous amount of oil to a frying pan. When the oil is hot, place the breasts into the frying pan for 4 minutes each side or until golden brown.
Once golden brown, take the chicken out of the frying pan and cut into strips.
Add the cooked spaghetti to the tomato sauce and mix together.
Place the chicken strips onto a bed of spaghetti and tuck in!

name: Chicken Noodle Salad
description: Crispy fried egg noodles add an awesome texture to this salad. Whip a big batch of this up at your next picnic. It'll go down a treat.
instructions: Cook the noodles following pack instructions, then drain well and rinse in cold water to remove the starch. Spread over a large baking sheet until dry (this should take around 20 mins).

Heat the oven to 180°C. Put the chicken thighs onto a large baking tray, drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 30 mins, until the chicken is cooked through and golden. Set aside to cool.

Meanwhile, fill a large deep saucepan half-full with oil and heat it to 180°C. Line a plate with kitchen paper. Tip the noodles into a large bowl and add the cornflour, then toss well. Carefully drop the noodles into the oil a handful at a time, then deep-fry for 3-5 mins until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on the lined plate. Season with a pinch of salt. Repeat with the remaining noodles. Set aside.
Put the sour cream in a bowl, then squeeze in the juice of ½ a lemon and add the mustard. Finely grate the garlic into the bowl and season well with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Peel the carrots into long ribbons, then tip them into a large bowl. Finely slice the celery and spring onions, and thickly slice the lettuces. Tip it all into the bowl. Shred your chicken before adding it to the bowl with 2 tbsp olive oil and most of the dill and parsley. Squeeze in the juice from 1 lemon. Toss well.
Add the crispy noodles to the bowl and toss again, then drizzle with the sour cream dressing. Finish with the reserved herbs and a crack of black pepper.

name: Chicken Noodle Soup
description: This is the ultimate comfort food for when you’re feeling a little rundown. Our chicken noodle soup recipe will nourish your soul and fill your stomach right up.
instructions: Finely dice the onion and celery, then peel and finely dice the carrots. Tear the cooked chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat then add the finely diced vegetables. Add a big pinch of salt and cook gently for 10-15 mins until really soft but not coloured.
Pour in 2L of chicken broth and bring to a simmer. Break the angel hair pasta into pieces and cook following packet instructions.
Scatter in the shredded chicken and leave to reheat for 1 min, then taste and season the broth with salt and cracked black pepper.
Roughly chop the parsley and pick the dill leaves. Spoon the soup into bowls and top with a scattering of the parsley and dill. Serve with garlic bread, if you like.

name: Chicken Oyakodon
description: This Japanese chicken and egg rice bowl is super easy to make but packed with flavour. It’s a really simple soothing dinner.
instructions: Use kitchen paper to pat dry the chicken, then season the thighs all over with salt.

Cook the chicken in a frying pan over medium heat for 8-10 mins, or until golden on both sides. Turn off the heat and transfer the chicken thighs to a plate to cool (don’t worry if they’re not fully cooked yet). Set aside the pan, we'll re-use it.
Chop the onion into ½ cm thick slices. Place the pan back over high heat, add the onion and cook for 5-7 mins, or until lightly charred.
Meanwhile, whisk the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt. Slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish.

To the charred onions, add the sake and give it a good stir to deglaze the pan, then add the mirin and soy sauce. Simmer over a medium heat until it looks like maple syrup. Add the unsalted chicken stock (or water if you prefer) and bring it back up to a simmer.
While the stock comes up to a simmer, cut the chicken into bite-sized chunks.
Add the chicken to the simmering mixture, skin side up. Leave to simmer for a minute to finish cooking off the chicken.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice according to package instructions.

Add ½ the egg mixture and gently swirl it around the pan. Pop the lid on and leave to cook for 30 seconds, then add the remaining egg mixture and pop the lid back on for another 30 seconds. The edges of the egg should slightly pull away from the pan, and the centre should still be a little runny (it will finish cooking when served on the hot rice).
To serve, spoon the rice into a bowl. Slide the oyakodon and broth on top. Garnish with the spring onions and a drizzle of toasted sesame oil.

name: Chicken Parm Melt
description: I’m Ben, one of the new food producers at Mob. This is my Chicken Parm Melt with a killer pesto aioli. Classic flavours that deliver, every single time. B x
instructions: Finely dice the shallots and mince two of the garlic cloves. Add plenty of olive oil to a medium saucepan and set over medium heat.
Add the chopped tomatoes, parmesan rind and the basil stalks. Bring to a simmer, reduce the heat and cook for 15-20 mins until reduced. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.
To make the pesto aioli, combine the fresh pesto, mayonnaise and grate in the remaining garlic clove. Season with salt and mix to combine.
Now for the chicken. Butterfly each breast, cover with a sheet of baking parchment and bash with a pan until you have an even thickness.
Now pop your flour, eggs and breadcrumbs in 3 separate bowls. Season the flour with salt and pepper. Beat the egg and season that, too.

Pass each breast through the flour, dusting off any excess and place it into the egg. Allow any excess to run off before coating it in the breadcrumbs. Reserve on a tray and repeat with the remaining chicken.
Preheat the grill to medium-high (200°C).
Cover the bottom of a frying pan with oil and set over a medium heat. Once hot, lay your first chicken breast down and cook until golden brown and crispy.
Flip it over, give it a baste and cook until the whole thing is golden, brown and the chicken is cooked through. Pop onto a tray and repeat with the remaining chicken.
Once the chicken is cooked off, top each with a spoon of tomato sauce, a few slices of mozzarella and heaps of parmesan cheese.
Pop it under the grill until the mozz is melty and the parmesan is starting to caramelise. Meanwhile, toast your buns.
To assemble, add another spoon of tomato sauce to the bottom bun. Top with the chicken and a few basil leaves. Chuck a big spoon of pesto aioli on the top bun and smash it on top.
Give it a squish, and get stuck in.

name: Chicken Parm Supreme
description: Crispy chicken. Molten cheese. A rich, garlicky marinara sauce. Heaven in a mouthful.
instructions: Start with the marinara sauce. Get a frying pan on the heat, add a big glug of olive oil and add crushed garlic cloves. Fry for 20 seconds and pour in your passata. Add the water and bubble down until thickened.
Once thick, add a big handful of fresh basil. Mix it in and remove the sauce from the heat.
Chicken time. Take a chicken breast. You are going to butterfly it. With a sharp knife, cut from one side, length ways, to half way through.
Lie the breast cut side down and cover with a piece of cling film. Get a rolling pin and bash the chicken until it is about the thickness of a £1 coin. Do this with all the chicken breasts.
Coat each breast in beaten egg (seasoned with salt and pepper) followed by breadcrumbs.
Heat a frying pan with some oil. Add the chicken piece by piece, frying for 4 minutes on each side until crisp and golden.

Spoon your sauce into a baking dish and lay your chicken pieces on top. Add 3 slices of mozzarella to each piece. Cover the chicken with grated Parmesan. Season with pepper and drizzle on some olive oil. Place under a hot grill for 10 minutes or until golden and bubbling.
Remove from the oven and tuck in. Enjoy!

name: Chicken Piccata with Rice & Peas
description: A lovely, simple dish that is far more than the sum of its parts. Lemon, capers and parsley flavour the chicken beautifully. Enjoy. Sophie x
instructions: Finely chop your parsley and grate your garlic.
Cut your chicken breasts in half horizontally to create 8 thin fillets. Place a sheet of cling film on top of your chicken fillets and bash with a rolling pin to create even thinner fillets.
Pour your plain flour into a bowl with a generous pinch of salt and grind of pepper. Dredge your chicken breasts in this mixture so that they are fully coated in flour. Defrost the peas.

Heat a large skillet pan over a medium-high heat with a small glug of olive oil and 15g of the butter. Once the pan is hot, add your chicken breasts a few at a time and fry for about 2 mins on each side until golden and tender. Remove your chicken from the pan and keep warm.

Add your garlic to the pan and cook for 1 min on a low heat. Add your chicken stock and simmer for a minute or so until reduced. Add the rest of your butter, capers and the juice of your lemon, then whisk to combine. Stir the parsley through.
Reheat the rice and share between plates. Pop your chicken fillets on top and pour over the sauce. Serve the peas alongside. Serve with any remaining lemon wedges.

name: Chicken Pistou Soup
description: This chicken pistou soup is a serious upgrade on your student days of pesto pasta. It's a quick, tasty soup that's suitable all year round.
instructions: Before you begin, make the No-Fuss Roast Chicken.

Cut the leek, celery and fennel bulb into a small-ish dice. Crush the garlic. Set a large saucepan over a medium-high heat and add a good glug of olive oil. Tip in the diced veggies with a pinch of salt and cook for 7-8 mins until just starting to soften. Tip in the garlic for another 1-2 mins.

Add in the chicken stock and bring to a boil. Season with a little salt and then add the pasta. Cook for 8 mins until just cooked. While the pasta cooks, cut the courgette into a small dice and quarter the tomatoes. Once the pasta is al dente, add the courgette and tomatoes for 2 mins.

Shred the leftover chicken and add to the pan for the final minute to warm through. Season to taste and add chopped dill and lemon juice to finish. Divide the soup between warm bowls and top with plenty of pesto.

name: Chicken Satay & Rainbow Quinoa Slaw
description: Juicy chicken skewers glazed in a honey-soy marinade, served up with a zingy peanut dressing and crunchy rainbow slaw. It’s fresh, filling and protein-packed.
instructions: Heat the grill to medium-high. If using bamboo skewers, soak them in water for at least 30 mins.
Cut the chicken into 3cm chunks. Finely grate the garlic into a bowl, then stir through the soy sauce and honey. Season with salt and black pepper. Add the chicken to the marinade and set aside.

Thinly shred the cabbage. Julienne or coarsely grate the carrot. Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the stems. Toss the cabbage, carrot, coriander leaves and stems with the cooked quinoa into a large bowl.

In another bowl, stir together the peanut butter, gochujang, soy sauce and honey. Squeeze in lime juice to taste and mix well. If it’s too thick, loosen with a splash of cold water until it’s drizzlable. Taste and season with salt, pepper or more lime if needed.

Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto the skewers and place them on a baking tray. Grill for 10–15 mins, flipping halfway and basting with any leftover marinade, until cooked through and lightly charred. If they’re browning too quickly, lower the tray or reduce the grill heat.
Toss the slaw with half of the peanut dressing and divide between plates. Add the chicken skewers on the side and drizzle over the remaining dressing to finish.

name: Chicken Satay Grain Bowl
description: Nutty, spicy, zingy and full of crunch. This chicken satay grain bowl is a midweek win that’s just as good for lunch the next day.
instructions: Zest and juice the lime into a bowl. Add the soy sauce, a pinch of salt and 1 tsp of black pepper. Stir to combine, then add the chicken thighs and toss to coat. Set aside to marinate while you prep the rest.

Set a heavy-bottomed frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, lay the chicken thighs into the pan and cook for 10 mins on one side without moving. Flip and cook for another 4–5 mins until nicely golden and cooked through. Set aside to rest.

For the satay sauce, mix the peanut butter, sriracha, soy sauce, lime juice, honey and water in a bowl until smooth. If it’s too thick, loosen with another splash of water. Taste and adjust — you want a good balance of zing and heat.

Strip the kale into a large mixing bowl, then add a good pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Massage with your hands for about a minute until softened. Drain the butter beans and stir them through. Heat the grains following pack instructions and tip into the bowl.
Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens. Add the whites to the bowl with a splash of the dressing and toss to combine.
Slice the rested chicken.

Divide the kale and grain salad between bowls or containers. Top with the sliced chicken, drizzle over the remaining dressing and finish with the spring onion greens, sliced chilli (if using) and a lime wedge for squeezing.

name: Chicken Satay Meatballs
description: Juicy chicken meatballs with a zingy mango salad and peanutty dipping sauce. A crowd-pleaser for grown-ups and kids alike.
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsPeel and finely grate all the ginger. Pick the coriander leaves and finely chop the stalks.

Tip the chicken mince into a mixing bowl with the grated ginger, the chopped coriander stalks, and a third of the grains. Season with salt and black pepper. Mix everything together well with your hands, then shape into small, walnut-sized meatballs using wet hands.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry the meatballs for 10–12 mins, turning regularly, until golden and cooked through. You might need to do this in batches. Once cooked, set them aside.

While the meatballs cook, peel the mango. Cut off a few chunks for the kids, then slice the rest into thin matchsticks. Do the same with the red pepper. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds, and cut a few chunky pieces for the kids. Matchstick the rest.

Toss all the matchsticked fruit and veg into a mixing bowl. Zest over the lime, squeeze in half the juice and add the soy sauce. Set aside a few whole coriander leaves for serving, then chop the rest and toss into the bowl.
Make the dressing. Stir the peanut butter, sweet chilli sauce, remaining ginger and soy sauce together in a small bowl. Add water, one tablespoon at a time, until it loosens to a drizzly consistency.
Heat the remaining grain pouch following the pack instructions.

Serve up! Kids Plate: Dish up the meatballs with the chunky fruit and veg on the side, plus a little bowl of dipping sauce.Parents Plate: Pile the grains onto plates and top with the salad and meatballs. Drizzle over the satay dressing, scatter with coriander leaves and serve with the remaining lime, cut into wedges.

name: Chicken Satay Noodles
description: A great peanutty noodle dish. Done in about 15 minutes. Really easy - a great midweek dinner option.
instructions: Add chicken breasts to a pan of boiling water. Boil for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Remove chicken from the water and shred it up.
Add noodles to the chicken water and cook for 3 minutes. Drain.
Get a wok on. Add your coconut milk, peanut butter, fish sauce and soy sauce. Mix everything together and bubble on a high heat for 30 seconds.
Add your chicken. Mix it in. Add your noodles. Stir everything together.
Add a handful of chopped spring onions. Stir them in.
Serve up the noodles into 4 bowls. Add some bashed up peanuts on top. Tuck in.

name: Chicken Satay Pittas
description: This is one of those dishes where combinations are the key. The peanutty chicken, zingy mango slaw, creamy dressing. All in a steaming hot pitta. Unreal scenes.
instructions: Start by slicing up your chicken and placing it into a mixing bowl.

Finely grate a knob of ginger and add this to the bowl followed by 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 200ml of coconut milk, fish sauce, grated garlic cloves, 1 tbsp of peanut butter and a glug of olive oil. Mix everything together and leave to marinate for 20 minutes (or longer if you have time).

Into a small bowl, add the remaining peanut butter, soy sauce and 100ml of coconut milk. Finely chop the rest of the ginger and your chilli. Add this to the bowl and mix together until you have a creamy satay sauce.

Slaw time. Grate your cabbage and carrot into a large bowl. Finely chop your coriander and mint and add this too. Slice up your mango and whack it in. Sprinkle a pinch of salt followed by your vinegar and mix everything together thoroughly.
Toast your pittas.
Once your chicken is marinated, add to a lightly oiled frying pan and stir until cooked through.
