Assembly time! Take your pitta and cut it open. Start with the chicken and dollop some satay sauce over the top. Stuff the pitta with some of that crunchy slaw. Add some more satay sauce and top with a sprinkling of peanuts. Tuck into this delightful little pitta and enjoy!

name: Chicken Schnitzel with Sauce Gribiche & Fennel Salad
description: A wicked smart chicken schnitzel with a creamy sauce gribiche and bitter fennel salad to cut through the richness.
keywords: Chicken Schnitzel with Sauce Gribiche & Fennel Salad
instructions: Start by making the sauce. Bring a pot of water to the boil and lower in the eggs. Boil for 8 mins before removing and plunging into ice water. Once cool enough to handle, crack and gently peel the eggs, using the bowl of water to help wash away any shards of shell.

Pop the eggs onto a board and chop them down into a fine dice. Don’t be super particular about it, just keep chopping until they’re nice and fine. Scrape into a bowl and add the mayo. Finely chop the shallots, cornichons, capers and herbs tip into the bowl, too. Season well with salt and black pepper and add the zest of the lemon, plus a tiny squeeze of juice. Your sauce should be like a loose, chunky egg mayo.

Slice the fennel as thinly as you can with a mandolin. Add to a bowl of ice water and let hang out for 15-20 mins. This isn’t completely necessary but will make the fennel super crispy and delicious. While the fennel is on ice, chunk up the tomatoes and finely chop the dill. Drain the fennel and dry as best you can with a salad spinner or in a clean tea towel. Combine everything in a bowl and season well with salt, lemon juice, olive oil and a little black pepper.

Set your chicken breasts out on a chopping board and use a sharp knife to butterfly each. To do this, carefully cut through one side of the breast, working your way horizontally across the meat opening it up like a book.

Sandwich each breast between two sheets of greaseproof paper and use a small saucepan or frying pan to gently bat the chicken out until it’s super thin. Set up three bowls, one with flour, one beaten eggs, one panko breadcrumbs. Season the chicken breasts very well with salt and pepper and then pass through the flour, egg and then the breadcrumbs.

When ready to fry, cover the bottom of a pan with 1 cm of vegetable oil, with a dash of olive oil for colour. Warm over a medium heat until shimmering, and then fry the schnitzels for 3-4 mins a side or until golden brown. They’re so thin that once they’re looking golden brown and delicious, they’ll be done.
Serve each schnitzel with a heaping spoon of gribiche, a wedge of lemon and a big handful of your fresh salad.

name: Chicken Shawarma Burger
description: Juicy chicken shawarma, minty yoghurt and a chopped salad burger relish, all loaded up into brioche buns.
instructions: Combine the first six ingredients in a small bowl and mix.
Slice the onion and add to a large bowl. Dice up the chicken thighs into roughly 1 inch pieces and add to the same bowl with the onions.
Pour over the spice mix and squeeze over the juice of a lemon. Add the salt and olive oil and mix really well to coat the chicken.
Cover and transfer to the fridge, ideally overnight but an hour or so is fine, too.
Once you’re ready to cook the chicken, preheat your grill to max. Spread the chicken and onions out in a single layer on a large baking tray and place into the oven for 15 mins.

While the chicken cooks, make the chopped salad relish. Take the core and seeds out of the tomato and add to a food processor along with the red onion, gherkin and coriander. Pulse until finely chopped.
Transfer the mix to a sieve and squeeze out as much liquid as you can, then transfer to small bowl. Add the red wine vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt, stir and set aside.
Finely chop the mint and mix through the Greek yoghurt with a pinch of salt.
Check that the chicken is cooked through and remove from the oven. It should be well browned and crispy on one side and soft and juicy on the other.
Toast the buns, then spread the bottom half with a layer of the minty yoghurt. Top with a big spoonful of the chicken and onions.
Spread the top layer of the bun with a spoon of the relish, then sandwich the burger together and enjoy.

name: Chicken Shawarma Kebabs with Green Chilli Butter
description: Juicy shawarma-spiced chargrilled chicken, with zingy slaw, garlicky sauce & lemony chilli butter on fluffy flatbreads. Big vibes, little effort.
keywords: Chicken Shawarma Kebabs with Green Chilli Butter Flatbreads
Chicken Shawarma Kebabs with Green Chilli Butter Flatbreads recipe
instructions: Heat the grill to medium-high.Mix the yoghurt and Al’Fez Shawarma Spice Mix in a big bowl. Cut the chicken into large chunks, season with salt, add to the bowl and toss to coat. Cover and chill.
Zest half the lemons into a heatproof bowl. Finely chop the chillies and parsley, add with a pinch of salt. Melt the butter, pour over, stir and set aside.
Shred the cabbage into a bowl with mint, vinegar, juice of the lemons, salt and pepper. Scrunch to soften, drizzle with olive oil, stir and set aside.

Thread the chicken onto skewers, folding any thinner bits in half, making sure to not pack the pieces too tightly. Lightly oil a baking tray and lay the skewers on top.

Grill the skewers for 3-4 mins until charred, flip and cook the other side. Rest for a few mins.
Warm the Al’Fez Lebanese Style Flatbreads under the grill for 1 min. Spread with the chilli butter, top with chicken, slaw and Al’Fez Garlic Squeezy Sauce. Fold up and dig in.

name: Chicken Skewer Naan Wraps
description: The spicy, charred chicken inside the warm naan, cooled by the fresh yoghurt dressing. A straight 10/10.
instructions: Dice up your thighs. Add to a bowl with ground ginger, ground coriander, cumin and cayenne pepper. Add a crushed garlic clove, 4 tbsp of plain yoghurt, salt and pepper. Add a drizzle of olive oil and mix everything together. Cover and leave to marinate for 40 minutes.
Raita time. Into a blender, add a handful of coriander, a handful of mint, 300g of yogurt, salt, pepper and olive oil. Add the zest and juice of a lime and blitz until smooth.
Place 8 wooden skewers in a bowl of water to soak.
Roughly cut your onion into chunks.

Take a skewer, add a piece of onion, chicken, more onion, more chicken and finish with a piece of onion. Use up the chicken and onions on all the skewers and place them on a baking tray. Place under the grill for 30 minutes, turning every 10 minutes.
Warm your naans.
Once the chicken is charred and cooked through, remove from the oven.
Chop up some iceberg lettuce.
Serving time. Add your chicken (removing the wooden skewer), some lettuce and a big dollop of raita onto a naan. Wrap it up and tuck in!

name: Chicken Soba Noodle Salad
description: Such a fresh little salad - a great lunchtime option!
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Add chicken breasts to a baking tray. Drizzle over some olive oil and a tbsp of soy sauce. Mix everything together. Add the chicken to the oven for 25 minutes until perfectly cooked through.
Once cooked, remove the chicken. Shred it with 2 forks and set aside.
Meanwhile, peel, de-seed and cut the cucumber into slices. Thinly slice the peppers and chilli. Pick the herbs, discarding the stems.
Cook the soba according to package instructions. When they are ready, drain and thoroughly wash under cold water.
Dressing time. Into a jar or bowl, add your olive oil, sesame oil, soy sauce and the juice of a lime. Mix everything together.
Serving time. Get a big salad bowl. Add all your elements in to the bowl. Scatter your chopped chilli, herbs and sesame on top. Add your dressing. Toss everything together, serve up and enjoy!

name: Chicken Souvlaki
description: Fire up your grill and make these glorious chicken kebabs. Loaded up with lovely fresh Greek flavours and thrown into flatbreads. A summer banger.
instructions: Soak your wooden skewers in a bowl. Set aside until later.
Chop your chicken thigh fillets into large chunks.

Tip the chicken chunks into a large bowl along with your greek yoghurt, dried oregano, dried mint, chilli flakes and a big pinch of salt. Grate in your garlic and the zest from your lemon. Give it all a good mix and leave to marinate for at least 1 hour, preferably overnight.
Make your tzatziki. Grate your cucumber and pop it in a sieve set over a bowl. Add the salt and give it a good mix. Leave it to drain for 30 mins - lots of water should come out of it.

Whilst your cucumber drains, prep your veg. Quarter, core and dice your tomatoes. Peel and finely dice your red onion. Roughly chop your kalamata olives. Roughly chop your parsley. Place all the veg in a bowl and add your lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Mix to combine.

Back to your tzatziki. Squeeze your cucumbers to remove any excess liquid, then pop in a clean bowl. Add your chopped mint, yoghurt, and the juice of your lemon. Season to taste with salt, then set aside.
Heat your grill to high.
Skewer your chicken onto the wooden skewers. Place them on a baking tray under the grill and cook for 15 mins, turning occasionally so they cook evenly.
Warm your flatbreads.
Assembly time. Spread some tzatziki on your flatbreads, then push your chicken off the skewers onto the tzatziki. Top with some tomato mixture and serve.

name: Chicken Souvlaki Salad
description: We’ve taken all of our favourite elements from a souvlaki wrap and turned it into a salad. Yes, you read that right.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Using scissors, snip the pitta into triangles straight into a bowl. Season generously, then drizzle in 1 tbsp of the olive oil, using your hands to coat the bread evenly. Tip out onto a large baking tray and spread into a single layer. Bake for 8–10 mins until crisp. Set aside.
Juice a quarter of the lemons, and finely slice the red onion. Toss together.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, mix together 2 tbsp of the olive oil with the dried oregano, smoked paprika, cumin and 1 tsp of the dried mint. Zest and juice of half the lemons and season with salt and pepper. Set aside – you will marinate your chicken in this once it’s cooked (the secret to extra flavour and juiciness).

Tear a large piece of baking paper onto the work surface. Lay half the chicken thighs on the paper, a few centimetres apart from each other, then top with another sheet of baking paper. Using a rolling pin satisfyingly bash the chicken to an even thickness, around 1cm (1⁄2in). Repeat until all the thighs are flattened, season and rub with the remaining 2 tsp of olive oil.
Get a large griddle or frying pan searingly hot. Once hot, lay in the chicken and cook for 4–5 mins on each side until cooked through and juicy. Transfer the hot chicken to the marinade bowl.

Tzatziki time. Coarsely grate half the cucumber and squeeze out as much water as you can. Put into to a bowl with the remaining 1 tsp of dried mint and the Greek yoghurt. Squeeze in the juice of the remaining lemon and season to taste.
Slice the rest of the cucumber into long diagonals, chop the tomatoes and shred the iceberg lettuce. Pick the mint leaves and roughly chop the parsley (stalks and all).

Assembly time. Slice the chicken and return to the marinade bowl. Divide the cucumber, red onion, tomato, lettuce and herbs between four plates. Scatter over the pitta chips, then top with the chicken, spooning over all the delicious marinade. Top with little dollops of tzatziki and grate over lemon zest to serve.

name: Chicken Spring Onion Meatball Miso Soup
description: A comforting and nourishing miso soup packed with juicy chicken meatballs, sweet napa cabbage and a deep umami broth. Perfect for a cosy night in.
keywords: Chicken Spring Onion Meatball Miso Soup
Chicken Spring Onion Meatball Miso Soup recipe
instructions: To make the meatballs, peel and grate the ginger and white onion. Mince the spring onions. To a large mixing bowl, add the minced chicken, egg and cornstarch. Use your hands to mix and squeeze until well combined and paste-like. Add the grated ginger, grated onion, minced spring onions, soy sauce, mirin and a pinch of salt and black pepper. Mix for a few more minutes until fully combined. Take small spoonfuls of the chicken mixture and roll them between the palms of your hands to form meatballs. Set aside.
To prep the soup, cut the napa cabbage into 2½ cm chunks. Peel and dice the carrot. Thinly slice the white onion. Set aside.
To cook the meatballs, heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large saucepan over a high heat then add the meatballs and brown them on all sides for 2-3 mins.

To build the soup, pour the mirin into the pan (leave the meatballs in) to deglaze, scraping up any bits stuck to the pan. Add the chicken stock. Add the cabbage, carrot and white onion to the pan. Cover with a lid and simmer on a medium heat for 15-20 mins.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the remaining spring onion and set aside. Place the miso paste in a small bowl. Ladle in a few spoonfuls of the hot chicken stock to help loosen it up. Use the back of a spoon to press and stir it into a smooth paste.
When the soup cooking time is up, turn off the heat. Stir through the miso paste until fully dissolved then stir through the sliced spring onion and sesame oil.
Ladle the soup into bowls and serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Chicken Stir-Fry
description: Everyone needs a banging chicken stir-fry recipe in their repertoire, and this one hits all the spots. It’s perfect for super quick cooking, high in protein and healthy. What more do you want?
instructions: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces, then scrape into a bowl. Get a clean board and knife out, remove the seeds from the peppers, then cut them into similar sized pieces to the chicken. Peel and slice the carrot, then slice the celery too. Finely chop the garlic and ginger.

Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over a high heat. Add the almonds to the pan and cook, constantly stirring, for 1-2 minutes until they’ve darkened slightly, then scoop them out with a slotted spoon and put them into a bowl.
Season the chicken well with salt and pepper, then add to the hot pan and fry for 5-6 mins until golden. Scoop the pieces out and put them into the bowl with the almonds.

Pour another splash of vegetable oil into the pan and leave to heat for 30 seconds. Carefully add the pepper, carrots and celery and fry for 6-7 mins until charring at the edges and softening. Then reduce the heat to medium and add the garlic and ginger. Fry for a minute, stirring constantly.

Add the chicken and almonds back into the pan along with the sugar snap peas. Toss well and leave to fry for 2 mins while you make the sauce. Spoon the cornflour into a small bowl and whisk in the soy sauce. Pour in the honey and whisk again then pour in the cold water. Pour into the pan and mix really well then simmer for 2-3 mins until the sauce has thickened.
Spoon into bowls and serve with steamed rice or cooked egg noodles, then tear over the coriander to serve.

name: Chicken Suya Skewers
description: When you want to create an African Faaji (party) in your home, here's a quick and easy recipe for our scrumptious suya. Plus, you can follow the link to pair it with our delicious jollof rice recipe. Don’t delay, make your suya today. From the Suya Pit (@thesuyapit).
instructions: If you don’t have metal skewers, soak wooden or bamboo ones in water for at least 30 mins.
Heat the oven to 225°C. Add all the dry spices into a large bowl with the kuli kuli. Stir through the stock powder, sugar and salt. Stir together and set aside ⅙ of it to use as a garnish, later.
Optional: Wash your chicken with either lemon, salt or vinegar and water. Use a kitchen roll to dry the chicken.
Dice the chicken into 3cm chunks and tip it into the spice bowl. Pour a drizzle of olive oil on top and mix together. Leave to marinate for 30 mins.
Thread the marinated chicken onto the skewers and place onto an oiled baking tray. Roast in the oven for 15 mins, turning halfway through.

Switch the oven to grill and cook the chicken skewers under the grill for 5-10 mins, turning them halfway through, until starting to char on all sides. Each grill works differently, so keep an eye on them.
Transfer the skewers to plates and sprinkle over the leftover seasoning. Top with some diced tomato, red onion and coriander, if using.
Plate up the ting and tell your belly it’s time to chow down.

name: Chicken Teriyaki Brioche Burger
description: Sweet and sticky teriyaki chicken in a fluffy brioche bun. Chicken burgers don't get much better than this.
instructions: Cut the brioche buns in half. Add the butter to a frying pan set over a medium heat and cook until the butter has melted. Add the brioche halves to the pan to toast them, occasionally checking the bottom so they don’t burn. Once golden, remove from the pan and set aside.

Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper on both sides. Lay skin-side down in a new, cold pan and turn the heat to high. Cook for 5 mins, flip, then cook for a further 5 mins. Remove and set aside.

Lower the heat to low-medium. Add the vinegar, light soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar. Grate the garlic clove and some of the ginger into the mixture, too. Swirl the pan for 1-2 mins until the sugar has dissolved.

Add cornstarch to a bowl with cold water. Stir well to create a slurry. While stirring the sauce, pour the slurry into the pan slowly. The sauce should thicken into a glossy (but not too thick) mixture. If too thick, add a splash of water. Turn the heat off.
Add the chicken to the pan and flip to glaze on both sides.
Dice the red onion and transfer to a bowl of cold water (this will remove the harshness). Cut the lettuce leaves in half and stack on top of each other. Finely slice the chives.

To assemble, lay a slice of cheese on the bottom half of each brioche bun. Add a piece of chicken, some drained red onion, lettuce, a generous dollop of mayo, chives and finally the top half of the brioche bun.

name: Chicken Thai Green Curry
description: This fragrant curry will blow you away. This one has medium spice, but you can add more or less chillis depending on how hot you like it.
instructions: Roughly chop your shallots, lemongrass, chillies, garlic, ginger and coriander.

Place all of these ingredients, plus the zest of half a lime, into your food processor with half of your fish sauce and a splash of vegetable oil, then blitz to a rough puree. You can also do this in a pestle and mortar. Set aside.
Chop your chicken into strips and slice your aubergine into 1cm wide half moons.

Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat, then add your chicken. Brown off for 3-5 mins, then remove from the pan. Add your aubergine chunks, along with another splash of vegetable oil, then fry over a medium heat for 4 mins until your aubergine is totally soft.

Add all of your curry paste to the aubergine pan and cook out for a few minutes until it is fragrant. You might see some oil separate out from the curry paste, but don't be alarmed - this is normal. Add your coconut milk and chicken stock and stir to combine, then bring up to a boil.

Add your chicken and green beans to the pan, then simmer over a medium heat for 15 mins until your sauce has thickened and your chicken and vegetables are tender. Your kitchen will smell amazing at this point. Add your sugar, the juice of half a lime and the remaining fish sauce, then season to taste with salt.
Serve your curry over rice and sprinkle with coriander leaves. Dig in.

name: Chicken Thighs with Jamón, Peas & Broad Beans
description: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs nestled in a bright, garlicky braise of jamón, white wine, sweet peas and broad beans. One pan, loads of flavour, and plenty of crusty bread required for the juices.
keywords: Chicken with Jamón Peas and Broad Beans
Kitty Cole's Chicken with Jamón Peas and Broad Beans
Chicken with Jamón Peas and Broad Beans recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Pat the chicken thighs dry with kitchen paper and season generously on both sides with salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large ovenproof frying pan or shallow casserole over a high heat. Place the thighs skin-side down and cook without moving for 6–8 mins until the skin is deeply golden and crisp. Flip and cook for a further 2 mins, then transfer the pan to the oven and roast for 15–18 mins until cooked through and the juices run clear. Lift the chicken onto a warm plate to rest, leaving all the pan juices behind.

Return the pan to a medium heat. Tear in the jamón (serrano or iberico ham is great) and cook for 1–2 mins until beginning to crisp at the edges. Finely slice the shallots and add them to the pan, cooking for 4–5 mins, stirring occasionally, until softened and golden. Finely slice the garlic and add it along with the paprika, then cook for a further minute until fragrant.

Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for 2 mins to cook off the alcohol, scraping up any sticky bits from the bottom of the pan. Pour in the stock and bring to a gentle simmer. Tip in the frozen peas and broad beans (and the drained cannellini beans, if using) and cook for 3–4 mins until just tender and bright green. Squeeze over the juice of the lemon and finish with a generous drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Nestle the rested chicken thighs back into the pan and serve straight from the pan with plenty of crusty bread to mop up the juices.

name: Chicken Tikka Skewers with Mango & Cucumber
description: Spicy chicken tikka skewers with a fresh and zingy side salad. This is destined to become a family favourite.
keywords: Juicy tikka-spiced chicken skewers served with a zingy mango and cucumber salad. There’s a punchy yoghurt-coriander sauce for the grown-ups and plain
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings Slice the chicken thighs in half lengthways and chuck into a bowl with the juice of half a lime, half of the yoghurt and all of the tikka paste. Season well with salt and pepper, then mix everything together. Set aside to marinate while you crack on with the rest — or cover and chill for up to 24 hrs.

Cut a few thin slices from the green chilli and set aside for garnish. Roughly chop the rest and add to a mini food processor with most of the coriander (stems and all), the remaining yoghurt and the juice of the limes (save wedges for serving). Blitz until smooth, season to taste, and set aside — this is your coriander sauce for the adults.
Heat the grill to high and line a baking tray with foil. Lightly oil the foil, then lay the chicken on top. Grill for 15–20 mins, flipping halfway, until gnarly and cooked through.
Halve the cucumber lengthways and scoop out the seeds with a spoon. Chop into chunks. Peel and chop the mango into similar-sized pieces, then gently toss both together in a bowl.
Cook the rice following pack instructions.

Serve up!Kids Plate: Spoon some rice onto each plate, add a skewer and a pile of the mango and cucumber salad.Parents Plate: Dish out the rice and chicken skewers. Spoon over some of the coriander sauce and top with a few sliced chillies and reserved coriander leaves. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

name: Chicken Tikka Sliders
description: These cheesy pulled chicken tikka sliders really hit the spot. Next time you're craving a takeaway, make these instead.
instructions: Mince the garlic. If using the hob, add all the ingredients for the chicken tikka to a large saucepan (leave out the food colouring if you prefer) along with about ½ a can of water or enough that the chicken is mostly covered. Stir and simmer for 40 mins or until the chicken is cooked through. If using a slow cooker, add all the ingredients for the chicken tikka to a slow cooker and cook on high for 4 hours or low for 6-7 hours.
Remove the cooked chicken from the slow cooker or saucepan and pull it apart using two forks. Heat the oven to 180°C. Halve the brioche buns. Mince the garlic and coriander.
Add the margarine to a small bowl and melt it in the microwave for 10 seconds then stir through the garlic and coriander.

In a large baking dish, layer the brioche bun bottoms then top with the pulled chicken tikka, ½ tsp of chutney per bun and the grated cheese. Add the brioche bun tops then brush over the garlic coriander butter. Sprinkle over the sesame seeds.

Cover the dish with foil and bake in the oven for 10 mins, then remove the foil and continue to bake for a few more minutes until the tops of the buns are lightly toasted and the cheese has melted inside. Serve up and enjoy!

name: Chicken Yaki Udon
description: The iconic stir-fried Japanese noodle is so easy to make at home!  Caramelised soy sauce udon, chunks of tender soy marinated chicken, and lots of veggies.  A super savoury and satisfying weeknight dinner.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Slice the chicken thighs into 2cm strips, then transfer to a bowl with the soy sauce. Set aside in the fridge to marinate.

Cook the noodles in the boiling water for 1 min less than pack instructions, then drain very well under cold water. Toss with your hands to remove all the starch. Leave the udon in the sieve, tossed with a bit of sesame oil to prevent the noodles from sticking together.
Combine the mentsuyu ingredients in a small saucepan, then boil for 3-5 mins until lightly syrupy (like maple syrup). Set aside in a bowl.

Finely slice the onion into half moons, cut the cabbage into bite-sized squares, then slice the carrots, peppers and mushrooms into matchsticks. Chop the spring onions into 5cm pieces. Mince the garlic. Set everything aside on a large plate. All the prep is now done – it’s time to stir-fry!

Heat a large pan and add a splash of oil when hot. Carefully add the chicken thighs at arm’s length, toss well in the oil, then lay each piece of chicken flat and leave to cook on each side for 2 mins, without tossing, until lightly golden.

Push everything to the side and tilt the pan so the oil comes to one edge. Add the garlic, cook for 1 min until lightly golden, then toss everything together. Add the onions, carrots, mushrooms, cabbage, peppers and a splash of water to deglaze the pan. If anything is sticking to the bottom, the water will help scrape it away – you don't want anything to burn.

Toss everything well, then add a splash of oil, the noodles and 4 tbsp mentsuyu sauce, saving a bit for later. Cook, tossing everything very well, for 1 min. Add 1 tsp dark soy sauce just for colour, then lay the noodles flat and allow to caramelise for 1 min (don’t move them). Toss and caramelise again.
Turn the heat off and add the spring onions, sesame oil and rice vinegar. Toss well to combine.
Serve with bonito flakes, ginger pickles, seaweed flakes, an egg yolk and chilli oil, if you like.

name: Chicken and Pineapple Curry
description: Our Fijian-inspired curry is peppery, zingy and a little bit sweet. Mop up that sauce with lots of rice. There will be no pineapple debate with this one.
instructions: Peel the skin of the pineapple and chop it up into small bite-sized chunks, you will need roughly 400g for this recipe. Enjoy the rest as a snack while you cook.
Blend up half the pineapple with half an onion and three cloves of garlic.
Pour this over the chicken and allow it to marinate in the fridge for 30 mins. The pineapple helps to tenderise the chicken.
Finely dice your remaining onion and the tomatoes. Grate the remaining two cloves of garlic and ginger.
In a large wok, add in 50ml of vegetable oil and fry the onions on a medium heat for 5 mins until lightly browned. Add in the grated garlic and ginger and fry for 2 mins.
Next, you’re going to want to add in the chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, ground cumin and 2 tsp salt. Fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Tip in the chopped tomato (along with their juices) and cook for 5 mins until the sauce is thick and jammy.

Add your marinated chicken to the pot and coconut milk, then give it a good mix. Put a lid on and allow it to simmer for 20 mins, stirring regularly. The pineapple has a lot of sugar so it has a tendency to burn. Keep an eye out for that.
Halfway through the 20 mins, add in the remaining chopped pineapple.
Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander.
Once the chicken is fully cooked, add in the coriander, the juice of two limes and 1 tbsp freshly ground black pepper.
Season to taste and serve with freshly steamed rice.

name: Chicken au Curried Poivre
description: A classic peppercorn sauce, but with even more flavour. This curried twist makes for a seriously rich and satisfying dish. Best served with a tangy salad to cut through the richness and some crusty bread to mop up every drop of sauce.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Coarsely grind or bash the peppercorns. Make sure your butter is fridge-cold.

Generously season the chicken legs with salt. Place them skin side down into an ovenproof frying pan over a medium heat. Cook undisturbed until the skin is golden brown, 8-12 mins. Transfer the chicken onto a plate, skin side up – it won’t be cooked through yet. Don’t wash out the pan.

Finely slice the parsley stems, setting aside the leaves for later. Add the stems to the empty pan along with the crushed peppercorns, crispy onions and curry powder. Set it over a medium heat and cook for 30 secs, stirring, until fragrant.

Pour in the vinegar (for the sauce) and water, then nestle the chicken back in, skin side up. Bring to the boil, then transfer the pan to the oven. Roast for 30-35 mins until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, for the salad, whisk together the Dijon mustard, vinegar and olive oil until emulsified. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.

Once the chicken is cooked, transfer it to a plate to rest. Place the pan back over a medium heat. Stir in the crème fraîche, cold butter and miso. Let the sauce reduce if you’d like it thicker. Taste and adjust with more salt, pepper or vinegar if needed.
Toss the salad leaves, walnuts and reserved parsley leaves in the dressing. Divide between plates.
Serve the chicken with plenty of sauce and some crusty baguette on the side.

name: Chicken with Chorizo Beans
description: Try batch cooking this recipe using IKEA 365+ containers. It's a great way to save energy in the kitchen and reduce your food waste by storing leftovers.
keywords: Crispy chicken with chorizo beans recipes
instructions: Heat a large sauté pan over a medium heat. Add your chicken thighs skin-side down and cook for 10 mins until crispy. Remove from the pan.
Whilst your chicken cooks, finely dice your onion. Dice your red peppers into 2cm big chunks. Finely chop your garlic and rosemary. Peel your chorizo and dice it into cubes.

Add a little olive oil to the chicken pan and tip in your onion. Cook over a medium heat for 10 mins until starting to soften. Add your pepper and chorizo to the pan and cook for 5 mins until chorizo is crisp and pepper is softened.

Get your tomato purée, garlic, rosemary and smoked paprika in the pan and let it sizzle for 2 mins. Tip in your cherry tomatoes and let them bubble, squashing them with the back of your spoon to break them down slightly. Cook for 5 mins.
Pour in your chicken stock along with your cannellini beans and let the mixture come to a simmer. Gently place in your chicken thighs skin-side up, and let the mixture gently cook for 40 mins.
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with more rosemary and serve.
Sprinkle your chicken with more chopped rosemary, then spoon it into your IKEA 365 containers and pop on the lid. Once cool, store in the fridge.

name: Chicken à la Norma
description: This one-pot wonder is a riff on the Sicilian pasta à la norma, combining the traditional aubergines, tomato sauce and basil with less traditional chicken legs. Even better: the oven does most of the work.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Season the chicken legs with salt. Cut the aubergine into 2cm chunks.
Add the aubergine chunks to a high sided roasting tray. Season with salt and drizzle with olive oil then roast in the oven for 20-25 mins until golden and softened, turning half way through.

Remove the tray from the oven. Add the cherry tomatoes, whole unpeeled garlic cloves and chilli flakes to the tray and give it a mix. Place the chicken legs on top and drizzle generously with olive oil then sprinkle with the oregano. Place in the oven for another 20 mins then lower the heat to 170°C and roast for another 20 mins or until the chicken is golden and the tomatoes have burst to create a sauce underneath.
Serve with plenty of fresh basil and grated Parmesan. And some crusty bread, if you like.

name: Chicken, Almond & Apricot Tagine
description: All those beautiful Moroccan flavours for under a tenner. The green olives cut through the rich tagine perfectly. The almonds bring the crunch.
instructions: Finely chop garlic and onions. Throw the onions into your tagine, or a normal pot if you don’t have a tagine. Fry until soft and then add the garlic.
When soft, add the cumin and ground ginger. Mix everything together, and then remove the onion mix from the tagine and set aside in a bowl.
Place your chicken thighs skin side down into the tagine. Brown the skins. Then turn over, and brown the undersides.
Once browned, put your onion mix back in the tagine. Cut a lemon in half, and put the halves into the tagine.
Pour in your chicken stock (dissolved in 500ml), so the tops of the chicken thighs are just above the water. Pop the lid on, and leave on a low-medium heat for one hour.

After an hour, remove the lid. Throw in a large handful of green olives, a handful of dried apricots and a handful of chopped coriander. Place lid back on for 10 more minutes. After ten minutes, remove lid.
If there is still too much liquid, just leave it to bubble away without the lid on for another 10 minutes.
Make your couscous using another stock cube. When it has taken the liquid add handful of chopped olives and coriander then set aside.
Once it is ready and the meat is falling of the bone, scatter your flaked almonds over the top. Serve with another handful of coriander leaves. Enjoy!

name: Chicken, Basil & Fennel High Protein Smash
description: An Italian-ish smoosh flavoured with fresh basil, Parmesan and fennel. The ultimate high-protein, low-effort lunch or dinner.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C. Season your chicken breasts with salt, pepper and a good drizzle of olive oil.
Put your chicken breasts on a baking tray and cook in the oven for 30 mins until cooked through.
Meanwhile, finely dice your cucumber and avocado, finely chop your basil, and grate your Parmesan.
When your chicken is cooked, chop it into even-sized pieces. Combine it with all the remaining ingredients in a large mixing bowl.
Now it’s time to ‘smoosh’ the mixture over a few slices of toast, a pitta bread, a bagel, or whatever you fancy.

name: Chicken, Carrot & Cabbage Chopped Salad
description: An alliterative salad of carrots, chicken and cabbage. The spicy peanut dressing is so good you'll want to bathe in it. But please don't.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Season your chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place your breasts onto a baking tray and get them in the oven for 25 mins. Allow them to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm.
Peel your carrots and de-seed your cucumbers.
Add your carrots, cucumber, cooked chicken breasts, and white cabbage to a chopping board and chop up into even-sized pieces.

Add pickled ginger, salted peanuts, coriander, and mint to the chopping board (reserving some peanuts and coriander for later) and keep chopping. Add all of your chopped ingredients into a large bowl.

Squeeze the juice from your limes and combine with the rest of the dressing ingredients and a splash of water to loosen it up. Add the dressing into your bowl and toss together. Garnish with an extra bit of coriander and a scattering of peanuts. Enjoy.

name: Chicken, Fennel, Tomato & White Beans
description: We are obsessed with fennel at MOB Kitchen, and it works a charm in this dish. Paired with roasted chicken thighs, cherry tomatoes and cooling yoghurt. Sublime.
ingredients: 1 Chilli Flakes (to taste, to serve, optional)
instructions: Chop the garlic cloves. Pick the fennel from and trim the bulb and thinly slice.

Season the chicken thighs all over with salt and pepper. Get a large high sided frying pan over a medium to high heat. Pour in some olive oil. Fry the chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes, turning halfway until browned (it doesn't need to be fully cooked at this moment). Transfer to a plate.

Chuck the fennel into the pan with a good pinch of salt. Fry, stirring regularly for around 5 minutes until the fennel has wilted. Add the garlic, cook for 30 seconds more then spoon in the harissa and fennel seeds if using. Give everything a good mix then pour in the white wine. Once the wine has nearly all bubbled away, turn down the heat and add the tomatoes. Drain one can of beans then tip them and the other two cans of beans, along with their water into the pan.

Stir everything together and place the chicken thighs on top. Put a lid on the pan and cook everything on a medium heat for 10 minutes, then remove the lid and continue cooking for 5-10 minutes until you are left with saucy beans and the chicken is cooked through.

Add the capers into the bean stew. Season to taste. Drizzle with a little olive oil then scatter over the fennel fronds. Serve out the pan with some yoghurt, and chilli flakes, if you like. Then, tuck in!

name: Chicken, Miso & Spring Onion High Protein Smash
description: Creamy, punchy and piled high on toast. Pulled chicken smooshed with miso, tahini and mayo, then folded through spring onions, cucumber and coriander, this is perfect for high protein meal prep.
keywords: Miso & Spring Onion Smoosh on Toast
Miso & Spring Onion Smoosh on Toast recipe
instructions: Shred the chicken into bitesize pieces and finely slice the spring onions and celery. Roughly chop the coriander and cucumber.

In a bowl, add the shredded chicken, miso, mayonnaise and tahini, mixing well until evenly coated. Then fold through the chopped spring onions, celery, coriander, cucumber and sesame seeds, until thick, creamy and scoopable. Season with black pepper and a little salt if needed.
To serve pile the mixture generously on top of toasted sourdough. Pop any leftovers in the fridge for later, they will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken, Miso & Spring Onion Smash Rice Bowl
description: Creamy, punchy and piled high on rice. Pulled chicken smooshed with miso, tahini and mayo, then folded through spring onions, cucumber and coriander, this is perfect for high protein meal prep.
keywords: Miso & Spring Onion Smoosh on Toast
Miso & Spring Onion Smoosh on Toast recipe
instructions: Pop the water, two of the spring onions, the garlic and the fine salt into a large saucepan and set over a high heat. Bring to the boil, then throw in the chicken breasts. Bring back to a simmer, pop the lid on and turn off the heat. Leave untouched for 25 mins, the residual heat will cook the chicken through. Then using tongs, remove the chicken from the liquid and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile finely slice the remaining spring onions and celery. Roughly chop the coriander and 3/4 cucumber, thinly slicing the rest for garnish.

Once the chicken is cool enough to handle, shred into pieces using two forks. In a bowl, add the chicken, miso, mayonnaise and tahini, mixing well until evenly coated. Then fold through the 3/4 of the chopped spring onions, celery, coriander, cucumber and sesame seeds, until thick, creamy and scoopable. Season with black pepper and a little salt if needed.
Heat the rice and divide between bowls. Add a dollop of the chicken mixture with the sliced cucumber, remaining chopped spring onions and a drizzle of crispy chilli oil to finish.

name: Chicken, Pepper & Cucumber Chopped Salad
description: A mediterranean-inspired chicken chopped salad that's tangy, filling, and super healthy. Whack in the fridge and set yourself up for delicious lunches all week.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Season your chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place your breasts onto a baking tray and get them in the oven for 25 mins. Allow them to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm.
Chop up the basil, the roasted red peppers, cucumbers, pistachios, and chicken into even-sized pieces. Toss together in a large bowl with kalamata olives.

Divide the salad between Tupperware containers with a dollop of cottage cheese in each box and pop them in the fridge. Keep the dressing separate – either pour a little over in the morning or stash it in a little pot inside your lunch box to add just before eating.

name: Chicken, Pepper & Cucumber Chopped Salad
description: A chicken chopped salad recipe that's tangy, filling, and super healthy. This one's perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Season your chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place your breasts onto a baking tray and get them in the oven for 25 mins. Allow them to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm.
Chop up the basil, the roasted red peppers, cucumbers, pistachios, and chicken into even-sized pieces. Combine in a bowl before topping with kalamata olives and the dressing. Toss vigorously.
Serve with a dollop of cottage cheese on each portion and enjoy.

name: Chicken, Pepper & Harissa Orzo
description: A simple one-pan dinner for when you can’t be bothered with faffing about with a million different bits of kit.
instructions: Chop the peppers into 2-3cm chunks, thinly slice the garlic. Drain and finely mince the sundried tomatoes. Dice the chicken into 3cm chunks. Pick the parsley leaves, finely mince the stems.

Place a saucepan over medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the peppers and cook until starting to soften, 5-8 mins. Then, stir the garlic, parsley stems and orzo through until fragrant.

Pour the chicken stock in and stir the harissa, sundried tomatoes and chicken through. Season with salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has absorbed, and the orzo and chicken are cooked, 10-15 mins. If the orzo is drying out too quickly, add a splash of water.
Stir the mascarpone  and sherry vinegar through, taste and season with more salt, if needed. Share between bowls, and finish with a scattering of parsley leaves.

name: Chicken, Pesto & Sun-Dried Tomato High Protein Smash
description: Shredded chicken, creamy cottage cheese and punchy pesto, loaded with fresh tomatoes and herbs. Perfect scooped onto toast or popped in the fridge for a quick high protein hit in the week.
instructions: Shred the cooked chicken and add to a large bowl with the cottage cheese and pesto. Mix until the chicken is well coated.

Finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes and spinach, quarter the cherry tomatoes, tear the basil and finely slice the spring onion. Fold everything through the chicken mixture, then season with salt and black pepper and mix until evenly combined and thick enough to scoop.
To serve, toast the sourdough and dollop the smash mix generously onto each slice. Pop any leftovers in the fridge, it will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken, Pesto & Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta
description: Shredded chicken, creamy cottage cheese and punchy pesto, loaded with fresh tomatoes and herbs all stirred through pasta for a super easy midweek dinner.
instructions: Bring a pan of water to the boil and cook the pasta according to packet instructions.
Shred the cooked chicken and add to a large bowl with the cottage cheese and pesto. Mix until the chicken is well coated.

Finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes and spinach, quarter the cherry tomatoes, tear the basil and finely slice the spring onion. Fold everything through the chicken mixture, then season with salt and black pepper and mix until evenly combined and thick enough to scoop.
To serve, combine the chicken mix with the pasta and divide between bowls. Pop any leftover mix in the fridge, it will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken, Prosciutto & Slaw Stuffed Jacket Potatoes
description: Crispy jacket potatoes loaded with your leftover Roast Chicken Legs with Roasted Grapes, Prosciutto Parsnips & Apple Slaw batch. Jacket potatoes have never been treated so well.
keywords: chicken prosciutto slaw stuffed jacket potatoes
chicken prosciutto slaw stuffed jacket potatoes recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Prick the potatoes all over with a fork, rub with a little olive oil and season with salt. Bake directly on the oven rack for 1hr, until the skin is crispy and the insides are fluffy.
Meanwhile, pull the meat from the chicken legs and roughly chop along with the prosciutto parsnips. Add the slaw and Dijon mustard and mix everything together.
Split the jacket potatoes down the middle and fill generously with the chicken mix. Snip over some chives and serve.

name: Chicken, Spinach & Cheddar Soup
description: If you want to eat your greens and hit your protein, this one’s for you. Shredded chicken in a vibrant green broth, topped with quick pickled onions for added zing.
instructions: Finely slice the red onion and add to a bowl with the juice of ¼ the lemon and a pinch of salt. Mix and set aside.

Finely dice the white onion and celery, and mince the garlic. Melt the butter in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook for 6-7 mins until soft and jammy. Add the garlic, coriander and chilli flakes and cook for another 3-4 mins, until the garlic is soft.

Add the frozen spinach and chicken stock and bring to a gentle simmer. Once the spinach has defrosted and the broth is simmering, add the chicken thighs and gently simmer for 20 mins until cooked through. Then, remove the chicken and use two forks to shred.
Pour the broth mixture into a blender then add the fresh spinach and grate in the Cheddar. Blend on high until vivid green and smooth. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
To serve, add the shredded chicken to a bowl and pour over the broth. Top with the pickled onions, a crack of black pepper and some extra grated Cheddar, if you like. Serve with toasted sourdough.

If batch cooking for the week, transfer the leftover chicken and broth to a container and the pickled onions to another. It will keep in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat the chicken and broth together until piping hot before serving.

name: Chicken, Spinach & Cheddar Soup
description: If you want to eat your greens and hit your protein, this one’s for you. Shredded chicken in a vibrant green broth, topped with quick pickled onions for added zing.
instructions: Finely slice the red onion and add to a bowl with the juice of ¼ the lemon and a pinch of salt. Mix and set aside.

Finely dice the white onion and celery, and mince the garlic. Melt the butter in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook for 6-7 mins until soft and jammy. Add the garlic, coriander and chilli flakes and cook for another 3-4 mins, until the garlic is soft.

Add the frozen spinach and chicken stock and bring to a gentle simmer. Once the spinach has defrosted and the broth is simmering, add the chicken thighs and gently simmer for 20 mins until cooked through. Then, remove the chicken and use two forks to shred.
Pour the broth mixture into a blender then add the fresh spinach and grate in the Cheddar. Blend on high until vivid green and smooth. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
To serve, add the shredded chicken to a bowl and pour over the broth. Top with the pickled onions, a crack of black pepper and some extra grated Cheddar, if you like. Serve with toasted sourdough.

If batch cooking for the week, transfer the leftover chicken and broth to a container and the pickled onions to another. It will keep in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat the chicken and broth together until piping hot before serving.

name: Chicken, Tomato & Mozzarella Traybake
description: Most traybakes are normally crunchy and crispy. We added some mozzarella for a delicious, stringy, cheesy hit. Fresh basil at the end is sublime.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.

Into a large baking tray add the tomatoes, peppers, the chicken thighs and the Kalamata olives. Tear the ciabatta into crouton size pieces then, add to the tray. Next, take the cloves from your bulb of garlic and add to the tray (no need to peel them). Pour a large glug of olive oil over the ingredients, ensuring each is coated. Sprinkle of a large pinch of salt and pepper, and then add the chilli flakes.
Time to get hands on. Rub all of the ingredients in the tray, ensuring everything is covered in oil and seasoning, before placing in the oven for 30 minutes.
Once 30 minutes is up, remove the tray. Toss the ingredients, basting them in the sauce. Place back into the oven for 15 minutes.

Remove from the oven, and toss the ingredients again and drain any excess liquid from the tray. Take your mozzarella balls and tear into little pieces. Scatter these across the top of the traybake. Drizzle the traybake with olive oil once more then, put it under the grill for 5 minutes.
Take the traybake out and set aside. Roughly chop up the basil. Plate up with a sprinkling of basil and enjoy!

name: Chicken, Tomato & Olive Stew with Cinnamon Brown Rice
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This juicy chicken stew is inspired by big Greek flavours, with kalamata olives and cinnamon-spiced rice. You are going to love it.
instructions: Thinly slice the garlic, quarter the tomatoes and drain the olives.

Place a saucepan with a drizzle of oil onto medium heat. Once hot, add the garlic and cook until fragrant. Stir through the chilli flakes, oregano, tomatoes and break in the chicken stock cubes. Top with the whole chicken breasts, pour over the water and squeeze in the tomato purée. Bring the mixture to a boil. Once boiling, add the olives, give it a stir, pop a lid on. Turn the heat down to low and simmer for 20 mins until the chicken is cooked through.

Once the chicken is cooked, transfer the breasts onto a chopping board (keep the stew on the heat) and shred using two forks. Return the chicken to the saucepan, and let it reduce for another 20-25 mins, stirring occasionally. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Before serving, stir through ¾ of the parsley through the stew.
Meanwhile, add a cinnamon stick into the cooked rice and reheat. Cover and set aside so the cinnamon can infuse into the rice. Thinly slice the parsley, stalks and all.
Serve the rice between bowls and ladle over the stew. Finish with a scattering of the remaining parsley.

name: Chicken-Fried Steak
description: The only thing better than fried chicken or steak? Chicken-fried steak. A classic from the American Deep South.
instructions: Grab two sheets of baking parchment. Trim the fat cap from your sirloin steaks and sandwich the meat between the two parchment sheets. Use a rolling pin or heavy based pan to bash the steaks out until they’re very thin.

Combine the bread flour and chicken, cayenne, garlic and onion powders in a bowl and season generously with salt and lots of black pepper. Crack the eggs into a large bowl and season with salt and hot sauce. Whisk together.

Dredge the steaks with the dry flour mix and then pass through the beaten egg and then move back into the dry mixture. Press the flour into the steaks, adding a little extra egg mixture to help improve the texture. Make sure you get lots of crackled texture on the dredge by scrunching the steaks in the flour like you might with fried chicken. Dust a tray with some of the flower mixture and lay the breaded steaks on top. Let them rest for 10-15 mins to set the crust.

While the steaks rest, make the gravy. Add the butter to a small saucepan and set over a medium heat. Melt and then tip in the flour. Whisk the flour through the butter and cook for 6-7 mins until toasty and lightly browned. Add the chicken stock, whisking constantly, until fully incorporated and then bring the whole lot to the boil. Season with salt, pepper and more chicken powder to taste. Keep warm.

Working in batches, shallow fry the breaded steaks in vegetable oil at around 180°C until golden brown and super crispy. They should take about 3-4 mins per side. Darin on kitchen paper and keep warm in a low oven while you fry the remaining steaks.

Add warm mash and steamed corn (if using) to plates before topping with a chicken fried steak and a healthy ladle of piping hot gravy. Finish with a few extra twists of pepper before getting stuck in.

name: Chickpea & Harissa Stew with Poached Cod & Breadcrumbs
description: A quick and spicy chickpea stew with poached cod and crispy lemon panko breadcrumbs. An incredibly satisfying weeknight meal. Harissa + cod = the perfect match.
keywords: Chickpea & Harissa Stew with Poached Cod & Breadcrumbs Recipe
Chickpea & Harissa Stew with Poached Cod & Breadcrumbs
instructions: Heat a glug of olive oil in a wide-based frying pan set over medium heat. Finely chop the onions and add to the pan with a pinch of salt and cook for 4-5 mins until soft. Finely slice the garlic and cook for another 1-2 mins until softened but not browned.

Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 8-10 mins until softened but still holding their shape. Stir in the harissa, allowing it to bubble for a few mins before adding the tinned tomatoes, drained chickpeas and vegetable stock, squashing a few tomatoes with the back of a fork to thicken the sauce. Let it simmer for 8-10 mins.
Drizzle the cod fillets with olive oil, season with salt, and nestle them into the sauce. Cover and cook for 5-7 mins until the fish is cooked through.
To make the breadcrumbs, heat a glug of olive oil in a frying pan, add the breadcrumbs with a pinch of salt, and fry for 4-5 mins until crisp. Stir in the zest of the lemon.
To serve, divide the cod and chickpeas between bowls and top with the crispy breadcrumbs, a dollop of yoghurt, a drizzle of extra olive oil, and a few coriander leaves.

name: Chickpea & Paneer Curry
description: Paneer was made for curries. And this simple yet incredibly fragrant chickpea curry with soft chunks of paneer is proof. Serve with fluffy Tilda Basmati Rice.
instructions: Start by cutting the paneer into 2cm chunks. Heat a tbsp of oil in a large saucepan and sear the paneer until browned all over. Once ready, remove and set aside.
Thinly slice the onions.
Blend the garlic, ginger and chillies with a splash of water until you have a smooth paste.

Heat a glug of oil in the saucepan over a medium heat and add the cumin, black mustard and fenugreek seeds. When they start to crackle and pop, add the sliced onions and a big pinch of salt. Cook for 6-7 mins.
Now add the garlic, ginger and chilli paste and cook out for another 4-5 mins.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder and garam masala.
Add the chickpeas and all of the liquid from the jar.
Cook for 10-12 mins.
Add the paneer and the cream and cook for another 10 mins.
Season and stir through chopped coriander.
Reheat the rice and serve with the curry.

name: Chickpea & Tofu Tikka Masala
description: Charred tofu chunks and saucy chickpeas in a creamy, spiced tikka sauce. It’s hearty, punchy, and tastes even better the next day.
instructions: Heat the grill to high.

Add half of the tikka paste to a bowl. Tear the tofu into chunky pieces and toss it through the paste. Season well with salt and pepper. Spread out on a foil-lined baking tray and slide under the grill for about 15 mins until golden and lightly charred.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for about 10 mins until soft and golden.
Stir in the remaining tikka paste and cook for a couple of minutes until fragrant.

Pour in the chopped tomatoes and coconut milk. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 mins. You can blitz the sauce smooth here with a stick blender if you want it silky or you can just leave it chunky.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then add them to the pan along with the grilled tofu. Simmer for another 5 mins to warm through.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, then serve up and scatter with fresh coriander leaves.

name: Chickpea & Tuna Salad
description: The perfect make-ahead meal, this warm salad is loaded with chickpeas and tuna for a flavour-heavy, healthy little number that's ideal for spring.
instructions: Empty the jar of chickpeas into a pan, water and all. Set over a medium heat and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 mins then turn off the heat and set aside.

Cut the tomatoes into even-sized chunks. Cut the peppers into strips and thinly slice the red onion. Chuck the lot into a bowl, season generously with salt and pepper and squeeze over the juice of a lemon. Throw in a splash of the pepper liquid, and toss everything together.
Drain the warm chickpeas and add to the salad along with the tuna and a dash of oil from the tin. Toss through the rocket and leaves from the basil.
Season, add 50ml of olive oil and more lemon juice if needed. Divide between warm plates and serve.

name: Chickpea Aguachile Verde
description: A bright and citrussy vegetarian aguachile recipe that requires absolutely zero cooking. This makes a lovely fresh side or a light main.
instructions: Dice the cucumber into 1cm pieces, then halve and finely slice the red onion.

Add the red onion to a bowl with the juice of a lime and a pinch of salt, give it a good mix with your hands and set aside. Slice the jalapeños and roughly the coriander – stalks and all, saving some leaves for garnish.

Add most of the cucumber to a blender along with the coriander, garlic, miso and two-thirds of the jalapeños. Squeeze in the juice of the remaining limes, then add the cold water and a couple of ice cubes if you have them. Blend until smooth, then taste and season with salt before chilling.
When you are ready to serve, halve, peel and slice the avocado then drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Pour the chilled aguachile into a large bowl and top with the chickpeas, avocado, remaining cucumber, pickled red onion and coriander leaves. Scoop up with the tortilla chips and enjoy.

name: Chickpea Curry
description: Sam Wise & Damnshaq knocking it out the park with their creamy coconut spiced chickpea curry. Tuck in with a toasted roti. Bob is your uncle.
instructions: Prepare your vegetables. Finely chop your spring onions, brown onions, garlic and scotch bonnet.

Heat a glug of sunflower oil in a pan and add the chopped veg (saving 1/3 of the spring onions for the couscous). Once the onions have softened, add in the fenugreek seeds and both the hot and mild curry powder. Fry for a couple of minutes.
Peel and chop your potatoes and carrots into small chunks and add them into the pan.
Drain the chickpeas and toss them through the sauce. Pour in your coconut milk, mix it together, and leave this to simmer for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, get your couscous on. Pour the dry couscous into a bowl, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and grate the zest of a lemon. Add boiling water to the couscous (enough to cover), wrap it in cling film and leave it to sit for 10 minutes. Once the couscous has absorbed the water stir it around and put into the fridge to cool.
Back to the curry. Add in the Maggi sauce and spinach, then cover with foil and leave to steam.
Whilst your curry is steaming, chop up both of your sweet chilli peppers, remove your couscous from the fridge and fold through along with the rest of your spring onions and crumbled feta.
Toast all of your rotis.
Remove the foil from the curry and give it a final stir.
Time to dish up! Place your couscous and curry on a plate and get dipping with your roti. Sam Wise and Damnshaq also chopped up an avocado to serve on the side. Enjoy!

name: Chickpea Palak Paneer
description: This spicy, comforting vegetarian curry comes in at a whopping 41g of protein per portion.
instructions: Dice the paneer and the tomatoes. Finely dice the onion, chop the chilli and finely grate the ginger and garlic.
Blanch ½ of the spinach in a pot of boiling water for 1 min then add to a blender with ½ of the chickpeas. Blitz until smooth.

Heat the ghee in a large pot set over a medium heat and add the onion. Cook for 10 min, then add the chilli, ginger and garlic. Cook for another minute or so. Add the tomatoes and cook for a couple of minutes until softened then add the garam masala. Add ⅕ of the water, season with salt, and cook until everything is totally soft and the oil is separating from the sauce.

Add the blended spinach and remaining chickpeas along with the remaining water and simmer for 5-7 mins. Add in the remaining fresh spinach and leave to wilt. Squeeze in the lemon and stir then season with salt and pepper to taste.
Meanwhile, heat a glug of oil in a medium pan over a medium heat. Add the paneer and fry for about 4 mins until golden and crispy.
Divide the curried chickpeas between bowls and top with the crispy paneer. Serve with the yoghurt and fresh coriander, and some rice if you like.

name: Chickpea Pancakes with Tamarind Salad
description: Loaded up with the freshest, zingiest salad, these chickpea pancakes are an ideal healthy midweek dinner. They are inspired by Gujarati pancakes called pudla.
instructions: Add your gram flour to a bowl along with your cumin seeds, then pour in 260ml of water and a pinch of salt. Mix to a batter, then leave to sit for 30 mins.
Cut your cucumber in half. Grate one half, then pop it in a sieve set over a bowl. Add some salt, and leave to allow any excess liquid to drain out for 20 mins.
Finely dice your tomatoes, cucumber and red onion. Deseed your pomegranate in half.
Finely chop your green chillies and mint.
Drain your chickpeas. Add your tomatoes, chickpeas, diced cucumber, ½ of your chopped chilli and red onion to a bowl. Add your tamarind sauce and a pinch of salt, then give it a good mix.

Back to your grated cucumber. Discard any excess liquid, then pop your cucumber in a bowl. Add your yoghurt, mint and ½ of your chopped green chilli, along with a pinch of salt, then give it a good mix.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat.

Add a little oil, then add a ladle of your batter, and swirl it round the pan until it forms an even layer. Cook for 1 min, then flip over like a pancake. Cook for a minute on the next side. Remove from the pan, then repeat with your remaining batter.
Place your pancake on a plate, then fill with your yoghurt and salad mixture. Fold the pancake over and serve!

name: Chickpea Peanut Butter Curry
description: All you need is 20 minutes to make this rich and creamy vegan peanut butter curry. The secret ingredient for injecting extra flavour is a splash of soy sauce.
instructions: The tip for actually getting this done in 20 mins is the prep. So start by mincing the garlic and ginger (no need to peel the ginger). Finely dice the onion and drain the chickpeas. Finely slice the chilli and finely chop the coriander, including the stems. Get the peanut butter opened with a spoon in there ready to scoop out. Measure out the spices into a small bowl and keep your salt and pepper to hand.

Grab a large pot and gather all of your ingredients so they are close by. Heat a good drizzle of olive oil on medium heat and add the chopped onion. Cook for 3 mins, then add the ginger and garlic and cook for another 2 mins, stirring often.
Add the spices, stir and cook for 30 seconds.
Then add the tinned tomatoes and break them up in the pan with a spatula as best you can. Don’t worry if there are bigger pieces, this adds a nice texture. Add the coconut milk and drained chickpeas.

Add the spinach, peanut butter and soy sauce and turn up the heat slightly. Let it bubble away, stirring occasionally, for a few minutes until thickened. When ready, take it off the heat, stir through the coriander, taste and season well with salt and pepper.
Top with the lime juice, fresh chilli, and chopped peanuts and vegan yoghurt, if using.

name: Chickpea Puttanesca
description: A chickpea twist on a classic dish - the mighty puttanesca. Salty capers and anchovies, big juicy kalamata olives, rich tomato sauce. You won’t miss pasta.
instructions: Finely chop the anchovies (keeping the oil in the jar), garlic and parsley stalks (keep the leaves separate).
Heat the anchovy oil from the tin in a pan and add the chilli flakes, chopped garlic, and anchovies. Simmer this down until the anchovies begin to dissolve.

Whack in your parsley stalks and pour in your tinned tomatoes and chickpeas. Break up the tomatoes with a wooden spoon and mix together with the tomato purée. Leave to simmer for 10 minutes until the chickpeas soften and you get a lovely thick, rich sauce.
Add in your capers and olives.
Stir through your parsley leaves (saving some for garnish).
Season with salt and pepper then serve with some parsley leaves scattered on top and a drizzle of olive oil. Enjoy!

name: Chickpea Tikka Masala Wraps
description: The curried onion, peppers and chickpeas combine with the speedy coriander sauce, yoghurt and lettuce for an absolute vibe. Use dairy-free yoghurt and wraps to keep this one plant based.
instructions: Toast the cumin seeds in a large frying pan over a medium heat until smelling amazing then tip into a blender or mini food processor. Roughly chop the ginger, green chilli and coriander (stalks and all). Add this too, along with the zest and juice of 1 lime, 2 tbsp neutral oil and 2-3 tbsp water. Blitz to a smooth green chutney, adding the final tbsp of water if needed, season to taste.

Slice the onions and peppers. Pour a good drizzle of neutral oil back into the same frying pan (no need to wash in between), scrape in the onions and peppers and fry over a medium to high heat for 6-8 mins until softened and getting caramelised.

Drain the chickpeas, add to the frying pan then stir in the curry paste. Cook, stirring for a couple of minutes or so to cook out the raw curry paste then squeeze in the remaining lime juice. Remove from the heat and season to taste.
Finely slice the iceberg lettuce.
Heat the wraps to your liking – if you have a gas stove then warming them directly over the flame creates a nice char.

Spread the yoghurt across the middle of each wrap then pile on the tikka masala chickpea mix. Top with the lettuce, coriander dressing and pomegranate seeds, if using. Roll into thick wraps, to serve.

name: Chickpea, Charred Corn & Roasted Pepper Salad
description: Chickpeas, charred corn and roasted red peppers come together to make a balanced weeknight meal ready in just 35 mins.
instructions: Microwave the rice according to packet instructions.
Meanwhile, drain the red peppers and thinly slice. Cut the kernels off the corn, pick the leaves off the herbs and finely slice the stems. Peel and finely dice the onion. Halve the tomatoes.
Add the onion into a large bowl with the zest of half a lemon and the juice of both. Season with salt and pepper, stir in 30ml of olive oil. Set aside.
Place a frying pan over high heat, no oil. Once hot, add half the corn kernels and cook until starting to char, 3-4 mins.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Add all the corn, roasted peppers, tomatoes, rice, chickpeas, chopped stems and herbs into the onion dressing, toss together. Season with salt and pepper.
Share the salad between your plates, finish with a drizzle of oil and any remaining herbs.

name: Chickpea, Tahini & Harissa High Protein Smash
description: Up your daily protein intake with this delicious smoosh. It's packed with Middle Eastern flavours like tahini and harissa.
instructions: Dice the peppers into small cubes and finely chop the parsley.
Combine all of the ingredients in a bowl (juicing in the lemon) and season with a generous amount of salt and pepper.
'Smoosh’ it over toast, pitta bread, a bagel or whatever you fancy. Sprinkle over some sesame seeds and any remaining parsley and enjoy.

name: Chilled Cherry Rice Pudding
description: A sultry chilled rice pudding topped with fresh cherries. Desserts don't get much more crispy and refreshing than this.
instructions: Halve the cherries and transfer to a small saucepan with a fifth of the caster sugar and the water. Place over a medium heat and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 8 mins until softened. Remove from the heat and squeeze in the juice from half the lemon. Set aside.
Mix the milk, cream, vanilla, cinnamon and zest of the lemon together in a bowl.

We’re going to cook this a bit like a risotto. Melt the butter in a large saucepan over a medium heat, add the rice and toast for a couple of minutes, then pour in the milk mix. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 mins.
Whisk the egg yolks and remaining caster sugar together in a bowl until pale, then take about 3 tbsp of the hot milk from the simmering rice, add to the yolks, mix well and set aside.

After about 20-25 mins, when the rice is cooked through but still al dente and most of the liquid has been absorbed, add the egg yolk mix to the rice and continue to cook, stirring continuously, for another 2-3 mins until the mixture is thick.

You can serve this hot or cold. If you're going for cold, divide the mix between small bowls or glasses, top it with cling film, and chill it in the fridge until it's cold. When you’re ready to serve, top with the cherries and then roughly chop and sprinkle over the pistachios.

name: Chilled Chicken Noodle Salad
description: Chilled soba noodles, juicy poached chicken leftovers and loads of crunchy veg, tossed with a chilli crisp dressing. A perfect heatwave meal.
instructions: Make the Poached Chicken & Ginger Broth.
Cook the noodles following pack instructions. Drain and rinse under cold water until completely cool. Set aside.
Shred the chicken and set aside. Peel the carrots and julienne both them and the cucumber into matchsticks. Thinly slice the spring onions and roughly chop the coriander.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, rice vinegar and chilli crisp. Taste and tweak with a pinch of salt if needed.
In a large bowl, toss the noodles with the dressing. Add the shredded chicken, carrots and cucumber. Give everything a gentle mix.
Top with spring onions, coriander and sesame seeds. Serve cold or at room temp.

name: Chilled Coconut Brothy Noodles
description: A perfect summer recipe, the brothy noodles are served up ice cold with refreshing herbs and loads of lime juice.
instructions: Heat your frying pan on medium, then finely slice the garlic. Fry the garlic for 2 mins, then add the curry paste, cooking for another 30 seconds. Pour the coconut milk into a blender with the fried curry paste, juice of 4 limes and the peanut butter. Blitz until smooth, thin out with water, then season generously with salt. Blend in a handful of ice cubes and blitz, and put in the fridge. If you don’t have ice cubes just blast it in the freezer before transferring to the fridge.

Slice your cucumbers on a sharp diagonal then chop into matchsticks. Finely slice the mint, then add to a bowl along with the cucumbers. Add the juice of the remaining lime, then the sesame seeds and season with salt. Finely slice the spring onions and cook the noodles according to package instructions, then rinse in cold water.
Plate up the noodles and pour over the chilled broth. Top with the cucumbers, spring onions, coriander and chilli oil.

name: Chilled Green Peanut & Aubergine Noodles
description: This is a really nice cold noodle dish that features tender aubergines and creamy tahini. It's a good one for a hot summer's day.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut the aubergine into batons, transfer to a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil before seasoning with salt and pepper. Cook in the oven for 20-25 mins until charred.

Meanwhile, put the tahini into a blender with the juice of both limes, miso paste, soy sauce, just a splash of water and a handful of ice cubes. Blitz until smooth, then add the coriander and remaining water. Blitz again until combined, then check and adjust the seasoning if needed.
When you’re ready to eat, cook the noodles following pack instructions, then drain and rinse in cold water to stop the cooking process. Toss the noodles in the sesame oil and set aside.
Halve the tomatoes. Finely slice the spring onions. Crush the peanuts.
Share the coriander broth between serving bowls, then top with the noodles, peanuts, aubergine batons, chilli oil and spring onions. Give it a good mix and get stuck in.

name: Chilli Cheese Bites
description: These cheesy molten cheese bites are incredibly addictive. Get ready for your new obsession.
instructions: Drain and finely chop the pickled and fresh jalapeños. Grate the cheeses and finely chop the American cheese slices.

Put a medium saucepan over a medium-high heat, add the butter and let it melt. Stir in the flour and mix well, cooking for 2 mins until it smells nutty. Gradually whisk in the milk until a smooth sauce forms. Let it come to a bubble for 2 mins, then take it off the heat before stirring through the jalapeños, cheese and mustard. Taste and season with salt and pepper, then tip into a large baking dish. Cover with cling film, making sure it touches the surface, and chill for a minimum of 3 hrs, or overnight if you have time.
Once chilled and set, roll 1 tbsp of mixture into a ball and place it on a baking sheet. Repeat until you have used all of the mixture, then return the croquettes to the fridge.
Next, prepare the breading station by cracking the eggs into a bowl and whisking together. Put the flour in another bowl and season with salt and pepper, then add the breadcrumbs to a third bowl.
Coat each croquette in flour, then egg and finally breadcrumbs. Bread the croquettes for a second time (egg first, then breadcrumbs). Set on a baking sheet and put into the freezer for 15 mins.

Heat the oven to 150°C. Heat a generous glug of oil in a small saucepan (don’t fill it more than ½ the way up) over a medium-high heat. Once at 170°C, add the croquettes three at a time and fry for 2-3 mins until crisp and golden.
Transfer the croquettes to a baking tray and chuck into the oven for 10 mins. Keep checking to make sure they don't explode!

name: Chilli Cheese Paratha
description: This Indian snack is oozing with molten cheese and chilli garlicky goodness. They will be demolished in seconds, I can promise you that. Seema x
instructions: Combine the plain flour, a pinch of salt and hot water (from the kettle) in a bowl and mix with a wooden spoon. Once it is cool enough to handle, knead the dough for 5 minutes until smooth. Pour in a tablespoon of oil and knead through. Cover and rest for 10 minutes

Meanwhile, prepare the garlic chilli oil. Grate the garlic into a small microwaveable bowl with the chilli powder, ¼ teaspoon salt and 2 tablespoons of oil. Microwave for 1 minute to soften and cook the garlic.
Roughly chop your coriander and finely slice your spring onions.
Divide the dough into quarters, and then the quarters into halves to form eight even balls.

Roll two balls into large circles about 2mm thick so they are about the same size. Spread ½ a teaspoon of the chilli garlic paste on to one circle, sprinkle on a handful of shredded mozzarella and shredded cheddar. Sprinkle on your coriander and spring onions, then press a second dough circle on top – you can use some water along the edges to help it stick if you need it too
Heat up a frying pan and pour in a small glug of oil. Slap on the paratha and cook on a high heat on both sides for 2 minutes. Flip using a large spatula.
Cut into quarters and serve whilst still hot and oozing with cheese.

name: Chilli Cheese Spud Salad
description: Bonjour! Willy here, this is my recipe for an absolutely mental chilli cheese jalapeño spud salad.
instructions: Boil your spuds in boiling salted water until tender, this will take around 13 mins.
Meanwhile, grate the cheese and finely chop the spring onions, chives and red onion.
Combine the veggies (saving a handful of chives) and mayo in a bowl and give it a mix. Chuck in the jalapeños and season to taste.
Drain the cooked spuds and while they’re still warm, add the grated cheese and toss together.
Now stir through the mayo mixture and divide between plates.
Top with your remaining chives and a handful of crispy onions.
Smashing.

name: Chilli Chocolate Con Carne
description: A slow-cooked chilli with a delicious hint of rich dark chocolate. Give it go!
instructions: Heat a splash of olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan set over a medium heat, then brown the beef in two batches on all sides. Once cooked, remove the beef from the pan. Finely slice the onions and add half of them to the pan with another glug of olive oil. Cook for 5 mins until starting to soften. Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic and chop the red pepper into 2cm pieces.

Add the garlic and red pepper to the pan and cook for 2 mins, then add the cumin, smoked paprika, chilli flakes and tomato purée. Cook for 1-2 mins, then pour in the chopped tomatoes, beef stock and drained and rinsed kidney beans. Return the beef to the pan, give it a stir and bring to the boil. Reduce to a simmer, cover with a lid and cook for 3-3½ hrs until the beef is falling apart and tender. Once cooked, give it a good mix and it will start to break up.

Grate the chocolate into the chilli, mixing well, then season with salt and pepper. Roughly chop the coriander. Serve the chilli in bowls topped with soured cream, the remaining onion, coriander and extra chilli flakes.

name: Chilli Con Carne Enchiladas
description: Elevate our Beef Chilli Con Carne batch recipe with these indulgent enchiladas. Stuffed with creamy ricotta and and baked until bubbling and golden. A perfect midweek feast if you ask us.
instructions: Make the Beef Chilli Con Carne.
Heat the oven to 200°C.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta with half the grated cheddar and a good pinch of salt and black pepper.
Thinly slice the red onion and place it into a bowl with the lime juice. Season with salt, toss together and set aside to pickle.
Spoon the ricotta mixture evenly down the centre of each tortilla, then roll them up and place seam-side down into a small baking dish.
Pour the beef chilli over the top, spreading it to cover the enchiladas. Sprinkle over the remaining cheddar.
Bake for 20 mins until the cheese is melted, golden and everything is bubbling.
Spoon onto plates and serve with the pickled red onions and a wedge of lime.

name: Chilli Con Carne Soup with Crispy Cheese Croutons
description: Turn your leftover Beef Chilli Con Carne into a hearty, smoky soup topped with crunchy cheddar shards. It's warming, filling and a little bit indulgent.
keywords: beef chilli soup with crispy cheddar croutons
instructions: Before you begin, make the Beef Chilli Con Carne batch recipe.
Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stalks.
Set a saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the tomato purée and coriander stalks. Cook, stirring, for a couple of minutes until the purée darkens.
Pour in the beef stock and beef chilli. Leave to simmer for 15–20 mins, then taste and season with salt and black pepper.

Meanwhile, coarsely grate the cheddar. Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, sprinkle in the cheese in an even layer. Let it melt until lacy and golden, then sprinkle over the cumin seeds. Cook for another 2 mins until golden and crisp at the edges. Transfer to a rack to cool completely, it will crisp up further as it cools.
