description: An unbeatable chocolate brownie recipe. Whisking the eggs and sugar whips air into the batter gives the brownie a thin, almost meringue-like, texture on top.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a 23x23cm baking pan/tin and line the inside with parchment paper, creating a slight overhang so you can lift the brownies out once baked.

In a medium bowl, combine the butter and chocolate. Place the bowl over a pot of gently simmering water. Stir the mixture occasionally until it has completely melted. Remove the bowl from the pot and allow the mixture to cool for 10 mins. It’s really important to let it cool to prevent it from scrambling the eggs when you add them.

In the large bowl of a stand mixer with the whisk attached, combine the eggs, egg yolks, granulated/caster sugar, and light brown sugar. Whisk for 3 to 4 mins or until the mixture becomes pale and fluffy. This is the secret to getting that nice shiny top on your brownies! (You can also mix these ingredients with an electric hand mixer.)

Once it is thick, very very slowly drizzle in the cooled melted chocolate mixture while still whisking on a low speed. It's important to do this slowly so the eggs can slowly adjust to the temperature of the warm chocolate.
Once the chocolate has completely incorporated, sieve in the flour, cocoa powder and salt. Use a hand whisk to gently mix these in until no more dry ingredients are visible. Don’t over mix.
Pour the batter into the pan/tin, spreading it to the edges. Sprinkle the chocolate chunks and a pinch of sea salt flakes over the top.
Place the pan/tin in the oven and bake for 24 or 27 mins. A wooden skewer inserted in the middle should still come out slightly wet.
Remove the pan/tin from the oven and allow the brownies to cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for 30 mins.
Carefully lift the cooled brownies from the tray and use a hot knife to cut them into slices before serving.

name: Chocolate Coconut Bars
description: All the chocolatey coconut vibes of that nostalgic treat, with a bounty of flavour in every bite. Make ahead for the ultimate pud or a quick snack to keep you going all week.
instructions: Fill a saucepan with a little water and set it over a medium heat. Break the chocolate into a heatproof bowl, add the coconut oil, then place it on top of the pan (making sure the base doesn’t touch the water). Let everything melt gently, stirring until smooth.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the shredded coconut, coconut cream, maple syrup, coconut oil, vanilla extract and a pinch of sea salt. Mix until it all comes together – it should hold its shape when pressed.
Use your hands to form the mixture into 8 to 10 bars. Place them on a baking tray lined with baking parchment and freeze for 10-15 mins until firm.
Once the bars are set, dip each one into the melted chocolate until fully coated. Lay them back on the tray.

Sprinkle with extra shredded coconut and a little flaky salt, if using. Pop in the fridge again for about 15 mins until the chocolate sets. Once ready, wrap the bars in baking paper and chill or freeze until needed (these last for a week in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer).

name: Chocolate Fondant Cake Recipe
description: For a classic chocolate fondant, you need ramekins. We took the recipe for the perfect melt-in-the-middle dessert and made it in a roasting tin. You're welcome.
instructions: Heat your oven to 160°C fan. Chop the butter into small cubes and add to a mixing bowl. Finely chop the chocolate and add to the bowl.
Butter a 20cm x 30cm roasting tin, then add a tbsp of cocoa powder and shake around the tin so the cocoa dusts the surface. Tip out any excess.

Add 5cm of water to the base of a small saucepan, bring to the boil then turn down the heat to a simmer. Place the bowl of chocolate and butter on top of the saucepan and gently melt, stirring regularly. Stir in the cocoa powder, vanilla essence, and a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Separate ¼ of the eggs, so you're left with just the yolks and add to a separate bowl with remaining  whole eggs and sugar. Use an electric whisk to whip the until the mixture is light and fluffy. Fold in the chocolate mixture, using a spatula to mix the two together. Try not to knock out too much of the air you’ve whipped into the eggs!

Use a sieve to dust the flour over the top of the mix. Fold the flour through the mix, making sure there are no white streaks of flour and the mix is homogenous. Tip into a prepared dish. Give it a wiggle to level out the mixture.
Bake for 18-20 mins, until it’s set around the edges with a decent wobble in the middle. Dust with cocoa powder and finish with a pinch of sea salt. Serve straight away with ice cream.

name: Chocolate Ganache Filling
description: Ganache is a velvety mixture of chocolate and cream used in lots of baking recipes to fill truffles, pies and tarts. Here’s how to make it.
instructions: Roughly chop the dark chocolate and chop the butter into cubes. Add both to a bowl with a pinch of sea salt and set aside.

Heat the cream in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of boiling water until it starts to simmer. Your aim is to heat the cream until it’s just hot enough to melt chocolate but not much hotter, so keep a close eye on it and don’t allow it to boil – it’s ready when it starts to bubble up just at the edge.

Remove from the heat and add the chocolate and butter, stirring to bring together and melt the chocolate. If necessary you can return the mixture to the double boiler very briefly, but make sure it doesn’t overheat or it will split. If your ganache splits, add some chilled cream and whisk hard to try to bring the emulsion back together.
Allow it to cool slightly before spreading over cakes.

name: Chocolate Ganache Glaze
description: Ganache is a velvety mixture of chocolate and cream used in lots of baking recipes to give cakes a smooth shiny glaze. Here’s how to make it.
instructions: Roughly chop the dark chocolate and chop the butter into cubes. Add both to a bowl with a pinch of sea salt and set aside.

Heat the cream in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of boiling water until it starts to simmer. Your aim is to heat the cream until it’s just hot enough to melt chocolate but not much hotter, so keep a close eye on it and don’t allow it to boil – it’s ready when it starts to bubble up just at the edge.

Remove from the heat and add the chocolate and butter, stirring to bring together and melt the chocolate. If necessary you can return the mixture to the double boiler very briefly, but make sure it doesn’t overheat or it will split. If your ganache splits, add some chilled cream and whisk hard to try to bring the emulsion back together.
Allow it to cool slightly before spreading over cakes.

name: Chocolate Hazelnut Doughnuts
description: Treat yourself, or someone you love, to my glorious chocolate and hazelnut doughnuts. These babies are stuffed to the brim and will melt your heart. Seema x
instructions: Warm the milk and sugar together in a saucepan until the mixture is just lukewarm – test this with your finger, it should be just warm to the touch.
Stir in the yeast and allow it to sit for 5-10 mins until it starts to foam slightly. This will let you know if your yeast is still alive.
In a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook, combine the flour and a pinch of salt.
Add in the yeasty milk and eggs and mix on a medium speed for 5 mins until the dough comes away from the side of the bowl.
Cover the dough in the bowl with a clean tea towel or cling film and allow it to relax for 5 mins.

Run your stand mixer again on a medium-high speed and spoon in 1 tsp of butter at a time until it’s absorbed into the dough. Your butter must be soft enough to push your finger through otherwise it won’t combine with the dough.
Knead the dough in the mixer for 8 mins on a medium speed to form a smooth and shiny dough.
Cover with a kitchen towel and allow the dough to rise until doubled in size. This could take anywhere from 30 mins to 1 hour.
Now onto your filling. Break up the dark chocolate and put into a large bowl with your hazelnut spread. Heat the double cream in the microwave until piping hot and pour this over your chocolate.
Allow it to sit for 3 mins and then stir until it’s completely melted. Blast it in the microwave for 30 seconds if there are a few chocolate lumps.
Cover with cling film, pressing down on the filling. Put it into the fridge until you are ready to fill your doughnuts.
Punch the dough to release all the air and pull out large tangerine-sized balls (roughly 60g).
Flatten the ball onto a floured work surface and fold the outside into the middle. Turn the ball over and roll it into a smooth ball with your hands.

Put each dough ball onto a lined and greased baking sheet. Cover with cling film and allow to rise until doubled in size. This should take about 20 mins. When proven correctly, they will spring back halfway when you gently press the side with your index finger.
Meanwhile, heat a large pot of oil with a thermometer – the sweet spot is 165°C/329°F, so try to adjust the heat levels to stick to that number

Fry your doughnuts in the hot oil, splashing the tops of them with oil until they start to bubble. Cook on both sides for 2 mins until golden brown. If you see a white ring (i.e. the white ring of confidence) then your doughnuts will be light and airy!
Allow your doughnuts to cool for 15-20 mins.
Spoon a few tablespoons of your filling into a bowl and microwave for 30 secs until its melted.
Scoop the rest of your filling into a piping bag with a nozzle, any shape nozzle will do.
Once cool, dip your doughnuts into the microwaved filling on one side to create your iced top. Poke a hole in the side and fill them with the chocolate filling in your pipping bag.
Sprinkle with crushed hazelnuts and serve immediately.

name: Chocolate Hazelnut Stuffed Chocolate Cookies
description: We've made a homemade version of everyone's favourite chocolate and hazelnut spread and stuffed it inside a gooey, soft cookie dough.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Tip all the nuts (for the cookies and the Nutella) into a roasting tray and roast for 10-15 mins, until golden brown. Set aside to cool. Tip 100g of the nuts into a blender and blend until they have released their oils, this takes around 3 mins — you'll need to scrape the mix down every 30 secs. Melt 150g of the chocolate. Stir in the icing sugar, cocoa powder and melted chocolate to the blender and whiz briefly to combine. Scrape everything into a bowl and set aside to cool. Once firm enough to scoop, scoop out ½ tbsp portions onto a baking tray lined with baking paper, you should make 11-12 scoops. Cover and set aside in the fridge until solid.
Roughly chop the remaining hazelnuts and the remaining 150g of dark chocolate.

Cut the cold butter into cubes and beat with the sugar until combined (this step is best done with a stand or electric mixer, but also works by hand, you’ll just need some extra elbow grease), then add the eggs one at a time. In another bowl, combine the remaining ingredients with ½ tsp of salt. Pour the dry ingredients into the butter mixture, and combine. Roll the mix into 22-24 pucks (around 45g each).

Take a cookie dough puck and press a Nutella scoop into the middle of it, then press another puck on top and seal around the scoop. Roll into a ball and then squash slightly, cover and set aside in the fridge for at least 1 hour, preferably overnight.
Heat the oven to 200°C and bake for 12 mins. Finish with a sprinkle of salt as soon as they come out of the oven, then allow to cool to room temperature before eating.

name: Chocolate Orange Eton Mess
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

All your favourite bits of an eton mess, smashed meringue, soft whipped cream, fresh fruit, with the wintry flavours of chocolate orange. All from Aldi.
instructions: Heat the oven to 110°C. Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise or dressing). Put the egg whites, 220g caster sugar and the brown sugar into a large heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water.
Using an electric mixer, whisk the egg whites and sugar on a low speed, over the heat, until the sugar has dissolved.
Now crank up the speed and whisk until you have a thick meringue and all the sugar has dissolved. Remove the bowl from the pan, then keep whipping until cool.

Melt a third of the chocolate and swirl through the meringue. Plop 4 or 5 big spoonfuls of meringue onto a lined baking sheet and bake for 1 hour, and then leave to cool in the oven for at least 2 hours.
Roughly chop 90g of chocolate and place in a heatproof bowl. Bring 175ml of cream to a simmer and pour over the chocolate. Leave to stand for 30 seconds, add a pinch of salt and stir into a ganache.
Add the remaining cream to a large bowl and add the remaining caster sugar and the zest of one orange.
Segment the oranges.
Roughly break up your meringues and chuck into a big bowl, add the cream, orange segments and pour over the choc. Gently fold together and divide between plates. Get stuck in.

name: Chocolate Pecan Pie
description: Our riff on an American classic. This cinnamon, ginger and chocolate pecan pie is perfect for an autumnal dinner party or Thanksgiving feast.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C fan.
Add the pecan pieces to a baking tray (if you’re using whole pecans, roughly chop them first). Once the oven is preheated, toast the nuts for 5-7 mins then set aside to cool.

Break the chocolate into 2-3cm pieces. Melt the chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of gently boiling water. Stir until melted then remove the bowl from the heat and leave for a minute or two to cool slightly.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the butter, sugar, maple syrup, salt, ground cinnamon and ground ginger. Pour in the melted chocolate and mix to combine.
Use a whisk or spoon to beat together the mixture. Add the soured cream, whole eggs and egg yolk then beat to combine. Stir through the toasted pecan pieces.

Pour the mixture into the pre-cooked 20cm pastry case. Bake for 10 mins then turn the heat down to 140°C fan and bake for another 25-30 mins until golden brown. The filling should wobble a little in the centre when shaken.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool fully before serving.

name: Chocolate Sponge Birthday Cake
description: This chocolate cake recipe is deceptively simple but gives you a luxurious, rich, velvety sponge that is decadent and not too sweet. Perfect for a birthday party.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Grease 2 x 8 inch cake tins. Make up the coffee and leave it to cool. Make sure your butter is at room temperature.
In a large mixing bowl, use an electric whisk to beat together the olive oil, sugar & vanilla extract.
Crack in the eggs and add the milk and beat gently until well combined.
In a separate bowl, sift together the flour, cocoa powder, bicarb and salt. Sir until evenly combined, then beat into the batter until smooth.
Slowly add the cooled coffee and mix until just combined evenly.

Divide evenly between your two cake tins and bake for 25-30 mins or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Leave to cool for 10 mins in the tins then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

Meanwhile, make the chocolate buttercream. Beat the butter alone for 4–5 mins on high speed. Sift in the cocoa powder and beat until you have a paste. Beat in the icing sugar and add the vanilla, salt, milk and most of the cream then beat together slowly at first on a low speed to bring it together. Beat on high for another 2–3 mins until it’s a smooth consistency. Add more cream if desired.
Spread the buttercream over one sponge and pop the other one on top, sandwiching them together. Spread more buttercream over the top. Sprinkle over the chocolate flakes and some sea salt, if using.

name: Chocolate Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: You didn’t think sticky toffee pudding could get any better. It’s chocolatey, sticky and it’s so indulgent. What a delight.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a 33cm x 25cm baking tray with baking paper and rub the sides with oil.

Finely dice the dates and pop them into a pan. Cover with 400ml of boiling water and the bicarbonate of soda. Bring this to a boil on high and cook for 5 mins until the dates have softened and it looks like a paste.
Chop the chocolate into large chunks and melt 100g in the microwave, 30 seconds at a time stirring in between until it’s fully melted.

In a large bowl add in the plain flour and sift in the cocoa powder and baking powder. Crack in the eggs, along with the vegetable oil, dates, vanilla bean paste, light brown sugar, milk and melted chocolate. Whisk together until it’s all combined.
Fold in the chocolate chunks and pour this lined baking tray.
Bake for 25-30 mins until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.

Meanwhile, make the sticky toffee sauce. Melt the butter and light brown sugar in a saucepan and cook for 5 mins until it starts to caramelise and brown. Gently pour in the double cream and mix well. Season with ½ tsp flakey sea salt and keep warm.
When the cake is cooked, allow it to cool for 10 mins and then slice into pieces. Serve with the toffee sauce and more sea salt.

name: Chocolate Swiss Meringue Buttercream
description: A classic silky smooth chocolate buttercream made using egg whites. Perfect for sandwiching between cakes.
instructions: Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make mayonnaise and salad dressings). Then, add the sugar and egg whites to a heatproof mixing bowl. Cut the butter into cubes and set aside.

Fill a large saucepan ¼ of the way with water and set it over a medium-high heat until simmering. Place the bowl, with the sugar and eggs, on top of the saucepan (the bottom of the bowl shouldn’t touch the water) and whisk constantly until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is hot and no longer grainy to the touch (rub it between your fingers to check).
Transfer the mixture to a stand mixer and beat on the highest speed, until the bowl is completely cool to the touch and you have stiff peaks.

Switch to the paddle attachment (to avoid air bubbles) and add all the soft, cubed butter all at once. It's very important that the butter is soft and the same temperature as the meringue, otherwise you risk the mixture splitting. Leave the mixer on a medium speed until the mixture comes together (it may look split to start with, but don't worry it will come together), then turn down to low until you have a smooth buttercream. Add the cocoa powder and whip until incorporated.
If the mixture looks split, don't worry; put the whole bowl in the fridge for 10-15 mins then whip again.

name: Chocolate Tea
description: This cocoa tea recipe from Ranette Prime is a classic of Tobago. It's made with raw chocolate cocoa balls infused with warm spices, tonka bean, and lemongrass.
instructions: Put the raw cocoa nibs and 1 cinnamon stick in a pan and roast gently for 3 mins over a low-medium heat (this is to intensify the flavour). The nibs will begin to release a chocolate aroma.

Transfer the nibs to a mortar and pestle. Grate the tonka bean (or scrape out the vanilla seeds) into the mortar. Add the nutmeg, bay leaves and a pinch of salt to the mortar and crush to a fine texture. Alternatively, use a blender.
The resulting cocoa will be dry in texture (it needs to be softened to mould), so transfer it to a bowl and microwave (medium heat, not high) for 1-2 mins. It should become warm and pliable.

Sift a thick dusting of cocoa powder onto a chopping board or counter. Divide the cocoa into 4 equal portions. Put a dusting of cocoa powder in your hand, then take a portion of the mixture and begin to mould into a ball. Repeat with the remaining 3 portions.
Dust the balls with extra cocoa powder and leave in a cool place (or refrigerate) to harden completely.
To make three cups of tea, put 4 cups of water into a pot along with the lemongrass, bay leaves and remaining cinnamon stick. Bring to a roaring boil, then lower the heat to simmer.

Grate 1 of the cocoa balls into a separate bowl, then transfer it to the pot of boiling water. Be careful, as it can foam and spill over the rim. Stir and allow the cocoa to dissolve, this should take around 3 mins.
Make the cornstarch slurry by mixing the cornstarch with 2 tbsp of water.

Increase to a medium heat and pour in the whole milk and condensed milk (to taste – some like it sweeter than others). Remove from the heat. Slowly whisk the cornstarch slurry into the liquid, whisking continuously to prevent lumps.
Sieve the tea before serving and finish with a cinnamon stick in each mug.

name: Chocolate Tiffin Fridge Cake
description: Solid chocolatey fridge bites with sticky fruit and crumbled biscuits. One of the easiest and tastiest desserts you'll ever make. A certified crowd-pleaser.
instructions: Grease a brownie tin or small high sided roasting tray with a little butter and line the base with baking paper.

Melt the butter, caster sugar, golden syrup, cocoa powder in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Once melted, crush in the biscuits and add the fruit of your choice. Mix everything together then tip into the tin, pressing down with the back of your wooden spoon into an even layer.

Break the chocolate into a bowl. Melt in the microwave in 30 second bursts, or over a saucepan of simmering water (making sure the bottom of the bowl doesn’t touch the water). Pour the melted chocolate over the tiffin and spread into a thin layer. Put the tiffin into the fridge for at least 2 hours, until set then cut into squares.
Keep in an airtight container in the fridge. Best eaten cold with a cuppa.

name: Chocolate Traybake Cake with Peanut Butter Frosting
description: A really simple chocolate cake that you will make time and time again. Topped with ridiculously nice peanut butter icing and using minimal kit for ease.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/160°C Fan. Grease a 20cm brownie tin or small roasting tin with the butter foil then line the base with baking paper.
Measure 125g butter into a microwaveable bowl. Break in the chocolate then zap in the microwave in 30 second bursts, stirring in between each one, until melted and glossy. Set aside.
Boil the kettle.
In a large bowl, whisk the sugar, flour and bicarb together along with a big pinch of salt until well combined - you want to get rid of any sugar lumps.

Crack the eggs into the bowl and add the yogurt. Pour in the melted chocolate mixture and whisk everything together until you have a smooth batter then whisk in 50ml boiling water - our secret ingredient.

Pour the cake batter into your prepared tin. Bake in the centre of your oven for 25 minutes until a knife/skewer pricked in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Leave to cool completely in the tin.

Frosting time. Tip the remaining butter into a bowl (make sure the butter is super soft - If not microwave for 10 seconds), add the peanut butter, icing sugar and a big pinch of salt. Using some elbow grease; whisk to combine. Slather on top of the cooled cake and top with a handful of roughly chopped salted peanuts if you like.
Eat and enjoy. These cakes will keep in a container out of the fridge for 3-4 days.

name: Chocolate and Peanut Butter Tart
description: Smooth and silky spiced chocolate ganache with a peanut butter caramel. You will be fighting for the last piece of this, Mob!
keywords: Peanut butter and chocolate tart recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Blend the pretzels into a fine crumb and melt the butter, combine
this with the pretzels.

Push this into a 24cm tart tin, make sure to push it to the sides
and it’s all evenly distributed.

Pop this into the oven for 5 mins until lightly golden and set aside
to cool fully.

For the peanut butter filling, put 300ml double cream, light
brown sugar and peanut butter into a pan. Heat on a medium heat
for 10 mins, stirring to get a thick peanut butter filling. Add in a
big pinch of salt.

Pour the hot peanut butter filling into the pretzel base and then
pop it into the freezer to chill whilst you make the chocolate
topping.

For the spiced chocolate topping, break up the chocolate. Heat up
300ml double cream and add in the cinnamon stick, cloves,
vanilla extract and grate in 1⁄2 the nutmeg. Bring this to a simmer
and then turn off the heat. Allow to steep for 30 mins with the lid
on.

Reheat the double cream in the pan and strain this over broken
chocolate. Allow to sit for 1 minute and then mix together to form
a smooth ganache. Add in a big pinch of salt and mix.

Pour the chocolate mixture over the set peanut butter filling and
smooth the top. Pop this into the fridge for an hour or until you’re
ready to eat it.
To make the honeycomb, start by lining a loaf tin with baking paper.

Mix the caster sugar, peanuts and golden syrup in a pan with the
heat off. Turn the heat on to medium and allow it to melt without
mixing. Cook for 5 mins until the sugar turns a deep caramel,
swirl the pan a few times to make sure all the sugar is melted.

Add in the bicarbonate and mix, immediately put this into the
loaf tin and allow to set for 30 mins.

Once it's hard, cut it into small shards and top your tart. Enjoy
the tart best at room temperature, slice into pieces and enjoy.

name: Chopped Roast Chicken Salad
description: Turn your leftover Summer Roast Chicken Dinner batch into a delicious salad. Crunchy potato croutons, finely chopped batch chicken and crisp iceberg, all tossed in a sharp, mustardy dressing. Lunch sorted.
instructions: Cut the batch Jersey Royals into crouton-sized chunks and crisp up in the air fryer or oven at 200°C for 8-10 mins, until golden. Finely chop the batch chicken and shred the lettuce.

Make the dressing: mix together the mayo, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce and the juice of the lemon. Finely grate in the Parmesan and season with black pepper. Toss in the chicken and shredded lettuce until well coated. Scatter the potato croutons over the top to serve.

name: Chopped Smoked Aubergine With Smoky Tomatoes & Grilled Flatbreads
description: Cooking your aubergines until they're blackened and on the verge of collapsing is a great way to bring the best out of them.
keywords: Chopped Smoked Aubergine With Smoky Tomatoes & Grilled Flatbreads
instructions: Preheat your BBQ to super hot. Pierce the aubergines all over and get them straight onto the grill to char and burn. Cook them for 13-15 mins, turning now and then, until completely burnt and collapsing.

Remove the burnt skins from the aubergines and start chopping the flesh on your board. Pour over the tahini and season with salt, keep chopping and chopping until you have a really smooth, spreadable consistency. Mix in a little olive oil with your knife and season with salt and lots of black pepper. Transfer to a plate.

Grab a metal sieve and tip in the tomatoes. Drizzle in a tiny bit of olive oil and season with salt. Stick the sieve over the coals of your BBQ and grill the tomatoes until super charred and gnarly. They’ll pop and burst as they cook, just keep shaking the sieve and keep things moving. Once cooked, tip them into a bowl with finely chopped parsley, chopped mint, molasses and a finely diced red onion. Add lemon juice, salt and pepper and set aside.

Mix the yoghurt and flour with a big pinch of salt in a bowl. Work into a shaggy dough, then tip out onto a work surface and knead until smooth. Turn the bowl over and cover the dough for 10 mins. Split the flatbread dough into 4 and roll each ball out into a rough circle.

Your BBQ should be hitting a medium heat now. Brush each flatbread with a little olive oil. Carefully lay the first flatbread onto the grill and cook for 1-2 mins each side. The flatbread should be nicely golden, a tiny bit charred and puff a little. Add more oil if you want a more golden, crispy bread. Keep the cooked flatbread in a clean kitchen towel while you grill the others.
Serve the chopped aubergine dip, topped with the smoky tomatoes with warm flatbreads.

name: Choripapa Tacos with Kimchi Salsa
description: Hearty chorizo and potato stuffed into a tortilla and garnished with zingy yoghurt and kimchi salsa.
keywords: Choripapa Tacos with Kimchi Salsa recipe
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut into 1cm cubes. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the greens from the whites. Dice the chorizo.
Into a frying pan, add the chorizo and place onto medium heat. Cook until the oils start seeping out, 2-3 mins. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the chorizo onto a plate.

Add a drizzle of olive oil into the frying pan, then drop the potatoes, spring onion whites and half the spring onion greens in. Strip the thyme leaves from the stalks straight into the pan. Cook, stirring, until the potatoes are cooked through and golden, 10-15 mins.

Meanwhile, finely chop the kimchi and add to a bowl with the remaining spring onion greens, a drizzle of olive oil and the juice of ½ the limes. Into another bowl, add the yoghurt and finely grate over the zest of ½ a lime.
Reheat the tortillas, then top with the choripapa mixture. Drizzle over the yoghurt, top with kimchi salsa and serve with lime wedges.

name: Chorizo & Aioli Potatoes
description: A patatas bravas-inspired potato salad that’s perfect for the summer. It’s got a nice tickle of a spice and it’s destined to be a hit at your next big dinner party.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Remove and discard the fronds (the bits at the very end) from 4 spring onions. Transfer to a baking tray, drizzle with oil and a good pinch of salt, then roast for 15-20 mins.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Halve the potatoes lengthways, then get them into the pan and cook for 12-15 mins until tender. Drain in a colander and leave them to steam dry.

For the aioli, add the egg yolks to a blender, then grate in the garlic. Whizz until it turns into a paste. With the blender still on, very gradually pour in the vegetable oil. When very thick, loosen it with a little lemon juice. Once all of the vegetable oil is used up, move on to pouring in the olive oil. Add the mustard and white white vinegar, then season with salt and the remaining lemon juice.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Remove the skin from the chorizo and crumble it straight into the pan. Cook for about 5 mins until crispy and the fat has rendered out. Set aside.
Cut the cooked spring onions into 3cm pieces. Finely slice the remaining raw spring onions on a diagonal.
Add the potatoes to a large bowl along with the aioli and raw spring onions. Divide between plates, then top with the roasted spring onions and crispy chorizo in its fat.

name: Chorizo & Chickpea Stew
description: Inspired by gumbo this hearty stew of full of spicy chorizo and soft chickpeas. Perfect with seasonal cavolo nero.
instructions: Prep your veg. Dice the onions, carrot, celery, jalapeño and green pepper. Slice the chorizo.
Pour your vegetable oil into a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add your flour, then whisk constantly for 5 mins until the colour darkens to a biscuity brown. This is your roux.
Once the roux is darkened, add in the vegetables and the smoked paprika. Cook for 4 mins. Add in the chorizo and cook for another 5 mins until the oil is stained red.
Slowly pour in the chicken stock and beer and then bring to a boil.
Add in the chickpeas, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 40-45 mins.
Roughly chop the cavolo nero and finely slice the spring onions.
Add in the cavolo nero and give it a mix. Cook for 2 mins until it has wilted down.
Season generously with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with spring onions and serve with rice.

name: Chorizo & Refried Bean Tostadas
description: Your new go-to brunch. Hot sauce for splashing over is absolutely non-negotiable.
instructions: Halve, peel and finely chop the onion. Scrape ½ into a small bowl and set the other ½ aside. Cut the cherry tomatoes into quarters and scrape into the small bowl with the ½ onion. Season with salt and cracked black pepper and squeeze in the juice of ½ the limes.
Peel and thinly slice the garlic cloves, then run a knife along the skin of the chorizo and peel the skin away. Cut into 1cm pieces.

Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a small frying pan set over a medium-high heat and add the chorizo. Fry for 3-4 minutes until the oil has turned a vibrant red and the chorizo is crisp. Use a slotted spoon to scoop it out onto a small plate.
Add one of the corn tortillas to the pan, tossing to coat in the oil, and fry for 2 minutes until crisp. Move onto a serving plate, then repeat with the other tortillas.

Add ½ the finely chopped onion, the garlic and cumin seeds to the same pan with a pinch of salt and fry for 3 minutes until smelling amazing. Carefully pour in the refried beans, along with the water. Season with salt and squeeze in the juice of the remaining lime.

Spoon the beans onto the crispy tortilla and top with the crispy chorizo pieces and the cherry tomato salsa. Finish each one with a spoon of soured cream,plenty of coriander leaves and hot sauce for splashing over.

name: Chorizo & Tomato Fish Stew
description: A rich, smoky low-cal, high-protein stew of crispy chorizo, juicy prawns and tender fish... ready in 20 and perfect for dunking crusty bread.
instructions: Chuck the diced chorizo into a medium deep frying pan over a medium heat and cook for about 3 mins, stirring often, until it releases its oil and starts to crisp. Add the prawns and cook for 2 mins on each side until golden. Remove the chorizo and prawns from the pan, setting aside for later.
Peel and finely slice the garlic and stir it into the pan. Cook for 1 min until softened, then pour in the tomatoes and the cannellini beans — liquid and all. Bring to the boil.

Cut the fish into bite-sized chunks. Add the prawns and chorizo back to the pan and stir it all together. Taste and check for seasoning. Pop the fish in, then scatter the spinach over the top. Cover with a lid and simmer gently for 3–4 mins, or until the fish is opaque and cooked through.
Pick the parsley leaves. Dish up the stew and top with parsley. Serve with crusty bread, if you fancy.

name: Chorizo Assassin's Spaghetti
description: If you like chilli and chorizo then you'll be in for a treat with this one. Enjoy.
instructions: Score the chorizo lengthways with a sharp knife, then peel away the papery skin. Cut the chorizo into 1cm cubes. Peel and thinly slice the garlic. Boil the kettle.

Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan (large enough to fit the spaghetti without breaking it) over a medium heat, add the chorizo and fry for 2 mins until starting to crisp and the oil has turned a deep red colour. Add the garlic, chilli flakes and spaghetti and fry for 2 mins, stirring to get the spaghetti well coated in the oil.
Pour the passata into a jug, add 300ml just-boiled water and mix well. Season well with salt and pepper and whisk to combine.

Pour 100ml of the tomato liquid into the chorizo pan and cook until the water has evaporated and the spaghetti is caramelising and sticking to the bottom of the pan a little, then flip the spaghetti and pour in another 100ml liquid. Keep repeating this process until the pasta has softened and caramelised (this should take 25-30 mins). If you run out of tomato liquid, just use water. The sauce will have reduced and will cling to the slightly crisp pasta. If not, add a splash of water. Season to taste.
Divide the spaghetti between two plates, tear over some flat-leaf parsley and drizzle with a little more olive oil.

name: Chorizo Baked Eggs
description: Want a breakfast that'll fuel you for the day? These chorizo baked eggs are spicy, warming, and the perfect weekend breakfast.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180ºC/356ºF.
Finely chop the chilli, the onion and the garlic cloves. Cut the peppers into strips, and break the chorizo into little nuggets.

Add the chorizo to a big pan. Fry until crisp. Then add the vegetables. Fry for 6 minutes, until slightly softened, and then add your tinned tomatoes. Fill up both tins with water, and pour that in too. Give it a stir and let it bubble away. You want the sauce to be a thick consistency, so allow it to reduce by around a half.
Take the sauce off the heat and smooth out the surface. Then make little holes in the sauce and gently drop in the eggs, so the yolks stay intact.
Place the whole pan into the oven for 12 minutes.
Remove the pan, and add crumbled feta and parsley. Enjoy

name: Chorizo Brussels Sprouts
description: We have perfected brussels sprouts. The key? Sherry vinegar & chorizo. We promise these will hit differently & upgrade your Christmas dinner forever.
instructions: Wash and trim the ends off the brussels sprouts. Peel off any loose leaves and cut all the brussels sprouts in half.
Crumble the chorizo into a large pan on a medium-high heat. Fry until crispy and fragrant, stirring often.
Add the brussels sprouts to the pan and mix to combine with the chorizo. Cook for 15 minutes on a high heat, stirring often, until the brussels sprouts are slightly charred and cooked through.
Roughly chop the almonds and add them to the pan. Stir through the sherry vinegar.

Finely chop your parsley, saving a quarter for garnish, and scatter over the chorizo sprouts. Season with a grind of pepper and stir. Serve and sprinkle the remaining parsley over the top. Dig in! Enjoy!

name: Chorizo Carbonara
description: This dish just makes sense – chorizo is an epic alternative to Guanciale (which is cured pork cheek – a traditional ingredient in Carbonara). Lemon juice provides a pleasant lift at the end.
instructions: Peel skin off chorizo, crumble into a frying pan and fry until crisp. Add your crushed garlic and a handful of rosemary leaves to the pan.
In a bowl, add your egg yolks and grated parmesan, with a generous amount of black pepper. Mix with a fork and set aside.
Get your pasta on and salt the water. Reserve a mug of pasta water.
Add a splash of pasta water at a time to the chorizo pan, bubble it down.
Once pasta is al dente add it to your chorizo. Take the pan off the heat. Fold the chorizo through the pasta.

Add the egg mixture and a little more of the pasta water. Keep folding it together and adding more until it becomes thick and creamy. Add a big squeeze of lemon juice. This lifts the dish perfectly. Serve with lots of cracked black pepper on top! Enjoy.

name: Chorizo Cauliflower Fried Rice
description: Sometimes we want a healthier version of our favourites. Cauliflower ‘rice’ works here because it soaks up the flavour from the chorizo, ginger, garlic and soy.
instructions:
Peel the chorizo and cut it into long diagonal slices. Get a large
frying pan over a medium heat and drizzle in a little oil. Add the
chorizo, then finely grate the garlic and ginger straight into the
pan. Chuck in the baby corn and mangetout. Leave to fry for
about 5 mins, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the cauliflower. Pulse the cauliflower to
the texture of ‘rice’ in a mini food processor, working in batches
if you need to – it will only take 30 seconds at a time. Tip the
cauliflower rice straight into the frying pan.
Turn up the heat. Add the edamame beans and give everything
a good mix. Push the contents of the pan to one side and then
crack the eggs into the free space. Use the wooden spoon to
scramble the eggs together, then stir them into the cauliflower
rice. Fry for a further 2 mins more.
Pour in the soy sauce and give everything a final mix. Tear over
the coriander and drizzle with chilli sauce. Serve at the table
straight from the pan for people to help themselves.

name: Chorizo Cheese Toastie
description: Chorizo is an absolute flavour bomb, but often recipes only use a small amount, so you have leftovers. There is a perfect way to use them up - this toastie.
instructions: Dice the chorizo and add to a frying pan over a medium low heat with a splash of olive oil.
Dice the onion and mince the rosemary and add to the chorizo. Cook for about 5 mins until soft and fragrant. Empty the contents of the pan into a bowl and set aside.

Spread one side of all of the slices of bread with half a tbsp of mayonnaise. Place 4 of the slices mayo side down into the pan. Grate over the cheese and then spread the chorizo mix evenly between all four slices.
Top with the remaining slices of bread (mayonnaise side facing up). Cook for about 3 to 4 mins and then flip and repeat on the other side. You want the bread to be golden brown and the cheese melted.
Remove from the pan, drizzle over the honey and plate up.

name: Chorizo Chilli Stew With Guacamole
description: The ultimate cheat’s chilli lacking none of the flavour and served with zingy guac and Cheddar cheese. Serve with some tortilla chips for scooping.
instructions:
Peel the chorizo and slice into rounds, roughly half a centimetre
thick. Get a large saucepan over a high heat. Drizzle in some olive
oil, then scrape in the chorizo. Leave to fry.
Meanwhile, remove the peppers from the jar with a fork, roughly
slice and add them to the pan along with the unpeeled garlic,
crushing the cloves into the pan. Add the Cajun seasoning and
stir, cooking for a further minute.
Open the tins of beans, drain the liquid in a sieve and then add to
the pan. Pour in the passata. Season with salt and black pepper
and give everything a good mix. Bring the chilli to the boil and let
it bubble away while you make the guac.
For the guacamole. Cut one lime in half and the other into four
wedges. Halve and pit the avocados and scoop out the flesh into
a small bowl. Squeeze over the juice from the lime halves, season
with salt and black pepper and then smash up with a fork.
Guac – done.
Tear the coriander over the chilli and serve at the table with the
bowl of guac, some Cheddar cheese for topping and the lime
wedges for squeezing over.

name: Chorizo Chilli con Carne
description: This chilli ticks all the boxes. Rich, smoky, and blessed with a gentle heat thanks to Bull’s-Eye Carolina Reaper Hot Sauce, it’s perfect for feeding a crowd.
instructions: Dice the onion, pepper and chorizo before adding them to a large pan over a medium-low heat along with a good drizzle of olive oil.
Sweat down for 5 mins until soft then add the minced garlic, tomato purée, Bull’s-Eye Carolina Reaper Hot Sauce and spices. Stir and cook for another 3 mins.
Empty the contents of the pan into a small bowl and set aside. Return the pan to a very high heat.
Add the beef mince to the pan along with a good pinch of salt. Cook for a few mins until the beef is browned all over.
Add the onion and pepper mix back to the pan along with the tinned tomatoes and half a can of water. Stir well, scraping the bottom of the pan.
Add the kidney beans, bring to a gentle simmer and leave to cook for at least an hour, stirring occasionally.
Once it’s all thickened up and rich, take off the heat and add a big squeeze of lime juice. Stir well and taste for seasoning.
Serve over rice with a sprinkle of chopped coriander and an (optional) spoon of sour cream.

name: Chorizo Mac & Cheese
description: We've made a lot of Mac and Cheeses, but this one is really special. The spicy smokiness of the chorizo is beautiful.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Add your peppers to a roasting tray and cook for 45 mins, until charred and soft.
Remove peppers from oven. Allow to cool. Peel off skins and remove seeds.
Add ⅔ of the peppers to a blender with the milk and a good grinding of pepper. Blitz until smooth.
Crumble your chorizo into a pan with a splash of olive oil. Cook until crispy, adding a small handful of rosemary after 5 mins. Once crispy, remove rosemary and chorizo from the pan and set aside.
Get your macaroni on (cook for 10 mins in salted boiling water).
Add the plain flour to the chorizo fat and whisk it in to make a paste. Start slowly adding the blended pepper mix, whisking as you go. You should end up with a nice thick red sauce.
Add grated cheddar and grated manchego. Mix it in until smooth.
Once the cheese is melted, add your macaroni and stir to combine. Add the crispy chorizo. Slice up your remaining roasted pepper and add that too.

Stir everything together, and then top it with any leftover cheddar and manchego. Whack the mac and cheese under the grill for 10 mins until golden and bubbling. Remove from the oven, spoon into bowls and enjoy!

name: Chorizo Pesto Pasta Bake
description: Ramping up a classic pasta bake with a fresh, homemade pesto sauce, stringy mozzarella cheese and a spicy chorizo kick. A Max Fosh masterpiece.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Chop your garlic and add it to a blender with the red peppers, sun-dried tomatoes, pine nuts, 2 tbsp of olive oil and most of the parmesan, leaving a handful to scatter over the pasta before baking. Give it a big old blend to get that delicious pesto consistency.
Bring a saucepan of water to a boil, add 1 tbsp of salt and cook the penne (see pack instructions).
Chop your chorizo and add it to a frying pan on a medium heat. Fry until crispy, then add the pasta to the chorizo. Pour in your pesto and fold everything together so it’s coated in the pesto.
Transfer the pesto pasta into a large baking dish. Slice up the mozzarella and sprinkle it onto the pasta with the rest of the parmesan.
Whack the dish in the oven for 15 minutes or until the cheese is completely melted and crispy.
Serve the pasta with a crack of black pepper and a pinch of chilli flakes. Chop up your basil for garnish and dig in!

name: Chorizo Romesco Risotto
description: We use smoky romesco sauce as the stock for our creamy risotto. It pairs beautifully with the crisp chorizo and untraditional but very wonderful red wine base.
instructions: Roughly chop your almonds. Finely dice your onion and grate your garlic. Dice your chorizo.
Toast your almonds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for a few minutes until they are golden.

Tip all but 20g of your almonds into your blender. Add with your peppers, tomato puree, paprika, chicken stock cube, vinegar and olive oil to the blender then whizz until smooth. Add 800ml water and whizz again. Warm on the hob in a saucepan.

Heat a little glug of oil in a large pan and add your chorizo. Cook over a medium-high heat for a few minutes until it is crisp and has released its fat into the pan. Remove the chorizo with a slotted spoon.

Add your onion to the chorizo fat and turn down the heat a little. Fry for 10 minutes until soft, then add your garlic. Cook out for 1 minute. Add your risotto rice to the pan and give it a good toast for a minute or so, making sure it gets fully coated in the onion mixture and starts to turn translucent.

Pour your red wine in the pan and stir until it has been absorbed. Ladle in your romesco stock bit by bit, stirring and allowing your rice to absorb it before adding more. By the time you’ve added all of your stock, your rice should be tender.
Grate your pecorino into the pan and add in most of your chorizo. Season your risotto to taste with salt and pepper, then give it all a good mix.
Serve up in bowls topped with your remaining almonds and chorizo, a sprinkle of chopped parsley, another grating of pecorino and a drizzle of good quality olive oil.

name: Chorizo Scones
description: Chorizo and Cheddar scones with a thyme and hot honey glaze. You won't want to stop eating these. Make extra, to be safe.
instructions: Line two baking trays with baking paper. Ensure your butter is very cold. Dice the chorizo.
Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the diced chorizo and fry for 2-3 mins or until crispy then transfer to a plate and set aside to cool.
Cut the butter into small cubes. Grate the Cheddar cheese.

Get the paprika, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, black pepper and diced butter into a mixing bowl. Use your fingers and thumbs to mix everything together until it resembles breadcrumbs.

In a bowl or jug, whisk together the egg and soured cream. Tip it into the flour mixture and stir with a spoon or spatula until roughly combined. Add the cooled chorizo, ¾ thyme leaves and ¾ of the grated Cheddar. Mix until just incorporated – there should still be dry bits at the bottom of the bowl.

Transfer the dough onto a clean work surface and use a rolling pin to roll it out into a 2cm rectangle. Sprinkle the dough with ¼ of the remaining Cheddar, then fold each short end of the dough into the centre, and fold the dough in half again. Turn the dough 90° and roll the dough out once again into a 4 ½ cm thick rectangle. Cut the dough into 6cm logs, then, each into triangles. Sprinkle the remaining Cheddar over the top.
Transfer the scones to your prepared baking trays and pop in the freezer for 30-45 mins until cold.
Heat the oven to fan 150°C. Bake the scones from cold for 25-30 mins until golden.
Once baked, remove from the oven, brush the tops with the hot honey and finish with a sprinkle of the remaining thyme. Leave to cool then enjoy!

name: Chorizo Tortilla & Zingy Aioli
description: The secret ingredient in this tortilla recipe? Ready salted crisps. Don't knock it 'till you've tried it.
instructions: Dice the chorizo. Place a medium pan over a medium heat and cook the chorizo until crispy and it has released its fat, 3-4 mins.

Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice the onion and three-quarters of garlic. Add the mayo into a small bowl, grate the remaining garlic into it and zest in the lemon. Season with salt and lemon juice, set aside.
Scoop the chorizo out, leaving the fat in the pan. Add a splash of olive oil, stir through the onion and garlic, cook until softened, 4-6 min. Tip into a large bowl and let cool down slightly

Crack the eggs into the onions and whisk thoroughly until foamy, 3-4 mins. Stir the chorizo and crisps through and season with some salt and plenty of black pepper. Let sit for 2-4 mins so the crisps soften slightly.

Place the empty pan back on medium heat with another splash of oil. Once hot, pour the egg mixture into the pan, stir rapidly, shaking the pan until the mixture thickens, 2-3 mins. Then, leave to set the sides and bottom, 2-3 mins. The mixture should still be wet in the middle.

Place a plate on top of the pan and invert the tortilla onto it. Add a splash of oil into the pan and slide the tortilla back, wet side down into the frying pan, tucking the sides in. Cook for 1-2 mins, until just set.
Slide or invert the tortilla onto a clean plate, serve wedges of it with a dollop of aioli.

name: Chorizo and Charred Spring Onion Rigatoni
description: Charring spring onions and almonds in smokey chorizo fat is only ever going to lead to big things. This is a very special pasta dish.
instructions: Peel the skin off the chorizo and roughly break it apart into small chunks. Then chop the spring onions in half.
Add the chorizo into a non-stick frying pan on medium heat without any oil and let the juices render out. Slice the red peppers.
Once the chorizo is beginning to crisp, add the almonds into the pan along with the spring onions and roasted peppers. Fry on a high heat for a couple of minutes until charred.
Pour in the red wine vinegar and mix together.
Add in the tomato purée and stir so that everything is coated.
Whack in the crème fraîche and stir together making it nice and creamy. Once all mixed together, season with salt and pepper and turn it down to a low heat.
Get your pasta on and salt the water. After about 5 minutes of boiling, take 1/2 a cup of pasta water and add it into the sauce. Mix together to loosen it up then continue to simmer.
Once your pasta is ready, drain and toss it through the sauce.
Finely chop your parsley and whack a handful into the pasta (saving some for garnish). Mix together and you're good to go. Serve it up in to bowls and scatter over the leftover parsley. Enjoy!

name: Chorizo and Halloumi Jambalaya
description: All the deep south flavours are packed into this one-pot beauty. We’ve put our spin on it by adding halloumi, and it's glorious. Perfect with fluffy Tilda rice.
instructions: Dice your halloumi into 3cm chunks. Slice your chorizo into lengths, then cut in half and slice into half moons.
Slice your onion, red pepper and green pepper into thin strips. Grate your garlic cloves.

Heat a large pan with a lid over a medium-high heat with a little olive oil. Tip in your cubes of halloumi and fry for a few minutes until the cubes are golden on all sides. Remove all the halloumi from the pan and set aside until later.
Add your chopped chorizo to the same pan. Fry for a few mins until crispy. Remove a third of the chorizo from the pan and set aside until later.
Tip your onions into the pan and cook over a medium heat for 10 mins, or until your onions are nice and soft. Add your sliced red and green peppers and cook for 5 mins more.
Add your garlic, hot smoked paprika, cayenne pepper and dried oregano. Cook for 2 mins until lovely and fragrant.

Add your chopped tomatoes, Tilda Easy Cook Long Grain Rice and chicken stock to the pan. Give it a stir then bring the mixture to a boil. Turn the heat down to a gentle simmer, then pop on a lid and cook for 12 mins. Remove from the heat and leave to sit with the lid still on for 10 mins more.
Meanwhile, thinly slice your spring onions.
Fluff your rice up with a fork, then sprinkle the dish with your spare chorizo and halloumi. Sprinkle with your sliced spring onions. Serve and enjoy!

name: Chorizo, Spinach & Gnocchi Bake
description: Chorizo and melted mozzarella over pillowy gnocchi in a rich tomato sauce. Proper weeknight no-brainer, and everyone's going to go mad for it.
instructions: Finely chop the garlic and slice the chorizo into rounds.
Set a large frying pan over a medium heat and add in the chorizo. Fry for 5-7 mins stirring occasionally, until the fat has nicely rendered and the chorizo is crispy.

Add the chopped garlic and chilli flakes to the pan. Cook for 30 seconds, and then add in your spinach. Once the spinach has wilted pour in your chopped tomatoes and season with salt and pepper. Fill the tins halfway with water, and pour that in. Turn down to a low-medium heat and allow to reduce and thicken.
While the sauce is reducing, cook the gnocchi according to packet instructions.

Preheat the grill. Add the cooked gnocchi into a large oven-proof dish and pour over the tomato sauce, mixing everything together. Gently shake the dish so the gnocchi is level, then over tear the basil and the mozzarella over the top. Finish with a generous crack of black pepper on top and grate over the Parmesan, and then place under the grill for 7-10 mins, until the cheese is golden and bubbling.
To serve, divide the gnocchi between bowls and dig in. Any leftovers will be great for lunches the next day.

name: Chorizo, Squash & Chickpea Soup
description: Smoky chorizo, sweet butternut and fennel seeds simmered into a rich, comforting soup. Deeply savoury, warming and made for rainy days.
instructions: Peel the butternut squash, deseed and cut it into roughly 1cm chunks. Trim the leeks, slice them into half-moons, then peel and finely slice the onion. Carefully peel the papery skin off the chorizo and chop or break it into small pieces. Finely slice the garlic.

Chuck the chorizo into a large heavy-bottomed saucepan over a medium-low heat. Once the fat starts to render and the chorizo is starting to crisp up, add the leeks and the onion. Fry for 10 mins, stirring occasionally until soft and just starting to get a little colour.
Add the fennel seeds and garlic stirring for another minute, then add the tomato paste and cook out for another couple of minutes.

Add the butternut squash, stirring to coat in the tomato paste. Drop in the parmesan rind, pour in the chicken stock and chickpeas (water and all). Bring to a simmer, and leave to cook away for 20 to 25 mins partially covered until the butternut squash is tender.
Once the soup is ready, season to taste and scatter over dill. Divide between bowls and dig in.

name: Christmas Dinner Gravy
description: A vegetarian xmas dinner gravy that will work for meat eaters, vegetarians and vegans. Made with caramelised vegetables, dried mushrooms and miso. Save the drained roasted veggies and use them to make my vegetarian stuffing, which really packs a punch.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan.

Roughly chop the onion, carrot, celery and garlic. Put them in a roasting dish along with the sage leaves and bay leaves and drizzle with olive oil. Slide into the preheated oven to roast for 15 mins until soft.
Meanwhile, add the miso and mushrooms to a small bowl. Pour over the boiling water and set aside for 10 mins to infuse.

Remove the vegetable tray from the oven and set it over a medium-high heat on the hob. Stir the veggies until they get a bit more colour, then mix in the flour and mustard and cook for one minute until sticky and bubbling. Add a splash of the infused miso and mushroom water and scrape the pan to deglaze any sticky bits, then transfer the mixture to a large saucepan.

Gradually whisk in the remaining infused boiling water, along with the soaked mushrooms, continually stirring to avoid lumps. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for around 5–7 mins until you have a thickened gravy.

Remove from the heat, strain through a sieve to get rid of any lumps and season with salt and pepper to taste. Discard the herbs. Set aside the mushrooms and roasted vegetables and use them to make my stuffing.
Store the gravy in a container until ready for use. Before serving, gently heat in a saucepan set over a moderate heat until hot.

name: Christmas Garlic Bread
description: The cheesiest and most outrageously garlicky garlic bread to ever land on your Christmas table.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Cut the bread in a criss cross pattern like a hedgehog.
Finely chop the rosemary.
Grate the garlic into a bowl, add in rosemary, 50ml of olive oil and a big pinch of salt.
Cut the cheese into small thin slices.
Brush the bread with the garlic oil making sure to get inside all of the crevices and cuts.
Spread the cranberry sauce into the cuts over the garlic oil and then stuff each slit with the cheese. Brush over with any remaining garlic oil and wrap the whole thing in foil.
Pop this in the oven for 20 mins or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Pull apart the cheese and enjoy.

name: Christmas Hasselback Potatoes
description: It doesn’t get much more Christmassy than this. A herby sage drizzle, gooey taleggio and tangy cranberry sauce. Delicious.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Place two wooden spoons on your chopping board and then place a potato in between the handles. Cut thin slices vertically in the potatoes, using the wooden spoons to stop you cutting all the way through. Continue with all the potatoes and gently pull the layers apart without breaking up the potato.
Place onto a baking tray, cover with olive oil and salt and bake for 1 hour or until very crispy and cooked all the way through.

Meanwhile, make the sage salsa. Finely chop the chives, sage and capers. Add this all to a bowl, grate in the garlic and the zest of a lemon. Add in the juice of half a lemon, mustard and drizzle in extra virgin olive oil. Mix well and season with salt and pepper.
Thinly slice the taleggio, and cut them into squares roughly the size of the potatoes.
Once the potatoes are cooked, push a thin slice of taleggio in each of the cuts. Pop it back into the oven and cook for another 5 mins until the cheese has melted.
Drizzle with the sage salsa and some cranberry sauce. Place onto your serving platter and enjoy hot.

name: Christmas Leftovers Curry
description:
In partnership with Patak's #ad
This easy leftover curry base is rich, warming and perfect any festive leftovers: turkey, veg or whatever you've got kicking about.
instructions: Finely chop the onions. Heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Add the onions with a big pinch of salt and cook for 10 mins, stirring every so often, until softened and starting to caramelise.
Meanwhile, peel the ginger and garlic, then grate them using a fine grater.
Once the onions are caramelised, scrape in the grated garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 min until fragrant, then stir in the spice paste and cook for another minute.

Pour in the chopped tomatoes, coconut milk and water. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down and let it simmer gently for 15 to 20 mins, stirring occasionally, until thick and luscious. Season with salt and black pepper. If you prefer a smoother sauce, blitz it with a stick blender at this stage.
Meanwhile, cut or tear your leftover protein or veg into bite-sized pieces.
Add the leftovers to the sauce and simmer for 5 mins until heated through. If it’s looking too thick, loosen it with a splash of water.
Squeeze over a little lemon juice, if using, then scatter with some chopped coriander, if using. Serve with warm basmati rice and naan.

name: Christmas Leftovers Platter With Cranberry Mustard Sauce
description: Want to know what to do with all your leftover Christmas vegetables? We've got just the recipe for you.
keywords: Christmas Leftovers Platter With Cranberry Mustard Sauce
Christmas Leftovers Platter With Cranberry Mustard Sauce recipe
what to do with Christmas leftovers
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Quarter the pickled onions.
Place the leftover veggies onto a tray with a drizzle of oil. Toss together, season with salt and pepper. Reheat in the oven, 10-15 mins until hot.
Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves and discard the stalks. Season the crème fraîche generously with freshly cracked black pepper.
In a bowl, add the cranberry sauce, whole grain mustard, pickled onion brine and olive oil. Stir together, taste and season with salt, if needed.
Add the roasted veg into a bowl with the pickled onions and parsley leaves, toss together.
Spread the crème fraîche onto a platter or plate, top with the roasted veg, and drizzle over the cranberry mustard sauce.

name: Christmas Roast Chicken
description: A gorgeous Christmas roast chicken recipe that'll put any roast turkey recipe to shame.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Tip the butter into a bowl and whisk a little, then add the spices along with a big pinch of salt and pepper. Finely chop the sage leaves and add to the butter, mix well.

Use your hands to slide under the chicken skin, releasing it from the breast meat (be careful not to break the skin!) Take 2 Tbsp of the butter and slide it under the skin, squishing it so it coats the breast meat. Use the rest of the butter to rub all over the outside of the chicken. Cut the lemon in half and push half of the lemon into the cavity of the chicken.

Slide the chicken into the oven for 90 mins, then slide a knife between the thigh and the crown – if the juices that run out are clear, set the chicken aside to rest for 15-20 mins. If the juices still run a little pink, slide the chicken back into the oven for another 10 mins before resting.

Put some sage and rosemary on a large platter, then carve the chicken and add to the platter. Spoon over any of the butter from the base of the chicken roasting tin. Serve with the remaining lemon half, sliced into wedges.

Place your turkey into a large baking tray and cover with the Christmas butter, making sure that you cover the entirety of the bird. At this point, cover the entire tray with tin foil and make a kind of tin foil tent. Now place the turkey in the oven.
Turn the oven to 180°C and cook for 2 ½ hours. The most important part of cooking the turkey is basting. Make sure you set yourself a timer every 30 mins so you don't forget!

name: Christmas Stuffing Sausage Rolls
description: Flaky pastry and tender sausage stuffing. These Christmas stuffing sausage rolls are unbelievable. Delicious.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Finely chop the sage leaves and onions. Heat a splash of olive oil in a non-stick frying pan set over a medium-high heat, then add the chopped sage and fry until it starts to crisp. Add the chopped onions and cook until soft, around 10 mins, then remove from the heat and tip into a bowl.

Squeeze the meat out of the sausages and add to the same bowl. Grate the apple, then squeeze the gratings to remove excess moisture and add to the bowl. Add the cheddar and breadcrumbs, then season generously with salt and pepper. Mix everything together and set aside.

Warm the cranberry sauce in a pan with a splash of water. This will loosen it so it spreads more easily. Meanwhile, unravel the sheet of puff pastry. Cut it in half lengthways and spread cranberry sauce over both rectangles, leaving a 1 ½ cm border.

Divide the stuffing mixture into two parts. Spread one half of the mixture along the length of one of the pastry rectangles. You want this to be in a cylindrical shape and slightly closer to one edge. Repeat for the other pastry rectangle.

Brush the top of the stuffing mixture and borders with beaten egg. Tightly roll the larger side of the pastry over the stuffing mixture to encase it. Use a fork to press down where the pastry meets. Cut into 12 sausage rolls, place on a tray lined with baking paper and chill in the fridge for 15 mins.

Brush the remaining egg over the sausage rolls and sprinkle over the sesame seeds and some sea salt. Bake for 30 mins until cooked through and deep golden-brown. Remove from the oven, stack them up and enjoy!

name: Chunky Herb Salad With Whipped Feta Dressing
description: Keeping your herbs whole doesn't just save you time but adds a nice textural element to this salad. The whipped feta is a ripper.
keywords: Chunky Herb Salad With Whipped Feta Dressing
instructions:
Add half the feta to a food processor with the yoghurt, mustard, finely grated
garlic clove and the zest and juice of the lemon. Whizz until smooth and scoop
out into the bottom of a big salad bowl.

Roughly tear the herbs straight into the bowl, cut up the celery into chunky
slices (on the angle is nice!) and get them in there too.

Scatter in the lettuce leaves and 2 tbsp of the seeds. Toss to combine, season to
taste and get onto a big platter. Finish with the remaining seeds, feta cheese and
a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Chunky Veg Vegan Frittata
description: This chickpea flour, frittata inspired tart is great for breakfast or packed lunch as it keeps well for up to 4 days and is a great way to up old herbs and veg.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Peel and chop the sweet potatoes and courgettes into 2cm cubes. Finely chop the herbs.

Prepare a medium-sized baking tray or a 30cm ovensafe skillet. Scrunch up some parchment paper to help it lay flat on in the pan and push it into the sides of the pan. Add in the sweet potato, drizzle with a third of the olive oil and season with salt and pepper and bake in the tray or skillet for 10 mins.

While the potatoes are in the oven, make the batter. Weigh out the chickpea flour and then sieve it over another large bowl through a fine mesh sieve. This is an important step to make sure you don’t end up with a lumpy mix. Mix the chickpea flour, milk, mustard, ½ tbsp salt, and remaining olive oil, water and plenty of pepper. Whisk well and set aside for the flour to absorb the liquids.

After the sweet potatoes have been in the oven for 10 mins, take them out and pop the courgette cubes into the same pan as the sweet potatoes over the top of them with a little drizzle of olive oil. Season and cook for a further 10-15 mins until the vegetables have softened.

Add the herbs to the chickpea batter and mix through. When the vegetables have come out of the oven, sprinkle some vegan feta over it all (if using), give them a toss to mix it through and help create a bit of space between them. Pour over the batter and scatter some more vegan feta over the top, if using.
Bake for 25-30 mins until set. Stick a toothpick through the middle, it should come out dry. Let it cool for at least 10-15 mins and enjoy hot or cold.

name: Chunky Vegetable Soup With Squash, Kale & Parmesan Croutons
description: Packed with vegetables and all sorts of goodness, this vegetable soup recipe will cure just any cold. Maybe. Don't use this as a substitute for actual medicine. Do eat it for dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel the squash then slice in half vertically and use a spoon to scoop out the seeds. Slice into 2-3cm chunks and tip into a tray. Tip the tomatoes into the tray, then finely chop the rosemary leaves and add to the tray too. Drizzle everything with olive oil and season well. Wrap the garlic in foil and add to the tray. Slide into the oven and bake for 20 mins.
Place the slices of bread on a baking sheet. Drizzle with a little olive oil.

Remove the tray from the oven and turn the grill to high. Unwrap the garlic and squeeze the soft garlic from the bulb into a large saucepan, then tip the rest of the contents of the tray into the saucepan. Add the stock along with the beans into the pan and bring to the boil. Simmer for 10 mins, then stir in the kale and add the juice of half of the lemon, taste and season, adding more lemon juice if you like. Cook for 2 mins, until the kale is wilted.

Slide the bread under the grill, cook for 1-2 mins, until golden, then remove and flip over. Finely grate half the Parmesan all over the top of the slices then slide back until the grill for 2 mins further, until the cheese is melted.

Spoon the soup into bowls, add a swirl of pesto to the top of each, then finish with a scattering of Parmesan. Finish with a crack of black pepper and either top with or dunk in the giant Parmesan crouton.

name: Cider Mezcal Margarita
description: You've never had cider like this. An apple-y twist on a margarita that combines refreshing cider with smoky mezcal. Homegrown chillies add a spicy kick.
instructions: Sprinkle your cinnamon and sugar onto a plate then rub a lime around the rim of your glass.
Dip your glass into the sugar mixture to create a lovely cinnamon sugar rim.
Add your ice, mezcal, triple sec, lime, a few slices of jalapeño/chilli, agave, and angostura bitters into a cocktail shaker.
Double strain into a rocks glass filled with ice.
Top with the cider.
Garnish with chilli and lime wedge. Enjoy.

name: Cider Pulled Pork Sliders
description: Juicy and incredibly addictive, these eatable pulled pork sliders are the one. Cooking with cider helps to cut through the richness.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Combine the brown sugar, smoked paprika, tomato purée, worcestershire sauce, English mustard and the ground black pepper in a bowl along with a good pinch of salt. Mix to combine. Remove the fat from the pork, pop the shoulder into a casserole dish and rub with the marinade before pouring in the cider.

Pop a lid on the dish and put in the oven for 2-3 hrs. Keep checking every hour to make sure it's not drying out - if it is, add a splash more cider or water. After this time, remove the lid and turn the oven temp up to 170°C. Let it cook for a further 40 mins to 1 hr until sticky and the liquid has reduced. Once the pork is cooked, shred the into pieces with 2 forks and keep warm.

For the slaw, halve the fennel and finely slice – we like to use a mandoline for this. Quarter the apple and finely slice, then finely chop the chives and red chili (remove the seeds if you don't like it spicy!).
Put all of the slaw ingredients into a large bowl and squeeze in the juice of your lemon before seasoning with salt. Give it a good mix with your hands and set aside for assembly.
Toast the buns in a pan, then stuff with a good amount of pulled pork and slaw. Serve the remaining slaw on the side so that everyone can help themselves.

name: Cinnamon Glazed Halloumi Toasts
description: Possibly the most perfect brunch recipe. Here, marinated halloumi cubes team up with a roasted red pepper spread, honey and fresh parsley leaves. Bliss.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and add the walnuts to a baking tray. Cook for 8-10 mins until golden and toasty. In the meantime, dice the halloumi into 2cm pieces. Mix the halloumi with the cinnamon, ground coriander and 2 tsp cumin, then zest in the lemon, setting aside for later.

For the red pepper spread, add drained roasted red peppers to a blender along with 200g of your toasted walnuts, ½ tsp of cumin, garlic and the juice of 1 lemon. Blend until smooth, then taste and season with salt and pepper.

Toast the bread and pick the parsley leaves. Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with 2 tbsp of olive oil, add the halloumi, cooking on both sides for 2-3 mins until nice and golden, before adding the honey and tossing to coat. Spread the roasted pepper mixture onto the toast and top with the halloumi. Drizzle with extra honey, scatter with parsley.

name: Cinnamon Rolls
description: If you love cinnamon rolls, it’s time you learned to make your own. We don’t know what’s better: the smell of these beauties baking in the oven or that first bite.
instructions: Pour the whole milk into a bowl and heat it in the microwave in 10 second bursts until steaming and warm to the touch. Add in the dried yeast and whisk to combine. Leave for 5 mins. Make sure your butter is at room temperature.

Fit a stand mixer with a dough hook and add the flour to the bowl along with the salt. Crack in the egg, then pour in the warmed milk and yeast mix. Start the mixer on a low setting for a minute then increase the speed to medium and mix for 5 mins until you have a smooth and elastic dough.
Turn the speed back to low and carefully add little pieces of the softened butter, only adding more once the last is incorporated into the dough.
Cover and leave to prove for 1 hour 30 mins until the dough has puffed.
Meanwhile, make the cinnamon filling by beating together all of the filling ingredients in a bowl until really soft and incorporated. Set aside at room temp.

Lightly flour your work surface and tip the dough from the bowl onto it. Flour the surface with flour, then use your hands to shape into a rough rectangle. Use a rolling pin to roll out to a rectangle that is roughly 40°Cm x 50°Cm.
Use a spatula to spread the cinnamon filling mix in an even layer all over the dough. Roll the dough into a spiral then cut into 5cm pieces.

Line a large, deep baking tin with baking paper, then arrange the dough pieces in this, with the flat, spiral side facing upwards, so that they have around 1cm gap between each of the pieces of dough, but are fairly snug in the tin. Cover and leave to prove for 45 mins. Alternatively, you can cover and chill overnight; just leave at room temperature for 20 mins before baking.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan and bake for 25-30 mins until risen, puffed and golden. Leave to cool in the tin for 20-30 mins before icing.

Tip the butter into a mixing bowl or stand mixer and, using electric beaters, whisk for a minute or so on its own to make sure it is super soft. Add in the icing sugar, vanilla and a pinch of salt and beat until smooth and incorporated. Add the cream cheese, one spoon at a time and whisk slowly to incorporate, repeating after each spoon. Spread over the rolls and tear into whilst still warm. Bosh.

name: Citrus Beer Braised Pork Leg
description: The key to this recipe is cooking your pork low and slow. The bitterness of the  beer and citrus helps to cut through the richness.
instructions:
Peel and cut the onions in half across the belly, leaving the top and tail attached.
Peel the garlic cloves and roughly chop the ginger.
Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Unpack the pork leg joint and pat dry with paper towels. Preheat your biggest
pan over a high heat and add a splash of olive oil. Colour the pork on all sides
but the skin. Work your way around methodically, don’t rush! Once the pork is
thoroughly browned, set aside.

Add the onions cut-side down and cook until very caramelised. Chuck in the
whole garlic cloves and the ginger. Cook until fragrant, a couple of mins, then
peel in the zest of 3 oranges in big strips. Add the juice and the beer plus 400ml
of water. Chuck in the rosemary, bay and sugar and stir. Season with a little salt
and pepper, nestle the pork back into the liquid, skin-side up, so most of the
meat is submerged (if you need to top up with water, that’s fine) and chuck in
the oven for 30-40 mins.

Once the skin has started to crackle and blister, reduce the heat to 140°C and
cook for a further 4-5 hours. Once completely tender and the skin is super
crispy, transfer the pork and braised onions and garlic to a serving platter, finish
with fresh orange zest. Skim the fat off the sauce, reduce a little and serve
alongside.

Slice the white onion very thin, add fresh orange segments and roughly torn
coriander stalks ‘n all. Toss with olive oil and serve over top.

name: Citrus Miso Salmon
description: Perfectly cooked salmon on your dinner table in 15 minutes. Zesty, fresh and packed full of miso-umami-ness.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/354°F.
Rinse your rice well and cook it in boiling water.

Finely chop the chilli and add into a jug. Zest and juice the ½ the orange and lime. Add the miso paste and honey. Grate in the garlic and ginger. Give it all a good mix with a fork. Season with salt if needed.

Dip each salmon fillet into the marinade and place individually onto some foil. Start wrapping the foil around the salmon to create a boat. Pour in 3 tbsp of the marinade and continue with each fillet to make four salmon parcels.
Place on a baking sheet and cook for 10-12 minutes, depending on the size of the fillets.

Meanwhile, chop each of your pak choi in half, keeping the root on so it stays together. Pour a small glug of oil into a frying pan and whack up the heat. Fry the pak choi for 2 minutes until charred. Add in 3 tablespoons of water and pop a lid on to continue steaming. Season with a tablespoon of soy sauce.
Now your rice should be ready. Drain and fluff up with a fork.
Open up each parcel, placing the salmon on a bed of rice then pouring over the steaming liquid. Add your pak choi and serve.

name: Citrus Salad
description: This recipe has all the makings of a delicious salad. Juicy blood orange, creamy feta, and tangy capers combine to make something really special. Enjoy.
instructions: Peel and chop the citrus into segments, slices and other random shapes, and add to a bowl along with any excess juice. Finely dice the shallot and lob those in too. Sprinkle in the capers and then season the lot with salt and a splash of olive oil.

Thinly slice the fennel on a mandolin or with a sharp knife and separate the radicchio leaves, halving or tearing any larger leaves. Combine the marinated citrus with the fennel, bitter leaves, crumbled feta, vinegar and mint.
Add a good glug of olive oil, season with salt and Aleppo pepper and toss everything together.
Divide the yoghurt between plates, swoosh across the bottoms, and serve the salad on top. Get stuck in.

name: Citrus Stuffed Pork Belly Porchetta
description: Adding orange and lemon to your porchetta helps to cut through the richness. This is a lovely, balanced porchetta recipe.
instructions: Flip the pork belly over so it’s skin side down. Grab a sharp knife and score a cross hatch pattern in the flesh approx 2cm deep and spaced 4cm apart. Mix the sugar and salt together and toast off the fennel seeds and black pepper in a dry pan. Coarsely crush the spices and mix into the salt and sugar mixture along with chilli, liberally season all of the pork with the spice mix on the flesh side. Place on a rack in the fridge and leave, uncovered, overnight.
