The next day, pat the meat and skin dry, but don’t rub off the spices! Zest the orange and lemon onto the flesh, squeeze over a little juice, finely grate the garlic cloves on and add a splash of cider. Add a splash of olive oil and start massaging the ingredients into the pork.

Time to tie it up, lay the porchetta skin side down on your cutting board. Cut 7-8 pieces of butchers twine or string into lengths that will comfortable wrap around the porchetta. Lay across your cutting laying top to bottom, with a 5cm gap between each string. Slap the pork on top and roll up into a log. Starting in the middle, tie the strings around the pork, working methodically with each string, to maintain the log shape.
Preheat the oven to 150°C. Set up a roasting tray with a rack over top. Fill the tray with the potatoes and sit the pork, seam side-down, on the rack over top. Slide into the oven for 2 hours.
Whip up a quick salsa verde by finely chopping your parsley and combining it with freshly cut orange segments, oregano, a crushed clove of garlic, capers, vinegar, and oil.

Remove from the oven and crank the heat up to max (250°C). Add the broccoli to the tray with the potatoes and slide the whole lot back into the oven for 15-20 minutes until the crackling is super crispy and bubbled.
Let the roast rest for at least 20 mins before slicing into thick rounds and serving, topped with your salsa verde. A serrated knife is best for this!

name: Citrussy Couscous Salad with Herby Tahini Dressing
description: A zesty and zippy salad with plenty of fresh herbs and a nutty tahini dressing.
keywords: Citrussy Couscous Salad with Herby Tahini Dressing
Citrussy Couscous Salad with Herby Tahini Dressing recipe
instructions: Remove and discard the skin from the grapefruit and the oranges. Segment or roughly chop the flesh and transfer to a large bowl, making sure all the juices are collected in the bowl, too. Finely dice the shallot and add to the citrus, then add 4 tbsp olive oil, the red wine vinegar and mix well. Season with salt and pepper, then set aside.
Cook the couscous in a large pan of simmering water for 6 mins, then drain. Finely slice the fennel.

Put the tahini, most of the mint and dill into a blender along with a splash of water. Squeeze in the lemon juice, then blitz until smooth. Scrape down the sides and blitz again, adding more water if necessary. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Just before serving, toss the fennel and watercress into the citrus bowl, along with the couscous. Drizzle the green tahini on top and crumble over the feta. Scatter with the remaining herbs and a sprinkle of chilli flakes, if you like.

name: Citrussy Harissa Lamb & Giant Couscous
description: Make this slow-cooked harissa lamb shoulder in advance and keep it in the freezer. It goes beautifully with the Middle Eastern zhoug dressing.
instructions: Dice the lamb into 3cm chunks. Halve and finely slice the onion. Peel half of the lemon skin using a vegetable peeler, with as little pith as possible, then do the same with the orange.
Add 3 tbsp of olive oil to a heavy bottomed pan over a high heat. Season the lamb with salt and pepper, then fry in batches until deeply golden and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium and cook the onions in the lamb fat with a big pinch of salt for around 10 mins until golden, then add the garlic and cumin. Cook for 1 min then add in the tomatoes, ⅘ of the water, lemon rind, orange rind and harissa. Pop the lamb back in.
Cover with a lid. After 1 hour 30 min, add the giant couscous. Add the remaining water and cook for another 30 mins. Squeeze in the juice of the orange.

In the meantime, make the zhoug. Deseed the green chilli and throw in a blender with half the coriander and mint, holding back a few leaves of coriander and mint for garnish. Add the olive oil to the blender and blitz. Juice in the lemon (the one you peeled for the lamb), mix to combine and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve up the stew topped with the zhoug and a few coriander and mint leaves.

name: Citrusy Miso Roast Chicken with Pickled Chilli & Chive Dressing
description: Roast chicken has always been one of my favourite things on the planet, and in this recipe, which takes inspiration from Ottolenghi's miso butter onions, the miso gives it a buttery, savoury boost and the citrus cuts through the richness. When it was topped with the vinegary dressing, my brother said it was the nicest roast chicken he'd had.
keywords: Citrusy Miso Roast Chicken with Pickled Chilli & Chive Dressing
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Using a pair of kitchen scissors, cut the backbone out of the chicken. Flip it over and press firmly on the breast to flatten the chicken, then turn out the legs so they are facing outwards.
For the marinade, squeeze the orange, lemon and lime juice into a large bowl. Crush and add the garlic and coriander seeds, along with the brown sugar, miso paste and dried tarragon.
Place the chicken in the marinade, skin side down, and optionally leave to marinate for 30 mins to 1 hr, but no longer, as the citrus can start to cure the chicken.
Place the potatoes and peeled whole shallots on a large baking tray and dot with knobs of butter. Put the chicken on top of the potatoes and pour the marinade over the top.
Roast in the oven for 45 mins, spooning the marinade over every 15 mins.

Once the chicken is cooked and the juices run clear, remove from the oven and place on a chopping board. Leave to rest for 15 mins. Meanwhile return the potatoes and shallots to the oven for a further 15 mins to crisp up.
To make the dressing, finely chop the chives and place in a heatproof bowl.
Toast the sesame seeds in a small pan until golden.
Pound the chillies, salt and garlic in a pestle and mortar (alternatively, you can use a mini food processor, or finely chop or grate the chillies and garlic by hand).
Add the oil to the sesame seeds along with the pounded garlic mix. Allow to sizzle for 2 mins, then pour over the chives in the bowl. Stir in the rice vinegar.
Once the chicken has rested, slice it into thighs, legs, wings and breast. Serve on top of the potatoes and shallots, and spoon over the tangy chive mix.

name: Clarified Espresso Martini
description: We've taken an espresso martini and clarified it. Simple as that. This smooth cocktail is going to wow at your next dinner party.
instructions: Juice your oranges until you have the desired amount of liquid.
Add your mezcal, orange juice, Kahlúa and coffee to a jug and mix.
Pour your cocktail mix into your milk. It is important you do it this way around as then the all the cocktail will touch the milk and clarify.
Leave to sit for 2-3 hours while everything curdles and the magic happens.
Pour gently through a coffee filter, at first it will run through cloudy but give it some time until it starts dripping clear.
Then switch to a new container and let it all pour through clear. Add the cloudy run off back into the funnel to filter.
After a few hours it should all be filtered and you’re left with a delicious drink.
Serve over ice, and here I used a little coffee froth to top to still give the iconic espresso martini foamy head. Garnished with three coffee beans.
Enjoy, the drink should last a few weeks in the freezer.

name: Clarified Piña Colada
description: A suave and smooth take on a classic piña colada recipe. A great one to impress your guests at a cocktail party.
instructions: Mix together your rums, coconut cream, lime juice and pineapple juice in a large container with a whisk.
Fill a second container with your milk and then pour in your cocktail. It is important to do it this way around so all your drink touches the milk and clarifies.
Let this sit for 2-3 hours in the fridge.
Once it's had time to rest, carefully and slowly pour the mixture into a funnel and coffee filter, leading to another container.
Let this drip until it turns clear, this may take 2 mins. Then carefully place the funnel and coffee filter into a new container and re-pour the filtered slightly misty liquid back into the funnel.
Wait until everything is filtered then bottle it up. This may take a few hours again.
Serve over a large ice cube with a pineapple frond. You can keep the bottle in the freezer and come back for more whenever you like.

name: Classic Bread & Butter Pudding
description: Bread and butter pudding as it should be done: thick-sliced white bread, lashings of custard, plump sultanas, and a crunchy sugar top. Simple.
keywords: classic bread and butter pudding recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Get out a medium-sized baking dish

Cut the crusts off the bread and spread each slice on one side with butter then cut into triangles. Lay half of the bread buttered-side down into the baking dish. Scatter over half of the sultanas and all of the mixed peel. Lay the remaining bread, buttered-side down, on top (you may need to overlap it slightly). Sprinkle over the remaining sultanas.

Crack the eggs into a large bowl. Pour in the milk and cream. Add the vanilla extract and a pinch of salt and whisk to form a smooth custard. Pour the custard over the prepared bread slices, pressing down on the bread so that it gets a proper soak.

Sprinkle the sugar evenly over the top. Bake in the oven for 35–40 mins until the top is golden brown and the pudding has puffed up slightly. Leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving at the table for everyone to help themselves and tuck in.

name: Classic Butter Brioche
description: We love brioche. It’s a sweetened French bread enriched with butter and eggs that you can flavour however you like. Think cardamom and date, orange and almond, dark chocolate, dried apricot and walnut, pistachio, cinnamon, or dried fruit soaked in Guinness and spices. The possibilities are endless.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the sifted flour, sugar and salt. In another bowl, crumble the yeast into the water, milk and egg yolks and whisk to dissolve and combine. Add this to the dry mixture and combine with your hands, or a spatula or pastry scraper if you have one, until the dough comes together – it will be very sticky at this stage.
Cover the surface with clingfilm and leave to rest at room temperature for 20 mins. Meanwhile, cut the room temperature butter into cubes.

Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 15–20 mins. Now add the butter, a few cubes at a time, kneading it into the dough, making sure the butter is incorporated before you add more. Add any flavourings you want to use now (dried fruits, nuts, chopped chocolate or zested citrus fruit etc). Lightly flour the dough all over and put it back into the bowl. Cover with cling film again and refrigerate for 1 hour.

Line a baking tray with baking parchment. Take the dough out, shape it into a loaf approximately 25 x 15cm and place it on your prepared tray, seam facing down. Once this is done, refrigerate for a further hour. Then remove from the fridge and leave to rest at room temperature for 30 mins.

Preheat the oven to 220°C fan. Brush the dough all over with the egg wash. Turn the oven down to 180°C and bake for 35–40 mins, taking care not to burn the top. You may need to turn the oven down to 150˚C after 30 mins if they are starting to over-brown.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool in the tin for 10 mins before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Classic Chicken Biryani
description: This is my absolute favourite chicken biryani recipe, full of rich, aromatic flavours that capture the essence of Indian cuisine. There are lots of biryani variations, from Hyderabadi chicken biryani to Pakistani biryani, but this one stands out for its perfect blend of spices, tender chicken, and fluffy rice.
instructions: Chop the thighs in half lengthwise.
Combine the chicken with the yoghurt until you are ready to use, or up to 12 hours.
Wash the rice well in cold water, three times until the water comes out clean. Allow it to soak in 1 litre of water for 30 mins.

In a dry skillet, toast the cumin seeds, coriander seeds, cloves, fennel seeds, black peppercorns and green cardamom. Toast for 1 min until fragrant and blitz in a spice grinder. If you haven't got a spice grinder, pound the mixture in a mortar and pestle until it forms a fine paste.
Finely slice the onions and finely chop the tomatoes. Thinly slice 1 lemon and chop the last one in half.
Heat up 50ml of oil in a pan and fry the onions until very crispy and darkened, about 15 mins. Remove ¼ of the onions and set aside.

Add in the biryani spice mix along with your chilli powder, ½ tsp turmeric, ground nutmeg, cinnamon stick, black cardamom and 2 tsp salt. Cook for 1 min, allowing the spices to bloom and become fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, whole green chillies, sugar, grate in the garlic and ginger. Cook for 5 mins until the tomatoes have softened and are bubbling.
Add in the chicken, yoghurt and 100ml of water. Mix well and cook for 10 mins until the chicken is 80% cooked through. Set aside.

Drain the rice, and cook in 1 litre of fresh cold water with 1 tbsp of ghee, 1 tsp salt, and the juice of half a lemon. Bring to a boil and then set a timer for 4 mins. Drain the par-cooked rice in a sieve and set aside.
Finely chop the coriander and mint. In a small bowl combine 1 tsp turmeric with 4 tbsp milk.

Spread the ghee or butter on the bottom of your heavy-bottomed pan. Spread over half the rice, and top with the cooked chicken and your curried sauce. Make a layer with half of your thinly sliced lemon and then cover it with rice. Top with more rice, mint, coriander, reserved onions. Sprinkle on the turmeric milk mixture to add some colour to the rice.
Cover with a lid and place on a medium heat until you can see steam coming out, then time for 5 mins.
Uncover, plate up with a squeeze of lemon and enjoy.

name: Classic Chicken Kyiv
description: A classic chicken kyiv recipe that we've served with buttery mash and lemony greens.
instructions: Start by making the garlic butter. Add the butter to a food processor and whizz until softened. Grate in the garlic cloves and finely dice and add the shallots. Roughly chop the herbs and bung those in, too. Now add the miso, chilli flakes and the zest of the lemon. Season well with salt and pepper and whizz the whole lot into a bright green, punchy garlic butter.

To build the kyivs, make an incision starting at the thicker end of each chicken breast with a small, sharp knife. You want to create a pocket in the chicken breast for the butter to sit in. The best way to do this is to push the knife in just over halfway, being careful not to cut out any side of the breast. Repeat with the other chicken breasts.

Use a teaspoon or a piping bag to fill each breast with a healthy portion of the butter, leaving the opening clean so you can get a good seal. Press the breast to flatten it slightly then press the edges together with your fingers to reseal the opening.

Now set up a bowl each of flour, egg and breadcrumbs. Pass the chicken breasts through each bowl, flour, egg, breadcrumb and then back through egg and breadcrumbs to get a really thorough coating. Pop the kyivs into the fridge for 20 mins.

Preheat the oven to 200°C. Prick the potatoes with a fork and place onto a lined baking tray. Slide into the oven for 60-70 mins, or until completely tender. Allow to cool briefly before halving and pushing the flesh through a sieve set over a small saucepan. Discard or eat the skins!
Once all your potatoes have been passed through the sieve, place the pan over the heat and gradually add the milk and butter until you’re happy with the texture. Season and set aside.

Strip the leaves from the cavolo stems and roughly chop, finely chop the stems. Preheat a lidded pan over a high heat. Once very hot, add a shot of oil and drop in the leaves. Season with salt and pepper and sauté the leaves for 2-3 mins before adding a splash of water and covering. Cook for 1 min before removing the lid, adding a squeeze of lemon juice
Preheat the oven to 170°C.

Cover the base of a large frying pan with a 1-2cm layer of olive oil. Set over a medium heat and once hot (170°C) cook the kyivs for 2-3 mins on each side until golden brown. Transfer to a tray and pop in the oven for 10-12 mins until cooked through.
Divide the mash between warm plates and serve with a handful of greens. Top each with a kyiv and serve.

name: Classic Dill Pickles
description: This recipe for homemade dill pickles from MOB contributor Ben Lippett really couldn’t be any simpler.
instructions: Cut four ridged cucumbers into spears or rounds. Thinly slice half a white onion and 2 cloves of garlic. Deseed and finely chop your chilli.
Pop all your veg in a bowl and add 10g salt, along with the dill, bay, and chilli. Set aside.
Leave for 2 hours. Drain the excess water from the vegetables and put them into a sterilised jar.
To make the pickling liquid, combine 240ml of water with the vinegar, sugar and spices in a pot and bring to a simmer.
Once all the sugar has dissolved, pour the hot brine over the cucumbers and seal the jar.

name: Classic Hunter’s Chicken
description: This is a pub classic and just about the most comforting thing you can make. Serve this hunter’s chicken recipe with the butteriest mash and some simple steamed greens.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

Lay a streaky bacon rasher on a chopping board and use the back of a large knife to stretch the rasher so it becomes elongated (you want it to be about 1.5 times its normal length). Repeat with the remaining rashers.

Season the chicken breasts lightly with salt and cracked black pepper. Taking one rasher at a time, wrap the rasher around the chicken breast, slightly overlapping it as you go, then repeat with another rasher so that the chicken is wrapped in two slices of bacon. Repeat with the remaining chicken breasts and bacon rashers. Put the chicken breasts into a roasting tin and into the oven for 25 mins.
While the chicken roasts, use a sharp knife to finely slice the chives, then set aside and finely grate the cheddar.

Mix the Worcestershire sauce and the BBQ sauce together, then spoon over the chicken, and scatter over the cheddar. Put back into the oven for 5 mins until the cheese and sauce are bubbling. Remove from the oven and top with the finely chopped chives.

name: Classic Meringues
description: Here is a simple meringue recipe which you can use and adapt to make different shapes and flavours.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 120ºC. Line a baking tray with baking parchment. Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolk (you can use the yolks as the base for Carbonara, to make your own mayonnaise and also for dressings). Make sure your egg whites are at room temperature.

In a bowl, use an electric whisk to whip the egg whites with the juice of the lemon for about 5 mins until thick and glossy with soft peaks starting to form. Slowly beat in the sugar, 2 tablespoons at a time, and continue until you have stiff peaks form (when you hold the whisk up, the mixture should stand in a firm peak).

Use a metal spoon to spoon out big fist-sized, roughly rounded dollops of the beaten whites onto your prepared baking tray and bake for 1 hour or until set. Turn off the oven and leave the meringues inside to dry for another hour, with the oven door closed.
Once cooled, serve or store in an airtight container until ready to serve (they’ll keep for up to two weeks).

name: Classic Mint Sauce
description: A very easy recipe for real homemade mint sauce. The perfect accompaniment to roast lamb, and a Sunday lunch must-have.
instructions: Pick the mint leaves and set the leaves. Reserve the mint stalks.
Heat the sugar, vinegar, salt and mint stalks in a small saucepan set over a medium heat. Bring the mixture to a boil then simmer for 3-5 mins.
Remove the pan from the heat and set aside until the mixture has cooled to room temperature.
Meanwhile, bring a medium pot of water to a boil over a medium heat. Fill a bowl with icy water.
Blanch the mint leaves in the boiling water for a few seconds then transfer to the icy water to refresh.
Squeeze the water out of the mint leaves, then finely chop and transfer to a bowl.
Set a sieve over the bowl and strain the cooled sugar and vinegar mixture through it, pouring the mixture over the mint leaves. Mix to combine.
Place the mint sauce in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days.

name: Classic Pork Tonkatsu
description: The ultimate fakeaway. Crunchy pork. Tangy sauce (so easy to make). Zingy slaw. Ticks all the boxes.
instructions: Make the sauce. Stir the Worcestershire and sugar together until dissolved. Then add the rest of the sauce ingredients in and mix until a glossy sauce forms. Set aside.
Slaw time. Finely slice or shred the cabbage. Add to a bowl with the rice wine vinegar, sesame seeds and season with salt. Mix everything together, set aside.
Pork time. Get three bowls out. Add flour to one, breadcrumbs in the other, and lastly, crack and beat the eggs into the next. Season all three with salt.
Dip the pork in the flour, followed by the eggs and then the breadcrumbs, making sure it is properly coated.

Place a pan on medium heat with enough oil to coat the bottom. Once hot, add the tonkatsu, and cook on both sides until golden, and the pork is cooked through, 7-10 mins. If the breadcrumbs are browning too quickly, turn the heat down a little. Take the pork out of the pan and allow to rest on a wire rack for a couple of minutes.
Reheat the rice, slice up the tonkatsu. Serve both on a plate with some slaw. Pour the sauce over the pork and finish with the remaining sesame seeds.

name: Classic Potato Gratin
description: A creamy, oozy, bubbling potato gratin is hard to beat. It’s the perfect side dish for a dinner party or festive celebration.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C fan. Grease a baking tin using ¼ of the butter.

Crush the garlic and add it into a large saucepan with the remaining butter, milk, thyme, cream, bay leaf and lots of freshly cracked pepper. Place it over a medium heat and let the mixture come to a simmer, then turn the heat down to low (the mixture shouldn’t bubble) and let it gently infuse for 10 mins. Season to taste with plenty of salt then strain the solids out through a sieve.

Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and use a mandolin or very sharp knife to slice the potatoes into 2-3mm slices. Rinse the potatoes in a bowl of cold water to remove excess starch, then drain and pat dry.
Get the potato slices into the prepared baking dish. Pour ¾ of the hot cream mixture over the potatoes, stir to evenly coat them, then pour the remaining hot cream over the top.
Slide into the oven and bake for 30-35 mins or until the potatoes are cooked through and the top is golden.

name: Classic Sausage Casserole
description: Whip up a hearty sausage casserole with Mob’s classic sausage casserole recipe. Tender sausages, rich broth, and fresh vegetables. Perfect for a cosy meal. If you’re after an easy recipe that will leave you feeling full and satisfied, you need to look no further. Enjoy.
instructions: Halve, peel and thinly slice the onion, then remove the top and seeds from the peppers, and cut them into long, 1cm-wide slices. Peel and finely chop the garlic.

Heat a shot of olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the sausages for around 5 minutes, until browned all over. Use tongs to lift them out of the pan and put onto a plate.
Add another shot of olive oil into the pan, then scrape in the sliced onions and peppers. Cook, stirring, for 10 minutes until softening and caramelising.

Add the chopped garlic and tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes, stirring regularly. Tip in the chopped tomatoes, chicken stock pot or cube, Worcestershire sauce and both cans of beans, along with the liquid from the cans. Bring to the boil and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Nestle the sausages into the pan and simmer for another 10 minutes, turning the sausages halfway, until they’re cooked through and the sauce has thickened slightly.

Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley (stalks and all) and scrape into a bowl. Finely chop the red chilli ( remove the seeds if you prefer less heat), add to the bowl then zest in the lemon. Drizzle in another shot of oil and add a little salt and plenty of cracked black pepper. Mix well.
Season the casserole to taste, then spoon into bowls and serve with the chilli gremolata on top and garlic bread for mopping up.

name: Classic Shortbread
description: These classic biscuits are buttery, crumbly and incredible with a cuppa. And they’re easier to make than you might think.
instructions: Line two baking trays with baking parchment. Ensure your butter is very cold. Cut the butter into cubes.

Sift the flour, sugars and salt together in a large bowl and mix to combine. Add the cold butter and use your fingertips and thumbs to rub the flour mix into the butter until it resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolk and vanilla and use your hands to gently bring the mixture together into a dough, being careful not to overwork it.

Using a rolling pin, roll the dough out on a floured surface to approximately 1cm thick. Use an 8cm cookie cutter (or 6cm if you prefer mini shortbreads) to cut the dough into circles. Place them on the prepared baking tray and refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours, but preferably overnight.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan.

Slide the baking tray into the oven and bake for approximately 12 mins, or until the edges are just starting to brown. Remove from the oven, cool on the tray for a couple of mins, then transfer to a wire rack. Dust the tops with more sugar and leave to cool completely.

name: Classic Sweet & Sour Chicken
description: Your favourite sweet and sour takeaway, done at home. Pineapple is crucial in this dish.
instructions: Start by chopping the onion and peppers into 2-3cm chunks, and thinly slice the spring onions.

Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk together with salt and pepper. Then stir through the cornflour (don't worry if it's a little lumpy). Cut the chicken into bitesize pieces and add to the bowl so they're all coated.
Heat the oil in a wok. Once hot, add the chicken. Fry until golden (do this in batches if you have to). Transfer to a rack. Discard most of the oil, leaving a little in the pan.
Add the chopped onion and peppers into the hot pan. Stir-fry until starting to soften a little, 3-5 mins.
Stir the pineapple, ketchup, rice vinegar, sweet chilli sauce and sugar into the peppers. Remove off the heat and toss the chicken through, until coated.
Reheat the rice.
Share the rice between plates. Top with sweet and sour chicken, a scattering of spring onion and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

name: Classic Tabbouleh
description: This could be the tabbouleh recipe to end all tabbouleh recipes. If you’re a fan of Middle-Eastern cuisine then you’re in for a treat, as this Lebanese tabbouleh recipe is certain to tick all the right boxes. Discover the freshness of Middle Eastern cuisine with our vibrant tabbouleh recipe. A delightful blend of herbs, grains, and tangy dressing.
instructions: Cook the bulgur wheat following pack instructions then drain really well through a fine sieve. Leave to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley leaves, then pick the mint leaves and finely chop those too. Scrape everything into a large bowl.
Very finely chop the spring onions and add these to the bowl. Dice the tomatoes into 1cm cubes, then cut the cucumber into similar sized pieces and add both to the bowl.
Drizzle in the olive oil, squeeze in the lemon juice and tip in the cooked and strained bulgur.
Use a spoon to mix all the ingredients together, then season really well with salt and black pepper and stir again.
Tip the flaked almonds into a small frying pan and put over a medium heat. Fry for 3-4 minutes, tossing regularly until evenly golden brown. Tip into the bowl and toss again.

name: Claypot Rice
description: This claypot rice dish from Angela Hui is a comfort classic. It's rich, meaty, and super moreish. If you want a fairly traditional Chinese clay pot rice recipe – this is it.
ingredients: Lap Yuk Chinese Cured Pork Belly
instructions: Start by washing the rice. Put the rice into a bowl, add enough water to cover, then use your hand to agitate the rice and swirl the grains. You’ll see the water go cloudy; discard the cloudy water, fill up with clean water and repeat at least three times until the water runs clear. Add 500ml of water and soak the rice for 30 mins. It’s important not to miss the soaking step as this helps the rice cook through evenly.
Next, make the sauce. In a small bowl, mix all the sauce ingredients together. Set aside.

You can either make this dish in a clay pot or a rice cooker. Place the meat on top of the washed, un-cooked rice, press the button, and cook normally. By cooking the meat and rice together, the fat from the meat seeps into the rice.

For those using a saucepan or clay pot, bring the rice to a boil on high heat and cover with a lid. Once bubbling, turn the flame down to the lowest setting possible and cook for 12 mins. Switch off the heat and let the rice stand for 1 minute with the lid still on. Once steamed, take the meat out and slice it.

Fluff the rice, return the meat to the rice along with the sauce, spring onions and an extra drizzle of sesame oil. Have fun stirring the rice and make a glorious mess together. Serve with greens or choi or eat as is.

name: Clementine Gin & Tonic
description: If you're bored of regular gin and tonic, this citrus version will pick you up on a Thursday after work. Rosemary makes this drink feel wonderfully seasonal.
instructions: Start by cutting your lemon into a few slices then cut the rest into wedges.
Add ice to a balloon gin glass.
Pour in your gin, squeeze two wedges of lemon and top with the Fever-Tree Spanish Clementine Tonic Water.
Garnish with a lemon slice and a sprig of rosemary.

name: Coca Cola Chicken Wings
description: A popular dish from the ’90s that we’re bringing back with style. Unlike most wing recipes, these are cooked on the hob to make the stickiest sauce.
instructions: Cut the chicken wings in half at the joint then pat dry with kitchen paper. Season with salt and black pepper. Thickly slice the ginger leaving the skin on.

Get a large wok or frying pan over a high heat. Drizzle in a good glug of neutral oil. Add the chicken wings and fry for around 15 mins, flipping regularly, until evenly browned. Add the ginger and chilli flakes to the pan. Stir and cook for a further 30 seconds.

Pour in the Coca-Cola, soy and Shaoxing wine or sherry and give everything a good mix. Bring to the boil then cover the pan with a lid (or baking tray) and lower the heat to medium. Leave the chicken wings to simmer away for 15 minutes, then remove the lid and turn the heat back up to high.
Cook for a further 15 mins until most of the sauce has evaporated and the wings are sticky and tender.
Give everything one final stir then pile onto a large serving plate. Thinly slice the spring onions (green and white parts) and scatter over the top. Serve at the table for people to help themselves.

name: Coconut "Chicken" Noodle Soup
description: This warming noodle soup takes only 30 mins to make is packed with veg and flavour. A perfect meal for going into autumn.
instructions: Smash your garlic and lemongrass. Roughly slice your shallot, chillies and ginger.
Mix your veg stock cubes with 1.2 litres of hot water.
Pour your coconut milk and vegetable stock into a pot and add your aromatics. Bring to a boil then let it simmer on low heat for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, slice your courgette width-wise into coins and fry on a griddle pan along with your chicken pieces and a glug of oil until crispy and golden.

Chop the ends of your pak choi and tenderstem broccoli. Add the broccoli into the broth for a few mins then add your pak choi and peas. Squeeze in the juice of half a lime, season with salt and pepper and let this all simmer on low heat.
Place your rice noodles into a heatproof bowl and cover with boiling water. Leave for a few mins then drain.
Take the pot off the hob and add a ¼ of the noodles into a bowl along with a ladle or two of the broth. Add a portion of your fried “chicken” and courgette, repeat for the remaining 3 bowls.
Slice your spring onion and add to each bowl along with a small handful of coriander and tuck in.

name: Coconut Cake
description: A simple coconut sponge cake recipe that uses both coconut milk and desiccated coconut. A gorgeous celebration cake.
instructions: Heat the oven to fan 150°C. Grease two round 16cm cake tins and line with baking paper. Make sure your butter is at room temperature.
Get the flour, baking powder and salt in a mixing bowl and whisk until combined.

In another bowl, use an electric whisk to beat the butter and sugar together for 2-5 mins until light and fluffy. Crack the eggs in, one at a time, and beat until combined each time before adding another.

Sift the flour mixture into the butter and beat until just combined. Pour in the coconut milk and desiccated coconut and use a spoon or spatula to fold everything together until you have a fully incorporated batter.

Divide the batter between the prepared cake tins. Bake in the oven for 30-40 mins until golden brown and a toothpick inserted comes out clean. Leave to cool in the tins for 10 mins then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

Meanwhile, make the buttercream. Beat the butter alone for 4–5 mins on high speed. Sift in the icing sugar and add the vanilla and cream then beat on a low speed to bring it together. Beat on high for another 2–3 mins.
To serve, spread the buttercream over both cooled sponges and pop one on top of the other, sandwiching them together. Sprinkle over the toasted coconut flakes.

name: Coconut Caramel Chicken Rice Bowl
description: Spicy, sticky and a little bit sweet. This caramel-coated chicken with fluffy rice and a zingy pickled slaw is perfect midweek food.
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear then drain. Add to a saucepan then pour in the water. Set the saucepan over a high heat. Once boiling, pop a lid on, turn the heat down to low and cook for 12 mins. Remove from the heat and leave covered for another 10 mins.

Meanwhile, peel the carrots then shave them using a peeler. Finely shred the cabbage. Finely grate the ginger. Chop the spring onion whites and chicken thighs into 2cm chunks. Thinly slice the spring onion greens.
Add the carrots and cabbage to a bowl, season with salt and toss to combine. Set aside.
Toss the chicken in the cornflour and season with salt.

Place a frying pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add the sugar, let it melt and cook for 4-6 mins until amber brown. Add the chicken, ginger, whole chillies and spring onion whites and stir fry for 2-3 mins until the veg starts to soften and the chicken is well coated in the caramel (it might smoke up a bit).

Add the coconut water, fish sauce and ½ the vinegar. Bring it to the boil then turn the heat down to low. Leave to gently simmer for 15-20 mins. Then, turn the heat up to high and cook for 5-8 mins until the sauce has reduced by half and the chicken is nicely glazed.
Meanwhile, squeeze as much moisture out of the cabbage mixture then pop in a bowl with the remaining vinegar. Toss through the spring onion greens and season with salt and sugar to taste.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the caramel chicken and pickled slaw.

name: Coconut Cauliflower Traybake Curry
description: All the flavours of a korma have been condensed into one beautiful tray. Getting a nice roast on the cauliflower is key here. Get on it MOB.
instructions: Heat your oven to 220°C/428°F.
Cut your cauliflower into large florets, halve your tomatoes and cut your red onion into wedges. Place all the veg in a large high-sided baking dish.

Mince your garlic and ginger then sprinkle them over the vegetables, along with the cumin, ground coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, ground cardamom and a generous pinch of sea salt. Drizzle with a little vegetable oil, then toss your cauliflower around in your hands until it is totally coated. Roast for 20 minutes, or until the cauliflower is charred and caramelised on the outside.
Turn the heat down to 200°C/392°F.

Pour your ground almonds, vegetable stock and coconut milk into the baking dish and give it a good stir. Return your dish to the oven for 25 minutes, or until your sauce has reduced to a thick consistency.
Meanwhile, roughly chop your coriander.
Pour your flaked almonds into a dry frying pan and toast over a medium heat for a few minutes, by which time you should have crisp and golden flakes.
Reheat your rice as per packet instructions. Check the seasoning of your curry, then serve it over rice. Scatter with your coriander and flaked almonds, then dig in.

name: Coconut Chicken Curry & Homemade Naan
description: This creamy coconut chicken curry is a fuss-free one-pan dish. Baking your naan while the pan is simmering is the trick to perfecting this evening meal.
instructions: Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Mince the garlic and ginger and then dice the onion. Set aside.
Dice the chicken thighs into small pieces, transfer to a bowl and season with the curry powder and a pinch of salt.
Set a large frying pan over a medium-high heat, add a splash of oil and the chicken pieces, then sear the chicken for 5 mins. Remove to a plate.
Add the garlic, ginger and onions to the same pan, add a little more oil and a splash of water, then fry over a medium-high heat for 10 mins.
Add all the seasonings to the pan and cook for 2 mins. Throw in the chicken, coconut cream and green beans, then simmer for 5-10 mins.
To serve, top the curry with coriander, cashew nuts and sliced red chillies, if you like. Serve on a bed of rice.
Mix the flour, yoghurt, sugar, and salt in a bowl until a dough is formed. Add a little more flour if the dough is too wet, or a little splash of water if too dry.
On a surface, knead the dough for 5 mins on a flat surface and allow to rest for another 10 minutes. Then split the dough into 4 portions.
Using extra flour and a rolling pin, roll out flatbreads into an oval shape with roughly 1 cm thickness.
Optionally - melt butter, minced garlic and a pinch of coriander in a hot pan.
On a non-stick pan at high heat, add the naan and cook for 1-2 mins. A bubble should form at the top of the surface, and once formed, flip the naan and cook for another 2 minutes.

name: Coconut Chicken Laab Rice Bowls
description: An easy, healthy laab-inspired recipe that we know you're going to love. This is miles tastier than bland gym food.
keywords: Coconut Chicken Laab Rice Bowls recipe
instructions: Rinse the jasmine rice in a sieve under running water, until the water runs clear, then tip it into a small saucepan with a lid.

Peel the shallots, then slice ¼ of one into small rounds. Half the remaining shallots, and finely slice them. Set these aside. Finely dice one of your chillies, leaving the seeds in if you like it hotter.

Get a sauté pan over a medium heat, pour in a glug of vegetable oil, then tip in your finely sliced shallots and chopped chillies. Cook these for about 10 mins, until they have softened and just started to caramelise.

Pour ½ of the coconut milk and all the water into your rice pan, along with a big pinch of salt, then get it over a high heat to bring it up to a boil. Turn the heat down to a very gentle simmer, then pop the lid on the pan. Cook it like this for 12 mins. Once this time is up, turn the heat off and leave the pan to sit with the lid on for 5 mins more.
Back to your sauté pan, tip the chicken mince into the pan along with a big pinch of salt, and fry for about 5 mins, until it has taken on some colour.
Pour the remaining coconut milk into the pan, then turn the heat right down. Simmer it for about 7-10 mins, until the chicken is tender and the coconut milk has totally reduced down.
Cut the baby cucumbers into matchsticks. Pick the coriander leaves from their stalks and the mint into small sprigs, and finely slice the remaining red chilli.
Take the chicken off the heat. Add the lime juice, the fish sauce and sugar to the pan, then taste and season with salt if needed.

Use a fork to fluff up your rice, then spoon it into four bowls. Top with the chicken, then place your lettuce, cucumber sticks and herbs on the side. Scatter the remaining sliced shallot rounds and red chilli on top, then serve it up.

name: Coconut Chutney Recipe
description: A sweet and spicy coconut chutney recipe that'll add some excitement to literally anything you eat it with.
instructions: Chop the ginger and transfer to a blender with the grated coconut, chilli, daria dal (if using) and a splash of water. Blend all the ingredients, season with salt and pour into a serving bowl. You can add more or less water, depending on how thick you like your chutney.

For the tarka, place a small saucepan over a medium heat with the oil. Once hot, add the mustard seeds, urid dal, asafoetida, curry leaves and dried red chilli. Fry for a few seconds, then pour straight over the chutney just before serving.

name: Coconut Crusted Paneer Bites
description: Crystelle Pereira has given the baking a break for a minute and created us these delicious coconut-crusted paneer bites. So moreish, you'll love them.
instructions: In a bowl, mix together all the dry ingredients (your cornflour and various seasonings) apart from the desiccated coconut and chilli flakes.
Add desiccated coconut and milk into two separate bowls.
Cut the paneer into 25 cubes. Take each cube, dip into the milk, then into the dry cornflour mixture, back into the milk, and finally into the desiccated coconut.
Once all 25 pieces have been coated, heat up your coconut oil in a non-stick pan on a medium-high heat and cook for a few mins on each side until crispy.

Now it’s time to make your honey. Start by finely dicing your chilli. Wipe down the pan and add the diced chilli along with your chilli flakes. Cook this on a dry pan on low heat for 1 minute. Then add in the honey and squeeze in the juice of a lime. Mix to combine and cook this for 4 mins, to allow the chillies to infuse in the honey. This will be very hot, so carefully pour into a small dish and leave to cool.
To serve, dip the paneer in the hot honey and enjoy.

name: Coconut Curried Lentils
description: These creamy curried coconut lentils are a one-pot wonder. Perfect for batch cooking and full of protein, nutrients and flavour. Serve with bread or rice.
instructions: Finely chop the onions and garlic. Grate the ginger (no need to peel it, just give it a good scrub). Rinse the lentils and pick out any stones.

In a large pot over medium-high heat, combine the oil, onion, garlic and 1 tsp salt. When it starts to sizzle, cover the pot, turn heat to low, and cook, stirring every so often, until the onion has softened and has turned translucent, about 7-8 mins.

Add in the ginger, mustard seeds, turmeric, ground coriander, cumin and chilli flakes. Cook, stirring often, until fragrant, about 1 min. Add the water, coconut milk, lentils, and 1 tsp salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce to low, cover and simmer, stirring a few times, for 40 to 50 mins, until the lentils are cooked through.
Stir in the spinach and return to a simmer. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Add in a few tablespoons of coconut yoghurt, the juice of one lime and stir through.
To serve, ladle the lentils into bowls and add a couple more spoons of yoghurt and finish with a sprinkle of chilli flakes if you like. Serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Coconut Dal
description: Eating this coconut dal is like getting a warm hug from your favourite aunt. It's fragrant, aromatic, and you can turn into three easy dishes.
instructions: Give your lentils a really good rinse in a sieve under running water, until the water runs clear.

Get them into a large saucepan, along with the water, turmeric and the coconut milk. Bring it up to the boil, then turn the heat down to a gentle simmer and cook for 30-35 mins, or until the lentils are totally tender. Use a spoon to skim off any scum from the top as it cooks.
Meanwhile, peel and finely slice your onion and garlic, finely chop your chillies and ginger, and roughly chop your tomatoes.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat, and add your coconut oil. Once it has melted, get your cumin seeds and mustard seeds in the pan. Cook them for about a minute, until they pop. Tip your sliced red onions and chilli into the pan, and cook these for about 15 mins, until they are softened and just starting to caramelise. Add your ginger and garlic, and cook for a minute longer.
Add the tomatoes into the pan along with the garam masala, and cook for 5 mins, until the tomatoes have broken down.

Once your lentils are soft, tip the onion mixture into the pan. Roughly chop your coriander and get this in there too. Give it all a good mix, then taste and season with salt. Loosen it up with more water if it needs it – you want it to be quite soupy.

name: Coconut Macaroons
description: These coconut macaroons are a surprisingly easy bake. Perfect for a gluten-free afternoon tea.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Grease a mini cake tin (with multiple moulds in one tray) with non-stick vegetable oil spray.
Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise or dressing).

Add the egg whites with all the remaining ingredients in a large saucepan and set over a medium heat. Stir and turn the mixture thoroughly and constantly with a spatula, making sure to scrape the bottom as you go. Cook until the mixture is drying out and just starting to turn brown and singe a little.
Scoop the mixture into the mini cake moulds. Bake for around 15 mins until crisp on the outside (keep an eye on them or they can dry out).
Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the trays for 10 mins before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Coconut, Ginger & Beetroot Soup
description: Earthy beets, warming ginger and creamy coconut milk come together for this bright pink showstopper of a soup.
instructions: Heat your oven to 175°C.
Wash and chop the beets. Melt ½ the coconut oil in a small pan set over a medium heat.
Toss the diced beets in the melted coconut oil and add to a baking tray. Roast in the oven for 45 mins, turning once halfway through.
While the beets are roasting, peel and chop the shallots, and grate the ginger.
Heat the remaining coconut oil in a large pot and sauté the shallots and ginger over a low flame, covered, until soft and fragrant.
Stir in the roasted beets, then pour enough stock to cover the beets. Simmer for 10-15 mins until the beets are very soft.
Transfer the mixture to a blender and blitz until smooth. Pour in the coconut milk and blend once more to combine, then add more stock as needed to adjust the consistency.
Squeeze fresh lime juice into the soup and divide across the bowls. Combine the sesame seeds and sesame oil and drizzle a few spoons over each soup.

name: Coconut, Ginger & Celeriac Soup with Activated Charcoal
description: Level up your soup game by adding smoky activated charcoal. This one is a moody grey soup for moody grey days.
keywords: Ginger & Celeriac Soup with Activated Charcoal
Ginger & Celeriac Soup with Activated Charcoal recipe
instructions: Peel and chop the white onion and ginger. Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pot set over medium heat, then add the onion and ginger. Cover the pot and sauté for about 5 mins until fragrant.
Carefully peel and chop the celeriac into small pieces (it can be hard to manoeuvre), then add to the pot. Pour in the stock and simmer for 20 mins, or until the celeriac is soft.
Transfer the mixture to a blender (or use a handheld mixer). Add the coconut milk and blend until very smooth.
Stir in the activated charcoal by hand to achieve a swirl effect.
Divide the soup across four bowls, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

name: Coconut, Peanut & Sesame Stuffed Aubergines
description: Hasselback aubergines filled with a sweet and spicy peanut and sesame paste then roasted on top of a coconutty chickpea curry. You’re going to love them.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Hasselback the aubergines (cut deep slits into the aubergine widthways, just less than 1cm apart, making sure not to cut down to the bottom) and salt generously, set aside whilst you make the paste.

Blitz the peanuts, sesame seeds, green chilli, ginger, tomato purée and ½ the garam masala in a blender or food processor until chunky. Add a splash of the coconut milk in and blend to make into a paste. Then mix through the desiccated coconut before seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Using your hands, fill the slits of the aubergine with the peanut sesame paste until it reaches the top of the aubergine, ensuring they are packed full of the paste.

Finely chop the garlic and coriander stalks. Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan and add the garlic, coriander stalks and curry leaves. Fry them off for 30 seconds until fragrant then add the remaining garam masala and cook for another 30 seconds. Add the tinned tomatoes, coconut milk (reserving just a drizzle for garnish) and drained chickpeas and mix to combine. Simmer for 10 mins until slightly reduced. Season to taste.
Pop the aubergines on top of the dish. Cover with tin foil and roast in the oven for 40 mins then remove the foil and cook for another 20 mins.
Remove from the oven and drizzle with the reserved coconut milk and a few coriander leaves for garnish and eat with roti.

name: Coconut, Spinach & Tomato Dal
description: Once you master dahl, it will become a regular. This one is creamy and coconutty, topped with a runny egg and chilli oil. Mandatory fresh coriander to finish.
instructions: Add lentils to a large saucepan along with the veg stock, coconut milk and ground spices. Season generously, then bring to the boil and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Next, peel and finely chop the ginger and roughly chop the nuts. Scrape into a bowl along with the chilli flakes and sugar. Finely slice the onion and garlic cloves - set aside separately.
Back to the dal - chuck in the tomatoes. Cook for a further 15 minutes, stirring regularly, until the dal has thickened and the lentils are tender.

Meanwhile, get a frying pan over a medium heat. Add half the vegetable oil to a pan over a medium heat until shimmering, then add the sliced onion. Cook for around 8 minutes, stirring until crisp then remove with a slotted spoon into the bowl with the ginger, nuts, chilli and sugar. Add the sliced garlic to the hot oil. Cook until the garlic is just turning golden then take the pan off the heat. Pour the garlic along with the oil into the bowl with the other chilli bits. Give everything a good mix.

In the same pan, heat the rest of the oil over a medium heat and crack in the eggs. Baste the eggs with the hot oil using a spoon until they are cooked to your liking, then remove with a slotted spoon.

Stir the spinach through the dal and squeeze in the lime juice. Once the spinach has wilted, taste and season with salt if needed, then divide between bowls. Top each with egg, then drizzle over the crispy chilli oil. Tear over some coriander to serve.

name: Coconut-Braised Chicken & Chickpeas
description: Braising your chicken in coconut not only tenderises the meat but imparts it with a lovely fragrant flavour. This recipe is guaranteed to get you top marks at dinner time.
keywords: Yellow Coconut Braised Chicken & Chickpeas recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan.

Pat the chicken skin dry with kitchen paper, then season the skin with salt. Pour in just enough netural oil to cover the base of a large ovenproof casserole dish and add the chicken skin-side down to the cold pan. Now turn the heat to medium low and cook on just one side for 8 mins, without interference – there should be a gentle sizzle as the chicken fat releases and the skin gets golden.

Meanwhile, mince the garlic, and finely slice the peeled ginger into rounds, and finely slice the onion into half moons. Bruise the lemongrass with the flat side of the knife and repeat to the red chillies.

Remove the chicken thighs and set aside on a plate (don’t worry about cooking it through now as it will be added back to the pan). Add the onion to the chicken fat and cook for 2 mins or until lightly golden. Now add the ginger, garlic, curry paste and curry powder and the thick white part of the coconut milk and cook for 2 mins or until it begins to lightly caramelise and thicken.

Add in the drained chickpeas, the remaining coconut milk, lemongrass, chilli, sugar, and fish sauce. Mix well then bring to a simmer. Return the chicken so it is skin-side up, and add just enough stock so the liquid is halfway up the chicken (you might need a bit more or less stock than listed in the ingredients). Bring to a simmer and cook in the oven for 45 mins uncovered until the chicken is cooked through.

When the chicken is ready, remove the hot dish from the oven and remove the lemongrass stalks and ginger pieces. Squeeze in the juice from ⅓ of the limes and taste for seasoning – add a splash more salt or fish sauce if needed. Allow the chicken to rest for 10 mins.
Divide the chicken between plates and sprinkle over chopped fresh coriander leaves and crispy shallots. Serve with your toppings of choice (I suggest cooked rice, lime wedges and fried eggs).

name: Coconutty Air Fryer Tofu & Quinoa Salad with Peanut Dressing
description: This is a lovely little coconutty tofu-y recipe that's perfect for meal prep and lunches throughout the week.
keywords: Lunch Box: Coconutty Air Fryer Tofu & Quinoa Salad with Peanut Dressing
Coconutty Air Fryer Tofu & Quinoa Salad with Peanut Dressing recipe
instructions: Tip the desiccated coconut into one bowl or tray, ⅗ of the coconut cream into another, and the cornflour into a third. Season each one with salt and pepper.

Cut the tofu into 3cm cubes. Dredge in the cornflour, coating all the sides. Dunk in the coconut cream and shake off the excess before tossing in the desiccated coconut, pressing down firmly to make it really stick. Set aside on a tray.

Add the tofu to the air fryer then drizzle with oil. Heat the air fryer to 180°C and cook for 15 mins, then flip and cook for a further 10 mins until evenly golden. Carefully remove from the basket and set aside.
Cut the Tenderstem into thirds and toss with olive oil, salt and pepper. Add to the air fryer basket and cook at 180°C for 8 mins. Add the tofu back in and cook for 2 mins until warmed through.
For the peanut dressing mix the peanut butter with the remaining coconut cream, juice of ½ the lime, the sesame oil and the soy sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Finely chop half of the mint and mix with the quinoa and the remaining lime juice.

Spoon out the quinoa between your Tupperware containers, top each with the broccoli and tofu and then garnish with mint and a pinch of chilli flakes, if you're feeling fancy. Box up and pop in the fridge - these will keep for up to 3 days.Keep the peanut dressing separate – either pour a little over in the morning or stash it in a little pot inside your lunch box to add just before eating.

name: Coconutty Air Fryer Tofu & Quinoa Salad with Peanut Dressing
description: This is a lovely little coconutty tofu-y recipe that's prepped in just 15 mins.
instructions: Put the desiccated coconut in one bowl or tray, ⅗ of the coconut cream in another and the cornflour into a third bowl or tray. Season them all.

Cut the tofu into 3cm cubes, then dredge in the cornflour, coating all the sides. Dunk in the coconut cream and shake off the excess before tossing in the desiccated coconut, pressing down firmly to make it really stick. Set aside on a tray.

Add the tofu to the air fryer then drizzle with oil. Heat the air fryer to 180°C and cook for 15 mins, then flip and cook for a further 10 mins until evenly golden. Carefully remove from the basket and set aside.
Cut the Tenderstem into thirds and toss with olive oil, salt and pepper. Add to the air fryer basket and cook at 180°C for 8 mins. Add the tofu back in and cook for 2 mins until warmed through.
Mix the peanut butter with the remaining coconut cream, juice of ½ the lime, the sesame oil and the soy sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Finely chop half of the mint and mix with the quinoa and the remaining lime juice.
Divide the quinoa between two plates and top with the broccoli and tofu. Drizzle with peanut sauce, then garnish with mint and a pinch of chilli flakes, if you like.

name: Coconutty Butter Bean Curry
description: A homemade sesame paste teamed with the nuttiness from a round of coconut milk and lots of fresh veg makes for an outstanding curry dish. Trust us.
instructions: Peel and chop the garlic. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over a medium-low heat and fry the garlic for 3 mins. Cut the Tenderstem into 2cm pieces. Drain the butterbeans (no need to rinse). Add the curry paste to the pot and cook for 1 min, before adding the butter beans, 4/5 of the water and coconut milk. Simmer away gently for 10 mins, until thickened.

In the meantime, get on with the herby topping by juicing the lemon. Finely chop the basil and mint. Add the crème frâiche to a bowl with the lemon juice, basil and mint, saving some mint leaves for serving. Loosen with the rest of the water and season with salt and pepper.
Get your sesame seeds into a processor and blitz until the oils start releasing and you've got a smooth paste. You’ll need to keep scraping the sides down — this will take about 3 mins in total.
Add the tenderstem to the curry and cook for 3 mins. Then add the sugar snaps. Pop a lid on and cook for 2 mins. Heat your flatbreads up according to package instructions.

Take most of your sesame paste and mix with 1 tbsp of the coconut sauce until combined. Keep adding the liquid gradually until you have a pourable, smooth consistency. This is key to preventing the curry from splitting. Pour the sesame mix back into the pan, mix well and season with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Top the curry with the herby drizzle, mint leaves and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Get your flatbreads on the table and tuck in.

name: Coconutty Butter Bean Traybake with Turmeric Tomatoes
description: Butter beans baked in a silky coconut and turmeric sauce, topped with bursting cherry tomatoes. Serve straight from the dish with warm flatbreads for scooping. It's delish.
keywords: Butter Bean & Coconut Gratin with Turmeric Tomatoes
Butter Bean & Coconut Gratin with Turmeric Tomatoes recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 230°C. If your coconut milk is set solid, gently warm in a small saucepan until just melted, otherwise go ahead with the next step.

Make the sauce. Peel and roughly chop the shallots, garlic and fresh turmeric (if you can't find it, an equal quantity of fresh ginger + ½ tsp ground turmeric will work too). Set aside a few spoonfuls of the coconut milk for garnish, then add the rest to a blender with all the sauce ingredients. Blitz until completely smooth, then pour into a round 30cm shallow casserole dish or a similar-sized baking tray. Add the drained butter beans and mix with the sauce.
Mix the whole cherry tomatoes with the olive oil, maple syrup, cumin seeds, fine sea salt and ground turmeric, and scatter over the beans.

Bake for 35 mins, rotating the dish halfway, until the beans have browned, the sauce has thickened and reduced and the tomatoes are soft and bursting. Pop the flatbreads in the oven for the last 5 mins to warm through.
While the beans are cooking, cut the cucumber into thin matchsticks and dress with the juice of half the lemon and the salt.

Drizzle the reserved coconut milk over the gratin. Top with a good grind of pepper, squeeze over the juice of the remaining lemon and add a drizzle of olive oil. Finish with the cucumber and serve with warm flatbreads for scooping.

name: Coconutty Lentils With Peanut & Coriander Chutney
description: A high-protein recipe that's perfect for a weeknight. She's filling, she's flavourful, she's the moment.
keywords: Coconutty Lentils With Peanut & Coriander Chutney
instructions: Finely slice the garlic and half the tomatoes. Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a large saucepan over a low-medium heat and fry the garlic for 3 mins, until lightly golden. Add the curry paste and fry for 30 secs before adding in the cherry tomatoes, lentils and around ¾ of the tin of coconut milk. Bring to a boil then reduce to a simmer, cook for 10 mins. Stir through the spinach.
In the meantime, bring a pot of water to a boil and carefully drop in the eggs. Cook for 6 min, then remove and drain under cold water. Once cool enough to handle, peel and set aside.

Roughly chop the coriander and then finely slice the green chilli. Add coriander and half of the chilli to a food processor with peanuts, lemon juice and reserved coconut milk. Blitz until smooth then season with salt and pepper.
Serve lentils in bowls topped with a drizzle of the peanut chutney, jammy egg, green chilli and more coriander, if you like.

name: Coconutty Mackerel Fried Rice
description: This dish is a bit like kedgeree with the same curried vibe, but I've intensified it by using coconut milk to fry the rice making it super aromatic and flavourful. Smoked mackerel is a great way to increase your protein and omega 3 intake and paired with egg it's a midweek dinner powerhouse.
instructions: Cut the Tenderstem broccoli into 3cm pieces. Roughly chop the coriander and slice the cucumber.

Heat the olive oil in a wok over a medium heat. Whisk the eggs, season with salt and pepper and add to the wok. Cook undisturbed until mostly set, around 10 seconds, then gently fold with a heatproof spatula and remove from the pan.

Reduce the heat to medium and pour in the coconut milk. Keep stirring and scraping the bottom of the wok so you caramelise the solids without them sticking and burning. This will take 5-10 mins. The coconut milk will be really fragrant, opaque and foamy.

Add the Tenderstem broccoli and cook for 2 mins, then tip in the cooked rice and curry powder. Add the peas and allow to thaw, then pour in the soy sauce and season with pepper. Remove the skin from the smoked mackerel and flake into big chunks. Gently stir through the rice along with the most of the coriander, egg and squeeze the juice of half the lime.
Serve up with the sliced cucumber, remaining lime, cut into wedges and extra coriander scattered over.

name: Coconutty Peanut Dumpling Traybake
description: Dumplings, peanut sauce, chickpeas and loads of veg, all baked in one tray. Feeds a crowd and sorts dinner with basically no effort.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely chop the coriander stalks and pick the leaves. Juice one of the limes and cut the other into wedges for serving.

In a large roasting tin, whisk together the peanut butter, coconut milk, coriander stalks and soy sauce until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Then drain the chickpeas and add to the tray along with your mixed veg and frozen dumplings or gyoza. Give everything a good mix.
Cover the tray tightly with foil and bake for 30–35 mins, until the sauce is bubbling and thickened. Cook for another 5–10 mins if the veg needs longer.
Peel back the foil carefully and add the lime juice. Scatter with coriander leaves, sesame seeds and chilli flakes, if using. Serve with additional lime wedges on the side..

name: Coconutty Potato and Chickpea Soup
description: This creamy broth is the perfect thing to warm your cockles. Fragrant with lemongrass and chilli, then finished with the most beautiful sizzling ginger oil.
instructions: Roughly chop your onion, 4cm of your ginger, 4 cloves of your garlic, your lemongrass and your finger chillies, removing the seeds.
Pop them all in a small food processor and whizz to a paste.
Heat a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add a splash of olive, then sizzle for a minute until fragrant.
Tip your curry paste into the pan and cook for 10 mins until it has darkened slightly and is deeply fragrant. Keep stirring it to ensure it doesn’t catch.
Meanwhile, peel and halve your potatoes.
Add your cumin, turmeric and ½ tsp of your chilli powder to the pan, then cook out for 1 min.
Pour in your coconut milk and vegetable stock, then bring to a simmer. Drain your chickpeas, and get these in the pan along with your potatoes. Add a pinch of salt, then simmer for 25 mins.
Meanwhile, make your sizzling ginger oil. Chop your remaining ginger into matchsticks. Finely dice your remaining garlic cloves.
Add all of these ingredients to a heatproof bowl along with your remaining ½ tsp chilli powder.
Heat 100ml of vegetable oil in a saucepan until it is very hot. Carefully pour your oil over the ingredients in a bowl, then mix to combine.
Pour your soup into bowls, then drizzle over your sizzling oil. Top with coriander, then serve.

name: Cod & Chickpea Salad on Toast
description: It's a well-known fact that everything is better on toast. And this Cod & Chickpea Salad is no exception. Enjoy.
instructions: Firstly, salt the cod. Dust the fillets of cod in a tsp of table salt, rubbing it over the surface to cover them in salt. Set aside in the fridge for at least 20 mins (it’s best if you leave them uncovered overnight)
Peel and finely dice ½ the onion and add to a bowl. Add the juice of one of the lemons and the sugar. Season well with salt and set aside to lightly pickle.

Cut the garlic cloves in half (no need to peel) and add to a saucepan. Cut the remaining onion half into wedges and add to the pan along with the fennel seeds. Add the cod and cover with cold water. Set over a medium heat and bring to a simmer. As soon as it starts to simmer take it off the heat and set aside for 10 mins. Then lift the cod onto a plate and leave to cool. You can move it to the fridge if you like.

Drain the chickpeas and add to a bowl, add the pickled onion. Flake the cod into the mix, then finely chop the parsley and add to the bowl. Add the dijon, remaining lemon juice and a generous glug of olive oil and toss well.

Toast the bread, drizzle with olive oil and add to the plate. Spoon the cod salad over the top and finish with a crack of black pepper and some extra parsley leaves- or some dill if you like. Serve with a little squeeze of extra lemon.

name: Cod & Curried Chickpeas
description: Topped with a big dollop of yogurt, and using only 7 ingredients, this cod is a perfect midweek staple.
instructions: Add a tbsp of olive oil to a saucepan over a medium heat. Add the curry paste to the oil and sizzle for 2 mins, then tip in the cans of chickpeas with their water. Bubble away for 10 mins, until thickened slightly.

Stir in the spinach and add the juice of the lime and season to taste. Turn the heat down to a simmer and drop the cod fillets in so they’re submerged. Cook on a simmer for 2 - 3 mins, until the cod is cooked through- careful not to touch it too much so the fillet doesn’t break apart!
Use a large spoon to gently lift the cod into a bowl. Add a spoonful of the chickpeas and spinach over the top.
Top with a dollop of yogurt, drizzle with a little olive oil and finish with a crack of black pepper and coriander.

name: Cod & Double Bean Traybake
description: Flaky white fish and lovely beans form the backbone of this healthy traybake. A lush midweek dinner.
instructions: Rub the cod fillets each with around 1 tsp of table salt, then set aside, uncovered in the fridge. If you have time, do this the night before, but even doing it at the start of the recipe will make a difference to how the fillets flake apart. Heat the oven to 180°C fan.
Make the aioli. Finely grate or crush the garlic into a small bowl and add the lemon juice, stir to combine, then add the mayo and season well.

Finely slice the onion and garlic. Heat a large glug of olive oil in a deep saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add the sliced onion along with a big pinch of salt and fry for 10 mins, until softened. Add the garlic, dried oregano and fennel seeds. Pour in the wine and allow to bubble until reduced by half. Add the butter beans along with any water from the cans/jars. Crumble in the stock cube and bubble away for 8-10 mins, until thickened.

Add the zest and juice of the lemon and season well, then stir in the green beans. Cook for a minute, then tip into a large roasting tray. Nestle in the cod fillets and bake for 10 mins, until the cod is flaking apart.

While it cooks, make the salsa. Finely slice the green beans and add to a bowl with the juice of the lemons, dijon and honey stir well. Finely chop the green chilli and add the bowl along with 2 tbsp olive oil. Season well.
Remove the cod from the oven and serve, drizzled with salsa and with a dollop of aioli for everyone. Serve the remaining lemon half, cut into wedges, on the side.

name: Cod & Pak Choi Laksa with Udon Noodles
description: A nourishing, punchy laksa with silky coconut broth, flaky cod and slurpable udon noodles. This one’s fast, fragrant and full of goodness.
instructions: Cut the cod into bite-sized pieces and set aside.
Peel and finely grate the garlic and ginger. Finely slice the kaffir lime leaves, discarding the tough stems.

Heat a large nonstick frying pan over a medium heat and give it a couple of sprays of olive oil. Add the garlic, ginger and a splash of water. Let that cook for 1 min to soften, then stir in the laksa paste and cook for 1 more min until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, then bring it all to a gentle simmer. Add the sliced makrut lime leaves and let everything bubble away for 5 mins.
Meanwhile, separate the pak choi leaves, trim the ends, and slice each leaf and stem in half lengthwise.

Add the pak choi and cod to the pan. Simmer gently for 5 mins, stirring a couple of times, until the cod is opaque and flakes easily. Stir in the soy sauce and fish sauce, adding more for seasoning if needed.
Cook the udon noodles following pack instructions, then divide between bowls. Ladle over the laksa and finish with picked coriander leaves.

name: Cod & Sweetcorn Fishcakes with Sweet Chilli Slaw
description: Crispy, curry-spiced fishcakes with sweetcorn, perfect for kids and adults alike. Served with a crunchy slaw and ideal for freezer stash dinners.
keywords: Cod & Sweetcorn Fishcakes with Sweet Chilli Slaw
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings 
Peel and chop the potatoes into chunks. Tip into a saucepan, cover with salted water and bring to the boil. Simmer for 15–20 mins until soft. Drain and steam-dry for a few minutes, then mash until smooth.
Heat the grill to high. Pat the cod dry, season with salt and pepper, and drizzle with olive oil. Pop it under the grill for 6 mins, until just cooked through. Set aside.

Thinly slice the spring onions, zest the lime, and drain the sweetcorn. Finely chop the coriander stalks (saving the leaves for the slaw and garnish).
Then add with half the Greek yoghurt, Thai curry paste to the potato mash. Flake in the grilled cod, keeping some nice chunky bits. Season with salt and pepper, then mix gently to combine.

Make the slaw. Finely shred the red cabbage and place in a bowl. Add the sweet chilli sauce, mayo, the remaining Greek yoghurt, juice of the lime, chopped coriander leaves, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix well to coat. (You can leave the dressing off the kids portion or serve on the side if).

Set up a breadcrumbing station: one plate with flour, one with a beaten egg, and one with panko. Form the fishcake mixture into patties (make smaller ones for the kids). One by one, coat each fishcake in flour, then egg, then panko.
If making ahead - at this point you can freeze.

Heat a generous lug of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the fishcakes in batches and fry gently for 3–4 mins on each side, turning occasionally, until golden and heated through.
Alternatively, cook in an air fryer at 200°C for 15–20 mins until crisp and hot.

Serve up! 
Kids Plate: Dish up the mini fishcakes with a little slaw on the side and a dollop of yoghurt.
Parents Plate: Dish up your larger fishcakes and the slaw. Garnish with a scattering of sesame seeds and remaining coriander leaves.

name: Cod & Tomatoes With Baked Coriander Rice
description: A fresh and flavourful dish that your GP will approve of . There's plenty of veggies and lean protein in this healthy recipe.
keywords: Cod & Tomatoes With Baked Coriander Rice
Cod & Tomatoes With Baked Coriander Rice recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Give the rice a good wash, a few rounds in fresh cold water should do it. Once the water is running clear, drain and set aside.

Grab a blender and stuff in half of the spinach, ginger, ⅘ of the coriander, the green chilli, and garlic cloves. Pour in the can of coconut milk and add in your water. Blend until smooth and bright green.

Thinly slice the red onions. Set a large saucepan (with a lid) over a high heat. Once hot, add a splash of olive oil and toss in two-thirds of the red onion. Cook with a pinch of salt for 5-6 mins over high heat, until starting to caramelise.

Tip in the rice and stir through the toasty onions and the rest of your spinach. Now add the green coconut milk mixture and bring to a simmer. Once hot, add the lid and slide into the oven for 25 mins.
Season the cod fillets with salt and pepper. After the rice has had 15 mins, remove the lid and add the cod fillets on top. Return the lid and slide back into the oven for a further 6-7 mins.
Remove from the oven and allow to rest for 5 mins.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and toss with the lime juice, the remaining coriander, and sliced onion. Divide the rice and fish between bowls and top with the fresh tomato and onion salad.

name: Cod Goujons with Homemade Tartare and Burnt Lemon
description: Crispy goujons paired with lemony, herby and salty tartare sauce. Sublime. Recipe by MOB Contributor Thomas Straker.
instructions: Starting with the cod, cut it into even sized goujons.
Get 3 bowls. Put your flour into the first, whisked eggs into the second and breadcrumbs in the last. Season the bowls with salt and pepper.

Dip the fish into the flour then egg then breadcrumbs. Make sure it is evenly coated and repeat for all the fillets. Place the battered fish onto a tray and set aside in the fridge until you are ready to use.

Mayo time. Separate the egg yolks from the whites (you can freeze the whites for later). Place the egg yolks, mustard and white wine vinegar into a bowl with a pinch of salt. Beat together with a whisk and keep beating whilst you add all of the oil bit by bit (olive and vegetable). If it gets too thick before you’ve finished adding the oil, loosen with a small splash of water, then add the rest of the oil.

Now for the tartare. Prepare all the ingredients - dice your shallots and cornichons, juice the lemon, grate the zest and roughly chop your capers and parsley. Mix together with the mayo (made in step 5) then place in the fridge until you are ready to use it.
For the burnt lemons, cut 2 lemons in half, get a frying pan on a high heat and place them in the pan cut side down. When they begin to burn on the bottom, remove.

Pour 2L of vegetable oil into a large pan on a medium-high heat. You want it nice and hot (around 180°C but not smokey), then drop in the goujons and fry until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper.
Arrange on a plate and serve with dollop of fresh tartare sauce, a wedge of lemon and a sprinkle of salt. Enjoy!

name: Cod Milanese With Chilli & Orange Dressing
description: You've had a veal milanese, you've had a chicken milanese, but have you ever had a cod milanese? This Italian-inspired recipe will be a hit with pescatarians.
keywords: Cod Milanese With Chilli & Orange Dressing
Cod Milanese With Chilli & Orange Dressing recipe
instructions: Grab a large piece of parchment paper and fold it in half. One by one, pop the cod fillets between the two halves and use a rolling pin or frying pan to gently bash them out flat. You don’t want to go too hard, cod isn’t as robust as chicken and can break into pieces. Take your time and try to get them as thin as you can.

Set up your breading rig, that’s one bowl of flour, one of beaten eggs and one of breadcrumbs. Mix the sesame seeds through the breadcrumbs and season well with salt and pepper. Season the cod fillets with salt, and carefully pass them through the three bowls, thoroughly coating with the sesame panko.
Mix the mayo with the finely grated garlic clove, season and set aside. Thinly slice the red onion and pick the parsley and dill leaves. Pop them into some icy water to crisp up.

Thinly slice the chillies and add to a bowl with the segments and juice of the orange, salt and pepper. If you need a bit more sharpness, add a drip of white wine or sherry vinegar, you might not need it depending on the orange.

Shallow-fry the cod in olive oil, working in batches, until crispy and cooked through. Drain and dress the herbs and red onion with your chilli orange dressing. Heat the rice according to the package instructions and divide between plates. Top the rice with a piece of crispy cod, a handful of salad and some extra dressing.
Add a dollop of garlic mayo to each plate and get stuck in.

name: Cod Wrapped in Parma Ham with Asparagus
description: A banging surf n' turf combo - the salty Parma Ham works an absolute charm with the fish
instructions: Remove your cod from the fridge and pat dry.

Preheat your oven to 180°C. Halve your potatoes. Put them in a baking tray then pick over the rosemary leaves and season with some salt, pepper. Drizzle with olive oil, and put into the oven for 35 minutes.

In the meantime, take your cod, and put it into a bowl. Finely grate over the lemon zest and squeeze over half of the and the juice (cut the remaining half into wedges for serving). Add salt, pepper and a drizzle of olive oil, and mix together.
Wrap 2 slices of Parma Ham around each cod fillet.

Snap the woody ends off the asparagus and discard. After 35 minutes in the oven, take out the potatoes. Add the cherry tomatoes and the asparagus. Place the parma ham wrapped cod on top, and put the tray back in the oven for 12 minutes or until the cod is opaque throughout.
Serve with the reserved lemon wedges. Enjoy.

name: Cod with Burst Tomatoey White Beans & Basil
description: Juicy cherry tomatoes, creamy white beans and salty olives all under flaky cod in one parcel that steams to perfection. It's ridiculously easy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Drain and slice the roasted peppers. Drain and rinse the white beans. Slice the basil and set aside.

Lay out a large rectangle of baking paper in front of you (per person), portrait. Add the beans, cherry tomatoes, roasted peppers, red wine vinegar, olives and olive oil to the bottom half of the baking paper, leaving a 10cm gap between the food and the edge closest to you. Season with salt and black pepper, then give it all a gentle mix. Pat the cod fillets dry and lay them on top of the veg. Season with a little more salt and pepper.
Fold the top half of the baking paper over the food then fold the outside edges over each other to seal (like a cornish pasty), creating a steam-tight parcel.
Bake for 15–18 mins, until the cod is cooked through and flakes easily.
Remove from the oven, open the parcel and remove the cod onto plates. Mix the basil through the veg and serve up.

name: Cod with Tomato & Pepper Couscous
