description: Zesty, steamy and seriously satisfying. This one-pot couscous dish makes the most of juicy peppers, flaky cod and punchy oregano. Fresh and fast.
instructions: Zest half the orange and set the zest aside. Cut two wedges from the orange for serving, then juice the rest into a measuring jug and top up with just-boiled water.

Heat the oil in a large ceramic casserole dish or lidded frying pan over a medium heat. Add the frozen peppers and cherry tomatoes, then pick over the oregano leaves. Cook for about 10 mins, stirring often, until the peppers have softened and the tomatoes are starting to burst.
Season the cod with salt and pepper. Nestle it into the veg and grate over the reserved orange zest. Cover with a lid and steam gently for 10-12 mins until the cod is opaque and flakes easily.

Meanwhile, tip the couscous into a bowl. Pour the orange juice and hot water mixture over the couscous. Cover with a plate and leave to stand for about 5 mins until all the liquid is absorbed. Fluff it up with a fork and season with salt and pepper.
Lift the cod out of the pan and set aside. Toss the couscous through the peppers and tomatoes until well combined.
Spoon the couscous onto plates and top with the cod. Pick over the parsley leaves and serve with the orange wedges on the side.

name: Cod with Tomatoey Baked Rice & Aioli
description: Expect plenty of bright, clean flavours in this recipe. Lemon, capers, and dill is a classic Greek combo.
keywords: Cod with Tomatoey Baked Rice & Aioli
instructions: Make the Greek Tomato Rice Traybake batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the flour onto a tray and season with salt and pepper. Pat the cod dry and coat in the flour on all sides.

Heat some oil in a frying pan set over a medium-high heat and add the fish. Cook for around 2 mins on each side until golden, then transfer to the oven to cook through for 8-10 mins (timings will vary slightly depending on the thickness of the cod).
Get the rice into a small saucepan set over a medium heat and cover with a lid. Meanwhile, finely chop the dill, then add to a bowl with the mayo and the zest and juice of the lemon.
Serve the rice topped with the cod and a dollop of the dill aioli, then scatter with capers.

name: Cod with Yoghurt, Peas & Harissa Butter
description: We've paired firm fillets of cod with a spicy harissa butter and a scrimmage of peas and broad beans. Lush.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Rub the cod all over with olive oil, then season with salt and pepper before placing on a lined baking tray.
Bring a pot of water to the boil, then add a generous pinch of salt. Add the peas and broad beans. Cook for 1 ½ mins, then drain and rinse with cold water to cool.
Combine the yoghurt, a splash of olive oil, and salt and pepper in a bowl, then add the cooled peas and broad beans. Mix well.
Roast the cod in the oven for 9-11 mins or until cooked and flaky.

Meanwhile, in a medium frying pan, add the tomatoes and a splash of olive oil and gently fry for 6-8 minutes until just starting to collapse then add the butter and harissa. Give the pan a shake then turn the heat to the lowest it can go to keep warm until you're ready to serve. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and grate in the zest.
Pick the herbs then dress with the lemon and a pinch of salt.
Divide the yoghurty peas between plates, then place the cod fillets on top. Spoon over a few spoonfuls of the tomato, harissa butter before piling the herb salad on top.

name: Cod “Aglio e Olio” with Polenta
description: Simple, clean flavours shine through in this flavourful dish. You won't believe how easy making perfect polenta is.
keywords: Cod “Aglio e Olio” with Polenta recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Season the cod fillets with salt and pepper and rub with a little olive oil before coating them in smoked paprika. Pop them on a lined baking tray and set aside for 5 mins.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the garlic and chillies and finely chop the parsley. Remove the stalks from the cavolo nero and finely chop them. Roughly chop the leaves.

Set a pan over a medium heat and add plenty of olive oil, enough to cover the bottom of the pan. Once just warm, add the garlic and chilli and gently cook for 5-6 mins. At this point, add the cavolo nero stems and leaves and add a splash of water. Season with salt and cook until the greens are nicely wilted. Finish with the parsley.
Slide the cod into the oven for 9-11 mins or until cooked and flaky.

Add the milk to a saucepan with the water and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer and whisk in the polenta. Cook for 6-7 mins or until the polenta is thick, creamy and has lost its raw bite. Whisk in the butter, season with salt and pepper and add some lemon zest to finish.

Divide the polents between warm plates and top with a cod fillet. Squeeze the juice of a whole lemon into the greens and then tip over the cod, adding lots of the garlicky, spicy oil. Serve with extra lemon wedges and get stuck in.

name: Coffee Caramel Yoghurt Cake
description: Heavy on the coffee caramel glaze and ridiculously moreish, you'll have your pals swooning over you after their first bite of this.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Line the bottom of a 20cm cake tin with baking paper, grease the tin and add 1 tbsp of flour. Tap the flour so it lightly covers the inside of the greased tin, including the sides. Tap any excess flour out.
Pour the oil into a large mixing bowl. Add the eggs and both sugars, whisk everything together until light and creamy.

In a separate bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder and bicarb together with ½ tsp of salt. In a small cup, stir together the coffee granules with 2 tbsp of boiling water. Fold the flour mixture into the egg mixture, then add the Greek yoghurt and coffee. Stir together then tip into the lined cake tin. Bake for 60-70 mins, until risen and golden, and a skewer comes out clean.

Whilst the cake bakes, make the caramel drizzle. Pour the cream into a saucepan along with the coffee and sugar, place over a low heat and cook until the sugar and coffee have dissolved, then, add the cubed butter, and a pinch of salt. Gently whisk until it comes together as a caramel sauce, cook for 3-5 mins until slightly thickened, then set aside to cool to room temperature. If the caramel is too thick once cooled, place it back on the heat with 1 tbsp of cream and stir until warm.
Turn the cake out onto a platter and pour the caramel over the top, gently pushing it over the edges of the cake to create a drip effect.

name: Coffee Jelly
description: Coffee jelly isn't just fun to eat, it's fun to make as well. This coffee jelly recipe will show you how to make these lovely, wobbly cubes.
instructions: Prepare your coffee and add to a saucepan with the water and agar.
Heat until boiling then bring heat right down and simmer until all the agar has dissolved.
Pour into a tray and place in the fridge to set. This should take about 2 hours.
While the jelly sets prepare the oat milk.
Pour your oat milk into the bowl with the agave and vanilla extract then mix until combined.
When the jelly is set, cut it into cubes and use a spatula to remove from a tray.
Pour into a glass and the fill with your oat milk. Enjoy!

name: Colcannon Fritters
description: Using incredible Ocado ingredients, these cheesy potato cakes topped with crispy bacon and poached eggs. We can’t think of a more perfect St. Patrick's brunch.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C
Peel your potatoes and chop them into chunks.

Pop your potatoes in a pan and fill it with enough cold water to cover them completely. Salt generously, then bring to a boil. Simmer for 15 mins until the potatoes are tender. Drain and allow to steam dry in the colander for a few minutes.
Meanwhile, shred your cabbage and slice your spring onions.
Heat a little oil in a frying pan over a medium heat, then tip in your cabbage. Fry for 7 mins until soft and tender.
Mash your potatoes with your butter and milk.
Tip your potatoes and cabbage into a bowl along with your spring onions and plain flour. Grate in some cheddar and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Shape your mixture into 8 chunky patties.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with a good glug of vegetable oil. Add your patties and fry for about 4 mins on each side until crisp and golden. Pop on a baking tray and slide into the oven to keep warm.
In the same pan, fry your bacon rashers for a few minutes until crispy.

Fill a deep saucepan with water. Once boiling, stir the water with a spoon to create a whirlpool. Crack an egg into the centre and cook for 3 mins until the whites are cooked through but your yolk is still soft.
Serving time. Pop two colcannon fritters on a plate and top with your poached eggs and bacon. Sprinkle with chopped chives and enjoy.

name: Cold Chicken Noodle Salad
description: Zingy and full of flavour, this salad is king of salads. Bouncy noodles and charred chicken tossed in a flavourful dressing with mint and cucumber. Fresh.
instructions: Add half of yellow thai curry paste into a bowl with the chicken and 2 tbsps of oil. Season with salt and pepper, mix together.

Place a large frying pan on medium heat, add 4tbsps of oil in with sunflower seeds, cook, stirring until toasted, 2-3 mins. Then add the remaining curry paste and cook for 1-2 mins. Transfer into a large mixing bowl.
Re-use the frying pan, place on medium-high heat with 2 tbsps of oil. Cook the chicken until fully cooked and starting to char, 8-10 mins, flipping half-way through. Transfer to a board and let cool.
Meanwhile, cook the vermicelli/rice noodles according to package instructions. Then, rinse under cold water until cool to the touch.

Stir the fish sauce through the sunflower seeds with the juice of the limes, taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed. Trim, halve and chop the cucumber into 1cm chunks, add to the dressing. Pick the mint, chop the tomatoes into 2cm pieces, peel and thinly slice the shallots. Add all three to the dressing.

Once the chicken has cooled, use two forks to shred it. Add the cold chicken and noodles into the mixing bowl, toss together. Taste and season with more salt, pepper, lime juice and fish sauce if needed.
Share the cold chicken noodle salad onto plates.

name: Cold Coconut Noodles with Silken Tofu & Edamame
description: Cold soba noodles drenched in a coconut-miso dressing, with crunchy edamame and silky tofu on top. Properly refreshing for when it's boiling out. You can make the dressing a day ahead - just give it a good stir before using, then dress your noodles right before you're ready to eat.
keywords: cold coconut noodles with silken tofu & edamame
cold coconut noodles with silken tofu & edamame recipe
instructions: Cook the soba noodles according to the packet instructions, then drain and rinse immediately under cold running water until completely cold - this stops them cooking further and stops them clumping. Leave to drain well in a colander.

Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2-3 mins, shaking occasionally, until lightly golden. Tip onto a plate to cool, then grind half in a pestle and mortar for garnish and leave the rest whole.

Peel and roughly chop the ginger, and peel the garlic. Zest and juice the limes. Add the coconut milk to a blender with the miso, whole toasted sesame seeds, ginger, garlic, lime juice and zest, soy sauce, sesame oil and the ice cubes. Blitz until completely smooth, then taste and adjust with more lime or soy sauce if needed. If it's very thick, loosen with a splash of cold water.
Pour boiling water over the edamame and leave for 2 mins, then drain and rinse under cold water. Cut the silken tofu into rough cubes directly from the packet, handling gently as it breaks easily.

Toss the cold noodles with most of the dressing until well coated. Divide between bowls and top with the edamame and silken tofu. Spoon over the remaining dressing and finish with the ground sesame seeds.

name: Cold Cucumber Udon With Ponzu
description: Super refreshing, mildly spicy, and perfectly balanced. Thick chewy homemade udon in the most perfect broth – a light and refreshing meal.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil.

Meanwhile, trim and finely slice the red chilli. Halve the ginger widthways, trim and thinly slice the green part of the spring onions, leaving the whites whole. Halve both citrus fruits. Slice the cucumber into thin half moons.

Add the dashi, soy sauce, ginger, spring onion whites into another saucepan. Place on medium-high heat and bring to the boil, once boiling, turn the heat off and let it infuse for 10 mins. Then, place a fine strainer onto a jug. Strain the soy mixture through the sieve, discarding the bits. Stir the rice vinegar, chilli, orange juice and lemon juice into the mixture. Set aside, in the fridge to cool.

Once the water is boiling, drop the noodles in, cook for 8-10 mins (depending on the thickness of the noodle) or according to package instructions. Then, drain and rinse under cold water – this will help firm up the noodles, creating that chewy texture.
Share the udon into bowls, pour over the cold ponzu and top with fresh cucumber, spring onion greens and furikake/sesame seeds.c

name: Cold Tofu Noodle Salad
description: Not all salads are made equal. This fresh and zingy noodle salad delivers a fair whack of protein thanks to the tofu. Treasure this one.
instructions: Drain and pat dry the tofu, chop into 2cm cubes.

Place a large frying pan on medium heat, add 4 tbsp of oil in with sunflower seeds, cook, stirring until toasted, 2-3 mins. Then, add half of the curry paste and cook for 1-2 mins. Transfer into a large mixing bowl.

Re-use the frying pan, place on medium-high heat with 4 tbsps of oil. Add the tofu and cook until golden on all side, 6-8 mins. Then, turn the heat down, stir through 1 tbsp of yellow Thai curry paste and cook for 1-2 mins until coated. Remove from the heat.
Meanwhile, cook the vermicelli/rice noodles according to package instructions. Then, rinse under cold water until cool to the touch.

Stir through the soy sauce, the juice of 2 limes and 4 tbsp of oil, taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed. Trim, halve and chop the cucumber into 1cm chunks, add to the dressing. Pick the mint, chop the tomatoes into 2cm pieces, peel and thinly slice the shallots. Add all three to the dressing.
Add the tofu and noodles into the mixing bowl, toss together. Taste and season with more salt, pepper or lime juice if needed.
Share the cold noodle salad onto plates, serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Confit Duck, Bacon and Beans
description: This is a bit of a treat, definitely a good one to impress a friend or special someone. Remember to keep the fat for later use (roast potatoes!)
instructions: Preheat your oven to 150°C.
Season the duck legs well with salt and set aside for at least 20 mins.
Add the duck fat to a heavy pan with a lid. If the fat has solidified slightly, place it into the oven for a few minutes to warm up and become liquid again.
Pat the duck legs dry with kitchen paper, then place them in the pan and make sure they're completely covered by the duck fat.
Place a piece of greaseproof paper over the top and push it down until a little of the duck fat goes over the surface to weigh it down.
Pop the lid on the pan and place it into the oven for two and a half hours.

To make the beans, add the pancetta to a saucepan and place over a medium heat with a splash of olive oil. After a few minutes, once the pancetta has started to go golden, finely slice and add the onion.
Cook for about 5 mins until the onion is softening, then mince the garlic and sage and add to the pan. Cook for another 2 mins.

Drain and add the cannellini beans and mustard, and pour in the stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 mins until most of the liquid has reduced and the beans are thick and saucy. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Once the duck is ready, remove from the pan (keep the fat, you can reuse it for things like roast potatoes!).
Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add the duck legs skin-side down along with a spoon of the duck fat. Fry for about 5 mins until the skin is golden brown and crispy. Season with flaky salt.
To serve, spoon up a nice portion of the beans and sit a duck leg on top. Great with a vinegary green salad.

name: Confit Garlic & Parmesan Roast Squash
description: Sweet and creamy roasted butternut squash with soft confit garlic cloves, cooked in the hollows of the squash. Perfect autumn food.
keywords: Confit Garlic & Parmesan Roast Squash Recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.

Cut the squash in half lengthways, then scoop out the seeds. Fill both scooped-out cavities with extra virgin olive oil, then place 3 whole unpeeled garlic cloves into each cavity so they’re submerged in the oil.
Season each half with salt and pepper, then place in the oven to roast for 30-35 mins, until golden and soft.
Carefully spoon out the garlic and allow it to cool for a minute, then squeeze out the soft insides onto a plate or chopping board.
Squeeze the juice of the lemon over the squash while it’s still hot, followed by a generous amount of Parmesan on each side, then chop it into chunks.
Serve the squash with a dollop of ricotta, the soft confit garlic, and a big green salad dressed with lemon juice and extra virgin olive oil. Simplicity at its best.

name: Confit Garlic Chipotle Caesar
description: What do you get when you combine garlic, chipotle, and Caesar salad? Something spectacular, that's what.
instructions: Start by making the confit garlic. Heat the oven to 160°C. Peel the garlic cloves and put them in a small ovenproof dish, then cover them with olive oil so they’re totally submerged. Cover with a lid or kitchen foil and slide into the oven for 30-40 mins, or until the garlic cloves are golden brown and super soft. Remove from the oven and allow to cool. You can do this bit ahead of time!

To make the dressing, combine the chipotle paste, mayonnaise, mustard and grated cheese in a bowl. Mix well and finely grate in the garlic clove. Add the zest and juice of the lemon and mix again. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Cut the focaccia into croutons and toss with olive oil. Tip into a frying pan and cook over a medium heat for 7-8 mins until golden brown and crispy. Set aside.

Roughly chop the kale, hispi, cucumber and lettuce. Add to a large bowl with the beans, chicken and parm. Tip in the croutons and dressing. Toss everything together and divide between plates. Add a few cloves of confit garlic to each plate and a drizzle of the garlicky oil. Finish with a couple of anchovies and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Confit Garlic Goat’s Cheese Toast
description: Less than 5 mins of hands-on cooking makes this the sweet spot between easy and impressive. Perfect for an indulgent breakfast or a starter to a dinner. Swap the goat's cheese for burrata if you prefer.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 130°C.
Halve the bulbs of garlic through the middle and place into a small saucepan. Fill with oil until submerged and then place into the oven for 1 hour.

Meanwhile, toast the sourdough and spread with a generous layer of goat's cheese (or burrata, if you prefer). Finely slice the chives and sprinkle over, along with a pinch of salt and some black pepper.
Once the garlic is cooked, remove from the oven and allow to cool for about 10 mins. Remove and squeeze over the toast, then spread.
Sprinkle with a pinch of salt, drizzle over the honey and enjoy.

name: Confit Garlic Tahini Dressing
description: A tangy, creamy dressing that'll go great on just about everything. It takes a bit of time but it's more than worth the effort.
instructions: Heat the oven to 150°C. Peel the garlic cloves and add to a small ovenproof dish, add enough olive oil to cover the cloves. Cover with a lid or piece of foil and slide into the oven for 40 mins, or until golden.
Scoop the garlic from the dish and add to the base of a bowl. Mash with a fork. Add a drizzle of the confit garlic oil, the Greek yoghurt, tahini, and juice of the lemon. Season with salt and pepper.

name: Confit Tomato Toast
description: My perfect brunch recipe. Peeling the tomatoes is totally optional. I think it’s worth it, they turn into little pearls of flavour. So luxurious. B x
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Cut a tiny cross in the bottom of each tomato. Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil and drop in the tomatoes. After 30 seconds, transfer them to an ice bath.
Peel the little skins off the tomatoes and chuck them into an oven-proof container or a small saucepan.

Smash the garlic cloves in their skins and get them into the pan. Split the chilli lengthways, leaving the stem intact and get that in there with the thyme. Cover the whole lot with plenty of olive oil and pop on the stove over medium heat for a couple of mins.

Now you're going to make a cartouche. Grab a piece of parchment paper that’s big enough to cover the pan and screw it up into a ball. Unwrap it and place it straight on top of the tomatoes so it’s touching the oil and submerging the toms.
Transfer the whole pan to the preheated oven and cook for 40 mins.

Once your tomatoes are cooked, pull them out of the oven and fish out the garlic. Squeeze the flesh out of the skins and purée on your board with the flat of a knife. Add to a bowl with the ricotta and season with salt and pepper. Mix the lot up.
Cut your baguette into four and then each piece in half lengthways. Add a bit of the confit oil to the cut side and toast in a hot pan.
Smear each piece of bread with a spoon of the garlicky ricotta and place it onto plates.
Add your tomatoes to a mixing bowl and tear in the basil leaves. Add the sherry vinegar and plenty of the confit oil. Season with salt and pepper and pile on top of the toasts.
Any leftover oil will keep in a jar in the fridge for 5 days. Chuck it into pasta, dunk bread in it, it's all delicious.

name: Confit Tomatoes with Tahini Yoghurt
description: A really low-effort, high-reward recipe for jammy roast tomatoes. It will yield far more confit tomatoes than you need so you can add them to salads, pasta dishes, sandwiches, or just spoon over toast for one of the most delicious snacks.
keywords: Confit Tomatoes with Tahini Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C.
Slice the top off the garlic bulb. Add the tomatoes, garlic bulb and thyme into a tray and drizzle enough olive oil to cover the bottom of the pan.
Sprinkle over some salt and cook for around an hour or until the tomatoes are soft and jammy.
Squeeze the roasted garlic from the tomatoes into the yoghurt along with the tahini and a pinch of salt. Stir to combine and then spread onto a plate, leaving a well in the middle for the tomatoes.
Spoon the confit tomatoes into the centre and sprinkle over some dukkah and flaky sea salt before dipping the bread in. Enjoy!

name: Cookie Dough Bliss Balls
description: Cookie dough fans, this one’s for you. These nutty, fudgy bliss balls taste like the real deal but are made with all the good stuff like dates, almond flour & cashew butter. Ideal for when you want a sweet hit without turning the oven on.
instructions: Roughly chop the dark chocolate. Chuck most of it into a food processor with the cashew butter, oat flour, almond flour, dates, vanilla extract & protein powder (if using). Blitz until a sticky dough forms.
Scoop out the mixture and roll into roughly 12 small balls. Press the remaining chopped chocolate into the outsides of the balls.
Pop them into the fridge to chill for at least 1 hr until firm.
Once set, transfer them to a Tupperware lined with baking paper – add another sheet between layers if you’re stacking them. Keep in the fridge for up to a week or freeze for up to 3 months.

name: Cookie Dough Pie
description: Three words: cookie dough pie. A flaky layer of homemade pastry slathered in Nutella and topped with hazelnut cookie dough. So good.
instructions: Pastry time. Measure 200g of flour into a bowl or food processor. Cut 100g of cold butter into small cubes. Add to the flour then either blitz or rub together using your fingertips until breadcrumbs form. Mix in 1 tbsp of caster sugar and a pinch of salt then pour in 2 tbsp of cold water. Blitz or beat until it just comes together, if it looks a little dry add 1 more tablespoon of water. Tip the pastry out onto your work surface and briefly knead until smooth. Cover and chill in the fridge for 30 mins.

Meanwhile make your cookie dough. Toast the hazelnuts, if using, then leave to cool. Soften (don’t melt) the remaining 120g of butter in the microwave. In a large mixing bowl beat it with both the sugars until creamy. Crack in the egg, add the vanilla extract and mix to combine. Tip in the remaining 180g of flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt. Beat to form a cookie dough. Roughly chop up the chocolate and hazelnuts, then mix through the dough.
Preheat your oven to 180°C.

Get your pastry out of the fridge. Flour your surface. Roll out the pastry to roughly 1cm thickness and line a 20cm tart tin. Press the pastry into the edges of the tin. Cut off any excess pastry and patch up any holes, if you have any.
Spoon the Nutella all over the base of the pastry, then use the back of your spoon to roughly spread. Don’t worry about it being a super even layer as you don’t want to break the pastry.
Spoon the cookie dough over the Nutella layer. Bake in the oven for 35 mins until the top is golden brown, the edges are set and the middle still a little wobbly.
Serve warm with ice-cream or cooled with a cup of tea.

name: Cookies & Cream Cake
description: An absolutely delicious chocolate and vanilla gluten-free sponge. Oreo lovers, this one's for you.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease and line a 23cm round cake tin. Separate the egg whites and yolkds into two separate bowls. Roughly chop the dark chocolate into 2-3cm pieces.
Use an electric whisk to beat together the butter and sugar for about 4 mins until light and fluffy. Add the egg yolks gradually and beat until combined.
Into a separate bowl, sift the cocoa powder and add the poppy seeds, ground almonds, salt and baking powder. Mix to combine.
Use an electric whisk to beat the egg whites, first on a slow setting, then on medium and finally on high, until they are thick and glossy with soft peaks forming.

Using a spoon, fold half the cocoa powder mix into the butter and sugar mixture, then very carefully fold in half the beaten egg whites (be careful not to knock the air out of the egg whites). Once combined, gently fold through the remaining the cocoa powder mix followed by the remaining egg whites.

Transfer the mixture to your prepared tin and level out to the edges. Bake for 25–30 mins, until risen and firm. Press the top of the cake gently with your fingertips to see if it feels baked through. Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tin for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely.

For the vanilla buttercream: Beat the butter alone for 4–5 mins on high speed. Sift in the sugar and add the vanilla and cream then beat on a low speed to bring it together. Beat on high for another 2–3 mins.
When the cake is cool, spread the buttercream on top (and around the sides, if you like) and dust with roughly chopped dark chocolate if desired.

name: Cookies & Cream Ice Cream Popsicles
description: It’s hard not to love anything that has Oreos in it, and they're perfect with vanilla ice cream. We used a silicone mould to freeze the ice cream into shape.
instructions: Into a sandwich bag, add the Oreo cookies and use a rolling pin to crush them.
Just before the ice cream is ready, add the crushed cookies and churn to incorporate them.
Work quickly to scoop the ice cream into 8 silicone popsicle moulds. Use a palette knife to completely smooth the top and freeze for 6 hours or overnight.

In a medium bowl, combine the milk chocolate, cocoa butter, and cocoa nibs. Place the bowl over a pan of gently simmering water. Stir constantly until everything has melted, then remove the bowl from the pan.
Allow the chocolate mixture to cool to about 104°F/40°C and then pour it into a tall, thin glass. You want a glass that’s deep enough so you can dunk the entire popsicle in.

Pop the popsicles out of the mould and work quickly to dunk them into the chocolate coating. Dangle the popsicle over the glass until the excess coating stops dripping, then flip it upright and place it on a baking tray lined with a silicone mat.
Place the popsicles back in the freeze until ready to use or serve immediately.

name: Cooling Tahini & Tomato Noodle Soup
description: Cold, creamy sesame and soy noodles with juicy tomatoes and a punchy crispy chilli dressing. It’s silky, savoury and seriously refreshing on a boiling hot day.
keywords: Cooling Tahini & Tomato Noodle Soup recipe
instructions: Add the water (you can substitute half of the water with ice cubes if you’ve got a good blender), tofu, miso, tahini, sesame oil and rice vinegar into a blender. Blend until smooth, season to taste with salt (this dish is served ice cold, so that the flavours will be slightly muted from the temperature). I recommend heavily seasoning to your taste.) Place in the fridge or freezer until cold.

Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice the spring onions, and chop the tomatoes into 2-3cm bite-sized chunks. Add both into a bowl with the crispy chilli oil (getting as much of the chilli crisp sendiment as possible) and vinegar, stir together, taste and season with salt, if needed.
Bring a pot of water to the boil. Cook the soba noodles following pack instructions, then drain and rinse under cold running water until completely cool.
Divide the noodles between bowls. Pour over the chilled sesame broth and finish with a generous spoonful of the tomato salad on top.

name: Coriander Chutney Beef Tataki
description: A rich and tasty beef tataki recipe with a fiery homemade chutney. This is one for the ages.
instructions: Put the steak onto a plate and rub with light soy sauce, a pinch of salt and black pepper. Set aside while you make the chutney.

Chop the shallot and chilli into rough chunks. Transfer to a blender with a large handful of coriander and mint, the sugar, rice vinegar, sesame oil, zest of 1 lime, juice of half a lime and a pinch of salt. Blend until fine and set the chutney aside in a bowl.
Add the ginger and garlic to a clean blender along with 1 tbsp water. Blend and set aside.

Grab a frying pan, add a glug of vegetable oil and heat on high for around 3 mins or until smoking. Add the steak and fry for 1 min each side, making sure to sear every part. Stand the steak up to sear the ends, 30 seconds each side. Remove and let the steak rest for 2 mins.
Slice the steak as thin as possible. Place the steak on the side of serving plates and, using the back of a spoon, brush with the garlic ginger paste.

Heat some more vegetable oil in a frying pan for around 3 mins or until smoking. The oil should be hot enough to sear the ginger garlic paste. If the oil is smoking or shimmering, that usually means it’s ready. Gently pour the oil over the steak.
To serve, place the chutney to the side of the steak but not on top. Add a wedge of lime and a handful of cress on top of the beef.

name: Corn & Pepper Rigatoni
description: Sweetcorn in pasta might sound a little chaotic but trust us on this. It's good.
instructions: Thinly slice the peppers and garlic cloves. Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a good glug of olive oil. Once hot, tip in the peppers and season with salt. Cook for 10-12 mins, stirring now and then, until wilted and starting to caramelise and turn jammy. Add the garlic and sugar and cook for another 3-4 mins. Once the sugar has started to catch on the bottom of the pan, tip in the paprika and deglaze with the vinegar. Cook for another 3-4 mins or so until super jammy.

Meanwhile, heat the grill to high, Bring a pot of water to the boil and season well with salt. Add the corn on the cobs for 4-5 mins before removing (keep the water!). Slide the cobs under the grill for 8-10 mins, turning regularly, or until charred. Stand the cobs up on your board and slice off the kernels.
Tip the corn into the pan with the peppers and add half of the Parm and all of the crème fraîche. Stir together.

Tip the rigatoni into the boiling water and cook for 8 mins, or until al dente. Transfer the cooked pasta to the sauce and toss to combine. Add a little pasta water if you need to loosen things up a bit. Keep tossing over a medium heat until you have a glossy sauce that is coating the pasta.
Tear in the basil, toss through and then divide the pasta between warm bowls. Finish with the remaining Parm.

name: Corn & Ricotta Gnocchi
description: If you’re debating what to have for dinner, make this. We used corn to make this sauce rich in fibre, which combines with the ricotta creates a creamy sauce.
keywords: best gnocchi recipe ricotta gnocchi recipe
instructions:
Thinly slice the garlic cloves and spring onions (both green and
white parts) while you boil a kettle.
 Pour the boiling water into a saucepan and add salt. Once
reboiling, drop in the corn cobs and cook for 3 mins, then
remove 2 of the cobs with tongs and transfer to a plate. Cook the
remaining cobs for 3 minutes more until completely tender, then
remove with tongs – making sure to keep the two lots of corn
separate. Turn down the heat on the water to low.
Get a large frying pan searingly hot. Lay in the less-cooked corn
and char the kernels, turning regularly. Once charred, set aside.
Holding the more-cooked corn upright, slice down with a knife,
removing the kernels from the cob. Put these into a blender with
the vegetable stock, ricotta and 2 tbsp of hot sauce. Blitz to a velvety sauce and season to taste.
Come back to the charred corn. Cut the kernels off the cob and
tip into a small bowl. Mix with the remaining 2 tablespoons of hot
sauce and season.
Put the frying pan back over a medium heat. Melt in the butter,
add the garlic and most of the spring onions and cook until soft,
then tip the spinach into the pan.
At the same time turn the heat back up on the pan of water; once
boiling, drop in the gnocchi and cook until the gnocchi just floats.
Use a slotted spoon to add the cooked gnocchi to the frying pan
with the spinach.
Pour in the sweetcorn sauce, toss everything together to warm
through and season to taste. Divide between four bowls, top with
the charred hot sauce corn and remaining spring onions. Serve with
a big green salad on the side. Get in.

name: Corn Dogs
description: American-style corn dawgs. Learn how to make this classic US snack by dipping smoked sausages in a cornmeal batter and deep frying them to perfection.
instructions: Tip the bread flour, sugar, polenta, salt and baking powder into a bowl and whisk together. In a separate bowl, pour in the milk and then crack in the eggs. Mix the wet mixture into the dry mixture until smooth and thick. Pour into a pint glass or tall container.
Cut the hotdogs to size. You want them just shorter than your tall container so they’ll fully submerge in the corn mixture. Insert the lollipop stick into the sausage.
Preheat a pot filled halfway with vegetable oil to 180°C.

Dip a sausage into the corn mixture until thoroughly coated and then carefully lower into the hot oil. Fry for 4-5 mins until a deep golden brown. Remove and drain on kitchen paper. Repeat with the remaining hot dogs.
Serve with ketchup and mustard.

name: Corn Gazpacho with Frozen Feta
description: A silky chilled sweetcorn gazpacho topped with a bright tomato and cucumber salad and clouds of grated frozen feta — a make-ahead summer stunner.
keywords: Corn Gazpacho with Frozen Feta recipe
instructions: At least a day ahead, place the block of feta in the freezer.
When you're ready to make the gazpacho, halve both cucumbers. Peel one half and chop into rough chunks. Slice the kernels off all the corn cobs. Core the peppers and chop into rough chunks.

Add the peeled cucumber and pepper chunks and corn kernels to a blender, the zest of half the lemon, the ice, water, oil, salt and vinegar. Blend until smooth. Taste and season with a squeeze of lemon juice, more salt and a little sugar or honey if needed. Pour into a container and place in the fridge until ready to serve.

When ready to serve, make the salad. Chop the tomatoes and remaining cucumber half into 3cm chunks. Pick the basil leaves, then toss the tomatoes, cucumber and basil together with a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and toss through the balsamic glaze.
Pour the gazpacho between bowls and top with the salad. Grate the frozen feta generously over the top and finish with a sprinkling of chilli flakes.

name: Corn Miso Noodle Soup
description: An easy and very special soup with homemade sweet-savoury corn broth and sautéed garlicky rocket. The perfect way to use up late summer and early autumn sweetcorn.
instructions: Start by making the stock. Using a sharp knife, carefully remove the kernels from the ears of corn. Reserve ⅓ of the kernels for the stock, and save the rest for another recipe.

Slice the onion and head of garlic in half (no need to peel them), and roughly chop the celery stalks. Heat a bit of oil in a large pot over a high heat, then add the onion and garlic, cut side down, and char until crispy and slightly burnt.

Add in the ears of corn, celery stalks, bay leaves, parsley, peppercorns, salt and water. Bring to the boil then reduce to a simmer and cook gently for about 2 hours, until reduced by a few centimetres.

Discard the solids and pour the broth into a blender, then add in the corn kernels and miso paste and blend on high for a few minutes. Strain again, and it’s ready to go! (If you’re making the stock in advance, cool it and store in the fridge. When you’re ready to make the final soup, warm up the corn stock in a pot set over a medium heat for a few minutes.)
To make the soup, cook the noodles in generously salted water following packet instructions, then strain and divide across 4 bowls.

Mince the garlic and thinly slice the spring onion. Heat up a glug of olive oil in a pan set over medium heat, then cook the garlic until fragrant (don’t let it burn). Add in the arugula and cook until wilted. Remove from the heat.
Pour the stock over the noodles, then top with the sautéed arugula, sliced spring onion and a spoonful of crispy chilli oil.

name: Corn Tonnato & Charred Green Bean Salad
description: I'm gonna be honest, tonnato has never been a favourite of mine, blended tuna just doesn't sound amazing. But in this salad it's genuinely really good. Surprisingly refreshing, the corn adds a touch of sweetness and helps mellow out the fishy flavours.
keywords: Corn Tonnato & Charred Green Bean Salad
Corn Tonnato & Charred Green Bean Salad recipe
instructions: Zest half the lemon and set aside.

Now make the tonnato. Drain the tuna and slice the kernels off the corn cob, discarding the cob. Add both to a blender with the kefir, olive oil and the juice of the zested lemon half. Blend until smooth, then taste and season with salt, pepper and more lemon juice, if needed. Set aside.
Trim the green beans, slice the kernels off the remaining corn cobs and thinly slice the chilli. Pick the parsley leaves, thinly slicing any soft stems, then roughly chop the almonds.
Drain the peppers and the remaining tuna, then chop the peppers into 2cm chunks.
Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the corn and almonds and cook for 5-7 mins, until the corn is starting to char and the almonds have toasted. Transfer to a large bowl.

Return the pan to the heat, reduce to a medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Add the green beans and let them sizzle for 1-2 mins, then pour in a splash of water, cover with a lid and leave to steam-fry for 3-4 mins, until tender but still crunchy. Transfer to the bowl of corn.

Reheat the grains, then toss through the corn and green bean mixture along with the capers, peppers, tuna, parsley stems, half the chilli and three quarters of the parsley leaves. Drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil and season with salt, pepper and as much lemon zest as you'd like.
Share the tonnato onto plates and top with the salad, then finish with the remaining chilli and parsley leaves.

name: Corn Tortillas
description: In Mexico we eat corn tortillas almost every day, and there is nothing better than making your own. You'll need a tortilla press and a plastic ziplock bag. Even though they seem difficult to make, once you learn the technique, you will never go back to buying corn tortillas.
instructions: Tip the corn flour into a large bowl and add the warm water. Mix well to form a soft dough.
Separate the dough into 40g balls, then return them all to the bowl. Cover with a clean tea towel.
Cut a plastic sandwich bag in half, so you have two pieces of plastic.

Open the tortilla press and place one piece of plastic on the base. Place a corn dough ball on top (in the centre of the tortilla press) and top it with the second piece of plastic. Close the tortilla press and press slightly. Open it, remove the top piece of plastic and roll the dough back into a ball – this will soften the dough so the tortilla will come out better.
Place the dough ball back into the centre, put the piece of plastic on top and press slightly again. Flip the tortilla over and finish pressing it. The tortilla should be around 1mm thick.
Turn the heat up in the pan to high. Carefully remove the plastic sheets from the tortilla.
Sprinkle your hands with cornflour to make sure the raw corn tortilla doesn’t stick to your hands. Slowly and carefully lay the corn tortilla over the hot pan.

Cook for around 10 seconds, then very carefully flip the tortilla and cook it on the other side for 25 seconds. By now, the tortilla should start to puff. If not, flip it and cook on the other side for another 10 seconds. Once the tortilla starts to puffs, remove it from the heat and cover it with a clean tea towel.
Repeat the process until all the corn tortillas are done.

name: Cornflake Air-Fried Chicken Salad
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A crispy, crunchy cornflake chicken salad with a genius hack to save you time and washing up.
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Lie the corn on the cob on a baking sheet and slide under the grill, turning occasionally until charred, then set aside to cool.

Heat the air-fryer to 200°C. Crush the cornflakes into small pieces and add to a bowl with the mixed seeds before seasoning with salt and pepper. Season the mayo with salt and pepper then brush it onto the chicken before rolling in the cornflakes to completely cover. Line the air-fryer basket with tin foil, and add your chicken. Cook for 10 mins, then flip and cook for another 4 minutes until golden, crispy and cooked through. 
If you don't have an air-fryer, bake at 180°C for 20 mins.
For the dressing, mix mayo and hot sauce until smooth, squeeze in the lime juice and loosen with water if needed. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Back to the corn! Remove the kernels with a sharp knife. Pull the lettuce leaves apart or roughly shred and add to a large mixing bowl. Finely slice the spring onions and celery and add to the bowl along with the charred corn and coriander leaves. Add half of the dressing and toss well, then tip onto a platter and scatter over the feta.

Remove from the chicken the airfryer and slice into pieces before serving with the salad. Drizzle with the remaining dressing, then slice the chives and scatter over the top. Finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Cornflake Chicken Sandwich
description: Breading your chicken in cornflakes is a really good idea. Putting that breaded chicken in a sandwich is an even better idea.
instructions: Cut the cucumber into matchsticks then transfer to a bowl. Zest the lime in a separate small bowl, then squeeze the lime juice over the cucumber, season, toss and set aside to quickly pickle.
Add the mayo and hot sauce to the lime zest. Stir and season to taste. Separate the lettuce leaves.

Tear two sheets of baking parchment. Lay the chicken breasts on one of the sheets, then place the second sheet on top and use a rolling pin or wine bottle to bash the chicken breasts out to an even 2cm thickness. Season the chicken on both sides with the fajita seasoning, salt and pepper.
Spoon the flour into a bowl. Crack the egg into a second bowl and whisk to combine. Add the cornflakes to a third bowl, smashing them into small pieces with clean hands.
Coat each chicken breast first in the flour, then the egg and finely the smashed cornflakes, patting to coat so that the chicken is evenly and well coated. Transfer to a plate.
Put a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cut the ciabatta rolls in half, then toast cut-side down in the pan. Set aside.

Use kitchen paper to remove any crumbs from the pan, then pour in enough vegetable oil to coat the base entirely in 2.5cm of oil. Heat the oil over a medium heat until it is visibly shimmering. Line a plate with kitchen paper.

Once the oil is hot, carefully lower the chicken breasts into the oil. Fry for 4 mins on each side – the chicken burgers should be golden, crisp and juicy on the inside. Transfer to the kitchen paper-lined plate and season with salt.
Spread the hot sauce mayo across the base of the toasted ciabatta rolls. Top with the lettuce, crunchy chicken and a pile of pickled cucumbers. Sandwich together to serve.

name: Cornflake Prawn Toast
description: You've had prawn toast. You've had cornflakes. But have you ever had cornflake prawn toast? Didn't think so.
instructions: Grate your ginger. Chop the white of your spring onion - save the greens for another time. Chop the chives.
Put half of your prawns into a blender along with your ginger, spring onion, shaoxing, soy and sesame oil. Blitz until smooth. Roughly chop the remainder of your prawns.

Carefully separate the egg white from the yolk (you can use the yolk to make mayonnaise, dressings or as the base for Carbonara). Tip all of these ingredients into a bowl and add the cornflour, egg white, salt and white pepper.
Cut discs out of your bread with a circular cutter.
Spoon a thick layer of the prawn mixture onto your bread circles and smooth them out with a knife.
Lightly crush your cornflakes and spread them out on a tray. Tip your prawn toast into the cornflakes to coat the top with it.
Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a high sided frying pan. Heat your oil to 180°C, and carefully add your prawn toasts cornflake side down. Fry for 3 mins, or until golden.
Leave your prawn toast to drain on the side on a plate lined with kitchen paper to take away the excess oil. Serve and enjoy!

name: Coronation Chicken & Jewelled Crispy Rice
description: Classic coronation chicken energy, but turned up. Crispy korma-spiced rice, sticky mango-glazed chicken and a creamy coconut sauce with pops of sweetness and crunch.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Line a baking tray with baking parchment.

Tip the rice onto the tray and toss with the korma paste and a drizzle of olive oil. Spread it out evenly, slide into the oven and bake for 30-35 mins, giving it a toss halfway, until golden and properly crispy.
Meanwhile, season the chicken breasts all over with salt and pepper. In a small bowl, stir the ginger garlic paste with the mango chutney and a splash of water to loosen it. Set aside.

Place a frying pan with high sides over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 6-10 mins, turning, until golden on both sides and cooked through. Pour the mango chutney mixture into the pan and baste the chicken until sticky and glazed. Transfer the chicken to a plate, cover with foil and set aside.

Return the empty pan to a medium heat with another drizzle of olive oil. Add the tomato purée and cook for 1-2 mins until darkened, then tip in the remaining korma paste, chicken stock and coconut milk. Bring to the boil and let it bubble for 5 mins. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Thinly slice the cabbage and stir it through the hot sauce to soften slightly.
Slice the chicken and toss the raisins through the crispy rice.
Spoon the cabbage and korma sauce into bowls. Top with the chicken and any glaze from the plate. Finish with a scattering of flaked almonds and a handful of crispy rice. Serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Coronation Chicken Jacket Potato
description: A curried spin on the classic jacket potato. Super simple steps to create incredible spuds.
instructions: Heat the oven to 230°C. Put the whole potatoes into a large saucepan filled with cold water. Bring to the boil over a high heat and cook for 10 mins.

Drain the potatoes, pat dry and set each one on a square of foil. Add a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt on top and wrap them up well. Transfer to a baking tray and roast in the oven for 40 mins. Alternatively, lightly coat your potatoes in olive oil and salt, wrap in foil and air fry at 200C for 40 mins).
Meanwhile, get started on the coronation chicken filling. Dice the chicken into chunks and transfer to a large bowl. Add the curry powder, garlic powder and yoghurt. Mix well.
Set a frying pan over a medium-high heat, add the chicken and cook for 5-7 mins. Alternatively, grill the chicken instead at 180°C for 15 mins total, 7 mins each side.
Dice the red onion and tear the coriander, then transfer to a large bowl with the mayonnaise and mango chutney. Add the cooked chicken, season to taste with salt and pepper and mix well.

Once the jacket potatoes are done, split them open, fill with a little butter and a light dusting of curry powder, then top with the coronation filling. Finish with a sprinkle of grated cheese on top, then air-fry or grill the tops at 200°C for 5 mins to get a melty finish.
Serve with salad, crisps and dip on the side.

name: Coronation Chicken Schnitzel Sandwich
description: A crunchy, crispy and golden chicken schnitzel sandwich dressed in a coronation curry mayo.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the red onion, then get it into a bowl. Add a good pinch of salt and the juice of the lime, then give it a little massage. Let it sit and pickle.
Cut each chicken breast down the middle depthways, so that you have two flatter fillets. Sandwich the chicken breasts between two bits of cling film, then bash them to flatten to about 3mm thickness.
Tip the flour into a bowl along with the curry powder and 1 tsp salt. Crack the eggs into another bowl and beat to break them down. Add the panko breadcrumbs to another bowl.
Dip your chicken breasts one at a time into the flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs so that they are totally coated. Pop them in the fridge until you are ready to eat.

For the curry mayo, peel and finely chop the garlic, then heat a small frying pan over a medium heat. Add a splash of vegetable oil, then add the garlic and tomato purée to the pan. Cook for 1 min, then tip in the curry powder and sizzle for 30 seconds. Remove the pan from the heat and allow it to cool a little.
Put the mayonnaise, yoghurt and mango chutney into a bowl, then pour the warm spice mix into it. Mix until well combined, then season with salt.
Peel and julienne the apple and add to the pickled onions. Finely shred the lettuce.
Toast the burger buns cut-side down in a large frying pan for a couple of minutes, until golden. Set aside.

Add a good glug of vegetable oil to the same large frying pan and bring it up to temperature over a medium heat. Carefully get your chicken breasts into the pan two at a time, and fry for about 3 mins on each side, until they are crisp and golden.

Spoon the mayo onto either side of the burger buns, then pop some lettuce on the base. Place your chicken fillets on top, then get the julienned apple and pickled onions on there. Pop the bun lid on top and serve.

name: Coronation Chickpea Sandwich Filler
description: A delicious veggie spin on a classic, packed with all the creamy, sweet ‘n’ spicy flavour you want with added crunch from Bombay mix. It's messy, but worth it.
instructions: Peel and grate the garlic. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Take off the heat and stir through the curry powder.
Finely chop the dried apricots and coriander. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

Add the Greek yoghurt, mayonnaise, mango chutney, chickpeas, flaked almonds, apricots, coriander, and the garlic curry mix to a large bowl. Zest and juice the lemon into the bowl and mix. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Serve however you fancy. We love this filler sandwiched between with thick slices of sourdough with crisp romaine, a handful of Bombay mix and a scattering of nigella seeds.

If you're making ahead, pop the filling into the fridge in Tupperware (it will keep for up to 3 days).

name: Coronation Prawn Toast
description: Mam Sham are here to rock your world with the juiciest coronation prawn toast recipe. Be ready for an absolute banger.
instructions: First things first, cook your prawns. Heat up a tablespoon of oil in a wide pan on a medium-high heat. When the pan's hot, add half of your curry powder and cook for a few seconds. Next, you're going to want to add your prawns to the pan with some salt and pepper and fry for a couple of minutes; when the prawns have changed colour and cooked through, take them off the heat.

Now it’s time to get started on the mayo. Place your egg yolks in a large bowl and whisk them to combine (you can freeze the whites for meringue). Add the mustard and continue to whisk before very slowly drizzling in the oil. It will take about 3 minutes of continuous whisking and drizzling before you get a nice thick silky consistency.

Add the rest of your curry powder to your mayonnaise along with with a pinch of salt and pepper. Whisk in the juice of a lime and your mango chutney. Add more or less of these flavourings to your taste. Finally, mix in the sultanas and add your prawns.

It’s nearly time to assemble, so get your bread in the toaster and chop up your celery into thin (but not too thin) chunks. Spoon your prawn mixture on to the toast, sprinkle the celery chunks plus some of the leaves over the top, add an extra crack of black pepper, then the pièce de résistance: a handful of crushed prawn crackers.
Feel free to add an extra squeeze of lime. Bone app the teeth.

name: Cottage Cheese Chicken Caesar
description: Everyone’s favourite salad made healthy. The cottage cheese dressing drops the calories substantially while upping the protein. It’s also incredibly delicious.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan.
Toss the Tenderstem broccoli in a glug of olive oil and season with salt. Lay it out evenly on a metal baking tray and roast for 15 mins until slightly charred. Remove and set aside.

Place the chicken thighs skin-side down on a chopping board. Run a knife along each side of the bone to expose the bone. Using scissors, cut underneath the bone to remove it. Repeat with the remaining chicken thighs.

Season the chicken thighs with salt on both sides and place them skin side down in a cold, non-stick frying pan. Place over a medium heat and cook for 6-8 mins until the skin is a deep golden brown and the thighs are almost cooked through. Flip the chicken over and cook for another 2 mins. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Tear the sourdough into bite-sized pieces and add to the pan you browned the chicken in. Toss the croutons around in the pan to absorb all the fat then transfer to a baking tray and slide into the oven to cook for 10 mins, until golden and crispy.
Make the dressing. Add all the dressing ingredients except the lemon to a blender and blitz until smooth. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Divide the romaine lettuce into individual leaves.

Dress the salad. Add the lettuce, Tenderstem, croutons and dressing to a large bowl and mix well until evenly coated. Pop everything on a large platter and top with the chicken and basil leaves. Finish with lashings of Parmesan and black pepper. Serve with any leftover lemon cut into wedges.

name: Cottage Cheese Pesto Pasta Salad
description: A quick and easy high-protein pasta salad you can make in under half an hour. Fresh, flavour, and a healthy twist on pesto pasta. Ensure to use a high speed blender to get the ultimate smooth sauce!
keywords: Cottage Cheese Pesto Pasta Salad recipe
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the fusilli and cook according to the packet instructions, until al dente. Drain, saving a cup of pasta water. Then rinse the pasta under cold running water until completely cool and shake off any excess water.

Whilst the pasta is cooling, add the cottage cheese and all the basil leaves to a blender with water. Grate in most of the Parmesan, saving some for finishing later. Blitz until smooth and bright green. Add a splash of water to loosen it if needed.
Halve the cherry tomatoes. Then wilt spinach by dropping into a colander and covering with boiling water.

Put the pasta into a large bowl and add the sauce, tossing everything together along with the cherry tomatoes and wilted spinach. Add a splash of the reserved pasta water to help it all come together if needed.
Divide between two bowls and finish with the remaining Parmesan and a crack of black pepper.

name: Cottage Cheese Tzatziki with Sausages
description: Super quick and easy- we’re making a high-protein tzatziki by using cottage cheese. It all happens in 20 mins. Super quick, extremely easy, incredibly eatable.
keywords: Cottage Cheese Tzatziki with Sausages recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Coarsely grate the cucumber into a bowl, season with salt, set aside.
Add the cottage cheese into a bowl, season with salt and finely grate the garlic in.
Place the sausages onto a tray with a drizzle of olive oil, roast until fully cooked, 15-20 mins.

Meanwhile, squeeze as much liquid from the cucumbers as possible, then, stir into the cottage cheese. Zest half the lemon into the mixture, taste and season with salt, lemon juice and pepper, if needed.

Drain and thinly slice the peppers.Trim and thinly slice the onion, place into a strainer and wash under cold running water until crisp. Pick the mint leaves. Add all of the onion, peppers, and mint to a bowl with the balsamic vinegar and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss and set aside.
Share the tzatziki cottage cheese between plates, top with the sausages, and serve with the salad.

name: Cottage Pie
description: Cottage pie is a classic British recipe. A family favourite. We've tweaked it a bit to enhance the flavours and ensure the elite cottage pie experience.
instructions: Preheat a large casserole or cast iron pot over a high heat. Add a splash of olive oil and brown off your beef mince in batches. Don’t add any salt yet! Once the beef is browned off, move to a plate or tray and repeat with the remaining mince.

While your beef is browning, chunk up the carrots, onion and celery and chuck them into a food processor. Blitz into a coarse paste. You can finely chop the lot if you don’t have a processor or you fancy the practice, this is just an easy time saver!

Add the veggies to the pan with the beef drippings (you can add an extra splash of oil here if you need it) and a big whack of salt and black pepper. Chuck in the rosemary sprigs whole and cook over a medium heat for 10-12 mins. Add the beef back to the pan, along with the tomato purée, Worcestershire sauce and mustard and cook for a further 5 mins.
Now crank up the heat to high and deglaze with the red wine. Reduce by half and add the beef stock. Lower the heat to a simmer and leave the sauce to bubble away for 40 mins.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Meanwhile, peel your potatoes and cut into even 5-6cm chunks. Boil in well seasoned water until very tender. This will take between 10-12 mins. Drain and allow to steam for 5 mins.
Mash until smooth with the butter and milk. Season with salt and add the grated cheddar.

Taste your ragù and season with more Worcestershire sauce, salt and black pepper (we like it very peppery!). Now roughly chop your chard, stems and all, and get it into the sauce. Pour into a baking dish and top with your mash.
Bake for 35-45 mins until golden brown and bubbling. Serve with steamy seasonal greens, peas, broccoli – whatever you fancy!

name: Courgette & Lemon Cake Recipe
description: A delightful fusion of moist courgette and zesty lemon, perfect for any occasion. It can also be adapted to be dairy free by using plant milk and butter alternative.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Grease 2 x 20cm springform cake tins with a little butter, then line the bases with baking parchment.
Coarsely grate the courgette using a box grater (no need to peel). Put the courgette into a clean tea towel and squeeze out any excess water. Zest the lemons.
Put the butter, sugar, flour and baking powder into a large bowl or the base of a hand mixer. Crack in the eggs, add the lemon zest, then whisk with an electric whisk to form a smooth cake batter.

Tip in the grated courgette and fold through the cake batter using a spatula. Divide the cake batter equally between your lined tins. Bake on the middle shelf for 20-25 mins until a skewer inserted into the centre of each cake comes out clean.
Leave the cakes to cool in their tins for 10 mins, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Once the cakes are completely cooled, make the lemon icing. Sift the icing sugar into a bowl, add the juice of one of the zested lemons and stir to form a drizzlable icing.

To assemble the cakes, put one onto a large plate and spread with the lemon curd. Sandwich together with the second cake, then spoon over the lemon icing. Don’t worry if it drips down the side – this looks cute. Leave the icing to harden, then cut the cake into slices, to serve.

name: Courgette & Red Pepper Rice Salad
description: We've upgraded your favourite greens by charring them and topping them with a pepper-infused, tomato sauce and crumbled feta.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Dice the onions, finely grate the garlic, quarter the tomatoes and chunk up the red peppers.

Chop half the courgettes into thick rounds and trim the bottom 3cm from the asparagus. Toss the veggies with oil, salt and pepper, spread out on a roasting tray and slide into the oven for 25-30 mins, until cooked and lightly charred. Thinly slice the remaining courgette and toss through the roasted veggies.

Set a medium saucepan over a medium heat and add 4 tbsp of olive oil. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and sweat for 5 mins. Add the garlic, cook for 2 mins, then add the ras el hanout and cook for another 5 mins. Tip in the tomatoes and half of the peppers and a splash of the pepper liquid. Cook for 10 mins, season to taste and lightly blitz with a hand blender.

Heat the rice according to the package instructions. Toss the rice with roasted veggies, raw courgette, and the remaining peppers. Tip onto a platter or onto plates, drizzle with the sauce and crumble over the feta. Finish with the basil leaves and serve with the lemon wedges.

name: Courgette Baba Ganoush
description: A baba ganoush-inspired dip made from chargrilled courgettes instead of aubergine. It's the perfect summer dip recipe.
instructions: Set the grill to high or use a very hot BBQ. Grill or BBQ the courgettes whole until blackened on all sides. This will take at least 15-20 mins if using a grill (less on a BBQ).
Meanwhile, roughly chop the fresh herbs and set aside. Crush the garlic to a paste and set aside.

Carefully remove the courgettes from the heat source and place on a chopping board to cool slightly. Slit the courgettes open lengthways to speed this up. When cool enough to handle, finely chop the courgettes (including the burnt skin) and scoop into a mixing bowl. Drain some of the liquid as it appears in the bowl if you like, or set the chopped courgettes over a sieve in a bowl for 10 mins. Alternatively, leave the liquid in for a looser texture.
Add the crushed garlic to the courgette bowl along with the tahini, cumin, lemon juice and zest and olive oil. Mix thoroughly, beating until creamy. Season with salt.
Spread the courgette mix out on a serving plate and dress with chilli flakes, sumac, a drizzle of olive oil, and the chopped herbs. Serve with flatbread, pitta or toasted bread on the side.

name: Courgette Butter Bean Pasta Salad
description: A high-fibre, high-flavour pasta salad that's packed with veggies. The toasted pumpkin seed sprinkle is elite.
keywords: Courgette Butter Bean Pasta Salad recipe
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the orecchiette or your chosen pasta according to the package instructions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to cool it down quickly. Set aside.
Tip the pumpkin seeds into a small frying pan over a medium high heat, toast for 2-3 mins, tossing regularly, until they start to pop. Tip onto a plate to cool a little.
Slice the courgettes into thin rounds or half-moons. No need to cook them, they’re delicious raw! Pit and halve the green olives, if not already pitted. Rinse and drain the butter beans.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl or jug, whisk together the pesto, olive oil, and the juice of the lemon. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, add the cooked pasta, raw courgettes, green olives, butter beans, and toasted pumpkin seeds. Shave the Parmesan and add to the bowl along with the mint leaves.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss everything together until well combined.
Serve the pasta salad in bowls or meal-prep boxes with the remaining toasted pumpkin seeds and Parmesan cheese grated over the top.

name: Courgette Butter Bean Pasta Salad
description: Lunches don't come better than a pesto pasta salad, and this one's jam-packed with veggies and beans. The toasted pumpkin seed sprinkle is elite.
keywords: Courgette Butter Bean Pasta Salad recipe
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the orecchiette or your chosen pasta according to the package instructions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to cool it down quickly. Set aside.
Tip the pumpkin seeds into a small frying pan over a medium high heat, toast for 2-3 mins, tossing regularly, until they start to pop. Tip onto a plate to cool a little.
Slice the courgettes into thin rounds or half-moons. No need to cook them, they’re delicious raw! Pit and halve the green olives, if not already pitted. Rinse and drain the butter beans.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl or jug, whisk together the pesto, olive oil, and the juice of the lemon. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, add the cooked pasta, raw courgettes, green olives, butter beans, and toasted pumpkin seeds. Shave the Parmesan and add to the bowl along with the mint leaves.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss everything together until well combined.

Divide the pasta salad between your Tupperware containers with the remaining toasted pumpkin seeds and Parmesan cheese grated over the top.
Once at room temp, box up and pop in the fridge ready to grab for lunch - they'll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Courgette Butter Beans with Green Olive Salsa
description: These creamy butter beans are basically summer comfort food in a bowl. Leave out the Parmesan if you want to make them vegan.
keywords: Courgette Butter Beans With Green Olive Salsa
instructions: Finely slice the courgettes. Add 2 tbsp of olive oil to a pan over a medium high heat. Add the courgettes with a big pinch of salt. Cook for 10 mins, until golden and soft. Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic.

Make the green olive salsa by finely chopping the green olives and tipping into a bowl. Add the dried oregano and juice of the lemon. Finely chop the parsley leaves and add to the bowl, season well. Drizzle with a tbsp of olive oil and set aside.

Add the sliced garlic and fennel seeds to the pan with the courgettes and cook for 2 mins further, then tip in the cans of butter beans along with the water from the cans. Add the veggie stock cube and turn the heat up to bring to a boil. Cook for around 5 mins, until thickened, squishing some of the butter beans against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce a little. Finely grate the Parmesan into the pan, then add the lemon juice. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Spoon into bowls, then top with the olive salsa and reserved parsley.

name: Courgette Chips
description: Ben's Dad ran an Italian in Oxford called Cibo. They did the best courgette chips - Perfectly crispy batter, with lovely soft courgette within. Here you go.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
To make your garlic aioli dip, start by wrapping your garlic up in foil and placing it into the oven for 35 minutes. Meanwhile, add your mayo to a small bowl.

Once the garlic is roasted, squeeze out the garlic using the back of a teaspoon so you are left with the roasted garlic cloves. Run a knife over the top to get rid of any lumps and add this to your mayo. Add a sprinkle of salt and pepper and mix well.

For your chipotle dip, pour your yoghurt into a bowl, add a sprinkle of salt and a grinding of pepper over the top. Thinly chop up your mint adding three quarters of it to the yoghurt. Mix together. Add your chipotle paste to the top and skim your teaspoon over the top to get a swirly effect.

Chip time. Take a frying pan and heat your vegetable oil, until it is bubbling. While it’s heating up, into a bowl, add your flour and soda water and mix together thoroughly until it is a nice smooth batter.

Take your courgettes and chop them up into small rectangles. Take each piece and coat it in the flour and soda water mixture. Once the oil is ready, add your coated courgettes to the pan and fry until golden brown.
Once the courgette chips are ready, take them out of the pan and serve with the remaining chopped mint and a sprinkling of salt. Dip the chips into those tasty dips and enjoy.

name: Courgette Frittata
description: A clean, fresh frittata. The basil, lemon and ricotta keep it really light. Lovely little lunch.
instructions: Preheat the oven 180°C. Start by cracking your eggs into a bowl. Next, grate in the parmesan and add a good grinding of pepper. Zest the lemon into the egg mix then roughly tear the basil into the bowl, whisk together.

Thinly slice up the courgettes and onion, using a mandolin. (If you don't have a mandolin, use a nice sharp knife. If you can, use a deep frying pan measuring approx 25cm - you'll use this for the frittata later on). Heat half of the oil in the pan over a medium to high heat, adding half the courgettes and onion mix. Season with salt and fry until the courgettes are nicely charred. Repeat with the rest of the oil and courgettes and onion mix.

Once the onion and courgette mix is lovely and golden, add the egg into the pan, turning the heat to medium. Pop the ricotta in dollops over the top of the top of the frittata. Leave it over the heat for a few minutes, until the sides are beginning to cook. Then place the frittata into the oven for 10 minutes.

After 10 minutes, check the top of the frittata is firm with a slight jiggle. Pop it back in the oven if it needs longer, checking every 2 minutes. Once done, remove from the oven and flip onto a board and flip back onto a plate. Garnish with the remaining parmesan, an extra dollop of ricotta and basil leaves. Tuck in!

name: Courgette Fritti
description: Fritti is just what you want to be eating when the sun is shining. These gorge courgette fritti go great with our homemade honey and feta dip.
instructions: Add the feta to a food processor and blend until smooth. Add the extra virgin olive oil, 1-2 tbsp of water, the juice of half a lemon and some salt and blitz again. In a small pan, combine the honey with the oregano and aleppo. Warm to infuse and set aside.
Fill a large pot just under halfway with vegetable oil and set over a medium heat, bring to 180°C.
Cut the courgettes into batons.
Whisk together the rice and plain flours along with the baking powder and caster sugar. Gradually whisk in the sparkling water until you have a loose batter, the texture of double cream.
Lightly dust the courgettes with rice flour, dunk briefly in the batter and carefully lower into the oil.
Lightly dust the courgettes with rice flour, dunk briefly in the batter and carefully lower into the oil.
Tip the feta dip into a bowl and drizzle with the infused honey.
Serve the hot, crispy courgettes with lemon wedges and the feta honey dip.

name: Courgette Parmigiana
description: An authentic parmigiana di zucchine recipe from the legend Gennaro Contaldo. This is the only Courgette Parmigiana recipe you’ll ever need.
instructions: First, make the tomato sauce. Finely chop the garlic. Heat olive oil in a pan over a medium heat and sweat the garlic for a minute or so. Add in the tinned tomatoes with about half a can of water. Roughly tear in your basil and some salt to taste. Lower the heat, cover with a lid and cook for about 25 mins.
Preheat the oven to 180°C/354°F.

Whilst the tomato sauce is cooking, slice the courgettes lengthways into 1cm slices. Lightly beat the eggs in salt and pepper. Dust the slices in flour and dip into the beaten egg. Heat 300ml of your Napolina Olive Oil in a large pan. Once hot, add the courgette slices and fry for a couple of mins on each side until golden. Remove and drain on kitchen paper.

Line an ovenproof dish with a little of the tomato sauce, then place a layer of courgette slices on top, followed by another layer of tomato sauce. Sprinkle over grated parmesan, roughly torn pieces of mozzarella and scatter over the basil leaves. Continue layering until you have used up all the ingredients, finishing with parmesan and mozzarella.
Cover with foil and bake in the oven for 20 mins. Remove the foil and continue to bake for another 10 mins.
Remove from the oven and leave to rest for about 15 mins to cool. Serve and enjoy.

name: Courgette Tart with Pesto, Ricotta & Black Olives
description: An easy courgette tart that's perfect for rustling up on a weeknight. The whole family will love this recipe.
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C. Pit and roughly chop the olives. Thinly slice the courgettes and set aside in a bowl.

Place the puff pastry sheet on a lined baking tray and score all around the edge, 2cm from the border. Beat the egg in a small bowl. Use a pastry brush to brush some of the egg over the scored border of the tart.
Mix the ricotta with the remaining beaten egg and the pesto. Season well with salt and pepper.
Add two-thirds of the olive oil to the courgette bowl and season well with salt and pepper.

Evenly spread the ricotta mix within the border of the tart base and arrange the sliced courgettes evenly on top. Add the olives and season again with plenty of black pepper and the remaining third of olive oil.
Bake in the oven for 30 mins until the pastry is nice and crisp and faintly golden-brown. Remove from the oven and cool on a wire rack for 5 mins before slicing.

name: Courgette and Cavolo Nero Soup with Cheesy Garlic Bread Croutons
description: This delicious green soup is topped with cheesy crunchy garlic bread croutons for an easy autumn dinner.
cuisine: Italian, Northern Italian, Italian-Inspired, Mediterranean, Mediterranean-Inspired
instructions: Add 3 tbsp of olive oil to a large pan and place over a medium heat. Dice the onion and fry gently for a few minutes along with the bay leaves.
Add the courgette and a good pinch of salt, cook for another few minutes.
Roughly chop and add the cavolo nero or kale and cook for about 5 mins until softened.
Dice the potato and add to the pan along with the chilli flakes (if using). Then add the stock and 3 of the peeled whole garlic cloves.
Stir well and bring to a simmer, cook until the potatoes are completely soft (about 20 mins).
While the soup cooks, make the croutons. Tear up the ciabatta into roughly 1 inch cubes.
Put the softened butter into a bowl (you can microwave it for a few seconds) then mince the remaining garlic and finely chop the parsley, add both to the butter with a pinch of salt and mix.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat, add the butter and then the bread. Fry well, tossing until golden brown and crunchy. Tip onto a plate and grate over the parmesan which will melt a little bit.
When the soup is ready, blitz with a stick blender until smooth. Then season with salt and lemon juice to taste. Finely chop the tarragon, add and stir.
Add the soup to bowls and top with the cheesy garlic bread croutons.

name: Courgette, Chickpea & Feta Fritters
description: Tangy courgette fritters that we've bound together with chickpeas and feta. These are the greatest snack on the planet.
instructions: Coarsely grate the courgette. Roughly crumble the feta. Roughly chop the coriander.

Drain the chickpeas if using canned, then roughly mash or blend to a very coarse paste, leaving plenty whole or partially crushed. Transfer to a bowl, then stir through the turmeric, yoghurt, courgette, eggs, feta and three-quarters of the coriander. Season with salt and pepper. Combine the flour and baking powder, then add to the bowl and gently fold through to make a batter.

Pour enough oil into a large frying pan to create a thin film, then set over a high heat. Working in batches, add heaped tablespoonfuls of batter to the pan and fry for about 2-3 mins until the bottom has firmed enough to flip over. Fry on the other side for 2 mins. When cooked, put on a warm plate covered with a cloth.
Serve drizzled with yoghurt and topped with the remaining coriander. Finish with hot sauce or chilli, if you like.

name: Courgette, Green Bean & Pepper Salad With Lemon Vinaigrette
description: Lots of fresh spring goodness going on here, courgettes, green beans, butter beans and plenty of herbs, all brought together by a preserved lemon vinaigrette that we're particularly happy with. And a little peppery salsa to go on top for good measure.
keywords: Green Bean & Pepper Salad With Lemon Vinaigrette
instructions: Place a frying pan over a high heat, add the green beans and cook for about 3 mins until they have some charred edges. Remove and add to a large bowl.
Finely chop the courgettes and add to the bowl along with the butter beans.

Finely chop the preserved lemon and add to a small bowl. Mix with the the juice of a lemon and equal parts of the olive oil, dijon, honey, thyme, and a pinch of salt. Pour over the beans and mix well.
Roughly chop the peppers and parsley and mix together in a bowl with the sherry vinegar and a splash of olive oil.
Plate up the beans and spoon over the peppers.

name: Courgette, Peach & Halloumi Skewers Recipe
description: Nothing screams summer barbecue like a halloumi skewer or a vegetarian kebab. These salty cubes of cheese are glazed in sweet chilli jam for a spicy sweet kick and served on top of a herby olive rice salad. Get ahead with your dinner party prep by assembling the skewers before you’re ready to eat so that it is a speedy cook job when it comes to eating. There’s not a better sunshine snack about.
instructions: If using wooden skewers, soak for 30 mins in cold water before using.
Peel and halve the onion, then cut three quarters of it into skewerable-sized chunks. Very thinly slice the remaining quarter and scrape this into a salad bowl.
