Zest the lemon on top of the red onion, then squeeze in half the juice, along with a big pinch of salt. Use your hands to scrunch the sliced red onion into the lemon juice - set aside to quick pickle (and make your rice salad dressing).
Squeeze the remaining lemon juice into a large bowl, stir in the chilli jam and half of the olive oil along with a good pinch of salt and pepper.

Halve the peach or nectarine and remove the stone, pat dry the halloumi. Cut both and the courgette into similar-sized chunks (you want between 8-12 chunks to have an even balance of ingredients per skewer!) to your red onion.

Scrape everything into the chilli jam bowl, and toss to coat. Then, alternating each ingredient, thread onto your skewers. You should get four skewers in total. Set aside, leaving any chilli jam marinade in the bowl for later.
Pick the leaves off the herbs, then roughly chop any bigger leaves and all the stalks. Add to the bowl with the finely sliced onion.

Finely slice the olives and add these too, along with the remaining olive oil. Heat the rice, add this in too, tossing well to combine, then season the rice salad to taste. You can add in the leftover chilli jam marinade here for a sweet kick, if you like.

Heat a BBQ or griddle pan to a high heat. Once visibly hot, lay in the skewers and cook for 5 mins, turning regularly until the onion and courgette have softened, the halloumi is crisp and the peach jammy.
Serve the skewers on top of the rice salad for a banging summer meal!

name: Cowboy Caviar Salad
description: This salad/dip hybrid packs in 10 plants towards your 30 plants per week gut health goal. It takes minutes to make and tastes absolutely delicious.
instructions: Combine the olive oil, red wine vinegar, juice of the lime and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.
Drain your beans and sweetcorn and add to the dressing.
Finely dice the tomatoes, pepper, red onion, avocado, jalapeños and coriander and add to the bowl with the dressing and beans.
Stir everything and check the seasoning, adjusting to your taste.
Enjoy as a dip with your favourite tortilla chips.

name: Crab & Cherry Tomato Tagliatelle Pasta
description: This crab & cherry tomato tagliatelle pasta recipe combines the natural sweetness of cherry tomatoes and crab to create a delightful and celebratory dish. This simple yet elegant tagliatelle pasta recipe is a wonderful choice for those who appreciate the nuances of Italian cuisine. The pairing of crab and cherry tomatoes enhances the delicate flavours of the tagliatelle, resulting in a harmonious balance of tastes. Ideal for both casual dinners and special occasions, this recipe showcases the versatility of tagliatelle pasta. Incorporate fresh garlic, basil, and a drizzle of olive oil to elevate the dish further, adding layers of complexity. For an authentic Italian experience, serve this tagliatelle pasta recipe with a side of crusty bread and a light salad. The simplicity of the ingredients and the ease of preparation make this dish a favourite among pasta enthusiasts and a standout in any collection of Italian pasta recipes.
keywords: Crab & Cherry Tomato Tagliatelle Pasta Recipe
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Finely slice the garlic and chilli, then quarter the cherry tomatoes. Finely chop the parsley (stalks and all).
Drop the tagliatelle into the boiling water and cook for 1 min less than pack instructions.

Meanwhile, heat a glug of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli then cook, stirring, for 1-2 mins until both are soft. Turn the heat up to medium-high, add the cherry tomatoes and pour in the white wine.

Simmer for a couple of minutes until the wine has reduced by half, then turn off the heat under the pan and stir through the crab. Once the tagliatelle is cooked, transfer the pasta directly into the sauce using tongs. Add a splash of the pasta cooking water to create a luscious sauce.
Stir through most of the parsley, zest in the lemon, then season to taste with salt, lots of black pepper and lemon juice.
Divide between two bowls, drizzle with a little extra olive oil and scatter over the remaining parsley. Yum.

name: Crab and Iced Fennel Linguine
description: The ultimate crab pasta. Using the brown crab meat and white wine to form the base of the sauce: out of this world. Iced fennel takes it to the next level.
instructions: Begin with the fennel. Chop off the fronds so that you are left with just the bulb. Then, slice the bulb into wafer thin slices, almost like shavings. Fill a large bowl with ice and water, then place your sliced fennel into the bowl for 20 minutes.

Finely chop the parsley, including the stalks. Slice the garlic cloves into thin discs and chop the red chillies as finely as possible (with the seeds). Remove the anchovies from the jar, saving the oil for later. Finely slice, then set these ingredients aside.

Into a large frying pan place the chopped garlic, parsley stalks, anchovies, the oil from the anchovies and a large glug of olive oil. Just before the garlic starts to go brown, add in the white wine, mix well.
Meanwhile, get the linguine on. Remember to save a cup of the pasta water for later.

Back to the sauce. After the mixture has been bubbling for five minutes, stir in the brown crab meat. Combine thoroughly, so that the crab disintegrates into a brown liquid. Add the pasta water and stir.
Once the linguine is cooked, pour into the pan, tossing so that the pasta is completely coated. Then add the white crab meat, the chopped red chilli and the remaining parsley, stirring well.
Over the top of the pasta mixture squeeze in the juice of half a lemon, before sprinkling in a large pinch of salt and pepper. One last stir and the pasta is ready to plate up.
Strain the fennel, setting aside. Spoon the pasta mixture into a serving bowl. Top with a handful of iced fennel, another sprinkle of salt and pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Then - tuck in!

name: Crackers Con Tomate
description: You know pan con tomate? Well, this is cracker con tomate! It’s so easy, so quick, and the perfect little snack. You can't get a quicker snack than this.
instructions: Grate the tomatoes into a bowl on the largest grating then season generously with salt. Give it a mix then pour into a fine sieve set over the bowl to catch any juices. Leave to sit for 5 mins. Pour off any juices into a glass (drink this with some ice in… it’s so good).
Finely chop the parsley. then add the grated tomatoes back into the bowl with extra virgin olive oil, a squeeze of lemon, parsley, and freshly ground black pepper. Stir and taste for seasoning.
Serve up in a bowl and scoop with crackers, enjoy!

name: Cranberry Chilli Jam
description: Sweet, spicy, and extremely nice. This cranberry chilli jam will add an extra bit of oomph to your Christmas dinner.
instructions: Chuck the cranberries, chillies (deseed the scotch bonnet if you want to) and ginger into a food processor or blender. Pulse until coarsely chopped and tip into a large saucepan.
Add the sugar and vinegar with a pinch of salt and set over a medium heat. Stir in the cinnamon stick and bring to a simmer. Cook over a low-medium heat, stirring regularly for 20-25 mins.

As the jam cooks, the bubbles will change from loose and liquidy to thicker and less regular. You can control how thick your jam will be by how long you cook it for at this stage. The longer you cook it, the thicker it will be! If you have a thermometer, you’re shooting for 104°C as a minimum. You can also check the texture of your jam by freezing a plate and adding a blob of jam to the frozen plate. This will cool the jam down rapidly and you can check the texture once set.

When you’re happy with your jam, fish out the cinnamon stick and store the jam in sterilised jars or Tupperware in the fridge. Your jam will keep in a sterilised jar for three months and for two weeks in a Tupperware in the fridge.

name: Cranberry Gimlet
description: A cranberry gimlet cocktail made using the leftover syrup from our cranberry sauce. For a non-alcoholic version, skip the gin and top it up with fizzy water for a long cranberry cooler.
instructions: In a cocktail shaker, add the gin, lemon juice, a few fresh cranberries and the cranberry sauce syrup.
Add the ice and shake well for around 20 seconds until the shake feels extremely chilled.
Strain into a small chilled cocktail tumbler or coupe.
Garnish with a couple of fresh cranberries.

name: Cranberry Sauce
description: The best ever cranberry sauce for your Christmas dinner table (and boxing day sandwiches). Use fresh or frozen cranberries, then save the leftover syrup to make our cranberry gimlet.
instructions: Remove the zest from the lemon in thin strips with no pith.
In a medium saucepan, combine the cranberries, sugar, water, lemon zest and a big pinch of salt.

Bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium heat. Once it reaches a boil, reduce the heat and let it simmer for around 3 mins, stirring occasionally until the cranberries start to pop and soften, some slumping in the mixture and some retaining their shape. Taste and add more sugar if you prefer it sweeter.
Remove from heat and let the sauce cool to room temperature; it will thicken as it cools.
Drain off 100ml of the liquid, or as much as needed to reach your desired consistency. Reserve the liquid to make my gimlet.
Transfer the cranberry sauce to an airtight container. It will last perfectly well for up to a week in the fridge.

name: Cream Cheese & Sun-Dried Tomato Pinwheels
description: Creamy pinwheels layered with sun-dried tomatoes and fresh spinach. Perfect for lunchboxes, picnics or on-the-go snacking.
keywords: Cream cheese and sundried tomato pinwheels
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Tip the cream cheese into a bowl. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon, sprinkle in the garlic granules, and season lightly with salt and black pepper. Mix everything together until smooth.
Drain the sundried tomatoes and finely chop them. Thinly slice the spring onions.
Lay one tortilla on a chopping board and spread over half of the cream cheese mixture. Scatter over half the sundried tomatoes, spring onions and baby spinach in an even layer.
Roll up the tortilla tightly, like a Swiss roll. Repeat with the second tortilla and remaining filling. Slice each roll into bite-sized pinwheels, about 2–3cm thick.
Eat straight away or keep in the fridge for up to 3 days in an airtight container.

name: Cream Cheese Frosting
description: A super quick and easy recipe for cream cheese frosting. It’s tangy, sweet and creamy. Spread it on red velvet cakes, carrot cakes or cinnamon buns.
instructions: Use an electric whisk to beat the butter in a large mixing bowl for 4–5 mins, then add the drained cream cheese and beat for another 2 mins.
Sift in the icing sugar and add the vanilla and beat for another 2 mins, until smooth and evenly incorporated. (Add more icing sugar if you prefer a firmer frosting.)

name: Cream Cheese Pasta with Crispy Chicken Meatballs
description: A lighter take on a classic. This creamy, lemony pasta tossed with golden chicken meatballs and sweet courgette makes for a super simple family dinner.
keywords: Cream Cheese Pasta with Crispy Chicken Meatballs recipe
Cream Cheese Pasta with Crispy Chicken Meatballs
chicken meatballs with cream cheese pasta
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Tip the chicken mince into a mixing bowl. Crack in the egg, add the breadcrumbs and season with salt and black pepper. Mix everything well with your hands, then roll into small, kid-friendly meatballs, about the size of a walnut. Pop them in the fridge for 10 mins to firm up.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, drop in the linguine and cook following pack instructions.
Meanwhile, peel and finely chop the garlic. Dice the courgettes. Finely grate the Parmesan. Zest the lemon and set aside.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a lug of olive oil. Once hot, add the meatballs and fry for 12–15 mins, turning often, until golden all over and cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Place a medium saucepan over a medium-high heat and add another drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the diced courgettes and fry for 3–4 mins until just golden and softening. Stir in the garlic and cook for another minute.
If you’ve got fussy eaters, now’s your moment: scoop the cooked courgettes out and set them aside, leaving the garlicky oil behind.
Add a ladle of pasta water to the garlicky oil and stir through the cream cheese. Mix until smooth and saucy.

Drain the pasta and toss it straight into the sauce. Add another splash of pasta water, then turn off the heat and stir through the grated Parmesan and juice of the half a lemon. Fold in the meatballs, saving a few for smaller plates if needed.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Dish out the pasta, with the reserved courgettes (if using), some more Parmesan and the chicken meatballs on the side.
Parents Plate: Dish out the courgette pasta and meatballs. Top with the basil leaves and scatter over the lemon zest, extra parmesan and black pepepr.

name: Creamed Sesame Spinach Orzo
description: Creamed spinach is our favourite side dishes. We've thrown the flavours of that into this easy orzo recipe.
instructions: Finely slice the garlic cloves and finely grate the ginger. Add a splash of sesame oil to a large pan and drop in the garlic and ginger. Sauté for 2-3 mins before adding the spinach and cooking to wilt. Add 600ml of the water and bring to a boil. Keep the 300ml of water aside for later.

Using a hand blender, whizz the mixture until smooth-ish. Bring back to a boil before adding the orzo. Add the extra water ladle by ladle if your mixture is looking too thick or sticking. Similar to a risotto, add more water until the orzo is cooked to your liking, looking gorgeous and glossy. This should take about 5-7 minutes.
While the orzo cooks, add the breadcrumbs and sesame seeds to a pan and toast until golden brown.
Finish the orzo by mixing through 3/4 of the crème fraîche and white miso. Then add the juice and zest of the lemon.
Spoon into bowls and garnish with the remaining crème fraîche and the crunchy sesame breadcrumbs.

name: Creamy  Potato Curry
description: A mild and creamy curry the whole fam can get behind. Packed with potatoes and spinach, it’s a one-pot winner for kids and a easy to dial up for grown-ups.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings

Finely dice the onion. Finely slice the garlic.
Place a large lidded saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and fry for 5–6 mins until softened.
Stir in the curry powder and turmeric. Cook for 1–2 mins until fragrant.
Peel the potatoes and chop into bite-sized chunks. Tip them into the pan, then pour in the chopped tomatoes, coconut milk and water. Stir well.
Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover with a lid and simmer for 35–40 mins until the potatoes are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Stir through the frozen spinach and let it wilt for a few mins. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Serve up! 
Kids Plate: Dollop the curry over basmati rice. 
Parents Plate: For the adults, top the curry and rice with coriander leaves, a squeeze of lime and a spoon of yoghurt and lime pickle, if using.

name: Creamy 'Nduja Linguine (Without Cream)
description: Simple, quick and delicious. A spicy take on a carbonara, you're going to love it.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil. Add your linguine and cook until al dente.
Separate 3/4 of your eggs, then add the yolks to a medium-sized bowl. Crack in the remaining egg/s.
Grate your parmesan into the bowl and season generously with pepper, then beat to combine.
Heat a saute pan over a medium heat. Add your ‘nduja and cook for a few mins until it has broken down, the oils are released, and your kitchen smells fragrant and spicy.
Grate in your garlic cloves. Pick your thyme leaves off their stalks and add these to the pan. Cook for 1 min on a medium heat (careful not to burn your garlic).
Pour in a ladle of your pasta cooking water. Mix it together until you have a smooth sauce. Get your linguine in the pan. Toss it around in the ‘nduja until it is fully coated.
Take your pan off the heat. Pour your parmesan and egg mixture into the pan and give it a toss, adding more pasta water if you need to make it super glossy.
Zest in your lemon and add the juice from half. Check the seasoning - you might need a little more salt and pepper.
Tong your linguine onto plates, then top with parmesan, lemon zest and pepper. Serve and enjoy.

name: Creamy Ajo Blanco & Pepper Cod
description: Ajo blanco has always been a little too thick for my liking, but Kitty Coles introduced me to her version that's silky smooth (with no bread) and it changed the game. This dish is inspired by her gorgeous Ajo Blanco, topped with a pantry ingredient salad that gets lifted by vibrant herbs. I've topped it with a pepper crusted cod fillet, but you could have it without, or sub the fish with any other protein you like.
keywords: Creamy Ajo Blanco & Pepper Cod recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Pour the boiling water over the blanched almonds for the Ajo Blanco and set aside until fully cooled.

Meanwhile, coarsely crush the black peppercorns and stir the paprika through. Line a baking tray with foil and add a drizzle of olive oil. Pat the cod dry, season with salt and place on the tray, then sprinkle all over with the pepper mixture. Scatter the remaining blanched almonds onto one side of the tray.
Once the water has cooled, add all the Ajo Blanco ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. Season to taste with salt and sherry vinegar, then set aside.
Drain the red peppers and slice into 2cm chunks. Drain and rinse the cannellini beans. Pick the basil and parsley leaves, discarding the basil stems. Thinly slice any soft parsley stems.

Slide the tray into the oven and cook for 8-10 mins, until the cod is cooked through and the almonds are toasted. Depending on the thickness of your fillets it might need a little more or less time, and if the fish needs longer, lift the almonds off the tray once they're toasted.
Toss the peppers, herb leaves and sliced stems, toasted almonds and beans together with a glug of olive oil and as much sherry vinegar as you'd like. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir the Ajo Blanco and share into shallow bowls. Top with the salad and fish, drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil and finish with some freshly cracked black pepper.
If you're prepping for lunch, toss the Ajo Blanco and salad together, season with sherry vinegar and share into boxes. Top with the fish, cover and pop in the fridge.

name: Creamy Avo & Lime Pasta
description: A super speedy pasta great for the whole clan, trust us the kids will love it.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Cook the pasta following pack instructions. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile, zest and juice the lime. Peel and crush the garlic. Halve the avocados, remove the stones and scoop the flesh into a blender or food processor.

Grate the Parmesan and add it to the blender with the garlic, avocado, lime juice and zest, olive oil, a good pinch of salt and a splash of pasta water. Blitz until smooth and creamy, adding more water if needed to loosen.
Taste and add extra lime juice, if you'd like it extra zingy.
Once the pasta is cooked and drained, return it to the pan and pour over the avocado sauce. Toss until everything is well coated.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Dish up as is for the kiddies. 
Parents Plate: Dish up the pasta with extra Parmesan, a crack of black pepper, basil leaves and a sprinkling of chilli flakes.

name: Creamy Bacon & Pesto Gnocchi
description: This pillowy gnocchi coated in a creamy pesto sauce is the quickest, most indulgent meal. Take it to the next level by topping it with crispy bacon.
instructions: Chop up the bacon into 3cm pieces and mince the garlic. Grate your Parmesan.
Add the bacon to a large frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Fry until golden brown and very crispy. Take out ¼ of the crispy bacon and reserve for later.
Add the chopped garlic to the bacon pan and cook for 1 min until fragrant. Add in the spinach and cook for a further 2 mins until the spinach has wilted.

Pour in the water and bring it to a simmer. Add your gnocchi and simmer for 5 mins. Add in your mascarpone and pesto. Grate in the parmesan. Give it a good stir so that the mascarpone melts and the sauce is hot. Season with black pepper to taste.
Sprinkle with the reserved crispy bacon and more Parmesan to serve. Enjoy.

name: Creamy Basil and Ricotta Spaghetti
description: Feed yourself and 3 friends for £2 with this super easy, creamy spaghetti. It'll only take you 20 minutes to whip up, too. Hannah x
instructions: Put your pasta onto cook in heavily salted boiling water.
Remove the basil leaves from the stalks and place them in a blender with a small drizzle of olive oil. Blitz for a few seconds until you have a herby paste.
Once the pasta is finished cooking, save a mug of pasta water and drain the rest. Add the ricotta and basil oil into the pan with the pasta and a splash of pasta water.
Give it a good mix and add more pasta water as needed.
Serve up and finish with a generous amount of black pepper.

name: Creamy Beans & Greens Pasta
description: A humble and delicious pasta dish. Lots of greens, cooked in garlic with creamy beans and pasta finished with juicy mozzarella and spicy pumpkin seed oil.
instructions: Trim and halve the fennel, then finely dice. Peel and slice the garlic. Strip the leaves from the cavolo nero stem and roughly chop them. Set everything aside.
Put a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add 4 tbsp olive oil and the pumpkin seeds, then fry for 2-4 mins until toasted. Transfer to a heat-safe bowl and stir the chilli flakes in.

Put the same frying pan over a medium-high heat with another 3 tbsp olive oil. Add the cavolo nero and fennel, then cook for 4-5 mins until wilted and the fennel has softened. Add the garlic, then tip in the veggie stock and the beans (with their liquid). Bring to a boil. Turn the heat down slightly and simmer for 6-8 mins until ¾ of the liquid has evaporated.
Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, cook the pasta for 2 mins under al dente.

Once your pasta is ready, use a slotted spoon to transfer the pasta into the greens mixture. Stir in some pasta water to loosen the sauce, if needed. Zest the lemon in, stir and taste. Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Divide the pasta between bowls, tear over the mozzarella and finish with the spicy pumpkin seed drizzle.

name: Creamy Bolognese Bean Bake
description: Rich leftovers of your Bolognese Ragú with butter beans, smothered in a creamy mustardy béchamel and grilled until golden. It's the perfect cosy dinner for those midweek nights when you need a little extra comfort.
instructions: Make the Bolognese Ragú.
Heat the grill to high.

Drain the butter beans, reserving a splash of their liquid. Add the leftovers of the Bolognese ragù to a small baking dish and stir through the beans. Loosen with a bit of the reserved liquid if it looks too thick.

Melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 3-4 mins until it smells nutty and starts to bubble. Gradually whisk in the milk until smooth. Simmer for 4-5 mins, stirring, until thickened. Stir in half the mustard and half the cheddar. Season with salt and loads of black pepper.
Pour the béchamel over the Bolognese mix and smooth it out with the back of a spoon. Sprinkle over the rest of the cheddar.
Grill for 5-8 mins until golden and bubbling.

name: Creamy Butter Beans With Sausage & Kale Pesto
description: A comfort food classic. If you haven’t tried kale pesto before, get on with it. It’s a wintry delight, you can thank us later.
keywords: creamy butter beans with sausage and kale pesto
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Add the kale and parsley to a food processor removing any stalks as you go.
Add the cheese, nuts (we used walnuts), garlic and olive oil and blend until you have a smooth texture. Season with salt and black pepper and taste.
Next, brown the sausages in a pan over a medium heat, season with salt then transfer to the oven to cook for 20-25 mins.
Meanwhile, crack on with the beans. Finely dice the shallot and thinly slice the garlic. Set a pan over a medium heat with a good glug of olive oil, add the shallots and begin to gently sauté.
After 5 mins, add the garlic and fennel seeds and cook for a few mins before draining and adding the beans.
Season with salt then turn up the heat and add the wine if using and reduce. Add the stock and reduce by half before adding the butter and tossing through. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the beans over the bottom of a plate then top with the sausage and dots of the pesto.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

name: Creamy Butternut Squash Pasta Sauce With Sage Butter
description: This decadent pasta sauce is made by roasting squash, garlic and chilli. The tahini makes it super creamy and the sage butter tops it all off.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C.

Peel and cube the squash into small 1cm pieces. Set the skin aside to use in a stock or roast it for a crispy squash skin snack. 
Slice the onion thickly.

Line a baking tray and spread the squash, onion and 6 of the garlic cloves (in their skins) on it. Drizzle with plenty of oil, season with salt and pepper and paprika. Roast for 30-35 mins or until soft and starting to brown, tossing halfway.

When cool enough to handle, remove the skin from the garlic cloves and the stem from the chili, if using. Take out a couple of handfuls of squash cubes for garnish and put the rest of the tray in a blender. Add the tahini, lemon juice, oat milk, olive oil and blend until smooth. Taste and season well with salt and pepper. Add a little more oat milk if you like but it’s ok if its quite thick as you will thin it down later with pasta water.

While the squash is cooking, make your fragrant butter. Grate or mince the last garlic clove. Melt the butter in a small pan on a low heat. Add the sage and heat until it starts to smell really fragrant, about 5 mins. Then add the garlic and chili and cook for another 3-4 mins, taking care not to let the garlic catch and burn - keep it on a very low heat. Season if you are using unsalted butter. Keep warm until you’re ready to serve to stop the butter from solidifying.
Cook your pasta according to package directions. Keep a cup of pasta water.
Drain the pasta and add the sauce to the pot (you may have some sauce left over, depending on how saucy you like your pasta). Heat gently and add a little pasta water to loosen it up.
To serve, plate the pasta with the remaining squash on top. Spoon over the butter and sprinkle generously with pepper.

name: Creamy Carrot & Parsnip Soup Recipe
description: This carrot and parsnip soup is a testament to how simple ingredients can create a wonderfully comforting meal. Using just a few vegetables and pantry staples, this hearty soup is perfect for batch cooking. It's ideal for freezing individual portions; simply reheat straight from frozen in a pan for a quick and easy meal. Alternatively, store the soup in the fridge, where it will keep well for up to a week. The recipe combines the natural sweetness of carrots with the earthy flavor of parsnips, making it both nutritious and satisfying. Seasoned with your favorite spices and herbs, this soup can be customized to your taste, whether you prefer a touch of cumin or a sprinkle of fresh coriander. For a creamy texture, consider adding a dollop of Greek yogurt or a splash of vegetable stock. Enjoy it with a side of crusty bread for a complete comfort food experience.
keywords: creamy carrot and parsnip soup recipe
instructions: Finely chop the onion. Scrape into a large saucepan. Add 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt, then cook over a medium heat, stirring regularly for 8-10 mins until soft but not coloured.

Meanwhile, peel the carrots and parsnips and slice into roughly 2cm chunks. Finely chop the garlic cloves, then add to the softened onions, along with the vegetables. Cook, stirring for 1 min, then strip in the thyme leaves. Pour in the stock.
Bring the mixture to the boil, then simmer away for 25 mins, or until the carrot and parsnip are completely soft.
While the soup simmers, toast the pumpkin seeds in a small, dry frying pan over a high heat for a couple of minutes until they begin to pop. Season with sea salt and set aside.

Once the veg is completely soft, turn off the heat, pour in the cream, then blitz using a hand blender until completely smooth. Season to taste with salt, pepper and nutmeg, if using. Add a little more water here if you like a thinner consistency. The soup can be made in advance, covered and reheated later if you like.
Reheat the soup if needed, then divide between bowls. Drizzle with a little more cream, then top with the toasted pumpkin seeds and a pinch of cayenne or smoked paprika, to serve.

name: Creamy Cashew & Tahini Chicken Salad
description: Turn your everyday Roast chicken into this fresh and nutty salad (you can also use Rotisserie chicken if you're short on time). Crisp cabbage and cucumber tossed in a creamy blended cashew and tahini dressing, finished with toasted cashews and sesame seeds.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Take the chicken out of the fridge about 30 mins before roasting – it cooks more evenly that way.

Slice the lemon in half. Crush the garlic cloves with the flat side of a knife, leaving the skins on. Stuff the chicken cavity with the lemon halves, garlic and thyme. Drizzle the chicken all over with olive oil. Get stuck in and rub it in properly. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Pop the chicken breast-side up in a roasting tray. Roast for about 50 mins–1 hr, or until the juices run clear when you pierce the thickest part of the thigh.For this recipe used a 1.5kg-2kg chicken, adjust the timings for a smaller or larger bird.
While the chicken is cooking, add 2/3 of the cashews into a bowl. Cover with the cold water and leave to soak for 10–20 mins.

Meanwhile, finely grate the ginger and garlic and add to a blender along with the tahini, soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil, honey add the soaked cashews and their soaking water. Blitz on high speed until smooth and creamy, adding a splash more water to loosen to a pourable consistency. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Toast the remaining cashews in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2–3 mins, tossing regularly, until golden. Tip onto a board, leave to cool, then roughly chop.

Finely shred the cabbage. Roughly chop the coriander. Halve the cucumber lengthways and slice into half-moons. Thinly slice the spring onions. Add everything to a large bowl, shred in the roast chicken and pour over most of the dressing. Toss well until everything is evenly coated.
Divide between bowls, scatter over the toasted cashews and sesame seeds and drizzle with any remaining dressing. Serve straight away.

name: Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Bowl with Limey Coriander Rice
description: Take your Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry batch to the next level with our zingy and herby rice, plus pickled and crunchy onions. It's delish.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry batch recipe.
Finely slice the red onion, then zest and juice the lime. toss the onion in ½ the lime juice, sugar, a pinch of salt. Let that pickle while everything else comes together.

Roughly chop the coriander and zest the lime. Reheat the rice according to package instructions and mix through the coriander, lime zest and a squeeze of juice. Taste and adjust with more salt or lime if needed — it should be punchy and fresh.

Warm up your creamy halloumi batch gently in a pan or microwave, just until loosened and warm. Pile the lime and coriander rice into bowls. Spoon over the quick-pickled onion, scatter with crispy onions and extra coriander, if you like.

name: Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry
description: A warming, one-pot curry packed with crispy halloumi, tender cauliflower and rich coconut spice. A proper weeknight winner that's perfect for batching, reinventing all week or simply stashing in the freezer.
instructions: Slice the onions. Cut the halloumi and cauliflower into bite-sized chunks. Grate the garlic and ginger.
Heat a large saucepan over a medium-high heat and add one tablespoon of the vegetable oil. Add the halloumi and fry for until lovely and golden. Remove from pan and set aside.
Add remaining vegetable oil to the pan, tip in the onions and cook for 8–10 mins until soft, golden and catching on the bottom.
Stir in the grated garlic and ginger, followed by the turmeric, chilli powder and garam masala. Cook for a minute until fragrant, then add the cauliflower and tomato purée.

Pour in the chopped tomatoes and coconut milk. Stir everything together and bring to the boil. Reduce to a medium heat and simmer for 20–25 mins until the curry has thickened and the cauliflower is tender. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Leave to cool before storing. The curry will keep for up to 4 days in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer. To reheat, whack a portion in the microwave or defrost straight in the pan.Eating some now? Simply serve with rice.

name: Creamy Cauliflower & Coconutty Lentils
description: This creamy sauce is almost a dal that’s blended until smooth, then layered up with roasted cauliflower and its crispy leaves, pickled onions, almonds and chilli. It’s a high protein, high fibre meal with big flavours and textures.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Mince the garlic and ginger (no need to peel the ginger). Finely dice the shallot. Finely slice the chilli. Roughly chop the almonds.
Heat a large pot or saucepan with a good drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Add the shallots and cook for 5-6 mins until translucent.

Meanwhile, chop the cauliflower into bite sized pieces and set aside any leaves. Add the cauliflower florets to a large baking tray and drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper and half of the hot paprika. Toss well and roast for 15 mins, then give them a shake and add the cauliflower leaves to the tray and roast for another 15 mins until the cauliflower and leaves are roasted and golden on the edges.

Add the remaining smoked paprika, chilli if using, curry powder, garlic, ginger and tomato purée to the pot and cook for 1-2 mins, stirring continuously, until fragrant. Take care not to burn them. Then add the lentils, coconut milk, tinned tomatoes, almond butter, stock cube and water. Bring to the boil and then lower to a simmer. Cook for 25-30 mins until the lentils are tender.

When the lentils are cooked through, you have the option to blend them into a creamy sauce or leave them as they are, both ways are delicious. If blending, let it cool slightly before pouring into a blender or use a stick blender to blend until smooth.
Add the cauliflower and leaves to the lentils and top with the fresh chilli, pickled onions, and roasted almonds and a drizzle of olive oil to finish.

name: Creamy Cauliflower Pasta Bake
description: This decadent but healthy dish is inspired by two nostalgic classics: cauliflower cheese and mac and cheese. The creaminess comes from the cauliflower itself.
instructions: Cover the cashews with boiling water and set aside to soak.

Preheat the oven to 200°C. Remove the leaves from the cauliflower and set aside. Chop the cauliflower into bite-sized pieces. Lay the florets into a baking dish with the garlic cloves and drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 25-30 mins, or until the florets are tender enough for a fork to easily pierce through them.
Cook the leaves on a tray in the oven, with a little drizzle of olive oil, for 5 mins, until just starting to crisp up at the edges.
Meanwhile, cook your pasta 2 mins less than package instructions. Drain and set aside.

Remove half of the cauliflower and place into a large blender. Squeeze out the garlic from its skin and add that in, too. Add the soaked cashews, oat milk, miso, mustard, onion powder if using, olive oil, lemon juice, vegan butter and season well with salt and pepper. Blend until smooth.
Stir the cauliflower leaves, the cooked pasta and the creamy sauce through the cauliflower until everything is evenly covered with sauce. Add a sprinkle of vegan cheese on top, if using.
Place under the grill for 4-5 minutes until the vegan cheese has melted and the top becomes crispy and caramelised.

name: Creamy Celeriac Pasta with Nutty Herb Crumb
description: This vegan pasta gets its creamy texture with the help of the celeriac. It’s full of umami and is very easy to make.
keywords: Creamy Celeriac Pasta with Nutty Herb Crumb
instructions: Peel the tough outer layer of the celeriac, then chop it into 2cm chunks. Trim and peel the garlic, then add them to a medium saucepan with the mushroom stock and garlic cloves. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and cook until soft, 8-10 mins.

Meanwhile, strip the rosemary off the stem and roughly chop. Lightly crush the walnuts and tip into a dry frying pan, place over a medium heat and toast for 3-4 mins, then add the breadcrumbs and rosemary with a drizzle of olive oil, stir and cook until golden and fragrant, transfer to a bowl. Zest the lemon and stir it through the breadcrumbs, season with salt and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper.
Once the celeriac and garlic cloves are soft, stir through the miso, then set the pan aside to cool down slightly. Once cooled, add to a blender and blend until completely smooth.

Rinse the saucepan then fill it with water. Season with plenty of salt and bring it to a boil. Once boiling, add the pasta in and cook 1 minute less than the packet instructions. Scoop out the pasta water. Drain the cooked pasta and add it back into the pan.

Pour the celeriac sauce over the pasta with the olive oil, place it on a medium heat and stir until piping hot. Add some pasta water and toss until you get a silky sauce that coats the pasta nicely. Season with salt, pepper and the juice of the zested lemon.
Top the pasta with the nutty and herby breadcrumbs.

name: Creamy Celeriac and Apple Soup
description: For this season’s celeriac, we have cooked up a deliciously comforting soup. Topped with lots of crunchy herbs to pack in extra flavour and texture.
instructions: Peel and chop up the celeriac into small chunks. Roughly chop the onions and celery, then peel and chop 3 of your apples. Pick the leaves off the thyme and grate the 4 cloves of garlic.
Slowly cook the onions and celery in a big glug of oil for 10-15 minutes until very soft.

Add the garlic, apple, celeriac, bay leaves and thyme, saving about a teaspoon of thyme for later. Pour over the stock and simmer for 30 minutes with the lid slightly ajar until the vegetables are tender.
Chop the remaining apple into small cubes, pick apart the sage leaves and thinly slice the garlic.
Blend the soup with a hand blender, along with the crème fraîche, then season to taste with salt and pepper.

Heat up the butter and a tablespoon of oil in a small pan. Add the apples and saute until lightly golden. Add in the sage and sliced garlic. Cook on a low heat for 2 minutes until the sage is crispy and the garlic is golden.
Serve the soup topped with the herby butter on top and some crusty bread on the side.

name: Creamy Chicken & Cashew Traybake Curry
description: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs in a creamy, smoky coconut and cashew sauce with charred broccoli and sweet roasted peppers. Just the kind of curry you want on a weeknight all cooked in one tray.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Season the chicken thighs and then lay in skin-side down and cook for 10 mins until the skin is super crisp. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Meanwhile, cut the red onion in half, then each half into six wedges. Trim the Tenderstem broccoli and cut in half. Tip both onto a large deep-sided baking tray, drizzle with oil and season with salt. Slide under the grill on high for 5-6 mins, turning halfway, until charred at the edges.
Pour the coconut milk into a blender along with the drained roasted red peppers, curry paste, cashew butter and the juice of the lime. Blitz with a pinch of salt until completely smooth.

Once the veg is charred, pour the sauce over the tray and nestle the chicken thighs on top skin-side up. Roast in the oven for 20-30 mins until the sauce is thickened and bubbling and the chicken is cooked through. (Add a ladle of water if needed to loosen).
Scatter the coriander over the curry and serve straight from the tray.

name: Creamy Chicken & Chorizo Pasta
description: Leftovers from our Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo batch recipe folded through silky mascarpone pasta, topped with cheese, crispy chicken skin and fresh chives. Yes, it’s as good as it sounds.
instructions: Make the Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo.
Peel the skin off the leftover chicken and place it into the air fryer at 190°C for 5-10 mins until crispy.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the pasta and cook for 2 mins under the packet timing for al dente.

Meanwhile, shred the chicken, grate the cheddar and finely slice the chives. Warm the chicken and chorizo mix in a saucepan set over a low heat. Stir through the mascarpone until it melts into a creamy sauce. Season with salt and black pepper.

Drain the pasta, reserving a mugful of the cooking water. Add the pasta to the sauce along with half of the grated cheddar. Stir through until piping hot and creamy, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen, if needed.
Divide between bowls. Top with the remaining cheddar, sliced chives and crumbled crispy chicken skin.

name: Creamy Chicken & Courgette Pasta
description: This easy chicken pasta recipe screams spring and summer. Full of fresh, creamy goodness.
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken with Schmaltzy Courgettes.
Get your pasta on to boil in generously salted water.
Thinly slice the garlic cloves and pop into a cold pan. Add a glug of olive oil and set over a medium heat. Bring the temperature up and begin to sizzle the garlic.
Cook for 2-3 mins before tipping in the crème fraîche. Tear in the leftover Roast Chicken and the Schmaltzy Courgettes.
Cook together for 4-5 mins before adding the zest and juice of the lemon. Add the cooked pasta and half of the Parmesan cheese.
Toss until creamy and divide between warm bowls. Top with extra Parmesan and get stuck in.

name: Creamy Chicken Stock & Leek Linguine
description: A ridiculously easy and indulgent pasta recipe reminiscent of a roast dinner, perfect for a date night or slow Sunday. Go on, treat yourself.
keywords: Creamy Chicken Stock & Leek Linguine recipe
instructions: Remove the outer layers of the leeks, then half and slice the leeks into pieces around 1cm thick. Put into a colander and rinse well to remove any grit. Peel and finely slice the garlic.
Melt the butter in a large pot over a medium heat and add the leeks and garlic. Cook for 10 mins until lightly golden, then add the pasta and stock. Simmer for 10-12 mins until the pasta is tender.

Add the Parmesan, mixing vigorously to emulsify. Pour in the cream and squeeze in the lemon juice. Taste for seasoning, then adjust with salt and black pepper. Serve up and top with tarragon, lemon zest and more Parm if you like.

name: Creamy Chicken Tagliatelle Recipe
description: This creamy chicken tagliatelle recipe will hit all of the nostalgia feels. We’ve made ours slightly fancier by making your own pesto – because that will make this dish a million times more delicious. Explore the comforting richness of our chicken tagliatelle recipe, where tender chicken meets luscious, creamy pasta in a deliciously satisfying dish. This chicken tagliatelle combines the delicate texture of tagliatelle with a velvety sauce made from fresh cream, homemade pesto, and Parmesan cheese, creating a delightful meal perfect for any occasion. This recipe is a delicious twist on classic Italian pasta dishes. Whether you're preparing a cosy Sunday lunch or a special dinner, this creamy chicken pasta is sure to impress. With just a few simple ingredients and straightforward cooking techniques, you can create a restaurant-quality dish right at home. Ready to elevate your pasta game? Try this irresistible chicken tagliatelle and enjoy a taste of Italy in every bite.
instructions: Tip the pine nuts into a small frying pan set over a medium heat and toast, tossing really regularly until evenly golden brown and smelling amazing. Tip into a high-powered blender and leave to cool for 5 mins.

Peel the garlic clove and add to the blender along with three-quarters of the basil, then finely grate the Parmesan and add this along with the lemon zest and juice. Spoon in 3 tbsp olive oil, add a pinch of salt and pepper, then whizz until super smooth. Add a few tablespoons of cold water if necessary. Alternatively, whizz in a bowl with a stick blender. Set the pesto aside.

Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and season really well with salt and pepper. Cut the courgette in half lengthways on a clean chopping board, then slice into ½cm half-moons. Cut the cherry tomatoes in half.

Heat a splash of oil in a medium frying pan over a high heat. Add the chicken and courgette pieces, then fry for 5-6 mins until caramelised and the courgette is softening. Chuck in the halved tomatoes and fry for 1 min. Pour in the double cream, then spoon in three-quarters of the pesto. Simmer for 1 min, then season with cracked black pepper.
Meanwhile, cook the tagliatelle in a large pan of boiling salted water following pack instructions.
Use tongs to transfer the cooked pasta straight into the frying pan. Toss really well in the sauce, adding a little of the pasta cooking water to loosen.
Divide between bowls, then top with the remaining basil leaves, the remaining pesto and finally a grating of Parmesan.

name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pie
description: A real classic with a few little refined twists to take it to another level.
keywords: Creamy chicken and mushroom pie recipes
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Brown the pancetta for about 5 mins and remove from the pan, leaving the fat.
Finely slice the onion and add to the same pan along with the butter. Sweat for 10 mins until soft, then remove.

Finely chop the chestnut mushrooms and roughly chop the wild mushrooms. Cook them off on a high heat in 2 batches until brown. Reduce the heat, chop the garlic and pick the thyme leaves and add both. Cook for another minute then remove from the pan.
Dice the chicken into roughly 1 inch pieces and brown off all over. Pour in the wine and scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze. Let the wine bubble off and evaporate almost completely.
Add the cream, mustard, Worcestershire sauce and return the mushrooms, onion and pancetta.
Bring the mix to a gentle simmer, turn off the heat and season with salt and black pepper. Leave to cool.
Pour the content of the saucepan into the pie dish and top with the circle of puff pastry.
Lay the sheet of puff pastry over the dish and use a sharp knife to trim off the excess.
Bake in the oven for 30 mins until the pastry is golden brown. Remove and allow to rest for 5 mins before serving.

name: Creamy Chickpea & Chicken Fattet
description: Creamy, tangy, crunchy and nutty. This fun and warming Middle Eastern dish is all about texture.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Drain the chickpeas, reserving the liquid. Thinly slice the garlic. Pick the parsley leaves. finely zest the lemon, then cut it in half and juice it.

Add the chicken breasts, 7-spice and garlic to a large saucepan and pour over the stock. Season with salt and pepper. Set over a medium heat and bring to the boil, then simmer gently for 10–15 mins until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, chop the flatbread into 2cm bite-sized pieces. Tip them onto a baking tray, sprinkle over the almonds and drizzle with olive oil. Slide into the oven for 5–8 mins until golden and crisp.
In a bowl, stir the tahini and Greek yoghurt together. Season with salt and a squeeze of lemon juice.

Once the chicken is cooked, transfer it to a board and shred using two forks. Return the shredded chicken to the pan with the cooking liquid. Turn the heat up, add the chickpeas and simmer until the liquid is mostly evaporated. Take off the heat and leave to cool for a couple of minutes, then stir through the tahini yoghurt until creamy. Add a splash of chickpea liquid if you want it saucier. Taste and season again if needed.

Spoon the creamy chicken mixture into bowls. Top with the crispy flatbread pieces, toasted almonds and parsley leaves. Finish with a sprinkle of lemon zest, some freshly cracked black pepper and any remaining lemon wedges on the side.

name: Creamy Chilli & Lemon Pasta
description: This high protein, high fibre pasta sauce takes no effort to put together but is packed with delicious lemony creaminess. It’s a perfect midweek dinner.
instructions: Cook the pasta until it’s al dente. Drain and set aside with a drizzle of olive oil to help prevent it sticking. Save a cup of pasta water.
Throw your butter beans into a blender with 1 tbsp olive oil, tahini (if using), nutritional yeast, and 100ml of butterbean liquid from the tin. Blend until smooth.
Finely slice the garlic and chilli. Heat a good drizzle of olive oil in a pan and cook the garlic and chilli for 3-5 mins on medium low heat, with a little salt. Take care not to let them burn.
Pour the creamy butter beans into the pan with the chilli and garlic. Stir to combine and then add the pasta and a good splash of pasta water. Stir to combine and season well with salt and pepper.
Zest the lemons and then squeeze the lemon juice over and toss well.
Finish with any fresh herbs you’ve got and more black pepper.

name: Creamy Chorizo & Mascarpone Rigatoni
description: This dish is the definition of comfort food. It’s ridiculously tasty and it comes together in just less than 30 minutes. Sophie x
instructions: Cook your rigatoni in plenty of boiling salted water for 11 mins, or until al dente.
Peel the skin off the chorizo and chop it into small chunks. Cook with a splash of olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, or until lots of the fat has rendered.
Thinly slice the garlic and add it to the pan with a pinch of chilli flakes. Cook gently for 1 minute.
Add the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins, or until it begins to darken.
Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, pressing down on the tomatoes to release their juices.
Stir in the mascarpone until fully melted and season the sauce with a good pinch of salt and pepper. Cook gently for 2 minutes.
Grate the parmesan and add it to the sauce, along with the parsley and basil.
Drain the rigatoni, reserving a mug of pasta cooking water, and mix into the sauce, adding a splash of the cooking water to help it all come together.
Plate up and top with a little more grated parmesan.

name: Creamy Coconutty Beans with Roasted Tomatoes
description: Enjoy this big batch of coconutty beans with rice, bread, or any grains you like. Maybe top it off with an egg, or a lovely salad.
keywords: Batch: Creamy Coconutty Beans with Roasted Tomatoes
Batch: Creamy Coconutty Beans with Roasted Tomatoes recipe
Creamy Coconutty Beans with Roasted Tomatoes
Creamy Coconutty Beans with Roasted Tomatoes recipe
instructions: Finely grate the ginger and garlic. Finely dice the onion. Drain the black beans.
Place a saucepan onto medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the cumin seeds and cook until it starts to shimmer, then add the onion and cook for 5-7 mins until translucent.

Stir through the ginger and garlic and cook until fragrant. Then, tip in the black beans, water and most of the coconut milk (reserve a couple of tbsp for garnish). Using a masher, smash some of the beans, then let the mixture gently simmer for 20-25 mins, until creamy and thickened (if it hasn’t thickened enough, smash some more beans). Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Meanwhile, turn the grill onto high. Place the tomatoes onto a baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt, and place under the hot grill until starting to char.
Stir the spinach into the beans until wilted.
Share the beans between bowls, drizzle over the remaining coconut milk and top with the roasted cherry tomatoes.

name: Creamy Cod Curry
description: An easy one-pot wonder with a creamy curry sauce and a spicy kick. Nutritious comfort food, perfect for eating after a long day.
instructions: Mince the garlic and slice the onion, then quarter the tomatoes. Dice the cod into nugget-sized pieces.

Set a lidded frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the vegetable oil, the garlic, onion, bay leaf, mustard seeds and some salt to the pan, then cook, tossing, for 5 mins until caramelised and translucent.
Add the quartered tomatoes and reduce with the lid on for 5 mins. After 5 mins, optionally remove the skin if you like.
Add all the seasonings and the tomato purée. Cook for 1 min, then add the cod pieces with a splash of water. Simmer for 2 mins – this is the stage where the oil will start to separate.
Add the single cream and stock, put a lid on top of the pan, then reduce for 5 mins.
Serve up! For those wanting extra spice and freshness top with asliced red chillies and coriander. Serve up with basmati rice.

name: Creamy Courgette Gratin
description: Thinly sliced courgettes are layered up with a nutmeg-spiked béchamel, fresh herbs, cheddar and Parmesan, then baked until golden. A big slice is served like a lasagne on a bed of tomato sauce.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the courgettes into ½cm-thick rounds. Add 3/5 of the olive oil to a large saucepan and place over a medium heat.

Add the courgettes, half the basil and a big pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, for 7 to 10 mins until the courgettes have softened and released some of their liquid. Drain well in a colander and give them a gentle press to remove all the excess liquid.
Transfer to an ovenproof dish which is small enough to give the courgettes some height.

Mix the crème fraîche, milk, flour and nutmeg together with a pinch of salt. Spread the courgettes into an even layer, then pour the crème fraîche mixture on top and grate over the cheeses. Bake for 25 mins until golden and bubbling.
Meanwhile, finely chop the garlic. Rinse out the saucepan you cooked the courgettes in and place over a medium heat. Add the rest of the olive oil and the chopped garlic.

Once the garlic is sizzling, add the remaining basil and chilli (if using). After 30 seconds, pour in the tomatoes. Cook for 25 mins at a gentle simmer until thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Leave the courgettes to rest for 10 mins after cooking and serve a generous slice on top of a few spoons of tomato sauce. Finish with a little extra cheese.

name: Creamy Courgette Pasta
description: Frying courgette with white wine is one of the great pairings. This pasta dish is a knockout.
instructions: Start by chopping your onions into semi-circular discs, before adding to a frying pan along with a large glug of olive oil and the chilli flakes. Chop up the courgettes and add to the pan, before beginning to fry gently on a low heat to allow the vegetables to soften.
As the onions and courgettes are frying - get the pasta on. Remember to save a cup of pasta water for later, as you will need it.

Once the onions are brown and soft, add the white wine to the pan, turning the heat up slightly so that the mixture simmers and bubbles gently. Stir well, before adding the pot of double cream to the vegetables, combining thoroughly.

As the mixture is simmering, add a sprinkle of salt and pepper and the zest of the lemon, before combining again. After another minute of stirring whilst it simmers, add the juice of the lemon to the mixture.

Once the pasta is cooked, pour it into the pan, stirring it so that the pasta becomes fully coated in the creamy sauce. Add the pasta water to loosen the sauce slightly, so that it becomes silky and smooth.

Grate the Parmesan, adding two thirds of this to the pasta mixture. Chop up your basil, also adding two thirds to the pan. Stir well. Serve immediately, garnishing with the remaining Parmesan and basil!

name: Creamy Courgette Penne Traybake
description: The easiest (and creamiest) dinner you'll cook this week. It's sort of a pasta bake, sort of a traybake, and completely delicious.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Finely slice the courgettes and add to a large roasting tin. Slice the top off the bulb of garlic, drizzle with a little olive oil, wrap in foil and snuggle into the tray. Slide into the oven for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Drop the penne into the boiling water and cook according to packet instructions.

Remove the tin from the oven, and remove the garlic, unwrap, and set aside to cool a little. Use a slotted spoon to scoop the pasta into the tray along with a big splash of pasta water. Add the cream cheese/mascarpone along with the smooshed garlic. Grate the Parmesan straight into the tray, then add the juice of ½ the lemon. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Taste and add extra lemon juice if it needs it – add a little more of the pasta water to loosen the sauce.
Spoon into bowls, top with more Parmesan, basil leaves and toasted pine nuts.

name: Creamy Courgette Rigatoni
description: Super simple creamy rigatoni with courgette and zingy lemon. A quick and balanced meal. You're welcome.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Add the pumpkin seeds to a dry frying pan and place over a medium heat, toast for 3-4 mins, until they start popping.

Tip the crème fraîche into a bowl, finely grate most of the parmesan in, saving some for grating over the top at the end. Add the mustard and zest of the lemon and season generously with black pepper and salt. Finely chop most of the parsley, saving a few leaves for garnish, stir in.

Trim the courgettes and slice them in half vertically. Slice into 1cm half-moons. Add 2 tbsp of olive oil to a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, fry the courgette for 10 mins until softened and browning in places.
Finely grate the garlic into the courgette, stir in the oregano, and remove from the heat.

Add the pasta to the boiling water and cook for 2 mins under al dente. Once the pasta is ready, use a slotted spoon to transfer into the courgettes. Place over a low heat. Add a small ladle of the pasta water, then stir in the crème fraîche mix. Add a little more pasta water if it looks dry, the sauce should be creamy and glossy. Taste and season with salt and pepper, then spoon into bowls.
Crack some black pepper on top and scatter over the reserved parsley and parmesan. Finish with a scattering of the toasted pumpkin seeds.

name: Creamy Curried Chicken Tacos with Kimchi
description: Leftover Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken gets a second life in these creamy, punchy tacos with tangy kimchi. Perfect for a speedy midweek dinner.
instructions: Make the Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken batch recipe.
Pick the coriander leaves, finely slice the stems. Use two forks to shred the leftover curried chicken. Reheat the chicken with a splash of sauce until piping hot.
Warm the tortillas for 30 seconds on each side until soft and lightly toasted.
Spoon the soured cream over the tortillas, top with the shredded chicken and kimchi. Sprinkle over the coriander and serve straight away.

name: Creamy Dal Porridge with Crispy Curry Leaf Drizzle
description: Inspired by Khichdi -  a popular dish in South Asian cuisines - this warming, creamy dal porridge is deeply comforting and makes the perfect meal to cosy up on the couch with or when you’re not feeling too great.
keywords: Dal Porridge with Crispy Curry Leaf Drizzle
Dal Porridge with Crispy Curry Leaf Drizzle recipe
instructions: Finely dice the onion. Grate the garlic and ginger. Tip the rice and lentils into a sieve and rinse under cold water until it runs clear.

Set a large saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the onion and cook, stirring, for 8-10 mins until softened and starting to brown at the edges. Add the garlic, ginger, rice and lentils and stir for a minute until the residual water has evaporated. Pour in the stock, bring to the boil and skim any scum from the surface. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 mins, then turn the heat down to low for another 10-15 mins until cooked through and creamy. If it's evaporating too quickly, add a splash of water.
Meanwhile, peel the butternut squash and remove any seeds. Coarsely grate. When there's 20 mins left on the porridge, stir the grated squash through.

Place a small frying pan over a medium heat with the oil for the topping. Once hot, add the cashews and cook for 2-3 mins until lightly golden. Turn the heat down to low, add the mustard seeds and curry leaves and stir until the popping has subsided. Transfer to a bowl and stir through the chilli powder. Season with salt and black pepper.
Divide the dal porridge between bowls. Swirl through the yoghurt and finish with a drizzle of the crispy curry leaf topping.

name: Creamy Edamame Orecchiette
description: This is the pasta you make when you want to eat green but still eat well. Cavolo nero blended into a smooth, savoury sauce, with edamame and butter beans adding real protein. Easy, filling, and exactly right for midweek.
instructions: Drain and rinse the butter beans. Remove the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and roughly chop. Finely chop the garlic.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta following pack instructions. Once cooked, add the edamame into a colander and drain the pasta over the top. Reserve some pasta water.
While the pasta is cooking, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant.
Add the cavolo nero to the pan with a good pinch of salt. Pop a lid on and cook for 3-5 mins, until the leaves have wilted.

Transfer the cooked greens to a blender with a couple of tablespoons of the butter beans and a splash of the pasta water. Blend until smooth, adding more water as needed to loosen. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Stir the green sauce through the pasta and edamame along with the remaining butter beans. Spoon into bowls and top with the basil and a crack of black pepper.

name: Creamy Garlic & Herby Chicken Gnocchi
description: If you haven’t tried cooking gnocchi in your air fryer yet, this is your sign. Golden and crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, they’re like tasty little pillows.
keywords: Creamy Garlic & Herb Chicken Gnocchi recipe
instructions: Finely dice the onion. Dice the chicken into chunks. Crush the garlic and finely chop the parsley.
Heat the air fryer to 180°C, then tip the gnocchi into the air fryer with ½ tbsp oil from the sundried tomato jar. Cook for around 15 mins until crispy.

Heat a large frying pan with another ½ tbsp sun-dried tomato oil. Add the onion with some salt, then cook for a few minutes to soften. Add the chicken and garlic and cook until softened and cooked through – about 10 minutes.⁣⁣
Add the seasoning, mixed herbs, sun-dried tomatoes and soft cheese to the pan along with the water. Mix it together for a few minutes.
Stir in the crispy gnocchi, the grated cheese and a small handful of parsley.
Season to taste, then share between bowls and top with more parsley and Parmesan.

name: Creamy Garlic Chicken Legs
description: There are a whopping 25 garlic cloves in this recipe but you won’t believe how mellow and caramelised the flavours are. Cook it for dinner and see for yourself.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C.

Grab a large ovenproof frying pan or dish and set it over a medium-high heat. Season the chicken legs with salt and sear them, skin-side down, in the pan with plenty of olive oil. Roll them around in the olive oil, cooking them for 8-9 mins, caramelising the skin and starting to build flavour in the pan. Once really nicely browned, whip them out the pan and onto a plate.

Set the pan back over a medium-high heat. Add the peeled garlic cloves and thyme to the hot pan and fry for 1-2 mins to infuse the chicken fat with the flavour. Tip in the chicken stock and pop the legs back into the pan. Cover with a lid or a cartouche (a lid made out of baking parchment) and slide into the oven for 40-45 mins. The chicken will braise, the garlic cloves will mellow and poach and the stock will slowly reduce and thicken.

Remove from the oven and fish the chicken out. Pop the pan back over a high heat and bring to a boil then leave to reduce by half or until you're happy with the consistency. Stir through the créme fraîche, capers, chopped dill and the zest and juice of the lemon. Add a splash of water to thin it out, if necessary.
Serve the chicken legs on top of warm mash (if you like), spooning over plenty of the garlicky sauce.

name: Creamy Gochujang Con Carne Rigatoni
description: This luxurious pasta puts a korean spin on your Beef Chilli Con Carne leftovers which makes it spicy, rich and ultra-comforting.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Beef Chilli Con Carne batch recipe.
Fill a large saucepan with salted water and bring to the boil. Once boiling, tip in the pasta and cook following pack instructions until al dente.
Meanwhile, finely grate the cheddar.

Set a medium saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the gochujang and cook, stirring, for 1–2 mins until darkened. Stir through the beef chilli with a splash of water to loosen, then heat until piping hot.

Using a slotted spoon, transfer the cooked pasta into the sauce. Pour in the double cream and add half the cheddar. Stir until evenly coated, adding a splash of pasta water if it’s too thick. Taste and season with salt and black pepper, if needed.
Share between bowls and top with the remaining cheddar.

name: Creamy Gochujang Gnocchi with Cavolo Nero
description: This spinach and mozzarella filled gnocchi takes just 5 mins to pan fry until it's super crispy. Add it to a creamy, smoky gochujang sauce for the perfect cosy mid-week dinner.
ingredients: 1Pack La Famiglia Rana Spinach & Mozzarella Filled Pan Fry Gnocchi
instructions: Thinly dice the shallot. Rip the cavolo nero from its stalks and finely chop the leaves. Thinly slice the garlic.

Heat a frying pan with the butter or a drizzle of olive oil as you prefer. Once melted, add the La Famiglia Rana Spinach & Mozzarella Filled Pan Fry Gnocchi and pan fry for 5 mins until crispy and golden. Tip onto a plate and set aside.
Place the frying pan back on medium heat, and fry the shallot and garlic for 2-4 mins until softened.
Add the tomato purée and gochujang and stir until everything is evenly combined. Add the cavolo nero with a splash of water. Place the lid on and cook for 3-4 mins, until vibrant green and softened.

Take the lid off and continue cooking for a few minutes until the sauce has thickened. Stir in the cream then add the gnocchi and ½ the Parmesan. Season with lime juice, salt, sugar and pepper to taste.
Share between bowls and top with more Parmesan.

name: Creamy Green Beans with Tomato Cheddar Salad
description: Creamy butter beans in our Super Greens & Garlic Sauce, topped with juicy tomatoes, tangy cheddar and a dollop of yoghurt. Toast on the side for maximum scoopage.
keywords: Creamy Green Beans with Tomato Cheddar Salad
Creamy Green Beans with Tomato Cheddar Salad recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the Super Greens & Garlic Sauce.
Halve the tomatoes and add them to a mixing bowl. Season with salt and a splash of sherry vinegar, then set aside to marinate.
Thinly slice the cheddar. Toast the sourdough in a toaster or under a hot grill until golden.
Add the Super Greens & Garlic Sauce and the butter beans to a saucepan. Set over a medium heat and warm through gently, stirring often. Taste and season with salt and black pepper, if needed.
Divide the creamy beans between bowls and swirl through the yoghurt.
Toss the sliced cheddar through the tomatoes, then spoon the salad over the beans. Serve with the toast on the side for dipping and scooping.

name: Creamy Green Halloumi & Chickpea Filo Pie
description: Think a pie's just for winter? Think again. This creamy green halloumi and chickpea filo pie is as refreshing as it is filling. Tuck in.
instructions: Peel and finely dice the onion. Peel and dice the garlic. Dice the halloumi into 2cm cubes and fry in a dry frying pan for 5 mins until golden, then remove and set aside. Add ⅙ of the oil to an ovenproof pan and fry the garlic and onion for 5 mins over a low-medium heat until golden, then tip in the chickpeas and their water (the specified weight in the ingredients list is for the combined weight of the chickpeas and their water). Bring it to a simmer and leave to bubble away for 5-10 mins until slightly reduced.

Blend half of the spinach with the water until smooth. Then take a large spoonful of the chickpea mixture and add it to the blended spinach, blitzing until smooth. Add this mixture to the chickpea pan and season with salt and pepper.

Wilt the remaining spinach through the chickpeas and add the halloumi back in, mixing well until the spinach has wilted. Add the lemon zest and juice. Finely chop the dill and mix through, along with the crème fraîche.

Brush a sheet of filo with some of the remaining oil, then scrunch it up and place it on top of the filling. Repeat with all the sheets of filo until you've used it up and covered the top of the pie. Scatter with sesame seeds and bake for 15-20 mins at 180°C or until evenly golden brown.

name: Creamy Green Pasta & Beans
description: Silky, herby greens blitzed into a sauce and folded through pasta with butter beans and edamame. This meal prep lunch is packed with protein.
instructions: Drain and rinse the butter beans. Remove the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and roughly chop. Finely chop the garlic.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta following pack instructions. Once cooked, drain and reserve the cooking water.
While the pasta is cooking, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant.
Add the cavolo nero and edamame to the pan with a good pinch of salt. Pop a lid on and cook for 3-5 mins, until the leaves have wilted and the edamame is bright green.

Transfer the cooked greens to a blender with a couple of tablespoons of the butter beans and a splash of the pasta water. Blend until smooth, adding more water as needed to loosen. Season to taste with lemon juice, salt and black pepper.

Stir the green sauce through the pasta along with the remaining butter beans. Spoon into Tupperware containers and top with the basil and a crack of black pepper. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Creamy Green Pasta & Beans
description: Silky, herby greens blitzed into a sauce and folded through pasta with butter beans and edamame. Packed with protein. And very, very green.
instructions: Drain and rinse the butter beans. Remove the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and roughly chop. Finely chop the garlic.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta following pack instructions. Once cooked, drain and reserve the cooking water.
While the pasta is cooking, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant.
Add the cavolo nero and edamame to the pan with a good pinch of salt. Pop a lid on and cook for 3-5 mins, until the leaves have wilted and the edamame is bright green.

Transfer the cooked greens to a blender with a couple of tablespoons of the butter beans and a splash of the pasta water. Blend until it is a smooth, silky sauce, adding more pasta water as needed. Season to taste with the lemon juice, salt and black pepper.
Stir the green sauce through the pasta along with the remaining butter beans. Spoon into bowls and top with the basil and a crack of black pepper.

name: Creamy Greens Pesto Pasta
description: Creamy, hearty and packed full of goodness, this recipe comes together in less than 20 minutes.
instructions: Boil some water in a saucepan, add a generous amount of salt, then tip in the pasta and broccoli. After 3 mins, scoop out the broccoli and transfer to a food processor. Allow the pasta to continue cooking in the boiling water.
Juice the lemon into a food processor and add all of the remaining ingredients (except the pasta), along with 150ml pasta water. Blitz until smooth.
Drain the pasta once it’s al dente (just about cooked but still a little firm), reserving some of the pasta water in case you need a little extra to thicken up the sauce.
Pour the sauce into the saucepan and stir through the pasta. Cook over a low heat for a few more minutes until the pasta is at the desired tenderness and the sauce is hot.
Plate up and sprinkle over some Parmesan shavings.

name: Creamy Halloumi & Roasted Veg Burritos
description: Take your Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry batch up a level with these easy burritos. Stuffed with roasted veg and zingy lime rice – they’re a perfect weeknight dinner or on-the-go lunch.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry batch recipe.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the peppers into strips and peel and quarter the red onion. Toss them on a baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil, smoked paprika and a good pinch of salt. Roast for 20–25 mins until soft and slightly charred.

Cook the rice following pack instructions. Meanwhile, roughly chop the coriander and zest the lime. Once the rice is done, stir through the lime zest, chopped coriander and a squeeze of lime juice. Taste and season with salt.
Reheat the Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry gently in a pan or microwave until hot and spoonable. Add a splash of water if it needs loosening.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan or microwave for 10–15 seconds so they’re soft and pliable.
To build, lay each tortilla flat and add a scoop of lime rice. Spoon over the creamy halloumi, then pile on the roasted veg. Add hot sauce or chilli flakes, if using.
Fold the sides in, roll up tightly from the bottom and wrap into a burrito. Serve straight away.

name: Creamy Halloumi Chickpea Curry with Charred Veg
description: Bulk up your leftover Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry batch leftovers with chickpeas and charred veg. A great way to hit your five a day and get dinner on the table in no time.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry batch recipe.

Drain the chickpeas and tip into a saucepan with your leftover Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry. Place over a low heat and cook until bubbling and thickened. Add a splash of water if needed to loosen the mixture.

Meanwhile, prep the veg. Slice the courgette and toss in a bowl with olive oil and a pinch of salt and set aside. Strip the leaves from the cavolo nero stalks, give them a rinse, then slice into bite-sized portions and stir into your curry. If you don't have cavolo nero, kale or spinach will also work a treat.
Drain any liquid from the courgette and char in a hot frying pan or under the grill for 5–7 mins until soft and blackened in spots. Toss with salt and nigella seeds.
Pick the mint and set aside.

Once the cavolo nero is softened and the curry is piping hot, spoon into bowls. Top with the charred courgette, a spoonful of yoghurt (if using), and scatter over the mint leaves and chilli flakes. Dig in!

name: Creamy Halloumi Curry
description: Looking for a deliciously different curry? Try a creamy halloumi curry! The salty, meaty flavour of halloumi, a Cypriot cheese, is incredible in this rich curry sauce. You could even toss in some sweet potatoes or potatoes for added heartiness.
instructions: Chop the halloumi and cauliflower into bite-size pieces. Cut onion into slices.

Heat a large pan and add a splash of vegetable oil. Add your onions. Cook on a medium-high heat so they start catching on the pan and softening. Once the onions are beginning to brown, add your cubes of halloumi.

As the halloumi starts to brown, add the grated garlic cloves, a grated knob of ginger, the turmeric, chilli powder and garam masala. Mix everything together, then stir through your cauliflower and tomato purée.
Pour in your tinned tomatoes and your coconut milk. Stir everything together. Simmer over a medium heat until the curry is nice and thick.
Meanwhile, cook your rice following packet instructions.
Serve the curry on top of your steaming rice. Garnish with freshly chopped coriander.

name: Creamy Halloumi Flatbreads & Tamarind Tomato Salad
description: Give your leftover Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry leftovers a fresh rebrand with our zingy, taramind tomato salad. All scooped up with warm flatbreads. Yum.
keywords: Creamy Halloumi Flatbreads with Tamarind Tomato Salad
instructions: Before you begin, make the Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry batch recipe.
Finely slice the red onion and soak it in a bowl of cold water with a pinch of salt. Let it sit while everything else comes together, this softens the bite but keeps the crunch.
Halve the cherry tomatoes. Pick and roughly chop the mint. Finely chop the red chilli.

Toss the tomatoes into a bowl with the tamarind paste, chopped mint, chilli, a glug of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Mix well, then leave to sit for 5–10 mins so the flavours can get to know each other.

Warm your flatbreads in a dry frying pan or low oven until soft and steamy. Then reheat your leftover Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry in a small pan or microwave until loosened and spoonable. Add a splash of water if needed.

To build, spread a generous layer of creamy halloumi across each flatbread. Pile on the tamarind tomato salad, then finish with extra mint and a drizzle of yogurt.Fold and eat with your hands or go full fork-and-knife if you’re feeling civilised.

name: Creamy Halloumi Jacket with Pickled Chilli Honey & Fennel Salad
description: A banger baked potato stuffed with your Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry batch, topped with sweet-spicy chilli honey, and served with a crisp, zippy fennel salad. What a glow-up.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 200°C.
Prick the potatoes all over with a fork, rub with a little olive oil and a good pinch of salt, then bake for 50 mins until the skins are super crisp and the insides fluffy.
Thinly slice the red chilli and add it to a small bowl with the white wine vinegar and a pinch of salt. Give it a mix and set aside to lightly pickle.
Reheat your curry leftovers in a pan or microwave until just spoonable, loosen with a splash of water if needed.
Warm the honey in a small frying pan. Add the pickled chilli slices and a small splash of the pickling liquor. Let it bubble for 30 seconds, then set aside.
Finely slice the fennel and toss it in a bowl with the rocket, a squeeze of lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice open the baked potatoes and fluff up the insides with a fork. Spoon over the warm Creamy Cauli & Halloumi Curry, then drizzle with the warm chilli honey. Serve alongside the fennel salad.
