name: Creamy Ham & Greens Macaroni
description: A comforting, creamy pasta that comes together in no time at all. Big flavour. Low effort. Perfect for the family.
instructions: Remove the outer layer of the leeks, then slice in half before cutting into half moons. Pop into a colander and wash thoroughly.
Cut the broccoli into small florets and finely chop the garlic.

Heat a glug of oil in a pan over a medium heat and add the leeks and broccoli with a big pinch of salt. Sweat them down until softened and then add the garlic, cooking for another 2 mins, until the broccoli is tender and the garlic is fragrant.
Get the pasta on to boil in a large pot of salted water. Reserve the pasta water and drain.

Pour in the double cream along with the peas and chopped ham, season with salt and lots of black pepper then bring it to a very gentle simmer. Cook for a couple of minutes until the peas are thawed and the cream has thickened. Transfer the pasta to the sauce directly from the water and mix well, adding another slosh of pasta water if you need to.
Serve up and grate over the Parmesan and a crack of black pepper.

name: Creamy High-Protein Miso Mushroom Soup with Sourdough
description: This quick and easy recipe brings together the rich, umami flavours of mushrooms and miso with the silky texture of silken tofu. The result is a high-protein, creamy soup that’s perfect for any time of day.
instructions: Dice the shallots, then wash and roughly chop the mushrooms. Heat a good drizzle of sesame oil in a pan set over a low heat. Once hot, add the diced shallots and sauté for 3-4 mins until fragrant and translucent.
Add the mushrooms and soy sauce, then sauté until the mushrooms have lost most of their water and are starting to sizzle and turn brown. Turn off the heat.
Put half of the cooked mushrooms into a blender, along with the miso paste, tofu and stock. Blend until creamy and smooth.
Return the blended soup to the pan, mix with the remaining mushrooms, and warm through.
Serve with a drizzle of chilli oil, a small handful of coriander and crusty toasted sourdough.

name: Creamy Hummus with Harissa Tomatoes
description: This method delivers the creamiest, silkiest hummus. Topped with harissa tomatoes and pine nuts, it's a delicious dish that’s perfect for sharing.
instructions: Boil the chickpeas in plenty of water with the garlic and a bay leaf and bicarbonate of soda if using, for around 30-40 mins or until very soft.
Blend the chickpeas with a clove of garlic and 100ml of the chickpea water from the tin (aquafaba).
Add the tahini and blend before adding 4 ice cubes. Blend again, then add the lemon juice, cumin and salt. Adjust the seasoning and consistency to your taste.

For the harissa tomatoes, add 2 tbsp of olive oil to a pan on medium high heat. Add half of the tomatoes and stir often while they cook for about 5-8 mins. They should have broken down and turned into a sauce. Then add the rest of the tomatoes and the harissa and cook for a few more minutes until they have just burst open.
Toast your pine nuts in a dry pan for a couple of minutes, shaking often to make sure they don’t burn. Roughly chop some parsley.
Drizzle your pita with some oil and herbs and toast in a pan or in the oven.
To serve, layer the hummus with the tomatoes and top with pine nuts, parsley and a good drizzle of olive oil. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Instant Noodles
description: This viral instant noodle recipe is a surefire way to add some excitement to a packet of ramen.
instructions: Start by mincing the garlic. Transfer to a serving bowl with the chilli flakes.

Add a splash of oil to a pan and heat on high for 1-2 mins, until the oil is shimmering. Carefully pour the hot oil into the garlic and chilli bowl, then stir to combine. Add the egg yolk, the mayonnaise and the soup sachet that came with the noodles. Stir vigorously until all is combined.

Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Meanwhile, slice the spring onions as finely as possible. Once boiling, cook the noodles following pack instructions (I like to do 1 min less for chewier noodles).

Once cooked, add the noodles straight from the pan, followed by the water. Give it a thorough stir until all the sauce at the bottom is combined. Add the spring onions and slice of cheese (the heat from the noodles will melt it slightly). Enjoy!

name: Creamy Kale Conchiglie With Charred Tenderstem
description: Who doesn't love a big old plate of green pasta? This recipe is as good for a healthy midweek meal as it is for a showstopper on the weekend.
instructions: First, tear up the flatbread into pieces and blitz into crumbs in a high speed blender. Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a pan over a medium heat and fry the breadcrumbs until crispy. Zest and juice the lemon, then add the zest into the breadcrumbs. Season with salt and pepper.

Now make the pasta sauce — get the kale into a large pot of salted water and blanch for 2 mins. Shock with cold water (this keeps the sauce nice and vibrant) and drain, squeezing out the moisture with your hands.

Heat the grill to high. Cut the tenderstem in half, put in a bowl and drizzle with 2 tbsp of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then transfer to the grill and cook for 6 mins, turning halfway. Once cooked, season with ½ of the lemon juice. If you need to, keep warm in the oven until serving.
Peel and roughly chop the garlic. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a pan and fry the garlic for 2 mins or until just turning golden. Grate the Parmesan.

Cook the pasta and save some water before draining. Add the cooked kale to a high speed blender along with the garlic oil, basil and around 3 ladlefuls of pasta water — then blitz until smooth. Add the crème frâiche and the remaining lemon juice, blitz again and check for consistency. You are looking for a really smooth sauce, so if it's looking a bit lumpy still, add more pasta water and keep blitzing! Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

Add the pasta back into the pot along with the sauce and Parmesan. Mix it all really well to emulsify and add more pasta water if it needs loosening. It might feel like a lot of water, but this dish can take it.
Plate up the pasta and top with the charred tenderstem and breadcrumbs.

name: Creamy Kale Pasta
description: This creamy cavolo nero and bean pasta is one of the most delicious ways to eat your greens. We’ve blitzed up cannellini beans to create a super creamy sauce, while upping the fibre and plant protein content.
instructions: Remove and discard the stems from the cavolo nero. Add the cavolo nero to a large pan of salted boiling water and briefly cook for around 20 seconds. Remove from the water and set aside.
Add your pasta of choice to the boiling water and cook for a minute shy of pack instructions.

Meanwhile, finely chop the garlic. Heat the olive oil in another pan and gently fry the garlic for a couple of mins until it becomes fragrant. Add in the lemon zest and the beans with some of their liquid and cook for around 5 mins until most of the liquid has drained and the beans are soft.

Add the beans and cavolo nero with a splash of pasta water to a blender and blitz to a smooth sauce. Add more water if the sauce needs loosening up. Then add it back into the pan and seasoning generously.
Add the pasta and a splash of the pasta cooking water to the pan with the sauce. Cook for another couple of mins, adding a bit more pasta cooking water if it needs it.
Divide the pasta between bowls and top with chilli flakes, a good drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and the seeds if you’re using.

name: Creamy Kale Salad with Mushrooms & Chickpeas
description: Say goodbye to boring salads. This creamy kale salad ticks all the boxes without being super complicated, with crunchy chickpeas, gut-loving sauerkraut and an addictive tahini dressing.
keywords: Creamy Kale Salad with Mushrooms & Chickpeas
Creamy Kale Salad with Mushrooms & Chickpeas recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and roast your mushrooms and drained chickpeas with a glug of olive oil and a pinch of salt for 20 mins, stirring the tray halfway.
Roughly chop the kale and pickled chillies.
In a large bowl, mix together your tahini and chilli brine before tossing in the kale and massaging until coated.
Add the remaining ingredients to the kale including the roasted chickpeas and mushrooms.
Serve immediately or store in the fridge for up to a few days.

name: Creamy Leek Potatoes
description: This is my version of a potato salad for when it's cold outside. They're so moreish and take just 20 mins to make. Hannah x
instructions: Cut the potatoes in half, place them in a pan of cold water and bring it to a boil. Simmer for 15 mins or until cooked.
Slice the leek in half length ways, then slice into roughly 1cm strips. Wash to get any dirt out.
Place a frying pan on a medium heat and sweat off the leeks in a glug of olive oil and the butter. Gently cook until softened before adding the garlic and cooking for a couple more mins.
Add the cream and the white wine and reduce for a few mins until the sauce has thickened and is glossy. Then grate in the parmesan.
Once the potatoes are cooked, strain them and add them to the creamy leeks. Season with salt and pepper, finish with the chopped parsley and tuck in.

name: Creamy Lemon & Asparagus Orzo
description: Creamy, lemony orzo livened up with spears of al dente asparagus. This is the perfect recipe for the spring and summer.
instructions: Fill a pot with plenty of very well salted water. Bring to the boil, then cook the orzo following pack instructions.
Meanwhile, add the pancetta to a large frying pan with a splash of oil, then place it over a medium heat. It will come up to temperature and begin to sizzle.

While the pasta cooks and the pancetta fries, trim the ends off the asparagus and cut them into roughly 3cm lengths. If the asparagus spears are very thick, half them lengthways first. Finely chop the garlic.
Once the pancetta is golden and crispy, add the garlic to the pan, stir well so it sizzles in the fat and then turn off the heat.

When the pasta is 3 mins away from being done, add the asparagus to the same pot and cook together for 3 mins. Take out a mug of pasta water and set aside. Drain everything, leaving a little water clinging to the pasta, and add it all to the pan with the pancetta.

Mix everything really well, with the pan over a low heat. Pour in the cream and parmesan, grind in plenty of black pepper, add the zest and juice of the lemon and mix well. Add a little pasta cooking water if it’s looking too thick. You want it creamy and loose.
Taste and add salt and pepper. Plate up, finish with extra Parm, pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Creamy Lemon And Cauliflower Pasta
description: This creamy, lemony pasta is rich and decadent but not too heavy. Topped with roasted cauliflower and flaked almonds, it's a perfect mid-week meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Cook your pasta according to the package instructions. Pasta water should be as salty as seawater. Drain and drizzle with a little olive oil to prevent it sticking and set aside.

Chop your cauliflower into small florets. Toss it with olive oil, salt and pepper and roast on the top shelf for around 20 mins, turning halfway. It should be charred in spots and still have a firm bite to it.

Chop your cauliflower leaves and wash them well. Remove the tough spine and drizzle them with a little olive oil and season. Add some chilli flakes if you like. Roast for 10-15 mins or until crispy, tossing half way. These are not part of the pasta dish but a great snack while you wait and saves them from the bin!
Add the butter beans, cashews, oat milk, nutritional yeast, garlic powder and salt to a high speed blender and blend until very smooth.
Add the juice of two lemons to the sauce and stir through. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Add the sauce to a pan along with the pasta and half of the cauliflower and heat through gently.

Plate the pasta with the rest of the cauliflower on top and drizzle with a good amount of olive oil and another squeeze of lemon juice. If using, add the chilli flakes, almonds and capers. Finish with plenty of lemon zest and black pepper.

name: Creamy Lemon Chickpea Stew
description: Using jarred chickpeas makes all the difference in this simple dish. It's creamy, zingy, and extremely comforting without feeling heavy.
instructions: Finely chop the red onions and thinly slice the garlic cloves and chilli.
Preheat a large sauté pan over a medium-high heat. Add a shot of oil and tip in the red onions. Season with salt and cook for 4-5 mins before adding the garlic and chilli. Cook together for 4-5 mins.

Pour in the cream and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce the heat and let it simmer for a minute or two to reduce the cream slightly. Use a peeler to remove the zest of the lemons in strips. Add to the pan along with the spinach and chickpeas along with the liquid from the jar.
Bring back to a boil and wilt the spinach through the cream. Bubble away for 3-4 mins before finishing with lemon juice and plenty of chopped dill and black pepper.

name: Creamy Lentil Curry & Cumin Roast Sweet Potato
description: This is a really quick veggie curry with hidden protein in it that gives it an extra creamy texture. Don't skip the crispy curry leaves on top, they add so much flavour.
keywords: Creamy Lentil Curry with Cumin Roast Sweet Potato
Creamy Lentil Curry with Cumin Roast Sweet Potato recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the sweet potato into 2cm pieces, then add to a baking tray with the cumin, the olive oil, salt and pepper. Pop in the oven for 20-25 mins, until soft and golden. Finely slice the green chillies, then finely chop the coriander.
Finely slice the onion. Heat the olive oil for the curry in a large pan over a medium heat and add the onion with a pinch of salt, cooking for 10-15 mins, until nice and golden.

In the meantime, add the tofu to a blender and blitz until smooth. Add the curry paste and tomato purée to the onions and cook out for a couple of minutes, until darkened in colour, before adding the blended tofu, the lentils and the water. Mix well, season with salt and pepper, then simmer gently for 10 mins.
Add the remaining olive oil to a small frying pan over a medium heat, add the chillies and cook for a minute or two before adding the curry leaves, cooking until nicely crisp. Remove from the heat.

Mix the coriander and the lemon juice through the curry, tasting and adjusting the seasoning if needed. Serve the curry up topped with the roast sweet potato, the coconut yoghurt and the curry leaf oil.

name: Creamy Mince Pasta Bake
description: This dish is inspired by the Cypriot classic, Makaronia Tou Fournou. This is my mum's vegan version which is easier to put together and tastes amazing.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C.

Melt the butter over a low heat in the pan. Add the flour and mix with a wooden spoon. The mix will be clumpy at this point. Slowly add the milk while whisking continuously with a rubber whisk so you don’t damage the pan.

Once you’ve added all of the milk, the mixture should be smooth. Add the cinnamon and then add 80g of vegan cheese and whisk on a medium heat until melted and combined. Allow the béchamel to thicken slightly and season well with plenty of salt and pepper. Remove from the pan into a bowl and set aside.

Wipe the pan clean. Chop the onion and mince the garlic. Drizzle a little olive oil in the pan and fry the onion for 4-5 mins on medium heat until translucent. Add the garlic and fry for another minute before adding the tomato purée and the vegan mince. Add another drizzle of olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Add the stock to the mince and add the mint and balsamic vinegar. Fry for 4-5 mins, adding more olive oil if needed, until the mince is browned and browned. Taste for seasonings.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta according to package instructions.
Add the pasta to the pan with the mince and pour a ladle of bechamel into the pan. Mix well to combine the pasta and the mince.
Pour the rest of the bechamel over the pasta and mince mix. Sprinkle the rest of the vegan cheese over the top and plenty of black pepper.

Cover the pasta and bake it for 10 mins until the cheese is melted (vegan cheese melts better when it steams for a little bit). Then remove the lid from the pan and grill for another 3-4 mins until the cheese starts to crisp up.

name: Creamy Miso Carrot Gnocchi
description: Carrots and cashews make the creamiest sauce for pillowy gnocchi. It's seriously moreish.
instructions: Scrub the carrots well and cut them into very thin slices.
Finely slice 5 garlic cloves and the shallots and sauté with a drizzle of oil for about 3 mins on medium low heat, stirring often to make sure they don’t catch.
Add the carrots and sauté for another 3-4 mins.

Add most of the cashews (reserve a handful for serving), water, salt, pepper and cover. Let it simmer on a low heat for about 15-20 mins, until the carrots have softened.Place the carrots into a blender with the miso and 1/3 of the olive oil and blend until smooth.

Meanwhile, make the pesto.Remove the thick stems from the parsley and the basil. Grate one or two garlic cloves, depending on your preference.Add the garlic, parsley, basil, the rest of the cashews, lemon juice, 1 tsp salt and nutritional yeast if using, to a small food processor and pulse until you have a chunky texture. Add 2/3 of olive oil and pulse again to combine. Add a little more oil or water if you prefer your pesto more runny. Season well with salt and pepper.If you don't have a food processor, you can finely chop all of your ingredients and stir together in a small bowl to combine.
Cook the gnocchi as per package instructions, drain and put back into the pot. Stir the sauce through the gnocchi and heat through.
If you have sauce leftover, it freezes well and can be used as a sauce for pasta, spelt, or orzo. It can also be thinned down a little and enjoyed as a soup.
The pesto keeps refrigerated for up to 5 days. If the oil solidifies in the fridge, add a dash of very hot water to loosen it up and bring it back to room temperature.

name: Creamy Miso Cauliflower and Sticky Squash
description: Creamy miso cauliflower mash with sticky maple squash. It tastes as good as it looks Mob.
keywords: miso cauliflower and sticky squash recipes
instructions: Peel the squash and chop it up into thick slices.
Peel the leaves off the cauliflower and roughly chop.
Toss the squash, cauliflower leaves with maple syrup, salt and pepper and pop onto a baking tray and bake for 15 mins at 180°C until the squash is soft and the leaves are crispy.
Cook the soften squash on a griddle pan until there are dark char lines.
Bring a pot of water to a boil and add in the cauliflower. Cook for 10 mins until soft and tender.
Add the cauliflower to a food processor with the miso paste, oat milk and 2 tbsp dairy-free margarine. Blend together until very smooth and season with salt and pepper.
Finely chop the garlic and roughly chop the parsley.
Spread the miso cauliflower on a plate and then add the sticky squash and crispy cauliflower leaves over the top.

Heat the remaining margarine in a saucepan until frothy. Add in the garlic and chilli powder, cook for 2 mins until lightly golden. Turn off the heat and add in the parsley and allow the parsley to crisp up.
Pour the chilli garlic ‘butter’ over the miso cauliflower and enjoy with some crusty sourdough bread.

name: Creamy Miso Mushroom Grains
description: Not like a risotto, but not NOT a risotto. Miso, mushrooms and garlic are cooked out with grains, chickpeas and silken tofu for a creamy, high protein boost.
instructions: Start by slicing the mushrooms. Then finely chop the garlic, chives and zest the lemon. Set these each of these aside to be used later.

Heat a quarter of the olive oil in a large pan over a high heat, then add the sliced mushrooms in an even layer with a pinch of salt, cooking until golden, then remove. You might need to do this in batches so as not to overcrowd the pan, so use another quarter of the oil for the second round.
Boil the water and crumble in the stock cube, stirring to dissolve. Then, using a high-speed blender, blitz the silken tofu with the white miso and your stock. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

Heat the rest of the oil in the pan over a medium heat and add the garlic, cooking gently for a couple of minutes until just turning golden. Add the grains (they'll reheat in the stock), chickpeas and your miso tofu mixture, stirring until combined, then simmer for 5 mins. Add most of the mushrooms, saving some for to garnish. Add the lemon zest and squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Serve the creamy grains up topped with the reserved mushrooms and the chives.

name: Creamy Miso Mushroom Pasta
description: This easy, creamy miso mushroom pasta is full of umami. Topped with nori seaweed, spring onions and sesame seeds, it's a Japanese-Italian fusion.
instructions: In a small bowl, add the miso paste and the warm water. Mix well until the miso dissolves. Set aside.
Finley slice the spring onions and cut the nori, if using, into thin ribbons. Pull the mushrooms apart into bite-sized pieces. Mince the garlic.

Add a few tablespoons of olive oil into a large frying pan, over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and garlic with a sprinkle of salt and pepper. Cook, stirring often, for about 10-15 mins, or until the mushrooms have caramelised.
When the mushrooms are done, remove them from the pan and set aside. Add in the butter and let it melt, then sift over the flour and mix well for about 1 min, until it starts to thicken.
Now, add the soy milk and nutritional yeast. Use a rubber whisk and stir until you have no lumps. Add the miso broth and whisk again. Bring to a gentle simmer for a few mins to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, cook the tagliatelle as per the package instructions, until al dente. Drain and save a cup of pasta water.

Add the cooked pasta and mushrooms back into the pan. Gently fold and mix to evenly coat the pasta with the sauce and to warm the mushrooms up again. Add a little pasta water to thin down the sauce if needed. Taste and season well with salt and plenty of pepper.
To serve, ladle the pasta into two pasta bowls, top with spring onions, nori and sesame seeds if using.

name: Creamy Miso Mushroom Pasta
description: The creamiest pasta imaginable. Umami-packed miso, fried mushrooms and cashew cream fill the dairy void and make this a savoury delight. Enjoy Mob. Sophie x
instructions: Pop your cashews in a bowl and cover with cold water. Leave to soak for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Start by making your breadcrumb topping. Finely chop your rosemary and whizz up your rye bread in a food processor.

Heat a small frying pan over a medium heat. Add a generous glug of olive oil and let it come up to temperature. Tip in your breadcrumbs and rosemary, then toast for a few minutes until they are crisp and golden. Set aside.
Drain your cashews from their water, then add to a blender along with 150ml water, the white wine, miso paste and bouillon powder. Blend until you have a very smooth paste.
Prep your veg. Slice your mushrooms, your cavolo nero and garlic.
Cook your pasta in boiling, salted water until al dente, then drain. Remember to reserve your pasta water.
Heat a little olive oil in a large saute pan over a high heat. Add your mushrooms along with a pinch of salt and fry for 5 minutes until they are caramelised and deep in flavour.
Add your cavolo nero and stir fry for a minute until starting to wilt. Tip in your garlic and thyme, and cook for a minute more.

Pour your cashew sauce into the pan and bring it to a simmer. Tip in your cooked pasta along with a good splash of pasta water, and give it all a mix until your pasta is coated in a silky sauce. You may need to add more pasta water to get the sauce to the perfect, glossy consistency.
Add the zest and juice of your lemon and season with salt and pepper.
Serve up with a sprinkle of your crispy crumbs, and enjoy!

name: Creamy Miso Noodle Soup
description: An extremely slurpable noodle soup with roasted shiitake mushrooms, miso broth and jammy eggs for good measure. This one is hearty and nourishing. Perfect for midweek.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.

Tear or slice the mushrooms into 1cm chunks, then spread them out on a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and ½ the soy sauce. Season with black pepper. Slide into the oven to roast for 30-35 mins, flipping halfway, until golden brown.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil, then lower in the eggs and cook for 7 mins. Drain and cool under running water before peeling.
Bring another pan of salted water to the boil. Add the soba noodles and edamame beans and cook following packet instructions. Drain and set aside.

Blitz the silken tofu and water together in a blender until smooth. Pour into a saucepan set over a medium heat and stir in the stock cube. Place the miso in a small sieve and partially submerge it in the soup. Use the back of a teaspoon to stir and dissolve the miso into the soup. Season with soy sauce to taste.
Thinly slice the spring onions.

To serve, divide the noodles and edamame between bowls, then ladle over the miso broth. Halve the eggs and add them to the bowls, along with the roasted mushrooms. Top with spring onions, a drizzle of chilli oil and a sprinkling of sesame seeds.

name: Creamy Miso Noodles with Mushroom Skewers
description: These saucy noodles topped with spicy mushroom skewers are a perfect match. Soba noodles have a delicious nuttiness but feel free to swap for any other noodle.
keywords: Creamy Miso Noodles with Mushroom Skewers
instructions: First make the mushroom marinade. Peel the ginger and add to blender with the soy sauce, half the maple syrup, garlic and a third of the chillis. Blitz until smooth. If you’re using wooden skewers, soak them in water.
Cut the mushrooms into bite sized chunks. Put the mushrooms and the marinade into a shallow bowl and mix well. Set aside. *See Tips for king oyster mushrooms.
Next, make the miso tahini sauce. In a blender, add tahini, sesame oil, white miso, the juice of half the limes, the remaining maple syrup, oat milk. Blitz until smooth and set aside.

Cook the soba noodles according to the packet instructions, stirring a few times to prevent sticking. Drain and run them under cold water, then place in a bowl with a good drizzle of sesame oil to prevent them sticking.

Skewer the mushrooms onto the sticks, finishing with a piece of chilli and spring onion if you like. Griddle the skewers over high heat on a griddle pan, turning frequently, until charred and cooked through.

Slice and wash the pak choi. Heat a saucepan with a drizzle of neutral oil and stir fry the pak choi until just wilted. Add the miso sauce and noodles to the pan and heat through. If the sauce is very thick, add a little water or some more oat milk.
To serve, spoon the noodles into a plate and lay the mushroom skewers on top, with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and a good squeeze of lime.

name: Creamy Miso Tahini Udon
description: A creamy carbonara style-udon in a parmesan, miso, and tahini sauce topped with crispy charred spring onions and mushrooms.
instructions: Chop the spring onions into large chunks and the mushrooms into thick slices.

Cook the spring onions in a large pan on a high heat for 5 mins until charred before removing them and setting them aside. Add in the mushrooms with a big glug of oil and cook for 8-10 mins until browned. Keep the mushrooms in the pan with the heat off.
Separate your egg yolks and whites. In a bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, parmesan, miso paste, tahini, chilli flakes and fresh black pepper. Grate in the ginger and add in the soy sauce.
Cook the udon in boiling water according to package instructions. Ladle in 150ml of the cooking liquid into the egg mixture, whisking continuously so the eggs do not scramble.

With the heat off, add the udon to the mushroom pan before throwing in the spring onions and egg mixture and tossing well to coat the noodles. Next, turn the heat on the lowest setting and continue mixing to create a thick and glossy sauce. Season with salt if needed.
Serve the noodles on a plate with some more parmesan and black pepper. Enjoy

name: Creamy Mushroom & Egg Breakfast Wraps
description: Creamy, savoury mushrooms, fluffy leek-scrambled eggs, fresh spinach and melty mozzarella all bundled into a wrap. Make them ahead and pan-fry when you're ready, meal prep doesn't get much better than this.
keywords: Creamy Parmesan Mushroom & Herby Leek Egg Wraps
Creamy Parmesan Mushroom & Herby Leek Egg Wraps recipe
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the shallot. Thinly slice the mushrooms. Peel and mince the garlic. Pick the thyme leaves and finely chop.

Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the butter and let it melt, then add the shallot and cook for 3-4 mins, stirring, until softened. Add the mushrooms, garlic and thyme, turn the heat up to high and season well with salt and black pepper. Cook for 8-10 mins, stirring often, until the mushrooms are browned and all the liquid has evaporated.

Pour in the chicken stock and sherry vinegar and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 1-2 mins until reduced by about two-thirds. Remove from the heat and stir through the soured cream, then finely grate in half the parmesan and fold through. Season to taste with salt and black pepper. Transfer to a bowl and refrigerate until completely cooled. Wash and reserve the pan.

Finely chop the parsley. Crack the eggs into a large bowl, add the soured cream and parsley, finely grate in the remaining parmesan, season with salt and whisk everything together. Trim the leek, cut in half lengthwise and thinly slice.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in the reserved pan over a medium heat. Add the leek, season with salt and cook for about 8 mins, stirring often, until tender and just starting to colour. Pour in the egg mixture and cook for a further 1 min, briefly stirring every few seconds, until the eggs are scrambled and just cooked through. Season to taste and transfer to a bowl to cool.
Add the baby spinach to a large microwave-safe bowl and microwave on full power for 45 seconds, until completely wilted. Drain off any excess liquid. Drain the mozzarella and tear into small chunks.

Lay out the tortillas and divide the creamy mushrooms, herby leek eggs, wilted spinach and mozzarella between them. Wrap each one up tightly, then wrap in foil or baking paper. Store in the fridge for up to three days. Serve cold, or pan-fry over a medium-low heat until warmed through and lightly crisp on the outside.

name: Creamy Mushroom 'No Chicken' Pasta
description: A beautifully indulgent plant-based pasta. The creaminess comes from walnuts, which also impart a brilliant depth of flavour here.
instructions: Add your walnuts to a saucepan along with the water. Bring to a boil, then gently simmer for 10 mins.
Drain your walnuts, then add them to a blender with your soy milk. Whizz until you have a totally smooth sauce.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil, then your veggie chicken pieces. Fry for 5 mins until golden, then remove from the pan and set aside.
Finely slice your mushrooms, shallots and garlic. Finely chop half of your sage.
Add a generous glug of olive oil to the same frying pan. Add your whole sage leaves, and fry for 2 mins until crispy and fragrant. Lift out of the pan with a slotted spoon, reserving the oil.
Working in a few batches to avoid overcrowding, add your mushrooms to the pan and fry for 5 mins over a medium-high heat until they are reduced and golden. Lift out of the pan.
Fill a large saucepan with water, then bring to a boil.
Add a little more olive oil to the pan, then add your shallots. Fry for 10 mins until soft.
Salt your water generously, then add your pasta to your boiling water, and cook until al dente.
Get your garlic and chopped sage in the shallot pan and cook for 2 mins more. Add your veggie chicken pieces, mushrooms and walnut cream sauce, then bring the whole mixture to a gentle simmer.
Add a ladle of pasta water along with your pasta, then give the whole thing a good mix. Add more pasta water if needed to get it really silky. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon into bowls, then garnish with your crispy sage leaves. Serve and enjoy!

name: Creamy Mushroom Gnocchi Soup with Rocket Pesto
description: A hearty plant-based soup with pillowy gnocchi in a peppery creamy broth, topped with a fresh rocket and parsley pesto. Proper nourishing food to keep you warm this winter.
keywords: Creamy Mushroom Gnocchi Soup with Rocket Pesto
Creamy Mushroom Gnocchi Soup with Rocket Pesto recipe
instructions: Finely chop the onion, mince the garlic and slice the mushrooms.

Melt the butter in a medium sized pot. Add the black pepper and cook on medium heat for a couple of minutes. Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring, for another minute before adding the mushrooms. Season with salt and turn the heat up slightly. Cook for 8-10 mins until fragrant and soft, then add the wine and allow the alcohol to evaporate fully.

Pour in the soya cream and water and add the stock cube. Drop in the thyme sprigs and bring to a gentle simmer. Add the wholegrain mustard, then remove 2-3 ladles of the soup and place in a blender. Blend until smooth and then return it to the pot.

Add the gnocchi and cook for another 5 mins or until the gnocchi has softened. Remove the thyme and discard. Add the vegan cream cheese, if using, and stir to melt through. Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry frying pan.

To make the pesto, finely chop the rocket and parsley and add to a small bowl or pestle and mortar. Add the toasted sunflower seeds, zest and juice of the lemon, nutritional yeast, salt and pepper and enough olive oil to achieve a drizzly consistency (about a tbsp per portion). Taste and adjust the seasonings and lightly crush the sunflower seeds if you like.
To serve, divide the soup into bowls and spoon over the pesto generously. Finish with some black pepper and some extra lemon zest.

name: Creamy Mushroom Miso Udon
description: An easy but decadent creamy vegetarian udon, full of umami from the miso paste and gooey soft-boiled egg. Pro tip: toast the sesame seeds and slightly crush in a pestle and mortar.
instructions: Finely mince the garlic cloves, finely dice the shallot, chop the mushrooms into thin slices, and slice the spring onions as finely as possible. Set everything aside.

Bring a saucepan of water to the boil over a high heat. Once boiling, add the eggs, gently, and set a timer for 6 mins. Get a bowl of ice-cold water ready. Once cooked, remove the eggs and transfer to the bowl of cold water.
Add the udon to the same saucepan of boiling water, then cook for 3 mins until the noodles have fully separated. Drain and set aside. Peel the eggs and slice in half, then set aside.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat for 2 mins. Add 2 tbsp olive oil to the pan, then the mushrooms. Fry for 5 mins, stirring occasionally (they should be golden). Add the garlic, shallots and butter, then fry for 1 min.
Add the mirin, soy sauce, cream and miso paste. Stir to incorporate. Add the udon and stir for 30 seconds. If the sauce is too dry, add a splash of water.
Plate up the udon, cover with sesame seeds, top with the sliced spring onion and add the egg. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Nori Noodles
description: Creamy and full of umami, this is a quick and fresh lunch box base that you can top with whatever you like.
instructions: Fill a saucepan with water and bring to the boil. Once boiling, cook the noodles following pack instructions. Once cooked, give them a good wash under cold running water.

Add the tahini, nori sheet, soy sauce, ice and rice vinegar into a blender. Whizz until creamy and the nori has been fully incorporated into the dressing. Season with salt and a touch of sugar, if too bitter.
Toss the dressing through the noodles and top with whatever protein you'd like.

name: Creamy Parm Egg Bagel with Bacon
description: The silkiest scrambled eggs. Loaded with parmesan cheese and layered on top of a cream cheese bagel, this is about as indulgent as it gets.
instructions: Whisk together the eggs and good grinding of black pepper. Toast your bagels.
Put your bacon into a non-stick pan with a small glug of oil, cook for 10 mins until very crispy. Take the bacon out and set it aside on some paper towels. Clean the pan and remove the oil.
Put the heat on a low setting and add in the butter and your eggs – don’t add any salt at this point.
Turn the eggs very gently in the pan, grating in parmesan as you fold them so the cheese is all gently layered in. Keep this on a very low heat for 5 mins until it's just set.
Schmear the bagels with a thick layer of cream cheese.
Chop up the bacon into small pieces along with your parsley.
Top the bagel with your scrambled egg, bacon, parsley and sprinkle of flaky sea salt.

name: Creamy Parsnip, Chestnut & Mustard Gratin
description: The only way you’ll want to cook parsnips from now on. This bubbling gratin with chopped chestnuts and a nutmeg and garlic cream is the easiest, most delicious Christmas side dish.
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Grease an oven-proof baking dish (approx 23 x 23cm) with ⅓ the butter.
Peel the parsnips, remove any especially big or woody cores and slice into even sized batons.
Bring a large pan of well salted water to the boil over a medium-high heat. Add the parsnips and boil for 3-4 mins then drain. Leave the parsnips to steam dry in a colander for 5 mins.

Meanwhile, roughly chop the chestnuts into 1-2cm pieces and add to a mixing bowl. Pour in the cream and spoon in the mustard. Finely grate in the garlic and nutmeg (at least ½ tsp for 4 people). Season generously with salt and plenty of black pepper and mix well to combine.
Transfer the parsnips to the gratin dish. Pour over the seasoned cream mix and dot the top with tiny bits of the remaining butter. Pop in the oven to bake for 20 mins until bubbling.
Remove the gratin from the oven and set to one side for at least 5 mins before serving.

name: Creamy Peanut & Courgette Chicken Noodles
description: Summer to me is synonymous with satay - there's nothing better than chowing down on a skewer under the roasting sun. This recipe is inspired by some of the flavours you find in the peanut sauce that I grew up having with my satay. Mix that with some summer produce and some noodles to make a quick dinner or lunch.
cuisine: Thai, Thai-Inspired, Asian-Inspired, Malaysian, Malaysian-Inspired, Pan-Asian, Indonesian-Inspired
keywords: Creamy Peanut & Courgette Chicken Noodles recipe
instructions: Chop the chicken breast into 2-3cm chunks. Add into a bowl with the olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss together.
Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions, then wash under cold water to cool down and drain fully.
Using a peeler, shave the courgette into long ribbons. Halve the tomatoes and season with salt. Pick the coriander leaves.
Add the peanut butter, sweet chilli and soy for the dressing into a bowl and stir together, then season with the juice of the lime. Add a splash of water to loosen it if it's too thick.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 5-7 mins, until golden and cooked through. Stir the remaining sweet chilli through until glossy, then toss the tomatoes and half the sesame seeds through.

Toss the noodles and courgette through the dressing and share into boxes or bowls. Top with the chicken mixture, the coriander and the remaining sesame seeds. Cut the remaining lime into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Creamy Pickle Dip
description: Take those half jars of pickles and last bits of herbs and create this delicious pickle dip topped with buttery onions. Best served with crispbreads.
instructions:
Peel, halve and finely slice the onions into half moons, then add them into a frying pan with 2 tbsp of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Cook on medium heat for 10-15 mins until soft and golden. Once cooked, add the butter in to melt and turn off the heat. Alternatively, I like to put the onions in a bowl with a pinch of salt and the oil, cover with cling film and microwave them for 6-8 minutes, stirring regularly until very soft, then adding them to a pan on a medium heat for the last few minutes until golden.
(If using spring onion, roughly chop them then add to the pan with the oil and salt, but cook on medium/high for 4-5 minutes until soft but slightly golden, adding the butter at the end to melt).
Zest the lemon. In a bowl, add 2 tbsp of mayo, 4 tbsp of the yoghurt, ½ of your chopped herbs, roughly chopped pickles, the juice of ½ a lemon, plus a good pinch of flakey sea salt and pepper.
Spoon over the onions with the melted butter and finish with the remaining herbs, lemon zest and some freshly cracked black pepper. Serve with a pile of crispbreads for scooping.

name: Creamy Prawn Gochujang Noodles
description: Chuck away those salty, powdered sachets that come with instant noodles and make this deliciously rich and saucy alternative instead!
instructions: Slice the garlic and chop the chives as finely as possible.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat for around 1 min. Add the olive oil and sliced garlic, then sauté for 1 min until soft but not coloured. Add the gochujang, bashing and stirring the paste to infuse into the oil until it gives off a reddish hue. Add the double cream, then stir well to make a smooth paste free from lumps.
Add the prawns and mascarpone, then cook for 2 mins or until the prawns turn pink. Turn the heat off.

Heat the water in a saucepan over a high heat until boiling. Once boiling, cook the noodles for 1 min shy of the cooking time stated on the pack. Drain the noodles, reserving 1/5 of the cooking water.

Turn the heat under the prawns back to medium. Add the cooked noodles, chives and the reserved noodle water. Mix for 1 min to coat the noodles with the sauce. Add more cooking water if it’s too dry – the sauce should be smooth and slightly runny.
Plate up, shaking the plate slightly to spread the noodles. Grate a generous amount of Parmesan on top. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Pumpkin Curry
description: This vegetarian curry is so simple and one of the most delicious things you can do with a pumpkin. Serve it over our favourite rice, Tilda Pure Basmati.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C/375°F.

Peel your pumpkin, cut in half lengthways, then into ½ inch wedges. Place in a baking tray with ½ tsp of your chilli powder, half of your cumin, a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt. Mix with your hands, then roast in the oven for 30-40 mins until tender and starting to caramelise. You want to get nice charring on the edges here.
Dice your onion and finely chop your garlic and ginger.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large saute pan. Add your cardamom pods and cinnamon stick and cook over a medium heat until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Tip your onion into the pan and lower the heat. Cook for about 20 mins until totally soft and caramelised. Add your ginger and garlic and cook out for a couple of mins until starting to turn golden.
Pour your passata into the pan along with your remaining cumin and chilli powder, then bring to a boil. Simmer for 20 mins until reduced and jammy.
Meanwhile, heat up your Tilda rice according to packet instructions.
Add your garam masala and honey to the pan and simmer for another 5 mins.
Add your coconut yoghurt to the pan, season to taste and simmer for another 5 mins. Add your roasted pumpkin and stir to combine.
Serve on top of rice with coriander to garnish. Enjoy.

name: Creamy Pumpkin Risotto with Caramelised Pecans
description: Your leftover Halloween pumpkin need not go to waste. Transform it into a creamy risotto topped with sticky maple pecans for an incredible dinner.
keywords: Creamy pumpkin risotto with caramelised pecans recipes
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C.
Peel your pumpkin and scoop out the seeds. Slice then dice it into cubes.
Toss your pumpkin into a tray and drizzle it with olive oil and salt. Roast for 45 mins until tender and starting to caramelise.
Finely dice your onion and finely chop your garlic cloves. Finely chop about half of your sage.

Heat your butter with a glug of olive oil in a large sauté pan. Add your remaining sage leaves whole and fry for about 3 mins until crisp - your butter will brown a little in this time, but that’s okay.
Lift out your sage with a spoon and save until later.
Tip your onion into the brown butter and cook gently for 15 mins until softened. Add your garlic, chilli flakes and chopped sage, then cook out for 2 mins.
Add your risotto rice and lightly toast it in the butter for a few mins until the grains start to turn translucent. Add your white wine and give the mixture a stir.

Once your rice has absorbed the wine, gradually add your stock in small increments. Stir all the while to allow your rice grains to absorb the stock before adding more liquid. It should take about 25 mins for all your stock to be added and your rice to be tender.
Meanwhile, reduce oven temp to 180°C.

Roughly chop your pecans, then toss them in a baking dish. Pour over your maple syrup and a pinch of salt, then toss to combine. Pop the dish in the oven and cook for 15 mins, stirring halfway through.
Mash your pumpkin in its roasting tray with a potato masher. It doesn’t need to be super smooth, but get it to a rough purée.
Grate the parmesan. Add your pumpkin to your risotto along with most of your parmesan. Give it a mix, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon your risotto into bowls and top with a drizzle of olive oil, crispy sage leaves, a little parmesan and your pecans. Serve and enjoy.

name: Creamy Quorn Sausage and Broccoli Pasta
description: Plant-based creamy pasta lovers need not miss out. Packed with herbs, lemon zest and crispy chunks of Quorn Brilliant Bangers, this one’s a total winner.
keywords: Creamy quorn sausage and broccoli pasta recipes
instructions: Finely slice your onion. Finely chop your garlic. Chop the tough ends off your broccoli, then chop in half.
Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil.
Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat, then add a glug of olive oil. Add your onion and gently fry for 10 mins until just softened.
Crumble your Quorn Brilliant Bangers into the pan, and fry for another 10 mins until they have crispy, caramelised edges and the onions are starting to darken too.
Add your silken tofu to a blender, then blitz to a smooth liquid.
Pick your thyme leaves into the pan, then add your chopped garlic. Cook for another 2 mins.
Pour in your wine and let it evaporate. Pour in your silken tofu and vegetable stock, then bring to a simmer. Cook gently for 10 mins.
Add your pappardelle to your salted water pan, and cook for 5 mins.
Once your 5 mins are up, add your broccoli and cook for 3 more mins. Finely chop your parsley.

Add the miso paste and a mugful of pasta water to your sauce, then drain your pasta and broccoli. Tip this into the pan, along with your chopped parsley. Zest in your lemon and add a good twist of black pepper, then give it a good mix.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Tong your pasta onto plates, then top with olive oil and black pepper. Serve and enjoy.

name: Creamy Red Pesto Sausage Pasta
description: Pesto pasta, but better. This healthy, high-protein pasta recipe has got a lot going for it. Expect superb Italian flavours in every forkful.
instructions: Finely dice the onion and bring a saucepan of salty water to the boil.

Heat a spray of oil in a separate large pan and add the onion over a low-medium heat. De-skin the sausages by making a shallow cut lengthwise down one side of the sausage with a sharp knife and pulling the skin off. Add the de-skinned sausages to the pan and break up with a spatula. Alternatively, you can use your fingers like they are scissors and pull around 2.5cm of sausage at a time out of the casing and into the pan. Increase the heat and cook for around 5 mins until cooked through.
Meanwhile, tip the pasta into the boiling water.
Add the garlic Italian seasoning, basil and paprika to the sausage pan, followed by the tomato purée and pesto. Stir to coat, then pour in the cream and a ladle of pasta water to thicken.

Leave to simmer for a few minutes until it thickens, then add the cooked and drained pasta, along with some extra pasta water to loosen it up if necessary. Share between three bowls and top with chopped basil and parsley.

name: Creamy Roast Chicken & Chickpeas with Sage & Lemon
description: Golden chicken thighs with the most comforting creamy chickpeas and a lemony herby sauce — all done in one pan. This is the perfect kid friendly dinner that the whole family will love.
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsHeat the oven to 180°C.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Add it skin-side down to a cold large frying pan, then set it over a medium heat. Let it cook for 10–12 mins until golden and crispy, then flip and cook for another 2 mins. Remove the chicken and set aside. Spoon out most of the fat, leaving about 2 Tbsp in the pan.
Pick and finely chop the sage leaves and peel and finely chop the garlic.
Tip the sofrito mix into the pan with the chopped garlic and sage. Scrape up any brown bits from the bottom of the pan and cook to soften, 5 mins.
Dump the chickpeas with their liquid straight into the pan. Finely grate over the lemon zest, add the stock pot and 150ml water. Bring up the to simmer.
Nestle the chicken back into the pan, skin-side up, and transfer to the oven. Bake for 45 mins until the chicken is golden and falling away from the bone.

Once out of the oven, lift out the chicken and stir the crème fraîche through the chickpeas. Portion out the kids plate (if they don’t like lemon) then fold in the spinach and squeeze over the lemon juice for the adults.

Serve up!Kids Plate: Spoon the beans onto one side of the plate. Cut the chicken from the bone and add to the plate. Serve with some cucumber slicesParents Plate: Dish out the beans and chicken and top with the crispy sage. Season well with pepper.

name: Creamy Roasted Pepper Chickpeas
description: Creamy, smoky, and packed with plant-based protein. This one-pan chickpea dish gets a silky boost from whipped silken tofu and roasted peppers — perfect for an easy weeknight dinner that still feels a bit fancy.
instructions: Finely slice the garlic. Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Roughly chop the roasted peppers and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Add the spinach to a colander in the sink and pour over two full kettles of boiling water until wilted. Set aside to drain.

Add the roasted peppers to a blender with the silken tofu, half the red chilli, and the juice of the lemon. Season generously with salt and pepper, then blitz until smooth. Finely slice the remaining chilli.

Heat a splash of the olive oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 3–4 mins until just starting to soften. Add the remaining oil along with the garlic and smoked paprika, and cook for another 2 mins until fragrant.
Tip in the chickpeas and pour over the roasted pepper sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 mins, then stir through the spinach until heated through. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Serve up in bowls, scattered with the sliced red chilli and fresh parsley.

name: Creamy Roasted Tomato & ‘Bacon’ Gochujang Pasta
description: This tomato gochujang pasta recipe blends bold flavours with a satisfying texture, offering a dish that’s both comforting and distinct. The tofu 'bacon' brings a smoky, savoury kick, while the gochujang-infused sauce creates a rich, spicy-sweet creaminess. To top it off, roasted cherry tomatoes add a refreshing burst of flavour, perfectly balancing the pasta's robust sauce.
instructions: Put all the marinade ingredients in a bowl and whisk together, then set aside. Drain the tofu from its water and pat dry to remove excess moisture. Chop the tofu into ½cm bite-sized pieces. Tip the cubes into the marinade, then mix to evenly coat. Set aside.
Heat your air fryer to 190°C. Slice the tomatoes in half and sprinkle with salt and drizzle with olive oil. Roast for 12-15 mins using the roast function.

Meanwhile, heat a drizzle of olive oil in a non-stick pan over a low-medium heat. Add the tofu pieces along with the remaining marinade. Let the tofu fry for around 8 mins, tossing now and then, until the pieces are slightly caramelised.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the garlic. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a low-medium heat, then add the garlic and lightly fry for 1 min until fragrant. Add the tomato purée and gochujang, then stir well and cook for 1 min. Add the soy milk, turn the heat to low and simmer for 5-8 mins. Squeeze the lime juice and add the maple syrup, stir again and turn off the heat.
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and add the pasta. Once it’s al dente, drain and reserve a mug of cooking water.
Combine the pasta with the gochujang sauce, ¾ of the roasted tomatoes and ¾ of the ‘bacon’ tofu pieces. If you feel like the pasta needs water, add a splash of the reserved pasta water.
Plate up the pasta, then top with the remaining cherry tomatoes, the remaining ‘bacon’ pieces, chopped coriander (if using) and a crack of black pepper.

name: Creamy Rose Harissa Spaghetti
description: Why more people are not coating their spaghetti in spicy harissa paste, tonnes of herbs and creamy mascarpone we do not know. So flavoursome. So saucy.
instructions: Thinly slice your garlic and finely chop your onion.

Cook your onion in the oil from the sundried tomatoes jar on a medium heat for 5 mins until softened. Turn the heat to low and add in your garlic and cumin seeds. Cook for another 5 mins until slightly golden.
Meanwhile, blend up the sundried tomatoes.
Add in the harissa paste and cook on a medium heat for 5 mins until the colour is darkened and the oil is stained red.
Meanwhile, pop you spaghetti in some heavily salted boiling water and cook until al dente, 7 mins.
Add tomato puree to the pan and cook with the harissa until the pasta is ready. It should turn a dark brown colour. Then add in the sun-dried tomatoes.
Meanwhile finely chop the parsley.
Add in 250ml of pasta water and mascarpone and mix well. Then add in the cooked spaghetti and cook for a further 2 mins tossing well so the pasta is fully cooked and coated well in the sauce.
Stir in the parsley and season to taste. Serve up in your bowls and enjoy.

name: Creamy Salmon Pasta Salad
description: The perfect summery pasta with barely any cooking! The peas go in frozen, chilling the whole dish as they thaw. It's seriously genius. Plus it's great for meal prep.
ingredients: 320g Honey Roast Hot Smoked Salmon Fillet
instructions: Get a large saucepan of well-salted water on to boil and add the pasta. Cook according to packet instructions, then drain, rinse under cold water and leave to drain off any excess water.

Finely chop the dill and add to a large bowl with the cooked pasta, crème fraîche and frozen petit pois - no need to defrost, they'll thaw in the salad. Zest and juice both lemons into the bowl, then add the capers. Break the salmon into flakes and add to the bowl. Mix well, seasoning generously with salt and black pepper.
To serve, divide between containers and top each with an extra grind of black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil, if you like. Pop in the fridge, ready to grab for lunch.

name: Creamy Salmon Pasta Salad
description: The perfect summery pasta with barely any cooking! The peas go in frozen, chilling the whole dish as they thaw. It's seriously genius.
ingredients: 320g Honey Roast Hot Smoked Salmon Fillet
instructions: Get a large saucepan of well-salted water on to boil and add the pasta. Cook according to packet instructions, then drain, rinse under cold water and leave to drain off any excess water.

Finely chop the dill and add to a large bowl with the cooked pasta, crème fraîche and frozen petit pois - no need to defrost, they'll thaw in the salad. Zest and juice both lemons into the bowl, then add the capers. Break the salmon into flakes and add to the bowl. Mix well, seasoning generously with salt and black pepper.

name: Creamy Sausage and Squash Gnocchi
description: Roast squash and caramelised sausage coming together to form one of the all time great gnocchi dishes. A hug in a bowl. Your MOB are going to love it.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C.
Peel your butternut squash and chop it into 1 inch cubes.

Place into a roasting tin with a drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper and toss with your hands to coat. Roast for 30 minutes until tender and caramelised, turning every so often to ensure they cook evenly.
Whilst your squash cooks, finely chop your onion, garlic and rosemary.

Heat a small glug of olive oil in a small frying pan. Add half of your chilli flakes and rosemary along with your panko breadcrumbs and fry for a few minutes until golden, crispy and smelling glorious. Set aside.

Heat a little olive oil in a large frying pan and add the meat from your sausages. Fry over a medium-high heat for 5 mins until cooked and golden, breaking up with the back of your spoon so you get lots of individual chunks.

Add your onion to the pan and turn down the heat to medium. Fry for 10 minutes until softened, then add your garlic, the rest of your rosemary, your remaining chilli flakes and fennel seeds. Cook for another 2 minutes.

Add your chicken stock and bring to a simmer, then tip in your gnocchi and simmer for 5 minutes. Give your mixture a good stir, then add your butternut squash, mascarpone and parmesan to the pan. Stir to combine, then season to taste.
Serve with a sprinkling of your breadcrumbs and a little more parmesan.

name: Creamy Sausage, Bacon and Brussels Sprout Tagliatelle
description: This gorgeous pasta uses up all your leftover Christmas dinner bits. We're talking sausage, bacon, sprouts, and even the cream from your Christmas pudding.
keywords: Best ways of using leftover Christmas dinner
bacon and brussels sprouts tagliatelle recipe
instructions: Place a large pot of well-salted water onto a boil.
Slice the bacon into ¼ inch thick strips, add to a large pan on a medium heat.
After a few mins, crumble the sausage onto your pan. At this point, add your pasta to the pot of boiling water.

Finely slice the Brussels sprouts and add to your pan. Cook for 4-5 mins until the sausage and bacon is turning golden brown and the sprouts have some good colour. Deglaze with a splash of white wine.
Reduce the heat to low, add the cream, a tsp of black pepper and half a mug of the pasta cooking water.
Drain the pasta (saving another mug of the water) and add to the pan. Toss well, adding more water as needed to create a thick, glossy sauce.
Plate up and serve with grated parmesan and a little more black pepper.

name: Creamy Sesame & Crispy Chilli Dressing
description: A silky tahini dressing with garlic, ginger and lime, finished with crispy chilli oil for heat, crunch and serious flavour.
instructions: Add the tahini to a bowl. Peel and finely grate the garlic and ginger straight in. Squeeze in the lime juice, add the honey and water, then whisk until smooth and creamy. Taste and season with salt.
For a marbled finish, pour the crispy chilli oil over the top and leave it untouched. Otherwise, stir it through for a fully mixed sauce.

name: Creamy Sichuan Soy Noodles
description: Loosely inspired by dan dan noodles and the viral tofu noodles, these creamy noodles are topped with a numbing soy mince for a high protein, meat-free dinner. I like to make the mince in a big batch and eat it throughout the week.
instructions: Soak the dried soy mince in boiling water for 5 mins, then drain. Finely grind the Sichuan peppercorns in a spice grinder or high-speed processor, or use a pestle and mortar if you have one. Add the silken tofu to a blender with the tahini, blitz until smooth and season with salt, then set aside. Finely chop the garlic and ginger and thinly slice the spring onions.

Heat a glug of neutral oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the garlic, ginger and most of the spring onions, cooking for a couple of minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Add the drained soy mince, ground cumin and ground Sichuan pepper and cook for another 30 seconds, then pour in the balsamic vinegar and light soy sauce.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and cook the udon noodles according to the packet instructions, then drain, reserving a mugful of the cooking water. Toss the noodles through the silken tofu, loosening with the reserved water if you need to. Finely chop the chives.
Serve the noodles topped with the soy mince, the chives, the remaining spring onions and a spoonful of chilli oil, if you fancy.

name: Creamy Spiced Chickpeas with Mango Salsa & Crispy Tofu
description: Chickpeas were the first legume I ever cooked with. They’re easy, versatile and cheap, while high in protein, fibre and complex carbs. This simple creamy sauce has just the right amount of spice for a quick weeknight meal, paired with the mango salsa for freshness and crispy tofu for extra protein and crunch. It’s the perfect harmony of delicious meets practical and healthy.
keywords: Creamy Spiced Chickpeas with Mango Salsa & Crispy Tofu
instructions: Start with the mango salsa, so the flavours can mingle while you prep the rest. Finely chop the red onion, mango flesh, chilli, red pepper and coriander leaves, then add to a mixing bowl with the juice of a lime and pinch of salt. Season to taste, adding a little more lime for zingyness or more salt for strength of flavour.

For the chickpeas, finely dice the onion, peel and crush the garlic, then peel and finely chop or grate the fresh ginger. Measure out all your spices, so they’re ready to go. If your chickpeas are not organic, drain and rinse them.

Add a splash of olive oil to a large, wide-sided sauté pan. When a piece of onion sizzles on contact, tip the rest in and fry over a low-medium heat with a pinch of sea salt for 8 mins. Add the garlic and ginger, then fry for 3-4 mins until the raw aroma subsides. Add a little more olive oil, then tip all the spices in and stir to gently cover the aromatics in them. Everything should be smelling fantastic at this point.

Add the tomato purée, mix well, then add all the chickpeas and their water (or the additional 100ml water if you drained and rinsed the chickpeas). Season to taste (some chickpea water is already quite salty, so do bear that in mind).

Add the silken tofu, nutritional yeast, cashews, a couple of spoons of the chickpea mix and the lemon juice to a blender. Blend together and season to taste. I usually add another pinch of salt. Pour this into the chickpeas and stir to combine. Take it off the heat and leave to stand while you prep the firm tofu.
Take the tofu out of the pack and give it a good squeeze, wrapped in a piece of kitchen paper. Crumble it into a medium mixing bowl with your hands, so it resembles chunky breadcrumbs.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a non-stick pan, then fry the tofu for 6-8 mins, stirring regularly, until it goes a medium shade of light-ish yellow. Add the tamari, fry until it turns deep brown (this may take up to 10 mins) then pour a little more olive oil in the pan and add the garlic and ginger. Fry until everything is well coated and the raw aroma of the garlic and ginger has subsided.

Heat the chickpeas through gently, season to taste, then plate up chickpeas first, then tofu crumble, then soy yoghurt, salsa, fresh coriander and nigella seeds (if you have them). Eat with a warm flatbread or sourdough toast.

name: Creamy Spiced Rice with Crispy Soy & Sesame Mushrooms
description: If you're a fan of meaty mushrooms, umami soy, and creamy rice, this recipe should be right up your street. Enjoy.
keywords: Creamy spiced rice with crispy soy and sesame mushrooms
instructions: Put the butter in a lidded saucepan and melt over a low heat. Add the chilli flakes, garam masala and turmeric, then toast for 1-2 mins. Add the rice and stir to coat.
Add the water, 2/3 of the coconut milk and the stock cube, then stir well. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to low and cook for 10 mins with the lid on.
Pop the spinach on top of the rice, stir well and replace the lid. Leave to steam for 10 mins.

Add the boiling water and the remaining coconut milk to a measuring jug, then pour this mixture into the pan to achieve an almost soupy consistency. Stir and season well with plenty of salt and black pepper.

Meanwhile, make the mushrooms. Tear them apart into thick strips. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and add the mushrooms. Cook over a high heat for 8-12 mins, stirring often, until golden and caramelised. Add the sesame seeds and soy sauce and stir-fry for another 2 mins until the soy sauce is absorbed.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Creamy Spiced Spinach Chickpeas
description: A creamy chickpea dish bursting with greens and spices. A healthy vegetarian crowdpleaser inspired by the flavours of a spinach fatayer.
instructions: Add all the spinach into a bowl and microwave for 4 mins, until defrosted. Squeeze the liquid out into a separate bowl and set aside. Add ½ of the spinach to a blender with the olive oil and 30ml of water from the spinach. Blitz until smooth.
Peel and finely dice the onions and thinly slice the garlic.

Add a drizzle of olive oil into a frying pan, increase the heat to medium-high and stir-fry the onions for 3-5 mins until softened and browning. Add the sumac, garlic and 7-spice and cook for a couple of seconds. Stir through the chickpeas and their liquid and the remaining spinach, cook until piping hot. Take off the heat and stir through the blended spinach.
Crumble over the feta and dollop the Greek yoghurt. Garnish with chilli flakes and fried onions. Serve with flatbreads.

name: Creamy Spicy Pork Ramen
description: If you like spicy noodles and slurping up soup, this one's for you. We’ve used oat milk to create a rich and creamy broth. It’s a great weekly staple that’s super easy to make without much prep.
instructions: Bring a saucepan filled with water to the boil. Once boiling add the spinach leaves and blanch for 30 seconds, stirring regularly. Remove the spinach and transfer to a bowl of ice cold water. Set aside.
To the same pan of water, add the beansprouts and blanch for 2 mins. Remove and set aside. Turn the heat off and set the pan and water aside to cook the noodles in later.

For the pork mince: finely mince the garlic clove and spring onion, separating the whites and greens. Heat a glug of sesame oil in a saucepan over a high heat for about a minute. Add the pork mince and fry for about 3 mins until browned, breaking the mince into small pieces with a spoon as you go. Add the doubanjiang, light soy sauce, white sugar, MSG, minced garlic, the spring onion whites and a pinch of salt and black pepper. Fry for a further 1-2 mins. Transfer everything to a bowl and set aside.

For the broth: to the same pan, add the chicken stock, oat milk, light soy sauce, mirin, MSG and a pinch of salt and black pepper. Bring to a boil over a high heat with the lid off. Simmer for 5 mins or until reduced by a quarter. Add the chilli oil and reduce the heat to lowest, set aside while we cook the noodles. Season to taste (it should be slightly overly salty).
Bring the pot of water used to cook the spinach back to a boil. Once boiling, cook the noodles a minute shy of the pack instructions, then drain and divide between bowls.
Ladle the broth over the noodles so they’re submerged. Add a handful of beansprouts and top them with a large spoonful of pork mince, then serve some spinach and the spring onion greens on the side.

name: Creamy Spinach & Miso Orecchiette
description: Peas are the forgotten hero of this pasta sauce. They’re delicious little protein packed balls that are cheap, long lasting in the freezer and quick to prepare.
instructions: Cook your pasta until it’s al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water, then drain and set aside.

Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic. Heat a medium-sized pan or pot with a drizzle of olive oil on medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes if using and cook for 1 min, stirring constantly. Add the spinach, peas and a pinch of salt and pepper, and cook for about another 2 mins until wilted.

Take the pan off the heat and remove half of the spinach mix and add it to a blender. Add about ¼ of a cup of reserved pasta water to the blender along with the miso, 1 tbsp vegan cream cheese and 1 tbsp of olive oil. Blend until smooth and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Tip the cooked pasta and sauce into the pan along with the spinach and pea mix. Gently heat through with a few splashes of pasta water until combined into a silky sauce.
Serve into bowls and top with more vegan cream cheese, plenty of pepper and some extra chilli flakes and a drizzle of olive oil if you like.

name: Creamy Spinach & Pea Orzo with Cod
description: Soft orzo, flaky cod, sweet peas and zingy herbs all in one pan. Light, bright, and packed with protein.
keywords: Creamy Spinach & Pea Orzo with Cod
Creamy Spinach & Pea Orzo with Cod recipe
instructions: Finely chop the dill and parsley, reserving a few leaves for garnish. Peel and finely dice the shallots and garlic.
Set a large lidded frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Once hot, add the shallots and garlic, seasoning generously, and cook for 3 mins until soft and translucent.
Tip in the orzo and stir to coat. Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 -10 mins, stirring occasionally.
Add the spinach and peas to the pan and mix through until wilted.

Add your chopped herbs to the orzo, stirring to combine. Then season the cod fillets with salt and pepper, then nestle them into the orzo. Cover with a lid and cook on low for 4–5 mins, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily and the orzo is al dente.
Squeeze over the juice of half the lemon and stir gently. Taste and season as needed.
Serve the orzo in bowls, top with the cod, a dollop of yoghurt, the reserved herbs and the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

name: Creamy Spinach Lentils with Burst Tomatoes
description: Creamy, herby lentils with silky spinach and sweet burst tomatoes. It's a bowl of comfort that's actually full of fibre and greens. Perfect for an easy midweek dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add the cherry tomatoes to a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season well with salt and black pepper. Slide into the oven to roast for 15 mins, or until the tomatoes are soft, blistered and starting to burst.
Meanwhile, pour boiling water over the spinach in a sieve set in the sink. Once fully wilted, leave to cool slightly, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can and set aside.
Finely chop the shallots and garlic. Pick the thyme leaves from the stems. Drain and rinse the lentils.

Heat another drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the shallots and garlic with a pinch of salt and cook for 5 to 7 mins, until soft and translucent. Add the thyme leaves and cook for another couple of minutes until fragrant.

Tip the lentils into the pan and stir to warm through, then add the spinach. Pour in the double cream and let everything gently bubble into a loose, creamy sauce. Taste and adjust with salt and black pepper.
Spoon the creamy lentils onto plates and finish with the burst tomatoes on top. Get stuck in!

name: Creamy Squash & Sausage Pasta
description: A simple sausage and squash pasta recipe that it's practically impossible to mess up.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Peel the squash and dice into 1cm pieces. Add to a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil, then season with salt and pepper before roasting in the oven for 20-25 mins, until soft and golden. Remove from the oven and allow to cool.

Finely chop the sage and grate the garlic, then get a large pot of salted water on to boil. For the sauce, heat olive oil in a pan over a medium heat. Score the sausage casings and remove the meat, adding to the pan as you go. Fry whilst breaking it up with a spoon, until caramelised, around 5 mins. Then add in the fennel seeds, sage and garlic cooking for another minute. Pour in the white wine and simmer until reduced, then add the cream, simmering for around 3 mins until thickened.
Add your pasta to the boiling water and cook for 1-2 mins less than the package instructions. Reserve a big mug of pasta water and drain, and grate the Parmesan.

Add the pasta and a big splash of pasta water to the sauce and increase the heat to high. Stir rapidly until the sauce coats the pasta, around 2 mins. Take the pan off the heat and add the Parmesan and squash, mixing to coat in the sauce.
Serve up in bowls topped with more Parm and a grating of nutmeg, if using.

name: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta Salad
description: A creamy, high-protein pasta that’s fresh, tangy, and super simple. Cottage cheese makes it smooth while keeping it light and filling.
keywords: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta Salad recipe
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta according to the packet instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving a splash of the pasta water, and leave to cool slightly. Finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes and garlic.
While the pasta cooks, heat the sun-dried tomato oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes, cooking gently for 1–2 mins until fragrant.
Pop the spinach into a colander or sieve and pour over two kettles of boiling water to wilt it. Squeeze out any excess moisture.

Stir the cottage cheese, pasta, wilted spinach, and most of the basil through the sun-dried tomato mix. Add a splash of the reserved pasta water if needed to loosen, and season well with salt and pepper.
Serve topped with Parmesan shavings and the remaining basil.

name: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta Salad
description: A creamy, high-protein pasta that’s perfect for meal prep. Cottage cheese makes it smooth while keeping it light and filling.
keywords: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta Salad recipe
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta according to the packet instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving a splash of the pasta water, and leave to cool slightly. Finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes and garlic.
While the pasta cooks, heat the sun-dried tomato oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes, cooking gently for 1–2 mins until fragrant.
Pop the spinach into a colander or sieve and pour over two kettles of boiling water to wilt it. Squeeze out any excess moisture.

Stir the cottage cheese, pasta, wilted spinach, and most of the basil through the sun-dried tomato mix. Add a splash of the reserved pasta water if needed to loosen, and season well with salt and pepper.
Serve topped with Parmesan shavings and the remaining basil. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pesto Penne
description: A creamy, tomatoey pasta recipe that everyone will ask for again. You can't beat this for a 25 minute dinner.
keywords: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pesto Penne recipe
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Put the cherry tomatoes on a baking tray, then drizzle with oil and season with salt and pepper. Slide under the grill for 7-10 mins until slightly charred and juicy, then set aside.  Grate the Parmesan, and then set it aside.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta following pack instructions. Once cooked, drain (reserve the pasta water) and set aside.

Peel and finely slice the garlic, finely chop the basil stalks and chop the spinach. Heat a splash of oil in a frying pan set over a medium heat and add the garlic and basil stalks. Fry for 2 mins, then tip in the tomatoes and their juices. Let it bubble before adding the penne, some pasta cooking water, crème fraîche, Parmesan, and pesto. Mix well, then wilt through the chopped spinach.
Season to taste, then serve up and garnish with basil leaves.

name: Creamy Tahini & Sumac Chicken Flatbreads
description: Warm flatbreads piled high with juicy leftovers from your Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake batch, with creamy tahini yoghurt and a fresh, zingy herb salad. A super speedy midweek dinner or lunch.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake batch recipe.
Quarter and thinly slice the spring onions lengthways. Pick the parsley leaves, discarding the stalks. Add both to a bowl of ice water and leave to curl and crisp up.

In a small bowl, stir the tahini and Greek yoghurt together, loosening with a splash of cold water if needed. Taste and season with salt, pepper and a touch of honey or sugar if you find it too bitter.
Reheat the chicken and veggies from the sumac chicken traybake and toast the flatbreads in a dry frying pan or under the grill until warmed through.
Drain the spring onions, then toss with the parsley, sumac and a pinch of salt.
Serve the flatbreads onto plates. Top with the tahini yoghurt and reheated Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake. Finish with the sumac onion salad.

name: Creamy Tahini Beans With Mushrooms
description: A rich and creamy vegan recipe that you're going to love. Dressing the beans in tahini gives this a lovely nuttiness and creaminess.
keywords: Creamy Tahini Beans With Mushrooms recipe
instructions: Roughly chop the mushrooms (I like to keep some pieces quite large). Mince the garlic.
Add a splash of olive oil to a frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and a good pinch of sea salt, then cook for 5-6 mins until caramelised.
Add the garlic and another splash of olive oil if they are looking a bit dry, then sauté for 2 mins until the garlic is fragrant.

Meanwhile, prepare the beans. Pour the beans and their stock into a pot or deep pan. Simmer over a medium heat until softened (this will take longer for canned beans and less time for jarred beans), adding more water if necessary. Add the tahini, cumin, paprika and plenty of salt and pepper.
When the beans have softened, add the spinach and cook for a few minutes until wilted. The beans should be creamy and saucy, not dry, so add more water and tahini if necessary.
To serve, ladle the beans into bowls and top with the mushrooms. Finish with another drizzle of tahini, some harissa and whatever extra toppings you like.

name: Creamy Tahini Beans on Pesto Toast
description: These rich, brothy beans spooned over crispy pesto toast are my version of beans on toast. It's a speedy, healthy and filling recipe, perfect for brunch.
instructions: Mince the garlic and drop it into a small pan with the olive oil. Fry the garlic on medium heat for 2-3 mins, making sure it doesn’t burn.

Pour the jar of beans into the pan with the liquid. Chop the herbs or use scissors to snip them directly into the pan. Heat the herby beans gently on low heat. Add a tbsp of tahini and stir, then repeat with the rest of the tahini, season with salt and pepper to taste. Once the tahini has been added, loosen with water a tbsp at a time until you have reached your desired consistency.
