Meanwhile, drizzle one side of the bread with a little olive oil and place under the grill for a few mins until toasted. Remove it and flip it over, then spread the pesto over it. Place it back under the grill for another few mins until toasted and crispy.

Place the toast, pesto side up, in a large, shallow bowl. Then spoon over the beans and finish with a good drizzle of olive oil, some more tahini and a squeeze of lemon. Add more herbs to the top and a grating of vegan cheese if using.

name: Creamy Tahini Miso Salmon Noodles
description: Transform your Zingy Green Miso Salmon batch into a cold noodle salad. With creamy tahini-miso dressing and udon noodles, this is the perfect fridge-raid dinner.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Zingy Green Miso Salmon batch recipe.
Fill a saucepan with water and bring to the boil. Cook the noodles following pack instructions. Once cooked, rinse well under cold running water to chill and remove excess starch.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for a minute or two, until golden and fragrant.

Add the tahini, nori, soy sauce, ice cubes and rice vinegar to a blender. Blitz until smooth and creamy – the nori should be fully incorporated. Taste and season with salt and a pinch of sugar if it’s too bitter.
Toss the dressing through the cold noodles until nicely coated. Flake the cooked miso salmon and mix through the noodles, along with any leftover roasted veg from the traybake.
Divide between bowls and finish with a scattering of toasted sesame seeds.

name: Creamy Tahini Sweet Potatoes
description: This dish is all about the combination. Soft, roasted sweet potatoes. Garlicky kale. Crispy, salty capers. The creamiest tahini dressing. It's a belter.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Peel and slice your garlic cloves
While your oven heats up, coat your sweet potatoes with a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt. Rub everything in. Then, put them in the oven for 60 minutes.

Time for your dressing. Add your tahini to a bowl, with the sesame oil, soy sauce, chilli flakes and the juice of the lemon. Mix it all together, adding a splash of cold water until it becomes a smooth dressing. Once mixed, taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a frying pan and add your capers. Fry these on a high heat until they are crispy. Using a slotted spoon, transfer them to a kitchen paper lined plate.
In the same pan, add your kale and garlic. Season with salt and pepper, and cook until wilted and vibrant green.

Once cooked, remove your potatoes from the oven and slice them length-ways. Add on a good spoonful of your tahini dressing. Then stuff the potatoes with the fried kale and generously sprinkle the capers on top. Drizzle more tahini dressing over the top, with a sprinkling of your remaining chilli flakes and you’re ready to tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Creamy Thai Red Lentil Soup
description: Thai-spiced lentils get blended into a velvety soup with crispy croutons and loads of coriander. Pure comfort in a bowl.
instructions: Make the Thai Red Curry Lentils batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Tear the sourdough into bite-sized chunks, toss with olive oil, salt and pepper, then spread onto a baking tray. Bake for 10–15 mins until golden and crispy.

Pick the coriander leaves and drop the stems into a saucepan with the Thai Red Curry Lentils leftovers and veg stock. Place over a medium heat and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring well to loosen the mix.
Blend everything until smooth and creamy, either using a stick blender straight in the pan, or by transferring to a jug blender. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Top with the crunchy croutons, a scattering of coriander leaves and a swirl of chilli oil.

name: Creamy Tofu ‘Bacon’ & Pea Pasta
description: Creamy, smoky, high-protein pasta with crispy tofu ‘bacon’ and sweet peas. Pure comfort with zero faff.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan.

Dice the tofu into small 1cm cubes and chuck into a bowl with the smoked paprika, soy sauce and maple syrup. Mix well, then spread out on a lined baking tray. Roast for 20 mins, giving it a mix halfway through, until crispy and golden.
Get a large saucepan of salted water on to boil. Once boiling, cook the pasta following pack instructions.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and garlic. Heat the olive oil in a second saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 10 mins until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic and cook for 2-3 mins more until fragrant. Tip in the frozen petit pois and cook for another couple of mins until vibrant and tender.
Zest the lemon, then cut it in half. Finely chop the chives.
Add the drained pasta straight into the pea mixture, followed by the Greek yoghurt, lemon zest and a squeeze of lemon juice. Stir well to combine. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Serve topped with the crispy tofu ‘bacon’ and a scattering of chives.

name: Creamy Tomato Aubergine Parmigiana Tortelloni
description: We've layered up La Famiglia Rana Aubergine Parmigiana Tortelloni with a creamy tomato sauce. Each tortellone is an explosion of flavours.
instructions: Fill a large saucepan with water and bring to a boil. Season well with salt.
Finely dice the onion and finely grate the garlic. Half the tomatoes and preheat a sauté pan over medium heat and add 1 tbsp of olive oil.

Tip in the onion and add a good pinch of salt. Cook for 3-4 mins and then add the garlic. Cook for 1-2 mins then add the tomato puree and cherry tomatoes. Keep cooking over medium heat until the tomato purée starts to catch on the bottom of the pan. Add a splash of water to deglaze and add the mascarpone cheese. Stir everything together to create a creamy sauce.
Toast your breadcrumbs in a dry frying pan until they’re golden brown.
Drop the tortelloni into the boiling water for 2 mins. Transfer to the sauce and toss to combine, adding pasta water to loosen.
Stir through most of the basil and the Parmesan cheese.
Divide the saucy pasta between 2 plates and top with the remaining basil, cheese and the breadcrumbs. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Tomato Gnocchi Bake
description: Creamy, cheesy, and packed with protein – this easy gnocchi bake is comfort food with a nutritious twist.
instructions: Heat your grill to high. Bring a small pan of salted water to the boil and cook the gnocchi for about 2 mins, until they float. Drain and set aside. Halve the cherry tomatoes.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for 2 mins until fragrant. Add the tomato purée and cook for another minute before adding the cherry tomatoes.
Mix well, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the chickpeas, gnocchi and cottage cheese until everything is combined. Season with salt and pepper.
If you’re not using an ovenproof frying pan, transfer the mix to a baking dish. Top with the parmesan and slide under the grill for 3–5 mins until golden and bubbling.
Scatter over the torn basil and serve straight away.

name: Creamy Tomato Gnocchi Bake
description: The star of this gnocchi bake is the cottage cheese, it packs the protein and keeps this comfort food still healthy. Plus you can meal prep it? What a win.
instructions: Heat your grill to high. Bring a small pan of salted water to the boil and cook the gnocchi for about 2 mins, until they float. Drain and set aside. Halve the cherry tomatoes.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for 2 mins until fragrant. Add the tomato purée and cook for another minute before adding the cherry tomatoes.
Mix well, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the chickpeas and cottage cheese until everything is combined. Season with salt and pepper.
If you’re not using an ovenproof frying pan, transfer the mix to a baking dish. Top with the parmesan and slide under the grill for 3–5 mins until golden and bubbling.
Scatter over the torn basil and serve straight away.

name: Creamy Tomato Noodles
description: Packet noodles paired with a creamy, dreamy tomato sauce bursting with umami flavours and ready in as little as 20 mins.
instructions: Into a bowl, add the miso, and grate the garlic in.
Add the tomato purée and gochujang into a frying pan with 2 tbsp of oil. Place on medium heat, and cook until darkened, 2-3 mins. Remove from the heat and whisk it into the miso mixture.
Cook your ramen noodles according to package instructions, reserving 300ml of noodle cooking water.

Return the ramen into the saucepan on a low heat with the miso mixture and 100ml of noodle water. Toss together until the sauce coats the noodles and is emulsified and glossy, adding more water as needed. Taste and season with soy sauce and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper.
Share between bowls and top with spring onion, furikake and an egg yolk. Mix through before eating.

name: Creamy Tomato Tuna Noodles
description: A flavour-packed 15-minute dinner. We’ve combined a rich tomato-garlic base with tender ramen noodles, canned tuna and a silky egg yolk sauce for a creamy, satisfying dish. Topped with capers, crispy onions and a hint of chilli, it's the perfect easy midweek dinner with minimal effort.
instructions: Finely grate the garlic and thinly slice the chilli. Drain the tuna. Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil.

Set a frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the tomato purée and garlic. Cook, stirring, until the tomato paste darkens, about 4-6 mins. Transfer to a large mixing bowl and stir in the red wine vinegar.
Once the water is boiling, cook the ramen noodles following pack instructions. Before draining, reserve the noodle water. Rinse the noodles under cold water.

Separate the egg yolks and add to the bowl with the tomato purée mix. Whisk in some of the reserved noodle water until smooth and creamy. Add the noodles and ½ the tuna to the bowl, tossing to coat. If needed, add more hot noodle water to loosen the sauce. Season with salt and black pepper.
Divide the noodles between four bowls. Top with the capers, sliced green chilli, crispy onions and the remaining tuna.

name: Creamy Trout & Bean Bake
description: A cosy, creamy bake of smoky trout, butter beans and greens, finished with lemon, dill and a cheesy topping. Easy oven comfort at its best.
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C and get on with the prep. Slice the leeks and roughly chop the cabbage, removing the tough core. Then grate the parmesan, finely slice the garlic, roughly chop the dill and zest and juice the lemon.

Add half of the oil to an oven safe pan and add the leeks, frying over low heat for 5 mins. Once the leeks are softened, add the cabbage stirring for 5 mins, until the cabbage has wilted down a little.

Add the garlic to the pan and cook for another minute until fragrant. Tip in the butter beans with their liquid, add all of the lemon juice and half of the zest, then bring to a gentle simmer. Pour in the stock, stir in the crème fraîche and half of the parmesan, then cook gently until everything is combined and just simmering. Take the pan off the heat.
Flake the trout into large pieces over bean mixture, discarding the skin. Gently fold in along with the chopped dill and season to taste.
Sprinkle over the remaining parmesan and transfer to the oven for 10-12 mins, until the cheese has melted, the mixture is bubbling and the cabbage is starting to char on the tips.
To serve, divide between bowls sprinkle over the remaining lemon zest, tear up some crusty bread for dunking.

name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
description: It’s time for a little slice of Italy. This Tuscan chicken recipe tastes absolutely delicious and is a guaranteed hit that only takes 40 minutes from fridge to table. And if you like cream and wine – which, let's face it, most of us do – this might just be your new go-to midweek recipe.
instructions: Peel and finely chop the onion, then peel and finely chop the garlic.

Drizzle the chicken breasts with a little oil and season really well with salt and pepper. Put a large, deep frying pan over a medium-high heat and put the chicken into the pan, skin-side down. Fry for 7-8 minutes until the skin is super crisp, then remove onto a plate, keeping them skin-side up.

Turn the heat down to medium and scrape in the onion along with a pinch of salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring regularly, until softened. Scrape in the garlic and cook for a minute, before adding the Italian seasoning, sun-dried tomatoes and white wine. Bubble for 2 minutes.

Pour in the stock and double cream and nestle the chicken breasts back into the pan, skin-side up. Bring to a simmer and bubble for 10 - 15 minutes, or until the chicken is fully cooked. Add a splash of water, if the sauce is thickening too quickly.
Cram in the spinach and grate over the Parmesan, stirring to wilt the spinach around the chicken.
Season with a little salt and plenty of black pepper to taste and serve with mash or crusty bread.

name: Creamy Whipped Feta & Brown Butter Corn
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This elote-inspired dip is absolutely dynamite. Creamy dip, fragrant corn and crispy homemade spicy tortilla crisps… what more could you ask for?
keywords: Creamy Whipped Feta and Brown Butter Corn
instructions: Heat the oven to fan 180°C. Cut the tortilla wraps into small triangles. Add them to a large baking tray with 3 tbsps of oil, chilli powder and season with salt and plenty of and toss to coat.
Arrange the seasoned tortilla triangles in a single layer on two large baking trays. Bake for 10-15 mins, once they come out they’ll crisp up.

Meanwhile, add the feta, Greek yoghurt and 2 tbsps of olive oil into a food processor. Blitz until broken down and fluffy. Season with the zest of 1 lime, salt, pepper and lime juice, mix. Spread onto a serving plate, cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.

Chop the kernels off the corn. Place a medium frying pan over high heat. Once hot, add the corn and cook until charred, 3-4 mins. Turn the heat down to medium, add the butter and stir until it starts to foam and eventually turns brown, this will take around 3-4 mins. You know the butter has browned when you can smell a nutty aroma. Take it off the heat.
Finely chop the coriander, stalks and all and stir through the corn.
Pour the hot corn brown butter over the whipped feta and top with a sprinkle of spring onion.

name: Creamy, Dilly Salmon Soup
description: Inspired by Finnish Lohikeitto, our brothy salmon soup is packed with dill, leeks and chickpeas for extra protein. The best part - it uses leftovers from your Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas batch.
keywords: Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas batch recipes
instructions: Before you begin, make the Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas batch recipe.
Thinly slice the leek and dill, separating the dill stalks from the fronds. Flake the salmon and zest ½ of the lemon and set aside.
Place a saucepan over medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the leeks and and cook for 8-10 mins, until softened.
Stir in the dill stalks and tip in the leftover chickpeas. Pour in your stock (veg stock will also work) and bring to a boil, then turn the heat down.
Stir the salmon through, until piping hot, and finish with the cream and dill fronds. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Pour the soup into bowls. Garnish with some freshly cracked black pepper and some lemon zest.

name: Creamy, Garlicky Pasta with Fennel-y Pork
description: A silky green garlic sauce meets rich, spiced pork and creamy cottage cheese. A proper comforting bowl of pasta with a fennel-y kick.
instructions: Place a large pot of salted water on to boil.

Once boiling, add the spinach and half of the basil. Blanch for 1 min until wilted and dark green, then use a slotted spoon to transfer to a colander. Leave to cool for a couple of minutes, then squeeze out any excess water.
Chuck the blanched greens into a blender with the garlic cloves and the cottage cheese. Season with salt and pepper, add a splash of cold water, and blitz until smooth.
Add the pasta to the boiling water and cook following pack instructions.

Meanwhile, set a frying pan over a medium-high heat with the olive oil. Once hot, add the pork mince, fennel seeds and three-quarters of the chilli flakes. Cook for 7–10 mins, breaking it up with a spoon, until golden and cooked through. Pour in the Worcestershire sauce, season with salt and pepper, and stir.

Once the pasta is al dente, use a slotted spoon to transfer it into the pan with the mince, off the heat. Stir through the green sauce and the remaining cottage cheese until hot, turn the heat up to medium, if needed. Add a splash of pasta water if it needs loosening. Taste and season again if needed.
Serve in bowls, then top with the remaining basil leaves and chilli flakes.

name: Crispy Air-Fryer Butterbeans
description: If you’re a crisp fiend, you will love these. Crispy, salty and moreish, and full of plant-based protein.
instructions: Heat the air fryer to 160°C. Drain and rinse the butterbeans.
Tip the beans onto a clean tea towel or long piece of kitchen roll. Wrap them up and pat them dry, making sure to move them around. The less moisture, the crispier the bean!

Add the beans to a mixing bowl and toss with the oil, garlic granules and salt. Tip them into the basket of the air fryer and cook for 20-25 mins. Halfway through cooking, tip the beans back into the same bowl, mix with the harissa and smoked paprika then return to the air fryer.
Remove the beans from the air fryer when golden and crispy. Serve hot or at room temperature.

name: Crispy Almond & Apple Fritters
description: These tender and crispy fritters are stuffed with apples, flaked almonds and a drizzle of Rude Health Almond Drink.
instructions: Chop up the apples into cubes, leave the skins on. Pop these into a bowl and grate in the ginger.
Add the juice of half a lemon with the light brown sugar, cinnamon, plain flour, oats, baking powder, 200ml of Rude Health Almond Drink, and ½ tsp salt. Mix well to make a thick batter.
Add vegetable oil to a large pan (roughly enough to deep-fry your fritters in) and bring it to a medium heat.
Using two spoons, spoon large blobs of mixture into the oil and fry for 5-6 mins until dark brown but not burnt. A slower medium fry will make them crispier.
While your fritters are crisping up, make your glaze by whisking icing sugar with 3 tbsp of Rude Health Almond Drink to form a smooth paste.
Drain your fritters, allowing them to cool slightly on paper towels to remove any excess oil, before dunking them in the glaze. If you don’t want them too sweet, drizzle the glaze on instead.
Enjoy hot with a cup of tea.

name: Crispy Artichoke & Tomato Salad with Whipped Feta Dressing
description: This salad's all about bold textures and big flavour - the crispy artichokes are a game changer.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Drain the artichokes, reserving the artichoke oil. Halve or quarter any large pieces, then tip them onto a baking tray and drizzle with the reserved oil. Roast for 15–20 mins until golden and crispy.
Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks and season with salt. Let them sit on a plate to release their juices. Pick the parsley leaves and set aside.

To make the whipped feta, add the feta, Greek yoghurt, olive oil and dill (stalks and all) to a food processor. Blitz until smooth and fluffy. Zest in half the lemon and stir through. Taste and season with honey, salt and black pepper.
If you don’t have a food processor, crumble the feta into a bowl, then whisk in the yoghurt and olive oil until smooth. Finely chop the dill, stir through with the lemon zest, and season to taste.
Toss the tomatoes (with all their juices) with the olives, grains, parsley and crispy artichokes. Add a drizzle of olive oil, squeeze in the lemon juice, and season well.
Spread the whipped feta across the base of your plates, then top with the salad.

name: Crispy Artichoke Patties With Nori Mayo
description: Artichoke petals torn into pieces are mashed with heart of palm to make a filling for these crispy vegan patties. They're soft and flaky with a unique flavour.
instructions: Drain the artichokes and the heart of palm.
Mash the heart of palm with a fork or potato masher until it’s combined into a chunky mashed texture. Place into a large bowl.
Tear the artichoke into flakes and add to the bowl.
Finely slice the celery and shallot.
Add celery, shallot, and seasonings to the bowl, mix and season with salt and pepper.
Form patties with the mixture, they should be about 4cm in diameter.
Put the patties on a tray and let them chill in the fridge while you make the mayo.
Blitz the nori in a food processor to a flaky powder. Add that powder to the mayo with a squeeze of lemon and mix through.

When the patties have chilled for at least 10 mins, prepare your ingredients for frying. In three separate bowls, add the flour, milk and breadcrumbs. Dip each patty first into the flour and dust off any excess. Then into the milk and finally into the breadcrumbs. Ensure they’re covered fully for an even fry.

Fry the patties for 3-4 mins on each side, until just browned and crispy. Alternatively, you can deep-fry the patties until they are golden brown. You can also bake them at 180°C for 20 mins, spray with oil first. Best served immediately.

name: Crispy Aubergine
description: A simple recipe for crispy aubergine. We'd recommend pairing this with some freshly made steamed bao buns.
instructions: Mix the sesame and panko together and add into a bowl, seasoning with salt and pepper. Tip the flour into a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Add the soy milk and lemon juice to another bowl and whisk until it creates a vegan buttermilk.
Take the aubergine and slice into 1 cm circular pieces, once done slice down the middle of each creating semi circles.

Now you have all your mixes and cut pieces it's time to dredge. Dip each piece in this order: vegan buttermilk, then the flour, then back into the vegan buttermilk, then finally into panko/sesame mix. Set aside on a plate or baking sheet.
Shred the lettuce and finely slice spring onion.

When ready to cook, tip enough vegetable oil into a saucepan so it comes halfway up the sides. Place over a high heat until the oil reaches 180 degrees, then turn the heat to medium. Line a plate with kitchen paper. Working in batches, add in the aubergine and allow each side to cook for 2-3 mins, until golden brown, remove and rest on kitchen roll to absorb any excess oil.

name: Crispy Bacon & Egg High Protein Smash
description: Creamy egg yolk, crispy bacon, and blistered tomatoes all smooshed together into something you'll want to eat for breakfast, lunch and honestly dinner too. Perfect for piling onto toast or stuffing into a wrap for on the go.
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to the boil and gently lower in the eggs. Boil for 10 mins, then transfer to cold water to cool. Peel the eggs, separate the yolks from the whites, roughly chop the whites and set aside.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Lay the bacon rashers and cherry tomatoes on a baking tray and roast for 10–12 mins, until the bacon is crisp and the tomatoes are blistered. Leave everything to cool slightly, then chop the bacon into small pieces.

Add the egg yolks to a bowl with the cream cheese and feta and mash together until smooth and creamy. Fold through the chopped egg whites, bacon, roasted tomatoes. Slice the spring onion (reserving a handful to garnish) and stir though. Season well with salt and black pepper and mix until thick and scoopable.
To serve, scoop generous rounds of the smoosh onto hot toasted bread and finish with more sliced spring onion.

name: Crispy Beef Dan Dan Noodles
description: Finn’s take on dan dan noodles is such a treat. Drenched in a creamy peanut-chilli sauce, topped with sizzling beef mince, greens and crushed peanuts - it's got all the textures going on.  And bonus - it's ready in under 30 mins.
instructions: Start with the prep for your mince. Grate your ginger and slice the spring onions, set aside the green parts for garnish later.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the mince for 8 minutes, until the water has evaporated and the fat starts to render and sizzle.

Add the ginger and white parts of the sliced spring onion. Sauté for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Pour in the Shaoxing wine and cook for 2 mins, until the alcohol is cooked off. Then season with the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and sugar. Keep on low heat so it stays warm.
Grate your garlic into a small bowl and add the remaining sauce ingredients, mixing everything together until smooth.
Boil the noodles according to packet instructions and add the choy sum for the final 45 seconds of cooking.

Toss the noodles with the sauce, loosening with a splash of noodle cooking water if needed. Plate with the choy sum and cooked mince, then finish with the green sliced spring onions, crushed peanuts and extra crispy chili oil, if you fancy.

name: Crispy Beef Moussaka Bowl
description: A crispy, herby, moussaka-inspired salad bowl with roasted aubergines, golden beef and zingy ricotta. A delicious midweeker.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

Slice the aubergines into 2cm rounds and season generously with salt. Use your hands to toss the slices so they’re evenly coated. Place them in a sieve over a bowl and leave for 15 mins to draw out excess moisture.
Meanwhile, add the ricotta to a bowl. Zest and juice the lemon, and add all the zest and half of the juice to the ricotta. Season with salt and black pepper, give it a good mix, then set aside.

Pick the parsley leaves. Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Chop the cherry tomatoes into chunks and finely slice the red onion. Chuck the parsley, chickpeas, tomatoes and onion into a bowl. Drizzle over a little olive oil, squeeze in the remaining lemon juice and season with salt and pepper. Mix well and leave to sit.

Brush the salt off the aubergines and pat them dry with kitchen paper. Drizzle olive oil over a large baking tray, lay out the aubergine slices, and drizzle with more olive oil. Roast for 30 mins, flipping halfway, until soft and golden. Toss the cooked aubergines through the salad.

Set a large frying pan over a high heat with another drizzle of olive oil. Fry half the beef mince, seasoning with salt and black pepper. Cook until it’s golden and crispy, then transfer to a bowl. Repeat with the remaining mince.

Grate the garlic into the empty pan (add a touch more oil if needed) and cook for 30 seconds. Squeeze in the tomato purée and cook for 1-2 mins until darkened. Return the beef to the pan, stir through the cinnamon and pomegranate molasses, then season to taste.
To serve, spoon the aubergine salad into bowls. Top with crispy beef and dollops of lemony ricotta.

name: Crispy Brussels Sprout Salad
description: Brussels sprouts are at their best when they're crispy and this baked salad is a delicious and different way to serve these seasonal favourites.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Wash the sprouts and remove any black outer leaves. Wash the kale and remove the very tough stems.

Finely slice the sprouts and place them onto a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Bake for 20-25 mins, until crispy, tossing once or twice to ensure they bake evenly.

Tear the kale into bite-sized pieces and spread on another baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Bake for 15 mins, on the lower shelf, until crispy, tossing once or twice to ensure they bake evenly.
Spread the pecans on a small tray and bake for 7-10 mins, until toasted and fragrant. Roughly chop and set aside.
Meanwhile, make your dressing. Whisk together the mayonnaise, miso, mustard, the juice of half a lemon and the maple syrup. Taste and adjust as you like.
Deseed the pomegranate.
Assemble the salad by adding the kale, sprouts and half of the pomegranate and pecans with the dressing. Finish by sprinkling the rest of the pomegranate seeds and pecans on top.
Best served fresh while it's crispy, but will keep in the fridge for a couple of days.

name: Crispy Buffalo Tofu with Chickpea Ranch Salad
description: This is the buffalo fix every veggie needs. Crispy smoked tofu in buttery hot sauce, with a cool chickpea ranch salad and dilly rice to soak it up. Delish.
keywords: Crispy Buffalo Tofu with Chickpea Ranch Salad
Crispy Buffalo Tofu with Chickpea Ranch Salad recipe
instructions: Break the tofu into chunky pieces, pat dry with kitchen paper, then add to a bowl with the cornflour, tossing well to coat. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the tofu, frying on all sides until nice and golden. Melt the butter in a small saucepan, add the hot sauce and whisk to combine, then set aside.

Finely chop the chives and dill. Slice the celery on a diagonal into thin 3cm long pieces, then drain and rinse the chickpeas. Add the buttermilk, mayonnaise, garlic powder, chives and the lemon zest and juice to a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and mix well, then add the celery and chickpeas, tossing to coat.
Reheat the rice pouches according to the packet instructions, then mix the dill through. Add the crispy tofu to the buffalo sauce and mix well before serving up with the rice and salad.

name: Crispy Cajun Prawn Burgers
description: The famous Po’ Boy sandwich inspired this crispy cajun prawn burger. The same vibe, but a different concept.
instructions: Add three-quarters of the prawns to a food processor and blitz until minced. Crack the eggs into a shallow bowl and beat.
Tip the minced prawns into a new bowl, then add the whole prawns, 2 tbsp beaten egg (reserve the rest for later), cornflour, cajun seasoning and salt and pepper. Stir together well.
Oil your hands and form 4 patties, 1cm thick. Place onto an oiled baking tray, cover and put in the fridge for 1 hr.
Meanwhile, thinly shred the cabbage (use a mandoline if you have one) and finely dice the pickles. Add both to a bowl. Cover and put in the fridge.
Tip the flour into a shallow bowl and the panko breadcrumbs into another. Coat a shrimp patty in flour, then egg and finally breadcrumbs. Repeat with all the patties.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fill with 1cm sunflower or vegetable oil. Once hot, add the prawn patties and fry for 4-5 mins each side until golden brown and cooked through (turn the heat down if they’re browning too quickly.)
Meanwhile, stir 40g mayo, all the mustard and 2 tbsp olive oil through the cabbage salad. Season with some pickle brine, salt and pepper. Toss together.
Toast the buns, then spread the remaining mayo over them all. Top with a crispy cajun prawn patty and some pickled cabbage slaw.

name: Crispy Cantonese Hot Honey Chicken
description: In Partnership With Aldi. #ad Sticky, crispy chicken thighs in a hot honey glaze, served over fluffy rice with a fried egg and crunchy herbs. Delish.
keywords: crispy chicken with egg and rice
instructions: Get your rice on following pack instructions.

Chuck the chicken thighs into a bowl and add the soy sauce for the marinade, sugar, black pepper and salt. Sprinkle over the cornflour and toss until fully coated and dry to the touch. Give everything a mix and let it sit for 5 mins while you sort the rest.

Heat a small frying pan over a medium-high heat with a generous lug of vegetable oil. Once hot, carefully add the chicken and cook for 5-7 mins on each side, or until crisp and golden. Remove and set aside to rest.
Crack the egg into the same pan and fry for 3 mins until the whites are set and the edges are golden, but the yolk is still runny. Season with a pinch of salt. Remove and set aside.

Pour away most of the oil, leaving about 1 tsp behind. Finely grate the garlic and chuck it into the pan over a medium heat. Let it cook for about 30 secs, then add the the remaining soy sauce, hot honey and chicken stock. Let it bubble away for 5-10 mins until thickened. Turn off the heat, return the chicken to the pan and flip it to coat in that sticky sauce. Slice it up.
Finely slice the spring onion and chop the coriander and chives.
Spoon the rice into a bowl. Top with the fried egg and the sliced chicken, drizzling over any leftover sauce from the pan. Finish with the your chopped herbs and sesame seeds. Dig in!

name: Crispy Cauliflower Bites with Peanut Butter Aioli
description: Peanut butter aioli might sound a bit strange, but trust us that it's the perfect accompaniment to these crisp and spicy cauliflower bites. A vegetarian banger.
instructions: Blitz up the gluten-free bread, eggs, milk, smoked paprika and thyme together to form a chunky batter. Add a large pinch of salt.
Pour your cornflour into a separate bowl.
Cut the cauliflower into florets then dredge them in the cornflour.

Meanwhile, heat up a litre of sunflower oil in a heavy-based saucepan until it reads 180°C on a cooking thermometer. If you haven't got a cooking thermometer to hand, one way to know whether your oil is at the right temperature is by dropping a small piece of bread into the oil. If that bread turns golden brown after about 30 seconds, it should be good to go.
Dip the cauliflower florets in the batter until they're evenly coated and drop gently into hot oil and fry for 6 mins until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels.
Grate the garlic in a bowl and pour over 2 tbsp of hot frying oil so the garlic sizzles and cooks
Add in the mayo, a pinch of salt, and your peanut butter. Whisk together until creamy.
Plate up the cauliflower and serve with a big dollop of the aioli for dipping.

name: Crispy Cauliflower Leaf Wings
description: Cauliflower leaves are as delicious as florets, and here is a glorious way to eat them. In the crispiest batter, with two out-of-this-world sauces. Addictive.
instructions: Cut the leaves off your cauliflower, saving the head for another occasion.
Make your blue cheese sauce. Pop your sour cream and mayonnaise into a bowl and crumble in your blue cheese. Give it a good whisk until you have a smooth sauce. Set aside.
Make your buffalo sauce. Melt your butter in a small saucepan. Once melted, add your hot sauce and honey. Whisk until you have a smooth, vibrant sauce that has thickened slightly. Keep it warm.
Get your oil heating up – fill a large saucepan a third of the way with vegetable oil and gently bring it up to 180°C/354°F.

Pour your flour, cornflour, cumin seeds, 1 tsp of salt and baking powder into a bowl and stir to combine. Add your cold water and whisk briefly to form a batter – it doesn't need to be totally smooth.

Dip your cauliflower leaves one at a time into your batter, then carefully place them into the hot oil. Fry for 3 mins or so until crisp and golden. Drain on a plate lined with kitchen towel and repeat with your remaining leaves.
Place your crispy cauliflower leaves onto a plate along with a bowl of blue cheese sauce. Drizzle with buffalo sauce and sprinkle with chopped chives, then serve.

name: Crispy Cauliflower Tacos
description: Crispy fried cauliflower, tangy lime-y cabbage and lots of smoky chipotle mayo. So simple and delicious.
instructions: Combine the mayo, chipotle paste, ¼ tsp salt and the zest of a lime.
Finely slice the red cabbage. Mix together with ½ tsp salt and the juice of a lime.
Chop up the cauliflower into small florets, and the stem and leaves into bite-sized pieces
Heat up a large pot of vegetable oil on medium heat.
Whisk together the self-raising flour, paprika and 1 tsp of salt. Add in a handful of ice and slowly whisk in the beer to form a light and airy batter.

Dip the cauliflower into the batter and then straight into the frying oil. Fry for 5-8 mins until cooked through and crispy. Continue with the stems and leaves. The leaves will only take a minute to cook.
Toast the tortillas on a dry saucepan.
Top the tortillas with the chipotle mayo, crispy cauliflower, then the zesty cabbage.Finish with a scattering of coriander leaves.

name: Crispy Cereal Squares
description: This is a nostalgic treat that you may not have made for years, but will want to again now. Crispy cereal set with chocolate or marshmallow. Choose your weapon.
instructions: Line the base of a brownie tin or small roasting tin with baking paper.

For the chocolate cereal squares, break the chocolate into a large saucepan, then add the golden syrup, butter and a big pinch of salt. Cook over a low heat, stirring regularly until the chocolate and butter have melted and are smooth and glossy.

For the marshmallow cereal squares, tip the marshmallows, butter and a big pinch of salt into a large saucepan. Cook over a low heat, stirring regularly until the marshmallows and butter have melted and are smooth and glossy.

Off the heat, tip in your chosen cereal and give everything a good mix so that each piece gets completely coated in the mixture. Scrape into your tin, smooth out the top then sprinkle over a little more salt if you like.
Put in the fridge for at least 2 hours to set then cut into squares. Will keep in a container in the fridge for a week.

name: Crispy Cheddar & Chilli Fried Egg Sandwich
description: Your standard fried egg sandwich has had a makeover. We've loaded this sarnie with tons of grated cheese, sweet chilli sauce and chilli flakes.
instructions: Coarsely grate the cheddar cheese.

Preheat a frying pan over high heat until very hot. Add half the the cheese in a pile in the middle of the pan, cook for 2-3 mins, until turning a little golden at the edges, then crack your egg into the middle. Let it splutter and sizzle until the cheese edges are lacy, crispy, and perfectly golden brown, and the egg is cooked through. Season with salt and a shed load of black pepper.
If you like your eggs a little more cooked through, use a spatula to flip it over. Then use a spatula to move to a plate. Repeat with the rest of the cheese and second egg.
Reduce the heat for the last 1 min of cooking. Cut open your bun, drizzle a bit more oil into the pan and toast the cut sides of the bun until golden and a little crispy.

Flip the bun out the pan and cover the bottom with the sweet chilli sauce. Slap the eggs on top, add the chilli flakes and little extra sweet chilli sauce then crown the sarnie with its lid. Smush down to burst the yolk for extra dip action.
Devour with a hot mug of tea. Bliss.

name: Crispy Cheese & Marmite Gnocchi
description: This 7-ingredient gnocchi is super affordable, comes together in 15 minutes and hits all of the comfort food notes.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Season with salt and add your gnocchi. Cook for 2 mins then remove with a slotted spoon, saving the water.
Finely slice the leeks and spring onions. Separate the whites of the spring onions from the greens.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a high heat, add a glug of oil and your blanched gnocchi. Cook for 5 mins, tossing regularly until golden brown and crispy. Remove from the pan onto a plate.

Add another glug of oil and chuck in your leeks and the whites of the spring onion. Cook over a medium heat, stirring regularly, with a small pinch of salt. Cook until the leeks are a pale green and have sweated down, you don’t want too much colour, this should take around 5 mins.

Add the cream cheese and a big ladle of the gnocchi cooking water. Stir until loose and creamy. Add the Marmite and stir until incorporated. Cook until bubbling again, then grate in three-quarters of the cheddar.

Add the gnocchi and a big handful of spring onion greens to the pan. Toss in with plenty of freshly cracked pepper and lemon juice, and have a taste. Adjust the seasoning, adding a little more gnocchi water if the mix is too tight.
Serve with extra cheddar, black pepper and spring onion greens. Get stuck in.

name: Crispy Chicken & Broccoli Rice
description: A wonderfully easy fail-safe way to enjoy chicken rice and broccoli. Say goodbye to dry chicken breast: this is crispy-skinned, juicy cooked chicken. Add a knob of butter to the sauce to make it extra silky!
instructions: Wash the rice in a large bowl with plenty of cold water. Rinse and repeat three times until the water runs clear. Soak the washed rice in water for 30 mins (you can skip this step if you're in a rush but it will take longer than described to cook later).

Meanwhile, start on the sauce. Roughly slice the onion, carrot, ginger and ½ the garlic cloves. Heat a knob of butter in a large pan set over a medium heat. Add the sliced vegetables and sauté for 10-15 mins until soft.

Add the light soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar and butter to the pan and sauté for a further 3 mins. Transfer everything to a blender and blitz until you have a fine sauce. Pour into a bowl and set aside (the longer it sits the better).

Mince the remaining garlic, finely dice the broccoli. Heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the minced garlic and fry for 1-2 mins until fragrant but not coloured. Add the broccoli, rice and a generous pinch of salt. Stir to combine and cook for another minute.

Add the chicken stock, stir once and cover with a lid. Turn the heat up to high and bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to the lowest setting and cook for 12 mins. Turn the heat off and leave the rice to sit with the lid on for another 10 mins.

Meanwhile, cook the chicken. Pat the chicken skin dry and season with a pinch of salt on both sides. Place the chicken skin side down into a cold pan and turn the heat up to medium. Cook for 5-6 mins or until the skin turns golden brown, then flip and cook for a further 2-3 mins. Remove and leave to rest for 3 mins. Slice the chicken into 1-2cm strips. Thinly slice the spring onion and set aside for garnish.

Now to serve. For each serving, pack a small bowl with the rice. Flip the bowl onto the middle of a plate and lift up the bowl, leaving behind a mound of rice. Pour the sauce around the rice, like a moat. Add the chicken thighs, a sprinkling of spring onions and a few cracks of black pepper.

name: Crispy Chicken & Brown Rice With Hot Sauce Salsa
description: Made up of crispy, skin-on chicken thighs, herby rice and a peach salsa spiked with hot sauce, here’s an easy weeknight win.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180ºC. Heat a splash of oil in a large ovenproof pan over a high heat. Season the chicken skin with salt and pepper and then add to the pan, skin-side down. Cook for 5–10 mins, until dark golden brown, then set aside on a plate.

Turn the heat down in the pan to medium. Finely slice the garlic and add to the pan along with the fennel seeds. Add the rice pouches with a splash of water. Finely chop most of the herbs, reserving a handful for the end, then stir the chopped herbs through. Add the juice of the lemon and season well.
Snuggle the chicken back into the pan with the herby rice, skin-side up. Slide into the oven and cook for 20–30 mins, until the chicken is cooked through.

Meanwhile, make the salsa. Slice the peaches in half, remove the pips and then roughly chop them into 1cm cubes then add to a bowl. Slice the cherry tomatoes into quarters and add to the bowl. Add the hot sauce, juice of the lemon and chilli flakes.
Mix the yoghurt with enough water to make it drizzle-able. Remove the chicken from the oven. Drizzle some yoghurt over the top and top with some of the salsa. Scatter with the reserved herb leaves.
Serve with the remaining yoghurt and salsa on the side.

name: Crispy Chicken & Carrot Rice
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Crispy chicken, buttery carrot rice & crunchy chicken skin - all the spiced, savoury goodness you need in a midweek dinner. Big flavour and barely any washing up.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Make sure you have an oven safe lidded casserole dish or frying pan.

Prep your ingredients. Finely dice the shallots and garlic. Grate the carrots and set aside. Remove the skins from the chicken thighs (you should be able to pull them off with your hands) and cut the skins into 2–3cm chunks. Wash the rice 4–5 times until the water runs clear.

Add the chicken skins to a cold frying pan. You want the skins to cook slowly until crispy, so set over a low heat for around 10–15 mins to let the fat render properly. Remove from the pan and set aside on kitchen paper.

Season the chicken thighs with salt and black pepper. Increase the heat to medium-high and sear the thighs in the rendered chicken fat for 3–4 mins on each side until golden. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Lower the heat to medium, then add the shallots and garlic to the same pan. Cook for 1 min, then stir through the chilli flakes, smoked paprika and cumin. Fry for 2–3 mins until fragrant.

Tip in the rice and cook for 2 mins to toast it. Stir through ¾ of the grated carrot and the zest of the lemon. Pour in the chicken stock and stir everything together. Nestle the chicken thighs on top.

Pop a lid on the pan and transfer to the oven. Bake for 30–35 mins until the rice is fluffy and the chicken is cooked through. Remove the lid and bake for a final 6–8 mins to allow the top to crisp up.
Once baked, allow the rice and chicken thighs to rest for 5 mins or so before serving with crispy chicken skin, Greek yoghurt, lemon zest and remaining grated carrot and coriander leaves.

name: Crispy Chicken & Charred Pepper Panzanella
description: The technique for cooking the chicken is similar to brick chicken, just without the brick. You'll have glassy, crispy chicken skin in no time. B x
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Start by deboning the chicken thighs. Pop a chicken thigh, skin-side down, on the board.

Run your knife along the either side of the bone, leaving as little flesh on the bone as you can. Once the bone is exposed, slip the knife underneath, again, snug to the bone and remove. Repeat with the other thighs.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Grab a roasting tin and set over a medium high heat.
Add a splash of olive oil and the chicken thighs skin side down. Cover with parchment and pop a heavy pan on top. Cook for 10 mins under the weight, until browned and crispy.
Meanwhile, tear up the ciabatta into small chunks, smash the garlic cloves and cut the pepper into strips.

Remove the chicken from the pan and add the garlic, peppers and bread. Toss to coat in the oil and chicken fat. Season with salt, nestle the chicken back into the pan, skin side up, and bang the tray into the oven for 25 mins.
While the chicken is roasting, cut the tomato into chunks and add to a large bowl. Core and slice the cucumber and thinly slice the onion. Get those in the bowl too.
Season with salt and pepper, add the vinegar and a healthy glug of oil. Let that all marinate while the chicken roasts.

Once the chicken is ready, remove from the pan and pop onto a plate. Fish out the garlic cloves and empty the bread and peppers into the salad bowl. Smush the garlic into a paste on your board and add to the bowl. Toss everything together to coat in the tomato and cucumber juices.
Finish with torn basil leaves and toss together.
Divide the salad between plates and top with the warm crispy chicken. Get stuck in.

name: Crispy Chicken & Creamed Corn
description: You might not always think of giving creamed corn a go. But this recipe is here to convert you.
keywords: crispy chicken corn on the cob
instructions: Pat the chicken dry, then season with salt. Pop onto a baking tray and set aside in the fridge for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, remove the sweetcorn from the cobs using a sharp knife. Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat an ovenproof pan over a medium heat and add the chicken thighs, skin-side down. Cook for 8-10 mins until deeply golden, then flip and sear the other side. Remove from the pan.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Remove around half of the chicken fat from the pan, then add the onion and most of the thyme. Cook for 10 mins over a medium heat, then add the garlic and sweetcorn. Cook for around 5 mins until the corn is just turning golden. Add the flour and cook for 1-2 mins before pouring in the wine. Reduce for a couple of minutes. Add the water and bring to a simmer. Pour in the cream, mix well and season with salt and pepper.
Pop the thighs back into the pan and scatter with a few more thyme leaves. Pop in the oven for 15-20 mins, until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, cut the lemon into wedges.
Grate the Parmesan over the chicken and serve up with greens or a salad, along with a wedge of lemon to squeeze over the top.

name: Crispy Chicken & Orange Salsa Tacos
description: We’ve used Old El Paso’s new Street Vibes Al Pastor soft taco kit to make these quick and easy tacos with juicy pulled chicken, crispy chicken skin and a zingy citrus salsa.
ingredients: 1 Old El Paso Street Vibes al Pastor Taco Kit
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.

Remove the skin from the chicken thighs and stretch the skin flat on the baking sheet. Pat it dry and season with salt. Place another piece of baking paper on the top followed by another baking tray to weigh it down then pop in the oven for 10-15 mins.
Meanwhile, add the juice of ⅔ of the lime and the seasoning mix to a medium bowl and mix to combine. Add the chicken thighs and massage the marinade into the meat.
Slice the red peppers and peel and dice the orange. Add both to a bowl along with the salsa and mix to combine. Pick the coriander leaves and slice the remaining lime into wedges.
Heat a large pan with a drop of olive oil over a medium heat. Add the chicken and cook for 10 mins until charred. Remove from the pan and shred.
To assemble the tacos, fill the soft tortillas with the shredded chicken, fruity salsa and a few coriander leaves. Serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Crispy Chicken & Pepper Bean Salad
description: Inspired by the smoky, sweet flavours of romesco, this bright salad pairs roasted chicken thighs and charred peppers with a crispy savoury granola of seeds, flaked almonds and crispy onions. Hearty enough for dinner, light enough for lunch.
keywords: Chicken & Pepper Salad with Nutty Sprinkle
Chicken & Pepper Salad with Nutty Sprinkle recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely grate the garlic into a large bowl, add a good glug of olive oil, season with salt and black pepper and mix together. Add the chicken thighs and toss until nicely coated, then transfer to a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 mins, until cooked through and golden.

Meanwhile, drain the peppers and roughly chop into 2-3cm chunks. Cut the tomatoes into similar-sized chunks. Drain the butter beans. Toss the tomatoes, peppers and beans together in a large bowl with a glug of olive oil, salt, black pepper and the sherry vinegar.

Spread the seeds and flaked almonds on a small baking tray, drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Slide into the oven for 4-6 mins, until golden and toasted. Tip into a bowl and stir through the crispy fried onions.

Discard any tough parsley stems and roughly chop the rest. Toss the parsley through the salad, then divide between plates or boxes. Slice the chicken and lay it on top. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and a generous sprinkle of the savoury granola.

name: Crispy Chicken & Pepper Bean Salad
description: Inspired by the smoky, sweet flavours of romesco, this bright salad pairs roasted chicken thighs and charred peppers with a crispy savoury granola of seeds, flaked almonds and crispy onions. Hearty enough for dinner, light enough for lunch.
keywords: Chicken & Pepper Salad with Nutty Sprinkle
Chicken & Pepper Salad with Nutty Sprinkle recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely grate the garlic into a large bowl, add a good glug of olive oil, season with salt and black pepper and mix together. Add the chicken thighs and toss until nicely coated, then transfer to a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 mins, until cooked through and golden.

Meanwhile, drain the peppers and roughly chop into 2-3cm chunks. Cut the tomatoes into similar-sized chunks. Drain the butter beans. Toss the tomatoes, peppers and beans together in a large bowl with a glug of olive oil, salt, black pepper and the sherry vinegar.

Spread the seeds and flaked almonds on a small baking tray, drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Slide into the oven for 4-6 mins, until golden and toasted. Tip into a bowl and stir through the crispy fried onions.

Discard any tough parsley stems and roughly chop the rest. Toss the parsley through the salad, then divide between plates or boxes. Slice the chicken and lay it on top. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and a generous sprinkle of the savoury granola.

name: Crispy Chicken & Potato Salad
description: Crispy roast chicken, warm mustardy potatoes and golden crunchy skins. This is the kind of potato salad you actually want to eat.
keywords: roast chicken thighs and potato salad
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Season the chicken thighs generously with salt and black pepper.
Peel the potatoes and cut into even 3cm chunks. Set aside.

Place a large ovenproof frying pan over a medium heat and add the chicken thighs, skin-side down. Cook, undisturbed, for 8–10 mins until the skin is golden and crispy (it won’t be fully cooked yet). Flip the thighs over, then remove the pan from the heat.
Add the potato skins into the pan, and coat in the chicken fat. Transfer to the oven and bake until the chicken is cooked through and the potato skins are crispy, 20-25 mins.

Meanwhile, place the peeled potato chunks into a saucepan with cold salted water. Bring to the boil and cook for 10–15 mins until just tender. Drain in a colander, reserving 100ml of the cooking liquid, and leave to steam-dry for a couple of minutes.
Finely chop the shallot and chives. Add the shallot to a large mixing bowl with the Dijon mustard and white wine vinegar. Stir to combine and leave to sit for a few mins.

Once the potatoes are slightly cooled. Crumble the chicken stock cube into the shallots, then whisk in the potato cooking liquid, olive oil and season to taste with sugar, pepper and salt, if needed. Tip the potatoes into the dressing with 3/4 of the chives. Gently mix together, until the potatoes start releasing their starch and it slightly thickens the dressing. Taste and adjust with more salt, sugar or pepper, if needed. If the salad is too thick for your liking, stir in more potato cooking liquid.

To serve, spoon the warm potato salad onto plates. Top with the crispy chicken thighs and scatter over the remaining chives. Crumble over a few of the crispier roast potato bits from the pan for crunch.

name: Crispy Chicken Au Poivre & Chips
description: Crispy chicken, piping hot homemade chips, and a zippy pepper sauce. Doesn't get much better than this. A gorgeous poultry take on steak au poivre.
instructions: Season the chicken well with salt and if possible set aside for 1-2 hours in the fridge. Don’t worry if you haven’t got this time, just crack on.

In the meantime, make the chips. Peel and cut the potatoes into chunky chips and tip into a large saucepan. Cover with cold water and season generously with salt. Set over a medium heat and bring to a bare simmer. Cook for 7-8 mins until just tender. Drain and allow to steam dry.

Preheat the oven to 220°C. Fill a tray with 1cm of vegetable oil and slide into the oven. Once hot, whip it out and carefully lower in the chips one by one. Turn to coat in the hot oil then return to the oven for 30-40 mins, turning regularly, until lightly golden.
Drain the excess oil from the chips and then return to the oven for 10 mins to finish.
Crush the garlic cloves, finely dice the shallot and roughly chop the peppercorns.

Pat the chicken breasts dry and preheat a large pan over a medium high heat. Add a shot of oil and lay the breasts in, skin side down. Add a weight on top and cook for 9-10 mins until super crispy, flip them over then add the rosemary, crushed garlic and butter.
Baste the hot butter over the chicken and then slide into the oven for 4-5 mins or until just cooked. Tip the contents of the pan out onto a tray and let the chicken rest.

Keep some of the fat in the pan and add the diced shallot and about 40 twists of black pepper. Cook for 2-3 mins over a high heat before adding the peppercorns and whiskey. Cook the alcohol off and then add the stock. Bring to a boil and reduce by two-thirds.
Finish the sauce with chopped chives, cream and vinegar.
Serve the chicken with lots of sauce and a heaping pile of chips.

name: Crispy Chicken Caesar Wrap
description: This might just be the ultimate wrap. It’s packed with crispy chicken pieces, bacon bits, and a punchy kale Caesar.
instructions: Finely chop the garlic. Sprinkle it with salt and use the flat side of your knife to smash it into a paste. Finely chop the anchovies and smash them into a paste, too.
Place the egg yolks in a bowl. Add the garlic and anchovy, as well as the Dijon mustard and juice of the lemon, and whisk until well-combined.
Very slowly pour in the oil, whisking continuously, until the dressing thickens and emulsifies. You want to do this slowly to ensure it doesn’t split.
Finely grate the parmesan and add it to the dressing, whisking until smooth. Set aside for later.
Season the chicken thigh fillets with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place the flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs in 3 separate bowls. Season the flour with salt and pepper. Beat the eggs and season them, too.
Dip the chicken fillets in the flour, egg, and then breadcrumbs respectively. Set aside.

Arrange the bacon in a single layer in a large frying pan and set over a medium heat. Cook until crispy on the bottom, then flip and cook until crispy on the other side. Transfer to a wire rack to cool, then chop into small pieces.

Heat a good glug of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add your chicken fillets and fry for a couple of minutes on each side until they are crispy and tender. Leave to cool slightly then slice into strips.
Wash, dry and chop your lettuce. Wash, dry and de-stem the kale, then roughly chop the leaves. Slice the tomatoes.
Place the kale in a large bowl, drizzle with a little olive oil and massage for 1 minute. This will help break the leaves down, which makes them much more pleasant to eat.
Add the lettuce and dressing and toss to coat.
Assembly time. Place the salad on a wrap and top with the sliced tomatoes, crispy chicken and bacon bits. Wrap up, serve and enjoy.

name: Crispy Chicken Fajita Linguine
description: WhatWillyCook's comfort dish of dreams. Juicy fried chicken thighs coated in a smoky, spiced crust, served on top of creamy linguine with charred peppers. Spicy, comforting and absolutely dangerous.
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C. Whisk the eggs in a bowl, add the chicken thighs and set aside to soak.
Mix together the cayenne pepper, half the smoked paprika, the chilli flakes, garlic powder, cumin, onion salt and a good grind of black pepper in a separate bowl. This is your spice mix.
Get your linguine on in a large saucepan of well-salted water and cook according to packet instructions. Just before draining, scoop out a few ladles of pasta water and set aside.

Meanwhile, roughly chop the coriander and set aside. Finely slice the peppers into strips. Heat a drizzle of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the peppers for 6-8 mins until slightly charred and soft. Add half the spice mix, stir to coat and cook for a further minute, then set aside.

Chicken time. In a bowl, mix together the cornflour, the remaining spice mix and the remaining smoked paprika. Lift the chicken thighs out of the egg and press into the flour mix, turning to get an even coating all over.

Heat a generous drizzle of vegetable oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the chicken for 5-7 mins on each side until golden and crisp, then transfer to a baking tray and place in the oven to keep warm.

Drain the linguine and return to the pan. Add the spiced peppers and cream cheese along with a splash of the reserved pasta water. Toss everything together until the sauce is silky and coats the pasta.
Remove the chicken from the oven and slice into strips. Divide the pasta between bowls, top with the chicken, squeeze over the lime juice and scatter over the roughly chopped coriander.

name: Crispy Chicken Harissa Stew
description: This is a killer take on a stew that uses harissa as one-stop shop for all the spicy, punchy flavour you need. Oh, and it’s all made in one pan – less waste, less washing up. Everyone’s a winner.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Thinly slice the onions and garlic. Cut the potatoes into 2cm chunks.
Heat a large oven-proof pan or roasting tin over a medium heat with a glug of oil.
Season the chicken with salt and brown, skin-side down, until crispy. This should take 7-8 mins.
Take the chicken out of the pan and add the sliced onions, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt. Cook for 9-10 mins until the onions are starting to caramelise.
Add the potatoes, harissa and garlic and cook for another couple of mins.
Add the tinned tomatoes along with a splash of water and bring to a simmer. Once that's all simmering away, nestle the chicken back into the pan.
Bang it into the oven for 30-35 mins until bubbling. You'll know it's ready when the potatoes and chicken are cooked through and the chicken skin is crispy and golden.
Stir in the butter and top with the fresh oregano.
Serve with a blob of yoghurt and get stuck in.

name: Crispy Chicken Meatballs & Pesto Chickpeas
description: Golden chicken meatballs, zingy pesto and creamy chickpeas, a one pan midweek dinner that the whole family will love. Plus the meatballs freeze like a dream.
instructions: Roughly tear the sourdough into chunks and chuck into a small bowl with the milk. Let it soak while you prep everything else. Peel and grate the carrot, then finely grate the garlic.

Add the chicken mince, grated carrot, garlic, oregano and egg to a large mixing bowl. Squeeze the bread to remove any excess milk, then crumble it into the bowl. Season generously with salt and pepper, then mix everything together using your hands until fully combined.
Roll the mixture into meatballs about the size of a walnut.

Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry the meatballs in batches for 10-12 mins, turning occasionally, until golden on the outside and cooked through. Transfer to a plate.

Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Add them to the same pan and fry for 3-4 mins until warmed through. Return the meatballs to the pan, then stir through the pesto and the juice of half the lemon. Taste and season.

Serve up!Kids Plate: Dish out the chickpeas and meatballs, with a dollop of yoghurt on the side if you like.Parents Plate: Roughly tear the basil and sprinkle it over the top. Finish with a grating of parmesan, if using.

name: Crispy Chicken Pancakes With Ginger Chilli Dressing
description: Move over duck, crispy chicken pancakes are here to stay. With a fiery ginger and chilli dressing and crunchy greens, this recipe gives the takeaway classic a run for its money.
instructions: Before you begin, make the No-Fuss Roast Chicken.
Preheat the oven to 170°C.

Sit your leftover roast chicken with the skin (legs are best but whatever you have left is fine) on a tray lined with parchment paper. Combine the coriander and fennel seeds in a pestle and mortar and coarsely crush. Add the five spice and stir to combine. Cover the chicken liberally with olive oil and coat with the spice mixture and season with fine sea salt. Slide into the oven for 35-40 mins until super crispy.

While the chicken roasts, make the pancakes. Combine the flour with 130ml of water from a boiled kettle, the honey, sesame oil and the salt. Use a fork to bring together into a shaggy dough and then knead for 5 mins until smooth. Using hot water makes this process much quicker! Rest the dough 5 mins before dividing into 12-14 little balls. Don’t sweat about them being exactly the same size at this point, it’ll be ok! Divide into pairs (6 or 7), brush a little sesame oil over each and then sandwich them together, oil sides facing each other.

Roll the little pairs out into big flat pancakes. They’ll separate when we cook them. Once they’re all rolled, reheat a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the pancakes for 1-2 mins per side, with a lid on, until lightly browned and cooked through. Once cooked, separate the pancakes and keep them stacked in a clean tea towel. Repeat with the remaining pieces of dough.
Finely grate the chilli and ginger and mix with the hoisin and the juice of the lime. Cut the cucumber and spring onions into matchsticks.
Remove the chicken from the oven and shred with two forks. Build your pancakes and get stuck in!

name: Crispy Chicken Rice with Chilli Garlic Sauce
description: One of the most addictive sauces you’ll ever eat. Includes added food theatrics, as you scorch the aromatics with hot oil to make the sauce – it’s really the star of the show!
keywords: Crispy Chicken Rice With Chilli Garlic Sauce
Crispy Chicken Rice With Chilli Garlic Sauce recipe
instructions: For the chilli garlic sauce, add the bird’s-eye chillies, garlic cloves and fresh ginger into a pestle and mortar and bash for a minute or so until a chunky consistency. Finely mince the coriander and spring onion, separating the whites from the greens. Add ½ the minced coriander and all the spring onion whites to the bashed aromatics then season with salt and set aside.
Add the remaining coriander and spring onion greens to a bowl of ice-cold water and set aside for garnish.

Heat the vegetable oil in a small frying pan set over a high heat for about 3 mins or until just smoking, then carefully pour the hot oil into the pestle and mortar to scorch the aromatics. Juice in ½ the lime (reserve the rest for later) and add the rice vinegar, sriracha, sugar and dark soy sauce. Mix well to combine then set aside.

For the rice, finely mince the garlic cloves and slice the fresh ginger into thin matchsticks. Wash the rice three times until the water runs clear then drain. Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the minced garlic, ginger matchsticks and whole spring onion and fry for a minute until softened, then add the rice, a pinch of salt and the chicken stock. Stir once to combine then pop a lid on, turn the heat up to high and bring to the boil. As soon as the water is at a rolling boil, turn the heat down to the lowest setting and set a timer for 18 mins with the lid on. Once cooked, turn the heat off and set aside, with the lid on, until ready to serve.

While the rice is cooking, pat the chicken skin with kitchen paper to remove as much moisture as possible, then season with a generous pinch of salt. Add the chicken thighs to a cold pan, skin-side down, and turn the heat to medium. Cook for 10 mins without touching or moving the chicken, until the fat is rendered and the skin is crispy and golden. Flip the chicken over and cook for another 3 mins or until cooked through, then remove, set aside to rest for 5 mins and slice into 1cm strips.
Just before serving, drain the water from the spring onion greens and coriander then season with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of the remaining lime juice.

To serve, divide the rice between plates and top with the chicken thighs. Generously spoon over the chilli garlic sauce, using the back of the spoon to spread evenly. Finish with the fresh spring onion greens and coriander mix.

name: Crispy Chicken Salad with Blue Cheese Ranch Dressing
description: Golden breaded chicken, crispy pancetta, crunchy sourdough croutons and crisp veg, all tossed in our punchy Blue Cheese Ranch dressing. It's addictive.
keywords: crispy chicken salad with blue cheese ranch dressing
crispy chicken salad with blue cheese ranch dressing recipe
chicken salad with blue cheese dressing
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Dice the sourdough and toss with the olive oil, salt and black pepper. Add the breaded chicken steaks and croutons to a large baking tray and bake for 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the croutons are golden and crisp.

Meanwhile, add the pancetta to a cold frying pan and set over a medium heat. Fry until the fat has rendered and the bacon's become all golden and crispy, then transfer to a plate with kitchen paper to remove the excess fat.
Slice the celery, quarter the radishes and separate the gem lettuce leaves. Finely chop the chives and set them aside for the dressing.

Next add the blue cheese, mayonnaise, buttermilk, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder and lemon juice to a high-speed blender. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt and black pepper and taste. Finally, stir through the chopped chives.
Add the lettuce, celery, radishes, croutons and most of the pancetta to a large bowl. Drizzle over the dressing and toss gently until everything is nicely coated.
Slice the chicken and arrange over the salad. Finish with the remaining pancetta and serve straight away.

name: Crispy Chicken Skin Sandwich
description: Layers of juicy chicken thigh teamed with fresh pesto, charred broccoli stems, perfectly crisp chicken skin and focaccia. The sando of summer.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180ºC. Use your hands to slide between the skin and the flesh of the chicken, then gently pull the skin away, keeping it as intact as possible. If it helps, use scissors to assist. Remove the skin and set aside, then place the chicken on a baking tray, add a little olive oil and season with a little salt and pepper. Cover with foil and slide into the oven for 25 mins, until cooked through, set aside to cool.

Meanwhile, lay a piece of baking paper over a baking tray and add the chicken skin, stretching the pieces out so they lie flat, you might need to use scissors to trim them down a little. Cover with another layer of baking paper, then top with a second baking tray or tin. Add a weight on top, I like to use a cast iron pan — use the heaviest oven-proof tin you have. Slide into the oven for 25-30 mins.

Finely slice the bottom half of the stems of the tenderstem broccoli and add to a bowl. Slice the gem lettuce and add to the bowl along with the capers. Add the juice of half a lemon, season with a little salt and pepper and set aside in the fridge.
Make the dressing by adding the mayo to a bowl then add the mustard. Finely chop the anchovies and add to the bowl, then finely grate the Parmesan in. Squeeze in the lemon juice and season well.
Add the top half of the tenderstem broccoli (the tips) to a small baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season well with salt and pepper.
Once the skin has cooked, remove from the oven and remove the weight, peel back the baking paper, the skin should be crisp and golden, set aside on some kitchen paper.
Turn the grill to high and grill the broccoli tops for 10 mins, until charred.
Use your hands to shred the cooled chicken into the dressing, toss well.

Assemble. Take the focaccia loaf and slice into 4 quarters. Slice each in half horizontally. Spread with pesto, then top with a big dollop of the dressed chicken, add some of the broccoli stems, then top with crispy chicken skin. Finish with a handful of salt, then spread the bread top with a little of the pesto and press together. Either wrap up for later, or halve it and tuck in straight away.

name: Crispy Chicken Spicy Honey Noodles
description: If you like spice, this is the one! Turn a packet of instant noodles into a proper meal you’ll make over and over again. This is a 7/10 on the spice ladder, but add more if you're feeling up for it.
keywords: Crispy Chicken Spicy Honey Noodles recipe
instructions: Season both sides of the chicken with salt. Add the chicken thighs, skin-side down, to a cold frying pan, then turn the heat to medium. Don’t touch or move the chicken (this keeps the skin crispy and helps to render the fat) for around 12 mins. Flip the chicken onto the meat side and cook for a further 8 mins. Turn off the heat and remove the chicken from the pan. Set both the chicken and pan aside.

Dice the red onion, slice the chilli and spring onion, then transfer it all to a bowl. Add three-quarters of your soy sauce along with half of the apple cider vinegar, half of the honey, and all the sesame seeds. Crush half of your garlic cloves into the bowl. Stir well to combine until the honey is dissolved. Set aside.

In a separate bowl, combine the gochujang with the chilli powder, the remainder of your soy sauce, all the mirin, all the oyster sauce, a few cracks of black pepper, the rest of your honey, the rest of your apple cider vinegar, the other half of the crushed garlic, and water. Mix to combine.
Boil a saucepan of water, add the instant noodles and cook for 1 ½ mins shy of cooking instructions. Drain, reserving the cooking water.

Set the frying pan you used for the chicken over a medium heat and add the gochujang sauce. Fry for around 1 min or until the sauce turns a darker red. Add the instant noodles and a splash of the cooking water. Stir until the sauce coats the noodles, adding more cooking water to loosen it up if needed.
Slice the chicken thighs. Plate up the noodles and add the chicken thighs on top. Top with the red onion mixture. Enjoy.

name: Crispy Chicken Thigh Noodle Salad
description: The best bit of chicken is the crispy skin. Turn this into a crispy topping for noodles and you are onto a winner.
keywords: Crispy chicken thigh noodle salad recipes
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C. Peel the skin off your chicken thighs, then debone them.
Finely chop your red chillies.
Place your chicken thighs in a bowl with half of your chillies, 1 tbsp of honey, 1 tbsp of your soy sauce, a glug of olive oil and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Leave to marinate for 10 mins.
Place your chicken skins on a baking tray lined with parchment. Place another piece of baking parchment on top, then top with another baking tray. Bake for 12 mins until crisp and golden.
Heat a frying pan over medium heat. Add your chicken thighs and cook for 5 mins on each side until tender.
Shred your chicken with two forks.
Pour your boiling water over your noodles and leave to sit for 1 minute. Drain in a colander and leave to dry for 15 mins, tossing occasionally to stop the noodles from sticking.

Add your remaining chopped chilli to a bowl along with your remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey, the zest and juice of a lime, and 2 tbsp olive oil. Whisk to combine, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Bring a pan of water to the boil. Salt, then add your sugar snaps. Boil for 2 mins until just tender, then drain and pop in a bowl of iced water to cool.
Meanwhile, quarter your radishes and finely slice your spring onions.
Add your noodles, chicken, chicken skin, sugar snaps, radishes, most of your spring onions and dressing to a bowl. Toss to combine.
Sprinkle with your remaining spring onions and serve.

name: Crispy Chicken Thighs
description: The ultimate recipe for juicy chicken thighs with the crispiest skin. This one is the perfect protein to upgrade any dish. Combine with your favourite base, side and dressing for a great make-ahead meal.
instructions: Place the chicken thighs skin-side down on a chopping board. Run a knife along each side of the bone to expose the bone. Using scissors, cut underneath the bone to remove it. Repeat with the remaining chicken thighs.
Add the chicken, skin side down into a cold, large frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Cook for 10-15 mins until the chicken skin is golden brown.
When the chicken skin is golden brown and crispy, flip the chicken thighs and cook for a further 2 mins. Remove them from the pan and set aside.
Thickly slice each chicken thigh and divide between Tupperware containers along with your favourite base, side and dressing. Pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Crispy Chicken Thighs with Sesame Green Sauce
description: These babies are going to taste as good as they look. Healthy, hearty and pretty much irresistible, this could be the tastiest dinner of your life. Enjoy.
keywords: crispy chicken thighs with sesame green sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Tip the potatoes into a pot and cover with cold water. Season generously with salt and set over a medium heat. Cook for 9-10 mins or until tender.

While the potatoes cooks, season the chicken thighs with salt and add to a frying pan with a shot of oil, skin-side down. Set over a medium heat and cook for 8-9 mins, without moving the chicken, until the skin is very crispy and golden brown.

Drain the potatoes and line a large baking tray with parchment paper. Tip the potatoes onto the tray and lightly crush with a bowl or a glass. Add the seared chicken and sprinkle the lot with olive oil, salt and half of the sesame seeds. Slide into the oven for 35 mins or until the potatoes are crispy and the chicken is cooked through.

While the chicken roasts, make the dressing. Roughly chop the spring onions and add to a blender with the herbs (stalks and all), the honey, sesame oil, and rice vinegar. Blend until smooth adding a bit of extra olive oil if you need to loosen things up a little. Season with salt and pepper and add a drop more vinegar if you need to.
When the chicken has 10 mins to go, toss the broccoli with oil and salt and add to the tray, roast for the last 10 mins.
Serve the crispy potatoes, broccoli and chook with a swoosh of green sauce, extra sesame seeds and fresh lime wedges.

name: Crispy Chicken With Turmeric Tahini Noodles
description: Bright yellow, turmeric-spiked noodles are a great partner for crispy chicken thighs in this easy weeknight dinner.
keywords: Crispy Chicken With Turmeric Tahini Noodles
Crispy Chicken With Turmeric Tahini Noodles recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Pat the chicken skin dry and season with a little salt. Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken, skin-side down, and cook for 8-10 mins, until the skin is golden and crispy, then flip over. If your pan is oven proof simply slide it into the oven, if not, transfer the chicken to a baking sheet, skin side up. Bake for 15-20 mins.

Meanwhile, make the noodle dressing. Tip the turmeric and curry powder into a deep saucepan (don’t worry you’ll use this pan again shortly) and place over a medium heat. Toast for a minute, until it starts to smell fragrant, then tip into a bowl. Fill the pan with water and place over a high heat.

Whisk the tahini and miso into the spices. Squeeze in the juice of one of the limes and whisk together – it’ll seize and look lumpy but don’t worry. Whisk in enough water to make it the consistency of single cream, it’ll take quite a lot of water to loosen it, up to around 60ml.

Slice the cucumber in half lengthways and add to a bowl. Use a teaspoon to scoop out the seedy core, then slice into half moons. Add to a bowl along with most of the coriander and mint leaves. Add two-thirds of your sesame seeds and the juice of ½ the lime. Season with salt.

Drop the noodles into the water and cook according to packet instructions then drain, rinse with a little cold water and tip into a bowl. Add the dressing and toss well. Taste and season, then spoon into bowls.

Top with the chicken, you can either serve the thighs whole, or you can cut away the bone and slice them. Snuggle the cucumber salad to the side of the bowl, then finish with the remaining sesame seeds, herb leaves and the remaining lime half to squeeze over at the end. Serve with chilli oil if you like.

name: Crispy Chicken and Creamy Feta Salad
