description: A twist on a classic Greek salad. Crispy chicken thighs with a creamy feta and cucumber tzatziki-inspired dressing make this perfect for the summer.
instructions: Debone the chicken thighs, leaving the skin on. Place into a bowl with 1 tbsp oregano, red wine vinegar, salt, pepper and grate in your garlic. Mix together and set aside.

Chop up the tomatoes into large wedges, scoop out the inside of ¾ of your cucumber and slice into crescents, set the rest of the cucumber aside for the dressing. Thinly slice the onion and half the olives. Toss the sliced cucumber, olives, onion with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp oregano and salt and pepper.

Place the chicken thighs skin-side down in a cold frying pan, then set over a medium heat. Cook for 5-7 mins until the fat has rendered and the skin is golden and crisp. Flip and cook for another 2-3 mins or until cooked through. Set aside to rest for at least 3 mins.
Meanwhile, make the feta dressing, blitz feta, greek yoghurt, the juice of the lemon, salt and pepper. Grate the remaining cucumber and mix this in with the feta dressing.
Slice the chicken and toss through the veggies with the sauce. Serve the salad in a bowl, finish with a sprinkling of oregano and enjoy.

name: Crispy Chicken with Juicy, Tomatoey Beans
description: Crispy chicken skin is something we crave pretty much twenty-four hours a day. This simple chicken dinner recipe has a foolproof method for getting the crispiest chicken skin in town.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Salt the chicken skin and pop in the fridge for 15 mins. Put the cherry tomatoes, olives and oregano onto a baking tray, season with salt and pepper and roast for 25 mins.

While the tomatoes are roasting, pop the chicken thighs into a large frying pan, skin-side down, and set over a medium heat. Allow the fat to start to render and the skin to get really golden brown and crispy (around 8-10 mins). Flip the thighs over, sear the underside then transfer to a baking tray. Slide into the oven for 15-20 mins or until the chicken is cooked through.
Finely slice the red onion and pop into ice-cold water. Finely chop the parsley.
Drain and rinse the beans and mix with the sherry vinegar and parsley. Gently stir through the roasted tomatoes and olives, then season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the beans onto a large platter and top with the crispy chicken thighs. Garnish with Parmesan shavings, red onion, and pesto. Serve with lemon wedges and bread to mop up all the juices.

name: Crispy Chicken, Brown Rice, Chickpeas & Tzatziki
description: A super healthy, one-pan, high-protein banger is on the table in under 30 minutes. What’s not to love?
instructions: Place the chicken thighs skin-side down on a chopping board. Run a knife along each side of the bone to expose it. Using scissors, cut underneath the bone to remove it. Repeat with the remaining chicken thighs. Once they're all prepped, season with salt and pepper. We prep them like this to ensure you get that crispy skin, but if you'd rather by skinless boneless thighs you can!
Cut the courgette in half lengthways and then into half moons. Cut the red onion into large chunks.
Add the chicken, skin side down into a cold, large frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Cook for 10-15 mins until the chicken skin is golden brown.

While the chicken is cooking, make the tzatziki. Grate the cucumber into a bowl and season with salt. Set aside for 5 mins then squeeze out the excess water. Add the squeezed cucumber to the yoghurt with the zest of the lemon and the juice of ½ the lemon. Grate in the garlic. Mix well to combine then season to taste with salt. Set aside.
When the chicken skin is golden brown and crispy, flip the chicken thighs and cook for a further 2 mins. Remove them from the pan and set aside.

Add the red onion, courgette and spices to the pan. Grate in the garlic then cook over a medium heat until soft. (If anything catches on the bottom of the pan, just add a little water and scrape it up). Add the drained chickpeas and cooked rice to the pan. Cook over a medium heat for 2-3 mins until everything has come together. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves and cut the chicken into thick slices.
To serve, divide the rice between plates then top with the chicken and tzatziki. Sprinkle over the parsley and finish with a lemon wedge.

name: Crispy Chicken, Brown Rice, Chickpeas & Tzatziki
description: A super healthy, one-pan, high-protein banger is on the table in under 30 minutes. What’s not to love?
instructions: Place the chicken thighs skin-side down on a chopping board. Run a knife along each side of the bone to expose the bone. Using scissors, cut underneath the bone to remove it. Repeat with the remaining chicken thighs.We prep them like this to ensure you get that crispy skin, but if you'd rather by skinless boneless thighs you can!
Cut the courgette in half lengthways and then into half moons. Cut the red onion into large chunks.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper and add skin side down into a cold, large frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Cook for 10-15 mins until the chicken skin is golden brown.

While the chicken is cooking, make the tzatziki. Grate the cucumber into a bowl and season with salt. Set aside for 5 mins then squeeze out the excess water. Meanwhile, chop the dill then add to the squeezed cucumber along with the yoghurt, the zest of the lemon and the juice of ½ the lemon. Grate in the garlic. Mix well to combine then season to taste with salt. Set aside.
When the chicken skin is golden brown and crispy, flip the chicken thighs and cook for a further 2 mins. Remove them from the pan and set aside.

Add the red onion, courgette and spices to the pan. Grate in the garlic then cook over a medium heat until soft. (If anything catches on the bottom of the pan, just add a little water and scrape it up). Add the drained chickpeas and cooked rice to the pan. Cook over a medium heat for 2-3 mins until everything has come together. Season with salt, pepper and MSG.
Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves and cut the chicken into thick slices.
To serve, divide the rice between Tupperware containers then top with the chicken and tzatziki. Sprinkle over the parsley and finish with a lemon wedge. Pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Crispy Chilli & Mint Pork
description: A quick simple lunch, packed with juicy crispy pork and fresh mint. Don’t forget the crispy egg, its what brings this meal to life.
instructions: Finely chop the garlic and red chillies.
Thinly slice the cabbage and pick the leaves of the mint.
Combine the fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar in a bowl.
Squeeze the sausages out of the casing into a bowl - once you start frying you will need to work fast so it's easier to get this prepped in advance.
Turn the wok on a medium high heat and once it starts to smoke, pour a large glug of cold oil around the edges.
Add in the chilli and garlic, cook for 30 seconds then immediately add in the sausage mince. Push down and break up the mince and fry for 5 mins until broken up and very crispy.
Add the cabbage and sauce and cook for 1 min, turn off the heat.
Toss in the mint.
Heat the rice.
Serve on a bed of fluffy rice and top with a crispy fried egg. Slice the lime and serve on the side.

name: Crispy Chilli Beef
description: This dish has it all: a tantalizing combination of sticky, crispy, sweet, and spicy goodness that makes it a standout favorite. Our crispy chilli beef recipe is a classic takeaway staple that delivers unbeatable flavor with every bite. The beef is expertly fried to achieve that perfect crispy texture, coated in a rich, glossy sauce that balances sweetness with a kick of spice. Whether you’re enjoying a casual meal at home or hosting a dinner party, this dish pairs wonderfully with your other Chinese favorites. Serve it alongside fragrant jasmine rice, crispy spring rolls, or steamed dumplings for a complete and satisfying feast. With its bold flavors and irresistible crunch, this crispy chilli beef recipe is sure to become a regular on your menu. Dive into this delectable dish and elevate your at-home dining experience to new heights.
instructions: Slice your onion and red chillies. Cut your spring onions into 3cm lengths. Grate your ginger and garlic. Set the veg aside until later.

Very finely slice your rump steaks, then pop them in a large bowl. Crack in your egg and give it a good mix before adding your cornflour, white pepper and a good pinch of salt. Mix again until the steak is evenly coated.
Heat a wok on a high heat with a generous glug of oil. Add your beef in batches and fry for a few mins until crispy. Remove from the pan with a slotted spoon and repeat with your remaining beef.
Add your onion to the same pan and stir fry for 3 mins.
Tip in your spring onions, red chilli, ginger and garlic and fry for 2 mins more.
Add your sriracha, tomato ketchup, rice wine vinegar, caster sugar and soy sauce to the pan. Give it a mix and let it bubble and reduce for a couple of mins.
Get your crispy beef back in the pan and cook for 2 mins.
Serve with egg fried rice.

name: Crispy Chilli Chicken & Edamame Rice Bowl
description: Spicy, sticky chicken mince with a punchy sesame-chilli dressing, served over jasmine rice with edamame, cucumber and spring onion. Ready in 30 mins and seriously good.
keywords: Crispy Chilli Chicken & Edamame Rice Bowl
Crispy Chilli Chicken & Edamame Rice Bowl
Crispy Chilli Chicken & Edamame Rice Bowl recipe
Crispy Chilli Oil Chicken Mince & Rice Bowl
Crispy Chilli Oil Chicken Mince & Rice Bowl recipe
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions, then spread it out on a tray and leave to cool, you don't want it warm when it goes into the salad.

Meanwhile, finely grate the garlic and ginger, finely slice the spring onions and finely dice the cucumber. Mix together the chilli oil, soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil and honey in a small bowl until the honey dissolves. It should be spicy, salty and a little sharp — adjust to your liking and set aside.
Cover the edamame with boiling water and leave for 2 mins, then drain and run under cold water.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a high heat until shimmering. Add the chicken mince and press it flat, don't touch it for 3-4 mins until a deep golden crust forms underneath. Break apart, flip the larger pieces and leave for another 2 mins. You want proper colour and crunch.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then toss through the mince. Take off the heat.

Add the cooled rice to a large bowl along with the edamame, cucumber, spring onions and mince. Pour over the dressing and toss well. Spoon into bowls or boxes, finish with the sesame seeds and serve or leave to cool and pop in the fridge to grab whenever you need.

name: Crispy Chilli Chicken Salad
description: This salad is the perfect combo of textures and flavours. The chicken adds crispness, the veg adds freshness, and the chilli soy dressing ties it all together.
instructions: Mince the garlic and ginger and place in a small saucepan with the chilli flakes.
Add a glug of vegetable oil and heat over medium heat. Cook until toasted and fragrant.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and whisk in the balsamic vinegar, soy sauce, and sugar. Leave to cool.
Trim the green beans. Boil in salted water until tender-crisp, around 3 mins, then drain.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the celery on a diagonal, peel the cucumber into ribbons, crush the peanuts, and roughly chop the coriander.
Season the chicken thigh fillets with salt and pepper on both sides. Place in a cold non-stick frying pan.

Heat the frying pan over medium heat and cook the chicken undisturbed for 6 mins, or until deep golden brown. Flip and cook for a further 4 mins, or until cooked through, then transfer to a chopping board to rest.
Place the green beans, celery, and cucumber in a mixing bowl. Add half of the dressing and toss to coat. Transfer to a platter.
Chop the chicken and place on top of the salad with the crushed peanuts and chopped coriander. Top with the remaining dressing then tuck in and enjoy!

name: Crispy Chilli Greens Rice Bowl
description: A hearty and nutritious rice bowl recipe that packs a fair bit of heat. A good one for a lazy weeknight when you don't want to compromise on taste.
instructions: Thinly slice the onion and cabbage. Chunk-up the mangetout. Cut the cucumber into slices and then matchsticks – set aside for later.

Set a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Add a splash of olive oil and chuck in the veggies. Cook for 3-4 mins over a very high heat until the greens are blistered, charred and tender. Tip in the chilli oil, half the peanuts, half the Thai basil and the ginger brine. Remove from the heat.

Heat the rice pouches according to pack instructions. Divide the rice between serving bowls and top with the stir-fried veggies. Tear over the remaining basil and top with the cucumber matchsticks. Return the pan to the heat and fry the eggs over a high heat until they’re super crispy. Serve on top of the veggies with extra crispy chilli oil and pickled ginger.

name: Crispy Chilli Oil Recipe
description:
What is crispy chilli oil? It's the ultimate condiment, elevating dishes with a spicy, savoury kick. Our homemade version combines hot chilli oil with crispy shallots, minced garlic, and a hint of numbing Szechuan pepper for a burst of flavour. This versatile chilli crunch can be made with various dried chiles, such as chiles de arbol, red chiles, or even jalapeños for a different heat level. Inspired by Chinese regional cuisines, particularly Sichuan, it also has roots in Malaysian, Vietnamese, and Indonesian cooking, making it a global favourite.

Crispy chilli oil is fantastic on dumplings, silken tofu, sushi, and stir-fries. Use it to spice up a bowl of noodles, top off a dish of black beans, or add depth to your favourite Thai food. The rich flavours blend well with fermented soybean and pickled ingredients, enhancing the savoury profile. Try it as a dip, drizzle over silken tofu, or even add to pesto for a fusion twist. Whether you're enjoying Chinese food or simply looking to spice up everyday meals, this condiment is a game-changer.
instructions: Thinly slice your shallots and garlic.

Pour your vegetable oil into a large pan. Add your shallots, then bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15 mins until the shallots are crisping up and just beginning to turn golden. Add your garlic, then simmer for another 5 minutes until your garlic has gone crispy. Don't let anything burn, you want the garlic and the shallots to only just be golden.
Remove them from the pan of oil and leave to drain and crisp up on a plate lined with kitchen paper for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, add your chilli flakes, soy sauce, both types of peppercorns and star anise, MSG and sugar to a large bowl. Pour your oil through a sieve into the chilli bowl and give it a good stir.
Add your crispy garlic and shallots back into the oil mixture. Leave to infuse for a day before eating.
Ladle your oil into sterilised jars and use within 1 month.

name: Crispy Chilli Paneer
description: This is a neat little crispy chilli paneer recipe. If you're a fan of paneer, chilli, and crispy-ness, this one's for you. Enjoy.
instructions: Start by making the batter for the paneer. Put the cornflour, water, ground black pepper, and chilli powder into a bowl. Grate in the ginger and garlic then season generously with salt. Mix well until smooth. Dice the paneer into 2cm pieces, then dredge in the batter.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat and add the paneer, shaking off any excess batter back into the bowl. Fry on all sides until crispy, making sure there's space between each piece, for around 7 mins. Remove from the pan and drain on kitchen paper.

For the sauce, start by grating the ginger and garlic. Trim and cut the green beans in half, then slice the pepper. Halve the green chilli, deseed and finely slice, or for less spice keep them whole and poke holes in them using a knife. Trim the spring onions and cut into 2cm pieces.

Heat a little oil in the same frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the spring onions, green chilli, red pepper and green beans, fry for 2-3 mins, add the garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 minute, then turn down the heat and add the soy sauce, vinegar, sriracha, chilli powder and a pinch of ground black pepper.

Pour in the water and mix, then add the leftover cornflour batter, mixing well. Simmer for a couple of minutes until glossy, then add the paneer back in, mixing well and adding more water if necessary. Serve topped with sesame seeds, with rice on the side.

name: Crispy Chilli Prawns Pil Pil
description: Cooking prawns in a spicy sauce brings out their sweetness in the best way. Make sure to get some bread to mop up the oil of this beauty.
instructions: Peel the prawns, leaving the tails on, if there is a black line down the top of the prawn, use a cocktail stick to dig it out – once you’ve hooked it out with the cocktail stick, you should be able to pull it out.

Peel and finely slice the garlic, then add to a small frying pan. Peel the ginger and cut into matchsticks, then add to the pan along with the chilli flakes, chilli powder and toasted sesame seeds. Cover with the vegetable oil and place over a medium heat, and cook for 10 mins, until the garlic and ginger are lightly golden. Add a big pinch of salt and If using, add the MSG.

Turn the heat up to medium high, then add the prawns, let them sizzle for 2-3 mins, spooning the hot oil over them. Scatter in the coriander and give everything a good stir, then remove from the heat.
Take the table straight away in the pan. Serve with bread to soak up all the crispy chilli oil in the pan.

name: Crispy Chilli Tofu
description: Your takeaway favourite just went vegan. Crispy, craggly tofu in a hot and sticky sauce is out of this world. This crispy chilli tofu recipe is seriously delicious. And seriously easy to make.
instructions: Slice your onion and red chillies. Cut your spring onions into 3cm lengths. Dice your red pepper into 2cm chunks. Grate your ginger and garlic. Set the veg aside until later.
Tear your firm tofu into thin pieces, then pop them into a large bowl. Add 1/3 of your soy sauce, cornflour, white pepper and a really good pinch of salt. Mix again until the tofu is evenly coated.
Heat a wok on a high heat with a generous glug of oil. Add your tofu in batches and fry for a few mins until crispy. Remove from the pan with a slotted spoon and repeat with your remaining tofu.
Add your onion to the same pan and stir fry for 3 mins, then add your red pepper and fry for another 2 mins.
Tip in your spring onions, red chilli, ginger and garlic and fry for 2 mins more.
Add your sriracha, tomato ketchup, rice wine vinegar, caster sugar and your remaining soy sauce to the pan. Give it a mix and let it bubble and reduce for a couple of mins.
Get your crispy tofu back in the pan and cook for 2 mins. Serve with rice.

name: Crispy Chorizo Croquetas
description: We’ve combined the best parts of tapas. Oozy croquetas. Smoky chorizo. Nutty manchego. Crispy balls of goodness, perfect to eat whilst feasting on Amazon Prime.
instructions: Peel your chorizo sausage, then finely crumble it into a bowl. Grate your manchego.
Pour your olive oil into a saucepan on a medium heat. Once the pan is hot, get your chorizo in there and fry for a couple of minutes until crisp.
Tip in your 30g of flour and smoked paprika, then cook out for 5 mins. Gradually add your milk, whisking until you have a smooth sauce.
Bring your mixture to a boil, then simmer for 5 mins until thickened. Add the manchego and stir to combine.
Pour into a wide dish to set in the fridge for 1 hour.
Pour your remaining flour, eggs and breadcrumbs into a bowl each.
Roll your mixture into balls and dip them in your bowl of flour, eggs, and then breadcrumbs respectively.
Heat a generous glug of oil in a small saucepan. Once hot, add your croquetas a few at a time and fry for 5 mins until crisp and golden. Keep warm and repeat with your remaining croquetas.

name: Crispy Chorizo Gnocchi with Salsa Verde
description: A minimal effort, hearty banger of a meal. Crispy chorizo and gnocchi pair beautifully with a zingy salsa verde. Ocado ingredients make this a delight.
instructions: Start by making your salsa verde. Roughly chop your parsley, basil and capers.
Tip them into a pestle and mortar and add a drizzle of olive oil and 2/3 of your sherry vinegar. Bash into a thick sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel your chorizo ring and chop into small chunks. Slice your garlic and chunkily dice your peppers.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add your chorizo and fry for a few mins until the meat has crisped up and released its fat into the pan.
Turn up the heat a little. Add your red pepper chunks to the pan along with your gnocchi and fry for 10 mins more until the peppers are soft and the gnocchi is crisping up.
Tip your sliced garlic in and fry for 1 min more.
Season your gnocchi with salt and pepper and your final tbsp of sherry vinegar. Give it a final stir.
Serving time. Spoon your gnocchi onto a plate and top with your salsa verde and some parmesan shavings. Enjoy.

name: Crispy Chorizo Loaded Potatoes
description: Our twist on a favourite tapas dish. Crispy potatoes. Even crispier chorizo. Punchy aioli. A match made in heaven using beautiful Ocado ingredients.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C. Pop in a roasting tray with a glug of olive oil in it to heat up.
Chop your potatoes into 1 inch cubes, leaving the skins on. Wrap your bulb of garlic in a square of baking parchment.

Remove the hot tray from the oven and carefully add your potatoes. Season with salt and toss until coated, then place in the oven. Place your garlic on a lower shelf. Roast for 45 mins, turning the potatoes occasionally so they brown evenly.
Roughly chop your red chilli, cloves of garlic and spring onions.
Place them into a blender with your smoked paprika, tomato purée and 4 tbsp olive oil. Blend until you have a fairly smooth paste.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Crumble in your chorizo and fry for a few mins until it is crispy. Remove from the pan.

Tip your vegetable paste into the same pan and cook for a few mins until fragrant. Add your flour and cook out for 2 mins, stirring until you have a smooth paste. Gradually pour in your chicken stock, whisking constantly so you have a smooth base.
Once all the stock has been added, pour in your passata and bring the mixture to a simmer. Cook for 5 mins, then season to taste with salt. This is your bravas sauce.
Back to the oven. Once 45 mins have elapsed, remove the garlic from the oven and roast your potatoes for another 10-15 mins.
Once your garlic is cool enough to handle, squeeze out the pulp. Pop it into a bowl along with your mayonnaise and mix to combine. This is your roast garlic aioli.
Roughly chop some parsley.

Assembly time. Pour your potatoes onto a plate and either pipe or spoon your bravas sauce over. Next, do the same with your roast garlic aioli. Sprinkle with the crumbled chorizo and some parsley, then serve.

name: Crispy Cod with Spring Onion & Sesame Butter Sauce
description: Crispy, golden cod with a zingy garlic, ginger & spring onion butter. High-protein, full of flavour, and seriously satisfying.
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then add to a saucepan with the water. Bring to the boil, cover, and simmer over a low heat for 10 mins. Remove from the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for 5 mins. Fluff with a fork and keep warm.
Pat the cod dry with kitchen paper and season well with salt. Dust the top side of each fillet lightly with the cornflour.

Heat the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the cod, cornflour-side down, and cook undisturbed for 6–8 mins until golden and crispy. Flip and cook for 1–2 mins more until just cooked through. Set aside.
Peel and finely slice the garlic. Peel and finely slice the ginger. Thinly slice the spring onion.

Melt the butter with the sesame oil in a small saucepan over a medium heat. Add the garlic, ginger and dried chillies, and cook for 1–2 mins until just golden. Pour the hot butter mix over the spring onion in a bowl and let it sizzle and wilt. Stir in the toasted sesame seeds, a splash of Maggi Seasoning or soy sauce. Taste and season with pepper and salt, only if needed.
Wilt the spinach in a separate pan with a splash of water and a pinch of salt, then drain.
Divide the sushi rice between bowls, add the spinach, and top with the crispy cod. Spoon over the sesame butter sauce. Finish with fresh coriander leaves and a wedge of lime.

name: Crispy Courgettes with Whipped Ricotta, Chilli & Honey
description: This summary snack is perfect for a hot day with a nice glass of something cold… Jordon x
instructions: Add the plain flour and cornflour to a bowl along with a pinch of salt and whisk to combine. Set aside.
Chop the courgettes into roughly 1-inch pieces, then pour into a colander, toss with a big pinch of salt, and set aside to drain.
Add the ricotta to a bowl along with a big pinch of salt, pepper and the zest and juice of half a lemon. Use a whisk to whip the ricotta for about a minute, until smooth and creamy.

When you’re ready to cook, pour the sunflower oil into a large pan, making sure it’s not more than half full. Heat over a high heat to 180°C (if you don’t have a thermometer, put a drop of the batter into the oil and if it sizzles gently you’re good to go).
Add the water and ice cube to the flour and mix. Grab the courgettes, dip into the batter and coat. Carefully add to the hot oil and cook for 3 or 4 mins until golden and crispy.
Remove from the oil onto a rack or plate lined with a paper towel. Sprinkle generously with sea salt.
Spread the ricotta on a plate, top with the crispy courgettes, the basil and chilli, then drizzle over the honey and a pinch of salt.

name: Crispy Cumin Corn Fritters & Smoky Salsa
description: Crispy crunchy corn and courgette fritters spiced with cumin and paprika served with a banging smoky salsa.
keywords: Spicy corn fritters and salsa recipes
instructions: Grate the courgettes in a bowl and season generously with salt.
Meanwhile make the salsa by charring the tomatoes, red onion, chilli and garlic over a flame on the hob or under a very hot grill.
Finely chop the coriander.

Add the garlic, chilli and onion to a pestle and mortar with a large pinch of salt. Pound to form a chunky paste then add in the tomatoes one by one and keep pounding until you get a chunky salsa. Add in the coriander, juice of a lime and season with salt.

Cut the corn off the cobs and add the kernels to your bowl of grated courgettes. Mix in the flour, 1 tsp salt, cumin and smoked paprika. This, in combination with the liquid from the courgettes, should be enough to form a batter.
Get a frying pan on medium heat and add in a big glug of oil.
Spoon in a few tablespoons of the batter and slightly flatten. Cook for 4 mins and then flip over and cook on the other side until very golden brown.
Allow to cool slightly so they crisp up and serve with the salsa.

name: Crispy Cumin Lamb with Brothy Rice
description: Cumin and lamb is one of the best flavour pairings. We've taken inspiration from the various Chinese cumin lamb dishes out there and combined elements of each to create this zingy and rich crispy cumin lamb with brothy rice. It's comforting and unbelievably delish.
keywords: Crispy Cumin Lamb with Brothy Rice
instructions: Pick the coriander leaves, then transfer to a bowl of ice water. Thinly slice the spring onions, separating the greens and whites. Add the greens to the bowl of ice water with the coriander. Thinly slice the coriander stems and pick the basil leaves.

Place a wok over a high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the mince and cook for 5-8 mins until browned and crispy. Stir through the coriander stems, spring onion whites, cumin seeds and szechuan peppercorns and cook for 1 min until fragrant.

Pour in the Shaoxing wine and let it evaporate completely. Add the oyster sauce and half the soy, then stir until glossy. Take off the heat and stir through the Thai basil until wilted. Transfer to a plate, then set aside.

Bash the ginger. Return the wok to a high heat. Once hot, add the ginger and let it sizzle for a couple of seconds. Pour over the stock, season with the remaining soy sauce and let it come to the boil.
Share the cooked rice between bowls, pour the broth over and top with the cumin lamb and herbs.

name: Crispy Curry "Chicken" Burger
description: We love curry, we love mayo, and we love burgers. We've loaded vegan chicken burgers into toasted buns with curried mayo and a zippy citrus cabbage slaw. Enjoy!
instructions: Finely slice your onion.
Heat a pan over a medium heat and add a glug of veg oil. Tip in your cumin seeds and toast for a minute until fragrant. Add your onions and cook for 20 mins until totally softened and caramelised.
Add your tomato purée and curry powder to the mix, then cook out for 2 mins. Leave to cool.
Finely shred your cabbage and radishes (use a mandoline, if you have one) and then finely chop your pickled chillies.
Add this to a bowl along with your coriander leaves, chillies and juice of your lime. Season to taste with salt.
Whizz up your onion mixture in a food processor, then mix it with your mayonnaise and hot sauce.
Cook your Happy Go Clucky burgers in the oven according to packet instructions.
Toast your buns in a dry frying pan.
Assembly time. Spread your mayo on the base of your bun, then top with your burger and slaw. Spread more mayo on the lid, then pop this on top. Serve and enjoy.

name: Crispy Curry Tofu Noodles
description: We’ve served the crispiest tofu with ramen noodles, a curried peanut sauce and a zingy pickled sprout slaw. Feels indulgent but is actually full of the good stuff.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Stir the cornflour and smoked paprika together and season with salt.
Chop the tofu into 2cm squares then toss them through the cornflour mixture. Transfer to a baking tray lined with baking parchment and drizzle with oil. Bake for 20-30 mins, until golden and crispy.

Meanwhile, finely grate the ginger and garlic into a saucepan. Add a drizzle of olive oil and set the heat to medium. Once sizzling and fragrant, add the tomato purée and curry powder and cook, stirring, until the tomato purée has darkened. Transfer the mixture to a heatproof bowl then stir through the peanut butter and vegetable stock powder.

For the pickled slaw, finely shred the brussels sprouts. Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the stems. Thinly slice the chilli. Place the sprouts, coriander stems and chilli into a bowl, pour the vinegar over and season the mix with salt, pepper and sugar to taste. Set aside to mingle.

Fill the empty saucepan with water and set it over a medium-high heat. Bring to a boil then add the ramen noodles and cook following packet instructions. Before draining, add a ladle of the noodle water (around 200ml, but reserve a little extra if you're increasing the serving or prefer a looser sauce) into the peanut butter mixture and whisk until smooth.
To serve, divide the peanut sauce between bowls. Top with the noodles, crispy tofu and brussels sprout slaw.

name: Crispy Egg Fried Rice
description: A quick, cheap take on this spicy, fragrant Indonesian classic. Works perfectly as breakfast or dinner.
instructions: Rinse your rice. Boil it in 2 times the amount of water.
Grate carrots and the ginger. Finely slice one red chilli, cloves of garlic, the coriander stalks and the onion. Slice up your pak choi, keeping the white stalks and the leaves separate.

Pour some vegetable oil into a large pan. Fry the onions and garlic until softened. Add the grated ginger and the sliced red chilli. Allow to soften. Add the coriander stalks and the grated carrot. Mix everything together, cook for a further minute or so. Add the cooked rice.
Mix together and add the Nasi Goreng Paste. Mix it all in.
Add the pak choi stalks. Allow to cook for 3 minutes and then add the pak choi leaves.
Mix everything together. Cook for a further minute and remove from the heat.
Serve the rice steaming hot and place the fried eggs on top. Cut into those runny yolks and enjoy!

name: Crispy Eggs & Chorizo Black Beans
description: Your new favourite brunch option. The chorizo-ey charred veggies and black beans.
instructions: Finely dice the onion and peppers. Place a frying pan over medium heat with the chorizo. Once the oil has come out, add the peppers and chilli, cook until softened, 8-10 mins.

Drain the beans, reserving the liquid. Add the beans into the veg, with a good crack of black pepper. Lightly crush some of the beans with a spoon, add a splash of bean liquid and leave to simmer on low heat until piping hot and thickened slightly. Taste and season with salt, if needed.

Time for those eggs! Add a generous amount of oil to a pan and fry your eggs until the whites are slightly crispy and the yolks are runny. A great way to ensure this is to baste the eggs in the hot oil with a spoon. Season with salt and pepper.
Share the beans onto plates and top with the crispy fried egg. Finish with a scattering of coriander and serve with a wedge of lime and tortilla crisps.

name: Crispy Feta Burger
description: Halloumi? Nah, I'll have feta thanks. This might seem a lot, but trust me, once it's crispy, covered in breadcrumbs and pickled bits and bobs, it rips. B x
instructions: Pat the feta dry with some kitchen roll. Season the flour with salt and pepper, crack the egg into a bowl and get the breadcrumbs in another. Pass the feta through the flour, egg, and breadcrumb to thoroughly coat.
Slice the aubergine and grill with a little olive oil in a very hot griddle pan until charred and cooked through. Season with salt and lemon juice.
Season the tomato with salt, pepper, and olive oil.
Toast the burger buns in a hot pan. Remove from the pan, add a good glug of oil and pop the feta in. Cook for 4 mins on each side until golden brown, crispy and cooked through.

Time to build. Add your pesto to the bottom bun and top it with your seasoned tomatoes before piling on the crispy feta, aubergine, pickles, herbs, and chilli jam. Crown with the top bun, give it a squish, and get stuck in.

name: Crispy Feta, Olive and Harissa Phyllo Parcels
description: These are the most simple but satisfying crispy phyllo parcels, perfect as a starter, or a to have with a cold beer...
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200c
Melt the butter in a small saucepan and put to one side.
Grab a sheet of phyllo and lay it out vertically. Leaving a 2 inch gap from the edge closest to you, spread the olive tapenade into a rough rectangle about the size of the block of feta.
Place the feta on top of the tapenade and cover with the harissa.
Now brush the whole surface of the phyllo sheet with the melted butter, using a pastry brush (a finger works well too!).
Fold the exposed edge of the pastry over the feta, and then continue to fold away from you. Fold the sides in and continue until you have a rectangular parcel and the feta is completely covered.
Repeat the same process using the second sheet of phyllo. Spread the entire surface with butter, place the wrapped feta on top and fold up.
Once you have the finished parcel, brush all over with the remaining butter and transfer to a baking tray. Place into the oven for 15-20 mins until golden brown.
Remove from the oven, allow to cool for 5 mins, then drizzle with the honey and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve warm and enjoy!

name: Crispy Fish Finger Katsu Salad with Curry Dressing
description: All the best bits of a katsu curry (crispy coating, curry mayo and pickles) but in a bright, crunchy salad. And yes, we’re using fish fingers.
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C. Add the fish fingers to a baking tray and bake for 15 mins, turning halfway. You can also air-fry them at 180°C for 10 mins.
Peel and finely slice the red onion. Add to a bowl with a big pinch of salt and the juice of half a lemon. Massage gently and set aside to pickle.
Heat the olive oil in a small pan over a low heat. Grate in the garlic and cook for 30 secs until fragrant. Stir in the curry powder, cook for another 10 secs, then take it off the heat.

In a small bowl, mix together the yoghurt, mayonnaise and mango chutney. Add the garlic curry oil and stir to combine. Loosen the dressing with a splash of water (one tablespoon at a time) until it’s the consistency of double cream. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Quarter the radishes. Halve the cucumber lengthways, then again into quarters. Chop into small chunks.
Finely shred the hispi cabbage and add to a large bowl with the remaining lemon juice, sesame oil and a pinch of salt. Massage for 1 min until it just starts to soften.
Heat the rice according to pack instructions. Tip into the cabbage bowl along with the cucumber and radish, then toss everything together.
To serve, divide the salad between plates. Top with crispy fish fingers, a generous drizzle of curry dressing, the pickled onions, sesame seeds and fresh coriander.

name: Crispy Fish With Salt & Vinegar Chips
description: No deep fryer in sight here, just oven chips and crispy pan-fried fish. Consider this a lighter take on fish and chips. We’ve chosen to use salmon as it’s dead simple to cook and your reward is delightfully crispy skin, but you could use cod, haddock, pollock, or whatever.
instructions: Peel and cut your potatoes into chunky chips. Wash under cold running water to ditch any excess starch and pop them into a big saucepan.

Cover with fresh cold water and add the vinegar and two big handfuls of salt. Bring to a bare simmer and cook for 8-10 mins. The vinegar sets the outside of the chip and they take on an almost bouncy texture. It’s weird, but it’s delicious, trust me.
Preheat your oven to 225°C.
Grab a large roasting tin and add a good layer of vegetable oil, as if you’re making roast potatoes. Preheat the tray in the oven.

Once your chips are cooked, fish them out of the salt and vinegar bath and let them steam dry for a couple of mins. Carefully remove the preheated oil from the oven and add the chips to the hot fat. Return to the oven for 35-40 mins, turning every 6-7 mins, until golden brown and crispy.

While your chips are roasting, season your salmon with salt and cook, skin-side down in a non-stick pan over a medium heat for 6-7 mins until the skin is crispy and golden brown. The salmon should be about 70% cooked, you can measure this by checking the change in colour moving through the fillet. Flip the fish for the last 30% and then rest.

Pour a kettle of boiling water over the peas in a heatproof bowl. Leave for 3 mins then drain. Using a fork, coarsely smush the peas with the zest of one lemon and the butter. Season with salt and pepper.
Once your chips are ready, season with salt. Divide between plates with the salmon and peas and finish with a lemon wedge. Serve with ketchup and tartar for dipping.

name: Crispy Fried Aubergine With Minty Ricotta & Sumac Onion Salad
description: We’ve coated aubergine slices in Parmesan breadcrumbs, shallow-fried them to crispy perfection and served them with creamy ricotta and a zingy parsley salad. Incredible as a starter or piled into a sandwich.
keywords: Crispy Fried Aubergine With Minty Ricotta & Sumac Onion Salad
Crispy Fried Aubergine With Minty Ricotta & Sumac Onion Salad recipe
instructions: Finely chop the mint and add to a bowl along with the ricotta and a big pinch of salt. Mix to combine then set aside.

Finely slice the red onion and add to a medium mixing bowl. Cover with cold water and use your fingers to break the onion slivers apart, swishing them around in the water a bit (this takes out some of the strength of the raw onion flavour) then drain.
Add the vinegar to the onions, mix well and leave to sit for 5 mins, then drain.
Finely chop the parsley and add to the onions along with the sumac, a big pinch of salt and a glug of olive oil. Mix well and set aside.

Slice the aubergines into roughly 1cm thick slices then lay them flat on your board and sprinkle generously with salt on both sides. Put the flour, breadcrumbs and whisked eggs on three separate plates. Grate the Parmesan into the breadcrumbs and mix to combine. Stir a pinch of salt through the flour.
Dust the aubergine slices first in flour, then the egg and finally the breadcrumbs until well coated. Pop them onto a tray or plate until ready to fry.

Pour the sunflower oil into a large frying pan until it’s about 1cm deep. Set the pan over a medium heat until the oil reaches 160°C. Carefully add the aubergine slices (don’t overcrowd the pan – you might need to do two batches) and fry for a few mins until golden then flip and repeat for the other side. Remove the aubergines to a tray or plate lined with kitchen paper and sprinkle generously with sea salt.
Spoon a big dollop of ricotta onto each plate and spread it out a bit. Top with a few slices of crunchy aubergine and some of the onion salad.

name: Crispy Fried Egg Salad & Cumin Rice
description: Crispy fried eggs drenched in a punchy, limey fish sauce dressing over fragrant cumin rice, I came back from Thailand completely obsessed with Yum Khai Dao and this is my version. Super easy to make and even easier to eat - I love it.
keywords: Crispy Fried Egg Salad & Cumin Rice
Crispy Fried Egg Salad & Cumin Rice recipe
instructions: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear, then add to a medium saucepan with the water, cumin and a big pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover with a lid and cook gently for 12 mins. Remove from the heat and leave to stand for 10 mins before fluffing with a fork.

Meanwhile, cut the tomatoes into wedges and finely slice the shallot. Grate the garlic and finely slice the chilli into a large bowl. Add the fish sauce, squeeze in the juice of the limes and add the sugar. Whisk together, taste and add a little more sugar if needed. Add the tomatoes and shallot to the dressing and set aside. Roughly chop the coriander.

Coat the bottom of a large frying pan with about 1cm of vegetable oil. Heat over a high heat, then carefully crack in the eggs, they will splutter! Baste the yolks with the hot oil and cook until the edges are golden and crispy but the yolk is still to your liking.
Stir the coriander through the tomato salad. Then serve up the rice topped with the tomato salad and crispy eggs, making sure to drizzle over the dressing.

name: Crispy Garlic Butter Prawn Gnocchi with Chilli Oil
description: Imagine Prawns Pil Pil in gnocchi form. A garlicky brown butter sauce with juicy prawns and burst cherry tomatoes all tossed with golden pan-fried gnocchi, which gives the same vibe as the toasty bread you have with prawns pil pil. Summer comfort at its best. In Partnership with Aldi. #ad.
cuisine: Italian, Italian-Inspired, Spanish, Spanish-Inspired, Mediterranean, Mediterranean-Inspired
keywords: Crispy Garlic Butter Prawn Gnocchi with Chilli Oil
Crispy Garlic Butter Prawn Gnocchi with Chilli Oil recipe
instructions: Finely chop the garlic. Heat half the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, add the gnocchi and cook for 6-8 mins, until golden, then remove from the pan with a slotted spoon.

Add the butter to the pan and melt until foaming and bubbly. Keep cooking and swirling the pan for 3-4 mins, until the milk solids turn golden and it smells like biscuits. Add the rest of the oil along with the garlic and cook for a minute. Add the prawns and cherry tomatoes and cook for 5 mins, until the prawns are bright pink and cooked through.
Zest and juice the lemon and finely chop the parsley. Tip the gnocchi back into the prawns and mix well to coat, then add the lemon zest, juice and parsley. Taste and season with salt and pepper
Serve up topped with a drizzle of the chilli oil and the remaining parsley.

name: Crispy Garlic Chicken with Lime Chilli Broccoli & Rice
description: This dish is all about the garlic sauce. We’ve cooked the garlic in three batches to release all the different layers of garlic flavour – an ode to a traditional Cantonese technique.
instructions: Mince the garlic and spring onion. Slice the broccoli into thirds diagonally. Thinly slice the red chilli. Cook the rice following pack instructions.

For the sauce, heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a small saucepan or frying pan set over a medium heat. Add ⅓ of the garlic to the pan and cook for 45 seconds, stirring occasionally. Add another ⅓ of the garlic and sauté for another 45 seconds. Add the remaining garlic along with the spring onion and cook for 30 seconds. Turn the heat off, add the oyster sauce and MSG, and stir to combine. Set aside while you cook the chicken.

For the chicken, mix the Chinese 5 spice with a generous glug of olive oil and ½ the salt. Get the chicken skin side down and brush the marinade onto the flesh. Flip it over with the skin facing upwards and sprinkle with the remaining salt.

Add the chicken to a cold frying pan skin side down and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook for 4-5 mins or until the skin is crispy then flip it over and cook for a further 2-3 mins. Remove from the pan and leave to rest for at least 2-3 mins.

Get the same pan back over a medium-high heat, add the broccoli and fry for 1 min. Add the sliced red chilli followed by the sake. Shake the pan (this will help the broccoli cook evenly) and cook for 2-3 mins. When the mixture is glossy and dark green, zest in the lime and add a squeeze of lime juice. Turn the heat off and toss to combine.

To serve, slice the cooked chicken thighs into 2cm strips. Spoon the rice onto one half of a plate and add the broccoli to the other side. Place the sliced chicken in the middle, sitting on top of the rice and broccoli. Generously spoon over the garlic sauce directly onto the crispy chicken skin. Enjoy!

name: Crispy Garlic Tomato & Cheese Toasts
description: Mini ciabattas transformed into pizza-like toasts loaded with fresh garlic slices, layers of cheese and cherry tomatoes. A breeze to make.
instructions: Preheat the grill to high.

Thinly slice the garlic cloves and add to a cold pan. Thinly slice the red onion and add half to the pan. Cover with olive oil and set over a medium heat. Cook until the onions and garlic are golden brown, 10-12 mins. Meanwhile, halve the cherry tomatoes using a couple of small plates. Add a handful of tomatoes to the bottom plate and place the second, facedown over the tomatoes. Run a bread knife through the middle, halving all the tomatoes at once.
Slice the ciabatta in half, rub with oil and grate over half of the cheese. Slide under the grill until golden brown.

Fish the crispy garlic and onions out of the pan and tip in the tomatoes. Cook for 2 mins in the hot oil and add a big pinch of salt and the sherry vinegar. Cook for 30 secs and add the remaining red onion and basil. Season and toss everything together.
Add the bread to four plates and top with the warm tomatoes. Scatter over the crispy garlic and onion oil and serve topped with remaining grated cheese.

name: Crispy Ginger Sesame Beef
description: The stickiest crispy beef stir fried with crunchy charred broccoli.  All in a gingery, sesame-ey sauce. Delicious.
instructions: Cut your beef into strips.
Add your cornflour into a bowl and dip in the beef strips. Make sure each strip is evenly coated.

Add a very big glug of vegetable oil to a wok. Once the oil is hot, throw in your beef. Fry the beef in batches so they have space to fry. Remove when nice, brown and crispy (about 3-4 minutes). Set the beef aside.
Pour away the leftover oil and clean your wok. Heat a small splash of vegetable oil in the wok and add your broccoli. Fry on a high heat so that it starts to char.
Finely chop your spring onions and slice your ginger and garlic. Once the broccoli is charred and al dente stir through the chopped spring onions and ginger. Fry for a minute then add in the garlic.
Add in the sesame oil and chilli oil and toss together. Then add in the honey, rice vinegar and soy sauce.
Time to reintroduce your beef. Chuck the beef strips into the pan and add 30ml of water. On a medium heat, keep tossing until your sauce comes together, thickens and turns nice and sticky.
Prepare your ready-to-eat rice.
Serve the jasmine rice into 4 bowls. Spoon over your gingery beef strips and scatter over the sesame seeds. Dig in!

name: Crispy Gnocchi Caesar Salad
description: We’ve swapped the croutons in a classic caesar salad with moreish, filled crispy gnocchi. It’s a real winner.
ingredients: 1Pack La Famiglia Rana Garlic & Mozzarella Filled Pan Fry Gnocchi
instructions: For the dressing, finely grate the garlic into a bowl. Add ½ the anchovies and mash with a fork to create a paste then stir through the mayo, mustard, the juice of the lemon and ½ the grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper. If it’s too thick, stir through a splash of cold water.
Roughly tear the lettuce and pick the parsley leaves (discarding the stalks) then toss with the rocket.

Heat a frying pan with a drizzle of olive oil or some butter as you prefer. Once hot, add the La Famiglia Rana Garlic & Mozzarella Filled Pan-Fry Gnocchi and pan-fry for at least 5 mins until crispy and golden.
Toss the salad mixture into the dressing, with the remaining anchovies, capers, and remaining grated Parmesan. Share between plates and top with the crispy gnocchi.

name: Crispy Gnocchi with Burrata and Pesto
description: Has a more summery dish ever existed? Creamy, oozy burrata; jammy, charred tomatoes; bright, fresh pesto; and golden gnocchi. Dreams can come true.
instructions: Bash your garlic to crush it slightly. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil, your garlic and the rosemary. Fry for a couple of minutes until the garlic is lightly golden, then remove from the pan.
Tip your gnocchi into the same pan, sprinkle in some salt and turn up the heat. Fry for 15 mins until crispy and golden all over.

In a separate frying pan, heat a little olive oil. Add your cherry tomatoes along with a pinch of salt, then fry these for 10 mins. They should be softened and charring, but not totally collapsed. Add your chilli flakes and fry for a minute more.
Make your pesto. Toast your pine nuts in a dry frying pan until golden.

Tip almost all of your pine nuts into a food processor, reserving a little, along with your basil. Grate in your parmesan and whizz to a paste. Gradually pour in the olive oil until you have a smooth green sauce. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Assembly time. Pour your gnocchi onto a large serving plate and top with your cherry tomatoes. Drizzle over some pesto, then tear your burrata over the top. Finish with a grinding of black pepper, a drizzle of olive oil and your remaining pine nuts. Serve and enjoy.

name: Crispy Gochujang Tofu with Pear Slaw
description: Chunky, crispy, sticky gochujang tofu served with brown rice and a pear, cabbage, spring onion and coriander slaw, leaning into Korean flavours for a midweek meal with a punch.
keywords: Crispy Gochujang Tofu with Pear Slaw
Crispy Gochujang Tofu with Pear Slaw recipe
instructions: Break the tofu into chunky pieces, then toss in a large bowl with the cornflour. Heat half the sesame oil in a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat, then add the tofu and cook for 8-10 mins, until golden and crispy. Mix the gochujang, honey and water together, then pour over the tofu to coat and remove from the heat. Swap the honey for maple syrup or agave to make it completely vegan.

Cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Finely slice the pear, cabbage and spring onion. Add the cabbage to a bowl with a pinch of salt and the rice vinegar, massaging until softened. Add the rest of the sesame oil, the toasted sesame seeds, the pear and the spring onion and mix to combine. Pick the coriander leaves.
Serve the rice with the slaw and sticky tofu, scattered with the coriander leaves.

name: Crispy Grilled Corn with Nutty Salsa Verde
description: Sweet, charred corn on the cob, topped with grated parmesan and smothered in a delicious, hazelnutty salsa verde. A side so good it’ll take centre stage! Zena x
keywords: how to cook corn on the cob
crispy grilled corn wtih nutty salsa verde
instructions: Finely chop the parsley, coriander, mint, red chilli, red onion and hazelnuts and mince the garlic. Transfer to a mixing bowl.
Add the red wine vinegar, sugar and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Set aside.
Heat a griddle pan or barbecue until hot.
Rub the corn with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Grill for 12 to 15 mins, turning regularly until lightly charred and cooked through.
Plate up the corn and grate over the parmesan. Top with the nutty salsa verde then serve and enjoy!

name: Crispy Harissa Lamb Hummus Bowl
description: Golden, spicy lamb, creamy hummus and fresh zingy salad all scooped up with crisp flatbreads. A dunker’s dream dinner.
keywords: crispy harissa lamb mince hummus bowl
instructions: Finely zest the lemon, then juice half the lemon, keeping the rest to serve.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a splash of olive oil. Add the lamb mince and fry, breaking it up with a spoon, for about 10 mins until deep golden and crispy. Stir through the harissa paste, cumin and chilli flakes, if using. 
Slice the green chillies into thin rounds and scatter half into the pan for extra heat. Let it sizzle for 2 mins until glossy and fragrant, then season to taste.
Finely slice the red onion and toss it in a bowl with the juice of half the lemon, sumac and a pinch of salt. Set aside to soften and lightly pickle.
Chop the tomatoes and cucumber into small chunks. Toss them with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of sumac, the lemon zest and a little chopped parsley for freshness.
Spread the hummus over the base of two shallow bowls. Toast the flatbreads in the lamb fat left in the pan until golden and crisp at the edges.

Pile the spicy lamb onto the hummus. Add the pickled onion and tomato-cucumber salad. Finish with the remaining chopped parsley, chopped dill, sesame seeds and the remaining sliced green chilli. Serve with the crispy flatbreads for dunking and the remaining lemon wedges.

name: Crispy Harissa Vegan Mince With Squash Hummus
description: This hummus bowl topped with veggie mince is the perfect balance of creamy, crispy, sticky textures and packed with flavour.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Peel and dice the squash into 2-3cm chunks. Toss with olive oil, the ras el hanout and salt and roast for 20-25 mins until just tender.

Add the squash to a food processor with the garlic, lemon juice, chickpeas, tahini, 45ml of olive oil and a splash of water. Whizz together until super smooth, add a splash more water if you need to. Season to taste.

Slice the onion as thinly as you can and add to a bowl. Finely chop the parsley and add to the bowl with the sumac and the juice of half a lemon. Add a pinch of salt and scrunch together, set aside to macerate.

Add the veggie mince to a frying pan. Dice the onion and chuck into the pan with a shot of oil and a pinch of salt. Cook over a high heat until crispy. Grate in the garlic and add the harissa and molasses. Stir together and cook until crispy, sticky and glazed.
Spread your warm hummus onto a serving plate, top with the crispy mince and sumac onions. Serve with grilled flatbreads or steamy pittas.

name: Crispy Honey Chipotle Wings
description: Crispy battered deep-fried wings coated in a sticky lime, honey and chipotle sauce. These are perfect for snacking on, just keep some napkins nearby.
instructions: Coat the wings in 100g cornflour and set aside.
In another bowl, combine the remaining 60g cornflour with 30g plain flour, ½ tsp salt, and 150ml of ice cold water. Whisk until smooth.
In a small saucepan, heat the butter with the Bull’s-Eye Louisiana Chipotle With Cajun Spices Hot Sauce, the juice of a lime, and 3 tbsp honey. Mix and bring to a bubble before cooking for 5 mins.
Heat up a large pot of vegetable oil for frying the wings.
Dip the wings in the batter and then straight into the frying oil. Deep fry on a medium-high heat for 5-6 mins until lightly golden and very crispy.
Toss the wings in the sauce and serve with finely chopped chives.

name: Crispy Honey Jerk Pork Bánh Mì
description: Get ready for a fusion feast! This recipe from Lauren Wilmott (@cheflaurenwilz) blends two well-known Jamaican recipes with classic Vietnamese bánh mì. It’s a tasty, textured delight, perfect for summer or for making the most of leftover pork belly.
keywords: Crispy Honey Jerk Pork Bánh Mì
Crispy Honey Jerk Pork Bánh Mì recipe
instructions: Start by prepping the pork the night before or at least 3 hrs prior. Begin by puncturing the entire pork skin with a knife, then generously sprinkle sea salt all over the skin. Next, score the flesh side of the pork both vertically and horizontally.
Blend all the jerk paste ingredients together. Reserve one-third of the jerk paste and massage the remaining two-thirds into the pork flesh only.
Place the prepared pork on a rack-lined tray in the fridge. Leave uncovered overnight to allow the flavours to soak in and the skin to dry.
On the day of cooking, heat the oven to 160°C. Remove the pork from the fridge and wipe away any excess salt from the skin, ensuring it's thoroughly dry.
Roast the pork in a roasting tin for approximately 40 mins until tender.
While the pork is cooking, thinly slice the carrot, shallot, peppers, Scotch bonnet and mango into julienne strips. Set aside.

Prepare the pickling liquor by combining the apple cider vinegar, sugar, white peppercorns and pimento seeds in a small saucepan. Add water, to taste. Simmer over a low heat for 5 mins until the sugar completely dissolves.
Place all the julienned vegetables (except the mango) into a heatproof bowl and pour the pickling liquor over them. Wrap the bowl in cling film to enhance the flavours.
Pick the coriander leaves and set them aside in cold water to keep them fresh.

After the initial 40 mins of cooking, increase the oven temperature to 220°C and continue to roast the pork for an additional 20-25 mins until the skin starts to blister and turns golden brown. Turn the grill onto low, then transfer the bellies under until the skin goes crispy and crackles, 3-6 mins.Let the pork rest for 15-20 mins before chopping.
Meanwhile, combine the reserved jerk paste with 2 tbsp water and 2 tbsp honey in a saucepan. Heat over a medium heat until it thickens into a sticky glaze.
Slice the pork bellies and brush with the prepared honey jerk glaze.
Cut open the baguettes and spread mayonnaise over the bread.
Layer slices of the glazed pork onto the bread, then top with the pickled vegetables and fresh coriander.
Serve and enjoy your flavourful crispy honey jerk pork bánh mì.

name: Crispy Honey Mustard Salmon & Grains
description: Sticky mustard-glazed salmon on top of zingy lemony grains with wilted greens. A weeknight winner that’s on the table in 15.
instructions: Place a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the salmon skin-side down and cook undisturbed for 5-6 mins, until it’s about three-quarters done.
Meanwhile, boil a full kettle. Put the spinach in a colander and pour over the boiling water to wilt it. Once cool enough to handle, squeeze out any excess water.
Roughly chop the dill. Zest ½ the lemon. Warm the grains if needed, then toss them with the spinach, dill, basil leaves and lemon zest. Season with salt and set aside.
Flip the salmon and add the mustard and honey straight into the pan. Let it bubble for a minute, then spoon the glaze over the fish as it finishes cooking through.
Squeeze a little lemon juice into the glaze to loosen it. Share the grains onto plates, top with the salmon and spoon over the sticky mustard glaze.

name: Crispy Kale & Creamy Avocado Salad
description: This one’s all about addictively crispy kale and spiced crispy chickpeas tossed with a creamy avocado dressing. Dotted with apple and a kick of red chilli.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Toss the chickpeas in oil, cayenne pepper and 1⁄2 tsp salt. Pop onto a baking tray and roast for 20 mins.
Massage the kale with 1 tbsp oil and 1⁄2 tsp salt until it feels moist. Add the kale to the baking tray and continue cooking for another 20 mins until everything is very crispy.
Thinly slice the apples and red chilli.
Grate your Parmesan then blend it with the juice of half a lemon, jalapeño, avocado and Dijon mustard until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook the bulgur wheat according to packet instructions.
Pile the bulgur wheat into a bowl and top with the crispy kale, chickpeas, apples and drizzle with the avocado dressing. Top with sliced chillies and enjoy.

name: Crispy Lamb Gnocchi
description: This is an easy gnocchi recipe with some serious brunt. Rich lamb, fragrant mint, and a hint of sweetness from pomegranate molasses? It's good. It's damn good.
instructions: Put a pot of water on to boil and season generously with salt. Set a large frying pan over a high heat and add a splash of olive oil.
Crumble the lamb mince into the pan and allow to brown, moving the lamb now and then, for 10 mins until very crispy. Meanwhile, thinly slice the red onions and pick the leaves from the mint.

Remove the lamb from the pan, leaving behind any residual fat. Add most of the onions (saving a handful) to the pan with the lamb fat and return to the heat. Cook with a pinch of salt until very caramelised. This will take 5-6 mins over a high heat. Sprinkle in the ras el hanout and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant.
Drop your gnocchi into the boiling water and cook according to the package instructions. Add a splash of the gnocchi water to the pan to slow down the cooking and start building a sauce.
Toss the cooked gnocchi through the lamb fat and onions, add the crispy lamb, the mint and the molasses. Toss together, adding water if you need to loosen things up.
Divide between warm plates and get stuck in.

name: Crispy Lamb with Creamy Brothy Rice & Za'atar
description: This soothing rice bowl is full of flavour with Lebanese 7-spice, sumac and a za’atar drizzle. A midweek winner that’s ready in under 30 minutes.
keywords: Crispy Lamb with Creamy Brothy Rice & Za'atar
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the garlic. Thinly slice the onions and toss with the sumac. Finely mince the coriander, stalks and all.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the lamb mince and cook for 5-10 mins until crispy, making sure to break up the mince as it cooks. Stir through the Lebanese 7-spice and ½ the garlic and cook for about 30 secs until fragrant. Transfer the lamb to a plate.

Set the same pan back over a medium-high heat. Add the remaining garlic, fresh coriander and dried mint and cook for about 5 mins until softened. Pour in the chicken stock and let it come to the boil. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, reheat the cooked rice. Melt the butter, transfer to a small bowl and stir through the za’atar.
Before serving, remove the broth from the heat and leave it for a minute to cool slightly. Stir through the kefir then taste and season with salt and pepper.
Divide the rice between bowls and ladle over the creamy broth. Top with the crispy lamb mince, sumac onions and a drizzle of za’atar butter.

name: Crispy Lemongrass Chicken
description: Lemongrass & chicken is a match made in heaven. So fragrant. The crunchy breadcrumb coating tops it off. We bake, rather than fry, to keep it healthy.
instructions: Preheat oven at 180°C/356°F and line a baking tray with greaseproof paper.

Prepare chicken breasts. Place a sheet of greaseproof on your work surface and fold in half to sandwich each piece of chicken between the two layers. Using a rolling pin, bash the chicken 2-3 cm thick. Do this in batches.

Get three bowls. In bowl one, mix all the dry ingredients together (panko breadcrumbs, flax seeds, garlic granules, sesame seeds, chilli flakes, zest of the lemons, salt, pepper). In bowl two, whisk the egg and the soy together. Last but not least, in a shallow bowl pour out your flour.
Dip each chicken breast into the egg then into the flour. Dust off any excess flour and then roll your chicken in the breadcrumbs. Fill in any gaps with egg and crumb.

Place your chicken breasts on your baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Then bake depending on your fillet size, however, we recommend 30 minutes making sure to turn your chicken pieces halfway through your cooking time. You want your chicken golden with a crisp texture.

While your chicken is in the oven make your side salad. To start with, deseed and slice your cucumber. Thinly slice your radishes and chop your herbs (mint and coriander), mix in a generous amount of salt.
Mix your fish sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, coconut (saving some for garnish) and lime juice together. Then mix with your salad veg.
For your citrus mayo, mix up all your glaze ingredients - mayo, lemongrass and a dash of water.
Chop your cashews then time to serve up. Thinly slice your chicken, spoon up some salad, a sprinkle of cashews and coconut, and drizzle of the citrus glaze.

name: Crispy Lemongrass Chicken & Corn Stir-Fry
description: Golden, caramelised chicken mince with sweet charred corn, fiery bird's-eye chillies and fragrant lemongrass. A punchy, speedy stir-fry that's on the table in 25 mins.
keywords: Sticky Lemongrass Chicken & Corn Stir-Fry recipe
instructions: Cut the corn kernels off the cobs. Bash the lemongrass with the back of a knife, then mince finely. Mince the garlic and finely slice the chillies.

Set a large wok over a high heat and add a generous glug of vegetable oil. Working in two batches, add the chicken mince in pieces and leave to fry for 5 mins without touching, so it crisps up. Break up any clumps and continue frying for 3-4 mins until golden brown all over.

Add the garlic, lemongrass and chillies (bird's-eye chillies pack a punch, so use fewer if you don't want it too spicy) season with salt and white pepper, then stir-fry for another minute. Add the soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar and toss to coat. Add a splash of water if you'd like it more saucier. Pop in the corn and stir-fry for a further 2-3 mins.
Heat the rice according to packet instructions. Cut the lime into wedges. Serve the stir-fry over rice with fresh mint and a wedge of lime.

name: Crispy Mushroom & Black Bean Tacos with Pea Guacamole
description: Tasty vegan tacos with a homemade pea guacamole. Vegan recipes don't get better than this.
keywords: Crispy Mushroom & Black Bean Tacos with Pea Guacamole
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Roughly chop the mushrooms and put them in a small baking dish. Add all of the mushroom spices and plenty of olive oil, salt and black pepper. Toss to combine and roast for 25-30 mins until golden and caramelised, stirring at least twice to get an even cook.

Meanwhile, make the beans. Finely slice the onion and mince the garlic. Fry the onion in a large saucepan with a little olive oil for 8-10 mins until softened, then add the garlic. Add the tomato purée, soy sauce and spices and cook for a few more minutes until all the flavours have combined.

Add the sun-dried tomatoes and drained beans. Rinse the bean tin and fill it halfway with water, then add this to the pan. Simmer for about 10 mins until most of the liquid has evaporated and the beans have really softened.
To make the pea guacamole, defrost the peas and then put all of the ingredients into a small blender and blitz until almost smooth. Set aside.

To assemble, brush one side of the tortillas with olive oil and heat on this side in a large frying pan. Fill one half of each tortilla with the beans and mushrooms, then close them up. Fry them in the pan over a medium heat for 2 mins on each side until crispy on both sides.
Serve with the pea guacamole, some extra lime and pickles, if you like.

name: Crispy Mushroom Fritters With Chilli Crisp Mayo
description: Umami-packed extra crispy mushroom fritters with spicy chilli crisp mayo. The two pair perfectly together and it only takes 10 minutes to whip up!
keywords: Crispy Mushroom Fritters with Gochujang Mayo
instructions: Trim the enoki, place them into a bowl and pull them into smaller chunks. Tear the remaining mushrooms into similar sizes and add them to the enoki. Tear up the sheet of nori into small flakes and add to the mushrooms.
Add both flours along with your smoked paprika, sesame seeds, and 1 tsp of salt into the mushrooms. Toss well.
Whisk the egg with the sparkling water together, then pour onto the mushrooms and toss well, until the flours have rehydrated and the mushrooms are covered in a paste.
Fill a deep saucepan halfway up with oil. Place it over a high heat and heat to 180°C. Line a plate with kitchen paper.
Drop batches of the mushroom batter into the oil and cook for 2-4 mins until crispy.
Mix the mayo with your chilli oil, set aside.
Serve the crispy mushroom fritters with the spicy mayo and a side of Spotify's Mushroom Jazz Mix playlist.

name: Crispy Mushroom Hoisin Noodles
description: A quick and delicious noodle stir fry with sweet hoisin and super crunchy mushrooms.
instructions: Tear the oyster mushrooms into small pieces.
Combine the cornflour, salt and five-spice powder in a bowl. Toss this with the mushrooms until evenly coated.
Fill a wok with some vegetable oil and bring it to medium heat, add in the mushrooms and fry for 5 mins until very crispy.
Make the sauce by combining the hoisin sauce, tahini, light soy sauce, sesame oil, and dark soy sauce.
Cook your noodles according to the package instructions, then run them under cold water.
Finely chop the garlic, spring onions, chilli and ginger. Slice up the sugar snap peas.
Remove the oil from the wok and wipe clean. Get the wok back on the heat and add in a big drizzle of oil.
Fry off the spring onions, ginger, garlic and chilli until fragrant for 2 mins.
Then add in the sugar snap peas and noodles and toss around in the aromatics, add in the sauce and give it another toss so they are evenly coated.
Serve it up in bowls and top with your crispy mushrooms and enjoy.

name: Crispy Mushroom Pancakes
description: For too long, vegans have been made to go without crispy duck pancakes. No more. We’ve replaced duck with meaty mushrooms in this completely plant-based recipe.
instructions: Tear your mushrooms into shreds with your hands.
Toss them in a bowl with your cornflour, five spice and pinch of salt, then toss to coat.

Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a frying pan. Add ¼ of your mushrooms, then fry for a few mins until crispy. You may need to flip them over. Remove from the pan and drain on a tray lined with kitchen paper, then continue with your remaining mushrooms.
Add just a little of your hoisin sauce to your mushrooms, and toss to coat.
Julienne your cucumber and spring onions.
Warm up your Chinese pancakes.
Serve your crispy mushrooms with your remaining hoisin sauce, cucumber and spring onions in your pancakes.

name: Crispy Mushroom Rice
description: The crispiest rice with buttery, woody roasted mushrooms. This umami-rich beauty is perfect for meal prep. Eat it fresh for dinner then transfer the leftovers to containers and enjoy it hot or cold the next day.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Wash the rice until the water runs clear, then place into a bowl and cover with water. Leave to soak whilst prepping the other bits (15-20 mins). Whisk the miso and stock together.

Meanwhile, finely slice or tear the mushrooms into 1cm chunks. Place onto a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil and ½ the soy sauce. Season with plenty of black pepper then slide into the oven to roast for 30-35 mins until golden brown, flipping the mushrooms halfway through.

Once the rice has soaked, drain the water. Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the butter and let it melt. Stir the soaked rice through, then pour in the rice vinegar, miso stock and remaining soy sauce. Bring to the boil, then place a lid on top and decrease the heat down to low. Cook for 15 mins, uninterrupted.
Meanwhile, finely slice the chives.
Once the rice has cooked, scatter the frozen edamame over, place the lid back on and continue cooking on low for another 10 mins (this will make the bottom of the rice nice and crispy).
Remove the rice from the heat and fluff it up using a fork. Make sure to scrape all the crispy bits of rice from the bottom of the pot.
Serve the rice between bowls and top with the mushrooms. Finish with a sprinkle of chives.

name: Crispy Mushrooms & Coriander Pappardelle
description: You already can't go wrong with pasta. And once you throw crispy mushrooms, coriander, spring onions and soy sauce into the mix, you've got yourself a winning mid-week meal.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Tear the mushrooms into thin strips, put them onto a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then toss together. Bake for 20-25 mins until golden-brown.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. Trim the spring onions and peel the garlic and ginger. Put them into a blender along with the coriander, stalks and all, and the rest of the sauce ingredients. Blend until smooth and set aside.
Lightly crush the Sichuan peppercorns. Trim and thinly slice the remaining spring onions. Once the salted water is boiling, cook the pappardelle for 1 min under al dente, reserving 200ml pasta water.
Once the mushrooms are golden, remove from the oven. Stir through the Sichuan peppercorns, soy sauce and rice vinegar. Return to the oven for 2-3 mins, until evaporated.

Re-use the pasta pan, and pour the sauce into it. Cook over a medium heat until fragrant and deep-green in colour. Toss the pasta through with some pasta water until saucy. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Share the pasta between plates and top with the mushrooms, sliced spring onions and black sesame seeds.

name: Crispy Okra Fries With Green Chutney
description: Okra is a super underrated vegetable. Coated in a light and crispy batter, our okra is excellent when dunked into a coriander-laced chutney.
keywords: Crispy Okra Fries With Green Chutney
instructions: Start by thoroughly washing your okra and letting it dry completely on a kitchen towel.
Slice each okra lengthways down the middle once, and then into quarters. Set aside.
Combine the salt, chilli powder, ground coriander and ground cumin, sprinkle over the sliced okra and mix it all together.
To make the batter, combine the chickpea flour and potato starch with the spices.
Split the dry mix into two bowls, adding 230ml of water to one to create a batter.
Preheat a pot of oil to 180°C.
Dip the okra in the wet batter and then dry, then deep fry in batches until crispy. This will take 4-5 mins. Scoop out the crispy fries and drain on kitchen paper.
To make the green chutney, combine all the ingredients in a blender and blitz, season to taste.
Serve the crispy okra fries with a pot of the zingy green chutney and get stuck in.

name: Crispy One-Pot Veggie Rice
description: All you need is one pot and whatever veggies you've got in your fridge to make this simple, weeknight-friendly recipe. It couldn't be easier. It's one of our favourite vegetarian one pot recipes.
instructions: First, start with your veg. Dice the onion, red pepper, courgette, and tomatoes. Grate half of your garlic cloves and grate and slice one lemon.
Using a large wide cast iron pan, heat up a large glug of oil and add in the onion. Cook on medium-high heat for 10 mins until caramelised and golden.
Add in the red pepper, courgette, smoked paprika, and your grated garlic. Give it a good mix. Continue cooking for 4 mins until the vegetables are softened and have some colour on them.
Add in the diced tomatoes and cook for another 5 mins.
Pour in the vegetable stock and generously season with salt.
Pour in the rice and give it one stir, make sure not to stir more than once because it will release the starch and make the rice stodgy.
Cook on the highest heat for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley.
Lower the heat to medium, put a lid on your pot, and cook for a further 5 mins.
Lower the heat to the lowest and cook for 10-15 mins, until you hear the rice starting to sizzle and crackle.
Turn off the heat and allow it to rest for 5 mins with the lid on.

Blitz up the remaining garlic with a large pinch of salt in a food processor. Once it’s a smooth paste slowly drizzle in the olive oil to form an extremely garlicky sauce. Mix this with the coconut yoghurt. While you're doing that, toast your flaked almonds in a dry frying pan.
Top the rice with parsley, flaked almonds, and a few generous dollops of the garlicky yoghurt. Finally, sprinkle over the lemon zest and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Crispy Parma Ham Gnocchi
description: Crispy gnocchi with tangy, sweet tomato sauce. Topped with crispy parma ham and ricotta. It's the combo of textures and flavours that makes this a worldy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Add the gnocchi, rosemary, cherry tomatoes and vinegar into a baking tray. Finely grate the garlic on top and add half the thyme. Drizzle over some olive oil, season with salt and pepper, toss together. Slide into the oven for 10 mins, until the gnocchi is golden and the tomatoes have softened.
After 10 mins, lay the parma ham on top, flat. Then, return to the oven for another 7-10 mins, until crispy.
Transfer the crispy ham onto a plate and crumble. Toss the gnocchi and tomatoes until saucy, adding a splash of water if needed. Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Spoon the gnocchi onto plates and top with a dollop of ricotta. Scatter over the parma ham and finish with the remaining thyme leaves.

name: Crispy Parmesan Eggs with Black Beans & Tortillas
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Mexican black beans with a charred red pepper salsa and a crispy Parm-fried egg. A delicious plate for brunch, lunch or dinner.
keywords: Crispy Parmesan Eggs with Black Beans & Tortillas
instructions: Finely dice the red onions and thinly slice the garlic cloves.

Heat plenty of olive oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Tip in the red onions and cook for 4-5 mins with a pinch of salt. Add the garlic, cumin and chilli powder and cook for 2 mins before adding the black beans with a splash of their cooking liquid. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 mins. Add another splash of water to loosen the mixture if you like.

Char the whole red chillies on the gas flame of your hob (or under your grill) before finely chopping. Tip into a bowl and add finely chopped parsley and finely chopped grilled red peppers. Season with the sherry vinegar and salt and black pepper to taste.

Finely grate the Parmesan into a large non-stick pan. Set over a medium heat and once the cheese starts to melt, crack the eggs in on top of the cheese. Cook for 4-5 mins – as the cheese cooks, it’ll crisp and fry into the whites of the eggs. If the whites need a bit of help cooking, add a lid for the last minute or so of cooking. Season the eggs with salt and pepper.
Heat the tortillas following packet instructions. Cut the lime into wedges.
Divide the beans between plates and top with the red pepper salsa and a crispy Parm-fried egg. Serve with the warm tortillas and a couple of lime wedges.
