name: Crispy Parmesan Potatoes with Fish Fingers & Tartar Sauce
description: Golden, cheesy roasties with crispy fish fingers all baked in one tray with a tangy dill tartar sauce to finish. It’s like a nostalgic fish and chip night, only way better.
keywords: crispy parmesan potatoes with fish fingers
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C. Finely grate the parmesan. Halve the potatoes and toss them in a bowl with the olive oil, a generous pinch of salt and some black pepper.

Dip the cut side of each potato into the parmesan, pressing to stick a thin layer of cheese onto each one. Arrange on the tray, cheese-side down, leaving space for the fish fingers. Nestle the fish fingers around the tray and and bake until both are golden and crispy and the potatoes are tender, about 30-40 mins.
Meanwhile, zest the lemon into a bowl. Chop half of the dill and finely dice the cornichons. Stir through the yoghurt along with the Dijon mustard. Season to taste, you want it punchy.
Cook the peas following pack instructions.
Cut the lemon into 4 wedges. Serve up the crispy potatoes and fish fingers with a big spoonful of tartar sauce, a lemon wedge and the peas on the side. Sprinkle over the remaining dill. Dig in.

name: Crispy Peanut Chicken & Peanut Curry Rice
description: Juicy, golden chicken thigh drenched in our peanut curry sauce with a crunchy, salty, limey slaw on the side. Dinner sorted.
keywords: Crispy Chicken & Peanut Curry Rice recipe
instructions: Season the chicken thighs generously with salt. Place them skin-side down into a cold frying pan, then set over a medium heat. Let them cook undisturbed for 7–10 mins until the skin is golden and crisp. Flip and cook for another 5–7 mins until fully cooked through.

Meanwhile, thinly slice or mandolin the courgette into a bowl. Pick the coriander leaves, discarding the stalks. Squeeze over half the lime and season the courgette with fish sauce to taste. Toss well and leave to sit.
Reheat the rice and the peanut curry sauce separately until piping hot.
Divide the rice between plates. Add two chicken thighs per person. Toss the coriander through the courgette salad and spoon that alongside. Drizzle over the warm peanut curry sauce to serve.

name: Crispy Pesto Chicken Thighs with Grated Tomato Dressing
description: Could you call this ‘Chicken Con Tomate’? No, but a raw tomato dressing adds a nice lift to this recipe.
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pop into the fridge for 15 mins. Add the potatoes to a pan and cover with cold water. Season with salt and set over a medium heat. Bring to a boil and cook for 10-12 mins until the potatoes are tender. Drain and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Add the basil, saving a few leaves for later, to a food processor. Tip in the pine nuts and finely grate in the garlic clove and Parm. Blitz, drizzling in olive oil, until you have a loose pesto. Season with salt and pepper, squeeze in the juice of the lemon and set aside.
Grab the potatoes and squash them a little, cracking the skins and breaking up the edges. Drizzle with olive oil and salt and get them onto a tray and into the oven to roast.

Pop the chicken thighs, skin side down into a large frying pan and set over a medium heat. Allow the fat to start to render and the skin to get really golden brown and crispy, around 8-10 minutes. Flip them over, sear the underside then pile on top of the potatoes. Slide back into the oven for 15-20 mins or until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are crispy.
Meanwhile, grate the tomatoes into a bowl on the coarse side of a box grater. Add 40ml of olive oil, season well with salt and pepper and add a splash of sherry vinegar.

Pull the chicken and potatoes out of the oven. Grab a serving platter and flood it with the grated tomato. Top with the crispy chicken thighs and potatoes and drizzle with the pesto dressing. Finish extra shaved Parm and the basil leaves.

name: Crispy Pitta Chips
description: These crispy pitta chips are perfect for meal prep. Add them to salads or combine with your choice of protein, carb and veg to create your ideal meal-prep dish.
instructions: Split the pitta in half so you have two thin layers of bread. Cut into whatever shape you fancy, I’ve gone for triangles.
In a mixing bowl, combine your garlic powder, onion powder, your remaining oregano, salt and pepper. Add the pitta pieces to the bowl and stir to coat.
Heat a good glug of oil in a pan then add your pitta pieces. Fry until crunchy and golden.
Transfer to an air tight container and store at room temperature until ready to serve. Enjoy with your choice of dip or as part of a meal-prep dish with your favourite protein, carb and veg.

name: Crispy Pizza Baguettes
description: This is the perfect easy snack. Healthier and tastier than a frozen pizza and ready in the same amount of time! Jordon x
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
In a small saucepan warm 2 tbsp of olive oil over a medium low heat. Finely chop and add the garlic and the oregano and let them sizzle gently for 2 mins. Don’t brown the garlic.
Add the tomatoes and a tsp of salt, bring to a simmer and leave for 10 mins.
Slice open the bread and spread with a layer of the tomato sauce. Pick the basil leaves and add, then tear up the mozzarella and use to top the basil leaves.
Drizzle with olive oil and place directly onto the rack in the oven, with a baking tray underneath.
Cook for about 6 or 7 mins until the cheese is golden and bubbly. Give it a blast under the grill if you need to.
Slice and serve!

name: Crispy Polenta Fries
description: These are an easy snack to make that are especially good if you have any mates round. You'll never look at polenta the same way again.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Cook the instant polenta according to the package instructions as quantities and timings differ between brands.

Once the polenta is cooked, pour it into any shallow square-sided baking tin or oven dish that can accommodate the polenta – you want it to be about 3cm in thickness. Smooth the top over with the back of a spoon and set aside for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, finely chop the chilli and mint and roughly chop the capers. Combine all those ingredients into a small bowl before mixing in the vegan yoghurt, then set aside.

Once the polenta has cooled and set, tip it out onto a cutting board and slice into roughly 8cm-long fingers. Pop the polenta sticks into a bowl and toss well with a generous drizzle of olive oil and a big pinch of salt.
Line a baking tray with baking paper, add the polenta sticks (keeping them spaced apart) and bake in the oven for 30 to 40 mins, turning once half way, until golden brown and crispy all over.
Remove onto kitchen paper, serve with a generous sprinkling of sea salt and the yoghurt for dipping.

name: Crispy Pork & Saucy Ginger Turmeric Noodles
description:
A rich, fragrant coconutty broth with crispy sausage and slurpy-worthy noodles. Ready in just 25 minutes, this easy and comforting bowl is perfect for a quick midweek dinner.

In Partnership With Aldi. #ad
keywords: Crispy Pork & Saucy Ginger Turmeric Noodles
Crispy Pork & Saucy Ginger Turmeric Noodles recipe
instructions: Squeeze the sausagemeat out of the casings and discard the skins. Finely grate the ginger and mince the chilli. Pick the coriander and mint leaves, discarding the mint stems and thinly slicing the coriander stems.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the sausagemeat and cook for 8-10 mins, breaking it up with a spoon, until golden and crispy. Transfer to a plate.

Add the ginger, chilli and turmeric to the same pan and stir-fry for a few seconds until fragrant. Pour in the coconut milk and stock, scraping up any caramelised bits from the bottom of the pan. Season with salt and black pepper, then bring to the boil.
Drop in the noodles and cook following pack instructions. Taste and adjust the seasoning with lime juice, salt and black pepper if needed. Add a splash of water if you want it saucier.
Divide the noodles between bowls. Top with the crispy sausage then ladle over the sauce. Top with toasted sesame seeds, fresh herbs and a wedge of lime.

name: Crispy Pork Belly Fried Rice
description: Leftover cooked rice is transformed into a glorious meal. Loaded up with Ocado crispy pork belly, spring onions and fish sauce, this is a winner.
instructions: Slice your pork belly into small pieces. Pop the pork belly into a bowl with 1 tbsp of your soy sauce, salt and pepper, then give it a mix and set aside briefly.
Finely slice your red chillies and spring onions, separating the whites from the greens. Finely chop your garlic.
Heat a wok over a medium heat. Add your pork belly strips in batches and fry until super crispy and golden. Remove with a slotted spoon before repeating with your remaining pork belly.
Add your red chillies, spring onion whites and garlic to the wok and fry for 2 mins until fragrant.
Tip your cooked rice into the pan along with your crispy pork belly and stir fry for a few mins more.

Make a well in the middle of your wok. Crack your eggs into the centre and mix until the yolks and whites are combined. Allow their texture to firm up, stirring to break up the eggs. Mix them into the rest of the rice once they are totally set.
Add your fish sauce and 1 tbsp soy sauce along with some salt and pepper to taste, then give it all a final mix.
Spoon your rice into a bowl and top with your green spring onion bits. Serve and enjoy.

name: Crispy Pork Belly Sandwich
description: We've stuffed juicy pork belly with crispy crackling into a baguette with pickled carrots, fresh veggies, zingy lime mayo, and an addictive lemongrass dressing.
instructions: Score the pork belly's skin about ½ cm deep, making sure you don’t reach the flesh as that will prevent you from getting a lovely crisp crackling. Generously salt the skin and place the belly on a tray in the fridge uncovered for 12-24 hours for the skin to dry.
Preheat oven to 200°C/392°F.
Place the prepared pork belly on the lowest rack of the oven and roast for 45-50 mins
When pork belly is fully cooked, put the grill on high and grill it for an additional 10-15 mins.
Chop up the carrot into matchsticks and combine in a bowl with the apple cider vinegar, sugar, and 1 tsp salt.
Blitz up the garlic, shallot, lemongrass, 2 red chillis, honey, soy sauce, brown sugar, fish sauce and msg in a food processor.
Pour out into a hot pan with 1 tbsp olive oil and 100ml of water and cook for 5 mins until thick and sticky.
Slice the cucumber into matchsticks and pick off the coriander leaves before finely chopping the spring onions and remaining red chilli. Set this all aside.
Combine the mayonnaise with the zest and juice of the limes.
Slice the pork belly into slices and brush on the lemongrass dressing onto both sides.

Slice your baguettes in half, spreading an ample amount of lime mayo on either side and topping with slices of your crispy pork belly. Follow all that with a healthy scattering of the pickled carrot, cucumber, red chilli and coriander. Finally, close up the sandwich and enjoy.

name: Crispy Pork Katsu Curry
description: A delicious take on a classic. With crispy pork cutlets, and warming spicy curry sauce, this one is a proper comfort dinner that’s well worth the effort.
instructions: Start by making your curry paste. Roughly chop the onion, garlic, ginger and green apple. Add to a blender or food processor and blitz until smooth. Heat a large saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the curry paste and fry for 5 mins until fragrant.

Stir through the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins until darkened. Add the curry powder, garam masala, salt and flour. Mix well and cook for another couple of mins until it forms a thick paste. Meanwhile mash the banana.
Add the chicken stock and stir through the mashed banana. Carefully blitz the sauce with a stick blender until smooth (or leave it chunky if you prefer).
Peel and chop the potatoes and carrots, then chuck them into the pan. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20–25 mins until the veg is soft.

Add the soy sauce, white wine vinegar and ketchup. In a small bowl, mix the cornflour with a spoonful or two of the hot curry sauce to make a slurry. Stir the slurry into the pot and simmer for 5 mins until thick and glossy.

Wash the rice in cold water until it runs clear, then drain. Add to a saucepan with enough water to just cover it (roughly 1cm above the rice line). Bring to the boil over a medium-high heat, then cover with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 12 mins, then turn off the heat and leave to steam for another 5 mins.

Place the pork steaks between sheets of cling film and bash them to about 1cm thick using something heavy like a rolling pin. Prick each steak a few times with a fork, then season both sides with salt and pepper.
Now set up a breading station with cornflour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs in separate bowls. Dredge each steak in cornflour, dip into the egg, then coat well in breadcrumbs.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, shallow-fry each cutlet for 3–4 mins on each side until golden and crisp. Transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper and then slice into strips.
Serve each portion with a bowl of rice, a ladle of curry sauce, sliced pork katsu and a scattering of pickled onions and spring onions, if using. Dig in!

name: Crispy Pork Pancakes
description: These crispy pork pancakes are inspired by the traditional flavours of a Peking duck but offer a more affordable alternative. Juicy, crisp, and simply flawless.
instructions: Roughly chop the onion along with 4 of your spring onions. Peel and roughly chop your garlic and ginger. Chop up the pork into large 10cm chunks.

In a large heavy-bottomed pot, set over a high heat, add a glug of oil. Sear your pork on all sides so it is deeply browned. Take out the meat and add in the chopped onion, spring onion, and ginger. Sauté the veg in the pork fat until golden brown, for about 5 mins. Stir in the garlic, five-spice and star anise and cook for 1 min until fragrant.

Deglaze the pot with 500ml of water, honey, apple cider vinegar, 2 tbsp of soy sauce, and 2 tbsp of hoisin sauce. Mix well and add the meat back in. Braise with the lid on a medium heat for 4 to 6 hours. You'll know your meat is ready when it's starting to fall apart when you press on it.
Preheat the grill to the highest setting.
Julienne the remaining spring onions and your cucumber.
Transfer the meat and cooking liquid into a large bowl and shred up the meat with two forks. Mix it well with the sauce and season with salt.

Lay out the meat in a thin layer onto a lined baking sheet. You may want to use two baking trays to avoid overcrowding the dish – the thinner the layer the crispier the pork! Grill for 5 mins until very crispy and browned.
To serve, warm up the Chinese pancakes according to packet instructions. Spread ½ tsp of hoisin sauce on a pancake, pile on the crispy meat, cucumber and spring onions. Wrap it up and enjoy.

name: Crispy Pork Spring Rolls
description: Crispy and chewy pork rolls that are perfect for a picnic and a delicious way to use up seasonal watercress!
instructions: Finely chop the bacon, spring onions, chilli, carrot and watercress. Add this into a bowl along with the minced pork.
Grate in the garlic and ginger, and mix in eggs, cornflour, soy sauce, fish sauce.
Mix the filling very well so it is evenly coated.
Preheat the oven to 230°C.
Fill a bowl with water and dunk the rice paper into the water only for 1 second.
Put onto your chopping board, after 30 seconds the paper will have hydrated and will be ready to use. If you oversoak then it will become too soft to handle.

Add two tbsp of the pork filling onto the paper. Wrap up the spring roll, it should stick to itself easily and then put to the side. Continue with the rest of the rolls, be careful not to place them next to each other otherwise they will stick.
Get a small bowl and fill it with vegetable oil.
Dunk the rolls into the oil and then place them directly onto your baking tray (this helps them get super crispy in the oven without having to deep fry!).
Bake for 12 mins, turning half way through.
Place onto your serving plate and serve with sweet chilli sauce.

name: Crispy Pork, Tahini & Chilli Oil Noodles
description: Inspired by dan dan noodles, these chilli oil tahini noodles are creamy, spicy, and extremely easy to make. The ultimate 20-minute noodle recipe.
instructions: First add the pork to a bowl along with the marinade ingredients. Mix well until fully combined. Set aside to marinate while you make the sauce.

For the chilli oil, crush the garlic, thinly slice the chilli, grind the peppercorns and mince the spring onion. Add all the chilli oil ingredients to a serving bowl. Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil until just shy of smoking and pour over the dry ingredients. Stir to combine, then add all the sauce ingredients to the same bowl. Stir again to combine, then set aside.
Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a frying pan over a high heat for around 1-2 mins. Add the pork and stir-fry for 3-4 mins or until nicely golden (almost brown in colour). Set aside.
Meanwhile, cut the cucumber into thin matchsticks and thinly slice the coriander. Set aside.
Bring a pot of water to the boil and cook the noodles 1 min shy of pack instructions. Drain, reserving 75ml of the cooking water, and immediately dump the noodles into the bowl of sauce.

Place the minced pork on top of the noodles, followed by the cucumber and coriander. Pour half the reserved cooking water into the bowl. Mix the noodles, making sure to get all the sauce from the bottom and all the toppings are fully combined. If the sauce looks too dry, add the remaining reserved water and mix again. Serve.

name: Crispy Potato Wedges With Sizzled Rosemary Salt
description: Potato wedges are super underrated. These crispy wedges are the perfect to just about anything. We've combined sweet potatoes and normal potatoes for variety.
keywords: Crispy Potato Wedges With Sizzled Rosemary Salt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Cut the potatoes into wedges, skin and all. Toss with olive oil, a tiny bit of salt
and pepper and lay out on a roasting tray. Slide into the oven and roast for 25-30
mins until golden brown and crispy.

While the potatoes are roasting, add 3 tbsp of oil to a small frying pan. Set over a
medium heat and when the oil is hot, drop in the picked rosemary leaves and
sizzle for 30 seconds. Drain on kitchen paper and allow to cool. Now scrunch
them into 2 tsp of fine sea salt.
Remove the potatoes from the oven and season with the rosemary salt.

name: Crispy Rice & Chicken Salad
description: Making crispy rice in your air fryer is a killer hack that'll forever change the way you make salads. Seriously. This Thai-inspired recipe is the bee's knees.
instructions: Preheat the Russell Hobbs Satisfry Air & Grill to 220°C. Add 3 tbsp of oil, 2 tbsp of red Thai paste and honey into a medium bowl. Break the rice up and toss through until evenly coated. Spread into the cooking pot in an even flat layer, air fry until crispy, 20-25 mins, half way through, stir to break up the rice.
Meanwhile, add the chicken thighs into a bowl with 1 tbsp of oil and the remaining red Thai curry paste. Season with salt and plenty of pepper. Toss together and let marinate.

Peel and thinly slice the shallot. Add into a bowl with the juice of the limes, fish sauce and 3 tbsp of oil, mix together, set aside. Thinly shred the cabbage and pick the mint leaves. Trim and quarter the cucumber widthways, then chop into 1cm batons. Halve the tomatoes.
Once the rice is out, change the setting on the Russell Hobbs Satisfry Air & Grill to 'grill' and grill the chicken until cooked through, 10-15 mins. Using two forks, shred the cooked chicken.
Add the cabbage, mint, cucumber and tomatoes into the shallot dressing. Toss together. Right before serving, rake the crispy rice so it breaks into small bits and individual grains.
Share the salad onto plates, layering the chicken throughout. Top with plenty of the crispy rice.

name: Crispy Rice & Poached Chicken Salad
description: Crispy rice, tender poached chicken and crunchy veg tossed in a punchy peanut-chilli dressing. This one’s all about the textures.
keywords: Crispy Rice & Poached Chicken Salad recipe
instructions: Rinse the chicken breasts under cold water. Add the chicken breasts to a saucepan and cover with cold water. Add salt and set over a medium heat. Once the water starts to steam, turn the heat down low — it should be just under a simmer. Poach for 10 mins, then remove from the water and set aside to rest.

To make the dressing, mix the peanut butter, chilli crisp, soy sauce and sherry vinegar in a small bowl. Whisk until combined. If your peanut butter is thick, loosen the dressing with a few tablespoons of water until it’s pourable. Season to taste with salt.

To crisp the rice, heat the sesame oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the rice and press it down into the pan. Cook undisturbed for 5 mins, then flip and cook for another 3 mins until golden and crisp. Transfer to a plate and leave to cool, then break into chunks.

Smash the cucumber lightly with the flat side of a knife, then roughly chop into bite-sized chunks. Cut the carrot into matchsticks (or grate it). Finely slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens if you like.
Slice the rested chicken into thin strips.
Toss the chicken, crispy rice, carrots, cucumber, beansprouts and spring onion whites with the dressing until well coated.
Divide between bowls, then finish with coriander leaves, spring onion greens and a sprinkle of togarashi, if using.

name: Crispy Rice & Salmon Ponzu Salad
description: Golden crispy sesame rice tossed with flaky salmon, fresh greens and edamame, all dressed in a punchy miso-ponzu dressing. Crunchy, savoury, fresh.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Line a baking tray with baking parchment.

Tip the cooked rice onto the tray and toss with the sesame seeds, olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Spread it out into one even layer, slide into the oven and bake for 30-35 mins, flipping halfway, until golden and properly crispy.

Meanwhile, tip the spinach and frozen edamame into a colander. Pour over freshly boiled kettle water until the spinach is wilted and the edamame defrosted. Leave to cool slightly, then squeeze out as much excess water as you can.
Trim the cucumber, halve it lengthways and scoop out the watery seeds with a spoon, then thinly slice.
Juice the lemon into a large bowl. Add the white miso, soy sauce and sesame oil, then whisk until smooth. Add the spinach, edamame and cucumber and toss to coat.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Season the salmon with salt, then add to the pan skin side down. Cook undisturbed for 5-7 mins, until about three-quarters cooked through. Remove from the heat, flip the salmon skin side up and leave to finish cooking in the residual heat. Break into large flakes.
Once the rice is crispy, add it to the bowl with the dressed veg, then gently toss through the salmon. Share between plates and enjoy.

name: Crispy Rice & Smashed Cucumber Salad
description: A fresh and fierce salad that's got a lovely textural crunch from the crispy rice.
keywords: Crispy Rice and Smashed Cucumber Salad
Crispy Rice and Smashed Cucumber Salad recipe
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and 1 tsp soy sauce. Heat a wok over a high heat and the sesame oil. Tip the eggs in and cook quickly into an omelette-esque disc. Tip the egg out onto a chopping board and cut into ribbons. Set aside to cool.

Return the wok to the heat and get smoking hot. Add the rice and cook for 5-6 mins, tossing now and then, until the rice has crisped up and has started to char. Try and keep the rice in little clusters if you can! Once nice and crispy, tip the rice out into a bowl.

Use a heavy pan or rolling pin to bash the cucumber until crushed. Cut into chunks and add to the rice bowl. Finely slice the spring onions, cut the celery into bite-sized pieces and halve the tomatoes, then get it all into the bowl. Tear the coriander leaves into the bowl, roughly chop the stems and add them too. Sprinkle in half of the cashews and add the egg ribbons.
In a separate bowl, combine the remaining soy sauce with the chilli oil, sugar and the juice of 2 limes. Pour over the rice and veggies and toss to combine.
Divide between plates and top with the remaining cashews and a little extra coriander.

name: Crispy Rice Bibimbap
description: Bibimbap is the perfect dish to make when you want to use up a bunch of leftovers or veg you have in the fridge. This bibimbap recipe is served with crispy rice and drizzled with a savoury, sweet, sour, slightly spicy sauce.
instructions: Trim the cucumber and cut it into quarters, widthways. Using a rolling pin or something heavy, smack the cucumber until it splits. Chop into roughly 2cm chunks. Transfer to a bowl with the kimchi, then set aside.
Add all the sauce ingredients into another bowl and stir together. Taste and season with more kimchi brine, if needed.

Add a drizzle of olive oil to a large frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the grated garlic and spinach and cook until wilted. Transfer to a bowl, drizzle over the sesame oil and sprinkle with a few pinches of sesame seeds. Season with salt, then set aside in a bowl.
Add another drizzle of olive oil to the same, now empty pan. Once hot, add the rice in one thin layer, cover and cook undisturbed for 7-10 mins, until golden and crispy on one side.
Drizzle olive oil into a new frying pan and set it over a medium-high heat. Once hot, crack the eggs in and fry to your desired doneness.

Share the crispy rice between bowls, top with the sesame spinach, kimchi-marinated cucumber and fried eggs. Finish with a sprinkling of sesame seeds and a drizzle of sauce, then mix together before eating.

name: Crispy Rice Omelette
description: When dinner needs to be fast, an omelette is the answer, or in this case a crispy rice omelette. Inspired by crispy rice salads, this dish pairs golden, crunchy rice with a just-set omelette and a punchy cucumber salad. It's super quick and obviously delish.
instructions: Whisk together the rice vinegar, soy sauce and crispy chilli oil in a bowl. Cut the cucumber into chunky pieces, halve the tomatoes and finely slice the spring onions. Add the cucumber, tomatoes and half of the spring onions to the dressing, toss well, then scatter in half of the sesame seeds. Pick and tear over the mint and season to taste with salt and pepper.

Put a small nonstick frying pan over a medium heat and add sesame oil. Once hot, add the rice and toss to coat. Cook for about 5 mins, stirring now and then, then press the rice into an even layer completely covering the bottom of the pan and let it cook undisturbed for 3 mins until the bottom is properly crisp.

Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a bowl, whisk well and season with salt and pepper. Pour the eggs over the rice, sprinkle over the remaining spring onions, cover with a tight-fitting lid and cook for 2-3 mins, until the eggs are just set.
Slide the omelette onto a plate, pile the cucumber salad on top and finish with an extra drizzle of crispy chilli oil and scatter over the remaining sesame seeds, then serve up.
If making more than 2 portions, cook in batches.

name: Crispy Rice Smoked Salmon Salad
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad. 

Crunchy rice, flaky salmon, punchy dressing. This big, bold salad delivers on flavour and texture – and it’s packed with protein.
keywords: Crispy Rice Smoked Salmon Salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Microwave the rice for 2 mins to loosen it up, then break it apart in the bag. Tip into a large bowl and stir through the soy sauce and vegetable oil. Spread it out on a baking tray and bake for 40 mins, mixing halfway, until golden and crispy.

Meanwhile, quarter the cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice the cucumbers and celery - use a mandoline if you like them razor-thin. Finely slice the spring onions, setting aside a small handful for garnish. Roughly chop the coriander.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together the peanut butter, soy sauce, sriracha and the juice of the limes. Taste and adjust with extra lime or a pinch of salt, if needed.
Add the tomatoes, cucumbers, celery, most of the spring onions and the coriander to a large mixing bowl. Pour over three-quarters of the dressing, mix well and season to taste.
Flake the salmon into big chunks and add to the bowl with the crispy rice. Gently fold everything together.
Plate up, then finish with the reserved spring onions, sliced chilli, a few coriander leaves and a final drizzle of the remaining dressing.

name: Crispy Rice With Curry Fried Eggs & Roasted Pepper Salsa
description: We’ve taken inspo from the Persian tahdig to create the base of this meal. Crispy and fluffy rice topped with a smoky salsa and crunchy asparagus. Woof.
keywords: Crispy Rice With Curry Fried Eggs & Roasted Pepper Salsa
instructions: Cook your rice according to package instructions, leave to cool down slightly.

Drain the roasted peppers. Chop them into small chunks. Finely chop the coriander. Halve and peel the avocado, chop it into small chunks. Add them into a bowl with a tbsp of olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and some lime juice.
In a bowl, whisk together the ground turmeric, 50g of Greek yoghurt and 1 egg. Season with salt and pepper. Stir the rice through the mixture until evenly coated.

Thinly slice the garlic and chilli. Trim the asparagus. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan on medium heat. Add the asparagus, cook for 2-3 mins, add the garlic and cook for another 1 min. Season with salt and pepper, transfer onto a plate.

Meanwhile, add a drizzle of oil into another large non-stick frying pan on medium heat. Once hot, add the rice mixture and flatten it out with the back of a spoon. Fry until golden brown and crispy on one side, 7-8 mins. Using a spatula break up the rice so you have both fluffy and crispy bits. This is key.

Re-use the asparagus pan to cook the eggs. Add another 3 tbsp of olive oil, stir in the chilli and curry powder and cook for roughly 30 secs. Crack in the eggs and fry until the edges are crispy and the whites are cooked. Baste the eggs with the hot oil to help the whites cook quicker. Season with salt and pepper.
Share the rice between your plates before topping with the asparagus, your remaining yoghurt, a crispy egg and the avocado and roasted pepper salsa. Tuck in.

name: Crispy Salmon & Green Grains
description: Risotto vibes, but quicker and a whole lot lighter. Blitz the green sauce, crisp up the salmon and you're basically done. Vibrant, nourishing and barely any ingredients.
instructions: Bring a small pan of water to the boil. Add the frozen peas and broad beans and cook for 3-4 mins, then scoop them out, keeping the water. Add the spinach to the pan for a minute, then drain. Alternatively, pour a kettle of boiling water over the lot to defrost the peas and beans and wilt the spinach, then drain.

Add three quarters of the peas and broad beans and all of the spinach to a food processor with the parsley. Basil works just as well here, or a mix of the two. Squeeze in the juice of half the lemon, pour in the extra virgin olive oil and season well with salt and black pepper. Blitz until you have a loose, spoonable sauce, adding a splash of water if needed.
Warm the spelt in the microwave or in a pan with a splash of water. Any cooked grain or pulse works here.

Stir the green sauce through the warm spelt. It should be a similar consistency to a risotto, so add a little hot water if you want. Taste and season with more lemon juice, salt and black pepper if needed.
Season the remaining unblitzed peas and broad beans with salt, black pepper, the juice of the remaining lemon half and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.

Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Pat the salmon dry and season well. Place the fillets skin-side down and cook for 5-6 mins, until the skin is deeply crisp, then turn over and cook for another 1-2 mins, depending on the thickness of the fillets. This also works in an air fryer at 200°C for 10-12 mins.
Divide the green grains between bowls and top with the salmon. Serve with the dressed peas and broad beans, and cut the remaining lemon into wedges for squeezing over.

name: Crispy Salmon Bento Bowl
description: Crispy-skinned salmon glazed in a punchy homemade teriyaki, served up with zingy pickled veg, sticky rice & crunchy cabbage. Clean, simple, delicious.
keywords: crispy salmon teriyaki bento bowl recipe
instructions: Use a sharp knife to remove the scales from the salmon skin. Scrape the blade against the grain until all the scales have come off, then rinse under cold water and pat dry with kitchen paper.

For the salad, whisk the vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and soy sauce together in a bowl. Finely slice the cucumber and radishes - we used a mandoline for speed but thinly slicing with a knife is fine. Toss them through the dressing and set aside.
Finely shred the white cabbage and set aside too.
Now for the teriyaki. Mix together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, grated garlic and black pepper in a small bowl.

Set a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, drizzle in just enough vegetable oil to coat the bottom. Add the salmon, skin side down, and cook for 4-5 mins until the skin is crispy and the fish is about 80% cooked through.
Flip the fillets, then pour the teriyaki sauce into the pan avoiding the skin to keep it nice and crispy. Cook for another 2 mins as the sauce reduces slightly.
Lift the salmon out and let the sauce bubble for a couple more minutes until thick and glossy.
To serve, spoon the rice into bowls. Top with a salmon fillet, some of the pickled veg and the shredded cabbage. Finish with a scattering of sesame seeds and a lemon wedge on the side.

name: Crispy Salmon Parcels
description: Crispy, juicy salmon parcels dipped in a fresh and gingery chimichurri-esque sauce? Yes, please. Made perfect by responsibly farmed SJÖRAPPORT salmon from IKEA.
instructions: Finely chop the spring onions and ginger. Chop the salmon into large pieces.
Marinate the salmon in soy sauce, honey, ⅓ of the chopped spring onions and ⅓ of the chopped ginger.

For the dipping sauce, finely chop the coriander, garlic, parsley and green chilli. Mix this in a bowl with the remaining chopped spring onions, ginger and a large pinch of sea salt. Next, mix in 4 tbsp of extra virgin olive oil and the juice of a lime.
In a separate bowl, combine 100ml of water with 2 tbsp of olive oil.

Remove the filo pastry gently out of its packaging and place it on a chopping board. Cut into three and brush over the olive oil-water mix until damp. Place a piece of salmon with some ginger and spring onion bits in the centre of each pastry segment and wrap it up in a parcel. Use more water/oil mix if it’s looking dry or is hard to fold.
Get a large frying pan and bless it with a big glug of oil.
Fry the parcels for 2 mins on either side until the salmon is cooked through.
Serve with the dipping sauce and enjoy.

name: Crispy Salmon With Spicy Chickpea Ragù
description: Nothing hits like a bit of a crispy salmon skin. We've made that lovely piece of fish with a comforting chickpea ragù.
keywords: Crispy Salmon With Spicy Chickpea Ragù
instructions: Dice the red onion and garlic. Heat a frying pan over a medium heat and add a shot of olive oil. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Cook for 4-5 mins before adding the garlic, caraway and fennel seeds and the chilli.

Cook for 9-10 mins until everything is looking jammy. Now tip in the passata and chickpeas (water and all) and bring to the boil. Reduce to a simmer and cook for 15 mins or so until the broth has reduced a little and the flavours have intensified. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.

Season the salmon with salt and heat a frying pan over a high heat. Once nice and hot, add a glug of oil and the salmon, skin-side down. Press down on the flesh to ensure the salmon skin makes even contact with the hot pan. Cook for 5-6 mins until the skin is super crisp, before flipping over, turning off the heat and allowing the residual heat of the pan to cook the fish through.
Finish the chickpeas with lots of chopped dill and lemon juice. Divide between warm bowls and top with a dollop of yoghurt and a piece of crispy salmon. Serve with lemon wedges.

name: Crispy Salt & Pepper Tofu with Curried Rice
description: Salt and pepper tofu, crispy from the oven or airfryer, glazed in sticky maple syrup and five spice, served over golden cashew curry rice. A flavour-packed veggie dinner that comes together in no time.
keywords: Crispy Baked S&P Tofu with Curry Rice
Crispy Baked S&P Tofu with Curry Rice recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.

Chop the tofu into 2cm cubes. Add the cornflour to a bowl, season with salt and whisk together. Toss the tofu through the cornflour mixture, then place onto a lined baking tray and drizzle with oil. Bake for 20-30 mins, until crispy and golden. Alternatively, air fry at 200°C for 10-15 mins, until golden and crispy.
Meanwhile, stir the maple syrup, five spice and white pepper together, adding the MSG if using. Season with salt. Thinly slice the chillies and spring onions. Roughly chop the coriander.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the cashews and stir-fry for 2-4 mins, until golden and toasted. Remove from the heat, stir in the curry powder, season with salt and black pepper, then stir through the cooked rice.
Once the tofu is crispy, toss it through the maple syrup mixture and return to the oven for 5-10 mins, or back in the airfryer for 2-5 mins, until sticky.
Toss the tofu with the chillies, spring onions and coriander. Divide the rice between plates and top with the salt and pepper tofu. Serve with a dollop of sriracha, if you like.

name: Crispy Sausage & Curried Pineapple Tacos
description: These sausage tacos are a total game-changer — bold, smoky flavour packed into every bite, topped with a fresh, zingy pineapple salsa that cuts right through the richness. The best part? The technique. Instead of cooking your sausages separately, you smash them directly onto the taco tortilla and cook them straight in a hot pan.
keywords: Crispy Sausage & Curried Pineapple Tacos recipe
instructions: Squeeze the sausage meat from the sausage casings and into a bowl. Discard the casings. Divide the sausagemeat equally between the tortillas, and spread the sausagemeat out into an even layer. Set aside.
Thinly slice the red cabbage and place into a bowl. Season with salt and the juice of 1 lime. Set aside.

Trim and slice the pineapple skin off, then dice into 1cm chunks. Add the pineapple to a dry frying pan on high heat, then cook until starting to char. Add the olive oil. Once hot, stir through the mustard seeds and let them shimmer for a couple of seconds. Drop in the curry leaves, remove from the heat and stir through the curry powder, transfer into a bowl and wash the frying pan. Once cooled down, season with salt, pepper and the juice of 1 lime.

Reuse the frying pan and place onto medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the tortillas in batches, sausagemeat-side down, and cook until golden-brown,3-5 mins. Flip and cook the tortillas for a couple of seconds until golden. Transfer to a plate and cover. Continue until all the tortillas are cooked.
Serve the tacos with cabbage slaw, soured cream and curried pineapple salsa.

name: Crispy Sausage & Fresh Tomato Tagliatelle
description: The trick to this pasta is adding the cherry tomatoes right at the end, with a ton of lemon juice and fresh basil, it keeps it all super fresh and light.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.
Add 2 tbsp olive oil to a large frying pan, add the pork mince, or if using sausages, squeeze the sausage meat from the casing into the pan. Fry until golden brown and crisp, around 10 mins.

While the pork sizzles, peel and slice the garlic and slice the cherry tomatoes in half. Pull the basil leaves from the stems. Drop the tagliatelle into the water and cook for 1 min less than packet instructions.

Add the tomato purée, garlic and fennel seeds to the pork pan and cook for 2 mins, then use tongs to transfer the tagliatelle across. Add 2-3 ladles of pasta water. Toss well, then add the cherry tomatoes and most of basil leaves. Squeeze in the juice of the lemons and season well. Finely grate half of the Parmesan into the pasta and toss well.
Swirl into bowls, top with the rest of the Parmesan grated over the top, the remaining basil leaves and a crack of black pepper.

name: Crispy Sausage Peanut Noodles
description: Crispy sausage bits. Charred spring onions. And an unbelievably creamy peanut sauce. What’s not to love?
instructions: Add the peanut butter, soy sauce, sugar, apple cider vinegar and 250ml water to a bowl and whisk until smooth.

Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat. Add the spring onions and cook, turning occasionally, until softened and nicely charred. Transfer to a chopping board and cut into 2cm chunks.
Cook the noodles in boiling water according to the package instructions. Rinse under cold water and drain.
Add 2 tablespoons of oil to the noodles and toss to coat. This will prevent them from sticking to each other.
Split the sausage casings and remove the sausage meat then mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat. Add the sausage meat and cook, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned and crispy.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli flakes and stir fry for 1 minute, then add the noodles, peanut sauce and spring onions and toss well to coat.
Turn the heat down to low and keep tossing until the sauce nicely coats the noodles, adding more water as necessary to loosen the sauce.
Thinly slice the red chilli. Plate up and garnish with the sliced chillies then you’re ready to dig in.

name: Crispy Sausage, Brie and Cranberry Parcels
description: Wonderfully crispy, gooey and festive. These parcels are going to be a big hit at your next Christmas party.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Add a small glug of oil into a pan and squeeze out the sausage meat out of the sausages.
Break up sausage meat with your wooden spoon and cook for 10 mins until crispy and cooked through.
Cut the brie into cubes.
Melt the butter in the microwave.
Cut the filo pastry with scissors into squares. Place one square onto a chopping board and brush liberally with butter. Place on another square diagonally and brush with butter.
Place on a cube of brie and then a ½ tsp of cranberry sauce and finally a tsp of crispy sausage.
Pull up the edges and squeeze them at the end to make a money bag. Repeat with your remaining filo.
Pop these onto a lined baking sheet and bake for 10 mins.
Place onto your serving plate and enjoy.

name: Crispy Scotch Bonnet Buffalo Chicken
description: Crispy chicken, parmesan eggs and a tasty scotch bonnet buffalo sauce. It's truly the stuff of dreams. Make it for your mates tonight, they'll love you for it.
instructions: Core the apples and slice into thin matchsticks. Thinly slice the celery.
Combine the mayonnaise, wholegrain mustard and juice of the lemon in a small mixing bowl. Add the apple and celery, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan set over a medium heat.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and whisk in the scotch bonnet jam and balsamic vinegar. Season with salt and pepper, to taste, then set aside.
Halve the chicken breasts lengthwise, then lightly pound to an even thickness of around 1½ cm. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Tear up the bread and place in a food processor. Blitz to fine breadcrumbs then transfer to a wide bowl.
Place the flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs in 3 separate bowls. Season the flour with salt and pepper. Beat the egg and season them, too.
Dip the chicken in the flour, then the eggs, then the breadcrumbs.

Heat a good glug of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add your chicken fillets and fry for a couple of minutes on each side until they are golden and crisp. Transfer to a kitchen towel-lined plate to drain.
Meanwhile, wipe out the pan, leaving a little bit of oil, and set it over a medium heat. Sprinkle the parmesan into 4 rough circles and cook for 2 mins, or until it begins to melt.
Crack the eggs onto the cheese and season with salt and pepper. Cover the pan and cook for 2 to 3 mins, or until the yolks are cooked to your liking.
To serve, plate up the slaw, add the crispy chicken and top with the parmesan fried egg. Whisk and reheat the sauce, if necessary, then drizzle it over the top. Serve and enjoy!

name: Crispy Sea Bass With Spicy Noodle Salad
description: Spicy noodles tossed with spring veg and topped with crispy sea bass. A super quick meal that packs a punch.
keywords: Crispy Sea Bass with Spicy Noodle Salad
instructions: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil.

Finely slice the garlic. Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the garlic and red curry paste and sizzle for a minute. Remove from the heat and transfer into a large bowl. Add the juice of 1 ½ of the lemons and 2 tbsp olive oil – whisk well to create the dressing. Taste and season with salt, if needed. Wipe out the frying pan.
Trim and slice the green beans into 3-5 cm pieces. Cut the top 5cm tips off the asparagus, then finely slice the stems.

Once the water is boiling, add the noodles and green beans and asparagus tips cook for 5 mins. Drain and rinse with cold water until no longer hot, then tip into the dressing. Trim the courgette, using a vegetable peeler, peel the courgette into long ribbons, and add them to the bowl. Roughly chop most of the coriander and add to the bowl, season generously and toss. Dish out onto 4 plates.

Pat the sea bass dry and season with salt. Heat 2 tbsp of oil in a frying pan over a high heat. Once the oil is shimmering, add the sliced asparagus stems and cook for a few mins. Push to the side of the pan and add the fish, skin-side down. Cook for 3 mins, untouched, until the skin is crisp and the flesh is beginning to cook through. Flip over for a final 30 seconds
Place the fish, skin side up, on top of the noodle salad. Scatter with the remaining coriander leaves. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Crispy Sea Bass with Ginger Sauce
description: You know that crispy skinned sea bass you get at Chinese restaurants? Well… it’s actually unbelievably easy to make it at home. Ginger here packs a punch.
keywords: Crispy Sea Bass with Ginger Sauce Recipe
Crispy Sea Bass with Ginger Sauce
instructions: For the chilli ginger sauce, add the bird’s-eye chillies and fresh ginger into a pestle and mortar. Bash for a minute or so until a chunky consistency. Stir the oil, vinegar, honey, soy sauce, Finely slice the spring onion, and stir through the chilli mixture
Pat the sea bass fillets dry and season with salt. Halve or quarter the pak choi.

Heat a frying pan with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the pak choi, cut side down with a splash of water. Place a lid on and cook for 4-5 mins, until softened. Transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm. Keep the pan on the heat.
Add another drizzle of oil into the pan. Place the sea bass fillets, skin side down, and cook for 3-4 minutes, until 3/4 cooked through. Flip the fillet, add the sauce and remove from the heat.
Reheat the rice.
Share the rice between bowls. Top with the bok choi and fish. Spoon over the pan sauce and serve immediately.

name: Crispy Sesame Beef Noodle Bowls
description: Looking for a spicy and more-ish dish? These banging ramen-inspired bowls are packed with crispy beef and deliciously chewy noodles. Check it out.
instructions: Start by boiling your eggs for 6 minutes.
Afterwards, place them into an ice cold bowl of water and allow the eggs to chill for 5 minutes.
Beef Time. Add a good drizzle of veg oil to a frying pan. Add your beef and break it up with a spoon.

Finely chop your ginger, garlic and slice your spring onions. Add them to the pan once the beef is nice and crispy. Add your soy sauce, chilli flakes (save a pinch for later), sesame oil and mix together.

Add your chicken stock to a saucepan. Once the stock is hot, add your egg noodles. When the noodles have softened, add your pieces of pak choi to the saucepan. Mix everything together. Once the pak choi has cooked through, it’s assembly time.

Add your noodles to a bowl, spoon in a few ladles of stock followed by the pak choi. Add the beef to your bowl and one boiled egg, cutting it open to reveal that runny yolk. Sprinkle some chilli flakes over the top and repeat for each bowl. Now, tuck into to this warming and tasty dish.

name: Crispy Sesame Feta, Roast Figs & Lemon Quinoa
description: Transport yourself to the Mediterranean with this bright and flavourful vegetarian lunch. The combination of sweet figs and salty feta is going to blow your mind. In a good way, of course.
instructions: Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Cook the quinoa according to the pack instructions. Drain well and set aside.

Halve each block of feta lengthways to make thinner slabs, then cut each piece into quarters — you should have 8 even slices. Tip the sesame seeds onto a plate and press each piece of feta into the seeds to coat one side. Set aside.

Finely chop the mint. Zest and juice the lemon. Toss the drained quinoa with chickpeas, lemon zest, and chopped mint. In a small bowl, whisk the lemon juice with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Drizzle over the quinoa and mix well.

Halve the figs and drizzle with a little olive oil and a pinch of salt. Air-fry at 180°C for 3–5 mins until soft and juicy. Remove the figs and add the sesame-coated feta. Air-fry at 200°C for 5 mins until golden and crispy.
Mix the honey with the balsamic vinegar and chilli flakes. Drizzle generously over the warm figs.
Spoon the quinoa salad onto plates or into containers. Top with crispy sesame feta and honeyed figs. Serve warm, or enjoy cold as a lunchbox.

name: Crispy Sesame Tofu Curry & Rice
description: Crispy tofu dotted with toasted sesame seeds, served with a simple coconut curry sauce and fresh herbs for a fragrant and easy dinner.
keywords: Crispy Sesame Tofu Curry & Rice recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Stir the sesame seeds and cornflour together. Chop the tofu into 2cm squares and toss through the sesame mixture. Transfer to a baking tray lined with baking parchment and drizzle with oil. Season with salt and bake for 20-30 mins until golden and crispy.
Meanwhile, peel and finely slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens.

Place a saucepan over a medium heat. Once hot, pour half the coconut milk in and cook until the fat separates. Add the spring onion whites and stir-fry until translucent. Add the curry paste and cook until fragrant. Pour in the water and remaining coconut milk, bring to the boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 10-15 mins until creamy. Taste and season with lime juice, salt and sugar.
Pick the dill and mint, discarding the stems. Toss both with the spring onion greens.
Share the rice between bowls, ladle over the curry sauce and top with crispy tofu, herbs and any remaining lime wedges.

name: Crispy Sesame Tofu with Sticky Sauce
description: Crispy tofu in a gingery, sticky sauce. One of the all time great tofu dishes for the MOB.
instructions: Chop your tofu up into little cubes. Dab cubes with kitchen roll to remove the excess moisture. Place the tofu cubes into a bowl.
Add 4 tbsp of your soy sauce, one heaped tbsp of grated ginger, a tsp of grated garlic, and sesame oil. Gently mix together.
Cover the bowl, place it in the fridge and leave to marinate for 15 minutes.

Remove tofu from the fridge. Pour a good helping of cornflour into a bowl. One by one, roll each tofu cube in the cornflour so they are coated on all sides. By the end, they should all have a gummy layer of cornflour on each side.
Pour 1 part rice to 2 parts boiling water into a pan and cook on a medium heat, until the rice has absorbed all the water.

Heat a large frying pan and pour in a good glug of vegetable oil. Place your tofu cubes in the pan. Cook on a medium heat. Each cube will need about 4 minutes on each side. Just keep turning them until all sides are golden.
Once golden on all sides, remove the cubes from the heat. Set them on some kitchen roll so any excess oil is soaked up.
Sauce time. Place a pan on the heat and pour in the leftover marinade. Add your last tbsp of soy sauce, a chopped red chilli, chopped spring onions, a tsp of grated ginger and a glass of water.

As the sauce is bubbling, mix one tsp of cornflour in with a glass of water until it is dissolved. Pour this water into the sauce and mix it in. Remove the sauce from the heat when it is thick and sticky.
Time to serve up. In a bowl, spoon in some rice, then lots of the crispy tofu and pour over some of the sauce. Garnish with some chopped spring onions and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Crispy Smashed Potato Salad
description: I absolutely love a potato salad – the crunchy smashed potatoes take this one to the next level. Thin, crispy potatoes go so well with the creamy tangy sauce and crispy onions on top!
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Drop the whole potatoes into a large pot of salted water – they should be just covered with water. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 - 15 mins until parboiled, a knife should slide through but don’t take them too far or they’ll turn to mush when you crush them. Drain and leave in the colander for 2 mins.

Tip the potatoes onto a large baking tray lined with baking parchment. Press the potatoes flat using the bottom of a glass. Drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 40-50 mins until really crispy on the edges.
Meanwhile, slice the cucumber lengthwise and scoop out and discard the middle – this is to prevent the sauce from getting watery. Finely chop the dill and chives.
Transfer the chopped herbs and cucumber to a bowl along with the remaining ingredients and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix well and set aside.
Once the potatoes are really crispy, remove from the oven and stir them through the sauce. Garnish with sliced spring onions and crispy onions – enjoy!

name: Crispy Smoked Tofu with Peanut Sauce
description: The peanutty sauce in this dish is an absolute 10/10. Rich, creamy, and full of flavour, it's the perfect complement to the crispy smoked tofu, adding depth and a nutty sweetness to every bite. Serve it with some steamed rice or fresh veggies for a complete, balanced meal, and you’ve got yourself an easy, crowd-pleasing dish that’s perfect for weeknights or when you're craving something delicious and comforting.
instructions: Get a saucepan on a medium heat. Add your coconut milk to the pan then grate in the ginger before adding the soy sauce and peanut butter. Whisk together until smooth, then bring to a simmer. Cook until thickened and pourable, around 10 minutes.
Get your rice on (follow pack instructions).
Cut your tofu into finger sized slices. Coat each piece of tofu in cornflour.
Heat 1/3 of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium high heat. Add the peppers and cook for 4 minutes until charred and softened, then remove.

Heat the rest of the oil in the same frying pan over a medium high heat. Add your tofu to the pan and fry for around 4 minutes on each side until golden and crisp. Add the peppers back in and warm through. Pick the coriander.
Serve your crispy smoked tofu and peppers on the hot rice. Pour your sauce over the top then scatter with coriander and chilli flakes. Serve with wedges of lime.

name: Crispy Spiced Salmon & Nutty Kale Salad
description: Heaps of kale, creamy white beans and buttery avocado piled high with a cumin-spiced salmon fillet and a sharp, garlicky Greek yoghurt dressing. Fresh, filling and ready in 25 mins - perfect for a weeknight dinner.
keywords: Kale Salad with Crispy Spiced Salmon
Kale Salad with Crispy Spiced Salmon recipe
instructions: Mix the ground cumin, smoked paprika and ground coriander together in a small bowl. Pat the salmon fillets dry, drizzle with a little olive oil and rub the spice mix all over the flesh and skin. Season well with salt and black pepper.

Make the dressing by grating the garlic into a bowl, then adding the Greek yoghurt, Dijon mustard, the juice of one lemon and the extra virgin olive oil. Whisk until smooth, adding a little water if needed to loosen to a dressing consistency. Season well with salt and black pepper and set aside.

Remove the woody stems from the kale, then tear into bite-sized pieces and place in a large bowl. Add a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil and massage firmly for 1-2 mins until the leaves soften, darken and lose their raw edge. Drain and rinse the cannellini beans, then add to the bowl along with the sliced avocado and toss gently to combine.
Toast the mixed seeds in a small frying pan over a medium heat for a couple of minutes until golden, then set aside to cool.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat and add a splash of olive oil. Place the salmon fillets skin-side down. Press down firmly with a spatula for the first 30 seconds to make sure the skin makes full contact with the pan. Cook for 4-5 mins without moving until the skin is deeply charred and crisp, then flip and cook for a further 2 mins on each side until golden, keeping the flesh slightly pink in the centre.

Spoon the dressing over the kale and beans and toss to coat. Scatter over the seeds and parsley, then divide between bowls. Lay the salmon on top, spoon over any juices from the pan, squeeze over the remaining lemon and serve immediately.

name: Crispy Spinach & Feta Wraps
description: Flaky, golden wraps stuffed with wilted greens, crumbled feta and melted mozzarella, served with a smoky, punchy chilli sauce. Crispy on the outside, gooey and herby within. Inspired by Turkish Gozleme.
instructions: Finely dice the onion. Set a large saucepan over a medium heat, add a big glug of olive oil and fry the onion for about 5 mins until softened. Add the garlic and fry for 1 min until fragrant, then add the kale, spinach and dill and cook for a further 3-4 mins, stirring, until completely wilted.

Drain off any excess liquid, then tip the greens onto a chopping board and finely chop. Transfer to a large bowl and leave to cool slightly. Crumble in the feta and grate in the mozzarella. Zest the lemon, then squeeze in the juice. Season with salt and mix well.

For the chilli sauce, mince the garlic. Add a glug of olive oil to a small saucepan over a medium heat, then add the red pepper paste, tomato paste, garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for about 10 mins, stirring occasionally, until deepened in colour. Pour in the water, stir to combine and keep warm.
Lay a wrap flat and spoon a quarter of the spinach filling into the centre. Fold in the sides, then roll into a tight square parcel. Repeat with the remaining wraps and filling.
Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with a glug of olive oil. Add the wraps and fry for 2-3 mins per side until golden and crispy all over. Serve with the chilli sauce alongside for dipping.

name: Crispy Spinach & Mozzarella Gnocchi with Brown Butter & Pumpkin
description: Pumpkin season is back, and this warming crispy pan-fried gnocchi dish is the perfect way to celebrate.
keywords: Crispy Gnocchi with Sage Browned Butter & Hazelnut Charred Pumpkin
Crispy Gnocchi with Sage Browned Butter & Hazelnut Charred Pumpkin recipe
ingredients: 2Pack La Famiglia Rana Spinach & Mozzarella Filled Pan Fry Gnocchi
instructions: Heat your oven to 220°C fan.

Peel, deseed and chop your pumpkin into small bite-sized pieces then add to a baking tray with a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Roast in the oven for 10 mins or until charred and softened, then remove from the oven.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the hazelnuts. When the pumpkin cooking time is up, sprinkle the hazelnuts over the charred pumpkin and return to the oven for another 5 mins.

Heat the butter (or a generous glug of olive oil, if you prefer) in a wide non-stick frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the gnocchi and pan-fry for a minute, then add the sage and continue cooking for 3-4 mins or until golden and crispy.
Remove the cooked pumpkin and hazelnuts from the oven and fold them through the gnocchi.
Divide the gnocchi between plates, grate over the pecorino and add a good grind of black pepper before tucking in!

name: Crispy Spinach and Ricotta Parcels
description: These simple and delicious spinach and ricotta parcels are perfect for a picnic. Watching the video will make folding them much easier.
instructions: Grab a large pan and place over a medium heat. Wash the spinach well and add straight into the pan with a pinch of salt. Cook for about 2 mins until the spinach has wilted. Set aside to cool.
Roughly chop the spinach and basil and place into a large bowl. Grate in a clove of garlic and your parmesan before adding the ricotta and nutmeg. Mix well.
Mix the flour in a small bowl with 5 tbsp of water. Melt the butter in a small pan and set aside. Preheat your oven to 180°C.

Take a sheet of filo and lay it out flat with the short end towards you. Cut it in half. Brush the long edge of one half with a light layer of the flour and water mix. Fold the right hand corner at 90 degrees and seal against the edge with the flour mix. Repeat with the second half.
Repeat that step again until you have a triangle. Open up the triangle like a cone and add 2 tbsp of the spinach mix.
Continue to fold over the excess, sealing with a little of the flour mix, until you have a triangular parcel. Repeat until you have used up all of the mix, which should make 8 parcels.
Place the parcels onto a baking tray and brush all over with the butter. Place into the oven for 15 to 20 mins until golden brown and crispy.

name: Crispy Spring Onion Pancakes
description: These crispy pancakes are my take on the Chinese street food staple of Cong You Bing. Perfectly flaky and irresistible with a spicy dipping sauce. Seema x
instructions: Combine the flour, a pinch of salt and hot water (the water must be boiling!) with a wooden spoon. Once it is cool enough to handle, knead for 10 minutes. It will be sticky at first but don’t add any more flour, it will form a really soft dough.
Wrap in cling film, and let the dough rest for 15 minutes.
Mix the sesame oil, 2 tablespoons of flour, and a pinch of salt to form a paste.
Grind up the Sichuan peppercorns in a pestle and mortar. Then finely chop up the spring onions.
Portion the dough into 4 pieces, cover remaining in cling film.
One piece at a time, roll the dough into a large circle. It should be the thickness of a pound coin (which is 2.80mm).
Spread about 1 teaspoon of sesame oil paste onto the dough before sprinkling on a pinch of Sichuan peppercorns and a handful of spring onions.
Tightly roll the pancake to form a log. Roll the log, tucking one end in a spiral to form a snail shape.
Gently press, and roll on it with a rolling pin gently to form a thick pancake. Keep each pancake separate, in between sheets of baking paper, until you are ready to fry.
Fry on both sides for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown. Serve hot with the spicy dipping sauce.
For the sauce, grate the garlic and ginger in a bowl. Pour in soy sauce, black vinegar, sesame oil, a tablespoon of water, chilli oil and a pinch of sugar, then mix to combine.

name: Crispy Spring Onion Potato Salad
description: Only 4 core ingredients make this banging potato salad. Spring onions done two ways maximise the flavour of this humble ingredient.
instructions: Bring a pan of water to a boil and salt it generously.
Cut your potatoes in half, then tip them into the water. Simmer for 15 mins until tender.
Finely slice your spring onions, separating the whites and the greens.
Heat some oil in a wok, then tip in your spring onion greens. Fry for 5 mins until crisp, then remove from the pan with a slotted spoon.
Add your spring onion whites to a bowl along with your lemon zest and lemon juice. Toss to lightly pickle.
Drain your potatoes in a colander, then leave to cool to room temperature.
Toss your potatoes with most of your crispy onions, mayonnaise and pickled onions. Add salt and pepper, then spoon onto a platter. Sprinkle with your remaining crispy onions, then serve.

name: Crispy Sprout Quesadillas
description: Sprouts aren’t just for Christmas. These quesadillas are a great way to use up sprouts during the festive season and beyond. They’re smoky, spicy and very cheesy. We've used flour tortillas but you can use corn if you can find them.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C fan.

Finely shred your brussel sprouts and get them in a large roasting dish. Sprinkle over your sweet smoked paprika, ground coriander and season generously with salt. Pour over a generous glug of olive oil and give it a really good toss so all the ingredients are combined.
Get your roasting dish in the oven and cook for 20 mins, tossing every 5 mins so that it cooks evenly.

Make your salsa. Roughly chop your garlic clove and green chilli (removing the seeds first), then pop them in a blender. Add your coriander (leaves and stalks), the juice of your limes and a glug of olive oil, then whizz it to a smooth sauce. Season it to taste with salt.
Grate your mozzarella and Cheddar, and mix them together in a bowl. Sprinkle the cheese onto one half of your flour tortillas, then fold them back over.

Heat a large frying pan over a low heat, and place a few tortillas in there. Cook them for about 3 mins on each side, until the cheese is melted. Transfer to a plate and cover with a tea towel to keep them warm whilst you finish the rest.
Pull your quesadillas open and fill them with the crispy sprout mixture. Drizzle over your coriander salsa, then serve them up.

name: Crispy Sweet Chilli Mince Bowl
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad
Crispy sweet chilli beef piled onto zingy lime broccoli rice. Big flavour, loads of crunch and weeknight-easy.
instructions: Add the olive oil to a large frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the beef mince and smoosh it down with the back of a wooden spoon so it spreads into an even layer. Leave it to crisp up before breaking it apart. You may need to do this in two batches to get proper caramelisation. Cook until golden and crispy, then lift out with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Meanwhile, finely slice the spring onions, separating the whites from the greens. Finely chop the garlic. Slice the pepper into thin strips. Cut the broccoli into small florets.

Rinse the rice, then add it to a saucepan with salted water. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid and simmer for 6 mins. Add the broccoli on top, pop the lid back on and remove from the heat. Leave to steam for 10 mins until the rice is fluffy and the broccoli is tender. Finely zest the lime and stir it through the rice and broccoli.

Return the frying pan to a medium heat. Add the garlic and the spring onion whites and cook for another 2 mins until fragrant. Then add the peppers and cook for another 5 mins until softened. Tip the beef back into the pan along with the sweet chilli sauce and soy sauce. Stir well to coat everything and cook for a couple of minutes until sticky and glossy. Season with black pepper.
Roughly crush the peanuts. Slice the avocado, if using, and cut the lime into wedges.
Divide the broccoli rice between bowls and top with the crispy sweet chilli beef. Finish with the crushed peanuts, spring onion greens and avocado. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Crispy Sweetcorn Fritters
description: One batter, two ways so everyone's happy. These crispy corn-packed fritters are perfect veg-packed snacks for kids and have a jammy roasted tomato and chilli oil twist for grown-ups too.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kid Servings
Finely slice the spring onions. Peel and finely chop the ginger.
Drain the sweetcorn and add into a large mixing bowl. Add the spring onions, ginger, turmeric and cumin. Crack in the eggs and give everything a good whisk.
Add the flour, baking powder, milk and a pinch of salt. Whisk to make a smooth, thick batter.
Place a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat and melt a knob of butter. Once hot, spoon in the batter to make fritters roughly 10cm wide.
Fry for 1-2 mins until golden underneath, then flip and cook for another 1-2 mins. Repeat with the rest of the batter, adding a little more butter if needed.
Roast the cherry tomatoes in a drizzle of oil at 220°C for 10–15 mins until jammy.

Serve up! 
Kids Plate: Dish out the fritters with a spoonful of yoghurt and a handful of the roasted cherry tomatoes.
Parent's Plate: Serve up your fritters with the yoghurt, jammy tomatoes, squeeze over the lime juice with an extra scattering of chopped spring onion and a spoonful of chilli oil, if you fancy.

name: Crispy Taco Bell-Style Nachos
description: Become the nacho master with this naughty little number. The key is to get your frying pan super hot when cooking the beef. Everyone loves the crispy bits
instructions:
Get a large frying pan over a super high heat. Drizzle in some
olive oil, then tip in the beef. Use the back of your wooden spoon
to break up the meat into small chunks. Peel the red onion, then coarsely grate it straight into the pan over the heat. Fry, stirring
occasionally, until all the liquid has evaporated from the pan.
Nacho building time. Pile the tortilla chips in a large serving dish.
Slice up the lettuces and put straight on top. Squish the cherry
tomatoes between your hands on top of the lettuce. Grate the Cheddar (no need to wash the grater first), cut the limes into
wedges and set both aside for a moment.
Back to the mince. Add the Cajun seasoning and some salt and
black pepper. Give everything a good stir and cook for 2 mins
more or until the beef is crisp before taking off the heat.
Top the nachos with the crispy beef. Dollop over some sour
cream, add jalapeños to taste, and then scatter over the grated
cheese. Serve at the table with the lime wedges for people to
help themselves. Nachos – done.

name: Crispy Tofu Bites
description: This recipe is the perfect way to get the crispiest tofu.
instructions: Press your tofu into a clean cloth to remove as much liquid as possible.
Tear the tofu into 3cm-sized chunks with nice rough edges.
Marinate the tofu pieces in soy sauce then cover them in cornflour. Repeat for all of your chunks until they're evenly coated.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan then add the tofu. Fry for a few minutes on each side until extra crispy.
Serve up with your favourite dipping sauce. We've gone for sweet chilli.

name: Crispy Tofu Miso Ramen
description: Joy Crookes came into the studio to whip up this absolute banger. The broth is deep and savoury, the tofu perfectly crisp, and the noodles beautifully chewy.
instructions: Tear the stems off the shiitake mushrooms and save the caps for later. Quarter the spring onions and onion. Halve the garlic bulb lengthways. Thinly slice the ginger.
Place the shiitake mushroom stems, spring onions, onion, garlic and ginger in a large stockpot. Add the kombu, dried porcini mushrooms and dried shiitake mushrooms and cover with 2l water.
Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer covered for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, quarter the shiitake mushroom caps from earlier. Lightly smash the garlic and thinly slice the ginger.
Place in a small saucepan with the kombu, soy sauce (or tamari), mirin and 150ml water. Bring to a simmer over high heat, then turn the heat down to low and simmer covered for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, place the white miso paste and tahini in a heatproof bowl.
Once the 30 mins have elapsed, strain the mushroom mixture into the heatproof bowl and whisk to combine. This is your flavour base.
Transfer the mushroom caps to a bowl and save for later. You can discard the garlic, ginger and kombu.
Back to the broth. Strain it into a clean saucepan. Add the flavour base and stir to combine. Keep warm, covered, over a very low heat.
Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil. Cook your eggs for 6 mins, then plunge into ice cold water to stop the cooking process. Once cooled, peel and halve.
Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil. Cook your noodles according to the package instructions then drain.
Finally, thinly slice the spring onions.
Pat the tofu dry with kitchen towel then slice it into 1cm thick slices.
Generously season the cornflour with salt and pepper then coat the tofu on both sides.
Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Cook the tofu until nice and crisp on both sides.
To assemble, divide the noodles between the serving bowls. Add the mushrooms, tofu, eggs, spring onions and extra toppings of your choosing. Ladle the hot broth over the top, then serve and enjoy.

name: Crispy Tofu Noodle Salad with Wasabi Vinaigrette
description: Crunchy, fresh and packed with bold flavours, this crispy tofu noodle salad with a wasabi vinaigrette is the perfect packed lunch.
keywords: Crispy Tofu Noodle Salad with Wasabi Vinaigrette
Crispy Tofu Noodle Salad with Wasabi Vinaigrette recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Line a baking tray with baking parchment.

Dice the tofu into 2cm pieces. Mix the cornflour, curry powder, and a pinch of salt in a tray, then toss the tofu in the mix to coat evenly. Spread onto the tray, drizzle with sesame oil, and roast for 20-25 mins until crisp and golden.
Cook the noodles following pack instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water. Toss in a large bowl with ⅓ of the sesame oil to prevent sticking.
Cut the mange tout in half. Shred the romaine and roughly chop the coriander. Add to the noodles and toss to combine. Thinly slice the radishes and set aside.

In a bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, light brown sugar, rice vinegar, wasabi paste, and remaining sesame oil. Finely grate in the garlic and whisk until emulsified. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

Box up the noodle salad and top with the crispy tofu, radishes and sesame seeds. If eating later, store the dressing separately in an airtight container. If eating now, drizzle the dressing over the top. Everything will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Crispy Tofu Noodles with Vibrant Turmeric Dressing
description: This bowl of crispy tofu noodles with a fragrant toasted coconut dressing is the immunity kick you need right now. Inspired by a gorgeous Hanoian chả cá, I've turned the original fish dish completely vegan (by accident).
instructions: Pick the dill and thinly slice the stalks. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the spring onion whites and greens. Roughly chop the peanuts and thinly slice the chili. Slice the tofu blocks in half lengthwise, then into 12 even slabs. Season with salt, coat in cornflour and set aside. Cook the rice noodles according to pack instructions.

For the dressing, place a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, pour in the coconut cream and cook, stirring, for 4-5 mins until the fat separates. Add the dill stalks and spring onion whites into the pan, cook for 1-2 mins until softened. Add the curry paste, olive oil and turmeric, stir-fry for 1 min until fragrant. Transfer the mixture to a bowl and set aside to cool.
Wash and dry the frying pan, then place it over medium-high heat. Once hot, add a generous drizzle of oil and fry the tofu for 3-4 mins on each side until golden and crispy.
Once the coconut dressing is cool, add the juice of the limes. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Toss the rice noodles through and ¾ of the spring onion greens.
Divide the noodles between bowls. Top with the crispy tofu, dill fronds, remaining spring onion greens, chilli and peanuts.

name: Crispy Tofu with Smoky Black Beans & Spicy Orange Salsa
description: I’ve heard that feijoada, the traditional Brazilian black bean stew, is sometimes eaten with slices of orange, to offset and freshen the richness in the beans. I got inspired by that flavour pairing to make this incredible dish. Whether you’re vegan, veggie or not, I promise you’ll love it.
keywords: Crispy Tofu with Smoky Black Beans & Spicy Orange Salsa
Crispy Tofu with Smoky Black Beans & Spicy Orange Salsa recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Line a baking tray with baking parchment.

For the tofu, whisk the cornflour and paprika together in a bowl. Chop the tofu into 2cm cubes, then season with salt and toss through the cornflour mixture until evenly coated. Tip onto the prepared baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Slide into the oven to bake for 20-30 mins until crispy and golden.

Meanwhile, for the beans, thinly slice the garlic and spring onions (separating the whites and greens). Place a saucepan over medium heat with a glug of olive oil. Once hot, add the spring onion whites and ½ the spring onion greens and stir-fry for 2-3 mins until wilted. Add the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for a minute until fragrant, then tip the black beans in, with their liquid and the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down. Leave to simmer until the tofu is crispy. Add a splash of water if it's getting dry. Before serving, taste and season with salt and pepper,if needed.

Whilst the beans are simmering, segment the oranges and mince the chili (as much as you would like to use). Toss the two together with the remaining spring onion greens. Squeeze any juices remaining from the orange remnants, then discard. Season with lime juice and salt.
To serve, divide the beans between bowls. Top with the orange salsa, crispy tofu and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Crispy Tofu with Spiced Rice
description: A classic vegan rice bowl, packed with protein from the crispy tofu and tonnes of spices to keep it interesting. Plus, it's on ready in 20 mins.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Slice the blocks of tofu in 2cm chunks , then toss with half the olive oil and all of the ground coriander. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut the cauliflower into florets, add to a baking tray and drizzle with the rest of the olive oil, then season with salt and pepper. Slide into the oven and cook for 15-20 minutes.

Tip the tahini into a bowl and add the juice of half of the lemon, don’t worry – it’ll seize up! Add water, 1 tbsp at a time until it loosens to a drizzle-able consistency. Season well with salt and pepper and set aside.
Heat a large frying pan over a high heat, once hot, add the tofu, cooking for 5- 6 mins, until golden. Then set aside.

Add the rice to a large bowl along with the miso paste. Roughly chop most of the coriander, saving some leaves to serve, and stir the chopped coriander through the rice with the rest of the lemon juice. Taste and season well.
Serve the rice topped with the cauliflower and tofu. Drizzle with the sesame dressing and top with more coriander, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

name: Crispy Tortilla Soup
