description: Speedy, spicy and properly satisfying, this tortilla soup comes together in one pot, topped with melty cheese, crispy bits and a hit of lime.
instructions: Add the crispy onions, chipotle paste and garlic purée to a saucepan with a drizzle of olive oil. Set over a medium heat and stir-fry for 1-3 mins until fragrant.
Pour in the passata, stock and kidney beans (including the liquid from the can). Turn the heat up to high, bring to the boil and let it simmer for 5 mins.
Taste and season with salt and a good squeeze of lime juice.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Top with grated cheese, some lightly crushed tortilla crisps and coriander leaves. Serve with any remaining lime wedges on the side.

name: Crispy Turmeric Tofu & Peanut Dilly Rice
description: Stir-fried marinated tofu, jammy caramelised onions and fragrant lemongrass in a savoury, tangy sauce, all spooned over peanut-studded jasmine rice with a generous handful of fresh dill.
keywords: Crispy Lemongrass & Turmeric Marinated Tofu recipe
instructions: Mix the soy sauce, vegetable oil, ground turmeric and curry powder together in a large bowl. Cut the tofu into 2cm-thick triangles and gently toss to coat in the marinade.

Thinly slice the onion and lemongrass, and roughly chop the dill. Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the marinated tofu in a single layer and fry for 2-3 mins until golden brown. Flip and cook for another 2-3 mins on the other side, then transfer to a plate.

Add the onion and lemongrass to the pan, season with salt and sauté for 6-7 mins until softened and starting to caramelise. Add any remaining marinade from the tofu along with the extra curry powder and let it cook for a minute. Pour in the soy sauce, rice vinegar and honey and let it reduce for a minute, then add the water. Add the tofu back in and cook for 5 mins until some of the liquid has evaporated. Scatter over most of the dill and stir through.

Meanwhile, cook the jasmine rice according to the packet instructions. Roughly chop the peanuts and mix through the rice. Spoon the tofu and saucy onions over the rice and finish with the remaining dill. Roughly crush the peanuts to serve and scatter over the top.

name: Crispy Za'atar Chicken Thighs with Roast Potatoes and Romesco Sauce
description: These crispy chicken thighs are coated in aromatic za’atar and served with golden fluffy roast potatoes on a bed of spicy, smoky romesco sauce. Jordon x
keywords: Crispy za'atar chicken thighs with roast potatoes and romesco sauce recipes
the best za'atar chicken thighs recipes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Rub the chicken thighs all over with olive oil and plenty of flaky sea salt.
Place a heavy pan over a medium heat and cook the chicken thighs skin side down for about 7 or 8 mins until the skin is golden and crispy. Take off the heat and season with 2 tbsp of za’atar.
Parboil the potatoes for 7 mins in heavily salted water. Drain and shake hard in the colander to rough up the outer surface.
Add 4 tbsp olive oil to a roasting tray and place into the oven. Let it heat up for 5 mins, then add the potatoes and shake well.

Place the chicken thighs skin side up on top of the potatoes and season the skin side with the remaining za’atar. Place the tray into the oven for about 20 mins or until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, make the romesco sauce.

Toast the blanched almonds for a few minutes in a dry pan over a medium heat. Add to the food processor along with the peppers, tomatoes, garlic, chilli flakes, smoked paprika and a tsp of salt. Blend until emulsified, then drizzle in the oil with the processor running.

On a large serving platter, spread the romesco evenly, top with the roast potatoes and then the chicken. Sprinkle with chopped parsley and a drizzle of olive oil. Best served with a simple green salad.

name: Crispy “Chicken” Pumpkin Katsu Curry Burger
description: Pumpkin adds beautiful sweetness to this katsu curry sauce. Loaded onto crispy vegetarian chicken burgers and topped with pickly bits, this is an autumnal delight.
instructions: First up we’ll make the curry sauce. Finely chop the onion and add to a saucepan over a medium heat along with 2 tbsp of neutral oil. Cook for about 5 mins until soft.
While the onion cooks, peel and cube the pumpkin, add to the pan and cook for another few mins.
Finely chop the garlic and add along with the curry powder and chilli (if using), cook for another 2 mins.
Add the flour a spoon at a time, stirring as you go.
Pour in the vegetable stock slowly, stirring constantly to avoid any lumps.
Simmer gently for 10 mins until the pumpkin is soft.
Use a stick blender to blitz the sauce until smooth, then continue to cook until thickened, about another 5 mins (you want it about the texture of double cream).
Add the soy sauce and half of the sugar, taste and add salt if needed.

While the sauce is reducing, finely slice the red cabbage and add to a bowl with the remaining sugar and pinch of salt. Massage into the cabbage, then add the white wine vinegar and toss well, set aside.
Fry the veggie burgers until golden on both sides. Meanwhile, toast your burger buns in a dry frying pan.

Spread a spoonful of the curry sauce onto both sides of the bun. Pop the burger onto the base and top with another spoonful of the sauce. Top with plenty of pickled cabbage and a sprinkle of coriander, then the top bun.
Serve with a small dipping bowl of the curry sauce.

name: Crispy, Crunchy Tempura Donburi
description: Tamia showed us how to create a perfectly light, crispy tempura. She’s a genius, here are her secrets.
instructions: To prepare your rice, tip it into a saucepan and fill with water until the rice is covered. Use your hands to stir the rice in a circular motion to help agitate and remove the starch, the water should become cloudy. Drain the water. Repeat this process until the water runs clear (I usually do around 5 cycles). Once the final rinse is complete, tip the rice back into the large saucepan, cover with cold water and set aside to soak for 30 mins.
Measure out your flours and placing them in the freezer. Place your sparkling water in the fridge.

For the dipping sauce, combine the dashi, soy, mirin, and sugar in a small saucepan. Place over a medium heat and bring to a simmer until the sugar is dissolved. Remove from the heat and set aside to cool.

Back to the rice. Drain and return your rice to the saucepan. Cover with 360ml water. Place over a high heat and bring to the boil. Once boiling, reduce the heat to a very gentle simmer, cover with a lid and cook for 12 mins. Turn off the heat, but do not remove the lid, and leave to steam for 15 mins.

For the tempura, begin by preparing your proteins and/or vegetables. For your prawns, if not already prepared, remove the head, shell, and legs, then devein. For your vegetables, the shape you cut these isn’t too important however they should be roughly equal size, we've used a aubergine, enoki mushrooms, broccoli and sweet potato and squash but any veg will work here. See below for a rough guide.

Pour your oil into a large and deep frying pan, it should come halfway up the side of the pan. Place the oil over a medium-high heat, we want it to reach 180°C. Take a tray or plate and line it with parchment paper.

Meanwhile, prepare your batter. Take two mixing bowls, one large and one slightly smaller. Fill the large mixing bowl with ice and place the smaller one inside. Take your flour from the freezer and sieve it into the smaller mixing bowl. Pour the sparkling water into the flour and whisk together until fully incorporated, it should be the consistency of double cream.

Once the oil has reached 180°C it’s time to fry! (If you have a thermometer to check the temperature of the oil then perfect, if not, use the top end of a wooden spoon & place it in the oil. If it bubbles around then the oil is hot enough to fry.)

Working in batches, take your prawns/vegetables and drop them into the batter. Use your chopsticks, or your fingers, to remove from the batter and let any excess batter drip off back into the bowl. Then gently lower into the oil. Fry for 2-3 minutes or until the tempura is a light golden brown and crispy.

Use a slotted spoon, tongs or your chopsticks to remove from the oil and place on a rack to drain. Repeat with the rest of your veggies/prawns, continuing to fry in batches to ensure maximum crispiness.
To serve, get your now cool dipping sauce and pour into two saucers. Any leftover dipping sauce will keep well in the fridge for around a week.
Now take your rice that has been steaming away to perfection and divide between two bowls. Share out your tempura equally, serve alongside the dipping sauce, and enjoy!

Aubergine: Cut into chunks and slice ¾ of the way up them to create a fan effect.Tenderstem Broccoli: Trim the ends and break into even-sized floretsSweet Potato: Peel and cut into discs of equal thickness. If the potato is extremely large then slice into half moon discsButternut Squash: Peel the squash and scoop out the seeds. Cut in half down the middle lengthways. Slice into discs of equal thickness.Peppers: Cut into equal-sized slicesAsparagus: Take either end of the asparagus and bend until the woody part breaks naturallyOnion: Peel the onion and cut widthways into thick discs. Separate the discs into rings of 1-2 pieces of onion.Green Beans: Top and tail each bean.Spring Onions: Top and tail the spring onion and remove the outer layer. Cut in half lengthways. Shred the spring onion by continuing to slice each half lengthways until you are left with shoestring-like pieces.

name: Croissant Mille-Feuille
description: This is a great recipe to use up any stale croissants. The filling is a creamy vanilla mascarpone with a sharp berry compote.
instructions: Roll the croissants flat, melt a knob of butter in a pan and add the croissants, 2 at a time. Fry on a medium heat until golden then remove from the pan and allow to cool.

Place the blueberries and raspberries in a medium sized sauce pan with the icing sugar and 2 tsp of water. Heat on a low to medium heat until simmering. One simmering cook the compote for 5 minutes until it has reduced and you have a glossy sauce with the berries slightly broken down. Allow to cool.

Add 250g of mascarpone to a bowl. Beat with a spatular until smooth. Add in the 300ml of double cream, 2 tbsp of sieved icing sugar and a drop of vanilla. Beat until the cream begins to thicken and is silky smooth. Place in a piping bag if you have one, if not you can just spoon the filling in later.

Time to build. Place one croissant on a plate, pipe in a generous amount of the vanilla mascarpone cream then top with the compote. Place a second croissant on top and dust with icing sugar. Build the second dessert with the remaining ingredients and serve!

name: Croque Kimchi
description: Tangy kimchi cuts through the richness of a croque monsieur perfectly. Enjoy with a zingy and crisp green salad.
instructions: Preheat the grill to high. Thinly slice the spring onions. Grate the cheddar. Put all the bread onto a baking tray and toast it on one side. Heat the oven to 220°C.
Put the butter in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Let it melt completely, then add the flour. Stir together until the mixture turns a light golden colour and it turns into a smooth paste.

Add the spring onions and cook for 2-3 mins until softened. Whisk in the milk a little at a time until it’s all incorporated and smooth. Cook the béchamel until it comes to a boil. Remove from the heat, stir through the mustard and half the cheddar, then season with salt and pepper.

Spread some béchamel over four toasted bread sides. Top with a sprinkling of cheddar, two slices of ham, kimchi and some more cheddar. Spread 1 tbsp béchamel onto the other slice of toasted bread, then sandwich the croques together, untoasted-side facing out. Spread more béchamel on top, finish with a light scattering of cheddar and bake for 10-15 mins until melted and bubbly.
Switch the oven to grill setting and grill the croques for 2-3 mins until golden on top. Serve immediately.

name: Croque Madame Croissants
description: The ooziest, cheesiest, most fabulous way to start the day. Cheese and ham and mustardy bechamel all loaded into Pret All-Butter Croissants. A total delight.
instructions: Bake your Pret All-Butter Croissants according to packet instructions.
Grate your gruyère. Finely chop your chives.
Heat your butter in a small pan over a medium heat. Once bubbling and going slightly golden, add your flour and cook out for 2 mins.

Gradually pour in your milk, beating all the while until you have a smooth sauce. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 2 mins until thickened. Add about a quarter of the Gruyère, your Dijon mustard and a small pinch of nutmeg. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Cut your croissants in half lengthways. Spread each side with a dollop of your béchamel. On the bottom piece, add two slices of ham and a good sprinkle of your Gruyère.
Place your croissants under the grill for 3 mins until the surfaces are lovely and bubbly.

While your croissants are under the grill, get a frying pan on over a medium-high heat. Add a small glug of olive oil and, once hot, crack in some eggs. Season the surface with salt and pepper, then fry for a few mins until the whites are set. Spoon some of the hot olive oil over the surface of the egg to speed this up.
Once your croissants are golden and oozing, remove from under the grill. Pop your egg on top of the base, then sprinkle with chives. Top with the lid of your croissant, then serve.

name: Crumpets
description: Crumpets aren't as scary to make as you might think. Jodie Nixon's simple guide will show you how to make these squidgy British classics in no time.
instructions: Boil your kettle. Add the plain flour, strong white flour, salt, sugar and bicarbonate of soda into a large mixing bowl. Make a well in the middle.

Add the milk and the just boiled water to a jug – you don’t want it really hot, it needs to be around body temperature (37°C), so let it cool down until just warm otherwise it will kill the yeast. Once cooled a little, whisk in the yeast.
Pour the liquid into the well, mixing slowly with whisk.

Cover the bowl with cling film or a clean damp cloth, then set aside in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size. This will depend on how warm it actually is, so keep an eye on it! If it's particularly warm, it might take less time – you want the surface to be all bubbly.
Grease your crumpet rings and a large pan with oil. Then set the pan over a low heat and bring up to temperature – this will take around 5 mins.
Add the crumpet rings to the pan, and pour in about 3 tbsp of batter to each.
Cook for around 12 mins or until the crumpets have set completely on top, and have formed lots of holes.
Then remove the rings, flip the crumpets and cook for 2 mins until cooked through and lightly golden on top. Remove from the pan and cool completely. Repeat until you’ve used all your batter.

When it comes to serving, pop in the toaster and cook until warm – this might take less time than your shop bought crumpets! Spread with lots of butter and your toppings of choice – I love honey and sea salt or loads and loads of Marmite!

name: Crunchy Cauliflower Bang Bang Bowls
description: Veggie dream. Make sure to leave the cauliflower florets in the oven until they are brown and crunchy. The sriracha mayo is simple and brings the dish together.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Break cauliflower into florets and chop up courgettes into bite-size pieces.
Get three bowls out. Add flour to one, eggs to another (whisking them up) and breadcrumbs to the last.

Dip veg into the flour, then eggs, and finally the breadcrumbs. (It's best to keep one hand for the dry ingredients and one hand for the wet ingredients). Add baking paper to a baking tray. Add the veg, season with salt and drizzle with a quarter of the olive oil. Put the tray in the oven for 30 minutes until golden and crunchy.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions.

Finely chop cucumber and radish. Add to a bowl with the juice of half the lime, the remaining olive oil, and the coriander (saving a few leaves for garnish), salt and pepper. Mix together and set aside.
Into a bowl add mayo, Sriracha and the juice of the remaining lime. Mix everything together.
Serving time. Add rice to a bowl. Top with bang bang veg, some avocado slices, the zingy radish salad, a big dollop of Sriracha mayo and some fresh coriander leaves. Enjoy!

name: Crunchy Egg Salad Bagels
description: Creamy-crunchy egg mayo loaded with almonds, celery and crispy chilli oil, piled into toasted bagels. Protein packed, and ideal for lazy weekend brunches.
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to the boil, then gently lower in the eggs and simmer for 8 mins to set the yolks. Transfer straight to a bowl of iced water. Once cool enough to handle, peel the eggs, cut them in half and separate the whites from the yolks.

Mash the yolks in a large bowl until as smooth as you can. Add the yoghurt and Dijon mustard, then finely zest in the lemon and squeeze in the juice. Measure out the lime pickle, finely chop any chunky bits on a board, then add it to the bowl and mix everything together. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Finely chop the egg whites. Finely chop the almonds, celery, red onion and chives, then fold everything into the yolk mixture until evenly combined.
To serve, toast the bagels. Slice the tomatoes. Spoon generous mounds of the crunchy egg salad onto the bagels and finish with the tomatoes on top.

name: Crunchy Green Salad with Vegan Yoghurt
description: Nothing hits the spot like a fresh and crunchy green salad. This one contains heaps of seasonal veggies dressed in vegan yoghurt.
keywords: Crunchy Green Salad with Vegan Yoghurt
Crunchy Green Salad with Vegan Yoghurt  recipe
instructions: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil. Break off and discard the woody ends of the asparagus. Slice the spears into 1cm diagonal pieces, keeping the tips larger. Cut the broccoli florets off and slice the stems into small pieces.
Blanch the asparagus, broccoli, mangetout and peas for 1½ mins, then drain and set aside to cool.
Peel the courgette into long ribbons. When you get to the core, chop it into small cubes. Finely chop the herbs. Finely slice the onion.
To make the vinaigrette, juice the lemon into a large mixing bowl and add all of the remaining dressing ingredients. Whisk to combine.

Add the blanched veg, courgette, onion, herbs, seeds and nuts to the dressing bowl with another good pinch of salt. Toss well, making sure everything is covered. Taste and adjust, adding more olive oil, salt or lemon juice to your taste.
To serve, spread some soya yoghurt onto the bottom of a large plate and pile the salad on top. Finish with an extra drizzle of olive oil.

name: Crunchy Herby Halloumi Fries
description: These halloumi fries have the perfect crispy, herby, sweet honey coat. Paired with a zesty, minty yoghurt dip. The flavours are sublime. A certi crowd-pleaser.
instructions: Line a baking tray with greaseproof paper then cut your halloumi into thick sticks (approximately finger width and length), and place on the tray.
Get 3 bowls, crack your eggs into one and whisk. In the other 2 bowls weigh out 80g of semolina in each.
Dunk the cheese sticks into your egg mixture then roll in your semolina. Make sure the halloumi has an even coating.
Repeat for all cheese sticks then lay on your baking tray and leave in the fridge for 30 mins to chill.
Mix together your dusting dry ingredients - sumac, za’atar, and sesame seeds then set aside.
Next, mix together your yoghurt ingredients. Pomegranate seeds, the juice of your lemon and a scattering of mint.
In a wide and deep pan, get your oil frying. Pour in enough oil to cover your fries then test it’s ready by dropping in some eggy semolina mixture. If it goes golden and crispy, you’re ready.
Fry your coated halloumi in batches until golden and crisp, then drain on kitchen paper.
Finally, glaze your halloumi with a generous squeeze of honey and sprinkle your dusting mix over the top.
Dunk your fries into the yoghurt and it’s time to tuck in!

name: Crunchy Katsu Fried Chicken
description: A nod to the Christmas tradition of eating fried chicken in Japan, this is our super easy, curry-spiced fried chicken with spiced gravy and a zingy slaw.
cuisine: Japanese, Japanese-Inspired, Korean, Korean-Inspired, East-Asian Inspired
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt and black pepper and set up 3 bowls. Add 100g of flour to one, crack the two eggs into another and pop the panko breadcrumbs into the third. Beat the eggs with a splash of cold water and a big pinch of salt.
Pass the chicken thighs through the flour, egg and breadcrumbs to coat. Set the chicken aside.

To make the gravy, add the butter to a saucepan and cook over a medium heat until nutty brown, then add the flour and cook for 2 mins. Throw in the spices and cook for 4-5 mins then gradually add the chicken stock, whisking constantly. Season with salt and pepper and keep warm.
Finely shred the cabbage and red onion and coarsely grate the carrot. Add to a large mixing bowl with the vinegar and mayo. Season with salt and black pepper and toss to combine.

Heat a good glug of oil in a frying pan and add the breaded chicken. Cook over medium heat for 4-5 minutes on each side, until nicely golden and cooked through. If the breadcrumbs are colouring too much and the chicken isn't cooked, then pop in the oven to finish cooking through. Serve with a big handful of coleslaw and a pot of gravy for dipping.

name: Crunchy Onion Smash Burgers
description: A crisp, lacy beef patty and crunchy fried onions. Burgers don't get better than this.
instructions: Before we get cooking, we need to get everything ready. Smash burgers happen super fast, so it’s important we’ve got everything ready to go.

Divide the beef into 4 x 100g balls. Peel and thinly slice the onion, then divide the slices in half. Cut 4 thin slices of tomato and chop the rest into fine-ish dice. Cut the celery into chunky diamonds and shred the cabbage as fine as you can.
Season the tomato slices with salt and black pepper and set aside.

Toss together the shredded cabbage, half the onion, the diced tomato and celery. Lightly crush half the sesame seeds and mix with 3 tbsp mayo and a big splash of pickled ginger brine. Pour this over the slaw and toss together.

Split the brioche buns in half and lightly toast in a large dry frying pan. Remove the buns and crank the heat up high. Add a splash of olive oil and toss in the remaining sliced onion. Cook for 1-2 mins on high until starting to char and caramelise. Add the four burger balls and, using a flat spatula, smash them down over the onions.
Season the top side of the burgers with salt and loads of black pepper. Cook for 2-4 mins until the bottom is crispy. Flip and cook for another minute or two.
Spread the remaining mayo over the toasted buns and top half the bun halves with a smash burger, a tomato slice, a pinch of Thai basil, sesame seeds and a pinch of pickled ginger.
Serve the burgers with a big helping of sesame slaw on the side.

name: Crunchy Onion Veggie Smash Burgers
description: Veggie burgers don't suck. But a lot of vegetarian burger recipes do. Rest assured that this is an extremely good vegetarian smash burger recipe.
instructions: Before we get cooking, we need to get everything ready. Smash burgers happen super fast, so it’s important we’ve got everything ready to go.

Divide the mince into four 100g balls. Peel and thinly slice the onion, cut 4 thin slices of tomato and chop the rest into fine-ish dice. Cut the celery into chunky diamonds and shred the cabbage as fine as you can.
Season the tomato slices with salt and black pepper and set aside.

Toss together the shredded cabbage, half the sliced onion, the diced tomato and celery. Lightly crush half the sesame seeds and mix with 3 tbsp mayo and a big splash of pickled ginger brine. Pour this over the slaw and toss together.

Split the brioche buns in half and lightly toast in a large dry frying pan. Remove the buns and crank the heat up high. Add a splash of olive oil and toss in the remaining sliced onion. Cook for 1-2 mins on high until starting to char and caramelise. Add the four burger balls and, using a flat spatula, smash them down over the onions.
Season the top side of the burgers with salt and loads of black pepper and cook for 3-4 mins until the bottom is crispy. Flip and cook for another minute or two.
Spread the remaining mayo over the toasted buns and top half the bun halves with a smash burger, a tomato slice, a pinch of thai basil, sesame seeds and a pinch of pickled ginger.
Serve the burgers with a big helping of sesame slaw on the side.

name: Crunchy Quinoa & Chicken Salad
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This healthy salad recipe is packed with fibre and protein. The crunchy quinoa adds a nice pop of texture.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the chicken thighs into a bowl. Finely grate the garlic over the chicken and squeeze in the lemon juice. Add the oregano, drizzle with olive oil and generously season. Mix and set aside.
Tip the quinoa onto a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season. Toss together and bake for 15-20 mins. The quinoa will crisp-up as it cools.

Meanwhile, strip the stems off the cavolo nero, tear the leaves into bite-sized chunks and transfer to a bowl. Season with salt and scrunch together until the cavolo nero wilts. Thinly slice the spring onions, drain the cannellini beans and toss both through the cavolo nero.
Add all the dressing ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. Taste and season.
Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, fry the chicken on both sides (10-15 mins in total) until golden brown and cooked through.
Toss three-quarters of the crispy quinoa through the bean mixture with 2 tbsp of the dressing. Slice the chicken.
Share the salad between plates, top with the chicken and drizzle over some more dressing. Sprinkle with the remaining crispy quinoa.

name: Crunchy Quinoa, Chicken & Bean Salad
description: This healthy salad recipe is packed with fibre and protein. The crunchy quinoa adds a nice pop of texture, the jalapeno dressing packs a punch!
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the chicken thighs into a bowl. Finely grate the garlic over the chicken and squeeze in the lemon juice. Add the oregano, drizzle with olive oil and generously season. Mix and set aside.
Tip the quinoa onto a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season. Toss together and bake for 15-20 mins. The quinoa will crisp-up as it cools.

Meanwhile, strip the stems off the cavolo nero, tear the leaves into bite-sized chunks and transfer to a bowl. Season with salt and scrunch together until the cavolo nero wilts. Thinly slice the spring onions, drain the cannellini beans and toss both through the cavolo nero.
Add all the dressing ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. Taste and season.
Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, fry the chicken on both sides (10-15 mins in total) until golden brown and cooked through.
Toss three-quarters of the crispy quinoa through the bean mixture with 2 tbsp of the dressing. Slice the chicken.

Share the salad between meal-prep containers, top with the chicken and drizzle over some more dressing. Sprinkle with the remaining crispy quinoa and parsley leaves. It will keep in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Roasted Broccoli
description: Spiced, sesame-crusted tofu and caramelised broccoli, all done in the oven on two trays. Make this batch and you've got the base for more delicious recipes, so you're sorted for the week.
keywords: Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Roasted Broccoli recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Working one block at a time, wrap the tofu in a clean tea towel and break it up into fine clumps into a large bowl. Cut the broccoli into florets.
Mix the spices, sesame seeds, salt and sugar in a small bowl. Add half the spice mix to the tofu, drizzle with vegetable oil and mix until combined. Tip onto a baking tray lined with baking paper.
Add the broccoli to the large bowl, drizzle with vegetable oil and toss with the remaining spice mix. Tip onto a second lined baking tray.

Place both trays in the oven and bake for around 20 mins, until the broccoli is browning and the tofu is golden. Halfway through, swap the oven positions of the trays and give the tofu a mix. Once ready, leave to cool and then transfer to airtight containers ready to power you through the week.

name: Crunchy Tofu Katsu
description: Tofu is a great swap here to keep this dish vegan. The katsu sauce is sublime.
instructions: Coarsely grate carrots and finely chop your onion. Finely grate ginger and garlic.
Heat 1/5 of your oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the carrot, onion, garlic and ginger and fry until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add your curry powder and garam masala, mix then add 1/5 of your flour. Mix well and cook for a minute or so.
Dissolve the stock cube in the water then pour into the pan along with the soy sauce and agave. Let the sauce bubble away for 3 minutes, until thickened.

Turn off the heat and blitz the curry sauce in a blender until very smooth. Drain the chickpeas and save the liquid. Then add the chickpeas to the sauce, add back into a pan and keep warm over a very low heat.
Get your rice on (follow pack instructions).
Tofu time. Slice each of your cubes of tofu into 6 even pieces.

Get 3 bowls out. Add the rest of your flour to one. Add the water from the chickpeas to the second and breadcrumbs to the third. Whisk the chickpea water until it is light and airy. Season the flour and breadcrumbs with salt and pepper.
Dip your tofu into the flour shaking off the excess, then into the whisked chickpea water, then the breadcrumbs, making sure to coat all the sides.
Add the rest of the oil to a pan over a medium high heat. Once it is hot, add your tofu in a single layer, frying for around 4 minutes on each side. once cooked, set aside and drain on kitchen paper.
Serve the tofu on top of your steaming rice with the curry sauce then scatter with sesame seeds and coriander.

name: Crushed Chickpeas & Herby Sumac Tomatoes
description: I had an incredible trip to Egypt a couple years ago where I fell in love with Syrian food and also had some unreal Egyptian dishes. One of the most memorable, was ful medames - a creamy fava bean dish, usually eaten for breakfast. I was inspired by that and Syrian Tis'iyeh (sans bread) for this dish.
keywords: Crushed Chickpeas & Herby Sumac Tomatoes recipe
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Carefully lower in the eggs and cook for 7 mins, until jammy, or a little longer if you like them more done. Transfer to a bowl of iced water to cool down, then peel.
Zest the lemon into a bowl and finely grate in the garlic. Add the cumin and the juice of the zested lemon, then set aside for a couple of minutes.
Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes into 2-3cm chunks and season with salt. Thinly slice the red onion, then pick the herb leaves, discarding the mint stems. Thinly slice the soft parsley stems.

Add the red onion to another bowl and squeeze over the juice of the remaining lemon. Stir the sumac through, season with salt and scrunch the onions a couple of times to help with the pickling. Set aside.

Drain the chickpeas, reserving a splash of the liquid. If you'd like the chickpeas hot, reheat them, if not, add them straight into the lemon and garlic mixture. Mash until creamy but still chunky, and if your chickpeas are tough, simmer them for 20 mins, until soft. Stir the tahini through, along with half the kefir. Season with salt and pepper, then stir the tsp of honey through. Loosen with more kefir or a splash of the reserved chickpea liquid until it has the texture of a chunky, loose mash.

Toss the tomatoes and their juices into the onions, along with the sunflower seeds, the parsley leaves and stems and the mint. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil, then taste and season with more salt, if needed.

Share the crushed chickpeas between bowls and top with the herby sumac tomato salad. Halve the eggs and sit them on top, then finish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper.

name: Crying Tiger Thai Steak Salad
description: Spicy, fresh and easy to make. Try this juicy sirloin steak with a Thai roasted rice dipping sauce, inspired by nam jim jaew.
instructions: Mix the oyster sauce, fish sauce and brown sugar together in a large bowl then add the steak. Massage the marinade into the meat then set aside.

Set a pot of boiling water over a medium heat and add the green beans. Cook for about 4 mins until tender then remove and set aside. Boil the eggs for 6 mins 30 seconds then plunge into ice cold water and set aside.
Wash and dry the lettuce leaves, cut the cucumber into slices at an angle and halve the cherry tomatoes. Set aside.
Heat a small dry pan over a medium heat and add the cashews. Cook for about 5 mins until nicely charred on both sides then remove and set aside.

For the Thai roasted rice dipping sauce, toast the jasmine rice in the same dry pan set over a medium heat. Move the pan occasionally so the rice browns evenly. Cook for about 3 mins until deeply golden brown and smelling like popcorn. Transfer to a pestle and mortar or blender and leave to cool. Once cool, grind to a fine powder then set aside.

Finely slice the green parts of the spring onions and discard the whites. Juice the limes. Mix the spring onions and lime juice with the toasted rice powder and the rest of the dipping sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Taste and add more lime juice if needed. For an authentic smoky aroma, briefly toast the chilli flakes for 30 seconds in a dry pan over a medium heat first, then grind into a rough powder.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan set over a medium heat. Lightly salt each side of the steak then sear for 30 seconds on each side. Repeat for another 30 seconds on each side for a medium-rare steak. Continue for a further 30 seconds on each side for a medium-cooked steak. Remove to a plate and leave to rest for 6 mins.
Meanwhile, peel and halve the egg. When the steak is rested, slice it into thin pieces.

To serve, lay out the lettuce, cucumbers, green beans and cherry tomatoes on a large plate with the steak slices, eggs, toasted cashews, and some crispy shallots. Spoon the dipping sauce over the steak and serve the remaining sauce in a small bowl.

name: Crème Brûlée
description: An indulgent vanilla custard filling with a caramelised torched sugar top. Creamy, crunchy and classic. A perfect dinner party dessert.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

Sit four 175 ml ramekins in a deep roasting tin that’s at least 7.5cm deep (you need it to be deep enough that you can lay a baking tray across the top of the tin to cover the ramekins without touching them).
Combine the cream and milk in a saucepan. Slice the vanilla pod open lengthways and scrape the seeds into the pan, using a sharp knife. Leave it off the heat for now.
Separate the egg yolks from the whites (you can freeze the egg whites in the freezer for meringue). Whisk the yolks and sugar together in a bowl for a minute until pale and fluffing up.
Set the pan with the cream over a medium heat and bring it almost to the boil. When you see bubbles start to appear around the edge, take off the heat immediately.

Slowly pour the hot cream into the beaten egg yolks, whisking as you go. Scoop off and discard the pale foam sitting on the top of the liquid (there will be several spoonfuls). Give the mixture a good stir.

Pour enough cold water into the roasting tin to come about 1.5cm up the sides of the ramekins. Pour the hot cream into the ramekins, filling them up right to the top (it’s easier to spoon in the last bit).

Lay a baking tray over the top of the roasting tin, sitting well above and completely covering the ramekins, but not completely covering the roasting tin; leave a small gap at one side to allow air to circulate.

Put the roasting tin in the oven and bake for 30-35 mins until the mixture is just set. To check, give the roasting tin a very gentle shake - if the brûlées are ready, they will wobble a bit in the middle. Don't go past this point!
Remove the ramekins and set them on a wire rack to cool for a few mins, then put in the fridge to cool completely (you can do this overnight if making them in advance).
When ready to serve, wipe round the top edge of the dishes, sprinkle 1 ½ tsp caster sugar over each ramekin and spread it out with the back of a spoon to completely cover.
Use a blowtorch to caramelise the sugar. Hold the flame just above the sugar and keep moving it round and round until caramelised. Serve when the sugar is firm.

name: Crème Brûlée Hot Chocolate
description: A rich and indulgent dark hot chocolate with a torched vanilla cream foam. The most comforting and delicious drink to keep you warm this winter.
instructions: For the hot chocolate: roughly break the chocolate into pieces into a medium saucepan. Add the water, sugar, cocoa powder, vanilla paste and salt. Set it over a medium heat and stir until the chocolate has melted.
For the cold foam: in a separate mixing bowl, add the double cream, whole milk, icing sugar, vanilla paste and salt. Whisk for 2-3 mins until fluffy.
Pour the dark hot chocolate into mugs and top with some cold foam.
Serve as is or, if you have a blow torch, top the cold foam with the demerara sugar and blow torch until caramelised.

name: Crème Pâtissière Filling
description: This thick and creamy vanilla pastry filling is useful for loads of bakes. Use it to fill doughnuts, as a base for tarts, or even as a luxurious cake filling.
instructions: Slit the vanilla pod open lengthways and scrape out the seeds into a heavy-based saucepan. Add the empty pod and milk to the pan and set it over a low-medium heat. Heat it slowly and gently until just boiling, to infuse the vanilla.
Meanwhile, use a spoon to mix the egg yolks and sugar together in a mixing bowl until fully combined. Sift in the flour and mix again until incorporated.

Slowly pour the just-boiling milk over the yolk and butter mixture and whisk the mixture constantly to prevent curdling. Transfer the mixture back into the saucepan and cook it over a medium heat for about 5 mins, whisking constantly, until very thick.
Pass the mixture through a fine sieve into a bowl and discard the vanilla pod. Place a sheet of clingfilm on the surface of the custard to prevent a skin forming. Leave to cool, then refrigerate.
In a separate bowl, use an electric whisk to beat together the cream until thick and creamy with stiff peaks forming (don't continue past this point). Fold the whipped cream into the chilled custard.
Use the crème pâtissière to fill doughnuts or as a base for tarts.

name: Cucumber & Wakame Salad with Peanut Sauce
description: Bulked-out cucumber and seaweed salad with a glorious creamy peanut dressing. A great dish to eat fresh, or even meal prep.
keywords: Cucumber & Wakame Salad with Peanut Sauce
instructions: Put all the dressing ingredients into a bowl and stir together until fully incorporated. Add 1 tbsp cold water at a time until creamy. Taste and season with salt, then set aside.

Place the wakame into a bowl and cover with cold water. Trim and quarter the cucumbers. Crush or bash the cucumber pieces using a heavy item or rolling pin until they break open, then cut them into 2cm pieces. Trim and quarter the radishes, then tip them and the cucumber pieces into a mixing bowl.

Reheat the grains and allow to cool slightly until warm. Toss them into the veggies. Drain the wakame and add to the mixing bowl along with the dressing. Toss together until evenly distributed, then share between plates.

name: Cucumber Breeze
description: A crisp and refreshing cocktail that's perfect for a sunny day. The cucumber notes
instructions: Using a peeler, peel your cucumber one or two times to make a long strip for garnish.
Blend up the remaining cucumber and strain through a sieve, collecting the juice.
Fill a cocktail shaker with ice and then go in with 50ml of the cucumber juice, lemon, St Germain and vodka.
Shake and strain into a rocks glass with ice.
Garnish with your cucumber strip and enjoy.

name: Cucumber Salad
description: This fresh cucumber salad pairs wonderfully with just about everything. They're a quick and easy way to add some zip to a meal.
keywords: Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Cucumber Salad
Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Cucumber Salad recipe
instructions: Finely slice the cucumber and add it to a bowl with the chilli oil, rice vinegar, a pinch of salt and the sesame seeds. Finely slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish.
Serve the cucumber salad with your protein of choice and top it with a scattering of spring onions.

name: Cumin Lamb Scotch Egg
description: A homemade scotch egg is special, forget overcooked eggs and bland sausage. These are super crispy and have a perfect runny yolk. Step aside dead scotch eggs.
instructions: Start by toasting your Sichuan pepper and cumin seeds. Get them into a small saucepan and set over a low heat for 5 mins or until they are toasty and fragrant. Coarsely crush in a pestle and mortar or spice grinder.
Now, roughly chop the spring onions, garlic, ginger, and chillies and chuck into a blender. Add the soy, black vinegar and your crushed spices. Blend until you have a smooth paste.

Add the lamb mince to a bowl and pour in your seasoning paste. Roughly chop the coriander and get that in the bowl too, along with a big pinch of salt. Thoroughly mix until you have a homogenous, slightly sticky mixture.
At this point, you can fry a little piece off to check the seasoning! Add a splash of soy or a pinch of salt if needed.
Boil 5 of the eggs for exactly 6 mins, then put them straight into a bowl of icy water. Peel the eggs and pop them on a plate.

Divide the mince into 5 roughly equal portions. Pick up one of the portions and place in your left hand, flatten out on your palm and place the egg in the center, now wrap the mince around the egg, pinching the meat together to seal the egg inside. Repeat with the remaining mince and eggs.
Pop the flour into a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Beat the remaining eggs in a separate bowl with a splash of water and a pinch of salt. Put the panko into a third bowl.
Now pass the eggs through the seasoned flour, beaten egg mixture and panko. To make them extra crispy, I like to go back into the egg and add a second layer of breadcrumbs.
Heat a pot of oil to 160°C, fry the scotch eggs in batches until golden brown, this should take around 5 mins. Drain on kitchen paper.
Finely slice the cabbage and scrunch with a pinch of salt.
Halve your scotch eggs and serve warm with a pinch of salted cabbage, mayo and chilli oil.

name: Cumin Lamb Stir Fry
description: Also known as 孜然羊肉, this popular dish from Xinjiang is aromatic and slightly numbing from the Sichuan peppercorns. Served with rice to make the perfect easy weeknight meal.
instructions: Using a sharp knife, cut the lamb into thin slices against the grain. Add the lamb to a mixing bowl along with the bicarbonate soda and enough cold water to fully submerge the lamb. Mix well then set aside for 20 mins to tenderise the meat.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the red onion, mince the garlic and thinly slice the ginger. Slice the leek on an angle into small pieces and halve the padron peppers. Remove the coriander leaves from the stems. Roughly chop the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems. Set aside.

Wash your rice three times until the water runs clear. Drain, then transfer to a large saucepan and add water until it reaches just below your first knuckle. Bring to the boil over a medium-high heat, then turn the heat to low and cover with a lid for 12 mins.
Remove the lamb from the water and give the lamb and bowl a good rinse. Return the lamb to the bowl and add all the marinade ingredients. Mix well.
Heat ⅗ of the vegetable oil in a wok set over a medium heat. Add the lamb and cook for a few mins, just to par-cook the lamb. Then transfer to a bowl and set aside. Drain the oil.

Heat the remaining vegetable oil in the clean wok set over a medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion, garlic, ginger, coriander stems, leeks and padron peppers and stir fry for 2 mins.
Grind the Sichuan peppercorns in a pestle and mortar.

Add the par-cooked lamb and marinade. Mix to combine, then add the chilli oil, chilli flakes, ground cumin and Sichuan peppercorns. Stir fry for another 2 mins (or longer if you prefer the lamb more well done).
Pour in the Shaoxing wine from the edge of the wok and mix until evenly coated. Remove the wok from the heat and stir through the roughly chopped coriander leaves.
Divide the rice between plates then top with the stir-fried lamb.

name: Curried Carrot Dal
description: The most simple, delicious dal. The turmeric is so earthy and warming. Topped with charred curried carrots and a cooling coriander coconut chutney. Heaven.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Peel the carrots and cut them into finger-length pieces. Transfer to a large roasting tray. Spoon over the cumin seeds and curry powder, season well with sea salt and black pepper. Drizzle over some oil. Use your hands to coat the carrots in the spices then spread out into a single layer. Roast in the oven for 35 minutes until completely tender and a little charred.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger. Get a saucepan over a medium heat. Pour a glug of oil. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes then add in the garlic and ginger. Cook for a minute more.

Add the turmeric and stir then add your lentils and give everything a good mix. Next, pour the hot water into the pan. Simmer the dahl away over a medium heat for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally until the lentils have absorbed the majority of the liquid, have completely broken down and are creamy.

Whilst the dahl and carrots cook add your chilli and coriander to a blender (save a small amount of coriander for garnish). Blitz until finely chopped then, add the desiccated coconut, 2/3 of the coconut yoghurt. Season with salt and black pepper. Blitz again to form a vivid green chutney to a drizzling consistency.

Cut the lime/s in half and squeeze the juice into the dahl, then add the rest of the coconut yoghurt, season with salt and pepper. Stir everything together, then divide between bowls. Top with the curried carrots, along with any roasting oils then spoon over the coriander coconut chutney. Scatter over the remaining coriander leaves. Next, tuck in and enjoy!

name: Curried Cauliflower Cheese Croquetas
description: Easy cheesy croquetas that combine everything you love about cauliflower cheese with a nice hit of spice.
instructions: Chop the cauliflower into florets. Steam for 5 mins until totally tender. Allow to cool slightly, then chop into small pieces.
Grate the cheddar. Finely chop the green chilli and garlic.

Put the butter in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Tip in the green chilli, garlic, cumin seeds and mustard seeds. Let them cook for about a minute until the seeds start popping. Once melted, tip in 50g flour and the curry powder. Cook for 3 mins. Gradually add the milk, whisking until you have a smooth sauce.

Bring the mixture to a boil, then simmer for 5 mins until thickened. Add the mustard, cheddar and cauliflower, then stir to combine. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Pour into a wide dish to set in the fridge for at least 3 hrs.

Tip the remaining flour, eggs and breadcrumbs into separate bowls. Roll your croqueta mixture into 22 evenly-sized balls (each one should be a little smaller than a table tennis ball). Doing this with wet hands will stop the mixture from sticking to your palms too much. Dip them in the flour, eggs and breadcrumbs respectively. Pop them in the fridge or freezer to chill while you make the mayo.

Finely chop the green chilli and garlic. Add the egg yolks to the small barrel of a food processor, plus the garlic and mustard. Run the machine, then gradually drizzle in the rapeseed oil. When the mixture looks very thick, squeeze in the juice of 1 lemon, then keep adding the oil. If you need to loosen it any more, do so with splashes of water. Add the green chilli, then whizz again. Season the mayo to taste with salt.

Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a small saucepan, taking the oil to about ⅓ of the way up the pan. Once it reaches 170°C, add the croquetas a few at a time, and fry for 4 mins until they are crisp and golden. Keep warm and repeat with the remaining croquetas.
Serve with a small grating of cheddar on top and a dollop of mayo.

name: Curried Cheese on Toast
description: Welsh rarebit, with a spicy twist. A rich curry paste gets mixed with cheese and milk before being spread on toast and grilled until bubbling.
instructions: Thinly slice one of the red onions and place in a small bowl. Add the juice of the lemon, season with a good pinch of salt and scrunch with your hand to quick pickle.
Finely dice the garlic, ginger and the other onion.
Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and cook for 1 min.
Add the onion and cook until softened and beginning to brown, then add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 min.
Add the garam masala, ground turmeric and Kashmiri chilli powder and cook for 30 seconds. Precise, I know, but ground spices can burn very quickly!
Stir in the chutney and transfer to a mixing bowl to cool.
Heat your oven grill to high.
Place the sourdough slices on a baking sheet and toast on both sides.
Meanwhile, grate the Cheddar. Add it to the curry paste with the milk and mix to combine.
Spread the mixture over the toasts. Pop them back under the grill until melted and bubbling.
Meanwhile, finely chop the fresh coriander.
Top the toasts with fresh coriander and some quick pickled onions, then tuck in and enjoy!

name: Curried Chicken Burgers With Romesco Sauce
description: Grilled chicken burgers with smoky homemade romesco and a tangy slaw. This meal is super easy, and is made even quicker if you prep your mise ahead of time.
keywords: Curried Chicken Burgers With Romesco Sauce
instructions: Place the chicken thighs, ground turmeric, and 2 tsp of curry powder into a bowl. Grate a clove of garlic into the chicken, add 2 tbsp of olive oil, season with salt and pepper, mix then set aside to marinate.

Trim and finely slice the fennel – If you have a mandoline slicer, now is the time to use it. If not, a sharp knife will do the job nicely. Trim and thinly slice the asparagus into rounds, keeping the tops whole. Add the fennel, asparagus, and its tops into the bowl with the juice of a lime, 2 tbsp of olive oil and 50g Greek yoghurt. Season with salt and pepper. Toss until evenly coated, set aside.

Drain the roasted peppers and add them into a blender or food processor with the almonds, 40ml of olive oil, and the remaining garlic and curry powder. Blend until you get a smooth thick sauce. Season with salt and pepper, then set aside.

Heat a drizzle of oil into a grill pan or non-stick frying pan on medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot, add the chicken thighs and cook for 5-8 mins on both sides until cooked, turn the heat down if the chicken is colouring too quickly.
Halve and toast the buns.

Slather some romesco onto the bottom bun. Top with two grilled chicken thighs, some fennel slaw, and spread yoghurt onto the top bun. Serve the burgers with the remaining fennel and asparagus salad alongside.

name: Curried Chicken Meatballs with Curried Coconut Noodles
description: These really are fantastic meatballs. Very easy to make, and to really hammer home how excellent this recipe is, my 3 daughters demolished this for their breakfast when I made this at home.
instructions: For the meatballs, add the chicken mince into a bowl with the green curry paste, soy sauce and fish sauce. Grate in the ginger and garlic, stir until evenly combined. Roll or spoon the mixture into walnut sized meatballs.

Heat a drizzle of vegetable oil in a wide pan set over a medium heat. Fry the chicken meatballs for 2-3 mins until nicely coloured but not yet fully cooked through. Add the sugar and stir well to coat, then cook for about 30 seconds until the sugar caramelises. Remove to a plate and wipe out the pan.

For the curried coconut broth, chop the garlic and finely grate the ginger. Heat a drizzle of vegetable oil in the same pan you used to cook the meatballs, set over a medium heat. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for about 30 seconds until aromatic. Add the curry paste and cook for another 30 seconds, giving the saucepan a good stir.
Add the coconut milk and water and bring to the boil. Thinly slice the lime leaves, discarding the central rib, and add them to the pan.

Add the chicken balls to the sauce and bring it to the boil, then lower the heat and gently simmer uncovered for about 10-15 mins until the chicken balls are cooked through. Season with fish sauce and soy sauce according to taste.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles following the instructions on the pack.
Divide the noodles between bowls. Top each serving of noodles with some chicken balls and coconut sauce, then top with coriander, along with plenty of crispy onions and a wedge of lime.

name: Curried Chicken Sandwich
description: Here's another easy recipe you can make with your batch-cooked Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken. It's really simple to make and is absolutely delicious.
instructions: Make the Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken batch recipe.
Squeeze the garlic bulb into a bowl and mix the mayo through.
Halve the marinated tomatoes and roughly chop half the cooked onions. Add both to a bowl, zest over ¼ of the lime and squeeze over the juice. Toss together then taste and season with salt, if needed.
Shred one chicken breast and the wings, discarding any bones. Toss through the onion mixture.
Slice the focaccia pieces in half and then toast them. Spread the mayo onto the cut sides, top with baby gem leaves, chicken salad and crispy shallots. Sandwich together.

name: Curried Chicken Schnitzel with Burst Tomato Butter Sauce
description: Crispy, juicy, flavourful chicken schnitzel and a beautiful burst tomato butter sauce to go along (everything should have this sauce drizzled over), it’s fab.
keywords: Curried Chicken Schnitzel with Burst Tomato Butter Sauce
instructions: Place the chicken between two squares of baking parchment. Gently bash with a rolling pin to flatten them to 2cm. Place the chicken in the buttermilk, season with salt, garam masala and curry powder. Mix and let marinate for a minimum of 1 hour, up to overnight.

Once ready, add the flour onto a plate, season with salt and pepper, and add the breadcrumbs onto another plate. Dip each chicken thigh into the flour, pat off the extra, then coat in egg, then breadcrumbs until thoroughly coated. Place the schnitzels onto a baking tray.

Place a large saucepan onto medium-high heat and fill with 1cm of oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook until golden brown and cooked through (turn the heat down slightly if it's browning too quickly), 3-4 mins on each side.
Meanwhile, peel, halve and finely slice the shallot and garlic, peel and finely dice the ginger, trim and mince the chilli. Finely mince the coriander.

Place another frying pan on medium heat with 2 tbsp of oil. Once hot, stir through the cumin seeds and fry for 20 secs. Add the shallot, cook until softened. Then add the garlic, chilli and ginger, cook for 2-3 mins. Pour in the chicken stock and tomatoes bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to medium-low and simmer until reduced by three-quarters, 7-10 mins.
Once reduced, remove from the heat, stir in the cold butter until the sauce has thickened. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice, then fold in the coriander.
Serve the curried chicken schnitzels with the burst tomato butter sauce.

name: Curried Chicken Skewers with Green Chilli Yoghurt
description: Just a handful of ingredients deliver a beautiful plate of food. The carrot salad might even be the star of the show!
instructions: Dice up the chicken and add to a mixing bowl along with the curry powder, 100g of the yoghurt and a big pinch of salt. Mix well and leave to sit for 15 mins.
Finely chop the mint and chilli (saving a pinch of each for garnish) and mince the garlic, mix everything with the remaining yoghurt and set aside.
Finely grate the carrot and mix with a pinch of salt and the juice of half the lemon.
Thread the chicken onto skewers and cook under a hot grill for 10 mins, turning half way, until nicely browned and cooked through.

Toast the pitta and pop onto a plate along with the grated carrot. Add a big spoon of the yoghurt and spread out slightly on the plate. Top with the chicken skewers and sprinkle with the remaining mint and chilli.

name: Curried Chicken, Lentil & Rice Soup
description: A nourishing chicken and brothy rice bowl with yoghurt and homemade curry oil. This one is simple but special, and only takes 35 minutes.
instructions: Pop your lentils and rice in a sieve and rinse under cold water until the water runs clear.
Tip them into a large saucepan and top it up with the water. Set the pan over a medium heat and bring the water up to a boil, then skim any scum off the top with a wooden spoon.
Turn the heat down to a simmer, then add your ground turmeric and chicken thighs. Simmer the mixture, uncovered, for 25 mins.
Meanwhile, peel your ginger and chop it into 2mm wide matchsticks. Peel and finely slice your garlic.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat and add your ginger, garlic, cumin seeds and curry leaves. Cook for a minute until the seeds and the curry leaves pop, but before the garlic takes on colour. Switch off the heat, then stir through your chilli powder. This is your spiced-infused oil.

Remove the chicken from the saucepan and use two forks to shred it into pieces. Return it to the saucepan with the lentils, rice and turmeric broth. Add the yoghurt and pour in ¾ of the spice-infused oil. Give it a mix, then season it to taste with salt.
To serve, divide the soup between bowls, drizzle over some remaining spice-infused oil and finish with some fresh coriander leaves.

name: Curried Chickpeas Loaded Sweet Potatoes
description: Super soft baked sweet potatoes stuffed with spiced chickpeas, crushed pistachios and creamy coconut yoghurt. A cosy plant-based meal that delivers on protein and flavour.
instructions: Heat your oven at 200C.

Place the sweet potatoes on a baking tin previously lined with baking paper and drizzle them with olive oil, pinch of salt and pepper. Brush them to evenly coat. Roast them for 40-50 mins until soft and juicy.
While the potatoes roast, dice the onions and mince the garlic. Heat a good glug of olive oil in a pan over a medium heat then add the onion and garlic. Let them cook until softened and brown.

Add the spices and stir to let the flavour infuse. Add the chickpeas and stir again. Add a splash of vegetable stock (the more you add, the creamier and saucier it will be). Add nutritional yeast and spinach and stir until wilted. Let it simmer on a low heat, stirring now and then. The chickpeas should be creamy and not too dry. If they are too dry, add more stock. Leave to simmer until the sweet potatoes are cooked. Finally stir through both types of yoghurts and gently heat through until warm.

To serve, divide the cooked sweet potatoes between plates and slice them open down the middle. Top with the creamy chickpeas, a dollop of vegan yoghurt (coconut or soy), crushed pistachios, coriander, sliced red chilli, and a pinch of salt and pepper.

name: Curried Clam Noodles
description: Clams are a lean source of protein and rich in vitamins and minerals. Cooking clams couldn’t be easier, and pair perfectly with the coconut sauce and noodles.
instructions:
Give the clams a rinse in a bowl of cold water, discarding any
that have broken shells and don’t stay shut when you squeeze them
tightly in the palm of your hand. Drain into a colander, then tip
back into the bowl and keep in the fridge while you prep.
Get a kettle on to boil. Put the rice noodles into a large bowl,
pour over the boiling water and leave for about 10 mins, or until
softened.
Finely chop the shallots, garlic, ginger and coriander stalks. Get
your largest saucepan (one with a tight-fitting lid) over a medium
heat. Pour in the rapeseed oil and add the shallots, along with a
pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until soft. Add the garlic,
ginger and coriander stalks, cook for 1 minute, then spoon in the
ground spices.
Give everything a good mix to combine, cook for 30 seconds
more until smelling amazing, then pour in the coconut milk. Turn
up the heat to medium-high and bring the sauce to the boil.
Once boiling, tip in the clams. Immediately put a lid on the pan
and cook, shaking the pan occasionally, for 3–4 mins until all the
clams have opened.
Meanwhile, very thinly slice the pak choi and roughly chop the
coriander leaves. Drain the noodles into a sieve.
Once the clams have opened, add the noodles, pak choi and most
of the coriander leaves. Give everything a good toss to combine,
cook for a further minute until the pak choi have just wilted, then
squeeze in the lime juice. Season to taste.
Divide the curried clam noodles between four bowls and scatter
over the remaining coriander to serve.

name: Curried Coconut Chicken & Rice
description: This tangy Thai-inspired recipe makes a very strong argument for chicken being the most delicious meats of all-time.
instructions: Put the chicken into a bowl. Grate the garlic on top, then stir half the oyster sauce through. Season with salt and pepper, then set aside to marinate. Pick the coriander and thinly chop the stalks. Set aside.

Place a saucepan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add a splash of coconut milk and cook for a couple of seconds. Stir through the coriander stalks, curry paste and remaining oyster sauce until fragrant. Add the water and remaining coconut milk, bring to the boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 10-15 mins.

Meanwhile, place a frying pan with a drizzle of oil over a medium-high heat. Once hot, cook the marinated chicken on both sides, until slightly charred and cooked through. Taste and season the broth with lime juice, salt, sugar and pepper.
Divide the rice between bowls, ladle the soup on top and finish with sliced chicken. Drizzle over the chilli oil and scatter with your crispy onions. Finish with the coriander leaves.

name: Curried Coconut Chickpeas On Toast
description: Imagine beans on toast with creamy coconut yoghurt, fresh ginger, garlic and lime. This is what you get with this saucy little curried chickpea number.
instructions:
Open the tins of chickpeas, drain into a sieve and rinse with fresh
water. Leave in the sieve to drain again while you make the base
of the curry.
Get a large frying pan over a low heat and dollop in a generous
tablespoon of coconut oil. While it is melting, finely grate the
garlic cloves and ginger straight into the pan. Turn up the heat to
high and add the curry powder. Fry for 1 minute, stirring, to cook
out the spices.
Tip in the chickpeas and give everything a good mix. Leave to fry,
stirring occasionally, while you toast the sourdough bread.
Empty the coconut yogurt into the pan, then half-fill the pot with
water and pour that in too and mix everything together. Bring to
the boil and let the chickpeas bubble away in the creamy sauce
for a minute or two. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Cut one lime into four wedges and the other lime in half. Squeeze
the juice of the halved lime over the chickpeas in the pan, then
scatter over the nigella seeds and tear over the coriander.
Divide the toast between four plates and top with mounds of
the curried chickpeas. Serve with the lime wedges on the side
for squeezing over.

name: Curried Corn on the Cob
description: Peanut, creamy and spicy corn on the cob. This rich west African - Gujarati meal was one of my mums favourites! Seema x
keywords: curried Corn on the Cob recipes
fun Corn on the Cob recipes
healthy Corn on the Cob recipes
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add in your corn cobs and boil for 7 mins. Remove the corn and set aside, reserve 1 cup of the boiling water.

In a blender, blend the onions until roughly chopped and set aside. Then blend the garlic, ginger and 5 chillies until smooth. Set this aside and then finally blend the tinned tomato and 50g peanuts until smooth.

Heat a large pot and add in a glug of oil. Fry the cumin seeds until they start to sizzle and then add in the blended onion. Cook for 5 mins on a medium-high heat until golden. Add in the tomato puree and cook for another 5 mins until darkened. Add in the garlic mixture and cook for 1 min until fragrant then finally pour in the blended tomato mix.
Add in the ground cumin, ground coriander, chilli powder, turmeric and 3 tsp of salt.
Cook for 10 mins until the colour has darkened and the sauce is thick.
Add the corn back in and give it cook mix, cook for 2 mins.
Pour in 200ml of the corn cooking liquid and the coconut milk.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 mins until the sauce is thick and nicely coats the corn.
Meanwhile roughly chop the saved peanuts, finely slice the remaining green chilli and coriander.
Serve in bowls with peanuts, chilli and coriander.

name: Curried Fish Burger
description: Between 2 Buns episode one – this one's a ripper. Crispy fried fish, spiced curried mayo, mango slaw, pickled cucumbers, and mint yoghurt. Oh, and a bun. B x
instructions: Mix together the yoghurt and mint with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Mix together a tablespoon of curry powder with the mango chutney and mayo.
Combine the cabbage, chilli, spring onion, coriander, and mango. Season with salt and a big squeeze of lemon.
Drain the pickled cucumbers.
Season the cod loin with salt. Whisk together the flours with the baking powder, remaining curry powder, and a pinch of salt. Whisk in the lager until smooth.

Heat a pan of vegetable oil to 190°C. Dredge the fish in some extra rice flour, pass it through the spiced beer batter and fry for 10-12 minutes until cooked through, crispy, and golden. Season with salt and drain on kitchen paper.

Toast the buns and build your burgers. Start with a layer of mint yoghurt, then follow it up with some pickled cucumbers. Lay the fish down, add a handful of slaw, and slather the top bun with your curried mayo. Crown your creation and give it a squish. Get stuck in.

name: Curried Fish Pie
description: Fish and prawns covered in a fragrant, rich coconut sauce; mash potato flecked with sweet slices of spring onions; and a cumin and mustard seed-spiced butter.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C.
Peel and quarter the potatoes. Tip into a large saucepan of cold salted water and bring to the boil. Once boiling, cook for 10-15 mins until mashable.

Meanwhile make the curried sauce. Thinly slice all the spring onions (green and white parts). Finely grate the ginger and garlic. Place a medium saucepan over a medium heat, add 50g of butter in and let it melt. Once melted, add half the spring onions and all the ginger and garlic. Fry, stirring, for 1 min. Spoon in the curry powder and flour, and fry for a further minute

Gradually pour in the coconut milk, whisking as you go to keep the sauce lump-free. Bubble the sauce away for 5 minutes until nice and thick. Season to taste with salt and black pepper. Add the baby spinach, turn off the heat and set aside to wilt.

Come back to the potatoes. Drain them in a colander and steam dry. Tip them back into their saucepan and mash. Melt the remaining butter in a small frying pan over a medium heat. Add the cumin and mustard seeds and fry for 30 seconds until the mustard seeds begin to pop. Pour the flavoured butter into the mash, add the remaining spring onions and mix well. Season with salt and black pepper.

Divide the fish pie mix, prawns and peas evenly over the bottom of a medium pie dish. Mix the spinach into the sauce then spoon over. Top with the spiced mash, using a fork to rough up the top and edges.

Bake in the oven for 25 mins until piping hot. Preheat your grill to high. Slide the pie under the hot grill for 5 mins until the mash is a little crisp and golden. Serve at the table and let people help themselves

name: Curried Ketchup Hot Dogs with Onion Jam
description: This is a take on the classic currywurst; juicy sausages with a sticky onion jam and spicy ketchup all loaded into hot dog buns.
keywords: curried ketchup hotdogs with onion jam
instructions: Melt the butter in a pan over a medium heat. Finely chop the onions and add along with a pinch of salt. Allow to cook down for about 20 mins until soft and sticky, then add the vinegar and sugar and cook for another 5 mins.
Mix the ketchup, mustard and curry powder in a small bowl. If you want to make them look a bit fancy, add the mix to a squeezy bottle.
Cook the sausages until golden brown and cooked through. Meanwhile, slice open the hotdog buns and spread with a layer of the onion jam.
Load the sausages into the buns, squeeze over the curried ketchup and finish with a sprinkling of finely chopped chives.

name: Curried Lentil, Sweet Potato & Coconut Gratin
description: This delicious, creamy, coconutty dish is something between a shepherd’s pie and a curry. With curried coconut cream bringing the creaminess and flavour, it’s a simple, healthy and incredibly tasty all-in-one.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Reserve a splash of coconut milk for topping the gratin and add the remaining coconut milk, curry powder, chilli powder and salt to a bowl. Whisk to combine.
Slice the sweet potato into very thin slices and add these to the bowl with the curried coconut milk and toss to cover each piece.
Drain the lentils.

Layer the lentils in a large cast iron pan or baking dish, then cover with the sweet potatoes and drizzle over the leftover coconut milk. Cover and bake for 35-45 mins, until the potatoes have softened, then remove the lid and place under the grill on high to crisp up for 5 mins.

To make the topping, slice the ginger into thin matchsticks and finely slice the garlic and chilli. Add olive oil to a small frying pan on medium-low heat. Add the ginger, garlic, chilli and curry leaves and fry until crispy for about 5 mins. Take care not to let it burn and remove it from the hot pan, along with the oil as soon as it’s ready.
To serve, drizzle the aromatic oil onto the gratin along with the remaining coconut milk.

name: Curried Mango Chicken & Garlicky Rice with Greens
description: Sticky, curry-glazed chicken with tangy mango sauce, garlicky rice and wilted greens. Who said healthy food had to be boring?
instructions: Rinse the jasmine rice in a saucepan under cold water until it runs clear. Add the measured water and a big pinch of salt.

Bash the garlic cloves for the rice and remove their skins. Add them to the rice and place over a high heat. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid, then turn the heat down to low. Cook for 12 mins, then remove from the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for 10 mins.

Butterfly the chicken breasts. In a bowl, mix together the curry powder and half the olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper, then toss the chicken through the marinade until well coated. Set aside.
Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with the remaining olive oil. Once hot, add the kale and cook for 2-3 mins until just wilted. Transfer to a plate.
Add the chicken to the empty pan and cook for 10-15 mins, turning halfway, until golden on both sides.
Finely grate the garlic and ginger into a small bowl. Stir through the mango chutney and water to make a loose sauce.
Once the chicken is golden, pour in the mango sauce and cook, basting, until it glazes the chicken and the meat is cooked through, 5-6 mins.
Use scissors to snip any large watercress into smaller pieces. Add it to the chicken with the kale, cover with a lid and leave to steam over low heat for 2-4 mins until the greens have wilted.

Fluff the rice with a fork and divide between Tupperware containers. Top with the glazed chicken, greens and any extra sauce from the pan. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Curried Mango Chicken & Garlicky Rice with Greens
description: Sticky, curry-glazed chicken with tangy mango sauce, garlicky rice and wilted greens. Who said healthy food had to be boring?
instructions: Rinse the jasmine rice in a saucepan under cold water until it runs clear. Add the measured water and a big pinch of salt.

Bash the garlic cloves for the rice and remove their skins. Add them to the rice and place over a high heat. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid, then turn the heat down to low. Cook for 12 mins, then remove from the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for 10 mins.

Butterfly the chicken breasts. In a bowl, mix together the curry powder and half the olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper, then toss the chicken through the marinade until well coated. Set aside.
Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with the remaining olive oil. Once hot, add the kale and cook for 2-3 mins until just wilted. Transfer to a plate.
Add the chicken to the empty pan and cook for 10-15 mins, turning halfway, until golden on both sides.
Finely grate the garlic and ginger into a small bowl. Stir through the mango chutney and water to make a loose sauce.
Once the chicken is golden, pour in the mango sauce and cook, basting, until it glazes the chicken and the meat is cooked through, 5-6 mins.
Use scissors to snip any large watercress into smaller pieces. Add it to the chicken with the kale, cover with a lid and leave to steam over low heat for 2-4 mins until the greens have wilted.
Fluff the rice with a fork and divide between plates. Top with the glazed chicken, greens and any extra sauce from the pan. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Curried Parsnip Soup Recipe with Crispy Garlic Topper
description: This creamy parsnip soup recipe is super comforting with warming spices – but it’s the crispy, spicy bits on top that bring it to life.  Parsnip soup is a delightful and warming dish perfect for any meal, from a cosy lunch to a hearty dinner. This parsnip soup recipe combines the natural sweetness of parsnips with aromatic garlic, ginger, and a touch of spicy cumin, creating a rich and flavourful experience. The ingredients are simple yet nutritious, featuring vegetables, stock, and a blend of spices like turmeric and thyme.. Pair this soup with crusty bread or crunchy croutons for added texture. Leftovers can be stored in the fridge or freezer, making it a convenient option for meal prep. Whether you're simmering this soup for a comforting lunch or spicing it up for dinner with a dash of chilli, this parsnip soup will surely become a favourite in your recipe collection.
keywords: Curried Parsnip Soup Recipe with Crispy Garlic Topper
instructions: Use a teaspoon to peel and discard the skin from the ginger. Cut the ginger into thin slices and then into matchsticks. Thinly slice the garlic cloves. Cut the shallots into thin rings. Peel and cut the parsnips into 3cm pieces. Set everything aside.

Heat a splash of the vegetable oil in a medium, lidded saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add one-quarter of the ginger, shallot and garlic and fry for 2 mins, stirring all the time. Chuck in the parsnip pieces along with the curry powder, then toss really well in the spiced oil.

Pour in the coconut milk and stock, season well with salt and pepper and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer, put the lid on (leave a small gap, so some steam can escape) and cook for 25 mins until the parsnip pieces are really soft. Use a stick blender to whizz until completely smooth. Season with salt and pepper and a squeeze of lime juice. Keep warm.

Heat the remaining oil in a small frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the remaining shallot rings and fry for 3-4 mins until beginning to just turn golden. Add the remaining garlic and ginger and cook for 2-3 mins until everything is getting caramelised. Scatter in the whole spices and chilli flakes and cook for another minute.
Divide the soup between bowls, spoon over the crispy bits and spices, then scatter with coriander leaves to serve.

name: Curried Roast Chicken Noodle Soup
description: Here's another recipe you can make with your batch-cooked slow-roasted curried coconut chicken. This chicken noodle soup is wholesome, warming, and absolutely delicious.
instructions: Make the Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken batch recipe.
Pick the coriander and finely mince the stalks.

Tip all the chicken liquor into a pan, top up with water or chicken stock until you have a total of 800ml of soup base. Add ½ of the onions in and the tomatoes. Stir the coriander stalks through. Shred the chicken thighs and add in to reheat.
Taste and season the soup with fish sauce, if needed. Cook the noodles according to package instructions.
Add the noodles into a bowl, pour over the soup, top with the veggies and chicken. Finish with a drizzle of chilli oil and serve with lime wedges.

name: Curried Roasted Roots & Sticky Mango Halloumi
description: Curried roots are an autumn game changer, we love how sweet and nutty they go when roasted. Here we’ve made a cheeky coriander chilli yoghurt and fried off some mango chutney glazed halloumi to go with for an epic veggie meal.
keywords: Curried Roasted Roots & Sticky Mango Halloumi
Curried Roasted Roots & Sticky Mango Halloumi recipe
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C.
Leaving the skin on the sweet potato cut into medium-sized pieces. Depending on your carrots and parsnips, peel and then cut into the same size pieces. Cut the onions into wedges.

Toss the veg on your largest roasting tray (or do it between two trays if easier) with the curry powder, plenty of seasoning and a good glug of neutral oil. Spread into a single layer then roast for 25-30 mins until tender and a little caramelised.

Meanwhile roughly chop the green chilli and three-quarters of your coriander (stalks and all). Add to a mini food processor or blender along with 100g yoghurt and 1 tsp mango chutney. Zest and juice in 1 lime, blitz until a vivid green yoghurt then stir back through the remaining yoghurt to thicken, season to taste.

Once the veg is nearly cooked through, cut the halloumi into cubes. Fry over a medium-high heat until nicely golden on both sides then remove the pan from the heat, stir through the remaining 2 tbsp mango chutney, onion or cumin seeds, tossing to coat the halloumi in the spiced glaze.

Mix the rocket, remaining coriander leaves, curried roots and remaining lime juice together. Spread the yoghurt across the bottom of a bowl, top with the roasted roots and crispy glazed halloumi, to serve. If you’re feeling extra hungry, eat it with bread.

name: Curried Sesame Air Fryer Schnitzel With Pickled Ginger Slaw
description: This is a curried sesame schnitzel which is essentially a massive nugget, and we've served it up with a pickled ginger slaw and garlicky mayo for your weeknight dinner needs.
