keywords: Curried Sesame Air Fryer Schnitzel With Pickled Ginger Slaw
Curried Sesame Air Fryer Schnitzel With Pickled Ginger Slaw recipe
instructions: Place a large piece of baking paper on a chopping board. Add the chicken with a good space in between. Cover with another piece of baking paper and bash the chicken until flattened – you're looking for it to be around 2cm thick.

Add the panko breadcrumbs to a shallow bowl and season with salt and pepper. Do the same with the flour in a second bowl, then whisk the egg into the third bowl, also seasoning generously with salt and pepper. Add ⅔ of the curry powder to the flour and the remaining ⅓ to the panko along with the sesame seeds.

Add the chicken to the flour and coat on both sides. Shake off the excess and dip in the egg coating well, letting the excess drip off. Finally, toss in the panko making sure all of the gaps are covered.
Add the chicken to the air fryer and heat to 200°C, cooking for 8-12 min, or until the juices run clear.
Meanwhile, grate garlic into a bowl adding the mayo and a big squeeze of lemon juice. Season well with salt.

Using a mandoline or a sharp knife, finely slice the cabbage. Finely chop the chives. Mix the cabbage and pickled ginger with a nice slosh of the pickled ginger juice. Mix through the chives and season with salt and pepper.
Serve the schnitzels up with the slaw and a nice dollop of mayo.

name: Curried Squash & Chickpea Puff Pie
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Curried chickpeas and butternut folded into rice and baked with puff pastry on top – this hearty dish is comfort in one pan. Treasure it.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Peel and halve the butternut squash. Scoop out the seeds and discard. Dice the butternut squash into 3cm cubes. Drain the chickpeas and combine with the squash in a bowl.
Toss with a few glugs of olive oil, season with salt and add 1 tbsp of curry powder. Chuck in the oven for 25 mins until the chickpeas are crispy and the squash is tender.
Meanwhile, dice the onion, garlic, chilli and ginger. Preheat a large sauté pan over a medium-high heat. Sweat off the veggies in a dash olive oil with a pinch of salt for 5 mins.
Add the remaining curry powder and cook for 1 min before adding the tomato purée. Cook for another 5 mins. Add the coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add the squash and chickpeas and stir through the rice. Roughly chop the coriander and fold through the mix. Allow to cool.
Top with the pastry, brush with oat milk and bake for 25-30 mins until puffed and golden.
Allow to cool for 10 mins and serve.

name: Curried Squash & Lentil Traybake
description: An autumnal one-tray wonder with chunky butternut squash and a gently spiced coconut curry sauce. It’s plant-based, nourishing and really easy to make – just whack it in a tray and let the oven do the work.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.

Wash the squash well. Cut the top and tail off, scoop out and discard the seeds and then cut 1-2cm slices. Drain the lentils, cut the onions into wedges and pick the coriander leaves. Thinly slice the chilli.

Add the curry paste, coconut milk and boiling water to a large baking dish and mix well. Add the lentils, onions, squash pieces and plenty of salt and pepper. Drizzle over some olive oil and slide into the oven for 25-30 mins or until the squash is cooked through.
Divide the squash and coconut curry between bowls and top with the coconut yoghurt, flaked toasted almonds, sliced chillies and fresh coriander before serving.

name: Curried Squash Soup
description: The flavours of a mild curry blended up in soup form. Introducing Mob's Curried Squash Soup. Topped with chilli cheese croutons, she's a proper winter warmer.
instructions: Finely slice your onions. Finely chop your garlic and ginger.
Peel and chop your squash into 3cm chunks.

Add a good glug of vegetable oil to your sauté pan. Add your onions and squash and cook for 15 mins over
a medium heat, until they are fully softened and have just begun to caramelise. Add your garlic
and ginger, then cook for 2 mins.

Tip in your bay leaf, chilli powder and garam masala, then add your tinned tomatoes and stock.
Bring to a gentle simmer and simmer for 25 mins.
Heat your oven to 200°C.

Cut your bread into 1 inch cubes. Add these to a baking dish with a drizzle of olive oil, then bake
for 9 mins.
Finely chop your green chillies and grate your cheddar.

Sprinkle your cheddar over your croutons along with your green chillies. Return to the oven for 3
mins until melted.
Pour your soup into a blender, then blitz until you have a smooth consistency.
Pour the soup back into the pan, then pour in your cream. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Spoon your soup into bowls. Top with an extra drizzle of cream, your croutons and a little
sprinkle of curry powder. Enjoy!

name: Curry Butter BBQ Chicken
description: Delicious homemade curry butter slathered onto spatchcocked chicken and cooked on the bbq for the best smokey, juicy results.
instructions: Kick things off by spatchcocking your chicken. Flip the chicken so it's breast-side down on the surface. Use a pair of strong kitchen scissors to remove the backbone by cutting up each side. Turn the chicken over and gently press down on the breastbone until you hear a light crack. Turn the legs out so the chicken lies flat.
Season the chicken generously with salt and pop into the fridge for 30 mins.
To make the curry butter, finely grate the garlic and ginger and tip into a food processor. Add the zest and juice of the orange. Set aside.

Pour 2 tbsp of olive oil into a small frying pan and pop over a low heat. Once warm, tip in the curry powder, chilli powder and ground coriander. Swirl into the oil and allow to bloom for 1 min, then remove from the heat. Once cooled, tip the spiced oil into the same food processor. Add the butter to the processor and blitz with the other ingredients until you’ve got a deep orange butter. Have a taste and season with salt and pepper.

Pull the chicken out of the fridge and use your fingers to separate the skin from the flesh. Stuff the spiced butter underneath the skin, saving a few tbsp. Rub the remaining butter on top of the skin and pop back in the fridge for 1 hr or overnight. Pull out of the fridge 1 hr before cooking.

Set up the Ninja Grill to the grill setting. Once ready, add your chicken, skin-side down, and grill for 8 mins until charred and gnarly. Pull out the chicken and switch to the roast setting. Return the chicken, skin-side up, for 20 mins with the thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the breast and cook until the temperature reaches 69°C. Rest for 30 mins to finish cooking.

Meanwhile, for the salad, chunk up the cucumber, thinly slice the onion and coarsely grate the carrot. Toss into a bowl with the picked mint leaves, plenty of salt and pepper, the nigella seeds and the zest and juice of 1 lemon. Toss together.
Carve the chicken with any resting juices on a big platter with the salad. Garnish with extra lemon wedges. Serve with cooling yoghurt and naan, cooked on the grill.

name: Curry Butter Cheesy Crumpets
description: Your favourite way to eat crumpets — lathered in butter and cheese — just got an upgrade. We're talking zesty curry butter, pickled onions and fresh chilli.
instructions: Make sure the butter is fully softened then grate the garlic and zest the lime. Heat oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Fry off the curry paste in some oil along with the garlic for 2 mins, then take off the heat and cool. Mix with the butter, lime zest (and a pinch of salt if using unsalted butter).
Finely slice the red onion and put into a bowl with the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Give it a little massage to soften up, and set aside.

Finely chop the chilli. Heat a grill to medium-high and slice the cheddar — don't be tempted to grate it! The cheese will split when it's mixed with the melted butter (trust us, we've tried it). Toast crumpets then pop onto a baking tray, spreading with the butter and topping with cheddar and Parmesan, if using. Slide under the grill and cook until bubbly and golden. Bring them out and top with the pickled onions, chilli and nigella seeds.
Pop any leftover butter into an airtight container and put in the fridge.

name: Curry Butter Kyiv
description: This isn't your mama's chicken kyiv. It's a solution for when you've got half a jar of spice paste in the fridge. You can use whatever you want in this one.
instructions: Heat a little oil in a frying pan and fry the curry paste off until thickened, then grate in the garlic, cook for 1 min. Then set aside to cool.
When the spice mix is cool, mix with softened butter and lemon zest and scoop into a piping bag.
Make an incision in the chicken breast with a sharp knife. Then get your flour, egg and breadcrumbs into 3 separate bowls.
Fill the chicken with the butter and press down to seal the opening. Pass the chicken through the flour, egg and breadcrumbs until nicely coated, then repeat. Put in the fridge for 30 mins.

Heat oven to 170°C. Cover the base of a large frying pan with a 1cm layer of olive oil. Set over a medium heat and cook the kyivs for 3 mins on each side until golden brown. Transfer to a tray and pop in the oven for 10-12 mins until cooked through.
Serve up with the kyiv with a salad and rice, enjoy!

name: Curry Cauliflower Cheese
description: Loading up cauli cheese with ginger, garlic and cumin seeds is a game-changer. Spicy and soothing, this is a mind-blowingly tasty dish using Ocado ingredients.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C.
Chop your cauliflower into large florets and roughly chop the leaves and stems.
Bring a pan of salted water to a boil. Add your cauliflower florets and leaves, then cook for 4 mins until just tender.
Add your butter to a large saucepan and add your cumin seeds. Fry for a minute until fragrant.
Add in your tomato purée and cook for 3 mins until the colour has darkened.
Spoon in your ginger and garlic paste, then cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add in your chilli powder and turmeric, then cook out for a further 2 mins.
Add your flour, then mix to a paste and cook for another 2 mins. Gradually pour in your milk in small increments, whisking constantly so you have a smooth paste before pouring in more.
Once all your milk has been added, bring your mixture to a boil and let it simmer for 2 mins until thickened.
Remove your sauce from the heat. Add your cheddar and stir until is has totally melted. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Tip your cauliflower into a baking dish and pour over your cheese sauce. Bake for 25 mins until golden and bubbly.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Curry Chicken & Rice Traybake With Mango Yoghurt
description: Curried chicken, buttery rice and mango chut-infused yoghurt. Need we say more?
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Halve and finely slice the onion, finely chop the coriander stems, then grate the garlic and ginger. Heat oil in a small frying pan and add the onions, cook for about 10 min until taking on a bit of colour, then add the coriander stems, ginger and garlic.

Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then add to a deep casserole dish or tray (around 20x30cm) along with the fried onions. Pour in the chicken stock, cherry tomatoes and diced butter, then season with salt and pepper before mixing well.

Slash the skin of the chicken. Mix the curry paste with 2 tbsp oil and rub all over the chicken thighs, getting right into the cuts and season with salt and pepper. Pop the chicken on top of the rice and cover with tin foil. Bake for 30 mins.
After 30 mins, uncover the rice and put back in the oven for 15 mins, until the chicken skin is nice and crispy. Whilst you’re waiting, mix the mango chutney and yoghurt.
Finely slice the chilli. Take the tray out of the oven and scatter with coriander leaves, chilli and mango yoghurt. Serve with citrus wedges.

name: Curry Fried Chicken
description: We had Melissa Thompson make her Curry Fried Chicken from her new book Motherland and it was all the things we love. Big flavours. Incredible textures.
instructions: Mix all the spices together and store in an airtight container for up to 3 months.
Shake before use, remove as much as you need, then grind it to a powder. Keeping the spices whole will help it to remain fresh and aromatic.

Cut each thigh into 2-3 pieces, each about 4cm big. Put the pieces in a bowl with the curry powder and mix well. Add the garlic, ginger, thyme, salt and a pinch of pepper and mix well, then add the coconut milk and mix to coat completely. Cover and marinate for at least 4 hours in the fridge, but ideally overnight.

To make the coating, mix the flour, cornmeal, salt and spices in a bowl. remove the chicken from the marinade, scraping off any big bits but otherwise leaving everything where it is, and place in the flour mix.
Turn the pieces over and press down, ensuring every nook and cranny is exposed to the flour. Remove and rest on a plate for at least 5 minutes, giving the starch enough time to adhere the chicken.
Mix together all the ingredients for the mayo in a small bowl.

Set up a wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper. Following all the usual precautions for deep-frying, pour enough oil into a saucepan to lie at least 10cm deep. Heat it to about 140°C. If you don't have a thermometer, a sprinkling of flour should sizzle gently a few seconds after being dropped into it.

Place a few pieces of chicken into the oil, making sure you don't crowd them. Fry for 3-4 minutes, until they start to colour, then remove with a slotted spoon to the wire rack. Continue until every piece has had its first fry.
Now increase the oil temperate to 180°C or until a pinch of flour sizzles almost immediately on contact with the oil.

Add the chicken pieces, starting with those that went first into the oil before. Fry for a further 2 minutes or until they have turned a deeper golden brown and are crisp. Remove and drain on the rack, continuing until all pieces have been fried twice.
Fry the scotch bonnet rings for a minute or so, then drain on the rack.
Serve the chicken with a sprinkling of fried chilli on top and the chilli and lime mayo for dipping.

name: Curry Leaf & Lentil Fried Rice
description: Inspired by Mujaddara, this rice dish is made even more substantial than your regular fried rice because of the lentils. I’ve played around with the flavours to make a fragrant, warming curry leaf rice perfect for a weeknight or meal prepped lunch.
keywords: Curry Leaf & Lentil Fried Rice recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the chillies and trim the green beans, cutting them into 1cm chunks. Bash and mince the ginger. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems, keeping them separate.

Place a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a glug of olive oil. Once hot, add the ginger, most of the chillies, coriander stems, crispy onions and curry leaves. Cook, stirring, for 2-3 mins until the curry leaves stop splattering.

Stir in the peas and green beans and cook for 3-4 mins, until the peas have defrosted and the beans are starting to soften. Toss in the rice and lentils along with the soy sauce and stir-fry until everything's heated through. Season with black pepper and more soy if needed.
Share between plates or boxes, top with a dollop of yoghurt and scatter over the coriander leaves and the remaining sliced red chilli.

name: Curry Leaf Hummus
description: Once you've livened up the olive oil base of your hummus with aromatic curry leaves, garlic, and spices, you'll never look back. Sexy and smooth. Sophie x
instructions: Peel and finely slice your garlic.

Pour about 100ml of olive oil into a frying pan and add your garlic. Gently bring up to a medium heat, stirring until your garlic is golden around the edges and starting to crisp up. Remove the garlic from the pan with a slotted spoon and drain on a plate lined with paper towel.
Add your cumin seeds, black mustard seeds and curry leaves to the same pan and fry for 2 minutes until they start to pop and go fragrant.
Pour your curry leaf mixture through a metal sieve set over a bowl to separate your oil. Pour your curry leaves and spices onto the plate with your garlic and leave to crisp up. Let your oil cool.
Once your oil has cooled, you can make your hummus. Pour your drained chickpeas into a food processor along with 1 tbsp of the liquid from the can. Add your tahini, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Run your food processor and gradually pour in your cooled down oil. Season to taste with salt, and add more lemon juice and olive oil if needed.
Pour into a bowl and smooth out with a spoon. Top with your crispy garlic, curry leaves and spices and another drizzle of olive oil. Serve as part of a mezze spread, with crudité or just on toast.

name: Curry Leaf Swirly Omelette
description: Golden, turmeric-spiked eggs swirled with crispy curry leaves and flopped onto hot rice. Savoury, speedy, and seriously comforting.
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, season with salt and whisk the turmeric in. Set aside for a couple of minutes.
Reheat the rice.

Set a non-stick pan over medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Add in the curry leaves and leave until they stop crackling. Pour the eggs in and leave to set for 15 secs before giving it a scramble. Once the egg starts to set, leave it alone until its cooked through, then remove from the heat.
Slide the omelette onto the rice, serve with a blob of ketchup and splash the soy sauce over the top. Dig in.

name: Curry Mustard Sausage & Coriander Lentils
description: A curry and honey mustard dip with a carottes râpées salad bulked out with puy lentils and juicy sausages. Just as good hot as it is cold, so lunch is sorted.
keywords: Curry Mustard Sausage & Coriander Lentils recipe
instructions: Add all the dip ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth. Season with salt and set aside.

Roughly chop the coriander and coarsely grate the carrots. Add the carrots into a bowl with the lentils, mustard and half the olive oil, then season with the juice of the lemon, salt, pepper and an extra touch of honey to taste, if needed.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat with the remaining oil. Once hot, cook the sausages for 10-15 mins, until cooked through and golden.
Share the dip between bowls. Toss the coriander through the lentils and spoon on top, then finish with the sausages. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Curry Oil Squash & Chickpeas With Lime Yoghurt
description: If you're a fan of butternut squash then you're going to go crazy for this one. Caramelised squash and crispy chickpeas? Check.
keywords: Curry Oil Squash & Chickpeas With Lime Yoghurt
Curry Oil Squash & Chickpeas With Lime Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the squash in half lengthways, trip the top and bottom, then cut into wedges lengthways. Use a spoon to scoop out the seeds. Tip the wedges onto a roasting tray.

Drain the chickpeas and then tip onto the same tray as the squash. Drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Scatter with the garam masala and toss well. Slide into the oven and cook for 30-40 mins, until the squash is soft and the chickpeas are crisp.

Meanwhile, peel and slice the garlic. Add 60ml of olive oil to a small frying pan over a medium heat. Add the curry powder and sliced garlic and cook for 2-3 mins until the garlic is softened. Make the lime yoghurt by adding the yoghurt to a bowl with juice of half of the lime. Season well, add a splash of water to loosen to drizzle-able consistency.

Pile the squash and chickpeas on a platter. Top with spoonfuls of the lime yoghurt. Drizzle with the garlic curry oil and finish with a scattering of coriander and chilli flakes. Serve with the remaining lime half on the side. Serve with naan bread on the side to swoop through the oil-y yoghurt at the end!

name: Curry Paste Yoghurt Dip
description: 'Twas once a time we would never have thought to combine a serving of leftover curry paste with our favourite yog to make a sensational dip. Get involved.
instructions: Drain the chickpeas, saving the liquid, and add to a processor along with grated garlic, lemon or lime juice, yogurt and curry paste. Blitz until smooth, then add some reserved chickpea water to loosen.

Finely chop the chilli, julienne the ginger and finely slice the shallot. Heat 3 tbsp of olive oil in a pan over a medium heat, and fry the curry leaves, chilli, ginger and shallot until crispy, around 5 mins, then drain off on kitchen paper.
Spread the chickpeas in a bowl and top with the crispy bits. Enjoy.

name: Curry Roasted Carrots and Parsnips with Chilli Yoghurt
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad 

Roasted roots to welcome in the new season, can't beat 'em! We got all the ingredients from Aldi for under a fiver per person. Bargain.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Cut your carrots and parsnips in half vertically.
Pop your veg in a large baking tray. Drizzle with your curry powder, olive oil and a pinch of salt, then roast for 45 mins, tossing every so often so that they cook evenly.
Roughly chop your mint and one of your green chillies. Finely slice your other chilli.
Add your yoghurt to a bowl along with your chopped mint, chopped chillies and lemon zest. Mix until totally combined, then season to taste with salt.
When 45 mins are up, get your veg out the oven and drizzle over your honey. Give the tray a toss, then pop it back in the oven for 15 mins.
Once your carrots and parsnips are cooked, toss your quinoa pouche into the tray. Toss to coat.

Swoosh your green yoghurt around your serving plate. Place your carrot mixture on top. Drizzle with your pomegranate seeds and finely sliced chillies. Finish with a little drizzle of olive oil, then serve with a wedge of lemon.

name: Cypriot Garlicky Aubergine Stew (Melinzana Yiahni)
description: This stew is rich, garlicky and comforting. Serve with garlic rice for a cosy winter meal.
instructions: First, sweat the aubergines. Cut them in half lengthwise, then slice them into 1cm half moons. Place them into a large colander and sprinkle with 6 tbsp of salt (don’t worry about the heavy salt, you will wash this off after). Toss well to make sure that every piece is covered. Set the colander over a bowl and set aside for at least 30 mins.
Once the 30 mins are up, rinse the aubergine slices quickly under running water to remove the excess salt and then pat them dry.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the onions and garlic.

In a large frying pan or pot with a lid, add 3 tbsp of olive oil and set over medium heat. Fry the onions with a sprinkle of salt for 5 mins, until translucent. Add the garlic and fry for a further two minutes, stirring often to make sure they don’t catch.
Add the aubergine to the pan and cook for 6-8 mins, stirring often. Add more olive oil or a splash of water if the pan is looking dry.

Once the aubergines have started to brown and soften, add the red wine and turn up the heat. Stir until the wine has completely evaporated. Then add the tomato puree, tinned tomatoes, bay leaf and sugar. Fill the empty tin with water and pour it into the pan. Put the lid on and let it simmer away for 30 mins. Drain the chickpeas and add them to the pot and cook for another 5-10 mins. Stir, season and check that the aubergine is fully cooked through. If they need more time, add a little more water and cook for a little longer until they are soft and fully cooked.
The stew should have a rich, thick sauce. Drizzle plenty of olive oil over the top and taste for seasonings.

Chop the parsley and sprinkle generously over the top.
 Serve with garlic rice or over pasta.

name: Dad's Puttanesca
description:
Dad's Puttanesca recipe is a simple yet delicious dish inspired by the flavours of sugo alla puttanesca. This classic Neapolitan recipe is a staple in the Mediterranean diet, featuring a savoury mix of anchovies, garlic, olives, and capers in a tomato-based sauce. Unlike bolognese sauce, it relies on pantry ingredients, making it perfect for quick pasta dishes.

Ideal for lovers of Italian food, this sauced dish pairs beautifully with common pasta like spaghetti or fresh pasta. To enhance the flavours, sauté the garlic and anchovies until fragrant, then mix in the tomatoes. Sprinkle some fresh parsley on top for an authentic Italian touch.

While it’s a tomato sauce, it contains less trans fat than creamy options like carbonara. To add a Mediterranean twist, pair it with a niçoise salad or even pita bread. Low in saturated fat and rich in seasoning, it's a great option for balanced meals.
instructions: Add your chopped anchovies and chilli flakes into a frying pan with a tablespoon of olive oil and a tbsp of oil from the anchovy tin. Fry for one minute.
Crush your garlic cloves and add with a large handful of finely chopped parsley stalks. Mix everything together.
Add your capers, your olives and pour in the plum tomatoes. Break the tomatoes up with a wooden spoon. Refill both the tins halfway with water and add to the sauce.
Get your pasta on.

Allow the sauce to reduce. Add a couple of tablespoons of your starchy pasta water to make it nice and glossy. Just when you are removing the pasta from the heat, season the sauce with salt and pepper and add a large handful of chopped parsley.

Drain the pasta and pour it into the saucepan with the puttanesca sauce. Mix everything together and remove from the heat. Serve with some parsley leaves scattered on top and a good glug of olive oil. Enjoy!

name: Dal Curry & Egg
description: Dal is one of our favourite comforting dishes. Here, we’ve taken inspiration from some of the flavours found in Seychellois curries. It's creamy. coconutty, umami, and warming.
instructions: Trim and bash the lemongrass, finely grate the ginger and garlic. Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear.

Place a saucepan on a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the lemongrass, ginger and garlic, fry until fragrant. Stir through the tomato purée and curry powder, cook until dark red, 2-3 mins. Pour the rice vinegar and soy sauce and let it evaporate before pouring the coconut milk, water, and red split lentils.

Bring the mixture to a boil, then decrease the heat to medium and let simmer until the lentils are cooked and the mixture has thickened, 25-30 mins. Add a splash of water into the saucepan if it’s getting too thick.
Meanwhile, finely slice the chilli and spring onions. Bring a saucepan of water to the boil, and crack the eggs into a container.
Once the water is boiling, reduce to a low simmer. Gently add the eggs into the water and poach until your desired consistency.
Share the dal between bowls, top with the poached egg, sliced chilli and spring onion. Enjoy with bread.

name: Dal Curry with Beetroot Sambal
description: A simple dal curry served on a bed of rice with fiery beetroot sambal. This is a picture-perfect weeknight dinner.
keywords: Dal Curry with Beetroot Sambal recipe
instructions: Make the Coconut Dal batch recipe.
Toast your desiccated coconut in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2 mins, then tip it into a bowl.
Pop a box grater over the same bowl, and grate in the beetroot. Squeeze in the juice of a lime, then give it a really good mix. Season with salt to taste.
Heat your rice following packet instructions, then spoon it into bowls. Top it with your dal and beetroot sambal, and some extra coriander leaves if you like. Serve.

name: Dal on Toast with Crispy-Fried Egg
description: You can't go wrong with a slice of toast. We've subbed out butter for a rich and warming dal curry.
instructions: Make the Coconut Dal batch recipe.
Thinly slice your onions then add to a bowl. Squeeze over the lime juice, mix to combine and set aside to quick pickle until you're ready to serve.

For the eggs, heat a frying pan over a high heat and add a generous glug of vegetable oil. Once the oil is hot, crack in your eggs season them with salt, then let them bubble and crackle. Spoon the hot oil over the whites to cook them.
Toast your bread in the toaster or under a grill.
Top each slice of toast with the dal, then pop a fried egg on top. Garnish with the pickled red onions and coriander leaves.

name: Dalgona Coffee
description: This sweet and delicious coffee drink orignates from Macau and became a global sensation during lockdown. Try out this Dalgona coffee recipe today.
instructions: Simply put all the ingredients into a blender and blend it up until soft and foamy.
Spoon into a glass and dust with cocoa powder.
Enjoy.

name: Danny’s Kimchi
description: Want to start making your own fermented foods but not sure where to start? Let us show you how to make kimchi, a delicious pickled cabbage that will flavour and probiotics to your meals.
instructions: Cut the cabbage into quarters lengthways and sprinkle generously with salt between the leaves. Set aside.
Roughly chop the spring onions, apple, radishes, carrot, chives and set aside.
To a blender, add the onion, garlic, ginger, gochugaru flakes, fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar and water and blitz to a paste.
Rinse the salt off the cabbage and get it in a mixing bowl, along with the spring onions, apples, radishes, carrots and chives. Pour over the blended paste and massage it into the veggies.
Put your cabbage mix in a sterilised jar and push down to compress the cabbage slightly.
Let the jar sit at room temperature for 2-5 days until it’s fermented to your liking. When you’re happy with the taste, get it in the fridge where it will last up to 3 months.

name: Dark Chocolate & Almond Croissant Pud
description: Charlotte from Pret makes her indulgent chocolate pudding using their crisp chocolate croissants and crunchy almond granola.
ingredients: 30g Pret Dark Choc & Almond Granola (to serve)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/360°F.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper and bake the Pret croissants according to package directions, keep the oven on for later. Once cool, slice them in half.
Roughly chop your almonds and dark chocolate.
Arrange the halved croissants into a greased dish. Sprinkle over 50g of chopped chocolate before drizzling the lot with almond butter and topping with your chopped almonds.

Place the milk, double cream, remaining chocolate, and sugar into a heatproof bowl set over a pan of simmering water and heat, stirring occasionally, until the chocolate has melted and the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat.
Separate your egg whites and yolks. Whisk the egg yolks with the vanilla extract in a large jug or bowl before slowly adding your milk mixture, whisking continuously as you go.
Pour the mixture over the halved croissants, making sure every bit of croissant is covered. Leave to stand for 20 mins.
Place the dish in the oven and bake for 25-30 mins, or until puffed and set on top.

Sprinkle the top of your pud with a handful of Pret's Dark Choc & Almond Granola before finishing the whole thing off with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and a dusting of icing sugar. Serve hot and enjoy

name: Dark Chocolate & Pistachio Meringues
description: Rich cocoa meringues dipped in dark chocolate and chopped pistachios. An incredible base for a dessert.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 120°C. Line a baking tray with baking parchment. Separate the eggs whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise).

In a bowl, use an electric whisk to whip the egg whites with the juice of the lemon and a pinch of salt for about 2 mins until soft peaks form. Slowly beat in the sugar, 2 tbsp at a time, and continue until thick and glossy and stiff peaks are forming (when you hold the whisk up, the mixture should stand in a firm peak). Sieve the cocoa powder then fold it into the meringue mix, using a metal spoon or spatula.
Using a metal dessert spoon (or a piping bag with the 1M nozzle / 1.5cm open star nozzle attached), transfer neat tablespoon-sized dollops of meringue onto your baking tray.
Bake for 1 hour, or until set, then turn off the oven and leave the meringues inside to dry for another hour with the oven door closed.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the pistachios, or grind them with a pestle and mortar until fine but not powdery.
When the meringues are cool, break the chocolate into pieces. Add to a heat proof mixing bowl and set over a pot of gently boiling water (a bain marie). Stir until melted.

Very carefully, dip the base of each meringue first in the chocolate, then in the crushed pistachio. Alternatively, use a teaspoon to zig-zag chocolate across the top of each meringue and dust with pistachio.

name: Dark Chocolate Chunk Cookies
description: Everyone needs a classic chocolate chip cookie recipe. We like them slightly crispy on the outside with a soft, chewy centre. Good chocolate makes a difference.
instructions: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, combine the butter, dark muscovado sugar, granulated sugar, and salt. Beat on medium-high speed until the mixture is light and fluffy, about 3 mins, pausing to scrape down the sides as needed.
Add the egg and beat until it has been fully incorporated, scraping down the sides to make sure all the butter is also incorporated.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, cornstarch, baking soda, and baking powder.
Place a sieve over the stand mixer bowl and sift the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients. Mix on low speed just until the flour has been incorporated.
Add the chopped dark chocolate and mix again to incorporate.
Roll the dough into 65g balls in your hand and place them on a baking tray. Cover with cling film and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 170°C fan.
Working in batches, place 6 dough balls on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Press a few more bits of chopped dark chocolate into the top of the balls.
Place the tray in the oven and bake for 12 to 14 mins or until lightly golden.

Remove the tray from the oven and while still hot, take a cookie cutter slightly larger than the baked cookie and quickly rotate it around the cookie. This neatens up the edges and gives you a perfectly round cookie.
Allow the cookies to cool on the tray for 5 mins before transferring them to a cooling rack to completely cool.

name: Dark Soy Chicken & Mushroom Pot Rice
description: A rich and umami dish that's got layers and layers of flavour. Rice doesn't get better than this.
keywords: Dark Soy Chicken & Mushroom Pot Rice
Dark Soy Chicken & Mushroom Pot Rice recipe
instructions: Fill a large bowl with cold tap water, then add the shiitake mushrooms. Leave to soak.

Use scissors to cut the chicken into thumb-sized chunks. Transfer to a medium-sized mixing bowl. Drain the mushrooms and discard the stems. Cut the tops into similar thumb-sized pieces then add them into the mixing bowl. Finely grate the ginger and add to the chicken, along with all the other marinade ingredients. Mix well and set aside.
Put the rice in a sieve and use your fingers to rinse all the grains under cold tap water. Shake the sieve to release all the starch, then set aside in the sieve to drain.

For the rice: Cut the spring onion whites into small chunks (reserve the green tops for later). Mince the garlic and ginger. Add the spring onion whites, garlic, and ginger into a large deep lidded frying pan with a drizzle of oil. Cook for 1 min over a low heat, or until lightly golden. Add the rice, mix well, and cook for another minute. Add the water, sugar and salt, then mix everything very well. Bring up to the boil, then pop the lid on, turn the heat down to low-medium and cook for 5 mins.
Pour all the marinated chicken and mushrooms on top of the rice (don’t mix it) then pop the lild back on. Turn the heat down to low and cook for 30 mins.

Turn the heat off, but keep the lid on for 10 mins to finish cooking. To serve, drizzle over some sesame oil and scatter over the finely sliced spring onion green tops and toasted sesame seeds. Use a rice paddle or spatula to reveal the rice beneath the sauce, then gently mix before serving. Eat with any steamed greens on the side, if you like.

name: Date Bark
description: This sweet and chewy date bark is the perfect healthy snack. Everyone is going to want some.
instructions: Line a small baking sheet with parchment paper. Split dates open and press each one, sticky side down onto the sheet making sure they overlap and stick together. Cover the top with more parchment paper and press firmly until you have a homogenous rectangle of dates. Flip them over so they are sticky side up and remove the top layer of parchment.
Drizzle peanut butter over the top and spread evenly. You can pop the peanut butter in the microwave for 20 seconds to loosen, if needed.
Chop up the peanuts and sprinkle them over the top of the peanut butter.
Melt the chocolate in the microwave with the coconut oil in 30-second bursts, stirring between each go until smooth and spread over the top.
Pop in the freezer for 15-20 minutes and portion. Finish with a sprinkling of flakey salt if you fancy.
Store in the fridge or freezer.

name: Date Night Marinated Tofu Steak
description: A sweet and tangy vegan tofu recipe that's perfect for a date night in the flat. It's a plant-based banger.
instructions: Slice your block of tofu into two evenly-sized slices. Mince your garlic.
Mix all ingredients (apart from the tofu) together to make a marinade.
Lightly score each side of the tofu slices (this will help them soak up more flavour) then pour over about two-thirds of the marinade. Set aside to marinate for at least 30 mins.

Once the tofu slices are marinated, heat up a tbsp of olive oil in a hot pan. Once the pan is hot, add your slices and cook for 4-5 mins, flipping halfway through and basting with the extra marinade as you go, until they're looking crisp on the outside. If your tofu looks like it's starting to stick or burn, add a splash of water to deglaze the pan.
When you remove the tofu, pour the sauce over each slice and spread the glaze evenly.
Serve over rice topped with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.

name: Dates With Caramelised Onions & Honey Mascarpone
description: Dates. Caramelised onions. Honey mascarpone. A bundle of flavours that, when brought together, make something delicious. The perfect recipe for Ramadan.
instructions: First, slice the onion thinly. Then, place a pan over a medium heat and add the ghee.
Immediately add ½ tbsp of honey to the ghee. I used a light flowery one for this.

Add the onions and lower the heat. You're not sautéing the onions! You want them to cook slowly for them to caramelise. If it looks like they're getting crisp, pour some water on the onions — this helps soften them.
Once slightly browned and soft, add the remaining honey.
When a jammy texture is achieved, remove from the heat. Taste and adjust sweetness accordingly. Set aside to cool. While the onions are cooling, slice and pit the dates.
Once pitted, add a smear of mascarpone to one half of the inside of the date. Scoop some onions and fill in the other half.
Serve immediately and enjoy! This can be stored in the fridge for about 3-4 days.

name: Deconstructed BLT Salad
description: All the elements you love in a BLT in salad form. Crispy bacon. Delicious slices of tomato. Lovely crispy lettuce. Crunchy croutons and goat's cheese. Whammy.
instructions: Chop your bacon into small strips and fry until crispy. Remove the bacon from the frying pan and leave to rest, leaving the fat in the pan.
Tear your ciabatta loaf into chunks and fry in the bacon fat with rosemary. Grate the garlic (or mince it) and add it to your lovely, browning croutons. Once finished, set aside.

Slice your vine tomatoes into discs and your cherry tomatoes in half. Place the tomatoes into a colander. Cover your tomatoes in salt and leave them for about 15 minutes. This will ensure that the moisture is drawn out.

Dressing time. Into a jar pour 5 tbsp of olive oil and your balsamic vinegar, oregano, chilli flakes, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cover your jar with a lid and shake the ingredients together until they are well combined.

Roughly chop your basil (saving some for garnish) and lettuce. Add into a large bowl along with your tomatoes, croutons, bacon pieces. Then, pour over your dressing and toss everything together using salad servers. Break your goat’s cheese into chunks and top your salad with it along with a drizzle of the dressing and some more fresh basil. Enjoy!

name: Deconstructed Salami Pizza
description: All the delicious flavours of a pizza but without the hassle. The crunchy ciabatta croutons are sublime.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F
Put tomatoes into a baking tray. Tear up your ciabatta into bitesize chunks and put in the tray.
Into a jar, put 3 tbsp of olive oil, your balsamic vinegar and cloves of garlic (crushed or finely chopped). Shake it, and then pour over the bread and tomatoes.
Add salt, pepper and crushed chillies, and put the tray in the oven for 45 minutes.
After 45 minutes, remove the tray. Mix everything around, coating the crispy bits in the juices. Add salami, and then place tray back in oven for 10 more minutes.
Dressing time. Take your basil. Chop it all up, finely, and put into a jar. Add a tbsp and a half of olive oil and shake it all together.
Take the tray out the oven, and tear your mozzarella on top. Drizzle your dressing over everything, and sprinkle over some crushed chillies, salt and pepper. Enjoy!

name: Deep Fried Apple Pies
description: A simpler, fresher and – dare we say it – better version of your favourite apple pie.
instructions: Peel and core the apples. Chop up the apples into small 2cm cubes.
Mix the apples with brown sugar, cornflour, cinnamon and ½ tsp salt.
Put the apples in a small pan with the water and cook for 10 mins until the apples have slightly softened and the sauce has thickened.
Transfer to a plate or a baking dish and spread out thinly to cool down completely.
Roll out the shortcrust pastry until it’s roughly half the thickness and cut it into 10 small rectangles to make 5 pies.
Add a tbsp of the apple filling to the centre and brush the edges with egg wash.
Add another piece of pastry on top and close the seam with a fork. Trim the edges and pop the pies on a baking sheet.
Freeze the pies for 30 mins.
Get a big pot of oil ready for frying. Heat the oil to a medium-high temperature (roughly 180°C).
Once the oil is hot, deep fry the pies for 5 mins or until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on a paper towel and enjoy piping hot.

name: Deep-Fried Courgette Tacos
description: A wonderful vegetarian taco recipe with homemade salsa macha and watermelon hot sauce. This one screams summer.
instructions: For the pickled onions, very thinly slice the onions and transfer to a small bowl. Cover with boiling water and leave for 1 min. Drain the onions well, add a pinch of salt, squeeze in the lime juice and stir well.

For the salsa, split the dried chillies open, remove the seeds and cut the stalks off. Heat a dry frying pan over a medium heat, add the dried chillies and toast for 1-2 mins each side until fragrant and slightly puffed – take care not to burn them. Remove from the pan and leave to cool.
In the same pan, toast the peanuts, sesame seeds and pumpkin seeds over a medium heat for 2-3 mins, until they become golden brown and fragrant. Remove from the pan and set aside to cool.
Put the toasted chillies, peanuts, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, cumin, oregano, chipotle flakes and a pinch of salt in a blender or pestle and mortar. Pulse or crush to form a coarse paste.

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the paste, grate in the garlic and cook, stirring, for 1 min until fragrant. Remove the pan from the heat and leave the paste to cool (it will thicken as it cools).

For the watermelon hot sauce, remove the seeds and stems from the Scotch bonnet, then roughly chop. Roughly chop the tomatoes, garlic and shallots, too. Put all of the ingredients apart from the watermelon into a non-reactive saucepan. Bring the liquid to a rapid simmer and cook for 3-5 mins to soften and combine. Remove from the heat.

Chop the watermelon into cubes. Using a hand-held stick blender, blitz the watermelon cubes into the Scotch bonnet mixture and keep blitzing until the sauce is completely smooth. Transfer to a small bowl (the sauce will keep well in the fridge for up to four days).

For the courgettes, very thinly slice the courgettes into rounds. Fill a small, deep saucepan one-third full with oil and place it over a medium heat. Heat the oil until a slice of courgette dropped in sizzles and floats to the surface immediately (or the oil temperature reads 180°C on a digital cooking thermometer).

In small batches, taking care not to overcrowd the pan, fry the courgette slices for 2-3 mins per batch, until they are just golden. Remove each batch using a slotted spoon and set aside on a plate lined with kitchen paper to drain any excess oil while you fry the remainder.
Squeeze the lime juice over the cooked courgettes and scatter with flaky salt to serve.
Slice the avocado and chop the coriander. Serve the tacos with sliced avocado, a big handful of coriander and some lime wedges for squeezing over.

name: Deep-Fried Hellim Böreği (Halloumi-filled Pastries)
description: What do you get when you mix halloumi with pastry? Something really delicious, that's what.
instructions: For the filling, peel and finely dice the onion. Pour the olive oil into a pan and set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the onion, stir, reduce the heat a little and soften for 12-15 mins until fully translucent and starting to colour.
Meanwhile, whisk the egg in a separate bowl and set aside. Grate the halloumi and finely chop the parsley. Transfer both to a bowl along with the dried mint and black pepper.
Once the onion is cooked, stir through the parsley, then remove the pan from the heat and set aside to cool fully.
Once the onion and parsley mixture has cooled, add them to the hellim mixture, then add the whisked egg to bind everything together. Allow to cool fully before using to fill the börek.

For the dough, sift the flour into a large bowl and stir through the salt. Make a well in the centre. Mix the warm water, vinegar and 3 tbsp olive oil in a heatproof jug and pour into the well. Give everything a good stir with a large spoon.

Use your hands to turn the dough out onto a clean work surface. Knead the dough for 5-6 mins until smooth, tuck the sides under to form a ball, then give it a gentle rub with the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil before returning the dough to the bowl and covering with a tea towel. Leave to rest for 30 mins.

Divide the dough into three equal-sized pieces and roll them into balls. Lightly flour the work surface, place one of the dough balls in front of you, and leave the other two to one side, covered with a damp tea towel to prevent them from drying out.

Start to roll out the dough ball, turning 45° each time you glide over with the rolling pin. Shape it into a large rectangular shape (around 50cm x 60cm). You don’t need to be too precise – it’s the thickness that matters the most.

Roll out the dough until it is extremely thin (around 1mm-2 mm), adding a dusting of flour when and where necessary. The dough should be sturdy enough that it doesn’t tear when the filling is added. It should also be floured enough to prevent it from sticking to the surface, but not so heavily floured that the parcels will burn in the pan. Repeat with the other two dough balls.

Prepare the börek by placing heaped tbsp of the chosen filling horizontally along the dough, approximately 8cm apart, starting 2cm up from the bottom and stopping halfway up the pastry, so that you can fold the unfilled dough over the other half.

Using a thin rolling pin, lift the dough up from the edge furthest away from you onto the rolling pin and lay it directly over the filled section of the pastry. Use the thinnest part of your hands to gently push down in between the filling portions to release any air that could get trapped in the pastry. Using a saucer or pastry cutter, cut around each mound of filling to create 6cm x 9cm parcels, ensuring that they’re as evenly shaped as possible.

For deep-fried saçta börek, pour enough oil into a large, deep frying pan so that it comes up to around 5cm deep, then heat the oil over a high heat to a temperature of 190°C. Test the oil by gently dropping in a small piece of dough. If it sizzles immediately, then the oil is hot enough to cook the börek.

Using a slotted spoon, carefully lower 3-4 börek into the hot oil and fry for 1-2 mins on each side (turning halfway through to ensure even cooking). Using the slotted spoon, remove the börek from the pan to a large plate lined with a couple of layers of kitchen paper, ensuring that you don’t place the börek on top of one another (so that they have space to drain off any excess oil).
Repeat until you have cooked all the börek and serve while hot and crispy.

name: Delica Pumpkin with White Beans, Radicchio & Rosemary Pangrattato
description: The sweet and nutty pumpkin is the star of the show here, served with bitter radicchio, creamy beans and garlicky breadcrumbs. This is the best kind of bowl food. If you can’t find Delica, then Onion squash (Red Kuri) or Crown Prince squash would work just as well.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.

Wash and dry the squash and scoop out and discard any seeds, then cut the squash into 6 wedges, each 3-4cm wide. Arrange on a small-medium baking sheet, so that they’re lying flat with plenty of space around them. Drizzle with a glug of rapeseed oil, then roast for a total of 40 mins, turning them after 25 mins, and again around 8 mins later. Season generously with salt.

Meanwhile, finely chop ⅘ of the rosemary (set aside the rest for later) and mince the garlic. Heat ½ the olive oil in a medium-sized frying pan set over a moderate heat. Fry the breadcrumbs and chopped rosemary for 6 mins or so, stirring frequently, until the crumbs begin to turn golden. Add ⅔ of the garlic and cook for 2 mins more, then remove from the heat and season with salt. Transfer to a bowl until required.

Using a small sauté or saucepan heat the beans, including cooking juices from the jar. Add the remaining garlic, double cream, the last sprig of rosemary and the parmesan rind (if you have one). Simmer gently for 5-10 mins. These beans should be nice and loose — add a splash of water if necessary.

Cut the radicchio into 3cm wide wedges. The last time you turn the squash, arrange the radicchio in the gaps between the squash wedges, carefully rolling them in the residual oil. Return the tray to the oven for the final 8 mins to warm and wilt the radicchio a little.
Make a dressing in a mixing bowl, whisking the remaining olive oil with the moscatel vinegar and maple syrup. Add the warmed radicchio to this and toss.
Divide the beans between two shallow bowls. Top with the radicchio and then the squash segments. Spoon any remaining dressing over the squash, then sprinkle generously with the breadcrumbs.

name: Dense Bean Salad with Tomato & Basil Vinaigrette
description: A 10-minute, protein-packed, flavourful bean salad with a fresh tomato and basil vinaigrette. Mix it up by using any types of beans you like. Perfect for packed lunches to last you all week.
keywords: Dense Bean Salad with Tomato & Basil Vinaigrette
Dense Bean Salad with Tomato & Basil Vinaigrette recipe
instructions: Drain and rinse the beans, then add them to a large salad bowl.

To a blender, add the tomatoes, shallot, garlic, olive oil, Dijon mustard and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and black pepper, then blitz until smooth. For a finer dressing, strain through a sieve and discard any pulp.
Tear the basil into pieces then add to the beans along with the rocket. Season with salt and pepper then toss to combine.

Plate or box up the beans then tear over the mozzarella. If eating later, store the dressing separately in an airtight container. If eating now, drizzle the dressing over the top. It will keep in the fridge for 3-4 days.

name: Devilled Croque Madame
description: Toasted bread layered with ham and a spicy devilled béchamel sauce. Beautiful.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Melt the butter in a pan over a medium low heat, add the flour and whisk until smooth. Add the curry powder, mix again and then slowly add the milk, whisking constantly.
Add the mustard, Worcestershire sauce and tabasco, then half of the grated Cheddar and whisk until smooth.

Grab 4 slices of bread and spread each with a little of the béchamel. Top each with 2 slices of ham, a handful of grated Cheddar and a second slice of bread. Transfer to a baking tray and pour over the rest of the béchamel.
Bake in the oven for about 15 mins until the top is golden brown (you can also grill it for a few minutes at the end).
While they bake, fry 4 crispy fried eggs and as soon as the Croque Madame comes out of the oven, top with the eggs and serve.

name: Dill Pickle Soup with Rye Croutons
description: If you're into pickles, you're going to be really into this dill pickle soup. It's tangy, briny, and extremely soothing. Get stuck in.
keywords: Dill Pickle Soup with Rye Croutons
Dill Pickle Soup with Rye Croutons recipe
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C. Tear or chop the rye bread up and drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and cook for 20 mins, or until crisp. You can also use the airfryer.
Peel and dice the carrots, dice the celery, finely chop the onion and finely chop the garlic.

Heat a splash of oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan and add the onion, celery, carrot and garlic. Sweat for 10 mins until lightly golden. Add the flour and cook off for 2 mins while stirring. Meanwhile, finely slice the gherkins and drain off the juice to use later. Halve the new potatoes.

Add the stock to the pan gradually, while stirring, and bring it to a boil. Add the potatoes and gherkins and a big splash of the gherkin juice, then simmer for 20 mins until the potatoes are fork tender. Chop the dill and stir most of it through the soup along with the soured cream and a squeeze of lemon juice, tasting and adjusting the seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve the soup topped with more soured cream and dill, along with the rye croutons.

name: Dilly Artichoke & Bean Salad
description: Crunchy fennel, salty feta and kidney beans tossed in a thick lemon and dill dressing, with a toasty seed sprinkle over the top. No delicate leaves to wilt, so it's just as good the day after.
instructions: Drain the jarred artichokes, then drain and rinse the kidney beans.
Thinly slice the fennel and spring onions. Put the spinach into a colander, then boil the kettle and pour the boiling water over until wilted. Leave to cool before squeezing the excess water out.
Add the pumpkin, sesame and fennel seeds to a frying pan and toast over a medium heat for 2-4 mins, until fragrant. Remove from the heat, leave to cool, then stir the chilli flakes through.
Squeeze the juice of the lemon into a bowl, then finely chop the dill and stir it through. Slowly whisk in the extra virgin olive oil until thickened. Season with the honey, salt and black pepper.

Pick and roughly chop the parsley, dill and mint leaves. Add the beans, artichokes, spinach, fennel and spring onions to a large bowl, then crumble in the feta and scatter over the herbs. Toss the dressing through and divide between plates. Finish with a sprinkling of the seedy mixture. It's just as good the day after, there's no delicate veg in here to wilt, which makes it a great one to prep ahead.

name: Dilly Chicken & Crushed Potato Salad
description: A simple springtime salad that makes use of leftovers from our Roast Chicken With Schmaltzy Courgettes batch. This one is as speedy as it gets.
keywords: Dilly Chicken & Crushed Potato Salad recipe
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken with Schmaltzy Courgettes.
Start by making the roast chicken and courgettes. Heat your oven to 200°C. Season your chicken with plenty of salt, inside and out and rub with 2 tbsp of olive oil.

Cut the courgettes into chunky rounds and tip into a roasting tray. Cut the onions into thin slices and finely chop the chillies. Add to the tray. Toss the veggies with oil, salt and pepper and sit the chicken on top.

Cut the very top off of each garlic bulb, grab a piece of foil and sit the garlic bulbs on top. Drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper and wrap into a little garlicky parcel. Sit that in the tray with the veggies and chicken and slide the whole lot into the oven for an hour.

After an hour, check if your chicken is cooked with a thermometer (you’re looking for a minimum of 70°C in the thickest part of the breast and thigh) or make a small incision and check if the juices run clear. If you’re all good, whip it off and let it rest, if it needs a little longer, pop it back in for 15 mins and check again.

While the chicken rests, smush up the flesh from your roasted garlic bulb into your veggies and pop the tray back into the oven for another 15 mins or so to finish the veggies off. Meanwhile, chop the tarragon.
Carve the legs and breasts off of the chicken. Cut the breasts into chunky slices and shred the meat from the legs.

Finish the veggies with lemon zest, lemon juice and the chopped tarragon. Optional: if batch cooking the roast chicken and courgette base for the week, portion out the chicken and veggies into Tupperware containers now.

Pop the potatoes into a pan and cover with cold water. Season generously with salt and pop onto a medium heat. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a bare simmer. Cook for 12-14 mins or until very tender. Drain, shock with cold water and set aside.
Finely dice the onion and stick in a large mixing bowl. Cover with lemon juice and set aside for 5 mins to quick pickle.
Finely chop the dill and dill pickles and add to the bowl. Break the potatoes into rough chunks and drop in. Add the mayo and give everything a toss together.
Shred the chicken into the salad and tip in the courgettes. Toss together, season with salt and pepper.
Divide between plates and get stuck in.

name: Dilly Courgette & Halloumi Salad on Yoghurt
description: Golden halloumi, smoky courgettes and a zingy lemon-dill dressing, all piled onto creamy Greek yoghurt. It’s salty, crunchy and seriously satisfying. Oh, and it only take 15 mins to make!
instructions: Drain the butter beans and set aside.

Slice the courgettes into 2cm-thick coins. Place a large frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the courgettes, cut-side down, and cook for 4-5 mins, flipping halfway through, until charred on both sides. Season with salt, then tip into a large bowl.

Meanwhile, split the halloumi down the crease and chop into 2cm chunks. Add to the same pan with a drizzle of olive oil and fry for 3-4 mins until golden on all sides. Tip into the bowl with the courgettes.

Quarter the beets and roughly chop the dill fronds. Add both to the bowl along with the butter beans. Zest the lemon into the bowl, squeeze in the juice and add a generous glug of olive oil. Toss everything together until well coated.
Spoon the Greek yoghurt onto the base of a plate and spread it out. Pile the courgette and halloumi salad over the top and serve.

name: Dilly Rice
description: This simple dill rice is ideal for meal prep. Combine it with your favourite protein, veg and dressing to create your perfect meal.
instructions: Wash the rice until the water runs clear. Pick and roughly chop the dill fronds. Finely slice the dill stems.

Melt the butter in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the orzo and cook for 3-4 mins, stirring constantly, until toasted and browned. Stir through the rice then pour in the water. Let it come to the boil then pop the lid on and turn the heat down to low. Leave it for 12 mins (don’t remove the lid), then remove the pan from the heat and set it aside for another 10 min, still covered. Before serving, stir through the dill fronds and stems.
Serve with your choice of protein and veg. If batch cooking for the week, transfer the rice to a container and store in the fridge until ready to serve.

name: Dilly Rice Salad & Cottage Cheese
description: Creamy cottage cheese meets herby, lemony rice packed with lentils, crispy shallots, and crunchy veg. A properly fresh, protein-packed salad.
keywords: dilly rice salad and cottage cheese
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and boil for 8 mins. Drain and transfer to cold water to cool. Once cool enough to handle, peel and set aside.
Finely chop the shallot and add it to a large bowl with the zest and juice of the lemon. Season generously with salt and let it sit to mellow.
Microwave the rice pouch following pack instructions, or heat in a pan until piping hot.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse the lentils. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds and finely chop. Finely chop the dill.
Toss the hot rice into the lemony shallot bowl and mix well. Stir through the lentils, tomatoes, cucumber and dill. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.
Halve the boiled eggs.
To serve, spoon the salad into bowls with a big dollop of cottage cheese on the side. Season the cottage cheese with salt and pepper, and top each bowl with the halved egg.

name: Dilly Rice Salad & Cottage Cheese
description: Creamy cottage cheese meets herby, lemony rice packed with lentils, crispy shallots, and crunchy veg. A properly fresh, protein-packed salad that's perfect for your weekly meal prep.
keywords: dilly rice salad and cottage cheese
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and boil for 8 mins. Drain and transfer to cold water to cool. Once cool enough to handle, peel and set aside.
Finely chop the shallot and add it to a large bowl with the zest and juice of the lemon. Season generously with salt and let it sit to mellow.
Microwave the rice pouch following pack instructions, or heat in a pan until piping hot.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse the lentils. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds and finely chop. Finely chop the dill.
Toss the hot rice into the lemony shallot bowl and mix well. Stir through the lentils, tomatoes, cucumber and dill. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.
Halve the boiled eggs.

Spoon the salad into your Tupperware containers with a big dollop of cottage cheese on the side. Season the cottage cheese with salt and pepper, and top each with the halved egg. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Dodie's Granny's Schnitzel
description: Dodie took this recipe straight from her Granny's playbook. It's a classic for good reason. Crispy juicy chicken and warm potato salad with lemon and dill. yum.
instructions: Add the potatoes to a large saucepan and cover with cold water. Season generously with salt and place over a medium heat. Bring to a simmer and cook until just tender, this should take around 12-14 mins. Drain the potatoes and allow to steam dry.

In a bowl, combine the yoghurt, mayo with lemon zest and a squeeze of juice. Roughly chop the cucumber, dill, coriander and parsley and finely chop the red onion and cornichons. Chuck the lot into the bowl with the potatoes and fold into a gorgeous potato salad. Set aside.
Butterfly the chicken breasts and bash out between two pieces of parchment paper until very thin. Pass through the seasoned flour, eggs and breadcrumbs to coat the chicken.

Set a large frying pan over a medium heat and cover the base with a thin layer of veg oil. Cook the chicken until golden brown and crisp, flipping once. Season with salt straight after the chicken leaves the pan.
Divide the schnitzels between warm plates and serve with a generous side of potato salad and a fresh lemon wedge.

name: Dom's Subs Meatball Grinder
description: Greg Boyce from Dom's Subs shows us how to make this twist on a meatball sub. This sanger is super juicy and perfect to take on a summery picnic.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut your bread rolls in half and scoop out the insides.
Put the insides into a bowl and cover with buttermilk and chicken stock, mix well and allow it to soak for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, roughly chop your parsley, finely chop up your onion and mince your garlic. Separate your egg white and yolks.
Add ½ tsp oregano, ground fennel seeds, parsley, onion, garlic, beef mince, pork mince, egg yolks, salt and pepper to the soaked bread and mix well. Grate in 50g of parmesan and mix it up again.
Shape your mixture into golf ball-sized balls and pop into a baking tray. Bake for 15 mins and then lower the temp to 180°C and continue cooking another 10 mins or until cooked through.

For the creamy Italian dressing, combine 100g mayo, 50g parmesan, ½ tsp dried oregano, apple cider vinegar and freshly ground black pepper in a bowl. Whisk that up until it reaches a creamy, sauce-like consistency
To make the 'nduja mayo, combine 100g mayonnaise with 2 tbsp of 'nduja paste, the juice of a lemon, and salt.
Finely shred your iceberg lettuce and chop up the broccoli into small pieces.
Get a pot of salted boiling water and blanch your broccoli for 3 mins. Set aside and season with salt.
For the Dom's Subs Juice: mix 50ml of your sherry vinegar with equal parts of olive oil.

Now it's time to build the sandwich. Spread 2 tbsp of 'nduja mayo on the inside of your hollowed sub rolls followed by 3 slices of mortadella, blanched broccoli, and your meatballs. Once all those ingredients are neatly tucked in your subs, you can coat them with the creamy Italian dressing. Use as much as you see fit. Top your filling with shredded lettuce and a drizzle of ‘juice’ before wrapping the whole thing up in tin foil. Slice it in half and enjoy.

name: Double Bean & Roasted Pepper Chilli
description: A hearty, smoky chilli packed with beans, roasted peppers, and chipotle spice. The whipped lime tofu on top keeps things fresh and creamy. It’s a proper banger for a cosy night in.
keywords: Double Bean & Roasted Pepper Chilli recipe
instructions: Finely chop the onion and garlic, and slice the roasted peppers. Heat the olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat, then add the onion and garlic. Season with salt, cook for 5 mins until softened and just turning golden.

Drain and rinse the beans, then add them to the pan along with the chipotle paste, oregano, and roasted peppers. Cook for 2 mins to let the flavours meld, then tip in the chopped tomatoes. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 mins, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the spinach and cook for another 2 mins until just wilted. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Meanwhile, blitz the silken tofu in a blender until smooth. Season with salt and pepper, then zest in the lime and mix well. Stir half of the whipped tofu through the chilli, keeping the rest for serving.
Cut the lime into wedges. Serve the chilli in bowls, topped with the remaining whipped tofu, fresh coriander, and a squeeze of lime.

name: Double Courgette & Chicken Dinner
description: Crispy chicken thighs with roast courgettes and a herby lemon courgette dip. This one’s a joy to cook and eat – and you can easily spruce up the leftovers for a delicious lunch the next day. Winning.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

For the chicken: Season the chicken on both sides with salt and pepper. Place skin side down in an oven-proof frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Leave to cook for 8-10 mins until the skin goes golden. Meanwhile, finely slice the onion and courgette.

Remove the pan from the heat and flip the chicken over. Nestle the sliced courgette and onion under the chicken, and sprinkle over the chilli flakes. Pour over the vinegar then slide the pan into the oven to roast for 35-40 mins until the chicken is golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, make the dip: Trim and roughly chop the courgette. Pick the mint leaves, saving a 1/4 to serve as your garnish. Add both into a food processor with the garlic, walnuts, 3/4 of the dill (stalks and all), Greek yoghurt and the zest of the lemon. Blitz until broken down into a bitty dip. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice. (If you don’t have a food processor, grate the courgette and garlic, finely chop the walnuts and herbs. Stir all the dip ingredients together and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. This makes a chunkier but still delicious dip.)
Share the chicken thighs and roasted veg onto plates, serve with a dollop of dip and a bundle of the remaining fresh dill and mint. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Double Lentil Rigatoni with Crispy Kale
description: A hearty and healthy vegan dinner that’s full of fibre, iron and protein from not one but two types of lentils. A perfect cosy weeknight meal.
instructions: Finely chop your shallots and sundried tomatoes and mince the garlic. Dissolve the stock cube in the boiling water to make your vegetable stock. Rinse the lentils. Set aside.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the shallot and a pinch of salt and sauté for 5-6 mins until softened. Add the minced garlic and cook for another 3 mins. Add the spices and most of the chopped sundried tomatoes (reserving a few for garnish) and fry for another minute.

Add the red lentils and vegetable stock to the pan and stir to combine. Bring the mixture to a boil over a medium heat then reduce the heat to low, cover with a lid and leave to simmer for 15-20 mins or until the lentils are cooked through. Lift the lid and stir occasionally as the lentils cook and add a splash more water if they’re drying out. Once cooked, remove from the heat and set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 180°C. Rinse, de-stem and roughly chop the kale. Add to a baking tray with oil and salt and roast for 10-15 mins until crispy (be careful to not let it burn).
Cook the pasta for a minute less than packet instructions then drain, reserving a mug of pasta water.

Get the silken tofu, nutritional yeast and ½ the cooked lentils into a blender. Add a glug of olive oil, the juice of the lemon and a pinch of salt and black pepper. Blitz to a thick, paste-like consistency (don’t over-blend) then season to taste, adding more salt or lemon if you think it needs it.
Add the blended mix, cooked pasta and remaining lentils back into the pan, set over a low-medium heat. Add a splash of pasta water, mix well and gently heat through.
Divide the rigatoni between bowls and top with the crispy kale. Finish with plenty of black pepper, the remaining sundried tomatoes for decoration and texture, and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Double Pumpkin Gnocchi Bake
description: This double pumpkin tray bake has everything looking for in cosy comfort food.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Pour the soup and the coconut milk into a deep roasting pan or baking tray and mix well.
Mix the butter beans and gnocchi into the baking tray with the soup.
Slice the pumpkin in half, scoop out the seeds, then slice into thin crescent slices.
Place the pumpkin on top of the gnocchi mix. Season with salt and pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.
Bake for 35-40 mins or until the pumpkin is cooked and starting to brown on top.
Meanwhile, finely chop the herbs, zest the orange and grate the garlic. Add these to a bowl with 2 tbsp of orange juice and 3 tbsp of olive oil and season well with salt and pepper.
Add the herb sauce on top of the gnocchi bake and serve.

name: Double Stacked Pesto Grilled Cheese
description: How do you make a grilled cheese (which, let's face it, is already an objectively perfect food) even better? By adding pesto, of course.
keywords: Double stacked pesto grilled cheese recipe
instructions: Grate the cheese. Toast one slice of bread. Spread half of the pesto across one of the slices of bread, top with half of the cheese. Spread the slice of toast with the remaining pesto and place on top of the cheese pesto-side up. Add the remainder of the cheese then top with the final slice of bread. Spread the outside of the top slice of bread with mayo, then scatter with the sesame seeds.

Place a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and place the toastie, sesame seed side down in the pan. Place another frying pan on top and press down. Allow to cook for 3-4 mins, until golden brown.

Spread mayo across the bread top, then scatter with sesame seeds, pressing them in a little so they stick. Flip the toastie over, so the freshly mayo’d and sesame’d side is now face down in the pan. Place the pan on top again to press the toastie down. Cook for another 3-4 mins, until the cheese is melted and the toastie is golden. Serve immediately.

name: Double Tenderstem Broccoli & Black Pepper Rigatoni
description:
Ok, this isn't a cacio pepe at all, but it does have a LOT of black pepper in it much like a cacio e pepe. We often forget of black pepper being an actual spice and using it can transform your food. It works so nicely here with the broccoli which is cooked down to create a clingy, glossy sauce. I love it and I hope you do too.

In Partnership with Aldi #ad
keywords: Double Tenderstem & Black Pepper Pasta recipe
instructions: Pop a large pan of well salted water on to boil. You want it to be salty, but not too salty, so don't be shy. Cut three-quarters of the Tenderstem into small pieces and add to the water, cooking for around 5 mins until fork tender, then remove with a slotted spoon. Don't get rid of the water yet - you'll use it to cook the pasta.

In the meantime, finely chop the garlic. Heat the grill to high. Add the remaining quarter of Tenderstem to a baking tray, drizzle with a quarter of the olive oil, season with salt, then mix well. Slide under the grill for 5-8 mins, until charred.
Return the large pot of salted water you cooked the broccoli in to the boil. Add the rigatoni and cook for 7 mins, until al dente, making sure to save the cooking water.

In another pan, heat the remaining olive oil over a medium-low heat, enough to coat the bottom of the pan. Add the garlic and cook out for a couple of minutes until fragrant but not golden, then chuck in the boiled Tenderstem and a ladle of its cooking water. Mush the Tenderstem down with a spoon until it resembles a chunky pesto.

Add the cooked pasta to the Tenderstem sauce with a good slosh of the reserved cooking water, then give it a good mix, bubbling gently and smooshing until the sauce coats the pasta. You might need to add more pasta water, but see how you go as you smoosh. You want it saucy but not watery. Grate in the Parmesan and add the black pepper (2 tsp is around 60 cracks). Tear in the basil leaves and squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Keep stirring vigorously until the sauce is glossy, emulsified and clinging to the pasta.

Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed, then serve up topped with the charred tenderstem and the remaining Parmesan grated over. To make it completely veggie, swap the Parmesan for a vegetarian hard cheese.

name: Double Tomato & Halloumi Pasta Salad
description: The ultimate pasta salad featuring wafer thin slices of halloumi. Destined to be a fan favourite after the first forkful.
keywords: Double Tomato & Halloumi Pasta Salad  recipe
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, tip the pasta in and cook following pack instructions until al dente. Fully drain once cooked.
Finely grate half the tomatoes into a bowl. Thinly slice the halloumi (use a mandoline if you have one) and add to the grated tomatoes.

Pour the olive oil into a frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the flaked almonds and cook until golden. Drop the fennel seeds and pul biber in, give everything a stir and pour into the halloumi bowl. Stir, then taste and season with salt, pepper and sherry vinegar.
Roughly chop the sun-dried tomatoes, pick the parsley and tear any big basil leaves. Wedge the nectarines and chop the remaining tomatoes into bite-sized pieces.
Toss the sun-dried tomatoes, chopped tomatoes, herbs, nectarine and pasta through the halloumi bowl and serve.

name: Double Tomato Creamy Pasta
description: Juicy cherry tomatoes and rich sundried tomato pesto make this silky pasta ridiculously tasty, and it’s all ready in 15.
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, add the pasta and cook until al dente, following pack instructions.

Meanwhile, add the cherry tomatoes to a pan with a drizzle of olive oil and place over a medium heat. Gently cook the tomatoes, stirring occasionally, until they’ve softened. Season with salt, then stir the water and pesto through until saucy.

Using a slotted spoon, transfer the cooked pasta into the sauce. Turn the heat up to medium-high and toss everything together until nicely coated. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen the sauce, if needed. Taste and season with salt.
Stir three-quarters of the basil leaves through, then share between bowls. Grate over the Parmesan and top with the remaining basil leaves.

name: Double Tomato Roast Chicken with Aubergine Yoghurt
description: Two kinds of tomato: jammy roasted ones in the chicken juices and fresh ones stirred through at the end, all spooned over smoky aubergine yoghurt.
keywords: Double Tomato Roast Chicken with Aubergine Yoghurt
Double Tomato Roast Chicken with Aubergine Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Place the chicken thighs in a large roasting tray with the cherry tomatoes and the unpeeled garlic cloves. Drizzle generously with olive oil, season well with salt and black pepper and roast for 40-50 mins, until the chicken is deeply golden and the tomatoes have collapsed and gone jammy.
Cut the aubergines into large chunks and spread them over a second tray. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and roast alongside the chicken for 30-35 mins, until completely soft.
Roughly chop the vine tomatoes, add to a bowl with a pinch of salt and leave to sit while everything roasts.

Lift the chicken and garlic out of the tray, leaving all the roasting juices and tomatoes behind. While everything is still warm, stir the chopped fresh tomatoes and most of the basil through the tray juices. The heat will just soften the tomatoes while keeping them fresh and bright.

Squeeze the roasted garlic out of its skins. Finely chop the roasted aubergine and add to a bowl with the Greek yoghurt, the roasted garlic, the juice of the lemon, the extra virgin olive oil and a pinch of salt and black pepper. Stir until creamy but still a little textured.
Heat the spelt according to the packet instructions. Any cooked grain works here, so swap in freekeh, bulgur wheat, brown rice or quinoa if that's what you've got.
Spoon the aubergine yoghurt onto plates and top with the chicken and a few spoonfuls of the tomatoes and their juices. Serve with the spelt, scattered with the remaining basil.

name: Dr. Oetker Chocolate Hazelnut Cheesecake
description: Treat yourself with these chocolate and hazelnut cheesecakes. Creamy, nutty, chocolatey and totally vegan. Delightful. Liam has smashed it with this one.
instructions: Soak all but 1 tbsp of the hazelnuts in 500ml of water for at least 30 minutes, preferably overnight.

Melt the butter in the microwave. Crush the digestive biscuits to a fine powder in a food processor or bowl, then add in the caster sugar and melted butter and mix to combine. Press one tablespoon into muffin cases in a muffin tray.
Melt the 150g dark chocolate in the microwave.
