Drain the hazelnuts and blend with the vanilla extract, maple syrup and oat milk. Once very smooth, drizzle in the melted chocolate and a big pinch of salt and continue blending.
Boil 100ml of water with the Dr. Oetker Vege-Gel and blend in with the hazelnut chocolate mixture.
Pour your cheesecake mixture into a small jug and gently pour the mixture into each mould. Pop into the fridge to set overnight.
Once set, prep your toppings. Melt the remaining 50g chocolate and finely chop the saved hazelnuts.
Carefully remove your cheesecakes from the moulds, then drizzle with your chocolate and top with your hazelnuts. Serve.

name: Drunken Noodles
description: These savoury, spicy noodles are ready in less than 20 mins. Flavoured with basil and soy sauce, they are the perfect fakeaway for a weeknight meal.
instructions: Soak your rice noodles in boiling water for 10 mins or according to the packet instructions
Mince the garlic, red chillies and onion, then chop the spring onions into 4cm pieces. Pick off the basil leaves and set them aside. Cut the chicken breast into very thin slices.
In a bowl, combine the fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce and sugar.
Heat up a large wok until it’s smoking, then add in a big glug of oil. Fry off the garlic, onion and chilli for 1 min until fragrant. Add in the chicken and cook for 3 mins until cooked through.
Add in your sauce and then immediately add in your soaked noodles. Mix well so that the noodles are evenly coated and then toss through your spring onions and basil leaves.
Serve immediately.

name: Dry Spiced Squash Curry
description: This curry works best with winter squash varieties that don’t quickly cook down into a mush, and that perhaps might also need a helping hand, flavour-wise — so Crown Prince and Acorn squash are particularly good, or you could use Butternut squash. Serve with chapatis or cook-from-frozen paratha, yoghurt, a mango or aubergine chutney and maybe some dal if you have leftovers.
instructions: Peel and remove the seeds from the squash then cut the flesh into 2-3cm cubes. Mince the ginger. Flatten the unpeeled garlic cloves with the back of a knife. Separate the coriander stalks and leaves, and finely chop both. Finely dice the chilli. Crack open the cardamom pods with the side of a knife.

Warm the olive oil in a large frying pan or wok placed over a medium-high heat. Add the chilli flakes, mustard seeds, minced ginger and bashed garlic. Cook for 90 seconds or so, stirring frequently, until the mustard seeds start to pop.
Add the diced squash, turmeric, cumin, cardamom pods, sugar and salt. Sauté for 2-3 mins, colouring the squash a little. Add a splash of water if the spices are sticking and burning.

Stir in the coriander stalks and diced green chilli plus the water. Cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low-medium and leave the squash to simmer/steam for 5 mins until the squash is tender, but not yet mushy.
Now remove the lid and cook with the lid off until there’s no water remaining. If the squash isn't quite tender at that point, add a splash of water and keep cooking until it is.
Throw in the chopped coriander leaves, stir carefully so as to avoid breaking up the squash, then serve with flatbreads and/or rice, yoghurt, pickles, and dal if you have some.

name: Dry-Brined Chicken Legs with Sweet & Sour Peppers
description: Dry-brining is a great way to get super flavourful, juicy chicken with mega crispy skin. Straight from Ben’s new book How I Cook - this chicken roasts over sweet & sour peppers for an banging weeknight treat.
keywords: Ben Lebus How I Cook recipes
instructions: Mix the caster sugar with 1 tbsp of fine sea salt and liberally season the chicken legs all over. If you’ve got time, you can leave these in the fridge overnight, or do this before you go to work, then whip them out when you get home. Don’t have that kind of time? No bother, just salt them for at least 30 minutes. Don’t forget to bring your chicken out to come to room temperature before cooking.
Preheat the oven to 250°C.

Cut the peppers into chunky slices – I like to take the cheeks off the side of the peppers and leave them in large, craggy shapes. Peel and halve the onions then cut them into 5mm-thick slivers and toss into a large roasting tin. Set the peppers on top of the onions, skin side up. Nestle in the bay leaves, coat the whole lot with lots of olive oil and sprinkle over a healthy pinch of salt, then slide into the oven and roast for 13–15 minutes, or until the peppers are starting to char and blister.

Thinly slice two of the garlic cloves and scrunch through the bay leaves in your hands. Pull the tray out of the oven, stir the sliced garlic, bay leaves and remaining sugar through the veggies, then push them to the sides and clear space in the centre. Pat the chicken legs dry and nestle them in the middle, skin side up. Slide back into the oven and reduce the heat to 190°C. Cook for 40–45 minutes until the chicken legs are brown and the skin is crispy and caramelised. After 30 minutes, add the vinegar and stir through the veggies for the last 10 minutes and check in on the chicken legs. If they need a bit more colour towards the end, crank up the heat to 210°C for the last 5–10 minutes.
While the chicken cooks, cook the fregola in boiling salted water for 8–10 minutes until just tender. Drain and toss with a little olive oil to stop it clumping.

Mix the tahini and yoghurt in a bowl. Add the grated zest and juice of the lemon, a big pinch of salt and finely grate in the remaining garlic clove. Add a little ice-cold water to loosen the mix into a shiny, swoop-able texture.
Pull the chicken legs out of the oven and let them rest for 5 minutes.

Spread some of the tahini across warm plates and top with fregola. Add a chicken leg to each and then cover with the jammy peppers, onions and bay leaves, with plenty of the roasting juices. Finish with a few twists of pepper and serve.

name: Duck Pancakes
description: Homemade duck pancakes, proving cooking duck is as easy as chicken and you can cook and glaze it all in one pan. These Chinese style pancakes are super fun to make and cooked in a pan with a little char for flavour.
instructions: First put the flour into a large bowl and set aside. Pour the hot water and all the remaining ingredients into a jug. Slowly pour the hot water mixture into the flour, using a spoon or chopsticks to stir, then knead for 5 minutes, adding a dusting of flour if it’s sticky. Cover the bowl and leave for 20-30 mins.

Meanwhile, pat the duck skin dry with kitchen paper and, use a knife to create rough criss-cross scores in the fat, (not the flesh). Sprinkle both sides generously with salt and leave on a plate to come to room temperature.

For the pickle, slice the cucumber in half on a diagonal, then use a small tsp to scoop out the watery core. Then finely slice on the diagonal. Combine in a small bowl with the remaining pickle ingredients. Set aside.
For the slaw, slice each spring onion into three chunks, then place them all into a long line and finely shred. Put into a bowl of cold tap water and set aside.

Now it’s time to shape and cook the pancakes. 
Dust your hands in flour and poke a hole in the middle of the dough. Keep squeezing the dough to make a massive doughnut, around the thickness of a 50p coin, then make a slit to turn the doughnut into a long log. Dust the log with flour and use scissors to cut it into 16 doughballs. Sprinkle all the pieces with flour, coating each piece well, then flatten them one by one with the fattest part of your palm. Divide into pairs and add a tsp of sesame to one pancake, then stick the two together. Repeat with the remaining dough pieces so that you have 8 dough stacks in total.
Take one dough stack and, using a rolling pin, roll it in to a circle the size of a ping-pong bat. Flour the circle, then repeat with the remaining dough stacks. Cover them all with a towel.

Cook the pancakes in a small, dry pan set over a medium heat, with the lid on, for 2 mins each side. Carefully remove the pancakes and let them cool for 30 seconds, then pull apart the 2 pancakes by finding a small opening., immediately wrap min a towel to keep them soft. Repeat with all the pancakes, stacking each one inside the towel. You should have 16 pancakes in total.

Mix all the honey glaze ingredients together in a small bowl. Set aside. Pat the duck dry with kitchen paper to remove the excess water, then add to a cold pan with no oil and no heat. Turn the fire to low-medium and cook for 6-7 mins – the fat will slowly release, giving you super-crispy golden skin. Flip the duck, then pour over the honey glaze and use a spoon to baste, spooning the glaze over the skin for 2 minutes. Remove the duck to a plate and rest skin-side up.
Drain any excess liquid from the cucumber pickle and decant into a nice bowl. Drain the spring onions well, then add to another bowl with the 1 tbsp sesame oil .
Finely slice the duck on a diagonal, transfer toserve on a serving plate and pour over any resting juices.

Before serving, ensure the pancakes are warm. You can microwave inside the kitchen towel for 30 seconds, or warm in the pan, with the lid on for 2 mins over a low-medium heat. Always keep the pancakes covered in order to keep them warm and soft.
Serve the duck with the pancakes, cucumber pickle, spring onion slaw, hoisin sauce and chilli oil or chilli paste.

name: Dukkah Tomato Salad
description: Dukkah is an Egyptian aromatic nut and spice blend, perfect as a topping for juicy summer tomatoes.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C/320°F.
To make the dukkah, toast all of the nuts separately (almonds: 8-10 mins, hazelnuts: 10-12mins, pistachios: 8-10 mins, sesame seeds: 6-8 mins).
Dry toast the coriander, fennel and cumin seeds separately in a pan. Toast for a few minutes each on medium heat until they begin to smell aromatic.
Grind the herbs in a spice grinder or pestle and mortar.
Pulse the nuts in a small food processor until you have a chunky crumb, take care not to over process into a powder- you should have large pieces of nuts.
Add the seeds to the nuts and season with salt to taste. Add the aleppo pepper here if you’re using it.
Slice the tomatoes and lay them flat on a plate. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle a few tablespoons of dukkah and finish with some basil leaves. Enjoy!

name: Dumpling Curry Traybake
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad

Crispy dumplings and Thai curry sauce get the traybake treatment, finished with a chilli crisp-style shallot oil you’ll want on everything. The ultimate saviour after a big one or when you’ve just crawled home from a festival.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.
In a large roasting tray, stir together the Thai curry paste, soy sauce, curry powder, sugar and coconut milk until smooth.
Add the stir-fry veg and dumplings. Toss everything to coat, then cover the tray with foil. Roast for 25 mins until the dumplings are cooked and the sauce is bubbling.

Meanwhile, finely slice the shallots and garlic. Add the oil to a small saucepan with the shallots and set over a low heat. Simmer for 10 mins until golden, then add the garlic and cook for another 5 mins. Use a slotted spoon to lift out the shallots and garlic and drain on kitchen paper.
Tip the chilli flakes into a small heatproof bowl and pour over the warm oil. Once it cools slightly, stir the crispy shallots and garlic back in. Season with a pinch of salt.
Pick the coriander leaves and slice the lime into wedges.
When the traybake is done, remove from the oven and give everything a gentle mix. Serve topped with coriander, sesame seeds and a big spoonful of the spicy shallot oil.

name: Dumpling Minestrone Soup
description: There’s a whole new world when you realise dumplings are just juicy meatballs that are covered pasta. They're glorious when dropped into a hearty minestrone soup recipe.
keywords: best soup recipe easy minestrone soup
instructions: Finely slice the garlic, onions and celery. Peel carrots and potato and matchstick all the remaining veg.

Add olive oil to a large sauce pot on medium high heat. Add onions, celery, garlic and a pinch of salt, then cook for 5 mins or until lightly golden. Add tomato paste, lots of black pepper and cook for 1 min. Add all the vegetables, cook for 5 mins or until slightly soft.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes, beans, chicken stock, soy sauce, sugar, chilli powder and all the basil stalks. Bring to the boil with a lid and simmer on low heat for 20 mins.
Pour in all the cherry tomatoes and cook for 5 mins without the lid. Add in all the dumplings and boil for 3 mins, gently stirring to prevent it from sticking.
Add most of the basil leaves, reserving some for garish, then drizzle a little olive oil and taste for seasoning, add a little salt if needed.
Serve into bowls and garnish with olive oil, and remaining basil

name: Dumpling Noodle Salad with Creamy Sesame & Crispy Chilli Dressing
description: Slurpy noodles, golden crispy dumplings and crunchy veg, all coated in our Creamy Sesame & Crispy Chilli Oil dressing for a serious kick. Texture heaven.
keywords: crispy dumpling noodle salad with creamy sesame & crispy chilli dressing
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water to cool completely. Set aside.

Finely slice the spring onions and halve the sugar snap peas. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds and slice into half-moons. Roughly crush the peanuts with the back of your knife and pick the coriander leaves. Then add everything to a bowl with the noodles.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the dumplings and cook for 8–10 minutes, turning regularly, until golden and crispy all over. (You can also do this in an airfryer at 180°C for 15-20 mins).

Add the tahini to a bowl. Peel and finely grate in the garlic and ginger, then add the honey, lime juice and water. Whisk until smooth and creamy, loosening with a splash more water if needed. Season with salt, then spoon the crispy chilli oil over the top for a marbled effect, or mix it through for a fully mixed dressing.
Add the crispy dumpling to your salad. Pour over the dressing and toss well to coat. Serve straight away while the dumplings are still crispy.
For a marbled finish, pour the crispy chilli oil over the top and leave it untouched. Otherwise, stir it through for a fully mixed sauce.

name: Dumplings In Chilli Vinegar
description: This quick and simple chilli vinegar dressing goes great with store-bought dumplings. Weeknight dinners don't get easier than this.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, with a big pinch of salt.
When the water is bubbling, pour in all the dumplings and stir so they don’t stick. Set a timer for 3 mins.
In the meantime, combine the chilli oil vinegar ingredients into a large serving dish.

As soon as the water boils again, add a cup of tap water to eliminate bubbles, and wait until the water comes back to a boil. If the dumplings float, use a sieve to remove them straight into the serving bowls of chilli vinegar.
Finish with sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

name: Easiest Rarebit Scones with Fried Egg & Ham
description: Inspired by Welsh Rarebit, these cheesy home-baked scones topped with sage-fried eggs are the perfect weekend brunch, especially when served with ham and lots of Worcestershire sauce as they are here.
keywords: Easiest Rarebit Scones with a Fried Egg & Ham Recipe
Easiest Rarebit Scones with a Fried Egg & Ham
instructions: Cut the butter into cubes. Ensure your butter is very cold (sometimes, I put it in the freezer for 10 mins while measuring everything out). Grate the Cheddar. Beat the egg.
Whisk the milk, juice of the lemon and Worcestershire sauce together in a jug, then set aside to thicken (this is a quick version of buttermilk).

In a mixing bowl, whisk together the plain flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt. Add the cold butter cubes and rub them in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs, but still has a few irregular chunks (these will create the layers). Add ½ the grated Cheddar.

Slowly pour in the thickened buttermilk and the beaten egg, bit by bit as you might not need all of it. Stir with a metal spoon until just combined, then knead gently with your hands until it just comes together with no dry patches (avoid overworking).
Tip the dough onto a lightly floured surface and flatten it into an even rectangle about 3cm thick.
Place the dough in the fridge to rest while preheating the oven to 220°C fan.
Remove the scones from the fridge and cut them into 4 thick pieces. Brush the tops with a little extra milk. Pile a small mound of the remaining grated Cheddar on each scone.
Bake in the oven for 12-15 mins, until risen and golden. Allow to cool while you prepare the eggs (or just eat them warm with plenty of butter and Marmite).

Heat a medium frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add a glug of olive oil and the butter. Add the sage leaves and crack in the eggs (if you're cooking more, do it in batches). Let them cook until the edges start to crisp, then season with salt and pepper.

Place the scones onto plates or a plate platter, split open then top with the fried eggs and sage and any melted butter. Serve with a slice of ham and some extra Worcestershire sauce all over, if you like.

name: Easter Egg Hot Chocolate
description: Got any leftover Easter eggs kicking about? We know that’s not likely but if you do, we’ve got a mega Easter egg hot chocolate recipe for you right here.
instructions: Lightly whip 60% of your double cream until you have very soft peaks and set aside in a cool place.
Roughly chop up your chocolate eggs.

Place the milk, icing sugar and remaining double cream in a sauce pan and gently warm over a medium heat. Add in the chocolate and reduce to a low heat. Stir for a couple of minutes until the chocolate has all melted and emulsified to create your hot chocolate. It should be a similar consistency to double cream and glossy.
Pour the hot chocolate into mugs and top each with a spoon of the whipped cream.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Easy Aloo Matar
description: This quick and easy (yet extremely delicious) potato and pea curry is a staple in homes across India, particularly in the north. I love eating it with steamed basmati rice drizzled with ghee, or simple rotis.
instructions: Peel and chop the potatoes into 3cm chunks. Transfer to a bowl and wash well to get rid of the excess starch.
Trim and finely chop the onion. Finely grate or mince the ginger and garlic. Thinly slice half the coriander.

Add a drizzle of oil to a wok or saucepan and place over a medium heat. Once the oil is hot, add the bay leaves and cumin seeds. Fry until they splutter. Add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the ginger and garlic, fry until fragrant, then stir through the powdered spices and crushed chillies.

Pour the canned tomatoes in and cook for 8-10 mins until thickened. Add the potatoes and the water and bring to a boil then turn the heat down to medium and cook, uncovered, for 25-30 mins until the potatoes have softened. Once the potatoes are cooked through, add a splash of water to loosen, if needed.
Add the peas and cook until hot. Stir through the chopped coriander and season with salt and lime juice.
Serve immediately, garnished with the remaining fresh coriander.

name: Easy Banana & Blueberry Pancakes
description: Fluffy banana pancakes studded with juicy blueberries, ready in minutes. Perfect for the little ones - and grown-ups too.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Defrost your frozen blueberries for the pancakes (you can skip this step if you're using fresh ones).
If you're up for the quick compote, tip the frozen blueberries into the pan with the water and honey and bring to a boil. Simmer for a minute then remove from the heat and allow to cool.

To make the pancakes, add the ripe banana to a bowl and mash together until smooth. Crack the egg into the bowl and whisk everything together. Add in the self-raising flour and a tiny pinch of salt and mix everything together until well combined, adding a splash of milk if its a little thick.

Melt a little knob of butter in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Scoop in heaped tablespoon of the mixture into the pan, keeping 2-3cm of space around each one, then drop some of the defrosted blueberries onto the surface of the batter. Cook for 2 minutes on the first side, until lightly golden, then flip and cook for another minute. 
Repeat until you've used up all your mix.
Plate up the blueberry pancakes, with your quite compote and yoghurt, or your kid's favourite topping.

name: Easy Birthday Sheet Cake
description: A super simple vanilla sheet cake that's perfect for a crowd. Topped with buttercream and rainbow sprinkles, of course.
keywords: best ever vanilla sponge cake recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease and line a 20 x 30cm roasting tin.

Sift the flour into a bowl. Add the sugar, salt and baking powder and whisk together. Use an electric whisk to beat in the butter until it is incorporated and the mixture appears to be evenly coated and looks like a fine crumble mix – 2–3 mins on medium speed.

Add the eggs and beat, first on medium, then on high, just until incorporated. Add the milk and vanilla and beat, on medium and then on high, for about 2-3 mins until the mixture is smooth and combined; it will appear a bit lighter in colour.
Pour the mixture into the prepared tin and level out to the edges. Bake in the oven for 25–30 mins, or until a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tin for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely.
Spread a generous layer of buttercream over the sponge and top with sprinkles of your choice.

name: Easy Burrito Bowl
description: This easy burrito bowl is loaded up with chilli and an assortment of fresh veggies.
instructions: Make the Beef Chilli Con Carne.
Reheat the Beef Chilli Con Carne in a saucepan until piping hot.
Heat the rice following packet instructions.

Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes into 1cm chunks and shred the lettuce. Place both into a bowl and season with salt, pepper and the juice of half the lime. 
Slice the avocado and pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stalks.

Toss the coriander stalks through the rice and share between bowls. Top with the Beef Chilli Con Carne, tortilla crisps, tomato salad, sliced avo and a dollop of soured cream. 
Finish with a scattering of coriander and serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Easy Celebration Cake
description: Got something to celebrate? Impress your friends and family with this beautiful cake. Looks like hard work, but it's actually really easy to make.
keywords: best ever vanilla sponge cake recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease and line two 20cm cake tins.

Sift the flour into a bowl. Add the sugar, salt and baking powder and whisk together. Use an electric whisk to beat in the butter until it is incorporated and the mixture appears to be evenly coated and looks like a fine crumble mix – 2–3 mins on medium speed.

Add the eggs and beat, first on medium, then on high, just until incorporated. Add the milk and vanilla and beat, on medium and then on high, for about 2-3 mins until the mixture is smooth and combined; it will appear a bit lighter in colour.
Divide the mixture between the two prepared cake tins and level out to the edges. Bake in the oven for 25–30 mins, or until a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tins for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely.

Spread a generous layer of swiss meringue buttercream on one sponge and sprinkle over a handful of fresh raspberries. Pop the other sponge on top, sandwiching them together. Spread the buttercream all over the top and sides of the cake. Fill a piping bag with more buttercream and use it to decorate the cake how you like. Top with a few extra raspberries and enjoy!

name: Easy Cheese and Onion Tart
description: This easy, cheesy tart is perfect for pleasing a big crowd or prepping ahead for delicious on the go snacking.
instructions: Take the butter straight from the fridge and cut into one-inch chunks. Add to a food processor along with the flour, egg yolk and two tablespoons of cold water. Pulse until the mix resembles breadcrumbs.
Transfer to a lightly floured surface, knead lightly, and bring together into a ball. Roll out to about 1⁄2-cm thick.

Grab a 20cm fluted pastry tin and carefully line it with the pastry. Press the edges into the corners, then trim the top to just above the level of the tin. Prick the base all over with a fork and place it into the fridge for 10 mins.
Preheat your oven to 200°C fan.
Line the pastry with tin foil, fill with baking beads and bake on a baking sheet for 15 mins until golden. Remove the beads and foil and bake for another 5 mins to cook the inside.
While the pastry cooks, finely slice the red onions. Add to a saucepan over a medium heat with a splash of olive oil and a pinch of salt and cook until softened, about 7 mins.
Pour in the cream, add the grated Cheddar. and then turn off the heat. Stir until the cheese dissolves, then taste and season well with salt and pepper.
Pull the pastry halfway out of the oven but leave it on the tray. Carefully pour the onions and cream mixture into the pastry until it's almost level with the top of the case.

Bake for 25 to 30 mins until the top is golden and the centre is soft-set. Remove from the oven, finely chop the chives and sprinkle over, then allow to cool for at least 30 mins.If making ahead, portion out into triangles and store in the fridge for up to 3 days. Or freeze for up to 3 months.

name: Easy Chicken Curry
description: A gentle, creamy chicken and veg curry made for little taste buds but still satisfying for grown-ups. Super cosy, speedy, and great for freezing.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Cut the chicken thighs into small bite-sized chunks.
Peel and finely dice the onion. Peel and finely slice the garlic. Peel and grate the ginger.
Place a large lidded saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for 5–6 mins until soft and fragrant.
Stir in the curry powder, turmeric and flour. Cook for 1 min, then add the tomato purée and cook for another minute until darkened.
Add the chicken and cook for 3–4 mins until just turning golden.
Pour in the stock and bring to the boil. Turn the heat down to low, pop the lid on and let it simmer for 15 mins until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Stir through the cream and frozen peas. Cook for 2–3 mins until the sauce is silky and everything's warmed through. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, cook the rice following pack instructions. Slice the green chilli for garnish.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Spoon the curry with the fluffy rice.
Parents Plate: Dish out and garnish with the coriander, green chilli and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Easy Chicken Fajita Rice
description: All the flavours of fajitas, none of the mess. Throw everything into one parchment parcel and let the oven do the work. Perfect for busy weeknights when you cannot face washing up.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the peppers into thin strips. Peel and finely slice the onion. Drain and rinse the kidney beans.

Lay out a large rectangle of baking paper (per person) in front of you, portrait. Arrange the peppers, onions, beans and rice on the bottom half of the paper leaving a 10cm gap between the edge closest to you.Drizzle with half the olive oil, season with salt and black pepper, then mix everything together.

Slice the chicken breasts into strips, roughly 4cm thick. Add the rest of the olive oil, fajita seasoning and a pinch of salt and pepper. Rub everything together to coat the chicken well - use your chopping board. Add your chicken on top of the vegetables. Fold the top half of the baking paper over the food then fold the outside edges over each other to seal (like a Cornish pasty), creating a steam-tight parcel. Repeat with the remaining ingredients.
Transfer to the oven and bake for 20 mins. Finish with a scattering of fresh coriander and lime wedges for squeezing. Get stuck in.

name: Easy Chicken Fajita Traybake
description: It's about time fajitas got a traybake makeover. Leave your spices, chicken, peppers and onions to do its thing and then  pile into warm tortillas and load with your fave toppings for the ultimate fakeaway.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Core the peppers and slice into strips. Peel and thinly slice the onions. Slice the chicken breasts into thin strips.

Chuck everything onto a large baking tray lined with foil, drizzle with olive oil and scatter over the taco seasoning. Toss well to coat evenly. Slide the tray into the oven and roast for 15–20 mins, until the chicken is cooked through and the veg is soft and golden at the edges.
Meanwhile, warm the tortillas following the pack instructions. Grate your cheddar and shred the lettuce.
To serve, pile the chicken and veg into the tortillas and load up with sour cream, guacamole, lettuce and cheese, or any other toppings you fancy.

name: Easy Chocolate Birthday Cake
description: A super simple chocolate sheet cake that's perfect for a crowd. Topped with chocolate buttercream and sprinkles, of course.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Grease and line a 20 x 30cm roasting tin. Make up the coffee and leave it to cool. Make sure your butter is at room temperature.
In a large mixing bowl, use an electric whisk to beat together the olive oil, sugar & vanilla extract.
Crack in the eggs and add the milk and beat gently until well combined.
In a separate bowl, sift together the flour, cocoa powder, bicarb and salt. Sir until evenly combined, then beat into the batter until smooth.
Slowly add the cooled coffee and mix until just combined evenly.

Pour the cake batter into the prepared tin and bake for 25-30 mins or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Leave to cool for 10 mins in the tin then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

Meanwhile, make the chocolate buttercream. Beat the butter alone for 4–5 mins on high speed. Sift in the cocoa powder and beat until you have a paste. Beat in the icing sugar and add the vanilla, salt, milk and most of the cream then beat together slowly at first on a low speed to bring it together. Beat on high for another 2–3 mins until it’s a smooth consistency. Add more cream if desired.
Spread a generous layer of the chocolate buttercream over the sponge and top with sprinkles of your choice.

name: Easy Chocolate Brownies
description: Proudly presenting: our ultimate brownie recipe. We’ve looked at all the credentials for what makes the best brownie and combined them in this glorious recipe.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas mark 4. Grease a 20cm brownie tin or high-sided roasting tray with butter and line the base with baking paper.

Snap the dark chocolate into a microwaveable bowl, add the butter and a big pinch of salt. Zap in the microwave on high in 30-second bursts, stirring in between, until the butter and chocolate are completely melted. Set aside to cool slightly. Roughly chop the milk chocolate.
Measure the sugar into a large bowl. Crack in the eggs. Using an electric whisk, whisk the eggs and sugar together until they have almost doubled in size and are very light and fluffy.
Pour in the melted chocolate mixture and add the flour and cocoa powder. Whisk briefly until everything is combined.

Smooth half the brownie batter into your tin. Scatter over half the milk chocolate then scrape the rest of the batter over the top. Sprinkle over the remaining milk chocolate and a big pinch of sea salt. Bake for 30 mins or until the edges are set and the centre still has a good wobble.
Leave to cool then cut into 12 squares.

name: Easy Eggs Royale
description:
Meet Eggs Benedict's noble cousin, Eggs Royale. Swapping out the bacon for smoked salmon takes this classic dish to a whole new level, making it perfect for a sophisticated brunch or indulgent lunch. Traditionally served on a toasted English muffin and topped with a perfectly poached egg, the dish is elevated further with a dollop of creamy Greek yoghurt or even a drizzle of buttery béarnaise sauce infused with dill or tarragon. Add a side of sautéed spinach to give it an Eggs Florentine twist, or pair it with a mixed salad for a lighter touch. For extra flavour, try a sprinkle of mustard or a dash of hot sauce.

Inspired by the grand dining traditions of eateries like Delmonico's Restaurant, where chef Charles Ranhofer famously shaped American cuisine, this dish fits right in among fine foods like soft-boiled eggs, American pancakes, and a Bloody Mary or glass of prosecco.
instructions: Melt the butter in a small pan until it foams, then turn off the heat.
Grab a heatproof bowl that will fit over a small pan. Separate half of the eggs and add all their yolks to the bowl with the white wine vinegar and a pinch of salt and whisk to combine.
Fill the pan with water and bring to a simmer, then place the bowl on top (make sure it’s not touching the water). Whisk the mixture and as it warms it will thicken, this will take 3 or 4 mins.
Now slowly pour in the melted butter, whisking to emulsify and remove from the heat. Taste and add salt and more vinegar if needed. Set aside somewhere warm.
Half and toast the muffins and top each with 2 slices of smoked salmon.
To poach the eggs, bring a large pan of water to a boil and then reduce the heat to barely a simmer. Grab a spoon and stir the water hard to make a whirlpool.
Crack in the remaining eggs (it’s easier to do 2 at a time) and the spinning water will keep them together as you crack them in.
Allow to cook for a couple of minutes, then remove with a slotted spoon and place on top of the salmon.
Pour over the hollandaise, top with finely chopped chives and a grind of pepper. Enjoy!

name: Easy Greens Orzo
description: Creamy, cheesy, totally green, this spinach pesto orzo is a brilliant way to sneak in the good stuff. A great one for fussy eaters who still love flavour.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the orzo following pack instructions.
While the orzo's cooking, toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over a medium heat until golden, then remove from the heat.
Peel the garlic and grate the Parmesan. Zest and juice the lemon.

Into a blender, add the mint, basil and toasted pine nuts (saving a few nuts and leaves for topping), garlic, lemon zest and most of the lemon juice, plus a ladle of pasta water, spinach, most of the Parmesan, a good glug of olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth, that’s your pesto done.
Drain the orzo and mix with your spinach pesto.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Dish up the kids, add a little extra cheese if they'd like.
Parents Plate: Dish out the orzo, squeezing over a touch more lemon juice for extra zing along with the remaining toasted pine nuts, basil leaves and grated parmesan to garnish. Finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Easy Greens Soup
description: The perfect soup recipe for using up leftover rice, or when you want something easy and super comforting.
instructions: Peel and bash the garlic and ginger, then pick the parsley leaves (keep the stems).

Add a drizzle of olive oil to a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the garlic, ginger and parsley stems, then cook until fragrant. Tip in all the spinach and sweat for 3-4 mins until wilted. Transfer the mixture to a blender with the parsley leaves, turmeric, and miso, then allow to cool fully before blending until smooth.

Add the cooked rice and stock to the saucepan and bring to the boil. Once boiling, turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 15-20 mins until the mixture is creamy. If you’d like it thicker, continue cooking to your desired consistency. Stir through the blended greens and watercress.
Divide between four bowls and top with a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Easy Oat & Raisin Breakfast Bars
description: Chewy, nutty breakfast bars packed with oats, seeds and raisins perfect for mornings when you're short on time. Make one big batch at the weekend and you'll have delicious unprocessed snacks to last you the whole week or whack them in the freezer to have an emergency stash.
keywords: oat and raisin breakfast bars recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 30cm x 20cm baking tin with baking paper.

Mash the bananas in a large mixing bowl until mostly smooth. Add the eggs, almond butter (peanut butter works great too), honey or maple syrup and vanilla extract and whisk everything together. Stir in the oats, raisins, seeds, baking powder, the optional sugar if using, and a pinch of salt. Leave the mixture to sit for 5 minutes so the oats soften slightly, it should look like thick porridge.
If you're using the optional chia (or as an alternative flax seeds could work too), or chocolate, roughly chop the chocolate into chunks and stir them all in now.

Spoon the mixture into the lined tin and smooth the top. Bake for 22-28 mins, until lightly golden and just set in the middle. Leave to cool completely in the tin before slicing into bars. They'll keep in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. You can also freeze them and toast them straight from frozen.

name: Easy Oven Jerk Chicken by Original Flava
description: Original Flava's sticky fiery jerk chicken with a side of rice, peas, and plantain. It pays homage to the delicious Caribbean flavours... a big dish.
instructions: Start by chopping onion then blend together the onion, 6 peeled garlic cloves, 1 tsp of pimento seeds, 1/2 of your fresh thyme, 2 spring onions, black pepper, ground nutmeg, sugar, salt, apple cider vinegar, juice of the lime, 2 chopped scotch bonnet peppers, soy sauce or browning sauce, and 50ml water. This is your marinade.
In another bowl, sprinkle your jerk seasoning over the chicken and rub it in. Then add your paste and massage it all together making sure all the meat is fully covered. Marinate overnight.
Wash the kidney beans and soak in a bowl overnight.
Once the chicken has been marinated and kidneys have been soaked preheat the oven 180°C/ 356°F.
Roast the chicken for 45 minutes.

Meanwhile, boil the kidney beans and whack in the salt, pepper, 1 tsp of pimento peas, 2 spring onions, 1/2 your thyme, 4 peeled garlic cloves, coconut milk, chopped onion and creamed coconut. Then add your washed rice (make sure there is enough water to cook the rice) and 1 whole scotch bonnet pepper then cook for 20 minutes until the rice is fluffy.
In another pan, fill it with vegetable oil and cook up some plantain. When frying you’re looking for a golden brown colour.
Finally, toss the rice into a dish with the chicken and fried plantain then dig into this delicious dish! Enjoy!

name: Easy Pork Belly Ramen
description: This might just be both the easiest and tastiest ramen you’ll ever make. As it turns out, a big pat of butter is a shortcut to making your ramen super creamy.
instructions: Slice the pork belly into thin strips.
Combine the sake, soy sauce and sugar in a small bowl with 120ml water.
Heat a splash of oil in a wok set over a high heat. Add the pork belly, turn the heat down to medium and stir fry until crispy and browned, around 5 mins. Then remove from the pan.
Drain the oil then add the sauce. Cook, tossing frequently, until reduced by half then add half of the butter.
Return the pork to the sauce and toss to coat. Stir fry for 1 minute then set aside.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan.
Roughly chop the garlic and ginger and transfer to a blender. Add the remaining butter, white miso paste and a ladleful of the hot dashi. Blitz until smooth.
Add the remaining dashi and blitz again. This is your broth, which you can heat up as needed.
Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil. Cook your eggs for 6 mins, then plunge into ice cold water to stop the cooking process. Once cooled, peel and halve.
Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil. Cook your noodles according to the package instructions then drain.
Finally, thinly slice the spring onions.
To assemble, divide the noodles between the serving bowls. Add the pork, eggs, spring onions and extra toppings of your choosing. Ladle the hot broth over the top, then serve and enjoy.

name: Easy Pulled Pork Sandwich
description: This pulled pork sandwich recipe from Ruben Dawnay (of Ruben's Reubens) is big, beautiful, and perfect for an alfresco dinner party.
instructions: Combine all of your dry rub ingredients and mix well. This will make more than you need, store the excess in an airtight container in your spice cupboard!
Place your pork onto a baking tray and sprinkle generously with 5-6 tbsp of the rub until covered on all sides. Leave to sit for an hour or so to allow the rub to adhere.
Place a large, deep pot (ideally cast iron) with a lid into the oven. Whack your oven on full blast (250°C).
Once heated, remove the pot, pour in a splash of oil and add the pork shoulder. Return to the oven for 10 mins to form a bark
Take the pork out of the oven again, pour the beer around it, cover with a lid and return to the oven. Turn down to 150°C and leave for 4 hours.

While your pork is cooking you can knock up a quick slaw. Use a peeler to get long ribbons of carrot. Thinly slice your cabbage and onion. Combine in a colander and add sugar, salt and vinegar. Leave over a bowl to drain.
After an hour, transfer the veg to a large bowl and add the mayonnaise.
When the pork has had four hours, remove it from the oven. Using two forks, pull the pork and give it a mix. Taste and season with more rub if necessary!
Toast your ciabatta, slice in half, pile in your pulled pork, top with some slaw and, if you like, your favourite condiment.

name: Easy Red Velvet Cake
description: A beautiful dense, rich red velvet cake with cream cheese frosting and a subtle hint of chocolate. It’s America’s favourite cake for a reason.
keywords: Lily Vanilli red velvet cake recipe
red velvet cake with cream cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease and line two 18cm round cake tins.

Use an electric whisk to beat together the butter and sugar for about 4 mins until light and fluffy, starting on a medium speed and increasing to high speed. The mixture should be pale and increased in volume. Add the eggs gradually, then the food colouring, and beat until just incorporated.

In a separate bowl, sift together the flour and cocoa. Add half the flour mix to the butter and sugar mix and beat until evenly incorporated, then add the other half and beat until combined. Beat in the buttermilk.

In a small bowl, using a clean spatula or teaspoon, mix together the bicarbonate of soda and cider vinegar (it will fizz up) and fold it immediately into the cake batter – don't use the electric whisk, just fold it in with a spatula by hand.

Divide the mixture between the two prepared cake tins and level out to the edges. Bake for 20–25 mins, or until a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out clean. Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tins for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely.

Meanwhile, make the cream cheese frosting: use an electric whisk to beat the butter in a mixing bowl for 4–5 mins, then add the drained cream cheese and beat for another 2 mins. Sift in the icing sugar and add the vanilla and beat for another 2 mins, until smooth and evenly incorporated. (You can add more icing sugar for a firmer frosting if desired.)
To assemble the cake, spread the cream cheese frosting over one sponge and pop the other on top, sandwiching them together. Spread another layer of cream cheese frosting over the top.

name: Easy Spicy Chicken Pasta
description: This flavourful, spicy chicken pasta is about to be slotted straight into your weekly rotation. If you like spice (and chicken) then you’re guaranteed to like this simple pasta dish. It’s got all the flavour you could ever want or need.
instructions: Cut the chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces. Scrape into a bowl and season well with salt and pepper.
On a separate, clean board, cut the cherry tomatoes in half.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large, deep frying pan set over a high heat. Once hot, fry the chicken pieces for 3-4 mins, tossing every now and again until caramelised. Use a slotted spoon to transfer to a clean bowl.

Add the cherry tomatoes to the pan and fry for a minute before adding the chilli flakes and sun-dried tomato paste. Cook for a minute, then pour in the white wine. Bubble for a minute, then add the chicken back to the pan along with the double cream. Season with salt and pepper and bubble for 5 mins.
Cook the tagliatelle in a large pan of salted, boiling water following pack instructions until al dente. Once cooked, use tongs to transfer the pasta straight into the pan with the sauce.
Finely grate in the Parmesan and toss everything together, adding a splash of pasta cooking water if it needs it.
Tear three quarters of the parsley leaves into the pasta and toss again. Divide between bowls and top with a few more parsley leaves.

name: Easy Sponge Cake
description: There are lots of vanilla Victoria sponge recipes out there but this might just be our favourite. We’ve sandwiched it with buttercream and jam but you could also whack it in a boozy trifle.
keywords: best ever vanilla sponge cake recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease and line two 20cm cake tins.

Sift the flour into a bowl. Add the sugar, salt and baking powder and whisk together. Use an electric whisk to beat in the butter until it is incorporated and the mixture appears to be evenly coated and looks like a fine crumble mix – 2–3 mins on medium speed.

Add the eggs and beat, first on medium, then on high, just until incorporated. Add the milk and vanilla and beat, on medium and then on high, for about 2-3 mins until the mixture is smooth and combined; it will appear a bit lighter in colour.
Divide the mixture between the two prepared cake tins and level out to the edges. Bake in the oven for 25–30 mins, or until a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tins for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely.
Spread a generous layer of buttercream on one sponge and a layer of jam on the other, then sandwich the two together. Dust over some icing sugar and enjoy!

name: Easy Sun-Dried Tomato & Harissa Farfalle
description: This quick and easy pasta sauce is made with just 4 ingredients and comes together in no time. It's creamy, tomatoey and a little bit spicy.
instructions: Add the butterbeans plus their liquid to a high speed blender, along with the sun-dried tomatoes, 1 tbsp of oil from the jar and 1-3 tbsp of harissa, depending on how spicy you would like it to be. Blend until smooth and season well with salt and pepper.
Cook your pasta to al dente. Save a mug of pasta water before you drain the pasta. Put the pasta back into the saucepan it was cooked in.
Pour the sauce into the pan with the pasta to heat through on a low heat. Add the reserved pasta water, bit by bit, until you have a perfectly silky sauce.
To serve, dish the pasta onto two plates and serve with some extra slices of sun-dried tomato on top.

name: Easy Tomato, Anchovy & Olive Galette
description: A lovely savoury galette that's perfect for sharing on a long weekend with your mates.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C.
Slice the tomatoes into roughly 1cm thick slices and lay them out on a baking sheet (we’ll use the same baking sheet to cook the galette on later).
Sprinkle over the vinegar and a good pinch of salt. Place into the oven for 10 mins (this will just par cook them gently to remove a little moisture).
While the tomatoes cook, make the pastry. Cube the butter and add to a food processor along with the flour and ½ tsp of salt. Blitz into a breadcrumb consistency.
In a small bowl, whisk the 2 eggs. Set aside a tbsp of the egg mixture and add the rest to the food processor and whizz again until a soft dough forms. If it’s too dry, add ½ tsp of cold water.
Tip the dough out, press into a disk and wrap with clingfilm. Pop it into the fridge to chill for 20 mins.

After 10 mins, remove the tomatoes from the oven and set aside. While the pastry chills, prep the rest of the toppings. Grate the cheese, pick the thyme leaves, drain the anchovies and finely slice the red onion.
Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured circle into a disk about 30cm in diameter and the thickness of a pound coin.
Transfer the pastry to a sheet of baking parchment.
Add the grated cheese to the centre, leaving a 5cm gap around the edge. Follow with the thyme leaves, then the tomatoes, anchovies, olives and onion.
Fold the exposed 5cm edge in over fillings to make the crust (it doesn't have to be neat) and brush with the egg you set aside earlier. A pastry brush is ideal for this but your finger will work too!
Slide the galette, on the parchment, onto the baking tray and into the oven for 40 mins until golden, turning after 20 mins.
Remove and allow to rest for 20 mins before eating. Serve with a fresh green salad.

name: Edamame Hummus & Quinoa Bowl
description: A fresh and punchy bowl loaded with creamy edamame hummus, jammy eggs and herby quinoa. Healthy, zesty, and a properly satisfying meal prep lunch for the week.
instructions: Cook the eggs in a small saucepan of boiling water for 7 mins, until jammy in the centre. Drain and cool under cold running water until easy to peel.
Boil the peas and edamame in salted water according to pack instructions. Drain and run under cold water to stop the cooking.
Zest and juice the lemons. Peel the garlic.
Add half of the edamame and peas to a food processor along with the cottage cheese, tahini, lemon zest and juice, garlic and water. Season with salt and black pepper, then blitz until super smooth.

Warm the quinoa following pack instructions, or use cold if you prefer. Tip it into a bowl with the remaining edamame and peas. Finely chop most of the mint and stir it through the quinoa. Season well with salt and pepper.

To serve, spread the hummus into Tupperware containers. Spoon the quinoa salad on top, then halve the eggs and place them on top too. Crumble over the feta and finish with the reserved mint leaves. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Edamame Hummus & Quinoa Bowl
description: A fresh and punchy bowl loaded with creamy edamame hummus, jammy eggs and herby quinoa. Healthy, zesty, and properly satisfying.
instructions: Cook the eggs in a small saucepan of boiling water for 7 mins, until jammy in the centre. Drain and cool under cold running water until easy to peel.
Boil the peas and edamame in salted water according to pack instructions. Drain and run under cold water to stop the cooking.
Zest and juice the lemons. Peel the garlic.
Add half of the edamame and peas to a food processor along with the cottage cheese, tahini, lemon zest and juice, garlic and water. Season with salt and black pepper, then blitz until super smooth.

Warm the quinoa following pack instructions, or use cold if you prefer. Tip it into a bowl with the remaining edamame and peas. Finely chop most of the mint and stir it through the quinoa. Season well with salt and pepper.
To serve, spread the hummus over your plates. Spoon the quinoa salad on top, then halve the eggs and place on each bowl. Crumble over the feta and finish with the reserved mint leaves.

name: Egg & Cheese Breakfast Quesadillas
description: The perfect batch breakfast. Super quick, packed with protein and easily customisable: mix it up with some extra crispy bacon, kimchi or really anything you have lying around. Just make sure you serve with hot sauce.
instructions: Crack the eggs into a large mixing bowl and whisk together with a good pinch of salt.

Melt the butter in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Once foaming, pour in the eggs. Using a rubber spatula, continuously move the eggs around from the edge into the centre until you have small curds forming. Remove from the heat and continue to cook the eggs in the residual heat of the pan until they are quite dry – further than you would normally take them for regular scrambled eggs.
Add the cream cheese to the pan and mix through. This will moisten the eggs and really help when reheating. Set aside and leave to cool slightly.

Now let’s build the quesadillas. Lay out the flour tortillas and sprinkle the grated mozzarella evenly over each one. Top with some of the egg mixture then fold the wrap in half. Pop them folded up into an airtight container, stacking them on top of each other (or wrap them up individually in clingfilm) and store in the fridge for up to 4 days.

If you’re adding any optional extras to the quesadillas (crispy cooked bacon, diced kimchi or thinly sliced spring onion), just pull the quesadillas open before cooking and add the additional ingredients.

When you’re ready to eat, place a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Once warm, add the quesadilla and cook for 2 mins on each side, until nicely browned and the cheese is melted. Cover in hot sauce and serve with a wedge of lime. Enjoy.

name: Egg & Cress Sandwich
description: A step up from your meal deal egg and cress, we’ve created this ultimate egg mayo sando with a peppery, garlicky and cheesy watercress pesto!
instructions: Start by boiling the eggs. Bring a pot of water to a boil and gently lower in the eggs. Cook for 8 mins – we are looking for the yolk to be set but still slightly jammy. When they are cooked, drain and cool them under some cold water. When the eggs are cool enough to handle, peel them.

Roughly cut the Parmesan into chunks. Get your watercress into a blender with the garlic, lemon zest, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Throw in your Parmesan chunks and 1 tbsp of olive oil. Blend until combined but still a bit chunky. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Finely chop the chives. Halve one egg lengthways, setting aside one of the halves for assembly. Add the rest of the eggs (that’s three and a half of them) to a bowl and mash them up. Add in the mayo, Dijon, chives and a squeeze of lemon juice and mix well, seasoning with salt and pepper.

Spread half of your pesto on one slice of the bread. Top it with the halved egg, cut-side down, then encase the egg with your egg mayo mixture. Add the rest of your pesto again and top it with the other slice of bread before wrapping up and cutting in half.

name: Egg Avocado Crunch Wrap
description: This is a high-protein breakfast that hits the spots. Plenty of healthy fats and plenty of flavour.
instructions: Start by grating the cheese on the coarse side of a grater, cutting the avo into thin slices, finely chopping the chilli (de-seeding if you like!) and dicing the tomato. Finley chop the coriander, stalks and all and set aside.

Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat with a fork to break up the yolks. Set a non-stick pan over a medium heat and add 2 tsp of olive oil. Tip in the eggs and cook, stirring constantly until they are just about set. Season with salt and pep, sprinkle in the cheese, remove from the heat and allow the residual heat to finish the cooking.

Lay your wrap out on a chopping board and add the avo slices to the centre. Season with salt and sprinkle over the chilli. Add a layer of tortilla chips in a circle around the avocado, then add the eggs, tomato and coriander. Pop the second wrap on top and fold the first wrap over and around it, tucking it around at each edge so it's sealed and none of the fillings will fall out.
Wipe out the pan and place the wrap, seam side down and toast over a medium heat on both sides until brown and crunchy. Serve with lime wedges and hot sauce.

name: Egg Fried Quinoa Bowl
description: A high protein, high fibre quinoa bowl that's perfect for a post-workout meal. Plus, it tastes amazing. There's no downside to this meal prep-friendly recipe.
instructions: Cook the quinoa according to package instructions. Five minutes before the end of the cooking time, add the edamame. Drain and set aside.
Grate your garlic and ginger. Dice your tofu, cut your broccoli into small florets, and roughly chop your coriander.
In a bowl, toss the diced tofu with olive oil, salt, and white pepper. Air fry at 200°C for 10 minutes until crispy.
Heat a little oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the broccoli and cook for a few minutes until starting to char.
Add the garlic and ginger, cooking for another minute, then pour in the soy sauce and water. Simmer until reduced.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan and crack in the eggs. Stir to scramble until just cooked through.
Mix in the quinoa and edamame, stirring everything together.
Plate up and top with crispy tofu, sriracha, coriander, and sesame seeds, if using.

name: Egg, Crispy Chilli and Coconut Porridge
description: A very delicious savoury porridge made with Rude Health Coconut Drink. Topped with crispy spring onions, crispy chilli oil and a fried egg.
instructions: Slice the ginger and crush with the back of a knife. Then roughly chop it up. Crush the spring onion whites with the back of a knife and roughly chop them up. Add them to a pot with the oats and Rude Health Coconut Drink. Cook on a low heat for 15 mins until the porridge is thick and cooked.
Meanwhile, finely chop the rest of the spring onions and coriander.
Finish with the shaoxing wine and soy sauce.

Thinly slice the garlic cloves and add them to a pan with some olive oil. Cook on a very low heat until just started to turn golden. Crack in the eggs and cook until the whites are crispy but the yolk is still soft.
Pour your porridge into a bowl and place your crispy egg on top.
Then sprinkle your crispy onions, chilli oil, spring onions and coriander on top. Drizzle over some sesame oil. Break open the egg yolk, mix it all together and enjoy.

name: Eggs Benedict With Jalapeño Hollandaise
description: This is what would happen if a McMuffin got an upgrade. Charred sausage patty, a perfectly fried egg and jalapeño hollandaise. A quirky take on a classic.
instructions: First, start the hollandaise sauce. Melt the butter in a small frying pan and cook, swirling the pan occasionally, until it's foamy and smells nutty. Remove from the heat and strain into a tall container to separate the milk solids (you can discard the solids). Set aside to cool slightly – if it’s too hot, the yolks will scramble. Heat an oven to a low heat.

Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander and half the pickled jalapeñ​​os. Finely slice the green jalapeños and red chillies. Score the sausage casing open and squeeze the meat into a bowl. Add the chopped pickled jalapeños, season well and give it a mix with your hands. Form into four equal-sized patties and set aside.

Heat a pan over a medium heat and add 1 tbsp olive oil. Once hot, add the sausage patties, squash down with a spatula and cook for 2 mins on each side (you might need to do this in two batches). Once charred and juicy, add a cheese slice on top, then transfer to the oven.
Put the sliced green jalapeños, red chilli, coriander and remaining pickled jalapeños into a bowl and mix to combine.

Back to the hollandaise! Put the egg yolks, 2 tsp cold water, 45ml pickled jalapeñ​​o liquor and a pinch of salt into a jug. Whizz until smooth using an immersion blender, then slowly pour the melted butter into the jug, whizzing with the stick blender to emulsify. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat, then crack in the eggs – I like to use a greased cookie cutter to make sure the egg is the same size as the muffin, but you don’t have to. Cook for 5 mins, or until set, basting with oil. Remove from the pan.

Meanwhile, halve and toast the muffins. Divide the cheesy sausage patties between muffin halves, topping each patty with a fried egg and a generous spoonful of hollandaise. Garnish with the remaining chopped jalapeños and coriander.

name: Eggs, Charred Broccoli & Garlicky Quinoa
description: Jammy eggs, chilli oil and charred tenderstem broccoli come together in a deeply savoury, satisfying bowl that works perfectly as a desk lunch. The flavours are rich and comforting without feeling heavy, plus it's great for making ahead to take to work.
keywords: charred broccoli & eggs with garlicky quinoa
instructions: Fill a kettle and boil it. Pour the boiling water into a saucepan and bring it back to the boil. Gently lower in the eggs, turn the heat down to a simmer and cook for 7 mins, until the yolks are jammy. Transfer to a bowl of ice-cold water to cool completely, then peel.

Meanwhile, quarter the Tenderstem. Place a large frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, chuck in the broccoli and cook for 3-4 mins until vibrant green and starting to char. Tip in the quinoa, sesame oil, garlic purée, spinach and half the sesame seeds. Stir for 2-3 mins, until everything is fragrant and the spinach has wilted.
Take the pan off the heat and stir through the soy sauce and chilli oil. Taste and season with salt, if needed.
Halve the eggs. Share the quinoa between lunchboxes, top with the eggs and finish with the remaining sesame seeds.

name: Eggy Guacamole Crumpets
description: Eggy crumpets - once you try them you'll never go back. Guacamole topping is sublime here.
instructions: Guac first. Grab a bowl. Add peeled avocados, chopped spring onions, a chopped red chilli, a chopped handful of coriander and the juice of a lime. Add a splash of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Mash everything together.
Crack 6 eggs into a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Dunk in your crumpets, squeezing them so they absorb the egg. Leave in the egg mixture for 2 minutes so it is properly absorbed.
Heat a pan with some olive oil. Fry the eggy crumpets for 4 minutes on each side.
Serve the crumpets with a big dollop of guacamole on top. Add some hot sauce, grate over some parmesan and tuck in!

name: El Pastor Smacos with Hot Pineapple Salsa
description: This might just be my favourite smaco yet. Charred pineapple salsa and smoky chipotle pork, the perfect balance of sweet and spicy. Don't skimp the chipotle paste, grabbing the best you can find really makes the difference.
keywords: El Pastor Smacos with Hot Pineapple Salsa
El Pastor Smacos with Hot Pineapple Salsa recipe
instructions: Smoosh the pork mince together with the chipotle paste, salt and pepper. Heat the grill to high.

Cut the pineapple into chunks, add to a baking tray and grill for 10 mins, until charred. Meanwhile, finely dice the red onion, finely slice the jalapeños and finely chop most of the coriander, saving a few leaves to serve. Once the pineapple has cooled, tip it into a bowl with the red onion, jalapeños and chopped coriander, then squeeze in the juice of half the limes and season with salt and pepper.
Finely slice the cabbage, add to a bowl with the juice of the remaining limes and season with salt.

Smoosh the pork onto the tortillas. Heat a glug of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the smacos pork-side down for 4-6 mins, until golden and cooked through, then flip and cook for 1-2 mins more.
Top with the cabbage, pineapple salsa and hot sauce. Garnish with the remaining coriander, if you fancy.

name: Emergency Gyoza Soup
description: When all you need is a quick and satisfying meal, don’t settle for anything less than gyoza soup.
ingredients: Crispy Chilli Oil (to taste, to serve, optional)
instructions: Bring 500ml water to a boil over a medium heat. Boil your frozen gyoza in the water for 2 mins (1 min less than the stated cooking time).
Meanwhile, add the soy sauce, balsamic vinegar, crispy chilli oil to a mixing bowl, crumble in the stock cube and give it a mix.
Finely slice your spring onions. Crack the egg into a separate bowl and give it a whisk.
Strain out the cooked gyoza from the pot of water and set aside. Add the ingredients in the mixing bowl to the cooking water (this will form the base of your soup).
Reduce the heat to low and drizzle in the egg to form thin wispy strands of egg, stirring continuously as you go.
Add the gyoza back in. Divide between bowls and top with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds and drizzle with extra crispy chilli oil, if desired.

name: Escovitch Cod & Chips
description: Experience island vibes with Twerk'N'Jerk's Jamaican-inspired fish and chips. Crispy fish fillets, seasoned fries, and zesty Caribbean flavours in every bite.
instructions: Set aside 2 tbsp of flour. In a large, roomy bowl, mix the remaining flour with the cornstarch and baking powder. Season lightly with a tiny pinch of salt and pepper.

Using a fork to whisk continuously, add the beer and the sparkling water to the flour mixture and continue mixing until you have a thick, smooth batter. Place the batter in the fridge to rest for 30 mins to 1 hour.

To make the escovitch topping place water, white vinegar and pimento seed in a saucepan and heat until boiling. Meanwhile slice you onion, carrot and ½ scotch bonnet pepper (without seeds). Once water and vinegar is boiling add sliced ingredients and boil for a further 2 mins. Remove from heat and leave to rest.
Then cut the potatoes into a little less than ½-inch-thick slices, then slice these into ½-inch-wide chips. Place the chips into a colander and rinse under cold running water.
Place the washed chips into a pan of cold water. Bring to a gentle boil and simmer for 3 to 4 mins.
Drain carefully through a colander, then dry with paper towels. Keep in the fridge covered with paper towels until needed.
Meanwhile, lay the fish fillets on a paper towel and pat dry. Season lightly with a little sea salt.

Heat the oil to 180°C in a deep-fat fryer or large, deep saucepan. Cook the chips a few handfuls at a time in the oil for about 2 mins. Do not brown them. Once the chips are slightly cooked, remove them from the oil and drain. Keep to one side.
Place the 2 tbsp of flour reserved from the batter mix into a shallow bowl. Toss each fish fillet in the flour and shake off any excess.
Dip into the batter, coating the entire fillet.

Check that the oil temperature is still 180°C. Carefully lower each fillet into the hot oil. Fry for approximately 8 mins, or until the batter is crisp and golden, turning the fillets from time to time with a large slotted spoon.
Meanwhile, chop up your fresh parsley and set it aside.
Once cooked, remove the fillets from the hot oil and drain on paper towels. Sprinkle with salt. Cover with parchment paper and keep hot.
Heat the oil to 200°C, then cook the chips until golden and crisp, or about 5 minutes. Remove from the oil and drain. Season with salt.
Serve immediately with the hot fish. Add tartar sauce and escovitch topping to fish and garnish with chopped parsley.

name: Espresso Martini
description: Who doesn’t love an espresso martini? Booze + coffee = perfection. Shaken, not stirred.
instructions: Pour all of the ingredients into a cocktail shaker with a big handful of ice. Shake really well.
Line two martini glasses up and pour the mixture through a small fine sieve into each of the glasses. Top with coffee beans to serve.

name: Espresso Martini Brownies
description: Your favourite cocktail in brownie form. A gooey, chocolatey, caffeine hit with the creamiest mascarpone topping, using wonderful Dr. Oetker ingredients.
keywords: The best espresso martini brownies recipes
instructions: Heat oven to 160°C.
Line a square cake tin with butter and baking paper.
Roughly chop your Dr. Oetker Dark Chocolate.
Set a heatproof bowl over a saucepan filled with boiling water. Add your chocolate and butter, then gently melt. Set aside to cool slightly.
Add your instant espresso powder to a bowl, then pour in half of your coffee liqueur and 1 tbsp boiling water. Give it a mix, then set aside to cool.
Add the sugar and ⁴⁄₅ of the eggs to a bowl and whisk them with an electric beater until light and mousse-y.
Gently fold in the chocolate mixture until it is mostly combined.
Sift in your plain flour, cocoa powder and baking powder. Gently fold it in. Add your cooled coffee and vanilla extract and give it one last mix.

Separate the yolk of the remaining egg (you can freeze the whites for later use). Add your mascarpone to a bowl along with the egg yolk, 2 tbsp sugar and your remaining coffee liqueur. Whisk to combine.
Pour your batter into your prepared baking tin. Pour your mascarpone mixture over the top, then swirl slightly with a palette knife. Top with the coffee beans. Bake for 30 mins.
Allow to cool totally, then cut into squares and serve.

name: Espresso and Chocolate Mousse
description: This dreamy espresso and chocolate mousse is easy enough for a weeknight treat but decadent enough for any dinner party.
instructions: Melt the chocolate over a bain-marie on low heat. Stir constantly so it doesn’t burn, using a wooden or plastic spoon.
Blend the tofu in a blender until fully liquidised.
Allow the chocolate to cool slightly, then add it to the tofu and blend again to fully combine, scraping down the sides.
Add the agave, milk and coffee and blend again. Taste for sweetness and add more sweetener if you like.
Pour the mix into ramekins or small glasses and refrigerate for at least 30 mins.
To serve, top with your favourite fruit (I've gone for raspberries) a squeeze of agave and some shaved chocolate.

name: Eton Mess Ice Cream
description: The only thing more perfect for a summer’s day than Eton Mess? Eton Mess ice cream. You are going to love this rich vanilla ice cream with mixed berry coulis and crushed meringues.
instructions: Pour the milk into a pan, add the vanilla pod and bring slowly up to scalding point – do not let it reach the boil. Cover the surface with clingfilm to prevent a skin forming, then leave to cool and infuse with the vanilla for approximately 1 hour. Once cool, carefully remove the vanilla pod from the pan and scrape out the seeds into the milk.

Meanwhile, make the berry coulis: place all the ingredients in a medium-sized heavy-bottomed pan and bring to the boil over a gentle heat, stirring continuously. Reduce to a simmer and heat for 15 mins, or until thickened (add a splash more water if it needs it). Allow to cool, then transfer the coulis to a liquidiser or use a hand blender to purée. Finally pass it through a sieve, pushing through as much of the pulp as possible and discarding any seeds.
Tip a bag of ice cubes into the sink and place a large wide metal bowl on top, to chill the bowl. Alternatively place a metal bowl in the freezer.
In a bowl, beat together the egg yolks and sugar until thick and fluffy – approximately 4 mins. Pour in the vanilla milk and stir until you get a thin custard.

Pour the mixture into a clean heavy-bottomed pan, place over a medium heat and stir continuously with a wooden spoon as you slowly bring it nearly to the boil. When the custard has thickened and the foam bubbles on the surface have disappeared, remove it from the heat, whisk it for a couple of mins with a large balloon whisk (this will help it to cool quicker), then pour into your cold, dry metal bowl.
Leave it to cool for approximately 10 mins, stirring occasionally to prevent a skin forming.

If churning in an ice cream maker: turn on your ice cream maker and crush the meringues. Once the mixture has cooled, stir in the cream, churn in the ice cream maker for 15 mins. Stir through the mixed berry coulis and the crushed meringues, then churn for another 15-20 mins. Transfer to an ice cream container and place in the freezer to set completely.

If churning by hand: once the mixture is cool, put it into the fridge for 1-2 hours. Remove, stir in the cream and transfer to an ice cream container. Pop it in the freezer for half an hour (meanwhile, crush the meringues) then give it a churn with a spoon and stir through the mixed berry coulis and crushed meringues. Return to the freezer to set completely.

name: Everything Bagel Seasoning
description: The classic New York bagel seasoning, ready to sprinkle on just about anything! You can throw this on bagels (obviously) or scones or even a slice of toast.
instructions: Mix everything together in a bowl and transfer to an airtight container.

name: Everything But The Bagel Smoked Salmon Quinoa Bowl
description: Seasoned with an addictive everything bagel-inspired seasoning, this smoked salmon quinoa bowl is packed with healthy fats and flavour.
keywords: Everything But The Bagel Smoked Salmon Quinoa Bowl
Everything But The Bagel Smoked Salmon Quinoa Bowl recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the chives and parsley, then transfer to a bowl. Set aside.
Combine the poppy seeds, soured cream, zest of half a lemon and a squeeze of juice in another bowl, to make a dressing. Season with salt and pepper.

Pick the dill fronds. Chop the cucumber and thinly slice the red onion. Dice or tear the smoked salmon into bite-sized chunks. Add everything to another bowl with the juice of a lemon, then stir the sesame seeds through and add a drizzle of olive oil. Toss together with the capers.
Reheat the quinoa and toss through the chive and parsley mixture.
Share the quinoa between plates. Top with the smoked salmon salad and drizzle over the lemon poppy seed dressing.

name: Everything Cottage Cheese & Lox Bagel
description: Everything bagel seasoning is everyone's favourite, so we’ve added it into cottage cheese as an easy and tasty high-protein cream cheese substitute. The perfect way to break your fast.
keywords: Everything Cottage Cheese & Lox Bagel recipe
instructions: Halve and toast the bagel.

Place a small frying pan onto medium heat. Add the both sesame seeds and toast until golden and starting to pop. Tip into a bowl, add the garlic granules, poppy seeds and stir the cottage cheese through. Season with salt, set aside.
Trim and thinly slice the red onion. Place into a strainer and wash under cold running water until crispy.
Place the bagel, cut-side up. Spoon over the everything bagel cottage cheese on both sides, top with smoked salmon, red onion, and capers.

name: Everything Salmon
description: As you might be able to guess from the title, this everything-bagel-seasoned salmon has it all. If you're after something healthy, delicious and easy to make, this is your guy.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C. Place a small baking tray in there to preheat.
Mix your poppy seeds, sesame seeds, garlic powder, onion powder and salt in a bowl. Give it all a mix.
Pat your salmon fillets dry, and place them on a board skin side down. Press your everything seasoning mix all over the salmon flesh (avoiding the skin).
Remove your hot baking sheet from the oven, and place a piece of baking parchment on it. Pop your salmon fillets skin side down on top, then drizzle on a little olive oil, and bake them for 7 mins.
Turn your grill up to high. Blast your salmon under the grill for 2 mins until the top has turned a little golden.
Serve your salmon with your base and dressing of choice.

name: Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas
description: Another day, another batch recipe. This one pairs a Mob favourite, our everything-bagel salmon with herby, zingy chickpeas. It's protein packed and perfect for powering more meals throughout the week.
keywords: everything salmon and green pesto chickpeas
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Mix all the everything seed mix ingredients together in a bowl.
Pat the salmon fillets dry, then press the flesh side of each fillet into the seed mix, coating all sides except the skin.
Drain the chickpeas, reserving the chickpea liquid. Using a vegetable peeler, peel half of the zest of the lemon.

Add the chickpeas and lemon zest into a baking tray, and stir the pesto through, adding a splash of the reserved chickpea liquid, until saucy. Place the salmon on top, seedy side up and transfer to the oven until cooked through, 7-10 mins (if you salmon fillets are thick, it will take a little longer).

Once the salmon is cooked to your liking, taste and season the chickpeas with some salt, pepper, or lemon juice - you're done! Leave to cool before storing.The cooked salmon will keep in the fridge for 3–4 days and in the freezer for up to 3 months (defrost in the fridge overnight and reheat gently in a low oven or flake it cold into dishes to avoid drying out).Eating it now? For a quick meal, enjoy with a fresh side salad, roasted veg, or rice.

name: Everything Salmon Hummus Bowl
description: When has hummus not made things better? This dish uses it to take your Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas leftovers up a notch, topped off with a crisp, juicy tomato salad. So good.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas batch recipe.
Reheat the salmon in the oven, microwave or a frying pan until piping hot.

To make the hummus, add your leftover chickpeas to a blender or food processor along with the tahini, ice cubes, water, olive oil and juice of half the lemon. Blend until smooth, adding more water if needed to loosen. Taste and season with salt.
Finely grate the garlic into a large bowl. Squeeze over the remaining half of the lemon and season with salt and black pepper.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes into 2cm chunks and thinly slice the spring onions. Add them all to the bowl with the garlic and lemon, drizzle over a little olive oil and toss to coat.
Toast the flatbreads until warm and golden. Spread the hummus over the base of your plate or bowl. Top with the hot salmon and the salad. Serve with the flatbreads on the side.

name: Everything Salmon Pesto Sandwich
description: Leftover salmon just got exciting. With our delicious creamy tahini dressing this sandwich takes your Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas batch to the next level.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas batch recipe.
Whisk the tahini and cold water together in a bowl until smooth and pourable. Taste and season with salt and black pepper. If it’s a little bitter for you, stir in a touch of honey or sugar.
Flake the salmon and stir it into the tahini dressing along with the pesto chickpeas. Tear in the basil leaves and mix everything together.
Toast the bread until golden.
Pile the pesto salmon chickpea mixture onto the toast, add the rocket and sandwich it all together.

name: Everything Salmon Rice Bowl
description: As you might be able to guess from the title, this everything bagel-seasoned salmon rice bowl has it all. If you're after a meal that's ideal for prepping ahead, nutritious, and delicious, this is the one.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C. Place a small baking tray in there to preheat.
Mix your poppy seeds, sesame seeds, garlic powder, onion powder and salt in a bowl. Give it all a mix.

Prep your salad. Smack your baby cucumbers with the side of a knife, then cut them into small chunks. Get them in a sieve set over a bowl, and sprinkle over a little salt. Leave them to sit whilst you prep the rest.

Finely slice your pickles and your spring onions. Finely chop your dill too. Get these in a bowl with your rice and quinoa, and your salted cucumber. Crumble in your feta and give it a good mix. Season with the juice of ½ your lemon and a little salt.
