Pat your salmon fillets dry, and place them on a board skin side down. Press your everything seasoning mix all over the salmon flesh (avoiding the skin).
Remove your hot baking sheet from the oven, and place a piece of baking parchment on it. Pop your salmon fillets skin side down on top, then drizzle on a little olive oil, and bake them for 7 mins.
Turn your grill up to high. Blast your salmon under the grill for 2 mins until the top has turned a little golden.

Spoon your salad into your Tupperware containers, then top with your salmon, a dollop of soured yoghurt and nestle in a little wedge of lemon. Box up and pop in the fridge ready for your when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Everything Salmon Rice Bowl
description: As you might be able to guess from the title, this everything bagel-seasoned salmon rice bowl has it all. If you're after something healthy, delicious and easy to make, this is your guy.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C. Place a small baking tray in there to preheat.
Mix your poppy seeds, sesame seeds, garlic powder, onion powder and salt in a bowl. Give it all a mix.

Prep your salad. Smack your baby cucumbers with the side of a knife, then cut them into small chunks. Get them in a sieve set over a bowl, and sprinkle over a little salt. Leave them to sit whilst you prep the rest.

Finely slice your pickles and your spring onions. Finely chop your dill too. Get these in a bowl with your cooked rice and quinoa, and your salted cucumber. Crumble in your feta and give it a good mix. Season with the juice of ½ your lemon and a little salt.
Pat your salmon fillets dry, and place them on a board skin side down. Press your everything seasoning mix all over the salmon flesh (avoiding the skin).
Remove your hot baking sheet from the oven, and place a piece of baking parchment on it. Pop your salmon fillets skin side down on top, then drizzle on a little olive oil, and bake them for 7 mins.
Turn your grill up to high. Blast your salmon under the grill for 2 mins until the top has turned a little golden.
Spoon your salad into bowls, then top with your salmon and a dollop of yoghurt. Serve with a little wedge of lemon.

name: Everything Salmon, Garlicky Rice & Balsamic Tomato Salad
description: Vibrant garlicky green rice, juicy balsamic tomatoes and flaked salmon from leftover Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas batch. It’s nutritious, speedy and most importantly delicious.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas batch recipe.
Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear, then drain well.
Add the spinach, water, garlic and butter to a blender and blitz until smooth.
Tip the rice into a medium-sized saucepan and pour over the green mixture. Bring to the boil, then cover with a lid and turn the heat down as low as it goes. Cook for 12 mins.

Turn off the heat and leave to stand, covered for 10 mins. Remove the lid and fluff up the rice with a fork, some of the spinach may sit on top, so just stir it back through. Cover again and leave for another 5 mins. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.

Meanwhile, pour the balsamic vinegar into a bowl and slowly whisk in the olive oil to make a dressing. Season with salt and pepper. Chop the tomatoes into 2cm chunks, then toss them through the dressing along with the pesto chickpeas.

name: Everything-But-The-Bagel Smoked Salmon Salad
description: All the best bits of a salmon bagel in salad form. Creamy, herby, crunchy, and zingy, with an everything bagel cream cheese twist.
instructions: Whisk the cream cheese and water in a bowl until light and fluffy. Stir in the poppy seeds, sesame seeds, and onion granules. Season with a pinch of salt and set aside.

Using a mandolin or sharp knife, finely slice the fennel, cucumber, and red onion. Pick the dill fronds and discard the stalks. If you want, chuck them all into a bowl of ice water while you prep the rest – it makes everything extra crispy. Tear the salmon into bite-sized chunks.
Zest a quarter of the lemon into a bowl, squeeze in the juice and slowly whisk in the olive oil until emulsified. Season with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of sugar. Taste as you go.
Drain the veg if using ice water. Toss it all together with the rocket, capers, torn-up salmon, and croutons until coated in the dressing.
Swipe a generous dollop of your whipped cream cheese onto plates and top each the salad.

name: Everything-Seasoned Salmon with Spiced Cauliflower & Bulgur
description: Roasted turmeric cauliflower and fluffy tomato bulgur, topped with crispy-skinned salmon crusted in a bold “everything bagel” spice blend. Finished with a balsamic drizzle for zing. It's a winner for meal prep.
keywords: Everything-Seasoned Salmon with Spiced Cauliflower & Bulgur
Everything-Seasoned Salmon with Spiced Cauliflower & Bulgur recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C fan.

Make the bulgur base: Pour water and olive oil into a saucepan. Stir in the tomato purée and pomegranate molasses. Season with salt and bring to the boil. Once boiling, stir in bulgur wheat. Return to the boil, cover, and turn the heat to low. Simmer for 10 mins until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork, then stir through the juice of the lemon. Taste and season again if needed.
In a bowl, mix the poppy seeds, white sesame seeds, black sesame seeds, garlic powder, onion powder, and a pinch of salt.
Pat the salmon fillets dry with kitchen paper. Press the flesh side only into the seasoning mix to coat evenly. Set aside.

Cut the cauliflower into rough florets. Peel the red onions and cut into chunky wedges. Tip the cauliflower and onion into a large roasting tray with unpeeled garlic cloves. Sprinkle over the turmeric, ground coriander, and season generously. Drizzle with olive oil and toss everything to coat. Roast for 20 mins.
Remove the tray from the oven. Nestle the salmon fillets in, skin-side down. Drizzle with a little olive oil and return to the oven for 10–15 mins, or until the salmon is cooked through and flaky.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl or jar, mix olive oil with balsamic vinegar to taste. Season with salt and pepper.

Divide the bulgur into containers. Top with the roasted cauliflower, onions, and garlic. Place a salmon fillet on top of each. Serve with the balsamic dressing drizzled over, or pack it separately if storing.

name: Extra Herby Chickpea Fatteh
description: Our fresh twist on fattet hummus. Toasty flatbreads, spiced chickpeas, creamy yoghurt-tahini, and crunchy nuts — this is proper comforting but full of punchy herbs.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.
Drain the chickpeas, reserving the chickpea liquid.

Tear the flatbreads into 2–3cm bite-sized chunks and tip onto a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt, then toast in the oven for 7–10 mins until golden and crisp. Toss through the Lebanese 7-spice and set aside.
Finely chop the dill, parsley and coriander (including stalks). Peel and finely mince the garlic. Add the paprika to a heatproof bowl.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the olive oil for the topping. Stir through the nuts and toast for 2–3 mins until golden. Tip the hot oil and nuts into the paprika bowl, stir well and leave to cool slightly.

Put the pan back over the heat with a small drizzle of olive oil. Add the garlic and fry for 1–2 mins until just turning golden. Stir in the chopped herbs and cook for another minute until just wilted.
Add the chickpeas and the reserved liquid to the pan. Season with salt and pepper, then cook until everything is hot and glossy.
Meanwhile, mix the yoghurt, tahini and the juice of half the lemon in a bowl. Season to taste.
To serve, divide the herby chickpeas between bowls, spoon over the yoghurt-tahini sauce, then drizzle with the paprika-spiced nuts and oil. Scatter over the crispy flatbreads to finish.

name: Fajita Fried Rice
description: This is an extra special vegan mushroom fajita rice you can whip up for a delicious weeknight dinner. It's a corker.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Combine the spices in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas and add 1 Tbsp of the fajita spice mix and a glug of oil. Toss to coat and bake until crispy and caramelised. This will take around 15 mins.
To make your spicy mayo, combine the vegan mayo with one finely grated garlic clove, a pinch of chopped coriander, 1 tsp of the spice mix and the juice of a lime. Give it a mix.
Dice up your onion, finely chop the coriander stems and roughly chop the mushrooms.
Preheat a wok over a high heat. Add the mushrooms and the remaining fajita spice mix. Cook until crispy, roughly 10 mins, then remove from the wok.
Preheat the wok again and add the onion with a splash of oil. Add the leftover rice and stir fry for 5 mins. Add the mushrooms and coriander stalks. Toss together and season to taste.
Divide between warm bowls and top with a dollop of your spicy mayo, crispy chickpeas and extra lime juice and coriander.

name: Fakeaway Zinger Burger
description: Our ridiculously crispy chicken burger, delicately spiced and sandwiched between soft brioche buns. Seriously finger-licking good.
instructions: For the marinade, combine the Greek yoghurt, smoked paprika, 2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tsp chilli powder, 2 tsps Italian herb mix, mustard, 1 tbsp sriracha, 1 tsp salt and the eggs in a bowl. Mix well until smooth then add in your chicken thighs and allow to marinate for at least 30 mins in the fridge.
Combine the plain flour, 2 tsp chilli powder, 2 tsp Italian herb mix, 2 tsp garlic powder and 3 tsp salt in a large bowl.
Combine the mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar and 2 tbsp sriracha in a small bowl.
Shred the lettuce and slice the tomatoes.
Heat up a big pot with enough vegetable oil to deep fry the chicken thighs.

Lift the chicken out of the marinade and shake off the excess mixture. Put it into the flour mix and press it to coat it. Press and scrunch the chicken into the flour at least 4 times so it will be well coated and has lots of craggy bits; this is what makes it extra crispy.
Deep fry the chicken for 5-6 mins until golden brown and cooked through. You can check it is cooked by checking with a meat thermometer - it should be 75°C.
Allow the chicken to drain in a metal sieve or colander. This will prevent the bottom from becoming soggy.
Toast the buns on a hot dry pan. Spread 1 tbsp of the spicy mayo on the bun before adding a layer of lettuce, tomatoes, the fried chicken and finally a slice of cheese. Close the burger and enjoy.

name: Family Meal Spaghetti
description: This recipe is straight out of The Bear. It’s the perfect recipe for the centre of the table.
instructions: Smash and peel your garlic cloves and add to a pot with roughly 100ml of olive oil. Chuck in the basil stems plus a handful of leaves, saving some for later. Place the pan over medium heat and let it lazily simmer for 1-2 mins. Turn off the heat and allow the mixture to steep while your start your sauce.

Add your butter to a large saucepan, place over a medium heat to melt. Meanwhile, halve your onion and add it, cut-side down, to the pan. As the butter starts to brown, the onion will begin to caramelise.
Add the tomatoes to the pan, breaking them down with a wooden spoon. Bring to a boil, add salt and pepper, pop a lid on and simmer for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, add your steeped oil mixture to a food processor and pulse until the garlic and basil are finely chopped. Set aside.
Bring a large pan of water to a rolling boil, season generously with salt.

When the sauce has simmered away, add the garlic and basil oil and stir until thoroughly mixed. Continue simmering for another 10 mins or so, until the sauce has thickened. Remove and discard the onion halves.
Drop your spaghetti into the boiling water and cook for 8-9 mins until al dente.
Toss through cooked spaghetti with a splash of pasta water until the pasta is beautifully coated. Serve family style topped with a handful of parmesan and extra basil leaves.

name: Fancy Summer Roast Chicken Dinner
description: No matter the season, I love a roast. This one has it all, my clotted cream Jersey Royals roast potatoes, a silky spinach, pea and butter bean purée, and a whole chicken roasted in white wine until the skin is crisp and golden. Make it once, then try out the remix recipes to use up every last bit of the leftovers.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Halve the lemons and break the garlic bulb into cloves. Stuff the cavity of the chicken with the rosemary, lemon halves and garlic. Pour the white wine into the cavity, then place the chicken breast-side down in a deep roasting tray. Pour the chicken stock into the bottom of the tray, drizzle the skin with olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper. Then cover the tray entirely with foil, making sure to seal the sides so no air escapes when the chicken is cooking. Roast for 45 mins.

Remove from the oven and carefully peel off the foil lid. Gently turn the chicken onto its back and baste thoroughly. Return to the oven for a further 15-20 mins, until the skin is crisp and golden and the thickest part of the thigh reaches 75°C. Remove from the oven and leave to rest.

While the chicken roasts, parboil the Jersey Royals in a large saucepan of salted water for 15-20 mins, until fork tender. Drain and transfer straight into a roasting tray with the clotted cream and a generous pinch of salt. Toss until the cream has melted and coated the potatoes. Once the chicken comes out to rest, increase the oven to 200°C and slide the potatoes in. Roast for 40 mins, turn, then roast for a further 20 mins until golden. Finish with an extra pinch of salt before serving.

Set aside a handful (around 100g) of the cooked Jersey Royals for the purée. Peel and mince the garlic. Add the spinach, peas, butter beans, the reserved potatoes, the single cream and the minced garlic to a blender. Blend until smooth, adding a splash of chicken stock if needed to loosen. Season well with salt and pepper, then stir through the salted butter.

Serve the chicken with the Jersey Royals and a generous spoonful of the purée. Divide the remaining chicken, potatoes and purée into three equal portions and refrigerate — these are your batch bases for the remix recipes.

name: Farinata
description: This simple chickpea pancake is quick to make, packed with fibre and plant protein and keeps really well. Have it as an alternative to bread with soup or salad for lunch or as a snack with your favourite dip.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Grease an ovenproof dish or baking tray with olive oil and place in the hot oven to warm up.
Put the chickpea flour into a large bowl and whisk in the water, followed by the olive oil and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Chop the rosemary and the toppings (cherry tomatoes, red onions or olives all work well).
Remove the hot dish from the oven, pour in the batter and top with the rosemary as well as the olives, onions and/or tomatoes, if using.
Bake for 30 mins until golden then remove from the oven and leave to cool.
Slice and serve!

name: Farinata with Antipasti and Pistachio Pesto
description: Farinata is an Italian savoury pancake made from just chickpea flour, olive oil and water. It makes a perfect base for fresh and roasted veggies or as a side.
instructions: First blend the chickpea flour with 450ml of cold water. Set aside for at least 15 minutes for the flour to absorb the water.

Preheat the oven to 200C. Slice the stem off of the broccoli and peel away the thick outer layer with a peeler. Use the peeler to slice the stem lengthways into ribbons. Then slice a handful of florets. Place on a baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper and roast for 10-12 mins until starting to brown.
Thinly slice the jarred artichokes and sun dried tomatoes.
To make the pesto, add the basil, chopped pistachio, nutritional yeast and 60ml of olive oil to a small food processor. Place into a bowl with a squeeze of lemon and season to taste with salt.
When the farinata mix has rested, add 2 Tbsp of zaatar, 60g of olive oil and 1tbsp of salt and mix it well.

Heat an oven proof saucepan over high heat and 4 tbsp of olive oil. Separate into two portions, in two bowls or pouring jugs. When the oil is hot (test by dropping a little of the chickpea mix - its ready when it sizzles up quickly), Pour half of the mix into the pan very quickly and give it a swish to get it even all around. Leave to cook for 3-4 mins and when the farinata starts to come away from the sides and the top has started to set, put it into the oven and broil for 10 mins, until it starts to crisp up at the sides. Repeat with the remaining half.

When it's finished cooking, carefully place the farinata onto a plate and spread a thin layer of pesto over it. Layer over the broccoli florets and ribbons, sun dried tomatoes, capers and dot over a little more pesto.

name: Fattoush With Creamy Preserved Lemon Dressing
description: A fresh, creamy and tangy salad. Made up of a mix of flavours and ingredients inspired by a combination of Egyptian and Syrian cuisine. A delight.
instructions: To make the dressing, finely chop the preserved lemon and parsley, add into a small bowl with the sour cream, nigella seeds and vinegar. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Into a bowl, add 3 tbsp of olive oil and the sumac, then season with salt. Peel and finely grate the garlic into the oil, then tear the flatbread into small pieces. Toss together until evenly coated. Spread in one even layer onto a baking tray. Bake for 7-10 mins until golden.

Meanwhile, trim and separate the baby gem leaves. Trim and thinly slice the radishes, pick the mint leaves and chop the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks. Thinly slice the spring onions on a bias and place in ice water with the radishes, baby gem leaves and mint to crisp them up.

Before serving, drain the veggies from the ice bath and pat dry or spin using a salad spinner. Add into a bowl with the tomatoes, juice of the lemon, pomegranate molasses and 3 tbsp of olive oil. Season with salt and toss together.
Serve the salad on a large platter or on plates and dollop over the preserved lemon dressing and crispy flatbread croutons.

name: Fennel Sausage & Broccoli Broken Lasagne
description: This one-pot recipe is a lovely tangle of lasagne sheets, sausage ragù, and mozzarella. Yum.
keywords: Fennel Sausage & Broccoli Broken Lasagne recipe
what can I make with lasagne
instructions: Remove the skins from the sausages and add them to a hot pan with a shot of olive oil. Use a spatula or wooden spoon to smash ‘em up, and cook them until nice and crispy.

While the sausages brown, finely chop the onion and fennel bulb and finely mince the garlic. Whip the sausage meat out of the pan and add another shot of oil. Tip in the onion and fennel and cook with a pinch of salt for 5-6 mins.

Add the garlic, chilli and fennel seeds and cook for a minute or two before adding a splash of water to deglaze the pan. Tip in the tomatoes, return the sausage to the sauce and add the chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 mins.
Roughly chop the broccoli and preheat the oven to 190°C.
Nestle the lasagne sheets into the sauce along with the chopped broccoli, leaving a few bits of pasta exposed out of the sauce to go crispy.
Top with torn mozzarella and lots of grated Parmesan cheese. Slide into the oven for 35-40 mins or until bubbling and golden.
Allow to rest for 5 mins before serving.

name: Fennel and Sausage Pappardelle
description: This pasta is incredibly simple and bursting with crispy sausages and juicy tomatoes. Henry from Peckham Cellars shows us how it’s done right.
instructions: Toast fennel seeds over low heat for 1 min until fragrant.
Remove the sausage meat from the skin. Finely chop the shallots, chilli, garlic basil and parsley. Cut the tomatoes lengthways.

Heat a frying pan over medium heat. Add your sausage meat and fry until golden. Add a large glug of olive oil, then add the shallots. Sweat them down for 5 mins until translucent, then add your fennel seeds, sliced chilli and garlic. Cook for 2 mins until fragrant and then add in your thyme.
Add your tomatoes and tomato purée. Season well with salt and pepper, and cook for 5 mins until the tomatoes start to break down.
Pour in your white wine and simmer for 25-30 mins, topping up with boiling water if it dries out.
Bring a pan of heavily salted water to the boil, then cook your pasta for a couple of mins less than the packet tells you to.
Turn your sauce up as your pasta is cooking and add a little pasta water
Add the cold butter to the sauce, then tong in your cooked pasta. Toss so that the pasta is totally coated in a glossy sauce. Season to taste.
Add the parsley and basil and toss one last time to combine. Plate up your pasta, then drizzle with olive oil and a sprinkle of fresh parmesan. Enjoy.

name: Fennel, Sausage and Courgette One-Pot Lasagne
description: I love this one-pot lasagne, and think it covers so many bases — it’s comforting enough to suit autumn/winter eating, but the fennel seeds, courgettes and lemon mean this is summer-ish too. It could be one you serve to family and friends, but is also low-key enough to make it to the mid-week menu too.
instructions: Score the sausages and strip the casings from the meat (discard the casings).  Grate the Parmesan, and then set it aside.

Set a low-sided, 26-28cm casserole or other oven- and hob-proof dish over a medium heat. Add 1 tbsp olive oil and, once warm, the sausagemeat. Use the back of a wooden spoon or similar to push and squash the sausagemeat so that it breaks up into a mince, then cook for 5 mins, stirring only occasionally so some browns.
Lightly bash the fennel seeds to grind them up. Stir them through the sausagemeat and add the water, deglazing the pan if necessary. Simmer for 2 mins, then transfer the mixture to a bowl.
Slice the courgettes into ½cm rounds, finely slice the garlic, strip the leaves from the thyme and finely zest the lemon.

Add the remaining oil to the same dish you used for the sausagemeat, plus the courgettes and a good pinch of salt. Fry for 4-5 mins over a medium-high heat, turning occasionally. It’s fine for the courgettes to colour a little. Reduce the heat to low, add the garlic, thyme, lemon zest and a generous grind of pepper, then cover and cook for 4-5 mins until the courgettes are soft and glossy, but are not mushy.
Return the sausagemeat to the dish, add the crème fraîche and stock, then stir and simmer for 5 mins. Heat the oven to 190°C.

Once the crème fraîche and stock have been simmering for 5 mins, add the lasagne sheets, breaking them in half as you submerge them in the liquid. Cook for 4 mins so the pasta softens, then remove the dish from the heat.

Arrange the lasagne sheets so that they are evenly distributed. Try to make them a little wavy and ruffled, and keep most below the level of the liquid. Cover with mozzarella and Parmesan, then bake in the oven for 15-20 mins until burnished and golden.

name: Fennelly Braised Sausage & Lentils
description: A rustic, warming recipe that you'll immediately want seconds of. Using good quality sausages will make all the difference.
instructions: Preheat a large saucepan over a medium high heat. Add a splash of olive oil and drop in the sausages. Roll them around the hot pan and let them pick up some colour. Once nicely browned, remove from the pan.
Dice the onion, fennel and celery and tip into the hot pan. Cook with a pinch of salt and a few twists of pepper for 5-6 mins. Finely grate the garlic and add to the pan along with the tomato purée.

Tip the sausages back into the pan with the wine, lentils, and tinned chopped tomatoes and water. Bring the whole lot to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and let bubble away for 35-40 mins, or until the sausages are super soft and braise-y and the lentils are tender.
Season with salt and pepper and divide between warm bowls. Finish with chopped parsley, olive oil and grated Parmesan.

name: Festive Espresso Martini
description: A good old fashioned Espresso Martini, with a cinnamon Christmas twist
instructions: Pour your ice, vodka, Kahlúa, and shot of espresso into a cocktail shaker.
Shake until a frost forms on the outside of the shaker (30 seconds to a minute).
Double strain into a chilled martini glass.

Garnish with a dusting of cinnamon. If you’re feeling fancy, hold a lighter under the cinnamon as you sprinkle and watch it cook the cinnamon as it falls to create a beautiful christmassy smell and bouquet for your drink.
Enjoy!

name: Festive Roast Turkey
description: The big day is here. If it's your first time cooking the Christmas or Thanksgiving dinner, we're here to guide you through it with this classic roast turkey recipe.
instructions: Turn the oven to 180°C. To make the spiced butter, tip the butter into a bowl and whisk a little, then add the spices along with a big pinch of salt and pepper. Finely chop the sage leaves and add to the butter then mix well.
Place your turkey into a large baking tray and cover with the spiced butter, making sure that you cover the entirety of the bird.
Cover the entire tray with tin foil and make a kind of tin foil tent. Now place the turkey in the oven.
Cook the turkey for 2 ½ hours, giving it a good baste every 30 mins (this is the most important part – set yourself a timer so you don’t forget).

After 2 ½ hours, remove from the oven and slide a knife between the thigh and the crown – if the juices that run out are clear, set the turkey aside to rest for 15-20 mins. If the juices still run a little pink, slide the turkey back into the oven for another 5-10 mins before resting.

Put some sage and rosemary on a large platter, then carve the turkey and add to the platter. Spoon over any of the butter from the base of the turkey roasting tin. Serve with the remaining lemon half, sliced into wedges.

name: Feta Baked Orzo
description: The Mob orzo bake to end all Mob orzo bakes. Spiked with oregano, salty olives and feta before being topped with fresh, lemony herbs, this one bangs.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Finely slice the onions and garlic and roughly chop the roasted peppers.
Heat a large ovenproof pan over a medium-high heat.
Cook most of the onion, saving a handful, in a glug of oil with a pinch of salt for 8-10 mins until they start to caramelise.
Add the oregano, garlic and chilli flakes and cook for a further couple of mins.
Now add the orzo, chopped tomatoes and peppers. Add the water and a splash of the liquid from the pepper jar.
Season with salt and pepper, crumble in the feta and scatter your olives over the top of the pan.
Bring to a simmer and transfer to the oven for 30-35 mins until cooked through and starting to brown on top.
While the orzo bakes, toss the dill, parsley and remaining sliced onion with a squeeze of lemon.
Top the orzo with the onion and herbs and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve with extra lemon wedges.

name: Feta Egg Salad Tacos with Charred Spring Onions
description: We've put some creamy feta eggs into tacos for the ultimate brekkie, but it’s so versatile, it could go in just about anything.
keywords: Feta Egg Salad Tacos with Charred Spring Onions
Feta Egg Salad Tacos with Charred Spring Onions recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the avocados.

Place a saucepan full of water and bring to the boil. Once boiling, gently drop the eggs in and lower the heat until the water is simmering. Cook the eggs for 6 mins, then transfer to a bowl full of ice water. Once the eggs have cooled to the touch, peel them.
Meanwhile, place a frying pan over a high heat (no oil). Once hot, add the spring onions, drizzle with oil and cook for 3-6 mins until starting to char on both sides. Thinly slice.
Put the feta into a bowl and mash to a paste. Add the eggs with a drizzle of oil. Mash to make a creamy egg salad. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Reheat the tortillas, then top with the egg salad, sliced avocado and some charred spring onions. Finish with a splash of hot sauce and lime juice.

name: Feta Fried Egg & Tomato Rice
description: Crispy fried egg and crumbly feta easily elevate your Greek Tomato Rice Traybake. A midweek winner with basically no effort.
instructions: Make the Greek Tomato Rice Traybake batch recipe.

Place a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, crumble in the feta, cook until it starts sizzling, almost melting 2-3 mins, then crack in the eggs and fry to your doneness. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide the hot rice between bowls, top each with a feta-fried egg, and scatter with dill fronds.

name: Feta Stuffed Jacket Potatoes with Dill Salsa
description: These simple stuffed jackets are a great way to liven up a baked potato. I like to serve them with a lemony tomato and cucumber chopped salad. Jordon x
keywords: Feta stuffed jacket potatoes with dill salsa recipes
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Pop the potatoes into a roasting dish, rub all over with a drop of oil and a pinch of salt and bake for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, make the dill salsa by blending the dill with the juice of half a lemon and a pinch of salt. Stir in a tablespoon of olive oil and set aside.
Prep the stuffing ingredients by roughly chopping the olives, finely chopping the chives and parsley, and adding them to a bowl along with the chilli flakes. Crumble in the feta and set aside.
Once the potatoes have baked, remove them from the oven and cut into halves. Scoop the middle of the potato out into a bowl and put the skins back into the oven to crisp up.
Mash the insides with the milk and a pinch of salt until smooth, then mix with the rest of the stuffing ingredients.
Refill the potato skins, drizzle each with some olive oil and place back into the oven for 10 mins until the tops are turning golden.
Drizzle over the salsa and serve. Great with a simple tomato and cucumber salad.

name: Fettuccine Alfredo with Leeks
description: Silky, buttery leeks work an absolute charm in the classic Alfredo. No cream anywhere near this dish - pasta water does the trick.
instructions: Firstly, cook your fettuccine.

While your pasta is cooking, slice your leeks into discs and add them to a frying pan with 50g knob of butter. Cook these on a medium heat until the leeks are smooth and silky, then remove them from the pan and set aside.

Take 450ml of your pasta water and pour half of it into the same pan you used to cook the leeks. Add your remaining butter and cook on a low heat, whisking together until the butter has melted. Then, add 150g of your parmesan, continuing to whisk until it has a sauce-like consistency.

At this point, add your cooked fettuccine. Toss through the sauce is with some tongs. Keep tossing until it is nice and creamy. At this point, add leeks along with a sprinkling of salt and pepper. Toss everything in, adding splashes of pasta water to keep it loose. Plate it up, sprinkle your remaining parmesan on top and get stuck in.

name: Fiery Chicken-less Noodle Soup
description: This hot and spicy pastina soup is the perfect home remedy for a cold, with scotch bonnet chilli to clear your sinuses and ginger and turmeric to boost your immune system. It’s chicken-less soup for the soul, and the sore throat.
instructions: Peel and finely dice the carrots (you can also coarsely grate them). Bash the ginger and turmeric. Poke a few holes in the scotch bonnet.

Heat the chicken stock, thyme, scotch bonnet, turmeric and ginger in a medium saucepan over a medium heat. Season very generously with freshly cracked black pepper. Let it come to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 mins.
Cook the carrots and pastina in the broth following the pastina packet instructions (about 4-5 mins).
Serve immediately.

name: Fiery Honey Roast Chicken & Garlic Aioli
description: Vinegar is one of the best ways of getting golden chicken and a perfectly balanced pan sauce - the vinegar mellows when roasting, and cuts through the chicken fat. The addition of honey and scotch bonnet turns the sauce into a tangy, spicy glaze that requires absolutely no work from you, since it's all done in the oven.
keywords: Fiery Honey Roasted Chicken & Garlic Aioli
Fiery Honey Roasted Chicken & Garlic Aioli recipe
ingredients: 4 Bone-In Skin On Chicken Leg & Thigh
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Season the chicken with salt and black pepper on all sides and set aside.

Add the honey and ¾ of the vinegar into a high-sided roasting tray and stir together. Halve the garlic bulb and pat the chicken dry, then place both in the tray, chicken skin-side up and garlic cut-side down. Finally add the scotch bonnets in whole. Slide into the oven and roast for 35-40 mins, until cooked through and golden.
When there's 5 mins left for the chicken, baste the legs with the sauce, adding a splash of water if it's evaporated a little too much. Return to the oven for the remainder of the time.
Add the remaining vinegar into a bowl with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper, then whisk to make a dressing, adding more oil if needed.

Once the chicken is cooked, leave to rest for a couple of minutes. Squeeze the garlic cloves into the mayonnaise and mash together. If you like spice, use a fork to mash the scotch bonnet into the chicken juices.

Share the chicken between plates and spoon over the chicken juices and the dressing. Add a dollop of the roasted garlic aioli to each plate and serve with the salad tossed with the dressing and baguette torn into pieces for dunking.

name: Fiery Pineapple Fried Rice
description: A spicy, smoky twist on fried rice. Simply spiced with chipotle paste, plus a touch of sweetness from pineapple.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the garlic and onion. Drain and mince the peppers. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems.

Add a drizzle of oil to a wok or frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the onion and garlic and fry for 2-3 mins until starting to soften. Add the coriander stems, chipotle and pineapple, then stir-fry until fragrant. Add the cooked rice, oyster sauce and peppers, then toss until coated.
In another frying pan, fry the eggs until cooked to your liking.
Spoon the fried rice onto plates and top with the fried egg and coriander leaves.

name: Fire-Roasted Salsa
description: This salsa roja tatemada is a delicious charred arbol chili salsa, and the one salsa recipe you must learn how to make well. This is probably one of the most common and used methods in Mexican cuisine to make spicy salsas. The charred bits on the vegetables add a lot of flavour to it. It was my dad’s preferred way to make salsas, and this recipe was his favourite.
instructions: Peel the onion and garlic. Heat a frying pan over a high heat. Add the tomatoes, onion and garlic clove and cook for about 10 mins until charred, turning the veggies from time to time. Transfer everything to a plate and set aside.

Fill a bowl with boiling water. Add the arbol chillies to the frying pan set over a high heat and fry them just for a few seconds. Transfer the arbol chillies to the bowl of hot water and set aside for 10 mins to rehydrate.
Once the chillies are rehydrated, place them in a blender along with the other pan-fried veggies. Add a generous splash of the water used to rehydrate the chillies.
Blitz using the pulse option. This way the salsa will have a smooth texture, but you will see some bits. If you don't have a pulse option, just blend it very quickly.

Squeeze in the juice of the lime, season to taste and add a splash more water if it needs it. Let the salsa sit for at least 30 mins then serve as a side dish to garnish tacos, eggs or anything you like.

name: Firecracker Beef Rice Bowl
description: A spicy, satisfying beef rice bowl with sweet-savoury sriracha glaze and crisp broccoli.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water 2–3 times until the water runs clear. Add it to a lidded saucepan with the water and a pinch of salt. Set over a medium heat. Once it starts to simmer, cover with the lid, reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 mins. Remove from the heat and leave to steam for 10 mins. Fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, peel and finely slice the onion. Peel the garlic and ginger and grate both into a bowl. Add the sriracha, honey, soy sauce and rice vinegar, and stir to make your sauce.
Thinly slice the red chillies. Trim and finely slice the spring onions.
Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with the oil. Once hot, add the onion and cook for 5-8 mins until softened.
Turn the heat up to high, add the beef mince and cook for 3–4 mins, breaking it up with a wooden spoon until browned.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 2–3 mins until thickened and sticky. Stir in the red chillies and cook for 1 more min.
Add the tenderstem to a heatproof bowl, cover and microwave for 2 mins until just tender.
Divide the rice between bowls. Top with the sticky beef and broccoli, then finish with the spring onion greens.

name: Firecracker Fried Rice
description: Transform any rice leftovers with Justin's fiery fried rice. It's the perfect weeknight dinner shortcut, that gets on the table in under 30 mins.
instructions: Dice the shallot and mince the garlic. Finely slice the spring onion and coriander, then set aside. Slice the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Toast the peanuts in a small pan over a medium heat for 1 min. Crush them using a pestle and mortar, or chop into chunks with a knife on a chopping board.
Heat a large frying pan or wok over a high heat and add two-thirds of the oil. Leave it to heat up for around 1 min, then add the shallots and garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

Add the curry paste and fry for a further minute until the oil turns a reddish hue. Add the chicken, mix to coat with the curry paste and cook for 4-6 mins. Add the rice and mix thoroughly for another 3 mins, breaking up any lumps.

Push the rice to one side, add the remaining oil and crack in the eggs. Scramble the eggs into ribbons. Once the egg is half cooked, mix everything together. Add the sugar, then pour the soy sauce and fish sauce along the sides of the pan. Toss in the coriander and spring onion and stir vigorously for a further minute.
Divide between bowls and top with a wedge of lime and the peanuts. Enjoy!

name: Firecracker Prawn Bánh Mì
description: The bánh mì might just be the greatest sandwich on Earth and this version, packed with sweet and spicy firecracker prawns, is one of the best you'll ever eat.
instructions: Cut your white cabbage and carrots in half. Then, using a mandolin if you have one or knife if you don’t, slice your white cabbage, carrots, and radishes into thin slices.
Lay your radishes on top of each other and cut into matchsticks. Repeat this step with the carrots.
Put your chopped carrots and radishes in a bowl with the juice of a lime. Add salt and mayonnaise and stir well. Set aside in the fridge while you prepare the rest.
Now it’s time to coat your prawns. Mix your panko breadcrumbs with chilli flakes on a plate. Add a layer of mayonnaise on another.
Dip the prawns into the mayo and then into the panko mixture until they are all fully coated
Drizzle with a little oil then put into the air fryer at 200°C for 8 mins.
While your prawns cook, make your firecracker sauce. Grab a small bowl and grate in the garlic and ginger. Then add the buffalo sauce, soy, and rice vinegar.

Once your prawns are crispy and golden, it’s time to assemble the bánh mì. Add a layer of mayonnaise on the inside of the baguette then top it with the slaw, prawns, sauce, and a generous helping of coriander.

name: Fish & Celeriac Stew
description: Charring the celeriac makes it all nutty and caramelised. With the flakey cod, in the rich tomatoey stew, it's a dream.
instructions: Take your cod out of the freezer and de-frost it.
Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Finely slice your onions and whack them on a baking tray with a pinch of salt, pepper, and a drizzle of oil. Place the tray in the oven and roast for 20 minutes.
Dice your celeriac, then heat a glug of oil in a pan and fry it over a low heat.
Slice your garlic and anchovies, and add them to the celeriac along with your fennel seeds and chilli flakes. Fry until golden brown.
Pour in your glass of wine and passata, stir together then bubble down for 5 minutes.
Toss through your chickpeas then keep bubbling for 10 further minutes until the sauce is nice and thick.
Chop the cod into chunks and stir it into the dish. Leave to simmer for 5 minutes for the cod to cook through.
Once the fish is nice and flakey, finely chop up your parsley and scatter into the dish with your roasted onions (saving some of each for garnish). Season and give it a good stir.
Serve up into 4 bowls and garnish with parsley, some roasted onion and a drizzle of oil. Enjoy!

name: Fish Finger Katsu Curry
description: Upgrade the classic freezer staple with this easy crispy fish finger katsu. The mild curry sauce is super comforting and veg-packed making it the great dinner for kids. This will make a little more sauce than you need but will be perfect for the freezer later.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Cook the fish fingers in the oven following pack instructions.
Finely dice the onion and pepper. Finely slice the garlic. Peel and grate the ginger. Peel and grate the carrots. Grate the courgette.
Place a medium saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry the onion, pepper, garlic, ginger, carrot and courgette for 5-6 mins until soft.
Stir in the curry powder and ground turmeric, then sprinkle in the flour. Cook for 1 min, stirring constantly.
Slowly pour in the stock, stirring as you go to avoid lumps. Add the honey, soy sauce and coconut milk. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 10-12 mins until the sauce is smooth and slightly thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the rice following pack instructions. Thinly slice the cucumber.
Use a stick blender to blitz the curry sauce until smooth. Season with a pinch of salt.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Dish out the rice topped with the fish fingers, a generous ladle of curry sauce and the sliced cucumber on the side.
Parent Plate: Do the same and garnish with thinly sliced red onion.

name: Fish Finger Katsu Sandwich
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Fish fingers are an elite comfort food and we’ve whacked them into a sarnie with a spiced mayo for quick and easy katsu-inspired vibes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel and grate the garlic then grate the ginger - no need to peel! Heat oil in a small frying pan over a medium heat and add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 mins, then add the curry powder. Cook for 1 min, then set aside to cool.

Place the fish fingers on a baking tray and cook for 14 mins. In the meantime finely shred the cabbage and spring onion, then peel and finely chop the carrot into matchsticks. Finely chop the coriander. Pop all of the veg and coriander into a bowl and squeeze in the lemon juice. Season with salt, massage for 30 seconds or so and set aside.
Mix the fried ginger and garlic with the zest of a lemon and mayonnaise – season with salt and lemon juice.

Toast the bun halves, then spread with some of the spiced mayonnaise. Top with the fish fingers, then a nice handful of the slaw, spread more mayo on the other side of the roll and press it down on top. Done!

name: Fish Finger Sandwich With Labneh Tartar
description: Vodka is the secret weapon in this fish finger sandwich recipe. You want to make sure your booze is as cold as humanly possible before you make the batter. An ice-cold batter hitting hot oil means super crispy, light fish fingers. Team them up with a light, tangy labneh tartar. Nailed it.
instructions: Start by making your tartar sauce. Get the labneh into a large mixing bowl.
Finely chop the cornichons, shallots and capers and beat into the labneh. Chop the herbs and lob those in too. Finish with plenty of black pepper, salt, lemon zest and juice. Set aside.
Pat your fish dry, remove the skin and cut into fingers.
Whisk together the rice flour, plain flour, baking powder and sugar.
Add the oil to a large saucepan and bring to 190°C.
To finish the batter, gradually whisk the vodka and beer into the dry mix.
Working in batches, dust the fish fingers in a bit of extra rice flour and dunk into the batter. Lift out and let the excess drip off.
Gently lay the fingers into the hot oil, cook for 3-4 mins until golden brown and super crispy.
Drain on kitchen paper and season with plenty of fine sea salt.
Toast the buns and add a dollop of tartar to the top and bottom. Chuck in a couple of fish fingers and a few lettuce leaves. Get stuck in.

name: Fish Finger Tacos with Sweetcorn Salsa & Avocado Smash
description: Crispy fish fingers tucked into soft tacos with zingy sweetcorn salsa, creamy avo smash and a punchy green sauce for the grown-ups.
keywords: fish finger tacos with sweetcorn salsa and avocado smash
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsCook the fish fingers in the oven following pack instructions.

Meanwhile, drain the sweetcorn. Peel and finely chop the red onion. Zest half of one lime and squeeze over a quarter of the juice. Toss everything together and season with salt and pepper — or leave some of the sweetcorn plain for fussy eaters.
Scoop the avocado into a bowl and mash with a quarter of the lime juice. Fold through half of the Greek yoghurt and season to taste.

To make the green sauce for the adults, add the coriander (stems and all, reserving a few leaves for garnish), pickled jalapeños (juice and all) and the remaining yoghurt to a blender. Blitz until smooth.
Warm the tortillas according to pack instructions.

Serve up! Kids Plate: Serve the fish fingers with a warm tortilla, a scoop of the sweetcorn salsa and a dollop of plain yoghurt on the side.Parents Plate: Spread the avocado smash over each tortilla. Top with a fish finger, a spoonful of salsa and a drizzle of the green jalapeño sauce. Scatter with reserved coriander leaves. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

name: Fish Sauce Chilli Chicken Rice Noodles
description: We love the combination of fish sauce, chilli, lime and chicken. We’ve added some light brown sugar here for sweetness but you could swap out for honey instead. The chicken is cooked and then reverse marinated for the ultimate juiciness.
keywords: Fish Sauce Chilli Chicken Rice Noodles
Fish Sauce Chilli Chicken Rice Noodles recipe
instructions: Using a rolling pin or wine bottle satisfyingly bash the cucumber until it begins to break, then cut into rough pieces. Put into a sieve over a bowl and lightly salt.

Finely chop the garlic and chilli, scrape into a bowl. Add the lime juice, fish sauce and brown sugar – stir until the sugar has dissolved – this is your dressing, it should be funky, sour and a little sweet, tip in the cucumbers, set aside.
Lightly season the chicken breasts, put between two pieces of baking paper and bash until roughly 2 cm thickness.
Soak the rice noodles in boiling water according to packet instructions.

Meanwhile, get a large frying or griddle pan over a super high heat. Once visibly hot, oil then lay in the chicken breasts. Cook for 3-4 mins on each side until cooked through and nicely charred. Transfer to a bowl. Pour the smacked cucumber dressing over the chicken and leave to reverse marinate, making sure to spoon some of the garlic and chilli over the chicken.
Finely slice the sugar snap peas. Roughly chop the cashews and coriander (stalks and all).
Drain the noodles, toss through the cucumber, cashews, coriander and sugar snaps.
Divide between two bowls then slice up the chicken and lay on top then pour half the dressing over each and top with toasted sesame seeds if you like, to serve.

name: Fish Sauce Pork Chops
description: These are pork chops like you've never seen before. With tangy fish sauce and refreshing pineapple som tam, you're in for a treat if you make this for dinner.
instructions: Start with the som tam – this can be made in advance (then chilled) up to 3 hrs before serving. Just bring to room temperature for 30 mins before eating.
Chop the pineapple chunks into bite-sized pieces, then chop the cucumber into similar sized pieces. Tip both into a bowl.

Finely chop the garlic and chilli and scrape into a small bowl. Halve and squeeze in the juice of 1 lime and spoon in the fish sauce and sugar. Stir everything together and adjust to your taste – add more lime juice, sugar or fish sauce, if you like. It should be a balance of salty, sweet, sour and funky. Pour over the pineapple and cucumber and mix well. Set aside, or chill if eating later.
Remove any rind from both pork chops, then use a small, sharp knife to lightly score the fat, ½cm deep, in a diagonal pattern along the fat. Season really well.
Slice the ginger, bash the garlic cloves and get all the other ingredients ready to go.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat and drizzle the pork chops with a little oil. Once hot, put the pork chops into the pan, fat-side down, using tongs to hold them upright in the pan. Fry for 1-2 mins until golden and crisping, then lay onto their sides and fry for 2-3 mins (depending on how chunky they are), then flip and cook for another 2-3 mins. Transfer to a plate.

Add the ginger slices and smashed garlic to the pan and toss in the pork fat for 1 min, then pour in the chicken stock, spoon in the sugar and fish sauce, then halve and squeeze in the juice of both limes. Turn the heat to medium and stir and bubble together for 2-4 mins until thickened.

Put the pork chops back into the pan, along with any juices from the plate and toss and turn in the sauce for 1 min until well coated and glazed. Remove the pan from the heat and leave to rest for 5 mins.
Finely chop the peanuts and roughly chop the coriander, then add both to the som tam.

Move the pork chops onto a board and remove the bones, then thickly slice. Divide the som tam between plates, then lay the sliced pork on top. Spoon over the glaze and serve with cooked white rice and extra peanuts and coriander.

name: Five Spice Meatball & Cabbage Soup
description: A chuck-it-all-in soup that cooks straight from frozen. This one's cosy and warming with a real five-spice kick, perfect for weeknights when you're low on energy and want something nourishing and delicious.
instructions: Start by roughly chopping the cabbage. Cut the ginger into thin matchsticks then grate the garlic. Finely chop the chives.
Add the cabbage, meatballs, five spice, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, chives and beef stock to a Tupperware before transferring to the freezer.
Once ready you're ready to cook, transfer the frozen contents of the Tupperware into a saucepan over a medium heat. Cover with a lid and allow to melt before gently simmering for 10 minutes.
Once the meatballs are cooked through, serve up and top with a drizzle of crispy chilli oil.

name: Five Spice Pork Belly with Rice
description: Rich, sticky pork belly spooned over fluffy rice, finished with chilli oil and a crisp coriander-spring onion garnish. Seriously comforting.
instructions: Prep your garnishes. Roughly chop the coriander, then finely slice one spring onion. Add to a bowl of cold water and leave to sit while everything cooks – this’ll make your garnish nice and crisp.
Roughly chop the garlic. Bash the ginger. Cut the ends off of 2/3 spring onions and keep them whole.

Set a large heavy-based saucepan with a lid over a medium-high heat and drizzle in the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the pork belly and sear for 2–3 mins, turning every 30 seconds, until all sides are golden.
Chuck in the chopped garlic, bashed ginger and two whole spring onions. Fry for another minute, stirring often. Sprinkle in the Chinese five-spice powder and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Pour in the beef stock, light brown sugar, light soy sauce and dark soy sauce. Give everything a stir, pop the lid on, and bring it to the boil. Once boiling, lower the heat to a low-medium and leave to gently simmer for 45 mins to 1 hr, until the pork is meltingly tender.
Lift out the aromatics and discard them. Let the pork cool slightly if batch-cooking or freezing before portioning it out.
Meanwhile, cook the rice following pack instructions.

Reheat the pork and gravy over a medium heat. Mix the cornflour with an equal amount of water in a small bowl to make a slurry. Once the gravy is bubbling, turn the heat to low and slowly pour in the slurry, stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Simmer gently until thickened into a glossy gravy – add more slurry if it’s too thin.

To serve, spoon rice into bowls. Ladle over the pork and glossy gravy. Finish each bowl with a sprinkle of sesame seeds, your chilled spring onion and coriander garnish, and a good spoonful of chilli oil.

name: Flaky Cod & Crispy Artichokes with Zingy Mayo
description: Jarred artichokes roasted at high heat until crispy nuggets, it's one of those genius little tricks that transforms a pantry staple. Served with flaky cod, wilted spinach, grains and a sharp lemony mayo. An easy dinner that tastes like you've worked harder than you did.
keywords: Crispy Artichokes & Fish with Zingy Mayo
Crispy Artichokes & Fish with Zingy Mayo recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Drain the artichokes, reserving the oil. Tip them onto a baking tray, drizzle with some of the reserved artichoke oil and toss to coat — the high heat will char them into the crispiest little morsels, perfect for salad. Roast for 15–20 mins, until golden and crispy.
Meanwhile, pat the cod dry and season with salt and black pepper. Finely zest half the lemon into the mayo, squeeze in half the juice, taste and season with salt and black pepper.

Once the artichokes are golden, toss the grains (they'll warm through in the oven) and spinach through the artichokes on the tray, then top with the cod and slide back into the oven for 7–10 mins, until the fish is cooked through.
Divide the grains and artichokes between plates, top with the fish and a dollop of zingy mayo. Serve with the remaining lemon half, cut into wedges.

name: Flaky Cod With Coriander Salsa
description: Cod isn't just for fish and chips. This simple and satisfying high-protein recipe makes the most of cod's mild flavour and flaky texture.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Roughly chop the cauliflower into florets and add to a large roasting tin. Drain and rinse the chickpeas and add to the tray. Drizzle with olive oil and add the ground coriander. Toss well until everything is well coated. Add the garlic bulb to the side in the roasting tray. Roast for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, blitz half of the coriander and mint with the edamame beans. Add the juice of a lemon and 3 tbsp olive oil, loosening with a little water if it’s particularly thick. Set aside.
Remove the veg from the oven, squeeze the garlic from the casing into the tin, then add the juice of a lemon. Roughly chop the remaining herbs and toss through. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Next, heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium high heat. Toast the sesame seeds in the dry pan until golden, setting aside in a small bowl. Then, drizzle the cod fillets in a little olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and add to the pan. Fry for 2-3 mins on each side, or until cooked through and flaking.
Spoon the herby veg onto plates, top with the cod and drizzle with the coriander and mint salsa over the top. Finish with a scattering of toasted sesame seeds to finish.

name: Flaky Salmon with Crisp Apple & Lemongrass Salad
description: A zingy, fragrant salad is the perfect side to rich salmon. I've been making this salad to have with absolutely everything lately, it's so delicious and levels up everything, even eggs. You could swap out the apple for any fruit (pineapple, mango, cucumber, strawberry, tomatoes) and it would be incredible.
keywords: crispy salmon with fresh apple & lemongrass salad
crispy salmon with fresh apple & lemongrass salad recipe
instructions: Pick the mint leaves, discarding the stems. Thinly slice the lemongrass, spring onion and chilli. Core the apples and slice into 1cm thick matchsticks.

Pat the salmon dry and season with salt and pepper. Place a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the salmon skin-side down and cook undisturbed for 5-6 mins, until it's about three-quarters done. Flip the salmon and remove from the heat. Leave in the pan until the salmon is cooked through. If you like yours more well done, place over a medium heat until your desired doneness.
Reheat the rice. Squeeze the lime into a bowl, then stir in the lemongrass, chilli and spring onion together and season to taste with fish sauce. Toss the apple and mint through just before serving.
Share the rice between plates or boxes. Top with the salmon, skin-side up, and serve the apple salad alongside. If making lunch for the next day, flake the salmon and toss through the salad.

name: Flattened Chicken, Rocket Salad & Parmesan Croutons
description: Crispy chicken, pressed down hard in a scorching hot pan until deeply golden, served with crunchy parmesan croutons, peppery rocket and a mustardy yoghurt. A proper weeknight dinner that punches well above its weight.
keywords: Flattened Chicken with Parmesan Croutons recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Tear the sourdough into bite-sized chunks and spread across a lined baking tray. Drizzle generously with olive oil, season with salt and scatter over most of the parmesan. Bake for 10–12 mins until deeply golden and crisp. Set aside to cool.

Meanwhile, flatten out the chicken. To butterfly: place each breast flat on a board and slice horizontally through the middle, stopping just before cutting all the way through, then open out flat. To bash: place between two sheets of baking paper and use a rolling pin or heavy pan to flatten to an even thickness of about 1.5cm. Either works, you're after an even thickness so the chicken cooks quickly and evenly.
Place the chicken in a bowl with the oregano, the zest and juice of the lemon and the olive oil. Season generously with salt and black pepper and toss to coat.

Heat a large heavy-based frying pan over a very high heat until really hot. Remove the chicken from the marinade and place in the pan. Press down with a second heavy pan and cook for 2–3 mins until deeply golden underneath. Flip, replace the weight and cook for a further 2–3 mins until cooked through with no pink remaining. Work in batches if needed, keeping the cooked chicken warm while you finish the rest.
In a small bowl, mix the yoghurt with the mustard and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and stir to combine.
Toss the croutons with the rocket, the lemon juice and extra virgin olive oil. Season well and toss again.
To serve, plate up each chicken breast with a generous spoonful of the mustard yoghurt and a mound of the crouton and rocket salad. Finish with the remaining parmesan grated over the top.

name: Flautas De Pollo
description: Inspired by the beloved Mexican snack. Crispy tortillas, topped with salsa, sour cream, avocado and crumbled feta. Recipe by MOB Contributor Hannah Thorne.
instructions: Char your chillies and tomatoes. Heat a pan to high heat and add your chillies. When they have a nice black char on each side remove them and repeat the process with the tomatoes. This will give your salsa a nice smokey taste and a lot more depth of flavour.
Take the onion and chop it into rough pieces. Leave a small amount for garnish. Grab your clove of garlic and smash it with the back of a knife.

Heat a pan over medium heat and add some oil. Cook the onion and garlic pieces until fragrant. Add in your chillies and tomatoes and stir together. If you want your salsa milder in heat be sure to add the chillies in small doses so you can measure your desired spice level.
Add the bunch of coriander and season with salt and pepper. Pour in enough water to slightly cover the ingredients but not submerge them and let it come to a boil.
Using a wooden spoon, mash the tomatoes and chillies. Then lower the heat to a simmer and leave it to cook for 20 minutes stirring occasionally.

Allow your sauce to cool down completely before using a handheld blender to roughly blitz the sauce in the pot. If the sauce is too thin add it back to the pot and let it simmer until it reaches the desired consistency. Once done, set aside.

In a medium sized pan add your chicken, one half of the onion, and the garlic clove. Fill the pot with enough water to fully cover the ingredients, add a pinch of salt and bring to a boil over medium to high heat. Once it has started to boil, lower the heat to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes.
Time to prepare your garnishes. Thinly slice your lettuce and set aside. Then, in a bowl, smash your avocado and add the juice of 1/2 a lime. Season with salt and pepper.
Take the remaining 1/2 a lime and squeeze the juice into your sour cream.

Time to check the chicken. Once cooked, take your chicken out of the water (reserving the stock left behind) and shred in a bowl. Add 2 tsps of your stock to the shredded chicken and season with salt and pepper.

Flautas time. Take your tortillas and add some of the shredded chicken. Roll the tortillas into a long flute shape and prepare to fry. If you're struggling to keep your flautas in the right shape, you can use toothpicks to hold them in place.
Next heat your oil in a frying pan. Place your flautas in the oil and fry until golden brown. It's important not to overcrowd your pan so you might have to fry in batches.
Assembly time. Plate up your flautas adding the shredded lettuce, lime infused sour cream, smashed avocado, onion slices, crumbled feta and your homemade salsa. Tuck in and enjoy.

name: Flour Tortillas
description: Tortillas de harina, or flour tortillas, are as Mexican as corn tortillas. Very popular in the North of Mexico, where people normally use them to make burritos, these delicious tortillas are perfect for making quesadillas or quesatacos.
instructions: Add the room-temperature butter to a bowl and pour over the hot water. Mix together until the butter has melted and is completely incorporated with the water.
Combine the all-purpose flour, baking powder and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Pour in the mixture of butter and water, a little at a time, mixing well with a spoon until the flour has absorbed all the water and there are no lumps.
Knead the dough for around 10 mins, until it feels soft and bounce back. Cover with a tea towel (to avoid it drying out) and leave to rest for 10 mins.
Once the dough has rested, divide it into pieces 40g each, and roll them out into perfect balls.
Place the dough balls on a baking tray, cover them with a sheet of cling film and a tea towel and leave to rest for another 10 mins.
When you’re ready to roll out the tortillas, heat a dry non-stick frying pan over a medium heat.
Slightly dust the work surface and the rolling pin with the extra flour. Roll a dough ball out as thin as you can, forming a circle.
Cook the flour tortilla in the hot pan for 30 seconds on each side. Flip and cook it for a little longer on each side until it puffs.
Remove it from the heat and wrap in a clean tea towel to keep warm. Repeat the process until all the tortillas are done.
Eat the tortillas immediately, or let them cool then store them in a resealable plastic bag. They’ll keep in the fridge for up to 5 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

name: Flourless Chocolate Cake
description: The flourless chocolate coffee cake has landed. It's all in the technique so follow the method to the letter. Topped with creamy icing and juicy berries.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C/320°F. Grease a 20cm or 23cm springform cake tin with a little butter and line the base with baking paper.

Break the chocolate into a bowl, add the butter. Melt in the microwave in 30 second bursts, or over a saucepan of simmering water (making sure the bottom of the bowl doesn’t touch the water). Once melted stir through the coffee, and set aside.
Next separate the egg whites and yolks between two large bowls. Using an electric whisk, whisk the egg whites until they hold their shape, looking like little soft mountains in the bowl.

Tip the sugar into the bowl with the egg yolks. Without cleaning the beaters (there’s no need) whisk the egg yolks and sugar together until they are super pale, thick and voluminous. Be patient, you want the egg yolks and sugar to treble in size - it will take a good 5 minutes.

Sift the cocoa powder into the whisked egg yolks, add a big pinch of sea salt and scrape in the melted chocolate mixture. Stir together using a large metal spoon or spatula then gently fold in a third of the egg whites to loosen the cake batter, then fold in the rest. The tip here is to be confident in your folding - you want to keep as much air as possible in the cake so make decisive large turns with your spoon. Once the mixture is no longer streaky, carefully spoon into your prepared cake tin.

If using a 20cm cake tin bake for 50 minutes - 1 hour. For a 23cm tin bake for 40- 50 minutes until the cake is just set on top and a skewer comes out clean. Don’t be tempted to open the oven door before then as with no flour in it the cake will deflate
Leave to cool, then serve with berries and something creamy of your choice. We like to pile everything into the middle of the cake. Impressive, and keeps for around 5 days, if it lasts that long.

name: Flourless Chocolate Dinner Party Cake
description: Make this rich, chocolatey gluten-free dessert for your next dinner party.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease and line a 20cm round cake tin. Break the dark chocolate into rough pieces and cut the butter into rough cubes.

Set a heatproof mixing bowl above a slightly smaller saucepan of boiling water over a medium heat (for a bain marie). Add the chocolate, espresso powder (if using) and butter to the bowl and stir until melted. Remove from the heat and set aside to cool to room temp.

Meanwhile, separate the egg whites and yolks into two separate bowls. Add the sugar to the egg yolks and whisk (using an electric whisk if possible) for 5 mins until yellow and creamy, then stir through the vanilla and salt.

In a clean dry bowl, use an electric whisk to beat the egg whites and baking powder together, starting on a low speed and increasing the speed gently until stiff peaks are formed. If working by hand, you may have to whisk for a while longer.

Stir the melted chocolate mixture into the yolk mixture, then sift in the cocoa powder. Stir in a small spoonful of the beaten whites and whisk thoroughly, then very carefully fold in the remaining whites in two parts, until just incorporated. Be careful not to overwork it or you'll knock the air out of the mixture.

Transfer the mixture to your prepared tin, level out to the edges and sprinkle the cacao nibs (if using) on top of the batter. Bake for approximately 25 mins – the middle should wobble slightly when the tin is shaken gently.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tin for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely or serving hot. Dust with the espresso powder before serving, if you like.

name: Flourless Chocolate Hazelnut Cake
description: Imagine if a brownie and a jar of Nutella had a child, and then that child had a massive glow-up. That's what this gluten-free chocolate cake is. Decadent.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Tip the hazelnuts onto a baking tray and slide into the oven to toast for 15-20 mins, they should be golden brown. Set aside to cool completely.

To grease and dust the cake tin: grease a 23cm cake tin with butter, then cut a circle the same size as the base and use it to line the base of the tin. Grease again with butter, then tip in a tbsp or so of cocoa powder and shake it around so all the sides are covered. Tip out the excess.

Cut the butter into 2-3cm cubes and add to a glass bowl. Roughly chop the chocolate and add it to the bowl. Either melt them together in short bursts in the microwave or in a glass bowl over a pan of simmering water. Once silky and smooth, whisk in the cocoa powder and vanilla extract and set aside.
Separate the eggs into two bowls. Use an electric hand whisk to whip egg whites until they stand in soft peaks when you lift the beaters up. Add the caster sugar and whip until thick and glossy.
Move to the bowl of yolks. Add the brown sugar and whip until thick and pale. You don’t need to wash the beaters in between. Add the chocolate mixture to the yolks and stir until combined.

Add a spoonful of the egg white and use the beaters to whip it in, then use a large spoon or spatula to fold in the rest of the egg white, be careful not to knock out too much air out of the mix, you want it to be combined but still voluminous.

Tip ¾ of the hazelnuts into a blender and blitz until floury. Careful not to blend for too long or they’ll start to release oils and become like a butter. You want them to be finely blitzed but not to become oily – I do this by blitzing them in small bursts. Fold the hazelnuts into the chocolate mix, then spoon into the prepared cake tin.
Transfer the cake into the oven for 25 mins, then remove from the oven and set aside for at least 25 mins to sink. The longer you leave it, the easier it’ll be to slice.
When ready to serve, crush the remaining hazelnuts. Slice the cake, then serve each slice with a dollop of crème fraîche and a scattering of crushed hazelnuts.

name: Fluffy Pancakes
description: Our take on the American classic. We’ve used sour cream and a splash of milk in place of buttermilk as it can sometimes be a pain to track down. Ben x
instructions: Sift the dry ingredients into a large bowl.
Melt the butter in the microwave or in a small pan.
Separate the eggs, then beat the yolks into the sour cream, melted butter, and milk.
Fold the yolk mixture into the dry ingredients.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks in a separate bowl and fold into the batter one-third at a time.
Leave the batter to rest in the fridge for 20 mins.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat, add a little butter, and a ladle of pancake batter.
Cook for 2-3 mins on each side and stack up on a plate.

name: Fluffy Ricotta Pancakes With Blueberry Maple Syrup
description: These ricotta pancakes are light and fluffy, with a creamy, custardy middle. They’re delicious with a knob of butter and lots and lots of blueberry maple syrup.
instructions: Zest and juice the lemon.
Pour the milk into a measuring jug. Whisk in the lemon zest and juice and leave to sit.
Place the blueberries and maple syrup in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then turn the heat down to low and simmer for 5 mins. Transfer to a bowl to cool.
Sift the self-raising flour, bicarbonate of soda and 1⁄2 tsp salt into a large mixing bowl.
Separate the eggs and drain the ricotta. Melt the butter in a small pan over a low heat.
Place the egg yolks, sugar, melted butter, vanilla extract and ricotta in a separate mixing bowl. Add the now-curdled milk and whisk until mostly smooth – a few lumps here and there is fine.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry mixture and whisk until just combined.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then, working in three batches, gently fold them into the batter using a large metal spoon.

Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat and grease lightly with butter. Pour in a ladleful of batter and cook until bubbles appear on the top of the pancake and the bottom is golden brown and set, around 2 mins.

name: Fondue Beans with Cornichon Sprinkle
description: There is no wrong time for fondue in life, and this one is the perfect answer for when you want a bowl of comfort. The cornichon and mustard sprinkle is a must,  it cuts through the richness perfectly.
keywords: Fondue Beans with Cornichon Sprinkle recipe
instructions: Place a saucepan over a medium heat and add the lardons. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 mins until golden and the fat has rendered. Tip in the butter beans along with their liquid.
Meanwhile, finely grate the Gruyère. In a small bowl, stir together the white wine and cornflour until smooth.
Pour the wine mixture into the beans and stir through the cheese. Leave to gently simmer over a low heat until smooth and creamy. Add a splash of water if you need it a little looser.
Thinly slice the cornichons and spring onions. Pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the stems. Tip everything into a bowl, stir through the wholegrain mustard and drizzle over the olive oil.
Divide the beans between bowls and top with the cornichon sprinkle.

name: Four Bean Spiced Stew
description: This vegan bean stew takes inspiration from the flavours of Moroccan cooking. A one-pot banger to serve up on cold winter nights using Ocado ingredients.
instructions: Slice your red onions and garlic and chop your ginger and coriander.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large saucepan. Add your cinnamon stick and cook for a minute until fragrant, then add your red onion and fry for 10 minutes until softening and starting to caramelise. Add your garlic and ginger, then cook out for a minute more.

Add your coriander, paprika, turmeric and tomato paste to the onions and give it a good stir, cooking out for 2 minutes until you have a fragrant and jammy mixture. Tip in your tomatoes and vegetable stock and bring to a simmer, then add your runner beans. Turn down the heat to a whisper, pop on a lid and simmer for 20 minutes until your beans are tender.

Tip your chickpeas, haricot beans and kidney beans into the pan and give a good stir. Simmer for 5 minutes until your beans are piping hot. Squeeze in your lemon juice and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Serve up in a bowl over couscous with toasted almonds and your chopped coriander.

name: Four Cheese At Speed Tortelloni
description: We've paired La Famiglia Rana Ricotta & Spinach Tortelloni – made using ingredients that are chopped, not blitzed – with an easy and delicious cheese sauce.
instructions: Fill a large saucepan with water and bring to a boil. Season well with salt.

Grab a sauté pan and tip in the mascarpone with 4 tbsp of water. Set over a low heat to warm. Once melted, crumble in the gorgonzola and grate in 20g of the parmesan. Gently melt over a low heat, adding the zest of your lemon
Roughly chop the rocket. When the sauce is smooth and creamy, drop the tortelloni into the boiling water for 2 mins. Transfer to the sauce along with the rocket and toss to combine.
Divide between warm plates and grate over the remaining parmesan. Dig in.

name: Four Cheese Lasagne
description: Here's our ultimate take on lasagne. We’ve chosen four of our favourite cheeses and combined them with a lemony, green filling to create a showstopper.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Chop the onion and garlic and finely chop the broccoli — stalks and all! Heat a big glug of oil in a large pot over a medium heat and sweat down the onion for about 5 mins before adding the broccoli and garlic along with a big pinch of salt. Continue cooking for around 5 mins, until the broccoli is just starting to colour.
Add the spinach to the pot and wilt — you may need to do this in batches. Once wilted, add lemon juice and zest, then transfer into a colander in the sink whilst you get on with the cheese sauce.

Grate your cheddar and half of the Parmesan. Crumble or tear your Gorgonzola. Then, melt butter in a saucepan and add the flour, cooking it out for 2 mins until it smells nutty. Gradually add in your milk, whisking constantly — this will ensure you get a nice smooth sauce.

Once all of the milk is added, add the bay leaf, mustard and a big pinch of nutmeg. Bubble away for 3-5 mins until thickened, then remove the bay leaf and add in your grated and crumbled cheese. Mix well over a low heat until all the cheese has melted, then taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

Time to assemble! Butter the baking dish. Ladle a couple of spoons of the cheese sauce into the dish and spread evenly. Add a layer of pasta sheets, cutting down if needed to fit snugly. Dot over some of the spinach mixture then continue layering with the cheese sauce and pasta sheets until everything is used up, ending with a layer of cheese sauce. This recipe makes a lasagne with 5 layers of pasta. Top with the mozzarella and grate over the remaining Parmesan. Put the dish onto a tray and bake for 30-40 mins, until golden and bubbly. Allow to cool for about 15 mins before serving.

name: Fragrant & Spicy Pork Bowl
description: Juicy pork mince, a punchy chilli-lime dressing, and herby cabbage. This bowl’s got crunch, heat and tonnes of flavour.
instructions: Thinly slice the bird’s-eye chillies and the shallot. Add both to a bowl with the juice of the limes, fish sauce and sugar. Mix it all together. It should be tangy, slightly sweet and savoury. Set aside.
Pick the mint leaves and discard the stems. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems. Defrost the edamame and chop the cabbage into bite-sized chunks (2–3cm).

Heat a large frying pan or wok over a high heat with no oil. Once hot, chuck in the cabbage, season with salt and cook for 4–6 mins, stirring occasionally, until it’s wilted and starting to char. Tip it onto a plate and set aside.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the water, fish sauce, coriander stems and pork mince to the pan. Season with salt and black pepper, then cook, breaking up the mince as you go, until it’s just cooked through. It should be grey, not browned — that’s how you keep it juicy.
Reheat the rice following pack instructions and divide between bowls.
Stir the cabbage, edamame, dressing and most of the herbs through the pork. Spoon the mixture over the rice, then finish with a scattering of the remaining herbs and any leftover lime wedges.

name: Fragrant Chicken Noodle Soup
description: Light but packed with flavour, this noodle soup uses our gorgeous Poached Chicken & Ginger Broth leftovers and is topped with loads of herbs, beansprouts, and chilli. Inspired by pho, but a little more freestyle.
instructions: Make the Poached Chicken & Ginger Broth.

Bring the leftover chicken broth to just below a simmer in a large saucepan. Stir in the fish sauce, salt and sugar, if using. Taste and tweak, it should be savoury, lightly sweet and properly seasoned.
Warm the poached chicken in the broth for a couple of minutes until hot through, then lift it out and shred.
Cook the noodles following pack instructions. Drain and divide between bowls.
Ladle the hot broth over the noodles, then top each bowl with a portion of shredded chicken.
Thinly slice the spring onions and Thai chillies. Pick the coriander and mint leaves. Slice the limes into wedges.
Scatter the spring onions, beansprouts, coriander, mint and chillies over each bowl. Add a wedge of lime and a good squeeze of sriracha to finish.

name: Fragrant Lemongrass Mushroom Soup
description: This creamy soup is a really beautiful thing. It's packed with lemongrass, ginger and garlic, then topped with crispy mushrooms and an incredible spicy oil.
instructions: Dice up your spring onions, separating the whites and the greens. Cut 300g of your mushrooms into thin slices. Peel and finely dice your potato. Finely chop your lemongrass, ginger and two cloves of your garlic.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a medium sized saucepan. Once melted, add your spring onion whites to the pan and cook over a low-medium heat for 5 mins until they’ve softened.
