Crumble your whole remaining mushrooms into the pan with your hands and turn up the heat. Fry for 10 mins until they have released all of their liquid and started to caramelise.

Add your garlic, ginger and lemongrass, then cook out for 2 mins. Add your potato, coconut milk and vegetable stock to the pan and bring the mixture to a boil. Turn the heat down and simmer for 15 mins.
Pour your mixture into a blender. Blend until totally smooth, then pour back into your pan on the hob. Loosen with water if it needs, then season to taste with salt and pepper.

Whilst your soup cooks, cook your toppings. Heat some oil in a frying pan and add your sliced mushrooms with a pinch of salt. Fry for 5 mins over a high heat until they are caramelised and crispy. Drain on kitchen paper.
Finely slice your remaining clove of garlic.
Heat a good glug of oil to the same pan and chuck in your spring onion greens, chilli flakes and garlic. Fry for 2 mins until crispy and sizzly.
Ladle your soup into bowls and top with your mushrooms and a spoonful of your flavoured oil. Serve up and enjoy.

name: Fragrant Lemongrass Squash Curry
description: An incredibly soothing plant-based curry. Rich with lemongrass, coconut milk, charred squash and tender lentils, this is going to be a new favourite of yours.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Peel your squash, then halve it. Scoop out the seeds, and chop it into 2cm wide half-moons.
Add to a large roasting dish and drizzle with olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Roast your squash for 40 mins until lovely and charred.
Peel and finely chop 4 of the shallots. Finely chop your lemongrass and garlic along with 2 of your red chillies.

Add your shallots to a pestle and mortar and bash to a paste. Throw in your lemongrass, chillies, and garlic one at a time, bashing each till it reaches a paste-like consistency before adding the rest.
Finely chop your coriander stalks.
Heat a large sauté pan over medium heat with a glug of olive oil. Add your shallot paste and cook out for about 5 mins.
Add your coriander stalks and garam masala, then cook out for 2 mins.

Pour your green lentils into a sieve and give them a really good rinse. Pop them into your spice pan, then add 800ml of water and your coconut milk. Bring the mixture to a simmer, and cook for 40 mins.
Meanwhile, finely slice your remaining shallots.
Heat a generous portion of olive oil in a frying pan. Add your shallots and fry for 5 mins until deeply crisp and golden. Remove from the pan with a slotted spoon, then drain on kitchen paper.
Roughly chop your coriander, and finely slice your red chillies. Halve one of your limes, and cut the others into wedges.
Check that your lentils are tender, then add the juice of your lime and a generous pinch of salt. Add your roasted squash to the pan.
Drizzle the top with your remaining coconut milk, crispy shallots, sliced chillies and coriander. Serve with extra lime wedges, and enjoy.

name: Fragrant Pork & Ginger Noodles
description: Think of this as soup dumplings deconstructed. Rich porky broth, shredded ginger, dark soy and black vinegar bring that iconic Xiao Long Bao vibe, but fast-tracked into a spicy, slurpy noodle bowl with juicy pork, soft veg and chewy rice noodles.
instructions: Cook the rice noodles according to packet instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens. Shred the ginger into matchsticks and finely chop the garlic. Chop the pak choi.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a pan. Fry the spring onion whites, garlic and the ginger for 1–2 mins, then add the pork mince. Cook until browned, breaking it up as you go.
Add the dark soy, light soy, black vinegar and chilli oil. Let everything bubble for a minute, then add the chopped pak choi for the final 2 mins to wilt.
Divide the rice noodles between bowls, spoon over the mince, veg and sauce and top with the spring onion greens and extra chilli oil if you like.

name: Fragrant Prawn Malai Curry
description: Rinku Dutt from Raastawala show us how to make her fragrant and delicate prawn malai curry. It's a winner.
instructions: In a mixing bowl, toss the prawns, turmeric and salt. Set aside for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, finely chop your onions.

Once the prawns are marinated, heat a glug of oil in a heavy-based shallow pan. Gently fry the prawns and sauté for 2 mins until they change colour slightly, but aren't yet fully cooked through. Immediately take them off the heat and place in a bowl to the side.
In the same pan, heat another glug of oil and the butter until melted. Add in the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves. Heat for 30 secs until fragrant.
Add your onions along the salt and sugar and cook for 10 mins until they're translucent.
Grate in the ginger and cook for another min.
Pour in the yoghurt and mix well, allow it to cook for 1 min.

Stir the coconut milk to remove any lumps from it before pouring it into your onion mixture along with the coconut cream and cooking for another 3 mins. Once it starts bubbling, lower the heat and add the prawns back in.
Cook for 4 mins until the prawns are fully cooked through. Finish with the garam masala, coriander leaves and some more butter. Turn off the heat, pop on a lid and let it rest for 5 mins.
Just before serving, gently mix in the garam masala and melted butter and serve with basmati rice.

name: Fragrant Prawn and Herb Omelette
description: A soft egg omelette inspired by Vietnamese cafes stuffed with prawns, spring onions and a tonne of herbs. An incredibly light, fresh and moreish dish.
instructions: Start by slicing your chilli, spring onions and cut one of your limes into wedges.

Place your red chillis (saving some for garnish) in a bowl with your peanut butter, sugar, soy sauce, fish sauce, rice vinegar, the juice from your remaining lime and water. Give it all a good mix until you have a smooth sauce. Set aside until later.
Beat your British Lion eggs in a bowl with 2 tbsp water and a generous pinch of salt.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a teaspoon of coconut oil and, once melted, add your prawns. Fry for a minute on one side, then flip over.
Pour your egg mixture into the pan so it forms a thin, even layer. Turn up the heat and cook for a minute, sprinkling in the spring onions as you go.
Tip your omelette onto a plate and open up the middle. Fill it with a handful of coriander, beansprouts, mint and your remaining sliced chillis. Serve up with your dipping sauce and enjoy.

name: Fragrant Quorn Vermicelli Salad
description: A spicy and vibrant crispy Quorn salad, with delicious vermicelli noodles and tangy cucumber. The perfect summer treat.
instructions: Slice your cucumber and sprinkle on ½ tsp salt, set aside for 10 mins.

Peel the skin off one of the limes and bash your lemongrass sticks. After this, blend your lemongrass, 2 red chillis, garlic, shallots, and a lime peel in a food processor with a splash of water. After this is all blitzed up, combine that mixture with your Quorn Mince using your hands.

Toast your rice on a high heat until it's golden brown and toasted. Then, transfer your rice to a mortar and pestle and grind it down until you form a fine crumb. Next, heat up your wok until smoking. Add a large glug of oil to your wok and fry your Quorn Mince mixture for 3-5 mins before adding in 1 tbsp brown sugar and setting that all aside in a separate bowl.
Squeeze the excess water out of your cucumber slices and combine them with the apple cider vinegar and 1 tbsp brown sugar.

Finely chop the coriander stems and spring onions before roughly chopping half of your bunch of coriander leaves and half of your bunch of mint leaves. Then, finely slice 1 red chilli and set this all aside.

Transfer your crispy Quorn Mince to a bowl and add 2 tbsp of your toasted rice powder, along with the remaining half of your coriander and mint leaves. Add a big drizzle of sesame oil and mix that all together nicely.
Combine your coriander stems with the juice of the limes, 3 tsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp sriracha, a pinch of salt and pepper as well as a splash of water in a separate bowl. This will form your dressing.
Cook your vermicelli noodles according to the package instructions.

Pile up the cooked vermicelli noodles in a bowl. Top them with your Quorn Mince mixture, your quick pickled cucumbers, spring onions, coriander, mint, the remains of your toasted rice powder and – finally – your dressing. Mix together and enjoy.

name: Fragrant Tomato & Egg Stir Fry
description: Another recipe inspired by my recent trip to Vietnam, it's a protein-rich, eggy and tomatoey number that I'm completely obsessed with. If you want to keep it veggie, swap the fish sauce for soy but add gradually as the salt levels will differ.
keywords: Fragrant Tomato & Egg Stir Fry recipe
instructions: In a bowl, whisk the eggs together with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Set a medium frying pan over a medium heat. Add a quarter of the butter and let it melt until foamy, then pour in a quarter of the egg mixture. Cook undisturbed for 2 mins until just set, then flip out onto a chopping board. Repeat with the remaining butter and egg mixture, a quarter at a time, until you have four omelettes. Roll each one into a log (like a crepe) and set aside.

Finely grate the ginger and finely chop the garlic and poke the cherry tomatoes with a knife. Add the sesame oil to a large frying pan over a medium heat, then add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 min until fragrant. Add the cherry tomatoes to the pan and crank the heat to high. Cook for a 2-3 mins, then smoosh the tomatoes down with a potato masher or the back of a spoon until saucy. Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, microwave the rice according to packet instructions. Finely chop the chives for garnish.

In a small bowl, whisk together the cornflour, fish sauce and water until smooth (you can use soy sauce instead if you want to keep this veggie). Pour into the tomato sauce and bubble for a couple of minutes until thickened.
Slice the omelette logs into strips, then gently fold them through the tomato sauce to heat through. Serve over the rice and scatter with the chives.

name: Fragrant Tomatoey Rice, Eggs & Chilli Oil
description: Is it a soup? Is it a stew? Well, it's actually very much like congee or jok - both of which are rice based, cooked in water or stock until the grains have broken down and turned into a more porridge-y consistency. It's incredibly comforting, and this one is flavoured with ginger, garlic and roasted tomatoes for a fragrant, easy and veggie midweek meal.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add the cherry tomatoes to a baking tray, toss with olive oil and a pinch of salt and roast for 15 mins, until charred and bursting.
Meanwhile, slice the ginger into matchsticks and finely slice the garlic. Finely slice the spring onions and separate the whites from the greens.

Add the cooked rice, garlic, ginger and spring onion whites to a medium saucepan and pour in the vegetable stock. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10-15 mins, until thickened. Season with the white pepper and soy sauce.

While the rice simmers, bring a separate small saucepan of water to the boil. Carefully lower in the eggs and cook for 7-8 mins, then lift out with a slotted spoon and cool under cold running water. Peel and halve.

Tip most of the tomatoes into the rice and gently stir through, saving a few for the top. Divide between bowls and top with the halved eggs, reserved tomatoes, spring onion greens and a drizzle of chilli oil, if using.

name: Frangipane
description: This creamy tart filling is made with almonds, butter, sugar and eggs. Use it to make our incredible bakewell tarts.
instructions: Use an electric whisk to beat the butter and sugar together for approximately 3 mins until thick and fluffy.
Beat in the ground almonds, then add the eggs one at a time, beating between additions. Finally beat in the flour and the citrus zest.

name: Frangipane Tart
description: A sweet, almondy frangipane tart that really hits the spot. Make your own pastry or use store-bought if you're in a rush.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180˚C fan.
Roll out the shortcrust pastry to an approx 30cm circle about 3mm thick and use it to line a 20cm tart tin, allowing extra to hang over the sides. Chill in the fridge for about 30 mins.

Take a large square of baking paper and scrunch it into a ball then un-scrunch it and press it into the chilled pastry case. Weigh it down with baking beans or rice, making sure they come to the top of the case. Slide into the oven and bake for about 20 mins, or until the pastry is starting to brown.

Meanwhile, make the egg wash by whisking together the egg yolk and milk. Remove the pastry from the oven and carefully remove the baking beans/rice and paper. Brush the pastry all over with the egg wash and bake for another 2 mins to seal. Remove from the oven and allow to cool to room temp.

Meanwhile, make the frangipane. Whisk the eggs in a small bowl. In a separate bowl, use an electric whisk to beat the butter and sugar together for approximately 3 mins until pale and creamy. Beat in the ground almonds, then add the eggs a little at a time, beating between additions. Finally beat in the sifted flour.

Spoon the frangipane into the pastry base then press in the fresh raspberries. Return to the oven to bake for 20–25 mins, or until the frangipane is golden brown. Try to avoid opening the oven before 15 mins have passed, as the delicate structure of the frangipane means it has a tendency to sink. Remove from the oven and place on a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust with icing sugar and serve with some mixed berry coulis and crème fraîche, if you like.

name: French Omelette
description: The best way to cook an egg. A dead simple recipe that everyone needs to master.
instructions: Crack your eggs into a bowl and beat them up with a fork. Finely chop your chives and beat them through the eggs.

Melt ½ the butter in a non-stick frying pan set over a medium heat. Once the butter is bubbling and foaming, pour in the eggs and use a spatula to keep the eggs moving around the pan until just starting to solidify in places, then stop touching them and leave them alone until almost cooked through.
Season generously with sea salt, then use your spatula to roll the omelette up and flip it out onto a plate. Brush with the remaining butter and sprinkle over some extra sea salt.

name: French Onion Giant Couscous Soup
description: This slow-cooked onion and mushroom soup is an absolute flavour bomb, packed with layers of umami and chewy goodness.
keywords: French Onion Giant Couscous Soup recipe
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the onions. Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a pot or deep pan set over a medium heat. Add the onions and cook for 30 mins, stirring frequently.

When the 30 mins is up, stir in the butter (or more olive oil if keeping things vegan) and continue stirring for a further 45 mins. At this point, the onions should have reduced significantly in volume and be super fragrant and dark.
Slice the mushrooms and add them to the pot, stirring for another 20 mins.
Deglaze the pot with the dry white wine and soy sauce. Continue cooking until the liquid has been absorbed by the onions and mushrooms.
Pour in the stock and bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer, add the pearl couscous, and cook for 15 mins. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, slice the spring onions for garnish.
Divide the dish across four bowls and garnish with sliced spring onions, a drizzle of olive oil, and a dash of single cream (or vegan creamer if you prefer).

name: French Onion Ramen
description: French onion soup and ramen are two extremely iconic comforting umami staples. We've combined the two in this warming recipe.
instructions: Remove the tops and bottoms of the onions, then slice in half and remove the skins, setting the skins aside for later. Finely slice all the onions along the grain (this will help keep their shape later), then peel and slice the garlic.

Add the butter, vegetable oil, onions, garlic and 1 tsp salt to a lidded medium-sized pot set over a high heat. Stir until all the butter has melted. Add a lid and reduce the heat to low. Leave to steam for 20 mins, checking and stirring after 10 mins to ensure no burning.
Meanwhile, combine all the stock ingredients plus a pinch of salt in a large jug. Set aside. Cook the noodles following pack instructions, then drain and rinse in cold water. Set aside.

Once the onions have been cooking for 20 mins, pour in the wine and increase the heat to high. Cook for 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until all the liquid has evaporated and the onions have slightly darkened and caramelised. Add all the stock mixture and thyme, then stir well. Lay the reserved onion skins on top of the ramen, put a lid on and reduce the heat to low. Simmer for 10 mins.

Remove the onion skins from the pot and discard. Add 2 tbsp grated cheddar and 2 tbsp lemon juice to the ramen, then mix well. Ladle the onion soup into two serving bowls, then divide the noodles between the bowls, letting them sit on the surface of the soup. Grate over a nest of cheddar cheese, top with the chilled diced raw onions, then carefully add 1 raw egg yolk per person. Finish with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil and, most importantly, a square of chilled butter.

name: French Onion Soup with Comté Grilled Cheese
description: Thinly sliced onions are caramelised with thyme and butter, cooked in beef broth and topped with bubbling cheesy toast. Surely there’s no better winter warmer!
instructions: Peel and slice all of the onions. Place a large saucepan over a medium heat and add 2 tbsp of olive oil and the onions along with a good pinch of salt.
Cook the onions, stirring occasionally, until they have softened and lost a lot of liquid. After about half an hour they should be pale golden and very soft.
Finely slice and add the garlic and the butter and cook for another 5 mins.
Pour in the stock and scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze. Pick the thyme leaves and add them to the pan, simmer for another 10 mins.
Now taste the soup and add salt as needed (check first because your stock might already be salty enough).
Slice your baguette into rounds. Separate the soup into oven-proof bowls, add a few slices of the baguette to each bowl and grate over the comté.
Place under a hot grill until the cheese is melted and golden. Finish with black pepper and serve hot!

name: Fresh & Creamy Nori Noodles
description: Creamy and full of umami, this is a quick and fresh meal you can make in as little as 20 minutes.
instructions: Fill a saucepan with water and bring to the boil. Once boiling, cook the noodles following pack instructions. Once cooked, give them a good wash under cold running water.
Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions. Trim, halve and scoop the seeds out of the cucumber, then slice into 1cm slices. Set aside.

Add the tahini, nori sheet, soy sauce, ice and rice vinegar into a blender. Whizz until creamy and the nori has been fully incorporated into the dressing. Season with salt and a touch of sugar, if too bitter.
Toss the tomatoes, spring onion and cucumber in a bowl with the sesame seeds and sesame oil. Season with salt.
Toss the dressing through the noodles and share between bowls, making sure to spoon over all the dressing. Top with the tomato and cucumber salad.

name: Fresh & Fragrant Shredded Chicken Bowl
description: Inspired by the flavours of a laab, this chicken bowl is a punchy weeknight dinner. A generous amount of fish sauce and lime give its that signature tang.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic. In a saucepan on medium-high heat, add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the garlic and Thai red curry paste, cook for 30 secs. Then add the chicken thighs and stock. Bring to the boil, turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 15-20 mins until the chicken is cooked.

Meanwhile, trim and finely slice the chilli and spring onion. Pick the mint leaves and coriander leaves. Finely slice the coriander stem. Trim the cucumber, halve and slice into thin half moons. Trim the baby gem and separate the leaves.
Transfer the cooked chicken onto a clean board or plate and shred using 2 forks. Keep the poaching liquid on the heat, turn it up to high and reduce by ¾ , 10-15 mins.
Cook the rice according to package directions.

Add the chicken into a large bowl with the poaching liquid, coriander stem, some coriander and mint leaves (reserving a few for garnish), spring onion, chilli and toasted sesame seeds. Season with fish sauce and lime juice. Toss together until evenly mixed.
Share the rice between your bowls. Top with the chicken mixture and serve with cucumber, baby gem leaves, reserved mint, coriander and lime wedges.

name: Fresh Ginger Cake
description: A fiery ginger loaf cake made with olive oil, soaked dates and sticky molasses. It’s sweet, spicy and very moist. It’s a special bake that’s easy to make.
instructions: Prepare a 1lb loaf tin by greasing it with butter and lining with baking paper. Add the dates to a bowl and cover with boiling water. Leave to soak for a minimum of 30 mins or overnight.
Drain the soaked dates then transfer to a blender and blitz into a paste. Measure out 50g of the blended date paste and set aside.
Peel and finely grate the fresh ginger. Heat the oven to fan 150°C.
Add the sugar, molasses, date paste and olive oil to a mixing bowl and use a wooden spoon to mix everything together until no lumps are left – the mixture will split, but don’t worry.
In a separate bowl, mix together the flour, spice mix and salt. Set aside.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the baking soda and the boiling water.

Add the baking soda and water mix to the sugar and date mix. Add the flour mix and grated ginger and crack in the eggs. Whisk together until you have a smooth batter (an electric whisk will make this faster).

Pour the batter into the loaf tin (it should only fill it ⅔ of the way). Bake in the oven for 30-40 mins, until a toothpick inserted comes out clean. Leave to cool for 10 mins in the tin then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Enjoy as is or drizzle over some salted caramel sauce, if you like.

name: Fresh Nam Jim Prawn Noodle Salad
description: All the flavour here comes from the Nam Jim dressing - zingy, fresh and punchy, with lime, fish sauce and coriander blitzed into a dressing you'll want on everything. Tossed through rice noodles with sweet prawns and crispy garlic.
instructions: Add all the nam jim ingredients into a blender and blitz until a smooth dressing forms. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more fish sauce, sugar (optional) or lime juice if needed.
Cook the rice noodles according to packet instructions. Once cooked, transfer to a sieve and run under cold water until cool.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems. Toss both with the prawns, half the crispy fried garlic and a drizzle of olive oil.

Pour three-quarters of the dressing over the noodles and toss together. Serve into bowls, top with the prawn mixture, then drizzle over the remaining dressing. Finish with a scattering of the remaining crispy garlic and serve with the remaining lime, cut into wedges.

name: Fresh Sesame Prawn Toast
description: Iconic flavours you know and love from prawn toast but with a fresh take. Sweet and tender fresh prawns work like a dream on a chewy crisp sourdough toast.
instructions: For the spicy pickle, grate the ginger using a microplane or the fine side of a box grater. Finely slice the chilli. Tip both into a small bowl along with the rice vinegar, honey and a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Divide the spring onions into greens and whites, then slice the green tops into long shreds and drop them into a bowl of ice water. Set aside. Slice the remaining spring onion whites into 3 chunks. Slice the ginger into three pieces ½ cm thick, then briefly massage the ginger between your hands to release its flavour.

Set a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add 2 tbsp oil, the spring onion chunks and the ginger chunks. Cook until they begin to sizzle, then reduce the heat to the lowest setting to slowly caramelise.

Meanwhile, prepare the prawns by slicing each one horizontally (leave the tail intact) and opening the prawn up like a butterfly. Use the back of your knife or your finger to pull out the black string. Pat the prawns dry on kitchen paper, then season with a good sprinkle of salt.

Push the spring onion and ginger chunks to the side of the pan, increase the heat to high, wait until the pan is hot, then add the prawns. Make sure each prawn is in contact with the pan to ensure a lovely char. Leave for 2 mins without touching. Give the pan a quick toss, then immediately remove the prawns to a bowl and turn the heat off. To the prawn bowl, add 1 tbsp of the spicy pickle liquid, the pickled chillies, 1 tbsp mayonnaise, the sesame oil and the soy sauce, then mix well. Set aside.
Spread mayonnaise over a single side of sourdough, then dunk onto a plate of black and white sesame seeds to coat, resulting in a beautiful sesame seed crust.

Remove everything from the pan, bring back to a medium-high heat, then place the plain side of the sourdough down into the pan to soak up all the juices. Toast for 2 mins or until golden, then flip and toast the other side for 2 mins, or until the sesame seeds are lightly golden. Remove onto a serving plate.

Remove the spring onions from the ice water and give them a good shake – they should be lovely and curly. Toss into the prawns with a pinch of salt. Dress the toasts with the prawns and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds. Add 1-2 tbsp mayonnaise to the spicy pickles to create a creamy mixture, then drizzle it all over the dish. Finish with some chilli oil for a vibrant pop and a good squeeze of lemon.

name: Fresh Tomato & Burrata Pasta
description: A seriously simple summer pasta made with a quick fresh tomato sauce and finished with creamy burrata, all on the table in under 30 mins.
instructions: Finely slice the garlic and chilli. Roughly chop the tomatoes into even pieces (you can leave the cherry tomatoes whole), if you're using a mix of varieties and sizes, that's ideal, just make sure the bigger ones are cut down so everything is an even size.

Set a large frying pan over a medium heat and add half the olive oil. Add the garlic and chilli and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant, then tip in all the tomatoes and stir everything together. Season generously with salt and black pepper, then reduce the heat and leave to bubble away for 15 mins, until the tomatoes have broken down into a loose, jammy sauce.
While the sauce is reducing, cook the pasta according to packet instructions. Before draining, reserve a mugful of the pasta cooking water.
Tear the basil leaves into the sauce, then add the drained pasta. Toss everything together, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen and make the sauce glossy.
Divide between bowls, tear half a burrata over each one, drizzle with the remaining extra virgin olive oil and finish with a generous crack of black pepper. Dig in.

name: Fried Breadfruit Balls
description: Crunchy nuggets of soft creamy breadfruit are the star of Juliet Friday Smith's recipe. A Grenada that goes great with breadfruit balls and scotch bonnet jam.
instructions: Fill a large pot with water and set over high heat to boil. Wash and peel the breadfruit using a vegetable peeler. Slice breadfruit into quarters and cut out the core that runs through the middle of the fruit. Cut into large chunks and place into boiling water. Boil for 30 mins until the breadfruit is tender.
While the breadfruit is cooking, finely chop the peppers, garlic, onion, and spinach.

Once the breadfruit has cooked (check if it’s tender with a fork), drain and leave to cool slightly. Place breadfruit into a large bowl and mash with a potato masher until smooth. Add the prepped veg, smoked paprika, curry powder and mix.

Beat the egg with the milk and add to the breadfruit mix bit by bit, combining well. With wet hands, scoop about a heaped tablespoon of the mixture into your hand, and form into balls. Roll the ball in breadcrumbs and set aside on a plate.
Fill a pan halfway with oil and set over medium heat. Once it's reached 160°C, carefully lower a few balls in to fry at a time. Fry for 3-5 minutes until golden brown, turning now and again.
Once crispy and golden, remove and drain on paper towels. Serve with our Scotch Bonnet Chilli Jam!

name: Fried Chicken Burger with Sprout Slaw & Gravy Mayo
description: This crispy fried buttermilk chicken burger with shredded brussels sprouts and chicken gravy mayonnaise is a festive banger.
instructions: Get the chicken thighs in a large mixing bowl and pour over the buttermilk. Transfer to the fridge to soak for 8 hours or overnight.

For the slaw, shred the brussels sprouts and thinly slice the spring onions. Add both to a medium bowl with a generous pinch of salt and the juice of the lemon. Using your hands, scrunch the veggies together for a minute or two to soften them, then add the mustard and ¼ of the mayonnaise and mix well to combine. Set aside.
For the gravy mayo, add the gravy granules to a small bowl. Pour over the boiling water and mix until smooth. Add the remaining mayonnaise and mix to combine.

Fill a heavy-based pan with vegetable oil, about ⅔ of the way up. Set it over a medium heat and bring the oil to 170°C (if you don’t have a thermometer, dip the handle of a wooden spoon in the oil; it’s ready when small bubbles form around the handle).
Meanwhile, in a shallow bowl, mix together the flour, cornflour, sage and paprika with a good amount of salt and pepper. Remove the chicken from the fridge.
Working one at a time, lift a chicken thigh out of the buttermilk and press into the seasoned flour. Scrunch it up until it is well coated and craggy (this will give you those crunchy bits later).

Carefully lower the chicken thighs into the hot oil and cook for 5-6 mins or until golden and crunchy on the outside and cooked through in the middle (the internal temperature should be 70°C). Transfer the chicken to a wire rack to drain any excess oil.
Halve the burger buns then toast them in a hot dry pan set over a medium heat.

To assemble the burgers, spread a generous dollop of gravy mayo on the bottom half of each bun and top with the slaw. Lay the chicken on top, then spread more gravy mayo on the other burger bun half and pop it on the top.

name: Fried Chilli Pork and Green Beans
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad. 

This delicious stir fry is packed with flavour and is so easy to make. I've served it with noodles but it would be just as delicious with rice. Enjoy!
instructions: Finely slice your red chillies. Finely chop your garlic. Take the ends off the green beans, then cut them in half. Cut your spring onions into 4cm lengths.

Heat your wok over a medium heat with a splash of vegetable oil. Add your pork and season with salt. Stir fry for about 5 mins, or until the pork is browned and the liquid has evaporated off. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.
Add your green beans, sliced chilli and spring onions to the same pan and fry for 3 mins, or until softened and charred. Add your garlic to the pan and cook for 30 seconds.
Get your pork back into the pan, along with your soy sauce, sugar and a pinch of white pepper. Pour in the water and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Bring a pan of water to a boil. Cook your noodles according to packet instructions, then drain.
Mix your cornflour with a splash of water to make a slurry then pour this into the pork mixture. Give it a good mix.
Allow the sauce thicken and the flavours to mingle by simmering for 3 mins. Adjust the seasoning if need be.
Toss the noodles through the pork mixture and share between plates.

name: Fried Christmas Pudding & Bay Custard
description: The best way to eat leftover Christmas pudding! Pan-frying slices of leftover Christmas pudding in a bit of butter and brown sugar helps the edges go all chewy and caramelised – and these are so good served with a bay-infused custard.
keywords: Fried Christmas Pudding & Bay Custard recipe
instructions: Start by infusing the milk for the custard. Add the milk, bay leaves and half of the sugar to a heavy-bottomed saucepan and heat until steaming. Remove from the heat and leave to infuse for at least 20 mins (longer is ideal, if you have the time).

To make the custard, heat the milk back up to steaming, then carefully remove the bay leaves. In a separate bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, remaining sugar and cornflour until smooth and slightly lightened in colour. Whisk in around a quarter of the hot milk, followed by the rest. Pour the custard back into the saucepan and place on a very gentle heat and stir continuously with a spatula until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (this is likely to take a good 10 to 15 mins). Pour the custard through a sieve into a jug and then cover the top with cling film to stop a skin forming. Place aside whilst you get on with the fried Christmas pudding.

Place a frying pan on a medium heat. Whilst the pan is heating up, sprinkle the brown sugar over the slices of Christmas pudding. Once the pan is hot, add the butter (it should immediately start to foam) followed by the slices of Christmas pudding. Fry for 2 to 3 mins on each side, until the edges have caramelised.
To serve, pour the custard into shallow bowls then place a slice of fried Christmas pudding in the middle of each bowl.

name: Fried Courgette & Porcini Lasagne
description: A gorgeous courgette lasagne that's great for the flexitarians. Making your own béchamel is more than worth it.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Soak the porcini mushrooms in the boiling water.  Grate the Parmesan, and then set it aside.
Thinly slice the courgettes, transfer to a colander and sprinkle with salt. Leave for 5 mins, then pat dry. Thinly slice the fresh mushrooms.

Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a deep pan or wok over a medium-high heat until a piece of courgette bubbles immediately. Fry the courgette in batches until they turn golden-brown. Remove using a slotted spoon and transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper to absorb any excess oil. Alternatively, you can bake the courgette slices in a single layer in the oven for 10 minutes or until tender.

Pour the milk into a saucepan and warm gently over a low heat. Melt a third of the butter in another pan over a medium heat, then add the flour and mix well. Add the warm milk, first in a thin steady stream, beating all the while with a whisk or wooden spoon until all the milk has been incorporated. Reduce the heat to low and cook the béchamel for 10 mins until thickened and smooth, whisking the mixture every now and then.

Meanwhile, drain the porcini (reserving the liquid) and finely chop them. Whisk the porcini liquid into the béchamel, leaving any sediment behind. Add plenty of freshly grated nutmeg to taste. Keep warm.

Crush the garlic. Add the finely chopped porcini, fresh mushrooms, garlic and olive oil to a frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Cook for 10 minutes until softened and most of the liquid has evaporated. Remove from the heat and add the mushroom mix to the béchamel. Add the cream, salt and black pepper to taste. Bring the mixture to a rapid boil, then turn off the heat.

Butter a 30cm x 20cm gratin dish and cover the bottom with a layer of pasta, then spread over a layer of mushroom béchamel and top with a layer of courgettes. Dot with butter and sprinkle over some of the grated Parmesan. Continue the process making layer after layer, finishing with a final layer of béchamel and a final sprinkling of Parmesan.
Cook in the oven for 30-35 mins until golden brown and bubbling. Serve topped with a little extra Parmesan.

name: Fried Eggs with Brown Butter, Lemon Pilaf
description: When you need dinner fast, eggs deliver. This recipe serves them over lemony brown-butter kale rice with crispy pumpkin seeds for crunch.
keywords: Fried Eggs with Brown Butter Lemon Pilaf
instructions: Add the butter to a frying pan set over a medium heat. Let it melt, then add the pumpkin seeds and cook, stirring occasionally, until the butter is browned, nutty and the seeds are toasted.

Stir the garlic purée and half the crispy onions into the butter. Cook for 20–30 secs until fragrant, then tip in the kale and cook for 2–4 mins until wilted. Add the rice and stir until everything is piping hot. Season with salt, black pepper, lemon zest and juice.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a separate frying pan over a medium-high heat. Crack in the eggs and fry until cooked to your liking. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the rice onto plates and top with the fried eggs. Add a dollop of Greek yoghurt and finish with a lemon wedge and the rest of the crispy onions.

name: Fried Eggs with Yoghurt and Za’atar
description: This super simple breakfast is a bit of a twist on regular fried eggs on toast. The yoghurt is a perfect creamy base for the fragrant fried eggs. Jordon x
keywords: Fried eggs with yoghurt and za'atar recipes
instructions: Lightly toast your bread, and then spread with a generous amount of the Greek yoghurt.
Meanwhile, warm 100ml of olive oil in a non-stick pan and fry the eggs. Season with salt and once they are almost cooked, add the za’atar and chilli to the oil.
Spoon the fragrant oil over the eggs to cook the top, then pop them onto the toast and add another drizzle of the oil.
Finely chop some mint and sprinkle over the top.

name: Fried Feta Eggs with Charred Pea Grains
description: Crispy, golden feta eggs on top of smoky charred peas and grains. This one's a great speedy dinner when you need to get food on the table in under 15 and still feel healthy.
instructions: Defrost the peas and drain off any excess water.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, chuck in the peas and leave them to char for 2-3 mins until smoky and blistered. Add the grains, spinach and half of the pumpkin seeds. Stir through the garlic purée and cook everything together for a few mins, until the spinach has wilted. Season with salt.

Meanwhile, crumble the feta. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in another frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, scatter in the feta, then crack the eggs straight on top. Let them cook for a few mins until the whites are set and the feta is golden and crispy around the edges. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.

Zest the lemon, then cut it into wedges. Then spoon the pea grain mix onto plates. Top with the feta eggs, grate over the lemon zest and finish with a sprinkle of chilli flakes. Serve with a lemon wedge on the side.

name: Fried Halloumi Salad With Fennel, Quinoa & Roasted Garlic Dressing
description: We love halloumi. Salty, squeaky, and great in a salad. We've thrown in some quinoa and fennel for a mega dinner.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. Drizzle the garlic bulbs with a little oil and wrap tightly in foil. Roast for 30-35 mins.

Meanwhile, cook the quinoa according to package instructions. Finely slice the fennel (use a mandoline if you have one), roughly chop the parsley, add the yoghurt, zest and juice of two lemons to a large bowl along with the squeezed out roasted garlic bulbs. Whisk well and season with salt and pepper. Add the cooked quinoa, fennel and parsley before giving it a good stir.

Onto the halloumi. Slice the halloumi into pieces. Heat oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the halloumi, cooking for 4-5 min on each side, until golden. In the meantime, cut the last lemon into wedges. Remove from the pan then serve up a big portion of fennel salad, topping with the halloumi and some lemon wedges!

name: Fried Lemon & Caper Spaghetti with Breadcrumbs
description: I’m a huge fan of cooking with ultra-thin slices of lemon. My storecupboard is never without pasta or capers – they are both star ingredients for me and my cooking.
instructions: Cook the breadcrumbs in ⅓ of the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat for 3-4 mins until golden brown, then set aside on a plate lined with kitchen paper to drain the excess oil.
Finely chop the garlic and very thinly slice half the lemon, removing any pips from the lemon.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta to al dente following pack instructions, then drain.

Meanwhile, cook the capers in the remaining olive oil over a medium-high heat for 45 seconds-1 min until fragrant and crisp, then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds over a medium heat until fragrant. Add the lemon slices and cook for 2-3 mins over a medium-high heat until very soft, even turning golden in patches.
Add the juice from the remaining lemon half, plus the chilli flakes and oregano. Season to taste with salt and a generous amount of black pepper.

Drain the pasta once cooked, reserving a little cooking liquid. Alternatively, use tongs to transfer the pasta directly into the pan with the fried lemons, with some cooking liquid still clinging as you do so. Add a little of the pasta cooking water if the mix looks a little dry, then add plenty of fried breadcrumbs to serve.

name: Fried Pickles With Caper Dill Yoghurt
description: Fried pickles — or frickles — make the tastiest little snacks. Served hot, these crispy morsels pair perfectly with a side of homemade caper dill yoghurt.
instructions: Start by making the dip. Now, if you want a super thick dip, hang the yoghurt for 1-2 hours in a sieve over a bowl in the fridge to thicken the yoghurt. Or you can buy hung yoghurt, or not bother at all, up to you.

Tip the yoghurt into a bowl and add a hefty pinch of salt. Finely chop 2 tbsp of the capers and add to the yoghurt. Add the garlic powder and stir to combine. Finely chop the herbs and get those into the bowl with the zest of the lemon. Cut the lemon into wedges and save for later. Taste the dip for seasoning and adjust with salt and pepper as you like.
Drain the pickles (save the brine) and pat dry. Cut into your desired shape, you can go for long spears or cut into 1cm thick coins.

Set up 3 bowls. In the first bowl, add the flour and 2 tbsp of the cajun seasoning, mix together and add a pinch of salt and pepper. In the second bowl, add the eggs with a splash of brine and a pinch of salt. Beat until smooth. In the third bowl, place the breadcrumbs.
Preheat a pot of vegetable oil (filled no more than ⅔) to 180°C. Pass the pickles through the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs, being very thorough and making sure each is nice and even.
Working in batches, fry the pickles until crispy and golden brown. Season the pickles with salt and the remaining cajun seasoning.
Serve the pickles right away with the yoghurt dip, lemon wedges and crispy capers. Great with a cold beer.

name: Fried Prawn Buñuelos
description: Buñuelos (essentially Spanish fritters) are often made sweet but we've filled them with prawns for a savoury twist. They're especially delicious paired with a glass of Fino Sherry, the driest and palest sherry with hints of herbs, fresh dough and almonds. The bone dry Fino complements the salty, fried buñuelos perfectly.
instructions: Tip the fish stock and salt into a pan and bring to the boil. Drop in the spinach and butter and cook for 1-2 mins to wilt the leaves and melt the butter. Whizz until smooth-ish with a stick blender.

While the mix is still over the heat, tip in the flour and beat it into the spinach mixture. Cook over a low heat, mixing constantly, until you have a smooth ball of dough that is coming away from the sides of the pan. Tip into a bowl and beat for 1-2 mins to cool down.

Once slightly cooler, beat the eggs into the dough one at a time. The batter will look pretty hectic to begin with, but persevere – it’ll come together. Once the eggs are in, beat in the zest of the lemon. Roughly chop the prawns and fold through the batter.
Heat a pan of sunflower oil to about 190°C. Spoon in bite-sized amounts of the batter and cook for 4-5 mins or until golden brown. Lift them out of the hot oil and drain.
Season with fine salt and plate up. Serve with lemon wedges and a big dollop of aioli.

name: Fried Salt & Pepper Tofu
description: This fried salt and pepper tofu is a nice twist on a takeaway classic. The cornstarch slurry is essential in thickening the sauce.
instructions: Cut the tofu into bite-sized squares, then transfer to a large mixing bowl. Add the water and 1 tbsp salt, then submerge the tofu for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, make the salt and pepper mix by grinding everything into a fine powder using a blender or pestle and mortar.
Finely chop the garlic, chilli and spring onions, then set aside.
Drain the tofu, then gently pat the tofu dry with kitchen paper if using firm tofu. Otherwise gently drain a softer tofu, and just leave it in the sieve to release excess water.
Cover a large plate in the starch and drop the tofu into the starch, making sure not to add any excess water. Coat the tofu in the starch and leave it to absorb for 3 mins. Whilst you heat the pan.

Add enough neutral oil to cover the base of a large pan by ½ cm. Gently drop in the tofu, making sure every piece is touching the oil. Now cook over a medium high heat until golden. Allow it to get crispy with no interference for 3 mins, then use a spatula to release the tofu - it is easier to flip them when they stick together, as the bigger pieces are less fiddly. The whole process should take around 10 mins, or until the tofu is lightly golden and no longer sticking to the pan.

Remove all the tofu to a kitchen paper-lined plate to soak up the excess oil. clean the pan with kitchen paper to soak up excess oil and any crispy bits. Add a splash of oil and the garlic, chilli and spring onions to and cook evenly until lightly golden.
Return the crispy tofu to the pan, and toss for 30 seconds. Now dust over 2-3 tsp of the salt & pepper mixture, then taste for seasoning. Transfer to a serving dish.
Garnish with spring onions and eat hot.

name: Frozen Cheeky Vimto
description: Port and WKD? Sounds like a great combo and it is.
instructions: Start by pouring 50ml of port into an ice cube tray and then fill the rest with WKD. Freeze this overnight.
Peel off some of the orange rind for garnish using a peeler, then cut and juice your orange.
Blend up your ice cube ingredients, then add your crushed ice and the rest of the WKD and blend again.
Pour into a large glass and garnish with your orange.

name: Frozen Forest Mojito
description: This cooling drink is straight from the forests of flavour. I’ve used all the best berries to create a sweet and refreshing taste you won’t be able to put down.
instructions: Cut and juice your lime, saving a slice of the lime for garnish.
Remove the tops off of your strawberries and cut them up into small chunks.
Add them to a bowl along with the raspberries and blackberries and put them in the freezer for 3-4 hours.
Remove them from the freezer and put your berries in the blender along with the white rum, lime juice, simple syrup and mint.
Blend until smooth then pour into a glass.
Garnish with the lime slice and a sprig of mint. Enjoy.

name: Frozen Gherkin Caprese
description: Don't knock it 'til you've tried it. Stick your gherkins in the freezer and shave them over this lovely, fresh caprese salad. Yes, really.
instructions: The night before making, pop the gherkins onto a tray and freeze overnight.
Roughly chop the tomatoes and pop into a sieve. Season with salt, toss and set over a bowl to catch the juice. Leave for 20 minutes.
Peel and finely slice the shallot and add to a bowl with olive oil, sherry vinegar, salt and pepper.
Serve the tomatoes up on a plate, then tear the mozzarella over the top. Spoon over the shallots and oil, then scatter the basil over the top. Grate over the frozen gherkins and get stuck in.

name: Frozen Hazelnut Tiramisu
description: Tiramisu, but not as you know it! We’ve used coffee ice cream and trifle sponge to create a cheat's, no-cook version of a classic dessert.
instructions: Bring the ice cream out of the freezer 10 mins before assembling so it's just softening. Layer half of the trifle sponge in a cling film lined tin (20x20cm) making sure there is overhang.

Tip the ice cream into a mixing bowl and stir quickly - this makes the ice cream easier to spread. Then drizzle half the rum over the sponge and then top with half of the ice cream. Flatten with a spatula then repeat the process with the remaining sponge, rum and ice cream.
Smooth the top and sprinkle with the hazelnuts, then get it back in the freezer as soon as possible. Freeze for at least 4 hours until set, preferably overnight.
When it's time to serve, take out of the freezer 5-10 mins before slicing. Dust with cocoa powder and heat a knife by dunking in hot water. Slice into bars and tuck in.

name: Frozen Mudslide
description: Ice cream cocktail? Yes please, I'l take two.
instructions: Put your crushed ice, vanilla ice cream and all the alcohol in the blender and blitz until smooth in texture.
Squirt the chocolate sauce around the inside of the glass in a fun pattern, then pour in your blended drink.
Garnish with some grated chocolate and dig in.

name: Frozen Orange Spritz
description: Frozen is always better than normal.
instructions: Pour your Aperol and orange juice into an ice cube tray and freeze for 4-5 hours or overnight. Freeze your strawberries at the same time.
Peel some rind off your grapefruit using a peeler and then juice it.
Add your frozen Aperol, orange juice, strawberries, grapefruit juice and Prosecco into a blender with the crushed ice.
Blend until it has a slushy consistency.
Wrap up the grapefruit rind tightly and spear it with a cocktail stick for garnish.

name: Frozen Root Beer Float
description: A frozen root beer float means a cocktail and a dessert all at once. I add bourbon, but a dark rum would be just as good. Stay frosty. B x
instructions: Pop open one of your root beers and fill an ice cube tray, cover and freeze until solid.
Empty the ice into a blender and add the bourbon and a good glug of extra root beer.
Whizz until thick and slushy, add a little more root beer if you need to get it going.
Divide between glasses and top with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

name: Fruity Coconut Grain Porridge
description: This is like a breakfast version of Thai mango sticky rice – decadent and rich, but with all kinds of nutrients from the different grains. It’s delicious hot or cold, making it perfect for meal prep. You can adapt it by using different frozen fruits, or by swapping the pudding rice for sushi rice if you like.
instructions: Rinse the pearl barley under cold water, then tip into a saucepan. Add ½ the coconut milk plus the water and salt. Place onto high heat and bring it to a boil. Once boiling, turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 10 mins, stirring occasionally.

Meanwhile rinse the quinoa and rice until the water runs clear. After the barley's been simmering for 10 mins, add the quinoa and rice in with the remaining coconut milk. Continue cooking for the another 20 mins, or until the porridge is cooked through and creamy.

Meanwhile, tip the frozen mango into a bowl or box and stir through the salt and sugar (skip or reduce the sugar if you prefer). Cover with a lid and set aside to thaw whilst the porridge cooks, or place it in the fridge if making ahead.

Once the porridge is cooked through, whisk the chia seeds through and season with as much honey as you like. You can add a splash of water into the porridge if it's too thick for your liking. If making ahead, transfer into boxes and place in the fridge for up to 4 days.

To serve, spoon the porridge into bowls and top with the fruit and its juices. Finish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds. If making ahead, the porridge thickens as it sits, so you’ll have to loosen it with a touch of water or milk, before enjoying it hot or cold.

name: Frying Pan Pizza
description: Here's an easy way to make a pizza, without a pizza oven. It all happens in a frying pan, gets finished under the grill and voila, pizza. Jordon x
instructions: Mix the flour and 650ml of lukewarm water together until it combines to form a rough mass. Dissolve the yeast in a tbsp of lukewarm water, then add to the dough and mix for a few mins.
Add the salt and keep mixing until you have a smooth elastic dough. This will probably take about 10 mins total mixing.
Shape in a large ball and place into a clean mixing bowl.
Cover and prove until doubled in size (a few hours at room temperature or overnight in the fridge).
Portion the dough into balls, place onto a clean tray leaving about 3 inches between each ball. Cover with clingfilm and allow to prove for another few hours until soft and pillowy.
In a bowl, crush the tomatoes by hand until pulpy, then season with salt. Chop or tear your mozzarella into chunks and put into a bowl.
Once ready, heat a frying pan over a medium high heat and preheat your grill on high. Stretch your pizza out on a well floured surface and place into your frying pan.
Spoon on 3 tbsp of the tomato sauce and spread across the base. Grate over a little parmesan, if using, then add a few basil leaves. Top with a handful of mozzarella.
Cook until the base is golden and crispy, about 3 mins, then place under the grill for another 2 or 3 mins until the top is golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Remove, finish with a drizzle of olive oil and serve hot!

name: Fudgy Chocolate Orange Traybake
description: Completely vegan, and also potentially the fudgiest chocolate cake you will ever eat. Coconut Collaborative Vanilla Custard is a must to cut the richness.
instructions: Preheat your oven 180°C/354°F.
Grease a 30cm x 20cm tray with oil, then line with greaseproof paper and coat with a drizzle more oil.
Slice 4 oranges as thinly as possible, saving the ends and any other pieces that don’t make the cut. Juice the ends and the scraps into a small bowl along with the caster sugar.
Pour slurry onto the tray and arrange the orange slices on top, overlapping as you go. You could even cut some of them in half to make a clean border around the edge.

Mix the flour, ground almonds, cocoa powder, bicarbonate of soda, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Pour in the coconut milk, vinegar, sugar, oil and the juice and zest of the last orange. Mix well until smooth and pour gently over the oranges in the tray.
Transfer the cake to the oven and bake for 35-40 minutes until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Leave to cool for 20 minutes then invert onto a large chopping board.
Peel off the greaseproof paper and serve with warmed Coconut Collaborative Vanilla Custard.

name: Full English Baked Eggs
description: Two worlds collide. Bringing the classic Full English to this Middle Eastern dish. The tomatoey sauce is brought to a new level with the sausage and bacon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Remove skins from the sausages and divide each sausage into 3 balls. Chop your bacon into chunks.
Add a small splash of oil to a pan. Cook the sausage and bacon until caramelising and browned.
Slice and add your mushrooms, then reduce them down. Add your chopped garlic cloves and a tsp of chopped rosemary. Mix it in and add your spinach.
Once it has wilted, pour in your tomatoes. Mix everything together, season well with salt and pepper. Reduce down until you have a thick sauce.
Make little dips in the sauce and add your eggs. Put the dish in the oven for 12 minutes until the eggs are cooked.
Serve with some lovely crispy sourdough toast! Enjoy!

name: Full English Gnocchi Traybake
description: As if a full English traybake isn’t good enough, we’ve added crispy pan-fried filled gnocchi for extra flavour and crunch. An incredible hungover brunch or lazy dinner.
ingredients: 2Pack La Famiglia Rana Tomato & Mozzarella Filled Pan Fry Gnocchi
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C fan. Chop your mushrooms into quarters. Get them in a large deep roasting tin with the cherry tomatoes (if they’re on a vine, leave them on), bacon rashers and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper then whack in the oven for 10 mins.
Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil (or a knob of butter if you prefer) and add the gnocchi. Lightly cook for 2-3 mins or until slightly golden and crispy.

Once the veggies and bacon have had 10 mins in the oven, take the tray out. Carefully lift off the cherry tomatoes and bacon. Tip the can of baked beans in around the mushrooms then top with the crispy gnocchi, cherry tomatoes and bacon. Use a spoon to create small craters then crack in your eggs.
Get the tray back into the oven for 3-4 mins or until the egg whites are just set and the yolks are runny.
Sprinkle over some chopped parsley then divide between plates and get stuck in.

name: Full English Traybake
description: Hungover, brain dead, or just fancy a fry up. We have got you covered with this banging full English traybake. Seema x
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Finely chop the parsley and add 1 tbsp into a bowl. Grate garlic into the bowl and add a glug of oil with a big pinch of salt. Mix this together and toss this with the mushrooms.
Break up the bread with your hands into large chunks and scatter onto a baking tray.
Slice the bacon in half.
Arrange the bacon, sausages, mushrooms and tomatoes over the bread.
Cover with foil and bake for 15 mins.
Remove the foil and return to the oven to bake until it's super crispy (this should take at least another 15 mins).
Crack the eggs on top and bake for 6 mins just until the whites are set.
Scoop out onto your plates and serve with baked beans and a cup of tea.

name: Full Vegan Breakfast
description: This is my idea of the ultimate vegan breakfast spread. It’s got heat, carbs, protein, textures and so much flavour. Whack it in the oven.
instructions: Start with the potatoes. Preheat the oven to 190°C. Cut the potatoes into quarters or halves if they are very small, making sure they are all a similar size. Place them into a baking dish with the tomatoes. Ideally the baking dish is not too big, so that everything fits snuggly in it, without too much empty space.

Mix the gochujang with 1 tsp of sesame oil, 1 tbsp of olive oil, ¼ tsp salt, ¼ tsp maple syrup and plenty of black pepper. Pour this over the potatoes and tomatoes and mix well to make sure everything is well covered.
Bake for 30-35 mins, tossing once or twice, until the potatoes are starting to crisp up on the edges and the tomatoes have yielded most of their juice.

Next, marinate the tofu. Slice the block into thin slices, the thickness of a £1 coin. Make the marinade in the dish or container that the tofu will fit in. Mix 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tsp maple syrup, ½ tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp tomato paste and 1 tbsp of olive oil. Pour this over the tofu and make sure all of the slices are covered. Set aside for now.

To make the mushrooms, roughly chop any large ones into bite-sized pieces and place in a baking dish. Mince the garlic and add this to the mushrooms with plenty of salt and pepper and a good drizzle of olive oil. Use plenty of olive oil, ideally there will be a little extra at the bottom of the dish, this will help get them extra juicy. Roast for about 20 mins, until caramelised.

Now, lay the tofu onto a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Make sure they are not overlapping. Bake for 8 mins, flip, brush with the extra marinade and bake for another 8-10 mins until it’s starting to crisp up on the edges.
To air fry, cook them at 200°C for 10 mins, flipping them and brushing the marinade over halfway through.
When they come out of the oven, brush them again with the remaining marinade. They should have a firm bite and be slightly crispy on the edges but not hard and crunchy.

To heat the beans, decant them into a small baking dish and add 1 tsp of soy sauce and 1 tsp of smoked paprika and mix. If using, sprinkle over the vegan grated cheese, then bake for about 10 mins on the lower shelf, until bubbling.
While everything is in the oven, slice your avocado and season with salt and pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Toast and butter your bread with vegan butter. Finely chop the chives.
To serve, dish out everything onto two plates or onto one big platter. Scatter over the chives and tuck in.

name: Gado Gado Peanut Noodle Salad
description: A gorg super salad loaded with fresh ingredients and coated in a moreish peanut sauce. Perfect for a healthy weeknight dinner or throw-together lunch.
instructions: Fill a medium-sized pot with water, add a big pinch of salt and bring to a boil. Add the rice noodles to a large bowl, cover with warm water and set aside for 10 mins, until pliable.

In the meantime, make the peanut sauce. Whisk together the peanut butter, dark brown sugar, soy and fish sauce. Use the fine side of a box grater or microplane to grate the garlic and ginger directly into the bowl. Grate the tomato and add along with the zest and juice of the lime. Finely dice the chilli and add to the bowl with a pinch of salt. You can also just chuck all your ingredients into a blender. Add enough water to turn the sauce into a silky dressing.
Make kecap manis by combining the honey, soy and salt. Set aside.

Snap or cut the green beans into bite-sized pieces, then drop into the pot of boiling water along with the beansprouts, cook for 1 min, then use a slotted spoon or tongs to transfer to a bowl. Then transfer your noodles from the warm water, into the boiling water pot and cook for around 1 mins or until softened and bouncy. Tip the noodles into a fine mesh sieve, drain and rinse under cold water to remove noodle starch and stop the cooking process.
Heat a tbsp of vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a high heat. Fry the eggs to your liking, remove from the pan and set aside on a plate.

Pat the tofu dry with a piece of kitchen paper, then slice into cubes. Add another tbsp of oil to the non-stick frying pan, turn the heat to medium-high, then add the tofu. Press and crush a garlic clove using the side of your knife (no need to peel it) then add that to the frying pan. Fry for 2 mins on one side, until the tofu caramelises, then toss. Add 2 tbsp of the kecap manis to the pan and caramelise for 2 mins or until sticky.

To serve, split the noodles between serving bowls and top with the beans and tofu, then pour over the peanut sauce. Top each bowl with a fried egg and the remaining kecap manis. Finish each serving with a fresh lime, spring onions, cucumber slices and crispy shallots.

name: Gado Gado Salad Bowl
description: This is our take on a classic Indonesian salad bowl. Featuring crunchy roasted peanuts, various vegetables, and crispy tofu, this is a summery dish that tastes like sunshine.
instructions: If you don’t have roasted peanuts, heat the oven to 160°C. Tip the peanuts onto a baking tray and roast in the oven for 15-20 mins, or until lightly golden, then remove and set aside. Don’t roast them too brown, as they will continue to brown out of the oven.
Fill a medium pot with water and season like you would pasta water. Add the baby potatoes and bring to the boil.

Meanwhile, slice the tempeh into 1cm-thick pieces, then into matchsticks. Now slice the tofu into 2cm pieces and cut into squares. Finely mince the garlic clove and set aside. Add a shot of oil to a large pan with a good pinch of salt, add all the tofu and tempeh and toss to coat every piece. Cook on each side for 2 mins, or until lightly golden, then add the minced garlic, toss to coat, and cook for 1 min. Add the maple syrup and toss for 30 seconds, then set aside in a small bowl.

Add the eggs to the boiling water and cook for 7 mins. Remove the potatoes when fork-tender and transfer to a large plate. Remove the eggs into a bowl of cold tap water and lightly crack the shell to soak, then set aside (this helps it peel easier). When the potatoes and egg are removed, add the beansprouts, cook for 2 mins, then remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to the plate. Cut the ends off the green beans, then half them and boil for 2 mins. Remove onto the plate. Now cook the spinach for just 30 seconds, then press against the pot to squeeze out some excess water before adding to the plate.

Slice all the cherry tomatoes into halves and set aside on another large plate. Slice the iceberg into ¼ wedges, finely slice the cucumber into slices, slice the potato into ¼ pieces, slice the lime wedges and then peel the eggs, by cracking the shell all over and peeling under the water, then cut in half, and place everything onto the same large plate.
Combine all the dressing ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.

To serve, place one layer of iceberg leaves on the base of your serving plates, creating a flower pattern. Squeeze out all the excess water from the spinach and place into a pile on the edge of the plate, then following a circular pattern add a handful of beansprouts, green beans, crispy tofu, tempeh, cherry tomatoes, eggs and cucumber, but leave a gap in the middle for the dressing. Add half the dressing into the centre, then add a heap of sweetcorn on the side. Garnish with roasted peanuts and crispy shallots over the dressing, and serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Garden Party
description: This is summer freshness incarnate. Zingy light and everything you want on a hot day when you're sat in the sun.
instructions: Start by juicing your lemon and picking the mint leaves off your stalks (saving the top of one of your stalks for garnish).
Use a peeler create thin strips of your cucumber and set aside.
Then one stalks worth of the mint to a bowl along with 25g of sugar and the lemon juice.
Gently muddle these to release the flavours of the mint and dissolve the sugar.
Put the rest of the mint and sugar into a blender and blend until combined to form a mint sugar.
Wipe a lemon wedge around the rim of the glass then grind the glass in the mint sugar to create a green rim around the glass.
Add ice to the glass, then the muddled mint lemon mixture, a few of the cucumber strips and then top off with sparkling water.

name: Garlic & Herb Chicken Mince Salad
description: Chicken mince and courgette ribbons piled onto a whipped white bean and chive dip. All the garlic and herb soft cheese flavours, just better balanced.
keywords: Garlic & Herb Chicken Mince Salad recipe
instructions: Tip the beans into a blender with the cottage cheese and chives, plus a splash of the liquid from the can. Blend until smooth, then season with salt and the lemon zest and juice.
Thinly slice the garlic and chilli. Using a peeler, shave the courgette into ribbons, then roughly chop the parsley.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the mince and stir-fry for 2-3 mins, until the fat starts to render, then add the garlic, pumpkin seeds and chilli and stir-fry for another 3-4 mins, until cooked through. Add a drizzle of the olive oil if it starts to catch. Season with salt and pepper.
Toss the mince through the courgette with the remaining olive oil. Leave to cool, then toss the parsley through and season with salt.
Share the dip between boxes or onto plates and top with the salad. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Garlic & Parmesan Roast Potatoes
description: Crispy, crunchy, and loaded with parmesan. This recipe for roast potatoes is a winner. You'll never want to go back to regular roast potatoes ever again.
instructions: Peel your potatoes and place them in a large saucepan, cover with cold water and season generously.
Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Put the potatoes on a high heat to par-boil for 10-12 mins. Once the potatoes are partially cooked, drain, give them a shake to ruffle the outsides and leave them to steam dry for 5 mins.
In the meantime, put your oil and butter in a saucepan and preheat on the stove. Preheat a tray in the oven.
Remove the tray from the oven and carefully add the potatoes and the hot oil, season with salt. Using a couple of forks, turn the potatoes in the hot fat and get them back in the oven.
Cook for 25 mins then remove from the oven.
Give the potatoes a shake and turn any that are colouring quickly, return the tray to the oven and continue cooking until the potatoes are nice and roasty.
Grate some garlic into 5 tbsp olive oil and toss through the potatoes with the rosemary. Cover with half the parmesan and return to the oven for the last 3-4 mins.
Serve with extra flaky salt, crispy rosemary and grated parm on top.

name: Garlic Beef Udon Soup
description: A taste of Japan right at home, it's simple, quick and easy, one of the most comforting bowls you could eat for breakfast, lunch or dinner!
instructions: Start by finely mincing the garlic. Slice the ginger lengthways as thin as possible, then lay it flat and slice into thin strips. Slice the spring onions as thin as possible and transfer to a bowl of ice-cold water.
Slice the steak as thin as possible and transfer to a bowl. Add the minced garlic, sugar, light soy sauce, sesame seeds and sesame oil to the same bowl with one-third of the mirin. Set aside.

Heat a frying pan over a high heat for 1 min. Add a splash of oil and the beef. Once in the pan, spread it out evenly and leave to caramelise for around 1 min. Flip over and cook for another minute, then set aside.

Heat a saucepan over a high heat and add the ginger, sake, the remainder of the mirin, soy sauce, dashi powder (or stock) and water. Bring to the boil. Once boiling, add the udon and stir for around 3 mins until the noodles have separated.

Divide the udon and soup between two bowls. Add the cooked beef on top. Drain the spring onions and place them on top of the beef, in a mound. Make a small well with your finger in the spring onion and place the egg yolk into the well. Enjoy!

name: Garlic Bread Mac & Cheese
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

The ultimate comfort food – creamy, cheesy pasta topped with crispy, buttery garlic bread chunks. A quick 30-minute recipe that’s perfect for a cosy dinner or indulgent side dish.
instructions: Add the milk, stock, garlic granules, thyme, whole unpeeled garlic cloves and mustard to a blender. Blitz until smooth.

Add the pasta to a large pan and strain the milk mixture into it. Add the bay leaves and season with salt and plenty of black pepper. Turn the heat up to medium-high, bring to the boil, then reduce to medium. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is al dente (follow pack instructions) and the sauce has thickened.
Meanwhile, turn the grill to high. Grate the Cheddar. Tear or cut the baguette into bite-sized chunks.
Once the pasta is cooked, stir through the Cheddar. Scatter over the mozzarella and baguette chunks.
Place under the grill until golden and crispy. Serve immediately.

name: Garlic Butter Crispy Chicken Rice
description: You've never had a chicken and rice recipe that's as good as this. Extremely garlicky and extremely delicious.
keywords: Garlic Butter Crispy Chicken Rice recipe
instructions: Wash the rice three times, or until the water runs clear. Add to a saucepan along with the cold water, cover with a lid and leave to soak for 30 mins. Turn the heat to high and bring to a boil then turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 10 mins. Remove from the heat and set aside with the lid on for another 10 mins to finish cooking.
Heat the soy sauce, mirin and brown sugar in a small saucepan set over a medium heat. Let the mixture simmer away until reduced by a third (about 5 mins). Transfer to a small jug and set aside.
Finely slice the chives and mince the garlic cloves.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan set over a medium heat. Add ⅓ of the garlic at a time, stirring for 30 seconds between each addition. Transfer the garlic butter to a large mixing bowl.
Add the chilli powder, zest of the lemon and ¾ of the chives (save the rest for garnish) to the garlic butter. Season with a pinch of salt and stir to combine. Set aside.

Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces. Add the chicken to a bowl and grate in the ginger. Add the  soy sauce and mirin and a generous pinch of salt and pepper, then mix thoroughly. Add the cornstarch and toss until covered.

Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a large frying pan set over a medium-high heat for around 3 mins. Carefully place the chicken in the hot oil, gently pushing the chicken pieces apart to prevent sticking. Cook for 10 mins, flipping the chicken over halfway through. Transfer the cooked chicken to the mixing bowl with the garlic butter and toss to coat.

Carefully separate the egg yolks from the whites (you can freeze the whites for meringue). To serve, divide the rice between bowls and top with the fried chicken. Make a small well in the centre of the chicken and add the egg yolk. Pour the sauce over the chicken and sprinkle with the remaining chives.

name: Garlic Butter Mushrooms with Salsa Verde
description: Foraged mushrooms are grilled and finished with a classic garlic butter sauce. Served in the Basque-style with an egg yolk and crusty grilled sourdough.
instructions: Mix the butter with the finely grated garlic cloves, salt and pepper. Grate the parmesan and tip half into the butter.

Finely chop the parsley, chives and capers and tip into a bowl. Add the zest and juice of a lemon and enough oil to bring it together into a salsa, roughly 80-100ml. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.

Clean the mushrooms, removing any dirt or soil. Preheat a large frying pan over a high heat fire. Add a dash of oil and toss in the shrooms. Cook with no salt until super brown and crispy. Add a big spoon of garlic butter and salt. Toss the shrooms in the butter until golden brown and delicious.
Meanwhile, grill your bread over the flames.

Separate the egg yolks (you can freeze the whites for later). Tip your mushrooms onto a serving plate and plop the egg yolk into the middle. Season the yolk with salt and pepper. Dress the plate with salsa verde and shaved parmesan. Serve with the warm, grilled bread.

name: Garlic Butter Prawn Noodles
description: Garlicky, buttery prawns tossed in a deeply a umami sauce, with loads of crunch from cashews and peanuts. Fast, delicious, and loaded with protein.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.
Mix together all the sauce ingredients in a small bowl and set aside. Finely slice the chilli. Peel and finely grate the garlic and ginger.

Place a large wok or frying pan over a medium heat. Add the butter and a drizzle of olive oil. Once melted and foaming, add the garlic, ginger and chilli. Cook for 2-3 mins, stirring constantly, until softened and lightly caramelised.
Add the prawns to the pan and cook for 1 min on each side until just turning pink.
Cook the udon noodles following pack instructions, then drain.

Add the spinach to the pan with the prawns and stir until just wilted. Tip in the noodles and pour in the sauce. Toss everything together over a high heat for 1-2 mins until the noodles are coated and glossy. Taste and season with more salt or black vinegar, if needed.
Roughly chop the cashews and toast them in a dry frying pan for 2-3 mins until golden and fragrant. Then stir through the noodles.
Thinly slice the spring onion.
Divide the noodles between two bowls and top with the toasted chopped cashews and scatter over the peanuts, sliced spring onion and a drizzle of chilli oil, if using.

name: Garlic Chilli Noodles
description: Stir fried noodles are some of the best things on the planet. This quick and easy chicken noodle dish is inspired by Thai pad see ew. It's garlicky and delicious.
instructions: Slice the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces, place into a bowl and add chicken marinade, then leave in the fridge.
Finely slice all the garlic cloves and your chilli. Wash the kale.
In a small bowl add chilli, five pieces of sliced garlic, honey, and vinegar for the chilli vinegar, set aside.
In another small bowl, combine the noodle sauce ingredients together and set aside.
In another bowl, whisk eggs with a pinch of salt and set aside.
Rinse the cooked egg noodles in hot water to loosen, drain and set aside.

Heat a large pan to high heat, add 2 tbsp of oil, then use tongs to add the chicken without the excess marinating liquid, as it can burn. Spread the chicken evenly on the pan and leave to cook for 2 mins without touching, this is to get a nice golden colour. Flip and cook for another 2 mins or until lightly golden.
Add the garlic and cook for another minute or until they have softened, don’t let it burn. Reduce the heat to medium-high if needed.

On high heat, push everything to the edge of the pan, add a tbsp of oil to the centre of the pan and pour in the eggs but don't touch them, allow the eggs to puff into a big omelette. Once the egg is mostly set, use tongs to break into big fluffy egg pieces.
Toss everything together then add the noodle sauce allowing it to cook for another minute to caramelise.
Add in your egg noodles, 2 tbsp of water and toss for 1 minute.
Add the kale and toss for 1 minute. Add a splash more of dark soy sauce for colour, if needed, but taste the dish before adding to avoid over-seasoning.
Add fresh coriander and serve immediately with the chilli vinegar on the side

name: Garlic Honey Soy Steak Sando
description: A quick, made-in-minutes steak sandwich slathered in a rich garlic soy gravy.
keywords: Garlic Honey Soy Steak Sando recipe
instructions: Mince the garlic and slice the tomato into discs. Add the garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, honey and half of the water to a frying pan set over a medium heat. Simmer for 3 mins.

Make a slurry with the cornstarch and the remaining water, then mix thoroughly. Turn the heat off the pan and slowly pour in the slurry while stirring. It should be smooth with the consistency of gravy. If too thin, add more slurry; if too thick, add a little cold water. Set aside while you make the rest of the sandwich.

Heat a new frying pan over a medium heat, then add the butter and gently toast the brioche on both sides (around 1 min per side). Keep an eye out so they don’t burn. Remove from the pan and add a slice of cheese to each slice.
Turn the heat up to high and add a splash of oil to the same pan. Season the steak with salt. Add the steak to the pan and cook for 2 mins per side for medium-rare. Remove and rest on a plate.
Slice the steak into thin strips, removing any bits of fat. Divide the steak slices between two slices of brioche. Generously coat with the sauce. Add tomato slices followed by a handful of rocket.
Press down with another slice of bread to complete the sandwich. Cut in half and enjoy!

name: Garlic Oil Hainanese Chicken Rice
description: A twist on a classic East Asian staple, the famous Hainanese chicken rice. All the same components, doused in tonnes of addictive crispy garlic shallot oil and fragrant garlic rice cooked with chicken broth. The chicken is served at room temperature to give it that silky texture, while the rice is served piping hot.
keywords: Garlic Oil Hainanese Chicken Rice recipe
instructions: Pour cold water into a large saucepan and bring to the boil. Cut a 1cm chunk of ginger and smash it using the back of a knife. Add the smashed ginger, 2 tsp salt, the turmeric and the chicken legs to the boiling water. Put the lid on and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 30 mins. Once cooked, remove the chicken to a bowl of ice-cold water. Reserve 100ml of the cooking liquid and set aside.
