Meanwhile, finely mince or blend the garlic. Divide the garlic in half and add half to a bowl of cold water. Stir well, then drain. Set the other half aside for the rice.

Finely dice the shallot and thinly slice the chilli. Add 5 tbsp vegetable oil to a small saucepan. Add the rinsed garlic, shallot and chilli to the cold oil. Turn the heat to medium-high and fry for 6-8 mins, stirring occasionally. Once the garlic and shallots have turned golden-brown, turn the heat off. Add ½ tsp salt, the sugar, 1 tsp MSG and oyster sauce. Stir to combine. Pour into a bowl and set aside.
Wash the rice in cold water, drain and repeat two more times, or until the water runs clear. Set aside.

Add a splash of vegetable oil to the same pan that you used for the garlic oil and heat on medium-high for 1 min. Add the remaining garlic and fry for 1-2 mins, or until fragrant but not brown. Add the washed rice, stir and fry for 1-2 mins. Ladle broth directly from the pot of chicken into the rice until it covers roughly 2-3cm above the rice. Put the lid on and turn the heat to high, bringing it to the boil. Once boiling, reduce the heat to its lowest setting and cook for 18 mins. Once cooked, turn the heat off, keep the lid on and set aside.
Meanwhile, finely mince or blend the spring onion and remaining ginger. Transfer to a small bowl. Add 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp MSG, then stir to combine.

Add 2 tbsp vegetable oil to a small pan set over a high heat. Leave for around 2 mins until just shy of smoking. Gently pour the hot oil over the spring onion and ginger mixture. Mix well and set aside.
Add the light soy sauce and sesame oil to the reserved cooking liquid. Stir to combine and set aside.
Slice the cucumber as finely as possible. Grab a large serving platter or plate with a rounded edge and cover with the cucumber.

Remove the chicken from the ice bath (skip this step if using boneless chicken). Lay the chicken skin-side down on a chopping board and run the knife along where the bones are. Using your thumb and index finger, push the meat away from the bone and pull the bone out (use a bit of force).

Chop the chicken into 2cm slices, skin-side up. Place the sliced chicken on top of the cucumber. Pour the reserved cooking liquid on top. Generously spoon the garlic oil on top of the chicken. Serve with the bowl of ginger sauce on the side and garnish with a large handful of coriander. Serve with a bowl of garlic rice and enjoy.

name: Garlic Oil Noodles With Grilled Chicken
description: Fragrant garlic oil, punchy noodles, and marinated grilled chicken come together in this big-flavoured, easy-to-love noodle bowl. It’s fresh, spicy, and utterly moreish.
keywords: Garlic Oil Noodles With Grilled Chicken
Garlic Oil Noodles With Grilled Chicken recipe
instructions: Soak the noodles. Place the dried pho noodles in a bowl of cold water and soak for 30 mins. Set aside.
Marinate the chicken. In a bowl, mix the chicken thighs with turmeric, soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, and cracked black pepper. Stir until the chicken is well-coated.

Cook the chicken. Heat a griddle or frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the vegetable oil and cook the chicken for 3–4 mins on each side, pressing gently for even browning. Remove from the heat and let rest.
Prep the aromatics. While the chicken is cooking, peel and mince the garlic cloves and shallot. Slice the Thai chilli thinly.

Make the garlic oil. Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the minced garlic, shallot, and sliced chilli. Gently fry for 2–3 mins until just golden. Stir in the soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and brown sugar. Mix well to dissolve the sugar, then set aside.
Cook the noodles. Bring a saucepan of water to a boil. Cook the soaked noodles for 1 minute less than the packet instructions. Drain and rinse under cool water until warm but not cold.
Prep the toppings. Thinly slice the brown onion and spring onion. Roughly chop the coriander and Thai basil. Cut the lime into wedges.

Assemble the bowl. Add the noodles to a large bowl and spoon over the garlic oil. Slice the grilled chicken into strips and arrange on top. Garnish with brown onion, spring onion, coriander, Thai basil, and fried shallots. Serve with a lime wedge.

name: Garlic Pizza Bread
description: Ever thought of topping a pizza bread with a whole bulb of garlic? No? Well, let us introduce you to our garlic pizza bread recipe. Slow cooking the garlic in olive oil, makes them super soft and caramelised, without any of the bitterness or spice that you find in raw garlic, making them the perfect thing to cover a pizza with.
instructions: Combine the flour with cold water and the yeast in a medium bowl. Cover and set aside at room temperature for 8-10 hours.

To make the confit garlic, heat the oven to 140°C. Peel the garlic cloves and place in a small ovenproof dish or pan. Cover with enough oil to submerge them all. Cover with a lid or foil and slide into the oven for an hour, until the garlic is golden and soft. Set aside to cool.

When ready to start making pizzas, return to the dough. Mix the remaining flour with the salt in a bowl, then tip into the dough and bring together, add a few tablespoons of water if needed. Knead until smooth.
Cut the dough into four. Roll and shape into four balls, then set aside on a baking tray. Drizzle with a little olive oil, then cover loosely with cling film and set aside for half an hour.
Tip the ricotta or cream cheese into a bowl, finely grate in half the Parmesan and season well.

When ready to cook, turn the oven up to 220°C. Flour your kitchen surface, then take one of the balls of dough and use your hands to press and stretch the ball into an approx. 25cm disk. Try to stretch and press out from the middle in order to create a crust around the edge. Lightly flour a large baking sheet and move the dough onto it.

Spoon a couple of tablespoons of the ricotta mix over the dough, leaving a gap around the edges for the crust, top with a handful of the grated mozzarella and finish by grating the Parmesan over the top. Slide into the oven and bake for 10-12 mins.
Spoon over the confit garlic cloves, a little of the oil from the confit garlic and finish with a scattering of parsley.

name: Garlic Prawn & Salmon High Protein Smash
description: Buttery gochugaru prawns, hot smoked salmon and creamy avocado smashed together with crisp cucumber and peas. Piled high on toasted sourdough, it's a proper crowd-pleaser.
keywords: Garlic Prawn and Salmon Smash recipe
instructions: Finely slice the garlic and chillies. Zest and juice the lemon.

Set a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the olive oil and butter. Once foaming, add the garlic, chillies and gochugaru. Cook for 2-3 mins until soft, then add the prawns. Cook for 90 seconds on each side until pink all the way through, then finish with the lemon zest and juice and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Remove the skin from the salmon fillets and add to a large mixing bowl along with the petit pois, edamame, sliced spring onions, light mayo, sesame seeds, prawns and cucumber. Using a pizza cutter, smash up the mix until evenly cut and well combined. Cut the avocado into large chunks and fold through. Season with salt and pepper.
Toast the sourdough. Pile the smash on top and finish with a drizzle of chilli oil and a scatter of sesame seeds.

name: Garlic Sesame Rice
description: This garlic sesame rice is perfect for meal prep. Combine it with your choice of protein, veg and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Tip the rice into a bowl, then wash it thoroughly. Drain, then repeat twice or until the water runs clear. Set aside.
Thinly slice the chives. Finely mince the garlic cloves and the pak choi. Set aside on separate plates.
Heat a saucepan over a medium-high heat for 1 min. Add the sesame oil followed by the minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds. Add the pak choi and fry for a further 1-2 mins.

Add the rice and stir to toast for 1 min. Add the chicken stock, a pinch of salt and a few cracks of black pepper. Put the lid on a bring to a boil. Once boiling, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 18 mins. Once cooked, turn the heat off, add the chives and sesame seeds, then gently mix to combine. Set aside.
Enjoy hot or, If batch cooking for the week, transfer the rice to a container and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Garlic Tahini Sauce
description: This garlicky tahini sauce is incredibly addictive. You can drizzle this on just about anything.
instructions: Add the garlic cloves (skins included) into a blender with the juice of the lemons and the ground cumin. Blend together until a purée is formed. Place a fine mesh strainer over a bowl and transfer the purée into it. Squeeze as much juice out of the purée as possible, then discard the solids.

Stir the tahini into the lemon juice mixture – the tahini will seize and go grainy, stir in 1 tbsp of cold water at a time until a smooth sauce forms, it should be as thick as yoghurt. Taste and season with salt.
Transfer the tahini sauce into a clean airtight container and store in the fridge for 1 week.

name: Garlic Tahini Sauce
description: This garlicky tahini sauce is incredibly addictive. You can drizzle this on just about anything, Mob.
instructions: Add the garlic cloves (skins included) into a blender with the juice of the lemons and the ground cumin. Blend together until a purée is formed. Place a fine mesh strainer over a bowl and transfer the purée into it. Squeeze as much juice out of the purée as possible, then discard the solids.

Stir the tahini into the lemon juice mixture – the tahini will seize and go grainy, stir in 1 tbsp of cold water at a time until a smooth sauce forms, it should be as thick as yoghurt. Taste and season with salt.
Transfer the tahini sauce into a clean airtight container and store in the fridge for 1 week.

name: Garlic Tomato and Basil Baked Eggs
description: Dunk the crunchy garlic croutons into your runny British lion eggs, and the perfectly sweet, fresh tomato sauce. It will become a household regular.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.
Chop the cherry tomatoes in half and place them in a bowl. Finely slice 4 cloves of garlic and chop up the chilli, removing all the seeds.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a large, oven proof pan over a medium heat and add the garlic. Fry for a couple of minutes, then add the cherry tomatoes until they begin to break up and dissolve.
Once the cherry tomatoes have turned mushy, pour in the passata, chopped chillies (saving some for garnish) and the stock pot. Stir together and leave to bubble on a medium heat for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, roughly tear up the ciabatta into chunks and put them into a bowl. Grate in the remaining clove of garlic. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Mix together and set aside.
Back to the tomato sauce. Toss through the spinach and most of your basil.
Once the spinach and basil have wilted, make 6 indents in the tomato sauce with the back of a spoon and carefully drop your British Lion eggs into them.
Place the croutons irregularly around the eggs, drizzle with olive oil and bake in the oven for 12 minutes.
Remove from the oven. Chop your leftover basil and scatter on top with the leftover chopped chillies, a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Then, get dunking!

name: Garlic and Parmesan Oyster Mushrooms
description: The crispiest, juiciest mushrooms ever to hit your mouth. These are really going to give meat eaters a run for their money.
keywords: Garlic and parmesan oyster mushrooms recipe
instructions: Combine the garlic powder with 1 tsp of salt. Finely chop the parsley.
Get a large pot of oil heating on medium-high heat, ready for deep frying.
Place your flour in a bowl, crack the eggs in another, and fill the third bowl with panko breadcrumbs. Season them all with salt.
Dunk the mushrooms in flour and then the eggs and finally press on the panko breadcrumbs.
Deep fry the mushrooms for 3 mins until golden brown and crispy.
Toss them in the garlic salt, grate on lots of parmesan on both sides of the mushroom and sprinkle with parsley.
Eat whilst still hot and enjoy the beautiful crunch.

name: Garlicky Artichoke & Chickpea Tagliatelle
description: This simple but delicious pasta is on the table in 15 minutes flat. It’s packed with flavour and only uses a handful of ingredients, making it a perfect weeknight dinner.
instructions: Heat a large pot of well salted water. Once boiling, cook the pasta al dente. Save a cup of pasta water, drain and drizzle with a little olive oil to prevent it from sticking.
Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic. Drain the artichokes and slice them if they are large pieces. Drain the chickpeas and set aside.
Toast the pine nuts in a small frying pan over low heat until golden, about 3 mins. Stir constantly to help prevent them from burning.

Heat a large pan or pot over medium heat and add a good glug of olive oil. Add the garlic and cook for one minute, then add the artichoke and cook for 3-4 mins, stirring frequently. Add the chickpeas and cook for another 4-5 mins, until the chickpeas and artichoke are starting to crisp up. Stir often to prevent the garlic from burning.
Add the drained pasta to the pan with the artichoke with a splash or two of pasta water, and toss well to combine. Season well with salt and pepper.
To serve, ladle the pasta onto plates, finish with the pine nuts, plenty of lemon juice and zest, chilli flakes if using and an extra drizzle of olive oil.

name: Garlicky Beans & Sausages With Salmoriglio
description: This veggie dish screams comfort. Creamy beans topped with the fantastic vegetarian sausages and a tangy salmoriglio to cut through all the richness.
keywords: Roasted Garlic Beans & Quorn Sausages With Salmoriglio
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

For the salmoriglio: zest half of the lemon into a bowl. Pick the oregano leaves, discarding the stems. Finely mince the parsley stems as well. Add both to the lemon zest and mix together. Pour 60ml of olive oil into the herbs and squeeze in the lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper, mix and set aside.
Peel and thinly slice the shallot. Peel and thinly slice all the garlic.
Place the vegetarian sausages onto a baking tray with a drizzle of oil, toss to evenly coat. Roast in the oven for 18-20 mins, until the vegetarian sausages are golden.

Add 4 tbsp of olive oil into a frying pan with the shallot and garlic. Place on medium heat and cook until lightly golden, 3-5 mins. Stir the beans and spinach through until thickened and wilted, 3-4 mins. Remove from the heat. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Serve the creamy beans into bowls, top with the vegetarian sausages, some salmoriglio, crushed croutons and chilli flakes.

name: Garlicky Broad Beans & Labneh
description: We've topped our homemade labneh with garlicky broad beans and it's a sure-fire yes from us.
instructions: Mix together the yoghurt and the juice of half a lemon and season with salt.
Line a sieve over a bowl with a cheesecloth or heavy duty kitchen paper. Tip in the yoghurt and leave to strain for 1-2 hours up to overnight (the longer it strains the thicker it will get).

Trim, peel and finely slice the shallot into rings, then separate the layers. Add 35ml of olive oil and the sliced shallot into a small non-stick frying pan and place onto medium-low heat. Simmer until the shallots turn golden brown, 10-15 mins.
Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice the garlic. Finely chop the coriander, stalks and all.

Using a slotted spoon, remove the golden shallots from the oil and place in a small bowl lined with kitchen paper. Return to the pan and stir in the garlic, cook for 1 min, then add the broad beans. Cook until the beans are hot, then remove from the heat and stir through the coriander. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Add the labne into a sharing bowl and stir in ¾ of the nigella seeds, top with the broad beans and oil and scatter over the remaining nigella seeds. Serve with warmed flatbreads.

name: Garlicky Cavolo Nero & Caper Spaghetti
description: Taking aglio e olio to the next level with deliciously charred cavolo nero, topped with salty capers and parmesan. It’s so simple and so good.
instructions: Boil a pan of water, salt it and add your spaghetti.
Chop up the cavolo nero and add it into a pan along with 6 tbsp olive oil. Then, fry until wilted.
Slice the garlic and add to the cavolo nero along with the chilli flakes, capers, a pinch of salt, and a tbsp more of olive oil. Cook on a medium heat.
Reserve a cup of pasta water from your spaghetti and add into the pan just before the garlic begins to brown.

Once the spaghetti is al dente, drain and chuck into the sauce on a medium heat. Toss it together to create an emulsion between the oil and pasta water - keep adding pasta water until you get the right consistency.
Once everything is combined and the sauce has come together season with salt and pepper, drizzle with olive oil and scatter over some grated parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Garlicky Charred Green Beans & Beef Rice Bowl
description: Inspired by a Din Tai Fung classic, we've got charred beans with loads of garlic and salty peanuts with the addition of some crispy beef mince. Dressed in a sweet sticky soy sauce, it's low effort and high reward. In Partnership with Aldi. #ad.
keywords: Garlicky Charred Green Beans & Beef Rice Bowl
Garlicky Charred Green Beans & Mince Bowl recipe
instructions: Trim the green beans and cut them in half. Peel and finely chop the garlic. Roughly crush the peanuts and pick the coriander leaves and set them aside for garnish later.

Add the light soy sauce and light brown sugar to a small pan over a medium heat and mix well, stirring until the sugar has dissolved. Once dissolved, let it bubble away for 5 mins, until thickened, then set aside.

Heat a quarter of the olive oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat and add half the beef mince, cooking for 5-6 mins until crispy and golden, then remove with a slotted spoon to drain on kitchen paper. Repeat with another quarter of the oil and the rest of the mince.

Add the remaining oil to the pan along with the green beans and cook for a couple of minutes, until charred and blistered, then remove with the slotted spoon to drain with the mince. Add the garlic to the pan and cook for 30 seconds, then tip the beans back in along with the beef. Crumble in the stock cube and pour in the sweet soy sauce.
Meanwhile, reheat your microwave jasmine rice according to packet instructions.

For the eggs, pour vegetable oil into a frying pan to a depth of about 5mm and heat over a medium-high heat. Crack in the eggs and cook until crispy, basting the yolks until cooked to your liking, then remove and drain.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls and top with the garlicky green beans and crispy mince and your fried egg. Finish with the coriander leaves and peanuts and lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Garlicky Chicken & Egg Rice Bowls
description: Inspired by the beloved Japanese dish of oyakodon, this one-bowl meal gets its flavour from juicy chicken thighs and lots of garlic and spring onions.
instructions:
Thinly slice the onion, green chillies and garlic. Thinly slice the
chicken thighs.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan, add the onion and
green chillies and fry over a medium-high heat for about 5 minutes
until softened but not coloured. Add in the garlic and cook for 1 min more.
Add the sliced chicken, chicken stock, soy sauce and Shaoxing
wine. Bring to a bubble and cook for 10 mins over a medium-low
heat.
Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a bowl and very gently mix a few
times – you don’t want the whites and eggs to be completely mixed.
Thinly slice the spring onions (both green and white parts).
Pour the eggs over the chicken and gently swirl in with a wooden
spoon and then sprinkle over three-quarters of the spring onions.
Pop a lid on the pan and cook for 3 mins until the eggs have set.
Spoon the chicken and eggs over bowls of steamed rice and then
pour over any remaining liquid for the rice to absorb.
Sprinkle with the remaining spring onions and enjoy.

name: Garlicky Chicken & Greek Rice
description: Juicy garlic-fried chicken piled onto herby tomato rice with a dollop of yoghurt. Fresh, fast and seriously good.﻿
instructions: Make the Greek Tomato Rice Traybake batch recipe.
Finely grate the garlic into a bowl, and add a drizzle of olive oil, Season generously with salt and pepper. Add the chicken thighs and rub well to coat. Leave to marinate.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken and fry for 8-10 mins until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile, warm the leftover Greek tomato rice in a saucepan over a low heat with a splash of water, stirring until piping hot throughout.
Pick the parsley leaves, and finely chop most of it, keeping a few whole for the garnish. Stir most of the chopped parsley through the rice, taste and season with salt and pepper.
Slice the chicken, then plate up the rice with the garlicky chicken on top. Add a dollop of yoghurt and scatter over the whole parsley leaves. Dig in.

name: Garlicky Fish Curry
description: This fragrant fish curry is a beautiful dish. Rich with curry leaves, it makes the most of tomatoes to make something so warming.
instructions: Finely slice your onion and garlic cloves. Halve your cherry tomatoes.

Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a frying pan over a low heat. Add your cumin seeds, black mustard seeds and curry leaves, then fry for 1 min until your kitchen is fragrant and your seeds start popping.
Tip your onions into the pan and fry for 10-15 mins over a medium heat until totally softened and starting to caramelise. Add your garlic, chilli powder and turmeric, then cook out for 2 mins more.
Tip your cherry tomatoes into the pan and cook for 5 mins, squishing them with the back of the spoon so they burst a little.
Chop your fish into large chunks. Add these to the pan along with 200ml water, garam masala, and a good pinch of salt. Pop a lid on the pan and leave to steam on a gentle heat for 6 mins.
Halve one of your limes, then cut the other into wedges. Chop your coriander.
Add the juice of 1 lime to your fish curry. Check the seasoning, adding more salt and chilli powder if necessary. Reheat the rice.
Share the rice and curry into bowls, top with some coriander leaves and serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Garlicky Green Bean Barley Bowl
description: Garlicky green beans and pearl barley are the stars of the show with a French-style shallot vinaigrette and a tangy goat’s cheese dressing. Light, perfect for meal prep and good for you!
instructions: Bring the stock to the boil in a large saucepan. Rinse the barley well, then add it to the stock pan. Cook for 25 mins or until tender.
Trim the green beans. Bring a pan of water to the boil and blanch the beans for 1 min. Drain and rinse in cold water, then dry well and set aside.

Finely chop the garlic, then add to a pan with a shot of oil over a medium-high heat. Cook for 2 mins, then add the green beans and cook for another 1-2 mins. Remove from the heat and squeeze in the juice of 1/2 your lemons, then season with salt and pepper.

Finely dice the shallot and mix with the vinegar, mustard, honey, salt and pepper. Set aside. Mix the goat’s cheese with the yoghurt until smooth. Set aside. Finely chop the parsley and mix it through the barley.
Swoosh some of the goat’s cheese yoghurt into a bowl, then top with barley, green beans, shallot vinaigrette and toasted almonds, and the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

name: Garlicky Lemon & Herb Chicken Flatbreads
description: A spring and summer staple. These garlicky, lemony chicken skewers are best when they're thrown in a flatbread with some fresh salad.
keywords: Garlicky Lemon & Herb Chicken Flatbreads recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Finely mince the dill, finely grate the garlic, add the garlic and half the dill into a bowl with the mustard and a generous drizzle of olive oil. Season generously with salt and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper.

Using scissors, snip the chicken into 3cm chunks, toss into the marinade. Thread the chicken onto some metal skewers. Place the skewers onto a baking tray and roast until cooked through,15-20 mins. Switch the grill onto high and grill until starting to char, flip and continue cooking until charred in places on both sides of the skewers.

Meanwhile, quarter the radishes and chop the cucumber into 1cm chunks. Add to a bowl, with the juice of the lemon and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Crumble the feta and toss through the salad.
Reheat the flatbreads, top with the skewers, salad, the rest of the dill, and a dollop of Greek yoghurt.

name: Garlicky Mustard & Lemon Brothy Beans with Seedy Sprinkle
description: These creamy garlicky braised cannellini beans are packed with flavour and only take half an hour to make. Cook up a big batch and you’ve got lunch sorted for days.
keywords: Garlicky Mustard & Lemon Brothy Beans with Seedy Sprinkle
Garlicky Mustard & Lemon Brothy Beans with Seedy Sprinkle recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the leek then rinse well in cold water. Thinly slice the garlic.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan set over a medium heat. Add the leek, garlic and a pinch of salt and cook for 10-15 mins until softened. Meanwhile, remove the tough stems from the kale and tear the remaining kale into bite size pieces.

Add the kale, cannellini beans and their liquid, stock, nutritional yeast (if using) and wholegrain mustard to the pan. Give everything a good stir then simmer for another 10 mins. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Meanwhile, for the seedy topping, toast all the seeds in a dry frying pan set over a medium heat for a few minutes until fragrant. Stir through the chilli flakes and plenty of salt and pepper.
To serve, spoon the creamy beans into bowls and top with the seedy mix. Finish with a glug of olive oil and some lemon zest and juice. Serve with some extra mustard, if you like.

name: Garlicky Mustard Chicken
description: This garlicky mustard chicken is perfect for meal prep. Combine it with your favourite carb and veg to create your perfect meal.
keywords: honey and mustard chicken with broth
high protein chicken broth recipe with rice
instructions: Add the chicken thighs and mustard to a bowl. Grate over the garlic and drizzle over some oil. Season generously with salt and pepper and give it a good mix. Set aside.
Heat a frying pan with a drizzle of oil over a medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken and cook on both sides until slightly charred and cooked through.

Serve the chicken with your choice of carb and veg. Sprinkle over some fresh dill, if you like. If batch cooking for the week, transfer the chicken to a container and store in the fridge until ready to serve.

name: Garlicky Mustard Chicken & Zingy Broth With Rice
description: Chloe's 'With Rice' series is back and better than ever - this garlicky mustard chicken is paired with a zingy broth and plenty of fluffy rice. It's a stunner.
keywords: honey and mustard chicken with broth
high protein chicken broth recipe with rice
instructions: Add the chicken thighs and mustard to a bowl. Grate over the garlic and drizzle over some oil. Season generously with salt and pepper and give it a good mix. Set aside.
Reserve a few dill and parsley leaves for garnish and finely chop the rest, stalks included.
Heat a frying pan with a drizzle of oil over a medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken and cook on both sides until slightly charred and cooked through.
Reheat the cooked rice and stir through the herbs.

Heat the stock in a saucepan over a medium heat. Whisk the egg yolks in a small bowl with the juice of half your lemons then pour the egg mixture into the hot stock. Whisk vigorously until it starts to thicken slightly. Season with salt, pepper and more lemon juice to taste (you want it quite tart).
Share the rice between four bowls and ladle over the broth. Top with the chicken and reserved herbs. Serve with any remaining wedges of lemon.

name: Garlicky Pancetta & Pea Spelt Spaghetti
description: A taste of spring in the depths of winter thanks to the magic that is frozen peas! Cooked here with loads of garlic and a little diced pancetta, half the mix gets whizzed up and tossed through wholesome spelt spaghetti until creamy, then topped with fresh ricotta.
instructions: Place a saucepan over a medium heat and add the olive oil, the pancetta and finely chopped onion and cook for 5 mins until the onion is soft and the pancetta has rendered its fat.
Meanwhile, put your pasta to boil in plenty of well-salted boiling water.
Finely chop and add the garlic, cook for 2 mins and then pour in the frozen peas and the water and stir well. Cook until the peas are tender.
Remove half of the mixture and add it to a blender along with 2 tbsp of pasta cooking water, half of the ricotta, and the parsley. Blend until almost smooth.
By this point, your pasta should be al dente so drain it and transfer to the pan with the peas.
Pour in your pea cream too and mix everything well. Taste and season, spoon into a bowl and then top each one with a nice spoon of ricotta, black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Garlicky Parmesan Chicken Wings
description: Garlic and Parm make the perfect match. Throw chicken wings into the mix and you're onto a winner. A great recipe for Iftar.
instructions: Add the buttermilk and all the spices for marinating to a large bowl, mix and add the chicken wings. Cover and pop into the fridge. Leave for at least an hour, ideally overnight.
To make the dry coating, add the plain flour, cornflour and spices to a large bowl.

To make the garlic butter, melt the butter in a small saucepan and grate in the garlic. Cook over a medium heat for 2-3 mins. Then, tip in the lemon juice and season to taste. Finely chop the herbs and add those at the last min. Set aside and keep warm.
Preheat a pot of oil to 170°C.

Pull the chicken out of the fridge. Grab a wing and shake off the excess buttermilk. Coat each chicken wing in the dry mixture, scrunching the dry coat in to make a craggy texture. Deep fry in vegetable oil for 6-8 mins until golden and crispy all over.
Toss the fried chicken wings in the garlic butter and grate over Parmesan.

name: Garlicky Pot Roast Chicken
description:
This chicken will change your roast dinners forever. Garlic and chicken stock make the 
most moreish gravy imaginable. A classic.
instructions: Heat the oven to 150°C.
Brown off the chicken all over in a large pan that can hold the chicken and has a lid.
Peel all your cloves of garlic (this may take a while!) and pick off your thyme leaves. Pick the leaves off your parsley and set aside for later. Cut one of your lemons into wedges.

Once the chicken is browned all over, place the garlic, thyme and parsley stalks around your chicken. Add your stock, 2 tbsp olive oil and a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Pop the lid on the pan and roast in the oven for an hour.
Turn the oven temperature up to 200°C.
Remove the lid from your dish, then return it to the oven for 20 mins to crisp up the skin.
Squeeze the juice of 1 lemon through the sauce and add some chopped parsley. Carve up and serve with some crusty bread and your remaining lemon wedges.

name: Garlicky Potato Skins
description: We’ve packed garlicky potato skins with a healthy dose of green veg and draped them with a tangy cornichon-spiked salsa verde.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Prick the potatoes all over with a sharp knife. Wrap the whole
garlic bulb in foil. Put the potatoes into a roasting tin, season and
bake for 1 hour until completely tender, adding the wrapped garlic
to the tin after 20 minutes. After 40 minutes it should be super soft.
Meanwhile, halve and thinly slice the leeks. Using one hand,
hold each cavolo nero stalk and use the other to strip the leaves
away from the stalk, then finely chop the stalks.
Get a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add 2 tsp of
the olive oil, the sliced leeks and chopped cavolo nero stalks along
with 3 tbsp of water. Cook until the water has evaporated
and the leeks are collapsed and soft. Add the cavolo nero leaves and
peas and cook for a few minutes more until everything is tender.
Stir through 2 tsp of the mustard, then scrape into a large
bowl and set aside.
Once the garlic is cooked, squeeze out onto a chopping board,
mash with a fork then stir through the greens.
Cut the baked potatoes in half and leave to cool a little, then
spoon the potato centre into the greens and mix together. Increase
the oven temperature to 220°C.
Put the potato skins back into the roasting tin, drizzle with a
teaspoon of olive oil and bake for 5 minutes so that they crisp
up slightly.
Meanwhile, grate the cheese. Season the filling to taste and then
load into the potato skins and sprinkle over the cheese. Return to
the oven for 10 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Salsa verde time. Chop the cornichons and parsley (stalks and all)
and mix together with the remaining teaspoon of mustard, 2 tbsp of olive oil and the red wine vinegar. Season to taste –
you want it punchy. Serve the cornichon salsa verde with the loaded
potato skins and a big green salad, if you like.

name: Garlicky Prawn Salad
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. 

Salads can be a great dinner when you want something that's a little bit on the lighter side. This garlicky prawn number comes together in just 20 minutes.

#ad
keywords: easy salad recipe 20 minute salad recipe
instructions: Trim and finely slice the cabbage and chilli, pick the basil leaves and halve your tomatoes.

Set a saucepan over a medium heat, and drizzle in a lug of olive oil, add the prawns and cook for 2 mins. Add the chilli and cook for another 2 mins. Add the garlic puree and cook for 1 more minute. Remove from the pan.

Add your sliced cabbage, tomatoes, lentils, pickled onions, basil leaves and the cooked garlic and chilli prawns to a large bowl and toss together. Sprinkle with salt and pepper to season and mix again.
Dress the salad with a splash of the pickled onion brine, and a little more oil to taste. Share onto a large platter or individual plates. Get stuck in!

name: Garlicky Prawns & White Beans on Toast
description: Juicy garlic prawns turned into a proper meal with creamy butter beans and garlicky-soaked sourdough. Bright, summery and done in under 20 mins.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic. Drain the butter beans, roughly chop the parsley and zest the lemon.

Pour half of the olive oil into a wide frying pan while the hob is off. Add the garlic to the cold oil, then place the pan over a medium heat and cook gently for 1-2 mins until the garlic is just turning golden. Watch it closely as it can catch quickly. Stir in the smoked paprika, chilli flakes and lemon zest and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Turn the heat up to high and add the prawns. Cook for 1-2 mins, stirring once or twice, until they're just starting to turn pink. Pour in the white wine and let it bubble away and reduce by half, about 2 mins.
Add the drained beans, stir everything together and simmer for a further 2 mins so the beans soak up the sauce.
Stir through most of the parsley and squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Meanwhile, toast the sourdough and drizzle with a little olive oil. Spoon the prawns, beans and all the juices over the toast, scatter over the remaining parsley and serve.

name: Garlicky Ratatouille Toast & Harissa Fried Eggs
description: Crispy toast rubbed with garlic and piled with our Ratatouille and a spicy fried egg. Proper brunch goals.
keywords: Garlicky Ratatouille Toast & Harissa Fried Eggs recipe
Garlicky Ratatouille Toast & Harissa Fried Eggs
instructions: Make the Ratatouille.
Pop your toast in the toaster or under a hot grill.
Heat the ratatouille in a small pan or in the microwave.

Heat the oil in a small frying pan over a medium heat. Once the oil is hot, add the harissa and stir to combine, then crack in the eggs. Cook whilst basting with hot oil until the yolks are cooked and the whites crisp, then remove from the pan and drain on kitchen paper before seasoning with salt and pepper.
Get the toast onto plates, poke holes in the bread before rubbing with garlic and drizzling with the vinegar.
Top with the ratatouille, fried egg and fresh parsley.

name: Garlicky Sesame Leeks
description: These spicy and tender braised leeks are the perfect thing to lay over a bed of fluffy rice for a quick lunch.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Char the leeks directly on the flame of your gas hob until they are evenly blistered. If you don’t have a gas hob, char them under a very hot grill.
Cut the ends off the leeks and cut them in half. Nestle them into a baking dish so they are tightly packed.
Finely chop the red chillies, or blitz them up in a food processor.
Add the chillies and 50ml vegetable oil to a pan on medium-low heat and cook for 10 mins until the oil is stained red.
Crush the garlic and roughly chop the garlic and ginger.
Add in the garlic, ginger and sesame seeds, stir for 1 min and then turn off the heat. Add in the soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, juice of the orange and 100ml of water.
Pour this over the leeks and cover with foil. If your leeks are still a bit tough, add more water. Braise in the oven for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the peanuts.
Sprinkle peanuts over the leeks and grate over orange zest.
Serve over sticky rice and enjoy.

name: Garlicky Slow Roast Lamb
description: Pull-apart slow-roast lamb shoulder, meltingly tender from four hours in the oven with garlic, rosemary and stock. Great on its own or as the base for a week of quick meals.
instructions: Heat the oven to 150°C. Drizzle the lamb with olive oil and season all over with salt and pepper, rubbing it in well. Pop it into a heavy roasting tin and scatter over the garlic cloves and rosemary sprigs, then pour in the stock. Cover the tin with a piece of baking paper, then tightly seal with foil. Roast for 3 hrs or until the meat is super tender and the bone pulls away easily (it may take a little longer depending on the thickness of the meat on your leg.
Increase the oven to 200°C, remove the baking paper and foil, and cook for a further 20 mins until the lamb is starting to crisp and turn golden.

Leave to rest for at least 20 mins, then shred the meat off the bone using two forks. Transfer the shredded meat into a container along with the garlic, smooshing it into the meat, then pour the roasting juices into a separate container. Once the fat has risen to the top skim it off and remove,  any leftover juices are brilliant frozen in ice cube trays and used in place of a stock cube.
If you're not prepping ahead, serve up alongside your favourite sides.

name: Garlicky Soy Sauce Bucatini
description: A garlicky, spicier version of your favourite pasta dish that you can make in a flash. This is my go-to meal for a quick dinner. Seema x
instructions: Cook your pasta in heavily salted boiling water for about 10 mins until al dente.
Meanwhile, add your olive oil to a pan over a low heat. Finely slice your garlic and add to the oil and cook gently for 4-5 mins until they're really soft.
Finely chop the ginger, spring onions and coriander.
Add the ginger, spring onions, and crispy chilli oil to your pan and continue cooking on a low heat until the pasta is ready. This should take about 5 mins.
Add a slosh of pasta water to the pan then add the soy sauce. Bubble away.
Transfer the bucatini into your pan of aromatics using a pair of tongs. By not fully draining your bucatini, you'll ensure that it keeps it keeps its glossy texture, mix well.
Turn up the heat to medium and give it a good stir so that the pasta absorbs most of the water. If it looks too dry, add small amounts of water until the pasta is well coated and shiny.
Stir in the coriander and mix well.
Serve up on bowls, using tongs to twirl the pasta into nests. Grate on lots of parmesan and enjoy.

name: Garlicky Spaghetti with Anchovies & Breadcrumbs
description: Yes, anchovies can be aggressive but they can also be the subtle, mellow, salty little kick that takes your pasta to a new level.
instructions: Drain the oil from the anchovies into a small frying pan and set aside.
Warm 5 tbsp of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Peel and mince the garlic and half of the parsley before adding them to the pan along with the anchovies and chilli flakes.
Put your pasta onto cook in heavily salted boiling water.
Cook gently, breaking up the anchovies with a wooden spoon so that they melt into the oil. Once the garlic is very lightly golden, remove from the heat.
Place the pan with the anchovy oil in over a medium heat, add your breadcrumbs and cook, stirring regularly, until they’re golden brown. Set aside.

Once the pasta is al dente, add to the pan with the anchovies and half a mug of the pasta cooking water, place over a high heat and stir well to create a glossy sauce. Mince the rest of your parsley and add along with the juice of a lemon.
Plate up and top with the toasted breadcrumbs.

name: Garlicky Spinach-Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
description: A nutty, savoury yoghurt teamed with homemade tahini, crunchy, zingy slaw and soft, sweet potatoes. Prepare to fall in love.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Thoroughly wash the sweet potatoes, prick with a fork and rub with 1 tbsp of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then add to a baking tray before baking for 30-45 mins.

Make the sesame yoghurt. Toast the sesame seeds in a pan on minimum heat, until golden. Reserve around 2 tbsp for garnish and add the remaining seeds to a mini food processor and pulse until sandy, then add 3 tbsp of olive oil. Keep mixing until smooth then tip into a bowl, stirring through the yoghurt. Season with salt, pepper and the juice of 1 lime. Gradually add in small splashes of water, mixing between each addition to take it to a drizzle-able consistency.

Finely slice the cabbage, spring onions and green beans then add to a bowl. Roughly chop most of the coriander (saving some leaves whole for garnish) and tip into the bowl. Squeeze in the juice of the remaining 2 limes and season to taste.

Roughly chop the garlic. Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, once hot, fry the garlic for 2-3 mins until softened but not taking on any colour. Add the spinach and stir until wilted and darkened in colour, season well.

When the potatoes are cooked, halve lengthways, season with a little salt and give them a splash of olive oil. Fill with the spinach mixture, drizzle with the tahini yoghurt and scatter with the reserved coriander leaves and sesame seeds. Serve alongside the hispi slaw.

name: Garlicky White Beans, Roasted Purple Sprouting Broccoli, Chilli & Lemon
description: If you're looking for a mid-week meal that's healthy and delicious, you're in the right place. Tuck in.
keywords: garlic beans purple sprouting slow cooker
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C
Peel the garlic cloves and get the garlic in a small saucepan, submerge in oil, and place on medium-low heat for 30 mins. Do not let the oil bubble!
Trim the broccoli, drizzle with olive oil, salt, and pepper, and roast in the oven for 20-25 minutes.

Dice the shallot and chilli. Sauté the diced shallot first in olive oil with salt for 5 mins and then add the sliced chilli and bay leaf. Add in your stock and then pour in the beans and their liquid. Let this simmer until thick.
Squish the confit garlic, using as much or little as you like (the rest can be stored covered in the oil, in an airtight jar) and stir it through the beans along with the juice of the lemon.
Top with the roasted broccoli, a drizzle of the confit garlic oil, a sprinkling of nutritional yeast, and serve with a hunk of bread.

name: Giant Couscous & Aubergine Salad
description: Big balsamic energy. Using our jammy Aubergine Alla Norma batch, this couscous salad’s tangy, herby and cheesy. It's super easy to make for a speedy dinner or lunch.
instructions: Make the Aubergine Alla Norma batch recipe.
Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the giant couscous and cook according to the pack instructions. Drain, then rinse under cold water until cool.
Meanwhile, pick the basil leaves and tear them into bite-sized pieces.
Tip the cooked couscous into a bowl with the aubergine alla norma. Season with salt and black pepper, then splash in some balsamic vinegar to taste.
Fold through the rocket and basil, then spoon onto plates. Crumble over the feta and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Giant Couscous Herb Salad
description: Here's a lovely couscous dish that you can use as a base for a wide range of proteins. It's really, really delicious.
keywords: chicken chorizo air fryer recipe uk
instructions: Start by cooking the couscous in boiling, salted water for 6 mins. Drain and rinse in cold water.
Mix the drained couscous with spinach. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Pick the herbs and finely slice the red onion. Mix together in a bowl.
Serve the couscous topped with a main of your choice and the herb salad. Finish with a drizzle of oil and a sprinkling of sumac.

name: Giant Crispy Chicken Summer Rolls with Spicy Peanut Sauce
description: Summer rolls are one of those things I'm completely obsessed with in summer but every time I make them I remember why I'd rather buy them. Enter my giant summer rolls which make  them much quicker to assemble and great for taking to work.
keywords: Giant Crispy Chicken Summer Rolls with Spicy Peanut Sauce
Giant Crispy Chicken Summer Rolls with Spicy Peanut Sauce recipe
instructions: Cook the breaded chicken breasts according to the packet instructions. Once cooked, slice into pieces and set aside.

While the chicken cooks, make the sauce. Squeeze the juice of the lime into a small bowl and add the peanut butter, sriracha, soy sauce and honey. Mix together, then loosen with a little water until it reaches the consistency of double cream. Set aside.

Shred the carrot, red pepper, cucumber, red cabbage and spring onions into thin matchsticks and set aside in separate bowls. Slice the avocado. Pick the coriander, or leave the stalks on if you like, which gives you more flavour and a bit of texture. Carefully peel away the iceberg lettuce leaves, keeping them as whole as possible, they'll act as a bowl to hold the shredded veg inside the roll.

Fill a large shallow dish or bowl with cold water. Soak the rice paper sheets, three at a time, until just pliable - don't over-soak or they'll tear.You'll need 3 sheets per summer roll - I've added 3 spare to the ingredients list so you'll have some to hand in case any rip.

Lay the three sheets slightly overlapping each other in a circle on a clean, damp tea towel. Layer an iceberg leaf on top, then fill with a handful of each of the shredded vegetables, some avocado, chicken and coriander. Fold in the short edges of the rice paper, then roll tightly from the bottom long edge up to seal like a burrito, using the tea towel to help if needed. If you get a hole in the rice paper, don't panic just soak three more sheets, lay the damaged roll in the centre and wrap it up again to double seal. Repeat with the remaining fillings.
To serve, cut your summer rolls in half with the peanut sauce alongside, or box up and pop in the fridge ready to grab when you need them for lunch.

name: Gilda Fried Olives
description: Taking the iconic Gilda pintxo and turning it into the perfect sharing plate. Anchovy-stuffed olives, breaded and fried until crispy. Served with a mustard mayo and a chilled glass of dry Fino Sherry. Salty, briny and creamy.
instructions: Drain both the olives and anchovies. Stuff one anchovy fillet into each olive, place onto a kitchen paper lined plate.
Into a bowl, add the mayonnaise and wholegrain mustard. Mix together, taste and season with guindilla chilli brine, set aside.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, whisk together. Pour the breadcrumbs and flour into two separate bowls.

Take each olive and toss through the flour, then dip into the egg and coat with breadcrumbs, back into the egg and once more into the breadcrumbs. Continue until all the olives have been breaded. Place onto a clean, dry plate.

Pour the oil into a saucepan, making sure it doesn’t fill it more than halfway up. Place on medium-high heat. Once it reaches about 180°C (test by dipping the edge of the olive into the oil, it should bubble), start frying the olives in batches, until golden and crispy.
Onto cocktail sticks, thread the top of a Guindilla chilli, followed by a fried olive, and the bottom of the Guindilla chilli, so the olive is encased on both sides. Enjoy with some chilled sherry.

name: Gilda Pasta
description: Inspired by my friend Anna Fraser (@chefannafrazer), this is my version of her Gilda Pasta, chock full of anchovies and peppers and pickled Guindilla chillis for a seriously punchy pasta, ready to upgrade your weeknight rotation.
instructions: Roughly chop the olives, removing the stones if they aren't pitted already, then drain and finely chop the roasted peppers. Finely slice the pickled guindilla chillies, then finely chop the garlic and parsley.
Get a big pot of salted water on to boil for the pasta. Once boiling, add the linguine and cook until al dente, reserving some of the cooking water before you drain.

Meanwhile, heat a large frying pan over a medium heat and add 8 anchovies (for 4 servings) along with the oil from the tin, plus the olive oil. Cook, stirring, until the anchovies have broken down into the oil. Add the garlic and cook for a minute, then add the roasted peppers, pickled guindilla chillies, olives and smoked paprika and cook for another minute.

Turn the heat to low and, using tongs, grab the pasta and add it straight into the anchovy sauce. Grate in the Parmesan and ladle in some of the cooking water, mixing well to melt the Parmesan and emulsify the sauce. Keep mixing vigorously and adding splashes of pasta water until the sauce is really glossy and clinging onto the pasta.
Grate in the lemon zest and squeeze in the juice, then add the parsley. Mix and taste, adjusting the seasoning with salt and pepper, or more lemon if needed.
Serve up with a drizzle of the extra virgin olive oil.

name: Ginger & Chilli Chicken Brothy Rice
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

We've done it, Mob. We've created the best chicken and rice recipe on the planet. You'll be making this one all of the time.
keywords: Ginger & Chilli Chicken Brothy Rice recipe
instructions: Grate half the garlic into a large bowl, then squeeze in the juice of half the lime and season with salt. Add the chicken and marinate in the fridge for at least 30 mins.
Meanwhile, finely slice the remaining garlic, cut the ginger into matchsticks and finely slice the chilli.

Place a frying pan with a drizzle of oil over a medium heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken and cook on both sides until slightly charred and cooked through (this will take 10-15 mins, depending on the thickness of your chicken). Transfer the chicken to a plate to rest.

Add the ginger, garlic and chilli to the pan, fry for 3 mins, then add the curry powder. Cook for 1 min. Pour in the stock and simmer for 5 mins. Remove from the heat and finish with juice of the remaining lime half and season with salt.
Pick the herb leaves and finely slice the red onion. Combine in a bowl.
Reheat the cooked rice and divide between serving bowls. Pour in the curry broth and top with sliced chicken and a scattering of herb salad.

name: Ginger & Chilli Tofu Scramble
description: This saucy, spicy, flavourful tofu dish is perfect for brunch, lunch or dinner. It’s thrown together in one pan with minimal prep and is packed with protein.
instructions: Mince the garlic cloves and slice the tomatoes in half. Peel and mince the ginger. Squeeze the tofu block in a tea towel over the sink to remove some of the water.

Heat a good drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan. Add the tomatoes and garlic and plenty of salt and cook for 3-4 mins on medium high heat until the tomatoes have softened. You can squash them down slightly to help them release their juices.
Add the spices and cook for a minute until fragrant, then add the tinned tomatoes. (If using plum tomatoes, break them down with a spatula or potato masher or with your hands.)

Then add the ginger and soy sauce and stir to combine. Crumble the tofu into the pan in large chunks (as it will break down into smaller pieces afterwards). Cook on low for about 3-5 mins, stirring occasionally.

Taste and season with salt and pepper. Finely chop the spring onion. Top the tofu with the crispy chilli oil, spring onion, coriander leaves and sesame seeds. This is lovely served both hot and at room temperature.

name: Ginger & Soy Steamed Salmon
description: Sticky salmon with ginger, lime and soy steamed in one parcel, perfect for evenings when you want to keep washing up to a minimum.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Peel and grate the ginger and garlic. Add to a bowl with the soy sauce, the zest of the lime and the juice of half of it. Pat the salmon fillets dry, then spoon over the marinade. Leave to marinate for 10 mins.

Finely slice the chilli. Cut the remaining lime into wedges. Lay out a large sheet of parchment paper per person, portrait. Add the rice and kale, then place the salmon on top, leaving a 10cm gap between the food and the edge closest to you. Drizzle over any leftover marinade. Scatter with the sesame seeds and chilli.

Fold the top half of the baking paper over the food then fold the outside edges over each other to seal (like a cornish pasty), creating a steam-tight parcel. Bake for 15–20 mins, depending on the thickness of your salmon.
Remove from the oven and serve with the lime wedges on the side.

name: Ginger & Spring Onion Chicken Broth
description: The most heart-warming soup. Crispy chicken skin and chilli oil deliciously contrast with the lightness of the gingery chicken broth.
keywords: Spring onion and ginger chicken soup recipes
instructions: Remove the skin from chicken and chop it up into small bits. Using a pair of cooking scissors helps to cut through the thick fat.
Roughly chop the spring onions and ginger. Slice the garlic bulb in half.
Add a glug of oil to the pan and gently cook the ginger, sliced garlic bulb and chopped spring onions for 2 mins until they're fragrant but haven't taken on any colour in the pan.
Add in the whole de-skinnned chicken and enough cold water to cover the chicken. Simmer for 1 hour until the chicken is cooked.
Take the chicken out of the stock and pull off the meat. Add the bones back into the stock and allow to simmer on a gentle heat for as long as you can. It'll need 1 hour at the very least.
To make the chilli oil, bash up the garlic, ginger and red chillies in a pestle and mortar with a large pinch of flaky sea salt to form a chunky paste.

Heat up a saucepan with the chicken fat and a small glug of olive oil. Fry until golden and crispy on a very low heat for 5 mins. Then add in the chilli paste and cook for a further 10 mins on a very low heat until the skin is crispy and the oil is stained red.
Cook the udon noodles following packet instructions.
Meanwhile, finely slice the spring onions and chop the coriander for the garnish.
Strain the soup and season with soy sauce and white pepper.
Add the udon to a bowl, ladle over the soup. Top with the shredded chicken, chilli oil, sliced spring onions and chopped coriander.

name: Ginger Basil Noodles
description: Taking your packet noodles to the highest level with a spicy chilli kick and a soft boiled egg on top. Ginger & basil work a charm. It's gonna rock your worlds.
instructions: Cut your spring onions into slices. Cut the ginger into matchsticks. Chop the garlic into discs. Finely chop the basil.
For the sauce, mix together your chilli oil, soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil and sugar. Set aside.

Get a wok over a medium heat and pour in a glug vegetable oil. Add the ginger and spring onions (saving a few for garnish) and fry for 3 minutes until they lightly colour, then scrape in the garlic. Cook for 2 more minutes.
In another pan, boil your water and add the stock cube. Once dissolved add your noodles and cook until soft, according to packet instructions.

Get the wok back on the heat and place in the drained noodles (without tipping away the water) along with your chilli sauce and basil (saving some for garnish). Toss everything together and mix it well.
In the leftover noodle water, boil your eggs for 5 minutes then remove and place in cold water to stop them from cooking and help to remove the outer shells.

You’re now ready to plate up. Dish your noodles into four bowls, peel your eggs and place them on top. Finally, add a drizzle of chilli oil, your remaining basil and spring onions then tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Ginger Chicken & Brothy Greens Soup
description: A freezer-friendly, chuck-it-all-in chicken soup that cooks straight from frozen. A seriously nourishing soup perfect for warming you up on those drizzly winter days.
keywords: ginger chicken and brothy greens recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the spring onions and finely grate the ginger and garlic. Add them to a freezer-safe container, then top with the watercress. Lay the chicken thighs on top and pour over the soy sauce, white pepper and chicken stock. Close and pop your container in the freezer.

When you're ready to cook, tip the frozen block into a large saucepan and place it over a medium heat. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15-20 mins, or until the chicken is fully cooked through and tender.
Using two forks, shred the chicken into pieces directly in the pan.
Ladle the soup into bowls and finish with a drizzle of chilli oil, if using. Dig in!

name: Ginger Chicken Sesame Rice
description: These perfectly cooked easy crispy chicken thighs on a bed of sesame rice will become part of your midweek staple. Paired with a punchy, tangy ginger oil sauce for dipping or pouring.
instructions: Tip the rice into a bowl, then wash it thoroughly. Drain, then repeat twice or until the water runs clear. Set aside.
Thinly slice the chives. Finely mince ¾ of the garlic cloves and the pak choi. Set aside on separate plates.

Heat a saucepan over a medium-high heat for 1 min. Add the sesame oil followed by the minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds. Add the pak choi and fry for a further 1-2 mins. Add the rice and stir to toast for 1 min. Add the chicken stock, a pinch of salt and a few cracks of black pepper. Put the lid on a bring to a boil. Once boiling, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 18 mins. Once cooked, turn the heat off, add the chives and sesame seeds, then gently mix to combine. Set aside.
Finely mince the ginger, spring onions, coriander and remaining garlic clove, or blend in a blender. Transfer to a bowl and add a pinch of salt and the MSG. Set aside.

Add the vegetable oil to a saucepan set over a high heat. Heat for 1-2 mins, or until just shy of smoking. Gently pour the oil over the ginger mixture and stir. Add the lime juice, sriracha, vinegar, dark soy sauce and 1 tsp sesame oil. Mix to combine.

Pat the skin side of the chicken dry with kitchen paper and season with a pinch of salt. Add the chicken skin-side down into a cold, dry, frying pan. Turn the heat to medium and cook for 5-7 mins. Flip the chicken onto the flesh side and cook for a further 5 mins, or until cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and rest for 1-2 mins.
Slice the chicken into 2-3cm pieces. Add the rice to a plate followed by the chicken. Put the sauce in a little dish and place on the side, or spoon over the sauce. Finish with fresh mint leaves.

name: Ginger Garlic Rice, Crispy Chicken & Spicy Slaw
description: Crispy-skinned chicken, aromatic ginger-garlic rice, and a zingy, crunchy slaw. This bold, spicy, umami-packed bowl hits all the right notes.
instructions: Debone the chicken but leave the skin on. Mince the garlic and ginger and thinly slice the shallot.

Make the rice. Heat the sesame oil and vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the shallots and fry for 3–5 mins until golden at the edges. Stir in the garlic, ginger and rice, and toast gently for 2 mins.

Pour in the chicken stock, add a pinch of salt, and bring to a boil. Cover with a lid, reduce to the lowest heat, and simmer for 18 mins. Once cooked, remove from the heat and let it steam with the lid on until ready to serve.

Pat the chicken thighs dry with kitchen paper, then season both sides with salt. Lay them skin-side down in a cold non-stick frying pan. Place over medium heat and cook for 7–9 mins until the skin is golden and crisp. Flip and cook for another 3 mins. Set aside to rest.

Make the slaw. Thinly slice the red cabbage, white cabbage, and bird’s eye chilli. Finely julienne the carrot and finely chop the coriander. In a bowl, combine all the slaw ingredients. Mix well until the sugar dissolves and the cabbage starts to soften.
Assemble. Slice the chicken into 1–2cm strips. Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the crispy chicken, and serve with a generous side of slaw. Drizzle over extra kecap manis and chilli oil to finish.

name: Ginger Lemon Lentil Porridge
description: Inspired by Khicidi (or Khichri) with plenty of gentle lentils, this recipe is a great source of protein and nutrition. We added lots of lemon ginger and aromatic ginger sesame oil for a proper warming bowl of serious cosy goodness.
instructions: Finely dice the onion, garlic and mince the fresh ginger using a microplane or the fine-side of a box grater. Slice the spring onions and set it aside for garnishing.

In a medium-sized sauce pan on medium heat, add a heaped Tbsp of coconut oil and onions with ½ a tsp of salt, then cook for 8 mins, or until lightly golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 mins or until aromatic. Add in half the cherry tomatoes and cook for 2 mins, using a spatula to smoosh them into the pan as they blister. Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, pepper, honey, and soy sauce and cook for 1 minute to release their aroma. Add lentils and rice and stir for 1 min or until the rice smells fragrant - make sure to control the heat as you don’t want anything to burn. Pour in all the stock ingredients, and squeeze in the juice from 1 whole lemon, then chuck in the whole lemon itself. Add in the tomato vines for extra flavor, mix well and bring to the boil, then reduce to the lowest heat and simmer for 30 mins. Stir halfway through to make sure nothing is sticking to the bottom of the pan.
In the meantime, make the ginger oil by combining minced ginger, a finely sliced spring onion into a small bowl with all the remaining ingredients into a small bowl, mixing well.

After 30 mins, remove the discard the tomato vines and use 2 spoons to squeeze out all the hot jammy lemon juice, and then discard. With a whisk carefully whisk vigorously, just until it is creamy. Optionally, add another cup of stock if you’d prefer a looser consistency. Pour in all the remaining cherry tomatoes, put a lid on and simmer for 5 mins or just until the tomatoes begin to pop. Taste for seasoning, especially if more stock was added, you may need a pinch more salt.
Serve into bowls and spoon over generous amounts of ginger oil, fresh spring onion, and a wedge of lemon.

name: Ginger Pork Patties
description: Juicy little pork patties with a gingery warmth, perfect with rice and cucumber for the kids, and a mellow spring onion oil drizzle for grown-ups.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Peel and finely grate the ginger. Peel and coarsely grate the carrot. Finely chop the garlic. Trim and finely slice the spring onions.

Add the ginger, carrot, garlic, spring onions, pork mince, soy sauce, honey, cornflour, a pinch of salt and some black pepper to a large bowl. Use your hands to mix everything together until well combined.
Shape the mixture into small patties — about the size of a golf ball, then flatten slightly.
Heat a drizzle of sunflower oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Fry the patties in batches for 3–4 mins on each side until golden brown and cooked through.

If making the spring onion oil for the adults, finely slice the remaining spring onions and pop them into a heatproof bowl. Heat the sunflower oil in a small pan until just smoking, then carefully pour over the spring onions. Let it sit for a few mins to mellow. 
Slice the chilli.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Serve the patties however your kids like. We've gone with sliced cucumber and cooked jasmine rice.
Parents Plate: Top the patties on the rice, add a drizzle of soy sauce, spring onion oil, a scattering of chopped chilli, coriander and a squeeze of lime.

name: Ginger Soy Prawn Ceviche
description: A simple homemade prawn ceviche recipe that's really refreshing. It's perfect for scooping with salted tortilla chips.
instructions: Skip this step if you’re using cooked prawns. Bring a saucepan of water to the boil, add a pinch of salt and add the prawns. Give it one stir and turn the heat off. Let it sit for 5 mins, then drain. Transfer to a bowl of ice-cold water. Set aside.
Zest a lime, the ginger and garlic into a large bowl. Add the soy sauce, juice of all the limes, yuzu juice, a pinch of salt and a few cracks of black pepper. Stir to combine.
Drain the prawns and dice each prawn into quarters. Add the prawns to the lime juice mixture and give it a mix.
Add the chilli flakes, paprika and cumin seeds to a small bowl. Heat a splash of oil over a high heat until slightly smoking, then add to the bowl. Stir well to combine.

Dice the cucumber, tomatoes, pepper, red onion and jalapeño as small as possible. Slice the coriander as fine as possible. Transfer everything to the bowl of prawns. Add the chilli oil and mix thoroughly until everything is combined.
Transfer to a plate or bowl and serve with your favourite tortilla chips.

name: Gingerbread
description: This classic festive biscuit is easy to bake and full of flavour. The dough is super forgiving and can be re-rolled countless times without changing the taste. Make it for Christmas or year-round.
instructions: Cut the butter into cubes then add to a medium saucepan set over a low heat, along with the sugar and golden syrup. Heat gently until the butter is melted, stirring occasionally, then turn up the heat and bubble away for a minute. Remove from the heat.

Measure the bicarb, spices and plain flour into a bowl. Tip everything into the saucepan and beat together until you have a smooth dough – at this point it will be sticky and wet, don’t worry it will firm up as it cools.
Put the dough into the fridge to set for 30 mins (you can leave it in the saucepan).
Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Line a couple of baking trays with baking paper.

Lightly flour a clean surface then roll out the gingerbread to roughly ½ cm thickness. Cut out whatever shapes you like from the dough and place them on the lined tray. Once you’ve cut out your biscuits, simply re-form the dough and re-roll, then repeat until all your biscuits have been stamped out.

Bake in the centre of the oven for 10-12 mins until the biscuits are slightly puffed up, darkening at the edges and firm. Leave to cool for 5 mins on the tray then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Once cool, mix the icing sugar with the water to form a thick icing then drizzle or pipe onto your gingerbread shapes.

name: Gingery Burst Tomatoes & Sardines with Rice
description: Burst cherry tomatoes, a ginger-spiked sauce and tinned sardines, it's pantry cooking at its best. Punchy, savoury and on the table in under 20 mins.
instructions: Thinly slice the garlic. Peel the ginger and cut the into thin strips.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 6-7 mins, until they start to darken in spots and burst open. Add the garlic and ginger, season with salt and stir-fry for a minute. Squish the tomatoes down with a fork to release the juices, then pour in the water along with the soy sauce and sesame oil. Cook for another 5-6 mins, until the sauce has thickened slightly.
Drain the sardines and add them to the pan. Cook for another minute until warmed through.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Then share between bowls, and top with the sardines. Finish with the fresh coriander.

name: Gingery Roast Chicken with Brown Rice & Avocado Salad
description: This ones for all the ginger lovers out there. From being roasted in with the chicken, fried crisp for scattering, and pickled in the chunky avocado salad, this recipe uses ginger to the max to make the ultimate fragrant rice bowl.
keywords: Triple Ginger Roast Chicken with Brown Rice & Avocado Salad
Triple Ginger Roast Chicken with Brown Rice & Avocado Salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel the ginger for the chicken and slice into 1cm slices.  Arrange the chicken thighs in a roasting tin with the neutral oil, the sliced ginger, the unpeeled garlic cloves and a good pinch of salt, tossing so everything is coated, then roast for 40-45 mins, until the skin is deeply golden and crisp and the chicken is cooked through.

While the chicken is cooking make the crispy ginger. Cut the remaining ginger into fine matchsticks and finely slice the garlic. Heat the neutral oil in a small frying pan over a medium heat and fry the ginger matchsticks for 2-3 mins, until golden and crisp, then add the garlic and cook for another minute, until lightly golden. Lift out with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper.
Dice the avocados and finely chop the pickled ginger. Combine in a bowl with the pickled ginger liquid and a pinch of salt, tossing gently so the avocado stays in chunky pieces.
Once the chicken is ready and resting, heat the brown rice according to the packet instructions.

Add the light soy sauce to the chicken so it mixes with the roasting juices. Serve the chicken over the brown rice with the avocado salad alongside, scattered with the crispy ginger and garlic, and the roasted garlic cloves for squeezing over.

name: Gingery Tomato Rice with Soy-Roasted Mushrooms
description: A fresh and fragrant dinner recipe that proves you don't need meat to have a filling dinner.
keywords: Gingery Tomato Rice with Soy-Roasted Mushrooms
Gingery Tomato Rice with Soy-Roasted Mushrooms recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Slice or grate the mushrooms, then put them onto a baking tray with the sesame oil, soy sauce and a big pinch of ground white pepper. Mix well to coat and roast for 25 mins.

Meanwhile, finely chop the garlic then peel and finely chop the ginger. Heat a splash of olive oil in a large lidded saucepan set over a medium heat and add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 5 mins. Add the tomato purée and turmeric and cook for 2 mins until thickened. Add the rice, chopped tomatoes and stock, stir and pop a lid on. Cook for 30 mins until the rice is cooked but still a bit soupy. Throw in your spinach and give it a mix once it's looking ready.
Deseed and finely chop the chilli. Finely chop the spring onions and pick the coriander. Serve the rice in bowls topped with the mushrooms, spring onions, coriander and chilli.

name: Glazed Cajun Meatballs & Charred Spring Onion Romesco
description: Rich and delicious meatballs coated in a spicy cajun glaze. This is a great dinner when you've got a craving for something meaty.
keywords: Glazed Cajun Meatballs & Charred Spring Onion Romesco
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Put the pork mince in a bowl. Peel the garlic and onion and grate them both into the pork bowl. Finely chop half of the parsley.
Add the chopped parsley, half the Worcestershire sauce and half the cajun seasoning to the meat bowl. Season with plenty of salt and mix thoroughly. Form into 12 meatballs.

Trim the spring onions. Put a large frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add half the spring onions and cook for 5-8 mins until charred and starting to soften. Transfer the onions to a blender. Drain the roasted peppers and add them to the blender, along with the smoked almonds and remaining cajun seasoning. Blend until smooth, then taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.

Pour 3 tbsp of olive oil into the same frying pan and set over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the meatballs and fry for 10-12 mins until cooked through. When cooked, add the honey, mustard and remaining Worcestershire sauce. Stir together until glazed.
Meanwhile, pop the flatbreads in the oven to warm up.

Thinly slice the remaining spring onions. Spread the romesco onto plates or a serving platter. Top with the glazed meatballs, drizzling over any sauce. Finish with the sliced spring onions, remaining parsley leaves and sesame seeds. Serve with flatbreads.

name: Glazed Gammon Joint
description: This glazed gammon joint recipe couldn’t be simpler and tastes a million miles better than the slices you get from the supermarket. Make sure to buy a gammon with the fat and rind attached. Just roast it in the oven and you’ll be living off glazed gammon in the weeks to come.
instructions: Peel the onion then cut it in half. Slice the orange in half too, then put both into your largest, widest saucepan along with the bay leaves. Place the gammon on top then pour in enough cold water to submerge the gammon.

Put the pan over a medium heat and bring the water to the boil. Once boiling, use a spoon to skim off any white foam that has risen to the surface then turn down the heat and simmer gently, uncovered, for 1 hour. Top up with more water if the pan needs it –you want the gammon to always be just covered by the water.

Line a roasting tin well with two layers of foil , leaving enough foil overlapping at each end to wrap the gammon in later. After 1 hour, carefully lift the gammon joint into the lined tin and leave until cool enough to handle. Discard the cooking water and gubbins.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 180°C. Mix the treacle and the mustard together in a small bowl.

Once the gammon is cool enough to touch (about 15 minutes later), cut away any string from the gammon, if it’s been tied, then use a small sharp knife to cut off the outer layer of skin and discard. Using the same knife, score a diagonal pattern evenly across the fat.

Spread the treacle mustard mixture all over the gammon, then cover loosely with the foil. Roast for 15 minutes then uncover, and roast for a further 20 minutes, until the outside of the ham is nicely caramelised but the meat is still juicy.
Leave to cool then cut into slices. It’s unreal in a sarnie with more mustard, eaten with egg and chips or even fried up for carbonara.

name: Glazed Pigs in Blankets
description: An incredible Christmas side dish. These piggies are glazed in an umami-rich sauce and roasted with sprouts. Charred. Sticky. Delicious. She's a belter.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C/374°F.
Chop the ends off your Brussels sprouts and cut them in half.
Make your glaze. Combine your Lee Kum Kee Plum Sauce, Lee Kum Kee Premium Oyster Sauce, sugar, lemon juice, 1 tbsp of vegetable oil and water in a bowl. Set aside.
Take a sausage and twist it in half. Cut the central point with scissors to create two mini sausages, then repeat with your remaining sausages. Wrap each sausage in one slice of bacon.
Pour your sprouts into a large baking dish and arrange your pigs in blankets over the top. Pour over your glaze, season with pepper, then roast for 25-30 mins.
Serve alongside all your other Christmas classics.

name: Gluten-Free Banana Chia Bread
description: We’ve made this gluten-free banana bread with ground almonds, buckwheat flour and chia seeds. It’s moist and just the right amount of sweet.
instructions: Heat the oven to 150°C fan. Grease a 1lb loaf tin and line with baking paper.
If your bananas aren’t ripe, place them onto a baking tray and bake in the oven for 10-15 mins until blackened and soft to the touch.
Add the bananas into a bowl and mash until smooth. Melt the butter in a small pan over a low heat.
Whisk the eggs and melted butter into the bananas. Add the milk and mix to combine.

In another bowl, mix together the caster sugar, ground almonds, buckwheat flour, gluten-free flour, gluten-free oats, chia seeds, gluten-free baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt. Fold this dry mixture into the banana mixture until just combined.

Pour the batter into the prepared tin (it should fill until almost to the top – leave 2cm). Slice the banana in half lengthways and pop it on top of the cake batter, along with the pecans and demerara sugar.
Bake for 50-60 mins or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean. Transfer to a wire rack to cool. Enjoy at room temp or toasted and topped with a pat of cold butter, if you like.

name: Gnocchi Al Pesto Genovese
description: We’ve kept the ingredients for this pesto very classic, but adapted it to work in a small blender which means that it all happens super fast and easy. Bright, vibrant and creamy, toss the pesto with fluffy gnocchi and crisp beans for a beautiful weeknight dinner.
instructions: In a small blender, pulse the pine nuts into a crumb. Mince the garlic, then add along with a pinch of salt and pulse again. Add the basil and pulse until smooth. Add half of the Parmesan, and pulse again to combine. Repeat with the remaining Parmesan.
Empty the contents of the blender into a bowl and stream in the extra virgin olive oil whilst stirring continuously.
Cook the gnocchi and green beans in boiling salted water until the gnocchi start to float to the surface. Drain and reserve some of the cooking water.
Toss the gnocchi with the pesto and add splashes of cooking water until you reach a creamy consistency.

name: Gnocchi Amatriciana
description: Toss your steaming hot, plump gnocchi with this rich, bacony, classic Italian sauce. An absolute belter of a dish.
instructions: Heat your oven to 220°C.
Pour your cherry tomatoes into a baking dish and drizzle with olive oil and salt. Pop in the oven and roast until they start to soften, 10-15 minutes.
Finely dice your red onion. Mince your garlic and your chilli.

Whilst your tomatoes cook, pop a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add a little glug of olive oil and add your onion. Fry for 10 minutes until softened, then add your pancetta to the pan. Fry for another 5 minutes until your pancetta is crisp and your onions have begun to caramelise.

Add your minced garlic and minced chilli to the pan and cook out for 2 minutes. Pour your passata into the pan and bring to a simmer. Turn down the heat and cook for 20 minutes until it has reduced into a delicious, jammy sauce.
Once the tomatoes have softened, tip the gnocchi in the tray with a glug of olive oil. Season with salt, give it a good stir and return it to the oven for another 10-15 mins.
Once the gnocchi is cooked, stir the sauce through. If you'd like it saucier, stir through a splash of boiling water. Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Serve up in bowls and sprinkle with a generous scattering of parmesan and torn up basil. Dig in.

name: Gnocchi Carbonara
description: Soft, pillowy gnocchi in a classic carbonara sauce. Your favourite pasta dish but even more comforting. It’s creamy, salty and hits the spot.
