instructions: Dice the pancetta. Add it to a cold frying pan set over a medium heat and cook until it’s rendered and crisp. Take off the heat and set aside.
Grate the pecorino and Parmesan cheeses. Whisk together the eggs, egg yolks, grated cheeses, black pepper and nutmeg in a bowl.
Cook the gnocchi following pack instructions then drain, saving the water.
Add the gnocchi to the pancetta, then add the egg yolk mixture with a splash of the cooking water. Mix vigorously until emulsified.
To serve, top with some extra grated Parmesan and some more black pepper, if you like.

name: Gnocchi Ragù
description: Chorizo takes this ragù to the next level. With piping hot gnocchi stirred through at the end - it is a phenomenal dish. A real show-stopper.
instructions: Slice up all your veg in to nice small pieces. Cube up your chorizo. Gently soften the garlic, onion, celery, chorizo and carrot in a heavy bottomed pan. Once softened, add the beef and the skinned sausage meat and continue frying until well browned.

At this point, pour in the red wine and let evaporate. Add the tinned tomatoes, the bay leaves and thyme. Add the rind of the parmesan, give it a stir, cover with a lid and leave to simmer on a low heat for 50 minutes.
After 50 minutes, your ragu should be nice and thick. Remove the lid, take out the Parmesan rind and the bay leaves, give it a stir and season to taste.
At this point, add your gnocchi straight in to the ragu. Cook for 8 minutes until it is cooked through. Serve the gnocchi into bowls with extra parmesan grated on top. Enjoy!

name: Gnocchi with Smashed Peas, Lemon & Parmesan
description: This is my smashed pea gnocchi. It's a stunner of a summer dish and dead simple. You can use fresh peas if you like, but frozen really are the best. B x
instructions: Add all but a handful of the frozen peas to a blender or pestle and mortar and pulse/smash until pulpy.
Trim and slice the asparagus, and roughly chop the basil.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil, season with salt and blanch the gnocchi until they float to the top. Fish them out into a bowl and coat with a dash of oil. Grab yourself a mugful of the cooking water and save that for later.
Zest and juice the lemon and set aside for later.
Blanch the asparagus and that extra handful of peas for 1 min, drain and set aside.
Now, heat a large frying pan over a high heat. Add a shot of oil and let that get nice and hot.
Add the gnocchi and cook until golden brown. Keep the gnocchi moving regularly.
Add the butter and cook until brown and the gnocchi is glazed and nut brown.
Add a splash of the cooking water, the smashed peas and the crème fraîche. Toss everything together to create a beautifully green sauce. Finish with the lemon juice, to taste.
Turn off the heat. Season with salt and black pepper. Add lemon zest, Parmesan, the blanched veg and chopped basil.
Keep tossing everything together until glossy and gorgeous. Adjust the seasoning if you need to.
Divide between warm plates, top with more Parmesan and black pepper and get stuck in.

name: Goat's Cheese & Pesto Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
description: You are going to love the contrast here between the fresh balsamic tomato salad and the meaty, cheesy grilled mushrooms with rich nutty pine nuts.
keywords: Goat's Cheese & Pesto Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
instructions:
Pull out the middle stalk from each mushroom and keep for
another time (fry in butter and have with scrambled eggs). Put
the mushrooms, hole-side-up, on a large baking tray and dollop
a spoonful of pesto into each hole. Cut the goat’s cheese logs
into four rounds each (to give eight rounds in total) and plonk one
round onto each mushroom. Drizzle with olive oil and season with
salt and black pepper. Place under the hot grill for 8 mins.
Meanwhile, halve the cherry tomatoes and mix these with the
salad leaves in a mixing bowl. Drizzle with a little olive oil and
season with salt, pepper and balsamic vinegar to taste. Divide the
salad between four plates.
Get a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the pine nuts and toast
until golden brown, shaking occasionally, then turn off the heat.
Use a fish slice or spatula to put two grilled mushrooms on top of
each salad and scatter over the toasted pine nuts to serve.

name: Goat’s Cheese & Charred Peach Lentil Salad
description: This one’s a salad that won’t feel like a salad. Crispy charred bits, sweet fruity peaches and honeyed chilli hazelnuts make it a real winner. You haven't had a lentil salad recipe like this before.
keywords: Goat’s Cheese & Charred Peach Lentil Salad
Goat’s Cheese & Charred Peach Lentil Salad recipe
instructions: Trim the ends off the green beans and cut the peaches in half and remove their stones. Drain the green lentils through a sieve.

Scatter the hazelnuts into a small frying pan over a medium heat and toast for 2 minutes, tossing regularly until browned. Roughly chop them, then tip back into the frying pan and set over a medium heat. Add two-thirds of the honey along with the chilli flakes and a pinch of salt, then toss together for a minute until sticky and glazed. Set aside to cool.

Heat a large griddle pan over a high heat for a few minutes until really hot. Drizzle the green beans with olive oil then scatter into the pan in one even layer and grill for 2 mins, turning halfway, until charred and cooked through. Tip into a large bowl with the green lentils and rocket.
Lay the peaches, cut side down, into the hot griddle pan and cook for 2-3 mins until really charred, then drizzle over the remaining honey to caramelise.
Drizzle oil and the balsamic vinegar into the salad bowl with the beans, lentils and rocket and toss everything together with some salt and cracked black pepper.
Divide between four plates, then top with the charred peach halves and crumble over the goat’s cheese. Finally, scatter with the honeyed chilli hazelnuts.

name: Gobi Manchurian
description: This popular Indo-Chinese cauliflower recipe from Antony Amourdoux is a real crowdpleaser. You'll love how sweet, sticky, and spicy it is.
instructions: Blanch the florets. In a large pot, bring the water to a boil, add the salt and add the cauliflower and blanch for about 3 mins. Transfer to cold water to keep the crunch.

Separately, in another bowl, mix the ingredients for the batter until fully combined (note: the batter should be more thick than runny). In a deep pan heat up the oil, dip the florets and coat them thoroughly with the batter and deep fry until golden brown. Set aside.

On to the sauce. Start by finely chopping your garlic cloves and fresh ginger. Deseed your green chillies and slice them up. Chop up your spring onion. Dice your green pepper into small cubes. In a large pan heat up the oil and sauté the garlic, ginger and green chillies on high flame, for about 2mins. Add the white ends of the spring onion and peppers sauté until they slightly change colour. Add the tomato sauce, vinegar, soy sauce, pepper, and salt. Mix well and sauté for a minute. Mix the cornflour and water to make a slurry. Add the slurry to the sauce and give it a good mix until the gravy slightly thickens and turns translucent.
Time to plate up. Add your fried cauliflower into the sauce and coat evenly, transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with chopped green spring onions.

name: Gochujang & Tomato Soup With Crispy Chickpea Croutons
description: A spicy plant-based soup with caramelised gochujang and a creamy coconut broth. Ideal when you're feeling under the weather.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan.
Peel and cube the sweet potato. Peel and chop the onion and roughly chop the red pepper. Drain the chickpeas.

Add the sweet potato, onion, red pepper and tomatoes to a large, lined baking tray. Add the chickpeas to a separate tray (or use the same tray but keep them separate). Drizzle with olive oil and roast for 20-25 mins until everything is soft and starting to caramelise. Remove from the oven and set aside.

Heat a little olive oil in a medium sized pot over a medium heat then add the smoked paprika and gochujang. Fry for a minute or two until the spices start to brown, then add the roasted vegetables, keeping the chickpeas to the side for topping.
Pour in the coconut milk (reserve a tiny drizzle for the end), water, soy sauce, rice vinegar and stock cube and summer for 10 mins. Use a hand or stand blender to blitz until smooth.
Roughly chop the peanuts and slice the green parts of the spring onion.
To serve, ladle the soup into bowls and top with the crispy chickpeas, sliced spring onion and chopped peanuts. Finish with a drizzle of crispy chilli oil and reserved coconut milk.

name: Gochujang Alaska Pollock Burger
description: Gochujang originates from Korea - it is a spicy & tangy fermented chilli rice paste. It works a charm in this crispy pollock patty, with a special burger sauce.
instructions: To start, finely grate your garlic and 1 knob of ginger into a bowl. Add 2 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp gochujang and a squeeze of lemon. Mix together and set aside.
Next, heat a glug of oil and fry your pollock until white in colour (for about 2 minutes).
Once you have fried your pollock, place in a bowl and roughly break it up. Add your breadcrumbs and sauce (prepared in step 1) then mix together so that the fish is fully coated.
Take a handful of this mixture and mould into a patty shape. Repeat until you get 4 patties then set aside ready for frying.
Slice your red cabbage and add to a bowl along with your beansprouts.
In a separate bowl mix together 3 tbsps of oil, sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey and the other knob of grated ginger. Mix until combined then add this to your red cabbage and mix it through.
For the burger sauce, mix together 2 tbsp mayo and 1/2 tbsp gochujang then set aside.
Now for your patty. Heat a glug of oil in a pan and fry each patty until crispy and golden brown then remove.
Then, cut your brioche buns in half and toast both sides, then you’re ready to layer up.
Take the base of your brioche bun and add a squeeze of burger sauce, followed by your patty, then a generous handful of cabbage mix. Pop your brioche bun on top and enjoy!

name: Gochujang Beans on Toast
description: What's better than beans on toast? Gochujang beans on toast, that's what.
instructions: Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.

Heat a medium pot with a drizzle of olive oil and add the onions with a pinch of salt. Cook over a medium heat for 3-4 mins, then add the garlic and ginger. Stir and cook for another 2 mins before adding the chopped tomatoes, drained beans, soy sauce, gochujang, sugar and paprika.
Simmer over a low heat for about 10 mins until slightly thickened. Taste and adjust seasonings, adding plenty of black pepper, more soy sauce or gochujang, if you like.
Meanwhile, toast the bread and thinly slice the spring onion.

To serve, spoon the beans over the toast, add a spoon of yoghurt, top with the spring onion, sesame seeds and coriander. Finish with a good squeeze of lime and a final drizzle of sesame oil, if using.
The beans keep well in the fridge for up to three days.

name: Gochujang Bolognese & Rice
description: A spicy, punchy twist on your classic Bolognese ragù leftovers. Stir through gochujang, pile over rice and finish with sesame and spring onions. Quick, fiery, delicious.
instructions: Make the Bolognese Ragú.
Thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens.
Add a drizzle of olive oil to a saucepan set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the gochujang and the spring onion whites. Cook for 3-4 mins until the paste darkens and the onions soften.
Stir through the Bolognese ragù with a splash of water if it’s looking thick. Let it bubble away until piping hot. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Reheat the rice and divide between bowls. Spoon over the Gochujang Bolognese, then finish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and the spring onion greens.

name: Gochujang Cauliflower Hummus Bowl
description: This is a hummus bowl like no other, with punchy, sticky, spicy cauliflower florets, a zingy kimchi slaw and a creamy sesame butter bean hummus to bring it all together. It’s a delicious combination of flavours and textures.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
First, make the batter by mixing together all of the ingredients in a large bowl. It should be the consistency of a thick pancake batter. Add a little more milk if needed.
Cut the cauliflower into medium sized florets. Add them to the batter and toss to cover well. Lat out the florets onto a lined baking sheet and spray with an oil spray if you like. Roast for 20 mins.
While they are roasting, make the gochujang sauce by mixing together all of the sauce ingredients.

After the 20 mins are up, remove the florets from the oven and dip each one into the gochujang sauce to cover well. Use a fork as they will be hot. Place them back onto the baking sheet and cook for another 10 mins.
(Air Fryer option: Air fry for 10 mins, turning halfway. Cover with the gochujang sauce and cook for another 6 mins, shaking halfway.)
To make the slaw, finely slice the cabbage and mix with the kimchi and a squeeze of lime.
To make the butter bean hummus, drain the beans and keep half of the liquid. Add all of the ingredients to a blender with the reserved butterbean liquid and blend until smooth. Season to taste.
To serve, spoon the hummus into shallow bowls and top with the slaw and cauliflower. Finish with a drizzle of tahini, a squeeze of lime and finely sliced spring onion.

name: Gochujang Crispy Kale Crisps
description: Crispy, spicy and delicious — these kale crisps make the perfect snack. They're also great for sprinkling over rice or stir fries for some added crunch.
instructions: Wash and dry the kale well.
Remove the tough stems from the kale and place in a large bowl. The weight of the kale in the ingredients list is after removing the stems.
Whisk together the gochujang and olive oil in a small bowl.
Pour the gochujang and olive oil mixture over the kale and massage with your fingers so that each leaf is covered and marinated. Sprinkle over the sesame seeds, if using.
Air fry at 150ºC for 5 mins, tossing once or twice. Or bake in the oven in a single layer, at 150ºC for 20-25 mins, tossing once or twice until perfectly crispy.
Enjoy immediately, on their own or sprinkled over rice or a stir fry. Store for up to 3 days in a sealed container at room temperature.

name: Gochujang Fish Curry
description: Gochujang adds a lovely bit of heat to this curry. The whole dish can be on the table in under 30 minutes.
instructions: Peel and finely dice the onion. Peel and mince the garlic and ginger. Finely slice the spring onions.

Place a frying pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4-5 mins until softened and golden, 4-5 mins. Add the anchovies and cook for 1-2 mins until they melt and break up. Stir through the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.

Add the gochujang and curry powder and cook until the mixture starts to caramelise and goes a darker red colour. Stir through the water, then add the fish fillets. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 5-7 mins until the fish is cooked through. The thicker your fillet, the longer it will take. The fish is cooked when it flakes easily and is opaque throughout.
Finish with a sprinkling of spring onion and serve over rice with a wedge of lime.

name: Gochujang Linguine
description: A recipe inspired by the flavours of our Sausage Gochujang Rigatoni dish, but made in just fifteen minutes. Iconic.
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and add the pasta. Once it’s al dente, drain and reserve the starchy water.
Meanwhile, mince the shallot and garlic, then roughly chop the coriander.

Tip the butter into a frying pan and, once it starts to melt, add the shallot and garlic. Fry over a low-medium heat for 2 mins, then add the gochujang and cream. Grate in three-quarters of the parmesan, the juice of the lime, the honey and three-quarters of the coriander.

Add the cooked pasta to the sauce along with a small ladle of starchy pasta water and keep mixing until it’s super glossy (if you feel that the pasta needs a bit more water, add another small ladleful).

Add a glug of olive oil to a separate frying pan set over a medium heat. Tip in the breadcrumbs and cook until lightly golden, then add the leftover coriander and grate in the remaining Parmesan (this topping is optional, but highly recommended!).
Plate up your linguine with the breadcrumb mix on top and a few good cracks of black pepper. Enjoy!

name: Gochujang Marinated Eggs
description: Rich, spicy, and sweet with a gochujang kick. These deep-red beauties are unreal over rice with a load of fresh spring onions.
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Gently lower in the eggs and boil for 6 mins. Transfer into iced water to cool fully, then peel.
Meanwhile, grate the ginger and add to a bowl with the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, gochugaru (or chilli flakes if you can't find it) and water. Mix well until smooth.
Pop the peeled eggs into a clean jar or container and pour over the marinade. Make sure they’re fully covered, top up with extra water if needed.

Chill for at least 4 hrs, ideally overnight, to let the spice do its thing. 
These eggs will last for up to 4 days in the fridge, the flavour gets stronger each day.
Serve however you like, halving them over hot rice, scattering with chopped spring onions and a drizzle of extra marinade works a treat.

name: Gochujang Salmon Traybake
description: Flaky salmon glazed in spicy-sweet gochujang, roasted with tender cabbage, peppers and spring onions. Big flavour, minimal effort.
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C fan.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce and hot honey together in a small bowl. Set aside.
Cut the cabbage into 2-3cm wedges, keeping the core intact so the leaves stay together. Trim the spring onions but leave them whole.

Chuck the cabbage, spring onions and frozen peppers into a medium roasting tin. Brush generously with most of the gochujang glaze, saving a bit back for the salmon. Spritz everything with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 10 mins.
Carefully turn the veg, then nestle the salmon fillets into the tin. Brush them with the remaining glaze and return to the oven for 8-10 mins, or until the salmon is cooked through and flakes easily.
Serve up the roasted salmon and veg. Pick over the coriander, sprinkle with sesame seeds if you like, and serve with lime wedges on the side.

name: Gochujang Sausage & Pepper Gnocchi Traybake
description: Put your Sausage Gochujang Ragú batch to good use with this creamy gnocchi traybake. It's easy to whip up on a weeknight and completely faff free.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sausage Gochujang Ragú batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Slice the peppers into strips and the red onion into wedges.

Toss the gnocchi, peppers and onion with olive oil, salt and pepper on a large baking tray. Roast for 20 mins, giving it all a good toss halfway through until the gnocchi is golden and the veg is soft and charred in spots.
While that’s roasting, warm the Sausage Gochujang Ragù in a saucepan or microwave-safe bowl until piping hot. Add a splash of water if needed to loosen.
Mix the ragú through the gnocchi traybake, loosening with water, if needed. Serve the traybake drizzled with chilli oil and some single cream (if you like), then scatter with coriander.

name: Gochujang Tofu "Mince" Rice Bowl
description: Sweet, spicy, and full of flavour, this Korean-inspired tofu bowl is all about balance. Crispy tofu “mince,” sticky gochujang sauce, and fresh crunchy veg. It’s quick, satisfying, and packed with protein.
instructions: Pat the tofu dry, then crumble it into small mince-sized pieces with your hands.
Heat the sesame oil in a large non-stick pan over a medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 5–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and crispy at the edges.
Grate the garlic and ginger — no need to peel. Peel and cut the carrot into matchsticks, and slice the cucumber into thin matchsticks too. Finely slice the spring onions, pick the mint leaves.

In a small bowl, mix together the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, garlic, gochujang, ginger and water. Pour the sauce into the pan with the crispy tofu. Stir-fry for a couple of minutes until glossy and well-coated.
Heat the rice according to the packet instructions, then spoon it into your Tupperware containers. Top with the gochujang tofu “mince,” edamame, carrot, and cucumber.
Finish with spring onion, lime wedges, mint and sesame seeds, if using. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Gochujang Tofu "Mince" Rice Bowl
description: Sweet, spicy, and full of flavour, this Korean-inspired tofu bowl is all about balance. Crispy tofu “mince,” sticky gochujang sauce, and fresh crunchy veg. It’s quick, satisfying, and packed with protein.
instructions: Pat the tofu dry, then crumble it into small mince-sized pieces with your hands.
Heat the sesame oil in a large non-stick pan over a medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 5–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and crispy at the edges.
Grate the garlic and ginger — no need to peel. Peel and cut the carrot into matchsticks, and slice the cucumber into thin matchsticks too. Finely slice the spring onions, pick the mint leaves.

In a small bowl, mix together the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, garlic, gochujang, ginger and water. Pour the sauce into the pan with the crispy tofu. Stir-fry for a couple of minutes until glossy and well-coated.
Heat the rice according to the packet instructions, then spoon it into a bowl. Top with the gochujang tofu “mince,” edamame, carrot, and cucumber.
Finish with spring onion, lime wedges, mint and sesame seeds, if using.

name: Gochujang Tofu Rice Bowl
description: Crispy tofu coated in a sweet and spicy sauce, served with quick-pickled veg and sticky rice, an epic recipe that's perfect for meal prepping.
instructions: Mince your garlic and slice your spring onion. Set aside in separate bowls.

Peel your carrot and slice it into long strips. Halve your cucumber, remove the seeds, and then slice it into long strips like the carrot. Cut the tops off your radishes and thinly slice them. Place your prepped veg in a glass jar or deep bowl.
Get a pot on medium heat and add your sugar, water and apple cider vinegar. Bring to a simmer then take it off the heat. Leave to cool then pour over your veg.
Now, cook your sushi rice according to package instructions.
Cut your tofu into small pieces and pat dry with a paper towel, this will absorb the water from the tofu.
Place your tofu with the cornflour and garlic powder in a plastic bag or sealed container and give it a good shake.
Get a wide, flat pan on medium heat, pour in a good glug of oil – enough so that it sits around 1½ cm high.

When your oil is ready, give your tofu a shake to get rid of excess cornflour before popping it into your pan and frying until crispy. Place the fried tofu cubes on a paper towel-lined plate or sieve.

Meanwhile, combine your gochujang, soy sauce, ketchup, maple syrup, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil, and water with your minced garlic in a small bowl. Pour this mix into a pan and bring to a simmer. Take it off the heat and add your fried tofu, giving it a good toss.
Serve your tofu with steamed rice, pickled veg and garnish with spring onions and toasted sesame seeds.

name: Gochujang Tomato & Aubergine Hummus Bowl
description: Sweet, spicy smoky chickpea and aubergine stew made with our Gochujang Tomato & Sweet Onion Sauce piled on top of creamy hummus. Scoop it all up with golden toast – proper satisfying stuff.
category: Gochujang Tomato & Sweet Onion Sauce Recipes
keywords: Gochujang Tomato & Aubergine Hummus Bowl recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the Gochujang Tomato & Sweet Onion Sauce.
Heat the oven to 220°C fan.

Trim the aubergines and chop into 2cm chunks. Tip onto a baking tray lined with baking paper, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt. Slide into the oven and roast for 20–25 mins, until soft and golden.

Meanwhile, add the chickpeas and Gochujang Tomato & Sweet Onion Sauce to a saucepan. Pick the coriander leaves and set aside. Finely slice the corinader stems, then stir them through the chickpeas. Trim and finely slice the spring onion. Toast the sourdough.
Once the aubergines are cooked, tip them into the saucepan with the chickpeas. Set over a medium heat and stir until piping hot.

Spoon the hummus into shallow bowls and spread it out to make a base. Top with the stew, then scatter over the spring onion, coriander leaves and sesame seeds. Serve with the toast on the side and get stuck in.

name: Gochujang Tomato & Sweet Onion Sauce
description: A rich, sweet-spicy sauce that brings serious depth to stews, traybakes and bowls. Better than anything from a jar and dead easy to make.
keywords: Gochujang Tomato & Sweet Onion Sauce recipe
instructions: Peel and quarter the onion. Finely grate the garlic.
Set a medium saucepan over a medium heat and add the butter. Once melted, stir in the gochujang and garlic. Cook for 2–3 mins until it darkens and smells fragrant.

Stir in the chopped tomatoes and onion. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Pop a lid on and simmer for 20–30 mins until the onion has softened. Then, take the lid off and simmer for another 5–10 mins until the sauce has thickened to your liking. Season well with salt and black pepper.

Pour the sauce into a clean, heatproof jar and seal tightly. Let it cool fully before storing.
If the jar is sealed, store at room temperature for up to 1 month. If unsealed, store in the fridge and use within 2 weeks.

name: Gochujang Tuna & Sweetcorn Air Fryer Jacket Potato Recipe
description: Elevate your air fryer jacket potato with a bold and flavourful twist by adding a Gochujang Tuna & Sweetcorn filling. This recipe combines the ease of air frying with the spicy-sweet depth of Gochujang to create a satisfying meal that’s both quick and delicious. The crispy skin of the baked potato, achieved through the air fryer, contrasts beautifully with the creamy, spicy tuna mixture, making it a unique take on the classic jacket potato. Perfect for a hearty lunch or dinner, this dish is as versatile as it is tasty. Whether you're using a white potato or sweet potatoes, the air fryer ensures they come out perfectly every time. Garnish with spring onions or a sprinkle of cabbage for added crunch and freshness. This air fryer jacket potato recipe is sure to impress with its combination of textures and flavours, turning a simple potato into a gourmet experience.
keywords: Gochujang Tuna & Sweetcorn Air Fryer Jacket Potato Recipe
Gochujang Tuna & Sweetcorn Air Fryer Jacket Potato Recipe
instructions: Prick the potatoes all over with a fork, then drizzle with 2 tsp oil and season with salt and pepper. Transfer to the basket of the air fryer and set the temperature to 200°C. Set the timer for 45 mins and cook until the skin is crisp, but a sharp knife slides into the middle easily.
Meanwhile, very thinly slice the spring onions and scrape three-quarters into a bowl. Roughly chop three-quarters of the coriander and scrape that into the bowl, too.

Drain the cans of tuna and sweetcorn and add to the bowl with the spring onions and coriander, then spoon in the mayo, gochujang and rice vinegar. Season with a little salt and pepper and gently fold together. Taste and adjust the seasoning, adding more gochujang if you want it spicier.

Put the jacket potatoes onto a plate and cut down the middle, gently pressing the sides to open it up. Season the inside with salt and pepper, then divide the tuna and sweetcorn mix over the potatoes.
Sprinkle over the reserved spring onions and coriander leaves and the sesame seeds. Serve with kimchi on the side.

name: Golden Aubergine Curry & Rice
description: This is a lovely brothy rice dish which makes an ideal midweek dinner.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Trim and chop the aubergine into 2cm chunks. Transfer to a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, toss and bake until softened and golden, 20-25 mins.
Peel and finely grate the ginger and garlic in a small bowl and stir the yellow curry paste through.

Meanwhile, add a drizzle of olive oil into a saucepan over medium heat. Once hot, fry the curry paste until fragrant, then pour in the vinegar and cook, stirring consistently, until evaporated. Pour the stock and water then let it come to the boil, reduce the heat and gently simmer. Taste and season with miso if needed.
Share the cooked rice between bowls and ladle the broth in. Top with the aubergines and garnish with crispy shallots and drizzle over with chilli oil. Garnish with coriander.

name: Golden Chicken with Herb & Feta Fregola
description: Buttery, pounded chicken breast over garlicky yoghurt and a lemony fregola. A speedy midweek meal, that's also packed with protein.
instructions: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil and cook the fregola for 10 mins until al dente. Drain and leave to cool.

Finely chop the parsley and dill and set aside. Zest the lemon and set aside, then cut it in half and squeeze over the cooled fregola along with a drizzle of olive oil. Crumble in the feta, season with salt and pepper, and toss everything together. Set aside.
Grate the garlic into a small bowl. Stir through the yoghurt, lemon zest, a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Spoon onto serving plates.
Butterfly the chicken breasts and place them between two sheets of baking parchment. Bash with a rolling pin until about 1cm thick. Dust both sides with the flour and season well.
Heat a splash of olive oil and the butter in a large frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 3–4 mins on each side until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan.
In the same pan, add the capers to the buttery juices with another squeeze of lemon juice. Let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Spoon the herby fregola over the yoghurt, top with the chicken breast and drizzle over any buttery pan juices to finish.

name: Golden Garlic Soup
description: This soup is a rich, golden hug for your soul, with a sunshine-y garlicky broth and plump little pearls of giant couscous. Perfect for when you need a bit of warmth in your life.
instructions: Start by finely chopping the onion and finely slicing the garlic. Melt the butter in a large saucepan set over a medium heat with a glug of olive oil. Add the onion and a pinch of salt and gently sauté for around 10 mins until softened – we don’t want it to burn or catch so keep your eye on it. Add the garlic and cook for another 5 mins. Season with black pepper.

Drain and rinse the chickpeas and add to the pan along with the giant couscous, stock and bay leaf. Grate in the turmeric. Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture simmer for 20-25 mins until the couscous is tender. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Remove the bay leaf.
Meanwhile, pick the dill fronds and parsley leaves.
Serve the soup up in bowls topped with the fresh herbs and a crack of black pepper.

name: Golden Garlicky Mushrooms & Whipped Tahini Bowl
description: Herby roasted mushrooms and lemony tahini are a match made in heaven. We’ve served them with freekeh to make a healthy, comforting and satisfying bowl.
keywords: Golden Garlicky Mushrooms & Whipped Tahini Bowl
Golden Garlicky Mushrooms & Whipped Tahini Bowl recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C fan.

Tear or slice the mushrooms into 1cm chunks then pop them on a baking tray. Finely grate the garlic over the mushrooms. Strip the rosemary needles off, discarding the stalks, and add them to the mushrooms. Drizzle with some olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss together. Roast for 25-30 mins until golden.

Meanwhile, add the water to a small saucepan and bring it to a boil over a high heat. Tip the freekeh in with a pinch of salt then stir and place a lid on. Turn the heat down to low-medium and simmer for 15-20 mins, until the freekeh has fully cooked and absorbed the water.
Pick the parsley and coriander leaves, and finely slice the stems.

For the whipped tahini, add the tahini, lemon juice, ice cubes, peeled garlic and ground cinnamon into a high power blender and blend until the tahini is fluffy and pale in colour. Season with salt and sugar, to taste.

Before serving, stir the herbs and stems through the roasted mushrooms. Spoon the whipped tahini onto the bottom of a plate or bowl then top with the freekeh and mushrooms. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Golden Halloumi With Grilled Chicory & Seedy Brown Rice
description: Golden halloumi served on a bed of spiced, herby, nutty rice. Grilled chicory, which when raw tends to have a bitterness, but cooked, it gets mellowed out.
keywords: Golden Halloumi With Grilled Chicory & Seedy Brown Rice
instructions: Finely grate the garlic clove into a mixing bowl, add the juice of one of the lemons and set aside. Cut the blocks of halloumi into 6 slices.

Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Tip the cumin seeds and coriander seeds into a dry pan. Place over a medium-high heat and toast until the seeds are fragrant, 1-2 mins. Then, tip into a pestle and mortar and roughly crush, add to the lemon mixture.
Add the seeds to the dry pan and toast until popping, 2-3 mins, then tip onto a plate and set aside.
Halve the chicory lengthways and drizzle with 1 tbsp of olive oil, season with salt and pepper and slide under the grill. Grill until tender and starting to lightly char, 5-6 mins.
Re-use the frying pan, and place it on medium heat with 2 tbsp of olive oil. Once hot, add the halloumi and cook on both sides until golden, 3-5 mins.

Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the package instructions, then tip it into the mixing bowl with the lemon and garlic. Add 2 tbsp of olive oil and the toasted seeds. Finely chop most of the herbs and add. Season well and toss.
Pile the rice into bowls, top with the chicory and halloumi. Top with the remaining herb leaves. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve on the side.

name: Golden Herby Broth with Eggs & Rice
description: A quick comforting brothy rice bowl with jammy eggs and loads of fresh herbs. We’ve added kefir for extra tang and creaminess, and to be good to your gut.
keywords: Smoky Spicy Broth with Mushrooms & Rice
instructions: Fill a saucepan full of water and place over a high heat. Once boiling, turn the heat down to medium, gently drop the eggs in and simmer for 7 mins. Transfer to an ice bath to cool down. Rinse out the pan.
Meanwhile, finely mince the coriander, parsley and dill (stalks and all) and thinly slice the garlic.

Place the rinsed pan onto medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the turmeric, garlic, fresh chopped herbs, dried mint and ¾ of the crispy onions. Cook, stirring, until the herbs have softened. Pour in the vegetable stock and let it heat up.
In the meantime, reheat the cooked rice and lentils then stir together.
Before serving, bring the broth off the heat and leave to slightly cool for a minute. Stir the kefir through the broth then taste and season with salt and pepper.
Share the rice and lentils between bowls and ladle the broth over. Top each with 3 jammy egg halves and the remaining crispy onions.

name: Golden Herby Chickpea Stew with Crispy Shallots
description: An easier spin on the classic Persian Ash Reshteh, this herby chickpea stew is warm, tangy and topped with the crispiest golden shallots.
keywords: Golden Herby Chickpea Stew with Crispy Shallots recipe
Golden Herby Chickpea Stew with Crispy Shallots
instructions: Drain and rinse the lentils. Finely slice two of the shallots. Mince the garlic.
Remove the woody ends from the herbs, then finely chop. Wash the spinach and roughly chop it.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large lidded saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the sliced shallots with a big pinch of salt and cook gently for 15 mins until soft and golden. Add the garlic and cook for another minute, then stir through the ground turmeric.
Add the chopped herbs and spinach to the pan, followed by the stock or water, lentils, chickpeas and cannellini beans (with their liquid). Bring everything to a gentle simmer and cook for 20 mins.

Meanwhile, finely slice the remaining two shallots. Add the a generous lug of olive oil to a small saucepan over a low-medium heat. Add the shallots and slowly bring up the heat. Cook gently for 15 mins until deeply golden. Transfer the crispy shallots to a plate lined with kitchen paper and remove the pan from the heat.
After a couple of minutes, stir the dried mint into the warm oil and set aside. Once completely cool, mix the crispy shallots back into the minty oil.
Stir in the lemon juice and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon the chickpeas into bowls, top with a swirl of soured cream and finish with the crispy shallots and mint oil.

name: Golden Pepper Linguine
description: A really vibrant, saucy pasta dish that uses the underrated yellow pepper as its base. Inspired by a dish one of our developers ate at Forza Win.
instructions: Finely slice the garlic and the peppers.

Finely slice the peppers and add to a baking tray, drizzle with oil and season with salt. Put in an oven at 200°C for 40 mins, mixing halfway. Once soft, add to a blender. Heat oil in a pan over a medium heat and fry the garlic for 3 mins, until golden, then add to the peppers – blitz until you have a smooth paste. Taste and season with salt and pepper, then transfer back into the garlic pan.
Grate the Parmesan and get the pasta to boil, before draining. Save the pasta water!
Tip the cooked pasta into the sauce pan directly, along with the Parmesan, chilli flakes, sherry vinegar and a big slosh of cooking water. Plate up and top with some more chilli flakes and Parmesan.

name: Golden Soy & Sesame Fried Rice
description: Eggy rice topped with freshly chopped spring onions and a handful of sesame seeds. It's an absolute belter.
instructions: Beat half of the eggs together in a bowl and set aside.
Heat up a non-stick frying pan with a tbsp sesame oil and add your diced onion. Sauté on a medium heat.
Add the peas and sauté for a couple of minutes with the onions.
After a couple of minutes move these ingredients to the side of the wok.
Add the whisked eggs gradually to the empty side of the wok, giving your eggs room to cook.
Stir in the Tilda Pure Basmati Rice, allowing each grain to be evenly covered with egg mixture. Add soy sauce, salt and pepper and mix well.

Take off the heat and serve the fried rice into four bowls. Separate your remaining egg yolks and place on top of each portion of rice. Garnish the bowl with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

name: Grandma Pie
description: This sheet-pan pizza is a New York classic. It’s crispy, saucy and garlicky. It might just be your new favourite pie.
instructions: Start by making the dough. Add the water to a large bowl. Tip in the yeast and flour and bring together with your hands until there are no dry lumps of flour left in the bowl. Don’t worry about kneading too much here, just make sure you’ve got all the flour hydrated.

Cover the bowl with cling film, or pop inside something airtight and leave for 1 hour. Tip the olive oil and salt over your dough and use your hands to squash into the dough. Keep mixing until the dough has come together.

Turn the dough out onto a clean surface and give it a brief knead – it will be sticky but don’t worry. Use a bench scraper to scoop the dough back up and into a clean bowl. Let it hang out for half an hour then give it a fold. Dunk your hands into cold water, grab the top of the dough and lift it up and over the main body of the dough. Turn the dough 90° and repeat the fold again. Complete four folds (this is one turn). Leave the dough for another half an hour and fold again.

Let it rest once more, then fold again and lob the whole lot into the fridge overnight for a long, slow prove. You can let the dough hang out at room temp, and it will be ready to shape and bake in roughly 2-3 hours. When it’s ready to bake, heat the oven to 220°C.

Line a roughly 20x35cm baking tray with parchment and a glug of olive oil. Pour the dough into the lined tray and carefully encourage it into the corners to fill the tray. Knock out most of the air. Slide into the oven for 10 mins to par-bake.

Tip the plum tomatoes into a bowl and use your hands to squish them through their juices. Finely grate the garlic cloves into the bowl and add a glug of olive oil and a healthy pinch of salt. Mix together.

Cut the mozzarella into slices and lay the cheese out over the parbaked base, then spoon the sauce evenly over top. Finish with grated Parmesan and then slide back into the oven. Lower to 200°C and bake for 30-35 mins.
Finish the pizza with the fresh basil leaves and some extra grated Parmesan. Cut into slices with scissors and serve.

name: Grapefruit Rice Noodle Salad
description: The best grapefruit noodle salad ever. This a simple no-cook salad that's perfect for a hot summery day.
instructions: Start by making your dressing, finely slice the chilli and the white part of lemongrass, removing the tough outer layer.

Add both to a small bowl with the juice of the limes, fish sauce, sugar and 2 tbsp water. Give it a good mix and taste for seasoning. Using a small knife, remove the skin and pith of the grapefruit, then segment into pieces.

Finely slice the cucumber and spring onions on a diagonal. Pick the mint leaves and Thai basil. Boil the kettle and soak the noodles for 3 mins, then drain and rinse in cold water. Once fully drained, add to a large bowl with the grapefruit, cucumber, spring onions, lemongrass and herbs. Pour over the dressing and set aside. Roughly chop the cashews.
Serve up topped with the crispy onions and cashews.

name: Gravy Mayo With Mashed Potato Croquettes
description: Yes — we really have combined two of our favourite things: mayo and gravy, and served it up with a gorgeous selection of crispy mashed potato croquettes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180ºC. Roughly chop the carrots, celery and onions and scatter into a roasting tin. Top with the chicken wings and thyme stems. Season well with salt and pepper and slide into the oven for an hour, until deeply golden.

In the meantime, peel the potatoes for your croquettes. Cut into quarters and add to a large pan. Add a tbsp of salt and cover with cold water. Bring to boil then cook for around 20 mins, until totally soft. Drain and allow to steam dry for 5–10 mins, then mash or put through a ricer, cover, and chill in the fridge until cold.

Remove the tray from the oven and toss in the flour, stir to coat, adding a splash of water to help scrape up any flavour from the bottom of the roasting tin — it should look like the wings and veg are coated in a sandy paste. Tip into a large saucepan and cover with water. Bring to the boil, then turn to a simmer and cook for 20–30 mins, then tip through a sieve into a large shallow frying pan. Place over a high heat, add the Marmite, and cook for 20 mins further, until really thick. tip into a bowl and set aside to cool.

Remove the potatoes from the fridge, add 1 egg and season well with lots of salt and pepper. Crack the remaining eggs into a shallow bowl and whisk together. Tip the flour into another bowl and the breadcrumbs into a final bowl. Working with one at a time, shape a tbsp of the mashed potato into an oval shape, then repeat with the rest of the potato mix. Drop each oval into the flour bowl, then the egg bowl and finally into the breadcrumb bowl, then line out onto a baking tray.
Tip the oil into a large deep saucepan, use enough oil to come around half way up the side of the pan. Place over a high heat and heat the oil until it reaches 180ºC.

Whilst the oil heats, make the mayo. Add the egg yolk to the bowl and whisk in the dijon mustard along with a small squeeze of the lemon half. Add a tiny splash of oil and whisk well. Slowly add the oil, a tiny splash at a time, whisking vigorously with each addition, until it starts to thicken and emulsify. Keep adding the oil, you can add a little more liberally once it’s emulsified, until you have a thick mayonnaise. Add 2–3 tbsp of the thick gravy and whisk well. Taste and season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.

Line a baking tray with kitchen paper. Once the oil is heated, add the croquettes, 3–4 at a time, and fry until golden and crisp. Remove from the oil with a slotted spoon and set aside on the lined tray. Season with a pinch of salt. Repeat with the rest of the croquettes.
Serve the crispy croquettes with the gravy mayo, topped with a big crack of black pepper.

name: Greek Baked Beans
description: These Greek-inspired beans are stunning. Fat butter beans gently simmered with veg and herbs make a lovely meal. A beautiful dish, rain or shine.
instructions: Heat your oven to 160°C.
Peel and finely dice your onion, carrot and celery. Roughly chop your tomatoes.
Heat a large ovenproof dish over a medium heat with a glug of olive oil. Add your onion, celery and carrot and cook for 10 mins until softened.
Add your dried oregano and tomato purée to the pan and cook for 2 mins. Add your chopped tomatoes and simmer for 5 mins until just starting to break down.
Drain your butter bean tins. Pour the beans into the pan along with your vegetable stock, bay leaf and cinnamon stick. Season with a little salt, then bring to a simmer.
Pop the lid on your dish and bake for 30 mins.
Remove the lid from the dish and give the mixture a stir. Pop it back in the oven without it’s lid on for 15 mins more.
Finely chop most of your mint, setting aside a few small leaves to garnish.
Remove your beans from the oven and season to taste. Add the chopped mint and stir to combine. Sprinkle with your remaining mint leaves and a little olive oil, then serve.

name: Greek Dense Bean Salad
description: Greek salad, but bulkier. This herby twist on Greek salad has all the best bits - feta, olives and ripe tomatoes and of course...beans!
instructions: Drain and rinse the kidney beans, chickpeas and butter beans. Dice the tomatoes into irregular chunks. Slice the cucumber in half lengthways, scoop out the seeds and chop. Remove the seeds from the pepper and chop into bite-sized chunks. Peel and finely slice the shallot. Pit the olives, if needed.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar and dried oregano. Add the sliced shallot and let it sit for a few minutes.

Tip in the chopped pepper, tomato, cucumber, beans and olives. Dice the feta and chuck it on top. Season with salt and pepper, then give everything a good mix before serving.
If making ahead, box up and chill until needed. The salad will last for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Greek Gnocchi Traybake
description: All the flavours of Greek salad in a warm comforting meal. This one is really low lift and the oven does most of the work. Make a big batch and reheat any leftovers in the microwave. Too easy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Zest the lemon, juice ½ the lemon and grate the garlic into a bowl. Add the olive oil, dried oregano, harissa and a pinch of salt and pepper. Whisk together to combine.

Halve the cherry tomatoes and dice the aubergine into 2cm pieces. Add the veggies to a baking tray then drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Mix together to coat then slide into the oven to roast for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion and add to a bowl along with the remaining lemon juice. Season with salt then set aside to lightly pickle.

Drain and rinse the lentils. Add the lentils, gnocchi and olives to the pan with the par-roasted veggies then pour over the prepared harissa dressing. Give everything a good mix then return to the oven for another 10 mins. Crumble over the feta then return to the oven for a final 5 mins until the feta is softened and slightly charred.
Divide between bowls then top with the fresh herbs, pickled onions and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Greek Halloumi & Lentil Bowl
description: Crispy air-fried halloumi, lemony herby lentils, and a creamy cottage cheese dressing. An easy meal prep lunch.
instructions: Cut the courgette into chunks. Chop the mint, setting aside a few leaves to garnish later. Cut the halloumi into 2cm chunks.

Chuck the courgette into the drawer of an air fryer. Spritz with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, then cook at 200°C for 15 mins. Toss in the cherry tomatoes, dried oregano and halloumi for the final 6 mins.
Peel the garlic. Zest the lemon, then juice it.

Blitz the garlic, cottage cheese, dijon mustard, tahini, lemon zest and juice in a blender with enough water to make a drizzling consistency (start with a tablespoon). Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Drain the lentils and chickpeas and tip them into a large bowl. Toss with the chopped mint and half the dressing.

Spoon the salad into Tupperware containers, top with the roasted halloumi and tomatoes, drizzle with the remaining dressing and garnish with the reserved mint leaves. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Greek Halloumi & Lentil Bowl
description: Crispy air-fried halloumi, lemony herby lentils, and a creamy cottage cheese dressing. A winning high fibre lunch or dinner.
instructions: Cut the courgette into chunks. Chop the mint, setting aside a few leaves to garnish later. Cut the halloumi into 2cm chunks.

Chuck the courgette into the drawer of an air fryer. Spritz with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, then cook at 200°C for 15 mins. Toss in the cherry tomatoes, dried oregano and halloumi for the final 6 mins.
Peel the garlic. Zest the lemon, then juice it.

Blitz the garlic, tahini, cottage cheese, Dijon mustard, lemon zest and juice in a blender with enough water to make a drizzling consistency (start with a tablespoon). Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Drain the lentils and chickpeas and tip them into a large bowl. Toss with the chopped mint and half the dressing.
Spoon the salad onto plates, top with the roasted halloumi and tomatoes, drizzle with the remaining dressing and garnish with the reserved mint leaves.

name: Greek Halloumi & Veg Traybake
description: A veg-packed mediterranean traybake, with golden roasted halloumi and chickpeas. This is the kind of dish you can pop in the oven and leave to do it's thing. We served it warm pittas and a dollop of tzatziki. Proper satisfying.
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C fan. Tip the frozen vegetables into a large roasting tray. Drain and stir through the chickpeas.
Slice the halloumi into 1cm thick then lay on top of the veg.  Season the whole thing with salt and black pepper, then drizzle with the olive oil.
Return the tray to the oven and bake for 25 mins until the halloumi is golden and the veg is cooked through.
Pick the dill. Finely zest over the lemon and cut the lemon into wedges to serve.
Warm the pittas, then stuff them with a spoonful of tzatziki, a generous helping of the roasted veggie mix and a squeeze of lemon juice.

name: Greek Lemony Chicken & Brothy Rice
description: Avgolemono is basically a method for thickening broth with eggs and lemon. It makes this soupy rice dish silky smooth and incredibly comforting. Simple Greek food at its best, made in one pot.
keywords: Greek Lemony Chicken & Brothy Rice recipe
instructions: Peel the onion and cut into quarters. Peel the zest of one of the lemons. Add both to a large saucepan with the water, chicken thighs and bay leaves. Season generously with salt and bring to a light simmer over a medium-low heat. Cook for 35 mins, until the chicken is cooked through.

Transfer the chicken to a board. Fish out the onion, lemon zest and bay leaves with a slotted spoon and discard. Reserve 300ml of the broth in a heatproof jug. Once the chicken is cool enough to handle, pull the meat off the bone and shred using two forks. You can finely chop the skin and add it back in, or discard it.
Set the pan of broth back over a medium-low heat and add the rice. Cook for 12-15 mins until almost fully cooked, then stir the shredded chicken back in.

Crack the eggs into a large bowl and whisk well. Squeeze in the juice of one of the lemons and whisk again. If the reserved broth has cooled, reheat it in the microwave or a small saucepan. Slowly pour it into the eggs in a thin, steady stream, whisking continuously as you go, this gently raises the temperature of the eggs without scrambling them.

Turn the heat under the pan down to its lowest setting. You want it steaming, not simmering. Pour in the egg mixture and stir constantly for 3-4 mins, until the soup has thickened and turned silky. Don't let it boil or the eggs will split. Taste and season generously with salt and black pepper.
Ladle into bowls and finish with a generous scatter of fresh mint leaves and a crack of black pepper. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Greek Pasta Salad
description: Rifling with orzo, feta, and briny olives, this Greek pasta salad is a dream summer dinner. Get this on the table to instantly transport yourself to the Mediterranean. It's also perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Thinly slice the red onion. Place in a bowl and cover with the red wine vinegar. Add a pinch of salt, mix well, and leave to pickle whilst you prepare the rest, stirring occasionally.

Whilst the onions are pickling, bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the orzo according to the package instructions until al dente, then drain and rinse with cold water to cool it down quickly.
Halve or quarter the cherry tomatoes, depending on their size. Dice the cucumber. Halve the kalamata olives, removing the pips if they have them.
Make the dressing, Whisk the olive oil, juice of the lemon, and honey together. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

In a large bowl, combine the cooked orzo, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, kalamata olives, and mint leaves. Add the pickled red onions (drained) and crumble the feta cheese over the top. Sprinkle chilli flakes and dried oregano over the salad.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss everything together until well combined. Spoon the salad into bowls and serve.
Optional: If batch cooking for the week, transfer the salad to containers and store in the fridge until ready to serve.

name: Greek Salad Halloumi Sandwich
description: A big, fat halloumi sandwich recipe stuffed with all the good bits of a Greek salad.
instructions: Thinly slice the red onion and transfer to a bowl. Cover with the red wine vinegar and set aside to pickle.
Zest the lemon into a bowl, squeeze in the juice and add the mayo. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Set three shallow bowls out in a row. Tip the flour into one, beat the egg into another and tip the breadcrumbs, oregano and lots of black pepper into the last bowl. Slice the halloumi into thin slices.
Coat the halloumi slices first in the flour, then egg and, finally, the breadcrumbs. Set aside.
Slice the cucumber and tomatoes. Slice the ciabatta in half and toast in a toaster or a frying pan.

Tip enough vegetable oil into a frying pan to come 1-2cm up the side. Place over a medium-high heat and warm the oil until a breadcrumb sizzles when you drop it in. Fry the halloumi for 2 mins each side, until golden and crispy.

Spread the lemon mayo over the base slice of focaccia, then spread the olive tapenade over the other slice. Top with the sliced tomatoes, pop the halloumi on top, then add the cucumber and pickled red onion. Finish with the mint leaves, add a drizzle of olive oil and some salt and pepper, then pop the lid on and tuck in.

name: Greek Stuffed Peppers
description: Gorgeous charred pepper stuffed with courgettes and potatoes. This gemista recipe is so, so, so good.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic (use a small food processor for this, if you like), then transfer to a bowl. Grate the courgette and add to the onion and garlic with plenty of salt and pepper.
Sauté the courgette mixture with ½ of the tomato purée and a good drizzle of olive oil for 8-10 mins over a medium-high heat, until the garlic is fragrant and the courgette is starting to caramelise.

Add the rice to the pan and cook for 2-3 mins. This will help seal the rice so that it doesn’t go too mushy in the oven. Add the chopped tomatoes, water and ½ of the stock cubes, then simmer over a low-medium heat for 10 mins, stirring occasionally. Add the pine nuts and oregano, then tear in the mint, if using. Season well with salt and pepper and continue to simmer.
Slice the bottoms (keep them for later) off the tomatoes – not the stem side – and scoop out the insides with a small spoon. Chop the insides finely and add them to the simmering rice.
Slice the tops off of the peppers (keep them for later) and trim down the stems if they are very long. Remove the insides and discard. Peel and chop the potatoes into large wedges.
Add the potato, tomatoes and peppers to a small baking dish where they will fit together very snuggly. Packing them fairly tightly will stop them from collapsing and falling over in the oven.

Finely chop the parsley and stir it through the rice. Spoon the rice into the peppers and tomatoes, overfilling them so the rice almost spills out of the top if you have enough to do that. Pop the lids of all the veggies back on.

Add hot water to a small bowl with the remaining stock cube and remaining tomato purée, plus plenty of salt and pepper. Carefully pour this over the peppers, tomatoes and potatoes. Drizzle olive oil over the whole dish and then cover tightly with foil.

Cook in the oven for 1 hr, then remove the foil and cook for another 20 mins until the tops are nicely charred and the water has turned into a sauce. Let the dish cool for 10 mins before serving. This dish is even better the next day.

name: Greek Style Tomato & Feta Fritters
description: These tomato fritters (ντοματοκεφτέδες in Greek) with a little twist of added feta are a perfect summer sharing plate, served up with creamy tzatziki.
instructions: Halve the cucumber lengthwise and scrape out the seeds. Grate the cucumber straight into a sieve and mix with a large pinch of salt. Allow to drain while you make the fritters.

Finely chop the tomato, onion and herbs. Reserve half of the mint and add everything else to a large bowl along with the egg. Grate in the courgette and add 100g of flour, the feta and a large pinch of salt, mix well.

Depending on the moisture in the tomatoes you might need to add the remaining flour to ensure the mix binds together. The batter should be thick and paste-like, add more flour, if needed, to get it to the right consistency.
Heat ½ an inch of vegetable oil in a nonstick frying pan. When the oil is hot, add the mix in heaped tablespoons, keeping each heaped heap a couple of inches apart.
Fry for about 3 mins on each side until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper.
Squeeze as much remaining liquid as possible from the cucumber and then combine in a bowl with the yoghurt, juice of half a lemon, the remaining mint and a pinch of salt.
Grate in the garlic, mix well and spread over a small plate. Stack a few fritters next to the yoghurt and serve.

name: Greek Tomato Rice Traybake
description: This Greek-ish inspired baked rice can be turned it into three very different recipes so you don't get bored. It’s packed full of tomatoes, olives and peppers so you can get your veg count up, plus I’ve bulked it out with a few extra.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Finely dice the garlic and onion, then slice the peppers. Drain the olives and break in half, then quarter the tomatoes.

Set a frying pan over a medium heat, add a splash of olive oil then the onions, garlic, peppers and bay leaves - make sure to season generously with salt. Cook for 10 mins, then add the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins until darkened in colour.

Add the stock, rinsed rice, butter beans, olives, dried mint and dried oregano and tomatoes. Bring to the boil, season with salt and pepper, cover with a lid and pop in the oven for 25 mins. Remove the lid and pop back in the oven for 10 mins to crisp-up on top. Squeeze in the lemon juice and add more seasoning to taste. Finish with the fresh parsley roughly chopped. Eat immediately, or divide into Tupperware for eating throughout the week.

name: Greek(ish) Tomato Barley
description: A tomatoey pearl barley dish that’s not unlike a risotto then topped it with a fresh, lemony broccoli salad. It's packed full of nutrients to keep us healthy but it also kind of tastes like you could be sitting in the sun, eating at a taverna on the beach. Bliss.
instructions: Rinse the pearl barley. Finely slice the garlic. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a pan over a medium heat and fry the garlic for 2 mins. Add the tomato purée, fennel seeds and cinnamon and cook for 1 min. Add the canned tomatoes, barley and stock, season with salt and pepper, then simmer for 45 mins, stirring often to prevent it from sticking to the bottom.

Heat the grill and grill the broccoli for 8 mins, turning halfway. Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion and tip it into a bowl with the lemon juice. Tear the olives in half, chop the dill and add both to the bowl along with the broccoli. Give it a mix and season with salt and pepper.
Serve the tomatoey barley in bowls and top with the broccoli salad.

name: Greek-ish Roast Lamb Salad
description: Leftovers from you Garlicky Slow Roast Lamb with crisp romaine, juicy tomatoes, salty feta and olives, all topped with cool tzatziki and quick-pickled red onion.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Garlicky Slow Roast Lamb batch recipe.
Peel and finely slice the red onion and add to a small bowl with the juice of half the lemon and a pinch of salt. Massage gently with your hands and set aside to quick-pickle.
Slice the romaine and cut the tomatoes into wedges. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds with a teaspoon and discard, then cut into pieces. Pick the mint leaves.

At this point you can reheat your leftovers of the Garlicky Slow Roast Lamb batch in the microwave. Toss the lamb with the dried oregano.The lamb is also great at room temperature so perfect for a lunchbox.

Drizzle the romaine with the olive oil, squeeze over any remaining lemon juice and season with salt and pepper. Arrange the romaine, lamb, tomatoes, cucumber, olives and feta in bowls. Top with the tzatziki, mint leaves and pickled onion.

name: Greek-ish Stuffed Aubergines
description: Juicy aubergines packed with herby rice, crispy feta and bursting tomatoes, topped with a swirl of tahini yoghurt. Yes please.
instructions:
Heat the oven to 200°C. 
If you’re using raw rice instead of cooked or microwaveable pouches, get it on to cook now following pack instructions. Set aside once done.

Halve the aubergines lengthways and place cut-side up on a lined baking tray. Drizzle with 1 Tbsp of olive oil and roast for 25 mins until softened but still holding their shape. If using rice pouches, cook them now.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, garlic and peppers. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and peppers and cook for 10 mins until soft. Stir in the garlic and tomato purée and cook for 2 more mins.
Add the cooked rice to the pan along with the dried mint and oregano. Season well with salt and black pepper, then mix thoroughly. Remove from the heat.

Once the aubergines are cool enough to handle, use a spoon to scoop out the flesh, leaving the skins intact. Roughly chop the scooped-out flesh and stir it through the rice mixture. Spoon the rice back into the aubergine skins and crumble over the feta.
Return the stuffed aubergines to the oven for 10–15 mins until the feta is golden.

While they bake, heat a lug of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook until they start to blister and char. Gently smoosh them with the back of a spoon until just bursting, then season with salt and black pepper.
For the tahini yoghurt, mix the yoghurt, tahini and a good squeeze of lemon juice in a bowl. Add a splash of water to loosen if needed, then season to taste.
To serve, spread some tahini yoghurt on each plate. Top with the burst tomatoes and stuffed aubergines. Drizzle with more tahini and scatter over the fresh mint.

name: Greekish Lemon Chicken & Potato Traybake
description: Wanna feel like you've been handed down a traditional greek supper? This is it. Inspired by the flavours of Greece, with lemon, garlic and oregano doing the heavy lifting, this easy traybake is all about comfort and seriously packs a punch.
keywords: Greekish Lemon Chicken & Potato Traybake recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the potatoes and add to a large, shallow baking tray, then toss with a third of the olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Roast for 20 mins, until they begin to crisp up.
Meanwhile, pat the chicken skin dry and season with salt and black pepper. Cut one lemon into wedges, pick the oregano leaves and finely grate the garlic.
Once the potatoes have had their 20 mins, add the chicken and lemon wedges to the tray, drizzle the chicken with another third of the oil and roast for 20 mins.

Add the garlic and the juice of the remaining lemon to the chicken stock and mix, then pour into the tray around the chicken. Scatter over the oregano, move the oven rack up one level and roast for another 15 mins.
Toss the green beans in the remaining oil, then scatter them over the chicken, nestling them into the tray where you can, and roast for a final 5 mins.
Serve the chicken and potatoes topped with crumbled feta.

name: Green Bean & Broad Bean Caesar
description: A veg-forward caesar with crisp green beans and sweet broad beans - and of course jammy eggs - that all get tossed in a punchy anchovy dressing. Don't skip the crunchy garlic pangritata, it adds the perfect crouton bite.
keywords: Green Bean & Broad Bean Caesar recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Tear the sourdough into rough chunks, finely grate in the garlic and toss both with the olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking tray and bake for 8-10 mins, stirring once, until deeply golden and crisp, keep a close eye towards the end, as they catch quickly. Set aside.

Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil. Add the broad beans and cook for 1 min, then scoop out with a slotted spoon and run under cold water. If you have a few minutes to spare, slip off the outer grey skins to reveal the bright green beans inside, it's not at all necessary but they taste noticeably sweeter for it.

Lower the eggs into the same water and cook for 6½ mins, then lift out and run under cold water. Trim the green beans, add to the pan and cook for 3-4 mins until just tender with a little bite. Drain and run under cold water.

While everything cools, make the dressing. Finely chop the anchovies and parsley and finely grate the Parmesan. Mix together the mayonnaise, yoghurt, anchovy, parsley, most of the Parmesan and the juice of half the lemon. Loosen with a small splash of water until it coats the back of a spoon. Season with black pepper, it probably won't need salt given the anchovies and Parmesan.

Peel and halve the eggs. Toss the green beans, broad beans and pangritata with the dressing and arrange on plates. Nestle the egg halves in alongside, shave over the remaining Parmesan with a vegetable peeler, and finish with a squeeze of the remaining lemon and a drizzle of the extra virgin olive oil.

name: Green Bean & Feta Pasta
description: A simple vegetarian pasta recipe that you can make in 15 minutes. Nothing more, nothing less.
instructions: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, add the spaghetti and cook according to packet instructions. Finely chop most of the parsley, saving some leaves for serving.
Peel and slice the garlic and green chilli. Add olive oil to the pan and add green beans and cook for 2 mins, then add the garlic along with the fennel seeds and green chilli.

Add the white wine, and cook until reduced by half. Add the cooked spaghetti. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and add the chopped parsley. Season to taste, then tip into bowls and top with the feta and toasted hazelnuts and a scattering of parsley leaves.

name: Green Bean, Pesto & Almond Salad
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A fresh and tasty spring salad. There's a hell of a lot you can do with a jar of pesto and a few fresh ingredients.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Tear the flatbreads into bite sized pieces and scatter onto a tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Grate over a little parmesan and slide into the oven for 10-12 mins or until golden brown and crispy.
Meanwhile, bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Drop in the beans and broccoli for 3-4 mins or until just tender, still with a little bite. Shock in icy cold water and then dry.

Add the pesto to a large mixing bowl and grate in some more Parmesan. Add the zest and juice of the lemon and a couple of glugs of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and mix to a loose pesto dressing.

Drop the cooked beans and broccoli into the bowl with the dressing. Halve the tomatoes and chuck them in, too. Add the almonds, flatbread croutons and the remaining parmesan, you can shave or grate, up to you!
Toss together and divide between plates.

name: Green Chicken, Kale and Crispy Chickpea Salad
description: We love a salad around here and this is one of our favourites. Tender, juicy chicken combine with fresh herby yoghurt and tangy pomegranate to make something absolutely delicious, and healthy too.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.

Drain your chickpeas, then pat them dry with a kitchen towel. Pour them onto a baking tray, and season them with half of the garam masala, as well as a drizzle of olive oil and a big pinch of salt. Toss the chickpeas so that they are evenly coated, then bake them for 30 mins until crispy.

Whilst your chickpeas cook, prep the rest. Add the coriander, green chilli, garlic clove, lime juice, half of the yoghurt, and ½ tsp salt. Whizz it up into a smooth green sauce. Taste and season with more salt, or lime if needed.
Pour the green sauce into the remaining yoghurt, and stir together (this is so it doesn’t get too thin).

Pour 1/3 of this sauce into a bowl. Bash your chicken until 1cm thick, then add to the sauce, along with your remaining garam masala, and give it a good mix. Place onto a baking tray lined with baking paper and slide into the oven until fully cooked, 15-20 mins.
Once your chickpeas are cooked, set them aside to cool a bit.
Peel and finely chop your red onion. Halve your cherry tomatoes. Add your red onion to the large bowl with a pinch of salt.
Pull your kale leaves off their stalks, and add the leaves to the onions. Drizzle with some olive oil, then massage your kale leaves, until the it looks a wet, dark green and has wilted.

Toss your cherry tomatoes and pomegranate seeds into the kale, and pour in your remaining green sauce. Give it a good toss so that the leaves are all coated, then add your chickpeas and briefly toss it again.
Spoon your salad into bowls, slice the chicken and serve it on top.

name: Green Chilli & Sausage Noodles
description: We bloody love a sausage and noodles situation. We’ve topped this dish with our bright and spicy green chilli oil. Winner, winner, sausage dinner.
instructions: Tip the rice noodles into a bowl and cover with warm water, set aside for 15 mins. Heat a tbsp of oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and squeeze the sausages from their casing into the pan, using a spatula to break up the meat. Fry for 10 mins, until crispy and browned.

Finely shred the hispi cabbage and finely slice three of the spring onions. Whisk the miso with the tahini and the juice of a lime, then add splashes of water until it comes together to make a loose sauce. It should be the consistency of single cream. Don’t worry if it seizes and looks clumpy at the start – keep whisking in the water and it’ll come together.

Tip the crispy sausage meat from the pan into a bowl, then add the shredded cabbage and spring onions to the pan along with a big pinch of salt, fry until softened, then stir through half of the crispy sausage meat.
Drain the noodles and rinse with a little cold water, then add to the pan with greens and toss well, add the sauce and toss well.

Twirl the veg and noodles into 4 bowls, top with the crispy sausage meat, then pour the green chilli oil over the top of each. Scatter with extra sesame seeds, coriander and a finely sliced spring onion. Serve with the final lime, cut into wedges, on the side.

name: Green Chilli & Walnut Pesto Pasta
description: Bright green homemade pesto is the secret ingredient in this simple pasta recipe.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Meanwhile, blitz the ingredients for the pesto into a smooth paste.
Drop the pasta into the boiling water and cook according to package instructions.

Heat a little olive oil to a large frying pan over a medium high heat. Add the kale and stir until starting to wilt, spoon in the pesto, then whisk in a ladle of the pasta water. Use a slotted spoon to move the pasta from the water to the large frying pan.
Toss the pasta well, taste and season with salt and pepper and extra lemon juice if needed. Spoon into bowls, grate with a little extra parmesan and finish with some extra black pepper.

name: Green Chilli Chicken
description: This green chicken soup is packed with protein, beans and tomatillo salsa. Topped with avo, cheddar and crunchy tortilla crisps.
instructions: Dice the chicken breast. Add the chicken, tomatillo salsa and chicken stock to a large saucepan. Finely grate in the garlic, season with salt and place over a medium heat. Let it simmer for 8–10 mins until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the jalapeño, avocado and radishes. Finely mince the coriander.

Once the chicken is cooked, stir in the cannellini beans (with their liquid) and the coriander. Let it warm through for another minute or two. Taste and season with more salt, black pepper and a good squeeze of lime juice.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Top with a handful of grated cheddar, sliced radishes, avocado and jalapeño. Serve with tortilla crisps on the side.

name: Green Chilli Chicken Freezer Burrito
description: Bursting with juicy chicken, punchy jalapeños & a zingy coriander-lime sauce, these freezer-friendly burritos are the packed lunch you’ll crave all week.
keywords: Green Chilli Chicken Freezer Burrito recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Get the chicken onto a tray and drizzle with 1 Tbsp olive oil. Sprinkle over two-thirds of the cumin, season with salt and pepper, then toss to coat. Roast for 18–20 mins until cooked through. Set aside to cool for 10 mins.

Meanwhile, rub the peppers with a little oil and char them over an open flame until blackened all over. Pop them into a bowl and cover with cling film to steam. You can also do this under a grill set to high.

Once cool enough to handle, peel off the skins, remove the seeds and add the peppers to a high-speed blender. Chuck in the garlic cloves, jalapeños, coriander, the remaining cumin, the juice of the lime, the tomatillo salsa, and a big pinch of salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth.

Shred the chicken using two forks. Drain and rinse the black beans. Grate the cheddar. Add the shredded chicken and black beans to a large mixing bowl. Pour over the green sauce and give everything a good mix. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for a few seconds on each side until soft and pliable.

To build the burritos, add a generous spoonful of the chicken filling to the centre of a tortilla, top with a sprinkle of cheddar, and a spoonful of rice. Fold the sides over the filling, then roll it up tightly away from you. Repeat with the remaining tortillas until you have used up all of the mixture.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the burritos seam-side down and cook for 1–2 mins to seal. Remove the burritos from the pan. You can eat them straight away, or then wrap each burrito tightly in baking paper and foil and pop in the freezer for later.

To reheat, take off the foil and baking paper.From frozen: Pop your burrito on a microwave-safe plate and cover it loosely with a lid or an upside-down bowl. Microwave for 3–4 minutes, flipping halfway, until it’s soft to the touch. Then stick it in the air fryer at 180°C for 15–20 minutes, or bake in the oven at 180°C for 20–25 minutes, until it’s hot right through.From chilled: Wrap it in a lightly damp paper towel to keep the tortilla soft. Microwave for 1–2 minutes, flipping halfway, then air fry at 180°C for 8-10 mins (or bake in the oven at 160°C for 15 mins) until piping hot throughout.

name: Green Chilli Chicken Meatballs
description: This is a spin on the viral Hailey Bieber meatballs. I've added cottage cheese to the meatball mix to punch up the protein, served in a simple tomato sauce, with fresh basil and another big dollop of cottage cheese on top which feels just as indulgent as burrata.
instructions: Very finely chop the shallots and garlic. Add half of each to a large mixing bowl and the other half to a medium non-stick frying pan with the extra virgin olive oil.

Finely chop most of the basil, reserving a few leaves for garnish, then finely chop the parsley. Finely chop one of the green chillies and thinly slice the other. Add the herbs and the finely chopped chilli to the bowl.
Zest the lemon into the bowl, then halve it and add the juice of one half. Grate in half the Parmesan using the same microplane.

Crumble the sourdough into the bowl between your fingers until it resembles breadcrumbs. Crack in the egg, add the cottage cheese and chicken mince and season generously with salt and pepper. Mix well with your hands until everything is combined and smooth. You can blitz the meatball ingredients together in a food processor to save time.

Wet your hands and roll the mixture into meatballs, placing them straight into the basket of an air fryer or onto a baking tray lined with non-stick baking parchment. An ice cream scoop makes quick, even work of the portioning. Air fry at 200°C for 10-12 mins, until golden. You may need to work in batches depending on the size of your air fryer.
Once the meatballs are in, turn the heat under the frying pan to medium-low and fry the shallot and garlic for around 4 mins, until soft. Add a splash of water if it starts to catch.

Add the chopped tomatoes, or passata if you prefer, along with the remaining lemon juice, and season generously with salt and pepper. Simmer over a low heat for 10 mins, until slightly reduced. Season to taste.
When the meatballs have browned, add them to the sauce to coat generously.

Divide the meatballs and sauce between bowls and top with the remaining cottage cheese, a grating of Parmesan and the reserved sliced chilli and basil leaves. They're perfect on their own, but just as good over pasta, rice or a salad.

name: Green Chilli Fish Traybake
