description: Flaky hake nestled in a vivid green chilli and coconut sauce, with a crisp, zingy apple and cucumber salsa on top.  The green chilli oil does all the heavy lifting here, it's sharp with just the right amount of kick. You've seriously never had a traybake this good.
keywords: Green Chilli Fish with Apple and Cucumber Salsa
Green Chilli Fish with Apple and Cucumber Salsa recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 240°C. Then get the jasmine rice on, cooking according to packet instructions.

Meanwhile, add all the green chilli oil ingredients to a blender and blitz until smooth. Taste it, jalapeños vary in heat, so add more if yours are mild and you like it fiery. Add 1½ tbsp of the oil to the fish fillets along with the salt, mix to coat and leave to marinate for 30 mins. Spoon 2 tbsp of the green chilli oil into a small serving bowl and set aside, leaving the rest in the blender for later.
If you're making the salsa, slice the apple and cucumber into matchsticks and toss with the salt and the juice of both limes. Set aside.

Add the coconut milk to the blender with the remaining green chilli oil and blitz until smooth, don't worry if it looks slightly curdled at this stage, it'll still taste great. Pour into a 34 x 25cm baking tray. Thinly slice the leek into rounds, add to the tray and mix well, then arrange the marinated fish fillets on top.
Bake for 14 mins, until the leeks are browned in places and the fish is just cooked.
Spoon the fish, leeks and sauce over the rice, then drizzle over some of the reserved green chilli oil. Top with the apple and cucumber salsa and finish with a good squeeze of lime.

name: Green Chilli Oil
description: This is really easy and looks super impressive! The trick to making the oil clear is boiling all of the moisture out of it – the more you know.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic, peel the ginger and slice into matchsticks. Finely slice the green chilli, add them all to a small saucepan along with the sesame seeds and cover with the oil. Put the pan over a low heat and cook for 10 mins, until the garlic and ginger are crisp.

Place a sieve over a bowl and tip the oil through, catching the crispy bits. Tip the oil into a blender, then tip the contents of the sieve into the bowl. Line the sieve with a cloth or clean tea towel and place back over the bowl.

Grab a bowl of ice water. Bring a pan of salted water to the boil, drop the basil leaves in, discarding the stalks, along with the coriander (stalks and all). Count to 10, then use tongs to transfer to the ice water.

Leave for 5 mins until cold, then remove, squeeze out as much water as possible and add to the blender with the oil, blitz until smooth as possible, then pour into the lined sieve and set aside to drip through, creating a vibrant green chilli oil.
If the oil isn’t super clear at this point, you can transfer it to a pan and boil for a couple of minutes until it goes clear (it’s a magic trick!). Cool, and transfer into a jar or bottle.

name: Green Coconut Noodle Soup
description: This cosy bowl is a hug for the soul. It's great to look at, and even better to eat.
instructions: Finely chop the shallots, garlic, chilli and ginger. Keep a few chilli slices to the side for garnish. Melt 1 tbsp of coconut oil in a pot. Add the shallots, garlic, chilli and ginger and season with salt. Sauté on low for 5-6 mins, until soft but not browned.

Meanwhile, remove the stems from the shiitake mushrooms. Finely chop these and add these to the pot and sauté for a few minutes more. Add 1L of water to the pot with the stock cube. Put a ladle of broth into a small mixing bowl and whisk through the miso – this will make sure that it’s completely dissolved. Add this back into the broth with 3 tbsp of soy sauce. Simmer on low until you have finished with the next steps.
Remove the tough stems from the coriander and set a few aside for garnish. Add this to a blender with the tin of coconut milk and blend until smooth.

Slice the shiitake tops thinly and chop the broccoli into small pieces. Add the shiitake and broccoli to a frying pan and fry with a tbsp of coconut oil and sauté until browned. Add a splash of soy sauce at the end and set aside.

When you are ready to serve, add the noodles to the broth and cook for the amount of time it states on the packet. Add the coconut coriander mix to the broth and remove it from the heat as soon as it’s hot enough. (The coriander will start to turn very dark if it’s heated too long).

Finely slice the chilli, if using. To serve, add the noodle broth to a bowl and top with the shiitake and broccoli. Finish with a good squeeze of lime juice, some extra coriander leaves and some chilli oil if you like.

name: Green Coconut Prawn & Noodle Salad
description: The secret ingredient in this fresh and flavourful prawn salad recipe is the chilli coconut dressing. It's so good you could bathe it in. Obviously don't do that, though. It'll sting.
keywords: Green Coconut Prawn & Noodle Salad recipe
instructions: Pour the coconut milk into a pan, place onto high heat and let it boil for 3-4 mins, until it has reduced by half. Pour the coconut milk into a blender and add the chilli jam and half the coriander in, let it cool down before blending until smooth. Squeeze the lime juice in and season with fish sauce.

Cook the noodles according to package instructions. Once the noodles are cooked, transfer to a sieve, and run cold water on them. Place a saucepan full of water onto high heat, bring to the boil and season generously with salt. Once boiling, drop the prawns in, remove from the heat and poach for 3-5 mins until cooked through. Drain and wash under cold running water until cool.
Pick leaves from the mint and remaining coriander, discarding the stalks. Halve the sugar snap peas and thinly slice the spring onions.

Add the dressing into a bowl with the rice noodles, prawns, mint, coriander, sugar snap peas and spring onions. Toss together with half of the crispy shallots, taste and season with more fish sauce, if needed. Finish with a drizzle of chilli oil and more crispy shallots.

name: Green Curry Leaf Prawns Recipe
description: You'll need to find a generous handful of fresh curry leaves for these incredible curry leaf prawns. We promise, you won’t have tasted prawns like these before! They’re zesty, herby, spicy and perfect as a snack, starter or a light main with a malabar paratha or rice. If you want a bit more gravy, you can let the sauce down a bit with coconut milk.
instructions: Peel and clean the prawns and remove the grit line by cutting a small incision down the back and removing with a fork, then transfer to a bowl. Add the turmeric, ginger paste, garlic paste and a pinch of black pepper. Season with salt and set aside for 15-20 mins.

Meanwhile, add a generous glug of oil to a small frying pan and place over a medium-high heat. Once hot, shallow fry most of the curry leaves, leaving a couple raw for later, until they change colour and become dark. Be careful: the curry leaves will make the oil splutter. You don't need the leaves to go crispy – just to cook through for a few seconds. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the curry leaves to a plate lined with kitchen paper.

Add most of the fried curry leaves (save a few for garnish) to a pestle and mortar, spice grinder or small blender. Add three-quarters of the garlic, turmeric, a pinch of salt and the water, then blend until you have a nice, thick chutney.
Finely mince the remaining garlic. Trim and thinly slice the red onion and chillies.

Heat the ghee in a pan or wok set over a medium-high heat. Fry the mustard seeds until they start popping, then, add the minced garlic, onion, green chilli and reserved raw curry leaves. Fry for 2-3 mins until the onion is golden brown.
Add the prawns and fry for a couple of minutes, until pink. Add the chutney with a splash of water and continue frying until the prawns are beautifully coated and cooked through.
Serve garnished with the remaining whole fried curry leaves.

name: Green Curry Lentils With Crispy Fried Eggs
description: A quick, easy, and protein-packed dinner that tastes way better than we've made that sound. Seriously. This is what you want for dinner tonight.
keywords: Green Curry Lentils With Crispy Fried Eggs
instructions: Thinly slice the garlic and roughly dice the onions. Strip the spring greens from the stems and finely slice them. Pick the basil leaves from the stems and finely halve, deseed, and slice the chilli.
Take a large, lidded frying pan and add 4-5 tbsp of olive oil. Add the garlic and onions and cook over a high heat for 2-3 mins. Add the curry paste and cook for a couple of mins.

Drain the lentils and toss into the pan, cooking on a high heat for 1-2 mins. Add the coconut milk and bring to a boil. Toss in the peas and spring greens, season generously, and drizzle with a little more oil and the sherry vinegar.

While it's bubbling away, heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Crack in the eggs and let them sizzle away, basting with oil occasionally until the edges are crispy. Once cooked, remove from the pan drain on kitchen paper.
Serve the lentils in warm bowls and top with the crispy egg, sliced chilli, and basil.

name: Green Curry Poached Chicken in Brothy Rice
description: So quick, so delicious! This dish is light, packed with nutrients, and bursting with flavour. Perfect for meal prepping and enjoying throughout the week.
keywords: Green Curry Poached Chicken in Brothy Rice
Green Curry Poached Chicken in Brothy Rice recipe
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions.
Finely slice the shallot into thin strips, thinly slice ½ the chillies and pick the Thai basil leaves. Toss everything together in a bowl, saving a few Thai basil leaves for later. Set aside.

Cook the curry paste: Heat ½ the coconut milk in a large pan set over a medium heat. Cook for 5-7 mins until the fat starts to separate and it becomes aromatic. Stir in the curry paste and cook for 5 mins, until the paste darkens and releases its fragrance. Add the sugar and cook for an additional 2 mins, letting it caramelise. Deglaze with ½ the fish sauce, scraping up any sticky bits.

Make the broth: Add the remaining coconut milk and stock to the pan. Bring the mixture to a simmer then transfer to a blender, reserving the pan for later. Add the spinach and coriander to the blender and blitz on high until smooth and vibrant green. Return the mixture to the pan.

Cook the chicken: Bring the broth back to a simmer. Add the chicken breasts and the remaining whole chilies then cover with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Let it gently simmer for 8-10 mins, or until the chicken is fully cooked through.

Transfer the chicken breasts from the broth to a plate and use two forks to shred the meat, then set aside. Add the baby corn to the simmering broth and leave to cook for 2 mins. Season the broth to taste with lime juice and salt, and the remaining Thai basil leaves and remaining fish sauce.

To serve, divide the rice between bowls then top with the shredded chicken. Ladle the vibrant broth over the chicken, then top with the shallot and herb salad. Finish with a wedge of lime for a burst of freshness.

Storage: If making ahead, divide the shredded chicken between containers and cover with the broth and baby corn. Store the rice and herbs in separate containers. To reheat, microwave the rice and meat/broth separately until hot.

name: Green Curry Soup With Ramen Crisp
description: I've used ramen noodles here not only in the green curry soup but also as a crispy topping. It's an addictive snack and as well as a delicious topping.
instructions: Drain the tofu. Blend the tofu with most of the coriander (keep some to the side for garnish) until smooth.
Chop the broccoli into bite size pieces and slice the sweetcorn once lengthways.
Add the noodles to a pot of hot water and cook as per the package instructions. Remove a few tablespoons of the noodles and spread them out on a tissue or tea towel and gently pat them dry.

To make the fried noodle crisp, heat enough sunflower oil to cover the bottom of a small saucepan. Check that the oil is hot enough by dropping in a tiny piece of noodle, if it sizzles immediately, it’s ready. Carefully add the noodles to the hot oil, spreading them in a circle.
Once the noodles have formed a firm crisp, carefully flip it to fry the other side. Take care not to burn it, it should be golden brown on both sides.
Repeat with to make another crisp and set them aside to drain on a kitchen towel. You can also sprinkle them with the ramen seasoning.
Heat up a drizzle of olive oil in a medium saucepan and add the curry paste. Fry for 2 mins, stirring constantly.
Add the stock cube, 600ml of water and the tofu coriander mixture. Bring to a boil and then turn down to a simmer. Add the broccoli and sweetcorn and cook for 3-5 mins until soft.

To serve, ladle the noodles into two bowls and then add the green curry broth into the bowls. Sprinkle with the remaining coriander. Top with the ramen crisp and break it up into pieces to create the crispy ramen bits.

name: Green Dal
description: Dal is appropriate at all times of the year. This green, veg-packed version is the textbook definition of soothing.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the cauliflower into florets and put on a baking tray. Drizzle with oil, salt and pepper, then transfer to the oven and cook for 15 min.

Pour the stock into a large pan and bring to the boil. Rinse the red lentils well and add to the stock, then grate in the ginger and the garlic. Add the curry powder and simmer for 15 mins until the lentils are soft.

Put the coconut milk into a blender with the coriander and blitz until smooth, then add to the lentil pan. Mix and season with salt and pepper. When the cauliflower is cooked, mix through the mango chutney.
Finely slice the chilli. Stir the spinach through the dal and top with the cauliflower. Garnish with coriander, chillies and a drizzle of coconut milk.

name: Green Eggs & Bacon Muffin
description: Herby green eggs, crispy streaky bacon and creamy garlic spinach piled onto a toasted English muffin. The perfect prep-ahead breakfast, packing lots of protein and even more flavour.
instructions: Finely chop the garlic. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat, add the garlic and cook gently for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Add the spinach with a splash of water, cover with a lid and cook, stirring occasionally, until wilted. Remove the lid and crank the heat to let any excess water evaporate. Stir in the cream cheese, season with salt and black pepper, mix well and keep warm.
Heat the grill to high. Line a baking sheet with foil, lay out the bacon rashers and slide under the grill for 5-7 mins until golden and crisp. Remove and leave to cool, then chop into small pieces.

Heat the oven to 180°C. Add four of the eggs to a blender along with the parsley and coriander. Blitz until smooth, then pour into a bowl. Crack in six more eggs, add the milk, season generously with salt and black pepper. Then whisk until foamy.

Pour the egg mixture into a lined baking tray and bake for 10-12 mins, until just starting to set around the edges with a slight crust forming. Carefully remove from the oven and crack the remaining six eggs directly on top. Return to the oven and cook for a further 7-10 mins, or until the eggs are just set with the yolks still runny.
Toast the muffins, spoon over the creamy spinach, then top with a slice of the baked egg, the chopped bacon and a drizzle of sriracha.

name: Green Goddess Chickpea Sandwich
description: This green goddess chickpea sandwich filling is packed with plant protein, polyphenols and fibre. You can customise the recipe with whatever you have on hand and it stores really well in the fridge for meal prep. If sandwiches aren’t your thing, it’s also a delicious way to add some extra fibre and protein into salads.
instructions: To a blender, add your avocado, kefir, juice of the lemon, garlic, ¾ of the parsley, ¾ of the dill, vinegar and a pinch of salt. Blitz until smooth.

Pour the dressing over the chickpeas and mash together. Taste to check the seasoning. Pile it into a sandwich or on top of a salad. Thinly chop the remaining herbs and spring onions and use them as a garnish.
We made ours into a sandwich with sourdough toast, tomatoes, avocado and sprouts. (If we had it, sauerkraut or kimchi would’ve been delicious too for extra probiotic benefits.)

name: Green Goddess Chopped Salad
description: A simple chopped salad with a green goddess dressing that's so good you'll want to swim laps in it.
instructions: Slice the cucumber in half lengthways and use a spoon to remove the fleshy center. Chop the lettuce, celery sticks, spring onions until all around the same size. Tip into a bowl with the cucumber halves and sugar snap peas. Toss in the brown rice and fresh herbs then mix everything together.

To make the dressing, halve and de-stone the avocado and add the flesh to a blender along with the green chilli, herb leaves and lemon juice. If you want the dressing a bit looser, add a splash of water. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Tip the dressing over the salad and toss well.
If you want to top with halloumi, cut the halloumi into 2cm cubes and pan fry in a dry pan over a high heat until golden on all sides. Tip on top of the salad and scatter with toasted sesame seeds.

name: Green Goddess Halloumi Rice Bowl
description: I seriously love this bowl - it's hearty, full of flavour and because it pops with vibrant colours, it feels super nourishing and nutritious. Exactly what I'd want to eat for dinner after a very long day at work.
keywords: Green Goodness Halloumi Rice Bowl recipe
instructions: Scoop the avocado flesh into a blender, then add the remaining sauce ingredients and blitz until smooth. Taste and season with salt or a splash more pickled chilli brine, then set aside.
Chop the halloumi into 2-3cm chunks and halve the cherry tomatoes. Season the tomatoes with salt and set aside, then roughly chop the remaining coriander.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a third of the olive oil. Once hot, add the pumpkin seeds and fry for 2-3 mins, until toasted. Using a slotted spoon, transfer them to a plate, leaving the oil in the pan.
Add the halloumi to the hot pan and fry for 3-4 mins, until golden on all sides. Transfer to a bowl, add the hot honey and toss together.
Add another third of the olive oil to the pan and, once hot, crack in the eggs and cook to your liking. Season with salt and black pepper.

Toss the tomatoes with the chopped coriander, pumpkin seeds and the last of the olive oil. Thinly slice the remaining pickled chillies and toss them through with a touch of pickled chilli brine, if it needs it.

Reheat the rice according to the packet instructions. Add the fried eggs to the rice with half the sauce, tear the eggs up and toss everything through. Share between bowls, top with the halloumi and tomato salad, then drizzle over more sauce and dig in.

name: Green Goddess Pasta Salad
description: A fresh and delicious pasta salad brought together with half a pack of bacon, roasted and fresh vegetables, and a lush avocado-mayo green goddess dressing.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C.
Get a pot of salted water to a boil.

Chop your courgette and peppers into small chunks. Place them on a baking tray, drizzle over some olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and pop them into the oven for 20 mins, until starting to char and crisp up.
Meanwhile, wash your spinach and pat dry with a paper towel.
Chop your white cabbage, cucumber and avocado into small chunks. Finely slice your spring onions. Add these all to a large salad bowl.
Place your tomatoes on the baking tray with your courgettes and peppers and drizzle them with a bit of oil before popping the tray back in the oven for 5 mins, until done to your liking.
Put your pasta in the boiling water, drain using a colander once al dente.
Fry your bacon until crispy.

To make the mayo, start by roughly chopping your garlic, shallot, avocado and herbs. Add these all to a blender or food processor, along with the juice of half a lemon, water, and spinach. Add your mayonnaise and give it a blitz.

Roughly chop your bacon into bite-sized pieces before adding it to your salad bowl along with your roasted vegetables and avo mayo dressing. Give it a good toss and finish with some lemon zest. Enjoy.

name: Green Goddess Roast Chicken Salad
description: A roast chicken is the perfect base for any salad (if you're short on time you could easily use a store bought rotisserie chicken). This one's tossed with white beans, crisp lettuce, blanched greens and a vivid, herby green goddess dressing.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Take the chicken out of the fridge about 30 mins before roasting – it cooks more evenly that way.

Slice the lemon for the chicken in half. Crush the garlic cloves with the flat side of a knife, leaving the skins on. Stuff the chicken cavity with the lemon halves, garlic and thyme. Drizzle the chicken all over with olive oil. Get stuck in and rub it in properly. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Pop the chicken breast-side up in a roasting tray. Roast for about 50 mins–1 hr, or until the juices run clear when you pierce the thickest part of the thigh.For this recipe used a 1.5kg-2kg chicken, adjust the timings for a smaller or larger bird.

While the chicken's cooking make the dressing. Juice the lemon and peel the garlic clove. Add the yoghurt, avocado, basil, chives, garlic, lemon juice and olive oil to a blender and blitz until completely smooth and vivid green. Season generously with salt and black pepper. If the dressing is looking too thick, loosen with a splash of cold water to a pourable consistency.

Once the chicken is done and has rested for 10 mins, shred the meat into bite-sized pieces and set aside. Core the apple and slice into thin matchstick strips. Snap the woody ends off the asparagus and trim the green beans. Blanch both in a large saucepan of salted boiling water for 1-2 mins until just tender, then drain and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking.

Drain the cannellini beans and roughly chop the romaine lettuce. Add both to a large bowl along with the asparagus, green beans and shredded chicken. Spoon over as much dressing as you like and toss gently to coat.
Arrange on a large platter or divide between bowls. Serve with any remaining dressing alongside.

name: Green Goddess Salad Dressing
description: A green goddess dressing that's so good you'll want to swim laps in it. Add it to salads to combine it with your choice of protein, veg and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Halve and de-stone the avocado and add the flesh to a blender along with the green chilli, fresh coriander, fresh mint and the juice of the lemon. Blitz to combine then season generously to taste with salt and pepper.
Toss the dressing through a salad or, if meal prepping for the week, transfer to a jar or container and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Green Goddess Soba Noodle Salad
description: This one is about as fresh as it gets. Chewy noodles, fresh dressing, and some crunchy veg. A winning combination.
instructions: Bring a pan of water to the boil, add the soba noodles and cook for according to packet instructions, then drain and rinse well with cold water.
Meanwhile finely slice the radishes and add them to a bowl with the juice of half of a lemon and a pinch of salt, set aside.

Finely slice the mangetout and add to a large bowl. Roughly chop the herbs and add them to the bowl. Halve the avocado and remove the pip. Peel, then slice into 1cm chunks and add to the bowl. Add the drained soba. Roughly chop the peanuts and add half to the bowl.

Peel and finely slice the garlic and add to a small pan. Peel the ginger and cut into matchsticks, then add to the pan along with 1 ½ tbsp olive oil. Place over a medium heat and sizzle until just starting to turn golden then tip into the large bowl with the rest of the ingredients. Add the juice of a half a lemon and toss well, season well with salt and pepper.
Twirl onto a plate, top with the sliced radishes, remaining peanuts and chilli flakes and a crack of pepper. Squeeze the juice of the last lemon half over the top.

name: Green Herby Chicken and Rice Soup
description: This one is healthy, nourishing, and delicious. Inspired by Molokhia, we've changed it up a bit and made this herby chicken soup. It'll have you feeling rested and rejuvenated. Give it a go.
cuisine: Middle-Eastern Inspired, Lebanese-Inspired, Cypriot, North African, Egyptian
instructions: Add the 7-spice into a bowl with salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Toss the chicken thighs through until evenly coated. Set aside.
Peel and finely slice the garlic and onion, and mince the coriander, stalks and all. Trim and thinly slice the jalapeño.
Add the onion into a bowl with the vinegar and season with salt. Toss together and set aside to pickle.

Into a saucepan, add a generous drizzle of olive oil and place on a medium-high heat. Once hot, cook the chicken on both sides until golden brown and cooked through, 8-10 mins. Transfer to a clean board or plate, cover and let rest.
Add the garlic and coriander into the chicken pan, and cook, stirring, until dark green and fragrant, for about 3-4 mins.
Then, pour the chicken stock and frozen chopped spinach. Gently simmer until the spinach has defrosted. Taste and season, if needed.
Reheat the rice according to the package instructions.
Slice the chicken into strips. Share the rice between bowls, top with the chicken and pour the soup over. Garnish with pickled onion and jalapeños, and a drizzle of pickled onion brine.

name: Green Herby Frittata
description: This is a take on kuku sabzi, a Persian dish which uses a lot of vibrant green herbs and is traditionally eaten in spring. Jordon x
instructions: Finely dice your onion and sweat in a large non-stick frying pan with about 3 tbsp of olive oil until soft but not brown for 4 to 5 mins.
While the onions are cooking, finely chop all of the fresh herbs and add to a large bowl.
Add the spinach to the onions along with a big pinch of salt.
Cook for a few mins until the spinach wilts completely.
Add the cooked onions and spinach to the bowl with the chopped herbs, then add the spices, eggs, flour, cranberries and pistachios. Mix well.
Preheat your grill to 180°C.
Place your pan back over a medium-low heat and add another 2 tbsp of olive oil and the butter. When the butter is foaming, add the frittata mix and flatten with the back of a spoon.
Allow to cook for about 5 mins, until you can see the edges setting and turning slightly darker.
Now place the pan under the grill for a few mins until the top has set.
Slide the frittata out onto a serving dish and drizzle with a little olive oil and a pinch of flaky salt.
Serve a warm slice along with a spoon of yoghurt.

name: Green Herby Lentils with Pasta
description: A high-protein pasta recipe which is perfect for a post-workout meal.
keywords: Green Herby Lentils with Pasta recipe
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the onions and garlic. Finely mince the parsley and dill, stalks and all.
Put half of the spinach into a blender, add the vegetable stock and blend until smooth. Chop the remaining spinach and set aside.
Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the onions and cook for 12-15 mins until deep golden brown. Transfer half to a bowl and set it aside.
Add the garlic, turmeric, dried mint, dill, chopped spinach and parsley to the frying pan, along with the pasta. Cook until fragrant, about 5 mins.

Pour a ladleful of spinach stock over the pasta, then cook, stirring, until the pasta absorbs the liquid. Add another ladleful and continue stirring, adding more stock until the pasta is cooked through or al dente.
Once the pasta is cooked, stir through the lentils and black beans, adding more spinach stock to thin it out. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Crumble the feta and toss with the reserved onions and dried fruit.
Share the pasta between bowls, drizzle over some yoghurt and finish with a sprinkle of the onion mixture.

name: Green Hummus Bowl
description: We've made a cheat-y hummus with loads of herbs and served it up topped with sticky halloumi. Dreamy, easy, dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Cut the tomatoes and cucumber into chunks and add to a bowl with a big pinch of salt. Set aside.
Cut the pitta breads into triangles and tip onto a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season well. Slide into the oven and bake for 10-15 mins, until golden and crisp. Set aside to cool.
Tip the hummus into a high-speed blender. Add the herb leaves, tahini and 2 tbsp of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and blitz. If it’s super thick, add enough water to loosen it a little.
Tip the pitta chips into the bowl with the tomatoes and cucumber. Add 2 tbsp of olive oil and the red wine vinegar. Add the parsley leaves, season well and toss.

Slice the halloumi into 1cm thick slices. Drizzle with olive oil. Heat a pan over a medium-high heat, add the halloumi slices and cook for 2 mins on each side, until golden. Squeeze the honey over the top and remove from the heat.
To serve, swoop half of the hummus up the side of the 2 plates. Divide the salad and halloumi between the plates. Scatter with sesame seeds and red pepper flakes to serve.

name: Green Kefir Dressing
description: A kefir-packed dressing that's so good you could drink it. This is what summer's all about.
keywords: Tomato & Chickpea Salad on Green Kefir Dressing
instructions: Scoop the avocado into a blender. Add the chives, the basil, anchovies and lime juice with the olive oil, blend until smooth. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the kefir into the dressing, giving it a quick whizz until mixed. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Set aside in the fridge.

name: Green Mac & Cheese
description: If you love macaroni cheese but want to sneak in a few nutrients, this recipe is for you. How much spinach can you squeeze into a mac’n’cheese? A lot.
instructions: Defrost the spinach. Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil.
Once the water is boiling, add the rigatoni and cook following pack instructions until al dente. Do not over cook. Drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, in a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat, then add the flour and whisk while cooking for 1-2 mins, stirring constantly, until it bubbles and begins to foam.
Gradually add in the milk, whisking constantly to avoid lumps. Cook for around 5-8 mins or until the sauce thickens. Add the mustard and remove from the heat.

Grate in ¾ of the cheddar cheese and all the Parmesan and stir until melted. Stir in the defrosted spinach and the just-cooked pasta, taste and season with salt, pepper and a very generous grating of nutmeg. Transfer to a baking dish.

Add the remaining grated cheddar cheese to the top. Slide under the grill until the top is bubbling and golden, 2-5. mins. Remove from the oven and dust over with some extra Parmesan to serve, if you like.

name: Green Noodles
description: These veggie udon noodles are high in protein and packed full of green goodness. They’re healthy, delicious and incredibly satisfying.
instructions: Start by making the crispy topping. Peel and slice the garlic, finely slice the chilli and peel and dice the shallot. Add to a small saucepan and cover generously with vegetable oil so the aromatics are fully submerged. Place the pan over a medium-high heat and cook for around 5-7 mins until browned and crispy.
Use a slotted spoon to scoop out the crispy aromatics and add to a bowl. Season with the sugar and MSG, if using, and set aside. (Save the oil in the fridge for other uses, such as frying eggs.)

Place a large pan of salted water over a high heat and bring to the boil. Once boiling, add the eggs and cook for 7 mins. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the eggs to a bowl. Rinse under cold water until cool enough to handle, then peel and set aside.

While the eggs are boiling, start on the green sauce. Peel the garlic and pull the cavolo nero leaves away from the stems. Add the cavolo nero leaves, spinach, garlic and coriander to the boiling water used for the eggs and cook for 3 mins. Use tongs to transfer the greens to a sieve, then rinse with cold water until cool enough to handle.

Squeeze out any excess moisture from the blanched greens, then add them to a blender along with the remaining sauce ingredients. Blitz until smooth, adding a splash of water to loosen a little, then tip the sauce into a large mixing bowl.
Drop the udon into the boiling water and cook following packet instructions (about 2 mins for fresh or frozen udon). Use tongs to transfer the noodles to the mixing bowl of sauce then toss to coat.
To serve, divide the noodles between bowls, scraping out all the sauce into the bowls. Top generously with the crispy garlic topping and finish with the halved boiled eggs.

name: Green Olive & Mint Pasta
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Everything you love about pesto pasta, but just a little different. You need one blender and one pan to pull this off, a perfect midweek meal.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Tip the pine nuts into a roasting tray, slide into the oven and roast for 10 mins, until golden brown.

Add the green olives, half of your mint leaves, and most of the pine nuts to a mini chopper or blender and blitz into a rough paste (or finely chop by hand). Add the lemon juice along with 80ml olive oil and season well.

Add the pasta to the pan of boiling water and cook according to package instructions, then use a slotted spoon or tongs to transfer the pasta into a large mixing bowl. Add the green olive pesto, half of the feta and the reserved pint nuts. Toss well, adding a cupful of pasta water as you do. Roughly chop the rest of the mint leaves and toss into the pasta. Taste and season.
Divide the pasta between bowls, then top with the rest of your crumbled feta and reserved mint leaves. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and black pepper.

name: Green Olive Pesto
description: If you hate olives, you'll hate this green olive pesto. But if you love olives? Well, my friend, you've just found your latest obsession.
instructions: Add the green olives, parsley and pine nuts to a blender. Peel the garlic cloves and add in, then roughly chop the Parmesan and add. Add the white wine vinegar and season generously with salt and pepper.
Add ⅓ of olive oil and begin to blend, then continue to add olive oil until you get to a thick pesto consistency.

name: Green Pea Soup with Jammy Eggs & Garlicky croutons
description: This vibrant green pea soup feels like a warm Swedish spring day to me. The dilly, sour cucumber salad contrasts so well with the sweetness of the peas.
keywords: Green Pea Soup with Cucumbers & Garlicky Croutons
Green Pea Soup with Cucumbers & Garlicky Croutons recipe
instructions: Finely chop the onion and set aside. Make the salad by roughly chopping the cucumbers into small, irregular pieces. Finely chop the dill. Add the cucumber and dill to a small bowl, season with salt, zest over the lemon and squeeze in the juice of half of it. Set aside.
Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and cook for 6 mins 30 seconds, then transfer straight into a bowl of cold water to stop the cooking. Once cool, peel and halve.

Now for the croutons. Tear the bread into small, irregular chunks. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over a medium-high heat (you'll use this for the soup). Add the bread and toast, tossing occasionally, for a few minutes until golden. Finely grate over the garlic and toss to coat, then continue toasting for another minute. Remove the croutons from the pot and set aside. If you'd rather use the oven, toast the croutons at 200°C for about 10 mins.

Now for the main event. Add the olive oil to the same large pot and add the chopped onion. Fry, stirring continuously, for 3-4 mins until softened. Pour in the water, add the peas and stock pots and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 3 mins. Turn off the heat, stir in the soured cream and season with salt and black pepper. Blitz until smooth with a stick blender or regular blender.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the cucumber salad, halved jammy eggs and croutons.

name: Green Romesco Prawns & Chickpeas
description: Big, punchy flavours with minimum faff. This green romesco’s smoky-sweet vibes are perfect with juicy prawns & crispy chickpeas. A proper satisfying bowl.
instructions: Heat the grill to high.
Grill the green peppers until charred all over. Transfer to a bowl, cover and leave for 10 mins. Once cooled, peel off the blackened skin, remove the cores and seeds, then set aside.

Roughly tear two-thirds of the coriander. Remove the stem and seeds from the green chilli. Add the grilled peppers to a blender along with the torn coriander, the green chilli, most of the pumpkin seeds (save some for garnish) and ¾ of the sherry vinegar. Blitz until smooth, then season well with salt and black pepper.
Pick the remaining coriander leaves and roughly chop most of them, keeping a few whole for garnish. Peel and thinly slice the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a nonstick frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Season the prawns with salt and black pepper, then fry for around 3 mins until pink and cooked through.
Add the garlic and chickpeas to the pan and cook for another minute, tossing everything together. Drizzle in the remaining sherry vinegar, stir through the chopped coriander, and season to taste.
To serve, spoon the romesco into bowls. Top with the prawns and chickpeas, then scatter over the reserved coriander leaves and pumpkin seeds.

name: Green Summer Orzo
description: A great, light orzo dish for the summer months. The flavours intensify once cold, so great the next day as well.
instructions: Add orzo to a pan of salted boiling water.
Toast your pine nuts.

Into a blender, add a handful of fresh mint, a handful of fresh basil, toasted pine nuts, a ladle of pasta water, the garlic, the zest and juice from the lemon/s (save a bit of juice to squeeze over the dish at the end). Add around 30% of your Spinach, 80% of the parmesan, salt, pepper and olive oil. Blitz until smooth.
Add petit pois to the pasta water just before the pasta is ready. Cook for 30 seconds. Drain pasta and peas.
Add pasta and peas to a wide pan. Pour over your spinach pesto. Mix everything together. Add your remaining spinach leaves. Mix them in until they wilt.
Serve the orzo with some Parmesan and pine nuts scattered on top. Squeeze on a bit more lemon juice and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Green Tahini Chicken Salad
description: A super fresh and simple midweek dinner. This nutty sauce acts as both a dressing AND a marinade for the chicken. Delightful.
instructions: Add your parsley, mint, tahini, the juice of your lemon, olive oil and the water to a blender with a pinch of salt. Blitz to a really smooth sauce.
Pour 1/3 of this mixture into a bowl along with your za’atar and a good pinch of salt. Add your chicken and mix to combine. Leave to marinade.
Very finely slice your courgettes using a mandoline, if you’ve got one, or a sharp knife.
Cut the ends off your baby gem and separate the leaves. Give them a wash to remove any dirt.
Heat a griddle pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add your chicken and fry for about 5 mins on each side until it is totally cooked through. Remove from the pan to rest for 10 mins.
Once your chicken has cooled enough to handle, slice it into pieces.
Add your lettuce to a bowl along with your sliced courgettes and chicken. Pour over your remaining dressing, then toss to combine.
Top with your crispy shallots, then serve.

name: Green Tortelloni With Crispy Breadcrumbs
description: We've combined La Famiglia Cooked Ham & Mozzarella Tortelloni with a vibrant green sauce in this quick and simple recipe.
instructions: Start by blitzing the croutons to a rough crumb in a food processor or pestle and mortar. Season with salt. Tip into a small frying pan with a dash of olive oil and a sprinkle of salt. Set over a medium heat and toast, stirring regularly until golden brown. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Bring a pan of water to boil, add the spinach and garlic for 1 minute, remove from the water immediately, rinse with cold water and drain well. Add to a blender with crème fraîche, olive oil, lemon juice, and Parmesan. Blitz until completely smooth, then season with salt and pepper.

Bring a large pot of water to the boil, then add in the tortelloni to cook for just 2 mins before draining, save some of the water! Add the green sauce to the pan along with the drained pasta and a slosh of pasta water, then mix well to combine.
Portion into bowls and top with the breadcrumbs and a drizzle of oil.

name: Greens, Eggs and Rice
description: An easy, healthy meal-prep recipe that's packed with protein and fibre.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C. Tear or slice the mushrooms into roughly 1cm chunks. Spread them out on a large baking tray. Sprinkle over the cumin, coriander, and sesame seeds. Drizzle with olive oil, season generously with salt, and toss to coat. Roast for 25–30 mins, or until golden and crisp around the edges.

Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain well. Blitz the spinach, water, garlic and butter in a blender until smooth and vibrant green. Tip the rice into a medium saucepan, pour over the spinach mixture, and bring to a boil. Cover with a tight-fitting lid, reduce the heat to the lowest setting, and cook for 12 mins. Turn off the heat and leave to steam for 10 mins. Fluff with a fork, mix through any settled spinach, and cover again for 5 mins. Season to taste.

Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and boil for 7 mins. Transfer immediately to a bowl of ice water for a couple of minutes, then peel. Roll the eggs gently in toasted sesame seeds until fully coated.
Mix the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together the kimchi brine, honey, peanut butter and vinegar. Slowly whisk in olive oil to emulsify. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Divide the green rice between containers. Top with roasted mushrooms and a sesame egg. Serve with the kimchi peanut dressing on the side.

name: Grilled Asparagus with Poached Eggs and Hollandaise
description: An absolute treat for a breakfast or brunch, the hollandaise is given a little twist by browning the butter first to give it a lovely nutty flavour. Jordon x
keywords: Grilled asparagus with poached eggs and hollandaise recipes
instructions: Start by trimming any woody ends from the asparagus and set aside. I also like to peel the bottom 3 inches or so from the stem, but you don’t have to. Then carefully separate the egg yolks from the whites for the Hollandaise (you can freeze the whites for meringue).

To make brown butter, melt the butter in a small saucepan over a medium heat. It will bubble for a few minutes, then once the bubbles have died down, you’ll see the milk solids sinking to the bottom of the pan and turning brown as they caramelise.

As soon as the mix starts to turn a light brown colour, turn the heat right down, and remove from the heat just before it reaches a hazelnut brown colour. Grab a heatproof bowl that will fit over a small pan. Add the egg yolks, white wine vinegar and a pinch of salt and whisk to combine.

Fill the pan with water and bring to a simmer, then place the bowl on top (make sure it’s not touching the water). Whisk the mixture and as it warms it will thicken, this will take 3 or 4 mins. Now slowly pour in the melted butter, whisking to emulsify and remove from the heat. Taste and add salt and more vinegar if needed. Set aside somewhere warm.
Heat a grill pan over a high heat and add the asparagus, turning over after 3 mins until charred on both sides. Meanwhile toast the sourdough.
Spread the toast with butter and top with the asparagus. To poach the eggs, turn the heat right down on the water, stir well to create a whirlpool and crack in the eggs.

Allow to cook for about 3 mins until the white are set. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on top of the asparagus. If you need to, warm up the hollandaise again by placing the bowl back over the pan of hot water and whisking. Pour the hollandaise over the asparagus and eat straight away.

name: Grilled Broccoli, Feta & Chimichurri Grain Bowl
description: Chimichurri is a herby Argentinian sauce usually paired with steak. Its chilli heat and acidity work perfectly with charred Tenderstem, grains, and salty feta.
instructions:
Bunch the broccoli stalks together and chop in half widthways
all at once. Lay out in a single layer on a baking tray, drizzle with
a splash of extra virgin olive oil and season with salt and black
pepper. Grill for 3–4 minutes on each side, turning with tongs,
until the broccoli is charred and the stalks are tender.
Meanwhile, chop the chilli into quarters and peel the garlic cloves.
Put the coriander, stalks and all, garlic and chilli into a mini food
processor. Blitz until finely chopped – you may have to unpick the
coriander stalks from the blade at first, but persist, they will break
down. Once chopped, add the oregano and extra virgin olive oil.
Blitz again, season with the red wine vinegar and salt and black
pepper to taste.
Squeeze the grain pouches to slightly break up the grains, then
heat in the microwave following the packet instructions and tip
into a large serving dish. Drizzle over most of the chimichurri,
then crumble over half the feta and stir together. Top with the
charred broccoli and crumble over the remaining feta. Drizzle
with extra chimichurri and serve.

name: Grilled Chicken & Artichoke Salad with Mustardy Dressing
description: This is a belter of a salad. Jarred artichokes are the secret ingredient here. They make all the difference.
keywords: Grilled Chicken & Artichoke Salad with Mustardy Dressing
instructions: Preheat the grill to high.
Place a small frying pan on medium-high heat. Once hot, add the pine nuts and toast, shaking the pan often until golden, 2-3 mins. Transfer to a bowl.

Add the chicken and Tenderstem into a bowl. Peel and grate 3 cloves of garlic, strip the leaves off the rosemary and roughly chop. Add both to the chicken with 2 tbsp of olive oil, then season with a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Add the chicken to a large baking tray and grill until golden, and starting to char, 10-12 mins. Then add the Tenderstem on top and cook until charred, 3-5 mins.
Meanwhile, trim and chop the lettuce into bite-sized chunks. Pick the mint leaves, trim and chop the cucumber in 2cm chunks. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions.
Drain and finely chop the artichokes. Transfer into a large bowl with the pine nuts. Add the zest of half a lemon and 50ml of olive oil, the juice of the lemons and wholegrain mustard.
Slice the cooked chicken into 2cm strips. Toss the lettuce, mint, cucumber, spring onion, broccoli and chicken into the dressing.
Share the salad onto a platter or plates.

name: Grilled Chicken & Herby Grapefruit Salad
description: This salad will put some pep in your step. The fresh mint and citrus in the salad gives this a lovely summery flavour profile.
keywords: Grilled Chicken & Herby Grapefruit Salad recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the spring onions. Combine the curry paste, spring onion whites and oyster sauce in a bowl. Add the chicken thighs, season with salt and pepper, then toss well.

Segment the grapefruits and transfer to a bowl. Squeeze the juice out of the grapefruit membrane into another bowl. Trim and thinly slice the shallot and add to the grapefruit juice along with the chilli jam, lime juice and spring onion greens. Season with fish sauce, then set aside.
Pick the mint leaves and coriander, discarding the stalks. Halve the sugar snap peas.

Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the coconut flakes and toast until golden. Transfer to the grapefruit juice bowl. Return the pan to a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Cook the chicken for 8-10 mins until golden and cooked through. Season to taste with fish sauce.
Reheat the rice and share between bowls. Top with the chicken. Toss the mint, sugar snaps and coriander leaves through the grapefruit salad and serve alongside.

name: Grilled Chicken Burger With Mojo Verde
description: We all love a chicken burger, and this one in particular has summer written all over it. Chicken breasts are bashed and tenderised before cooking.
keywords: Grilled Chicken Burger With Mojo Verde
instructions:
Toast the cumin seeds in a small dry frying pan over a medium
heat until smelling amazing, then set aside to cool slightly.
Mojo verde time. Put three-quarters of the coriander (stalks and
all) into a blender along with the garlic clove, sherry vinegar, half
the pickled jalapeños and 1 tablespoon of the olive oil. Tip in the
cumin seeds, pour in 2 tablespoons of water and blitz to a smooth
green sauce, adding a splash more water if it needs loosening – you
want it to be a thick, drizzle-able consistency. Season to taste and
put in the fridge.
For the salsa, halve the avocados, remove the pits and cut into
cubes, then tip into a bowl. Cube the peppers, chop the remaining
coriander (stalks and all) and add these to the avocado. Finely
chop the remaining jalapeños and stir into the salsa with another
tablespoon of olive oil, then season with salt, pepper, a splash of
sherry vinegar and the pickling liquid from the jalapeños to taste.
Set aside.
Put two of the chicken breasts between two sheets of baking
paper, a few centimetres apart from each other. Using a rolling pin,
bash the chicken to tenderise and flatten it slightly to a thickness of
about 2cm. Repeat with the remaining chicken breasts, then
season them all with salt and pepper. Rub over the remaining 2
tsp of olive oil.
Get your largest griddle or non-stick frying pan searingly hot.
Lay in the chicken breasts, cook for 4–5 mins each side until the
chicken is cooked through and juicy.
Cut the buns in half, lightly toast in the pan, then assemble your
burgers. Spread the base of the buns with half the mojo verde sauce,
then top with chicken, then avo salsa, then rocket. Drizzle over the
remaining mojo verde and sandwich together to serve – with chips
if you like.

name: Grilled Chicken with Burnt Pepper Salsa & Lemon Yoghurt
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Crispy grilled chicken served on a bed of creamy lemon yoghurt, with a spicy salsa and croutons cooked in the chicken fat. All made using ingredients from Aldi.
instructions: Add the ginger, a tablespoon of olive oil, and the zest and juice of a lime to a blender and blitz for a few seconds until smooth.
Season the chicken all over with salt and then rub over the dressing. Leave to marinade for at least an hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Once ready to cook, preheat your oven to 220°C.
Place a large oven-proof pan over a medium high heat and sear the chicken all over until golden brown, about 8 mins.
Make sure the chicken is skin-side up, then transfer the pan to the oven and roast for about 12 mins until the chicken is cooked through and the juices run clear when pierced with a knife.
While the chicken roasts, add the yoghurt to a bowl, grate in the zest of a lemon and add half of its juice along with a big pinch of salt. Mix well and set aside.

Add the red pepper, a handful of coriander, a pinch of chili flakes, and the remaining lemon juice to a blender along with a tablespoon of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Pulse until coarsely chopped. Set aside.
Tear the ciabatta into roughly one-inch chunks and set them aside.

Once the chicken is ready, remove it and allow it to rest for a few minutes. While the chicken rests, add the ciabatta to the pan you cooked the chicken in along with a big pinch of salt and roast in the oven until golden and crispy, about 7 mins.
Spread the yoghurt across a large plate, top with the chicken and croutons and drizzle over the salsa.

name: Grilled Cod in Green Curry Butter with Herby Tomatoes & Garlic Rice
description: This dish features herby tomatoes and flaky, tender cod. It's deliciously aromatic and makes a wonderful midweek dinner.
instructions: Preheat the grill to high.

Start by making the curry butter. Pick the leaves of the herbs. Peel the shallot and garlic, then destem and deseed the chillies. Place all three into a blender with the rest of the curry butter ingredients, except the butter. Blend until smooth, then add the butter and blitz until incorporated. Set aside.

Prep the salad. Cut the tomatoes in half and place them on a baking tray. To make a dressing, finely mince the lemongrass and add to a mixing bowl along with the sugar and boiling water. Stir together until the sugar dissolves. Then, stir through the fish sauce and juice of the lime. Set aside. Pick the leaves of the herbs and set aside.

Start the rice. Finely mince the garlic and spring onions. Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large frying pan set over a low-medium heat. Add the garlic and gently fry until fragrant and lightly golden in colour. Turn the heat up to high, add the cooked rice and fry until hot. Add the sliced spring onions, sugar and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Cook the cod. Place the cod onto the baking tray with the tomatoes and add a drizzle of oil. Season with salt. Place the cod and tomatoes under the grill for 4 mins, until the cod is cooked and the tomatoes are starting to wilt. Add a heaped tbsp of the curry butter to each cod loin then grill for another 2-3 mins, until the butter starts to melt. Remove both from the oven and set aside for a few minutes to rest.

Toss the tomatoes and prepared herbs into the salad dressing. To serve, divide the rice and cod loins between plates. Finish with a pile of salad and drizzle over any remaining curry butter and dressing.

name: Grilled Courgette Salad With Buttery Hazelnuts & Frozen Goat's Cheese
description: This one is as light as it sounds. Give the frozen goat's cheese ago, it might surprise you.
keywords: grilled courgette salad with buttery courgettes
instructions: Freeze the goats cheese overnight.

The next day, roughly chop the hazelnuts. Melt the butter in a pan over a low-medium heat and add the hazelnuts. Keep a close eye on it, as you don’t want the butter to burn. Cook until the hazelnuts are golden, then remove and set aside.

Chop the courgettes into irregular, 4cm shapes. Transfer to a bowl with some olive oil, salt and pepper. Heat a large frying pan over a high heat and add the courgettes in a single layer, cut side down. Cook for 2 mins each side until nice and charred, then remove from the pan to cool to room temperature.
Meanwhile, pick the mint leaves and set aside.
Add the courgettes to a serving plate or bowl then spoon over the buttery hazelnuts and drizzle with the hot honey. Grate over the frozen goats cheese and scatter with mint.

name: Grilled Cucumber Salad with Crispy Chickpeas and Lemon Dressing
description: Grilling cucumber makes it smoky and juicy. A zingy preserved lemon dressing, sweet roasted peppers and some salty feta rounds it all out. Jordon x
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Drain the chickpeas and put them onto a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, add the ras el hanout and a big pinch of salt and mix.
Place into the oven for about 25 mins until golden and crunchy. You could make double the amount of these just to snack on.
If you’re using the little Lebanese cucumbers, you don’t need to peel them. For supermarket ones, the skin can be a bit thick so go ahead and peel them.
Slice the cucumbers in half lengthways. If using regular cucumbers, also halve them widthways. Grab a teaspoon and use it to scrape out the seeds from the middle.
Put the cucumbers into a bowl and rub all over with a tsp of salt and set aside for 20 mins. The salt will season the cucumbers but also pull out some of the moisture.

Meanwhile, finely chop the preserved lemon and the coriander and add them to a small bowl along with the zest and juice of 1 lemon, a tbsp of the preserved lemon brine, 2 tbsp of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Mix.
Heat a griddle pan until it's really hot. Drain the liquid from the bowl of cucumbers, then place them cut-side down onto a sheet of kitchen paper to dry off any excess moisture.
Place the cucumbers cut-side down into the pan. Leave them for 3 or 4 mins to get some good colour and then flip and repeat on the other side.

Remove the cucumbers from the pan onto your chopping board and cut into roughly 2-inch pieces. Drain the peppers and cut them into roughly the same size pieces as the cucumber. Add both to a bowl, pour over the dressing, and mix well.
Spoon the cucumber and peppers onto a plate, sprinkle over the crispy chickpeas, and crumble over the feta. Season with more salt, lemon juice, and chilli to taste.

name: Grilled Curry Cod Paratha Wraps
description: This Indian-inspired recipe is an excellent way to add some excitement to some frozen parathas. It's light, bright, and super flavoursome.
instructions: Preheat the grill to high. Cut the cod into 4-5 cm chunks and toss with 3 tsp salt in a large mixing bowl. Tip in the curry paste and 5 tbsp yoghurt. Zest and juice a lemon into the bowl and give the lot a really good mix. Cover and pop into the fridge for 20 mins.

Chunk up the courgettes and toss with olive oil and salt. Chuck onto a tray and slide under the grill for 10-15 mins, turning regularly, until charred and gnarly. Meanwhile, peel the garlic cloves and roughly chop 2 green chillies.

To make the chutney, put the peanuts, cumin, garlic, chopped green chilli and 4 tbsp oil into a blender. Tear in the coriander and juice in a lemon. Blend into a smooth green chutney, season to taste and add more lemon if you want to!

Thread the cod onto 4 skewers, making sure the fish chunks have plenty of marinade on them. Pull the courgettes out from the grill and rest the cod skewers on top of the veg. Slide back under the grill for 4-5 mins.
Meanwhile, cook the paratha following pack instructions. Thinly slice the remaining green chilli and red onion.

Once everything is ready, divide the paratha between plates. Add a swoosh of the remaining yoghurt and top with courgettes and a couple of skewers. Drizzle over the coriander chutney, sliced chillies, red onions and pomegranate seeds. Serve with extra lemon.

name: Grilled Fish Tacos with Salsa
description: You can use whatever fish you like for these tacos. Just make sure it is nice and flaky. The grilled pepper salsa is an absolute must.
instructions: Preheat the grill to maximum.

Place the peppers and chillies onto a baking tray. Slide under the grill for 15 minutes, turning every 5 minutes until they are evenly blackened. Add to a bowl and cover (monitor the veg as grill heats vary). Leave the veg to steam for 10 minutes.

Scoop the avocados into a food processor with the coriander stalks. Add a big pinch of ground cumin, sour cream/Greek yoghurt, add the zest and juice of 1 lime. Blitz until smooth, season to taste, set aside.
Fish marinade time. Crush the garlic into a bowl. Add the remaining ground cumin and a large crack of black pepper. Pour in a good glug of olive oil, mix.
Lay the fish fillets on a baking tray. Season with salt, then evenly spoon the marinade over. Set aside.

Back to the peppers and chillies. If they are too hot to handle, leave to cool for longer. Take them out of the bowl keeping the pepper juices. Remove the seeds and peel away any blackened skin. Roughly chop the flesh and return to the bowl.
Finely chop the onion, roughly chop the coriander leaves. Add to the peppers and chillies with the remaining lime juice. Mix and season to taste.
Slide the fish under the grill for 6-8 minutes until it is just cooked through and flakes into large pieces. Add to a bowl and scrape over all the spiced oil.
Shred the red cabbage and heat the tacos or tortillas. Bring everything outside for people to help themselves.

name: Grilled Halloumi Spring Salad
description: This fresh salad is dressed in zingy ginger, chilli and lemon dressing. Plenty of parsley and mint for freshness and even some giant crunchy croutons, too.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Tear or cut the ciabatta into large 2cm chunks. Place on a baking tray and drizzle with 3 tbsp of olive oil. Toss together until nice and coated. Season with salt and pepper, then bake until crunchy, 15-20 mins.

For the dressing, zest both lemons and squeeze the juice into a large mixing bowl. Trim and finely chop the chilli. Peel and grate the ginger into the bowl, then, stir the lemon zest in along with 60ml of olive oil, season with salt and some sugar, if needed.

Trim and thinly slice the radishes. If you have a mandoline, this is the time to use it. If not, a sharp knife will do. Add them into the dressing. Pick the mint and parsley leaves – if you love a parsley kick, finely slice your parsley stalks. Trim the romaine lettuce hearts and separate the leaves, halving or quartering any large ones. Add the romaine and some of the herbs to the dressing, reserving a few herbs for garnish. Don’t toss anything yet!
Add the peas into a microwave-safe bowl, and microwave until defrosted. Drain the excess water out and add the peas to the salad bowl. Season the yoghurt with some salt and pepper and mix together.
Slice each halloumi block into six even-sized slabs. Heat a large frying pan with a drizzle of olive oil on medium heat. Once hot, add the halloumi and cook on both sides until golden, 3-5 mins.
Add the croutons to the bowl with the dressing and mix. Taste and season, if needed.
Tip onto a platter or plates, top with the halloumi, finish with the yoghurt and any reserved mint or parsley leaves along with a big crack of black pepper and some olive oil.

name: Grilled Halloumi by Bubala
description: Helen Graham from Bubala joins us in the MOB studio to cook her phenomenal grilled halloumi.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Place the nigella seeds, coriander seeds, pepper and urfa chilli flakes in a spice grinder or pestle and mortar and blitz or crush to a fine powder. Stir the spices through the honey and set aside.

Halve each block of halloumi so you're left with 4 thick pieces. Heat a dash of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat, then pan fry for 3-5 minutes on each side until golden and crisp. Transfer to the oven to heat through for 5 minutes. By this point, it should be gooey.
To serve, place a slice of halloumi on each plate and season with a little lemon juice and zest. Drizzle over the spiced honey and serve immediately.

name: Grilled Lamb Flatbreads With Pink Pickled Onions
description: Tender leftover lamb bolognese thrown onto a flatbread with some quick pickled onions. Easy.
keywords: Grilled Lamb Flatbreads With Pink Pickled Onions
Grilled Lamb Flatbreads With Pink Pickled Onions recipe
instructions: Start by making the pickles. Finely slice the onions and jalapeño and get them into a heatproof bowl. Add the vinegar, sugar and water to a small saucepan and bring to a boil. Once hot, pour over the onions and chillies. Leave to cool at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Stick the flatbreads onto a lined baking tray and top with the leftover bolognese. Slide into the oven for 15 mins.
Remove from the oven and top with picked mint leaves, crumbled feta, a dollop of yoghurt and a big handful of your pickles.

name: Grilled Lemony Garlic Chicken & Maroulosalata
description: Maroulosalata is the underdog of Greek salads. Maroulo translates to lettuce and salata is salad, making this a lettuce salad. Loads of dill and mint tossed with romaine, spring onions and feta for a flavour-packed, low-lift dinner, topped with lemony and oregano chicken you can't beat.
keywords: Grilled Lemon & Garlic Chicken with Maroulosalata
Grilled Lemon & Garlic Chicken with Maroulosalata recipe
instructions: Trim the fat from the chicken, then dice into chunky pieces. Add to a bowl with the olive oil, then zest and juice the lemon over the top. Add the oregano, cumin and garlic powder, season with salt and black pepper and mix to coat. Cover the bowl and pop it in the fridge for 30 mins, if you have time.

In the meantime, halve the cucumber lengthways, then scoop out the seeds with a teaspoon and discard before finely slicing. Finely chop the dill and mint, then slice the romaine and spring onions. Zest and juice the lemon into a large bowl and add the olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper, then whisk to emulsify.

Heat the grill to high. Spread the chicken out on a baking tray in a single layer and grill for 20 mins, turning halfway, until charred at the edges and cooked through. Add the salad ingredients to the dressing bowl, crumble in the feta and toss to mix. Serve up with a wedge of lemon, if you like.

name: Grilled Mackerel Flatbreads with Dill Mustard Slaw
description: Locally caught mackerel, butterflied, salted and grilled over a hot BBQ. The crispy grilled fish is served with homemade flatbreads, also cooked on the barbie.
instructions: Butterfly the mackerel. Sprinkle the flesh of the mackerel with salt and set aside for 40 mins. This will firm it up and make it much easier to grill.
Start by making the flatbread dough. Combine the flour, baking powder, yoghurt and oil with 1 tsp salt and 2 tbsp water, and bring together into a rough dough.
Tip onto a lightly floured surface and knead for a few minutes until slightly smooth, then divide into four pieces and roll each into a ball. Set aside, covered.

Make the slaw by thinly slicing the cabbage, onion and carrots on a mandolin (or with a sharp knife) and mixing with finely chopped parsley, dill, the vinegar, and mustard. Season and add a squeeze of lemon if needed.
When ready to cook, roll the dough balls out on a lightly floured surface into rough circles, then grill for 1-2 mins on each side until golden and slightly charred. Set aside.
Grill the mackerel skin-side down until cooked through, you shouldn’t need to turn them at all.
Top each flatbread with a spoonful of sour cream, a handful of the slaw, crispy mackerel fillets and finish with olive oil, salt and lemon juice.

name: Grilled Mackerel with Ratatouille
description: This Mediterranean classic is the perfect summer recipe utilising a bounty of vegetables. It's great eaten warm once cooked, but even better eaten the next day when the flavours have had a chance to deepen and get to know each other.
instructions: Cut the aubergine into large-ish bite sized pieces, then the courgette into 1cm coins. Peel, halve and thinly slice the onion, then deseed and cut the peppers into 1cm strips. Peel and thinly slice the garlic cloves, then cut the tomatoes into quarters.

Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large deep frying pan over a high heat and tip in the aubergine and courgette. Fry for 6-8 mins, tossing regularly until golden and caramelised. Use a slotted spoon to scoop out onto a plate. You can do this in batches if your pan isn’t quite big enough.

Pour another generous glug of olive oil into the pan and add the onion, pepper pieces, garlic and thyme. Add in a big pinch of salt, reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring regularly for 8-10 mins until the onions have started to colour and soften.

Add the aubergines and courgettes back into the pan along with the quartered tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10-12 mins until the tomatoes have begun to soften. Remove from the heat, season with salt and black pepper and the sherry vinegar.

Heat the grill to high. Lightly crush the fennel seeds in a pestle and mortar, then sprinkle on both sides of the mackerel fillets. Put onto a baking sheet, skin side up and drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt. Put under the grill for 2-3 mins until the skin has crisped and caramelised. No need to flip the fish – the hot grill & tray will have just cooked the fish underneath the crispy skin.
Heat another generous glug of olive oil in a small frying pan over a high heat. Add the basil leaves and cook and stir for a minute until shrivelled and crisped slightly.
Spoon the ratatouille between plates, top each with a mackerel fillet and some of the basil and its fragrant oil.

name: Grilled Nectarine & Courgette Chickpea Salad
description: A fresh, summery salad with a zingy mint dressing that’s on the table for 10 minutes. Perfect as a side or light meal.
instructions: Slice the courgettes into medium chunks at an angle. Cut the nectarine into segments. Lightly brush courgettes and nectarine with olive oil and grill them on a grill pan on a medium heat until golden brown and charred on both sides.
Meanwhile, whisk together all the dressing ingredients, saving a few mint leaves for garnish. Season to taste.
Divide the chickpeas in serving bowls along with the charred courgettes and nectarines, drizzle with the dressing and finish with more mint leaves. Season to taste with salt if needed.

name: Grilled Orange & Za'atar Lamb Chops
description: Charred chilli and za’atar chops with a zesty, minty yoghurt sauce. A flavour combo from heaven. The tastiest chop you’ll ever chomp on.
instructions: Place your lamb chops, 4 tbsp yoghurt, za’atar, chilli powder, and the zest of half an orange into a bowl. Grate in your garlic, salt, pepper and add a drizzle of olive oil then mix together until evenly coated. Cover and leave to marinate for 30 minutes.

Time for the sauce. Chop your mint (saving some for garnish) and add into another bowl along with the rest of your yoghurt, the zest of half an orange and a squeeze of orange and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper, and drizzle with olive oil. Stir together and leave in the fridge until ready to use.
Once your chops are ready, get them on a high heat griddle pan and cook for about 5 minutes on each side until cooked through and nicely charred.
Stack them on a plate, drizzle your zesty yoghurt over the top and scatter over the leftover mint, a grating of orange zest and a pinch of chilli powder. Tuck in!

name: Grilled Peach Sally
description: Grilled peach is something the MOB need in their lives. It gets all sticky and charred. Perfect in this crunchy, fresh salad.
instructions: Cut and pit your peaches whilst you heat up a griddle pan.
Add your peaches and cook until nice and charred. Remove from the pan.
Add sliced Halloumi, cook until charred.
Crush your hazelnuts. Add hazelnuts and flaked almonds to a pan until lightly toasted. Add honey to the pan along with a generous handful of thyme. Cook for a minute more.
Finely chop your celery and your green apples.
Dressing time. Mix a cup of olive oil, Dijon, a pinch of salt, the juice of half a lemon and a good grinding of pepper.
Chop up your lettuce, assemble all the ingredients and pour over your dressing. Mix and enjoy!

name: Grilled Peach Salsa with Smoky Lime Tortilla Chips
description: Homemade tortilla chips are so easy to make. They're the perfect accompaniment to this summery salsa, which is the ideal combo of savoury, sweet and spicy.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C / fan 180°C.
Place the smoked paprika, garlic powder and ancho chilli flakes in a large bowl with 50ml vegetable oil and a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Mix well to combine.
Cut the tortilla wraps into small triangles. Add them to the bowl and toss to coat.
Arrange the seasoned tortilla triangles in a single layer on two large baking trays. Bake for 10 mins.
Remove from the oven and add the zest of the limes. Toss to coat then bake for a further 10 mins, or until nice and crisp. Leave to cool on the tray.
Meanwhile, quarter and stone your peaches. Place in a bowl and toss with olive oil.
Set a griddle pan over a medium-high heat. Griddle the peaches until charred on both sides. Transfer to a plate to cool.
Deseed and finely the tomatoes. Finely chop the red onion. Deseed and finely chop the jalapeño. Juice the limes. Finely chop the peaches.
Transfer everything to a bowl, season with salt and pepper and mix to combine.
To serve, top the salsa with a drizzle of olive oil then tuck in with your tortilla chips and enjoy!

name: Grilled Peach and Burrata Salad
description: One for the summer days. When you char peach slices on a griddle pan, the juices caramelise and they get even sweeter. Perfect with creamy burrata & pistachios.
instructions: Toast the pistachios in a pan with no oil until nice and golden, set to the side to cool.
Lightly oil a griddle pan. While you are waiting for the pan to get hot, halve your peaches, deseed and cut into slices.

Griddle the peach slices until nice marks appear, turn half way. You can use a heavy pan or baking tray as a weight on top of the peaches to encourage the marks. When all the peach slices are griddled, put to the side on a plate.
For the sweet herb drizzle, whizz up the basil with the honey, a generous pinch of salt, 2 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp water.
Roughly chop the pistachios and drain the burrata balls from the juice.
Plate up, starting with a handful of rocket, then place the slices of peaches, tear the burrata, drizzle on that herb dressing, sprinkle the toasted pistachios and season with salt and pepper. Enjoy!

name: Grilled Pineapple Pavlova
description: A classic pavlova given a fresh pineapple twist. It’s sure to become a household favourite. Plus it’s dairy free.
instructions: Heat the oven to 150°C. Line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Separate your egg whites into a clean bowl - any grease in the bowl will stop the whites from properly whipping up. (You can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise or dressing)

Starting on a slow speed, use an electric whisk to whip up the egg whites. Once they begin to turn white and frothy increase the whisk speed and continue whisking until they just hold their shape. When the egg whites get to this stage, gradually add the sugar, 1 tbsp at a time. Whisk for a few seconds in between until you have a glossy, shiny meringue with peaks that hold.

Once all the sugar has been added, spoon in the cornflour, white wine vinegar/lemon juice and vanilla extract and briefly whisk to combine. Using a metal spoon dollop your meringue mixture onto the middle of your lined baking tray. Use the spoon to spread the meringue into a rough circle around the size of a pasta bowl, making a divet in the middle of the pavlova where your yoghurt will sit.

Bake for 10 minutes, then turn the oven temperature down to 120°C/248°F and continue to cook for 2-2 1/2 hours until the pavlova is cooked through. You will know it is done as it will come away from the paper easily. Once cooked, leave to cool.

Pour the pineapple juice into a small saucepan over a high heat. Leave to bubble for 20-25 minutes until the liquid has evaporated and the juice has reduced to a syrup that coats the back of your spoon. Keep a close eye on the juice for the final 5 minutes, as it will look like it’s not doing anything and will go from watery to syrupy in a matter of seconds
Meanwhile, heat a grill or griddle pan to maximum.

Cut the skin off the pineapple, cut into quarters lengthways then slice into wedges. If grilling, place the pineapple on a baking tray and slide under the grill for around 12 minutes, turning the tray around halfway, until the pineapple is nicely charred. If on a griddle, fry for around 3 minutes on each side.
All of these components can be done in advance (even the day before). Assemble just before you eat.
Spoon on the coconut yoghurt then top with the pieces of grilled pineapple, drizzle over the pineapple syrup and tear over the mint leaves. Then tuck into this naughty little pavlova.

name: Grilled Pork Fillet with Ginger Sauce and Garlic Butter Rice
description: In Partnership With Aldi. #ad. This pork fillet gets the star treatment with zingy ginger sauce and garlic butter rice. Feels fancy, but it’s way easier than it looks.
keywords: Grilled Pork with Ginger Sauce and Garlic Butter Rice recipe
Grilled Pork with Ginger Sauce and Garlic Butter Rice
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Rub oil over the pork fillet and season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat a griddle pan or frying pan over high heat for a couple of minutes, then sear the fillet on all sides for 1–2 mins until golden. Transfer the pork to baking tray and keep the pan to cook the veg later on.
In a small bowl, mix the water and honey together, then brush it all over the pork. Cook in the oven for 13–15 mins.

While the pork’s cooking, get on with the ginger sauce.Finely chop the spring onion and red chilli, then set aside.Zest and juice the lemon. Roughly chop the ginger and onion, then chuck them into a blender with everything else for the sauce (except the sesame seeds, spring onion and chilli). Blitz until it’s slightly chunky – you don’t want a purée. Tip it into a bowl and top with the chopped chilli, spring onion and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

Now, for the veg. Slice the mushrooms in half and remove the woody ends from the asparagus. Return the pan you used for pork to the heat. Once hot, add the asparagus and mushrooms and cook for 2 mins on each side until lightly charred. Transfer to a bowl, drizzle over the olive oil and a pinch of salt, and give it all a toss.

Finally, make the rice. Chop the chives and set aside. Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat. Add the garlic, a pinch of salt, and sugar, and fry gently for 3–5 mins until golden and fragrant. Heat the rice following pack instructions. Stir the garlic butter and chopped chives through the rice until it’s glossy and fragrant.
Take your pork out of the oven once cooked and let it rest for at least 5 mins.
To serve, spoon the rice onto plates. Once it's nice and rested, slice the pork into 2cm slices and lay over the rice with the asparagus and mushrooms. Finish with a drizzle of the ginger sauce.

name: Grilled Prawns with Avocado Salad
description: Pop another prawn on the barbie and serve it up with a fresh and creamy avocado salad.
keywords: Grilled Prawns with Avocado Salad recipe
instructions: Pile coals over to one side of your BBQ to create a hot, direct cooking side, and a warm, indirect cooking side.
Add the juice of one of the lemons to a bowl. Cut the shallots into rings and add to the lemon juice. Add a pinch of salt and set aside for 10 mins.
Chunk up the avocados and slice the cucumbers and lettuce. Add everything to a bowl along with the rocket.
Tip the yoghurt into a blender with half of the herbs. Finely grate the garlic into the blender, then add the juice of the remaining lemon and season well with salt and pepper. Blend until smooth.

Toss the prawns with oil and season with salt. Pile onto the grill and leave to caramelise for 3-4 mins. Turn over and cook for another couple of mins before whipping off the grill when bright pink and crispy.
Pour the yoghurt dressing over the chopped veggies, add the lemony shallot rings and toss together. Pile onto a platter and top with the grilled prawns.

name: Grilled Short Rib Lettuce Cups
description: Juicy beef short rib in a spicy, citrussy, soy dressing. These lettuce cups are a great way to see how delicious beef can be.
instructions: Grab your short ribs and look for any silver skin. It’ll look like shiny, whitish, silver strips of meat against the red rib meat.
