Slip your knife under these and trim them away, they’ll be super tough and we don’t want that. Once the short ribs are clean of any silver skin, they’re ready to marinade.

In a large bowl, combine the soy, brown sugar and the zest and juice of two limes. Dice the ginger and two of the chillies and add to the marinade. Finely grate the garlic in and stir to combine. Add the ribs and toss to coat. Marinade for at least 30 mins and up to 6 hours.

Fire up your BBQ and let the coals get really hot. While they’re heating up, pull the short ribs out of the marinade, leaving a good amount of marinade on the ribs. Add them, bone side up to begin with and cook, turning regularly, over that ripping hot heat, until they are charred all over. I like to dab on marinade as they cook, to lacquer on and char.
You want to cook these for about 10-12 mins, or until medium. If you’ve got a thermometer, stick it into the thickest part of the rib and when it reads 50°C, pull the meat off to rest for 15 mins.

Heat the rice according to the package instructions. Separate the gem lettuce into separate leaves, cut the cucumber into slices, pick the herbs into little stalks and thinly slice the spring onions. Arrange on a platter with the peanuts and kimchi.
Tip the rice onto a warm plate. Carve the rested short ribs off of the bones and into thin slices. You want to carve against the grain here – very important!
Serve over the rice with extra sliced chillies, lime and the platter of veggies to make wraps. Get stuck in.

name: Grilled Sticky BBQ Chicken
description: It's not a barbecue until someone burns a bit of chicken. Avoid any disasters with this foolproof barbecue chicken recipe. The sweet and sticky glaze is an elite addition.
instructions: Pile coals over to one side of your BBQ to create a hot, direct cooking side, and a warm, indirect cooking side.

Start off by making the rub. Toast the fennel, black pepper and cumin seeds in a dry pan over the hot side of your BBQ. Once fragrant, tip into a pestle and mortar and coarsely grind. Add the oregano, paprika and garlic powder. Mix together.

Season the chicken well with salt and toss with the mustard. Lay out on a tray and season generously with the spice rub. Grill over the hot side of the BBQ for 9-10 mins, turning regularly until charred and crispy. It won’t be cooked through just yet, so move it to the indirect side of the BBQ and add the lid. Allow to cook gently for 35-40 mins with the lid on.

Once the chicken has had 35 mins or so, remove the lid and check the texture. It should be pulling away from the bone, super smoky and tender. Mix the ingredients for the glaze in a small bowl and brush over the chicken pieces. Return the lid and allow the glaze to bake onto the chicken for a few minutes.
Serve with coleslaw, fresh corn, rice and lemon wedges.

name: Grilled Tomato & Chilli Noodles
description: The easiest, most delicious vegan dinner that comes together in just 25 minutes. It’s great eaten fresh and hot for dinner. Or, make it ahead and eat it cold for lunch the next day.
instructions: Heat the grill to high.
Place the tomatoes onto a baking tray. (If making ahead for lunch, simply halve the tomatoes and keep them raw.)
Pick the coriander and mint leaves, discarding the mint stems. Trim and thinly slice the spring onion and coriander stalks. Place all the herbs and spring onion into a bowl of ice water.
Cook the noodles in a large pan of boiling water following packet instructions. Once cooked, drain the water and give the noodles a good wash in cold water.
Slide the tomatoes under the grill and cook for 6-10 mins until softened and starting to char. (Skip this step if making ahead for lunch.)

Combine the vinaigrette ingredients in a medium bowl. Tip in the charred cherry tomatoes and mix to combine. Taste and season with some salt, if needed. (If making ahead, don’t tip the tomatoes into the dressing.)
Drain the herb mixture and add to a small bowl along with the sesame oil and seeds. Toss to combine.

To serve, divide the noodles between bowls. Top with the dressed tomatoes and herb salad. If making ahead, share the dressing into boxes. Layer on top the noodles, halved raw tomatoes and herb salad. Refrigerate until ready to eat and shake to dress the noodles.

name: Grilled Zhoug Chicken & Tomatoes
description: If you haven't made zhoug before, this is your sign to start. Punchy, herby and just the right amount of spicy, here it doubles up as a marinade for grilled chicken thighs and a drizzle over blistered vine tomatoes. Proper good.
instructions: Start with the zhoug. Lightly crack the cardamom pods using the back of your knife. Add the coriander seeds, cumin seeds and cracked cardamom to a small frying pan over a medium heat and toast for 2-3 mins until fragrant. Pick out the cardamom seeds and discard the pods.

Tip the toasted spices into a food processor and blitz until they've broken down slightly, you don't want a fine powder. Trim the chillies and add to the processor along with the garlic and all the fresh coriander, stems and all. Blitz until broken down, then gradually pour in the olive oil until emulsified. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon, taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Heat the grill to medium-high. Spoon half the zhoug into a bowl with the yoghurt and stir together. Add the chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Line a baking tray with foil and drizzle with a little olive oil. Arrange the chicken on one side. Halve the tomatoes and place cut-side up on the other side. Season everything with salt and slide under the grill for 15-20 mins, until the chicken is cooked through and starting to char and the tomatoes have softened and blistered. If things are colouring too quickly, drop the tray down a level or reduce the grill heat.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Divide between plates and top with the chicken and tomatoes, then drizzle over the remaining zhoug and a dollop of yoghurt.

name: Gringas
description: Crispy pan-fried flour tortillas filled with melted cheese. This recipe also uses leftover al pastor pork meat from our al pastor pork recipe, but you can skip this if you don't have any or are short on time.
instructions: Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the uncooked al pastor pork meat and fry until cooked through and caramelised (about 3 mins each side for thin slices, but don't overcrowd the pan). Remove the meat from the pan, leave it for 5 mins to rest then chop it into small pieces and se aside. If you don't have any al pastor pork meat, skip this step.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and fresh coriander and set aside.
To make the gringas, heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add one or two flour tortillas to the dry pan and cook for 30 secs over a medium heat to warm through.

Add a handful (about 40g) of grated mozzarella to each tortilla. Once the cheese has melted, add a handful (about 40g) of cooked al pastor pork and a sprinkling of coriander then fold the tortilla over so you have a half moon. Cook for a couple of mins until the tortilla is golden brown on the bottom, then flip the whole thing over and brown the other side. Remove the gringas from the pan and wrap in a tea towel to keep warm or, if possible, serve immediately. Repeat for all the tortillas.
Serve the gringas with the chopped onion, more fresh coriander and salsa verde (or another salsa of your choice).

name: Guacamole
description: The word guacamole comes from the union of two Nahuatl words: ahuacatl (avocado) and molli (sauce). This sauce is the most loved by all Mexicans. It is prepared in different ways, but the traditional ingredients are usually the same: good avocados, tomatoes and onions. Perfect to snack on with some totopos (tortilla chips) and beers or to add to tacos.
instructions: Finely dice the tomato, onion, fresh jalapeño and coriander. Make sure your avocados are perfectly ripe.
Slice open the avocados, carefully remove the pit and use a spoon to scoop out the flesh. Add the flesh to a bowl and mash it using a potato masher (don’t mash it too much – some texture is good).

Add the diced tomato, onion, chopped jalapeño and coriander and squeeze in the juice of the lime (don’t add too much lime juice – remember this is an avocado sauce, so as long as you use perfect and creamy avocados, the salsa will be delicious). Season with salt to taste and mix well.
Serve with totopos (tortilla chips).

name: Guinness Can Chicken
description: Gareth Thomas cooks up a stunning dish with us. Roasting a chicken on a Guinness can gives a beautiful savoury flavour. Packed with herbs and served with slaw.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C/374°F.

Open up the can of Guinness and pour out roughly half the can to save for later. Stand the chicken up and push the can into the cavity, standing the chicken up vertically. Place the chicken onto a baking tray.
In a bowl combine your dried herbs; oregano, basil, rosemary, thyme, along with the chilli flakes, garlic powder, light brown sugar and a tsp of salt
Rub the tomato purée onto the chicken, making sure you fully cover the surface.
Press your dry rub onto the chicken. Firmly push it onto the skin so most of it sticks on – this will form a thick crispy crust on your chicken.
Pop it in the oven for an hour.
Meanwhile make the slaw. Finely shred the fennel, apple and cabbage. Finely chop your parsley.
In a small bowl mix the mustard, mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, and sugar with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Dilute it with 2 tbsp of water and massage it into your chopped veg.
When the chicken is done, allow it to rest for 5 minutes before carefully removing it from the tin.

Measure about 350ml of liquid from the chicken-y Guinness can, making up the difference with the Guinness saved earlier if it is less than this. Pour any juices in the baking pan into a saucepan along with the Guinness.

Add in your chicken stock, light brown sugar, tomato purée and the apple cider vinegar. Heat on a medium heat until it starts to bubble. Mix a tbsp of flour with 2 tbsps of water and add this in, whisking vigorously as you pour. Continue cooking for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Carve your chicken and serve it with the Guinness gravy, fresh slaw and chips.

name: Guinness and Mushroom Stew
description: The Original Flava lads make a banging Jamaican mushroom stew for the MOB. Packed with warming allspice, fruity scotch bonnet and smooth Guinness.
instructions: Start by prepping your veg. Dice your onion and your red, yellow and green peppers. Slice your spring onions. Finely chop your garlic and scotch bonnet.

Tip your mushrooms into a large bowl and add your browning (or soy sauce if using) along with your allspice. Season generously with salt and pepper. Tip in all of your chopped veg and a few sprigs of thyme, then stir to combine. Pop in the fridge to marinate overnight, or for a couple of hours.
Heat a glug of oil in a large saute pan. Tip your veg mixture in and fry for 10 mins until all the veg has softened and is starting to reduce and caramelise slightly.
Pour in your veg stock gradually and bring to a simmer. Sprinkle on your cornflour and stir to mix in - this should make your sauce thick and glossy.
Time to pour your Guinness into the pan. Let it simmer for 5 mins until you have a glossy sauce.
Serve over rice and peas alongside fried plantain. Enjoy!

name: Guinness-Glazed Pork Belly Buns
description: Who knew Guinness could be used to create a banging bao bun? We didn’t, until we tried it, and it’s fabulous. This paste packs a serious punch.
instructions: Separate the spring onions into white and green parts. Finely slice both and set aside. Slice half of the chilli and split the other half lengthways. Finely chop the ginger and garlic.

Cut the pork belly into 3cm chunks and pop into a large saucepan. Cover with cold water and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 4-5 mins, skimming off any scum that floats to the surface. Drain the pork and rinse out the pan.
Melt the brown sugar in the clean pan over a medium heat. Add the pork and roll around in the caramel.
Add the star anise, the whites of the spring onion, the ginger and garlic and the halved chilli. Cook for 2-3 mins until fragrant.
Now add the soy, wine and Guinness Paste.
Cover with fresh water (approx 600ml) and braise for 30-40 mins until the pork is just tender.
Remove the pork and reduce the liquid to a sweet sticky glaze. Add the pork back to the pan and toss to coat in the Guinness glaze.
Finely slice the cabbage and cucumber.
Steam your bao buns, split in half and stuff full of cabbage, cucumbers, juicy pork belly and top with spring onion and fresh red chilli.
Get stuck in.

name: Gunpowder Potatoes With Garlic Yoghurt Aioli
description: Level up your potatoes with this super spice mix, quick pickled onions and a crunchy almond topping, all balanced out with a  cooling yoghurt aioli. They make a perfect side dish or add some roasted veggies, beans or tofu to turn it into a complete meal.
keywords: Gunpowder Potatoes With Garlic Yoghurt Aioli
Gunpowder Potatoes With Garlic Yoghurt Aioli recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and put a large baking tray inside to heat up.

To make the pickled onions, finely slice the red onion and place into a jar. Heat the apple cider vinegar, water, salt and sugar in a small saucepan. When the sugar and salt have dissolved, pour the mixture over the onions and set aside to pickle.

Boil the potatoes for 6-8 mins in well salted water, until you can pierce them with a fork. They should be soft but not fully cooked, as they will be finished in the oven. When cooked, drain and set aside to steam dry.

Crush the cumin, coriander and fennel seeds with the peppercorns and mix with the garam masala, salt, chilli powder, chilli flakes if using, and olive oil in a large bowl that will fit the potatoes in. Mince the ginger and the garlic and add this to the spice mix before adding the potatoes in and giving it a good mix. Make sure all of the potatoes are well covered, then add them to the hot baking tray.
Add oil to your baking tray and roast the potatoes for 25-30 mins, tossing once, until very crispy.
While the potatoes are roasting, make the aioli. Mince the garlic clove and mix with the yoghurt, mayonnaise and a good squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt. Whisk to combine.
Finely slice the chilli.
To serve, spread the aioli onto a large plate and top with the potatoes, pickled onions, chilli, toasted almonds and parsley.

name: Gyoza Peanut Noodles
description: Delicious gyoza, soft egg noodles and a thick peanut sauce, with charred veg and lime-pickled spring onions to keep it fresh. Fakeaway sorted in 25 mins.
instructions: Finely slice your peppers, ginger, half the spring onions and carrots. Add to a wok with a splash of vegetable oil. Cook on high so they char and soften.

While they are cooking, finely slice the rest of the spring onions and add to a bowl. Squeeze in the juice of a lime, add a pinch of salt and mix everything together. (This will lightly pickle the onions, making them less intense).
In another bowl, add peanut butter, soy sauce and water. Mix everything together until you have a thick sauce.
Cook 300g of egg noodles and gyozas (follow pack instructions).

Once the noodles are ready, add them to the wok. Stir everything together. Add your pickled spring onions and peanut sauce. Add a handful of coriander. Toss everything together and remove from the heat.
Serve the peanut noodles, with the gyozas, onto plates. Garnish with coriander and spring onions. Enjoy!

name: Gyros with Chimichurri Yoghurt Sauce
description: I've made a Greek style gyro with Mexican flavours and it really works. Chimichurri flavoured yogurt and spicy lime sunflower seeds wrapped up with vegan kebab.
instructions: Start by pickling your onions, they will be ready by the time the rest of your ingredients are. Finely slice the onion. Add 120ml of water, 120ml apple cider vinegar, 1 ½ tsp sugar, 1 ½ tsp sea salt, and ¼ tsp red pepper flakes to a small saucepan.

Soak the sunflower seeds in the lime juice and set aside for 5 mins to absorb. Add 1 chili, salt and paprika and mix. Add a little oil to a pan and fry on medium for a few minutes until crispy but take care not to burn.
In a blender, add in your yoghurt, coriander, 1 red chilli and the juice of half a lime. Blend until smooth and season with plenty of salt and pepper.
To cook the kebab protein, simply add a little oil to a frying pan and sauté until the sides start to crisp up.
Slice the cucumber and remaining chilli and chop up some coriander for garnishing.
To assemble, warm through your wraps then layer on the yoghurt, the kebab protein and the cucumber. Sprinkle over some sunflower seeds and finish with the pickled onion, sliced chilli, and coriander.

name: Hackney Buns
description: Move over Chelsea buns. Our version is the Hackney bun, named for its East London roots and Guinness-soaked fruit.
instructions: Mix together the sultanas and Guinness in a bowl and pop in the fridge to soak overnight. Drain, set the fruit aside and reserve the syrup.
Roughly cut the butter into cubes. Heat the milk and butter in a saucepan over a medium heat, swirling until the butter is melted – don’t let it boil. Remove from the heat and leave to cool.
In a bowl, whisk together the flour, salt and sugar, mixing thoroughly to distribute the salt.
Whisk the yeast into the cooled butter mixture, then whisk in all the egg yolks until you have an even mixture.

Pour the yolk and butter mixture into the flour mix and use your hands to lightly bring it all together until you have a dough that’s sticky but not sloppy (you may need to add a little more water or flour to achieve this consistency).

Turn the dough out onto a unfloured surface and knead for 20 mins until feeling smooth and bouncy. You may need to use a bench scraper at the beginning if the dough sticks to the surface. Tip the kneaded dough into a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a tea towel then leave in a warm place to rise for 1 hour.
While the dough rises, line a 25cm square baking tin with baking parchment.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface. Use a rolling pin to roll it out evenly into a rectangular shape until it’s about 25 x 35cm and 1cm thick.
For the topping: Melt the butter in a pot over a low heat. Brush the pastry all over with most of the melted butter, then sprinkle all over with the dark brown sugar and drained soaked sultanas.

Roll the whole thing up lengthways like a big Swiss roll – the tighter the better! Brush some of the remaining butter around the outside, then cut into 12 slices approximately 2cm wide, using a small serrated knife. Place the buns in rows in your prepared tin, leaving small gaps to allow for a further rise. Leave in a warm place to prove for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 200˚C fan. Once proved, bake for 20–30 mins, or until golden brown.

Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tin for 10 mins before transferring to a wire rack. When cooling, brush all over with the leftover Guinness syrup and sprinkle with the remaining caster sugar.

name: Hainanese Spatchcock Chicken
description: If you’ve tried this Hainanese ginger spring onion sauce, you already know why I have made an entire roast chicken recipe around it.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper. Slice the shallots in half and place them on the tray. In a small bowl, mix the dark soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar and salt to make the marinade.

To spatchcock the chicken, flip the chicken over breast-side down. Use strong kitchen scissors to cut along both sides of the backbone and remove it. Place the backbone between the shallots, then lay the chicken on top, breast-side up. Brush the chicken all over with the marinade and roast for 45-50 mins, or until cooked through.
Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain. Crush the garlic and slice the ginger into 1cm pieces.

Heat a drizzle of sesame oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 min until fragrant. Stir in the rice and coat the grains in the oil until glossy. Pour in the water, add the sugar and salt, and bring to the boil. Reduce to the lowest heat, cover with a lid and cook undisturbed for 20 mins.

For the gravy, finely grate the ginger. Trim and finely slice the whites of the spring onions, setting the greens aside for the slaw. Add the grated ginger and spring onion whites to a bowl with the sesame oil, rice wine vinegar and sugar. Season with salt and set aside. Once the chicken is cooked, pour the roasting juices into the bowl and stir to combine.
For the slaw, thinly slice the reserved spring onion greens into long strips and place them in a bowl of ice water until they curl. Drain, then season with sesame oil and salt.

Before serving, carve the chicken and fluff the rice. Divide the rice between bowls and top with the chicken and spring onion slaw. Drizzle over the Hainanese gravy. Serve with chilli oil and lime wedges.

name: Hainanese e Olio Pasta
description: Aglio e olio with a twist. We've coated spaghetti in the ginger spring onion sauce that comes with Hainanese chicken. The result: Hainanese e olio pasta.
instructions: Finely slice all the spring onions, then roughly chop again into smaller pieces. Set aside, reserving ½ of the green bits in a separate bowl. Slice the ginger into 4 pieces around ½ cm thick, then cut into thin strips and finally dice into small pieces. Bring a medium-sized pan of salted water to the boil. Add the pasta and set a timer for 1 min less than pack instructions.

Add 4 tbsp olive oil to a medium-sized pan, coating the base of the pan entirely, then set the heat to medium-high. Add the ginger and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the spring onions and cook for 1 min or until soft and fragrant – don’t let them burn. Reduce the heat to the lowest setting and leave to simmer for 2 mins, then add the honey or sugar, soy sauce and a pinch of salt.

When the pasta is ready, use tongs to fish it out (allow the pasta water to cling to the spaghetti strands) and toss into the aromatic oil. Add 3-4 tbsp pasta water to loosen the pasta until it’s glossy.

Turn off the heat, then add a squeeze of lemon juice, the sesame oil, sesame seeds, chilli flakes, the reserved chopped green spring onions and some black pepper. Add a few more tbsp pasta water if the pasta is not looking glossy, then add the parmesan. Add more salt or lemon to taste. Plate with extra grated Parmesan and toasted sesame seeds.

name: Half Grilled Chicken with Burnt Chilli Hot Sauce
description: Halving your chicken is a quick and easy way to getting it cooked faster. Plus, it means more surface area for crispy skin. Always a win.
keywords: Half Grilled Chicken with Burnt Chilli Hot Sauce
Half Grilled Chicken with Burnt Chilli Hot Sauce recipe
instructions: We’re going to start by separately removing the two halves of the chicken and then removing the bones. Begin by removing the first two joints of the wing, the tip and the flat, leaving the drumette attached to the breast. Just slide through the cartilage with your knife. Remove the wishbone and then cut away the breast from the breast bone, keeping your knife snug to the bone. Draw your knife back to free up the leg, pop out the joint, and remove from the body (including the drumette) being careful to keep the skin between the breast and the leg attached. Lift away half of the chicken. Repeat with the other side.

To remove the leg bones, pop the chicken skin-side down onto your cutting board and use your knife to trace along the thigh and drum bones, exposing them from beneath the skin. Slide your knife underneath and cut them away from the flesh. Repeat with the other half. You now should have two halves of deboned chicken, with just the drumette (little wing) attached.

To make the brine, mix your cold water with fine salt. Stir until completely dissolved. Lower in the deboned chicken and set aside in the fridge for 2 hours. Whilst the chicken is brining, prepare your BBQ for grilling.Tip for scaling: For the brine your water quantity should be equal to the weight of the chicken, and the salt quantity should be 5% of that weight.

Once brined, remove the chicken and discard the brine. Pat the chicken very dry with paper towels and rub with olive oil. Grill over a medium heat (nothing too hot!), skin side down, for 12-13 mins or until very crispy. Flip and finish the meat side for 4-5 mins or until fully cooked, if you’ve got a thermometer, you’re looking for 68-69°C. Once cooked, remove from the heat and rest in a little olive oil.
Whilst the chicken rests, toss the spring onions with olive oil and grill until blackened and wilted.
Carve up the chicken into chunks and serve with the grilled onions, lemon juice, a big dollop of tahini and plenty of the chopped chilli hot sauce.

Mix the tahini and yoghurt in a bowl with finely grated garlic and lemon zest and juice. Season with salt and let the mixture down with water if it’s a little thick. You’re after a thick, spoonable texture.

Toss the chillies with a little oil. Pile onto a raging hot grill and cook until very charred. Once completely blackened, tip into a bowl and cover to steam through. Clean the chillies of their charred skins and deseed. Finely chop the flesh into a paste and mix with olive oil and sherry vinegar. Season and set aside.

name: Halloumi & Burnt Broccoli Salad
description: Burnt broccoli is a barbecue must-have. This simple salad pairs charred broccoli with salty halloumi. Get on it.
instructions: Pile coals over to one side of your BBQ to create a hot, direct cooking side, and a warm, indirect cooking side.

Pop your bulgur wheat into a bowl and rinse well with cold water. Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and pour in the rinsed bulgur. Cook for 10 mins, then drain. Pop back into the pan and cover with a lid, then allow to steam for 10 mins.

Cut the halloumi into chunky cubes and split the broccoli into quarters through the stem. Oil and salt the broccoli and get it straight onto the hot side of your grill. Cook, undisturbed, for 4-5 mins or until the cut-side of the broccoli is super charred. Flip over and give the broccoli another 4-5 mins.

While the broccoli grills, finely chop the chilli, cucumber, red onion and parsley. Tip into a bowl with the warm bulgur, then add the fresh peas, the juice of the lemon and the vinegar. Add the oregano and parsley.
Once grilled, pull the broccoli off the grill and roughly chop. Toss through the bulgur. Add plenty of olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Toss everything together and set aside.
Roll the diced halloumi in oil, then add to the hot side of the BBQ. Grill the halloumi for 3-4 mins, turning now and then, until golden brown and crisp.
Pile the salad onto a platter and top with the halloumi. Roughly chop the almonds and scatter over the top. Serve!

name: Halloumi & Orange Salad
description: Halloumi, orange and balsamic glaze. A flavour trifecta from the heavens.
instructions: Toast your nuts on a low heat and set aside.
Slice up your fennel and grill evenly on both sides.
In a separate pan, pour the balsamic glaze, squeeze in some fresh orange and grate some orange zest. Mix on a low heat.
Slice up your Halloumi and grill evenly on both sides using olive oil to prevent the cheese sticking to the grill.
Remove the skin on your remaining oranges and slice.
Add your mixed leaves, toasted nuts, some mint, your sliced orange and some of your glaze into a bowl. Toss away.
Add your fennel and Halloumi and some more of your glaze. Toss again.
Serve and dress with olive oil and more glaze if you choose to do so. Munch away!

name: Halloumi & Pomegranate Salad
description: A fresh and vibrant salad that’s good enough to be eaten on its own or as a side. The saltiness of the halloumi goes great with the sweetness of pomegranate.
instructions: To make the croutons, heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the olive oil. Rip up the sourdough into small pieces and fry until crisp and golden brown, sprinkle in the za’atar for the last min or so. Tip out the croutons and set aside.
Cut the halloumi into 3cm cubes, add a splash more oil to the pan and start searing off the cheese. Working in batches, cook over a medium heat, turning occasionally until golden brown on all sides.
Halve the pomegranate and break open to expose the seeds. Separate the seeds from the white pith and set aside. Dice the veggies into equal-sized pieces and finely chop the herbs.
In a large bowl, combine all the ingredients for the dressing, season with salt and pepper, and mix.

Add the chopped veg and half the herbs to the bowl with the dressing along with halloumi, croutons and pomegranate. Toss gently together to dress the salad and transfer to a sharing plate. Top with the remaining herbs and serve.

name: Halloumi & Roasted Grape Giant Couscous
description: Roasted grapes are a current obsession - we love how jammy they go when they burst. Their sweetness is perfect with salty halloumi in this simple, one pan veggie tray bake that you’ll be making on repeat.
keywords: Halloumi & Roasted Grape Giant Couscous recipe
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.

Rinse the giant couscous in a sieve then tip into a medium roasting tin. Finely slice the red onion, add to the tin along with the grapes on their vine. Mix the smoked paprika with the vegetable stock then pour this into the tin. Give everything a good stir.
Cover in tin foil and roast for 25 mins. Meanwhile toast the nuts of your choice, roughly chop if needed. Slice the halloumi.
Remove the tin from the oven - the couscous should now be cooked, take off the tinfoil and stir through the kale.
Turn the grill to high. Lay the halloumi slices on top of the traybake, drizzle over the honey then slide under the grill until the halloumi is nicely golden and grapes bursting, 3-5 mins.
Scatter over the toasted nuts and dill, plus a sprinkle more smoked paprika, to serve.

name: Halloumi & Sweetcorn Fritters
description: Golden sweetcorn and halloumi fritters that freeze beautifully. Quick to reheat, crisp on the outside and gorgeously fluffy on the inside.
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsDrain the sweetcorn and trim and finely slice the spring onions.
In a large bowl, whisk the flour with a pinch of salt and pepper. In another bowl, whisk the eggs and milk together, then add to the flour mix.

Whizz a quarter of the sweetcorn in a food processor and stir it into the batter along with two-thirds of the spring onions and the remaining whole sweetcorn. Cut the halloumi into small cubes and fold into the mixture.

Chop the cucumber and tomatoes into chunks. Set aside some for the kids. For the adults, toss the rest in a bowl with the remaining spring onions, the red wine vinegar, a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat a large nonstick frying pan over a medium heat and coat the base with olive oil. Drop heaped tablespoons of batter into the pan and cook for 2–3 mins per side until golden brown.

At this stage, the fritters can be transferred to a baking sheet and frozen. Once solid, tip them into a freezer bag. To reheat from frozen, cook in a frying pan over a medium heat for about 3 mins per side until piping hot.

Serve up! Kids Plate: Serve the fritters with cucumber batons and chopped tomatoes.Parents Plate: Dish out the fritters with the cucumber and tomato salad on the side. If you're looking for extra protein you could even add a poached egg.

name: Halloumi Bake
description: The quickest and tastiest dish about. You will love this one MOB.
instructions: Chop up your aubergines and add them into a non-stick frying pan. Cook until they brown, remove from the pan and set aside.

Add your chopped onion along with most of the fennel seeds and chilli flakes, and a shot of oil. Give it a good stir. Chop up your fennel, peppers and courgettes. Add to the pan and stir everything together.

Once the peppers and onions have cooked through, add the aubergine, olives and capers. Add the passata, chop up your basil and add this along with your vegetable stock, salt and pepper. Mix everything together and add 100ml of water and keep mixing. Cook for 12 minutes on a medium heat. Once the sauce is nice and thick, flatten it out with the top of a spoon.

Chop up your Halloumi and place each slice on top of the thick mixture. Sprinkle the remaining fennel seeds and chilli flakes over the top. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil. Place under the grill for 12 minutes until golden and bubbling. Tuck into this dish and enjoy!

name: Halloumi Breakfast Sandwich
description: The silkiest eggs with chopped chives, golden halloumi & a smokey chipotle and sweet chilli mayo. All in a toasted brioche. An incredible mouthful.
instructions: Finely chop the chives and set aside.
Prepare the burger sauce. Add the mayo, chilli jam and chipotle paste into a bowl and stir together.
Slice the halloumi into even chunks and add into a bowl along with a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and toss together.
Heat a glug of oil in a pan and fry the halloumi until golden brown. This will take a few minutes each side.
Get a bowl and crack in your eggs. Add in a generous pinch of pepper and whisk it up.

Melt a big knob of butter in a pan. Once melted, add in your eggy mixture. Keep stirring as it begins to scramble. You want to make sure the eggs stay nice and liquidy. Whack in the chives (saving some for garnish) and a pinch of salt, then mix together and remove from the heat.
Slice your buns in half and lightly toast

Time to load up. Start with a big dollop of your chilli mayo sauce, followed by 3 slices of your halloumi and finally a spoonful of your scrambled egg. Scatter over your leftover chives, season well and tuck in!

name: Halloumi Buddha Bowl
description: Minimal ingredients and maximum flavour. The tangy creamy peanut dressing perfectly ties together all the fresh Ocado veggies and crispy halloumi.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/ 350°F.
Add your pearl barley to a pan along with 1L of water. Bring that to a boil and cook the grains for 50 mins until tender.
Cut the sweet potato into thin medallions.
Coat the sweet potatoes in olive oil, salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 30 mins until tender and caramelised.
Thinly shred your cabbage, pick the leaves off of your coriander, and chop your halloumi into triangles strips before slicing one red chilli and finely chopping the other.
Massage the red cabbage in a bowl with salt and the juice of 1 lime.
Combine 2 tbsp peanut butter and the juice and zest of 1 lime with finely chopped chilli and 4 tbsp of boiling water to form a thin dressing. Don't forget to season the dressing with salt and pepper.
Add a small glug of oil to the pan and fry the halloumi on either side for 2 mins until golden brown.

Now it's assembly time. Place a generous base layer of pearl barley in a large bowl before topping it with your sweet potato medallions, quick-pickled cabbage, coriander and halloumi. Drizzle with the peanut dressing, sprinkle on your fresh sliced chillies and enjoy.

name: Halloumi Burgers with Curried Romesco Sauce
description: Grilled halloumi burgers with smoky homemade romesco and a fresh and tangy slaw. Does dinner get better than this?
keywords: Halloumi Burgers with Curried Romesco Sauce
instructions: Trim and finely slice the fennel. If you have a mandoline, now is the time to use it. If not, a sharp knife will do the job nicely. Trim and thinly slice the asparagus spears into rounds, keeping the tops whole. Add the fennel, asparagus, and asparagus tops into the bowl with the juice of 1 lime, 2 tbsp of olive oil, and 50g Greek yoghurt. Season with salt and pepper. Toss until evenly coated and set aside.

Peel the garlic cloves. Drain the roasted peppers and add them into a blender with the almonds, 40ml of olive oil, the curry powder and half of the garlic. Blend until a smooth thick sauce appears. Season with salt and pepper, then set aside.

Slice each halloumi block into four slices. Heat a drizzle of oil into a non-stick frying pan on medium-high heat. Once hot, add the halloumi and cook for 2-4 mins on both sides until golden, turn the heat down if the halloumi is colouring too quickly. Turn the heat down to low, add 2 tbsp of olive oil, grate in the remaining garlic, and stir through the ground turmeric. Turn to coat the halloumi, 1 min.
Halve and toast the buns.

Slather some romesco onto the bottom bun. Top with two slices of halloumi, some fennel slaw, and spread a good blob of yoghurt onto the top bun. Serve the burgers with the remaining fennel and asparagus salad.

name: Halloumi Con Tomate With Seedy Drizzle
description: We love pan con tomate so I’ve taken inspo from that and made a whole meal out of it. Golden halloumi, in a fresh tomato sauce with a seedy herby drizzle.
instructions: Trim, peel and finely dice the onion. Peel the garlic and thinly slice, drain the peppers and finely chop or pulse in a food processor until finely minced. Pick the oregano leaves, discarding the stalks. Halve the tomatoes. Using the coarse side of a box grater, grate the flesh of the tomatoes into a bowl, discarding the skin. Chop the halloumi into 2cm cubes.
Add a drizzle of olive oil into a frying pan on medium heat. Once hot, add the halloumi and cook until golden on all sides, 4-5 mins. Transfer into a bowl, leaving the fat in the pan.

Place the empty pan back on medium heat. Add the onion and sweat until translucent, 3-4 mins. Stir through the garlic, pepper and grated tomatoes, season with salt and pepper and cook for 15-20 mins until thickened, and the water has evaporated.

In another small saucepan add 60ml of olive oil and pumpkin seeds. Place on medium heat and cook until the seeds have toasted and split open, 2-3 mins. Take it off the heat and stir through the oregano leaves and sesame seeds.
Serve the halloumi on top of the tomato sauce. Drizzle over the seedy oregano oil. Mop it up with some flatbreads, if you like.

name: Halloumi Crouton Super Salad
description: The salad to end all salads. The halloumi croutons bring the heat - once you've tried them you'll be making them every week, guaranteed.
instructions: Preheat the oven 180°C/356°F.
Cut your peppers into chunks. Add to a roasting tray with salt, pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Roast for 40 minutes or until charred and soft.
Pesto time. Into a blender, add a handful of basil leaves, the juice of a lemon, garlic clove, toasted pine nuts and Parmesan. Add 5 tbsp of olive oil and blend until smooth.
Courgette time. Cut your courgettes into thin strips. Drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper. Add to a hot griddle pan and cook for 6 minutes on each side.

Halloumi time. Cut your halloumi into small cubes. Get three bowls out. Add plain flour to one, eggs to another (whisk them up) and breadcrumbs to the third. Dip your halloumi in the flour, then the eggs and then the breadcrumbs.
Get a pan on the heat. Fill it up 2cm high with vegetable oil. Heat the oil. Add the croutons to the pan. Cook for 4 minutes until golden brown.
Remove croutons from the heat and place them on some kitchen roll.
Halve your cherry tomatoes.
Add all of your ingredients, along with a bag of rocket and any leftover pine nuts, to a large salad bowl. Pour over your pesto dressing, toss it all together and serve it up. Enjoy!

name: Halloumi Gnocchi Curry Traybake
description: This bold and fiery traybake blends crispy halloumi, pillowy gnocchi and a rich coconut curry sauce. Topped with tangy pickled chillies and cooling yoghurt – it’s big on flavour, low on effort.
instructions: Quick-pickle the chilli. Finely slice the Scotch bonnet and add to a small bowl with the vinegar, sugar and a good pinch of salt. Mix well and set aside to pickle while you cook.
Preheat the oven to 200°C fan.
Make the curry sauce. Chuck all the curry sauce ingredients into a blender and blitz until smooth. Pour into a saucepan and bring to the boil. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Dice the halloumi and peppers into bite-sized chunks. Tip into a large roasting tray with a drizzle of olive oil and season well. Roast for 10 mins.
Take the tray out, add the gnocchi, then pour over the hot curry sauce. Give everything a good mix, then return to the oven for 20–25 mins, until bubbling and golden at the edges.
Serve it up. Top with dollops of yoghurt, fresh coriander and a scattering of pickled chillies.

name: Halloumi Grains with Green Tahini
description: A hearty, herby grain bowl with crispy halloumi and a punchy green tahini dressing. Perfect for a fresh, filling make-ahead lunch.
keywords: Halloumi Grains with Green Tahini recipe
instructions: Cut the courgettes into irregular 4cm pieces. Break the halloumi down its natural split, then cut into chunky pieces about the same size as the courgettes.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the halloumi and cook on all sides until golden – no need for oil. Remove from the pan.
Add the olive oil to the pan, then fry the courgettes on both sides until charred. Remove and season with salt and black pepper.

For the dressing, add the basil, tahini, juice of the lemons, ½ the jalapeños and all the water to a blender and blitz until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper, then taste and adjust if needed.
Mix the quinoa with the courgettes and season with salt and black pepper. Thinly slice the remaining jalapeño.

Box or plate up the courgette quinoa and top with the halloumi and sliced jalapeño. If eating later, store the dressing separately in an airtight container. If eating now, drizzle the dressing over the top. Everything will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Halloumi Parmigiana
description: The mash up you never knew wanted.. until now. The flavour and texture of the halloumi works wonders in this parmigiana recipe.
instructions: Heat a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add a big splash of olive oil and then add the harissa paste and sizzle for a minute, then add the passata. Add the sugar and red wine vinegar, season well with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, then turn the heat down and cover with a lid.

Meanwhile, slice the aubergines lengthways and season with salt. Put two large frying pans or griddle pans over a high heat. Working in batches, add the slices to the pans and char on each side until blackened and soft, then move to a bowl.
Heat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan. Taste the sauce and season with a little extra vinegar, sugar or salt if it needs it.

Spoon a little sauce into the base of a deep roasting tin around 20cm x 30cm. Arrange a layer of aubergine over the sauce, then cover with another spoon of the sauce. Finely grate a layer of Parmesan over the top, then repeat with the next layer of aubergine slices. You should finish with a layer of sauce.

Slice the halloumi into 0.5cm thick slices and layer on the top. Finish with a thick layer of grated Parmesan. Slide into the oven and bake for 30 mins, then turn on the grill and cook for 5-7 mins further or until golden brown. Set aside for 5 mins, then slice into 4 to serve.
Scatter with parsley and serve.

name: Halloumi Peanut Curry
description: Peanut butter and halloumi might not be the first ingredients that come to mind for a curry but this creamy spicy curry is a wonder. Make it for dinner tonight.
instructions: Chop up your spring onion, mangetout and pepper into strips, before beginning to fry in a pan with a large glug of oil. Peel the ginger, slicing it into thin strips. Once the vegetables have softened add in the ginger, stirring well.
Cut the halloumi into rectangle shaped pieces. Add this to the pan, frying the mixture until the halloumi is crispy and brown.

Next up - the sauce. Into the pan goes the sweet chilli, soy sauce and the peanut butter. Combine thoroughly, before adding the coconut milk and the juice of the lime. Turn the heat down and let the curry bubble until it is a creamy, thick consistency.
Whilst the curry is bubbling, get the rice on (see pack instructions).
Now that the curry is creamy and thick, add 2 tsp of chilli flakes. Roughly chop the coriander, before adding two thirds to the mixture. The curry is now ready!

Serving time! Spoon some basmati rice into a bowl, topping it with the curry. Garnish with another sprinkling of chilli flakes, some of the leftover coriander and a handful of peanuts. Repeat for the rest of your MOB. Enjoy!

name: Halloumi Saag Aloo
description: Saag aloo is a curry house favourite, made extra special with the addition of salty halloumi nuggets. Packing in all the flavour with lovely Ocado ingredients.
instructions: Finely dice your onions. Grate your ginger and garlic. Finely chop 2 of your red chillies, and slice the third.
Heat a large sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a good glug of oil, then add your cumin seeds. Cook for 2 mins until fragrant.
Tip in your onions and cook for 15 mins over a medium heat until soft and caramelised.
Meanwhile, prep your potatoes. Peel and dice them all into 3cm chunks.
Pop the potatoes in a pan of cold salted water and bring them to a boil. Cook for 15 mins until just tender.
Dice up your halloumi and fry it in a separate pan with a bit of oil until those cubes are golden on all sides.
Add your tomato purée, garlic, ginger and chopped chillies to the onions. Cook for 3 mins until the colour has darkened. Tip in your turmeric and cook for 2 mins more.
Add your thawed spinach to the pan along with 100ml of water and cook for 5 mins.
Add half of your spinach and onion mixture to a blender and blitz until smooth. Tip this back into the spinach pan and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Tip your potatoes and halloumi into the pan and gently stir to combine.
Garnish the mixture with your sliced red chillies, then serve.

name: Halloumi Tabbouleh
description: We have spent a long time perfecting our tabbouleh. It is so fresh, with a lovely spiced back note from the cinnamon. A dreamy dish with the halloumi & tahini.
instructions: Rinse the bulgur wheat in running water until the water runs clear. Bring clean water to a boil in a saucepan and season with salt. Add the bulgur and simmer for 10-15 minutes until the water has absorbed. Cover and leave to steam for 2 minutes, then fluff the grains with a fork and allow to cool.

Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes in half, remove any stems and spoon out the seeds so you are left with just the flesh. Finely dice the flesh then scoop up the tomatoes and drain away any excess moisture. Place into a large mixing bowl.
Finely chop the spring onion and add into the bowl. Squeeze in the juice and zest of a lemon and season with salt and pepper. Mix everything together.
Time for the tahini dressing. In a cup mix together the tahini, grate in the garlic, olive oil, salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Add water splash by splash until you have a nice creamy tahini dressing.

Slice the halloumi and add into a bowl. Season with olive oil, salt and pepper. Heat a non-stick frying pan on a medium-high heat and whack in the halloumi. Fry each piece of halloumi on both sides until golden brown and set aside.

While the halloumi is frying, finely chop your herbs. It is important not to bruise them so try to chop them as finely as possible on the first chop through so that you don’t have to go back and forth lots of times.
Add the herbs and the spices into the tomato bowl along with the cooled bulgur and pomegranate. Season with salt and pepper then drizzle with olive oil and toss together.
Immediately serve up the herby tabbouleh (you don't want to leave it sitting around for too long). Top with your golden halloumi, and drizzle over the tahini dressing.

name: Halloumi With Corn & Roasted Red Pepper Salad
description: Halloumi slices, charred corn and roasted red peppers come together to make a balanced weeknight meal ready in just 35 mins.
instructions: Microwave the rice according to packet instructions.
Meanwhile, drain the red peppers, thinly slice. Cut the kernels off the corn, pick the leaves off the herbs and finely slice the stems. Peel and finely dice the onion. Halve the tomatoes.
Add the onion into a large bowl with the zest of half a lemon and the juice of both. Season with salt and pepper, stir in 30ml of olive oil. Set aside.
Place a frying pan over high heat, no oil. Once hot, add the corn kernels and cook until starting to char, 3-4 mins. Meanwhile, slice each halloumi block into 6 slices.
Reuse the pan, add a drizzle of olive oil and place on medium-high heat. Once hot, add the halloumi and cook until golden on both sides.
Add all the corn, roasted peppers, tomatoes, rice, chopped stems and herbs into the onion dressing, toss together. Season with salt and pepper.
Share the salad between your plates and top with the halloumi, a drizzle of oil and any remaining herbs.

name: Halloumi in Blankets
description: Your veggie mates will love these. Herby halloumi, flakey pastry, and the freshest tzatziki dip. They are sensational.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Cut the halloumi into thick sticks - 12 sticks per block. Add them to a large bowl and season with your oregano, dill, a grind of pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Massage the seasoning in to coat the halloumi.
Lay one sheet of puff pastry out and evenly spread the harissa paste on top. Slice the puff pastry into 12 even strips. Repeat for your other roll of puff pastry.
Roll up one stick of halloumi in one strip of puff pastry. Place the pre-cooked halloumi blankets on a baking tray (baking paper is optional here). Repeat for the remaining halloumi pieces.

Carefully separate the egg yolks from the egg whites (you can use the whites for meringue). Beat the egg yolks together and brush the puff pastry with a coating of egg wash. Season with salt and sprinkle your fennel seeds over the top. Bake for 30 minutes, until golden.

Meanwhile, make your tzatziki. Pour the yoghurt into a bowl. Halve and deseed your cucumber. Grate the cucumber and squeeze out as much liquid as possible before adding the gratings to the bowl. Finely chop a handful of mint and it to the bowl with the juice of your lemon. Mix well and season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Serve the Halloumi in Blankets with your fresh tzatziki and enjoy!

name: Halloumi with Nectarines, Tarragon and Basil
description: This summery banger from Helen Graves' new book, "Live Fire" really hits the spot. It's written for the BBQ but works a treat on a griddle pan in the kitchen.
instructions: Prepare a BBQ or cast-iron griddle pan for cooking over a high heat.
Rub the nectarines with a little oil and cook, cut-side down, for about 5 mins, turning occasionally, until charred and softened.
Once cool enough to handle, dice the grilled nectarines and combine in a bowl with the tarragon, basil, chilli flakes, lemon and lime juice and a little salt.
Rub the halloumi with a little oil and cook quickly on the BBQ or griddle pan for a minute or so on each side, or until charred. Serve immediately with the nectarine mixture.

name: Halloumi, Tomato, Chickpea & Herb Salad Bowl
description: Warm tomatoey chickpeas with crispy halloumi, hummus and pitta chips for swiping. Crunchy, comforting and fresh, this one has it all.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Add to a baking tray then drizzle with olive oil and season with the dried oregano and a pinch of salt and pepper. Slide into the oven to roast for 15-20 mins until starting to collapse.

Cut the pitta into triangles and toss in a bowl with a small glug of olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Transfer to a separate baking tray and roast in the oven for 10-15 mins until crisp and golden.

Meanwhile, drain, rinse and pat dry the chickpeas. Add to a bowl along with a glug of olive oil, the sumac, cumin and a pinch of salt and pepper, and mix to combine. Break the halloumi down its natural split and dice into 2cm pieces.
Heat the grill. Add the chickpeas and olives to the roast tomato tray then scatter around the halloumi. Slide under the grill for 8-10 mins or until the halloumi is charred.
Pick the parsley and dill leaves and finely slice the red onion, then add to a bowl and mix to combine.
To serve, grab a plate and give it a swoosh of hummus. Top with the warm tomatoey chickpeas, halloumi, pitta chips and herb salad.

name: Halloumi, Za'atar and Orange Brussels Sprouts
description: Charred Brussels sprouts are great, but they are transformed by the fragrant additions of za'atar, pomegranate seeds, orange and halloumi. Incredible stuff.
instructions: First, get your chopping done. Cut your halloumi into 1cm thick slices. Peel and slice your red onion, then carefully chop the very tough end off your Brussels sprouts and half them.
Heat your griddle pan over a high heat. Place your halloumi in the pan and griddle for a couple of minutes on each side, or until they are golden with lovely charred lines. Set aside until later.
In a large frying pan over a medium heat, add a glug of olive oil. Add your red onion to the pan and fry for 10 minutes until just softened.

Tip your sprouts into the pan and fry for 10 minutes, stirring every so often until they are tender with beautiful caramelised edges. Add a splash of water half way through to steam them. Pop your halloumi back into the pan to heat up for a couple of minutes.
Grate the zest from your orange into the pan and add a sprinkle of za’atar.
Pour your sprouts into a bowl and garnish with your pomegranate seeds and a squeeze of orange juice. Serve!

name: Halloumi-Stuffed Greek Flatbreads
description: Forget the takeaway, these flatbreads are a game-changer. Super fresh and easy to whip up on a weeknight.
instructions: Weigh the flour into a bowl, add the baking powder, spoon in the yoghurt and add a big pinch of salt. Mix together in the bowl until you have a shaggy dough, then tip out onto a lightly floured work surface and knead for just a few minutes until you have a smooth dough. Put back into the bowl, cover and leave for 10 mins for the dough to relax.

Meanwhile, cut the cucumber into quarters lengthways, then into 1cm slices. Chunk up the tomatoes into bite-sized pieces and halve and thinly slice the red onion. Tip everything into a bowl with the olives, then drizzle in 2 tbsp oil, half of the red wine vinegar and sprinkle in the oregano. Season and toss well
Spoon the tahini into a small bowl and add the remaining red wine vinegar. Season and add 3-4 tbsp cold water until you have a drizzleable sauce.
Come back to the flatbreads. Tip back onto a lightly floured work surface and divide the dough into four. Flour each piece and roll out to an 18cm circle.

Get a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add one of the flatbreads to the pan and cook for 1-2 mins until risen, bubbly and puffy, then flip and repeat on the other side. Wrap in a clean tea towel while you cook the rest.

Get another large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cut the halloumi into 1cm-thick slices. Put into the pan without any oil and cook for 1-2 mins on each side until golden brown, then flip and repeat.
Spread each of the flatbreads with some of the tahini sauce, pile in some of the salad, hot chips if using, halloumi and finally some chilli sauce, if you’re a spice head like us.

name: Ham Hock & Pickled Veg Noodle Salad
description: Pulled ham hock means less faff and more flavour – this zingy noodle salad's ready in minutes and full of crunch and tonnes of fresh herbs.
keywords: Ham Hock & Pickled Veg Noodle Salad
instructions: Whisk the vinegar, boiling water and sugar in a bowl until the sugar has dissolved. Season generously with salt.

Finely slice the radishes and carrots (you can use a mandolin if you’ve got one) then cut into matchsticks. Finely slice the chillies. Add the sliced veg and chillies to the pickling liquid and set aside to pickle. The longer they sit, the punchier they’ll be.
Cook the rice noodles following pack instructions. Once cooked, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Slice the chives and coriander stalks into 2cm lengths. Pick the mint and coriander leaves, discarding the mint stems. Then pull apart your ham hock into thin pieces.
Divide the noodles between bowls and drizzle over some of the pickling liquid.
Toss the pickled veg, herbs and ham together, then pile on top of the noodles. Finish with a scattering of crispy onions and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Ham, Egg & Chips Salad With Lemony Bacon Dressing
description: Ham, egg and chips — but not as you know it. We've turned this British classic into a delicious salad with a bacon dressing, jammy eggs and chips for croutons!
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220ºC. Finely slice the potatoes and chop them into thin matchsticks. Soak the potatoes in cold water for 10 mins, rinsing twice, and then draining and patting dry. Finely chop the rosemary and add to a tray along with the dried potatoes. Drizzle with oil and season with salt and pepper. Transfer to the oven and cook for 10 mins, before giving them a mix and returning to the oven for another 8-10 mins. Keep an eye on these, they can catch!

Meanwhile, make the mayo. Heat a pan and add ½ tbsp of vegetable oil along with the lardons. Cook on a medium-low heat until all the fat has been rendered out. Tip the fat into a measuring jug and top up with vegetable oil to make 100ml of liquid. Zest the lemon and set aside. Crack 2 egg yolks into a bowl and add the dijon, a pinch of salt and a big squeeze of lemon juice. Using a whisk, whip it all up until combined. Add a splash of the lardon oil and whisk vigorously, repeat this around 4 times — this will prevent splitting. Add the rest of the oil by pouring in a slow, gradual stream. Keep whisking until emulsified, then taste and add lemon zest, remaining lemon juice, crispy lardons and black pepper. If you find the dressing too thick, loosen with cold water.

Next, cut the tomatoes into wedges and add to a sieve, seasoning with salt. Let them hang out over a bowl, catching the juice to drink later (a treat). Tear the little gem lettuce into pieces and finely chop the chives. Bring a small pan of water to a boil and add 4 eggs before reducing to a simmer and cooking for 7 mins. Drain the eggs and submerge in icy water to stop them cooking, then peel and halve around the belly.

Once the potatoes are cooked, you're ready to assemble. Put the little gem lettuce in a bowl and mix with most of the dressing, giving it a good mix. Grab a large platter and add the little gem, potatoes, tomatoes and eggs, drizzle with dressing and top with chips and chives.

name: Ham, Egg & Cress High Protein Smash
description: Cheesy, eggy and packed with protein. This smash is perfect for whacking in the fridge for easy and quick lunches to have all week.
instructions: Place a pan of water over a high heat and bring to the boil, lower in your eggs and simmer for 8 minutes. Remove into iced water to cool before peeling. Separate the yolks from the whites and then add both into a large mixing bowl.

Using scissors, cut the cress into the same bowl followed by the chives. Using a peeler, grate in your cheddar. Toss in the ham and cornichons, followed by the mayonnaise, mustard and some salt and pepper.
Chop everything through with a pizza cutter, until you have an ‘egg salad’ consistency.
To serve, spoon out onto some freshly toasted bread and top with some of your favorite crisps and a few extra cornichons.

name: Hand-Pulled Biang Biang Noodles with Spicy Pork & Garlic
description: Learn to make biang biang noodles from scratch. We’ve served them with spicy ground pork and a garlicky aromatic sauce.
instructions: For the homemade biang biang noodles: Combine all the ingredients in a large mixing bowl and use a spoon to bring it together as a dough. Using your hands form it into a ball. Place into a clean bowl and cover with 2 damp tea towels. Rest for 30 mins. (If the dough is sticking to your fingers, add an extra tbsp of flour, and if the dough ball has dry patches then add an extra tsp of water at a time).

Knead the dough for 4 mins and form into a ball. Cover with a damp tea towel for 5 mins to let the dough relax. Use a knife to cut the dough into 8 pieces. Use your hands to roll each piece into a log, then use a rolling pin to roll each log into a flat oval, around 15 cm long.

Pour a generous amount of vegetable oil onto a large plate. Coat each piece of dough very well in oil then layer on top of each other. Cover the plate with cling film and set aside for 2 hours at room temperature. (Alternatively, make the dough the night before, leave in the fridge and remove at least 1 hour before cooking)

For the sauce: Peel and roughly slice the ginger. Roughly chop the chillies. Separate the green and white parts of the spring onions and set aside the green parts to use later with the pork mince. Put the spring onion whites, ginger, chilli, garlic and a pinch of salt in a blender and blitz to a rough paste (or use a pestle and mortar). Transfer to a medium heat proof mixing bowl.

Heat the vegetable oil in a small saucepan set over a high heat and bring to a smoking point then immediately pour the hot oil over the spring onion, ginger mixture. Add the remaining sauce ingredients, mix well and set aside at room temperature.
For the pork mince: Crush the garlic and finely slice ½ of the remaining spring onion green tops (from the sauce ingredients). Mix together the corn flour and cold water in a small bowl.

Heat a glug of sesame oil in a large pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the pork mince, flatten into a patty shape and leave to sear for 2 mins or until lightly golden. Add the garlic, spring onions and ground cumin, break up the meat and cook for another minute, until the aromatics are lightly golden. Then, add the soy sauce and oyster sauce and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds. Stir through the corn flour water and leave to cook for 30 seconds. Remove the pork mixture to a small bowl, cover and set aside at room temperature.
When the noodles have rested, fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.

Before pulling the noodles, prep all the ingredients as the noodles come together very quickly. Warm the mince in the microwave if needed. Add 4 tbsp of noodle sauce into each serving bowl, slice the spring onions, and gather the roasted peanuts, crispy shallots, chilli oil and pickles ready for garnishing.
Take a piece of dough and use a chopstick to gently press a horizontal mark into the middle of it. On a clean work surface, gently pull the dough horizontally around 1 arm's length long.
Hold the dough in both hands and lightly pull and slap it onto the work surface (making a biang biang sound) until you create a long ribbon and the dough can’t stretch anymore.
Place the dough down on the surface and tear it apart through the middle dent until you have a large ‘O’ loop shape. Place onto a work surface and repeat with all the dough.

Add all the noodles into the boiling water and cook for 3-4 mins. Taste for doneness; they should float to the top and look slightly translucent on the edges. Use tongs to transfer to a sieve and shake off the excess water. Share the noodles into the serving bowls. Quickly top with the minced pork, roasted peanuts, crispy shallots, spring onions and a heaped tbsp of chilli oil per portion.

name: Hand-Rolled Trofie With Pesto & Beans
description: Making your own pasta is super satisfying. We've paired this easy homemade pasta shape with pesto and beans. It's a ripper.
instructions: Tip the fine semolina onto your work surface, using a bowl to create a well in the middle of the semolina. Fill the semolina volcano with warm water. Using a fork, begin mixing the semolina into the water gradually until you have a thick paste. Now, using your hands, incorporate the rest of the semolina to form a shaggy dough.
Knead for 5 mins until the surface is smooth and elastic. Form into a ball and rest the dough under an upturned bowl for 15 mins.

While the dough rests, make the pesto and beans. Trim the ends of the beans and cut into 4-5cm lengths. For the pesto, add the basil and pine nuts to a food processor, finely grate in the Parm and garlic and whizz to a thick paste. Add olive oil gradually until you have a thick-ish pesto. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.

To roll the trofie, pinch off a marble-sized piece of dough and place it on your work surface. Using the palm of your hand, roll that piece of dough forwards, forming it into a sausage shape. Now, draw your hand backwards, dragging the outside edge of your palm over the sausage whilst applying a little pressure. The dough will twist and turn into a beautiful little spiral. Repeat with the rest of your dough.

Bring a pan of salted water to a boil and drop the beans in for 3 mins. Now, add the trofie in for a further 1-2 mins. Scoop the pasta and beans out into a large mixing bowl and add a few generous spoonfuls of the pesto. Toss together with a splash of hot pasta water to loosen if necessary.
Divide between warm bowls and top with extra Parmesan.

name: Handmade Potato & Taleggio Tortelli
description: Fresh pasta is something else. We’ve stuffed these homemade tortelli with a mixture of potato and taleggio and cooked them off in a hazelnut and sage butter.
keywords: Potato & Taleggio Tortelli With Hazelnut Sage Butter
instructions: To make the pasta dough, dry blend the semolina and the flour together. Pour out onto a clean work surface and create a well in the centre. Add the eggs and, using a fork, beat the eggs together. Slowly incorporate the flour into the centre of the well until you have a thick paste. Bring the walls of flour into the paste and knead until you have a smooth, springy dough. Wrap in cling film, or cover with an upturned bowl and rest for 30 mins. You can also knead the dough in the smeg stand mixer using the dough hook attachment.

To make the filling, peel and cut the potatoes into equal-sized pieces. Add to a pan, cover with cold water and season with salt. Bring to a simmer and cook until soft. Drain and allow the potatoes to steam dry. Mash the cooked potatoes with the other stuffing ingredients until homogeneous. Season with salt and pepper.

Roll out the pasta using the Smeg pasta roller attachment. Pass one-third of the dough through the widest setting, and keep working your way down until you have landed on the second thinnest setting. Cut the pasta sheets into squares and cover with a damp towel. Repeat until all the pasta is rolled out.

To make the tortelli, add a half teaspoon of filling to the centre of a square of pasta. Dab some water over two of the edges. Fold the square roughly in half, intentionally not lining up tjhe corners. Wrap the pasta around your fingers and squeeze the two halves together to connect the pasta into a round. Repeat with the remaining pasta.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the butter to a sauté pan and set over a medium heat. Add the hazelnuts and cook until nut brown. Chuck in the sage leaves and cook until fragrant. Toss the pasta into the boiling water and cook for 60-90 seconds. Transfer to the hot butter with a big ladle of pasta water. Toss, toss, toss until the sauce is creamy and emulsified and the pasta is nicely glazed in brown butter. Finish with lemon and salt.
Divide between warm plates and serve.

name: Hanoi-Style Turmeric Cod & Dill Noodle Soup
description: Inspired by a bowl of Chả Cá Lã Vọng eaten in Hanoi, this is a brothy, noodle-packed version loaded with a serious amount of dill. Light, comforting and absolutely full of flavour.
keywords: Hanoi-Style Turmeric Fish & Dill Noodle Soup
Hanoi-Style Turmeric Fish & Dill Noodle Soup recipe
Hanoi-style turmeric fish & dill rice noodles
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Add the turmeric, curry powder, half the vegetable oil and a third of the fish sauce to a large bowl. Finely grate the garlic and ginger straight in, season with salt and a generous crack of black pepper and mix until combined. Cut the cod into large, even pieces roughly 10cm chunks, and toss into the curry marinade. Set aside.
Chop the spring onions into thirds and roughly chop most of the dill, saving a few fronds to serve. Add the spring onions to the fish and gently toss to coat in the marinade.
Bring the water to the boil in a medium saucepan. Crumble in both stock pots and add the remaining fish sauce. Taste, season with salt and leave on a low heat.

Tip the fish and spring onions onto a lined baking tray and spread out in a single layer. Drizzle over the remaining veg oil and roast for 7-9 mins, then scatter over the chopped dill and return to the oven for a further 1-2 mins, or until the fish is cooked through and the dill is just wilted.
Meanwhile, cook the rice noodles according to packet instructions.

Drain the noodles and divide between four bowls. Ladle over enough broth to cover, then top with the fish, spring onions and dill. Finish with the reserved dill fronds and the lime, cut into wedges, and serve straight away.

name: Harissa & Honey Roast Parsnips
description: Sticky caramelised parsnips are elevated to a new level of deliciousness with the addition of harissa in this honey roast parsnips recipe. The combination of honey and harissa creates a perfect balance of sweetness and spice, making these honey roast parsnips an irresistible side dish. Roasted to perfection in the oven, these parsnips develop a beautifully caramelised exterior while remaining tender inside. This honey roast parsnips recipe is ideal for a Christmas dinner or any roast meal, adding a flavorful twist to your traditional side dishes. You can serve them alongside roast potatoes, carrots, and other vegetables for a complete roast dinner. The glaze of honey and harissa not only enhances the natural sweetness of the parsnips but also gives them a gorgeous, sticky finish. Perfectly seasoned with salt and pepper, these parsnips are so delicious that you'll be eating them straight off the tray.
keywords: harissa and honey roast parsnips recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel the parsnips, slice off the woody tops, then halve them lengthways and cut into 2½cm pieces. Transfer to a large roasting tray, add 2 tbsp oil and a good pinch of salt and pepper, then toss well. Spread into an even layer so that they cook evenly. Roast for 20 mins.

After 20 mins, use a fish slice to flip the parsnips. Mix the honey and harissa together in a small bowl, then add to the tray and strip in the thyme leaves. Toss so that everything gets coated in the spiced herby honey mix.
Return to the oven for 8-10 mins until the parsnips are tender and nicely caramelised in places.

name: Harissa & Maple Courgette Rice Salad
description: These courgettes are the best you’ll ever make. Super crisp on the outside but juicy in the middle, then tossed in a glossy spicy and sweet sauce. Yum.
keywords: Harissa & Maple Courgette Rice Salad recipe
instructions: Grate the zest of the lemon into a small bowl, then squeeze in the juice. Stir through the rose harissa and maple syrup, then add a 1 Tbsp of water. Season lightly with salt and black pepper and set aside.
Cut the courgettes into 2cm-thick slices. Finely shred the sugarsnaps or mange tout. Halve, slice or quarter the tomatoes, depending on size. Roughly chop the smoked almonds and set aside.

Heat the rice following pack instructions, then tip it into a large mixing bowl. Drizzle in half the dressing and mix well. Add the shredded sugarsnaps and tomatoes and gently fold to combine. Season to taste.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the courgette slices in a single layer – work in batches if needed. Fry for 2-3 mins on each side until golden and crisp on the edges, then flip and cook the other side.
Take the pan off the heat and pour in the remaining dressing. Toss the courgettes for a minute until everything’s sticky and glazed.

Tear most of the dill and mint into the rice salad and fold it through. Spoon the salad into bowls, then top with the sticky courgettes and any pan juices. Scatter over the chopped almonds and finish with the remaining herbs.

name: Harissa Aubergine Pilaf
description: Tender aubergine embedded in fragrant and spicy harissa-spiked Tilda Basmati and Wild Rice. Top with cooling lemony yoghurt, crispy onions and toasted almonds.
instructions: Slice your onions and chop up the aubergine and peppers into small chunks.
Add a big glug of oil into the pan and cook the chunks of aubergine with a pinch of salt in a heavy-bottomed pan on all sides until they're golden brown. Set aside once finished.
Fry one of your onions in a glug of oil for 10 mins until very soft and caramelised. Add in the ground cumin, ground coriander and cook for 1 min.
Grate in the garlic and add the harissa paste with a tsp of salt and cook for 1 min until the garlic has softened and the harissa is fragrant.

Rinse the Tilda Basmati and Wild Rice very well in cold water, add it into the pan along with the veg stock and mix well. Toss in your cooked aubergine and red peppers, pop on a lid and cook on a gentle simmer for 25 mins.
Meanwhile, finely chop your coriander and toast your almond flakes.
Heat 3cm of oil in a frying pan and heat to a medium heat. Gently fry your remaining onions until crispy and caramelised. Drain on a paper towel.
Zest the lemon into yoghurt, stir in the juice of half the lemon and season with salt.
When the rice has cooked, fluff it up with a fork and mix in half the coriander.
Serve with lemony yoghurt, flaked almonds, crispy onions and more coriander.

name: Harissa Brown Butter Gnocchi
description: Gnocchi from scratch. It’s about a million times better than the store-bought stuff and way easier than you might think. Best slathered in brown butter sauce.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Prick your potatoes all over with a fork, put them on a baking tray and slide them into the oven to roast for an hour until a knife slides through with no resistance at all.

Slice your potatoes in half and leave them to steam for a few mins, until they’re cool enough to handle, then scoop the flesh from the skin (Don’t throw away the skins! Make some stuffed skins or bake with oil to make some potato skin crisps.)
Press the flesh through a sieve onto your kitchen surface and season well with salt and pepper, then grate a little fresh nutmeg over.

Sieve the flour over the top. Use a knife to chop through it all to make a big crumbly mess, then use your hands to bring the mix together. Cut the block into 8 triangles. Cover with a damp tea towel.

Dust your surface liberally with flour, then take each eighth, one at a time, and roll it into a long log. Use the back of a table knife to chop into 3cm lengths. Set aside on a baking tray and repeat with the rest of the dough.

Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil, then drop a handful of the gnocchi in at a time and boil for 2 mins, until they float up to the surface. Use a slotted spoon to transfer onto a plate or a clean baking tray to steam a little- repeat with the rest- don’t throw away the water!

Make the sauce. Heat a frying pan over a medium heat and then add the butter. Cook, whisking constantly until it’s turning brown and starts to smell like digestive biscuits, around 2-3 mins, then add the harissa paste. Turn the heat down, take a spoon of the gnocchi water and whisk it in. Toss to make a silky sauce then leave on a very low heat.

Heat another large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a tbsp of butter. Once melted, add the gnocchi and fry until golden on both sides. Tip the sauce in and toss, toss, toss. Add the lemon juice and toss some more. The sauce should perfectly coat the gnocchi – season well and tip into bowls. Top with fresh parsley and a scattering of parmesan to serve.

name: Harissa Bulgur Wheat Traybake
description: Food cooked in one tray has never tasted this good. Fluffy bulgur wheat. Juicy tomatoes. Warming spices. A kick of rose harissa. A beautiful lunch.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C/400°F.
Drain your chickpeas, then tip them into your roasting tray along with your cherry tomatoes, cumin and cinnamon. Drizzle with a glug of olive oil and a sprinkle of salt, then roast for 30 mins.
Add your bulgur wheat to the roasting tray along with your hot vegetable stock and harissa paste. Give it a good stir, then cover the tray tightly with foil and bake for 15 mins longer.
Whilst your bulgur wheat cooks, roughly chop your parsley.
Once cooked, remove the foil and fluff the bulgur wheat with a fork. Season to taste.
Sprinkle with the chopped parsley and a dollop of yoghurt, if using. Serve and enjoy.

name: Harissa Chicken & Chickpea Soup
description: Treat future you with an all-in-one soup that cooks straight from frozen. Spicy, sweet and deeply comforting, this chicken soup basically cooks itself.
instructions: Start by finely chopping the parsley. Grate the garlic and halve the cherry tomatoes. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

Add the parsley to a tupperware then top with the harissa, garlic, pomegranate molasses, cherry tomatoes, star anise, chickpeas and chicken stock. Pop the chicken on top and season with salt and pepper.

Pop into the freezer until you’re ready to cook. Once you are ready, transfer the frozen contents of the Tupperware into a saucepan. Cover with a lid and heat on a medium, cooking until melted. Once melted, simmer for 15 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and the soup is piping hot.
Shred the chicken up in the soup and serve up!

name: Harissa Chicken & Cottage Cheese Hummus Bowl
description: Creamy lemony hummus, spicy harissa chicken and garlicky greens all piled into one seriously satisfying high-protein bowl.
instructions: First, make the hummus. Peel the garlic. Drain the chickpeas, reserving the liquid from the can. Tip the chickpeas into a food processor with the zest and juice of half of the lemons, the tahini, one of the garlic cloves and the cottage cheese. Blitz until smooth, loosening with a splash of the reserved chickpea liquid if needed. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Finely slice the remaining garlic cloves. Roughly chop the frozen peppers.

Place a nonstick frying pan over a medium heat and add half of the olive oil. Add the chicken mince, season with salt and pepper and cook, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until no longer pink. Add half of the sliced garlic and cook for 1 min, stirring constantly.

Add the frozen peppers and cook for about 3 mins until warmed through. Stir in the harissa and cook for another minute until the chicken is fully coated. Pour in the water and let everything gently simmer while you get on with the spinach. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the remaining olive oil. Add the remaining garlic and the cumin seeds and cook for about 1 min until fragrant. Add the spinach in batches, letting it wilt down before adding more. Squeeze over the juice of half a lemon and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon the hummus into bowls, top with the harissa chicken and peppers, then pile on the garlicky spinach. Finish with a drizzle of tahini and serve with warm flatbreads on the side.

name: Harissa Chicken & Minty Couscous
description: Harissa Chicken. So simple, yet so good. This dish combines the rich, smoky heat of harissa with tender, juicy chicken to create a flavour-packed meal that you’ll keep coming back to.
