The beauty of harissa is its versatility—whether you prefer it fiery hot or more on the mild side, you can easily adjust the spice level to suit your taste. Serve it with fluffy couscous, roasted veggies, or a fresh salad for a balanced, satisfying dinner. It's perfect for weeknights when you want something quick but flavorful, and it’s bound to become a go-to in your recipe rotation.
instructions: Roughly cut the chicken thighs into chunky strips and whack them in a bowl with 2/3 of the yoghurt and half of the harissa paste. Season with salt and pepper then massage the mixture into the chicken.
Cook the couscous to packet instructions. Run a fork through the grains once cooked then cover with a chopping board or clean tea towel until ready to serve.
Heat a glug of oil in a frying pan set over a medium heat then get the chicken in, stirring occasionally and leaving to cook for around 12 minutes.
Chop your mint and coriander and finely slice your cucumber. Add the herbs and cucumber to the couscous with the juice of the lime. Season with salt and pepper and toss to combine.
Divide the couscous between four plates then top with the chicken, a dollop of yoghurt, a drizzle of the remaining harissa and the chopped herbs.

name: Harissa Chicken Kebabs & Tangy Couscous Salad
description:
In Partnership with Al'Fez. #ad

Juicy harissa-infused chicken kebabs served over a tangy couscous salad with olives, roasted peppers and pickled onions. Proper sunshine-in-a-bowl vibes.
keywords: Harissa Chicken Kebabs & Zesty Couscous Salad recipe
Harissa Chicken Koftas & Zesty Couscous Salad
instructions:
Heat the oven to 220°C. 
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water to stop them catching under the grill.

Chop the chicken into 3cm chunks and chuck into a bowl. Grate in the garlic and stir through the Al'Fez Harissa Paste. Season with salt and pepper, then thread the chicken onto skewers. Drizzle a little olive oil onto a baking tray, arrange the skewers on top and roast for 10–15 mins, until cooked through and golden.
Tip the Al'Fez Moroccan Spiced Couscous into a bowl, pour over the boiling water and cover with a plate or lid. Let it steam for 5 mins.

Meanwhile, halve the olives. Drain the peppers and finely chop. Chop the cherry tomatoes into 2cm chunks (halve the small ones). Thinly slice the red onion. Add the onion to a large bowl with the red wine vinegar and a pinch of salt. Give it a toss and set aside to pickle.
Pick the parsley leaves, discarding the stalks. Then fluff the couscous with a fork, then chuck the chopped tomatoes, peppers and olives into the pickled onion bowl.

Just before serving, toss the parsley through the couscous along with the contents from pickled onion bowl. Season to taste. Spoon the couscous salad into bowls and top with the harissa chicken and a dollop of yoghurt and get stuck in!

name: Harissa Chicken Skewers & Zesty Yoghurt Slaw
description: The key to perfectly tender, flavourful chicken skewers? Natural yoghurt. Marinated in the yog and teamed with a cucumber slaw. Delicious.
instructions: Preheat the grill to high.

Add the self-raising flour and baking powder into a large bowl with 1 tsp of salt, mix. Stir through the yoghurt until a dough forms, then knead for 3-5 mins until smooth. Divide the dough into 4 balls, cover and let rest whilst preparing the rest.

Cut the chicken thighs into 3cm bite-sized chunks. Peel the garlic. Add the chicken into a bowl with the harissa, 30g of yoghurt, and grate the garlic in. Season with plenty of salt and pepper, mix together. Thread the chicken onto skewers and place on a baking tray.
Trim and finely slice the fennel and radishes.
Slide the chicken under the grill until the chicken is cooked and charring in bits, flipping halfway through, 8-12 mins.

Meanwhile, place a pan on medium-high heat. Dust a work surface with a little flour and roll the balls of dough out until thin, around 2mm. Once the pan starts smoking, place a flatbread on and cook on both sides until golden and almost charred, for a total of 2-3 mins.
Add the fennel and radishes into a bowl. Add the zest of 1⁄2 the lemon, stir through the remaining yoghurt and season to taste with salt, pepper and some lemon juice.
Serve the skewers with flatbreads, fennel and radish slaw and any remaining lemon wedges.

name: Harissa Chicken Traybake with Herby Grains
description: Charred harissa chicken and jammy onions grilled to perfection, served over lemony courgette grains with loads of herbs and a dollop of yoghurt. It's a belter.
instructions: Heat the oven grill to high.
Cut the chicken thighs into quarters. Peel and finely slice the onions. Grate the garlic.
Add the chicken, onions, harissa and grated garlic to a large bowl. Drizzle in some olive oil, season with salt and black pepper, and toss to coat.

Tip everything onto a baking tray and spread into an even layer. Slide under the grill on the top shelf and cook for 5-15 mins, turning halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and the edges are starting to catch. (all grills differ! Keep an eye)
While that grills, dice the courgette. Finely chop the dill and parsley.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Chuck in the courgette and fry for 6–8 mins until golden and soft, seasoning as you go.
Tip in the grains and stir through until hot. Take off the heat, then stir through the herbs and squeeze in the juice of half a lemon. Taste and tweak the seasoning if it needs it.
Serve the grilled chicken and onions over the herby grains with a big spoonful of Skyr yoghurt on the side.

name: Harissa Chicken Traybake with Jammy Tomatoes & Olives
description: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs roasted over burst cherry tomatoes and briny olives, served with a punchy harissa yoghurt. A proper low-effort tray bake that delivers.
keywords: Harissa Chicken Tray Bake with Jammy Tomatoes & Olives
Harissa Chicken Tray Bake with Jammy Tomatoes & Olives recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.

Tip the cherry tomatoes and olives onto a large baking tray. Drizzle over the olive oil, season with salt, black pepper and the oregano, then toss to coat. Nestle the chicken thighs skin-side up on top and season well with salt and black pepper, then drizzle over a little extra olive oil to help the skin crisp up.
Roast for 35–45 mins until the chicken is golden, the tomatoes have burst and everything's bubbling. If the skin needs extra colour, slide it under the grill for 2–3 mins at the end.
Meanwhile, microwave the wild rice pouch according to the packet instructions. Stir the yoghurt and harissa together in a small bowl. Squeeze in the lemon juice and add a pinch of salt.
Spoon the cooked rice into bowls and top with the chicken and all those jammy tomato and olive tray juices. Finish with generous dollops of harissa yoghurt and lots of torn parsley.

name: Harissa Chicken, Za'atar Cauliflower & Leeky Butter Beans
description: Harissa-marinated chicken thighs roasted over buttery leeks and cauliflower, finished with a creamy Parmesan butter bean situation. Perfect for on the go lunches.
keywords: Harissa Chicken Za'atar Cauliflower & Leek Butter Beans recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Add the chicken thighs to a large mixing bowl with the harissa paste, honey and the juice of half the lemon. Season with salt and black pepper, mix well until evenly coated and set aside.
In a separate bowl, mix together the olive oil, za'atar, honey and a good pinch of salt. Cut the cauliflower into quarters and toss through the spice paste until well coated.
Slice the leeks in half lengthwise, then cut into half moons. Wash and dry well. Finely slice the chives. Roughly chop the parsley. Slice the garlic, leaving the skin on.

Drizzle a little olive oil into a deep oven tray. Place the cauliflower quarters flat-side down on one side of the tray, then add the leeks and garlic to the other side. Drizzle a little more oil over the leeks and season with a pinch of salt. Place a wire rack over the top of the tray and arrange the chicken thighs on top, skin-side up. Roast for 30-40 mins, until the chicken is cooked through and the skin is golden.

Remove from the oven and transfer the chicken and cauliflower to a plate to rest. Place the oven tray directly on the hob over a medium heat. Stir the Dijon mustard through the leeks, then add the butter beans with all their liquid. Pour in the bone broth and bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 mins until slightly thickened, then remove from the heat. Stir through the Parmesan, chives, parsley and a squeeze of the remaining lemon. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

Divide the beans between four airtight containers, top each with a chicken thigh and a wedge of cauliflower. To reheat, microwave for a few minutes until piping hot. Serve with a dollop of yoghurt on the side. Or you can eat cold straight from the fridge.

name: Harissa Chickpea Bowl with Sun-Dried Tomatoes
description: This recipe is a weeknight saver. A comforting chickpea bowl that delivers both on flavour and nutrition in less than 30 minutes.
keywords: chickpea and spinach bowl quick vegan dinners
instructions: Dice red onion and garlic cloves. Roughly chop the sun dried tomatoes. Pit the kalamata olives and roughly chop them.

Heat a glug of olive oil on a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Once the olive oil is hot add red onion and fry until it begins to develop some colour. Add garlic, a pinch of salt and let cook for another 2 mins until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste, sun dried tomatoes and kalamata olives and harissa paste. Leave to cook 2-3 mins and let the flavours infuse. If the mixture starts to dry out, add a ladle of vegetable stock.

Add the chickpeas, previously drained from their stock, and vegetable stock. Cook over a medium-high heat for 15-20 mins or until the sauce starts to thicken. Turn off the heat. If you'd like it saucier, add a splash of water.
Add in the spinach and nutritional yeast and stir until the spinach has wilted completely. Season with salt and pepper to taste and let the dish sit for 5 mins before serving.
Divide into bowls and serve with toasted sourdough bread.

name: Harissa Chickpea Kofte Bowl
description: Dr Rupy joins us to make the very best veggie koftes. Gently spiced and served with harissa tahini, this dish is brought to life by Arla Skyr Creamy 5% Yogurt.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Finely chop your red onion and mince your garlic cloves. Finely chop your parsley leaves and stalks.

Put the chickpeas, garlic, spices, red onion, parsley stalks, eggs, breadcrumbs, soy sauce, tomato purée and a big pinch of salt and pepper into a food processor. Blitz until the mixture comes together as a paste.
Squeeze into sausage shapes and place on a baking tray. Drizzle with the olive oil and cook for 15-20 minutes in the oven, turning halfway until golden brown.
Meanwhile, prepare the salad. Dice your tomatoes and cucumber. Toss the tomatoes, cucumber and your parsley leaves with some olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon, sumac, salt and pepper.
Mix the tahini, remaining lemon juice and harissa paste together to make a dressing. Use a splash of hot water to loosen it if needed, then season to taste with salt.
Warm your pitta breads in the toaster.
Place the koftes in a bowl with the salad, wholemeal pitta, lots of Arla Skyr Creamy 5% Yogurt and drizzle over the harissa tahini dressing. Serve and enjoy.

name: Harissa Chorizo Prawn Rice
description: Chorizo and prawn is a winning combination. Add some spicy harissa and tangy salty feta into the mix and trust us, you’ve got a belter of a dish.
instructions: Peel and slice the chorizo, finely slice the onions.

Get your largest high sided frying pan over a medium to high heat. Pour in a good glug of olive oil, chuck in the chorizo and onions with a pinch of salt. Fry, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes until the onions have collapsed and softened and the chorizo has released its oil.
Meanwhile finely chop the garlic cloves and halve the cherry tomatoes.

Add the garlic cloves and fennel seeds (if using), to the frying pan, stirring for 1 minute then tip in the rice. Spoon in the harissa paste and give everything a good stir so that each grain of rice gets coated in the onion and spices.

Chuck the cherry tomatoes into the pan and pour in the white wine. Once the wine has nearly bubbled away, pour in 2/3 of the stock. Mix then leave to bubble for 18-20 minutes, stirring occasionally until the stock has been absorbed and the rice is cooked with a slight bite. At this point, turn down the heat to low and pour in the remaining stock.

If using prawns with their shells on, heat a griddle or large frying pan over a high heat. Fry the prawns for around 2 minutes on each side until they have turned completely pink and their shells have slightly blackened. Scatter over the top of the rice. If using prawns without their skin, chuck the raw king prawns into the rice, and leave for 2-3 minutes to cook through.

Zest 1 of the lemons into the rice, squeeze in the juice and season to taste. Crumble over the feta and tear over the parsley. Drizzle the rice with some olive oil, then cut the other lemon into wedges for serving. Enjoy.

name: Harissa Cod & Chickpeas
description: You only need six ingredients to make this easy recipe for harissa cod and chickpeas. It's spicy and incredibly satisfying.
instructions: If you have the time, remove the cod from packaging and toss in 2 tbsp salt, set aside on a plate in the fridge, uncovered, for up to 24 hours. Then, rinse and pat dry. This makes the cod flaky and amazing so if you have even half an hour, do it!

Add 2 tbsp olive oil to a large deep frying pan over a medium high heat. Add the harissa paste and fry for 2 mins. Add the cherry tomatoes to the pan and fry for 2-3 mins, then use a potato masher or the back of a large spoon to squish them so they burst. Add the chickpeas, along with the water from the can. Season with salt and pepper and turn down the heat to medium. Simmer for 10 mins, until thickened.

Snuggle in the cod fillets, then spoon the sauce over the fillets to help them cook. Gently bubble for 3-5 mins, until the cod is flaking apart. Gently put each fillet into a shallow bowl, then spoon the chickpeas and tomatoes over and around it.
Top each with a big dollop of mayo and some parsley leaves. Finish with extra olive oil and a big pinch of salt and pepper.

name: Harissa Courgette Grains with Tahini Dressing
description: This one-pan, creamy spiced grain bowl, which also happens to be vegan, is going to become your Monday night regular. A casual little weeknight dinner.
keywords: Harissa Courgette Grain Salad With Tahini Dressing
instructions:
Thinly slice the courgettes into half-moon shapes. Cut the lemon
in half.
Get a frying pan over a high heat and drizzle in a good glug
of olive oil. Chuck in the courgettes. Crush in the garlic cloves. Fry, stirring occasionally, for 5 mins until the
courgettes are softened and slightly charred.
Meanwhile, put the tahini in a small bowl and squeeze in the juice
from the lemon halves. Stir, then slowly mix in enough warm water
to make the dressing a thick drizzling consistency. (Adding the
lemon juice may make the tahini seize up at first, but when you
add the water it will turn smooth.) Season with salt and pepper.
Back to the courgettes. Add the harissa paste to taste. Squeeze
the unopened grain pouches with your hands to break up the
grains, then open and tip them into the pan along with a splash
of water. Stir and leave to heat through while you chop the dill.
Stir the chopped dill through the grain mixture, season to taste
with salt and pepper and pile onto a large serving dish. Drizzle
over the tahini dressing and serve with extra harissa, if you like.

name: Harissa Lamb Sausage Rolls
description: A great alternative to your classic sausage roll. Spicy, herby, cheesy goodness, all encased in a crisp pastry shell.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C/374°F.
Finely slice your red onions. Finely chop your parsley.
Heat a medium-sized frying pan over a medium heat. Add a generous glug of olive oil, then add your onion to the pan. Cook gently for 25 mins until soft and caramelised. Allow to cool.
Tip your lamb mince into a bowl and add your feta, caramelised onions, chopped parsley, harissa paste, ground cinnamon, an egg, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Mix until totally combined.
Crack your egg into a bowl and give it a good beat. Unroll your puffy pastry.
Arrange in a sausage shape down the length of the pastry, then brush one edge with egg wash. Fold the other edge over the filling and roll it over so you have a tight roll and sealed edge.
Brush the exterior of your rolls with egg wash and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Pop in the fridge to chill for an hour, or until your pastry feels firm.
Chop each roll into 10 segments and arrange spaced apart across 2 baking sheets.
Bake for 25 mins, or until they are a deep golden brown and your pastry looks tender and flaky. Serve hot or room temperature.

name: Harissa Lentils on Crunchy Toast
description: Savoury and saucy lentils on top of extra crunchy fried toast. A quick and simple meal that's light yet comforting.
keywords: Harissa Lentils on Crunchy Toast recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the garlic. Drain and finely dice the peppers.

Place a saucepan over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the garlic and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant, then tip in the harissa, peppers and lentils. Pour in the stock and let it come to the boil. Reduce the heat and gently simmer for 10 mins. Taste and season with salt.
Meanwhile, add a generous drizzle of olive oil to a frying pan. Fry the bread on both sides until golden brown, adding more olive oil if needed. Pick the dill and mint.
Place a piece of toast into a bowl or plate with high sides, then spoon over the brothy lentils. Garnish with the herbs and a wedge of lemon. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Harissa Lentils with Charred Peppers and Olive Salsa
description: An unbelievably simple plant-based meal with heaps of flavour. Merchant Gourmet Puy Lentils, charred peppers and the most addictive olive and hazelnut salsa.
keywords: Harissa lentils with charred peppers and olive salsa recipes
instructions: Heat your grill to high.
Drizzle your peppers with salt and olive oil. Place them under the grill and cook for 10 mins until soft and blackened, turning every so often so they cook evenly.
Meanwhile, make your olive salsa. Add your hazelnuts to a dry frying pan and toast for 3 mins until lightly browned. Allow to cool slightly, then roughly chop your nuts.
Finely chop your olives and parsley.
Tip most of your hazelnuts, your olives and parsley into a bowl along with the zest and juice of ½ lemon, 4 tbsp olive oil and a generous pinch of salt. Mix to combine.
Allow your peppers to cool slightly, then peel off their skin and discard their seeds. Tear the flesh into rough strips.

Make your dressing. Combine your harissa paste, the juice of ½ lemon, 3 tbsp olive oil and a good pinch of salt in a large bowl. Tip in your Merchant Gourmet Puy Lentils and pepper strips, then toss to combine. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon your lentil salad onto plates and spoon on your olive salsa. Sprinkle with your remaining hazelnuts and a drizzle of olive oil, then serve and enjoy.

name: Harissa Mac and Cheese
description: Creamy and spicy mac and cheese with tangy harissa. It's also made totally vegan using Violife!
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Finely chop 4 cloves of garlic and coriander.
Add 50ml of vegetable oil to a pan and add in the flour. Cook on medium heat for 7-8 mins until it turns a dark golden brown. Then add in the garlic and cook for 3 mins.
Then pour in the oat milk and keep mixing until you get a smooth consistency.
Meanwhile, pop the macaroni in some boiling water and cook for 5 mins.
Grate the Violife Epic Mature Cheddar and add this to the pan and keep mixing until it's smooth and melted.
Add in the harissa paste, juice of a lemon and 1 tsp salt.
Save 200ml of pasta water and add the macaroni to the baking dish.
Add in 200ml of pasta water so it’s very loose. Transfer this to a baking dish.

Grate in the remaining garlic into a small bowl and add in 2 tbsp of olive oil. Mix well and then add in the breadcrumbs, coriander and grated Violife Prosociano Wedge. Season well with salt and pepper
Sprinkle this over your pasta and bake for 20 mins until golden and bubbling.
Allow to cool for a few mins and then tuck in!

name: Harissa Mango Chicken & Coriander Couscous
description: I always forget how quickly couscous rehydrates, so this is the perfect meal to make when you're ravenous. All the flavour comes from two condiments that pack a punch — make sure you use your favourite brands, for an delicious quick meal.
keywords: Harissa Mango Chicken & Coriander Couscous recipe
instructions: Add the chicken thighs to a bowl with half the harissa paste. Season generously with salt, mix together and set aside.

Now get on with the cucumber salad. Thinly slice the cucumber and add to a separate bowl. Season with salt, toss together and tip into a sieve to drain for 10 mins. Zest half the lemon into a bowl with the Greek yoghurt and olive oil. Season to taste with a squeeze of lemon juice, salt and pepper.

Add the couscous to a heatproof bowl. Pour the boiling water over, season with salt and cover tightly. Set aside to steam for at least 5 mins. Meanwhile, set aside a few coriander leaves for garnish and finely chop the rest, stalks and all.

Chicken time. Place a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the olive oil and fry the chicken for 8-10 mins, turning halfway, until cooked through. Add the mango chutney, water and remaining harissa. Stir together and baste the chicken until glazed, adding a splash more water if needed.

Fluff up the couscous with a fork, stir through the chopped coriander and divide between plates or boxes. Top with the chicken and its glaze. Toss the cucumber through the yoghurt dressing and serve alongside. Finish with freshly cracked black pepper, the reserved coriander leaves and any remaining lemon cut into wedges.

name: Harissa Meatballs & Herby Quinoa
description: Spicy meatballs, burst tomatoes and herby quinoa. Finished with a dollop of yoghurt to cool things down,  this one’s a proper weeknight winner that you can make in no time.
instructions: Place a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the meatballs and sear all over for 5-6 mins until browned.
Tip in the cherry tomatoes and cook for 4-5 mins, stirring occasionally, until the meatballs are cooked through and the tomatoes are starting to burst.
Stir the harissa and water together to make a sauce, then add it to the pan. Let it bubble for a minute. Add a splash more water if you want a looser sauce.
Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander and reheat the quinoa. Toss the two together and season with a pinch of salt.
Share the quinoa between plates. Top with the meatballs, tomatoes and harissa sauce. Add a dollop of yoghurt on the side.

name: Harissa Roast Lamb & Sticky Aubergine Cous Cous
description: Leftover Garlicky Slow-Roast Lamb Leg with golden roasted aubergine and cherry tomatoes, tossed through harissa-spiced giant couscous with dried apricots and a dollop of cool yogurt.
keywords: Harissa Lamb & Sticky Aubergine Giant Couscous
Harissa Lamb & Sticky Aubergine Giant Couscous recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the Garlicky Slow Roast Lamb batch recipe.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the aubergine into 2cm rounds and toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper. Spread out on a lined baking tray and roast for 15 mins. Toss the cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper, add to the tray and continue roasting for a further 10 mins, until the tomatoes are soft and beginning to burst.
Meanwhile, cook the giant couscous according to the packet instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water. Roughly chop the dried apricots and parsley.
Add the couscous to a large bowl with the harissa, cinnamon and dried mint. Squeeze in the lemon juice and mix well, then fold through the roasted vegetables. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Reheat the lamb if you like, or serve at room temperature. Serve the couscous topped with the lamb and extra parsley, with a dollop of yogurt alongside if using.

name: Harissa Salmon with Chickpeas & Lime Yoghurt
description: Big spice, soft chickpeas, crispy salmon — all tied together with a zingy lime yoghurt. It’s quick, punchy and proper good.
instructions: Cut the salmon into chunky pieces and season with salt and pepper. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a non-stick frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the salmon, skin-side down, and cook for 2-3 mins until crisp. Flip and cook for another 2 mins on the other side.

Mix the harissa paste, honey and water in a small bowl. Pour the mix into the pan and let it bubble around the salmon for 30 seconds or until cooked through. Baste the fish with the sauce, then lift it out and set aside to rest.

Finely slice the garlic and the cavolo nero. Add both to the pan and cook for 1 min. Tip in the chickpeas, cumin, paprika and a pinch of salt, then pour in the vegetable stock. Let it simmer for 5 mins until slightly thickened but still brothy.
While the chickpeas cook, zest the lime and squeeze in the juice of half. Stir it through the Greek yoghurt with a pinch of salt.
To serve, spoon the chickpeas into bowls and top with the harissa-glazed salmon. Add a generous dollop of the lime yoghurt and finish with fresh coriander, if you’ve got it.

name: Harissa Tahini Cauliflower
description: Creamy tahini and spicy harissa over roasted cauliflower. On a rich and aromatic chickpea stew? Doesn't get much better.
instructions: Preheat oven 180°C/ 356°F.

Slice the cauliflower into eighths and place in a baking tray. Sprinkle salt, pepper, a teaspoon of ground coriander and a teaspoon of cumin over the top. Drizzle with olive oil and place in the oven for 30 minutes.
Dice your aubergine, add to a frying pan and cook until it starts to brown.
Dice an onion and add it to the pan with a splash of olive oil. Mix together. Chop up some parsley stalks and add this to the pan and mix well.

Pour the can of chickpeas into the pan, add harissa and continue to mix all the ingredients together, adding salt and pepper to taste. When the chickpeas are soft, add a handful of parsley leaves and take off the heat.
Add tahini and the juice of your lemon into the bowl. Mix until combined.
Add half a cup of water and continue to mix until you have a nice creamy consistency.
Serve the roasted cauliflower on a bed of the chickpea and aubergine mix and dress with your lovely tahini dressing. Serve and enjoy!

name: Harissa Tomato Bruschetta
description: Cherry tomatoes chucked in a frying pan with olive oil and harissa are fried until they just begin to burst, then spooned over cool yoghurt and garlic toasts.
instructions:
Toast the bread. Meanwhile, peel the garlic clove. As each piece
of toast is ready, rub it on one side with the garlic, then spread
with a big spoonful of Greek yogurt and put onto plates.
Get a large frying pan over a super high heat and drizzle in a
good glug of olive oil. Chuck in the cherry tomatoes and season
with salt and black pepper. Fry for 2 minutes until the tomatoes
just begin to burst. Stir in the harissa paste to taste, then remove
from the heat.
Spoon the hot tomatoes over the cool yoghurt toasts, making sure
to spoon over all the flavoured oil from the pan too. Finely grate a
little lemon zest over each plate of bruschetta and tear over a few
basil leaves to finish.

name: Harissa Tomato Pasta Salad
description: Add a little heat to your summer picnic with this harissa tomato pasta salad. It's a lovely healthy dinner option.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the rigatoni and cook according to the package instructions. Drain the pasta and rinse it under cold water to stop the cooking process. Set aside to cool completely.
While the pasta is cooling, halve the cherry tomatoes and slice the roasted red peppers into thin strips. Roughly chop the parsley and roasted almonds.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, harissa paste, lemon juice, lemon zest, and honey (or maple) syrup until well combined. Season well with salt and pepper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled rigatoni, cherry tomatoes, roasted red peppers, parsley, and roasted almonds.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss everything together until the pasta and vegetables are evenly coated with the dressing.
Spoon into bowls, top with a few extra parsley leaves and a sprinkle of chopped almonds.

name: Harissa Tuna Crunch Pasta Salad
description: Forget croutons, this pasta salad gets its crunch from crispy air fried pasta. Tossed in spicy harissa tuna, with crisp gherkins and cucumber to make it extra punchy.
keywords: harissa tuna crunch pasta salad recipe
ingredients: 2x 145g Can Tinned Tuna in Olive Oil
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the fusilli and cook according to the pack instructions, then drain and leave to steam dry.

Set aside a quarter of the cooked pasta in a bowl and toss with the olive oil, smoked paprika, a pinch of salt and pepper until well coated. Tip into the airfryer and cook at 200°C for 8 mins, shaking the tray every couple of minutes, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, drain the tuna and finely slice the red onion and gherkins. Halve the cucumber, scoop out the seeds with a teaspoon, then slice. Chop most of the dill, saving a little for garnish.

Add the tuna, red onion, gherkins and cucumber to a large bowl with the garlic powder, harissa, yoghurt, dill and apple cider vinegar. Add the remaining pasta and the crispy pasta, season with salt and pepper, then mix well to coat. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Serve topped with the crispy onions and reserved dill. Dig in!

name: Harissa Tuna Rice Bowl
description: Inspired by eating slata tounsiya in La Marsa, right on the beach. Vibrant, fresh and made even heartier with rice - seriously quick and unbelievably easy.
keywords: Chloe René harissa tuna rice bowl
instructions: Finely chop the parsley, then trim and smack the cucumber. Chop the cucumber and tomatoes into 2-3cm chunks and add to a bowl with the olives. Squeeze in the juice of your half lemon, season with salt, then toss together and set aside.

Now for the sauce. Squeeze the juice of the remaining half lemon into a bowl, then stir in the harissa, honey and extra virgin olive oil and season with salt. The harissa is the main flavour provider here, so use your favourite one.
Reheat the rice according to the packet instructions, then add it to a bowl with the parsley and a third of the tuna. Drizzle over half the sauce and toss together until evenly combined.
Share the rice between bowls, top with the salad and the remaining tuna, then drizzle over the rest of the sauce and dig in.

name: Harissa Vegetable Traybake
description: A harissa-spiced chunky aubergine and cabbage traybake with crispy chickpeas and blistered cherry tomatoes. A healthy colourful dinner that’s packed with nutrients and tastes absolutely delicious.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Cut the cabbage into chunky wedges and roughly chop the aubergine and red onion. Arrange on a baking tray along with the cherry tomatoes and chickpeas. Drizzle over a glug of olive oil and stir through the harissa. Season with salt and pop into the oven for 35 mins, turning halfway.
To serve, spread a tablespoon of Greek yoghurt over each plate and top with a dollop of harissa. Top with the roasted vegetables and a sprinkling of fresh parsley.

name: Harissa and Cumin Potatoes with Crispy Chickpeas and Yoghurt
description: These potatoes are cooked in a spicy tomato sauce for a super warming bowl of goodness, finished with fresh yoghurt and crunchy chickpeas.
keywords: Harissa and cumin potatoes with crispy chickpeas and yoghurt recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Line a baking tray with baking paper, drain and add the chickpeas, 1 tbsp cumin seeds, a generous glug of olive oil and a big pinch of flaky salt.
Mix well and place into the oven for 25 mins until golden brown and crunchy, shaking the tray a few times during cooking.
Finely slice the onion and add to a saucepan over a medium heat along with 100ml of olive oil. Allow to cook for about 7 mins until the onion starts to soften.
Finely slice the garlic and add it to the saucepan along with your remaining 2 tbsp of the cumin seeds as well as the harissa and tomato purée. Cook for another 2 mins.
Dice the potatoes into roughly 2cm cubes, add to the pan and mix well. Pour in the vegetable stock and bring to a simmer, cook for about 20 mins until the potatoes are soft but not mushy.

Finely chop the mint and stir through the yoghurt with a pinch of salt. Once the potatoes have cooled slightly, drizzle all over with the yoghurt, top with the crunchy chickpeas and and a handful of chopped coriander, if you like.
Eat with flatbreads or spoon over rice. Enjoy!

name: Harissa and Mackerel Rigatoni
description: Spicy, tomatoey rigatoni with flaky mackerel, loads of harissa heat and a hit of lemon. Fast, fiery and exactly what weeknights are for.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of well-salted water to the boil. Add the rigatoni and cook for 2 mins less than the pack instructions.
Meanwhile, finely chop most of the parsley and set aside, save the remaining leaves to serve.
Thinly slice the garlic. Place a frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Add the garlic and cook for about 1 min until softened but not coloured.

Stir in the harissa paste and cook for 1 min more. Tip in the cherry tomatoes whole, then prick each one with a knife so the skins split. Use the back of a spoon or a potato masher to squash them slightly as they cook.
Add the mackerel, breaking it up gently with a spoon. Season well with salt and black pepper, then cook for 2 mins until everything is warmed through and saucy.

Using a slotted spoon, transfer the rigatoni straight into the sauce and toss well to coat, add in a big splash of pasta water. Squeeze in the juice from half of the lemon and stir in the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Spoon into bowls, scatter over the remaining parsley and serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges on the side.

name: Harissa and Tomato Gnocchi
description: Making gnocchi from scratch isn't as hard as you might think. The sauce we toss these in is a garlicky tomato sauce enriched with harissa paste and silken tofu.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Add your potatoes to a baking tray, then rub with salt and olive oil. Stab each potato with a fork, then bake for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, make your sauce. Start by finely slicing your garlic.
Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat. Add your garlic and cook very gently for 2 mins. Tip in your chopped tomatoes, then simmer for 30 mins until reduced.
Add your tofu and rose harissa to the tomato sauce, then whizz to a smooth sauce with a stick blender.
When your potatoes are cool enough to handle, cut them in half. Scoop out the flesh and set the skins aside. You can use them to make loaded potato skins if you fancy saving on food waste.
Push your potato flesh through a potato ricer or a fine sieve set over a bowl. Add your flour and a generous pinch of salt, then mix to combine.
Turn your dough out onto a surface and briefly knead until smooth. Divide your dough into 2 evenly sized pieces.
Roll each piece of dough with your hands until it forms a sausage shape about 1 inch wide. Cut into ½ inch wide pieces.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook until the gnocchi float to top, then cook for a further 30 seconds and remove from the water.
Add your miso paste to your tomato sauce. Add the zest of your lemon, and the juice of half of it. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Add a splash of pasta water to your sauce, along with your gnocchi. Gently toss to coat, trying your best not to break up the gnocchi.
Spoon onto plates, and top with a drizzle of olive oil, basil leaves and a crack of black pepper. Serve and enjoy.

name: Harissa-Spiced Shepherd’s Pie
description: Your classic shepherd’s pie has had a delicious makeover. Spiked with spicy harissa and topped with sweet potato mash, it's a dish you're going to bloody love.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C.
Prep your vegetables for your pie filling – finely dice your onion, carrot, and celery stick, then grate your garlic.

Heat a frying pan over a high heat. Add a little olive oil, then half of your lamb mince. Cook until the meat is browned, but not necessarily cooked all the way through. Remove from the pan, then repeat with the rest of your lamb. Set aside.

In the same pan, add a glug of olive oil and then tip in your onion, carrot, and celery. Turn the heat down to medium and fry for 10 minutes until softened and starting to caramelise. Add your garlic, cumin, cinnamon, and turmeric and cook out for 2 minutes.

Return your lamb to the pan along with your chopped tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a boil, then turn down the heat and simmer for 30 minutes or until your lamb is tender and your sauce has reduced to a lovely glossy consistency. Add your peas and 3 tbsp of harissa paste, then simmer for another 3 minutes before seasoning to taste with salt and pepper.
Peel and chop your potatoes into 2-inch pieces. Place in a cold pan of water and bring up to the boil. Cook for 15 minutes, by which time they should be tender.

Drain over a colander in the sink and let them steam dry there for a minute or so. Return to your frying pan, then mash with a potato masher until smooth. Add your remaining harissa paste and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Pour your lamb filling into a pie dish and top with your potato. Mark the surface with a fork, then bake for 25 minutes. Your top should be golden and your sauce bubbling around the edges.
Serve up with a big pile of greens.

name: Hasselback Butternut Squash
description: Hasselbacking BNS is the way forward. The tops get all squidgy and charred, while the inside is perfectly cooked. Served with the freshest chimichurri dressing.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 215°C/419°F.

Start by peeling your squashes. Cut them in half and de-seed. Place them on a baking tray, flat side down. Add a generous drizzle of olive oil over the top and season with a pinch of salt and a grinding of pepper. Place into the oven for 15 minutes.

Once 15 minutes is up, take them out of the oven. It’s hasselback time. Take one butternut half and cut across the squash with about 0.5cm intervals, making sure that you stop before you hit the bottom of the squash. Repeat this for the remaining squashes (yep, it is spelt squashes). Place back in the oven for 20 minutes.
Take them out and baste the squashes with the juices in the tray. Whack back in the oven for a further 20 minutes.

Onto the chimichurri. Start by chopping your mint, parsley, chilli, red onion. Add everything into a small bowl as well as your red wine vinegar, oregano, capers, 5 tbsp of olive oil, a pinch of salt and a grinding of pepper. Mix together.
Toast your almonds until golden.

Once your squashes are done, take them out of the oven and serve with a quarter of the chimichurri sauce, a small handful of almonds and crumble a quarter of feta over the top. Repeat for your MOB and tuck in. Enjoy!

name: Hawaiian Pineapple Chicken
description: A delicious take on the classic sweet and sour chicken. You'll keep coming back for more...
instructions: Cut your chicken thighs into chunks and add to a bowl. Add cornflour, salt & pepper. Mix together.
Heat oil in a large wok (or large frying pan). When the oil is hot, add the chicken and cook until golden. Remove the chicken and wipe down the pan.
Slice up your onions and peppers and add them to the pan with a splash of olive oil. Once the onions have softened, add the chicken again.

Drain the pineapple (but reserve the juice). Add the pineapple chunks to the wok and cook for a further two minutes. Grate your ginger and slice your garlic, then stir in and cook for a further minute.
Combine the reserved pineapple juice, soy sauce, lime juice, sriracha and the tomato puree in a bowl. Mix together and add to the wok.
Continue cooking on a high heat until the sauce is nice and thick. Once cooked, turn off the heat and serve over boiled rice. Sprinkle with coriander and tuck in!

name: Hawaiian Pizza Sandwich
description: Hawaiian pizza is divisive. But there's no arguments about how delicious this ham and pineapple pizza-ish sarnie is.
instructions: Start by removing the pineapple skin then slice into wedges around the core. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat and dry fry the pineapple for 15 mins, turning on each side until nice and charred.

Finely dice the chilli, jalapeño and red onion. Remove the pineapple from the pan and cool, then finely dice and add to a bowl with the chilli, jalapeño, lime juice, red onion, apple cider vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Using a stick blender, whizz the tomatoes until smooth then season well with salt. Halve the ciabatta and toast until golden in a pan over a medium heat, then preheat your grill to high.

Spread half of the ciabatta with tomato sauce then tear over the mozzarella, then put under the grill until bubbling and golden. Remove from the grill and top with the ham, charred pineapple salsa and basil. Top with the remaining piece of ciabatta and tuck in.

name: Hazelnut & Beetroot Pasta
description: This vibrant and delicious dish is both nutritious and satisfying. The natural sweetness of the beetroot pairs beautifully with the pasta and creates a stunning color, making it as visually appealing as it is tasty.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Tip the hazelnuts onto a baking tray, then toast in the oven for 6-8 mins until evenly golden. Leave to cool, then roughly chop one-quarter of the nuts and set aside for later.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, drop in the pasta and cook for 1 min less than pack instructions.

Meanwhile, drain the beetroot and roughly chop. Put into a food processor along with three-quarters of the basil (stalks and all), the whole toasted hazelnuts, garlic clove, extra virgin olive oil and a third of the ricotta. Finely grate in the Parmesan and lemon zest. Blitz everything together to form a finely chopped pesto. Season with salt, black pepper and lemon juice to taste (start with about half a lemon, then taste and add more if needed).

Once the pasta is cooked, drain, saving a large mugful of pasta water. Tip the pasta back into its saucepan. Stir the beetroot pesto through the pasta, adding enough pasta water so that each piece of pasta gets coated and saucy. Reheat a little if needed.
Divide the pasta between bowls. Dot with the remaining ricotta, drizzle with a little more oil then tear over the remaining basil leaves and scatter over the chopped hazelnuts to serve.

name: Hazelnut & Spiced Chicken Schnitzel With Pickled Oranges & Fennel
description: Hazelnut-coated chicken schnitzel and a zesty pickled orange side salad. Expect loads of different textures and flavours.
keywords: Hazelnut & Spiced Chicken Schnitzel With Pickled Oranges & Fennel
instructions: Make the pickle. Add the water, vinegar, caster sugar and salt into a sauce pan. Bring to the boil. Immediately turn off the heat and allow to cool completely.

Halve the fennel bulb lengthwise and very finely slice. Peel the orange, then thinly slice. Transfer both to a large bowl then pour over the cooled pickle liquor. This will last 3-4 days in the fridge, so just drain off before using.

If you have stale bread, cut off the crusts and add it to a food processor with the hazelnuts and spices. Blitz until you have breadcrumbs. If you already have fresh breadcrumbs, crush the nuts and spices in a pestle and mortar or blender until fine, then stir into the breadcrumbs.
Place each chicken breast between two pieces of baking parchment. Bash them with a rolling pin, one at a time, to flatten to about 1cm thick. (you can also butterfly these first if you want)

Get three wide bowls out. Add the flour to one, seasoning with a pinch of salt and pepper, then the breadcrumbs and sesame seeds to another, and finally beat the eggs in the last bowl. Prepare an empty baking tray to put the chicken on once breaded.

Dip each piece of chicken into the flour, coating every surface by patting it into the meat. Shake off any excess, then dip into the egg mixture, again making sure every bit of the meat is coated. Finally dip the chicken into the spiced breadcrumb mix (toss it into the bowl, so every little bit is covered), then place the breadcrumbed chicken breasts onto the prepared tray.

Get a large frying pan over a medium heat and add all the oil so it comes to 1½ cm up the pan. Allow the oil to heat up. Once hot, add in one piece of chicken at a time so as not to overcrowd the pan, and fry for 3 mins each side until golden on both sides. Lift out and onto a plate lined with kitchen paper, then repeat.
This also works great in the oven if you don't want to fry. Simply preheat the oven to 190c then place them on a baking tray drizzled with olive oil and bake for 15-20 minutes.
Mix the herby mayo ingredients together in a small bowl. Serve the schnitzels with a dollop of the mayo and a pile of pickled fennel and orange.

name: Hazelnut Chocolate Croissant Traybake
description: Heaven in a dessert. This moreish pud has everything: chocolate, butter and toasted hazelnuts. Not to mention, it's good for brunch, too.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Unroll the puff pastry onto a large baking tray. Once the oven is preheated, bake the pastry until golden on top, 15-20 mins. Then, rotate the sheet 180 degrees and transfer to a wire rack. Place back in the oven, turn the heat down to 160°C and continue to bake until super crispy, brown and dried throughout, 20-25 mins.

Meanwhile, add the hazelnuts onto a baking tray and place in the oven until toasted, 15-20 mins. Then, let it cool down. Once cool, reserve 40g of the toasted hazelnuts, then add the rest into a blender and blitz until floury, or finely ground. Roughly chop the remaining whole hazelnuts.

Chop the chocolate into small chunks. In a bowl, combine the softened butter, 85g sugar, 1 egg, toasted hazelnut flour and ½ tsp of salt — this is the hazelnut frangipane. Increase the oven temperature to 180°C.
Add the remaining sugar into the blender and blend until very fine and white, it should become icing sugar. Crack the other egg into a small bowl, add 1 tsp of icing sugar and whisk together.

Once the puff pastry is done baking, use a long serrated knife to split it in half lengthwise. Spread the hazelnut frangipane onto the base layer of puff, then evenly scatter the chopped chocolate on top. Return to the oven and bake for 10 mins.

Meanwhile, gently brush the egg wash onto the top of the pastry, sprinkle over the chopped hazelnuts. After 10 mins, place the top onto the frangipane base and bake for another 10-15 mins, until golden.
Sift the remaining icing sugar on top, then cool down for 10 mins for the frangipane to set. Use a sharp serrated knife to cut into slices.

name: Hazelnut Mocha Overnight Oats
description: All the best bits of a mocha, but in overnight oat form. Plus Nutella. No need to say more, really.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Tip the instant coffee into a small heat-proof measuring jug and add the boiling water, mixing well.

Add the oats, half the yoghurt, cocoa powder, coffee, maple syrup, protein powder (if using), milk (any will work), vanilla and salt to a bowl. Mix well and set aside. 
If your protein powder thickens things too much, add a splash more milk to loosen.
Tip the hazelnuts onto a baking tray and roast for 12–15 mins until golden and fragrant. Let them cool, then roughly chop.
In a separate bowl, mix the remaining Greek yoghurt with the Nutella until smooth.

Spoon the oats into jars or containers. Top with the Nutella yoghurt and scatter over the hazelnuts. Dust with a little extra cocoa powder, if you're feeling fancy.
Chill overnight, ready to grab for breakfast tomorrow.

name: Healthy Chicken & Broccoli Chopped Salad
description: This one’s a bit of a packed lunch hero. Quinoa, chicken and broccoli bring the bulk, and a zingy miso dressing ties it all together. Tastes even better the next day.
keywords: Lunch Box: Chicken & Broccoli Chopped Salad
Lunch Box: Chicken & Broccoli Chopped Salad recipe
instructions: Boil the broccoli in a pot of salted boiling water for 3-4 mins until it’s just about cooked. Remove the broccoli and allow it to cool.

Preheat your oven to 180°C. Season your chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place your chicken breasts onto a baking tray and get them in the oven for 25 mins. Allow them to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm.
Heat up your quinoa according to package instructions.
Squeeze the juice from your limes and combine with the rest of the dressing ingredients in a bowl.
Chop up the coriander, the cooked broccoli, and chicken into even-sized pieces. Toss with the quinoa in a large bowl.

Divide the salad between your Tupperware containers and stick them in the fridge.Keep the dressing separate – either pour it over in the morning or stash it in a little pot inside your box to add just before eating.These will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Healthy Chicken Gyros with Fresh Tzatziki
description: Spicy chicken in warm pittas, with a fresh tomato salsa and the perfect cooling tzatziki. What more could you want?
instructions: Dice chicken into small chunks and add to a bowl. Grate the cloves of garlic and red chilli into the bowl. Add 3 tsps of oregano. Add the zest of your lemon. Add 4 tsps of your yoghurt, salt and pepper.
Rub together and cover with cling film. Leave in fridge for 15 minutes.
Tzatziki time. Pour the rest of the yoghurt into another bowl. Add a small bunch of finely chopped mint, the juice of the lemon, and grated cucumber. Season well and mix it all together.
Tomato salsa. Finely chop your tomatoes. Add to a bowl with 2 tsps of oregano, salt, pepper and olive oil.
Finely chop your lettuce.
Put a griddle pan on a medium to high heat. Once it is hot, add your chicken. It needs 3 minutes on each side.
Warm some pittas. Assemble to gyros and tuck in. Enjoy!

name: Healthy Chicken Meatball Grain Bowl
description: A bright green grain bowl packed with lean chicken meatballs and plenty of quinoa. This is what healthy weeknight dinners are all about.
instructions: Grate the Parmesan, and then set it aside. Finely chop the red onions. Add a shot of oil to a frying pan and tip in the onions with a pinch of salt. Cook for 7-8 mins until lightly coloured and starting to soften.

Tip the chicken mince into a bowl. Grind the fennel seeds coarsely and tip into the chicken along with the cooked onions, ½ of the Parmesan, the breadcrumbs and egg. Finely chop half of the parsley and get that in there, too. Zest in ¼ of your lemons and season with salt and pepper. Mix thoroughly until the mince starts to become sticky. Form into medium-sized meatballs and set aside on a tray.

Put the basil, remaining parsley, yoghurt, and remaining half of your Parmesan into a blender and whizz together to make a green, drizzly sauce. Add a squeeze of lemon juice and season with salt. Add a splash of water if it's too thick.

Remove the stalks from the cavolo nero and tear into manageable pieces. Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Add a shot of oil and then your meatballs. Cook for 10-15 mins, rolling around the pan, until browned and cooked through. Whip them out the pan, crank up the heat and drop in the cavolo nero. Cook for 3-4 mins until browned and wilted.

Cut the remaining lemon into wedges. Heat the quinoa following pack instructions and divide between bowls. Top with a few meatballs, the cavolo nero and a drizzle of basil sauce. Serve with the lemon wedges and a good crack of black pepper.

name: Healthy Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: In less time than it takes to visit your local shop and pick up a packet of ultra-processed cookies, you could be enjoying our amazing healthy alternative.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Roughly chop the pecans and chop the dark chocolate into chunks.
In a bowl, mix together the milled flax and water then set aside.
In a separate bowl, combine the brown sugar and olive oil. Add in the flax mixture and give it a good stir.
Fold in the ground almonds. Sprinkle in the chocolate chunks, pecans and a pinch of sea salt and fold again.
Roll the cookie dough into equal balls and flatten with your palm (it helps to wet your hands slightly) then pop in the oven for around 10 mins.
Leave to cool and then enjoy!

name: Healthy Chocolate Spread
description: Making this nutty chocolate spread is incredibly easy, and even without the usual palm oils and unwanted additives, it will last in the fridge for a full 2 weeks. Spread it on sourdough or use it as a dip for apples and other fruits.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan/350°F and line a baking tray with baking parchment.

Lay the hazelnuts and sunflower seeds on the tray in a single layer and toast in the. oven for 8-10 mins. Check continuously as oven temperatures vary and nuts burn quickly. You want the nuts and seeds to be golden.
Put the chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, making sure the bowl does not touch the water. Stir until melted.

When the nuts are ready, transfer to a food processor or high-powered blender and blitz continuously for 6-8 mins (scraping down the sides when necessary) until smooth – the mixture will resemble nut butter.
Add the melted chocolate and maple syrup and blitz once more to combine. Spread on toast, or transfer to a jar and use within 2 weeks.

name: Healthy Fruity Flapjacks
description: These healthy flapjacks are packed with oats, peanut butter and banana, naturally sweetened and perfect for kids and adults alike. Great for lunchboxes, after-school snacks or whenever you need a quick, nutritious sweet hit.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Line a small baking tray with baking parchment.
Peel and mash the bananas in a large bowl using a fork. Grate in the apple (skin and all), then add the nut butter, maple syrup, oats and cinnamon. Stir together to combine.
Scrape the flapjack mixture into your lined tin, pressing it down into a compact even layer.
Bake in the centre of the oven for 15-18 mins until the top is nicely golden. Leave to cool completely.

Once the flapjacks are cold, snap the dark chocolate into a heatproof bowl and melt over a pan of barely simmering water (or in the microwave on high in 30-second blasts). Once melted, smooth on top of the flapjacks and leave to set – put into the fridge if your patience is testing you.
Once the chocolate is set, cut into 10 rectangles to serve.

name: Healthy Green Queen Pasta
description: Nurture your insides and glow on the outside with this easy green pasta with hidden legumes in the sauce! Great for kids and those who aren’t fans of the texture of beans.
instructions: Cook the pasta in plenty of well-salted boiling water for 1 min less than the pack states. Drain, reserving the cooking water.

Finely chop the shallot and crush the garlic. Add the onion to a wide frying pan set over a low-medium heat, season with salt and sauté for 10 mins, until trasnluscent. Add the garlic and fry for 2 mins.

Fill a kettle and boil. Add the spinach and basil into a strainer and pour the boiling water over until wilted. Let cool down slightly and squeeze out any excess water. Add both to a blender with the onion and garlic, beans, lemon juice, nutritional yeast and pasta water, season generously, then blend until super smooth. Add more pasta water if you'd like it runnier. Season with more salt and pepper, if needed.
To serve, combine the pasta and sauce, then top with vegan burrata. Finish with some freshly cracked black pepper.

name: Healthy Herby Courgette Fritters
description: One of the best ways to nourish your gut microbiome is to eat a wide range of plants and these courgette fritters are an easy, delicious way to do that. We’ve served them with a probiotic-rich tahini yoghurt dipping sauce.
instructions: Grate the courgettes and get them in a sieve over a bowl with a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Thinly slice the spring onion, chilli, basil and parsley.
Squeeze out the liquid from the courgettes and add to a mixing bowl, along with the herbs, chilli and spring onion.

Sprinkle the chickpea flour in with the courgettes, a couple of tablespoons at a time, and mix together until it forms a thick, spoonable batter (you might need slightly more or less than listed depending on how watery the veg is).
Combine the dipping sauce ingredients in a bowl and season with salt.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and then add a spoonful of the courgette batter, flattening it slightly with a spoon.
Fry for a couple of minutes on each side until crisp and golden. Serve with the dipping sauce.

name: Healthy Kid-Friendly Granola
description: Crispy, crunchy granola with gentle cinnamon warmth and no nasties - just the good stuff. This is the perfect batch brekkie that kids and grown-ups will both love.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kid Servings
Heat the oven to 160°C.

Grab the biggest mixing bowl you’ve got and chuck in the rolled oats, mixed seeds, chopped nuts, flaxseed and chia seeds. Add the cinnamon and ginger — they just give a gentle warmth and natural sweetness, nothing spicy.

Carefully separate the egg yolks from the whites (you can use the yolks to make mayonaise, dressings). Melt the coconut oil in a small saucepan over a low heat. Pour it into the bowl with the apple juice, honey or maple syrup and egg whites. Give everything a really good mix so it’s evenly coated.

Line a large baking tray (or two smaller ones) with baking paper. Spread out the granola in an even layer and bake for 30–40 mins, giving it a stir every 10 mins until golden and crisp. Leave to cool completely.
Once cool, stir through the raisins and tip into airtight jars or containers.

Serve up!
Kids & Parents Plate: Dish out the granola into bowls with cold milk, spooned over yoghurt, or on top of pancakes, whatever works for your crew.

name: Healthy No-Bake Millionaire’s Shortbread
description: Millionaire's shortbread, but made with good stuff - sticky dates, creamy nut butter and a crunchy buckwheat base. What’s not to love?
instructions: Get the dates for the caramel into a bowl and cover with boiling water. Leave to soak for 20 mins, then drain.
For the base, add the buckwheat, dates, melted coconut oil and almond butter to a food processor. Blitz until you have a finely textured crumb.
Line a tray roughly 18cm x 24cm with baking paper, then press the base mixture in evenly using the back of a spoon. Firm it down well.

For the caramel, add the soaked dates, almond butter, water, maca powder (if using) and salt into a high-speed blender. Blitz until completely smooth then spoon the caramel over the base and spread it out evenly.

Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil on a low heat in the microwave or in heat-proof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water. Once melted, pour over the caramel layer and tip the tray side to side so the chocolate can flood the empty spaces.
Chill or freeze until set. If freezing, remove from the freezer and sit on the side for a couple of minutes before slicing. Use a warm knife to slice into bars for clean edges.

name: Healthy Plant-Based Katsu Curry
description: We’ve reduced waste with this katsu curry sauce by blending the ingredients together rather than straining them out. Perfect with veggie goujons or your fave breaded protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Start by prepping the ingredients for the curry sauce. Dice the carrots into 1cm pieces, peel and chop the onion, roughly chop the garlic and ginger. There's no need to peel the carrots or the ginger!

Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a large pot over medium heat, and add the carrots and onions. Fry for 10 mins until the veg is softened, then add your garlic and ginger. Fry for 2 mins until aromatic, before adding the curry powder and chilli powder. Cook for 30 sec. If the pan is looking a bit ‘dusty’ add a little splash of oil, as you will be adding the flour next.

Add the flour and cook out for 1 min. At this point, there will be dark bits stuck to the bottom of the pan but don't worry - it's all flavour! Gradually add in your vegetable stock, whisking continuously so there are no lumps, and scrape off all the tasty bits on the bottom of the pan. Add soy sauce and sugar, then simmer for 10 mins. Blend smooth and loosen if needed.

To make your quick pickles, peel the carrot and chop it into thin matchsticks. Cut the cucumber and radish into thin matchsticks. Add all of the veg into a bowl and season with rice vinegar, toasted sesame seeds, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Cook your rice according to package instructions and pop the veggie goujons (for flexitarians, fish fingers or chicken goujons would also work well instead) in the oven for 6 mins.
Slice the goujons and serve with katsu sauce, rice and quick pickles.

name: Healthy Snickers Balls
description: Got a sweet tooth? Make up a batch of these Snickers-inspired date and peanut butter balls. They're the perfect healthy snack.
instructions: Add the dates, peanut butter, poppy seeds, chocolate and peanuts (not the garnish amounts) to a food processor and blend until you have a fine crumb.
Portion into equal-sized balls and squeeze them tightly so they hold their shape.

Chop the peanuts for the garnish. 
Melt the chocolate and dip each ball into the chocolate to cover. Place on a parchment-lined baking tray and sprinkle with chopped peanuts and sea salt.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

name: Healthyish Chicken Korma
description: Chicken kormas are far from the basic curry house option. Rich with cardamom, cinnamon and almonds, this luxurious honey is fit for a queen. Sophie x
instructions: Chop your chicken breasts into large chunks.
Pop them in a bowl with 150g of your yoghurt, 1 tsp of your ground cardamom and a big pinch of salt. Give it a good mix, then pop in the fridge to marinate for a couple of hours.
Peel and slice your onion. Grate your garlic and ginger.
Heat a glug of oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add your cinnamon stick and onions to the pan, then fry for 10 mins until soft and starting to caramelise.

Add your garlic and ginger and cook out for 2 mins before adding your remaining cardamom, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric, chilli powder and tomato purée. Cook for a minute longer until fragrant.

Turn the heat right down. Tip your yoghurt, ground almonds, 300ml water and your chicken along with its marinade into the pan and bring to a gentle simmer. Add a good pinch of salt and pop the lid on – simmer for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, toast your flaked almonds for a couple of mins in a dry frying pan until golden and fragrant. Chop your coriander.
Once your cooking time is up, add your mango chutney to the korma and season to taste with salt.
Serving time. Spoon your chicken korma over rice and sprinkle with your coriander and flaked almonds. Serve with rice or naan.

name: Hearty Chicken & Sweet Potato Traybake
description: This one-tray chicken and sweet potato stew hits the spot. It’s aromatic, a little bit spicy and a little bit sweet, and couldn’t be easier to make.
keywords: Hearty Chicken & Sweet Potato Traybake recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Chop the sweet potatoes into 3cm chunks. Strip the thyme leaves and discard the stalks. Prick a few holes into the scotch bonnet. Peel the garlic cloves, ginger and onion. Thinly slice the onion. Season the chicken with salt and pepper on both sides and set aside.
Add the thyme leaves, whole garlic and ginger, peanut butter, tomato purée and stock into a blender and blitz until smooth. Set aside.
Add the sweet potatoes and scotch bonnet to a baking tin and spread them out.

Place a frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, put the chicken thighs into the pan, skin-side down, and cook for 8-10 mins until the skin is deep golden brown. Transfer to the baking tin, on top of the sweet potatoes.
Add the onions into the empty frying pan and sweat until translucent. Pour the peanut butter stock in and bring it to the boil.

Once boiling, pour the peanut butter mixture into the chicken tray in an even layer, over the chicken and sweet potatoes. Slide into the oven to roast for 40-45 mins or until the chicken is fully cooked.
Before serving, reheat the brown rice. Taste the peanut sauce and season with salt, pepper and lime juice if needed.
To serve, share the rice between bowls and top with the hearty sweet potato and chicken stew. Serve any remaining lime wedges alongside.

name: Hearty Chicken, Kale & Potato Soup
description: A beautiful low and slow dinner recipe that'll warm up your stomach and soul. The addition of garlicky croutons is an absolute stroke of genius.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Peel and finely slice 2 cloves of garlic and slice the spring onions. Heat a tbsp of the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and spring onions along with a big pinch of salt. Fry for 2 mins, then add the fennel seeds and fry for 30 secs longer. Tip in the stock and bring to the boil.
Chop the potatoes into bite-sized chunks, around 3 cm. Add to the pan, cover with a lid and cook for 5 mins.

Tear the bread into chunks and tip onto a roasting tray. Finely grate the garlic into a small bowl and add the remaining tbsp of olive oil. Pour that garlicky oil over the bread chunks and toss well. Season with salt and roast for 10 mins, until crispy and golden. Set aside.

After the potatoes have been cooking for 10 mins, reduce the heat to a low simmer and lower the chicken thighs into the pan, cover with a lid and cook on super low for 10-15 mins, until cooked through. Remove the chicken with a spoon, then use two forks to roughly shred. Check the potatoes are done, turning the heat back up and boiling them a little longer if they’re still a little firm. Stir through the kale, and cook for 2 mins further, until it’s wilted down. Taste and season, adding the juice of half of the lemon. Stir the chicken back through.
Spoon the soup into bowls, top with the garlicky croutons, a drizzle of olive oil, and a scattering of dill. Serve with the other half of the lemon, cut into wedges on the side.

name: Hearty Greek Salad with Whipped Feta
description: In partnership with Aldi UK. Golden smashed spuds piled high with juicy tomatoes, olives and a punchy feta yoghurt dressing. Crispy, fresh and seriously satisfying. #ad #aldiuk
keywords: crispy smashed potato Greek salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Wash and dry the potatoes, then tip them onto a large baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and rub to coat. Space them out so they’re not touching, then roast for 25 mins.
Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes into chunky pieces. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds with a spoon and thinly slice. Halve the olives, reserving a splash of their brine.
Tip the tomatoes, cucumber and olives into a large bowl. Add a splash of the olive brine and toss together.

Once the potatoes have had 25 mins, take the tray out of the oven. Using the bottom of a glass, press each potato down until about 1cm thick. Drizzle with a little more olive oil and return to the oven for 20–30 mins until golden and crispy.

Zest the lemon into a blender, then squeeze in the juice. Add the feta, yoghurt and oregano, then blitz until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste. If you don’t have a blender, crumble the feta into a bowl, stir through the lemon zest and juice, oregano and yoghurt.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for a couple of minutes until golden.

Once the potatoes are crisp, tip them into the bowl with the veg. Add a glug of olive oil and the toasted sesame seeds, then gently toss everything together. Spread the dressing onto plates and pile the smashed potato salad over the top.

name: Hearty Grilled Apricot Caprese
description: This salad highlights a bunch of gorgeous seasonal produce and makes a filling grilled apricot caprese – a refreshing, fruity twist on a classic.
instructions: Halve and pit the apricots, then chop half of them into wedges. Put a non-stick frying pan or grill pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the apricots cut-side down and grill for 5-6 mins until charred. Set aside.

Meanwhile, strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stalks. Roughly tear the leaves into a large bowl. Zest and juice 1 lemon over the cavolo nero and season with salt. Using your hands, massage the cavolo nero until wilted.
Re-use the same frying pan to toast the pumpkin seeds over a medium-high heat for 2-3 mins. Set aside.
Trim the courgette and use a peeler to shave ribbons into the cavolo nero bowl. Toss together. Trim and finely slice the fennel (use a mandoline if you have one), then add to the greens.
Put 1 grilled apricot into a blender with the remaining lemon juice and 40ml olive oil. Blend until smooth, then taste and season with salt and pepper. Pick the basil leaves.
Drain and rinse the cannellini beans, then add to the salad bowl along with the apricot dressing. Toss together.
Put the basil leaves, pumpkin seeds and 65ml olive oil into the same blender. Blend until a pesto forms. Drain and cut the mozzarella into 1cm slices.
Divide the salad between plates. Arrange the apricots and mozzarella on top, then finish with dollops of pesto.

name: Hearty Grilled Apricot Salad
description: You can’t not have a salad in a summer meal plan! This one is bursting at the seams with fresh vegetables and gorgeous jewel-like apricots.
instructions: Halve and pit the apricots, then chop half into wedges. Place a non-stick frying pan or grill pan onto high heat. Once hot, add the apricots cut side down and grill until charred, 5-6 mins.

Meanwhile, strip the leaves of the cavolo nero from their stalks. Roughly tear the leaves into a large bowl. Zest and juice 1 lemon onto the cav and season with salt. Using your hands, massage the cavolo nero until wilted.
Re-use the same pan as the apricots, to toast the pumpkin seeds on medium-high heat, 2-3 mins.
Trim the courgettes and use a peeler to shave ribbons into the cavolo nero, toss together. Trim and finely slice the fennel, use a mandolin if you have one, add to the greens
Add 1 grilled apricot into a blender with the juice of the rest of the lemons and 40ml of olive oil. Blend until smooth, then taste and season with salt and pepper. Pick the basil leaves.
Drain and rinse the beans, add to the salad bowl along with the toasted pumpkin seeds, and the dressing, toss together.
Re-use the blender and add the basil, pumpkin seeds and 65ml olive oil. Blend until a pesto forms.
Share the salad between your plates. Arrange the apricots on top, and finish with dollops of pesto and yoghurt.

name: Hearty Mushroom and Lentil Ragù
description: This ragù is super satisfying and rich, but completely vegan! Plus, the lentils mean is has some good protein in there too. Winner winner.
keywords: Hearty mushroom and lentil ragù recipes
instructions: Start by placing the dried mushroom into a bowl and covering with 250ml of boiling water. Leave to soak while you do the rest of the prep.
Dice the onion and carrot (or whizz in a processor until finely chopped), it should be small but doesn’t have to be neat.
Place a saucepan over a medium heat, add a generous amount of olive oil (3 tbsp/50ml) and add the onion and carrot with a pinch of salt. Cook for about 8 mins until soft but not browned.
While the onion and carrot cook, finely chop all of the mushrooms.
Empty the contents of the pan into a bowl and wipe out. Place the pan back over a high heat and add the mushrooms and a pinch of salt.
Drain the soaked mushrooms (keep the soaking liquid) and finely chop. Add those to the pan too.
Cook until the mushrooms have released most of their moisture and taken on some colour, you want a nice golden brown.

Add the wine and let it bubble away until almost completely evaporated, then turn down the heat to medium. Return the onion and carrot to the pan along with both tins of lentils (drain them first), the mushroom soaking liquid and a tsp of salt.
Bring the ragù to a simmer and cook for about 15 mins. While the sauce is cooking, put the pasta on to boil in plenty of salted water.
Once the pasta is al dente, drain and combine with the ragù. Finely chop the parsley, add and mix well.
Add 75ml of olive oil to a small pan and place over a medium heat. Pick and add the sage leaves and fry for a couple of mins until crisp
Plate up the pasta, top with a few crunchy sage leaves and a drizzle of the oil they cooked. Add a sprinkle of chilli, if you like.

name: Hearty Niçoise Salad
description: A fresh and filling niçoise salad that's perfect for eating during the summer months. Best enjoyed al fresco.
instructions: Place a pot of water on to boil. Once boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook for 6 mins until jammy. Leave for longer if you want them cooked more. Drain and run cold water over the eggs until cooled down, or transfer them to an ice bath. Peel and half once cool.
Meanwhile, drain the tuna and butter beans. Chop the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks and season with salt.

For the dressing, finely dice the shallot, then strip the oregano leaves from the stems and mince. Add both to a small bowl with the juice of the lemon and mix. Let it sit for a couple of minutes before stirring the mustard and vinegar through. Slowly whisk in the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Toss the tuna, beans, olives, greens and tomatoes together with the dressing. Share between bowls and top each with two egg halves.

name: Hearty Peanut Stew With Crispy Okra
description: Hearty and comforting vegetarian peanut stew inspired by Senegalese Mafé. This west African peanut stew recipe is flavoured with scotch bonnet, garlic, ginger and thyme.
keywords: Hearty Peanut Stew With Crispy Okra
instructions: Trim and thinly slice the okra. Chop the sweet potatoes into 1cm cubes. Drain and finely mince the roasted peppers. Peel the garlic, onion and ginger. Thinly slice the garlic and onion and finely grate the ginger. Discard the scotch bonnet stem, then thinly slice (if you prefer a milder dish, see notes).
Place a frying pan over medium-high heat with a generous drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the okra and fry in batches for 3-4 mins until golden-brown. Transfer to a bowl.

Add the onion to the same pan and stir-fry for 3-4 mins until softened. Stir through the thyme sprigs, garlic, ginger and ¾ of the scotch bonnet, then fry until fragrant. Add the sweet potato and peppers, then mix through the tomato purée and peanut butter. Cook, stirring, for 3-4 mins until the paste darkens.

Pour the vegetable stock, stir and bring to the boil. Once boiling, turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 15-20 mins until the sweet potato has softened, the stew has thickened and the oil has separated. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Share the rice between bowls and top with the stew. Sprinkle over the okra before tucking in.

name: Hearty Sausage & Pepper Bean Stew
description: Sometimes a big bowl of stew is the only thing you want as the weather gets colder. With sausages and tonnes of beans, this one makes for a great crowd pleasing family meal.
instructions: Remove the sausages from their skins and break them into small, roughly 2cm chunks. Finely chop the onion, carrot and courgette, and cut the peppers into bite-sized pieces. Finely chop the garlic.

Set a deep frying pan or large saucepan over a medium-high heat with a good glug of olive oil. Add the sausage pieces and fry for 3-4 mins, tossing regularly until golden all over. Scoop out onto a plate and set aside.

Tip the onion, carrot, courgette and peppers into the same pan with another drizzle of oil, if needed. Season with a small pinch of salt and cook for 8-10 mins until softened and starting to caramelise.

Stir in the tomato purée and garlic. Cook for 2 mins until fragrant. Pour in the tinned tomatoes, drained beans and water, then add the sausages back into the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 30 mins, stirring occasionally, until the stew is thickened and rich.
Taste and season with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Serve up!Kids Plate:  Spoon into bowls for the kids. Parents Plate: Top with parsley leaves, a few slices of red chilli and a spoonful of yoghurt. Serve with toast on the side.

name: Herb & Halloumi Salad
description: Every salad should have crispy chunks of halloumi in it. That's a fact.
instructions: Place a baking tray in the oven and preheat the oven to 200°C.
Tear the halloumi and flatbreads into 2cm chunks. Transfer both to a bowl with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Toss together, and transfer to the hot baking tray. Roast until golden for 20-25 mins.
Meanwhile, pick the dill, mint, and parsley leaves. Finely slice the dill and parsley stalks. Add the herbs into a bowl of ice water. Trim and thinly slice the sugar snaps.

Finely dice the shallot, place into a small bowl or jar with the lemon juice. Stir the honey and mustard through and whisk the olive oil a little at a time until incorporated (if using a jar, add all the ingredients in, close and shake until emulsified). Season the dressing to taste with salt and pepper.
Drain the herbs and toss the sugar snaps, walnuts, and chickpeas through with ¾ of the dressing.
Share the salad between bowls with the croutons and halloumi. Drizzle over the remaining dressing.

name: Herb Crusted Cod With Creamy Beans & Watercress Pesto
description: A fresh and vibrant dish that's full of lean, mean protein. A healthy meal that's perfect for a quick midweek dinner.
keywords: Herb Crusted Cod With Creamy Beans & Watercress Pesto
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Blitz pitta into breadcrumbs, then heat 1 tbsp oil in a small frying pan. Add the breadcrumbs and toast until crisp. Finely chop the parsley and zest the lemon. Mix half of the parsley and the zest of 1 lemon through the breadcrumbs and season with salt and pepper.

Start making the pesto. Finely chop the watercress and smoked almonds before grating one clove of garlic. Combine with the zest and juice of the zested lemon and mix together with 6 tbsp olive oil until it’s all combined but still a bit chunky. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Alternatively, you can use a pestle and mortar.

Take your cod fillets and place on a foil-lined baking tray. Scatter the breadcrumbs over the fish and pack it down evenly to create a crust. Transfer the tray to the oven and cook fish for 12-15 min, until the fish is cooked through.

For the beans, roughly chop 3 garlic cloves. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan over a medium-low heat and add the garlic, cook for around 2 min. Chuck in your beans along with the liquid from the cans – then simmer for around 5-10 mins, until thickened. Stir through the yoghurt, remaining parsley and juice of 1 lemon. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve the creamy beans drizzled with pesto and topped with the cod.
