name: Herb Crusted Fennel With Creamy Beans & Watercress Pesto
description: If you're not a fan of fennel, you will be after you've tried this recipe. The simple homemade pesto is the pièce de résistance.
keywords: Herb Crusted Fennel With Creamy Beans & Watercress Pesto
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Blitz pitta into breadcrumbs, then heat 1 tbsp oil in a small frying pan. Add the breadcrumbs and toast until crisp. Finely chop the parsley and zest the lemon. Mix half of the parsley and zest of a lemon through the breadcrumbs and season with salt and pepper.

Start making the pesto. Finely chop the watercress and smoked almonds before grating one clove of garlic. Combine with the zest and juice of 1 lemon and mix together with 6 tbsp olive oil until it’s all combined but still a bit chunky. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Alternatively, you can use a pestle and mortar.

Take your fennel and cut each bulb in half. Place them on a foil-lined baking tray. Roast for 20 mins, then scatter the breadcrumbs over the cut side of the fennel and pack it down evenly to create a crust. Roast for another 15-20 mins, until the fennel is tender.

For the beans, roughly chop 3 garlic cloves. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan over a medium-low heat and add the garlic, cook for around 2 min. Chuck in your beans along with the liquid from the cans- then simmer for around 5-10 mins, until thickened. Stir through the yoghurt with the remaining parsley, half of the pesto and the juice of 1 lemon. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve the creamy beans drizzled with the remaining pesto and topped with the crusted fennel.

name: Herb-Crusted Chateaubriand
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Perfectly tender pink beef with a bright green herby crust. A seriously impressive (and surprisingly easy) showstopper for your festive dinner party or Sunday lunch.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Rub the wagyu chateaubriand with a glug of olive oil and season with a little salt and pepper.
Heat a large frying pan over a high heat until searingly hot, then add the beef and cook on all sides for 3-4 mins, until well browned.

Move the beef to a small roasting tray then slide it into the oven. Cook for 18 mins for rare, or use a meat thermometer to check; you want the middle of the meat to be around 51-55°C. Remove from the oven and set aside to rest for 10-15 mins.

While the beef rests, remove the leaves from the rosemary and thyme and add them to a blender, along with the peppercorns, breadcrumbs and a pinch of salt. Blitz until you have a bright green breadcrumb mixture.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the breadcrumbs and toast for 2-3 mins, until crisp. Be careful not to take them too far – you want them to remain bright green! Tip them onto a plate or tray.
When the beef has rested, use kitchen roll to pat it dry, then use a brush or spoon to brush the beef with the mustard.
Just before you’re ready to serve, roll the beef in the bright green breadcrumbs. Use a spoon to press more of the crumbs around the sides to make sure you have a nice even crust.
Slice and serve alongside all your favourite festive or sunday roast sides.

name: Herby 'Chicken' Orzo with Harissa Tomatoes
description: This is a one tray number, packed with flavour with minimum effort.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Mix the harissa with the olive oil and the zest of the lemon. Marinate the vegan chicken pieces and set aside.
Mince the garlic and slice the sun-dried tomatoes.
Boil the water for the stock and add two stock cubes.
Mix the orzo, sun-dried tomatoes and cherry tomatoes with the stock and minced garlic in a deep baking tray and cover tightly with foil. Bake at 180°C for 15 mins.
After 15 mins, remove the orzo and stir through the spinach. Place the chicken on top of the orzo. And drizzle the whole tray with some olive oil.
Bake, uncovered for the last 15 mins or until cooked through.
To serve, drizzle some vegan greek yoghurt, a squeeze of lemon juice and some parsley over the top.

name: Herby Brothy Pasta Soup with Halloumi
description: Move over Parmesan, grated halloumi is having its day. We've grated halloumi over this steaming, nourishing bowl of pasta soup to add flavour and boost the protein. It's perfect with the lemony herby broth and sumac drizzle.
instructions: Finely dice the onion and thinly slice the fresh dill, parsley and coriander, stalks and all.

Melt the butter in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4-5 mins until softened and translucent. Then add the herbs and dried mint and stir until wilted (this will be very quick).
Pour over the stock and let the mixture come to the boil. Drop in the pasta and cook following packet instructions.

Meanwhile, make the drizzle. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the nigella and sesame seeds and cook until toasted, then tip into a bowl and stir through the sumac. Set aside.
Once the pasta has finished cooking, give the soup a stir and season with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Serve into bowls and grate over some fresh halloumi. Finish with a drizzle of the nigella mixture.

name: Herby Chicken & Courgette Tacos
description: Jazz up leftovers from our Roast Chicken with Schmaltzy Courgettes batch with these banging tacos. Loaded with salsa, jalapeños, feta and crème fraîche.
cuisine: Italian, Italian-Inspired, Mediterranean, Mediterranean-Inspired, Mexican, Mexican-Inspired
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken with Schmaltzy Courgettes.
Shred the chicken with two forks. If cold, warm it with the courgettes in a frying pan set over a low heat until hot. Season with salt and black pepper.
Crumble the feta and thinly slice the jalapeño.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan for 30 seconds on each side until soft and flexible.
Spoon the chicken and courgette mixture onto each tortilla. Top with the tomato salsa, a dollop of crème fraîche, crumbled feta and some sliced jalapeño.

name: Herby Chicken & Courgette With Brothy Rice
description: This is comfort in a bowl. Lemony broth and soft rice elevate our Roast Chicken with Schmaltzy Courgettes leftovers. It's giving Avgolemono energy, but with no eggs involved.
keywords: Herby Chicken & Courgette With Brothy Rice
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken with Schmaltzy Courgettes.
Bring the chicken stock to the boil in a large saucepan. Add the rice and cook, stirring, for 10-12 mins until soft.
Meanwhile, shred the leftover chicken and finely chop the dill and parsley.
Once the rice is cooked, stir in the chicken and courgettes. Simmer for another 2-3 mins until everything is piping hot.
Squeeze in as much lemon juice as you like, then stir through the chopped herbs. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle over a little olive oil and serve with a wedge of lemon.

name: Herby Chicken Caesar Schnitzel
description: What happens when you cross a chicken schnitzel with a Caesar salad? Magic.
instructions: Lay out a piece of baking parchment or cling film on your work surface. Put 1 chicken breast on top, cover with another piece of baking parchment or cling film and then bash the chicken with a rolling pin until it’s around 3mm thick. Repeat with the remaining chicken breasts.

Tip the plain flour onto a baking tray and season with salt and pepper. Crack the eggs onto another tray and whisk, then season with salt and pepper. Finally, tip the breadcrumbs onto another tray and season them, too.
Dip the chicken breasts one at a time into the flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs so that they are totally coated. Pop them in the fridge until you are ready to fry.

Add around 1cm oil to a large frying pan, then bring it up to temperature over a medium heat. It needs to be around 170°C. Carefully pop the chicken breasts into the pan, two at a time, and fry for about 3-5 mins each side, basting as they cook, until the chicken is crisp and golden. Remove from the pan and drain on a rack lined with kitchen paper.

For the salad, slice the romaine, then finely slice the cornichons and jalapeño (remove the seeds if it’s particularly spicy). Transfer everything to a large bowl. Chop the parsley and add to the bowl, then finely chop the chives and set them aside.
Put the mayo, anchovies, garlic and the juice of the lemon into a blender. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt and a generous grinding of black pepper.
When you’re ready to serve, toss the salad with the dressing. Serve the schnitzel on plates, top with the salad, then finish with a good grating of Parmesan and the chives.

name: Herby Chicken Caesar Smacos
description: I combined two of Mob's most popular dishes smashed chicken tacos and our ceasar salad to make these herby chicken caesar tacos, I call them smacos - the office went wild for them and I think you probably will too.
instructions: Start by making the dressing. Peel the garlic clove. Add the mayo, anchovies, garlic, the Parmesan for the dressing, the parsley for the dressing and the juice of the lemon to a blender. Blitz until smooth, then season with black pepper and set aside.
Slice the romaine and add to a large bowl with the parsley for serving and the croutons. Set aside.

Add the chicken mince to a bowl with the dried oregano, season with salt and pepper and mix well with your hands. Smoosh around a tablespoon of the mince mixture onto each tortilla, spreading it right to the edges.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the tortillas mince-side down and fry for 4-6 mins until golden and cooked through, then flip and cook for a further minute.
Dress the salad with the Caesar dressing and toss to coat. Serve the smacos topped with the salad and a scatter of the remaining Parmesan.

name: Herby Chicken Mushroom Orzo
description: This creamy one-pot orzo is packed with chicken and mushrooms, finished with fresh herbs and parmesan. An absolute belter of a dish.
instructions: Prep your veg. Finely dice your onion, slice your mushrooms and finely chop your garlic, rosemary, thyme and parsley.
Chop your chicken into thin slices.
Melt your butter in a large saute pan over a medium-high heat. Add your chicken and cook for a few minutes until golden and just tender. Remove from the pan.
Turn the heat down and, to the same pan, add your onion and cook it for 10 minutes until it is totally softened. Tip in your garlic, rosemary and thyme and cook out for a minute.

Tip all your mushrooms into the pan and whack up the heat. Fry off for a couple of minutes until they have released their liquid, reduced and started to caramelise. Pour your wine into the pan to deglaze it, and let it all evaporate.

Add your orzo to the pan along with your chicken and hot chicken stock. Give it a good stir, then bring it to a simmer. Turn down your heat to medium-low and cook for 8 minutes, by which time your orzo should still be tender but maintain a slight bite.
Add your creme fraiche and parmesan to the pan along with most of your parsley and a good sprinkle of salt and pepper.
Serve in bowls sprinkled with more parsley and a little more parmesan, if you like.

name: Herby Chicken, Pepper & Quinoa Salad
description: Healthy lunch meal prep made easy with this high-protein chicken quinoa salad. It's fresh, tasty, and will keep you satiated throughout the day. What's not to love?
instructions: Thinly slice the roasted peppers. Peel and finely slice the onion, then rinse it under cold water in a sieve until crisp. Pick the mint leaves. Toss the sliced onion, peppers, and mint together in a bowl with the balsamic vinegar and olive oil. Season well with salt and black pepper.

Rinse the quinoa under cold water until it runs clear. Tip into a saucepan with water and a good pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 15–20 mins, or until all the water is absorbed. Remove from the heat and let it steam with the lid on for 5 mins. Fluff with a fork.

Make the Zhoug dressing. Lightly crack the cardamom pods open using the back of your knife. Add the coriander seeds, cumin seeds and crushed cardamom pods into a small frying pan. Place on medium heat and toast until fragrant, 2-3 mins.
Remove the cardamom seeds and discard the pod.

Add the spices into a food processor or blender and blitz until they have broken down slightly (don’t let them become a fine powder). Trim the chillies and add them to the spices with the garlic clove, herbs (stems and all). Blend until broken down, then gradually add the olive oil, until emulsified. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Place the chicken thighs in a bowl. Finely grate over the garlic, add the Dijon mustard and lemon juice, and season with salt and loads of black pepper. Mix well to coat. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken for 10–15 mins, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through. Rest for 5 mins, then slice.
Divide the quinoa between your containers. Top with sliced chicken and spoon over the pepper and mint salad. Serve with a pot of Zhoug dressing on the side.

name: Herby Chickpea Pancake With Strawberry Harissa Jam
description: Chickpea flour comes to life with a load of fresh herbs, transforming into a delicious savoury pancake. Complimented with a moorish strawberry harissa jam.
instructions: First, make the strawberry harissa jam. Chop up the strawberries into small pieces and add to a saucepan. Add the sugar and cook on medium heat for 15-20 mins or until the strawberries have broken down and the liquid has reduced. Add the harissa and season with salt and pepper. Taste and add more harissa if you like.
Meanwhile, weigh out the flour and whisk 450ml water in slowly to make sure it's smooth with no lumps, then whisk through the olive oil, salt and pepper. Set aside.
Finely chop the herbs or pulse in a food processor until chopped.
Use a 20cm non-stick frying pan to make a single pancake or a larger one and use the whole mix to serve 2.

Heat the pan on high, add some olive oil and, once it's hot, pour in the mix and turn the heat down to medium. Let it cook for about 10 mins until the top has started to set. Then cover with a plate or a lid and cook for another 5 mins, or until the top has set enough to flip it over. (You can check this by touching the middle gently). Use the lid to carefully flip it over and cook for another 2 mins to brown the other side.

Serve immediately with a generous helping of cream cheese and jam, topped with pine nuts and some extra herbs and maybe another drizzle of harissa if you like. The jam will keep for 4 days sealed in a jar in the fridge.

name: Herby Courgette Fritters
description: These easy courgette fritters are a great way to use up leftover herbs lurking in the fridge. Served with a delicious tahini mayo.
instructions: Grate the courgettes into a colander, mix with a large pinch of salt and squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
Finely chop the basil and parsley and add to a large bowl along with the courgette, eggs, flour, cumin, a large pinch of salt and plenty of black pepper. Mix well and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the mayo with the tahini, a squeeze of lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Add three tablespoons of olive oil to a frying pan and place over a medium heat. Once the oil is shimmering, add a large spoonful of the mix into the pan and flatten slightly.
Fry for about 2 mins, then flip and repeat, until both sides are golden brown.
Transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper to cool for a minute, and then plate up.
Sprinkle with a pinch of chilli and some flaky salt and serve up along with the tahini mayo.

name: Herby Courgette and Halloumi Fritters
description: These crispy courgette fritters are a total game changer. It's a great way of using up wilting herbs you have in the fridge to give them a new lease of life.
instructions: Coarsely grate your courgette, then place in a bowl and sprinkle over a good pinch of salt. Leave for 20 minutes to draw out the moisture, then squeeze out the excess liquid through a sieve in the sink.
Coarsely grate your halloumi and roughly chop your parsley and dill.

In a large bowl, add your courgette, halloumi, chopped parsley and dill, gram flour, baking powder, egg, chilli powder and a pinch of salt. Stir to combine with a wooden spoon until you have a very thick batter.

In a large frying pan, heat a really good glug of vegetable oil over a medium heat. Take a scoop of your batter with a metal spoon and help to shape it with a second spoon - it should be shaped like a small rugby ball.
Gently lower into the oil and fry for a few minutes on each side until crisp and golden, turning to ensure the fritters cook evenly and all the way through.
Serve with some tzatziki whilst still hot and crisp.

name: Herby Couscous & Chickpea Salad With Creamy Tahini Dressing
description: Chickpeas and giant couscous tossed with fresh parsley, roasted peppers and onions finished with creamy tahini dressing and salty feta. Yes, please.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.

Take the top off the peppers, remove the stem and chop into 2cm cubes. Peel and cut each red onion into 8 wedges. Add them onto a baking tray with 2 tbsp of olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Roast the veggies for 25-30 mins until softened and starting to char in places.
Meanwhile, add the giant couscous to a sieve and give it a rinse. Cook the giant couscous per package instructions, then drain and wash under cold water until cold to the touch.

While the couscous cooks, drain the chickpeas and transfer to a bowl. Chop the tomatoes into 1cm cubes and add to the bowl. Zest 1 of the lemons and add to the bowl, finely chop the parsley leaves and stalks and add them as well.

To make the tahini dressing, add the tahini and the juice of both lemons. Whisk in water, 1 tbsp of water at a time, to loosen. Season with salt, pepper and sugar (if needed). Tip into the chickpea bowl along with the drained giant couscous. Set aside.
Once the veggies are roasted, toss them through the couscous and chickpea salad along with the watercress.
Share into plates or spoon onto a platter and finish with a scattering of feta and flaked almonds.

name: Herby Curried Chicken Noodle Salad
description: Transform leftovers from our Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken into a fresh noodle salad with zingy herbs and lime. It’s light, speedy and full of flavour.
instructions: Make the Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken batch recipe.
Cook the rice noodles according to packet instructions, then rinse under cold water to cool and stop the cooking. Drain well and set aside.

Use two forks to shred the leftover chicken. Scoop out a spoonful or two of the coconut sauce to mix through the salad. Pick the mint leaves and discard the stems. Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the stems.
Toss the cooled noodles with the shredded chicken and coconut sauce, mint, coriander, and a generous squeeze of lime juice. Season with salt and black pepper. Give everything a final toss to coat.
Divide between bowls and tuck in.

name: Herby Curried Chickpeas With Curry Leaf Tarka
description: Here, herbs and spices reign supreme, making this a really easy, high reward recipe. We're talking herby chickpeas topped with a curry leaf tarka. Tuck in.
instructions: Toast 1 tsp cumin seeds and ½ tsp coriander seeds in a dry pan, then grind using a pestle and mortar.

Roughly chop then blitz the onion, garlic, ginger and chilli in a high speed blender. Heat 3 tbsp of oil in a pot and fry the onion purée with a pinch of salt for about 5-7 mins. Add the ground spices and fry for 1 min. Look for when it starts to come together.

In the meantime, put half of your spinach in a colander and pour over boiling water until wilted. Rinse in cold water and give it a squeeze to remove the moisture (it doesn’t look like much but it adds lots of colour and balances the flavours out). Add everything to a high speed blender with most of the coriander and most of the coconut milk, saving some of both for serving.
Drain the chickpeas and add to the pan, followed by the herby coconut milk. Season generously with salt, bring to a gentle simmer and bubble away for a couple of mins.
Blend about a ¼ of the chickpea mixture until smooth, then return it to the pan along with the remaining spinach. Cook down until the spinach has wilted.

Whilst the chickpeas are bubbling, finely slice the garlic, pick the curry leaves off the stems and deseed and finely chop the chilli. Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a frying pan and add the curry leaves, 1 tbsp cumin seeds, 1 tbsp mustard seeds, finely sliced garlic and a finely diced red chilli to the oil. Cook for 1-2 mins, until the seeds are popping, then take off the heat and transfer to a heatproof dish.
Squeeze the lemon juice into the chickpeas and mix well. Serve in bowls, topped with the curry leaf oil and a scattering of coriander leaves.

name: Herby Feta Scrambled Eggs
description: This is an incredibly simple, fresh twist on scrambled eggs that uses one of our favourite ingredients: feta. It's a winner.
instructions:
Place a non-stick frying pan over a medium-low heat and add the
butter. Thinly slice the garlic, add to the pan and cook gently for
about 2 minutes until softened but not browned.
Meanwhile, finely chop all of the herbs and set aside.
Lightly beat the eggs in a bowl and stir in three-quarters of the
herbs. Pour into the pan and crumble in three-quarters of the feta.
Cook gently while stirring all the time until the mixture is just set –
you want soft, silky curds.
Plate up, or pop straight on top of some toast. Finish with the
remaining herbs and feta, the smoked paprika and a good drizzle of
olive oil.

name: Herby Freekeh
description: A nutty and delicious freekeh lunch box base that you can load up with all of your favourite ingredients.
instructions: Pour the water into a saucepan and bring to the boil. Stir through the freekeh, then put a lid on the saucepan and turn the heat down to low-medium. Simmer for 10-15 mins until the freekeh is cooked and has absorbed all the water.
Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley and zest the lemon. Once the freekeh has cooked and cooled a little, stir through both.

name: Herby Grains & Whipped Feta Salad with Jammy Eggs
description: I always have herbs lying around, and stirring them through grains is the best way to make a quick, satiating lunch - a little like tabbouleh, but heavier on the grains. The preserved lemon adds another layer of lemony depth. Seriously easy, high in protein and actually good for you.
keywords: Herby Grains & Whipped Feta Salad recipe
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil.
Add the feta and cottage cheese to a food processor and whizz together until smooth and fluffy. Zest in the lemon, then taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed. Set aside.
Reheat the grains, then set aside to cool. Meanwhile, squish or halve the olives. Finely mince the herbs and preserved lemon.
Once the water is boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook for 7 mins until jammy, or until your desired doneness. Peel and halve the eggs.
Once the grains have cooled down a little, toss with the olives, cooked lentils, preserved lemon, herbs and a generous glug of olive oil. Season with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Spread the whipped feta onto the base of your plate or box, top with the herby grain salad and eggs.

name: Herby Green Rice Shakshuka
description: This bright green herby shakshuka is packed with parsley and spinach before being topped with toasted pumpkin seeds. Delicious.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Finely dice half the onion, then finely slice the rest. Blitz together the garlic and cooled stock along with half of the spinach and most of the parsley (save some for garnish).

Heat a splash of oil in a heavy bottomed, ovenproof pan with a lid, then add the diced onion. Cook gently for 2 mins. Add the fennel and cook for 30 seconds. Add the rice along with the green stock and remaining spinach. Bring to a simmer, then pop a lid on. Slide into the oven for 15 mins.
Pop the sliced onion into a small bowl along with the juice of half a lemon (save the rest for serving). Season with salt and scrunch with your hands.

Remove the pan from the oven and make eight divots to crack the eggs into. Crack the eggs in and pop back in the oven for 5-10 mins, checking to see when the eggs are set. After 10 mins, if you want them more set, remove the pan from the oven and set aside with the lid on for a couple of minutes until done to your liking. Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry frying pan.
Top with yoghurt, the remaining parsley, pickled onions and pumpkin seeds.

name: Herby Green Soup with Tahini & Za'atar
description: A fresh and satisfying soup with cannellini beans, fresh herbs, lemon and za’atar. Ready in just 15 minutes, this one’s perfect for a quick plant-based lunch.
keywords: Herby Green Soup with Tahini & Za'atar
Herby Green Soup with Tahini & Za'atar recipe
instructions: Drain the cannellini beans.

Add ⅔ of the drained beans to a high speed blender along with the spinach, tahini, dill, parsley, cumin, mustard, stock cube and water. Blend until smooth then transfer to a saucepan. This is your soup base.
Add the remaining drained beans to the soup. Bring the soup to a simmer over a medium heat then cook for 5-10 mins.
Stir through a good glug of olive oil and the juice of ¾ the lemons, then season to taste with plenty of salt and pepper.

To serve, ladle the soup into bowls and top with a drizzle of za’atar and an extra drizzle of tahini and olive oil. Finish with a pinch of salt and pepper, and the zest and juice of the remaining lemon.

name: Herby Grilled Halloumi with Cherry Salsa
description: Tangy cherry salsa meets salty golden halloumi in this super fresh herb-packed summer plate. It’s bold, bright and ridiculously moreish.
keywords: herby grilled halloumi with cherry salsa
instructions: Split the halloumi along its natural crease, then chop into 2cm cubes. If using fresh cherries, halve and pit them. Set aside.
Pick the mint leaves and place them in a bowl of cold water. Finely chop the parsley and coriander, including the stalks. Quarter the cucumber lengthways, then finely dice.

Add the chopped herbs and cucumber to a bowl and set aside. Add the cherries to a separate bowl. Stir in the pomegranate molasses, sumac and honey. Squeeze in the lemon juice and mix. Taste and adjust with a little more honey if needed – it should be sweet and sour. Set aside.

Pour the water and a splash of olive oil into a saucepan. Set over a medium-high heat and bring to the boil. Once boiling, stir in the bulgur wheat, let it return to the boil, then cover and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 10 mins until the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from the heat and fluff up the bulgur with a fork. Squeeze over the remaining lemon juice and season with salt. Let it cool for a few mins, then stir through the cucumber herb mix.
Set a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, fry the halloumi pieces for 5–7 mins until golden on all sides.

Divide the herby bulgur between plates and top with a dollop of yoghurt, the grilled halloumi, and a generous spoonful of the cherry salsa. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and scatter over the mint leaves.

name: Herby Grilled Salmon Quinoa Bowl
description: Crispy-skinned salmon with lemony quinoa, herby cottage cheese and a crunchy cucumber salad. Fresh, filling and seriously high in protein.
instructions: Finely slice the dill and chives, keeping them separate. Thinly slice the cucumber and red onion. Tip the cucumber into a bowl, season with salt and stir through the vinegar.
Wash the red onion under cold water until crisp. Stir the chives through the cottage cheese and season with salt and black pepper.

Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Once boiling, gently drop in the eggs and cook for 7 mins until jammy — or a little longer if you prefer them firmer. Transfer to a bowl of ice water to cool, then peel.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Once hot, add the salmon skin-side down and cook undisturbed until it’s about three-quarters of the way done. Remove from the heat and flip to finish cooking through.
Reheat the quinoa and stir through the dill. Season with salt and grate in the zest of the lemon. Toss the red onion through the cucumber just before serving.
Divide the quinoa between plates. Top with the crispy salmon, a jammy egg, a dollop of herby cottage cheese and a pile of cucumber salad.

name: Herby Halloumi with Dilly Rice & Tzatziki
description: Golden halloumi, charred courgettes and fragrant buttery rice tossed with dill and toasted orzo. Served with a quick homemade tzatziki for freshness and zing, ideal for meal prep.
keywords: Herby Halloumi Lunchbox with Dilly Rice & Tzatziki
Herby Halloumi Lunchbox with Dilly Rice & Tzatziki recipe
instructions: Rinse the long grain rice under cold water until it runs clear. Pick and roughly chop the fronds of dill, and finely slice the stems. In a saucepan over medium heat, melt salted butter. Add orzo and toast for 3–4 mins until golden. Stir in the rice, pour over water and season with salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce to low. Cook undisturbed for 12 mins. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 mins. Just before serving, fluff with a fork and stir through the dill fronds and stems.

In a spice grinder or pestle and mortar, grind nigella seeds, coriander seeds, Urfa chilli flakes and a pinch of black pepper to a fine powder. Stir the spice blend into honey and set aside. Halve each block of halloumi, then cut each half into 2 triangles. Heat a little olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat and fry the halloumi for 3–5 mins per side until golden. Transfer to a plate and drizzle over the spiced honey. Finish with a grating of lemon zest if you like.

Slice the courgettes into thick 3–4cm coins. Season with salt. Heat a generous amount of olive oil in the frying pan. Once hot, lay the courgettes cut-side down. Cook for 4–5 mins until well charred, then flip and cook for 2–3 mins more. Remove from the heat and let them sit in the pan for 5 mins to finish cooking through.

Make the tzatziki. Halve the cucumber lengthways and scoop out the seeds. Finely dice the flesh. Add to a bowl with yoghurt, grate in garlic, and finely chop the mint. Zest and juice the lemon into the mix, season with salt and pepper, and stir well.
Divide the rice between containers. Top with charred courgettes and halloumi. Serve with a dollop of tzatziki on the side or in a separate pot for freshness.

name: Herby Ham & Egg Cottage Cheese Pot
description: A whipped, lemony chive cottage cheese base layered with baby spinach, salty ham and a jammy boiled egg. High protein and ready in under 20 mins, perfect for a prep-ahead snack.
keywords: Herby Ham & Egg Cottage Cheese Pot
Herby Ham & Egg Cottage Cheese Pot recipe
instructions: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil. Carefully lower in the egg and cook for 7 mins.

While the eggs are cooking, place the cottage cheese in a small blender or mini food processor with the chives and the juice of the lemon. Blitz until smooth and creamy, you want it spreadable but not liquid, and don't over-blitz or the mixture can turn watery. A mini food processor works best here, though a stick blender in a tall jug also does the job. Season well with salt and black pepper, then taste and adjust the lemon if needed.
Once the eggs are ready, transfer to cold water then carefully peel and halve.
Spoon the herby cottage cheese into the base of a jar or pot. Add a layer of baby spinach, then the tear in the ham. Top with the egg halves and finish with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Eat straight away or seal and pop in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Herby Leeks With Chickpeas & Chilli Feta
description: This gorgeous, vibrant green dish from Dr Rupy is a great way to get in some veg. The chilli feta is a real chef's kiss touch.
keywords: Herby Leeks With Chickpeas & Chilli Feta
instructions: Preheat the grill to high.
Slice your leeks into half moons about 2cm thick. Slice your garlic. Separate the stalks and leaves of your green herbs and roughly chop. Roughly chop your baby spinach.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, flameproof, lidded casserole over a medium heat.
Add the leeks, garlic and some seasoning, and cook gently with the lid on for 10 mins, stirring occasionally.
Add the cumin and oregano and cook for a further 2 mins before adding the herb stalks.
Add the spinach in batches and stir into the mixture until wilted (about 5 mins) then add half the herb leaves, reserving the rest for garnish.
Add the chickpeas and toss through the green vegetable mixture. Crumble over the feta and transfer to the grill for a few minutes until the feta is just melted and starting to brown.
To serve, scatter over the remaining fresh herb leaves, add the lemon juice and drizzle over the chilli oil.

name: Herby Melon Salad with Grated Halloumi
description: Grated halloumi that melts into every bite takes this salad to the next level, its salty richness is the perfect combo with juicy melon. It's the ultimate no cook meal.
keywords: Herby Melon Salad with Grated Halloumi
instructions: Zest half the lemon and set aside.

Add the pumpkin seeds, mustard, olive oil and lemon juice into a blender. Blend until creamy and smooth. No blender? Just finely chop the pumpkin seeds and add them into a bowl with the lemon juice, slowly whisk in the olive oil until emulsified. Taste and season with salt, sugar, pepper and sherry vinegar, you can adjust the acidity by adding a little more vinegar or sugar.
Drain and rinse the cannellini beans. Chop the cucumber and melon into bite-sized chunks. Pick the mint and parsley leaves, discarding the stalks.
Chuck all the herbs, cucumber, melon and crutons into a big bowl with the dressing and lemon zest, toss well. Divide between plates, then finely grate the halloumi over the top to finish. Enjoy!

name: Herby Mushroom Stroganoff
description: Luxurious, creamy goodness for the plant-based peeps out there. We’ve veganised this paprika-spiked sauce and loaded it with crispy mushrooms.
instructions: Add your cashews to a small saucepan. Cover with cold water, then bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, finely slice your onions. Finely chop your garlic.
Chop your chestnut mushrooms into quarters, leaving wild ones whole.
Heat a frying pan over a high heat with a little olive oil. Add your mushrooms in batches so as not to overcrowd the pan. Fry for a few mins on each side until a deep golden brown.
Heat a large sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a good glug of olive oil, then tip in your onions. Cook gently for about 25 mins until softened.
Once your cashews have cooled, drain them from their liquid. Add them to a blender along with the water, then blitz to a smooth paste.
Pick your thyme leaves into the pan with the onions along with your garlic and tomato purée. Cook out for 2 mins.
Tip your flour and paprika into the pan, then cook out for 2 mins more.

Pour your veg stock into the pan gradually, beating your mixture to a smooth paste before adding more. Once all your stock is added, bring your mixture to a simmer for 2 mins to thicken. Whilst this is simmering, separately cook your rice according to package instructions.
Add your cashew cream to the pan along with all but a handful of your mushrooms, then bring to mixture to a simmer. Cook for 5 mins to warm the mushrooms through.
Add your Henderson's Relish, Dijon mustard and most of your parsley to the pan. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle over your remaining mushrooms and parsley, then serve with rice.

name: Herby Omelette Tomato Sandwich
description: This is the perfect breakfast or lunch recipe that will set you up for a great day ahead. Give it a go.
instructions: Start by halving the baguette lengthways, drizzling with olive oil and toasting it cut-side down in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat until golden.
Lightly rub the peeled garlic across the toasted surfaces of both sides of the baguette. Half the tomato and rub that over both toasted sides, too. Set aside.
Add the finely chopped herbs to a bowl with the eggs and a pinch of salt. Whisk well.

Return the pan to a medium heat, add a generous drizzle of olive oil and pour in the eggs. Stir vigorously as they cook. After about 1 min, when they are beginning to set but are still loose and custardy, stop stirring.
Grate the cheese over the eggs, then tilt the pan and roll up the omelette from one side.
Pop it into the baguette and add the mayo, if you like. Enjoy!

name: Herby Pancake Soup
description: Herby pancake noodles served in a piping hot beef broth. This soup is really popular in Austria and Southern Germany – try it and you’ll see why. The great thing is, your pancakes don’t have to be perfectly round, since they’re turning into noodles anyway.
instructions: Finely chop the herbs. In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, flour, milk, olive oil (or you can use melted butter if you prefer), herbs and a sprinkle of salt until a thick batter forms.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a non-stick pan set over medium heat. Pour a ladle of batter into the pan, turn the pan a few times to distribute the batter, and fry until golden on both sides (since the pancakes are being rolled up and cut up, they don’t have to be perfect!). Once the pancake is browned on both sides, remove it from the pan using a spatula and allow it to cool on a plate. Repeat this process until all the batter is used.
Roll up each pancake and cut into thin strips. Divide the strips across the bowls.
Heat up the beef stock in a medium-sized pot. Once hot, pour it over the pancake strips and sprinkle with chopped chives.

name: Herby Pea Pancakes
description: Grab those frozen peas from the back of the freezer and make these unbelievably delicious cottage cheese pancakes. We’ve topped ours off with a runny egg, Greek yoghurt, avocado and crispy chilli oil.
instructions: Finely chop the herbs and spring onions and set aside.
Add the cottage cheese and egg to a blender and blitz until smooth. Add in most of the frozen peas and blitz again quickly, avoiding the mixture becoming totally smooth.

Pour the mixture into a bowl and stir through the flour, zest of the lemon and a pinch of salt. Once combined, fold through the herbs, spring onions and the remaining frozen peas. If the batter seems too thick, add water until you have a spoonable consistency.
Add a splash of olive oil to a hot frying pan and add spoonfuls of the batter to form pancakes. Cook for a few minutes on each side until golden.
Plate with the toppings of your choice: we love topping the pancakes with sliced avocado, soft-boiled eggs, a dollop of Greek yoghurt and a drizzle of crispy chilli oil.

name: Herby Poached Chicken Soup
description: A herbaceous and soul-affirming chicken soup recipe. Poaching your chicken is a great way to get it incredibly tender.
instructions: Pop your chicken in your largest saucepan or stock pot. Roughly chop the fennel, ginger, shallots (skin-on), carrots and halve the bulb of garlic. Drop in the herbs and spices plus a heaping handful of salt and 1 tbsp of whole black peppercorns.

Cover the whole lot with cold water and pop a lid on. Set over a medium-high heat and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer and cook for 5-6 mins before removing from the heat and leaving, still covered, on the stove for 90 minutes. By the time you come back to the chicken, it will be fully cooked, gently poached in the residual heat.
Whilst the chicken is poaching, prep the finishing veggies. Cut the celery, leek, fennel, carrot and spring onions into bite size pieces. Roughly chop the dill and pickles, too.

Once your chicken is cooked, remove from the broth and allow it to rest for 10 mins. Pass the broth through a fine sieve into a clean saucepan and set over a high heat. Bring to a boil and reduce by half to intensify the flavour.

Shred the meat from the cooked chicken and cut into bite sized pieces. Once your broth has reduced, tip in the pasta and the fennel, carrot, leek and celery and cook for 8-9 mins until al dente. When the pasta is cooked, stir through the spring onions, dill and chopped pickles. Season well with salt and black pepper and divide between warm bowls.
Finish each bowl with a spoon of crème fraîche and a pinch of chilli flakes.

name: Herby Roast Chicken Caesar Sandwich Filler
description: This sandwich filler is a game-changer. Thanks to the robustness of the kale, it stays fresh in the fridge for 3 days, meaning you can make banging sandwiches throughout the week.
keywords: Herby Roast Chicken Caesar Sandwich Filler
Herby Roast Chicken Caesar Sandwich Filler recipe
instructions: Remove the chicken from the fridge 30 mins before cooking to bring it to room temperature. Heat the oven to 190°C fan.
Grab a large roasting tray and drizzle enough olive oil to coat the base. Peel and quarter the onions, then place them face-down in the roasting tray.

Pat the chicken dry with kitchen paper. Using your fingers, carefully lift the skin to create a space and rub the butter underneath. Stuff the cavity with ½ the lemon and the thyme. Season the skin generously with salt.

Place the chicken on a rack in the top half of the oven and slide the tray of onions into the shelf below (roasting the chicken on a rack lets the heat circulate around it, resulting in delicious rotisserie-style chicken, and the onions below will soak up all the juices). Roast for 1 hr 20 mins. Once cooked, remove from the oven and rest for 30 mins. Shred the meat with your hands.
To make the Caesar dressing, add the mayonnaise, yoghurt, anchovies, garlic, Dijon mustard, and juice of the remaining lemon to a blender and blitz until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper.

Roughly chop the parsley. Put the kale into a large bowl with a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Scrunch with your hands to soften, then toss in the parsley, shredded chicken, dressing and grated Parmesan.

Box it up and enjoy easy sandwiches all week with zero faff! It will keep in the fridge for 3 days. Sandwich the filling and roasted onions between slices of your favourite bread and you’re good to go.

name: Herby Sesame Cod with Turmeric Rice
description: This dish is inspired by Vietnamese cha ca. With Sesame-crusted flaky cod, fragrant turmeric rice and zingy lime dressing, this is as fresh as it gets
keywords: herby sesame cod with turmeric rice
instructions: Season the cod fillets with salt and place them on a plate or rack. Chill in the fridge for at least 30 mins (or up to overnight) to firm up the texture.

Wash the rice in cold water until it runs clear. Thinly slice the spring onions, setting the green tops aside in a bowl of ice water with picked dill fronds. Finely grate the ginger, thinly slice the garlic, zest the lime and set aside.

Place a large lidded frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the spring onion whites and cook for 2–3 mins until softened. Stir through the ginger, garlic and turmeric until fragrant, about 1–2 mins. Tip in the rice with the water, season with salt and bring to the boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12–15 mins until the rice is tender.
Pat the cod dry, then coat all over with sesame seeds. Thinly slice the chillies and mix in a bowl with the lime zest and juice. Season with fish sauce to taste and set aside.
Take the pan off the heat and arrange the sesame-coated cod on top. Cover with the lid and let the fish gently steam in the residual heat for 10 mins. Heat the grill to high.
After steaming, transfer the pan under the grill for 3–4 mins until the cod is golden and fully cooked through.
Fluff the turmeric rice with a fork and divide between bowls. Top with the sesame cod, scatter with dill and spring onion greens, then drizzle over the chilli lime dressing.

name: Herby Spring Veg with Burrata
description: We set out to make a green ratatouille but ended up somewhere even more delicious. Roasted veg, basil pistou, gooey burrata and a crispy chilli crumble.
instructions: Heat your oven to 220°C.
Wash and thinly slice the leek and courgette. Cut the pepper into medium-sized chunks and the asparagus into small chunks.

Transfer the leek, courgette and green bell pepper to a large roasting tin, drizzle with olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper. Toss to coat, arrange in a single layer and roast for 15 mins.
Take the veg out of the oven and add the asparagus. Toss to coat, then pop back into the oven for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, boil and drain the peas according to the package instructions.
Place the garlic in a mortar and pound to a paste with a pestle. Add the basil and olive oil and pound until well combined. Alternatively, you can do this in a food processor.
Transfer the roasted veg to a large bowl. Add the peas, a big squeeze of lemon juice and the basil mixture and toss everything together. Taste, adjust the seasoning and leave to cool.

Cut the bread into slices, chuck it into the same tray and drizzle with olive oil. Bake in the oven for 10 to 15 mins, or until crisp. Meanwhile, deseed and chop the chilli. Leave the bread to cool for 5 min then blitz in a food processor with the chilli, salt and pepper.
To serve, plate up the veg on the bottom of a large plate or platter. Top with the burrata and chilli crumb then tuck in and enjoy!

name: Herby, Creamy Chicken Salad & Roast Potatoes
description: Roast dinner for lunch? Great idea. This herby chicken salad’s creamy, zingy, and properly satisfying, especially when it’s piled up next to those golden roasties.
keywords: creamy chicken salad with roast potatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Wash and dry the potatoes, then chuck them onto a baking tray. Drizzle over one-third of the olive oil, rub it into the potatoes, season with salt and pepper, then roast for 20–25 mins until golden and cooked through.

Add the chicken breasts to a bowl with the garlic powder, onion powder and the remaining olive oil. Toss everything together, then lay the chicken on a lined baking tray and roast for 15–20 mins, until cooked through. Let it rest for a couple of minutes once done.
Meanwhile, zest the lemon. Thinly slice all of the chives. Thinly slice the celery and cucumber. Pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the soft stems.

Chuck the cottage cheese into a blender with the chives, the parsley stems, garlic powder and onion powder. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt, pepper and a good squeeze of lemon juice. Stir through as much of the lemon zest as you like.

Finely dice the cooked chicken. Add it to a large bowl with the cottage cheese dressing, chopped celery, cucumber and half of the parsley leaves and remaining chives. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more salt, pepper, lemon juice or zest if needed.

Spoon the chicken salad into your Tupperware containers with the roast potatoes on the side. Finish with a drizzle of any remaining olive oil and a scattering of the rest of the chives and parsley. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Herby, Creamy Chicken Salad & Roast Potatoes
description: This herby chicken salad’s creamy, zingy, and properly satisfying, especially when it’s piled up next to those golden roasties.
keywords: creamy chicken salad with roast potatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Wash and dry the potatoes, then chuck them onto a baking tray. Drizzle over one-third of the olive oil, rub it into the potatoes, season with salt and pepper, then roast for 20–25 mins until golden and cooked through.

Add the chicken breasts to a bowl with the garlic powder, onion powder and the remaining olive oil. Toss everything together, then lay the chicken on a lined baking tray and roast for 15–20 mins, until cooked through. Let it rest for a couple of minutes once done.
Meanwhile, zest the lemon. Thinly slice all of the chives. Thinly slice the celery and cucumber. Pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the soft stems.

Chuck the cottage cheese into a blender with the chives, the parsley stems, garlic powder and onion powder. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt, pepper and a good squeeze of lemon juice. Stir through as much of the lemon zest as you like.

Finely dice the cooked chicken. Add it to a large bowl with the cottage cheese dressing, chopped celery, cucumber and half of the parsley leaves and remaining chives. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more salt, pepper, lemon juice or zest if needed.
Spoon the chicken salad onto plates with the roast potatoes on the side. Finish with a drizzle of any remaining olive oil and a scattering of the rest of the chives and parsley.

name: Herby, Green Toad in the Hole
description: A bright green toad in the hole recipe. A summery alternative to a British classic served with a zingy fennel and herb salad.
keywords: Green Toad in the Hole recipe
instructions: Put the flour, a big pinch of salt and a generous grind of pepper into a large bowl. Set aside.

Put the milk, mustard, dill, and half the parsley into a blender, then whizz until smooth and well combined. Crack in the eggs and whisk. Slowly pour this mixture into the flour, whisking all the time, until you get a smooth batter. Set aside for 30 mins.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the sausages onto a large, deep roasting tin and drizzle with a half of the olive oil. Cook in the oven for 10 mins, turning once, until really golden.
When the sausages are golden, carefully remove the tray from the oven and pour the batter over. Quickly transfer it back to the oven and cook for 30-35 mins until puffed and golden.

Meanwhile, make the salad by finely slicing the red onion and fennel. Add to a bowl with the sumac, juiced lemon, the remaining olive oil and remaining parsley, leaves picked and stalks discarded. Mix the harissa with the yoghurt and season with salt and pepper.
When the toad is done, remove from the oven and allow to cool before serving (or topping) with the fennel salad.

name: Hidden Veg Meatball Chilli
description: In Partnership with Aldi. Big flavour, no complaints. This one’s loaded with secret veggies, spicy beans and golden meatballs and even a melty cheese topping if you’re going all-in. #ad
instructions: Heat a large deep frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry the meatballs for around 4 mins, turning often, until golden all over. Scoop them out onto a plate.

Grate 1 of the red onions, along with the courgette, carrot and sweet potato using a coarse box grater — or chuck them through the grater attachment of a food processor. Thinly slice the remaining onion. Juice the lime over the sliced onion in a small bowl. Season with salt and scrunch with your hands, then set aside to pickle.

Add all the grated veg to the empty pan along with a pinch of salt. Cook for 15 mins, stirring regularly, until everything’s softened. Stir in the cumin, paprika, cinnamon, chilli powder and tomato purée. Cook for another couple of mins to toast the spices.

Drain the roasted peppers and add them to the pan along with the cherry tomatoes. Bring to the boil, then use a hand blender to blitz everything into a smooth sauce. Add a splash of water if it’s looking too thick.

Drain the beans, then stir them into the sauce. Nestle the browned meatballs back in and let it simmer for 6-8 mins until the meatballs are cooked through. If you're adding cheese, grate the cheddar now. Scatter it over the top and pop the pan under a hot grill for 2-3 mins until bubbling and golden.

Serve up! Spoon the chilli into bowls and serve with your chosen carb.Kids’ Plate: Pair the chilli with rice or tortilla chips and add their favourite dips on top or on the side.Parents’ Plate: Top the chilli with pickled onions, sliced green chilli, and dips. Garnish with chopped coriander.

name: High Protein Black Lentil Curry
description: Inspired by dal makhani, this rich and comforting curry gets its silky, creamy texture from blended silken tofu instead of cream, keeping it high in protein and completely dairy free.
instructions: Finely dice the onion, and grate the garlic and ginger.
Before you start the dal, get the rice on. Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs clear, then cook according to the packet instructions.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and onion and fry for 5-6 mins until translucent and softened. Season generously with salt. Add the garlic and ginger and fry for another minute. Add the tomato purée and chilli powder and cook for 2–3 mins, stirring, until caramelised and darkened (if you like it spicier add a little more chilli powder).
Tip in the black lentils with all their liquid and the water. Cover with a lid and cook for about 15 mins until the stew has thickened and the lentils have softened.

Blitz the silken tofu in a blender until smooth, a stick blender works too. Stir it into the lentils and continue cooking for 6-8 mins until warmed through and slightly darkened. Taste for seasoning, salt will enhance the flavours of this dish so don't be shy!
Serve the curry over the rice with a dollop of coconut yoghurt and the coriander scattered over.

name: High Protein Celery & Chicken Salad with Creamy Coriander Dip
description: This is the recipe that changed me from being creeped out about chicken mince, to kind of obsessed... it's creamy, light, peppery and tangy basically everything I look for in a meal. The best part, it looks amazing but takes so little time to come together.
keywords: Crisp Celery & Chicken Mince Salad with Creamy Coriander Dip
Crisp Celery & Chicken Mince Salad with Creamy Coriander Dip recipe
instructions: Add all the ingredients for the dip into a blender and blend until smooth. If you can get your hands on the jarred chickpeas they're usually softer, but canned will do too. Season with salt and the juice of the lime. Cover and place in the fridge to thicken.
Meanwhile, finely grate the garlic. Thinly slice or mandolin the radish and celery.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the chicken mince straight into the dry pan and stir-fry for 8-10 mins, until cooked through and starting to brown and catch on the pan. Add the garlic, oyster sauce and dark soy sauce, stirring until the mince is evenly coated and starting to caramelise. Remove from the heat and stir the celery and radish through. Taste and season with salt, black pepper and the juice of the lime if needed.
Share the dip between boxes or plates. Top with the salad and serve with the remaining lime, cut into wedges.

name: High Protein Cheeseburger Egg Smash
description: All the flavour of a cheeseburger in one loaded egg mayo smash. Cheddar, crispy bacon, tangy cornichons and the classic burger sauce flavours, piled into grilled brioche buns. It's seriously good and ideal for whacking in the fridge for an easy grab and go high protein lunch or snack.
keywords: Cheeseburger Egg & Bacon Brioche Buns recipe
instructions: Bring a pan of water to the boil. Once boiling, carefully lower in the eggs and cook for 8 mins.
Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Lay the bacon on a baking tray and grill for 8-10 mins, until crisp and golden. Once it's ready leave to cool slightly.

Transfer the eggs to a bowl of cold water to cool, then carefully peel off the shells. If you like, you can separate the yolks from the whites at this point: slice a knife down the side of each white and gently pop the yolk out.

Add the eggs to a large bowl with the mayonnaise, ketchup, Greek yoghurt and Dijon mustard. Grate in the cheddar, snap the cornichons into bite-sized pieces and add them in with a splash of the brine. Break the grilled bacon over the top with your hands, then, using a pizza cutter, smash everything together until nicely mashed and mixed.

Grill the brioche buns, then place a dollop of the smash in each one. Serve up and enjoy. If you're prepping ahead transfer the smash into airtight containers and chill in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: High Protein Cheesy Pesto Egg Smash
description: A creamy, cheesy egg smash loaded with pesto, cottage cheese and Parmesan, with toasted pine nuts for crunch and a squeeze of lemon to lift it. Perfect for whacking in the fridge for a quick high protein meal ready in minutes.
keywords: High Protein Cheesy Pesto Egg Smash
instructions: Bring a pan of water to the boil. Once boiling, carefully lower in the eggs and cook for 8 mins.
Meanwhile, toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2-3 mins, tossing regularly, until golden. Tip out and set aside.

Transfer the eggs to a bowl of cold water to cool, then carefully peel off the shells. If you like, you can separate the yolks from the whites at this point: slice a knife down the side of each white and gently pop the yolk out.

Add the eggs to a large bowl with the Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese and pesto. Grate in the Parmesan and squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Season with salt and black pepper, then, using a pizza cutter, smash everything together until nicely mashed and mixed. Stir through most of the toasted pine nuts, saving a few to scatter on top. Taste and add another squeeze of lemon juice if needed.
Toast the bread and pile the smash onto each slice and serve. If you're prepping ahead transfer the smash into airtight containers and chill for up to 3 days.

name: High Protein Chicken Caesar Egg Smash
description: Everything you love about a Caesar in one loaded egg mayo smash. Roast chicken, salty anchovies, sharp Parmesan and Dijon, all smashed through creamy egg mayo with a squeeze of lemon. Stash this in the fridge and you'll have the perfect protein packed lunch ready all week.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Place the chicken breasts on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Roast for 15-20 mins, until cooked through, then set aside to cool slightly before shredding or chopping into pieces.

Meanwhile, bring a pan of water to the boil. Once boiling, carefully lower in the eggs and cook for 8 mins. Transfer to a bowl of cold water to cool, then carefully peel off the shells. If you like, you can separate the yolks from the whites at this point: slice a knife down the side of each white and gently pop the yolk out.

Add the eggs to a large bowl with the Greek yoghurt, mayonnaise and Dijon mustard. Finely chop the anchovies and add them in with the anchovy oil. Grate in the Parmesan, then zest in the lemon and squeeze in the juice. Finely chop the chives and add most of them, saving a little to serve. Season with salt and black pepper, then, using a pizza cutter, smash everything together until nicely mashed and mixed.
Add the shredded chicken and fold through.

For each serving, lay out a 2-3 leaves of iceberg lettuce, slightly overlapped. Then dollop a portion of the smash mix inside and roll up like a wrap. Cut in half and serve straight away. If you're prepping ahead, transfer the smash into airtight containers and chill for up to 3 days.

name: High Protein Chicken Caesar Pasta Salad
description: Deeply golden roast broccoli, shredded chicken and kale tossed in a creamy cottage cheese Caesar dressing, finished with crispy breadcrumbs and parmesan shavings. This is the perfect pasta salad when you want to hit your protein goals but still want a little comfort.
keywords: Roast Broccoli & Chicken Caesar Pasta Salad
Roast Broccoli & Chicken Caesar Pasta Salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the broccoli with the 2/3 of the olive oil for the salad, season and roast for 20-25 mins until deeply golden.
Add the kale to a bowl and season with a pinch of salt and the remaining 1/3 olive oil. Massage for a few minutes until softened, then set aside.
In a small saucepan add the olive oil for the breadcrumbs and add in the fresh breadcrumbs, toast on a medium heat stirring regularly for 8 mins until lightly golden.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta according to packet instructions, then drain and rinse in cool water.
Blend all the dressing ingredients until smooth.
In a large mixing bowl toss the pasta with the dressing, chicken, kale and broccoli and season with salt and pepper.
To serve, divide between bowls or containers and with the parmesan grated into shaving using a peeler and crispy breadcrumbs.

name: High Protein Chopped Broccoli Salad
description: This crunchy broccoli and quinoa salad is perfect for meal prep as it’s made with sturdy ingredients that will stay crunchy in the fridge
instructions:
Rinse the quinoa very well and add to a saucepan. Cover the quinoa with double the amount of water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil and then reduce the heat and simmer for 12 mins. 
Drain and rinse under cold water in a colander. Set aside or in the fridge to cool while you prepare the rest.
Finely chop the broccoli florets. Peel the tough skin from the broccoli stem and finely chop the broccoli stem or grate it on a cheesegrater. Add to a large bowl.
Drain the chickpeas, finely chop the red onion and add these to the bowl. Add the dried cranberries, sunflower seeds and peanuts to the bowl.

To make the dressing, mix all of the ingredients in a jar and shake well to combine. 
You can mix the dressing before storing as the ingredients will stay crisp and absorb the dressing well. Keep refrigerated for up to 3-4 days.

name: High Protein Everything Bagel Egg Smash
description: Inspired by a classic salmon bagel and that seasoning we're all obsessed with, this egg smash is your new go-to meal prep lunch. Smoked salmon, fresh dill and chives, all finished with a crunchy everything bagel seasoning. Great for sandwiches, on toast or on it's own for a high protein snack.
keywords: Smoked Salmon & Everything Bagel Egg Mayo
Smoked Salmon & Everything Bagel Egg Mayo recipe
instructions: Bring a pan of water to the boil. Once boiling, carefully lower in the eggs and cook for 8 mins. Transfer to a bowl of cold water to cool, then carefully peel off the shells. If you like, you can separate the yolks from the whites at this point: slice a knife down the side of each white and gently pop the yolk out.

Add the eggs to a large bowl with the cream cheese and mayonnaise. Squeeze in the lemon juice. Roughly chop the dill and chives and add those in too. Season with salt and black pepper, then, using a pizza cutter, smash everything together until nicely mashed and mixed.
Tear or slice the smoked salmon into pieces and fold it through the smash and sprinkle in the everything bagel seasoning.

To serve, slice a bagel in half for each person and pile a generous dollop of the smash onto the bottom half, then sandwich with the top and serve. If you're prepping ahead transfer to airtight containers and store in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: High Protein Feta & Harissa Egg Smash
description: A punchy egg smash with fragrant harissa, salty feta and a squeeze of lemon, topped with seeds for crunch. Perfect in a sandwich, slathered on toast or eaten straight from the tub.
keywords: Harissa & Feta Egg Mayo with Seeds
Harissa & Feta Egg Mayo with Seeds recipe
instructions: Bring a pan of water to the boil. Once boiling, carefully lower in the eggs and cook for 8 mins.

Transfer the eggs to a bowl of cold water to cool, then carefully peel off the shells. If you like, you can separate the yolks from the whites at this point: slice a knife down the side of each white and gently pop the yolk out.

Add the eggs to a large bowl with the Greek yoghurt, mayonnaise and harissa. Crumble in the feta, then zest in the lemon and squeeze in the juice. Finely chop the parsley and add that in too. Add the mixed seeds, season with salt and black pepper, then, using a pizza cutter, smash everything together until nicely mashed and mixed.
Toast the sourdough, and add a dollop of the smash on each slice and serve. If you're prepping ahead transfer to airtight containers and store in the fridge for up to 3 days.

name: High Protein Greek Chicken 'Tabbouleh'
description: Ok so calling this a tabbouleh is a little bit of a stretch, but it does have a lot of the same flavours in there. Instead of using bulgur wheat I've swapped in spiced chicken mince for a high protein alternative and it is very, very delicious indeed. The leftovers are also great to have in the fridge for an easy grab and go lunch.
instructions: Finely chop the garlic. Heat half the olive oil in a large frying pan or wok over a high heat. Add the chicken mince and cook for 6-8 mins, until golden, then add the garlic and cook for another minute. Stir in the dried oregano, dried mint, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika and ground cumin, season with salt and black pepper and set aside.
Drain and finely chop the roasted red peppers. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds and finely chop. Finely chop the mint and parsley.

Add the peppers, cucumber, mint, parsley, pomegranate seeds and chicken mince to a large bowl. Grate in the zest of one lemon, then squeeze in the juice of both along with the remaining oil. Season with salt and black pepper and mix well.
If using, swoosh the tzatziki through a bowl and top with the chicken salad to serve.

name: High Protein Italian Deli Pasta Salad
description: Juicy roast chicken, salty mortadella, torn mozzarella and blistered cherry tomatoes tossed with pasta in a creamy basil pesto dressing. This high protein number is perfect for making ahead this summer.
instructions: Cook the pasta according to packet instructions, then drain and leave to cool.

Meanwhile, heat the oven to 180°C. Add the chicken breasts to a baking tray, drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. On a seperate tray, add the tomatoes, halved, with a little olive oil and a pinch of salt. Roast for 20-25 mins until the chicken is cooked through and the tomatoes have collapsed, then set aside both to cool.
Blend the cottage cheese with the pesto, juice of the lemon and water until smooth. Then once the chicken is cool enough to handle shred it into bitesize pieces.
In a large mixing bowl, toss together the pasta, chicken, mortadella, mozzarella, roasted tomatoes, rocket and basil. Spoon over the dressing and gently combine.
To serve, divide between bowls or containers and an extra grind of black pepper.

name: High Protein Prawn Cocktail Pasta Salad
description: All the flavours of a prawn cocktail, tossed through pasta with crisp little gem, avocado and a tangy Marie Rose dressing. It's super retro and that's why we love it.
instructions: Cook the pasta according to packet instructions, for the final few minutes of the cooking time add in the edamame for a minute or two, then drain. Rinse the pasta and edamame under cold water and leave to cool.
Chop the avocado and cucumber into cubes, shred the lettuce and finely chop the chives.
Juice the lemon into a small bowl and add the remaining dressing ingredients. Mix together until combined.
In a large mixing bowl, add the pasta and edamame and toss with the prawns, lettuce, avocado, cucumber and chives. Fold through the dressing and chill before serving.

name: High Protein Smashed Cucumber & Chilli Chicken Pasta Salad
description: Smashed cucumber, a creamy cottage cheese and miso dressing and a big spoon of crispy chilli oil mixed with chicken and pasta make a phenomenal high-protein pasta salad that satisfies all your cravings. It's bound to be in your regular rotation this summer.
keywords: Smashed Cucumber & Chilli Chicken Pasta Salad
Smashed Cucumber & Chilli Chicken Pasta Salad recipe
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the macaroni and cook according to the packet instructions. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool to the touch, then set aside.

Add the cottage cheese, Greek yoghurt and white miso to a blender and blend until smooth. Zest in half the lime, then taste and season with salt and a squeeze of lime juice. Pour into a bowl and spoon over the crispy chilli oil, then set aside.

Smash the cucumbers (you can use a pan, rolling pin or pestle), then chop into 1-2cm chunks. Roughly chop the coriander leaves, saving a little to serve, and thinly slice the stems. Drain the sweetcorn and cut the chicken into 1cm chunks.

Add the macaroni, chicken, cucumbers, sweetcorn and coriander to a large bowl and drizzle over the dressing. Toss everything together, then share between plates or boxes. To serve, top with the reserved coriander and a little more crispy chilli oil, if you'd like.

name: High Protein Tuna & Sweetcorn Pasta Salad
description: It's a classic for a reason. This pasta salad comes with a creamy cottage cheese dressing for an extra hit of protein that works amazingly with the flaky tuna, sweetcorn and a hit of lemon and capers. It's also great for making ahead.
keywords: Cottage Cheese & Sweetcorn Pasta Salad recipe
ingredients: 3x 145g Can Tinned Tuna in Spring Water
instructions: Bring a pot of water to the boil and cook the pasta according to the packet instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Meanwhile, fill a small saucepan with water, bring to the boil and add the sweetcorn for 2-3 mins until soft, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Finely chop the red pepper and parsley.
Blend the cottage cheese with the mayonnaise, the juice of the lemon, salt and pepper until smooth. Season well.
Drain the tuna and add to a large mixing bowl with pasta, sweetcorn, capers, red pepper, parsley and pour over the dressing. Season with salt and black pepper and mix everything together.
To serve, divide the pasta between bowls or containers and add an extra grind of black pepper.

name: High Protein Tuna Caesar with Butternut Squash
description: Zingy lemon yoghurt, roast squash, and seared tuna come together in this high-protein low-cal bowl topped with crispy Parmesan shards. Simple but seriously satisfying.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Chop the butternut squash into 5cm pieces, chuck onto a baking tray with half the olive oil, season with salt and black pepper, then roast for 20 mins or until tender and starting to colour.

Peel and finely grate the garlic into a mixing bowl. Mash the anchovies and garlic together using a fork to form a paste. Zest over half the lemon (save the rest for later), then squeeze in the juice. Add the yoghurt, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard and plenty of black pepper. Whisk together, loosening with splashes of cold water until it’s as runny as you like.

Heat a nonstick frying pan over a medium heat. Finely grate the Parmesan directly into the pan in an even layer and cook until bubbling. Remove from the heat, let it cool for a couple of minutes, then gently lift the Parmesan crisp out. Once cool, snap into shards.
Strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and finely shred the leaves. Toss into a bowl with a pinch of salt and the remaining lemon juice. Scrunch it all together with your hands to soften.

Brush the tuna steaks with the remaining oil and season with salt and black pepper. Heat a large nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat, then cook the tuna for 2 mins per side for a pink centre. Transfer to a plate to rest, then sprinkle over the reserved lemon zest.
Toss the roasted squash and lemony dressing through the cavolo nero, then divide between plates. Slice the tuna and lay it on top, finishing with the Parmesan crisps.

name: High-Protein Air Fryer Granola
description: Let us show you how quick and easy it is to make healthy granola at home in your air fryer. This one is super high in protein too. A guaranteed good start to your day.
instructions: Heat the air fryer to 160°C.

If the coconut oil is solid, melt it in a saucepan over a low heat. Alternatively pop it in the microwave in a microwave-safe bowl for 15 seconds at a time, stirring between each burst until completely melted.
Crush the hazelnuts with a large knife then chop into small pieces. Add to a large bowl along with all the other ingredients, except the egg whites.

Seperate the egg whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise). Add the egg whites to a separate large bowl and whisk until soft and fluffy (this will take around 4-5 mins with a hand whisk). Gently fold the egg white through the dry ingredients.
Add the uncooked granola to the air fryer tray in a single layer (you might need to do this in batches). Cook for 15-20 mins, mixing halfway, until completely golden and toasty.
Leave to cool before serving immediately, or storing in an airtight container for up to 10 days.

name: High-Protein Bagels
description: These easy high-protein bagels use just five ingredients (plus salt) and require no yeast or proving. Perfect for a quick and healthy breakfast or snack. Make a big batch, slice ‘em up and whack ‘em in the freezer until you're ready to eat. Make sure you use 0% yoghurt as these won't work with any other types of yoghurt!
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Add the white bread flour, wholemeal bread flour, Greek yoghurt, baking powder and salt to a large bowl. Mix with a spoon until it forms a dough, then transfer to a lightly floured surface and knead for a minute until it comes together. (Or, if using a stand mixer, add all of the ingredients to the bowl and mix with a dough hook for a minute.)
Crack the egg into a bowl and whisk well. Fill a small bowl with warm water.

Cut the dough into equal pieces (if you're making the recipe to serve 6, cut it into 6 pieces, etc.). Flour the surface again, then roll each piece into a sausage. Feel free to sprinkle over a little extra flour if the dough gets too sticky. 
Dab the ends with warm water and press them together to form a ring. Repeat with the remaining dough.
Sprinkle your chosen seasoning onto a plate. Brush each bagel with the beaten egg, then press the egg-washed side into the seasoning. Place onto a lined baking tray.
Bake for 20-25 mins until golden and firm. Allow to cool, then slice in half before freezing.

name: High-Protein Breakfast Beans & Eggs
description: A high-protein breakfast recipe that's great for meal prep. You'll be craving this every morning.
instructions: Pick the herb leaves, finely slice the coriander stalks and discard the oregano stalks. Finely dice the onion and finely grate the garlic.

Place a frying pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the onion, season generously with salt and pepper then cook until translucent, 4-6 mins. Then, add the coriander stems, oregano, garlic and tomato purée. Cook, stirring, until the tomato purée has darkened, 2-3 mins.
Tip the beans, liquid and all, into the tomato purée along with the water. Let it come to a boil then turn the heat down to low and simmer until creamy and thickened, 6-10 mins.

In the meantime, place a pot of water on to boil. Once boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook until soft-boiled, 6-7 mins, or more if you want a harder set. Transfer to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking. Let the eggs cool down before peeling the shell off.
Taste and season the beans with more salt and pepper if needed and share between boxes. Top with the feta, a boiled egg and a wedge of lime.
To reheat, remove the egg or cut it in half before microwaving.

name: High-Protein Breakfast Burritos
description: Filled with crispy potatoes, pork mince, egg and cheese, these high-protein breakfast burritos are super high in protein and will have your tastebuds soaring any time of day!
instructions: Chop the potatoes into small chunks around 1-2cm wide. Microwave for 3-4 mins to soften, then spray with some low-calorie spray and season with ½ tsp onion powder, ½ tsp paprika, salt and pepper. Air fry at 180°C for 10-15 mins, or until crispy.

Meanwhile, tip the mince and the remaining onion powder and paprika into a frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Break the mince up as it cooks and add the Worcestershire sauce and tomato purée. Cook for around 5 mins, then set the mince aside and wipe the pan so it’s mostly clean.
Carefully separate one of the eggs, (you can use the yolk to make your own mayonnaise). Add 3 tbsp of egg white per serving to a bowl with the remaining whole egg, salt and pepper. Whisk to combine.

Add the butter to the frying pan over a low heat until it starts to melt. Pour in the eggs and leave them to set for around 10 seconds at a time before folding them over. Repeat for a couple of mins until they’re almost at your desired consistency, then remove from the heat. They will continue to cook a little once removed from the heat, so be careful not to overdo them.

Now it’s time to assemble your burrito! Heat the wrap to make it flexible, then spread ½ tbsp chilli jam onto the centre of each wrap, followed by the potatoes and the egg. Chop the chives and sprinkle over the egg, then add the pork mince, the mozzarella, and finally another drizzle of the remaining chilli jam. Fold either side in and then roll it up, tucking it under as you go so it holds together nicely.
Wipe the pan clean from the egg, then reheat it to a medium heat and pop the wrap in (flap-side down to hold it together). Cook for a couple of minutes each side until browned.
Leave to cool for 5 mins, then cut in half and enjoy!

name: High-Protein Cacio e Pepe
description: The Italian classic you know and love with protein-packed tofu twist. Creamy, comforting and ridiculously easy, cacio e pepe, but make it gym-friendly.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Grind the black peppercorns using a spice grinder or pestle and mortar.
Once the water is boiling, cook the pasta following pack instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving about 300ml of pasta water.
Meanwhile, chuck the tofu into a blender with the Cheddar, most of the Parmesan, Dijon mustard, garlic powder and most of the ground black pepper. Season with salt and blend until smooth and creamy.

Tip the drained pasta back into the pot. Pour over the sauce and stir to coat. Add a splash of the reserved pasta water to loosen to your desired consistency. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more salt or pepper if needed.
Share between bowls and finish with extra Parmesan and a good crack of black pepper.

name: High-Protein Cauliflower Mac & Cheese
description: Creamy, cheesy, and packed with protein. This tofu-powered mac and cheese is a lighter take on a proper comfort classic.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil.
Cut the cauliflower into florets, toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then roast for 15 mins until just tender and golden. Grate the cheeses.
Add the pasta to the boiling salted water and cook according to the packet instructions. Drain, reserving a little of the pasta water.
In a blender, combine the silken tofu, Dijon mustard, garlic powder, parmesan, and a pinch of nutmeg. Season well with salt and pepper, then blend until smooth and creamy.

Return the pasta and roasted cauliflower to the pan. Pour over the tofu sauce and stir to coat. Add most of the cheeses (saving a handful for the top) and heat gently for a couple of minutes until the cheese has melted, loosening with a splash of pasta water if needed.
Transfer to an ovenproof dish, sprinkle with the remaining cheese, and bake for 10 mins until golden and bubbling. Finely chop the parsley.
Serve the pasta bake topped with chopped parsley and a crack of black pepper.

name: High-Protein Cauliflower Soup With Sticky Onions
