description: This soup packs in some secret protein by swapping out coconut milk for silken tofu. It gives it a delicious creamy texture without an overpowering taste.
instructions: Chop two onions and all of the garlic. Peel and cut the potato into 2cm cubes. Roughly chop the cauliflower into small pieces, including the stem.

At the 3-4 tbsp oil to a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook until translucent and softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add the garlic, stir, and cook for another minute or so, until fragrant but not browned.
Make the stock by dissolving the stock cubes in the boiling water.
Add the curry powder, ground turmeric, garam masala, and coriander. Stir, allowing the spices to toast for about 30 seconds.
Add in sweet potato, cauliflower, vegetable stock, and silken tofu. Cover and simmer until vegetables are very tender and easily pierced with a fork, about 25-35 mins.
Using an immersion blender, or a standing blender, blend the soup until it is smooth and creamy. Add a little more water if you want a thinner texture.

To make the tarka topping, start by finely slicing the remaining onion. Melt 3 tbsp coconut oil in a frying pan on medium low. Add the mustard seeds and sizzle for a minute or two, before adding the red onion and a pinch of salt. Fry the onion for 10-15 minutes on a medium-low heat until softened and slightly sticky, stirring often.
Then, add the curry leaves, turmeric and chilli flakes, along with a pinch of salt. Sizzle over a low-medium heat for a final 2-3 minutes. Drizzle on top of the soup to serve.

name: High-Protein Cheese & Pickled Onion Sandwich Filler
description: A tangy, cheesy sarnie filling packed with protein and texture. Incredible in sandwiches, on toast or eaten with a spoon straight from the bowl.
instructions: Drain and quarter the pickled onions. Finely chop the celery and red onion.
Grate the Cheddar and Red Leicester.
Add the cottage cheese to a bowl along with the grated cheeses, chopped onions and celery. Stir through the mustard and pickled onion juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Mix well until everything’s combined.

Serve however you like, I like to serve this with chopped spring onions (yes more onion!) in toasted ciabatta rolls with a handful of crisps on top. 
If you're making ahead, pop the filling into the fridge in Tupperware (it will keep for up to 3 days).

name: High-Protein Chocolate & Peanut Mousse
description: A luxurious chocolate mousse that’s high in protein and ready in just 10 minutes. You’ll be making this post-workout dessert on repeat.
instructions: Finely chop the chocolate and add to a microwave-safe bowl. Melt the chocolate pieces in the microwave in 30-second bursts, taking the bowl out and stirring after each burst to get rid of any lumps. Set aside to cool slightly.

Add the silken tofu, cottage cheese, peanut butter, cocoa powder, maple syrup and vanilla to a blender. Zest in the peel of the orange and add a pinch of salt, then blitz until smooth. Add the melted, cooled dark chocolate and the protein powder, if using, and blitz again.
Pour the mixture into a small baking dish or individual ramekins.
Serve immediately, or leave in the fridge to set overnight if you prefer a thicker texture. Top with greek yoghurt, cherries, olive oil or granola, if you like.

name: High-Protein Egg Mayo
description: A creamy, tangy twist on classic egg mayo, made with protein-packed cottage cheese and punchy Dijon mustard, with a hint of sharpness from capers and vinegar.
instructions: Bring a large pan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and cook for 8 mins, then drain and cool under cold running water. Peel the eggs. Meanwhile, finely chop the chives and cornichons.

Cut the eggs in half and remove the yolks. Mash the yolks in a bowl, then chop the whites and add them in. Stir through the chives, cornichons, vinegar, cottage cheese and mustard. Season with salt and white pepper.
Peel and finely slice the red onion.

Spoon the egg mayo onto a bagel, slice of toast, a jacket potato – whatever you fancy – and top with the red onion. Finish with some more chives, if you like. The egg mayo will keep in the fridge for 2 days.

name: High-Protein Ribollita with Crumbled Sausage
description: Ribollita is my favourite Italian soup, but I’ve mixed it up a bit here by crisping up the bread and crumbling in chicken sausage for a protein boost. Comforting, healthy and delicious, you will go back for seconds.
keywords: High-Protein Ribollita with Crumbled Sausage recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Get the chicken sausages into a bowl and use a fork to smash them up into small pieces. Dice the onion and celery and thinly slice the garlic.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large heavy pan set over a medium heat. Add the sausage pieces and cook for 6-7 mins until browned. Using a slotted spoon, remove from the pan and set aside. Add the diced veggies to the pan with a good pinch of salt. Cook the mixture, stirring regularly, for 8-10 mins until soft and caramelised. If catching on the bottom of the pan, just add a splash of water and scrape the bits up.
Meanwhile, tip the canned tomatoes into a bowl and use your hands to crush them. Remove the cavolo nero leaves from the stem and roughly chop. Drain the butter beans.

To the pan with the caramelised veggies, add the garlic, chilli flakes and fennel seeds and cook for a minute or two over a medium heat. Add the tomato purée and bay leaves and cook out for another few minutes. Add the canned tomatoes, butter beans and chicken stock and bring to a simmer, then add the cavolo nero and leave to simmer for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, dice the bread into cubes and transfer to a baking tray. Drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt then roast in the oven for 15 mins, until golden brown.

To plate, add the croutons to the bottom of the bowl and ladle over the soup. Cover with some grated Parmesan and top with the crumbled sausage. Finish with salt, loads of black pepper and some parsley leaves.

name: High-Protein Sesame Pork Rice Bowl
description: This is a high-protein pork dish that you can make on a weeknight in only 35 minutes. It's really that easy.
keywords: high protein sesame pork rice bowl
instructions: Pat your pork tenderloin dry and season well with salt. Rub with a couple of tbsp of sesame oil and the Chinese five spice. Set aside for 10-15 mins.

Finely slice the whole bunch of spring onions and separate the green ends from the more oniony white bits. Finely chop the ginger and garlic. Use a peeler to shave the cabbage super fine. Toss the cabbage with salt and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the soy, honey and gochujang with a drop of sesame oil and the juice of 2/3 of your limes.

Preheat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add a shot of oil and lay in the tenderloin. Cook over a medium heat (nothing too crazy hot!) for 12-15 mins or until the pork is caramelised and when squeezed, is firm with a little bounce. Whip it out the pan and rest while you make the sauce.

Add the ginger, garlic and spring onion whites to the pan and cook in the residual fat for 1-2 mins. Pour in the soy mixture and bring to a boil. Once boiling, tip in the sesame seeds and remove from the heat.
Heat the rice following pack instructions.
Cut the pork into thick slices and season with salt.
Divide the rice between warm bowls and add a handful of shredded cabbage, some spring onion greens and a few slices of pork. Spoon the warm sesame sauce over your bowls and finish with a lime wedge.

name: High-Protein Smoothie Bowl
description: Stop drinking shop-bought protein shakes and make this healthy, high-protein breakfast smoothie bowl instead. Packed with fruit, protein and healthy fats, it's the perfect post-workout fuel or quick breakfast.
instructions: Add all the ingredients to a blender. Blend until smooth and creamy. If you prefer a thinner consistency, add a splash of extra almond milk. Squeeze in some lemon juice for a little extra zing and pour it out into a bowl.
Finish with your toppings. We've gone for some fruit, granola, peanut butter, a drizzle of honey and more chia seeds for extra crunch. But add whatever you fancy.

name: High-Protein Stuffed Aubergines
description: These easy stuffed aubergines are packed full of protein and flavour.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Add the boiling water in a jug and mix through the stock cube until dissolved. Mix the stock through the soy protein and cover with a plate to steam. Set aside for at least 15 mins.

Cut the aubergine in half and score in a criss cross pattern all along the flesh. Place it cut side down on a lined baking sheet. 
Bake for 35-45 mins, until very soft inside (this will depend on the size of your aubergine).
Drain the soy protein in a colander and squeeze out the excess water with the back of a spoon.

Finely chop the onion and garlic. Sauté the onion in a large frying pan on medium heat for 3-4 mins with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the garlic and stir for another minute before adding your spices (ras el hanout or a mix of cumin, paprika and chilli) tomato paste and balsamic vinegar.

Add the soy protein and the mashed aubergine flesh to the pan with a drizzle of olive oil and season well. Fry the mix for 7-8 mins until starting to crisp up. Taste and add more seasonings as you like. Mix in the pine nuts.
Spoon the mixture back into the aubergine skins. Drizzle with a little olive oil and grill for 3-5 mins until crispy on top.
Cook your rice or couscous. Finely chop the parsley.
Serve the aubergines with your chosen grain and top with plenty of parsley, some extra pine nuts, and pomegranate and tahini if using. Finish with a good squeeze of lemon and enjoy.

name: High-Protein Tiramisu Overnight Oats
description: Start your day with some serious protein with these healthy tiramisu overnight oats. Who doesn’t want tiramisu for breakfast?
instructions: Start off by making your coffee. Mix the freshly ground coffee with the boiling water.

For the base, add the oats, coffee, maple syrup, oat milk, hemp seeds, vanilla extract, sea salt and protein powder (if using) to a large bowl. Mix well and pour into a baking dish, or individual glasses. Leave to sit for 20-30 min.
For the topping, mix the greek yoghurt, maple syrup, oat milk and vanilla extract in a separate bowl. Pour the topping on top of the oat base then set aside in the fridge overnight.
To serve the next morning, remove the oats from the fridge and dust with cocoa.

name: Hoisin Duck 'Sausage' Rolls
description: This recipe from Crystelle Pereira takes all the best bits of duck pancakes and throws them into a sausage roll. Yum.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170°C, if not marinating. Otherwise preheat 10 mins before cooking.
First make the marinade. Place all the ingredients in a bowl and mix well to combine.

Using a sharp knife, carefully score the duck skin in diagonal lines, then rub the marinade all over the duck, making sure to rub it inside the scored lines. You can then either leave the duck to marinate for a few hours or place it on a roasting tray straight away and cook it for 45 mins.
Once cooked, remove the duck from the oven and turn up the oven temperature to 200°C.

Remove the duck from the bone, and use two forks to shred the duck meat, fat and skin into fine pieces. If the meat is still pink, don't worry as this will be going back in the oven. Once shredded, add the duck to a food processor along with the spring onions and pancetta and pulse until almost smooth, similar to the consistency of sausage meat.
Next, make the hoisin sauce. Combine all the ingredients in a bowl and mix well. Spoon 4 tbsp of the sauce into the shredded duck mixture and mix to combine.

Next, assemble your rolls. Ensure the duck is cool to the touch before assembling the pastry (it should be by now). Cut your sheet of puff pastry into four long strips widthways (approximately 26cm x 9cm) and spread 1⁄2 tbsp of hoisin sauce over each piece. Divide the duck mixture into four and distribute it down the middle of each strip. Now fold over each pastry strip lengthways, to enclose the meat and, using a fork, press down to seal tightly and create a pattern down each side. Cut each log into 8 pieces, 4cm long.

Brush beaten egg over each roll and sprinkle with a few sesame seeds. Arrange them on a lined baking tray and, if your kitchen is warm and your pastry is getting warm and soft, place it in the freezer for about 10 mins to firm up - this will help the pastry rise when you bake the rolls.
Bake in the oven for 20-25 mins until the pastry has puffed up and is golden brown.

name: Homemade Baked Beans On Toast
description:
The baked beans of your dreams: rich, tomatoey, endlessly customisable and deeply
comforting. Better than any brand in a can.
instructions: Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic cloves.
Heat the oil in a saucepan, add the onion and cook, stirring frequently, over a low to medium heat until it is soft and translucent. Add the garlic and cook for a further minute and a half.
Dissolve the vegetable stock cube in 100ml of water and add this to the pan together with the tomato purée, paprika, thyme and Henderson's Relish. Cook for two more minutes, stirring continuously.

Drain the beans and add those to the pan together with 250g of the passata. Simmer for at least 8 minutes until the sauce is piping hot and slightly thickened. At this point you can judge whether you like the beans at this consistency, or slightly runnier – in which case, just pop in the rest of the passata and cook for a couple of minutes more.
Season generously with salt and pepper and dollop onto hot buttered toast, your English breakfast or wherever you want your beans. Enjoy.

name: Homemade Butternut Squash Ravioli
description: No pasta machine. No fuss. Just perfectly formed butternut ravioli. Give it a go MOB.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Cut your squash into cubes. Add to a baking tray with salt, pepper and olive oil. Roast for 30 minutes until soft.
When the squash is ready, add it to a bowl with grated parmesan, ricotta, chopped thyme, chopped sage leaves, the zest of a lemon, salt and pepper. Mash it all together.

Pasta Time. It is easy. So easy. You just have to have faith and be persistent. Measure out 200g of flour and pour it onto a surface. Make a well in the middle. Crack eggs into a bowl and whisk together. Pour the egg mix into the well.

Mix the egg into the flour with a fork. Once it has absorbed, dust your hands with flour and start working the dough. If it is slightly dry, add a small drop of water. It will start off quite sticky but if you keep kneading and beating it about, it will become soft and smooth.
Once smooth, wrap it in cling film and refrigerate for 20 minutes.

Once it has cooled, take the dough from the fridge. Cut it into quarters. Take 1 quarter, place it on a surface covered with flour and roll it out with a rolling pin. Roll it thin. Half the thickness of a 10p piece. It doesn’t matter if it is a bit thicker but the thinner the better.
Cut out circles with a cutter. Each quarter of the dough should give you 8 circles. You’ll need 32 circles to make 16 ravioli.
Lay out the circles. Place a little dollop of filling in the centre of 16 of them.

Run water around the edge of the filling and put another pasta circle on top. Squeeze it down around the filling. Then take a fork and press down around the edges of the ravioli so it is sealed. Done!
Heat a pan of water and season with salt. Add your ravioli. They should take 4 minutes. They are ready when they all float to the top.
In the meantime, get your sauce on. Melt butter in a pan. Add sage leaves and 12 drops of lemon juice. When the butter starts to brown, remove from the heat.
Serving time. Place ravioli on a plate. Pour the butter sauce over the top. Add the crispy sage leaves, sprinkle over some extra Parmesan and bob's your uncle! Enjoy!

name: Homemade Cafe Patrón
description: We've come through for all your coffee Tequilla needs.
instructions: Cut open your vanilla pod and place it in the bottle of tequila. Leave that overnight in a safe space.
Add the freshly ground coffee to the bottle and put in the freezer for 5/6 hours to allow it to cold brew.
Take out and strain through a coffee filter into a large jug.
Now add your water and sugar to a pan and bring it to a simmer.
When the sugar mixture has dissolved, add the sieved coffee tequila to the bottle along with the sugar syrup and give it a good shake.
Serve up a big old shot and enjoy.

name: Homemade Cavatelli Pasta With Fresh Tomato Sauce
description: Handmade pasta has never been so easy! This is a naturally vegan pasta shape made famous across the South of Italy.
keywords: Homemade Cavatelli Pasta With Fresh Tomato Sauce
instructions: Arrange the flour making a small fountain with a well in the centre.
Add water and salt a little at a time and knead by hand until the water is absorbed.
Keep kneading the dough, the result will be a compact, smooth, homogeneous ball.
Cover the ball in cling film and let it rest for about half an hour so that the dough can be easily
After 30 mins, knead the dough a little bit before starting your cavatelli shaping. If you poke it with your thumb, the dough should slowly bounce back.
To shape your cavatelli, work one piece at a time and make a small roll from which you will take a chunk of around 1 cm wide.
Apply a little pressure against a tray or a plate or your working surface and dig the cavatello inside with your index and middle fingers, curling the edges.
If you want to decorate the cavatello, you can use a “rigagnocchi” paddle or a ridged butter paddle instead of a tray/plate.
Continue like this until you run out of dough.
Once you have finished, admire your amazing handmade pasta and don’t forget to sprinkle with a little bit of semolina so pasta won’t stick!

Your cavatelli are ready to be enjoyed with your preferred pasta sauce! Try them with a slow cooked fresh tomato sauce with some fresh basil and Parmesan cheese (or without cheese for the vegan version).
Gently crush 2 cloves of garlic with your hand or a knife.
Drizzle some extra virgin olive oil in a large pan and warm it up.
Add the garlic cloves and cook until golden, then remove them.
Add the cherry tomatoes (previously cut into halves) and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add the fresh basil and let the sauce cook on a gentle heat for 15-20 mins.
The secret is to add a pinch of sugar to balance the acidity of the tomatoes and if you like a little spicy kick, add some chilli flakes or fresh chilli to the garlic. Buon appetito.

name: Homemade Chicken Broth
description: A good homemade chicken broth recipe is the basis of so many wonderful dishes, so having a good one in your locker is invaluable. Use it to make a chicken noodle soup, if you fancy. Perfect for soups, stews, and more. Enjoy rich, nutritious broth in just a few simple steps.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Cut the onion into quarters, keeping the skin on. Half the leek and wash really well, then cut into chunks. Peel the carrot and cut into chunky pieces along with the celery. Divide everything between two large roasting trays, then do the same with the chicken wings. Season both trays well with salt and drizzle with a little olive oil.
Roast for 1 hour, flipping everything halfway until golden and caramelised.

Scrape everything from the trays into your largest saucepan. Pour cold water into the two trays and put them back in the oven for 5 mins. Remove and scrape the trays well with a wooden spoon or spatula to remove all of the crusty bits from the bottom, then pour all of this into the large pan.
Pour 3L of cold water into the pan and add the peppercorns and bay leaves.
Put over a high heat and bring to a gentle simmer. Use a ladle to scoop any fat or scum that floats to the top, and discard.
Simmer gently for 6 hours, then carefully strain through a metal sieve.

name: Homemade Ciabatta
description: You can't beat the smell freshly baked bread. And this simple ciabatta recipe is your one-way ticket to making your kitchen smell delicious.
instructions: The night before you want to make your ciabatta, make the overnight biga. Tip the flour, warm water and yeast into a bowl and mix really well until no lumps of flour remain. Cover with cling film with a small hole poked into it and leave for 12 hours.

The next day make the dough. Tip the flour, warm water, oil, salt and overnight biga into a large bowl and use clean hands to mix everything together until fully incorporated. It’ll feel like a scarily wet dough but stick with it!

Leave for 30 mins covered with the cling flim then wet your hands and pick up a corner of the dough, stretch it up without ripping it and fold it towards you, up and over the dough. Repeat with the other three corners, wetting your hands each time. You should feel the dough tighten up a little as you go. Repeat this every 30 minutes for another 1 hour, then leave the dough to prove for a further 1 ½ hours untouched (so 3 hours in total).
Get a rectangular baking tray (roughly 20 × 30cm/8 × 12in) with a slight lip ready and cut two large, long strips of baking paper, flour them.

Tip the dough out onto a heavily floured work surface (this dough can be a sticky beast) and flour the top. Shape into a rough square using clean floured hands, then use a knife or dough scraper to cut into two rough rectangles – don’t worry if they’re not perfect. Carefully place each onto the pieces of baking paper and lift onto the tray, placing the loaves alongside each other – this will help them keep their shape. Don’t be too rough with the dough, you want to keep all those bubbles and air.
Leave for 1 hour to prove.
Heat the oven to 220°C and put a heavy baking sheet or pizza stone in to heat up for at least 30 mins.

When ready to bake, lightly flour the baking sheet or stone, then carefully flip each ciabatta onto it. Repeat with the other loaf then bang in the oven for 20 minutes until golden brown and hollow when tapped on the bottom.
Cool on a wire rack then serve with oil and vinegar for dipping.

name: Homemade Cooking Chorizo
description: Level up your Mexican cooking by making your own chorizo. It’s delicious, easy to make and will completely transform your Mexican dishes.
instructions: Remove the stems and seeds from the dried guajillos and ancho chillies. Place the chillies in a bowl and cover with boiling water. Set aside for around 10 mins to rehydrate.

Once soft and hydrated, remove the chillies from the water and place them in a high-speed blender along with the vinegar, all the spices, vegetable oil and salt. Blitz well until smooth (this is the adobo for the chorizo).
Pass the adobo through a sieve to remove any bits that did not blend properly.
In a large bowl, mix the minced pork and the adobo until all the meat is well combined with the adobo.

Leave to rest for at least 2 hrs before cooking with it. You can store the chorizo in a plastic Tupperware container, in sandwich bags or in sausage cases. Or, divide it into small sausage-sized pieces, wrap them in cling film then wrap them again in tin foil or pop in a sandwich bag and store in the freezer. The chorizo will keep in the fridge for up to 4 days or freezer for up to 3 months.

name: Homemade Crisps
description: Making crisps from scratch actually doesn't take too much. Here, we're perfected the ultimate crisp recipe, and even made a sweet chilli seasoning to go with.
instructions: Slice the potatoes about 3mm thick and place in a large bowl. Rinse in cold water until the water runs clear, then soak for 30 mins in water with your vinegar.
Heat a large, deep pan about ⅓ full with oil to 160ºC. Meanwhile, drain the potatoes and dry them very well with kitchen towels.
Fry in batches (they will take longer if you overcrowd the pan), stirring as you first add them, until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper and season lightly with salt or spice mix.
Eat immediately, or allow to cool, then store in an airtight container (they should be good for 24 hours or so).

Add the first 7 of the spices to a spice grinder or a pestle along with ½ tbsp of parsley and 1 tbsp of sugar, then blitz or pound until dusty. Stir through the remaining ½ tbsp of parsley and ½ tbsp of sugar until combined. When the crisps have come out of the oil, tip into a bowl and toss with the seasoning in batches. Simple.

name: Homemade Doner Kebabs
description:
This homemade doner kebab recipe couldn't be easier. It's all about spicing the lamb mince, and this flavour combo is the one.
Lamb doner kebabs at home offer a delicious, flavorful experience that's both satisfying and customizable. Originating from Turkey, these kebabs feature tender, spiced lamb cooked on a vertical rotisserie, creating a savory, juicy delight. When made at home, you can enjoy the same mouthwatering taste without needing a specialized rotisserie. By marinating lamb in a blend of yogurt, garlic, and aromatic spices like cumin and paprika, you'll infuse it with rich flavor. Cooking it on a grill or in the oven ensures a crispy exterior while keeping the inside succulent. Whether served in warm flatbread with fresh vegetables and tangy sauces or alongside sides like salad or rice, homemade lamb doner kebabs are versatile and perfect for any meal. Enjoy the satisfaction of recreating this street food classic in your own kitchen, adding your personal touch to every bite.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Throw the mince into a bowl. Add cumin, fennel seeds, cayenne and dried oregano. Add grated garlic clove. Season with salt and pepper. Mush everything together.
Form the mince into a fat sausage, similar to an aubergine shape. Wrap it tightly in tin foil and place in the oven for 30 mins.
Tzatziki time. Grab a bowl. Add your yogurt, grated cucumber (squeeze the gratings to remove excess water), the juice of a lemon, salt and pepper. Mix together. Cover and whack in the fridge.

Pickled onion time. Grab a bowl. Add a finely sliced red onion, the juice of a lemon and a pinch of salt. Scrunch the salt and lemon juice into the onions. Leave out until you serve. (The acidity of the lemon will take the sharpness out the onion).
After 30 mins, remove the lamb from the oven. Remove the tin foil. Place it under the grill for 2 mins on each side so it gets brown and crispy. Watch that it doesn't burn.
Remove the doner from the oven. Slice it thinly with a sharp knife.
Add a big handful of parsley to your pickled onions.
Assembly time. Take a warm pitta. Dollop in some tzatziki and add some doner strips. Spoon in some pickled onion, dollop on a bit more tzatziki and tuck in!

name: Homemade Falafel
description: Falafels. They’re delicious. We've come up with the ultimate falafel recipe here that you can make at home. It's well worth the effort.
instructions: In a large bowl, add the dried chickpeas and split fava beans, cover completely with cool water and leave to soak for at least 12 hours, up to 24 as a max. They should plump up to almost twice their size. Drain and rinse.
Trim and chop the onion into quarters. Trim the spring onion, and chop into thirds. Trim and peel the garlic. Trim the chilli and roughly chop the herbs.

Add the chickpeas and fava beans into a food processor and pulse until the mixture breaks down into a finely ground crumb – do this in batches to not overcrowd the processor. Then, tip into a large bowl.

Add the onion, garlic, chilli, herbs and ground cumin into the food processor and pulse until almost puréed, it should be very finely chopped with no large chunks. Add this into the bowl with the chickpea and fava beans. Stir the olive oil in, and mix thoroughly.

Stir through the baking powder, 1 tbsp of salt and sesame seeds. Cover and place in the fridge for at least 30 mins, up to 1 day – this will help the dough firm up and make it easier to shape. Once cold, scoop 2 tbsp of the falafel mixture (if you want large falafels use more mixture) and shape into balls, don’t compact them too much. Place on a baking tray, continue shaping until no mixture remains.

Once you’re ready to fry, fill a medium saucepan with the sunflower/vegetable oil. The amount of oil should not be more than ¾ of the capacity of your saucepan. Place on high heat and heat up to 180°C. Test the oil to see if it’s ready by putting a wooden chopstick into the oil, it should bubble but not aggressively.

Once hot, fry the falafel in batches of 4-6 at a time, until golden brown on both sides and cooked through, 5-6 mins. Using a slotted spoon or a spider, transfer the cooked falafels onto a kitchen paper lined plate or tray. Continue frying until all the falafels are cooked. Enjoy the falafels as a wrap or as a side, while still crispy and hot.

name: Homemade Hash Browns
description: Making hash browns hungover might seem like a big fuss, so instead of making 12 little fiddly hashy b’s, just make one massive crispy fella. Dead easy.
instructions: Peel and coarsely grate the potatoes. This works best with a food processor with a grater attachment if you’ve got one, but a box grater will work just fine! I’d reach for the food processor if the hangover is anything above a 6/10. Try to make the spud strands as long as you can.
Rinse the potato 3 or 4 times in cold water to remove excess starch and dry thoroughly with a salad spinner or clean tea towels.
Set a large, non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and add 5-6 tbsp of olive oil. Add the potatoes in an even layer, press down into a big hash brown shape and season thoroughly.

Cook for 10-15 mins until brown and crisp and flip out onto a plate. Add another 1-2 tbsp of oil to the pan and return the hash brown, uncooked-side down. Cook for another 10-15 mins until full crisp and cooked through. Chop that big crispy hash brown into chunks and break out the sauce. Get stuck in.

name: Homemade Labneh With Spicy Olive Butter
description: This spicy and olive-heavy labneh is the perfect dinner party dip. Never made homemade labneh before? Your life is about to change.
keywords: Homemade Labneh with Spicy Olive Butter
instructions: Start by lining a sieve over a bowl with a J-Cloth. Tip in the yoghurt and leave to strain for 1-2 hours, or overnight, depending on the thickness of your yoghurt and the texture of labneh you’re after.

To make the spiced butter, set a small saucepan over a medium heat. Add the butter and cook until nut brown. Finely grate in the garlic and sizzle for 30 secs. Tip in the aleppo pepper and season with salt, lemon zest and juice and finely chopped sage.
Squash the green olives with the heel of your hand and chuck them into the butter. Thinly slice the red onion.

To serve, swoosh the labneh over a large serving platter. Top with the warm spiced olive butter and scatter over the herbs and sliced red onion. Serve with crudites (on ice if you’re feeling fancy) and warm grilled bread.

name: Homemade Lamb Burgers
description: Pomegranate seeds + spiced lamb patties = a match made in culinary heaven.
instructions: Finely chop your onion and cloves of garlic.
Gently fry them until soft, then your cumin.
Remove from the heat and tip into a bowl. Add the lamb mince and chopped parsley. Mix together and then make 8 thin patties.
Place on a plate and put into the fridge for 20 minutes to firm up.
Now for the feta topping. Add your feta, yoghurt, a handful of chopped mint, the juice of half a lemon and the pomegranate seeds to a bowl. Mix them all together. Done.
Take out your patties. Place on a very hot griddle pan and cook for 3 minutes each side. At the same time, toast your ciabatta rolls.

To serve, place a dollop of the feta topping on the base of the roll. Then add a patty. Then more topping, then another patty, then any leftover mint leaves and pomegranate seeds you have, and then the top of the roll. Enjoy!

name: Homemade Mr Whippy
description: Always wanted to make a Mr Whippy at home? Well, we've cracked the recipe. This easy ice cream recipe is an awfully tasty way to cool off.
instructions: Line a large baking tin with cling film, making sure there's some overhang.

Pour the cream into a large bowl and whisk into soft peaks. Pour in the condensed milk, vanilla extract and sea salt. Fold it to combine, then pour into your lined baking tin. Transfer to the freezer and set for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

Cut off the end of a piping bag, and use a star nozzle if you have one, it's not essential but I like it. Using the cling film to help you, remove the ice cream from the baking tin and cut into pieces. Quickly transfer to a large mixing bowl and whip up using an electric whisk, or if you have it – a stand mixer. Scoop it into your piping bag and swirl into cones. Top with your choice of toppings and get stuck in!

name: Homemade Pesto Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
description: The zesty, pestoey sweet potato mix in this dish is nothing short of divine. The lemon zest works wonders. Absolute wonders.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F
Place sweet potatoes in baking tray. Drizzle olive oil over the top. Season with salt and pepper, and add a teaspoon of chilli flakes. Place in oven for 50 minutes.

Now for the pesto. In a frying pan add the cloves of chopped garlic and a teaspoon of chilli flakes. Just before the garlic starts browning, add your spinach leaves. Add a small cup of water to help the spinach wilt. Cooking for 30 seconds or so – you don’t want the spinach to completely lose it’s shape.
Remove pan from heat and place the spinach into a bowl.
Toasting the pine nuts. Place your nuts into a frying pan. No oil. Medium heat. They should take 3 minutes or so. Keep jiggling them about to make sure they don’t burn.
Once cooked, add to the spinach bowl.
Grate parmesan. Add most of it to the mixing bowl. Add the zest of one lemon, and the juice of half the lemon. Add a handful of chopped basil.
After 50 minutes, remove sweet potatoes from oven. Slice them along the top and remove flesh. Add flesh to the mixing bowl, and set the skins aside.
Mix everything together in the bowl, and then refill the sweet potato skins.
Finish with a scattering of leftover pine nuts, parmesan and basil. Squeeze a few drops of lemon over the top, and Bob’s Your Uncle.

name: Homemade Potato Smileys
description: This is it – our homemade version of potato smileys. Smiley potato faces made with real mashed potatoes. You're not going to believe how good these are.
instructions: Peel the potatoes and add to a large saucepan. Cover with cold water and a large pinch of salt. Bring to the boil and cook for 20 mins, or until totally soft. Drain in a colander until dry to the touch, then push the potatoes through a potato ricer, or press through a sieve into a large bowl.
Add the breadcrumbs and cornflour and a tbsp of table salt and mix well. Tip onto a clean surface to bring together, then return to the bowl. Cover and set aside in the fridge for 20 mins.
Fill a large saucepan halfway up with vegetable oil and heat to 180°C.

Grab a two sheets of baking paper. Cut the dough into four and take one of the quarters and place in the middle of the baking paper, press down then top with the other sheet of baking paper. Use a rolling pin to roll it out to around 1cm thickness. Peel away the top baking sheet, then use a glass to cut circle shapes into the rolled out dough. Use a straw to create the eyes, then carefully cut the mouths with the tip of a sharp knife.
Use a spatula to transfer the smileys into the hot oil, cook for 2-3 mins, until golden brown. Set aside to drain on kitchen paper, season with a pinch of salt.
Repeat with the rest of the dough, then give all the finished smileys a quick reheat in a hot oven if you need to. Serve with a big fat dollop ketchup.

name: Homemade Soup Dumplings (Xiao Long Bao)
description: These chubby homemade soup dumplings are bursting with flavour. Literally. You won't find an easier xiao long bao recipe than this.
instructions: Into a small pot, combine all the ingredients except the gelatine leaves, and bring to a boil for 8 mins with a lid, just to infuse the aromatics into the liquid.
In the meantime soak the gelatine leaves in a bowl of cold tap water for 3 mins or until softened like contact lenses, squeeze the excess liquid out and set aside.

Take the small pot off the heat and add all the gelatine leaves, mix until dissolved then strain into a shallow pasta bowl. When cool enough, place it into the freezer for 30 mins to quickly set up, then leave in the fridge for another 30 mins or until needed. This can be done up to 2 days before.

Grab a large bowl and add flour, oil and salt and add ¾ of the boiled water, leaving a little water behind. Use a chopstick or the back of a wooden spoon to mix everything, then use your hands and create a dough ball. If the dough ball feels dry add some of the remaining water and knead until it is soft and feels like play-dough. It should not be stuck to your fingers, just add more flour if this happens.
Knead for 2 mins or until smooth, cover in cling film or throw into a sandwich bag, set aside for at least 25 mins. This dough can be made up to 2 nights before.
Grab a large bowl and add all the ingredients into the bowl except for the spring onions and water/chicken stock. Use a fork or chopsticks, to mix in one direction until a big meatball forms.

Add the water/chicken stock in 2 parts, mixing in between until the meatball absorbs the liquid, then add the renaming liquid. Finely slice the spring onions and mix just until it is evenly incorporated. Clingfilm the bowl and leave in the fridge until needed.

When the jelly is fully set, use a knife to score the jelly into small cubes, roughly the size of peas. Then scoop all jelly onto the dumpling filling and use a spatula to mix until the jelly is evenly incorporated into the dumpling filling, cling film and leave in the fridge.

Prep the steamer basket by cutting a circle of baking paper that fits the bakers, then cut multiple finger-sized holes so that steam can escape, then lightly oil the baking paper and leave inside the steamer basket and set aside.
Roll the dough into a log the width of a round cherry tomato and use scissors to cut into 25 pieces, slightly smaller than the size of a cherry tomato, or 12g each if you want to be exact.
In a small pot combine a 1:1 ratio of cornflour and flour and mix with fingers, use this for dusting.

Lightly dust all the pieces of dough and toss with your hands to lightly coat. Turn the pieces of dough upwards so the sticky part is facing you, then use the fattest part of your palm to press down firmly, revealing a coin shape. Repeat for all the dough pieces, then cover with a lightly damp tea towel to prevent them from drying out.

Using the dusting flour, roll out each piece of dough, roughly 10 cm in diameter, trying to keep the centre of the wrapper a bit thicker than the edges of the wrapper. Lightly dust each side if needed, then place onto a sheet of cling film, and lightly cover with cling film.
Repeat to all pieces of dough, stacking the wrapper on top of each other, making sure to lightly dust between each wrapper and always covering with the cling film, to prevent it drying out.

Place 1 Tbsp of filling in the center of a wrapper and create multiple folds around the filling, making sure to seal it super tight by pinching everything together in the centre. Alternatively fold the dumpling like a tortellini, which is very simple. Fold the dumpling in half and seal all the edges like a purse.

Use your pinky finger to lightly dent the middle of the dumpling and the fold the edges together and squeeze to seal, to create a tortellini shape. Place it into the steamer basket. Repeat folding the dumplings as desired, ensuring whatever method you choose, they are tightly sealed and add the dumplings to the steamer basket giving 3 cm space between all the dumplings.

Find a saucepan that snugly fits the steamer baskets, and fill the pan ½ way with water. Bring the water to a boil, then add the steamer basket and reduce the heat medium low. Steam for 8 minutes and reveal.
In the meantime combine vinegar and thin slices of ginger together for the dipping sauce.

When eating, do not burn your mouth, these are pockets of boiling soup. Place a dumpling onto a spoon, pour a tsp of vinegar, poke or bite a small hole to release the heat, drink the soup to test the temperature, then eat.

name: Homemade Spinach and Ricotta Cannelloni
description: Spinach and ricotta is the perfect filling for your Cannelloni. A lovely, clean dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Start with the tomato sauce. Chop the cloves of garlic. Fry in a pan with a glug of olive oil until soft.
Pour in your tins of tomatoes. Add a splash of water to the tins to get all the leftover tomato off the sides, and pour that in.
Pour in your balsamic vinegar, and let that simmer until it resembles a thick sauce. Add a handful of chopped basil, season with salt and pepper, remove from the heat and set aside.

Filling time. Wilt all your spinach in a pan. Squeeze it so you get rid of any excess water, and then chop it up. Put in a bowl, and add your ricotta, half your Italian style hard cheese (grated), the zest of a lemon, some salt, pepper and olive oil. Mix everything together.
Stuffing time. Spoon the filling into any bag with a corner. Cut a little hole in the corner, and then squeeze the filling into the cannelloni tubes. Line the tubes up in a baking dish.
Cover the stuffed tubes with tomato sauce. Top everything with slices of mozzarella. Grate the rest of the Italian style hard cheese over the top.
Place in an oven for 30 minutes or until the cheese is golden. Bish bash bosh. Done. Enjoy!

name: Homemade Sweet Chilli Jam
description: A savoury jam with a gently hot, red-peppery flavour. Recipe by MOB Contributor Thomas Colson
instructions: Chop your chillies and bell peppers and blend finely in a food processor.
In a large saucepan, add the sugar and vinegar and bring the mixture to the boil.
Add your pepper and chilli mixture to the saucepan and cook for 10 minutes.
Allow your mixture to cool down for at least an hour.
Next, sterilise four jam jars by soaking them in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Add your jam to the jars let cool completely before enjoying.

name: Homemade Sweet Potato Gnocchi
description: Browned, rich butter over soft, plump little gnocchi. The roasted sweet potato makes this dish so rich and moreish. Enjoy.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Place 2 sweet potatoes on a baking tray and bake until soft.
Spoon out the flesh of the sweet potatoes and add to a bowl with a heaped tablespoon of ricotta, 40g of grated Parmesan and a small handful of chopped rosemary. Add a pinch of salt and mash together.

Add plain flour to the mix, bit by bit, mixing as you go. Once it is all mixed together, pick up the dough with your hands and form it into a lump. Remove the dough from the bowl and place on a floured surface.
Cut the dough into quarters. Take one quarter and roll it out into a long sausage. Cut up the sausage into little gnocchis at regular intervals.

Once you have cut up all the gnocchis, get a pan of water on the heat. Once the water starts boiling, add your gnocchi. After 4 minutes, it should float to the top. Cook for a further 30 seconds. Remove the gnocchi from the water, drain and drizzle with some olive oil.
Sauce time. Add 3 tablespoons of butter to a frying pan. When it starts browning, add a tablespoon of rosemary leaves and 1 crushed garlic clove. Fry for 30 seconds.
Add spinach. Once it has wilted, pour in your gnocchi. Coat the gnocchi in the butter and season with salt and pepper. Remove the pan from the heat.
To serve, spoon the gnocchi into a bowl. Grate on some Parmesan and dollop on some ricotta cheese. Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Homemade Turkey Twizzlers
description: Ever wanted to make your own turkey twizzlers at home? Now you can with our homemade turkey twizzlers recipe.
instructions: Get a pan of water on to the boil, then pop the sausages in, Cooking for 1 min until just set. Drain and steam dry, before skewering through the middle vertically. Using a small knife, cut around the sausage from top to bottom to create a spiral (take care not to cut all the way through, as the sausage should still be intact), then spread the sausage out a bit.

Whisk the eggs on a shallow plate. Tip the flour, mustard powder, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika and some salt and pepper onto another shallow plate. Add the breadcrumbs to a third plate. Dip the skewers into the flour, making sure to get it in all the gaps, then roll in the egg (drain off the excess), before rolling in the breadcrumbs.
Heat an air-fryer to 200°C and add the skewers. Cook for 12-15 mins. Serve with potato smileys and a big blob of ketchup.

name: Homemade Udon Noodles
description: I think we can all agree your average shop bought udon noodles are just not as good as the homemade stuff. This homemade udon noodles recipe is easy as it gets.
instructions: Add the water and salt into a measuring jug and mix until dissolved.
Add the plain flour into a large bowl. Using your hands stir ¾ of the salty water though, until incorporated and a dough forms. Add more water, a little at a time if the dough is too dry and crumbly.
Transfer the dough into a large sandwich bag and close, leaving a small opening. Let the dough rest for 30 mins.
Sandwich the dough bag between 2 clean tea towels. Using the heel of your feet, step on top of the dough to flatten. Continue doing this until the dough has flattened completely.

Remove the dough from the bag and fold in the edges to ball the dough up again. Place back in the bag, close, leaving a small opening. Place between the tea towel and repeat flattening it. Repeat this step 4-6 times, until the dough is smooth (it should feel as soft as an earlobe).
Once soft, fold in the edges to make a ball and place in the bag, entirely closed and let rest for 2 hours up to overnight.

Once rested, lightly dust a clean work surface with cornflour. Flatten the dough with your hand, then roll it out into a rectangle until 5mm thick (you can make them thicker or thinner if you want). Dust some more cornflour onto the dough then fold the longest length into halves or thirds.
With a sharp knife, slice 5-7mm strips of noodles, unroll them and dust with more cornflour so that they don’t stick (you can make them thicker or thinner if you want).

Bring a large saucepan of unsalted water to the boil. Once boiling, drop the noodles in, cook for 8-10 mins (depending on the thickness of the noodle), then drain and rinse under cold water - this will help firm up the noodles, creating that chewy texture.
Serve in your broth or sauce of choice and add your toppings.

name: Homemade Wontons
description: A foolproof recipe for homemade wontons. We love them in a rich, soothing broth or dunked into chilli vinegar.
instructions: If you are making the broth, you're going to need to prep your veggies. Finely slice your fresh ginger and carrots before chunking your spring onions. Now, add all the ingredients into a large pot, bring to a boil and simmer for 20 mins. Optionally use a sieve to remove all the bits, keeping just the mushrooms and broth for serving.

Finely dice shiitake mushrooms and add to a large mixing bowl. Roughly cut the prawns into ¼ chunks, and add half to the bowl. Finely dice and mince the other half the prawns until a sticky paste forms and add to the mixing bowl. Add all the remaining ingredients except the water and mix in one direction with a fork or chopstick until a large meatball forms. Then add the liquid in two parts and mix until the meatball has absorbed it, then add remaining and mix until absorbed again. Cling film the bowl and leave in the fridge for at least 10 mins.

If making noodles, boil the noodles now. Whilst the noodles are boiling add the pak choi for just one minute to cook and then remove and set aside. Drain the noodles and toss well with a little sesame oil and set aside on a plate.

To make the wontons, Add just a tsp of filling in the centre of the wrapper, with 1 chunk of prawn. Fold in half like a purse and bring the edges into the middle. Use the filling as glue to seal around it, and allow the excess dough to hang - as this will be eaten like a noodle. Just ensure the wrapper is tightly sealed around the filing so nothing leaks when boiled. Place onto a large plate and cover with a lightly damp tea towel, so they don’t dry out and repeat.
You can now freeze as many wonton as you’d like. If freezing, place wontons on pieces of parchment for easy removal in future.

In a large pot of boiling water, add as many many wontons as desired. When the wontons float, add a cup of cold water to deflate the bubbles, and bring to a boil one more time. Serve straight into bowls or add to a large plate, tossed with sesame oil to prevent them from sticking.
If you're making wonton noodle soup, grab a serving bowl and assemble the soup, noodles, wonton, pak choi and finish with chilli oil, sliced spring onions and a drizzle of sesame oil.
If you choose the chilli oil vinegar add all the ingredients into a serving bowl, with the hot dumpling water, wontons, and serve with sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

name: Homity Pie Recipe
description: This homity pie is a British vegetarian classic. Stuffed with loads of cheese, potato and onion, it is comfort food at its best. And the best part is you don’t need to pre-bake the pastry beforehand. Serve hot with some charred Tenderstem or at room temp with a mustardy green salad instead.
instructions: Start with the pastry. Make sure your butter is cold, and then cut it into small cubes. Put into a food processor along with both of the flours and a pinch of salt. Blitz until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs then crack in the egg and pulse again until the pastry is just coming together, then bring together with your hands. Wrap in cling film and chill in the fridge for 20 mins.

Meanwhile, peel and chop your potatoes into chunky 4cm pieces. Put into a large pan of cold salted water and bring up to the boil. Once boiling, cook for 12-15 mins until the potatoes are tender, drain into a colander and steam well. Tip back into the saucepan and cover with a lid.

Come back to the pastry. Roll it out on a floured work surface into a rough circle large enough to line the base and sides of a deep, 20cm pie dish or, if you haven’t got one, a 20cm springform, deep cake tin. You want the pastry to be about 27-30cm in circumference. Line the base and sides with the pastry, pushing it well into all the edges. Trim off any excess pastry hanging over the edge, then put back into the fridge to chill whilst you carry on with the filling.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Put a flat baking tray into the centre of the oven to heat up.

Halve the leek, wash thoroughly to get rid of any grit and finely slice. Half and finely slice the onions. Scrape both into a large saucepan. Add the butter and a splash of olive oil along with a big pinch of salt. Cook over a low-medium heat for 15 mins, stirring occasionally until super soft and beginning to caramelise.

Finely chop the garlic, strip the thyme leaves from their sprigs. Add both to the pan, cook, stirring for another couple of minutes, then tip in the cooked potatoes. Pour in the double cream and grate in the nutmeg, give everything a good stir to combine and turn off the heat.

Finely grate all of the cheese. Stir two thirds of the cheese through the filling, season with a little salt and lots of black pepper to taste, then spoon the filling into the chilled unbaked pie case. Scatter the remaining cheese over the top of the filling.

Put the pie onto the preheated baking sheet and bake for 40-45 mins until the pastry is golden and crisp. If the cheese catches and starts to brown too quickly, place a piece of foil very loosely over the top (the filling might look done but you need to cook it for 40 minutes so the pastry fully cooks).
Leave to cool for at least 20 mins before removing from the tin and slicing into fat wedges to serve.

name: Honey & Ginger Braised Chicken Legs With Fluffy Rice
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Let the slow cooker do all the work, simply sear off your chook and bung it all in the pot and go put your feet up. Scoop up the ingredients from Aldi.
keywords: Honey & Ginger Braised Chicken Legs With Fluffy Rice
instructions: Grab your chicken legs and split into drum and thigh by cutting straight down through the joint.

Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Season the chicken legs thoroughly with salt and pepper and add to the pan, skin-side down with a shot of oil. Cook until the skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip ‘em over and seal the other side.
While the chicken is cooking, peel and crush the garlic cloves and finely slice the ginger and one of the chillies. Chunk up two of your spring onions.
Add the browned chicken to your slow cooker and add the chopped aromatics to the hot chicken pan. Sauté for 1 min and add to the slow cooker bowl.

Mix the soy, ketchup and honey together and pour all over the chicken. Set your slow cooker to high and cook for 4 hours until very tender and glazed with the sauce. Remove the chicken from the sauce and set aside. You can strain out the aromatics if you like, but the squishy, slow-cooked garlic cloves and spring onions are delicious, so we like to keep ‘em in!
Heat up the rice according to the package instructions.
Finely slice the remaining spring onion and chilli for garnish.
Serve your beautifully tender, glazed chicken over the steamy rice and finish with extra spring onions and chilli.

name: Honey & Ginger Margarita
description: This margarita is everything you'd want and need when the sun is out. It's got a nice balance of sweet and heat.
instructions: Place your ginger in a cocktail shaker and using a blunt object squish it to a pulp.
Add in your lime, honey, tequila, Cointreau, and ice.
Shake for 10 seconds.
Double strain into a glass filled with ice.
Top with ginger beer and then garnish with candied ginger skewered with a tooth pick, or garnish with a lime wedge.

name: Honey & Mustard Roasted Chicken Legs
description: Crispy chicken legs with a sticky honey mustard glaze and crunchy fennel salad to keep everything fresh. This one's easy, delicious and perfect for a weeknight. Don’t skip the crusty baguette at the end to soak up all those chicken-y juices.
keywords: Honey & Mustard Roasted Chicken Legs Recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Season the chicken legs well with salt and pepper. Lay them skin-side up in your largest roasting tray, then drizzle over 1 tbsp olive oil. Roast for 30 mins.
Add olive oil, mustard, honey and the zest and lemon juice into a separate salad bowl. Whisk together and season with salt and pepper to taste – this is your salad dressing.
Now mix the olive oil, mustard and honey into a small bowl for the chicken. Whisk together with a fork and set aside.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a small, dry frying pan over a high heat until browned and beginning to pop. Set aside.

Once the chicken has been roasting for 30 mins, add the grapes to the tray then pour the honey and mustard mix over the chicken legs. Baste with some of the chicken fat from the bottom of the pan, then return to the oven for 20 mins until the chicken is cooked through and crisp and the grapes are starting to burst.

While the chicken is having its final roast, make your salad. Very finely slice the fennel, saving the green fronds, then toss in the salad dressing. Slice the cucumber, then add this too. Separate and tear the Little Gem leaves, add to the salad along with the toasted pumpkin seeds, then toss everything together. Taste and add more lemon juice if it needs it.
Serve the roasted chicken legs and grapes alongside the salad in the middle of the table for people to help themselves, alongside a baguette for mopping up.

name: Honey BBQ Cheesy Beef Sliders
description: Sweet, sticky, and oh-so satisfying. These high-protein beef sliders are an excellent high-protein dinner.
keywords: Honey BBQ Cheesy Beef Sliders recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

For the seasoned beef, slice the onions lengthways. Heat a glug of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat, and cook the onions with the balsamic vinegar until softened. Add the beef to the pan and cook until browned and cooked through.
Add the BBQ seasoning, passata, tomato purée, Worcestershire sauce and honey to the pan with the beef. Season with salt and pepper and mix together. Leave to simmer for a couple of minutes.
Halve the burger buns and lay out the bottoms in a large baking dish. Drizzle over the BBQ sauce, followed by the seasoned beef and grated mozzarella and cheddar cheese.

Meanwhile, melt the butter and mince the garlic and parsley then combine in a ramekin. Add the tops of the buns to the filled bottoms, then brush over the garlic and herb mix. Sprinkle over the sesame seeds.
Loosely cover the dish with foil and bake in the oven for 10 mins, removing the foil halfway through.

name: Honey Chipotle Air Fryer Salmon
description: This honey chipotle air fryer salmon is perfect for meal prep. Combine it with your choice of carb, veg and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
keywords: Honey Chipotle Air Fryer Salmon Bowl
Honey Chipotle Air Fryer Salmon Bowl recipe
instructions: To make the marinade, add the ancho chilli paste, honey and the juice of your limes to a bowl and mix to combine.
Pop the salmon on a plate, skin-side down. Use a spoon to coat the salmon with the marinade. Set aside at room temperature for 10 mins.
Place the salmon in the air fryer and cook at 180°C for 8-10 mins (depending on the thickness of your salmon) until cooked through.
Optional: If batch cooking for the week, transfer the salmon to a container and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Honey Chipotle Air Fryer Salmon Bowl
description: Sticky, sweet and spicy salmon with a zingy black bean and corn salad. This one’s healthy and fresh but feels like a treat.
keywords: Honey Chipotle Air Fryer Salmon Bowl
Honey Chipotle Air Fryer Salmon Bowl recipe
instructions: To make the marinade, add the ancho chilli paste, ½ the honey and the juice of ½ your limes to a bowl and mix to combine.
Pop the salmon on a plate, skin-side down. Use a spoon to coat the salmon with the marinade. Set aside at room temperature for 10 mins.
For the pickled red onions, finely slice the red onion and add to a bowl along with the juice of ½ the remaining lime and a pinch of salt. Mix to combine then set aside until ready to serve.
Place the salmon in the air fryer and cook at 180°C for 8-10 mins (depending on the thickness of your salmon) until cooked through.
For the salad, add the olive oil, remaining honey and the juice of the remaining limes to a large salad bowl along with a pinch of salt and pepper. Whisk to combine.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and dice the avocado. Drain and rinse the beans. Drain the sweetcorn. Thinly slice the chilli. Add all to the salad bowl and mix to combine.
Reserve a few coriander leaves for garnish. Finely chop the rest and toss through the salad before serving.
To serve, divide the salad between plates then top with the salmon and pickled onions. Finish with a dollop of yoghurt and the coriander leaves. Serve with tortilla chips, if you like.

name: Honey Fried Halloumi & Kale Salad with Yoghurt Dressing
description: Honey-coated halloumi is the perfect addition to this summery salad. It's fresh, it's healthy, and the high-protein yoghurt dressing will help you hit your macros.
keywords: Honey-Fried Halloumi & Kale Salad with Yoghurt Dressing
Honey-Fried Halloumi & Kale Salad with Yoghurt Dressing recipe
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Slice the halloumi into 1cm-thick slices. Set a large frying pan over a medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and fry the halloumi until golden on both sides (about 1-2 mins each side).
Meanwhile, finely chop the dill and slice the avocado. Set aside.
While still over the heat, drizzle the halloumi with the honey and sprinkle over the dill and chilli flakes. Fry for a few more minutes.
Slice the courgette into rounds and lay onto a baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil and slide under the grill for 5 mins, until a little charred. Set aside to cool slightly.
Coarsely chop the kale and place in a large bowl with the cooked courgette, bulgur and lentils.
For the dressing, finely grate the garlic clove and juice the lemon. Transfer both to a bowl along with the remaining dressing ingredients. Mix well.
Stir the dressing through the kale salad and season with salt. Divide the salad between deep plates and top with the fried halloumi and avocado.

name: Honey Garlic Chicken with Broccoli Rice
description: A sweet, sticky and spicy honey garlic chicken that’s packed with flavour. Served with broccoli rice, it’s the perfect packed lunch or meal prep dinner.
keywords: Honey Garlic Chicken with Broccoli Rice
Honey Garlic Chicken with Broccoli Rice recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Dice the broccoli into small pieces. Cook the rice following pack instructions, adding the broccoli 4 mins before the end of the cooking time.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the spring onions. Dice the chicken into 3cm pieces. In a bowl or flat tray, mix the garlic powder, chilli powder, flour and a pinch of salt.
Toss the chicken in the mix to coat evenly, then transfer to a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Slide into the hot oven to roast for 15-20 mins, until cooked through.

Mince the garlic then add to a bowl along with the gochujang, soy sauce, honey and the juice of the limes. Mix to combine then pour over the chicken and pop it back in the oven for another 5 mins until sticky.
Box or plate up the broccoli rice, top with the sticky chicken, and drizzle over any remaining sauce. Scatter over the spring onions and sesame seeds. It will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Honey Gochujang Chicken Rigatoni
description: Creamy gochujang pasta with shredded chicken, lime and honey. A high-protein, no-nonsense midweek meal with real flavour.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Thinly slice the chives and grate the parmesan and set aside for later.
Drizzle the chicken breasts with olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Wrap them in foil to make a tight parcel and place onto a tray. Roast for 15–20 mins until cooked through.
Once boiling, add the pasta to the water and cook according to pack instructions until al dente.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Stir in the gochujang and tomato purée. Let it cook for 2-3 mins until darkened and fragrant. Pour in the cream and stir through the honey and lime juice. Let it bubble gently until thickened slightly. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Once the chicken is cooked, using 2 forks shred the meat ready to add to the pasta.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked pasta straight into the sauce, then toss through the shredded chicken until everything is glossy and coated.
Divide the pasta between bowls and finish with the grated Parmesan, a squeeze of lime juice and chopped chives.

name: Honey Harissa Camembert
description: The baked camembert of your dreams. Oozy cheese stuffed with sticky honey and spicy harissa paste? Yeah, go on then.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C.
Add your honey and harissa to a bowl. Mix to combine.

Cut a disc about 5cm wide out of the centre of your camembert,
leaving a layer on the bottom. Place it back in its wooden base,
making sure there is no plastic attached.

Spoon your harissa and honey mixture into the middle of your
camembert, then place the extra circle of camembert on top.
Bake for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, tear your pitta into bite-sized pieces. Finely chop your parsley.

Add a little olive oil to a frying pan and add your torn pitta. Fry
gently for 5 mins until your pitta is crispy, turning occasionally
to ensure they cook evenly. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and
parsley, then set aside.

Remove your pitta from the oven and dunk your pitta chips in it
whilst it is still hot.

name: Honey Harissa Carrot Couscous with Feta Dressing
description: A sweet, smoky, and tangy grain bowl featuring roasted honey-harissa carrots, crispy chickpeas, and a creamy feta dressing. Perfect for a vibrant and satisfying meal.
keywords: Honey Harissa Carrot Couscous with Feta Dressing
Honey Harissa Carrot Couscous with Feta Dressing recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C fan. Halve the carrots lengthways and cut into 4cm pieces.
In a small bowl, mix the honey and harissa.
Toss the carrots with a splash of olive oil, cinnamon, salt, and black pepper. Spread onto a baking tray and roast for 20-25 mins.
Pat dry the chickpeas and add them to the baking tray. Roast for another 15 mins until crispy. Once cooked, toss with the harissa-honey mixture.
Meanwhile, place the couscous in a bowl, season with salt, and cover with boiling water. Place a plate on top to trap the steam and let sit for 5 mins. Fluff with a fork
Mix the couscous with chopped parsley and chopped olives Season to taste.
In a blender, blitz the feta, Greek yoghurt, and lemon juice until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper.
To serve, divide the couscous into serving boxes, top with the roasted carrots, roasted chickpeas, and drizzle with the feta dressing. Refrigerate until needed. No need to reheat before serving.

name: Honey Harissa Carrots With Whipped Feta
description: Delicious, spicy sweet carrots on a bed of creamy whipped feta, perfect with some warm flatbreads.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C.
Trim the green tops off your carrots, then toss them into a roasting tray. Drizzle with olive oil, cinnamon and a pinch of salt and pepper. Roast for 30 mins.

Finely chop a handful of your carrot tops until you have about 2 tbsp worth. Add them to a pestle and mortar with the juice of a lemon and a drizzle of olive oil, then bash until you have a chunky green sauce.
Add your yoghurt into a medium-sized mixing bowl and crumble in your feta finely. Whisk until the feta has totally incorporated, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Drain your chickpeas and toss them onto your carrot roasting tray. Return them to the oven for 15 mins until they are crisp.
Mix your honey and harissa paste together in a bowl.
Pour your honey and harissa paste onto your carrots and chickpeas and give them a toss until they are all coated.
Spoon your whipped feta yoghurt onto a serving plate and top it with your chickpeas and carrots. Drizzle with your carrot top oil, then serve and enjoy with bread to dip into it.

name: Honey Mustard Chicken & Lentils
description: A little bit sweet and a little bit spicy, this honey mustard chicken recipe is a knock out.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Season your chicken leg with salt and black pepper and add to a foil-lined tray. Slide into the oven for 10 mins.

In a small mixing bowl combine the hot honey (if you can’t find hot honey, add 1 tsp of chilli flakes to regular honey!), mustard powder, and half of the sherry vinegar. Mix together and spoon over the chicken leg. Return to the oven for 10-15 mins, glazing now and then, until the chicken is cooked through.
While the chicken is finishing cooking, chunk up the cabbage, drain/unpack your lentils and pick the herbs.
Preheat a frying pan over a high heat. Add a shot of oil and, once very hot, tip in the cabbage. Stir-fry for 2-3 mins until the cabbage has taken on some good colour.

Add the lentils and toss through the cabbage. Add the remaining vinegar, a little olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. At the last minute, toss through the picked herbs and you’re all done.
Grab a plate and spread the yoghurt over the base. Top with the lentils and finally your sticky, spicy honey mustard chicken. Get stuck in.

name: Honey Mustard Chicken with Peas & Pancetta
description: Crispy pan-fried chicken thighs in a creamy tarragon sauce. Make the sauce ahead and keep in the freezer for a quick midweek meal.
keywords: honey mustard chicken with peas and pancetta
instructions: Pat the chicken skin dry with a paper towel and season with salt. Pop in the fridge for 15 mins.

Finely chop the shallot and garlic. Add a splash of olive oil to a cold, heavy-bottomed frying pan. Add the chicken, skin side down, and turn on the heat to medium. Cook the chicken for about 15 mins until the skin is deeply golden, then flip and cook for another 2 mins until cooked through. Remove to a plate and drain the fat to a bowl (you can use this in another recipe).

If your pancetta isn’t already diced, cut it into small pieces. Reduce the heat to low-medium and add the pancetta. Cook gently until the fat has rendered and the bacon is crispy. Remove from the pan, leaving about 1 tbsp of fat behind.

Add the shallots and garlic to the pan and cook for 5 mins until softened. Add the wine (this is optional so leave it out if you prefer) and leave to reduce. Add the stock and bring to a simmer, then add the cream. Simmer for 5 mins.
Add the honey, both types of mustard and frozen peas and cook for another 3 mins. Mix well and season with salt and pepper to taste (it will already be salty from the pancetta).
Stir in most of the tarragon, keeping a few leaves back for garnish. Add the chicken thighs and pancetta back into the pan and coat with the sauce.
Divide between plates and garnish with the remaining tarragon. Serve with your carb of choice (rice or mash are perfect) and any green veg you fancy (spinach and cavolo nero work great).

name: Honey Mustard Pork Chop & Garlicky Chickpeas
description: Juicy pork chops glazed in mustardy goodness, served over garlicky chickpeas with loads of herby parsley. A midweek failsafe.
instructions: Season the pork chops generously with salt and pepper on both sides, then set aside. Pick the parsley leaves and finely slice the soft stems. Gently crush the garlic for the pork and set aside.
Finely grate the garlic for the chickpeas into a saucepan. Add the parsley stems and chickpeas (with their liquid), then set over a medium heat and let it gently simmer until ready to serve.

Pat the chops dry. Add the olive oil to a frying pan and place the pork chops fat-side down. Set over a medium-high heat and let the fat render for 3–4 mins. Once browned, sear both sides of the chops for 5–6 mins until golden and cooked through. Transfer to a plate to rest.

Pour the chicken stock into the empty pan and add the crushed garlic. Let it bubble and reduce by half, then take it off the heat and stir through the honey and wholegrain mustard. Taste and season with salt, pepper and a splash of sherry vinegar.
Slice the pork chops and stir any resting juices into the sauce. Spoon the garlicky chickpeas into bowls, top with the pork, then drizzle over the sauce. Finish with a scattering of parsley leaves.

name: Honey Mustard Salmon with Dilly Rice & Everything Bagel Cream Cheese
description: Sticky salmon, sharp pickled salad, punchy dill rice and a creamy dollop of Everything Bagel cream cheese. Plus 40g of protein per serving? This is a midweek dinner done right.
instructions: Mix the mustard and honey in a bowl. Season, then coat the salmon all over. Leave to marinate while you crack on.

Thinly slice the cucumber and red onion, then chuck into a bowl with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt. Scrunch together and set aside to lightly pickle. Chop the dill and zest the lemon, set aside.

Rinse the rice, then tip it into a saucepan with double the amount of cold water. Bring to the boil, cover, then turn the heat right down and simmer for 10 mins. Take off the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for another 5 mins. Once cooked stir through the chopped dill, then season and fluff it all up.
Mix the cream cheese with everything seasoning, the lemon zest and a pinch of black pepper. Add a splash of water to loosen and set aside.

Pop the skinless salmon into the air fryer. Air fry at 200°C for 8-10 mins until caramelised and cooked through.
If you don't have an airfryer roast in the oven at 200°C fan for 12–15 mins until caramelised and just cooked through.

Divide the rice between bowls, then pile on the pickled salad and nestle in the salmon. Add a generous dollop of the everything bagel cream cheese, then scatter over more everything seasoning and a few fronds of fresh dill. Serve with a lemon wedge for squeezing. Done.

name: Honey Sesame Feta & Chickpea Traybake
description: Honey sesame feta and chickpeas baked until golden and sticky, with big savoury-sweet flavour and crisp edges. A simple traybake that delivers maximum payoff with minimal effort.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the courgette lengthways, then cut into irregular 3cm pieces. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Pick the mint leaves. Cut the feta block in half horizontally to make two thin slabs, then cut into triangles.

Chuck the courgette, tomatoes, chickpeas and olives into a roasting tin. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and black pepper, then toss everything together. Nestle in the feta triangles. Slide the tray into the oven and roast for 20 mins, or until the feta is golden and the veg is juicy.
Take it out of the oven and finish with a drizzle of honey, a scattering of sesame seeds and the fresh mint leaves. Serve straight from the tray.

name: Honey Soy Chicken & Sesame Spinach
description: Super glossy, umami-packed chicken with a refreshing sesame spinach salad. A dish that proves healthy doesn’t have to be boring.
keywords: Honey Soy Chicken & Sesame Spinach recipe
instructions: For the sauce, mix together the honey, Dijon mustard, soy sauce, rice vinegar, oyster sauce and black pepper in a medium-sized mixing bowl. Set aside.
Finely slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish. Cook the rice following packet instructions.

For the spinach salad, bring a medium pan of water to the boil over a high heat. Add your spinach and cook for 30 seconds before draining and rinsing under cold water. Squeeze out the excess moisture. In a medium-sized mixing bowl, whisk together the tahini, soy sauce, rice vinegar and sesame seeds, then mix through the blanched spinach until even coated.

For the chicken, slice the chicken thighs lengthways into four pieces each and season well with salt and pepper. Set a large frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the vegetable oil, followed by the chicken. Cook for 8-10 mins until cooked through with some colour. Once cooked, reduce the heat and pour over the sauce. Toss well and leave to reduce until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon.

To plate up, add the rice to the bottom of the bowl, top with the chicken and spoon over the excess sauce. Add the spinach and sprinkle over the spring onions. Serve with a wedge of lemon and togarashi (or toasted sesame seeds, if you prefer).

name: Honey Sriracha Chicken Bowls
description: This is the easiest and most delicious way to cook your chicken thighs. Sticky, spicy and sweet. So delicious.
instructions: Place the chicken skin-side down on a frying pan. Cook on a low-medium heat for 10 mins until the skin gets really crispy. Remove the chicken, leaving the chicken fat behind and chop the chicken into small bites.
Combine the sriracha, honey, soy sauce in a bowl.

Finely chop the spring onions and garlic. Save a handful of spring onions and then add the other spring onions and garlic to the chicken fat and cook for 5 mins with a pinch of salt until softened and fragrant.
Pour in the sauce and your chicken pieces and bring to a bubble until the sauce is thick and the chicken is cooked through.
Sprinkle over the saved spring onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve with steamed rice and enjoy.

name: Honey Sriracha Tofu Bowl
description: A quick, punchy bowl that’s big on flavour and protein. Sweet, spicy, and satisfyingly crunchy. Ideal for a speedy solo dinner that still feels special.
instructions: Pat the tofu dry, then cut it into small cubes. Heat the sesame oil in a large non-stick pan over a medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 8–10 mins until golden and crisp on all sides.
Grate the garlic and ginger – no need to peel. Slice the roasted red pepper into strips. Finely slice the spring onion and cut the lime into wedges for serving.
In a small bowl, whisk together the sriracha, honey, soy sauce, garlic, and ginger with 1-2 tablespoons of water to loosen. Add the yoghurt to a bowl with the kimchi and mix.
Pour the sauce into the pan with the crispy tofu and toss to coat. Let it bubble for 1–2 minutes until sticky and glossy.
Heat the rice according to the package instructions and add it to a bowl. Top with the honey sriracha tofu, roasted red pepper and kimchi yoghurt.
Sprinkle over the peanuts and spring onion, serve with lime for squeezing.

name: Honey Sriracha Tofu Bowl
description: A quick, punchy bowl that’s big on flavour and protein. Sweet, spicy, and satisfyingly crunchy. Ideal for a healthy packed lunch.
instructions: Pat the tofu dry, then cut it into small cubes. Heat the sesame oil in a large non-stick pan over a medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 8–10 mins until golden and crisp on all sides.
Grate the garlic and ginger – no need to peel. Slice the roasted red pepper into strips. Finely slice the spring onion and cut the lime into wedges for serving.
In a small bowl, whisk together the sriracha, honey, soy sauce, garlic, and ginger with 1-2 tablespoons of water to loosen. Add the yoghurt to a bowl with the kimchi and mix.
Pour the sauce into the pan with the crispy tofu and toss to coat. Let it bubble for 1–2 minutes until sticky and glossy.
Heat the rice according to the package instructions and add it to a Tupperware container. Top with the honey sriracha tofu, roasted red pepper and kimchi yoghurt.
Sprinkle over the peanuts and spring onion. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch – they’ll keep for up to 3 days. Serve with a lime wedge for squeezing

name: Honey Za’atar Halloumi, Herby Pomegranate Slaw & Hummus
description: Crispy, golden halloumi tossed in sticky honey and za’atar, piled over zingy pomegranate slaw and creamy hummus. Lunch doesn’t get better than this.
instructions: Slice the cabbage in half lengthways and finely shred. Thinly slice the red onion. Roughly chop three-quarters of the dill. Add everything to a large bowl.

Drizzle over the pomegranate molasses, squeeze in the juice of half a lemon, and add the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then mix well to combine. Let the slaw sit and lightly pickle while you cook the halloumi.

Cut the halloumi into 2cm cubes. Set a frying pan over medium-high heat (no oil needed). Fry the halloumi cubes for 1–2 mins on each side until golden and crisp. Drizzle in the honey and sprinkle over the za’atar. Cook for 30 seconds, tossing to coat, then take off the heat.
Divide the hummus between two containers or plates. Spoon over the herby slaw, top with the sticky halloumi and finish with the remaining dill.

name: Honey Zhoug Halloumi Grains
description: Zhoug is a Yemeni sauce built on coriander and lemon that brings life to everything it touches. Here those flavours land on golden halloumi and herby grains.
instructions: Chop the halloumi and courgette into 2-3cm chunks and thinly slice the chillies.
