Reheat the grains and leave to cool. Finely chop the coriander, stalks and all, then toss it through the cooled grains with half the chillies and half the extra virgin olive oil. Zest and squeeze in the juice of the lemon, season with salt and set aside.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Once hot, add the courgette and halloumi and fry on all sides for 4-5 mins, until golden brown. Add the cumin seeds and cook for a couple of minutes, until fragrant. Remove from the heat and stir the honey and a quarter of the chillies through.

Share the grains onto plates and top with the halloumi and courgette. Finish with a dollop of Greek yoghurt, the remaining extra virgin olive oil and the last of the chillies. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Honey-Dijon Chicken Thighs
description: Sweet, sticky, and ridiculously easy to make. These honey mustard chicken thighs are serious business.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
In a large bowl, squeeze the juice of the lemon and whisk it together with the honey, Dijon mustard, paprika, and olive oil.
Add the chicken thighs to the bowl and toss until well coated. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Arrange the chicken thighs in a single layer on a baking tray.
Roast for 35 mins, or until the skin is crispy and the chicken is cooked through.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side.

name: Honey-Dijon Roast Chicken with Leek-y Parmesan Chickpeas
description: Pure high-protein comfort. Crispy, sticky chicken thighs paired with creamy, cheesy chickpeas, all topped off with a refreshing, herby yoghurt. Store everything separately and it’ll stay fresh for up to 5 days – plus, it reheats beautifully!
keywords: Honey-Dijon Roast Chicken with Leek-y Parmesan Chickpeas
Honey-Dijon Roast Chicken with Leek-y Parmesan Chickpeas recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Prepare the chicken: Into a large bowl, squeeze the juice of ¼ of your lemons and whisk together with the honey, paprika and ½ the Dijon mustard. Add the chicken thighs and toss until well coated. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Roast the chicken. Arrange the chicken thighs on a baking tray in a single layer and roast in the oven for 30 mins, or until the skin is crispy and the chicken is cooked through.

Make the herby yoghurt sauce: While the chicken is cooking, add the yoghurt, green chilli, ½ the parsley, ½ the dill and the juice of the remaining lemon to a blender. Add a good pinch of salt and blend until smooth. Set aside.

For the leeks and chickpeas: Wash and trim the leeks and slice them in half lengthwise, then cut into thin half-moons. Thinly slice the garlic. Heat a little olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the leeks and garlic and cook for 8-10 mins, stirring occasionally, until the leeks are soft and jammy. Stir in the remaining Dijon mustard and the chilli flakes and cook for another minute.

Add the drained chickpeas and chicken stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 3-4 mins, until the mixture thickens and becomes creamy. Grate in the Parmesan and season to taste with black pepper and salt. Once the chicken is cooked, pour all the roasting juices into the chickpeas.

Assemble the dish: Spoon the creamy chickpea mixture onto plates. Top with the crispy chicken thighs, a generous sprinkle of the remaining fresh parsley and dill, and a drizzle of the herby yoghurt sauce. Enjoy!

name: Honey-Fried Chorizo with Tomato & Mozzarella Salad
description: Sweet and spicy chorizo on a medley of fresh tomatoes and mozzarella.
keywords: Honey-Fried Chorizo Over Tomatoes & Mozzarella recipe
instructions: Slice the tomatoes into large 3cm chunks, then transfer to a bowl with a pinch of salt, pepper and the red wine vinegar. Allow to sit for 15 mins.
Very thinly slice the red onion, then transfer to a bowl with ice-cold water and set aside.

Slice open the chorizo sausages, then crumble the sausagemeat into small chunks. Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the oil and the chorizo. Fry for 3-4 mins until crisp and the oil is bright red. Turn off the heat and add the honey. Allow to cool a little (2 mins) before transferring to the tomato bowl.
Drain the mozzarella balls then tear them onto a plate. Spoon over the tomato and chorizo. Drain the onions then scatter them on top. Serve with bread for scooping.

name: Honey-Glazed Roots & Halloumi Salad
description: A no-faff salad built from a spiced roasted veg and crispy halloumi traybake, finished with pomegranate, chickpeas, rocket and creamy hummus.
keywords: honey carrot and parsnip halloumi traybake
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Peel the carrots and parsnips, then cut into long, even-sized chunks. Remove the tough core from the parsnips.
Grease a large roasting tin with oil. Tip in the carrots and parsnips, then toss with most of the olive oil, cumin seeds, a generous pinch of salt and black pepper. Roast for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut the halloumi into chunks and drain the chickpeas. After 20 minutes pop the halloumi on top of the veg and drizzle with the honey. Roast until everything is tender and starting to turn golden, for another 10 mins.
Drain the chickpeas, and toss with the rocket, pomegranate seeds and roasted veg and halloumi. Serve with dollops of hummus and dig in and a lemon wedge.

name: Honeycomb
description: All you need to make delicious crunchy cinder toffee is sugar, golden syrup, bicarb and a sugar thermometer. Perfect for decorating bakes, giving as a festive gift or just eating as it is.
instructions: Line a large baking tray with baking paper.

Place the sugar and golden syrup in a large saucepan with a sugar thermometer attached. Set over a low heat and stir slowly until the temperature reaches around 150°C (the hard crack stage). This might take 4–5 mins, so be patient – keep a close eye on the thermometer, as it might suddenly start to rise much faster.

Remove from the heat, add the bicarbonate of soda and stir very quickly and evenly. It will bubble up as the bicarbonate of soda releases carbon dioxide very rapidly – this is what makes the amazing honeycomb effect. Make sure you stir well or you may be left with a bitter, soapy taste.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking tray and leave to cool completely. Break the cooled slab of honeycomb into pieces to serve.

name: Hong Kong French Toast
description: Nguyen (aka @gnochgnoch) is here to show you how to make her perfect Hong Kong french toast. Run to the kitchen and make this now. Right now.
instructions: Spread your Biscoff on the first slice of bread, your peanut butter on the second, and Biscoff once again on the third. Stack them on top of each other.
Cut the crusts off so it forms a neat square.
Now create your egg mix. Combine your eggs, milk and a sprinkle of cinnamon, and mix well. Then, take your bread stack and dredge it in the egg mix on all sides.
Heat up your oil to 180-190°C. You can use a chopstick to test the temperature – if the oil starts bubbling right away when you put the chopsticks in, it’s ready.
Place the block of bread in the pan and fry each side for 1-2 mins until it turns golden brown.
Once it's looking all golden, remove the toast onto a drying rack or on a paper towel so that either the excess oil drips out or the towel soaks it up.
Serve with a knob of butter and a healthy drizzle of condensed milk.

name: Hot & Juicy Aubergine & Tahini Slaw Focaccia Sandwich
description: With a little time and patience, but very little effort, you can have this sandwich of  your dreams. Spicy, crunchy and saucy, all loaded into one focaccia.
keywords: Hot & Juicy Aubergine & Tahini Slaw Focaccia Sandwich
instructions: Preheat the oven to 240°C.
Slice the aubergine into 3cm rounds. Drizzle with plenty of olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper. Bake on a lined baking tray for 35 mins, flipping halfway.

Meanwhile make the slaw. Finely slice the cabbage and add to a large bowl. Finely slice the spring onions, chilli, and finely chop the parsley, including the stems and add these to the bowl. Add the tahini, lime juice, mustard, 2 tbsp of olive oil and plenty of salt and pepper. Toss with your hands and lightly massage the cabbage to get it to soften. Set aside.
Next, make the aubergine glaze. In a small bowl, add the harissa, pomegranate molasses, date syrup and 1 tbsp olive oil and salt and pepper and stir to combine.

When the aubergines are ready to come out of the oven, brush them with the glaze, pop them back into the oven for 3 mins, then flip them and brush the other side and get them back into the oven for 3 more minutes. You should have about a tablespoon of the glaze leftover, keep this to the side.

To assemble, slice the focaccia open and spread the remaining glaze onto the top side. Spread the vegan mayo onto the bottom, pile up the aubergines, then the slaw and chopped almonds or sesame seeds. Close it up, cut it in half and tuck in. Like most sandwiches, this is best served fresh.

name: Hot Chicken Katsu Curry
description: An easy katsu curry recipe from Wagamama. This is an excellent fakeaway recipe for any occasion. It's hot, it's spicy, it's delicious.
instructions: Finely chop your onion, garlic and ginger.

Heat a small glug of vegetable oil in a large wok and add your onion, garlic and ginger. Fry for a few minutes over a medium heat until softened, then add your mild curry powder and turmeric and cook out your spices for a minute. Tip in your flour and cook out for another minute before gradually adding your vegetable stock, beating constantly until you have a smooth sauce. Add your coconut milk, soy sauce and sugar and stir to combine. Simmer for 5 minutes, then season to taste and remove from the heat.
Strain your sauce through a sieve into a bowl and discard all the bits left in the sieve. Set aside.

Clean your wok, then heat a dash of vegetable oil in there over a medium heat. Add your chilli flakes and toast for a minute until fragrant, then squeeze in your sriracha and a drop of Tabasco. Set aside.
Slice your chicken breast in two widthways to create two thin fillets. Beat your egg and pour it into a bowl. Add your flour and panko breadcrumbs to separate bowls.

Dip a chicken fillet in the flour, egg and breadcrumbs respectively to coat your chicken. Repeat with your remaining fillets. Heat a good glug of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add your chicken fillets and fry for a couple of minutes on each side until they are crispy and tender.
Reheat your katsu sauce and pour in your chilli mixture. Stir to combine. Slice your chicken fillets and place on a bed of rice with some side salad. Spoon your sauce over and serve!

name: Hot Cross Bun French Toast
description: The most delicious way of reinvigorating your stale hot cross buns. A very good breakfast or dessert using Ocado ingredients.
instructions: Halve your hot cross buns.
Crack your eggs into a bowl and add your milk, caster sugar and cinnamon. Beat with a fork until you have a totally combined mixture.
Pop a knob of butter in a large frying pan and heat it over a medium-high heat.
Dip your hot cross buns in the egg mixture, turning so that all sides are coated.
Place your hot cross buns in the frying pan a few at a time, frying for 2 mins on each side until golden.
Time to plate up. Arrange your hot cross buns on a plate and top with a dollop of yoghurt. Slice your banana onto the plate, then drizzle with honey. Serve and enjoy.

name: Hot Dog Fried Rice
description: Turn a pack of franks into a five-star meal with this easy hot dog fried rice recipe.
instructions: Thinly slice the hot dogs and finely dice the celery and onions. Very finely chop the red chillies (leaving seeds in if you like it hot!) and garlic cloves. Cut the chives into 2-3 cm batons.

Preheat a large frying pan or wok over a high heat. Once smoking hot, add a shot of sesame oil and the hot dogs. Cook, tossing regularly, for 2-3 mins or until crispy. Tip the hot dogs out onto a plate and add a little more oil.

Once the oil is hot, tip in the celery and onion and cook, stirring occasionally so they catch and become charred and a little smoky. Add the garlic and chillies and stir fry for 2-3 mins before tipping out.
Add a little more oil and the rice to the pan. Stir fry briefly and then crack the eggs in. Scramble the eggs and toss through the rice. Add the hot dogs and cooked veggies and stir through the rice.
Toss through the sugar, white pepper, and soy sauce. Finish with the chives and serve.
Garnish with hot sauce and crispy onions, if you like.

name: Hot Fudge Sun-date
description: This hot fudge sundae-inspired date recipe is perfect for Ramadan or any event where you want a sweet little canapé.
instructions: Make your hot fudge sauce by heating your ingredients in a saucepan.
Break up brownie pieces and add about 2 tbsp of hot fudge. Mix until it reaches a texture that's soft but easily holds together.
Stuff the brownies into the dates.
Top with whipped cream, place a cherry on top of the cream and sprinkle your nuts on top.
Drizzle remainder of hot fudge sauce on top of dates and serve!

name: Hot Halloumi, Corn & Quinoa Bowl
description: Golden halloumi, sweetcorn and smoky peppers tossed through fluffy quinoa and finished with hot honey and lime, all made in 15 mins. This one's a proper taste of sunshine.
instructions: Place a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Drain the corn.
Split the halloumi down the crease and chop into 2cm chunks. Add to the hot pan along with the corn and cook for 3–4 mins until the halloumi is golden on all sides.
Meanwhile, reheat the quinoa. Drain and roughly chop the roasted peppers and coriander. Toss the three together with a squeeze of lime and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper.
Take the pan off the heat and toss the halloumi with the hot honey. Taste and season with salt, if needed.
Spoon the quinoa mix onto plates and top with the hot halloumi and corn. Finish with some lime zest and a lime wedge on the side.

name: Hot Honey & Orange Braised Chicken Tacos
description: A spicy chicken taco recipe that's got a nice bit of sweetness and acid from the combination of hot honey and fresh oranges. It's perfect dish to eat alongside a glass of cream sherry served over ice with a slice of orange.
keywords: Hot Honey & Orange Braised Chicken Tacos
Hot Honey & Orange Braised Chicken Tacos recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C. Season the chicken thighs with salt and pop them skin-side down into an ovenproof pan. Cook over a medium heat without touching for 9-10 mins, or until the skin is golden brown and crispy. Remove from the pan and set aside, leaving the rendered fat behind.

Roughly chop the shallots and peel and smash the garlic cloves. Throw the lot into the pan with the hot chicken fat and cook for 1-2 mins. Add the spices and chipotle, the zest and juice of the orange, the vinegar, honey and beer. Bring to a simmer, nestle the chicken back in and slide into the oven for 35-40 mins.
Once cooked, whip out the oven and pull the chicken off the bone. Stir the chicken meat through the sauce, reducing a little if you need to.
Slice the avocado and season with salt and pepper. Cut the chillies into slices, roughly chop the coriander and finely dice the onion. Heat the tortillas following pack instructions.

Load up the tortillas with some chicken, a slice of avocado, some chilli, onion, coriander, soured cream and a bit of extra hot honey. Serve with lime wedges and, if you're up for a drink, pour yourself a glass of creamy sherry over ice with an orange wedge.

name: Hot Honey Chicken Salad Bowl
description: Sticky hot honey chicken, crispy-edged sweet potato and herby quinoa, all topped with spicy crazy feta and quick-pickled red onion. They're calling these slop bowls, which whether you like it or not, kind of fits. I love them, they’re so much better made at home than the expensive pick-n-mix salads you buy for lunch, so give this one a go.
keywords: Hot Honey Chicken Salad Bowl recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Dice the sweet potatoes into 2cm chunks, no need to peel. Tip onto a large baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and toss to coat.

On a separate large metal baking tray, scatter the chilli powder, flour and a big pinch of salt. Add the chicken thighs and toss to coat evenly, then drizzle with olive oil and toss again. Slide both trays into the oven and roast for 35-40 mins, until the chicken is cooked through and the sweet potatoes are softened and golden.

Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion and add to a bowl with the red wine vinegar, honey and a pinch of salt. Scrunch with your hands and set aside to quick-pickle while everything cooks. (You can speed this up by popping it in the microwave for 30 seconds.)

Add the chilli flakes to a dry frying pan over a medium heat and toast for about 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the honey and red wine vinegar and cook for a minute longer until bubbling. Once the chicken is cooked through, coat it in the glaze, then slide back into the oven for 5 mins until sticky.
Finely chop the jalapeños. Crumble the feta into a bowl, add the jalapeños and crush together with a fork. Drizzle with olive oil, season well and set aside.
Add all the dressing ingredients to a jar or bowl, season well with salt and pepper, then whisk or shake until combined.
Cook the quinoa pouches according to packet instructions, then tip into a bowl. Roughly chop the coriander, stir through the quinoa and drizzle with a little olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice the cucumber into rough chunks. Tip the kale into a bowl and massage with a spoonful of the dressing until softened.

Add the kale to the base of the bowl and mix with the coriander quinoa, before dividing between four containers or bowls. Top with the sweet potato, chicken, cucumber and pickled red onion. Spoon on the spicy feta. Box up and refrigerate for up to three days. Drizzle with the dressing, then chop and toss just before eating.

name: Hot Honey Chicken Salad with Ranch-ish Dressing
description: We’ve coated this chicken in a spiced cornflake crumb, air-fried it until golden then drizzled it with sticky chilli honey. Finished with a creamy, herby ranch-ish dressing and fresh salad. This is a great recipe for using up any salady bits and bobs in the fridge but we like to use celery, romaine and radish for freshness and crunch.
keywords: Crispy Hot Honey Chicken Bowls with Ranch-ish Dressing
Crispy Hot Honey Chicken Bowls with Ranch-ish Dressing Recipe
instructions: Finely chop the chives and add them to a bowl with the buttermilk, mayonnaise and lemon juice. Mix to combine, then season with salt and black pepper.
Slice the chicken into strips. Mix ½ the tandoori masala and garlic powder in a bowl with a pinch of salt. Add the chicken and toss to coat.

Blitz the cornflakes in a mini processor until fine, then tip into a new bowl and mix with the remaining tandoori masala, garlic powder and a pinch of salt. Into a third bowl, crack the egg and whisk with salt and black pepper.

Dip each chicken strip into the egg, draining off the excess, then press into the cornflake mix to coat. Transfer the chicken to the air fryer basket and drizzle with olive oil. Air-fry at 200°C for 13 mins.

Meanwhile, mix the honey and chilli flakes in an oven-safe ramekin and place it in the air fryer alongside the chicken for the last 5 mins of cooking time. Remove the chicken from the air fryer and drizzle with the hot honey.If you're cooking for pickier eaters you can also serve on the side.
Prep your salady bits – you can use anything you've got in the fridge but we like to slice up some radish, celery and romaine lettuce.
Divide the salad between bowls then top with the chicken and pour over the ranch-ish dressing.

name: Hot Honey Crispy Pork & Crackling Sandwich
description: Crispy, spicy, juicy. This pork and crackling sandwich is stacked with all the adjectives.
keywords: Hot Honey Crispy Pork & Crackling Sandwich
instructions: Pick the rosemary needles off, discarding the stem. Finely chop and add into a small bowl with 13g of salt. Finely grate the garlic into the salt and stir together.
Pat the pork belly dry and rub the garlic paste onto the pork, leaving the skin clean. Place on a rack and in the fridge uncovered, overnight.

Bring the pork up to room temperature. Pat the skin of the pork dry, then using something sharp, stab the skin all over. Place the whole shallots onto the baking tray, drizzle with oil and place the pork on top.
Preheat the oven to 160°C. Once hot, roast the pork for 50-60 mins. Turn the heat up to 220°C, once hot, roast until the skin starts to blister and goes golden brown, 20-25 mins.

Take the pork out, transfer the shallots to a plate and turn the grill on low. Place the pork under the grill and cook until the skin has puffed up and has gone crispy, 4-6 mins, making sure to not burn the skin. Let the pork rest for 15-20 mins before chopping.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the apple. De-stem the cavolo nero and tear into bite seized chunks. Place the greens into a bowl with a pinch of salt and massage until wilted, 2-4 mins. Stir through 20ml of apple cider vinegar, apple and 3 tbsp of olive oil. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Place the honey into a microwave safe bowl. Trim and finely chop the chilli and add to the honey. Place in the microwave and heat up for 30 secs until piping hot. Stir through the remaining apple cider vinegar and set aside to infuse.

Toast the focaccia, discard the shallot peels. Chop the pork into slices. Spread the mayo onto the cut sides of the bread, top with the roasted shallots, crispy pork and apple slaw. Drizzle over the hot honey and sandwich together.

name: Hot Honey Halloumi & Crispy Rice Bowl
description: I'm obsessed with fruit in salty, savoury salads, and a touch of vinegar makes this recipe scream summer. The crispy rice has flavours that remind me of Greece, perfect for a hot London evening when I'm dreaming of holiday. Nectarines or peaches both work - you do you!
keywords: hot honey halloumi & crispy rice bowl
hot honey halloumi & crispy rice bowl recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add the rice to a bowl with a third of the olive oil, the tomato puree, ground cumin, dried mint, salt and pepper. Mix well, then transfer to a baking tray and roast on the top shelf for 20-25 mins, stirring occasionally, until lightly charred at the edges.

Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion. In a large bowl, whisk together the remaining olive oil, the red wine vinegar, salt and pepper. Slice the nectarines and vine tomatoes, then add to the bowl with the onion and dressing, along with the black olives, crushing them gently between your fingers as you go to release their briny flavour. Toss to combine, then pick the mint leaves and add most to the salad, setting a few aside for garnish.

Dice the halloumi and add to a dry frying pan over a medium heat (add a small splash of oil if your pan isn't non-stick). Fry for 5 mins, turning occasionally, until golden on all sides, then remove the pan from the heat. Drizzle over the hot honey and toss to coat. Season the yoghurt with salt and black pepper.
To serve, divide the crispy rice between containers, then top with the peach salad and sticky halloumi. Scatter over the reserved mint leaves and toasted sesame seeds. Pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Hot Honey Halloumi & Crispy Rice Bowl
description: I'm obsessed with fruit in salty, savoury salads, and a touch of vinegar makes this recipe scream summer. The crispy rice has flavours that remind me of Greece, perfect for a hot London evening when I'm dreaming of holiday. Nectarines or peaches both work - you do you!

name: Hot Honey Halloumi with Lentils & Nectarines
description: Salads don’t get much better than this hot honey halloumi with lentils and nectarines. It’s sweet, salty, crunchy and packed with plants and fibre to nourish your gut microbiome. And it has enough protein to keep you feeling satisfied.
keywords: Hot Honey Halloumi with Lentils & Nectarines
Hot Honey Halloumi with Lentils & Nectarines recipe
instructions: Finely slice the red onion and add to a jar or bowl with a sprinkle of salt. Pour over the red wine vinegar and enough water to cover the onions then place in the fridge for at least 30 mins.
Quarter the nectarines and slice the halloumi block down the middle so you have two flatter rectangles.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a medium pan over a medium heat and the halloumi halves. Leave to cook for at least 3 mins until golden and crispy then turn and cook the other side.
While the halloumi is cooking, add the dressing ingredients to a large salad bowl. Taste and adjust the seasoning, and add more honey for sweetness or vinegar for acidity to your preference.
Chop up the kale. Add the chopped kale and massage the dressing into the kale until coated. Top with the cooked lentils, pickled red onions, nectarines, mint leaves and pumpkin seeds.
Add the honey, chilli flakes and nigella seeds to the halloumi pan and cook for another minute until glazed all over. Remove from the pan and cut into thick slices.
Add the halloumi to the salad and toss everything together. Enjoy!

name: Hot Honey Mezcal Margarita
description: A sweet, smoky, and spicy margarita we've made using mezcal and hot honey. This is a ripper.
instructions: Add your hot honey to a mixing bowl with the hot water. Stir until it is dissolved.
Add your salt and a splash of water into a small pot, then stir until it’s dissolved.
Juice all your limes until you have the right amount of juice.
Get a large mixing jug and add your mezcal, cointreau, hot honey syrup, salt solution, and lime juice. Mix with a whisk.
Pour all this in your bottle and store in fridge or freezer.
When you're ready to drink, use a small amount of hot honey on the rim and sprinkle over the Tajín. Then fill your glass with ice and pour in your batched cocktail to enjoy!

name: Hot Honey Mustard Salmon
description: Another day, another batch recipe. This one's a whole side of salmon glazed in hot honey and chipotle, then blasted under the grill until sticky and caramelised. It makes the perfect base for easy midweek dinners or can be served straight away over rice.
keywords: Hot Honey Mustard Salmon Batch recipe
instructions: Trim the spring onions and roughly chop into 2cm pieces. In a small bowl, mix together the hot honey, chipotle paste, wholegrain mustard, Dijon mustard, paprika and olive oil.
Season the salmon with salt and pepper, then spoon the glaze over the top so it's well coated. Transfer to a baking tray with the chopped spring onions.

Heat the grill to max. Pop the salmon tray on the top shelf and grill for around 10 mins, until just cooked through and lightly caramelised on top (depending on the thickness of your salmon you might need a few minutes more or less). Remove and leave to rest for a few minutes before flaking into large pieces.
Box up the salmon into containers and nestle in the spring onions and keep in the fridge ready to use throughout the week, or serve straight away with your choice of sides.

name: Hot Honey Mustard Salmon Bagels
description: Who doesn't love a classic salmon bagel? This one uses up leftovers from our Honey Mustard Salmon batch piled onto a bagel slathered in chive cream cheese with capers, red onion and spring onions. A lunch worth getting excited about.
keywords: Hot Honey Mustard Salmon Bagels recipe
instructions: Finely slice the red onion and set aside. Then juice the lemon and finely slice the chives and add to a bowl with the cream cheese and a pinch of salt and pepper.

Slice the bagels and spread the chive cream cheese generously on both halves. Top with the leftover Hot Honey Mustard Salmon and leftover spring onions straight from the fridge (no need to reheat) then finish with the capers and sliced red onion. Wrap up and enjoy.

name: Hot Honey Mustard Salmon Tacos
description: Leftovers from your Hot Honey Mustard batch with a crisp fennel slaw and cool garlic yoghurt piled into soft tortillas. The kind of tacos that make leftover night feel like a treat.
keywords: Accessible Ingredients Season: All year Type: Tacos Time: Under 20 mins Nutrition: High Protein
30 Plus Protein Practical USPs: Meal Prep
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Slide the leftover salmon and spring onions onto a baking tray and warm through for 5-8 mins.

Meanwhile, finely slice the fennel on a mandoline and julienne the apple. Toss together with the juice of the lemon and olive oil and season with a pinch of salt. In a small bowl, mix together the Greek yoghurt with the finely grated garlic, the juice of the half lemon and a pinch of salt. Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for around 30 seconds each side.

To assemble, spread the garlic yoghurt over each tortilla, scatter over some of the warm spring onions, then top with the fennel and apple slaw and finish with the warm flaked salmon. Squeeze over some lime juice and serve straight away.

name: Hot Honey Mustard Salmon with Turmeric Rice & Slaw
description: Leftovers from your Hot Honey Mustard Salmon, flaked over golden turmeric rice, a crisp fennel and apple slaw and garlicky yoghurt. A fresh, feel-good bowl that doesn't feel like leftovers.
keywords: Hot Honey Mustard Salmon with Turmeric Rice & Fennel Apple Slaw
Hot Honey Mustard Salmon with Turmeric Rice & Fennel Apple Slaw recipe
instructions: Rinse the rice and add to a saucepan with the water, turmeric, finely grated garlic and butter. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a low heat, cover and cook for around 12 mins until tender. Turn off the heat and leave to steam while you get on with the rest.
Heat the oven to 160°C. Slide the leftover salmon and spring onions onto a baking tray and warm through for 5-8 mins.
Meanwhile, finely slice the fennel on a mandoline and julienne the apple. Toss together with the juice of the lemon and olive oil and season with a pinch of salt.
In a small bowl, mix together the Greek yoghurt with the finely grated garlic, the juice of the half lemon and a pinch of salt.

Divide the turmeric rice between two bowls and scatter over the warm spring onions. Top with the salmon, the fennel and apple slaw, then spoon over the garlic yoghurt. Scatter with the fresh dill and parsley to finish.

name: Hot Honey Smashed Pork Tacos with Kiwi Salsa
description: The next time you buy sausages from the supermarket, give these a try. The sausage meat will be spread onto tortillas and cooked until juicy. Topped with a red chilli, lime and kiwi salsa to cut through the richness of the sausagemeat, adding a little more fresh heat, served with sour cream.
instructions: Remove the casing off the sausages. Stir the sausagemeat and hot honey together, then spread the sausagemeat onto one side of the tortillas.
Peel and finely mince the kiwis, chillies and coriander (for the salsa). Add both into a bowl, zest in ¼ of the lime, then stir together and season with salt and lime juice.
Thinly shave the cabbage into a bowl. Set aside

Place a frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, cook the sausagemeat, sausage side down, 2-3 mins, or until cooked through. Then flip and toast the tortilla for a couple of seconds. Transfer to a tray and cover, whilst you cook the remaining tortillas.
Toss the cabbage slaw with a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt.
Share the tacos between plates, top with some soured cream, cabbage slaw, kiwi salsa and crumble over the feta. Squeeze remaining lime to taste.

name: Hot Pepper Meatballs with Naan
description: Spicy and fragrant lamb meatballs cooked over a warming roasted tomato and pepper sauce. All mopped up with naan. What a treat.
keywords: Hot Pepper Meatballs with Naan recipe
instructions: Preheat the grill to high.

Quarter the tomatoes and onions, making sure to leave the skin on - that’s where all the flavour is. Add your chopped vegetables onto a baking tray with a large glug of oil and salt, grill until starting to char, 8-12 minutes (keep an eye on it, depending on your grill it could take less or more time). Then, change the oven settings and heat to 180°C.

For the meatballs: Add the parsley, tomato, ginger, garlic and walnuts into a food processor and blitz until finely minced. Generously season with salt, then transfer into a bowl with the lamb mince, chilli powder, cinnamon, all spice. Portion the mince mixture out and make 4 meatballs per person.
When the veggies are roasted, remove the onion peel  and drain the peppers.  Blend it all with a hand blender. Add the sumac and season with salt if needed, pour into a baking dish.

Place the meatballs in the sauce, and slide into the oven for 15-20 mins, until fully cooked. Thinly slice the red onion and pick the parsley leaves, optionally, place into a bowl of ice water to crisp. Before serving, toss through a drizzle of oil and season with salt.
Spread a dollop of hummus over a side of your bowl and add in the meatballs and sauce. Serve with some of the parsley onion salad and some naan.

name: Hot Roast Chicken Sandwich
description: Who doesn't love a good sandwich? This roast chicken sandwich comes with a rich and wonderful gravy for dipping. Now, that's what we call a moist maker.
instructions: Begin by taking the chicken out of the fridge an hour before you’re ready to cook it. Take a piece of kitchen roll and pat the chicken dry all over. Set aside. Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Next, make the garlic and herb rub for the chicken. Take the leaves from a few sprigs of rosemary and thyme and finely chop. Mince three cloves of garlic and add to a bowl with the herbs along with a few big pinches of salt and pepper and 2 tbsp of olive oil. Mix to combine then, using your hands, rub the mix all over the chicken.

Peel the onions, cut them in half and place them in a roasting tray with a halved bulb of garlic and a few sprigs of rosemary and thyme. Sit the chicken on top and place in a preheated oven for 1hr 20mins. The chicken is done when the juices run clear.

Take the chicken out and allow it to rest on a plate while you crack on with the gravy. Remove the onions and garlic from the roasting tray, making sure to leave as much cooking juices in the tray as possible. Optionally, you can save the onions to put in the sandwich later.

Put the roasting tray on the hob, set over a medium heat and add 4 tsp of plain flour. Cook for a minutes or so to allow the flour to soak up the juices from the pan then pour in a good splash of white wine (about 125ml). Allow the wine to bubble away making sure to be constantly whisking to avoid lumps.

After a couple of minutes, add the chicken stock and whisk while bringing to the boil. Allow the gravy simmer for 20 mins, whisking every so often. After 20 mins, pass the gravy through a sieve into a small saucepan and set aside.
While the gravy is simmering, make the garnish. Pick the leaves of the parsley and add to a bowl with thinly sliced red onion and a squeeze of lemon juice.

Now the chicken has rested, it’s time to carve. Cut down between the leg and the breast, pop the joint, then cut through to remove the legs. Next, remove the breast by slicing down along the bone from the middle of the bird. With clean hands, remove the meat from the legs and any excess left on the carcass.
Next, slice your baguettes leaving one side attached and fill liberally with the chicken. Place the sandwiches back in the oven for 10 mins to crisp up while you heat the gravy.
Fill the sandwiches with a little bit of the garnish and then serve each sandwich with their own pot of dipping gravy and enjoy.

name: Hot Sauce Egg Salad Sandos
description: A meal prep high-protein breakfast that's genuinely delicious. This spicy egg salad sando is a hell of a way to start the day.
keywords: Hot Sauce Egg Salad Sandos recipe
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Gently lower in the eggs, reduce to a simmer, and cook for 8 minutes. Transfer to a bowl of ice water and let them cool fully before peeling.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the chives. Stir the cottage cheese and herbs into a bowl with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the peeled eggs and mash into a creamy, chunky mix. Taste and season with hot sauce and salt to your liking. Add more of less hot sauce depending on your preference. Box up and place in the fridge until ready to use.
Spoon the egg salad onto a slice of bread, and sandwich together for a fluffy and spicy egg salad sandwich.

name: Hot Sauce Roast Chicken & Crispy Blue Cheese Salad
description: The king of chicken salad. The blue cheese dressing is so good in this dinner party-appropriate recipe that your guests might just want to bathe in it.
keywords: Hot Sauce Roast Chicken & Crispy Crouton Salad With Blue Cheese Dressing
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Peel and finely chop the garlic and add to a small bowl with the softened butter and hot sauce. Mash and mix really well.

Starting from the neck of the chicken, prise your hand between the breast and the skin to create a large pocket over the breast of the chicken. Push three-quarters of the softened butter into this pocket, smoothing it to create an even layer. Rub the remaining butter over the surface of the chicken. Season the chicken all over really well and splash over some more hot sauce.

Put the chicken into a large roasting tin and roast for 45 mins. After 20 mins, remove the chicken from the oven and baste the bird in the buttery juices. Meanwhile, cut or tear the sourdough into chunky croutons and set aside.

Once the chicken has been roasting for 45 mins, baste again, then add the croutons to the tin. Toss well, then return to the oven for a final 20 mins, until the chicken is cooked through (the juices will run clear when pierced in the thigh, or reads 70C on a digital thermometer) and the croutons golden and crunchy. Move the chicken to a large plate or platter and loosely cover with foil. Rest the chicken for 20 mins while you make the salad.
For the dressing, crumble 100g blue cheese into a bowl, then stir through the soured cream, vinegar, 1 tbsp cold water and some seasoning to make a dressing.

Trim the ends from the Little Gems, then cut into chunky pieces and do the same with the chicory. Slice the celery and mix everything together in a salad bowl. Add half the dressing and toss well, then divide between plates.

Remove the legs from the chicken and portion into thighs and drumsticks, then remove the breasts and slice. Divide the meat between the plates and top with a good spoon of the remaining dressing, the crunchy croutons and any buttery resting juices from the tray. To finish, crumble over the remaining blue cheese and splash over more hot sauce, if you like things spicy.

Trim the ends from the little gem, then cut into chunky pieces and do the same with the chicory. Slice the celery and mix everything together in a salad bowl. Add ½ the dressing and toss well and divide between plates.

Remove the legs from the chicken and portion into thigh and drumsticks, then remove the breasts and slice. Divide between the plates and top with a good spoon of the remaining dressing, the crunchy croutons and any buttery resting juices from the tray and finally crumble over the remaining blue cheese and splash over more hot sauce, if you like things spicy.

name: Hot Smoked Salmon Bowl with Miso Lemon Vinaigrette
description: Creamy potato salad meets flaked salmon and a zingy miso dressing in this dreamy lunch bowl. It’s fresh, punchy, and perfect for prepping ahead.
keywords: Hot Smoked Salmon Bowl with Miso Lemon Vinaigrette
Hot Smoked Salmon Bowl with Miso Lemon Vinaigrette recipe
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Meanwhile, halve any larger Jersey potatoes so they’re all roughly the same size. Once the water’s boiling, add the potatoes and cook for 10–15 mins until a knife slides in easily. Drain and set aside to cool slightly.

Peel and finely slice the red onion. Add to a small bowl, squeeze over the juice of ¼ of the lemon and add a pinch of sea salt. Massage with your hands for 30 seconds to soften and lightly pickle. Set aside.
Finely chop the chives. In a large mixing bowl, stir together the Greek yoghurt, chopped chives, half the wholegrain mustard, and a good pinch of salt and pepper.
Once the potatoes are cool enough to handle, toss them into the yoghurt mix and stir until well coated.
In a small bowl, whisk together the miso paste, remaining lemon juice, white wine vinegar, olive oil, remaining mustard, and honey. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Thinly slice the cucumber. Rinse and dry the spinach. Flake the hot smoked salmon into bite-sized chunks, removing any skin if needed.

Divide the spinach and cucumber between bowls or containers. Add a generous scoop of potato salad, then top with the flaked salmon and quick-pickled onions. Finish with a good drizzle of the miso vinaigrette.

name: Hot and Sweet Beet Tahini Sauce
description: This vibrant and versatile sauce is perfect for drizzling on roasted veggies, grains, or on warm or cold salads. It's pretty punchy so  less is more to start.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C
Wash the beetroots well and remove the tail and any stems and leaves (the stems are great pickled and the leaves can be sautéed with garlic).
Drizzle some oil over the beets and season with salt and pepper. Rub the salt into each one well and then wrap them individually and tightly in silver foil.
Bake for 1.5 to 2 hours or until they are very soft inside.
Remove them from the oven and allow to cool before unwrapping. Using gloves, rub the skins off of each beetroot. They should come off fairly easily. If not, use a peeler.
Weigh out 300g of beetroot and roughly chop them. Save the rest for another dish, they keep well in the fridge for 4-5 days.

Roughly chop the chilli and peel and chop the ginger. Add these to a high-speed blender with the beets, tahini, agave, salt, olive oil and 150ml cold water and blend until smooth. Add the juice of 3 limes, taste, and add more lime juice if you like.
Taste and adjust to your preference. Add more agave for sweetness or more water to thin it down.
Keep the sauce in a jar in the fridge for up to a week.

name: Hummus & Crispy-Honey Halloumi Pittas
description: Warm pitta wedges, creamy hummus, crispy golden halloumi and a punchy salad with dill, pomegranate and hot honey. Everyone’s happy.
keywords: hummus and crispy honey halloumi pittas
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsPeel and finely slice the red onion, then chuck into a bowl with a pinch of salt and the juice of the lemon. Scrunch it together with your hands to soften slightly.
Halve the cucumber and slice into half-moons. Halve and slice the avocado. Pick the dill fronds, saving a few for garnish.

Set aside one-third of the cucumber, avocado and pomegranate seeds for the kids’ plates. Toss the rest with the lemony onion, most of the dill and half the olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper.
Toast the pitta breads, then slice into triangles and set aside.
Slice the halloumi into 1cm pieces. Heat the remaining olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the halloumi for 1–2 mins per side until golden and crispy.

Serve up!Kids Plate: Spoon a dollop of hummus onto each plate. Add the pitta triangles, a few pieces of crispy halloumi and the reserved cucumber-pomegranate salad.Parents Plate: Spread the hummus onto each plate. Top with the salad mix, golden halloumi and a drizzle of hot honey. Scatter with reserved dill and serve with pitta on the side.

name: Hummus With Toasted Cinnamon & Almond Drizzle
description: Take your store-bought hummus to the next level. This toasted almond and cinnamon drizzle zhuzhs it right up, making it look super impressive.
keywords: Hummus With Toasted Cinnamon Almond Drizzle
Hummus With Toasted Cinnamon Almond Drizzle recipe
instructions: Put the olive oil and flaked almonds into a saucepan set over a medium heat. Cook until the almonds turn a light golden colour, then add the cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds until they stop shimmering. Remove from the heat and stir through the sumac and cinnamon. Season with salt and pepper.
Decant the hummus into a bowl and drizzle with the toasted almond and cinnamon oil. Serve with flatbreads.

name: Ice Cream With Frozen Mango, Lime & Toasted Sesame Seeds
description: Ever thought about freezing your mangos? Well, you will now.
instructions: Peel the mango and cut into wedges. Pop in the freezer overnight.
Get the ice cream out of the fridge 10 mins before you’re ready to serve. Meanwhile, zest the lime.
Scoop the ice cream into a bowl and grate over the mango. Top with the lime zest, tajin, a pinch of salt and toasted sesame seeds.

name: Ice Cream, Breadcrumbs, Warm Dates & Olive Oil
description: We want to talk about this breadcrumb topping… trust us, stale bread has never tasted better. You will never look back. The breadcrumbs are toasted in butter and brown sugar and will give you a summer’s worth of the best ice-cream topping. If there's one thing you should make of mine, it’s this!
instructions: If you're making the breadcrumbs, remove and discard the crusts from the bread, then tear them into small chunks and blitz in a food processor to create fine-ish breadcrumbs.

Add the butter to a medium frying pan set over a medium heat. Allow it to melt and begin to foam, then add the breadcrumbs and stir, coating them in the butter. Stir often for 3-4 mins until the bread starts to turn light golden. Add the sugar and toss to coat again, then stir constantly for another 2 mins until they are golden brown. Tip onto a plate, then sprinkle with a little sea salt and allow to cool.
Pit the dates, transfer to a microwavable plate and microwave for 30 seconds on high. They might need a little longer, depending on your microwave.
Scoop balls of ice cream into bowls, then add a date or two and some cherries to each one, if using. Top with the breadcrumbs and a small drizzle of your best extra virgin olive oil.

name: Iced Dan Dan (ish) Noodles
description: This soup has got all the flavours of dan dan noodles but we've kept it vegetarian – which means less cooking time and less washing up. Winner.
instructions: Combine chilli oil, soy sauce, tahini, five-spice, and black vinegar in a bowl or jug. Add the cold water gradually whilst stirring until you have a smooth soup consistency. Chill until very cold, you can either pop in the fridge for at least 2 hours or stick in the freezer for max 30 mins.
When you’re ready to eat, cook the noodles according to package instructions and then drain and rinse in cold water to stop the cooking process. Toss the noodles in the sesame oil and set aside.
Cut the cucumber into matchsticks. Finely slice the spring onions. Roughly chop the peanuts.
Pour the soup broth into a bowl, top with the noodles, a couple of ice cubes, peanuts, cucumber and spring onions. Give it a good mix and get stuck in.

name: Iced Green Gazpacho With Chipotle Seed Drizzle
description: Green gazpacho with chipotle seed drizzle. This one is spicy with pickled jalapeños, a lil sweet from frozen peas and herby with mint and coriander.
keywords: Iced Green Gazpacho With Chipotle Seed Drizzle
Iced Green Gazpacho With Chipotle Seed Drizzle recipe
instructions: Add peas to a blender (no need to thaw!) with most of the mint and coriander (saving some for garnish), pickled jalapeños, roughly chopped cucumber, and garlic. Blitz well until smooth and then loosen with water. Pop the soup in the fridge for a few hours or until really cold.

Make the chipotle pepitas by heating olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the pumpkin seeds and toast for 3 mins until smelling nutty, then stir through the chipotle paste and cooking for another 30 seconds. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Slice the green chilli. Serve the soup in chilled bowls with a couple of ice cubes, then top with the chipotle seeds, feta, green chilli, and remaining herbs.

name: Iced Green Goddess Soup
description: A vibrant, herby chilled soup topped with golden halloumi and toasted sesame seeds. It's full of avocado, spinach, natural yogurt, garlic, and green chilli.
instructions: Halve and remove stones from the avocados and slice. Halve and remove seeds from the green chilli. Wash the spinach, then peel and roughly chop the shallot. Add half of the avocado to a blender with spinach, celery, yoghurt, most of the dill, most of the basil, your peeled garlic, shallot and green chilli. Blitz until smooth and season with salt and pepper before squeezing in the lime juice. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed, then pop in the fridge for at least a couple of hours until very cold.
Dice the halloumi into even-sized cubes and fry in a dry pan over a medium heat until golden all over.

If you feel like the soup needs additional acidity, add in the red wine vinegar. Serve the soup in chilled bowls with a couple of ice cubes then top with avocado, sesame seeds, halloumi, and remaining herbs.

name: Iced Turmeric White Chocolate Milk
description: This iced turmeric is inspired by haldi doodh, a traditional Indian healing drink. We’ve given it a twist by adding white chocolate. Enjoy it hot or cold.
instructions: Add 400ml milk to a saucepan. Crush the cardamom pods. Roughly chop the ginger and add to the milk with all the spices. Season with ½ tsp salt and all the black pepper.
Turn the heat up to medium-high and bring the milk to the boil. Once boiling, turn the heat down and simmer for 5-10 mins.
Meanwhile, chop the white chocolate. Remove the milk from the heat, strain into a bowl, add the white chocolate and let it sit for a couple of minutes until the white chocolate melts. Stir together.

Add the remaining cold milk to the white choc turmeric concentrate. Tip ice into glasses, pour over the turmeric white chocolate milk and top with whipped cream. Finish with a dusting of turmeric or cinnamon, or finely grate over more white chocolate.

name: Icy Kimchi Noodle Soup
description: This icy kimchi noodle soup is cold, spicy and seriously refreshing. Chilled miso broth, chewy noodles and a crunchy cucumber salad on top.
instructions: Chuck all the broth ingredients into a blender and blitz until smooth. Season generously with salt and a bit more honey if needed – since it’s served ice-cold, the flavours will taste milder, so don’t be shy with seasoning.

Pour the broth into an airtight container and stick it in the freezer for 30 mins to 2-3 hrs. The longer you leave it, the icier it gets. You can rake it with a fork to make savoury snow or let it semi-defrost before serving.
Bring a pot of water to the boil. Cook the noodles following pack instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water until completely cool.

Defrost the edamame in a bowl of cold water and drain off any excess water. Trim the cucumber and slice thinly using a knife or mandolin. Chuck it into a bowl with the edamame, kimchi, sesame seeds and vinegar. Season with a pinch of salt and toss to coat.
When you’re ready to eat, spoon the icy broth into bowls, mix through the noodles and top with the cucumber salad.

name: Icy Spicy Noodles
description: Cold noodles are delicious but have you ever had an ice cold noodle soup? This Korean-inspired dish is so tasty and refreshing. Don't knock it till you try it!
instructions: Quarter the spring onions, slice the ginger and smash the garlic cloves. Place in a saucepan with the beef stock, pear juice and soy sauce.
Bring to a simmer over high heat, reduce the heat to medium and cook for 15 mins.
Strain the stock into a large mixing bowl, add the ice cubes and stir to combine.
Season with salt, to taste, then store in the fridge until ready to use.
Slice the cucumber into small matchsticks.
Place in a bowl and toss with 1 tsp salt, then add the rice vinegar and sugar and toss to combine.
If you’re making the spicy sauce, place the gochujang, soy sauce, sugar and gochugaru in a bowl.
Grate in the garlic and pear and mix to combine.
Last bit of cooking. Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Season with salt, add the noodles and cook according to the packet instructions.
Drain, rinse with cold water and drain again.
To assemble, place the noodles in a bowl. Top with some of the pickled cucumber and a pinch of kimchi.
Ladle in the cold broth and add some of the spicy sauce. Add a couple of ice cubes, stir to combine, then tuck in and enjoy.

name: Immune-Boosting Ginger, Turmeric & Coconut Lentils
description: These nourishing lentils are packed with anti-inflammatory ingredients to boost your immune system and warm your soul during colder months.
instructions: Peel the butternut squash. Chop butternut squash and carrot into bite-size 2cm pieces. Dice onion and garlic cloves, grate the ginger, and shred the kale.

Heat a good glug of olive oil on a non-stick saucepan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the onion and fry until it begins to develop some colour. Add the garlic and ginger with a pinch of salt and let cook for another 2 mins until fragrant.
Add the turmeric and cumin and let the spices toast for a minute but don’t let them burn. If the pan is too dry, add a ladleful of vegetable stock.
Stir through the carrots, butternut squash, the remaining vegetable stock and coconut milk and leave to simmer for 25 mins until the carrots and the squash are tender.

Add the split lentils and leave to simmer, stirring regularly, for another 10 mins or until the lentils are fully cooked. The lentils will absorb a lot of the liquid so if it gets too dry, add a couple more ladles of water or vegetable stock.
Turn off the heat and mash about ⅓ of the carrot and squash chunks with a fork.
Stir through the nutritional yeast, the juice of the lemon and the shredded kale. Continue stirring until the kale just starts to wilt. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Divide between bowls and serve with 2 slices of toasted sourdough each.

name: Immunity Balls
description: An immunity boosting drink that’s (a) fun to make, and (b) good for your health. All you have to do is reheat them when you're feeling under the weather.
instructions: Using a knife, peel half of your lemons and all of your oranges.
Add all of your ingredients (including the unpeeled lemons) into a blender and blend until smooth.
Pour into your ice cube moulds and freeze them overnight.
Add 4-7 ice cubes, depending on your preference, to a mug with hot water.
Sip and be healed.

name: Immunity Ginger, Turmeric & Coconut Lentils
description: These nourishing lentils are packed with anti-inflammatory ingredients to boost your immune system and warm your soul during colder months.
instructions: Peel the butternut squash. Chop butternut squash and carrot into bite-size 2cm pieces. Dice onion and garlic cloves, grate the ginger, and shred the kale.

Heat a good glug of olive oil on a non-stick saucepan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the onion and fry until it begins to develop some colour. Add the garlic and ginger with a pinch of salt and let cook for another 2 mins until fragrant.
Add the turmeric and cumin and let the spices toast for a minute but don’t let them burn. If the pan is too dry, add a ladleful of vegetable stock.
Stir through the carrots, butternut squash, the remaining vegetable stock and coconut milk and leave to simmer for 25 mins until the carrots and the squash are tender.

Add the split lentils and leave to simmer, stirring regularly, for another 10 mins or until the lentils are fully cooked. The lentils will absorb a lot of the liquid so if it gets too dry, add a couple more ladles of water or vegetable stock.
Turn off the heat and mash about ⅓ of the carrot and squash chunks with a fork.
Stir through the nutritional yeast, the juice of the lemon and the shredded kale. Continue stirring until the kale just starts to wilt. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Divide between meal-prep containers. Store in the fridge for up to 3 days until ready to reheat and eat. Serve with 2 slices of toasted sourdough each.

name: Immunity Tofu & Ginger Noodle Protein Bowl
description: Protect your immune system this winter with this warming bowl of goodness, filled with vitamins, anti-inflammatories and plant proteins. A very quick and comforting vegan dinner.
keywords: Immune-Boosting Tofu & Ginger Noodle Protein Bowl
instructions: Peel and finely chop your ginger, garlic and shallot. Dissolve the stock cube in the boiling water.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a medium saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the ginger, garlic and shallot and a pinch of sea salt and fry for about 5 mins, until fragrant.

Add ¾ of the tamari and fry for another 2 mins, stirring regularly. Add the stock, bring everything to a bubble, then reduce to a low simmer. Leave it to gently bubble away, stirring occasionally, while you cook the mushrooms and noodles.
Roughly tear the mushrooms apart with your fingers and add to a baking tray. Rub them with a little olive oil and the remaining tamari then roast for 15-18 mins until crispy.
Cook the noodles following packet instructions. Add the edamame to a sieve and sit them in the top of the boiling noodle water for 1 min so they can thaw.

Drain and rinse the edamame in cold water and set aside. Drain and rinse the noodles for a few minutes in cold water then place in a bowl with a small drizzle of olive oil to prevent them sticking together.
Squeeze the water from the tofu with a paper towel and cut it into 1cm cubes.
To serve, start with a couple ladles of broth in each bowl then add a handful of noodles, edamame, tofu and crispy shiitake mushrooms. Top with a few coriander leaves and a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Indian Prawn Karahi With Lime Pickle Yoghurt
description: This Indian dish is named after the pan it's cooked in. The karahi is similar to a wok and is used for high heat, quick cooking. This prawn recipe is healthy and nutritious.
keywords: Indian Prawn Karahi With Lime Pickle Yoghurt
Indian Prawn Karahi With Lime Pickle Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Remove the tops off the peppers and their seeds. Cut into 4cm pieces. Peel and cut the onion into similar-sized pieces. Trim the ends off the green beans and cut into 4cm pieces. Scrape everything into a bowl. Finely dice the tomatoes and finely slice the green chilli, then set both aside.
Spoon the turmeric, coriander and cumin into a shallow bowl, then drain the prawns really well and add to the bowl. Add a pinch of salt, then toss really well.

Heat half of the vegetable oil in a large frying pan, karahi or wok set over a high heat. Once hot, carefully add the prawns and stir-fry for 2 mins until turning pink and slightly charred. Scoop out onto a plate. Tip in the chunky chopped vegetables along with the remaining vegetable oil and fry for 5 mins, stirring every now and again until softening and caramelised. Scrape in the tomatoes and sprinkle in half the green chilli along with the water. Turn the heat to medium and cook for 10 mins until the tomatoes have collapsed and the veg is cooked.
Meanwhile, finely chop the lime pickle and stir it through the yoghurt.
Add the prawns back to the pan, spoon in the garam masala, half and squeeze in the lemon and stir through the coriander. Season to taste.
Spoon the prawn stir-fry into a serving bowl, spoon over some of the yoghurt and sprinkle over the remaining chilli and a few coriander leaves.

name: Indonesian Sambal Fried Chicken (Ayam Geprek)
description: There's always room for another take on fried chicken. This dish known as Ayam geprek is marinated chicken that's pounded, deep-fried and finished with a spicy sambal, it's a super popular dish that originates from Indonesia. Here's our take on it.
instructions: With a sharp knife, butterfly the chicken to make it as flat as possible. Chuck into a bowl, add all the marinade ingredients to the chicken and mix well.
Add all the batter ingredients together and stir with a whisk until smooth. Set up a bowl of cold water.

Take the marinated chicken and plunge it into the batter mix and coat well. Then take it out and plunge it into cold water, and then back into the batter mix. This technique creates layers of batter that clump together, making the batter even crisper when fried. Repeat the process 3 or 4 times with each piece of chicken.
Preheat a pot of oil to 170°C, and fry the chicken until golden brown and wonderfully crispy. This will take 6-7 mins.

Get a pestle and mortar and add all the sambal ingredients to it, pound them together until a paste is formed. (You can use a food processor for this if you prefer). Then using the hot oil from the fried chicken pour a spoon over the paste to cook it. It’ll sizzle, and bring out all of the flavours.

Take the deep fried chicken and something to pound it with, and begin crushing it. You want it to crack and break up a little, but not too much. Then douse the chicken in the sambal and work it into the cracks and craggly bits.
Serve with steamed rice and garnish with cucumbers, lettuce leaves and lime.

name: Indoor BBQ Kebab Platter
description: As great as the British summertime is, sun isn’t always guaranteed. The key is in the marinade and in cooking the meat as close to your grill as you can.
instructions: Preheat your grill on full power.

Finely chop the rosemary, mint and garlic and add to a mixing bowl (reserving a tbsp of the chopped mint) with the yoghurt, lemon zest, chilli, sumac, a tbsp of olive oil and 1 tbsp of salt (remember this is a marinade not a dip!). Cut the chicken into roughly 1 inch cubes and add to the bowl, mix well and set aside at room temperature.
Finely slice the onions and chilli and finely chop the parsley. Add everything to a bowl with the lemon juice, sumac, a pinch of salt, and drizzle of olive oil. Mix well and set aside.

Roughly chop the tomatoes and slice the cucumber and add to a bowl with the reserved mint. Cut both ‘cheeks’ off the lemon and squeeze the middle over the tomatoes and cucumber, add a big pinch of salt and drizzle of olive oil and mix well.
Thread the chicken onto skewers and set them over a high-sided oven dish so the meat is suspended. Place under the grill as close as you can get it to the element without touching.
Cook for 3 mins, flip the skewers and cook for another three minutes. They should be charred and golden on the outside and cooked through but still juicy in the centre.

Spread the hummus over a large platter and top with the skewers. Drain any liquid from the onion and tomato salads and plate them up alongside the skewers. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and serve with warm flatbreads, lemon slices, extra fresh herbs and sumac and the tzatziki on the side.

name: Instant Almond Butter Milk
description: Cheaper than shop bought and you can make them as creamy, light and sweet as you like. Plus they’re completely zero waste by reusing old jars or glass bottles.
instructions: Blend all ingredients until smooth for at least 2 minutes.
Store in a sterilised glass jar or bottle for 3 days.

name: Instant Cashew Milk
description: Cheaper than shop bought and you can make them as creamy, light and sweet as you like. Plus they’re completely zero waste by reusing old jars or glass bottles.
instructions: Blend all ingredients until smooth for at least 2 minutes.
Store in a sterilised glass jar or bottle for 3 days.

name: Instant Mushroom Miso Ramen
description: A quick and simple lunch recipe you can make in one go and eat throughout the week.
keywords: Mushroom Miso Ramen Lunch Pots recipe
instructions: Use a speed peeler to peel the carrot into thin ribbons. Finely slice the shiitake mushrooms and the spring onions. Chop up your tofu into even-sized cubes.
Add ¼ of the miso, soy sauce, sesame oil and chilli flakes into each pot and stir to combine. Layer the rest of the ingredients into the pots. You can break up the noodles if needed.
When ready to eat, add 470ml of boiling water to each pot and set aside for 5 mins to cook the noodles and soften the veg.

name: Instant Noodles Upgrade
description: Making your packet ramen spectacular is a pretty personal thing. This recipe is our go-to for when your low on time, energy and want something delicious.
instructions: Bring a pan of water to the boil. Drop the egg in and cook for 6 mins.

Cook the noodles according to packet instructions, drain but reserve 50ml of water. Tip into a bowl, then whisk the water with the soy and the packet of flavouring. Tip over the noodles and toss well.

Drizzle with the tahini and chilli oil. Peel the egg, halve and whack on top. Finely slice the spring onions and scatter over, along with the coriander leaves and toasted seeds. Tuck in, preferably from the sofa.

name: Instant Pumpkin Seed Milk
description: Cheaper than shop bought and you can make them as creamy, light and sweet as you like. Plus they’re completely zero waste by reusing old jars or glass bottles.
instructions: Blend all ingredients until smooth for at least 2 minutes.
Store in a sterilised glass jar or bottle for 3 days.

name: Instant Rava Dosa Recipe
description: A gorgeous restaurant-style rava dosa recipe that you can make at home. Serve it with all of your favourite chutneys.
instructions: Finely grate the ginger, trim and finely dice the onion and thinly slice the coriander, stalks and all.

Combine all the ingredients in a large bowl (except the oil or ghee) to make a thin batter. Let it sit for 10 mins. Once rested, add more water if required – the batter needs to be very thin to achieve those characteristic dosa holes.

Heat a non-stick pan over a medium-high heat. Add a ladle full of the batter in and cook for 30 seconds. Don’t swirl the pan – just add a few more tablespoons of batter to any areas that haven’t already been covered.
Drizzle over some oil or ghee and allow the dosa to cook for 2-3 mins until the edges turn golden. Scrape off any excess batter for a super-crisp and thin dosa, if you like.
Peel the dosa off the pan and serve with your favourite chutneys. Check out my coconut and tomato chutney recipes (also on mob.co.uk) for inspiration.

name: Instant Sunflower Seed Milk
description: Cheaper than shop bought and you can make them as creamy, light and sweet as you like. Plus they’re completely zero waste by reusing old jars or glass bottles.
instructions: Blend all ingredients until smooth for at least 2 minutes.
Store in a sterilised glass jar or bottle for 3 days.

name: Iraqi Lamb Dolma
description: A one-pot wonder from Philip Juma. Stuffed onion shells, stuffed peppers, and vines leaves slow cooked in lemon juice, garlic and pomegranate molasses.
instructions: Begin soaking your rice in plenty of water.
In a medium saucepan, poach your lamb ribs in cardamom, and one garlic bulb (cut in half). Bring to the boil, removing the ‘scum’ as it boils. Drain and set aside.
Cut the ends from your white onions and then make an incision halfway down not going past the core/middle.
In a medium saucepan, on a low simmer, poach the onions in salted water for 10-15 mins. You should see the onion layers coming apart.
Once soft, run cold water over the onions. Carefully remove each onion layer and set aside.
Prep your vine leaves by removing from the jar and rinsing in cold water.
For your peppers, make a slit in each and set aside.
Now that your vegetables are all ready, let’s start on the stuffing.
Drain the rice and add to a large bowl. Add the lamb mince.
Dry mix all the spices and 20g salt. Add to the rice and lamb along with the sunflower oil, half your pomegranate molasses, tamarind paste, and water.
Stuff your onions and peppers.
Roll your vine leaves.
Now we can begin layering the pot.
In a medium saucepan, place the lamb ribs at the bottom of the pot. Layer on your vine leaves, followed by the onions and then, finally, the baby peppers.
Finely slice one bulb of garlic and add to the saucepan.
Drizzle with the remaining pomegranate molasses and the juice of your lemons.
Season with salt and add water until it reaches the peppers.
Bring to a boil with the lid on. Then bring down to a simmer until the water has reduced. After 1 hour, remove from the heat and you’re ready for that dolma reveal.

name: Iraqi-Style Saffron Braised Chicken
description: Braising your chicken in this beautiful saffron sauce gives it an unreal texture and flavour. One to whip out at special occasions.
instructions: If you’ve got the time, add the saffron to the rose water and cover it with 3 tbsp of boiling water the night before you want to make your chicken. Cover and leave in the fridge overnight. If not, simply mix them at the start of the recipe on the day with the same quantity of boiling water.

The next day, season your chicken thighs with fine sea salt. Add a good glug of oil to a large pot and set over a high heat. Add the seasoned chicken, skin-side down and sear until golden brown and crispy.

Cut the potatoes into rough chunks and add to the pan. Crumble in the chicken stock cube and pour over boiling water to cover the contents of the pan. Add the cardamom and salt, thinly slice one lemon and add that to the pan too. Bring to a simmer and let cook away for 35 mins. Once chicken is cooked through and the potatoes and lemons have softened, add the steeped saffron and rose water.
Let it come back to a simmer then add the remaining lemon juice.
Scatter over the herbs and olives.
Serve your braised chicken over steamed basmati rice with plenty of sauce.

name: Island Brunch Bowl
description: A delicious plant-based brunch bowl from chef Collin Brown, Executive Chef at Turtle Bay. One of the stars of this dish is ackee – Jamaica’s national fruit.
instructions: To make the sautéed ackee, start by combining the spices and pop them in a jar, this will make more than you need, but will hang it out happily in your spice cupboard until next time. Drain and rinse the tin of ackee.
Roughly chop the onions, spring onions and yellow pepper.

Preheat a large saucepan over medium heat and add a shot of veg oil, wait until it heats up. Add one diced onion and yellow pepper to the pan and cook over medium heat for 5 mins. Add one of the chopped beef tomato, the rinsed ackee and 1 tsp of the spice mix – cook and stir for 5 mins, remove from heat and set aside to keep warm.

For the Callaloo, preheat another saucepan over medium heat and add a shot of vegetable oil, wait until it heats up. Sauté one of the chopped white onions, one spring onion, half scotch bonnet, one yellow pepper, and thyme from one sprig in oil for 5 mins. Add the remaining chopped tomato and then stir in the callaloo. Season with the from before spice mix, then add one of the tins of coconut milk. Simmer for five minutes and set aside.

For the curried chickpeas, preheat your saucepan over medium heat and oil, wait until it heats up. Sauté one chopped white onion, chopped garlic cloves, one chopped spring onion, half scotch bonnet (chopped) and fresh thyme for 5 minutes. Add all seasonings (tsp each curry powder, teaspoon turmeric and teaspoon spice mix) and stir for a few minutes to let the spices release. Add in the drained chickpeas and stir.
Add in a tin of coconut milk, season with salt and simmer for at least 10 mins (the longer the better) set aside.

Peel the plantain and cut into 1cm diagonal slices. Drizzle just enough oil into a nonstick pan to coat the bottom, and place it on medium heat.When the oil begins to shimmer, add plantains (work in batches). Fry for 1 ½ mins on one side, flip and cook for 1 ½ mins on the other side.
Remove plantains from the pan and drain on the kitchen roll. Quickly sauté the cherry tomatoes until bursting.
Finally, add everything to a bowl, garnish with fresh chopped chillies, chopped spring onion and a few sprigs of coriander. Serve with fresh roti.

name: Italian Dumplings Recipe With Spicy Tomato Sauce
description: Malfatti translates as ‘malformed’ in Italian, so don’t be too precious when forming these light, cheesy ricotta balls. You won’t find an easier Italian dumplings recipe on the internet. Become a master of Italian cooking by starting with this delicious gateway dish into what makes the cuisine of Italy so special.
keywords: Italian Dumplings With Spicy Tomato Sauce
instructions: Start the sauce first by thinly slicing the garlic and chilli, removing the seeds if you like. Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a deep frying pan set over a medium heat.

Add the garlic and chilli cook gently for 3-4 mins until smelling amazing, then tip in the tomatoes. Use a metal spoon or potato masher to crush the tomatoes a bit. Season with salt and pepper and simmer gently for 30 mins. At this stage you could use a stick blender to whizz the sauce until smooth, if you want a fancier finish. Season to taste.

For the malfatti, finely chop the garlic. Melt the butter in a large, deep frying pan set over a medium heat, then add in the garlic. Cook gently for 3-4 mins until smelling amazing, then tip in all of the spinach. Use tongs to toss and turn the spinach until it is all wilted. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from the heat and transfer the spinach into a colander or sieve set over a bowl. Leave to drain and cool.

Once cool enough to handle, use your hands to squeeze out as much liquid as possible (you’ll need to be thorough with this, or your malfatti won’t hold). Tip into a food processor and pulse to finely chop.
Add in the ricotta, egg yolks, then grate in the Parmesan and nutmeg and tip in the flour. Pulse briefly together to combine so you have a thick, sticky dough. Season well with salt and pepper.

Sprinkle around an even layer of plain flour onto a plate and also lightly flour a baking tray. Use slightly damp hands to form the dough into golf ball-sized dumplings, then roll in the flour and put onto the tray. Repeat with the remaining dough.
Fill a large pan with salted boiling water. Divide the tomato sauce between 4 shallow bowls - the malfatti cook quickly, having it plated means you can eat it hot!

Add the malfatti to the boiling water and cook for 1-2 mins until they float, then use a slotted spoon to remove from the water, drain well and put straight onto the sauce. Grate over plenty of parmesan, drizzle with oil and scatter with basil leaves to serve.

name: Jacket Aubergine with Spiced Lamb, Rice & Tahini Yoghurt
description: Aubergines roasted until collapsing, split like a baked potato and loaded with ras el hanout lamb, toasted pine nuts and a lemony tahini yoghurt. It's way easier than it looks.
cuisine: Middle-Eastern Inspired, North African, Moroccan-Inspired, North African-Inspired
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper. Place the aubergines on the tray, pierce them a few times with the tip of a knife, then brush with olive oil. Roast for 40 mins, until the aubergines are completely tender.
In a bowl, mix together the yoghurt, tahini and the juice of most of one lemon. Season generously with salt and pepper, then set aside.

Peel the onion and garlic, then dice the onion and finely chop the garlic. Roughly chop all your fresh herbs and set aside. Cook the rice in the microwave for half the instructed cook time, then set aside.

Place the pine nuts in a large frying pan over a medium-low heat, no oil needed. Shake the pan frequently or stir constantly for 3-5 mins, until they turn golden brown and smell fragrant. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

Heat a glug of olive oil in the same pan over a medium heat, then add the onion and sweat down until translucent. Add the garlic and cook for 2 mins, until fragrant. Turn the heat up to high, add the lamb mince, season with salt and pepper and cook for 5-8 mins, until browned. Stir in the ras el hanout and cook for a further 2 mins, then add the honey, stock pot and the water to deglaze. Cook for 1 more min, until everything is coated and glossy. Add the rice and stir until fully combined. Turn off the heat, then fold through most of the fresh herbs and pine nuts, saving a few of each to serve. Squeeze in the rest of the lemon juice, taste and season with salt and pepper.

To serve, grab some tongs and place an aubergine in the centre of each plate. Use a knife to slice down the aubergine lengthways and spread it open as you would with a jacket potato. Season with salt and pepper, then spoon on the lamb mixture. Drizzle with the tahini yoghurt and sprinkle over the rest of the herbs and pine nuts. Slice the remaining lemon into fat wedges and serve on the side.

name: Jackfruit Chipotle Tostadas
description: Jackfruit is a wonderful meat substitute. It absorbs the roasted tomato and chipotle sauce beautifully and has an incredible meaty bite.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.

Chop the tomatoes into quarters and do the same with the garlic. Pop the tomatoes onto a roasting tray and drizzle with olive oil. Push the pieces of garlic into the tomatoes, then sprinkle with oregano and salt. Roast for 30-45 mins until charred. Push on them gently halfway through to press out the liquid from the tomatoes.

Whilst the tomatoes and garlic are roasting, make the salsa. Chop up your raw tomatoes, red onion and coriander. Place all of those ingredients into a bowl with any liquid that the tomatoes have released whilst you were cutting them, then season with salt and lime juice.
Back to the jackfruit prep. Chop up the onions and heat a small glug of oil in a large saucepan. Fry the onions with the cumin seeds for 10 mins until soft.

Add in the tomato purée and chipotle and cook for another 5 mins until it has darkened in colour. Add in the roasted tomatoes and any of the remaining liquid in the tray. Drain the tinned jackfruit and add it into the pan with 500ml water. Bring to the boil and allow to simmer for 30 mins.

Refried bean time. Chop up the remaining onion and red chilli and fry in a glug of oil for 5 mins with the cumin seeds. Add in the pinto beans along with the liquid from the tin. Cook for 5 mins until most of the liquid has evaporated. Mash well and season with salt.
Remove the jackfruit from the sauce and shred it with a fork. Add it back into the sauce and season with salt.
Toast the tortillas in a dry saucepan until crisp. Spread on a tablespoon of refried beans, then the pulled jackfruit and, to finish, the salsa.

name: Jalapeño & Cheddar Pesto
description: A very untraditional pesto that's packed with spice. This one has got a real something-something.
instructions: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry frying pan. Add the coriander, jalapeños and toasted pumpkin seeds to a blender. Peel the garlic clove and add in, then roughly chop the cheddar and add. Add the lemon juice and season generously with salt and pepper.
Add ⅓ of olive oil and begin to blend, then continue to add olive oil until you get to a thick pesto consistency.

name: Jalapeño & Coconut Chicken Thighs
description: This is sort of what you'd get if a coconut chutney and a chicken traybake had a baby. It’s deceptively simple to make and incredibly delicious.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Season the chicken thighs with salt.
Heat a large frying pan over medium heat (no oil needed). Add the desiccated coconut and cook, stirring constantly until golden and toasted, 2-4 mins. Tip onto a plate.
Put the chicken thighs into the empty pan, skin-side down, and cook for 8-10 mins until the skin is deep golden brown. Transfer to a baking tray.
Blend the sauce ingredients together until smooth. Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed. Pour into the baking tray and transfer the chicken into the oven until cooked through, 30-40 mins.
