Meanwhile, reheat the rice. Thinly slice the remaining jalapeño and cut the lime into wedges.
Once the chicken is cooked, serve the rice into bowls. Ladle in the sauce and top with the chicken. Finish with a sprinkling of the toasted coconut, jalapeño and a wedge of lime.

name: Jalapeño Bottle Caps
description: Deep fried pickled jalapeños – you can't get better than a fistful of these with a cold beer. Tangy, spicy, and completely moreish.
instructions: Drain the jalapeños, reserving the pickling liquid they came in. Blot them well with kitchen paper to dry and toss them with flour until coated.
Add the oil to a medium-sized deep saucepan so that it comes no more than halfway up the sides and set over a high heat until the temperature reaches 180°C.
Pour the reserved pickling liquid into a large bowl with plain flour and the fajita seasoning. Dip the jalapeños in the batter, then scoop them out using a fork and transfer straight to the hot oil.
Fry for 2 mins until golden and crisp, then remove and drain on kitchen paper to soak up any excess oil.
In a small bowl, mix the coriander, soured cream and lime zest. Cut the zested lime into wedges.
Serve the jalapeños with a sprinkle of salt and pepper, the dipping sauce and the lime wedges.

name: Jalapeño Butter Chicken Kyiv
description: I bet you thought Chicken Kyiv couldn't get any better? Well, it just did. Pickled jalapeños bring spicy, tangy punch to this flavour bomb.
instructions: Finely chop the jalapeños, spring onions, garlic and parsley. Add to a bowl with the softened butter and beat together. Season with salt and pepper and set aside. You can do this in a food processor or mini chopper if you have one!

Make an incision starting at the thicker end of each chicken breast with a small, sharp knife. You want to create a pocket in the chicken breast for the butter to sit in. The best way to do this is to push the knife in just over halfway, being careful not to cut out any side of the breast. Repeat with the other chicken breasts.

Use a teaspoon or a piping bag to fill each breast with a healthy portion of the butter, leaving the opening clean so you can get a good seal. Press the breast to flatten it slightly then press the edges together with your fingers to reseal the opening.

Now set up a bowl each of flour, egg and breadcrumbs. Pass the chicken breasts through each bowl, flour, egg, breadcrumb and then back through egg and breadcrumbs to get a really thorough coating. Pop the kyivs into the fridge for 20 mins.
Remove the tough stalks from the cavolo nero and set aside. Preheat the oven to 170°C.

Peel the potatoes and cut into big chunks. Boil in seasoned water until just tender, this will take around 12-13 mins. Mash the potatoes with the milk, grated parmesan and a knob of extra butter. Keep warm while you cook the kyivs.

Cover the base of a large frying pan with a 1cm layer of olive oil. Set over a medium heat and cook the kyivs for 2-3 mins on each side until golden brown. Transfer to a tray and pop in the oven for 10-12 mins until cooked through.
Cook the cavolo nero in a pan with olive oil and salt and finish with a squeeze of lemon.
Serve the warm mash topped with kyivs, cavolo nero and lemon wedges.
Get stuck in.

name: Jalapeño Caesar Dressing
description: A nice and spicy dressing you can throw on anything.Big on umami, this one.
keywords: Tomato Salad With Jalapeño Caesar Dressing
instructions: Peel the garlic and finely chop the pickled jalapeños.
Add the garlic to a pestle and mortar (if you don't have one use a blender or just finely chop everything), smash the garlic then add the anchovies, smooshing them into a paste.

Add the jalapeños and keep smooshing until it comes together, then add the mayo and the lemon zest before juicing in half of the lemon – taste and adjust with the remaining lemon juice if needed. Grate in the Parmesan. Give it a good season with some black pepper and taste again. If you think it needs salt, add it.

name: Jamaican Bully Beef
description: Corned beef deserves more love. Jackson Mclarty shows off what you can do with a tin of corned beef and a few store-cupboard ingredients in this simple dish.
instructions: Trim and finely chop the pepper and tomato. Peel and thinly slice the garlic, finely dice the onion. Thinly slice the spring onion and pierce the scotch bonnet, making sure to keep it whole.

Place a saucepan on medium-high heat with 1 tbsp of oil. Once hot, add the pepper, garlic, onion and scotch bonnet. Cook until softened, 3-4 mins. Stir through the all-purpose seasoning and thyme and cook for 1-2 mins.

Add the corned beef into the pan and break it up using a spatula, cook for 3-4 mins. Stir through the tomatoes along with the tomato purée, sweetcorn, and ketchup until the tomatoes have softened and the mixture has thickened, 4-5 mins. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Serve with fried plantain, rice and garnish with spring onion.

name: Jammy Eggs With Blistered Tomatoes & Pesto Lentils
description: A tomato and pesto situation teamed with oh-so perfect jammy eggs. The perfect 6-ingredient recipe, great for meat eaters and vegetarians alike.
instructions: Get a saucepan full of water to the boil. Add the whole cherry tomatoes into a frying pan on medium-high heat with 2 tbsps of olive oil. Cook until starting to char, 5-7 mins.
Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice the onion. Add them to the tomatoes and cook until softened, 4-6 mins.
Once the water is boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook until soft boiled, 6-7 mins.
Once the onions have softened, stir through the spinach until wilted. Then add the lentils and ¾ of the pesto. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Mix the remaining pesto with 20ml of olive oil. Peel and cut the eggs in half.
Share the lentils between your bowls, top with eggs and a drizzle of pesto.

name: Jammy Tomatoes & Creamy Butter Beans On Toast
description: This is the most perfect weeknight meal with burst toms and a creamy, dreamy butter bean smoosh.
keywords: Jammy Tomatoes & Creamy Butter Beans On Toast
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C fan.
Peel and finely slice shallots, then add into a small bowl with the juice of a lime and a pinch of salt.
Place the cherry tomatoes into a baking dish with the sumac, 4 tbsp of olive oil and salt and pepper. Mix well and cook for 25 min until charred and blistered.

Meanwhile, drain the butter beans and add to a blender with the yoghurt and grated garlic. Whizz until smooth then season with salt and pepper. If it's looking a bit stiff, add a little of the butter bean water.
When ready to serve, halve and toast the sourdough before spreading with the butterbean purée. Top with the jammy tomatoes and shallots, then top with a grating of lime zest and some coriander.

name: Japanese Carrot Ginger Dressing Soup with Sesame Crackers
description: If you love Japanese carrot ginger salad dressing, you will love this soup. It’s sweet, zingy and aromatic and goes perfectly with these homemade sesame crackers.
keywords: Japanese Carrot Ginger Dressing Soup with Sesame Crackers Recipe
instructions: Start by making the crackers. Preheat the oven to 160°C and line a baking sheet with baking paper or a silicone baking mat.

In a medium bowl, mix the sesame seeds, flax seeds and salt. In a small separate bowl, mix the miso paste, water and sesame oil. Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir until a thick consistency is achieved. Let the dough rest for 10 mins to allow the flax seeds to gel.

Wet your hands with water and flatten the dough onto the baking sheet. Bake for 10 mins, then remove briefly to score into pieces (triangles, squares, or any shape you prefer). Return the sheet to the oven and bake for an additional 30 mins, or until golden and crispy. Cool down before serving.

Meanwhile, get started on the soup. Peel and roughly chop the shallot, finely chop the garlic, and grate the ginger. Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large pot set over medium heat. Add the chopped shallot and sauté, covered, for about 5 mins. Add the garlic and ginger, sautéing for an additional 3 mins until fragrant.

Scrub the carrots clean and remove the ends (no need to peel), then roughly chop them and add to the pot along with the miso paste. Pour in enough vegetable broth to cover the carrots and simmer for 20 mins, or until they’re soft (you may not need the full amount of stock).
While the soup is cooking, thinly slice the radishes and chop the spring onions. Toss them with a splash of sesame oil and rice vinegar to create a simple garnish.
Blend the soup until smooth and garnish with a few sesame miso crackers and the marinated radishes and spring onion.

name: Japanese-Inspired Green Goddess Bowl
description: A classic green goddess but with a Japanese-inspired sesame dressing that's aromatic, creamy, and clings onto greens you throw at it. Dreamy.
instructions: Blend all the dressing ingredients together until bright green and smooth. Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed. If the dressing looks too thick, add more lime juice – it should be scoopable but still have a little movement. Set aside in the fridge.

Slice the cucumber into thin diagonal strips, then lay the pieces of cucumber slightly on top of each creating a long line, slice into thin strips, working all the way down the line and add to a large bowl. Cut the lettuce in half and make diagonal slits around the core to remove it. Finely shred one lettuce half and chop the other half into rough cubes. Tip into the cucumber bowl. Roughly slice the coriander and add to the bowl. Drain and rinse the can of beans in a sieve, washing away all the bean juice. Dry the beans very well and sprinkle with a generous pinch of salt, then add to the bowl of greens. Season the greens with a drizzle of sesame oil, a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt. Toss well.

Grab a big serving platter and swoosh the creamy dressing all over it. Use tongs to pile the slaw on top in an even layer, trying to leave behind any liquid leaked from the veggies. Top with avocado slices, fresh herbs, toasted sesame seeds, a generous drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a good pinch of flaky sea salt. Pour your favourite tortilla chips into bowls and serve alongside the salad.

name: Japanese-Inspired Minced Beef Curry
description: Japanese curry is one of those dishes that always hits. Comfortingly spiced with a rich, thick sauce, soft potato and beef, all in one pot. Make a big batch and thank yourself later.
instructions: Finely mince the garlic and grate the ginger. Peel the carrot and potatoes and roughly cube.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with the vegetable oil. Add the beef mince and cook for 5-6 mins, until browned on one side, then break up any clumps and continue cooking until just cooked through.

Add the ginger and garlic to the pan and fry for a minute. Add the flour and curry powder and let toast for a minute, then add the potatoes and carrot. Pour in the water and sugar, cover with a lid and cook over a low heat for 10-15 mins, until the potatoes are cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Tip in the peas and stir through for a minute, just to heat through.

Meanwhile, bring a small saucepan of water to the boil. Cook the eggs for 6 mins 30 seconds, then transfer to a bowl of cold water to stop the cooking. Once cool enough to handle, peel and slice in half.
Heat the rice according to the packet instructions.
Season the curry with salt and black pepper, and loosen with a splash more water if needed. Then divide the rice between bowls and top with the curry, jammy eggs and pickled sushi ginger.

name: Jason's Bajan Macaroni Pie
description: Chef Jason Howard has made us this golden, comforting macaroni pie. It’s one of the most popular dishes in Barbados and a Bajan take on mac and cheese.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Start by cooking off your macaroni, in salted boiling water for 7 mins.
Drain, holding onto some of your pasta water as you’ll need it to help out with your cheese sauce later on.
Dice the onion and grate the Cheddar cheese. Preheat a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the oil and onions to sweat in the pan with a big pinch of salt for 6-7 mins. Finely chop the garlic and toss into the pan with the thyme.
Once everything is translucent, add your flour and cook out for 2-3 mins. Now, start whisking while adding your milk slowly, until you have a thick, smooth sauce.

Now add your mustard and combine well. If your mix is still too stiff at this point add a bit of your pasta water and whisk until smooth. Coarsely grate the cheddar and add 350g to the sauce with the mayo and sugar.
Now add the pasta to your sauce and mix thoroughly. Pour into a baking tray and cover with the remaining 150g of Cheddar.
Bake in the oven for 30-45 mins until golden brown on top. Serve with a chopped green salad on the side.

name: Jelly's Sichuan Noodles
description: This recipe is inspired by one of my favourites, Dan Dan Noodles. It’s got everything. It’s savoury, spicy, acidic and so addictive.
instructions: Place a wok over a medium high heat, tip in the Sichuan peppercorns, then toast for 2 mins until fragrant. Tip the toasted peppercorns into a mini chopper and blitz into a powder. If you don’t have a mini chopper or spice grinder, use a pestle and mortar to crush or finely chop with a knife. Set aside.
Slice your cucumber into matchsticks and put into a bowl of iced water and set aside. This is optional, but ensures that your cucumber stays crunchy.

Heat 2 tbsp of oil in the wok over a high heat, chuck in your pork mince and stir fry for 2-3 mins, until browned. Add the Shaoxing wine, 2 tbsp of the soy sauce, 1 tsp of the blitzed/crushed Sichuan peppercorns and 1 tsp sugar. Cook for a minute and then remove from the heat and set aside.
Drain the cucumber matchsticks and pat them dry. Lightly crush or roughly chop your peanuts. Bring a large pan of water to the boil. Season with salt.

Lay out 4 bowls and into each bowl add 1 tsp tahini, 3 tbsp chili oil, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp crushed Sichuan peppercorns, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tsp of MSG. Finely grate a garlic clove into each bowl. Do not mix it yet. This is going to create a delicious sauce.
Drop the noodles into the pan of boiling water and cook according to packet instructions. Remove from the heat and use a small jug to reserve a cup full of the noodle water. Drain the noodles.
Add around 3 tbsp of the noodle water to each bowl.

Assembly time. Place the hot noodles into each bowl along with a spoonful of the pork mince. Top with the cucumber and crushed peanuts. Just before eating, give a big mix so the sauce is coating the noodles. Eat straight away!

name: Jerk Lentils and Roti
description: Jacob King (aka Peng Vegan Munch) shows us how to make the most saucy Caribbean dish, featuring everyone’s favourite legume paired with delicious roti.
instructions: Dice your garlic, ginger, onion and scotch bonnet.
Fry your diced veg in a large pan with a tbsp of vegetable oil until soft and slightly browned.
Add your dried spices and stock powder then fry for a few mins. Add a splash of water to deglaze the pan and simmer for another minute.
Wash your green lentils and set aside.

Add the fresh thyme, chopped tomatoes, a cup of water, brown sugar and washed lentils to the pan and the simmer on a medium heat for 15 mins. You want the lentils to absorb the liquid and become proper saucy.
Gradually add the water to the flour and combine into a firm dough, cover and rest for 30 mins.
Break into 6 equal-sized pieces and roll out thin over a floured surface before dry frying for a minute or 2 on each side.
Serve up the lentils with freshly cooked roti and enjoy.

name: Jolene's Salt & Pepper Chicken
description: Jolene, Xien's mum, came into the studio to show us how to make her famous salt and pepper chicken. A real takeaway classic, this one's a goodie!
instructions: Chop your chicken into small chunks, pop them into a large mixing bowl.
Whisk your egg and add ½ of it to your chicken along with the milk, white pepper, Shaoxing wine and 1 teaspoon of salt. Give it a good mix and pop it in the fridge.
In a separate mixing bowl, combine all the ingredients for seasoning the chicken. Set aside.
Chop your onion into pieces, mince your garlic, red chilli and thinly slice your spring onions. Pop them into a bowl and set them aside for later.
In a separate mixing bowl, mix the potato starch with the self-raising flour.
Add the marinated chicken pieces to the flour mix. Then, one by one, shake the excess flour off the chicken and add the remaining flour mix to the chicken.

Pour 1.5 litres of oil into your wok on medium heat, pop a chopstick in and if bubbles emerge, your oil is ready. Place half your chicken pieces into the oil and fry until lightly golden. Place them on a paper-lined tray and deep fry the remaining chicken pieces.
Repeat, and deep fry the chicken pieces again (this time until crispy and golden).

Add a glug of oil to a wok, then fry your prepped veg from earlier. Add your crispy chicken and the seasoning mix. Give it a good toss until everything is combined and the chicken is evenly coated in seasoning.
Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Jollof Rice
description: Pair this jollof rice with your Chicken Suya Skewers. It's absolutely delicious. From the Suya Pit (@thesuyapit).
instructions: Roughly cut the onion and peppers and transfer to a blender. Add the garlic, plum tomatoes and scotch bonnet chilli and blend until smooth.

Heat 50ml vegetable oil in a large pot set over a medium heat. Add the blended mixture and the tomato purée. Cook for a few minutes until fragrant then cover with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Simmer for 10-15 mins.

Meanwhile, wash the rice. Add the thyme, stock powder, rice and water to the pot and stir well. Increase the heat to medium-high, bring the rice to the boil, then cover with a lid. Turn the heat down to low and cook for 25 mins, stirring every 5-7 mins. When the rice is done, keep the lid on and let it rest for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, slice the plantains into ovals (or any shape you like). Season with a little salt and set aside for 5 mins.
Add the vegetable oil to a saucepan with high sides and heat over a medium heat to 175°C. Carefully drop the plantain in and fry for 3-5 mins until golden brown. Transfer to kitchen paper to drain.
Plate up the ting and tell your belly it’s time to chow down.

name: Jollof Rice
description: Oyinda Robinson's easy guide to an absolutely delicious homemade jollof rice, Nigerian style. Fresh tomatoes and spicy infused rice. The ultimate jollof recipe.
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, red pepper, one and a half chopped onions and paprika together in a food processor. If using tinned tomatoes there is no need for water but if using whole tomatoes, add a splash of water.
Get a large saucepan over a medium heat. Drizzle in a 2 tablespoons of the oil, chop up the other onion half and fry, stirring occasionally, until soft. Remove the onion and set aside.

Using the same pan, drizzle in the remaining oil and add your blended ingredients, as well as the thyme, both stock cubes, bay leaves (some whole and some torn up), the tomato purée and the whole scotch bonnet. Then, let this simmer until the oil begins to separate, around 15 mins, whilst you prepare your rice.
Wash the rice to remove any starch, you will know the starch has washed away once the water runs clear.

Add the rice to the pan, and stir it in. Cover in two parts boiling water. Bring it to a simmer and then let it putter away for 10 mins or so until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is cooked through.
Season to taste with salt and black pepper. Then cover the saucepan and steam over a very low heat for 10 mins.
Add your softened onions to the pan and mix them in. Cover and let it steam for a further 10 mins. Serve at the table for everyone totuck in!

name: Jollof Rice by Selasi
description: Selasi shows us how it’s done: Jollof Rice, the Ghanaian way. Topped with crispy herby chicken thighs and fried plantain. A feast for the MOB.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200ºC/392°F.

To make your chicken stock, blend together your thyme, onion, garlic, ginger and 160ml of water. Pop your chicken thighs in a large non-stick pot and pour your blended mixture over them with a seasoning of salt, paprika, and crumbled Maggi stock cube. Leave this to simmer on a low heat for 20 minutes, then remove the chicken from the stock and set this aside for later (keep the stock).

Now for your tomato stew. Add your oil and tomato purée to the leftover stock and cook this gently on a medium heat. Meanwhile, whizz together your fresh tomatoes, red pepper, red onion and scotch bonnet. Pour these blitzed ingredients to the stock and cook this on a medium heat for 20 minutes turning it into a thick stew.

Thoroughly wash your rice, drain any liquid, and then add this to your stew alongside 100ml water. Cover the pot and leave this to cook on a medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring very occasionally to evenly distribute the rice.

Chop up your green beans and carrots, then add to the stew and give a gentle stir. Place some parchment paper or tin foil directly onto the rice to cover it and control the steam. Leave this to cook for a further 20 minutes and then set aside.

For the herby chicken, whizz together all of the ingredients until it forms a rough paste (basil, coriander, parsley, garlic, oil and breadcrumbs). Spread this over your chicken and roast in the oven for 20 minutes until it’s crispy, tender, and delicious.

To make the plantain, heat your oil in a wok or frying pan on a medium heat. Whilst this is heating up, peel your plantain and dice it. Season your chunks with the cayenne pepper/chilli powder, the ground ginger, and the salt. Once your oil is bubbling, fry your plantain until golden. Then, using a slotted spoon, remove it from the oil and place in a bowl lined with kitchen roll to drain the excess oil.
Dish up your Jollof rice, then top with your plantain and chicken. An iconic Ghanaian recipe that you’re bound to love - get cooking and enjoy MOB!

name: Jordon's Interview Salad
description: This salad is so good it got me a job! Creamy labneh is mixed with sweet onions, tossed with crunchy pitta, and used to dress a vibrant summer salad. Jordon
instructions: Start by making the labneh. Spread a clean tea towel out onto your work surface. To the tub of yoghurt, add ½ a tsp of salt and the zest of half a lemon. Stir well.

Empty the yoghurt out onto the tea towel and bring the four corners together. Tie the tea towel either to the tap over the sink, or somewhere convenient that you can leave it in a sieve with a bowl underneath. It should look like one of those hanging lunchboxes on a stick that they have in cartoons.

Allow the labneh to hang and strain - depending on the thickness of the yoghurt you started with, this may take from 30 mins to 2 hours. Ultimately, you want a consistency between Greek yoghurt and cream cheese.
Peel and finely slice your onions. Peel your cloves of garlic and crush them gently.

Add 100ml of olive oil to a saucepan and place over a low heat. Add the onion, garlic and a large pinch of salt, then allow to sizzle gently for at least 20 mins until very soft and golden, but not too browned. Discard the garlic, and set the onions and all the cooking oil aside to cool.
While the onions cook, prepare the vegetables. Use a box grater to grate the courgette into a bowl. Add a pinch of salt, mix and set aside.
Slice the bottom off the baby gem lettuce and separate the leaves into a large mixing bowl. Slice the artichokes into quarters and add to the bowl along with the baby gem.
Open up the pitta breads so you have two thin layers of bread, then tear them into roughly 2-inch squares (they don’t have to be neat).

Put a frying pan over a medium heat, add your butter and a tbsp of olive oil. Once hot, add the pitta bread and fry until golden and crunchy. Take off the heat and add a pinch of salt, a tsp of chilli flakes and a tsp of sumac and toss well. Set aside to cool.

Pop the pan back over a medium-high heat and add a splash of olive oil. Give the grated courgette a squeeze, then add them to the pan. Move it around and let it fry for 3 or 4 mins. Set aside to cool, then repeat with the peas.

To assemble, mix the now-cooled onions and their cooking oil into the labneh. Add the peas and courgettes to the bowl with the baby gem and artichokes, a pinch of salt, the juice of 1 lemon. Add the labneh and mix well to coat everything.
Just before you’re ready to serve, mix through the pitta (keep a few to sprinkle on top). Finish with lots of chopped mint, plenty of sumac and olive oil. Serve and enjoy!

name: Jordon's Tarte Tatin
description: I learnt to make this in Paris and I look forward to it every Autumn. So simple and so comforting. Jordon x
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Roll out the puff pastry to around 5mm thick.
Using the base of the frying pan as a guide, cut a circle of the pastry slightly larger than the base.
Prick gently all over with a fork and place into the freezer for at least half an hour.
Meanwhile, peel, quarter and core all of the apples.
Melt the sugar in the same frying pan over a low heat. Do not stir, just tilt and shake the pan gently to move the sugar as it melts. You want it to darken somewhat but stay away from dark brown.
Once all of the sugar has melted, roughly cube and stir in the butter until it has melted.
Place the apples round side down into the pan, fit as many as you can in one layer. Sprinkle with a generous pinch of sea salt.
Place into the oven for 25 mins to bake the apples.
Remove the pastry disc from the freezer, place over the apples and tuck the edges down a little. Use a knife to prick a few holes in the pastry to allow air to escape as the pastry rises.
Place back into the oven for 30 to 40 mins until the pastry is lightly golden.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool for at least 30 mins.
Place a plate slightly bigger than the the pan over the top and flip the tarte tatin over. Slice and serve warm with a dollop of thick cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

name: Jordon’s Ribollita
description: This vegan dish is from Tuscany, where I learned to make it. A perfect winter warmer, using Napolina ingredients it’s easy, cheap and delicious.
instructions: Dice the onion, carrot and celery. Warm a generous glug of olive oil in a large heavy pan over a medium heat. Add the diced veggies to the pan, along with a pinch of salt.
Sweat the mix down for a few mins, then add the tomato purée, bay leaves, whole rosemary sprigs, chilli flakes and ⅔ of the garlic cloves.
Cook for another few mins until fragrant. Break up the plum tomatoes into a bowl, then add to the pan along with the vegetable stock.
Using a fork, mash ½ the drained beans into a paste. Add to the pan and mix well until it becomes slightly thick. Cook for about 30 mins.
Whilst the ribollita cooks, strip the cavolo nero leaves firmly from the stalks and roughly chop them. Add the cavolo nero and your remaining drained beans to the pan and cook for a further 20 mins.
Meanwhile, cut a thick slice of ciabatta per serving and toast in a pan or under the grill. Rub the toast with the remaining garlic clove.
Once the ribollita is ready, add salt and pepper to taste.

Now the important bit - place a slice of the garlicky toast in the bottom of each bowl and pour the stew on top. Leave it for a few mins until the bread goes soft (trust me). Add a drizzle of olive oil and a sprinkle of cheese (if you like). Enjoy.

name: Jordon’s Winter Panzanella
description: This is a winter take on the classic summer salad panzanella, subbing out the tomatoes for fennel and oranges. Jordon x
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Slice the bread thickly and remove the crusts, then cut roughly into large cubes. Place into a baking tray and drizzle generously with olive oil and a large pinch of salt.
Toast the bread in the oven for about 8 mins until golden and crunchy all over, then remove and set aside.

While the bread toasts, fill a large mixing bowl about half full with cold water (add a few ice cubes if you have them. Finely slice the red onion and add to the bowl with the water. Stir and leave to sit for about 5 mins.
Meanwhile, trim and finely slice the fennel. If you have a mandolin, now is the time to use it. If not, a sharp knife will do the job nicely.
Use a knife to peel and slice the orange into rounds about 1cm thick.
Drain the onions and add the fennel and oranges to the bowl. Drain the butterbeans and add those too, then tear in the basil and roughly chop and add the parsley.
Squeeze in the juice of a lemon, a generous pinch of flaky salt and plenty of olive oil (at least 3 or 4 tbsp).
Mix really well and then taste and add more salt or lemon as needed, it should be sweet, tangy, crunchy and very fresh.

name: Juicy Braised Chicken & Cheese Crisp Quesadillas
description: Crispy, cheesy quesadillas stuffed with leftover pulled chicken from our Braised Turmeric Chicken batch. Dunk 'em in that golden dipping sauce for the ultimate bite.
instructions: Make the Turmeric Braised Chicken.

Finely slice the red onion and to a bowl with a pinch of salt and the juice of half the limes. Scrunch with your hands and set aside to lightly pickle. Pick the coriander leaves and discard the stems.

Warm the turmeric chicken in a saucepan over a low heat until hot. Spoon out some of the golden broth and set it aside in a small bowl, this is your dipping sauce. 
Use two forks to shred the chicken in the pan, then take off the heat.

Set a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Sprinkle a small handful of cheddar directly into the dry pan, roughly in a tortilla-sized circle. Once it starts to melt and bubble, press a tortilla on top. Leave for 30 seconds, then flip and toast the other side until golden and pliable. Repeat with the remaining cheese and tortillas.

Spread a dollop of soured cream over the cheese side of each tortilla. Fill with shredded chicken, then top with the pickled onion and coriander leaves. Fold in half and serve with the warm dipping broth on the side.

name: Juicy Chipotle Chicken Pasta Bake
description: Pasta bakes are a weeknight saviour when you just can't be bothered. This creamy, spicy one uses leftovers from your Juicy Pulled Chipotle Chicken batch and is packed with tomatoey goodness.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Juicy Pulled Chipotle Chicken batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 200°C.
Cook the rigatoni in a large saucepan of salted boiling water until al dente. Drain and reserve a splash of the pasta water.
Finely chop the shallot and garlic. Grate the mozzarella and cheddar. Finely chop the chives.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the shallot and a pinch of salt, then fry for 4-5 mins until soft and translucent. Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 min, then add the tomato purée and let it sizzle for a minute.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and bring to a simmer. Let it bubble for 5-7 mins until slightly thickened, then season with salt to taste.
Stir the pulled chicken through the sauce along with a splash of pasta water to loosen. Add the cooked rigatoni and mix well to coat everything in the sauce.
Tip into a small baking dish and scatter over the cheeses. Bake for 15–20 mins until golden, bubbling and crisp at the edges.
Top with chopped chives to serve.

name: Juicy Chipotle Pineapple Chicken & Rice
description: This chicken and pineapple traybake is inspired by tacos al pastor. Paired with coriander rice and a stunning array of toppings, this makes for an effortless prep-friendly dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add the chipotle and cumin to a baking tray. Grate the garlic in, season generously with salt and mix together. Toss the chicken through the marinade with a drizzle of olive oil. Arrange the chicken and bake for 15-20 mins until fully cooked.

Meanwhile, trim and slice the pineapple into 2cm chunks. Thinly slice the onion. Put the onion slices into a bowl and squeeze the juice of 1 lime over them. Season with salt and set aside to pickle. Pick half the coriander leaves and finely mince the rest. Dice the avocado into even-sized cubes.
Once the chicken is cooked, add the pineapple to the tray, switch the oven setting to grill and cook until the pineapple and chicken start to char.
Reheat the rice and stir the minced coriander and zest of half a lime through. Season with salt.

Divide the rice between Tupperware containers, then top with the chicken and pineapple, avocado, pickled onions, store-bought tomatillo salsa and remaining coriander leaves. Box up and pop in the fridge ready to grab and go (they'll keep for up to 3 days).

name: Juicy Cod, Tomatoes & Chilli Butter
description: Snuggling your fish and veg into a tight parchment parcel keeps the cod juicy while all the garlicky chilli butter goodness gets locked in. Steam, unwrap and dig in.
keywords: cod with potatoes and chilli butter
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Finely slice the shallot. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Finely chop the chilli. Grate the garlic. Chop the rosemary and drain the potatoes.

Lay out a large sheet of parchment per portion, facing portrait. Arrange the shallots, cherry tomatoes and potatoes on the bottom half of the paper leaving a 10cm gap between the food and the edge closest to you. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. If you’re scaling up for more people, just use a parchment-lined baking tray and a tight foil lid instead. Cooking times might vary, so keep an eye on it.

Pat the cod fillets dry with kitchen paper and season on both sides. Pop them on top of the veg, then spoon over the grated garlic. Dot the butter over the fish, then scatter with the chopped chilli and rosemary.
Fold the top half of the baking paper over the food then fold the outside edges over each other to seal (like a cornish pasty), creating a steam-tight parcel.
Transfer to a baking tray and bake for 18–20 mins, depending on the thickness of your cod. Serve straight from the foil.

name: Juicy Grilled Chicken & Crispy Coriander Rice
description: Juicy grilled curry-spiced chicken with a golden, crackly rice cake packed with herbs, peas and crispy onions. Proper comfort, minimal effort.
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Butterfly the chicken breasts. Add them to a bowl with the curry powder, yoghurt and the juice of half a lemon. Season well with salt and mix until coated. Lay the chicken out on a foil-lined tray and slide under the grill. Grill for 10-15 mins, turning once, until cooked through and lightly charred.
Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander, including the stalks. Tip the cooked rice into a bowl and toss through the coriander, peas and crispy onions. Season lightly with salt.

Place a frying pan with high sides over a medium heat and add a generous drizzle of olive oil, swirling to coat the base. Tip the rice mixture into the pan and press it down firmly. Dot the butter over the top, cover with a lid and cook for 5-7 mins until the butter has melted and the rice is steaming.
Remove the lid and continue cooking for another 5-10 mins until the bottom is deeply golden and crisp. Turn the heat up slightly if needed.
Place a plate over the pan and carefully invert to turn the rice out in one piece.
Serve the crispy rice with the grilled chicken, a dollop of Greek yoghurt, some lemon zest and a wedge of lemon on the side.

name: Juicy Harissa Tomato Hummus Bowl With Couscous
description: This speedy, healthy, filling bowl is a perfect mid week meal.  Feel free to use shop bought hummus to make this even quicker.
instructions: First, make the hummus. Blend the chickpeas with a clove of garlic and the chickpea water from the tin (also known as aquafaba).
Add the tahini and blend before adding the ice cubes. Blend again, then add the lemon juice, cumin and salt. Adjust the seasoning and consistency to your taste.

For the harissa tomatoes, add a good drizzle of olive oil to a pan on medium high heat. Add half of the tomatoes and stir often while they cook for about 5-8 mins. They should have broken down and have turned into a sauce. Then add the rest of the tomatoes with the za'atar and the harissa and cook for a few more minutes until they have just burst open.
Cook the couscous according to package instructions.
Toast your pine nuts in a dry pan for a couple of minutes, shaking often to make sure they don’t burn. Roughly chop some parsley.
To serve, layer the hummus with the tomatoes and couscous and top with pine nuts, parsley and a good drizzle of olive oil.

name: Juicy Pork Tacos with Zingy Jalapeño Slaw
description: Whip this up in as little as 15 minutes, using your batch-cooked Spicy Pork Ragù. It's fresh, zingy and utterly delish.
instructions: Make the Spicy Pork Ragù batch recipe.

Finely shred the cabbage and add to a bowl. Pour in a splash of jalapeño brine, a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Toss well and let it sit to soften slightly. Adjust the seasoning with more brine or salt to taste.
Warm the pork ragù in a saucepan over a low heat. If it’s on the thick side, add a splash of water to loosen it. You can gently press the pork with a spoon to shred it slightly, if you like.
Set a dry frying pan over a medium heat and warm the tortillas for 30 seconds on each side until soft and flexible.
To build the tacos, lay down some slaw, spoon over the juicy pork, then finish with a few pickled jalapeño slices and crumbled feta. Serve straight away.

name: Juicy Prawn Noodles With Coriander Pesto
description: We love jazzing up ramen noodles and this fresh and flavourful recipe – packed with herbs and juicy prawns – feels just the right amount of fancy.
keywords: Juicy Prawn Noodles With Coriander Pesto
instructions: Cook the noodles according to packet instructions.
Make the pesto by blitzing your ingredients together in a food processor. If you don’t have a food processor, a pestle and mortar will also do the job. Season well with salt and pepper.

Drain the noodles and rinse well, tipping them into a large bowl. Add the edamame or peas to the noodles. Peel the cucumber into long ribbons, stopping once you hit the seedy middle, and add the ribbons to the bowl. Throw in the pesto, toss, and taste. Add more salt and pepper, if necessary.

Toss the prawns with a tbsp of olive oil. Heat a pan over a high heat and, once the pan is really hot, add the prawns and season well. Cook for 2 mins, until browned and cooked through, then tip in with the noodles and toss well. Slice the spring onions.
Twirl the noodles into bowls, top with the extra herbs, sliced spring onions and sesame seeds. Serve with the lime, cut into wedges, and serve on the side.

name: Juicy Pulled Chipotle Chicken
description: This smoky, spicy pulled chicken is ridiculously juicy and endlessly versatile. Pile it into tacos, rice bowls or toasties for an easy midweek win.
instructions: Finely dice the onion, grate the garlic and thinly slice the peppers.

Set a large saucepan (a shallow casserole pot is best) over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the onion and peppers. Cook for 5–7 mins until softened, then add the garlic, coriander, cumin, chipotle paste and tomato purée. Cook for 2 mins until fragrant and slightly darkened.

Add the chicken thighs to the pan and pour in the chicken stock. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to the boil, over a medium heat for 25–30 mins until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened. Add a splash of water if you want it saucier, or let it reduce more if you want it thicker.
Use two forks to shred the chicken directly in the pan. Stir it all together so everything’s coated in that smoky sauce.
If prepping ahead, let it cool to room temp and then spoon into a container and chill until needed.

name: Juicy Steak Tacos
description: Tacos de carne asada, or juicy steak tacos with refried beans and all the classic toppings. This recipe uses leftover refried beans and red salsa from my other recipes. These tacos are very popular in the North of Mexico, where taquerias sell their own secret recipes with lots of different toppings. If I had to choose, they’re probably my favourite taco recipe.
instructions: Season the steak with the garlic salt and a pinch of black pepper.
To prep the toppings, dice the onion and coriander and cut ¾ of lime into wedges. Pop them in bowls or on a plate, but keep them separate. Get the spicy salsa in a bowl.
Heat the sunflower oil in a skillet set over high heat. Add the steak and fry it for 3 mins on either side (this will give you a medium steak; cook it for more or less time if you prefer).
While the steak is frying, gently heat the refried beans in a saucepan set over a medium heat until warmed through.
Mash the avocados in a bowl and season with salt and squeeze in the remaining limes (the lime juice will stop the avocado turning brown).
When the steak is cooked, remove it from the skillet and let it rest for 5-10 mins.

Wipe out the steak pan (make sure it's really dry) then set it over a medium-high heat. Add the corn tortillas, one at a time, and heat for 15-30 secs on each side. Wrap them in a tea towel to keep warm.
Place everything on the table and let everyone help themselves to build their own steak tacos!

name: Kabab Hindi (Lamb Kofta)
description: A spicy and aromatic recipe for kabab hindi (lamb kofta) from Imad Alarnab. Lamb meatballs don't get better than this.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the minced lamb with the salt, 7 spices mix and black pepper. Use your hands to make sure all ingredients are mixed well.
With a sharp knife, finely dice the white onion and add to the mixture.
Finely slice the garlic and add to the bowl. Mix together.

Meanwhile, get cracking with your musabaha sauce. In a saucepan, add the olive oil and diced onions. Sweat until the onions have a little colour. if you would like extra flavour, you can add an additional tsp of cumin seeds at this stage.
Add your 7-spice mix, black pepper, salt and tomato purée and mix well together.

Add the fresh tomatoes, and cook them for approximately 30 minutes, or until soft. Stir throughout. The tomatoes are going to naturally add water to the sauce, so stop cooking once it turns into a purée-like consistency.
Take your sauce off the heat, and tip into an oven-proof tray.
Shape the meat into balls and add to the tray with the sauce.
Cook in the oven for 35 mins at 200°C.
Serve with toasted pine nuts (optional) to add a crispiness and enjoy with the musabaha.

name: Kahlúa Espresso Martini
description: Kahlúa Espresso Martini - made with three key ingredients: Kahlúa coffee liqueur, Absolut Vodka and Lavazza Espresso. An old classic. Dangerously good.
instructions: Add all the ingredients and ice into a shaker.
Shake for 15 - 20 seconds, for that velvety foam.
Strain into a martini or cocktail glass.
Garnish with 3 coffee beans, for good luck.

name: Kale & Olive Bucatini
description: Earthy, silky, lemony pasta jewelled with black olives and covered with a cloud of parm. This kale pasta is a delight. Yum.
instructions: Finely slice the garlic, chop the olives and kale, discarding any tough stalks (these can be saved for soups and stews).
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil, drop in your pasta and cook for one min less than the pack instructs.
While the pasta is cooking, set a frying pan over a medium heat with a good glug of olive oil.
When the oil is hot add the garlic, chilli flakes and olives and allow to gently fry for a couple of mins. Turn up the heat, add the kale and a ladle of pasta water and allow the kale to wilt.
When the pasta is cooked, transfer it to the frying pan using tongs.
Grate in a good amount of Parmesan and toss well to create a glossy sauce.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice, season with salt and pepper to taste and tuck in.

name: Kale & Walnut Pesto Pasta
description: Perfect for the night before a training day or a lunch before an evening session. This pesto pasta recipe is a real breath of fresh air.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Strip the kale from the stems and add to the boiling water along with the peeled clove of garlic and cook for about 5 mins until tender.
Use a slotted spoon to remove the kale and garlic and add to a blender. Add the walnuts, juice of the lemon, 2 tbsp of olive oil and a large pinch of salt and whizz until not quite smooth.
Bring the water in the pan back to a boil, add the pasta and cook until al dente.
Drain the pasta, saving a mug of pasta water, then return to the pan along with the kale pesto.
Mix well, adding a little pasta water to get a nice creamy consistency. Plate up the pasta, top with a spoon of ricotta, a pinch of chilli flakes and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Kebabs With Aji Verde
description: Grilled zesty kebab, pickled onion, and a generous dollop of aji verde - a Peruvian green sauce made with mayo, coriander, and jalapeños. Heaven in a mouthful.
instructions: Preheat the grill to maximum.

First lightly pickle the red onion. Thinly slice and scrape into a bowl. Season with a good pinch of sea salt. Squeeze in the juice of 1 of the limes then use your hands to scrunch the onion with the lime juice - this will encourage it to soften. Leave to one side.

Tip the mince into a large bowl. Add the ground spices (ground cumin/coriander and paprika), crush in one of the garlic cloves, and season well with salt and plenty of black pepper. Shape the mince into 8 sausages, roughly in the shape of a kebab. Place on a roasting tray and drizzle over a tiny amount of olive oil if using beef or pork mince. Whack under the grill on the middle shelf for 12 minutes, turning halfway. This will mean that the kebabs crisp and cook at the same time.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. Put the mayonnaise, coriander (stalks and all), remaining garlic clove and jalapeños with 1 tbsp pickling juice into a blender or mini food processor. Blitz to a vivid green sauce, adding a splash of water if you need it and season to taste.
Cut the remaining lime into wedges. Slice the lettuce and heat the wraps if you like.
Spread most of the sauce along the middle of the wraps, top with the lettuce, grilled kebabs and pickled onions and drizzle over the remaining sauce. Serve with the lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Kedgeree
description: A breakfast classic with smoked haddock, jammy eggs, basmati rice and fragrant curry spices. Packed full of flavour and protein.
instructions: Put the eggs into a small pan filled with boiling water and cook for 7 mins. Drain and run under cold water, then peel and set aside.

Get the smoked haddock in a deep frying pan and pour over 750ml of cold water. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer gently for 5 mins. Use a slotted spoon to scoop the fish out onto a plate, then break into bite-sized pieces.

Wash the rice until the water runs clear then tip into a saucepan and measure in 500ml of the fish poaching liquid. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat to a very gentle simmer, put on a lid and cook for 10 mins until all of the liquid has been absorbed. Remove from the heat and keep the lid on while you prepare the rest.

Finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger. Put the butter into a deep frying pan over a medium-high heat and scrape in the onion, garlic and ginger and a pinch of salt. Cook gently for 8-10 mins, stirring regularly, until softened, then add the curry powder. Cook for a minute then tip in the peas, flaked fish and cooked rice. Roughly chop the coriander and thinly slice the green chilli.
Add ¾ of the coriander, the juice of the lemon and plenty of salt and pepper, then stir to combine.
Divide between 4 plates and top with the remaining coriander leaves, crispy onions and mango chutney and lime pickle on the side. Cut the eggs in half and top each plate with a half.

name: Keema Pau by Dishoom
description: Dishoom's Naveed Nasir cooks the classic Keema Pau, inspired by the Radio Cafe in Mumbai. Tender, spiced lamb mince, served with hot buttered rolls.
instructions: Grate the ginger and garlic using the finest section on your grater. Set aside.
Roughly chop your coriander, mint, 1 chilli and spring onions. Then using a hand blender, blend it all together to create a paste and set aside (this is your green paste).
In a separate pan heat a glug of oil. Chop your red onion and fry over a medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring regularly.
When the onion becomes pink in colour add your grated ginger garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes. Then add the ground coriander and cook for a further 2 minutes.
Pour in the yoghurt and simmer for 3 minutes giving it a good stir.
Now, time to add the mince. Toss your mince, salt and bay leaves together and keep stirring until browned. Then, sprinkle over your flour and give it a good stir.
Add the green paste with a splash of water, mix and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add your peas, 2 whole green chillies and leave to simmer for 15 minutes. Once this is done whack the lid on, turn off the heat and leave to sit for 10 minutes
Whilst this is cooling, lightly toast your buns and chop your other red onion ready to serve.
When the Keema is ready, split between 4 bowls and serve with a fresh wedge of lime, coriander leaves, chopped red onion, and your bread buns. Tuck in!

name: Kefir Cherry Ice Cream
description: It’s finally feeling like summer and what better way to cool down and pack in some probiotics for your gut health than with this kefir cherry ice cream.
instructions: Add most of your frozen fruit to a blender with most of the kefir and blend. Give it a stir and see if you’re happy with the texture: add more fruit if you want it thicker or more kefir if you want it runnier and creamier.

Serve immediately if you like or, for a scoopable consistency, pop the ice cream back into the freezer for at least an hour before serving. Enjoy with your favourite toppings: we used extra virgin olive oil (don’t knock it until you try it!) and cacao nibs.

name: Kefir Delight
description: This fermented kefir and yoghurt bowl with seasonal fruit and crunchy nuts and seeds is perfect for when you want something sweet but healthy too. Kefir has over ten times more microbe varieties than yoghurt, making it super beneficial for your gut microbes.
instructions: Stir the kefir and the lemon curd into the yoghurt.
Top the creamy mixture with seasonal fresh fruit, frozen raspberries and mixed nuts and seeds.

name: Keftedes with Herbed Rice, Tzatziki & Tomato Salad
description: Crispy Greek meatballs with zesty rice, creamy tzatziki and a bright tomato salad. Proper sunshine food.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until clear. Add to a pot with 450ml water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 mins. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 mins.

While the rice cooks make your keftedes. Peel and finely grate the onion. Peel and mince the garlic clove. Tear the stale bread into a bowl, soak in water for a few mins, then squeeze out the excess moisture.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the beef mince, grated onion, minced garlic, soaked bread, egg, finely chopped mint, dried oregano, salt, pepper and cumin. Add a splash of red wine or vinegar. Mix well with your hands until smooth. Chill in the fridge while you continue.
Finely chop the spring onions, mint and dill. Zest and juice the lemon. Add everything to the cooked rice, season with salt and stir well. Set aside and keep warm.

Make the Tzatziki. Grate the cucumber and squeeze out the excess liquid. Peel and mince the garlic. Finely chop the mint. In a bowl, combine the grated cucumber, yoghurt, garlic, mint, juice of the lemon and salt to taste. Stir and chill.

Now for your tomato salad. Chop the tomatoes into wedges or chunks. Pit and roughly chop the olives if needed. In a bowl, combine the tomatoes, olives and capers. Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with dried oregano and season with salt. Toss and leave to sit.
Take the meat mixture from the fridge and shape into small meatballs. Roll each one lightly in plain flour.
Heat a generous drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the keftedes in batches for 8-10 mins, turning until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve up the herbed rice with the keftedes, a big spoonful of tzatziki, and the tomato salad on the side and tuck in.

name: Kerala Egg Curry
description: This fragrant Kerala egg curry is a dish that’s guaranteed to disappear in seconds! It's ridiculously delicious, especially with a Malabar parotta or hopper for scooping up. You can replace the eggs with chicken or vegetables, but personally I don't think anything beats a perfectly soft-boiled egg in this dish.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Add the eggs and boil for 6 mins, then plunge them into a bowl full of cold water to prevent them from cooking further. Peel and set aside.
Meanwhile, finely mince or grate the green chilli. Thinly slice the onion. Chop the tomato into 2cm chunks. Finely mince the ginger. Finely mince the garlic.

Heat the coconut oil in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Once hot, drop a few curry leaves into the pan and cook until crisp. Remove using a slotted spoon to a plate lined with kitchen paper. Set aside.

Add the mustard seeds to the hot pan. Once they splutter, add the cardamom, fennel seeds, ginger, garlic, chilli, onions and remaining curry leaves with a hit of salt. Cook for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the remaining spices and cook for 1 min.
Add the tomato chunks and cook for 6-8 mins, until everything has broken down and come together into a thick paste. Add a splash of water and continue simmering for 2-3 mins.
Add the coconut milk and simmer for a couple of minutes, until the mixture is creamy and has thickened slightly. Add the eggs and baste them in the sauce for 2 mins, until hot.
Garnish with chilli oil, fried shallots, and the fried curry leaves.

name: Kerala-Inspired Prawn Curry
description: This delicious prawn curry is inspired by fragrant and aromatic Kerala flavours. Best served over fluffy rice.
instructions: Thinly slice the banana shallots. Cut the ginger into matchsticks. Mince the garlic. Thinly slice the green chilli. Finely chop the tomatoes.
Melt 2 tbsp coconut oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds and cook for 1 minute.
Add the shallots and curry leaves and cook until the shallots have softened, around 5 mins.

Add the garlic, ginger and green chillies and cook for 1 minute then add the Kashmiri chilli powder, ground turmeric and ground coriander and cook for 30 seconds. This will help prevent the spices from burning.
Wash the rice then top it up with water, and put it on in a pot on the hob with the lid on for 10 minutes until fluffy.
Add in the tomatoes, 150ml water and tamarind paste and season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine, cover and simmer over a low heat for 10 mins. You should end up with quite a thick curry.
Stir in the prawns, cover and simmer over a low heat until they’re cooked through, 3 to 5 mins.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a small frying pan. Add the mustard seeds and cook for 1 minute then add the curry leaves and cook until beginning to crisp.
Pour the mustard seeds and curry leaves over the curry, then tear over the coriander.
Serve with a generous bowl of rice.

name: Keshia's Jerk Chicken
description: This classic Jamaican dish is over four hundred years old and a beautiful representation of Caribbean culture. Once barbecued, you get incredible flavours.
instructions: Start by brining the chicken. Fill a bowl with 1 litre of boiling water and add the sugar and salt. Whisk until dissolved, then allow to cool. Once the brine liquid has cooled place the chicken pieces into the brine, cover the bowl with cling film and leave in the fridge overnight.

Whilst the chicken is brining, you can prepare the ingredients to make the jerk paste. Using a side of a spoon, peel the skin off the ginger, then roughly chop along with the scotch bonnet and spring onions. Peel the onions, the garlic cloves from their bulb and pick the thyme leaves off their stalks. To the blender add the scotch bonnet, garlic, spring onion, onion, ginger and thyme. Next, add the fresh ground spices - all spice, cinnamon, nutmeg and blend to a rough paste. Finally, squeeze in the lime juice, add the soy sauce, brown sugar, oil and a pinch of salt, then blend again until the paste comes together evenly.
Preheat your oven to 170°C/338°F.

Remove the chicken from the brine, discard the brine liquid and pat your chicken dry with paper towels. Place the chicken on a baking tray skin side up and score the skin with a knife. Rub the chicken with 8 tbsp of the jerk paste, ensuring it covers the meat and gets all inside the scores you made. Cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes. After 40 minutes, remove the foil and bake for a further 10 to allow the skin to crisp and any excess moisture to evaporate.
Once the chicken is ready, serve with coleslaw and hard dough bread.

name: Kibbeh (Spiced Bulgur & Beef Croquettes)
description: A Lebanese staple. Made with a combination of bulgar and beef, these flavourful croquettes go beautifully with a side of homemade muhammara.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
To make the filling, add the beef mince into a large bowl with the pomegranate molasses, toasted pine nuts/sunflower seeds, 7-spice and ¾ tsp of salt.
Peel the onion and grate into the meat mixture. Using your hands, thoroughly mix together. Form the mixture into 16 meatballs. Place on a baking tray line with baking paper.
Bake the meatballs until golden brown and cooked through, 8-10 mins. Then let cool down slightly whilst making the dough.
To make the dough, add the bulgur, 7-spice, cumin and coriander seeds into a large mixing bowl and season with salt. Pour over 250ml of boiling water and set aside until absorbed, 8-10 mins.
Add the beef mince into a food processor with 20g of ice cubes, pulse until a smooth paste forms. Peel the onion.
Once the bulgur has absorbed the water, use a fork to fluff up the mixture, cooling it down a little. Add the processed meat into the bulgur, grate the onion in and add ½ tsp of salt.
Knead the meat mixture until it forms a pliable dough (if it feels too stiff, work in a few drops of cold water until smooth and pliable).

Divide the dough into 16 portions. Wet your hands and wrap each cooled meatball in a portion of dough, making sure to fully encase the meatball. Smooth the dough all around and press to compact the dough. Repeat with the remaining meatballs.
Fill a medium saucepan halfway up with oil and place over medium-high heat. Once hot (around 180°C) gently drop a few kibbeh in and fry until golden brown, 4-6 mins.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked kibbeh onto a wire rack or a plate lined with kitchen paper to drain.
Serve with the Muhammara.

name: Kidney Bean Curry
description: This tomatoey kidney bean curry, with fragrant gingery spices, is a simple yet satisfying dish that makes the most of store cupboard ingredients. This recipe combines tender kidney beans with a rich tomato sauce, flavoured with aromatic spices like cumin, coriander, and ginger. The result is a hearty, comforting meal that’s both delicious and budget-friendly. Perfect for a quick weeknight dinner, this curry is packed with flavor and nutrition, thanks to the protein-rich beans and nutrient-dense tomatoes. Whether you serve it over fluffy rice or with warm naan bread, it’s a versatile dish that doesn’t skimp on taste despite its simplicity. The use of readily available ingredients means you can whip up this meal with minimal fuss, making it a go-to recipe for those days when you want something easy yet deeply satisfying
instructions: Finely chop the onions, ginger, and garlic.

Get a large saucepan over a medium heat. Pour in a good glug of neutral oil. Add the onion along with a pinch of salt. Fry, stirring regularly for 5 minutes until soft then scrape in the ginger and garlic. Cook for a minute more.

Spoon in the curry powder and the coriander, cumin and mustard seeds into the pan. Cook, stirring for a minute until smelling fragrant then tip in the chopped tomatoes and kidney beans along with their water. Season well with salt and pepper, bring the curry to the boil then turn down the heat and simmer gently for 15 minutes until thickened. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Squeeze in the lime juice and season to taste.  Reheat the rice and serve into bowls. Top with the curry and tear over some coriander. Serve with a dollop of mango chutney.

name: Kimchi & Tofu Noodle Soup
description: Inspired by kimchi-jjigae, this soup packs a maximal punch in minimal time. It’s soft, silky and so tangy from the fresh kimchi.
keywords: Kimchi and tofu noodle soup recipes
instructions: Grate the garlic and finely chop the red chillies.
Heat up a glug of vegetable oil in a pan and fry off the garlic and chilli for 30 seconds. Pour in the vegetable stock. Add in three quarters of the kimchi, ramen noodles and give it a good mix.
Very gently take out the silken tofu from its packaging and slice it into large pieces.
Once the stock has dissolved and the ramen is halfway cooked, add your tofu into the soup. Keep the soup on a gentle simmer and try not to stir it too much to avoid breaking up the tofu.
Finely chop the spring onions.
Serve the soup into bowls being careful not to break the tofu. Sprinkle with spring onions, your remaining kimchi and a drizzle of sesame oil.

name: Kimchi Baked Beans With Sesame Fried Eggs
description: Baked beans, but not as you know them. We’ve made these the best ever by enriching the sauce with flavour-packed kimchi and topping with a crispy fried egg.
keywords: Kimchi Baked Beans With Sesame Fried Eggs
instructions: Start by finely dicing your bacon, finely chopping the onion and finely slicing the garlic. Heat your oil in a large pan and fry the bacon and onion for 8 mins, until the bacon is lightly golden. Add in the garlic and cook for 1 min before adding the tomato purée. Cook out for 1 min, until darkened in colour. Next add the brown sugar, smoked paprika, and soy sauce.

Drain your beans and add them to the pan along with the passata, kimchi, and a splash of water. Cook for 5 mins until reduced and thickened, adding another splash of water if drying out. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

Heat 4 tbsp of oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Crack in your eggs and sprinkle with the sesame seeds. Cook until crisp around the edges and remove from the pan, draining on some kitchen roll.

Finely chop the spring onions. When the beans have reduced, pop some toast in the toaster or into a grill pan, cooking until golden. Serve the beans on toast topped with a sesame egg and garnished with spring onions.

name: Kimchi Cauliflower Creamy Macaroni
description: A spicy spin on two classics: Mac and Cheese, and Cauliflower Cheese. Prepare for the tastiest sauce, made by blending cauliflower with cashews and kimchi.
instructions: Cover the cashews in boiling water and set aside. Chop the cauliflower into bite-sized pieces, including the stem.

You’ll need to steam or boil all of the cauliflower. You can also microwave the florets in batches in a microwaveable bowl, covered, with a little water at the bottom. Half will be blended into the creamy sauce and half will be left whole for the bake.

Steam the cauliflower for about 10-15 mins, or until just tender. Remove half of the cauliflower and put it into a small to medium sized baking dish. Try to leave the harder stem pieces behind, so they can become the sauce rather than be eaten whole in the bake.
Leave the other half to continue cooking for another 5-7 mins, until very tender and falling apart.

When the second batch of cauliflower has finished steaming and is very soft, transfer it to a blender with the cashews, nutritional yeast, plant milk, kimchi and gochujang (if using). Blend until very smooth and season well with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, cook the macaroni al dente. Drain and pour into the baking tray with the cauliflower. Pour over the creamy sauce and mix well.
Scatter some vegan cheese, if using, over the top, and finish with a sprinkle of chilli flakes.
Bake for 5 mins uncovered under the grill on a medium heat, until golden brown.

name: Kimchi Fried Rice
description: Kimchi is king. If cooking veggie, check your kimchi to make sure it doesn’t contain shrimp. Go bold, the more potent the kimchi – the better the rice.
instructions:
Slice the pak choi, keeping the white stalks and leaves separate,
and set aside.
Get a large frying pan or wok over a high heat. Drizzle in some
sesame oil and use a fork to add the kimchi straight from the jar,
(saving the juice for later) and the white pak choi stalks. Stir-fry for 1 minute, then tip in the pouches of rice. Use the back of your
spoon to break up the rice grains and give everything a good stir.
Turn down the heat to medium.
Get a second large frying pan over a high heat and drizzle in
a good glug of sesame oil. Crack in the eggs. Once the whites
begin to set, sprinkle over the sesame seeds and chilli flakes, then
use a spoon to baste the egg whites with the sesame oil until
they begin to crisp. Turn off the heat.
Back to the rice. Turn the heat back up and then stir through a
large splash of kimchi juice and the pak choi leaves. Tear in most
of the coriander leaves. Cook for a further minute.
Divide the kimchi fried rice between four bowls. Top each portion
with a sesame and chilli fried egg and tear over the remaining
coriander leaves to serve.

name: Kimchi Mac and Cheese
description: My all-time favourite mac and cheese recipe, filled with tangy kimchi and spicy gochujang. Perfect festival food. Seema x
instructions: Roughly chop up your garlic, spring onions and kimchi. Grate the cheddar and emmental cheese.
Get a large pan of boiling salted water and cook your pasta.
Get a large pan on a medium heat and melt the butter with half the olive oil. Add in the garlic and cook for 4 mins until golden and softened. Whisk in the gochujang and cook for 1 min.
Whisk the flour into the butter and cook for 2 mins. Then slowly drizzle in half the milk whisking constantly to form a thick paste. Add the remaining milk and mix until smooth.
Add in grated cheese, honey and the cooked pasta. Mix well until combined.
Fold in the kimchi and spring onions and season to taste. You may not need any salt if your kimchi is already very salty.
Finely chop the parsley and grate 3/4 of the parmesan cheese. Combine these with the breadcrumbs in a bowl along with the rest of the oil. Preheat your oven to 200°C/180°C fan.
Spoon the mac and cheese into an oven tray and top with the breadcrumbs. Grate on the remaining parm and bake for 20 mins until the top is browned and the inside is gooey.
Allow to cool for 5 mins and enjoy.

name: Kimchi Peanut Butter Toast
description: This is my go-to breakfast for when I want something quick, filling and super tasty. Full of gut healthy kimchi, protein and fibre packed crunchy peanut butter.
instructions: Toast your bread. Finely slice the spring onion greens.
Spread the peanut butter thickly over the toast. Squeeze over the agave and a sprinkle of salt, if you like. Pile on the kimchi and finish with the sesame seeds, tahini and spring onion if using.

name: Kimchi Squash Risotto
description: A one-of-a-kind, hearty risotto that is jam-packed full of umami flavour. It's a belter, and you must try it.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C.
Peel your butternut squash and chop into 2cm cubes.
Place the squash onto a wide baking tray and season well with salt, pepper, and olive oil. Pop into the oven for 30-40 mins (you want them to be soft but still hold well).
Meanwhile, crumble your chicken stock cubes into a pot of boiling water and bring to a simmer on low heat.
Finely chop your parsley and set aside.
Now, finely mince your onion, carrot and celery.
Get a saucepan on medium heat, pour in a good glug of olive oil and add your minced veg. Season vigorously with salt and pepper then stir well and fry for 8-10 mins until softened.
Meanwhile, cut the pears into roughly 1cm cubes, discarding the core. Add your pear cubes to your saucepan once the onions in your mirepoix are starting to become translucent.
Get your arborio rice into the saucepan and stir well for a minute. Next, you’re going to want to gradually pour your wine in until the wine is absorbed. Give it another good stir.
Gradually add a ladle of stock and stir well. Continue to add the remaining stock, a ladle at a time, stirring constantly. You don’t want to take your eyes off this!

When your risotto is creamy and the rice is al dente, grate in most of your parmesan and throw in your chopped parsley. Roughly cut your kimchi into 2cm pieces and add to your risotto. Season to taste.
Blend half of your cooked squash cubes with a splash of water in a food processor or blender. Add that to your saucepan along with the remaining chunks of roasted squash, giving it another good stir.
Tightly roll your seaweed sheet and cut into small pieces.
Plate up your risotto, sprinkle with the remaining parmesan and garnish with small pieces of dried seaweed.

name: Kimchi Tuna Melt Wrap
description: Spicy tuna with gooey melted cheese inside a crispy, toasted wrap. Perfect for meal prep or a quick, satisfying lunch.
instructions: Finely slice the spring onions, roughly chop the kimchi, and finely dice the celery. Add to a medium mixing bowl along with the drained tuna, cream cheese, mayo and sriracha. Mix everything together until well combined.
Finely slice the red onion using a mandoline or sharp knife. If you prefer a milder flavour, soak it in iced water for a few minutes, then drain well. Grate the Cheddar and set aside.
Choose your base – wraps, pitas, flatbreads, or even bread all work well.
Spread a layer of the tuna mix onto your chosen base, followed by a layer of red onion. Top with grated mozzarella and Cheddar.
Toast in a non-stick pan or pop in the air fryer for 6 mins until crispy and the cheese is melted. Serve immediately.

name: Kimchi Udon Noodle Soup
description: Are you a fan of tomato soup? This noodle soup has all the flavours of that classic but tastes even better and spicier!
instructions: Start by cracking the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and whisk with a fork for around 45 seconds until the yolk and whites are combined.

Heat a small frying pan over a medium heat, add a splash of oil and swirl to cover the pan. Add half the egg mixture, swirl the pan to create a thin egg ‘pancake’, then cook for 1 min. Once cooked, flip the egg over and cook for a further 30 seconds. Set aside and repeat the process with the remaining half of the egg mixture to make another egg ‘pancake’. Set aside to cool.
Once cool, stack the two sheets of egg on top of each other and roll into a cylinder. Slice thinly into ribbons.
Slice the spring onions as finely as possible, then transfer to a bowl of cold water (add ice if you have it). Set aside.

Cut the white onion into thin strips. Stack the cabbage leaves on top of each other and slice into thin strips. Dice the tomato into big cubes. Heat a saucepan over a medium heat for around 1 min. Add a splash of oil and the tomato, onion, cabbage leaves and kimchi, then sauté for 2 mins.

Add the stock, soy sauce, sugar and a pinch of salt, then whack the heat up to high until boiling. Once the liquid is boiling, put the lid on and cook for 5 mins. After 5 mins, add the udon, gently shaking the noodles to separate them, and cook for 3 mins. Pour into bowls.
Drain the spring onion and add half on top of each bowl. Nestle the egg ribbons into the bowl. Gently place an egg yolk on top. Enjoy!

name: Kisir Style Couscous
description: A fresh little couscous salad topped with salty fried halloumi, fresh pomegranate, and herbs. The perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Boil the kettle.

Measure the couscous into a large bowl. Spoon in the paprika, tomato purée, harissa and a generous amount of salt and pepper. Pour over enough boiling water to just cover the couscous - you want it submerged by about a cm. Give everything a quick mix, cover and leave to steam.
Meanwhile, toast the nuts in a dry non-stick frying pan over a medium heat until lightly golden. Leave to cool then roughly chop along with the peppers, tomatoes and the mixed herbs.

Come back to the couscous. Use a fork to fluff up the grains then scrape in all the nuts, peppers, tomatoes and most of the mixed herbs. Zest the lemon or lime then add this and squeeze in the juice to taste. Drizzle in a couple of generous glugs of olive oil, mix everything together and season to taste.
Cut the halloumi into thick slices. Put the frying pan back onto a medium to high heat. Add the halloumi and fry for 1-2 minutes on each side until crisp and golden.
Pile the kisir into bowls or serve out of the one it is in. Top with the slices of fried halloumi, remaining herbs and pomegranate seeds. Then tuck in!

name: Kolkata Egg Roll Recipe
description: We love street-side kathi rolls, and this is one of the easiest versions of them. We've kept it simple, but go ahead and add any filling of your choice if you feel like.
instructions: Slice the pepper and cucumber into matchsticks. Finely dice the onion and thinly slice the green chillies. Crack the eggs into a bowl, season with salt and whisk well.
Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the peppers and sauté until only starting to soften. Transfer to a plate.

Leave the pan on the heat, add 1 paratha and cook until golden on both sides. Once it’s almost cooked through, pour some whisked egg on top of the paratha, enough to cover in one even layer (roughly 2 eggs per paratha). Sprinkle some green chilli and red onion over the egg, then flip so the egg cooks through. Repeat this process with the remaining three parathas.

Build your rolls by layering them up with the sautéed green pepper, cucumber, pickled onions and chaat masala. Once you’ve loaded them up, fold one edge of the paratha towards the inner side to form the bottom of the egg roll. Then, begin to roll it up tightly until you reach the end.

name: Korean BBQ Chicken Rice Box
description: Sticky gochujang chicken thighs with fluffy sushi rice, a crunchy quick carrot and cucumber pickle, with an jammy egg on top to finish. Make it ahead and future you will definitely thank you.
keywords: Korean BBQ chicken and rice meal prep
Korean BBQ chicken and rice meal prep recipe
instructions: Start by getting the rice on. Rinse the sushi rice under cold water until it runs clear, then drain. Add the rice and water to a small saucepan, bring to the boil, then cover and reduce to a low heat. Cook for 12 mins, then turn off the heat and leave covered for another 12 mins to steam.

Meanwhile, get on with the chicken. Mix the gochujang, vegetable oil, soy sauce, rice vinegar, caster sugar and sesame seeds together in a large bowl. Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces, add to the marinade with a generous pinch of salt and mix well until evenly coated.

Separate the spring onion greens from the whites. Finely slice the greens and set aside for serving. Cut the whites into roughly 2cm pieces. Place a large frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the chicken and fry for 8-9 mins, until nicely browned and the chicken is cooked through, then add the spring onion whites, stirring for a couple more minutes. Pour over any remaining sauce and reduce until sticky.

While the chicken cooks, bring a small saucepan of water to the boil. Get your eggs straight from the fridge and lower them in. Cook for 7 mins, then transfer to a bowl of cold water. Once cool, peel and set aside.
For the quick pickle, finely slice the cucumber and shave the carrots into ribbons using a peeler. Toss with the rice vinegar, caster sugar, salt and sesame oil.

Divide the rice between four containers, top with the chicken and quick pickled vegetables. Halve the eggs and place on top, then finish with the sliced spring onion greens. Box up and pop in the fridge ready to grab for lunch, it will last for up to 3 days.

name: Korean Dirty Fries
description: Mob’s ultimate dirty fries recipe: Crispy fries, melted cheese and flavourful toppings. If you’re after something indulgent that you can make really easily at home, then this homemade dirty fries recipe is just the ticket. Loaded fries are easy to make and just as delicious.
instructions: Heat the oven and cook the french fries following pack instructions.
Peel and finely chop the garlic. Thinly slice the spring onions. Roughly chop the kimchi.

Meanwhile, heat a shot of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and add in the mince. Use the back of a spoon to reak it up into small pieces. Fry for around 8 mins until the liquid has evaporated and the mince is starting to get really crisp. Turn the heat to low and scrape in the chopped garlic and half of the sesame seeds. Fry for 2 minutes until smelling amazing, then stir in half of the gochujang and remove from the heat. Season with salt and black pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise,rice vinegar and the rest of the gochujang. Add a pinch of salt and whisk again.
Turn the oven to 200°C.

Arrange the fries on a large baking tray lined with baking parchment, then scatter over the mince. Add the chopped kimchi. Sprinkle over the cheese and then the remaining sesame seeds. Put into the oven for 10-12 mins until the cheese is golden and bubbling.
Spoon over the gochujang mayo and scatter with the sliced spring onions and coriander leaves to serve.

name: Korean Hand-Torn Miso Noodle Soup
description: Known as sujebi, this traditional Korean noodle soup is a nice and spicy dinner.
keywords: Korean Hand-Torn Miso Noodle Soup recipe
instructions: To make the noodle, combine all the dough ingredients in a medium-sized mixing bowl, then use the back of a wooden spoon to bring everything together. Knead the dough for 1 min, wrap in cling film and set aside.

For the soup, slice the shiitake mushrooms, onion and garlic. Add to a large pot with miso paste, mirin, sugar, ¼ tsp salt, 1 tsp white pepper, soy sauce, fish sauce and all the water/stock. Grind or blend the toasted sesame seeds into a coarse powder and add to the pot. Set the heat to medium and bring to a simmer with a lid on, then turn the heat down to its lowest setting and cook for 10 mins.

In the meantime, peel the potato and carrot. Slice the potato into 1cm half-moons. Slice the carrot and courgette into matchsticks. Cut the spring onion whites into 2.5cm chunks and slice the green tops for garnishing. Set everything aside on a plate.

Increase the heat under the soup to medium. Arrange a small bowl of tap water next to you and fetch the dough ball. For this stage, wet your fingers and work as quickly as possible for an even cook of the noodles. Use a quick tearing motion at the edge of the dough ball to create little thin noodle blankets. The beauty of this is its irregular look – but try to keep the pieces thumb-sized and as thin as possible. Keep wetting your hands to prevent any stickage. Mix the noodles with a spatula halfway though tearing to ensure the noodles don’t stick together, and continue to tear all the remaining dough quickly, then mix everything well briefly to prevent stickage.
Add all the cut vegetables on top of the noodle broth. Mix everything well and simmer with the lid on for 5 mins.
