Turn the heat off, then add the sesame oil and kimchi brine. Ladle the soup into individual bowls and serve with kimchi, remaining spring onion tops, sesame seeds and chilli oil on top.

name: Korean Japchae Noodles with Garlicky Beef
description: This quick and delicious Korean noodle recipe is inspired by Japchae, using sweet potato noodles and sticky gochujang beef.
instructions: Soak the sweet potato noodles in warm water. Drain and set aside.

Slice the beef into 1 inch strips and set aside any large chunks of fat from the steak (you can use this later for frying). Mix all the marinade ingredients together in a large container and add the beef. Massage the marinade into the meat for 1 min then set aside in the fridge.

Bring a medium-sized pot of water to a boil. Add all the spinach and cook for 1 min, then use a sieve to remove. Leave to cool then squeeze out all the excess water with your hands. Set aside in a large mixing bowl. In the same boiling water add your eggs and cook for 5 mins (go for a little shorter if you've got smaller eggs), then remove, peel and set aside for later.

Cook the noodles in the same boiling water following pack instructions then drain and set aside in a large mixing bowl. Add a generous glug of sesame oil and toss well to prevent sticking. Cut the noodles a few times with scissors (this will make them easier to mix later).
In the meantime, finely slice the white onion, carrot, bell peppers, and shiitake mushroom into matchsticks, mince the garlic and slice the spring onions into chunks.

Heat a large pan over a high heat then add a splash of sesame oil along with any leftover pieces of beef fat (if using) and cook until lightly golden. Add the white onions and spring onions with a pinch of salt for 2 mins until lightly charred then tip into the large mixing bowl with the noodles.

Next add the bell peppers and carrots to the pan and cook for another minute, adding a splash more sesame oil if needed. Cook just until lightly charred then tip into the large mixing bowl with the noodles and other veggies.
Heat up the same pan with a splash of sesame oil. Add the mushrooms and cook for 2 mins until golden.
Add the beef and its marinade to the pan, give it a quick toss and then lay each piece of beef flat against the pan. Cook for a minute on each side then turn off the heat.
Add the beef and mushrooms to the bowl with the noodles and veggies and toss well to combine. Add the rice vinegar to the hot pan to deglaze it then scrape all the juices into the mixing bowl.

To make the noodle sauce, crush the garlic and mix all the ingredients together in a medium bowl. Then add this sauce to the large mixing bowl with the noodles, veggies and beef. Toss very well, using tongs or clean/gloved hands.
Divide between bowls and top with the sesame seeds. Serve with lettuce cups, boiled eggs and kimchi, if you like.

name: Korean Marinated Eggs (Mayak Eggs)
description: Our take on the viral drug eggs. These guys are the ultimate lunch meal prep. Super quick, super easy and so so delicious, just whack them in the fridge overnight and you've got a shortcut to a seriously satisfying lunch or dinner.
keywords: Korean Marinated Eggs aka Mayak Eggs aka Drug Eggs
Korean Marinated Eggs aka Mayak Eggs aka Drug Eggs recipe
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil over a high heat. Once boiling, gently add fridge cold eggs to the hot water and simmer for 7 mins. Remove from the water and place straight into iced water to cool. Once cool enough to handle, peel the eggs.
To make the marinade, finely mince the garlic and finely slice the spring onions and chillies. Add to a container, along with all the remaining ingredients, and whisk to incorporate.
Pop the eggs into the marinade so they are covered and place a paper towel over the top. This will make sure the marinade is evenly distributed.
Pop them in the fridge overnight, or for up to 4 days. Serve with freshly cooked rice and drizzle over the as much marinade as you like.

name: Korma Dal with Honey Halloumi
description: Creamy, gently spiced Dal topped with golden, sticky Halloumi. Perfect for scooping up on a cosy weeknight or making ahead for lunches.
keywords: tikka dal w/ sticky halloumi recipe
instructions: Rinse the red lentils under cold water until the water runs clear, then finely grate the garlic and ginger.
Heat a large saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the curry paste and fry for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for another minute.

Add the lentils, coconut milk and water. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 15 mins, or until the lentils are soft and the dal has thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Meanwhile, cut the halloumi into 2cm chunks. Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the halloumi and cook without oil until golden and charred on all sides.
Reduce the heat slightly and stir through the honey so it coats the Halloumi and turns glossy and sticky.

Roughly chop the coriander. Spoon the Dal into bowls, top with the sticky halloumi and finish with the coriander. This makes a substantial serving but if you'd like to bulk out the meal you can also serve with rice or naan.

name: Kung Pao Quorn
description: Our veggie take of the classic Chinese takeaway with juicy tender Quorn Pieces. Packed with chillies, Sichuan peppercorns and peanuts for a mouth-watering bite.
instructions: Pop the frozen Quorn Pieces in a bowl and toss with 1 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of cornflour, 1 tbsp of Shaoxing wine and a pinch of salt.
Chop the whites of the spring onions into large chunks, a similar size to the Quorn Pieces. Finely slice the green part and keep it separate. Grate the ginger and the garlic.
Remove the seeds, then cut off the stems of the dried chillies. Take out the seeds and the stems, then cut the chillies to a similar size as the Quorn Pieces.
Bash the Sichuan peppercorns in a pestle and mortar.
In a bowl, make the sauce. Mix 100ml water, 1 tbsp of Chinese black vinegar, 1 tbsp of Shaoxing wine, 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tsp of cornflour, 1 tsp of sesame oil and a pinch of sugar.
Heat up a wok with a small glug of oil and gently fry the peanuts. Remove and set aside.
Add a big glug of oil to the wok and fry the Quorn Pieces for 2 mins.

Add the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns. Keep everything continuously moving for 2 mins on high heat, then add in the ginger, garlic and white spring onions. Toss and cook for 30 secs, then add in the peanuts. Pour in the sauce and mix well, allow to cook for another min.
Transfer onto a serving plate and sprinkle with the green spring onions. Serve with rice.

name: Kyiv Butter Turkey Crown
description: A turkey crown can be the perfect fit for Christmas day – smaller than the whole bird and better for those who like the white breast meat. We’ve slathered a garlicky butter under the skin to keep the meat juicy while it cooks, and make it taste banging. If you're looking to elevate your next festive meal or special occasion, this turkey crown recipe is the perfect choice. A turkey crown, which consists of the breast meat of the turkey with the bones removed, offers a succulent and easy-to-carve alternative to a whole bird. This recipe ensures that you achieve a perfectly roasted turkey crown with tender, juicy meat and a golden, crispy skin. Ideal for holidays like Christmas or Thanksgiving, or even a hearty Sunday lunch, this dish is both impressive and manageable. The recipe includes tips for seasoning, cooking times, and how to use a meat thermometer to ensure your turkey crown is cooked to perfection.
instructions: The night before cooking the turkey, remove all the packaging, pat it dry with kitchen paper and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight – this will help the skin get super crisp. Now is also a good time to weigh the crown and calculate the cooking time (20 mins of cooking per kilo + 40 mins).

The next day, heat the oven to 170°C. Make sure your butter is at room temperature. Tip the softened butter into a bowl. Finely grate the garlic and add to the bowl, then finely chop the parsley and add this, too. Zest in the lemon, then squeeze in the juice. Season well with salt and pepper and mix well.

Starting from the neck end, use clean hands to gently prise the skin away from the breast meat, creating a large pocket that covers both breasts. Add the butter and spread to an even layer underneath the skin. Any remaining butter can be slathered over the external skin. Season the whole turkey well with salt and pepper.

Put the turkey crown into a large roasting tray, skin-side up, and roast for 30 mins. Remove from the oven and baste well with the butter. Continue basting every 30 mins until the calculated cooking time is up (see step 1) and a digital thermometer reads 65°C when pushed into the thickest part of the meat, or the juices run clear when skewered in the thickest part.
Move the crown onto a serving platter along with any butter from the tray. Cover the turkey with foil and leave to rest for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, you can make your gravy using the nice gubbins from the tray. Carve and serve.

name: Lamb & Chickpeas With Celery Apple Salad
description: Thinly sliced apple adds a nice element of sweetness and acidity to the salad in this humble batch recipe.
keywords: Lamb & Chickpeas With Celery Apple Salad
Lamb & Chickpeas With Celery Apple Salad recipe
instructions: Make the Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake.
Gently warm through your leftovers from the Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake.
Mix the tahini with the juice of the lemon and a pinch of salt. Add a little water to create a creamy, pourable texture.

Cut the apples into matchsticks and thinly slice the celery and cucumber. Pick the mint and dill leaves. Chuck it all into a large mixing bowl and pour over the tahini. Toss together and serve a big handful over the top of the chickpeas and lamb.

name: Lamb & Courgette Koftas with Green Pepper Salsa
description: Juicy spiced lamb koftas, charred under the grill and piled onto warm lemony spelt with a punchy herby green pepper salsa. High in protein and fibre-packed thanks to the spelt, it's as good for you as it is delicious.
keywords: Grilled Spiced Lamb & Courgette Koftas with Green Pepper Salsa
Grilled Spiced Lamb & Courgette Koftas with Green Pepper Salsa recipe
instructions: Cook the spelt according to the packet instructions. Once tender, drain if needed, then dress with the juice of the lemon, olive oil and a generous pinch of salt. Set aside and keep warm.

While the spelt cooks, prepare the courgette. Coarsely grate it into a clean tea towel, gather up the sides and squeeze out as much liquid as possible, this is important to stop the koftas from becoming wet and falling apart. Tip the drained courgette into a large bowl.

Add the lamb mince along with the finely grated garlic clove, cumin, coriander, chilli flakes and a generous seasoning of salt and black pepper. Mix firmly with your hands until everything is evenly combined. Roll into roughly 20 balls, slightly smaller than a golf ball. Place on a lightly oiled grill tray and set aside.

Make the salsa. Finely chop the green pepper, pickled green chillies and the remaining garlic clove and add to a bowl. Roughly chop the parsley and mint leaves and add along with 4 tbsp of olive oil and the juice of the lemon. Stir well to combine, taste and season generously with salt and black pepper. Set aside to let the flavours come together.
Heat the grill to its highest setting. Drizzle the koftas lightly with olive oil and grill for 10–12 mins, turning once halfway through, until charred in places and cooked through.
Mix into the Greek yoghurt with a drizzle of olive oil, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Spoon the spelt onto a large warmed platter. Arrange the koftas on top and spoon over the green pepper salsa generously. Serve with the Greek yoghurt and lemon cut into wedges alongside.

name: Lamb & Dauphinoise Stew
description: This lamb is ridiculously tender and features creamy dauphinoise potatoes and briney olives. It's a show-stopper.
instructions: Cut the lamb neck into 4cm chunks. Add them to a bowl along with the salt and the flour. Give it a mix so each piece is coated.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a little olive oil, then one-third of the lamb. Brown it for a couple of minutes on each side, then remove from the pan and repeat with the remaining lamb chunks. Set all the browned lamb aside.
Peel and finely dice the onion, carrot and celery. Heat a casserole dish over a medium heat with a generous glug of olive oil, then tip in the diced veg. Cook for 15 mins until soft.
Add the thyme leaves to the dish, then grate in one clove of garlic and add the tomato purée. Cook for 2 mins. Heat the oven to 160°C.

Pour in the wine and let it reduce by two-thirds. Get your lamb into the pan, along with the olives and chicken stock. Bring it up to a simmer, then pop on a lid and transfer to the oven. Cook for 2½ hrs.
Peel the potatoes, then finely slice them on a mandolin.

Pour the double cream and milk into a large saucepan, then grate in the garlic and nutmeg. Season to taste with salt and lots of black pepper. Bring to a simmer and add the potatoes. Simmer for about 15-20 mins, or until the cream has thickened and the potatoes are cooked.

Reduce the oven temperature to 180°C. Once the lamb is cooked, adjust the seasoning. Transfer it to a baking dish, then spoon the potato and cream mixture on top. Sprinkle over the gruyère, then bake in the oven for 30 mins.
To serve, finely chop the parsley and sprinkle it on top.

name: Lamb Doner Smacos with Burnt Chilli Sauce
description: Another day another smaco. This one's inspired by the ultimate late night treat lamb doner. It's packed with a fresh tomato salad and the burnt chilli sauce seriously packs a punch.
keywords: Lamb Doner Smacos with Burnt Chilli Sauce
Lamb Doner Smacos with Burnt Chilli Sauce recipe
instructions: Dice the red pepper and gently crush most of the garlic with the back of a knife. Quarter the tomato for the burnt chilli sauce. Add to a baking tray with the red chillies and grill for 8-10 mins, until charred. Tip into a food processor with the tomato purée, sugar and vinegar, then blitz and season with salt and pepper.
Mix the yoghurt with the juice of the lemon and the dried mint, then grate in the remaining garlic. Mix well and season with salt and pepper.

Mix the lamb mince with the shawarma spice, salt and pepper, then smoosh onto the tortillas. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry for 4-6 mins, or until golden and cooked through. Flip and cook for 1-2 mins more.
Quarter the remaining tomatoes and finely slice the red onion. Pick the parsley leaves. Add to a bowl and season with salt, pepper, a drizzle of olive oil and the sumac.
Top the smacos with the salad, burnt chilli sauce and yoghurt sauce, and get stuck in.

name: Lamb Kebabs On Minted Green Romesco With Radish Salad
description: Succulent – and well-spiced – lamb kebabs on a bed of minted green romesco sauce. This is a great summer recipe.
keywords: Lamb Kebabs On Minted Green Romesco With Radish Salad
instructions: Start by marinating your lamb. Crush or grate the garlic and the zest of the lemon into a bowl, along with the dried mint. Whisk in 2 tbsp of the olive oil along with a big pinch of salt. Take each of the lamb steaks and slice in half lengthways, to create two strips. Add the lamb into the bowl and toss well.
If you’re using wooden skewers, soak them in water and leave soaking until needed.

Make the green romesco. Use the open flame of the hob, or turn your grill to its highest setting. Add the green peppers, leaning them on the open flame until they start to blacken, use tongs to turn them as they char so they’re black on all sides and have collapsed, around 25 mins. Transfer to a bowl and cover with cling film or a plate. If you’re using the grill, place the peppers on a tray and slide them under the grill, turn them as they blacken on each side until they’re totally charred.

While the peppers char, make the salad. Whisk the juice of half of them lemon and remaining tbsp of olive oil with a big pinch of salt and pepper. Finely slice the radishes and add to the bowl and set aside to pickle a little.

Return to the peppers, remove the cling and taking one at a time, remove the charred skin, it should simply slide off. Open the pepper up and remove the core and seeds, then add the fleshy skin to a bender or mini chopper. Repeat with the rest of the peppers. Tip the rest of the romesco ingredients into the chopper and blitz into a smooth paste. Season generously with salt and pepper, set aside.

Take each strip of lamb and thread it onto the skewers, the trick here is to poke the skewer through the strip around 1cm from the end, then fold it back over itself to poke it through again, then repeat back over again so you’ve created an S shape. Repeat with the whole strip of lamb so you end up with the lamb woven up the skewer.

Heat a large frying pan (large enough to hold the skewers flat) over a high heat. Once searingly hot, add half of the lamb skewers. Cook for 4-5 mins on each side until charred, but still juicy and a little pink. Set aside to rest. Add the remaining lemon half, flesh-side down to the hot pan and cook for 2 mins, until its charred, remove and set aside. Take the pan off the heat.
Finish the rest of the salad by pulling the herb leaves from the stems and adding to the radishes you don’t want to chop any leaves here, toss well.

Spread the romesco across the base of a platter. Top with the charred skewers, then pile the salad into one corner. Roughly chop the reserved hazelnuts and scatter over the top. If using, sprinkle with sumac. Serve with pitas and the charred lemon half on the side for squeezing over.

name: Lamb Kleftiko
description: Roasted for over an hour with just a few simple ingredients, this lamb kleftiko recipe is great for sharing with the family. Serve it with crispy roast potatoes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Drizzle the lamb shoulder in a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Add to a tray and slide into the oven for 30 mins until starting to colour.
Meanwhile, dice the vine tomatoes into 1 cm-sized pieces.

Remove the lamb tray from the oven and add the dried bay leaves, dried oregano and diced tomatoes. Add water to cover the bottom of the tray. Cover with foil, return to the oven and cook for 2 hours further.
Serve with plenty of the juices, roast potatoes, and some chopped up fresh parsley on top.

name: Lamb Koftas With Garlic Mayo & Pitta
description: Super simple lamb koftas teamed up with lightly toasted pittas, homemade garlic mayo and fresh veggies.
instructions: Finely slice half the garlic cloves and chop the herbs. Mix all the lamb mince, dried herbs and spices, including the zest of the lemon. Mix through the parsley and half the fresh mint. Form the koftas into small oval balls. (there should be around 12 for 4 servings).
Fry in a griddle pan over a medium-high heat to get some lovely char marks, cooking on each side, about 8-10 mins in total. Once cooked, keep warm.
Place the rest of the mint, mayo, minced the remaining garlic and the juice from 1/2 the zested lemon in a bowl and mix well. Season with salt and pepper, adding more lemon juice if needed.
Thinly slice the tomatoes, red onion and iceberg lettuce. Set aside.
Lightly toast the flatbread before adding a thin layer of the garlic mayonnaise, the koftas and topping off with the veggies. Finish with some more garlic mayo. Enjoy.

name: Lamb Leg Steaks with Curry Butter Onions
description: Repeat after us: ‘Curry butter makes everything better’, especially drizzled over crispy lamb steaks and meltingly soft onions. Introducing Mob’s lamb steak recipe. Juicy, tender, and full of flavour, this easy-to-follow recipe is perfect for meat lovers.
keywords: Lamb Leg Steaks with Curry Butter Onions
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
In a small bowl, mash together the softened butter with the curry powder and some salt and pepper.
Peel the onions, then cut into quarters through the root end.

Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat and toast the whole spices for 1 minute, tossing every now and again, until they’re smelling amazing and the mustard seeds are beginning to pop. Scrape out into a small roasting tin.

Heat ½ tbsp olive oil in the frying pan and lay the onions in on one of their cut sides. Fry for 3 mins, until charred, then flip onto their other cut side and repeat for another 3 mins. Add ⅔ of the butter to the pan. Cook and baste for a minute until the butter is foaming then tip into the roasting tin. Pour in the chicken stock and spoon in the mango chutney and mix well. Cover with foil and put into the oven to roast for 25 mins.
Once the onions are nearly cooked, drizzle ½ tbsp olive oil over the lamb leg steaks, turning to coat them evenly, then season well with salt and pepper on both sides.

Put the frying pan back over a high heat. Once hot, add the lamb steaks and cook for 3 mins on one side, then flip. Cook for 2 mins on the second side then add the remaining curry butter and baste for another minute.
Move the steaks onto a plate, pour over the butter and leave to rest for 5 mins, then slice.

Spoon the onions and sauce onto a serving platter and top with the sliced lamb steaks, then spoon over any butter and resting juices. Squeeze over the lime juice and scatter with mint leaves to serve.

name: Lamb Leg Steaks with Hot Hummus, Couscous & Sumac Tomatoes
description: Spiced lamb, silky hummus and juicy sumac tomatoes come together for a total flavour bomb. All built on fluffy couscous. Big vibes. Big flavour.
keywords: Lamb Leg Steaks with Hot Hummus
instructions: Tip the couscous into a bowl with a pinch of salt. Pour over the boiling water, cover with a plate and set aside to steam while you get on with everything else.

Zest the lemon, then juice it and set both aside. Slice half the red onion as thinly as you can, then finely chop the rest. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Add to a bowl with the sliced onion, sumac, the juice of half the lemon, a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Mix and leave to pickle slightly.
Finely chop the garlic.

Rub the lamb leg steaks with the dried mint, cumin, salt, pepper and a drizzle of oil. Heat a frying pan over a high heat and sear the lamb for 3-4 mins on each side for medium-rare. Set aside to rest for a few minutes.

Drizzle a little more olive oil into a small saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the finely chopped red onion and chopped garlic. Cook for 2 mins, then add the drained chickpeas, water, the tahini, salt and pepper. Bring to the boil, then pour into a high-speed blender and blitz until smooth. Add the juice of the remaining half lemon and keep warm. Add a splash of water if needed – it should be saucy.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and stir through a drizzle of olive oil and some finely chopped parsley.

To build your bowls, spread a generous spoonful of hot hummus in the base. Add a scoop of couscous, a few slices of lamb and top with the tomato salad. Finish with more chopped parsley and a little pinch of sumac, if you fancy.

name: Lamb Massaman Curry
description: Our take on the fragrant Thai curry. Packed with melt-in-the-mouth lamb and all the spices, this comforting dish is perfect served over Tilda Jasmine Rice.
instructions: Pour your cloves, cardamom, coriander seeds and cumin seeds into a frying pan. Toast over a medium heat for a few mins until fragrant. Grind in a pestle and mortar or spice grinder.

Roughly chop your shallots, lemongrass, garlic, half your chillies and galangal. Tip into a food processor along with your toasted spices, turmeric and kaffir lime leaves. Add your coconut milk, then pulse until you have a smooth curry paste, scraping down the sides with a spatula so it all gets mixed in.
Chop your lamb into 5cm chunks.

Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large casserole pan. Tip in your curry paste along with a quarter of your coconut milk before your adding star anise and cinnamon stick. Fry over a medium high heat for 5 mins until the mixture is fragrant and taking on a golden colour.

Add your lamb chunks to the pan and stir to coat, frying for another couple of mins. Add the rest of your remaining coconut milk and chicken stock, then bring the whole thing to a boil. Simmer for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, peel your potatoes and cut into quarters. Finely chop your peanuts, roughly chop your coriander and slice your remaining red chilli.
Add the potatoes to the pan and simmer for another 45 mins.
Add your tamarind paste and brown sugar to the pan and season to taste.
Cook your Tilda Jasmine Rice according to packet instructions.
Scatter with peanuts, chopped red chilli and coriander and serve with rice.

name: Lamb Meatballs with Chipotle Butter
description: Ultra silky hummus topped with juicy and tender lamb meatballs, made even better with chipotle butter. Rich, comforting and delicious.
instructions: For the meatballs, finely grate half the garlic and peel and finely grate half of your onions (or blend them, for ease). Add both to a bowl with the ground cumin, breadcrumbs and water, then mix together. Add the lamb mince, season with the salt, then mix thoroughly until sticky. Roll all of the mixture into golf-ball-sized meatballs. Transfer to a plate, then set aside.

For the hummus, first drain the chickpeas, keeping the liquid. Add them and the remaining hummus ingredients into a blender and whizz until smooth. Adding a splash of chickpea liquid if it's too thick. Taste and season with salt, if needed. Set aside.
Peel and thinly slice the remaining red onion, place into a bowl, and season with salt. Squeeze over the lime juice. Stir together and set aside to pickle. Pick the mint leaves, discarding the stems.

Place a frying pan over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, fry the meatballs for 13-15 mins until cooked through. Add 2/3s of your chickpeas, your butter and chipotle, then let the butter melt and baste the meatballs. Cook until the chickpeas are heated through.
Spread the hummus onto plates or a sharing platter. Top with the meatballs and remaining chickpeas, then drizzle over the chipotle butter. Garnish with the pickled red onion and mint.

name: Lamb Neck Osso Buco
description: This is everything you want to eat: slow-braised saucy lamb, cheesy polenta, and a tangy, fresh salsa verde. We use bone-in lamb neck chops from the butcher’s.
instructions: Get a large saucepan or casserole over a high heat. Season the lamb neck chops generously with salt and black pepper. Drizzle some olive oil into the pan. Fry the meat for around 5 mins until evenly browned. Transfer to a plate.
Meanwhile chop the onion, carrot and celery. Once the browned meat is on a plate, scrape the veg into the pan. Turn down the heat and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft.

Finely chop four garlic cloves. Add them to the pan, cook for 1 min more then stir in the tomato purée and thyme. Pour in the white wine. Once mostly bubbled away, put the lamb back into the pan, pour in 1 litre of chicken stock and add the rind from the Parmesan. Bring to a boil then reduce the heat to low, season with salt and black pepper, put on a lid and simmer away for 2–2½ hours until the lamb is completely tender. The meat will come away from the bone.
Carefully transfer the lamb onto a plate. Turn up the heat and reduce the sauce then return the meat to the pan and keep warm. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.

Salsa verde time. Grate the remaining garlic clove into a small bowl. Finely chop the parsley and roughly chop the capers. Scrape into the bowl. Add 1 tbsp of red wine vinegar and 3 tablespoons of olive oil. Season to taste with salt and black pepper and add more vinegar if you like the sharpness.
Pour the remaining chicken stock into a large saucepan and bring to the boil. Finely grate the Parmesan cheese onto a chopping board.

Grab a whisk. Pour the polenta into the boiling stock, whisking continuously to combine. Keep whisking for a minute or so to get out any lumps as the polenta cooks and thickens. Once it is at the consistency of a loose mash, take off the heat, stir in the butter and Parmesan and let it melt. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Spoon the polenta into four bowls. Top each one with the lamb neck osso bucco then spoon over the salsa verde to serve.

name: Lamb Ragù
description: A beautiful take on the Italian ragu, this recipe is a true labour of love that brings a touch of Italian authenticity to your table. The whole dish is made completely from scratch, from the rich, deeply flavoured meat sauce to the freshly made pasta. Slow-cooked for hours, the ragu features a blend of finely ground beef, aromatic vegetables, and a robust tomato base, simmered with red wine and herbs to achieve a complex, mouthwatering taste. The sauce is carefully balanced with just the right amount of seasoning, creating a hearty and satisfying meal. Accompanied by tender, homemade pasta that perfectly absorbs the savoury sauce, this ragu is a celebration of Italian culinary tradition. Serve it with a sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and a side of crusty bread for an unforgettable dining experience. Ideal for a cosy family dinner or an impressive gathering with friends, this ragu showcases the artistry of traditional Italian cooking.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 130ºC/266ºF.
Place a large casserole pot over a high heat and add a good glug of oil. Season the lamb generously with salt and sear off the lamb shoulder until well browned, then remove from the casserole pot.
Peel and roughly chop the onion, carrot, celery and garlic. Add the vegetables and thyme sprigs to the casserole pan and cook until soft and well coloured.
Add in the tomato paste and cook for one minute. Then add the wine and reduce by half. Once reduced, add the tomatoes and stir to break them up.

Add the lamb into the pan, cover with chicken stock and bring to the boil. Place a lid on the casserole pan and cook in the oven until tender and flaking away from the bone. This will take around 4-5 hours.

When the lamb is ready, remove the casserole pan from the oven and allow to cool. Take the lamb out of the casserole dish and strain the liquid into a saucepan. Whack the saucepan onto the heat and reduce until thick.
Once the lamb is cool enough to handle, shred down the meat and fold through the thickened sauce.
Place your meat sauce (the ragu) into a frying pan and heat gently.
Get your pasta on. Once al dente, drain the pasta making sure to reserve a generous splash of the pasta water.
Toss the pasta through the ragu and add the chopped parsley. Stir through the pasta water and keep tossing to create a lovely rich sauce.
Serve up on warmed plates and grate over your parmesan cheese. Enjoy!

name: Lamb Ragù Rigatoni
description: The richest lamb ragù. The beauty of this one is that the oven does all of the work, meaning you can sit back, relax, and get some music on until it's ready.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 140°C.

Start by seasoning the lamb shoulder thoroughly with sea salt. Preheat a large casserole pot or Dutch oven on a medium-high heat and brown the entire surface of the lamb chunks in a little olive oil, this will take around 10-15 mins. In the meantime, dice the onion, carrot and celery, then peel and slice the garlic.

Remove the lamb from the pot and drain any excess fat leaving 3-4 tbsp in the pan. On a medium heat, add the garlic, chilli flakes and anchovies over a medium-high heat and cook out until the garlic just starts to brown, at this point, add the onion, carrot, celery, and fennel seeds and reduce heat to medium. Cook this out for at least 10-15 minutes until softened and lightly caramelised.

Add the wine and reduce until almost dry, then add the tomatoes, stock (or water) and bring to a simmer. Add the lamb back to the pot with the rosemary and bay leaf, place a lid on and put in the oven for around 3 hours. The lamb is done when you can pull apart with forks.
Start boiling water for your pasta and cook according to package instructions.
Remove the pot from the oven and allow it to cool a little. Skim some of the fat from the surface, pull the meat and stir through the sauce.
Add any salt and pepper if needed, and finish with a generous splash of sherry vinegar for some acidity. Toss with cooked pasta, then top with torn basil and a grating of Parmesan.

name: Lamb Shank Nihari
description: This beautiful Lamb Shank Nihari is made using a pressure cooker and a lot of love. The layers of flavour in this recipe are next level.
instructions: Start by patting the lamb shanks dry with a kitchen towel and season with salt. Sear in 1 tsp of veg oil and ghee, then put aside.
To a pan, add finely chopped onion, brown for 5 mins on high, then add ginger and garlic paste, cook for 2 mins then add everything listed under ‘for the base’, cook down for 5 mins.
Whisk yoghurt and add it, keep stirring.
Combine all the spices for the nihari masala and grind to a fine powder, save a tsp and add the rest to the pan (with the yoghurt) and keep stirring for 2 mins.
Add the lamb and the curry base (comprised of ingredients listed in the 'For The Base' section) to the pressure cooker along with 2 green chillies, ½ inch of sliced ginger, and 6 cups of water.
Bring it to the boil then pop the lid on, once the pressure is high, turn the heat down to low and cook for 18 mins.
Release the pressure and skim off the excess oil, save this for later.
Turn the heat up and let the sauce reduce for 5 mins.
Mix flour with water to create a slurry and add it to the nihari .
Simmer till the sauce has thickened and reduced by a quarter.
Serve with julienned ginger, coriander, chopped chillies and reserved oil.

name: Lamb Stew With Pearl Barley & Butternut Squash
description: A good stew always goes down a treat. This hearty lamb stew is rich with red wine and aromatics.
keywords: Lamb Stew With Pearl Barley & Butternut Squash
instructions: Cut the lamb into 3cm chunks and toss with a little olive oil. Peel and finely slice the red onion and garlic cloves. Heat a large casserole pan over a high heat, add the lamb chunks and cook for 3-5 mins, turning as they brown. Try not to move them around too much, you want to get a nice dark brown colour on each side before you turn the chunks. Remove and set aside on a plate.

Turn the heat down to medium, add a splash of olive oil and add the onions along with a big pinch of salt, sizzle for 10 mins, until softened, then add the garlic and cook for 2 mins, then add the tomato purée and spices and stir well, cook for 2 mins further.

Add the red wine and chicken stock, and simmer for 5-10 mins. Once the liquid is simmering, add your lamb back in and turn down the heat to low before covering. You'll want to cook this on a gentle simmer for 3 hours until the lamb becomes extremely tender.

Meanwhile, peel, deseed and butternut squash and cut it into 2-3 cm chunks. Once your lamb has simmered for 3 hours, add your squash chunks to the pot and cover with a lid and cook for 20 mins. Add the pearl barley and cook for another 20 mins.

Remove the lid, and add ½ the lemon juice, you might need to add more water to loosen the stew. Spoon the stew into bowls, top with a dollop of yoghurt, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Finish with a scattering of mint leaves and serve.

name: Lamb Tagine
description: This fragrant tagine is the ultimate winter warmer. It's packed with fall-apart-tender lamb, soft butternut squash, apricots, and warm spices.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Peel and cut your onions and squash into 2-3cm chunks. Quarter the tomatoes, and roughly chop half of the garlic keeping the remaining cloves whole.

Preheat an oven-proof casserole or large cast iron pot over a medium-high heat. Season your lamb with salt and pepper. Add a splash of veg oil to the pan and start the browning off the lamb. Don’t overcrowd your pan, you may want to work in batches here!

Sear all the sides until the lamb is nicely browned then set aside. Now add your onions, whole garlic cloves and squash and cook in the lamb fat for a few minutes with a pinch of salt and pepper. Add the chopped garlic, the ras el hanout and cinnamon stick. Cook for a further 2-3 mins.

Now, add in the tomato purée and cook for another couple of mins. Now chuck the lamb back into the pan along with the quartered tomatoes. Add the stock (you can use water if you don’t have stock) to cover the lamb and veggies and bring to a boil. Move the pot to the preheated oven and leave, uncovered, for 80-90 mins.
Remove the core of the preserved lemons and slice the rind into slivers. After around 45 mins, add the preserved lemons and whole dried apricots to the tagine.

After 90 mins or so the lamb should be tender and the sauce should have reduced and thickened. Skim off any excess fat if there's too much! Have a taste and season with extra salt, black pepper or a couple of extra lemons if you fancy.
Serve topped with torn mint and flaked almonds alongside steamy, herby couscous, yoghurt, and extra lemons.

name: Lao Gan Ma Roast Potatoes With Garlic & Sesame Mayo
description: Nailing the perfect roast potato can feel like a lot of pressure. But slather them in crispy chilli oil and top with spring onions and sesame seeds for spuds no one will forget.
keywords: Lao Gan Ma Roast Potatoes With Garlic & Sesame Mayo
Lao Gan Ma Roast Potatoes With Garlic & Sesame Mayo recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Peel the potatoes and cut into medium sized chunks. Add to a large pan of cold salted water and set over a high heat. Bring to a boil and then reduce to a simmer, cook for 10-15 mins until fork tender. Carefully drain and let the potatoes steam dry for 10-15 mins.

Take a large roasting tray and fill with enough vegetable oil to cover the bottom of the tray. Place in the oven for 5 mins to heat up. Cut the top off the garlic, drizzle with a little oil and wrap in tin foil.
Take the tray out of the oven and add the potatoes with the wrapped bulb of garlic. Place in the oven for 55 mins, until the potatoes are really crisp and golden.
Heat honey and lao gan ma (or other chilli oil) in a saucepan over a medium heat then add in the soy and balsamic. Gently simmer for around 5 minutes until thickened.

Add the mayo to a bowl with sesame oil, before squeezing in the roast garlic and a squeeze of lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper. Drizzle the chilli oil glaze the potatoes and garnish with sesame seeds and spring onions.

name: Lap Cheong Fried Rice
description: There are many variations of fried rice recipes his one stands out as truly elite. The addition of lap cheong (Chinese sausage) and Mama Yu’s Chilli Oil brings a depth of flavour that elevates any meal – try it and you’ll thank us later.
instructions: Mix the rice with a small amount of water to separate the grains. Dice the onion, mince the garlic and slice the spring onions (separating your whites and greens). Slice the Chinese sausage.
Add the sausage with a splash of vegetable oil to a wok set over medium-low heat and cook for 3-5 mins.
Remove the sausage from the wok and add the onion, garlic and spring onion whites with a glug of vegetable oil. Fry over a low-medium heat for a few mins until softened.

Turn the heat to medium, then add the rice, soy sauces, oyster sauce, sesame oil, sugar and white pepper. Fry for 2-3 mins over a medium-high heat. Add the frozen peas, give it a toss for 30 seconds then add the sausage. Mix well and remove from the heat.
Fry the eggs to your liking in a separate pan. Add the fried eggs to the rice and garnish with coriander, toasted sesame seeds and chilli oil.

name: Lasagne Fresca
description: We’re talking layers of homemade pasta, stacked with a refreshing mix of fennel, chilli and tomato, torn up pieces of mozz, anchovies and fresh basil leaves.
instructions: To make the pasta dough, dry blend the semolina and the flour together. Pour out onto a clean work surface and create a well in the centre. Add the eggs and, using a fork, beat the eggs together. Slowly incorporate the flour into the centre of the well until you have a thick paste. Bring the walls of flour into the paste and knead until you have a smooth, springy dough. Wrap in cling film, or cover with an upturned bowl and rest for 30 mins.

While the pasta rests, make the fillings. Tip the fennel seeds, chilli flakes and garlic into a blender with 6 tbsp of olive oil. Blend on high until the seeds are broken down. Add the tins of tomatoes and blitz until smooth. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.
Melt your butter in a medium-sized saucepan over a medium heat. Once foaming, add your flour and whisk to a paste. Cook for 2 mins.

Now, gradually pour in your milk in small increments, beating constantly to ensure that you have a smooth mixture before adding more milk. Once all the milk is added, bring the mixture to a boil and allow it to thicken. Add 15g of grated Parmesan and season to taste with salt.
Tear the mozz into chunks and pick the leaves from the basil. If the anchovies are in oil, drain them. You can chuck the oil into your tomato sauce for an extra flavour boost.

Time to roll out your pasta. Grab a pasta machine or rolling pin. If using a machine, pass one-third of the dough through the widest setting, and keep working your way down until you have landed on the second thinnest setting. You want to use a rolling pin to initially roll out the dough so it fits into the machine. Roll out your dough and cut into sheets just larger than the baking dish you will be using.

Bring a pot of water to a boil, season with salt and cook the pasta sheets 2 at a time for 30 secs-1 min. Transfer to an ice bath with a few tbsp of oil added to stop the cooking. Transfer the iced sheets to a tray and keep blanching until all the pasta is cooked.
Preheat the oven to 190°C.

Now start building your layers. Start with a thin layer of tomato sauce in the bottom of the dish, then pasta, then a layer of béchamel, then a layer of mozzarella, anchovies and basil leaves, and repeat. We want lots of thin layers here, so less is more with the fillings. Leave some of the pasta sticking out over the sides for extra crispy bits and build the lasagne very tall, it will sink once it’s cooked! You’re shooting for 24 (including sauces) layers in total. Finish with a layer of béchamel with dollops of tomato sauce on the top and sprinkle with grated parm.
Bake for 35-40 mins until bubbling and delish. Serve with a salad and the remaining parm.

name: Lasagne Mac & Cheese
description: An easy version of a lasagne or a meaty version of a mac and cheese? This mash-up of two classics is simple, comforting and, of course, delicious.
instructions: Finely dice the onion and garlic. Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat, add the beef and cook for 5 mins until caramelised and golden – you’ll need to do this in batches, otherwise the meat will just steam. Remove the beef from the pan and set it aside.

Add another glug of olive oil to the pan before tipping in the onion. Cook for 5-7 mins until golden and translucent. Add the garlic and thyme, cook for 2 more mins, then add the tomato purée. Cook for 1 min. Reduce the heat to low, return the beef to the pan and pour in the milk and beef stock. Season the ragù with black pepper, cover with a lid and simmer for 45 mins, stirring regularly.

Meanwhile, start the sauce by grating all three cheeses. Melt the butter in a large pot and add the flour, cooking for 2-3 mins or until it smells nutty. Gradually add the milk, stirring after each addition, then bring to the boil, reduce to a simmer and cook for 2 mins until thickened. Add the mustard and Parmesan, along with half of the cheddar and mozzarella, then season with salt and pepper.

Heat the grill to high. Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, add the macaroni and cook for 1 min less than pack instructions. Drain the pasta, reserving a mug of the cooking water. Mix the pasta with the ragu and a slosh of reserved water, mixing well to coat all of the pasta. Transfer to a baking dish and pour over the cheese sauce. Scatter the remaining mozzarella and cheddar on top and put under the grill for 5-10 mins until bubbling and golden.

name: Lasagne Soup
description: An incredibly easy soup, bursting with flavour. It’s the perfect way to use up the last few lasagne sheets that for some reason never make it into an actual lasagne.
instructions: Peel the garlic and trim the chillies. Put all the base ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth.

Place a saucepan over a medium heat, then add a drizzle of olive oil. Tip in the pepper mixture and cook for 3-4 mins, stirring until thicker. Pour in the stock and let it come to a boil, then turn the heat down to medium and simmer the soup for 10-15 mins.
Meanwhile, discard the stems of the cavolo nero and tear the leaves into small bite-sized chunks. Break the lasagne sheets into halves.
Squeeze the sausagemeat from the casings. Add a drizzle of olive oil to a new pan and, once hot, cook the sausagemeat (break it up using a spatula) for 5-8 mins until crispy.

Add the lasagne sheets to the soup one by one, then cook for 3 mins, stirring occasionally to separate them from each other. Stir through the cavolo nero and cook for another 3-5 mins until both the pasta and cavolo nero are tender.
Share the soup between bowls, then top with yoghurt and crispy sausagemeat.

name: Lasagne al Forno
description: This is my ‘north star’ lasagne: 7-8 layers of pasta, a rich and very meaty ragù, and a comforting blanket of white sauce. We've made our own lasagne sheets, but feel free to go with dried ones if you want to save time. This lasagne al forno is perfect for family gatherings or cozy dinners, providing a heartwarming meal that’s sure to please everyone.
instructions: First make the ragù (on the day is fine, but a day in advance is better). Put half of the olive oil in a casserole dish or a large oven-proof dish set over a medium heat. Finely dice the garlic, celery, onion, and carrots. Add the garlic, celery, onion and carrots and a large pinch of salt, stir and sauté for 10-12 minutes until softened but not coloured, stirring occasionally.

In a separate large frying pan or wok set over a high heat, first fry the lardons in the remaining oil until bronzed (6-8 minutes). Transfer to a plate, leaving the oils in the pan. Add the beef mince and fry, stirring only occasionally to try and brown the meat a little. After 6 or 7 minutes, transfer to a plate, and then fry and brown the pork mince for 6-7 minutes. Transfer all the meats and their juices to the dish holding the now-softened vegetables.

Heat the oven on to 150°C. Increase the temperature underneath the casserole dish a little, then pour in the tinned tomatoes. Fill half of one can with water and wash out both cans into the pot. Add the milk, oregano, sugar, vinegar, and season with salt and black pepper. Bring to a simmer, place a lid on top and cook in the oven for 90 minutes until intense.

On a clean surface, create a mound of flour, and then make a crater in the middle of it. Break the eggs into the crater, then use a fork to pop the yolks and beat the eggs, gradually drawing flour into the liquid. After a while, use the fork or a bench scraper to turn and chop the flour and eggs into a scraggy mix. Then use your hands to bring the mixture into a ball of dough. Knead, using the bottom of your palms to stretch and push the dough, eventually into a smooth, silky but elastic ball. It’ll take 8-10 minutes, but it’s therapeutic. Put in a sealable bag and leave to rest for 90 minutes or more (overnight in the fridge is fine).

When ready to roll, cut the dough in half, flatten it a little with your palms, then run through a pasta machine, beginning with the widest setting, ending with the pasta around 1mm thick (probably 2-3 settings from the thinnest). Dust with semolina to avoid it sticking and cut to lengths 2-3mm shorter than your lasagne dish (it will swell when blanched).

When ready to assemble, par-boil the pasta sheets. Do this in 2-3 batches (to save space and stress), the second two while you are building the lasagne. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and spread 2-3 tea towels over your kitchen surface. Cook ⅓ of the pasta sheets for 1 minute, until they rise to the top of the water. Pick them out with tongs or a slotted spoon and lay them over the tea towels. Repeat as required.

Make the white sauce. Do this by melting the butter in a medium-sized saucepan set over a moderate heat. Add the flour and stir with a spatula until the combination (a ‘roux’) is slack, light golden in colour and smells only slightly nutty (30-60 seconds). Add a splash of milk (about 60ml), and stir into the roux, again using the spatula, until the liquid is completely incorporated. Repeat 3 or 4 times, then begin to increase the amount of milk you’re adding, and use a whisk instead of a spatula, each time ensuring there are no lumps before adding more milk.

Once all the milk is in, add the grated nutmeg, white pepper, and half the Parmesan, and gently cook over a low heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and generously coats the back of a spoon.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Spoon a small ladle-worth of ragù over the base of your 1 x 2.5 litre oven-proof dish. Lay pasta sheets over the top, trimming to fit as necessary. Then add layers of ragù, dotted with white sauce, and pasta, until the dish is full, leaving enough white sauce to cover the top at the end. Quantity-wise you should have enough to create 6-7 layers of ragù, and 7-8 layers of pasta, depending on the dimensions of your dish, so judge the sauce quantities accordingly.
Cover the lasagne with Parmesan and bake for 35-40 minutes, until fully bronzed and bubbling. Leave to rest for 15 minutes, then serve.

name: Lavender Shortbread
description: These biscuits are buttery, crumbly and delicately aromatic. Bring them to a summer picnic with fresh lemonade and make your friends very happy.
instructions: Line two baking trays with baking parchment. Ensure your butter is very cold. Cut the butter into cubes. Ground the dried lavender in a pestle and mortar.

Sift the flour, sugars, salt and ground lavender together in a large bowl and mix to combine. Add the cold butter and use your fingertips and thumbs to rub the flour mix into the butter until it resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolk and vanilla and use your hands to gently bring the mixture together into a dough, being careful not to overwork it.

Using a rolling pin, roll the dough out on a floured surface to approximately 1cm thick. Use an 8cm cookie cutter (or 6cm if you prefer mini shortbreads) to cut the dough into circles. Place them on the prepared baking tray and refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours, but preferably overnight.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan.

Slide the tray into the oven and bake for approximately 12 mins, or until the edges are just starting to brown. Remove from the oven, cool on the tray for a couple of mins, then transfer to a wire rack. Dust the tops with more sugar and leave to cool completely.

name: Lazy Butter Chicken
description: Saransh came into the studio to make us an easy version of his famous butter chicken and it blew us away. The most flavourful creamy curry with a warming heat.
instructions: Dice the onions and finely slice the garlic.
In a large pan, heat half the butter and 30ml oil and add the onions and garlic. Cook until they’re light golden.
Now go in with all of the kashmiri chilli, ground coriander and salt and cook for another 2 mins.
Add the tomatoes, cashew nuts and 50ml water and bring to a boil. Cover and let it simmer for 30 mins.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth and saucy.
Gently toast kasuri methi (fenugreek leaves) in a pan for about 3 mins until fragrant.
Crush in a pestle and mortar and add to the curry base along with the cinnamon, cardamom and honey.
Add the cream and butter and shred in the leftover chicken. Cook for a further 5 mins.
Serve with rice or naan bread and garnish with another drizzle of cream and a pinch of methi.

name: Lazy Cottage Cheese & Tomato Pasta
description: Cottage cheese is the ultimate hack for a protein-packed pasta sauce. It melts down into the tomato sauce until creamy and rich, and with fresh basil and spinach stirred through it's a no-chop, fuss-free weeknight winner.
keywords: Cottage Cheese and Tomato Pasta recipe
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta according to packet instructions until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.

Meanwhile, pour the tomato sauce into a frying pan and warm over a medium heat for 2–3 mins until bubbling. Toss in the spinach and let it wilt for 1–2 mins. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.

Add the drained pasta to the pan and toss until evenly coated in the sauce, add the cottage cheese and stir until it's all combined. Add a little more pasta water to loosen if needed. Grate in most of the Parmesan and tear in most of the basil, stirring through.
Serve topped with the remaining Parmesan and basil.

name: Lazy Dumpling Laksa
description: This laksa traybake is the ultimate hands-off dinner. A silky fragrant coconut broth with juicy dumplings and greens, all baked together for a seriously satisfying midweek dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel and finely grate the garlic and ginger. Finely slice the lime leaves, discarding the tough stems.
Add the garlic, ginger, lime leaves, curry paste, coconut milk and water to a roasting tin. Whisk everything together to combine.
Tip in the spinach, edamame and dumplings. Stir gently, then cover the tin tightly with foil. Bake for 25-30 mins until the dumplings are cooked through and the broth is piping hot.
Remove from the oven, give everything a stir to mix the spinach through, then drizzle over the soy sauce and fish sauce.
Serve up with a scattering of coriander and lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Lazy Lasagne
description: We've stretched the definition of a lasagne to its breaking point in this quick and delicious recipe made with La Famiglia Rana Bolognese Tortelloni.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to boil. Preheat the grill to high.
Use the tip of a knife to poke the cherry tomatoes, this makes them burst faster.

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat, add 1 tbsp tomato puree and cook for 1 min, then add the cherry tomatoes. Cook for 5 mins, using a spoon to encourage them to burst, then season with salt and pepper. Grate or use a garlic crusher to crush in the garlic and add the oregano. Stir in a handful of the basil, then turn the heat down a little and bubble away.

Add the tortelloni to the water and cook for 2 mins, then tip into a small high sided roasting tin. Tip the tomato sauce over the top and stir well. Spoon the ricotta in big dollops over the top, then grate the parmesan over the top, slide until the grill for 2 mins until golden.
Top with fresh basil to serve.

name: Leek & Olive Filo Pie
description: A beautiful summery pie perfect for picnics and barbecues. Loaded up with herbs, fresh lemon zest and savoury feta cheese. Enjoy MOB.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C/350°F.
Finely slice your leeks. Roughly chop your mint and dill. Finely chop your olives.
Heat some olive oil in a large frying pan over a gentle heat. Tip in your leeks along with a pinch of salt and cook for 10 mins until they have totally softened.

In a large bowl, add your leeks, mint, dill and kalamata olives. Add your feta and ricotta. Zest in your lemons, then season with salt and pepper. Give it a really good mix so that you have a smooth, green-flecked mixture. Fold in the butterbeans, juice and all.
Pile the filling into a pie dish.

Working one at a time (keeping the remaining sheets covered with a tea towel) brush eahc sheet with olive oil then scrunch up lightly and place on top of the filling. Repeat with the remaining filo sheets to fully cover the pie. Sprinkle with sesame seeds, if using.
Bake until the filo is golden and the filling is piping hot, about 15 mins.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Leek & Pancetta Risotto
description: Creamy silky leeks and crispy pancetta. It is a beautiful combination in a risotto.
instructions: Place the pancetta into a pan and begin to fry on a medium heat until it becomes crispy. Remove the meat from the pan, leaving the fats.

Chop up your leeks into small discs, then add to the pan with the pancetta fat. Fry on a medium heat, allowing the leeks to soften. Once soft, add the glass of wine and stir well. Now set the them aside.

Into the same pan add half of the butter. Finely chop the onion, then place into the pan and begin to fry gently. Once the onion is translucent, add the arborio rice, making sure you stir and combine thoroughly.

Now for the stirring. Into the mixture add one third of your 1L stock, stirring as you pour. Keep stirring the risotto until the rice has absorbed all the liquid and the mixture is sticky. At this point, add another cup of stock, repeating the stirring process. This cycle is to be repeated until all the stock has been absorbed. The consistency of the risotto should now be thick and creamy. Feel free to try to risotto, to ensure the rice is al dente (if you run out of stock and its not ready, simply add some boiling hot water).

Now that the rice is cooked, add the leeks and pancetta back into the pan, combining well. Grate the parmesan and finely chop the parsley. Then add two thirds of both to the pan, along with the rest of the butter and large sprinkling of pepper. Stir well.
Time to plate up. Spoon the risotto into a serving bowl. Top with the a sprinkle of the remaining parmesan and parsley, some salt and pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Tuck in!

name: Leek & Potato Soup
description: Super simple, and super satisfying. This leek and potato soup is a classic for me. Finished with a savoury granola, it doesn't get tastier than this.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Halve and wash your leeks. Roughly chop ¾ of them.
Put the rest of your halved leeks in a tray with a pinch of salt and a drizzle of oil. Toss to coat, then roast in the oven for 20 mins.
Peel your potatoes, then chop them into large chunks. Peel and crush your garlic.
Add your potatoes to a large bowl filled with cold water.
Heat 80g of butter in a large saucepan. Add the leeks, along with half of your thyme leaves, garlic and a pinch of salt. Sweat them down for 5-10 mins.
Add in the potatoes, cover with stock and bring the mixture to a simmer. Simmer for 15 mins.
In a frying pan, add your honey with thyme, ground mixed spice, chilli flakes and a pinch of salt. Once melted, add in the oats and mixed seeds, then stir to combine.
Line a baking tray with baking paper, then pour your oat mixture onto the tray. Put the tray in the oven, and cook for 10 mins until the mixture is golden.
Once the leeks are roasted, remove them from the oven and finely chop them. Get these in a bowl.
Remove the seeds from the preserved lemons and roughly chop them. Add these into the bowl of leeks with a drizzle of olive oil, then season to taste with salt.
When the potatoes are tender, blend until smooth. Add a tablespoon of crème fraîche, and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Pour the soup into a bowl and top with the leek and lemon mix, clusters of the granola, a drizzle of oil and a little more crème fraîche. Serve and enjoy!

name: Leek & Potato Soup With Crispy Cheese Topper
description: This is the world's most comforting soup. Fact. We’ve made it even better by adding a crispy cheesy top made from the potato peelings.
keywords: Leek & Potato Soup With Crispy Cheese Topper
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Wash the potatoes thoroughly, then dry. Use a potato peeler to peel the potatoes. Put the peelings on a baking tray. Cut the potatoes into 2cm cubes.

Wash the leeks thoroughly, then cut ⅙ of the leeks into 1cm coins and put them on the tray with the potato peelings. Halve and thinly slice the remaining leeks. Peel and thinly slice the garlic cloves.

Heat the butter in a large saucepan over a medium-high heat and add the thinly sliced leeks, diced potato and sliced garlic. Strip off the thyme leaves and add a big pinch of salt, put on the lid and cook for 15 mins, stirring every now and again and until the leeks have softened.

Meanwhile, drizzle a little olive oil over the baking tray with the leeks and potato peelings and scatter over the nigella seeds and season well with salt and pepper. Put into the oven for 15 mins until crisp, then grate over the cheddar and put back into the oven for a final 5 mins.

To finish off the soup, pour in the vegetable stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 mins. Pour in the double cream and use a stick blender to whizz until completely smooth. Season with salt and lots of cracked black pepper.
Spoon the soup into bowls and top with some of the crispy cheesy potato and leek topping. Scatter with parsley leaves and drizzle with a little more cream to serve.

name: Leek & Sweet Potato Soup
description: This leek and sweet potato soup is a recipe you can make in just one tray. The buttery leeks and soft sweet potatoes are a match made in heaven.
keywords: Leek and Sweet Potato Soup recipe
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C.

Peel your sweet potatoes, chop them into small chunks then spread evenly on a pan. Finely slice your leeks and add them to a roasting tray with a bulb of garlic in the centre. Drizzle with oil and top with dots of butter, season well and cook for 25 mins, or until nice and soft. You don’t want them to catch.
Remove the sweet potato chunks and leeks from the oven and add these to large saucepan or casserole dish.

Dissolve your stock cube into the boiling water and add into the sweet potato and leek mix. Deglaze the tray you used to cook your veggies and add the liquid from that tray into your vegetable stock. Now, add in the flesh of your roasted garlic bulb and thyme. Leave it to simmer while you prepare your bread.
Cut the sourdough into thin slices and lightly toast.
Butter your toast and finely grate your cheddar over the top. Place in the oven until the cheese has melted. Set aside.
Time to blend. Take a hand blender and blend the sweet potato and leek mix until thick and smooth. Add some apple cider vinegar for a bit of acid.
To finish, ladle the soup into your bowl and season. Tuck in with a side of delicious grilled cheddar toast!

name: Leek Orzo with Chicken Stock
description: Buttery leeks & silky smooth orzo. Why didn't we pair them before?? It was always gonna work. The fennel seeds bring a lovely aniseedy note.
instructions: Finely slice the leeks and set them aside.
Heat a glug of olive oil and a knob of butter in a pan until fully melted. Then add your fennel seeds, chilli flakes and mix together.
Add your chopped leeks to the pan and toss them together with the butter until soft and wilted down.
Once soft, add your orzo and mix together.
Add your chicken stock to the pan along with the Parmesan rind. Simmer for 10 minutes stirring every minute.
Once the stock has been absorbed, grate in your parmesan and mix together with a good season of salt and pepper. Plate up and tuck in!

name: Leek and Celeriac Gratin
description: Celeriac and leeks are layered with a lush garlic sauce and baked until bubbly in this dauphinoise-inspired dish. The crisp breadcrumbs and Gruyère are crucial.
instructions: Start by prepping your vegetables. Peel your celeriac, cut it in half, and chop it into thin slices. Halve your leeks, discarding the woody ends, and slice them into thin half-moons. Grate your garlic and pick your thyme leaves off their tough stalks.

Melt your butter in a large saucepan. Add your leeks and cook over a low-medium heat for 15 minutes until they are totally soft and sweet. Pop your garlic and thyme into the pan and cook out for 1 minute.

Pour your cream and milk into the pan and season with salt and pepper to taste. Add your celeriac and simmer for 15 minutes until your cream has thickened and your celeriac is just tender. Add your nutmeg.
Whilst your mixture simmers, grate your Gruyère. Combine with your panko breadcrumbs in a bowl and set aside.
Pour your celeriac and leek mixture into a baking dish and top with your cheese and breadcrumbs. Cover with foil and bake in the oven for 20 minutes.
Remove your foil, then bake for another 20 minutes until golden and bubbly.
Serve up with some crusty bread, a roast chicken, or just on its own.

name: Leek, Pancetta & Chickpea Broth
description: Pancetta and leek are great when they're together and this comforting broth is a lovely recipe to get on the stove for a chilly day or night.
instructions: Dice the pancetta. Grab a large pot and set over a medium heat. Add a shot of oil and tip in the pancetta. Cook for 5-6 mins until crispy and the fat has rendered. Add the fennel seeds to the pan and cook for 1-2 mins. Finely slice the garlic and chilli and bung that in, too.

Wash the leeks and cut into chunky rounds. Dump those into the pot and sauté for 4-5 mins until starting to soften. Add the chickpeas, their water and the chicken stock. Bring to a simmer and let the broth bubble away for 20 mins.
Finish with chopped dill and lemon juice, then serve with warm crusty bread.

name: Leek, Tenderstem & Feta Frittata
description: A herby frittata bursting with greens, grilled feta and a kale salad topped with crispy croutons made from the homemade flatbreads you knocked together earlier.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180C. Tear the leftover flatbreads into large chunks and add them into a tray with 1 tbsp olive oil. Season with salt and bake for 10-15 mins until crispy. If you didn't save any flatbread, use any bread you have!
Finely slice the broccoli stalks, then roughly chop the florets. Trim and thinly slice the leeks.

Add 3 tbsp of olive oil into a medium sized oven-safe frying pan on a medium-high heat. Add the leeks and broccoli to the pan, season with salt and fry until softened, 4-5 mins, then add the garlic and cook for a further 1 min.

Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a bowl, and season generously with salt and pepper. Finely chop most of the parsley(stalks and all), saving a few leaves for the salad, then add the chopped herbs to the eggs and whisk until incorporated.

Remove from the pan from the heat, space the veggies out into one layer and pour the eggs over, making sure to get into every nook. Crumble the feta over and bake for 20 mins, or until a knife comes out clean.

While the frittata cooks, zest the lemon and squeeze the juice of the zested lemon into a bowl add the kale, then drizzle 3 tbsp of olive oil, season with salt, pepper. Using your hands massage/squeeze for 3-4 mins, until the kale leaves wilt and are not as tough. Set aside.

Toss your croutons into the salad and drizzle with yoghurt. Top with the reserved parsley leaves and some extra feta, if you like. Slice up the frittata and serve on plates or in meal-prep boxes with a side of salad.

name: Leek, Tenderstem & Feta Frittata
description: A herby frittata bursting with greens, grilled feta and a kale salad topped with crispy croutons made from the homemade flatbreads you knocked together earlier.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180C. Tear the leftover flatbreads into large chunks and add them into a tray with 1 tbsp olive oil. Season with salt and bake for 10-15 mins until crispy. If you didn't save any flatbread, use any bread you have! If you're short on time you can skip this step.
Finely slice the broccoli stalks, then roughly chop the florets. Trim and thinly slice the leeks.

Add 3 tbsp of olive oil into a medium sized oven-safe frying pan on a medium-high heat. Add the leeks and broccoli to the pan, season with salt and fry until softened, 4-5 mins, then add the garlic and cook for a further 1 min.

Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a bowl, and season generously with salt and pepper. Finely chop most of the parsley(stalks and all), saving a few leaves for the salad, then add the chopped herbs to the eggs and whisk until incorporated.

Remove from the pan from the heat, space the veggies out into one layer and pour the eggs over, making sure to get into every nook. Crumble the feta over and bake for 20 mins, or until a knife comes out clean.

While the frittata cooks, zest the lemon and squeeze the juice of the zested lemon into a bowl add the kale, then drizzle 3 tbsp of olive oil, season with salt, pepper. Using your hands massage/squeeze for 3-4 mins, until the kale leaves wilt and are not as tough. Set aside.

Toss your croutons into the salad and drizzle with yoghurt. Top with the reserved parsley leaves and some extra feta, if you like. Slice up the frittata and serve on plates or in meal-prep boxes with a side of salad.

name: Leek, Tulum & Caraway Börek
description: This börek recipe was created by Sertaç Dirik, head chef of Mangal 2. It's a wizard dish to make at your next dinner party.
instructions: Slice the leeks in half lengthways and rub with a little oil. Season with salt and cook, cut-side down in a large saute pan over a high heat. Cook until well charred and set aside to cool.

Thinly slice the onions and garlic. Set the same pan, back over a medium heat. Begin to sauté your onions on a low temperature with a shot of oil and plenty of salt and pepper, add your garlic and allow to brown slightly – remove from heat and add to a large mixing bowl.
Roughly chop the cooled leeks and fold through the onion mixture. Add the cheese and mix it all together. Season to taste with salt and add the lemon juice. Set aside

To make the caraway butter, toast the seeds in a pan over a gentle heat until fragrant. Add the butter and let it melt and infuse with caraway flavour. Once everything is mixed and smelling incredible, remove from heat.
Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Unroll your pastry and layer a couple together, with butter brushed in between. Spread your filling all over the pastry sheets leaving roughly 1 inch empty around the edges.

Roll your börek into a tube, and swirl in a spiral shape. Brush generously with egg yolk and bake for 20 mins. Remove from the oven and brush with caraway butter, ensuring there are seeds evenly distributed throughout.
Bake for a further 5 mins and allow to cool.
Slice and serve.

name: Leek-y Beans
description: High protein, high flavour, and low effort. These leek-y beans are a dreamy weeknight dinner.
instructions: Finely slice the leeks, discarding the tough green tops (these can be added to a stock) then tip the leeks into a large bowl and rinse well with cold water.
Add a glug of olive oil to a large frying pan over a medium high heat, add the leeks along with a big pinch of salt and sizzle, stirring often, until softened, around 10-15 mins.
Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic and roughly chop most of the parsley, saving some leaves to serve.

Add the sliced garlic and fennel seeds and cook for a min, then add the butter beans, along with the water from the cans. Add the stock cube and Dijon and bring to the boil. Bubble for 10 mins, until thickened, use a spoon to crush the beans a little to thicken it further.
Add the juice of the lemon and the chopped parsley, season with salt and pepper.
Spoon into bowls and top with a drizzle of yoghurt, toasted pumpkin seeds and parsley leaves. Finish with a big crack of black pepper.

name: Leek-y Gnocchi Traybake
description: Creamy, tangy, and packed with greens, this one-tray wonder is a weeknight hero. Roasting the leeks brings out their natural sweetness, while Dijon and crème fraîche add just the right amount of zing.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan.
Prep the veg. Trim and discard the tough outer layer of the leeks, then cut them into 3cm chunks. Halve the Tenderstem broccoli. Peel and finely slice the garlic. Grate the Parmesan and set aside.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl, mix the crème fraîche and Dijon mustard with a good pinch of salt and pepper. Set aside.
Tip the leeks into a large roasting tray, drizzle with olive oil, scatter over the fennel seeds, and season well. Toss to coat and roast for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, pour boiling water over the gnocchi in a large bowl. Leave to sit for 1 minute, then drain well.

Add the blanched gnocchi, sliced garlic, and Tenderstem to the tray. Pour over the vegetable stock, toss everything together, then sprinkle over the grated Parmesan. Return to the oven for 15–25 minutes, or until golden and tender.
Once out of the oven, stir through the crème fraîche and mustard mix until glossy and creamy. Taste and season with salt, pepper or a pinch of sugar, if neeed.
Pick and roughly chop the parsley, then scatter it over the tray before serving.

name: Leek-y Parmesan Chickpeas
description: These creamy, cheesy chickpeas go great with just about everything. Serve them with fluffy rice or flatbreads for a full-on meal. We love quick chickpea recipes.
instructions: Wash, trim, and slice the leeks in half lengthways, then cut into thin half-moons. Thinly slice the garlic.
Heat a little olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the leeks and garlic, then cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and jammy.
Stir in the Dijon mustard and chilli flakes, then cook for another minute.
Add the drained chickpeas and chicken stock, then bring to a simmer. Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens and becomes creamy.
Grate in the Parmesan and season to taste with salt, black pepper, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Serve immediately.

name: Leeky Basil Chickpeas
description: Creamy, lemony chickpeas with golden leeks, wilted greens, and a healthy amount of cottage cheese. An easy, protein-packed bowl.
instructions: Trim and finely slice the leek, discarding any tough outer layers. Wash well in a bowl of cold water to remove any grit, then drain.

Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the leek and cook for about 5 mins until soft and golden. Finely chop the garlic and stir it through. Cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant.
Tip in the chickpeas with their liquid and add the frozen edamame. Bring everything to a gentle simmer. Add the spinach a handful at a time, letting it wilt before adding more.
Tear in most of the basil, saving a few leaves for garnish. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and season well with salt and black pepper.
Spoon into bowls and top each with a dollop of cottage cheese and the remaining basil.

name: Leftover Boxing Day Green Eggs and Ham
description: Forget about your usual festive sandwiches with our no-fuss traybake. Pile in all your favourite leftovers with some bright greens and call it a day.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C / 390°F
Tear up the sourdough bread into large chunks and place in a large baking dish. Lightly pour on olive oil and roast in the oven for 15 minutes until very golden.

Turn oven down to 160°C / 320°F. Roughly chop the leek, discarding the end, and finely chop the spring onions, green chilli and garlic. Cut the Comté into cubes, shred the leftover gammon into large pieces and finely chop the parsley. If your kale or spinach leaves are large then chop those up too.

Pour a large glug of oil into a pan and add the leeks. Cook on a low heat for 5 minutes until softened - you don’t want any colour! Add the spring onions, chilli and garlic and cook for a minute until fragrant.
Throw in the kale and cook for 5 minutes until slightly wilted, then add the spinach and continue cooking for a further 5 minutes.
Sprinkle in the sumac and lightly season with salt and pepper, before mixing in the cream
Add the spinach mixture to the baking dish, nestled between the bread and top with cubes of cheese and ham. Allow some pieces of the bread to peak through.
Make wells in the mixture and crack in the British Lion eggs before covering with tin foil.
Cook for 10-15 minutes until the yolks are just set.
Spoon in dollops of cranberry sauce and sprinkle with parsley before cracking into the dish.

name: Leftover Chicken Caesar Wraps
description: Got some leftover roast chicken from your Sunday lunch? These Caesar salad wraps are a great way to use up all the tasty scraps and morsels.
instructions: Before you begin make the No Fuss Roast Chicken.

Mix the mayonnaise, Worcestershire sauce and mustard in a medium mixing bowl. Finely grate in the garlic clove and roughly half of the Parmesan. Add the zest and juice of the lemon, plenty of black pepper and mix.
Roughly chop the chicken and finely chop the anchovies. Mix these through the dressing.
Remove 4-6 large leaves from the iceberg and then roughly chop half of the remaining lettuce. Mix through the dressing along with some cubed avocado and the croutons. Grate in the remaining Parmesan.

Toast the wraps and build. Lay out two sheets of greaseproof paper and lay on your large leaves of lettuce. Nestle the flour tortillas inside and load up with your Caesar salad. Wrap the lettuce and tortillas up and around the salad. Wrap with paper, slice in half and serve.

name: Leftover Chicken Curry Pilau
description: This is a delicious recipe that can be made with any leftover chicken curry you have at home. Give it a go today.
instructions: Put the rice in a bowl and wash with several rounds of cold water, gently swirling it with your hands until the water runs somewhat clear. Once washed, cover with fresh water and leave to soak for 15 mins. Meanwhile, thinly slice the onion and set aside.

Heat the ghee or butter in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the cumin seeds, peppercorns, cloves and cardamom. After 1 min, add the onion with a pinch of salt and fry for 8-10 mins until deep brown.

Add the leftover chicken curry and stock and bring to a simmer. You will need about 500ml liquid for the rice to cook properly. The liquid you cook your rice in needs to be fairly thin, and not too rich or creamy. So only add enough stock to run the curry down to about 500-600ml. If you have a very thick curry, save some of the sauce to serve with your rice, and use stock to water the rest down to cook your rice. Season to taste.
Drain the rice and discard the water.

Add the rice to the simmering curry and increase the heat to high. Bring everything to the boil and cook for about 3 mins until the water level drops to the level of the rice. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan with a tight-fitting lid or foil and cook for 20-25 mins. Turn off the heat and rest the pilau for 5 mins before removing the lid and gently fluffing up the rice with a fork.
Chop the ginger into matchsticks. Finish the pilau with the chopped mint, coriander and ginger matchsticks. Serve immediately with any warmed-up leftover sauce from the curry.

name: Leftover Chip Shop Potato Bread
description: Stop throwing away chip shop chips and turn them into a beautiful loaf of potato bread. Served with a whipped salt and vinegar butter. An iconic makeover.
instructions: Get your chips and water in a large saucepan. Set it over a medium heat and bring the water to a simmer.
Remove the pan from the heat, add the butter and use a stick blender to blitz it into a smooth purée. Set aside to cool slightly until just warm.
