Mix together the flour and yeast in a large mixing bowl. Add the potato purée and use your hands to knead it until it comes together in a dough. Add the salt and continue to knead until smooth. Pop it back in the bowl, cover with a tea towel and leave it to prove until doubled in size (just under an hour).
While the dough proves, line a 2lb loaf tin with baking paper.

Lightly sprinkle the dough with flour and transfer it to a lightly floured surface. Use a dough scraper to push it into roughly the same shape as your loaf tin, flouring it as much as necessary if it’s sticking.
Transfer the dough to the loaf tin, cover with a tea towel and leave it to prove again until almost doubled in size (just under an hour again).
Meanwhile, heat your oven to 200°C.

Get the bread in the oven to bake for 35 mins until lightly golden and cooked through (if you have a temperature probe, it should be about 90°C in the centre). Transfer to a wire rack to cool a little.

While the bread cools, make the salt and vinegar butter. Put the room temperature butter in a mixing bowl and add the sea salt and malt vinegar. Use a whisk to whip the butter until soft and the salt and vinegar has been evenly incorporated.
Serve the bread warm with good quality butter.

name: Leftover Chocolate Hot Chocolate
description: This indulgent hot choc is the perfect way to use up leftover chocolates after Christmas.
instructions: Pour about 60% of your double cream into a mixing bowl. Use a whisk to lightly whip it until it is thickened and glossy with very soft peaks. Set aside in a cool place.
Roughly chop up your leftover chocolates.

Place the milk, icing sugar and remaining double cream in a saucepan and gently warm over a medium heat. Add in the chocolate and reduce to a low heat. Stir for a couple of minutes until the chocolate has all melted and emulsified to create your hot chocolate. It should be glossy and a similar consistency to double cream.
Pour the hot chocolate into mugs and top each with a spoon of the whipped cream.
Serve and enjoy!

name: Leftover Christmas Toastie
description: Pile your festive leftovers into some slices of fresh sourdough. It's oozing with festive flavours and will be sure to cure your Christmas hangover.
instructions: Slice the sourdough loaf into 8 even slices, grate the Comte and crumble up the stilton cheese.

Lay out 4 slices of bread. Now, this is the important bit: spread one side of every slice with ½ tbsp of mayonnaise each – the mayonnaise is the ultimate trick to a crispy and golden toastie. On the other side of the bread spread ½ tbsp of soft butter.

On the buttered side, cover your bread slices with half your cheese mix. Place on pieces of gammon and a drizzle of gravy. Finish with a final layer of cheese. Spread cranberry sauce on the buttered side of the remaining 4 slices of bread, then top your layered bread with these cranberry side down and mayo side up.

Heat 1 tbsp of butter in the base of a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add 2 of the toasties, mayonnaise side down, and fry for 3 mins, using a spatula to press them down so they become golden and crisp. Flip and cook the other side for another 3 mins.
Remove from the heat and repeat with the other 2 toasties. Slice in half and get stuck in.

name: Leftover Dal Fritters
description: Crispy fragrant fritters that will clear out all of your leftovers in one meal. Ours are topped with perfectly poached British Lion eggs for a delicious brunch.
instructions: Finely dice your red onion and finely chop the coriander and red chilli.

Add your chopped onion to a bowl along with your coriander (reserve a tbsp for garnish), flour, leftover dal, rice, and saag. Crack in a British Lion egg and add a pinch of salt, then gently stir to combine.
Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a small glug of vegetable oil. Add 2 tbsp of batter, press down with a fish slice fry for 2 mins before flipping and frying on the other side.

Boil a big pan of water and add a pinch of salt. Place a wooden spoon in the middle and stir to create a whirlpool effect before cracking a British Lion an egg into the middle. Poach for 2 mins in simmering water, then remove with a slotted spoon. Repeat with the remaining four eggs. We use British Lion eggs because have been produced to the highest standards of food safety.
Serve a stack of fritters with the poached eggs on top. Dollop on raita and mango chutney, sprinkle with coriander and enjoy.

name: Leftover Ham and Brie Folded Flatbreads
description: The naughtiest Christmas sarnie about. The sweet cranberry sauce, the oozing brie, and thick ham. It's all in the combo. So simple. So good.
instructions: Open up your flatbreads and spread 1 tbsp of chutney over each flatbread.
Add 3 slices of brie to one side, top with a slice of ham and then another layer of brie. Fold the flatbread over and repeat with the other 3.
Heat the frying pan to a medium heat and add a knob of butter. Once melted, add your flatbreads. Cook for 3 minutes on each side, until they are nice and golden and the brie is gooey and melting.
Remove your flatbreads from the heat and allow to cool for 1 minute before tucking in! Enjoy!

name: Leftover Naan Croque Madame
description: The ultimate breakfast hack to use up leftover naan from your takeaway. Topped with a perfectly runny British Lion egg yolk, you don't want to miss out on this!
keywords: how to use up extra naan bread
instructions: Finely chop the spring onions and green chilli. Grate the cheddar cheese and cut the naan into four equal pieces.

Spread the mango chutney onto two pieces of naan and sprinkle on half your cheese. Add the spring onions, green chilli and ham on top, then finish with the remaining cheese. Close the sandwich with the remaining pieces of naan.
Heat up a frying pan and melt a knob of butter.
Gently heat the sandwiches for 3 mins on either side until the cheese has melted. Take them off the heat and put them aside.
Add a big glug of oil into the frying pan and fry 4 eggs for British Lion 3 mins, until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Serve the sandwiches with the fried eggs on top and enjoy.

name: Leftover Porridge Bread
description: Stop throwing away leftover porridge oats. This low-waste porridge bread transforms your leftover breakfast into an absolutely delicious loaf. You are very, very welcome.
instructions: Combine all the ingredients except the salt in a large bowl or standing mixer. Mix to combine (if you’re doing it by hand, use a spoon as it’s sticky) until a dough starts to form. Work the dough for a minute or two then add the salt. Continue to work the dough for a few more mins.
Place the dough in an oiled bowl, cover with a damp tea towel and leave to prove for an hour until doubled in size.

Line a bread tin with baking paper. When the dough has risen, use your hands to shape the dough into a smooth shape then pop it in the lined tin. Cover with the tea towel and leave to prove again for 30 mins. Heat the oven to 190°C.
Sprinkle the dough with extra oats then bake in the oven for 35-40 mins until the bread is nice and crisp on the bottom with good colour on top. Cool on a wire rack.
Serve in chunky slices with lots of butter, if you like!

name: Leftover Pumpkin Stuffed Shells
description: Leftover pumpkin is put to use in these stuffed pasta shells. Topped with the crisp seeds to minimise waste and maximise texture, this dish is a worldie.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C/375°F.

Peel and dice up your pumpkin into 1 inch chunks, setting aside the seeds until later. Chuck on a baking tray along with your chilli and garlic, drizzle with olive oil and salt, then bake for 45 minutes until tender and caramelised.

In a separate tray, add your pumpkin seeds and toss with a splash of oil and a pinch of salt. Bake in the oven for 20 mins, tossing every so often so that they brown evenly. When cooked, they should be a deep golden colour and crisp when crunched on. Set aside until later.

Once cooked, allow your pumpkin mixture to cool down a little before popping it into a food processor. Squeeze your garlic out of it’s skin and add this to the blender too along with your red chilli. Blitz it until you have a chunky puree. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Cook your pasta shells according to packet instructions. Stuff your pumpkin mixture into the shells, then set to one side.

In a large pan over a medium heat, melt your butter. Once melted, add your sage leaves and fry for 2 minutes until crisp. Remove your sage leaves from the pan and set aside. Add your flour and mustard powder and beat into a paste - cook out for 2 minutes until the mixture smells biscuity. Gradually pour in your milk in small increments, beating until smooth before adding more. Once all your milk is added, bring your mixture to a boil before turning the heat down to a simmer for a couple of minutes, until your sauce thickens.
Add your cheddar, parmesan and nutmeg to the pan and stir to combine. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Pour your mixture into a baking dish and nestle your stuffed shells into it. Top with your mozzarella. Bake in the oven for 25-30 minutes.
Sprinkle with your crispy sage leaves and pumpkin seeds, then serve up immediately!

name: Leftover Roasted Root Soup With Stuffing Croutons
description: Make the most of your leftovers carrots, parsnips, onions, and potatoes by making a hearty soup. The stuffing croutons are so good you'll want them all year round.
keywords: Leftover Roasted Root Soup With Stuffing Croutons
Leftover Roasted Root Soup With Stuffing Croutons recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add water to the stuffing following pack instructions, then spread the stuffing in a thin layer over the base of a large, lightly greased baking tray. Rough-up with a fork and pop in the oven for 20 mins. After it’s cooked, break the stuffing up and toss in a little oil, then pop back in the oven for 20-30 mins until crispy – keep checking on it and giving it a mix, so it doesn't burn. Meanwhile, finely chop your parsley.

Set a large pot over a medium heat and add the stock. Roughly chop up the vegetables and add them to the stock, then simmer for 10 mins. Cool slightly, then blend with a stick blender until smooth. Mix through the cream. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Once the stuffing is crisp, pour the soup into bowls and top with a drizzle of cream, crispy stuffing, Parmesan and some parsley.

name: Leftover Turkey & Crispy Onion Brothy Rice
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A leftover turkey recipe that rivals a boxing day sandwich. Packed with umami and aromatics, it’s the nourishing bowl you need after Christmas or Thanksgiving.
keywords: Leftover Crispy Onion Turkey & Brothy Rice
instructions: Crush both fresh gingers (for the broth and sauce) and keep them separate. Thinly slice the spring onions and separate the whites and greens.

For the broth, use a large knife to break the turkey carcass down into smaller chunks, then add to a saucepan. Add the fresh ginger and spring onion whites and tip in the water. Season well with salt and pepper.
Set the saucepan over a medium-high heat and bring the water to a boil, then turn the heat down to low-medium and let it simmer for 40-50 mins, skimming any foam that appears.
While the broth cooks, shred the leftover turkey meat and set aside. Thinly slice the red chilli and add to a mixing bowl along with the crispy onions and spring onion greens, then set aside.
For the sauce, combine all the ingredients for the sauce in a clean saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Let the mixture come to a boil then cook for 7-10 mins until thickened and syrupy.

When the broth cooking time is up, strain the mixture through a sieve, keeping all the broth and discarding the solids. Season to taste with salt and pepper and keep it gently simmering over a low heat.

Add the shredded turkey to the broth for 5-10 mins or until thoroughly reheated, then fish out the meat with a sieve and toss it in the mixing bowl with the crispy onions, red chilli and spring onions. Meanwhile, reheat the cooked rice.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls and ladle over the broth. Top with the turkey mixture and finish with a drizzle of the sweet soy sauce.

name: Leftover Turkey Baguette
description: Too much Christmas turkey? Here's the freshest way to make use of your leftovers and spice them up with a crunchy slaw and delicious sriracha mayo.
instructions: Get your leftover turkey into a large bowl. Add your lemongrass and ginger paste. Grate your garlic and add it to the turkey with your honey, fish sauce and 1 tbsp of vegetable oil. Give it a big mix and set aside.
To make the sriracha mayo, simply and the mayo and sriracha to a bowl and mix. Set aside.

Peel your carrots. Finely slice your carrots and cucumber into thin batons. Finely slice your radishes in thin circles. Finely chop your chilli and add all the vegetables to a large bowl. Chop a handful of coriander, leaving a handful for later, and add to the salad. Season with the vinegar and a pinch of salt. Toss the salad to combine and set aside.
Turkey time. Add a splash of vegetable oil to a large pan or wok and fry for 5 minutes until nice and crispy.

Slice your baguettes open and spread 2 tbsp of pâté on one side of each baguette. Load up each baguette with turkey, salad, sriracha mayo and a couple of sprigs of coriander. Close the Bánh Mì, slice in half and dig in! Enjoy!

name: Leftover Turkey Madras Curry
description: This is the perfect leftovers recipe: turkey curry. It’s between Christmas and New Year and you’re sick of eating boring food and also have an abundance of turkey… so in steps the turkey madras. Comforting with a real vicious kick.
instructions: Spoon the coriander, cumin and fennel seeds into a small frying pan along with the black peppercorns and dried chillies, if using. Put over a medium heat and toast for 1-2 mins until they smell amazing. Pour into a spice grinder and whizz until powdered. If not using dried chillies, mix the chilli powder in now.
Finely chop the onion, peel the ginger and garlic cloves, then cut the chillies in half lengthways.

Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan over a medium-high heat and scrape in the onion along with a big pinch of salt. Cook for 10 mins, stirring every now and again, until softened and beginning to caramelise.

Use a fine grater to grate in the garlic and ginger, then cook for 1 min. Add in the ground spice mix, chopped tomatoes, coconut milk and the halved bird’s-eye chillies. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer gently for 30 mins until the sauce is thick and luscious. Stir once or twice during cooking. At this stage you can use a stick blender to whizz until smooth, if you like.
Meanwhile, cut or tear the cooked turkey into bite-sized pieces.
Add the turkey to the curry and simmer for 5 mins to fully reheat the meat – you may need to add a splash of water if it’s too thick.
Season with salt and pepper. Cut the lemon in half and season with a little of its juice.
Serve scattered with coriander leaves and with rice and naan.

name: Leftover Turkey Pillow Pie
description: Turkey, leek and tarragon. Name a more iconic trio. Such a good way to use up the leftovers and so, so cheap. Get on it MOB and impress the family.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Finely slice the bacon and add to a large frying pan. Fry until beginning to get crispy.
Add finely sliced leeks to the pan with a tbsp of olive oil. Fry leeks on a medium heat until soft.
Once soft, add your leftover turkey meat and stir it in. Add a large handful of chopped tarragon. Mix again.
Add plain flour. Stir it into the mixture until it has all absorbed.
Start adding your milk, bit by bit, mixing as you go. After pouring in the full pint of milk, you should have a delicious thick pie filling.
Double cream time. Pour in double cream to make it extra creamy. Season very generously with lots of pepper and a good pinch of salt. Mix everything together.
Your filling should be very thick. If it is too loose, keep it on the heat until enough moisture has evaporated and the filling has thickened up.
Pie time. Lay out a sheet of baking paper on a baking tray. Roll out your first sheet of puff pastry and place it on the baking paper.
Separate the egg yolks from the whites (you can freeze the whites for later). Add the yolks to a small bowl and beat together - this is your egg wash.

Spoon in your filling, keeping a 2cm border free around the edge. Smooth the filling out with a spoon. Brush some of the egg wash around the border and place the second pastry sheet on top (roll it out to make sure it fits with enough overlap).
Press the 2 sheets of pastry together around the edge. Cut off any loose bits. Go around the edges with a fork, pressing it down to create a seal.
With a knife, run diagonal lines across the top of the pie to create a lattice effect. Brush it all over with remaining egg wash. Sprinkle on some sea salt.
Place the pie in the oven for 35 minutes or until the pastry is golden.
Remove from the oven, slice it up and serve with a big dollop of mustard. Enjoy.

name: Leftover Turkey Risotto
description: Porcini mushrooms bringing the depth in this creamy risotto. The perfect way to use up those Thanksgiving or Christmas leftovers.
instructions: Put your porcini mushrooms in a bowl and add 500ml of boiling water. Leave them to re-hydrate. Whilst they do, you have time to make your stock.
Into a pan add a knob of butter, olive oil and diced onion. Fry onion until soft and add crushed garlic cloves. Mix it in and pour in your risotto rice.

Start adding stock and give it a good stir on a medium heat. Add another 2 spoonfuls and stir thoroughly. Repeat this process gradually as the rice continues to soak up the stock until you have run out of stock. If the rice isn’t cooked through, just keep adding water or vegetable stock until it is.
Add your grated Parmesan and leftover turkey. Mix it in.
In a separate pan fry your sliced chestnut mushrooms until brown.
Once cooked add them to your risotto, along with your porcini mushrooms, a large handful of chopped parsley, a knob of butter, salt and pepper and tuck in with your MOB. #makethemostofyourleftovers

name: Leftover Turkey and Halloumi Gyros
description: Simply adding garlic, chilli and oregano to your leftover turkey transforms it. Make sure you fry it on a high heat for that charring.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.

Add the turkey to a large mixing bowl. Add 3 tbsp of yoghurt, 2 tbsp of oregano and your chilli flakes. Crush or grate your garlic and add it to the bowl. Season with a few grinds of pepper and mix together until the turkey is fully coated in the yoghurt mixture. Cover the bowl and leave the turkey to marinate in the fridge for 15 minutes.

Tzatziki time. Pour the remaining yoghurt into a bowl. Grate your cucumber and squeeze the liquid out of the gratings with your hands before adding to the yoghurt. Finely chop your mint and add a handful into the bowl, saving a handful for later. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, squeeze in the lemon juice and mix it all together. Set aside for later.
Heat a frying pan to a medium to high heat and drizzle with olive oil. Add your turkey and fry for 6 minutes until heated through and slightly crispy. Remove from the pan and set aside for serving.

Slice your halloumi into 8 pieces and add it to the pan with a splash of olive oil. Add a pinch of the remaining oregano and a few grinds of pepper to each of the halloumi slices. Cook for 2 minutes on each side or until golden brown.
Add the flatbreads to a baking tray and splash a couple of drops of water on top. Place in the oven for 3 minutes or until nice and toasted.

Serving time. Add a big dollop of tzatziki to your flatbreads, followed by some turkey, halloumi and more tzatziki. Add a scattering of chopped mint and a final drizzle of olive oil. Tuck in and enjoy.

name: Leftover Vegetable Flammkuchen
description: Pile up your leftover veggies onto this simple, crispy German flatbread topped with delicious Ocado smoked streaky bacon. A perfect weekday meal.
instructions: Combine the flour, 150ml water, ½ tsp salt and 2 tbsp of olive oil in a large mixing bowl. Mix to form a dough and knead for 3-5 mins until it's smooth and elastic. Cover and allow to rest whilst you prepare the rest of the ingredients.
Slice up your onions and chop the peppers into large chunks. Chop up the bacon into small cubes.

Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add your bacon and fry until mostly cooked. Add in the onions and peppers and cook for 5 mins until translucent and softened. Grate in the garlic, add in the spinach, and cook for a further minute or so until the spinach has wilted.
Combine the crème fraîche and nutmeg in a small bowl and season with salt.
Preheat the oven to 200°C/390°F.
Roll out the dough as thinly as you can (roughly the thickness of a pound coin) and place it on a lined baking tray. Fold the corners to make a crust and spread on the crème fraîche.
Sprinkle on your onion topping and leftover spinach and bake in the oven for 20-25 mins until the crust is golden.
Slice it up and eat immediately.

name: Leftovers Chicken Stock
description: A rich and flavourful chicken stock. The perfect way to end your week and clear your fridge of any odds and ends.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Cut the garlic bulb and onions in half. Pop those alliums onto a tray with the chicken carcass and give it all a good drizzle of olive oil.
Roast this in the oven for 30 mins or until the bones are deeply golden.
Put the roasted bones and veg into a large stockpot. Cover with water (the quantity doesn't matter you just need to cover everything) and add in any veg scraps you have lying around.
Bring to a simmer and cook for a minimum of 2 hours and up to 10 hours. Top up the water if it's looking low.
Strain the stock and season very liberally with salt. You will need a good fistful of salt.
Store the stock in an air-tight container in your fridge for 3-4 days or, conversely, portion it up and pop it in the freezer

name: Lemon & Garlic Kebab Bowl
description: A simple, summery lunch that's built for meal prep. Herby turkey mince pressed into a tray, grilled until charred, then served with a lemon-dressed tomato and cucumber salad and a good dollop of hummus.
keywords: Lemon & Garlic Turkey Kebab Bowl recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely chop the dill and grate the garlic. Peel and finely slice the red onion. Add the turkey mince to a large bowl with the dill, garlic and half the sliced onion. Grate in the lemon zest, season generously with salt and black pepper and mix well to combine.

Transfer the mix to a baking tray (approximately 24x32cm) and press down into the edges. Score into 8 long strips, this makes it easier to portion later. Drizzle with a third of the olive oil and bake for 15 mins. If there's a lot of liquid in the tray, pour it away. Crank the grill to high and slide the tray back under for 3-5 mins, until the kebabs are charred on top.

While the kebabs are in the oven, cut the tomatoes and cucumber into irregular pieces and add to a bowl with the remaining sliced onion. Squeeze over the juice of the lemon, drizzle with the remaining olive oil, season with salt and black pepper and toss together.

Divide the salad between containers and once the kebabs are cooked and have cooled, slice up and nestle in with the salad along with the hummus and flatbreads, if using. Box up and pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Lemon & Garlic Kebab Bowl
description: A simple, summery bowl that's built for meal prep. Herby turkey mince pressed into a tray, grilled until charred, then served with a lemon-dressed tomato and cucumber salad and a good dollop of hummus.
keywords: Lemon & Garlic Turkey Kebab Bowl recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely chop the dill and grate the garlic. Peel and finely dice the red onion. Add the turkey mince to a large bowl with the dill, garlic and the diced onion. Grate in the lemon zest, cumin and paprika, season generously with salt and black pepper and mix well to combine.

Transfer the mix to a baking tray (approximately 24x32cm) and press down into the edges. Score into 8 long strips, this makes it easier to portion later. Drizzle with a third of the olive oil and bake for 15 mins. If there's a lot of liquid in the tray, pour it away. Crank the grill to high and slide the tray back under for 3-5 mins, until the kebabs are charred on top.

While the kebabs are in the oven, cut the tomatoes and cucumber into irregular pieces and slice the remaining half of red onion. Add into a bowl altogether, squeeze over the juice of the lemon, drizzle with the remaining olive oil, season with salt and black pepper and toss together.
Once the kebabs are cooked, slice up and serve alongside the salad, hummus and flatbreads, if using.

name: Lemon & Poppy Seed Sunshine Pots
description: Start your day off right with these easy no-cook lemon and poppy seed yoghurt pots. They're healthy, high in protein, and perfect for busy weekday mornings.
keywords: Lemon & Poppy Seed Sunshine Pots recipe
instructions: In a small bowl, stir together the lemon curd, turmeric, cinnamon, and cardamom.
Zest the lemon and then, in a separate bowl, mix the lemon zest and poppy seeds into the Greek yoghurt.
Gently swirl the spiced lemon curd through the yoghurt, being careful not to fully mix – you want a marbled effect.
Divide the mixture between jars or containers, cover, and refrigerate until needed.

name: Lemon Basil Ice Cream
description: Here’s the trick to beautiful, fuss-free ice cream that only takes a few minutes to make. The lemon basil flavour is super fresh and summery.
instructions: Pick the basil leaves and roughly chop.
In a small pan, combine the sugar, water, chopped basil leaves and heat gently until lightly simmering. When the sugar has melted turn off the heat and leave to steep and cool.
Cut ⅓ of the top of your lemons and scoop out the flesh to make your lemon bowls. Save the flesh and put the skins into the freezer.
In a sieve, push the lemon flesh through a sieve to get the juice.
Once the basil simple syrup is cooled, pour the cream into a large mixing bowl and whisk until soft peaks (careful not to over whisk here otherwise your cream will split!)
Once you have soft peaks, slowly whisk in the condensed milk until combined, then the basil simple syrup until combined, and lastly the lemon juice.
Spoon the mixture into a loaf tin, cover and freeze for 6-8 hours or until set.

Once set, serve up your ice cream in the frozen lemon cups or bowls with a garnish of lemon zest. If you're dead-set on everyone having a lemon cup, simply scoop out the flesh of 6 extra lemons (preserving the flesh for later) and freeze the halves along with the other lemons. Otherwise, use bowls and enjoy!

name: Lemon Cheesecake Bliss Balls
description: If cheesecake and energy balls had a baby, it’d be these. Packed with lemon zest and coconut, they’re tangy, chewy and the ultimate keto-friendly sweet snack.
instructions: Chuck the almond flour, coconut, almond butter, coconut oil, maple syrup, vanilla extract and salt into a food processor. Blitz until it all comes together in a soft, sticky dough.
Add the lemon juice and zest, then pulse a few times just to mix through.
Scoop out the dough and roll into balls using your hands. You should get around 12.
Break the chocolate into pieces then melt in the microwave in 30 second bursts or in a bain marie. Drizzle over the lemon bliss balls, add a little extra zest to finish if you fancy.
Pop them in the fridge to chill for 1 hour until set. Ready to go!
To store, transfer the bliss balls to a Tupperware lined with baking paper. If stacking, add another sheet between layers. Keep in the fridge for up to a week or freeze for up to 3 months.

name: Lemon Chicken
description: Crispy fried chicken coated in a sticky, tangy and slightly sweet lemon sauce. Fakeaways at their best.
instructions: Chop up the chicken into large chunks and separate the whites and yolks of your eggs into separate bowls.
Coat the chicken in the juice of half a lemon, ½ tsp white pepper powder, ½ tsp sugar, 1 tbsp soy sauce and two egg whites. Mix well and allow it to marinate for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the remaining half of your lemon, and mince the onion, garlic and ginger. Following that, zest and juice two additional lemons into a bowl.
Combine the chicken stock, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and ½ tsp white pepper powder in a jug.
Heat up a pan with 5cm of vegetable oil to deep fry the chicken
Pour 200g of plain flour into a bowl and tip in your chicken along with its marinating liquid. Mix it well with your hands, scrunching up the chicken so that there are lots of craggy bits.
In a small cup, combine the cornflour with 1 tbsp water.
Deep fry each piece of chicken in batches for 3-4 mins until golden brown, set aside to drain on a paper towel.
Heat up a large wok until smoking and pour a large glug of oil around the outside of the wok. Stir fry the onion, ginger and garlic for 1 min until golden brown.
Pour in the chicken stock mixture and bring the sauce to a bubble.
Add the cornflour mix and whisk to combine. Simmer the sauce for 2 mins until it is thick and glossy
Toss in the chicken and lemon juice and mix well. Cook for 30 secs and serve on a bed of steamed rice. Top with toasted sesame seeds, lemon slices and enjoy.

name: Lemon Chicken & Orzo Soup
description: This light yet comforting chicken soup is full of zesty lemon, fresh dill, and hearty orzo. Perfect for using up leftover chicken and guaranteed to lift your mood on a chilly day.
keywords: lemon and dill chicken orzo soup
instructions: Dice the carrot, onion, and celery to create a veg base mix. Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over a medium heat. Add the veg base mix and cook until softened but not coloured, about 5 mins.
Peel and crush the garlic, then stir it through the veg for 1 min until fragrant. Pour in the chicken bone broth and bring everything to the boil.
Tip in the orzo, shred over the leftover chicken and add the chickpeas (including their liquid). And simmer for 7- 8  mins, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is tender.
Pick and roughly chop the dill, then stir it through the soup with plenty of black pepper.
Ladle into bowls and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing over the top.

name: Lemon Chicken Quinoa Bowl
description: Zingy grilled chicken, fluffy quinoa and a herby yoghurt that hits all the right spots. This one’s got crunch, creaminess and big citrus energy.
instructions: Chuck the feta in the freezer — it’ll grate way easier later.

Score the chicken breasts in a criss-cross pattern. Peel and finely chop the garlic, then zest one of the lemons and squeeze in the juice of half. Add the olive oil, dried oregano and season well with salt and pepper. Toss the chicken in the marinade and leave for 20 mins or up to 4 hrs.
Meanwhile, cook the quinoa according to pack instructions.
Peel and finely slice the red onion. Squeeze over the juice of the remaining half of the first lemon. Season with salt and pepper, scrunch with your hands and set aside to pickle.
Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat. Grill the chicken for about 5 mins per side until charred and cooked through. Rest for a few mins, then slice.
Dice the cucumber. Toss it in a bowl with the pickled onions and pomegranate seeds. Pick in most of the dill, season with salt and pepper and give it all a mix.
Zest the second lemon into a bowl and stir through the Greek yoghurt. Grate in the frozen feta and mix well.
To serve, spoon the quinoa onto plates. Top with the sliced chicken, the cucumber salad and a dollop of the lemon feta yoghurt. Sprinkle with the rest of the dill. Serve with lemon wedges.

name: Lemon Drizzle Loaf
description: You can’t beat a proper lemon loaf cake. Lemony, light and simple. Let the sugar and lemon icing set into that incredible crunchy topping before you eat it.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160ºC. Grease a 900g (2lb) loaf tin with oil and line the base with baking paper.
Finely zest the lemons into a large bowl. Add the flour, sugar, eggs, yoghurt and oil along with a big pinch of salt and whisk to a smooth cake batter.

Scrape into the loaf tin and smooth out the top. Bake in the centre of the oven for 35-40 mins until the cake is well risen, deep golden brown and a skewer or a knife inserted into the centre comes out clean.

Drizzle time. While the cake is still warm juice 1 lemon into a bowl. Stir in the remaining caster sugar then spoon over the top of the loaf cake. Leave the icing to set whilst the cake completely cools then grab yourself a cuppa and cut a slice.
Will keep for up to 5 days in a container out of the fridge.

name: Lemon Meringue Pie
description: Crisp buttery pastry with a zingy lemon cream filling and a torched meringue top. An incredible dinner party dessert to impress your guests. 1 pie makes 8 servings for this recipe, we don't recommend scaling up or down.
instructions: Start by making the pastry.  Ensure your butter is very cold. Cube or grate the cold butter into a bowl and return to the fridge to chill. Chill the mixing bowl of a standing mixer and the paddle attachment in the fridge for 30 mins.
Sift the flour, salt and icing sugar into the standing mixer. Add the cold butter and combine in quick pulses until it just resembles breadcrumbs.

In a separate bowl crack in one the eggs for the pastry, then with the other carefully separate the yolk from the white, and add the yolk to the bowl, setting aside the white for the meringue (don't cool, they'll need to be at room temperature). Whisk together the egg and extra yolk. Gradually add to the mix until it just comes together as a dough. Wrap in clingfilm and refrigerate for at least 30 mins. Heat the oven to 180°C.
Roll out the shortcrust pastry to an approx 30cm circle and 3mm thickness and use it to line a 23 x 2.5cm fluted tart tin. Pop in the freezer for 30 mins.

Remove the dish from the freezer. Take a large square of baking paper and scrunch it into a ball then un-scrunch it and press it into the chilled pastry case. Weigh it down with baking beans or rice, making sure they come to the top of the case. Slide into the oven and bake for about 15-20 mins, or until the pastry is starting to brown. Then remove the baking parchment and beans and bake for another 7-10 mins. Remove from the oven, trim away any messy pastry edges and set aside to cool.
While the pastry bakes, make the lemon filling. Cut the butter into cubes and return to the fridge.

Zest one of the lemons into a heatproof bowl and add in the sugar and salt. Using your hands, massage together until fragrant and the sugar has a wet sand consistency. Juice all the lemons into bowl (you should have around 260ml).

Carefully separate the egg yolk from the white (add the egg white to your other reserved white for the meringue). In a mug, whisk the cornflour with 2 tbsp of the lemon juice and add to the bowl. Add the remaining lemon juice along with the egg yolk. Whisk to combine.

Set a small pan of water over a medium heat until simmering. Place the bowl with the lemony egg mixture on top of the simmering water (make sure the water isn’t touching the bottom of the bowl) and whisk for 10-20 mins until thickened.

Once thickened, remove the bowl from the heat and whisk in the cold butter, a cube at a time, until it’s all incorporated. Pour the lemon filling mixture into the cool pastry base and place in the fridge for 2-3 hours until fully cooled.

When the pie has cooled and set, make the meringue topping. Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise) and add to the 2 reserved egg whites from the pastry and filling (you should have 6 egg whites in total). Make sure the whites are at room temperature, if they're a little cool leave to stand for 5 mins.

Juice the lemon for the meringue and add to a mixing bowl with the egg whites. Use an electric whisk to whip until soft peaks form – approximately 5 mins. Slowly beat in the sugar, a couple of tbsp at a time, and continue until stiff shiny peaks form.
Scoop the meringue over the set pie and use a blowtorch to caramelise the meringue (or pop it under a hot grill for a few seconds). Serve and enjoy!

name: Lemon Pasta
description: A perfect intro to homemade pasta, featuring a low lift sauce with big flavours.
instructions: Start by making the pasta. Whisk the eggs together in a jug. Tip the flour into a bowl and use your fist to create a dent in the middle of the pile of flour. Tip the eggs in, then use a fork to mix together. Once it’s starting to combine, get your hands in there and draw it together into a shaggy dough.

Tip onto the kitchen surface, knead it together for a few minutes (don’t worry if it feels very firm at this point). Once it feels smooth, wrap the dough in cling film, then leave to sit in the fridge. This will give the gluten in the dough time to relax so it’ll be much easier to roll by hand.
Whisk the crème frâiche with the Parmesan and lemon juice.

Remove the dough from the fridge and cut into 4 pieces. Covering the other with cling film or a damp tea towel. Take each piece and begin to roll it out on the surface, roll until it's around 2mm thick. If it’s sticking to the surface too much, dust the surface with a little flour. If it starts to spring back at you, simply cover with a sheet of cling film and leave it for 5 mins to relax, then return to rolling it out.

Dust the sheet with semolina and roll it up like a swiss roll. Use a knife to cut the roll into thick ribbons, then unravel. Dust again with a little more semolina, then lay out to dry on your kitchen surface for around 10-15 mins, until feeling leathery. Repeat with the rest of the pasta.

Whilst the pasta dries, bring a pan of salted water to the boil. In a large frying pan, add the crème fraîche sauce and gently heat. Drop the pasta into the boiling water and cook for 3-4 mins, then use tongs to transfer the pasta into the crème fraîche sauce. Add the peas and toss everything together, adding a slosh of pasta water to keep the sauce silky. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Use tongs to swirl into bowls, top with the toasted pine nuts, parsley leaves, and extra Parmesan.

name: Lemon Pistachio Shortbread
description: Our nutty, citrus twist on a classic shortbread. These will make your kitchen smell incredible.
instructions: Line two baking trays with baking parchment. Ensure your butter is very cold. Cut the butter into cubes. Finely grate the zest of the lemon and crush the pistachios in a pestle and mortar.

Sift the flour, sugars, salt, lemon zest and crushed pistachios together in a large bowl and mix to combine. Add the cold butter and use your fingertips and thumbs to rub the flour mix into the butter until it resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolk and vanilla and use your hands to gently bring the mixture together into a dough, being careful not to overwork it.

Using a rolling pin, roll the dough out on a floured surface to approximately 1cm thick. Use an 8cm cookie cutter (or 6cm if you prefer mini shortbreads) to cut the dough into circles. Place them on the prepared baking tray and refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours, but preferably overnight.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan.

Slide the tray into the oven and bake for approximately 12 mins, or until the edges are just starting to brown. Remove from the oven, cool on the tray for a couple of mins, then transfer to a wire rack. Dust the tops with more sugar and leave to cool completely.

name: Lemon Posset
description: A classic pudding consisting of only three ingredients: lemons, double cream and sugar. Super tangy and creamy, it’s a perfect dinner party dessert.
instructions: Measure the caster sugar into a saucepan and add the zest of ⅔ the lemons. Rub the lemon zest into the sugar and leave for a minute or two to bring out the lemon flavour.
Meanwhile, juice the lemons into a jug and measure out 75ml juice.

Pour the double cream into the saucepan with the sugar then set it over a low heat. Cook it gently, stirring occasionally until the sugar has dissolved, then turn up the heat to medium and bring the cream to the boil. Bubble away for a minute then take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.

Pour the posset into four serving vessels – ramekins, fun small bowls, or even glasses work well here. Transfer to the fridge for at least 4 hours until chilled and set. Enjoy as is or with shortbread biscuits for dunking.

name: Lemon Spaghetti
description: This lemony pasta is super quick, rich and zingy. The carbonara-style execution means the sauce needs no cooking and it's done in 15 mins. Jordon x
instructions: Start by getting your pasta to a boil in a pan of salty water, by the time it’s done the sauce will be ready.

Separate your egg yolks into a bowl (you can freeze the whites for meringue) and add the zest and juice from half your lemon/s before throwing in a good pinch of salt, the black pepper, and grated Parmesan. Mix well into a loose paste.
Add a ladle of pasta water to a large mixing bowl, swirl it around a bit, and then pour it out.

Once the pasta is al dente, drain it and add it to the warm bowl along with the egg mix. Stir well, adding splashes of pasta water until you have a creamy emulsified sauce. Taste and then add as much juice of the remaining lemon as needed.
Serve with a little more Parmesan, pepper and lemon zest.

name: Lemon Tahini Instant Noodles
description: We've upgraded your average instant ramen noodles with a creamy lemon tahini broth and crispy chilli oil.
instructions: If using courgette and carrot, finely slice them into thin batons with a julienne peeler or a knife. You could also peel them into thin ribbons with a speed peeler.
Boil a pot of water on the hob with 1 stock cube. Add the noodles, courgette and carrot and boil for 4 mins (or as long as the noodle package states).
Set a cup of the cooking water (stock) aside and drain the noodles.
Pour the cup of stock into a medium sided serving bowl. Pour in the tahini and squeeze the lemon into the stock and whisk until well combined into smooth sauce.
Add the noodles and veg into the bowl with the lemon tahini sauce and mix well until all of the noodles are covered in sauce.
Top with a tablespoon of chilli oil and sesame seeds.

name: Lemon, Honey and Thyme Cake
description: This polenta cake is a one-bowl wonder. Rich with Onken Yogurt, fragrant lemons and a herby honey syrup, you are going to love the soft texture of this one.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C/160°C fan.
Grease a 20cm cake tin with melted butter and line it with baking parchment.
Add your olive oil and 200g of honey into a large bowl. Crack in your eggs, then add the zest of one lemon along with its juice. Spoon in your Onken Set Natural Yogurt. Mix to combine.
Add your ground almonds, baking powder, polenta and a pinch of salt.
Pour your batter into your cake tin and bake for 35 mins - a skewer inserted in the centre should come out clean.

Meanwhile, pour your remaining 50g of honey into a small saucepan. Zest and juice your remaining 2 lemons, then add your thyme sprigs. Warm over a gentle heat, stirring occasionally until you have a smooth syrupy mixture.
Allow your cake to cool in its tin for 10 mins, then poke little holes in the top with a skewer. Pour over the syrup, then allow the cake to cool completely in its tin.
Cut into slices and serve with a dollop of Onken Set Natural Yogurt and a few extra thyme leaves.

name: Lemongrass & Coconut Butternut Soup
description: The best shout for some Halloween munching. Better than any Thai squash soup you’ll get in the supermarkets.
instructions: Finely slice onion, red chilli, cloves of garlic, the coriander stalks and the ginger. Set them aside.
Trim, peel and de-seed the butternut. Then, chop into 2cm chunks. Trim and gently bash the lemongrass to release it's oils.

Get a large pan on the heat and pour in a glug of olive oil. Add your onion, ginger, garlic, coriander stalks and 1/2 of the chilli. Fry until softened, then add the lemongrass stalk. Mix it in and add your squash.
Stir it about. Pour both the coconut milk and stock in, bring the mixture to the boil and place a lid on. Reduce the heat down to medium and let simmer, until the butternut has softened, 15-20 mins.
Discard the lemongrass stalk. Take a hand blender and blitz the squash mixture.
Turn up the heat and bubble the soup down until thickened to your liking. Taste and season with salt.
When ready, pour soup into bowls, scatter with coriander leaves, some of the reserved chilli and drizzle over some olive oil. Enjoy!

name: Lemongrass Chicken Patties & Lettuce Cups
description: Crispy and seriously juicy lemongrass chicken patties perfect for wrapping up in lettuce with herbs, rice and a sticky sweet chilli sauce. Just as good cold the next day and great for freezing too . Also just skip the chilli sauce and they are great for kids too!
instructions: Trim the tough outer leaves from the lemongrass and roughly chop the tender centres. Roughly chop the coriander, slice the spring onions, then add everything to a small food processor with the garlic and ginger and blitz until finely chopped. If you don't have one, finely grate the lemongrass, garlic and ginger, finely chop the coriander and thinly slice the spring onions by hand.

Add the lemongrass mixture to the chicken mince with the fish sauce, a generous pinch of salt and a little black pepper. Grate in the zest of one lime, keeping that lime back for the dipping sauce. Mix well, then shape into 16 small patties.
Heat a little neutral oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the patties for 4-5 mins on each side, until deeply golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile, grate the ginger into a bowl and stir together with the sweet chilli sauce, fish sauce and the juice of the zested lime. Taste and add another squeeze of lime if it needs balancing.

Heat the rice according to the packet instructions. Separate the lettuce leaves, thinly slice the sugar snap peas and cucumber and roughly pick the mint, Thai basil and coriander leaves. Cut the remaining limes into wedges.

Arrange the rice, lettuce leaves, sugar snap peas, cucumber and herbs on a serving platter. Serve with the patties, the lime wedges and the sweet chilli dipping sauce for spooning over or dipping, then wrap everything up in the lettuce leaves with a little rice, plenty of herbs and a generous drizzle of the sauce. These are also brilliant with quick pickled carrots or sliced radishes if you fancy another layer of crunch, and the patties are just as good cold, which makes them ideal for meal prep lunches.

name: Lemongrass Grapefruit Prawn Salad With Toasted Coconut & Peanut
description: A zingy Thai-inspired salad with plenty of acid and heat. Ideal for eating on a hot summer's day.
instructions: Place the eggs into boiling water and cook for 6½ mins, then set aside. Refill the pot with salted water and bring to the boil. Once boiling, cook the prawns until cooked through, then transfer to a large bowl.
Pick all the mint and coriander leaves and transfer to a small bowl of ice cold water (this will help them get crispy, crunchy and bring them back to life). Finely slice the coriander stems.

Segment the grapefruit, and place into the prawns. Squeeze the juice out of the grapefruit membrane onto the segments. Finely slice the red onions and add to the mixing bowl. Slice the cucumber for garnish and set aside.

For the dressing, trim and bash the lemongrass and garlic then finely mince. Thinly slice the lime leaves and chillies. Add everything to a small mixing bowl, with some coriander stems, half the sugar and all the remaining dressing ingredients (add more sugar if your grapefruit is very sour/bitter) and mix well.

Add the coconut to a small pan set over a high heat and continuously toss for 2 mins or until deeply golden brown, then set aside in a small bowl to stop it cooking. Pound the roasted peanuts and combine with the coconut, then add the crispy shallots, too.
When you are ready to serve, drain the herbs and toss through the grapefruit and prawns. Add the crispy coconut garnish, then all the dressing and gently toss.
Serve immediately. Eat as a side or serve with the rice, boiled eggs and cucumbers.

name: Lemongrass Pork Meatball Bowl
description: These fragrant, spicy lemongrass meatballs use lean pork mince and punchy aromatics. A zingy, nutritious midweek recipe to add to your locker.
instructions: Add the lemongrass, half of the coriander, half of your green chillies, half of the spring onions, half the ginger, and all of the garlic to a food processor along with the fish sauce, soy and two-thirds of your sugar. Whizz into a coarse paste.
Add the pork mince to a bowl and chuck in the paste. Mix thoroughly until the pork starts to become sticky and is totally homogenous. Pop into the fridge for 15 mins.

Meanwhile, combine the rice vinegar with the remaining sugar in a bowl. Cut the remaining ginger and chilli into matchsticks, and cut the cucumber and carrot into small batons. Sprinkle with salt and allow to sit for 10 mins. Drain off any excess moisture then add to the vinegar and sugar mixture. Set aside.
Cook the sushi rice according to the package instructions and keep warm.

Shape your pork mixture into ping pong ball-sized meatballs. Set a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the meatballs one by one, browning on all sides. Keep cooking, rolling around, until the meatballs are cooked through and starting to char. Add the sweet chilli sauce and a dash of soy sauce. Glaze the meatballs with the sweet chilli.
Finely slice your remaining spring onions. Serve the meatballs over the steamy sushi rice with a handful of pickled veg and the remaining coriander and spring onion on top.

name: Lemongrass Pork Meatballs & Tomato Brothy Rice
description: Somewhere between a noodle soup and a rice bowl, these fragrant meatballs and nourishing broth make the perfect mid-week dinner when you need a bit of comfort but still want something fresh.
keywords: Lemongrass Pork Meatballs & Tomato Brothy Rice recipe
Lemongrass Pork Meatballs & Tomato Brothy Rice
instructions: Remove the casings from the sausages and discard. Finely mince the lemongrass, finely grate the ginger and garlic. Place all three into a bowl and add the sausage meat, thoroughly mixing until combined. Evenly divide the mixture into 12 and roll into meatballs, set aside.
Peel and thinly slice the shallots, chop the tomatoes into 2cm chunks.

Set a saucepan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the meatballs sear for 6-7 mins, until golden brown (they don’t need to be cooked through at this stage). 
Transfer to a plate and return the pan onto the heat.

Add the shallots and tomatoes into the hot saucepan and cook for 6-10 mins, until softened. Stir the ketchup through, cook for a 1-2 mins, then pour the stock in. Let it come to a gentle simmer before dropping the meatballs. Cook for 7-10 mins, until they are cooked through. Taste and season the broth with fish sauce and lime.
Reheat the rice and pick the herb leaves, discarding the stems.
Divide the rice between bowls. Ladle the meatballs and broth in. Serve with the herbs, some chilli oil and a wedge of lime.

name: Lemony 'Nduja and Mascarpone Risotto
description: The finest risotto imaginable. Spicy, creamy, and light from a touch of lemon juice, this is the silkiest dinner you could ever cook up.
instructions: Finely dice your onion. Finely chop your cloves of garlic and parsley.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large sauté pan over a medium heat. Add your onion and cook gently for 20 mins until totally soft, but not taking on colour. Add your ‘nduja and garlic and cook for another 2 mins until the ‘nduja has darkened slightly.
Tip your cherry tomatoes into the pan and cook for 5 mins, squashing them with your wooden spoon so that they collapse a bit and create a jammy sauce.
Pour your arborio rice into the pan and toast the grains for 2 mins until slightly translucent.

Turn your heat down. Pour your hot chicken stock into the pan a ladle at a time, stirring until the rice has fully absorbed the liquid before adding more. This should take about 25 mins, but add more hot water if necessary.
Check that your rice grains are tender. Add your mascarpone, 3/4 of the grated parmesan and salt and pepper to taste. Take your risotto off the heat and pop a lid on it. Let it rest for 5 mins.
Add your chopped parsley and the zest of the lemon to the risotto, then add any more hot water you need to give it your desired consistency – I like mine fairly silky and loose.
Spoon your risotto into bowls and top with a drizzle of olive oil and more parmesan. Serve and enjoy.

name: Lemony Chicken & Pepper Rice
description: Golden chicken thighs over lemony rice with peppers, then topped with a bright feta and pomegranate salad for the grown-ups.
keywords: lemony chicken and pepper rice bake
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsSlice the lemon into ½ cm rounds. Peel and slice the garlic. Pick the oregano leaves.

Heat 2/3 of the olive oil in a large ovenproof casserole dish set over a medium heat. Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Add the chicken and lemon slices to the pan and brown on all sides for about 6–7 mins, until the chicken is golden and the lemon lightly caramelised. Remove to a plate.

Add the garlic and half of the oregano to the pan and cook for 1 min, stirring. Add the rice and frozen peppers, stirring to coat. Pour over the chicken stock and bring to a simmer. Return the chicken and lemon slices to the dish, cover cook for 20-25 mins, or until the chicken is cooked through and the rice is tender.
Meanwhile, make the pomegranate salad for the adults. In a bowl, toss the remaining oregano and olive oil together, then add the pomegranate seeds and crumble in the feta.

Serve up!Kids Plate: Dish out the rice and chicken, cutting the chicken into bite-sized pieces for little ones.Parents Plate: Serve the rice and chicken with the lemon slices on top. Finish with the pomegranate salad.

name: Lemony Chicken with Braised Lettuce & Peas
description: Who needs crunchy lettuce when you can have braised lettuce? Cooked soft in gorgeous chickeny juices, it's a simple, seasonal winner. Ready to convert anyone who thinks lettuce shouldn't be cooked.
keywords: Crispy Lemony Chicken with Braised Lettuce & Peas
Crispy Lemony Chicken with Braised Lettuce & Peas recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Pat the chicken skin dry then season with salt. Add the oil to a heavy-bottomed frying pan and set over a medium-high heat.

Add the chicken thighs skin-side down, you may need to do this in batches. Once sizzling, leave to cook without touching for 7-8 mins, until nicely golden. Flip and cook for another minute to sear the underside. Transfer to a baking tray and pop in the oven for 20-25 mins, until cooked through.
In the meantime, finely dice the shallot and finely chop the dill. Halve the romaine lettuce, then drain and halve the potatoes.

Add the butter to the pan and melt. Once foaming, add the romaine and cook over a high heat for a couple of minutes, until charred, then remove from the pan. Add the shallot and reduce the heat to medium, cooking it out for a couple of minutes. Add the stock, bring to the boil and reduce by half, this'll take around 10 mins.

Add the lettuce back into the pan cut-side up along with the potatoes, then simmer for a couple of minutes before adding the frozen peas. By now the chicken should be cooked, so pour the resting juices into the pan along with the dill and the juice of half the lemon. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Cut the remaining lemon half into wedges and serve up as is, or with crusty bread for mopping.

name: Lemony Confit Garlic Orzo
description: This delicious pasta number is made with just 5 ingredients. It was a big hit in the test kitchen. We're sure you and your Mob will love it too!
instructions: Peel the garlic cloves. You want to keep them whole so don’t smash them!
Peel the lemon rinds into long strips and halve and deseed the red chillies.
Pop the garlic cloves, lemon rind and deseeded chillies in a small saucepan and cover with 750ml olive oil, or enough to cover.

Heat the saucepan over low heat and cook gently for 30 mins or until the garlic is soft. You want the oil to barely be simmering. If it starts to bubble, remove the pan from the heat to cool a little then pop it back onto the stove to continue cooking.
Strain the oil into a bowl. This oil is liquid gold - store it in a jar and use it on/in everything!
Cook the orzo in plenty of boiling salted water until al dente, reserving some of the cooking water for later.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the chillies and grate the parmesan. Place both in a bowl with the garlic and season well with salt and pepper. Mash into a paste.
Add a ladleful of the orzo cooking water to the cheesy confit garlic paste and mix to loosen.
Drain the orzo and return it to the pot. Add the cheesy confit garlic paste and another splash of orzo cooking water and toss.
Toss until a luscious sauce forms and the orzo is nicely coated in it, adding more pasta water as needed.
To serve, top with a sprinkle of parmesan and the confit lemon pieces - enjoy!

name: Lemony Mushroom Carbonara
description: This twist on a classic carbonara is an absolute delight. We swap out guanciale for mushrooms for an umami hit - they pair amazingly with the lemon and herbs.
instructions: First, prep your ingredients. Quarter your mushrooms and finely chop your garlic and parsley. Remove your thyme leaves from their sprigs - you should have about 1 tbsp of leaves.
Grate your parmesan and pecorino.
Bring a large pan of water to a boil, then season liberally with salt. Add your pasta and cook according to packet instructions, until al dente.

In a medium sized bowl, add the egg yolks - save your egg whites for use at a later date or freeze. Add your parmesan and pecorino and zest your lemon into the mixture. Grate in lots of black pepper, then stir to combine.

Heat a large saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add a large knob of butter to the pan and, once melted, tip in your mushrooms. Cook until the mushrooms have released their liquid and started to caramelise. Add your garlic and thyme and cook out for a minute, ensuring it doesn’t burn.

Drain your pasta, reserving the pasta water, then tip it into the pan along with a ladle of pasta water and toss together so that the mixture is totally combined. Turn the heat off in your pan, then add your egg mixture. Mix together in the pan, letting the residual heat from the pasta cook your egg mixture until you have a silky pasta that coats each shell, adding more pasta water where needed.
Add a handful of chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice, then give it one last stir.
Serve topped with more cracked black pepper and some parmesan.

name: Lemony Mustard-Crusted Salmon & Potatoes
description: Zingy mustard salmon, buttery spuds and tender asparagus, all baked in parchment for a no-fuss midweek dinner that feels a bit fancy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the lemon in half, then cut a few thin half-moon slices from one half and keep the other for squeezing over later. Trim the woody ends off the asparagus, drain and halve the potatoes and then roughly chop the dill.
Season the salmon with salt and pepper. Spread over the wholegrain mustard, dot with butter and lay a few lemon slices on top.

Lay out a large sheet of baking paper per person, portrait. Arrange the potatoes, asparagus and capers in a single layer on one half of the paper, then sit the salmon on top. Drizzle with olive oil, season and give everything a gentle mix. Fold the top half of the paper over, then fold and crimp the edges to seal it up tight, think Cornish pasty. Repeat for each parcel.If you’re scaling up for more people, just use a parchment-lined baking tray and a tight foil lid instead. Cooking times might vary, so keep an eye on it.
Pop the parcels onto a baking tray and slide into the oven for 15-20 mins, until the salmon flakes easily when pressed.

Remove from the oven and carefully open the parcels and lift out the salmon and set aside. Stir the chopped dill through the potatoes and asparagus. Serve everything up with the remaining lemon for squeezing over.

name: Lemony Olive Braised Chicken
description: A super-simple and super lemony chicken that’s based on one of our favourite dishes ever: preserved lemon and olive tagine.
instructions:
Pour the olive oil into a heavy-based saucepan and place over the
lowest heat. Add the chicken thighs, skin-side down (you may need
to do this in batches). Cook for 10 mins until the chicken skin is
very crispy and the fat has rendered out. Remove the chicken and
set aside on a plate.

Meanwhile, dice the onion and slice the garlic. Juice 2/3 the lemons (you want 100ml of lemon juice) and thinly slice the remaining lemon. Break apart the olives with your fingers, removing the stones. Drain the butterbeans, keeping the liquid.

Add the onion to the chicken fat and cook for 5 mins over
a medium-high heat until lightly golden. Add the garlic, black
peppercorns and turmeric and cook for 2 mins more.
Pour in the white wine to deglaze the pan and let the alcohol cook off for 5 mins, or until the onions are sticky.

Add the butter beans into the pan with the chicken stock, lemon juice, lemon slices and olives. Top with the chicken, skin side up. Cover and cook for 15-20 mins until the chicken is cooked through. Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed. Add a splash of bean liquid, if you'd like a runnier sauce.
Season with salt and black pepper before serving with warm crusty bread. Enjoy!

name: Lemony Spiced Chickpea Soup
description: This is the soup to end all colds. It’s got a combination of turmeric, garlic, ginger, lemon and pepper that will see you through this cold season unscathed.
instructions: Finely chop the onion before grating or mincing the garlic and ginger. Zest the lemons and slice them in half. Set aside.
Drain and rinse two cans of chickpeas.
Add 2 tbsp of oil to a medium pan and sauté the onion for 3-5 mins, then add the spices, chilli flakes, ginger, and garlic.

Sauté for a further 2 mins and then add the drained chickpeas. Fry for 5-8 mins, stirring often, until the chickpeas start to soften and slightly crisp up. Remove 3-4 tbsp of chickpeas from the pot and save on the side for garnish.
Add the coconut milk and stock and stir well.
If you like, you can use a potato masher to mash some of the chickpeas in the soup. This will give it a chunky texture. Stir through the spinach.
Simmer for 10 mins and then add the juice and zest of the two lemons. Start with one and taste it, adding more to your liking. Season well with salt and pepper.
To serve, ladle the soup into two bowls, topping with a big dollop of coconut yogurt and some fresh mint leaves, if using. Finish with a sprinkle of chilli flakes if you like.

name: Lemony Spinach Pesto Lentils
description: The only thing that I can cook when I can’t be bothered to cook, is a version of these super speedy pesto lentils with crispy fried eggs and a lotta herbs.
instructions: Add a big glug of olive oil to a large frying pan over a medium high heat and crush in the garlic, no need to peel! Add the fennel seeds and toast for a min, then add the spinach and stir until it wilts down and is bright green.
Meanwhile, roughly chop most of the herbs, saving a few for the top.
Stir in the lentils with a splash of water. Then add the herbs and the juice of your lemon. Stir in the pesto, season well then tip into a bowl.
Heat another tbsp of olive oil in the pan, crack the egg into the hot oil and fry to your liking.
Top the lentil bowl with a little yoghurt, the fried egg, and the nuts on top. Finish with a crack pepper.

name: Lentil & Halloumi Salad with Orange Dressing
description: Fresh, zingy, and loaded up with plenty of halloumi. This lunch box salad hits all the right notes.
keywords: Lentil & Halloumi Salad with Orange Dressing
Lentil & Halloumi Salad with Orange Dressing recipe
instructions: Heat grill to high. In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, and the juice of half the orange. Season with salt and pepper. Finely chop the shallot and add it to the bowl.
Drain and rinse the lentils, then tip them into the bowl with the shallot. Finely chop the parsley and dice the beetroot, then add both to the bowl. Toss to combine.
Slice the halloumi into thick pieces and place them on a tray lined with foil. Grill for 3–4 mins on each side until golden and crisp around the edges.
Add the grilled halloumi and rocket to the salad. Toss everything together until coated in the dressing, then taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Spoon your salad into your Tupperware containers. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Lentil & Halloumi Salad with Orange Dressing
description: Fresh, zingy, and loaded up with plenty of halloumi. This salad hits all the right notes.
keywords: Lentil & Halloumi Salad with Orange Dressing
Lentil & Halloumi Salad with Orange Dressing recipe
instructions: Heat grill to high. In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, and the juice of half the orange. Season with salt and pepper. Finely chop the shallot and add it to the bowl.
Drain and rinse the lentils, then tip them into the bowl with the shallot. Finely chop the parsley and dice the beetroot, then add both to the bowl. Toss to combine.
Slice the halloumi into thick pieces and place them on a tray lined with foil. Grill for 3–4 mins on each side until golden and crisp around the edges.
Add the grilled halloumi and rocket to the salad. Toss everything together until coated in the dressing, then taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Serve up and dig in while the halloumi’s still warm.

name: Lentil Tofu Ragù & Chickpeas
description: Smoky, savoury lentil ragù with crispy roasted tofu. Super hearty and packed with plant-based protein. A weeknight winner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Crumble the tofu with your hands into mince-sized chunks. Tip onto a lined baking tray, season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15 mins until starting to char, then set aside.

Finely chop the carrot, celery, onion and garlic. While you're prepping, roughly chop the fresh parsley and set aside for garnish later. Heat oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the chopped carrot, celery, onion and garlic and a pinch of salt. Cook for 10–15 mins until soft and starting to caramelise.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins to darken and intensify.
Drain the chickpeas and lentils. Add both to the pan along with the chopped tomatoes, miso, tofu and stock. Season again, then simmer for 15–20 mins until thickened.
Meanwhile, make your tahini drizzle. Juice the lemon into a small bowl and add the tahini, salt and pepper, giving it all a good mix, then add in a splash of water to loosen.
Once the ragu is ready, serve up into bowls with the chopped parsley and tahini drizzle. Any leftovers are perfect quick meal stashed in the fridge or freezer.

name: Lentil, Potato and Cumin Soup with Crispy Onions
description: This is my take on shorbet el adas, a Lebanese soup of creamy lentils, warming cumin and zingy lemon. A soothing winter dinner.
keywords: potato and cumin soup with crispy onions recipes
instructions: Place a large saucepan over a medium low heat and add 3 tbsp of olive oil. Finely dice one of the onions and add to the pan with a pinch of salt, sweat for a few mins until soft but not browned.
Roughly dice the potato and add to the pan along with the cumin, turmeric and chilli flakes (if using), cook for a minute.
Add the lentils, stir well. Dissolve both of the stock cubes into 1L of hot water and add to the pan along with the whole peeled garlic cloves.
Bring to a simmer and allow to cook for about 30 mins until the potato and lentils are both soft.
While the soup cooks, make the crispy onions. Slice the remaining onion and toss with the flour. In a large pan, heat about 2 inches of sunflower or vegetable oil.
If you have a thermometer, bring the oil to 180c. If not, after a couple of minutes test to see if it’s hot enough by dropping in a small piece of onion. It should bubble and sizzle.
Fry the onion in 2 batches for a few minutes until golden brown. Drain onto kitchen paper.
Once the soup has cooked, use a hand blender to whizz it up until it’s thick and smooth. Add the juice of one lemon, stir, then taste for seasoning and add salt as you like.
Add the soup to bowls, roughly chop your parsley and sprinkle over, then add a handful of crispy onions and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve with another wedge of lemon for squeezing over.

name: Lesan El Asfour (Egyptian Beef & Orzo)
description: Tender, fall-apart braising beef matched with roasted red peppers and a fragrant tomato sauce. Simple yet delicious. And did we say it's made in just one pan?
instructions: Trim and finely chop the red pepper and onion. Trim, peel and finely slice the garlic.

Add half the ghee/butter into a large frying pan and melt. Then, add the orzo and toast, stirring constantly until golden. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the orzo into a bowl, leaving the fat in the pan.
Add the beef chunks into the hot fat and sear all sides — do this in batches if needed so you get a nice colour on the meat. Transfer the beef into another bowl.
Add the remaining ghee/butter into the pan. Stir the onion and garlic until softened, 4-5 mins.
Meanwhile, drain the peppers and place into a blender with the passata, blend until smooth.

Pour half the chicken stock in with the cinnamon, scrape the bottom of the pot, then add beef chunks, the rest of the stock and passata mixture. Bring to a boil, turn the heat down to medium, place a lid on and simmer until tender, 50-60 mins.
Once tender, remove the lid, add the toasted orzo and 150ml of water, stir until the orzo is cooked, 15-20 mins. Taste and season with sugar, salt and pepper, stir through the pomegranate molasses.
Garnish with lots of fresh parsley, and enjoy.

name: Light & Brothy Miso-Grilled Fish With Rice
description: This one is a mashup of miso soup and Seychellois bouillon bread – it’s light, brothy and takes no time to come together. Watercress adds so much flavour to the broth as well as packing this meal with loads of nutrients. Mackerel is in season right now, so I would highly recommend using it, but salmon or any other fatty fish will work perfectly (just make sure your fillets are skin-on.)
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites from the greens. Roughly chop the watercress. Combine the tahini and chilli oil in a small bowl, then set aside.

Place the fish fillets onto an oiled baking tray, skin-side up. Grill for 5-10 mins until fully cooked through and the skin goes golden in places. Turn the grill down a little if it’s too hot (every grill works differently, so keep an eye on your fillets).
Meanwhile, pour the fish or dashi stock into a saucepan with the spring onion whites. Place over a medium-high heat and heat through. Reheat the cooked rice.

Add the miso paste to a cup, ladle in a little hot broth and stir together until diluted. Pour the mixture into the saucepan, taste and add more miso, if needed. Stir the watercress through the stock until wilted.
Share the rice between bowls. Ladle the broth over the rice, top with the grilled fish and drizzle over the spicy tahini. Finish with a scattering of spring onion greens.

name: Light & Brothy Tomato Soup
description: Soup season is not over, It’s summer and this light and brothy soup is the perfect weeknight dinner. It’s vibrant and highlights gorgeous summer tomatoes.
keywords: light and brothy tomato soup recipe
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the shallot, trim and halve any large tomatoes into 3cm chunks, leave any cherry or small tomatoes whole.

Place a deep saucepan over medium-high heat with 2 tbsps of oil. Once hot, add the shallots and tomatoes, cook until they both have softened, 4-5 mins. Using the back of your wooden spoon, lightly smash the tomatoes until they burst. Stir through the yellow thai curry paste, cook for 2-3 mins.
Meanwhile, strip the leaves of the cavolo nero off, discard the stems and rip the leaves into bite size chunks.

Pour the vegetable stock and 200ml of water into the tomatoes. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to medium-low so that its barely simmering. Add the cavolo nero and quinoa and cook until piping hot and wilted.
Take off the heat and stir half the basil leaves through. Taste and season with lime juice, fish sauce/soy sauce, black pepper and salt.
Share the soup into bowls and top with the remaining basil and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Lime & Basil Spritz
description: Frangrant basil and lime makes this a perfect summer sipper. This one's finished with blood orange soda for an extra citrus fizz.
instructions: Fill a wine glass with ice cubes.
Squeeze the juice from one of your limes. Cut the other into rounds.
Pour your vodka over your ice, followed by your lime juice.
Pour in your blood orange soda, then finish with a slice of lime and a sprig of basil.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Lime Pickle Chicken & Coconutty Rice Salad with Mango Dressing
description: This is a lovely little fresh and summery chicken and rice salad. It's really easy to whip up on a weeknight and will have your kitchen feeling like summer no matter the weather outside.
keywords: coconut lime chilli chicken salad recipe
instructions: Using a sharp knife, remove bone from thighs.

Finely chop the lime pickle, transfer to a large bowl and add the mayo. Mix until smooth, season with salt and pepper, then add the chicken thighs. Mix well to coat, then allow to marinate for at least 1 hr.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Tip the marinated chicken onto a baking tray, then cook in the oven for 10 mins, then turn the grill to high. Grill the chicken for around 10 mins until charred and cooked through.
Meanwhile, make the slaw. Shred the cabbage, then halve the cucumber, scoop out the seeds and slice. Finely slice the mint and red onion. Add everything to a bowl.
For the dressing, add mango flesh, chillies and olive oil into a blender and purée until smooth. Season with lime juice, salt and pepper and mix with the yoghurt. Loosen with water if needed.
Toast the coconut flakes in a pan until golden. Heat the rice following pack instructions.

Squeeze the lime juice into the slaw and toss right before serving. Plate up the rice with the slaw and chicken, then drizzle with mango dressing. Garnish with coconut flakes and more mint, if you like.

name: Lime Wasabi Fish Finger Sando
description: A fish finger sandwich is perfect for those lazy days. Who makes their own fish fingers anyway?
keywords: Lime Wasabi Fish Finger Sando recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cook the fish fingers following pack instructions.
Meanwhile, slice the chives as finely as possible and thinly slice the red onion. Fill a bowl with cold water and soak the onions for 2 mins, then drain. Set aside.
Combine the mayonnaise, wasabi, soy sauce, chives and a squeeze of lime juice in a bowl. Use a grater to zest the outside of the lime and add to the sauce.

Set a pan over a medium heat. Add a knob of butter. Toast the slices of bread for 1-2 mins, pressing down gently and occasionally moving them around the pan to ensure even toasting. Once golden, flip and repeat on the other side. Set the toast aside.

Place one piece of bread on a plate. Add a generous dollop of sauce and spread evenly. Add 4 fish fingers, followed by half the red onion. Lastly add a slice of American cheese and another piece of bread on top. Repeat for the second sandwich.
Gently press down on the sandwich and slice straight down the middle. To be extra indulgent, flip the sandwich upright and dollop over the remaining sauce and sprinkle with chives.

name: Limoncello Spritz
description: Refreshing, zesty, and exactly what you want to be sipping on when the sun is out.
instructions: Put your mint leaves in your glass with your St-Germain and muddle.
Add your limoncello, ice, and sparkling water then stir.
Top up each glass with prosecco and then garnish with lemon wheel and mint leaves. Enjoy!

name: Lip-Tingling Sichuan Chicken & Sticky Rice
description: Poached chicken drenched in a Sichuan chilli oil dressing, piled over jasmine rice with refreshing cucumber. It's a serious spicy delight.
keywords: Cold Chilli Oil Poached Chicken Rice
Cold Chilli Oil Poached Chicken Rice recipe
instructions: Mandoline the cucumber into thin slices, toss with a generous pinch of salt and set aside to draw out the excess water while you cook everything else.

Rinse the jasmine rice and add to a small saucepan with the water. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a low heat, cover and cook for around 12 minutes until tender. Turn off the heat and let it steam while you prepare the chicken.

Bring a separate saucepan of water to a gentle simmer. Add the ginger, spring onion and salt, then lower in the chicken breasts. Simmer very gently for 2–3 minutes, then turn the heat off, cover and leave to poach in the residual heat for about 12 minutes, until just cooked through and very tender. Reserve 4 tbsp of the poaching liquid before removing the chicken.

While the chicken poaches, grind the Sichuan peppercorns, then mix together with the chilli oil, soy sauce, black vinegar, sesame oil, grated garlic and sugar in a bowl. Stir in the reserved poaching liquid to loosen.
Lightly squeeze the salted cucumber to remove the excess liquid. Finely slice the spring onions.
Remove the chicken from the poaching liquid and slice into thick pieces. Spoon over the chilli oil dressing so the chicken is well coated.
Divide the rice between two bowls. Top with the sliced chicken, salted cucumber and plenty of the chilli oil dressing. Finish with the spring onions and sesame seeds and serve.

name: Loaded Chilli Nachos
description: Nachos aren't just for the cinema. We've loaded these up with chilli and cheese – it's not a light dinner. But it is a damned good one.
instructions: Make the Beef Chilli Con Carne.
Preheat your grill to high and reheat your leftover Beef Chilli Con Carne in a saucepan over a medium heat.
Chop the tomatoes and avocado into 1cm chunks and grate the cheddar. Lightly season the tomatoes with salt and set aside.

Add the tortilla crisps onto a large baking tray. Dollop the warm chilli all over it and top with grated cheddar cheese. Place under the grill until the cheese has melted, 4-8 mins (every grill is different, some might take longer, some might need less time.)
Once melted, top with the soured cream, avocado chunks, tomatoes and tear over some fresh coriander and tuck in!

name: Loaded Chipotle Chicken & Sweet Potato Wedges
description: Crispy sweet potato wedges loaded with leftovers from your Juicy Pulled Chipotle Chicken batch with melty cheese, salsa and soured cream. Like nachos but sweet, spicy and roasted.
keywords: Loaded Chipotle Chicken & Sweet Potato Wedges recipe
Loaded Chipotle Chicken & Sweet Potato Wedges
instructions: Make the Juicy Pulled Chipotle Chicken.
Heat the oven to 200°C.
