Finely slice the red onion an dpop in a small bowl. Add the juice of 2/3 lime over, mixing well. Leave to pickle.
Trim the sweet potatoes and slice into wedges. Tip onto a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Toss to coat, then roast for 20–25 mins until tender and golden.
Meanwhile, warm the pulled chipotle chicken in a saucepan over a low heat until piping hot. Finely grate the cheddar. Pick the coriander leaves and set aside.

Once the wedges are ready, divide between plates and scatter over half the grated cheddar. Top with the hot pulled chicken, dollops of soured cream and salsa, then finish with remaining cheddar and coriander.
Drain the liquid from the pickled red onions and scatter over each plate.
Serve with extra lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Loaded Masala Beans & Eggs on Toast
description: Beans on toast, but better. These loaded masala beans make for a mean weeknight dinner.
keywords: Loaded Masala Beans & Eggs on Toast
Loaded Masala Beans & Eggs on Toast recipe
instructions: Finely chop the onion and green chilli, then set aside. Grate the cheddar, then set aside as well.

Heat the rapeseed oil in a pan over a medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add the onion and sauté until soft and translucent. Add the garlic paste, ginger paste, curry leaves and green chilli. Sauté for 2-3 mins until fragrant. Stir through the curry powder, ground coriander, turmeric, chilli powder and ½ tsp salt. Cook for 1-2 mins until the spices are well blended and aromatic.
Add the baked beans to the pan, stirring to combine with the spice mixture. Simmer for 5-7 mins. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
While the beans are simmering, toast the sourdough. Butter generously and pile some cheese on top.
In a separate pan, heat 2 tbsp butter or some oil over a medium heat. Fry the eggs however you like them – I have mine sunny-side up and runny.

For the chilli oil tarka, first finely chop the curry leaves. Heat the butter in a small pan over a medium heat until melted. Add the mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add the curry leaves and chilli powder. Fry for a few seconds until the spices are fragrant, then remove from the heat.
Finely chop the coriander and green chillies.

It’s now time to build the toasts. Place a slice of cheesy sourdough toast on a serving plate. Spoon the piping hot masala baked beans generously on top. Top each slice with a fried egg. Finally, drizzle the chilli tarka over the egg. Garnish with the chopped coriander and green chillies, then serve immediately!

name: Loaded Turkey Burritos With Pineapple Salsa
description: We’ve used turkey mince for these burritos, which is low in saturated fat but high in protein. An easy dinner.
keywords: Loaded Turkey Burrito With Pineapple Salsa
instructions:
Start with the salsa. Very finely chop the red onion. Scrape half
into a small bowl. Peel and dice the pineapple and add to the bowl
of onion. Roughly chop half the coriander (stalks and all) and add
this too. Zest and squeeze in the juice of 1 lime, season and set the
salsa aside.
Next, stir the hot sauce into the yoghurt and season. Very finely
shred the cabbage and scrape into a new bowl. Squeeze over the
juice of the other lime, season then scrunch together with your
hands – this will help it soften slightly.
Get a large frying pan over a high heat. Pour in the olive oil, then
tip in the turkey mince. Use the back of your spoon to break the
mince into smaller pieces, season, then add the remaining chopped
red onion. Fry, stirring occasionally, until the mince is cooked
through and browned, then stir through the fajita seasoning.
Meanwhile, heat the rice until piping hot, roughly chop the
remaining coriander and mix together. Slice the avocados.
Assembly time. Heat the tortillas, then add to the centre of each
the spiced turkey, coriander rice, red cabbage, pineapple salsa, avo,
hot sauce yoghurt and pickled jalapeños, if using. Fold over the
ends and roll up to seal. Cut in half and enjoy.

name: Loaded Veggie Quesadillas
description: The perfect dinner party dish. Cheesy. Veggie. Crunchy. The whole 9 yards.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Slice up your veg into chunks and whack them on a tray. Season with salt, pepper and olive oil. Roast for 40 minutes until cooked through and caramelised.
Remove veg from oven.
Get a frying pan on the heat and add some oil. Rub it around the pan with some kitchen roll so it is all covered.
Place a tortilla on the base. Add a heaped tsp of red pesto and spread it out. Grate over a large handful of cheddar and add a large spoon of the roasted veg.
Top with more grated cheddar and place another wrap on the top. Cook on a medium heat for 5 minutes until the bottom layer of cheddar has melted.

Flip the quesadilla by placing a plate on top of it and turning the pan over. Slide the quesadilla from the plate and put it back into the pan. Cook for another 5 minutes and remove from the heat when all the cheese has melted.
Repeat this 3 more times with your remaining veg and tortillas, carve up your quesadillas and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Loaded Wedge Salad with Blue Cheese & Chorizo
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad. 

This super simple salad comes together in minutes. Funky blue cheese and smokey chorizo work wonders with lettuce. A great speedy lunch or summer BBQ side. B x
keywords: loaded wedge salad with blue cheese and chorizo
instructions: Mix the yoghurt and blue cheese in a bowl, mash together with fork to break up any larger chunks of blue cheese. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper and add the zest and juice of 2 limes for a tangy, funky dressing.
Thinly slice the red onion and toss with a big pinch of salt and the juice from the remaining lime. Set aside for 10 minutes to quick pickle.
Cut your Iceberg into wedges. Be sure to cut through the root so the lettuce stays intact.
Dice up your chorizo and add to a medium frying pan. Set over a medium heat and cook until rendered and crispy. Save all of the oil!
Roughly chop your parsley.

Add the wedges of lettuce to a big serving plate and cover liberally with the blue cheese dressing. Add the pickled onions and the crispy chorizo. Drizzle over the chorizo oil and scatter with chopped parsley.
Get stuck in.

name: Loco Moco Hawaiian Smash Burger
description: Hawaiian comfort food at its finest. Smashed beef patty on rice with thick gravy and a crispy fried runny-yolk egg. Seriously one of the easiest simple midweek meals that you'll never get bored of.
keywords: Loco Moco Hawaiian Smash Burger & Gravy
instructions: Quarter the mushrooms and set aside. Finely chop the chives and set aside for garnish.

For the patties, finely dice the white onion then add to a large mixing bowl along with the other patty ingredients and a pinch of salt and black pepper. Using clean hands, mix until fully combined, squeezing the beef to tenderise it. Divide into round burger patties (one per person) and set aside.

For the gravy, melt the unsalted butter in a small saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the flour and mix to combine. Cook whilst stirring for 2-3 mins or until smelling toasty. Slowly pour the beef stock into the roux, a little at a time, stirring constantly until combined. Add the Worcestershire sauce, black pepper and light and dark soy sauces then cook, stirring constantly, for another 2-3 mins. Remove from the heat and set aside.

For the mushrooms, heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large frying pan set over a high heat. Add the mushrooms and fry for 2-3 mins until golden. Season with a pinch of salt then transfer to a plate and set aside.

For the patties, heat another generous glug of vegetable oil in the same pan set over a high heat. Add the beef patties and use a burger press or the base of a heavy saucepan to flatten the patties. Season with a pinch of salt and cook for 2 mins per side, then transfer to a plate and set aside.
For the eggs, heat a final glug of vegetable oil in the same pan, crack in the eggs and cook to your liking.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice. Finely chop the chives.
To serve, divide the rice between plates, top with a burger patty then pour over a ladle of gravy. Finish with the fried mushrooms, eggs, chopped chives and a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Long Island Iced Tea
description: Vodka, gin, white rum, triple sec and tequila. Need I say more?
instructions: Juice your lemon and save a slice for garnish.
Add your sugar and water to a pan, simmering until the two are mixed and form a simple syrup, let it cool.
Measure out your spirits and pour them all along with the simple syrup and lemon juice in a cocktail shaker with some ice.
Shake well.
Strain into a highball glass with ice and garnish with the lemon.
Enjoy.

name: Mac & Chickpeas
description: Sometimes pasta isn't always the answer. Our chickpea twist on this classic is packed with delicious squash, perfect for an evening where you want something indulgent but still a bit healthy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Soak the cashews or sunflower seeds in boiling water for 15 mins. Wash and chop the leeks into half-moons. Remove the rosemary needles and finely chop them. Dice the onion and crush the garlic. Set everything aside.

Deseed the squash, reserving the seeds. Score the fleshy part and roast in a roasting tin, cut-side down, for 20-30 mins or until the flesh begins to collapse. Rinse and dry the pumpkin seeds then roast them in oil and salt for 15-20 mins on a separate tray.

Meanwhile, fry the onion and leek in a frying pan for 10 mins over a medium heat in plenty of olive oil with a pinch of salt and a few big twists of black pepper. Stir occasionally – don’t let them burn.
Add all the ‘cheesy’ sauce ingredients to a bullet or blender, including the soaked nuts, then set aside, add a splash of water to loosen.

Put the garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika and nutmeg, plus more oil if needed, into the frying pan with the onion and leek. Fry for 3 mins. Dissolve the stock cube in water and deglaze. Add the chickpeas and turn the heat to low.

The squash should be done by now. When it’s cool enough, scoop out the soft flesh with a spoon and pop it into the same blender. Whizz until you get a silky smooth sauce and season with salt and pepper.

Pour the cheesy sauce over the chickpea mix. Mix in well and leave on a low heat whilst you whizz-up the bread in a clean, dry bullet cup or blender. Add the crumbs to a large bowl, along with 1½ tbsp olive oil, the garlic powder, ½ tsp salt and the rosemary. Toss well to combine and layer over the chickpeas in a thin crust. Roast in the oven or under the grill until golden and bubbly.

name: Macaroni Cheese
description: We're going back to basics with this simple but perfect mac and cheese.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, add the macaroni and cook for 1 min less than packet instructions. Drain the pasta, reserving a mug of the cooking water.
Whilst the pasta cooks, grate the cheddar cheese.

Melt the butter in a large, deep pan over a medium heat. Once melted, whisk in the flour to form a sandy paste. Cook this, whisking constantly, for 2-3 mins, until it starts to smell a little nutty. This is how you know the flour has cooked out and you can be sure your sauce won’t taste of raw flour.

Add the milk to the pan, a big splash at a time, whisking constantly and making sure it’s all absorbed into the paste. Doing it like this ensures you don’t get a lumpy cheese sauce. Keep adding until you’ve added all the milk, then add the cheese and whisk until it’s melted into a creamy, cheesy sauce. Add the mustard and season generously with salt and black pepper.

Remove the sauce from the heat, add the macaroni and a splash of the reserved pasta water. Stir together until all the pasta is coated with the cheese sauce. You want the sauce creamy, but just a little looser than you think, add more pasta water if you need to.

Spoon into a 25 - 30cm baking dish. Grate the parmesan over the top, then slide into the oven and bake for 25 mins, until golden and bubbling. If it's not browning enough, turn on the grill for the last 5 mins. Cool for a few mins before serving (so you don’t scald your mouth!).

name: Mackerel & Beetroot Lentil Bowl
description: Earthy beetroot, smoky mackerel, and creamy yoghurt over a warm bed of lentils and chickpeas. Quick, punchy, and packed with protein.
instructions: Peel and finely chop the red onion. Slice the broccoli stems and cut any larger florets in half.
Heat a small deep nonstick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion with a splash of water and cook for 8–10 mins until soft, adding a little more water if it starts to catch.
Add the broccoli stems and florets, lentils and chickpeas along with a splash of their liquid and gently simmer for 2–3 mins until warmed through.
Cut the beetroot into 1cm chunks. Flake the mackerel. Pick the dill leaves. Cut the lemon into wedges.
Spoon the lentils and chickpeas onto plates. Top with the beetroot, mackerel and broccoli. Finish with a dollop of yoghurt, a scattering of dill and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Mackerel Paté
description: This classic mackerel paté is perfect for festive canapés or starters. Or just spread it over toasted sourdough for a lovely lunch.
instructions: Peel off and discard the skin of the mackerel. Transfer the fish to a mixing bowl and use a fork to mash it until broken up.
Thinly slice the spring onions.
Combine all the ingredients in the mixing bowl with the mackerel, including the zest and juice of the lemon. Mix together and season to taste with salt, black pepper and more lemon juice if needed.
Serve with toast.

name: Mackerel, Petit Pois & Feta High Protein Smash
description: Here's a protein-packed recipe that you can 'smoosh' over a bagel, toast, pitta bread or whatever takes your fancy. It's a game-changer.
instructions: Boil your petit pois (or regular peas) for 1-2 mins. Roughly chop your mackerel and mint and juice your lemon.
Combine all of the ingredients in a bowl before ‘smooshing’ over toast, pitta bread, a bagel or whatever you fancy.
Enjoy!

name: Malaysian-Inspired Chana Dal Curry
description: A chana dal curry inspired by Malay cuisine – a melting pot of cultures and flavours. This is perfect with some freshly made roti or paratha.
instructions: Rinse and soak the chana dal in hot water for at least 3 hours.

Peel and roughly chop the onion. Peel the galagnal, garlic and trim the lemongrass. Add all of them into a food processor with the ground spices and pulse until a fine paste forms. Discard the tough stalks from the makrut lime leaves and thinly slice.

Place a saucepan on medium heat. Once hot, add half of the coconut milk and cook, stirring, until the oil separates and the coconut solids turn golden, 3-5 mins. Add the curry paste and toast for 2-3 mins. Then, add the drained chana dal, curry leaves, lime leaves and cook for 2-3 mins until fragrant. Stir through the remaining coconut milk and your water. Bring to the boil, turn the heat down to medium-low and simmer until the chana dal has softened and the oil has separated from the curry, 60-90 mins (the longer you've soaked it, the quicker it will cook). Stir the tamarind paste through and season with fish sauce. Top it up with water if the curry is looking too dry and thick – it should be quite loose.
Spoon the curry into bowls and mop up with some roti or paratha.

name: Malfatti (Ricotta Gnocchi)
description: These little ricotta dumplings come from Tuscany, they’re a bit like ravioli without the pasta. So simple and delicious. Jordon x
instructions: Gently crush your two cloves of garlic, then peel them.
Start by making a simple tomato sauce. In a saucepan, warm 3 tbsp of olive oil over a medium heat and add your garlic.
After a few minutes they should be lightly golden brown. Strip the leaves from the basil and add to the oil (be careful, it might spit!).
Stir and cook for 1 min, then add the chopped tomatoes and 1 tsp salt. Leave to simmer for about 15 mins until thickened. Taste again and add salt as needed.
Now the malfatti. First, wilt the spinach in a hot pan with a pinch of salt and a splash of water.
Drain the spinach and once cool, wring out as much liquid as possible (otherwise the mixture will be runny) then finely chop.
In a large mixing bowl combine the spinach, ricotta, parmesan, flour, egg, nutmeg, a tsp of salt and a good grind of black pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Line a tray with greaseproof paper and a dusting of flour.
Now take a spoon of the mixture and use your hands to roll it into a little ball, slightly smaller than a golf ball.
Pop them on the tray, then repeat with the remaining mix.
Cook the malfatti in plenty of boiling salted water. Once they all float to the surface, give them another minute, then drain.
Warm up the tomato sauce and make a little bed on the plate, then top with the malfatti. Add a grating of parmesan if you like.

name: Mallika Basu's Butter Chicken Curry
description: Mallika shows us how to make this classic Punjabi curry, served perfectly over Basmati rice.
instructions: Turn the grill on to high. Make the chicken tikka first. Chop the chicken into 2-3cm chunks and finely grate the ginger and garlic. Put into a bowl along with the rest of the tikka ingredients. Mix together.

Line a baking tray with foil and drizzle over some oil. Spread the chicken pieces onto it, then slide under the hot grill. Grill until fully cooked, and starting to char, 10-15 mins - every grill if different, so it may take a little less or more time.
Get your basmati rice on - cook according to packet instructions for the best results.

To make the curry, put the passata and sour cream into a heavy-based pan and stir well. Place over a low heat, adding the chilli powder and garam masala and finally the butter. As it starts bubbling, tip the chicken into the pan, along with their juices and the fenugreek leaves. If the curry starts splattering, loosely cover it with a lid.

Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes, or until you see the butter oozing through the curry and the colour deepens to a rich red. Add salt to your taste. Sprinkle with fresh coriander. Serve on a bed of steaming hot basmati rice.

name: Manchego & Green Olive Tortilla
description: A Mob twist to the Spanish classic - green olives and manchego work beautifully in this recipe. Also delicious eaten cold the next day.
instructions: Slice your onion into discs. Halve the discs, and then add to a frying pan with some olive oil. Fry until soft and slightly browned, and then remove from the pan and set aside.

Slice your potatoes into discs. Add them to the pan, and fry until soft and browned on each side. This takes roughly 5 minutes on each side on a medium heat. Once browned and softened, remove from heat and set aside.
Into a big bowl, crack your eggs. Add a cup of chopped green olives, a handful of chopped parsley, your cooked onions and potatoes, and a good sprinkle of salt and pepper. Whisk everything together.

Pour some oil into a large pan and place on a medium-low heat. Pour the tortilla mix into the pan. Crumble ¾ of the manchego on top. Cook for 15 minutes, occasionally running a spatula around the edge so it doesn’t stick.

After 15 minutes, remove pan from heat, and place a large plate on top of it. In one quick motion, flip the pan over, so the plate is now on the bottom. The tortilla should now be resting on the plate.
Place the pan back on the heat. Slide the tortilla off the plate and back into the pan, making sure you push all the bits of potato and onion under the tortilla as you do this.
Cook for 5 more minutes on a medium-low heat, and then remove the pan. Place the plate back on top, and flip again.
Grate over your last bit of manchego and add a small handful of parsley. The perfect breakfast. Enjoy.

name: Mandarin Scotch Bonnet Kosho
description: A fiery, citrussy scotch bonnet kosho that you can use to add a bit of heat to just about anything.
instructions: Start making the kosho three weeks before you want to eat it. First, rinse the jalapeños and scotch bonnets and leave them to air-dry on some kitchen paper.
Wash the mandarins and lemons in warm water, carefully rubbing any dirt off the skins. Leave on kitchen paper to air-dry.
Halve the jalapeños and scotch bonnets, remove the seeds and pith using a teaspoon, then cut them into tiny dice. Tip into a mixing bowl, sprinkle with ⅓ of fine sea salt and mix well.
Transfer everything to a sieve, then rest the sieve over a mixing bowl. Cover the chillies with a saucer. Leave at room temperature for 8 hours or overnight.
The next day, the chillies will have expelled about half their weight in water. Label and freeze the salty chilli liquid.

Clean your kitchen counter well, then wash an average-sized jam jar and lid, chopping board, large knife and tablespoon. I like to pour boiling water into the jar to make extra sure it’s free from nasties.

Using a citrus zester, zest all the citrus fruit onto a chopping board (don’t use a Microplane or grater). Squeeze the mandarin juice through a sieve and into a mixing bowl. Discard the seeds. Separate and freeze the mandarin juice.

Place the drained chillies on top of the citrus zest, then pour ⅔ of the salt on top. Mix the chilies, citrus zest and salt into each other. Fill the clean jar with the salty citrus and chilli mixture, pressing it down as you go to get rid of any air pockets – they are your enemy!

Clean around the inside rim of the jar with a piece of kitchen paper dipped in white vinegar, removing any stray solids. Close the jar, label it with the date and leave at room temperature for three weeks out of direct sunlight. After three weeks, transfer the jar to the fridge where it will keep happily for six months, ready for when you want to make the prawns.

Juice the zested lemons and mix with the remaining mandarin juice. This mixture is a tasty drink chilled as it is, or sweetened with 2 tbsp sugar and frozen into ice lollies. You could also mix with chopped fresh oregano and use it to cure fish. 
Keep the left-over salty chilli water and use it for salting sauces and giving them a little chilli kick. It will keep well in the kitchen for about five days.
 
The ferment will live happily in the fridge for about six months. It’s great on grilled courgette, in noodle soup, mixed with melted butter and spread over fish after steaming, or mixed with oil and used to marinate chicken breast before pan-frying.

name: Mandarin and Scotch Bonnet Kosho Prawns
description: These spicy prawns are super fresh and zingy. Make a big old platter of them and serve them  at your next pescatarian dinner party for a guaranteed good time.
keywords: mandarin and scotch bonnet kosho prawns
instructions: On the day you want to cook the prawns, take the frozen mandarin juice and spicy chilli liquid out of the freezer first thing in the morning and leave on the counter to defrost.
Wash, pat dry and finely chop the coriander. Butterfly and devein the prawns. Drizzle with enough of the salty chilli liquid to coat them all over, plus the rapeseed oil.
In a bowl, mix together the kosho with the mandarin juice and half the chopped coriander.

Cook the prawns on a smoking hot griddle pan starting flesh-side down for 1-2 mins. Turn over and spoon the mandarin-chilli-herb mixture onto the prawn flesh, cooking for a further 1-2 mins until just opaque and cooked through.
Transfer the prawns to a large serving platter and sprinkle with the remaining coriander. Eat straight away.

name: Mango Chutney Glazed Halloumi & Coconut Dal
description: Elevate your batch of Coconut Dal with sweet-spiced halloumi and hot naan. It's sweet, spiced, and super easy to make.
instructions: Make the Coconut Dal batch recipe.
Cut the halloumi into bite-sized chunks. Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the stems. Thinly slice the chilli and set it aside for garnish.
Set a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Fry the halloumi for 5–7 mins until golden on all sides. Turn the heat down, stir in the mango chutney and toss to coat. Tip onto a plate.
Pour the dal into the empty pan and stir through the coriander stems. Warm over a medium heat until piping hot, loosening with a splash of water if it’s thickened.
Warm the naan breads until soft and pliable.
Spoon the hot dal into bowls. Swirl in a dollop of yoghurt, pile the glazed halloumi on top and finish with the coriander leaves and sliced chilli. Serve with the warm naan for scooping.

name: Mango Harissa Fish & Minty Tomato Bowl
description: If you like mango, harissa, fish, and mint, you need look no further. This recipe is really easy to make and very, very tasty.
instructions: Pat the halibut dry and season with salt on all sides.
Thinly slice the shallot, halve the tomatoes and pick the mint leaves and discard the stems. Add everything to a bowl with the juice of the lime and a pinch of salt.

Make the salsa. Start by finely dicing the mango and adding it to a bowl with the harissa and the zest of half the lime. Stir together, squeeze in the juice from the remaining lime half, add a drizzle of olive oil, then season with salt. Set aside.
Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, place the fish into the pan and cook for 2-5 mins on each side until cooked through.
Meanwhile, heat the rice following pack instructions.
Share the rice between bowls, then top with the fish and tomato salad. Finish with a drizzle of mango harissa salsa.

name: Mango Pancakes
description: This is our riff on a viral pancake recipe that tastes just as good as it looks. And, boy, does it look good.
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl with the milk and whisk until combined. Add the flour and whisk until you have a smooth batter.

To cook, heat a nonstick pan over a medium heat and add a drop of oil. Spread the oil evenly with a pan, you can use kitchen paper to do this. Add a small ladle of pancake batter to the pan and rotate the pan until the pancake batter is covering the whole bottom of the pan easily.
Cook for about 40 seconds, then flip and cook for another 20-30 seconds. The aim here is for the pancake to be cooked with no colour.
Set the pancakes to one side and allow them to cool.
Meanwhile, make the cream filling. Place the double cream and icing sugar in a bowl and whisk until you have soft peaks.

To assemble, place one pancake on a plate. Put a couple of basil leaves in the middle. Peel your mango and take a good slice. Add this on top of the basil and then cover the mango with a generous amount of the whipped cream. Fold in each edge until you have a parcel.
Slice in half and enjoy!

name: Mango Sticky Rice Recipe
description: Here's a mango sticky rice recipe that everyone is going to go gaga for. It's the ultimate summer cooler.
instructions: Put the rice into a large mixing bowl, then add enough boiled water to cover the rice by 2½ cm. Leave to soak for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, make the salted coconut custard. Combine the cornflour and water in a small bowl. Mix until there are no lumps, then set aside.

Mix the can of coconut milk very well (so the fat and water are evenly combined), then pour half of it into a small pan. Bring to a simmer over a low heat, then add the sugar and ½ tsp salt. Mix the cornflour mixture with your finger (as it may have separated), then tip it into the sugary coconut milk. Keep mixing for 2-3 mins over a gentle simmer to thicken the mixture until it resembles a light custard. Set aside with cling film on the surface to prevent lumps from forming.

Drain the rice in a sieve and shake off any excess water. Grab a damp tea towel or muslin cloth and place directly onto a steamer. Tip the rice into the cloth in a doughnut shape with a hole in the centre, then cover the rice with the cloth. Make sure to leave a gap all around the towel and the basket to let steam through. If you don't have a steamer rack, then place the cloth on a sieve that will fit a pot, with a tight fitting lid. Fill the pot around halfway with water, making sure not to touch the basket/sieve. Add a tight fitting lid and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low-medium and cook for 20 mins.

Meanwhile, make the coconut syrup. Combine the remaining coconut milk, sugar and 1 tsp salt in a small pot. If you have a pandan leaf, tie it into a knot and add for extra aroma. Cook over a medium heat just until it bubbles, then turn off the heat and set aside. The syrup will need to be reheated when the rice is cooked.

When the rice is ready, heat the coconut syrup just until bubbling, then turn off the heat. Carefully remove the rice – it will be steaming hot. Add the rice to a mixing bowl and quickly pour over the hot coconut syrup. Gently mix to coat each grain, then cover with a lid, plate, or cling film and leave for 20 mins.
After 20 mins, fold the bottom part of the rice up to the top to mix evenly. Leave it to sit for another 20 mins (or until needed, as it will keep at room temp all day).

When you are ready to serve, lightly grind the toasted sesame seeds and have the roasted peanuts ready, if using. Peel and slice the mangos into big chunks (you want to do this fresh, to prevent the mango from browning) and serve on plates with a few scoops of sticky rice. Pour over the custard and sprinkle over the sesame seeds and peanuts.
If you prefer a warm custard, you can also warm this just before serving!

name: Mango, Chilli & Lime Dressing
description: Fresh, fruity and gently spicy, this mango dressing is filled with lime and chilli for a zingy finish that will liven up any salad.
instructions: Zest the lime and then cut it in half ready for juicing. Deseed and finely chop the chilli (if you fancy a bit more spice an extra chilli).
Roughly chop the mango and add it to a high-speed blender with the lime juice, cumin, olive oil and water. Blitz until smooth, then taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Stir through the chopped chilli and lime zest and you're done!

name: Mango-Glazed Meatballs & Garlicky Greens
description: Sometimes you just want a pile of garlicky greens for dinner, and that's exactly what inspired this. Juicy mango chutney glazed meatballs, loads of good-for-you veg and fragrant cumin yoghurt for a little creaminess. It makes great leftovers and you can even freeze the meatballs too.
keywords: Mango Chutney Meatballs on Creamy Cumin Yoghurt
Mango Chutney Meatballs on Creamy Cumin Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Coarsely grate the onion into a large bowl. Add half the cumin seeds and season generously with salt and pepper. Add the pork mince and mix thoroughly, then roll into 20 meatballs. Set aside.
Lightly crush the remaining cumin seeds and stir into the yoghurt. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the crushed garlic and let it infuse for a minute, then add the tenderstem broccoli, green beans and kale and cook for 3–4 mins until wilted and bright green. Transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm.

In the same pan, add another drizzle of olive oil and cook the meatballs for 8–10 mins, turning regularly, until golden all over and cooked through. Spoon in the mango chutney with a splash of water and toss to glaze.
Spread the yoghurt across the base of each plate. Top with the greens and meatballs, and finish with a squeeze of lime.
If prepping ahead, pile the greens into a container, top with the meatballs and bring the yoghurt on the side.

name: Maple Bacon, Egg & Cheese Bagels
description: Loaded with gooey cheese, soft-set eggs, and sticky maple bacon, these make-ahead breakfast bagels deliver big flavour with zero fuss. Exactly what you need after a big one.
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk together with the salt. Slice the bagels in half, spread the cream cheese onto the cut sides.

Place a frying pan over medium heat. Add the bacon rashers in and fry for 6-8 mins until crisp. Take it off the heat and drizzle over the maple syrup and toss to coat. Break the bacon into shards, then tip onto a plate to cool down.

Return the pan to a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add a ladle full of the whisked egg and swirl it around so it covers the bottom of the pan. Sprinkle some maple bacon on top and place both bagel halves, cream cheese side down, onto the eggs.

Once the eggs are cooked, place a plate over the pan and flip everything out. Fold any overhanging egg in, and top one bagel half with 2 cheese slices. Drizzle over any maple bacon sauce and sandwich them together.
Wrap the bagels in foil, and let the cheese melt for a couple of minutes before tucking in.

If you're making these ahead of time, let them cool completely and then wrap and freeze. Unwrap and defrost the bagels in the microwave or overnight in the fridge, then reheat in a 180°C oven for 8-15 mins, until hot throughout.

name: Maple Black Pepper Pork Belly with Creamy Potato Salad
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This is our riff on honey mustard ham. Sweet, sticky pork belly glazed with maple syrup, fiery black pepper and wholegrain mustard. A killer Sunday lunch.
keywords: maple black pepper pork belly recipes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper and lay out the pork belly slices on top. Season with salt and pepper and bake for 30-35 mins until crispy and golden brown, flipping halfway through.
Meanwhile, add the maple syrup, 2 tbsp vinegar and black pepper to a small saucepan and bring to a boil, cook for 2-3 mins until slightly reduced.
Add the salad potatoes to a medium saucepan and cover with cold water. Season with salt and bring to a bare simmer. Cook for 13-15 mins until tender. Drain and allow to steam dry.
Mix the wholegrain mustard with the mayo and remaining vinegar.
Cut the apple into matchsticks and finely slice the spring onions and celery.
Mix the mustard mayo through the cooked potatoes with the spring onions, apple and celery.
Roughly chop the parsley and add to the potato salad.
After the pork has had 35 mins, brush with the maple glaze and pop back in the oven for 5-10 mins, brushing with more glaze now and then, until golden and caramelised.
Divide the salad between warm plates and top with a couple of slices of pork, drizzle over any extra glaze and get stuck in.

name: Maple Peanut Paprika BBQ Ribs
description: Learning how to barbecue ribs is a fine art. In this BBQ ribs recipe, we'll show you how to get the juiciest ribs around. The maple glaze? Out of bounds.
keywords: Maple Peanut Paprika BBQ Ribs recipe
instructions: Remove the membrane from the pork ribs – it’s on the cupped side of the rack and looks like a thin, white film. You can whip it off by peeling it away from the bones, using a piece of kitchen paper to help you grip. Once removed, dump the racks into a large pot and cover with cold water.

Bring to the boil and let boil for 1-2 mins. Remove the racks, tip out the water and replace with fresh cold water. Add a good handful of salt, return the racks to the pot and set over a medium heat. Once simmering, bubble away for 45-55 mins.
Meanwhile, mix the glaze ingredients together in a small bowl with a pinch of salt, then set aside.
For the peanut crunch, roughly chop the peanuts and finely chop the coriander, then transfer both to a bowl with a big pinch of salt, the sesame seeds and sugar. Set aside.
Pile coals over to one side of your BBQ to create a hot, direct cooking side, and a warm, indirect cooking side.

Once cooked, remove the ribs and place on a rack. They’ll look a bit grey and sad right now, but have faith. Add to the hot side of the grill and cook, turning now and then, for 5-6 mins until starting to brown and crisp nicely.
Take a brush and start painting the ribs with the glaze as they cook. Flip and let the glaze caramelise and bake onto the ribs. Keep painting more onto the ribs as they cook.
Once super shiny and glazed, whip the ribs off and give them one more baste with the sauce. When nice and sticky, add a handful of the peanut mixture. Cut into ribs and serve.

name: Maple-Glazed Heirloom Carrots with Pomegranate Molasses
description: These sticky, sweet, gently-spiced carrots will look beautiful on your table.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. Peel and trim the carrots. Chop the fresh parsley.
Toss the carrots with olive oil, maple syrup, pomegranate molasses, ground cumin, salt, and pepper.
Spread the carrots in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 mins, turning occasionally, until tender and caramelised.
Arrange the carrots on a serving platter, drizzle with extra pomegranate molasses, and garnish with pomegranate seeds and parsley.

name: Mapo Tofu
description: Spicy, numbing and aromatic, this Sichuan classic will soon become one of your weeknight favourites. Served best with a bowl of Tilda Long Grain Rice.
instructions: Finely slice your spring onions, separating the whites to the greens. Mince your ginger and garlic.
Grind your Sichuan peppercorns in a pestle and mortar.
Cut your tofu into small cubes. Bring a pot of salted water to boil, add your tofu then bring to a simmer for 2 mins, then set aside (make sure it doesn’t fall apart).
Add 2 tbsps of veg oil into your wok then add your ground peppercorns. Fry for 30 seconds until crispy then set aside.

In the same wok, add your pork mince, sugar, chilli bean sauce and Sichuan peppercorns. Fry for a few mins until the colour of the meat darkens. Then add your garlic, ginger, the whites of the spring onions, shaoxing wine, soy sauce and chicken stock. Bring to a boil for 10 mins.
Then, mix your cornstarch with 100ml water and add to your wok and give it a good stir.
Add chilli oil, spring onion greens and sesame oil and give it a good mix. Then gently add in your tofu and bring, put a lid on and bring to simmer for 3 mins.
Plate up and serve with your fluffy rice.

name: Marbella Cod Parcels with Crushed Lemon Potatoes
description: One paper parcel does all the work here. The harissa, green olives and cherry tomatoes steam together with the fish, so every last juice ends up as the sauce. Minimal washing up too so it's a result on a weeknight.
keywords: Marbella Fish en Papillote with Crushed Lemon Potatoes
Marbella Fish en Papillote with Crushed Lemon Potatoes recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Halve the cherry tomatoes, drain and roughly chop the sun-dried tomatoes and halve the olives. Slice most of the lemon for the fish into rounds.

Cut 4 large sheets of baking paper. Divide the cherry tomatoes, sun-dried tomatoes and olives between them, then top each with a cod fillet and a few lemon slices. Any white fish works here, haddock or pollock are both great. Mix the harissa with the juice of the remaining lemon for the fish and spoon over the fish. Season with salt and black pepper, then fold the paper over and crimp the edges tightly to make sealed parcels.
Place the parcels on a baking tray and bake for 12-15 mins, depending on the thickness of the fish, until cooked through.
Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of well-salted water to the boil and cook the new potatoes for 15-20 mins, until tender. Finely chop the parsley, then zest and juice the lemon for the potatoes.
Drain the potatoes, then lightly crush with the olive oil, parsley, lemon zest and juice. Season well with salt and black pepper.
Serve the parcels with the crushed lemon potatoes alongside, opening them at the table so all the tomato, olive and harissa juices stay trapped around the fish.

name: Margarita Pitcher
description: The classics are the classics for a reason. This Margarita pitcher is zippy, refreshing, and perfect for sharing with your friends on a hot day.
instructions: Halve your limes and squeeze out the juice.
Add lime juice to a jug halfway filled with ice.
Add tequila, Cointreau and a bit of agave syrup (if you like it sweet). Give it a stir then top it off with Mexican lime soda.
Rub your glass rims with lime and garnish the rims with salt. Pour your pitcher into your glasses, garnish with lime wedges, and enjoy.

name: Marie Rose Sauce
description: An absolute classic. Making your own marie rose sauce couldn’t be easier. Use it in a prawn cocktail or to level up your sandwiches.
instructions: Add all the ingredients into a bowl and stir together. Season to taste with black pepper and cayenne powder.
Use the marie rose sauce to make a prawn cocktail.

name: Marinated Halloumi Summer Bowl with Spicy Pico De Gallo
description: Treat yourself to marinated halloumi on a bed of brown rice, with a creamy herby dressing, spoonful of pico de gallo and a sprinkling of pumpkin seeds.
instructions: Place a saucepan full of water to the boil. Chop the halloumi into 2cm chunks and finely chop half the parsley. Place a frying pan on a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the halloumi and cook until golden on all sides, 5-7 mins. Transfer to a bowl, with the zest of half a lemon, chopped parsley, plenty of freshly cracked black pepper and 20ml of olive oil, set aside to marinate.

Once the water is boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook until very soft, 5 mins. Drain and run under cold water until cool to the touch. Remove the shell and place the eggs into a blender with the remaining parsley, zest of 1 lemon and 20ml of olive oil. Blend until smooth, season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Add a spoonful of water to loosen.

Meanwhile, finely dice onion, drain and thinly slice the peppers. Drain and rinse the black beans. Add 2 tbsp of onion into a small bowl, set aside. Tip the rest of the onion into a large bowl with the peppers, beans and lentils.
Dice the tomatoes, mince the jalapeños, and finely chop the coriander. Add into the small bowl with the onions, season with salt, pepper, lemon juice and 2 tbsp of olive oil.
Cook the rice according to package instructions and tip into the peppers.
Share the rice between bowls, top with the marinated halloumi, a drizzle of creamy dressing, a spoonful of pico de gallo and some pumpkin seeds.

name: Marinated Lentils & Charred Tenderstem with Jammy Eggs
description: Jammy soft-boiled eggs, miso and roasted red pepper marinated lentils, charred Tenderstem and a big dollop of Greek yoghurt. It's the kind of vegetarian meal that just makes you feel good.
keywords: Marinated Lentils & Charred Tenderstem with Jammy Eggs
Marinated Lentils & Charred Tenderstem with Jammy Eggs recipe
instructions: Finely chop the roasted red peppers. In a large bowl, whisk together the miso paste, red wine vinegar, olive oil, honey and chilli flakes. Grate in the garlic, then add 50ml of the liquid from the roasted red pepper jar along with the chopped peppers and season with salt and black pepper. Tip in the lentils (drained if needed) and mix until well combined. Set aside.
Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and cook for 6 mins 30 seconds. Transfer to a bowl of cold water to stop the cooking, then peel and set aside.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil and the Tenderstem broccoli, season with salt and cook for 5 mins, turning occasionally, until charred all over and tender.

To serve, spoon a generous dollop of Greek yoghurt onto each plate. Pile on the marinated lentils and lay the Tenderstem alongside. Halve the eggs and place on top. Finish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a grind of black pepper.

name: Marinated Tofu Summer Bowl With Spicy Pico De Gallo
description: Treat yourself to marinated tofu on a bed of brown rice, with a creamy herby dressing, spoonful of pico de gallo and a sprinkling of pumpkin seeds.
instructions: Chop the tofu into 2cm chunks. Place a non-stick frying pan on medium-high heat with 5 tbsp of oil. Once hot, add the tofu and cook until golden on all sides, 5-7 mins. Transfer to a bowl, with the zest of half a lemon and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper, set aside.

Add the parsley into a blender with 80ml of olive oil. Blend until smooth. Pour ⅓ of the mixture onto the tofu, mix. Season the remainder of the parsley oil with salt, pepper and lemon juice - this is the dressing.

Finely dice onion, drain and thinly slice the peppers. Drain and rinse the black beans. Add 2 tbsp of onion into a small bowl, set aside. Tip the rest of the onion into a large bowl with the peppers, beans and lentils.
Dice the tomatoes, mince the jalapeños, and finely chop the coriander. Add into the small bowl with the onions, season with salt, pepper, lemon juice and 2 tbsp of olive oil.
Cook the rice according to package instructions and tip into the peppers.
Share the rice between bowls, top with the marinated tofu, a drizzle of zingy parsley dressing, a spoonful of pico de gallo and some pumpkin seeds.

name: Marinated Tomato and Ricotta Casarecce
description: A pasta dish fit for a heatwave. The only thing that needs cooking? The pasta. Tossed with juicy tomatoes and creamy ricotta, this one is a winner.
instructions: Finely chop your tomatoes, then add them to a bowl. Grate in your garlic clove and lemon zest, then add the juice of ½ your lemon, 2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Leave them to sit at room temperature.
Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Salt it well.
Pour your pasta into your water and cook it until al dente.
Meanwhile, finely chop your dill.
Add your ricotta to a bowl along with 2 tbsp olive oil and then grate in your parmesan. Give it a good whisk until it is totally smooth.
When your pasta is cooked, add a ladle of your pasta water to the ricotta mix, and whisk until it comes together.
Drain your pasta, then combine with your ricotta, tomatoes and herbs. Give it a good mix.
Spoon into bowls and finish with some more fresh herbs and some black pepper. Serve and enjoy!

name: Marinated Tomato and Ricotta Pasta Salad
description: A pasta salad fit for a heatwave. Tossed with juicy tomatoes and creamy ricotta, this one is a packed lunch winner.
instructions: Finely chop your tomatoes, then add them to a bowl. Grate in your garlic clove and lemon zest, then add the juice of ½ your lemon, 2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Leave them to sit at room temperature.
Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Salt it well.
Pour your pasta into your water and cook it until al dente.
Meanwhile, finely chop your dill.
Add your ricotta to a bowl along with 2 tbsp olive oil and then grate in your parmesan. Give it a good whisk until it is totally smooth.
When your pasta is cooked, add a ladle of your pasta water to the ricotta mix, and whisk until it comes together.
Drain your pasta, then combine with your ricotta, tomatoes and herbs. Give it a good mix.

Divide between your Tupperware containers and top with a crack of black pepper in each. Once they've cooled a bit, box up and pop in the fridge.
These will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Marinated Za'atar Beetroot, Feta & Minty Grains
description: Earthy beetroot marinated in za’atar and balsamic, paired with creamy cumin-spiked beetroot sauce, fresh mint, tangy feta and herby grains. It’s vibrant, punchy, and perfect for a speedy lunch.
instructions: Dice ¾ of the beetroot into small chunks and toss in a bowl with the za’atar, two thirds of the balsamic vinegar, a splash of olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Set aside to marinate.

Roughly chop the remaining beetroot and add to a blender with the crème fraîche, remaining balsamic, the garlic clove, cumin, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Blitz until completely smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Finely slice the roasted red peppers and set aside. Chop the mint finely, reserving a little for garnish.
Warm the grain pouches in the microwave according to the pack instructions, then tip into a large bowl. Stir through the red peppers, most of the mint, and a little lemon zest. Taste and season.

Spread a spoonful of the beetroot sauce on each plate. Top with a handful of lamb’s lettuce, a pile of the minty grains, spoonfuls of marinated beetroot, and crumbled feta. Finish with extra mint and a final drizzle of olive oil, if you fancy.

name: Marmite Beef Ragù With Pappardelle
description: Marmite is your new secret weapon in the world of slow cooking beef. Start with this and get creative. No Marmite? Bovril is grand.
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cut the beef into 4cm chunks. Once the oil is hot, add the beef and cook for 2 mins on each side until well browned. Remove and set aside on a plate.

In a food processor or mini chopper, blitz the onion, celery, and carrot together to make a rough paste. Add the remaining tbsp of olive oil to a large saucepan over a medium-low heat and add the rough paste with a big pinch of salt, fry for around 10 mins, until totally soft, then finely grate the garlic into the pan along with the tomato purée and dried oregano. Cook for 2-3 mins further.

Turn up the heat, add the white wine and bubble down by half, add the stock and plum tomatoes and bring to a boil. Then turn the heat down and add the beef back to the pan. Pour in the milk, and cover with a lid. You can now either leave on the lowest heat on the hob and simmer for 3-4 hours (it needs to be very lightly bubbling) or, if your pan is ovenproof, heat your oven to 140°C, slide the pan in, and cook for 3-4 hours.
Remove the cheeks or chunks of steak and use two forks to shred.
Add the Marmite to the sauce, turn the heat up and bubble for 5-10 mins, until slightly thickened, then return the meat to the pan. Taste and season.

When ready to cook it, bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and add the pappardelle. Cook for a minute less than package instructions then use tongs to move the pasta into the sauce, bringing a little pasta water with it.
Toss well, then twirl into bowls and top with Parmesan and basil leaves.

name: Marmite Butter Beans with Butternut Squash, Soft Eggs & Cottage Cheese
description: Creamy Marmite beans with tender squash, soft eggs, and cottage cheese. Cosy, savoury, and packed with umami.
instructions: Peel the butternut squash and cut into 2cm chunks. Add to a large nonstick deep frying pan with water over a medium heat. Simmer, covered, for 15 mins, topping up with splashes of water if needed, until the squash is nearly tender but still has a bit of bite.
Strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and tear into large pieces. Add to the pan for the final 5 mins of squash cooking time, so it softens but stays vibrant.
Meanwhile, bring a pan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and boil for 7 mins for soft centres. Run them under cold water until cool enough to handle, then peel and set aside.
Tip the butter beans (with their liquid) into the pan. Simmer, covered, for another 5 mins until the squash is very tender.
Add the Marmite to the pan and gently stir it through. Grate in half the Parmesan and stir to melt.
Spoon the beans into bowls. Halve the eggs and place on top. Add dollops of cottage cheese and finish with the rest of the Parmesan. Season with black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil, if you like.

name: Marmite Chicken
description: Marmite is a brilliant ingredient to use in a sauce. Savoury, umami heaven. The vinegar and spring onion cuts through the richness. A lovely little mouthful.
instructions: Cook the rice following pack instructions.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken into bite-sized chunks. Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Half fill a separate bowl with cornflour.
Coat each piece of chicken by dipping it first in the cornflour, then the egg, then back in the cornflour.
Heat a wok over a medium-high heat with a good splash of vegetable oil. Fry the chicken in batches for 4 mins, until golden and crisp. Set aside.

Drain the wok and give it a wash. Dry it off, then place it back on the heat with a small splash of vegetable oil. Grate in the garlic and fry for 20 secs until fragrant. Stir in the soy sauce, vinegar, honey, Marmite and water. Bring to the boil and cook for 5 mins, skimming off any scum.

For the cornflour slurry, mix together the cornflour and water in a small bowl or mug. Stir it into the sauce and let everything bubble away until nicely thickened. Return the chicken to the wok, stir to coat and continue to cook for 3 mins over a medium heat. Meanwhile, thinly slice the spring onions.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls and top with the chicken. Pour over any extra sauce and finish with the spring onions.

name: Marry Me Chicken Pasta Bake
description: Creamy, spicy, cheesy and beyond delicious. This meal prep pasta bake brings heat and comfort in equal measure.
keywords: Marry Me Chicken Pasta Bake recipe
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the pasta and cook until al dente, following pack instructions. Scoop out a mug of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Meanwhile, slice the cherry tomatoes in half and tear the basil leaves.

Add the cottage cheese, sundried tomato paste, gochujang and garlic powder to a blender along with a splash of the reserved pasta water. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add more water as needed to loosen.

Tip the drained pasta into a large bowl along with the cooked chicken, halved cherry tomatoes and basil. Pour over the sauce and stir everything together until well coated. Add more pasta water if it looks a bit dry.

Transfer the pasta to an ovenproof dish, grate the Parmesan over the top and place under a hot grill for 5–10 mins until golden and bubbling on top. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch – they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Marry Me Chicken Pasta Bake
description: Creamy, spicy, cheesy and beyond delicious. This pasta bake brings heat and comfort in equal measure.
keywords: Marry Me Chicken Pasta Bake recipe
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the pasta and cook until al dente, following pack instructions. Scoop out a mug of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Meanwhile, slice the cherry tomatoes in half and tear the basil leaves.

Add the cottage cheese, sundried tomato paste, gochujang and garlic powder to a blender along with a splash of the reserved pasta water. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add more water as needed to loosen.

Tip the drained pasta into a large bowl along with the cooked chicken, halved cherry tomatoes and basil. Pour over the sauce and stir everything together until well coated. Add more pasta water if it looks a bit dry.
Transfer the pasta to an ovenproof dish, grate the Parmesan over the top and place under a hot grill for 5–10 mins until golden and bubbling on top.

name: Marry Me Halloumi Bowl
description: A zippy and satisfying bowl featuring golden halloumi, smoky bulgur, and a tangy tomato yoghurt dressing. Packed with fresh herbs, crunchy seeds, and pomegranate molasses, this dish is perfect for a balanced and flavourful meal.
instructions: Heat a large saucepan over medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil, then stir in the bulgur wheat. Fry for 2 mins until golden. Add the smoked paprika and cook for another 30 seconds. Cover with boiling water until 2cm above the bulgur, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15 mins.
Make the tomato yoghurt dressing by blending the Greek yoghurt, sun-dried tomatoes, and lemon juice until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

Cut the halloumi into small 2cm-sized pieces. Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the halloumi pieces and cook on all sides until golden and charred. Pour in the pomegranate molasses and let it bubble and thicken, coating the halloumi.
Assemble the bowl: toss the sliced cherry tomatoes and most of the torn basil through the cooked bulgur wheat. Season with salt and black pepper.
Divide the bulgur into serving boxes. Top with the glazed halloumi, tomato yoghurt dressing, and mixed seeds. Garnish with the remaining basil leaves.
Refrigerate until needed. No need to reheat before serving.

name: Masabacha Bowl
description: An alternative to all of the usual hummus bowls we see on the internet, let us introduce you to masabacha (also known as musabaha and msabbaha). It's rich, creamy, and super satiating.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and add the Tenderstem to a baking tray then drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper. Roast for 15 min, until tender and charred.

In the meantime, heat oil in a small saucepan. Once hot, add the sunflower seeds and cook for 3-5 mins, until golden. Pour everything into a small bowl and add the smoked paprika and cumin seeds. Season lightly with salt.
Slice the fennel finely, then toss with the lemon juice and chilli flakes. Finely chop the parsley.

Tip the chickpeas and their juice into a saucepan, heating them gently. Take off the heat and add tahini, grated garlic, and the rest of the lemon juice. Give it a good mix, then mash with a masher or fork until smooth-ish, season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the warmed chickpeas into shallow bowls and add the fennel salad and broccoli. Drizzle with the sunflower seed oil and scatter with parsley. Serve with flatbreads.

name: Masala Fried Eggs & Cheese Toast
description: Fry your eggs in curry paste, throw it on some buttered bread with a load of cheddar and enjoy our take on this iconic street food.
keywords: Masala Fried Eggs & Cheese Toast recipe
instructions: Grate cheddar and mix with sliced chilli and coriander set aside.
Dice onion, tomato and a big handful of coriander and set aside.

Grab a medium-sized pan and get it on a medium heat. Slice your bun in half and butter the bread on both sides. Toast the bun halves, butter-side down, until lightly golden. Flip the bun halves and add the grated cheese on top. Cover with a lid and allow to melt 1-2 mins before removing and setting aside on a different pan. Make sure the pan is not too hot or it will burn the bread.

Into the same pan you fried your bread, add a tbsp of neutral oil. Add in your onion and cook for 2 mins. Add diced tomato and curry paste and cook for 1 min then a big handful of chopped coriander and toss for an extra minute. Make two wells and crack your eggs on top. Let the aromatics create a crust on the whites and fry until the eggs have set.
Place eggs on top of your cheesy toast. Add fresh chilli, coriander and a squeeze of lime.

name: Masala Fries
description: Crispy fries tossed in a spicy masala sauce topped with yoghurt, fresh coriander and quick-pickled onions. They’re insanely delicious!
instructions: Heat your oven to 220°C.
Thinly slice one of the red onions and place in a small bowl. Add the juice of the lemon, season with a good pinch of salt and scrunch with your hand to quick pickle.
Arrange the Strong Roots Crispy Skinny Fries in a single layer in a large baking tray. Cook according to the package instructions.
Finely chop the other red onion, garlic and ginger.
Heat a generous splash of vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the finely chopped red onion, season with salt and cook until caramelised and starting to brown.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 min then add the garam masala, cumin, coriander, chilli powder and turmeric and cook for 30 seconds. Precise, I know, but ground spices burn quickly!
Add the passata and brown sugar and cook for 5 mins, or until slightly thickened. Set aside.
Roughly chop the coriander.
Place the Strong Roots Crispy Skinny Fries in a large bowl. Add the spicy masala sauce and toss well to coat.
Transfer to a platter and top with the chopped coriander, some quick-pickled onions and a few dollops of yoghurt. Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Masala Frittata and Kachumber Salad
description: This fresh and spicy frittata using British lion eggs is going to be your new favourite brunch dish.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Finely slice 1 1/2 red onions and the coriander stems. Set your coriander leaves to one side.

Place a large, non-stick, ovenproof frying pan over a medium heat. Pour in a good glug of oil and tip in the sliced onion along with a pinch of salt. Stir occasionally for around 6 minutes, or until softened.
Meanwhile crack the British Lion eggs into a bowl and whisk them together. Season the egg mixture generously with salt and black pepper.
Add the coriander stems, turmeric, garam masala and 1 tsp chilli powder to the pan. Stir for one minute until fragrant and then add in the spinach along with half of the cherry tomatoes.

Once the spinach has mostly wilted, pour in the whisked British Lion egg mixture. Leave the frittata to fry for a minute or so until the egg around the side of the pan has begun to set. Once set, transfer to the oven for 10 minutes.

Kachumber time. Finely chop the remaining red onion, halve the remaining cherry tomatoes, chop the cucumber and the coriander leaves. Place in a bowl. Add the zest and juice of the lemon followed by the remaining chilli powder. Mix, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Remove the frittata from the oven. Serve topped with mango chutney, yoghurt and kachumber salad.

name: Masala Haldi Doodh
description: Curl up with a steaming mug of this golden milk, with throat-soothing honey, immune-boosting turmeric and warming spices. An Indian home remedy to help you fight off a cold.
instructions: Lightly crush the peppercorns, bash the fresh turmeric and ginger and split the cardamom pods open.

Add all the ingredients to a saucepan, adding the honey to taste, and set it over a medium heat. Bring to the boil then turn the heat down to low, place a lid on and leave to gently infuse for 10 mins.
Strain and drink straight away.

name: Mascarpone & Red Pesto Stuffed Chicken Breasts
description: A really simple, clean dish. Stuffed chicken breasts taken to a new level.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Chuck all of your spinach in a pan and wilt it. Remove from the heat. Place the wilted spinach in a sieve and squeeze out the water.
Put the spinach in a bowl. Add red pesto and mascarpone. Season with salt and pepper and mush everything together.
In another bowl, add oregano, the zest of a lemon, salt and pepper. (This will be the rub to go on the outside of the breasts). Mix it together and set aside.
Chicken Time. Take each chicken breast and cut a hole in the thicker side of the breast. Use your fingers to prod away until you have made a cavity inside the breast.
Spoon in your filling to each chicken breast. You want them to be really filled up. Once you have done this to all the chicken, roll them in the oregano and lemon zest rub.
Get a pan on a medium heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil and then add your chicken. Cook for 4 minutes on each side so they are nicely browned and caramelised.
Place the pan in the oven for 12 minutes, until cooked through.
Add the bulgur wheat to a pan of boiling water and crumble in a chicken stock cube for extra flavour. Cook according to pack instructions.
Serve the breasts on the steaming hot bulgur wheat with some lemon juice squeezed over the top. Enjoy!

name: Matcha Tea Gin Sour
description: This mean, green cocktail might look like those juices you get at the gym but it's actually a delicious cocktail. This Matcha tea gin sour is set to impress.
instructions: First off, put your matcha whisk in a small glass of hot water. This will allow the bamboo to soak up the hot water and spread out its whisky bits more, meaning you’ll get a frothier matcha when it comes to whisking.
Pour your sugar and water into a pan and gently heat until the sugar dissolves. This is your sugar syrup.
Juice the lemon and separate the egg white from the yolk.
Add your matcha powder to a bowl along with your hot water and gently whisk side to side. Make sure you whisk side to side and not in circles to ensure the foamiest matcha.
Add your lemon juice, sugar syrup, gin, egg white and matcha to a cocktail shaker and give a dry shake.
Now add your ice to the shaker and give it a wet shake for 20 seconds.
Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass and dust with a small amount of matcha powder for garnish, then sip away.

name: Mayonnaise
description: Mayo is one of those things people buy loads of but rarely make because of how ‘hard’ it seems. Turns out: it's super easy.
instructions: Add all the ingredients into a jar or bowl.
Place a stick blender into the bottom of the bowl and blend until smooth and emulsified.
Taste and season with salt.

name: Meatball & Courgette Kebabs With Fennel & Pumpkin Seed Slaw
description: Juicy and flavourful kebabs on a bed of mustardy and tangy crème fraîche served with fresh and zingy fennel slaw. Easy does it.
keywords: Meatball & Courgette Kebabs With Fennel & Pumpkin Seed Slaw
instructions: If using skewers, soak them in water while you prep everything else.

Squeeze the sausage meat out from their casings into a bowl. Finely grate the garlic directly into the bowl, add the dried oregano and season generously, use your hands to mix well. Roll into golf ball-sized balls, the mixture should make approx. 20 meatballs. Set aside on a plate in the fridge to firm up.

Now, make the slaw: shave the fennel as finely as you can into a bowl. Add the lemon zest and juice along with 1 tbsp of olive oil, toss and use your hands to massage the lemon juice into the fennel. Roughly chop the parsley and toss into the slaw. Finally, add the toasted pumpkin seeds along with a big pinch of salt and pepper, set aside.
Trim and chop the courgette into 2cm discs, add to a bowl with 2 tbsp olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss well.

Heat the grill to its highest setting. Take each kebab skewer and thread on the pork meatballs and courgettes, alternating between the two until you have 3 meatballs and 3 pieces of courgette on each skewer. Line up on an oiled baking tray. Slide under the grill for 10 mins, turning halfway, until the meatballs are browned and cooked through and the courgettes are charred.
Whisk the mustard into the crème fraîche, season with salt and pepper and spread over plates or a platter. Top with the kebabs, serve the fennel slaw and flatbreads alongside.

name: Meatball Gnocchi Bake
description: Nothing subtle about this dish. Just a massive bowl of delicious warming gnocchi with meatballs in it. Superb fuel for a winter's night. Get on it.
instructions: Soak the fresh breadcrumbs in the cream and set aside.
Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic. Fry in a pan on a medium-low heat with a drizzle of olive oil.
While it is frying, slice up the stalks of the parsley and add to the pan, mixing everything together until the ingredients have softened. Take off the heat.
In a separate bowl place your minced beef. De-case the sausages, pushing the meat out of the sausage into the bowl and discarding the skins.
Add the fried onion, garlic and parsley into the mix. Add your soaked white breadcrumbs to the bowl. Begin to mix everything together.
Once mixed, create small meatballs, placing on a chopping board or tray. Cover and leave to rest in the fridge for 20 minutes.

After 20 mins, remove the meatballs from the fridge and begin to cook the meatballs in a large deep frying pan on a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Gently turn the meatballs, letting them gain shape as they cook.
Once they have browned off, add 2 tins of tomatoes to allow the meatballs to cook through.
Add the gnocchi to the meatball pan and mix everything together, making sure everything is covered in tomato sauce. Let simmer for 5 mins.
Top with mozzarella and pop your pan under the grill until bubbling - this will take a couple of mins. Serve and enjoy.

name: Meatball Macaroni Soup
description: Meatballs and pasta is an Italian classic, as is minestrone. Put the two together and what have you got? Something that’s not very classic, but very delicious.
instructions:
Tip the beef mince into a large bowl. Coarsely grate in half the
onion and 2 of the garlic cloves. Add 1 tsp of the oregano, the
breadcrumbs and plenty of seasoning, then crack in the egg. Using
your hands, scrunch the flavourings through the meat, then shape
into 20 small meatballs. Put into a roasting tin and slide into the
fridge to chill while you start the soup.
Finely chop the remaining onion half and the carrots and
celery. Get your largest saucepan over a medium heat. Pour in 2 tbsp of the olive oil, then tip in the veg along with a pinch
of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft.
Meanwhile finely chop the remaining 3 garlic cloves and cut the
rind off the Parmesan. Add the garlic, the remaining 2 tsp of
dried oregano and the chilli flakes to the pan and cook for a minute
more. Tip in the plum tomatoes, add the Parmesan rind and pour in
the stock. Bring the soup to the boil, breaking down the tomatoes
with the back of your spoon, then bubble for 10 mins.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Brush the meatballs with 1 tbsp of olive oil. Bake in the
oven for 12–15 mins until cooked and browned.
Meanwhile drop the macaroni into the soup and cook for 1
min less than stated on the packet instructions. Once cooked,
stir in the spinach until wilted, then season the soup to taste.
While your pasta cooks, make the salsa verde. Roughly chop the
parsley (stalks and all) and add to a mini food processor along with
the capers, the juice of the lemon and the remaining tablespoon of
olive oil. Add a tablespoon of water and whizz to a rough sauce, then
season to taste with salt.
Divide the soup between four bowls and top each with five
meatballs. Add a spoonful of salsa verde to each one and finely
grate over the Parmesan to serve.

name: Meatball Patty Smashburgers
description: These sandwiches are beautifully simple, but pack a lot of flavour with the use of beautiful value Ocado ingredients. The smashed basil mayo is glorious touch.
instructions: Finely slice your garlic.

Heat a little oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add your sliced garlic and chilli flakes, then cook out for 2 mins. Tip in your tinned tomatoes and bring to a simmer. Cook over a gentle heat for 30 mins until your sauce has thickened up. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Add your basil to a pestle and mortar and bash it to a fine paste. Add your mayonnaise and mix until you have a vibrant green sauce.
Squeeze the sausages out of their skins into a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Mix to combine, then divide into 8 equal-sized balls.

Heat a frying pan over a high heat. Add a couple of your sausage balls, then place a piece of baking parchment on top of the pan and pop a heavy-bottomed pan on top. Fry for a minute or two until crisp, then flip.

Tear off some mozzarella and drape it over the top of your patty before adding a splash of water to the pan and carefully putting a lid on it. Cook for 2 mins more, until your cheese is melted. Repeat with your remaining sausage patties and cheese.
Cut your ciabatta rolls in half and toast them cut-side down in the sausage fat.
Assembly time. Dollop some tomato sauce onto the base of your bun, then top with two sausage patties. Spread some of your basil mayo onto the lid of the bread, then place it on top and serve.

name: Meatball Sliders
description: We've got Big Zuu, the BAFTA-winning chef, here showing you how to make his classic meatball sliders. It's the sandwich of your dreams, Mob.
instructions: Heat a small knob of butter and oil in a frying pan, slice half of your garlic and onions, and start to sweat.
Add the tomato purée and cook for 5 minutes.

Add a tin of plum tomatoes and crush it by hand straight into the pan. Mix that in then add in your salt, pepper, garlic powder and Italian seasoning mix. Pop a lid on, let that cook down and reduce for 30 mins
Slice the rest of your onion, garlic, parsley, salt and chilli and add that into a bowl followed by your beef mince. Get your hands in there and mix that all together.
Form the mixture into 6 even-sized meatballs, and place them onto a tray with baking paper and into the oven at 180°C for 25 mins or until cooked through.
Cut a circle into all your bread rolls, the same size as your meatballs, and push it down.

Make a garlic butter by mixing together the rest of your butter with parsley and garlic. Spread it in and around the bread rolls then get those in the oven for 5 mins. Remove from the oven when crispy.

Take the meatballs out and add them to the tomato sauce, get them coated then transfer each meatball into a bread roll and put a spoonful of sauce onto each one. Sprinkle with mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake until the cheese is golden and melted, then top with fresh parsley. Get stuck in and enjoy!

name: Meatballs Aglio e Olio
description: Juicy homemade meatballs served on a bed of creamy, cheesy polenta. This hearty recipe is perfect for any occasion.
instructions: Add the beef mince and salt to a bowl. Scrunch with your hands then set aside for 10 mins. Put the breadcrumbs and milk in another bowl, then allow to soak for 10 mins until the bread is completely soggy and breaks apart easily.
Meanwhile, finely grate the garlic, beat the egg and chop the parsley.  Grate the Parmesan, and then set it aside.

Add the soaked bread, one-quarter of the garlic, beaten egg, oregano and fennel seeds to the meat bowl, then scrunch everything together with your hands until it's all evenly combined. Divide into 16 balls and place on a tray or plate. Chill in the fridge for 1 hr to firm up (this helps when frying them off later).
Heat a glug of oil in a large frying pan. Once hot, fry the meatballs (in batches, if necessary), browning them on all sides for around 5 minutes until evenly golden. Set aside on a plate.

Add the cherry tomatoes to the pan and fry in the fat from the meatballs for 6-8 mins until they start to blister and soften a bit. Add the remaining garlic, capers and chilli flakes and cook for 2 mins before returning the meatballs to the pan.

Pour the water (or an equal amount of white wine, if you have some spare) to the pan then cover with a lid (I grab whatever will cover the pan, which sometimes means a big baking tray or heatproof bowl) and steam for 5-8 mins until cooked through. Turn off the heat, add the parsley and squeeze in the lemon juice, give it a good toss then allow to rest in the pan for 5 mins.
Meanwhile, cook the polenta following pack instructions, then when ready, turn off the heat and add the Parmesan, butter and seasoning.
Spoon the polenta onto plates, then top with the meatballs and sauce.

name: Meaty Pulled Mushroom Barbacoa Tacos
description: Quick and easy veggie tacos with smoky roasted mushrooms, zingy pickled radish and a crispy cheese skirt. Made with Old El Paso’s new Street Vibes Barbacoa soft taco kit.
ingredients: 1 Old El Paso Street Vibes Barbacoa Soft Taco Kit
instructions: Shred the oyster mushrooms with a fork and pop them into a bowl with the soy sauce, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Add the mushrooms and cook for 8-10 mins until charred and golden. Remove to a bowl, stir through the barbacoa sauce and set aside.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the radish and onion and add to a bowl with the juice of ⅔ of the lime, the honey and a pinch of salt. Give them a mix then set them aside to pickle and turn bright pink.
Get the soured cream in a small bowl and stir through the seasoning packet (as much as you like). Grate the cheddar. Pick the coriander leaves and slice the remaining lime into wedges.

Set a large frying pan over a medium heat and sprinkle in a small handful of grated cheese – about half the size of the tortilla. Once it’s bubbling, place the tortilla wrap on top. Let it cook for a few mins until the cheese is turning gold and crisp. Remove the pan from the heat and let it cool and crisp up slightly.

Remove the wrap from the pan and flip it over so the cheese is on the inside. Fill it with the barbacoa mushrooms and top with the pickles, seasoned sour cream, some coriander leaves and a lime wedge.

name: Mediterranean Baked Salmon & Chickpeas
description: A zesty one-dish wonder where flaky salmon meets juicy chickpeas, salty olives and punchy sundried tomatoes. Barely any effort, big sunny flavours.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Halve the olives. Strip the oregano leaves from their stalks and chop them. Zest the lemon and cut one half into thin slices. Set everything aside.

Halve the cherry tomatoes. Tip the chickpeas into a medium ovenproof casserole dish (juice and all). Grate in the garlic, then add the cherry tomatoes and drizzle over the olive oil. Stir through half the lemon zest and oregano, plus all of the olives. Season well.

Nestle the salmon fillets into the chickpeas. Spread over the sundried tomato pesto. Season with salt and black pepper, then scatter over the remaining lemon zest and oregano. Crumble the feta on top and tuck the lemon slices into the dish.
Bake for 10-14 mins, or until the salmon is cooked through to your liking.
To serve, dish out the chickpeas and top with the salmon. Serve with lemon wedges from the remaining half.

name: Mediterranean Chicken Gnocchi Traybake
description: Juicy chicken meatballs baked over a crispy, golden gnocchi tray with courgette, cherry tomatoes and salty hits of feta. Dead simple and full of flavour.
cuisine: Italian, Italian-Inspired, Greek, Greek-Inspired, Mediterranean, Mediterranean-Inspired
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C. Pick the basil leaves, setting aside the smaller ones for garnish. Finely chop the rest and chuck into a large bowl with the chicken mince. Crumble in one-third of the feta, season with salt and pepper, then mix well with your hands. Shape into 8 meatballs.

Slice the courgette into half moons. Tip the courgette, gnocchi, cherry tomatoes and olives onto a roasting tray. Drizzle with the olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss everything together so it’s well coated.
Top with the meatballs. Break over the remaining feta into chunky, crouton-sized pieces. Bake for 25 mins, or until everything is golden and the meatballs are cooked through.
Once the traybake is ready, scatter over the reserved basil leaves and serve up!

name: Mediterranean Marinated Tofu
description: This Mediterranean marinated tofu is a great way to easily sneak in some extra protein. It’s zingy and herby and makes a great swap for feta.
instructions: Pat the tofu dry with a clean kitchen towel.
Crumble or cube the tofu and add it into a clean jar.
Add the rest of the ingredients to the jar and give it a good shake.
You can eat immediately, but the tofu will be marinated after a couple of hours and will continue to develop in flavour.
Keep in the fridge for up to 7 days. If the olive oil becomes solid in the fridge, just let it come back to room temperature before serving or add a splash of boiling water to the jar and mix.

name: Mediterranean Traybake
description: The croutons make this traybake. Golden and crunchy. With the roast garlic and the herby dressing drizzled on at the end. Minimal washing up. Ideal.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Halve your artichoke hearts, chop up the peppers, break off the ends of your asparagus, slice your onions and place into a baking tray. Add your olives, garlic, and tomatoes.

Break up the ciabatta and add this to the tray. Season with a pinch of salt and a good grinding of pepper. Sprinkle your chilli flakes in. Give the tray a generous drizzle of olive oil and stir it all together. Place into the oven for 30 minutes.

Dressing Time. Chop up your basil and thyme and add this to a small jar or glass. Add the juice of a whole lemon and pour in roughly 30ml of olive oil. Add a pinch of salt and pepper and mix everything together.
