Once 30 minutes is up, take the tray out of the oven and give it a good stir. Place it back into the oven for another 20 minutes.
Once it’s cooked, take it out of the oven and pour the dressing over the top. And that’s it, so simple! Time to tuck in.

name: Mee Goreng Mamak
description: Mee goreng mamak is a popular dish typically found in mamak stalls (Malaysian eateries run by Indian Muslims). Whenever I go back to Malaysia, I can smell the local mamak stall serving this dish from a mile away. It's so delicious and quick to make, making it the perfect weeknight meal.
instructions: Mince the garlic and finely chop the shallot. Add a big glug of vegetable oil to a wok set over a medium-high heat, then add the garlic and shallot along with the sambal. Stir-fry for 1-2 mins.
Slice the chicken into thin strips then add to the wok and fry for 4 mins. Add some more oil, if needed.
Meanwhile, chop the tofu in half and slice the tomato into wedges.

Add the fresh egg noodles to the wok along with the sauces and seasonings, tomato and tofu, toss everything together to coat the noodles evenly for 1 minute (you want the noodles to be slightly smoky for wok hei).

Wash the choy sum and chop into three parts lengthways, and add to the wok. Push everything in the wok to the side and crack the eggs in. Wait for the eggs to slightly cook, then lightly scramble them.
Wash the beansprouts, add to the wok and stir-fry for a few mins until the vegetables are slightly wilted (but make sure not to overcook the noodles).
Serve your mee goreng mamak with crispy shallots, crushed peanuts, extra sambal and a wedge of lime, enjoy!

name: Melted Aubergines with Rice & Beans
description: Tender, jammy aubergines soaking up a rich coconut, garlic and black bean rice - all cooked in one tray. Finished with a crisp herby sugar snap salad and a proper kick of scotch bonnet. A super easy veggie weeknight dinner.
keywords: Melted Aubergines with Rice & Beans recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Chop the aubergines into 3cm chunks and add to a large bowl with the olive oil and the tikka masala paste. Season with salt and black pepper and toss to coat.
Wash the jasmine rice until the water runs clear. Lightly bash and peel the garlic cloves. Boil the water in a kettle.

Add the rice, garlic and drained black beans to a deep-sided baking tray. Pour over the boiling water and coconut milk, add the scotch bonnet whole and season with salt. Scatter the aubergines on top and slide into the oven. Cook for 30-35 mins, until the liquid has fully absorbed and the rice and aubergines are cooked through. Remove from the oven, cover tightly with foil and leave to rest for 5-10 mins.

Meanwhile, squeeze the lime juice into a bowl, drizzle in the olive oil and season with salt and as much honey as you like. Pick the herb leaves, discarding the mint stalks, and thinly slice the coriander stalks. Halve the sugar snap peas. Just before serving, toss all three into the dressing.
Fluff the rice with a fork, then serve onto plates. Top with the aubergines, the sugar snap salad and a dollop of yoghurt.

name: Melted Broccoli & Anchovy Pasta
description: A quick pasta recipe, perfect for a weeknight. Melted broccoli in a garlicky, chilli oil, finished with a shower of parmesan. It doesn't get any better.
instructions: Trim the broccoli stalk, then chop the broccoli into smaller chunks, place into a food processor and blitz until minced. Peel the garlic cloves and finely mince. Thinly slice the chilli. Grate the cheese.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.

Meanwhile, drizzle 5 tbsp of olive oil into a large frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, add the garlic, chilli and anchovies, cook until the fish has broken down, 3-4 mins. Add the balsamic and let it evaporate fully. Add the broccoli and cook until almost mushy, 6-7 mins.
Once the water is boiling, add the pasta in and cook for 3 mins until it’s just under al dente.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer the pasta into the pan with the broccoli. Add some pasta water and stir through until the sauce emulsifies and the broccoli breaks down even more.
Take it off the heat, stir through three-quarters of the cheese, adding more pasta water if necessary. Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Serve the pasta with a sprinkle of the remaining cheese and some chopped parsley.

name: Melted Courgette Gnocchi Traybake with Tahini
description: Courgettes get melty and golden, gnocchi goes crispy-edged, and it all gets slicked in a lemony sumac dressing and drizzled with creamy tahini. This is a traybake to remember.
keywords: Melted Courgette Gnocchi Traybake with Tahini
Melted Courgette Gnocchi Traybake with Tahini recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan.
Prep the courgettes. Cut them into irregular 3cm chunks. Spread onto a large roasting tray and toss with half of the olive oil and a sprinkling of salt.

Roast the courgettes for 20-30 mins. Remove the tray, give everything a shake, then add the gnocchi and roast for a further 5–8 mins until the courgettes are golden and the gnocchi is crisping at the edges.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining olive oil, sumac, honey, the zest of the whole lemon, and the juice of half. Season well.
Once the tray is out of the oven, let it cool slightly, then toss the courgettes and gnocchi through the dressing.
Make the tahini sauce. Grate the garlic into a separate bowl. Add the tahini and remaining lemon juice. Stir with a splash of water until smooth and pourable. Season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle the garlic tahini sauce over the traybake, sprinkle with chilli flakes and sunflower seeds, and scatter over picked mint leaves.

name: Melted Leek Pesto Pasta
description: This isn’t your bog standard basil pesto. It's melted leek pesto pasta, made with confit garlic and leek.
instructions: Trim the leeks, and slice into 2cm rounds. Peel the garlic cloves and add both to a small saucepan with 150ml of olive oil. Place onto medium-low heat and let gently sizzle until both are soft, 15-20 mins. They shouldn’t colour, if they are, decrease the heat. Once softened, let cool down.
Meanwhile, add the walnuts into a dry pan on medium heat, cook the walnuts until toasted, 2-4 mins, then let cool down completely.

Add the cooled walnuts and Parmesan into a blender and blend until finely broken down, transfer into a small bowl. Add the leek mixture into the blender with 90ml of infused olive oil and blend until smooth, stir into the walnut mixture. Wash the blender.

Remove the stem off the chillies and place into the blender with the remaining 60ml of infused oil, blend until smooth. Finely mince the parsley and pick the oregano leaves. Pour the chilli oil into a frying pan, place on medium heat and cook for 2-3 mins. Add the herbs and cook for 2-3 mins until dark green. Remove from the heat and let cool down. Zest ¼ of the lemon into the oil and season with lemon juice.

Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, cook the pasta according to package instructions. Toss the spaghetti and pesto together with a little pasta water until creamy. Taste and season with salt.
Share between bowls and drizzle over the chilli oil.

name: Merguez Spiced Lamb Linguine
description: This spiced lamb pasta is reminiscent of merguez sausages — a spicy lamb sausage. Complete with a tangy drizzle of crème frâiche, crispy lamb harissa oil and cooling mint, this dish is beautifully balanced.
instructions: Thinly slice the onion and garlic. Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil.

Place a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, pour a glug of olive oil into the pan, add the lamb mince, season with salt. Use a wooden spoon or spatula to break up the mince, fry until brown and crispy, around 10-15 mins. Once crispy, use a slotted spoon to transfer the mince to a bowl, leaving all the oil and fat in the pan.
Spoon 3 tbsp of the crispy lamb in a separate bowl and stir in a third of the harissa paste and another glug of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste, and set aside.

Return to the pan. Turn the heat down to medium, stir the cumin seeds into the hot oil and fry for 30 secs, add the onions and cook them until softened, 4-5 mins. Add the garlic and tomato purée, cook for 1 min further, then stir through the ground coriander, paprika, and the remaining harissa. Add the remaining lamb into the spices and stir to coat.
Meanwhile, drop your pasta into the boiling salted water for 2 mins less than package instructions. Reserve 400ml of pasta water.
Using tongs, transfer the pasta from the water into the lamb pan, along with a big slosh of pasta water. Toss together, adding more pasta water until you create a silky sauce.
Share the pasta between your plates and top with a drizzle of the crème frâiche, the crispy lamb harissa oil and a few mint leaves.

name: Mexican Bean & Tortilla Soup
description: You may not think tortillas in soup would work well together, but we're here to tell you that it does. And best of all? It's completely vegan.
instructions: Finely chop the red onion, crush the garlic, finely chop the jalapeño and slice the pepper. Heat a shot of oil in a frying pan, then tip in the red onion, jalapeño and garlic. Cook for 5-7 mins until softened and fragrant.

Add the beans, paprika, cumin, chipotle paste and tomato purée, then cook for 3 mins, stirring often, until everything is caramelised and starting to brown. Add the red pepper and cook for 1-2 mins, then add the chopped tomatoes, stock cube and water. Simmer for 15 -20 mins until everything is cooked and the beans have softened. Add ⅓ of the yoghurt and stir through before stirring.
Finely chop the pickled jalapeños and coriander.
To serve, ladle the soup into bowls and top with the pickled jalapeño, the rest of the yoghurt and chopped coriander. Crumble over the tortilla chips.

name: Mexican Charro Beans
description: Frijoles charros, or charro beans, from the North of Mexico. Originating from the “charrerias” ranches where cowboys would cook in metal pots using ingredients they had handy, these beans are simple, hearty and full of flavour.
instructions: Finely dice the tomatoes, white onion, green pepper, bacon, chorizo, fresh coriander and pickled jalapeño. Don't combine these ingredients yet as you'll use them at different times.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large cast iron pot set over a medium heat. Add the onion and tomato and fry for 2 mins, stirring from time to time. Add the green pepper and continue to fry until the onion is translucent and the tomatoes are mushy.

Add the bacon and fry for about 3-5 mins until slightly crispy at the edges, stirring constantly to fry it evenly. Add the chorizo and fry everything for another 3 mins until the chorizo releases its fat and starts to turn crisp.

Finally, add the pinto beans and their juices along with a splash of water, the pickled jalapeño, jalapeño vinegar, fresh coriander and sea salt. Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer for 10 mins.
While the beans simmer, dice the avocado.
Divide the beans between bowls and garnish with the avocado. Roll a tortilla and enjoy the frijoles charros like a proper Mexican: biting the tortilla and eating a spoonful of beans.

name: Mexican Dense Bean Salad
description: A plant-based, dense bean salad that uses silken tofu to create the most delicious dressing, which is a similar vibe to a herby, limey avocado crema.
instructions: Drain and rinse the black beans and kidney beans. Drain the sweetcorn. Drain and slice the roasted peppers.
Peel and finely slice the red onion. Add it to a small bowl with the juice of one lime and a pinch of salt. Massage and set aside.
Halve the cherry tomatoes. Peel, pit and dice the avocados. Add the beans, sweetcorn, peppers, tomatoes and avocado to a large mixing bowl.

Add the silken tofu to a high-speed blender with most of the coriander, the juice of the remaining two limes and the jalapeños (seeds removed if you’re not into spice). Grate in the garlic, add the tahini and season generously with salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the bean mixture, then add the pickled onions. Toss well to coat everything, taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

Scatter with the remaining coriander and serve. If making ahead box up for later and chill until needed. 
The salad will keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Mexican Pickled Onions
description: These cebolla encurtidas, or red pickled onions, are an easy but important dish for any Mexican party. Store a batch in the fridge and use them to garnish tacos, tostadas or any Mexican antojito.
instructions: Peel and cut the onion into thin strips then place in a mixing bowl.
Add the salt to the onions and mix to combine. Set aside for around 10 mins (this will remove some of the moisture of the onion).
Rinse the onions under cold water to get rid of the salt, then pat the onions dry.
Add the vinegar, water, oregano, peppercorns and bay leaf to the bowl with the onions. Mix well and leave to pickle for a few hours.
Serve as garnish for tacos or any Mexican antojito.

name: Mexican Pickled Vegetables
description: Also known as escabeche, these pickled jalapeños, carrots, cauliflower and shallots are the perfect topping for Mexican dishes like nachos, tacos and tortas. Jarred pickled jalapeños just don’t compare.
instructions: Remove the stems from the fresh jalapeńos then cut into strips. Peel and dice the carrots and peel the garlic cloves. Peel and halve the shallots lengthways, leaving the root ends intact so each half holds as one piece. Cut the cauliflower into tiny florets.
Heat the sunflower oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add all the vegetables and fry for around 5 mins, stirring constantly.
Add the white wine vinegar, water, salt, oregano, peppercorns and bay leaves. Cook over low heat for 10 mins, stirring constantly.
Turn the heat off and leave the mixture to fully cool. Once cooled, transfer to a sterilized glass jar. Keep in the fridge and enjoy whenever you like!

name: Mexican Style Plant-Based Burger
description: Changing the burger game one plant-based patty at a time. A toasted bun, fresh and zesty guac, caramelised onions, and peppers all in one magnificent mouthful.
instructions: Place your Meatless Farm Burger patties in a large bowl. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with 1 tsp of paprika and 1 tsp of cumin. Grate the zest of one lime over the patties and add the hot sauce. Massage the seasoning into the patties and set aside for later.

Slice 1 avocado into a large mixing bowl with the juice of 1 lime. Slice your spring onion and add to the bowl. Cut a handful of coriander and whack it in there as well. Season with a pinch of salt, a drizzle of olive oil and a few cracks of black pepper. Mash the avocado mixture with a fork and set aside.

Add a few glugs of olive oil to a frying pan on a medium heat. Slice all the peppers and your red onions. Add the veggies to the pan and season with 1 tsp of paprika, 1 tsp of cumin, a pinch of salt and some cracked black pepper.

Cook the veggies for approximately 15 minutes or until soft and caramelised, stirring often. Once the onions and peppers are cooked, add the water and stir for another minute before transferring to a bowl.
Burger time! Add a drizzle of olive oil to the frying pan. Cook the Meatless patties on each side for approximately 4 minutes until crispy.

Now to assemble the beast. Slice your burger buns and lightly toast in a dry frying pan for a minute or two. Drizzle with olive oil, spoon on the caramelised peppers and onions, place the Meatless burger patty on and top with the fresh avocado mixture. Dig in! Enjoy!

name: Mexican Style Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
description: The creamy cheddar. The zingy guac. The smokey, pepper + bean potato filling. Such a satisfying dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Drizzle olive oil over the sweet potatoes. Add salt and a small handful of chilli flakes (optional).
Bake sweet potatoes for 50 minutes or until soft.

Whilst the potatoes are in the oven, sort the guacamole. Scoop the flesh out of your avocados and add to a bowl. Add a handful of chopped coriander leaves, the juice of a lime, a finely chopped red chilli, some salt, pepper and olive oil. Mash.
Chilli time. Finely chop your onion and peppers.
In a pan, add a splash of olive oil. Add the chopped garlic, cumin, and paprika.

Once the garlic has softened (1 minute) add the peppers and onion. Fry until soft, on a medium to low heat. Add a bit of water if it starts catching on the pan. This should take about 15 minutes. Once softened, add your black beans. Mash everything together.
Remove your sweet potatoes from the oven. Scoop out the flesh and save the skins. Add the flesh to the black bean chilli. Mix everything together.

Assemble time. Stuff the sweet potato skins with the chilli. Add a big dollop of guac. Top with a generous grating of cheddar, and garnish with spring onions, red chillies and the remaining coriander.

name: Mexican-Inspired Corn on the Cob
description: This recipe is inspired by the Mexican street food snack Elote. After eating corn this way - you’ll never look back.
instructions: Heat a griddle pan or BBQ until hot.
Season the corn with salt and pepper and grill for 12-15 minutes, turning regularly until lightly charred and cooked through.

Once tender, put on a serving plate. Leave to cool for 2 minutes and then brush or spoon over the mayonnaise, turning so that the corn gets completely coated. Finely grate over the cheese and sprinkle over the chilli powder. Cut the lime into wedges for squeezing over.
Great as a side for any BBQ, or just a snack.

name: Mexico City Fried Quesadillas
description: Mexico City’s fried quesadillas, the ultimate street snack. Here’s how we make them at home – they might take a bit of effort, but we promise they’re worth it.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over medium heat. Boil your potatoes (skin on) for 15 mins over a medium heat until soft but firm so they can be cut in cubes.
Soak your morita chile in boiling water for 30 mins. Remove potatoes from the water and allow to cool down for 15/20 mins until you can handle them without burning your hands!

Remove the skin and dice the potatoes into cubes, roughly 3-4 cm in size. Your potato should be firm enough not to break down. If it is a little too firm, you can fry it longer in the pan to allow the cooking process to finish. Chop your hydrated morita chile and reserve to one side. Remove the seeds if you are not keen on spice!

Peel, break down and fry the chorizo in a medium pan. Allow the oils to render out and the meat to get crispy. While your chorizo cooks, dice your onion and your garlic in small cubes. Also break down your soaked morita chile.

Once the chorizo is cooked, strain the excess fat and reserve to one side as you will incorporate it into the potatoes for an extra 3 mins. Do not waste your chorizo fat – reserve to one side as it will be needed later in the recipe. Using the same frying pan, bring your pan to medium/low heat: add back onto your pan some of that chorizo fat oil. Fry your onions gently for 3 mins and add the diced garlic and morita chile, stirring often for an extra 2 mins. Season with salt.

Add potatoes and fry for 3-4 mins. You want your potatoes to soak in this red liquid gold. Season with salt and pepper before adding the chorizo back in. Cook at the same heat for 3-4 mins. Rest to the side and let it cool down for a good 20-30 mins until it reaches room temp. The contents of your quesadilla should be either cold or room temperature before going inside your raw masa.

In a large bowl, mix all your dry ingredients together. That’s your maseca, salt, and plain flour. In parts, add water to the dry mix and gently but firmly knead the dough to mix all ingredients. Do this for 5 mins until you get a smooth consistency. Squeeze it in between your fingers to allow all ingredients to mix.

The dough should feel hydrated enough to be shaped into a ball however at this stage it should still feel dry. It is important the water you use is warm from the tap, not hot! To test – make a small ball and crush it. If the edges of the masa dough break, your dough needs more liquid.

Make a small hole in your dough and add in your oil before adding baking soda and vegetable oil. Knead your dough for 3 mins and do a test with a small ball to see if you need to add more water to the dough. If so, mix for another 2 mins. Wrap your dough in cling film and let it rest at room temp for 30 mins.

Cut the tomatoes in half. Remove all seeds with a knife or by giving them a squeeze. Blitz the tomatoes first. Cut your onions into squares, finely chop your garlic, remove the bird’s eye chilli stems. Add to your blitzed tomatoes and then throw in salt, sugar, cumin, and coriander. Blitz using the pulse function but make sure not to do it for too long. You want a chunky salsa. Add in your squeezed lime and adjust the seasoning.

Grate your Turkish or mozzarella cheese using the largest holes on a grater. To make the crema, mix the crème fraîche and sour cream. Add water and salt while mixing it together. You want the crema to be pourable. Slice the lettuce in thin strips.

Grab a freezer bag and a tortilla press. Place your plastic sheet on each side of the press. Make a 55g dough ball. Place the ball on the plastic sheet on the bottom side of the press. With three fingers, press the dough down to create a ball.

Place the other plastic sheet on top of your ball. Gently bring down the top of the press and press down once, firmly. Do not press your tortilla too thin otherwise it may break when folding the ingredients in it.

Grab one rough tortilla in your hand. Fill it with a bed of grated cheese and your chorizo potato mix. Do not allow the ingredients to touch the edges so you can fold in half and close the tortilla comfortably using the plastic sheet to fold the quesadilla in half and gently press to glue the edges together.

Once your oil has reached 170°C, carefully lower in the quesadillas. Fry two at the time making sure they do not stick together and they are turned around evenly over 3 to 4 mins of frying.If your oil is too hot, the dough will cook too quickly and come out bubbly instead of smooth. Let the quesadilla rest on a mesh tray for two minutes before finishing.
With a small knife open the belly of the quesadilla from top to bottom to allow space to stuff the quesadilla with lettuce. Top with crema, salsa and crumbled ricotta!

name: Mezze Meatball Hummus Bowl
description: All the joy of a mezze platter in one high-protein bowl. Creamy hummus topped with leftovers from our Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake, sweet roasted veg, zingy sumac onions and warm flatbread for scooping. Yum.
instructions: Make the Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake.

Peel and finely slice the red onion. Add to a bowl with a pinch of salt and the sumac, then scrunch with your hands to soften. Set aside to marinate while you prep everything else. Pick the parsley leaves and stir them through the onions just before serving.

Add the tomato purée to a saucepan with a drizzle of olive oil. Set it over a medium heat and cook for 3–4 mins until darkened and sticky. Tip in the meatballs and roast veg, along with 100ml water. Simmer for a few mins until hot and slightly thickened. Taste and season with salt, if needed.
Spoon the hummus into shallow bowls and use the back of a spoon to spread it out. Top with the hot lamb mix and a generous pile of the sumac onions.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan or directly over a flame until soft and charred. Serve alongside for scooping.

name: Microwave Steamed Eggs
description: Inspired by Japanese chawanmushi, the eggs are steamed in the microwave until set, silky and custardy. Topped with chilli crisp and spring onions. Eaten with rice for a gentle and quick dinner.
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl. Whisk together with the dashi or stock, soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Place a strainer over another bowl and strain the egg mixture through – this will ensure silky eggs. Thinly slice the spring onion.

Pour the eggs into a large enough microwave-safe bowl, remove any foamy bits and put in the microwave. Cook the eggs on 500W for 7-10 mins. After 5 mins, the custard should start setting. Cook in bursts of 30 seconds until ready.
Drizzle the silky eggs with some chilli crisp and the soy sauce, then scatter the spring onions on top.

name: Mighty Mushroom Mac & Cheese
description: Why haven't we used mushrooms in a mac & cheese before now, we'll never know. Taleggio works a charm here - give it a go when you need something comforting.
instructions: Quarter your mushrooms. Add to a pan with a splash of olive oil. Fry until brown.

Add sliced garlic cloves and a handful of sliced thyme leaves. Squeeze a few drops of lemon juice in. Mix everything together. Once the garlic begins to go brown, remove everything from the pan and set aside.
Add 5 tablespoons of olive oil and plain flour to the pan. Whisk it together. Start adding your whole milk, bit by bit, whisking it in. Keep adding milk until you have a smooth white sauce.
Get your macaroni cooking.
At this point, crumble in the mozzarella and add taleggio to the pan. Stir it in until it melts and you have a smooth white sauce.
Re-add your mushrooms and a large handful of parsley. Mix it in.
Drain your cooked macaroni and add to the sauce. Mix it in. Season with salt and pepper and add a big squeeze of lemon juice. Smooth out the top of the mac and cheese. Add your remaining taleggio.
Place under the grill until the taleggio is golden and bubbling.
Remove from the oven, serve it up, scatter over some more chopped parsley and enjoy!

name: Milk Bread
description: This milk bread recipe doesn’t need any special equipment, but still creates the fluffiest, softest loaf ever. It’s wildly impressive and all of that is down to the yudane (Japanese flour paste) and the sweet, sweet kneading.
instructions: For the yudane, combine the flour and boiling water in a bowl and stir until completely mixed. Cover and chill in the fridge for a couple of hours, or up to overnight.
Once the yudane is ready, heat the milk until lukewarm (around 35°C) and stir the sugar and yeast into it. Whisk together and let sit for 5 mins.

Pour the milk mixture into a large bowl, tear the yudane into it, then add the butter, flour and salt. Stir until a dough forms, then tip onto a clean surface. Knead the dough for 20-30 mins until smooth – the dough will be very tacky and sticky at first, but trust the process and it will transform itself. You know it’s ready when you can gently stretch the dough until it goes so thin you can see shadows through it. Form the dough into a ball and transfer to a greased bowl. Cover and prove for 1-1½ hrs until doubled in size.

Tip the dough out and split it in half, then roll each half out into a long rectangle. Take a dough half and fold the long sides in so the seams meet in the middle, then starting from the short side furthest from you, tightly roll into a thick log. Repeat with the other half.

Grease a 2LB (see notes) loaf tin and place both logs into it, seam-side down so they touch in the middle. Cover and prove for another 45 mins until puffy – test by gently poking it with a wet finger (if it slowly bounces back leaving an indentation, it’s ready). Halfway through proving, heat the oven to 185°C.
Bake for 25-30 mins until golden brown. Once baked, brush the top of the loaf with some melted butter, if you like. Allow the bread to cool for at least 30 mins before eating.

name: Millionaire's Shortbread Date
description: Everything you love about a millionaire's shortbread, but in date form. The perfect sweet pick-me-up.
instructions: Heat the cream until it’s steaming in a saucepan. Once it’s looking right, pour your cream over the chocolate chips in a heatproof bowl. Add your vanilla extract and give it a good stir.

Cut up your shortbread into inch-sized pieces. Add your shortbread pieces to your chocolate sauce and use a spoon to mix it all together. Add your chocolatey mixture to your dates and place them onto a plate. Drizzle your stuffed dates with a generous amount of caramel. Top with flaky sea salt. Dig in.

name: Minced Beef & Broccoli Stir Fry
description: Sweet, savoury and packed with umami. This sticky beef stir-fry hits hard and comes together in minutes.
keywords: Minced Beef & Broccoli Stir Fry recipe
instructions: Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Mix all the sauce ingredients together in a bowl and set aside.
Mince the garlic and ginger. Cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets. Slice the spring onions and set aside.
Place the broccoli in a heatproof bowl with the water. Cover and microwave for 3 mins until just tender. Drain and set aside. Alternatively, blanch it in boiling water for 2 mins.
Place a wok or large frying pan over a high heat with the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the beef mince and stir-fry for 3–4 mins until browned.
Add the ginger and garlic to the pan and cook for 2 mins until fragrant.
Tip in the broccoli and pour over the sauce. Toss everything together for 2–3 mins until the sauce thickens and coats the beef and veg.
Drizzle over the sesame oil and toss again. Remove from the heat.
Serve topped with sesame seeds, the sliced spring onionsand extra white pepper if you fancy.

name: Mini Baked Pepper Frittatas
description: These colourful little egg muffins are packed with cheesy goodness and sweet peppers. Perfect for lunchboxes, after-school snacks or weekend picnics.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kid Servings
Heat the oven to 160°C.
 Drizzle a little olive oil into a 12-hole muffin tin and use your fingers or a bit of kitchen paper to coat the sides and bottoms.
Slice the peppers into small bite-sized chunks. Finely chop the spring onions. Grate the cheddar and set aside.
Crack the eggs into a large mixing bowl. Add the milk, oregano, a generous pinch of salt and some freshly cracked black pepper. Whisk until smooth and well combined.
Divide the chopped peppers and cheddar evenly between the muffin holes. Scatter over the spring onions. Pour in the egg mixture until each hole is nearly full.
Bake for 20–25 mins until puffed up, golden on top and just set in the middle. Let them cool slightly in the tin, they’ll firm up a bit as they cool.

Serve up with your kids' favourite fruit and veg sticks. 
They will keep for up 3-4 days in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer.

name: Mini Egg Shortbread Fingers
description: A six-ingredient recipe for the tastiest shortbread fingers studded with Mini Eggs, baked and ready in as little as 25 mins.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Line a 20cm x 30cm baking tin with baking paper.
Tip the butter into a bowl and add the both sugars. Beat together, using either an electric whisk, handheld whisk or spoon, until light and creamy. It should have doubled in volume.
Add the egg yolk and whisk it in, then use a sieve to sift in the flour. Add a pinch of table salt and use a wooden spoon to bring the dough together.
Roughly chop the Mini Eggs and stir most of them through the dough, saving a handful for the top. It will be pretty crumbly, don't panic!

Tip the shortbread mixture into the baking tin and press it down until compact with no gaps. Sprinkle over the remaining Mini Eggs and press them in slightly. Bake for 20-25 mins, until lightly golden then take out of the oven. Using a sharp knife, score the shortbread about halfway through, into 16 fingers. This will make them easier to cut once they are cool.
Once cooled, cut the shortbread fingers and enjoy with a cuppa.

name: Mini Sesame Toasts
description: Filled with a delicious mushroom tofu mix and finished with a crispy sesame skin, these mini sesame toasts are so fun to make.
instructions: To begin with, blitz the nori sheets into small pieces. Peel and roughly chop the ginger and garlic. Roughly chop the spring onions and mushrooms.

Add all of the ingredients, except the bread, to a blender or small food processor and blend into a thick paste, scraping down the sides as needed. Add a splash of water if it's too thick to get around the blender. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut circles out of the bread (you can use a cookie cutter or a glass). Save the edges of the bread and turn them into breadcrumbs for another use.

Flatten each circle of bread slightly and hold it in the palm of your hand to make a taco shape which you can then fill. Carefully load the bread with the filling and use the back of a spoon to cover the edges of the bread with the filling which will help the sesame seeds stick to it.
Fill a small bowl with the sesame seeds and roll the open edge into it, so the sesame seeds stick.

Prep your frying station. Fill a small frying pan with vegetable oil and heat on medium-high. To check the oil's hot enough, drop a small piece of bread in and if it sizzles immediately, then it's ready.

To shallow fry, carefully lower the sesame toast into the oil and fry for about 2 mins on each side, until golden brown. Remember that they will continue to cook after you remove them from the oil, so don’t let it get too dark. Repeat with each piece of sesame toast and lay them onto a kitchen towel.
To air fry, spray each toast with oil and cook at 180ºC for 10 mins. Flip, spray again and fry for another 5 mins.
Serve with lots of fresh leaves and sweet chilli sauce.

name: Mini Sticky Toffee Cakes
description: These mini sticky toffee cakes are rich, moist and gently spiced. They’re delicious as they are or topped with oozy salted caramel sauce.
instructions: Grease a cupcake tin with butter and set aside. Heat the oven to fan 160°C.
Soak the dates in the boiling water with the spices. Leave to steep for a minimum of 30 mins or up to overnight. Once cooled, blitz into a paste.
Add the butter and sugar to a bowl and whisk together for 5-7 mins until fluffy and pale.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating together until thoroughly combined.
In another bowl, whisk the flour and bicarbonate of soda until combined. Add to the butter mixture until a paste forms, then fold in the date mixture.
Slowly add the milk to the date batter until a loose cake batter forms – it will split, but don't worry.

Pour the batter evenly into the cupcake tin – around 60g of batter per cupcake. Bake for 15-20 mins until a toothpick inserted comes out clean. Remove from the oven and allow to fully cool in the tins.

Meanwhile, make the salted caramel sauce: Add about ⅕ of the sugar to a large pan and set it over a medium heat. Gently ‘swipe’ the sugar from side to side to ensure it’s heating evenly. Turn the heat down if you think it's looking too dark – you want a lovely light caramel colour. Once this first layer looks like it’s starting to melt, add another layer (about ⅕ of the sugar again), and so on until all the sugar has dissolved and caramelised. This will take a while but is worth it!
Gently warm the cream in another pan, then slowly add it to your caramelised sugar, stirring to incorporate it gradually. Leave it to cool slightly then add the sea salt to taste.
Transfer the cooled cakes from their tins to a plate or wire rack then drizzle the salted caramel. Finish with an extra sprinkling of sea salt and serve with vanilla ice cream, if you like.

name: Mint & Sesame Pesto
description: A minty, creamy pesto that's especially great on grilled cheese sandwiches or plain pasta.
instructions: Add the mint, sesame oil, and sesame seeds to a blender. Peel the garlic clove and peel the ginger and roughly slice, then add in. Add the lime juice and season generously with salt and pepper.
Add ⅓ of olive oil and begin to blend, then continue to add olive oil until you get to a thick pesto consistency.

name: Minty Pepper Salad
description: Super quick and easy, this minty pepper salad will add some colour and flavour to your lunch.
keywords: Cottage Cheese Tzatziki with Sausages recipe
instructions: Drain and thinly slice the peppers. Trim and thinly slice the onion, place into a strainer and wash under cold running water until crisp. Pick the mint leaves. Add all of the onion, peppers, and mint to a bowl with the balsamic vinegar and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss and then let the flavours get to know each other.
Serve with your favourite mains and dressings.

name: Misha's Meaty Meatballs
description: Created by Ben's best friend. Lamb mince works perfectly here. So simple. Delicious, rich meatballs on a bed of herby, steaming rice. Give it a pop.
instructions: Add your breadcrumbs to a bowl. Cover with twice the amount of whole milk. Set aside and wait until the crumbs have soaked up the liquid.

Add the soaked breadcrumbs to a mixing bowl with 1 crushed garlic clove, lamb mince, a handful of parsley stalks, 3 tsp harissa paste, salt and pepper. Mix everything together. Cover and place in fridge for 15 minutes.

After 15 minutes, remove mince from fridge. Divide into little meatballs. Add meatballs to a non-stick frying pan with a splash of oil. Cook until browned on the outside. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Get your rice on (follow pack instructions).
Remove excess oil from pan. Add 2 crushed garlic cloves. Before they start browning, add your tomatoes. Break them up with a spoon. Add 2 tsp of harissa and mix everything together.
Reintroduce your meatballs. Stir them in and cook the sauce until it is nice and thick.
Once the sauce is thick, add a handful of chopped parsley and basil. Season with salt and pepper, mix everything together and remove the meatballs from the heat.
Serve on a bed of steaming hot rice and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Miso & Sesame Butter Cod with Broccoli Rice
description: This is a really easy, foolproof dinner that's full of goodness and flavour. If you're looking to convert a fish hater, make them this.
keywords: miso & sesame butter cod with broccoli rice
miso & sesame butter cod with broccoli rice recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely slice the spring onions, then separate the whites from the greens. Melt the butter in a small saucepan, then whisk in the miso, honey, soy sauce, the zest of the lime, sesame seeds and the whites of the spring onions. Bubble away for a minute, then take off the heat. Squeeze in the juice of the lime and set aside.

Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Chop the broccoli into small florets, smaller than you'd usually. Add the rice to a lidded saucepan and pour in the water. Bring to the boil, then cover with the lid, reduce the heat to low and cook for 4 mins. After 4 mins, scatter the broccoli over the top. Give everything a quick stir, replace the lid and cook for another 8 mins. Turn off the heat and leave the rice to steam for 10 mins while you crack on with the cod.

Pat the cod dry and season with a little salt and black pepper. Remember the miso is salty, so don't go too overboard. Drizzle with the sesame oil, then pop onto a parchment lined baking tray and slide into the oven for 12-15 mins. This is going to vary depending on how thick your cod is, so keep an eye on it.
Pick the coriander leaves.
Plate up the rice, then top with the cod, spooning over the miso butter. Garnish with the coriander and spring onion greens.

name: Miso Beans & Spring Onion Pesto
description: Brothy miso beans with a spring onion and sesame pesto. This is big on savoury flavour and a great recipe for warming yourself up on a nippy winter night.
keywords: Miso Beans & Spring Onion Pesto recipe
instructions: Trim and thinly slice the spring onion whites, then roughly chop the green part.

For the pesto: peel and add the garlic, ¾ of the toasted sesame seeds and the parmesan into a food processor, pulse until broken down. Add the spring onion greens and olive oil, pulse until combined. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Stir through the sesame oil and remaining sesame seeds. Set aside.

Add a drizzle of oil into a saucepan and place over medium heat. Once hot, add the spring onion whites and cook for a few seconds until softened, then add the spinach and dashi or stock. Bring to the boil, then add the beans and their liquid, cook until piping hot and wilted. Remove from the heat and stir through the miso paste. Season with soy sauce to taste and pepper.
Share into bowls, top with the spring onion pesto, freshly cracked black pepper and some Parmesan.

name: Miso Braised Fennel
description: Buttery and tender slow-braised fennel topped with a spicy cashew and lime crumb. The fennel is so soft it melts in your mouth and makes the perfect side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Slice your fennel bulbs in half and place them into a deep baking tray with the flat sides facing down.
Combine 1 litre of boiling water with the butter and miso paste. Mix to combine.
Pour the miso liquid over the fennel, cover with foil and pop into the oven for 30 mins. Flip the fennel over, basting with the liquid and cook for another 30 mins with the foil removed.
Meanwhile, crush the cashews.

Add a big glug of oil into a saucepan and gently toast your cashews for 2 mins. When the cashews are slightly browned, add chilli powder and cook for an additional 30 secs. After that, add your breadcrumbs and a pinch of salt.
When the fennel is fork-tender, remove it from the oven and place it onto your serving dish. Drizzle with more miso sauce and sprinkle on your cashew crumb. Finish with lots of lime zest and enjoy.

name: Miso Broccoli & Spring Onion Udon
description: A vegetarian noodle dish that's ready in just 20 minutes. Miso gives this a proper thump of umami.
keywords: Miso Broccoli & Spring Onion Udon recipe
instructions: Bring a medium-sized pan of water to the boil. Add eggs and cook for 7 mins. Once done, plunge them in ice-cold water to prevent further cooking.

Get a cast iron skillet over a medium-high heat. Cut the spring onions into 4cm lengths, then toss them with a little oil and get them in the pan. Cook them for about 3 mins per side. Remove from the pan.
Toss the broccoli with a little oil, then get it in the skillet pan. Cook for about 4 mins per side, until tender with a light char.
Grate the Parmesan, crush the garlic and finely chop the ginger. Tip the egg yolks into a large bowl. Add the miso paste, garlic, ginger and Parmesan, then season with lots of black pepper.
Bring a pan of water to the boil and salt it. Add the udon and cook following pack instructions.
Drain the udon and, while still hot, tip them into the egg mixture. Add the broccoli and spring onions, then give it a really good mix.
Transfer the udon to warmed bowls. Peel and halve the eggs, add a half to each bowl and finish with shichimi togarashi. Serve.

name: Miso Brothy Mushrooms with Savoury Sesame Rice
description: This one is bursting with umami flavours, with fluffy sesame butter rice, roasted mushrooms and a miso broth. The most comforting, nourishing bowl.
keywords: Miso Brothy Mushrooms with Savoury Sesame Rice
Miso Brothy Mushrooms with Savoury Sesame Rice recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.

Tear or slice the mushrooms into 2cm chunks then place onto a baking tray. Sprinkle over the pul biber and ¾ of the toasted sesame seeds. Drizzle over some olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss together then slide into the oven to roast for 25-30 mins.
While the mushrooms cook, cook the rice following packet instructions. Thinly slice the spring onions.
Add the nori and softened butter to a food processor or blender and blitz together until the nori breaks down into the butter. Transfer to a bowl, stir in the remaining sesame seeds and set aside.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Add the spring onion whites with ½ the greens and cook for 1-2 mins until wilted. Pour the stock in and bring to a gentle simmer. Before serving, stir the miso through and taste and season with salt, if needed.
Stir the seaweed sesame butter through the cooked rice.
Share the rice between bowls and ladle over the miso broth. Top with the roasted mushrooms and a sprinkling of the remaining spring onion greens.

name: Miso Brothy Noodles with Soy Mushrooms
description: An umami explosion. This nourishing, flavourful vegan dinner is ready in just 20 minutes.
keywords: Miso Brothy Noodles with Soy Mushrooms
Miso Brothy Noodles with Soy Mushrooms recipe
instructions: Put a pot of water on to boil. Mince the garlic and ginger. Finely slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens. Roughly tear the mushrooms into strips. Set aside.
Cook the soba noodles in the pot of boiling water following packet instructions, then drain, rinse and set aside.

While the noodles are cooking, heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large pan set over a high heat. Add the sliced spring onion whites and mushrooms and a pinch of salt then fry for 5-7 mins until the mushrooms have started to caramelise. Add the dark soy sauce and cook for another minute then transfer the mushrooms to a bowl and set aside.

Add another glug of vegetable oil to the pan and turn the heat to medium. Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 min, stirring constantly. Pour in the water and stock cube, mixing well until the stock cube has dissolved. Scrape any leftover bits on the bottom of pan from the mushrooms into the stock to add flavour. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Meanwhile, drain the tofu and use your hands to break it into large bite-sized pieces. Add the tofu to the broth and leave to simmer for a few minutes to warm through the tofu. Just before serving, stir the miso paste through the broth.
To serve, divide the noodles between bowls and top with the tofu broth and mushrooms. Finish with the spring onion greens, a drizzle of chilli oil and plenty of sesame seeds.

name: Miso Brown Butter Baklava
description: This baklava might be one of the best I’ve ever had! The saltiness of the miso tames the sweetness of the sugar syrup, making for a perfectly balanced dessert.
instructions: Heat your oven to 140°C fan.
Blitz the pistachios and walnuts in a food processor until finely chopped.

Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. It will bubble for a few minutes. As the bubbles die down, the milk solids will sink to the bottom and turn brown as they caramelise. Once the butter smells nice and nutty and has changed from pale yellow to brown, take the pan off the heat.
Whisk the miso paste into the hot butter then pass it through a sieve into a heatproof bowl and leave to cool while you prepare the filo.
Trim the filo to fit a 35cm x 25cm baking tin. Brush the interior with some of the miso butter.
Place 1 sheet of filo on the base of the tin. Brush with some of the miso butter. Repeat with 4 more filo sheets, for a total of 5 miso buttered sheets.
Spread half of the nut mixture over the top filo sheet.
Top the nuts with 4 miso buttered filo sheets.
Spread the remaining nuts over the top filo sheet.
Finally, top the nuts with 5 miso buttered filo sheets.
Use a sharp knife to cut deep lines into the pastry to create either diamonds or squares.
Bake the baklava for 1 hour on the bottom rack of your oven for 1 hour.
Shortly before it’s done, place the sugar in a small saucepan with 400ml water.
Stir to dissolve over medium heat and add a slice of lemon.
Cook until the sugar syrup reaches 106°C. If you don’t have a food thermometer, cook until the syrup reduces to the consistency of runny honey. This should take 10 to 15 mins.
Pour the syrup over the hot baklava and leave it to cool to room temperature. Once cooled, you can tuck in and enjoy.

name: Miso Butter & Sausage Pasta
description: Red miso is the funkier, saltier and sharper sister of white miso. Combine it with crispy, slightly sweet pork and cabbage for a flavourful fusion. Seema x
instructions: Bring a pot full of water on to boil. Heat up the oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Remove sausage meat from their casings and add to the pan along with chilli flakes, cook until nicely golden, about 6 mins.
Pop the pasta in boiling water and cook according to package instructions. Reserve the pasta water.
Meanwhile, chop up the cabbage into large 5cm pieces.
Grate the garlic into the sausage mix and add the cabbage. Stir well until the cabbage has wilted, 3-4 mins.
Mix the miso, mirin and butter with a splash of pasta water into a small bowl. Then, pour into the browned sausage mix.
Toss in the cooked pasta, grate in the parmesan and lots of freshly ground black pepper. Mix well, adding more pasta water if it starts to look dry.
Serve up with more parmesan and some black pepper.

name: Miso Butter Air Fryer Roast Chicken
description: Discover a delectable twist on classic roast chicken with our Miso Butter Air Fryer Roast Chicken recipe. This dish takes advantage of the air fryer’s unique cooking method to deliver a juicy, perfectly roasted whole chicken with an irresistible miso butter glaze. The air fryer roast chicken combines the savoury richness of miso with the crispy texture achieved through air-frying, offering a healthier alternative to traditional roasting. The miso butter adds a delightful umami flavour that permeates the chicken, making it a standout at any meal. Ideal for a quick weeknight dinner or a festive Sunday roast, this recipe ensures tender, flavorful chicken with minimal effort. Perfectly cooked with a golden-brown exterior and succulent interior, our air fryer roast chicken promises to be a new favourite in your cooking repertoire.
keywords: Miso Butter Air Fryer Roast Chicken Recipe
Miso Butter Air Fryer Roast Chicken
instructions: Tip the softened butter into a bowl, then spoon in the miso. Zest in the lime, then peel and finely grate in the garlic and do the same with the ginger. Add a pinch of salt and pepper, then mix really well. Set aside.
Line the air fryer basket with foil.

Starting from the neck end, gently pry the skin of the chicken away from the breast meat, making a large pocket underneath the skin, covering both breasts. Push down on the breast of the bird to gently flatten it (this is to make sure it doesn’t touch the element of the air fryer).
Spread the softened butter over the breast meat in an even layer.
Put the chicken into the lined basket, breast-side down, set the temperature to 180°C and set the timer to 35 mins. Cook!

After 35 mins, carefully flip the chicken so it’s breast-side up, spoon over some of the juices and butter and roast for 25 mins or until the skin is golden and crisp, the juices run clear and a temperature probe inserted at the thickest part of the chicken reaches 70°C.
Transfer the cooked chicken to a plate to rest with any juices and butter, then squeeze over the lime juice. Loosely cover with foil and leave to rest for 15 mins.
Cut the spring onions into 8cm pieces, then cut in half lengthways and thinly shred. Scatter over the chicken with the coriander leaves and sesame seeds to serve.

name: Miso Butter Mushrooms & Furikake Rice
description: Juicy miso butter mushrooms with seasoned fluffy rice. A simple meal that's so satisfying to eat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut the mushrooms into small, equal-sized pieces. If you are using enoki, just cut away the ends.
Whisk together the butter, miso and olive oil until you form a smooth marinade.

Lay two large pieces of silver foil in a bowl and place half of the mushrooms and the marinade into each. Place a chilli on top if using. Wrap it up tightly and place in an oven dish. Cook for 25 mins or until all the mushrooms are soft and cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to packet instructions and finely slice the spring onion.

To make the furikake seasoning, add the two nori sheets to a blender and blitz until you have very small pieces, taking care not to turn it into a powder. Then add the sugar, two tablespoons of sesame seeds, salt and chilli flakes if using. Pulse until fine, again taking care not to over process into a dust. Empty out into a small bowl and mix through the last tablespoon of sesame seeds.
When the rice is cooked, divide into two bowls and spoon over plenty of furikake and top with some spring onion.

Remove the mushrooms from the oven when they are ready. Keeping them in the silver foil, place them in a bowl and open up the parcel. Don't forget to pour that delicious mushroom juice all over your rice!

name: Miso Butter Onions
description: The humble onion is transformed with just two additional ingredients - miso paste and butter. Recipe from Flavour by Yotam Ottolenghi and Ixta Belfrage.
instructions: Heat your oven to 240°C fan/464°F.
Halve your onions lengthways and discard the papery skin. Trim any dry tops and carefully trim the base, ensuring that your onion halves remain whole.
Melt your butter in a large pan or in a heatproof bowl in the microwave. Add your miso paste and a litre of warm water, then whisk together until you have a homogenous sauce.
Place your onions cut side down in a large, high-sided baking tray. Pour over your miso water, then tightly cover with tin foil. Bake for 35 minutes.

Remove your tray from the oven, discard your foil and flip your onions over. Give the onions a good baste with a spoon, then return to the oven. Bake for another 45-50 minutes, basting well every 10 minutes. Your onions should be deeply golden and soft with gentle charring around the edges. Your sauce will be lovely, thick and golden.
Transfer your onions to your chosen serving plate and pour your lovely sauce all over the top. Serve whilst still hot and juicy.

name: Miso Butter Roast Chicken & Radishes
description: A rich roast chicken dish with caramelised radishes and mushrooms, finished with a luscious miso butter sauce. Perfect for a comforting yet classy meal.
keywords: Miso Butter Roast Chicken & Radishes recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan. Make sure your butter is at room temperature.

Generously season the chicken thighs with salt and black pepper. Place them skin-side down into an ovenproof frying pan over medium heat. Cook undisturbed for 8-10 minutes until the skin is golden brown. Transfer to a plate, skin-side up.
In the same pan, add the halved radishes and mushrooms sliced into 1cm-sized chunks. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until golden brown.
Pour in the chicken stock and rice vinegar, bring to a boil, then place the chicken skin-side up back on top.
Transfer the pan to the oven and roast for 25-30 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
Reheat the rice and divide it into serving boxes.
Once the chicken is cooked, place it on top of the rice with the roasted vegetables.
Whisk the miso, mirin, butter, and half the sesame seeds into the pan juices. Drizzle over the chicken and rice.
Finish with the remaining sesame seeds and serve.

name: Miso Butter Salmon Rice
description: Sweet, salty, sticky miso butter slathered over salmon, paired with rice, zingy cucumber, and spring onion crunch. A dreamy weeknight bowl.
instructions: Preheat the grill to high heat. Rinse the sushi rice until the water runs clear, then cook with the measured water using your preferred method (rice cooker or saucepan). Set aside with the lid on to steam.
Season the salmon fillets with salt and leave to sit while you prep the rest.
In a small bowl, mix the softened butter with the white miso until smooth and combined.

Finely slice the cucumber and add to a bowl with the rice vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and the juice of half a lemon. Toss together and leave to lightly pickle. Then trim and thinly slice the spring onions and set aside for later.

Pat the salmon dry with kitchen paper and spread the miso butter evenly over the top of each fillet. Place under a hot grill for 4–6 mins until golden and cooked through, with the butter bubbling. If your salmon is browning too quickly, move the salmon lower in your grill.

Meanwhile, set a saucepan filled with water over medium heat and bring to the boil. Once, boiling, reduce the heat and carefully drop in your eggs. After 5-6 minutes remove and place in a bowl of cold water. Once they're cool enough to handle peel the shell off.
Fluff the rice and divide between bowls. Top each portion with a salmon fillet and any of the miso butter from the tray. Finish with the sliced spring onion and a pile of the pickled cucumber.

name: Miso Caramel Apple Overnight Oats
description: Sticky dates and miso blend into an addictive miso caramel flavour in these overnight oats. Combined with grated apple, cinnamon and topped with vanilla yoghurt and blueberries, this makes for a delicious, fuss-free breakfast.
keywords: Miso Caramel Apple Overnight Oats recipe
instructions: Coarsely grate the apples into a large bowl, discarding the cores. Chop the dates into 2cm chunks and add them to the bowl along with all the remaining oat ingredients. Mix well, then taste and add a touch more maple syrup if you'd like it sweeter.
If you're making ahead, you can portion into containers at this point, otherwise just cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or until ready to serve.
To serve, spoon into bowls and top with a dollop of vanilla yoghurt, a handful of blueberries and an extra drizzle of maple syrup.

name: Miso Caramel Chocolate Mousse
description: The easiest chocolate mousse, with minimal tricky techniques and setting times. The chocolate paired with miso caramel is heavenly. Another lovely Ocado recipe.
instructions: Place your toffees in a saucepan with your milk and gently heat until the toffees have melted. Stir to bring it together as a smooth sauce. Add your miso paste and mix to combine.
Divide your mixture between 6 ramekins, or into one large one. Allow to cool.

Cut your chocolate up into small pieces and add it to a saucepan along with your mini marshmallows and butter. Set the pan over a gentle heat and occasionally stir until melted. Remove the pan from the heat and allow it to cool a little.
Pour your double cream into a bowl and whisk it until it forms medium-stiff, soft peaks.
Fold your cream into your chocolate bowl until you have a totally combined mixture.
Pour your chocolate mix on top of your caramel in the ramekins and smooth the top so you have an even surface. Allow to set in the fridge for 30 mins.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Miso Caramels
description: Sticky, sweet and slightly savoury miso caramels. These are so quick to make and are perfect for anyone with a sweet tooth.
instructions: Grease a square tin and line with baking paper.
Whisk the miso, honey, double cream, caster sugar, light brown sugar in a pan until completely dissolved. Add in the butter and bring to a boil.

Cook for 15 mins or until a thermometer inserted reads 125°C. To check its ready, add a small amount into a glass of cold water. If it's the right temp, you should be able to roll it up into a soft ball.
Pour into the lined square tin, and tap it on the surface a few times to remove the bubbles. Sprinkle liberally with sea salt and allow to cool fully (will take around 2 hours).
Slice into bite-sized pieces and enjoy.

name: Miso Chicken, Sesame Broccoli & Rice
description: This high-protein packed lunch is next-level. Juicy miso chicken, nutty sesame broccoli, and sticky rice.
instructions: Start by mixing the miso paste, rice vinegar and sugar in a bowl. Rub the mixture all over the chicken breasts and set aside to marinate while you prep everything else.

Rinse the rice 2–3 times under cold water until it runs clear. Add to a lidded saucepan with the water and a pinch of salt. Set over a medium heat. Once simmering, pop the lid on, reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 mins. Turn off the heat and leave to steam for another 10 mins. Fluff with a fork.
Cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets and place in a heatproof bowl with a splash of water. Cover and microwave for 2½ mins until tender. Drain and toss with the soy sauce and sesame seeds.

Heat the butter and vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once sizzling, add the chicken breasts and cook for 4 mins on one side. Flip and cook for another 4–5 mins until golden and cooked through (you might need a little longer depending on the size of the breast). Turn off the heat and leave to rest in the pan for 3–4 mins.

Slice the chicken and plate everything up into Tupperware containers — fluffy rice, sesame broccoli and juicy miso chicken. Spoon over any buttery pan sauce and finish with a lemon wedge. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Miso Chicken, Sesame Broccoli & Rice
description: This one-pan weeknight dinner is next-level. Juicy miso chicken, nutty sesame broccoli, and sticky rice.
instructions: Start by mixing the miso paste, rice vinegar and sugar in a bowl. Rub the mixture all over the chicken breasts and set aside to marinate while you prep everything else.

Rinse the rice 2–3 times under cold water until it runs clear. Add to a lidded saucepan with the water and a pinch of salt. Set over a medium heat. Once simmering, pop the lid on, reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 mins. Turn off the heat and leave to steam for another 10 mins. Fluff with a fork.
Cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets and place in a heatproof bowl with a splash of water. Cover and microwave for 2½ mins until tender. Drain and toss with the soy sauce and sesame seeds.

Heat the butter and vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once sizzling, add the chicken breasts and cook for 4 mins on one side. Flip and cook for another 4–5 mins until golden and cooked through (you might need a little longer depending on the size of the breast). Turn off the heat and leave to rest in the pan for 3–4 mins.
Slice the chicken and plate everything up — fluffy rice, sesame broccoli and juicy miso chicken. Spoon over any buttery pan sauce and finish with a lemon wedge.

name: Miso Coriander Pesto
description: The combination of tahini, miso, and coriander in this pesto results in a creamy, herby sauce.
instructions: Add the coriander, miso and tahini to a blender. Peel the garlic clove and peel the ginger and roughly slice, then add in. Roughly chop the spring onions and add in. Add the lime juice and season generously with salt and pepper.
Add ⅓ of olive oil and begin to blend, then continue to add olive oil until you get to a thick pesto consistency.

name: Miso Egg Rice Bowl
description: Jammy soft-boiled eggs nestled over sushi rice, drizzled in a miso sesame dressing and topped with a bright, zingy sugar snap salad. A perfect veggie weeknight supper or a great meal prep lunch.
keywords: Miso Sesame Eggs over Sushi Rice with Sugar Snap Salad
Miso Sesame Eggs over Sushi Rice with Sugar Snap Salad recipe
instructions: Rinse the sushi rice in cold water until the water runs clear, then cook according to the packet instructions. Cover and set aside to keep warm.

Fill a medium saucepan with water and bring to a rolling boil. Lower the eggs in carefully and cook for 6 mins if they're at room temperature, or 6 mins 30 secs if they're coming straight from the fridge. If you're using large or small eggs you will need to adjust the time by a minute or so to get that jammy centre. Transfer immediately to a bowl of ice cold water and leave for 5 mins, then peel and set aside. The eggs can be boiled and peeled up to 2 days ahead, keep them unpeeled in the fridge and dress just before serving.

Make the miso sesame dressing. Whisk together the miso paste, sesame oil, rice wine vinegar, soy sauce and honey until smooth. Add the warm water gradually, whisking until the dressing is loose and pourable. Stir through the toasted sesame seeds and taste, it should be salty, nutty and just slightly sweet.

Slice the sugar snaps thinly on the diagonal and finely slice the spring onions. Pick the coriander leaves. Juice the limes into a bowl, add the sesame oil and toss everything together with a pinch of salt.

Divide the sushi rice between bowls. Halve the eggs and nestle four halves into each bowl. Spoon the miso sesame dressing generously over the eggs and rice. Pile the sugar snap salad alongside, scatter over the chilli flakes and serve.

name: Miso Garlic Salmon with Coconutty Quinoa & Green Beans
description: I’ve never been a salmon lover but this was the recipe that truly converted me. The salmon is marinated in a savoury, umami, punchy concoction that goes so nicely with the soothing creamy and coconutty quinoa - you seriously won't miss rice. It's a proper midweek banger.
keywords: Miso Garlic Salmon with Coconutty Quinoa & Green Beans
Miso Garlic Salmon with Coconutty Quinoa & Green Beans recipe
instructions: To make the marinade, grate in the garlic and add the miso, honey and rice vinegar to a small bowl. Whisk until combined. If you can't find red miso, white will work just as well.
Lay the salmon fillets in a large baking tray skin side up and spoon over the marinade.

For the quinoa, add the quinoa, coconut milk (make sure it's light full fat will make the quinoa too stodgy) and water to a saucepan. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 20 mins, until the liquid has absorbed and the quinoa is fully cooked. Remove the lid and fluff with a fork. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat the grill to high. Add the green beans to the baking tray alongside the salmon, drizzle with the olive oil and season with salt and black pepper.

Slide under the grill for 5-10 mins, until the salmon flakes into big chunks with a slight blush in the centre. Keep an eye on it, cooking time depends on the thickness of your fillets, and the fish will keep cooking a little once it's out of the grill.
Finely slice the spring onions and cut the lime into wedges. Divide the coconut quinoa between bowls and top with the salmon, green beans, spring onions, a lime wedge and the sesame seeds.

name: Miso Gochujang Salmon & Nori Rice
description: Take your Zingy Green Miso Salmon batch to new heights by pairing it with our fluffy nori rice and a sweet-spicy Gochujang drizzle. It's a belter.
keywords: miso gochujang salmon and nori rice
instructions: Before you begin, make the Zingy Green Miso Salmon batch recipe.
Rinse the rice under cold water until it runs clear, then cook following pack instructions.

Meanwhile, tear up the nori sheet and add it to a food processor with the butter. Blitz until the nori is fully broken down and combined with the butter. Scrape into a bowl, stir through two-thirds of the sesame seeds and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the Gochujang and honey. Add a splash of water and stir to loosen into a drizzly sauce.

Stir the nori butter into the cooked rice and share between plates. Reheat the salmon and veg in the microwave and place on top. Finish with a drizzle of Gochujang honey sauce and a sprinkling of sesame seeds.

name: Miso Grilled Cabbage
description: Charred cabbage drizzled with an incredible creamy tahini miso dressing. Soft + crisp. The perfect side to any dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Get your griddle pan on and prepare the cabbages. Remove the outer leaves from the cabbage and slice into half then into quarters. Brush the quarters with sesame oil and when the griddle pan is hot, add in the cabbage quarters, two at a time, until nicely charred. Turn the cabbages half way through and brush each side with extra oil.
Once griddled, put all the cabbage halves into a baking tray and lightly roast in the oven for 8 minutes.
For the dressing, mix together the miso, tahini, soy, grated ginger, mirin and a splash of water.
Separate the coriander leaves and stalks. Plate up the cabbage and drizzle over your miso dressing. Sprinkle the sesame seeds and coriander leaves on top then tuck in!

name: Miso Maple Chicken with Rice
description: Sweet, salty and addictive. This miso-maple-glazed chicken is served with fluffy rice and a crunchy, zingy edamame salad.
instructions: Butterfly the chicken breasts and season both sides with salt and pepper. Crush the garlic cloves, discarding the skins.
Stir the maple syrup, soy sauce, miso and water together in a small bowl. Set aside.

Thinly slice the cucumber. Defrost the edamame. Fill a kettle and bring to the boil. Add the spinach to a colander and pour over the boiling water until wilted. Let it cool slightly, then squeeze out any excess water.
Tip the sliced cucumber into a bowl, stir the vinegar in, season with salt and set aside.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add the olive oil. Pat the chicken dry, then place into the pan. Cook for 8–10 mins, flipping halfway, until golden on both sides.
Add the garlic and pour in the miso-maple mixture. Let it bubble away, basting the chicken as it cooks, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through. Add a splash more water if needed.
Reheat the rice. Stir the edamame, spinach and sesame seeds through the cucumber to make the salad.
Share the rice between plates and top with the glazed chicken and crunchy salad. Spoon over any leftover glaze from the pan.

name: Miso Maple Chicken with Rice
description: Sweet, salty and addictive. This miso-maple-glazed chicken is served with fluffy rice and a crunchy, zingy edamame salad. Perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Butterfly the chicken breasts and season both sides with salt and pepper. Crush the garlic cloves, discarding the skins.
Stir the maple syrup, soy sauce, miso and water together in a small bowl. Set aside.

Thinly slice the cucumber. Defrost the edamame. Fill a kettle and bring to the boil. Add the spinach to a colander and pour over the boiling water until wilted. Let it cool slightly, then squeeze out any excess water.
Tip the sliced cucumber into a bowl, season with salt and set aside.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add the olive oil. Pat the chicken dry, then place into the pan. Cook for 8–10 mins, flipping halfway, until golden on both sides.
Add the garlic and pour in the miso-maple mixture. Let it bubble away, basting the chicken as it cooks, until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze and the chicken is cooked through.
Reheat the rice. Stir the edamame, spinach, rice vinegar and sesame seeds through the cucumber to make the salad.

Share the rice between Tupperware containers and top with the glazed chicken and crunchy salad. Spoon over any leftover glaze from the pan. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch - they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Miso Maple Ramen Eggs
description: These umami-packed eggs are sweet, salty, spicy and seriously addictive. Perfect with sticky rice, noodles or eaten straight from the fridge.
instructions: Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs gently and boil for 6 mins for that jammy centre. Once done, plunge into a bowl of iced water and chill for 3-5 mins. If you haven’t got any ice, just leave the, in a bowl under cold running water.

Meanwhile, peel the garlic and give it a bash. Chuck it into a medium bowl or container with the soy sauce, maple syrup, miso paste, rice vinegar, chilli flakes and water (ingredient quantity). Give everything a good stir until the miso dissolves.

Carefully peel the eggs, then pop them into the marinade. Make sure they’re fully submerged – weigh them down with a small plate or cover with some kitchen towel. Place everything into a sealed container.
Pop them in the fridge and chill overnight. The longer they sit, the more flavour they soak up.

Slice in half and serve with ramen, rice bowls or just snack on them cold, no judgement here!
These eggs will last for up to 4 days in the fridge, the flavour gets stronger each day.

name: Miso Mushroom Bean Bowl
description: A filling, tasty, and high-protein bean bowl that's completely vegan. It doesn't get much healthier than this.
instructions: Soak the cashews in boiling water for 15 mins until plump and soft. Meanwhile, roughly tear up the mushrooms with your hands and dice the onion.
Fry the mushrooms in a stainless steel frying pan for 7-8 mins with a little olive oil and salt, until they begin to crisp up and turn a nice shade of brown. Remove and set aside.
Pour all the cashew cream ingredients into a blender and blitz until you have a thick, silky and pourable paste. Season to taste.

In the same frying pan (no need to clean), fry the diced onion in plenty of olive oil with a pinch of salt for 6 mins. Add the garlic and fry for 2 mins. Finely grate the tofu directly into the pan and fry for 5 mins.

Tip in the butter beans and their juices. Bring to a simmer, stirring frequently for 10-15 mins. Add half the crispy fried mushrooms, 4 tbsp cashew cream and the soy sauce or tamari. Stir well and season to taste. ​​Add a splash of water if you want it saucier.
Meanwhile, blanch the cavolo nero in boiling water and transfer it to a bowl. Add olive oil, a squeeze of lemon, salt and pepper to make a lemony cavolo nero oil.
Decorate with the rest of the cream, mushrooms, chives, the lemony cavolo nero oil, sesame seeds and plenty more extra virgin olive oil. Serve with crusty sourdough.

name: Miso Mushroom Gravy
description: This miso mushroom gravy is so delicious and so easy to make, you might never go back to instant gravy again.
instructions: Put the dried mushrooms in a heatproof bowl and pour over 300ml boiling water from the kettle. Set aside and leave to soak.
Chop the onion and the mushrooms.
Heat the butter in a medium saucepan over a low-medium heat, and cook the onion for about 5 mins until translucent.
Add the mushrooms and season well with salt and pepper. Cook for another 8-10 mins until softened.
Boil the kettle and add 800ml of boiling water to a heatproof bowl. Add two stock cubes, the miso and 1 heaped tbsp of flour. Whisk well until there are no lumps.
Add this stock to the pot along with the dried mushrooms and their soaking liquid. Take care not to add the grit at the bottom of the bowl.

Gently simmer for 10-15 mins to thicken, then blend with an immersion stick blender or in a blender. Add the smaller amount of soy sauce, taste and season with salt and pepper. Then taste and decide if you would like to add a little more soy sauce.

Return to the heat if you want to thicken it up. 
Enjoy immediately or store it in the fridge for up to 3 days and heat it up gently on the hob or in the microwave.
Will keep frozen for up to three months.

name: Miso Mushroom Noodles With Edamame
description: A whack of mint adds some freshness to this high-protein noodle recipe.
instructions: Tip the rice noodles into a large bowl and cover with boiling water.
Make the dressing by whisking the miso with 3 tbsp olive oil and the juice of 1 ½ lemons. Season with salt and pepper.

Roughly chop the mushrooms. Add a tbsp of olive oil to a pan and add the mushrooms along with a pinch of salt. Fry for 5-7 mins, until golden. Meanwhile finely chop (or grate) the garlic. Once the mushrooms are golden, add the garlic to the pan and cook for 2 mins further and then remove from the heat.
Drain the noodles and rinse with cold water to remove any starch. Then add to a large bowl, add the edamame, beansprouts, and most of the mint leaves. Add the dressing and toss well.
Swirl the noodles into bowls and top with garlic-y mushrooms, toasted sesame seeds and fresh mint. Serve with the remaining lemon half, cut into wedges.

name: Miso Mushroom Quiche
description: This miso mushroom pie is umami, creamy and flaky, served with a bright wafu style sauce to balance the flavours.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C.
Place the dried mushrooms in a heatproof bowl and cover with boiling water. Set aside.
Drain the dried mushrooms and keep the broth to one side.
Chop the fresh and dried mushrooms and stir fry until browned and cooked through. Add 2 tbsp of soy sauce and sauté for another minute or two.
Remove the tofu from the packet and pat it dry. Add it to a blender with the miso and milk, plus 100ml of the mushroom broth. Blend until very smooth, taste and season well with plenty of pepper.
Mix the mushrooms through the tofu.

If using filo pastry and a cake tin, remove the pastry from the packet and cover with a wet tea towel to stop it from drying out. Lay a circle of parchment paper at the bottom of the tin and brush the sides with olive oil. Lay the sheets one over the other, brushing each with a little oil to help them stick. Hang the extra filo over the side, you can trim this down after. Make sure all of the filo is brushed with oil to prevent it burning.

Pour the tofu mushroom mix into the pastry and smooth out the top. Sprinkle the top with plenty of black and white sesame seeds. Bake for 35-45 mins or until it’s set and starting to brown on the top.
Allow to cool for 10 mins before serving.
To make the sauce, finely slice the chilli and spring onion. Whisk them together with 2 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp rice wine vinegar, 1 tbsp mirin and 1 tbsp soy sauce.
To serve, drizzle a teaspoon of the sauce over individual slices. Keep in the fridge and warm leftovers in the microwave or covered with foil in the oven.

name: Miso Mushroom Soba Noodle Soup
description: A light and refreshing soup, perfect for a summer's day. Filled with lots of crispy mushrooms and soft tofu, this one is super easy to throw together.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pan over a medium heat and fry your wild mushrooms with cumin seeds, chilli flakes, and a large pinch of salt for about 10 mins until crisp . Finish with soy sauce and cook for another minute.

Smash the ginger and garlic with the back of your knife to bruise. Add to a saucepan with the miso paste, honey and water. Mix well, then bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring a pan of salted water to a boil. Cook the soba noodles according to package instructions.
Dice the tofu and add to the soup. Then drop in the spinach to wilt.
Add the noodles to a bowl, ladle over the soup and top with crispy mushrooms, sesame seeds and a drizzle of sesame oil.

name: Miso Onion Beans & Greens
description: A simple veggie dish featuring slow-roasted onions, buttery miso beans, and tender greens. Perfect for a comforting and nourishing meal with deep, savoury flavours.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan.

Arrange the quartered onions, finely sliced garlic, and drained butter beans on a large baking tray.
TOP TIP: Make sure to add the mixture into an appropriate sized tray, if the tray is huge, and you don't have much in it, the liquid will evaporate quicker
In a bowl, whisk together the melted butter, miso paste, stock cube, and water until combined. Pour over the onions and beans. Cover the tray with foil.
Roast for 30 mins, then remove the foil and roast for another 30 mins until the onions are charred and tender. Remove the leaves from the stems of the cavolo nero and slice them up.
Stir in the cavolo nero and return to the oven for another 5 mins until wilted.
Reheat the rice, remove beans from the oven, and squeeze in the lime juice. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper.
To serve, divide into bowls and drizzle with chilli oil.

name: Miso Onion Soup
description: A simple and delicious tray soup that's worth simmering up on the weekend.
instructions: Heat your oven to 240°C.
Halve your onions lengthways and discard the papery skin. Trim any dry tops and carefully trim the base, ensuring that your onion halves remain whole.
Melt your butter in a large pan or in a heatproof bowl in the microwave. Add your miso paste and a litre of warm water, then whisk together until you have a homogenous sauce.
