Place your onions cut-side down in a large, high-sided baking tray. Slice up your ginger into thin coins. Pour over your miso water, then add in your ginger and rice before tightly covering it with tin foil. Bake for 35 mins.

Remove your tray from the oven, discard your foil and flip your onions over. Give the onions a good baste with a spoon, then return to the oven. Bake for another 45-50 mins, basting well every 10 mins. Your onions should be deeply golden and soft with gentle charring around the edges. Your sauce will be lovely, thick and golden. After you’ve removed your onions, turn your oven down to 180°C.
Transfer your mixture to a pot with your vegetable stock, stir, and then blitz. Finish with a squeeze of lime juice.

Slice up your bread into rough cubes. Add your cubes of bread to a roasting tray, cover with olive oil and roast for 10 mins. Once they’re looking brown, top with a generous grating of Gruyére and add back into the oven until the cheese is melted.
Serve the soup into bowls, top with your croutons, lime zest, and more olive oil.

name: Miso Pea Pesto Udon
description: Miso pea pesto udon - my take on a umami pesto recipe. A super comforting dish that's packed full of flavour and only takes 15 mins to make! Xien x
instructions: To make your pesto, add basil, mint, sunflower seeds, peeled garlic, peas, green chillies, the zest of one lemon, the juice from two lemons, 2 sheets of nori and miso to a food processor. Add most of your parmesan to your processor along with a large glug of olive oil (enough to bring it all together to a smooth consistency). Season with salt and pepper then blitz until smooth.
Cook your udon according to package instructions, reserving some of the noodle-cooking water for later.
Mix your pesto with the udon, adding a small ladle of noodle-cooking water at a time (enough to bring it all together).
Top each plate of udon with torn pieces of nori, grated parmesan and chilli oil. Enjoy!

name: Miso Salmon
description: A fresh and flavour-packed flaky miso salmon. Pair it with whatever you like for a nutritious and delicious lunch.
keywords: Miso Salmon Spring Green Noodle Salad
Miso Salmon Spring Green Noodle Salad recipe
instructions: Mince the ginger. Put all the marinade ingredients into a bowl and add the salmon fillets, tossing well to coat. Set aside in the fridge. You can marinate the salmon up to 24 hours in advance, or use it immediately.
Put the marinated salmon fillets skin side down onto a baking tray lined with foil. Turn the grill to 200°C and, when hot, cook the salmon for just 7 mins. Remove and set aside.
Garnish your salmon with toasted sesame seeds and pair it with your favourite base.

name: Miso Salmon & Green Tea with Rice
description: Inspired by Japanese ochazuke, this cosy bowl features fragrant green tea broth, sesame rice, flaky miso salmon and an umami-packed spring onion condiment.
keywords: miso salmon and green tea rice
instructions: Tear the nori into pieces and tip into a blender with half of the sesame seeds. Blitz into a rough powder. Stir through the remaining sesame seeds and set aside.
Trim and thinly slice the spring onions. Add the spring onion whites into a bowl with the toasted sesame oil, white miso, mirin and the nori sesame mixture. Stir until well combined and set aside.

Pour the dashi into a saucepan and bring to the boil. Once boiling, lower the heat and add the green tea teabags, mirin and shoyu soy sauce. Let it steep for 3–4 mins, then fish out the teabags. Taste and adjust seasoning with a splash more mirin or shoyu if needed — but don’t go too hard, the miso condiment will bring extra saltiness.

To serve, divide the cooked rice between bowls. Pour over the green tea broth, then top with flaked salmon and a generous spoonful of the spring onion miso condiment. Add a dab of wasabi, if you like a kick and finish with some spring onion greens.

name: Miso Salmon & Noodles
description: These miso salmon noodles are seriously hard to beat. The creamy nori noodles are seriously cooling on a hot day and the cucumber pickle really ties the entire dish together. Plus it's packing more than 45g of protein per serving.
instructions: Bring a large pan of water to the boil and cook the noodles according to packet instructions. Once cooked, drain and rinse thoroughly under cold running water. Add the tahini, soy sauce, ice cubes, rice vinegar and nori to a blender. Blitz until smooth and creamy. Toss the cold noodles through the dressing until well coated. Set aside.

Preheat the grill to medium-high. In a bowl, mix together the miso, mirin, maple syrup, the zest of the lemon and grated ginger. Add the salmon fillets and coat thoroughly. You can marinate for up to 24 hours or use straight away. Place the salmon fillets, skin-side down, on a foil-lined baking tray. Grill for 7–10 mins, until lightly charred and cooked through.
Make the cucumber salad. Finely slice the cucumber and add to a bowl with the chilli oil, rice vinegar, sesame seeds, and a good pinch of salt. Toss to coat and set aside.

If you're making it, prepare the spring onion dressing. Finely slice the spring onions and mince the ginger. Place in a heatproof bowl with the salt, MSG (if using), and sugar. Heat the oil in a small pan over high heat until smoking hot. Carefully pour it over the spring onion mix and allow it to sizzle. Stir well and let sit for at least 5 mins to infuse.
Divide the noodles between containers or bowls. Top with grilled salmon and cucumber salad, then drizzle generously with the spring onion dressing.

name: Miso Salmon & Spicy Smacked Cucumber Salad
description: Take your Zingy Greens & Miso Salmon Traybake leftovers to the next level with this smacked cucumber salad. Perfect for a hot day lunch or no cook dinner.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Zingy Greens & Miso Salmon Traybake batch recipe.
Stir all the chilli oil dressing ingredients together in a large mixing bowl.
In a separate small bowl, mix the tahini dressing ingredients together with a splash of cold water until you’ve got a smooth, spoonable consistency.
Flake the cooked miso salmon. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions.
Trim the cucumber and cut into quarters width ways. Using something heavy (like a rolling pin or meat mallet), smack the cucumber until it splits and cracks. Chop into rough 2cm chunks.
Chuck the smashed cucumber, spring onions, miso salmon and green veg from the batch, sesame seeds into the chilli oil dressing and toss well to coat.
Spoon the tahini dressing across the base of your plates. Pile the cucumber salad over the top and spoon over any leftover chilli oil dressing.

name: Miso Salmon Burgers
description: The charred misoey salmon patties are out of this world. Garlicky, fresh smacked cucumber. All in a charred brioche bun. So, so good.
instructions: Roughly chop the salmon fillets. Put half into a food processor and blitz to a paste. Add the miso, ginger, lime zest, the rest of the salmon and 1 tbsp of soy sauce. Pulse very briefly until roughly combined. You want some nice chunky bits of salmon in with the paste rather than it all turned into mush.
Tip the mix into a bowl and stir through the panko breadcrumbs. Shape into four burgers and chill whilst you make the smacked cucumbers.

Now the fun part. Get a rolling pin or something heavy and hit the cucumber until it has collapsed and starts to break. Cut into random diagonal pieces. Place in a bowl and stir in the salt. Leave to sit for 10 minutes to draw out some of the water from the cucumber.
Dressing time. Grab a bowl. Crush in the garlic cloves and mix with 1 tbsp of Sriracha sauce, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp of soy sauce, sugar and lime juice.
Mix the remaining Sriracha sauce with the mayonnaise.
Pour a drizzle of oil into a non-stick frying pan. Fry the salmon burgers for 3 minutes on each side.

Assembly time. Drain the water off the cucumbers and mix with the dressing. Cut the buns in half, (toast in the frying pan if you like), spread the bottom of each bun with the sriracha mayo. Top each with a salmon burger and pile on the smacked cucumber slaw. Drizzle over the dressing. Bam.

name: Miso Salmon Spring Green Noodle Salad
description: A fresh and flavour-packed green noodle salad with flaky miso salmon. Yes, please.
keywords: Miso Salmon Spring Green Noodle Salad
Miso Salmon Spring Green Noodle Salad recipe
instructions: Finely mince the ginger. Put all the marinade ingredients into a bowl and add the salmon fillets, tossing well to coat. Set aside in the fridge. You can marinate the salmon up to 24 hours in advance, or use it immediately.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil and add salt as you would with pasta water. Cut the broccoli into bite-sized pieces, if you like.
Meanwhile, combine all the noodle sauce ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.

Cook the broccoli in the boiling water for 1 min, then use a slotted spoon to set aside in a bowl. Add the peas to the pot and cook for just 1 min, then remove using a slotted spoon or sieve. Roughly chop half of the peas to release the sweet flavour, if you like.
Cook the noodles in the same water, then strain and rinse very well in a bowl of cold water, then strain again. Toss in 1 tsp sesame oil and set aside so they don’t stick.
Put the marinated salmon fillets onto a baking tray lined with foil. Turn the grill to 200°C and, when hot, cook the salmon for just 7 mins. Remove and set aside.

Toss the noodles and veg with the sauce in a large bowl. Divide between serving plates, then finish with a fillet of salmon on top and garnish with toasted sesame seeds. Serve with lemon wedges on the side.

name: Miso Sweet Corn With Togarashi Yoghurt
description: Shichi-mi tōgarashi is one of many Japanese flavour bombs, transforming something simple into something incredible. Make a jar and use on noodles or veggies.
instructions: Peel your oranges carefully, trying to avoid the white pith as it’s bitter. Toast them in the oven at 100°C for 45- 55 mins or until they are totally dry. You can also remove them a bit earlier and let them finish drying out at room temperature, which might take another day (to save you some electricity).

Use a spice grinder or a good blender to grind the ingredients for the togarashi. Blitz the orange into a powder. Blitz the nori into fine flakes. Blitz the pepper flakes and sichuan peppercorns together. Pulse the sesame seeds until just broken down. Mix everything together adding the ground ginger here. 
Mix the red pepper and Sichuan peppercorns last and slowly to your taste as it can be very spicy.
Melt 3 tbsp butter and whisk with 1 tbsp miso paste.
Mix the yoghurt with 1 tbsp togarashi and the juice of half a lime and season with salt. Taste and add more togarashi if you like.
Microwave sweetcorn in the husk for 3 ½ mins. If you are using hulled corn (without husks), you can microwave them in a tupperware with a little water in the bottom and the lid slightly ajar.
To serve, brush the corn with miso butter. Smother the whole corn with yoghurt using the back of a spoon. Finish with more togarashi, black sesame seeds, chives and orange zest.

name: Miso Tahini Roast Sweet Potato Bowls
description: Nothing more, nothing less than a bowl of total goodness. Charred tender stem broccoli, the softest sweet potatoes, and the creamiest miso-tahini dressing.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Start by peeling the skins of your potatoes and chopping them up into large chunks. Place them onto a baking tray and pour a drizzle of oil over the top, 1 tsp chilli flakes and a pinch of salt and mix everything together with your hands. Place into the oven for 45 minutes.

Tahini time. Into a small bowl, add your tahini, your remaining chilli flakes, miso paste, white wine vinegar and 3 tbsp of warm water. Next, peel and grate your ginger into the bowl and mix together until smooth.
Place your broccoli onto a baking tray. Drizzle over a glug of vegetable oil, a sprinkle of salt, 2 tsp of sesame oil and mix together. Place into the oven for 15 minutes.
Into a frying pan, add your cashew nuts with a sprinkling of salt and a tsp of sesame oil. Cook until they begin to brown.

Serving time, start with some sweet potato and some broccoli. Slice up your avocados and add half to the bowl. Drizzle your tahini sauce over the top, followed a small handful of cashews. Roughly chop up your coriander and sprinkle a handful over the top. Repeat for the rest of your MOB and tuck into this fresh little dish. Enjoy!

name: Miso Walnut Double-Thick Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Unashamedly thick cookies inspired by the Levain Bakery in New York – thick and gooey in the middle (when warm) and crisp on the edge. A winner!
keywords: Miso Walnut Double-Thick Chocolate Chip Cookies
instructions: To make the miso walnuts, heat together the mirin, caster sugar and white miso over a medium heat. When boiling, add the toasted walnuts and mix together, cooking for 2 mins more over a low heat until thickened. Remove from the pan and leave to cool completely before using.
To make the cookies, cream the butter with the sugars until well combined but not aerated – it should look a little fluffy.
Whisk in the egg, scraping down as needed to make sure it’s evenly combined. Sift the dry ingredients together, then fold through the emulsified butter/egg mixture.
Add the walnuts and stir through to break them up a bit before mixing in the chocolate. Form into loose 180g balls, keeping them looking and feeling airy!
At this stage you can chill the dough overnight if you like, or you can bake right away. I didn’t notice a super significant difference.
Preheat the oven to 170°C. Line a large, flat baking tray with baking paper.
Spread the balls of dough on the baking tray. Bake for 18 mins (though you could do 16 mins or up to 20 mins to suit your taste!).

Leave to cool completely on a cooling rack. Sprinkle a little extra salt on top if you like and then leave to cool. Ideally enjoy whilst still a little bit warm, but they are just as good completely cooled! The texture will change from gooey to more firm.

name: Miso, Pecan & Maple Roasted Parsnips
description: Sticky, salty, sweet roasted roots with toasted pecans, thyme and umami-packed miso. Delicious.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Scrub the parsnips, don’t worry about peeling them. Halve any of the larger parsnips lengthways. Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil and pop the parsnips in for 5-6 mins. Drain and let steam dry.
Tip the blanched parsnips into a large roasting tray, drizzle with oil and a pinch of salt and pepper, toss to coat and arrange in a single layer, then roast for 35 mins.
Add the butter, miso, maple syrup and vinegar to a pot and bring to a boil. Reduce by a third. Pour over the parsnips and toss to coat. Sprinkle over the thyme and crumble over the pecans.
Return to the oven for 10 mins until glazy and lightly charred. Serve ‘em up to share.

name: Miso, Rosemary and Maple Glazed Ham
description: Nothing says winter like a roast ham. We've used miso to give salty, umami depth to this sticky, savoury glaze recipe.
instructions: Start by weighing the gammon joint and calculating the cook time. It's 20 mins per 450g plus an extra 20 mins.

Roughly chop the leek, carrot, onion, celery and halve the garlic. Get them into a large stock pot with the ham, bay, 3 of the rosemary sprigs and the peppercorns. Cover with cold water and bring to a simmer.
Cook in the simmering water for ⅔ of the total cooking time then allow to cool completely in the stock. Remove the skin with a small, sharp knife and score the fat.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan. To make the glaze, finely chop half the zest of the orange and the remaining rosemary. Add the sugar to a medium sized pan and cook over a low heat to a dark caramel.

Add a ladle of the ham stock (Keep the remaining stock, it makes delicious soup) and deglaze. If the caramel solidifies, simply set it over the heat to melt again. Now add the juice from half an orange, miso, maple syrup and vinegar along with your orange zest and rosemary. Bring to a boil and cook down for 2-3 minutes.
Brush the ham with some of the glaze. Slide into the oven to roast for the remaining cook time or until the ham is sticky, charred and caramelised. As it cooks, baste every 10 minutes with glaze.
Stuff into sandwiches with cheddar, good chutney and shredded lettuce for a killer snack.

name: Miso-Glazed Chicken with Sweet Potato & Edamame
description: Sticky miso glaze brings heaps of flavour to this speedy chicken meal prep lunch, loaded with tender sweet potato, greens and a nutty sesame crunch.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
For the marinade, peel and finely chop the garlic. Add it to a shallow bowl with the miso paste, soy sauce, honey and crunchy chilli oil. Whisk until smooth.
Score the chicken breasts in a criss-cross pattern to help the marinade sink in and speed up cooking. Add to the bowl and coat well. Transfer to a roasting tray.
Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into 3cm chunks, then toss them through the marinade.
Tip the potatoes into the roasting tray and slide into the oven. Roast for 20-25 mins, giving the sweet potato a toss halfway through.
With 5 mins to go, drizzle the broccoli with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Add the broccoli and edamame to the tray with the chicken and sweet potato.

Divide the sweet potato, edamame, broccoli and chicken between Tupperware containers. Scatter over the mint leaves and sesame seeds. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Miso-Glazed Chicken with Sweet Potato & Edamame
description: Sticky miso glaze brings heaps of flavour to this speedy chicken traybake, loaded with tender sweet potato, greens and a nutty sesame crunch.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. For the marinade, peel and finely chop the garlic. Add it to a shallow bowl with the miso paste, soy sauce, honey and crunchy chilli oil. Whisk until smooth.
Deeply score the chicken breasts in a criss-cross pattern to help the marinade sink in and speed up the cooking. Add to the bowl and coat well. Transfer to a roasting tray.
Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into 1.5cm chunks, then toss them through the marinade.

Tip the potatoes into the roasting tray with the chicken and slide into the oven. Roast for 20-25 mins, or until the chicken and sweet potato are cooked through, giving the sweet potato a toss halfway through.
With 5 mins to go, drizzle the broccoli with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Add the broccoli and edamame to the tray with the chicken and sweet potato.
To serve, divide the sweet potato, edamame, broccoli and chicken between plates. Scatter over the mint leaves and sesame seeds.

name: Miso-Glazed Parsnips
description: Glazed with miso and maple, piled on top of tahini yoghurt and drizzled with a homemade chilli butter, these are set to be the best parsnips of your life.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180ºC fan. Scrub your parsnips, there's no need to peel them here! Halve most of parsnips lengthways, cutting any chunkier ones into quarters. Tip into a roasting tray. Add a tbsp of oil and season with salt, toss well, slide into the oven and roast for 25-30 mins until soft and golden. They might need a little longer if your parsnips are much larger.

Meanwhile, make your chilli butter. Finely slice the red chilli and garlic, peel the ginger and cut into matchsticks. Add the butter to a pan over a low heat and cook for around 3-5 mins, whisking as you go, until it’s brown and smells a bit like digestive biscuits. Add the chilli, garlic, and ginger and cook for 2-3 mins further, it’ll look very frothy- don’t worry just keep stirring. Add the sesame seeds and chilli flakes and cook for a minute further, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Add the yoghurt to a bowl and add the tahini, then squeeze in the juice of half of the lime. Season with salt and whisk together. Set aside.

Whisk the miso and maple together. Add a splash of oil to loosen a little. Remove the parsnips from the oven, tip the glaze all over them and give them a good shake, then return to the oven for 3-5 mins, until sticky and golden.

Spoon the yoghurt over the base of the dish, top with the caramelised parsnips. Drizzle with the chilli butter. Slice the spring onions and scatter over the top along with the coriander leaves and some extra sesame seeds. Serve with the remaining lime half, cut into wedges, to squeeze over at the table.

name: Miso-Stuffed Ongiri
description: You'll find these handheld snacks all over Japan. They are perfect for eating on the go and easy snacking.
instructions: Tip the rice into a bowl and wash it in several changes of cold water until the water runs clear. Drain really well.

Add the rice to a small lidded saucepan with 300ml of water. Set over a medium heat and bring to a simmer. Cook for 1 minute, then turn the heat to very low, pop the lid on and cook gently for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave it to steam for another 10 minutes.
Take the lid off. Season the rice with a pinch of salt, then fold through the rice vinegar and sugar. Let the rice cool slightly until it’s just warm.

Lightly wet your hands and take a handful of rice. Use a spoon to place about ½ tsp of miso in the middle, then shape the rice around it. Use an onigiri mould if you’ve got one, or shape into a triangle with your hands. Compress the rice gently but don’t squash it. You should get around 4 ongiri (or 6 if you'd like them more bitesize).
Pop them in the fridge to firm up completely.
Cut the nori into strips about 3cm x 10cm. Sprinkle the furikake onto a plate, if using.

Wrap a strip of nori around each onigiri to make a makeshift handle, then roll two of the triangle’s sides in the furikake. 
Pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Mixed Berry Coulis
description: Level up your dessert game with this adaptable fruit coulis recipe. Use raspberries, blackberries, pitted stone fruit or any frozen berries.
instructions: Place all the ingredients in a medium-sized heavy-bottomed pan and bring to the boil over a gentle heat, stirring continuously. Reduce to a simmer and heat for 15 mins, or until thickened. Add a splash more water if necessary.
Allow to cool, then transfer the coulis to a liquidiser or use a hand blender to purée. Finally pass it through a sieve, pushing through as much of the pulp as possible and discarding any seeds.

name: Mob Fried Chicken
description: The ultimate speedy fried chicken. The spice combo is spot on. So easy. Crunchy on the outside. Tender, perfectly cooked chicken on the inside.
instructions: Use a sharp knife to cut the chicken legs in half where the drumstick and thigh meet - you will be able to feel the two knuckle joints with your hands.

Put 1 tbsp of salt, 2 tsp of smoked paprika, 2 tsp of oregano, 2 tsp of garlic powder and 2 tsp of onion powder in a bowl along with the chicken pieces. Mix well so that they are all evenly coated. Leave at room temp for 30-45 minutes, depending on how much time you have.

Get your dredging station ready. Mix the remaining spices, salt, plain flour and cornflour in a bowl. In a separate bowl, crack in 1 egg, whisk and stir in the buttermilk. Have a baking tray ready for your coated chicken.
One by one, dip the chicken pieces into the buttermilk mixture, followed by the flour mixture. Make sure each piece is completely covered. Transfer to the tray.
Fill up the biggest, deep, heavy-bottomed saucepan you have half way with oil. Put on a medium heat to maintain a steady temperature and heat until simmering.

To test that the oil is ready, mix 1 tsp of the leftover buttermilk with the flour to make a craggy dough. Drop it into the oil and you are looking for it to brown, puff up and rise to the surface in a minute - any quicker and the oil is too hot.
Starting with a tester, fry the chicken in batches for around 12 minutes until super crispy - turn once halfway.

Check the first one to make sure the chicken is cooked through. If the chicken browns too quickly on the outside but isn’t cooked all the way through, you will need to turn the temperature down on the oil. If you have a thermometer you want it to be 160°C/ 320°F. The temperature will drop once the cold chicken goes in so keep adjusting the heat. Don’t cook more than 3 pieces at once.
Transfer the fried chicken to a wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen roll. Sprinkle with sea salt. M.F.C done.

name: Mob's Apple Crumble
description: We've spent a long time perfecting this dish. With a crisp, golden top and a fruity, sweet base. Your go-to crumble. Enjoy.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/400°F.

Make your filling. Peel and core your apples, then dice into 2cm chunks. Place 3/4 of your apples into a medium sized saucepan along with your sugar, the juice from your lemon and your water. Bring to a simmer over a medium heat, then cook for 15 mins until the mixture is breaking down and turning nice and saucy. Add your remaining apples and stir to combine - these will hold their shape when the crumble bakes to give you juicy apple chunks. Set aside.

Dice your butter into 1/2cm chunks. Pour your flour, cinnamon and nutmeg into a large bowl, then add your butter and rub through with your fingertips until your butter has all broken down and coated your flour - this mixture should resemble fine yellow breadcrumbs. Add your oats, soft brown sugar and demerara sugar (reserving 2 tbsp for later), then continue to rub in until your mixture resembles small pebbles. Pop your bowl in the fridge to rest for 15 mins - this will ensure it stays biscuity and crisp when baked.
Transfer your apple mixture to a pie dish, then top with your crumble mixture. Sprinkle with your remaining demerara sugar.
Bake for 25-30 mins until you have a golden and crisp top. Serve with a big scoop of vanilla ice cream and dig in.

name: Mob's Bacon Röstis
description: Taking your brunch game to the next level with these crispy, bacon-y röstis. Topped with yoghurt, harissa and spring onions. Mouthful straight from heaven.
instructions: Slice your bacon into small pieces. Drizzle olive oil into a frying pan on a medium heat. Add your bacon and sauté until golden brown and crispy. Slice 3 of your spring onions, leaving one for later, and add them to the pan. Stir until they have softened and add the contents of the pan to a separate bowl, keeping the oil in the pan for later.
Grate your potatoes. Once grated, squeeze out excess juices so they are nice and dry for frying.

Then, add potato to your bacon along with a grinding of pepper and mix together. Next, take a handful of the grated potato and form a potato patty. Repeat this until you have run out of the potato mixture.
Re-heat the oil you saved earlier. Once hot, add your rösti’s to the pan and fry until golden brown on either side.

Time to plate up! Add 2 rösti’s to your plate along with a dollop of yoghurt and a tsp of harissa paste. Chop up your remaining spring onion and parsley and sprinkle over the top. Repeat for your MOB and tuck in.

name: Mob's Breakfast Frittata
description: It’s finally happened: A Full English inside a Frittata. You'll get it the moment you take your first bite of this Frankenstein beauty.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Chop up your bacon into bite-size chunks and add this to a frying pan on a medium heat.
Squeeze the meat out of your sausages and roll them into small balls. Add them to the bacon.
Chop up your mushrooms and add to the pan, giving everything a good stir. Add your tomatoes (whole) and stir. Allow everything to cook.

As everything begins to brown and the tomatoes are cooked, grate your garlic into the pan. Add a good grinding of pepper and salt. Add the spinach and stir until it begins to wilt. Take the pan off the heat.
Egg time! Crack all of your eggs into a large mixing bowl. Pour in your milk, add salt and pepper and whisk until smooth.
Pour the whisked egg into the frying pan, making sure you cover all of the food. Place the pan in the oven for 13 minutes.
Once it’s done, serve with a slice of sourdough and tuck into this wonderful breakfast.

name: Mob's Buddha Bowl
description: We spent a while perfecting our Buddha bowl. It hits the spot. Crispy kale. Crunchy veg. Lovely creamy tahini dressing. Delicious roast sweet potatoes. Go on...
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into medium sized chunks. Put onto a roasting tray, drizzle with olive oil and add 1 miso paste sachet. Season with salt and pepper. Toss everything together and roast for 40 minutes until soft.
Quinoa time. Get your quinoa on - follow pack instructions. Add 1 sachet of miso paste to the water to amp up the flavour.

Veg prep time. Cut the cucumber in half length-ways, scrape out the seeds and slice. Thinly slice the red cabbage. Slice the radishes and avocado, squeeze a little remaining lemon juice over the avocado to stop it going brown.

Dressing time. Add your tahini to a bowl with the juice of half a lemon, a grated garlic clove, salt, pepper and olive oil. Add enough water to make a drizzleable dressing - don’t worry the tahini always seizes when you first add the lemon juice, keep adding water until it comes back together. Once thick and creamy, season with salt and pepper.
Kale time. Add your kale to a roasting tray. Season with salt and pepper. Drizzle over some olive oil. Mix together and roast for 10 mins until crispy.
Serving time. Add your quinoa to a large bowl. Then add all your various bits. Top with roasted kale, some coriander leaves and tahini dressing. Tuck in.

name: Mob's Caprese Frittata
description: Cheesy, stringy mozzarella takes this frittata to the next level. Topped with sweet, juicy tomatoes. Go on...
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Drizzle a generous amount of olive oil into a deep frying pan. Halve your tomatoes and add them to the pan. Give them good stir on a medium heat and allow them to slightly soften.
Next, chop up your garlic and chilli and add this to the tomatoes and mix together. Add the basil and spinach and allow everything wilt. Add some pepper and a pinch of salt.
Egg time! Crack your eggs into a bowl, add your milk and some salt and pepper. Whisk it all together until smooth.
Take half of the tomatoes out of the pan and set aside for later.

Add three-quarters of the egg mix to the frying pan, making sure it covers the tomatoes. Break up one of your mozzarella balls and distribute it around the pan. Add roughly 5 tbsp of the tomato mixture (leaving some for later).

Pour the last of the egg mixture into the pan. Break up the remaining mozzarella ball and distribute it around the pan. Finish with a grinding of pepper, a pinch of salt and good drizzle of olive oil. Place in the oven for 12 minutes.

Once cooked, take it out of the oven and pour the remaining tomatoes over the top of the frittata. Drizzle a generous amount of balsamic glaze over the top and you are ready to devour this beauty of a dish.

name: Mob's Chicken Katsu Burger
description: The crunchy breaded chicken. The delicious katsu mayo. The zingy slaw. All shoved inside a toasted brioche bun. Go on...
instructions: Katsu mayo time. Add mayo, veggie stock cube, garam masala, curry powder and runny honey to a bowl. Mix well and set aside.
Zingy slaw. Grate your radishes and half a cabbage. Add to a bowl with sesame oil, the juice of a lime and a large handful of chopped coriander. Mix everything together and set aside.
Chicken time. Get three bowls out. Add flour to one, eggs to another (whisk them up) and breadcrumbs to the third. Dip your chicken thigh in flour, followed by the eggs and then the breadcrumbs.

Get a pan on the heat and add a very large glug of vegetable oil. Once the oil is hot, add your chicken thighs. Cook for 4 minutes on each side until the breadcrumbs are golden. Keep turning the chicken until it is cooked through.
Toast your brioche buns.

Assemble time. Add a very large dollop of katsu mayo to your bun. Add your chicken. Add a large spoonful of the zingy slaw. Dollop some more katsu mayo on the top half of the bun and place that on top of the burger. Take a bite and enjoy!

name: Mob's Chicken Kyiv
description: We spent a long time perfecting our Kyiv. And this is it. With a herby tarragon butter. On a bed of bacony mash. It's out of this world.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C/354°F.
Add 150g of butter to a bowl with a large handful of chopped tarragon and chopped parsley. Grate in 2 garlic cloves. Season with salt and pepper. Mash together.
Wrap your butter in cling film. Mould into a cylinder shape. Place in the fridge for 30 minutes to firm up.
Chop up your bacon and add to a pan. Cook until crispy.
Get your potatoes boiling in a pan of water.

Once cooked through, drain and re-add to the pan. Add 1 1/2 tablespoons of butter, a handful of chopped parsley and tarragon, salt, pepper and a small drizzle of olive oil. Mash everything together. Once mashed, add your bacon and fold it through. Set mash aside.

Chicken time. Cut a slit into the thick side of each chicken breast. Work the knife and your index finger into the slit and make hole to hold the butter. Ideally you want to keep the slit quite small so the butter doesn’t flow out.
Take your butter out the fridge. Cut up into small discs. Squeeze them into each of the four chicken breasts.
Lay out 3 bowls. Fill one with flour, the other with 3 eggs (whisk and season with salt and pepper) and the last with breadcrumbs.
Dip your chicken in the flour, next the eggs and then the breadcrumbs.
Heat a large frying pan with a good drizzle of oil. Add your breasts to the pan. Cook for 4 minutes on each side, until the breadcrumbs are golden.
Remove the breasts from the frying pan and add to a roasting tray. Place in oven for 14 minutes until cooked through. Serve the chicken on a large spoonful of the bacon mash. Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Mob's Chicken Madras Recipe
description: Sack off the takeaway and give Mob's super simple Madras a go. The curry sauce is so fragrant and rich.
instructions: Add garam masala, chilli powder, turmeric and crushed cardamom pods (pod and seeds) to a wide frying pan with a splash of oil. Cook for a minute on a medium heat to toast the spices.
Add crushed garlic cloves and a large knob of grated ginger. Stir them in. Add finely chopped onions. Coat the onions in the spices.
Add your chicken thighs and cook for 5 minutes until nicely browned.
Add a heaped tablespoon of tomato paste. Stir it in and add tins of plum tomatoes. Break them up with a spoon, bring the curry to a boil. Turn down the heat and allow to simmer for 20 minutes.
Get your rice on – follow pack instructions.
Once the chicken is cooked through, add a chopped green chilli, salt and pepper.
When the curry is nice and thick, remove from the heat. Serve over steaming rice and enjoy!

name: Mob's Chorizo Quesadillas
description: The cheesiest quesadillas around. Chorizo adds the nicest depth and the guac really lifts the flavours.
instructions: Peel and slice the chorizo. Slice the onions and peppers.
Get a frying pan on the heat and add some oil. Fry the chorizo until its releasing its oil.
Add the onions, fry until then soft and whack in the peppers. Give everything a good stir. Cook until peppers are soft and everything is crisp.
Make a quick salsa. Halve the cherry tomatoes, squeeze in some hot sauce (about 1 tbsp), lime juice and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Make a quick guac. Smash the avocado with lime juice, salt and pepper.
Scrape the chorizo mix out of the pan. Whack the pan back on the heat.

Put a wrap in the pan. Add a layer of grated cheese, the fried chorizo, onions and peppers, guac and salsa. Top with more grated cheddar. Place another wrap on top. Cook on a medium heat for 3 minutes or until the bottom layer of cheddar has melted.
Flip the quesadilla by placing a plate on top of it, turning the pan over and sliding the quesadilla from the plate back onto the pan. Cook for a further 3 minutes.
Repeat this with the rest of the tortillas, adding a bit more oil to the pan each time. Cut into quarters, serve with more hot sauce and lime wedges.

name: Mob's Chorizo Rösti & Romesco Sauce
description: We combined two of our favourite things - chorizo and röstis. The romesco sauce is divine (tangy and savoury), topped with a perfectly poached egg.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Slice up your red peppers and add to a baking tray. Season with salt, pepper and olive oil. Roast for 40 minutes until charred and soft.
Toast the almonds in a dry frying pan for 3-4 mins until they start to turn golden.
Slice up your chorizo. Add to a pan with no oil and fry on a low heat, gradually building up to a high heat until crispy and the fat has rendered out.

Grate your potato and squeeze out any excess juice. Then, add your chorizo to a mixing bowl with your grated potatoes, a large handful of chopped parsley, 2 eggs, self-raising flour and a sliced onion. Season with salt and pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Mix everything together.
Line a baking tray with a sheet of baking paper.
Divide your potato mix into 4. On the baking tray, mould each quarter into a rösti. Place the tray in the oven for 50 minutes until the röstis are golden and crispy.

Romesco sauce time. Roughly chop up your peppers and add them to a blender with your toasted almonds, a teaspoon of smoked paprika, a handful of parsley, red wine vinegar and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Blend until you have a smooth dollopable sauce.

Egg time. Heat a pan of water. Once simmering, whisk the water to form a whirlpool. Once the spinning water has slowed down, add an egg. Cook for 3 minutes and remove. If it needs longer, pop back in for 30 seconds.

Take your röstis out of the oven. For each plate add 1 rösti followed by a generous dollop of romesco sauce and top with your poached egg. Top with chopped parsley, a pinch of smoked paprika, salt, pepper and olive oil. Tuck in.

name: Mob's Curried Chickpea Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
description: The softest sweet potatoes loaded with spiced curried chickpeas, a dollop of coconut yoghurt, the crispiest shallots and scattering of pomegranate. A belter.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Place the sweet potatoes on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Season them with a good amount of salt, pepper and 1 tbsp of curry powder. Rub the curry powder into the sweet potatoes and whack in the oven for 1 hour.
Finely slice the shallots and boil them in enough vegetable oil to cover and then cook until golden and crispy. Remove these from the pan, drain the excess oil and cover with a pinch of salt.

In another pan heat a drizzle of olive oil and grate in the ginger, garlic and 2 tbsp of curry powder to create a paste. Add the chickpeas and give them a stir to coat. Next, add the coconut yoghurt, a large handful of spinach and the finely chopped coriander (saving some for garnish). Squeeze in the juice from the whole lime and season to taste. Cook for about 3 minutes, stirring often.

Once the chickpea sauce has been made, cut the baked sweet potatoes in half and generously fill them with the mixture. Sprinkle the remaining coriander and a handful of pomegranate seeds on top. Finally, add a dollop of yoghurt and the crispy shallots then repeat for your MOB. Tuck into this delicious dish! Enjoy!

name: Mob's Easy Arancini (using leftover Risotto)
description: These naughty arancini balls are the best way to use leftover Risotto. End of. The steaming rice. The crunchy shell. The garlicky, basilly tomato sauce. Yum.
instructions: For this dish, your leftover risotto has to be cold. Divide it into balls (slightly smaller than the size of a tennis ball). Roll your balls and place on a board.

Lay out three bowls. Fill the first with flour. The next with eggs- beat them, and season with salt and pepper. Fill the third bowl with breadcrumbs, a handful of chopped rosemary, chopped thyme and the grated Grana Padano. Mix it all together.
Take one of your balls. Dip it into the flour, the egg and then your Grana Padano herby breadcrumbs. Once all of the balls are nicely coated, place them back on the board.
Get a saucepan on the heat and add a glug of vegetable oil. Throw a few of the breadcrumbs into the oil. Once they start browning, the oil is hot enough.
Add your arancini to the pan. Move the balls around with a metal spoon until they are a deep golden brown. At this point, remove the arancini from the pan and place on a piece of kitchen roll.

Tomato sauce time. This is so simple. Just finely chop a garlic clove. Add to a frying pan with a glug of olive oil. Before the garlic starts to brown, pour in your passata. Season with salt and pepper. Bubble the sauce down until it is nice and thick. Throw in a handful of basil leaves. Once wilted, the sauce is ready.
Serve your arancini in a dish. Pour the tomato sauce over the top. Grate some Grana Padano over it all and tuck in!

name: Mob's French Onion Mac & Cheese
description: French onion with mac & cheese. The greatest culinary pairing since PB & J. The crispy golden breadcrumb, caramelised onion and gruyère topping is ridiculous.
instructions: Finely slice the onions. Get a frying pan over a medium heat. Melt a third of the butter in the pan. Add the onions with a good pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally until completely collapsed, soft and caramelised. This will take around 30 minutes.

Once the onions are cooked, pour in the white wine and add the thyme, stripping the leaves from the stalks straight into the pan. Leave to bubble away by half then take the pan off the heat. The onions can be done in advance and kept in the fridge.
Cook the macaroni in a large pan of boiling salted water for 2 minutes less than packet instructions. Drain once ready.

Meanwhile make the cheese sauce. Melt the remaining butter in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Once melted add the flour, whisk to combine - this is your roux. Whisking constantly, slowly pour the cold milk into the flour mixture, adding a little at a time, in order to get a smooth sauce. Once all the milk has been added, bubble the sauce away for 5 minutes until thickened.
Grate in all the cheddar and half the gruyere cheese. Once the cheese has melted take the sauce off the heat, add the dijon mustard and season with salt and pepper.

Add the cooked macaroni and caramelised onions into the cheese sauce, reserving a tablespoon of the onions. Mix well to combine, and then top with the remaining onions, a grating of gruyère and your breadcrumbs. Add a handful more thyme leaves.
Place under the grill until bubbling and golden brown. Remove from the oven and tuck in. Enjoy!

name: Mob's Massaman Curry
description: We have perfected the ultimate Massaman paste - it is so fragrant and takes this dish to the highest level.
instructions: Slice the onion and set aside. Peel and quarter your potatoes. Boil for around 25 minutes.

Get on with making your paste. Slice up your shallots, spring onions and lemongrass. Add this to a blender along with your garlic, chilli powder, galangal, ginger, coriander seeds, cumin, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, kaffir lime leaf, pepper and turmeric. Add a good glug of olive oil. Blend until it forms a smooth paste.
Get your rice on (see pack instructions).

Pour a drizzle of olive oil into a hot wok or cassorole dish. Add in the onions and fry for 5 mins, until softened. Stir in your Massaman paste, once you can smell the aromas from the paste, pour in your coconut milk. Refill the can with water and pour into the pan.
Bring the pan to the boil and add your chicken, your cooked potatoes, sugar, onion powder and soy sauce. Allow the curry to reduce on a medium-low heat until you have a nice thick sauce.
When the curry has reduced, add your peanuts. It’s now ready to serve on a bed of rice. Top with a sprinkle of peanuts and tuck into this delicious Thai classic.

name: Mob's Mighty Meatball Marinara Sub
description: Sack off subway, this meatball marinara is the real deal. Fennel seeds in for the win.
instructions: Start by placing your fresh white bread (without crusts) in a bowl. Pour enough milk over the bread so that it is covered and leave to soak.

Into a large bowl, add your pork and beef mince, a finely diced onion, 2 cloves grated garlic, a large handful of parsley, ground fennel seeds, 3 egg yolks, a good sprinkle of salt and pepper, and your milk soaked bread. Mix everything together with your hands.
Divide the mixture into 12 balls.
Place a frying pan on a medium-high with a good glug of vegetable oil. When the oil is hot, place your balls into the pan.
After 4 minutes, turn the balls. Keep turning the balls until they are brown on all sides. Remove the balls from the pan, and place them on a plate to sit.

Wipe out the pan and place back on the heat. Fry two cloves of finely chopped garlic for 1 minute. Add your passata and a glass of water. Season with salt and pepper, and add a large handful of chopped parsley. Mix everything together, and allow the sauce to simmer until it has thickened.
Reintroduce the meatballs to the pan. Turn the balls around in the sauce, and leave to cook over a medium heat for 7 more minutes, bathing the balls regularly.
Assemble time. Cut a large ciabatta loaf in half length ways. Spoon over some of your marinara sauce onto the bottom half. Add the meatballs, and cover them with the remaining sauce.

Lay a thin slice of mozzarella over each ball. Sprinkle over some more ground fennel seeds and place the sub under a grill for 7 minutes, or until the cheese has melted. Place the top half over the sub in the oven as well so it can toast.
When the cheese has melted, remove the sub and place on a board. Take the top half of the loaf and give it a good drizzle of olive oil. Place it on top of the meatballs, carve it up and enjoy!

name: Mob's Mustard Chicken
description: Tarragon and mustard are really the perfect partners for chicken. Such a delicious dish. All on a bed of steaming bulgur wheat. A real warmer.
instructions: Place the thighs on a large frying pan and cook both sides until golden brown. Remove the thighs from the pan and set aside, leaving the chicken fat in the pan.
Chop your onion and fry in the reserved chicken fat for about 5 minutes.
Add your bacon lardon pieces, stirring until cooked through.
Mince your garlic and add to the pan with your rosemary sprigs. Pour the white wine into the pan and allow your ingredients to simmer away.
Stir in the Dijon mustard and double cream along with the white wine vinegar, a pinch of salt and pepper. Give it a good stir.
Prepare your bulgur wheat.

Time to bring it all together. Roughly chop your tarragon and add it to the pan with the cooked chicken thighs. Make sure to flip the thighs over every few minutes to allow them to be fully covered in the sauce.
You’re now ready to serve up the delicious MOB Mustard Chicken on a bed of bulgur wheat. Enjoy!

name: Mob's Pulled Chicken Burger
description: The time has come for the best pulled chicken burger around. The soft bun, zingy guac and a soft pulled chicken with a sticky BBQ sauce. It's a thing of beauty.
instructions: Into the Crock-Pot Lift & Serve slow cooker, place your chicken, chipotle paste, passata, 2 tbsp of barbecue sauce, chop up your onion and add this along with a sprinkling of salt and pepper. Mix together to make sure the chicken is coated completely, then leave this to cook on the ‘Low’ heat setting for 6 hours.

Guac Time. Into a bowl, add your avocados and mix with a fork until it resembles a chunky guac. Next, chop up your coriander and add to the bowl, followed by the juice of your lime, a sprinkle of salt and pepper and mix together.

Once your chicken is done, shred it all up within the Crock-Pot Lift & Serve slow cooker. Lightly toast your buns and add a squeeze of barbecue sauce to the bottom bun, then add a spoonful of your chipotle chicken followed by a spoonful of guac. Add 2 leaves of lettuce and top it off with your bun. Repeat for the rest of your MOB and tuck in.

name: Mob's Speedy Fry Up
description: The speediest fry up you’ll ever cook, guaranteed. The key here is high heat and some good multitasking. Get into the zone and smash it in 12 minutes.
instructions:
Get two large frying pans over a high heat and drizzle a little oil
into each. Place the chipolatas in one of the pans. Space out the
rashers of bacon in the other.
Roughly chop the mushrooms, then chuck them into the pan with
the bacon. Nestle the cherry tomatoes between the sausages in
the pan. Fry for about 8 mins, turning the sausages and bacon
when needed, until everything is cooked through and to your
liking. Turn down the heat on the bacon pan if it is crisp before
the sausages are done.
Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a large measuring jug. Whisk
together with a fork and season well with salt and black pepper.
Add a knob of butter. Blast in the microwave for 30 seconds at a time, stirring after each blast, until you have super creamy
scrambled eggs. Stop cooking just before the eggs are set as
they will carry on cooking in the jug.
Toast the bread and put it onto a plate. Serve the sausages,
tomatoes, bacon, mushrooms, scrambled eggs and toast at the
table, with plenty of condiments for people to help themselves.

name: Mob's Stuffing Gnocchi
description: On the 6th day of Christmas, my true love gave to me… Mob’s Stuffing Gnocchi. Two worlds collide. Gnocchi and the best part of your Christmas dinner.
instructions: Get a frying pan over a high heat. Pour in a good glug of olive oil, tip in the breadcrumbs and stir. Chop up your rosemary and add half to the pan and stir. Once golden brown, crush in 2 garlic cloves, a sprinkle of salt and a grinding of pepper. Grate the zest of the lemon and mix it all together and set aside.
Pour in a splash of olive oil into a new pan then squeeze the sausages out of their skins and break them up into the pan. Fry for 5 minutes until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon onto a plate.

Finely chop the onion, celery stalks, remaining garlic clove and rosemary. Add the onion and celery to the pan and cook using the sausage oil, cook on a lower heat. Add your remaining rosemary, garlic, chilli flakes and your cooked sausage meat. Mix together.

Pour in the chicken stock. Once boiling, tip in the gnocchi. Cover the pan with a lid and cook for 4 minutes until the gnocchi is ready. Chop up your parsley, saving some for garnish, and add to your gnocchi, mix together.
Serve with a sprinkling of your garlicky breadcrumbs, a crack of pepper and the remaining parsley. Dig in! Enjoy!

name: Mob's Ultimate Bacon Sarnie
description: We've nailed the ultimate bacon sarnie. Crispy bacon, buttery fried bread and a sauce combo sent from heaven. This is the bacon sandwich of your dreams.
instructions: Start by frying your bacon. As it cooks, take a saucepan and place it on top of the bacon to flatten it. Flip the bacon once it begins to get crispy on one side. Once both sides are crispy, set aside.

Add your butter to the pan and stir until its melted. Once melted, add your slices of sourdough making sure you cover them in butter. Once golden brown on one side, flip it over. Meanwhile, whack your bacon back in the pan with your sourdough to coat them in butter. And you’re ready to plate up!

Start with a drizzle of ketchup on one of your slices of sourdough. Next, a few drops of Tabasco to add a kick, and finally a drizzle of brown sauce. Pile up 4 rashers of bacon and top it off with another slice of sourdough then tuck into the best bacon sarnie you will ever eat.

name: Mob's Ultimate Hot Dog
description: Bring in the sun with our fully-loaded hot dogs, topped with a superb jalapeño cheese sauce, jammy onions, smoky bacon and crispy garlic chips.
instructions: Chop up the bacon into small pieces and fry in a large frying with a small glug of oil until very crispy and browned, for about 10 mins.
Meanwhile, very thinly slice the garlic and slice your onions.

Use a slotted spoon to remove the crispy bacon and turn the heat to low. Add in the garlic slices and cook them in the bacon fat for 2 mins or until just turning golden. Remove using a slotted spoon and set aside.
Add the sliced onions to the bacon fat and cook on a low heat for 30 mins until darkened and caramelised.

Meanwhile, make the cheesy jalapeño sauce. Finely chop your jalapeños and cook them in the butter in a small saucepan for 5 mins. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 min. Slowly pour in the milk, whisking constantly, and bring to a boil. Once the sauce starts to thicken, add in your Red Leicester cheese and American cheese slices. Whisk the sauce until the cheese has melted and season generously with salt and pepper
Cook the sausages in a large frying pan for 10 mins until cooked through and crispy.
Finely chop the chives.
Pop the sausages in the hot dog bun, smother with the cheese sauce, top with caramelised onions, crispy bacon and crispy garlic. Finish with the chives and serve immediately.

name: Mob's Vegan Shakshuka
description: The naughtiest vegan Shak there is. The creamy tahini is the perfect sub for the egg. Dip in your garlicky, crunchy ciabatta croutons. Enjoy.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Start by finely chopping your onions and 1 clove of garlic. Add a drizzle of oil to a frying pan followed by your onions and stir. Once they begin to become translucent, add 1 clove of garlic.
Add ground coriander and three tsp of harissa paste to your pan. Mix together.

Chop up and add your roasted peppers and tinned tomatoes. Fill up your empty tins with water and add to the mix. Break down the tomatoes with your spoon and leave to simmer on a low heat for 15 minutes.

Tahini time. Add your tahini to a bowl along with a pinch of salt and pepper. Squeeze in the juice of a whole lemon and then grate the zest in too. Add a glug of olive oil and a splash of water to the bowl. Mix together until it begins to thicken. Set aside.

Chop up your half of parsley and grate your remaining garlic cloves. Add to a new bowl and pour in around 5 tbsp of olive oil along with a pinch of salt and a grinding of pepper. Mix together until fully combined. Cut your ciabatta in half and dress it evenly with the garlic mixture. Whack your ciabatta in the oven for 15 minutes.

Whilst your ciabatta is toasting, chop up your remaining parsley (saving a handful for garnish) and add it into your simmering shakshuka sauce, followed by a pinch of salt and a grinding of pepper. Take your ciabatta out of the oven once the edges are slightly charred.

Spoon out holes in your shakshuka and dollop in your tahini sauce. Take your harissa paste and make a yolk in the middle of the tahini circles (you may need a few more tsp for this). Repeat this until there are dollops evenly distributed around the pan. Sprinkle the remaining parsley over the dish and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Mob's Wild Alaska Salmon Burger
description: Teriyaki salmon - crispy on the outside. Flakey on the inside. With a delicious, gingery beetroot slaw. A great fish burger for the MOB.
instructions: Spoon 4 tbsp of mayonnaise into a bowl, add 2 tbsp of Teriyaki marinade, grate half a knob of ginger in and mix well until smooth. Leave to chill in the fridge.

To prepare your slaw, grate your beetroots and squeeze all of the moisture out using your hands. Grate a whole knob of ginger and finely chop the coriander. In a new bowl, mix the beetroot with 2 tbsp of mayonnaise, half the ginger, coriander, the juice of 1 lime and the red wine vinegar.
Patty time. Remove the skin from your sockeye salmon fillets. Chop up 2 fillets into very small pieces and chop the other 2 fillets into chunks. Put the salmon in a large mixing bowl.

Add the Panko breadcrumbs, 2 tbsp of Teriyaki marinade, the remaining ginger (grated) and the chilli flakes. Using your hands, mix the contents and keep mixing until you have created a firm ball. On a chopping board, separate the patty mixture into 4 separate patties.

Time to get BBQ-ing! Baste each side of the patties with Teriyaki marinade (you will need about 1 tbsp). Cook on the BBQ until both sides begin to char. Halve your brioche buns and lightly toast them on the BBQ - make sure to toast both sides.
Now, assemble your burger! Spread some of your prepared mayonnaise onto the bottom bun, pop the patty on top followed by some beetroot slaw. Tuck right in!

name: Mob-Style Chilaquiles
description: Paying homage to the classic Mexican dish Chilaquiles.  Tortilla chips with fresh salsa, a crispy egg and crumbled feta. An absolute worldy of a dish.
instructions: Finely chop the red onion and garlic cloves. Halve the cherry tomatoes and roughly chop the jarred jalapeños.
Get a non-stick frying pan over a medium to high heat. Drizzle in a generous glug of olive oil.

Scrape in the onion, along with a pinch of salt. Fry, stirring, for around 3 minutes until the onion has started to soften then add the garlic. Cook stirring for 30 seconds then chuck in the tomatoes and most of the jarred jalapeños, or chilli if using. Crank up the heat, fry the salsa for around 2 minutes until the tomatoes have begun to burst then tip into a bowl.
Squeeze the lime juice into the warm salsa, season with plenty of salt and black pepper to taste.
Put the pan back onto the heat. Drizzle in a little more oil, fry the eggs to your liking.

Divide the tortillas between four bowls. Top each with the fried salsa and an egg. Roughly chop the coriander, then crumble over the feta, coriander and remaining jalapeño or chilli. Naughty lunch treat.

name: Mob’s Cannellini Pasta
description: One of the tastiest dishes ever created in the MOB Studio. Rich, tomatoey pasta, with smoked bacon and softened cannellini beans. Comfort food at its finest.
instructions: Slice your bacon into small squares. Drizzle olive oil into a large pan on medium heat. Add your bacon to the pan and cook until crispy. Once cooked, remove the bacon from the pan and save the oil for later.
Finely dice your onion, celery, carrots, garlic and chop the rind off the parmesan. Add the onion, celery and carrots to the leftover oil and sauté for 5 minutes.

Finely chop a handful of rosemary. Add your bay leaves to the pan along with the rosemary, garlic and chilli flakes. Give it a big stir, add the bacon and cannellini beans and stir again to combine all of the ingredients.
Pour in the chicken stock and passata and mix together. Grate 2 tbsp of parmesan into the pan and stir. You can add the parmesan rind at this point as a tasty tip to add extra flavour to the dish.
Add the dry pasta and cook, stirring, for 15 minutes on medium heat or until the pasta is al dente and the sauce has thickened.
Serve with a sprinkling of grated parmesan, a couple of rosemary sprigs, a pinch of chilli flakes and a drizzle of olive oil. Dig in!

name: Mob’s Guinness Chocolate Cake Recipe
description: This chocolate Guinness cake is deep, damp and decadent while being unbelievably simple. It’s a simple baking recipe made using everyone’s favourite Irish stout. It keeps well for about a week in an airtight container, and you can happily make the cake the day before, wrap in its tin and then ice it before serving.
instructions: Heat your oven to 160°C fan. Butter a 23cm springform cake tin then line the base with baking parchment.

Cut the butter into cubes and put into a large saucepan. Pour in the Guinness, set over a low heat, stirring occasionally until melted, then whisk in the soft brown sugar and cocoa powder. Remove from the heat.

Crack the eggs into a jug, whisk in the yoghurt and vanilla extract then tip into the saucepan, along with the flour and bicarb. Whisk until a super smooth chocolatey batter forms, then pour into your lined tin. Bake in the centre of the oven for 50 mins- 1 hr until the cake begins to shrink from the sides of the tin and it is springy to touch. Leave to cool in its tin.

Once cool, remove the cake from its tin and make the icing. Sieve the icing sugar into a bowl, add all the remaining icing ingredients then using an electric whisk, whisk together until a smooth frosting forms. (It's really important both the cream cheese and butter are at room temp so they mix together nicely!)
Spread the icing all across the top of the cake and cut into fat slices to serve.

name: Mob’s Gumbo
description: Our take on a Creole classic. A cajun-spiced chicken, sausage and okra one-pot that will transport you to Louisiana.
instructions: Dice the onions, pepper and celery to create your cajun ‘trinity’. I like to go for a pretty chunky dice to give the gumbo some texture. Roughly chop the okra and thinly slice the garlic cloves, too.

Cut the chicken thighs and sausage into bite-sized chunks. Season the chicken and sear off in a large saucepan or dutch oven with a little vegetable oil until browned all over. Remove the chicken from the pan and then add the sausages. Cook until crispy and then remove from the pot.

Time to cook the roux, the most important bit! Tip the vegetable oil into the pan and whisk in the flour. Cook over a medium-low heat for 10-12 mins until very dark, whisking constantly. Tip in the cajun trinity with a pinch of salt and cook in the hot roux for 6-7 mins. Add the garlic, cayenne pepper and cajun seasoning.

Tip in the stock and bring to a boil, whisking now and then. Add the chicken and sausage back to the pan along with the bay leaves and thyme. Cook the lot for an hour or so before adding the chopped okra. Cook for another 10 mins or so – the okra will help thicken the gumbo. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice.
Divide the rice between bowls and ladle over generous portions of the gumbo. Top with sliced spring onions and get stuck in.

name: Mob’s Peri Peri Roast
description: We have amplified our favourite cheeky takeaway, so you can enjoy it with all the best bits of a roast with maximum peri peri flavour.
instructions: Pre-heat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Half your potatoes and slice your peppers and get them on a tray. Slice your onions and place on a different tray, making room in the middle for your chicken.
Drizzle with olive oil and rub in your peri peri seasoning on both trays. Place in the oven and roast for 30 minutes.

Take both trays out the oven. Baste your chicken using the juice in the baking tray. Add tenderstem broccoli to your potato and pepper tray, drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with salt. Return both trays back to the oven then roast for a further 30 minutes.
Baste your chicken and leave to rest for 10 minutes on a wooden board. Set aside your potatoes, peppers and tenderstem broccoli.

Gravy time. Take your onions still in the baking tray and place on the hob, adding in 100ml water and your red wine vinegar. Bring to the boil and bubble down on a high heat until you get a nice thick sauce.
Carve your chicken and plate up with a healthy dose of gravy. Enjoy!

name: Mocha Almond No Churn Ice Cream
description: Decadent and fudgy mocha and almond butter ice cream. It’s a perfect summer treat.
instructions: Place the tin in the freezer. Chop and freeze the bananas for at least 24hrs.
Blend all of the ingredients except the chocolate in a blender until smooth.
Roughly chop the chocolate and keep a handful to the side. Pulse the rest into the ice cream mix until combined but still chunky.
Pour the mix into the frozen tin and drizzle some extra almond butter and chocolate on top.
Cover with silver foil and freeze for at least 3 hours. When ready to serve, allow it to thaw for 10 mins before serving.

name: Molten Double Pistachio & Vanilla Cookies
description: Soft, sweet and incredibly moreish, these vanilla pistachio cookies are on another level. Make extra and keep a few in the freezer for when you’ve got a cookie craving.
keywords: molten double pistachio and vanilla cookies
instructions: Start by making the pistachio filling. Split the vanilla pod in half lengthwise and scrape the seeds out into a medium mixing bowl. Add the pistachio cream and mix to combine. Set aside the pod.
Line a baking tray with baking parchment. Using a spoon, scoop out 12 blobs of the vanilla pistachio cream onto a tray. Place the tray in the freezer for 1-2 hrs until the cream has fully solidified.
Meanwhile, leave the empty vanilla pod in a warm place for 2 hours to dry out, or pop it in a preheated oven at 160°C for 10 mins. Set aside until you're ready to make the cookie dough.

For the cookies, roughly chop the pistachios and white chocolate. Heat the butter and pistachios in a saucepan set over a low heat, stirring, until the butter has melted. Transfer to a mixing bowl and leave for 3-5 mins to cool.
Add the light brown sugar and the deseeded vanilla pod to a blender and blitz until the vanilla pod has fully broken down into the sugar.
Stir the vanilla sugar, egg and extra egg yolk through the cooled melted butter. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, bicarb and salt.

Tip the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients and mix to combine until a dough forms. Stir through the chopped white chocolate. Cover the dough with cling film and chill in the fridge for at least 30 mins.
Line two baking trays with baking paper and remove the frozen pistachio cream from the freezer.

Divide the dough into 12 pieces, about 72-74g each, and use your hands to roll it into balls. Flatten each cookie dough ball, press a frozen puck of pistachio cream into the middle and wrap the dough around. Place on the lined baking tray and repeat until all the cookies are formed. Cover with cling film and place in the freezer for at least 30 mins, or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 190°C. Once hot, slide the cookies in and bake for 10-15 mins until golden brown. Remove and tap on the counter to deflate. Let them cool before tucking in.

name: Monkfish with 'Nduja & Tomato Butter Beans
description: Discover the exquisite flavours of monkfish with our easy-to-follow monkfish recipe. Perfectly cooked and packed with deliciousness! If grilled fish is your sort of thing, this recipe will be just the ticket. Tender, delicious, and pretty easy to whip together, this dish is a surefire hit.
keywords: Monkfish With 'Nduja & Tomato Butter Beans recipe
instructions: Remove any sinew from the monkfish, then cut into large bite-sized pieces. Dust over the smoked paprika and season well. Toss well and chill while you make the sauce.
Thinly slice the fennel and peel then thinly slice the garlic cloves.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large, deep frying pan (that you have a lid for) and fry the fennel over a medium-high heat for 6-7 minutes until caramelising.
Turn the heat down to medium and add the garlic, 'nduja and fennel seeds. Stir and toss everything around for 2-3 minutes, breaking the 'nduja up with the back of the spoon.
Pour in the white wine and bubble away for 2 minutes.
Tip the cherry tomatoes into the pan, then drain the butter beans and add to the pan. Season with salt and black pepper, then bubble away for 30 minutes until the sauce has reduced.
Remove the monkfish pieces from the fridge and nestle into the sauce. Put on a lid and simmer for another 8 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Meanwhile, toss the rocket in the sherry vinegar.
Once the fish is cooked, drape a little of the rocket over the top of the stew, then divide between shallow bowls, along with the rest of the rocket salad.

name: Moorish Lamb Kebabs by Ainsley Harriott
description: The legend Ainsley Harriott joins us in the MOB studio making lamb kebabs from his new book ‘Ainsley’s Mediterranean Cookbook’. Yeah boiiiiiiii.
instructions: Grate the garlic, crush the cumin seeds and trim the excess fat off the lamb, cutting into 3cm cubes.
Combine 3 tbsp of oil, vinegar, garlic, oregano, cumin seeds, paprika, cayenne pepper, turmeric with a generous pinch of salt and pepper in a large bowl.

Add your lamb to the bowl and toss together with your hands so that the marinade coats the meat. Cover with cling film and marinate in the fridge for at least an hour, or overnight if you have the time.

Whilst the lamb is marinating, make the dukkah. Toast the nuts in a dry pan until lightly browned and fragrant. Transfer into a food processor. In the same hot pan, toast the remaining spices for 1 minute until fragrant. Blitz everything in the food processor until it resembles coarse sand.
Get your veg ready. Slice the tomatoes and red onion, and finely chop the coriander leaves.
Preheat a griddle pan to medium-high heat.
Divide the marinated lamb onto eight skewers. Place onto the hot griddle pan and cook for 8 - 10 minutes until they are tender with some nice charring, turning occasionally so that they cook evenly.
Mix the yoghurt with another squeeze of lemon and a pinch of cayenne pepper to taste. Season with salt and pepper.

Arrange the tomatoes and onion on a serving platter, sprinkle with salt, zest of the lemon and drizzle with olive oil. Scatter with 2 tablespoons of dukkah, your chopped coriander and a squeeze of the lemon.
Drizzle the kebabs with the yoghurt dressing and serve up with the tomato salad and some toasted flatbreads.

name: Moqueca Fish Burger
description: Moqueca is a traditional Brazilian seafood stew. Ixta Belfrage has taken the flavours of that dish and thrown them into a burger.
instructions: Add the fish fillets to a 30 x 23cm high sided baking tray and season with ½ tsp of fine salt, ½ tsp sugar and 2 tbsp oil. Mix to coat.
Add all the ingredients for the moqueca to a blender and blitz until completely smooth. Add to the tray with the fish and mix to coat. Leave to marinate for 30 mins at room temperature.
While the fish is marinating, make the slaw. Mix the cabbage mayo, lime juice and fine salt together and set aside.

Preheat the oven to 240°C fan. Transfer the tray of fish to the oven for 22-24 minutes, or until the fillets are beginning to turn golden-brown on top. The sauce should have thickened and reduced considerably, and should be bubbling vigorously. Set aside to cool for 5 mins.
While the fish is cooling, spread a little mayo on each cut half of brioche, then toast in a very hot pan until golden brown.
When you're ready to serve, stir the spring onions, green chilli and coriander into the slaw.

Place a fish fillet on each brioche half and spoon over plenty of sauce. Squeeze over some lime juice, then top with a generous spoonful of slaw and the other half of the bun. Serve with lime wedges and more sauce alongside, for dipping your burger into.

name: Morning Milk Tea Chia Pudding
description: Move over overnight oats. This creamy healthy chia porridge with infused tea and spiced nuts and seeds is here to transform your mornings. Make a big batch and you’ve got breakfast for days.
keywords: Morning Milk Tea Chia Pudding recipe
instructions: Pour the water, salt and milk into a saucepan and bring to a boil. Once boiling, add the teabags then remove the pan from the heat and let the tea steep for 4-5 mins, until you have a dark brew.
Strain the tea mixture into a bowl or box and season to taste with maple syrup. Then, stir through the chia, oats and hemp seeds. Cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 5 hours, ideally overnight.

Meanwhile, make the cinnamon nuts: Roughly chop the pecans. Heat the oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the pecans, sunflower seeds and flaked almonds and cook, stirring, until toasted and golden. Remove from the heat and stir through the cinnamon, salt and maple syrup. Transfer to a jar or box and cover with a lid. Place in the fridge until ready to use.
To serve, spoon the oat mixture into bowls (mix through a splash of milk if it's thickened too much). Serve with a dollop of Greek yoghurt, and top with the maple cinnamon nut mix.

name: Moroccan Spiced Cauliflower & Couscous With Harissa Spiked Yoghurt
description: Couscous is so quick and easy to prepare, and makes the perfect base for this cauliflower and chickpea dish. The harissa yoghurt adds a nice bit of spice.
keywords: Moroccan Spiced Cauliflower & Couscous With Harissa Spiked Yoghurt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
If using whole cumin and coriander seeds, lightly grind them in a pestle and mortar. Add all of the spices plus salt and pepper, pomegranate molasses and the olive oil to a small bowl and mix.

Cut the cauliflower in half and then into quarters or thirds (depending on how big it is). Peel the onion and cut into eighths, keeping the stem intact. Place the cauliflower and onion onto a large baking tray and drizzle over the olive oil spice mix.

Make sure the cauliflower is well covered, rub the spice mix into the crevices. Bake for 15 mins on the middle shelf, toss and bake for another 15 mins until cooked through and caramelised on the edges.

Meanwhile, prepare the couscous. Measure the couscous and place in a heatproof bowl. Boil the kettle and measure out 480ml boiling water and pour this over the couscous. Add a drizzle of olive oil and half the harissa, if using and stir well. Cover with a lid or plate and set aside
Drain the chickpeas and add these to the couscous along with remainder of your harissa and season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
To make the harissa yoghurt, add the vegan yoghurt to a small bowl and stir through the harissa.

To serve, lay the couscous onto a large platter or bowl, add the cauliflower, harissa yoghurt, toasted almonds, parsley, and a final drizzle of olive oil and some extra pomegranate molasses if you like.

name: Moroccan Sweet Potato & Chickpea Soup
description: Bursting with warm flavours such as cinnamon, cumin and coriander, and featuring Medjool dates, this Moroccan-inspired chickpea soup delivers on flavour and nutrition. With protein-rich chickpeas, wholewheat giant couscous, vibrant sweet potatoes and tomatoes, every spoonful is a nutritional powerhouse. Perfect for fuelling your active lifestyle, or simply for a comforting, delicious meal.
instructions: Pit the dates and finely chop them along with the garlic, onion and carrot

Add the onions and a generous amount of olive oil to a non-stick saucepan set over a low-medium heat. Cook until slightly translucent. Add the carrots and a pinch of salt, then cook for another 2 mins.
Add the garlic, spices and chopped dates with a splash of vegetable broth. Slowly sauté and stir this mixture for 8-10 mins until the onions and carrots are very soft.
Meanwhile, wash and chop the sweet potatoes. Drain the chickpeas.

Turn the heat to medium and add the sweet potatoes, chopped tomatoes, chickpeas, vegetable stock and giant couscous to the pan. Simmer until the sweet potatoes are fork-tender and the giant couscous is cooked (about 8-10 minutes)
Turn off the heat. Roughly chop the coriander and stir it through. Season with salt and black pepper, then squeeze the lemon straight into the pan.
Let the soup sit for 7-8 mins before serving.

name: Moules Marinières
description: Classic Belgian dish of mussels cooked with a twist. Beer, garlic and cream, cooked from a stove on the beach. Great for sharing.
instructions: Wash the mussels well and discard any that don’t close when tapped. Remove the beards.
Tie the bay, thyme and rosemary together with butcher’s twine to make a bouquet garni.
Place a large pan over a medium heat and add the butter. Finely chop and add the remaining leek, onion and garlic along with the bouquet garni and cook for a few minutes until soft.
Turn the heat up high, add the mussels and the beer and put a lid on the pan. Cook for 3 mins, shaking the pan occasionally.
Add the cream and parsley and remove from the heat. Taste, season with salt and pepper and serve in bowl with warm crusty bread.

name: Moussaka
description: A rich and creamy classic moussaka. We once made moussaka for 150 people and learned about this alternative topping: lighter than a bechamel, it soufflés better and cuts through the richness of the moussaka. We also realised that baking the aubergine rather than griddling, saved heaps of time and created a banging result. We hope you love it.
instructions: Heat a splash of olive oil in a large casserole pan or saucepan set over a medium high heat. Tip in the lamb mince and season with a pinch of salt, then use the back of your spoon to break down the mince slightly. Cook for 10-12 mins, stirring occasionally until all the liquid has evaporated and the mince starts to brown and caramelise. Remove with a slotted spoon into a bowl.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and garlic. Once the lamb is browned, transfer it to a plate and set aside. Add the onion to the pan with a pinch of salt, and cook, stirring regularly for 6-8 mins until soft and golden.

Add the garlic, cinnamon, oregano, smoked paprika and tomato purée to the pan. Cook for a couple of mins, stirring the spices into the onion, then pour in the red wine. Once the wine has bubbled away and reduced by half, pour in the plum tomatoes, using your spoon to break them down into pieces. Refill the tinned tomato can halfway with water and pour that in too. Add the lamb back in. Turn down the heat to medium and leave the sauce to simmer away for 30 mins until you have a rich sauce, then season to taste.

Meanwhile, heat the oven to 190°C fan. Cut the aubergine into 5mm rounds, lay onto a large roasting tray, drizzle well with olive oil and season. Peel the potatoes then cut into 3mm round slices (a mandolin also works well here) and lay on a separate baking tray (overlapping is fine), drizzle with some oil and season. Put both trays into the oven for 15 mins, until the aubergines are soft, and the potatoes are soft and beginning to crisp and roast in places.

Assembly time. Layer the potato slices into the bottom of a medium roasting dish. Top with ½ the moussaka filling then ½ the aubergine slices, then repeat. The moussaka can be assembled like this and kept in the fridge for a day before making the topping and baking.

Once ready to eat, turn the oven to 180°C fan. Crumble the feta into a large bowl, finely grate in the nutmeg, Parmesan and lemon zest then measure in the yoghurt. Crack in the eggs then whisk all together, seasoning with a little salt and lots of black pepper.
Spread the topping across the moussaka. Bake for 40-50 mins (it will take longer if baking from cold) until puffed up, bubbling and burnished.

name: Mozzarella & Prosciutto Stromboli
description: We all love pizza, but it doesn't travel well. Cue the stromboli, pizza’s swirly cousin. Packed with mozzarella and Italian cold cuts, it's perfect for picnics.
instructions: Pour 325ml lukewarm water into a large bowl. Add the yeast and sugar and whisk to dissolve.
Leave to stand for 5 mins. It should get foamy, or at the very least, creamy. If it doesn’t, your yeast is likely dead and you’ll need to start over with fresher yeast.
Add the strong white bread flour and 10g fine sea salt and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured work surface. Knead until smooth, elastic and no longer sticky, around 5 mins.
Divide the dough into two and roll into balls.
Place each ball in a floured bowl, cover with a cloth and leave to prove in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened but not browned, 7 to 10 mins.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, then add the crushed tomatoes and basil sprigs. Season with salt and pepper and stir to combine.
