Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 30 mins, stirring occasionally. Adjust the seasoning to your liking and leave to cool.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the mozzarella and pick the basil leaves.
Punch down the dough to expel the air then turn it out onto a floured work surface and knead it for 1 minute to further deflate it.
Roll each dough ball into a ½ cm-thick rectangle. Spread with some of the marinara, leaving a 2cm border around the edge. Top with the deli meats, mozzarella slices and basil leaves.
Roll the dough up into a log and tuck in the ends to enclose the filling.
Place the two stromboli on two greaseproof paper-lined baking trays and leave to rise for 30 mins.
Heat your oven to 200°C / fan 180°C.
Beat the egg. Brush the stromboli with the egg wash, sprinkle with flaky salt and bake for 25 to 30 mins, or until well risen and golden brown.
Leave to cool for 10 minutes, then slice thickly and serve with any remaining marinara.

name: Mozzarella Grilled Turkey Steak with Caper & Cherry Tomato Sauce
description: This is a spin on a dinner we used to eat a lot growing up, but with a bit more of an adult spin on it. Still bangs, though.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Cut the baking potatoes into 2cm cubes and tip into a large bowl. Pour in 1 tbsp of the oil, the dried herbs and loads of salt and pepper. Toss really well so everything is coated, then tip onto your largest baking tray. Spread into an even layer, then roast in the oven for 25 mins.
After 25 mins, flip all the potatoes and roast for another 25 mins until super crisp and crunchy.
Meanwhile, cut the cherry tomatoes into quarters and scrape into a bowl, then drain and tear the mozzarella into small pieces. Transfer the mozzarella pieces to a separate bowl.

When the potatoes have about 2 mins left, heat an ovenproof frying pan over a high heat. Drizzle the turkey steaks with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and season well with salt and black pepper. Heat the grill to high and take the potatoes out of the oven.
Put the turkey steaks into the hot pan and cook for 2 mins until charred, then flip. Cook for 1 min, then scatter in the capers and cherry tomatoes.
Scatter the turkey steaks with the grated mozzarella and put under the hot grill for 6-8 mins until the cheese is melted, golden and bubbling.
Remove from the oven, scatter with the parsley and serve with the crispy potatoes and a big green salad or veg.

name: Muhammara
description: Bursting with flavour, here's our take on a classic Middle Eastern dip. Made up of roasted peppers and walnuts, it's just the right amount of sweet and spicy.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C.
Place the walnuts onto a baking tray and roast until toasted and golden, 7-10 mins.
Drain the roasted peppers and place into a food processor with the breadcrumbs, aleppo pepper, pomegranate molasses, ground cumin, toasted walnuts and 40ml of extra virgin olive oil.
Blitz until all the ingredients have broken down into a thick paste, it shouldn't be smooth. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and pomegranate molasses.

name: Muhammara With Leeks And Grains
description: Muhammara is a classic Levantine dip, found in many Middle Eastern countries but loved all over the world. I’ve turned it into a sauce and made it a meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Roast the peppers and leeks for an hour on a baking tray, turning once, until they are blackened on the skins.
Toast walnuts in a dry frying pan for 5 mins, tossing once or twice. Set aside a handful for garnish.
Meanwhile, boil the spelt in salted water for 20 mins, drain and pour it back into the pot. Add the drained tin of chickpeas, a drizzle of olive oil and season well with salt and pepper.

When the leeks and peppers come out of the oven, place them in a bowl and cover with cling film. This will steam them and help remove the skin. Peel the skin off of the peppers and remove the seeds. Save two peeled peppers to the side.

To make the muhammara, add the peeled peppers (except the two extra ones), walnuts, tomato purée, olive oil, chilli flakes, cumin, pomegranate molasses, lemon juice, ¼ tbsp salt and sumac, if using, to a food processor. Blend until you have a paste that’s not quite totally smooth. Taste and add more lemon, salt or chilli if you like.

Take the leeks and peel off the burnt skin, about 2-3 of the outer layers. Slice them in half lengthways and open them up so that the layers lie flat. Slice a few times lengthways again and pull them apart to create ribbons. Set aside in a bowl.

Take the two remaining peppers and slice them into long pieces, a similar width to your leeks. Add them to the bowl of leeks and season with salt and pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Toss to mix them all together well.
To serve, lay a generous portion of muhammara onto a plate, spoon on the grains and chickpeas, then lay the leeks and peppers over the top. Finish with some chopped parsley and the remaining walnuts.

name: Mujadara
description: This is a speedy version of the Lebanese dish Mujadara. You really can't go wrong with rice and lentils, which is exactly what this dish is offering. Enjoy.
instructions: Finely slice the shallot, then separate the layers. Pour the olive oil into a small frying pan and place onto medium heat. Add the shallot then simmer, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 mins until the shallots turn golden. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the shallots to a plate lined with kitchen paper.
Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves and finely slice the stalks. Stir the nigella seeds into the yoghurt and season with salt and the juice of half a lemon. Set aside.

Add the cumin seeds and parsley stalks to the hot shallot oil and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Tip the rice and lentils in, stirring to thoroughly mix. Cook until piping hot, 2-3 mins. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Stir half the shallots through, remove from the heat and cover with a lid.
Slice the remaining lemon half into wedges. Toss the parsley leaves through the mujadara and share between bowls. Enjoy with nigella seed yoghurt, your remaining shallots, and a lemon wedge.

name: Mulled Aperol
description: You've had mulled wine before, but what about mulled Aperol?
instructions: Use a peeler and get make a twist for garnish.
Toast your cinnamon in a dry pan.
Add your honey, white wine, apple juice and aperol and gently heat until a the honey is dissolved and the drink is warmed.
Strain and serve in a thick glass or mug so your fingers don’t burn.
Garnish with a cinnamon stick and orange twist. Enjoy.

name: Mulled Wine
description: This mulled wine ticks all the boxes. Fragrant, sweet and gently spiced for a real wintery treat.
instructions: Lightly toast the cinnamon stick, cloves and star anise in a saucepan until aromatic, be careful not to burn.
Cut the orange in half and squeeze in the juice then add the whole orange. Pour in the red wine and add the sugar.
Stir well until the sugar dissolves. Warm until the wine just starts to gently bubble, then turn off the heat and allow to infuse for 15 mins.
Pass through a strainer to remove the spices.
Simply add the mulled wine into little individual bags or tubs of your choice. Warm gently before serving and enjoy.

name: Mushroom & Lentil Gnocchi
description: A beautifully easy mushroom and lentil ragu tossed with pillowy gnocchi. Weeknight dinner made easy.
instructions: Make the Mushroom & Lentil Ragù.
Reheat the Mushroom & Lentil Ragú in a saucepan set over a medium heat.
Cook the gnocchi in boiling water according to package instructions, or until they float to the top.

Remove the gnocchi from the boiling water using a slotted spoon and transfer directly into the ragù. Add a slosh of the gnocchi cooking water and mix well. Pour in the cream and mix before tasting and adjusting the seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve up in bowls topped with finely chopped chives, grated Parmesan, and black pepper.

name: Mushroom & Lentil Lasagne Soup
description: All the comfort of a lasagne but in slurpable form. Made using our Mushroom & Lentil Ragù batch. Cosy, hearty, and so easy.
instructions: Make the Mushroom & Lentil Ragù.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the tomato purée and cook for 2-3 mins until darkened and sticky.
Pour the Mushroom & Lentil Ragù and stock in. Season with salt and pepper, then bring to a simmer. Pick the parsley leaves, finely slice the stems.

Snap the lasagne sheets in half, add them into the soup along with the parsley stems, stir well and simmer until al dente (look at package instructions for timings). Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed. Add a splash of water, if you’d like it looser.
Ladle into bowls and top with plenty of grated Parmesan and parsley leaves.

name: Mushroom & Lentil Ragù
description: A mushroomy, lentil ragù that just gets better with time. Perfect for batch cooking.
instructions: Peel the onion, carrots and garlic. Blitz coarsely along with the celery in a food processor. Remove from the processor and repeat with the mushrooms. If you don't have a food processor you can finely chop it all, but do not be tempted to grate it!

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat and add the blitzed onion, carrot, garlic and celery. Add a big pinch of salt and cook for 10 mins until completely softened. Add the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins before tipping in the mushrooms. Cook for 5 mins until softened.
Drain and add the lentils, along with the tinned tomatoes, miso, and stock, then simmer for 30-40 mins until reduced. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with your choice of carb (gnocchi, pasta, bread, potatoes, etc.). Optional: if you're batch cooking the ragu for the week, portion it out into Tupperware containers.

name: Mushroom & Lentil Ragù with Red Pepper Sauce & Tahini
description: We’ve kept this one nice and simple by topping our Mushroom & Lentil Ragú batch with an almondy, red pepper sauce that comes together in no time at all. Warm up some bread for scooping and get stuck in.
keywords: Mushroom & Lentil Ragù With Red Pepper Sauce & Tahini
Mushroom & Lentil Ragù With Red Pepper Sauce & Tahini recipe
instructions: Make the Mushroom & Lentil Ragú.
Reheat the Mushroom & Lentil Ragu in a saucepan over a medium heat.

For the red pepper sauce, add most of the almonds, drained red pepper, red wine vinegar and peeled garlic to a blender, blitzing until smooth. Add a glug of olive oil and keep blitzing until you’ve reached the desired consistency (it should be drizzle-able). Season with salt and pepper.
Finely chop the parsley.
To serve, divide the lentils between bowls. Top with the red pepper sauce, a drizzle of tahini, the remaining almonds and a scattering of parsley. Scoop with warm bread and enjoy.

name: Mushroom & Pork Larb Burrito
description: We adore larb at Mob and thought it would would amazingly well in a burrito. We tested it. It does. Great meal-prep option also.
instructions: Add some vegetable oil to a wok followed by your pork mince. Mix everything together. As it starts to brown, get on with the mushrooms. Slice them up and run your knife over them, cutting them into very small pieces.
Add the mushrooms to the wok and mix everything together thoroughly. Once the mince has browned, take it out of the wok and set aside.
Get your rice on (see pack instructions).
Chop the ginger into strips, chop up your coriander stalks, red chillies, mint stalks and dice your onion. Add them all to the wok and stir.

Add the fish sauce and the soy sauce. Mix everything together and allow the sauce to bubble. Once bubbling, add your pork mushroom mince. Chop up the rest of your coriander (leave 2 handfuls for later) and mint and add this to your mince.
Salsa Time. Chop up your tomatoes. Mix them with the kidney beans and 1 handful of the remaining coriander. Add a drizzle of olive oil, salt, pepper and mix together.

Prepping station. Take a tortilla and add 2 tbsp of rice. Drizzle Sriracha over the rice and sprinkle a pinch of coriander over the top. Add 2 tbsp of the pork mushroom mince and top it off with the salsa.

To roll the burrito: fold the sides in and gently roll it until you reach the end. Once folded, lightly toast either side in a frying pan until the tortilla begins to brown. Take it off the heat and wrap it up in some foil. Repeat this process 3 times and then tuck into these beautiful burritos.

name: Mushroom & Root Veg Nut Roast
description: This festive centrepiece is a great alternative to the usual vegan mains, is made with beetroot and celeriac florets on top of a nutty mushroom and lentil base.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Cook the lentils if you are not using them pre-cooked. If you are using ground flax as a binder, add it to a small bowl with 3 tbsp of water. Mix and set aside.

Roughly chop the mushrooms. Add 1-2 Tbsp butter to the pan and let it melt. Sweat down the shallots for about 7-8 mins until translucent, on a medium heat. Then add the garlic and sauté for 2 mins more. If using ground flaxseed, add it to a small bowl with 3 tbsp of water and set aside.
Pick the leaves off of the thyme sprigs. Toast the walnuts for 6 mins and then finely chop or blitz in a food processor to a coarse texture.

Add the mushrooms and thyme and turn up the heat. Sweat them down until all of the moisture is gone. You might need two pans for this as you don’t want to overcrowd the mushrooms in one pan. They need plenty of space to caramelise.
Once all of the water has evaporated from the mushrooms (this will take up to 15 mins), add the balsamic and soy sauce and stir for a few mins until they evaporate at the end and season well.
Stir through the walnuts, flaxseed if using, 2 tbsp of cream cheese, lentils and check again for seasoning.

Grease your cake tin with some butter around the sides and line the bottom with baking paper. Spoon the mushroom mixture into the tin and use the back of a spoon to even out the surface. Pop it onto a tray as it may leek. Bake for 30 mins, until golden brown on top. Set aside to cool for 15 mins before removing from the cake tin.
Start this step while the mushroom bake is in the oven. Peel and thinly slice the celeriac and beetroot. Use a mandoline if you have one or a very sharp knife to slice them about 3mm thin.

Put the celeriac and beetroot into two separate trays, season well and drizzle with olive oil, tossing to make sure that each slice is evenly coated. Cover tightly with foil and roast for 20 mins, until soft and supple enough to crumple.
In a bowl, mix the rest of the cream cheese with 4 tsp of the mustard, miso, mayo sauce. Taste and add a little more mustard if you like.
Once the bake has cooled, spread the cream cheese mix over the top with the back of a spoon, taking care not to scrape off the top.

Then, scrunch the pieces of celeriac and beetroot and place them one by one onto the cream cheese. Place them close to one another so that they hold their shape. Continue until you have covered the whole top of the roast. Use any leftovers as a side with the miso mayo dressing and herbs.
Finally, finish with a good drizzle of the miso mayo mustard all over the top, a sprinkle of pomegranate seeds and dill.
If you need to heat it up, put it in a large baking tray and cover loosely with tin foil to stop it from drying out in the oven.

name: Mushroom & Sage Pasta
description: The ultimate umami comfort food. Creamy pasta shells, fresh mushrooms, fragrant parmesan and a garlicky sage mouthful. It's so simple and so delicious.
instructions: Finely dice the onions, slice the mushrooms and crush the garlic.
Pour some olive oil in the pan, add the onions and a pinch of salt, then cook for around 10 minutes until they start to go transparent. Then add the garlic and sage and cook for a further 2 minutes.
Add the mushrooms to the pan and give everything a good mix so that the mushrooms are coated. Whack in the butter and allow it to melt into the mixture then give it a good stir.
Once the butter has melted add the crème fraîche, give it a mix and then let it simmer for about 10 minutes until the sauce starts to pick up some colour.
While the sauce is simmering, get your pasta on.
To finish off the sauce add the parmesan and a good splash of pasta water, but save some for later, and then season well with generous amounts of pepper and salt to taste.
Add the pasta to the sauce and give it a good stir. Plate it up with another sprinkle of parmesan and garnish with a little sprig of sage. Serve and enjoy!

name: Mushroom & Spelt Risotto
description: This cosy autumnal mushroom and spelt risotto is earthy, nutty and so easy to make. You and your gut microbes will love it. Like humans, mushrooms have the ability to make vitamin D from sunshine so pop yours on the window sill for around 20 mins before using.
instructions: Finely chop the shallot and garlic.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the shallot and fry for a few minutes until translucent and slightly golden. Add in ½ the garlic and the fresh thyme and continue to cook for a further minute.
Add the spelt to the pan and stir to coat then cover with the stock.
Leave to simmer for around 40 mins until the spelt is cooked, topping it up with more stock or water as needed if it’s drying out.

In the last 10 mins of cooking time, slice the mushrooms and roughly chop the parsley. Heat a glug of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and remaining garlic and fry until golden. Season with salt and black pepper.
Divide the spelt between plates and top with the mushrooms and a sprinkling of fresh parsley.

name: Mushroom & Tofu Butter Curry
description: This creamy, rich and decadent curry is a spin on butter chicken, but I’ve used caramelised mushrooms for flavour and cubed tofu which absorbs all of the flavour and gives a great protein boost.
instructions: Chop the mushrooms into bite-size pieces. Cube the tofu into small cubes. Finely chop the onion, mince the garlic and ginger.
Cook your rice according to package instructions.

Melt 1 tbsp vegan butter in a large frying pan on medium high heat. Add the mushrooms with some salt and pepper and cook for about 5-7 mins, until they are golden and caramelised. Remove them from the pan and set them aside in a bowl.

Remove the mushrooms from the pan and melt another 1 tbsp of butter on medium high heat. Add the tofu and cook for about 5 mins, tossing occasionally, until they are golden on each side, about 5 mins. Add 1 soy sauce, stir for 1 minute and then remove from the pan and add them to the bowl with the mushrooms.

Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil, Cook the onion for about 5 mins until translucent, then add the garlic and ginger, spices, and 1 tbsp of butter. Cook for about 3 mins until all of the flavours have combined, then stir through the passata and tomato paste. Add the coconut milk and simmer for 5 mins until the sauce has thickened. Add the mushrooms and tofu back into the pan. Simmer for another 5 mins all together until the sauce has thickened a little more and all of the flavours have absorbed into the tofu.
To serve, dish the rice out into bowls and spoon over the curry. Finish with coriander leaves and some more chilli flakes or fresh chilli if you like.

name: Mushroom Gnocchi Bake
description: A delicious, warming bake. Taleggio and mushrooms are the perfect partners for gnocchi.
instructions: Slice up your mushrooms. Add olive oil to a frying pan over a medium heat add the mushrooms and cook until golden. Finely chop the parsley.
Grate in your garlic, then add thyme leaves, half your chilli flakes and half of your parsley. Zest in the lemon and mix well.
Add the single cream. Allow it to bubble down then add your spinach. Pop a lid on the pan and allow the spinach to wilt.
Add gnocchi to a bowl and cover with boiling water. Leave for 5 minutes.
Back to your sauce. Once the spinach has wilted, add the juice of 1/2 your lemons.
Add a little of water from the gnocchi bowl to the sauce. Mix together. Drain the gnocchi and add to the sauce.
Mix everything together. Season well with salt and pepper. Add more gnocchi water if needed.
Pour the gnocchi into an oven proof dish. Top with slices of taleggio, sprinkle on the rest of the chilli flakes and place under the grill for 10 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
Spoon out the gnocchi, top with the remaining chopped parsley and tuck in. Enjoy!

name: Mushroom Katsu Burger
description: If you need a dirty vegan burger in your life, this one is for you. Spiced sauce, a crispy portobello mushroom and a fresh slaw are going to rock your world.
instructions: Start by making your sauce. Finely chop your onion and your carrot.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add your onion and carrot, then cook out for 10 minutes until soft and caramelised.
Add your ginger and garlic to the pan and cook out for 2 minutes before tipping in your curry powder and flour. Give it a good mix to coat your vegetables and cook out for 2 minutes longer.

Pour in your vegetable stock along with your brown sugar and soy sauce, then simmer for 5 minutes until thickened and slightly reduced. Season to taste, then set aside to cool briefly. Pop it in a blender and blitz to a smooth sauce, then return it to the saucepan to stay warm.

Now make your slaw. Finely chop your cabbages and slice your spring onions. Pop both in a bowl along with your vegan mayonnaise, rice wine vinegar and a pinch of salt. Give it all a good mix and set aside until later.

Whisk your flour and soy milk together in a bowl with a pinch of salt to form a thick paste. In a separate bowl, tip your panko breadcrumbs. Get your portobello mushrooms and dip them in the thick paste until they are fully coated. Transfer them to the panko breadcrumbs bowl and toss until fully coated.

Heat a good glug of vegetable oil in a high sided frying pan over a medium-high heat. Gently place your mushrooms in the oil and fry over a medium heat for about 4 minutes on each side, by which time they should be deep golden brown and crisp, with a tender mushroom within.

Time to assemble your burgers. Halve your buns and spread the base with your curry sauce. Place your mushroom on top, along with a handful of slaw and some pickled ginger. Eat whilst still crisp and hot.

name: Mushroom Koupes (Bulgur Balls)
description: These savoury treats are a Cypriot classic. Minced herby mushroom mix wrapped in a bulgur wheat shell that's crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside.
instructions: First, soak the bulgur wheat. Add it to a large metal bowl with 525ml of boiling water and one stock cube and give it a stir. Cover with a plate and set aside for an hour or two to absorb all of the water.

Finely chop the onion. Finely dice the mushroom. You can also use a food processor but make sure to pulse the onion and mushroom separately if you do. Don’t overfill the bowl and pulse slowly, scraping down the sides to make sure that you end up with a nice chunky texture.
Finely chop the herbs and mince the garlic.

Add 3 tbsp of olive oil to a saucepan and fry the onion with a sprinkle of salt for 2-3 mins on medium heat, until they’re starting to become translucent but not browned. Add the mushrooms and garlic and fry until softened and cooked through. Add more olive oil if it starts to become dry. Add the cinnamon and set aside.
Wipe the pan clean and lightly toast the pine nuts. Mix through the mushrooms. Add the zest of one lemon and the chopped herbs.
When the bulgur wheat is cool, add the flour and knead for 3-5 mins until the mixture comes together and is not crumbly.

To form the koupes, take 50g of the bulgur mix and roll it into a ball. With your finger, press a hole into the ball and open it up, pressing the sides evenly to make the hole bigger. Fill it with 1 tbsp of the mushroom mixture, and close up the hole by carefully pushing the bulgur dough over the hole. They don’t have to be perfectly round, they often come in an oblong shape, too. (See the video for a visual on how to do this.) Repeat to make about 12 balls.

To fry, fill a saucepan with enough oil to cover the koupes and heat to 180°C. Deep fry in batches for 3-5 mins until browned. Remove from the oil and place on a paper towel to absorb any excess oil. Repeat with the remaining koupes and serve immediately.
Serve with plenty of lemon, as they are best eaten with a big squeeze of fresh lemon juice squeezed into the cracked open koupes.
They keep for 2 days, sealed in the fridge. To reheat, pop them in the oven for 5 mins to crisp up again.

name: Mushroom Mapo-ish Tofu
description: Our vegan take on a Sichuan classic with spicy, aromatic tofu and meaty shiitake mushrooms. Be warned: it’s addictive.
instructions: Peel and finely chop the ginger and garlic. Finely slice the chilli. Mince the Shiitake mushrooms as finely as possible (or use a mini chopper). Mix the cornflour with water and set aside. Finely chop the spring onions. Drain and slice the tofu into 3cm pieces. Drain and rinse the beans.

Heat a glug of vegetable oil (or another neutral oil) in a wok or a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the Chinese five spice and cook for 30 seconds. Add in the garlic, ginger and chilli and cook for another 30 seconds. Add in the mushrooms, season with salt and cook for a couple of mins until golden.

Add the bean paste and the black beans, along with the water, and mix well. Make the cornflour slurry by mixing together the cornflour and water in a small bowl then add to the pan. Season with salt, to taste, then simmer for about 5 mins until the sauce is starting to thicken then gently stir through the tofu. Simmer for another 5 mins or until the tofu is hot and the sauce has thickened. Taste and season with salt, if needed.
Season with, salt, sesame oil, sugar and Chinese black vinegar to taste.
Divide between plates and top with the sliced spring onions. Serve with crispy chilli oil and cooked rice, if you like.

name: Mushroom Mayhem Tortelloni
description: La Famiglia Rana's delicious Mushroom & Mascarpone Tortelloni is the hero of this recipe. Delicious al denta pasta and fresh mushrooms? A winning combination.
instructions: Bring a large pan of water to a gentle boil.
Start by roughly chopping the mushrooms to similar sized pieces.
Heat 3 tbsp olive oil to a large frying pan over a high heat. Add the mushrooms with a pinch of salt and cook for 5 mins, until golden.
Meanwhile, finely chop the garlic, remove the leaves from the thyme and finely chop the parsley (stalks and all).
Add the finely chopped or grated garlic, thyme and parsley to the mushrooms to fry for another minute before adding in the white wine to bubble. Turn down the heat to low

Empty the La Famiglia Rana Mushroom & Mascarpone Tortelloni into the boiling water and cook for only 2 mins. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the pasta to the mushroom sauce with a big splash of pasta water. Finely grate the parmesan into the pan and add the lemon juice. Toss until the silky sauce coats the pasta. Season well with salt and pepper.
Tip onto plates and serve with extra grated Parmesan and a scattering of walnuts.

name: Mushroom Miso Barley Bowl
description: This is for those who love creamy mushrooms.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice your onions into thin strips and leave to soak in white wine vinegar whilst you prepare the salad - use enough vinegar to cover the onions.
Pour the pearl barley into a large sauce pan and cover with water. Stir in the miso paste and the skin of the ginger. Continue to boil until the pearl barley is soft. Drain and set aside.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a frying pan and add the mushrooms. Slice your ginger into matchsticks and throw them in to give the mushrooms a kick. Slice your garlic into thin discs and add to the frying pan with 1 tbsp of soy sauce. Sprinkle a few chilli flakes over the mushrooms and leave to one side.

Dressing time. To a jar, add your tahini, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp chilli flakes, 2 tbsp white wine vinegar, a splash of olive oil and water. Screw the lid on tight and shake until all of the ingredients are combined.
To prepare your kale, spread the leaves out on a baking tray. Cover in olive oil, salt and pepper and roast for about 10 minutes.

Use your pearl barley as the bed for the salad and top with your mushrooms, roasted kale, pickled red onion, fresh coriander and a sprinkle of chilli flakes. Drizzle your dressing over your salad and get stuck in.

name: Mushroom Ragù & Polenta
description: This rich mushroom ragù is super meaty and satisfying, served on a bed of creamy polenta.
keywords: Hearty mushroom ragù and polenta recipe
instructions: Add 30g of butter to a large saucepan. Dice the onion and sweat over a medium heat. Dice the celery and add to the pan along with the rosemary and thyme. Cook for another 10 mins until soft and fragrant, then use a slotted spoon to remove from the pan.
Meanwhile, mince all of the chestnut mushrooms (they don't need to be neat!).
We’ll cook the mushrooms in two batches. Add the minced mushrooms to the pan, turn up the heat and cook for a few minutes, stirring regularly until they’re nicely browned. Remove from the pan.

Tear up the wild mushrooms so they keep some of their shape. Add the wild mushrooms and brown all over. Once they have some good colour, add other mushrooms and the onion and celery back into the pan and mix together.
Pour in the wine and allow to bubble off until almost completely evaporated.
Now pour in the vegetable stock, bring up to a gentle simmer and allow to cook for 20 mins.
Once the ragù is thick and saucy, mince up the parsley and stir it through.
Cook the polenta in boiling salted water, add the butter and stir. Loosen with water as necessary until you have a soft creamy texture.
Plate up a generous portion of polenta and top with a big spoon of the mushroom ragù. Best served with a big hunk of crusty bread.

name: Mushroom Risotto
description: The lads from Pastore have blessed the MOB Studio, teaching us the ultimate way to make mushroom risotto. So simple yet so effective.
instructions: Bring the stock up to just below a simmer in a saucepan.
Dice up your onions, crush two cloves of garlic, and then finely chop your remaining three cloves of garlic.

Tear your shiitake mushrooms into small pieces. Add half of your butter to a frying pan with a little oil until it begins to foam. Fry off your mushrooms until they're golden, this should take about 10 mins, then add in your 2 cloves of crushed garlic.

Drain off the mushrooms, saving the oil/butter mixture. In the same pan, add your diced onion. Cook until they start to become golden, for about 5 mins. Next, add your 3 finely chopped cloves of garlic.
When the garlic has started to sweat for 2 mins add your risotto rice.

The idea is to slightly toast the rice, so when you drag your spoon across the bottom of the pan the rice should feel like it’s slightly sticking to the pan. This should take roughly 3 mins on a gentle heat.
Add your wine and cook off for 30 secs.
Add your stock ladle by ladle until the risotto is al dente, this should take about 15 mins. Add your butter and 50g grated pecorino cheese and leave to rest for 10 mins.
Save a little stock so that you can adjust the consistency of your risotto if needed.
Meanwhile, separate your egg yolks and finely slice your raw chestnut mushrooms.
Plate up your risotto with the cooked mushrooms over the rice. Top with your fresh egg yolks, sliced raw chestnut mushrooms, a generous amount of fresh black pepper, and more cheese. Enjoy.

name: Mushroom Shawarma & Chickpea Hummus
description: Got 15 minutes to make lunch? Make this nourishing vegan chickpea hummus bowl with spiced oyster mushrooms. It’s full of plants and full of flavour.
instructions: Add the drained chickpeas to a saucepan. Fill it with boiling water, add the baking soda and leave to boil for a few mins (this softens the outer skin of the chickpeas for a smoother hummus). Drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, thinly slice your red onion and shred your mushrooms using two forks.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the red onion and fry for a few minutes until starting to soften.
Add the chickpeas, tahini, garlic, juice of the lemon, water and ice cubes to a blender and blitz, adding more water, salt and lemon as needed to achieve your desired taste and consistency.
Add the mushrooms to the pan with the onions and fry for a few mins until golden. Add your spices and salt, mix to combine and leave to cook off for 30 seconds until fragrant.
To serve, add the hummus to a bowl and top with the spiced mushrooms. Sprinkle over the sumac and fresh parsley and serve with some warm pitta bread, if you like.

name: Mushroom Skewers with Ezme & Hummus
description: A plant-based skewer recipe that you're going to love. We've paired charred mushroom skewers with a tangy Turkish-inspired salad and creamy homemade hummus.
keywords: Mushroom Skewers with Ezme & Hummus recipe
instructions: Finely chop the preserved lemons and remove the pips. Place them into a pestle and mortar and add the garlic and spices, olive oil and salt and pepper, then grind into a paste. If you don't have a pestle and mortar, mince the garlic and mix everything in a bowl.

Tear the mushrooms if they are very big and then add to a large mixing bowl. Peel and cut the onion into eighths and break up the layers. Add the preserved lemon paste to the mushrooms and onions with some extra olive oil and toss to combine well. If you have time, you can leave them to marinate for an hour in the fridge.

Preheat the oven to 200°C and alternate the mushrooms and onions onto the skewers. Line a baking tray and place the skewers onto it. Bake for 10 mins on the top shelf, then turn and bake for another 10-15 mins until golden and crispy on the edges. Finish with a drizzle of pomegranate molasses and a sprinkle of sea salt if you like.

Finely chop the onion, chilli, cherry tomatoes, pepper and parsley and keep them all on the chopping board. Once they are all chopped, push them together and chop again to combine all of the flavours and make sure everything is chopped very fine. Add all of the ingredients to a bowl and season with plenty of salt and pepper. Add the lemon juice, pomegranate molasses and Aleppo pepper.
Drain the chickpeas and save the chickpea water.
Add all of the ingredients to a high speed blender and blend until smooth. Taste and adjust seasonings or add more lemon juice to your preference.
To serve, plate up the hummus and top with the ezme salad. Add the mushrooms skewers on the side and scoop it all up with the flatbread.

name: Mushroom Stew with Cannellini Bean Mash
description: If you’re looking for wintery comfort food that also improves your gut health, we’ve got you. This mushroom stew with cannellini bean mash feels like a warm hug and is packed with fibre and plant protein.
keywords: Mushroom Stew with Cannellini Bean Mash
Mushroom Stew with Cannellini Bean Mash recipe
instructions: Finely slice the shallot and garlic. Slice the mushrooms.

For the bean mash, heat a glug of oil in a medium pan over a medium heat. Add ½ the garlic and ½ the rosemary and thyme sprigs and cook for a minute or two until the garlic starts to turn translucent.
Add the beans with ½ their bean juice. Season with a pinch of salt and simmer for 10 mins until the beans are soft enough to mash with a wooden spoon.

For the mushrooms, heat a glug of olive oil in a separate pan over a medium heat and add the shallot, sage leaf and remaining garlic, rosemary and thyme. Gently fry until the shallots are translucent and slightly caramelised. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook for a further 5 mins.
Add a splash of vegetable stock to the mushrooms then season to taste and tear in the cavolo nero.
Divide the bean mash between plates and top with the mushrooms.

name: Mushroom Stuffed Savoury Crêpe
description: This quick and easy stuffed crêpe is perfect for brunch, lunch or dinner. You can play around with the fillings and use up any leafy greens or veggies you like.
instructions: Start by weighing your chickpea flour and sifting it into a large bowl. This is an important step to make sure the batter is smooth and has no lumps.
Add the water to the flour and olive oil and whisk well. Set aside on the counter, covered with a plate while you prepare the filling.
Slice the mushrooms, onion, and mince the garlic.

Set a large non-stick frying pan on medium heat. Fry the onion with a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt, for about 5 mins, until translucent. Add the mushrooms and garlic and season again with salt and pepper. Cook for about 6-8 more mins, until the mushrooms are cooked and starting to brown and caramelise.
Add the kale or spinach to the mushrooms and fry for 4-6 mins until wilted. Add chilli flakes here if using and season to taste.
Remove the mushrooms from the pan and set them aside. Wipe the pan clean, then add a small amount of oil and spread it around the pan. Set the heat to medium-low.
Pour a big ladle of chickpea batter into the pan so it spreads in a thin layer, evenly to the edges of the pan. It should be the thickness of a crêpe.
Cook it for about 3-4 mins on medium-low heat until the edges start to brown and curl away from the pan. Use a small rubber spatula to carefully lift an edge to check if the bottom is cooked.

When it's cooked, spread half of the mushroom mix over one-half of the crêpe and fold the other half over. Carefully shuffle the crêpe onto a plate and top with pesto and crème fraîche, if using. Repeat for the second crêpe.

name: Mushroom and Miso Pie
description: A creamy, cheesy mushroom pie filled with lots of juicy Quorn Pieces. Possibly the best pie you will ever have. Don't believe us? Try it out for yourself.
keywords: Miso quorn and mushroom pie recipes
instructions: Finely chop the onions and garlic before slicing up the mushrooms.
Pick the leaves off the thyme and finely chop the tarragon.

Sauté the onions in a pan with a glug of oil. Cook for 5 mins until softened, then add in the mushrooms with a big pinch of salt. Cook for 15 mins until the water has evaporated and the mushrooms start to crisp up.
Add in the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add in the flour and mix well so that there are no large bits.
Combine the miso paste with 300ml of hot water, whisk until it's dissolved.
Slowly pour the miso liquid into the mushrooms, mixing well in between so the flour doesn't form lumps.
Add in the Quorn Pieces and bring to a bubble. Grate in the comté cheese and stir through the crème fraîche, thyme and tarragon.
Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Pour this into your pie dish and allow it to cool down for 20 mins.
Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Cover the pie with the puff pastry, trim the edges and crimp them with your thumb and forefinger.
Brush with egg yolk and pop into the oven for 30 mins until the pastry is puffed and golden.
Allow to cool for 30 mins, slice and serve.

name: Mushrooms & Cavolo Nero On Toast With Ricotta
description: Who knew that mushrooms and cavolo nero were best friends with ricotta? This recipe comes together in half an hour and will brighten up any lunchtime blues.
keywords: Mushrooms & Cavolo Nero On Toast With Ricotta
instructions: Begin by adding the ricotta to a bowl with the juice of half a lemon and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Whisk to combine.
Rub the slices of bread with a little olive oil on both sides and then grill in a griddle pan until golden brown.
Roughly chop the mushrooms but not too small.
Strip the leaves of the cavolo nero and then roughly chop it up. Mince the garlic.
Set a large pan over a medium-high heat and add 2 tbsp of olive oil. When hot, add the mushrooms and season the salt and pepper.

Cook the mushrooms for 4 mins until they have lightly browned all over. Add the butter, allow it to melt and then add the garlic and thyme. Cook for a minute before adding the cavolo nero and seasoning with salt and pepper.
Add the juice of half a lemon and cook for 4 mins or until the cavolo nero has wilted. Spread the ricotta mix over each slice of bread and top with the mushrooms and cavolo nero.
Fry up your eggs and top off your toasts.

name: Mushy Pea Linguine
description: 6 ingredients. 12 minutes. Crispy bacon. Creamy ricotta. Sweet peas. It's a game changer.
instructions: Cut bacon into small bits and chuck into a pan. Fry until crispy.
Get the linguine on.
Rest a colander over the pan and add the peas.

After 5 minutes, the peas should be ready. Remove from the heat and put in a bowl. Add ricotta, a handful of chopped mint and the juice of a lemon. Season with salt and pepper, a drizzle of olive oil and mash.
Take half of the peas and blend with 3 ladles of pasta water.
Drain pasta. Pour pasta into the bacon pan. Add the blended mushy peas and the rest of the mushy peas.
Dollop ricotta over the top and squeeze over some lemon juice. Enjoy!

name: Mushy Peas
description: You can’t have fish and chips without mushy peas. Fact. Making your own mushy peas recipe couldn’t be simpler and these will 100% be better than anything you might get at the chippy. This mushy peas recipe uses traditional ingredients like marrowfat peas, giving it an authentic taste and creamy texture. Simple and easy to prepare, mushy peas offer a delightful complement to various main courses. Ideal for both family dinners and casual gatherings, this dish is not only delicious but also rich in protein. Whether you're a fan of classic British food or just looking for a tasty side, this mushy peas recipe is sure to satisfy your chip shop craving. Keep any leftovers in the fridge and enjoy a hearty, nutritious meal any day of the week.
instructions: Drain the marrowfat peas through a fine sieve (discard the liquid), then tip them into a small saucepan. Pour in the chicken stock and put over a medium-high heat. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat slightly and simmer for 20 mins until the peas are starting to collapse and it has thickened. Remove from the heat.
Use a potato masher to roughly crush the peas, then add the butter and season with the vinegar, salt and white pepper to taste.

name: Mustard Paprika Chicken With Marinated Peppers
description: Dijon mustard is your new BBQ secret weapon, combined with paprika and garlic, it’s a winner. We cooked this on the Weber Lumin Electric Barbecue, dead easy.
keywords: Mustard Paprika Chicken With Marinated Peppers
instructions: Chuck the chicken legs onto a baking tray and season generously with salt and pepper.

Put the Dijon mustard, paprika and 3 tbsp olive oil into a small mixing bowl. Finely grate in 3 of the garlic cloves and mix thoroughly. Pour the marinade over the chicken legs and massage together. Leave to marinate for 1 hr or up to overnight in the fridge.

Preheat the Weber Lumin Electric Barbecue to high heat. Half the shallots, skin on, and chuck into a bowl with the whole peppers. Coat with a little olive oil and salt. Put on the grill, shallots cut-side down, close the lid and let blister, turning the peppers regularly, for 9-10 mins. Let the shallots really char on the cut side.

Pull the peppers and shallots off the grill, chuck them into a bowl and cover with a plate. Let the veggies steam for 5-6 mins. Once steamed, peel and roughly chop the peppers and sling them into a bowl. Tear over the oregano and add 3 tbsp olive oil, the vinegar and salt and pepper. Set aside in a warm place. Peel the burnt skins from the shallots and separate into petals.

With the grill still set to high, add the chicken legs, skin-side down. Close the lid and let ‘em cook for 7-8 mins until the skin is super crispy and charred. Flip ‘em over and lower the heat to medium, close the lid and cook for 25 mins, moving now and then, until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, mix the tahini and yoghurt in a small bowl and grate in the last garlic clove. Add the zest and juice of one lemon and stir together until smooth. Season and set aside.

Lift the lid of the BBQ and chuck the flatbreads onto the chicken to warm through. Grab a platter and lay down the warm flatbreads, add the marinated peppers, roasted shallots and top with the chicken. Let all the chicken juices soak into the flatbreads. Add dollops of tahini yoghurt and wedges of lemon to serve.

name: Mustardy Chicken & Bacon Sandwich Filler
description: A match made in culinary heaven, this chicken and bacon filling makes the ultimate high protein sandwich - plus there's cornichons involved, what a win.
keywords: Mustardy Chicken & Bacon Sandwich Filler recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Add the chicken to a roasting tray, drizzle with olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Roast for 25 mins, then rest for 10 mins before dicing.
Turn on the grill. Lay the bacon onto a tray and cook for 5–10 mins until crispy. Chop into shards.
Finely chop the chives and cornichons.
In a bowl, mix the yoghurt, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, honey and apple cider vinegar. Add the chopped chives, cornichons, diced chicken and crispy bacon. Mix well and season with salt and pepper.

Serve however you like, but we love this filling stuffed between tiger bread with rocket and juicy tomatoes.
If you're making ahead, pop the filling into the fridge in Tupperware (it will keep for up to 3 days).

name: Muttar Paneer
description: A mild, creamy Punjabi curry for all you cheese lovers. Fried paneer, sweet peas and all the spices. Ditch your takeaway and have this instead. Sophie x
instructions: Place your onion, garlic, ginger and chilli in a food processor and blend to a paste. Scrape into a bowl.

In the same food processor, add the plum tomatoes from their tin, discarding the juice. Blend to a paste. Don’t worry about washing it up in between blends - it will just add more flavour to the tomatoes.
Cut your paneer into 1 inch cubes.
Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a little vegetable oil and your paneer, then pan fry on all sides until crisp. Remove from the pan.
Pour a small glug of oil into the same frying pan. Add your cumin seeds and cardamom pods and fry for a minute until fragrant.
Add your onion paste to the same pan and cook out for 10 minutes until your paste is a light golden brown. Add your coriander, turmeric, garam masala and chilli powder. Cook out for 2 mins.
Add your chopped tomatoes and tomato puree and simmer for 5 minutes until they have darkened and gone jammy. Pour in your cream and the water, then simmer briefly.
Tip in your peas and paneer. Simmer for 10 mins, then season to taste with salt.

Top with a drizzle of cream and a sprinkle of coriander, then serve up with rice or chapatis.Freezing TipsLet the curry cool to room temperature before transferring it to an airtight Tupperware. Store in the freezer for up to 3 months. When ready to eat, either reheat straight in a pan over a low heat, pop in the microwave until piping hot, or leave in the fridge to thaw before reheating

name: Myriad's Sushi Onirigazu
description: Hey, It's Em from Myriad Recipes here with my Sushi Sandwich. I’ve been making sushi since I was a kid and this is one of my favourite ways to eat it! Enjoy.
instructions: Pour your sushi rice into a saucepan and rinse with water several times. Once the water is clear, drain the rice and then pour in 75g of cold water. Place your pan on high heat. Once the water is boiling, turn the heat to low, place on your lid, and leave to cook for 10 mins. Once the 10 mins is up, turn the heat off, remove the lid and transfer into a bowl. Leave the rice to cool down completely.
In a small bowl, combine your crab stick strips with 2 tbsp mayonnaise, ½ tbsp soy sauce, and black pepper. Give it a good mix and then set it aside.
Grab a frying pan, place it on medium heat, and drizzle in some veggie oil. Crack your egg into the pan and whisk it up. Form it into a square omelette and then set it aside to cool.
Prep your avocado.
In a little bowl, combine your 2 tbsp rice wine vinegar with 1 ½ tbsp sugar, and ½ tbsp salt. Then, pour it over your cool sushi rice and give it a good mix.

Time to assemble! Lay down a piece of cling film on your work surface (long enough to wrap up your sushi sandwich). Place down a nori sheet with the corner angle facing you. Layer on with sushi rice, avocado, crab, egg, avocado, more sushi rice, and a final nori sheet (with the non-angled side of the square facing you). Wrap it all up using a bit of rice wine vinegar to help the sides stick, then tightly wrap with clingfilm and place it into the fridge for 15 minutes.
Combine 1 tbsp sriracha and 1 tbsp mayonnaise to make your dipping sauce.
Slice open your onigirazu, serve it up with your spicy dipping sauce, and enjoy!

name: N*ndo's Fino Pitta
description: This extra cheeky recipe is a riff on everyone's favourite item from Nando's: the fino pitta. Juicy chicken thighs and a killer marinade. You'll love this.
instructions: For the peri peri marinade, add all of the ingredients to a blender and season generously with salt and pepper – and I mean generously. Blitz until smooth. Marinate the chicken thighs in the sauce for a minimum of 1 hr (but ideally overnight) in a covered bowl.

For the onion relish, peel and finely slice the red onions. Melt the butter and a splash of olive oil in a large pot and cook the onions with a big pinch of salt for 30-40 mins until sticky and soft. If they start to catch, just add in a splash of water and give it a good mix. Add the sugar and vinegar, then gently simmer for about 5 more mins until really sticky – give it a taste and adjust the vinegar and sugar to your liking. Set aside.
For the aioli, grate the garlic and zest and juice the lemon into the mayonnaise. Give it a good mix and season with salt and pepper. Done! Slice the halloumi and separate the romaine leaves.

Heat your grill to high. Remove the chicken from the fridge and bring it up to room temp for 20 mins, then transfer to a tray. Slide under the grill and cook for 20-25 mins until the chicken is cooked through and charred. In the meantime, heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over a medium heat and add the halloumi. Cook for 2 mins on each side until golden.
Time to assemble! Warm your pitta, then fill with aioli, chicken, halloumi, relish and lettuce. Voilà!

name: Nashville Hot Air Fryer Chicken Legs Recipe
description: If you're craving crispy, spicy chicken with minimal effort, this Nashville Hot Air Fryer Chicken Legs recipe is perfect for you. These air fryer chicken legs deliver all the bold flavours of classic fried chicken, but with less oil and mess. Coated in a fiery mix of smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, and garlic powder, the chicken legs develop a crispy skin that rivals deep-fried alternatives. The airfryer method ensures even cooking, leaving the chicken tender and juicy inside while perfectly crispy outside. Whether you’re serving them with fries, a fresh salad, or dipping in honey mustard, this recipe for air fryer chicken legs makes for a quick and delicious dinner. Pair it with your favourite sides like coleslaw or roasted vegetables for a satisfying meal with a spicy kick.
keywords: Nashville Hot Air Fryer Chicken Legs Recipe
instructions: Spoon the buttermilk into a bowl or container along with the hot sauce and plenty of salt and pepper. Add the chicken legs and toss really well to coat. You can leave this to marinate for up to 12 hrs, or you can use it straight away.
Put the flour into a shallow bowl with the baking powder, garlic powder, paprika and cayenne pepper, plus plenty of salt and pepper. Mix until well combined.
Take the chicken legs, one at a time, from the buttermilk mix and straight into the flour, really patting to coat. Repeat with the other chicken leg and put onto a plate while you prep the air fryer.

Line the basket of the air fryer with foil, then lay in the chicken legs, skin-side up. Give the chicken legs a really good spray with oil, to evenly coat, then set the air fryer to 190°C and put the timer on for 45 mins.
Check and shake the basket every 15 mins or so. Give the chicken legs another spray of oil if they need it.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small pan and add all the sauce ingredients. Whisk together until even – adjust the spice level and seasoning to your liking. Reheat the sauce just before the chicken is ready.
Once the chicken is super crisp, pour over the sauce and serve with buttered bread and sliced pickles, if you like.

name: Nectarine & Burrata Salad With Charred Lemon Dressing
description: Creamy burrata, smoky sweet nectarine, and a fresh lemon dressing. This is summer on a platter.
keywords: Nectarine & Burrata Salad With Charred Lemon Dressing
instructions: Preheat the grill to high. Halve and pit the nectarines, then chop into wedges and drizzle with a little olive oil. Halve the lemons. Lightly drizzle olive oil onto the flatbreads and sprinkle over the oregano.
Once the grill is hot, grill the nectarines on both sides and the lemon until charred for 5 mins.
Remove and add the bread to the grill, cook until crispy 3 mins.
Meanwhile, finely chop the preserved lemon. Drizzle in the honey and 5 tbsp of olive oil, season with salt and pepper, then squeeze the juice of the charred lemon.

Trim the courgettes and use a peeler to shave ribbons into a large bowl. Add the nectarines to the courgette and tear the bread in. Pick the mint leaves and add ¾ in with the fruit. Drizzle three quarters of the dressing over and give everything a good toss.
Plate the nectarine panzanella onto a large serving dish. Top with scoops of burrata and garnish with the remaining mint, dressing and a sprinkle of sumac (if using).

name: Nectarine Granita with Vanilla Cream, Honey, Olive Oil & Thyme
description: Here's a refreshing homemade granita recipe using in-season nectarines. We've paired it with vanilla ice cream, honey, and even thrown in a few savoury elements with olive oil and fresh thyme. Dreamy.
instructions: Freeze the nectarines overnight.

The next day, pick the thyme leaves and set aside. Pour the double cream into a large bowl and add the vanilla and sugar. Whisk with either a hand whisk or electric whisk until you have very soft peaks that just about hold their shape.

Get the nectarines out of the freezer and grate a single nectarine into each serving bowl. Add a dollop of the whipped cream, a drizzle of honey, olive oil, a pinch of salt and a scattering of thyme to each bowl.

name: New Potato Tart With Rocket Pesto
description: This spring vegetable tart really showcases the bright flavours of the season. The sweet, waxy new potatoes are at their best from April to July.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C Fan. Wash the potatoes, keeping the skin on. Slice the leeks thinly, then wash them well. Mince three of your garlic cloves.

Slice the potatoes thinly on a mandolin or with a knife. Heat a saucepan on medium with a good glug of olive oil. Add the leeks and garlic and sauté until the leeks have softened slightly. Add the potatoes and sauté until they are soft and almost cooked through fully, about 8-10 mins, stirring often.

Meanwhile, mix the milk with the Oat Fraiche and grate a pinch of nutmeg into it. Use a whisk to mix it together well. Once the potatoes are soft, turn off the heat and add this to the saucepan and mix well, making sure the potatoes and leeks are fully covered. Set aside.

Lay out your puff pastry and score the edges about 1.5cm from the edge along each side. Make sure you don't cut all the way through to the bottom. Poke the inner square many times with a fork and brush the frame with a little milk.* Bake for 5 mins.

Take the tart out and lay the potato mix evenly into the inner square. Grind plenty of fresh pepper onto the top and a sprinkle of salt. Bake for 30-35 mins until the potatoes are starting to crisp up and brown on top and the pastry is golden brown.

While your pastry is cooking, make the pesto. Roughly chop the rocket (save a few leaves for the topping) and one garlic clove and add these to a food processor with 60ml of olive oil, 80g pine nuts and the juice and zest of half a lemon. If you have nutritional yeast, you could add a teaspoon here for a cheesy taste. Pulse until you have a chunky texture and season generously with salt and pepper.
Roughly chop the chicory, mix in a bowl with a little olive oil and lemon. To serve, scatter the chicory and a few rocket leaves over the tart, then spoon on the pesto generously.

name: New York Cheesecake With Burst Blueberries
description: Outrageously good. This creamy yet fruity cheesecake is finished with beautifully burst blueberries for a decadent take on your classic New York Cheesecake.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C. Add the biscuits and bran flakes into a food processor, break them down into a fine crumb. If you don't have a food processor, add them into a large ziplock or sandwich bag and bash them with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until they break down into fine crumbs.

Melt the butter and mix into the biscuit crumbs with 1 tsp of fine salt and 1 tbsp of sugar. The mixture should be sandy but once you squeeze some of it, it should be able to retain the shape without easily crumbling apart.

Lay a round piece of baking paper onto the bottom of a 20cm springform pan, butter the inside of the springform pan on all sides, including the baking paper. Add 60% of the crumb mixture into the springform and evenly push the mixture into the sides. Using a glass or something with a 90° angle, push and compact the crumbs into the sides of the pan, making sure they come up the sides completely. Add the remaining crumbs and push into the bottom of the springform pan. Parbake the crust in the oven for 10-12 mins, until set.
Once the crumb base is cooling, turn the heat up to 200°C.
Add the room-temp softened cream cheese into a large bowl with the goat's cheese, vanilla paste and salt. Mix together.
In another bowl, massage together the zest of ½ a lemon and 250g of granulated sugar. Whisk through the cornflour until incorporated.
Crack the eggs and egg yolk into another bowl and give them a whisk. Gradually stir the sugar mixture and eggs into the cream cheese, alternating between both.

Heat up the double cream in a small saucepan over high heat until it comes to a boil. Whisk it into the cream cheese mixture in one steady stream — this warms the batter and helps release any air pockets that may have been introduced whilst whisking.
Place the crumbed pan onto a baking tray, then slowly pour the batter into it. Bounce a spoon on the surface of the batter to dislodge any air bubbles, keep doing this until no more bubbles come up.

Bake the cheesecake at 200°C for 12-15 mins until the cheesecake has puffed slightly. The top may start to go golden, this will bring more flavour to the cheesecake. Turn the oven off and open the oven door slightly for 10 mins.

After 10 mins, lightly ‘drape’ foil on top of the cheesecake, close the oven door, and turn the oven up to 120°C. Bake for 1-1.5 hrs until the cheesecake has set and only the middle has a slight wobble (the wobble shouldn’t touch the edges, only the middle).

Turn the oven off, and let the cheesecake cool down in there for 45 mins. Remove it from the oven and let it cool fully at room temperature, before placing it in the fridge for a minimum of 12 hours. Before serving, let the cheesecake come up to room temperature.

Whilst the cheesecake is in the fridge, add half the blueberries, ½ tsp of salt, 120g granulated sugar and the juice of the zested lemon into a saucepan. Mix together and let macerate for 10 mins. Then, turn the heat up to medium and cook the mixture down until the blueberries release their juices and the mixture gets thicker, 6-8 mins. Add the remaining blueberries and cook for another 2-3 mins. Remove from the heat and transfer to a bowl. Let the blueberries cool down completely before serving.
Slice up your cheesecake and drizzle over the burst blueberries.

name: New York Style Poppy Seed Bagels & Lox
description: It’s time you made your own bagels. These beauties have that signature chewy crust and will have your house smelling like a NYC bagel shop.
instructions: Tip the flour and yeast into a bowl with the sugar and fine salt. Blend the dry ingredients together before tipping in the warm water. Use your hand to bring the ingredients together into a shaggy dough. You want to incorporate all of the flour in the bowl, so keep mixing until there are no dry spots left!

Tip the dough out onto your countertop and knead for 8-10 mins until it is smooth, springy and has lots of strength. You can test this a few different ways, but my go-to is the window-pane test: using your thumb and forefinger on each hand, grab a corner of your dough and stretch it out as thin as you can. You should be able to see light passing through it (like a windowpane) before it tears. If it tears too easily, get back to kneading!

Once you’re happy with the gluten development, pop the dough into a bowl and cover. Allow to prove at room temperature for about an hour, or until doubled in size. Once proved, tip the dough back out onto your worktop and divide into 100-110g pieces. Flatten each piece into a long rectangle. Roll the dough up into a sausage, roughly 20-22cm long and about an inch thick.

To form the classic bagel shape, join the two ends of the sausage in the palm of your hand, wrapping the loop around the top of your hand. Roll the two ends together between your palm and the worktop, joining them together. Roll them until the join is roughly the same size as the rest of the bagel.

Line a couple of trays with parchment paper and set the bagels out on them to prove. Make sure you give them plenty of space to grow and cover them loosely with plastic wrap. You can either prove them at room temperature for an hour or so (until doubled in size) or you can do it overnight in the fridge. I prefer the overnight prove as you get a much nicer texture and flavour!
When your bagels are just about proved, preheat the oven to 220°C and set up a tray filled with the poppy seeds. Cut the paper between the bagels so each is sitting on a little square of parchment.

Fill a large pot with water (roughly 5 litres) and add the treacle and bicarbonate of soda. Whisk to combine and set over a high heat. Bring to a boil and then carefully lower in your proved bagels on the paper, peeling it off once they’re floating. Cook for about 30 seconds a side (flipping them over so both sides cook) before scooping them out with a slotted spoon or spider. Drop them straight into the poppy seed filled tray and flip them around a few times, completely coating them in the seeds. Repeat with the remaining bagels.
Put the poached bagels back onto a tray lined with parchment and slide into the oven for 20 mins until a deep golden brown. Whip them out and allow to cool on a rack for at least 15-20 mins.
Split the bagels in half and stuff with sliced smoked trout, cream cheese, sliced raw red onions and capers.

name: Nigella Seed Gnudi With Curried Tomato Butter
description: If you love gnocchi, you probably also love gnudi. Soft, fluffy ricotta dumplings, swimming in tomato sauce. We've added curry leaves for a fun twist.
keywords: Nigella Seed Gnudi With Curried Tomato Butter
Nigella Seed Gnudi With Curried Tomato Butter recipe
instructions: Season the ricotta with salt, stir and place into a fine mesh sieve over a bowl. Let it drain for at least 1 hour.
Finely grate the Pecorino and add 15g into a bowl. Add the ricotta, breadcrumbs, flour, nigella seeds, ½ tsp of salt in with it. Crack the eggs in and stir together. Season with lots of pepper.

Evenly scatter half of the semolina onto a tray. Scoop 1 tbsp worth of ricotta dough with a spoon and plop onto the semolina, repeat this with the rest of the ricotta mix. Scatter the remaining semolina on top of the ricotta dumplings and place in the fridge overnight to dry.

Meanwhile, add the curry leaves into a blender with 30ml of oil. Blend until broken down, then pour into a small saucepan and place on medium heat. Cook for 2-3 mins until dark green, then strain through a fine mesh sieve into a bowl.
Pour the peeled tomatoes into an empty saucepan and crush to break the tomatoes down. Grate the garlic in and cook on medium-high heat, stirring occasionally until thickened, 6-10 mins.

After drying, remove from the fridge and roll the dumplings into tight round circles. Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, gently drop the gnudi in and cook until they float to the top. Add the cooked gnudi into the tomato sauce on medium heat and toss through, adding a splash of water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Share onto plates and scatter over the remaining Pecorino and mint leaves. Serve with a fresh crack of black pepper and a drizzle of curry leaf oil.

name: No-Churn Coconutty Mango Sorbet
description: It is ridiculously hot. Cool yourself down with this easy 4-ingredient sorbet that takes minutes to make. If tropical vibes are your thing, you’ll love this!
instructions: Place the frozen mango chunks in a high-powered blender or food processor.
Add the coconut milk, agave nectar and zest and juice of the limes.
Blitz until smooth, scraping down the sides and blending as necessary.
Enjoy immediately, or freeze for 1 hour for a firmer texture.

name: No-Churn Ice Cream With Miso Cinnamon Caramel Swirl
description: We've upgraded your standard tub of vanilla ice cream and drizzled it with a miso cinnamon and caramel sauce and studs of toasted pecans.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C and toast the pecans for 8-10 mins. Once toasted, cool and roughly chop, then set aside.

For the caramel put the sugar in a saucepan and cook it down until bubbling and amber. Do not stir. Just swirl the sugar in the pan, and note that the sugar will clump before melting so be patient - this will take around 10 mins. In the meantime dice the butter. When your sugar is amber in colour, add the butter - be careful it will bubble! Pour in the cream and whisk. If it starts to seize, heat gently until liquid again. Next, add in the miso and cinnamon and whisk to combine, set aside to cool.

For the ice cream, pour the condensed milk, double cream, vanilla and salt into large bowl and whisk together until quite thick. Add the pecans (and alcohol, if using) and mix again. Add about ⅓ of the ice cream to a 1 litre container and pour over some of the caramel, then swirl into the ice cream, gently. Continue in layers with the remaining ice cream and caramel, saving some caramel for serving. Cover with cling film making sure it's touching the surface of the mixture. Put a lid on and freeze for 8 hours or overnight.
Before serving, remove the ice cream from the freezer and let it thaw for 15 mins before scooping. Warm the caramel gently and drizzle over the ice cream.

name: No-Churn Mini Egg Ice Cream
description: Four simple steps and you'll have yourself a punnet of the greatest ice cream, ever.
instructions: Pour the condensed milk, double cream, salt, and vanilla into a large bowl and whisk together. Add the vodka or rum, if using. Roughly chop the Mini Eggs and stir through.
Tip into a 1 litre container, cover with cling film, making sure it’s touching the surface of the mixture.
Place the lid on freeze until solid, 8 hours, preferably overnight.
Before serving, remove the ice cream from the freezer and let thaw for around 15 mins before scooping. Serve in waffle cones if you want, topped with salted caramel sauce.

name: No-Fuss Roast Chicken
description: Golden, juicy and a winner every time. Our classic roast chicken is the ultimate batch meal it's leftovers can be used to make more delicious meals throughout the week.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Take the chicken out of the fridge about 30 mins before roasting – it cooks more evenly that way.
Slice the lemon in half. Crush the garlic cloves with the flat side of a knife, leaving the skins on. Stuff the chicken cavity with the lemon halves, garlic and thyme.
Drizzle the chicken all over with olive oil. Get stuck in and rub it in properly. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Pop the chicken breast-side up in a roasting tray. Roast for about 50 mins–1 hr, or until the juices run clear when you pierce the thickest part of the thigh.
For this recipe used a 1.5kg-2kg chicken, adjust the timings for a smaller or larger bird.
Let it rest for at least 15 mins before carving – it’ll be much juicier, promise.

name: Noodle Bowl with Crispy Tofu and Charred Pak Choi
description: Doctor Rupy Aujla shows MOB how to make his crispy tofu noodle bowl, slathered with his special sweet-spicy sauce. A comforting bowl sure to cure any cold.
instructions: Start off with boiling the kettle.
Slice the tofu into 1cm thick slices, chop the pak choi into halves and cut the limes into wedges. Roughly chop the coriander leaves.
Heat your brilliant'broth through in a saucepan on very low heat

Pop your noodles into a heatproof bowl and pour your boiling water over the top until they are just covered. Put a plate on top and leave for 8 minutes to soften, or according to packet instructions. Drain the water away and divide between your serving bowls.

Heat up a saucepan over medium heat, then pour in a small glug of vegetable oil. Toss the tofu in the cornflour, then add to the pan and fry on both sides until crispy. Put to one side on kitchen paper to cool and soak up any excess oil.
Brush the pak choi and mushrooms with sesame oil, then grill on a hot griddle pan until charred on each side - this should take about 3 minutes per side.
Toast your sesame seeds on a dry saucepan until golden brown.

Make your sweet and spicy sauce for the tofu. Grate the ginger and garlic into a bowl. Add in the tomato puree, maple syrup, chilli pepper, soy sauce and sesame oil, then give it a good mix. Add a splash of hot water to loosen the sauce if needed and coat your tofu.

Build your noodle bowls by pouring the hot brilliant’broth over the noodles in four bowls. Stack with pak choi, crispy tofu and beansprouts. Garnish with lime wedges, coriander, and sesame seeds, and serve.

name: Nori Egg Wraps with Miso-Peanut Butter Slaw
description: Fluffy nori omelette wraps stuffed with crunchy rainbow slaw and a punchy miso-peanut dressing. These taste as good as they look, plus their perfect for making ahead.
instructions: Finely zest the lime then squeeze the juice into a bowl. Whisk in the peanut butter, miso, ⅔ of the soy sauce and honey.
Finely slice the spring onions. Toss the rainbow slaw mix into the dressing. Fold through the coriander leaves and half of the spring onions..
Whisk together the eggs with the remaining ⅓ soy sauce.

Put a nori wrap in a 26cm nonstick frying pan so that the wrap fits neatly into the base. Pour over half of the eggs, using the curved side of a spoon to evenly distribute the egg over the wrap, pushing up into the corners as far as you can go.

Sprinkle over the remaining spring onions then cover with a tight fitting lid and cook for 2-3 mins, until the eggs are set and puffy. Slide onto a plate an repeat with the remaining nori wrap and egg mixture.

Once you've gone through all the egg mix. Take each nori omelette and layer another sheet of nori on top, sandwiching the egg in the middle, then dollop the slaw in the middle and roll up. Serve with sriracha, if you fancy.

name: Not-Your-Average Tomato & Mayo Sarnie
description: Thick-cut salted tomatoes, drenched in cheesy garlic mayo, sandwiched between slices of hot, toasted white bread. You’ll want another one the second it’s gone.
instructions: Slice the tomatoes into thick 1 cm slices. Place onto a tray and season with salt, set aside (make sure they’re room temp, to get the best flavour.)
Finely grate the cheese and garlic into a bowl. Stir the mayo through and season with plenty of freshly cracked black pepper.

Toast the bread if you fancy. Slather one side of each slice with the cheesy mayo, then layer on the salted tomato slices onto 1 side. Drizzle over a little olive oil, then sandwich together and get stuck in.

name: Nourishing Lemon & Herb Chicken Soup
description: Another from our soup series that cook straight from frozen. This one's a riff on an Italian minestrone with extra tender chicken for protein plus lots of herbs and veg, it's definitely hug in a bowl vibes.
instructions: Finely chop the dill and parsley, including the stalks! Peel and cut the carrot into thin matchsticks (or very finely dice). Finely slice the celery and grate the garlic.

Add the dill, parsley, ditalini (any other small pasta shape will do!), carrot, garlic and celery to a freezer safe Tupperware along with the chicken stock and the zest of the lemon. Top with the chicken breast, seasoning it with salt and pepper, then pop into the freezer until ready to use.
When you're ready to cook, transfer the frozen contents of the Tupperware into a saucepan set over a medium heat. Cover with a lid, allow to melt. Then simmer the soup for 10 mins.
Flip the chicken and cook for another 5 mins, until the chicken is cooked through. Once cooked, remove the chicken from the pan and shred into bite-sized pieces and add back into the soup.
Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Sprinkle over some parm and chilli flakes if you fancy too and dish up.

name: Numbing Aubergine White Bean Bowl
description: Crushed Sichuan peppercorns add a nice hum to this recipe. It's spicy, tingly, and will shake up your palate in all the right ways.
instructions: Cut the aubergines into 3-4cm batons. Sprinkle them with salt and let sit for 20-30 mins. In the meantime, trim the ends of the beans, thinly slice the garlic and finely chop the spring onions. Cut the ginger into matchsticks and finely slice the bird's eye chillies.

Preheat a wok over high heat and add a shot of vegetable oil. Add the aubergines and cook over a high heat until tender and caramelised. Drain the beans, saving the bean liquid for later. Add them to the wok and stir fry for a further 2-3 mins. Add the ginger, garlic, spring onion whites and half the chilli. Stir fry for 2-3 more mins.
Season with salt, add the peppercorns, oyster sauce, and black vinegar. Finish at the last minute with the spring onion greens and remaining chilli.

Tip the beans into a food processor. Add 2 tbsp of sesame and a spoon of the fried ginger, garlic, spring onion, and chilli. Add a splash of black vinegar. If the bean mix is too thick, loosen with the reserved bean liquid. Whizz until smooth then taste and season with salt. Set aside.
To serve, spread a swoosh of white beans over the bottom of the bowl, add the stir fried, spicy veggies and top with crushed crackers and sesame seeds.

name: Nuoc Cham (Vietnamese Fish Sauce Dressing)
description: A vibrant, tangy, and umami-forward Vietnamese dipping sauce that pairs perfectly with grilled meats, spring rolls, noodles, and salads. The balance of sweet, salty, sour, and spicy makes it a must-have condiment.
keywords: Nuoc Cham (Vietnamese Fish Sauce Dressing) recipe
instructions: Mince the garlic and ginger and finely chop the chillies.
In a small bowl, combine the minced garlic, ginger, and chopped chillies.
Add the fish sauce, rice vinegar, lime juice, sugar, and water.
Stir well until the sugar is fully dissolved.
Let sit for at least 5 mins to allow the flavours to meld.
Serve immediately or store in the fridge for up to a week.

name: Nut Butter Cups
description: Salty, snappy and loaded with nut butter. A twist on the classic choc treat, made ahead and ready whenever you need a sweet hit.
instructions: Blend everything except the chocolate and coconut oil until you get a smooth, sticky texture.

Add a spoonful of the mixture into each hole of a silicone mini cupcake tray. Press down until compact. Dollop a teaspoon of nut butter into the centre of each, then repeat with the remaining mixture until you have filled up each cup. Bang the tray on your work surface to help the nut butter settle into the base. Pop into the freezer for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, melt the dark chocolate and coconut oil in the microwave in 30-second bursts, or over a bain-marie, until smooth. Pour the chocolate into a jug.
Take the tray out of the freezer and pour a little melted chocolate over each cup to cover the nut butter. Tap the tray gently to even out the tops. Return to the freezer until set solid.
Once frozen, pop the nut butter cups out of the tray. Store them in the freezer, or keep in the fridge if you're eating them soon. These last for a week in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer.

name: Nut Roast Wellington
description: Genuinely the nicest plant-based roast accompaniment about. Nuts, sweet squash and umami-packed mushrooms all packed into crisp pastry. An absolute delight.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C/374°F.
Start by prepping your vegetables. Peel and dice your squash, dice your onion, dice your celery and grate your garlic. Roughly chop your mushrooms and finely chop your thyme and rosemary.
Pop your squash on a baking tray and drizzle it with olive oil, salt and pepper, then roast for 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, place your roughly chopped mushrooms in the food processor and pulse to a fine mince.
Heat some oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Tip in your onion and celery, then cook out for 5 minutes until soft.

Add your mushrooms to the pan and turn up the heat. Cook out for 5 minutes until they have released their liquid and started to become caramelised. Add your garlic to the pan along with your chopped herbs and cook out for a minute more. Set aside until later.
Place your nuts in a food processor and pulse until your nuts resemble chunky crumbs.
Pour the nuts in a dry pan and cook on a low heat for 5 minutes, or until they have turned slightly golden and smell lovely and fragrant.

Pop your roasted squash in a large bowl and break it up with a wooden spoon until you have a thick paste. Tip your onion and mushroom mixture, your chopped nuts, breadcrumbs and miso paste into the bowl along with a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Give it all a really good mix until all the ingredients are totally combined.
Melt your coconut oil in a microwave or small saucepan, then mix with your maple syrup.
Place a baking sheet in the oven to preheat.
Unroll your sheet of puff pastry and cut it into a square, saving your excess pastry for later.

Place your mixture in a thick log just off centre from the middle, leaving an inch on either end. Brush the edges with your coconut maple mixture, then fold the edges over the filling so that the two sides just overlap. Press the pastry with your fingers to seal the edge, then seal the two ends by pressing down with a fork.
Cut out decorative shapes from your excess pastry and place these on top of your roll.

Brush your wellington all over with your coconut maple liquid, then place on a pre-heated baking tray lined with parchment. Bake for 40 minutes, or until your wellington is shiny, crisp and golden brown. Serve with all the other Christmas trimmings.

name: Nutty Sesame & White Chocolate Chunk Cookies
description: Brown butter and tahini are the secret ingredients in these cookies. Learn how to perfectly brown your butter to get the most flavour into the cookie batter.
keywords: Nutty Sesame & White Chocolate Chunk Cookies
instructions: Add the butter to a saucepan over a medium heat, stir until it starts to foam and eventually turns brown, this will take around 3-4 mins. You know the butter has browned when you can smell a nutty aroma. Take off the heat and pour into a small bowl, leave to cool.
