In another bowl add all the dry ingredients together: flour, baking soda, salt and whisk to incorporate. Chop the white chocolate into small pieces.

In a bigger bowl, whisk egg, egg yolk, vanilla and both sugars together until thick and creamy. Drizzle in the tahini and whisk until it is incorporated. This will thicken the mixture slightly. Slowly pour the cooled butter into the mixture and whisk until everything has emulsified and there is no pool of melted butter floating on top.

Switching to a spatula, fold the dry ingredients along with the white chocolate chunks into the sugar mixture until there are no dry spots left. Cover with cling film and chill in the fridge overnight or a minimum of 2 hours.

Preheat the oven to 190°C and line a large baking tray with baking paper. Take the cookie dough out from the fridge and create balls of 2 tbsp worth of dough. Roll the balls into the black sesame seeds and place on the baking tray, making sure to space them out.

Once your oven is up to temperature, bake the cookies for 8-12 mins, until evenly golden - the middle will look a little undercooked and the edges should look crispy. Take them out and bang the tray down onto your counter - this will help deflate the cookies quickly and create a chewier middle. Let them cool down a little before tucking in. As they cool down, they’ll firm up.

name: Nutty Strawberry & Lime Cottage Cheese Pot
description: Creamy cottage cheese, juicy strawberries and a crunchy nut and seed topping. No cooking needed, ready in five and packed with protein - what more could you want for a meal prep breakfast?
keywords: Lime & Nut Cottage Cheese Pot recipe
instructions: Zest and juice the lime into a small bowl then stir through the cottage cheese until well combined. Spoon into the base of a jar or pot.

Hull and slice the strawberries, then layer them on top of the cottage cheese. Roughly chop the mixed nuts and pop in a separate container or airtight bag with the coconut flakes and mixed seeds ready to scatter over when you're ready to eat. (You can add them straight away, this just ensures they keep their crunch if you're prepping ahead).
Seal and refrigerate for up to 2 days.

name: Oat, Sour Cherry & White Chocolate Cookies
description: These buttery oat cookies are so moreish, they should come with a warning. The sweetness of the white chocolate with the tartness of the dried cherries is a match made in heaven.
keywords: Sour Cherry & White Choc Chip Oat Cookies
Sour Cherry & White Choc Chip Oat Cookies recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Line a baking tray with baking parchment. Break the white chocolate up into small 2-3cm chunks.
Add the butter and both sugars to a bowl and use an electric whisk to beat them together for 5-7 mins until pale and fluffy. Crack the egg in and beat until incorporated.

In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, cornflour, malt powder, ground cardamom, bicarbonate of soda and salt. Tip into the beaten butter and egg mix and stir to combine. Then stir in the oats, sour cherries and white chocolate.
Use your hands to portion the mixture into cookies – around 70g per cookie – and spread them out in a baking tray, making sure there’s room between each one.
Bake for 12-15 mins until golden. Leave them to cool for 10-15 mins before serving.

name: Oaty Crumble Topping
description: This handy crumble recipe will pull together any fruity or creamy dessert. Bake it in the oven over chopped fruit for a traditional crumble, or bake it in advance and sprinkle over ice cream or yoghurt. The possibilities are endless.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan and line a baking tray with baking paper. Ensure your butter is very cold. Slice the cold butter into cubes. Put all the ingredients into a bowl and rub together with your fingers to form breadcrumbs. Spread the mixture on the lined baking tray and put into the freezer for 10 mins (this will firm up the butter that you’ve softened with your hands).
Transfer to the oven and bake for 10–15 mins, then remove and turn the oven down to 170°C fan. Allow the crumble to cool completely before crushing up with your hands or a rolling pin.

name: Okra Pachadi Recipe
description: This South Indian dish is great as a side, either chilled or at room temperature. It always brings back childhood memories of eating sadya meals on banana leaves.
instructions: Wash and thoroughly dry the okra, then trim and slice it into 1cm chunks. Transfer to a bowl with a sprinkle of salt, then toss and set aside.
Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan until dark and aromatic. Transfer to a pestle and mortar or electric spice grinder with the green chilli. Grate in the coconut, then coarsely grind.
Heat the coconut oil in a frying pan and add the mustard seeds. Once they crackle, add the okra with a pinch of salt and the curry leaves. Stir-fry for 4-5 mins.
Add the turmeric and asafoetida and cook for 1 min. Add the cumin and coconut mixture and cook for 2-3 mins.
Remove the okra from the heat. Mix the yoghurt with water and add to the cooked okra – add a splash more water if needed. Stir well, then taste and season with salt, if needed.
Before serving, make the tarka. Heat the coconut oil in a small pan over a medium heat. Add the mustard seeds, curry leaves and dried chilli. Once they sizzle, pour it all over the pachadi and serve.

name: Old Fashioned
description: This is my favourite cocktail and I hope I did it justice. Enjoy
instructions: Add one teaspoon of soft brown sugar to your glass along with two dashes of Angostura bitters.
Muddle them together until it forms a paste at the bottom.
Cut a slice of the rind of an orange to use as garnish and another slice to rub around the rim for aromatics.
Place a large ice cube in the glass then add your double measure of whiskey.
Stir the drink for 1-2 mins, then add your orange garnish.
Stir for a further minute and a half then enjoy.

name: Olive & Almond Pesto Lentils With Halloumi
description: A fresh and tangy lentil bowl with plenty of caramelised halloumi.
keywords: Olive & Almond Pesto Lentils With Halloumi
Olive & Almond Pesto Lentils With Halloumi recipe
instructions: Cook the lentils in the stock according to instructions, then drain. Heat oven to 160°C and add the flaked almonds to a baking tray. Pop in the oven for 12-15 minutes until golden. Once cooled, add half of the almonds to a blender with the olives, olive oil, red wine vinegar, peeled garlic and half the rocket. Blitz smooth and season with salt and pepper.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat and dice the halloumi into 2cm pieces. Add to the pan (no need for oil!) and cook whilst flipping for about 10 minutes until golden on each side. Drain and slice the red peppers.
Mix most of the pesto through the lentils along with the remaining rocket, capers and the roasted red peppers. Top with halloumi and the rest of the pesto.

name: Olive & Herb Buttery Rice
description: Fresh, briny, and loaded with goodness — this buttery herb recie is a great base for so many meals.
instructions: Finely slice the garlic and chop the herbs. Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear.
Heat a medium-sized saucepan over medium heat and add the butter. Once melted, add the garlic and cook for 8 mins until caramelised.
Stir in the olives, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of sugar (if using). Cook for another minute.
Tip in the washed rice, then pour in the chicken stock (or water). Bring to a boil, then cover with a lid and reduce the heat to as low as possible.
Cook for 12 mins, then turn off the heat and let the rice sit for 15 mins.
Once ready, fluff the rice with a fork, mix through the chopped herbs, and season to taste with salt and black pepper. Serve immediately

name: Olive & Tuna Pie
description: We've filled this bronze pie crust with a puttanesca-inspired mixture of tuna and olives.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Tuna Ragú.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Add the Tuna Ragù to a bowl with the olives, lentils, tomato purée and water, stir together and transfer to a small ovenproof dish.
Top the filling with puff pastry and cut a hole into the middle to let the steam out. Brush with olive oil and bake for 20-25 mins until golden.

name: Olive Oil Leeks with Giant Couscous & Yoghurt Dressing
description: Leeks are one of my favourite vegetables – a soft, sweet allium that pairs brilliantly with lemon. Here I’m cooking sliced leeks in a generous measure of olive oil to soften and colour just a little, before adding preserved lemon and green olives.
keywords: olive oil leeks with giant couscous
instructions: Cook the couscous following pack instructions. Drain.
Slice the leeks into 4cm pieces and wash well to remove any dirt. Drain well.

Add the olive oil, the leeks and a big pinch of salt and pepper to a large frying pan. Cook over a medium heat, stirring to coat in the oil, until nicely coloured around 3 - 4 minutes. Turn the heat down to low, cover the pan and cook the leeks gently for 15-20 mins, stirring halfway through until they are very tender.

Meanwhile, finely chop the garlic, coriander stalks, green olives and preserved lemon. Once the leeks are tender, add your chopped ingredients (plus the coriander seeds) to the leek pan and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Blend the coriander leaves, lemon juice and yoghurt, adding salt and pepper to taste, until you have a smooth green sauce. Stir this into the cooked couscous and season to taste with salt and pepper.
To serve, spoon and spread the dressed couscous over plates or a platter and top with the leek mixture. Crumble the feta and sprinkle the chilli and sumac (if using) on top.

name: Omelette with Brothy Crushed Tomatoes & Rice
description: A comforting rice bowl inspired by omurice, with a sweet and salty miso broth. You’ll be making this on repeat.
keywords: Omelette with Brothy Crushed Tomatoes & Rice
Omelette with Brothy Crushed Tomatoes & Rice recipe
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl then add the soy sauce, sugar and mirin. Whisk together then set aside. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens, and set aside.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the tomato purée and spring onion whites and cook for 2-4 mins until the tomato purée has darkened and the spring onions have softened.

Add the can of plum tomatoes and use a potato masher to crush the tomatoes. Leave to cook for about 8-10 mins or until thickened. Pour in the dashi and leave to gently simmer whilst you finish the rest of the dish.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice and share between bowls.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a small non-stick frying pan set over medium heat. Once hot, add some of the egg mixture to the pan (if you’re cooking for 1, use all the mixture; if you’re cooking for 4, use ¼ of the mixture, etc.) and leave it to set for 15 secs before giving it a scramble. Once the egg starts to set, leave it alone until it’s cooked through then remove from the heat and serve on top of a portion of rice. Repeat this process so you have an omelette for every portion.
Before serving, stir the miso through the broth.
Ladle the broth over the rice, around the omelette, and drizzle over some chilli oil. Finish with a scattering of spring onion greens.

name: Omu Rice & Quick Pickled Cucumbers
description: This is the lazy version of the viral Japanese omu rice - soft omelette, punchy fried rice and quick pickled cucumbers for crunch. Still mega. Still impressive.
instructions: Halve the cucumber lengthways, then chop into chunky, bite-sized pieces. Tip into a colander with a good pinch of salt and leave to sit for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, peel and finely chop the carrot. Finely chop the courgette and thinly slice the onion. Peel and finely chop the garlic and ginger.
After 10 mins, transfer the salted cucumbers to a bowl. Add the garlic and rice vinegar, give everything a good mix and set aside to pickle.

Heat the toasted sesame oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the chopped carrot, courgette and onion. Fry for 5 mins, stirring regularly, until softened. Add the ginger, cooked rice and frozen peas. Cook for another 3-4 mins until hot, then season with the dark soy sauce. Scrape into a bowl and keep warm.

Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat together. Pour into the same pan and gently swirl for texture as they start to set. Cook for 2-3 mins until mostly set but still soft. Spoon the fried rice onto one half of the omelette, then carefully fold the other side over.
Serve the omu rice on plates with a generous spoonful of the pickled cucumbers and a drizzle of crispy chilli oil.

name: One Pan Chorizo Gnocchi
description: Chorizo & peppers really are a match made in heaven. This whole dish is also in one pan, so minimal washing up. Ideal.
instructions: Break your chorizo ring into small chunks and start to fry in a large pan. Chop your peppers into cubes and add them to the pan, stirring them and allowing them to fry in the chorizo fat.
Once the chorizo and peppers begin to cook, add your cherry tomatoes whole. Stir and continue to cook on a high heat. Slice your red chilli and garlic and add them to the pan.
In a separate bowl, cover your gnocchi with boiling water and allow it to soak for 10 minutes.

While the gnocchi is soaking, pour the red wine vinegar into the frying pan and stir it in with the mascarpone. You should now have a creamy sauce. Add a pinch of salt and pepper to taste. Roughly chop your basil and throw that in there too.
Drain your gnocchi and thoroughly mix it in to your sauce. Serve up with a sprinkling of parmesan and more fresh basil. Get stuck in, MOB! Enjoy!

name: One Pan Chorizo Kale Gnocchi
description: Spicy chorizo, pillowy gnocchi & a creamy broth all coming together in one glorious pan. A quick, comforting mid-week dinner, with barely any washing up.
instructions: Finely chop the onion, thinly slice the garlic.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large, deep ovenproof frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the chorizo and cook for 3–4 mins, stirring occasionally, until it’s crisp and the oil has turned a deep red.
Turn the heat down to medium and chuck in the onion, garlic and a pinch of salt. Cook for 6–8 mins until soft and translucent.
Add the gnocchi to the pan and toss it through all that lovely oil. Pour in the chicken stock, bring to the boil, then simmer for 3–4 mins until the gnocchi is just cooked.
Stir through the shredded kale and cream cheese, and cook for a further minute to wilt the kale and melt the cheese.
Finely grate over the parmesan, drizzle with a little more oil and crack over some black pepper to finish.

name: One Pan Crispy Prawn & Giant Couscous
description: Golden seared prawns on a bed of smoky, tomato-drenched couscous. It's got all the vibes of a proper paella with about a fraction of the faff.
keywords: Crispy Prawn & Pearl Couscous Paella recipe
instructions: Grate the tomatoes on a box grater. Finely mince the garlic and cut the red pepper into strips. Finely chop or pick the parsley leaves and set aside for garnish later.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat and add the olive oil. Season the prawns with salt, add to the pan and sear for 2 mins until golden. Flip and cook for another 30 seconds, then remove from the pan and set aside.

Add the red pepper strips to the pan and fry for 2-3 mins until softened. Add the grated tomatoes, garlic, chilli flakes and smoked paprika. Cook for 8-10 mins, stirring occasionally, until the oil starts to separate and the tomatoes have cooked right down.

Stir in the couscous, toasting for a minute. Pour in 800ml of the stock, cover with a lid and cook over a medium-high heat for 5 mins. Reduce the heat to low and cook for another 8 mins, or until the couscous is cooked through. If it starts to dry out, add more stock. Place the prawns on top to heat through, then turn off the heat and leave to rest for 2-3 mins.
Scatter over the parsley and serve with the lemon cut into wedges.

name: One Pan Pepper & Chorizo Orzo
description: Chorizo, red peppers and basil - coming together to create an absolute worldy of an orzo dish. Great for meal-prep.
instructions: Begin by finely slicing the garlic and red chilli. Dice the red peppers into small squares, halve the cherry tomatoes. Set aside.
Preheat a large, deep non-stick saucepan on medium high heat. Add the chorizo to the pan, cooking it until it is nice and crispy. Take out and set aside for later.

In the same pan, add the olive oil then the garlic and chilli, cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the diced red peppers and cherry tomatoes. Cook on medium heat until the tomatoes start to blister.
Once the tomatoes are blistered and bubbling, add the passata and water. Season with salt and pepper well, add the orzo and give everything a stir.
Bring to the boil, and then turn down to a medium heat. Allow it to simmer for 12 minutes, stirring regularly so the orzo doesn’t stick to the bottom of the pan.
After 12 minutes, the orzo should be al dente. If it needs a bit more time, give it a couple more minutes. Add a splash more water if needed. Once the orzo is cooked, stir in the crispy chorizo.
Remove from the heat, and serve with a handful of fresh basil leaves scattered on top.

name: One Pan Prawn & Tomato Rice
description: A juicy, low-effort one-pan wonder with sweet tomatoes, fluffy rice, and garlicky prawns. Big flavour, barely any chopping, and perfect for weeknights.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Peel and slice the garlic. Set a shallow casserole dish over a medium heat with the olive oil. Once hot, cook the garlic for about 1 min until softened but not coloured.

Tip in the frozen peppers with a pinch of salt and pepper and cook for 3 mins or until defrosted, tossing occasionally. Add the paprika and stir for 1 min. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook, stirring, for 3 mins to reduce the liquid a bit.
In a jug, dissolve the chicken stock pot in the boiling water.

Pour the rice into the dish, then add the hot stock and bay leaf. Bring to the boil, give everything a quick stir, taste and season, then cover and transfer to the oven for 20 mins, or until the water is nearly all absorbed.
Fold in the prawns and return to the oven, uncovered, for another 5 mins until the prawns are pink and cooked through.
Pick the dill and fold most of it through the rice. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Dish up the rice and prawns, then top with the remaining dill and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

name: One Pan Sausage Bolognese
description: Sausages are the perfect shortcut to getting saucy bolognese goodness in no time. Made all in one pan, this makes a rich comforting pasta perfect for weeknights when you need a little more indulgence.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large wide pan on medium heat and cook the vegetable base mix for 7 mins, until defrosted and softened. Peel and finely slice the garlic then add to the pan with the oregano and fry, stirring for another minute.

Squeeze the sausages out of their skins and into the pan, fry for 5 mins, breaking up with a wooden spoon, until they are starting to colour. Add the tomato pureé and cook off for another minute, then add in the spaghetti, passata, chicken stock and plenty of black pepper to the pan. Bring to a simmer stirring the spaghetti until it starts to bend.

Cover and simmer gently for 12-13 mins, stirring every couple of mins (this will prevent the spaghetti from sticking together), or until the pasta is cooked and the sauce has thickened. Add another few splashes of water if necessary to loosen.

Divide between bowls and top with grated parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil, if you fancy. Top Tip: One pot pastas are starchier than normal pastas and need to be served immediately as the pasta will continue to absorb the liquid as it sits. You can loosen with additional water.

name: One Pan Turmeric Salmon Orzotto
description: Golden salmon, crispy skin and creamy coconut orzo with a turmeric kick. It's a delish one-pan midweek dinner that kids will devour.
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsRemove the skin from the salmon fillets. Season both the fish and the skin with salt and pepper. Heat a third of the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Place the salmon in skinned-side up and the salmon skin and fry for 3–4 mins until golden. Transfer to a plate, golden side up (it won’t be cooked through yet). Keep cooking the skins until crispy, about 5 mins.
Peel and finely chop the garlic and ginger. Pick the coriander leaves and set aside for garnish, then finely chop the stalks.

Reduce the heat to medium-low. Wipe out the frying pan, then add the remaining olive oil to the pan. Chuck in the garlic, ginger, coriander stalks and orzo. Season with salt and pepper and fry for 2 mins, stirring. Add the turmeric and cook for 1 min more.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken stock, bring to the boil and cook, stirring every minute or so, for 10 mins.
Fold in the edamame and bring back to the boil. Nestle the salmon on top (keep the crispy skin aside),cover and cook for 4-5 mins until the salmon is just cooked through and the orzo is tender.

Serve up!Kids Plate:  Spoon out the orzo and flake the salmon into bite-sized pieces.Parents Plate: Fold most of the coriander leaves through the orzo. Dish up with the salmon, then crumble over the crispy skin and scatter with the remaining coriander leaves.

name: One Pot Beef Shin Lasagne
description: Sticky, pull-apart beef shin is a great way to fill a lasagne. Our zero-cook white sauce is also 10/10. Give this one a go MOB.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 170°C/338°F.
Finely chop the onion, carrot, celery and garlic cloves. Set aside.
Season the beef shin pieces generously with salt and black pepper.
Pour a good glug of oil into a shallow ovenproof casserole dish/frying pan, fry the beef over a high heat in batches until browned on all sides. Set aside on a plate.
Turn down the heat, add the pancetta and fry until crisp. Add the onion, carrot, celery and garlic. Cook until softened.

Add the bay leaves, tinned plum tomatoes and red wine. Add the beef and all its juices back into the pan. Season generously, place the lid/tin foil on top and place in the oven for 3 hours. You want the meat to be falling apart and to have a thick tomato sauce.
Once cooked, stir through the marmite - this will dial up the meaty flavour. Use two forks to shred the meat. Season to taste and tip the sauce into a large bowl. Don’t clean the pan.
Mix the ricotta and mascarpone with the milk so that it becomes a spreadable consistency. Grate in a good amount of nutmeg and season with salt and pepper.

Time to assemble the lasagne. Spoon a small amount of meat into the bottom of the dish, top with a layer of lasagne sheets, you will need to break one sheet per layer, followed by a decent layer of meat sauce. Dot over 1/4 of the ricotta mix, spread and grate over loads of Parmesan.
Repeat for 3 more layers until everything has gone, remember to save a good amount of ricotta mix for the top and grate over even more Parmesan.
Bake in the oven for 40 minutes at 180°C, until a cutlery knife inserts easily. Let it stand for 5 minutes before tucking in. Serve with salad.

name: One Pot Cheesy Sausage & Ravioli Bake
description: Ravioli baked in a rich sausagey tomato sauce and topped with melty mozzarella-cheddar cheese. The easiest pasta bake going.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Set a shallow oven-proof pan over a medium-high heat with the olive oil. Squeeze the sausage meat out of the skins and break into small pieces over the pan. Cook for 5 mins, stirring  until browned.

Pick the thyme leaves and add to the pan. Peel and finely chop the garlic.  Take the pan off the heat and stir in the garlic. Pour in the tomato pasta sauce then tip in the ravioli and toss everything together until well coated.
Nestle in the frozen spinach cubes, no need to defrost!
Scatter over the grated mozzarella and cheddar, then bake in the oven for 20 mins until golden and bubbling.

name: One Pot Chicken Cider Pie
description: Adding cider to the filling really cuts through the richness, giving it this lovely tangy taste. A great chicken pie.
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C/428°F.
Dice up your chicken thighs into chunks, season with salt and pepper. Brown them off in an ovenproof frying pan that you will be cooking your pie in. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

Finely slice the leeks and cut the mushrooms into quarters. Melt a knob of butter in the pan. Add the leeks and cook for 3 minutes until wilted. Whack in the mushrooms with a pinch of salt and fry until soft. Sprinkle in the flour.
Give everything a good mix. Cook for a minute. Pour in the cider. Bubble away for a minute.
Add the cream and mustard. Stir the sauce until combined. Add the chicken again, with 3/4 of the parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from the heat.
Melt the second knob of butter and use it to brush over 6 filo sheets. Crumple the pastry with your hands and place on top of the pie filling. Once the whole filling is covered transfer to the oven.
Cook for 20 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown.
Sprinkle over the remaining parsley and serve with mustard.

name: One Pot Creamy Chicken & Tomato Orzo
description: The easiest, creamiest dish about. It's a perfect midweek treat.
instructions: Start by frying your chicken thighs on a medium heat. Fry them until they're cooked through and brown on each side. Set aside for later.

Thinly slice the chilli and garlic. Add some more olive oil into the now empty pan and add the rosemary, chilli, and tomatoes. Give everything a good stir to allow for the tomatoes to soften slightly.

Orzo time! Add your orzo to the pan followed by your chicken stock, passata and single cream. Keep stirring until the orzo has cooked through and the pasta is creamy, adding a splash of water if needed. Add salt and pepper. Tear up your basil, add stir through.
Now it’s ready to serve - Slice up your chicken thighs. Share the orzo between bowls and top with chicken. Grate some Parmesan over the top, and tuck in.

name: One Pot Tomatoey Couscous
description: Tomatoes, on tomatoes, on tomatoes...this one-pot couscous is tangy, nutty and loaded with savoury depth. A real umami bomb that's super speedy.
instructions: Finely mince the sundried tomatoes. Drain the lentils, if needed.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the sun-dried tomato oil, nuts and sunflower seeds. Cook, stirring often, for 3–5 mins until golden and toasted. Stir in the caraway seeds and cook for another 30 seconds, then tip the mixture into a bowl and set aside to cool.
Return the empty pan to a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Tip in the giant couscous and cook, stirring regularly, for 3–5 mins until lightly golden.

Add the lentils, minced sundried tomatoes and tomato purée. Stir to coat everything evenly, then pour in the water. Season with salt and pepper and bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10–15 mins (or follow the couscous packet instructions), stirring occasionally, until cooked through.

Meanwhile, chop the fresh tomatoes into bite-sized chunks. Tip into a bowl with the balsamic vinegar and a good pinch of salt. Mix well and set aside to macerate. Finely slice the chives and stir them through the tomato salad just before serving.
Once the couscous is cooked, taste and adjust the seasoning.
Spoon the couscous onto plates, top with the juicy tomato salad, a big dollop of Greek yoghurt and a generous spoonful of the crunchy spiced nut drizzle and chopped chives.

name: One Tray Chicken & Fondant Potatoes
description: Golden, crispy-skinned chicken baked over soft, stock-soaked potatoes with lemon, rosemary and sweet onion, all in one tray so you can have a delicious hands off dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Place skin-side down in a deep, heavy-bottomed casserole dish or ovenproof pan. Set over a medium heat and cook for around 10 mins until the skin is golden and crisp, then flip and cook for another 2 mins.

Meanwhile, halve the potatoes. Working in batches, nestle as many potatoes as you can (cut-side down) into the space around the chicken to brown in the chicken fat for 2 mins. Remove and repeat with the rest. Peel the onion and cut into 6 wedges, also browning in the pan as the chicken cooks.
Smash the garlic cloves. Strip the rosemary leaves from their stalks and roughly chop.

Push the chicken to one side of the pan, Shuffle the potatoes to cover the bottom of the potatoes, scatter over the garlic and rosemary, and season everything with salt and black pepper, then place the chicken on top (skin side up). Cut the lemon in half and tuck it into the pan. Pour over the chicken stock.
Transfer the pan to the oven and roast for 30 mins, until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.
Lift the chicken out onto a plate to rest. Put the pan back on a high heat and simmer to reduce the stock slightly.
Shave the parmesan over a bowl of rocket and toss with a little oil. Spoon everything into bowls and pour over any remaining pan juices and serve with the salad. .

name: One Tray Pesto & Prosciutto Wrapped Cod
description: Juicy cod fillets wrapped in crispy prosciutto, baked over chickpeas, sweet tomatoes and peppers all finished with a dollop of pesto. Simple but lush.
keywords: one-tray cod with pesto and crispy parma ham
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C. Cut the cod into 4 equal pieces. Season with salt and black pepper, then spread the tops with pesto. Wrap each piece in a slice of prosciutto .

Drain the chickpeas and add them to a large roasting tray along with the frozen peppers and cherry tomatoes. Toss everything together gently, and season with salt and pepper then place the cod on top.
Drizzle over the olive oil, then bake for 10-12 mins, or until the cod is opaque and cooked through.
Carefully lift the cod and tomatoes out of the tray. Spoon the chickpeas and veg onto plates, top with the cod and finish with an extra drizzle of pesto, if you fancy.

name: One Tray Roast Chicken Noodles
description: Give your roast chicken an asian twist with this noodle salad. The resting juices collect in the tray, get hit with ginger, garlic and sesame, and coat the noodles in something genuinely brilliant. Bonus - it makes unreal leftovers.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Rub the chicken all over with the neutral oil and season generously with sea salt. Place in a roasting tray and roast for 45 mins. Remove the chicken from the oven, sprinkle with half the sesame seeds and slide back in for a final 10 mins, until the skin is deep golden and the juices run clear.

Once your chicken is ready and out of the oven, leave it to rest in the tray for at least 20 mins. The resting juices will collect in the tray and form the base of the noodle dressing so don't skip this.
While the chicken rests, cut the cucumber into matchsticks and cook the noodles according to the packet instructions. Drain well and set aside.

Lift the chicken from the tray and shred the meat. Very finely grate the garlic and ginger into the resting juices and stir to combine, then place the tray back in the oven for 5 mins to warm through. Remove and stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, rice wine vinegar and chilli oil. Add the drained noodles and toss until well coated. Taste and adjust with more sesame oil, soy or chilli oil if you want.
Divide between bowls, top with the shredded chicken, the remaining sesame seeds and cucumber matchsticks and serve immediately. You can eat at room temp or store away to eat cold for lunches.

name: One-Pan Cheesy Beef & Broccoli
description: Easy, satisfying, and nutritious. For the days you don't feel like cooking, it doesn't get easier than this one pan wonder. Bonus points for only washing one pan at the end!
keywords: one pan cheesy beef broccoli recipe
instructions: Cook the mixed rice and grains following pack instructions and set aside. Wash the broccoli stalk and cut into bite-sized pieces. Thinly slice the beef. Grate the cheese.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the cooked rice to the middle of the pan and put the chopped broccoli stalks around the rice in a circle. Pan fry for 3 mins, without stirring.
Add the beef to the pan around the rice, with the broccoli. Let that sear for 3 mins on medium heat. Add the soy sauce, chilli oil and sesame oil to the rice in the centre of the pan.

When the beef is 80% cooked, mix everything in the pan together. Top with the coriander and cheddar cheese. Continue to cook for 2 mins until the cheese is melted and the beef is cooked to the desired tenderness.
Meanwhile, fry the eggs (if using) sunny side up on a medium heat for 2-3 mins depending on how runny you like them.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the eggs and any leftover coriander leaves.

name: One-Pan Courgette & Pesto Lasagne
description: This lasagne is perfect for when courgettes are in season. Great for something a little lighter and quicker.
instructions: Finely slice the onions and garlic.

Heat a large cast iron skillet with a good drizzle of olive oil. Add the onions and cook for 4-5 mins with a sprinkle of salt. Meanwhile, use a speed peeler to slice the courgette into ribbons. When you can’t slice into them anymore, chop the remaining middle into bite sized pieces.
Once the onions have softened and are starting to caramelise, add the garlic, tomato purée and chilli flakes if using.
Add the courgettes and season again generously with salt and pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Cook the courgettes for 6-8 mins until wilted but still a vibrant green, stirring often.
Boil the kettle and measure out 500ml of boiling water into a heatproof bowl. Add the stock cube and stir to dissolve. Drain the chickpeas.

Pour the chopped tomatoes, chickpeas and boiling stock into the pot and stir. Break the lasagne sheets into roughly three pieces each and push them down into the pan as best you can so that they are submerged.
Turn the heat down to a low simmer and pop the lid on. Cook for 15 mins or until the pasta is cooked through, stirring at least twice to make sure the bottom doesn't stick.
Add the spinach and 3 tbsp of pesto and stir to combine. Add a few dollops of vegan cream cheese over the top and a drizzle of olive oil and finish with a few basil leaves, if using.

name: One-Pan Sausage and Roasted Pepper Lasagne
description: An easy, breezy one-pan recipe that the whole family is going to love. If you've never made a ragù from sausages before, you've never lived.
keywords: One-Pan Sausage and Roasted Pepper Lasagne
One-Pan Sausage and Roasted Pepper Lasagne recipe
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C.
Blitz the drained roasted peppers with water until smooth.

Finely chop the onion, garlic and rosemary. Squeeze the sausages out of their casings into a pan set over a medium heat. Using the back of a spoon, crumble the sausage into pieces and cook until golden. Using a slotted spoon, remove the sausages and add in a glug of oil along with the onion and garlic and chilli flakes, if using. Add a pinch of salt and cook that out for 8 mins. Add the fennel seeds and rosemary and cook for two more minutes.
Tip in the blitzed peppers along with the tinned tomatoes. Add the sausages back in, along with a handful of basil leaves. Season with salt and pepper, then bring to a simmer.
Blanche the fresh lasagne sheets for 1 minute in boiling water, then drain.

Nestle the lasagne sheets into the ragù, then dot with mascarpone before tearing over the mozzarella and grating over the Parmesan. Slide into the oven and cook for 35-40 mins or until bubbling and golden.
Remove from the oven and allow to rest for 5 mins before serving.

name: One-Pot Bacon & Leek Gnocchi
description: A quick and easy midweek dinner with pillowy gnocchi and a delicious creamy sauce. It’s high in protein and uses light cream cheese, making it healthier than it looks.
instructions: Slice the leek in half lengthways then wash it and thinly slice it into half-moons. Dice the red onion and bacon. Crush the garlic cloves. Set aside.

Pour a small dash of olive oil into a large lidded frying pan and use a sheet of kitchen roll to spread the oil around. Get the diced bacon into the cold pan, then set it over a low-medium heat. When the fat starts to run out, increase the heat to high and cook for a few minutes on each side until crispy. Transfer the bacon to a bowl and set aside.
Return the pan to a medium heat and add another dash of olive oil. Add the onion, garlic, leek and a pinch of salt and cook for around 8 mins, until softened.
Add ¾ of the crispy bacon pieces back into the pan (keeping the rest for the topping). Stir in the mustard, mixed herbs and some black pepper. Stir in the stock then bring to the boil.
Stir the gnocchi through the sauce then reduce the heat to low-medium so the sauce is just simmering. Pop the lid on and leave for 2-3 mins until the gnocchi is cooked through.
Stir through the cream cheese and season with salt and pepper to taste.
To serve, divide the creamy gnocchi into bowls. Top with the remaining bacon bits and some grated Parmesan, if you like.

name: One-Pot Baked Orzo With Artichokes & Chickpeas
description: I love a one pot number, especially when it’s got all of the elements to make a full meal in one. All of the flavour from the artichokes, pesto and shallots get absorbed by the orzo to make this really delicious dish.
keywords: One-Pot Baked Orzo With Artichokes & Chickpeas
One-Pot Baked Orzo With Artichokes & Chickpeas recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Finely chop the shallot and mince the garlic.

Add the shallot, garlic, orzo, artichokes with some artichoke oil, drained chickpeas, spinach, pesto and chilli flakes if using to a large casserole dish with a lid. (If you don’t have one with a lid, you can cover it tightly with silver foil).
Add boiled water and season with plenty of salt and pepper, then stir well to combine.
Cover with the lid (or foil) and bake for 20 mins. Remove the dish from the oven and stir well. Return to the oven for 5 mins with the lid off.
While the orzo is baking, toast the pine nuts on the lower shelf for 4 mins.
To finish, zest the lemon and squeeze the lemon juice over the orzo. Add the vegan cheese, if using, and finish with the pine nuts and fresh basil.

name: One-Pot Chicken & Bean Cacciatore
description: A proper one-pot full-course meal . The rosemary, olives and red wine are what gives the chicken its characteristic cacciatore flavour.
instructions: Get your largest high-sided frying pan or casserole over a high heat. Drizzle in a good glug of olive oil. Season the chicken pieces generously with salt and black pepper then place skin-side down into the pan. Fry for 5–6 mins, turning occasionally, until the skin is evenly golden. You may need to do this in two batches.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the onions, peppers and garlic. Once the chicken is nicely browned, set aside on a plate. Reduce the heat to medium and scrape the onions and peppers into the pan. Add a pinch of salt then fry, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes until soft.

Scrape in the garlic, cook for 1 minute more then add the chilli flakes and rosemary. Stir together then spoon in the tomato purée. Give everything a good mix then pour in the red wine. Leave to bubble away until reduced by half, then tip in the tins of plum tomatoes. Bring thesauce to the boil.

Drain the beans and add to the pan along with the olives. Season well with salt and black pepper then nestle the chicken pieces in. Put on a lid and leave to simmer away for 20 minutes. Remove the lid and cook for a further 10 mins until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has reduced slightly. Season with salt, black pepper and a splash of balsamic vinegar.
Roughly chop the parsley and scatter over the top. Serve at the table for people to help themselves. We like to eat this with a crusty ciabatta.

name: One-Pot Chicken & Leek Pie
description: A lovely and comforting British pie made in one pan and served with grilled tenderstem.  Easy, delicious and there's barely any washing up to do.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Remove the puff pastry sheet from the fridge and unroll it. Choose an oven-safe frying pan, and cut the puff pastry about 1cm bigger than the circumference – if the pastry isn’t large enough, use a rolling pin to make it larger. Place the cut-out pastry onto a tray, cover and place it in the fridge.

Trim and thinly slice the leeks and garlic. Roughly chop the parsley, and zest the lemon. Slice the chicken into 3cm chunks. Place the leeks into a colander and give them a rinse. Place the frying pan with a drizzle of oil over a medium heat, add the leeks in with a generous pinch of salt, cook until softened and starting to brown.

Add the chicken and garlic in with the leeks, fry until the chicken is partially cooked, 4-5 mins. Stir in the flour and cook for another 2-3 mins. Slowly add the stock, a little at a time, stirring constantly until fully incorporated and smooth, then simmer for around 10 mins until thickened. Remove from the heat and stir in the yoghurt, parsley and the lemon zest. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Whisk the egg. Using a pastry brush, brush the filling up the sides of the frying pan – this will help the pastry to stick to the pan. Place the pastry on top of the pie and press the sides into the pan. Clean your brush and paint the pastry with the whisked egg, then cut a cross in the middle so that the steam can escape during baking. Bake for 25-30 mins, until golden brown.
Meanwhile, place your tenderstem onto a large baking tray, drizzle with oil and season generously with salt.

Once the pie is cooked, remove it from the oven. Be careful, it’ll be super hot at this stage. Turn your grill to high, and grill the broccoli until cooked through and charred, around 5 mins. Season the charred broccoli with lemon juice.
Serve the pie onto your plates with the broccoli.

name: One-Pot Chipotle Pasta With Smoky Seedy Topping
description: This smoky pasta is a complete meal that comes together in one pot and in just 30 minutes. It’s packed full of flavour from the chipotle and protein and fibre from the chickpeas. A smokey seedy topping and plenty of lime finish the dish off.
keywords: One Pot Chipotle Pasta With Smoky Seedy Topping
One Pot Chipotle Pasta With Smoky Seedy Topping recipe
instructions: Mince the garlic.

Drizzle a splash of olive oil into a pot or pan for which you have a lid for. Add the garlic, half of the smoked paprika, tomato purée and chipotle paste. Cook on a medium-low heat for 3 mins, stirring often to ensure it doesn't burn.
Add the chopped tomatoes and until thickened, 8-10 mins. Then add the water to the pot along with the pasta and stir well.

Add the water to the pot along with the pasta and stir well. Bring to a simmer on medium heat, cover with the lid and cook for 15-18 mins, stirring and often to make sure the bottom doesn't catch or burn. Add a splash more water, if needed.
Drain the chickpeas and finely chop the jalapeños.

Just before it’s finished cooking, add the spinach and chickpeas, stir and pop the lid back on for 2-4 mins to wilt the spinach and soften the chickpeas. Test the pasta to make sure it’s cooked through to your liking. If it needs more time, add a splash of water and cook for a few minutes longer.

To make the seedy topping, heat a glug of olive oil in a small frying pan over medium heat. Add the seeds and cook, stirring often, for 3-5 mins until toasted and fragrant. Remove from the heat and add the other half of the smoked paprika and a pinch of salt.

Add your seedy oil to your pasta along with your sliced jalapeños and a splash of the pickled jalapeno juice.Serve the pasta with a good spoonful of vegan sour cream or yoghurt, some lime juice and chopped coriander then taste the pasta for seasoning. Finish with the smoky seeds and top with more sliced jalapenos for extra spice if you fancy.

name: One-Pot Courgette, Lemon & Rocket Rigatoni
description: Who doesn't love a one pot pasta recipe? Courgettes cooked low and slow until they melt into a silky, lemony sauce that clings to every piece of rigatoni. Finished with peppery rocket and plenty of Parmesan, it's fresh, comforting and perfect for summer.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide, high-sided frying pan or sauté pan over a low heat. Finely dice the onion and add it to the pan. Cook gently for around 8 mins, stirring occasionally, until completely soft and sweet.

Finely slice the garlic and stir it into the onion. Dice the courgettes into small cubes, then add them to the pan with a generous pinch of salt and stir to coat. Increase the heat to medium, cover with a lid and cook for 8-10 mins, stirring once or twice, until the courgettes are soft and lightly caramelised.
Using a potato masher, roughly mash about half of the courgettes in the pan to help create the sauce.

Add the pasta and pour over the boiling water (straight from the kettle). Increase heat to high. Ensure it is boiling vigorously. Cover and cook the pasta according to packet instructions. Check the pasta occasionally to ensure it is not sticking, adding more water if needed. Cook until the pasta is cooked and a light courgette sauce remains at the bottom of the pan.

Finely grate the Parmesan (or a vegetarian hard cheese, if you'd like to keep it veggie). Halve the lemon and squeeze the juice of one half into the pasta. Add a generous grinding of black pepper and most of the Parmesan, reserving a little for serving. Toss everything together until glossy and coated.
Place the rocket in a bowl, squeeze over the juice from the remaining half of the lemon, add a drizzle of the extra virgin olive oil and toss to coat.
Divide the pasta between bowls, top with the dressed rocket and finish with the remaining Parmesan.

name: One-Pot Crispy Broccoli Rice & Sweet Soy Cod
description: Fluffy rice, tender cod and crispy broccoli all cooked in one pot with a sticky, sweet soy glaze. This healthy weeknight supper seriously hits the spot.
instructions: Add the honey, oyster sauce and dark soy sauce to a bowl. Stir together, then add the cod fillets and mix to coat evenly. Set aside.
Wash the rice under cold water until it runs clear.

Finely grate the garlic. Trim and separate the broccoli stems from the florets — cut the florets into 2–3cm chunks, and thinly slice the stems. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites from the greens. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems. Place the leaves into a bowl of ice-cold water to keep them fresh.

Place a large frying pan with a lid over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the sesame oil and broccoli stems. Cook for 4–6 mins until softened. Add the spring onion whites, coriander stems and garlic, then stir until fragrant.
Tip in the washed rice and pour in the water. Season with salt. Let it come to the boil, then cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low and leave to steam for 12 mins.
After 12 mins, add the broccoli florets and cod fillets on top of the rice. Replace the lid and cook for another 10 mins on low.

Heat the grill to high. When the fish is done steaming, remove the lid and transfer the pan under the grill for 3–4 mins until the fish has started to colour and is cooked through (if your fish is thicker, it may need a little longer).
Fluff the rice with a fork with a squeeze of lime and spoon onto plates. Top with the grilled cod, then finish with sesame seeds, spring onion greens and coriander leaves.

name: One-Pot Curried Coconut & Peanut Chicken Rice
description: A fuss-free, one-pot wonder full of flavour! It’s simple and balanced, but also jam-packed with flavour. Plus it requires minimal washing up, making it perfect for a weeknight dinner.
instructions: Slice the onion into chunks and the peppers into strips. Add a splash of olive oil to a large saucepan set over a medium heat (or a wok with a lid), then add the onion and peppers and cook until softened.

Crush the garlic, finely chop half of the chilli (or more/less, depending on how spicy you want it!), leaving the other half for topping later, and add to the pan. Dice up the chicken into bite-sized chunks, increase the heat and and stir the chicken through the saucepan, season with salt and pepper. Cook for around 5 mins until slightly browned. Meanwhile, rinse the uncooked rice.

Add the curry powder, peanut butter, honey, soy sauce, lime juice, stock and rice. Stir and bring to the boil. Cover and reduce the heat to low, leave to cook for 10 mins. After 10 mins pour in the coconut milk, re-cover and cook for a further 12 mins. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 5-10 mins to steam. This step is essential for fluffy rice!
While it’s cooking, crush up the nuts, slice the chilli and spring onion. To serve, divide the rice between bowls and top with the nuts, chillies and spring onion.

name: One-Pot Fish Biryani
description: Learn to make this classic Indian dish at home. It's gently spiced with perfectly cooked cod, served with a cucumber yoghurt.
instructions: Stir all the spices together in a small bowl and set aside.

Peel and thinly slice the onions. Grate the garlic into a mixing bowl and add ½ the spice mix, the juice of the lime and a glug of olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper and give it a good mix. Toss the fish through this mixture and set aside in the fridge to marinate.
Wash the rice until the water runs clear.

Set a frying pan with high sides over a medium heat with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, for 7-10 mins until golden brown. Transfer the onions to a plate.

Turn the heat down to medium and add another drizzle of olive oil. Add the curry leaves and cook until they splutter then stir in the remaining spice mix, rice and ½ the browned onion. Cook for a couple of seconds then pour in the stock. Bring to the boil then place a lid on, turn the heat down to low and let the rice cook undisturbed for 12 mins.

After 12 mins, scatter the peas over the rice and top with the fish. Place the lid back on and leave it on a low heat for 10 mins to finish cooking. Don’t remove the lid until finished. Heat the grill to high.

Meanwhile, make the yoghurt. Coarsely grate the cucumber and squeeze out as much water out as possible. Get the yoghurt in a bowl then stir through the grated cucumber and garam masala. Taste and season with salt.
When the fish cooking time is up, remove the lid and pop the pan under the grill for 3-4 mins until the fish has started to colour and is fully cooked through.
Fluff the rice using a fork and spoon into bowls. Top with the fish, a scattering of the remaining browned onions and a dollop of cucumber yoghurt. Finish with some coriander.

name: One-Pot Miso Butter Cod & Rice
description: Tender cod with caramelised miso butter, umami mushroom rice and a fresh spring onion slaw. A stress-free fish dinner that doesn't skimp on flavour. And just one pot to wash up? Win.
keywords: One-Pot Miso Butter Cod & Rice recipe
instructions: Make sure your butter is at room temperature. Prep your ingredients: Wash the rice until the water runs clear, then place into a bowl, cover with water and leave to soak. Season the cod with salt and pepper then place onto kitchen paper. Finely slice or tear the mushrooms into 1cm chunks. Stir the softened butter, miso and mirin together in a bowl and set aside.

Place a frying pan (with a lid) onto medium-high heat with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the mushrooms and cook for 10-15 mins until browned, stirring only a couple of times. Transfer the mushrooms to a plate. Don’t wash the pan.

Drain the rice then tip it into the empty frying pan. Set over a high heat and pour over the stock. Bring the mixture to the boil then place the lid on and turn the heat down to low. Leave to cook for 12 mins.
When the rice cooking time is up, pat the cod dry and place the fillets on top of the rice. Spread the miso butter onto the fish then cover with a lid and cook for another 10 mins.
Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Trim and cut the spring onions into thirds then thinly slice lengthwise and place into a bowl of ice water until curly.

When the fish cooking time is up, remove the lid and scatter the crispy mushrooms onto the rice. Slide the pan under the grill for 3-4 mins until the miso butter has started to colour and the fish is fully cooked through.
Drain the spring onions and toss with the sesame seeds and oil in a small bowl. Fluff the rice using a fork and spoon into bowls. Top with the fish and spring onion slaw.

name: One-Pot Mushroom Lasagne
description: This is a bit of a cheats lasagne, using broken lasagne sheets instead of layering, and is all done in one pot. Low on effort but big on flavour.
instructions: Use a tissue or kitchen towel to gently remove the dirt from the mushrooms.

Finely chop the onion and mushrooms. You can also use a food processor to pulse in batches, but roughly chop them to similar sizes first. Take care not to over process, so that the mushrooms and onions don’t turn into a pulp.
Finely chop or grate the garlic. Roughly chop the sun dried tomatoes. Rinse the lentils.
Heat a glug of oil in a large pan set over a medium heat and add the onions. Cook for 5 mins until softened then add the garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and sun-dried tomatoes. Season well with salt and pepper, and sauté until the liquid has evaporated and the mushrooms start to brown and caramelise - about 8- 10 mins.
Meanwhile, make the stock. Add the boiling water to the stock cubes stirring until dissolved. Preheat the oven to 190C.

Once the mushrooms have started to brown, add the harissa if using, and the tomato puree and plum tomatoes, crushing them into the pan with the back of a fork. Add the lentils, ¾ of the stock, season well with salt and pepper, and stir. Simmer on medium-high for 10 mins with the lid slightly off, to allow some steam out. Stir the pot occasionally.
After 10 mins, add the rest of the stock and stir well. Break up the lasagne sheets into large pieces and add them to the pot, pushing them down so they're submerged.
Cover with the lid and bake in the oven for 30 mins.

Remove the pot from the oven and give everything a good stir. 
Check that the pasta and lentils have cooked through. The lentils should have a firm bite but not taste powdery or tough. (If they need a little more time, add a splash of water and put the pot back into the oven, for 5-10 more minutes.)
Sprinkle the cheese over the top and close the lid again. Return to the oven for 10 minutes so that the cheese can melt.
Then, remove the lid and place under the grill for a few minutes to crisp up the top, keeping a close eye to prevent it burning.
Let the lasagne rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.

name: One-Pot Rice & Cod with Garlicky Tahini Sauce
description: This warming, gently spiced one-pot rice is the answer to your midweek meal dilemmas. It’s full of goodness, so easy to make and absolutely delicious.
keywords: One-Pot Rice & Cod with Garlicky Tahini Sauce
One-Pot Rice & Cod with Garlicky Tahini Sauce recipe
instructions: Wash the rice until the water runs clear.
Finely grate the garlic into a bowl. Add the 7-spice and a drizzle of olive oil, season with salt and pepper and mix to combine. Toss the fish fillets through the mix then set aside.

Melt the butter in a frying pan with high sides, set over a medium heat. Stir the cardamom pods, rice and chickpeas through the melted butter, then pour in the water. Let the mixture come to a boil then cover with a lid, turn the heat down to low and cook for 12 mins.

Halfway through the rice cooking time, place the cod fillets on top of the rice, pop the lid back on and leave to cook for the remainder of the time. When the time is up, remove the pan from the heat and leave covered for another 10 mins for the rice and fish to finish cooking. (If the fish hasn’t fully cooked after this time, place the dish under the grill for a couple of minutes, until fully cooked.)
Meanwhile, prep the salad. Peel and thinly slice the onion then add to a bowl with the sumac. Toss together then set aside. Drain the artichokes and pick the parsley leaves then set aside.
For the tahini sauce, grate the garlic into a bowl and squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Stir the tahini through. Season to taste with salt and sugar. Set aside.
Before serving, toss the artichokes and parsley leaves into the sumac onions along with an extra drizzle of olive oil. Season to taste with salt and some lemon juice.
To serve, fluff the rice and divide between bowls. Top with the fish, salad and a drizzle of tahini sauce.

name: One-Pot Squash, Mascarpone & Greens Lasagne
description: Squash season has arrived. This cheat’s butternut squash and mascarpone lasagne is everything we love about autumn. It’s cosy, cheesy and oozy. And there’s only one pot to wash up.
instructions: Peel and finely dice your onion. Finely slice your sage leaves too, as well as your garlic.

Heat a large shallow casserole dish over a medium heat. Add 2 tbsp olive oil, then get the onion and sage into the pan. Cook for about 15-20 mins, until they have softened and just taken on a bit of colour.
Meanwhile, peel your squash and chop it into 2cm chunks, discarding the seeds.

Add the garlic and chilli flakes to the pan with the onion and sage and cook for another 2 mins. Add the diced squash and pour in the vegetable stock. Bring to a boil then reduce to a simmer. Pop a lid on the pan, and simmer it for 15-20 mins, or until the squash is tender.
Heat your oven to 200°C fan.

Mash about ⅓ of the squash with a potato masher (this will give the mixture a nice texture) and give everything a good mix. Season with salt to taste, then tear up your cavolo nero leaves and add them in. Tear your lasagne sheets in half, and nestle each into the dish, until you have a tangle of squash, greens and pasta.

Spoon your mascarpone in blobs over the surface, then grate over your parmesan. Tear up your mozzarella, and dot this around the surface too. Sprinkle over your breadcrumbs, then drizzle over a little olive oil. Bake your lasagne in the oven for 25 mins.
Spoon it into bowls, and serve it up.

name: One-Pot Thai Green Chicken Curry
description: The king of thai curries. This zingy and addictive thai green chicken curry is the perfect one pot to meal prep for the week.
instructions: Slice the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces. Trim the baby corn and mange tout. Finely slice the red chilli. Pick some coriander leaves for garnish and cut the lime into wedges.
Set a large saucepan over a medium heat. Pour in half the coconut milk and cook for 5 mins until the fat starts to split and it smells toasty.
Add the Thai Green Curry Paste and stir for another 5 mins until darker and super fragrant. Tip in the chicken and cook for 3–4 mins until just sealed.
Sprinkle in the sugar and let it bubble for 2 mins. Pour in half the fish sauce and scrape up any sticky bits.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and the chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15 mins until slightly thickened and the chicken’s cooked through.
Chuck in the baby corn and mange tout for the final 2 mins. Stir through most of the coriander and the remaining fish sauce. Taste and season.
Serve over cooked rice and top with fresh chilli, crispy shallots, coriander leaves and a wedge of lime.

name: One-Pot Tomato Orzo
description: Here's an incredibly simple vegan orzo dish that's loaded with rich, beautiful tomatoes. It's an absolute winner.
instructions: Finely slice your garlic. Dice up your red chilli and finely chop your basil. Quarter your large tomatoes.
Heat a little glug of olive oil in a frying pan. Add your sliced garlic and red chilli and gently fry for a couple of mins until fragrant.
Tip your cherry tomatoes into the pan along with your quartered tomatoes. Cook for 10 mins, smooshing with the back of your spoon to break down the tomatoes.
Add your orzo and your vegetable stock. Give it a good stir, then simmer for 8 mins.
Season with salt and pepper, then add your basil and stir to combine.
Spoon into bowls and add a drizzle of olive oil. Serve and enjoy.

name: One-Pot Tomato Pasta
description: This is a full meal made in one pot. Similar to a classic puttanesca but totally vegan. The silky sauce cooks with the pasta to make the easiest weeknight meal.
instructions: In a large pot, add the olive oil and garlic and cook on medium heat for 1 min. Then add the tinned tomatoes and plenty of salt and pepper and cook for 3-4 mins until fragrant. Roughly chop the olives.

Add the olives, pasta and fill the two empty tomato tins with water (or measure 800 ml of water) and pour them into the pot. Bring to the boil, stir, then lower the heat to medium. Cover, with the lid slightly ajar to let some steam out. If your pan doesn't have a lid, you can pop a piece of parchment paper into the pot, covering the pasta snuggly, which will trap most of the heat but let some steam out.
Check how long your pasta will take to cook and set an alarm for half of that time. I used rigatoni which takes 15 mins in total, so I set an alarm for 6 mins.
At your halfway point, add in the chickpeas and spinach and give everything a good stir. Cover again with the lid and cook for the rest of the pasta’s cooking time, stirring occasionally.

At the end of the cooking time, if your pasta is still not cooked and the pan is looking a little dry, add another half or full tin of water and continue cooking until the sauce has thickened and the pasta is cooked to your liking. Season well with salt and pepper and enjoy.

name: One-Pot Vegan Puttanesca
description: We’ve given the Italian store-cupboard classic a vegan makeover, with added harissa for flavour and chickpeas for plant-based protein. And there’s only one pot to wash up.
instructions: Finely slice the shallot and mince the garlic.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a large lidded frying pan or pot set over a medium heat. Add the shallot and sauté for 4-5 mins, then add the garlic, tomato paste, chilli flakes and harissa (or skip the chilli flakes and/or harissa if you prefer it less spicy) and cook for another minute.

Drain the chickpeas and add to the pot with the tinned tomatoes, olives, capers, artichokes, veg stock cube, balsamic vinegar, pasta and water. Mix to combine and season very well with plenty of salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low-medium and leave to simmer for 5 mins with a lid on slightly ajar to let some steam out.
Give everything a stir and cook for another 10-15 mins with the lid on. Give it another good stir and make sure the pasta is cooked through; most of the water should have been absorbed.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over a low-medium heat until golden and fragrant.
To serve, divide the pasta between plates and top with some freshly cut chives and a handful of toasted pine nuts.

name: One-Pot Veggie & Leek Pie
description: Taking the well-loved British chicken and leek pie, making it veggie, and cooking it in one pan. We’re serving ours with grilled Tenderstem. Easy and delicious.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Remove the puff pastry sheet from the fridge and unroll it. Choose an oven-safe frying pan, and cut the puff pastry about 1cm larger – if the pastry isn’t large enough, use a rolling pin to make it larger. Place the cutout pastry onto a tray, cover and place it in the fridge.

Trim and thinly slice the leeks and garlic. Roughly chop the parsley, and zest the lemon, set aside for later. Place the frying pan onto medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil, sear the veggie chicken and transfer to a plate.

Meanwhile, put the leeks into a colander and give them a rinse. Place the now empty frying pan with a 1 tbsp of olive oil onto medium heat, add the leeks in with a generous pinch of salt, cook until softened and starting to brown.

Add the meat substitute and garlic to the leeks and cook for around 3 mins. Stir in the flour and cook for another 2-3 mins. Slowly add the stock, a little at a time, stirring constantly until fully incorporated, then simmer for around 5 mins until thickened. Remove from the heat and stir in the yoghurt, parsley and lemon zest. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Whisk the egg. Using a pastry brush, brush the filling up the sides of the frying pan - this will help the pastry to stick to the pan. Place the pastry on top of the pie and press the sides into the pan. Clean your brush and paint the pastry with the whisked egg, then cut a cross in the middle so that the steam can escape during baking. Bake for 25-30 mins, until golden brown.
Meanwhile, place your tenderstem onto a large baking tray, drizzle with oil and season generously with salt.

Once the pie is cooked, remove it from the oven. Be careful, it’ll be super hot at this stage. Turn your grill to high, and grill the broccoli until cooked through and charred, around 5 mins. Season the charred broccoli with lemon juice.
Serve the pie onto your plates with the broccoli alongside.

name: One-Tray Baked Chicken Rice with Chilli Vinegar
description: Crispy chicken skin, tender thighs and fluffy aromatic rice with a garlicky vinegar dressing. What more could you want from a chicken traybake?
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

Heat a large ovenproof pan over a medium heat. Season the chicken thighs with salt and cook, skin side down, for 8-9 mins or until crispy. Flip ‘em over and briefly seal the bottom then remove from the pan and set aside on a plate. Carefully remove the skin and pop the skins on a separate oven tray.

Finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger and tip them straight into the pan with the chicken fat and a pinch of salt. Cook for 8-9 mins until nicely coloured. Cut the spring onions into chunky lengths and wash the rice 2-3 times or until the water runs clear.

Tip the rice into the same pan and cook for 4-5 mins until toasty. Now add the stock and soy sauce then pop the chicken thighs back into the pan. Scatter over the spring onions, pop a lid on and slide into the oven for 35-40 mins. Slide the tray with the chicken skin on it into the oven for the last 10-12 mins until super crispy.
Meanwhile make the chilli vinegar: finely chop the chillies (seeds and all) and finely grate the garlic clove. Add to a small bowl and mix together with the vinegar and sugar. Set aside.
Finely chop the coriander and spring onions and add to a bowl. Use a peeler to shave in the cabbage and toss everything together.

Once baked, allow the rice and chicken thighs to rest for 10 mins or so before dividing between bowls and serving with crispy chicken skin, cabbage salad and plenty of the chilli vinegar, or you can serve on the side for pickier eaters.

name: One-Tray Harissa-Glazed Salmon
description: Crispy sweet potatoes, charred broccoli and sticky-sweet salmon glazed in harissa and honey. All roasted on one tray for maximum flavour, minimal clean-up.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Line a baking tray with foil to prevent sticking. Peel the sweet potato and chop into 2cm chunks. Tip onto a baking tray, season with salt and black pepper and spritz with olive oil. Roast for 15 mins until nearly tender.
Meanwhile, mix the honey, harissa and soy sauce in a small bowl to make your glaze. Season the salmon fillets and brush them all over with the glaze, reserving some to drizzle at the end.
Once the sweet potatoes have cooked, nestle the salmon and broccoli onto the same tray. Spritz the broccoli with a little olive oil, then spoon over half the remaining glaze.
Return the tray to the oven and roast for another 8–10 mins until the salmon is cooked through and the broccoli is just charred.
Heat the rice following pack instructions.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls and top with the sweet potato, broccoli and salmon. Drizzle over the remaining glaze and finish with a dollop of Greek yoghurt.

name: One-Tray Thai Red Chicken & Pumpkin Curry
description: An easy but impressive weeknight dinner that’s perfect for the colder months. Just brown some chicken, blitz up a quick sauce in the blender and let the oven do the work.
keywords: one-tray thai curried chicken and pumpkin
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Trim, halve and scoop the seeds out of the pumpkin. Chop it into 3cm thick chunks then place in a large baking dish.

Get the chicken thighs in a cold frying pan, skin side down. Set it over a medium heat and cook for 10-mins without turning until the skin is golden brown. Transfer the thighs to the baking dish, resting them on top of the pumpkin.

Meanwhile, pick the coriander leaves and add the stems into a blender with the curry paste, coconut milk, crumbled chicken stock cube, water, fish sauce and sugar. Blend until smooth then taste and season with more fish sauce or sugar, if needed.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and pumpkin. Pop it in the oven for 35-40 mins until the pumpkin is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Before serving, reheat the rice.
Serve the chicken and pumpkin curry with the rice. Garnish with a lime wedge and the coriander leaves.

name: Onion Bhajis & Poached Eggs
description: Switch up your standard brunch with these crispy bhajis - top with poached British Lion eggs for the best breakfast ever.
instructions: Slice your red onion, chop your coriander and grate your ginger.

Add the red onion, ginger, the coriander stalks, ground coriander, cumin seeds, curry powder, baking powder, gram flour, a pinch of salt, and water into a mixing bowl. Mix the ingredients with your hands until combined.

Pour a glug of vegetable oil into a frying pan. Take a small handful of the bhaji mixture and shape using your hands. Once the oil is hot, add your shaped bhajis into the pan and fry for a few minutes on each side, until crisp and golden brown. Set aside and repeat until all the bhaji mixture has been used up.

Fill a large saucepan with water and bring to a boil. Add a pinch of salt, then stir the water with a wooden spoon to create a whirlpool effect. Crack your British Lion egg and gently lower into the centre of the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes until your whites are set but your yolks are still beautifully runny. Repeat this step for each egg.
Stack two bhajis on a plate and pop two poached eggs on top. Drizzle with mango chutney and sprinkle on the remaining coriander. Dig in.

name: Onion Squash, Sage & Hot Honey Orzo
description: This roasted red kuri squash orzotto with hot honey is a little bit sweet, a little bit spicy and incredibly moreish. The perfect autumn comfort food. Onion squash is also known as ‘Red Kuri’. It’s sweet, nutty and super tasty. If you can’t find it, then Crown Prince squash, Hubbard squash or Delica Pumpkin would work just as well.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.
Cut the squash in half from stem to tip. Scoop out the seeds and set to one side. Keep the skin on the white onion and quarter it through the root. Halve the tomatoes.

Cut each half of the squash into 4-6 wedges and spread over a baking sheet, making sure there’s plenty of space between each piece. Arrange the onion quarters, tomatoes and unpeeled garlic cloves in the gaps, cut-side down, then drizzle with a generous glug of rapeseed oil, turning the squash pieces so they’re glossy. Sprinkle with the chilli flakes and a generous pinch of salt. Roast for 35-45 mins, until the squash are bronzing and blistering at the edges, turning the wedges over after around 25 mins.

Meanwhile, spread the squash seeds over a small baking sheet, using two forks to separate the seeds from the flesh. Don’t worry too much if some are attached or there are still clumps of flesh – it all tastes good. Drizzle with a glug of rapeseed oil, and add a good sprinkle of salt. Roast in the oven for 20-25 mins until golden, shuffling the tray once or twice. When there’s 10 mins left, add the sage leaves to the tray, dragging them through the oil first.

Cook the orzo in salted boiling water for 2 mins less than the packet time (so probably 8 mins), until the chalkiness is just gone, but the grains are not totally swollen. Drain through a sieve and rinse under a cold running tap to cool them down. Mix with a fork to separate the grains then return to the saucepan.

Once the squash pieces are tender and coloured at the edges, transfer half to a blender, along with the tomatoes, onion pieces, garlic and any juices on the tray (remove the skins from the onion and garlic as you do this). Add the butter, a pinch of salt and ⅔ of the stock to the contents of the blender and blitz until it’s a silky smooth sauce.
Add a drizzle of hot honey to the squash pieces, then return to the oven (turning it off at the same time).

Pour the sauce into the orzo pan and set over a low-medium heat to warm through for 2-3 mins. Grate in ⅔ of the Parmesan and squeeze in the lemon juice. The orzo will swell and stiffen but you want something that flows like the loosest risotto, so add more stock if you need to, then check for seasoning before dividing between pasta bowls or plates.
Top with the squash wedges, a grating of Parmesan, the roasted seeds and sage and a really generous drizzle of hot honey.

name: Oniony Pasta & Lentil Salad
description: I had Cypriot orzo version of Mujadara recently and couldn't stop thinking about it. This pasta salad is my version - onion marmalade, crispy onions and nigella seeds give it real depth, with parsley, lemon and creamy cottage cheese cutting through. Even if you're not a cottage cheese fan, whipping it gives an almost Greek yoghurt texture. Can't find caramelised onion marmalade? Sub in roasted garlic paste, caramelised onions, or onion chutney.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.
Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the soft stems.
Add the cottage cheese to a blender and blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper, then stir the nigella seeds through.

Pour the olive oil into a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the almonds and cook until toasted and golden, 1-2 mins, then add the cumin seeds and parsley stems and cook for a couple of seconds, until fragrant. Pour into a bowl and leave to cool.
Once the water's boiling, add the pasta and cook according to the packet instructions. Stir the microwave cooked lentils in too, until piping hot, then drain fully and leave to cool.

Squeeze the juice of the lemon into the infused oil, then stir the marmalade and crispy onions through and season with salt and pepper. Stir the pasta and lentils through, then toss the parsley leaves through right before serving.
Spread the cottage cheese over your plates or boxes and top with the pasta salad.

name: Oozy Butternut Orzo
description: The ooziest orzo about. The Goat's Cheese brings that nice sharp kick to complement the rich roasted butternut. Such a freshy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Cut your butternut squash into cubes and place on a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place in the oven for 30 minutes or until soft.
Remove squash and place 3/4 of it in a blender. Place the remaining quarter back in the oven for another 10 minutes until brown and caramelised.
Add the stock cube to the blender with half the water and blitz smooth.
Get a large frying pan on the heat. Add a splash of olive oil and a chopped clove of garlic. Once softened, pour in the squash purée. Mix it about and add your orzo.
Keep mixing the orzo and add the rest of the water in splashes, mixing through and cooking until it resembles a loose, oozy risotto.
Add your remaining squash and a handful of chopped basil. Mix it all together and turn off the heat.
Serve up with dollops of goat's cheese and more parm and basil if you like. Enjoy!

name: Oozy Jammy Eggs
description: While the humble egg seems simple to cook, getting the perfect jammy yolks and soft whites is an art. These eggs are made with meal-prep in mind, ready for you to chuck on toast, add to salads or eat straight from the fridge for a high-protein snack.
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan with water to and bring to a rolling boil.
Use a spoon to gently lower in the eggs into the boiling water. Don’t overcrowd the pan or lower the heat.
Set a timer for 6 mins if the eggs are room temp, or 6 mins 30 secs if they’re cold.
While they boil, fill a bowl with cold water and ice. Once the timer goes, transfer the eggs to the ice bath for 3 mins to stop them cooking further.

Peel if you’re eating them now – run them under cold water as you go to make it easier. 
If you’re storing them, keep unpeeled eggs in the shell for up to 7 days in the fridge. Peeled eggs should be stored submerged in cold water in a sealed container – they’ll stay fresh for up to 4 days.
To reheat, pop a cold egg in a bowl of warm water for 5 mins. The yolk stays oozy and delicious.

name: Orange Polenta Cake Recipe
description: This delicious polenta cake recipe couldn't be simpler, no fancy equipment required, just whisking the wet into the dried ingredients. It also keeps super well, in an airtight container at room temperature, for up to a week. If you want to get into baking, this recipe is the perfect place to start.
instructions: Heat your oven to 140°C.
Lightly grease a 23cm springform cake tin with the olive oil and line the base with baking parchment.
Zest the oranges into a large bowl.
Whisk in four-fifths of the caster sugar along with all the ground almonds, polenta and baking powder.
In a separate bowl, crack in the eggs. Add the olive oil and whisk together.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry, whisk together until a smooth cake batter forms then pour the batter into the lined tin.
Bake for 50 mins until the cake comes away from the sides of the tin and a skewer inserted into the centre comes out with a few crumbs attached.
Measure the remaining caster sugar into a small saucepan and squeeze in the orange juice. Gently cook set over a low heat for around 5 mins until the sugar has dissolved.

Prick the warm baked cake all over the top with a skewer then pour the syrup evenly over the cake. Leave the cake in its tin to cool then cut into fat slices to serve, with some crème fraîche if you like.

name: Orange and Vanilla Cheesecake
description: A beautifully creamy and perfectly set orange and vanilla cheesecake, made by Ocado's own Hannah.
instructions: Remove the cream cheese from the fridge 30 mins before cooking to allow it to get to room temperature and soften. Preheat the oven to 150°C.
Crush the biscuits to fine crumbs either by whizzing in a food processor or put them into a polythene bag and bashing them with a rolling pin.
Melt the butter in the microwave and combine it with the crushed biscuits. Spoon this mixture into the base of a 20cm (8in) springform tin, pressing the biscuit well into the base.

Spoon the cream cheese into a large bowl and beat well to soften it. Add the golden caster sugar, double cream, eggs, vanilla extract and grate the zest of your oranges. Mix well until all the ingredients are evenly combined. Pour this mixture over the top of the biscuit base.
Bake in the oven for 30 mins then turn off the heat and allow to finish cooking for 1 hour in the heat of the oven. (The cheesecake will still be quite wobbly at this stage).
Carefully remove from the oven and chill overnight or at least 4 hours. Slice into portions and enjoy.
