name: Orzo & Herby Turkey Meatballs in Mushroom Broth
description: This soup is a bowl of pure umami. It’s perfect for gloomy winter evenings, or any time your taste buds need a pick-me-up.
keywords: Orzo & Herby Turkey Meatballs in Mushroom Broth
Orzo & Herby Turkey Meatballs in Mushroom Broth recipe
instructions: First, make the broth (you can do this in advance and store it in the fridge/freezer until ready to make the soup). Halve the onion, cut the ginger into slices, and halve the head of garlic.
Heat a glug of sesame oil in a large pot over a medium heat. Sear the onion, ginger and garlic for about 5 mins, until very fragrant and slightly burnt.
Roughly chop the button mushrooms, then add them to the pot along with the miso paste, stirring well to ensure everything is nicely coated in the miso. Continue cooking for about 5 mins.

Add the dried mushrooms, kombu seaweed, salt, peppercorns and water. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer gently for at least 2 hours, allowing the stock to reduce significantly. Strain and discard the solids.

Meanwhile, make the meatballs. Whisk the eggs in a large bowl with a generous glug of olive oil, then stir in the breadcrumbs and continue mixing to create a paste-like consistency. Mix in the salt, chilli flakes, fennel seeds, and coriander seeds.

Finely chop the fresh herbs and spring onion, and mince the garlic clove. Stir these in, along with half of the minced turkey. Gradually add the rest of the meat, incorporating it gently so as to keep the mixture light and fluffy.
Refrigerate the mixture for about half an hour, then roll it into balls with the diameter of a £1 coin (lightly coating your hands in oil beforehand helps prevent sticking).
Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan set over a medium-high heat and place as many meatballs as you can fit, leaving enough space between balls to turn them (you can work in batches!).
Cook the meatballs for about 10 mins on medium heat, turning every now and then to ensure all sides are nice and golden. Remove from the pan, but do not wash the pan (yet).

Peel and then thinly slice the onion and garlic cloves, then add them to the pan you used to fry the meatballs, along with another swish of olive oil. Stir with a wooden spoon to scrape up some of the browned bits on the bottom of the pan, and sauté on medium heat until fragrant, about 5 mins. Deglaze the pan with a bit of stock and continue cooking for 5 mins or so.
Meanwhile, lay out the cabbage leaves and cut out the tough inner stem, then roll them up and cut thin slices.

Add in the rest of the stock, the cabbage leaves, and the orzo. Cook over a medium heat for 7 mins, or until the orzo is cooked following pack instructions. Add in the meatballs and simmer for a minute or two, until they are warmed up.
Finely chop the parsley for garnish, then season the soup with salt, pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil. Divide across four bowls and top with crème fraiche, and chopped parsley.

name: Orzo Cacio e Pepe
description: We have nailed the cheesy, creamy pepperiness of an authentic cacio e pepe, and this is the easiest version in existence. Everything’s cooked in one pan.
instructions: Measure 750ml of water into a large saucepan. Bring to the boil and season with salt. Drop in the orzo pasta. Cook for 7–8 mins, until you are left with around 100ml of water and the orzo pasta is nearly cooked
Meanwhile finely grate the Parmesan cheese onto a chopping board. Crush the peppercorns, and then toast them in a pan with no oil, until they start smoking.

Once the orzo is ready, lower the heat to medium and stir in the butter. Once melted, stir in the Parmesan in three additions, waiting for the first to melt before adding the next one. Once all the Parmesan has been added you should be left with a silky, glossy sauce. Add a splash more water if the sauce looks a little thick.
Stir through the cracked black pepper and finely grate in the lemon zest. Spoon the orzo into four bowls. Heaven.

name: Orzo Carbonara
description: Pairing the best pasta with the best sauce, it was always gonna work. An absolute belter of a dish and it only takes 15 minutes.
instructions: Grab a bowl. Crack your eggs and seperate the yolks from the whites. Add your egg yolks to the bowl, then grate in the Parmesan and a generous amount of black pepper. Mix with a fork and set it aside.
Chop up your bacon into small bite-size pieces and throw into a cold frying pan. Turn the heat up to medium and cook until crisp.
Bring a saucepan of salted water to a boil and add the orzo. Cook al dente, for 2 minutes less than on the package instructions.
Chop up the garlic and add this to the bacon followed by the chilli flakes. Take a ladle of the pasta water and add this too.

Once your pasta is cooked, drain and reserve the pasta water. Add the orzo to the pan and mix. Add a drop of pasta water to your egg and Parmesan mix and stir until smooth, then pour it into the orzo mixing well. Keep adding pasta water and mixing until you have a silky, creamy texture. Serve it up and tuck into this delightful little dish!

name: Orzo Primavera
description: A one-pan wonder perfect for summer. Here's our take on a classic primavera pasta, but using orzo.
instructions: Heat a splash of olive oil in a pan. Slice your asparagus into thirds and begin frying. Once browned, remove them from the pan and set aside.
Finely chop the onion. Slice the garlic and chilli into thin slices. Fry the onion and chilli in the same pan used for the asparagus. Once the onions are starting to turn translucent, add the garlic.
Boil the water and add the vegetable stock. Add the orzo to the pan, along with the stock.

Allow the pasta to cook for 8 mins before adding the broad beans, petit pois and asparagus. Once the pasta is fully cooked, finely chop the basil and mint and stir these in. Add the parmesan and stir until creamy.
Season with salt and pepper. Top with your burrata, more grated parmesan if you fancy, black pepper and fresh basil to serve. Enjoy!

name: Orzo With Chicken, Za'atar & Lemon
description: Za’atar and lemon bring a citrusy kick to this orzo. A simple and delicious way to make the most of any roast chicken leftovers.
instructions: Before you begin make the No Fuss Roast Chicken.

Set a large saucepan over a medium heat and add the chicken stock and if using, the saffron. Bring to a simmer, turn the heat to low and let the whole lot tick over for 40 mins. Once done, strain and keep warm.
If you have any leftover chicken bones add these to the pan first with a shot of olive and roast in the hot pan until browned, before adding the stock.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, chilli and one of the garlic cloves. Preheat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a generous amount of olive oil. Tip in the red onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 8-10 mins until just starting to caramelise.
Add the chopped chilli and garlic and cook for 2-3 mins before adding the orzo. Stir through the base and toast for 1-2 mins, before adding the za’atar.
Now begin adding your stock, a ladle at a time, cooking the pasta like a risotto, until tender and silky. Shred the leftover chicken and stir through the orzo.
Finely grate the remaining garlic clove into the yoghurt along with the zest and juice of the half of the lemons.

To finish the orzo, add the remaining lemon juice and zest and adjust the seasoning. Divide the cooked orzo between warm bowls. Top with the garlicky yoghurt, a little extra za’atar and some picked dill and parsley.

name: Oven Baked Mushroom Risotto
description: Baking this risotto in the oven means you don't have to constantly stir, and you can still get a deliciously creamy vegan risotto at the end.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Finely chop the shallot and garlic.

Shred the mushrooms by pulling them apart into smaller pieces. Drizzle with oil, season well and and a few sprigs of thyme. Add to a baking tray and roast for 15-18 mins or until golden and crispy, tossing once halfway through to help them cook evenly.

Get yourself a large, deep pan with a lid. Add the butter to the pan on medium heat. Add the chopped shallot and fry until translucent, about 4 mins. Add the garlic and a splash of olive oil and sauté for another 3-4 mins until softened and fragrant. Take care that the onion and garlic don't catch and start to brown.

Make your stock in a large heatproof receptacle. Add the rice to your pot and stir to make sure it's all covered and glossy. Slowly add the stock to the pot, stirring constantly. Add a few thyme sprigs on top of the rice.
Bring to the boil, cover with the lid and bake for 18 mins. Stir once at the 10 min mark if you like.
When the risotto is ready to come out, the rice should be cooked through but still have a firm bite. Remove the thyme sprigs.

Heat the of oat milk with a little boiling water. Whisk the miso through the hot milk until combined and smooth. Stir the milk through the risotto slowly until you reach the consistency that you like. Add the nutritional yeast, taste it and season well with salt and pepper. Optionally here, you can add another tablespoon or two of vegan butter to make it richer.
Add the mushrooms to the risotto and finish with a sprinkle of parsley.

name: Oven-Baked Lamb Kebab with Tahini & Chopped Salad
description: A really quick and easy way to bake kebab in the oven. Stuff it in a warm flatbread with loads of chopped salad, garlicky tahini yoghurt and fresh chilli.
keywords: kebab oven recipes. tahini yoghurt dressing
instructions: Preheat the grill to hot.
Finely chop the onion, garlic and ½ the parsley, then mix with the mince, ½ tsp salt and the cumin, then knead well with your hands for a few minutes, until combined thoroughly.
Line a baking tray with baking paper, and pat the meat evenly onto it.

Mix the Turkish pepper paste, water and olive oil in a small bowl and season with salt and pepper. Brush this mixture over the meat and grill for about 8-12 mins until the meat is cooked through. If it's colouring too quickly, bring it down a level or turn the grill down a little.

Meanwhile, finely chop the salad ingredients and remaining parsley and combine with the juice of ½ the lemon and a good pinch of salt and pepper and put to one side. Finely chop the green chilli and set aside for garnish.
Blend or whisk the yoghurt and tahini into a smooth sauce. Finely grate the garlic and mix it through the sauce then put to one side.

To serve, briefly heat the flatbreads under the grill or in a dry pan and serve the kebab in the flatbreads along with some of the cooking juices, chopped salad, tahini yoghurt, pickles and chilli. Drizzle over a little more olive oil and serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges to squeeze over.

name: Oven-Cooked BBQ Pork Ribs
description: If you haven't tried the award-winning pork ribs from London's Rack City Ribs (@rackcityribs), you've been missing out. Here they've shared the recipe for their iconic slow-cooked and glazed ribs with Sticky Bourbon sauce. Perfect for a summer BBQ or weeknight cheat meal. These ribs are finger-licking good and easy to prepare. Get ready to impress your friends with this delicious and approachable recipe!
instructions: Remove the pork membrane from the ribs.
Combine the rub ingredients in a bowl, then rub it over both sides of the ribs (most should be on the meaty side). Set aside to marinate for 20 mins.

When ready to cook, heat the oven to 160°C. Place the ribs in a deep baking tray in a single layer. Pour water underneath the ribs, cover with foil and transfer to the oven. Bake for 1 hr 30 mins or until the meat is pretty tender.
Meanwhile, pour all the glaze ingredients into a pot and bring to the boil. Reduce to a simmer and cook for 20 mins to reduce the glaze.
Remove the ribs from the oven and turn the heat up to 180°C. Remove the foil, drizzle with olive oil, then return the ribs to the oven for 15 mins or until the rub has become nice and crusty.
Meanwhile, line a new baking tray with foil.

Once cooked, remove the ribs from the oven and transfer to the lined tray. Pour any juices from the tray over the ribs. Flip the ribs so they’re bonier-side up. Slather with the glaze, then bake for 10 mins.
Remove from the oven, then turn the ribs over so the meaty side is up. Slather with the glaze and bake for 5 mins. Repeat two or three more times until you've got a thick glaze on the ribs.
Cut the ribs into individual or multiple rib portions and serve with any remaining glaze.

name: Oven‑Roasted Chicken Adobo with Rice & Peanut Butter Greens
description: This recipe is inspired by the classic Filipino dish, Chicken Adobo. It balances savoury, tangy, and slightly sweet flavours. Chicken is braised in a bold sauce of vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns. The vinegar takes centre stage, giving the dish its signature tang while cutting through the richness of the meat. The best part? It has 50g of protein.
instructions:
Heat the oven to 200°C. 
Pat the chicken dry and season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Set a large ovenproof pot over a medium-high heat with the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the chicken skin-side down and cook for 8 mins until golden and crispy. Transfer to a plate.
Peel and thinly slice the onion. Smash the garlic cloves. Turn the heat down slightly and chuck both into the same pot. Fry for 3 mins until soft and fragrant.
Pour in the rice vinegar, soy sauce, water and brown sugar. Chuck in the bay leaves and lots of cracked black pepper. Stir well to lift up all the caramelised bits.
Nestle the chicken back into the pot, skin-side up. The skin should sit above the liquid so it stays crisp. Transfer to the oven and roast for 25–35 mins until the chicken is fully cooked and golden.

Meanwhile, rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Add to a lidded saucepan with the turmeric and chicken stock. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 10 mins. Remove from the heat and let it steam for another 10 mins.

While the rice steams, heat a splash of olive oil in a pan set over a medium heat. Add the greens and cook until wilted. Zest the lime, then juice it. Stir the peanut butter, lime juice and a dash of soy sauce into the greens until glossy. Season to taste and keep warm.
Once the chicken is done, transfer it to a plate. If the sauce in the pot looks too thin, place it over a medium heat and bubble for 3–4 mins to thicken slightly.

To serve, spoon the turmeric rice onto plates, top with the crispy adobo chicken, drizzle over that gorgeous sauce, and finish with the peanut butter greens. Top with lime zest or chopped spring onions, if you like. Dig in!

name: Overnight Strawberry & Matcha Brekkie Bowl
description: A creamy chia and seed pudding with a serious matcha punch, topped with a fruity strawberry compote. Make a big old batch and enjoy it for days.
keywords: Overnight Strawberry & Matcha Brekkie Bowl recipe
instructions: For the overnight base: Add the matcha, tahini, fresh ginger, salt and water into a blender and blitz together until smooth. Place a fine mesh strainer over a bowl or box and pour the matcha mixture through. Season to taste with honey, then stir through the remaining ingredients for the overnight base. Cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 5 hours, ideally overnight.

Meanwhile, for the strawberry topping: Add the frozen strawberries, apple juice and salt to a saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Bring the mixture to the boil then turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 3-5 mins until the fruit has defrosted. Mix the cornflour and water together in a mug then pour into the strawberries, bring the mixture to the boil, whilst stirring, and cook until thickened to your liking. Transfer the strawberry compote to a box, cover and refrigerate.
Toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan set over a medium heat for 4-5 mins until golden. Transfer to a box and store at room temperature.
When you’re ready to serve, spoon some of the matcha pudding into a bowl and top with the strawberry compote and toasted flaked almonds.

name: PB & J Overnight Oats with a Chocolate Smash Lid
description: For all the peanut butter lovers, this one’s for you. We’ve taken the classic combo and made these delicious overnight oats with jammy layers plus a snappy choc top you get to crack open. It’s a fun one.
keywords: PB&J Overnight Oats with a Chocolate Smash Lid recipe
PB&J Overnight Oats with a Chocolate Smash Lid
instructions: Mix the oats, milk, yoghurt, maple syrup, peanut butter and a pinch of salt together in a bowl until combined.
If the jam is stiff, warm it briefly in the microwave or in a small pan over a low heat so it loosens up.
Melt the dark chocolate with a splash of coconut oil in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water, or in the microwave in short bursts. Stir until smooth.
Layer the oat mixture and jam into glasses or jars. Pour over the melted chocolate to cover the top, then chill in the fridge overnight or for at least 4 hrs.

name: Paccheri With Broccoli, Chilli & Almonds
description: Big Southern Italian vibes here with a super simple pasta. The broccoli gets twice-cooked and becomes super creamy while the broccoli cooking water becomes the pasta cooking water. Smart!
instructions: Bring a large pan of well salted water to a boil. Separate the broccoli into florets, then peel and cube the stem, removing any woody bits.
Add the broccoli to the water and boil for about 5 mins until softened.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add a generous splash of olive oil. Finely slice the garlic and add it to the pan with the anchovies and cook for about 2 mins, breaking down the anchovies with the back of a spoon.
Finely chop and add the oregano and chilli flakes, sizzle for about 30 seconds and then add a splash of the cooking water from the broccoli to stop them frying.
Once the broccoli is soft, add to the pan with garlic but don’t drain. We’ll use this water to cook the pasta.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente. Meanwhile, keep cooking the broccoli gently in the olive oil and garlic mix, breaking it down with a wooden spoon until it becomes almost creamy.
Once the pasta is cooked, add directly to the pan with the broccoli and toss well along with the juice of a lemon and some of the pasta cooking water. Taste and add salt as needed.
In a small pan, toast the almonds until just golden, remove and roughly chop.
Plate up the pasta and top with the toasted almonds.

name: Pad Krapow Folded Dumpling Soup
description: Aromatic Thai chicken dumplings in a piping hot chicken broth. A cosy and comforting dumpling soup that’s on the table in half an hour.
keywords: Pad Krapow Folded Dumpling Soup Recipe
instructions: Using a sharp knife, very finely chop the Thai basil, fresh coriander, spring onions, garlic cloves and red chilli. Add to a medium-sized bowl along with the minced chicken, tamari, sesame oil and fish sauce, and mix to combine. (Pro tip: heat up a tiny splash of oil in a frying pan and cook a teaspoon of the mixture to check the seasoning, then season to taste if needed.)

Start wrapping your dumplings. Fill a small bowl with water. Add a small spoonful of filling to a dumpling wrapper, then moisten the edge of the wrapper with a bit of water and carefully fold it into triangles, making sure there is no air trapped inside. Repeat until the filling is used up.

To cook the dumplings, either steam them in a lined bamboo steamer basket for about 10-12 mins, or bring a large pot of water to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium, and gently simmer them for about 8-10 mins.

In a separate pot, bring the stock to a boil and then reduce to a gentle simmer. Once the dumplings are cooked, divide them across 4 bowls and top with the hot stock. Serve with an extra splash of soy sauce, a drizzle of chilli oil and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

name: Pad See Ew Chicken Noodles
description: A classic recipe for stir-fried Thai chicken noodles. Full of flavour and quick and easy to make for dinner.
instructions: Slice the chicken thigh into strips then add to a small bowl with fish sauce and pinch of salt, and set aside in the fridge. Mince the garlic and cut the broccoli into 3cm chunks. Set aside.

If your fresh rice noodles are stiff, add them to a microwave safe bowl and microwave in 1 min bursts until the noodles are soft and pliable enough to roll out into long strands. Add the dark soy sauce, toss well and set aside at room temperature.
For the dipping sauce, mince the garlic and finely slice the chilli. Combine both with the rice vinegar in a small bowl.
Combine all the noodle sauce ingredients in a small bowl and mix well.

The remaining steps will happen very quickly so ensure all your ingredients are at arm’s length: Heat a generous glug of sesame oil in a large pan set over a high heat. When the pan is hot, add the chicken and leave to cook, without moving it, for 2 mins on each side until golden. Turn the heat down to medium and remove the chicken.

Add another glug of sesame oil then cook the garlic for 30 seconds or until lightly golden. Crack the eggs into the garlicky oil, and scramble into large chunks. Add the greens, noodles and ½ of the noodle sauce. Toss everything well and cook for 1 min.

Return the chicken to the pan along with the bean sprouts then toss well. Leave the noodles to caramelise without interference for 30 seconds, then toss and repeat until the noodles are slightly charred. Add some of the remaining noodle sauce, if needed for flavour and moisture.
Divide the noodles between bowls and top with sliced cucumbers, dipping sauce, roasted peanuts and crispy shallots.

name: Padrón Pepper & Manchego Chicken Salad
description: This one's got a short and simple ingredient list, but the flavour combination really packs a punch. Inspired by sunny Spanish ingredients, it's a light but filling dinner and any leftovers make perfect lunches for the next day.
instructions: Butterfly the chicken breasts. Add a generous drizzle of olive oil to a bowl, season generously with salt and pepper, then stir the paprika through. Add the chicken, coat all over in the marinade and set aside.
Using a peeler, peel the Manchego into shards and set aside. Roughly chop the almonds.

Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with another drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the Padrón peppers and cook for 5-6 mins, turning occasionally, until they start to soften and the skins blister and char. Transfer to a plate. If you can't get Padrón peppers, use a green pepper chopped into 2-3cm chunks instead.
Return the pan to a medium heat and add in the marinated chicken and fry for 4-5 mins on each side, until cooked through. Transfer to a plate, cover with foil and leave to rest.
Add the chopped almonds to the hot pan with the measured amount of olive oil and cook, stirring, for 3-4 mins until toasted. Tip the almonds and oil into a small bowl for the dressing.
Add the juice of the lemon to the oil and almonds, stir then taste and season with salt, pepper and the honey, this is your dressing. Leave to cool, then toss through the peppers, cheese and rocket.
Divide the chicken between plates and top with the salad to serve. If you're making it for tomorrow's lunch, keep the dressing in a separate container and drizzle over just before eating.

name: Paella Mixta
description: This meat and seafood paella recipe from Omar Allibhoy is the best of both worlds. It's surf and turf done right.
instructions: Crumble the saffron into the shellfish stock. Keep warm over the lowest heat.
Place a paella pan over medium heat with the olive oil and seasoned chicken. Fry for 6 mins until golden. Add the squid rings and sauté for a further 4 minutes.

Add the garlic, closely followed by the smoked paprika and the grated tomatoes, cook for about 2 mins until the oil starts separating from the tomato paste. Add the rice and stir all together for a couple of minutes, making sure the rice gets coated with the oil and sears.

Carefully add the hot stock to the pan and give it a good stir distributing the rice evenly. Taste the stock and adjust the seasoning if necessary. Cook on a high heat for the first 10 mins, scatter the prawns and mussels over the top and continue to cook over low heat for the remaining 8 minutes. If you want a “socarrat” crispy bottom bring the heat up to it’s maximum for just 1 minute. Let it rest for 5 minutes before eating it. Buen provecho!

name: Palak Paneer Chicken Meatballs
description: Inspired by a classic palak paneer, but instead I've added in some chicken meatballs, which stay super juicy from being braised in the lightly spiced spinach sauce. Anything packed with greens is my favourite type of dinner, and this one reheats beautifully too.
instructions: Defrost the spinach for the meatballs. Once it's cooled a little, squeeze out as much water as you can. Thinly slice the spring onion. Finely grate the paneer and add 75% of it to a large bowl with the chicken mince. Add the garam masala and spring onion, season generously with salt and black pepper and stir to combine. Portion into five meatballs per person and pop in the fridge to firm up.

Wash the basmati rice until the water runs clearer. Add to a medium saucepan with the water, place over a high heat and bring to the boil. Put the lid on, turn the heat down to low and leave to steam for 12 mins. Remove from the heat, fluff with a fork and replace the lid for a further 10 mins, until fully cooked.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. Pick half the coriander leaves and set aside for serving. Add the coriander stems and remaining leaves to a blender with half the frozen spinach, the cashews, water, garam masala and ginger garlic paste. Blend until very smooth. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Place a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the garnish cashews and toast, stirring, for 4-5 mins until golden. Transfer to a plate and return the pan to the heat.

Add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the meatballs and cook on all sides until golden brown. Pour in the sauce and season with salt and black pepper. Leave to simmer for 10-15 mins, until thickened and the meatballs are cooked through, add a splash of water if the sauce gets too thick, or simmer a little longer to thicken further. Squeeze in the lemon juice, then stir the remaining frozen spinach through and let it wilt into the sauce.
Divide the rice between plates. Top with the chicken meatballs and sauce, then scatter over the remaining paneer, reserved coriander leaves and toasted cashews.

name: Pan Con Tomate
description: The most delicious pan con tomate - a classic Spanish dish. Big juicy tomatoes and garlic on crispy sourdough bread. Recipe By MOB Contributor Thomas Straker.
instructions: Chop your tomatoes in half and grate them into a bowl. Pour in a big glug of olive oil, season with salt to taste and stir together.
Thinly slice your sourdough into 1cm thick pieces. Allow for two slices per person.
Place a pan over a medium heat and pour in a large glug of oil.
Add two slices of bread and fry until golden brown and crisp. Flip and repeat on the other side.
Peel your garlic, remove the fried sourdough from the pan and brush over with the raw garlic.
Spread a generous amount of your tomatoes over the sourdough. Drizzle over a small glug of olive oil and tuck in!

name: Pan Con Tomate with White Beans
description: This Catalan tapas dish is made using just a handful of simple, fresh ingredients. We’ve added beans for extra fibre and plant protein to keep you fuller for longer.
keywords: Pan Con Tomate with White Beans
Pan Con Tomate with White Beans recipe
instructions: Thinly slice ½ of the garlic (keep the rest whole).
Gently fry the sliced garlic in a large pan with a generous glug of olive oil for 30 seconds over a low heat.
Add the beans along with their liquid and a generous pinch of salt. Add a splash of water and leave to simmer for 5 mins.
While the beans are cooking, prepare the tomato by grating it into a bowl. Add a generous glug of olive oil and a generous pinch of salt and stir to combine.
Toast the sourdough and rub with the remaining garlic clove and drizzle over some olive oil.
Serve the beans with the grated tomato on top.

name: Pan Roasted Courgettes With Anchovies, Capers & Lemons
description: We've crosshatched our courgettes here for optimum surface area caramelisation. Paired with anchovies, capers, and lemons? Out of bounds.
instructions: Halve the courgettes lengthways, keeping the stem intact. Score the cut sides in a 1cm diamond pattern, sprinkle with salt and set aside for 30 mins.
Finely chop the parsley and segment the lemons. Cut the segments into smaller chunks, squeeze any juice left in the trim into a bowl and save for later.

Grab a large non-stick pan and cover the base with a light layer of olive oil. Set over a medium heat. Pat the courgettes dry and gently lay, cut-side down into the pan. Cook over a medium heat for 10-12 mins, untouched until the cut side is a beautiful golden brown.
Leave the courgettes cut-side down and add the butter. Continue to cook until the courgette is tender and the butter is nut brown. Fish out the courgettes and lay out on a warm serving platter.
Add the capers to the hot butter. Allow to sizzle for 1 min then remove from the heat, tip in the lemon segments, leftover juice, anchovies and most of the chopped parsley.
Season to taste, adding more lemon juice if wanted and spoon over the roasted courgettes, topping with the remaining parsley.

name: Pan-Fried Hellim Böreği (Halloumi-filled Pastries)
description: What do you get when you mix halloumi with pastry? Something really delicious, that's what.
instructions: For the filling, peel and finely dice the onion. Pour the olive oil into a pan and set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the onion, stir, reduce the heat a little and soften for 12-15 mins until fully translucent and starting to colour.
Meanwhile, whisk the egg in a separate bowl and set aside. Grate the halloumi and finely chop the parsley. Transfer both to a bowl along with the dried mint and black pepper.
Once the onion is cooked, stir through the parsley, then remove the pan from the heat and set aside to cool fully.
Once the onion and parsley mixture has cooled, add them to the hellim mixture, then add the whisked egg to bind everything together. Allow to cool fully before using to fill the börek.

For the dough, sift the flour into a large bowl and stir through the salt. Make a well in the centre. Mix the warm water, vinegar and 3 tbsp olive oil in a heatproof jug and pour into the well. Give everything a good stir with a large spoon.

Use your hands to turn the dough out onto a clean work surface. Knead the dough for 5-6 mins until smooth, tuck the sides under to form a ball, then give it a gentle rub with the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil before returning the dough to the bowl and covering with a tea towel. Leave to rest for 30 mins.

Divide the dough into three equal-sized pieces and roll them into balls. Lightly flour the work surface, place one of the dough balls in front of you, and leave the other two to one side, covered with a damp tea towel to prevent them from drying out.

Start to roll out the dough ball, turning 45° each time you glide over with the rolling pin. Shape it into a large rectangular shape (around 50cm x 60cm). You don’t need to be too precise – it’s the thickness that matters the most.

Roll out the dough until it is extremely thin (around 1mm-2 mm), adding a dusting of flour when and where necessary. The dough should be sturdy enough that it doesn’t tear when the filling is added. It should also be floured enough to prevent it from sticking to the surface, but not so heavily floured that the parcels will burn in the pan. Repeat with the other two dough balls.

Prepare the börek by placing heaped tbsp of the chosen filling horizontally along the dough, approximately 8cm apart, starting 2cm up from the bottom and stopping halfway up the pastry, so that you can fold the unfilled dough over the other half.

Using a thin rolling pin, lift the dough up from the edge furthest away from you onto the rolling pin and lay it directly over the filled section of the pastry. Use the thinnest part of your hands to gently push down in between the filling portions to release any air that could get trapped in the pastry. Using a saucer or pastry cutter, cut around each mound of filling to create 6cm x 9cm parcels, ensuring that they’re as evenly shaped as possible.

For pan-fried saçta börek, heat a large, shallow frying pan over a low-medium heat. Once hot, add the börek to the dry pan and cook for a couple of minutes on each side until the pastry is cooked and the filling is soft and oozy. Drizzle with honey to serve.

name: Pan-Fried Salmon with Charred Corn & Chilli Lime Butter
description: Crispy-skinned salmon fillets sitting on a pile of deeply charred, buttery corn with punchy chilli, lime and a scatter of fresh coriander. On the table in half an hour.
keywords: Pan-Fried Salmon with Charred Corn & Chilli Lime Butter
Pan-Fried Salmon with Charred Corn & Chilli Lime Butter recipe
instructions: Heat a large dry frying pan over a very high heat until smoking. Cut the kernels from the corn cobs. Add the corn to the pan in a single layer (work in batches if needed) and cook without stirring for 3–4 mins until deeply charred underneath. Toss and cook for a further 2 mins until charred all over. Tip into a bowl and set aside.

Wipe out the pan and return to a medium heat. Add the butter and leave to melt until it begins to foam. Finely grate in the garlic, finely slice the chilli (saving a handful for garnish) and add both to the pan. Cook for 1–2 mins until fragrant and just golden. Add the charred corn back to the pan and toss well to coat in the butter. Zest and juice the limes straight in, season generously with salt and keep warm over a very low heat while you cook the salmon.

Pat the salmon fillets dry with kitchen paper and season generously on both sides with salt and black pepper. Set a frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of oil back to the pan and place the fillets in skin-side down. Press gently with a spatula for the first 30 seconds to prevent curling. Cook for 5-6 mins until the skin is deeply golden and crisp, then flip and cook for a further 1–2 mins — keeping the flesh slightly pink in the centre.
Meanwhile, reheat your microwave rice pouches according to packet instructions.

Finely slice the spring onions on the diagonal. Arrange the salmon on a large warmed platter or divide between plates. Spoon the charred corn and chilli lime butter generously over and around the fish. Scatter over the spring onions, the remaining lime cut into wedges, coriander leaves and remaining chilli and serve immediately.

name: Pan-Fried Soup Dumplings (Sheng Jian Bao)
description: If you're looking for something that'll impress, these soup dumplings are just the ticket. They're crunchy on the bottom, soft and fluffy on the top and filled with a steaming hot soup.
instructions: Slice the ginger and set aside. Combine all the ingredients except the gelatin leaves in a small saucepan and bring to the boil for 5 mins with a lid on just to infuse the aromatics into the liquid.
Meanwhile, soak the gelatin leaves in a bowl of cold water for 3 mins, until softened.

Take the saucepan off the heat. Squeeze the excess water from the gelatine leaves and mix the gelatin leaves into the soup until dissolved. Pour into a shallow pasta bowl and remove the ginger. When cooled, transfer to the freezer for 20 mins, then leave in the fridge for 1 hour or until needed. When the jelly is fully set, it should be very firm.
To make the wrappers combine the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Pour the warm water over the flour, then use the back of a wooden spoon to mix together until a dough forms.

Quickly work the dough on a flat surface (doing this quickly will stop the dough from sticking to your hands): slap the dough onto a flat surface, stretching the dough into a long rope, then form back into a ball and repeat for 2 mins, making sure not to break the rope – this is the key to fluffy dumplings later.

Coat a separate bowl and your hands with vegetable oil. Work the dough quickly to form a rough ball, then place it into the oiled bowl. Cover the bowl with a damp tea towel then wrap it in another tea towel and leave to rise in a warm place for 1 hour.

Mince the ginger and garlic and thinly slice the spring onions. Get the pork mince in a large mixing bowl along with all the remaining ingredients. Using a fork, mix in one direction until a big meatball forms. Cling film the bowl and chill until needed.

Now it’s time to incorporate the soup jelly. Remove the soup jelly from the fridge and use a knife to slice it into small cubes, roughly the size of peas. Scoop all the jelly into the dumpling filling and mix until evenly incorporated. Cover and refrigerate until needed.

Now it’s time to shape the buns: combine the dusting flour ingredients in a small bowl and set aside. Grab the dough, punch to deflate, then work it into a ball. Use your finger to poke a hole in the centre of the dough to create a doughnut shape. Then use a pair of scissors to make a single cut, revealing a log-shape. Roll out the log and divide into 13 pieces, roughly 30g each.
Sprinkle your work surface with dusting flour and shape each piece into balls. Cover with a damp tea towel and leave for 5 mins.

Sprinkle over more dusting flour and roll each piece into a circle around 10cm in circumference or the size of your palm and overlap each piece on a clean work surface and cover with a lightly damp tea towel.
Pour 2 tbsp of vegetable oil in a medium pan so it’s covering the whole surface.

Add a heaped tbsp of filling into a wrapper and tightly pleat the dough into a ball, ensuring there are no gaps. If you’re new to pleating: bring four edges of the wrapper together and pinch in the middle to create a four-petal flower-like shape, then pinch all the gaps to make a ball. As long as there are no holes, you will have delicious juicy dumplings.

Flip the dumpling so it’s seam-side down and place it on the outer edge of your pan. Repeat shaping and adding the dumplings in a circular pattern inside the pan, seam-side down. Cover the dumplings with a damp tea towel and leave in a warm place for 15 mins. Freeze any leftover filling for next time you’re making dumplings.
Meanwhile, prep the garnish: finely slice the spring onions and get the sesame seeds in a small bowl near the stove top.

Cover the dumplings in enough room temp water so the tops are just poking out. Now turn the heat to medium high, with a lid on, just until it begins to boil, then reduce the heat to medium and cook for 10 mins. Most of the water should be evaporated. Sprinkle over the spring onions, sesame seeds and a drizzle of vegetable oil then cook with a lid on for another 30 seconds. Use a spatula to check the bottoms are golden brown, then turn off the heat.

Soak a tea towel with cold water and place it on a work surface with the hot pan on top; it will create steam and help release the dumplings. Use a spatula to release the dumplings from the edge of the pan then flip them onto a plate.
Serve with black Chinese vinegar, or combine a 3:1 ratio of rice vinegar to soy sauce. Drizzle with chilli oil and pull apart to eat!

name: Pan-Roasted Chicken Thighs with Herby Rice & Pickled Salad
description: Mad about crispy chicken skin? Follow this recipe for the crispiest ever chicken thighs. We've served them with a pickled salad and a mound of herby rice.
keywords: Pan-Roasted Chicken Thighs with Herby Rice & Pickled Salad
instructions: Ask your butcher to debone the thighs, or do it yourself by using a small, sharp knife to slice lengthways either side of the bone and then carefully work your way around each end.

Season the thighs all over with salt and leave to come up to room temperature. Place the thighs skin-side down in a heavy-based frying pan and then turn the heat to low-medium. Once they begin to sizzle, cook the thighs for about 15 mins, skin-side down. As they come up to temperature, the fat will render from under the skin and it will turn golden brown and crispy.

Meanwhile, get the rice on. There are lots of ways to cook basmati rice, but my favourite is to add a 2:1 ratio of water to (well rinsed) rice, bring it to the boil, turn the heat to a low simmer, cover with a lid and cook for 10 mins. Turn the heat off and leave to steam for a few minutes.
Meanwhile, finely slice the cucumber, red onion and chilli and add to a bowl with the vinegar and sugar. Stir well and set aside.
Finely dice the shallots and finely chop the herbs. Set aside.

By now the chicken should have been cooking for about 15 mins and the rice for about 12 mins (including steaming time). Turn the rice off and leave it to steam. Flip the chicken thighs to cook the top – they will be almost cooked through, so this will only take about 2 mins.

Remove the thighs and set them aside on a plate to rest for a few minutes. Meanwhile, add the shallots to the chicken fat in the pan and cook for 2 mins until soft. Tip the shallots, any remaining chicken fat, three-quarters of the herbs and the juice of 1 lemon into the rice. Mix well.
Plate up a mound of rice, slice the chicken thighs into nice thick slices and lay them on top, then finish with a pile of the pickled salad. Top with the remaining fresh herbs and a wedge of lemon.

name: Pancetta, Leek & Goats’ Cheese Potato Frittata
description: This potato frittata has all the makings of a banging meal. Protein-packed to keep you fuller for longer with tangy, creamy goats’ cheese, sweet leeks and salty pancetta. This recipe is the ultimate weekend breakfast or brunch – a meal that’ll really keep you going throughout the day. Any leftovers make a great take-to-work lunch or late-night dish straight from the fridge.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Cut the new potatoes into 1cm rounds. Drop into the boiling water and cook for 6 mins, then drain into a colander and leave to steam dry.

Meanwhile, tip the pancetta into a large, ovenproof, high-sided frying pan with a splash of olive oil set over a medium-high heat. Fry, stirring occasionally for 6-8 mins until the fat has rendered and the pancetta is crisp.

Halve the leeks lengthwise, wash, then finely slice. Add the leeks to the pan with the pancetta, along with another 2 tsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally until the leeks have completely collapsed and softened.
Heat your grill to high.

Meanwhile, finely chop the garlic cloves and strip the thyme leaves from the sprigs. Crack the eggs into a jug and whisk well with a fork until the yolk and white are fully combined. Season with salt and a generous amount of black pepper.

Add the garlic and thyme to the pan with the leeks, cook for 1 min more, then tip in the potatoes. Cook, stirring for a couple more minutes, then press everything into a compact layer and pour in the beaten egg.

Swirl the pan so that the beaten egg is evenly coating all the filling, then dot the goats’ cheese across the top. Slide the frittata under the grill for 4-5 mins until the egg has just set with the slightest wobble in the middle. Leave until cool enough to slice and serve with a balsamic-dressed salad. Yum.

name: Paneer, Courgette and Chilli Fritters
description: These Apetina paneer fritters are the ultimate brunch dish by Crystelle pereira. Topped with a perfect runny egg, this has Sunday morning written all over it.
instructions: In a dry pan, toast the sesame seeds on a low heat for 5 mins until fragrant. Leave to oneside.
Grate courgette and place in a large sieve over the sink/a bowl.
Grate Apetina paneer, ginger and garlic in a bowl.
Finely dice one chilli, 2 spring onions and add to the paneer mixture, along with the toastedsesame seeds and chilli flakes. Mix until combined.
Press out as much water as you can from the courgette, then add it to the paneer mixture.
Finally add in the flour and mix together.
In a separate bowl, beat 2 eggs with salt, pepper, gochujang and soy sauce until wellcombined. Add this to the paneer mixture.

Heat up roughly 2 tablespoons of coconut oil in a frying pan on medium heat, then add 4large tablespoons of the paneer mixture and flatten them out to form four even-sized fritters.Fry for 3 mins on each side.
Then, add some more coconut oil to the pan, and fry two eggs.
Arrange fritters on a plate and squeeze over some lime juice. Top them with your fried eggsand garnish with sesame seeds, spring onions and more chilli flakes if desired.

name: Paprika & Sun-Dried Tomato Beans with Tofu Feta
description: We use this mix of cherry toms, garlic and paprika in a plant-based full English breakfasts instead of ketchup. It’s delightfully flavoursome, fresh, smoky and sweet. Paired with beans and tofu feta, it makes the perfect high-protein dinner.
keywords: Paprika & Sun-Dried Tomato Beans with Tofu Feta
Paprika & Sun-Dried Tomato Beans with Tofu Feta recipe
instructions: For the tofu feta, crumble the tofu into a medium bowl and add the remaining ingredients. Stir well to combine. Season to taste and transfer to the fridge while you make the beans.
Dice the red onion, crush the garlic, halve the tomatoes and finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes.

Add a splash of olive oil to a large sauté pan. Once the oil is hot, add in the onion and fry over a medium heat with a small pinch of salt for 7-8 mins. Add the garlic and fry for 2-3 mins, then add the smoked paprika and fry for 1 min. Add the sundried tomatoes, stir, then add the cherry tomatoes and a pinch of sea salt. Cook for around 10 mins, stirring regularly, until you can squish them down into the pan to make a jammy sauce.

Pour two to three tablespoons of liquid out of the beans cans, then tip them into the pan with the remaining canning liquid. Stir and heat through, then add the basil and nutritional yeast. Cook over a medium heat for 5 mins, then season to taste.
Serve with the tofu feta and optional toppings.

name: Paprika Butter Eggs
description: Poached eggs? Greek yoghurt? Beautiful browned Paprika butter? This simple recipe has got it all. A quick meal that can be eaten at any point of the day.
instructions: Thinly slice the garlic. Melt the butter in a small pan and cook whilst swirling for around 8 mins, until the milk solids have browned and it smells nutty and looks a bit foamy. Add the sliced garlic and paprika, then remove from the heat.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat and halve the lemon. Add it face down to the hot pan and cook for 3-4 mins until charred and sticky. Once it's cool enough to handle, squeeze the juice into the yoghurt and season well with salt and pepper.

Heat a small pot of water and make a small whirlpool using a utensil. Sieve the eggs to remove the wispy bits and then tip into the middle of the vortex. Reduce the heat and cook for 5 min until the whites have set but the yolks still runny. In the meantime, slice and toast the sourdough and top with the lemony yoghurt. Top each slice with two poached eggs, drizzle with garlicky brown butter, and garnish with dill and a pinch of sumac, if you like.

name: Paprika Chicken & Chorizo Toasted Wrap
description: This wrap is absolutely bursting with flavour, thanks to the juicy, paprika chicken that pairs perfectly with the chorizo. Toasting wraps is honestly revolutionary and just helps all of the flavours melt together. It’s perfect for a high-protein lunch that everyone in the family can enjoy.
keywords: Paprika Chicken & Chorizo Toasted Wrap recipe
instructions: Dice the chicken into small chunks, approximately 1-2cm wide. Finely dice the onion and finally slice the chorizo into discs, then chop each disc into quarters.

Put the onion, chorizo and chicken into a non-stick frying pan set over a medium heat. Sprinkle the paprika over the chicken and fry for around 10 mins until the onion has softened and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the tomato purée, then remove from the heat. Tip the mixture into a bowl with the soft cheese and mozzarella, then mix well.
Heat the wrap in a microwave, then scoop the mixture into the centre of the wrap. Fold either side in and then roll it up, tucking it under as you go so it holds together nicely.

Reheat the pan that you just used, then pop the wrap in, spreading the remaining bits of the mixture on top for extra crispiness! Cook for a few minutes each side over a medium heat until golden and crispy.⁣
Leave to cool for 5 mins, then cut in half and enjoy.

name: Paprika Garlic Chicken Flatbreads With Whipped Feta
description: Juicy paprika-spiced chicken, creamy feta yoghurt and punchy tomato salad on toasted flatbreads. Absolute weeknight win.
keywords: Paprika Garlic Chicken Flatbreads With Whipped Feta
Paprika Garlic Chicken Flatbreads With Whipped Feta recipe
instructions: Peel and grate the garlic into a bowl. Stir in the paprika and Greek yoghurt. Cut the chicken into 2–3cm chunks and add to the bowl with a pinch of salt. Mix well to coat.
If using skewers, thread on the chicken and grill under a hot grill for 6 mins, flip and cook for another 2 mins until charred and cooked through. Alternatively, air fry at 220°C for 8-10 mins.
Finely slice the red onion and mix with a pinch of salt, lemon juice and sumac, if using. Set aside to pickle slightly.
Quarter the cherry tomatoes and chop the cucumber into bite-sized chunks. Add to the onions and mix well.
In a small bowl, crumble in the feta and stir through the remaining yoghurt until combined. Season to taste.
Toast the flatbreads in a dry pan or under the grill until warm and slightly charred.
To serve, spread the feta-yoghurt mixture over the flatbreads, pile on the paprika chicken, then spoon over the tomato salad. Finish with fresh parsley, mint, dried oregano and a lemon wedge.

name: Paprika Pork Chop With Sweet & Sour Peppers
description: Sweet and sour peppers cut through the richness of the pork chop in this recipe like a hot knife through butter. Unbeatable.
keywords: Paprika Pork Chop With Sweet & Sour Peppers
Paprika Pork Chop With Sweet & Sour Peppers recipe
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Add the fregola and cook for 10 mins until cooked through. Drain and rise and set aside.

Cut the peppers into strips and thinly slice the onions and garlic cloves. Preheat a large frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add a splash of olive oil and drop in the peppers and onions. Add a pinch of salt and stir. Scrunch the bay leaves in your hand and drop them in.

Now cover your frying pan with a lid, this will simultaneously steam and sauté the peppers and onions. Shake the pan now and then and keep everything moving. After about 5 mins over high heat, the peppers and onions should be starting to soften and pick up a little colour. The pan should also smell like bay leaves!
Add the garlic and cook for another 2-3 mins before sprinkling in the sugar and sherry vinegar. Stir to coat the onions and peppers and then remove from the heat.

Season the pork chops with salt and dust with the paprika. Rub with a little olive oil and add to a cold pan, fat-side down. Set over a medium-high heat and begin rendering the fat, this should take 3-4 mins. Once the fat is brown and crispy, sear each side of the pork chops and drop in the rosemary. Keep cooking the pork chops for 5-6 mins or until they’re medium.
Remove the pork chops from the pan and rest on a plate, pouring over the rosemary and any juice from the pan.

Tip the fregola into a bowl. Finely chop the parsley and add to the bowl along with a big pinch of salt and a splash of olive oil. Spread the yogurt onto the base of the plates, top with the herby fregola and the sweet and sour peppers and onions, and top with a pork chop. Get stuck in.

name: Paprika Prawns & Garlicky Mashed Beans
description: Smoky paprika prawns on a bed of creamy garlicky beans. High in protein and ready in under 30 mins.
instructions: Zest the lemon and set aside. Thinly slice the chilli and half of the garlic. Pick the parsley leaves and finely slice the soft stalks.
Devein the prawns if you like, then set aside.
Place a saucepan over a medium heat. Pour in the beans with their liquid and grate the remaining garlic. Bring to the boil for 2-3 mins, then reduce to a low simmer while you cook the prawns.

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the parsley stalks, sliced garlic and three-quarters of the chilli. Cook for 1-2 mins until softened, then chuck in the cherry tomatoes. Cook for 5-7 mins, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes burst.
Add the prawns and smoked paprika to the pan. Stir through and cook for 2-3 mins, until the prawns are cooked through. Season with salt, pepper, lemon zest and lemon juice.

Meanwhile, lightly mash the beans in the saucepan. Stir through the cottage cheese and season to taste with salt, pepper, lemon zest and more juice, if you like. Add a splash of water for a looser consistency.
Spoon the garlicky mashed beans into bowls. Top with the paprika prawns and pan juices. Finish with parsley leaves, the remaining chilli and a wedge of lemon on the side.

name: Paprika Salmon with Brown Rice & Spicy Chorizo Dressing
description: Sticky paprika salmon, tossed through punchy rice with sweet peppers and peas. Add crispy chorizo dressing for a fiery grown-up upgrade.
instructions: Finely chop the shallots and garlic. Dice the roasted red peppers.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the shallots and garlic with a small pinch of salt and cook for 5-6 mins until soft and golden.

Stir in a third of the smoked paprika, then add the sun-dried tomato paste and chopped red peppers. Tip in the pouch of wholegrain rice and the frozen peas. Stir everything together and cook for another couple of minutes until heated through.

Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Cut the salmon into chunky pieces. Drizzle with olive oil and toss with the remaining smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Lay the salmon pieces on a foil-lined baking tray. Grill for 4 mins, then flip and grill for another 3-4 mins until cooked through and slightly charred.

While the salmon grills, finely dice the chorizo and scrape it into a dry frying pan set over a medium heat. Cook for 5-6 mins until crisp and the oil has turned deep red. Stir in the sherry vinegar, then remove from the heat.

Serve up! Scoop the rice and peas into bowls.Kids Plate: Flake over the salmon and mix it through. Adults Plate: Top with a piece of salmon. Spoon the chorizo dressing over the top and finish with torn basil leaves.

name: Paprika, Red Pesto & Sausage Rigatoni
description: A very simple weeknight recipe with a rich sauce made from shallot, crumbled sausages, garlic, tomato purée, paprika and cream. Finish with basil and bon app.
instructions: Finely dice the shallot and thinly slice the garlic. Score the skins of the sausages open. Heat the oil in a pan and add the shallots, cooking until translucent, then add the garlic and crumble in the sausage meat. Cook until the sausage is crispy and golden, around 5-7 mins.
Meanwhile, add all the pesto ingredients into a blender with the juice of the lemon and blitz together.

Bring a large pan of water to the boil and cook the rigatoni according to pack instructions. Drain, reserving some pasta water. Grate the parmesan. Add the cooked pasta directly to the sausage pan, then add the pesto. Add a good slosh of pasta water and mix vigorously until emulsified. Pick the basil leaves and add most of them to the pan, along with the cream and seasoning.
Serve in bowls and finish with extra parmesan and fresh basil, if you like.

name: Paratha (Flaky Flatbreads)
description: We researched all sorts of flaky flatbreads you find in the world (paratha, buss up shut, roti, meloui, msemen) to find the best technique to make the flakiest flatbreads.
instructions: Add the flour, baking powder and salt into a bowl, mix together well. Then add the water and ghee and bring the dough together. Let rest for 15-20 mins.
Knead the dough until smooth and portion into 8 balls, place on a greased baking tray, cover and rest for 1 hour.

On a lightly floured surface, flatten the dough slightly with the heel of your hand, then lightly flour and roll out into a circle, it should be around 1-2mm thick. Brush with some melted ghee, dust with a pinch of flour and roll up into a long log. Coil each end of the log inwards (like a snail’s shell) until they meet and stack them onto each other. Press down firmly and repeat with the remaining balls of dough. Place back onto the baking tray, cover and let rest for a minimum of 1 hour.

Once rested, place a frying pan over medium-high heat. Lightly grease a surface and a rolling pin. Flatten the coiled up dough balls, then roll out into 0.7cm-1cm thick circles. Place on the hot frying pan and cook on both sides until translucent, golden brown, and crispy in parts. Transfer to a clean kitchen towel, lightly brush with more ghee and crumple the flatbread until flaky, continue this process with all the dough balls. Cover the flatbreads with the tea towel to let them steam whilst cooking the rest.

name: Parma Ham Carbonara
description: When you fry Parma ham, the flavour completely changes. It is saltier and nuttier; the perfect thing to add to a carbonara.
instructions: Into a bowl, add egg yolks and grated parmesan, with a generous amount of black pepper. Mix with a fork and set aside.
Get your pasta on and salt the water. Reserve 8 tbsp of pasta water.

Slice your Parma ham into strips and place into a frying pan and fry until crisp and set aside. Chop up your garlic. Add to pan, and cook until translucent. Then re-add the cooked ham and mix together. Add 2 tbsp of pasta water to the pan and bubble.
Once pasta is al dente, drain and add it to your ham. Take the pan off the heat. Fold the Parma ham through the pasta.

Add the egg mixture and 3 more tbsp of pasta water. Keep folding it together and adding pasta water until it becomes thick and creamy. Keep adding the pasta water gradually if it needs to be creamier.
Chop up your chives and add this to the pan and toss everything together. Serve with lots of cracked black pepper on top! Enjoy.

name: Parmesan Brussels Sprouts
description: These Parmesan-crusted sprouts are made with just three ingredients and are absolutely packed with flavour. We’ll be serving them on the side of everything all sprout season-long.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Trim the bottoms off your sprouts and halve them lengthways.
Line a baking tray with baking parchment and grate over the Parmesan in a thin layer. Drizzle with olive oil and place the sprouts on top, cut side down. Drizzle more olive oil over the top.
Roast in the oven for 25 mins until the sprouts are golden and crispy.

name: Parmesan Carrots
description: These Parmesan baked carrots are perfect for meal prep. Combine them with your choice of protein, carb and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel the carrots, halve them lengthwise, then chop into smaller chunks. Transfer to a bowl, then drizzle over 1 tbsp oil. Add the paprika, garlic granules, onion granules and 1 tsp salt, then toss to combine. Grate the Parmesan, and then set it aside.

Spread the Parmesan over a large, shallow plate. Tip the carrots on top, then coat them in the Parmesan really well. Lay the carrots, flat-side down, onto a lightly oiled baking tray. Bake in the oven for 25 mins.
Serve hot and enjoy! Or, if batch cooking for the meat, let the carrots cool then transfer to a container and store in the fridge until ready to serve.

name: Parmesan Carrots With Hot Honey Mayo
description: These Parmesan baked carrots are the ultimate dinner party side dish. Sweet, sticky, and just the right level of cheesy.
keywords: Parmesan Carrots With Hot Honey Mayo
Parmesan Carrots With Hot Honey Mayo recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel the carrots, halve them lengthwise, then chop into smaller chunks. Transfer to a bowl, then drizzle over 1 tbsp oil. Add the paprika, garlic granules, onion granules and 1 tsp salt, then toss to combine. Grate the Parmesan, and then set it aside.

Spread the Parmesan over a large, shallow plate. Tip the carrots on top, then coat them in the Parmesan really well. Lay the carrots, flat-side down, onto a lightly oiled baking tray. Bake in the oven for 25 mins.
Meanwhile, combine the mayo, honey and chilli oil in a small bowl.
Serve the crispy Parmesan carrots with the hot honey mayo on the side.

name: Parmesan Cauliflower Steaks
description: This dish is a beautiful way of using the entirety of a cauliflower. Served with a gorgeous cauliflower leaf pistachio pesto. Another winner with Ocado.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/400°F.
Cut the leaves off your cauliflower. Cut each vertically down the middle of its stalk. Trim away the edges so that you have two steaks. Save the cauliflower leaves.
Place your cauliflower steaks on a baking tray and rub each steak with salt, pepper and olive oil. Roast for 30 mins.
Remove your cauliflower steaks from the oven and flip them over. Grate over 45g of parmesan onto the steaks, then return to the oven for 10 mins.
Finely chop your cauliflower leaves.
Bring a pan of water to a boil. Add salt, then tip in the scraps of your cauliflower and cauliflower leaves. Simmer for 5 mins until tender, then drain and allow to cool.

Once your boiled cauliflower bits are cool, tip it all into a food processor. Add your basil, 40g of your pistachios and your remaining parmesan, then blitz until you have a smooth paste. Add 200ml olive oil and lemon juice then blitz until smooth again. Add more olive oil until you have the sauce at a drizzle-able consistency. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Finely slice your chillies. Toast your remaining pistachios, then finely chop them.
Arrange your cauliflower steaks on a plate. Drizzle with your sauce, then sprinkle with your sliced chillies and chopped pistachios. Serve and enjoy.

name: Parmesan Cauliflower Steaks With Pistachio Pesto
description: This dish is a beautifully simple way of using up the entirety of a cauliflower. Served with a gorgeous cauliflower leaf and pistachio pesto.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Cut the leaves off the cauliflowers, then cut each one vertically
down the middle of its stalk. Trim away the edges so that you end
up with four steaks. Save the cauliflower leaves and the offcuts/
scraps.
Place the cauliflower steaks onto a baking tray and rub each one
with salt, pepper and 1 teaspoon of olive oil. Roast for 30 mins,
then remove from the oven and flip them over. Grate 45g of
the Parmesan over the steaks, then return to the oven for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, finely chop the cauliflower leaves.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Add salt, then tip in the
scraps of cauliflower and the leaves. Simmer for 5 mins until
tender, then drain and allow to cool.
Add the cooled cauliflower pieces and leaves to a food processor
along with the basil, two-thirds of the pistachios and the remaining
Parmesan, then blitz until you have a smooth paste. Add the 4 tbsp of olive oil and the juice of the lemon then blitz
again; stir in just enough water to make the sauce a drizzle-able
consistency. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Toast the remaining pistachios in a dry frying pan over a medium
heat until smelling toasty, then finely chop them. Thinly slice the
chillies.
Arrange the cauliflower steaks on two plates. Drizzle with the
pesto, then sprinkle with the sliced chillies and chopped pistachios.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Parmesan Chicken Salad
description: This salad is all about the dressing – yoghurt, parmesan and lemon. Tangy, cheesy, salty and fresh. Pour it all over this bountiful salad and enjoy.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180ºC/356°F.

Whack your chicken fillets into a baking tray, drizzle oil over them, and season them with salt and pepper. Massage them slightly and flip them over so they’re evenly seasoned. Pop your full head of garlic in the centre of the baking tray, between the fillets and then roast this for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile in a medium bowl, combine your Greek yoghurt, 4 tbsp of olive oil, the juice of a lemon, your parmesan, and salt and pepper. Add 2 tbsp of water and mix everything together. This will make a thick creamy dressing.

Once cooked through, remove your chicken from the oven and remove the garlic from the baking tray. Take the garlic and crush the whole head with the flat of a large knife. This will naturally allow the skin to peel off, but make sure it’s all removed from the fleshy interior before chopping this up finely until it forms a chunky paste. Stir this into your cheesy dressing.

Using two forks, shred your chicken in its tray and allow it to sit whilst you prep your veg. Separate the leaves from your baby gem lettuces and slice your radishes, then carefully dice your avocado. Add all to a large salad bowl, along with your shredded chicken and basil leaves. Top this off with your cheesy dressing and mix it all together. Tuck in MOB, this one’s a winner.

name: Parmesan Chicken With Lemony Fennel Salad
description: We've partnered up juicy chicken breasts with nutty quinoa and a fresh yoghurt dressing. A real protein-packed dinner.
instructions: Roast your garlic for around 25-30 mins. Cook quinoa according to package instructions and drain the chickpeas. Finely slice the fennel (use a mandolin if you have one) and roughly chop the parsley.

Zest 1/2 of the lemon. Add the yoghurt and lemon zest to a large bowl along with the squeezed out roasted garlic bulbs. Whisk well and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Add the cooked quinoa, chickpeas, fennel and parsley before giving it a good stir.

Take the chicken and season on both sides with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the chicken breasts, cooking for 7-8 mins on each side, until golden and cooked through (depending on the size of the breast you might need more or less time). Remove from the pan and set aside for 5 mins, then shave the Parmesan into pieces.
Serve up a big portion of fennel salad, top with the chicken and Parmesan.

name: Parmesan Churros & Marinara Sauce
description: Ever tried savoury churros? How about savoury churros made with a Parm-infused dough? We're salivating just thinking about them.
instructions: Start by making the sauce. Finely dice the shallots and garlic cloves. Preheat a medium saucepan over a high heat and add a good glug of oil. Tip in the shallots with a big pinch of salt and cook until translucent. Drop the heat to medium and add the garlic and chilli.
Cook for 2-3 mins then add the tomatoes. Bring to a simmer and cook for 14-15 mins until reduced and the oil is starting to split out. Season and set aside.
For the churros, dice the butter into small cubes. Combine the butter, 6g of salt and 5g of sugar in a saucepan with 200ml of water.
Bring to a boil and add the flour. Cook over a medium heat, beating vigorously for 2-3 mins until the sides of the pan are clean. Transfer the dough to a clean bowl.
Keep beating the dough for a min or so to let it cool down. Finely grate in 50g of Parmesan and beat into the dough.
Now beat in the eggs one by one until you have a smooth, glossy choux paste.
Transfer to a piping bag with a star nozzle. Preheat a pot of oil to 180°C.
Pipe the mix into the hot oil, snipping off with scissors at the length you’d like and fry for 2-3 mins until golden brown.
Season the warm churros with salt and pepper, and serve topped with the dill and some extra Parmesan. Finish the platter with a few wedges of lemon and a pot of the marinara for dipping.

name: Parmesan Fried Egg With Jalapeño Salsa
description: This fried egg with a crisp cheese skirt is one of our favourite egg recipes. Which is saying something. We like it just on its own with a dash of Worcestershire sauce plus an additional dash of a hot sauce
instructions: Make the salsa first by finely dicing the shallot and jalapeño before combining them in a small bowl. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and leave for 5 mins, before stirring in the lime juice, olive oil and finely chopped coriander.

Coarsely grate the mature cheddar and finely grate the Parmesan. When you’re ready to eat, arrange the cheddar in a fried-egg-sized pile in a well-seasoned cast-iron or other non-stick pan and set it over a medium heat. Scatter the Parmesan over the top. Make an indent in the middle as a landing spot.

Crack the egg into the target area before the cheese is fully melted, then fry for 2 ½ mins (or a tiny bit longer) until the cheese is golden and crisping. Remove from the heat before anything burns. If the egg white is not quite set, leave in the hot pan for 30–60 seconds more.
Once off the heat, allow the cheese to cool and harden for 30-60 seconds more, warming the tortilla in a dry pan over a medium-high heat while you wait.
Use a fish slice or spatula to carefully prize the egg and its crispy cheesy skirt from the pan, and transfer onto the warm tortilla.
Spoon salsa liberally all over, fold in half and eat immediately. You’ll have some salsa leftover. Make another?

name: Parmesan Rösti With Hot Sauce Eggs
description: Soaking your potatoes in water expels some of the starch and enables your röstis to get super crispy. The longer you leave them, the crispier your röstis will be.
keywords: Parmesan Rösti With Hot Sauce Eggs
Parmesan Rösti With Hot Sauce Eggs recipe
instructions: Peel and grate your potatoes on the coarsest grater you can find. Pop the grated potato into a bowl and cover with cold water. Add a tbsp of salt, then leave to soak for 30 mins.
Heat your oven to 160°C.
Coarsely grate your onion and finely grate your Parmesan.
Line a colander with a clean tea towel. Tip in your grated potato, then gather the top of the tea towel up to tighten the whole thing up into a ball. Squeeze out all the excess liquid you can.
Tip your dried potato into a bowl, then add your grated onion and three-quarters of your Parmesan. Add a pinch of salt and a generous grinding of black pepper, then mix to combine with your hands.

Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a frying pan. Add small handfuls of your potato mixture a couple at a time, pushing down on them with a spatula to flatten them. Fry for about 3 mins on each side until they are super crispy and golden.
Keep your röstis warm on a tray in the oven whilst you cook the rest.

When all your röstis are cooked, move onto your eggs. In the same pan, crack in your eggs. Sprinkle them with a little salt, and fry for about 2 mins. The base should get very golden, and the whites should bubble up nicely
Finely chop your chives.
Put two röstis on each plate, and top with your fried egg. Sprinkle over your remaining Parmesan and chives, then pour over your hot sauce. Enjoy!

name: Parmesan Sprouts
description: Crispy and lemony parmesan sprouts. So simple and perfect alongside your roast dinner.
keywords: delicious ways of using Brussels sprouts
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Cut all the Brussels sprouts in half and toss with olive oil and salt.
Pop these onto a baking tray cut side-down and bake for 30 mins, turning halfway through, until caramelised and crisp.
Grate the parmesan over the sprouts and then pop the tray back into the oven for 5 mins until the cheese melts.
Finely chop the parsley.
Pour the sprouts into a bowl and grate over more parmesan, lemon zest, orange zest and sprinkle over the parsley.

name: Parsley Pesto Linguine
description: This delicious creamy walnut and parsley pesto is totally plant-based, simple and delicious. A perfect way to use up old herbs for a delicious dinner.
keywords: Creamy walnut and parsley linguine recipe
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook your pasta until al dente.
Grate the garlic clove into your food processor (it won't break down enough if you just blend it). Add the walnuts, reserving a few for garnish, and blitz until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Add the parsley, removing any big stalks, and 100ml of olive oil and blend until smooth.
Once the pasta is ready, drain and reserve a large mug of the cooking water.
Toss the pesto and pasta together along with the juice of the lemon, adding pasta water as you go until you have a smooth and creamy sauce.
Season with salt and pepper and plate up, finishing with a few more chunks of walnuts and a sprinkle of parsley.

name: Parsley Sauce
description: A classic, silky and delicious parsley sauce. Amazing with white fish, poultry and pork. Especially good with mashed potato, ham and peas.
instructions: Pick and finely chop the leaves from the parsley stalks.

Melt the butter in a medium saucepan set over a medium heat. Once melted, add the flour and whisk into a loose paste. Cook the paste over a medium heat, constantly stirring, for 1-2 mins until you get a golden colour and biscuity aroma. The goal here is to just cook out the raw flour.
Slowly add the milk a little at a time and whisk constantly until you have a smooth sauce and all the milk is incorporated.

Turn the heat off and whisk in the Dijon mustard and Worcestershire sauce. Season with lemon juice and salt to taste. Finish by stirring through the chopped parsley. The sauce should be glossy and pourable. If it is too thick, just add a little warm water until you achieve the desired consistency.
Serve warm. If making in advance, keep the sauce in the fridge for up to three days or in the freezer for up to a month. Defrost overnight in the fridge and gently reheat over a low heat.

name: Parsnip Mash Recipe
description: Bored of spud mash? Parsnips make for a richer, nuttier mash that works well with anything you would usually serve the old faithful with. A delightful and nutritious alternative to traditional mashed potatoes, this parsnip mash offers a subtly sweet and earthy flavour. This parsnip mash recipe showcases the creamy texture and rich taste of parsnips, perfect for elevating any meal. Whether you're preparing a cosy family dinner or planning a festive Christmas dinner, this side dish is sure to impress. The recipe is simple yet versatile, allowing you to add your favourite seasonings or mix in complementary ingredients like garlic, butter, or fresh herbs. With its smooth consistency and delicious flavour, parsnip mash makes an excellent accompaniment to roasted meats, veggie dishes, or as a base for savoury gravies. Ideal for both everyday meals and special occasions, this parsnip mash is a must-try for anyone looking to add a unique and flavourful twist to their side dish repertoire.
instructions: Peel the parsnips and cut into even, chunky pieces. Fill a pan with boiling salted water and carefully add the parsnips. Cook for 15 mins until the parsnips are cooked through but not collapsing.

Drain the parsnips using a colander, then tip them back into the pan. Add the cream and butter, then season with salt and plenty of cracked black pepper. Use a potato masher to mash the parsnips to the texture you prefer. You can keep mashing for a smoother finish, or go for a rough crush – up to you.
Season with salt and pepper again and serve.

name: Parsnip Purée Recipe
description: This smooth-as-silk parsnip purée recipe is incredibly easy to make and is a great accompaniment to most grilled or roast meats. A swoosh on the bottom of your plate will make you feel like René Redzepi, or that handsome guy in The Bear. Parsnip purée is a luxurious and velvety side dish that elevates any meal with its subtly sweet and nutty flavour. This parsnip purée recipe transforms humble root vegetables into a creamy delight that pairs beautifully with a variety of main courses. Whether you’re serving a traditional Thanksgiving dinner, a festive Christmas feast, or a comforting Sunday roast, this puree will add a sophisticated touch. Ideal alongside roasted meats like schnitzel or meatloaf, or even with a delicate fish dish, it’s a versatile addition to your culinary repertoire. Blended with garlic cloves and a touch of cream or plant-based milk, the puree achieves a silky texture and rich taste.
instructions: Peel the parsnips and cut into even, chunky pieces. Fill a pan with boiling salted water and carefully add the parsnips. Cook for 15 mins until the parsnips are cooked through but not collapsing.
Meanwhile, put the double cream into a small saucepan with the garlic clove, thyme sprigs and black peppercorns and gently bring to the boil. Once boiling, remove from the heat and set aside.
Once the parsnips are cooked, strain them through a colander, then tip into a food processor or blender.

Put a fine metal sieve over the processor or blender and pour in half the flavoured cream. Season with salt and pepper. Whizz the parsnip until really smooth, then add enough of the remaining flavoured cream to create a velvety smooth purée.

If you want to be super fancy and restaurant-y, discard the garlic and thyme from the sieve and put the sieve over a bowl. Strain the purée through the sieve, into the bowl, pushing it through. Season to taste and serve.

name: Pasilla Beef & Black Bean Chilli Crunchy Tacos
description: Rich, tangy Pasilla chillies bring a real depth of flavour to these hard shell beef tacos. Make them for family or friends and watch them disappear.
keywords: crunchy tacos with pasilla beef and black bean chilli
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C/160°C fan.
Thinly slice ½ the red onion and place in a bowl. Pour over boiling water to cover the onions then drain. Squeeze over the juice of ½ the lime and add a pinch of salt.

Cut the remaining red onion into 4 wedges and dry fry in a large pan over a medium heat, along with the unpeeled garlic cloves and cherry tomatoes, for about 6-8 mins until lightly charred. Remove to a small bowl.
Stem and deseed the Pasilla chilli. Add to the dry pan for a minute then remove from the heat and add to the small bowl with the other charred ingredients.

Add boiling water to the same bowl, just enough to cover the charred ingredients, and leave for 5 mins then drain and reserve the liquid. Discard the garlic skins (they should slip off) and transfer the rest of the solid ingredients to a blender. Blitz to a smooth purée with a splash of the soaking liquid and a big pinch of salt.

Heat ½ of the olive oil in a pan over a moderate heat then fry the mince off until the liquid evaporates and the meat begins to brown. Add the ground spices to the mince and fry off for 30 seconds, then add the blended Pasilla and onion paste to the mince and fry for another 2 mins.

Add 2 tbsp of the soaking water, cover with a lid and simmer gently over a low-medium heat for about 25-30 mins, adding a splash more water if you think the pan needs it, until the sauce is thick and flavourful and the mince is melting and tender.

Meanwhile, slice the red and green peppers. Heat the remaining olive oil in a separate large frying pan over a medium-high heat, add the peppers and fry for 5-7 mins until soft and slightly caramelised. Add salt and pepper to taste then set aside.
Drain the beans and stir into the beef along with the chocolate. Leave to warm through for a few minutes, adding salt and plenty of black pepper to taste.
Fill each taco shell with spoonfuls of the Pasilla beef mince, followed by some sautéed peppers and bake in the oven for around 10 mins to warm through.
Meanwhile, crush the crunchy corn, crumble the feta and thinly slice the jalapeño chilli.
