Serve the filled taco shells sprinkled with the pink onions, feta cheese, crunchy corn, coriander leaves and sliced chilli, along with a drizzle of the sour cream and a dash of hot sauce if you like. Serve the remaining lime, cut into wedges, on the side for squeezing over the tacos.

name: Pasta Alla Gricia
description: What do you get if you take the eggs out of a carbonara or add guanciale to a cacio e pepe? This Pasta alla Gricia is one of our favourite Roman classics.
instructions: Place a large pan of water onto boil, add salt until it tastes slightly salty.
Using the guanciale or pancetta straight from the fridge will make it easier to cut. Slice into ¼ inch-thick lardons and set aside.
Add your pasta to the boiling water. Whilst the pasta cooks, place a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the guanciale. If using pancetta, add a drizzle of olive oil too.
Grate the pecorino into a bowl. Take a few tbsp of the pasta water and add them to the cheese, then mix into a paste.
Cook the guanciale for 5 to 7 mins until it’s golden brown and a good amount of the fat has rendered out. Add a tsp of ground black pepper during the last minute of cooking.

By this point, your pasta should still be only three-quarters of the way cooked. Add a big ladleful of the cooking water to the pan with the guanciale before draining and add the pasta (reserve another mug of the pasta cooking water).

Toss continuously to emulsify the pasta water and fat from the guanciale until you have a creamy starchy mixture. Add the cheese and continue to mix and toss, adding more water as needed until you have a glossy sauce.
Serve with a little more black pepper.

name: Pasta Frittata
description: Go to the beach in Naples and you’ll see kids eating slices of ‘a frittata 'e maccarune’. It’s the perfect use for leftover pasta, Jordon x
instructions: Cook the bucatini in boiling salted water until al dente.
Meanwhile, fry the pancetta until golden brown, set aside.
Dice the mozzarella and add to a large bowl. To the same bowl, add the eggs, cooked pancetta, parmesan, a pinch of salt and a teaspoon of black pepper. Mix well.
Once the pasta has cooked, drain and add it to the bowl and mix well.
Set a frying pan over a medium heat, add a splash of olive oil.
Add the pasta and flatten with a spatula. Fry for about 5 mins (left gently to check).
Great served hot with a pile of crunchy fresh salad. Enjoy!

name: Pasta Primavera (Spring Pasta)
description: A glossy green number to get a spring in your step (sorry). Asparagus, peas, pistachios and basil tossed through silky spaghetti, so simple and fresh. Jordon x
instructions: To make the blitzed pea mixture, add the garlic, pistachios, parmesan, the peas, the juice of your lemon and the basil leaves (saving a few for garnish) into a blender along with 3 tbsp of olive oil, 3 tbsp of water and a pinch of salt. Blitz until smooth.

Put the pasta onto boil in plenty of salted water. While it cooks, prepare the asparagus by removing the tough bottoms and the tips (make sure to reserve the tips). Now shave the main part of the stalks into strips using a vegetable peeler and set aside.
Once the pasta is about 2 mins from being ready, add the asparagus and the rest of your peas in along with the asparagus tips you saved earlier.

Drain everything (reserving a mug of cooking water) and return to the pan, add in the blitzed pea mixture along with a big splash of cooking water and mix well until creamy and saucy. Taste and add salt and another squeeze of lemon, if you like.
Plate up and top with a little more grated cheese and a pinch of chilli flakes.

name: Pasta Shells Stuffed With Tofu Ricotta
description: This is my take on a classic stuffed pasta shell bake, using a protein and flavour packed tofu mixture and a herby drizzle to finish it off.
keywords: Pasta Shells Stuffed With Tofu Ricotta
Pasta Shells Stuffed With Tofu Ricotta recipe
instructions: Cook the shells for 9 mins in boiling, salted water, until barely cooked (they will continue to cook in the oven). Drain and drizzle with some olive oil to prevent them from sticking. Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Meanwhile, make the tofu ricotta. First, zest the lemon and set the lemon zest aside. Add the tofu, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, miso, garlic powder and salt and pepper to a small food processor or blender. Blend until almost smooth. Taste and adjust the seasonings.

In a medium sized baking dish (about 21 x 26cm) pour in the marinara. Spoon about half to three quarters of a tbsp into each of the pasta shells, then place them snuggly into the marinara. Drizzle over a little olive oil, then cover tightly with silver foil. Bake for 25 mins.
Roast the nuts in the oven until golden brown, about 3-5 mins, on the lower shelf.

While the pasta is cooking, make the herby drizzle. Finely chop the herbs, mince the garlic and deseed and finely chop the chilli (you could also use a small food processor for this). Add these all to a small bowl with the reserved lemon zest, enough olive oil to loosen it into a drizzle, and plenty of salt and pepper.
Check that the pasta is cooked through, if not bake for another 5 mins.
Finish with chopped nuts and the herby drizzle and an extra sprinkle of nutritional yeast if you like.

name: Pasta e Lenticchie (Pasta with Lentils)
description: Another wonderful recipe by Gennaro Contaldo. Saucy Napolina spaghetti with lentils – a simple staple dish that is perfect for a weeknight dinner.
keywords: Pasta e Lenticchie (Pasta with Lentils) recipes
instructions: Finely chop the onion, carrot, and celery.
Heat olive oil in a large saucepan on medium heat, then add your onion, carrot and celery. Cook for about 15 mins until softened – this is your soffritto.
Whilst the soffritto is cooking, crush the garlic clove. Add the garlic, chilli (if using), and bay leaves and continue to sweat for a minute or so.

Add the lentils along with their liquid as well your tomato purée and vegetable stock. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover with a lid, and simmer for about 5 mins. Remove the lid, break the spaghetti up into pieces and add to the pan. Continue to cook without the lid on for about 10 mins until the pasta is cooked.
Remove from the heat, divide between 4 bowls, sprinkle with parmesan and drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil. Tuck into this bad boy.

name: Paste e Fagioli alla Genovese
description: Every region of Italy makes pasta and beans a little bit differently. This version, inspired by Liguria, is topped with their famous green pesto.
keywords: Paste e Fagioli alla Genovese recipe
instructions: Start by finely dicing the onion and celery. Place a saucepan over a low-medium heat and add a generous glug of olive oil. Add the onion and celery and cook for a few minutes until softening.
Roughly chop the tomatoes and add along with ½ the garlic (leave the clove whole but crush gently) and rosemary and cook for another 5 mins.

Add the beans and all of the liquid from the jar into the pan (jarred beans are slightly more expensive but much nicer than tinned). Now refill the jar by half and add that too. Stir and simmer for 10 mins.

While the beans simmer, add the remaining clove of garlic, pine nuts, basil and the olive oil (the full amount stated in the ingredients list) to a blender a whizz for a few seconds. Empty into a small bowl, grate in the Parmesan and stir.
Remove about ⅓ of the beans, add to the blender and whizz for a couple of seconds until you have a thick purée. Empty that back into the pan and mix.
Add the water to the pan and bring it up to a gentle boil.
Break up the lasagna sheets into roughly two-inch pieces and add to the pan. Simmer until al dente, probably about 5 mins, but taste to check!
Plate up into shallow bowls, top with a nice drizzle of the pesto and finish with a drizzle of olive oil, some parmesan and a pinch of chilli flakes, if you like.

name: Pastel De Nata
description: With a crisp crust and a custardy filling, a good pastel de nata is one of the most delicious things ever. This is a foolproof guide to making them.
instructions: First things first, you want to make the custard. This should be very cold when you bake it. Combine the sugar, water, cinnamon and lemon zest in a small saucepan and bring to the boil. Stir until clear and set aside, this is your sugar syrup.

Add the flour to another saucepan and whisk in a little of the milk to form a paste. Now gradually whisk in the rest of the milk. Split the vanilla pod, scrape out the seeds and add to the pot. Cook the milk over a medium heat, whisking constantly until thickened and it starts to simmer. Remove from the heat and whisk in the sugar syrup.

Separate your egg yolks in a large bowl (you can freeze the whites for meringue). Now pour the thickened milk mixture over the top and whisk everything together. Pass through a sieve to remove the cinnamon, lemon peel and any lumps. Season with salt and chill.

Make sure your butter is in the fridge cold and then cube it and chuck into the bowl of a stand mixer. Tip in the flour, salt and sugar, add the paddle attachment to the bowl and pop the whole thing in the freezer for 10 mins to get super cold. Now pop the bowl into the base of the mixer, attach the paddle and mix on low speed for 5-6 mins to “rub in” the butter to the dry ingredients. Slowly stream in the ice cold water until you have a shaggy dough. Tip it out and form into a disc. Rest for 20 mins in the fridge wrapped in a tea towel.
Once rested, lightly flour a clean surface and pop your dough down. Lightly flour a rolling pin and roll your dough out into a rough rectangle 40-50cm by 15-25cm and about 1cm thick.

Cut the second quantity of cold butter into thin slices and shingle in the middle 2/4 of the dough, leaving the top ¼ and the bottom ¼ free. Fold the bottom quarter of the dough up and over the butter, and the top quarter down. Meet them in the middle and pinch together, sealing in the butter. Now roll the dough out into the same size rectangle as it started, being careful not to let the butter squidge out the sides. Fold the top third over the middle third, and then bottom third over that. Squidge the layers together a little, wrap and place into the fridge for 20 mins to firm up.

Repeat the rolling and folding process once more. So, roll the pastry out into the rectangle shape (the opposite direction this time) and fold into thirds. Wrap and chill for 10 mins. Now roll out into a large rectangle that is about ¼ cm thick. Make sure you use plenty of flour here, you don’t want it to stick! Cut the rectangle into two smaller rectangles down the middle. Pop one of the pieces onto a tray and into the fridge.

Take the third quantity of butter (softened) and spread half of this over your first piece of pastry. With the long edge towards the bottom (towards you) roll up the pastry into a log. Keep the spiral as tight as you can. A good way to do this is to roll the top edge very thin and stick it to the surface. That way you can pull against it and create tension in the roll. Once rolled up, wrap and chill until firm, this should take about 20 mins in the fridge or 6-7 mins in the freezer. Repeat with the remaining butter and pastry.

Grab one of your pastry logs and cut it into 2 pieces. It should have a beautiful spiral pattern on the cut side. Grab your moulds and pop a piece of pastry, cut side down, into each. Now, using your thumbs (you can dip them in water to make this easier!), push down in the centre of the spiral of pastry and work the pastry up the sides of the mould, making the pastry as thin as you dare. This takes a bit of practise, but after a couple, you’ll be away. Repeat with all of your moulds and pastry.
Get your oven on now, preheat to 250°C.
Line your tart moulds up on a tray, I find you can do around 15 at a time. Carefully pour in the chilled custard so the tarts are ¾ full.

Time to bake! Slide the tray into the oven and bake for 9-10 mins until the custard has blistered black spots and the pastry is a deep golden brown. Carefully remove from the moulds as soon as you can, and leave to cool for a good 10-15 mins on a wire rack. Repeat with the remaining tarts. Dust with icing sugar and cinnamon and serve warm from the oven. I like mine with a strong black coffee. Bliss.

name: Pea & Asparagus Tortelloni
description: This super speedy sauce is the perfect partner for La Famiglia Rana Tortelloni – Italy's best kept secret. It’s all good to go in 10 mins flat.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic, de-seed and finely chop the red chilli, zest the lemon then remove the leaves from the oregano stalks. Chop the tips off the asparagus, about 2 cm from the end, then chop the stalks into 0.5 cm rounds (discarding the tough end bits)
In a small frying pan, add the seeds to toast for a minute on a medium high heat until lightly golden, then set aside to cool.

In the same pan, add the olive oil, garlic, chilli and oregano. Place on medium-high heat. Once the garlic starts to sizzle, fry for 1 min until light golden in colour before adding the lemon juice and zest, peas and the asparagus. Turn the heat down and cook for 2 minutes until the peas and asparagus are bright green and just cooked.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to the boil. Empty the La Famiglia Rana Spinach & Ricotta Fresh Tortelloni into the gently boiling water and cook for just 2 mins.

Scoop a few splashes of pasta water into the peas then drain the pasta and add to the pot. Toss together and serve up with the asparagus ends, toasted seeds, then a generous grating of Parmesan and black pepper.

name: Pea & Leek Soup With Chilli Jam Goat’s Cheese Toasts
description: This is our take on an old school comfort leek and potato soup with some frozen peas and a bag of salad thrown in to make this as vibrant as it is comforting. Plus cheesy chilli jam toasts for pizazz.
instructions: Wash, halve and finely slice the leeks. Scrape into a large saucepan along with the butter, if using, or a good drizzle of olive oil. Season, cook over a medium heat, stirring occasionally for 8-10 mins until soft.
Meanwhile peel and dice the potato into small roughly 1cm cubes. Finely slice the garlic cloves.
Add the garlic to the leeks, cook for 2 mins more, add the potato and pour in the stock. Bring to a boil then leave to simmer away for 15 minutes until the potato is completely cooked.
Heat the grill to high, grate the cheese.

Add the peas and salad bag to the soup, cook for a couple more minutes until the peas are defrosted and the leaves wilted, remove from the heat, use a hand blender to blitz until a completely smooth, vivid green soup – season to taste. Keep the soup warm.
Toast the bread on both sides under the grill then spread each slice with 1 tbsp of chilli jam and top with the cheese. Slide back under the grill until the cheese melts and is bubbling and golden.
Serve bowlfuls of the soup with the cheese toasts for dunking.

name: Pea & Mint Soup with Flax Crackers
description: Crunchy, savoury crackers add crunch and dimension to this fuss-free, easy pea-sy pea and mint soup.
keywords: Pea & Mint Soup with Flax Crackers Recipe
Pea & Mint Soup with Flax Crackers Recipe
instructions: Start by making the crackers. Heat the oven to 150°C. Line two baking trays with baking paper (or reusable silicone baking mats).
Mix all of the ingredients except the water and olive oil in a bowl. Pour in the warm water until covered and stir to combine then set aside for 20 mins, until the texture is slightly gelatinous.

Stir in the olive oil (this will help prevent the mixture from sticking to the parchment baking paper). Spread the mixture over the lined baking trays, using a spatula to spread it out into an even, thin layer, about 3mm thick.
Bake in the oven for 15 mins, then remove and score into pieces (squares or triangles). Return to the oven to bake for a further 60 mins, or until crispy.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool down before carefully lifting from the tray using a wide, thin spatula. The crackers can be stored in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
Meanwhile, start on the soup. Finely chop the onion, mince the garlic clove and pick the mint leaves.
Heat a splash of olive oil and the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for about 5 mins until soft and fragrant.
Add the garlic and cook for an additional minute or so, until fragrant.
Add the peas, fresh mint leaves and about ⅔ of the vegetable stock. Cover the saucepan with a tight-fitting lid and cook for 10 mins, or until the peas soften.
Transfer the soup to a food processor or blender and blitz until smooth. Add more (or all) of the remaining vegetable stock to adjust the thickness of the soup. Season to taste.
Divide across four bowls. Serve with an extra drizzle of olive oil and a couple of flax crackers (recipe below).

name: Pea & Pesto Lasagne
description: There is a traditional pesto lasagne from the Liguria region known as ‘Lasagne alla Portofino’. This is a slight twist on that because we’ve included peas — both within the layers and in the pesto itself. The peas ensure it’s extra green and saucy.
instructions: First, make the pesto. Separate the basil leaves from the stalk (discard the stalks), roughly chop the garlic and dice the Parmesan. Defrost your peas in the microwave. Put all the pesto ingredients in a blender or food processor and blitz until smooth. Set aside.

Next, make the white sauce. Melt the butter in a medium-sized saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 30-60 seconds with a spatula until the combination (a ‘roux’) is slack, light golden in colour and smells only slightly nutty. Add a splash of milk and stir with a spatula until the liquid is completely incorporated. Repeat three or four times, then begin to increase the amount of milk you’re adding and use a whisk instead of a spatula, each time ensuring there are no lumps before adding more milk. Once all the milk is in, add the nutmeg and white pepper, then gently cook over a low heat for 10 mins, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and generously coats the back of a spoon. Set aside.

Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and spread two or three tea towels over your work surface. Cook one-third of the pasta sheets for 3-4 mins until they’re floppy. Pick them out with tongs or a slotted spoon and lay over the tea towels. Repeat when needed, as you assemble the lasagne.

The exact number of layers your lasagne will have depends on the dimensions of your dish, but assume it’ll be six or seven layers of pasta. Defrost your peas at this stage as well. To assemble, first spread a ladleful of white sauce over the base of a 2.5L ovenproof dish. Lay 3-4 sheets of par-boiled pasta on top, to fit the dish. It’s good if they’re slightly ruffled (so not totally flat), as that will create texture. Cover with another ladle of sauce and two large spoons of pesto, using the back of a spoon to mix and spread the sauces over the pasta. Add around one-sixth of the cheese and one-sixth of the peas (you don’t need to be too precise). Repeat until the pasta sheets and sauces are used up, saving a ladleful of white sauce for the top. If there’s any pesto or mozzarella left, add that on top too.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Cover the lasagne with Parmesan and bake for 35-40 minutes, until fully bronzed and bubbling. Leave to rest for 15 mins, then serve.

name: Pea Pasta Salad
description: Creamy, zesty pea and mint pasta salad, perfect for on-the-go lunches and packed lunches.
instructions: Tip the frozen peas into a bowl and pour over enough boiling water to cover. Leave for a couple of mins to defrost, then drain.
Cook the pasta in a pan of boiling salted water following pack instructions. Drain, then rinse under cold running water to cool it down completely.
Add half the peas to a high-powered blender with half the mint leaves, the juice of the lemon, Dijon mustard and mayonnaise. Add a pinch of salt and black pepper, then blitz until smooth and creamy.
Halve the cucumber lengthways, then slice into half moons.

Tip the cooked pasta back into the pan along with the blended pea sauce, the remaining peas and the cucumber. Toss everything together until coated. Taste and season if needed. Then transfer to Tupperwatre containers, and stash in the fridge until needed. It will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Pea Pasta Salad with Chilli, Hazelnut & Lemon Salsa
description: Creamy pea and mint pasta salad with a punchy hazelnut salsa, perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Tip the frozen peas into a bowl and pour over enough boiling water to cover. Leave for a couple of mins to defrost, then drain.
Cook the pasta in a pan of boiling salted water following pack instructions. Drain, then rinse under cold running water to cool it down completely.
Add half the peas to a high-powered blender with half the mint leaves, the juice of the lemon, Dijon mustard and mayonnaise. Add a pinch of salt and black pepper, then blitz until smooth and creamy.
Prep the salsa. Roughly chop the remaining mint, hazelnuts and chilli in a small bowl and mix together. Then halve the cucumber lengthways and slice into half moons and set aside.

Tip the cooked pasta back into the pan along with the blended pea sauce, the remaining peas and the cucumber. Toss everything together until coated. Taste and season if needed. Then transfer to Tupperware containers, sprinkle over the nutty salsa and stash in the fridge until needed. It will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Pea and Ham Hock Soup
description: An easy peasy (sorry) soup that you can make in just ten minutes. Just what you need when the weather is grey and miserable.
keywords: easy pea and ham hock soup
pea and ham hock slow cooker
old fashioned pea and ham hock soup
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a medium-sized saucepan over a medium-low heat and grate in the garlic, cook for 1 min. Then add the peas and spinach and pour in the vegetable stock.

Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 5 mins, until the veg is tender. Using a stick blender, blitz the soup until smooth, then stir through the pesto and squeeze in the juice of half a lemon. Finely chop the chives.
Pour the soup into bowls and top with ham hock, a scattering of chives and a drizzle of cream if you have it.

name: Peach & Burrata Chopped Salad
description: This is a gloriously summery chopped salad that's perfect for when the sun is shining. Or when it's not. Give it a go.
instructions: Pick the mint leaves. Cut the peaches in half and discard the pits. Cook the grains following pack instructions and set aside to cool.
Add the broccoli to a pan of boiling water and cook for 2 mins, then drain and run under cold water.

Put the broccoli, mint and Parma ham on a chopping board and chop everything into rough chunks. Add the peaches to the board and chop again, until the peaches are also in rough chunks. Tip everything into a bowl, along with the rocket and mixed grains.
Combine the olive oil, balsamic, honey and a pinch of salt in a separate bowl. Mix well, then add to the other bowl.
Stir well and then top your salad with a ball of burrata before slicing it open. Mix the cheese around a bit and serve!

name: Peach Margarita
description: Peachy liquid deliciousness with a boozy kick
instructions: De-stone, roughly chop and blitz your peaches until you’ve got a smoothish purée.
Strain the blitzed peaches through a sieve to create a really smooth, silky peach juice. Set aside.
Zest the lime onto a plate, add the sugar and mix to create the rim.
Rub a wedge of lime around the rim of your glass and dip it in the sugary zest.
Juice your lime.
Add the strained peaches, tequila, triple sec, peach liquor, lime juice and agave to a cocktail shaker with ice.
Shake hard for 20 seconds to mix well and chill.
Put a large ice cube into your rimmed glass and strain in your cocktail.
Garnish with some slices of fresh peach and enjoy.

name: Peaches and Cream Crêpes
description: Peaches and cream are one of my favourite dessert combinations. Caramelizing peaches makes them extra sweet and slightly crisp, all smothered in almond cream.
instructions: For the crêpe batter blend up the plain flour, milk, eggs and 1 tbsp oil in a blender until smooth. Alternatively, whisk them together really well, and then strain to remove any lumps. Set aside to rest for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile whip up the double cream with the mascarpone, almond extract and honey.
Drain the peaches and save the liquid.
Turn on a grill pan or frying pan to high heat and add a drizzle of oil. Fry your peaches until golden and caramelised.
Heat the remaining peach liquid and add in brown sugar and butter. Reduce to half to make a thick peach syrup.

Heat a large frying pan and spray with oil. Pour about ¼ of crêpe batter into the pan and swizzle the pan so the batter coats the bottom evenly. Cook on either side for 1 minute or until golden brown.

To assemble, lay the crêpe out flat, and spread on your almond cream. Place your caramelised peaches on. Crush Amaretti biscuits in your hands and sprinkle those on top. Fold your crêpe in half, and then half again. Drizzle with the peach syrup and enjoy

name: Peachy Tahini Toast
description: Toasted in the oven upside down to keep all the moisture in the peach so it stays juicy and delicious. Perfect with my nutty dukkah which you can find on site.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Slice the peaches. Chop the nuts.
Lay a sheet of baking paper on a baking tray. Sprinkle the nuts on the sheet to around the size of your bread slice. Drizzle some agave onto the nuts, then lay the sliced peach over the nuts.
Generously spread your bread with tahini. Lay the bread onto the nuts, and press down gently so it sticks.
Toast in the oven for around 5 mins or until your bread is as toasted as you like it.
Remove from the oven and lay a plate or another tray on top of the toast. Carefully flip it over and remove the baking paper. Best served immediately. Enjoy!

name: Peanut & Aubergine Stir-fry on Creamy Butter Beans
description: We’ve paired rich and sticky stir-fried aubergine with creamy tahini soy butterbeans. Perfect for a quick midweek vegan dinner.
instructions: Cut the aubergine into cubes about 1cm in size. Place them in a bowl, sprinkle over some salt and toss well. Set them aside while you prepare the rest.
Finely slice the chilli and spring onion, setting aside some of the green tops for garnish. Mince the garlic cloves. Roughly chop the peanuts.
Heat a large frying pan over a high heat with a good drizzle of sunflower oil.
Turn the heat to high and cook the cubed aubergine, spring onion and chilli for about 5-8 mins, stirring often, until the aubergine has softened and is starting to char.

Add the garlic, ketchup, soy sauce, maple syrup, peanuts (save some for topping) and chilli flakes, if using. Cook for another 1-2 mins, then remove from the heat. Squeeze in the juice of ⅔ of your limes and stir through.

Meanwhile, add the butterbeans and their liquid to a pan. Add the tahini, a splash of soy sauce and the spinach and cook on medium heat until the spinach has wilted and the beans have warmed through. If you are using tinned beans, you may need to add a few tablespoons of water to the pot and cook them for a little longer to make sure they’re soft and creamy.

To serve, ladle the beans into bowls, then top with the stir-fried aubergine. Finish with a drizzle of tahini, the reserved peanuts and the spring onion. Finally add the zest and juice of the remaining lime.

name: Peanut & Cucumber Ramen Noodle Salad
description: This refreshing noodle salad recipe is just about the healthiest thing you can make with a packet of instant noodles.
keywords: Peanut & Cucumber Ramen Noodle Salad recipe
instructions: Put the edamame in a heatproof bowl and cover with hot water to defrost. Meanwhile, cook the noodles following pack instructions. Rinse the cooked noodles under cold water and set aside.
For the sauce, peel and mince the ginger and transfer to a small bowl. Add the soy sauce, peanut butter, sesame oil, lime juice, agave, water and gochujang, then whisk to combine. Set aside.

Slice the cucumber in half lengthwise and scoop out the watery seeds with a spoon (you can drain the water out of this and drink it, if you like!). Slice the cucumber into 0.5cm diagonal slices and transfer to a large bowl.
Roughly chop the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems. Pick the mint leaves. Roughly chop the peanuts. Finely slice the spring onion.
Add all of the herbs to the cucumber bowl along with the edamame, spring onion, dressing and noodles. Toss well.
Finish with a drizzle of sesame oil and top with the peanuts and kimchi.

name: Peanut Butter Aubergine Curry
description: Creamy, peanut buttery curry. Freshened with lime and coriander. Done in 30 minutes. Get it MOB.
instructions: Cube your aubergines. Add them to a pan with no oil and cook on a medium heat until they are shrivelled and browned - you'll have to do this in batches. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Add a splash of oil to the pan. Throw in a chopped brown onion, a chopped red pepper, and finely sliced garlic cloves. Add a small knob of grated ginger, turmeric and garam masala. Mix everything together.
At this point, get your rice on (cook following pack instructions).
Once the onions are softened, add peanut butter and mix it in. Pour in your coconut milk and your chickpeas (chickpea water included).
Mix everything together and reintroduce the aubergines.
Bubble the curry down until it is nice and thick (should take 5-6 minutes on a medium heat).
Add your spinach and allow it to wilt.
When the curry is ready, add a handful of chopped coriander and squeeze in the juice of a lime. Season to taste and remove from the heat.
Serve the curry on top of your basmati rice and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Peanut Butter Chicken Curry
description: This a rich and indulgent peanut butter chicken curry that tastes even better than it sounds. Give it a go tonight and thank yourself later.
instructions: Chop the chicken into 2-3cm bite-sized pieces. Juice the lime, and add to a large bowl with all the remaining marinade ingredients, mixing to combine. Add the chicken pieces and toss, ensuring they are well coated in the marinade. Cover and chill for 1-2 hrs, or overnight for best results.

Once marinated, grill or air fry the chicken on the highest setting for 10-15 mins until charred in places. Don’t worry if the chicken hasn’t cooked through fully – it will be simmered in the curry later. Set aside.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and chop the coriander. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat and add the chopped onion. Cook for 5-6 mins until they start to brown slightly. Add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook for 2-3 mins until fragrant. Stir in the chopped tomatoes and tomato purée, then cook until the mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate from the sauce.

Add the ground coriander, garam masala, kasoori methi, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt to the tomato mixture. Cook for 2 mins. Lower the heat and stir in the peanut butter until fully incorporated. Pour in the cream, mixing well to create a smooth, creamy sauce. Let the curry simmer for 10 mins, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Return the cooked chicken to the pan, stirring to coat it in the sauce. Simmer for 6-8 mins to ensure the chicken is heated through.
Top with chopped coriander and a drizzle of cream or melted butter, just before serving.

name: Peanut Butter Chilli Oil Noodles
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Fresh, spicy, umami-bomb veggie noodles with crispy leeks. Easy to make and on your table in less than 30 minutes.
instructions: Start by making the crispy leeks: cut the leeks into thin matchsticks and get them in a cold frying pan along with the vegetable oil. Turn the heat to medium-high and cook for 5-7 mins or until golden, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, get started on the noodle sauce: mince the garlic, ginger, spring onion and coriander. Get them in a large mixing bowl with the chilli powder, salt and granulated sugar.

Transfer the crispy leeks to a plate, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and set aside. Set aside ⅓ of the leek oil for garnish. Heat the remaining leek oil for another minute until almost smoking then pour it into the mixing bowl with the aromatics and stir to combine.
Add the peanut butter, soy sauce, apple cider vinegar and water to the noodle sauce mixing bowl and stir to combine.
Cook the noodles a minute shy of the packet instructions. Meanwhile, cut the cucumber into thin matchsticks and roughly chop the coriander.
Drain the noodles and add to the mixing bowl with the sauce. Add the sliced cucumber and chopped coriander and mix until everything is fully combined and well-coated.
Divide the noodles between bowls, drizzle over the remaining leek oil and top with a generous amount of fried leeks. Enjoy!

name: Peanut Butter Chocolate Banana Bread
description: This banana bread is a peanut-y and chocolatey with an indulgent twist on a classic. Wholesome. Tasty. Liam Charles. All the good stuff.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/354°F.
Line and grease a loaf tin.
Mash the banana with the vegetable oil, light brown sugar, Dr. Oetker Vanilla Extract, and all but 1 tbsp of your peanut butter.
Roughly chop up 150g of your Dr. Oetker Very Dark Chocolate and peanuts.
Whisk the flour and Dr. Oetker Baking Powder in a bowl together. Add in the dark chocolate and peanuts (save a tablespoon of peanuts for later).
Add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture and mix well.
Pour your batter into the loaf tin and sprinkle with the tablespoon of peanuts.
Bake for 45-50 mins. If your banana bread looks like it’s browning too much, top with foil after 30 mins.
Melt the saved peanut butter and chocolate to drizzle over the top. Cool to room temperature, then serve.

name: Peanut Butter Chocolate Bars
description: Packed with loads of peanuts and sticky dates these bars are the perfect prep-ahead snack to power you through the week. No baking, no fuss, just blend, chill and slice!
instructions: Chuck the peanuts into a food processor and blitz until they look like coarse flour.
Add the dates, peanut butter and a pinch of salt, then blend again until a sticky dough forms.
Break up the dark chocolate and tip into the mixture. Pulse a few more times to mix them through.
Press the mixture into a lined tray or mould, roughly 17cm x 24cm – it should be about 2 cm thick. Chill for 20–30 mins to firm up.
To store, wrap the bars in baking paper and chill or freeze until needed (these last for a week in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer).

name: Peanut Butter Jelly Burger
description: Who'd have thought peanut butter and jam would work in a burger?! Spicy satay sauce. Punchy chilli jam. It may sound strange, but we promise you it is divine.
instructions: Start by making your chilli jam. Roughly chop your shallots and chillies, then pulse them in a food processor until you have a coarsely chopped mixture.

Heat a small saucepan over a medium heat with a little glug of olive oil. Add your shallots and chillies, and fry for about 5 mins until fragrant. Tip in your sugar and vinegar, then gently simmer for about 10 mins until you have a thick jammy consistency. Leave to cool.
Cut your cucumber into thin slices. Pop them in a bowl with the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt. Mix with your hands and set aside to quickly pickle.
Move onto your satay sauce. Finely slice your shallot. Bash and finely chop your lemongrass. Finely chop your red chilli.
Add your chopped shallot to a sauté pan with a glug of olive oil. Cook out for about 4 mins, until fragrant and softened, then get your chilli and lemongrass in there. Cook for another 2 mins.
Tip in your coconut milk and bring the mixture to a simmer. Once it has reduced by half, add your peanut butter and 50g of brown sugar. Simmer for 5 mins, then add your dark soy sauce.
Once your mixture has cooled slightly, pour it into a food processor with 75ml of water. Whizz to a smoothish sauce. Season to taste with salt.
Finely shred your lettuce, and pick your coriander leaves off their stalks.
Cut your buns in half, and toast them on a griddle pan.
Heat a griddle pan over medium heat. Add your veggie burgers, and cook for a few mins on each side until they are nicely charred.

Assembly time. Spoon 1 tbsp of satay sauce onto the base of your bun, then pop your burger patty on top. Spoon over a blob of chilli jam, then top with lettuce, coriander and cucumber pickles. Put a little more satay sauce on the lid of the bun, then place this on top. Serve and enjoy!

name: Peanut Butter Overnight Oats, Three Ways
description: Our favourite overnight oats recipe. Make a big batch and mix up the toppings throughout the week. The yoghurt and almond milk make it extra creamy, the blueberries and vanilla give a burst of flavour, and the peanut butter and protein powder make it high in protein.
instructions: For the oats, combine all the oat ingredients in a mixing bowl and whisk together until well combined. Pour into an airtight container and refrigerate overnight.

For the yoghurt topping, add the yoghurt to a clean mixing bowl with the honey and almond milk. Whisk vigorously for about 2 mins until the mixture becomes shiny and slightly aerated. Pour into a separate airtight container and refrigerate overnight. The oats will keep for 4 days.

In the morning, serve up a portion of the oats into a bowl and top with the yoghurt. Finish with toppings of your choice: we love a scattering of crunchy nut cornflakes; a drizzle of honey and some grated frozen strawberries; or a sprinkling of cinnamon, sliced banana and a handful of granola.

name: Peanut Butter Paneer Curry
description: This midweek curry is the perfect veggie number to comfort while also getting in a dose of veg. It's good eating.
instructions: Chop the red onions. Scrape into a large saucepan, with a good drizzle of neutral oil and a pinch of salt. Cook over a medium heat, stirring occasionally for 6-8 mins until softened.

Meanwhile, peel and roughly chop the ginger and garlic. Add to the pan, turn the heat to medium high and cook out for 2-3 mins then add cumin seeds, all the chilli powder, garam masala and tomato purée. Cook, stirring for a few minutes more.
Add the peanut butter along with water. Using a hand blender blitz until a smooth and creamy curry sauce, season to taste – if you like your curry a little thinner - add a splash more water.
Get started on your topping by toasting cumin seeds in a small frying pan until they’re smelling amazing – tip ‘em into a small bowl.
Very finely chop the remaining red onion, add to the bowl with the toasted cumin seeds and some seasoning, stir together.
Cut the paneer into bite-sized cubes. Heat the curry sauce until simmering then add the paneer, peas and spinach. Cook until the spinach is wilted and paneer soft, around 2-3 mins.
Swirl the yoghurt through the curry, top with the cumin, red onion, and some coriander if you like. Serve with cooked basmati rice.

name: Peanut Chicken Curry
description: Yoghurt and peanut butter lend a creaminess to this curry without making it feel too heavy. You're going to love this.
instructions: Thinly slice the shallots and garlic and grate the ginger. Cut the chicken breasts into 1⁄2cm-thin strips.

Get a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add 1 tbsp of the coconut oil, then once melted, add half the chicken to the pan with a pinch of salt. Fry for a few mins until it is browned on all sides, then use tongs to transfer to a bowl. Repeat with the remaining chicken.

Add the remaining tbsp of coconut oil to the pan, then turn down the heat to low. Add the curry leaves, cumin seeds and black mustard seeds to the pan and cook for 1 min until fragrant. The seeds will pop in the heat, so be careful.
Add the shallots to the pan, then cook for 5 mins until completely softened. Add the chilli powder, turmeric, garlic and ginger and cook for 1 min more.
Return the chicken to the pan along with 500ml of water, then bring the curry to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 mins over a medium-low heat.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the coriander and peanuts.
Once your 5 mins are up, add the spinach to the curry and allow it to fully wilt. Stir in the yoghurt and peanut butter and season to taste with salt.
Sprinkle the curry with the coriander and peanuts and serve.

name: Peanut Chicken Noodle Salad
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Addictively moreish, peanutty, chicken-y noods with loads of crunchy stuff – perfect for any day of the week.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Grab your chicken, put onto a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Cover with foil and bake in the oven for 15-20 mins, until cooked through (timing will depend on the thickness of the chicken breasts).

Next up is the crispy topping — peel and finely slice 4 garlic cloves, then halve, deseed and finely slice 2 of the chillies. Finely slice ¾ of the ginger into thin matchsticks, then slice the shallot in half before finely slicing. Heat a big glug of oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and add the aromats. Sizzle away over a medium heat for 5-8 mins until golden and crisp. Scoop the aromats out of the oil and drain on a piece of paper towel, then season with salt.

To make your sauce, start by juicing the limes. Add 100g of the peanuts to a blender and blitz until smooth, before adding lime juice, soy sauce and 2 grated cloves of garlic. Grate in the remaining ginger (no need to peel!) and 50ml of water, then blitz to combine.
Prepare the noodles according to package instructions and drain before rinsing in cold water. Roughly chop the coriander and 50g of the peanuts.

Back to the chicken – once cooked, shred with a fork. Add the chicken to the noodles along with the beansprouts, dressing and most of the coriander, saving some for serving. Mix really well to combine. At this point, if the noodles look like they need a looser dressing, add splashes of water and give it a good mix between each addition.
Serve the noodles topped with chopped coriander, peanuts and a good scattering of the crispy bits!

name: Peanut Chicken Salad
description: This is basically satay chicken in salad form. Creamy coconut chicken, a rich savoury peanut dressing, crisp greens, fresh lime, and heaps of salty peanuts on top. Fresh, crunchy, and seriously good.
instructions: Finely chop the red chilli and grate the garlic and ginger. Then dice the chicken thighs into bitesize chunks. Throw everything into a large bowl with the remaining marinade ingredients.
Add a splash of olive oil and mix everything together. Cover and leave in the fridge for 10 minutes to marinate.
Dressing time. Add all the ingredients to blender and blitz to combine. (You can also do this in a bowl with a whisk).

Chicken time. Set a large frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Fry your chicken in batches for 7-9 mins, until it’s cooked through and sticky – pour all of the marinade juices into the pan while cooking.

Now, for your salad base. Finely slice the romaine lettuce and roughly chop the coriander and cucumber into small chunks. Add everything to a large bowl along with the chicken and salted peanuts (saving a handful for garnish). Drizzle over the dressing and toss everything together.
To serve, divide the salad between bowls and drizzle over any leftover dressing on top with the remaining peanuts and some extra sliced chilli if using.

name: Peanut Chocolate Dates
description: These sweet and fudgy dates are the ultimate health snack. Store them in the fridge and thank yourself later.
instructions: Using a knife, cut down one side of the date and open it up slightly.
Fill the cavity with ½ a teaspoon of peanut butter and close the date around the peanut butter. Repeat with the remaining dates.
Place the dates in the freezer for at least 1 hour.
Melt the dark chocolate and coconut oil together in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring between each go until smooth and spread over the top.
Dip each date third into the melted chocolate and place on a tray lined with greaseproof paper and sprinkle with sea salt.
Chill in the freezer for at least another hour. You can store in the freezer or fridge depending on your preference.

name: Peanut Curry Beans on Toast
description: Beans on toast with a glow-up. A nutty, saucy, spicy twist that’s ready in 10 and totally hits the spot.
keywords: Peanut Curry Beans on Toast recipe
Peanut Curry Beans on Toast peanut curry beans
instructions: Tip the butter beans and peanut curry sauce into a small saucepan and set it over a medium heat. Let everything warm through, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, toast the sourdough. Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the stems. Thinly slice the spring onion.
Once the beans are piping hot, give them a taste and season with salt and black pepper, if needed.
Plate up the toast, spoon over the warm beans and finish with coriander and spring onion. Drizzle over a little olive oil, if you fancy.

name: Peanut Curry Noodles & Crispy Tofu
description: Using our silky peanut curry sauce, with the crispiest tofu, these noodles are the ultimate, no-fuss weeknight dinner.
keywords: Peanut curry noodles and crispy tofu
instructions: Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Pick the coriander leaves and discard the stems.

Chop the tofu into 2cm chunks and toss through the cornflour. Season with salt. Drizzle with olive oil and air-fry for 15–20 mins until golden and crisp. Once cooked, toss the tofu through the kecap manis to glaze.

Meanwhile, bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Cook the udon noodles following pack instructions. Drain and run under cold water to stop them sticking. If you want the noodles hot, return them to the pan with a splash of water and the peanut curry sauce. Stir over medium heat until warmed through. Otherwise, just mix the sauce straight through the cold noodles.
Divide the noodles between bowls. Top with the crispy glazed tofu, coriander and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds.

name: Peanut Curry Sauce
description: A rich, velvety curry sauce packed with peanuts, coconut & Thai spice. Comes together fast & keeps for weeks. Pour it over literally anything.
instructions: Finely grate the garlic. Finely slice the coriander, stalks and all. Whisk the peanut butter through the stock.

Set a saucepan over a medium-high heat and pour in half of the coconut milk. Let it bubble away, stirring now and then, until the fat splits and the solids start to toast and brown slightly, this gives the sauce loads of flavour.
Stir in the curry paste, coriander and garlic. Cook for 2-3 mins until fragrant.
Pour the soy sauce and let it fully evaporate. Then add the passata, bring to the boil and simmer for 5-10 mins until slightly thickened.

Pour in the peanutty stock mixture along with the rest of the coconut milk. Stir to combine, bring back to the boil and then reduce the heat. Simmer for 15–20 mins, stirring occasionally, until thickened to your liking.
Once it’s nice and glossy, taste and season with salt, black pepper and a good squeeze of lime juice.

Pour the sauce into a clean, heatproof jar and seal it tightly. Let it cool fully before storing (if sealed properly, it’ll keep at room temperature for 1 month. If not sealed, store it in the fridge and use within 2 weeks).

name: Peanut Kimchi Dressing
description: A creamy, spicy dressing that'll taste great on literally anything. The secret ingredient? Kimchi brine.
instructions: Combine the kimchi brine, honey, peanut butter and vinegar in a mixing bowl. Stir to combine before adding the olive oil and seasoning well with salt and pepper.

name: Peanut Pork Pappardelle
description: A peanut butter sauce spiked with chilli oil and lathered over a perfectly cooked portion of pappardelle.
instructions: Whisk together the peanut butter, soy sauce, half of the chilli oil, the juice from 1.5 limes and a splash of water to create a loose sauce. Taste and add more lime juice if you fancy. Save 1 lime for later to serve.
Finely shred the cabbage and put a pot of water on to boil. Season with salt.
Preheat a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Add a shot of olive oil and tip in the pork mince. Break up with a spoon and fry until brown and crispy.
While the pork sizzles away, finely slice the garlic and onion and cut the ginger into thin matchsticks. Once the pork is crispy, tip them into the pan and stir fry through the meat for 2-3 mins.
Tip in the cabbage and cook until wilted. Drop the pappardelle into the boiling water and cook until al dente.

Transfer the cooked pasta to the pork and pour over the peanut sauce. Toss together to coat the pasta and loosen with cooking water if needed. Cut the chives into 3cm lengths and toss most through the pasta.
Divide between warm bowls and serve with the remaining chilli oil, lime wedges, thinly sliced spring onions and the remaining cut chives.

name: Peanut Sriracha Noodles
description: A spicy, creamy noodle dish that takes just 10 minutes to cook. Don't know what to have for dinner tonight? Have this.
instructions: Get a pan of salted water to the boil. Meanwhile, very finely slice the sugar snaps into long pieces. Toss in a bowl with half the lime juice. Roughly chop the peanuts, if using.
In a separate large bowl stir together the peanut butter, Sriracha, soy and remaining lime juice or rice wine vinegar to make your sauce.

Unravel the noodles with your fingers into the pan of salted boiling water and cook for 1 min then, using tongs, transfer the noodles straight into the sauce. Toss together, adding a splash of the cooking water to create a silky, luscious sauce.
Divide between bowls and top with the shredded sugar snaps, salted peanuts (if using) and more sriracha and soy, if you like. Boom.

name: Peanutty Aubergine, Cauliflower & Coconut Curry
description: What was quite a classic Italian sauce has been transformed into something entirely new with the addition of peanut butter, coconut milk, and curry paste.
instructions: Make the Aubergine Alla Norma batch recipe.
Heat oven to 200°C. Cut the cauliflower into florets and add to a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 15 minutes until slightly charred.
In the meantime, add ginger, onion, garlic, and coriander stalks to a blender with the curry paste. Blitz until smooth.

Heat oil in a pan over a medium heat and add the paste, cooking it out until thickened. Tip in the coconut milk, aubergine batch, and peanut butter. Simmer for 15 mins to allow the flavours to develop.

Finely slice the chilli and pick the coriander leaves. Add in the cauliflower to heat through and serve up. Top with the chilli, coriander, and peanuts then get stuck in. Serve with cooked rice, if you like.

name: Pear & Chicory Salad With Feta & Homemade Croutons
description: A bitter chicory salad perfectly balanced with sweet pears. This fun salad number has all the textures — it's crunchy, soft and chewy at the same time.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Cut the flatbreads into triangles and add to a large baking tray. Toss with 1 tbsp of the oil, season with salt and bake for 10-15 mins, until golden and crisp.

Whisk 8 tbsp of olive oil with the zest and juice of 1 lemon, grate in the ginger and season well. Tip the cumin seeds into a dry frying pan and place over a medium-high heat. Toast until fragrant, 1-2 mins. Add the cumin into the dressing and set aside. Use the same pan to toast the mixed seeds until they pop, then set aside.

Pull the chicory leaves from the stems and add to a large mixing bowl. Slice the pears in half, then lie flat and cut into wedges — cutting away the tough centre. Toss into the bowl with the chicory. Pick the herb leaves from the stalks and add too. Tip in the dressing, mixed seeds and the flatbread chips and toss well. Crumble the feta, then gently toss together.
Tip into a large bowl or 4 bowls. Finish with the zest of the second lemon and a crack of black pepper.

name: Pearl Barley
description: A high-fibre grain base that ticks a lot of boxes. You can load this up with a range of proteins and dressings for the ultimate lunch.
keywords: Brown Butter Beef Kofta Barley Bowls
instructions: Rinse the pearl barley. Place a saucepan on medium-high heat. Tip the barley and water in, let it come to the boil. Place a lid on, decrease the heat to low and cook for 40 mins, adding more water if needed.
Top the barley with your protein of choice.

name: Pearl Barley & Spiced Turkey Soup Recipe
description: This turkey soup recipe is the epitome of nourishing comfort, making it a fantastic choice for batch cooking. It’s packed with vegetables, nutty pearl barley, and tender turkey meat, offering a hearty and satisfying meal. The recipe is incredibly versatile, allowing you to substitute cooked chicken meat if you prefer. Perfect for preparing in advance, this turkey soup will keep in the fridge for up to a week, or you can freeze individual portions for a quick and easy meal anytime. The soup is also customisable with your choice of vegetables and fresh herbs, such as dill and parsley, to enhance the flavour. Whether enjoyed as a cosy dinner or a hearty lunch, this turkey soup is a wholesome addition to your recipe repertoire. For those who enjoy making soups, this recipe is a great alternative to chicken noodle soup or minestrone, bringing comfort and convenience to your kitchen.
keywords: Pearl Barley & Spiced Turkey Soup Recipe
instructions: Finely chop the onion. Finely slice the celery then peel the carrot and turnip or swede and cut into similar-sized pieces. Scrape all the veg into your largest saucepan.
Add the oil and a good pinch of salt. Cook over a medium heat, stirring occasionally for 15 mins until the veg has collapsed and softened.

Meanwhile, peel the ginger then finely grate the ginger and garlic. Add to the saucepan and cook, stirring for 1 min, then stir in the cumin, mustard seeds, turmeric and cinnamon, if using. Cook for 1 min more then pour in the stock.
Bring the soup base to a boil, drop in the pearl barley and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 30 mins.

After 30 mins, use your hands to shred the turkey meat into small chunks and add to the pan. Cook for a further 5 mins until the meat is heated through, the pearl barley has a pleasing bite and the vegetables are soft.

Roughly chop the coriander (stalks and all), then stir most of it through the soup. Finely slice the chilli. Season the soup with salt, pepper and lemon juice to taste, then ladle into bowls and top with the remaining coriander and chilli to serve.

name: Pearl Barley Super Salad
description: A lovely fresh fruity salad. Meal-prep doesn't get much better. Mango & mint match made in heaven. A deliciously healthy and simple salad.
instructions: Get your pearl barley on. Follow pack instructions. Add a veggie stock cube to the water.
Veg prepping time. Halve your cherry tomatoes. Cube your red peppers, avocado and cucumber (peel and de-seed the cucumber).
Add the veggies to a bowl along with your cooked pearl barley. Add the mango and pomegranate seeds.
Finely chop a handful of basil, coriander and mint. Add to the bowl along with a finely chopped chilli.

Add your vinegar, soy sauce, the juice of a lime and your olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Mix everything together. Serve in bowls or add to your tupperware and take to uni or work the next day!

name: Pecan Brittle
description: Pecan brittle can be eaten on its own or used as a garnish for ice creams, cakes and tarts. The little bit of baking soda in this recipe makes the brittle lighter and easier on the crunch, leaving it somewhere between a brittle and a honeycomb. You’ll need a sugar thermometer for this one.
instructions: Line a baking tray with baking parchment and clip a sugar thermometer to a medium-sized heavy-bottomed pan.
Put the sugar, water, liquid glucose, lemon juice and salt into the pan and stir to combine.

Turn the heat onto medium and leave the mixture alone – don’t stir it. Watch the thermometer carefully. When it reaches 120°C (the hard ball stage, this should take about 5 mins) add the nuts, stir to coat and continue to cook for another 5 mins or so until your mixture is a deep brown colour and around 150°C.

Remove from the heat, stir in the bicarbonate of soda and, very carefully, immediately pour it out onto your prepared baking tray. It will foam up and is very hot so be extremely careful not to burn yourself.
Leave to cool then crack into pieces and enjoy! It will keep in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

name: Pepper & Chickpea Butter Curry with Chicken Tenders
description: Creamy, mild curry packed with chickpeas and sweet peppers, blitzed silky smooth and topped with crispy chicken tenders. A proper comfort dinner for the whole family.
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsThinly slice the onion and red pepper. Finely chop the garlic and ginger.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the sliced onion and pepper and cook for 15 mins until soft and sweet.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and tomato purée. Cook for 2 mins until fragrant and darkened slightly.
Add the garam masala, water and double cream. Let everything bubble away for 15 mins.

Use a hand blender to blitz the mixture until completely smooth. Dot in the butter and stir until melted and silky. Drain the chickpeas and stir them into the sauce. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Meanwhile, cook the chicken tenders following pack instructions.
Serve up! Spoon the curry into bowls, top with the crispy tenders, and finish with sliced red chilli, fresh coriander and a wedge of lime for the adults. Serve with rice, if you like.

name: Pepperoni Pizza Pasta
description: If you love pepperoni pizza then you’re in for a treat. Gooey mozzarella, crispy pepperoni and glossy pasta. Delish.
instructions: Finely chop the shallots and garlic.
Add a big glug of oil to a frying pan and add in the pepperoni. Cook for 5 min until very crispy. Set aside the crispy pepperoni on a paper towel.
Roughly chop the crispy pepperoni.
Add your chopped shallots and cook for another 5 mins. Then add in the garlic and cook for 1 min until fragrant.
Add in the chopped tomatoes, oregano and half of your crispy pepperoni. Cook for 15 mins until the sauce has thickened.
Pop your spaghetti to cook in some salted boiling water.
Tear up the mozzarella and basil.
Once the sauce is thickened and your pasta is al dente, add the spaghetti to the pan along with 150ml pasta water and toss together until the pasta is well-coated.
Stir in the torn mozzarella and basil, and mix until the cheese is slightly melted.
Serve with a sprinkling of parmesan cheese and enjoy.

name: Peppery Pea Soup
description: We’ve thrown a leftover bag of frozen peas into our pea soup with crispy halloumi croutons. Yes you heard us right: cheese croutons.
instructions: Wash then roughly slice the leek (both green and white parts). Cut the potato, skin on, into smallish cubes and roughly chop the garlic.

Get a large saucepan over a medium heat. Pour in a good glug of olive oil, chuck in the leek with a big pinch of salt, cook for 5 mins until softened. Add the garlic and potatoes, stirring for 2 mins then pour in the vegetable stock.
Bring the soup to the boil and simmer for 15 mins until the potatoes are cooked. Meanwhile, cut the halloumi into 2cm cubes.

Tip the frozen peas into the saucepan, cook for 2 mins more then add the salad leaves. Once the salad has wilted take the pan off the heat. Blitz the soup until smooth and season with vinegar, salt and pepper to taste, adding a little water if it’s a too thick. Keep the soup warm over a low heat.
Get a frying pan over a high heat. Fry the halloumi for 2-3 mins, turning regularly until golden.
Ladle the soup between bowls, top with the halloumi croutons, a big pinch of chilli flakes, crack of black pepper, a good drizzle of olive oil and the capers (if using).

name: Perfect Almond Buttercream
description: Need almond buttercream to fill your cakes? Here’s how to make it. The grainy texture makes it perfect for the inside of cakes, then you can use one of our other buttercreams to frost the outside.
instructions: Make sure your butter is at room temperature. Use an electric whisk to beat the butter in a large mixing bowl for 4–5 mins on high speed.

Sift in the icing sugar and add the ground almonds, vanilla and a little splash of double cream. Beat on a low speed and continue to add double cream gradually until you reach your desired thickness. Beat for a further 3 minutes, until smooth and light.

name: Perfect Charred Tenderstem Broccoli
description: This charred broccoli is perfect for meal prep. Combine it with your choice of protein, carb and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
keywords: Pesto Butter Beans with Charred Tenderstem Broccoli
Pesto Butter Beans with Charred Tenderstem Broccoli recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Lay the broccoli onto a baking sheet and drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and slide into the oven for 10-15 mins, until charred.
To serve, grate over the Parmesan and sprinkle over some chilli flakes. If batch cooking for the week, transfer to a container and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Perfect Chocolate Buttercream
description: Need chocolate buttercream to frost your cakes? Here’s how to make it.
instructions: Use an electric whisk to beat the butter in a large mixing bowl for 4–5 mins on high speed. Sift in the cocoa powder and beat until you have a paste.

Beat in the icing sugar and add the vanilla, salt, milk and most of the cream then beat together slowly at first on a low speed to bring it together. Beat on high for another 2–3 mins until it’s a smooth consistency. Add more cream if desired.

name: Perfect Custardy Scrambled Eggs and Crisps
description: Eggs are hard to master. Cooking the perfect custardy scramble, even harder, but I’m here for you. These are, no doubt, the best scrambled eggs I’ll ever have, and you can now make them at home.
keywords: Perfect Custardy Scrambled Eggs and Crisps
Perfect Custardy Scrambled Eggs and Crisps recipe
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, season with salt and whisk together. Set aside. Finely slice the chives and toast the bread.

Pour the eggs into a cold frying pan and add the cold butter. Put the pan over a low-medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, until the butter has melted and the eggs are starting to set. There should be no runny egg left – it should still be loose.

Remove from the heat and stir through the cream cheese. Taste and season with more salt if needed. Spoon the custardy scrambled eggs onto the toast, then sprinkle over half the chives. Crush the crisps on top and finish with the remaining chives and some freshly cracked black pepper.
Spoon the custardy scramble onto the toast, and sprinkle over half the chives. Crush the crisps on top and finish with the remaining chives and some freshly cracked black pepper.

name: Perfect Ham & Cheese Sarnie
description: The sandwich your lunch break deserves, this one takes ham and cheese to the next level.
instructions: If your butter’s still cold, chuck it into a food processor with the cornichons and blitz until smooth. No food processor? Finely chop the cornichons and mash into softened butter.
Stir the mustard and mayo together in a bowl to make a quick dijonnaise.
Grate or thinly slice the Emmental and toast the bread or baguettes until golden.
Spread the cornichon butter on one side of each bottom slice. Layer with cheese, sauerkraut and ham. Smear the dijonnaise over the top slices, then sandwich together and press lightly. Dig in!

name: Perfect Jasmine Rice
description: Want to know how to cook perfect rice? We’re here to show you how with this incredibly simple step-by-step guide. You’ll never make disappointing rice again.
keywords: Best way to cook sticky rice
instructions: Add the rice to a saucepan and wash it until the water runs clear, then drain.

Add the water to the saucepan with the rice and set the pan over a high heat. Bring it to the boil, place a tight-fitting lid on, turn the heat down to low and let it steam for 12 mins – do not remove the lid during this time.
Once the 12 mins have passed, remove the pan from the heat. Fluff the rice with a fork then pop the lid back on and leave it for another 10 mins to finish steaming.
Before serving, fluff the rice using a fork.

name: Perfect Potstickers
description: You can make crispy delicious potsticker dumplings at home using store-bought dumplings.
instructions: Pick a pan that will fit 24 dumplings. You don’t want any huge gaps and want them to fit all nicely snug.
Bring a medium-sized nonstick pan to medium heat and add neutral oil to the pan and swirl it all over to coat every bit.

Place all the dumplings in the pan, creating a circular pattern by starting from the edge and working towards the centre. Increase the heat to medium high for 2-3 mins or until the bottoms of the dumplings are lightly golden brown.

In the meantime, prepare a lid big enough for your pan and combine ½ cup of water with cornflour and mix well. When the dumplings have light browned, mix the water mixture and pour into the pan, adding more to fill just under half of the dumplings, quickly put the lid on and bring to a boil (this will take about 2 mins depending on water temp). Then reduce the fire to medium-low heat and cook for 5 mins. Remove the lid, increase to medium high heat for 1 min or until the excess water has evaporated leaving a lightly crispy edge. Turn the heat off and set aside.
Soak a tea towel in water and lightly squeeze, place onto a flat surface and plonk the hot pan on top, it will get a little steamy. This will help release the pot stickers from the pan

Grab a plate large enough to fit the pan, place the plate on top of the dumplings, place your hand on the back of the plate, with your other hand on the pan handle and confidently and firmly flip the plate, place it down on the table. Carefully lift the pan to reveal the potstickers.

name: Perfect Roast Potatoes
description: Golden, crunchy outsides and ethereally fluffy centres, these spuds are seasoned to perfection with Maldon sea salt.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Peel and quarter the potatoes. Add to a pan and cover with cold					water. Season with salt and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat					and simmer for 2 mins.

Drain and shake the potatoes hard in the colander to rough up
the outside. Sprinkle with 3 tbsp of flour.

Add the goose fat to a large roasting tin and place in the oven for
5 mins.

Remove the tray, add the potatoes to the hot fat, season well
with Maldon salt and roll around in the roasting tray.

Return to the oven for about 40 mins, until they’re golden
brown all over. Halfway through cooking, flip the potatoes over.
Remove and season with Maldon salt.

name: Perfect Vanilla Buttercream
description: Need vanilla buttercream to frost your cakes? Here’s how to make it.
instructions: Use an electric whisk to beat the butter in a large mixing bowl for 4–5 mins on high speed.

Sift in the icing sugar and add the vanilla and cream then beat on a low speed to bring it together. Beat on high for another 2–3 mins until it's a smooth consistency. Add more cream for a looser buttercream if desired.

name: Peri Peri Burrito
description: We have taken the best bits of a burrito and given it a Portuguese twist. Packed full of spicy rice, beans & delicious Quorn Makes Amazing Peri Peri Strips.
instructions: Dice the white onion and sauté half in a pan in a glug of olive oil. Cook for 10 minutes until very soft. Meanwhile, wash the rice until the water runs clear.
Add in the cayenne pepper, turmeric, paprika, and grate in the garlic and toast for 1 minute.
Add the rice, 300ml water, chopped tomato and salt to taste. Cover the pan with a lid and simmer for 10 minutes. Fluff the rice up with a fork and allow to cool slightly.

In a separate pan, heat up a glug of oil and pop in the cumin seeds. When they start to sizzle, add in the other half of the white onion and cook for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add in drained cannellini beans and warm through for a few minutes. Season with salt and set to one side.
Dice the tomatoes, red onion and coriander, then combine in a bowl with any juices from the tomato. Season with salt and the juice of one lime.
Gently fry the Quorn Peri Peri Strips in a frying pan with a small glug of oil until warmed through and slightly crispy.

Warm your tortilla, then place it onto a sheet of foil. Layer on the rice, beans, Quorn Peri Peri Strips, salsa and spinach. Roll up the tortilla into a burrito shape and wrap with the foil to keep it together. Cut in half and serve. Optionally, you can toast the burrito in a pan too.

name: Peri Peri Chicken & Wild Rice
description: Spicy, buttery chicken with the freshest, garlicky sweetcorn, kale and coriander wild rice. If you love a cheeky Nando’s, then this one’s for you.
instructions:
Get two large frying pans over a high heat and add a knob of
butter to each along with a splash of oil. Season the chicken fillets
with salt and black pepper and chuck into one of the pans. Fry for
4 mins, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, crush the unpeeled garlic cloves into the other pan,
stir and cook for 30 seconds. Squeeze the unopened wild rice
pouches with your hands to break up the grains, then open and
tip the rice into the pan with the garlic. Open and empty in the
tin of sweetcorn with its juices and add the kale. Season with salt,
pepper and chilli flakes to taste. Leave to heat through.
Back to the chicken. Pour in the peri peri sauce and cook,
occasionally basting the chicken with the sauce, for 2 more
mins until the chicken is cooked through.
Cut the lime into four wedges.
Divide the rice between four bowls and top with the peri peri
chicken. Add a lime wedge to each bowl and tear over some
coriander to serve.

name: Peri Peri Falafel Pitta
description: We’ve given falafel a smoky makeover. Packed with chickpeas, red pepper, and paprika. Stuffed in pittas with PERi-PERi slaw. A glorious sandwich.
instructions: Soak your chickpeas overnight in a bowl of water.
Thinly slice one of your red onions.
Place your sliced red onions in a bowl and squeeze over the juice from your lemon. Add a pinch of salt and mix with your hands. Leave it to pickle.
Time to make some slaw. Finely shred your white cabbage and peel and julienne your carrot. Place in a bowl with the mayonaise and give it a good mix. Set aside until later.
Roughly chop your remaining red onion, red pepper, garlic, and parsley.

Drain and dry your soaked chickpeas, then put them in the food processor with your red onion, red pepper, garlic, parsley, paprika, ground cumin, ground coriander, cayenne pepper, chickpea flour, baking powder, Nando’s PERi-PERi Salt and a pinch of regular salt in a food processor. Pulse until you have a smooth mixture that binds together when squeezed.
Shape your mixture into small patties.

Heat a generous glug of oil over a medium heat. Add a few of your falafel patties and fry for 3 minutes on each side until they are deeply golden and crisp. Drain on a plate lined with a paper towel and repeat with your remaining patties.
Toast your pittas and slice your cucumber into thin discs.
Make an incision in the long side of your pitta to create a pocket. Stuff it with your falafels, slaw, pickled onions and cucumber. Drizzle with some more Nando’s Vegan PERinaise, then enjoy.

name: Peri Peri Halloumi & Sweet Potato Hummus Bowl
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad. 

A spicy, smoky bowl stacked with sticky halloumi, roasted sweet potato and zingy slaw. An easy veggie dinner that clears the fridge and hits the spot.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

Cut the sweet potatoes into bite-sized chunks and chuck them onto a baking tray. Drizzle over the olive oil and the juice of half the lemons, then toss with half the peri peri seasoning and a good pinch of salt. Roast for 25–30 mins until golden and soft. Got other veg knocking about? Chuck that in too – peppers, courgettes, red onions… it all works.

Slice the halloumi into thick strips. Mix the honey and remaining peri peri seasoning in a small bowl. When the veg is nearly done, place a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the halloumi and fry for 2–3 mins on each side until golden. Brush over the honey mix and fry for another 1–2 mins until sticky and caramelised.

Finely shred the red cabbage. Chuck both into a bowl with a squeeze of lemon juice, adjusting to taste. Season with salt and mix well. Got any other crunchy bits lurking in the fridge? Grated carrot, radishes or lettuce all work nicely here.

Spoon the hummus over the two thirds of the bottom of the bowl and Top with the roasted sweet potato, shredded veggies and sticky halloumi. Spoon over a little extra peri peri honey if you fancy, then finish with sliced chilli, coriander, a lemon wedge and sesame seeds. Serve with toasted flatbreads, and enjoy.

name: Peri Peri Halloumi Burger
description: The peri peri mayo and the halloumi come together here to form the perfect mouthful. A great veggie burger option.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C/356°F.
Cut your peppers and red onion into chunky 2-inch pieces (make sure they're not too small).

Get the peppers and red onion chunks on a baking tray. Add the lemon half to the tray, cut side down. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Slide the tray into the oven to bake for 45 mins until the peppers are beginning to char.
Remove the tray from the oven. To a blender, add ⅔ of the peppers, all the onions and the squeezed out pulp of the roasted lemon.
To the same blender, add the paprika, oregano, red wine vinegar, whole red chilli, garlic clove and a glug of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and blitz until smooth. This is your peri peri.
In a small bowl, mix your blitzed peri peri with the mayonnaise.
Cut the halloumi into 1cm slices. Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat then add the halloumi and cook for 4 mins on each side until golden brown and crispy.
Cut your burger buns in half and quickly toast them, cut side down, in the hot pan until lightly toasted.

Time to assemble. Take your base bun and spread over a layer of peri peri mayo. Top with some halloumi, some roasted peppers, a small handful of salad leaves, more mayo, more halloumi and finally the bun top. Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Peri Peri Roasted Aubergine, Herb Salad & Rice
description: Whole aubergines roasted until silky and collapsing, split open and drenched in a smoky, spiced peri peri sauce. You'll want to save this one to impress your plant-based pals!
keywords: Peri Peri Roasted Aubergine & Rice recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Prick each aubergine a few times with a fork and place on a baking tray. Roast for 35–40 mins until the skin is charred and the inside has completely collapsed, they should feel totally soft when squeezed.
While the aubergines roast, roughly chop the shallots, chillies and garlic, they'll all get blended so don't worry about precision.
Set a saucepan over a medium heat, and add the olive oil, once hot add the shallots, chillies and garlic, along with a pinch of salt. Fry for around 5 mins until softened and just starting to colour.

Add the smoked paprika and oregano to the pan and cook for a further minute, then add the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins until jammy. Add a small splash of water to deglaze the pan, then pour everything into a blender. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and blend until smooth. Taste and adjust the salt, heat or lemon to your liking.
Put the rice on now so it cooks alongside everything else. Rinse the long grain rice under cold water, then cook according to packet instructions.
Finely slice the red onion into half moons and pick the leaves from the parsley. Toss together with the olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice.

Let the aubergines rest for 2 mins, then split open lengthways like a jacket potato, the inside should be silky and steamy. Spoon over plenty of the peri peri sauce so it soaks right in. Serve alongside the rice with the herb salad scattered over and your fluffy rice.

name: Peri Peri Sweet Potato Salad
description: Seema's Peri Peri twist on a classic potato salad. The sweet potatoes can really take the heat, and with lots of fresh veg it's full of crunch. It's a banging side or lunch and great for making ahead too.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/354°F and set the grill to the highest setting.
Dice the sweet potatoes, leaving the skins on, then toss them in a glug of olive oil and 2 teaspoons of Nando's PERi-PERi Salt. Roast for 30 minutes, turning halfway through.
Coat the corn on the cob with olive oil and grill for 5 minutes on each side to char the corn. You could also do this on a hot griddle pan.
Meanwhile, prep your veggies. Dice the red onion, red pepper and celery. Half the cherry tomatoes and roughly chop the coriander. When the corn has cooled, chop off the kernels.

In a large bowl whisk together the Nando's Vegan PERinaise, apple cider vinegar, the juice of your lime and 2 teaspoons of Nando's PERi-PERi Salt. Pour in the chopped veggies and cooked sweet potato, stir well to combine.
Season with salt if needed and enjoy.

name: Peri Peri Tofu with Spiced Rice & Herby Peas
description: Sticky, spicy tofu with that smoky char you love, piled onto turmeric rice with zingy minty peas. Think Nandos – but fresher, faster, and plant-based.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Mix the peri peri marinade with the maple syrup and a small pinch of salt in a bowl.

Slice each block of tofu in half lengthways to make four pieces. Hasselback the tofu by making deep cuts across the surface, being careful not to slice all the way through. Brush each piece with half the marinade and drizzle with a little olive oil. Transfer to a lined baking tray and roast for 25 mins, brushing again halfway through with the remaining marinade.
While the tofu roasts, finely slice the green chilli and mince the garlic. Add them to a heatproof bowl with the cumin and turmeric.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a small pan over a medium heat. Once hot, pour it over the spice mix – it should sizzle. Heat the rice pouches following pack instructions, then tip into a large bowl. Mix through the hot spiced oil and season well with salt and pepper.
Bring a small pot of water to the boil. Add the peas and cook for 3 mins. Drain and return to the pan.
Finely chop the parsley and mint. Toss the herbs through the peas along with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, pepper and a pinch of chilli flakes, if using.
Slice the lemon into wedges.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the peri peri tofu and herby peas. Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: Peri-Peri Chicken & Halloumi Flatbreads With Cabbage Slaw
description: Cheeky peri peri vibes with juicy chicken, squeaky halloumi, and a zingy yoghurt slaw – all packed into soft flatbreads. This one bangs.
keywords: Peri-Peri Chicken & Halloumi Flatbreads With Cabbage Slaw
Peri-Peri Chicken & Halloumi Flatbreads With Cabbage Slaw recipe
instructions: Cut the chicken and halloumi into bite-sized cubes and toss with the peri peri seasoning, a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt.
