Set a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 6-8 mins until golden and cooked through. Remove to a plate, then add the halloumi to the same pan and cook for 2 mins on each side until golden.

Finely shred the cabbage using a knife or peeler. Chuck it into a bowl with the yoghurt, zest the lemon, add a good squeeze of lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Roughly chop the parsley and mix it through. Set aside.
Toast the flatbreads in a dry pan until warm and slightly charred.
Load them up with a generous spoonful of slaw, then pile on the chicken and halloumi. Finish with a squeeze of lemon and a drizzle of hot sauce, if you like.

name: Peroni Nastro Azzurro Negroni
description: This isn’t just fun to say, it’s also delicious to drink. It’s a little less strong and a lot more smooth than a typical Negroni thanks to the orange juice.
instructions: Using a peeler, peel your entire orange, or as much as you are able. Juice your orange and set aside the juice for later.
Tightly wrap up the orange rind into a tight roll, then spear it with a toothpick to create a guide hole. Take the toothpick out and now spear it with the rosemary sprig to create the garnish.
In a large mixing glass, add ice and then the gin, Campari, sweet vermouth and orange juice then stir.
Strain out into a large glass and top with Peroni Nastro Azzurro.
Dash a couple of drops of Angostura Bitters on top and garnish with your orange rose. Enjoy!

name: Peshwari Naan
description: A curry house classic. Soft, pillowy naan stuffed with a sweet and nutty mixture. Perfect for mopping up your favourite curry.
instructions: Combine the plain flour, instant yeast, ½ tsp of salt, ½ of sugar, 3 tbsp of oil and 150ml warm water. Knead for 10 mins until it forms a smooth dough. Cover and allow to rise in a warm place for 30 mins.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a microwave.

Blend up your flaked almonds, sultanas, desiccated coconut, brown sugar, cinnamon, cumin, melted butter, 1 tbsp of water and a big pinch of salt. Reserve some almonds and sultanas for garnish at the end.
Divide the dough into four sections and roll each into a ball. Gently press it down and add 2 tbsp of the filling. Pinch the edges into the centre to seal the edges of the naan.
On a floured surface, gently roll out the dough ball until it’s 10cm in diameter. Repeat to make 4 naans.
Heat up a pan until it’s smoking hot, and drizzle with some vegetable oil.
Cook the naan on either side for 2 mins until puffed and golden. Repeat with the remaining naans.
To serve, spread the naan with butter and sprinkle over some toasted flaked almonds, sultanas and coriander leaves.

name: Peshwari Swirls
description: Bake Off alumni Chigs has taken the flavours of a Peshwari naan and thrown them into these lovely sticky buns. Thanks, Chigs.
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together lukewarm whole milk and instant yeast. Allow this to bloom for 5-10 mins until frothy.

In the bowl of a stand mixer, whisk together plain flour, sugar, and fine sea salt. Add in the unsalted butter. Rub in using your finger tips. Using the dough hook attachment set on medium-low speed, add in the yeast mixture, whole eggs, and egg yolk. Mix for 5-10 mins.

Tip the dough out on a lightly floured work surface and knead for 2-3 mins. Place the dough in a lightly greased bowl and cover with a damp tea towel. Allow the dough to rest in a warm area for 90 mins.
To make the Peshwari filling, put all the ingredients in a bowl and mix with your hands until fully combined.
Preheat the oven to 175°C.

To assemble the swirls, punch the air out of the proofed dough and pop it on to a lightly floured work surface. Flattening it into a large rectangle using a rolling pin. It should be the thickness of a pound coin, about 5mm.

Spread the Peshwari mix across the whole rectangle. Tightly roll from the bottom all the way to the top. Slice into 5cm thick segments. You can use a sharp knife or wrap string around the log and pull to cut.
Place the segments into a greased 21cm springform cake tin and cover with a damp tea towel.
Let rise at room temperature for 30-45 mins.
Bake for 15-20 mins until golden brown. Brush the tops of each bun with melted butter and serve warm.

name: Pesto Asparagus & Halloumi Traybake
description: Asparagus and halloumi roasted with green pesto until charred, then finished with a dollop of crème fraîche and a squeeze of lemon. Creamy, veggie and all on one tray.
keywords: Pesto Asparagus & Halloumi Sheet Pan recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the Tenderstem broccoli and asparagus into 2cm pieces. Drain and rinse the butter beans and dice the halloumi into 3cm cubes.

Tip the broccoli, asparagus, butter beans, halloumi, peas and pesto onto a large baking tray, drizzle with the olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Toss together, then slide into the oven and cook for 10-15 mins, until the halloumi is golden and charred at the edges.
Remove from the oven and stir through the crème fraîche. Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve straight from the tray.

name: Pesto Butter Beans
description: These pesto butter beans are perfect for meal prep. Combine them with your choice of protein, carb, veg and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
keywords: Pesto Butter Beans with Charred Tenderstem Broccoli
Pesto Butter Beans with Charred Tenderstem Broccoli recipe
instructions: Tip the butter beans into a saucepan along with the water from their cans, bring to the boil. Add the pesto, taste and season, adding a splash of white wine vinegar if it needs it.
If batch cooking for the week, transfer the pesto butter beans to a container and store in the fridge until ready to eat. Top with some Parmesan and chilli flakes before serving, if you like.

name: Pesto Butter Beans with Charred Tenderstem Broccoli
description: A healthy little number that you can knock together fairly quickly. An excellent way of using up a few tins of butter beans.
keywords: Pesto Butter Beans with Charred Tenderstem Broccoli
Pesto Butter Beans with Charred Tenderstem Broccoli recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Lay the broccoli onto a baking sheet and drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and slide into the oven for 10-15 mins, until charred.
Tip the butter beans into a saucepan along with the water from their cans, bring to the boil. Add the pesto, taste and season, adding a splash of white wine vinegar if it needs it.
Spoon the beans into bowls, top with the charred broccoli and finish with a pinch of chilli flakes and a grating of Parmesan.

name: Pesto Carbonara
description: If you like pesto pasta and carbonara, we’ve put them together to create a stunning 15 minute, 5 ingredient meal.
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Add the lardons into a frying pan and place onto medium heat. Cook until golden, 3-5 mins. Then, remove from the heat.
Once boiling, cook the pasta 1 min under al dente.
Meanwhile, crack the egg into a bowl, add the egg yolks and stir the pesto through.
Using tongs, add the pasta into the pan with the guanciale. Whisk through 45ml of hot pasta water into the pesto.
Pour the pesto mixture onto the pasta on low heat and toss, adding more pasta water to thin the sauce out if needed. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Share the pasta between bowls, making sure to spoon over all the sauce.

name: Pesto Chicken Pastina
description: We're obsessed with pastina. The tiny shapes mean that whatever you cook it with feels really cosy and comforting. We cooked this one in a lemony, creamy chicken stock and topped it with pesto for a light, summery meal.
instructions: Peel and finely dice the carrots, celery and onion. Finely chop the garlic. Pick the thyme leaves.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the chopped veg and cook for 5-7 mins. Add the garlic, bay leaf and thyme, then cook for 2 mins until just turning golden. Add a pinch of salt.
Pour in the chicken stock and add the chicken breasts. Cover with a lid and cook on the lowest heat for 10-12 mins.
Remove the chicken from the pan and shred. Tip the pastina into the pan and simmer for 4-6 mins. Stir through the cream and the juice of your lemon.
Ladle the pasta into bowls. Top with the chicken and pesto.

name: Pesto Eggy Bread & Caprese Bean Salad
description: Eggy bread, but if it bumped into an Italian. Pesto-soaked bread under melted mozzarella, with a caprese-inspired balsamic tomato and bean salad that brings that freshness. This is serious midweek lifesaver that will please everyone.
keywords: Caprese with Pesto Eggy Bread recipe
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Crack the eggs into a bowl, grate in half the Parmesan and whisk with the pesto, then season with salt and pepper.

Chop the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks and place in a bowl with the balsamic and the extra virgin olive oil, then season with salt and set aside. Drain the beans and wash them thoroughly to remove any bean juices.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Dip both sides of each slice of bread into the egg mixture until fully coated, then cook in the pan on both sides for 3-4 mins, until golden and cooked through, then transfer to a tray. Use your favourite bread here, any will do.
Sprinkle the low-moisture mozzarella over the bread and slide under the grill for 3-5 mins, until melted. Grate the remaining Parmesan over.
Tear the mozzarella into the tomatoes and toss through with the basil leaves and beans. Share the bread and salad between plates and serve.

name: Pesto Green Beans & Broccoli
description: These pesto green beans and broc are perfect for meal prep. Combine them with your choice of protein, carb and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Drop in the beans and broccoli for 3-4 mins or until just tender, still with a little bite. Shock in icy cold water and then dry.
Add the pesto to a large mixing bowl and grate in the Parmesan. Add the zest and juice of the lemon and a couple of glugs of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and mix to a loose pesto dressing.
Drop the cooked beans and broccoli into the bowl with the dressing. Scatter over the toasted almonds and toss together.
If batch cooking for the week, transfer to containers and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Pesto Hasselback Potato Traybake
description: An easy vegan recipe by Bunch that you can throw in the oven, this hasselback potato traybake is taken to the next level by heaps of vegan pesto.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan.

Scrub the potatoes clean and halve them lengthways. Carefully slice 2mm thin segments through the potato, cut-side down, using a chopstick on either side to stop the knife from going all the way through. The potatoes should be intact at the base.
Cut the garlic bulbs in half through the middle of the cloves.

Lay the potatoes and garlic halves on a large lined baking tray. Drizzle plenty of olive oil over the potatoes, making sure to get some into the crevices and over the flat side too. Drizzle some olive oil over the cut side of the garlic halves and place them cut-side down on the baking tray. Sprinkle plenty of salt and pepper and bake for 20 mins.
Peel and cut the onion into eighths.
Once the 20 mins are up, remove the tray and brush the top of each potato generously with 2 tbsp of vegan pesto.
Lay the cherry tomatoes, broccoli and red onion around the potatoes. Add the herbs here over the top. Drizzle with oil and season well. Bake for another 10 mins.
Remove the tray from the oven and scatter the olives, if using, around the tray and bake for another 5 mins.
When ready to serve, drizzle more pesto all of the vegetables and finish with a shaving of lemon zest, if using.

name: Pesto Minestrone Soup
description: An easy pesto minestrone soup recipe that's plant-based, delicious, and incredibly quick.
instructions: This recipe was written to make 4 servings.
Chop the Tenderstem broccoli into small pieces. Finely chop all of the herbs. Drain the beans.
Add a ¼ of the pesto, nutritional yeast, chili flakes and miso with a little salt and pepper into each pot and stir well to combine.
Layer up the veggies and beans and top with the almonds.
When ready to serve, pour over about 300ml of boiling water and set aside for 5-8 mins to soften.

name: Pesto Pasta e Ceci with Flaked Salmon
description: On the table in under 25 mins, this quick, creamy green pasta is loaded chickpeas, flaked salmon and tonnes of herby goodness. Comforting, but still fresh.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Everything Salmon & Green Pesto Chickpeas batch.
Flake the salmon. Peel the garlic. Add the water, garlic, basil and spinach to a blender and blitz until smooth. Finely grate the Parmesan.
Pour the stock into a saucepan and season with salt. Bring to the boil, then tip in the pasta and cook for half the time stated on the packet. Add a splash of water if it’s looking dry.
Pour in the green spinach mixture along with the leftover chickpeas and flaked salmon. Stir well and cook for the remaining pasta time, until everything’s hot and the pasta’s al dente.
Take the pan off the heat and stir through half the Parmesan. Spoon into bowls and finish with the remaining Parmesan on top. Dig in!

name: Pesto Pasta with Burrata & Crispy Breadcrumbs
description: A silky spinach pesto perfect for little ones, with burrata and a crispy breadcrumb upgrade for grown-ups. This one's perfect for batching and a great freezer sauce staple.
keywords: Spinach Pesto Rigatoni with Burrata & Crispy Crumbs
Spinach Pesto Rigatoni with Burrata & Crispy Crumbs recipe
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings 
Toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 3–4 mins until golden and fragrant. Tip into a bowl to cool.

Add the cooled pine nuts to a high-speed blender with the garlic, baby spinach and 3/4 of the basil. Finely grate in the Parmesan, then squeeze in the lemon juice. Add the cold water and half the olive oil, then blitz until smooth. If it’s too thick, add another splash of water.

If making ahead, now freeze the pesto in cube trays, then transfer to a freezer bag. It’ll keep for up to 6 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge.
Cook the pasta following pack instructions. Drain, then stir through a few tablespoons of the pesto.

For the adults, make the crispy breadcrumb topping. Heat a frying pan over a medium heat and add the remaining extra-virgin olive oil with the panko breadcrumbs. Fry for 4–5 mins, stirring often, until golden and super crisp. Finish with parmesan.

Serve up! 
Kids Plate: Dish out the pasta (add some grated cheese if they'd like).
Parents Plate: Tear the burrata over the pasta and scatter with the crispy breadcrumbs and the remaining basil leaves. Add a twist of black pepper and you're done.

name: Pesto Salmon Orzo Salad
description: A fresh and vibrant orzo salad with air-fried salmon, roasted courgette and juicy cherry tomatoes, all tossed in a zesty mustard dressing and finished with a drizzle of pesto. Cook once and you've got gorgeous lunches for the week.
keywords: Lunch Box: Pesto Salmon Orzo Salad recipe
Lunch Box: Pesto Salmon Orzo Salad
instructions: Cut the courgette into irregular 2cm pieces. Add to a bowl, toss with olive oil, salt and black pepper, then tip into the air fryer basket. Cook at 200°C for 5 mins.

Pat the salmon dry then rub with olive oil, salt, black pepper and fennel seeds. Add the cherry tomatoes to the air fryer basket with the courgettes, then place the salmon on top, skin-side down. Reduce the heat to 180°C and cook for 8-10 mins, depending on the thickness of the salmon. If it’s not fully cooked, continue in one-minute bursts.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Drop in the orzo and cook following packet instructions.
In a large bowl (the same one from earlier to save on washing up), whisk together a glug of olive oil, the juice of the lemon, Dijon mustard and a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Roughly chop the parsley. Remove the salmon from the air fryer and set aside. Tip the roasted veg into the dressing along with the drained orzo and parsley. Mix well.
Spoon the orzo salad into your Tupperware containers, flake the salmon over the top and finish with a drizzle of pesto. Box up and pop in the fridge (these last for up to 3 days). Lunch is done.

name: Pesto Salmon Orzo Salad
description: A fresh and vibrant orzo salad with air-fried salmon, roasted courgette and juicy cherry tomatoes, all tossed in a zesty mustard dressing and finished with a drizzle of pesto. A gorgeous plate that’s perfect for meal-prepping lunch.
instructions: Cut the courgette into irregular 2cm pieces. Add to a bowl, toss with olive oil, salt and black pepper, then tip into the air fryer basket. Cook at 200°C for 5 mins.

Pat the salmon dry then rub with olive oil, salt, black pepper and fennel seeds. Add the cherry tomatoes to the air fryer basket with the courgettes, then place the salmon on top, skin-side down. Reduce the heat to 180°C and cook for 8-10 mins, depending on the thickness of the salmon. If it’s not fully cooked, continue in one-minute bursts.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Drop in the orzo and cook following packet instructions.

In a large bowl (the same one from earlier to save on washing up), whisk together a glug of olive oil, the juice of the lemon, half the Dijon mustard and a pinch of salt and black pepper. Taste and add more mustard, if you like.
Roughly chop the parsley. Remove the salmon from the air fryer and set aside. Tip the roasted veg into the dressing along with the drained orzo and parsley. Mix well.
Serve the orzo salad topped with the salmon and a drizzle of pesto.

name: Pesto Sausage Rolls
description: The humble sausage roll. Here is your bible to making the best little munchies around. With a pestoey twist on a classic, it's the ultimate crowd-pleaser.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Add a drizzle of olive oil to a frying pan. Dice the onion and add it to the pan with 1 tbsp of rosemary. Cook for 4 minutes until the onions are soft and translucent.

Pour the cooked onions into a large bowl. Squeeze out the meat from your sausages into the bowl and season with a pinch of salt, a good grind of pepper and add your pesto. Pat your mozzarella dry with kitchen roll to remove any excess liquid and tear the mozzarella into the bowl. Mix all the ingredients together and set aside.
Pastry time. Take your puff pastry and cut it in half longways. Spoon half of your sausage mixture onto the middle of your puff pastry to create a long sausage, leaving about 2cm around the edges.
Separate your eggs and beat the egg yolk (you can save the egg whites for an omelette or freeze for meringue). Brush the egg yolk over the edges of your puff pastry.

Fold one side of puff pastry over the sausage and seal the edges using a fork. Brush the top of the pastry with egg yolk and sprinkle with the remaining rosemary, the fennel seeds and a pinch of salt. Cut the sausage roll into 8 evenly sized smaller sausage rolls and repeat with the other half of your pastry.
Line a baking tray with baking paper and place the sausage rolls on top. Bake for 45 minutes and dig in! Enjoy!

name: Pesto Steak & Cottage Cheese Bowl
description: A fresh and flavourful high protein steak bowl. Perfect for when you want something light but filling!
keywords: pesto steak and cottage cheese bowl
instructions: Remove the steaks from the fridge and season generously on both sides with salt, set aside.
Get on with your cottage cheese. Roughly mince the olives and sun-dried tomatoes. Stir them into the cottage cheese. Season with pepper and mix everything together. Cover and set aside.

Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat. Pat the steaks dry and drizzle with a little oil on both sides. Place the steaks into the hot pan. Cook the steaks to your desired doneness. Transfer to a plate, cover with foil and leave to rest.

Stir the dressing ingredients together into a large bowl, season to taste with salt and pepper. Thinly slice or mandolin the radishes. Cut the cucumber into quarters, smash the cucumber until it splits and chop into bite sized chunks. Add both into the dressing with the rocket and toss together.
Slice the steaks and share between plates with the cottage cheese and salad.

name: Pesto Veggie Traybake
description: Roasted veggies, the crunchiest ciabatta croutons, with a delicious, rich homemade pesto dolloped on top. It just works.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C.

Pesto time. Add the fresh basil to a food processor with 8 tbsp of olive oil. Finely grate your parmesan and add it to the food processor with half of the garlic, half of the pine nuts and a pinch of salt. Blend until you achieve a creamy pesto consistency, season to taste and set aside for later.

Slice your peppers, onion and courgette. Slice your aubergine and cut each slice into quarters. Add the veg to a large bowl and sprinkle with oregano, fennel seeds, chilli flakes and a big pinch of salt and pepper. Mix through until the vegetables are coated in seasoning.
Spread your veg out onto two baking trays. Keep the cherry tomatoes on the vine and add to both trays. Whack in the oven for 25 minutes.

Crouton time. Chop your ciabatta into bite-sized chunks and add to a large bowl. Add a good drizzle of olive oil over the bread. Crush your remaining garlic and chop the parsley and add it to the bowl. Give it a good mix so that the garlic and parsley fully coat each piece of ciabatta. Season with a pinch of salt and a grind of pepper.

Remove your trays from the oven and spread your garlic croutons onto each tray. Tear and add your mozzarella in the same way. Spoon your pesto evenly over each tray and bake for 10 minutes until the mozzarella is melted.
Sprinkle the remaining pine nuts over both trays and bake for 5 minutes.
Add a final drizzle of olive oil to each traybake and dig in! Enjoy!

name: Pesto and Kale Stuffed Shells
description: Baked pasta is the most comforting meal out there. Fact. We’ve loaded these giant shells up with Sacla' Basil Pesto and ricotta, and she is a beauty.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C/354°F.
Finely slice your garlic.
Heat a little olive oil in a small saucepan and add your garlic. Cook over a gentle heat for 2 mins until fragrant.
Tip in your chopped tomatoes and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 30 mins over a medium heat until your sauce has reduced. Add your crème fraîche, then season to taste with salt and pepper.

Whilst your sauce cooks, finely chop your kale, discarding any tough stalks. Add a little olive oil to a sauté pan set over a medium heat. Add your kale with a pinch of salt, then fry for 5 mins until wilted. Allow to cool slightly.
Transfer your kale to a bowl and add your ricotta, Sacla' Basil Pesto and the zest from your lemon. Give it a good mix, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Cook your pasta shells according to packet instructions. Allow to cool slightly.
Stuff your pesto and kale mixture into the shells.

Pour your tomato sauce into a baking dish and nestle your stuffed shells into it. Tear over your mozzarella ball and evenly distribute it over the surface of your shells. Bake your dish in the oven for 25 mins.
Spoon your pasta onto plates and serve.

name: Pesto-y Summer Orzo
description: Pestoey orzo with lovely salty bursts of flavour from the capers and the olives. Make sure you use Kalamatas! A great summer dish for the MOB.
instructions: Cube your aubergines and cook in a pan without oil. Once cooked, set aside.
Get your orzo on.
Finely chop up a red onion, a handful of parsley and add 2 teaspoons of capers. Pan fry until the onions are translucent.
Add your aubergines and kalamata olives.
Pour in 2 tablespoons of red wine vinegar and allow to evaporate.
Add 2 heaped teaspoons of sun-dried tomato pesto and a tin of plum tomatoes. Mix well. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Mix in the cooked orzo and a handful of chopped parsley leaves. Serve and enjoy MOB!

name: Philly Cheesesteaks
description: American-style subs with tender beef short ribs and melted Swiss cheese. A classic for a reason.
instructions: Pop the short ribs onto a tray and into the freezer for 10-15 mins. Once super cold and firm, use a long, very sharp knife to cut the ribs into thin strips. Cut the onions into a chunky dice.

Preheat your pan over a high heat. Add a shot of olive oil and tip in the onions. Add a pinch of salt and cook for 4-5 mins until softened and beginning to caramelise around the edges. Shimmy the onions over to one side and crank the heat to max. Add the sliced short rib and cook, undisturbed for 2 mins. Now use two spatulas to cut the meat more and break down the slices even further.

Once well coloured on one side, toss the meat through the onions and season generously with salt and black pepper. Lay the sliced cheese over the top, covering the whole pan. Keep cooking – the underside of the steak and onions will get crispier and crispier whilst the top gets melty and gooey.

Split the bread open and spread with mayo. Toast in a dry pan until golden brown. Add a little more mayonnaise and then load with the cheesy steak. Wrap with foil and then allow to steam for a couple of mins. This will allow everything to meld and properly melt. Now slice open and get stuck in.

name: Pickle Brine Roast Chicken With Spring Onion Potato Salad
description: A delicious (and nutritious) recipe. The pickle brine helps to tenderise the meat in this high-protein dinner.
keywords: Pickle Brine Roast Chicken With Spring Onion Potato Salad
instructions: Start by spatchcocking the chicken. Use a strong pair of kitchen scissors to cut along either side of the spine, from the neck to the tail, and remove. Now flip the chicken over and press down on the breast to flatten.

Set a sieve over a large bowl and pour in the jar of pickles. Add your spatchcocked chicken to the brine, topping up with 500ml of water and 10g of salt. Cover and chill for 8-24 hours. Put the pickles back in the jar for later. Go to work, have a nap, go workout, whatever.
Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Pull the chicken out of the brine and pat dry with kitchen paper. Toast off the fennel and coriander seeds in a dry pan and coarsely grind with a pestle and mortar, a spice grinder or with a small pan. Combine with the paprika 2 and 1 tbsp of olive oil. Rub all over the chicken. Halve the garlic bulb and trim the ends of the spring onions.

Lay the spring onions and garlic into a roasting pan and lay the chicken on top, breast side up. Slide into the oven and roast for 40-45 mins, or until the chicken is cooked through. Set aside to rest for 30 mins.
Add the potatoes to a saucepan and cover with cold water. Generously season with salt and bring to a boil. Cook for 15-20 mins until tender. Drain and leave to cool.

Scoop the onions and garlic out of the tray. Finely chop half of the spring onions, the red onion and half the pickles and stir through the potatoes. Finely slice the hispi cabbage and chuck in the bowl too. Fold through the chopped dill, sour cream, and the zest and juice of your lemon. Season with salt and pepper and chuck in any extra pickle juice from the jar.
Serve the chicken to share with the potato sally, remaining pickles and the spring onions and garlic on the side, with extra lemon wedges for squeezin’.

name: Pickled Beetroot and Crispy Mint Salad
description: Pickly bits are essential in a summer salad to cut through the freshness, in this case using beetroot. The crispy mint oil also makes this extra special.
keywords: Pickled beetroot and crispy mint salad recipes
instructions: Finely slice your beetroot into rounds with either a mandoline or a very sharp knife. Pop them in a heatproof bowl.
Add your cumin seeds to a small saucepan, and toast over a low heat for 2 mins until fragrant. Add your apple cider vinegar, 150ml water, and your sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Pour your liquid over your beetroot and set aside.

Finely slice your garlic. Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a frying pan of a medium heat, then add your garlic. Cook for 30 seconds, then add your dried mint. Immediately take your pan off the heat, and allow it to cool.
Cut your tomatoes into chunks. Peel your cucumbers into strips, discarding the seedy middles.
Add your tomatoes to a sieve set over a bowl. Sprinkle over a pinch of salt, then leave to sit for 15 mins.
Tear your olive bread into bite-sized pieces.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Add your bread and fry for a few mins with a pinch of salt until they are crisp and golden.

Once all your ingredients have cooled to room temperature, you can assemble. Add your tomatoes, cucumber, feta and croutons to a bowl with a drizzle of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon. Toss to combine.

Layer about a third of this mixture onto your serving plate, topping with some of your beetroot before continuing on like this for the remaining two layers. Drizzle with your crispy garlic mint oil and a pinch of salt, then serve.

name: Pickled Jalapeño Chicken Soup
description: Warming, comforting and healing, this slightly spicy pickled jalapeño soup is the perfect meal to have when you’re in need of a little TLC.
instructions: Trim, wash and thinly slice the leek. Trim and chop the fennel into 1cm chunks. Pick the dill, discarding the thick stalks. Finely mince the parsley, stalks and all, and thinly slice the garlic.
Pour a drizzle of olive oil into a saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the leek and fennel and cook for 3-5 mins until softened. Add the parsley and garlic, then cook until fragrant.

Add the stock, pickled jalapeños and their brine, and chicken thighs to the saucepan. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 10-15 mins until the chicken is cooked through. Transfer the chicken to a plate.
Add the pasta to the soup and cook following pack instructions. Meanwhile, shred the chicken using two forks and add it back to the soup.

Once ready, taste and season the soup with some more jalapeño brine, if needed. Stir through the dill and divide between bowls. Top with a dollop of soured cream and some freshly cracked black pepper.

name: Pickled Jalapeño Mac & Cheese
description: Mac and cheese is universally known as comfort food. I've combined it with one of my other comforts, cheesy jalapeño nachos form the cinema – making this one of the greatest things you can eat while watching a movie in bed. The secret is the one and only plastic cheese, which gives it that signature flavour. Generously topped with crispy onions, because you deserve it.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Cook the macaroni in lightly salted boiling water for about 10 mins, or a few minutes less than the recommended cooking time on the packet. It will finish cooking in the sauce in the oven.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan and stir in the plain flour. Cook this mixture for about 2 mins. Then slowly drizzle in the milk in three additions, making sure to whisk well after each addition.

Grate in the Cheddar and red Leicester, and add the slices of American cheese, and mix until all the cheese has melted. Finely chop the jalapeños then add to the pan along with the pickling liquid and cooked pasta. Stir everything together and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the cheesy pasta mixture into a baking dish and top it with the crushed tortilla chips, crispy shallots and a generous sprinkle of grated Parmesan.
Bake for 20 mins, or until it's golden and bubbling. Allow to rest for 5 mins, and enjoy.

name: Pico de Gallo
description: A classic pico de gallo is the perfect salsa for welcoming friends. It’s best made a few hours in advance, to really accentuate the taste. It’s one of the most popular salsas in Mexico and everyone has their own version. This is mine. My family would make this salsa for every party or carne asada we had. It’s a simple salsa, but packed with Mexican flavours.
instructions: Dice the tomatoes and onion. Finely chop the jalapeño and coriander. Place everything in a bowl.
Add the lime juice and season with the salt. Mix well and keep in the fridge for at least 30 mins before serving. Serve with totopos (tortilla chips).

name: Pigs In Duvets
description: Sweet, mustardy pigs in a blanket wrapped in flaky pastry. Our version of an American pigs in blankets recipe is the perfect start to a festive meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Unroll the puff pastry sheet. Divide into 16 equal-sized rectangles and cut them out. Place the rectangles onto a baking paper-lined tray, cover and refrigerate until needed.

Mix the honey with 1 tbsp mustard and brush each pig in a blanket with the mixture. Place each glazed pig in a blanket onto the middle of a puff pastry rectangle. Join the two edges and seal using a fork – it should look a little like a sausage roll.

Pick the leaves from the thyme stems. Add the leaves to the salt and massage together. Crack the egg into a small bowl, whisk and brush the egg on top of each roll. Sprinkle thyme salt over the puff, then bake for 20-25 mins until the pastry is golden and the sausages are cooked.
Serve the pigs in duvets with the remaining mustard.

name: Pigs in Blankets Burger with Bread Sauce Mayo
description: Everyone’s favourite Christmas side in burger form. These festive bacon-wrapped sausage burgers are unbelievably good.
keywords: Pigs in Blankets Burger with Bread Sauce Mayo
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan. Thinly slice the onion.

Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large frying pan set over a low-medium heat. Add the sliced onion and a generous pinch of salt then cook gently for 20 mins until softened and starting to caramelise. Add ⅕ of the cranberry sauce and cook for another 5 mins.

While the onions are cooking, in a separate small saucepan, add the bread sauce mix and milk. Set it over a medium heat and bring the mixture to the boil, then turn the heat down to low and simmer for 2-3 mins until thickened. Set aside to cool completely.
Wrap each sausage in a rasher of bacon to make the pigs in blankets. Add to a baking tray then roast in the oven for 20-25 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile, halve the buns and toast them cut side down in the burger pan until golden.
In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise and juice of the lemon with the cooled bread sauce. Season with salt, pepper and ground nutmeg to taste.
Once the sausages are cooked, cluster them in groups of 3 and layer a slice of cheese over each cluster. Place back in the oven for a few minutes until the cheese has melted.

To assemble the burgers, spoon some bread sauce mayo on the bottom of each bun and top with a lettuce leaf. Lay a cluster of cheesy pigs in blankets on top and top with the cranberry sauce onions. Spread more mayo on the other half of the burger bun and pop it on the top.

name: Pimped Up Ramen
description: Steve Mangleshot from Wagamama shows us how to pimp up your basic instant noodles in the final Wok From Halls video.
instructions: Finely chop your garlic and ginger. Slice your spring onions and red chilli. Slice your chicken breasts in half width ways, then slice into thin strips.

Heat a wok over a medium-high heat with a glug of vegetable oil. Tip your chicken into the pan, then add your garlic and ginger. Stir fry for a couple of minutes until your chicken is tender, then add your worcestershire sauce and soy sauce and keep stirring for a couple more minutes until starting to char. Add your spring onions, saving a handful for later, then set aside and keep warm.
Add your miso paste and softened butter to a bowl and give it a good mix until you have a smooth paste. Add your cornflour and stir again.
Cook the eggs for 6 minutes until soft boiled. Run under cold water to prevent them cooking any more, then, once cooled, peel and cut in half vertically.

Pour your water into your wok and bring to a boil. Turn down to a simmer, add your chicken stock cube and your noodles. Cook for a couple of minutes until your noodles are tender, then add your miso paste mixture and simmer for a minute until your mixture has thickened slightly.
Time to serve up. Add your noodles to your bowls and top with your spinach and chicken. Cut your soft boiled eggs in half and sprinkle with sliced red chilli and your remaining spring onions.

name: Pineapple & Mint Margarita
description: Mint adds a lovely refreshing edge to this margarita. It's fresh, it's fruity, it's delicious.
instructions: Cut your pineapple up and weigh up the desired amount, saving a slice for garnish. Also pull out a couple fronds off the top for garnish.
Juice your limes and pick five springs of mint leaves off their stalks.
In a cocktail shaker add your pineapple and mint then using a blunt object squish it down a couple times to juice it.
Add your tequila, agave, lime juice and ice.
Shake vigorously for 15 seconds.
Double strain into your glass over ice.
Garnish with some mint, your reserved pineapple chunk and your pineapple fronds. Enjoy!

name: Pineapple and Coconut Cream Crêpes
description: This is a pineapple twist on my peaches and cream crêpes. These crêpes will take you straight to the beach, holding an ice-cold pina colada. Seema x
instructions: For the crêpe batter blend up the plain flour, milk, eggs and 1 tbsp oil in a blender until smooth. Alternatively, whisk them together really well, and then strain to remove any lumps. Set aside to rest for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, whip up the double cream with the creamed coconut and honey. You may need to gently warm your creamed coconut if it’s too solid.
Drain the pineapple and save the liquid.
Turn on a grill pan or frying pan to high heat and add a drizzle of oil. Fry your pineapple until golden and caramelised. Chop the pineapple into large chunks.
Heat the remaining pineapple juice and add in brown sugar and butter. Reduce to half to make a thick syrup, finishing with a tbsp of your coconut double cream mixture.

Heat a large frying pan and spray with oil. Pour about ¼ of crêpe batter into the pan and swizzle the pan so the batter coats the bottom evenly. Cook on either side for 1 minute or until golden brown.

To assemble, lay out the crêpe flat and spread on your coconut cream. Place on your tinned pineapple and then fold your crêpe in half and then half again. Drizzle with the pineapple syrup and grate on some lime zest.

name: Piri Piri Chicken & Herby Lemon Chickpeas
description: Smoky piri piri chicken on creamy, lemony chickpeas. This one's fresh, fiery, and full of protein. Perfect for your weekly meal prep.
keywords: piri piri chicken and herby lemon chickpeas
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Bash the chicken breasts between two sheets of baking paper until about 1cm thick. Drizzle with half the olive oil, sprinkle over the piri piri seasoning and season well with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a baking tray lined with foil and bake for about 12 mins, or until fully cooked. Set aside then slice before serving.
Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic. Using a vegetable peeler, peel off a few strips of lemon zest. Finely slice the red chilli, if using.

Heat the rest of the olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for a couple of minutes until just golden. Stir through the fennel seeds and chilli and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Pour in the chickpeas along with around half of their liquid, add the lemon zest strips and season well with salt and pepper. Mix, then cover with a lid and simmer gently for 10 mins.
Finely chop the parsley. Take the pan off the heat and stir through the Greek yoghurt and most of the chopped parsley.

Slice the cooked chicken and serve it in a Tupperware container on top of the creamy chickpeas. Finish with a bit more parsley if you fancy. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Piri Piri Chicken & Herby Lemon Chickpeas
description: Smoky piri piri chicken on creamy, lemony chickpeas. This one's fresh, fiery and full of protein.
keywords: piri piri chicken and herby lemon chickpeas
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Bash the chicken breasts between two sheets of baking paper until about 1cm thick. Drizzle with half the olive oil, sprinkle over the piri piri seasoning and season well with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a baking tray lined with foil and bake for about 12 mins, or until fully cooked. Set aside then slice before serving.
Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic. Using a vegetable peeler, peel off a few strips of lemon zest. Finely slice the red chilli, if using.

Heat the rest of the olive oil in a large lidded frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for a couple of minutes until just golden. Stir through the fennel seeds and chilli and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Pour in the chickpeas along with all their liquid, add the lemon zest strips and season well with salt and pepper. Mix, then cover with a lid and simmer gently for 10 mins.
Finely chop the parsley. Take the pan off the heat and stir through the Greek yoghurt and most of the chopped parsley. Add the juice of a wedge of lemon and stir until gorgeous and creamy.
Slice the cooked chicken and serve it on top of the creamy chickpeas. Finish with a bit more parsley if you fancy and a lemon wedge on the side.

name: Piri-Piri Chicken Minestrone
description: Fiery piri-piri sauce brings serious heat to this warming, veg-packed minestrone. Pasta, juicy chicken, and watercress.
instructions: Finely dice the carrot, celery and onion.
Place a pot over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the olive oil followed by the diced veg. Cook for 5–7 mins until softened.
Meanwhile, chuck all the piri-piri sauce ingredients into a blender and blitz until smooth.

Pour the piri-piri sauce into the pot along with the chicken stock. Season with salt and bring to the boil. Once boiling, add the chicken breasts, cover with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Let the chicken poach for 10–15 mins or until cooked through.
Roughly snip the watercress using scissors.
Transfer the cooked chicken to a board and turn the heat back up. Once the soup is boiling again, add the pasta and cook following pack instructions until al dente.
Meanwhile, shred the chicken.

When the pasta is ready, remove the pot from the heat and stir through the shredded chicken and watercress until wilted. Taste and season with salt and pepper if needed. Ladle into bowls and get stuck in.

name: Piri-Piri Roast Chicken
description: Chicken marinated in Mozambican piri-piri sauce then roasted in the oven on a bed of potatoes. We've served this spicy chicken with green onion and lemon.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C. Remove the stalks from the chillies. Peel the garlic cloves. Add the chillies, garlic, tomato purée and olive oil into a blender with the apple cider vinegar and smoked paprika. Blend until smooth, taste and season with salt. Trim, peel and chop the onion into wedges.

Flip the chicken, breast side down. Using some kitchen scissors, cut out the spine/backbone of the chicken. Flip so it’s breast side up and press down onto the breast until you hear a crack. Turn the legs out so the chicken lays flat. Generously season both sides of the chicken with salt and pepper.

Add the potatoes, onion wedges and pour the piri-piri sauce into a roasting tin or ovenproof pan, season with salt and pepper, toss together. Place the chicken on top of the potatoes and slow roast for 2-2.5hrs, until the chicken has coloured and the potatoes are buttery soft. After 1.5 hours, baste the chicken with the piri-piri juices every 20 mins.
Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves. Finely chop half the leaves and all the stalks.

Once the chicken is cooked, transfer to a chopping board to rest for 10-15 mins before carving. Zest ½ the lemon onto the potatoes, and stir through the chopped parsley. Taste and season with some salt and lemon juice.
Share the chicken, potatoes and onions between plates, making sure to drizzle over the chicken juices in the tin. Scatter over the parsley and serve with any remaining lemon wedges.

name: Pistachio & Raspberry Overnight Oats
description: Creamy pistachio butter overnight oats, swirled with raspberry jam and topped with fresh raspberries. Nutty, fruity and ready before you even wake up.
instructions: Add the pistachios to a small frying pan over a medium heat. Gently toast, stirring, for 3-5 mins until starting to colour.

Tip the toasted pistachios into a food processor with the salt and blitz until a fine crumb forms. Add the maple syrup and continue blitzing until the mixture comes together into a paste, the longer you go, the smoother it'll get. Stop when you like the texture.
Tip the pistachio butter into a large bowl, zest the lemon in and add the remaining oat base ingredients, whisking together. Cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 5 hours, or until ready to serve.
To serve, spoon a portion of the oat base into bowls. Add a dollop of vanilla yoghurt, swirl through some raspberry jam and finish with the fresh raspberries and extra pistachios.

name: Pistachio Beef Kebab
description: Beef mince kebabs crusted in pistachios, roasted over charred peppers and tomatoes, served with garlic yoghurt and warm flatbreads. Perfect for when you want BBQ-style food, without turning on the BBQ.
instructions: If using bamboo skewers, soak in hot water until needed. Heat the oven to 220°C.

Drain and chop the peppers into 3-4cm chunks and halve the tomatoes. Finely chop half the parsley, then pick the remaining leaves and thinly slice their stalks. Finely grate half the garlic and half the shallot into a large bowl (or pulse both in a food processor until broken down, then transfer to a bowl). Zest the lemon into the bowl, then add the cumin, the chopped parsley and stalks, and the mince. Season generously with salt and pepper and mix together. Divide into two portions per person (eight portions total) and roll into balls.

Pulse the pistachios in a food processor until a fine crumb forms, then tip onto a plate. Using oiled hands, thread each portion of mince onto a skewer and flatten into a long sausage shape. Roll the kebabs in the pistachio crumb to coat.
Arrange the tomatoes and peppers on a large baking tray, place the skewers on top and drizzle with a little oil. Slide into the oven for 20-25 mins, until fully cooked through.
Meanwhile, finely grate the remaining garlic into the yoghurt. Season with salt, a squeeze of lemon juice and black pepper.

Toast or warm the flatbreads and divide between plates. Top with the roasted veg, kebabs and a dollop of the garlic yoghurt. Finish with a drizzle of any cooking juices, a little olive oil and the remaining parsley leaves. Serve with any remaining lemon cut into wedges.

name: Pizza Fritta
description: This is the most delicious fried dough finished with various toppings. We've used artichokes, burrata and Calabrian chilli but you can choose what you like!
instructions: Blitz the tomatoes smooth with a stick blender. Pour into a sauce pan and bring to boil, turn down heat and simmer for 5-6 mins, season with salt.
Mix water and flour in a bowl, combine till shaggy, leave for 30 mins (this is the autolyse) makes it easier to knead and gives the dough strength.
Crumble in yeast and turn out onto a cold surface. Knead to combine yeast. Then add salt and knead to combine until the dough is smooth and elastic.
At this point I would leave the dough for anywhere between 24 and 72 hours in the fridge.
On the day you using it divide into 8 equal amounts (115g each) and roll into tight balls. Leave to prove again at room temp for 4-6 hours.
Pour 1L veg oil into large deep metal pot, heat to 200°C.
Stretch out the dough balls into pizza shapes (as round as possible) and the correct size for your pan.
With two hands gently drop the stretched dough into the oil (drop away from your to avoid getting flicked with hot oil).
Use a metal spoon to adjust the dough if it has folded on top of itself.
Fry until golden occasionally turning the dough over so both sides are evenly cooked.
Drain on a bit of kitchen roll/blue roll.
Top with the tomato sauce, then ⅓ buratta each, then a few pieces of artichoke and some Calabrian chili with its oil, tear up a few basil leaves then a sprinkle of flaky salt and you’re done!

name: Pizza Soup
description: It's all the things you love about pizza, in slurpable soup form. Trust us: it's delicious.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Halve the tomatoes and peel and cut the onion into wedges. Slice off the top of the garlic bulb and drizzle with a little olive oil and sprinkle over some salt before wrapping it up in some silver foil. Add the tomatoes to a baking tray cut side up, and add the onion and the garlic. Drizzle with oil, then season with salt, pepper and oregano. Put in the oven for 50 mins-1 hour until softened and charred.

When cooked, transfer the veg into a large pan. When cool enough, carefully unwrap the hot garlic and squeeze into the pan. Roughly chop the basil stalks and add into the pan along with the stock, then simmer for 5 mins. Blend smooth with a stick blender, then add the red wine vinegar and season to taste.
Cut the bread into rounds and pop onto a baking tray. top with mozzarella ad parmesan and grill for 5 mins until golden and bubbling.
Heat a splash of oil in a pan and add the pepperoni, cooking until crisp.
Serve the soup in bowls then top with cheese on toast and pepperoni. Grate over some Parmesan and enjoy.

name: Piña Colada Rice Pudding
description: Rice for dessert? This creamy coconut rice with maple rum glazed pineapple will convert even the most stubborn rice pudding skeptics.
keywords: Maple Rum Glazed Pineapple with Coconut Rice
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Get the coconut flakes on a baking tray and place under the grill for 1-3 mins until golden and toasted. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.
Trim and slice the pineapple into 2cm chunks. Add to the baking tray, spreading them out evenly. Place under the grill and cook until starting to char on both sides, flipping halfway through.

Meanwhile, mix the maple and rum together in a small bowl. Once the pineapple has charred, transfer it to a plate, drizzle over the maple mixture and toss. Return to the baking tray and pop under the grill for 1 min until bubbling.

Pour the coconut milk into a saucepan with the vanilla, cinnamon stick, salt and sugar. Mix the cornflour with a splash of water and pour into the coconut milk mixture. Place on a medium heat and whisk until it starts to bubble. Taste and add more sugar, if needed.
Meanwhile, reheat the cooked rice.
Share the rice between bowls, ladle in the coconut sauce and top with the pineapple. Scatter over the coconut flakes and some lime zest.

name: Pińa Colada
description: You'll be able to hear that tropical music when you sip these down
instructions: Cut up the pineapple, saving a slice and a pulling out a leaf for garnish.
Crush your ice (I put it in a tea towel and slam it against hard surface)
Put your crushed ice into a blender with the rum, pineapple juice, cream of coconut and the fresh pineapple chunks.
Blend until smooth.
Pour into a glass of your choosing and garnish with the pineapple piece, leaf and glacé cherry.

name: Plant-Based Butternut Mac & Cheese
description: The ultimate plant-based mac and cheese. The crunchy rosemary and breadcrumb topping is everything.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Place your chopped butternut squash into a baking tray. Add 4 garlic cloves (leave the skin on). Drizzle a generous amount of olive oil, salt and pepper over the top. Mix it all together and place it in the oven for 45 minutes.
Into a pan add 2 tbsp vegan butter with your sage and rosemary.
Once the herbs begin to crisp, add your breadcrumbs, 2 tbsp nutritional yeast and salt. Cook until golden and set aside.
Get your macaroni on (cook in boiling water until al dente).
For the roux, melt the remaining 2 tbsp of butter in a large pan and melt with the smoked paprika. Whisk in the flour and cook for 2 mins.
Slowly drizzle in your oat milk, whisking constantly to form a thick sauce. Add in the remaining 4 tbsp nutritional yeast, mustard and marmite.
Once roasted, add 3/4 of your butternut squash to a blender. Squeeze out the garlic from the skins and add that too. Finally, add 200ml water and blend until smooth.
Pour the blended butternut squash into the roux and mix well. Season with salt and pepper.
Macaroni Time! Add the cooked macaroni to the pan and mix together well.
Spoon your creamy mac and cheese onto a plate and sprinkle with the herby breadcrumbs. Enjoy

name: Plant-Based Fakeaway Kebab
description: A proper kebab shop-style kebab made with Quorn and loaded with all the good stuff. Crunchy pickles, fresh tomatoes and roasted garlic sauce make it a delight.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Slice the top of your bulb of garlic and drizzle it with olive oil and a pinch of salt. Wrap it in a square of kitchen foil, then place on a baking tray and roast for 45 mins.

Meanwhile, prep your fresh garnishes. Halve and core your tomatoes, then finely dice them along with your red onion and parsley. Pop your tomatoes, onion and parsley into a bowl, then squeeze over the juice of your lemon and sprinkle with sumac and a pinch of salt. Set aside until later.
Place your vegan mayo and dairy-free yoghurt into a bowl with the zest of a lemon.

Slice your cucumber in half and scoop out the soft middle. Finely slice into mini crescent shapes. Chop your dill. Place your cucumbers in a bowl and add the dill, the juice of your remaining lemon, your vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt. Give it all a good mix and set aside to soften.
Finely shred your lettuce.

Back to your roast garlic. When cool enough to handle, squeeze the caramelised insides out of the garlic skin and into the mayo mixture. Mix it vigorously with a fork to break up the garlic and add in a pinch of salt.
Pan fry your Quorn Makes Amazing Turkish Style Kebab with a glug of oil for 3-4 minutes over a medium-high heat until warmed through and slightly caramelised.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and toast your flatbreads for a couple of minutes on each side to warm.

Assembly time. Place a flatbread on a plate and spread with some of your roasted garlic sauce. Top with your lettuce, some sumac tomatoes, pickled cucumber and Quorn Makes Amazing Turkish Style Kebab. Serve and enjoy.

name: Plant-Based Mince & Peanut Butter Udon
description: This dish is all in the sauce. Follow the measurements to the letter, it is perfect. The chilli oil. The peanut butter. The five spice. It is incredible.
instructions: Start with the peanut butter sauce. Into a bowl add your peanut butter, chilli oil, soy sauce and 2 tbsp of warm water, mix together until smooth.

Into an oiled wok over a high heat, crumble the mince and add a pinch of salt, a grinding of pepper and your five spice. Cook for about 12 mins or until crispy, breaking up the Meatless Farm Mince with a wooden spoon as you go. Halve your broccoli and add to the wok, and cook off for a few mins.

Whack in your noodles to the wok and toss together. Next, spoon in your peanut butter sauce, slice up your spring onion (saving one for garnish) and add to the wok. Fold everything together and cook for a few mins to get everything hot.
Serve with a drizzle of chilli oil, and a sprinkling of your remaining spring onion and tuck into this delicious dish. Enjoy!

name: Plant-Based Roast Pumpkin Pasta
description: Basil and butternut squash work beautifully together. Topped with the crunchy pumpkin seeds. Go on.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Peel, de-seed and chop up the pumpkin. Add to a roasting tray with salt, pepper and olive oil. Add 5 cloves of unpeeled garlic. Roast until soft and caramelised (about 45 minutes).
Slice the leeks and add to a frying pan with a splash of olive oil. Fry until soft and buttery and set the pan aside.

When the pumpkin is ready, remove from the oven. Place 2/3 of the roasted pumpkin in a blender. Add 50ml of water, salt and pepper. Squeeze the roasted garlic cloves out of their skins into the blender. Blitz until smooth.
Add the pumpkin sauce to the leeks and give it a stir. Add unsweetened yoghurt and your roasted pumpkin. Stir everything together.
Get your pasta on.
Toast your pumpkin seeds in a frying pan on a medium heat with no oil.
Add 3-4 tbsp of the starchy pasta water to your pumpkin sauce. Add a large handful of chopped basil. Season with salt and lots of pepper.
Once the pasta is cooked, drain and add to the sauce. Toss everything together.
Serve the pasta in bowls with your toasted pumpkin seeds scattered on top. Enjoy!

name: Plant-Based Sausage Rolls
description: It's all about the filling, and this one is perfect. Spiced. Squidgy. Tender. Caramelised on the outside. Everything you want from a sausage roll.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C/392°F.

Start by dicing your shallots and adding them to an oiled pan. Cook the shallots for 3 minutes until soft and translucent, stirring often. Chop up your chestnuts, sage and apricots and whack them into the pan. Season with a pinch of salt and your nutmeg. Cook for another 3 minutes and then tip the mixture into a large bowl.
Tear the Meatless Farm Mince into the bowl, season with a pinch of salt and pepper, and mix.
Pastry time. Take your pastry and cut it in half longways. Spoon half of your sausage mixture onto the middle of your pastry to create a long sausage, leaving about 2cm around the edges.

Brush the oat milk over the edges of your pastry. Fold one side of pastry over the sausage and seal the edges using a fork. Brush the top of the pastry with oat milk and sprinkle with your poppy seeds and a pinch of salt.
Cut the sausage roll into 8 evenly sized smaller sausage rolls and repeat with the other half of your pastry.
Line a baking tray with baking paper and place the sausage rolls on top. Bake for 30 minutes or until the pastry is golden and puffed up. Dig in! Enjoy!

name: Plant-Based Tahini "Chicken" Flatbreads
description: These saucy tahini chicken flatbreads are made with vegetarian chicken pieces for a delicious plant-based summer wrap.
instructions: Finely chop all of the herbs and add to a large bowl along with the tahini, a tablespoon of water and the juice of half a lemon. Drizzle in two tablespoons of olive oil and mix well. Set aside.
Grate the clove of garlic into the greek yoghurt, add a tablespoon of water and a pinch of salt. Mix.
Drizzle the Impeckable Chicken Breasts with a splash of olive oil and toss in the ras el hanout.
Heat a frying pan over a medium high heat and add a drizzle of olive oil.
Add the Impeckable Chicken Breasts and cook for about 3 mins on each side until golden brown, remove and slice into roughly 1cm-thick slices.
Spread the yoghurt over the flatbreads, top with the Chicken Breasts, drizzle over the tahini sauce and add a spoonful of pickled cabbage.
Sprinkle over the chilli flakes, drizzle with olive oil and serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Plant-Based Wellington
description: The classic British wellington but with no meat. It's been swapped out for meatless mince, caramelised onions and a marmite gravy sauce. A dish to impress.
instructions: Preheat the oven 200°C/ 392°F.

To start the wellington filling, finely dice one of your onions and celery and grate the carrot. Put them in a saucepan with some olive oil and cook on a low heat until they’re soft, then add finely chopped garlic and rosemary then stir on the heat for one minute.

Whack the onion, celery and carrots into a bowl, add the grated beetroot and Meatless Farm Meat-Free Burgers and the paprika. Get in with your hands to combine it into a mixture and season it well with lots of salt and pepper.
Put the mixture onto a sheet of clingfilm and roll it out into a cylinder and then place it in the fridge to cool while you make your mushroom duxelles.

Very finely chop the mushrooms and put them in the pan with a sprig of thyme and your bay leaves. Fry the mushrooms for about 10 minutes stirring often until you have a softened mixture. Season the mushrooms and pour over the white wine and cook for about 10 minutes until all the wine has been absorbed.

Assembling the wellington is easy, so don’t stress. Take out the pastry sheet and unroll it, then slice out a large enough piece to act as a base for the wellington and place it on a large baking tray. Remove the mixture from the fridge and place it on top of the piece of pastry. Spread the mushroom mixture over the top of the wellington. Slice strips of pastry and plait it over the wellington filling.

Put the tenderstem broccoli on the baking tray too and drizzle with some olive oil, salt and pepper. Place your perfectly assembled wellington and broccoli in the oven for approximately 30 mins, or until the pastry is golden and the broccoli is charred. You may need to take the broccoli out earlier than the wellington so keep an eye on it!

While the veg and wellington are cooking, start making the onion gravy! Slice the remaining onion finely, add a generous glug of oil into the pan and cook the onions very slowly on a low heat until they are super soft and almost mushy.

Once the onion is soft, add the crushed garlic and vinegar and cook it for a further minute. Next, add the flour and stir for another minute until a paste almost forms then add the vegetable stock cube (dissolved in 500ml water) and stir well to ensure there are no lumps in your gravy! Add the tsp of marmite and stir well.
Strain your gravy and put in a gravy boat, but keep the onions as they make a delicious addition to your meal.

Take the wellington and broccoli out of the oven and get ready to plate up! Place your broccoli on the plate, slice into the wellington with a sharp knife and put it on top of the broccoli. Add the onions to your plate and pour the gravy on top for the perfect meatless wellington dinner. Enjoy!

name: Plantain Focaccia with Curry Leaf Oil
description: This sweet, spicy, and salty focaccia has got a lot going for it. Even novice bakers will be able to knock this one out of the park.
keywords: Plantain Focaccia with Curry Leaf Oil
instructions: Start by making the curry leaf oil. Heat the olive oil in a small frying pan over a medium heat. Add the curry leaves to the oil, allow to sizzle and fry until crispy and fragrant. Allow to cool a little, then blend the curry leaves and oil until smooth. Pass through a sieve to remove any stems, then set aside.

To make the dough mix 400ml warm water with the agave and yeast. Allow the yeast to activate for 5-6 minutes till foamy. In the base of the stand mixer add the flour and salt and mix to combine. Then add the foamy water and olive oil and allow to knead for 5-6 minutes in your stand mixer till you have a smooth slightly sticky dough.

Grease a 35 x 25cm rectangle roasting tray with some of the curry leaf oil and transfer the dough into the tin. Spread it out as far as it can go with your hands, then cover tightly with cling film. Allow to rise in a warm place until doubled for 45 mins to 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Once the dough has doubled in size, lightly oil your hands and spread the dough into the corners. Cut the plantain into rounds, not too thin! Make dimples in the dough using your fingers and add the plantain all of the dough in lines. Add more of that wonderful curry oil on top of the dough and add flaky sea salt on top.
Allow to bake for 20-25 minutes until golden and crispy. Remove from the tin, slice up and serve warm with extra curry leaf oil for dipping.

name: Poached Chicken & Ginger Broth
description: Gently poached in a ginger and spring onion broth, this chicken comes out super juicy and packed with delicate flavour. Eat it warm with rice or shred it cold into salads.
instructions: Pop the chicken into a large pot and cover with cold water or chicken stock, if you’ve got some knocking about. Chop the spring onions into big chunks. Roughly slice the ginger and smash the garlic. Chuck it all into the pot with the salt.

Set the pot over a high heat and bring it up to a proper rolling boil. Turn the heat down to a simmer, and cook the chicken for 20 mins. After the 20 mins is up, turn off the heat. Whack a lid on and leave it to poach gently in the hot liquid for 90 mins. This is known as a steep method to cook the chicken.

After 90 mins, take off the lid and remove the chicken. Leave it to rest at room temperature for at least another 30 mins. Remove the skin and set aside for later (you'll use this for the remix recipe Poached Chicken, Garlic Rice, Ginger & Chilli Sauce). Carve off the breasts and shred the legs.
Strain the broth into a bowl or jug, chucking out the spring onions, ginger and garlic. Don’t waste that broth, it’s gold. Perfect for sipping or spooning over rice.

name: Poached Chicken & Gravy Rice
description: Think of your favourite Chinese takeaway (meat and lots of gravy on rice), all done at home, fuss-free and packed with comforting flavour.
instructions: For the chicken, add the rock sugar and a splash of water to a saucepan set over a medium heat. Stir thoroughly for around 2 mins to dissolve the sugar. Keep stirring for 5 mins – the sugar will slowly caramelise and turn golden brown.

Cut the roots off the spring onion. Add to the pan along with the chicken thighs, whole garlic cloves (skin on), ginger (whole), cinnamon stick, star anise, water, a big pinch of salt and the light and dark soy sauces. Put the lid on and turn the heat up to high. Once boiling, lower the heat to low and cook for 25 mins.

For the rice, finely mince the garlic cloves. Cut the ginger into slices then lay flat and slice into matchsticks. Cut and discard the roots off the spring onion. Wash the rice in a bowl until the water is murky, then discard the water and repeat two more times, or until the water is clear, then drain the water completely.

Heat a saucepan over medium heat and add the vegetable oil. Add the minced garlic, ginger matchsticks and spring onion, then stir and fry for 1 min. Add the rice, a pinch of salt and the chicken stock. Stir once to combine and put the lid on, then turn the heat up to high and bring to the boil.

As soon as the water is boiling, turn the heat down to the lowest setting. Set a timer for 18 mins (don’t take the lid off during this time). Once cooked, turn the heat off and set aside, keeping the lid on until ready to serve.

For the garnish, slice the spring onions into thirds, then slice each third lengthways, as thin as possible, into strips. Cut the coriander into thirds, around 2 inches long. Transfer the spring onion and coriander to ice-cold water.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove it from the liquid and transfer to a plate. Discard all the aromatics and leave the broth in the saucepan over a low heat.

To a mug, add the cornstarch and equal parts water. Stir well to combine then slowly drizzle this slurry into the simmering broth while stirring, to avoid any lumps. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon: if too thin, add more cornstarch slurry; if too thick, add a splash of cold water. Taste for seasoning, adding a pinch of salt and more light soy sauce if lacking.

Slice the cooked chicken into strips. Divide the rice between two shallow plate bowls, then add the sliced chicken on top and drizzle over a generous amount of gravy. Drain the spring onion and coriander, then use as a garnish. Enjoy!

name: Poached Chicken Breast
description: These perfectly juicy chicken breasts are actually super easy to make, served with garlicky rice and an addictive spring onion sauce for the perfect meal prep.
instructions: Pop the water, spring onions, garlic cloves and salt in a large saucepan, set over a high heat and bring to the boil.
Once boiling, throw in the chicken breasts, bring back to a simmer, pop the lid on and turn off the heat. Leave untouched for 25 mins. The residual heat will cook the chicken.
Using tongs, remove the chicken from the liquid and set aside to cool. Once cool enough to handle, slice the chicken.
Divide between Tupperware containers with your favourite base, side and dressing and store in the fridge until needed.

name: Poached Chicken Breast With Crispy Chilli Oil
description: These perfectly juicy chicken breasts are actually super easy to make, served with garlicky rice and an addictive spring onion sauce for the perfect meal prep.
keywords: Poached Chicken Breast With Crispy Chilli Oil
Poached Chicken Breast With Crispy Chilli Oil recipe
instructions: Pop the water, whole spring onions, garlic cloves and salt in a large saucepan, set over a high heat and bring to the boil.
Once boiling, throw in the chicken breasts, bring back to a simmer, pop the lid on and turn off the heat. Leave untouched for 25 mins. The residual heat will cook the chicken.
Using tongs, remove the chicken from the liquid and set aside to cool. Once cool enough to handle, slice the chicken.
Top with your favourite crispy chilli oil and store in the fridge with your favourite base and side for a great make-ahead meal.

name: Poached Chicken, Garlic Rice & Spring Onion Sauce
description: These perfectly juicy chicken breasts are actually super easy to make, served with garlicky rice and an addictive spring onion sauce that makes for a super satisfying (and healthy) dinner.
keywords: Garlic Butter Rice & Spring Onion Sauce
instructions: Make the rice. Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear. Roughly chop the shallots into chunks and peel the garlic cloves. Throw both into a food processor and pulse until finely chopped (or finely chop by hand).

Pop a medium sized saucepan over a medium heat and add the butter. Once melted, throw in the shallot and garlic mix and cook for 10-12 mins until caramelised. Add the salt and sugar and cook for a further minute. Deglaze the pan with the dark soy sauce, scraping up any browned bits on the bottom.

Tip in the washed rice followed by the chicken stock. Bring to the boil then pop the lid on and reduce the heat to as low as possible. Cook for 12 mins, then turn the heat off and let sit for 15 mins.

For the chicken, pop the water, spring onions, garlic cloves and salt in a large saucepan, set over a high heat and bring to the boil. Once boiling, throw in the chicken breasts, bring back to a simmer, pop the lid on and turn off the heat. Leave untouched for 25 mins. The residual heat will cook the chicken. Then, using tongs, remove the chicken from the liquid and set aside to cool. Once cool enough to handle, slice the chicken.

For the sauce, finely slice the spring onions and mince the ginger. Add both to a heatproof bowl along with the salt, MSG and sugar. Heat the vegetable oil over a high heat in a small pan until smoking then carefully pour the hot oil over the spring onion mixture. Mix and set aside to marinate for at least 5 mins.
For the garnish, slice up the cucumber and set aside.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the sliced chicken and cucumber, along with the spring onion sauce. Dig in!

name: Poached Chicken, Garlic Rice & Spring Onion Sauce
description: These perfectly juicy chicken breasts are actually super easy to make, served with garlicky rice and an addictive spring onion sauce they make a great make-ahead lunch to take to work.
keywords: Garlic Butter Rice & Spring Onion Sauce
Garlic Butter Rice & Spring Onion Sauce
instructions: Make the rice. Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear. Roughly chop the shallots into chunks and peel the garlic cloves. Throw both into a food processor and pulse until finely chopped (or finely chop by hand).

Pop a medium sized saucepan over a medium heat and add the butter. Once melted, throw in the shallot and garlic mix and cook for 10-12 mins until caramelised. Add the salt and sugar and cook for a further minute. Deglaze the pan with the dark soy sauce, scraping up any browned bits on the bottom.

Tip in the washed rice followed by the chicken stock. Bring to the boil then pop the lid on and reduce the heat to as low as possible. Cook for 12 mins, then turn the heat off and let sit for 15 mins.

For the chicken, pop the water, spring onions, garlic cloves and salt in a large saucepan, set over a high heat and bring to the boil. Once boiling, throw in the chicken breasts, bring back to a simmer, pop the lid on and turn off the heat. Leave untouched for 25 mins. The residual heat will cook the chicken. Then, using tongs, remove the chicken from the liquid and set aside to cool. Once cool enough to handle, slice the chicken.

For the sauce, finely slice the spring onions and mince the ginger. Add both to a heatproof bowl along with the salt, MSG and sugar. Heat the vegetable oil over a high heat in a small pan until smoking then carefully pour the hot oil over the spring onion mixture. Mix and set aside to marinate for at least 5 mins.
For the garnish, slice up the cucumber and set aside.

To store, divide the rice between Tupperware containers and top with the sliced chicken. Pop the cucumber in its own separate container and the spring onion sauce in another. Get everything in the fridge.

When ready to eat, pop the chicken and rice container, with the lid loosely on but not sealed, in the microwave for 60 seconds or until piping hot. Let it sit for another 60 seconds before removing the lid. Top with the spring onion sauce and some cucumber slices, and a drizzle of your favourite chilli oil.

name: Poached Chicken, Garlic Rice, Ginger & Chilli Sauce
description: Garlicky rice cooked in golden chicken broth, juicy poached chicken leftovers, a fresh sugar snap salad and a spicy, buttery sauce to tie it all together.
instructions: Make the Poached Chicken & Ginger Broth.
Slice the leftover chicken skin into small pieces. Heat a large saucepan over a medium heat and fry your reserved chicken skin until golden and crispy. Scoop it out and set aside.

Peel and thinly slice half of the garlic cloves. Add to the pan and fry in the rendered fat for 1–2 mins until golden. Stir in the washed rice, then pour 125ml (per serving) of your leftover poaching broth and a big pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, cover, then turn the heat down and simmer for 12 mins. Kill the heat and leave to sit for 10 mins.

Finely chop the remaining garlic cloves. Peel and grate the ginger. Melt the butter in a small pan set over a low heat, then cook the garlic and ginger until fragrant. Stir in the sriracha, oyster sauce and lime juice. Simmer for 1 min, then add another 2.5 Tbsp (per serving) of the leftover poaching broth. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Meanwhile, gently warm the poached chicken in a pan of hot broth over a low heat. Don’t boil, just heat it through so it stays juicy.
Thinly slice the sugar snaps and roughly chop the coriander. Toss together with a splash of lime juice and a pinch of salt to make a quick salad.
To serve, spoon the garlicky rice onto each plate, top with the warm chicken leftovers, a generous drizzle of the sauce, a handful of the sugar snap salad and a scatter of crispy chicken skin.

name: Poached Eggs with Green Chilli Butter
description: A twist on the much loved Turkish egg dish, çılbır. We’re putting it on toast and adding some greens and drizzling over an incredible herby green chilli butter.
keywords: Poached Eggs With Green Chilli Butter
instructions: First up, make your chilli butter. Melt the butter in a small pan over a low heat and gently cook until browned and starts to smell nutty.
Meanwhile, finely chop your mint, coriander stems, and then the green chilli (seeds and all), place in a heatproof bowl. Pour the hot butter onto the chilli mixture, season with salt.

Peel and finely chop the garlic. Heat 3 tbsps of oil in the empty frying pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for 1-2 mins, then add in the greens. Keep stirring until wilted. Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Add to a blender with 20ml of olive oil and blend until smooth. Stir through the yoghurt.

Bring a pot of water to the boil. Meanwhile, sieve the eggs to remove the watery whites and transfer into a ramekin. When the water is bubbling, turn the heat down to low, gently plop the egg into the water and cook the egg for 4 mins until set, remove the egg with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper.
Cut two slices of sourdough and toast.
Get your bread and top with the yoghurt, poached eggs and the green chilli oil. Garnish with coriander leaves and lemon zest before tucking in.

name: Poached Soy Salmon Rice Bowl
description: A quick dinner with big flavours. Poaching the salmon in mirin, soy and aromatics is an easy way to get perfectly tender fish while making a sweet sticky sauce at the same time.
instructions: Rinse the rice twice in cold water until the water runs clear then drain. Get the rice and the water in a saucepan and leave to soak for 30 mins. Make sure your butter is fridge-cold.

Pop the lid on the pan and set it over a high heat. Bring to a boil then turn the heat down to low and cook for 11 mins. Remove from the heat and set aside, with the lid still on, for at least 10 mins or until needed.
While the rice is cooking, give the ginger a bash with the back of a knife then add to a saucepan along with the whole spring onion, mirin, light soy sauce, sake (if using) and brown sugar.

Set the saucepan over a high heat and bring the liquid to a boil. Gently drop the salmon fillets in, then cover with a lid. Reduce the heat to low-medium. Cook for 8-10 mins until the salmon is just cooked through.
Meanwhile, mince the garlic. For the garnish, finely slice the chives, cut the nori into matchsticks and cut the lemon into wedges.

Transfer the cooked salmon to a plate and discard the spring onion and bashed ginger. Return the saucepan to a high heat, add the minced garlic and cook the mixture for 1-2 mins until reduced and thickened. Remove from the heat, add the cold butter and swirl the pan until incorporated.

Using your fingers or a fork, gently flake the salmon fillets into large chunks. Divide the rice between bowls and top with the flaked salmon and a generous serving of the sauce. Finish with the chives, shredded seaweed and lemon wedges.

name: Pollo Piccante
description: 6 ingredients create a thing of beauty. I've used my favourite stock Boosh Bone Broth here from Ocado to create a wonderfully simple yet punchy dish. Ben x
instructions: Butterfly your chicken breasts. Pop them in a bowl and season them generously with salt, pepper and olive oil.

Heat a frying pan over a medium high heat. Add a glug of olive oil, then get your chicken in the pan. Sear your chicken for a couple of mins on each side, then remove it from the pan and set aside until later.
Peel and slice your cloves of garlic. Finely slice your peppers. Roughly chop your parsley.

Add your peppers, garlic and chilli flakes to the chicken pan and cook them for 10 mins until softened. Add half of your stock to deglaze the pan, scraping the bottom with your spoon to lift off all the caramelised bits.

Add your remaining stock and white wine into the pan, then bring to a gentle simmer. Get your chicken back in the pan and cook it for 2 mins. Flip over and cook for 2 mins more. By this time, your sauce should be beautifully reduced.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then sprinkle with your chopped parsley and serve.

name: Polyphenal Salad with Roasted Carrots & Cauliflower
