description: A delicious autumnal salad with roasted veggies and tahini yoghurt. This one is packed with polyphenols, which are rocket fuel for your gut microbes.
keywords: Polyphenal Salad with Roasted Carrots & Cauliflower
Polyphenal Salad with Roasted Carrots & Cauliflower recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan.
Roughly chop up your carrots and cauliflower and place on a tray with the unpeeled garlic cloves, a drizzle of olive oil and a sprinkle of salt. Roast for 25-30 mins, turning halfway.
In a bowl, mix together the yoghurt, tahini, roasted garlic, a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon.
Separate your radicchio leaves and roughly chop your parsley.
Spread your tahini yoghurt mixture onto a plate and top with the roasted vegetables, radicchio, pumpkin seeds and fresh parsley (you can use any fresh herbs you like).

name: Pomegranate & Pistachio Pavlova Wreath
description: Whip up your British Lion eggs to make a delicious pavlova. Piled high with fruit and pistachios, this will be a beautiful centrepiece on your Christmas table.
instructions: Pre-heat your oven to 140ºC/284ºF then roughly chop your pistachios.

Separate your British Lion egg whites and yolks, saving your yolks for another meal – perhaps a hollandaise sauce for a tasty way to start the day. Place your egg whites in a large bowl and whisk to stiff peaks with electric beaters.

Add a spoonful of sugar and whisk again until your mixture forms stiff peaks. Add more sugar and whisk again, continuing in this way until all of the sugar has been added and you have a thick and glossy mixture.
Add the cornflour and half of the chopped pistachios and gently fold in until totally incorporated.

Line a large baking tray with parchment and gently spoon your mixture into a large circle on your tray, allowing odd peaks to stick up to give texture. Gently smooth out the top to accommodate your toppings later.
Bake for 1 hour, or until you have a crisp, white shell and leave to cool completely.

Add your double cream and icing sugar to a bowl and whisk until it forms thick, soft peaks, being careful not to over-whip it - it should look smooth, not fluffy. Add your yoghurt and fold through with a spoon.
Deseed your pomegranate and discard the skin.
Add your cream to the top of your pavlova and finish with your raspberries, pomegranate seeds, remaining chopped pistachios and mint. Serve and enjoy!

name: Pomegranate Pork Belly Flatbreads with Tomato Ginger Salad
description: A vibrant, juicy, sticky, porky number that's absolutely perfect for a summery lunch. You’re going to love it.
keywords: Pomegranate Pork Belly Flatbreads With Tomato Ginger Salad
instructions: Cut the pork belly into 3cm chunks and pop into a large saucepan. Cover with cold water and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 4-5 mins, skimming off any scum that floats to the surface. Drain the pork and rinse out the pan.

Smash the head of garlic, set 1 clove aside, then peel and crush the rest. Peel, halve, and thinly slice both your onions, then set one aside with the garlic clove from earlier. Roughly chop 50g of the ginger. Pick the leaves from the parsley, keeping the stalks.

Add 2 tbsp of olive oil to the pan and set over a high heat. Brown off the pork belly in batches until golden brown. Now chuck in the crushed garlic cloves, half the onion, the ginger and all of the parsley stalks. Just cover with water, around 900ml, season with salt and bring to simmer. Braise for 30-40 mins until the pork is just tender.

While the pork is braising combine 2 tbsp of the molasses with the juice of half a lemon and 2 tbsp of olive oil. Grate in the remaining ginger and whisk to combine, taste and season as you like. Cut the tomatoes into chunks and chuck into the pomegranate and ginger vinaigrette. Set aside to marinate.

Add the tahini to a bowl and finely grate in the remaining garlic clove. Whisk in enough water to produce a light, creamy tahini sauce, the texture of yoghurt. Sprinkle the sumac over the remaining sliced onions and massage in with salt and the juice of half a lemon. Set aside.

Preheat the grill to high. Scoop the pork out of the broth and brush with the 4 tbsp molasses. Lay out on a lined baking tray and stick under the grill until crispy and gnarly, brushing now and then with the molasses. Chuck the flatbreads onto the tray and grill for 1-2 mins until toasty.

Toss the parsley leaves through the tomato salad. Set each flatbread down on a large plate and add a swoosh of tahini sauce, a handful of tomato salad and some of the crispy pork. Finish with the sumac onions and chop up the remaining lemon into wedges. Add a wedge to each plate and serve.

name: Ponzu Soba Salad With Crispy Salmon & Pickles
description: This is a noodle dish that feels so wholesome and nourishing but so moreish at the same time. The bright lemon zest, umami soy sauce and wonderfully fatty salmon wrap around the buckwheat noodles so well.
keywords: Ponzu Soba Salad With Crispy Salmon & Pickles
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil over a medium-high heat.
Pat dry the salmon fillets with kitchen paper, then sprinkle with salt all over. Set aside on a plate.
Thinly slice the chilli and add to a small bowl with the vinegar and salt and set aside to pickle.
Peel and thinly slice the ginger and garlic. Slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens. Add the spring onion whites to a small bowl and set aside.
Dice the courgette into 1cm cubes. If using frozen peas, add to a bowl of room temperature water and set aside.
Combine all the mock ponzu ingredients into a small bowl.

Cook the soba noodles in the boiling water following packet instructions then drain and rinse very well. Shake off any excess water then return the noodles to the pan you cooked them in. Drizzle with sesame oil, then stir through the spring onion greens and a pinch of salt.

Drizzle some sesame oil on the salmon skins. Heat a glug of neutral oil in a frying pan set over a high heat. Place the salmon in the pan, skin side down. Turn the heat down to medium and cook for 2-3 mins. Then, flip over and cook for 30 seconds. Remove from the heat and set aside for now.

Into the same pan, add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 min until fragrant. Add the diced courgettes and cook for about 5 mins until caramelised and slightly charred. Turn off the heat, squeeze in the juice of ½ the lemon, toss through the peas and season with a pinch of salt.
Pile the noodles into a serving bowl and top with the greens, some ponzu and the salmon. Scatter over the pickled chilli and some of the spicy vinegar.

name: Popcorn Cauliflower
description: We have the perfect "popcorn sauce" - sweet, sticky and tangy. When you toss the cauliflower through it, magic happens.
instructions: In a bowl, mix together your cornflour, plain flour with a sprinkling of salt and pepper. Add a splash of water, adding bit by bit to the flour mix, stirring continuously until you have a smooth batter.
Heat a pan with vegetable oil, ready for frying.
Slice your cauliflower into medium-sized florets. Coat your cauliflower florets in the cornflour mixture.
Once your oil is hot, submerge your cauliflower and fry them for 6 minutes until slightly browned. Remove and set aside.
Get your rice on (follow pack instructions).

For the sauce, add a tbsp of vegetable oil to a pan. Grate your garlic and ginger and add to the pan. Cook these for 30 seconds, then add your sweet chilli, sriracha, vinegar and soy sauce. Stir everything together and bubble away for a couple of minutes until nicely combined.
In to a small glass, add 1 tsp of the cornflour and mix with 2 tbsps of water. Pour this into the sauce.
Once the sauce is nice and thick, add in your cauliflower, making sure to coat them in the sauce. Serve the cauliflower on a bed of steaming rice and get stuck in!

name: Poppadom Nachos Chaat
description: These chaat-inspired nachos are banging. Mini poppadoms coated in tangy, spicy sauces. Topped with fresh bits. A great snack for an Amazon Prime night in.
instructions: Blend up 150g yoghurt, coriander, ¾ of the mint, ginger, green chilli and the juice of ½ lemon in a food processor. Season with salt and set aside.
Finely chop up the mint and red onion. Slice the tomato in half and scoop out the insides. Chop into a small dice.

Lay out your poppadoms on a large platter. Drizzle on the remaining 50g plain yoghurt along with your spicy green chutney and your tomatoes and onions. Next, layer on the tamarind sauce and mango chutney. Finish the platter off with finely chopped mint, pomegranate seeds, and a sprinkle of chaat masala. Serve immediately.

name: Poppy's 15-Hour Potato
description: Poppy O’Toole came to the studio and made her famous 15-hour potato. Crispy, golden bars of indulgent potato, worth every second.
instructions: Peel and slice the potatoes very thin on a mandoline, or with a sharp knife.

Add the cream to a medium saucepan. Smash the garlic cloves and add to the cream. Set over a medium heat and bring to a simmer. Simmer the cream with the garlic for 5-10 mins until it has thickened a little. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the thinly sliced potato to the cream and toss to thoroughly coat.
Preheat the oven to 130°C.
Line a (roughly) 29cm by 19cm tin with parchment and pour in the creamy potatoes. Arrange the potatoes in layers, they don’t have to be exact just flat.

Add a piece of parchment to the top of the potato cake and a layer of baking beans on the top. This helps to cement the spuds together. Slide into the oven for 2-3 hours or until you can push a knife easily through the cake.

Once cooked, remove from the oven and pop another tray, or something flat on top and weigh it down with tins of beans, a bag of sugar, or whatever you’ve got. Leave to cool to room temperature then place in the fridge for at least 12 hours, or overnight.
Once set, turn out your potato cake and unwrap. Cut your slab of spuds into your desired shape.
Fill a deep pan with vegetable oil and preheat to 170°C. Carefully lower in your potatoes and deep fry until golden and crispy.
Season with flaky salt and enjoy.

name: Porcini Mushroom Spaghetti
description: You could never imagine that a vegan pasta could be so savoury. Rich with porcini mushrooms and creamy JÖRD Oat Drink, this is the silkiest spaghetti about.
instructions: Warm your oat milk in a saucepan over a medium heat, or in a heatproof jug in the microwave.
Add your porcini mushrooms and leave to soak for 15 mins.
Finely chop your garlic.

Drain the liquid from your porcini mushrooms, reserving it to use later. Place your rehydrated mushrooms into a food processor along with your chestnut mushrooms and pulse until you have small chunks.
Heat a large sauté pan on medium heat. Tip in your mushrooms with a pinch of salt, and cook for 5 mins until the mushrooms are reduced and really caramelised.
Get a pot of water on to boil. Season generously with salt, then tip in your pasta and cook until al dente.

Add your tomato purée, garlic and thyme leaves to the mushroom pan and cook for 2 mins. Tip in your flour and cook out for 1 min, then gradually pour in your mushroom-infused oat milk, beating all the while. Let it simmer for a few mins to thicken.

Get a ladle of your pasta water in the pan, then tip your pasta into the pan. Toss to coat the pasta, adding more pasta water if needed to get a super shiny sauce. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon your pasta onto plates, then garnish with olive oil, more thyme leaves and chopped parsley. Serve it up!

name: Pork & Fennel ‘Marry Me’ Pasta
description: Crispy fennel-spiked pork piled over creamy, vodka-laced tomato pasta with wilted spinach and loads of parmesan. It’s rich, a little bit spicy and date night worthy.
keywords: pork and fennel marry me pasta
instructions: Zest the lemon and lightly crush your fennel seeds with the back of a knife or with a pestle and mortar. Slice the chives for your garnish and set aside. Then finely dice your shallots, grate the garlic and parmesan for the pasta sauce ready to throw in later.

Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the pork mince and fry for 10 mins, until deeply browned and crispy at the edges, breaking it up as it cooks. Stir through the crushed fennel seeds, chilli flakes, oregano, lemon zest and a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Cook for another minute until fragrant, then remove from the pan and set aside.
Meanwhile, bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the fusilli until al dente. Reserve a good splash of pasta water before draining.

Returning to the frying pan you used for the mince, add the olive oil to start the sauce. Chuck in the shallots with a pinch of salt and cook for 5 mins, until soft and translucent, then add the garlic and cook gently for another 30 seconds. Stir in the tomato purée and cook it out until it darkens and turns glossy. Deglaze with the vodka and let it bubble for a minute.

Lower the heat and stir through the crème fraîche with a splash of reserved pasta water to create a silky sauce. Remove from the heat and mix in the parmesan until melted and smooth. Add the pasta and spinach, tossing until the spinach wilts and the sauce coats every piece. Loosen with extra pasta water if needed.
Spoon into bowls and top generously with the crispy fennel pork. Finish with chopped chives, extra parmesan and plenty of black pepper.

name: Pork Belly Benedict With Gochujang Hollandaise
description: A rich and decadent brunch recipe that's perfect for a long, lazy weekend. Pork belly for breakfast? Go on then.
keywords: Pork Belly Benedict With Gochujang Hollandaise
Pork Belly Benedict With Gochujang Hollandaise recipe
instructions: Ribbon the cucumber and apple and finely slice your green chilli.
Add the above to a pickle of rice vinegar, water, salt and sugar.
Create the marinade by mixing teriyaki, dark soy, lime and rice vinegar.
Marinate pork belly (in strips) before adding to a covered dish and roast for 45 mins at 180°C.
Remove the cover from the dish and further cook for 45 mins until dark and crispy.
To make the hollandaise, vigorously whisk the egg yolks and rice vinegar until frothy.
In a separate pan, slowly melt butter and gochujang together until warm.
Gradually pour the melted butter mix into the egg yolks and continue to whisk. Once mixed, set aside. You can slowly reheat later if needed.
Poach the eggs until almost done and set aside, allowing to cook through.
Toast the crumpet and bring everything together.
Top the Benedict with sesame seeds (we like a mixture of white and black) and long slices of spring onion.

name: Pork Belly Sriracha Tacos
description: Pork belly, marinated in honey, garlic and spicy sriracha. Roasted until perfectly crispy and slapped in a taco. Well, what more do you want?
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C.
Flip the pork belly so it’s skin side down, season with salt and lots of black pepper and score the flesh in a diamond pattern.
Mix the honey, finely grated garlic cloves, rice vinegar with half of the sriracha. Tip this onto the meat side of the pork belly and brush over. Keep the skin clean.

Lay two sheets of foil out on your work surface or chopping board and lay the pork belly, marinade side down, on top. Wrap the foil up and around the meat of the pork belly, leaving just the skin exposed. Rub the skin with a little olive oil and season liberally with salt. Set the whole lot onto a baking tray and slide into the oven for 2 hours and 30 mins. Check on the pork after 30 mins and adjust the foil around it. The meat will have shrunk and you want to foil nice and tight.
Meanwhile, mix the miso and the mayonnaise and pop into a little bottle or piping bag, this is totally optional, but makes for a nice finishing move/drizzle pattern when plating your tacos.
Finely shred the cabbage with a knife or speed-peeler and finely slice the red onion.

When the pork belly has had 2 hours 30 mins, crank the oven to max and watch that skin turn to crackling. This will take 15-20 mins. Don’t worry if the marinade starts to char a little, you want that.
Allow the pork to rest for 10-15 mins, then slice with a bread knife.

Warm the tortillas and build your tacos. Start with some miso mayo, shredded cabbage, red onion and top with crispy pork belly. Finish with extra mayo and sriracha. Serve with lime wedges and get stuck in.

name: Pork Carnitas Tacos
description: Rich and tender slow-cooked shredded pork, served in corn tortillas. A popular way of cooking pork in the centre states of Mexico, this one is even better when made the day before.
instructions: Dice the pork belly and shoulder into about 4cm chunks then place the meat in a large bowl. Squeeze in the juice from the orange and add the salt. Cover with cling film and pop in the fridge for half an hour.

Meanwhile, make the salsa verde: peel the onion and garlic cloves and add them to a saucepan along with the fresh tomatillos. Cover them with water. Bring to a boil over a medium heat then lower the heat and simmer for 10 mins. Meanwhile, roughly chop the coriander.

Strain the vegetables from the water (don’t discard the water yet) and transfer them to a blender, adding the coriander, salt and pinch of caster sugar. Blend until smooth. If the salsa is too thick, add a splash of the water until it’s the desired consistency. Cover and set aside until ready to serve.

When the pork has marinated, melt the lard in a large cast iron pot set over a medium heat. Stir through the garlic cloves (you can leave their skins on), herbs and peppercorns followed by the pork meat, making sure that the meat is properly coated and submerged in the lard.
Cook over a medium heat until the lard starts boiling steadily then lower the heat, cover with the lid and cook for 15 mins.
Pour the Coca-Cola and water over the meat, cover with the lid and let the carnitas cook slowly on a low heat for 2 more hours.
When the pork cooking time is nearly up, prep your toppings: finely chop the onion and coriander and cut the lime into wedges.
Once the meat is tender and falling apart easily, remove the pan from the heat and set aside to rest while you warm the tortillas.
Heat a dry non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the corn tortillas, one at a time, and heat for 15-30 secs on each side. Wrap them in a tea towel to keep warm.
Using a knife, remove and discard the fat from the meat. Chop the pork meat roughly and serve it on a platter.
Place everything on the table and let everyone help themselves to build their own steak tacos!

name: Pork Chops With Feta, Tomato & Cherry Salad
description: Juicy pan-fried pork chops with a refreshing tomato, feta, and cherry salad. This is a great showcase of how to properly deploy seasoning.
instructions: Season the pork chops well with salt and set aside for 10 mins.
Thinly slice the shallots into rounds, separating the rounds into individual rings. Tip into a bowl and add the vinegar. Set aside for 5 mins to quickly pickle.
Now it’s time to marinate the other veggies. Chop the tomatoes into random chunks and toss into a bowl. Thinly slice your courgette and add to the bowl. Pit the cherries and add to the bowl
Season well with salt and pepper. Tear in the dill and toss through olive oil, stir the shallots through the sally. Leave this to hang out for 30 mins.

Preheat a large frying pan with olive oil over a medium heat. Cook the salted chops, fat-side down for 3-4 mins to render. Once the fat side is golden brown and crispy, sear each side of the chop. Cook, turning every minute or so until a deep golden brown and cooked to your liking. I like to cook them medium.
Pull the chops out of the pan and onto a tray, pouring over any residual fat left in the pan. Rest for 10 mins. Carve the rested chops off the bone and into thick slices. Transfer to warm plates.
Tip the salad onto the plates and top with feta, black pepper, chilli flakes and extra oregano.

name: Pork Dumpling Sando
description: Juicy and flavoursome pork dumpling filling, sandwiched between two slices of crunchy white bread, coated in sesame seeds. Like a prawn toast and pork dumpling hybrid.
instructions: Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, then transfer to a bowl with the rest of the filling ingredients. Stir together until the mixture changes consistency and becomes sticky.
Divide the mixture between four slices of bread, then evenly smooth out. Top each one with another slice of plain bread to make sandwiches, then cut the crusts off.

Spread some mayo over the top of each sandwich. Tip the sesame seeds onto a plate or baking tray. Place the sandwiches into the seeds, mayo-side down, and gently pat so the sesame seeds stick. Spread mayo onto the other side of the sandwiches, then flip and coat in sesame seeds so all sides of each sandwich are coated in seeds.
Add a generous drizzle of oil to a frying pan and place over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the sandwiches and cook on both sides until golden brown (4-5 mins in total).
Transfer the sandwiches to a baking sheet and bake at 200C for 10-15 mins until cooked through. Slice into quarters or triangles before serving.

name: Pork Fillet with Butter Beans & Salsa Verde
description: Pork fillet is taken to the next level in this recipe with the addition of creamy butter beans and a dreamy salsa verde. Prepare to fall in love.
keywords: Pork Fillet With Butter Beans & Salsa Verde
instructions: Heat the oven to 200ºC fan.
Remove the pork tenderloin from the fridge. Pat dry, rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Leave on the side to bring up to room temperature whilst you prep the rest of the meal.

For the butter beans, mince the garlic and finely dice the celery and shallots. Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic, celery and shallots with a pinch of salt and sweat down for 10 mins until softened.

To prep the salsa verde, fry off the sage in a hot frying pan with a drizzle of olive oil for around 30 seconds. Drain on a kitchen towel then roughly chop and set aside. Dice the shallots and add them to a bowl with the red wine vinegar. Mix to combine and leave for 15 mins to lightly pickle.

For the pork, roughly chop the shallots and get them in an oven tray. Sear the pork in a hot frying pan on all sides then place it on top of the sliced shallots, in the oven tray. Roast for 15 mins, turning halfway through.

Back to the butter beans: pour the drained beans into the pot with the softened celery, shallots and garlic. Add the chicken stock and Parmesan rind. Bring to a simmer and leave to gently bubble away for 15 mins.
When the pork is cooked, remove from the oven, cover in foil and leave to rest for 10 mins then cut into thick slices.

To finish off the salsa verde, chop the parsley and get it in a separate bowl with the olive oil and a pinch of salt. Add the pickled shallots and ⅔ of the red wine vinegar. Stir through the chopped sage and season with more salt and red wine vinegar to taste.
To finish off the beans, remove the Parmesan rind, grate in the Parmesan and season with salt and black pepper.
Divide the beans between bowls then top with a few slices of pork and a spoonful of salsa verde. Serve with the roasted shallots and some Tenderstem broccoli, if you like.

name: Pork Lettuce Cups
description: The perfect summer sharer. Think crispy bits of sausage cooked in a Thai green curry paste with lime juice, coriander and mint - wrapped up in lettuce cups.
instructions: Mince your garlic, finely slice your chilli and red onion then set aside in three separate bowls.
Make a quick red onion pickle by squeezing the juice of half a lime onto the onions before giving it a mix with a sprinkle of sea salt. Set aside until later.

Squeeze the sausages out of their casings then add to a pan and fry with a small glug of oil until crispy. Add your garlic to the pan and fry for a few mins until fragrant. Now go in with your curry paste, soy sauce, sugar and the juice of half a lime – fry for around 5 mins on low heat. Once it’s nearly done, add most of your coriander and mint leaves and fry for just a minute.
Crush your peanuts in a pestle and mortar.
Wash your lettuce leaves and pat down dry with a towel.
Assembly time: spoon the pork into the lettuce cups, top with pickled red onions, sliced red chilli and the remaining herbs. Sprinkle over your crushed peanuts.
Serve with sweet chilli sauce and enjoy.

name: Pork Mince Stir-Fry with Cabbage Slaw
description: This stir-fry came about because we had some excess dumpling filling leftover one day — so we decided to fry it up and make a pork mince stir-fry recipe! It’s cooking made easy. The zingy cabbage slaw works perfectly with the deep, savoury mince and should be an essential addition to all of your stir-fries.
instructions: Cut the cabbage half in half again through the root and use a sharp knife or potato peeler to really finely slice it. Tip into a bowl and dress with the sesame oil, rice vinegar, pinch of sugar and a pinch of salt. Toss well.
Peel the ginger, then cut into slices, then matchsticks, then finely chop. Finely chop the garlic. Cut the spring onions into 4cm pieces.

Drizzle a large frying pan or wok with a little vegetable oil and set over a high heat. Add the pork mince to the pan and break up a little with a wooden spoon. Leave to fry for 2 mins, then flip and break up again. Scatter in the sesame seeds and 4cm pieces of spring onion and continue frying the mince for another 2 mins until starting to get nice and crisp. Add in the ginger and garlic and cook for 2 mins until smelling amazing.
Turn the heat to low and spoon in the miso, soy sauce and water. Mix really well and cook for 1 min until the mince is glossy and coated in the sauce.
Spoon rice onto plates and top with some of the crispy, saucy mince. Add a pile of the cabbage to the side and top with the finely sliced spring onion and some more sesame seeds.

name: Pork Minute Steaks on Pan Con Tomate
description: If you like pork and tomatoes then this one will definitely hit the spot. It's fresh, light, and surprisingly easy. Enjoy!
keywords: pork minute steaks pan con two tomates
instructions: Grate the large tomatoes into a bowl, discarding the skins. Season with salt, then set aside for 15 mins (or as long as it takes to prepare everything else).

Lightly crush ⅓ of the garlic cloves and finely slice the remaining cloves. Add ⅔ of the olive oil to a medium frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the cherry tomatoes with the crushed garlic and a pinch of salt. Gently fry for 8-12 mins, shaking the pan every so often until the tomatoes start to collapse, burst and caramelise in parts.

Season the pork medallions with salt and pepper, then heat a frying pan so it gets really hot, like you would for a steak. Once hot, add the rest of the olive oil, then fry the steaks (in two batches if necessary) for 2 mins on each side until deeply golden. Turn the heat right down and add the butter, sliced garlic and thyme. Lightly fry until the garlic starts to turn very lightly golden. Transfer everything to a plate to rest.

Toast the ciabatta and arrange on a serving platter. Drain the grated tomato through a fine sieve then tip back into the bowl with the red wine vinegar. Spoon the grated tomato onto the toast, followed by the pan-fried tomatoes, and then finally the pork steaks and their juices.
Season it all with sea salt and pepper, then eat immediately.

name: Pork Tenderloin with Spiced Rhubarb Sauce & Pickled Rhubarb Herb Salad
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad

Sweet, sharp and herby. This pork tenderloin with spiced rhubarb sauce and zippy herb salad is a proper spring show-off dinner, but still nice and easy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until it runs clear. Tip into a saucepan with double the amount of water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then cover with a lid, turn the heat down to low and simmer for 10 mins. Take it off the heat and leave to steam with the lid on for 10 mins, don’t peek! Fluff with a fork before serving.

Thinly slice your rhubarb for the salad. Juice the lemon and combine with honey and add the sliced rhubarb. Toss and let sit for 10–15 minutes while preparing the pork and sauce. This lightly pickles the rhubarb.

Season pork tenderloin with salt, pepper, and rosemary. In a pan, heat oil and sear the tenderloin on all sides until golden brown (2–3 mins per side). Remove and place on a tray to roast for 15–20 min. Let rest 5–10 min before slicing.

Meanwhile, make the spiced rhubarb sauce. In the same frying pan, cook the garlic and chilli for 1 min. Add the chopped rhubarb, honey, mustard, cider vinegar and water. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 12–15 mins, stirring occasionally, until the rhubarb breaks down into a sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning, add more honey if too tart, or a splash more water if too thick.
To make the salad dressing, whisk together the juice of the lemon, honey, mustard and olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper.
Drain the pickled rhubarb. In a large bowl, toss together the herbs, rocket and spinach with the drained rhubarb. Dress just before serving.
To serve, spoon the basmati rice onto plates. Top with slices of pork and plenty of the warm rhubarb sauce. Serve the herb salad on the side with the lemon wedges.

name: Pork and Mushrooms Meatballs with Braised Lentils and Jam
description: his dish is inspired by some interesting Scandinavian flavours. The jam might sound odd but, trust me, it really works with the meatballs. Jordon x
keywords: Pork and mushroom meatballs with braised lentils and jam recipes
instructions: Finely chop all of the mushrooms (they don’t need to be neat, just mince them up, use a food processor if you like).
Place a large pan over a medium-high heat and add a splash of olive oil. Add the mushrooms and a pinch of salt and cook for about 5 mins until the mushrooms have browned nicely.

Remove the mushrooms into a large bowl and wipe out the pan. Mix the milk and breadcrumbs together and finely chop the parsley, then add both to the mushrooms along with the pork mince, egg, nutmeg, plenty of black pepper and a tsp of salt.
Mix really well with your hands until combined. Grab a tray and set it next to your mixing bowl. Roll the mix into meatballs about the size of golf balls and place onto the tray.
Place your pan back onto a medium-high heat and add a splash of olive oil. Add the meatballs and cook for about 5 mins until nicely browned all over, then remove from the pan.
Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery (again feel free to use a food processor here) and add to the pan. Cook over a medium heat for about 7 mins until softening.

Pour in the lentils and the vinegar and cook for a minute, stirring. Pour in the chicken stock, bring up to a simmer and cook for about 30 mins until the lentils are tender. Keep an eye on the lentils and add more stock of a splash of water if needed.

Once the lentils have cooked through and the mix is saucy (they should be nice and saucy but a lot of the liquid should have been absorbed by this point), finely chop and add most of the dill along with the mustard and a tbsp of the sour cream. Stir through, taste and add salt if needed.
Return the meatballs to the pan and simmer for another few mins until they are hot all the way through.
Spoon the meatballs, lentils and sauce into bowls, add a sprinkle of dill, a dollop of sour cream and a spoon of jam to each bowl.

name: Pork, Ricotta & Fennel Seed Meatballs with Tomato Cream Butter Beans
description: Making meatballs is a great way to stretch the quantity of meat you buy, bulking it out with extra ingredients that bring flavour and boost texture.
instructions: Lightly crush your fennel seeds in a pestle and mortar, if you have one. Leave them whole if not. Now, combine the mince, ricotta, egg, breadcrumbs and fennel in a large bowl. Mix well, then finely grate in the pecorino and season generously with salt and pepper. Vigorously mix for a couple of minutes, until the mixture feels cohesive and a bit sticky.

Wet your hands and roll the mixture into balls about the size of ping-pong balls. Put the meatballs onto a plate and chill for 30 minutes to firm-up. If making ahead, cover and leave in the fridge until the next day.

Finely chop the garlic. Set a large frying pan over a medium heat, add enough oil to lightly coat the base, then fry the meatballs in a single layer in a large frying pan over a medium heat, in batches if needed, for 5-8 mins until nicely browned all over. Transfer to a plate, leaving the fat behind in the pan.

Drain the beans, keeping the liquid for later if needed. Add the garlic and sage to the pan, then cook over a medium heat for 30 seconds until aromatic. Add the tomato purée and a big pinch of chilli flakes, then stir in the beans and cream and season well. Heat the oven to 200°C.

Bring the pan to a simmer, then add the browned meatballs back to the pan with an optional splash of water to loosen just a little (no more than 80ml). Bring the pan back up to a simmer, put the lid on and transfer to the oven for 25-30 mins, or until the meatballs are fully cooked through. Add the reserved bean liquid if it needs loosening. You can remove the lid and give the pan a flash under a hot grill to colour if you like, but this isn’t a necessity.
Remove from the oven and finish with extra grated pecorino, a splash more olive oil and a few extra chilli flakes, if you like.

name: Portobello And Hummus Mash With Crispy Garlic
description: This is a twist on a British classic, sneaking in some extra protein and nutrients to make the creamiest mashed potatoes. Finished with crispy garlic and pesto.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190ºC.

Peel and chop the potatoes. Set a big pot of water to boil. Add plenty of salt and the chopped potatoes and boil for 15-20 mins until the potatoes are soft. Drain and save a cup of the starchy potato water. Pop the potatoes back into the pot.

Mash the potatoes with a fork or potato masher until smooth and then stir the hummus through. Add a generous drizzle of olive oil and add some of your saved potato water. Keep adding olive oil and potato water and mixing well until you have your desired consistency - it should be nice and creamy. Season well with salt and pepper.

Mince 2-4 garlic cloves into a small bowl and mix with 5 tbsp of olive oil, salt and pepper. You can remove the stem if you like as this can be a little tough to eat, especially on bigger mushrooms. Brush the mushrooms with the garlic oil and bake for 15 mins with the gills facing upward.

If you have a griddle pan, you can char the mushrooms for a few mins on the hot griddle to give them a smokey flavour. If you don't have a griddle pan, use a frying pan to cook the mushrooms, making sure to flip them from side-to-side to check that they are done. Slice them thinly and keep them covered in the oven (with the oven off) until ready to serve.

Slice the remaining garlic thinly. Heat up a small frying pan with enough sunflower oil to cover the bottom of the pan, about half a centimetre deep. Fry the garlic on a medium heat until golden brown, stirring often to make sure it doesn't burn. Add the chilli flakes and fry for another minute or two until fragrant, then remove from the pan and add into a small bowl to stop them from cooking further and burning.

Heat up the mash if needed, gently on the stove, adding a little more liquid if needed.
 To serve, spoon plenty of mash into a bowl and dollop a few teaspoons of pesto onto it, swirling it through. Top with the mushrooms and crispy garlic and chilli and enjoy.

name: Pot-Sticker Pork & Spring Onion Dumplings
description: These homemade potsticker dumplings (or guō tiē) are filled with a juicy pork and spring onion mixture.
instructions: Make the dumpling wrappers. Grab a large bowl and add flour, oil and salt and ¾ of the kettle-boiled water, leaving a little water behind. Use a chopstick or the back of a wooden spoon to mix everything, then use your hands and create a dough ball. If the dough ball feels dry, add some of the remaining water and knead until it is soft and feels like playdough. It should not be stuck to your fingers, just add more flour if this happens.
Knead for 2 mins or until smooth, cover in cling film or throw into a sandwich bag, and then set aside for at least 25 mins. This dough can be made up to 2 nights before.

Make the dumpling filling. Mince the garlic and ginger. Grab a large bowl and add all the ingredients into the bowl except for the spring onions and water. Use a fork or chopsticks to mix in one direction until a big meatball forms. Add the water in 2 parts, mixing in between until the meatball absorbs the liquid, then add the remaining liquid. Finely slice the spring onions and mix just until it is evenly incorporated. Clingfilm the bowl and leave in the fridge until needed.

Continue making the wrappers. Roll the dough into a log the width of a round cherry tomato and use scissors to cut into 16 pieces, roughly the size of a cherry tomato, or 15g each if you want to be exact.
In a small pot combine a 1:1 ratio of cornflour and flour and mix with fingers, use this for dusting.

Lightly dust all the pieces of dough and toss with your hands to lightly coat. Turn the pieces of dough upwards so the sticky part is facing you, then use the fattest part of your palm to press down firmly, revealing a coin shape. Repeat for all the dough pieces, then cover with a lightly damp tea towel to prevent them from drying out.
Using the dusting flour roll out each piece of dough, roughly 10 cm in diameter. Lightly dust each side if needed, then place onto a sheet of cling film, and lightly cover with cling film.
Repeat to all pieces of dough, stacking the wrapper on top of each other, making sure to lightly dust between each wrapper and always covering with the cling film, to prevent it drying out.

If you’re using store-bought wrappers, grab a small bowl of tap water, and lightly wet the edges of the wrapper with your index finger before folding, skip this step if your wrappers are freshly made.
Now to fold the dumplings. Prep a large plate or tray and lightly dust it, for the folded dumplings to sit on.

Place 1 tbsp of filling into the centre of a wrapper, then fold it in half like a purse and pinch the middle closed. Fold the dumplings like in the video, using your index finger as the guide to crimp around. As long as the dough is sealed tight, it doesn't matter how they look, they will be juicy. Place each dumpling onto the plate or tray and lightly push down to create a flat bottom, cover with a lightly damp tea towel so they don’t dry out. Repeat with all the wrappers.
Combine all the dumpling dipping sauce ingredients in a bowl and set aside.

Now to cook the dumplings. Heat a non-stick heavy frying pan over a medium-low heat. Add 2 tbsp of neutral oil and swirl over the entire surface of the pan. Arrange the dumplings neatly so each dumpling is completely flat on the surface of the pan.

Cook until the bottoms of the dumplings are lightly golden brown, using your hands to check one dumpling bottom. Now, carefully add the warm/boiling water, keeping at arm's distance from the pan. Immediately add a lid and cook for 5 mins – or once you can hear sizzling, which means the water has evaporated. Feel free to check at 4 mins – it won’t ruin the dumplings.
Lift the lid and fry the dumplings for around 1-2 mins or until the bottoms are golden, checking whenever to make sure they don’t burn. Then turn off the heat.

Place the pan onto a soaking wet cold tea towel and carefully place the pan on top, it will steam. When the steam stops, this will help release the dumplings from the pan. Use a spatula and run it around the edge of the dumplings. Place a plate on top and flip. Alternatively, just remove the dumplings with a spatula. Serve immediately with the dipping sauce on the side and chilli oil.

name: Potato & Cauliflower Stuffed Parathas
description: These mean green vegetable-stuffed parathas are deceptively easy to make. If you've never made your own parathas before, now is the perfect time.
instructions: Start by adding chapati flour, salt, vegetable oil to a large bowl. Gradually pour in 120ml of warm water and use a wooden spoon to mix everything together.
Once the mixture comes together, use your hands to knead the dough for a few minutes, it will be sticky at first but keep kneading till it’s soft, pliable and you can easily form a ball.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 mins or overnight.

Peel and boil the potatoes in salted water until very tender. Mash them and add chopped green chilli (you can deseed if you like!), fresh coriander and all the ground spices, mix well and season to taste.
Grate the cauliflower and add to a bowl along with the spices and mix well.
Divide the dough into 8 equal-sized balls.
On a lightly floured surface, use a floured rolling pin to roll out 2 dough balls into roughly equal-sized circles.
To one of the circles, add 1-2 tbsp of the potato or cauliflower filling and spread it around, leaving a small border.
Place the other circle on top and use water to seal the edges.
Fry in 2 tbsp of vegetable oil until golden and crispy on both sides, 2-3 mins per side. Get stuck in!

name: Potato Latkes With Caramelised Tomato Aioli
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

If you're a fried potato fan, these crispy latkes are for you. They're perfect scooped into the zingy caramelised tomato aioli.
keywords: Potato Latkes With Caramelised Tomato Aioli
instructions: Peel and grate the garlic into the mayo, add the Dijon mustard and stir through. Zest ¼ of the lemon into the mayo and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Set aside.
Peel and trim the onion. Into a large bowl, crack the egg in and whisk the baking powder, breadcrumbs and paprika in. Season with 1 tsp of salt and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper, set aside.

Coarsely grate the potatoes and onion onto a clean tea towel. Gather ends of the towel in each hand and twist over a sink to wring out as much liquid as possible. Toss mixture to loosen and wring out again (the drier the mixture the crispier the latkes).
Toss the potato mixture into the egg mix and evenly coat.
In a small saucepan on medium heat, add 4 tbsp of olive oil. Once hot, stir through the tomato purée and cook until it goes dark red and caramelises, 3-5 mins. Drizzle onto the aioli.

Add enough oil to fill a frying pan, place on medium-high heat. Once hot, drop 1 tbsp worth of potato mixture in (it should shimmer as soon as the potato hits the hot oil, if not, the oil is too cold). Use a spoon to press down and shape into a rough disc. Fry until golden on both sides, 3-4 mins on each side. Transfer to a wire rack or a kitchen paper lined plate. Season with salt.
Serve the latkes onto a sharing plate with the caramelised tomato aioli.

name: Potato Rosti with Brown Butter Fried Eggs & Sage
description: This potato rosti is the ultimate crispy brunch dish you'll crave, especially if you're nursing a hangover. Ideal for breakfast or brunch, it pairs exceptionally well with a variety of accompaniments.
keywords: Potato Rosti Recipe With Brown Butter Fried Eggs & Sage
instructions: Peel and coarsely grate the potatoes into a clean tea towel. Halve and thinly slice the onion. Put the butter into a small bowl and melt in the microwave.
Gather the top of the tea towel together so the potato is completely encased, then hold it over the sink and squeeze as much water as possible from the potato.
Tip the dry potato into a clean bowl. Add the sliced onion along with 2 tbsp of the melted butter, then season really well with salt and pepper. Mix well.

Heat a pat of the butter in a medium frying pan (roughly 28cm) over a medium heat, then pile in all of the potato – you want the potato to be about 2 ½ cm thick. Gently press to make sure there is lots of contact with the bottom of the pan.

Fry for 6-8 mins until the bottom is super golden and caramelised. Carefully flip the rosti out onto a plate, then add a pat of more butter and slide the rosti back into the pan. Continue to cook for another 6-7 mins or until the bottom is a deep caramel colour and is super crunchy.

Once you’ve flipped the rosti and got it back into the pan, get another frying pan over a high heat. Pour in the melted butter and cook for 1-2 mins, gently whisking, until smelling nutty and has turned a light golden colour. Crack in the eggs, then baste them with some of the butter and cook for 1-2 mins until the white is cooked through and the yolk is still runny. Add the sage into the butter in the gaps between the eggs and cook for 1 min, then remove from the heat.

Slide the rosti out onto a board and cut into quarters. Put each onto a plate then top with a fried egg and some of the sage. Cut the lemon in half and squeeze into the butter, then spoon over. Serve with hot sauce for splashing over and a green salad.

name: Potato, Cheese and Onion Pasty
description: A British holiday classic. Deeply caramelised onions and cheddar are what make our pasties so delicious.
instructions: Heat your oven to 170°C.
Cut 240g of your butter into cubes.
Pop your flour and 1 tsp of salt in a large mixing bowl. Add your cubed butter and rub in until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add 180ml of cold water and mix thoroughly.
Tip your dough onto your work surface and knead for 5 mins until smooth and elastic. Wrap your pastry in cling film and pop it in the fridge to rest for an hour.
Meanwhile, prep your filling. Peel, halve and slice your onions. Peel your potatoes, then halve and finely slice them.

Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat. Add your remaining butter to the pan and, once melted, tip in your onions and thyme leaves. Fry on a medium heat for 30 mins until really soft and starting to caramelise, deglazing the pan with water occasionally if it looks like they are sticking.
Tip your potatoes into the pan and cook for 5 mins more. Season with salt and very generously with pepper.
Tip your onion and potato mixture into a bowl and, once cool, add your grated cheddar. Stir to combine.
Roll your pastry out to 2mm thickness and use a small bowl to cut out circle shapes about 10cm wide.

Arrange your filling to one side of each circle, then brush the edges with beaten egg and fold over. Seal the edges by pressing down, then twist them inwards to create a braid pattern. Brush the surface with egg wash.
Bake on a parchment-lined baking tray for 40 mins until golden and crisp. Eat hot or cold.

name: Potato, Courgette and Cumin Fritters
description: These fritters are so easy, everything gets grated and mixed in one big bowl. Minimal washing up, maximum flavour. Jordon x
instructions: Wash, peel and use the coarse side of a box grater to grate the potatoes into a large bowl.
Peel the skin off your onion, then grate it. Grate your courgette.
Add a tsp of salt and mix well. Now empty the mix into a colander and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Return to the bowl.
Add the eggs, cumin, cornflour and 10 turns of a pepper mill. Mix well.
Set a frying pan over a medium heat and add a generous glug of sunflower oil.
Take a little ball of the mixture and check to see if the oil is hot by frying for a couple of minutes on each side until golden brown. Let it cool and then check for seasoning.
Now take about 2 tbsp worth of the mix, squeeze and press into a patty. Fry for about 3 mins on either side until crisp and golden brown. Repeat.
Place on a tray lined with kitchen paper and into a warm oven while you repeat with the rest of the mix.
Finely chop 3 tbsps of dill and mix into the yoghurt along with the zest and juice of half a lemon, and a pinch of salt.
Plate up the fritters, sprinkle with flaky salt and a good spoon of yoghurt for dipping.

name: Poulet Au Vinaigre
description: A bit of classic French cooking! A creamy braised chicken which is balanced by the vinegar added during cooking. Serve this up with buttery mash for an indulgent dinner.
instructions: Start by seasoning the chicken legs generously all over with salt. Place a large wide pan (which you have a lid for) over a medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and brown off the chicken legs for a few minutes on each side until golden.

The chicken will release quite a lot of fat, drain all but a tbsp from the pan. Finely dice and add the shallots, cook for 2 mins, then add the finely chopped garlic and tomato purée and cook for another minute.
Add the vinegar and after a minute or so once it has mostly evaporated, pour in the wine. Bring the wine to the boil, reduce by half and then pour in the chicken stock.
Finely chop the tarragon and add half to the stock. Nestle the chicken legs back into the sauce, they should be about half to ¾ submerged. Pop a lid on and cook over a low heat for 45 mins.
Remove the chicken and set aside on a plate. Pour the cooking liquid through a sieve into a clean saucepan and bring to a simmer. Use a ladle to skim the fat from the surface.
Now add the cream, mustard, remaining tarragon, and finely chopped chives and bring to a simmer, then turn off the heat.
To serve, pour the sauce back into the pan you cooked the chicken in, lay the chicken into the dish and take it to the table.
Plate up on a bed of buttery mash. Enjoy!

name: Prawn & 'Nduja Risotto
description: This risotto is super indulgent and a perfect dinner party dish, with prawns and 'nduja. It's a ripper.
instructions: Finely dice your onion. Finely chop your cloves of garlic and parsley.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large sauté pan over a medium-high heat. Add your prawns and fry for 3 mins until pink and curled. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Add some more olive oil to the same pan. Tip in your onion and cook gently for 20 mins until totally soft, but not taking on colour. Add your ‘nduja and garlic and cook for another 2 mins until the ‘nduja has darkened slightly.
Pour your chicken stock and passata into a saucepan, and gently warm on the hob.
Pour your arborio rice into the pan and toast the grains for 2 mins until slightly translucent.
Turn your heat down. Pour in your wine and let it reduce.

Pour your hot tomatoey chicken stock into the pan a ladle at a time, stirring until the rice has fully absorbed the liquid before adding more. This should take about 25 mins, but add more hot water if necessary.
Check that your rice grains are tender. Add your single cream and salt and pepper to taste. Take your risotto off the heat and pop a lid on it. Let it rest for 5 mins.
Meanwhile, heat a glug of oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add your capers and fry for a few mins until crispy. Drain on kitchen paper.

Add your prawns, chopped parsley and the zest of a lemon, and a squeeze of lemon juice to the risotto, then add any more hot water you need to give it your desired consistency – I like mine fairly silky and loose.
Spoon your risotto into bowls and top with a drizzle of olive oil, a little more chopped parsley and crispy capers. Serve and enjoy.

name: Prawn & Mango Coconut Bowl
description: Juicy garlicky prawns, zingy mango salsa, and a toasted coconut sprinkle. This one’s sunny, fresh, and just a little bit fancy.
instructions: Peel and dice the mango. Thinly dice the red onion. Add both to a bowl with the juice of half the limes and a pinch of salt. Stir and set aside to pickle.
Thinly slice the garlic. Devein the prawns, if needed. Pick half of the coriander leaves and finely chop the rest, including the stalks.

Set a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the desiccated coconut and toast it dry for 2–4 mins until golden. Tip into a small bowl and stir through the chilli flakes and crispy onions. Set aside.

Return the empty pan to a medium-high heat with the olive oil. Once hot, add the garlic and cook for 2–3 mins until fragrant and just golden. Tip in the prawns and cook for 2–4 mins, stirring occasionally, until pink and cooked through. Remove from the heat.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice. Stir through the finely chopped coriander and divide between bowls.

Spoon the garlicky prawns and mango salsa over the rice. Finish with a generous sprinkle of the coconut mixture and a scattering of the remaining coriander leaves. Serve with any leftover lime wedges.

name: Prawn & Mango Curry
description: This recipe from Karan Gokani is an absolute corker. It's tangy, it's spicy, and a great curry to add to your arsenal.
instructions: Tip the prawns into a bowl. Sprinkle over the turmeric and a pinch of salt and stir to combine. Set aside to marinate.
Thinly slice the shallots and green chilli, mince garlic and dice the tomato. Set aside, keeping the ingredients separate for now.
Heat some coconut oil over medium heat. Add the cinnamon stick and fenugreek seeds and fry for 15 seconds.
Then add the shallots and fry for a couple of minutes until softened. You don’t want them to brown in this recipe so it's all pretty quick!
Add the garlic and cook for another minute, before adding the curry leaves and pandan leaves.
After 15-20 seconds add the tomatoes and cook till they break down, 2-3 mins.

Now add the dried spices and cook for 30 seconds. Turn the heat down and add the prawns, green mango and chilli. Cook for 3 mins, add the coconut milk and cook for another 2-3 minutes until the prawns are fully cooked through.
Taste and add more salt if you like.
Garnish with some chilli oil and fried curry leaves and enjoy with some simple steamed basmati rice.

name: Prawn & Pepper Chopped Salad
description: A swift chopped salad recipe using pre-cooked king prawns. It’s fresh. It’s tasty. It’s exactly what you want for lunch today.
keywords: King Prawn & Pepper Chopped Salad recipe
instructions: The first thing you’re going to want to do is de-seed your cucumbers. Now, get out a chopping board and chop up the peppers, cucumbers, and sugar snap peas into even-sized pieces.
Add your prawns, avocado, mango, coriander, and mint onto the same chopping board and chop again. Add all your ingredients into a large mixing bowl.
Heat up your quinoa according to package instructions and add it to the bowl with the rest of your chopped ingredients.
Squeeze the juice from your limes and combine with the rest of the dressing ingredients. Add the dressing into the bowl and toss vigorously. Serve and enjoy.

name: Prawn & Pickled Ginger Chopped Salad
description: This is a wonderfully refreshing chopped salad that's perfect for seeing in the summer months.
instructions: Cook your rice according to packet instructions and leave to cool. Scoop out the seeds on the cucumber and slice in half lengthwise and peel the carrots.
Place your cucumbers and carrots onto a board and chop them into even-sized pieces. Add the smoked salmon, sushi ginger and prawns to the chopping board and continue to chop.
Tip your chopped ingredients into a bowl along with the rice, edamame and sesame seeds.
Make the dressing by mixing together the ginger juice from the jar along with your soy and rice vinegar.
Pour the dressing into the bowl and toss it all together.

name: Prawn & Rice Salad with Mango, Chilli & Lime Dressing
description: Juicy prawns, fluffy rice and crunchy veg tossed through our delish Mango, Chilli & Lime Dressing. Fresh, zingy and seriously moreish.
keywords: prawn and rice salad with mango
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Add the cashew nuts to a baking tray and roast until golden and fragrant, then remove and leave to cool.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Zest the lime and then cut it in half ready for juicing. Deseed and finely chop the chilli (if you fancy a bit more spice you can add extra). Roughly chop the mango and add it to a high-speed blender with the lime juice, cumin, olive oil and water. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt and black pepper. Finally, stir through the lime zest and chopped chilli.
Heat the rice following pack instructions. Halve the cherry tomatoes, then peel the carrots and cut them into fine matchsticks. Pick the Thai basil leaves.
Add the rice to a large bowl along with the prawns, tomatoes, carrots, Thai basil, coconut chips and roasted cashews. Pour over the dressing, toss well to coat and serve.

name: Prawn Cocktail
description: An absolute classic. This retro starter is a winner, and perfect for a dinner party or Christmas Day.
instructions: Bring a saucepan full of salted water to the boil over a medium-high heat. Once boiling, drop the prawns in and simmer for 2-4 mins until cooked through. Meanwhile, fill a bowl with icy water.
Drain the prawns and transfer to the icy water. Once they’ve cooled down fully, drain and pat them dry.
Remove the heads from the prawns (if they haven’t already been removed) and peel off the shells off, leaving only the tail on for ½ of them.
Shred the iceberg lettuce and place into the bottom of your chosen serving dish (a short, wide wine glass or a sundae dish work well).
Add the fully peeled prawns to a separate bowl with ½ the marie rose sauce and toss to combine.

To serve, spoon the dressed prawns onto the lettuce, and top with more marie rose sauce. Finish by hanging the undressed prawns around the rim, with the tails hanging over the edge. Sprinkle over a touch of paprika and serve immediately.

name: Prawn Dumplings
description: A fail-safe prawn dumpling recipe. These deliver on fun and flavour. A great one if you're after a weekend project.
instructions: Chop the prawns into a rough but fine dice. You’re going for a coarse mince texture. Sprinkle sake on the chopped prawns and leave for at least 30 mins.

Meanwhile make the dough. Mix the flour and water in a bowl to form a shaggy dough. Tip out onto a clean surface and knead for 5-6 mins or until smooth. Cover with an upturned bowl and leave to rest for 10 mins.
Finely chop the shallot, bamboo shoots and chives and combine with the prawn mixture. Tip in the vegetable oil, cornflour, sesame seed oil, sugar, salt and white pepper. Mix to combine and set aside.

Uncover and briefly knead the dough again and make the wrappers. Flatten the dough slightly with a rolling pin. Cut in half, then feed one half through a pasta machine, passing the dough through each setting twice until you reach the fourth thickest setting. Keep the other half covered while you do this. Grab a ring cutter (7-8cm across), and punch out circles to create your wrappers. If you don’t have a pasta machine, you can use a rolling pin, you’re shooting for a strip of dough around 1mm thick.

Fill the wrappers with a teaspoon of the prawn mixture, fold the dough in half and pinch together with your fingers. Pleat around the edge with your fingertips to create a strong seal, you can use water to help you stick the wrappers if necessary. Repeat with the remaining wrappers and wrapper dough. Keep the dumplings on a tray.

Set up a steamer or steamer basket and line with parchment. Transfer the dumplings, working in batches if necessary, to the steamer and cook for 9 mins. If you don’t have a steamer, you can boil the dumplings. Simply drop into simmering water for 5-6 mins.
While the dumplings steam, preheat a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Add a splash of veg oil and transfer the steamed dumplings to the pan. Cook for 1-2 mins until golden brown and crisp.
Finely chop the chillies, briefly fry off in a splash of veg oil and tip into the soy sauce. Mix and serve with your crispy dumplings.

name: Prawn Moilee Recipe
description: This dead easy Keralan prawn curry is packed with flavour and ready in minutes – you'll find yourself making it again and again. It's such a versatile dish for a quick weeknight meal or a weekend feast, and works equally well with pumpkin, chicken or fish if you want to switch it up
instructions: Put the prawns, turmeric and a squeeze of lime into a bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Marinate for 15 mins.
Thinly slice the garlic. Mince the ginger. Halve the tomatoes (if using) and green chillies.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add the coconut oil. Once hot, add the fenugreek seeds if using, mustard seeds and curry leaves. Once they all sizzle, add the shallots, ginger and garlic, season with salt and give it a good stir. Cook for 2-4 mins until softened.
Pour in the coconut milk followed by the prawns, tomatoes and green chillies. Reduce the heat to low, then simmer for 10 mins.
Serve with a drizzle of chilli oil on top.

name: Prawn Pad Thai
description: An easy prawn pad Thai recipe with an addictive dipping sauce. This is the pad Thai recipe of your dreams.
instructions: Roughly cut the rice noodles with scissors into 15cm-long sticks. Transfer to a large bowl, then cover with boiling water. Leave for just 2-4 mins in hot water. As soon as they begin to bend, strain well and set aside on a plate.
Pat the prawns dry with kitchen paper and add to a small bowl with a good pinch of sea salt. Mix well and set aside in the fridge.
Pat the tofu dry with kitchen paper and cut into small squares. Set aside on a large plate.

Mince the garlic and slice the shallots for the sauce. Cut the spring onions into 2 ½ cm chunks, dividing the whites from the greens. Set everything aside on the plate with the tofu. Add the beansprouts to this plate, too.
Whisk the eggs in a small bowl with a pinch of salt and set aside. Crush the peanuts and set aside in a small bowl.
For the dipping sauce, mince the garlic and slice the chilli. Transfer to a small bowl, add the remaining ingredients, stir well and set aside.

For the pad Thai sauce, add a glug of oil to a small pot set over a medium heat. Add the prepared garlic, shallots and spring onion whites, then cook for 2 mins or until aromatic and lightly golden. Now add all the remaining ingredients, mix well and bring to a simmer, then turn the heat off and set aside.

The pad Thai will now come together very fast, so make sure all your ingredients are in arm's reach. Set a large pan or wok over a high heat and add a glug of oil. When the pan is hot, sear the prawns for 1½ mins on each side, without touching, so they are lightly golden on both sides. Remove the prawns back to the same bowl (they will be cooked again).

Sear the tofu in the same pan until lightly golden, then add the pickled radish and cook for 1 min. Add all the rice noodles and all the sauce on top and toss everything together until all the noodles are coated.

Push everything to the edge of the pan, add a splash of oil to the empty space, swirl it all over the pan and add all the eggs into the space. Allow the eggs to briefly set like an omelette. Then push all the noodles back on top of the eggs and toss everything well.

Add all the beansprouts and half the crushed peanuts, then toss well using tongs to loosen the noodles. Cook for 1 min, then throw in the spring onion greens and prawns and toss for 1 min. Turn the heat off and taste to see if the noodles are cooked, as you don’t want them to get mushy. You can always turn the heat back on to cook further, if needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with a squeeze of lime, the remaining peanuts, chilli flakes and dipping sauce on the side.

name: Prawn Tacos With Mango Coriander Salsa
description: Never made your own prawn tacos before? You've never lived, my friend. This is the ideal recipe for summer. Get grilling.
keywords: Prawn Tacos With Mango Coriander Salsa
instructions: Preheat the Ninja grill to medium-high.
Peel and grate the garlic. Place the prawns in a bowl with a drizzle of oil, the ancho chilli, tomato purée and garlic. Season with salt and pepper, stir together and set aside.
Peel and thinly slice the red onion, add into a bowl with a large pinch of salt and the juice from your limes. Mix together and set aside to pickle.

Zest a lime into a bowl. Add the coriander into a food processor with the olive oil. Blitz until the coriander has broken down. Transfer into the bowl, add the zest from 1/3 of your limes into the coriander mixture, season with salt and juice from all the remaining limes.
Remove the mango cheeks, scoop out the flesh and cut into a rough dice. Stir through the coriander mixture.
Cook the prawns on the grill until opaque and cooked through, 5-7 mins. Reheat the corn tortillas on the Ninja grill until pliable. Scoop the avocado flesh out of its skin and slice thinly.
Share the prawns between the tortillas, top with avocado slices, mango and coriander salsa and lime-pickled red onions.

name: Prawn Toast Smacos with Spicy Cucumbers
description: Prawn toast in taco form. The sesame crust crisps up in the pan and the spicy cucumbers cut bring all the zing and spice. Ready in 30 mins.
keywords: Prawn Toast Smacos with Spicy Cucumbers
Prawn Toast Smacos with Spicy Cucumbers recipe
instructions: Roughly chop the ginger, chilli and half the spring onions. Add to a food processor with most of the coriander, the fish sauce and half the sesame oil. Blitz until it's roughly chopped, then add in the prawns and egg. Blitz again until you have a coarse mixture and set aside.

Cut the cucumber into quarters lengthways, then cut into small, irregular pieces. Add to a bowl with the soy sauce, grated garlic, rice vinegar, chilli oil and remaining sesame oil, then mix and set aside. With the rest of the spring onions, cut off the green parts and slice into very thin matchsticks. Pop into icy water if you like, this will help them curl up. Keep the white parts in the fridge to use in another recipe, they're great chucked into a stir-fry or a fried rice.
Add the sesame seeds to a large plate. Spread each of the tortillas with the prawn mix, then pop them onto the plate of sesame seeds, prawn side down.
Heat a lightly oiled frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the tortillas prawn side down and cook for 2-3 mins, until golden and cooked through, then flip and cook for another 1-2 mins.
Top with the cucumber salad and the rest of the coriander, the spring onions and some extra chilli oil, if you like.

name: Prawn Wonton Soup
description: John Javier whipped us up the most beautiful bowl of wonton soup you ever saw. Treat yourself and cook this one up.
instructions: In a pot on medium heat, sweat the onions, ginger, garlic and dried shrimp until translucent. Add the peppercorns and cook for a further minute.
Add the chicken stock and bring to a simmer for 1 hour.
Turn off the heat and add the anchovies and sliced jamon. Make sure they are fully submerged.
Infuse for 20 minutes before passing through a fine strainer. Allow the liquid to gently fall through making sure not to press down on the solids. Discard the solids.
Season broth with salt to taste.
Chop prawn meat with a knife until it reaches the texture of coarse mince.

Place prawn mince in a large metal bowl with sesame powder, dashi powder, sesame oil, msg, sugar, salt and egg. Using your hand, mix all the ingredients together vigorously making sure everything is well combined. Continue to mix everything with your hand until the mixture thickens and becomes extremely sticky (roughly 5 minutes).

Line your chopping board with wonton wrapper sheets and place a teaspoon of prawn mix in the centre of each sheet. Dip your finger in a small bowl of water and rub it around the edges of the wonton sheet – this will help seal the wrapper.

Bring the corners of the wrapper together and pinch the edges firmly to create a ‘money bag’ shape with the wonton. Make sure the filling is not exposed once the edges are sealed, otherwise they will explode when you cook them. You can make them in advance and store them in a lightly greased container so they do not stick before cooking.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. About 1 teaspoon of salt per litre will do.
Cut the yellow chives into 2cm batons (if you have opted for spring onions, slice them 1-2mm thick).
In a smaller pot, bring the wonton broth to the boil.
Blanch prawn wontons in the boiling salted water for about a minute. They will rise to the surface when they are fully cooked. Strain the wontons and divide into bowls.

Pour the wonton broth into the bowls with prawn wontons and garnish with the sliced spring onions and cress. If desired, you can serve them with a side of chilli oil and Chinese red vinegar for dipping the prawn wontons into.

name: Prawn and Avocado Summer Rolls
description: Samah Lakha (@londonbruncher) came into the studio and made some fresh summer rolls, perfect for a quick snack.
instructions: Pan fry your prawns for 2 mins on a medium heat until they curl and turn pink. Season with paprika.
Slice the carrot, cabbage and avocado into thin strips.
Cook the noodles according to package instructions and soak in cold water (this prevents it from cooking further).
Mix everything together for the dipping sauce.
Dip the rice paper sheets in cold water for a few seconds until softened - don't over-soak them as they will continue to soften.
Assemble time. Add some of the prawns, veg and noodles to the bottom third of the rice paper. Top with a spoonful of the dipping sauce and herbs. Carefully roll, tucking the ends in.
Cut the rolls in half and serve with the dipping sauce - enjoy!

name: Prawn and Chorizo Linguine
description: We're back with an OG Mob banger. The naughtiest surf 'n' turf combo about - salt, crispy chorizo with plump, fresh prawns.
instructions: Slice the chorizo into bite-sized pieces. Add to a frying pan (skillet) over a medium heat and cook until crispy.
Once crispy, add a pinch of dried chilli flakes and the raw prawns. Cook the prawns until they are pink, then add a chopped garlic clove. Cook for a further 30 seconds, and then pour in the passata.
Get the linguine on (follow the instructions on the packet).
Meanwhile, bubble the sauce down until it is nice and thick. Then throw in a handful of chopped basil (keep some whole leaves to garnish) and season well with salt and pepper.
Drain your pasta and pour it into the sauce. Mix everything together and serve, with a drizzle of olive oil and the basil leaves scattered on top.

name: Prawn and Chorizo Orzo
description: Surf and Turf with orzo is a match made in heaven. The freshest, basilly, garlicky tomato sauce.
instructions: Finely chop the garlic. Tear all of your chorizo into small pieces and place in a frying pan on a medium heat. Stir the chorizo until crispy (3 minutes). Add the chopped garlic and a tsp of chopped chillies and stir to fully coat the chorizo.
Add all of your tomatoes to the frying pan and combine with the chorizo. Sauté for 5 minutes so the tomatoes become soft.

Add the orzo to the pan and fold into the chorizo and tomatoes until fully covered. Pour in the chicken stock and stir. Allow the orzo to simmer for 7 minutes, stirring occasionally so it doesn’t stick to the bottom of the pan.

Add the prawns, cover and simmer for 5 minutes. At this point, the orzo should be al dente and the prawns should be pink and cooked to perfection. If it needs a bit more time, give it a couple of minutes.
Finely slice all of your basil, scattering most of it over the orzo, saving a third for later. Season with a few grinds of pepper, a pinch of salt and give it all a stir.

Time to plate up! Spoon the orzo into a bowl and add the second tsp of chopped chillies. Sprinkle the rest of the basil over to garnish with an extra pinch of salt, pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Dig in!

name: Prawn, Courgette & Tomato Tagliatelle
description: You can't beat a good pasta recipe and this one is very, very good indeed. Lovely fresh prawns in a tomato and courgette sauce. Easy.
instructions: Finely grate the courgettes into a bowl using a box grater, then use the same grater to coarsely grate the tomatoes into another bowl.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add the prawns. Fry for 1 min then scatter in the paprika and toss and fry together for another minute until the prawns turn pink and are starting to caramelise. Use a slotted spoon to scoop them out and into a bowl.
Add the courgette to the pan along with a large pinch of salt and reduce the heat to low-medium. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 15 mins until the courgettes are very soft.
Add the grated tomato to the pan and cook gently for another 5 mins until thickened slightly.
Meanwhile, bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the tagliatelle following pack instructions.
Put the parsley and garlic onto a chopping board and finely chop everything together. Scrape into a bowl, finely grate in the lemon zest and season with a little salt to make a gremolata. Set aside.

Use tongs to transfer the tagliatelle straight into the courgette and tomato pan, sloshing some of the pasta water in as you go. Add the prawns back to the pan and toss really well. Add a little more pasta water if needed and drizzle in more oil as you toss to make a glossy, coating sauce. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and add lots of black pepper. Season with more salt, if needed.
Divide the pasta and sauce between bowls, then top with the gremolata, a drizzle more oil and black pepper.

name: Prawn, Tofu & Cabbage Pad Thai
description: Sweet, tangy, chewy, and crunchy. This Pad Thai remix is big on flavour, fast on the hob and very satisfying.
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in hot water for 90 seconds, then rinse under cold water. They should be very al dente — they’ll finish cooking in the pan.
Slice the spring onions into 2cm chunks, separating the whites and greens. Finely shred the cabbage. Dice the tofu into 1cm cubes. Crush the peanuts. Set everything aside.
Make the sauce by mixing the tamarind purée, brown sugar, fish sauce, dark soy sauce, and grating in the garlic.

Set a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat with the oil. Once hot, add the tofu and prawns. Fry for 2–3 mins, tossing regularly, until the tofu is golden and the prawns are pink. Remove and set aside.
Add the cabbage to the pan and stir-fry for 2–3 mins until it starts to char and wilt.
Tip in the noodles and pour over the sauce. Stir-fry for a minute or two until the sauce thickens and coats everything.
Push the noodles to one side of the pan and crack in the eggs. Leave to set slightly, then scramble until just cooked. Mix through the noodles.
Return the prawns and tofu to the pan, along with the bean sprouts and spring onion whites. Toss everything together for 1–2 mins until hot and combined.
Divide between bowls and top with crushed peanuts, coriander and lime wedges. Finish with chilli flakes if you like it spicy.

name: Prawns Pil Pil With Ciabatta
description: These king prawns are cooked in olive oil laced with paprika and shedloads of garlic, and then served with crusty ciabatta for mopping up all the oily goodness.
instructions: Heat the ciabatta in a low oven, 120°C.
Finely slice the garlic cloves and the red chilli. Dry the prawns on kitchen paper and season with salt and black pepper.
Get a small saucepan over a medium heat. Pour in the olive oil and heat until just shimmering. You want the oil to be hot but not nuclear otherwise the garlic and chilli will burn.

Add the garlic and chilli. Fry for 1 min until sizzling, then add the prawns. Cook, stirring occasionally, for a further 2–3 mins until all the prawns have turned pink. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the smoked paprika.
Tip the prawns along with their oil into a serving bowl. Roughly chop the parsley and scatter over the top. Serve with the ciabatta for dunking.

name: Prep-Ahead Spicy Beef Noodle Soup
description: There are evenings when only a noodle soup will do. This one you've prepped, tucked away in the freezer, ready to become something deeply savoury and warming the moment you need it most. It's meal prep at its best.
instructions: Pop the steak in the freezer for 20 mins to 1 hr. Once partially frozen, slice as thinly as possible.
Separate the cabbage into leaves and chop into bite-sized pieces. Cut the tofu into slices, thinly slice the mushrooms and cut the spring onions into 2.5cm (1 inch) pieces.
To make the sauce, grate the garlic into a bowl and add the soy sauce, salt, gochujang, tahini, chilli oil, honey, beef stock cubes and gochugaru. Mix well to combine.

Divide the steak, cabbage, tofu, mushrooms and spring onions evenly between four zip-lock freezer-proof bags along with the dry vermicelli noodles. Pour a quarter of the sauce into each bag, press out any excess air, seal and pop flat into the freezer.

To cook, add the bone broth or water to a large saucepan and bring to a simmer. Drop in a frozen block of prepped hot pot, put the lid on and simmer for 7-10 mins until cooked through and piping hot. Season with your favourite seasonings (we love a drizzle of crispy chilli oil) and enjoy. Alternatively, place a frozen block in a large microwave-safe bowl, cover with boiling water and microwave for 7 mins.

name: Prep-ahead Tuna Puttanesca
description: A proper puttanesca with tuna, briny olives and a punchy tomato sauce tossed through spaghetti , then steamed or microwaved straight from frozen whenever you need them. Cook this pasta once and you've got four meals ready to go.
ingredients: 4x 145g Can Tinned Tuna in Spring Water
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the spaghetti for about 4 minutes less than the packet instructions, you want it well underdone as it'll finish cooking later. Before draining, scoop out a couple of ladles of pasta water and set aside. Drain the pasta, rinse under cold water until completely cool, then set aside.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the red onions and garlic. Set a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the olive oil. Once hot, add the red onion, garlic, anchovies and capers. Cook for 3–4 mins, stirring, until the onion is soft and the anchovies have melted into the oil.
Add the chilli flakes, olives and chopped tomatoes and cook for 6–8 mins until slightly reduced. Drain the tuna and add it to the pan along with a ladle of the reserved pasta water. Mix well.

Add the cooled pasta to the pan and toss everything together until emulsified and well coated. Remove from the heat, then finely chop the parsley and toss it through along with the Parmesan and a squeeze of the lemon. If the sauce is too tight, loosen with a splash more pasta water, you want it quite loose so it freezes and reheats well.
Divide the pasta between four super cubes or freezer-safe containers, grate over the Cheddar, then seal and freeze.

To reheat: either thaw overnight in the fridge and microwave until piping hot, or place the frozen cube in a steamer basket over a pan of simmering water and steam until heated through. Or take it to work frozen and microwave it there.

name: Probiotic Bircher Muesli
description: If you’re looking to set yourself up for a healthy week, prepping a bircher muesli is a fantastic way to pack in loads of plants. By swapping some of the yoghurt for kefir, you’re getting a healthy dose of fermented foods too. This recipe was made for customising so feel free to flavour yours however you choose.
instructions: Grate the apple into a large bowl before mixing in the remaining ingredients.
Cover and place in the fridge for at least a couple of hours and ideally overnight.
To serve, sprinkle over any nuts or seeds you like. Enjoy!

name: Proper Homemade Doughnuts
description: Learn to master this easy recipe and you’ve got the keys to the fried dough kingdom. Stuff ‘em with whatever you like. Jam, custard, curd – anything goes.
instructions: Add the flour, sugar, yeast and salt into the bowl of a stand mixer. Mix to combine.
Pour the milk into a small saucepan and heat so that it's warm to the touch, not hot. Whisk in the eggs and pour into the dry mix.
