Add the dough attachment to the mixer and set on a low speed for 7-8 mins. Once you’ve got a strong, springy dough, gradually add the softened butter, bit by bit, until fully incorporated. Mix for another 3-4 mins on low.

Tip the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and briefly knead for about 2 mins by picking up and slapping back down onto the bench. The dough will be very sticky to begin with, persevere and it will become easier to work with. A bench scraper is really handy here. Then, shape the dough into a rough ball and add it to a lightly floured bowl. Cover with a damp tea towel and leave to proof for 60-70 mins or until at least doubled in size.
Meanwhile, get some fillings ready and set up your shaping station. Also, grab some piping bags, this makes filling dead easy.

Cut twelve 7x7cm squares of parchment paper (if you’re making small doughnuts, cut 20 squares) and grab a bench scraper or table knife. Set up a digital scale and dust lightly with flour. Once your dough has proofed, punch the air out of it and turn out onto the bench.

Cut the dough into portions. For medium doughnuts cut the dough into 60-65g portions, for small doughnuts, cut into 30-35g portions. Shape the dough into a ball by flattening it out onto the surface and tucking the corners in all the way around. Flip the dough over so the seam is flat against the bench and using the cup of your hand, roll the dough around to form a ball.
The surface tension of the bench and dough will form the doughnut into a smooth uniform ball. This might take a bit of practice, just keep at it, once you’ve got it, you’ve got it!

Transfer the dough ball onto one of the parchment squares, and slide under a damp tea towel. Repeat with the remaining dough balls. Leave to proof for another 50 mins or so, until at least doubled in size again.

To set up the frying station you want a large pot, filled halfway with veg oil. Gradually bring this to 165°C monitoring regularly. You’ll also need a tray lined with kitchen paper to drain your cooked doughnuts, plus a slotted spoon.

Once proofed, fry your doughnuts in batches. Carefully lower each doughnut into the oil, paper-side up. If correctly proofed, they will float to the top straight away. Remove the paper and fry for 3 mins until the underside is dark brown. Gently flip and cook for another 3 mins until golden brown on both sides. Remove from the oil and drain on the lined tray. Repeat with the remaining doughnuts.
Roll the doughnuts in extra sugar and use a chopstick or butter knife to create a hole in the doughnuts. Pipe in the fillings of choice and serve straight away.

name: Proper Tomato Soup
description: Nothing beats a bowl of homemade soup. This recipe for cream of tomato soup is an absolute classic. You’ll never touch the tinned stuff again.
instructions: Peel the onion and carrot and dice into 1cm cubes. Add the butter to a large saucepan over a medium heat, then add the onion and carrots along with a big pinch of salt. Fry gently for 10 mins until softened.

Finely chop the garlic and add it to the pan along with the tomato paste and fry for 2 more min. Add the tomatoes and use your spoon to break them up in the pan, refill one of the cans of tomatoes with water and add to the pan along with the stock cube and the sugar. Bring to the boil, then turn to a simmer and cook for 40 mins.
Use a stick blender to blitz into a smooth purée, taste, and season with the vinegar. Add the cream and gently reheat.
Tip into meal-prep containers. Store in the fridge for up to 3 days until ready to reheat and eat. Top with some extra grated Cheddar cheese and a crack of black pepper if you like.

name: Prosciutto & Mozzarella Panini
description: This panini recipe has it all –it’s creamy, spicy, salty, fresh and zingy. And stuffed between two slices of toasted bread. It makes the perfect sandwich for lunch (or dinner) and features high-quality ingredients that will fill you up for hours to come.
instructions: Cut the ciabatta in half horizontally. Drain the ball of mozzarella and cut it into 1cm slices. Drain the roasted peppers and cut in half.
Smear one side of the ciabatta with the pesto and the other with the harissa. Layer in the mozzarella, prosciutto and roasted red peppers, then stuff with handfuls of the rocket.

Heat a griddle pan or panini press over a medium-high heat. Put the ciabatta into the pan and put another heavy frying pan on top (if using the griddle pan), or shut the lid to press. If your griddle isn’t big enough, cut the panini in half to fit it in.
Toast for 2-3 minutes, then flip and repeat. Cut in half and serve with a big pile of crisps.

name: Prosciutto Piadina
description: You can find these delicious sandwiches eaten all over the Romagna region of Italy. This is our version.
instructions: Add the flour, salt and baking soda to a large bowl and mix. Tip in the olive oil and mix through the dry ingredients. Now add 225ml of room temperature water to the bowl. Mix with your hands until you have a shaggy dough.
Tip out onto a clean work surface and knead for 5-6 mins. Wrap the dough in plastic and let rest at room temp for 20-30 mins.

Divide into 6 balls and roll out into roughly 20-30cm flatbreads. Add to a dry pan and cook over a high heat for 1-2 mins on each side until lightly charred and cook through. Keep warm in a dry tea towel.

Now, it’s time to build. Lay out your piadina and fill each quarter with a different ingredient. In the top left lay the prosciutto, top right sliced mozzarella seasoned with salt and pepper. Bottom left seasoned sliced tomato with balsamic vinegar and bottom right a handful of fresh rocket. Now pull the bottom half up over the top, and fold again into quarters. Wrap in parchment paper to secure and serve. Repeat with the remaining piadinas.

name: Prosciutto Wrapped Chicken with Sage & Quinoa
description: Impressive dinners usually mean piles of washing up - not this one. Wrapped in a simple parchment parcel, chicken with salty prosciutto and nutty quinoa cooks itself in the oven.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Lay out a large rectangle of baking paper in front of you, portrait. Arrange the Tenderstem Broccoli in a single layer on the bottom half of the paper leaving a 10cm gap between the edge closest to you and the food, then scatter over the quinoa. Drizzle with the olive oil, season with salt and black pepper and mix everything together. Repeat with the remaining ingredients.If you’re scaling up for more people, just use a foil-lined baking tray and a tight foil lid instead. Cooking times might vary, so keep an eye on it.

Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Place the sage leaves on top of each chicken breast, then wrap with prosciutto to seal. Lay the wrapped chicken on top of the veg and quinoa. Fold the top half of the baking paper over the food then fold the outside edges over each other to seal (like a cornish pasty), creating a steam-tight parcel. Transfer to the oven and cook for 15-20 mins, depending on the thickness of your chicken.

If you’d like crispy prosciutto, then heat the grill to high. Unwrap the parcel, remove the chicken and transfer to a baking tray. Slide it under the grill for 2 mins, or until the prosciutto is golden and crisp. Cut the lemon into wedges.
Squeeze over the lemon juice before serving and dig in.

name: Protein & Fibre Flapjacks
description: These no-bake protein flapjacks are the perfect grab-and-go snack. Packed with seeds, nut butter, and protein powder, they’re ideal for a post-workout refuel or a midday energy boost. They take just 20 minutes to prep and can be customised however you fancy.
instructions: Add the oats, protein powder, peanut butter, almond milk, flaxseeds, chia seeds, and mixed seeds to a large bowl. Mix everything together until you have a thick, cookie dough-like paste.
Line a small baking tray with parchment paper. Press the mixture firmly into the tray, smoothing the top with the back of a spoon.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours, or until firm. Once chilled, slice into 6 bars or squares.
Eat as-is or jazz them up with your favourite toppings—try a dollop of yoghurt, some fresh berries, or a drizzle of melted dark chocolate and tahini.

name: Protein Date Balls
description: These protein and peanut butter-packed date balls are the perfect healthy snack. Take them with you wherever you go.
instructions: Add all the ingredients to a food processor and blend until you have a fine breadcrumb texture.
Portion into equal-sized balls and squeeze them tightly into balls. Crush the peanuts.
Roll the balls in the crushed peanuts and finish with flaky salt. These will last up to a 7 days in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer.

name: Protein French Toast with Peanut Butter & Homemade Jam
description: This French toast is packed full of goodness with plenty of protein and fibre to help you feel full and energised for the day ahead. It’s simple and delicious, like pudding for breakfast!
keywords: Protein French Toast with Peanut Butter & Homemade Jam
instructions: Start by making the jam, this recipe makes 310g jar worth per serving. Juice the lemon (you'll need a teaspoon per serve). Tip the berries into a saucepan set over a medium heat and cook for 5-7 mins until juicy. Then stir in the lemon juice and mash to your desired jam consistency. Add the chia seeds and honey, cook for a few minutes until thickened, then set aside to cool.
Combine the milk and protein powder in a shallow dish to form a paste. For each serving, add one whole egg and the whites of the other egg, then whisk together with the protein paste until smooth.
Heat a non-stick frying pan and soak both sides of each slice of bread in the egg mixture. Once the pan is hot, add the soaked bread to the pan. Cook over a medium heat for a few minutes each side.
Load the slices of toast onto a plate, then add the yoghurt, peanut butter and jam. Drizzle with the honey and the extra peanut butter, then scatter the crushed peanuts on top.

name: Protein Pancakes
description: These are the protein pancakes to end all protein pancakes. They’re light, fluffy and very delicious. Packed with over 30g of protein per portion. Make a batch and freeze them for an easy 2-minute breakfast.
instructions: Make the pancake batter. Add the greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, whole egg, milk, protein powder and vanilla extract to a blender. Blend on a high speed until completely smooth, about 45 secs. Pour the mixture into a large mixing bowl.

Add the flour, baking powder and salt to the mixing bowl with the wet ingredients in it and whisk gently until just incorporated. You don’t want to overmix it so some small lumps are fine. Leave it to sit in the bowl at room temperature for 5 mins.

Now cook the pancakes. Set a non-stick frying pan with a lid over a low heat to warm up, about a minute. Spray the pan lightly with some oil, then add a ladle of pancake batter into the pan and pop the lid on top. If your pan is big enough you can cook multiple at a time. Cook for 2 ½ mins. Using a spatula, flip the pancake over and put the lid back on the pan. Cook for another 2 mins. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Repeat with the remaining batter.
Once cool, pop them in a ziplock bag and keep in the freezer. Microwave for 1-2 mins to defrost.
Serve with your choice of toppings. Greek yoghurt, fresh fruits and honey work great.

name: Protein Peanut Butter Cups
description: These high-protein peanut butter cups will satisfy your sweet tooth. They're an easy, no-bake high-protein snack.
instructions: Make the peanut butter filling. Warm the peanut butter in the microwave for 20–30 secs until runny. Stir in the protein powder until smooth and thick.
In a heatproof bowl, melt the dark chocolate and coconut oil together until glossy — either in short microwave bursts or over a pan of simmering water.

Assemble the cups. Line a mini muffin tin or silicone mould with paper cases. Spoon 1 tsp of melted chocolate into the base of each case. Add 1–2 tsp of the peanut butter filling, then cover with another spoonful of melted chocolate.
Transfer to the fridge or freezer and chill for at least 1 hour, or until fully set.
To serve, peel from the cases and enjoy straight from the fridge or slightly softened at room temp.

name: Pudina (Mint) Chutney
description: We've got the perfect dip for your samosas. Enter, Pudina Chutney. A breeze to make and loaded with flavour – be careful, because she's got a kick.
instructions: First, zest and juice 1 lime. Then, add all of the ingredients into a food processor and blitz into fine paste. Serve with hot samosas and a cup of chai.

name: Pulled Chicken Peri Peri Rice
description: Nothing more or nothing less than a bowl of fiery goodness. The lovely spiced peri peri rice, the tender chicken. The sweet bursts from the corn. Phenomenal.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Place your chicken breasts on a baking tray and sprinkle over your paprika, along with a glug of olive oil and a sprinkling of salt and pepper. Rub this all into the breast, then whack the tray in the oven for 30 minutes.

Veg time. Chop your peppers and red onion into large chunks, slice your lemon in half and put it all onto a baking tray along with the corn. Drizzle over some olive oil and sprinkle some salt and pepper on top before getting it into the oven for 30 minutes.
Once cooked, remove your chicken from the oven, it’s pulling time. Get two forks and tear apart your cooked chicken breasts. Then, set aside temporarily.

In a frying pan, heat a glug of olive oil. Chop your red chillies and garlic and add them to the pan. Add your oregano. Fry until the garlic and chilli are soft, then add your peri peri rice pouch to the pan. Mix everything in the pan together.

Into a large bowl, add your rice, pulled chicken and roasted veg, along with a handful of chopped coriander and chopped mint. Slice the corn off of the cob and add it to the bowl. Mix everything together and you’re ready to serve. Plate up the rice and get stuck in!

name: Pulled Chipotle Chicken & Pineapple Tacos
description: Smoky chipotle chicken and zingy pineapple salsa are a match made in taco heaven. With your leftover from your batch, midweek tacos just got a whole lot easier.
keywords: Pulled Chipotle Chicken & Pineapple Tacos recipe
instructions: Make the Juicy Pulled Chipotle Chicken.

Trim and peel the pineapple, then finely dice it. Finely dice the red onion and add both to a bowl with the juice of half the limes. For a spicier salsa, finely chop the Scotch bonnet. If you prefer it mild, just halve the chilli and let it infuse. Stir the chilli through the pineapple mix and set aside.
Warm the pulled chipotle chicken in a saucepan over a low heat until piping hot. Toast the tortillas in a dry frying pan for 20–30 seconds on each side until warm and flexible.
Pick the coriander leaves and discard the stalks.
Lay out the tortillas and load them up with the hot chipotle chicken, spoonfuls of pineapple salsa and a scattering of fresh coriander. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

name: Pulled Chipotle Chicken Jacket Potato
description: Golden crispy jackets stuffed with leftovers from your Juicy Pulled Chipotle Chicken batch, topped with feta, salsa and zingy pickled onions. It's super easy and utterly delicious.
keywords: Pulled Chipotle Chicken Jacket Potato recipe
instructions: Make the Juicy Pulled Chipotle Chicken
Heat the oven to 200°C.
Scrub the potatoes, prick them all over with a fork, then rub with olive oil and salt. Bake directly on the oven shelf for 1 hr until crisp on the outside and fluffy inside.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the red onion and squeeze over the juice half the limes. Season with a pinch of salt and set aside to pickle. Pick the coriander leaves from their stems and set aside.
Warm the leftover pulled chipotle chicken in a saucepan set over a low heat until piping hot throughout. Add a splash of water if needed to loosen the sauce. Crumble the feta.
Once the potatoes are cooked, cut a deep cross into each one and squeeze from the base to open. Fluff up the inside with a fork, then pile in the hot chipotle chicken.
Top each jacket with a spoonful of salsa, crumbled feta, the quick-pickled onions and fresh coriander. Serve with lime wedges and hot sauce on the side.

name: Pulled Mushroom Ragù
description: The richest, umami-est mushroom ragu you could dream of. Pulled oyster mushrooms replace meat here, and they do it well. Delightful.
instructions: Pop your porcini mushrooms in a heatproof jug and pour over 400ml boiling water. Leave to soak for 20 mins, then remove your mushrooms from the liquid and finely chop them (but keep your liquid).
Prep your veg. Finely dice your onion, carrot and celery. Finely chop your garlic, rosemary and thyme.

Heat a small glug of olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Add a few of your king oyster mushrooms at a time with a pinch of salt and sear them hard for a few minutes until browned and softened, turning occasionally so that they cook evenly. Repeat with your remaining mushrooms.
Place your mushrooms on a chopping board and finely shred them with 2 forks. Set aside until later.

Heat a glug of olive oil over a medium heat in a cast iron pot. Add your onion, carrot and celery and fry over a medium-low heat for 10 minutes until softened. Tip in your tomato puree, garlic and all but a tsp of your rosemary and thyme. Cook for another 2 minutes.

Pour your wine into the pan and stir until it has evaporated. Add your chopped tomatoes, porcini mushroom stock, chopped porcini, shredded oyster mushrooms, marmite and bay leaf to the pan. Give it a good mix and bring the mixture to a boil. Turn down the heat and simmer for an hour.

Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a frying pan. Add your breadcrumbs and remaining herbs along with a pinch of salt and give it a good stir. Toast for about 5 minutes over a medium heat until you have crisp, golden breadcrumbs. They go quickly, so keep an eye on them.
Cook your spaghetti according to packet instructions in salted water. Drain, saving a mugful of pasta water.
Season ragu with salt and pepper, then toss in your spaghetti along with your pasta water. Mix with your tongs until your sauce coats your spaghetti beautifully, adding more pasta water if needed.
Serve up in bowls with your crispy breadcrumbs.

name: Pulled Pork Burger
description: The perfect, sticky pulled pork. Sharp pickles. All on a toasted brioche bun. Great shout for a big hungry crowd.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 140°C. Rub the pork shoulder all over with the paprika, 1/4 of the sugar and a generous amount of salt and pepper.
Place the pork into a roasting dish or a casserole dish with a lid. Pour in the apple cider and stock, cover with tin foil/lid and cook for 5 hours, until shreddable with two forks.
Meanwhile, make the BBQ sauce. Add the ketchup, apple cider vinegar, soy sauce, the remaining sugar and a good few dashes of tabasco and the water to a pan. Bring to the boil.

Add the pork juices/stock from the roasting tray and a the smoked paprika. Let it simmer, stirring regularly for 10 minutes until thickened. Leave to cool completely - you want the BBQ sauce to be tangy to cut through the pork later.
Onto the slaw. Finely slice the red onion, shred the cabbage and carrots. Mix with the mayonnaise, extra apple cider vinegar and a splash of pickling liquor from the gherkin jar. Season to taste.
Once your pork is cooked, tip the liquid into a jug and pour off any fat. Pull the pork with two forks and add 3/4 of the BBQ sauce. Mix well to combine and add cooking liquor to taste.

Cut the buns in half (toast them if you like). Spoon in a dollop of the remaining BBQ sauce followed by the pulled pork, a big handful of slaw and some sliced gherkins. Serve with the remaining slaw on the side. Pulled pork done.

name: Pumpkin & Parmesan Soup with Crispy Sage Butter
description: A smooth, vibrant pumpkin soup seasoned with Parmesan and topped with a fragrant sage and chilli butter. A classic flavour combo for autumn.
instructions: Peel and roughly chop the pumpkin and onion.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Sauté the pumpkin and onion for about 10 mins until starting to soften then add the chicken stock and leave to simmer for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, grate the Parmesan, finely chop the sage leaves and roughly chop the hazelnuts.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and add the cream, ⅕ of the chopped sage and the Parmesan. Blitz with a stick blender then season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Heat the butter in a small pan over a medium-high heat until sizzling then stir through the remaining chopped sage, hazelnuts and chilli flakes.
Divide the soup between bowls and drizzle over the fragrant butter.

name: Purple Cabbage Soup
description: This soup is beautiful and delicious, and it doesn’t hurt that the anthocyanins in red cabbage are full of antioxidants.
instructions: Peel and chop the onions and garlic. Heat a few spoons of olive oil in a large pot over medium heat then add the onions and garlic and sauté for about 5 mins, or until fragrant.
Roughly chop the cabbage into chunks, and peel and dice the potatoes. Add to the pot, season with salt and pepper to taste, then sauté for an additional 5	 mins to allow the flavours to meld.

Pour in the broth and bring to a gentle boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 20 mins, or until the potatoes are fork-tender. Transfer the mixture to a blender and blitz until very smooth, adding the cream as you blend. Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt and pepper, if necessary.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Roughly chop the chives, pistachios and parsley. Garnish the soups with a drizzle of olive oil, and sprinkle with the chives, pistachios, and fresh parsley.

name: Puttanesca Eggs
description: What do you get when you cross a shakshuka with a puttanesca sauce? Puttanesca eggs. This recipe is tangy, tomatoey, and perfect for when you want a quick and easy dinner.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the garlic cloves, and thickly slice the olives.

Pour 1 tbsp of oil from the anchovy tin into a large, deep frying pan over a medium heat and add the anchovies, sliced garlic and chilli flakes. Cook gently, stirring regularly for a few minutes until the garlic is soft and the anchovies have broken up. Pour in the passata, add the sugar if using, capers and green olives and bring to a simmer. Bubble gently for 10 mins, stirring occasionally, until thickened slightly, then season with salt and lots of cracked black pepper.
Cut the sourdough into 4cm-wide fingers and brush with the remaining 1 tbsp anchovy oil.

Turn the heat under the frying pan down to low-medium. Use a large spoon to make four wells in the tomato sauce and crack an egg into each one. Put on a lid, or cover with a baking tray, and simmer very gently for around 6-8 mins until the whites of the eggs are just set but the yolks are runny (checking every now and then so they don't overcook).
Meanwhile, heat a griddle pan or frying pan over a high heat and grill the bread for 1 min on each side until crunchy, caramelised and a little charred.
Tear over the parsley leaves and serve with the bread soldiers for dunking and scooping-up all that lovely sauce and yolk.

name: Puttanesca Gnocchi Traybake
description: Like a puttanesca, but with tinned tuna and chewy gnocchi for a gorgeous midweek bake.
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C. Drain the tuna and set aside.
Toss the gnocchi in half of the oil and season with salt and pepper. Pop into the oven and cook for 5-10 mins, until golden.
Get half of the cherry tomatoes into a blender and blitz until smooth, or use a stick blender.

Finely slice the garlic and chilli (deseed it if you like it less spicy!). Heat the rest of the oil in a large pan over a medium heat and add the garlic and chilli, cooking out for 2 mins. Add the tomato purée and cook for another 1-2 mins before adding the blitzed cherry tomatoes, and the remaining un-blitzed cherry tomatoes, olives, capers and water (use it to swill out the blender and tin before adding in). Season with salt and pepper and bring to a simmer for about 15 mins.
Gently mix the tuna through the sauce along with torn basil.
Pour the sauce over the gnocchi then tear over the mozzarella and grate over the parmesan. Slide back into the oven for 15-20 mins until bubbling and golden.

name: Puttanesca Pasta Bake
description: We’ve turned the classic puttanesca into a comforting vegan pasta bake. Packed with flavourful ingredients and flaky vegan tuna.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the garlic, drain the capers and olives. Roughly chop the capers and slice the olives into small pieces. Separate the basil leaves from the stalks, and keep both. Using a fork, break the vegan tuna into small pieces.

Pour the olive oil into a large saucepan. Add the garlic and place over medium heat. Cook for 1 min to infuse the oil. Once golden, stir through the tomato paste, cook until it has darkened and gone a deeper red, 3-4 mins. Stir through the capers, chilli flakes and olives.

Add the tins of plum tomatoes into the pan and break the tomatoes up with a wooden spoon. Stir through the sugar, basil stalks, the water and season with salt and pepper. Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for 15-20 mins, until thickened.
Meanwhile, bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil and cook your pasta 2 mins shy of packet instructions.
Reserve a big mug of pasta water, then drain the pasta. Preheat your grill to high. Remove the basil stalks from the sauce.

Stir the pasta, vegan tuna and three-quarters of the basil leaves through the sauce, loosening with the reserved pasta water, if needed. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Transfer the mixture to an ovenproof dish. Grate the vegan cheese over and place it under the grill until the cheese has melted and goes golden.
Garnish with the remaining fresh basil leaves.

name: Puttanesca Pasta Salad
description: We love puttanesca pasta. And we love salads. We've combined the two here for a fresh and fierce lunch or dinner recipe.
instructions: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Add the pasta and cook following pack instructions.

Quarter the cherry tomatoes and add to the bowl with the kalamata olive and capers. Use a peeler to peel the Parmesan into the bowl. Finely chop most of the parsley and add to the bowl along with the chilli flakes.

Once the pasta is cooked through, tip into a sieve and run under cold water until cool. Tip into the bowl. Add the lemon juice and 2-3 tbsp olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper and toss well.
Tip into a bowl and top with the reserved parsley leaves.

name: Puttanesca-Style Focaccia Pizza
description: A dead simple focaccia pizza that we've topped with a puttanesca-inspired topping, perfect for a dinner party with Spotify.
instructions: Add 360g of warm water to a large bowl or stand mixer along with the yeast and sugar. Whisk together and add the flour. Mix and knead in the bowl for 8-9 mins until you have a strong, slightly sticky dough. Leave to rest for 30 mins.

Add 20g of water to a bowl and add the salt and 40g of olive oil. Mix to combine. Add to the rested dough and knead for a further 7-8 mins to incorporate. Shape into a rough ball and pop the dough in the fridge for 5-6 hours or leave at room temp for 1-2 hours.

While the dough rests, make the sauce. Thinly slice the garlic cloves. Add a good few glugs of olive oil to a small saucepan and set over medium heat. Add the garlic and sizzle for 1-2 mins. Add the chopped tomatoes and the stalks of the basil. Turn down the heat and let simmer for 20-25 mins. Season with salt and pepper and allow to cool.

Line a 24cm x 30cm baking tray with parchment and add a splash of olive oil. Tip your dough into the tray and squish into the corners. Allow to proof for 1 hour at room temperature or until doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.

With damp hands, create dimples in the dough by pressing down the length of the bread with your fingertips. Top with the tomato sauce, torn mozzarella, thinly sliced red onion, capers, anchovies, black olives and chilli flakes. Give the ingredients a little squish into the bread.
Bake for 25 mins until golden brown and cooked through. Now remove from the oven and top with extra sauce, mozzarella, torn basil leaves and some fine grated parmesan.
Serve warm from the oven with salad.

name: Quick & Cheesy Barbacoa Glazed Beef Tacos
description: We’ve used Old El Paso's new Street Vibes Barbacoa kit to bring the tastes of street food to your own kitchen, with these tasty tacos. They've got the signature smokiness of barbacoa but are ready in just 20 minutes.
ingredients: 1 Old El Paso Street Vibes Barbacoa Soft Taco Kit
instructions: Grate the garlic cloves into a small bowl and add the whole Old El Paso Seasoning Mix and the tomato purée. Mix together.

Place a large pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the beef mince, season with salt and cook for 5-8 mins until browned and crispy in places. Take it off the heat and stir through the Old El Paso Smoky Cooking Sauce. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

Place the empty pan back onto a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the spice and tomato purée blend (from step 1) and cook for 2-3 mins until it turns dark red. Then, add the bay leaves and pour the beef stock in. Bring it to the boil, reduce the heat down to low and simmer whilst cooking the rest of the meal.
Very finely dice the onion and mince the coriander (stalks and all) and set aside.

Heat a new frying pan over a medium heat. Dip a tortilla into the simmering sauce and place into the hot pan. Once toasted, flip and cover with grated mozzarella. Cook for a few more seconds, until the cheese is starting to melt then transfer to a tray. Continue with the rest of the tortillas.
Top the cheesy tortillas with the beef (quickly reheat the beef first if needed), the diced onion and the coriander. Serve with some lime wedges and any extra sauce on the side for dipping.

name: Quick & Creamy Butter Bean Bowl
description: This creamy, cosy vegan butter bean bowl is filling and delicious and comes together in just 20 minutes.
instructions: Finely slice the garlic. Heat a pot or deep saucepan over medium-low heat with a drizzle of olive. Stir fry the garlic for a few minutes until just starting to become fragrant and translucent. Drain the butterbeans, reserving the liquid of 1 can.

Add the drained beans, liquid and tomatoes to the pan. Reduce the heat to low. Stir for a few minutes until the tomatoes are starting to soften. Squash the tomatoes with the back of a spoon so that they release their juices. Stir through the spinach
Add the vegan cream cheese and stir to create a creamy sauce with the tomato juice and butterbean liquid.
When the spinach has wilted, season well and taste. Add a squeeze of lemon juice and some chilli flakes if using. Serve with crusty bread or with rice.

name: Quick & Easy Soda Bread
description: This easy soda bread recipe makes a lovely crusty, fluffy loaf. It requires no prior bread-making skills, and can be whipped up in the time it takes for your oven to preheat.
instructions: Heat the oven to 230°C. Put a baking tray onto the middle rack of the oven.
Sift both flours, salt and bicarbonate of soda into a large bowl, then mix together. Make a well in the centre and pour in the buttermilk. Stir the dough together until no pockets of flour remain.
Spoon onto a large piece of baking parchment. Using wet hands, gently pat into a uniform round. Scatter the oats on top and gently pat them all over the loaf.
Transfer the dough to the preheated tray. Bake for 45-50 mins until golden brown all over. Allow to cool for at least 30 mins, until just warm, before slicing into it.

name: Quick & Easy Yoghurt Flatbreads
description: These flatbreads come together so quickly and are far superior to anything you’ll ever buy in the supermarkets. They’re going to become one of your staple recipes.
instructions: Combine the flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Mix well.
Stir through the yoghurt until a dough forms, then knead together until thoroughly incorporated. Divide the dough into four balls, cover and let rest for 10 mins.

Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat. Dust a work surface with a little flour and roll each ball of dough out until thin, around 2mm. Once the pan is hot, add a flatbread and cook on both sides until golden, for a total of 2-3 mins. Continue until all the flatbreads are cooked.

name: Quick & Spicy Beef Ramen
description: Proper ramen takes days to make but this is a simple way to get your fix. It’s spicy, umami and salty. Slurp it up until it’s gone.
instructions: Mix together the soy sauce, vegetable oil, black pepper and a pinch of salt in a mixing bowl. Add the steak and make sure it’s well coated in the sauce, then set aside to marinate.

For the broth, smash the ginger with the back of a knife and peel and halve the onion. Add to a large saucepan along with the remaining broth ingredients and a pinch of salt and mix to combine. Set the pan over a high heat, pop the lid on and bring the mixture to a boil then turn the heat down to low-medium and let it simmer for 30 mins.

Meanwhile, prep your garnish. Thinly slice the white onion, spring onion and fresh coriander. Add to a mixing bowl and mix until fully combined, then set aside. Cut the lime into wedges and set aside.

When the broth has 10-15 mins left, cook the steak. Heat a dry frying pan over a high heat for a minute. Add a glug of vegetable oil and swirl the pan around to coat it in the oil. Gently place the steak into the pan and cook for 1 min 30 secs per side (this will give you a medium steak; adjust timings if you prefer it more or less cooked). Transfer the steak to a plate and set aside to rest.

For the beansprouts and noodles, bring a pan of water to the boil. Add the beansprouts and cook for 30-45 secs then fish them out with a sieve and set aside. Add the ramen noodles to the same pan and cook for a minute less than packet instructions then drain and divide between the serving bowls.
Cut the rested steak into thin strips.

To serve, ladle the broth over the noodles. Top with the slices of steak along one side and the beansprouts along the other. Put a generous handful of the onion coriander mix in the middle. Drizzle over the sesame oil and chilli oil and finish with a wedge of lime.

name: Quick & Spicy Noodle Soup
description: Low effort, high reward – quick and creamy Thai green noodle soup. A perfect weeknight dinner that barely requires you to chop. Chuck things into pans and done.
instructions: Put a large, deep saucepan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add one of the coconut cream tins and cook until the oil separates and the coconut solids turn golden.
Meanwhile, pick the leaves off the coriander, set aside.

Add the curry paste and coriander stems to the coconut oil, then cook, stirring, for 2 mins. Pour the chicken stock in along with enough water to fill the saucepan, then bring to the boil. Turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 10-15 mins to make a broth (skim off any foam that comes up).
Meanwhile, cook the noodles following pack instructions. Trim and thinly slice the radishes (use a mandoline if you have one).
Strain the broth through a fine mesh sieve, then stir through the remaining coconut cream and watercress until wilted. Season with fish sauce, lime juice and black pepper.
Divide the noodles and soup between bowls, then top with a drizzle of chilli oil, radishes, crispy shallots and coriander leaves to serve.

name: Quick & Spicy Pappardelle "Biang Biang Noodles"
description: A quick and satisfying pasta recipe inspired by biang biang noodles. On the table in under half an hour.
instructions: Bring a pot of lightly salted water to the boil for the pasta (season lightly, as it will impart flavour on the pasta – remember you can always add more salt later).

Meanwhile, mince the garlic and ginger, then finely slice the spring onions (reserve a small handful of the green tops for garnish – place into a bowl of cold tap water to make them super crunchy). Finely slice all the coriander stems to make 3 tbsp. Keep the leaves for garnish.
Combine all the sauce ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.

Put all the oil, ginger and spring onions into a pasta pot, or medium sized pot. Turn the heat to medium, then cook until the ginger starts to sizzle and turns lightly golden brown. Reduce the heat to low, add the garlic and sesame seeds, then cook for 1 min, mixing all the time so nothing burns. Once the seeds are lightly golden, turn off the heat and immediately add the chilli flakes (if your sesame seeds are pre-toasted, then add with the chilli flakes). Pour in the sauce, mix well and set aside.

Boil the pappardelle in the boiling water 30 seconds less than pack instructions. Then use tongs to transfer the noodles straight into the sauce pot, allowing some pasta water to come with it. Turn the heat to medium and toss with pasta water, to make it glossy. Turn off the heat and add all the sliced coriander. Taste for seasoning – you may need a dash of salt depending on the saltiness of your pasta water, and you may want to add a small splash more fish sauce.

Divide between serving bowls and top with crushed peanuts, chilli oil and the drained spring onion tops and coriander leaves. Eat with steamed greens and fried eggs, if you like. Optionally serve with more rice wine/black vinegar.

name: Quick & Thick Vanilla Custard
description: A beautifully rich vanilla custard pastry cream that's perfect for filling doughnuts or using up in bread and butter pudding.
instructions: Stir the egg yolks and sugar together in a heatproof bowl.

Heat the cream in a pan with the salt and vanilla pod until hot but not boiling. You’ll know it’s hot when it starts to steam. Pour the hot cream over the egg yolks slowly and evenly, whisking continuously as you go. Get someone to help you here if possible – they can pour while you whisk.

Place the bowl over a pan of simmering water to make a double boiler, and heat, whisking continuously with a large balloon whisk, until it thickens. The custard is ready when the bubbles disappear. Another good test is to drag your wooden spoon through the middle of the custard – if it is ready the spoon will leave a mark that takes a moment to disappear. It should take about 8 mins to get to this stage.
Remove the vanilla pod, split it lengthways and scrape the seeds into the custard. If necessary sieve the custard through a fine mesh to eliminate any lumps, then pour into a jug and serve at once.

name: Quick Beef Chilli with Peppers and Onions
description: Smoky, spicy and unbelievably cosy. This one-pot beef chilli with rice hits the spot every time. Pile it high with Cheddar, sour cream and a squeeze of lime, for easy meals throughout the week.
instructions: Peel and dice the onion. Dice the red pepper. Peel and finely slice the garlic.

Set a large saucepan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the beef mince and fry for 5–6 mins, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned all over. Season well with salt and black pepper, then transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, heat another drizzle of oil if needed. Add the onion, pepper and garlic. Fry for 6–8 mins until soft and starting to catch.
Add the bay leaves, cayenne, cumin, oregano and smoked paprika. Stir and cook for 1–2 mins to toast the spices.
Squeeze in the tomato purée and stir for 2 mins until deepened in colour.

Pour in the chopped tomatoes and chicken stock, then return the browned beef to the pan. Give it all a good stir, bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer for 25–30 mins until rich and thickened. Taste and season.
While that bubbles away, cook the rice according to pack instructions if you haven’t already. Grate the Cheddar and cut the lime into wedges.
Spoon the chilli over bowls of rice. Top with sour cream, grated Cheddar, a few coriander leaves and a wedge of lime. Finish with black pepper.

name: Quick Brothy Smoked Mackerel Udon
description: Smoky flaked mackerel and silky udon noodles in a light, miso-spiked broth with peppery watercress. Plus it's on the table in 15 minutes.
keywords: Quick Brothy Smoked Mackerel Udon recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the ginger and add to a large saucepan with the watercress and stock. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to a gentle simmer. Whisk in the miso until dissolved. Taste and add more miso or salt if needed.
Add the udon noodles to the broth, flake in the mackerel and stir for a couple of minutes until piping hot.
That's it! Divide between bowls and finish with a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Quick Chicken Tikka Masala
description: A really quick, easy take on the classic. The key here is to get that chicken nice and charred before it goes in to the curry.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.

Start by making the chicken marinade. Place the chicken thighs in a bowl. Add the ground turmeric, chilli powder, ground coriander and garam masala. Grate in the garlic and add the yoghurt. Season with salt and pepper, add a drizzle of olive and mix everything together. Cover and leave to marinate for 30 minutes.
Time to get on with the curry sauce. Slice up the brown onions. Add to a large pan with a good drizzle of olive oil. Cook on a medium heat until the onions are lovely and caramelised.
Finely chop the garlic clove and knob of ginger then add to the onions and cook for a minute until fragrant.

Add the turmeric, chilli powder, ground coriander and garam masala to the pan and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir through the tomato purée, followed by the passata and water. Give it a good mix.
Pour in the single cream, stir it through and bring the sauce to the boil. Once it is bubbling, turn it down. Let it simmer away so it can thicken.
Get your rice on (follow pack instructions).

Chicken time. Heat a griddle pan. Once very hot, add your chicken thighs in batches. Cook on a high heat for 4 minutes on each side, until charred. Place the char-grilled thighs in the oven for 10 mins or until they are cooked through.
Place the chicken on a board and cut into big pieces. Add to the curry sauce and fold everything together. Season the curry with salt and pepper.
Serve the chicken tikka masala over a bed of steaming rice. Garnish with some chopped coriander. Enjoy!

name: Quick Creamy 'Nduja Rigatoni
description: Spicy, creamy and ready in under 20 minutes. 'Nduja melts into crème fraîche for a sauce that clings to every piece of pasta, with a squeeze of lemon to balance it out. Great for weeknights when you need something delicious, fast.
instructions: Peel and finely chop the onions and roughly chop the parsley. Grate the Parmesan.
Bring a large saucepan of well-salted water to the boil and cook the pasta according to packet instructions. Before draining, reserve a mugful of the pasta cooking water.

Meanwhile, set a large frying pan over a medium heat and add a glug of olive oil. Add the onions with a pinch of salt and fry for 10 mins, until soft and translucent. Add the 'nduja and stir through, cooking for 2-3 mins until it melts into the oil and turns glossy.

Add the crème fraîche and stir to combine, then squeeze in the lemon juice. Add the drained pasta to the pan with a splash of the reserved cooking water and toss everything together until the sauce coats the pasta, adding more cooking water to loosen if needed.
Remove from the heat, stir through the parsley and most of the Parmesan. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
To serve, divide between bowls and finish with the remaining Parmesan.

name: Quick Flatbreads with Masala Chickpeas
description: Dr Rupy Aujla, of the Doctor's Kitchen, makes the freshest flatbreads using Arla Skyr Yogurt. Topped with spiced chickpeas and chilli oil. Check 'em out.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C/400°F

Make your flatbreads. Combine the Arla Skyr yogurt and flour with a pinch of salt in a bowl to
form a soft dough. Cover with cling film or a clean tea towel and let it rest for 15 mins.

Meanwhile, make your crispy masala chickpeas. Drain your chickpeas and pop them into a baking tray, then drizzle with a small glug of extra virgin olive oil. Grate in one clove of garlic and sprinkle on the garam masala and fennel seeds, then season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat the chickpeas in the oil and spices.
Roast for 15 mins, or until crispy.
Roughly chop your spinach and coriander. Quarter your tomatoes.
Once your chickpeas are done, throw your spinach and coriander leaves into the baking tray and let them wilt in the residual heat. Add your tomatoes to the tray and give it a mix.
Back to your flatbreads. Knead the dough for a couple of minutes on your work surface. Divide the dough into 8 balls.
Lightly oil your workbench. Using a rolling pin, roll each piece of dough out into a 15cm circle.
Heat a non-stick frying pan to a high heat and cook the flatbreads for 30 seconds on either side until golden brown.

Whilst your flatbreads are cooking, get a medium-sized saucepan filled with water and on to boil. Gently lower your eggs into the boiling water and cook for 6 and a half mins. Dunk the boiled eggs iced water to stop them cooking, then peel, halve and set aside.
Brush your flatbreads with a clove of garlic and drizzle with olive oil.
Top your flatbreads with the spiced chickpea mixture and halved boiled eggs. Drizzle with your chilli oil and a dollop of Arla Skyr yogurt. Serve and enjoy.

name: Quick Italian-Inspired Chickpea & Lentil Bowl
description: A hearty vegan stew with sun-dried tomatoes and black olives, topped with pesto and fresh basil leaves. Quick and easy to make for dinner tonight.
instructions: Dice the carrot, onion, celery and garlic. Chop the sun-dried tomatoes. Pit the olives. Chop the fresh basil.
Heat a good glug of oil on a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Once hot add the carrot, the celery and the onion and the garlic. Let the veggies cook for 5 mins.
Add the sun-dried tomatoes, black olives and the chilli and leave to cook for another 5 mins, stirring now and then.

Add the pulses and the chopped tomatoes. Add the pinch of bicarbonate of soda. (You’ll see it react with the chopped tomatoes, removing their acidity and bringing out their sweetness) and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 10 mins (cook for longer if you want a thicker consistency, or at a little water if it’s a bit dry).
Remove the pan from the heat and stir through the nutritional yeast.
To serve, divide between bowls and top with pesto, soy yoghurt and scatter over the fresh basil.

name: Quick Poached Chicken Pho
description: A lighter, faster take on pho. Fragrant broth, slippery noodles, and loads of fresh herbs. A warming weeknight hero.
instructions: Peel and slice the ginger, roughly chop the onion and smash the garlic cloves with the side of a knife.
Rinse the chicken breasts under cold water.
Pour the chicken broth into a large saucepan. Add the ginger, garlic, onion, sugar, salt, MSG and star anise. Drop in the chicken breasts and set the pan over a medium heat.
Once it starts to simmer, turn the heat down to low and poach the chicken gently — it should stay just below a simmer. Cook for 10–12 mins until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift the chicken out and set aside to rest. Strain the broth into a clean pan or bowl, discarding the solids. Stir in the fish sauce and keep the broth hot.
Meanwhile, soak the noodles in freshly boiled water for 3 mins until just tender. Drain and rinse under cold water to stop them cooking.
Finely slice the spring onions. Pick the mint and coriander leaves. Thinly slice the chillies if using.
Shred the rested chicken using two forks.

To serve, divide the noodles between bowls, pour over the hot broth, and top with the shredded chicken, beansprouts, herbs and spring onions. Add chilli oil or bird’s eye chillies if you fancy a kick.

name: Quinoa
description: Quinoa is one of our favourite grains. Use this recipe to make the perfect base for your lunch. It's foolproof.
instructions: Wash the quinoa.
Place into pan with water and a pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, turn down to low and cook for 15-20 mins until the water has been absorbed.
Remove from the heat and let steam for 5 mins. Fluff using a fork.

name: Quinoa & Fennel Salad
description: This fennel and quinoa salad with a roast garlic dressing is perfect for meal prep. Combine it with your choice of protein, carb and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Drizzle the garlic bulbs with a little olive oil and wrap them tightly in foil. Pop them on a baking tray then slide into the oven to roast for 30-35 mins.
Meanwhile, cook the quinoa following packet instructions. Finely slice the fennel (using a mandolin if you have one) and roughly chop the parsley.

Into a large bowl, add the yoghurt and the zest and juice of the lemons along with the squeezed out roasted garlic bulbs. Whisk well and season with salt and pepper. Add the cooked quinoa, fennel and parsley before giving it a good mix.
Enjoy with your choice of protein and carb. If meal prepping for the week, transfer to a container and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Quinoa, Prawn & Avocado Super Salad
description: A fresher than fresh salad. Ideal for lunches and meal prep. The dream team flavour combo.
instructions: Get your quinoa on. It should take 15 minutes in boiling water but check the packet for cooking directions.
Place the prawns in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and add 1 tbsp of olive oil. Mix together. Throw the prawns onto a hot griddle pan. They should take 1 ½ minutes on each side.
In the meantime, cut avocados into small cubes and add to a salad bowl. Peel and de-seed cucumber, chop into small chunks and add that too.
Once the prawns are pink and cooked through, remove them from the heat and add to a bowl, along with the cooked quinoa. Add a handful of chopped basil.
Dressing time. Add cider vinegar to a jar with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Mix it all together.
Pour the dressing over the salad, toss it together and serve! Enjoy!

name: Quorn, Pickled Ginger and Grapefruit Salad
description: A really beautiful, fresh salad. Sticky Quorn Roasted Sliced Fillets tossed up with fried green beans, pickled ginger, zingy grapefruit, and tonnes of herbs.
instructions: Toast the peanuts in a dry frying pan and then crush in a pestle and mortar.
Cut the ends of the green beans and thinly slice your shallots.
Pop the green beans into a frying pan with a glug of oil and a pinch of salt. Fry for 3-5 mins until they are crispy. Set aside to drain on a paper towel.
Add the shallots to the same pan, with more oil if needed and fry for 10-15 mins until very crispy and golden. Set aside to drain on a paper towel.
Finally, add the Quorn Roasted Sliced Fillets to the frying pan with 2 tbsp of soy sauce and 2 tbsp brown sugar. Cook for 5 mins until the pieces are coated and sticky.

Thinly slice the cabbage, finely chop the mint and grate the carrots. Cut off the ends of the grapefruit and slice off their skin. Cut along the lines of each segment to release the flesh in slices. Reserve the central part.

For the dressing, roughly chop the pickled ginger and finely chop the red chillies. Combine the ginger, chillies, 1 tbsp of soy sauce, sesame oil, the juice and zest of a lime, and 2 tbsp of ginger pickling liquid. Squeeze the central part of your grapefruits in too. Season with salt.
Get all your ingredients into a bowl and pour in your dressing. Top with a handful of crushed peanuts. Serve and enjoy!

name: Radish Salad Recipe
description: This radish salad is a vibrant, zesty dish that perfectly awakens your taste buds with its refreshing and gingery flavour. Ideal as a side or a light main, this radish salad recipe combines crisp radishes with a punchy vinaigrette, making it a delightful addition to your green salads repertoire. It pairs wonderfully with rice, offering a contrasting texture and flavour. For a complete meal, enjoy it alongside a sriracha fried egg or a protein-rich salmon fillet. This radish salad is not only a refreshing choice but also complements a variety of dishes, including those on a Mediterranean diet or served with pita bread. Enhance the flavour profile with a touch of white wine vinegar or fresh dill for an extra layer of freshness. Perfect for a picnic or as a quick, nutritious lunch, this radish salad will quickly become a favourite in your salad rotation.
instructions: Toast the coriander seeds in a small dry frying pan over a high heat for 1-2 mins until smelling amazing, then tip into a pestle and mortar or spice grinder and leave to cool. Once cool, roughly grind.

Peel the ginger then finely grate half of it into a large bowl. Add the sesame oil, a splash of olive oil and the zest and juice of the lime. Whisk together with a fork to make a dressing, adding sugar, salt and pepper to taste, as well as more lime juice if you like a sour kick.
Cut the remaining ginger into as thin matchsticks as you can, then finely slice the radishes and cucumber into rounds.

Add the radishes, cucumber and ginger matchsticks to the dressing bowl, along with the ground toasted coriander. Pick in most of the mint and coriander leaves. Roughly chop the cashews, add most of them to the bowl, then toss the salad together in the dressing so that everything gets nicely combined.
Pile the salad onto a platter. Top with the remaining cashews, mint and coriander then sprinkle over a few chilli flakes to serve, if you like.

name: Raffaello Cake
description: Inspired by the flavours of a Raffaello, this coconutty Raffaello cake recipe is to die for. It's boozy and beautiful.
instructions: For the sponge, start by heating the oven to 175°C. Butter the base and sides of a round 20cm springform cake tin and line the base with baking parchment.
Whisk the eggs, water and sugar in a stand mixer with the whisk attachment until light and fluffy.

Sift the flour, baking powder and salt over the mixture, then gently fold it together using a spatula. Add the ground almonds and fold gently, making sure not to overmix as this will cause the cake to be dense.
Pour the batter into the tin and level the surface. Bake for 40 mins until the cake is golden brown on top and a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean. Set aside to cool in the tin.
Once completely cool, remove from the tin and slice it into three separate layers, horizontally, using a cake wire or a serrated knife.

For the coconut cream, combine the double cream and coconut cream in a medium saucepan set over a high heat and bring to the boil. Remove the pan from the heat, then add the white chocolate and coconut rum. Leave for 2 mins, then stir until the chocolate is melted and the mixture is smooth. Cover with plastic wrap touching the surface of the cream, to prevent a skin forming, then chill in the fridge for 6 hrs.

When ready to serve, remove the coconut cream from the fridge. Whisk the chilled coconut cream with the mascarpone in a stand mixer with the whisk attachment on high speed, until the mixture thickens. Add the desiccated coconut and mix to combine.

For the almonds and coconut, tip the almonds into a dry frying pan set over a medium heat, then toast, tossing often, until golden brown. Set aside to cool completely. Toast the coconut in the same way and set aside to cool completely.

To assemble, place the first sponge cake layer on a cake board or serving plate and soak the sponge with one-third of the amaretto. Spread one-third of the coconut cream over the top of the first cake layer. Top with the second cake layer and soak this with another one-third of the amaretto, then spread half of the remaining coconut cream over the top. Top with the final cake layer and soak it with the remaining amaretto. Spread the remaining coconut cream over the top and sides of the cake.

Sprinkle the toasted coconut over the top of the cake. Cover the sides of the cake with the toasted almond flakes. Chill the cake in the fridge for at least 1 hr before serving. The cake will keep in the fridge for up to two days. Serve at room temperature.

name: Rainbow Vegetable Fritters
description: These rainbow veggie fritters are the perfect way to use up whatever leftover vegetables you have in your fridge. Here we’ve served them with a garlicky tahini dipping sauce.
instructions: Using a grater (or a mandolin or food processor if you have one), finely shred or slice the cabbage, sprouts, carrot, courgette, spring onions and red chilli. Add to a bowl with the drained sweetcorn a pinch of salt.

Sprinkle in the chickpea flour, a couple of tablespoons at a time, mixing with your hands until it starts to bind together and adding more chickpea flour as needed (you might need more than the specified weight depending on how wet the veg are).
To make the dipping sauce, mince the garlic and finely chop the parsley and juice the lemon then combine with the rest of the dipping sauce ingredients in a small bowl.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Drop a tbsp or so of mixture into the pan and fry for a couple of mins on each side until golden and crispy. Serve with the dipping sauce.

name: Ramen Eggs (Ajitsuke Tamago)
description: Elevate your ramen experience with our killer ramen eggs recipe, also known as ajitsuke tamago in Japanese cuisine. These savoury, marinated eggs are the perfect addition to your bowl of ramen noodles, adding a rich depth of flavor and a touch of umami. The soft-boiled eggs are bathed in a flavorful soy-based marinade that infuses them with a delightful balance of salty and sweet notes, creating a succulent, perfectly seasoned treat. Ideal for enhancing ramen soup, these eggs also make a fantastic topping for stir-fries or a simple snack on their own. Whether you're enjoying a bowl of instant ramen or a homemade noodle dish, these ramen eggs provide a gourmet touch that transforms an everyday meal into something special. Easy to prepare and incredibly versatile, this recipe is a must-try for any fan of Japanese cuisine.
instructions: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil, then carefully lower in the eggs. Reduce the bubble to a gentle simmer and set a timer for 6 mins 30 seconds. Get a bowl of ice cold water ready, then once the timer goes off, lift them straight into the cold water. Once cold, peel the eggs and put them into a small, tall container.

In a small bowl or jug, mix together the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, chilli flakes and star anise. Roughly chop the spring onions, peel and bash the garlic with the side of a chef's knife, then peel and thickly slice the ginger and add these to the bowl/jug too. Pour in 100ml water and mix really well. Pour over the eggs, ensuring they are mostly submerged.
Cover and put into the fridge for at least 6 hrs, but no longer than 24 hrs, turning them every now and again to get an even colour.
Remove from the liquid and cut in half to serve.

name: Ranch Cottage Cheese & Tomato on Toast
description: Pan con tomate, but better. Creamy herby cottage cheese, kind of like ranch (that condiment Americans love) and topped with jammy eggs. It’s surprisingly super filling and takes just 10 minutes to make.
keywords: Ranch Cottage Cheese & Tomato on Toast
Ranch Cottage Cheese & Tomato on Toast recipe
instructions: Place a saucepan of water on to boil. Once boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook for 6 mins, until jammy. Toast the bread.

Add the cottage cheese into a bowl and finely grate the garlic into it. Finely mince the parsley, chives, dill (stalks and all). Add all three into the cheese, zest half of the lemon and squeeze in as much juice as you like. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper, mix together.
Spread the ranch-style cottage cheese, make a divot in the middle, and grate the tomato in. Top with the eggs and a drizzle of olive oil. Finish with some salt and pepper.

name: Ras el Hanout Salmon With Bean Hummus
description: One for the cumin lovers out there, this speedy salmon is going to be a regular on your dinner table. We love the contrast between the hummus and crunchy salad.
keywords: Ras el Hanout Salmon With Bean Hummus
instructions:
Toast the cumin seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat
until smelling amazing. Set aside to cool.
Salad time. Drain and rinse half of the butter beans, then shake off
any excess water and tip into your largest salad bowl.
Thinly slice the spring onions (both green and white parts)
and roughly chop the coriander (stalks and all). Add these to the
bowl. Peel and grate the carrots and add too, along with the rocket,
three-quarters of the toasted cumin seeds and 2 tablespoons of the
olive oil. Finely grate in the zest of both lemons. Toss together, then
season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Set aside.
Next, lay the salmon fillets, skin-side down, on a cold frying pan
and rub 1 teaspoon of ras el hanout over each one. Season with salt
and pepper, drizzle with the remaining tablespoon of olive oil and
fry for 7 minutes, then flip and cook for 2 more minutes until the
salmon is just cooked and flakes easily.
Meanwhile, make the hummus. Drain the rest of the
butter beans over a bowl, saving the liquid. Tip the beans into a
food processor or blender and add the garlic, tahini, remaining
cumin seeds and the juice of 1⁄2 lemon. Blitz until completely
smooth, adding in some of the bean water until it’s at your desired
consistency – you’ll need about half. Season to taste.
Scrape the hummus into a saucepan and place over a low heat,
stirring occasionally to warm through.
Spread the warmed hummus onto four plates. Put a piece of
salmon on top, drizzle over any oil from the pan, then pile the salad
next to it. If you’re really hungry, serve with flatbreads.

name: Raspberry & Elderflower Mille-Feuille
description: If the thought of making mille-feuille scares you, look no further. This here is an easy alternative to this classic French dessert. C'est bon.
instructions: Take your puff pastry out of the fridge 25 mins before starting. Unroll the pastry sheet and cut into 12 equal pieces, prick with a fork, then transfer to a lined baking tray, making sure there is space in between each one. Dust with 4 tbsp of icing sugar, then top with another piece of baking paper. Weigh down with a baking tray and cook for 20 min. Until golden and crisp.
Whip the cream into stiff peaks, then fold through the custard and vanilla. Get the raspberries into a bowl with the elderflower cordial, sieve in the remaining icing sugar and mix.

Transfer the cream mixture into a piping bag and pipe onto 1 piece of the pastry, give it a little smoosh with a spoon to make a well, then fill with some of the raspberries. Repeat until you have 3 layers of pastry then dust with icing sugar.

name: Raspberry Custard
description: Think normal custard's a bit boring? We've got you covered. This raspberry custard will make you wish it was always pink.
instructions: Add the raspberries and the golden caster sugar to a saucepan over a medium heat. Cook the raspberries until they have broken down and then simmer for a couple of minutes to thicken. You might need to squish them slightly with a spoon! Set aside to cool.
When the raspberry mixture has cooled, pass it through the finest sieve you have to discard the seeds.
Now onto the custard. Add 2/5 of the golden caster sugar to a large bowl and add in the egg yolks, whisking until it looks creamy. Add in the cornflour and whisk again until combined. Set aside.

Heat the remaining golden caster sugar in a saucepan along with the milk, cream, vanilla extract and a tiny pinch of salt. Stir over a medium heat until the sugar has dissolved. Just before it starts simmering remove from the heat and cool down for a couple of minutes - if it's too hot it will scramble the egg yolks. Carefully and gradually pour the warm milk into the egg yolks, whisking constantly until all the mixture has been used up. Transfer back into the saucepan over a medium heat and stir until thickened. Remove the pan from the heat, take your fridge cold butter, finely dice and add it in. If the butter is too warm it won't emulsify properly, so work quickly!

Add the raspberry purée to the custard, then pass through the sieve again to make sure it's really smooth. If not using immediately, cover with cling film making sure it touches the surface and transfer to the fridge. Please note, the colour will fade slightly over time.

name: Raspberry Pistachio Chocolate Fondants
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

An easy and impressive pistachio and raspberry-laden chocolate fondant recipe. A dessert for date night.
instructions: Remove the pistachios from their shells and tip onto a chopping board. Finely chop the nuts and move to a small bowl.

Rub the 25g of butter between six dariole moulds, generously greasing the interior of each thoroughly. Tip the chopped nuts into one of the moulds and, over the next mould, roll the nuts around the interior so they stick to the butter and the excess falls into the next mould. Repeat until all the moulds are lined with pistachios.
Add the remaining 150g of butter to a heatproof bowl. Chop the chocolate and add to the bowl with the butter. Set over a pan of barely simmering water and allow it to melt and come together.

Crack the eggs into a large bowl and add the egg yolks. Add both sugars and best with an electric whisk (or by hand) until you have a thick, ribbony, light mixture. Sift in the flour and fold to combine. Add the chocolate and fold everything together.
Fill the prepared moulds two thirds to three quarters full, you should use all of the mix, and pop into the fridge to chill for at least 45 mins.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Bake the lava cakes for 11-12 mins in the preheated oven.

Once cooked, allow to stand for 2-3 mins before running a knife around the edge and turning out onto plates. Serve with a handful of crushed raspberries and a scoop of raspberry ripple ice cream. Get stuck in.

name: Raspberry, Almond Butter and Chia Seed Porridge
description: Soak your oats overnight with your chia seeds for the smoothest porridge imaginable. Topped with almond butter, berries and maple syrup for a nutty, sweet kick.
instructions: Pour your Quaker Oat So Simple and chia seeds into a bowl and cover with 200ml water. Leave to soak overnight.
Toast your almonds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 5 minutes until they are turning golden and fragrant. Roughly chop.

When you are ready to eat, pop your oat mixture into a small saucepan and add your oat milk. Bring it to a gentle simmer over a medium heat and cook for 5 minutes, stirring until your oats have turned tender and transformed into a thick, creamy porridge.
Pour your porridge into a bowl and top with a drizzle of maple syrup, a dollop of almond butter. a scattering of raspberries and your chopped almonds.

name: Raspberry, Chocolate and Macadamia Flapjacks
description: Chewy, chocolatey and full of fresh raspberries. Liam Charles shows the MOB how to make these incredible flapjacks.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/354°F. Then line a 20 x 20cm baking tin with dairy-free butter and parchment.
Roughly chop your macadamias.
Pour your dairy-free butter, sugar and golden syrup into a large saucepan. Stir over a medium heat until they are all melted into a glossy sauce.
Allow to cool for 10 minutes, then tip in your rolled oats, macadamias and your Dr. Oetker Jumbo Chocolate Chips. Give it all a good stir until it’s combined.

Pour half your oat mixture into your lined tin and smooth the surface so it’s even. Push in half of your fresh raspberries and then pour over the remaining mixture. Top with the remaining raspberries and press down to flatten.
Bake for 35 mins until the top is golden and crisp.
Whilst they bake, finely chop your Dr. Oetker Extra Dark Chocolate.
Add your chocolate to a heatproof bowl and heat in the microwave for 2 minutes, pausing and stirring after every 30 seconds until your chocolate is smooth and melted.
Drizzle your flapjacks with your melted chocolate, then leave to cool. Cut into squares and enjoy!

name: Rasta Pasta
description: Little Simz brought her unique flair to the kitchen, cooking up one of her favourite comfort foods: rasta pasta. The bold flavours of jerk spices and scotch bonnet blend perfectly with a creamy, rich cheese sauce, creating a dish that's fiery, indulgent, and really tasty. With a vibrant mix of colourful vegetables and tender pasta, this rasta pasta is the perfect balance of heat and creaminess. Whether you're looking for something to spice up your weeknight dinner or impress guests, Little Simz's take on rasta pasta is an absolute winner for any occasion.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Finely slice the peppers. Finely slice the spring onions. Pick the leaves off your thyme stalks.
Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a slice of olive oil and some peppers, then fry for 10 mins until softened.

Add your tomato purée and cook out for 5 mins until darkened. Grate your garlic into the pan, then add most of your spring onions, thyme leaves, jerk seasoning, all purpose seasoning and paprika into the pan. Cook for another 2 mins.
Add your pasta to your boiling water and cook until al dente.
Poke your scotch bonnet a few times with a fork to pierce it. Pop this into the pan. Pour in your cream, and bring to a gentle simmer.

When your pasta is ready, add a ladle of the cooking water to your creamy sauce. Lift your pasta out of the water with a slotted spoon, and get this in the sauce. Mix until totally combined, adding more pasta water as you need to make it glossy.
Grate in your cheddar, then season to taste with salt and pepper. Add extra chilli flakes if you’d like it extra spicy.
Spoon into bowls and serve with your remaining sliced spring onions and a little black pepper.

name: Ratatouille
description: A classic for a reason! This ratatouille is cooked all in one pot for minimal washing up and is packed with nutritious, versatile veg.
instructions: Cut the aubergine into 2cm pieces, then do the same for the courgette and the peppers. Finely chop the garlic, then peel and finely slice the red onion.

Add a quarter of the olive oil to a large heavy-bottomed saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Working in batches, add the aubergines, courgettes and peppers. Cook each batch for about 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until golden all over. Transfer to a bowl as you go. The veg won’t be fully cooked yet - this step is all about building flavour.

Add the rest of the oil to the same pan. Don’t worry if the bottom’s caught a bit, that’ll lift when the liquid goes in. Tip in the red onions with a big pinch of salt and cook for 10 mins until soft and jammy. Stir in the garlic and dried thyme and cook for another 2 mins.

Pour in the chopped tomatoes, then add the browned veg back in along with the cherry tomatoes, red wine vinegar and sugar. Season well with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, pop on a lid and let it bubble gently for 30 mins. Take the lid off and cook for another 5 mins to thicken everything up.
Tear in the basil and squeeze over the juice from half a lemon. Give it all a stir and serve.

name: Ratatouille Caper Pasta
description: Simple pasta made with our punchy Ratatouille, capers, and plenty of parmesan. Super satisfying and ready in no time.
instructions: Make the Ratatouille.
Get your leftover ratatouille warmed through in a small pan or the microwave.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and add the pasta. Cook according to package instructions and then drain, reserving some of the water. Add the pasta back into the pot.
Toss the ratatouille and the capers through the pasta, mixing well. Add a slosh of pasta water if it needs it, then adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve in bowls topped with grated parmesan, freshly torn basil, a crack of pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Dig in.

name: Ratatouille Chickpeas & Golden Halloumi
description: Golden nuggets of crispy halloumi on top of chickpeas tossed through our Ratatouille. A proper filling, veggie bowl of goodness.
instructions: Make the Ratatouille.
Warm the ratatouille in a small pan. Add the chickpeas with a splash of their water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut the halloumi into small cubes. Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the halloumi and cook for 5-6 mins, turning until golden all over. Remove from the heat.
Spoon the ratatouille and chickpeas into bowls. Top with golden halloumi, dollops of pesto and a few torn basil leaves, if using. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and a crack of pepper.

name: Ratatouille Panzanella With Spicy Oregano Pesto
description: The star of the show – roasted veggies, herby pesto with loads of olives and crunchy chunky croutons. This is a supreme salad.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Trim and chop the aubergine into 3cm-sized chunks. Place onto a tray and drizzle generously with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, roast for 25-30 mins.
Tear the ciabatta onto a tray, drizzle with 2 tbsp of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, bake until golden brown, 15-18 mins.
Meanwhile, make the dressing. Add the balsamic vinegar and 7 tbsp of olive oil into a large salad bowl. Season with salt and pepper, then stir together.

Discard the tough oregano stems. Add the cheese into a food processor and blitz until broken down. Add the oregano leaves, trim the chilli, peel the garlic and add both into the processor. Pick all the parsley leaves and set aside, add the parsley stems in and blitz until broken down. Add 70ml olive oil and blend until a pesto forms.
Chop the tomatoes into 3cm chunks. Drain the peppers, chop into 3cm chunks. Add the two to the dressing with the olives and mix together.
Once everything is ready, toss the roasted aubergines and three-quarters of the parsley leaves and bread into the salad.
Serve the salad, top with shaved Parmesan and the spicy oregano pesto.

name: Ratatouille with Cheddar Dumplings
description: A match made in heaven: cheddar dumplings on a bed of warming ratatouille. The dumplings are so easy to make from scratch. This is a special one MOB.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Slice up your onions, celery, aubergine, courgettes and red peppers.
Place your pan on a medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and add your veggies. Mix well.
Slice up your garlic cloves and add to the pan followed by your oregano and chilli flakes. Mix well.
Add two tins of tomatoes, refill the tins with water and pour into the pan. Add one stock cube and another tin of water, mixing everything in. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes.

Grab a mixing bowl. Add the self-raising flour, a knob of butter, a pinch of salt and baking soda. Knead everything together to form a dough. Add 150g of grated cheddar, a teaspoon of oregano and continue to mix. Add the milk and mix together using a spoon.
Create a baguette shape with the dough and slice into 8 pieces. Form balls out of these pieces and place around the ratatouille pan. Grate the remaining 50g of cheese over the dumplings.
Place the pan in the oven for 35 minutes to bake.
Garnish with some chopped basil and enjoy.

name: Ratatouille with Parmesan Polenta & Crispy Breadcrumbs
description: Creamy parmesan polenta topped with our rich Ratatouille leftovers and lemony crispy breadcrumbs. A proper cosy bowl.
keywords: Ratatouille with Parmesan Polenta & Crispy Breadcrumbs recipe
Ratatouille with Parmesan Polenta & Crispy Breadcrumbs
instructions: Make the Ratatouille.
Reheat the ratatouille in a small pan or microwave.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-low heat. Add the panko and fry for 3-4 mins until golden, stirring regularly. Remove from the heat. Grate in the lemon zest and season.
Grate the parmesan.
In a saucepan, heat the stock and milk until simmering. Gradually pour in the polenta while whisking. Stir for 4-5 mins until thickened. Stir in the parmesan and butter, then season to taste.
Divide the creamy polenta between bowls. Top with the ratatouille and scatter over the lemony breadcrumbs.

name: Ratatouille with Vegan Basil Pesto Croutons
description: A classic Southern French summertime food given a twist with the addition of delicious crunchy pesto croutons, kept vegan thanks to Sacla’ Vegan Basil Pesto.
keywords: Summery Ratatouille With Sacla’ Vegan Basil Pesto Croutons
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.

Tear the sourdough into roughhewn 2cm cubes and place onto a baking tray large enough that they’re all well spaced out. Drizzle generously with olive oil and a pinch of salt and bake in the oven for 10 mins.
After 10 mins, remove the bread, add half the jar of Sacla’ Vegan Basil Pesto to the tray and toss well. Return to the oven for 5 mins.
Dice the aubergine into roughly 2cm cubes and brown off in a large pan over a medium-high heat with a good pinch of salt. Set aside.
Dice the courgette into roughly 2cm cubes and repeat, browning off in the pan with a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Repeat the same process with the peppers.

Finely dice the red onion and cook over a medium heat with a glug of olive oil until softened but not browned. Finely chop the garlic, add it to the pan, and cook for a minute. Add in your chopped tomatoes before roughly chopping half of the basil and adding that, too. Simmer for 10 mins.
Return the vegetables to the pan and cook for another 5 mins.
Transfer the vegetables to a big serving dish, scatter the croutons over the top and top with the rest of the basil, the remaining Sacla’ Vegan Basil Pesto and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Ravioli Ragù
description: This is the perfect dinner for when you're in need of a bit of comfort. It's filling, nourishing, and pretty easy to make.
instructions: Finely chop the onion and celery and peel and finely chop the carrots. Finely chop the garlic and set aside.

Heat a splash of oil in a large, deep lidded frying pan or casserole dish over a medium-high heat. Add the beef mince and fry for 6-8 mins, stirring to break up the meat, until any liquid has evaporated and the beef is starting to crisp up. Use a slotted spoon to scoop it out and into a bowl.

Pour another splash of oil into the same pan and add the onion, celery and carrot. Add a big pinch of salt, then cook for 10 mins over a medium heat until the vegetables are soft but not coloured. Add the garlic and fry, stirring, for 2 mins, then pour in the red wine and bubble for 2 mins. Return the mince to the pan and add the chopped tomatoes, chicken stock and Marmite. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 40 mins until thickened slightly.

Meanwhile, put the bunch of basil, stalks and all, into a blender. Zest in the lemon, then halve and squeeze in the juice. Finely grate half of the Parmesan into the blender. Season with salt and lots of black pepper, then add 2-3 tbsp cold water (you want it to be a drizzleable consistency) and whizz until completely smooth and a vibrant green colour.

Once the ragù is cooked, add the ravioli to the pan. Mix really well and push the ravioli into the sauce, submerging the pasta as much as possible. Put the lid on the pan and simmer for 4-6 mins until the ravioli is cooked through.
Divide between four bowls, grate over the remaining Parmesan and leave to melt for a minute before spooning over the vibrant basil sauce.

name: Raw Courgette Salad Over a Pot of Ricotta
