description: This is a light, summery courgette salad that's served over plenty of ricotta and toasted sourdough. If you haven't tried raw courgette before, this is your chance.
instructions: Boil a small pot of water, then add the basil and blanch for 30 seconds. Drain and rinse under cold water, then squeeze with your hands to get out as much water as possible.
Transfer the basil to a high-speed blender with the oil and a pinch of salt. Blend for 10 seconds until smooth and vibrant green. Pour into a jar (keeps for up to two weeks in the fridge).
Slice the courgettes into ½cm-thick rounds and add to a bowl with 2 tbsp of the herb oil. Squeeze in the lemon juice, add a pinch of salt and freshly ground black pepper and mix well.

Open the ricotta and scrape a knife around the edges of the pot to release it. Place a small plate over the top and flip it over. Squeeze the container a little and let it fall out onto the plate like a panna cotta.
Spoon the courgettes over the ricotta, then finish with a generous grating of Parmesan and lemon zest, if you like. Serve with a stack of toasted sourdough.

name: Red Acorn Squash & Smoked Mussel Red Curry
description: This is a sweet, smoky and spicy Thai-style red curry using seasonal squash and tinned mussels. The firm-fleshed acorn squash is ideal perfect here, although could also use hubbard or butternut squash. It’s a satisfying, light meal that’s ready in 25 minutes.
instructions: Slice the squash into 1cm thick segments.
Cook the rice following pack instructions (if using).

Set a medium-large sauté pan, wok or saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add a splash of vegetable oil and fry the squash for 5-6 mins, turning them only occasionally, so the flesh darkens and colours a little. Season generously with flaky sea salt and transfer to a plate.

Add the oil from the tinned mussels to the pan, plus the solid top half of the coconut milk (leaving the thinner coconut water below). Cook over a moderate heat for 4 mins until the surface becomes a little shiny.
Stir in the red curry paste and leave to bubble for a further 4 mins, until richly coloured and fragrant.
Now stir in the fish sauce, sugar and the remainder of the tin of coconut milk. Return the squash to the pan and simmer for a final 4 mins.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the lime leaves, Thai basil and bird’s eye chilli (if using).
Add the mussels, sugar snap peas, lime leaves, chilli and ⅔ of the basil to the curry. Warm them through for 20 seconds, then remove from the heat.
Divide between bowls and garnish with the remaining basil. Serve with the rice in a separate bowl nearby.

name: Red Curry Prawn Toast
description: A twist on one of my favourite dim sum. Fragrant red curry gets mixed in with chunky prawns before the whole thing is fried until crisp. Perfection. Seema x
instructions: Blend together the red chillies, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, ground coriander, ground cumin, coriander and the juice and zest of a lime in a blender until smooth. Add in half the prawns and blend until smooth.
Roughly chop the remaining prawns.
Combine the blended prawns with the chopped prawns and season with salt.
Pour the desiccated coconut into a shallow bowl.

Spread a thick layer of your prawn mix on top of each slice of bread and then press those slices, prawn-side down, into the bowl of desiccated coconut. The aim is to make sure the top of each slice is covered in coconut. Next, cut each piece half diagonally to make neat triangles.

Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a medium-sized frying pan. Add your slices of bread prawn-side up and fry for 2 mins until you have a crispy golden base. Carefully flip over and cook for 2 mins on the other side until crisp.
Drain your toast on a plate lined with kitchen paper while you repeat the process with your remaining un-fried slices.
Serve hot with sweet chilli sauce.

name: Red Curry Sausage Rolls
description: The sausage roll you didn't know you needed. Loaded up with a Thai curry paste made with red chillis, lemongrass and garlic for a fragrant twist on a classic.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C/374°F.
Heat a medium sized frying pan over a medium heat. Tip your cumin seeds and your coriander seeds into it and toast for a couple of minutes until your spices are fragrant.
Pour your spices from your pan into your pestle and mortar and crush them into a powder, removing 1 teaspoon for later.

Roughly chop your garlic, shallots, ginger, lemongrass and red chillis. Place these one at a time into your pestle and mortar and pound into a paste, adding the next part once the ingredients in your mortar have formed a paste.

Heat a little oil in the same frying pan that you toasted the spices in. Add your curry paste and cook out for 5 minutes, by which time your kitchen should be filled with lovely, fragrant smells. Remove from the pan and allow to cool.

Squeeze your sausages out of their casings into a bowl, discarding the cases. Zest your limes into the bowl and add your fish sauce. Add your cooled down curry paste along with a good pinch of salt and pepper, then bring the mixture together with your hands.

Crack your egg into a bowl and give it a good beat. Unroll your puff pastry. Arrange your mixture in sausage shape down the length of the pastry, then brush one edge with egg wash. Fold the other edge over the filling and roll it over so you have a sealed edge. Seal by pressing down with a fork.
Brush the exterior of your roll with egg wash and sprinkle with your remaining crushed coriander and cumin seeds. Pop in the fridge to chill for half an hour, or until your pastry feels firm.
Chop your roll into 10 segments and arrange spaced apart across 2 baking sheets.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until they are a deep golden brown and your pastry looks tender and flaky. Serve hot or room temperature.

name: Red Curry Smoked Mackerel Fried Rice
description: Smoked mackerel is incredibly underrated and really shines bright in this quick and simple fried rice recipe.
keywords: Red Curry Smoked Mackerel Fried Rice
Red Curry Smoked Mackerel Fried Rice recipe
instructions: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil and lower in the eggs. Cook for 6½ mins before removing and plunging into ice water. Peel the soft-boiled eggs and set aside.

Flake the mackerel fillets into bite-sized chunks, finely slice the garlic and spring onions and halve the tomatoes. Slice the cucumber in half, lengthways, and use a small spoon to remove the seeds. Cut into thin slices.

Set a wok over a high heat and add a shot of sesame oil. Add the cooked rice and break up with the back of a ladle or spoon. Cook for 2-3 mins until it starts to crisp-up and caramelise. Tip out onto a plate and return the wok to the heat.

Add another shot of oil and tip in the garlic and curry paste. Cook for 1-2 mins before adding the tomatoes. Stir fry for 2-3 mins until they start to blister and the skins loosen. Now return the rice to the pan and toss through the curry paste, mackerel, and tomatoes.
Add the spring onions, soy sauce and basil leaves. Add the juice of 1 lime and divide between warm bowls. Serve with sliced cucumbers, extra lime, and a soft-boiled egg.

name: Red Hot Chicken Burger
description: This guy is inspired by the imitable Nashville Hot Chicken. Yes you should try and get hold of Red Hot Cheetos and yes, it is worth it. B x
instructions: Chuck your chicken thighs into a bowl and cover with the liquid from the pickle jar. Add a big pinch of salt and set aside for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, whisk together the flour, cornflour, 3 tbsp garlic powder, half of the paprika and cayenne and all of the white pepper. Season generously with salt and pepper and set aside.

Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat and cook until it just starts to brown. Add the remaining garlic powder, paprika and cayenne. Add a big pinch of salt and 50ml of Frank’s hot sauce. Give it a taste, it should be very spicy. Whisk to combine and keep warm on the stove.
Whisk together the buttermilk and remaining hot sauce.
Heat the vegetable oil to 170c and drain the chicken from the brine.
Pass the chicken through the buttermilk mixture and into the seasoned flour making sure it is well coated all over. Pass through both again to give the chicken a craggly, ruffled texture.
Fry the chicken for 10-12 mins until crispy and cooked all the way through. While the chicken is frying smash up the Cheetos in a pestle and mortar.
Dice the pickles and fold through the mayo. Finely shred the iceberg lettuce.
As soon as the chicken comes out, dunk it into the red hot butter and pop onto a plate.
Toast your buns and you’re ready to build. Bottom bun, pickle mayo, shredded lettuce, hot chicken, handful of Cheetos and topped off with more pickle mayo and the top bun.
Give it a squish, and get stuck in.

name: Red Pesto Gnocchi
description: A simple gnocchi recipe that you can make in just 15 minutes. Now, that's what we call a speedy dinner.
instructions: Start by making the pesto: add the sun-dried tomatoes and red chilli to a blender with the smoked almonds. Peel the garlic clove and roughly slice the Parmesan, then add in. Add the harissa paste and lemon juice and season generously with salt and pepper. Add ⅓ of olive oil and begin to blend, then continue to add olive oil until you get to a thick pesto consistency.
Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the gnocchi and cook for 2 mins. Drain, reserving a cup of the water.

Add a splash of olive oil into a large frying pan over a high heat. Add the gnocchi and toss until crispy, around 2-3 mins. Spoon in the pesto and toss well. Add some of the cooking and keep tossing so the sauce coats the gnocchi. Taste and season.
Tip into bowls, top with grated Parmesan, basil and a drizzle of olive oil. Finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Red Pesto Tofu Grain Bowl
description: Punchy pesto-coated tofu, juicy roast peppers and grains, all wrapped up in parcels for a low effort veggie dinner with barely any washing up. Get this in your weekly rotation.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely slice the red pepper and roughly chop the basil, saving a few leaves for serving.
Tear off one large sheet of parchment paper per portion and lay them in front of you, facing portrait.

Tip the grains straight from the pouch (no need to microwave, they'll cook in the parcel) between the parchment sheets, then scatter over the peppers, olives and chunks of tofu, leaving a 10cm gap between the food and the edge closest to you. Season with salt and black pepper and drizzle with olive oil. Spoon over the red pesto, Fold the top half of the baking paper over the food then fold the outside edges over each other to seal (like a cornish pasty), creating a steam-tight parcel. Bake for 20 mins.
Remove from the oven, carefully open your parcel, give it all a quick mix and top with the reserved basil leaves. Dig in!

name: Red Wine Braised Turkey Legs
description: Red wine is the secret to turning these turkey legs into a dish you'll never forget. We're all about dark meat here.
instructions: Divide each leg into thigh and drum by cutting through the joint and set aside. Remove two-thirds of each wing by cutting through the joint between the flat and the drumette.
Mix 1 tbsp of fine salt with ½ tbsp of sugar and generously season all parts of the turkey with this mixture. Pop onto lined trays and into the fridge for a minimum of 4 hours, ideally overnight.

Time to cook. Preheat the oven 160°C. Pat your turkey legs dry, coat with a little oil and colour in a large frying pan, skin side down, over a medium heat. Once the thighs and drums are brown, transfer to a deep baking dish. Cut the onions into wedges and colour in the same pan as the turkey legs, transfer to the baking dish. Halve the garlic bulbs and colour in the same pan. Chuck the herbs into the pan, deglaze with the red wine, bring to a boil and add 1.5L of the stock. Pour over the browned turkey legs, cover with foil and pop into the oven for 1 hour.
After the legs have cooked for 1 hour, remove the foil and increase the oven temperature to 195°C. Cook for 50-60 mins further.
To make the gravy, pour off the herby, turkey leg braising liquid into a saucepan with the remaining stock. Bring to a boil, reduce slightly and season to taste.
Serve the braised legs on a platter with extra herbs and topped with flaky salt and a few spoons of gravy. Finish with a little gravy and serve. Serve the remaining gravy on the side.

name: Red Wine Poached Pear Crumble
description: A combination of two of the best desserts around. A pear poached in a delicious red wine from B. INK and a comforting crumble. Winter warmer certified.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C.
Peel, halve and remove the stones from the pears. Add them to a pan with ⅔ of the sugar and the wine, bay leaves, orange zest and juice.
Bring to a simmer and poach cut side down for 5-6 minutes, or until just tender. Remove from the pan and reduce the wine by a third or to a light syrup.

To a mixing bowl, add the remaining sugar, breadcrumbs, almonds, oats, butter, salt and egg yolk and mix thoroughly. Don’t worry about rubbing anything in with your fingertips, this crumble is dead simple. No faff.
Add the pears to a baking dish cut side up, cover with the (strained) poaching syrup and the crumble mixture.
Bake for 45 mins and serve with cold cream.

name: Refried Bean Tostadas
description: These tostadas de frijoles refritos are one of the many antojitos (little cravings) we eat in Mexico. A perfect way to use up stale corn tortillas and leftover fried beans.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan.
Line two baking trays with tin foil and place the corn tortillas on top, keeping them separated so they don’t stick to each other.

Slide the trays into the oven to bake for 20 mins, flipping the tortillas halfway through, until evenly toasted on both sides and hard, crunchy and golden brown (this is when the tortillas become tostadas!).
Remove them from the oven and transfer to a cooling rack for 5 mins.

In the meantime, heat the refried beans in a saucepan set over a low-medium heat until warmed through. Finely shred the iceberg lettuce, finely dice the salad tomatoes and thinly slice the avocados. Crumble the queso fresco.

To make the tostadas, spread a tbsp of refried beans over each one, garnish with the shredded lettuce, diced tomato, a few slices of avocado, some crumbled queso fresco, sour cream and a salsa of your choice.

name: Refried Black Beans
description: The best side dish to serve at any Mexican meal. At home there is always some fried beans in the fridge. I grew up eating fried pinto beans, as I am from the north of Mexico, but black beans are just as good. Traditionally they are fried with pork lard, but frying them with a good vegetable oil is fine. Beans are always present on a Mexican table, especially when having a feast.
instructions: Finely chop the onion. Heat the oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the onion and fry for 2 mins, stirring to avoid burning.
Add the beans and their bean juice, then season with the salt (only if using unsalted canned beans, otherwise skip the salt).
As soon as the mixture starts boiling, lower the heat and mash with a potato masher until the beans are creamy and smooth.
Serve as a side dish as is.

name: Remi Wolf's Spiced Sausage Pasta
description: If pasta and sausage are your thing, have a go at this pasta dish made by the one and only Remi Wolf. Tuck in.
instructions: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Peel and finely dice the onion.

Whilst the water comes to a boil, grab a large frying pan and place over medium-high heat. Add a shot of olive oil, then squeeze the sausages out of their casing into the pan, use a spatula to break it up in the pan, then sizzle until golden and crisp, around 10 mins. Tip the crispy sausage from the pan onto a plate.

Add another shot of olive oil to the pan, then add the onion along with a big pinch of salt. Cook for 6-8 mins, until softened. Drop the spaghetti into the boiling water and cook for 1 min less than the package instructions.

Peel the garlic and finely grate directly into the pan. Sizzle for a minute further, then add the spices and tomato paste and stir well, cooking for a couple of mins. Return the sausage meat to the pan then turn the heat down to low, then stir in the double cream. Add the soy, harissa and honey.

Use tongs to transfer the pasta from the water to the frying pan, then finely grate most of the Parmesan into the pan, saving a little for the top. Toss well with the sauce, adding splashes of water to keep the sauce glossy as you toss the paste. Season generously with salt and pepper, then add the zest and juice of the lemon.
Swirl into bowls, top with the remaining Parmesan and serve.

name: Rhubarb & Blood Orange Overnight Oats
description: Tangy rhubarb, sweet blood orange and crunchy fennel-spiced walnut granola. Fresh, fruity and prepped ahead for a lush start to the day.
keywords: Rhubarb and Blood Orange Overnight Oats recipe
Rhubarb and Blood Orange Overnight Oats
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Chuck the oats into a bowl with the milk, Greek yoghurt, maple syrup and a pinch of salt. Stir to combine, then cover and chill in the fridge overnight.
Peel one of the blood oranges, then slice the peel into thin strips. Segment both oranges, collecting any juice that drips out.

Cut the rhubarb into 3cm pieces then add to a pan and cover with 200ml water and juice of the blood oranges and sugar. Bring to a very gentle simmer and cook for 6 mins, then remove from the heat. 
Strain the the rhubarb into a bowl and then pop the juice back on the stove over a medium heat, simmering and reducing until its thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Cool and pour back over the rhubarb, then add in the orange segments.

Mix the oats in a bowl with the walnuts, maple syrup, fennel seeds and a pinch of salt. Pop on a baking dray and drizle over the coconut oil and slide into the oven. 
After for 10 mins, add the orange peel and return the tray into the oven for another 5 mins. Remove and cool.

Fill glasses or Tupperware containers with the oats then top with the rhubarb compote before scattering with granola.
If making ahead it's best to keep the granola separate and add it in the morning so it keeps its crunch. These will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Rhubarb & Custard Pie
description: A big and beautiful pie filled with tart rhubarb. This is the perfect sunshine dessert. Serving it with cold custard is essential.
instructions: To make the pastry, cut the butter into 2cm cubes, and place in the fridge to keep cold. Add flour, ½ tsp salt and sugar into a large mixing bowl. Mix together until evenly combined.

Using your hands, toss the cubes of cold butter into the flour mixture. Quickly break and smash the pieces of butter in the flour into smaller chunks (it’s ok if they are not all the same size). Add 100ml of ice cold water into the mixture. Stir with a fork until a shaggy dough forms. Add a tsp more of water at a time if it's too dry.

Gather the dough into a mound. Using your hand, squeeze it together to form large clumps, place them onto a clean work surface. If you have some dry floury areas, leave it in the bowl and stir a few teaspoons of ice cold water until you can squeeze the dough together. The texture should not be sticky, it should still be a little dry.

Split the dough into 3 chunks, then flatten on top of each other, this is key to getting flakey pastry. Flatten and shape into a thick disc. Wrap in cling film and refrigerate the dough for at least 1 hour.

To make the filling, cut the rhubarb into 4-5 cm lengths and toss with the sugar and ½ tsp salt. Set aside for an hour, then add the zest and juice of the lemon, vanilla, cinnamon, and cornflour. Toss to coat.

Cut the rested dough into two pieces, one ¾ of the dough, one ¼. This is for your base and the lid. Roll out the bigger piece of dough into a rough circle, big enough to line a 18 - 20cm cake tin or pie dish.

Roll the other piece of pastry into a circle large enough to drape over the pie and seal in the filling. Crimp the edges together and cut a couple of vents in the top, brush with egg wash and sprinkle with the demerara sugar, and cover the top lightly with foil.
Bake at 200°C for 1.5-2 hrs until golden brown and bubbling. Let cool down for at least 40 mins before serving. Serve with cold custard.

name: Rhubarb Crumble & Ginger Custard
description: I love it when rhubarb arrives. It’s the first new fruit of the year and a real sign that spring is on its way. This simple rhubarb crumble recipe lets the rhubarb shine, served with a warming gingery custard.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C. Cut the rhubarb into roughly 4cm pieces
Place into a large pan in one layer and sprinkle over 1/4 of the sugar.
Pour over your water, bring to a simmer and cook for about 5 or 6 mins, then turn off the heat and leave to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, in a food processor combine the flour and remaining sugar. Cube up the butter, add and pulse until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Remove the rhubarb from the pan using a slotted spoon and transfer it to a baking dish. Pour the crumble mixture on top, then sprinkle over the oats.
Bake in the oven for about 25 to 30 mins until golden brown. Leave to rest for 5 mins before serving.

Whilst the crumble bakes, make the custard. Add the milk, sugar, cornflour, ginger and vanilla extract to a saucepan and bring up to a gentle simmer, stirring to dissolve the sugar, then turn the heat to minimum.
While the milk is warming, whisk the egg yolks in a bowl. Now add the egg yolks bit by bit to the milk, whisking each time, until they’re all added.
Keep warming gently and stirring until the custard is glossy and coats the back of a spoon.
Serve up a big spoon of the crumble and drizzle over the custard.

name: Rhubarb Negroni
description: A sweet negroni inspired by rhubarb and custard. This is a delicious cocktail recipe.
instructions: Cut your vanilla bean lengthways and scrape out the contents.
Find a jar or container large enough to store everything, then cut your rhubarb to just below the length of the jar and fill it up with the rhubarb and the vanilla pod.
Now, pour in your gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth. Close the container and leave it to infuse in the fridge for a couple of days depending on how strong you want the flavour of the rhubarb to be.
We wanted ours to taste very vanilla-y so I added a teaspoon of vanilla paste to the custard and mix.

Remove your rhubarb from the container and, this is important, pour your cocktail into your custard and NOT the other way around. It won’t be the end of the world if you do, but the clarification process works better when you’re pouring booze into dairy.
Leave this mixture for 3-4 hours to clarify – this should remove any overpowering notes and make the flavour deeper and richer as well as removing suspended solid particles from a liquid.

This next step is also important. Filter your cocktail using a coffee filter and a funnel, let it run until the drops coming out the bottom are noticeably clear and without particles. Then change to a new container and pour the first run off back in carefully into the filter. This should ensure your drink comes out fully clear.
Feel free to do a second run through if you want to double clarify your cocktail.
Jar this finished cocktail up and store it in the fridge for whenever you want it.
For garnish, we sprinkled sugar over the top of a piece of the infused rhubarb and flamed it until a glaze formed. Serve over ice and enjoy.

name: Rhubarb Oat Bran Cake
description: Cake that’s healthy and delicious? You heard right. This oat bran, kefir and olive oil cake packs in loads of fibre and probiotics to help improve your gut health. We’ve topped it with rhubarb but you could use any seasonal fruit.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Chop your rhubarb into inch-sized pieces and lay it in a baking tray. Sprinkle over the brown sugar and a splash of water then roast in the oven for 10 mins until soft.
Combine the brown sugar and olive oil in a large oven-proof tray. Stir in the egg and then the kefir. Add the oat bran, baking powder and a generous pinch of salt and mix until combined.
Top the cake mixture with the cooked rhubarb.
Bake for 20 mins then set aside to cool slightly before cutting into slices. Serve as is or with Greek yoghurt and a drizzle of honey.

name: Ribollita
description: A hearty Tuscan stew with veggies, beans and stale bread. Make a big batch and keep it in your freezer for those cold evenings when you’re craving something comforting.
instructions: Chop your onion, celery, carrot and garlic into a fine dice (this will form your sofrito) and add to a pan with a glug of olive oil and the sprig of rosemary. Season with salt and pepper and sauté the sofrito for 10 mins.

Add the Parmesan rind, pearl barley, tinned tomatoes and borlotti and cannellini beans along with their liquid. Cover with a lid and cook for 30-40 mins until the pearl barley is cooked, adding a splash of extra water if it’s drying out.
Chop the cavolo nero and spring greens and add to the pan then continue to cook for another 10 mins.
Meanwhile, finely chop the red chilli and grate the Parmesan.
To serve, place a piece of stale sourdough in the bottom of each bowl and ladle over the ribollita. Top with the fresh chilli, thyme leaves, grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Rice Salad with Jammy Eggs & Charred Asparagus
description: You've heard of a pasta salad, but how about a rice salad? The bright green dressing in this adds a nice bit of zip. Topped with jammy eggs? It's out of bounds.
keywords: Rice Salad with Jammy Eggs & Charred Asparagus
instructions: Cook your rice according to package instructions. Tip it out onto a large tray or wide surface and let it cool down completely.
Boil the eggs for exactly 6 mins, then put them straight into a bowl of icy water. Peel the eggs and pop them on a plate.
Cut the fennel into eight wedges. Trim the asparagus spears and cut them in half. Add the fennel and asparagus into a bowl with a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then toss to coat.

Halve and scoop out the avocado into a blender. Save half of the coriander leaves from the bunch, then add the stalks and remaining leaves to a blender along with the Greek yoghurt, juice of a lime, 50ml of olive oil and 35ml of water. Blend until smooth, season with salt and pepper, set aside.
Heat a griddle pan over high heat until smoking hot. Add the fennel and asparagus and cook until nicely charred, 6-8 mins.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the chilli and roughly chop the almonds.

Time to plate up. Halve the eggs. Add the rice and half the charred vegetables into a large bowl with some dressing, toss together until coated. Share the dressed salad topped with the remaining veggies, jammy eggs, smoked almonds, chilli, and your remaining coriander leaves. Finish with a drizzle of the remaining dressing.

name: Rich Bean Chilli with Spicy Jalapeño Sauce
description: A lovely rich and warming chilli topped with a zingy green sauce. You can make this in a flash.
instructions: Make the Veggie Chilli Sin Carne.

Put most of the coriander into a blender with the jalapeños, garlic, lime juice and a nice slosh of the jalapeño pickle juice. Season with salt and whizz until smooth – loosen with water if it’s a bit thick!
Heat the leftover Veggie Chilli Sin Carne through until piping hot and top with the spicy coriander sauce and the remaining coriander leaves. Eat as is, or scoop up with tortilla chips.

name: Ricotta Stuffed Crispy Fried Olives
description: These are the perfect thing to eat on a hot day with a cold glass of beer. Jordon x
keywords: Ricotta stuffed crispy fried olives recipes
instructions: Add the ricotta, chilli flakes, 1 tbsp of the oregano, a large pinch of salt, and a splash of olive oil into a bowl. Mix well until combined.
Spoon the mix into either a squeezy bottle with a nozzle or a piping bag. Pipe the mix into each olive, filling the gap where the stone has been removed. Set aside.
Add a tbsp of the remaining oregano and a pinch of salt to both the flour and the breadcrumbs and mix well.

Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk. Now take each olive and toss in the flour, then dip into the egg mix and finally toss in the breadcrumbs until well coated. Repeat the process, dipping into the eggs and then again into the breadcrumbs.

Set the olives aside onto a plate. Place a large pan over a medium high heat and add the vegetable oil. Heat until the oil reaches about 180°C (you can test by dipping the edge of an olive into the oil, if it bubbles and sizzles then it’s ready).
Add the olive to the oil and fry for about 4 mins until golden and crispy, then remove onto a plate lined with kitchen paper, sprinkle with salt and leave to cool for a minute before eating.

name: Ricotta Stuffed Shells with Bolognese
description: These delicious ricotta stuffed shells are baked in a rich Bolognese ragù. Give this one a go for a truly indulgent dinner.
keywords: Ricotta Stuffed Shells with Bolognese recipe
instructions: Place a large pan over a medium heat and add the pancetta and butter. Fry for about 5 mins until golden.
Meanwhile, dice the onion, carrot, and celery. Add to the pan with the pancetta and cook for about 5 mins until softened.
Remove the contents of the pan into a bowl and return to a hight heat. Add the beef and a big pinch of salt and cook until browned all over, breaking it up with a spoon as you go.
Pour in the red wine and let it evaporate. Lower the heat, return the onion and pancetta mix to the pan and stir well.
Add the milk and stock followed by the tomatoes and bring up to a very gentle simmer. Cover and leave to cook for an hour and 30 mins, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, finely chop the basil and add to a bowl with the ricotta and a pinch of salt. Mix well and set aside.
Cook the pasta in plenty of salted water until al dente, then drain and allow to cool. Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Once the ragù is ready, season to taste and pour it into a large baking dish.
Take the cooled pasta and use a teaspoon to fill each shell withricotta, then nestle it down into the ragù.
Grate the Parmesan over the top and place into the oven for 20 mins until golden.
Sprinkle with basil leaves and allow to rest for 5 mins before serving.

name: Rigatoni with Broccoli
description: A classic dish from Puglia combining rigatoni pasta with a very simple sauce made using the entire head of broccoli. The broccoli is boiled in the pasta cooking water, then sizzled until soft with garlic, anchovies (optional) and chilli while the pasta cooks.
instructions: Put a large pan of well-salted water onto the boil (it should taste pleasantly salty). Cut the florets off the broccoli and roughly chop into very small pieces.

Peel and discard the tough skin from the broccoli stalk and then cut the remaining stalk into strips about 1cm thick. Cut the strips in half lengthways and widthways so you have roughly thumb-sized rectangles.
Once the water is boiling, tip in the broccoli florets and stalk pieces and let them cook for about 5 mins until quite tender – you should be able to skewer them on a fork easily.

Meanwhile, put a large frying pan with nice high sides over a low-medium heat and add the olive oil. Roughly chop the olives. Now you’ve got two choices: either slightly crush the garlic but leave it whole to be removed later (milder), or chop the garlic and add the whole lot (stronger). Either way, add the garlic to the oil along with the olives, chilli and anchovies, if using.

Let the garlic cook gently for a couple of minutes, but don't let it go brown. The anchovies will dissolve into the oil and by now your broccoli should be ready, so use a slotted spoon to scoop it out of the water and put it straight into the pan with the garlic, making sure you get a good splash of the water in there as well.

Add the pasta to the broccoli water and cook until al dente. Meanwhile, mash the broccoli with the back of a wooden spoon to create a creamy sauce with the oil and water. Zest the lemon and add to the broccoli, then squeeze the juice in and turn the heat off until the pasta is cooked.
Once al dente, add the pasta to the pan with the broccoli plus a splash of pasta water. Mix well over a medium heat until the pasta is saucy and well coated. Taste and add more salt if needed.
Plate up and finish with a drizzle of olive oil, pepper and an extra pinch of chilli, if you like.

name: Risotto Rice Pudding
description: Using risotto rice to make rice pudding, it work's a charm. So creamy. Spiced with vanilla & cinnamon. With jam stirred through. Absolutely delicious.
instructions: Put the rice, milk, sugar, vanilla and ground cinnamon into a large saucepan along with a pinch of salt.
Cook over a medium heat, stirring regularly for 20 minutes, until the rice has absorbed a lot of the milk and is cooked, with a slight bite.
Add any optional extras if using after 10 minutes (see notes).
Serve warm or cold.
If eating cold you might want to stir through a little more milk as the pudding will set in the fridge. Finish how you like.

name: Roast Asparagus & Chorizo Salad
description: A flavourful, seasonal salad recipe with a sweet and tangy dressing you'll want to drizzle on just about everything.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut the potatoes into roughly 3cm chunks. Add them to a saucepan and cover with water, then generously salt the water and bring to the boil.
Meanwhile, trim and discard the woody ends off the asparagus and chop the rest into 3cm lengths.
Peel the chorizo, quarter it lengthways and cut into 2cm cubes. Transfer to a large roasting tin with the asparagus and tomatoes.

Once the potatoes are boiling, peel the garlic and add to the same saucepan. Cook for 3 mins, then drain everything well and add to the roasting tin. Add a splash of olive oil and a very big pinch of salt, then mix well.
Roast in the oven for 15 mins, at which point the asparagus and potatoes should be tender and the chorizo soft and sizzling. Give it another 5 mins if not.
While everything roasts, mix together the balsamic, honey, a splash of olive oil, and the oregano.
Remove the roasting tray, pour over the dressing, mix well and let sit for a couple of minutes.
Add the green leaves and mix well, making sure they get well coated in the mix of dressing, chorizo and tomato juices.
Plate up, drizzle over some juices from the bottom of the tray and grate over a generous coating of Parmesan.

name: Roast Broccoli with Tahini Dressing and Sesame Chilli Crisp
description: Yinka Ogunbiyi (aka Food Fire and Soul) makes the ultimate veggie centrepiece – a beautiful roasted broccoli with a tahini dressing and homemade chilli oil.
keywords: Roast broccoli with tahini dressing and sesame chilli crisp
instructions: Preheat your oven to 225°C.
Finely slice your garlic and spring onions. Heat your oil in a pot on medium heat then add your sliced vegetables. Cook for 10 mins until golden brown and caramelised.

Prepare your chilli garlic crisp by mixing the soy sauce, chilli flakes, paprika, salt and MSG in a separate bowl. Add this mix to the garlic onion oil and let it cook for another 5 mins, giving it a good stir. Turn off the heat and leave to cool.
Chop your broccoli in half and drizzle liberally with salt and pepper, nestling it into the nooks and crannies of the florets. Roast in the oven for 20 mins until browned, crispy and just tender.

Prepare your tahini dressing by blending the olive oil, apple cider vinegar, lemon juice, tahini, honey with a big pinch of salt and pepper to get a smooth and creamy consistency. Add more lemon, honey, salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon out your dressing onto your best plate and place the broccoli on top. Sprinkle the chilli crisp on top and dig in.

name: Roast Carrot & Rice Salad With A Charred Pepper Dressing
description: Who knew roasted carrots and rice went so well together? The perfect springtime salad, this one's bursting with fresh ingredients and the easiest dressing.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Cut the bottom off the garlic, drizzle with oil and wrap in tin foil. Cut your carrots in half lengthways. Add the carrots to a baking tray along with the garlic and cook for 40 mins, until the carrots are tender and the garlic is squidgy.

Drain and roughly chop the jarred roasted peppers and ribbon the courgette with a peeler. Add the peppers to a food processor along with the garlic and the juice of 1 lemon. Blend and season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl whisk together 4 tbsp olive oil and the juice of 1 lemon before adding the watercress and courgette, tossing to combine. Heat the rice according to package instructions.
Chop most of the mint and parsley, saving some whole for garnish. Roughly chop the almonds. Mix the rice and chopped herbs with the red pepper sauce, then taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
To serve, load a plate up with the dressed rice, then top with salad and the roasted carrots. Garnish with almonds and remaining herbs, then tuck in.

name: Roast Carrot, Chicken & Butter Bean Salad
description: Like a roast dinner in salad form, this high-protein salad will make the perfect recipe when you've got the in-laws over for dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the chicken breasts onto a baking tray, then drizzle over a glug of olive oil, the chilli flakes, salt and pepper. Slice half of the lemons and lay the slices on top of the chicken. Transfer to the oven and cook for 15-20 mins until cooked through. Set aside to rest for 10 mins, then slice.

Meanwhile, peel and slice the carrots into irregular, 3cm pieces. Pick the thyme leaves. Transfer the carrots to a roasting tin, drizzle with oil and sprinkle the thyme on top before seasoning with salt and pepper. Pop in the oven for 25 mins or until soft and slightly charred.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the courgettes and drain and rinse the butter beans. Transfer both to a large bowl with the juice of a quarter of the lemons and half the pesto.
Put the yoghurt into a bowl. Grate in the garlic, then add the remaining juice of ½ the lemon. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide the garlic yoghurt between plates, then top with the butter bean salad, roasted carrots, shredded chicken, pesto, and torn basil leaves. Serve with bread.

name: Roast Celeriac Recipe With Salsa Verde
description: These celeriac steaks are butter-basted and finished in the oven so they’re crisp and caramelised on the outside and meltingly soft within. Finished with a bright, vibrant and punchy salsa verde. You won’t believe how delicious this roasted celeriac recipe is.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

Top and tail the celeriac, then use a large knife to trim off all of the skin, without taking off too much flesh. Cut two 2cm-thick steaks from the middle of the celeriac. Save the rest for soup or mash (can tag both). Use the flat side of the knife to bash the garlic cloves on the chopping board to flatten them.
Pour a drizzle of olive oil over the celeriac steaks and season really well with salt and pepper.
Heat an ovenproof frying pan, big enough to fit both steaks, set over a medium-high heat.

Lay the celeriac steaks into the pan and cook for 3 mins on one side, until caramelised. Flip and cook for 2 mins, then turn the heat down to medium, add the butter and smashed garlic cloves and baste the celeriac steak for another minute, then flip and baste the other side for a further minute. Put the pan into the oven and roast for 15 mins, until the celeriac steaks are charred and soft.

Finely chop the parsley and scrape into a bowl. Roughly chop the capers and add to the bowl along with the mustard, red wine vinegar and a splash of olive oil. Season with salt and cracked black pepper.
Remove the celeriac steaks from the oven and divide between plates, spooning on some of the butter. Serve with a good drizzle of salsa verde.

name: Roast Chicken & Apple Slaw Bao Buns
description: Got leftovers from your Roast Chicken Legs with Roasted Grapes, Prosciutto Parsnips & Apple Slaw batch? Try the slaw and chicken leftovers stuffed into soft steamed bao. It's a beauty.
keywords: chicken and apple slaw bao buns
chicken and apple slaw bao buns recipe
instructions: Finely chop the parsley.
Pull the meat from the chicken legs (You'll need 1 leftover chicken leg per serving) and warm through in the microwave for 1-2 mins until piping hot.
Steam the bao buns according to the packet instructions.
Fill each bun with the warmed chicken, top each with a spoonful of your leftover apple slaw and finish with the chopped parsley. Serve straight away.

name: Roast Chicken & Fresh Tomato Salad
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Crispy chicken thighs and juicy in-season tomatoes are the key ingredients in this fresh and flavourful salad.
keywords: Roast Chicken & Fresh Tomato Salad recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Pat the chicken dry and generously salt the chicken on both sides.
Place the chicken skin-side down into an oiled oven-proof frying pan. Put onto medium-high heat and cook the chicken until the skin goes golden brown.
Meanwhile, peel and wedge the onion. Once the chicken is golden, add the onion into the pan, transfer to the oven and roast for 15-20 mins, until fully cooked.
Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes into 2cm chunks and transfer to a bowl with the balsamic and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Share the cottage cheese and chicken between the plates. Toss the roasted onions and basil leaves into the salad and serve alongside. Enjoy with ciabatta.

name: Roast Chicken & Giant Couscous With Creamy Yoghurt Sauce
description: Inspired by Palestinian Maftoul, this dish features giant couscous cooked in flavourful stock with sweet peppers, roasted chicken and a tangy yoghurt sauce.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Add the chicken thighs into a roasting tin or tray with the ras el hanout and 2 tbsp of olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper, then mix together until evenly coated. Roast, skin-side up for 30-35 mins, until cooked through.

Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice the onions. Remove the stem and chop the peppers into 1cm chunks. In a large saucepan on medium heat, add 3 tbsp of olive oil. Once hot, add the onions and peppers, cook until softened and starting to colour, 10-15 mins. Pour the chicken stock in and bring to the boil.

Tip the giant couscous or orzo into a sieve and give it a rinse, then add to the saucepan. Cook, stirring frequently, according to package instructions (top it up with more chicken stock or water if it's evaporating too quickly).

Add the Greek yoghurt into a small bowl with the tahini and the juice of a lemon. Stir until it comes together and season with salt, pepper and sugar (if needed). If it’s too thick, add 1 tbsp of water at a time until smooth. The sauce should be a little looser than Greek yoghurt. Set aside.
Reserve a few parsley leaves and finely chop the rest (stalks and all).
Once the couscous is cooked, take it off the heat, taste and season with salt. Stir through the chopped parsley, then add a little lemon zest to taste.

Spoon the couscous onto plates and top with the roasted chicken. Drizzle with the yoghurt sauce and any sauce from roasting the chicken. Finish with a wedge of the zested lemon and a scattering of the reserved parsley leaves.

name: Roast Chicken & Grape Traybake
description: Sweet and savoury, this chicken traybake is the perfect answer for any dinner. Buttery roasted garlic sauce, braised radishes, roasted grapes and herby rice, this dish is rich, but still fresh.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Pat the chicken dry and season generously with salt. Place skin-side down in a large frying pan and set over a medium-high heat. Cook for 6-8 mins until the skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip and remove from the heat.

Meanwhile, halve the radishes, trim and chop the leeks into 2cm rounds, then add both to a baking tray. Separate the garlic cloves, keeping each clove in its skin, and add to the tray, along with the grapes.
Place the chicken skin-side up on top of the veggies, sprinkle the oregano all over, then drizzle with olive oil. Roast for 20-25 mins until the chicken is fully cooked.

Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves and finely slice the stems. Reheat the rice following pack instructions. Tip the rice into a bowl and toss through the zest of half the lemon and all the parsley. Season with salt and pepper.

Remove the chicken from the tray, squeeze the roasted garlic out and discard the skins. Mash the garlic into a paste, then toss the cold butter through the veggies until the sauce thickens. Add a splash of water if it’s too thick, then taste and season with salt, if needed.
Share the rice between plates, then top with the sauce and chicken. Serve with any remaining lemon wedges.

name: Roast Chicken & Herby Pepper Burritos
description: Insane burritos made with our leftover Roast Chicken & Peppers batch. A great weeknight staple.
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken & Peppers.
Shred the leftover roast chicken. If cold, warm it with the peppers in a saucepan set over a low heat with a splash of water until piping hot.
Finely chop the parsley. Reheat the rice, then stir through the chopped parsley.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan for 30 seconds on each side until flexible.

Grate the cheddar and sprinkle down the centre of each tortilla. Spoon over the soured cream and herby rice, then add the chicken and pepper mixture. Roll up each tortilla tightly into a burrito – tuck in the sides, then roll from the bottom up.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan set over a medium heat. Once hot, place the burritos seam-side down and cook for 5-8 mins, flipping halfway, until toasted and golden.
Serve hot with some chilli sauce on the side.

name: Roast Chicken & Pepper Caesar Salad
description: A cheeky Caesar salad made with leftover Roast Chicken & Peppers batch. Dinner doesn't get quicker or easier than this.
keywords: Roast Chicken & Pepper Caesar Salad recipe
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken & Peppers.
Trim and separate the lettuce. Add it into a big bowl with the veggies from the roast. Add the avocado, dressing and some of the chicken juices.
Slice or shred the chicken, add to the salad with the croutons and Parm shavings. Toss, taste and season with salt and pepper.
Share between bowls.

name: Roast Chicken & Pepper Traybake
description: This is the easiest, juiciest chicken recipe. All done in one tray, it’s possibly the laziest but yummiest batch meal to make.
keywords: Batch Recipe: Roast Chicken & Peppers recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Flip the chicken, so its breast side down. Using a pair of strong kitchen scissors, snip the backbone/spine out. Turn the chicken over and press down on the breasts until you hear a crack. Turn the legs out so the chicken lies flat.
Add the paprika, oregano and a generous pinch of salt into a bowl with a good amount of freshly cracked black pepper, mix together. Sprinkle the seasoning onto the chicken.

Trim and chop the pepper into 2cm chunks, peel and wedge the onions. Thinly slice the garlic cloves. Add all of the veg into a tray and pour the vinegar in. Place the chicken on top, drizzle with olive oil and roast until fully cooked, 40-50 mins.

name: Roast Chicken & Pepper with Mash
description: Chicken and mash is an elite combination. This recipe uses up leftovers from our Roast Chicken & Peppers batch, so you're on the way to a speedy weeknight dinner you'll want on the table every week.
keywords: Roast Chicken & Pepper with Mash recipe
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken & Peppers.
Peel the potatoes and chop into 2cm chunks. Add them into a saucepan full of salted water and place onto high heat. Boil for 15-20 mins, until cooked through. Drain, reserving 100ml of water.
Mash the potatoes. Place onto medium-low heat and stir through the butter and milk until incorporated. Season with salt and pepper.
Tip the juices into a frying pan and bring to the boil. Once boiling, turn the heat down to a simmer and cook the sauce out until slightly thickened, 3-5 mins.
Reheat the chicken, veggies and mash in the microwave until hot. If you don’t have a microwave, tip the chicken and veggies into a baking tray and roast at 220°C until hot, 5-10 mins.
Share the mash between bowls, top with the veggies and chicken. Drizzle over the sauce.

name: Roast Chicken & Sticky Shallots With Stuffing Breadcrumbs
description: A bit like a roast dinner, but a little lighter, brighter and autumnal with charred lemon gravy and jammy shallots, all tossed with a rustic sage sourdough stuffing, that gets hand torn and chucked in with the easiest juicy roast chicken.
keywords: Roast Chicken & Sticky Shallots With Stuffing Breadcrumbs
Roast Chicken & Sticky Shallots With Stuffing Breadcrumbs recipe
instructions: Remove the chicken from the fridge 30 mins before you want to cook it, to let it come up to room temperature. Heat the oven to 190°C.
Grab a large rimmed roasting tray and drizzle enough oil to cover the base of the pan.

Halve and peel the shallots then place them face down into a roasting tray, along with half of a lemon, cut-side down. Remove the top of the garlic, drizzle with oil and wrap in tin foil, then place in the corner of the baking tray.

Pat the chicken dry with kitchen paper, then using your fingers, get under the skin of the chicken gently lifting it up to create a space. Rub the butter into this space making sure it's spread all over. Fill the cavity with the remaining lemon half and a handful of thyme. Season the chicken skin generously with salt, then place the whole chicken on a rack above the tray of shallots on the shelf below. Roast for 1 hour 20 mins.
Meanwhile, tear the bread into chunks and finely chop the sage. Toss the bread in olive oil, sage, onion salt, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Add the bread to the tray of shallots and cook for the final 20 mins until golden.

When the cooking time is up, remove the chicken from the oven and set aside to rest. Remove the lemon from the roasting tray and squeeze over the kale with a pinch of salt. Using your hands, massage the kale until wilted.
Take the pan juices and strain into a jug, then whisk in sherry vinegar and olive oil to emulsify. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Cut the remaining lemon into wedges. Carve the chicken and plate up with the croutons, sticky shallots and roasted garlic. Scatter with parsley, serve with the lemony kale and drizzle with the chicken fat vinaigrette.

name: Roast Chicken Legs with Roasted Grapes, Prosciutto Parsnips & Apple Slaw
description: Golden roast chicken with jammy bursting grapes, crispy prosciutto parsnips and a sharp apple slaw. Your new favourite Sunday batch cook.
keywords: roast chicken legs with roasted grapes
roast chicken legs with roasted grapes recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Place the chicken legs in a large baking dish with decent-sized gaps between them. Drizzle with olive oil and season generously with salt and black pepper. Roast for 35 mins.

Meanwhile, peel the parsnips and cut into roughly 5cm lengths. Add to a large saucepan of salted water and parboil until just fork-tender, then drain. Wrap each piece in prosciutto and brush lightly with olive oil.

Remove the tray from the oven and tuck small bunches of grapes between the chicken legs. Nestle the prosciutto parsnips alongside. Drizzle the grapes with olive oil and season with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Return to the oven for a further 20 mins, until the chicken is cooked through, the grapes are jammy and bursting, and the parsnips are golden and caramelised.

While everything's in the oven, make the slaw. Finely shred the red cabbage into a large bowl. Grate or matchstick the apples and carrot into the bowl. Squeeze over the juice of the lemon and toss together. Add the mayonnaise, season with salt and black pepper and mix well. Finely chop the parsley and stir through.
Serve the chicken and parsnips with the roasted grapes spooned over and the slaw on the side.

name: Roast Chicken Salad with Gravy Dressing
description: Pretty much just an assembly job. The dressing (gravy + parmesan + lemon + olive oil + salt + pepper) is out of this world. It's become my weekend go-to. Ben x
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Time to prep your chicken. Slice up your onion into quarters, arrange 3/4 on the tray and place your chicken on top. Scatter your garlic cloves around the edge and with your broken up rosemary sprig. Rub butter onto the outside of the chicken and season liberally with salt and pepper, adding the remaining piece of onion and 1/4 of a lemon inside the cavity. Pop the tray into the oven for 1hr 15m.

Tenderstem prep: get a frying pan on high heat. Slice your broccoli in half length-ways, and then add to pan with no oil and toast for 10 mins until soft and charred. Take the pan off the heat and wait to cool. Add a splash of oil and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Tomato prep time: chop your tomatoes and add into a colander with a pinch of salt. Mix together and leave the moisture to drain.

Time to assemble your salad base. Slice your peppers, avocado, basil, chilli and lettuce. De-seed your cucumber by slicing once lengthways and spooning out the center then chop. Assemble in the bowl with your olives, tomatoes and tenderstem broccoli. Keep each part compartmented for presentation.
Dressing time. Add 4 Tbsp of olive oil, juice of your remaining 3/4 lemon, salt and pepper to a jar and grate in 50g of parmesan. Set aside for the moment.

After your chicken has cooked, remove from the oven and let rest for 10 mins. Remove the lemon and onion from the cavity and drain the juices from the chicken into the tray. Set the chicken aside on board.

Add your roasting tray with the onions, rosemary, garlic and lemon to the hob with 100ml of water and whack up the heat. With a wooden spatula, scrape off the sticky bits and squeeze the onion, garlic and lemon to release any juices. Bubble down on a high heat until you have a lovely rich, thick gravy and then sieve. Pick out onion slices and add to salad bowl.
Back to the dressing. Add 2 Tbsp of your gravy to your dressing jar and shake up to mix.
Time to carve your chicken. Add the sliced up chicken breast to your assembled salad bowl, saving the rest of the meat for meal prep and other recipes.
Pour over your gravy dressing and toss together, adding a bit more gravy, parmesan and basil to taste. Serve into bowls and enjoy!

name: Roast Chicken Sandwiches with Leftover Herby Mayo
description: Mayo is such a great blank canvas when it comes to sandwiches. Any herbs will work in this recipe, so get creative. B x
instructions: Before you begin, make the No-Fuss Roast Chicken.
Roughly chop the herbs and capers.
Grab a mixing bowl and add the mayonnaise, the chopped herbs and the capers. Add a big squeeze of lemon, season with salt and pepper and mix.
Cut your focaccia into sandwiches and toast the inside.
Slice up your leftover chicken into bite-sized chunks. Slice the cucumber and tomato, season with salt and pepper. Separate the lettuce leaves

Time to build. Start with the bottom slice of each focaccia, slather with the mayo, top with cucumber, chicken, tomato and lettuce. Add another dollop of the mayo, crown with the lid and give it a squish.
Slice them in half and get stuck in.

name: Roast Chicken Thighs with Confit Garlic & Hummus
description: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs, when done right, really are something special. These are slow-roasted over nutty spelt and hummus, with sweet confit garlic cloves and a bright lemony cucumber number on the side.
keywords: Roast Chicken Thighs with Confit Garlic and Hummus
Roast Chicken Thighs with Confit Garlic and Hummus recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Pat the chicken thighs dry with kitchen paper and place them skin-side up in a large roasting tray. Place the garlic cloves in a small ovenproof dish and pour over enough olive oil to just cover them. Drizzle a little olive oil over the chicken, season generously with salt and black pepper, and toss to coat. Put both the chicken and the garlic in the oven.

Roast for 20 mins until the skin is golden and starting to crisp. Turn the oven down to 180°C and continue roasting for a further 20-25 mins until the skin is deep golden and the juices run clear when you pierce the thickest part. Keep an eye on the garlic and remove it early if needed. You want the cloves very lightly golden and completely soft all the way through.

While the chicken cooks, simmer the spelt (or barley, farro, freekeh or rice) in a large saucepan of well-salted boiling water for 25-30 mins until tender with a little bite. Drain and toss with a spoonful of the warm confit garlic oil, a good squeeze of one of the lemons and seasoning.
Dice or slice the cucumber and toss with a squeeze of the remaining lemon and a pinch of salt.

To serve, spoon the hummus into bowls and spread it around the edges. Spoon the warm spelt over, lay the chicken thighs on top and spoon over some of the roasting juices. Tuck the confit garlic cloves around and serve immediately.

name: Roast Chicken Traybake with Carrotes Rapées Salad
description: A good traybake solves everything. This one stars crispy chicken thighs, soft shallots, saucy paprika chickpeas and a sharp French-style carrot salad that properly earns its place.
keywords: Roast Chicken Traybake with Carrotes Rapées Salad recipe
Roast Chicken Traybake with Carrotes Rapées Salad
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel and quarter the shallots and halve the garlic bulb through the middle.
Drain the chickpeas and tip into a large baking tray along with the chicken stock, thyme, garlic bulb halves and shallots.

In a bowl, mix a drizzle of olive oil with the paprika, half the mustard, and the chicken thighs. Season well with salt and black pepper, then rub everything together. Lay the thighs skin side up on top of the chickpeas.Slide into the oven and roast for 30–40 mins until the chicken is golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, coarsely grate or julienne the carrots. Finely chop two-thirds of the parsley. Add both to a bowl with the remaining mustard, a good squeeze of lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil. Season to taste with salt and black pepper. Mix well, then adjust with more lemon if you like it punchy.
To serve, spoon the saucy chickpeas and shallots into bowls. Top with the roast chicken thighs and a generous handful of the carottes râpées salad. Finish with the remaining parsley.

name: Roast Chicken With Schmaltzy Courgettes & Grains
description: A simple batch cook recipe using which makes the most of leftover roast chicken. It's quick, healthy, and filling.
keywords: Roast Chicken With Schmaltzy Courgettes and Grains
Roast Chicken With Schmaltzy Courgettes and Grains recipe
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken with Schmaltzy Courgettes.
Heat the pouches of grains according to the package instructions.
Reheat your Roast Chicken with Schmaltzy Courgettes leftovers in the microwave.
Divide the yoghurt between the two plates, top with the grains, chicken and courgettes. Finish with a sprinkling of chilli flakes, a drizzle of olive oil and a lemon wedge.

name: Roast Chicken with Charred Spring Onion Mayo
description: It wouldn't be right if I didn't do a roast chicken recipe for summer, and this one is so easy and delicious. You could even skip the charred spring onions and just make the herb and Parmesan mayo with everything else, plus the potatoes tossed in the chicken juices.
instructions: Start by making the spring onion mayo. Get a griddle pan or large frying pan over a high heat, then trim the spring onions and add them to the dry pan. Let them char and soften for 5-8 mins, turning as you go. Remove from the pan and allow to cool slightly on a plate, before finely chopping along with the chives. Grate the Parmesan, and then set it aside.
Combine the spring onions, chives, mayonnaise, Parmesan and a generous amount of black pepper in a bowl. Mix well and set aside.
Place your chicken onto a roasting tray or ovenproof pan. Season it all over with the fine salt, then set aside at room temperature for 30 mins. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 230°C.
Place half a lemon and the thyme up the cavity of the chicken then rub the olive oil all over the chicken. Wrap the unpeeled garlic cloves in foil.

Roast the chicken in the oven for 30 mins, then add the white wine to the tray. Turn the oven down to 190°C and roast for a further 25 mins until cooked through (this time will differ depending on the size of your chicken), then allow to rest for 25 mins. Remove the garlic from the foil and squeeze the soft garlic into the tray or pan.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes for 15-20 mins (I like mine to be super soft), then drain and transfer to a bowl.

Lift the rested chicken out of the tray and onto a chopping board, then pour all the chicken juices from the tray plus the garlic over the potatoes. Finely chop the parsley and add that too, along with the juice of the remaining lemon half and salt and pepper.
Carve the chicken, then pile it onto a platter with the potatoes and all the juices. Serve alongside a big green salad and the spring onion mayo.

name: Roast Chicken with Fennel & Tomato Orzo
description: This recipe is the dream one pan. The orzo is packed full of deep, roasted chicken-y flavour, sweet tomatoes and fragrant fennel. A perfect centrepiece.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 240°C.

Rub the chicken with a shot of olive oil and liberally season with fine sea salt. Halve the lemon and stuff into the cavity with a handful of fresh thyme. Place the chicken into a cast iron pot or large roasting tin and roast for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, slice the fennel, dice the onion and thinly slice the garlic.
Coarsely crush the fennel seeds in a pestle and mortar or spice grinder.
Empty the tomatoes into a bowl and crush coarsely with your hands. Add the stock and season with salt and pepper.
Once the chicken has had 30 mins, pull it out of the oven and pop it onto a plate (it’s still not quite cooked yet, so don’t be tempted to have a nibble). Turn the oven down to 190°C.
Cook off the fennel, red onion and fennel seeds in the same pan, in the residual chicken fat with a pinch of salt until softened. Add the garlic and cook for a further few mins.
Now add the orzo, white wine, stock and crushed tomatoes. Stir thoroughly and pop the chicken back on top. Tear the mozzarella into chunks and dot around the chicken.
Chuck the whole lot back in the oven for 30 mins until the chicken is cooked through and the orzo is tender.
Finish with torn parsley leaves and the fennel tops. Don’t forget to grab the lemon out of the chicken and squeeze over the orzo.
Get stuck in.

name: Roast Chicken with Gravy & Braised Garlicky Greens
description: A simple roast chicken recipe cooked with a mass of garlicky greens. The homemade gravy recipe is absolutely on the money.
keywords: Roast Chicken with Gravy & Braised Garlicky Greens
Roast Chicken with Gravy & Braised Garlicky Greens recipe
instructions: Start by removing the wishbone from the chicken, open up the front of the cavity and use a small, sharp knife to expose either side of the wishbone. Trace up the bone with the tip of your knife to the breast bone to expose both sides. Cut down and through each of the connections to the wing and then pull the bone out.

Mix the caster sugar with fine salt and use this to season the chicken liberally, inside and out. Halve the lemon and stuff into the cavity of the chook along with the thyme and most of the rosemary (reserving some extra for the gravy). Set on a tray and pop into the fridge for 4-6 hours.

While the chicken dry brines, roughly chop the carrot, shallots and celery. When ready to roast, preheat the oven to 220°C. Dab the chicken dry with kitchen paper and then rub generously with olive oil. Preheat a pan or roasting tray over a high heat and add a shot of oil and a knob of butter. Roast the veggies briefly in the hot fat so they pick up a little colour before plonking the chicken on top and sliding into the oven for 30-40 mins.

During this time, the chicken will become golden brown and crispy, once looking gorgeous, turn the oven down to 160°C and cook for another 25-30 mins or until the breast hits 68°C. Remove from the oven and remove from the pan, leaving the veggies behind

Pop the roasting pan or tray back onto a high heat and get things sizzling again. Dump in the white wine, bring to a boil and reduce by two-thirds before adding the chicken stock. Bring back to a boil and reduce by half. Strain through a fine sieve into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer.

Pop the cornflour into a dish and add 1-2 tbsp of the hot gravy to make a smooth paste. Pour this back into the hot gravy and whisk to thicken. Have a taste, season with sherry vinegar, salt and pepper. Finish the gravy with chopped rosemary and butter.
Carve the rested chicken and serve on a platter over braised greens. Top with gravy and serve.
Roughly chop your spring greens, removing any very woody stems. Finely slice the garlic and chilli.

Set a lidded pan over a medium heat and add a glug of olive oil. Add the garlic and chilli and sizzle for a minute until fragrant. Drop in the greens and sauté for 3-4 mins. Crank up the heat and add the wine. Add a lid and cook for 6-7 mins until wilted and softened.
Remove the lid and keep cooking until the wine has reduced until almost dry. Finish with salt, pepper and lemon juice to taste.

name: Roast Chicken with Mushrooms & Creamy Polenta
description: Juicy whole roast chicken with buttery Parmesan polenta and crispy sage-fried mushrooms. Simple, comforting and full of flavour. Perfect Sunday food.
keywords: Roast Chicken with Mushrooms & Creamy Polenta Recipe
Roast Chicken with Mushrooms & Creamy Polenta
instructions: Place the chicken on a roasting tray or ovenproof pan. Season it all over with fine salt, then set aside at room temperature for 30 mins. Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 230°C.

Rub olive oil all over the chicken, then roast in the oven for 30 mins. After that, add the white wine (or water if you prefer) to the tray then reduce the oven temperature to 190°C and continue roasting for another 25 mins or until the chicken is cooked through (the time may vary depending on the size of your chicken). Allow the chicken to rest in the tray for 25 mins.

While the chicken is resting, prepare the mushrooms and polenta. Cut the mushrooms (you can use any variety but I prefer a mix) in half or quarters if large, but keep ones like small chanterelles whole. Finely grate or chop the garlic.

Heat a large dry frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms, without any oil, and toast them for 4 mins until starting to turn golden. Add the butter, a generous glug of olive oil and the sage leaves and fry for an additional 5 mins until the mushrooms are golden and the sage is crisp, adding in the garlic for the final minute.

In a separate saucepan, add the milk and water and bring to a boil over a medium heat. Reduce to a simmer, then whisk in the polenta. Cook for 6-7 mins or until the polenta is thick, creamy, and no longer has a raw taste. Whisk in the butter and Parmesan, then season with salt and pepper.
Remove the chicken from the tray and pour the juices into a small saucepan along with the white wine vinegar. Gently heat the mixture.
If the polenta becomes too stiff, add a bit more water and mix thoroughly until smooth again.

Carve the chicken into parts: halve the breasts, and separate the thighs and drumsticks. Dollop the polenta onto a platter, then top with the chicken and the warmed juices. Finally, pour over the crisp mushrooms and sage, and serve immediately.

name: Roast Chicken with Schmaltzy Courgettes
description: A big, beautiful batch recipe where we've roasted a chicken over a bed of courgettes and garlic. Expect some serious flavour with this one.
keywords: Batch Recipe: Roast Chicken With Schmaltzy Courgettes
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Season your chicken with plenty of salt, inside and out and rub with 2 tbsp of olive oil.

Cut the courgettes into chunky rounds and tip into a roasting tray. Cut the onions into thin slices and finely chop the chillies. Add to the tray. Toss the veggies with oil, salt and pepper and sit the chicken on top.

Cut the very top off of each garlic bulb, grab a piece of foil and sit the garlic bulbs on top. Drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper and wrap into a little garlicky parcel. Sit that in the tray with the veggies and chicken and slide the whole lot into the oven for an hour.

After an hour, check if your chicken is cooked with a thermometer (you’re looking for a minimum of 70°C in the thickest part of the breast and thigh) or make a small incision and check if the juices run clear. If you’re all good, whip it off and let it rest, if it needs a little longer, pop it back in for 15 mins and check again.

While the chicken rests, smush up the flesh from your roasted garlic bulb into your veggies and pop the tray back into the oven for another 15 mins or so to finish the veggies off. Meanwhile, chop the tarragon.
Carve the legs and breasts off of the chicken. Cut the breasts into chunky slices and shred the meat from the legs.
Finish the veggies with lemon zest, lemon juice and the chopped tarragon.
Serve and enjoy the chicken and courgettes as they are. Or, if you're batch cooking for the week, divide between Tupperware and stick in the fridge.

name: Roast Chicken, Prosciutto & Apple Chopped Sarnie
description: Who doesn't love a leftover sandwich?This sarnie is packed with your leftover Roast Chicken Legs with Roasted Grapes, Prosciutto Parsnips & Apple Slaw batch. Yum.
instructions: Pull the meat from the chicken legs (you'll need 1 leg per serving) and roughly chop, alongside the leftover prosciutto parsnips and apple slaw. Chop eveyrthing together until evenly mixed.
Pile the chicken slaw mix generously between two thick slices of farmhouse bread per person and serve.

name: Roast Cod with Turmeric, Ginger & Shallot Sauce
description: Roast cod sitting on a silky, warmly spiced shallot and ginger sauce, with a fresh crunchy sugar snap salad on top. All on the table in under an hour.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel and halve the shallots and ginger. Place the halved shallots cut-side down on a large roasting tray along with the ginger and whole chillies. Wrap the whole garlic bulb in foil with a drizzle of olive oil and add to the tray. Drizzle everything generously with olive oil, season with salt and roast for 25–30 mins, until the shallots are deeply golden and caramelised and the garlic is completely soft.
Meanwhile, cook the jasmine rice according to the packet instructions, then set aside covered to keep warm.

Remove the tray from the oven. Squeeze the garlic cloves from their skins then tip everything into a blender along with the turmeric, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil and the juice of the lime. Blitz until smooth, adding the cold water gradually until the sauce is loose and pourable. Taste and adjust with more soy if needed.

Place the cod fillets on a separate lightly oiled roasting tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season generously with salt. Roast for 12–15 mins, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily when pressed.
Finely slice the sugar snap peas on the diagonal and the chilli, then toss together in a bowl with the coriander leaves, and squeeze in the juice of half the remaining lime and the sesame oil.
To serve, spoon the rice into bowls. Spoon a few tablespoons of the sauce onto each plate and top with the cod. Finish with the sugar snap salad and serve with the remaining lime cut into wedges.

name: Roast Duck Breast with Pedro Ximinez Cherries
description: This recipe for duck breast will see you never reach for the chicken again. If home cooking is your thing but you’ve never thought much of duck, this indulgent recipe is here to change your mind. Duck with fruit is an age-old combination, but we’ve added some Pedro Ximénez sherry for a deeply fruity, boozy sauce, packed full of cherries.
keywords: Roast Duck Breast with Pedro Ximinez Cherries
Roast Duck Breast with Pedro Ximinez Cherries recipe
instructions: Use a sharp knife to score the skin of each duck breast in shallow cuts in a diamond pattern. Season really well with salt all over.
Cut the cherries in half and remove the stones. Halve, peel and finely chop the shallot.
Heat the oven to 180°C.

Put the duck breasts skin-side down into a cold frying pan, then put over a medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot and the duck breasts are really sizzling, cook for 5 mins, having a peek at the skin – it should be super golden and crisp and the fat should have rendered into the pan.

Put a wire rack over a baking tray and put the duck breasts onto it, skin-side up. Put into the oven for 8-10 mins (depending on size) to roast. After this, move onto a plate, still skin-side up, and leave to rest for 5 mins.

Meanwhile, put the duck fat pan over a low heat and scrape in the shallots along with a pinch of salt. Cook for 5 minutes until the shallot is soft. Pour in the chicken stock and sherry, turn the heat to medium and bring to a bubble. Scatter in the cherries and spoon in the cherry jam. Bubble for 8-10 minutes until the cherries are just softening and the sauce is glossy and thickened slightly. Season lightly with salt and plenty of cracked black pepper.
Slice the duck breasts and pour any resting juices into the sauce and serve.

name: Roast Garlic Linguine
description: Kind of like a Cacio e Pepe but with soft, squidgy, caramelised roast garlic. This dish is all in the technique. It is so creamy, you'll be making it on repeat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/365°F.
Place your garlic bulbs on a piece of baking paper and wrap them up. Place the garlic parcel in a roasting tin and whack in the oven for 45 minutes.
Very finely grate your Parmesan and your pecorino and add to a mixing bowl. Grate in the zest of a lemon.
Place a frying pan on the heat. Add 1.5 tbsp of pepper into the pan. Toast the pepper, mixing it around the pan, and remove from the heat as it starts properly smoking. Add to the cheese bowl.

Once the garlic is done (it will be squidgy if you press it), remove from the oven. Peel back the skin and with a knife, squish out the roast garlic within. Once all the garlic is squeezed out, discard of the skins. Chop the garlic up until you have a nice smooth paste. Add to the cheese bowl.
Get a fork and mix the cheese and garlic together. Once it is all combined, you should have a nice thick paste.

Now you need to get everything ready, as speed and timing are key. Get a jug out, and boil your kettle. Put your pan on the heat, and add your water – don’t fill it, you only need enough water to cover the pasta (you need the water to be very very starchy).
Add a nice big pinch of salt to the water and bring to the boil. Then add your linguine.
After 4 minutes, with your jug/mug remove 300ml starchy water from pan. Add it bit by bit to your cheese paste, making sure it is all nicely combined. You’ll end up with a nice creamy consistency.
Back to the pasta – after 8 minutes in total, drain the pasta and pour about 200ml pasta water into another cup. You’ll need this.
Add the pasta back to the pan and put the pan back on a very very very low heat. Quickly, pour over your sauce. Start beating the sauce through the pasta.

As it begins to thicken, keep adding splashes of your pasta water. Keep beating and adding splashes. If it gets stringy or lumps of cheese appear, don’t worry. Just keep beating hard and adding water. This will take about 3 minutes – what you are going for is a thick creamy emulsion. Turn off the heat and keep beating for 1 final minute.
Once the consistency of your pasta resembles the photo, you’re ready to go.
Serve the pasta on to 4 plates. Top with an extra grinding of pepper, a sprinkle of cheese and a nice squeeze of lemon juice (it really cuts through the rich cheese and garlic). Enjoy!

name: Roast Paprika Chicken with Herby Cottage Cheese Cucumbers
description: Gently spiced chicken thighs roasted until golden and crispy, served with cool herby cottage cheese dressed cucumbers and crispy new potatoes. On the table in under an hour.
keywords: Roast Chicken Thighs with Cottage Cheese Dressed Cucumbers
Roast Chicken Thighs with Cottage Cheese Dressed Cucumbers recipe
instructions: Heat your oven to 220°C. Place a large roasting tin in the oven while it heats up, a hot tin gives the potatoes a head start on crisping. Scrub the potatoes if they need it - no need to peel. Halve smaller ones, quarter larger ones so they're roughly even in size then toss in a bowl with the olive oil and a generous seasoning of salt and black pepper. Tip into the hot roasting tin in a single layer, cut-side down. Roast for 35–40 minutes, turning once halfway through, until deep golden and crispy on the outside and completely tender inside.

While the potatoes roast, season the chicken thighs generously with salt and black pepper on both sides. Heat a splash of olive oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over a medium-high heat. Place the chicken thighs skin-side down and cook without moving for 6–8 mins until the skin is deep golden and crisp. Flip and cook for a further 2 mins, then transfer the pan to the oven and roast for 15 mins.

Remove the pan from the oven and bash the garlic cloves with the flat of a knife. Add them to the pan along with the paprika and dried oregano, turning the thighs to coat. Return to the oven for a further 10–15 mins until the chicken is cooked through and the juices run clear. Remove from the oven, squeeze over the juice of the lemon and leave to rest for 5–10 mins.

While the chicken roasts, make the cottage cheese dressing. Put the cottage cheese, herbs, olive oil and the juice of the remaining lemon into a blender and blitz until smooth. Add a splash of cold water and blitz again until it reaches a pourable consistency. Season well with salt and black pepper.
Slice the cucumber into rounds or on the diagonal and toss gently in the cottage cheese dressing until well coated.
Serve the chicken with all the pan juices, a generous mound of the dressed cucumbers and a pile of crispy potatoes.

name: Roast Peach, Mortadella & Mozzarella Sandwich
description: It's no secret that a sweet and savoury combo is a match made in heaven, and this sarnie is a testament to that.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200℃. Halve and pit the peaches, then transfer to a baking tray. Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, the honey, thyme and a pinch of salt, then roast in the oven for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, slice the focaccia rolls in half, then spread the bottom halves with the pesto.

To assemble, tear the mozzarella and add on top of the pesto. Layer up the mortadella in ruffles, then top with the peaches. Cover with rocket, then spread mustard over the top bread halves. Close the sandwich, press down and slice through the middle.

name: Roast Pork Shoulder with Mustard, Apples & Beans
description: This mustard-glazed pork shoulder roasts low and slow ‘til fall-apart tender, with sweet apples, buttery beans and epic crackling on top. It's a showstopper.
keywords: roast pork shoulder recipe with mustard
