instructions: The night before, remove the pork from its packaging, score the fat of the joint with a small sharp knife and put onto a rack over a large baking tray. Boil the kettle and pour the hot water over the skin of the pork. Pat dry with kitchen paper, drain away the water, then sprinkle all over with sea salt. Put into the fridge, uncovered, overnight.

The next day, heat the oven to 220°C. Peel and thickly slice the onion and put into the bottom of a large, deep roasting tin. Put the pork joint directly on top, skin-side up. Drizzle with a little oil, spreading to evenly coat.
Put into the oven for 35-40 mins until the skin is starting to caramelise and look crispy.
Turn the oven down to 150°C. Pour the cider and chicken stock all around the pork, but not on the skin, then return to the oven for 2 hrs.
Meanwhile, peel the apples, then cut vertically into quarters, remove the core and cut each piece in half lengthwise. You should have 8 pieces from each apple.

After the 2 hrs, tip the apples into the tray around the pork, along with the beans and all their liquid from the jars. Mix and put back into the oven for 1 hr until the crackling is crisp and the meat meltingly tender.
Carefully lift the pork joint off the beans and onto a large plate or baking tray. Leave loosely covered for 10 mins to rest.

Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the kale and cook for 1 seconds to 2 minute, just until it turns bright green and softens a touch. Drain, and then place it in a bowl of iced water to stop it cooking (you can run under cold water too). After a minute, drain.
Spoon the mustard and crème fraîche into the beans and stir well. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper. Roughly chop the parsley and stir this in, too.
Lift the pork back onto the beans, pouring in any resting juices, and take the whole thing to the table for people to dig in. Serving your blanched kale alongside.

name: Roast Pork with Crackling
description: A classic recipe for roast pork belly with extremely crispy crackling. Make sure you use a boneless skin-on pork belly joint. Serve it with apple sauce for the perfect dinner party or Sunday lunch.
instructions: Coarsely grind the peppercorns and pick the rosemary needles off, discarding the stems. Finely chop and add both to a small bowl with the salt. Finely grate in the garlic and mix to combine.

Pat the pork belly dry with kitchen roll. Rub the garlic paste onto the pork flesh, leaving the skin clean. Place on a wire rack and pop in the fridge overnight (or at least for a few hours), uncovered, so the skin can dry out.
When the drying time is up, heat the oven to 160°C fan. Remove the pork from the fridge and leave it to come up to room temperature (about 30 mins).

Pat the skin of the pork dry, then wrap the belly in tin foil, skin side up, leaving the skin exposed. Transfer to a baking tray and slide it into the oven to roast for 50-60 mins, then turn the heat up to 220°C and roast for about 20-25 mins or until the skin starts to blister and turn golden brown.

Remove the pork from the oven and turn on the grill to a low heat. Place the belly under the grill and cook for 3-6 mins until the skin has puffed up and gone crispy, turning it every couple of minutes to ensure the skin doesn't burn.
Remove the pork from the oven and leave to rest for 10-15 mins, before cutting and serving with apple sauce.

name: Roast Potato Aloo Chaat
description: Ghee roasted potatoes, crispy on outside and soft on the inside. Our take on a classic roast potato chaat infused with curry paste and inspired by India's popular street food snack: aloo chaat. It’s not hard to see why it’s up there with samosas and chicken tikka masala as one of the great foods of India.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Peel potatoes and cut into quarter chunks, then add to a large pot and cover just enough water. Season with a big pinch of salt and boil potatoes until fork tender. Drain the potatoes and fluff well inside the pot. Tip the potatoes back into the strainer to air dry.
Grab a large rimmed baking dish, add enough oil to cover the surface, then spoon in the butter/ghee and slide into the oven for 10 mins or until the oil is hot.

Very carefully remove the hot tray of oil onto the stove top and carefully drop in the potatoes, it should sizzle. Use tongs to toss the potatoes in oil. Roast for 20 mins, removing and flipping for 1-1 ½ hours or until crispy golden.
In the meantime, make the zesty lime yoghurt by combining your yoghurt and lime with salt and leaving it in the fridge. Finely slice red onion and coriander for garnishes.

When the potatoes look golden dollop in the curry paste, mango chutney, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Toss, return to the oven for 10 mins to let everything sizzle. Then remove and add sliced onions in the tray and toss.
Swoosh all the lime yoghurt onto a big serving plate, top with crispy potatoes, garnish with pomegranate seeds, red onion, coriander and serve with mango chutney on the side.

name: Roast Squash, Chickpea & Harissa Lasagne
description: Authentic to nowhere, but also very much inspired by the flavours of North African cuisine, this lasagne is sweetly spiced, intense, chunky and textured. I really like serving it with additional dollops of harissa as a condiment. I’ve specified rose harissa — which is perfumed and also not too punchy — but a standard harissa would work well too.
cuisine: Italian, Italian-Inspired, North African, North African-Inspired
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Use a pestle and mortar to bash and lightly grind the cumin seeds, then combine them with the ginger, cinnamon and a pinch of flaky sea salt. Finely dice the onion and carrots. Use a vegetable peeler or small knife to remove the rind from the orange.

Cut the squash in half lengthwise (no need to peel). Scoop out the seeds, then cut the flesh into ½cm-1cm crescents. Pick the coriander leaves from their stalks and roughly chop them up. Finely chop the coriander stalks.

In a large bowl or roasting tin, toss the squash in half of the olive oil until glossy, then add the spice rub and ensure each piece is well coated. Arrange over 2-3 baking trays, so they sit in one layer, and roast for 15-20 mins until soft and lightly browned.

Meanwhile, drizzle the remaining oil into a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of salt and sauté for 5 mins without colouring. Stir in the carrot and chopped coriander stalks and cook for 4-5 mins, stirring occasionally. Pour in the chickpeas and any stock in the jar, plus the chopped tomatoes, orange rind, honey, harissa, cinnamon stick and a generous amount of salt and pepper. Simmer for around 15 mins, so the sauce becomes glossy and reduces by one-third. Remove from the heat, pick out the cinnamon stick and orange rind, then stir through the coriander leaves.
In a mixing bowl, combine the crème fraîche, milk and two-thirds of the Parmesan.

Assemble the lasagne in a 2-2.5L ovenproof dish. Cover the base with a little less than one-third of the sauce, then a layer of pasta, then sauce, then pasta. Arrange the squash in one layer, then spoon and spread a touch more than one-third of the crème fraîche mixture on top. Now add another layer of pasta, then sauce plus any remaining squash. Top with a final layer of pasta and the remaining crème fraîche mixture, then cover with Parmesan. Bake for around 35 mins, until bubbling and golden.
Leave to rest for 10 mins before dividing into portions and serving with dollops of harissa to taste.

name: Roast Sweet Potato & Quick Sausage Ragù
description: Crispy-skinned roast sweet potatoes loaded with a rich, spiced sausage ragù, creamy yoghurt and crunchy smoked almonds. A proper weeknight winner.
keywords: Roast Sweet Potato & Quick Sausage Ragù
Roast Sweet Potato & Quick Sausage Ragù recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Scrub the sweet potatoes, dry them and rub with a little olive oil. Transfer to a baking tray and roast for 40 mins until soft.

Meanwhile, trim and halve the green beans, thinly slice the onion and garlic. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems. Roughly chop the almonds. Squeeze the sausagemeat out of its casings and crumble into pieces.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the sausagemeat and cook for 7-10 mins until browning. Stir in the onion, coriander stems and garlic and cook for 10 mins until softened. Season with salt, black pepper and the cinnamon.

Add the tomato purée and cook for 2-4 mins until dark red. Pour in the stock, add the green beans and leave to simmer for 5-7 mins until thickened. Add a splash of water to loosen if needed. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
To serve, split a roast sweet potato in half per person and spoon over the sausage ragù. Top with a dollop of yoghurt, the coriander leaves and the almonds.

name: Roast Sweet Potato Salad with Gochujang Tahini Sauce
description: A flavour-packed salad featuring roasted sweet potatoes, crispy chickpeas, and a spicy-savoury gochujang tahini dressing.  Perfect for meal prep.
keywords: Roast Sweet Potato Salad with Gochujang Tahini Sauce
Roast Sweet Potato Salad with Gochujang Tahini Sauce recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan. Cut the sweet potatoes into wedges.
In a bowl, toss the sweet potato wedges with a splash of olive oil, salt, black pepper, and cumin. Spread onto a baking tray.
Drain the chickpeas and add to  the same bowl, toss them with the remaining oil and seasoning left in the bowl. Set aside.
Roast the sweet potatoes for 25 mins. Flip the potatoes, add the chickpeas to the tray, and roast for another 15 mins until golden and crisp.

Make the dressing: In a bowl, whisk together the gochujang, tahini, soy sauce, maple syrup, and lime juice. Loosen with a little water until it reaches a drizzleable consistency. Taste and season with salt, if needed.
Place the kale in a colander and pour over boiling water until wilted. Squeeze out excess liquid, roughly chop, and mix through the lentils.

To serve, divide the lentil mixture into serving boxes. Top with roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas. Drizzle with the gochujang tahini sauce and garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

name: Roast Sweet Potato Salad with Miso Tahini Chickpeas
description: This dressing makes use of two of my favourite storecupboard staples: miso and tahini. I’ve blended them with some ground cumin, garlic and enough cold water to form a creamy, deeply flavoursome dressing to drench chickpeas in.
keywords: roast sweet potato salad with miso tahini chickpeas
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a large baking tray with baking parchment.
Peel and slice the sweet potato and onion into 1cm-thick slices.

Toss the sweet potato and red onion with half of the olive oil and season with the coriander seeds, a big pinch of salt and black pepper. Transfer to the lined tray in a single layer and roast for 20-25 mins or until tender.

Meanwhile, blend the tahini and miso together with the garlic, cumin and chilli, then blend in the rest of your olive oil and the water to give a consistency of double cream, then season to taste with salt and pepper.

Heat the grill to high, pour the miso dressing over the sweet potato and onion in the tray, then add the drained chickpeas and grill under a high heat for around 8 minutes until bubbling with some colour.
Meanwhile make a dressing with the honey, the zest and juice of your lime, and sesame seeds. Put it to one side.

Remove the tray from the grill, then pile the glazed chickpeas and sweet potatoes onto a serving plate, cool for 5 minutes or so and roughly chop the coriander. Add this to the dish, along with the crumbled feta, then spoon over with the lime and sesame dressing and drizzle with some extra olive oil to serve.

name: Roast Sweet Potato Wraps With Chickpea Katsu Sauce
description: Roasted sweet potato, creamy coconut curry sauce and fluffy rice all wrapped up in a golden tortilla. Freezer-friendly and great for batch prep.
keywords: Roast Sweet Potato & Chickpea Wrap With Coconut Katsu Sauce
Roast Sweet Potato & Chickpea Wrap With Coconut Katsu Sauce recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Chop the sweet potatoes into 3cm chunks. Toss with olive oil, salt and pepper on a baking tray, then roast for 25–30 mins until golden and soft.

Finely dice the onion, carrot, garlic and ginger. Set a large saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 8 mins until soft and starting to caramelise.

Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 min, then stir in the curry powder and cook out for 30 secs until fragrant. Then pour in the coconut milk and water. Season with salt and pepper, cover and simmer on a low heat for 10 mins.

Meanwhile, strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stalks. Add the leaves into a heat-proof bowl and cover with boiling water. Let them sit for 5 mins, then drain. Once cool enough to handle, squeeze out as much liquid as possible and roughly chop. Set aside.
Back to the katsu sauce, once all the veg has softened, blitz until smooth using a stick blender (or let it cool and use a high-speed blender). Squeeze in the lime juice, season to taste.
Mix the sweet potatoes through the sauce with the drained chickpeas and cavolo nero.

To assemble, spoon some rice into the centre of each wrap. Top with a generous spoonful of the curry mix. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly away from you. 
 Seal seam-side down in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2–3 mins, or air fry seam-side down at 200°C for 5 mins until golden and crisp.

Wrap each one in baking paper and foil. Freeze until needed.
To reheat, remove the foil and wrap the burrito in damp kitchen paper. Microwave for 2 mins, then air fry at 180°C for 7–8 mins or bake at 160°C for 10 mins until piping hot throughout.

name: Roast Sweet Potato with Chickpea & Coconut Curry
description: A healthy, quick, vegan curry packed with flavour and goodness. You can make this for a quick lunch, but it's equally comforting for dinner. If you don't like sweet potato, swap it for baked jacket potato. And if you want to make it a little more indulgent, grate over some mature cheddar before drizzling over your favorite chilli oil.
keywords: Roast Sweet Potato with Chickpea & Coconut Curry
Roast Sweet Potato with Chickpea & Coconut Curry recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Scrub and wash the sweet potatoes thoroughly. Dry them and rub with some coconut oil. Transfer to a baking tray and roast in the oven for 30-40 mins until soft.
Meanwhile, chop the onion and green chilli. Finely mince the garlic. Set aside.

Discard any thick kale stems, then transfer the kale to a baking tray and drizzle with vegetable oil. Toss together to coat evenly, then season with salt. When there are 10 mins of cooking time left for the sweet potatoes, add the kale to the oven and roast for 10-15 mins until crispy.

Meanwhile, heat a generous spoonful of coconut oil in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and, once they splutter, add the onion with a pinch of salt. Grate the ginger. Cook for 2-4 mins until softened, then add the ginger and garlic and cook for 2 mins. Tip in all the dry spices, curry leaves and green chilli. Cook for 1 min, then stir through the tomato purée and cook for 2-3 mins until darkened.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of water, then cook for 3 mins until they’re coated in all the spices. Add the water and coconut milk and continue cooking until the curry is nice and thick.
To serve, split one roast sweet potato in half per person and pour over some curry. Tear over the coriander to finish.

name: Roast Veg & Raw Tomato Salad
description: Charred peppers and aubergines pair beautifully with fresh, in-season tomatoes in this vegetarian salad recipe.
keywords: Roast Veg & Raw Tomato Salad  recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the tomato into rough 3cm chunks, then add to a large bowl with a generous pinch of salt. Set aside.
Slice the top of the garlic bulb off, drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with a little salt, then wrap the whole thing up in foil. Set aside.
Halve the shallots (or quarter the onions). Prick the aubergine all over with a knife. Transfer them both to a baking tray with the pepper and garlic, plus a splash of olive oil. Roast for 20 mins.

Remove the garlic (set aside) and give the onions a toss, then return to the oven for 15-20 mins until the aubergine and pepper is completely softened and the red pepper skin is slightly charred. The pepper might take a little longer here depending on your oven, so give it another 5-10 mins if necessary.

Remove everything from the oven, place in a bowl then cover with a plate or cling film so it steams for 20 mins. Finely chop the parsley then squeeze out the roasted garlic in to the bowl with the veg.

Take everything out of the bowl, leaving any juices behind. Split open the aubergine and scoop out the insides, then roughly chop or tear. Deseed the peppers and peel the skin off. Roughly tear the peppers and shallots, then transfer to the tomato bowl, along with the aubergine, parsley and your drained brown lentils. Season to taste with salt and pepper, then add in the lemon juice.
In a small pan over a medium heat, add the butter to melt. Once foaming add the cumin, fennel seeds and chilli flakes to toast for 30 seconds in the butter until fragrant.
Spoon the vegetables onto a platter. Top with dollops of yoghurt, then pour over the spiced butter. Eat alongside flatbreads or sourdough.

name: Roasted Artichoke Recipe With Garlic Drizzle
description: A simple roasted artichoke recipe with an addictive garlic drizzle.
keywords: Roasted Artichoke Recipe With Garlic Drizzle
Roasted Artichoke Recipe With Garlic Drizzle recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Trim the artichoke stalk. Peel what remains of the stalk until you have removed all of the thick skin (you will remove about one-third of the thickness of the stalk).
Cut the lemon in half, then slice about 3cm off the tip. Slice the artichoke bulb in half lengthways. Immediately rub the lemon all over the open sides of the artichoke to stop it from browning.

Dig into the middle of each artichoke heart with a spoon to remove all of the hairs, as these are not edible. Place a peeled garlic clove into each hole where you removed the hair from. Drizzle each side with plenty of olive oil and season with salt and pepper, then cut two slices of lemon and place them over the garlic. Wrap each stuffed artichoke half tightly in foil and bake for around 30-40 mins, depending on their size. Check at 30 mins – if a knife cuts through the heart with no resistance, they’re ready.

Remove the artichokes from the foil. Remove and discard the lemon slices. Pour any lemon juice that has pooled into the heart into a small bowl. Take each garlic clove and place them into the bowl with the lemon juice and mash with a fork. Add some olive oil and a squeeze of lemon and some salt and pepper. Drizzle this dressing over the artichoke.
Finish with lemon zest, chopped parsley and chilli flakes, if you like.

name: Roasted Asparagus With Preserved Lemon & Olive Salsa
description:
Asparagus season is just getting started so kick the season off with a belter. This olive salsa is a real
workhorse, it’s fantastic with BBQ’d fish, grilled pork chops or a banging steak. You’re going to love it.
keywords: Roasted Asparagus with Preserved Lemon & Olive Salsa
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Trim the woody ends of the asparagus and toss with olive oil, salt and pepper. Add to a baking tray and roast for 9-10 mins until tender and caramelised.
While the asparagus is roasting, grab a pestle and mortar. Add the garlic clove and a big pinch of salt. Smash the garlic down and grind into a paste.
Roughly chop the green and black olives, finely chop the shallot and add the lot to the mortar.
Remove the flesh from the preserved lemons and finely slice the rind. Roughly chop the mint and add both to the salsa.
Now bring everything together with a squeeze of lemon juice and plenty of olive oil.
Pile the roasted asparagus onto a plate and top with plenty of olive salsa.

name: Roasted Aubergine & Pesto Tart
description: Pizza, meet pastry. A match made in heaven, this is perfect for a summery lunch or quick dinner. It's even better the next day.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Slice the aubergine into 1cm thick rounds. Rub with oil and salt and grill over a high heat until caramelised and tender. Set aside.
Take a saucepan and add a good glug of oil. Smash and peel the garlic clove and add to it to the pan. Set over a medium heat and allow the garlic to infuse the oil.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and add them to the pan with the garlic. Season with salt and pepper. Chuck in a handful of basil with the stalks, saving a few leaves for later.
Cook on a medium heat, stirring regularly, for 5-6 mins until saucy, pour into a bowl and let cool.
While the sauce cools, roll out your pastry. You want it about 1cm thick. Score a 3cm border and prick the middle with a fork. Beat your egg with a pinch of salt and brush around the border.
Now bake the pastry for 20 mins until lightly golden. If the centre has puffed, push it back down with the back of a fork.

To build the rest of the tart, spread the base with your cherry tomato sauce and layer on your aubergine. Top with torn mozzarella, sundried tomatoes and a drizzle of oil. Return to the oven for 10 minutes to melt the cheese and finish cooking the pastry.
Once baked, top with fresh pesto, the remaining basil leaves and a grating of parmesan cheese.
Slice it up and get stuck in.

name: Roasted Aubergine Curry & Pol Roti
description: Karan Gokani, director of Sri Lankan restaurant group Hoppers, blessed the studio with this truly wonderful and warming dish best accompanied with pol roti.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan.
Chop your aubergines into 3cm thick chunks and dice your red onion.

In a large bowl, toss the aubergine with the vegetable oil, ½ tsp of the ground turmeric and a generous pinch of salt. Spread on a large roasting tray in a single layer and roast for 15 mins, tossing every 5 minutes or so.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the mustard and fenugreek seeds.

Once the mustard seeds stop crackling, add the cinnamon stick, curry leaves, onion, garlic, ginger, lemongrass and dried chillies. Stir well to coat in the oil, add a pinch of salt and continue to cook for 8-10 mins, stirring occasionally until the onions are soft and translucent.
Add the curry powder and remaining ½ tsp ground turmeric and cook for a further minute, adding a splash of water if they begin to stick to the pan.
Add the coconut milk, stock and tamarind, reduce the heat to low and cook 3-4 mins until the liquid has reduced to half.
Stir through the roasted aubergine and sugar and continue to simmer for 3 mins, then season to taste with salt.
Finely chop your red onion, green chilli and curry leaves.

Add your chopped chillies and onion to a large mixing bowl along with your flour, curry leaves, coconut oil, and desiccated coconut. Mix the ingredients together, adding a little warm water at a time, to bring together a cohesive dough that does not stick to the hands. The dough should have the consistency of play-dough.
Knead for about 5 minutes by hand. There’s no need to use a stand mixer for this.
Leave to rest at room temperature, covered with cling film for at least 30 mins, or longer if preparing ahead.
Roll out into 6-inch discs the thickness of two stacked one pound coins. I prefer a slightly rough, natural look rather than perfect circles.

Heat a dry non-stick pan or well-seasoned cast-iron pan over high heat and then reduce heat to medium and cook the rotis for 4-5 mins flipping halfway through (The key is not to use oil or fat when cooking the rotis and to cook them on a hot dry pan).
Serve immediately with your curry or store in a box wrapped in a clean kitchen towel.

name: Roasted Aubergine Omelette & Double Garlic Fried Rice
description: Inspired by Filipino Torta Talong - this dish is bursting with umami flavour and ready in less time than you think.  If you can’t find fried garlic, either finely mince a couple cloves of garlic until lightly golden, or substitute with crispy fried onions. To keep this completely vegetarian, use mushroom stir-fry sauce instead of oyster sauce.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Halve the aubergines lengthways and place on a baking tray, flat-side down. Season with salt and drizzle over a generous amount of olive oil. Slide into the oven for 30-35 mins, until golden and softened.
Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a bowl, add the soy sauce and whisk together. Set aside. Gently bash the garlic cloves.

Add a drizzle of oil to a wok or large frying pan with the bashed garlic and place over a medium heat. Once the garlic starts to sizzle and loses its raw sharpness, add the rice and crispy fried garlic. Stir-fry until piping hot, then add the oyster sauce and stir until evenly combined. Taste and season with salt and black pepper, then transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm.

Place the empty pan back over a medium heat with a little more oil. Once hot, add the roasted aubergine and press down until about 1cm thin. Fry for a couple of minutes on each side, then remove from the pan. Repeat with each half.

Working one portion at a time, add a little more oil to the pan if needed and pour in a quarter of the egg mixture, swirling it to cover the base. Place a squished aubergine half on top, then cover with a lid and cook for 2-4 mins, until the top has just set to your liking. If the egg is browning too quickly, turn the heat down a little. Repeat for each portion.
Divide the garlic fried rice between plates, top with the aubergine omelette and finish with a squeeze of ketchup.

name: Roasted Aubergine, Tomato and Mozzarella Salad
description: All the best bits of an aubergine parm in a fresh vibrant salad. Crunchy ciabatta croutons and jammy tomatoes, perfect for the summer.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Chop the aubergine into large wedges and score the outside of them with a knife. Slice the tomatoes into thick slices. Rub them with olive oil, salt, pepper and dried oregano.
Place a bulb of garlic on a piece of foil and drizzle with olive oil. Wrap tightly and pop onto a baking tray with the aubergine and tomatoes
Bake the aubergine, tomatoes and garlic in the oven for 30 mins.
Roughly rip the ciabatta and toss with olive oil and salt. Pop them in a baking tray in the oven for the final 15 mins of roasting.
Squeeze the garlic out of its peel into a bowl and mash together with salt, pepper, red wine vinegar and 4 tbsp of olive oil.

Toss the rocket, watercress and basil with half of the dressing. Then layer that onto your plate. Top with roasted aubergine, tomato and ciabatta croutons. Grate on some parmesan cheese, and tear some mozzarella. Drizzle on some more dressing and serve.

name: Roasted Baharat Chicken & Potato Salad
description: Nothing beats a traybake for a weeknight dinner.  Fresh fennel, roasted apricots and creamy roasted garlic dressing make the potato salad extra special.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Rub the chicken with a drizzle of olive oil and generously season with salt and pepper. Evenly sprinkle the baharat over the chicken and rub in. Set aside.
Put the garlic bulb on a square of foil with a drizzle of oil, then scrunch the foil to close. Halve and pit the apricots, then halve the potatoes.
Put the apricots, potatoes and garlic bulb onto a large baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt. Place the chicken on top and bake for 30 mins, until the chicken is cooked through.

Meanwhile, pick the fennel fronds and thinly slice the fennel – use a mandoline if you have one. Set both the fronds and fennel slices aside. Pick the basil leaves and set aside. Zest 1 lemon into a large mixing bowl. Add the juice from all the lemons and 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Once the chicken and veg are cooked, squeeze the roasted garlic into the lemon dressing. Mix together, then toss the potatoes, apricots, fennel and half the basil leaves through.
Serve the warm potato salad with the chicken. Finish with a scattering of fennel fronds and tear over the remaining basil leaves.

name: Roasted Banana Split
description: This healthy version of a childhood classic will satisfy all of your sweet-tooth cravings in a super healthy way. It's also a great use for overripe bananas.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190C.
Pierce the bananas all over with a fork and place on a lined baking tray. Roast for 20 mins, flip and roast for another 10 mins. They should be jet black all over.
Meanwhile, roast the pecans for 5-6 mins, tossing once. Roughly chop.
To prepare the bananas, Slice them down the middle, lengthwise. I like to mash them slightly with a fork at this point, to get maximum surface area for the toppings.
Layer up the tahini, syrup, nuts, and yoghurt, Chop the chocolate or use a speed peeler to carve it into thin shavings over the bananas.

name: Roasted Broccoli with Caesar-ish Sauce and Smoky Seedy Drizzle
description: This vegan caesar-ish sauce is a super flavourful, quick and easy way to pack flavour onto roasted broccoli, and you don’t need a blender for it.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Cut the broccoli in half from lengthways, then cut each piece in half again so you have 4 big wedges. Repeat with the second broccoli head.
Place the broccoli onto a lined baking tray and drizzle with plenty of olive oil and rub in some salt and pepper. Cook for 20 mins on the middle shelf.

To make the caesar-ish sauce, finely chop ⅔ of the capers until they are almost minced. Add them to a bowl along with the rest of the sauce ingredients, including the juice of the lemon, and whisk until combined. Season well with plenty of salt and pepper. Adjust the flavour to your liking by adding more capers for texture, lemon juice for acidity or dijon or miso for more depth.

Toast the seeds in a small frying pan on medium heat for a couple of minutes until starting to brown. Add the sesame oil and olive oil and cook for another minute or two, then add the chilli flakes, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt and pepper.

To serve, spoon most of the sauce onto the bottom of a large plate and arrange the broccoli on top. Drizzle over the remaining sauce and the seedy drizzle and a few of the remaining capers, if you like.

name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Chestnut Crumble & Smoked Bacon
description: The best way to cook sprouts? Roasted in a hot oven and served with crispy bacon and crunchy breadcrumbs. Get stuck in.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C / 400°F. Halve the sprouts, finely chop the chestnuts, dice the bacon, and chop the fresh parsley.
Toss the sprouts with ½ the olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20-25 mins, until crispy and browned.
In a pan, cook the bacon until crispy. Drain on paper towels.
In the same pan, add the remaining olive oil, chestnuts and breadcrumbs. Cook until the breadcrumbs are golden brown. Stir in parsley and season with salt and pepper.
Toss the roasted sprouts with the chestnut crumble and crispy bacon. Serve hot and enjoy!

name: Roasted Butternut Ramen-ish
description: We spent a long time perfecting this broth. It is so savoury and rich. Topped with the charred veggies and a perfectly jammy egg.
instructions: Begin by preheating the oven to 180°C.
Peel both of your butternut squashes. Deseed and chop into chunks.

Add the squash into a roasting tray with a glug of vegetable oil, a big pinch of salt and half of your curry powder. Mix together and whack it into the oven for 40 mins until the squash is soft and tender. Stir halfway through.
At this point, remove 2/3’s of the butternut squash from the oven and pop the remaining 1/3 back in for another 15 minutes until it becomes browned and caramelised.

Add the 2/3’s of the squash into a blender along with the white miso, the rest of your curry powder, sesame oil, chilli oil and the vegetable stock pot. Add in a small splash of water and blitz until you have a fine butternut squash paste.

Finely chop the knob of ginger and grate the garlic cloves. Add the ginger and garlic into a deep saucepan with a splash of vegetable oil. Fry on low to medium heat. Just before it begins to colour add the butternut paste and cook for around a minute.
Just before the butternut paste starts to catch add in boiling water. Stir it together and bubble down on a medium heat until you have a thick broth consistency (looser than a soup).

Meanwhile, quarter your pak choi. Get a griddle pan on the heat and when hot add in the quartered pak choi and corn on cobs (if you do not have a griddle pan use a non-stick frying pan without oil). Griddle for 3-4 minutes on both sides until charred. Once cooked set aside.
Time to boil the eggs. Boil for 5 minutes, remove and add into a bowl of icy water to stop the eggs from cooking. Remove after a few minutes and peel away the shell.
Get your instant packet noodles and chuck them into the broth. Cook for 3-4 minutes.

Serving time. Into a bowl, add a handful of noodles and fill with ramen broth. Cut the corn off the cob (making sure it stays together) and add into the bowl along with the pak choi. Take the caramelised butternut squash from the oven and place that in the bowl. Chop your runny egg in half and add on top. Drizzle over with more chilli oil and enjoy!

name: Roasted Carrot & Date Salad
description: I’ve called this a salad but it’s quite wholesome and hearty with grains and roasted veggies, so it makes a great standalone dish as well as a side. Jordon x
keywords: Roasted carrot and date salad recipe
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Peel and chop the carrots, get them in a roasting tray with the oil and salt and into the oven.
Cook the giant couscous in salted water. Meanwhile mix the honey, vinegar and 2 tbsp of oil together in a small bowl.
After about 20 mins of roasting, pour that mix over the carrots and pop back into the oven for another 10 mins.
Tear up the dates and remove the stones, then slice the parsley. Add both to a big bowl along with a good pinch of salt, the chilli flakes, cumin and a big squeeze of lemon.
Then go in with the carrots and a splash of that glaze from the pan and give everything a good mix.
Stir the salt and ground coriander into the yoghurt and spread the mix over a big plate. Spoon over the carrots and couscous and finish with a good drizzle of olive oil.

name: Roasted Carrot Soup With Sesame Halloumi Croutons
description: Soup is a staple in our flat. It never fails to blow my mind the flavour you get out of roasted veg. Here, I’ve gone for classic carrot with some cumin, garlic and pomegranate molasses for a tangy kick. Plus there are spicy sesame cheese ‘croutons’ on top, because why not?
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C/200°C fan.
Peel your carrots (no need to do this if they’re really fresh), then chop into medium-sized chunks. Cut the onion into 8 wedges. Peel the garlic cloves, keeping them whole.

In a large roasting tray, toss the carrots, onion and garlic cloves with the olive oil, cumin seeds and plenty of seasoning, then spread into a single layer so that everything roasts evenly. Roast for 20–25 mins until soft and caramelised.

Once the veg is roasted, heat up the vegetable stock in a medium-sized saucepan. Add the roasted veg, then blitz with a handheld blender until smooth. If you like a thinner soup, add a splash of water. Season with 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses, and salt and pepper to taste.
Cut the halloumi into crouton-sized cubes (up to you how big or small you make these).

Heat a large frying pan over a medium–high heat and add the halloumi. Fry for 3–4 mins, turning regularly until the cubes are evenly golden and crisp on all sides, then drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses while still in the pan. Once the croutons are evenly glazed, scatter over the sesame seeds and chilli flakes, if using, so that each piece of cheese gets covered. Take off heat.

Reheat the soup and roughly chop the herbs (stalks and all). Divide the soup between two wide, shallow bowls. Top with the halloumi croutons, along with the herbs and a drizzle of pomegranate molasses. Serve.

name: Roasted Carrots Chimichurri Traybake
description: Everybody loves roasted carrots, and this veggie dish has them as its centrepiece with roasted radishes and a burst of green peas. Chimichurri brings the heat.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Zest a lemon, trim and halve the radish. Finely slice the garlic and trim the carrots.
Place the carrots and radishes into a large deep roasting tray with 2 tbsp of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then toss together. Roast for 30-35 mins until tender.

Meanwhile, make the chimichurri. Trim and finely dice the chilli, finely chop the parsley and mint. Add half of the parsley into a bowl with your mint, chilli, and the juice of both lemons. Add in 50ml of olive oil and season with salt, pepper, and sugar (if needed). Set aside.
Transfer the carrots onto a plate, cover, and set aside. Add the garlic, frozen peas and cooked brown rice to the tray and return to the oven for 3-5 mins, until piping hot.
Stir the lemon zest and remaining parsley through the rice, and serve onto plates. Share the carrots and drizzle the chimichurri all over.

name: Roasted Carrots with Tahini Yoghurt
description: Caramelised roasted carrots with a garlicky tahini yoghurt and a herby carrot top sauce. This one is packed with polyphenols for your gut microbes and would make an incredible side for any meal.
keywords: Roasted Carrots with Tahini Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Chop the tops off the carrots and slice off the top of the garlic head.
Place the carrots in a baking dish with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Add the garlic, cut side down, and roast for 20-30 mins until the carrots are tender and caramelised.
While the carrots are roasting, make the carrot top dressing. Finely chop the shallots and carrot tops and add to a bowl with the apple cider vinegar, a lug of olive oil and salt to taste.
In a separate bowl, mix together the yoghurt and tahini. Add the roasted garlic cloves, squeezing out the flesh, and season to taste.
To serve, spread the tahini yoghurt onto a plate and top with the roasted carrots. Drizzle over the herby carrot top dressing and enjoy!

name: Roasted Cauli & Cannellini Bean Soup
description: A beautiful plant-based soup that comes together in no time. It's perfect for batching at the weekend and enjoying for lunch throughout the week.
keywords: Roasted Cauliflower & Cannellini Bean Soup recipe
instructions: Pre-heat the oven to 190°C. Quarter your onions. Break the cauliflower into small and medium-sized florets and whack on a baking with the quartered onions. Slice the top off a head of garlic, wrap it in foil, and then add it to the tray as well. Season with salt, pepper, cumin, and a good drizzle of olive oil. Mix well to cover then roast for 30 mins, or until the cauliflower, onion and garlic are all tender and slightly browned.

Reserve a small handful of cauliflower for garnish, then tip the rest into a blender with the roasted onion. Squeeze out the roasted garlic cloves, then add the cannellini beans, the nutritional yeast, and half of the miso paste. Cover with vegetable stock. Blend until creamy and combined.

Pour into a saucepan to warm, seasoning to taste with salt and pepper. Add the butter and the rest of the miso paste, stirring well to melt. To serve, ladle the soup into bowls. Top with chopped chives and the reserved cauliflower. If you fancy it, feel free to drizzle each bowl with olive oil, vegan cream, and crispy chilli oil.

name: Roasted Cauliflower and Green Tahini Salad
description: A beautiful meal prep dish loaded with all the good stuff. Charred cauliflower and spiced chickpeas are gorgeous with the herby, nutty, vibrant dressing.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/400°F.
Cut your cauliflower into large wedges, keeping the stalk intact so they don't fall apart. Finely chop the cauliflower leaves.

Pop the cauliflower wedges on a baking tray along with a drained jar of chickpeas. Sprinkle on your cumin and smoked paprika. Drizzle on some olive oil and a pinch of salt, then rub it all in with your hands.
Roast for 30 mins.
Whilst your cauliflower roasts, finely chop your parsley and deseed your pomegranate.
Remove your roasting tray from the oven and flip your cauliflower wedges over. Tip your cauliflower leaves in. Toss to combine, then return to the oven to roast for 10 mins.

Spoon your tahini into a blender and squeeze in your lemon juice. Add your parsley, honey, a pinch of salt and 3 tbsp of water, then blend to combine. You may need to add more water to get it to drizzling consistency.

Tip your lentil pouches into a large bowl before throwing in your cauliflower leaves and chickpeas. Add most of your pomegranate seeds, olive oil and a pinch of salt, then toss to combine. Top with your roasted cauliflower. Drizzle with your green tahini sauce, then sprinkle with some more pomegranate seeds. Serve up and enjoy.

name: Roasted Cauliflower, Miso & Chestnut Soup
description: Caramelised cauliflower, miso and chestnuts make up this rich and creamy, umami soup that’s easy enough to whip up on a weeknight but is also perfect for a special occasion.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Cut the cauliflower into large pieces and place on a baking tray. Add the garlic cloves in their skins to the tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20-25 mins until golden and starting to char and the garlic is soft.

When cool enough to handle, remove the skins from the garlic cloves. Add the cooked cauliflower to a large blender along with the peeled garlic, white miso, lesser amount of oat milk, chestnuts, nutritional yeast, olive oil, water and stock cube. Blend until smooth and season well with salt and pepper. Alternatively, place everything into a large pot and use an immersion blender to blend until smooth.
Heat the soup up on the stove in a large pot and add more oat milk or water to thin down if needed.
Toast the bread and rub it with garlic cloves and then drizzle with a little olive oil to make garlic bread. Top with vegan cream cheese and a drizzle of crispy chilli oil, if you like.

name: Roasted Chicken & Peppers with Parsley Rice
description: Insane burritos made with our leftover Roast Chicken & Peppers batch. A great weeknight staple.
keywords: Roasted Chicken & Peppers with Parsley Rice recipe
Roasted Chicken & Peppers with Parsley Rice
instructions: Make the Roast Chicken & Peppers.
Finely chop the parsley.
Shred the leftover chicken and peppers. Warm gently in a saucepan with a splash of water until piping hot.
Stir the chopped parsley and olive oil through the hot rice. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Spoon the parsley rice into bowls and top with the chicken and pepper mixture.

name: Roasted Chipotle Pepper Soup
description: This soup is sunshine in a bowl. Loaded up with smoky peppers and spices, then topped with feta and coriander. Any excuse to use crisps as a garnish. Sophie x
keywords: bell pepper soup roast veg soup
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/400°F.
Start by prepping your veg. Core, deseed and halve your peppers. Peel and quarter your red onions and halve your tomatoes.

Toss the peppers, onion and tomatoes in a large roasting tin with your unpeeled garlic cloves, chilli, chipotle chilli flakes and cumin seeds in the tin. Drizzle it with olive oil and a generous pinch of salt, then roast for 45 mins.
Pour your roasted vegetables into a large pot and add your vegetable stock. Blitz with a stick blender until really smooth, then bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour your soup into bowls and sprinkle with coriander and a crumbling of feta. Serve up with tortilla chips and enjoy.

name: Roasted Chorizo, Tomato & Garlic Soup
description: The crispy chorizo bits scattered on the end make this dish. Sack off the ready made supermarket soup and make your own. It's so easy, you won't regret it.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.

Grab a baking tray. Add tomatoes, roughly chopped peppers, a whole bulb of garlic and a heaped tablespoon of rosemary leaves along with a glug of oil. Season with salt and pepper and place in the oven for 30 minutes.

Crumble your chorizo into a frying pan. Cook over a medium heat until crispy. Remove the chorizo and save for the end. Pour the chorizo fat into your roasting vegetable tray, making sure everything is coated. Place the tray back in the oven for another 15 minutes.
When the vegetables are cooked and caramelised, remove the tray from the oven.
Pour the vegetables into a large saucepan. Add 500ml of chicken stock, a large handful of basil leaves and red wine vinegar. Bring to a simmer and blitz the soup with a hand blender until smooth.
Serve with the crispy chorizo scattered on top and a nice hunk of crusty bread.

name: Roasted Garlic Baba Ganoush
description: This is our ultimate Baba recipe, with the addition of basil at the end. Not traditional, we know, but lifts it perfectly. Give it a go.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Slice the top off the garlic bulb, drizzle with oil and wrap in tin foil. Add the garlic bulb to a tray and place in the oven for 15 mins. Meanwhile, chop your pitta into triangles and add to a bowl. Drizzle with half the olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Add the pitta to the tray alongside the garlic and return to the oven for another 15 mins. Then remove from the oven and set aside, until the garlic is cool enough to handle.

As the pitta is cooking, char the aubergines directly over a flame on a gas stove. As the aubergines begin to cook, the skin will start to blacken. Once the skin is completely charred and black, remove the aubergines and place in a bowl before covering with cling film. They will steam, allowing you to be able to peel the blackened skin off easier. Leave to cool until you are able to safely handle, then remove the charred skin. Then chop off the ends.

Add the aubergine flesh to a bowl, then squeeze in the garlic bulb. Combine the aubergine and garlic with a fork, mashing it up, before adding the tahini, lemon juice and the rest of the olive oil. Mix well and season with salt and pepper.
Roughly chop up the basil and sprinkle over the Baba Ganoush along with a healthy drizzle of olive oil, if you like. Serve with the pitta and get stuck in.

name: Roasted Garlic Chicken Pie
description: If you're looking for a rich, winter-warmer of a dish, this is the one for you. The sauce is flavoured with lots of herbs that pair wonderfully with the garlic.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C/356°F. Wrap your bulbs of garlic in baking parchment, then place on a baking tray and roast for 45 mins. Set aside until cool enough to handle. Squeeze your garlic out of it’s skin by pressing a knife down on it. Discard the skins, saving the caramelised flesh until later.

Take two thirds of your pastry and roll it out to 2mm thickness. Line your pie dish with your pastry, folding it into the edges on the base and pressing into the sides so that it sits snug against the sides of the dish. Line with a square of parchment and fill with baking beans, uncooked rice or uncooked pulses.

Pop your pie dish in the oven for 10 mins (still at 180°C/356°F) until your sides have puffed up and crisped slightly. Carefully remove your baking beans and parchment, then whack in the oven for 5 minutes longer until you have a crisp base. Turn up the oven to 190°C/374°F.
Chop your chicken into 2 inch pieces. Slice your onion.

Heat a large saute pan over a medium heat. Add a little olive oil, then tip in half of your chicken thigh chunks. Season with salt and pepper and fry over a high heat for 5 mins until it has gone nice and golden. Remove from the pan, then repeat with your remaining chicken.

In your empty pan, add your butter and let it melt. Tip your onions into the same pan along with your rosemary and thyme sprigs. Cook over a medium heat for about 6 mins until totally soft. Add your pancetta and turn up the heat, frying until your pancetta is crispy and the onions are caramelised.

Add your flour and cook out for 2 mins until it starts to smell biscuity, then gradually pour in your stock in small increments, whisking all the while to ensure you have a smooth sauce. Once your stock has finished, do the same with your milk. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 2 mins until your sauce has thickened.
Add your chicken and roasted garlic to the pan along with some salt and pepper, and stir to combine. Simmer for 2 mins.

Pour your filling into a pie dish and top with your pastry. Beat your egg and brush this over the top of your pastry. Place on a baking sheet in the oven and bake for 25-30 mins. Serve up by itself, or alongside some mash and greens.

name: Roasted Garlic Chicken Soup
description: The most nourishing chicken broth. Loaded up with roasted garlic and all the herbs, this is just the ticket to get you through the winter months.
instructions: Roast the chicken for 1 hour at 190°C.
Allow to cool, then remove all of the flesh from your bones and set aside.
Halve one of your onions and slice half your bulb of fennel into wedges. Pop your chicken carcass back in the oven along with your cut onion and fennel for 30 mins until browned.

Add the carcass to a large pot along with your roasted veg, celery stick, the stalks of your thyme and the stems from your parsley. Fill with water until the carcass is totally covered in the pot. Bring to a boil, then gently simmer for 2 hours. Strain the lumps out of the liquid.
Wrap two bulbs of garlic in kitchen foil and roast for 45 mins at 180°C until totally soft.
Meanwhile, finely dice your remaining onion and fennel. Finely chop your remaining cloves of garlic.
Fry the veg gently for 20 mins in olive oil with thyme leaves until softened and starting to caramelise. Add your chopped garlic and cook out for 2 mins.
Add 1l of your chicken stock and roasted garlic to the pot and bring to a simmer. Blitz your mixture with a stick blender.
Shred 400g of your chicken with two forks - save the rest for other meals.
Add your shredded chicken to the pan along with chopped parsley and tarragon. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Finish with crème fraîche, a little more parsley and fennel fronds, then serve and enjoy.

name: Roasted Garlic Dauphinoise Potatoes
description: Dauphinoise potatoes are one of the more luxurious sides out there. Flavoured with sweet roasted garlic for a glorious spin on a classic.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C.
Wrap your garlic bulbs in kitchen foil, then place them in the oven and cook for 40 mins.
Peel your potatoes.

Using a mandolin, or a very sharp knife, carefully slice your
potatoes into 2mm thin rounds.

Pour your double cream and milk into a saucepan. Season
generously with salt and pepper.

Once your garlic is cool enough to handle, squeeze out the
caramelised pulp. Discard the skin.

Add your garlic pulp to the cream pan along with a generous grating of nutmeg.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.

Tip your potatoes into the pan and cook for 10 mins until they
are just tender. Check the seasoning and adjust if necessary.

Pour your mixture into a rectangular baking dish. Cover with foil
and bake for 45 mins.
Grate your Gruyère.

Remove your dish from the oven and turn the temperature up to
200°C.

Sprinkle your cheese over the top. Bake for another 15 mins until
melted.
Carve into squares and serve.

name: Roasted Grapes On Toast
description: Roasting grapes might sound a bit odd but trust us: it really works. The natural sweetness of the grapes really shines in this plant-based recipe.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Behead the bulb of garlic, add a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of sea salt, wrap in foil and roast in the oven for 40 mins.

Add all the grapes, thyme, and red chilli to a baking tray and toss to coat in the balsamic oil, agave, and olive oil. Add to the oven for 20 mins into the same roasting tin as the garlic, bake till sticky and caramelised. Allow the grapes to cool for 10 mins.
Zhuzh up the cream cheese by adding in finely chopped parsley and chives with a squeeze of lemon juice.
Toast the sourdough bread and spread the roasted garlic on it before layering it with a generous spread of vegan cream cheese. Finally, top your slices of toast with the sticky roasted grapes. Enjoy.

name: Roasted Halloumi & Aubergine Traybake
description: Traybakes are so simple to make, but the garnishes here make it look like a showstopper and boost the number of plants in the dish, giving you plenty of polyphenols and a boost of fibre.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan and line two large baking trays with baking parchment.
Drain and pat dry the chickpeas. Cut the peppers into 2cm chunks. Cut the halloumi into 1cm cubes.

Put the chickpeas, tomatoes, peppers, halloumi and unpeeled garlic cloves on one tray with ¾ each of the cumin, ground coriander and chilli powder. Season with salt and pepper and drizzle with ¾ of the olive oil. Toss to coat.

Cut each aubergine in half lengthways and score a 2cm deep criss-cross pattern into the flesh of each one. Sprinkle with the remaining ground spices and drizzle with the remaining olive oil, season and place on the other baking tray. Place both trays in the oven for 40 mins.
While the veg cooks, roughly chop the coriander and thinly slice the spring onions for garnish.
Mix the tahini, kefir and sumac in a bowl and season. When the vegetables are ready, squeeze the garlic from the skins into the sauce, mash them in and stir to combine.

Transfer the chickpeas, halloumi and veg to a serving dish and stir in ¾ of the fresh coriander. Place the aubergine halves on top and scatter with the remaining coriander, spring onions, pomegranate seeds, lime juice and the sauce.

name: Roasted Halloumi and Pickled Citrus Grain Salad
description: A vibrant and refreshing grain salad featuring roasted halloumi, pickled citrus, and a creamy kefir dressing. Packed with fresh herbs and textures, it’s a perfect light meal or side dish.
keywords: Roasted Halloumi and Pickled Citrus Grain Salad
Roasted Halloumi and Pickled Citrus Grain Salad recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan.

Time to get prepared. Tear the halloumi into bite-sized shards. Dice the cucumber into 2cm-sized pieces. Thinly slice the shallots, segment your oranges and squeeze the juices remaining from the orange remnants into a bowl. Pick the leaves from the parsley and mint.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Place the cherry tomatoes on the tray and top with the torn halloumi. Roast for 10-15 minutes until the halloumi is golden and the tomatoes are tender.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, toss the shallots and orange segments with the reserved orange juice and lime juice. Let sit to pickle.
Add the parsley stems to a blender. Set the parsley and mint leaves aside.
For the dressing, add the mint, coriander, lime zest, lime juice, kefir, olive oil, and honey to the blender. Blend until smooth. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Reheat the grains and divide them into serving boxes.
Toss the pickled orange and shallots with the cucumber, roasted halloumi and tomatoes, then spoon over the grains.
Once cooled, scatter over the parsley and mint leaves. Drizzle with the kefir dressing and refrigerate until needed. No need to reheat before serving.

name: Roasted Hispi Cabbage With Harissa Dressing & Pangrattato
description: Grab a jar of harissa along with some dijon mustard, aioli, and whatever you fancy to make a quick and zingy dressing. Perfect slathered onto charred wedges of hispi cabbage.
keywords: Roasted Hispi Cabbage With Harissa Dressing & Pangrattato
Roasted Hispi Cabbage With Harissa Dressing & Pangrattato recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Cut your cabbage into quarters and rub with olive oil and plenty of salt.

Heat an oven proof pan over a high heat and burn the cut sides of your cabbage. Chuck in the butter, a smashed garlic clove and sherry vinegar. Roll the cabbage around in the butter and stick the whole pan into the oven for 10-15 mins.
Grab your jar of harissa and add the remaining vinegar. Give it a good shake.
Meanwhile, toast off the breadcrumbs with a glug of oil in a pan over a medium heat.
Finely chop the parsley and mix through the toasted breadcrumbs.

Pull the hispi cabbage out of the oven and pour the butter and vinegar mixture into the jar of harissa. Top with lid and give it a good shake, add a splash more vinegar or water if it needs loosening up.
Transfer the hispi to a serving platter and cover in the warm dressing. Top with the breadcrumbs.

name: Roasted Marinated Peppers With Seedy Crusted Feta
description: Sweet roasted peppers and a block of salty, seed-topped feta? Go on then.
keywords: Roasted Marinated Peppers With Seedy Crusted Feta
instructions: Preheat the grill to max.

Toss the peppers with oil and salt and add to a roasting tin. Slide under the grill
to blister and char for 6-7 mins, turning regularly until they’re very blackened.
Pull out and cover with an upturned tray or add to a covered bowl, to steam
through.

Grab a large mixing bowl and add 5 tbsp of olive oil with the red wine vinegar.
Grate in the garlic cloves. Then thinly slice the red onion and chop the cucumber into half moons, add both into the bowl. Scatter
in the herbs. Season with salt and pepper.

Peel the blackened skin from the peppers and toss through the herby dressing.
Set aside to marinate.

Tip the seeds out onto a plate and season with pepper. Unpack the feta and dip
each side in the seeds, they will stick naturally to the cheese.

Drizzle with olive oil and slide under the hot grill for 3-4 mins until golden
brown.

Spread the peppers over a large serving plate and serve the feta in the middle.
Slice up some crusty bread to eat alongside.
Get stuck in.

name: Roasted Miso Veg with Marinated Tofu
description: This is one of those dishes that can be served hot or cold, by itself or with something carby. Its versatility and ease make it the perfect weeknight dish. Z x
instructions: Heat your oven to 220°C / fan 200°C.

Pat the tofu dry with kitchen towel then cut into 2cm cubes. Place in a bowl, season lightly with salt and pepper, drizzle with vegetable oil and toss to coat. Arrange in a single layer in a large roasting tin.
Quarter the tenderstem broccoli. Remove the root and quarter the pak choi. Core the bell peppers and cut into medium-sized chunks. Quarter the spring onions.
Place the veg in a separate large baking tray. Drizzle with vegetable oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Arrange in a single layer; some overlap is ok.
Roast the tofu and veg for 15 minutes, or until the tofu is golden and the veg is cooked and charred in places.

Meanwhile, crush the sesame seeds with a pestle and mortar. Add the apple cider vinegar, honey and white miso paste, along with the juice of the lime and 4 tablespoons of vegetable oil. Whisk until well-combined.
Thinly slice the red chilli and pick the coriander leaves.
To assemble the dish, place the tofu and veg in a large bowl. Top with the red chilli, coriander leaves and as much of dressing as you'd like. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Panzanella Traybake
description: A new take on the classic Panzanella - it works so well as a bake. The croutons are crunchy and caramelised. The perfect contrast to the melted mozzarella.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.

Chop the aubergine and peppers into 2-3cm chunks, slice the red onions in 1cm slices. Pile into the largest roasting tray you have and season well with salt and black pepper. Drizzle over a good glug of olive oil, toss everything together then spread into a single layer. Roast in the oven for 20 minutes.
After 20 minutes, chuck the cherry tomatoes into the pan. Return to the oven for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, tear the bread into large croutons, toss with some olive oil and sea salt.
Scatter the croutons on top and return to the oven for 10-15 minutes, until the vegetables are cooked through and the croutons are crisp.
Toss the basil, balsamic vinegar and some olive oil through the salad and share between plates. Tear the mozzarella and top the salads with.

name: Roasted Pepper & Anchovy Rigatoni
description: When the weather's hot, you need meals that involve minimal cooking. Jarred peppers, anchovies and capers bring beautiful tang to this pesto sauce, and keep you cool.
instructions: Get some salted water on to boil for your pasta.
Toast your walnuts in a frying pan.

Tip your walnuts into a blender along with your jarred red peppers, basil, anchovies, capers, parmesan and red wine vinegar. Add salt, pepper and a generous glug of olive oil. Blend until smooth to make the pesto.
Cook your pasta 2 mins less than the packet tells you to - this will ensure it’s nice and al dente. Drain in a colander, reserving a mugful of pasta water.
Add your pasta back into the pan and add your pesto and pasta water. Stir to combine, and check the seasoning - it may need more parmesan, olive oil, salt or pepper.
Spoon your pasta into bowls. Sprinkle with parmesan, drizzle with olive oil and twist over a little black pepper. Serve and enjoy!

name: Roasted Pepper & Harissa Bean Stew
description: Stuffed with roasted red peppers, cannelinni beans and a good ol' heaping tablespoon or two of harissa, here's a simple stew that's ready in under 25 mins.
instructions: Chop the carrots and courgette into 2cm pieces. Peel and roughly chop the garlic. Finely chop the parsley stalks and set aside the leaves. Drain and slice the roasted peppers.

Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan set over a medium heat. Add the carrot and parsley stalks with a big pinch of salt and fry for 8 mins until tender. Add the garlic and courgette, and cook for another 2 mins until aromatic.
Add the cannellini beans and their juices along with the harissa, tinned tomatoes and roasted peppers. Bring to the boil then reduce to a simmer for 10 mins. Stir through the fresh parsley leaves.
Heat the pitta following packet instructions.
To serve, divide the beans between bowls and top with a swoosh of yoghurt and a drizzle of olive oil. Finish with any remaining parsley. Serve with the warm pitta.

name: Roasted Peppers
description: These perfect roasted peppers are ideal for meal prep. Combine them with your choice of protein, carb and topping to create a gorgeous meal-prep dish.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C.
Place the whole Romano peppers on a baking tray, drizzle over a good glug of olive oil and roast for 15 mins.
Pair your peppers up with the rest of your lunch components.

name: Roasted Peppers with Spinach Yoghurt, Fried Onions and Walnuts
description: A delicious and wholesome centrepiece, perfect for a dinner party if you wanna wow your guests. All the flavours, this one really hits the spot. Xien x
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C.
Place the peppers on a baking tray, drizzle over a good glug of olive oil and roast for 15 mins.
To make your spinach yoghurt, blanch the spinach in a pot of boiling water, then drain and set aside. Once cool, squeeze out as much water as possible. Chop into small chunks and set aside.
Mince a clove of garlic and fry in a pan with a glug of olive oil, then add your spinach to the pan. Fry for just a few mins then take it off the hob.
Toast your walnuts then roughly chop them.
Mince another clove of garlic and mix it in with the yoghurt and fried spinach. Add 80% of your walnuts, squeeze in ½ a juice of lemon, season with salt and pepper and give it a good mix.
Roughly chop your parsley, coriander and dill. Finely slice your spring onions and pop them all into a bowl with a glug of olive oil.
Slice your onion and pop them into a bowl with a good glug of olive oil. Microwave for 4 mins at medium heat until crispy.

Now it's plate up time. Smoosh your spinach yoghurt on a big plate, add your roasted peppers, top with the crispy onions, drizzle over the herby oil and sprinkle the remaining walnuts on top. Tuck in.

name: Roasted Potato Salad With Apricots, Fennel & Veggie Sausages
description: This is an extra special take on the classic (but boring, sorry) potato salad. Fresh fennel and roasted apricots take things up a gear or two.
instructions: Preheat the oven to fan 190°C. Put the garlic bulb on a square of foil with a drizzle of oil, then scrunch the foil to close.
Pick the fennel fronds and thinly slice the fennel – use a mandoline if you have one. Halve and pit the apricots, then chop them into 1cm chunks. Halve the potatoes. Pick the basil leaves.

Put the apricots, potatoes and foil-wrapped garlic bulb onto a large baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and your baharat spice mix. Place the veggie sausages on top and bake for 30 mins, until the sausages are cooked through.
Meanwhile, zest 1 lemon into a large mixing bowl. Squeeze the juice from all the lemons and add 30ml of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Once the sausages and veg are cooked, squeeze the roasted garlic into the lemon dressing. Mix together, then toss the potatoes, apricots, fennel and half the basil leaves through.
Serve the warm potato salad with the sausages. Finish with a scattering of fennel fronds and tear over the remaining basil leaves.

name: Roasted Purple Sprouting Broccoli with Puy Lentils and Tahini Dressing
description: This salad is full of vibrant green veg and Merchant Gourmet Puy Lentils. Tossed with a creamy tahini and lemon dressing, it's ideal for a quick lunch.
keywords: Roasted Purple Sprouting With Puy Lentils and Tahini Dressing recipes
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Trim the end of the purple sprouting broccoli, then halve widthways and any thicker stems lengthways.
Place in a roasting pan, drizzle generously with olive oil and salt, toss well and place into the oven for about 15 mins, turning once, until cooked through with some good colour.
Meanwhile, heat a splash of olive oil in a large pan over a high heat, add the kale and stir fry for a few mins until charred and crispy. Set aside.
Add the lentils to a bowl along with the juice and zest of half a lemon, a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Mix well
In a small bowl mix the tahini with the juice of a lemon, a glug of olive oil and a splash of water. It should be creamy and emulsified but not too thick, the consistency of double cream.
Once cooled, add the broccoli, kale, and lentils to a bowl, pour in the dressing and toss well.
Plate up and top with a generous sprinkle of chopped mint and a big spoon of pomegranate seeds.

name: Roasted Rack of Lamb with Garlicky Yoghurt
description: This rack of lamb has crispy fat and perfectly pink meat. Contrast that with the cooling, garlicky yoghurt and you’ve got an absolute winner. It’s our ultimate rack of lamb recipe – perfect for a special occasion. Follow this step-by-step guide for a flawless rack of lamb.
keywords: how to make rack of lamb recipe
instructions: Remove the lamb from the fridge 1 hour before beginning cooking.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Use a sharp knife to lightly score the fat of the lamb in a 1cm diamond pattern. Drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil, rub all over and season really well with salt and pepper.

Put a frying pan over a medium-high heat and scatter the cumin seeds into the pan. Toast for 1 minute until smelling amazing, then tip into a pestle and mortar. Roughly grind and then tip onto a plate. Put the pan back over the heat and lay the lamb rack into the pan, onto its scored fat side. Fry for 3-4 mins, using tongs to lift and check that the fat is super golden and crisp. Use the tongs to hold the rack on each of its two ends for 30 seconds to seal, then remove from the pan and roll and coat in the ground cumin seeds.
Move the lamb rack into a small roasting tin, fat side up and roast for 20 mins.

Meanwhile, make the garlicky yoghurt. Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl and zest in the lemon. Cut the lemon in half then squeeze in the juice from ½. Peel the garlic clove and use the same grater to grate the garlic into the yoghurt. Season with salt and pepper, then add 4-5 tbsp of cold water and mix well.
Remove the lamb from the oven and move onto a plate. Cover loosely with foil and rest for 15 mins.

Spoon the yoghurt onto a serving platter, then slice the lamb between the bones into cutlets and place them onto the yoghurt. Scatter with parsley leaves and sprinkle with a little more flaky salt to serve.

name: Roasted Red Onions with White Beans & Fried Breadcrumbs
description: Hands down one of my favourite ways to cook with red onions. Roasting the sliced onions hard until they colour with natural sugars, then hitting the softened onions straight out of the oven with plenty of red wine vinegar is a winning way to cook them.
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C and line a large baking tray with baking parchment.
Peel the onions and slice into 1cm-thick rings. Arrange the onions in a single layer on the baking tray, then add 2/5 of your olive oil to coat, plus a good pinch of salt and plenty of black pepper.

Bake for 30 mins until softened and bronzed, removing from the oven after 15 mins to stir through the dried oregano (flip the onions over at this stage). If you want yet more colour, grill under a high heat for 5-10 mins to speed the process up. Remove from the oven and immediately splash all over with the vinegar.
Meanwhile, cook the breadcrumbs in ⅖ of your olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat for 3-4 mins until toasted and golden brown. Set aside on a plate lined with kitchen paper.
Drain the beans, then finely chop the parsley, chilli and anchovies. Stir all three through the beans, plus the remainder of your olive oil.
Add the onions and beans to a large serving plate, adding extra vinegar if you like. Roughly chop the oregano and sprinkle all over, adding a generous spoon of fried breadcrumbs to serve.

name: Roasted Spiced Aubergine, Giant Couscous & Yoghurt Sauce
description: This dish is inspired by Palestinian Maftoul – giant couscous cooked in spiced stock with onion and peppers, roasted aubergine and tangy yoghurt sauce.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Cut the aubergines into quarters, lengthwise. Place them onto a baking tray and drizzle with 2 tbsp of olive oil. Season with salt and rub to coat evenly. Roast for 20-25 mins until softened, golden brown and starting to char.

Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice the onions. Remove the stem and chop the peppers into 1cm chunks. In a large saucepan on medium heat, add 3 tbsp of olive oil. Once hot, add the onions and peppers, cook until softened and starting to colour, 10-15 mins.

Stir the ras el hanout through the vegetables and cook for 30 secs. Pour the stock in and bring to the boil. Add the giant couscous/orzo into a sieve and give it a rinse. Once boiling, add the giant couscous/orzo and boil, stirring frequently, according to package instructions (top it up with more stock or water if it's evaporating too quickly).

Add the Greek yoghurt into a small bowl with the tahini and the juice of 1 lemon. Stir until it comes together and season with salt and pepper. If it’s too thick, add 1 tbsp of water at a time until smooth. The sauce should be a little looser than Greek yoghurt. Set aside.
Reserve a few parsley leaves and finely chop the rest (stalks and all). Zest a quarter of the remaining lemon.
Once the couscous is cooked, take it off the heat, taste and season with salt. Stir through the chopped parsley and lemon zest.
Spoon the couscous onto plates and top with the roasted aubergine. Drizzle with the yoghurt sauce. Finish with a wedge of lemon and a scattering of the reserved parsley leaves.

name: Roasted Squash & Feta Hand Pie
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

What's hand pie? A fancy word for a pasty. We picked up everything for these perfect pastries at Aldi.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Peel the butternut squash and dice into 2cm cubes. Place in a roasting tin with the ground cumin and cinnamon. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat.
Slice the top of the garlic bulb. Nestle the bulb into the butternut squash and drizzle with olive oil.
Roast for 40 mins, or until the butternut and garlic are tender. Squeeze the garlic into the butternut and mash it all together. Leave to cool.

Crumble in the feta and pick the thyme and add them, too. Mix to combine. Divide the puff pastry sheet into 4. Fill with a few spoonfuls each. Place another sheet of puff pastry on top to cover, press down then cut and seal the sides with a fork.
Brush with egg wash then bake for 15 mins or until nice and golden.

name: Roasted Squash & Mozzarella Salad
description: This seasonal winter salad satisfies all the cravings. It’s hearty, healthy and nutritious.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Remove the mozzarella from the fridge and allow it to come to room temperature.

Thoroughly wash the butternut squash and dry it. Trim, halve and scoop out the seeds. Slice into 1cm-thick half-moons. Place onto a large baking tray, or two separate trays, season with salt and drizzle with olive oil. Roast for 25-30 mins until caramelised.

Meanwhile, roughly chop the hazelnuts and pick the sage leaves. Tip the nuts into a frying pan with the olive oil. Set the pan over medium heat, once hot, toast the hazelnuts for 2-4 mins until golden brown. When the nuts are almost golden, add the sage leaves and fry for 30-45 seconds until crisp. Transfer both onto kitchen paper to drain, and pour the oil into a bowl to cool down.

Discard any thick and tough kale stems. Season the kale with salt and massage until wilted. Once the oil has cooled down, stir through the balsamic vinegar and season with salt and pepper. Tear the mozzarella into chunks.
Scatter the kale onto a sharing platter, top with the squash and torn mozzarella. Drizzle over the balsamic dressing and sprinkle over the hazelnuts and crispy sage.

name: Roasted Squash with Crispy Grains & Cannellini Hummus
description: This roasted squash with olive salsa, white bean hummus and crispy grains packs in plenty of fibre and over 10 plants per plate, making it a feast for you and your gut microbes.
keywords: Roasted Squash with Crispy Grains & Cannellini Hummus Recipe
Roasted Squash with Crispy Grains & Cannellini Hummus
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C.
If using a small butternut squash, halve it lengthways and remove the seeds. If using a large squash, halve it and remove the seeds then cut it into large chunks.
Get the squash on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil and a pinch of salt. Add the unpeeled garlic cloves to the tray.

Roast for around 20-30 mins or until the squash is fork tender then remove the garlic cloves and sprinkle over the pre-cooked grains. Place back in the oven for another 10 mins or so, until the squash is completely tender and the grains are crispy.

Meanwhile, squeeze the flesh from the roasted garlic cloves into a blender and add the drained beans, tahini, juice of the lemon and a pinch of salt. Blitz with a couple of ice cubes until it’s completely smooth. Taste to check the seasoning and set aside.
Chop the olives and parsley together then add to a bowl with the olive oil and apple cider vinegar. Mix to combine and season to taste.
Assemble your plate with the hummus on the bottom, topped with the roasted squash, crispy grains, olive salsa and some sliced red chilli.

name: Roasted Squash with Zhoug
description: Zhoug is a spicy condiment from Yemen which comes in different varieties. This is a green version which contrasts beautifully with the sweet roasted squash.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°c
Wash, peel and slice the butternut squash into roughly 2cm thick slices. Toss in a roasting tray with a good drizzle of olive oil and a big pinch of salt and roast for about 40 mins until golden.
In a bowl, mix together the greek yogurt and goat's cheese with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon. Set aside.
Grate the garlic into a blender before chopping up your chilli and adding to the blender along with the coriander, cardamom, cumin and chilli flakes.
Squeeze in the juice of a lemon and add about 100ml of olive oil. Whizz until not quite smooth.

Once the squash is cooked, remove and allow to cool slightly. Spread the yoghurt and goat's cheese mixture across a large plate and then pile up the squash, drizzling each layer with some of the zhoug.
Roughly chop and toast the hazelnuts, sprinkle over the top and finish with the rest of the zhoug and some more chilli flakes, if you like.

name: Roasted Squash, Fennel and Chickpea Salad
description: A riff on a recipe by Diana Henry I'm very fond of. Warm spiced veg with a creamy tahini and date drizzle is out of this world. The perfect winter salad. Soph x
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/400°F.
Chop your squash into crescent moons 1cm thick - no need to peel it. Cut your fennel and red onions into chunky slices, saving your fennel tops for later.

Place them all on a large baking tray and add your cumin, 1 tsp of Aleppo chilli flakes, a good pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Toss to combine, then roast for 35 mins until tender and caramelised.
Slice your fennel tops into thin rounds and place in a small bowl. Add your white wine vinegar, sugar and 50ml of boiling water. Give it a good stir and set aside until later.
Roughly chop your parsley.

Drain your chickpeas and pop them onto a baking tray with your remaining Aleppo chilli flakes, za’atar, a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Toss to combine, and pop in the oven for the final 10 minutes of the other veg’s roasting time.

Place your tahini and yoghurt in a medium sized bowl. Add the zest and juice from your lemon along with 70ml water and a pinch of salt. Whisk until you have a smooth, drizzle-able sauce, adding more water if needed.
Tip your pine nuts into a dry frying pan set over a medium heat and fry for 5 minutes until golden and toasted. Tip out onto a plate to cool.

Assembly time. Pour your chickpeas onto a large platter and arrange your roasted veg on top. Drizzle with a generous amount of your tahini dressing and your date syrup. Drain your pickled fennel tops and scatter them on top, along with your chopped parsley and pine nuts. Serve whilst still warm with a pile of flatbreads.

name: Roasted Squash, Halloumi & Wild Rice Bowl
description: Salty halloumi, sweet roasted squash served on top of wild rice and finished with a nutty tahini drizzle, it doesn't get any better.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Peel and slice up the butternut into thin slices. Toss in a tbsp of olive oil, a pinch of salt and thyme leaves. Bake for 20-30 mins until tender, turning halfway through.

Split the halloumi down the crease and chop into 2cm chunks. When theres 10 mins left for the squash, add the halloumi to the tray, drizzle with some oil and cook for the remainder of the time, until golden.

Zest the lemon and pour the tahini into a bowl. Add a squeeze of lemon juice and season with salt and a touch of honey or sugar. Stir together, adding 1 tbsp of cold water at a time, until you get a velvety, creamy consistency.
