Reheat the rice and share between bowls. Top with the squash and halloumi, drizzle over the tahini and finish with a scattering of pomegranate seeds and dill.

name: Roasted Summer Fruit Frozen Yoghurt Pops
description: Roasting fruit is a great way to use up any that’s about to go off, especially useful in the summer glut of strawberries and cherries.
keywords: Roasted Summer Fruit Frozen Yoghurt Pops
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.

Wash the fruit well. Remove the tips of the strawberries and cut into halves (or quarters if they are very big). Cut the cherries in half and remove the stones. Lay all of the fruit onto a lined baking tray and drizzle over 2 tsp of the maple syrup or agave and the balsamic vinegar.
Toss well to combine and roast for 25 mins, tossing halfway. They should have released a lot of their juices and become concentrated in flavour.
Use a fork to mash the fruit together and break it up. You can completely break up the strawberries and leave most of the cherries whole as they give a lovely texture.
While the fruit is cooking, mix the maple syrup or agave into the yoghurt.
To prepare the ice pops with ice pop moulds, alternate filling them with the fruit and the yoghurt. If you are using granola, add a little to the base or the top.
To prepare in yoghurt pots, use the same steps as above and place a teaspoon or small wooden stick into each pot. It’s ok if it rests on the side.

To prepare in a small cake tin, add dollops of yoghurt and berries and keep going until you have used up all of your ingredients. Sprinkle over some granola, if using. Cover the top with silver foil and poke holes into it where you want to add the sticks and carefully poke them through.
Freeze for at least 3 hours.

Run hot water over the moulds or yoghurt pots to release. Or run the sides of the tin under hot water to release the yoghurt from the tin (take care not to get water inside. Allow to thaw for 5-6 mins before cutting. Pop any pops you won’t be eating straight away into a Tupperware and back into the freezer.

name: Roasted Tomato & Butternut Dal Traybake
description: A rich, roast-y traybake dal with caramelised tomatoes, creamy coconut and tender squash. Big flavour, minimal faff.
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsHeat the oven to 180°C fan.
Peel the butternut squash, remove the seeds and cut it into bite-sized cubes. Halve the tomatoes and cherry tomatoes. Peel and finely slice the red onion and garlic.

Tip the squash, tomatoes, onion and garlic into a large roasting tin. Add the curry powder, turmeric, a good drizzle of olive oil and a big pinch of salt. Toss everything together and roast for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse the lentils.
After 30 mins, take the tray out of the oven. Stir in the lentils and coconut milk, then return to the oven for 15 mins, until bubbling and golden at the edges.
Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Serve with a dollop of yoghurt, a spoonful of mango chutney, and fresh coriander. Warm flatbreads or rice on the side are essential for mopping it all up.

name: Roasted Tomato & Coconut Dal
description: Give your Coconut Dal batch a glow-up with jammy roast tomatoes, punchy lime chutney and crispy onions on top. Scoop it all up with hot naan.
instructions: Make the Coconut Dal batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 220°C.
Tip the cherry tomatoes onto a tray, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 10–15 mins until soft, jammy and starting to burst.
Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the stems.
Tip the dal into a saucepan and stir through the coriander stems. Warm over a medium heat until piping hot, loosening with a splash of water if it’s thickened in the fridge.
Pop the naan into the oven for the final 2 mins of the tomato roasting time to warm through.
Spoon the dal into bowls, then top with the roast tomatoes, spoonfuls of lime chutney, a scattering of crispy fried onions and coriander leaves. Serve with the warm naan for scooping.

name: Roasted Tomato & Pepper Soup with a Giant Cheese Pretzel Crouton
description: Tomato soup and grilled cheese are a match made in heaven. Here’s our twist on the classic combo, with added roasted red peppers and Parmesan-crusted pretzels.
keywords: Roasted Tomato & Pepper Soup with a Giant Cheese Pretzel Crouton
Roasted Tomato & Pepper Soup with a Giant Cheese Pretzel Crouton recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Chop and deseed the bell peppers, core and quarter the large tomatoes, and peel and chop the onion.
Arrange the prepared vegetables (including the cherry tomatoes) in an oven-proof dish. Drizzle with olive oil and toss to coat evenly. Sprinkle generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Roast the vegetables in the oven for 45 mins, turning every 15 mins.
Meanwhile, grate the Parmesan using the large holes on a box grater. Slice the pretzel into large chunks, so you have one for every portion.

Sprinkle the grated Parmesan onto the lined baking tray, making little circles the same size as your pretzel pieces, ensuring that there are no blank spots. Top with the pretzel pieces and bake in the oven for about 10 mins until golden brown. Cool down on a plate lined with paper towels.

Once the vegetables are roasted and slightly blackened, transfer them to a blender and blend until smooth. Use the vegetable stock to adjust the consistency as needed. Season to taste with salt, pepper, and olive oil.
To serve, divide the soup across the bowls and top with the Parmesan-pretzel croutons.

name: Roasted Tomato Spaghetti
description: Simple. Uncomplicated. Delicious. Don’t let the long cooking time deter you, the pay off is sensational, with about 15 minutes of actual hands-on time.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C.

Open your tins of tomatoes and pour into a colander. Fill the empty tins with cold water and gently pour over the tomatoes, we want to wash the juice off the tomatoes without breaking them up. Once the water has drained off, put your washed tomatoes into your roasting tray.
Peel and thinly slice the garlic. Add it to a small, cold frying pan with two big pinches of salt and enough olive oil for the garlic to be submerged.

Place the garlic on a low heat and bring up to temperature. Take your time, garlic burns really easily so go slow. When it gradually starts to turn golden it’s ready, take it off the heat and add it to the tomatoes.

Roast in the oven for 45 mins — avoid stirring during the roast, as we're looking for the top of the tomatoes to burn slightly. After 45 mins and once the tomatoes begin to char on top, remove the tray from the oven and give it a good stir, before placing it back in the oven for another 45 mins.

After cooking for 90 mins your sauce will be nearly ready. If you think it needs more time roasting, then mix it again and put it back in the oven. It should have lost nearly all the water and begin to look a little oily and gnarly.
Cook your pasta in seasoned water. Add 4 big ladles of your tomato sauce to a frying pan and add the butter. Chuck in the cooked pasta with a little Parmesan and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Toss the pasta through the sauce, adding pasta water to loosen, and divide between warm bowls. Top with extra Parm and you’re good to go.

name: Roasted Tomato Spaghetti Soup
description: This is somewhere in between a tomatoey pasta soup and a very saucy pasta sauce. All you need to do is roast the tomatoes and shallots with the garlic and blend them into the most delicious, creamy sauce to throw your favourite pasta into.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Slice off the top of the garlic bulb and drizzle with a little olive oil and sprinkle over some salt before wrapping it up in some silver foil.
Peel and slice the shallot into eighths.

Add the tomatoes, shallot and garlic into a baking tray where they fit snuggly. If they are too spread out, too much of the juices will evaporate. Drizzle over plenty of olive oil and a generous amount of salt and pepper.
Roast on the middle shelf for about 40-50 mins or until the tomatoes are super soft and juicy and starting to char in spots. The garlic should be very soft and cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in plenty of salted water to slightly al dente, 1 minute less than stated cooking time. Save a cup of pasta water.

Take the tray out of the oven when it’s ready and remove and discard any tomato stalks. Let the garlic cool slightly before squeezing out the cloves into the tomatoes. Give it a mix and scoop out a few tablespoons of the tomatoes and set aside for topping.

Blend the garlic tomatoes with all of their juices until smooth. Depending on how much liquid you got out of your tomatoes, you may want to add a splash or two of pasta water. It should be a soupy consistency. Taste and season well.
To serve, ladle the soup into two bowls, then twirl in the pasta and pile on the reserved roasted tomatoes. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and some harissa, if using.
If you have leftover soup, this can be frozen but without the pasta.

name: Roasted Tomato and Mascarpone Tagliatelle
description: Pasta can be a labour of love, but this tagliatelle is worth it. Roasted tomatoes tossed with creamy mascarpone, chilli and garlic makes a beautiful sauce.
instructions: Pour your flour onto a clean work surface and clear a circle in the middle. Crack your eggs into the well and beat with a fork, gradually dragging in flour and beating together until you have a stiff dough that has incorporated all the flour.
Knead briefly until your dough goes smooth, then cover with cling film or a clean tea towel and leave to rest for 30 minutes.
Heat your oven to 160°C/320°F.
Tip your cherry tomatoes into a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil and a pinch of salt. Pop in the oven to roast for 40 minutes.

Cut your pasta dough into 4 equal-sized pieces. One by one, roll out your dough to the 2nd thinnest setting on your pasta roller, or about 1mm thick if rolling by hand. You should have 4 long, thin, smooth sheets by the end. Cut each in half horizontally so you have 8 long sheets.

Attach your pasta shape cutter to your pasta roller. Run your sheets of dough one by one through your tagliatelle setting so that you have lots of lovely pasta strips. If you are cutting by hand, cut each length of pasta into strips 1cm wide. Dust your pasta with your semolina and set it aside on a parchment-lined baking tray.
Fill a pan with water, salt liberally, and bring to a boil.
Finely slice your garlic.
Heat a little olive oil in a saute pan over a gentle heat and add your garlic and chilli flakes. Fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add your tomato purée and cook it out for a minute before adding your roasted tomatoes and mascarpone.
Cook your tagliatelle for 1-2 minutes in the boiling water.

Add a ladle of pasta water to the tomato sauce, then lift your pasta out of the boiling water with tongs and drop it into your saucepan. Grate in your parmesan and mix until you have a smooth sauce that coats all your pasta, adding more pasta water if you need more silkiness.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then serve up with an extra sprinkle of parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Roasted Winter Veg & Chicken Salad
description: This cosy-meets-fresh salad is all about golden roasted veg, juicy chicken, and a creamy peanut dressing. Sweet, nutty, and zingy all in one.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Slice the sweet potato into 1cm-thick rounds. Trim and halve the Brussels sprouts. Toss both with half the olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 20 mins until golden and tender. Drizzle with the maple syrup.
Meanwhile, add the apple cider vinegar to a bowl with the powdered peanut butter and 1 Tbsp water and whisk until you’ve got a drizzly dressing. Season to taste.

Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Heat the remaining oil in a nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 7–8 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through. Set aside to rest for 1 min, then slice.
Tear the radicchio into bite-sized pieces and chuck it into a large bowl with the rocket. Add the roasted veg and toss with the dressing.

Spoon the salad into Tupperware containers, top with the sliced chicken, scatter with pomegranate seeds and crumble over the goats’ cheese. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Roasted Winter Veg & Chicken Salad
description: This cosy-meets-fresh salad is all about golden roasted veg, juicy chicken, and a creamy peanut dressing. Sweet, nutty, and zingy all in one.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Slice the sweet potato into 1cm-thick rounds. Trim and halve the Brussels sprouts. Toss both with half the olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 20 mins until golden and tender. Drizzle with the maple syrup.
Meanwhile, add the apple cider vinegar to a bowl with the powdered peanut butter and 1 Tbsp water and whisk until you’ve got a drizzly dressing. Season to taste.

Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Heat the remaining oil in a nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 7–8 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through. Set aside to rest for 1 min, then slice.
Tear the radicchio into bite-sized pieces and chuck it into a large bowl with the rocket. Add the roasted veg and toss with the dressing.
Plate up the salad, top with the sliced chicken, scatter with pomegranate seeds and crumble over the goats’ cheese.

name: Rocket & Ricotta Filo Pie
description: Is it a börek? Is it a spanakopita? Let’s be honest, it’s neither… but it is really damn tasty. The honey really is the cherry on top, so don’t skip it.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Dunk the rocket into boiling salted water for 1 minute and refresh in icy cold water.
Squeeze out the excess water and roughly chop.
Add the rocket to a mixing bowl with the ricotta and feta cheese. Season with salt, pepper and the zest of your lemon. Beat together.
Melt the butter over a very low heat and then beat in the egg.

Now to build. Lay out a sheet of filo, with the longer side running along the bottom, and brush with the butter and egg wash. Lay another sheet, slightly overlapping, again with the longer side running over along the bottom. You’ll now have a very long sheet of filo.
Brush with more of the butter and egg wash and keep layering up the pastry, each time slightly overlapping until you have four layers.
Spoon your filling into a long sausage along the bottom edge of the pastry sheets. Roll up like a big cigar.
Now, gently coil the roll into a spiral shape. Don’t worry if it cracks a little, it’s not the end of the world.
Now brush liberally with the butter and egg wash and sprinkle with flaky sea salt and sesame seeds.
Pop it onto a baking tray lined with parchment and bake for 25-30 mins until golden brown.
Take it straight out the oven and drizzle with honey.
Get stuck in.

name: Rocky Road
description: Who doesn’t love rocky road? A classic fridge cake with crushed biscuits, marshmallows, dried fruits and nuts, chocolate and anything else sweet you’ve got lying around. Perfect for using up leftover chocolate, biscuits and sweets.
instructions: Bash up your biscuits – the best way to do this is put them in a bowl and use the end of a rolling pin to break them into pieces. You want some irregular chunks. Roughly chop the nuts, crunchie bar, and the marshmallows if using big’uns.

Line a brownie tin or small roasting tin with baking paper. Break the chocolate into a medium saucepan, add the butter, golden syrup and a pinch of salt. Cook over a low-medium heat, stirring occasionally until melted.

Add in all of your other ingredients, stir to coat then scrape into your tin and smooth into a compact layer. Put into the fridge to set – at least 4 hours should do it. Once set, cut into 12 rectangles, and keep in the fridge for whenever a craving hits.

name: Rolled Eggs Breakfast Wrap
description: Inspired by Ugandan Rolex, we’ve taken the same rolled egg technique to make the base of this wrap. Fill it with anything you want, for a versatile and delicious breakfast on the go.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Thinly slice the mushrooms, cut each of the onions into eight wedges and place onto an oiled baking tray (you may need two trays). Season with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and cumin. Toss together and roast until golden and softened, 25-30 mins.

Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a bowl and season them with salt and garam masala. Whisk together. Pour boiling water over the spinach to wilt. Once cooled down a little, press down to squeeze out any excess water.

Place a frying pan, roughly the size of your tortillas onto medium heat with a drizzle of oil. One hot, add just enough whisked eggs to cover the bottom of your pan, swirl around and let the bottom set. When the top of the omelette is still wet, place the tortilla on top, then flip. Toast the tortilla for a couple of seconds, then transfer to a plate. Continue this process until all the tortillas have been cooked.

Once the tortillas are done, finely grate the halloumi into a strip on one side of each omelette and cover with the roasted veggies, spinach and some hot sauce. Roll up the tortillas and wrap them in foil or parchment paper.

These rolled egg wraps can be eaten fresh or stored in the freezer until ready to eat. Reheat from frozen in the microwave until defrosted, or pan fry on medium-low until thawed and piping hot throughout.

name: Romesco Beans & Sesame Toast
description: Toasty, sesame-crusted eggy bread meets smoky romesco beans with a salty hit of feta. An ultra-satisfying veggie dinner or brunch plate.
instructions: Drain the roasted peppers and add them to a blender along with the sundried tomatoes, bread, almonds and their oil. Blitz until smooth. Taste and season with salt, black pepper and a splash of sherry vinegar – it should be punchy and tangy. Pour into a bowl and set aside.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk in the soy sauce. Pour the sesame seeds onto a plate. Pick the parsley leaves and discard the stems.
Dip both sides of each bread slice into the egg mixture, then press one side into the sesame seeds. Set aside.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, fry the bread, sesame-side up, until golden on both sides. Transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper.

Tip the butter beans into a large pan with the romesco sauce. Set over a medium heat and stir together until warmed through, loosening with a splash of water if it’s too thick. Taste and adjust with more salt, pepper or vinegar if needed. (You can also serve the beans cold – just stir the two together.)
Cut each toast slice into quarters. Spoon the beans into bowls, crumble over the feta and top with parsley leaves. Serve with the sesame toast on the side.

name: Romesco Chicken Traybake
description: I'm going to say that this is the best traybake dinner. Crispy chicken, charred spring onions and a beautiful romesco sauce made from roasted peppers. Sophie x
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/400°F.
Halve your new potatoes. Cut your peppers into chunky slices and discard the seedy middles. Halve your lemon.

In a large baking tray, pop your potatoes and peppers. Season with 2 tsp of your smoked paprika, a pinch of salt and a tablespoon of the olive oil. Saving the remaining for later. Toss until all coated.
Nestle your chicken thighs and lemon halves in the tray and season the skin of the chicken with salt. Roast for 25 mins.
Add your spring onions and almonds to the tray and roast for another 5 mins.
Remove your almonds and half of your peppers from the tray. Return the tray to the oven for another 25 mins.
Roughly chop your almonds.
Pop your peppers in a bowl covered in a clean tea towel to steam – this will help you to peel them more easily. When the peppers are cool enough to handle, peel off their skins and discard them.

Add the pepper flesh to a food processor along with your almonds, remaining tsp of smoked paprika and sherry vinegar. Pulse to a paste, then dribble in the remaining olive oil until your mixture looks smooth and emulsified. Season to taste with salt.
Remove your tray from the oven and drizzle it with your romesco sauce and a sprinkle of chopped parsley. Serve and enjoy.

name: Romesco Chickpeas
description: Healthy weeknight dinners don't get much simpler than this. Packed with fibre and protein, this romesco chickpea recipe is a winner.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic. Halve all the cherry tomatoes. Heat 1/4 of the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, add the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 2 mins, stirring regularly. Add the chickpeas, along with the water from the jar, and stir to combine.
Add the cherry tomatoes, then cover with a lid and cook for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, add most of the roasted almonds, the rest of the olive oil, and the other ingredients for the sauce into a blender. Season with plenty of salt and pepper and blitz into a smooth sauce.

Stir the sauce into the chickpeas, taste and season. Spoon into bowls or meal-prep boxes, top with feta, the rest of the roasted almonds, parsley and chilli flakes. It will keep in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Romesco Chickpeas
description: Healthy weeknight dinners don't get much simpler than this. Packed with fibre and protein, this romesco chickpea recipe is a winner.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic. Halve all the cherry tomatoes. Heat 1/4 of the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, add the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 2 mins, stirring regularly. Add the chickpeas, along with the water from the jar, and stir to combine.
Add the cherry tomatoes, then cover with a lid and cook for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, add most of the roasted almonds, the rest of the olive oil, and the other ingredients for the sauce into a blender. Season with plenty of salt and pepper and blitz into a smooth sauce.
Stir the sauce into the chickpeas, taste and season. Spoon into bowls, top with feta, the rest of the roasted almonds, parsley and chilli flakes, and dig in.

name: Romesco Cod & Chorizo Pepper Grains
description: A light, flavour-packed fish supper with a caraway and almond crust, jammy roasted peppers, smoky chorizo and a garlicky lemon aioli. It's sunshine on a plate.
keywords: Almond Cod & Chorizo Pepper Salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.  Drain the peppers and thinly slice them along with the shallots and fennel. Add to a large baking tray with the thyme and a drizzle of olive oil, toss the chorizo through and slide into the oven for 10-15 mins, until the veg has softened.

Meanwhile, zest the lemon. Season the cod with salt all over and set aside. Toss the almonds with the caraway seeds. Finely grate the garlic into the mayo, then season with some of the lemon juice, the zest and a pinch of salt.

Once the veg has softened, stir the grains through. Pat the cod dry and rub with a little olive oil. Place the cod on top of the veg, then press the almond and caraway mixture over the top of each fillet. Slide back into the oven for 7-10 mins, until the cod is cooked through and the nuts are golden and toasted. If the almonds are browning too quickly, loosely cover the tray with foil.
To serve, divide the grains and veg between plates, top with the almond-crusted cod and finish with a dollop of aioli and a wedge of lemon.

name: Romesco Gazpacho & Grilled Cheese
description: Classic gazpacho is getting a romesco makeover. Chilled soup, topped with 'nduja oil served with mustardy grilled cheese sarnies.
instructions: Drain the peppers and add to a large blender. Pick the basil leaves, trim and roughly chop the cucumber. Reserve some basil leaves then add the rest of it to the peppers, with the cucumber, tomatoes, garlic, and almonds. Pour 70ml of olive oil and blend until smooth. Season with plenty of salt, pepper and lemon juice. Do this in batches if your blender isn’t large enough. Pour into a large bowl, cover and set in the fridge.
Coarsely grate or slice the cheddar into thin slabs. Spread the mustard onto 1 half of the bread and sprinkle with cheese, top with the remaining bread.
Pour 4 tbsp of oil into a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the sandwiches until golden on both sides and the cheese has melted, 8-10 mins.
Meanwhile, in a small frying pan, add 20ml of olive oil and the 'nduja, place on medium heat. Once hot, add the 'nduja and cook for 2-3 mins. Remove from the heat.
Share the gazpacho into bowls, top with the nduja oil and reserved basil leaves. Serve with the grilled cheeses.

name: Romesco Mac & Cheese
description: We always wondered why romesco and mac & cheese hadn't been combined. The flavours work perfectly together. Tangy, smoky, cheesy, rich. The perfect mouthful.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C.

Chop your peppers up into small pieces and place them in a baking tray. Coat the peppers with olive oil, salt and pepper. Peel the cloves of garlic and place them on the baking tray. Whack the tray in the oven for 25 minutes. After 25 minutes, push the peppers to the side and add the almonds to the tray. Pop back into the oven and cook for another 10 minutes.
Get your macaroni on, see the packet for instructions.

Romesco time! Take your peppers out of the oven and put them in a blender along with most of your toasted almonds, peeled cloves of garlic, olive oil and red wine vinegar. Then, sprinkle in your smoked paprika, salt, pepper, parsley (save some for the top) and a splash of water. Blend it all together until you have a smooth, sauce-like consistency.
Add the romesco sauce to a saucepan and add half of your grated mozzarella and cheddar. Cook on a medium heat until these have melted, stirring continuously.
Once your macaroni is cooked, add it to your sauce, stirring it through so that it is covered. Sprinkle your remaining cheddar, mozzarella and remaining almonds on top.
Place the pan under a hot grill for 8 minutes, or until the cheese is golden-brown on top. Get that baby plated up and dig in!

name: Root Vegetable Gratin
description: Want comfort food that also supports your health goals? Look no further. We’ve added beans to the creamy miso sauce in this root veg gratin to add extra fibre and plant protein, making this plant-based dinner even more nutritious and satisfying. The vegetables also each have their own unique mix of phytochemicals, polyphenols and prebiotic fibres which can help to support your gut health.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Add your cashews to a small bowl and cover them with boiling water. Leave them to soak for at least 10 mins.
Thinly slice your vegetables as thin as you can using a knife or mandolin. Layer them, along with the thyme leaves, in an ovenproof dish.
Add the drained beans, soaked cashews, garlic, milk and miso paste to a blender and blitz to a pourable sauce. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Cover the vegetables with the sauce, pushing them down to ensure they are submerged.
Drizzle the olive oil over the top and place in the oven for an hour until the vegetables are soft and the top is golden and crispy.

name: Rosemary Aioli BLT
description: Level up everyone’s favourite sarnie with a homemade rosemary infused aioli. Crack open an Inch's cider to sip on the side.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Lay the bacon out on a parchment-lined baking tray. Slide into the oven for 12-13 mins, flipping halfway, until rendered and very crispy.

Meanwhile, whip up the aioli. Add the yolks and dijon to the bowl of a food processor. Finely grate in the garlic and add the juice of the lemon. Season with salt and turn the processor on. Slowly stream in the oil until you have a thick, rich aioli.
Strip the leaves from half of the rosemary and finely chop. Blitz into the aioli, season to taste and you’re all done. Tip into a bowl and set aside.
Cut the tomatoes into thick slices and season very generously with olive oil, salt and pepper. Set aside to macerate.

Once the bacon is crispy, pull it out the oven and remove from the tray, leaving the fat behind. Pop the remaining rosemary onto the tray, toss in the fat and slide back into the oven for 2 mins to crisp up. Remove and set aside.

Lay out your slices of bread (toasted, if you like) and add a generous spoon of aioli to each side. Lay down the lettuce leaves and top with seasoned tomatoes. Pile on the crispy bacon and crumble over the crispy rosemary leaves.
Add a lid, cut in half and get stuck in. Pairs perfectly with an Inch’s Cider.

name: Rosemary Butter Beans with Grilled Peaches, Tofu Feta & Rocket
description: Peach salads are summery, beautiful and delicious. But they are lacking somewhat in the protein department, if eaten as a veggie main… so, enter these rosemary butter beans with grilled peaches, rocket and tofu feta.
keywords: Rosemary Butter Beans with Grilled Peaches
instructions: Start with the tofu feta. Squeeze the tofu in kitchen paper to draw out any excess water. In a mixing bowl, break the tofu apart into small, irregular chunks with your hands. Squeeze in the lemon juice, then add the remaining ingredients and ½-1 tsp salt. Gently toss to combine.

Finely chop the shallots and mince the garlic. Heat a splash of olive oil in a large, wide-sided sauté pan. When a piece of shallot sizzles on contact, tip the rest in and fry over a low-medium heat for 8 mins with a pinch of sea salt. Add the garlic and fry until the raw aroma subsides (at least 3-4 mins). Pour in the beans plus their juices, plus a little water to loosen the mixture if needed. Add the stock cube and rosemary sprigs. Simmer for 15-20 mins, stirring occasionally.
Season the butter beans to taste and remove the rosemary sprigs. Lower the heat while you prep the peaches.

Cut the peaches into neat segments, discarding the stones. Brush with a little olive oil, then place flesh-side down in a griddle pan and cook for 2-3 mins each side, until slightly charred. Remove and set aside.
Grate the tomato, discarding the skin, into a small bowl, then add the olive oil, sherry vinegar and a pinch of salt. Mix well, then taste and adjust the salt level.
Tip the rocket into a large bowl and add half of the tomato dressing. Toss well.
Serve the warm butter beans in bowls, topped with the grilled peaches, the dressed rocket, tofu feta and a final drizzle of the reserved tomato dressing. Eat with toast or grains.

name: Rosemary Roast Potatoes
description: Crispy, golden rosemary-infused roast potatoes. An essential part of the perfect Christmas dinner.
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into equal-sized pieces. It’s up to you how big you go – you are the master of your roast potatoes.

Tip the potatoes into a saucepan and cover with cold water. Season very generously with salt and set over a medium heat. Bring the potatoes to a bare simmer and cook for 10-12 mins or until completely tender. They should be almost falling apart. Carefully drain and allow to cool uncovered, ideally overnight but at the very least for a few hours, on a tray in the fridge.

Heat the oven to 220°C. Grab a large roasting tin, cover the base with vegetable oil and preheat in the oven. Once hot, add the potatoes, coating them in the hot oil. Slide the tin into the oven for 35-40 mins, turning the potatoes every now and then.

Pull out of the oven and add the butter, toss to coat, then back into the oven for 10-15 mins. Meanwhile, finely chop the rosemary and mix with equal parts flaky salt. Add plenty of black pepper and mix to make an amazing seasoning mixture.
Serve the potatoes with plenty of rosemary salt sprinkled on top.

name: Rotli
description: Rotli, roti, chapati - what you call this bread depends on where you are from. These rotli are the ones my mum makes and I think they are the best. Seema x
instructions: Combine the chapati flour with a pinch of salt, 1 tbsp of oil and 200ml of boiling water straight from the kettle. Mix it with a spoon until its cool enough to handle. Knead for 5 mins to form a sticky dough. Pour 1 tbsp of oil over the dough and continue to knead so the dough is less sticky and very soft.
Cover the dough and allow it to rest for 15-20 mins.
Heat up a frying pan to a high heat, allow it to warm up for 2 mins.

Pinch off a golf ball-sized piece of dough and liberally dust your work surface with flour. Roll the dough gently into a small circle and then coat it again with flour. Continue rolling until you form a thin circle that is about 15cm in diameter.

Place the rotli face-side down in the frying pan. Cook for 30 seconds until small bubbles appear and then flip it. Allow to cook for a further 30 seconds and flip again. Then, using a clean tea towel, press down on the rotli. This will help it to puff up - press down on the parts that are puffing up to push the air to all the sides of the rotli.
Whilst one is cooking, roll out the next rotli – bring in a friend to help you. Continue rolling and cooking the rotli until you have run out of dough.
Enjoy with a curry, or even spread with butter and sprinkled with sugar as a snack.

name: Ruben's Leftover Chicken Reuben
description: We had Ruben's Reubens in the studio making his take on a reuben sandwich using up his leftover roast chicken. Give this one a go.
instructions: Finely dice your shallot and gherkin.
Combine all the ingredients for the Russian dressing and give it a mix. Season with salt and pepper.
Shred your chicken pieces and add them into the bowl of Russian dressing. Set aside.
Spread some butter onto both sides of your sourdough slices.
Spread some of the dressed chicken onto one slice of bread before topping it with the sauerkraut and a few slices of cheese. Cover with the other slice of bread.
Get it in a toastie machine or in a hot pan, fry until both sides are golden and the cheese is melted. Serve and enjoy!

name: Ruben’s Latkes
description: Ruben Dawnay's from Ruben's Reubens has shown us his take on a latke, and they are sublime. Who doesn't love a crispy fried potato cake?
instructions: First, grate the potatoes and onion into a bowl.
Using a clean tea towel, squeeze as much liquid out of the potato mixture as possible. You can do this is in a couple of small batches. Place back into a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, crack the eggs and give them a whisk.
Add the eggs, flour and salt to the potato then give it a good mix.
You should be able to form some loose patties with the mixture. Feel free to add a little more flour if you think it needs more binding.
Once you’re happy with the mixture, place a large frying pan on medium heat and fill with about 2 inches of oil.

When the pan is hot, squeeze a golf ball-sized amount of mix between your palms to make a patty. Place carefully into the oil and repeat until the pan is full (leaving a bit of space between each latke).
Fry for about 5 minutes, or until golden, then flip and do the same again.
Remove to a kitchen paper-lined plate and season with a little more salt.
Serve with your condiment of choice, but traditionally these are enjoyed with apple sauce and sour cream!

name: Rude Health Mushroom Crêpes
description: These crêpes are not only vegan but because they make use of Rude Health Buckwheat Flour (which isn’t actually a type of wheat at all) they’re also gluten free.
instructions: First off, let’s make the cashew cream – shout out Sophie Wyburd for this one! Drop your cashews into boiling water and let them cook for 20 mins.

While the cashews cook, make the crêpe batter. In a mixing bowl, whisk together the Rude Health Buckwheat Flour and baking powder with a good pinch of salt. Next, you’re going to want to whisk in your Rude Health Oat Drink until you have a smooth batter.
Drain the cashews and add to a blender along with 150g of water and a tbsp of miso. Blend until smooth and creamy. Set aside.
Set a large frying pan over a high heat. Slice your mushrooms, add them to the pan with a pinch of salt and cook for a few minutes until they take on some colour and the moisture is evaporating.
Reduce the heat to medium, slice the garlic and add to the mushrooms along with a generous drizzle of olive oil.
Cook for another 3 to 4 mins. Finely chop the chives, roughly chop the tarragon and add both to the pan. Cook for 1 min.
Add the cashew cream, stir well and bring to a gentle simmer. Season the mix with salt and pepper, then keep warm over a low heat while you make the crêpes.
Set a large, non-stick pan over a medium heat with a drop of oil. Add a ladleful of batter and use the back of the lade to spread it thin so it covers the base of the pan.
Cook for about 3 mins, then use a spatula to flip and cook for another minute on the other side. Remove and keep warm in the oven while you make the rest of the crêpes.
When the crêpes are all ready: spoon over the creamy mushroom mix, sprinkle over a few more chives, roll up, and enjoy!

name: Rum & Rhubarb Fizz
description: This fizzy little number is set to be your drink of the summer. It's not too sweet and makes the most of seasonal rhubarb. Anyone can make this.
instructions: Grab your longest, pinkest rhubarb stalk and use a peeler to make a few ribbons.
Finely chop the remaining rhubarb and pop it into a heat-proof bowl. Add the grenadine and toss to coat.

Heat the syrup to a simmer and pour over the chopped rhubarb. Let that steep until it's around room temperature. Pass through a fine sieve and store in the fridge. The syrup will keep for up to a week.

Peel the lemon and make twists for the garnish. Juice the lemon, and carefully separate the egg white from yolk (you can use the yolks to make mayonnaise). Combine 25ml of the rhubarb syrup with the rum, 25ml of lemon juice and 1 tbsp of egg white in a cocktail shaker. Add one ice cube and dry shake for 10 secs. Now fill to the brim with ice and shake again for 15 secs.
Strain into a chilled tumbler, top up with sparkling water and garnish with a rhubarb ribbon and a lemon twist.

name: Rum-ble In The Jungle
description: Nothing like those subpar rum cocktails you're used to. This fruity number's made with rum and comes finished with caramelised banana strips.
instructions: To begin with, slice up both bananas into long strips — reserving two strips. Place them on a baking tray and sprinkle with sugar. Either use a blow torch or high temperature grill to caramelise the sugar on top, then leave to cool.
Mash up the remaining banana strips, and place in a pan with the sugar and water. Heat gently until the sugar is dissolved and the banana has infused the syrup.
Fill a cocktail shaker with ice and then go in with the banana syrup, triple sec, rum and pineapple juice. Shake vigorously for 10 seconds.
Double strain into a rocks glass with ice. Garnish with your caramelised banana slices and enjoy.

name: Saag & Paneer Curry with Homemade Naan
description: A comforting midweek curry that will impress your flatmates and family. It’s fully veggie and comes served with homemade naan.
keywords: saag and paneer curry with homemade naan
instructions: Start with the naan. Put all the ingredients plus a splash of water into a large bowl and mix well. Knead until a dough forms (this will take about 5 mins) and set aside.

Dice the paneer into bite-sized cubes. Set a lidded frying pan over a medium-high heat, then add a splash of oil, the paneer, turmeric, curry powder and a pinch of salt. Fry for 5 mins until all sides of the paneer are golden.
Meanwhile, slice the onion, mince or finely chop the garlic, chop the green chillies and chop the coriander.

Remove the cooked paneer from the pan and set aside on a plate. Add the onion, ginger and 3/5 of the minced garlic into the same pan with a pinch of salt. Cook for 7 mins until translucent, then add the spinach and cook with the lid on over a medium heat for 5 mins. Once half reduced, add all the spices and cook for another 10 mins (you can add extra chillies at this point, if you like). Return the paneer to the pan and cook for 5-10 mins, depending on your choice of texture.

Combine the butter, the rest of the minced garlic, and the chopped coriander in a bowl. Next, roll out the naan dough balls into flatbread shapes. Set a fresh, large frying pan (non-stick or cast-iron is best) over a high heat, then add one naan at a time. Toast on one side for 3 mins until bubbles have formed, then quickly flip and cook for another 3 mins. At this point, baste in the garlic, coriander and butter mix.
Top your curry with fresh chillies and coriander. Serve!

name: Saag Tofu Lentils
description: A hearty, feel-good bowl that’s packed with protein and big flavour. Creamy lentils, spiced tofu, and silky spinach come together for the ultimate comforting dinner.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Pat the tofu dry, then tear into pieces. Toss with half of the olive oil, a pinch of salt, and some pepper. Spread out on a baking tray and roast for 15 mins, until golden and crisp around the edges. Toss with the lime pickle.

While the tofu cooks, finely dice the onion, ginger and garlic. Heat the remaining olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for 5 mins until soft and starting to turn golden.

Stir in the curry powder. Cook for another 30 secs until fragrant. Add the lentils, stock cube, coconut milk, and water. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 20 mins, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and creamy.
Stir through the spinach and cook for 2–3 mins until wilted.
Spoon into bowls, top with tofu and scatter with fresh coriander.

name: Saffron Prawn & Chickpea Stew
description: There’s a misconception that healthy food has to be boring or complicated but this prawn and chickpea stew proves otherwise. It comes together quickly in one pan and packs in so much flavour and nutrition, with over 25g of protein and almost 9g of fibre per serving to support your gut health.
instructions: Add your saffron to a small bowl and pour over the boiling water. Leave it for 15-20 mins to bloom.
Finely dice your onion, garlic cloves and red chilli. Slice your red pepper. Roughly chop your fresh parsley.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a pan set over a medium heat. Fry your onions for a few minutes until golden and caramelised then add the chopped garlic, chilli and sliced pepper and cook for a further 2 mins.

Add the paprika and cook it off for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the drained chickpeas and the zest of the lemon then pour in the saffron stock. Leave to simmer for around 5 mins or until the sauce has thickened.
Taste to check the seasoning then add in the prawns and cook for a further 3 mins until they are cooked through.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and the fresh parsley. Serve on its own or with some toasted sourdough.

name: Saffron-Infused Potato Gratin with Gruyère & Thyme
description: A bubbling, golden brown potato gratin with a delicate saffron twist. This one is an absolute crowd pleaser.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C / 375°F. Grease a baking dish with butter. Thinly slice the potatoes and onions. Mince the garlic. Grate the Gruyère cheese.
To infuse the Saffron, warm the milk in a small saucepan and add the saffron threads. Let it steep for about 10 mins.

Meanwhile, in the prepared dish, layer half of the potatoes, onions, and garlic. Season with salt, pepper, and thyme. Sprinkle with half of the Gruyère cheese. Repeat with remaining potatoes, onions, garlic, and cheese.
Combine the cream with the saffron-infused milk, and pour it evenly over the potatoes.
Dot the top with butter and bake for 45-60 mins, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden brown.
Let the gratin cool slightly before serving.

name: Saganaki
description: Saganaki is a quick and easy recipe for the summer. Temperatures are important. You want cold cheese, a hot pan, and don't you dare move that cheese around.
instructions: Begin by making your honey liquid. Place honey, half your lemon juice and ouzo in a jar and shake super hard to bring together. Leave to the side.

Place a heavy small pan over a high heat. While the pan heats up, add the kefalograviera to the plain flour and cover, before dusting off the excess. Once the pan is hot, add the olive oil and then place the floured cheese on top.

Let the cheese sizzle for 2 mins or until you see a caramelised crust start to form around the sides. Using a thin spatula, aggressively push under cheese and flip. Cook for another min before pouring half your honey liquid in. Let the liquid cook for half a min before taking it off heat and finishing with a squeeze of lemon and dried oregano.
Repeat process with second piece.
For the peach salsa, dice your peach and add it to a bowl with the thyme leaves, lemon juice and salt. Set aside.
To serve, plate up the cheese with a good spoonful of your peach salsa

name: Salmon & Caponata Chickpeas
description: Perfectly cooked salmon and tangy caponata-inspired chickpeas.
instructions: Finely chop the onion and celery and cut the aubergine into bite-sized chunks.
Heat the olive oil in a deep frying pan over a medium heat. Add the veg along with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 mins until softened.
Meanwhile, slice the olives, pick the basil leaves and finely slice the stalks.

Add the basil stalks and tomato purée to the pan. Give everything a good stir and cook for 1 min, then tip in the chickpeas along with their liquid. Add the olives and sultanas. Give everything a good stir, simmer away for 5 mins then stir through most of the basil leaves and season with salt, pepper and vinegar to taste.

Season the salmon fillets. Place the fish on top of the chickpeas and cover the pan with a lid (if you don’t have a lid that fits, you can use a large baking tray). Cook for 8-10 mins until the fish is cooked through – it should flake into large chunks. Scatter over the remaining basil and drizzle with a little extra olive oil, to serve.

name: Salmon & Sesame Smash with Soba Noodles
description: The same creamy sesame salmon smash, this time tossed through cold soba noodles with crispy chilli oil and curled spring onions on top. Great in a lunch box.
keywords: Salmon & Sesame Smash with Soba Noodles
Hot Smoked Salmon Smash Soba Noodles
instructions: Peel and grate the ginger into a large bowl. Add the Greek yoghurt, sesame oil, sesame seeds, rice vinegar and sugar with a pinch of salt, then mix until smooth and glossy.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the soba noodles and cook according to packet instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water until completely cool. Drain again well. Meanwhile, cut the 3 spring onions into fine strips and drop them into a bowl of cold water so they curl up.

Flake the hot smoked salmon into the dressing, discarding any skin. Scoop out the avocado flesh, dice the cucumber and finely slice the remaining spring onion. Squeeze the pickled ginger dry and finely chop. Add everything to the bowl along with the edamame, then smash together with a fork, leaving some texture.

Tip the noodles into the bowl and toss until every strand is coated in the dressing. Taste and season with a little more salt, then divide between bowls or boxes. Drain the spring onion curls and pile on top, then finish each portion with a tsp of the crispy chilli oil and a scattering of crispy fried onions.

name: Salmon Ceviche Tacos
description: Jonny Marsh (a private chef for pro footballers) brings us the freshest salmon ceviche taco recipe. Using the most beautiful and fresh Alaska salmon. Insane.
instructions: Descale and skin the salmon. Dice into small cubes.
Finely chop the red chilli, ¾ of the ginger and coriander.
Add the salmon to a bowl along with the juice and zest of ½ the limes, ½ the chopped chilli, ginger and ½ the coriander. Leave this in the fridge to marinate.
Grate the carrot and shred the red cabbage and savoy cabbage.
For the slaw dressing, combine the soy sauce, honey, rice wine vinegar, juice of ½ the remaining lime and sesame oil. Grate in the garlic and remaining ginger and give it a mix.
Massage ½ the dressing into the carrots and cabbage.
Peel the mangos with a speed peeler and cut down the side of the stone and side into small cubes. Add the remaining chilli and coriander.
Get a pan on medium to high heat and cook the soft taco shells for 30 seconds. Brush the inside of what will be your taco with a little of the soy dressing. Take the tacos out of the pan.
Reduce the remaining dressing in your pan over a low heat to make a sticky glaze.

Get your marinated salmon out of the fridge. Pile up the slaw onto your taco shells before topping with the salmon, mango salsa, and final drizzle of soy glaze. Serve with a lime wedge, if you like. Enjoy.

name: Salmon En Croûte
description: A great Valentines day dish. Go to your fish monger & get some nice salmon to make this really special.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Splash some olive oil into a frying pan. Add sliced garlic cloves. After 20 seconds, add your spinach. Once wilted, remove from the heat and squeeze through a sieve to drain.
Add the spinach to a bowl with a horseradish and sour cream. Add a handful of chopped dill, a handful of chopped parsley, salt and pepper. Mix together.
Roll out your sheet of puff pastry. Cut it in half.

Line a baking tray with baking paper. Add 1 of the pastry halves to the paper. Add some spinach mix and then add your salmon fillet. Top with spinach. Fold the pastry over, crimp it, brush with egg yolk and sprinkle with some sea salt. Repeat with the other pastry half.
Place the tray in the oven for 30 minutes or until the pastry is golden and crisp. Serve and enjoy!

name: Salmon Fishcakes with Grains & Slaw
description: Crispy salmon fishcakes served with a limey yoghurt slaw and hearty grains. A fresh, feel-good dinner that’s speedy, satisfying and kid-approved.
keywords: salmon fishcakes with grains and slaw
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsRoughly chop the salmon. Add half to a food processor and pulse to a coarse paste. Dice the rest into small chunks. Finely chop a quarter of the red onion and stir through the salmon along with a third of the grains. Season with salt and pepper, then shape into patties. Chill for 10 mins to firm up.

Finely grate the zest of the lime into a large bowl, then squeeze in most of the juice. Add the yoghurt, honey and half of the olive oil. Season well and whisk to combine — this is your slaw dressing.

Finely shred the cabbage and thinly slice the remaining three-quarters of the red onion. Toss half of the onion and all of the cabbage into dressing. Use your hands to scrunch everything together until slightly softened. Taste and season again. Portion out a kid’s serving, then finely chop most of the dill (reserving a few fronds for garnish) and mix into the slaw for the adults.
Toss the remaining half of the onion with the remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt, then scrunch it to soften — this is your quick pickle for garnish.
Heat olive oil in a frying pan set over a medium heat. Fry the fishcakes for about 3 mins on each side until golden and cooked through.
Warm the remaining grains for serving.

Serve up!Kids Plate: Dish up the grains and slaw, top with a fishcake and serve with a dollop of ketchup.Parents Plate: Spoon the grains and slaw onto each plate. Top with a fishcake and finish with a few dill fronds and quick pickled onions and a drizzle with chilli sauce, if you fancy.

name: Salmon Pasta
description: Make our delicious salmon pasta with fresh or smoked salmon, a rich sauce, and fresh herbs. Perfect for a quick, satisfying meal! This is a creamy but light spring-summer salmon pasta recipe that’s sure to be on weekly rotation in your kitchen. This pasta dish uses everyday ingredients that you’ll easily have in the fridge. Enjoy.
instructions: Peel and finely chop the garlic. Remove the woody ends from the asparagus, then cut into 2cm thick pieces on the diagonal. Roughly chop the dill. Set aside.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large, deep frying pan (which has a lid) over a medium-high heat. Season the salmon fillets well, then put into the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes on each side until golden.
Meanwhile, get a large pan of salted water up to the boil, then cook the rigatoni following pack instructions.
Once the salmon is golden brown on each side, add the sliced garlic and fry for 30 seconds, moving it around so it doesn’t burn.
Tip in the asparagus and put a lid on the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes, tossing everything around now and again.

Use two forks to flake the salmon into bite-sized pieces, then add the cream cheese. Zest in the lemon, then squeeze in the juice of ½. Add the frozen peas and season with a little salt and plenty of cracked black pepper.

Drain the pasta, reserving a cup of the water. Add the pasta to the salmon pan, tossing really well so it all gets coated in the sauce. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen and give a creamy finish. Add in ¾ of the dill and toss really well. Check for seasoning, adding more lemon juice, if you like.
Divide between two plates and finish with the remaining dill, more cracked black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Salmon Pasta Salad
description: A Niçoise-y take on pasta salad with scrumptious flakey salmon, this makes a perfect light dinner ideal for sunny evenings.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Quarter the plum tomatoes and toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper, and roast for 30 mins until softened.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta according to packet instructions, adding green beans for the last 2 mins. Drain and cool completely under cold running water.

For the dressing, blitz the herbs, the olives, the chillies, capers, olive oil, and lemon juice with salt and pepper until you have a rough pesto. Adjust with more lemon or chilli brine if needed. (You can also finely chop by hand.)
Fill a saucepan full of water and place over a high heat. Once boiling, turn the heat down to medium, gently drop the eggs in and simmer for 7 mins. Transfer to an ice bath to cool down.

Season the salmon with salt. Heat a frying pan over high heat with a glug of neutral oil. Once hot, add the salmon skin-side down. Press gently on the flesh so the skin makes even contact with the pan. Cook for 5–6 mins until the skin is crisp, then flip the fillets to colour on each side for a minute or two before turning off the heat, and letting the residual heat finish cooking.
In a large bowl, toss the pasta, dressing, green beans, remaining olives, pickled chillies, and roasted tomatoes, and peel the cooled boiled eggs and set aside.
Flake the salmon into chunks and toss gently through the salad.
Serve with the halved boiled eggs and scatter over the anchovy fillets if you'd like an extra salty kick.

name: Salmon Wedge Salad with Ranch Dressing
description: Everything you want from a salad. Ice-cold crunchy iceberg, crisp-skinned salmon flaked over the top, salty capers and a herby, garlicky ranch. On the table in 30 mins.
keywords: Salmon Wedge Salad with Ranch Dressing
Salmon Wedge Salad with Ranch Dressing recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Place the salmon fillets skin-side up on a lined baking tray. Rub all over with the olive oil and season generously with salt and black pepper. Roast for 12-15 mins, until just cooked through and the skin is crisp. This also works in an air fryer at 200°C for 10-12 mins.

While the salmon cooks, make the dressing. Add the Greek yoghurt, mayonnaise and Dijon mustard to a bowl. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and finely grate in the garlic, then finely chop the dill and chives and stir them through. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper. Add a splash of water to loosen the dressing if needed.
Remove any outer leaves from the iceberg, then cut it into quarters through the core, or six wedges if it's a big one. Arrange the wedges on a large serving platter.
Spoon the ranch dressing generously over and around the lettuce. Roughly chop the capers and scatter them over the top.

Flake the fish into large pieces over the salad. Pick over the remaining dill and scatter with the pickled chilli, if you're using it. Finish with plenty of black pepper and a drizzle of the extra virgin olive oil, then cut the remaining lemon into wedges to serve.

name: Salmon With Caramelised Onion Rice & Shaved Broccoli Salad
description: A faff-free dinner that'll introduce you to a brand-new way of eating broccoli. Simple goodness.
keywords: Salmon With Caramelised Onion Rice & Shaved Broccoli Salad
Salmon With Caramelised Onion Rice & Shaved Broccoli Salad recipe
instructions: Halve and finely slice the onion; finely chop the garlic.
Add the oil and butter to a large, non-stick pan and set over a medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 10–15 mins, stirring often, until soft, sticky, and golden.

Add the garlic and cook for 1–2 mins. Stir in the rice and pour over the water. Cover with a lid and cook on low heat for about 10 mins, until the rice is tender and water absorbed. Stir gently, cover, and let steam off the heat for 10 more minutes.

Meanwhile, prepare the broccoli salad. Trim the florets from the broccoli and finely slice each one (or shave with a mandoline). In a bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, yoghurt, za’atar (if using), tahini, salt and pepper. Add the broccoli and toss to coat. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Season the salmon with salt. Heat a frying pan over high heat with a glug of oil. Once hot, add the salmon skin-side down. Press down gently on the flesh so the skin makes even contact with the pan. Cook for 5–6 mins until the skin is crisp, then flip the fillets, turn off the heat, and let the residual heat finish cooking.
Serve the salmon over the caramelised onion rice with the broccoli salad and a sprinkle of extra za’atar, if using.

name: Salmon With Corn & Roasted Red Pepper Salad
description: Salmon fillets, charred corn and roasted red peppers come together to make a balanced weeknight meal ready in just 35 mins.
instructions: Microwave the rice according to packet instructions.
Meanwhile, drain the red peppers and thinly slice. Cut the kernels off the corn, pick the leaves off the herbs and finely slice the stems. Peel and finely dice the onion. Halve the tomatoes.
Add the onion into a large bowl with the zest of half a lemon and the juice of both. Season with salt and pepper, stir in 30ml of olive oil. Set aside.
Place a frying pan over a high heat, with no oil. Once hot, add half the corn kernels and cook until starting to char, 3-4 mins.

Meanwhile, lay the salmon skin-side down, in a cold non-stick frying pan. Place over a medium heat and cook for 10 mins until the skin is crisp and most of the salmon is pale pink. Flip over and remove the pan from the heat.
Add all the corn, roasted peppers, tomatoes, rice, chopped stems and herbs into the onion dressing, toss together. Season with salt and pepper.
Share the salad between your plates and top with the salmon and a drizzle of oil.

name: Salmon With Crispy Bagel-Seasoning New Potatoes & Pickled Onions
description: We’ve taken everything bagel seasoning and thrown it onto the crispiest new potatoes. Paired with zingy salmon, it’s a winner.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Slice the new potatoes in half and toss with two-thirds of the olive oil, salt, and pepper. Wrap the garlic bulb in foil after coating it in a little oil.

Spread the potatoes onto a low-sided baking tray (you might need two so as not to overcrowd) along with the wrapped garlic and roast for 20 mins. Remove from the oven, toss the potatoes, then sprinkle over the sesame and poppy seeds. Return to the oven for a further 15 mins until golden and crispy.
Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion and place in a small bowl with the juice of half a lemon and a pinch of salt. Scrunch with your fingers and set aside to lightly pickle. Set aside.
Place the salmon on a separate baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 8 mins, depending on the thickness. Remove from the oven and rest for 5 mins.
Unwrap the roasted garlic and squeeze the cloves into a small bowl. Finely chop the herbs and mix with the cream cheese, lemon juice and zest, capers, garlic, salt, and pepper until smooth.
To serve, plate up the crispy potatoes with a generous dollop of herby cream cheese, flaked salmon, pickled onions, and extra herbs and lemon if you like.

name: Salmon With Kimchi & Tahini Noodles
description: Salmon, kimchi and tahini combine in this bright and beautiful recipe. It's a fresh and healthy lunch or dinner that's packed with flavour.
keywords: Salmon With Kimchi & Tahini Noodles recipe
instructions: Mix all the dressing ingredients in a large bowl, ready for the noodles.

Cook the noodles according to packet instructions. Before draining, reserve half a mug of the cooking water. Add a few tablespoons at a time of this to the dressing to loosen it to your desired consistency.
Drain and rinse the noodles under cold water until completely cooled. Toss with the dressing.
Finely slice the cucumber into long matchsticks and set aside in a bowl with a small pinch of salt.

Season the salmon with salt. Heat a frying pan over high heat with a glug of oil. Once hot, add the salmon skin-side down. Press gently on the flesh so the skin makes even contact with the pan. Cook for 5–6 mins until the skin is crisp, then flip the fillets to colour on each side for a minute or two before turning off the heat, and letting the residual heat finish cooking.
Divide the noodles between bowls and top with cucumber and heaped spoonfuls of kimchi.
Flake the salmon over the top and finish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

name: Salmon with Charred Broccoli & Fennel Slaw
description: Charred broccoli and crisp fennel tossed through a lemony, herby yoghurt dressing, with golden pan-fried salmon on top. Perfect for serving up to your pals in the summer and you can get it on the table in under 30 mins.
keywords: Salmon with Charred Broccoli Slaw recipe
instructions: Cut the florets away from the broccoli head, roughly chopping any larger ones so they're all a similar size, then thinly slice the stalk. Finely slice the fennel, finely grate the garlic and roughly chop the dill. If you're not a fennel fan, shredded white cabbage works as a great substitute here.
Stir together the Greek yoghurt, the garlic, the Dijon mustard, the lemon zest, half the chopped dill and the juice of half the lemon. Season well with salt and black pepper.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Season the salmon all over with salt and black pepper, then cook for 3-4 mins on each side, depending on the thickness, until deeply golden and just cooked through. Transfer to a plate. This also works in an air fryer at 200°C for 8-10 mins, skin-side up, until the skin is crisp and the fish flakes easily.

Return the pan to a high heat and add the broccoli (you won't need any extra oil here). Leave it undisturbed for a minute or two until lightly charred in places, then toss and cook for up to 5 mins more, until charred but still crisp. Squeeze over the juice of the remaining lemon half.
Toss the fennel with most of the yoghurt dressing, then fold through the charred broccoli and the remaining dill.
Divide the slaw between plates and top with the salmon. Spoon over the remaining yoghurt dressing and cut the remaining lemon into wedges for squeezing over.

name: Salmon, Coriander & Miso High Protein Smash
description: Here's a protein-packed recipe that you can 'smoosh' over a bagel, toast, pitta bread or whatever takes your fancy. It's a gamechanger.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Add the salmon to a tray with the water and 1/2 the soy sauce. Cook in the oven for 15 minutes.
4 minutes before the cooking time for the salmon is up, add the broccoli to the tray. Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander.
Roughly chop the cooked broccoli into bite-size pieces, and use a fork to break the salmon into flakes.
Mix together the miso paste, vinegar and ginger paste in a medium bowl.
Add the salmon and broccoli to the bowl, followed by the coriander. Mix to combine.
‘Smoosh’ over toast, pitta bread, a bagel or whatever you fancy.

name: Salsa Verde
description: A classic tomatillo salsa to add some heat to any taco. There are many salsa recipes, but this one is probably the one that all Mexicans love. I highly recommend using fresh tomatillos when you make it at home.
instructions: Peel the onion and garlic cloves and add them to a saucepan along with the fresh tomatillos and jalapeños. Cover them with water. Bring to a boil over a medium heat then lower the heat and simmer for 10 mins. Meanwhile, roughly chop the coriander.
Strain the vegetables from the water (don’t discard the water yet) and transfer them to a blender, adding the coriander, salt and pinch of caster sugar.
Blend until smooth. If the salsa is too thick, add a splash of water until it’s the desired consistency.

name: Salsa Verde Pasta
description: Salsa verde is one of our favourite sauces. It’s often served with meat and fish but this oily, herby sauce makes for the best pasta sauce – don’t be afraid to add plenty of olive oil, it needs it!
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.

Start by making the salsa verde. Finely chop the herbs and add them to a large bowl. Add the anchovies to a mini chopper or food processor along with the oil from the tin. Add the dijon, mustard, garlic and lemon juice and blend until smooth. Add this mixture to the bowl with the herbs. Add enough olive oil to the salsa verde to make it a loose consistency – it can take quite a lot. Add the capers.
Drop the pasta into the boiling water and cook according to package instructions. Once the pasta is cooked, use the tongs to slosh the pasta into the bowl – toss well then twirl onto plates.
Top with grated Parmesan to serve.

name: Salt & Pepper Roasted Chicken Thighs
description: A healthy spin on a takeaway classic. Pair this with some vegetables and some slow-release carbohydrates for the ultimate weeknight dinner.
keywords: Salt & Pepper Roasted Chicken Thighs recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Slice the onions and finely slice the garlic, then spread them evenly on a baking sheet.
In a large bowl, mix the salt, MSG (if using), sugar, five spice, white pepper, black pepper, garlic powder, cumin, and olive oil. Add the chicken thighs and toss to coat well.
Arrange the chicken thighs evenly over the onions on the baking sheet.
Bake for 30 minutes or until the chicken is golden, crispy, and cooked through.
Serve immediately with your favourite sides.

name: Salt & Pepper Tofu
description: Nothing hits the spot like salt and pepper tofu. This fakeaway classic is the epitome of a crowdpleaser. Whip it up in just 20 minutes.
instructions: In a bowl, add roughly 1 tbsp of pepper, a big pinch of salt and the sugar. Give it a mix and set aside.
Slice your tofu into 1 inch cubes. Add the cornflour to a bowl and dip the tofu in one by one. Fry time! Pour roughly 1 inch of vegetable oil into a large frying pan on a medium-high heat.
When the oil is hot, add the tofu and fry until crispy on all sides before removing from the heat and set aside for later.
Finely chop your spring onions, garlic and chillies. In a new pan, add a glug of vegetable oil and fry the spring onions, garlic and chilli on a medium heat until soft and fragrant.
Add the tofu and stir to combine with the spring onion mixture. Sprinkle the black pepper, salt and sugar mix over the tofu and stir through until fully coated.

name: Salt and Pepper Parmentier Potatoes
description: We have reinvented your classic takeaway salt and pepper fries. Tiny crispy nuggets of potato, loaded with onions and peppers take this to the next level.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C/392°F and turn on your kettle.
Peel and chop your potatoes into small cubes. Add them to a large saucepan and cover with boiling water. Once they've come back up to the boil, cook for 5 minutes.
In a large oven tray, drizzle in a large glug of oil and pop it into the oven to heat up.

Once the potatoes are cooked, drain the water and put them back into the saucepan. Add 2 tablespoons of flour and put a lid on the pan. Shake up the potatoes to make them fluffy – this will make them super crunchy.
Place the potatoes into the tray and put it back into the oven and cook for 30-45 minutes, stirring regularly so they brown evenly.
Whilst your potatoes cook, chop up the onions and peppers into chunks a similar size to the potatoes. Slice the chilli and spring onions, then grate the ginger and garlic.

When your potatoes are almost done, heat up a large wok to the highest setting. Get the wok smoking hot so you can char your veg. Drizzle in a large glug of oil and add in your onions, peppers and chilli. Cook for 5 minutes until charred and softened. Add in the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes. Add in your five-spice and MSG.
Throw in all your crispy potatoes and toss to generously coat them in your seasoned veg. Season with salt, sprinkle with your spring onions and enjoy immediately.

name: Salt-Baked Sea Bass
description: One for a special occasion. Perfectly tender, flaky fish with delicious caramelised potatoes and garlicky kale.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Cut the new potatoes and tomatoes roughly into halves, then tip
them into a roasting tin big enough so they can spread out and not
sit on top of each other (this is key to crispy edges).
Pour over a good few glugs of olive oil, then scatter over
2–3 sprigs of thyme, a couple of pinches of salt and a good grind
of pepper. Toss everything together, then put onto the top shelf of
the oven. After 20 mins, remove the tin, give everything a good
shake and return to the oven for another 15 mins.
Meanwhile, prep your fish. Pat the sea bass dry with some
kitchen paper and rub a pinch of salt into the cavity. Cut 3–4 lemon
slices and stuff into the cavity with a few thyme sprigs.
Pour the coarse sea salt into a large bowl, add 4 tbsp of
water and stir together. Find a roasting tin large enough to hold
the fish and tip a layer of salt into it, about 1cm thick, just
under where the fish will sit and place the fish on top. Then cover
the whole fish with the rest of the salt, patting down until you have
encased the entire thing neatly in a salt mound.
Now back to the potatoes. Once all the liquid from the tomatoes
has evaporated and everything is starting to go golden and sticky,
it’s time to put in the fish. Slide the fish onto the shelf below the
potatoes and cook for 25 mins.
Meanwhile, strip the cavolo nero leaves from the tough stems
and chop them into strips about 4cm thick. Steam these for
3 mins, then tip into a bowl. Add a squeeze of lemon juice, the
chilli flakes, a good glug of olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper
and give it a good mix.
Take out the fish and check to see if the potatoes are done.
The tomatoes should have disintegrated and everything should
be golden and sticky. If they aren’t ready yet, whack the oven
temperature up to 220°C 7 for 5–10 mins.
Make the chilli oil: finely chop the chilli and whisk into the olive
oil along with grated zest and juice of the lemon.
When everything is ready, smash the top of the salt crust with
the back of a spoon and clear away all the salt. Peel off the skin and
use a large knife or fish slice to serve the fish.
Once the top side of the fish is served, peel back and remove
the fish bones to get at the fillet underneath. Serve the fish drizzled
with the chilli oil, with the potatoes and tomatoes and cavolo nero
alongside.

name: Salted Caramel Bars
description: Your snack drawer just levelled up. These savoury and sticky caramel bars are plant-based, freezer-friendly and far too easy to eat five at once!
instructions: Blitz the almonds in a food processor until crumbly - don’t go too fine, you still want some texture.
Chuck in the dates, almond butter, maca powder, vanilla extract and a pinch of salt. Blend again until it comes together into a sticky dough.
Line a loaf tin with baking parchment. Tip in the mixture and press it down firmly to an even layer.
Scatter over the extra nuts, if using, and press them gently into the surface.
Chill in the fridge until firm for at least an hour then slice into bars.
Once ready, wrap the bars in baking paper and chill or freeze for the ultimate grab-and-go snack. These last for a week in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer.

name: Salted Caramel Blondies
description: Liam's salted caramel blondies, a perfect combination of sweet and salty marbled with Dr. Oetker White Chocolate Chunks for an added richness.
instructions: Heat oven to 160°C.
Line a 20cm square tin with butter and baking parchment. Melt the butter in a small saucepan or microwave.
Meanwhile, add your toffees to a small saucepan with 20ml milk. Heat over a low heat until you have a thick caramel. Season with a pinch of salt.
Whisk your brown sugar into the melted butter, then add your eggs, vanilla bean, Dr Oetker caramel flavouring, sea salt flakes and 50ml milk. Whisk until you have a thick and silky mixture.
Sift in your flour and baking powder, then fold through the mixture. Add all but a handful of white chocolate chunks and fold these through the mixture.

Pour your mixture into your tin. Bake for 25 minutes, then remove from the oven and add your remaining white chocolate chunks and a drizzle of your salted caramel. Return to the oven for another 15 minutes. They will have set edges but a slightly jiggly middle when set.
Leave to cool to room temperature. Chill in the fridge for a couple of hours - this will give them their super fudgy texture. Cut into squares and serve.

name: Salted Caramel Brownies
description: Rich, fudgy brownies with a homemade salted caramel drizzle. Delicious served warm with vanilla ice cream.
instructions: Start by making the salted caramel. Add about ⅕ of the sugar to a large pan and set it over a medium heat to caramelise. You want to caramelise it very gradually. Starting with your layer of sugar in the base of the pan, resist the temptation to stir but gently ‘swipe’ the sugar from side to side to ensure it’s heating evenly. Turn the heat down if you think it's looking too dark – you want a lovely light caramel colour.

Once this first layer looks like it’s starting to melt, add another layer (about ⅕ of the sugar again), and so on until all the sugar has dissolved and caramelised. This will take a while but is worth it! Make sure your butter is at room temperature.
Gently warm the cream in another pan, then slowly add it to your caramelised sugar, stirring to incorporate it gradually.
Leave to cool then add the sea salt to taste.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 180°C fan. Line a 25cm square tin with baking parchment.

For the brownie batter, whisk the eggs in a large mixing bowl. Melt the chocolate in 10-second bursts in the microwave or in a small heatproof bowl set over a pot of boiling water, then add to the bowl with the eggs. Set aside.

Melt the butter in a small pan set over a low heat, then add the sugar and stir until dissolved. Pour into the bowl with the chocolate and eggs. Use an electric whisk to beat the mixture for 3–4 mins (you can do this by hand, but it will take longer).
In another bowl, whisk together the sifted cocoa powder and flours. Fold the cocoa flour mix into the chocolate mixture, then stir in the pecans and vanilla extract.
Transfer the batter to your prepared tin and drizzle/pour the salted caramel over the brownie mix, however much you like (reserve the leftovers).
Bake the brownies in the oven for 18-20 mins, or until you have a crisp top and a middle that wobbles when you gently shake the tray.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool and set in the tin before transferring to a plate. Eat them warm, or keep them in the fridge for later.

name: Salted Caramel Burnt Basque Cheesecake
description: These beautiful, burnished cheesecakes come from the San Sebastián region of Spain but this is a twist on the classic that you can try in your kitchen at home.
instructions: First, line a 7-inch cake tin with greaseproof baking paper, making sure the paper is above the edge of the cake (the tin will be really full). Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Make the caramel by adding 3/4 of the sugar to a pan and heating it slowly until you have a dark caramel. Add in the double cream and stir until you have a smooth caramel. Add the salt then allow to completely cool.

In a bowl, cream together the cream cheese and the remaining caster sugar. Next, sieve in the flour and mix until it’s combined with no lumps. Now beat in the eggs, one at a time, until the batter comes to a nice smooth consistency.
Once the caramel sauce is cool, add it to the cream cheese and then stir until it's fully incorporated into the mix.
Add the mix to the lined tin and bake in the oven for 30 mins
Remove from the oven and allow to fully cool (3-4 hours) before serving to allow the middle to settle.

name: Salted Caramel Kahlúa Elixir
description: A sweet and delicious cocktail with a lovely salted rim. This is a delicious coffee cocktail.
instructions: Rim your chosen glass with caramel sauce and a sprinkle of salt, then set aside in the freezer to set.
Put your Kahlúa into a cocktail shaker with salted caramel vodka, dark rum, and syrup with some ice. Shake well for 10 seconds.
Fill your glass with large ice and strain your cocktail in. Garnish with a sprinkle of sea salt and enjoy.

name: Salted Caramel Popcorn
description: Moreish, crunchy and salty sweet homemade popcorn. Get a film on and get stuck in. The added baking soda and long exposure to a low heat here lightens the caramel to a crisp crunch, so it’s not so heavy and doesn’t stick in your teeth the way caramel can. Enjoy, plus it's also great for making ahead!
instructions: Heat the oven to 100°C fan. Line two baking trays with parchment paper.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the maize, cover with a lid and heat gently. Shake the pan and wait to hear the corn popping. Once it has all popped – this should take 4–5 mins – remove any unpopped corn, transfer the popped corn to a metal or glass bowl and set aside.

Heat the sugar, salt, butter and liquid glucose in a heavy-bottomed pan set over a low heat. Stir slowly with a wooden spoon to gently incorporate everything as the butter melts and the sugar dissolves. Once the sugar has dissolved, turn the temperature up to high and heat for 3 mins, then remove from the heat and add the bicarbonate of soda (it will fizz up!).
Spoon the caramel over the popped corn and mix so it’s lightly and evenly coated.
Transfer to your prepared baking trays and bake for 45-60 mins, or until slightly puffed – it should be light and crispy, so if it’s not quite ready, return it to the oven for a little longer.
Remove and allow to cool a little before breaking apart into small clusters.

name: Salted Caramel Profiteroles
description: Profiteroles are easier to make than you might think. Well, these ones are.
instructions: Melt 100g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add 240ml water and bring to a rapid simmer.
Add the flour and a pinch of salt and mix continuously with a wooden spoon until the dough comes away from the sides of the pan.
Transfer the dough to a mixing bowl and leave to cool for 10 mins.
Heat your oven to 220°C / fan 200°C and line 2 large baking trays with greaseproof paper.
