Add 1 egg to the cooled dough mixture and beat with a wooden spoon until combined. Repeat with the remaining eggs, ensuring each egg is fully incorporated before adding the next.
Using a teaspoon, spoon 15 blobs of the dough onto each of the baking trays. You want each blob to be 1 heaped teaspoon worth of dough.
Bake for 18 to 20 mins, or until golden brown and risen.
Meanwhile, place the remaining 60g butter in a saucepan with the light brown sugar, single cream, vanilla extract and 1 teaspoon of salt and bring to a simmer over medium-low heat.
Cook for 5 mins, stirring constantly, then transfer to a heatproof bowl to cool. The sauce will thicken as it cools.
Take the profiteroles out of the oven and cut a small split in the base of each one to let the steam out. Cool on a wire rack before filling.
Meanwhile, crush up the peanuts.
Once the profiteroles have cooled, halve them horizontally and fill each of them with a heaped tablespoon of Jude’s Salted Caramel Ice Cream.
Dip the top of each of the assembled profiteroles in the salted caramel sauce and sprinkle with some crushed peanuts.
Stack them up onto a large plate, serve and enjoy!

name: Salted Caramel Sauce
description: A handy recipe for luxurious salted caramel. Delicious drizzled over just about anything.
instructions: Add about ⅕ of the sugar to a large pan and set it over a medium heat to caramelise. You want to caramelise it very gradually. Starting with your layer of sugar in the base of the pan, resist the temptation to stir but gently ‘swipe’ the sugar from side to side to ensure it’s heating evenly. Turn the heat down if you think it's looking too dark – you want a lovely light caramel colour.

Once this first layer looks like it’s starting to melt, add another layer (about ⅕ of the sugar again), and so on until all the sugar has dissolved and caramelised. This will take a while but is worth it!
Gently warm the cream in another pan, then slowly add it to your caramelised sugar, stirring to incorporate it gradually.
Leave to cool then add the sea salt to taste.

name: Salted Crunchy Nut Cornflake Tart
description: This isn't just any old cornflake tart recipe. This is a salted Crunchy Nut cornflake tart. It's sweet, it's salty, and it can be all yours.
keywords: Salted Crunchy Nut Cornflake Tart recipe
best cornflake tart recipe cornflake tart
instructions: If you're making your own pastry (if not, skip to the next step), start by chopping the butter into small pieces. Tip them into a bowl with the flour and icing sugar. Using your hands, rub together quickly until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolks and cold water and stir until the dough comes together. Form into a ball, wrap in cling film and put in the fridge for 30 mins.

Heat the oven to 180°C. Roll the pastry out on a lightly floured surface into a circle that’s 2cm bigger than a 23cm tart tin and around 1cm thick. Dust with a little flour, then roll the pastry circle onto the rolling pin and drape the pastry over the tart tin. Press the edges into place, making sure there is pastry overhanging, then fold the edges back in on themselves to double up, still allowing space for overhang. Prick the base with a fork and put in the fridge for 10 mins to set.

Scrunch up a piece of baking parchment and use it to line the tart, filling it with baking beans (if you don’t have baking beans, use rice). Pop in the oven for 15-20 mins, then remove the beans and paper and bake for a further 5-10 mins or until the pastry looks dry and golden. Using a serrated knife, trim the pastry edges down.

For the filling, melt the butter and golden syrup together in a saucepan until combined, then tip in the cornflakes and peanuts, crushing slightly. Mix well. Spread the jam over the pastry base, then top with the cornflake mixture, pressing it down and piling it up. Bake for 7-10 mins until golden and smelling nutty. Allow to cool and set, then serve with hot custard.

name: Salted Honey & Yoghurt Cheesecake
description: This is a lighter version of the cheesecake you might already be familiar with: it’s rich thanks to a combo of soft ricotta, tangy yoghurt and honey.
instructions:
Line a sieve with a clean tea towel and set it over a bowl. Add
the yoghurt and ricotta to the lined sieve, then leave to strain for a
couple of hours at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a 15cm springform tin with two squares of baking paper.
Tip the ricotta and yoghurt into a large bowl, discarding any of
the liquid that has come out of it, and whisk until smooth.
Add all but a tablespoon of the honey and whisk again. Add the
eggs one at a time, whisking until you have a totally smooth batter
before adding the next one. Add the vanilla extract, the zest of the
orange and the sea salt, then whisk until just combined.
Pour the cheesecake mixture into the lined tin and bake in the
middle of the oven for 45 minutes. When it is done, it should be set
around the edges but jiggle in the middle.
Leave to cool to room temperature, then pop your cheesecake
into the fridge to chill for a couple of hours.
When ready to serve, finely chop the pistachios. Remove the
cheesecake from the tin and top with the remaining honey and
chopped pistachios.

name: Saltfish Fritters
description: These crisp, savoury, and spicy fish cakes are a Grenadian classic from Juliet Friday Smith. Eat them with fried breadfruit balls and scotch bonnet chilli jam.
instructions: Rinse then soak the saltfish in cold water overnight. Drain and soak again for 1-2 hours. Drain again. Have a taste and if the saltfish is still quite salty, add enough water to cover then boil for 10 mins. Strain, and remove any bones before breaking up using a fork or pulse a few times in a food processor until flaked/in chunks.

Finely chop the ginger, spring onion, garlic, coriander, parsley, peppers and onion. Add the fish, picked thyme leaves, spring onions, ginger, onion, red pepper, garlic, coriander, and parsley to a large bowl and mix well. Add spices: turmeric, nutmeg, allspice, black pepper, cayenne if using, and lime juice. Mix again.

Tip in the cornflour, baking powder then start adding the plain flour bit by bit, followed by some water until desired consistency is achieved. You want it holding together but not too dry. If in doubt, add less water than more.
Rest mixture for about 20 mins to allow the flavours and batter to come together.

Fill a large pot halfway with vegetable oil, and set over medium heat. Once the oil has reached 170°C, scoop about 1 tbsp of the batter to the pot. Fry on each side/overall for 3-5 minutes until golden brown.
Once fried, drain on kitchen roll then serve! These are great bites to eat with any condiments, try our Scotch Bonnet Chilli Jam.

name: Sambal Aubergine
description: Niyi (aka @novicekitchen_) joined us to make the most delicious sambal aubergine – an umami bomb of a dish that reminds Niyi of his travels around Indonesia.
instructions: Cut the aubergine into one-inch thick circles, place in a bowl and season generously with salt then set aside for 15 mins (this draws out the moisture and will give the aubergine a better sear).
Finely slice your radishes and set aside.
Now to make the sambal, peel the garlic, ginger and shallots.
Add the garlic, ginger, shallots, chillies and makrut lime leaves (or lemongrass) into a blender and pulse into a chunky paste.
In a frying pan, pour in 3 tbsp of olive oil, add the sambal paste and 1 tbsp of Demerara sugar. Cook this on a medium to low heat for 5 mins until fragrant.
Once the sambal is cooked, pour this into a bowl with soy sauce and honey. Mix this all together to create the final sauce and season to taste.
Heat up some olive oil in a frying pan on a medium to high heat until the oil is very hot.
Place the aubergines in the pan and sear for 6 mins on each side or until golden brown.
Add a generous knob of vegan butter to the frying pan. Whilst the butter is melting, pour in the sambal mix and use a spoon to baste the aubergine slices for 1-2 mins.
Garnish with some coriander and radishes and serve on a bed of rice.

name: Sambal Green Bean Omelette with Rice
description: This is a recreation of one of Xien's favourite childhood dishes – Chinese homestyle green bean omelette served with rice, and Mama Yu’s Sambal, of course. It’s a simple dish but when seasoned right, the flavours really come out, making it the perfect quick and easy weeknight meal.
keywords: Sambal Green Bean Omelette with Rice
Sambal Green Bean Omelette with Rice recipe
instructions: Wash your rice three times until the water runs clear. Drain, then transfer to a large saucepan and add water until it reaches just below your first knuckle. Bring to the boil over a medium-high heat, then turn the heat to low and cover with a lid for 12 mins.
Meanwhile, mince the garlic. Wash the green beans, chop off the ends then finely chop into small pieces.
Whisk the eggs in a large bowl and season with the salt, white pepper and curry powder.

Add a glug of oil to a wok over a medium-high heat and add the minced garlic. Fry until lightly golden, then add chopped green beans and sauté for 2-3 mins. Remove and add everything to the bowl of whisked eggs.
Add a small ladle of oil to the now-empty wok, then add the eggs and green beans mixture back into the wok.
Fry the eggs for 1-2 mins on one side, then flip and fry for 1-2 mins, depending on how cooked you like your omelette.
Serve the omelette with rice, sambal and crispy shallots on top. Enjoy!

name: Sambal Smashed Potatoes with Peanut Sauce
description: Crispy, smashed potatoes dipped in the dreamiest peanut sauce with a drizzle of spicy sambal on top. It’s the best of both worlds. What more could you want Mob?
keywords: Sambal smashed potatoes with satay sauce recipes
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil, then add your potatoes. Simmer for 15 mins until your potatoes are tender, then tip them into a colander and leave to steam dry for a few mins.
Bash a clove of garlic with the side of your knife to crush it slightly. Pour a good glug of olive oil into a large baking tray along with your garlic and heat in the oven for 5 mins.
Meanwhile, make your peanut sauce. Mince the garlic and finely chop the shallot.
Get a pot on to a medium heat, add 2 tbsps of vegetable oil and your chopped alliums. Fry for a few mins until golden.

Add the chilli and turmeric powder, and mix well. Pour in 180ml water, coconut milk and soy sauce. Add in tamarind, sugar, peanut butter and a smashed lemongrass stalk. Bring to a boil, making sure to regularly stir so the bottom of the pot doesn’t burn (this will take around 5 mins).
Turn the heat down for the peanut sauce and let it simmer for 30 mins.

Back to the potatoes. Using the base of a heavy pan, lightly press down on your cooked potatoes to individually smash them. Add them to your baking tray of hot oil in the oven and sprinkle with a generous pinch of salt. Roast for 25 mins until the bases are crisp and golden.
Meanwhile, make your sambal sauce. Roughly chop the garlic, ginger and shallots and finely chop the lemongrass. Blend with 3 tbsp of vegetable oil and transfer to a bowl. This is your garlic paste.
Roughly chop the chillies and tomato. Blend your chopped chillies and tomatoes up with chilli flakes and 2 tbsp of vegetable oil. This is your chilli paste.
Heat your wok with 200ml of vegetable oil on low heat. Add the garlic paste and cook for 15 mins.
Flip your potatoes over after the first 25 mins of roasting and return to the oven for another 25 mins until the potatoes are golden all over.
Back to the sambal. Add in the chilli paste, lime juice and sugar to your garlic paste in the pan and cook for another 20 mins on low heat until the oil separates from the paste.
Swoosh your peanut sauce on a large plate and top with your smashed potatoes. Drizzle some sambal on top, garnish with chopped coriander and crushed peanuts, and tuck in.

name: Sambal Sprouts
description: Spicy, tangy and incredibly delicious Brussels sprouts. Who ever thought we would be fighting for the last sprout?
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Cut all the Brussels sprouts in half and toss with olive oil and salt.
Pop these onto a baking tray cut-side down and bake for 30 mins, turning halfway through until caramelised and crisp.
Now, make the sambal. Blend up the red chillies with 2 tbsp of water until smooth and transfer into a bowl. Blend up the shallots, ginger, garlic and lemongrass with 2 tbsp of water until smooth.
Heat up 100ml of vegetable oil in a large wok and add in the red chillies. Cook for 10 mins until the oil is stained red and the chillies darken.
Add in the shallot mix and continue cooking for another 10 mins.
Pour in the tomato purée and cook for 5 mins until the purée has darkened, then add in the chopped tomatoes, brown sugar, fish sauce and 1 tsp salt. Cook for 5 mins or until the oil separates.
Add in the sprouts and toss well. Taste and adjust the seasoning if necessary.
Toast the peanuts and lightly crush them. Sprinkle the peanuts over the sprouts and serve.

name: Sangria
description: Sangria. It's one of the best drinks on the whole damn planet. God bless the Spanish for inventing something to use all those miscellaneous leftover wines for. Here's how to make the perfect sangria.
instructions: Start off my slicing then quartering the lemon and one of the oranges, as well as chopping the apple into small pieces.
Juice the other oranges, mix in the sugar and set aside.
Put all the fruit and orange juice in a large pitcher along with the bottle of wine and double measure of brandy.
Chill for 4 hours to overnight in the fridge to allow all the flavours to meddle and for the mixture to cool.
Serve in a glass with ice, top it off with sparkling water and a slice of orange as garnish. Enjoy.

name: Sardine Spaghetti
description: A simple store-cupboard pasta that's packed with flavour and perfect for any day of the week.
instructions: Finely chop the garlic and shallots.
Add a big glug of olive oil and sauté the shallots, garlic, and chilli flakes.
Add the anchovy fillets and break them down into the shallots with the back of a wooden spoon.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes with the olive oil from the sardines and cook for 15 mins until the sauce has reduced.
Pop the pasta on to cook in a pot of salted boiling water.
Add in the pasta with 100ml of pasta water to the tomatoes and squeeze in the juice of a lemon. Pop the sardines in too.
Finely chop the dill.
In a small frying pan add a glug of olive oil and add in the drained capers. Fry for 5-6 mins until they are crispy and then drain on a paper towel.
Add ¾ of the dill to the pasta and toss well. Season with salt and pepper as necessary.
Serve in bowls with dollops of ricotta, crispy capers and reserved dill.

name: Sardine, Lemon & Jalapeño Linguine
description: Cooking the lemon for a minute in the boiling water stops this pasta from becoming too bitter, and instead helps create a delicious sweet and salty sauce when paired with the nutty brown butter and tinned sardines. The breadcrumbs are optional but incredible if you have the time to make them!
instructions: If you’re making the breadcrumbs, put the slices of bread and ½ the jalepeno into a mini chopper and blitz into breadcrumbs. Add some olive oil to a pan over a medium high heat and then add the breadcrumbs. Cook for 2 - 3 mins or until the breadcrumbs are golden brown and crisp. Tip into a small bowl. Finely dice the remaining ½ jalapeno and add the breadcrumbs along with a big pinch of salt, set aside.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Thinly slice the lemon into rounds, removing any seeds. Drop the lemon slices into the boiling water and cook for a minute to soften and mellow. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
In the same saucepan, add the spaghetti and cook following pack instructions until al dente. Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic and thinly slice 1/2 the jalapeño.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the butter. Let it melt and cook for 2-3 mins until it turns nutty and brown. Watch it closely so it doesn’t burn. Add the garlic and jalapeño, then cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant and softened.
Add the blanched lemon slices to the brown butter and let everything bubble together for 2-3 mins so the lemons soak up all that flavour and lightly caramelise at the edges.

Once the pasta is cooked, use tongs to slosh the pasta into the brown butter pan. Toss well until glossy and emulsified, adding a little more water if needed. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.

Gently break the sardines into large pieces and add them to the pan. Carefully fold them through the pasta so they stay chunky and don’t completely disappear. Cook for 30 seconds just to warm through.
Divide between bowls and top generously with the crispy spicy breadcrumbs.

name: Satay Chicken & Roasted Squash Curry
description: We wanted to create a curry with blended roasted butternut as the base, and this is what we landed on. Guaranteed it will become a staple in your kitchen.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Cut your butternut squash into cubes. Transfer to a baking tray and drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt. Roast in the oven for 45 minutes.
Chop your ginger, chilli, garlic, spring onion and peppers.
Cut your chicken into strips. Drizzle olive oil into a pan and add the chicken strips and stir. Add the ginger, chilli, garlic, spring onion and peppers.
Once your butternut squash is cooked, add it to a blender with 50ml of water and a tbsp of peanut butter. Blend until smooth.
Add the blended mixture to the pan along with the coconut milk. Allow it to bubble down and thicken.
Add a handful of coriander, salt, pepper and the juice of a whole lemon.
Serve on steaming rice (cook according to pack instructions) and sprinkle some crushed peanuts over the top. Tuck in to the creamiest curry ever!

name: Satay Chicken Burgers
description: Chargrilled, fragrant chicken with the most luscious satay mayo in a squishy bun. Your new favourite summer barbecue dish.
instructions: Roughly chop your lemongrass and garlic.
Pop them in a pestle and mortar and bash to a fine paste. Add 1 tbsp of your chilli oil, your ground coriander and turmeric and bash again until all combined.

Spoon your paste into a bowl and add your chicken thigh fillets along with a good pinch of salt, a twist of pepper and a drizzle of vegetable oil. Give it all a good mix, then pop in the fridge to marinate for an hour.
Make your satay mayo. Pop your peanut butter in a bowl along with your remaining tbsp of chilli oil, coconut yoghurt, soy sauce and mayonnaise. Add 2 tbsp of boiling water and give it a good mix.
Slaw time. Peel your carrots and julienne them. Finely shred your red cabbage. Pop it all in a bowl along with your coriander leaves and squeeze in your lime juice. Give it a good mix.
Heat a griddle pan on a medium-high heat. Add your chicken thighs and cook for about 4 mins on each side until tender and cooked through with a lovely charred exterior.
Halve your brioche buns and toast them in a dry frying pan.

Assembly time. Spread some of your satay mayo on the base of your bun, then add a chicken fillet on top. Top with a good handful of slaw. Spread a little more mayo on your burger bun lid, then pop it on top of the slaw. Eat and enjoy!

name: Satay Chicken Rice Bowls
description: This recipe took about 15 attempts to get it nailed. You’re gonna be happy we persisted, because the satay sauce is an absolute banger.
instructions:
Get a large frying pan over a high heat. While it is getting hot,
season the mini chicken fillets lightly with salt and black pepper.
Drizzle some olive oil into the pan. Chuck in the chicken and fry
for 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until browned.
Meanwhile, cut one lime in half and the other into four wedges.
Set aside.
Satay sauce time. Put the peanut butter, soy sauce, creamed coconut and chilli flakes to taste into a bowl. Squeeze in the juice of the lime halves. Boil the water and pour into the satay mix. Stir with a fork briefly to combine – don’t worry if there are a few lumps of coconut as they will cook out in the pan later.
Pour the satay sauce over the chicken in the pan and tip in the
edamame beans and mangetout. Tip in the packets of rice, stir to
break up the grains, then cook for a further 2 minutes to heat the
rice through until steaming.
Pile the satay chicken rice into four bowls and then tear over the
coriander. Scatter with extra chilli flakes and serve with the lime
wedges and extra soy sauce, if you like.

name: Satay Sweet Potato Noodles
description: Creamy satay noodles meet golden roasted sweet potato. A super comforting, nutty midweek win that’s big on flavour, light on effort.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings 
Heat the oven to 180°C.

Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into bite-sized chunks. Slice the pepper into thin strips. Tip both into a large baking tray, drizzle with sunflower oil and a pinch of salt, then roast for 25 mins until soft and golden.

Meanwhile, finely grate the garlic and ginger.
Place a small saucepan over a medium heat with a splash of sunflower oil. Gently cook the garlic and ginger for 2 mins. Add the peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, curry powder, coconut milk and lime juice. Stir until smooth and gently warmed through, about 3-4 mins, then remove from the heat.
Cook the rice noodles following pack instructions. Drain, then rinse under cold water to stop them sticking.
Thinly slice the spring onion. Slice the cucumber into half-moons.
Toss the noodles with the satay sauce and a splash of water to loosen it slightly (it will thicken as it cools).

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Dish out the noodles and top with the roasted sweet potato and peppers, and cucumber.
Parents Plate: Do the same and add the extra garnish of sliced spring onion.

name: Saucy & Zingy Three-Bean Salad
description: I love a citrusy Aguachile vibe in the heat, it's light enough for the summer but still packs a punch. This salad takes inspo from the flavours, but swaps out fish with beans to make more of a dense bean salad situ. Since the beans marinate in that zingy sauce, it only gets better with time - making it perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Thinly slice the red onion and toss with the jalapeño pickle brine for the salad. Season with salt and set aside to quick-pickle. Chop the feta into 1cm cubes and defrost the edamame.

Now make the sauce. Roughly chop the tomatoes and add to a blender with the hemp seeds. Blitz until smooth, then season with the hot sauce (start witha dash at first and add to your taste), the remaining jalapeño pickle brine, salt and the juice of the limes, it should taste salty and zingy.

Drain and rinse the kidney beans and butterbeans, then tip into a large bowl. Add the jalapeños, feta, pickled onion, edamame and remaining hemp seeds, then toss everything together with a drizzle of olive oil.
Divide the bean salad between bowls or boxes and pour over the sauce. Serve with the tortilla crisps.

name: Saucy 'Nduja Chicken & Chickpea Traybake
description: Crispy-skinned thighs roasted in a sweet and spicy yoghurt sauce that blitzes down to something silky and absolutely addictive. Served with chickpeas and flatbreads and you're sorted. Love this? Try Ixta's dinner party-worthy version: Spicy Mango, 'Nduja & Scotch Bonnet Roast Chicken.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Peel the garlic and add whole into a large high-sided roasting tin (approximately 35 x 26cm), along with the remaining sauce ingredients, whisking to combine.
In a large bowl, toss the chicken thighs with the olive oil, mango chutney, 'nduja and salt. Mix well until everything is evenly coated, then arrange the thighs on top of the sauce, skin-side up.
Roast for 45 mins, rotating the tin halfway through, until the chicken is crisp and well browned.
Remove from the oven. Transfer the chicken to a tray. Leave the sauce to cool for 5 mins, then scrape it all into a blender and blitz until completely smooth.

Pour the blended sauce back into the tray along with drained chickpeas, then nestle the chicken back on top, skin-side up. Return to the oven for 5 mins to warm through, popping the flatbreads in on another oven shelf at the same time.
Serve the chicken with the chickpeas and sauce. Halve the lemons and squeeze over the juice, scatter over the roughly chopped coriander and scoop up with the warm flatbreads.

name: Saucy Aubergine Rigatoni
description: This sauce is loosely based on caponata, the Sicilian summer vegetable stew, but with added tomatoes to make it more... saucy.
instructions: Cut the aubergine into roughly 2cm dice, pop into a large saucepan over a high heat with a big pinch of salt and cook for 3 or 4 mins until browning at the edges.
Add 3 tbsp of olive oil and cook for another 5 mins until soft. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Meanwhile, dice the onion and celery. Once the aubergine is cooked, return the empty pan to a medium heat and add a generous splash of olive oil.
Add the onion and celery and a pinch of salt. Cook for about 5 mins until softened.
Crush the olives in half using your palm or side of a knife and add to the pan for a minute along with the capers and basil, then pour in the vinegar and bubble for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, crush up with your spoon and let it cook down for about 15 mins.
Return the aubergines to the pan with the the tomato sauce, along add the sugar and mix well. Set aside while you cook the pasta in plenty of boiling salted water.
While the pasta cooks, toast the almonds in a dry pan over a medium heat until golden brown. Set aside.
Mix the pasta and sauce together, plate up and top with the flaked almonds, some more basil and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Saucy Aubergine, Chickpea & Ricotta Bake
description: This one couldn't be easier. Take the saucy aubergine batch recipe and mix it with some high-protein chickpeas, before grilling with cheese until golden and bubbly. A midweek winner.
instructions: Make the Aubergine Alla Norma batch recipe.
Heat the grill to medium-high. Transfer the base to a saucepan and heat through over a medium heat until piping hot.
Mix drained chickpeas and some torn basil through the sauce, then dot with the ricotta and mozzarella before grating over Parmesan.
Top with a few more basil leaves and slide under the grill until golden and bubbling, around 20-25 minutes.

name: Saucy Chicken Teriyaki Noodles
description: Sticky, glossy chicken, noodles and loads of teriyaki sauce. A proper midweek dinner that’s way better than a takeaway, but just as comforting.
instructions: Slice the chicken thighs and chuck them into a bowl with the white pepper, light soy sauce and two thirds of the dark soy sauce and all the teriyaki sauce. Mix well and leave to marinate while you crack on.

Prep the veg. Peel and smash the garlic cloves and thinly slice the ginger. Set aside. Thinly slice the Chinese cabbage and chop the spring onions in 3 cm pieces, separating the whites from the greens. Also, slice a few of the spring onion greens for garnish and set aside.

Set a wok over a medium heat and pour in lug of vegetable oil. Once hot, add the garlic and ginger. Fry for a couple of minutes until golden and fragrant, then remove and set aside, leaving the infused oil in the wok.

Add the marinated chicken to the wok (leaving the aside the marinade to add later) and fry for 4-6 mins on each side, depending on their thickness. Pour in a fifth of the water along with the remaining dark soy sauce. Cover with a lid for 7-10 mins, until the chicken is cooked. Take out the chicken and set aside.
Add the egg noodles to the wok along with the spring onion whites and Chinese cabbage. Stir-fry over a high heat for about 30 seconds. Chuck in any leftover marinade along with the remaining water.

Spoon a few tablespoons of the sauce from the wok into a small bowl. Stir in the cornflour until smooth, then pour it all back into the wok. Keep stirring until the sauce thickens – if it’s still too thin, add more cornflour, a teaspoon at a time.

Add the 3 cm spring onion greens and cook for another 30 seconds, then take the wok off the heat. Serve the noodles piled high with slices of the chicken and a scatter over the remaining sliced spring onion greens to garnish. Enjoy!

name: Saucy Chilli Chicken & Spring Onion Stir Fry
description: Crispy, golden chicken thighs tossed with loads of spring onions, smashed garlic, ginger, Sichuan pepper and a serious hit of chilli. It's inspired by one of my favourite Chinese dishes: La Zi Ji.
keywords: Saucy Chilli Chicken & Spring Onions Stir Fry
Saucy Chilli Chicken & Spring Onions Stir Fry recipe
saucy spicy stir-fried chicken with green onions
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions, so it's ready at the same time as the chicken.
Cut the chicken thighs into small bite-sized pieces and add to a large bowl with the soy sauce, cornflour and water. Mix thoroughly and leave to marinate while you prep everything else.

Cut the spring onions into 5cm pieces, slice the ginger into strips, then peel and smash the garlic with the back of a knife. Blitz the Sichuan peppercorns in a small blender or crush them in a pestle and mortar.

Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over a high heat. Add the ground Sichuan pepper, garlic, spring onions and ginger and stir-fry for 2 mins, until everything catches some colour and starts to soften. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

Wipe out the wok and return it to a high heat. Add a little more oil and once it's smoking, add half the chicken. Stir-fry for 5-6 mins, until evenly browned and cooked through, then transfer to the bowl with the aromatics. Repeat with the remaining chicken.

Add everything back into the wok, chicken, aromatics and all, along with the chilli flakes. Add more or less depending on how much heat you're after, as the spice level will depend on the heat of your chilli flakes. Season with salt, black pepper and the sugar. Pour in the remaining water and let it bubble and reduce for 1-2 mins, until you've got a glossy, saucy coating. Turn off the heat.
Serve over the rice with an extra pinch of chilli flakes and a grind of black pepper.

name: Saucy Greek Keftedes
description: Get stuck into these Greek beef meatballs with a rich tomato sauce and fresh mint yoghurt. Make extra sauce, freeze the rest and thank us later.
instructions: Grate ½ the red onion and ½ the garlic into a large mixing bowl. Finely chop the parsley and add it to the bowl, along with ½ the dried oregano.

Add the beef mince to the bowl and give everything a good mix. Crack in the egg and add the breadcrumbs. Season with salt and pepper then set aside in the fridge for an hour (this will make the meatballs easier to shape).

Meanwhile, dice the remaining red onion and slice the remaining garlic. Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pot over a medium heat and fry the onion with a pinch of salt for 4 mins, until slightly softened. Add the garlic and continue cooking for 5 mins. Drain and rinse the beans. Finely chop the fresh mint.

Add the cinnamon (if using) and the remaining dried oregano, give it a stir and pour in the canned tomatoes, olives, butter beans and water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 mins until reduced. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Remove the beef mixture from the fridge and use your hands to shape it into balls approx 60g in size (you want 3 per person). Heat a glug of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and fry the meatballs for 10-15 mins or until golden and cooked through. Check to see the meat has turned brown and isn’t pink. Add the meatballs and ⅔ of the fresh mint to the tomato sauce and stir to combine.
Mix the yoghurt with the remaining fresh mint and a squeeze of lemon juice then season with salt and pepper.
To serve, divide the meatballs and sauce between plates and drizzle over the minty yoghurt.

name: Saucy Harissa Gnocchi Traybake With Tahini Drizzle
description: One tray, 30 mins and a short list of everyday ingredients are all you need to get this saucy, hearty meal on the table. It's got fibre and protein.
keywords: Saucy Harissa Gnocchi Traybake With Tahini Drizzle
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.

Add the plum tomatoes to a medium-sized baking dish and mash them with a fork or potato mash. Mince the garlic and roughly chop the sun dried tomatoes, if using. Add these to the tomatoes along with the harissa, gnocchi, drained butterbeans and plenty of salt and pepper. Stir to combine, then add the cherry tomatoes. Sprinkle over the nutritional yeast, if using.
Cover with silver foil and bake for 15 mins covered, then remove the foil and bake for another 10 mins.

Meanwhile, make the tahini drizzle. Whisk together the tahini, lemon juice, 1 tsp of olive oil and 1 ½ tbsp of cold water until smooth and season well with salt and pepper. Add more water if needed, to thin it out to a drizzle consistency.
When ready to serve, drizzle the tahini over the traybake and scatter over your herbs.

name: Saucy Harissa Stir-Fried Tofu with Charred Tenderstem
description: Crispy crumbled tofu coated in a sticky, spicy harissa sauce, served over jasmine rice with charred tenderstem and a runny fried egg. It's the perfect vegetarian weeknight bowl.
keywords: Saucy Harissa Stir-Fried Crumbled Tofu with Charred Tenderstem
Saucy Harissa Stir-Fried Crumbled Tofu with Charred Tenderstem recipe
instructions: Finely crumble the tofu with your hands and set aside. In a small bowl, mix together the harissa, chilli powder, honey, ginger, soy sauce, red wine vinegar and 100ml of the water until combined. In a separate small bowl, mix the cornflour with the 30ml of water and set aside.

Set a large frying pan over a high heat and add a generous glug of olive oil. Once hot and shimmering, add the crumbled tofu and sauté for 5-6 mins until it starts to turn golden. Pour over the harissa sauce and stir to coat, then add the cornflour mixture. Cook for another 2-3 mins until the sauce thickens and clings to the tofu. Season with salt and black pepper and set aside.

Wipe out the pan and return to a high heat with a little more olive oil. Add the tenderstem and fry for 3-4 mins until charred in spots. Pour in the 50ml of water, cover with a lid and steam for 2-3 mins until the tenderstem is cooked through but still has some bite. Transfer to a plate.
Add a little more olive oil to the pan and crack in the eggs. Fry for 2-3 mins until the whites are bubbly and set but the yolks are still runny.
Divide the rice between bowls and spoon over the saucy tofu. Add the tenderstem and top each bowl with a fried egg. If you'd like to keep this vegan, just leave the egg out.

name: Saucy Home-Style Tofu with Thai Basil & Cashews
description: Crispy golden tofu tossed in a sticky, gingery soy sauce with Thai basil and crunchy cashews. Better than a takeaway and on the table in 25 mins.
keywords: Saucy Home-Style Tofu with Thai Basil & Cashews
Saucy Home-Style Tofu with Thai Basil & Cashews recipe
instructions: Cut the tofu into 3cm triangles and pat dry with a tea towel. Thinly slice the spring onions and chillies (set aside a handful for garnish), finely mince the ginger and thinly slice the garlic. If you like a more or less spice you can reduce or increase the chillis to your taste.

Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Once the oil is shimmering, add the tofu and fry for 3 mins until golden brown. Flip and fry for another 3 mins, then remove from the pan and set aside.
Mix the cornflour and water together until smooth, then combine with the soy sauce, sugar and the juice of the lime in a small bowl.

Add the spring onions, chillies, ginger and garlic to the pan and fry for 1-2 mins until fragrant (add an extra drizzle of oil if needed). Pour in the sauce and return the tofu to the pan, tossing to coat. Cook for another minute until the sauce has thickened slightly, then take off the heat, season with black pepper and stir through the Thai basil and cashews (saving a handful for garnish).
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Then share between bowls and top with the tofu, and the remaining cashews and sliced chillis.

name: Saucy King Prawn Crispy ‘Instant Noodles’
description: A Chinese classic, made at home. Affordable, easy and addictive. Doused in gravy, crunchy on the top, soft on the bottom.
instructions: Start by prepping the vegetables. Slice the asparagus tips into thirds and slice the mushrooms. Slice the carrot into thin strips diagonally, then lay them flat and slice into matchsticks. Slice the babycorn in half lengthways, and slice the mangetout in half.
Bring a pot of water to the boil. Once boiling, add the instant noodles and cook following pack instructions. Drain and set aside, allowing the moisture to evaporate.

Slice the spring onion into thirds. Slice the thirds lengthways into thin matchsticks. Cut the small bunch of coriander into thirds. Add the spring onion and coriander to a bowl of cold water. Set aside.

Heat a wok or large frying pan over a medium heat. Add a glug of oil. Add the cooked instant noodles and spread them against the bottom of the pan, forming a round pancake shape. Shake the pan occasionally to ensure the bottom doesn’t burn. After 5 mins, once the bottom of the noodles are nicely browned and crispy, flip the noodles onto a plate, brown-side up.

Put the pan back on the stove, still over a medium heat, and add 2 tbsp oil. Add the prawns/tofu, asparagus, mushrooms, babycorn, mangetout and carrots, then stir-fry for around 3 mins. Add the chicken stock, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and white pepper. Stir to combine and bring to a boil, around 3 mins. Once boiling, mix the cornstarch and cold water to make a slurry. Turn the heat to low and slowly drizzle in the slurry whilst stirring. The sauce should thicken, if too thin add more slurry, if too thick add a splash of water. Add in the sesame oil and cook for 1 minute, then turn off the heat.

Add the noodles to a large plate, crispy side up. Pour the sauce on top of the noodles. Drain the water from the spring onion and coriander and add on top. Drizzle with your favourite chilli oil and enjoy!

name: Saucy Lime Noodle Salad
description: Fresh, filling and smothered in a lime, ginger, and coriander sauce, this salad makes a great packed lunch if you manage not to slurp it all up for dinner.
instructions: Boil Soba noodles according to package directions, drain and rinse with cold water.
Roughly chop the broccoli.
Boil broccoli for 2 minutes in salted water, add edamame for another 1 minute. Drain and run under cold water to cool down.
Slice the courgette and carrot into thin batons using a knife or a julienne peeler.
To make the dressing, add the coriander, tahini, water, juice of 3 limes, ginger, miso and agave and blend until smooth.

To serve, add all of the vegetables to the noodles and top with plenty of dressing. Sprinkle some sesame seeds on top and finish with chilli oil, if using. Serve with the crispy seaweed on top and on the side.

name: Saucy Noodles with Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Broccoli
description: Your Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Roasted Broccoli batch meets its match. Wheat noodles tossed in a rich tahini and chilli oil sauce, topped with quick-pickled cucumber and plenty of fresh coriander.
keywords: Saucy Noodles with Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Broccoli
Saucy Noodles with Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Broccoli recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Spread the leftover tofu and broccoli onto a baking tray and reheat for 10 mins until warmed through.
Mix all the dressing ingredients in a large bowl and season with salt.
Thinly slice the cucumber and add to a small bowl with the white wine vinegar and a pinch of salt. Mix and set aside.
Cook the noodles according to packet instructions. Drain and tip straight into the bowl with the sauce. Toss to combine, then divide between bowls.
Top with the tofu and broccoli, the quick-pickled cucumber and a handful of fresh coriander.

name: Saucy Sausage, Sweet Potato & Beans
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad. 

A lovely one-pot winter warmer of sausages, sweet potato and beans finished with a gremolata to keep things fresh. Perfect for a cold weeknight dinner.
instructions: Peel and dice the sweet potato into roughly 3cm cubes.
Place a large pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Add the sausages and potatoes and cook for 5 mins until well coloured.
Reduce the heat to low, finely slice the onions and garlic and add along with the tomato puree and rosemary. Cook for another few mins until the onion softens.
Pour in the beans and the water. Pop a lid on the pan and cook for about 10 mins until the potatoes have softened.
Peel a few strips of the lemon zest using a vegetable peeler. Finely mince the lemon zest and the parsley and mix together to make a gremolata.
Plate up with sausages and beans and sprinkle over the gremolata and a drizzle of olive oil. Finish with a squeeze of the lemon juice.

name: Saucy Spiced Chickpeas & Lentils
description: Inspired by Egyptian koshari, this is tangy, deeply spiced and completely addictive. Saucy chickpeas and lentils with a punchy garlic yoghurt - high protein, high fibre and perfect for meal prep.
keywords: Saucy Spiced Chickpeas & Lentils with Garlic Yoghurt
Saucy Spiced Chickpeas & Lentils with Garlic Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Finely chop the garlic and drain and rinse the lentils.

Add the oil to a large saucepan over a medium heat, then add the garlic and fry for a couple of minutes until lightly golden. Add the tomato purée and cook for 2-3 mins until darkened, then add the 7 spice (sub in garam masala or baharat if you can't find it) and cook for a couple of seconds.

Tip in the chickpeas and their liquid, the drained lentils, red wine vinegar, chopped tomatoes and water. Season with salt and black pepper, bring to the boil then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 mins. Add the rice (no need to reheat in the microwave it will cook through in the pan) and cook for another 3 mins.
Pour a couple of kettles of boiling water over the spinach until wilted, then press out as much water as possible. Add the spinach to the pan and mix well to combine.
For the yoghurt, add the yoghurt to a bowl and grate in the garlic, then season with salt and black pepper and mix well.
Serve up the lentils topped with the garlic yoghurt, crispy onions and hot sauce, if using.

name: Saucy Tikka Noodles
description: These noodles are deliciously saucy, featuring Planted chicken tikka skewers and creamy coconut milk.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and add the almonds to a tray. Cook for 10 mins or until golden.
Heat half of the oil in a small pan and add the tikka paste – cooking for a couple of minutes until the moisture has evaporated and the paste thickened.
Add the paste to a blender with coconut milk and the juice of a lemon, blend smooth then season generously with salt before popping in the fridge. This will help to thicken the sauce up.

Finely chop the mint and red onion, then halve and scoop the seeds out of the cucumber and tomato before also finely chopping. Slice the cheeks off the mango, score the flesh and remove with a sharp knife before finely dicing. Add the mint, onion, cucumber, tomato, and mango to a bowl before adding the juice from the remaining lemon and salt. Shred the cabbage as finely as you can.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles for 6 mins or according to package instructions. Drain and rinse in cold water.
Heat the rest of the oil in a pan over a medium heat, cook the skewers for around 7 mins turning frequently to char on all sides.
Toss the noodles with the chilled sauce and cabbage.
Plate up the noodles then top with the skewers, mango salsa, and almonds.

name: Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Cucumber Salad
description: Silky, spicy and umami, these gochujang noodles are perfectly balanced with a fresh cucumber salad. Yes please.
keywords: Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Cucumber Salad
Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Cucumber Salad recipe
instructions: Finely slice the cucumber and add it to a bowl with the chilli oil, rice vinegar, a pinch of salt and the sesame seeds. Finely slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Grate in the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 mins. Add the tomato purée and cook for another 2 mins, then remove from the heat. Add the cooked mixture to a blender with the silken tofu, soy sauce and gochujang. Blitz until smooth, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. Return this sauce mixture to the pan.
Cook the noodles following the pack instructions, then drain, reserving some of the cooking water. Toss the noodles through the sauce, loosening with a splash of the reserved cooking water if needed.
To serve, divide the noodles between plates and top with the cucumber salad, a drizzle of crispy chilli oil and a sprinkling of spring onions.

name: Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Smoked Tofu
description: Silky, spicy and umami, these gochujang noodles are perfectly balanced with a fresh cucumber salad and smoked tofu. And it's preppable? Yes please.
keywords: Lunch Box: Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Cucumber Salad
Lunch Box: Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Cucumber Salad recipe
Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Cucumber Salad
Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Cucumber Salad recipe
instructions: Finely slice the cucumber and add it to a bowl with the chilli oil, rice vinegar, a pinch of salt and the sesame seeds. Finely slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish.

Cut the smoked tofu cut into 2cm pieces. Set a frying pan over a medium heat with a splash of oil. Once hot, add the tofu, cooking on all sides until golden. Then add in the soy sauce and maple syrup, let it bubble away until it gets nice and sticky and then take off the heat. Set aside.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Grate in the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 mins. Add the tomato purée and cook for another 2 mins, then remove from the heat. Add the cooked mixture to a blender with the silken tofu and gochujang. Blitz until smooth, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. Return this sauce mixture to the pan.
Cook the noodles following the pack instructions, then drain, reserving some of the cooking water. Toss the noodles through the sauce, loosening with a splash of the reserved cooking water if needed.

Dish out the noodles between Tupperware containers. Top each with the cucumber salad and crispy tofu, a drizzle of crispy chilli oil and a sprinkling of spring onions.
Box up and pop in the fridge - these will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Sauerkraut and Mushroom Pierogi
description: Pierogi are a Polish staple; crispy dumplings with spiced mushroom and sauerkraut. Topped with garlicky caramelised onions and lemony coconut yoghurt. Seema x
instructions: Wash the shiitake mushrooms in cold water and then soak in 200ml of hot water for 30 minutes.

For the dough, place the flour into a large bowl and stir in ½ tsp salt. Make a well in the middle and pour in 125ml cold water and 50ml olive oil. Stir with a wooden spoon and then start kneading with your hands. This will form a very dry dough, but keep kneading for 5 minutes until it comes together. Wrap in cling film or cover with a bowl and allow to rest for at least 1 hour.

Roughly chop your chestnut mushrooms, 1 brown onion, and garlic. Sauté the onion with cumin in a glug of vegetable oil in a large saucepan until browned for about 7 minutes. Add in the mushrooms and continue to cook until they are very soft and browned, this may take 15 minutes. Mix in the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the sauerkraut, marjoram, bay leaf, sugar, vegetable stock and the shiitake mushrooms with their soaking liquid. Mix well and allow to simmer for 20 minutes or until most of the liquid has evaporated.

Take out the shiitake mushrooms along with ¼ of the filling and blend in a food processor. Return it back to the pan and give it a good mix. Season with salt if required (this may depend on how salty the sauerkraut is). Place in a bowl so that it can cool down.

Meanwhile, slice up the 3 remaining onions. Heat a few large glugs of oil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan and cook the onions on a low heat until caramelised, this can take about 20 minutes. Add in a splash of water if they keep sticking to the bottom of the pan. Once they are cooked grate in 3 cloves of garlic and a big pinch of salt. Mix well and cook for a further minute.
Mix together the coconut yoghurt and the zest of half a lemon. Add in a 3 tbsp of water and mix to reach the consistency of sour cream.
Finely chop the chives.

For the pierogi dough, knead the dough for about 1 minute so it is uniform and then divide into 4. Roll each piece of dough into a rectangle and pass it through a pasta machine. Keep passing it through the machine until you get to the second last thinnest setting.

Cut out large circles either using an 85mm cutter or the bottom of a glass. You can press the scraps back together and reroll them, but reroll them last so they can relax whilst you roll the other pieces.

Place 1 tsp of filling in the centre, and lightly dampen half of the wrapper. Fold in half and press down to seal. You can leave it as is, press down with a fork to seal or crimp like a Cornish pasty.
Continue rolling the dough and making pierogi, placing on a heavily-floured baking tray
Heat up a large pot of salted water and another pan with a glug of oil
Boil the pierogi for 2-3 minutes, or until they float. Then immediately pan fry them until crispy.
Serve with the lemony yoghurt, caramelised onions and chives.

name: Sausage & Cauliflower Bread & Butter Bake
description: This savoury take on a bread and butter pudding is unbelievably good. It’s proper hearty cooking for the colder months.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Remove the crusts from the bread and cut into bite-sized pieces. Use scissors or a sharp knife to slice the sausages into bite-size coins. Chop the cauliflower into bite-sized florets.
Bring a large pan of water to the boil and add the bay leaves, thyme, fennel seeds, ¼ of the garlic cloves and a big pinch of salt.
Add the cauliflower and boil in the water for about 5 mins or until soft and cooked through. Drain and reserve the cauliflower cooking water to make the sauce.
Melt the butter in a medium pan over moderate heat. Add the flour and beat to combine, stirring for a couple of minutes until the mixture foams and bubbles in the pan.

Gradually whisk in 500ml of the hot cauliflower water (this is if you’re cooking for 4 people; increase or decrease if making for a different number) and whisk vigorously to ensure no lumps form. Turn down the heat and cook the sauce for about 10 mins, stirring often, until the sauce has thickened. It should be viscous and the consistency of double cream.
Add the double cream, red wine vinegar and Dijon mustard and check for seasoning, adding salt and black pepper to taste.
Meanwhile, in a large frying, cook the sausage slices in a generous glug of olive oil for 3 mins until browning in places.

Finely chop the remaining garlic and add to the pan, then continue to cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the chopped-up bread and give the pan a good stir to combine over a low heat for another 2 mins. Take off the heat, add the cooked cauliflower and give the pan another thorough mix. Transfer everything to a buttered baking dish.
Pour the sauce over the sausages, bread and cauliflower in the dish and finely grate the Parmesan over the top.

Cook in a preheated oven for 35–40 mins until bubbling and some pieces of the bread on the top have turned crisp and golden brown. Grate over some extra Parmesan and serve with more Dijon mustard, if you like.

name: Sausage & Chorizo Ragù
description: Smoky chorizo and crispy sausage all cooked down in a rich tomato stew with chunky rigatoni. Why didn’t we think of this before?
keywords: the best sausage and chorizo pasta recipes
instructions: Finely dice the onion, carrot, celery and mince the garlic.
Heat up a large sauce pan and pour in a large glug of olive oil. Decase the sausage and chorizo and crumble these into the pan. Fry for 10 mins until very crispy and golden.
Add in the onion, carrot and celery and continue cooking for another 10 mins until the vegetables have softened.
Add in the tomato puree and garlic, then cook for 5 mins until the tomato purée has darkened.
Deglaze the pan with the red wine, scraping all the brown bits from the bottom of the pan.
Pour in the tins of chopped tomatoes, rinse the cans in water and add this to the pot.
Allow to simmer on a low heat for 1 hour. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley.
Get a pan with boiling salted water. Try to use as little water as possible to cook your pasta, this will result in starchier water which will make for a glossier sauce.
Pop your rigatoni into the water and cook until al dente, 2 mins less than the cooking instructions on the package.
Pour some of the pasta water into the ragù and bring to a bubble. Add in the pasta and allow to cook for the remaining two mins until the pasta is cooked. Add more pasta water if needed.
Stir through the parsley and plate up your pasta.
Grate over the parmesan and enjoy.

name: Sausage & Fennel Pasta
description: An easy, aromatic pasta recipe that you're immediately going to add to your midweek meal roster. This one's an instant classic.
instructions: Heat a wide frying pan on a medium heat. De-skin your sausages, adding little balls of sausage meat to the pan with a splash of oil. Fry until brown on all sides, then remove sausage meat.
Finely chop your onion and slice the garlic. Add the onion to the pan with the sausage fat. Cook for about 10 mins over a low-medium heat until translucent.

Add the garlic, the chilli flakes and the fennel and cook for 30 secs or so until the garlic is fragrant. Add your tomato purée, stir it in and cook for 5-10 mins until it starts caramelising on the pan.
Add your cream and three-quarters of your grated Parmesan. Mix everything together, and season with salt and pepper.
Get your pasta cooking in a pan of salted boiling water. Once the water is starchy, add a good cup of it to your tomato sauce, to loosen it.
When your sauce is bubbling and lovely, add in your sausage meat. Stir it in, and then tear in some basil.
When the pasta is al dente, add it to the sauce. Stir it through, adding more pasta water. Cook it all down until it all comes together.
Serve in warm bowls, top with more Parmesan and basil and some olive oil. Enjoy.

name: Sausage & Greens Cheat's Lasagne
description: All the indulgence of a lasagne with a fraction of the washing up to do afterwards. Packed with crispy sausage. Silky cavolo nero sauce. Lots of cheese.
instructions: Finely slice your shallots, garlic and rosemary.

Heat an oven-proof sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a little olive oil, then squeeze in your sausagemeat. Fry for about 5 mins until golden, then remove from the pan with a slotted spoon and set aside. There should be some fat remaining in the pan.

Add your shallots to the same pan and cook for 10 mins until softened. Add your garlic, rosemary and chilli flakes, then cook for another 2 mins. Add your cavolo nero to the pan along with your chicken stock, then cook for 5 mins until it is soft and reduced.
Heat your oven to 210°C.
Pour the mixture into a blender, then blitz until smooth.
Pour your green sauce back into your pan, then get your sausages back in there. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Tear your lasagne sheets in half, then arrange these in the pan.
Pour your double cream over the top, then tear on your mozzarella. Grate over your parmesan and nutmeg, then bake for 25 mins.
Serve and enjoy!

name: Sausage & Kale Fusilli
description: A dead simple weeknight pasta that punches well above its weight. Easy sausage meatballs, tonnes of garlic and a hit of chilli and fennel work perfectly with the kale and a glossy parmesan cream sauce.
instructions: Finely chop the garlic and parsley, setting aside the parsley to garnish later. Then squeeze the sausage meat out of their skins and roll into small meatballs.

Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the sausage meatballs for 6-8 mins, turning regularly, until browned all over and cooked through. Remove the sausage meatballs and set aside. Deglaze with a tiny splash of water, scraping up any caramelisation from the bottom of the pan.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in a large saucepan of well-salted boiling water according to packet instructions. Reserve a ladle of pasta water before draining.

Now back to your sausage pan. Once the water has evaporated, add another drizzle of olive oil to the pan. Once hot, add in the chilli flakes, fennel seeds and chopped garlic. Fry for 1-2 mins until fragrant. Add another splash of water to stop the frying, turning the heat down slightly, then add the kale and cook for 3-4 mins, stirring, until tender and bright green.

To finish the sauce, pour the cream into the pan with the kale and grate in most of the parmesan. Let it bubble away for 2 mins until the parmesan has melted. Add the drained pasta along with a ladle of pasta water and toss everything together. Return the sausage meatballs to the pan, then zest the lemon into the pan and squeeze in the juice of half the lemon. Toss again and season with salt and black pepper, adding a little more lemon juice to taste.
To serve, divide between bowls and scatter over the chopped parsley and some extra parmesan.

name: Sausage & Kimchi Broth with Mixed Rice
description: A Korean-inspired rice and grain bowl with a gochujang, kimchi and anchovy broth and a crispy sausage crumb. Welcome to umami heaven.
instructions: Squeeze the sausage meat from the casings into a bowl and discard the casings. Set aside.

Place a strainer over a bowl and tip the kimchi into it. Squeeze as much of the kimchi brine out as possible. Set the brine aside and mince the kimchi. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens.

Place a wok or large frying pan onto medium heat. Once hot, add a drizzle of sesame oil and the sausage meat. Break up the meat with the back of your spoon and cook whilst stirring for 5-8 mins until golden brown and cooked through. Transfer to a bowl and cover with a plate to keep warm.

Place the wok back onto high heat with a drizzle of sesame oil. Once hot, add the anchovies, spring onion whites, and minced kimchi. Cook until softened and the anchovies have disintegrated. Add the gochujang and cook for 2-3 mins until darkened and caramelised. Pour in the water, bring it to the boil, then remove from the heat and stir through the kimchi brine. Taste and season with salt and sugar, if needed.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice and mixed grains then mix together.
Share the mixed rice between bowls. Ladle over the kimchi broth and top with the sausage mixture. Finish with a sprinkle of spring onion greens and sesame oil.

name: Sausage & Roasted Pepper Quesadillas with Parmesan Dip
description: A cheesy, crispy quesadilla packed with sausagey goodness and dunked in a cheesy dip. A total crowd-pleaser the whole fam will love that's perfect for snacking, lunch or tea time.
keywords: Sausage & Roasted Pepper Quesadillas with Parmesan Dip
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings 
Peel and finely slice the red onions. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook gently for 20 mins until really soft. Add the sugar, if using, and balsamic vinegar. Stir through and cook for a few more minutes until jammy, then take off the heat.

Meanwhile, make the dip. 
Grate the parmesan add to a blender with the soured cream and a squeeze of lemon juice. Blitz until smooth, taste and season with salt and black pepper. Set aside.

Once the onions are softened, add the sugar, if using, and balsamic vinegar. Stir through and cook for a few more minutes until jammy, then remove from the pan and set aside (keeping the pan to cook your sausage meat).

Grind the fennel seeds in a pestle and mortar or spice grinder. If you don’t have one, leave them whole – no stress.
Squeeze the sausagemeat out of the skins into a bowl and mix with the ground fennel seeds.
Place your onion pan back over a medium-high heat and cook the sausage meat, breaking it up with a spoon, for 8-10 mins until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Drain and rinse the cannellini beans, then roughly chop the roasted peppers and basil. Chuck the beans, roasted peppers, crispy sausage and basil into a bowl and season with salt and black pepper.
Add a generous spoonful of the mixture onto one half of each tortilla. Top with a spoonful of the caramelised onions and a handful of mozzarella. Fold over to make a half-moon shape.
Heat a clean pan over a medium heat. Toast each quesadilla for 2-3 mins per side until golden and the cheese has melted. You can do this in batches or keep them warm in a low oven.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Cut into small triangles and serve with the Parmesan dip on the side and some extra veggies, we've gone for cucumber.
Parents Plate: Cut into larger triangles and serve with the parmesan dip. If you're after extra heat add a sprinkle of chilli powder or your favourite hot sauce.

name: Sausage & Sticky Onion Ragù
description: This ragù ticks all the boxes. Rich, meaty and warming using delicious Jolly Hog Proper Porker Sausages with plenty of sticky onions.
instructions: Finely slice the onions. Heat the butter in a large saucepan over a low-medium heat. Add the onions and cook until the soft and golden. This should take about 10 mins. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Add a drizzle of olive oil to the pan and set it over medium heat. Crumble in the Jolly Hog Proper Porker sausages, removing the skin, and break up the sausage meat with the back of a spoon.
Cook for a few mins until golden and lots of the fat has been released, then remove from the pan with a slotted spoon.

Finely chop the garlic and add it to your pan along with the tomato purée, chilli flakes and fennel seeds. Cook for another 3 mins. Then mix in the onions, cooking until they are soft and caramelised.

Turn up the heat and add your sausages back to the pan with the red wine. Let it bubble away until almost evaporated, then pour in the chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, pop a lid on and then turn the heat down low.
Allow it to cook for an hour and a half at a very gentle simmer, stirring occasionally. If you're making ahead, once it's ready leave to cool and stash in the fridge or freezer for later.

Cook your tagliatelle in plenty of boiling salted water. Once al dente, drain (reserving a mug of pasta water) and mix well with the ragù, adding a splash of the cooking water to emulsify. Plate up and top with some finely chopped parsley and a sprinkle of grated Parmesan.

name: Sausage And Green Olive Paccheri
description: Like a white pizza? Then you’ll love this pasta. Sausage and green olive paccheri. Bosh.
instructions: Preheat a large frying pan over a medium heat and add a glug of olive oil. Remove the skins from your sausages, and get them in the pan.
Break them up with your wooden spoon and cook down until browned and crispy. Remove from the pan and set aside, leaving all the rendered fat in the pan.
Now finely dice the shallots and garlic and get them into the pan with a big pinch of salt. Cook down for 6-7 mins.
Add the browned sausage, fennel seeds and chilli flakes to the pan and cook for 2-3 mins.
Turn up the heat and add the white wine to deglaze the pan. Cook down until reduced by half. Add the broccoli, a splash of water and turn the heat down to low. Cook for 20-25 mins.
Now bring a big pot of water to a boil, season generously with salt and drop in your pasta.
Smash your olives with the flat of a knife and pick out the stones. Discard the stones and add the olives to the sauce.
Once the pasta is cooked, add it to the sauce with another ladle of pasta water, the crème fraîche and lemon zest. Toss everything together to create a creamy sauce.
Finish with lemon zest and plenty of parmesan. Divide between warm plates and get stuck in.

name: Sausage Gochujang Chickpea Soup with Garlic Croutons
description: A spicy, smoky soup made from your Sausage Gochujang Ragù batch and chickpeas for a super speedy and comforting midweek dinner.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sausage Gochujang Ragù batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Tip the ragù into a saucepan and set over a medium heat. Stir in the drained chickpeas and stock, then bring to a simmer. Cook for 10–15 mins until slightly thickened.

Scoop out roughly a quarter of the soup and blitz until smooth using a blender or stick blender. Pour it back into the pan and stir through. This makes the soup extra creamy while keeping some chunky texture.

While the soup simmers, tear the sourdough into bite-sized chunks. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, garlic granules, salt and black pepper. Spread out on a tray and bake for 12–15 mins until golden and crisp.
Finely chop the chives, and then ladle the soup into bowls. Top with the crunchy garlic croutons and a scattering of chives to finish.

name: Sausage Gochujang Linguine with Sesame Pangrattato
description: Fusion pasta at its finest, using a batch of your Sausage Gochujang Ragù with silky linguine, crispy chilli oil, and a nutty sesame crumb topping for extra crunch. What's not to love?
keywords: Sausage Gochujang Linguine with Sesame Pangrattato
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sausage Gochujang Ragú.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the linguine until just al dente. Reserve a ladle of pasta water before draining.
Grate the parmesan.

In a small frying pan, toast the panko breadcrumbs with a drizzle of olive oil and 1 tsp of the sesame seeds over a medium heat. Stir regularly for 3–4 mins until golden and nutty. Remove from the heat and stir through the grated parmesan.

Heat the Sausage Gochujang Ragù in a large frying pan over a low heat until warmed through.Add the cooked pasta to the ragù along with a splash of the reserved pasta water. Toss until glossy and fully coated, adding more water if needed.
Divide between bowls and scatter over the sesame pangrattato. Finish with a drizzle of crispy chilli oil, a pinch of sesame seeds and lime wedges on the side, if you like.

name: Sausage Gochujang Ragú
description: It’s in the Mob hall of fame for a reason. Spicy, creamy and ridiculously good tossed through pasta, and now you’ve got a batch of it for the week or to stash in the freezer.
instructions: Finely chop shallot and garlic. Remove the sausages from their casings.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Crumble in the sausage meat and fry until well browned and caramelised, you want proper colour here for max flavour so be patient. Add a splash of water to deglaze the pan, scraping up all those tasty brown bits. Tip the sausage out onto a plate and set aside.
Return the pan to a medium heat and add the butter. Once melted, add the chopped shallots and garlic. Cook for a few mins until softened and fragrant.
Grate the Parmesan and juice the lime. Add the gochujang, single cream, honey and lime juice to the pan. Stir in the Parmesan and let it melt into the sauce.
Tip the sausage back into the pan and stir to combine. Let it bubble gently for 10 mins until thick and glossy. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.

Leave the sauce to cool and then box up in containers. The sauce will keep in the fridge for 3-4 days and in the freezer for 3 months (you can reheat straight in the pan from frozen). Hungry now? Toss it through some pasta for a speedy, spicy dinner.

name: Sausage Gochujang Rigatoni
description: This spicy sausage pasta is a new favourite of ours, and we’re confident that it’ll become one of yours, too. On the table in 20 mins, it’s a weeknight hero. Sweet, fiery, and incredibly easy to make. You're going to love our sausage gochujang rigatoni.
instructions: Mince your shallot and garlic.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Decase your sausages and crumble the meat into the pan. Fry until the sausage meat is well browned, adding a splash of water to deglaze the pan when it's really well caramelised (don't do this too early, as the caramelisation is crucial for the flavour of the dish). Remove the sausage meat to a plate and set aside.
Return the pan to a medium heat and add the butter. Once melted, add the minced shallot and garlic and fry for a few minutes until softened and fragrant.

Add the gochujang, single cream, honey and the juice of the limes. Grate in ¾ of the Parmesan. Finally, add your caramelised sausage bits back to the pan. Give it a good mix and season to taste with salt and pepper. Leave it to simmer while you cook the pasta.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over a medium-high heat. Add the pasta and cook until al dente following packet instructions, then drain the pasta and reserve the water (this pasta water is the key to bringing your sauce together).

While the pasta cooks, finely chop the coriander. Heat a glug of olive oil in a separate pan set over a medium heat, then toss in your breadcrumbs and fry for a minute until golden. Remove the pan from the heat then grate in the remaining Parmesan and add a small sprinkling of coriander. Mix to combine then set aside.
Add your cooked pasta to the pan with the sauce. Add a small ladle of the pasta cooking water and keep mixing until it’s super glossy. If the pasta is a little dry, add another small ladleful.
Add the remaining coriander to the pasta and give it another mix.
To serve, divide the pasta between bowls. Scatter over the coriander breadcrumbs and grate over some lime zest. Tuck in.

name: Sausage Meatballs with Tomato Romesco
description: Making your own meatballs from sausages is a great little shortcut that'll ramp up the flavour of this dish and save you time in the kitchen.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Whip the skins off of the sausages and roll into little meatballs. Cut the leeks into chunky rings and tip into a roasting tray with the whole, unpeeled garlic cloves and the cherry tomatoes.
Top with the meatballs, drizzle the lot with olive oil and season with salt, black pepper and the dried oregano. Slide into the oven for 25 mins.
Whip the tray out of the oven, add the butter beans, and pop back in for another 15-20 mins.

Add the tomatoes, pepper and almonds to a blender. Remove the garlic cloves from the oven and squeeze the flesh into the blender. Whizz until smooth, drizzling in olive oil as you go, season with salt and pepper and half of the sherry vinegar.
Finely chop the parsley.
Pull the tray out of the oven, add the remaining vinegar and finish with chopped parsley.
Add a few spoons of the romesco sauce to your plates and top with generous helping of the beans, veggies and meatballs.

name: Sausage Mushroom Orzo
description: We know you're mad about orzo, sausages, and mushrooms, so that's why we've created a dish that has all three. An easy dinner that's seriously satisfying.
instructions: Soak your dried mushrooms in 300ml boiling water for 15 mins.
Finely chop your parsley.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with a good drizzle of olive oil. Tip in your breadcrumbs with a pinch of salt and your chopped parsley, then fry for a few mins until crisp and golden. Remove from the heat.

Remove the mushrooms from the liquid, reserving the stock until later. Place your rehydrated mushrooms into your food processor along with your chestnut mushrooms and pulse until you have small chunks.

Squeeze your sausages into a pan and cook until crispy, breaking up with the side of your spoon. Tip in your pulsed mushrooms and cook for 5 mins until reduced and caramelising, then pour your wine in.
Finely chop your garlic.
Get a pan of water on to boil. Season generously with salt, then tip in your orzo and cook until al dente, about 7 mins.
Add your tomato purée, garlic and thyme leaves to the pan and cook for 2 mins more. Add your porcini mushroom liquid and let it simmer for a minute.
Add your single cream along with a ladle of your pasta water, then tip your orzo into the pan. Grate in your parmesan, then toss to coat the pasta. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon your pasta onto plates, then garnish with olive oil, Parmesan, and your toasted breadcrumbs. Serve it up!

name: Sausage Ratatouille Melt
description: A big and beautiful sandwich recipe made with a batch of our signature sausage ratatouille traybake. This isn't one for the faint-hearted.
instructions: Start by making the sausage ratatouille traybake. Heat the oven to 180°C. Roughly chop all your vegetables and chuck them in a baking tray

Add the sausages, rosemary, bay leaves, tinned tomatoes and whole garlic clove to the tray. Mix everything together and get it in the oven for 45 mins, then remove and set aside. Optional: if you're batch cooking the sausage ratatouille traybake for the week, portion it out into Tupperware containers now.
Turn the oven temperature up to 220°C.

Split the ciabattas into half lengthways and open up into sandwiches. Drizzle with olive oil and load up with the traybake veggies. Cut the sausages into halves, lengthwise, and put them on top of the veggies.
Tear over the mozzarella, season with salt and pepper and slide into the oven for 5-6 mins, or until perfectly golden.
Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion and chilli and toss into a bowl with the rocket. Dress with salt, lemon juice, and olive oil and toss together.
Load the rocket salad into the warm sandwiches and get stuck in.

name: Sausage Ratatouille Traybake
description: Ratatouille & sausages. A match made in heaven. This is a ridiculously simple dish with minimal washing up.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Roughly chop all your vegetables and chuck them in a baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil and pinch of salt.

Add the sausages, rosemary, bay leaves, tinned tomatoes and whole garlic clove to the tray. Mix everything together, season generously with salt and pepper and get it in the oven for 45 mins.Give it a check half way through, turning the sausages and veg so they get nicely browned all over.
Sprinkle over a bit more fresh rosemary to serve.

name: Sausage Ratatouille With Almond Pesto Traybake
description: A ratatouille-inspired sausage traybake that we've jazzed up with a tangy almond pesto.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Roughly chop all your vegetables and chuck them in a baking tray.
Add the sausages, rosemary, bay leaves, tinned tomatoes and whole garlic clove to the tray. Mix everything together and get it in the oven for 45 mins.

While the sausages are cooking, finely chop the almonds and parsley. Add to a bowl, grate in the zest of lemon then squeeze in the juice. Grate in the garlic, add olive oil then whisk to emulsify. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle over a bit more fresh rosemary to serve.

name: Sausage Ratatouille with Black Lentils & Yoghurt
description: Sausages and lentils is a classic combination. We've served ours with yoghurt and dill for freshness. You'll love it.
keywords: Sausage Ratatouille With Black Lentils & Yoghurt
Sausage Ratatouille With Black Lentils & Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Start by making the sausage ratatouille. Heat the oven to 180°C/356°F. Roughly chop all your vegetables and chuck them in a baking tray.

Add the sausages, rosemary, bay leaves, tinned tomatoes and whole garlic clove to the tray. Mix everything together and get it in the oven for 45 mins, then remove and set aside. Optional: if you're batch cooking the sausage ratatouille traybake for the week, portion it out into Tupperware containers now.
Heat the lentils according to the package instructions. Roughly chop the dill.
Divide the traybake between a couple of bowls along with the lentils. Add dollops of yoghurt, chopped dill and lemon wedges. Serve.

name: Sausage Roll Samosas
description: Esha from Big Mum’s Samosas teaches the MOB how to make these deliciously flaky sausage roll samosas with a tender filling and fragrant mint chutney.
instructions: Firstly mince two cloves of garlic and your chives. Add the garlic to a hot pan with a glug of oil. Cook for 2 mins until golden brown.

Add in your sausage meat and cook for 5 mins. When it is ¾ cooked, add in ½ tsp salt, ½ tsp black pepper, paprika, onion salt, thyme, chilli flakes and chives. Cook for another 3 mins or until the sausage meat is cooked through. Leave to the side and allow it to cool down.

For the pastry, combine 120g plain flour with 115ml warm water. Mix together with a wooden spoon to form a sticky dough. Pour onto a clean work surface dusted with flour and knead until the dough is no longer sticky and very soft, about 10 mins.
Let the dough rest covered for 5 mins.
Pinch a golf ball-sized dough ball and roll to form a smooth ball. Roll each ball into a large circle that is 3mm thick.

Heat up a large nonstick pan and cook the dough for about 15-20 secs per side until you see bubbles and it is slightly transparent. You don't want to cook the dough fully, keeping it undercooked at this stage helps it get extra crispy when frying.
Once all your pastry is cooked, pile them on top of each other and cut down the middle to form semi-circles.
Check that your meat has cooled down then add your cheese and mix it well. The meat must be cooled down so the cheese doesn't melt.
To make the glue, add 100ml water to 50g plain flour and beat until it has a paste-like consistency.
To fill your pastries, make them into a cone, and glue one end and start filling. Once done, fold and glue again.
Fill up a large saucepan with vegetable oil to deep fry the samosas.

Check your oil is hot enough before deep frying. You can test this by using a bit of the pastry you cut earlier. If that pastry bubbles up and rises, then your oil is hot enough and you can cook your samosas.
Cook your samosas for 2-3 mins on medium heat until golden brown and crispy.
For the chutney, blend up 2 cloves of garlic, coriander, mint, the juice of a lemon, sugar and ½ tsp salt. Blend until smooth, adding a splash of water if needed and season to taste.
Serve the hot samosas with the chutney and enjoy.

name: Sausage Traybake With Broccoli Salsa
description: This one might look time-consuming, but it's just about getting all the bits into the oven. It’s super hands-off, and the result is a hearty comforting meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.

Trim and chop the aubergines and tomatoes into 2cm-sized chunks (leave any small tomatoes whole). Trim the broccoli and chop the stem into 1cm chunks. Discard the tough oregano stems, and thinly slice the garlic.

Add the chopped veg, broccoli stalks, oregano and garlic into an oven-proof dish with 2 tbsp of balsamic vinegar, 5 tbsp of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss it all together. Place the sausages on top. Roast for 35-40 mins, until the sausages are cooked and the veggies have softened.

Meanwhile, roughly chop the broccoli florets. Add the olives and parsley into a food processor and blitz until finely minced. Transfer into a bowl.
