Add the broccoli into the processor and blitz until finely minced. Add the minced broccoli to bowl of minced olives along with 70ml of olive oil and the remaining balsamic vinegar. Season with salt and pepper and mix. Set aside.
Drain the peppers and chop them into 2cm chunks.

Add the couscous into a heatproof bowl with 245ml of boiling water, season with plenty of freshly cracked black pepper. Cover tightly and set aside to rehydrate, 10-15 mins. Once ready, grate in the Parm, mix, taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Stir the roasted peppers into the veg. Share the couscous between your plates, top with the sausage traybake and the broccoli green olive salsa.

name: Sausage and Pea Pasta
description: A ridiculously affordable simple pasta packed with peas, runner beans and crispy sausage bits. Perfect for a 20-minute meal.
instructions: Slice up the runner beans into 2cm pieces.
Squeeze your sausages out of their skins straight into a large pan with a small glug of oil. Brown on a gentle heat, breaking up the meat as you go, for about 10 mins.
Put your pasta in a pot of heavily-salted boiling water and cook according to the package instructions.
Add the chill flakes, peas and runner beans to the sausage mix, cooking for about 30 seconds. Scoop out 4 tablespoons of this mix and set aside in a separate bowl.
Add 200ml of pasta cooking water to that pan along with the mascarpone and parmesan. Mix well to form a sauce.
Toss in your pasta and mix well, adding more pasta water if necessary. Season with more parmesan, salt and pepper to taste.
Top with a final shaving of parmesan and the cooked sausage and runner bean mixture you reserved earlier. Give it a good crack of black pepper and enjoy.

name: Sausage, Bean & Cheese Melt
description: We've taken inspiration from the nation's favourite bakery chain to make this Sausage, Bean & Cheese Melt, perfect for a hangover.
instructions: Dump the beans into a small saucepan and set over a medium heat. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer and cook until the bean liquid has reduced and is quite thick. Add the Worcestershire sauce (you can add more if you like, I would) and mix. Set aside and let it cool to room temp.
Coarsely grate the cheddar and mozzarella and mix.
Cut the sausages into 1cm rounds or chunks – whatever you fancy. Stir the sausage through the beans along with the cheese.

Unfurl the pastry and cut each sheet into 6 rectangles. The easiest way to do this is to orient the pastry landscape, grab a pizza wheel and run one cut across the middle of the sheet. Now cut the two sheets into 3.
Beat the egg with a pinch of salt. You’re ready to build.

Grab a sheet of pastry, top with around 3 heaped tbsp of the bean mix. Brush egg wash around the edge of the pastry, you can do this with your finger or a brush, and carefully stick another piece of pastry over top. Seal the edges with a fork, brush with a little egg wash and cut three little vents in the top. That’s your melt done.
Repeat with the remaining pastry and filling. Freeze separated by parchment and you’re ready for your next hangover.
To bake, slide into an oven preheated to 180°C for 30 mins until golden brown and bubbling. Let them cool for 5-6 mins before eating to avoid burning your mouth and being hungover at the same time.

name: Sausage, Kale & Green Olive Rigatoni
description: Like a white pizza? Then you’ll love this pasta. It's rich, creamy, and mega savoury.
instructions: Preheat a large frying pan over a medium heat and add a glug of olive oil. Remove the skins from your sausages, and get them in the pan.
Break them up with your wooden spoon and cook down until browned and crispy. Remove from the pan and set aside, leaving all the rendered fat in the pan.
Now finely dice the shallots, fennel and garlic and get them into the pan with a big pinch of salt. Cook down for 6-7 mins.
Add the browned sausage, fennel seeds and chilli flakes to the pan and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Turn up the heat and add the white wine to deglaze the pan. Cook down until almost completely gone. Add the milk and turn the heat down to low. Cook for 20-25 mins.
Now bring a big pot of water to a boil, season generously with salt and drop in your rigatoni.
While your pasta is cooking. Add the kale to the sauce along with a ladle of pasta water and wilt for 1-2 mins.
Smash your olives with the flat of a knife and pick out the stones. Discard the stones and add the olives to the sauce.
Once the pasta is cooked, add it to the sauce with another ladle of pasta water, the mascarpone and lemon zest. Toss everything together to create a creamy sauce.
Finish with a big squeeze of lemon juice, divide between warm plates and get stuck in.

name: Sausage, Kale & Taleggio Gnocchi Bake
description: Inspired by our favourite pizza from Franco Manca. Taleggio is the best melting cheese. The sausage combo is a dream.
instructions: Squeeze the sausage meat out of the sausages and form into little balls. Splash some olive oil into a frying pan, add the balls and fry until browning. Add a sliced garlic clove and a teaspoon of chilli flakes.
After 20 seconds, add your kale. Add a small splash of water and cook for 5 minutes until the kale has wilted.
Place your gnocchi in a bowl and cover with boiling water. Leave for 5 minutes.
Add your ricotta to the sauce and mix it in. Add 4 or 5 tablespoons of the starchy gnocchi water. Season with salt and pepper and mix everything together.
Drain the gnocchi and add to a baking dish. Place the kale sausage mix on top of the gnocchi and mix together. Top the gnocchi with thin slices of taleggio and add another tsp of chilli flakes.
Place under the grill for 10 minutes or until golden and bubbling. Dole out and enjoy!

name: Sausage, Spinach & Spaghetti Minestrone
description: This sausage, spinach, and spaghetti minestrone is incredibly easy to cook and even easier to eat.
instructions: Cut ⅔ of the courgettes into 2cm, then peel the remaining courgette into long thin ribbons. Peel and thinly slice the garlic cloves.

Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium-high heat. Use a small knife to split and remove the skins of the sausages, then break the sausagemeat into little meatballs, rolling them up roughly in your hands before dropping them into the pan. Cook for 3-4 mins until golden and crisp.
Add the diced courgette to the pan along with a pinch of salt and fry for 6 mins, stirring occasionally, until beginning to caramelise and soften.
Meanwhile, zest the lemon onto a plate, then cut the lemon in half. Put the courgette ribbons into a bowl and squeeze over the lemon juice, add a pinch of salt and toss well. Set aside.
Scrape the garlic into the sausagemeat pan along with the chilli flakes, if using. Cook, stirring, for 1 min until smelling amazing, then pour in the chicken stock.

Bring to a simmer, then roughly snap the spaghetti into short pieces (about four snaps per length of spaghetti) and add to the pan. Simmer for 8-10 mins until the spaghetti is just tender. Turn off the heat.
Add the spinach to the pan and stir well. Leave to gently wilt for 2 mins, then season really well with black pepper.
Divide between four bowls and top with a pile of courgette ribbons and a good drizzle of pesto. Finish with a sprinkle of lemon zest, more black pepper and a swizz of olive oil.

name: Sausage, Squash and Taleggio Lasagne
description: Shake up your lasagne game with this beautiful dish. Crispy sausage. Caramelised squash sauce. Funky taleggio. A wonderful match.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/400°F.

Peel and chop your butternut squash into large chunks. Whack it onto a large baking tray and drizzle with ½ tsp of your chilli flakes, a drizzle of olive oil and a sprinkle of salt and pepper. Roast for 40 mins.
Meanwhile, dice your onion and finely chop your garlic.
Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a glug of olive oil and tip in your onion. Fry for 5 mins until starting to soften.

Squeeze your sausages out of their skins into the pan and fry for 5 mins until crisp. Tip in your garlic, remaining chilli flakes and fennel seeds and cook for a minute longer. Tear in your basil, then set aside.
Place half your roasted squash in a food processor and blitz until you have a chunky purée.
Roughly chop your taleggio.

Heat your butter in a saucepan on a medium-low heat. Once the butter is melted, tip in your flour and cook out for 2 mins. Gradually pour in the milk, beating all the while until you have a smooth sauce. Add your butternut purée, taleggio and a grating of fresh nutmeg. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Assembly time. In a rectangular baking dish, add a spoonful of sausage meat and a drizzle of your sauce. Add your lasagne sheets on top of that mixture, then another layer of sausage meat, some butternut chunks, and sauce. Continue doing this in subsequent layers until you've used up all your ingredients.
Sprinkle the top with some mozzarella, then cover with foil and bake for 25 mins.
Remove the foil and bake for 20 mins more.
Leave to stand for 5 mins, then serve and enjoy!

name: Sausages & Lentils with Roasted Grapes
description: A stunning hearty winter dish with braised lentils, sausages and roasted grapes for little pops of something sweet. Finished with crème fraîche for a bit of creaminess.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C.
Toast your coriander seeds in a dry frying pan set over a medium heat for a minute, until fragrant. Transfer to a pestle and mortar and bash them to turn them into a rough powder.
Finely dice your onion and celery. Finely chop your garlic and rosemary leaves.
Add the onion and celery to the same pan, along with your crushed coriander seeds and chopped rosemary, and cook them over a gentle heat for 15 mins until the veg is all totally soft.
Add the tomato purée and chopped garlic to the pan, and cook it out for 3 mins until it darkens.

Turn up the heat a little, then pour in the red wine. Let it reduce down by about half, then add the chicken stock. Once your pan is simmering once more, tip in the lentils, then season with a generous pinch of salt and lots of black pepper. Bring it up to a boil, then simmer it for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, using scissors, snip the bunch of grapes into little clusters. Get them in a roasting tray along with the sausages. Drizzle them with a little olive oil then roast in the oven for 35 mins.
Adjust the seasoning of your lentils. Spoon your lentils into bowls, and top them with your roasted sausages and grapes. Top each bowl with a dollop of crème fraîche, and serve it up.

name: Savoury Hong Kong-Style French Toast
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

We’ve made a savoury version of Hong Kong French toast filled with gooey cheese and Aldi’s Mighty Yeast Extract. It's like a cheesy toast and omelette in one.
keywords: Savoury Cheesy-Inspired Hong Kong-Style French Toast
instructions: Preheat your oven to fan 180°C. Grate the Cheddar cheese and finely slice the chives.
Spread the butter and marmite on both sides of two slices of bread, and on one side of the remaining four slices.

Take a slice that has only been buttered on one side, place it butter-side up, add one-quarter of the grated cheeses onto it and top with a slice of bread that has been buttered on both sides. Top with more cheese and place a slice of bread that has only been buttered on one side. Make two sandwiches like this.
Crack four eggs into a shallow dish, season with salt and pepper, and add the chives. Whisk together until thoroughly combined. Dunk the sandwich in the egg mixture until all sides are coated.
Drizzle 4 tbsp of oil into a frying pan so that the bottom is covered, place over medium-low heat. Once hot, add the sandwiches in, cook on all sides until golden and the cheese has melted, 5-7 mins.
Once cooked, place them onto a baking tray, turn the oven off and slide them in to keep them hot.
Return the frying pan to a medium-high heat with another 2 tbsp of oil. Once hot, crack the remaining eggs in and fry until the whites are cooked through and the yolks are still soft, 3-4 mins.
Top the cheesy, savoury Hong Kong-style French toast with your fried egg and tuck in.

name: Savoury Peanut Beans & Sesame Eggs
description: A cosy, nourishing bowl that packs a punch in terms of flavour. The peanut butter, eggs and butter beans provide loads of protein to keep you fuller for longer. Batch-cook a load of the beans and slaw and thank yourself later.
keywords: Savoury Peanut Beans & Sesame Eggs recipe
instructions: Trim and finely mince the lemongrass and scotch bonnet. Finely grate the garlic and ginger.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the lemongrass, ginger, garlic, scotch bonnet and tomato purée and fry for 3-4 mins until the tomato purée has darkened. Pour in the water, butter beans and their liquid and stir the peanut butter through. Bring the mixture to the boil, then lower the heat to low and leave to simmer until ready to serve. Before serving, taste and season with salt and pepper. Add a splash of more water if needed.

Meanwhile, bring a saucepan full of water to the boil. Once boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook for 7 mins. Transfer to a bowl of ice water for a couple of minutes, before peeling them. Add the sesame onto a plate and gently roll the eggs in them until covered.
For the slaw, finely shred the cabbage and pick the mint leaves. Toss into a bowl with the vinegar, oil and sesame seeds. Season with salt and set aside.
To serve, spoon the beans into bowls. Halve the eggs and place on top of the beans along with some minty cabbage slaw.

name: Savoury Shallot & Pork Noodles
description: Sausages are the ultimate shortcut in this recipe and the natural sweetness of the shallots really tie this dish together.
instructions: Place a saucepan of salted water on to boil. Once boiling, cook the noodles following pack instructions. Reserve some of the noodle water.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice the chillies. Transfer to a bowl with the vinegar, season with salt and set aside.
De-case the sausages and thinly slice the shallots.

Place a frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, add a drizzle of oil and crumble the sausages in. Cook for 6-8 mins until the sausages are cooked through and browned. Transfer the sausage to a plate using a slotted spoon, leaving any fat behind in the pan.

Add the shallots to the frying pan and cook for 3-5 mins until starting to colour. Stir through the white pepper, then return the sausage to the pan with the soy sauce, oyster sauce, noodles and watercress. Toss together until the watercress has wilted. Remove from the heat and toss through three-quarters of the pickled chillies and all of the pickling liquid. Add a splash of noodle water if dry
Share the noodles between bowls and top with the remaining pickled chilli.

name: Savoury Shortcrust Pastry
description: A handy pastry recipe that’s perfect for tarts and pies. We've included two sets of instructions to make the dough by hand, or in a food processor or stand mixer.
instructions: Ensure your butter is very cold. Grate the cold butter into a bowl and return to the fridge.

Sieve the flour and salt into a large mixing bowl. Add the grated butter and work it into the flour, rubbing the mixture between your thumb and fingers but handling as little as possible – until it resembles rough breadcrumbs.

Add the water very gradually and evenly, 1 tsp at a time, and continue to work the dough with your hands until the water is incorporated enough to bring the dough together into one piece – careful not to add too much. Form into a round ball then wrap in clingfilm and refrigerate for at least 30 mins.

Remove the dough from the fridge and allow it to come to room temperature. Knead it very gently on a lightly floured clean surface to gently soften the dough. Use a floured rolling pin to roll the dough out to your desired thickness.
Use the pastry to line the tart or pie tin of your choice then bake in an oven at 180°C fan until browning and starting to crisp.
Grate the cold butter into a bowl and return to the fridge. Chill the mixing bowl and the pastry attachment in the fridge for 30 mins.
Sift the flour and salt into a large bowl. Add the butter, then cover with a plate and transfer to the freezer for 10 mins.
Transfer to your food processor or stand mixer and combine in quick pulses to just bring it to the breadcrumbs stage.
Add the water gradually, mixing as you go, until it comes together as a dough. Add an extra splash if it’s too dry.
Wrap the dough in clingfilm and refrigerate for at least 30 mins.

Remove the dough from the fridge and allow it to come to room temperature. Knead it very gently on a lightly floured clean surface to gently soften the dough. Use a floured rolling pin to roll the dough out to your desired thickness.
Use the pastry to line the tart or pie tin of your choice then bake in an oven at 180°C fan until browning and starting to crisp.

name: Savoy Cabbage Spicy Bean Bake
description: A simple bean-y bake recipe that's loaded with veggies and protein. If you're a fan of cabbage recipes, you're going to go gaga for this vegan recipe.
keywords: Savoy Cabbage Spicy Bean Bake recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Grate the garlic and finely slice the sundried tomatoes.

Put the canned tomatoes, garlic and 'nduja into a large roasting tin (preferably one with a lid). Mix well and break up the plum tomatoes if using instead of chopped. Add the cherry tomatoes, butter beans, sundried tomatoes and plenty of salt and pepper. Mix well.
Cut the cabbage in half, then cut each half into four wedges, keeping the stem intact. Arrange the cabbage into the tomatoes snugly, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Place the lid on or cover the tin tightly with foil. Bake for 30 mins.
To serve, drizzle with lots of tahini, lemon juice and zest and some more 'nduja. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil, fresh herbs and nuts.

name: Scallops with Brown Butter & Capers
description: Pan-seared scallops are super impressive, yet couldn’t be simpler. All you need is a super hot pan to get a caramelised crust on them. Served with loads of brown butter and salty capers, for a date night win. We can get you cooking perfect restaurant-quality scallops with our easy guide. Learn tips for selecting, preparing, and searing scallops for a delicious, restaurant-quality meal at home.
instructions: Get a medium, non-stick frying pan over a medium heat, tip in the butter and let it melt. Once melted, carry on cooking the butter, whisking occasionally until it has turned from golden and foamy to a caramel brown colour and smells super nutty. Pour into a heatproof bowl and set aside. Zest the lemon and set aside.
Pat the scallops dry with kitchen paper then season with salt. Drizzle over ½ tbsp olive oil.
Using a second piece of kitchen paper, wipe out the butter sediment from the frying pan then put over a high heat.

Leave the pan to get super hot (you want the scallops to sear as soon as they hit the pan), then add ½ tbsp olive oil.. Carefully place in the scallops and cook for 2 minutes on the first side until the underneath is deeply caramelised, then flip the scallops and cook for 1 minute more.

Take the pan off the heat, pour the brown butter back in, then add the capers and squeeze in the lemon juice. Baste the scallops a few times in the browned butter then divide the scallops and caper butter between two shallow bowls.
Sprinkle over the lemon zest, crack over lots of black pepper and use scissors to snip over the chives to serve, along with crusty bread for mopping up all that buttery goodness.

name: Scampi Sarnie
description: Nothing says summer like eating a scampi sarnie in the sun. This homemade version will show you how to make your prawns perfectly crisp and golden.
instructions: Peel the prawns and whip out the grit line by cutting a small incision down the back and removing with a fork. Mix the flours, baking powder and sugar in a medium bowl. Slowly whisk in the vodka and the beer until you have a loose batter.

Roughly chop the jalapeños and tip into a bowl. Finely chop the shallots and dill and get them in there too along with the mayonnaise and the zest of the lemon. Shave the white cabbage and toss with a little salt. Slice and season the tomatoes and toast the bread.
Preheat a pot of oil to 190°C.

Working in batches, toss the prawns in the extra rice flour and coat in the batter before carefully lowering into the hot oil. Fry for 3-4 mins or until golden brown. Fish out of the hot oil and drain on kitchen paper. Season with salt.
Add some jalapeño mayo to both sides of the sandwich, top with a handful of cabbage, a few slices of tomato, pickles and some hot scampi. Add hot sauce to your taste, pop the lid on and get stuck in.

name: School Dinner Chocolate Cake
description: The softest, bounciest, and best ever chocolate cake recipe. This one took a long time to develop but it was worth it to achieve chocolate cake perfection.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease and line a deep baking tray with baking paper and set aside. In a large bowl mix together the flour, bicarbonate of soda, both sugars, salt and the cocoa powder. If there are any hard lumps of sugar break using your fingers.

In another large bowl whisk together the eggs, vanilla and soured cream. Finely chop the chocolate and dice the butter, then add both to a pot, melting over a medium heat whilst stirring until totally combined. Add the coffee granules to a jug and top up with the boiling water.

Pour the soured cream mix into the dry ingredients along with the coffee and melted chocolate, fold together using a large metal spoon until combined – do not over mix. Pour into the lined baking tray and pop into the oven for 50 mins to 1 hour until cooked. You can check if it's cooked or not by poking it through the centre with a skewer – if it comes out clean, the cake is ready!
Set aside to cool, remove from the baking tray, sprinkle with the granulated sugar and slice.

name: Scones with Homemade Roasted Strawberry Jam
description: Freshly baked scones, still a little warm from the oven, smothered in clotted cream and strawberry jam. Whether you’re cream or jam first, making your own scones is the way forward.
keywords: Scones with Homemade Roasted Strawberry Jam Recipe
Scones with Homemade Roasted Strawberry Jam
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C fan. Make sure your butter is fridge-cold.

Start by making the jam. Hull your strawberries then put them, whole, into a small roasting tin and sprinkle over the sugar. Get them into the hot oven to roast for 1 hour until the strawberries have broken down and the liquid has mostly evaporated and turned jammy. Remove from the oven and add the juice of ½ the lemon (save the other half for your scones). Stir, then scrape your jam into a bowl or jar to cool. If you want to make this in advance, keep it in a sterilised jar for up to a month.
Scone time: turn your oven to 200°C fan. Lightly dust a baking tray with flour.
Measure the milk into a jug, squeeze in the lemon juice and set aside for 5 mins to curdle (boom you’ve made buttermilk).

Cut the cold butter into cubes. Add to a large bowl then whisk the flour on top. Add a good pinch of salt then use your fingertips to rub the butter and flour together until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs then, using a cutlery knife, stir in the sugar.

Crack the egg into the jug of homemade buttermilk and whisk well with a fork to combine. Pour just over ¾ of this mixture into the dry scone mix, using your cutlery knife to bring the dough together. You want the dough to just come away from the sides of the bowl but it by no means needs to look smooth. The secret to perfect scones is not overworking the dough.

Tip the dough onto your floured surface then use your hands to pat together into a rectangle about 2cm thick. Lightly flour a 6cm round or fluted cutter and use it to cut equal scones out of the dough (about 70g each).
Put the scones onto the baking tray and brush the tops with the remaining buttermilk mixture. Bake in the top of the oven for 10-12 mins until risen and golden.
Transfer to a wire rack to mostly cool then tear open and serve with the roasted strawberry jam and clotted cream. Unreal.

name: Scotch Bonnet & Ginger Chilli Jam
description: A fresh and fragrant chilli jam that's commonly found in Grenada. This recipe from Juliet Friday Smith is perfect with breadfruit balls and saltfish fritters.
instructions: Sterilise 6 x 250ml jam jars by either running them through a hot dishwasher cycle (without dishwasher soap) or by putting them in a 130°C oven upside down with the lid off for twenty minutes.
Core and deseed the pointed red peppers and cut into chunks. Deseed the scotch bonnet peppers and chop them in half. Wear gloves if you can or make sure to wash your hands afterwards.

Blitz the red peppers in a food processor first then add the scotch bonnet peppers and blitz again until you have fine pieces of chilli and pepper. Peel the ginger with a spoon and grate it into the chilli and pepper mix.

In a large pot heat the white wine vinegar on a low heat. Add the jam sugar and leave until it is fully dissolved. You won’t need to stir it. Once the sugar is dissolved turn up the heat to get the vinegar boiling and add the chilli, pepper and ginger mix. Leave it to boil for 10 mins - I simmered for 4 more mins to get a thicker consistency. Check halfway through and use a wooden spoon to scrape any mix on the sides back into the liquid.
Leave to cool for 30 mins then ladle into the jam jars and seal. The jam will last 6 months in the jar and up to a month in the fridge once opened.

name: Scotch Bonnet Chickpea Stew with Cucumber Chutney
description: Inspired by the iconic Indo-Trinidadian street food 'Doubles', this warmly spiced chickpea and lentil curry is rich, hearty and high protein, served with a bright, herby cucumber chutney to cut through the heat.
keywords: Caribbean Curried Chickpeas & Lentils with Cucumber Chutney
Caribbean Curried Chickpeas & Lentils with Cucumber Chutney recipe
instructions: Finely mince the garlic, ginger and half the scotch bonnet (make sure to wash your hands after!). Set a large saucepan over a medium heat and add the vegetable oil. Add the garlic, ginger and scotch bonnet and sauté for 2 mins until fragrant. Add the curry powder and ground cumin and continue sautéing for another minute.

Pour in the red lentils and the chickpeas, including all the liquid from the cans, then add the water. Cover with a lid and cook for 25-30 mins, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are starting to fall apart. Season with salt, then continue cooking uncovered for a few minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice under cold water until it runs clear, then cook according to the packet instructions.

While the rice is cooking, make the chutney. Grate the cucumber into a medium bowl. Finely chop the coriander and the remaining half of the scotch bonnet and add to the bowl. Squeeze in the juice of both limes, add the honey, season with salt and mix well. Set aside.

Serve the curry over the rice with a generous dollop of coconut yoghurt and the cucumber chutney alongside. The chickpea stew is great made ahead and will taste even better the next day. The cucumber chutney is best eaten within a day or two.

name: Scotch Bonnet Coconut and Crispy Tofu Noodles
description: Rich, creamy and a little bit spicy. Let the scotch bonnet do all the work in this simple noodle soup.
keywords: Scotch bonnet and coconut noodle soup recipes
instructions: Blend up the onion, ginger, garlic and scotch bonnet in a food processor to make a chunky paste.
Finely chop the spring onions.
Add a glug of oil into a pan and then fry off the onion mixture for 10 mins until fragrant and the onions are translucent.
Add in the tomato purée and cook this out for 5 mins until the colour darkens.
Crumble the stock cube into a jug and add in 800ml boiling water.
Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable stock, bring this to a gentle simmer.
Pour the desiccated coconut, cornflour and oat milk into three separate bowls. Season each bowl with a pinch of salt.
Add a large glug of oil into a saucepan.
Chop up the tofu into small pieces. Dredge each individual piece in the cornflour, then the oat milk, and then finally press it into the desiccated coconut.
Fry the tofu until golden brown and crispy.
Add the pak choy into the soup and cook for 2 mins.
Cook the noodles in boiling water according to package instructions.
Add the cooked noodles to a bowl then add in the soup. Top with pak choi, crispy tofu and finally the spring onions.

name: Scotch Bonnet and Honey Cauliflower
description: A fiery and sweet scotch bonnet cauliflower. Coated in a sticky sauce and topped with crispy curried leaves, this will hit all your taste buds and more.
keywords: Scotch Bonnet and Honey Cauliflower recipes
instructions: Cut your cauliflower into large florets, separate the leaves and finely slice them. Finely slice the red onion and roughly chop up two red peppers.
Blend up the remaining red pepper with your garlic, ginger, scotch bonnet and tomatoes.
Heat up a large pan and add in a glug of oil. Cook the red onions on a medium heat for 10 mins until softened and slightly caramelised.
Add in the tomato purée and cook for 5 mins until darkened.

Pour in the blended sauce along with the cauliflower, chopped red pepper, 200ml water, thyme, 1 tsp salt and lots of freshly ground black pepper. Mix well and allow to cook for 15 mins until the sauce is thickened and the cauliflower is tender.
Meanwhile, finely slice the spring onions.

Heat up a separate frying pan with a large glug of oil. When the oil is smoking hot, carefully add in the cauliflower leaves along with 1 tbsp of curry powder, ½ tsp salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Allow to fry for 5 mins until golden and crispy then finish with 2 tbsp of honey. Continue mixing until the cauliflower leaves are very caramelised and crisp.
When the cauliflower is cooked, add in 3 tbsp of honey and taste for seasoning. If it’s still too spicy, add in some more honey and salt.
Finish by pouring over the curried cauliflower leaves and spring onions. Serve on rice.

name: Sea Bass With Orange, Fennel, Chilli & Watercress
description: This is the perfect recipe for when you want to cook something impressive and healthy. For the crispest sea bass skin, make sure the pan is super hot.
instructions:
Put the extra virgin olive oil and vinegar into a large bowl, season
with salt and black pepper to taste and whisk together with a fork.
Cut the root and top off the fennel bulb and discard. Cut the bulb
into quarters lengthways, then thinly slice into long strips. Tip the
sliced fennel into the bowl with the dressing.
Peel the orange, then slice into rounds, removing any big bits of
pith and the pips. Add to the bowl with the fennel. Thinly slice the
red chilli and scrape into the bowl.
Get a large frying pan over a super high heat. Season the sea
bass fillets with salt and black pepper on both sides. Once the
pan is searing hot, drizzle in a little olive oil and then place the fish
fillets in the pan, skin-side down. Press down on each fillet with a
fish slice or spatula to encourage them to crisp up evenly. Cook
for 2–3 minutes, then flip over and cook for 1 minute on the other
side or until the fish is cooked through.
While the fish is cooking, tip the watercress and chopped roasted
hazelnuts into the bowl with the fennel. Toss everything together
with your hands and adjust the seasoning. Divide between four
plates. When the sea bass is cooked, serve alongside the salads.

name: Sea Bass Yuzu Ceviche with Umami Crisps
description: A Japanese twist on a classic Peruvian ceviche, paired with homemade spicy umami crisps. This one’s a crowd pleaser.
keywords: Sea bass Yuzu Ceviche with Umami Crisps
instructions: Start by making the crisps. Use a mandolin (or sharp knife) to cut the potato into discs, as thin as possible. Rinse the discs in a bowl of cold water to draw out the starch then drain and lay them out on a clean tea towel to dry. Place a second tea towel on top and press down to remove any excess moisture.

Half fill a large saucepan with vegetable oil. Set it over a medium-high heat for 5 mins to heat the oil. Carefully lower the potato discs into the hot oil and fry for 2-4 mins until golden. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the crisps to a clean dry bowl. Sprinkle over the salt, sugar, MSG and cayenne powder and toss until evenly coated. Set aside.
For the sauce, juice the lemon and lime into a bowl. Grate in the ginger and add the rest of the sauce ingredients and a pinch of salt. Mix to combine and set aside.
Slice the sea bass fillets into very thin strips. Thinly slice the cucumber and red onion. Pick the coriander leaves and cut the chives into thirds.
Lay the cucumber slices out on a serving plate. Place the raw sea bass slices on top then sprinkle over the chives.
Heat the olive oil and sesame oil in a small frying pan set over a medium-high for 2-3 mins until just shy of smoking, then pour the hot oil over the fish to sear it.
Pour the sauce over the fish. Top with the red onion and coriander leaves, and serve with the crisps on the side.

name: Sea Bream Ceviche
description: Learn how to cure fish and crisp tortillas to make a fresh and zingy ceviche with crunchy tortilla crisps.
instructions: Trim and peel the sweet potato. Cut it into 1cm chunks and add the potato to a pan and cover with water. Bring to the boil and simmer for 7-10 mins until the sweet potato is fork tender. Drain and leave to cool down.

Finely chop the coriander stalks and mince the chilli. Add the coriander stalks and chilli into a bowl, squeeze over the fresh lime, orange and lemon juice. Peel and grate the ginger into the citrus juice, stir and season with salt. Let marinate for 10-15 mins.

Trim and thinly slice the onion — if you have a mandoline, now is the time to use it. If not, a sharp knife will do the job nicely. Place them into a sieve and wash them to remove some of the sharpness. Add them into a bowl of ice water, this will make them extra crispy.

Meanwhile, place a large saucepan over a medium-high heat and add the vegetable oil (the oil should only fill ⅓-½ of the pot, not more). Heat until the oil reaches about 180°C. Line a plate with kitchen paper or place a wire rack over a baking tray. Fry the tortillas for 30-45 secs until crispy, then transfer to the plate or wire rack. Season with salt as soon as it comes out from frying, as the tortillas cool they’ll get more crispy.
Meanwhile, cut the fish into 2cm chunks, and stir through the citrus mixture along with 3 tbsp of olive oil. Drain ½ of the onion and stir through the fish, leave to marinate for 5 mins.

Peel and cut the avocado into 1cm cubes. Drain and dry the remaining onion and stir through the fish along with most of the coriander leaves. Top the ceviche with a sprinkling of corn nuts, avocado, and sweet potato. Finish with a smattering of coriander leaves. Smash the crispy tortillas and serve alongside for scooping.

name: Sea Salt & Rosemary Focaccia
description: Shop-bought focaccia is fine, but it has nothing on making your own. Don't let the preparation put you off, because the end result is superb.
instructions: Add the water to a large bowl. Tip in the yeast and flour and bring together with your hands until there are no dry lumps of flour left in the bowl. Don’t worry about kneading too much here, just make sure you’ve got all the flour hydrated.

Cover the bowl with cling film, or pop inside something airtight and leave for 1 hour. Tip the olive oil and salt over your dough and use your hands to squash into the dough. Keep mixing until the dough is together.

Turn the dough out onto a clean surface and give it a brief knead, it will be sticky but don’t worry. Use a bench scraper to scoop the dough back up and into a clean bowl. Let it hang out for half an hour then give it a fold. Dunk your hands into cold water, grab the top of the dough and lift it up and over the main body of the dough. Turn the dough 90° and repeat the fold again. Complete four folds, this is one turn. Leave the dough for another half an hour and fold again.

Let it rest once more, then fold again and lob the whole lot into the fridge overnight for a long slow proof. You can let the dough hang out at room temp, and it will be ready to shape and bake in roughly 2-3 hours. If the temperature of the room is higher (eg in summer), the proofing time may be less. Check after 1.5 hours.

When ready to bake, line a roughly 20x35cm baking tray with parchment and a glug of olive oil. Shape the dough into the lined tray and carefully encourage to fill the tray. Try not to knock much air out of the dough.
Cover and leave to proof until the dough is super puffy again. If shaping straight after the folds, this will take 2 hours. If after time in the fridge, this will take roughly 20-30 mins.
Preheat the oven to 230°C.

Strip the rosemary leaves from the stems and sprinkle all over the dough with a generous shower of flakey salt. Drizzle with olive oil and lightly wet your hands. Use your fingers to dimple the dough all over, being careful not to overpress the dough.

Slide into the oven for 20-25 mins until golden brown and baked through. For an extra crispy crust, remove from the tin and slide back into the oven directly onto the shelf for 7-10 mins, until golden all over.
Serve warm with dips, make sarnies, do whatever you like.

name: Seafood Paella Recipe
description: The secret to this seafood paella recipe lies in its flavourful stock. To create an authentic paella de marisco, you start by roasting prawn heads and shells in a cast iron skillet, infusing the rich prawn flavour into the stock used for cooking the rice. This method ensures that every grain of rice is imbued with delicious prawn essence. The process begins with a sofrito of onions, garlic, and tomatoes, which forms the base of the dish. Adding ingredients like mussels, squid, and clams enhances the dish, making it a true showcase of Spanish cuisine. Garnish with parsley and a squeeze of lemon for a vibrant finish. This seafood paella embodies the essence of Spanish food, with each bite offering a taste of the sea. Perfect for a lunch or dinner, this dish will transport you straight to a Spanish restaurant in Valencia.
instructions: Remove the heads and shells from the prawns and transfer to a small bowl. Clean and gut the squid, if your fishmonger hasn’t already, then cut the body into 1cm rings, and the tentacles into 2-3 pieces. Clean and debeard the mussels, if the fishmonger hasn’t already. Put the prawn bodies, squid and mussels back in the fridge for the time being.

Pour 1 tbsp oil into a saucepan set over a high heat and, once hot, add the prawn heads and shells. Fry for 4-5 mins, stirring occasionally until caramelised, then add the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins while stirring. Pour in the stock, add the saffron, if using, and bring to a gentle simmer. Simmer for 30 mins, then use a potato masher to crush the shells and prawn heads as much as possible. Pour into a large jug through a sieve, squeezing as much liquid as possible out. You should have roughly 750ml liquid. If not, add more boiling water to make it up to 750ml.
Finely chop the onion and fennel, then peel and finely chop the garlic.

Heat 3 tbsp oil in a large, deep frying pan set over a medium heat and add the onion and fennel with a pinch of salt. Cook for 8-10 mins until they're soft, then scrape in the garlic and scatter in the fennel seeds and cook for 2 mins until smelling amazing.
Add the rice and stir to coat each grain in the oil before pouring in the wine and bubbling for a few minutes.
Pour in the 750ml of stock, season with salt and pepper and bring to the boil. Put on the lid and cook over a low-medium heat for 20 mins, until the rice is very nearly cooked.
Remove the lid and nestle in the prawn bodies, squid pieces and mussels, then put the lid back on and cook for another 6-8 mins until everything is cooked and the mussels have opened.
Scatter over the parsley and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing over and a big green salad.

name: Seared Prawn Ponzu Glass Noodle Salad
description: This fresh summery salad uses a Cantonese technique of scorching the aromatics with hot oil to bolden the flavours and bring the dish together! Even easier if you use cooked prawns. This recipe also pairs well with white rice.
keywords: seared prawn ponzu glass noodle salad
instructions: Boil the kettle. Submerge the noodles in a bowl of boiling water. Set aside.

Skip this next stage if you’re using cooked prawns. Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Add a generous pinch of salt. Add the prawns, stir, then turn the heat off and leave to cook for 3 mins. Drain the prawns and add them to a bowl of cold water. Set aside.

Smash the garlic with the back of your knife and finely dice. Using a teaspoon, scrape the ginger to remove the skin. Cut five discs of ginger, as thinly as possible. Lay the discs flat on the chopping board and thinly slice into sticks. Cut the chilli in half, remove the seeds, lay flat and slice the chilli lengthways into strips, as thinly as possible. Cut the spring onions into thirds, cut each third in half lengthways, lay flat and cut into thin strips. Set aside.

For the sauce, put the light soy sauce, sugar, MSG, juice of both limes, sesame oil, sesame seeds and a generous pinch of salt and black pepper into a bowl. Stir thoroughly to combine, until the sugar has dissolved.
Drain the prawns and slice them in half lengthways, down the back of the prawn. Thinly slice the cucumber, onion and celery. Pick the coriander and mint leaves, toss together.

Drain the glass noodles and spread over a large plate bowl. Cut the noodles two or three times with scissors. Pour the sauce mixture over the noodles. Add the tossed salad on top, followed by the prawns. Add the spring onions on top of the prawns followed by the chilli, ginger and garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan over a high heat for 3 mins or until smoking. Carefully pour the hot oil over the ginger, chilli and garlic.
Toss everything together, making sure the sauce at the bottom coats everything. Enjoy.

name: Seared Tuna & Olive Grains
description: Perfectly seared tuna on a bed of olive-studded grains, with roasted peppers and jammy eggs. Light, bright, and full of protein.
instructions: Season the tuna steaks with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Finely dice the shallot and add to a bowl with the juice of the lemon. Stir in the honey, oregano and a pinch of salt. Whisk in the olive oil to make your dressing.
Finely mince the olives, sundried tomatoes and roasted peppers. Stir into the dressing, then add the hot grains and toss well to coat.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Once boiling, reduce to a medium heat, gently lower in the eggs and cook for 7 mins until jammy. Transfer to an ice bath, leave to cool, then peel.

Place a frying pan over a high heat with the remaining olive oil. Once hot, add the tuna steaks and sear on both sides until golden and just cooked through. Transfer to a board to rest for a couple of minutes.
Toss the grains and parsley leaves together, then divide between plates. Slice the tuna and halve the eggs, then top both onto the grain mix.

name: Seared Tuna & Olive Tapenade Beans
description: If a dish screamed summer in the Med this is it. Seared tuna with cannellini and green beans in a punchy Kalamata olive dressing. Juicy tomatoes, salty olives and plenty of lemon, ready in under 30 mins.
keywords: Seared Tuna & Olive Tapenade Beans recipe
instructions: Cut the vine tomatoes into big chunks, then dress with a quarter of the extra virgin olive oil, the dried oregano and a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Trim the green beans, then cook for 2-3 mins, until they turn bright green and are just tender but still with plenty of bite. Drain and run briefly under cold water, then leave to dry.
Drain and rinse the cannellini beans. Add them to a large serving bowl with the cooled green beans.

Finely chop the olives and parsley and add to a small bowl. Finely grate in the garlic, then add the juice of the lemon and the remaining extra virgin olive oil. Season with black pepper and a small pinch of salt, remembering the olives are already salty, so taste it first, you might not need as much.
Spoon two-thirds of the olive dressing over the beans. Toss well and leave to sit while you cook the tuna, so the beans can soak up the dressing.

Heat a griddle pan or large frying pan over a high heat. Pat the tuna steaks dry, rub with the olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Cook for 1-2 mins on each side, depending on their thickness and how pink you like them in the middle. Transfer to a plate and squeeze over the juice of the remaining lemon.
The tomatoes should have released their juices, which will add to the dressing. Toss them through the bean salad.
Spoon the dressed beans onto plates, then slice the tuna and arrange it over the top. Drizzle over the remaining olive dressing to serve.

name: Secret Courgette Mint Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: These mint chocolate chip cookies are delicious, and count as one of your five-a-day. You honestly won't believe these have got courgette in them.
keywords: Secret Courgette Mint Chocolate Chip Cookies
instructions: Coarsely grate the courgette and tip into the middle of a clean tea towel. Wring out the excess water and put the dry courgette into a bowl. Set aside.
Combine the oats, flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Set aside.

Tip both sugars into a large bowl. Finely chop the mint leaves and rub into the sugars for a couple of mins to release the oil. Add the butter and beat together until light and fluffy. Whisk in the egg.
Add the dry ingredients to the bowl and break in the chocolate. Tip in the courgette and bring everything together to form a dough. Cover and chill for 2 hours.

Heat the oven to 175°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Take 2 tbsp of cookie dough and roll it into a ball. Put on the lined sheet, leaving plenty of space for spreading. Repeat with the remaining cookie dough.
Bake for 15 mins until cooked through and golden brown.

name: Seeded Sandwich Loaf
description: This may be the softest, fluffiest sandwich bread you’ll ever have. Dotted with mixed seeds, it’ll revolutionise your sandwiches, toasties and anything else you have with it.
instructions: Combine the water, sugar, yeast, olive oil, both flours, salt and all the seeds in a big bowl. Stir together until incorporated. Cover and let the dough rest for 30 mins.

Lightly flour a clean surface, tip the dough out onto it and knead until smooth – add the least amount of flour possible. The dough will feel very sticky at first, but keep on kneading and it’ll come together. Trust the process.

Form the dough into a ball, place it back into the bowl and cover. Allow it to prove at room temperature for at least 1 hr, until doubled in size. Meanwhile, grease a 2LB (see notes) loaf tin with oil.

After proving, lightly flour a clean surface and tip the dough onto it. Stretch the dough into a rectangle, and roll it out to double the length of the tin. Take both short sides and fold them towards the middle, so that the edges meet – the dough should be approximately the same length as the tin. Rotate 90 degrees, take the closest long edge to you and tightly roll it into a log. Place the log of dough into the greased tin, seam-side down. Loosely cover with cling film and prove for 30-45 mins, until when poked, the dough slowly bounces back, leaving a slight indentation.

Halfway through proofing, heat the oven to 180°C. Tip the ice into a baking tin and place onto the bottom of the oven (this will help the bread rise well and create a thin crust). Slide the loaf into the oven and bake for 35-40 mins, until golden brown and cooked through. The bottom should sound hollow when tapped.
Allow to cool for at least 30 mins before slicing.

name: Seeded Turkish Chicken Wraps with Tomato Salsa & Yoghurt Cucumbers
description: Juicy spiced chicken thighs and caramelised onions, piled into sesame-toasted wraps with charred tomato salsa, cool garlicky cucumber yoghurt and a scatter of pomegranate seeds. Perfect for feeding a crowd on a sunny day.
keywords: Sticky & Spicy Chicken Kebabs with Charred Tomato Salsa & Yoghurt Cucumbers
Sticky & Spicy Chicken Kebabs with Charred Tomato Salsa & Yoghurt Cucumbers recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Mince the garlic, dice the chicken into 3cm pieces and thinly slice the onions. Scatter the onion into a medium, lipped oven tray, then pour over the stock and white wine. Sprinkle over two tsp of the brown sugar, season well with salt and set aside.

Heat the olive oil in a small saucepan over a medium heat. Once hot but not smoking, remove from the heat and stir through the ground coriander, smoked paprika, sweet paprika, chilli flakes and cumin seeds, they'll bubble and sizzle. Stir through the salt, garlic, tomato paste and remaining tsp of brown sugar. Pour the mixture over the diced chicken and toss well to coat.

Arrange the chicken over the onion in the oven tray. Bake on the upper rack for 25 mins, until the chicken is golden and cooked through. Remove the chicken and transfer to a medium bowl. Strain the tray juices into a small bowl and set aside. Return the tray to the upper rack for a further 5-10 mins, until the onions are nicely caramelised. Add the onions to the bowl with the chicken, squeeze over the lemon and toss together.

While the chicken bakes, make the charred tomato salsa. Cut the red onion into two wedges. Set a cast-iron skillet or griddle pan over a high heat with a small drizzle of oil. Add the onion wedges, three of the tomatoes and the chilli. Cook for 4-5 mins, turning once or twice, until charred and starting to soften. Remove from the pan and leave to cool for 5 mins.

Once cooled, finely chop the charred veg and add to a bowl. Dice the remaining five tomatoes, mince the garlic and roughly chop the coriander. Add to the bowl along with the pomegranate molasses and a drizzle of olive oil. Season well with salt and toss together. Set aside.

Cut the cucumber in half lengthways and deseed using a teaspoon. Thinly slice on an angle. Mince the garlic and finely chop the dill. Add the cucumber, garlic and dill to a bowl along with the yoghurt, season with salt and toss together.

Set a large frying pan over a high heat. Brush both sides of each tortilla with the reserved chicken pan juices, then sprinkle one side with sesame seeds and a pinch of Aleppo chilli flakes. Fry each tortilla for about 1 min on each side, until lightly charred.

To serve, fill each toasted tortilla with the chicken and onion mixture, yoghurt cucumbers and a spoonful of tomato salsa. Scatter over the pomegranate seeds, wrap tightly and wrap in a piece of baking paper to catch the juices. Serve the remaining salsa on the side.

name: Seedy Chicken Schnitzel with Winter Caesar
description: A crispy air fryer chicken schnitty topped with kale caesar salad. This winter wonder will make you very happy on even the most cold and miserable of days.
keywords: Seedy Schnitzel with Winter Caesar recipe
instructions: Lay out a piece of baking parchment or cling film on your work surface. Put 1 chicken breast on top, cover with another piece of baking parchment or cling film and then bash the chicken with a rolling pin until it’s around 3mm thick. Repeat with the remaining chicken breasts.

Tip the plain flour onto a baking tray and season with salt and pepper. Crack the eggs onto another tray and whisk, then season with salt and pepper. Finally, tip the breadcrumbs and seeds onto another tray then season and mix to combine.
Dip the chicken breasts one at a time into the flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs so that they are totally coated. Pop them on a plate and keep in the fridge until you are ready to cook.

Heat the air fryer to 200°C for a few minutes. Pop the breadcrumbed chicken breasts into the air fryer basket and drizzle with olive oil. Cook for 8-12 min, or until the juices run clear. If you have a temperature probe, it should read 73.9°C.

For the salad, remove the kale leaves from the stems and then roughly chop. Add the kale to a large bowl and squeeze in the juice of the lemon, along with a pinch of salt. Massage until wilted. Slice the romaine lettuce and add to the bowl with the kale. 
De-core the apple, slice and set aside.

For the caesar dressing, put the mayonnaise, yoghurt, anchovies, garlic, Dijon mustard and the juice of the remaining lemon into a blender. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt and a generous grinding of black pepper.
When you’re ready to serve, toss the salad with the dressing. Serve the schnitzel on plates, top with the sliced apple, then finish with a good grating of Parmesan if you like.

name: Seedy Crusted Feta
description: This seedy crusted feta is perfect for meal prep. Combine it with your choice of carb, veg and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Preheat the grill to max.

Tip the seeds out onto a plate and season with pepper. Unpack the feta and dip
each side in the seeds, they will stick naturally to the cheese.

Transfer the feta to a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Slide under the hot grill for 3-4 mins until golden
brown.
Enjoy with your choice of carb and veg. If batch cooking for the week, transfer the feta to a container and store in the fridge until ready to serve.

name: Seedy Crusted Feta
description: This seedy crusted feta is perfect for meal prep. Combine it with your choice of carb, veg and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Preheat the grill to max.

Tip the seeds out onto a plate and season with pepper. Unpack the feta and dip
each side in the seeds, they will stick naturally to the cheese.

Transfer the feta to a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Slide under the hot grill for 3-4 mins until golden
brown.
Enjoy with your choice of carb and veg. If batch cooking for the week, transfer the feta to a container and store in the fridge until ready to serve.

name: Seedy Feta & Giant Couscous Salad
description: After a healthy vegetarian lunch you can prep-ahead for the week? This feta and giant couscous salad will hit the spot.
keywords: Seedy Feta & Giant Couscous Salad recipe
instructions: Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the giant couscous and cook for 6 mins, or until tender. Drain and rinse under cold water. Finely slice the red onion and pick the parsley and dill. Toss the herbs and onion through the couscous with the spinach and a generous squeeze of lemon juice. Season well with salt and pepper.

Slice the courgettes into 3–4cm-thick coins. Heat a large frying pan over high heat and add enough olive oil to coat the base. Season the courgette coins with salt and place cut-side down into the pan. Fry for 4–5 mins until blistered and charred, then flip and cook the other side for 2–3 mins. Turn off the heat and leave them to sit in the pan for 5 mins.

Preheat the grill to high. Tip the seeds onto a plate and season with black pepper. Press each side of the feta into the seeds so they stick. Place the seeded feta on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, and grill for 3–4 mins until golden and lightly crisp.
Make the creamy green dressing. Add the avocado, anchovies, lime juice, chives, basil, kefir and olive oil to a blender. Blitz until smooth and creamy. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon the couscous mixture into containers. Top with chunks of seedy feta and blistered courgette. Serve with the green dressing on the side.

name: Seedy Pork Schnitzel with Sage Fried Eggs
description: This one is as good as it looks. This pork schnitzel can be put together in just 20 minutes and makes a delicious mid-week meal. Enjoy.
keywords: seedy pork schnitzel with sage fried eggs
instructions: Preheat the oven or air fryer to 220°C.

Tip the potatoes into a pan and cover with cold water. Season generously with salt and set over a medium heat. Bring to the boil, reduce to a simmer and let bubble away for 10-12 minutes until the potatoes are tender. Drain and let steam.

Start by bashing out the pork chops. Remove any rind and excess fat before sandwiching the chops between two sheets of parchment paper. Using a heavy pan, bash the pork chops out until they’re super thin.
Set up a station with three bowls, one flour, one egg, one with a mixture of the seeds and breadcrumbs.

Season the pork chops well with salt and pepper and pass through the flour, egg and then the seedy breadcrumb mix. Drizzle with a little oil and lay out on a baking tray. If you’ve got a rack they can rest on while they cook, use it! Slide the pork into the oven/air fryer for 10 mins or until golden brown and crisp.

While the pork bakes, rough up the potatoes by shaking them around in the pot. Finely chop the red onion and dill and tip into the pan with the mustard as well as the zest and juice of a lemon and plenty of olive oil. Toss everything together to coat and season with salt and pepper.

Set a frying pan over a medium heat and add a good glug of olive oil, drop in the sage leaves and sizzle for 30 seconds before cracking in the egg. Season with salt and pepper and fry until done to your liking.
Serve the pork schnitzels with a spoon of potato salad, a lemon wedge, and a sage-fried egg.

name: Seema's Crispy Spring Onion Noodles
description: These noodles are inspired by Shanghai spring onion oil noodles. With only a few ingredients, it's cheap to make and will soon be a staple in your home. Seema x
instructions: Finely slice your spring onions, separating your whites from the greens. Finely chop your ginger, garlic and chillis.
Heat a very generous glug of oil in your wok over medium heat, add the spring onion whites, and let them fry slowly on the lowest heat for 5 minutes.
Add nearly all of the remaining spring onions, saving a handful for later, and gently fry until they are a deep golden brown – this can take up to 20 minutes.
Once browned, strain out the crispy spring onions and transfer the oil to a jar for storing.
Into the wok, add 4 tablespoons of spring onion oil. Once hot, add your garlic, ginger and chillis and stir fry for 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook your noodles for a minute in boiling water.
Toss in the cooked noodles along with your soy sauce and give the mixture a good toss.
Add about half of your crispy spring onions and season with salt if needed.
Plate up and top with more crispy onions as well as your fresh ones. Eat up.

name: Seema's Dal
description: This is my all-time favourite comfort food, especially when I’m missing home. My mum helped me (well I helped her) with this recipe, we hope you love it! Seema
instructions: Wash the red lentils at least 3 times in warm water until the water comes out clear. Place in a large pot with the water and boil for 15 minutes.
Blend the chopped tomatoes in a hand blender.
In a mortar and pestle, bash the ginger, garlic and half of the chilli powder to form a thick paste.

In a large pan, pour two glugs of vegetable oil and heat on medium. Add in the black mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Once they start bubbling add in the chopped tomatoes. Quickly pop a lid on - they will spit out so be careful.
Add in the turmeric, cumin powder, coriander powder, the rest of the chilli powder, the salt and the pounded garlic and ginger paste. Cook on a medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Thinly slice 6 cloves of garlic and the jalepenos, finely chop the coriander and chop 4cm ginger into matchsticks.
For the garlicky oil, heat up the vegetable oil in a small pan and gently cook the thinly sliced garlic and curry leaves until golden.

To check if the dhal is cooked, press a few grains between your fingers to feel if they are tender. Drain the dhal and add it into the curried tomatoes. Add in a mug or so more of water and continue cooking for 2 minutes. Season to taste and stir in ¾ of the coriander.
Pour over garlicky oil over the dhal and put a lid on to allow the garlic flavour to infuse through.
Finish with the remaining ginger, chopped chilli and coriander and serve with a big bowl of rice or just on its own.

name: Seema's Mum's Chicken Curry
description: My mum's chicken curry is what I miss most when I’m away from home. It’s iconic in our family and I’m so excited for us to share this recipe with you. Seema x
instructions: Blend the onion in a food processor until it's roughly chopped.

Heat up 3 large glugs of oil in a large pot. When the oil is hot, add in the cumin seeds. Once the seeds are bubbling, add the cinnamon stick, cloves, black peppercorns, star anise and dried bird's eye chillies. Cook them for 30 secs until they are fragrant.
Add in the blended onion cook for 10 mins on a low heat until they are caramelised and translucent.
Blend the tinned chopped tomato, garlic, fresh bird's eye chillies, and half the ginger in the food processor – don’t worry about washing it between uses.

Once the onions are browned, add the blended tomato mix and chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, ground turmeric and ½ tsp salt. Cook for 10 mins, until the oil starts to separate from the sauce. You can add an extra glug of oil here to help fry the spices.
Add in the chicken and mix well so it’s coated. Cook for another 5 mins.
Pour in 250ml water and mix with the chicken. Pop on a lid and cook for 15 mins.
Finely chop the coriander, julienne the remaining ginger and slice the jalapeños into thick coins.
After 15 mins, stir in the yoghurt and garam masala along with half of fresh coriander, half the julienned ginger and half the sliced jalapeños.
Garnish with the remaining coriander, ginger and chilli. Pop a lid on the pot until you’re ready to serve. Enjoy with rice or freshly made rotli.

name: Seema's Ultimate Gochujang Chicken Burger
description: A crispy chicken burger laced with spicy gochujang. You queued over two hours for this bad boy, and now you can finally make it for yourself.
instructions: Combine your chicken in a bowl with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 1 tbsp gochujang, 2 eggs, yoghurt, ½ tsp white pepper and ½ tsp of salt. Allow to marinate in the fridge for 30 mins or ideally overnight.
Finely chop 5 spring onions and grate your ginger and garlic into a bowl. Whisk in the sour cream, gochujang, 1 tsp apple cider vinegar, sesame oil, honey, 2 tbsp soy sauce, and chilli oil bits.
Shred the cabbage and finely chop the coriander and spring onions. Mix 100g mayo, 3 tbsp apple cider vinegar and ½ tsp salt. Mix it all together scrunching it up with your hands.
Blitz 100g mayo with your kimchi. Taste and add salt, if needed. This will depend on how salty your kimchi already is.
Season the plain flour with 1 tsp salt.

Dunk your chicken pieces into the flour, pressing and squeezing the flour into every crevice of the chicken. Lift the chicken pieces out of the flour and repeat the squeezing process 3 times – the aim is to form lots of craggy bits.
Get a big pot ready (enough for frying) and fill with enough oil. Deep fry the chicken until cooked through and golden brown.

Toast the brioche buns and add in a few dollops of the slaw to the base. After that, layer on your crispy chicken and drizzle over lots of the spicy sauce. Spread the kimchi mayo on the top bun and press down the burger.
Enjoy, but make sure to have a lot of napkins to hand.

name: Self-Saucing Chocolate Pudding
description: The queen of cupcakes, Jemma Wilson, blesses us with the only chocolate pudding recipe you'll ever need. Gooey and fudgey, what more could you want?
keywords: the best self-saucing chocolate pudding recipes
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C (fan assisted).
Grease an 25 x 20cm baking dish with melted butter.

For the topping, sift the muscovado sugar and cocoa powder into a mixing bowl and whisk to combine. Set
aside.
For the cake batter, grab a separate mixing bowl. Sift in all the dry ingredients: the plain flour, caster sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder and pinch of salt. Whisk to combine.

Gently warm the milk in a small pan over a low heat to no warmer than body temperature. Add the warm milk to a clean mixing bowl along with the butter and whisk to combine. Add the egg and vanilla extract and whisk to combine.
Add the egg mixture to the dry ingredients and mix well to combine.
Tip the cake batter into the baking dish and even it out with an off-set spatula or the back of a spoon.
Scatter over the brown sugar and cocoa topping in an even layer.
Spoon the boiling water carefully over the top being careful not to create craters. Don't pour from a height using the jug or you'll disturb the cake batter.
Bake for 25 mins until a skewer comes out clean when poked into a spongey bit.
Cool for 10 mins then serve warm with a dollop of double cream.

name: Sesame & Ginger Cod Wrap
description: This is a special one. Marinate your cod in sesame, ginger and soy. Fry it on a high heat so you get the caramelised crispy bits. Perfect in a wrap.
instructions: Chop up the cod into chunks.
Chop your ginger into matchsticks and mix together 4 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp sesame oil, and the juice of a lime. Season with a pinch of salt, mix with the cod, and marinate for 30 minutes.
Cabbage time. Chop your red cabbage into quarters and slice as thinly as possible so that you have shavings of cabbage. Do this by running your knife through point to point.
Add this into a bowl with the juice of a lime, 4 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tbsp sesame oil. Mix together and place in the fridge.
Mayo time. Add 6 tbsp mayo to a bowl along with a tbsp of hot sauce and a tbsp soy sauce and mix together

Prepare avocado. Remove the skin and chop it into square chunks. Thinly slice your coriander then mix together (saving some coriander for garnish) with a squeeze of lime juice - you don’t want this mushy. Season with salt and pepper.
Once the cod has marinated, remove from the fridge, and add to a hot pan of vegetable oil. Fry until caramelised and tender

Warm a tortilla and then get your plate and layer up. Place a dollop of your mayo in the centre of the tortilla and use a spoon to spread it out, add a wad of cabbage, a spoonful of flakey cod and the avocado mix. Scatter with your leftover coriander, then wrap up and tuck in!

name: Sesame Crispy Chickpea Salad
description: Crispy chickpeas are a wonderful addition to this bright and flavourful salad.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Drain and pat the chickpeas dry. Place onto a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Toss to evenly coat and season with salt. Place in the oven and roast until golden and crispy, 25-30 mins.
Meanwhile, trim and separate the romaine leaves. Trim the Tenderstem and halve. Trim and chop the cucumber into small 1cm chunks.

For the dressing: stir the tahini, soy sauce, sugar, rice vinegar, dashi powder (skip the dashi to keep it vegan), toasted sesame seeds, water, and the juice of the lemon until creamy. It’ll split at first, but keep going. Add a tbsp of water at a time if you want it thinner.
Meanwhile, tear the sourdough bread into 2cm pieces, place onto another baking tray and drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, toss, then roast until golden brown, 10-15 mins.
Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, add the broccoli and cook for 3-4 mins until tender. The last minute, drop the peas and edamame to reheat. Let fully drain.
Divide the lettuce between bowls and top with the veggies, chickpeas, croutons, crispy onions and furikake. Drizzle the dressing over and serve with a wedge of lemon. Toss before eating.

name: Sesame Crusted Cod & Creamy Chilli Chickpeas
description: Crispy sesame cod, spicy chickpeas and a glossy tahini sauce. A mid-week win that is way easier than it looks.
keywords: Sesame Crusted Cod and Creamy Chilli Oil Chickpeas recipe
Sesame Crusted Cod and Creamy Chilli Oil Chickpeas
instructions: Season the fish all over with salt and place onto a plate or rack. Set aside in the fridge for a minimum of 30 mins, up to overnight - this will help with the texture of the cod, making it more firm.
Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Defrost the spinach and squeeze any excess moisture out. Keeping the bean liquid, drain the chickpeas. Stir the tahini, miso, vinegar and the juice of half the lemons, adding in the cold water, until it becomes smooth. Taste and season with sugar and salt, if needed.
Finely slice the chives and set aside.

Pat the cod fillets dry, then coat all over in the sesame seeds. Place onto a baking tray lined with baking paper, drizzle with a little olive oil and bake for 10–15 mins, until the fish is cooked through and the sesame is golden.
Meanwhile, set a medium saucepan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 4–5 mins until they start to blister and soften.
Tip in the chickpeas, spinach and any leftover sesame seeds. Add a splash of chickpea liquid and cook for 2-3 mins until everything’s warmed through.

Take the pan off the heat and stir through the tahini dressing. If it looks a bit thick, add another splash of chickpea liquid to loosen. Taste and adjust with more miso or a pinch of sugar if it needs it. Set to low heat to keep warm.

Swirl half the chilli oil through the creamy chickpeas and spoon into bowls. Top each with a sesame-crusted cod fillet, drizzle with the rest of the chilli oil, scatter over the chives and serve with a wedge of lemon.

name: Sesame Crusted Salmon With Minty Butter Beans
description: Ready in under 30 mins and prepared with the freshest ingredients, this salmon dish is about to become a favourite in your household.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic cloves. Heat a glug of olive oil in a heavy bottomed pan over low-medium heat and add the garlic. Cook gently for 3 mins, until the garlic is really aromatic and starting to turn golden.
Tip the butter beans into the pan, juice and all, then add the kale in batches, adding more when the previous lot has wilted.
Zest and juice ½ the lemons and cut the remaining lemon into wedges. Finely chop the fresh mint. Set aside.
Transfer ⅓ of the bean mix to a blender and blitz until smooth along with the water. Add back into the pan.
Add the lemon zest, lemon juice and sugar snap peas to the beans. Mix to combine and simmer away for about 3 mins, then turn the heat down to low until you're ready to serve.
Meanwhile, get started on the salmon. Get ⅔ of the sesame seeds onto a plate, then take the salmon and press into the seeds, skin-side down.

Place the salmon fillets in a cold frying pan and set it over a low-medium heat. Cook for 10 mins until the salmon is 90% cooked through then flip and cook for another minute. Discard the seeds you used to coat the salmon with.
Serve the beans topped with the salmon, fresh mint, remaining sesame seeds and a wedge of lemon.

name: Sesame Eggs
description: These sesame-coated eggs are perfect for meal prep. Combine them with your choice of carb, veg and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
keywords: Savoury Peanut Beans & Sesame Eggs recipe
instructions: Bring a saucepan full of water to the boil. Once boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook for 7 mins. Transfer to a bowl of ice water for a couple of minutes, before peeling them. Add the sesame onto a plate and gently roll the eggs in them until covered.
Carefully transfer the eggs to a container and store in the fridge until ready to serve.

name: Sesame Eggs With Minty Butter Beans
description: Ready in under 30 mins and prepared with the freshest ingredients, this dish is about to become a favourite in your household.
instructions: Start by peeling and finely slicing the garlic cloves. Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a heavy bottomed pan over medium-low heat and add the garlic. Cook gently for 3 mins, until the garlic is really aromatic and starting to turn golden. Tip the beans into the pan, juice and all, along with the kale. You will likely need to add in batches, adding more when the previous lot has wilted.
Zest and juice one of the lemons, then pick the mint leaves.
Take out around 350g of the bean mix, and blend until smooth along with 150ml of water. Add back into the pan.
Mix the lemon zest and juice through the beans, then cut the remaining lemon into wedges for serving. Add the sugar snaps and simmer away for about 3 mins.

Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium high heat. Once shimmering, crack 2 of the eggs in and fry until the white is set and starting to crisp up around the edges. Add the sesame seeds to the pan for the last minute, spooning them, with a little of the oil in the pan, over the edges of the eggs. Remove with a slotted spoon onto a plate and repeat with the remaining eggs.
Serve the beans topped with the sesame-fried eggs, mint leaves, and a wedge of lemon.

name: Sesame Eggs with Chilli Crisp Rice & Greens
description: Crispy rice, spicy greens and sesame-fried eggs, this punchy 15-minute dish hits every texture and flavour craving at once.
instructions: Add the olive oil to a frying pan and place over a high heat. Once hot, add the rice and cook for 5–6 mins, tossing occasionally, until the grains are crispy and the surface is golden or starting to char.

Add the garlic purée, peas and spinach to the pan. Toss everything together and cook for another couple of minutes until the spinach is wilted and the peas are defrosted. Remove from the heat and stir through the chilli oil.

Meanwhile, set another frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the sesame seeds and crack in the eggs. Fry to your liking, spooning the sesame oil over the eggs as they cook. Season with salt and black pepper.
Share the rice between plates and top with the sesame eggs.

name: Sesame Halloumi
description: We love halloumi. It's salty, delicious, and the perfect main for your work-from-home lunch.
instructions: Squeeze the lemon juice into a bowl, then stir in the honey, sesame seeds, chilli flakes if using, a good pinch of salt and black pepper and 3 tbsp water to make the halloumi dressing.
Drain and cut the halloumi into thick slices. Get your largest frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the halloumi and fry for around 2 mins on each side until crisp and golden.
Turn down the heat to the lowest setting, pour in the sesame honey dressing and cook for 1 min more, using a spoon to baste the halloumi in the dressing.
Throw the halloumi onto a base of your choice and enjoy!

name: Sesame Halloumi & Watermelon Salad
description: The saltiness of the halloumi in this recipe pairs wonderfully with the sweetness of the watermelon. This is our kind of salad.
instructions: Halve, then quarter the watermelon and cut away the green rind. Slice into random triangular pieces. Pile the watermelon high on a big salad platter, or divide between four plates.

Pick the mint leaves and zest the lemon. Squeeze the lemon juice into a bowl, then stir in the honey, sesame seeds, chilli flakes if using, a good pinch of salt and black pepper and 3 tbsp water to make the halloumi dressing.
Drain and cut the halloumi into thick slices. Get your largest frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the halloumi and fry for around 2 mins on each side until crisp and golden.
Turn down the heat to the lowest setting, pour in the sesame honey dressing and cook for 1 min more, using a spoon to baste the halloumi in the dressing.
Top the watermelon with the halloumi and dressing, then scatter over the mint leaves and lemon zest to serve. Unreal.

name: Sesame Mackerel Salad
description: Miso and tahini add a thump of richness to this smoked mackerel salad. Healthy and delicious, what more could you want?
instructions: Get a medium-sized pan of salted water on to the boil. Top and tail the green beans, then add to the boiling water along with the edamame. Cook for 3 mins.
Pop some ice in a large bowl filled with cold water, then spoon the cooked beans straight in with a slotted spoon. Let them chill in there, then drain and pat dry.

Add the miso paste to a bowl along with the tahini, vinegar, honey, sesame oil and water. Grate in the ginger and squeeze in the juice of the lime, then give it a good whisk until it comes together as a smooth dressing. Season with salt to taste.

Add the spinach to a large bowl, then tip in the cooked beans. Cut the avocado into chunks, then add this too. Break the mackerel into pieces and pop into the bowl, then drizzle over the dressing. Toss until combined.
Spoon the salad into bowls, then sprinkle over the sesame seeds and coriander leaves. Serve it up.

name: Sesame Miso Chicken Caesar Salad
description: Caesar dressing from scratch, made even better with miso. Umami-packed salad with homemade croutons, juicy chicken, crisp lettuce and the creamiest dressing.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Separate the leaves of the romaine — if you want extra crunchy lettuce, add them into a large bowl of ice water. Right before serving, drain the romaine and let it completely dry.
Finely grate the cheese. Place the chicken and 2 tbsp of miso into another bowl, mix together until evenly coated. Season with salt and pepper.

Zest half of the lemon and then cut in half. Grate the garlic into a food processor and squeeze in the juice of 1 lemon, set aside. Add the egg yolks, anchovy fillets, dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, white wine vinegar and the remaining miso into the garlic, blend until a paste forms. Slowly trickle in 100ml of olive oil whilst blending until the dressing thickens. If it's too thick, add a teaspoon of water at a time, if it’s too thin, add a little more oil.
Once the dressing has thickened, taste and season with salt, plenty of fresh cracked pepper and more lemon juice if needed. Fold in the lemon zest and 50g of cheese, then set aside.

Cut or rip the bread into 2cm cubes and place into a bowl. Drizzle over 2 tbsp of olive oil and season with salt and plenty of black pepper. Toss it all together and place on a baking tray. Bake the bread for 15-20 mins, until golden and crunchy.

Place a frying pan over medium heat with 2 tbsp of oil. Once hot, add the chicken in and cook until the chicken starts to brown and char in some spots, 4-5 mins on each side. Pour in the mirin, soy and 40ml water. Stir through the sugar and 1.5 tbsp of toasted sesame seeds, cook, spooning the sauce over the chicken until it thickens and glazes it, 4-6 mins. Rest the chicken, then slice before serving.
Toss the salad with the dressing, top with the croutons, sticky sesame miso chicken, the remaining grated cheese and toasted sesame. Finish with some more freshly cracked black pepper.

name: Sesame Miso Dressing
description: This Sesame Miso Dressing is guaranteed to up your salad game. Whip it up in just 5 minutes and enjoy.
instructions: Add the miso to the bowl and whisk in the pickled ginger liquid, honey, sesame oil, and fish sauce.
Once combined, add the sesame seeds and the juice of the lime.
Whisk and add salt or a splash more lime juice if you need to.

name: Sesame Miso Salmon Tacos
description: These tacos are a brilliant way to turn yesterday’s leftovers from your Zingy Green Miso Salmon batch into a next-day banger.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Zingy Green Miso Salmon batch recipe.
Thinly shred the cabbage and add into a bowl with the veg from the salmon. Add the sesame oil, rice vinegar and season with salt. Toss together and set aside.
