In a small bowl, stir the Gochujang into the mayo. Reheat the salmon and tortillas until warm and flexible.
Spread the spicy mayo over the tortillas, top with the salmon and slaw. Serve with a lime wedge for squeezing.

name: Sesame Noodles
description: These sesame noodles, also known as ma jiang mian, are suitable for most work from home days. They’re delicious and take just 15 minutes to make.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Cook your noodles following pack instructions, reserving the starchy cooking water. Crush the peanuts and set aside.
Add a splash of vegetable oil to a frying pan set over a medium heat along with the pork mince and dark soy sauce. Fry for around 6 mins until cooked. Set aside.
Meanwhile, mix all the seasoning ingredients together in a small bowl. Divide this mixture between two serving bowls and add a ladle of the starchy noodle-cooking water to each bowl. Mix well.
Divide the cooked noodles between the serving bowls, mix everything together and top with the cooked pork mince, coriander, crushed peanuts and a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Sesame Prawn Toastie
description: The classic Chinese takeaway dish made in your toastie maker. Crunchy, fried sesame toast with ginger and garlic infused prawns inside - delicious.
instructions: Roughly chop half of your prawns. Set aside.

Grate your ginger and garlic clove. Combine in a bowl with the soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and just the egg white (you can use the yolk to make mayonnaise). Add the remaining prawns and place in a food processor blending until you have a smooth paste.
Finely chop your spring onions and add to the paste with the rest of your chopped prawns.
Freeze for 20 minutes.
Turn on your toastie maker and pour sesame seeds into a wide-rimmed bowl.

Butter bread on one side. Using a spoon, smear filling onto the unbuttered side of the bread. Heap it into the middle so it thins towards the edges. Carefully place the slice into the sesame seeds prawn-side down and press so that the seeds stick. Turn over and press extra seeds into any bare patches.

Brush both sides of the toastie maker with vegetable oil. Carefully place slices onto the toastie maker so the buttered side is underneath and the sesame seeds are on top. Close the lid. When light goes off, open toastie maker and turn toastie through 90 degrees so the toast is cut into four triangles. Close lid and toast for a further 3 minutes. Remove your prawn toasts from the toastie maker and cut along the lines. Serve with dipping sauce of your choice - we like to combine soy sauce and shaoxing wine.

name: Sesame Salmon, Cabbage Slaw & Crispy Rice
description: Crispy pan rice, flaky salmon and a creamy tahini and sesame dressing, all done in 25 mins. The kind of weeknight dinner that feels way more impressive than the effort involved.
instructions: Using a mandolin or vegetable peeler, finely shave the cabbage. Then roughly chop the coriander, this acts as salad leaves in your slaw so you can go a little chunkier.

Heat half the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the cooked rice in one even layer. Scatter the butter over the top, cover and cook undisturbed for 7–10 mins, until deeply golden and crispy on the bottom.

Meanwhile, place a second frying pan over a medium heat with the remaining tsp of olive oil. Season the salmon with salt, then add skin-side down. Cook undisturbed for 5–7 mins, until about three-quarters cooked through. Remove from the heat, flip skin-side up and leave to finish cooking in the residual heat.

Now for the dressing. Squeeze the juice of the lemon into a bowl and add the mayonnaise, tahini, sesame oil and sesame seeds. Taste and season with soy sauce and salt and add a splash of cold water to loosen if needed. Add the cabbage and coriander and toss through.
Divide the crispy rice and slaw between plates and top with the salmon skin-side up. Drizzle over any remaining dressing and squeeze over the remaining lemon half to serve.

name: Sesame Tofu Toast
description: My favourite takeaway side reinvented for vegans. Tofu is whizzed up with lots of lovely things, spread on bread and fried. Crispy, fragrant, just delightful.
instructions: Roughly chop your spring onion, ginger, garlic and coriander.

Place your tofu in a food processor or blender along with your spring onions, ginger, garlic and coriander. Add your cornflour, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Whizz up until you have a thick paste.

Cut your crusts off your slices of bread. Spread each slice with a thick layer of your tofu mixture. Sprinkle the surface of each with sesame seeds and press down with your fingers so that they stick.

Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a medium sized frying pan. Add your slices of toast tofu side up and fry for 2 minutes until you have a crispy golden base. Carefully flip over and cook for 2 minutes on the other side until crisp.
Drain your toast on a plate lined with kitchen paper whilst you repeat the frying with your remaining toast slices.
Cut each slice of toast into 4 triangles and serve up with crispy chilli oil.

name: Shakshuka-Inspired Gnocchi
description: This dish is inspired by the flavours of shakshuka, a Middle Eastern and North African dish full of tomatoes and spices. I added some lemony tofu crumbles too.
instructions: First, marinate the tofu. Pat it dry and crumble the tofu, then add the juice of 1 lemon, the nutritional yeast and ½ -1 tsp salt (taste as you go - I like this quite salty) a sprinkle of pepper and ½ tbsp of olive oil. Use a fork to mix it into crumbles and set aside.
Drain and slice the red peppers about 1cm thick. Finely chop the onion and garlic.
For the gnocchi, add 2 tbsp of olive oil into a large pan or pot over medium heat. Fry the onion for about 5 mins until softened, then add the garlic and fry for a further 2 mins.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, paprika and cayenne pepper if using, and cook, stirring, for a further 1-2 mins. Then add the peppers and cook for a few more minutes.

Mix in the tomatoes, gnocchi and harissa and simmer gently, stirring from time to time, for 7-10 mins. If the sauce becomes a little too thick, add a splash of water. It’s done when the gnocchi is cooked and the tomatoes have turned into a lovely sauce. Taste and season well with salt and pepper, adding more harissa if you like.
To serve, ladle the gnocchi into bowls and top with some crumbled tofu. Finish with a sprinkle of coriander, a drizzle of olive oil and a few twists of pepper.

name: Shallot Tarte Tatin
description: This tart is covered in delicious caramelised shallots and finished with a zingy basil dressing.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Unroll the puff pastry and cut into a circle slightly wider than the base of your frying pan. Transfer the pastry to a baking tray and put into the freezer while you prepare the shallots.
Peel and halve the shallots and place cut side up into the same pan you used to measure the pastry. You want enough that the entire base is covered by a single layer but without overlapping.
Add a drizzle of olive oil and a good pinch of salt and fry over a medium heat for about 4 mins. Turn the shallots and cook for another 5 mins until the cut side is golden brown.
Pour in the red wine vinegar and let it bubble away and evaporate. Finely chop the rosemary, sprinkle over and then turn off the heat.
Remove the pastry from the freezer and place over the shallots, then place the pan into the oven for 30 mins.

Meanwhile, make the basil drizzle by crushing the garlic in a pestle and mortar along with a pinch of salt until creamy. Add the basil and mix until you have a paste. Drizzle in 3 tbsp of olive oil and stir well.
Alternatively, whizz the garlic, basil, olive oil and salt in a blender until combined but not completely smooth.
Remove the tart from the oven and flip over onto a plate. Drizzle over the basil oil, a pinch of chilli flakes (if you like) and some freshly chopped parsley.

name: Sharing Steak With Black Pepper & Parmesan Butter
description: A big piece of meat to share is a great way to tackle cooking for a crowd. You could serve this with any flavoured butter, I love this one! B x
instructions: Pull your steak out of the fridge about an hour before you want to cook it. Season with plenty of flaky salt and rub with a dash of olive oil.
Chuck your peppercorns into a small saucepan and toast over a medium heat until fragrant. Coarsely grind in a pestle and mortar or spice grinder.

Add the butter to a mixing bowl and grate in the parmesan and garlic. Finely chop your parsley and get that in there too along with the zest and juice of one lemon and your ground peppercorns. Beat everything together, season with salt and set aside.
Now light the Weber Genesis BBQ, add the Weber Crafted Sear Grate and get it raging hot.

Grill your steak, turning regularly, until medium-rare or medium. You can use the Weber Connect Thermometer to check the internal temperature. For medium-rare, pull the steak off the barbecue at 42°C and rest for 15 mins. For medium, pull it off at 48°C and rest for 15 mins.
Brush your steak with a tablespoon of the butter while it rests. Pop the rest of the butter into a small saucepan and melt on the barbecue.
Carve the bone from your steak and then cut into 1-2cm thick slices. Cover the steak with the melted parmesan butter.
Serve with extra lemon wedges plus some bread, a few salads and a cold beer for the ultimate barbecue centrepiece.
Get stuck in.

name: Shaved Sprout Salad
description: If brussels sprouts aren't your favourite part of a roast dinner then you're not doing them right. This sprout salad is super fresh and delicious.
instructions: Trim and wash the brussels. Slice them as thinly as you can and add to a large mixing bowl. Season with salt and toss.
Place the pancetta into a cold pan and begin to fry on a medium heat until it becomes crispy. Remove the meat from the pan and set aside. You can clean off your pan after this.
Add the butter to a small saucepan and cook until nut brown.
Thinly slice the pear and onion and roughly chop the parsley, add to the bowl with the shaved sprouts.

To make the dressing, combine the brown butter and orange juice in a small mixing bowl. Whisk in the vinegar and mustard. Season with salt and pepper to taste. The dressing should be tart, sweet, rich and smoky, with a decent punch of mustard.
Toss the dressing with the shaved veggies and finish with the crispy pancetta lardons and a good grating of parmesan. Toss everything together and serve.

name: Shawarma Spiced Halloumi Rice Bowl
description: Chunky, golden shawarma-spiced halloumi, roasted mushrooms and fluffy buttery rice. It’s just like a kebab, but in a bowl...
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Wash the rice until the water runs clear, then drain well.

Melt the butter in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the orzo and toast for 5-10 mins, stirring regularly, until deeply golden. Stir through the rice, then pour in the water. Bring to the boil, then pop a lid on, reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins. Once the time is up, remove the pan from the heat and leave it to steam for 10 mins with the lid on.

Meanwhile, split the halloumi down the crease and chop into 2cm chunks. Halve any larger mushrooms.
Peel and finely grate the garlic into a bowl. Stir through the yoghurt, tomato purée, and Al'Fez Shawarma Spice Mix to taste. Season with salt, then toss in the halloumi and mushrooms until well coated.

Line a baking tray with baking parchment. Tip the marinated halloumi and mushrooms onto the tray and spread out. Roast for 15-20 mins, until golden and starting to char.
Peel and finely slice the red onion, then toss it with the sumac (if using) and a pinch of salt. Set aside to soften slightly.

Pick the parsley leaves and finely slice the stalks and half the leaves.
Once the rice is ready, fluff it with a fork and stir through the chopped parsley. Season to taste.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the roasted halloumi and mushrooms. Finish with the sumac onions, parsley leaves and a generous drizzle of Al'Fez Tahini Squeezy Sauce.

name: Shredded Chicken & Tahini Lettuce Cups
description: Shredded chicken, crisp gem lettuce and a creamy, nutty tahini dressing with a kick of chilli oil. Light, fresh and genuinely fun to eat - just scoop and go.
keywords: Shredded Chicken & Tahini Lettuce Cups recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Add the chicken breasts to a baking tray, drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Slide into the oven and cook for 20 mins, until cooked through, then set aside to cool.

Make the dressing. Add the tahini to a bowl with the juice of the lime and mix well — it'll clump up at first, but don't worry. Slowly add water, a splash at a time (you'll need quite a lot), until it forms a creamy dressing. Stir through the soy sauce. Dollop the chilli oil on top and marble it through by dragging a spoon through it. Set aside.
Shred the chicken. You can use a hand mixer, or just add the cooked breasts to a bowl and pull apart with two forks.
Slice the cucumber into matchsticks and add to the chicken bowl. Roughly chop most of the coriander and add to the bowl.

Cut the base from the gem lettuce heads and pull the leaves apart. Spoon the tahini chicken filling into each cup, top with the remaining coriander leaves, a scatter of sesame seeds and a little extra chilli oil.

name: Shredded Chicken & Warming Spring Onion Brothy Rice
description: This dish is inspired by my love for Cantonese spring onion ginger oil and bai qie ji. The broth is perfectly fragrant and savoury, with juicy poached chicken and veg. A quick and delicious brothy rice meal, perfect for eating fresh or even meal prepping.
keywords: Shredded Chicken & Warming Spring Onion Brothy Rice
Shredded Chicken & Warming Spring Onion Brothy Rice Recipe
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions.

Trim and thinly slice the spring onions. Finely grate the ginger. Add both into a saucepan, with a drizzle of sesame oil. Set the pan over a medium heat and gently cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 mins until the onions have wilted.

Add the white pepper and pour the chicken stock in. Let it come to the boil then turn the heat down to low-medium, season with salt and gently drop the chicken thighs in. Leave for 10-15 mins until fully cooked.
Meanwhile, trim and chop the pak choi into 2-3cm chunks. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems.
Once the chicken is cooked, use a slotted spoon to transfer it from the broth to a large bowl. Leave to cool for a couple of mins, then use two forks to shred it. Cover to keep warm.

Add the coriander stems and pak choi into the hot broth and cook for 2-4 mins, until wilted. Then use a slotted spoon to transfer the veg to the chicken bowl. Add the sesame oil and coriander leaves and toss to combine. Taste and season the broth with salt and white pepper, if needed.
To serve, share the rice between bowls and ladle the broth over. Top with the chicken mixture and a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Shredded Chicken Congee
description: This comforting Chinese classic is perfect for when you’re feeling under the weather. It’s hearty, warming and easy to make. Make it as simple or spicy as you like by adapting the amount of chilli oil.
instructions: Add the chicken stock, chicken stock cube, ½ the fresh ginger (kept whole) and ½ the spring onion (kept whole) to a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over a high heat then add the whole chicken breast, cover with a lid and turn the heat down to low. Simmer for 25 mins then remove the chicken and leave to cool. Leave the stockpot off the heat for now.
Meanwhile, cook the eggs in boiling water for 5 mins 45 seconds then remove to a bowl of cold water and set aside.
Add the jasmine rice to the chicken stock. Partially cover with the lid and bring to a boil over a high heat then lower the heat to medium and cook for 20 mins.

Meanwhile, cut the remaining fresh ginger into thin strips and finely mince the remaining spring onions and coriander then add all three to a bowl and stir to combine. Shred the chicken using fingers or a fork. Peel and halve the eggs.

When the rice time is up, vigorously run a fork through it for 1 min to break up the grains then pop the lid on and simmer for another 5 mins. Repeat the process, leaving it to simmer for another 5 mins.
Remove the pot from the heat, add the shredded chicken, light soy sauce, white pepper and MSG and give everything a good mix. Season with salt to taste.
Ladle the congee into large bowls. Add a generous handful of the spring onion mixture, the eggs, a sprinkle of crispy fried garlic and a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Shredded Chicken Noodle Salad
description: It's a fresh and delicious noodle salad recipe that's ridiculously easy to make. The best high-protein dinner you can make in 15 minutes.
instructions: Add the rice noodles to a bowl and cover with the boiling water. Add the dark soy and stir. Set aside.

Meanwhile, finely slice two-thirds of the garlic cloves. Heat the vegetable oil in a small frying pan over a medium heat for around 1-2 mins. Add the garlic and stir for 1 min or until slightly golden but not burnt. Drain the noodles and add back into the bowl. Pour the garlic and oil over the noodles and toss to combine.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Once boiling, add the chicken breasts, lower the heat and cook, covered, for 10 mins. Remove the chicken and set aside to cool. Reserve 90ml cooking water.
Pound the bird’s-eye chillies and the remaining garlic cloves in a pestle and mortar, or chop finely.
For the dressing, combine the fish sauce, sugar, rice vinegar, lime juice, reserved cooking water, pounded chilli and garlic in a bowl. Stir thoroughly until the sugar has dissolved. Set aside.
Chop the peanuts into small pieces. Set aside. Slice the leek in half, lay it flat and slice into matchsticks.

Add a splash of more oil to a frying pan set over a medium heat and leave to heat up for 2 mins. Add the leeks and fry for 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until golden brown. Remove and sprinkle with a pinch of salt.

Chop the mint, coriander and Thai basil into 1cm pieces. Slice the celery diagonally into thin strips. Thinly slice the red onion and cucumber as fine as possible. Using your fingers, shred the chicken into strips. Transfer everything to a mixing bowl. Toss the salad until thoroughly combined.

Divide the garlic noodles between plates. Grab a generous handful of the chicken salad and place on top. Sprinkle with crushed peanuts, fried shallots and, finally, fried leeks. Give the dressing a stir and generously pour over to serve.

name: Shredded Chipotle & Pineapple Chicken Tacos
description: Sticky, spicy chipotle chicken loaded into soft tortillas with a zingy pineapple salsa. For an extra whack of protein, we've added herby cottage cheese.
instructions: Pour the pineapple juice and chicken stock into a saucepan. Stir through the chipotle paste (add less if you don't like spice) and season with salt. Nestle in the chicken breasts, set over a medium-high heat and bring to the boil. Turn the heat down to medium-low and simmer for 10-15 mins, until the chicken is cooked through.

Meanwhile, finely dice the red onion. Roughly chop the pineapple and add both to a bowl. Zest one of the limes and set the zest aside. Squeeze over the juice of two limes and season with salt. Toss together and set aside to pickle.

Pick a few coriander leaves for garnish, then chuck the rest (stalks and all) into a blender with the cottage cheese. Blitz until smooth and season with salt and lime zest - If you don’t want to blend, finely chop the coriander and stir it through instead.

Once the chicken is cooked, transfer it to a board and use two forks to shred. Return the shredded chicken to the pan and crank the heat to high. Let it bubble away for 5-10 mins, or until the sauce coats the chicken nicely.
Toast the tortillas in a dry frying pan or directly over a flame until soft and warmed through.

Build your tacos. Fill each tortilla with the juicy chipotle chicken, a generous spoonful of the coriander cottage cheese and the tangy pineapple salsa. Scatter with the reserved coriander leaves and serve with lime wedges on the side.

name: Shredded Egg Mayo Pittas
description: Creamy, spicy egg mayo stuffed into a toasted pitta with cool cucumber and a hit of sriracha. A proper upgrade on a lunchbox classic, ready in 20 mins and good in the fridge for three days.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and cook for 8 mins 30 secs. Transfer to a bowl of iced water and leave to chill for a few minutes, replacing the water and ice if needed to keep them cooling quickly. Peel and set aside.

Make the egg mayo. Add the yoghurt, mayonnaise, sriracha and the juice of the lime to a bowl and season well with salt and black pepper. Using a potato ricer, press the eggs straight into the bowl — or grate them on a box grater, or mash with a fork if you prefer. Add the chopped coriander and stir everything together well. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Slice the cucumber. When ready to serve, toast the pittas, then split and stuff with the egg mayo and cucumber slices. Finish with extra sriracha if you like.

name: Shredded Halloumi & Steak Tacos
description: Crispy shredded halloumi pressed into a corn tortilla, topped with juicy paprika-rubbed sirloin, creamy avocado and a punchy sweetcorn and jalapeño salsa. A proper taco night upgrade.
instructions: Start with the salsa. Finely dice the tomatoes, finely slice the roasted red peppers and finely chop the jalapeño and parsley, then add everything to a small bowl. Drain the sweetcorn and tip it in. Squeeze in the lime juice, add the hot sauce and a splash of olive oil, then season well with salt and black pepper. Taste and add more hot sauce if you like. Set aside.

Drizzle the steaks with a little olive oil, sprinkle over the paprika and season generously with salt and black pepper. Rub with your hands until the steaks are well coated. Place a large frying pan over a high heat and, once very hot, add the steaks standing fat-side down, use tongs to hold them in place, and cook for 20-30 seconds until the fat is golden. Tip them onto their sides and cook for 1 min 30 secs on each side. For the last 30 seconds, add the butter and spoon it continuously over the steaks, then remove from the pan and set aside to rest.

While the steak rests, toast the tortillas. If you have a gas hob, add them one by one directly over the flame, flipping until lightly charred. If not, heat a dry pan until very hot and toast them one at a time, flipping halfway. As each one comes off, wrap it in a clean tea towel, adding each to the pile and re-wrapping as you go — this keeps them soft and pliable.
Halve, pit and peel the avocado, then slice. Set aside.

Now for the crispy halloumi. Place a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat — it's important the pan is non-stick here. Use a peeler to shred the halloumi directly into the pan in a thin, even layer. Allow to cook for about 20 seconds, until you can see the edges turning lightly golden, then press a tortilla on top and push it down firmly with a spatula. Flip it out onto a tray so the halloumi is on top, then repeat with the remaining tortillas, wiping out any stray halloumi between batches if needed.

Slice the steak against the grain, then across into cubes, and hit with a little more salt. Top each taco with avocado, steak and salsa, then finish with a squeeze of lime and extra hot sauce if you like.

name: Shredded Sumac Chicken Sandwich with Aioli
description: Juicy leftover sumac chicken tossed in a garlicky mayo-mustard dressing with fresh herbs and spring onions, stuffed into toasted bread. It's banging.
keywords: shredded sumac chicken salad sandwich recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake batch recipe.
In a large bowl, finely grate the garlic, zest half of the lemon and squeeze the juice in. Season with salt and set aside.

Shred the chicken from the sumac chicken traybake and roughly chop the roasted onions from the traybake into 1cm chunks. Pick the parsley and coriander leaves, thinly slicing the stalks. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions.

Stir the Dijon mustard and mayonnaise into the garlic mixture, then add the chicken, roasted onions, spring onions and herb stalks. Toss together until well coated. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.

Toast the bread, then spread the chicken salad over one slice of each sandwich. Toss the parsley and coriander leaves together, place on top of the chicken salad and drizzle with olive oil. Sandwich together and eat straight away.

name: Shredded Turkey Ravioli with Crispy Sage & Hazelnut Butter
description: Leftover turkey just had a glow up. Tossed with buttery hazelnuts, crispy sage and loads of cheese - this ravioli is fast, rich and deeply satisfying.
instructions: Grate the Parmesan. Zest the lemon, then cut it in half and squeeze the juice into a small bowl.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil.
Shred the turkey. Pick the sage leaves from their stalks. Roughly chop the hazelnuts.

Add the butter to a frying pan set over a medium heat. Once foaming, stir in the hazelnuts and cook for 3-4 mins until toasted. Add the sage leaves and cook until crispy and dark green. Use a slotted spoon to lift the sage and hazelnuts out onto a plate, leaving the butter in the pan.
Tip the turkey into the pan with the butter and fry for 6-7 mins until golden and starting to crisp.
Drop the ravioli into the boiling water and cook following pack instructions.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked ravioli straight into the pan with the turkey. Add a splash of pasta water and stir vigorously until the butter emulsifies into a glossy sauce.
Remove from the heat. Toss the Parmesan through and season with salt, pepper, lemon zest and a squeeze of lemon juice to taste.
Spoon the ravioli between plates and scatter over the crispy sage and toasted hazelnuts.

name: Shrimp & Grits
description: Buttery corn grits and cajun-spiced prawns. An iconic Southern US combo.
instructions: For the grits, add the water to the pan and whisk in the corn grits (or you can use polenta if you prefer) and bay leaves. Set over a medium heat and bring up to a boil, whisking constantly until the pan is up to temperature. We’re going to cook the corn grits for 50-60 mins and while you don’t need to stand there the entire time whisking away, you want to check in every 5-10 mins and give it a good stir.

Once the pan approaches a boil, the grits will thicken considerably and start to plop and spit a little. Turn the heat way down to low and let it tick over, stirring now and then to make sure nothing is sticking or scorching. If things start to get a bit too thick, you can add a splash of water to loosen it up.

While the grits are cooking, get started on the shrimp. Add the pancetta to a pan and set over a medium heat. Render until crispy then remove from the pan, leaving the fat behind. Cut the garlic cloves and spring onions into thin slices and the red pepper into a small dice.
Toss half of the cajun seasoning into a bowl with the flour and add the prawns. Toss to coat.

Add the butter to the pan and once melted, add the prawns to the hot pancetta fat and butter and colour on both sides until brown and crispy. Add the garlic, red peppers and spring onion whites. Cook for 1-2 mins before adding the remaining cajun seasoning and a splash of water (or stock if you prefer). Bring to a boil, season and remove from the heat.

Back to the grits. Once the corn grits have had 45 mins or so in the pan, finish it by whisking in the butter. This is the moment to adjust the texture of your grits to your liking. I like the texture to be just holding its shape, so it will gently relax into the bowl. If it’s too thick, add a little water, too thin, keep cooking! Season to taste and then divide between warm bowls.
Spoon the prawns over the hot grits and finish with the spring onion greens.

name: Sichuan Aubergines
description: A whole roasted aubergine is a beautiful thing. Add a sticky Sichuan pepper sauce, creamy tahini and crispy peanuts and you’ve got yourself an absolute banger.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/180°C fan.
Pierce the aubergines all over with a small knife and rub with vegetable oil. Bake in a roasting tin, turning occasionally, for 1 hour, or until completely softened.
Meanwhile, toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan over medium heat until nice and fragrant, around 1 min. Transfer to a mortar and pound with a pestle until ground.

Mince the garlic and finely chop the ginger. Place them in a bowl with the ground Sichuan peppercorns, light soy sauce, garlic chilli paste, sugar, rice wine vinegar, and the water. Mix the corn flour with a couple of tablespoons of water and add to the sauce.

Whisk the tahini and toasted sesame oil until smooth then add the water and whisk again until smooth. It will split and look like it won’t emulsify but trust the process! After a couple of minutes, it will come together in a thick, creamy sauce. Season with salt and set aside.

Take the aubergines out of the oven. Place the sauce in a large wok and bring to a simmer over high heat. Add the whole aubergines and cook for 3 mins, turning often to coat the aubergine in the sauce.
Thinly slice the spring onions.

To serve, smooth the tahini sauce on the base of a serving dish. Place the aubergines on top, use a sharp knife to split them open slightly, and drizzle over the sauce. Top with a sprinkle of crispy onions, peanuts and spring onions.

name: Sichuan Chicken Sando
description: A crispy, shallow-fried chicken escalope dusted in Sichuan peppercorn and chilli powder, sandwiched between fresh ciabatta with a zingy coriander slaw to cut through the spice. Cut it in half and share it – or eat the whole thing yourself.
instructions: Finely ground the Sichuan peppercorns to a powder in a pestle and mortar (or use a pre-ground version). Add a large pinch of salt and the five spice then mix to combine.

To flatten the chicken, fold a large piece of greaseproof paper around the chicken breast then bash it with a mallet or rolling pin until it’s about 1-2cm thick. Generously sprinkle the spice mixture over both sides of the chicken.

Crack two eggs in a small bowl and vigorously beat with a fork for about 30 seconds then transfer to a plate. Get the flour and a pinch of salt on a separate plate and mix to combine. Pour the panko breadcrumbs onto a third plate.

Add the chicken to the plate of flour and flip to cover both sides, making sure every part of the breast is covered. Repeat with the beaten egg and then finally the breadcrumbs, pressing your fingers down onto the chicken to make sure they’re really stuck on.

Fill a large frying pan with vegetable oil so it’s about 1cm deep. Heat the oil over a medium-high heat for 2-3 mins then gently place the breaded chicken into the oil. Cook for 2-3 mins per side, basting the chicken with the hot oil as you go to make it extra crispy. When it’s golden brown, remove to a plate and dust both sides with the chilli powder.
Discard the oil from the pan and set the pan back over a medium heat. Slice the ciabatta in half and toast it in the pan, cut-side down, for 1-2 mins or until golden brown. Remove to a plate.
Thinly slice the red onion and cucumber and roughly chop the coriander. Add them to a bowl with the juice of the lime and a pinch of salt then mix to combine.
Mix the chilli oil and mayonnaise together in a small bowl.

To assemble the sandwich, generously spread the chilli mayonnaise over the bottom slice of ciabatta. Place the fried chicken on top followed by the American cheese and the coriander slaw. Top with the ciabatta and enjoy.

name: Sichuan Chilli Oil
description: This is one of the easiest chilli oils you’ll ever make. There’s no chopping, no fuss, just chuck all your ingredients into a bowl and pour hot oil on top.
instructions: Put the red pepper flakes, chilli flakes, sesame seeds and MSG into a heatproof bowl.
Toast off the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan until fragrant, then crush in a spice grinder or pestle and mortar and add to the bowl.
Heat your oil to 180°C and carefully pour over the dry spices.
Leave to infuse for 10-20 mins.
Use straight away or pour into a sterilised jar and refrigerate. This will keep for up to 2 weeks in the fridge.

name: Sichuan Pepper & Cumin-Spiced Lamb & Mushroom Lasagne
description: If you like things like mapo tofu and biang biang noodles, and you like lasagnes, then we reckon you’ll love this.
keywords: Sichuan Pepper & Cumin-Spiced Lamb & Mushroom Lasagne
instructions: Put the dried mushrooms in a jug or other heat proof container. Pour over just-boiled water, cover with a plate and leave to rehydrate for 20 mins or more. Get a bit of your prep out of the way by peeling and finely grating the ginger, finely slicing the spring onions, and mincing the garlic.

Pour a glug of oil into a large casserole, high-sided frying pan or wok set over a high heat. Add the lamb and fry for around 8 mins, stirring only occasionally, so that it colours and crisps a little.

Meanwhile, separately grind the cumin and Sichuan peppercorns to coarse powders using a pestle and mortar. Add to the lamb, along with the garlic, ginger, and spring onions. Reduce the heat to medium, cook for 2 mins, then stir in the chilli bean paste and caster sugar. Add the rehydrated mushrooms and the stock from the jug, and bring to a gentle simmer.

While the lamb is cooking, use a food processor to finely chop the button mushrooms (do this in batches). Add the remaining oil to a separate large frying pan, set over a medium-high heat. Put the chopped mushrooms into this and sauté the mushrooms for 8-10 mins, so they reduce in volume, moisture cooks away and they darken. Add the shaoxing wine and soy sauce. Let these bubble and absorb into the mushrooms, then sir the mushrooms into the lamb ragù.

Par-boil the pasta sheets. To do this, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and prepare a large mixing bowl, adding the sesame oil and chilli oil into the base of this. Cook half the pasta sheets for 3 mins, until they’re floppy. Pick them out with tongs or a slotted spoon and transfer to the bowl, tossing in the oil so that they are slick and slippery. Repeat, adding the remaining sheets to the bowl and gently mixing so that all the pasta is glossy (add more oil and chilli oil if you think it’s needed).
Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Whizz up the tofu in a food processor so that it’s a silky purée.

Assemble the lasagne. Put a ladleful of mostly liquid from the ragù into the base of the dish. Cover with a layer of pasta sheets, then one quarter of the ragu, and one quarter of the tofu, dotted over the top of the ragù in splodges. Repeat, alternating oil-slicked pasta sheets, ragu and tofu, until you have five layers of pasta. Finish by smudging the top layer of pasta with any remaining smears of ragu and tofu, and spoon any oils from the pasta bowl over the top. Cover with foil. Bake for 20 mins, then remove the foil and cook for 15-20 mins more until the top is blistered, crisp and a little brown. If you’re a fan, you could spoon a little more oil over the top.
Leave to rest for 15 mins, then serve.

name: Sichuan Pickled Plums
description: Sweet, spicy, and dangerously addictive, these pickled plums from MOB contributor Ben Lippett are the perfect accoutrement to any meal.
instructions: Halve and pit your plums.
Add all the ingredients to a saucepan and bring to a simmer.
Cook for 5-6 minutes until the plums are just starting to soften.
Remove the plums from the liquid and add them to a clean jar. Reduce the pickling liquid by a third, pour over the plums and seal the jar.

name: Sichuan Ragù
description: This twist on a classic bolognese sauce combines pork mince with Sichuan flavours and crispy chilli oil. A bold and comforting dish that’s a little spicy, a little smoky and full of umami richness.
instructions: Chop the onion, celery and carrot and crush the garlic cloves. Grind the Sichuan peppercorns in a pestle and mortar. Dice the pancetta.

Fry the pancetta in a large pan over a medium heat until crispy then remove and set aside. Add the onion, celery, carrot, garlic and bay leaf to the same pan with the pancetta fat and cook on a low-medium heat for 7 mins until starting to soften.
Add the pork mince, the ground Sichuan peppercorn and ½ the crispy chilli oil then fry on a medium-high heat for 5 mins until the pork is nicely browned and caramelised.
Turn the heat down to low-medium heat then add the pancetta and red wine to the pan. Cook for about 10 mins until the wine has evaporated.

Add the tomato purée and cook off until the mix starts to darken, then add the stock, tinned tomatoes, oyster sauce, soy sauce, cinnamon, white pepper and your bay leaf. Give it a good mix and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Turn the heat down to low and cook for at least an hour until the pork is tender, adding the milk 30 mins before the end and a splash of water if it’s drying out. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring a pot of salted water to boil. Cook your linguine until al dente then drain and reserve a few ladles of the pasta cooking water.
Add your cooked linguine to your bolognese along with a ladle of the water. Mix well to combine, adding more pasta water if it needs to bring it together.
To serve, divide the Sichuan ragu linguine between bowls, grate over your Parmesan and drizzle over the remaining chilli oil.

name: Silken Tofu & Smacked Cucumber Salad
description: Cold, creamy tofu topped with crunchy smashed cucumber, crispy onions, and a punchy soy-chilli dressing.
keywords: silken tofu and smacked cucumber salad
instructions: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil and gently lower in the eggs. Boil for 8 mins, then transfer to a bowl of cold water to cool. Once cool enough to handle, peel and halve.

Halve the cucumber lengthways, then smack it with a rolling pin to break it up. Roughly chop into bite-sized chunks and pop into a colander over a bowl. Sprinkle with a little salt and leave to drain for 10 mins. Pat dry with kitchen paper.
Grate the garlic into a small bowl. Add the soy sauce, rice vinegar (start with 4 tbsp, add more if needed), chilli oil (if using), sesame oil and white pepper. Whisk to combine and set aside.
Carefully remove the silken tofu from the pack, gently pat dry with kitchen paper and pop into bowls or on plates. Slice the tofu from top to bottom, not going all the way through.
Finely slice the spring onions and pick the coriander.
Toss the cucumber with the soy dressing, then spoon over and around the tofu. Top with the crispy onions, sesame seeds, coriander, spring onions and halved eggs.

name: Silky Bacon & Tomato Spaghetti
description: This uses the techniques of a carbonara to make the glossiest pasta. Loaded up with sharp, sweet cherry tomatoes and smoky bacon, this makes a delightful speedy dinner.
instructions: Bring a large pan of water up to a boil. Salt it generously.
Halve your cherry tomatoes. Chop your bacon into 2cm slices.
Get your spaghetti into your boiling water and cook until al dente, about 8 mins.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Add your bacon and fry for about 5 mins until the fat has rendered out and it’s started to crisp up. Remove from the pan with a slotted spoon, saving the fat in the pan.
Get your tomatoes into the bacon fat pan and turn down the heat. Fry them for a couple of mins until they start to break down, squishing them up with the back of your spoon.
Separate three of your egg yolks into a bowl, then crack in the other whole egg. You can save your whites for another time.
Grate your Parmesan into your egg yolks, then grate in a generous amount of black pepper. Beat the mixture until it is smooth.

Turn the heat off on your tomato pan. Once your pasta is cooked, tong it into the pan. Add your cheesy egg mixture and a ladle of pasta water, then give it a really good mix until you have a super glossy sauce.
Tear in your fresh basil, then tong your pasta onto plates and serve.

name: Silky Eggs & Crispy Mushrooms
description: Inspired by Japanese chawanmushi, the eggs are steamed in the microwave until set, silky and custardy. Topped with pan-fried crispy mushrooms, chilli crisp and spring onions. Eaten with rice for a gentle and quick dinner.
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl. Whisk together with the dashi or stock, soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Place a strainer over another bowl and strain the egg mixture through – this will ensure silky eggs.
Wash the empty bowl, then add the cornflour with salt, pepper and cold water, whisk together.
Trim the mushrooms and tear into thinner bunches or strips, add into the cornflour mixture and toss to coat, set aside. Thinly slice the spring onion.

Pour the eggs into a large enough microwave safe bowl, remove any foamy bits, cover with cling film or a large plate and place in the microwave. Cook the eggs on 500W for 5-8 mins. After 5 mins, the custard should start setting, cook in bursts of 30 secs until ready.
Meanwhile, place a frying pan onto medium high heat with enough oil to coat the bottom of the pan. Once hot, add the mushrooms and cook until golden and crispy on both sides, 3-4 mins.
Drizzle the silky eggs with some chilli crisp, the soy sauce and scatter with the crispy mushrooms and spring onions.

name: Silky Pepper Pasta
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Chargrilled peppers add a lovely bit of sweetness to this easy Italian-ish pasta recipe.
instructions: Place a pot of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, cook the pasta for 1 min under al dente.

Drain and add ¾ the peppers to a blender and blend until smooth add to bowl and finely grate in the cheese. Separate the eggs, discarding the whites and add the yolks into the bowl and whisk together.
Thinly slice the remaining peppers.

Once the pasta is cooked, drain, reserving water. Pour the pepper mixture onto the hot pasta. Place onto low heat whilst tossing together. Add a splash of pasta water if it gets too thick. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Stir the remaining peppers through.
Share into bowls and finish with basil leaves and some more Parm.

name: Silky Spicy Prawn Scissor-Cut Noodles
description: Homemade chewy noodles tossed through the silkiest spicy prawn sauce. It’s the perfect date night, dinner party or treat-yourself type of food.
instructions: For the noodles: Add the flour, water and salt into a food processor or large bowl and blitz or stir together until a cohesive dough forms. Add 1 tbsp of water at a time if the dough is too dry. Place into a bowl, cover and let rest for 20-25 mins.
Meanwhile, remove the heads and shell from the prawns. Devein the prawns (optional) then set aside. Peel and thinly slice the garlic. Trim and thinly slice the spring onion.

Heat a generous glug of oil in a saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the prawn heads and shells and cook, stirring, for 4-5 mins until pink and fragrant. Add the garlic, spring onion whites and ⅔ of the gochujang then fry for one minute until the onion has softened. Pour in the water, making sure to scrape the bottom of the pan. Bring the mixture to a boil then turn the heat down to medium and leave it to simmer for 15-20 mins to infuse the flavours.

When the sauce cooking time is up, sieve out the solids then get the sauce back over a medium-high heat. Leave the sauce to bubble away until reduced by half. Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to the boil.

To cook the noodles: Coat a clean pair of kitchen scissors with some oil. Snip 1cm-thick pieces of the dough into the boiling water and cook until they have floated up to the surface, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. Drain the cooked noodles and reserve some noodle cooking water (see ingredients list for quantity).

Add the raw prawns into the sauce with the remaining gochujang, noodles and most of the reserved noodle water, stirring until the prawns are cooked and the sauce is silky, glossy and coats the noodles. Add a splash more noodle water if necessary. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lime juice.
Share the noodles and prawns into bowls and top with spring onions. Serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Simple Orzo Minestrone
description: Minestrone comes in countless different regional variations depending on where you are and who is cooking.
instructions: Dice the onion, carrot and stick of celery.
Put a large saucepan on a medium heat and add 3 tbsp of olive oil.
Add the diced vegetables and cook gently for at least 10 mins until soft and fragrant but not brown.
Mince the garlic and add along the rosemary and tomato purée. Fry for another 3 to 4 mins
Add the stock and bring to a gentle simmer.
Meanwhile, cook the orzo in well-salted water until very al dente. Drain and add to the soup, simmer for a couple of minutes. Taste for seasoning.
Pour into bowls and top with chopped parsley, black pepper and the cheese, if you like.

name: Singapore Curry Noodles with Prawns & Fluffy Eggs
description: These easy singapore curry noodles are the right level of spicy with plenty of plump prawns. It's the perfect noodle recipe.
instructions: Pat all the prawns dry with kitchen paper and leave on a plate in the fridge.

Soak rice noodles in a bowl of boiling hot water for 2-3 mins, just until bendy and not cooked. Drain, then place into a bowl and pour over all the curry powder and mix well until evenly coated, use a pair of scissors and make just 4 random cuts into the noodles, then set aside.
Combine all the noodle sauce ingredients into a small bowl.
Thinly slice the garlic, then slice the carrots, red bell pepper and onion. Cut the spring onions into chunks.
Beat the eggs in a small bowl with a good pinch of salt.

Get a large pan or wok on a high heat and add 2 tbsp of vegetable oil. Let the oil get hot for a minute, then pour in the eggs. Allow the eggs to puff for 1 min then use a spatula to create big folds, layering the egg on top of each other to build big fluffy pieces of egg. Remove and set aside.

Add another tbsp of oil, allow the pan to get hot and add the prawns for 1 minute, then add the onions and garlic onions and and cook for 2 mins. Then toss in all the vegetables, the fluffy egg, add the noodles, noodle sauce and a good drizzle of sesame oil. Toss everything well for 2 mins, coating every noodle (this is why you cut them with scissors!). Season to taste with more fish sauce and soy if needed.

Squeeze the lime and toss for another minute, the noodles should be lovely and bouncy, taste for salt and turn the heat off as you don't want to over cook it. Finish with a drizzle of sesame oil and your fresh coriander.

name: Singapore Noodles
description: Contrary to what its name suggests, this is actually a Cantonese classic. We’ve omitted prawns and pork to make a non-traditional vegan version of that dish.
instructions: Boil your kettle. Pop your rice vermicelli in a large bowl whilst it boils.
Prep your veg. Finely slice your onion, red pepper, carrot, mangetout and spring onions into thin strips. Crush your garlic.
Pour your boiling water over your noodles and leave to sit for 1 min. Drain in a colander and leave to dry for 15 mins, tossing occasionally to stop the noodles from sticking together.
Mix your soy sauce and Shaoxing rice wine up in a bowl and place it next to your hob.
Heat a wok over a high heat. Add a glug of your vegetable oil, then tip your onion into the wok. Fry for 2 mins before tipping in your red pepper, carrot and mangetout. Fry for 3 mins until softened.

Tip in your curry powder, chilli powder and garlic then cook for 1 min. Tip your noodles into the wok and stir fry for a couple of mins longer. Add the soy sauce mixture, your spring onions and a pinch of salt and mix to combine.
Give one last season to taste, then serve up and enjoy.

name: Six-Ingredient Cauliflower Orzo
description: This hearty, healthy dish is a full meal in one pot which uses just six ingredients. Creamy, zesty, easy and super satisfying.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Peel the leaves from the cauliflower and remove the very tough spines, keeping any smaller leaves intact.

Break the cauliflower down into medium-sized pieces and drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place the cauliflower florets and in a large, deep baking tray or cast iron pan with a lid (or you can use a deep tray and cover with foil). Wrap your garlic in foil and nestle in between the cauliflower. Roast the cauliflower (uncovered) for 30-40 mins at 220°C until starting to brown, tossing halfway.
While the cauliflower is cooking roast the leaves on a small baking tray for 6-8 mins or until crispy and set aside.
Meanwhile, zest and juice half the lemons and set aside. Then slice the remaining lemon into 0.5cm rounds, and add on top of the cauliflower for its final 10 mins.
Cook the orzo in vegetable stock per packet instructions. Drain and set aside. Meanwhile roughly chop the parsley.

Once the cauliflower is ready, remove the lemon slices. Squeeze out the garlic cloves directly into the dish, add the lemon zest, juice, chopped parsley. Drain, then add cannellini beans along with the orzo. If using, also stir through the vegan cream. Give it all a good mix and season with salt and pepper, and top with the crispy leaves and the roasted lemon slices.

name: Six-Ingredient Squash Tacos
description: We used a whole squash to make charred slices with a crunchy seed topping and crispy skins. Pair it with citrussy courgette ribbons for the ultimate bite.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Peel the squash, cut it in half and deseed. Keep the skin and seeds in separate bowls.

Slice the squash halves into about 1cm half moons. Place in a large bowl and drizzle with 2-3 tbsp of olive oil and 1-3 tbsp of harissa, depending on how spicy you would like them to be. Season with salt and pepper and mix well to make sure all of the slices are evenly coated.

Lay the squash slices out on a large lined baking tray and bake for 15 mins, then take them out and flip them and bake for another 10 mins until golden. You can also griddle them to get nice char lines on them or broil them very quickly.

Shave the courgettes into ribbons with a speed peeler (or regular peeler) and place in a bowl. Squeeze two limes into the bowl with a sprinkle of salt. Toss the courgette your hands to evenly coat and set aside to marinate. Lots of liquid will come out of the courgettes so you may want to drain them before putting them in the tacos so that they don’t make the tacos soggy.
Pan fry the seeds with a little drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper for about 6-8 mins on medium heat until they are crispy and start to pop. Stir them often to make sure they don’t burn.
To make crispy squash skins, drizzle the skins in a little olive oil, salt and pepper and roast for 10 mins on the lower shelf.
To make the harissa yoghurt, pour out about half of the tub into a bowl and add a tsp of harissa to it. Gently fold through to make nice swirls.
Gently char the tortillas on a hot griddle pan or frying pan for a minute or two each side, until starting to brown and crisp up.
To assemble, spoon a layer of yogurt onto the tortillas, then layer the squash, courgette, seeds and crumble over the crispy skins. Finish with plenty of lime zest and enjoy.

name: Sizzle Butter Chicken Naan
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Turn store-bought naan into a meal to remember with this quick and satisfying weeknight dinner.
instructions: Chop the chicken into even-sized chunks. Chop the coriander stalks (set the leaves aside for later) and zest the lime. Finely dice the chilli.

Grate the garlic and ginger into a large bowl, then add the yoghurt, coriander stalks and lime zest. Mix well, then tip in the chicken. Stir to coat, then cover the bowl and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hrs (or ideally overnight).

Heat the oven to 220°C. Thread the marinated chicken onto skewers, then transfer to a baking tray. Cook in the oven for 15 mins. If you want a bit more colour on them, slide the cooked chicken skewers under a hot grill until charred.
Meanwhile, shred the cabbage and finely slice the red pepper. Combine in a large bowl with the coriander leaves and lime juice to make a slaw. Season with salt and pepper, then set aside.
Toast the naan, then transfer to a serving plate and spread with the extra yoghurt. Top with the slaw and chicken pieces.

Put the butter into a small pan set over a medium heat with the finely diced chilli. Once melted, swirl the pan and wait until it starts to froth. Add the curry powder, keep swirling for a couple of seconds, then spoon over the chicken. Enjoy.

name: Sizzle Butter Salmon With Raita Rice
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

We've topped perfectly cooked salmon with sizzling curry butter here for a guaranteed good time. A quick, affordable midweek dinner.
keywords: Sizzle Butter Salmon With Raita Rice
instructions: Cook the rice according to packet instructions, then tip into a bowl and fluff up.
Finely mince the garlic and ginger. Whisk the garlic and ginger into the yoghurt and add in the juice of the lime. Mix and season well with salt and pepper.

Rub the salmon skin in a little oil, then season with a pinch of salt. Place the salmon in a cold non-stick pan, skin-side down. Place the pan over a medium heat and cook for 7 mins- don’t touch it! This is the trick to perfect crispy skin!

Meanwhile, roughly chop most of the herbs, saving a few for garnish, and toss through the rice. Cut the cucumber into 1cm chunks and toss into the rice, then add the yogurt dressing and toss well. Taste and add more lime juice if necessary. Spoon the raita rice into bowls and top with the salmon.
Add the butter to a small pan over a medium heat, once melted, whisk until it starts to froth up, then add the garam masala and curry powder and let bubble up.
Spoon the curry butter over the top of the salmon, it’ll sizzle as it hits it. Finish with the reserved herbs and the lime, cut into wedges, on the side.

name: Sizzling Fish
description: The easiest and best way of having fish on any given day. Quick, flavourful, light and balanced.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Finely grate the garlic and ginger. Place both into a bowl with the cod fillets. Season with salt and pepper, then toss together to evenly coat.
Place each fillet of fish onto a sheet of baking paper. Fold to enclose the fish inside. Set aside.

Place the Tenderstem on a baking sheet and drizzle with some oil, season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15 mins until, starting to char. When there are 10 mins left for the broccoli, push them to one side of the tray and place the fish parcels onto the same tray. Bake for 10 mins until the cod is opaque and cooked through.

Trim and quarter the spring onions widthways. Halve each portion of spring onion lengthways, then finely slice into long matchsticks. Add into a bowl and toss with the red pepper flakes and curry powder.
Share the cooked rice, Tenderstem and fish between bowls. Drizzle the fish with soy sauce and rice vinegar, and top with the spring onion mixture.
Pour the oil into a small saucepan set over a high heat. Once hot, immediately pour over the spring onions and serve.

name: Sizzling Sichuan Noodles
description: These hot oil noodles are crazy delicious, in large part due to the amazing flavour of Sichuan peppercorns. We hope you'll love these as much as we do!
instructions: Place the Sichuan peppercorns in mortar and pound with a pestle until ground. Transfer to a large heatproof bowl.
Mince the garlic and ginger. Add that minced mixture to the Sichuan peppercorns along with your dark soy sauce, rice vinegar and sugar.
Heat the vegetable oil to 170°C in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Carefully add the hot oil to the Sichuan peppercorn sauce and mix well to combine.
Cook the noodles in lightly salted water according to the package instructions.
Meanwhile, deseed and thinly slice the red chillies and finely chop or crush the peanuts.
Drain the noodles and add them to the sauce, along with the red chillies and peanuts.
Toss well to coat then plate up, tuck in and enjoy.

name: Sizzling Spring Onion Soup
description: The easiest spring onion noodle soup you can make in 10 minutes. You're going to love this weeknight dinner.
instructions: Set a pot of water over a medium-high heat and bring to the boil. Add the wontons and noodles, then cook following pack instructions.
Heat the broth in a pot over medium-high heat and bring to a boil, then turn the heat down and let it simmer.

Meanwhile, combine all the seasonings in one bowl. Mince the garlic and slice the spring onion greens. Divide the garlic, spring onions and coriander between two serving bowls, then add half of the seasoning mixture to each bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pot set over a medium-high heat for 2 mins (keep your eye on the oil and make sure no water touches it!), then pour the hot oil over your seasonings and mix well.
Add half the cooked noodles to each bowl, pour half the broth on top of each serving, then finish with the cooked wontons and a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Sizzling Spring Onion Tofu
description: Silken tofu topped with a chilli-spiked soy sauce, crispy spring onions, and spring onion oil. Hoping to convert some tofu haters with this one!
instructions: Thinly slice the spring onions on a deep diagonal.

Pour the vegetable oil in a frying pan and heat to 180°C. Fry the spring onions until evenly browned. Strain the oil into a bowl, leaving the spring onions to cool in the sieve. They will crisp up as they cool.

Roughly chop the garlic and ginger. Deseed and roughly chop the red chilli. Transfer to a mortar and pound with a pestle until a rough paste forms. Once the paste is suitably pounded, transfer it to a heatproof bowl.Add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and sugar and mix until the sugar is dissolved.

Place 60ml of the spring onion oil back into the frying pan. Heat the oil to 180°C. Then, carefully pour it into the sauce and stir to combine. (Cool the remaining oil then store it in a jar for future use. It will keep in the fridge for a month.)
Place the silken tofu blocks on a plate. Slice the tofu into 1-2cm slices. Reheat the rice according to package instructions, and pick the coriander leaves, discarding the stems.
Share the rice between plates and top with silken tofu. Spoon the sauce over and serve with some coriander leaves and sesame seeds.

name: Sliced Apple and Ginger Sour
description: This superb cocktail recipe does a great job at balancing sweet with sour.
instructions: Core and finely slice the apple into matchsticks, set aside for garnish. Finely chop the ginger and pop it into a heat proof bowl with the ginger shot.
Heat the syrup to a simmer and pour over the ginger. Let it steep until room temperature. Pass through a fine sieve and store in the fridge. The syrup will keep for up to a week.
Carefully separate the egg white from the yolk (you can use the yolk to make your own mayonnaise or dressing). Then juice the lemon (you'll need 35ml per serve).

Combine 15ml of the ginger syrup with the rum, 35ml of lemon juice and egg white in a cocktail shaker. Add one ice cube and dry shake for 10 secs. Now fill to the brim with ice and shake again for 15 secs.
Strain into a chilled sours glass and garnish with a lemon twist.

name: Slow Cooked Courgette Pasta
description: This is my version of Gabe's slow-cooked courgette pasta. It’s so easy to make but being patient when cooking your courgettes is the key. Sophie x
instructions: Finely slice your garlic. Chop your courgettes into ½ cm thick rounds.
Heat a large sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a generous glug of olive oil, then tip in your garlic. Cook for 1 min until fragrant.
Add all of your courgettes to the pan and give them a good mix so that they are all coated in the oil, and no garlic sticks to the base of the pan.
Cook over a very low heat for an hour and a half, stirring occasionally to prevent them from sticking. Don’t worry if your courgettes break down and lose their shape - this is the point!
Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil. Add your spaghetti and cook until al dente.
Grate your pecorino into a bowl, then add a ladle of pasta water. Mix to combine.
Roughly chop your mint.

Add your spaghetti to your courgettes, along with your mint, pecorino mix and another splash of pasta water. Give it a really good mix with tongs to combine. Zest in your lemon and add the juice, then season the whole mix to taste with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Tong onto plates, then top with a little more pecorino. Serve and enjoy!

name: Slow Cooked Spiced Chicken Rice Bowl
description: Perfectly pulled chicken and black beans on a bed of rice, paired with a lime crema, smashed avo pieces and a generous sprinkling of coriander. Delish.
instructions: Add the chicken thighs to a bowl and along with the zest and juice of 1 orange and 2 limes. Finely grate the garlic in and add a shot of oil, the chipotle and cumin. Season generously with salt and leave to marinade for 1 hour in the fridge.
Add two layers of foil to a clean bowl in a criss-cross pattern. Add the chicken thighs and half the marinade. Gather the ends up into a parcel and seal.

Add to the Russell Hobbs Satisfry Air & Grill and slow cook for 1 hour. Remove from the cooking basket and tip into a bowl. Shred the chicken with two forks, mix the cooking juices through the meat. Switch your Russell Hobbs Satisfry Air & Grill onto its 'air fry' setting and pop your chicken back into the Satisfry. Cook for 3-4 mins until the top is crispy and caramelised. Keep warm.

To make the crema, tip the sour cream and mayo into a bowl. Season with salt and add the zest of 2 limes. Mix to combine. Mash the avocados with half a diced onion, salt and the juice of ½ a lime. Finely slice the remaining half onion and the chilli.
Drain and rinse the black beans. Heat the rice according to the pack instructions.

Divide the rice and beans between four warm bowls. Top with pulled chicken, beans, lime crema and smashed avocado. Tear over coriander and serve with the sliced chilli and onion and orange and lime wedges.

name: Slow Cooker Chicken Shawarma
description: All the juicy shawarma vibes with barely any effort. Chuck it all in the slow cooker, come back to tender spiced chicken, fluffy couscous and creamy yoghurt.
instructions: Finely zest both lemons into a large bowl, then squeeze in the juice from one half. Add the yoghurt, shawarma spice blend, a big pinch of salt and black pepper, and mix to combine. Toss in the chicken thighs and coat well. You can cook this straight away, or leave to marinate in the fridge for 30 mins or even overnight if you like.
Peel the onion and cut into six wedges. Slice the peppers into 1cm strips. Add both to the insert of a slow cooker and drizzle with olive oil. Give it a quick mix.
Lay the chicken on top of the veg, then cover and cook on high for 3 hrs or low for 6 hrs, until the chicken is cooked and tender.
Stir in the couscous, then cover again and leave to sit for 5 mins so the couscous absorbs all the flavour.
Pick most of the coriander leaves and toss through the pot. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges.
To serve, spoon  into bowls and top with a spoonful of yoghurt, the rest of the coriander and a lemon wedge.

name: Slow Cooker Chicken Thigh Ragù
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Set it and forget — this recipe is incredibly easy to make, but the end result is extremely delicious. Tender chicken and rich tomato sauce, so moreish.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the onion and garlic. Remove basil leaves from stalks, reserving the stalks.

Drizzle 2 tbsp of oil into a frying pan and place over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the chicken to the pan, season with salt, and fry on each side until golden brown, it should take 3-4 mins. Add the finely sliced onions to the pan and cook until softened, around 3-5 mins, finally add the finely sliced garlic and cook for another min.

Tip the content of the pan into a slow cooker with passata, basil stalks and 50ml water, then cook on low for 2-3 hours until chicken is tender. (If you don’t have a slow cooker, bring the mixture to a boil, reduce the heat and simmer on medium-low for 1 hour, until the chicken is tender. Then, using a fork, pull the chicken apart.)
Stir the sauce until the chicken starts falling apart to create your ragù sauce, stirring the basil leaves through.
Bring a pan of salted water on to boil. Drop the pasta into the pan and cook for 1 min less than package instructions. Reserve 200ml of pasta water.
Stir the butter and pasta through the sauce, thinning it out with some pasta water if needed. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

name: Slow Roast Lamb Flatbreads
description: This is based on a dish Sophie Wyburd's mum always makes for parties with a load of salads. I'm doing mine with fresh flatbreads and hummus. Such a crowd-pleaser.
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C fan/140°C/280°F.
Halve your shallots, leaving their skins on. Bash your unpeeled garlic cloves to crush them slightly.

Heat a large roasting tin on the hob over a high heat and add your lamb shoulder fat side down, then salt generously. Brown for a couple of minutes until the fat has rendered a bit, then remove from the pan.

Tip your shallots, garlic cloves, cinnamon stick and coriander seeds into the same pan along with a generous pinch of salt and fry for 5 minutes in the lamb fat. Pop the lamb shoulder back into the pan fat side up and pour in your chicken stock.
Bring the stock to a simmer, then secure foil tightly around the edge of the tin. Pop your lamb in the oven. Cook for about 14 hours – I tend to do this overnight.
Now, make your flatbreads. Toast your coriander seeds in a dry frying pan, then crush them in a pestle and mortar.

Pop them in a bowl along with your flour, yeast, 2 tsp of salt, 2/3 of the olive oil and warm water. Give it a good mix until you have a rough dough, then turn it out onto your work surface and knead for 5 mins.
Pop your dough in a lightly oiled bowl covered in a tea towel and leave to rise until doubled in size – this will take about an hour.

Make your hummus. Drain your chickpeas, reserving the water from their can. Add them to a food processor along with the chickpea water, the tahini, lemon juice, za’atar and a good pinch of salt. Blend until smooth.
Pour the rest of the olive oil into the machine whilst it’s running until you have a smooth and emulsified hummus. Season to taste with salt.
Back to your flatbreads. Heat a cast-iron pan on a very high heat. Turn your dough out of the bowl and divide it into 8 equal-sized pieces. Roll each into a 2mm thick circle.
Pop one at a time into your hot, dry pan and cook for a minute on each side. They should bubble and get a slight char on them.
Remove your lamb from the oven and start to pull it with a pair of forks – this should be very easy to do as the lamb will be practically falling apart.
Roughly chop your mint.
Assembly time. Spread some hummus on your flatbread and top with lamb, mint, pomegranate and chillies. Serve and enjoy.

name: Slow Roast Lamb with Giant Couscous & Zhoug
description: A gently spiced, slow roasted shoulder of lamb with charred tomatoes, giant  couscous and zhoug. A perfect dish to share around a table with friends.
keywords: Slow Roast Lamb With Giant Couscous & Zhoug
instructions: Use a small knife to make little 2cm incisions all over the shoulder of lamb.

In a small bowl, mix the harissa with the sumac and 1 tbsp of fine salt and rub all over the shoulder of lamb. Leave to marinade for a couple of hours at room temperature, or overnight in the fridge (allow 2 hours to come to room temperature before cooking).

When you're ready to cook, preheat the oven to 150°C. Slice the onions into thick rounds about 2cm wide and place in a layer over the bottom of a large cast iron dish which is big enough to hold your lamb shoulder. Snuggle the whole garlic bulb in the side of the tray.
Place the lamb on top of the onions, cover with a sheet of baking parchment and then the lid.
Place into your oven for around 5 hours, check the lamb with a fork to make sure it’s very tender, if not re-cover and give it another 30 mins.
While the lamb cooks, make the zhoug. Chop up your chilli and add to a mini chopper along with the coriander, cardamom and cumin.
Squeeze in the juice of a lemon and add about 100ml of olive oil. Whizz until not quite smooth. Set aside in a bowl.

This is also a good time to char the tomatoes so they’re ready for later. Get a large frying pan very hot, add the tomatoes and cook for about 5 minutes until charred on both sides. Set aside in a bowl.
Once the lamb is tender, remove from the oven and allow to rest for 20 mins.
Remove the bulb of garlic and squeeze into the bowl with the tomatoes, add the onions that cooked under the lamb too.
Cook the giant couscous in a large pan of boiling water according to packet instructions. Drain, then while still hot add the tomatoes, garlic and onions.

Skim off most of the fat from the juices in the pan which the lamb cooked in and then add that to the couscous. Add a generous pinch of salt and half the juice of the second lemon, stir well, taste and add more salt and lemon as you like.
Pile the couscous into a serving dish, gently pull apart the lamb and lay over the top, then drizzle over the zhoug and serve.

name: Slow Roast Pork Belly Gyros
description: Possibly best gyros you'll ever eat. The crunchy crackling. The Za'atar. It's sublime. Absolutely sublime.
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C/338°F.
Place your pork belly on a baking tray. Score the skin diagonally in each direction to create diamond shapes on the skin.
Add 3 heaped tsp of za’atar, crushed garlic clove, a large pinch of salt, pepper and a glug of olive oil. Get your hands involved and mix everything together, rubbing the za’atar into the meat.
Make sure the pork is skin side up. Sprinkle some more salt on the skin and place in the oven for 1½-2hrs. Turn the heat down to 150°C if it's colouring too quickly.

Pickled onion time. Grab a bowl. Finely slice the red onions and chuck them in. Squeeze the juice of a lemon over the onions and add a good pinch of salt. Scrunch the lemon juice and salt into the onions. Place the bowl in the fridge for a couple of hours.

Tzatziki time. (Remember to squeeze the cucumber gratings to get rid of the excess water). Mix your yoghurt, a grated cucumber, lemon zest, the juice of one lemon, salt, pepper, olive oil and a large handful of chopped mint. Mix everything together and set aside.
Tomato time. Finely chop up your tomatoes and add to a bowl with a heaped teaspoon of za’atar, salt, pepper and olive oil. Mix everything together.
Just before you take out the pork, add a handful of chopped parsley to the onions and mix it in. This will ensure the parsley doesn’t get soggy.
After 2 and a half hours in the oven, the pork should be done. To make sure the skin is crackly, just leave the pork under the grill for 5 minutes, checking it regularly to make sure it doesn’t burn.
Remove the pork from the oven and carve it up into slices.

Assemble time. Take a warm pitta, and spoon in some tzatziki. Add a good spoon of the pickled onions. Add a generous helping of the pork, topped with tomatoes and a dollop more of the tzatziki, and serve! Enjoy!

name: Slow Roast Tomato & Egg Curry Rice
description: The flavours of an egg drop curry but presented in a different way. Roasted tomatoes, fragrant spices, and perfectly cooked eggs come together in this comforting and aromatic dish.
keywords: Slow Roast Tomato & Egg Curry Rice
Slow Roast Tomato & Egg Curry Rice recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan.
Toss the halved tomatoes with salt, garam masala, black pepper, and two-fifths of melted ghee or oil. Mix well and spread onto a baking tray.
Roast for 30-40 mins until soft and slightly caramelised.
Cook the rice according to package instructions.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining ghee in a pan over medium heat. Add the curry leaves, finely sliced garlic, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, and chopped chilli. Cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant, then remove from heat.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the eggs and cook for 7 mins for soft yolks. Drain and cool under cold water before peeling.
In a bowl, mix the finely sliced red onions with lime juice and a pinch of salt. Massage gently with your hands and set aside to pickle.
To serve, divide the rice into bowls. Top with roasted tomatoes, eggs, coriander, and pickled onions. Drizzle the spiced ghee and roasting juices over the dish.

name: Slow Roasted Creamy Courgette Pasta
description: Slow roasting your courgettes makes them become concentrated in flavour and have an incredibly creamy texture, making them the perfect base for sauce.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Pierce the courgettes all over with a fork and place on a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Slice the top off of the garlic bulb and drizzle with a little olive oil. Wrap it tightly in foil and place with the courgettes.
Bake for 35-55 mins, depending on the size of your courgettes. They should be super soft and starting to brown on the outside. If in doubt, cook them for longer.
Toast the hazelnuts for 3-5 mins until golden. Roughly chop and set aside.
Meanwhile, cook your pasta 1 minute less than package instructions. Drain, put back into the pot and drizzle with a little olive oil to prevent sticking.

When the courgettes are ready, halve them and scoop out the inside with a spoon into a bowl. Keep the skins to one side for now. Squeeze out the garlic into the bowl and add a good drizzle of olive oil, plenty of salt and pepper (more than you usually would, the courgettes need it!) and mash the garlic into the courgettes until everything is combined into a sauce. Tear the smoky courgette skins into small pieces and add it to the sauce.

Put the pasta pot on low heat and pour in the courgette sauce. Gently heat and toss to combine, adding a little more olive oil if you like. Add the vegan cream cheese here, if using. Once warm, add the zest and juice of one lemon and toss again. Taste for seasoning and adjust as you like.
Serve into bowls and finish with more lemon zest from the second lemon, more pepper, more lemon juice if you like and sprinkle over the chopped hazelnuts.

name: Slow Roasted Tomato, Garlic & Aubergine Pasta
description: Weeknight dinners don't get better than this. Slow-roasted tomatoes, garlic, and aubergine are a killer combination.
instructions: If you haven't yet cooked up a batch of roasted vegetables as part of your meal plan, then you can do this now.

Heat oven to 180°C. You will need multiple trays, and may have to do this in batches. Add all of the tomatoes into a large baking dish and drizzle with 4 tbsp of olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper. Dice the aubergines into 2cm pieces and add to the tray, drizzling with olive oil, salt and pepper. Remove the tops of the garlic bulbs and wrap individually in tin foil. Add them to the tray. Put everything in the oven and roast for 35-40 mins.

Cook the pasta, then drain, reserving some of the water. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan over a medium heat and add the capers, frying for 2 mins. Add the roasted cherry tomatoes and gently heat, squashing gently so that they burst slightly.
In the meantime, squeeze out the roasted garlic and smoosh up with the back of a knife. Add to the tomatoes and mix until combined. Stir through the roasted aubergine and simmer for 5 mins.

Roughly chop parsley and finely grate the Parmesan. Take the tomato sauce off the heat and add the pasta along with the parmesan, parsley, the juice of 1 lemon and a ladle full of pasta water. Mix really well until emulsified and smooth, then serve up topped with more parmesan, a drizzle of oil and more parsley, if you like.

name: Slow-Cooked Chicken with Cannellini Beans & Pea Salad
description: A sultry slow-cooked chicken served with creamy cannellini beans and a fresh green salad. The capers add a nice pop of brine.
keywords: Slow-Cooked Chicken with Cannellini Beans & Green Salad
Slow-Cooked Chicken with Cannellini Beans & Green Salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Season the chicken legs all over with salt. Peel and slice the shallots in half lengthways. Peel the skin of ⅔ of the lemons into strips with a peeler. Peel the garlic cloves but leave them whole.

Add the olive oil, shallots, capers, thyme, lemon peel, garlic and paprika to a high-sided baking tray that's just big enough to fit the chicken legs in. Give it a mix then add the chicken, turning once so it’s evenly coated in the oil.
Roast the chicken in the oven for 25 mins, then turn the heat down to 170°C and roast for 30 mins or until the chicken is golden starting to fall away from the bone.

Remove and set aside the chicken and thyme from the tray, leaving the cooking juices behind. Add the drained beans and water to the tray, then add the chicken back on top and roast for a further 15 mins.
Meanwhile, slice the sugar snaps in half lengthways. Cook the peas and sugar snaps in a pot of salted boiling water for 2 minutes until just cooked, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Pick the leaves from the herbs and add to a bowl with the veg then squeeze over the juice of half a lemon then season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the chicken and beans onto a platter before topping with the salad or serving alongside.

name: Slow-Cooked Lamb Pilau With Cucumber Raita
description: Have a little patience and you'll be sorely rewarded with this fall-apart lamb pilau. An ideal recipe for Ramadan or any time of the year.
keywords: Slow-Cooked Lamb Pilau With Cucumber Raita
instructions: To make the pilau, thinly slice the onions, garlic and ginger and fry off in a large casserole pot in ghee for 10 mins or until the onions are lightly brown.
Add the spices and keep cooking for 2 mins.
Use a kitchen towel to remove any excess moisture from the lamb before dicing into 5cm chunks and adding it to the pan. Fry the lamb with the onions until it's nicely browned on all sides.
Add 750ml of water and bring it to the boil. Simmer on a low heat for 45-60 mins or pressure cook for 14 mins, until the lamb has cooked through and is falling off the bone.

To make the crispy onions, thinly slice the onions using a sharp knife or mandoline. Arrange them in a single layer and sprinkle over cornflour. Heat up vegetable oil to 180°C and fry the onions till golden and crispy all over, this will take roughly 3-5 mins.
To make the pickled onions, thinly slice the red onions using a sharp knife or mandoline. Add to a bowl, add vinegar, 20ml boiling water, sugar and salt. Mix until the sugar and salt have dissolved.

To make the raita, add the yoghurt to a bowl. Coarsely grate in the cucumber, finely grate in the garlic and finely chop and add the green chilli. Season with salt and finish with finely chopped mint.
Once the pilau is cooked, there will be plenty of cooking liquid/stock in the pot, drain it into a measuring jug. As we are cooking 600g of rice, we need roughly 1500ml of stock.
Make up the difference with water, adding it back to the lamb and bringing it to the boil.
