Add the rice to a large bowl and rinse with cold water. Drain the rice and repeat the washing process until the water runs clear. This usually taking 3 rounds of washing.

Add the washed rice to the pot with the lamb and the stock. Bring to a boil and cook on high for 12 mins, then cover and reduce heat to the lowest for 10 mins. Take it off the heat but don’t remove the lid for another 10 mins. Remove the lid and fluff the rice with a fork.
Serve the steaming pilau with a bowl of the raita and the crispy and pickled onions.

name: Slow-Cooked Lamb Shoulder With Parmesan Butter Beans
description: Master the art of slow-cooking big hunks of meat using this one top tip. It involves a bit of everyday kitchen equipment you’ve all got kicking around.
keywords: Slow-cooked Lamb Shoulder With Parmesan Butter Beans
instructions: Heat the oven to 140°C fan. Put your largest frying pan over a high heat. Rub the lamb in a little oil and place, fat-side down in the pan, cook for 4-5 mins, checking regularly, until it’s browned on the big surface. Transfer to a large deep roasting tin.

Peel the onions, then halve them and cut them into wedges. Tip the onions into the large frying pan along with a little more olive oil and a big pinch of salt. Fry for 5 mins, until golden. Tip your onions into the roasting tin with the lamb. Add the fresh oregano, sage and rosemary. Cut the bulb of garlic in half horizontally and add it to the tray. Pour over the chicken stock and the white wine. Cover the tray with foil. This ensures your meat will steam and get extra tender. Cook for 3 ½ hours.

To make the salsa, finely chop the herbs and anchovies and add them to a bowl. Finely slice the spring onions and add along with the capers, mustard, olive oil, and white wine vinegar. Into a separate bowl, zest the lemon and set it aside for later, then squeeze the juice of the zested lemon into the salsa. Mix to combine, season well and set aside.

Drain the beans, then add a handful (approx 1/2 a tin or 1/3rd of a jar) into a blender and blitz, or add to a bowl and mash them as much as you can. Mix the blitzed beans with the rest of the drained beans in a bowl.
Remove the lamb from the oven and remove the foil, the lamb should be melting off the bone. Very gently lift the lamb out and place it onto a seperate baking tray. Turn the oven up to 180°C.
Drain the onions through a sieve into a large saucepan. Remove the woody stalks from the sieve and discard them. Tip the jammy onions back into the roasting tray along with the bowl of beans.

Use a spoon to skim the fat from the surface of the cooking liquid in the large saucepan, you want to remove as much of the clear fat that will be sitting on top of the brown cooking liquid, (add it to a bowl and save it for roasting potatoes) then add 150ml of the cooking liquid to the tray of beans, season well.
Add the lamb back on top of the beans back and whack everything into the oven and cook for another 30 mins, until the lamb is golden and crispy in places.
Meanwhile, put the saucepan with the rest of the cooking liquid over a high heat and bring to the boil, cook until it boils down to the consistency of a loose gravy. Taste and season to taste.
Whisk the crème frâiche with half of the Parmesan and half of the lemon zest. Season to taste with salt and pepper, and add more lemon zest if needed.

Remove the lamb and beans from the oven and set the grill to high. Set the lamb aside to rest. Add the crème frâiche mix into the beans, then grate the rest of the Parmesan over the top. Slide the beans under the grill and grill for 15 mins, until golden and bubbling.
To serve, spoon the reduced cooking liquor over the lamb, reserving some to serve. Serve with the cheesy beans and salsa.

name: Slow-Roasted Curried Coconut Chicken
description: This batch recipe is extremely hands-off and makes for the juiciest chicken, so tender it falls off the bone - and did we mention we've designed a great selection of meals to make your chicken go further!
instructions: Heat the oven to 150°C. Put the coconut milk and curry paste into a bowl and whisk together. Season with fish sauce and set aside. Peel and wedge the onions.
Gently bash the lemongrass to release its flavour. Stuff it into the chicken’s cavity along with the whole garlic bulb. Season the chicken all over with salt and pepper.

Transfer the onions to a baking tin, place the chicken on top and pour the coconut milk mixture all over. Once the oven is hot, roast the chicken for 2 hrs 30 mins–3 hrs until cooked through. Rest the bird for 20 mins before carving it, separating the breasts, wings, thighs and drumsticks.
Meanwhile, prick the raw tomatoes a few times using the tip of a knife, halving any large ones.

Add the carved chicken to a Tupperware container, add the onions and garlic bulb to another Tupperware container, and finally add the raw tomatoes to a third Tupperware container. Pour all of the pan juices over the tomatoes then set aside to marinate until ready to use. Don't skim off the fat; it's a combination of chicken fat and the separated coconut milk fat, and it holds loads of flavour!

name: Slow-Roasted Squash with Maple Bourbon Glaze
description: We’ve taken butternut squash to the next level with a sticky maple syrup and whiskey glaze. An incredible side dish.
keywords: slow-roasted squash with maple bourbon glaze
butternut squash with maple bourbon glaze
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C / 350°F. Peel and deseed the butternut squash and cut it into wedges.
Toss the squash wedges with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange on a baking sheet and roast for 25-30 mins until softened.
To make the glaze, set a small saucepan over a low-medium heat. Add the maple syrup, bourbon and cinnamon. Stir to combine and simmer until slightly thickened.
Brush the roasted squash with the maple bourbon glaze. Return to the oven and roast for an additional 10 mins. Meanwhile, toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry frying pan.
To serve, arrange the squash on a platter and sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds.

name: Smacked Cucumber Dumpling Salad
description: Two fantastic dishes meshed into one – it's a bowl full of dreamy smacked cucumber dumpling salad, the best dinner you could ever make yourself. A refreshing and spicy dish perfect for a quick side or light meal. Don’t forget to garnish with sesame seeds and fresh herbs like parsley or coriander (aka cilantro for any Americans out there) for added flavour and crunch – we’ve thrown in some fresh radishes here for some of that vegetable freshness. This salad combines the cool crispness of cucumbers with the savoury warmth of dumplings, making it an exciting addition to your recipe collection.
instructions: For the dressing: stir all the creamy tahini dressing ingredients together into a bowl, adding 1 tbsp of cold water at a time until the dressing goes creamy. Taste and season with more sugar or soy sauce, if needed.
For the salad: add the rice vinegar, soy sauce and sesame oil into a bowl.

Trim the cucumber. Cut it into quarters, widthways. Using a rolling pin or something heavy, smack the cucumber until it splits. Chop into roughly 2cm large chunks. Trim and thinly slice the radishes and spring onion. Add the cucumber, spring onion whites and radishes into the dressing and toss together, let marinate for 5-10 mins.
Meanwhile, pan-fry the dumplings according to package directions.

Spoon the tahini dressing onto a sharing plate. Toss the dumplings into the cucumber salad and spoon over the creamy dressing. Sprinkle over the remaining spring onions and drizzle over the chilli oil.

name: Smashed Beef & Onion Hummus Bowl
description: Crispy beef smash patties on a silky bed of hummus, topped with juicy tomatoes and punchy pickled jalapeños.
instructions: Pick the parsley leaves and finely slice the soft stems. Tip the beef mince, baharat, parsley stems and salt into a mixing bowl.
Very thinly slice or mandoline the onion, then stir it through the mince. Roughly portion the mixture into four balls — no need to shape them.
Chop the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks and place in a bowl with a pinch of salt. Let them sit to release their juices.

Drain the chickpeas, reserving a splash of their liquid. Tip the chickpeas, tahini and olive oil into a blender with some of the reserved liquid. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt and a splash of pickle brine to taste.Shortcut: Use good-quality ready-made hummus if you're short on time.
Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Get a sheet of baking paper and a heavy-bottomed pan ready.

Once hot, add a meatball to the pan. Cover with the baking paper and smash down with the heavy pan to flatten. Remove the paper and weight, then let it cook until golden and crusted. Flip and cook through on the other side. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the rest.
Toss the pickled jalapeños and olive oil through the tomatoes. Season with a splash of pickle brine. Toss through the parsley leaves just before serving.
Spoon the hummus onto plates and spread it out. Top with pieces of the smash patties and a big helping of the tomato-jalapeño salad.

name: Smashed Chicken & Curried Celery Remoulade
description: I recently had the most phenomenal vegetarian schnitzel at Holy Carrot - it was served with Café de Paris butter, and a celeriac remoulade with lots of dill. I took inspo from the flavours to create a quick and nourishing mid-week meal. It also sparked my new obsession with raisins - which I now love.
keywords: Smashed Chicken & Curried Celery Remoulade recipe
instructions: Start with the remoulade. Add the juice of the lemon into a blender with the mayonnaise, mustard, yoghurt and dill (stalks and all). Blend until smooth, then tip into a large bowl. Drain and roughly chop the capers, then stir them through. Taste and season with salt and black pepper. Add the raisins, then set aside.

Butterfly the chicken breasts so they're an even thickness. In a bowl, mix the curry powder with a good drizzle of olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper. Toss the chicken through until coated.
Thinly slice the celery. Pick the dill fronds and parsley leaves, thinly slicing any soft stems.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 5-7 mins, turning once, until golden on both sides and cooked through. You may need to do this in batches, transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm.

Heat the grains according to the packet instructions. Toss the celery, dill, parsley and grains through the remoulade. Slice the chicken. Divide the salad between boxes and top with the chicken. Leave to cool and pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Smashed Chicken & Curried Celery Remoulade
description: I recently had the most phenomenal vegetarian schnitzel at Holy Carrot - it was served with Café de Paris butter, and a celeriac remoulade with lots of dill. I took inspo from the flavours to create a quick and nourishing mid-week meal. It also sparked my new obsession with raisins - which I now love.
keywords: Smashed Chicken & Curried Celery Remoulade recipe
instructions: Start with the remoulade. Add the juice of the lemon into a blender with the mayonnaise, mustard, yoghurt and dill (stalks and all). Blend until smooth, then tip into a large bowl. Drain and roughly chop the capers, then stir them through. Taste and season with salt and black pepper. Add the raisins, then set aside.

Butterfly the chicken breasts so they're an even thickness. In a bowl, mix the curry powder with a good drizzle of olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper. Toss the chicken through until coated.
Thinly slice the celery. Pick the dill fronds and parsley leaves, thinly slicing any soft stems.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 5-7 mins, turning once, until golden on both sides and cooked through. You may need to do this in batches, transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm.

Heat the grains according to the packet instructions. Toss the celery, dill, parsley and grains through the remoulade. Slice the chicken. Divide the salad between plates or boxes and top with the chicken.

name: Smashed Chicken Tacos With Salsa Rossa
description: Juicy smashed chicken, charred tomato salsa, and a crunchy yoghurt slaw. These tacos are messy in the best way.
keywords: Smashed Chicken Tacos With Salsa Rossa
Smashed Chicken Tacos With Salsa Rossa recipe
instructions: To make the salsa rossa, halve the cherry tomatoes, peel and roughly chop half the onion, and smash one-third of the garlic. Chuck everything onto a tray with the chillies and grill for 6–8 mins until nicely charred.

Transfer to a blender with half of the coriander and the juice of half of the limes. Blitz until smooth — or leave it chunky if that’s more your vibe. You can also chop it all if you fancy something rustic.
Grate the remaining onion and add to a bowl with the chicken mince, cumin, oregano, garlic powder, salt and remaining garlic cloves. Mix well and divide into even-sized balls.
Finely shred the cabbage and mix in a bowl with the yoghurt, juice of half a lime, and a good pinch of salt. Stir through half of the remaining coriander.
Place a ball of chicken mince onto each tortilla and press to flatten into an even layer, right to the edges.

Heat a medium frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, spray lightly with oil. Lay in the tortillas, chicken side down, and cook for 4–6 mins until golden and crisp. Flip and toast the other side for 1–2 mins.
Serve the smash tacos with the slaw, a big spoonful of salsa rossa, the rest of the coriander, and extra lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Smashed Chicken Tacos with Pineapple Salsa
description: Indulgent and fresh. These crispy pan-fried tacos with a spicy pineapple salsa are seriously good, and they’re perfect for meal prep. Just fry them up when you’re ready to eat.
keywords: Smashed Chicken Tacos with Pineapple Salsa
Smashed Chicken Tacos with Pineapple Salsa recipe
instructions: Grate the onion into a large bowl. Add the chicken mince, grated mozzarella and spices. Season with salt and pepper and mix to combine.

Lay out the tortillas and divide the chicken mix between them. Use a fork to smash the chicken into the tortilla, making sure to go right to the edge. If making ahead, stack the tortillas up between sheets of greaseproof paper in a container and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or the freezer (covered in foil) for up to 3 months.

To make the salsa, dice the jalapeño, pineapple and red onion and chop the coriander. Mix together and season with lime juice, hot sauce and salt to taste. If making ahead, transfer to a container and store in the fridge for up to 3 days.

When ready to eat, finely shred the cabbage, slice the avocado and crumble the feta. Heat a medium sized non-stick frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add a little olive oil and place the taco, chicken side down, into the pan. Cook over a medium heat for 4-6 mins until nicely browned. Flip and crisp up the tortilla.
Plate up with the salsa, avocado, cabbage, feta and a wedge of lime. Douse in your favourite hot sauce, add a dollop of sour cream and enjoy!

name: Smashed Chicken with Piccalilli Salad
description: Piccalilli's the UK's take on Indian pickles - but milder, with a tang that makes your lips pucker. This salad takes that inspo and pairs it with chicken. Simple, full of veg, and you'll be back for more.
keywords: smashed chicken with piccalilli salad recipe
instructions: With a sharp knife carefully butterfly the chicken breasts and season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Meanwhile, cut the cauliflower into small, bite-sized florets, peel the carrots into ribbons, then trim and halve the green beans. Roughly chop the dill, finely slicing any soft stems.
Once the water is boiling, add the cauliflower and green beans and cook for 3-5 mins, until tender. Transfer to a bowl of ice water to cool.

Meanwhile, make the dressing: finely grate the ginger into a bowl, then stir through the turmeric, mustard and vinegar. Slowly whisk in the olive oil until emulsified and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 7-9 mins, turning once, until cooked through and golden.
Drain the veg and toss through the dressing with the carrot ribbons and chopped dill. Leave the chicken to cool, then divide between containers and top with the salad. Pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Smashed Chicken with Piccalilli Salad
description: Piccalilli's the UK's take on Indian pickles - but milder, with a tang that makes your lips pucker. This salad takes that inspo and pairs it with chicken. Simple, full of veg, and you'll be back for more.
keywords: smashed chicken with piccalilli salad recipe
instructions: With a sharp knife carefully butterfly the chicken breasts and season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Meanwhile, cut the cauliflower into small, bite-sized florets, peel the carrots into ribbons, then trim and halve the green beans. Roughly chop the dill, finely slicing any soft stems.
Once the water is boiling, add the cauliflower and green beans and cook for 3-5 mins, until tender. Transfer to a bowl of ice water to cool.

Meanwhile, make the dressing: finely grate the ginger into a bowl, then stir through the turmeric, mustard and vinegar. Slowly whisk in the olive oil until emulsified and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 7-9 mins, turning once, until cooked through and golden.
Drain the veg and toss through the dressing with the carrot ribbons and chopped dill. Divide the chicken between plates and top with the salad.

name: Smashed Courgette & Parmesan Pappardelle
description: Pasta. It's hard to find something more beloved than pasta. This smashed courgette and Parmesan pappardelle is a godsend.
instructions: Slice the courgettes as thinly as you can, pile them into a big cast iron pot or your biggest frying pan. Drizzle over a generous amount of olive oil and season generously with salt. Set over a medium heat stir the courgettes to coat in oil and salt.

Cook for 25 mins, stirring every now and then, until the courgettes are starting to collapse. Thinly slice the garlic and add to the pan. Cook for another 10 mins or so. Roughly chop the rocket and basil and stir through the sauce.
Cook the pappardelle according to the package instructions.
Add half the parm. Add the pasta to the sauce with a good splash of pasta water and toss together.
Add the juice and zest of the lemon and season with salt and pepper.
Divide between warm bowls and top with the remaining cheese.

name: Smashed Cucumber, Halloumi and Tahini Salad
description: A salty and spicy quick summer salad. This recipe is great for when you're after something fresh to brighten your lunch
instructions: Gently bash the cucumbers with a rolling pin until they break up into large pieces. Chop these up into bite-sized pieces then trim and thinly slice the spring onions.
Chop up the halloumi into 2cm chunks and pan-fry them with a glug of olive oil until golden brown and crispy, 3-5 mins.

In a large bowl, add in your tahini, soy sauce, rice vinegar and crispy chilli oil. Stir together and add 1 tbsp of cold water at a time until the dressing is smooth. Taste and season with salt, if needed.
Add the cucumbers, halloumi and spring onions to the dressing. Toss well and serve up in bowls with some more chilli oil, enjoy!

name: Smashed Herby Beans & Artichoke Sandwich
description: A hefty plant-based sandwich that will make everyone be extremely jealous of your lunch. This one's a keeper, Mob.
instructions: To being with, make your pesto. Using a pestle and mortar, bash the herbs, garlic, 25ml olive oil and ¼ tsp salt until combined. Add half of the pine nuts and bash again until just broken down but still chunky. You can also use a small food processor, just take care to pulse and not overblend into a puree. You want to keep lots of texture here. Otherwise you can also chop the herbs and nuts.
Drain and rinse the beans and add them to a large bowl. Add the pesto and nutritional yeast to the beans and mash with a fork, leaving some beans whole for a chunky mash.

If the artichoke hearts are very big, chop them into bite-sized pieces. Add the artichokes and the remaining pine nuts to beans and mix well. Add the juice of 1 lime, taste and see if you would like it tangier, I added the juice of two limes. The lime juice also helps to keep it fresh.
Taste and season well with salt and pepper. You might like to add some of the artichoke oil to the mix to make it more creamy.

To build your sandwich, spread the bean mix over the bottom generously, then add plenty of rocket on top. Season the rocket with a little salt and pepper and a quick drizzle of olive oil. Spread some vegan mayo, if using, over the top slice and close the sandwich.
This mix will keep well in the fridge for up to 3-4 days.

name: Smashed Merguez Beef Flatbreads
description: One of the sausages I miss the most since moving to the UK is a good merguez. So, I decided to spice up some mince with the flavours of the OG sausage to make a quick, comforting wrap that's just as good made ahead and eaten the next day.
instructions: Heat the grill to high. In a large bowl, add the mince, harissa and cumin seeds, grate in the garlic, season with salt and black pepper and mix together well.
Portion the mince into four and spread one portion onto each flatbread, pressing it right to the edges. Transfer to a baking tray and drizzle with a little olive oil. Set aside.
Drain and thinly slice the jarred peppers. Using a mandolin, thinly slice the onion and add to a bowl of ice water to get them extra crisp.
Add the peppers then zest the lemon over them. Squeeze half of the juice over too. Season with salt and a drizzle of olive oil.
Slide the flatbreads under the grill on the middle shelf for 5-7 mins, until the mince is fully cooked through. If it's catching too quickly, move the shelf further from the grill.

Drain the onions and toss with the peppers. Add a dollop of yoghurt to each flatbread, top with the pepper and onion salad and a few dill fronds, then roll up and serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges.
If prepping ahead, let the flatbreads cool a little before adding the toppings, rolling them up and wrapping in foil. Reheat before eating.

name: Smashed Pea Dip
description: This lemony, herby pea dip couldn’t be quicker or easier to make. It’s delicious as a snack with crackers, or even as a meal topped with grains and roasted vegetables.
instructions: To thaw the frozen peas, put them in a sieve and run them under some cold water.
Roughly chop the spring onion and tear the green chilli into pieces.
Add all the ingredients, including the juice of the lemon and a pinch of salt, to a blender and blitz.
Taste and add extra salt or lemon juice if needed.
Serve as a dip, topped with some pickled red onions, alongside our seedy crackers. Or top it with any roasted veggies, grains, nuts and seeds you like for a more substantial meal!

name: Smashed Prawn Tacos
description: We love prawns and we love tacos, so what could be better than smashed prawn tacos?
instructions: Preheat the grill to high. Add the prawns, chipotle, sundried tomatoes, cumin and fish sauce into a food processor. Blitz until the prawns break down into a paste.
Pick half the coriander leaves and mince the rest. Using a vegetable peeler, thinly shave the cabbage, toss with the juice of ½ a lime, then season with salt. Thinly slice the avocados.

Add the cherry tomatoes to a baking tray and place under the grill for 5-10 mins until they blister and char. Transfer to a bowl and mash whilst still hot. Let them cool down and season with salt and the juice of 1 lime. Before serving, fold the minced coriander through.

Divide the prawn filling between the tortillas (around 1 heaped tbsp each) and spread into one even layer, all the way to the edges. Place a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, cook the tacos, prawn-side down, for 2-3 mins until cooked through, then flip and cook the tortilla until charred in spots. Transfer to a plate and cover. Continue until all of them are cooked.
Top the tacos with cabbage, avocado, burnt tomato salsa and the remaining coriander. Serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Smashed Sausage & Kale Toastie
description: A quick, comforting grilled cheese with crispy Cumberland sausages, an autumnal kale pesto and (of course) lots of melted cheese.
instructions: Spread the sausages onto the inside of ½ your slices of bread. Grate or thinly slice the cheddar.

Place a frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, add the kale and cook until wilted. Transfer to a food processor with the smoked almonds, peeled garlic clove and olive oil. Blitz until broken down. Season with salt and pepper. Slather onto the remaining slices of bread.
Set the empty frying pan back over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Cook the slices of bread with the sausage, sausage side down, for 5-10 mins until golden brown and cooked through.
Flip the slices of bread and sprinkle over the grated cheese. Top with the other slices of bread (kale side inside) and drizzle with oil.
Reduce the heat to low-medium and cook the toasties for 3-4 mins on either side until golden brown.
Serve immediately whilst still hot.

name: Smashed Sausage Mojo Verde Tacos
description:
These simple smashed sausage tortillas are stacked with spiced pineapple and red peppers, and topped with a zingy mojo verde. Cook them for your mates and watch them disappear.

In Partnership With Aldi. #ad
instructions: Start by preparing the smashed sausage tortillas. Squeeze the sausage meat from the sausage casings and into a bowl. Discard the casings. Spread the sausage meat out on your tortillas so you have an even layer on each. Set aside.

Next, get started on the spiced pineapple and peppers. Use a sharp knife to trim away the pineapple skin then dice the fruit into 1cm chunks. Slice the jarred red peppers. Heat a dry frying pan over a high heat then add the pineapple chunks and cook until starting to char.

Add ⅓ of the olive oil to the pan with the pineapple and leave for 20 seconds until the oil is hot. Remove the pan from the heat. Stir through the curry powder and transfer the mixture to a separate bowl. Wash the frying pan.
Add the red peppers to the bowl with the pineapple. Season with salt, pepper and the juice of the lime, and mix to combine.

For the mojo verde, put ¾ of the coriander (stalks and all) into a blender along with the garlic clove, red wine vinegar, half the pickled jalapeños and ⅓ of the olive oil. Tip in the cumin seeds and water and blitz to a smooth green sauce, adding a splash more water if it needs loosening (you want a thick, drizzling consistency). Season to taste with salt, pepper and the sugar, if using. Set aside in the fridge.

Next, cook the smashed sausage tortillas. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the tortillas in batches, sausagemeat-side down, and cook for 3-5 mins until golden-brown. Flip them over and cook the other side for about 10 seconds until golden. Transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm. Continue until all the tortillas are cooked.

To serve, stack the smashed sausage tortillas with the spiced pineapple and peppers and top with a generous drizzle of mojo verde, a few rocket leaves and the remaining coriander leaves and pickled jalapeños.

name: Smashed Sausage Tacos with Feta Crumble
description: These smashed chorizo tacos are fresh, spicy and fruity and on the table in just 20 minutes. Made with Old El Paso’s new Street Vibes Al Pastor soft taco kit.
ingredients: 1 Old El Paso Street Vibes al Pastor Taco Kit
instructions: Squeeze the chorizo sausage meat out from the sausage casings into a bowl (use regular pork sausages if you prefer). Discard the casings. Divide the sausage mixture equally between the tortillas then spread the meat onto the tortillas so you have an even layer on each. Sprinkle ¾ of the seasoning packet onto the sausage side of the tortillas.

Heat the olive oil in a small saucepan set over a medium heat until it just reaches smoking point. Meanwhile, thinly slice the cabbage and avocado. Toss the cabbage with some salt and lime juice. Thinly slice the spring onion and mince the coriander. Add both to a bowl with the sesame seeds, crumbled feta and remaining seasoning packet. Pour the smoking hot oil over and toss together.

Place a frying pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the tortillas in batches, sausage meat side down, and cook for 3-5 mins until golden-brown. Flip and cook the tortilla side for a couple of seconds until golden. Transfer to a plate and cover. Continue until all the tortillas are cooked.
Serve the tacos with the cabbage slaw and some sliced avocado. Add as much fruity salsa as you want and any remaining feta or lime wedges.

name: Smashed Szechuan Chicken
description: This is my take on Sichuan's famous bang bang chicken, a deliciously spicy dish that delivers a real punch. The szechuan chicken is tender and juicy, coated in a flavourful, fiery sauce made with classic Szechuan peppercorns for that iconic numbing heat. The dish is balanced with a rich combination of garlic, soy sauce, and chili oil, offering layers of flavor with every bite. Serve it warm with a bowl of steamed rice to absorb the mouth-numbing chicken juices, and you’ve got a simple, but bold meal. Perfect for those craving a taste of authentic Chinese cuisine.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to boil and poach your chicken for 10-15 mins on a gentle simmer until cooked through. Reserve the water.
Julienne your ginger and shred your cabbage.
Remove your chicken from the water and place your chicken onto a chopping board, smash it with a rolling pin to shred it up.

Heat up the soy sauce, balsamic vinegar, chilli oil, Sichuan peppercorns, and 500ml of the chicken poaching liquid. Grate in your garlic and add in your ginger. Heat until it's bubbling and slightly reduced for about 3 mins.
Place your chicken and cabbage into the liquid and mix gently.
Transfer onto your serving plate along with the juices and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and chilli powder.
Serve with rice and eat this with a spoon so you get that lovely juice at the bottom!

name: Smoked Aubergine & ‘Nduja Lasagne
description: This right here will be the most epic lasagne you've ever made. Layers of 'nduja and aubergine ragù, topped with a cheesy béchamel and sprinkled with Parm.
instructions: Place your aubergines directly over the naked flame of your hob. Cook them for 5 mins, turning them frequently so that they soften and char evenly. Remove them with heatproof tongs, and place them on a plate to cool slightly.
Finely dice your onion. Finely chop your garlic.

Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat, and add a glug of olive oil. Tip in your onion, and cook for 15 mins until softened. Whilst it cooks, peel the charred skin off your aubergines, and shred the soft flesh.
Add your chopped garlic and ‘nduja, then cook for 2 mins more. Tip in your cherry tomatoes and aubergine, then simmer for 15 mins to thicken the sauce slightly.
Finely chop your parsley, then add this to the sauce, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Heat your oven to 200°C.
Whilst your ragù simmers, make the white sauce. Melt your butter in a medium-sized saucepan over a medium heat. Once foaming, add your flour and mix to a paste. Cook for 2 mins.

Gradually pour in your milk in small increments, beating all the while to ensure that you have a smooth mixture before adding more milk. Once all the milk is added, bring the mixture to a boil and allow it to thicken. Grate in all of your Pecorino, and 3/5 of your Parmesan, then tear in your mozzarella ball, and whisk to combine. Season to taste with salt.

Pour a little of your white sauce into the base of a 30 x 20cm baking dish. Arrange your lasagne sheets neatly on top, snapping sheets where necessary to plug the gaps. Pour over ¼ of your remaining ragù followed by ¼ of your remaining white sauce, then more lasagne sheets. Continue like this until you are out of all your mixtures.

Mix the top layer so that the ragù and white sauce combine, pushing it all the way to the edges so the lasagne sheets are totally covered. Sprinkle the surface with your remaining Parmesan, then bake for 30 mins.
Let your lasagne stand for 5 mins before serving. Enjoy!

name: Smoked Aubergine Milanese
description: Crunchy, creamy, smoky aubergine nugget with tomato sauce – an amazing vegetarian take on a milanese (or katsu) to enjoy over steaming hot rice or spaghetti.
instructions: Char the aubergines on a gas hob or under the grill. As the aubergines begin to cook, the skin will start to blacken. Once the skin is completely charred and black, remove the aubergines and place them into a bowl and cover. As they cool, the skin will loosen, allowing you to peel the charred skin easily from the aubergine. Season with salt.

For the sauce, pour the peeled tomatoes into an empty saucepan and crush to break the tomatoes down. Grate the garlic in, add a drizzle of oil and cook on medium-high heat for 6-10 mins, stirring occasionally until thickened. Season with sugar, salt and MSG.
Meanwhile, peel the aubergines. Using a fork, flatten each one down until it's around 2cm thick. Season with salt.

Crack the eggs onto a plate, pour the vinegar and season with salt, whisk together. Add the flour and breadcrumbs onto two separate plates. Coat the aubergines in flour, then eggs and lastly breadcrumbs.
Pour enough oil to coat the bottom of a frying pan with 1cm of oil. Turn the heat up to medium-high. Once hot, fry the aubergine on both sides until golden brown. Season with salt and pepper.
Zest half the lime. Re-heat the sauce and sprinkle the aubergine with lime zest. Serve with some tomato sauce and rice.

name: Smoked Fish Finger Sandwiches with Dill & Mustard Mayo
description: Smoked fish works brilliantly with pickled ingredients, so I’m riffing here on a classic fish finger sandwich. I’ve also made a mayonnaise using Dijon mustard and lots of chopped dill, plus a big spoonful of soured cream for extra acidity. Enjoy.
keywords: smoked fish finger sandwich with mayo
instructions: To make the mayo, separate the egg (reserve the white) and blend the egg yolk, mustard, garlic, a pinch of salt and black pepper and vinegar in a food processor for 30 seconds. Alternatively, do this by hand with a bowl and a whisk (crush the garlic first, though).

Slowly add one-third of the olive oil in a very thin drizzle while blending or whisking vigorously, then add the remaining oil in a thin stream while mixing to make a nice, thick mayonnaise. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Finely chop the dill, then mix it through the mayonnaise along with the soured cream. Set aside.
Cut the fish into equal-sized pieces, season with pepper and dust in the flour.
Beat the egg white in a bowl with the cold water, then add the fish, draining any excess, before coating in the breadcrumbs. Brush off any excess and set aside.
Pour the oil into a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Cook the fish fingers for around 3 mins on each side until they have turned golden brown, have a good crust and are cooked through.
Transfer to a plate lined with dry kitchen paper to soak up excess fat. Wipe clean the pan with kitchen paper.
Add the butter to the pan, then stir in the sauerkraut and stir-fry for 3-5 mins over a high heat until piping hot and beginning to colour.
Slice the gherkins and split the rolls.
To serve, add the fish fingers to the rolls with the sauerkraut, mayonnaise and gherkins.

name: Smoked Mackerel Kedgeree
description: Fish for brunch? Feels weird but trust us, once you’ve tried this classic combo you won’t look back. It is the kind of food you want when you are run-down.
instructions:
Pour the boiling water into a saucepan over a medium heat. Add
the eggs and set a timer for 6 ½ mins (for soft-boiled).
Meanwhile, get a large frying pan over a high heat and drizzle in a
decent amount of oil. Peel the red onion, then coarsely grate the
onion and the ginger directly into the pan. Add the curry powder
and cook, stirring, for 1 min.
Squeeze the unopened rice pouches with your hands to separate
the grains a bit, then open and tip into the pan along with a
decent splash of boiling water. Add the frozen peas, stir and cook
for a minute to defrost the peas.
Peel the skin off the mackerel and flake into the pan. Turn the heat
down low, season with salt and pepper and leave to heat through.
Drain the eggs, place in a sieve and run under cold water until
cool enough to handle. Peel the eggs and cut in half. Cut the
lemon into four wedges. Top the kedgeree in the pan with the
egg halves, lemon wedges and torn coriander. Serve straight from
the pan into bowls.

name: Smoked Mackerel Salad with Lime & Ginger Dressing
description: When you want food with zing, this is exactly it. Smoky flaked mackerel, charred spring onions and bright blitzed dressing tossed through warm grains and sweet peas. Hearty, fresh and gets better as it sits.
instructions: Place a frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Trim the ends of the spring onions and once the oil's hot, add the whole spring onions and cook for 6-10 mins, turning occasionally, until softened and starting to char.
Meanwhile, juice the two limes into a blender, add the remaining dressing ingredients and blitz until smooth.

Once charred, transfer the spring onions to a chopping board. Add the frozen pea medley to the empty pan with a splash of water, cover and leave to defrost for 4-5 mins, then drain. Tip the grains into the pan and toss through the peas until piping hot.

Roughly chop the spring onions. Flake the mackerel, discarding the skin. Pick the mint leaves. Add the grains and peas to a large bowl with the spring onions and mint, pour over the dressing and toss everything together. Season with salt and pepper.
Share between plates or pack into boxes and serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Smoked Mackerel, Mint & Cucumber Chopped Salad
description: A fresh and flavourful chopped salad recipe that’s packed with plenty of healthy fats thanks to the addition of smoked mackerel.
instructions: Cook your quinoa according to package instructions and allow it to cool.
Add your frozen peas to a microwave-safe bowl and microwave for 2 mins on high. Once cooked, allow them to cool.
Add your cucumber, mackerel, and mint (reserving some of the mint for garnish later) to a chopping board and chop them up into rough chunks.
Add your chopped ingredients all to a bowl and throw in your cooked quinoa and peas.
Make a quick dressing by combining the olive oil, mustard, honey and juice of the lemons. Mix until emulsified and season with salt to taste.
And the dressing to the bowl and toss it vigorously. Garnish with some torn mint and salt. Serve and enjoy.

name: Smoked Oat Fishcakes
description: These fresh smoked haddock fish cakes are packed with crunchy spring onions and Quaker Oats. Serve with a bright beetroot dip for the perfect spring meal.
instructions: Peel and chop your potatoes, then pop them in a pan of cold water and bring them to a boil. Simmer for 15 mins until tender.

Bring the milk to a simmer in a small saucepan. Poach your haddock for 5 mins in the milk before removing it entirely, reserving 50ml of the poaching liquid. Peel away the skin from the fish and shred it into flakes using two forks.
Roughly chop the spring onions and parsley.

Put the potatoes into a bowl and mash them up. Add in the fish, spring onions, parsley, a squeeze of lemon, mustard, 50g of jumbo oats and 50ml of your poaching liquid. Season generously with salt and pepper and shape the mixture into 8 patties.
Blend up the remaining 100g of Quaker Jumbo Oats and pop into a bowl.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl.
Dip the patties in the egg and then the oats and fry until golden brown for 2 mins on either side.
Blend the crème fraîche and beetroot with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Serve the fish cakes with the beetroot dip and leafy greens.

name: Smoked Rosemary & Rum Old Fashioned
description: This is a fun take on a traditional Old Fashioned where we’ve used rum instead of bourbon and maple syrup in place of simple syrup. Yum.
instructions: Peel your orange for garnish.
Using a lighter, burn your rosemary sprig until it's smoking a little, then upend your chosen glass and let the smoky flavour take hold.
When you think it's smoky enough, put your glass right way up again and pour in your maple syrup and Angostura bitters.
Add a large ice cube and the orange peel.
Stir for 2-5 minutes to allow the ice to melt, chilling the rum and letting the flavours mellow.
Add in your rosemary sprig and enjoy.

name: Smoked Salmon & Egg Cottage Cheese Pot
description: Creamy cottage cheese layered with smoky salmon, spinach and a soft-boiled egg. A protein-packed pot that's ready to grab straight from the fridge, perfect for an on the go breakfast.
keywords: Smoked Salmon & Egg Cottage Cheese Pot
Smoked Salmon & Egg Cottage Cheese Pot recipe
instructions: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the egg and cook for 7 mins for a large egg (6-6.5 mins for medium, 5-6 mins for small), then transfer immediately to a bowl of cold water. Once cool enough to handle, peel and halve.

Roughly chop the chives and add to small bowl with the cottage cheese. Season well with salt and black pepper and stir everything together. Spoon the mixture into the base of a wide-mouth jar or container. Add a loose layer of spinach, then lay the smoked salmon over the top.
Place the egg halves on top of your pots and scatter over the dill. Tuck the lemon wedge into the side. Seal and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Squeeze over the lemon just before eating.

name: Smoked Salmon Blinis
description: An absolute classic, these blinis are light and very moreish. Leaving the batter to ferment gives them their characteristic texture and flavour, so don’t skip it. Serve these canapés DIY for people at your next dinner party to help themselves or as impressive snacks when having people over. If you make this smoked salmon blini recipe in advance, cover then reheat in a low oven for 5 mins to refresh them slightly before serving. It’s the ultimate appetiser.
instructions: Very gently warm milk in a jug in the microwave in 10 second bursts or in a small saucepan set over a low heat until lukewarm. Pour into a large bowl. Sieve in the plain flour, add the fast action dried yeast and whisk together to make a smooth paste. Cover with a clean tea towel and leave to ferment for 1 hr.

After 1 hr very finely chop most of the chives and separate the egg. Add the yolk to the fermented flour paste (putting the white into a medium clean bowl), along with the finely chopped chives and remaining milk. Sieve in the remaining plain flour and add a big pinch of salt. Whisk briefly to combine.

Clean the whisk you are using then whisk the egg whites until they are white, fluffy and holding their shape. Working in batches, use a metal spoon to fold the egg whites into the blini batter in a figure of eight motion, trying to keep as much air as possible in the batter itself. Once all the egg whites are incorporated, re-cover with the tea towel and leave for 30 mins for the batter to get super bubbly.

Meanwhile, mix the crème fraîche with the horseradish, the zest and juice of half the lemon and season with salt and lots of black pepper, to taste. Cut the remaining half lemon into small wedges to serve. Cut the smoked salmon into long thin strips, then use your fingers to curl the strips into little rosettes to go on top of each blini.
Melt a quarter of the butter in a large non-stick frying pan set over a medium heat and use a piece of kitchen paper to spread the butter across the entire pan.

Spoon heaped teaspoons of the blini mixture into the pan, leaving enough space between each one to allow for spreading. Cook for a minute or so, until the sides are set and the top is super bubbly, then flip and continue cooking for a further minute on the second side. The blinis should be light, fluffy and nicely golden.
Continue cooking all the blinis, top with the horseradish crème fraîche and smoked salmon, then snip over the remaining chives and serve with the lemon wedges for squeezing. Enjoy.

name: Smoked Tofu Spicy Noodle Salad
description: Spicy noodle salad packed with spring veggies and finished with smoked tofu- a perfect quick and well-rounded meal.
instructions: Bring a pan of salted water to a boil. Chop the tofu into 1cm cubes.

Finely slice the garlic. Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil into a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the garlic and Thai red curry paste and sizzle for a minute. Remove from the heat and transfer into a large bowl. Add the juice of 1 ½ of the lemons and 2 tbsp more olive oil- whisk well to create the dressing. Taste and season with salt, if needed. Wipe out the frying pan.
Trim and slice the green beans into 3-5 cm pieces. Cut the top 5cm tips off the asparagus, then finely slice the stems.

Once the water is boiling, add the noodles and green beans and asparagus tips cook for 5 mins. Drain and rinse with cold water until no longer hot, then tip into the dressing. Trim the courgette, using a vegetable peeler, peel the courgette into long ribbons, add them into the bowl along with the asparagus stems. Roughly chop most of the coriander and add to the bowl, season generously and mix together.
Heat the now-empty frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the smoked tofu. Cook the tofu until golden on its sides, 4-5 mins.
Toss the tofu into the noodle salad and share onto plates. Scatter with the remaining coriander leaves. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve on the side.

name: Smoky & Cheesy Black Bean Quesadillas
description: A great veggie take on the Quesadilla. The sweet bursts from the corn make this dish. Great for the Dinner-Party MOB.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Finely chop the peppers and onion. Place in a frying pan on a medium heat. Once softened, add the smoked paprika. Allow to soften further for another 5 minutes.

Wrap two corn on the cob in tin foil. Place on a baking tray and place in oven for 20 minutes, turning half way through. When ready, remove from oven and slice off the sweetcorn and set aside in a bowl.
Add your black beans to the pan. Add salt, pepper and a handful of chopped coriander. Mash everything together and remove from heat.

Salsa time. Scoop out the flesh of your avocados into a bowl. Add the finely chopped tomatoes, a handful of coriander, the juice of a lime and season with salt, pepper and olive oil. Mash everything together and put in the fridge.

Quesadilla time. Heat a frying pan. Drizzle in some olive oil. Place a white tortilla wrap on the pan. Scatter some cheddar over it. Spoon some black bean mix on top. Scatter over some sweetcorn. Scatter more cheddar on top, and cover with another wrap.
Cook for 4 minutes, and then flip it. The wraps should be golden, and the cheese should be melted. When they are, remove from the heat and slice into quarters.
Serve the quesadillas with the cold salsa! Enjoy!

name: Smoky Aubergine & Red Pepper Chilli
description: Grilling the vegetables – plus the addition of some dark chocolate and a spoonful of chipotle paste – is the secret to adding that extra oomph to this chilli.
instructions: Preheat your grill to high.

Slice the aubergine, pepper and 1½ red onions into medium-sized chunks. Spread out onto your largest baking tray. Drizzle liberally with olive oil and add some salt and black pepper to season. Cook under the hot grill for 15 mins, tossing the veg every 5 mins, until collapsed and blackened in places.

Meanwhile finely chop all the garlic cloves. Scrape two-thirds into a small bowl to be used later. Get a large saucepan over a medium heat and drizzle in a little oil. Add the remaining garlic, fry for 30 seconds and then spoon in the cumin and oregano. Cook for 30 seconds more. Add the chipotle paste and tip in the chopped tomatoes.

Drain the kidney beans and add to the pan. Refill one of the cans halfway with water. Pour that in too. Bring to the boil and season with salt and black pepper. Add the grilled veg and the chocolate to the pan. Give everything a good mix then leave the chilli to simmer away for 20 mins.
Turn the oven to 200°C.

Thinly slice the remaining onion half and scrape into a small bowl. Cut your lime in half and squeeze in the juice. Season and scrunch with your hands as this will help the onion quick-pickle. Set aside.

Finely chop most of the coriander and add to the bowl of chopped garlic. Pour in 4 tbsp of olive oil. Slice the baguette on a diagonal, lay the bread onto a baking tray and spoon over the garlic oil. Bake in the oven for 10 mins until crisp and golden.

name: Smoky Aubergine & Tomato Dip
description: We've taken two classics — Baba Ganoush and Persian Mirza Ghasemi — and made this delicious aubergine dip loaded with tomatoes, eggs and a drizzle of spicy oil.
instructions: Preheat the Ninja Smoker to 180ºC.
Lightly oil your aubergines and prick them all over using a fork. Place the aubergines and garlic bulb in the Ninja Smoker and cook until both are completely soft — 1 hour 10 mins.
Place a strainer over a bowl and grate the tomatoes into the strainer, season the tomato pulp with salt and set aside.
Meanwhile, soft boil the eggs. Bring a saucepan of water to the boil and gently drop the eggs in, cook for 6 mins. Then drain and place the eggs in a bowl of ice water.

Clean and reuse the saucepan. Add 6-8 tbsp of olive oil and the tomato purée, and place on a medium-high heat. Once hot, cook and stir until the tomato paste darkens, 2-3 mins. Then, add the cumin and fennel seeds. Cook and stir until the spices have toasted, 2 mins. Remove from the heat and stir the turmeric and pul biber through, set aside.
Halve the datterini tomatoes and season with salt and pepper, set aside.

Once the aubergines are soft, scoop the inside of the aubergines and place into a bowl. Remove the garlic cloves from their skins and add to the aubergine. Using a fork, mash them into a rough pulp. Add the grated and drained tomato pulp to the bowl with the tahini, and 3 tbsp of olive oil. Stir together, season with salt and pepper. If it needs to be loosened, add a few spoons of tomato water.

Serve the dip onto a plate or multiple plates, top with some datterini tomatoes, soft boiled eggs and drizzle over the spiced oil. Finish with a scattering of mint leaves and scoop with warm flatbreads.

name: Smoky Aubergine with Pistachio Ricotta
description: Use the Weber Crafted Roasting Basket to get the aubergines soft and smoky. Top with creamy pistachio ricotta and crunchy breadcrumbs for a veggie BBQ staple.
keywords: Smoky aubergine with pistachio ricotta recipe
instructions: Heat your barbecue on a high heat.
Put your aubergines into your Weber Crafted Roasting Basket, and drizzle with olive oil. Place on the barbecue and close the lid. Cook for 40 mins.
Fill a small saucepan with water, then pop in your pistachios. Simmer for 5 mins, then leave to cool.
Finely slice your red chillies. Roughly chop your mint.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Add your chillies, and fry for a couple of mins until the oil is slightly tinged red. Add your breadcrumbs, and fry for a few mins until crisp.
Allow your breadcrumbs to cool. Mix through the zest of a lemon, your chopped mint and a good pinch of salt.
Once your pistachios are cool, add your pistachios to a food processor along with your ricotta, lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Whizz to a smooth sauce.
Cut your aubergine open down the centre. Spoon in your pistachio whipped ricotta, then sprinkle with some grated pecorino and your breadcrumbs. Serve!

name: Smoky Bacon Beans on Fried Bread
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A twist on a british comfort classic – beans on toast made with a different flavour profile. A quick and easy meal made with mostly pantry ingredients.
keywords: Smoky Bacon Beans on Fried Bread
Smoky Bacon Beans on Fried Bread recipe
instructions: Thinly slice ½ the onions then toss with the vinegar, a pinch of sugar and a little salt. Set aside. Mince the garlic and finely dice the remaining onion.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the lardons with a drizzle of olive oil and cook until golden brown and crispy. Transfer to a plate, leaving the fat in the pan. Pour the olive oil (the full quantity listed in the ingredients list) into the pan and fry the bread in batches until golden on both sides. Transfer the fried bread to serving plates.

Add the diced onion and garlic to the pan and stir-fry for 6-8 mins until soft. Stir in the smoked paprika and bay leaf, then return the lardons to the pan. Pour in the black beans with their liquid and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 4-5 mins until thickened. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Spoon the beans over the fried bread and top with the pickled onions and a splash of the pickle juice.

name: Smoky Bacon and Radicchio Spaghetti
description: A simple pasta that uses minimal ingredients for maximum effect. Caramelised radicchio pairs beautifully with smoky bacon and Napolina Spaghetti.
keywords: smoked bacon and radicchio spaghetti recipes
instructions: Finely chop your red onion. Finely slice your radicchio and your streaky bacon.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with a little olive oil. Get your streaky bacon in the pan and fry for 5 mins until the fat has rendered and the bacon is starting to crisp up.

Add your onion and cook for 15 mins until softened. Tip in your radicchio and cook for 5 mins more until everything is lovely and caramelised. Tip in your wine and allow it to bubble down and reduce a little.
Get a large pan of water on to boil. Salt generously, then add your Napolina Spaghetti and cook according to packet instructions.

Lift the spaghetti out of the water and into the bacon pan. Add a little pasta water and mix until your sauce has emulsified a little and the pasta looks glossy. Add more pasta water until you get the desired consistency, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Tong your pasta onto plates, then finish with a sprinkle of parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve and enjoy.

name: Smoky Chicken & Chorizo Bowl with Aioli
description: This is really delicious and can be made really easily using leftovers from our Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo batch recipe. Enjoy!
instructions: Make the Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo.

Reheat the leftover Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo, until piping hot. You can do this using a tray inside the air fryer, or in the oven or microwave. Using the air fryer will make the chicken skin the crispiest again!
Drain and slice the peppers. Add the mayo to a bowl and grate in the peeled garlic, squeeze in the lemon juice and season with salt and black pepper. Serve alongside the salad.

name: Smoky Chicken & Chorizo Chickpea Stew
description: Here's another tasty recipe that you can make with your batch-cooked Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo. It's a stunner.
keywords: chicken and chorizo air fryer recipe
instructions: Make the Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo.

Add the leftovers from your Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo batch to a saucepan (minus the chicken) along with the canned tomatoes and the jar of chickpeas (including the liquid). Simmer until piping hot. Add the chicken to the air fryer and heat until piping hot and the skin is crispy, then remove and chop.
Mix the spinach through the base until wilted. Serve in bowls and top with the chicken, yoghurt and parsley.

name: Smoky Chicken & Chorizo with Herby Rice
description: Leftovers from our Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo batch recipe piled over a bed of warm herby rice. Proper comfort, ready in no time.
keywords: Smoky Chicken & Chorizo with Herby Rice
Smoky Chicken & Chorizo with Herby Rice recipe
instructions: Make the Air Fryer Smoky Chicken & Chorizo.
Finely chop the parsley and dill.
Peel the chicken skin off and place it into the air fryer at 190°C for 5-10 mins until crispy.
Meanwhile, warm the leftover chicken and chorizo mix in a saucepan set over a low heat with a lid on, until piping hot. Add a splash of water if it’s thickened in the fridge.
Reheat the rice, then stir through the minced herbs with a drizzle of olive oil.
Divide the herby rice between bowls and top with the smoky chicken and chorizo. Finish with a crack of black pepper, the crispy chicken skin and an extra drizzle of olive oil, if you like.

name: Smoky Chicken Bulgur Bowl
description: A beautiful bulgur bowl packed with charred chicken and a fistful of delicious herbs and spices.
keywords: Smoky Chicken with Bulgur Bowl recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Thinly slice the parsley stems and set aside. Reserve the leaves for later.

Combine the pul biber, half the tomato purée, the juice of a lemon, thinly sliced parsley stems, and half the yoghurt in a large bowl. Add the chicken, mix well so that it’s all coated, then transfer the marinated chicken to a greased baking tray. Roast for 15-25 mins until cooked through, then remove.
Switch the grill to high and grill the chicken until starting to char. Flip and continue cooking until the chicken is charred in places on both sides.

Meanwhile, pour the water and olive oil into a saucepan. Add the remaining tomato purée and two-thirds of the pomegranate molasses, season with salt and bring the mixture to a boil. Once boiling, tip the bulgur wheat in, let it come back to the boil, then cover and turn the heat down to low. Cook for 10 mins until the bulgur has absorbed the water. Once absorbed, use a fork to fluff it up. Taste and season with the juice of a lemon and more salt, if needed.

Pick the mint leaves and thinly slice one-third of it. Transfer the sliced mint to a bowl along with the remaining yoghurt, the zest of half a lemon and a squeeze of juice. Mix well and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Toss the parsley leaves and remaining mint leaves with the pomegranate seeds and a drizzle of olive oil. Before serving, add the remaining pomegranate molasses and toss.
Divide the bulgur between serving plates. Top with the chicken skewers and pomegranate salad. Finish with a drizzle of minty yoghurt.

name: Smoky Chicken Kofta Bowl
description: Smoky chicken koftas, a fresh tomato salad and silky hummus all wrapped up with flatbreads. A midweek winner that comes together in under 40 mins.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Crush the garlic and zest the lemon. Pick parsley leaves and set aside for later, then finely chop the parsley stalks and red chilli.

Grate half the onion into a large bowl and add the crushed garlic, lemon zest, parsley stalks, chilli and chicken mince, a touch of olive oil and salt and pepper. Mix for about 3 mins until it gets really sticky.
Wet your hands with cold water and shape the mix into 12 koftas. Lay them onto a lined baking sheet and chill in the fridge until ready to cook.
Finely slice the remaining onion and add to a bowl of iced water - this will make it less sharp.

Chop the tomatoes into rough pieces and finely slice the courgette. Drain the onions into a small bowl and add the parsley leaves, tossing everything together with a drizzle of olive oil and the juice from half the lemon. Season with salt.

Make the spice blend by mixing the smoked paprika, brown sugar and cumin. Sprinkle half the mix over the chicken koftas giving them a gentle roll to coat the sides. Take the other half of the spice mix and whisk with a good drizzle olive oil, seasoning with salt.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Fry the koftas for about 5 mins, turning until seared and golden all over (do this in batches if needed). Transfer to a lined baking tray, drizzle with the remaining spiced oil mixture and roast for 6 mins until cooked through.
Spoon the hummus into bowls, top with the salad and koftas, then finish with a drizzle of the smoky sweet juices from the tray. Serve with flatbreads and dig in.

name: Smoky Chipotle Chilli
description: The trick to bags of flavour in this chilli is blackening the onion and garlic for the chipotle sauce. It adds a smoky depth which complements the chipotle. Ideal for batch cooking, you could even double the quantities of this chipotle chilli con carne and then keep portions in the freezer - ideal for when you need an instant Mexican-inspired meal to hand. If you enjoy cooking with spice, you’re going to really get a kick out of the flavours in this simple chilli.
instructions: Peel the onion. Cut in half then finely chop one of the halves, leaving the other whole. Peel the garlic cloves, leaving them whole. Finely chop the red pepper and set it aside along with the chopped onion.

Get a large saucepan, or casserole pan that you’ll cook the chilli in, set over a high heat. Once visibly hot, add the halved onion and whole garlic cloves to the dry frying pan. Cook for 3-5 mins, flipping halfway through, until both are becoming nicely charred, then remove the pan from the heat.

Put the charred garlic and onion into a blender. Add the cumin seeds to the pan and let them toast in the residual heat for a minute or so, tossing them so they don’t burn, then tip them into the blender. Add the chipotle paste, plum tomatoes, tomato purée and dried oregano then blitz until it becomes a smooth sauce. This is the base for your chilli.

Set the pan back over a high heat. Tip in the mince along with 1 Tbsp olive oil. Season, then fry for 5-8 mins, breaking the mince up with the back of your spoon until evenly crisp and browned. Remove with a slotted spoon into a bowl.
Turn the heat down to medium, add the chopped onion and pepper along with 1 Tbsp olive oil. Cook, stirring occasionally until soft, around 8-10 mins.

Add the mince back to the pan, then pour in the chipotle sauce along with the kidney beans and all of their water, then half fill the can with water and add that into the pan, too. Add the dark chocolate, if using.

Simmer the chilli, stirring occasionally, for 30 mins until the sauce has thickened and is clinging to the meat, then season to taste. Serve with all your favourite accompaniments: rice, coriander, sour cream, smashed avo, lime wedges, tortilla chips, grated cheddar, if you like. Enjoy.

name: Smoky Chipotle Chunky Squash Soup
description: A delicious vegan soup recipe that'll warm you up from the inside-out. It's got a lovely smoky depth and gets a nice hit of creamy protein from the beans.
keywords: Smoky Chipotle Chunky Squash Soup recipe
instructions: Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic. Peel the squash and remove the seeds. (See notes for how to use these up). Chop the squash into small cubes. Remove the stems from the cavolo nero and chop into bite-sized pieces.

Heat a medium-sized pot and add a good drizzle of olive oil, then add the onion and cook on a medium-low heat for 5-7 mins until softened. Add the garlic, squash, cavolo nero, and chipotle chilli flakes. Stir and cook for about 5-8 mins until fragrant and the squash is starting to soften.
Drain the beans and add them to the pot. Add the vegetable stock and smoked paprika.
Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to a gentle simmer and cook for about 20 mins, uncovered until the squash and beans are tender.
Meanwhile, toast the pumpkin seeds in the oven, air fryer or in a dry saucepan for a few minutes, until crispy.
Stir the soup and lighty crush some of the squash and beans to make the soup creamier. Taste the soup and season with salt and pepper.
To serve, ladle the soup into bowls and grate over some vegan Parmesan-style cheese, if using, crush on the pumpkin seeds and add a final drizzle of olive oil.

name: Smoky Chipotle Tofu Mince
description: Smoky, deeply savoury and endlessly versatile, this chipotle tofu mince is your new batch-cook hero. Packed with black beans and white miso for a rich, umami depth that'll have you coming back for more.
instructions: Crumble the tofu into small mince-like pieces. Finely dice the onions, then mince the ginger and garlic.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the crumbled tofu and fry for 10-15 mins until lightly golden. Season generously with salt and pepper. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

Add the onion to the same pan, adding a little more oil if needed. Stir-fry for 5-7 mins until translucent, then add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1-2 mins until no longer pungent. Add the cumin, chipotle paste and tomato paste and stir to coat. Tip in the black beans along with their liquid and the water. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and leave to gently simmer for 15-20 mins until slightly thickened. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Stir the tofu back through the pan. Dissolve the miso in a splash of water and stir it in. Cook for a couple of minutes until glossy. Taste and season with salt if needed.

name: Smoky Chorizo & Pepper Sauce
description: Rich, spicy chorizo is the star of this tomatoey pepper sauce. Bang it on pasta, rice, or straight-up toast. Big flavour. Minimal fuss.
instructions: Finely chop the red onions and thinly slice the garlic. Dice the chorizo. Slice the roasted peppers into strips, about 1–2cm wide. Finely chop the parsley.

Heat a large saucepan over a medium-high heat with a good glug of olive oil. Add the chorizo and cook for 3–4 mins until starting to crisp and release its oil. Add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook for 4–5 mins until softened. Drop in the sliced garlic and cook for 1 more min.
Tip in the chopped tomatoes and the sliced peppers. Season with salt and a little black pepper. Simmer for 15–20 mins until thickened.
Stir through the parsley and taste, adjust the seasoning to your liking.

Ladle the sauce into a clean, heatproof jar and seal tightly. Let it cool completely. If sealed properly, it’ll keep in a cupboard for up to 1 month. If not, pop it in the fridge and use within 2 weeks. Or whack it in the freezer, it'll last for up to 3 months!

name: Smoky Chorizo Black Beans & Feta Fried Eggs
description: Our Smoky Chorizo & Pepper Sauce turns a simple tin of black beans into something deep, rich and properly satisfying. Topped with eggs fried into golden puddles of crispy feta and you’ve got a speedy midweek dinner that hits like a treat.
keywords: Smoky Chorizo Black Beans & Feta Fried Eggs recipe
Smoky Chorizo Black Beans & Feta Fried Eggs
ingredients: Third of Smoky Chorizo & Pepper Sauce
instructions: Before you begin, make the Smoky Chorizo & Pepper Sauce.
Drain the black beans and tip them into a small saucepan with the chorizo pepper sauce. Set over a medium heat and gently warm through, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile, pick the coriander leaves and set aside.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, scatter in the crumbled feta, then crack the eggs straight over the top. Let them cook until the whites are set and the feta is golden and crisp around the edges. Season with salt and black pepper.
Spoon the hot beans onto plates and top with the feta fried eggs. Finish with the coriander leaves and serve up.

name: Smoky Chorizo Cottage Pie
description: Say goodbye to boring cottage pies and hello to this next-level Spanish-inspired version, with a chorizo and beef filling and a creamy, cheesy mash potato top. A serious winter warmer.
instructions: Peel and finely dice your onion. Finely dice your peppers too, as well as your garlic and green chilli.

Heat a large casserole dish over a medium heat, and add 1 tbsp olive oil. Peel the skin off your cooking chorizo, and crumble the meat into the pan. Cook it for about 5 mins, breaking it up with your spoon to make a mince-like texture. It should crisp up a bit, and render out the fat.

Remove your chorizo from the pan with a slotted spoon, and add it to a large bowl. Add your onion to the chorizo fat. Cook it with a pinch of salt for 15 mins, until it has softened a bit, then tip in your diced red peppers. Cook these for another 10 mins.

Whilst your onion cooks, brown your beef mince. Heat a large frying pan over a high heat with a little oil, then add about half of your beef mince to the pan in small chunks. Season it with salt, and fry the beef for about a minute on each side, until it is deeply caramelised, but not cooked through. Add it to the chorizo bowl, and repeat with your remaining beef.
Add your garlic, hot smoked paprika, ground cumin, ground coriander and ¾ of the green chill into the pan, and cook them out for 2 mins.
Drain your black beans, then add these to the pan, as well as your chorizo and beef, chopped tomatoes and beef stock. Bring it up to a boil, then turn the pan down to a very gentle simmer.
Simmer your chilli for 2 hours, stirring it frequently to make sure it doesn’t stick.
When your chilli has 20 mins left, heat your oven to 190°C fan.
Make your mash. Peel your potatoes, and chop them into large chunks, and add them to a large saucepan.

Cover the potatoes with cold water, and season the water to taste with salt as though it was a soup. Bring it up to a boil over a high heat, then turn it down to a simmer, and cook the potatoes for 15 mins, or until they are tender.

Grate your cheddar. Drain your potatoes in a colander set over the sink, then add them back to the saucepan. Add the milk and butter, then mash your potatoes with a potato masher. Sprinkle in your cheddar and fold it through, then season it to taste with salt and pepper.

Once your chilli has finished cooking, season it to taste with salt and pepper. Spoon your mash directly on top of it, and even it out with the back of a spoon. Trace lines on the top with a fork. Slice your remaining green chilli up and arrange them on top. Bake it for 40 mins.
Serve it up with peas.

name: Smoky Chorizo Pepper Pasta
description: Spicy, cheesy and satisfying – this 20-minute pasta number is your new midweek hero.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Smoky Chorizo & Pepper Sauce.
Fill a large saucepan with salted water and bring to the boil. Once boiling, add the pasta and cook according to pack instructions. Just before draining, reserve 100ml of the pasta water.

Return the drained pasta to the saucepan over a medium-high heat. Stir through the chorizo pepper sauce and cook until piping hot, loosening with a splash of pasta water if needed. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Serve into bowls and finish with plenty of grated Parmesan. Dig in.

name: Smoky Chorizo, Cod & New Potato Traybake
description: Lemony homemade aioli cuts through the rich, meaty fish and smoky chorizo, bringing balance and brightness to this hearty, warming traybake.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.

Cut any large new potatoes in half. Thickly slice the onions, pepper and chorizo. Add to your largest roasting tin (or two small tins). Drizzle with olive oil, add the fennel seeds, smoked paprika and season with salt and black pepper. Toss together. Nestle in the garlic bulb then spread everything out into a single layer so it roasts evenly. Roast in the oven for 35–40 mins until the potatoes are golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile season the cod with salt - this will keep the fish firm and succulent.

Come back to your veg. If spread across two tins, tip everything into one. Give everything a good toss and pour in the wine. Nestle the cod into the tin. Return to the oven for 12–15 mins until the fish is cooked through.
Meanwhile, add the mayo into a bowl, season with lemon juice. Squeeze the roasted garlic into the mayo, season with salt and stir together.
Cut the remaining lemon into wedges, pick the parsley leaves.
Share the veg and fish onto plates with any juices. Top with the garlic mayo, serve with a sprinkle of parsley leaves and a lemon wedge.

name: Smoky Chorizo, Pepper & Mozzarella Toast
description: Hot toast. Smoky sauce. Creamy mozzarella. A banging lunch you can quickly whip up when you have a spare 10 mins.
ingredients: Third of Smoky Chorizo & Pepper Sauce
instructions: Before you begin, make the Smoky Chorizo & Pepper Sauce.
Reheat the chorizo pepper sauce in a small saucepan until hot. Meanwhile, toast the sourdough until golden.
Tear the mozzarella into chunky pieces.
Place the toast on plates and spoon over the hot chorizo pepper sauce. Top with mozzarella, rocket and a good drizzle of olive oil.

name: Smoky Courgette Dip
description: This is my super simple courgette dip. All you need is courgettes, tahini, lemon, olive oil and herbs. It's smokey and delicious and I know you'll love it.
instructions: Pierce the courgettes all over with a fork.
Roast at 200°C for about an hour or until completely blackened, turning once or twice.

Remove from the oven and allow to cool. Carefully slice the skin lengthways down the middle and scoop out the flesh with a spoon into a large bowl. Use a fork to mash the courgette into a chunky texture.
Add the tahini, lemon, olive oil, salt and pepper and stir through.
Finely chop the parsley and mint and mix through the dip, saving some for garnish.
Serve in a shallow bowl and top with a good drizzle of olive oil, more tahini, pomegranate and sumac if using.

name: Smoky Grilled Cheese Burgers
description: The ultimate barbecue cheese burgers. Making your own burgers from scratch is so much better than getting the tight and dry store-bought versions.
instructions: Pile coals over to one side of your BBQ to create a hot, direct cooking side, and a warm, indirect cooking side.
Mix the mustard, ketchup and mayo in a bowl. Finely dice the shallots and add to the sauce with a good few dashes of Tabasco. Mix thoroughly.
Split your mince into four roughly equal balls. Form each one into a patty, roughly 3cm thick and just wider than your buns. Set aside.

Pop a frying pan onto the BBQ over the coals and drop in the bacon along with a shot of olive oil. Fry until golden brown and crispy before flashing on the BBQ for a little smoke. Move over to the indirect side of the BBQ to rest.

Drop the burgers onto the hot side of the grill and sear for 3-4 mins each side. Add a slice of cheese to each burger, then shift over to the indirect side. Add a lid and leave to slowly melt for 1-2 mins. Meanwhile, finely shred the lettuce.
Briefly toast the buns on the grill before adding a dollop of sauce to each side. Top with a burger and a couple of slices of bacon. Add some shredded lettuce and pickles. Serve straight away.

name: Smoky Grilled Lettuce Caesar Salad
description: Smoky and fresh – this grilled lettuce caesar is the ultimate summer side. Yes, the lettuce is grilled, don’t knock it till you try it .
instructions: In a food processor, add the mayo, dijon mustard, anchovies, the juice of the lemon and half the chives. Process until broken down and creamy. Taste and season with salt, pepper. Halve the baby gems lengthways and drizzle the cut side with a little oil.
Place a grill pan over high heat. Once smoking, place the gems cut-side down and cook until charred, 3-4 mins. (You can also do this on a hot BBQ grill, it’ll take half the time to char).
Meanwhile, thinly slice the remaining chives. Using a vegetable peeler, shave the Parmesan into shards – you can also do this by thinly slicing with a sharp knife.
Add the grilled gems onto a sharing plate. Drizzle the dressing over and garnish with the croutons and Parmesan shards.

name: Smoky Grilled Mushroom Döner
description: If you find it hard to believe that a döner kebab can be healthy, we're here to prove you wrong. This veggie-style grilled mushroom döner will have you feeling like you're post night out minus the regret. Enjoy.
instructions: Start by tearing the mushrooms into thick pieces, then slice the peppers. Tip it all into a bowl with the olive oil, smoked paprika, dried rosemary, cumin and ground coriander. Season with salt and pepper, then marinate for at least 1 hr but preferably overnight.

For the sauce, finely chop the mint, grate the garlic and crumble ⅔ of the feta. In a small bowl, combine the yogurt, mint, garlic, dill, white wine vinegar and feta, then season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

When you're ready to cook, heat the oven to 220°C or as hot as it will go. Thread the mushrooms and peppers onto skewers, then transfer to a tray and cook for 10-15 mins until charred, then flip and cook for another 10-15 mins. The timings will vary depending on your oven, so keep an eye on them.
Finely slice the red onion and tip into a bowl, then squeeze over the lemon. Deseed and dice the tomatoes and shred the lettuce, then add both to the same bowl. Toss with the sumac and set aside.
Toast the pitta and fill with the sauce, grilled veg and red onion salad. Top with the remaining feta and get stuck in.

name: Smoky Grilled Potatoes with Burnt Chilli Mayo & Pickles
description: Why fry when you can grill? The age-old question...Answered by these killer smoky, crispy, spicy potatoes. Once you start eating them, it’s very hard to stop. B x
instructions: Add the vinegar and sugar to a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, stir to combine and then add the ice. Leave to cool to room temperature.
Meanwhile, thinly slice 1/4 of the chillies and the red onion. Add to the pickle liquor and set aside.
Add the salad potatoes to a large pan and cover with cold water. Season with salt, bring to a boil and simmer until just tender. This should take around 13 mins.
Drain and leave to steam dry for a few minutes.
Coat the remaining chillies with olive oil and grill on a hot barbecue until thoroughly charred. Finely chop until almost a paste and mix with the mayo. Add a big squeeze of lemon juice and season.
Now toss the potatoes in olive oil and get them onto the grill. Grill until charred, crispy and smoky.
Chuck the potatoes on a plate and cover with the chilli mayo and pickles. Thinly slice the spring onions and scatter over. Get stuck in.

name: Smoky Halloumi Fajitas
description: Why have we never added halloumi to a fajita? It's out of this world. With smokey veg and crunchy tortilla chips crumbled on top. The veggie dream.
instructions: Slice up your onions and peppers into strips and add them to the pan with some olive oil. Once they have cooked, add 1/2 of your seasoning sachet. Add a sprinkle of salt and pepper and stir.
Next, chop up your coriander and add to your pan and mix together. Set aside.

Halloumi time. Slice up your halloumi and add to a bowl. Add your remaining seasoning, along with a grinding of pepper and a glug of olive oil. Mix together with your hands so the halloumi is covered in the seasoning. Add your halloumi to a well oiled frying pan and cook until golden on both sides.

It’s loading up time. Add your tortilla to a pan. Heat for 1 minute on each side. Take your tortilla wrap and add a spoonful of your vegetable mixture. Then add 2 slices of halloumi, a squeeze of the salsa and a dollop of sour cream. Take your tortilla crisps and break them up into small pieces and scatter on top. Add your remaining coriander Repeat for the rest of your MOB and tuck in.
