name: Smoky Honeyed Feta & Tomato Salad
description: A smoky, slightly spicy salad that'll steal the show at your next dinner party. One for the feta lovers out there.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Cut the tortillas into triangles and brush with a little olive oil. Add to a baking tray and slide into the oven for 14 mins until crispy and golden.
Mix the chipotle paste and honey in a small pan and bring to a simmer. Pop the feta into an ovenproof dish and pour over the honey chipotle mixture. Slide into the oven and bake for 8-9 mins.

Meanwhile, boil the corn cobs for 4 mins in salted water. Remove the corn from the husks with a knife and tip them into a large bowl. Thinly slice the onion and add to the bowl. Roughly chop the tomatoes and tip into the bowl. Season with salt, olive oil and the juice of two limes.
Tip in the crispy tortillas and toss through the salad.

Thinly slice the radishes and chop the coriander, stalks and all. Tip the tomato salad onto a large serving platter and top with the radishes, coriander and jalapeños. Add the sweet, smoky baked feta and serve.

name: Smoky Mac and Cheese Pastacini
description: This is a great way to use up leftover pasta, fried like arancini until golden and crunchy and served with a fresh slaw.
instructions: If not using leftover pasta, cook 300g tubetti or other small pasta shape in plenty of boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium heat. Once it foams, add the flour bit by bit, whisking as you go, until you have a smooth paste.
Cook for a min, then slowly pour in the milk, whisking constantly. Add the paprika and chilli and whisk again to incorporate. Cook for about 3 mins until the sauce starts to thicken.
Grate in the cheese, stir and continue to cook until you have a smooth, thick and creamy sauce.
Add the pasta to the sauce and mix well to combine, then allow to cool to room temperature.
Into 3 separate bowls add the flour, eggs and panko breadcrumbs. Form the pasta mix into golfball size rounds and then dredge in the flour, then dip into the egg and finally the breadcrumbs.
Transfer to a clean tray and place into the fridge for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, make the slaw by grating the apples, carrot and fennel into a bowl. Squeeze out any excess moisture and then season with the mustard, vinegar, a third of the mayo, salt and pepper.
Mince up the basil and mix with the remaining mayo and set aside.
Fill a large pan half full with vegetable oil, you want it about 2 inches deep. Heat the oil to 180c and then add the pastacini in batches and fry for about 3 mins until golden brown.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer to a plate lined with a paper towel and fry the rest.
Plate up 3 of the pastacini, a couple of spoons of the slaw and a good dollop of the basil mayo.

name: Smoky Maple Mushroom Bagel
description: This is my ultimate juicy, smoky, maple mushroom bagel.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Slice the mushrooms to about half a centimetre thick and place in a wide, shallow bowl or large tupperware box.
Mix the olive oil, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, soy sauce, smoked paprika, miso, and black pepper until combined to make the marinade.
Pour the marinade over the mushrooms and carefully mix to make sure each slice is covered.

Lay the mushrooms out onto baking paper on a large baking tray. If you have a wire rack, this will help them cook more evenly. Roast at 180°C for 10 mins, flipping halfway through. Alternatively, air fry for 6 mins at 180°C.

To serve, slice the bagel open and toast in the oven or on a hot pan until crispy. Slice your tomato. Spread vegan cream cheese, if using, on the bottom half of the bagel, then layer up the mushrooms, tomato, and lettuce on top. Spread the mayo onto the top half, close, and enjoy.

name: Smoky One-Pot Gochujang Pasta
description: A rich, silky pasta with spicy gochujang and sweet roasted peppers. Ready in just 30 minutes, this one’s a fiery, cheesy, one-pot dream.
instructions: Drain the roasted peppers and finely mince them. Set aside. Peel the garlic.
Add the milk, stock, garlic, tomato purée, and gochujang to a blender. Blend until smooth.

Tip the pasta into a large pan, then pour in the blended stock mixture. Stir together, bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to medium. Leave to simmer, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is al dente (normally around 10 mins, but follow pack instructions). Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
While the pasta is cooking, finely slice the spring onions and grate the Cheddar.
Once the pasta is cooked, stir through the chopped peppers and grated Cheddar. Divide between bowls and top with a scattering of spring onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

name: Smoky Pepper Croquetas
description: Our favourite bit of tapas turned plant-based. Crispy nuggets spiked with smoky paprika béchamel and charred peppers. So moreish.
instructions: Drain your roasted peppers and pat them dry with paper towel. Halve lengthways and finely slice them.
Pour your olive oil into a small saucepan on a medium heat. Once hot, get your peppers in there and fry for a couple of minutes until fragrant.
Tip in 55g of your flour, smoked paprika, and 1 tsp of your PERi-PERi Salt, then cook out for 5 minutes. Gradually add 400ml oat milk, whisking until you have a smooth sauce.
Bring your mixture to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes until it has thickened.
Pour your croqueta mix into a square tin and leave to set in the fridge for 4 hours.
Pour your remaining flour, oat milk, and breadcrumbs into a bowl each. Season your flour with a tsp of Nando's PERi-PERi Salt and stir to combine.
Roll your mixture into balls and dip them in your flour, oat milk, and breadcrumbs respectively.
Heat a generous glug of oil in a small saucepan. Once hot, add your croquetas a few at a time and fry for 5 minutes until crisp and golden. Keep warm and repeat with your remaining croquetas.
Serve whilst still hot with your Nando's Vegan PERinaise.

name: Smoky Pork Fillet with Orange Chickpeas
description: This recipe features tender pork loin, zesty orange, and refreshing fennel. It's a great way to ease yourself into the spring months. Enjoy.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Mix the coffee and seasoning together in a small bowl. Season the pork fillet with salt and pepper and rub well with the coffee mixture. Thinly slice the red onions and garlic cloves.

Preheat an ovenproof frying pan over a medium high heat. Add a shot of olive oil and add the pork fillet. Sear well on all sides, allowing some of the spice rub to catch on the pan. Once coloured, remove the pork from the pan and throw in the onions. Cook for 3-4 mins before adding the garlic.

Tip in the chickpeas (plus the liquid from the jar) and bring to a boil. Cook off some of the liquid, chunk up the peppers and olives and tip into the pan. Add the zest and juice of one of the oranges and then sit the pork back on top. Slide into the oven for 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the fennel and add to a bowl. Toss with the juice of the other orange, a shot of olive oil and roughly chopped dill.
Remove the pork from the oven and allow to rest for 5 mins before carving into chunky slices. Serve the chickpeas, topped with a couple of pork slices and a handful of fennel salad.

name: Smoky Prawn & Paprika Fidueá
description: A classic Spanish one-pot packed with juicy prawns, broken pasta and a rich, smoky tomato sauce. It’s like paella’s pasta cousin.
instructions: Grate the tomato. Finely chop the onion and garlic.Tip the prawns into a bowl with a glug of olive oil, a pinch of smoked paprika and some salt. Give them a good mix.
Heat a large frying pan over a high heat with a little olive oil. Add the prawns and fry for about 30 seconds on each side until browned, then remove and set aside.

Wrap the spaghetti in kitchen paper and bash it with a rolling pin until it breaks into short pieces. Add more olive oil to the pan and toast the spaghetti for a few minutes until golden brown. Remove and set aside.
Add another drizzle of oil to the pan, then fry the onion and garlic for about 5 mins until softened and just starting to colour.
Stir in the grated tomato, the rest of the smoked paprika and the chilli flakes. Let it cook on high for 5 mins until it thickens and most of the liquid has evaporated.

Return the toasted spaghetti to the pan and stir to coat. Pour in the fish stock and bring to the boil. Turn the heat down and simmer for about 8 mins without stirring. Top with prawns and turn up the heat for 5 mins, until the pasta’s cooked through and the bottom’s crisp.
Chop the parsley and scatter over the Fidueá and serve with a wedge of lemon.

name: Smoky Pulled Aubergine Ragu
description: A smoky ragu is a beautiful thing, and not something you come across often. The flavour is pretty incredible and if you leave out the parm it’s totally vegan.
instructions: Dice up your onion, celery and carrot as small as you can to make your sofritto.
Preheat a large saucepan over medium heat, add the sofritto with a big glug of oil and a pinch of salt. Cook for 10 mins until soft and translucent.

Add the fennel seeds and finely grate in the garlic. De-seed and finely chop the chilli and get that in there too. Cook for 5 mins then add the white wine and turn the heat down to low. Let the wine slowly reduce for 10 mins.
Add the tinned tomatoes to a small bowl and crush with your hands. Add them to the saucepan and cook gently for 15 mins.

Meanwhile, place the aubergines directly over a gas burner or under a hot grill. Cook, turning regularly, for 10 mins until totally blackened and collapsing. Steam in a covered bowl for 2 mins before carefully peeling off the burnt skins.
Pull the cooked aubergines into bite sized pieces with two forks and add them to the ragu. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Now cook the pasta in boiling salted water according to the package instructions. Add your pasta to the ragu along with a handful of basil and a load of parmesan cheese.
Toss together, divide between warm bowls and top with extra parmesan, basil and a drizzle of olive oil.
Get stuck in.

name: Smoky Roasted Pepper Lasagne
description: The best veggie lasagne in town. Roasted peppers and chipotle flakes lend ridiculous depth and smokiness to the Quorn Mince ragù.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C/400°F.
Cut your peppers in half, remove their stalks and deseed them.
Pop on a baking tray and roast skin side up for 30 mins until softened with charred skins.

Cover your baking tray with a kitchen towel to allow the peppers to steam and cool, then peel off and discard the skins. Whizz your pepper flesh in a food processor along with your plum tomatoes until smooth.
Put your dried porcini mushrooms into a heatproof jug and pour over 400ml boiling water. Set aside for 20 mins.
Finely chop your onions and grate your garlic.

Heat some olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add your onion and fry for 15 mins until softened and starting to caramelise. Add your garlic, chipotle chilli flakes and tomato purée and cook for 2 mins more.

Tip your Quorn Mince from frozen into the pan and fry for 5 mins until it's all coated in the onion mixture. Pour in your red pepper and tomato mixture along with your porcini mushrooms in their liquid and a bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 mins until reduced and fragrant. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Whilst your ragù simmers, make the white sauce. Melt your butter in a medium-sized saucepan over a medium heat. Once foaming, add your flour and smoked paprika and mix to a paste. Cook for 2 mins.

Gradually pour in your milk in small increments, beating all the while to ensure that you have a smooth mixture before adding more milk. Once all the milk is added, bring the mixture to a boil and allow it to thicken. Add your cheddar and season to taste with salt and pepper.

Pour a little white sauce into the base of your baking dish, followed by a little ragù. Arrange your lasagna sheets neatly on top, snapping sheets where necessary to plug the gaps. Pour over 1/3rd of your remaining ragù followed by 1/3rd of your remaining sauce, then more lasagna sheets. Continue like this until you are out of all your mixtures.

Mix the top layer so that the ragù and white sauce combine, pushing it all the way to the edges so the lasagna sheets are totally covered. Sprinkle the surface with your mozzarella, then bake for 30 mins.
Leave the lasagne to stand for 5 mins once out of the oven, then serve.

name: Smoky Romesco Potato & Sausage Platter
description: An impressive platter that's suitable for any dinner party situation. Making your own romesco is a necessary flex.
instructions: Add the potatoes into a saucepan full of water. Season generously with salt and place on medium-high heat. Boil for 10-15 mins until tender. Drain then drizzle with 1 tbsp of oil.
Place a frying pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, drizzle in some olive oil and add the sausages, fry until cooked through, 10-15 mins.
Meanwhile, drain the roasted peppers and add into a blender with the smoked almonds and sweet paprika. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Pick the dill and parsley, discarding the stalks. Chop the tomatoes and sausages into bite-sized chunks, add to a bowl with the potatoes, herbs, and lemon zest, toss together. Drizzle with some oil and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Spread the romesco onto a platter or plates, top with the herby potato salad. Dollop the soured cream and finish with crispy onions and a good crack of black pepper.

name: Smoky Salmon Fish Cakes Recipe With Chilli Yoghurt
description: An easy, breezy salmon fish cakes recipe that's loaded with extra protein thanks to broad beans and peas. It's a good 'un.
keywords: Smoky Salmon Fish Cakes Recipe With Chilli Yoghurt
instructions: Peel and roughly chop the potatoes. Tip them into a pan and cover with cold water. Generously salt and place over a medium heat. Once simmering, cook for 10-12 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with a spoonful of yoghurt. Set aside to cool a little.

Flake the salmon into large pieces. Pour a boiled kettle over the peas and broad beans and let sit for a minute or two before draining. If you like, you can peel the tough outer skin from the broad beans, but this is optional. Finely chop the herbs.

Tip the peas, broad beans and salmon into the bowl of mash and fold them together. Don’t overwork the mix or you’ll break down the fish too much, we want nice big flakes in there. Add two thirds of the herbs and the zest of two lemons. Season with lots of black pepper and salt and then form into little fish cakes. Roll them through flour, then beaten egg then in the panko breadcrumbs and then chill for 10-15 minutes.
Cut the cucumber and red onion into slices and toss together with the remaining herbs, salt, lemon zest and juice. Drizzle with olive oil and set aside.
Preheat a frying pan over a medium heat. Add a generous glug of olive oil and once hot, add the fishcakes. Fry gently on either side, turning now and then, until golden brown and hot throughout.
Season with flaky salt and divide between plates. Serve with cucumber salad, lemon wedges and a dollop of yoghurt topped with chilli oil.

name: Smoky Sausage Ragù with Cheesy Spuds
description: Stuffed skins normally take hours to do, but not today. You blast these tatties in the microwave to get them done quickly, then finish them under the grill.
keywords: Smoky Sausage Ragu with Cheesy Spuds
instructions: Finely slice your onion. Finely chop your garlic.

Heat a saute pan over medium heat, then squeeze your sausages out of their skins and straight into the pan. Break up the chunks with your spoon, and fry for about 5 mins until golden. Lift your sausage meat out the pan, leaving the fat in there.
Stab your potatoes all over with a fork, then rub them with a little olive oil and some salt.
Place them on a large plate, then microwave for 6 mins.
Tip your onions into the sausage pan and fry for about 15 mins until golden and totally soft. Add your garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes, then cook for another 2 mins.
Flip over your potatoes, then return to the microwave for another 6 mins.
Tip your sausages back into the pan, along with your passata. Simmer for 15 mins.
Heat your grill to high.
Grate your cheddar. Finely slice your spring onions. Put a handful of the greens to one side. Finely chop your jalapenos.
Halve your potatoes, then carefully scoop out the middles, leaving the skins in tact.
Place the middles in a bowl with 2 tbsp of olive oil and mash with a fork. Add 100g of your cheddar, spring onions, and jalapenos, then give it all a good mix. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Load your mixture back into your potato skins, then top with your remaining cheddar. Put these under the grill for about 5 mins until the cheese is melted.
Add two potato skins to a plate, then spoon over your sausage mix. Top with your extra spring onion greens and a dollop of sour cream, then serve.

name: Smoky Sea Bass Piccata
description: You've probably heard of chicken piccata but this smoky sea bass piccata is just as good, if not better. A summer belter.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Tip the potatoes into a large pan and cover with cold water. Season well with salt and set over a medium heat. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer for 5 mins until the potatoes are just tender. Drain and tip onto a roasting tray. Drizzle with oil and salt and slide into the oven for 15 mins.
While the potatoes are cooking, trim roughly 2 cm from the bottom of the asparagus and finely dice the shallots and garlic. Chop the dill.
Toss the asparagus spears with oil and salt. Once the potatoes have been roasting for 15 mins, add the asparagus to the tray and slide back into the oven.

Preheat a large frying pan over a high flame. Once very hot, add 4 tbsp olive oil. Pat dry and season the bass fillets with salt. Carefully place them skin-side down into the pan, laying away from you.

Press gently on the fillets to ensure an even crisp and cook over a high heat for 2-3 mins. Remove from the pan and set aside. In the residual fat, cook the shallots for 2 mins, add the ’nduja, garlic, paprika and capers and cook for a couple more mins. Tip in the wine and reduce by half.

Cube the butter and whisk into the sauce. Reduce the heat to low as you do this. Sit the fish (skin-side up this time) back in the butter sauce to finish cooking. Finish the lot with a big squeeze of lemon and chopped dill. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges.
Pull the veggies out of the oven and divide between warm plates. Top with bass, plenty of sauce and lemon wedges.

name: Smoky Sesame and Broccoli Noodles
description: Crispy charred broccoli with creamy tahini noodles. The smoky tofu makes these noodles something special, so get it in your Ocado shopping bag immediately.
keywords: Smokey Sesame and Broccoli Noodles recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C/390°F.

Finely chop the stalks of your broccoli but make sure to leave the top in large florets. Finely slice the whites of your spring onion and roughly chop the green ends. Mince one red chilli and all of your garlic before finely slicing your remaining red chilli.
Crumble the tofu into a large tray, add in your florets and toss with olive oil and salt. Bake in the oven for 30 mins until the tofu is crisp and the broccoli is charred.
Mix 3 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp tahini and 2 tbsp water in a bowl.

Heat a wok until smoking and add a big glug of oil. Fry your broccoli stalks, the finely sliced whites of your spring onions, and minced red chilli. Cook for 2 mins until they are lightly browned and soft.
Add in the garlic and cook for 30 secs until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce along with the egg noodles and toss well. Add in the charred broccoli and crispy tofu before giving it another good mix.
Finish with the sliced chilli and spring onion greens to serve.

name: Smoky Spicy Broth with Mushrooms & Rice
description: This roasted mushroom and spicy chipotle brothy rice is bursting with umami. An incredibly soothing vegan dinner for the colder months.
keywords: Smoky Spicy Broth with Mushrooms & Rice
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Tear or slice the mushrooms into 1cm chunks. Sprinkle the cumin, coriander and sesame seeds on top and drizzle with olive oil. Season generously with salt and roast for 25-30 mins, until golden.

Meanwhile, set a saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the tomato purée and cook until dark red. Then, stir the chipotle and mushroom stock through. Leave it on the heat until hot, then turn it down to low. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lime juice.
Pick the coriander leaves off, finely slice the stems and half of the leaves. Reheat the cooked rice and stir through the chopped coriander.
Share the coriander rice between bowls and ladle over the broth. Top with the mushrooms and coriander leaves. Serve with any remaining lime.

name: Smoky Spicy Roasted Mushrooms
description: These smoky spicy roast mushrooms are perfect for meal prep. Combine them with your choice of protein, carb and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Tear or slice the mushrooms into 1cm chunks. Sprinkle the cumin, coriander and sesame seeds on top and drizzle with olive oil. Season generously with salt and roast for 25-30 mins, until golden.
Allow the mushrooms to cool then transfer the mushrooms to a container and store in the fridge until ready to serve.

name: Smoky Tahini “Chicken” Salad with Crispy Chickpeas
description: Step into chillier months in style and make a roasted root salad. This one uses Garden Gourmet's Chargrilled Bites, the perfect addition to any wintry number.
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C.

Cut the carrots in half lengthways and add to a large roasting tin. Peel, top and tail the red onion and cut into 6 wedges. Separate the onion petals and toss them into the tray along with the Garden Gourmet Chargrilled Pieces and the drained and rinsed chickpeas.
Add a generous glug of olive oil to the tray along with the fennel seeds and 1 tbsp of the paprika. Season generously with salt and pepper and toss to coat.
Pop into the oven for 30-40 mins, or until the carrots are gnarly and tender, and the chickpeas and Garden Gourmet Chargrilled Pieces are crispy.

Cut the tomatoes into bite sized chunks and add to a large mixing bowl. Add the bulgur to the bowl along with the juice of one lime and a glug of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and mix thoroughly.
To make the tahini sauce combine the tahini with the remaining paprika and the juice of the remaining lime. Grate in the garlic clove and mix in enough cold water to create a creamy dressing.

Pull the traybake out of the oven. Toss the bulgur and tomatoes through the other ingredients and pile generously onto a platter. Top with the creamy, smoky tahini dressing, lime zest and torn dill fronds. Serve with extra lime wedges for squeezing.

name: Smoky Tempeh Brunch Bowl
description: Smoky tempeh 'bacon', blistered cherry tomatoes, and zingy edamame guac come together in this absolute banger of a grain bowl.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Rinse the quinoa under cold water, then cook in a pan of salted boiling water for 12–15 mins until fluffy. Drain and set aside.
Slice the tempeh and chuck it into a bowl with the smoked paprika, soy sauce, maple syrup, half the olive oil and a pinch of black pepper. Toss to coat, then spread out on one side of a baking tray.

Toss the cherry tomatoes with the rest of the olive oil and some salt and pepper. Add to the other side of the tray, then slide it into the oven for 15 mins until the tomatoes are soft and blistered and the tempeh is golden.
Finely chop most of the parsley, saving a few leaves for garnish. Stir the chopped parsley through the cooked quinoa.

Grate the garlic and squeeze the lime. Add both to a blender with the edamame and a pinch of salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth, adding a splash of water if needed to loosen it to a hummus-like consistency.

Spoon the quinoa into a bowl and top with the roasted tomatoes and crispy tempeh. Add a big dollop of the edamame guac and finish with the rest of the parsley. Serve with a wedge of lime on the side, if you like.

name: Smoky Turkey & Bean Chilli
description: This hearty, smoky chilli is packed with shredded turkey, grilled peppers & a kick of spice. Proper comfort food, perfect for cold nights.
instructions: Finely grate the cheddar. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stalks. Thinly slice the onions and garlic. Drain the grilled peppers and roughly chop. Shred the turkey. Drain and rinse the beans.
Add one-third of the sliced onion to a small bowl with the juice of half a lime. Season with salt and set aside to pickle.
Set a large saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the rest of the onion and cook for 5–7 mins until soft and translucent.
Stir in the rosemary, garlic, coriander stalks, smoked paprika and cumin. Cook for 1–2 mins until fragrant.

Tip in the chopped tomatoes, grilled peppers, kidney beans and chicken stock. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down and let it simmer for 15–20 mins until thickened slightly — it should be like a loose stew.
Stir the turkey through the chilli and cook for 3–4 mins until piping hot. Taste and season with salt, pepper or more lime juice if needed.
Ladle the chilli into bowls and top with grated cheddar, pickled onions and coriander leaves. Serve with any extra lime wedges on the side.

name: Smoky Veggie Enchiladas
description: Smoky beans are the perfect filling inside these soft, warming enchiladas. Lots of cheddar on the top takes these to the next level.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Finely chop the peppers, onion and 1 garlic clove. Add to a frying pan with a splash of oil. Fry until softened.
Add large handful of finely chopped coriander stalks, cumin and paprika. Mix together.
Pour in black beans with the tin water. Bubble your bean mix down. Once the beans have softened, season with salt and pepper. Add a handful of fresh coriander and mash everything together.
Tomato sauce time. Crush 2 garlic cloves into a pan with a splash of olive oil. After 15 seconds, pour in your passata. Bubble it down until it has thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon in half of your tomato sauce to a baking dish.
Fill each of the 8 tortillas with an equal amount of the bean mixture. Wrap the tortillas up. Lay them side by side in the baking tray. They should be nice and snug when they are all in.
Pour the remaining tomato sauce over the top, making sure you don’t cover the edges of the tortillas (you want the edges to get nice and crispy).
Cheese time. Grate 150g of your cheddar. Scatter it over your enchiladas.
Place baking dish in the oven for 45 minutes or until the cheddar is golden and bubbling.
Serve the enchiladas with a handful of fresh coriander and any leftover grated cheese scattered on top. Enjoy!

name: Smoky White Bean & Green Pepper Chilli
description: Another day, another batch. This veggie one involves smoky charred peppers, creamy white beans and a tangy tomatillo salsa simmered down into a brothy, warming chilli. Great for batch cooking and even better the next day.
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Halve the green peppers and remove the stems and seeds. Place skin-side up on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Slide under the grill and cook for 7-15 mins until the skin starts to char and blister. Once charred, rinse off most of the char under cold water, then finely dice.
Meanwhile, finely dice the onions, thinly slice the garlic and jalapeños.

Place a large pot over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the peppers and onions and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 mins until softened. Stir in the garlic, jalapeños, cumin, coriander and oregano and cook for 2-3 mins until fragrant. Pour in the vinegar and let it evaporate, then tip in the tomatillo salsa (if you can't find it, normal salsa will work) and stir through.

Let the mixture come to the boil, then add the beans and their liquid along with the stock. Bring back to the boil, season with salt, then reduce to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 15-20 mins to thicken slightly, it should still be brothy.

Divide between bowls and serve with crusty bread. Box up any leftovers once cooled and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat in a pan over a medium heat until piping hot, adding a splash of water to loosen if needed.

name: Snickers Millionaire's Shortbread
description: A classic millionaire's shortbread recipe with a little twist. Peanuts give this sweet treat an extra little something. It’s sweet, buttery and delicious!
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Grease and line a 20cm x 20cm brownie tin with parchment paper.

Start by using a wooden spoon to beat the sugar and unsalted softened butter until light and fluffy. Mix in the peanut butter. Use a sieve to sift the flour in along with a pinch of salt and mix well, the mixture will be crumbly at this point. Press into the base of the tin, prick with a fork and bake in the oven for 20 mins.

Make the caramel layer: Cut the butter into 2cm cubes and place in the fridge to keep cold. Tip the sugar into a non-stick frying pan and place over a medium heat. Leave it undisturbed until the sugar starts to melt into a dark caramel colour and gently swirl it around to make sure all the sugar is melted, for 4-6 mins. Turn the heat down to low and whisk in the butter, add the cream and whisk well, then add the golden syrup and a pinch of salt.
Scatter the peanuts over the shortbread base, then pour the caramel evenly over the top. Place in the fridge to set - it should take around 2 hours.

Melt the dark chocolate in a bowl, it’s easiest to do this in blasts in the microwave, or by tipping the chocolate into a glass bowl and placing it over a pan of simmering water until melted. Stir the butter into the dark chocolate until combined.
Tip the melted dark chocolate all over the caramel in one even layer. Place in the fridge to set completely, 45 mins minimum.
Cut the millionaire into squares or rectangles before serving.

name: Solo Pan Pizza Calabrese
description: A simple, one-person pizza recipe that you don't need any fancy kit to make. This one's a beauty.
instructions: Combine 110g of the flour with 100ml cold water and the yeast in a medium bowl. Mix in the morning, cover and set aside at room temperature for 8-10 hours. Go to work, go out and hang, whatever.

When you get home, mix the remaining flour with the salt. Tip into the dough and bring together, add 5-10 ml more water if needed. Knead into a smooth dough, shape into a ball and set aside covered with an upturned bowl for 45 mins.

Meanwhile, tip the tomatoes into a small bowl. Add 1 tbsp of olive oil, salt and pepper, and finely grate in the garlic clove. Mix to combine. Tear the mozzarella into pieces and pick the basil leaves.
When you’re ready to cook, preheat the grill to max. Take a 20-25cm oven proof pan and set over a medium heat. Whilst your pan heats up, tip some flour onto your surface and grab the dough ball.

Using the tips of your fingers, press down in the middle of the dough ball and work your way out to the edge, shimmying the dough around to create a defined crust. Once roughly the same shape as your pan, scoop it up, dust off the excess flour and carefully lay into the hot pan.

Spread over your tomato sauce and top with cheese, salami, sliced chilli and the basil. Cook until the base is golden and crispy, this will take 4-5 mins, then slide the pizza under the grill to finish cooking.
Finish with the grated parmesan and a little olive oil.

name: Sopa Bullabesa de Almería by José Pizarro
description: The king of Spanish cuisine, José Pizarro, shares his Bullabesa- the pernod is the secret ingredient. Bit more expensive but worth it.
instructions: Soak your saffron in two tbsp of boiling water, then finely chop up your onion and fennel, saving the fennel fronds for later use.
Pour a generous glug of olive oil into a large frying pan over a medium heat and whack in your fennel and onion chunks. Cook these gently, stirring occasionally, for 15 minutes until softened.
Add in your pimentón and saffron along with it’s water, then add in the in the wine and pernod. Leave this to bubble for a couple of minutes, and soak up the delicious smells.
Peel and chop your tomatoes, zest and juice your orange, then add this all to your frying pan along with the stock. Have a taste to test your seasoning, then bring this all to a simmer.

Chop your monkfish into chunks. Add these chunks to the pan, then cook for a further 4 minutes before chucking in your clams and prawns. Leave this to cook for another 3 minutes until the prawns go a lovely pink and the clams open up (some won’t, but don’t stress, just discard them).
Scatter your fennel fronds over this, and serve with crusty bread to soak up the lovely broth. Gather your MOB round and tuck into this rich and simple feast.

name: Sopa Negra(ish) Beans
description: This rich and hearty black bean soup is packed with flavour, spice and the perfect balance of fresh toppings. Topped with jammy eggs and a zingy salsa, it's a simple but seriously satisfying dish.
instructions: Finely dice the onion, garlic, red pepper, jalapeño and tomatoes. Heat a glug of olive oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the garlic, red pepper, jalapeño and ½ the onion and cook for 10 mins until softened.

Add the ground cumin, oregano and ⅓ the tomatoes to the pan. Season with salt and black pepper, then cook for 5 mins until soft. Tip in the black beans with their juices and add the water. Simmer for 10 mins, stirring occasionally, until the beans are soft and starting to break down. Mash slightly with a potato masher if needed. Squeeze in the juice of ½ the lime and adjust seasoning to taste.
Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and cook for 8 mins. Drain, run under cold water and peel.

To make the salsa, add the remaining tomatoes and onion to a bowl. Roughly chop the coriander, saving a few leaves for garnish, and stir through the beans along with the juice of the remaining lime. Season with salt to taste. Finely slice the jalapeño for garnish.
Divide the beans between bowls. Halve the eggs and place on top. Spoon over the salsa and scatter with jalapeño slices and the reserved coriander leaves.

name: Sophie's Dirty Martini
description: A classic for a reason. Just 3 ingredients for the cleanest, classiest cocktail. I like my martini stirred, not shaken.
instructions: Add some ice to a large glass or a glass jar. Pour in your gin, vermouth and olive brine, then stir the mixture until the jar is very cold to touch.
Strain your cocktail into a chilled martini glass. Pop an olive on a cocktail stick and drop this into the cocktail. Serve and enjoy!

name: Sophie's Leek and Taleggio Paccheri
description: This is inspired by an Alpine dish I ate as a kid, but with the addition of soft leeks. Spiced with nutmeg and bold taleggio, it's a comfort classic. Sophie x
instructions: Finely chop your leeks and garlic.
Heat your butter in a large sauté pan and, once melted and foaming, add your leeks. Cook gently for 20 mins until totally softened.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Tip in your paccheri and cook for 13 mins, until al dente.
Back to the sauce. Add garlic to the leeks and cook out for 2 mins. Pour your double cream and milk into the pan and bring them to a gentle simmer.
Chop your taleggio into rough chunks, then add this to the sauce and stir to melt. Add your nutmeg and most of your parmesan, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Tip your pasta into the pan along with a ladle of pasta water. Stir until your sauce clings to your pasta beautifully.
Spoon your pasta into bowls and sprinkle with a little parmesan, black pepper and olive oil. Serve and enjoy.

name: Sophie's Pasta with Chickpeas
description: The best meals involve the double carb of Napolina macaroni and chickpeas. A beautiful one-pot dish packed with tonnes of rustic flavour.
instructions: Finely dice your onion, carrot and celery.
Cut a cross on the skin of your tomatoes, then place in a bowl of boiling water for one minute. Once cool enough to handle, peel back the skins. Cut into quarters.
Add your pancetta to a large heavy-bottomed casserole dish and fry until crisp.
Tip your onion, carrot and celery. Cook for 15 mins more until your pancetta has rendered its fat and become crispy, and your soffritto is soft.
Add your Napolina Tomato Purée and cook out for a minute before adding your quartered tomatoes. Cook for 5 mins until the tomatoes are breaking down and becoming jammy.
Pour your chickpeas into the pan and add 1 litre of water. Chuck in your rosemary sprig and parmesan rind, then simmer for 20 mins.
Remove the parmesan rind and rosemary sprig. Pour ⅓ of the liquid into a blender and blitz until smooth. Return the liquid to the pan.
Season the liquid to taste with salt and pepper. Add your macaroni and cook for 8 mins more, stirring to stop it from sticking and adding more water where necessary.
Portion up into bowls, then sprinkle with a little more parmesan and a drizzle of Napolina Extra Virgin Olive Oil. Serve.

name: Sore Throat Soother
description: This syrup is the ideal home remedy for when you’re fighting off a cold, with immune-boosting honey, ginger and garlic. Dissolve it into boiling water for a soothing hot drink or eat it directly from the jar. Feel better soon Mob.
instructions: Peel and quarter the shallot. Peel and gently bash the garlic and thinly slice the ginger.
Add all of the ingredients to a saucepan with ½ of the honey. Place over a medium heat and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer then leave for 6-7 mins to soften the ingredients and melt the honey.
Take it off the heat and let it cool down a little then stir through the remaining honey.
Store in an airtight jar in the fridge for up to 1 month. Dissolve 1 tbsp of the mixture in a mug of hot water or broth for a soothing hot drink, or eat it directly from the jar.

name: Sour Cherry Pie
description: You can make this classic pie dessert using fresh or frozen sour cherries. It’s a real winner. Perfect served warm with ice cream.
instructions: Start by making the pastry base. Cut cold butter into small 2cm pieces and set aside. Add the flour, salt and sugar to the bowl of a stand mixer with a paddle attachment, and stir to combine.

Add the butter and beat very gently, just enough to coat the flour with the butter, until mostly pea-sized pieces of butter remain; they can be a little uneven in size but no huge bits. Don’t over-beat the mixture. If doing by hand, work quickly with cold, dry hands, rubbing the butter into the flour mix between thumb and fingers.
Combine the water, vinegar and ice in a small bowl. Gradually add this to the flour mix, a tbsp at a time, with the mixer on low, until it just comes together into a ball.
Split the dough into two pieces, flatten each into a disk, wrap in clingfilm and rest in the fridge for an hour (or preferably overnight – it will last for 3 days if wrapped airtight).

Once rested, remove ½ the pastry from the fridge and leave for about 5 mins or until it’s just soft enough to roll, but still very firm. Roll the piece out on a clean floured surface until it’s large enough to line a 25 cm pie dish then carefully lift the pastry over the rolling pin and into the dish. Return the lined pan to the fridge to rest for at least another hour.

Meanwhile, make the filling. Add the cherries, lemon juice, granulated sugar, brown sugar, cornflour, mixed spice, salt to a large mixing bowl and stir to combine. Set aside to soak for 1hr. Then, strain the mixture through a sieve into a saucepan and set the sieve of cherries aisde. Set the saucepan with the cherry liquid over a medium heat and cook until the liquid becomes thick and starts bubbling, 5-6 mins. Remove from the heat, let cool down to room temperature and whisk ½ the eggs in.
When the pastry has almost finished resting, heat the oven to 190°C.

To make the lattice pastry top, remove the remaining chilled dough from the fridge and roll it out to a 12 inch circle on a lightly floured surface. Cut the dough into ½ inch strips using a sharp knife (12 strips per pie).
Fill the rested pastry-lined pie dish with the filling.

Arrange ½ the dough strips across the pie top, leaving about a ½ inch of space between each strip. Now weave the strips: place the remaining strips perpendicular to the first set, weaving them over and under the existing strips. Try to keep the strips evenly spaced so you have a symmetrical pattern. Trim any excess dough and press the edges of the lattice strips to the sides of the bottom crust, sealing them together.
Whisk the remaining egg with the water to make an egg wash. Brush the pastry with the egg wash and dust with the demerara sugar.
Bake in the preheated oven, on the lowest shelf for 50-60 mins, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or at room temperature with cream.

name: Sourdough Crumpets
description: You will not believe how easy it is to make your own crumpets. So squidgy. Perfect with a big knob of salted butter. Recipe by MOB Contributor Thomas Colson.
instructions: In a medium bowl, mix together all the ingredients. The batter should be slightly thicker than pancake mixture.
Place your frying pan on a very low heat.
Place a lightly oiled egg ring into your frying pan.
Pour in the mixture until the egg ring is about half full.

When the bubbles have formed on the crumpets, and when the surface has dried out (at least 6 minutes) gently pull up the egg rings and let the crumpets drop back into the pan, then set aside the egg rings.
Flip the crumpet around and cook the top for 5 minutes until golden brown.
Repeat this with all the crumpets. Serve and enjoy with marmite or honey!

name: South Indian Coconut Prawn Curry Pasta
description: This recipe is a curry/pasta fusion that uses all of the best ingredients. It's spicy, creamy, and nourishing.
keywords: south indian coconut prawn curry pasta
instructions: Finely chop the onion, grate the garlic and ginger, slit the green chillies in half, halve the cherry tomatoes and chop the coriander. Set everything aside.

Heat the coconut oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add the cumin seeds, chopped onion, lemongrass and curry leaves. Cook for 5-7 mins until the onion is soft and translucent.
Meanwhile, peel and devein the prawns by cutting a small incision down the back and removing the grit line with a fork.

Add the garlic and ginger to the pan and cook for 2-3 mins until fragrant. Add the prawns, turmeric and a pinch of salt, then cook for 30 seconds before adding the coconut milk. Simmer the sauce for 3 mins, then remove the prawns with a slotted spoon. Set the sauce aside while you cook the pasta.

Cook the pasta in a large pot of salted water until al dente. Using tongs, transfer the cooked pasta to the curry sauce and heat over a medium-high heat for 3-4 mins. Return the prawns to the pan along with the green chillies, tomatoes and fish sauce. Squeeze in the lime juice. Cook for a final 3 mins, ensuring the prawns are fully cooked through and the pasta has absorbed most of the curry sauce.
Finish with the chopped coriander and chilli oil, just before serving.

name: Soy & Black Vinegar Braised Chinese Cabbage
description: This Chinese cabbage recipe is a symphony of flavours, offering spicy, sweet, sour, and salty notes in every bite. Braised with soy sauce and black vinegar, the cabbage absorbs the robust and tangy elements, making it a standout dish. Perfect for stir-frying or serving as a main course, this recipe brings the essence of Chinese cuisine to your table. Pair it with steamed rice or noodles to soak up the delicious sauce, or add it to a hot pot for a comforting meal. Whether you're a fan of Sichuan peppercorns or the subtle heat of chilli crisp, this dish can be adjusted to suit your taste. Ideal for a quick dinner, the Chinese cabbage recipe can also be enhanced with green onions, garlic, and ginger for extra depth
keywords: Soy & Black Vinegar Braised Chinese Cabbage Recipe
instructions: Cut the cabbage in half lengthways, then in half lengthways again. Cut the cabbage into 6cm chunky pieces. Peel and finely chop the garlic, then peel and finely chop the ginger.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large, deep frying pan or wok set over a high heat. Add the cabbage and fry for 4-5 mins, tossing regularly until charred and beginning to soften.
Turn the heat to low and add the garlic, ginger, cumin seeds, Sichuan peppercorns and chilli flakes. Toss for 2 mins until smelling amazing.
Pour in the chicken stock, soy sauce, vinegar and sugar and simmer away gently for 30 mins until the cabbage is meltingly tender.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the peanuts or cashews and finely chop the chives.
To serve, scatter the nuts and chives over the cabbage.

name: Soy Baked Chicken with Garlic Rice
description: Honey and soy-baked chicken thighs with a garlicky one-pot chicken rice and a quick citrus coriander salad. A fuss-free midweek staple inspired by Hainanese chicken.
keywords: Soy Baked Chicken with Garlic Rice
instructions: Get all the ingredients for the chicken, except the sesame seeds, into a large bowl. Give everything a good mix, making sure the chicken is thoroughly coated, then pop in the fridge to marinate for at least 30 mins.
Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with tin foil.
Put the marinated chicken on the tray, skin side up, and sprinkle over the sesame seeds. Bake in the oven for 20 mins then remove and set aside to rest for 5 mins.

Meanwhile, rinse the rice two or three times until the water runs clear then drain. Mince the garlic and ginger and cut the spring onions into thirds. Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a small saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Add the garlic, ginger and spring onion and sauté for 1-2 mins until fragrant but not browned.

Add the drained rice to the same pan and toast for 1 minute. Pour in the chicken stock and a large pinch of salt. Pop the lid on, turn the heat to high and bring to a boil. Once boiling, immediately turn the heat down to the lowest setting and cook, with the lid on, for 18 mins. Remove the pan from the heat and set aside until ready to serve.
For the salad, roughly chop the coriander and thinly slice the cucumber and red onion. Add to a bowl along with the juice of the lime and the sesame oil and mix to combine.

When ready to serve, chop the chicken into strips. Divide the rice between plates and top with the sliced chicken, spooning over any leftover juices from the oven tray. Serve with a handful of the salad.

name: Soy Butter Aubergine Noodles
description: Easy, breezy, umami noodles. This is a great recipe you can get on the table in 30 minutes.
instructions: Cut the aubergine in half lengthways, then into 4 long batons. Then slice in half again through the belly to make stubby batons. Add to a bowl with a good pinch of salt, massage and set aside.
Boil a pot of salted water and cook egg noodles as instructed. Strain the cooked noodles and reserve a cup of noodle water on the side.
Finely slice the garlic and spring onions, reserving the spring onion greens for garnish, then squeeze out any excess water from the aubergines with your hands and set aside.

Bring a large pan to medium high heat, add a drizzle of oil, then add aubergines straight to the pan and cook for 2 mins, or until slightly blackened. Use a spatula to release any excess liquid, flip and repeat on the other side.

Add a ladle of noodle water to the pan to cook the aubergines for 1 min, then reduce the heat to low. Add in neutral oil followed by your butter, garlic, and spring onions. Cook for 2 mins or until lightly golden and aromatic.

Then add white wine vinegar, soy sauce, dark soy sauce and toss well, then cook for 1 min and add the egg noodles, tossing for 1 min or until glossy. Add a small ladle of noodle water if needed and toss again until glossy, then turn off the heat.
Zest the lemon, and season with a squeeze of the juice, add black pepper, chilli flakes, sesame seeds, and all the spring onion greens, serve.

name: Soy Garlic Rice
description: This umami-rich garlicky rice is a great base for so many dishes, top with your favourite protein, side and dressing and you've got a delicious make-ahead meal.
instructions: Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear. Roughly chop the shallots into chunks and peel the garlic cloves. Throw both into a food processor and pulse until finely chopped (or finely chop by hand).

Pop a medium sized saucepan over a medium heat and add the butter. Once melted, throw in the shallot and garlic mix and cook for 10-12 mins until caramelised. Add the salt and sugar and cook for a further minute. Deglaze the pan with the dark soy sauce, scraping up any browned bits on the bottom.

Tip in the washed rice followed by the chicken stock. Bring to the boil then pop the lid on and reduce the heat to as low as possible. Cook for 12 mins, then turn the heat off and let sit for 15 mins.
Divide the rice between Tupperware containers and top with your favourite protein, side and dressing and pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Soy Glazed Chicken, Charred Corn & Crispy Rice
description: Sticky soy chicken, sweet charred corn, and golden crispy rice, finished with fresh herbs and a squeeze of lime. This disappeared fast in the Mob kitchen, and it’s easy to see why. Serious crunch, bold savoury-sweet flavour, and a properly satisfying hit in every bite.
keywords: soy chicken & charred corn crispy rice
instructions: Add the chicken thighs to a bowl with the Chinese dark soy sauce and soy sauce, mixing well and then set aside to marinate for a few mins while you get on with the rest of the prep.
Dice the butter and set aside for the rice later. Slice the kernels from the corn cob, thinly slice the spring onions and coriander stems and pick the leaves ready for your salad.

Place a frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the corn and cook for a few mins until starting to char. Transfer to a bowl and leave to cool slightly, then toss with the chopped spring onions and coriander stems and leaves.

Keep the empty pan over the heat and turn it down to medium. Add a drizzle of olive oil, then add the chicken and cook for 7-10 mins, turning halfway, until cooked through and nicely charred. Remove from the heat, cover with a lid and set aside while you get on with the rice.

In another non-stick frying pan, over a medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the cooked rice in one even layer. Scatter the diced butter over the top, cover and cook undisturbed for 7-10 mins, until deeply golden and crispy on the bottom.
Once the rice is ready, quickly reheat the chicken then remove from the heat and toss through the honey so it goes all glossy and sticky.
To serve, flip and break up the crispy rice and divide between plates. Slice the chicken and pile it on top with the charred corn salad. Finish with a squeeze of lime, and an extra wedge on the side.

name: Soy Glazed Grilled Fish Bowl
description: I will always order unagi on a nigiri menu: the buttery melt-in-your-mouth fish glazed with the perfect sweet and savoury sauce is unmatched. I've taken inspo from that perfect bite, to make a whole dish of it. And yes, I’m not using eel, because that is actually a hard ingredient to find. Instead I use sea bass, but this could easily be swapped for salmon, cod or any fish you like.
keywords: Soy Glazed Grilled Fish Bowl recipe
instructions: Wash the sushi rice until the water runs clear. Add it into a saucepan along with the water. Place onto high heat and let it come to the boil. Once boiling, cover and turn the heat down to low, cook for 12 mins. Then turn the heat off and leave it covered, undisturbed for another 10 mins.

Meanwhile, add all the sauce ingredients into a small pan. Whisk together and place onto medium-high heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-8 mins until the sauce has thickened and coats the back of a spoon. Remove from the heat and set aside – the sauce will thicken as it cools.
Meanwhile, line a baking tray with foil and grease it. Season the sea bass fillets and transfer them onto the tray, skin side down. Set aside. Preheat the grill to medium-high.

For the salad, thinly slice or mandolin the cucumber and place into a bowl. Toss with a sprinkling of salt and set aside for 5-10 mins. Then, wash and squeeze the extra juice out of the cucumbers, and place back into the bowl with the rice vinegar, sugar, and sesame seeds. Toss together, taste and season with salt, if needed. Defrost the edamame and toss through the salad.

Slide the fish under the grill and cook for 2-3 mins, until the fish is still raw but starting to turn opaque. Brush a layer of the sauce onto the top of the fish and slide under the grill for another 30-60 secs until caramelised. Brush another layer of sauce and continue this process until the fish is fully cooked (it should only need 4-6 mins in total for thin fillets). If the sauce is starting to burn before the fish is finished cooking, turn the grill down to medium and continue the process.
Fluff the rice and serve into bowls. Top with the grilled fish and salad. Drizzle over any remaining sauce and serve with crispy seaweed, if desired.

name: Soy Poached Chicken & Sesame Sauce
description: A delicate, perfectly balanced plate of food where every ingredients plays its part.
keywords: Soy Poached Chicken & Sesame Sauce recipe
instructions: Pop the chicken into a large pot and cover with cold water or if you’ve got it, chicken stock. Chunk up the spring onions and drop those in along with the roughly chopped ginger, smashed garlic cloves and the soy sauce.
Set over a high heat and bring to a rolling boil. Remove from the heat, add a lid and set aside for 90 mins. The residual heat will fully poach the chicken.

For the sesame sauce, pop the sugar, vinegar, tahini and soy sauce into a blender or bowl and whizz together until smooth. Add icy cold water as needed to loosen, until you have a creamy sauce. Finish with the sesame seeds and set aside.

To cook the rice, rinse it well with cold water until most of the starch has been washed away. Drain and pop into a saucepan with the salt, sugar and vinegar. Cover with 480ml of the chicken cooking liquid, add a lid and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 8-10 mins, or until the rice is full cooked and the liquid has been absorbed. Remove from the heat and allow to rest for 10 mins.
Cut the cucumber into thin slices and finely chop the spring onions. Remove the meat from the chicken, you can carve or shred, up to you!
Return the shredded/carved chicken to the broth. Set the pan over a medium heat for 5-10 mins until warmed through.

Divide the rice between bowls, top with some chicken, a handful each of cucumber and spring onion and a good few ladles of the warm chicken cooking liquid. Add a spoon of soy and a generous spoonful of the sesame sauce.
Get stuck in.

name: Soy Sauce Chicken & Fudgy Eggs with Spring Onion Ginger Oil
description: A simple and saucy chicken recipe. The spring onion ginger oil adds a lovely flavour.
keywords: Soy Sauce Chicken & Fudgy Eggs With Spring Onion Ginger Oil
Soy Sauce Chicken & Fudgy Eggs With Spring Onion Ginger Oil recipe
instructions: Boil a full kettle of water. Place the chicken legs into a large rimmed dish or pan, skin-side up. Pour the boiling kettle water over the chicken skin – it will immediately tighten the skin. Leave it to soak for 1 min, then drain, pat dry with kitchen paper and pour over the dark soy sauce. Set aside in the fridge.
Slice the ginger. Slice the entire garlic bulb in half (keep the skin on). Quarter the shallots and remove the skin. Cut the spring onions into chunks.

Add a splash of oil to a medium-sized saucepan or casserole dish set over a high heat. Add the aromatics (make sure the garlic bulbs are face down) and cook for 1 min or until fragrant. Now add the rice wine, followed by the remaining braising liquid ingredients and bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to the lowest fire. Ladle the sauce over the chicken for 2 mins, then add a lid and leave it to cook for 15 mins. Turn the heat off to leave it to steam for 30 mins, without opening the lid.

Meanwhile, boil a small pot of water, add the eggs once boiling and cook for 6 mins, then plunge into a bowl of very cold tap water. Lightly crack the shells and leave in the water until the eggs have cooled. Peel the eggs once cooled (they will be fragile, so peel delicately) and set aside. Slice the tofu into squares and set aside.

For the scallion ginger oil, first finely dice the spring onions and use a microplane or box grater to grate the ginger. Add the oil and minced ginger to a small pan set over a high heat. Cook for 30 seconds just until the ginger gets lightly golden, then add all the spring onions, mix well and turn the heat off. Add all the remaining ingredients and set aside in a small bowl.
Combine the cornstarch slurry ingredients in a small bowl.

Now remove the rested chicken legs onto a plate and use a sieve to remove all the aromatics. Squeeze the garlic bulbs, releasing the cloves back into the sauce. Add in the eggs and tofu and bring to a boil. Use your finger to give the cornstarch slurry a mix and pour half into the sauce, then mix for 1 min. Only add more if it needs more thickening – it should be a delicate gravy-like texture. Then turn the heat off.
Serve the chicken over the rice, with the eggs and tofu. Pour a ladle of sauce over the chicken, then serve with a few tsp ginger scallion oil all over the chicken and rice.

name: Soy Sauce Chicken Noodles
description: Super easy chicken thighs braised in caramelised sweet soy sauce. Shredded off the bone on top of noodles, with a rich gravy made from the braising liquid. Paired with a tangy carrot and beansprout salad.
instructions: Put the chicken in a bowl, pour in ⅗ of the dark soy sauce and massage until coated well.

Add the rock sugar and equal parts water to a saucepan. Heat over a medium heat and slowly stir to dissolve. Once dissolved, slowly stir until the water has evaporated. Keep stirring until the sugar has caramelised into a darkish brown colour – this should take 5-7 mins. Once caramelised, immediately pour in the water (the full quantity listed in the ingredients).

Add half of the spring onions, the garlic cloves, ginger (slightly smashed), star anise, cinnamon stick, the rest of the dark soy sauce, ⅗ of the light soy sauce, MSG and a generous pinch of salt. Put the lid on and bring to the boil over a high heat. Once boiling, gently drop in the chicken and pour in the remaining sauce from the bowl. Put the lid on, lower the heat to medium and cook for 15 mins.
Turn the heat off and let sit for a further 30 mins. After which, remove the chicken to a plate to cool. Meanwhile, make the salad.
Thinly slice the remaining spring onion top and set aside. Cut the carrot diagonally into discs, lay the discs flat and slice into thin matchsticks, julienne-stlye.

Bring a pot of water to the boil, add the carrot and beansprouts, cook for 30 seconds then remove to a bowl. Add the sliced spring onion, ½ of the remaining light soy sauce, rice vinegar and chilli oil to the bowl. Toss to combine and set aside. Turn the heat off the saucepan and keep for later use.

Remove the aromatics from the sauce (spring onion, garlic, ginger, star anise, cinnamon) and turn the heat to high. Mix the cornstarch with equal parts water to make a slurry. Once boiling, turn the heat off the pan and slowly pour in the slurry whilst stirring to thicken the sauce.

Once the chicken has cooled, use a fork to shred the meat off the bone. Discard the bones. Bring the pan used for the beansprouts back to the boil and cook the noodles following pack instructions. Drain the noodles, and add back to the pan along with the sesame oil and the rest of the light soy sauce. Mix well to coat.
Plate the noodles, add the shredded chicken on top and generously pour over the thickened sauce. Finish with some finely sliced chives, if you like. Add a handful of salad to the side.

name: Soy Sticky Pork Belly Recipe
description: Ore Oduba's sticky pork belly, slow-cooked until it's properly falling apart, then lacquered in a sweet, salty soy and honey glaze. Serve it over fluffy rice that soaks up every last bit of that sauce.
instructions: Slice your onions, spring onions, ginger and garlic. Cut the pork belly into roughly 1-inch cubes.

Bring 1 litre of water to a boil. Once it’s simmering, add the pork, spring onion, onion, ginger, and garlic, and cook for 3-4 minutes. Remove the pork and aromatics from the pan and drain on a plate lined with a paper towel.
Clean and dry the pot, then return it to high heat and add the olive oil. Return the pork to the pan and cook until browned. The oil may pop and splatter, so be careful.

Add the brown sugar, then reduce the heat to low. Stir continuously until the sugar has melted and the pork is evenly coated in a sticky caramel. Immediately add the soy sauces and rice wine, stirring continuously for about 10 minutes more, or until the liquid has reduced to a thick glaze.

Add the remaining 250ml of water. Stir and simmer for about 45 minutes. Make sure the mixture is at a low simmer, not boiling. Stir every 10 minutes or so, adding more water if the pot is getting dry.
Meanwhile, cut the end off the pak choi to separate your leaves. Steam pak choi for 5-6 minutes so the leaves are wilted but the stalk retains its crunch.
Lift the lid off the pork - the sauce should coat the pork in a very thick glaze. If it is too runny, continue to stir, uncovered, until the liquid has reduced and thickened.
Serve pork immediately over a bowl of rice and sprinkle with spring onions. Lay your pak choi leaves on the side and eat up.

name: Soy-Glazed Chicken, Rhubarb Slaw & Crispy Rice
description: Sticky chicken thighs glazed with soy sauce and honey, shatteringly crispy jasmine rice and tangy rhubarb, all tossed in a punchy fish sauce and bird's-eye chilli dressing. A proper weeknight banger that's on the table in 30 mins.
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Make the dressing for the slaw first. Add the bird's-eye chillies and garlic to a pestle and mortar and bash until a paste forms. Squeeze in the juice of one lime, add the fish sauce and honey, and stir to combine. Taste and adjust with more lime juice, honey or fish sauce as needed.

Add the chicken thighs to a bowl with the dark soy sauce and honey, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat. Line a baking tray with foil and lay the chicken on top with the marinade. Slide under the grill for 10-15 mins, until fully cooked through. If the chicken is charring too quickly, lower the tray or cover loosely with foil.

Meanwhile, place a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Add the olive oil and butter. Once foaming, add the cooked rice and cook for 5-6 mins, tossing now and then, until crispy and starting to char in places, try to keep it in little clusters if you can. Tip into a large bowl.
Trim and thinly slice the rhubarb, finely mince the lemongrass, cut the carrots into thin matchsticks, roughly chop the peanuts and roughly chop the coriander, stalks and all.

Add the rhubarb, lemongrass, carrots, coriander and peanuts to the bowl with the crispy rice. Pour over the dressing and toss everything together. Divide between plates and top with the grilled chicken.

name: Spaghetti & Meatballs In 'Nduja Sauce
description: A Mob take on spaghetti and meatballs. Sausage meat makes the meatballs extra juicy. With the ‘nduja sauce, it’s a straight 10/10.
instructions: Squeeze the sausages from their skins into a large bowl. Dump in the beef mince and finely grate in the onion. Season generously with salt and black pepper, mix together then use your hands to shape into large meatballs. Place on a baking sheet.
Get a large non-stick frying pan over a medium–high heat. Drizzle in some olive oil and fry the meatballs for 5–6 minutes, in batches if you need to, until evenly browned. Set aside on a tray.

Reduce the heat to low. Finely chop the remaining onion, scrape into the pan, along with a drizzle more oil if needed. Turn up the heat to medium, fry, stirring occasionally, until soft. Finely chop the garlic.

Add the garlic and tear the 'nduja into the pan. Fry, smooshing with the back of your spoon to break it up until the 'nduja is pretty much melted. Tip in the chopped tomatoes along with half a tin of water. Bring the sauce to the boil, lower the heat and simmer away while you cook the spaghetti. Season with salt and black pepper.
Get a large saucepan of salted water on to boil, then drop in the spaghetti. Cook for a minute less than the packet instructions say to.
Add the meatballs back to the tomato sauce. Simmer for 5 mins, then flip each one over and continue to cook until the pasta is done.

When the pasta is cooked, drain in a sieve or colander but save a half of a mugful of the cooking water. Tip the pasta back into the saucepan. Push all the meatballs to one side and spoon the sauce into the spaghetti. Toss together, adding a little pasta water to create a silky sauce.
Divide the pasta and sauce between four bowls. Top each with five meatballs, tear over the basil and serve with a hunk of Parmesan on the side ready for grating. Heaven.

name: Spaghetti & Meatballs with Hidden Veg Sauce
description: A big comforting bowl of spaghetti & meatballs is always a winner, this one’s loaded with hidden veg and makes a great freezer stash. Even the fussy ones will love it.
keywords: Spaghetti & Meatballs with Hidden Veg Sauce
Spaghetti & Meatballs with Hidden Veg Sauce recipe
instructions: Grate half the onion into a bowl. Add the breadcrumbs and mix until fully hydrated. If you're using bread, blitz it into crumbs first. Chop the basil stalks, if using, and add to the breadcrumbs and onion mixture.

Finely chop the rest of the onion, the celery, carrot and garlic. No need to peel the carrots! Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large lidded saucepan over a medium heat. Add add the onion, celery, carrot and garlic, sweating it down for about 10 mins until softened.

In the meantime, chop the courgette into small chunks. Add to the pan and cook for another 5 mins. Tip in the chopped tomatoes and water, season with salt and pepper, then bring to the boil. Turn the heat down and simmer for 15 mins. Let it cool slightly, then blitz until smooth using a blender or stick blender. Return the sauce to the pan on the lowest heat.

Back to the meatballs! Add the beef mince to a large bowl with the breadcrumb mix, egg, half the Parmesan, a pinch of salt & pepper, and the basil stalks. Mix everything with your hands until fully combined, then roll into golf ball-sized meatballs.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Fry the meatballs in batches for 8–10 mins until golden on all sides.
Get the spaghetti on to cook in a large pan of salted water following pack instructions. Drain, saving a splash of the cooking water.
Add the spaghetti to the sauce and toss together. Use the reserved water to loosen the sauce if needed,it should be glossy and cling to the pasta. Tear in the basil leaves, if using.
Serve up the pasta, top with the golden meatballs, the rest of the Parmesan, and a final hit of basil if you fancy.

name: Spaghetti Alla Nerano
description: A favourite from the bay of Nerano, this is a perfect example of making simple ingredients shine. Traditionally this pasta is made with Provolone del Monaco, but it’s hard to find outside of the region. The best alternative is an equal mix of Parmesan and pecorino.
instructions: Finely slice the courgettes into rounds about 3mm thick (this is much easier and faster with a mandoline).
Heat the olive oil in a high-sided pan to 170°C. You can test this by throwing in a round of courgette – it should sizzle immediately.

Fry all of the courgettes in batches until it’s deep golden brown, placing the fried courgettes onto a large paper towel-lined baking tray as you go. Once they're all fried, transfer to a bowl, toss with a tsp of salt and place into the fridge. You can skip the rest in the fridge and this will still be delicious, but leaving them for a few hours, or even better overnight, will really deepen the flavour of the courgettes. It’s also a great way to get ahead the day before.
Place a large frying pan over a low heat and add the courgette, a quarter of the butter and 2 tbsp of water. Warm gently, stirring occasionally.

Put the spaghetti on to boil in lightly-salted water. Once the pasta is still nice and al dente, transfer to the pan with the courgettes along with 100ml of the cooking water. Tear in the basil leaves, add the remaining butter and stir vigorously.
Add most of the cheese (save 2 tbsp for garnish) then continue stirring to make a creamy, glossy sauce that coats the pasta.
Plate up and top with the cheese.

name: Spaghetti All’assassina
description: This unusual pasta dish from Bari in Puglia is made by cooking the pasta and spicy sauce together in a frying pan. Don’t be afraid to let it really burn on the edges and get crispy.
instructions: Heat a small saucepan over a medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil and the tomato purée and cook for a minute. Add the water and ½ the salt and mix to combine. Bring to a boil then turn off the heat and set aside. This is your tomato broth.

Meanwhile, crush the garlic. Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large frying pan (ideally cast iron) set over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and sizzle for 30 seconds, then add the tinned tomatoes. Bring to a simmer and stir in the remaining salt.

Place the spaghetti directly on top of the sauce, then ladle in a quarter of the tomato broth. As the broth simmers and the pasta cooks, gently move it around a bit with a spoon. You want to keep adding broth as it reduces, allowing the pasta to cook but also to catch in places and even burn on the edges.

Once the pasta is al dente, stop adding broth and let the spaghetti fry and toast slightly in the sauce, if you need to. This is an observational process; you’ll have to keep an eye on it and adjust to your liking.

Ultimately, you want to end up with quite a ‘tight’ tomato sauce, and pasta which is cooked through, crispy and charred in places. Serve on warm plates with a drizzle of good olive oil and an extra pinch of chilli, if you like.

name: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: The key to the ultimate spaghetti bolognese is milk. A generous glug of the stuff tenderises the meat and evens out the acidity of the tomatoes.
keywords: easy toad in the hole recipe
chorizo toad in the hole recipe
instructions: Get a large saucepan over a medium heat and drizzle in some olive oil. Tip in the pancetta and fry until crisp, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile finely chop the onions, carrot, celery and garlic. Add to the pan along with a further drizzle of olive oil and fry for 8–10 mins until soft.
Turn up the heat to high and tip in the beef mince. Use the back of your spoon to break the mince up and fry until brown.

Pour in the red wine and let it bubble away over the high heat until reduced by half. Pour in the stock and milk followed by the plum tomatoes. Season well with black pepper and add the bay leaves. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to a low simmer, cover and cook for 1 1⁄2 hours.
Check it every 20 mins or so and give it a good stir. If it is catching on the pan, just add a splash of water.

After 1 1⁄2 hours, remove the lid and simmer for 30 minutes. Season to taste, remove from the heat and leave with the lid on for 15 minutes. The sauce is even better made the day before and then reheated.
In this time, get your pasta on. Cook in a large pan of boiling salted water for 1 min less than the packet instructions say. Drain in a colander when ready.
Toss your pasta through the bolognese, then pile it into four bowls. Serve with lots of Parmesan grated over the top and tuck in!

name: Spaghetti Hoops On Toast
description: Throwing it back to this after school fave, made with just one pan and a few ingredients. It’s comfort on a plate. Who doesn't love a double carb situation?
instructions: Mince the garlic, lightly crush the fennel seeds in a pestle and mortar and finely chop the fresh oregano.
Grate the tomatoes and discard the skin.
Heat butter and a drizzle of olive oil in a large/deep non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add in the garlic, crushed fennel seeds, fresh oregano and chili flakes to fry for 1 min.
Then stir in the tomato purée, freshly grated tomatoes and paprika, season with salt and cook for 4 mins.
Meanwhile, warm up your veg stock in a saucepan.
Add the dried pasta to the tomato pan along with the stock and sugar. Simmer for around 20 min stirring occasionally to stop the pasta from sticking.
Thickly slice, toast and butter your bread just before serving.
Pile the hoops on top of your toast and grate over your favourite cheese.

name: Spaghetti Squash & Confit Tomatoes with Tomato Oil Pesto
description: Spaghetti squash is a natural wonder, turning into genuinely realistic noodles once cooked. Here it’s paired with bold with bold, bright, invigorating flavours in a meal that’s mostly hands-free to make.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Line a baking sheet with baking paper.

Wash and dry the squash, then use your largest knife to cut it in half, stem to tip. Scoop out the seeds and stringy flesh in the middle (we’re not using these but you could arrange them around the squash when roasting, season and save them for snacking another time).

Drizzle the cut surface of the squash with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, sprinkle with salt, then place cut-side down on the parchment paper. Bake for 35-40 mins, until the juices are seeping out the bottom and you can leave a finger dent in the skin when you press it. Carefully turn the squash over and leave to steam for 5 mins.

While the squash is cooking, arrange the tomatoes in a roasting tin – we want them to snuggly fit, 1-2 layers deep. Cut the garlic bulb in half and nestle the halves among the tomatoes, cut side down. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil, then scatter over the sugar and sea salt. Give the tray a shuffle and roast in the hot oven for 25-30 mins.
When the squash and tomatoes are cooked, remove them from the oven, flip the squash over so it’s cut-side up and set both aside to cool a little.

While you wait, add the basil, Parmesan and pine nuts to a blender or food processor. Squeeze in the flesh from ¾ of the roasted garlic cloves (discarding the skins) and 6 tbsp of the tomato cooking juices. Whizz to a purée, adding a little more olive oil or tomato cooking juices if needed.

Season the squash very generously with salt and black pepper. Scoop a large amount onto each plate, then gently use a fork to scrape, separate and fluff the flesh into spaghetti-like strands. Grate a little extra Parmesan over the top, then ladle confit tomatoes onto the plate, and add a really generous spoonful or two of the basil pesto.

name: Spaghetti Vongole
description: Clams, Parsley, Tomatoes. It’s an absolute classic. The perfect date night meal.
instructions: Finely slice cloves of garlic.
Get a large saucepan on the heat and splash in some olive oil. Add your garlic and a tsp of crushed chillies. Fry for about 40 seconds and add your cherry tomatoes.
Add your spaghetti to a large pan of boiling water.
After 2 minutes, add your clams to the sauce pan and pour in your wine. Bring to the boil and cover with a lid.
Cook for about 5 minutes, until all the clams have opened up. Add a large handful of chopped parsley.
Remove the pasta from the heat and sieve. Pour it into the sauce. Mix it around, drizzle over some olive oil and serve! Enjoy!

name: Spaghetti With ‘Nduja, Runner Beans & Lemon
description: Al dente spaghetti swaddled around a spicy mix of 'nduja and runner beans. This is a pasta recipe to remember.
instructions: Put the spaghetti in a large pan of boiling salted water and cook for 2 mins less than the packet instructions say.

While the spaghetti is cooking, finely dice the onion and add to a pan with the ‘nduja, tomato purée, zest of the lemon and peeled clove of garlic. Place over a medium low heat, stir occasionally and allow the onion to cook in the fat from the ‘nduja without browning. Add some pasta cooking water, remove the garlic and turn off the heat while you wait for the pasta to finish cooking.
Top and tail and the beans and cut them into roughly two-inch lengths. Once the pasta is cooked but still al dente, add the beans to the boiling water with the pasta.

Drain the pasta and beans (reserving a mug of the cooking water) and transfer into the pan with the onion, place back over a medium heat. Tear in the basil leaves, squeeze in the lemon juice and toss well, adding the reserved water as you go to make it nice and saucy. Taste and add salt or more lemon if needed.
Plate up and top with pecorino or Parmesan, black pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Spaghetti with Spicy Tomato & Pepper Sauce
description: A taste of summer in the middle of winter, this super simple sauce uses jarred tomatoes and peppers to bring you sunny vibes all year round. Tangy tomatoes and sweet peppers with a good kick of chilli, tossed through spaghetti. It's exactly what you need for a quick, fresh midweek meal.
keywords: tomato garlic chilli pasta sauce recipe
instructions: Grab a blender, drain the peppers and add them along with the tomatoes, then whizz until almost smooth.
Place a big frying pan over a medium low heat, add the olive oil and then either very finely chop, crush or grate your garlic cloves and add them.

Cook the garlic very gently in the oil until fragrant but not coloured (about 2 mins), add the chilli and cook for another 30 seconds, then pour in the pepper and tomato mix and add a big pinch of salt.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for about 15 mins. While the sauce bubbles away gently, cook your spaghetti in a big pan of well salted water until al dente.

Transfer the pasta to the pan with the tomato and pepper sauce and mix it really well so that the spaghetti is well coated and glossy. Turn off the heat, add about 1/3rd of your grated cheese and mix gently until the cheese has melted into the sauce. You might need to loosen it up with a splash of pasta water.
Taste now and add salt if needed, then plate up into warm bowls and top with the remaining cheese and some black pepper.

name: Spanakopita
description: This is my recipe for the perfect spanakopita, a spinach pie. As close to the ones we eat at home in Cyprus as possible, it's a real treat. #ad
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Strip the leaves from the cavolo nero and chard and discard the stems. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and one by one, blanch the greens for a minute before refreshing in ice water. Repeat with the rocket and spinach. Once iced, squeeze as much water as possible from the greens before finely chopping. Set aside.
