Finely dice the onions and finely grate the garlic cloves. Set a large pot over a medium-high heat and add plenty of olive oil. Once hot, drop in the onion, add a pinch of salt and cook for 3-4 mins or until translucent. Add the garlic, stir through the hot oil and then tip in the chopped greens. Cook for a minute, stirring everything together and then remove from the heat. Add the zest and juice of the lemons before finely chopping the herbs and getting them in there too. Crumble in the feta and mix everything together, seasoning to taste.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan.

Line a large baking sheet with parchment and lay out your first sheet of filo, brush with butter, and then lay another down, sightly overlapping. Repeat the process, brushing each sheet with butter until you have roughly 8 sheets of filo down. Add your filling to the centre and shape into a rough dome. Fold over the filo to encase the filling, ruffling the excess at the top of the pie. Brush with more butter and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Slide into the oven and bake for 30-40 minutes or until a rich golden brown and crisp. Allow the pie to rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Serve with a tomato salad and get stuck in.

name: Spanakopita Breakfast Wraps
description: These crispy, cheesy breakfast wraps are inspired by the classic Greek spanakopita, but we've twisted them into the perfect grab-and-go brekkie.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C fan. Blitz the cottage cheese in a blender until smooth. Crack all the eggs (but one) into a large bowl and whisk well. Fold through the blended cottage cheese and season generously with salt and pepper.
Separate the last egg – whisk the white and set aside for later. Add the yolk into the egg mixture.

Line a large baking tray with parchment paper. Pour in the egg mixture and bake for 15 mins until puffed and golden. Turn the tray around and bake for another 5 mins for even cooking. Let it cool slightly if serving straight away, or completely if prepping ahead.
While the egg’s in the oven, peel and finely dice the onions, and peel and finely chop the garlic. Finely chop the dill and mint. Zest the lemon and set aside.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and garlic, season with a pinch of salt, and cook for 10 mins until soft and just golden.

Place a large colander over the sink. Add the spinach in batches and pour over boiling water to wilt. Once cool enough to handle, squeeze out as much liquid as you can. Roughly chop the wilted spinach and set aside.
Add the spinach to the pan with the softened onion and garlic. Stir through the dill, mint, lemon zest and crumbled feta. Season generously – the feta can handle it!

Cut the baked egg sheet into even rectangles. Warm the tortilla wraps in a dry pan or microwave until soft. Place an egg slice in the centre of each wrap, top with the spinach-feta filling, fold in the sides, then roll up tightly like a burrito.

Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat. Place each wrap seam-side down and cook for 2–3 mins to seal. Brush the tops with the reserved egg white, sprinkle over sesame seeds, then air fry at 200°C for 5 mins until golden and crisp.
Remove any foil, wrap in damp kitchen paper and microwave for 2 mins. Finish in the air fryer at 180°C for 7–8 mins (or in the oven at 160°C for 10 mins) until piping hot.

To Meal Prep: Assemble and seal the wraps, then store in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat as above.To Freeze: Once cooled, wrap each wrap tightly in foil or cling film. Freeze for up to 2 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge before reheating.

name: Spanakopita Halloumi Bowl
description: A herby, lemony, sumac-y giant couscous bowl with crispy halloumi and toasted pine nuts. This lunch box is full of nutrients but really satisfying.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Tip the pine nuts onto a baking tray and roast for 10-12 mins until golden.

Meanwhile, finely chop the red onion and garlic. Heat a splash of olive oil in the biggest pot you have set over a medium heat. Add the onion and fry for 5-7 mins then add the garlic and cook for another 2 mins.
Add the spinach a big handful at a time, stirring until wilted before adding another handful. Once all the leaves are wilted in the pan, remove the spinach mix to a plate and set aside to cool.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil then add the giant couscous. Reduce to a simmer and cook the couscous for 8 mins, then drain and transfer to a large salad bowl.
Meanwhile, break the halloumi down its natural split and dice into 2cm pieces. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the halloumi, cooking on all sides until golden.

Squeeze as much of the liquid out of the spinach mix as you can, then finely chop and add to the couscous. Finely chop the dill, parsley and mint, and set aside a small handful for garnish, then add the rest to the couscous and mix to combine. Grate in the zest of the lemon with a squeeze of the juice and the sumac, then season with salt and pepper.

Divide the couscous between Tupperware containers and top each with halloumi, a dollop of yoghurt, roasted pine nuts and remaining fresh herbs.Box up and pop in the fridge ready for lunch. These will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Spanakopita Halloumi Bowl
description: A herby, lemony, sumac-y giant couscous bowl with crispy halloumi and toasted pine nuts. This one is full of nutrients but really satisfying. Chuck the leftovers into a container and reheat in the microwave the next day for an easy lunch.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Tip the pine nuts onto a baking tray and roast for 10-12 mins until golden.

Meanwhile, finely chop the red onion and garlic. Heat a splash of olive oil in the biggest pot you have set over a medium heat. Add the onion and fry for 5-7 mins then add the garlic and cook for another 2 mins.
Add the spinach a big handful at a time, stirring until wilted before adding another handful. Once all the leaves are wilted in the pan, remove the spinach mix to a plate and set aside to cool.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil then add the giant couscous. Reduce to a simmer and cook the couscous for 8 mins, then drain and transfer to a large salad bowl.
Meanwhile, break the halloumi down its natural split and dice into 2cm pieces. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the halloumi, cooking on all sides until golden.

Squeeze as much of the liquid out of the spinach mix as you can, then finely chop and add to the couscous. Finely chop the dill, parsley and mint, and set aside a small handful for garnish, then add the rest to the couscous and mix to combine. Grate in the zest of the lemon with a squeeze of the juice and the sumac, then season with salt and pepper.
To serve, divide the couscous between bowls and top with the halloumi, a dollop of yoghurt, roasted pine nuts and remaining fresh herbs.

name: Spanakopita Orzo
description: A Greek-ish classic turned into a the ultimate meal prep dinner. It’s fresh, filling and is ready in 30. Super simple. Seriously mega.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Tip the pine nuts onto a baking tray and roast for 10-12 mins until golden.

Finely slice the onion and chop the garlic. Heat a splash of oil in the biggest pot you have, then add the onion and fry for 10 mins over a medium heat. Add the garlic, cook for another 2 mins and pour in the wine, cooking off until evaporated.

Add a big handful of spinach and rocket – it will take a few goes to get it all wilted down. Keep wilting and adding the leaves until it’s all used up, then remove the mixture from the pan and set aside to cool.

Tip the orzo into the pan along with the vegetable stock. Give it a mix once its added to the pot to prevent sticking, bring it up to a simmer, cover with a lid and cook for 10 mins until the liquid has been absorbed.

Meanwhile, squeeze as much of the liquid out of the spinach mix as you can, then finely chop. Finely chop the dill and mix most of it through the orzo, along with the chopped spinach. Grate in the zest of the lemon with a squeeze of the juice, then season with salt and pepper.
Spoon out the orzo into your Tupperware containers. Once cool, top with crumbled feta, the pine nuts and the remaining dill.Box up and pop in the fridge - they'll last for up to 3 days.

name: Spanakopita Orzo
description: A Greek classic transformed into a nutritious, midweek meal that's ready in 30 minutes. This spanakopita orzo is going to be a regular on your dinner table.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Tip the pine nuts onto a baking tray and roast for 10-12 mins until golden.

Finely slice the onion and chop the garlic. Heat a splash of oil in the biggest pot you have, then add the onion and fry for 10 mins over a medium heat. Add the garlic, cook for another 2 mins and pour in the wine, cooking off until evaporated.

Add a big handful of spinach and rocket – it will take a few goes to get it all wilted down. Keep wilting and adding the leaves until it’s all used up, then remove the mixture from the pan and set aside to cool.

Tip the orzo into the pan along with the vegetable stock. Give it a mix once its added to the pot to prevent sticking, bring it up to a simmer, cover with a lid and cook for 10 mins until the liquid has been absorbed.

Meanwhile, squeeze as much of the liquid out of the spinach mix as you can, then finely chop. Finely chop the dill and mix most of it through the orzo, along with the chopped spinach. Grate in the zest of the lemon with a squeeze of the juice, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve the orzo in bowls topped with crumbled feta, the pine nuts and the remaining dill.

name: Spanakopita Pancakes
description: Adding spinach and dill to the batter gives these pancakes their green herby goodness, then we’ve stuffed them with a creamy cottage cheese filling and topped them with a runny fried egg for a protein boost. Remember to factor in an extra hour for letting the pancake batter rest – it's worth it!
instructions: For the batter, get the spinach into a blender with the dill, milk, eggs and a pinch of salt. Blitz until smooth, then add the flour, pulsing until just combined – don’t overmix. Set aside to rest for at least an hour, or pop it in the fridge until ready to use.

To cook the pancakes, melt the butter in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a ladle of batter, swirling to coat the pan. Cook until the edges set and the surface bubbles, then flip and cook the other side. Transfer to a tray and cover with parchment to stop the next pancake from sticking. Repeat until all the batter is used. Keep warm in a low oven.

For the filling, get the spinach into a colander and pour over a kettle of boiling water, then leave to cool. Squeeze out as much water as possible and roughly chop.Finely chop the onion and garlic. Roughly chop the dill and parsley. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat, then gently cook the onion and garlic for 7-10 mins until soft. Stir in the spinach, cottage cheese, chopped herbs, most of the feta (save a few crumbles for garnish) and a good pinch of salt and black pepper. Squeeze in lemon juice to taste. Keep warm on a very low heat.
To cook the eggs, heat a glug of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Crack in the eggs, basting with the oil until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked to your liking.

To serve, grab the pancakes from the oven and top each with a generous spoonful of the spinach mixture and a fried egg. Fold over the edges, scatter with sesame seeds, the remaining feta and more herbs, if you like.

name: Spanakopita Roast Chicken
description: Kitty's take on spanakopita in roast chicken form. Crispy chicken legs served over garlicky wilted spinach and yoghurt, loaded with feta, fresh dill and buttery filo shards for that classic Greek pastry crunch. Utterly delish.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Place the chicken legs in a large, high-sided roasting tray. Zest the lemon over the chicken and drizzle with the olive oil and rub all over with the dried oregano and plenty of salt and black pepper. Roast for 30 mins.

Meanwhile, make the filo shards. Melt the butter. Lay the filo sheets on a large lined baking tray, brushing each one generously with melted butter as you stack them. Scatter over the sesame seeds and bake alongside the chicken for 10–12 mins until deeply golden and crisp. Remove and leave to cool — the shards will crisp up further as they cool.

Remove the chicken from the oven. Bash the garlic cloves with the flat of a knife and roughly chop the spring onions. Add both to the tray, toss everything together in the chicken juices and return to the oven for a further 10–15 mins, until the skin is deeply golden and crisp and the juices run clear when the thickest part of the thigh is pierced. Remove the chicken legs from the tray and set aside to rest.

Add half the spinach to the roasting tray and toss well so it's coated in the chicken juices. Return to the oven for 3–4 mins until just wilted. Add the remaining spinach, toss again and place back in the oven for a further 2–3 mins until wilted down. This also works with frozen spinach. Add the blocks straight to the tray and roast, stirring halfway through.
Remove the tray from the oven. Stir the yoghurt and most of the dill through the spinach. Squeeze over the juice of half the zested lemon (for the chicken) and season well with salt and black pepper.

Spoon the yoghurt spinach onto a large plate or divide between plates and arrange the chicken legs on top. Scatter over the remaining dill and break the filo into rough shards. Crumble the feta into larger chunks and pile everything on top. Serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges alongside.

name: Spanish Omelette
description: This Spanish omelette recipe has minimal ingredients, but it’s all about gentle, careful cooking to get a caramelised crust with an oozing centre. These flavours are perfect for breakfast (and lunch and dinner).
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut in half lengthways and cut into 2-3mm thick slices. Halve and thinly slice the onion.

Heat a glug of the oil in a small, deep, non-stick frying pan (roughly 22-25cm in diameter) over a medium heat. Add the onion to the pan with a pinch of salt and cook for 5 minutes, stirring regularly until beginning to soften and caramelise. Tip in the sliced potatoes, mix well and cook for 20 minutes, carefully flipping and stirring every few minutes. You want the potatoes to be cooked, starting to caramelise but not collapsing. Ensure your potatoes are evenly spread and touching the surface of the pan for an even cook.

While your potatoes are cooking, crack the eggs into a large bowl and whisk them together with a fork. Season really well with salt and black pepper. Scrape in the onions, potatoes and oil from the pan into the bowl and fold together. Leave to sit for 15 minutes.
Heat a splash of oil in the frying pan, now over a medium-low heat – you want to cook the eggs gently. Pour the eggs, onions and potatoes into the pan, spreading everything so it’s even in the pan.

Cook gently for 6-8 minutes, having a peek at the underside to check if it’s lightly golden. Use a spatula to gently press in the sides of the omelette as it cooks, to create an even, round side. When ready to flip, the underside will be golden and the top will still be soft and runny in the middle.
Carefully slide the omelette out onto a large plate. Put the pan over the plate and omelette and, in one swift movement, flip the omelette back into the pan, so the lightly golden side is facing up.

Put back over a medium heat and cook for 2-3 minutes, using the spatula to press the edges to make them neat and rounded. You want the underside to be lightly golden, but you’re looking to keep some of that wobble inside in the very centre.
Slide out onto a plate, cut into wedges and serve with a green salad, if you like.

name: Spatchcock Chicken Traybake Curry
description: Spatchcocking a chicken sounds harder than it actually is and when it's all flattened out the chicken roasts in half the time. Here it sits on a bed of peppers and onions, smothered in a rich, fragrant madras and coconut curry sauce that bubbles down around the rice. Yum.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Spatchcock the chicken by placing it breast-side down and using sharp kitchen scissors or poultry shears to cut down either side of the backbone to remove it. Flip the chicken over so the breast side is facing up and press down firmly on the breastbone to flatten it.

Thickly slice the onions and peppers and scatter into a large roasting tray. Lay the chicken on top, breast-side up. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and black pepper and roast for 30 mins until beginning to crisp.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. Peel and roughly chop half the ginger and add it to a blender with the curry paste, tinned plum tomatoes and coconut milk. Blitz until smooth and season with salt and black pepper.

Once the chicken has had its 30 mins, tip the rice straight into the tray (no need to microwave first, it'll cook in the sauce) and pour the sauce all over. Return to the oven for another 30 mins, until the sauce is bubbling and thickened and the chicken is cooked through.

While the chicken finishes off, make the cucumber salad. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds and thickly slice. Tip into a bowl. Peel and grate in the remaining ginger, finely chop the chilli and add to the bowl along with the zest and juice of the lemon. Season and toss together.
To serve, shred or carve the chicken and serve straight from the tray with the curried rice, naans and cucumber salad, and fresh coriander alongside.

name: Spatchcock Chicken With Chicken Braised Vegetables
description: We've got a double upskill with this recipe. You'll learn how to spatchcock a chicken and make a homemade mayo. Good stuff.
keywords: Spatchcocked Chicken with Chicken Braised Vegetables
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the fennel into 4 wedges lengthways. Slice 500g of the radishes in half lengthways. Tip the veg into a large roasting tray, scatter with the fennel seeds, and season well. Add 50ml water and set aside. Wrap the garlic bulb in foil and put in the side of the tray.
Spatchcock your chicken. Flip the chicken so it's breast side down on the surface. Use a pair of strong kitchen scissors to cut away the backbone by cutting up each side.
Turn the chicken over and gently press down on the breastbone until you hear a crack. Turn the legs out so the chicken lies flat.
Finely chop the herbs. Mix the softened butter with the zest of 1 lemon and your finely chopped herbs. Season well with salt and pepper.

Use your hands to gently separate the skin from the chicken. The easiest way to do this is to slide your hand under the skin and gently pull it away from the meat. This creates a cavity for the butter – ensuring perfect crispy skin.

Press most of the butter into the cavity, making sure you spread it as much across the surface of the meat as possible. Lightly rub the remaining butter on the outside. Slice the zested lemon in half and add half to the veg tray.

Place a rack over the top of the radishes and fennel. Put the chicken on the rack and transfer to the oven. If you don’t have a rack that sits on top – use the rack of your oven, sliding the tray of veggies underneath. Roast for 35-40 mins. You can tell if your chicken is cooked by sliding a knife where the thigh meets the body, if the juices run clear then the chicken is cooked through.

In the meantime, make the mayo. Finely chop the herbs and set aside. Add the egg yolk to a bowl, add a little squeeze of lemon and ½ tsp of the mustard and whisk together. Whilst you keep whisking, pour in the oil in a continuous light stream, until it comes together to form a glossy mayo. Add the remaining juice of the lemon, the herbs, and the rest of the mustard and season very generously with salt. Finish with a crack of black pepper.
Pickle the remaining radishes. Finely slice the remaining radishes and add to a bowl with the juice of a lemon, the sugar and a big pinch of salt. Toss well and set aside.

Remove the chicken from the oven, set aside for 15 mins to rest (use a plate or tray with a lip so the juices don’t go everywhere). Squeeze the lemon juice from the roasted lemon over the veg, then discard the squeezed lemon. If your veg is still looking a little under, return the veg to the oven for 15 more mins.
Remove the garlic and unwrap the foil, squeeze the golden garlic cloves from their skin into the mayo and whisk well. Toss the veg and season with a little fresh lemon juice.

Carve up the chicken. Remove the legs by gently pulling them from the breast crown. Then slice down where the bones meet. To separate the thighs and legs, gently pull apart, then slide your knife down between the joint.

Cut the breasts away from the crown by sliding your knife down both sides of the centre bone and then following it down around the ribcage to release the breasts. Cut through the joint where the wing tip meets the breastbone. Save the carcass to make chicken stock! Slice the chicken breast.

Add the chicken to a platter along with the veg. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve on the side. Scatter with the pickled radishes, dill and serve alongside the herby mayo. I love serving this with french fries and a fresh salad.

name: Speediest Chipotle Shakshuka
description: The ultimate hangover cure – saucy, smoky, spicy eggs. Serve our speediest ever shakshuka straight out of the pan so everyone can get stuck in.
instructions:
Get a large frying pan over a high heat. Drizzle in some olive
oil, then empty the passata straight into the pan. Add 1–2
tbsp of chipotle paste (to your taste), then pick out the
roasted peppers with a fork, leaving their juices behind, and tear
into the pan. Give everything a stir and season with salt and black
pepper. Let bubble away for 1 minute.
Crack the eggs into the pan and season with salt and black
pepper, then cover with a lid. Cook for 4–5 minutes, until the
whites are just set but the yolks are still runny.
Meanwhile, toast the pitta breads, tear into pieces and put into
a serving bowl.
Once the eggs are cooked, dollop over spoonfuls of the natural
yogurt, scatter over the parsley and serve at the table with extra
black pepper and the pitta breads for dunking.

name: Speedy Chicken Udon Noodle Soup
description: A quick and easy chicken udon noodle soup. It's a hug in a bowl you can make in just 15 minutes. Winner winner, chicken dinner!
keywords: Speedy Chicken Udon Noodle Soup recipe
instructions: Put the eggs into a pot of boiling water set over a low-medium heat and cook for 6 ½ mins. Transfer the cooked eggs into a bowl of ice water, peel and slice in half.
Meanwhile, pour your broth into a separate pot and bring to the boil. Turn the heat down, add the udon and cook following pack instructions.
Wash the pak choi and chop the white stems off, then add to your pot of udon and cook for just a few mins.
Combine the miso, dashi, white pepper, sesame oil and light soy sauce in a bowl and whisk well for 1 min. Divide between the serving bowls (this will be the base of your dish).
Divide the noodles between the serving bowls, top with a few ladles of the broth, then finish with cooked chicken breast, the pak choi, eggs, coriander and a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Speedy Chickpea and Harissa Soup
description: This soup comes together in no time and packs a nutritional punch. The creaminess comes from blending half of the chickpeas and the rest give a chunky texture.
instructions: Blend up the tomatoes, harissa, a tin of drained chickpeas, red peppers, tomato purée and 2 tbsp of tahini. Start with less harissa, if you prefer less heat.
Blend until smooth, then transfer to a saucepan to heat through. Drain the other tin of chickpeas and add them to the pot. Fill the tomato tin with water and pour it into the pot.

Use a fork or a potato masher to mash up the chickpeas a little. They should have a chunky texture and some can still be whole. Season well with salt and pepper. Make sure the soup is heated through well.
To serve, drizzle more tahini and harissa over the top, a sprinkle of sesame seeds and parsley.

name: Speedy Chilli Paneer
description: A south Indian-style chilli paneer recipe. Every time one of our team makes this for the rest of the kitchen, it disappears in minutes. There are various versions of this dish across India, but this one is our favourite.
instructions: Cube the paneer, then soak it in a bowl or pan of just-boiled water for 15 mins.

Chop the lemongrass stalk, then mince it. Trim and finely dice half of your onions, then chop the remaining onion into large pieces. Finely mince the ginger and garlic. Trim and chop the pepper into large pieces. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions. Chop the green chilli. Set everything aside.
Combine the tomato purée, soy sauce, water and sugar in a small bowl.

Add a drizzle of oil to a saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the ginger, garlic, green chilli, lemongrass, finely diced onion and curry leaves. Season with salt and stir-fry for 3-5 mins until the onions have softened. Stir through the tomato mixture and cook for 1-2 mins until thickened. Remove the sauce from the heat.

Drizzle some oil into another pan and place over a medium-high heat. Drain the paneer, pat dry, then add to the hot oil with the large pieces of onion, pepper and the red chilli powder. Cook, stirring, for 3-5 mins until the veggies have softened a little, but still have bite.

Now add the sauce to the paneer pan and cook until everything's nicely coated. Garnish with spring onions and serve immediately. If it’s a little dry, add a splash of water. Taste and season with salt, if needed.

name: Speedy Cod, Spinach & Chickpea Curry
description: A warming, coconutty curry packed with flaky cod, hearty chickpeas and sweet roasted peppers.
instructions: Cut the cod into two large pieces and season with salt and pepper.

Place a medium, deep nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Chuck in the cherry tomatoes and cook for 5 mins, tossing occasionally, until they start to burst. Add splashes of water if they begin to catch.

Stir through the curry paste and cook for 1 min until fragrant. Add the frozen peppers and drained chickpeas, coating them in all that curry goodness. Pour in the coconut milk then bring everything to a simmer.

Nestle in the cod pieces, cover with a lid and cook gently for 8 mins until the fish is opaque and flakes easily. About halfway through, scatter over the spinach and let it wilt, then gently fold it through the soup.
Meanwhile, microwave the poppadoms following pack instructions — no need for oil.
Ladle the curry into bowls and lightly crush the poppadoms over the top or serve them whole on the side for scooping.

name: Speedy Creamy Miso Soup
description: A high-protein plant-based soup made from butter beans and miso. Delicious.
instructions: Melt the butter and whisk it through the soy sauce. Taste and add a little more soy sauce, if you like. Pop it in the fridge to set while you make the soup.
Put the canned beans (with their liquid) into a blender with the remaining ingredients. Blend until smooth and the fats have emulsified, which will make it extra creamy.

Pour the blended mixture into a pan. Fill the empty bean can halfway full with water, then tip this into the pan. Add more water if you like, depending on how thick you like your soup. Heat through well and season to taste. Add an extra bit of vegan butter to give it a velvety texture, if you like. You can also add a bit more miso paste if you think it needs it.
To serve, top the soup with chilli oil and sesame seeds. Toast the bread and spread it with the soy butter, if using.

name: Speedy Creamy Tomato Spaghetti
description: Think vodka pasta, minus the hassle. With dish there's chopping in sight, just a silky, creamy tomato sauce that comes together in 20 mins.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and cook the spaghetti following pack instructions until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.

Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the pre-chopped garlic and cook for 30-60 seconds until fragrant – don't let it brown. Add the tomato purée and stir it through. Cook for 2–3 mins until it darkens and starts to smell sweet.

Add a splash of the reserved pasta water and stir until you've got a glossy, smooth sauce. Stir through the crème fraîche and let it bubble for about a minute until you've got a silky pink sauce. Season with salt, black pepper and chilli flakes, if using.
Add the drained pasta straight into the sauce and toss to coat, adding a splash more pasta water if it needs it. Stir through most of the Parmesan and tear in most of the basil.
Serve with the remaining Parmesan grated over and the rest of the basil scattered on top, and an extra dollop of creme fraîche if you fancy.

name: Speedy Green Bean Stew with Dill Rice
description: A nourishing bowl of green bean and tomato stew, served with buttery dill-infused rice. An easy and satisfying midweek veggie dinner to add to your rotation.
keywords: Speedy Green Bean Stew with Dill Rice
instructions: Wash the rice until the water runs clear. Pick and roughly chop the dill fronds. Finely slice the dill stems.

Melt the butter in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the orzo and cook for 3-4 mins, stirring constantly, until toasted and browned. Stir through the rice then pour in the water. Let it come to the boil then pop the lid on and turn the heat down to low. Leave it for 12 mins (don’t remove the lid), then remove the pan from the heat and set it aside for another 10 min, still covered. Before serving, stir through the dill fronds and stems.
Meanwhile, peel and finely slice the onion. Trim and halve the green beans.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan set over a medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 2-3 mins until softened. Stir through the ground cinnamon then add the plum tomatoes and crush them using a masher. Leave to cook down for 6-10 mins until thickened.

Add the green beans and pour in the stock. Bring to a boil and leave to cook for 5-8 mins until just tender (if you like your green beans cooked for longer, go for it). Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Share the dill rice between plates and top with the green bean stew, a dollop of greek yoghurt and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Speedy Harissa Mushroom Hummus Bowl
description: Smooth, garlicky hummus with savoury mushrooms and blistered cherry tomatoes. This nourishing vegan bowl hits the spot.
instructions: Drain the chickpeas and reserve ¼ of them for later. Add the rest to a blender along with just under ½ of the chickpea water. Add ½ the garlic, tahini, juice of ½ the lemon, a good pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil and blend until smooth. Taste and add more lemon juice or salt if needed or more water if it’s too thick.

Cut the mushrooms into quarters (eighths if they’re very large) and melt the butter in a pan. Add the mushrooms to the pan with a good pinch of salt and cook on medium-high heat for 5 mins. Then add the cherry tomatoes and the remaining chickpeas and cook for another 5-8 mins until the tomatoes have started to break down and release their juices. Add a splash of water if it starts to dry out – it should be quite saucy. Slice the sun-dried tomatoes and add these too, along with a tbsp or two of the oil from the jar. Add the harissa, season well and remove from the heat.

To make the garlic spinach, mince the remaining garlic and add it, along with the spinach, to a frying pan with a little olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook on low heat until the spinach has wilted, about 3 mins, stirring often to make sure the garlic doesn’t burn. Turn off the heat and add a splash of vinegar and stir again.

To serve, spoon 3-4 tbsp of hummus into the base of a bowl, ladle in the saucy harissa mushrooms and top with the garlic spinach. Finish with a drizzle of tahini and olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice. Scoop it up with a warm pitta.

name: Speedy Jalapeño, Mango & Prawn Chopped Salad
description: A light, bright, sweet, and spicy chopped salad. Using cooked prawns is a great time-saver.
instructions: Cook your brown rice according to packet instructions and leave to cool. Peel and cut your mango into wedges.
Place your cucumbers, spring onions, coriander and jalapeños onto a board and chop into even-sized pieces. Add the mango, avocado, and prawns to the chopping board and continue to chop.
Tip your chopped ingredients into a bowl along with the brown rice and add ¾ of the tortilla chips, roughly crushing them in your hand.
Make the dressing by mixing together the jalapeño juice from the jar along with your honey, oil, and salt. Shake it forcefully inside of the jar to emulsify.
Pour the dressing into the bowl and toss it all together.
Serve with the remaining tortilla chips crushed on top.

name: Speedy Mushroom Flatbreads with Red Onion Hummus
description: This recipe is more than the sum of its parts — the mushrooms, hummus and flatbread all go great together. You're going to want to make this again and again.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190ºC.
Slice or pull apart the mushrooms into equal-sized pieces. Peel and slice the onions into eighths.

Lay the mushrooms onto a large baking tray and drizzle over about 4 tbsp of olive oil and season well. Mix to make sure all of the mushrooms are coated and bake for 20-25 mins, or until nicely caramelised. Toss them a few times while cooking to make sure they cook evenly.

Put the onions into a smaller baking dish, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and plenty of pepper. Roast for 10 mins on the lower shelf. After the 10 mins, remove them to add the balsamic vinegar and stir, then roast for another 20-25 mins, tossing halfway to make sure they cook evenly. They should be very soft and caramelised without too many crispy edges.

Once the onions have come out of the oven, you can make the hummus. Blend the chickpeas, 100ml water or aquafaba (water from the chickpea can), tahini, garlic, 1 tbsp olive oil, 4 heaped tbsp of the roasted onions, the juice of half a lemon and 1 ½ tsp salt in a blender until very smooth. Taste and season. Add more lemon juice if you like.
To make the flatbreads, add the flour, soya yoghurt, baking powder, 2 tsp of olive oil, ½ tsp of salt and plenty of pepper to a large mixing bowl. Use a fork to mix everything together.

Dust a clean work surface with some flour and tip out the dough. Gently knead for 1 min until it comes together into a smooth ball. Divide the dough into 4 portions. Dust the surface with a little extra flour and roll each portion with a rolling pin into oblong or round shapes, around 0.5cm thick.

Place a dry frying pan over medium heat and, once hot, add the first flatbread and cook for 2-3 mins on each side. It should be speckled with darker spots and be pillowy and fluffy. Repeat with the remaining flatbreads.

Once all of your elements are ready, you can assemble the flatbreads. Brush the flatbreads with a little oil and salt and pepper if you like. Spread a layer of hummus over them, then pile on the mushrooms and the remaining red onions. At this point you can pop them under the grill for a few mins to heat them up, but they are just as lovely at room temp as they are hot.
To finish, scatter over the pine nuts and, if using, the chopped parsley.

name: Speedy Parmesan Roast Chicken & Onions
description: Perfect roast chicken with Parmesan and caramelised onions, on the table in just 45 minutes. Less time, less faff and even more flavour than a Sunday roast.
keywords: Speedy Parmesan Roast Chicken & Onions recipe
parmesan roast chicken parmesan roast chicken recipe
instructions: Season the chicken pieces generously with salt. Preheat the oven to 225°C fan.

Heat the butter and olive oil in a heavy-based oven-safe frying pan set over medium-high heat. Place the chicken skin-side down in the pan for 5-8 mins until the skin is lightly golden and starting to crisp up (it will finish crisping up in the oven).
Meanwhile, thinly slice the onions.
Remove the chicken from the pan and add in the onions to fry for a few minutes in the chicken fat until lightly golden.
Place the chicken back in along with the whole garlic cloves and transfer the pan to the oven for 10 mins.

Carefully pour in the wine (or water if you prefer) around the chicken and add the Parmesan rind. Reduce the oven to 200°C then return the chicken to the oven for about 15-20 mins or until cooked through (the breasts will cook faster than the legs so you may need to remove them after 15 mins and continue cooking the legs for another 5 mins).
Remove the dish from the oven and squeeze over the juice of the lemon. Leave the chicken to rest for at least 5 mins.
Serve with more grated Parmesan, seasonal greens and crusty bread.

name: Speedy Smoky Harissa Butter Beans
description: The quickest, most satisfying lunch or light dinner that’s on the table in just 10 minutes. It’s quick, it’s healthy and it’s very delicious. And you it's preppable? Say no more.
keywords: 10-Minute Smoky Harissa Creamy Butter Beans recipe
instructions: Add the cherry tomatoes to a pan with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Set it over a medium-high heat and cook for about 5 mins until starting to soften and burst open. Add a splash of water if they’re catching on the bottom of the pan.
Mince the garlic and add it to the tomatoes in the pan along with the tomato paste, ¾ of the harissa and the smoked paprika.

Add the tinned butterbeans and ½ their liquid to the pan then stir in the vegan cream cheese. Bring the mixture to a boil then turn down the heat and simmer for 5-10 mins until the beans have softened and the broth has thickened (it should be creamy).

Meanwhile, finely chop the herbs. Then ladle the beans into bowls or meal-prep boxes. Drizzle over the tahini and some remaining harissa. Finish with the chopped herbs and flaked almonds. It will keep in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Speedy Spag Bol
description: A lightning-fast pasta that let's your Bolognese Ragú batch truly shine. It's the ultimate midweek classic, done in 15 mins.
instructions: Make the Bolognese Ragú.
Fill a large saucepan with water and salt it generously. Bring to the boil over high heat.
Drop in the spaghetti and cook for two mins less than the pack says for al dente. Reserve 200ml of pasta water, then drain.
Grate the Parmesan.

Return the pasta to the pan with the ragù and a splash of the pasta water. Cook over a medium heat, stirring, until the sauce clings to the pasta and everything’s piping hot. Add more water if it needs loosening. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Divide between bowls and finish with plenty of grated Parmesan.

name: Speedy Spicy ‘Nduja Sugo
description: This recipe uses just a handful of ingredients to create a rich, flavourful pasta sauce ready in as little as 20 minutes. What a treat.
instructions: Cook the pasta following pack instructions.

Thinly slice the onions, garlic and chilli. Halve the cherry tomatoes using a couple of small plates. Add a handful of tomatoes to the bottom plate and place the second, face-down over the tomatoes. Run a bread knife through the middle, halving all the tomatoes at once. Roughly chop the basil.
Heat a glug of oil in your biggest frying pan over a high heat. Add the garlic, onion and chillies to the pan and cook for 2-3 mins. Scoop in the ‘nduja and cook for 1-2 mins until melted.

Add the tomatoes and stir them through, keeping the heat high. Add the sherry vinegar, season with salt and add a ladle of water from the pasta pot. Bring to a boil and cook for 4-5 mins while the pasta finishes cooking.
Drain and transfer the pasta to the sauce. Grate in the pecorino. Stir through half of the basil leaves and vinegar to finish. Garnish with remaining basil.

name: Speedy Steak Tagliata
description: A solo steak is one of life’s simple pleasures, and nothing highlights that better than steak tagliata. This classic Italian dish combines perfectly cooked steak with fresh, vibrant ingredients.
instructions: Pull the steak out of the fridge and allow it to come to room temperature. Season generously with salt and let sit for 10 mins. Meanwhile, preheat a frying pan over a high heat, rub the bread with olive oil and toast in the hot pan. Remove from the pan and rub with a halved garlic clove, set aside.

Bring the frying pan back to smoking point over a high heat, add a shot of oil and carefully lay the steak in. Cook for 2-3 mins on each side until medium-rare, remove from the pan and pop onto the toasted bread to rest. The bread will soak up all the delicious resting juices. Chuck the tomatoes into the pan with a shot more oil and cook for 3-4 mins until blistered and bursting. Finely slice the remaining garlic clove and add to the pan for the last minute or so.
Remove the pan from the heat and add the balsamic vinegar and a splash of water to deglaze. Keep warm while you whip up the salad.
Tip the rocket into a bowl with the parsley leaves. Shave in the parmesan cheese and dress with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, pepper and lemon juice. Toss together.

Carve the steak into thin slices and transfer to a plate. Tip over the tomatoes, balsamic glaze and sizzled garlic. Serve the tagliata salad on the side of the steak with the toasted beefy bread for mopping.

name: Speedy Sun-Dried Tomato & Chickpea Soup
description: A tangy sun-dried tomato soup recipe that you won't believe is plant-based.
keywords: Speedy Sun-Dried Tomato & Chickpea Soup recipe
instructions: Put the canned tomatoes, sun-dried tomatoes, tahini, half of the chickpeas and harissa, if using, into a blender. Blitz until smooth.

Pour the mixture into a pot, then add one full can of water, the rest of your chickpeas, and the stock cube. Simmer for 5-10 mins until the chickpeas have softened slightly and the tomatoes have cooked, mashing down some of the chickpeas with a fork if you like, to create a chunky texture. Taste and season well with salt and pepper.
To serve, ladle the soup into bowls and drizzle with tahini, olive oil and harissa. Sprinkle over some sesame seeds, if you like.

name: Speedy Thai Red Curry Noodle Soup
description: This soup is full of flavour thanks to the punchy curry and chilli pastes and the peanut butter brings a nutty creaminess. Ready in just 15 minutes, it’s your new favourite noodle soup.
keywords: Speedy Thai Red Curry Noodle Soup
Speedy Thai Red Curry Noodle Soup recipe
instructions: Cut the tofu into small cubes. Finely dice the shallot and mince the garlic and ginger. Roughly chop the toasted peanuts and set aside.

Add a splash of vegetable oil to a hot frying pan. Add the tofu and half of the soy sauce, then cook for 3-5 mins over a medium heat until golden brown on all sides. Remove the tofu from the pan and set aside.

Add a little more oil to the same pan and fry the diced shallot for 5 mins until softened. Add the minced garlic and ginger and cook, stirring often, for 3 mins until fragrant but not browned. Add the curry paste and cook for 2-3 mins, stirring often.
Add the water, sambal oelek, remaining soy sauce, stock cube, agave, peanut butter, vegan fish sauce and coconut milk to the pan, then simmer gently for 5 mins.
Add the broccoli and cook for 5 mins, then add the noodles and cook for 1 min, or until softened.
Divide between bowls and serve topped with the tofu, chopped peanuts, coriander and plenty of lime zest and juice.

name: Speedy Udon Miso Noodle Soup
description: This noodle soup is a testament to a well-stocked cupboard. All you need is a handful of long life staples to throw this nutritious and delicious meal together.
keywords: Speedy Udon Miso Noodle Soup recipe
instructions: Mince the ginger and garlic. Prepare 1.5L of boiling water. Drain the tofu and cut it into small cubes.
Heat a saucepan over medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, stirring to make sure they don't burn. Add the boiling water to the pot.
Add the dried shiitake and stock cube. Remove a ladle of the broth and add it to a small bowl. Add the miso to the bowl and whisk to combine. Set aside.
Add the soy sauce, noodles, tofu cubes and simmer for a minute or two before adding the spinach. Stir until wilted. Add the miso broth back into the pot and turn off the heat.
To serve, ladle the noodle soup into bowls, top with kimchi if using, crispy chilli oil and sesame seeds.

name: Speedy Wakame Noodles
description: These noodles are nourishing, warming, and absolutely delicious. Best of all, you can whip them up in just 10 minutes. Enjoy.
instructions: Place the wakame into a bowl full of water. Leave to rehydrate whilst you do everything else.
Meanwhile, finely slice the spring onion. Crack the egg, discarding the egg whites, keeping only the yolk (try to keep it intact.)
Cook the instant noodles according to package instructions. Drain the wakame seaweed, transfer to a bowl with a pinch of sesame and mix through the sesame oil and season with salt.
Add the noodles into a serving bowl. Ladle the broth over. Top with spring onions, chilli crisp, sesame seeds and the egg yolk. Mix before eating.

name: Spice Crusted Salmon With Grilled Chicory & Brown Rice
description: Perfectly cooked salmon crusted in a cumin and coriander seed mixture, served with grilled chicory and herby rice. Simple. Sophisticated. Scrumptious.
instructions: Finely grate the garlic clove into a mixing bowl, add the juice of 1 lemon and set aside.

Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Tip the cumin seeds and coriander seeds into a dry pan. Place over a medium-high heat and toast until the seeds are fragrant,1-2 mins. Then, tip into a pestle and mortar and roughly crush, tip onto a plate. If you don't have a pestle and mortar, add into a sandwich bag and bash using a heavy pan or rolling pin.  Add the seeds to the dry pan and toast until popping, 2-3 mins then tip onto the spices, mix and set aside.
Halve the chicory lengthways and drizzle with 1 tbsp of olive oil, season with salt and pepper and slide under the grill. Grill until tender and starting to lightly char, 5-6 mins.

Take the salmon and press it, skin-side down into the spiced seeds to create a crust. Lay the salmon crust-side down, in a cold non-stick frying pan. Place over a medium heat and cook for 10 mins until the skin is crisp and most of the salmon is pale pink. Flip over and remove the pan from the heat. Leave to sit whilst you mix the rest of the ingredients, the salmon will continue to cook.
Cook the rice according to package instructions, then tip into the mixing bowl with the lemon and garlic. Add 2 tbsp of olive oil. Finely chop most of the herbs and add. Season well and toss.
Pile the rice into bowls, top with the chicory, then the crusted salmon. Top with the remaining herb leaves. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve on the side.

name: Spice-Crusted Tuna & Red Pepper Beans
description: Big on protein. This smoky bean stew with spice-crusted tuna is the answer to all your weeknight dinner dilemmas.
keywords: spice-crusted tuna and red pepper beans
instructions: Finely dice the onion and thinly slice the garlic, zest the lemon. Drain the red peppers and finely chop them. Pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the stems.
Cover the tuna steaks in the Cajun seasoning, pressing to coat all over. Season with salt and set aside.

Heat a saucepan over a medium heat with half the olive oil. Once hot, add the onion and cook, stirring, for 4–5 mins until soft and translucent. Add the garlic, parsley stems and tomato purée, then cook for 2–4 mins, stirring, until the purée darkens.

Tip in the white beans and their liquid, followed by the chopped red peppers. Season with salt and black pepper, then bring to the boil. Turn the heat down to low and let it simmer gently while you cook the tuna. Add a splash of water to loosen if needed.

Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat with the remaining olive oil. Once hot, add the tuna steaks and sear for 3–5 mins on each side, or until nicely coloured and beginning to char. Remove from the heat and let them rest for a couple of minutes.

Taste the beans and adjust with more salt, pepper and lemon juice, if needed. Spoon the beans into bowls. Slice the tuna and lay it over the top. Finish with a sprinkle of lemon zest, parsley leaves and any remaining lemon wedges on the side.

name: Spiced Arayes & Cucumber Salad
description: Crispy stuffed pitas, spiced with harissa and loaded with juicy beef, meet a fresh, punchy cucumber slaw. Hands-on eating encouraged.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.

Add the beef mince to a mixing bowl with the panko breadcrumbs, harissa, pomegranate molasses, tomato paste and salt. Coarsely grate in the red onion. Use your hands to mix everything together until evenly combined.
Halve the pittas, then stuff each half with a portion of the meat mixture, pressing it in evenly. Brush both sides with olive oil.
Arrange the pittas meat-side down on an oiled wire rack set over a baking tray. Slide into the oven and cook for 10–15 mins or until the meat is cooked through and the pittas are crisp and golden.
Meanwhile, use a mandolin or sharp knife to finely slice the cucumber and cabbage. Tip into a sieve, season with salt and toss well. Leave to sit for 10 mins to soften.

Finely chop the dill, stalks and all. In a bowl, mix together the soured cream, mustard, the zest of ¼ of the lemon, and as much juice as you like. Season with salt and black pepper, then stir through the drained cabbage and cucumber. Add more lemon juice to taste.
Once the arayes are cooked, plate them up with the slaw and any extra lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: Spiced Aubergine & Lentil Stew Hummus Bowl
description: Loaded hummus is always a good idea, and this one goes the extra mile. A saucy, spiced aubergine and lentil stew blends into the creamy hummus below.  It’s a full meal, packed with protein, fibre and flavour and is perfectly scoopable.
keywords: Spiced Aubergine & Lentil Stew Hummus Bowl
Spiced Aubergine & Lentil Stew Hummus Bowl recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Slice the aubergine into thick rounds, about 2cm thick. Lay them onto a tray, brush with olive oil on both sides, and season with salt and pepper. Add the cherry tomatoes to the tray around the aubergines. Roast for 15 mins, then flip the aubergines. Roast for another 10-15 mins until softened and golden.
Finely slice the onion and chilli. Mince the garlic and ginger.

Cook the onion until softened, about 7 mins. Add the minced garlic, ginger, and half of the sliced chilli, then the tomato purée and spices and cook for 1 minute. Add the plum tomatoes and fill the tin ¾ full with water. Break up the plum tomatoes with the spatula and add plenty of salt. Let it simmer for 15 mins on medium high until thickened. Add the cooked lentils and stir to heat through for a few mins, then remove from the heat.
Add the roasted cherry tomatoes and aubergine and stir.

To serve, spread a thick layer of hummus in a shallow bowl and top with the stew. Finish with a good squeeze of lemon, a drizzle of olive oil and tahini. Garnish the sliced chilli, any fresh coriander and capers.
Serve with toasted pitta bread.

name: Spiced Aubergine With Harissa Lentil Ragù & Whipped Tahini Sauce
description: Pairing tender sliced aubergines with a spicy harissa ragù was a stroke of genius, if we do say so ourselves. This vegan weeknight recipe is a winner.
keywords: Sliced Aubergine With Harissa Lentil Ragù & Whipped Tahini Sauce
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cook the lentils following pack instructions, then drain and set aside.

Slice down lengthways through the middle of 1 aubergine (keep the top intact), then turn the aubergine 90° and slice down lengthways again to create four ‘legs’. Slice down each leg in half, to create eight segments. Repeat with the second aubergine.

Drizzle the aubergines with a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper, getting into all of the insides. Place on a lined baking tray and roast for 35-40 mins, turning once or twice, until soft and cooked inside.

Meanwhile, make the lentil ragù. Finely slice the onion and mince the garlic. Add a good drizzle of olive oil to a frying pan and add the onion with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring often, for about 8 mins until softened. Add the garlic and tomato purée and harissa and cook for 1 min before adding the canned tomatoes. Cook for another 6-8 mins, then add the cooked lentils.
To make the tahini sauce, whisk all of the ingredients together and season to taste.
To serve, spoon the tahini onto the bottom of a large serving plate and place the aubergines on top. Pour over the ragù and finish with the almonds and herbs.

name: Spiced Beef & Hummus Bowl
description: Juicy spiced beef, sweet roasted peppers and garlicky kale, all loaded onto a bed of creamy hummus. Flatbread on the side for scooping, obviously.
instructions: Place a frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the beef mince and frozen onion. Break the mince up and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3–5 mins until browned.
Meanwhile, drain the roasted peppers and roughly chop into bite-sized pieces.
Stir the garlic purée and garam masala through the beef and cook for 1 min until fragrant. Toss in the kale and chopped peppers, and cook for another 1–2 mins until the kale has wilted.
Season with salt, squeeze in the lemon juice and drizzle over the honey. Mix everything together well.
Spread the hummus across the base of two shallow bowls. Top with the beef mixture and serve with flatbreads on the side.

name: Spiced Beetroot Flatbreads
description: Making your own flatbreads is a breeze. Topped with gently spiced beetroot and tahini sauce, this is a winner.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.

Make your flatbread dough. Pop your flour, yeast, caraway seeds, salt, olive oil and the warm water. Give it a good mix until you have a rough dough, then turn it out onto your work surface and knead for 5 mins.
Pop your dough in a lightly oiled bowl covered in a tea towel and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Peel your beetroot, then chop them into quarters. Place them on a baking tray, and drizzle with your ground cumin, ground cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to combine.
Wrap your bulb of garlic in foil, then nestle this into the beetroot roasting tray. Roast for 45 mins.
Pickle your radishes. Finely slice your radishes, then pop them in a bowl. Squeeze over the juice of half your lemon and a good pinch of salt, then mix together with your hands. Set aside to pickle.

Make your crispy capers. Heat a good glug of olive oil in a frying pan, then add your capers. Fry for around 5 mins until they are crispy. Spoon out of the oil, then drain on a baking tray lined with kitchen towel.
Once your roasted garlic is cool enough to handle, squeeze the caramelised pulp out of the skins.
Pop the garlic pulp into a bowl along with your tahini. Add the juice of your remaining lemon, then add 75ml of warm water. Whisk until you have a smooth, thick sauce. Season with salt.
Finely chop your parsley.
Back to your bread. Heat a cast iron pan or frying pan on a very high heat. Turn it out of the bowl and divide it into 8 equal sized pieces. Roll each into a 2mm flatbread shape.

Pop one at a time into your hot, dry pan and cook for a minute on each side. They should bubble and get slight char on them. Wrap the flatbreads in a clean tea towel to keep warm whilst you cook off the rest.
Spread your flatbreads with your tahini mixture, then top with your roasted beetroot and pickled radishes. Sprinkle on your capers and chopped parsley, then serve and enjoy.

name: Spiced Brioche Poppy Seed Bagels
description: What's better than brioche? Brioche bagels. These cinnamon and cardamom bagels are an absolute treat. Just wait until you try them toasted and buttered.
instructions: Combine the spices in a bowl and set aside.

In a large bowl, whisk together the sifted flour, sugar and salt. In another bowl, crumble the yeast into the water, milk and egg yolks and whisk to dissolve and combine. Add this to the dry mixture and combine with your hands, or a spatula or pastry scraper if you have one, until the dough comes together – it will be very sticky at this stage.
Cover the surface with clingfilm and leave to rest at room temperature for 20 mins. Meanwhile, cut the room temperature butter into cubes.

Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 15–20 mins. Now add the butter, a few cubes at a time, kneading it into the dough, making sure the butter is incorporated before you add more. Add the spice mix and knead it in, making sure it’s fully incorporated. Lightly flour the dough all over and put it back into the bowl. Cover with cling film again and refrigerate for 1 hour.

Line two baking trays with baking parchment. Remove the dough from the fridge. Weigh out 60g pieces, roll them into individual balls and place on your prepared tray. Leave for 5 mins to allow the gluten to relax. Poke a finger through the centre of each ball and work the hole so that you can fit a finger in from each hand, pointing in opposite directions. Then turn one finger over the other in a twiddling motion. Make the hole bigger than you think it needs to be, to allow for the dough stretching back and then swelling during proving.
Preheat the oven to 180°C fan.
Whisk together the egg wash ingredients. Brush the bagels with the egg wash, sprinkle with the poppy seeds, then leave to prove for 15–20 mins.

Bake for 10 mins, or until the bagels have a nice even golden colour across the top (check for browning on the bottom too). Remove and allow to cool on the tray for 10 mins before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Spiced Brown Rice & Chickpeas
description: This simple chickpea-packed recipe makes a great base for meal prep throughout the week. High fibre, high flavour, low effort.
keywords: Spiced Brown Rice and Chickpeas recipe
instructions: Cut the courgettes in half lengthways, then slice into half moons. Cut the red onions into large chunks.
Place a medium frying pan over medium heat and drizzle with olive oil.

Once hot, add the red onions, courgettes, smoked paprika, cumin, and coriander to the pan. Grate in the garlic and cook until softened, stirring occasionally. If anything catches on the pan, add a splash of water to deglaze.
Add the drained chickpeas and cooked rice to the pan. Stir everything together and cook for 2–3 minutes until heated through.
Season with salt, black pepper, and MSG (if using). Store in a Tupperware container along with your favourite protein, or by itself and pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Spiced Carrot Risotto
description: This warming, autumnal risotto is the perfect balance of flavours and textures. The brown butter maple walnuts take it to the next level.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.

Cut the carrots into small pieces and pop them in a large roasting tin. Add the cinnamon and nutmeg, season with salt and pepper and drizzle with olive oil. Toss to coat then roast for 35 mins, or until tender.
Meanwhile, finely chop the walnuts and place in a bowl.

Melt the butter in a small saucepan over a medium heat. It will bubble for a couple of mins, then once the bubbles have died down, you’ll see the milk solids sink to the bottom of the pan and turn brown as they caramelise.
As soon as the mix starts to turn a light brown colour, remove the saucepan from the heat, add sage leaves and leave to sizzle for 1 minute.
Add the sage brown butter to the walnuts with the maple syrup and a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss to coat and pop in the oven for 10 mins. Leave the nuts to cool while you move back to the carrots.
Place the roasted carrots in a blender with the vegetable stock (just the stock listed until 'For the carrots') and blitz until smooth. Save for later.
Onto the risotto. Bring the stock (the stock listed under 'For the risotto') to a simmer then reduce the heat to low and cover. You want to keep the stock warm over very low heat.

Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-low heat. Finely chop your onion and garlic. Add the onion to the pan and cooking until translucent, then add garlic and cook for a further minute.
Add the risotto rice and cook, stirring often, until the grains begin to look translucent. Now add the wine and let it bubble away, stirring frequently, until the pan is almost dry.

Add one ladleful of the vegetable stock and cook, stirring almost constantly, until the liquid is absorbed. Repeat this process with the remaining stock until the rice is cooked. It should be tender with a very slight bite. The whole process should take around 25 mins. If you run out of stock before the rice is cooked, add one ladleful of hot water at a time and cook until the rice is done.
Stir in the carrot purée, parmesan and butter. Season with salt and pepper, to taste, then cover the saucepan and allow the risotto to sit for 3 mins before serving.

name: Spiced Carrot Soup
description: IKEA 365+ food containers are the perfect vessels for Madeleine Shaw’s vibrant, veg-packed soup. Limit your food waste by making a big batch for the week.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C.
Finely chop your shallots, garlic and ginger. Finely dice your carrots into cubes.
Fry the shallots in the coconut oil for 5 mins then add the garlic, ginger and curry paste and fry for a minute.
Stir in the carrots and season the dish, then add the stock and coconut milk. Simmer for 30 mins.
While the soup is simmering, make your topping. Roughly chop your almonds. Mix the almonds, tamari and maple together and roast for 15 minutes. Then leave to cool.
Back to the soup. Add the juice of a lime and your peanut butter to the liquid, then blend until smooth with a hand blender.
To serve, pour the soup into bowls. Add the almonds, basil leaves, yoghurt and chopped spring onions. Serve and enjoy.

name: Spiced Cauli, Chicken & Couscous Traybake
description: All the North African flavours you love in one golden traybake. Juicy spiced chicken, roasted cauliflower, sweet apricots and fluffy couscous – weeknight dinner, sorted.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Pat the chicken thighs dry with kitchen paper. Cut the cauliflower into 6 wedges, removing the thick green leaves but keeping the core and light green leaves  intact.

Add the chicken thighs and cauliflower onto to a large roasting tray. Sprinkle over the Moroccan seasoning, salt and pepper, then drizzle everything with the olive oil. Rub it all together so it’s evenly coated.
Slide into the oven and roast for 30 mins, or until the chicken skin is golden and crisp and the juices run clear.
Meanwhile, pick the coriander leaves and roughly chop the dried apricots.

Once the chicken is cooked, transfer it to a plate to rest. Tip the couscous, apricots and half the coriander into the tray. Pour over the chicken stock and stir gently to soak up all the roasting juices and flavour.
Return the tray to the oven for 3 mins while the chicken rests.
To serve, fluff the couscous, return the chicken on top, then scatter over the toasted almonds and remaining coriander.

name: Spiced Cauliflower Sandwich with Herby Whipped Tofu
description: Meet your new favourite vegan sando. It’s got big flavours and a satisfying combo of textures, with spiced roasted cauli, a crunchy slaw and a creamy pesto-whipped tofu.
keywords: Spiced Cauliflower Sandwich with Herby Whipped Tofu
Spiced Cauliflower Sandwich with Herby Whipped Tofu recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.
Remove the leaves from the cauliflower and set them aside. Cut the cauliflower into florets.
Lay the florets on a baking tray. Drizzle over plenty of olive oil and season with the paprika, cumin and salt and pepper. Toss well and roast for 15 mins until cooked through but still firm.

While the florets are roasting, remove and discard the tough stems from the cauliflower leaves. Finely slice the leaves and finely chop the parsley. Add to a small bowl along with the juice of the lemon, sesame seeds, chili flakes, olive oil and a pinch of salt. Toss well, season to taste and set aside.

To make the whipped tofu, drain the tofu then add it to a high speed blender. Juice in the lemon and add the remaining ingredients. Blend until smooth, adding a splash more water if it needs loosening.
Heat a dry frying pan over medium-high heat. Slice the ciabattas in half and drizzle both sides with a little olive oil. Toast in the hot pan on both sides until golden.

Spread the whipped tofu on the bottom side of the roll then top with the cauliflower, slaw and a sprinkling of extra sesame seeds. Spread the wholegrain mustard on the other side then pop it on top to close the sandwich.

name: Spiced Cauliflower, Almond Curry Sauce and Chilli Yog
description: You can never have too much sauce! This tasty veggie centrepiece has two: an almond-based, coconutty curry and a chilli yoghurt. I have no doubt you'll love it!
instructions: Thinly slice the red onion and place in a small bowl. Add the juice of the lemon, season with a good pinch of salt and scrunch with your hand to quick pickle.
Heat your oven to 220°C/ fan 200°C.
Cut the cauliflower into florets.

In a large bowl, combine the ground cumin, ground coriander, ground turmeric, ground cinnamon, garam masala and Kashmiri chilli powder with a generous pinch of salt and pepper and glug of extra-virgin olive oil.
Add the cauliflower florets and toss to coat. Transfer to a roasting tin and roast for 25-30 mins, or until cooked through but with a slight bite.
Meanwhile, slice the red onion, garlic and ginger and crush the cardamom pods.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add sliced red onion, season with salt and cook until softened.

Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, then add the crushed cardamom pods, ground cumin, ground coriander, ground turmeric, Kashmiri chilli powder and ground clove and cook for another minute.
Transfer to a food processor and add the blanched almonds, coconut milk and a splash of water. Season with salt and pepper, to taste, and blitz until smooth.
Combine the Greek yoghurt and Kashmiri chilli powder with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Spread the yoghurt on the base of a platter. Top with the cauliflower and drizzle lots and lots of that curry sauce on top. Finish with the quick-pickled onions, flaked almonds and fresh coriander then serve with the perfect side, a cold Good Earth Kombucha – enjoy!

name: Spiced Chicken & Roasted Carrot Pilaf
description: This pilaf rice recipe is perfect for using up leftovers. We've used chicken but feel free to use whatever your heart desires.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.  Rinse your rice under cold water 2-3 times until the water runs clear, add to a sieve and set aside.

Thinly slice the red onions and garlic. Set a large lidded pot over a high heat. Add the butter and ¾ of the onions and cook with a pinch of salt until gnarly, caramelised and starting to catch on the pan, this will take roughly 5-6 mins.

Add the garlic and cook for 1 min. Crush the cardamom pods and add to the pan with the turmeric, cinnamon and curry leaves. Chunk up the leftovers and add to the pot with the rinsed rice. Stir to coat everything in the spicy butter, season with salt and pour in the stock.
Bring to a simmer, then add a lid and pop into the oven for 20 mins to cook through. The liquid should all be absorbed by the rice, which will be tender and fluffy.
While the pilaf bakes, add the remaining onions to a bowl with the coriander. Add the juice of one lime and a pinch of salt. Toss together. Cut the remaining lime into wedges.
Allow the rice to rest for 5 mins before serving with the onion salad, extra lime and a blob of yoghurt.

name: Spiced Chicken Hummus Bowl
description: This hummus bowl is super simple to whip up on a weeknight, but boy does it pack a punch. Crispy chicken mince with minty chickpeas and a fresh tomato and cucumber salad, it's all I want to eat in the summertime. Ready in 30 mins, this one's going on repeat.
instructions: Roughly chop the tomatoes and dice the cucumber. Add the tomatoes to a large bowl, season with salt, drizzle over ⅖ of the extra virgin olive oil and toss. Leave to sit, the juices that collect will become part of the dressing. Finely grate the garlic, finely chop the parsley and pick the mint leaves.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat until shimmering. Add the chicken mince and press it down into the pan, resist stirring. Leave undisturbed for 3–4 mins until a deep golden crust forms on the bottom. Break it up, flip the larger pieces and leave again for 2–3 mins. You want it crackly and browned, not grey. Season with salt.

Add the garlic to the pan and cook for 30 seconds until just golden. Add the cumin, coriander, paprika and chilli flakes, stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, then toss everything together. Take off the heat and leave to cool.

Add the chickpeas, parsley, mint and cucumber to the bowl with the tomatoes. Once the mince has cooled, add it to the bowl too. Squeeze over the juice of the lemon, drizzle over the remaining three tbsp of extra virgin olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Toss well and taste for seasoning.
Divide the hummus between bowls and use the back of a spoon to spread it out and create swoops. Pile the chicken and salad on top and serve.

name: Spiced Chicken Meatballs & Green Bulgur
description: Comforting and zingy in equal measure. Herby green bulgur with cranberries and lentils, spiced chicken meatballs and cool cottage cheese. Big on protein too.
keywords: Spiced Chicken Meatballs & Green Bulgur recipe
instructions: Pour the water into a saucepan, season with salt and bring to the boil. Once boiling, add the bulgur, bring back to the boil and put a lid on top. Turn the heat down to low and cook for 10 mins, until the water has absorbed, then set aside.

Meanwhile, make the meatballs. Thinly slice the spring onions and add into a bowl with the mince, cottage cheese, cinnamon and black pepper. Season generously with salt and mix thoroughly, then portion out into 12 and roll into meatballs. Set aside.
Coarsely grate the courgette, finely chop the parsley and cranberries and zest the lemon. Add all four into a bowl with the lentils and the extra virgin olive oil.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Once hot, cook the meatballs for 10-12 mins, until golden brown and cooked through.
Fluff the bulgur with a fork, then add it into the grated courgette. Toss together and season with salt, pepper and the juice of the zested lemon.
Share the cottage cheese and bulgur between plates and top with the meatballs. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Spiced Chicken Shawarma Rice Bowl
description: Juicy, shawarma-spiced chicken piled high over warm rice, with jammy roasted tomatoes, sweet onions and a cool hit of garlicky yoghurt. Delish.
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C and start with the veg prep. Slice the red onion into wedges, grate the garlic for the chicken and thinly slice the cucumber and chop the fresh parsley.
Add the red onion wedges and cherry tomatoes to a baking dray with a drizzle of olive oil and salt, tossing to coat. Roast for 20–25 minutes until softened and lightly charred at the edges.

While the veg is cooking, get on with the chicken. Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken mince and fry for 10 mins, until browned, breaking it up well so it caramelises rather than steams (you can do this in batches as well to help the meat crisp up).
Once the meat is golden and crispy, stir through the ground cumin, coriander, paprika, chilli flakes, grated garlic, harissa and salt. Fry for 5 mins, until fragrant and cooked through.
Grate in the remaining garlic for the sauce into a small bowl and squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Mix with Greek yoghurt, olive oil, and salt until smooth and creamy.
Mix the roasted tomatoes and onions with the julienned cucumber and chopped parsley. Add a sprinkle of salt and another squeeze of lemon juice.
Warm the rice and divide between two bowls. Spoon over the roasted tomato and onion salad. Top generously with the kofte-spiced chicken mince and finish with garlic yoghurt over the top.

name: Spiced Chicken Skewers with Yoghurt Flatbreads
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Homemade yoghurt flatbreads are the perfect vessel for these tangy grilled chicken skewers.
keywords: Spiced Chicken Skewers With Yoghurt Flatbreads
Spiced Chicken Skewers With Yoghurt Flatbreads recipe
instructions: Chuck the yoghurt, curry powder, grated garlic clove and finely chopped chilli into a bowl. Add the zest and juice of a lemon, season with salt and pepper and mix. Chunk up the chicken thighs and tip into the bowl. Stir through the marinade and set aside for 30 mins.

Add the self-raising flour, baking powder and salt into a large bowl and mix to combine. Stir through the yoghurt until a shaggy dough forms, then knead for 3-5 mins until smooth. Divide the dough into 4 balls, cover and let rest for 5 mins.

Place a frying pan on medium-high heat. Dust a work surface with a little flour and roll the balls of dough out until thin, around 2mm. Once the pan starts smoking, place a flatbread on and cook on both sides until golden and almost charred, for a total of 2-3 mins. Keep the flatbreads warm folded up in a clean cloth or tea towel.

To finish the chicken, preheat the oven to 220°C. Thread the chicken onto two skewers, creating a large kebab and drizzle with olive oil. Pop onto a tray and slide into the oven. Roast for 15-20 mins or until charred and completely cooked through. If you want a little more colour on the chicken, crank up the grill and finish under there.
Halve the tomatoes and toss with oil and salt. Scatter in some mint leaves and finish with a squeeze of lemon.
Remove the chicken from the skewers and pile onto the flatbreads with extra yoghurt, mint leaves, the tomato salad and a dollop of chutney. Save the leftover flatbreads.

name: Spiced Chicken Soup With Yoghurt & Flatbreads
description: A cosy, aromatic stew is the perfect way to use up roast chicken leftovers. Packed with chickpeas and finished with lemon, yoghurt, and warm flatbreads, it’s the ultimate comforting dinner.
instructions: Before you begin, make the No-Fuss Roast Chicken.
Finely chop the red onion, ginger and garlic cloves.

Preheat a large pan over a medium-high heat. Add a shot of olive oil and tip in the diced onion. Add a pinch of salt and cook for 5-6 mins before adding the spices, garlic and ginger. Cook for 3-4 mins before adding the chickpeas (and their liquid) and chicken stock. Bring to a boil and cook for 8-10 mins until thick and reduced a little. Roughly chop the cavolo nero and add to the stew, cooking for another 10-12 mins.

Shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces and stir through the soup. Add the zest and juice of the lemon and finish with chopped dill and a generous glug of olive oil. Serve with yoghurt, a sprinkle of ras el hanout and warm flatbreads.

name: Spiced Chicken With Chilli Tomato Salad & Zingy Tahini Dressing
description: A fast and flavour-packed meal with punchy chicken thighs, tempered rice with crispy cashews, a chilli-spiked tomato salad, and a silky tahini dressing to tie it all together. Ideal for making ahead and eating hot or cold.
keywords: Spiced Chicken Lunchbox with Chilli Tomato Salad & Zingy Tahini Dressing
Spiced Chicken Lunchbox with Chilli Tomato Salad & Zingy Tahini Dressing recipe
instructions: Heat a splash of olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the cashews and fry until golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Lower the heat, then add the mustard seeds and fry until they begin to pop. Add the urid dal, asafoetida, ginger, curry leaves, turmeric, and dried chillies. Fry for 3–4 mins until the lentils are golden. Remove from the heat and squeeze in the juice of the lemons. Stir through the cooked rice and cashews season well and set aside.

In a bowl, combine the grated garlic, sumac, Lebanese 7-spice, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then add to the bowl and mix until coated. Heat a large frying pan with oil over medium-high heat. Cook the thighs for 8–10 mins, turning until deeply golden and cooked through. Rest briefly, then slice.
In a bowl, combine the chopped tomatoes with the finely sliced spring onions. Stir through the crispy chilli oil and rice vinegar. Season with salt and toss to coat. Set aside.

Add the unpeeled garlic cloves to a blender with lemon juice and cumin. Blend until smooth. Pour the purée into a fine mesh sieve set over a bowl and press to extract the liquid. Discard solids. Whisk in the tahini — it will seize and thicken. Add a splash of cold water at a time, whisking, until you reach a smooth, yoghurt-like consistency. Season with salt.
Divide the lemon rice between lunchboxes. Top with sliced chicken and spoonfuls of tomato salad. Pack the tahini dressing separately and drizzle on when serving.

name: Spiced Chicken with Cashew Curry Leaf Sprinkle
description: Spiced golden chicken with a crunchy curry leaf cashew sprinkle and a zesty yoghurt cucumber salad. It's delish.
keywords: spiced chicken with cashew curry leaf sprinkle
chicken and rice with cucumber yoghurt
instructions: Finely grate the garlic into a large bowl. Add the curry powder, a generous pinch of salt and black pepper, then drizzle in enough olive oil to make a paste. Stir the chicken thighs through until coated, then set aside to marinate.

For the sprinkle, roughly chop the cashews and add ½ Tbsp curry powder to a heatproof bowl. Add a generous drizzle of olive oil to a frying pan set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the chopped cashews and fry, stirring, until golden. Using a slotted spoon, transfer them to the curry powder bowl, leaving the oil in the pan.
Return the pan to the heat and fry the mustard seeds and curry leaves in the remaining oil until the sizzling subsides. Tip the toasted spices into the cashews and mix well.

Thinly slice the cucumber or mandolin it into a bowl. Stir through the yoghurt and grate in the zest of ¼ of the lemon. Season with salt and pepper. Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the stalks.
Return the pan to a medium heat. Once hot, fry the chicken thighs for 10–15 mins, flipping halfway, until golden and cooked through.
Reheat the rice and divide between bowls. Toss the coriander leaves and stems through the cucumber salad.
Top each bowl with chicken, the cucumber salad, a dollop of yoghurt, and a big spoonful of the spiced cashew sprinkle. Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: Spiced Chicken, Coconut Greens & Rice
description: Spiced chicken thighs laid on top of jasmine rice that steams itself in coconut milk in the oven. Fragrant, a little sweet and all done in one tray.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add the chicken thighs to a large bowl, season generously with salt and pepper. Finely grate half the garlic, then stir through the curry powder and soy sauce. Set aside.

Wash the rice until the water runs clear. Bash the ginger. Add both to a deep-sided baking tray and pour over the boiling water and coconut milk. Season with salt.
