Lay the chicken on top, then slide into the oven and cook for 25-30 mins, until the water has fully absorbed and the chicken is cooked through.

Meanwhile, trim and halve the green beans. Finely grate the remaining garlic into a frying pan, add the green beans and desiccated coconut and drizzle with the olive oil. Stir everything together, cover with a lid and place over a medium-high heat. Steam-fry for 2-3 mins, then remove the lid, add a splash of water and cook until the beans are tender, adding a splash more water if needed to keep the steam going. Remove from the heat and season with salt and pepper. Grate over a quarter of the lime zest.
Fluff the rice with a fork and divide between plates. Top with the chicken and beans. Serve with the remaining lime cut into wedges.

name: Spiced Chickpea Stew with Crispy Meatless Mince
description: A spicy chickpea stew in rich tomatoey sauce, topped with the crispy plant-based mince. It's healthy. It's veggie. It's delicious.
instructions: To start, chop up a garlic clove and whack into a pan with a glug of olive oil, your plant-based mince, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp smoked paprika and 1 tsp cinnamon. Break up and fry until crispy. Set aside and cover with foil.
Next, finely chop your onion and 2 garlic cloves. Heat a glug of oil and fry the onion and garlic for 5 minutes.
When soft, add 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp sugar, a sprinkle of salt and your cumin. Mix together.
Next, toss in your chickpeas with their water and chopped tomatoes and mix. Then add your stock cubes and mix until fully dissolved.
Chop your coriander, add to the tomato mix (saving some for a garnish) then set aside.
In a separate bowl, mix together your tahini, lemon juice, glug of oil, cup of water, salt and pepper. Keep stirring until you have a thick paste and set aside.

Once finished, its time to plate up. Spoon your stew into 4 bowls and drizzle with your tahini paste. Sprinkle over your crispy mince (re-heating in a pan if required) and any leftover coriander leaves then tuck in!

name: Spiced Duck Ragu with Zesty Breadcrumbs
description: This recipe is inspired by an old Venetian-style duck ragu, flavoured with cinnamon and topped with crunchy orange breadcrumbs. a perfect blend of tender duck legs and a flavourful sauce that will elevate your pasta dishes to new heights.
instructions: Place the duck legs skin side down into a large, cold pan, then place the pan over a medium heat (this will let the fat render as the legs come up to temperature) and cook for about 5 mins each side until golden and crispy.
Remove the duck from the pan and set aside.
Finely chop the onion and celery and add to the pan. Cook for about 10 mins until softened.
Peel the garlic and add along with the sage, bay leaves and cinnamon and cook for another 2 mins.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble away and reduce by three quarters.
Add the chopped tomatoes, the stock, and a big pinch of salt and pepper. Bring up to a simmer, return the duck to the pan (make sure it’s submerged) and cover with foil or parchment and a lid.
Simmer gently for about 2 hours until the duck is tender.
Remove the duck from the pan and discard the skin and bones. Shred the duck and return to the sauce.
Put the pasta onto cook in plenty of boiling salted water.
Meanwhile, heat a frying pan over a medium heat and add a splash of olive oil. Add the breadcrumbs and cook until golden brown. Remove from the heat, grate in the orange zest, mix well and set aside.
Once the pasta is cooked, combine with the sauce and a splash of pasta water, mixing well to emulsify.
Plate up and top with the zesty breadcrumbs.

name: Spiced Fish with Mango Salsa
description: The fragrance from the cinnamon and the allspice and the beautifully flakey fish, partnered with the fresher than fresh mango salsa. Heaven in a mouthful.
instructions: Coat your cod with a drizzle of olive oil, allspice, and salt. Grate one of your scotch bonnets over the cod and rub everything in, then marinate for 15 minutes.

To make your salsa, slice half of the tomatoes in half, chop up the mango, spring onion, and coriander, then squeeze the juice of the lime on top. Mix it all up in a bowl with some salt, pepper and olive oil.

Heat up a glug of olive oil in a pan whilst you slice your onions and peppers. Then, add your onions and peppers to the pan along with allspice, cinnamon, thyme; grate in your other scotch bonnet and cook on a low heat. Fry until the onions have softened, then add the remaining tomatoes.
Once the tomatoes have softened, add your veggie stock and bring to the boil before adding your cod. Cover to steam for 10 minutes.
Cook your Caribbean rice & peas according to the packet instructions.
Portion up your rice with the cod then garnish with your salsa and get stuck in!

name: Spiced Green Chickpeas & Paneer
description: A punchy, protein-packed veggie curry with paneer and creamy green spinach sauce. Perfect for weeknights when you want something quick and healthy.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Add the spinach and cook for 1-2 mins until wilted. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the spinach to a blender with some water from the pan and blitz until smooth.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Dice the paneer into 2cm cubes and finely chop the garlic.

Heat the oil in a pan over a medium heat. Add the mustard and cumin seeds and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant and popping. Stir in the chopped garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until golden.
Pour in the spinach purée and tip in the chickpeas. Stir through the chilli powder, if using, and add the paneer. Bring everything to a gentle simmer for 3-4 mins. Pick the coriander.
Take the pan off the heat and leave to cool slightly. Then stir through the Greek yoghurt and season to taste with salt and black pepper.
To serve, spoon into bowls and top with coriander and a sprinkle of nigella seeds, if you fancy.

name: Spiced Green Coconut Chickpeas
description: A gorgeous, green batch cook recipe that you can eat as it is or turn into a range of delicious dishes. Chickpeas have never tasted this good.
keywords: Batch Cook: Spiced Green Coconut Chickpeas
instructions: Add all the spinach into a bowl and microwave for 4-8 mins until defrosted. Squeeze the water out into a separate bowl and set aside. Add half of the spinach to a blender with half of the coconut milk, then blitz until smooth. Set aside.
Thinly slice the chillies, then grate the garlic and ginger.

Pour half of the remaining coconut milk into a saucepan and place onto medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the coconut milk splits. You'll know it's split when it starts to resemble coconut oil with little bits of toasted grain in it. Add the cumin seeds and cook until they start to shimmer. Stir the chilli, garlic, ginger and garam masala through, then add the tomato purée and cook for 3-4 mins until darkened.

Stir the chickpeas and blended coconutty spinach mixture through. Add the remaining spinach and coconut milk, stir and bring to the boil. Season with salt and pepper, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10-15 mins until creamy. Add a splash of the spinach water to loosen, if needed. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Divide the mixture between three containers. Refrigerate or freeze until needed.

name: Spiced Halloumi & Chickpea Saag
description: A creamy, spicy hug of a curry. Halloumi and chickpeas bring the protein, and it only gets better with time, so batch it up!
instructions: Dice the halloumi into 1.5cm cubes. Heat a large deep frying pan over a medium-high heat. Dry-fry the halloumi for 3-4 mins until golden on most sides, then remove and set aside (no need to wash the pan).

Add the ghee or butter to the same pan. Peel and finely chop the onion, then fry for 3-4 mins until softened and golden at the edges. Peel and mince the garlic, peel and mince the ginger, then finely chop the green chilli, if using. Stir these into the pan and cook for 1 min.
Add the curry powder and half of the garam masala, then stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add all the spinach to the pan (fresh in batches, frozen all at once). Cook, stirring, for 8-10 mins until wilted and most of the liquid has evaporated.

Add the chickpeas and stir through. Remove from the heat and leave to cool slightly for a few minutes. Add the yoghurt and gently stir through, off the heat! Season with salt and lemon juice to taste.
Add the halloumi back to the pan and heat through gently. Sprinkle over the remaining garam masala.
Serve over rice with some fresh coriander and sliced red chillies.

name: Spiced Halloumi Fries
description: Aromatic spices and halloumi = the flavour combination of your dreams. Topped with the cooling herby yoghurt. Heavenly.
instructions: Finely chop the red onion. Slice the red chilli. Set both aside.
Pat the halloumi blocks dry and cut into fries.
Mix together the flour, turmeric, cumin and coriander seeds on a plate. Roll the fries in the mixture, ensuring they are all evenly covered.
Blend the yoghurt with the mint, half the coriander, 1 green chilli, 1 garlic clove and a squeeze of lemon. Season with salt and pepper. You want it to be a vivid green colour.
Fill a wide frying pan up to about 2cm with oil. Heat until visibly bubbling.
Carefully lower in one of the Halloumi fries as a tester - you want them to go golden but if the oil is too hot they will colour too much and burn.
Cook the Halloumi fries in batches until they float. Once cooked, lay them out on a few layers of kitchen paper to remove any excess oil.
Pile the Indian Halloumi fries onto a platter. Dollop on the yoghurt & mango chutney. Whack on the chopped onion, chilli and the remaining coriander. Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Spiced Hot Toddy
description: We've made a Hot Toddy using rum instead of whiskey, and it really is delicious. The perfect winter cocktail doesn't ex...
instructions: Put your kettle on.
Slice your lemon in half and save a slice for garnish, then juice it.
Get your lemon juice, honey, rum, star anise, cinnamon stick and lemon slice in a glass or mug with a handle.
Fill it up with hot water and mix to dissolve all the ingredients.
Wait until slightly cooled and tuck in.

name: Spiced Iced Caprese Soup
description: We all love a summery Caprese salad, so guess what? We've turned it into an iced soup! It's lovely and refreshing.
instructions: Cut tomatoes into quarters. Peel and roughly chop the cucumber, then peel the garlic. Halve the chilli and remove its seeds. Add all the vegetables into a blender and blitz until smooth. It needs to be really smooth, so keep blending!

With the motor running, add the sherry vinegar and olive oil in a continuous stream. This will emulsify and thicken the soup. If you like, you can pass the soup through a fine sieve to make it extra smooth. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Pop in the fridge to chill for at least a couple of hours or until very cold.
When you’re ready to eat, pre-heat the oven to 180°C. Make the croutons by tearing up the ciabatta and drizzling with oil, salt and pepper. Cook for 15 mins or until golden.
Serve the soup in chilled bowls with a couple of ice cubes, then top with the torn burrata, basil leaves, croutons, and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Spiced Kedgeree with Smoked Haddock
description: This quick kedgeree dish using ready-cooked rice is a delight. Cooked up with smoky fish spiced with fresh lime leaves and cumin seeds.
instructions: Dice the onion, pick the coriander leaves, discarding the stems.
Add the eggs to a small saucepan and cover with water, bring to boil and simmer for 6 minutes. Once cooked, leave eggs in a bowl of iced cold water to cool down. Then, peel and halve the eggs.
In another saucepan, place the haddock and cover it with some water. Add the 1/2 lime leaf and bring to a boil. Turn down the heat to a gentle simmer and poach for 5 minutes.
Remove the fish and the kaffir lime leaf from the pan and set to the side - you can flake the fish at the end.

Place the empty pan on a medium heat, add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, sauté your onion until transluscent. Add the mustard and cumin seeds to the saucepan and heat for a couple of minutes until fragrant.
Grate the lemon zest, ginger and garlic into the onions. Stir-fry for a minute, and then add the curry powder, remaining lime leaf, a squeeze of lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir through the cooked rice with 2 tbsp water, until piping hot. Remove from the heat and flake the fish through. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Share the rice onto plates and top with a drizzle of yoghurt, egg and a scattering of coriander.

name: Spiced Keema Mix
description: This spiced keema is my go-to uni meal prep. It’s delicious, speedy and versatile – mix it with rice, pasta and potatoes, or toast it between two cheesy parathas.
instructions: Finely chop or grate the garlic and ginger and dice the onion. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat, pour in the oil, then add the garlic and ginger and fry gently until caramelised.

Carefully tip in the chopped onion, along with a pinch of salt and a few cracks of black pepper. Cook for 5-10 mins until translucent, then add the mince to the pan and cook for around 7-10 mins until browned.
Add all the spices and allow the powders to cook in the oils and infuse with the minced meat for another 5 mins.
Squeeze in the tomato purée and a splash of water, stir until thickened. Season to taste with salt and pepper, if needed.
Serve garnished with coriander leaves and chopped green chillies, if you like. Eat alongside paratha or roti, and side salad, raita, and onion or mango pickle.

name: Spiced Lamb & Filo Pie
description: The crispiest pie topping with a lip-smacking spicy lamb filling. It’s impressive, deceptively simple and oh-so good.
instructions: Finely chop the onion and red peppers, then dice the potato.
Bash the garlic, ginger and red chillies in a pestle and mortar with a big pinch of salt to make a thick paste.

Add a big glug of oil to a pan and fry off the onions for 10 mins until soft and slightly golden. Add in the tomato purée and cook for 5 mins until it has darkened. Then add the chilli paste and cook for 2 mins until fragrant. Add in the turmeric, allspice and paprika and give it a mix.
Add in the lamb mince and cook for 10 mins until it’s cooked through.
Add in the potatoes with 100ml of water and cook for 5 mins just until the potatoes are half cooked.
Mix in the chopped red peppers.
Season with salt and pepper, then allow this filling to cool fully in a bowl.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Melt the butter and combine with 150ml of water.
Brush the butter water mixture over the filo pastry, and lay out 3 sheets in the bottom of a 20cm cake tin. Fill with the lamb mixture and cover the top with more brushed filo pastry.
Bake in the oven for 30 mins or until the top is golden brown.
Allow to cool for 10 mins before cutting.
Slice up and serve warm!

name: Spiced Lamb Burger
description: This is my spiced lamb burger. It's hot, juicy, salty, tangy and crunchy. Everything you want out of a burger. @dinnerbyben x
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the red onion into rings. Separate the rings and pop them into a heatproof bowl.
Add the vinegar and sugar to a small saucepan and bring to a boil. Add 30ml of water, a bay leaf and the coriander seeds. Pour over the onions and set aside.
Combine the lamb, harissa, and smoked paprika in a mixing bowl. Season with salt and mix thoroughly for 2-3 mins.
Fry off a small piece and taste for seasoning. Add a little more salt or spice if you fancy, and form into four burger patties.
Slice up your feta, drain your pickled onions, and wash the watercress.
Coarsely grate the cucumber, season with salt and squeeze over a sieve to remove the excess moisture.
Add to a bowl with the yoghurt, season with salt and mix.
Toast off your buns and slice up and season the tomato with salt, pepper and olive oil.
Preheat your cast iron pan over a medium-high heat.
Cook the burgers, giving them a gentle smash as they hit the pan, until they’re sitting around medium doneness. This should take about 4-5 mins on each side.

Now, time to build. Start with the bottom bun, a spoon of the cucumber yoghurt, top with a slice of tomato and the lamb burger. Now add some sliced feta, a handful of pickled onions and watercress. Finish with more cucumber yoghurt and the lid.
Smash it in half, and get stuck in.

name: Spiced Lamb Chops With Chilli Mint Salsa
description: A simple, summery and spicy dish that'll make you forget about any overcooked lamb chops you've ever had before. Pairs perfectly with sunshine and Inch’s Cider.
keywords: Spiced Lamb Chops With Chilli Mint Salsa
instructions: Add 2/3 of the yoghurt to a bowl and tip in the garam masala. Finely grate in the ginger and 2/3 of the garlic cloves. Add the juice of half a lemon, a big pinch of salt and a good glug of oil. Season the lamb thoroughly with salt and pepper and chuck into the yoghurt mix. Cover and place in the fridge to marinade for at least 30 mins up to overnight.

Finely grate the rest of your garlic into the remaining yoghurt, season to taste and set aside. Thinly slice the red onions, dice the tomatoes, cut the cucumber into bitesize chunks, and drain the chickpeas.

Preheat the grill to high. Slide half of your chillies under there with a little oil and cook until charred. Pull from the pan and finely chop into a paste. Add to a bowl with a few tbsp of oil and mix to create a gnarly chilli oil.
Pull the lamb chops out the marinade, leaving a little on the chops. Cook in the pan over medium-high heat for 4 mins on each side until medium. Pull out and rest on a tray.
Tip the onions, cucumber, tomatoes and chickpeas into a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Add a little olive oil and a few mint leaves. Add the juice from half your lemons and set aside.

Add ¾ of the remaining mint to a food processor. Add 4 tbsp of oil, the remaining half of the chillies finely chopped (seeds too if you like it hot) and the juice from your remaining lemon and just a dash of olive oil. Whizz into a smooth green salsa and season to taste. Set aside.
Heat the flatbreads according to the pack instructions.
Set the bread onto a large platter and tip on the chopped salad. Top with the charred gnarly lamb chops. Finish with the mint chilli salsa, chilli oil, garlic yoghurt, and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Spiced Lamb Meatball Orzo
description: This is one of those insanely comforting dishes that you can eat all year round. Plump little meatballs. Rich tomato orzo. Lemony crème fraîche. A beauty.
instructions: Grate ½ the onion. Combine with breadcrumbs in a large mixing bowl and leave to sit and hydrate for 5 mins.
Roughly chop your parsley.
Into the mixing bowl with the breadcrumbs, add your lamb mince, parsley, cinnamon, and plenty of salt and pepper. Combine with your hands.
Roll into golf-ball sized balls. Fry for about 3 mins until they have taken on some colour on the outside, but aren’t totally cooked through. Set aside.
Finely slice your remaining onion. Finely chop your garlic.
Add a glug of olive oil to a wide casserole dish, then tip in your onions. Cook for about 15 mins on a medium heat until caramelised.

Add the garlic and chilli flakes in with the caramelised onions, and cook for another 2 mins. Pour in your white wine and let it reduce by half. Add your passata and the water, then simmer for 15 mins on a low heat.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil.
Tip your orzo into the water and cook for 7 mins.
Add your meatballs to the tomato sauce and gently simmer for another 5 mins.
Drain your orzo. Gently mix with the sauce and meatballs to combine, adding some pasta water to loosen it up where necessary. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Combine the zest and juice of ½ the lemon in a bowl with your crème fraîche. Drizzle this over the top of the orzo, then top with grated parmesan, fresh basil leaves and more black pepper.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Spiced Lamb Meatballs with Minty Fennel Slaw
description: Juicy fragrant meatballs and a lovely little slaw. This has summer written all over it. Perfect with a refreshing Inch's Cider.
keywords: Spiced Lamb Meatballs with Minty Fennel Slaw
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Get your lamb mince into a large mixing bowl and season with salt.
Toast the whole spices in a dry pan until fragrant, then coarsely grind in a spice grinder or pestle and mortar.
Add the breadcrumbs to a bowl and add 60ml of cold water.

Add the spices, soaked breadcrumbs, raisins and pine nuts to the lamb and give everything a very thorough mix. You want the mix to be a bit sticky. Now roll into golf ball-sized meatballs, pop onto a tray and set aside.

Drain and rinse the chickpeas and chuck them into a roasting tin with a glug of oil, two whole chillies and half a thinly sliced onion. Thinly slice the other half and save it for later. Roast the chickpeas for 30 mins until crispy, golden and delicious.

While the chickpeas roast, pan fry the meatballs in a glug of oil over a medium heat until golden on all sides and cooked through. This should take about 15 mins. Add your harissa to the pan for the last couple of mins and finish with a big squeeze of lemon juice. Let the meatballs rest while you finish the other bits.
Pull the chickpeas out of the oven, deseed and chop the roasted chillies and stir through with lemon juice and a handful of chopped mint.
Finely slice the fennel and chuck into a bowl with the remaining onion, chillies, mint and finish with salt and lemon juice.
Mix the yoghurt and tahini with salt, lemon juice and enough water to give a loose, spreadable consistency.
Spread the yoghurt and tahini on the bottom of a plate, top with the chickpeas and meatballs, plus any beautiful oil and lemon from the pan, and finish with the fennel salad. Get stuck in.

name: Spiced Lemon Rice
description: This South Indian recipe is a great way to use up leftover rice. Make a big batch of the lemon mix and store it in the fridge for weeks. Just mix with some cooked rice any time and serve hot, warm or even cold.
instructions: Squeeze the lemon juice into a bowl. Set aside.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the cashews and fry until golden. Transfer to a kitchen paper-lined plate using a slotted spoon, then set aside.

Turn the heat down to low. Tip the mustard seeds into the same pan and fry until the seeds crackle, then add the remaining ingredients (except the lemon juice and rice). Fry everything for 3-4 mins until the lentils are golden.
Add the hot mixture to the lemon juice bowl and stir well. Add the cashews and allow the dish to rest for 15 mins.
Stir the cooked rice through the rested mixture. Serve warm or cold.

name: Spiced Lemon Rice
description: This South Indian recipe is a great way to use up leftover rice. Make a big batch of the lemon mix and store it in the fridge for weeks. Just mix with some cooked rice any time and serve hot, warm or even cold.
instructions: Squeeze the lemon juice into a bowl. Set aside.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the cashews and fry until golden. Transfer to a kitchen paper-lined plate using a slotted spoon, then set aside.

Turn the heat down to low. Tip the mustard seeds into the same pan and fry until the seeds crackle, then add the remaining ingredients (except the lemon juice and rice). Fry everything for 3-4 mins until the lentils are golden.
Add the hot mixture to the lemon juice bowl and stir well. Add the cashews and allow the dish to rest for 15 mins.
Stir the cooked rice through the rested mixture. Serve warm or cold.

name: Spiced Lemon Rice with Curry Leaves, Lemon Peel & Tuna
description: A speedy, easy rice dish spiced with fresh curry leaves, whole green chillies and lemon peel with fennel, mustard and nigella seeds. With so few ingredients, this is a winning midweek, storecupboard staple of a recipe.
keywords: spiced lemon rice with curry leaves
instructions: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear, then drain well. Finely dice the onion.

Tip the butter into a medium saucepan set over a medium heat, then add the curry leaves, whole green chillies, fennel seeds, black mustard seeds and nigella seeds. Cook for 30 seconds until the seeds pop and sizzle, then add the onion and cook over a slightly lower heat for around 10 mins until soft.

Add the rice, water, the zest of the lemon in thin strips, a pinch of salt and plenty of black pepper, then cover the pan and cook for about 20 mins, or until all the water has been absorbed and the rice is cooked through.

When the rice is cooked, add the juice of the lemon and fluff up the rice with a fork to serve. Check the seasoning, adjusting with more salt and pepper as necessary, then flake in the tuna. Finish by drizzling the reserved tuna can oil over the dish.

name: Spiced Lentils with Couscous & Buttered Pine Nuts
description: Adding dried fruits to savoury ragù is a great way to add nutrients and flavour. We’ve used apricots and spices to turn this batch cook into a warming, tagine-inspired dish.
instructions: Make the Mushroom & Lentil Ragú.
Reheat the Mushroom & Lentil Ragú in a saucepan over a medium heat.
Dice the apricots and add to the lentils.

Put the couscous into a bowl and pour over the boiling water. Season with salt, pepper and a drizzle of olive oil, then cover with a plate or cling film. Leave to stand for 5-10 mins (or according to package instructions) then fluff up with a fork.
Melt the butter in a separate pan over a medium heat and add the pine nuts. Cook until the butter starts to smell nutty, then remove from the heat and add the spices.
To serve, divide the couscous between bowls and spoon over the lentils. Top with the buttery pine nuts and parsley.

name: Spiced Pea and Potato Rolls
description: We were inspired by a filling you might traditionally find in a samosa to create this delicious vegetarian sausage roll.
instructions: Start by prepping your vegetables. Dice your potatoes into 1 inch chunks, slice your onion, grate your garlic and ginger, and finely dice your chilli. Roughly chop your fresh coriander.

Place your potatoes in a medium-sized pan of water and season with salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes or until your potatoes are tender. Drain in a colander and leave to steam dry there.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a sauté pan over medium heat. Add your cumin seeds and mustard seeds, then cook out for a minute until fragrant and starting to pop.
Pop your onions in the pan and cook over a medium heat for 15 minutes, until soft and caramelised. Add your garlic, ginger, and chilli to the pan and cook out for another 2 minutes.

Add your cumin, ground coriander, ½ tsp turmeric, chilli powder, and garam masala along with your peas and cook for 5 mins. Tip in your potatoes and lime pickle, stirring so that the potato chunks are totally coated in the spices and onions. Stir through the chopped fresh coriander.
Season to taste and set aside to cool.

Beat your egg or coconut oil with your remaining turmeric. Unravel your puff pastry. Place your filling in a line slightly off-centre on the puff pastry. Cut diagonal incisions on the longer edge of pastry. Brush the other side with beaten egg or coconut oil, then fold the cut side over.
Press the edges to seal, then brush the entire outside with egg wash. Chill in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Heat your oven to 190°C. Cut your roll into 4 lengths, then place spaced apart on a large baking sheet. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until your pastry is tender and golden.

name: Spiced Pork Belly With Rice
description: Ginger + allspice come together to make the most delicious sticky pork. Fragrant and deeply savoury. Served on a bed of creamy coconut rice and beans.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C/392°F.

Cut the pork belly slices into 3cm pieces. Whack into a roasting tin, drizzle with a little olive oil, sprinkle over the all or mixed spice and season well with salt and black pepper. Toss together then separate the pieces out into a single layer. Roast in the oven for around 30 minutes, turning halfway until turning golden and crisp.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. In a blender or mini food processor, blitz the chillies, garlic, ginger, thyme leaves, brown sugar, vinegar and most of the spring onions with 200ml water to make a sauce. Mix through half the cinnamon and season well with salt and pepper.
Once the pork belly has been cooking for 30 minutes, bring it out of the oven and pour over the spiced sauce. Return to the oven for a further 20 minutes, stirring halfway.

Meanwhile, rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water until it is no longer cloudy. Drain, then tip into a saucepan. Drain and rinse the beans, add them too. Pour in the coconut milk, then refill the can halfway with water and pour that in. Season well with salt, add the remaining cinnamon, and bring to the boil. Once boiling turn down the heat to low, whack a lid on the pan, and simmer the rice for 15 minutes until all the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender. If the rice is done before the pork, turn off the heat and keep the lid on the pan to keep warm.
Finely slice the remaining spring onions. Serve the rice topped with the spiced pork. Scatter over the spring onions and serve with a big salad and corn if you like.

name: Spiced Ratatouille With Halloumi Croutons
description: We’ve taken everything you love about ratatouille and given it a twist by adding in a load of whole spices. The halloumi croutons make this a belter of a dish.
instructions: Cut the aubergine, courgette and mixed peppers into medium-sized pieces. Season well with salt and black pepper.

Get your largest saucepan over a high heat and drizzle in a good glug of olive oil. Chuck in a third of your veg. Fry for 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until beginning to soften. Transfer to a bowl and repeat. Tip all the veg out of the pan.

Finely slice four spring onions and chop the garlic cloves. Put the saucepan back over the heat and drizzle in a little more oil. Scrape in the spring onions and garlic, cook for 1 minute then add the cumin and coriander seeds, chilli flakes and 1 tsp of nigella seeds. Cook for 30 seconds until everything smells amazing then tip all your veg back into the pan.

Add the tins of tomatoes. Refill one tin with water and pour that in too then give everything a good stir. Bring to the boil, turn down the heat and leave the ratatouille to simmer away for 45–50 mins until all the veg is completely cooked. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.

Halloumi time. Cut into cubes and chuck into a bowl. Add the remaining nigella seeds and toss to coat. Get a large non-stick frying pan over a high heat. Fry the halloumi for 2–3 mins, turning regularly, until golden and crisp. Finely slice the remaining spring onions.
Divide the ratatouille between four bowls. Top with the halloumi croutons and scatter over the remaining spring onion. Serve with naan or chapatis, if you like.

name: Spiced Red Cabbage with Pomegranate Molasses & Orange
description: This Christmas-y cabbage is the perfect combo of sweet, sour and savoury, with pomegranate seeds for extra crunch. It tastes even better the day after so it's a good one to prep in advance.
keywords: Spiced Red Cabbage with Pomegranate Molasses & Orange
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C fan.
Very thinly slice the onion and cabbage, keeping them separate for now. Heat the olive oil in a large ovenproof pan set over a moderate heat. Add the onion and fry for 5 mins until softened.
Add the bay leaves, peeled garlic, bay leaves, star anise, cinnamon stick and dried red chilli to the pan and cook for another minute, until fragrant.
Add the cabbage to the pan and stir well to coat. Sauté for 5–7 mins, until the cabbage starts to soften slightly.

Thinly peel the zest of the orange and add to the pan, along with its juice. Stir in the water, molasses, a generous pinch of salt and plenty of freshly ground black pepper. Stir well to coat the cabbage in the mixture.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then cover with a lid and transfer to the oven to cook for 30–35 mins, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is tender and has absorbed most of the liquid.
Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley and remove the pomegranate seeds from the fruit (or use packet pomegranate seeds if you prefer).
Remove the cabbage from the oven and pick out the garlic, whole spices, orange zest and bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning, adding a bit more salt or molasses as desired.
Before serving, stir through the parsley and scatter over the pomegranate seeds.

name: Spiced Roast Tomato & Pepper Bowl
description: A herby, spicy, sweet vegetable bowl, with a crunchy side salad. All topped with a garlicky red wine dressing and crispy capers. A really nice healthy dish.
instructions: Preheat the grill to high. Drain the peppers, thinly slice.

Add the tomatoes, coriander seeds and fennel seeds onto a baking tray. Season with salt and pepper, drizzle with oil. Slide onto the middle rack, under the grill. Roast for 10-15 mins, until the tomatoes are starting to soften and char a little, and the spices have toasted. Turn the grill down a little, if the veg/spices are colouring too quickly.
Thinly slice the fennel. Pick the parsley leaves. Add the fennel and peppers into a bowl with the vinegar. Season with salt.
Place a frying pan with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the capers. Fry for a few minutes until crispy. Transfer them into the veg. Reheat the quinoa according to packet instructions.
Once the tomatoes are ready, tip them along with the spices into the pepper mixture. Toss together.
Share the quinoa between plates and top with the salad. Finish with a crumble of feta.

name: Spiced Roast Tomato Soup
description: Ginger in a tomato soup sounds unusual. It works beautifully though, bringing a really nice fragrant warmth. Give it a go.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Halve the tomatoes and place on a baking tray (chopped sides facing upwards). Drizzle olive oil over the tomatoes. Add the garlic cloves (skins on) to the tray along with the ginger (skin on). Sprinkle a pinch of salt over the tray. Roast in the oven for 20 minutes.
Remove the baking tray from the oven and move the tomatoes over to one side of the baking tray.
Slice up your onions, add them to the tray along with whole red chilli. Drizzle olive oil and salt over the top and place back into the oven for 25 minutes.
Take the tray out of the oven and peel the skin off the ginger and squeeze the garlic out of the skins.

Add the contents of the baking tray to a saucepan, followed by the coconut milk and vegetable stock. Blend until a smooth orange colour. Add a drizzle of white wine vinegar and a pinch of pepper. Mix together.

Remove the soup from the heat and ladle into bowls. Top with a drizzle of olive oil, a few drops of coconut cream and a scattering of chopped coriander. Serve with two slices of toasted sourdough and enjoy!

name: Spiced Rum Pumpkin Milkshake
description: An autumnal cocktail made with vanilla ice cream, pumpkin purée, spiced rum, and cinnamon.
instructions: Add all your ingredients to a blender, then whizz to combine.
Pour into a glass, then top with squirty cream and a pinch of cinnamon.

name: Spiced Röstis With Carrot Slaw & Poached Eggs
description: A perfect marriage of contrasting flavours and textures. The potato röstis, all crispy exterior and tender interior, provide a sturdy base for the poached eggs.
keywords: Spiced Potato Cakes With Carrot Slaw & Poached Eggs
instructions: Slice the spring onions and add them to a mixing bowl. Finely grate in the garlic and zest the lemon in. Now, finely chop the coriander stems and add them in, too. Grate the potatoes into a tea towel, and squeeze as much water out as possible then tip into the mixing bowl. Stir well and set aside while you make the slaw.

Make the carrot slaw. Roughly chop the kale, add it to a bowl and massage with the juice of the lemon until soft. Use a peeler to peel the carrots into long ribbons into a bowl – you can discard the skin if you like. Add most of most of the coriander leaves, add in your ras el hanout, season, toss well and set aside.

Separate the grated potato mixture out into 8 portions. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat, add 1 portion of the potato mixture in and flatten with a spatula. Cook for 2 mins, then flip and cook on the other side for 2 mins. Pile them onto plates as you cook and repeat the process with the remaining potato mix. You should be able to make 2 röstis per person. Add a splash of more oil and fry the eggs to your liking.
Top the cakes with a dollop of yoghurt and the fried eggs. Serve the slaw on the side, scatter with remaining coriander to serve.

name: Spiced Sausage & Pineapple Tacos
description: Transform your Spiced Sausage & Roasted Pineapple Traybake batch with these tacos. There's fresh jalapeño, a punchy pineapple and pepper salsa all piled into warm tortillas with a cool dollop of soured cream. Ready in 20 mins from your batch.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Spiced Sausage & Roasted Pineapple Traybake batch.
Thinly slice the jalapeño and pick the coriander leaves, thinly slicing the stems. Using a mandoline or veg peeler, finely shred the cabbage and set aside.

Tip the vegetables and pineapple from the batch into a food processor along with the coriander stems. Pulse until a rough salsa forms, you can also hand-mince if you don't have a processor. Transfer to a bowl, season with salt and squeeze over the juice of one lime.
Reheat the sausages in a frying pan over a medium heat for a few mins until warmed through. Warm the tortillas in the pan for 30 seconds each side. Slice the sausages on the diagonal.

Share the tortillas between plates and spread with a dollop of soured cream. Layer the shredded cabbage on top, then add the sliced sausages. Spoon over the salsa, scatter with jalapeño and fresh coriander leaves, and serve with the remaining lime cut into wedges.

name: Spiced Sausage & Pineapple Traybake with Coriander Rice
description: Another spin on your Spiced Sausage & Roasted Pineapple Traybake, with herby coriander rice topped with the smoky sausage batch and a cool dollop of soured cream.
keywords: Sausage & Pineapple Traybake with Coriander Rice
Sausage & Pineapple Traybake with Coriander Rice recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the Spiced Sausage & Roasted Pineapple Traybake batch.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Tip your batch leftovers onto a tray and cover with foil, pop into the oven to reheat for 5-6 mins.
Meanwhile, microwave the rice according to the packet instructions until piping hot. Finely chop the coriander. Zest the lime half into the rice, then toss the coriander through.
Divide the rice between plates, top with the sausage batch and add a generous dollop of soured cream. Serve with the zested lime half cut into wedges for squeezing.

name: Spiced Sausage & Pineapple Wraps
description: Crispy toasted burritos stuffed with leftovers from your Spiced Sausage & Roasted Pineapple Traybake batch, plus a creamy feta and soured cream filling.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Spiced Sausage & Roasted Pineapple Traybake batch.
Crumble the feta into a bowl and stir through the soured cream until combined.
Lay out the tortillas and spread the feta mixture down the middle of each one. Top with the sausages, vegetables and pineapple from the batch, then scatter over the coriander.
Fold in the sides and roll each tortilla tightly into a burrito. Place a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the wraps and toast for 4-6 mins, turning regularly, until golden all over.
Wrap in foil or parchment and serve with hot sauce alongside.

name: Spiced Sausage & Roasted Pineapple Traybake
description: These sticky sausages roasted with caramelised pineapple, peppers and slow-roasted garlic make the perfect batch cook that works all week long.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Chop the onions into 2-3cm wedges and dice the peppers and pineapple into 3cm chunks. Tip everything into a large baking tray along with the whole garlic bulb. Season with the cumin, smoked paprika, salt and black pepper, drizzle with olive oil and toss together. Slide into the oven for 10-15 mins, until starting to soften.
Lay the sausages on top of the veg and return to the oven for 15-20 mins, until the sausages are cooked through.
Turn the grill to high. Once hot, slide the tray under for 5-7 mins until the sausages are golden and caramelised.
Remove from the oven, squeeze the roasted garlic cloves out of their skins and mix thoroughly through the tray. Serve straight away, or divide into portions and store in the fridge for up to 3 days.

name: Spiced Scrambled Eggs With Crispy Chilli & Garlic
description: Loaded naan bread basted with spiced scrambled eggs and sprinkled with coriander, crispy garlic and chilli.
instructions: Finely slice the chilli, garlic and spring onions. Whisk up the eggs. Roughly chop the coriander.

First, make the crispy bits by heating 100ml oil in a small frying pan over a medium heat and adding the chilli and garlic. Cook for about 5 mins, until golden and crisp, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel.
Heat the naan according to package instructions.

In another frying pan, add a small splash of oil and heat over medium. Add the curry paste and spring onions, cook until the spring onions are softened. Then add the butter and cook until the butter has melted. Pour in the egg and most of the coriander, and allow to set slightly before mixing gently. Continue cooking and folding until the eggs are soft set.
Spoon onto the warm naan and scatter with remaining coriander and crispy garlic and chilli. Serve with your choice of chilli sauce and tuck in.

name: Spiced Shakshuka With Herby Green Tahini
description: A delicious (and verdant) shakshuka recipe that's perfect for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Make sure to use high-quality eggs.
keywords: Spiced Shakshuka With Herby Green Tahini
Spiced Shakshuka With Herby Green Tahini recipe
instructions: Heat a frying pan over a medium heat and toast the cumin seeds until fragrant, then remove from the pan and grind in a pestle and mortar. Peel and finely slice the garlic, drain and slice the red peppers and drain the beans. Heat oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the garlic for 3 min until turning golden. Add the cumin and smoked paprika, frying for a couple of minutes. Next, add in the tinned tomatoes, sliced peppers and the cannellini beans – simmer for 15 mins, until reduced and thickened.
Roughly chop the parsley, saving a few leaves for garnish. Add to a blender with the tahini and the juice of a lemon. Process until nice and smooth then loosen with water.
Now we are ready for the eggs – make indentations in the tomato sauce and crack an egg into each one. Pop a lid on and simmer gently on low for 6 min, until the eggs are just set.
Pop the pan on the table and drizzle with the herby tahini sauce, and scatter over the remaining herbs. Serve with toasted crusty bread and get stuck in.

name: Spiced Smashed Potato Salad with Tahini-Ginger Dressing & Crispy Mint
description: A cut above the rest — say hello to your new favourite way to make potato salad, with a spiced, cinnamon-infused oil, tahini dressing and crispy mint leaves.
instructions: Add the potatoes to a pan and cover with cold water. Season with salt and set over a medium heat. Bring to a boil and cook for 10-12 mins until the potatoes are tender. Drain, steam dry and set aside.
Mix together the ingredients for the spiced oil along with salt and pepper.

Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place the potatoes onto a baking tray with the olive oil, bake for 15 mins until golden. Take them out of the oven, squash them using a flat surface, cracking the skins and breaking up the edges. Drizzle with spiced oil and salt, place back in the oven for 20-25 mins, until crispy.

Halve the cherry tomatoes. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon into a small bowl and grate in the garlic and ginger. Add the tahini and mix together, loosening with a little splash of water, a bit at a time, until smooth.
Now get on with the crispy mint. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and add the mint leaves. Sizzle until they darken slightly in colour then remove and drain on kitchen paper.
Add the crispy potatoes and halved tomatoes to a platter, drizzle with tahini dressing and scatter with crispy mint and the coriander leaves.

name: Spiced Squash & Chickpea Curry Traybake
description: A nice and spicy vegetarian traybake curry that's perfect for a lazy weeknight. You'll be making this one again and again, Mob.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel the butternut squash, cut it in half, then remove and discard the seeds. Cut the squash into 5cm pieces.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Dice the onion into 2.5cm cubes. Finely chop the green chilli. Set everything aside.

Combine the butternut squash, chickpeas, onion, garlic paste, ginger paste, cumin seeds, curry leaves, green chilli, curry powder, ground coriander, turmeric, chilli flakes, 1 tsp salt and coconut oil in a large bowl. Toss well, until the squash and chickpeas are well coated.

Spread the squash and chickpea mixture in a single layer over a large baking tray lined with baking parchment. Roast in the oven for 25-30 mins, or until the squash is tender and starting to caramelise.

Remove the tray from the oven and pour the coconut milk over the roasted vegetables. Stir to combine and coat everything evenly. Return to the oven and cook for 10-15 mins, until the coconut milk has thickened slightly.
Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander.
Check the finished traybake for seasoning, then squeeze the juice of ½ lime over the top. Garnish with the coriander and serve with rice, rotis or bread.

name: Spiced Squash, Chickpea & Pistachio Traybake
description: When squash is in season, there are so many delicious things to do with it, but serving it with dates, tahini and tangy pomegranate molasses creates a perfect medley of textures and flavours that complement each other so well. Serve this with couscous, bulgur wheat, freekeh, rice or any other whole grain if you like. If you can’t find pomegranate molasses, you can use balsamic glaze instead.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan.
Halve the squash lengthways (no need to peel). Scoop out the seeds and then quarter each half lengthways, so you have eight long pieces. Cut each piece into 2–3cm chunks.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas and pat them dry with a clean tea towel, removing any skins that come loose.
Add the squash chunks and chickpeas to a large baking tray (use two trays if it looks overcrowded – they need space to cook or they will become mushy).

Lightly grind all the spices using a pestle and mortar or spice grinder, keeping some intact. You could even leave them all intact if you like; this will give a chunky texture and pops of flavour. Add the spices to a bowl and mix in the sesame seeds, salt and olive oil.

Tip the spice mix into the tray(s) with the chickpeas and squash and mix very well, making sure everything is evenly coated. Bake, uncovered, for 20 minutes, then toss and bake for another 15–18 minutes until the chickpeas are slightly crispy and the squash is tender inside and starting to crisp at the edges.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the pistachios and parsley. Remove the stones from the dates and tear them into large pieces.
Once the squash is cooked, remove the tray from the oven and scatter over the pistachios and dates, then return to the oven for another 2–3 minutes.
Drizzle over the tahini and pomegranate molasses, along with some more olive oil, and sprinkle with salt. Add the lemon zest and juice, and scatter over the parsley to finish. Serve.

name: Spiced Tofu & Roasted Broccoli Kale Salad
description: Kale, nutty quinoa, avocado and edamame, all tossed with your leftover Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Roasted Broccoli batch. The miso and lime dressing pulls it all together into something that tastes like far more effort than it is.
instructions: Mix all the dressing ingredients in a small bowl. Season with salt and thin with a splash of water, a tablespoon at a time, until runny.
Cut the kale into thin strips. Add to a large bowl, season with salt and massage with your hands for a couple of minutes until the kale turns deep green.
Add the cooked quinoa to the bowl with half the dressing and toss to combine. Divide between plates.

Top each plate with the leftovers of your crunchy tofu & roasted broccoli batch, along with the edamame beans. Peel and slice the avocado and divide among the plates, then scatter over the roasted cashews, a pinch of salt and the remaining dressing.

name: Spiced Tomato & Prawn Curry
description: Spiced tomato and prawn curry using a super secret special ingredient (tinned tomato soup). The curry is phenomenal and only uses six ingredients, so we’re extracting as much flavour as possible from each one of them.
instructions: Remove the heads and shell from the prawns and set aside. Devein the prawns (optional).

Place a saucepan on medium-high heat with half of the coconut milk. Cook the coconut milk, stirring occasionally until the coconut splits and the solids are golden. Add the prawn heads and shells. Cook, stirring for 4-5 mins until pink and fragrant.

Stir through the red Thai curry paste and cook for 30 secs. Pour in the can of tomato soup, the remaining coconut milk, and 100ml of water, making sure to scrape the bottom of the pan. Bring to a boil, turn the heat down to medium and let simmer for 10-15 mins to infuse the flavours.

Meanwhile, trim the green beans and cut into thirds. Strain the soup, discarding the prawn shells. Place the soup back onto medium-high heat, drop the green beans, cook for 5 mins, then add the prawns and cook 3-4 mins, until cooked through. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lime juice.
Share the soup between your bowls and enjoy with bread or rice.

name: Spiced Tomato Salad with Bhaji-ish Onions
description: The most summery salad I think you’ll ever lay your eyes on! Ripe, sweet tomatoes and crispy onion bhajis. The dressing is spicy, creamy, and super addictive.
keywords: Tomato & Bhaji Salad With Spicy Yoghurt Dressing
instructions: To make the bhajis, fill a small, deep saucepan halfway with oil and heat to 160°C. Peel and finely slice the onion, then toss in cornflour and turmeric. Then chop the tomatoes and put in a sieve over a bowl and season with salt. Drink the tomato juice you collect, cook's treat!

Whack your yoghurt into a bowl and then add the zest of a lime along with a big squeeze of juice. Season with salt and pepper, then taste and adjust the lime juice if needed. Put back in the fridge until you're ready to assemble.

While you're waiting for the oil to come up to temp, take a small saucepan and heat the olive oil for the dressing. Add the cumin and mustard seeds, and when they start to pop, take off the heat and add in the madras powder. Once cooled, whisk in the dijon and lime juice. Season with salt and pepper.

When the pot of oil is up to temp, add in the onions – you'll need to do this in batches. Cook for 3-4 mins, until golden then drain on kitchen paper – sprinkle with the cumin powder, ground coriander and salt whilst they are still warm. Set aside.
Spread the yoghurt onto a plate and top with the tomatoes, dressing, crispy onions and mint.

name: Spiced Tomato Sauce & Jammy Eggs on Sourdough
description: The spicy sauce in this recipe is inspired by doro wat – an Ethiopian stew. We've layered it onto toasted sourdough with a jammy egg for a quick and delicious meal.
keywords: Spiced Tomato Sauce & Jammy Eggs on Sourdough
instructions: Peel and finely grate the garlic and ginger. Thinly slice the jalapeño.

Add the ghee into a saucepan and lightly crush the cardamom pods. Once hot, simmer the cardamom and caraway seeds until fragrant. Add the ginger, garlic and berbere, then cook until fragrant. Pour in the plum tomatoes and crush to break them down. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 10-15 mins until thickened.

Meanwhile, bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Once boiling, turn the heat down slightly to a gentle boil, then add the eggs and cook for 6 mins until jammy. Drain and place in an ice bath or keep cold water running over them.

Toast the bread, discard the cardamom pods from the sauce, then slather the sauce onto the toast. Peel and halve the eggs, then place onto the toasts. Garnish with jalapeño slices and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Spiced Veggie Gyros
description: The spiced roast veggies and the cooling tzatziki come together perfectly to form one of the all time great mouthfuls.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Finely chop the courgettes, red onion and peppers into bite-size pieces. Break cauliflower up into little florets. Place on a baking tray. Add in the chickpeas, along with a splash of the starchy chickpea water, disgarding the rest.
Pour over a good glug of olive oil, add cayenne pepper, garam masala, a sprinkle of salt and pepper, and mix everything together. Place in oven for 30 minutes.

Tzatziki time. Pour a pot of yoghurt into a bowl. Add a small bunch of finely chopped mint, the juice of one lemon, and one grated cucumber. Grate in a clove of garlic, season well and mix it all together.
After 30 minutes, remove the vegetables from the oven, mix them about, and then place back in the oven for 15 more minutes.
Assemble time. Take a warm pitta. Load it with your spiced vegetables, tzatziki, pomegranate seeds, some more vegetables, more tzatziki, more pomegranate seeds, and tuck in.

name: Spicy & Sour Fish Curry
description: Inspired by my love for asam pedas, this recipe uses a shop bought red curry paste cooked down with tamarind and fish sauce to make a delicious, quick and easy weeknight meal.
instructions: Mince your garlic and ginger and slice your shallot.
Heat a very generous glug of vegetable oil in a wok set over a medium heat. Add the red curry paste and fry for about 3 mins until fragrant, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the minced garlic, ginger and sliced shallots to the wok and fry for 2 mins until fragrant and slightly softened.
Add the tamarind paste, curry powder, brown sugar, fish sauce and a pinch of salt to the wok and mix well to combine. Pour in the water, give it a stir and let the mixture come to a gentle boil.
Meanwhile, chop the ends off the okra and slice the tomatoes into half.

Wash your rice three times until the water runs clear. Drain, then transfer to a large saucepan and add water until it reaches just below your first knuckle. Bring to the boil over a medium-high heat, then turn the heat to low and cover with a lid for 12 mins.

Place the sea bass into the wok, submerging it in the broth. Lower the heat to a simmer and cook for 6 mins. Add the okra, tomatoes and the juice of the lime to the broth and leave to simmer for another 6 mins.
Divide the rice between bowls and serve with the seabass, a generous serving of the broth and some fresh coriander.

name: Spicy 'Nduja Pizza
description: This 'nduja pizza is fresh and spicy, with a delicious crispy base, cooked on the Weber Crafted Glazed Baking Stone.
instructions: Mix the flour and water together until it combines to form a rough mass (don’t knead) and leave for half an hour to autolyse.
Dissolve the yeast in a Tbsp of lukewarm water, add to the dough and mix for a few mins. Then add the salt and keep mixing until you have a smooth elastic dough. Probably about 10 mins total mixing.
Remove, shape, cover and prove until doubled in size (a few hours at room temperature or overnight in the fridge).
Portion and ball the dough then leave to prove again for a few of hours until ready to use.
Preheat your BBQ with Weber Glazed Baking Stone to max.
In a bowl, crush the tomatoes by hand until pulpy, then season with salt. Chop or tear your mozzarella into chunks and put into a bowl.

Once ready, stretch your pizza out on a well floured surface. Spoon on the tomato sauce and spread across the base. Grate over a little parmesan, if using, then add a few basil leaves. Top with a handful of mozzarella and then spoon on a few blobs of nduja.
Slide the pizza onto a lightly floured peel and then onto the Weber Glazed Baking Stone. Close the lid and allow to cook for about 3 or 4 mins until you have a crispy base and golden crusts.
Slide onto a board, drizzle with a little olive oil and slice.

name: Spicy 'Nduja and Burrata Pasta
description: Spicy, rich tomato and 'nduja pasta topped with a ball of creamy burrata and a drizzle of crispy garlic and parsley oil. A banging combo.
instructions: Mince the onion and finely slice the garlic. Pick the leaves of the parsley and finely chop the stems.

Heat 1/3 of the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onions and 1/2 the garlic, cooking until browned for around 10 mins. Add  the chilli flakes and parsley stems and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the tin of chopped tomatoes and 'nduja and cook on a low heat for 15 mins.
Add the remaining olive oil in a small pan over a low heat and add the remaining garlic. cook gently for about 5 minutes, stirring often until the garlic is golden.
Pop your pasta on to cook in boiling salted water. Cook according to package instructions, then drain, reserving the water.
Ladle some pasta water into the tomato sauce and mix well. Bring it to a bubble then add in the cooked pasta.

Add in the cold butter and toss the pasta together to emulsify it into the sauce. Season generously with salt and pepper, then squeeze in lemon juice to taste. If it's looking a bit dry, add another ladle of pasta water and keep mixing until shiny and thick.
Serve the pasta topped with torn burrata, parsley and crispy garlic chips.

name: Spicy Apple Rib Sandwiches
description: Elliot Cunningham of Lagom makes a phenomenal sandwich using Bull’s-Eye Carolina Reaper Extra Hot Sauce. Soft, sticky pork. Spicy apple sauce. It’s a winner.
instructions: The day before eating, combine all of the dry brine ingredients – that's your salt, sugar, fennel seeds, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, onion granules and garlic granules – in a shallow tray. Make sure they’re mixed together nicely.

Liberally sprinkle the brine over the pork slices, making sure to get seasoning on every crevice. Cover and place in your fridge overnight. This process will not only help give the pork flavour all the way through, but also changes the texture to ensure you get nice juicy pork.
Heat your oven to 160°C.
Remove the pork belly slices from the fridge and place into a baking tray with a drizzle of vegetable oil. Cover the tray tightly with tin foil.
Cook for 1 ½ hours, flipping the slices over half way through. We want them to be cooked through and soft, but not falling apart.

Whilst your pork cooks, make your spicy apple glaze. Wrap your two cooking apples in tin foil and place them at the bottom of the oven, or into the coals of a barbecue. Cook until the apples are super soft - about 20 mins.

Set the apples aside until cool enough to handle. Remove the core and seeds as best you can and place the flesh in a food processor. Add a tablespoon of honey and your Bull’s-Eye Carolina Reaper Extra Hot Sauce. Add more or less to taste.
Blend the mixture, and add the juice of your lemon. Set aside.
Mix your mayo. Add your mayonnaise to a bowl, then grate in your clove of garlic and squeeze in your lemon juice. Mix thoroughly.
Pour your vinegar and sugar into a pan along with 690ml of water. Bring to a boil. Once the sugar has dissolved, leave to cool.

Shred your cabbage, onion and carrot very finely. You can use a mandoline or a very sharp knife. Finely chop your parsley. Combine your sliced cabbage, onion and carrot in bowl and mix in your parsley. Dress with vinegar up to an hour before serving.
Remove your tray from the oven and place your pork belly slices onto a plate to cool slightly.
Heat your barbecue to a high heat.

In a small bowl, combine the cooking juices from the pork and ⅓ of your spicy apple glaze. Place your pork belly slices onto the barbecue and brush on your glaze. Flip the pork belly slices, then continue to glaze until you’re happy with the colour and coverage. You want to get a nice char on it.
Cut your baguette into sections and toast slightly.

Apply a liberal layer of the cool mayo on the base, followed by our zingy vinegar slaw. Get your spicy pork belly slices in there, then cover it with more of the spicy apple sauce. Place the top piece of bread on, serve and enjoy.

name: Spicy Aubergine Pitta With Peanut Dressing
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

We've thrown fudgy chunks of aubergine into a pitta and drizzled them liberally with a creamy peanut dressing
keywords: Spicy Aubergine Pitta With Peanut Dressing
Spicy Aubergine Pitta With Peanut Dressing recipe
instructions: Pop 2/3 of the peanuts into a blender and blitz until smooth. You'll need to intermittently scrape down the sides. Add the garlic, ginger, water and a squeeze of lime juice, then blitz until smooth and combined. Season with salt and pepper. Crush the rest of the peanuts with the back of a knife and set aside.

Dice the aubergine into 2cm pieces. Toss in a splash of oil, the curry powder, salt and pepper. Heat a frying pan over a medium high heat and add the aubergine, turning often until charred. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Chop the cucumber, scoop out the seeds and slice. Deseed and finely dice the chilli. Pick the mint leaves and finely chop, then finely slice the red onion. Toss the cucumber, chilli, mint and red onion in a bowl, squeeze over the remaining lime juice and season with salt.
Toast the pitta and slice open round one edge to create a flap. Open up, spread with peanut sauce, then stuff with the slaw, aubergine and crushed peanuts.

name: Spicy Aubergine Stew with Herby Rice
description: A fiery, smoky aubergine stew using our Aubergine Alla Norma batch, served over herby rice with a cooling yoghurt dollop. Lazy dinner vibes with full-on flavour.
instructions: Make the Aubergine Alla Norma batch recipe.
Pick the parsley leaves, set a few aside for garnish and finely chop the rest.
Stir the harissa into the aubergine alla norma and warm it through in a saucepan over a medium heat. Taste and season with salt and black pepper, if needed.
Reheat the rice according to pack instructions. Stir through the chopped parsley.
Spoon the herby rice onto plates, then top with the spicy aubergine stew and a generous dollop of yoghurt. Finish with the reserved parsley leaves.

name: Spicy Aubergine and 'Nduja Rigatoni
description: A spicy, zingy pasta that makes the most of summer aubergines. Get it on the table in under 30? Result!
instructions: Get your rigatoni on to boil in a large pan of salted water. Cook until al dente.
Set a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Dice your aubergine into roughly 2cm squares. Roughly chop your mint.
Add your aubergines to the pan with a good pinch of salt and keep them moving. Fry for about 3 mins.
Once the aubergine has taken on some colour, add the ‘nduja and a splash of the pasta cooking water. Mix well.
Now, add the oregano and a good drizzle of olive oil, mix again and cook for another couple of mins.

Finally, drain your pasta (reserving a little pasta water) and add to the pan with the aubergine. Keep mixing over a medium heat until you have a thick glossy sauce, adding splashes of pasta water where necessary.
Finally, add a handful of mint and a big squeeze of lemon juice. Plate up and top with grated pecorino, if you like. Serve and enjoy.

name: Spicy Bacon & Kimchi Fried Rice
description: Possibly the ultimate go-to lunch. This quick dish is big on flavour and only takes 30 mins to throw together.
keywords: Spicy kimchi and bacon fried rice recipes
instructions: Wash your rice in a pot and give it a good rinse until the water runs clear. After that, fill your pot with water and bring it to a boil for a few mins on high heat. Once it’s started to boil, lower the heat, pop a lid on, and simmer it for 12 mins. Leave your rice at room temperature to cool down.
Slice your spring onions and chilli and set aside. Slice your bacon into small pieces.
Mince your garlic and chop your shallot before adding them to your wok with a glug of veg oil. Stir fry for a few mins then add your bacon until it's lovely and crispy.

Add your kimchi and rice to your wok with the gochujang and soy sauce. Mix well until every grain of the rice is coated. Now, add in your peas and sesame oil. Give it a quick mix and then take it off the hob.
Fry your eggs with a glug of oil in a separate pan until the edges are crispy and the yolks are jammy.
Plate up your rice with a fried egg on each plate. Top with a scattering of sesame seeds, sliced spring onions and chilli.

name: Spicy Baked Meatballs
description: The secret ingredient to make our meatballs super soft? Mushrooms. Blitz them up and mix them with your pork mince for delicious umami flavour. Incredible.
instructions: Make your sauce. Heat a little olive oil in a medium sized saucepan, then add your grated garlic and chilli flakes. Cook over a medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant, then add your passata. Bring to a boil, then pop a lid on and simmer over a medium heat for 30 mins. Season to taste, then set aside.

Whilst the sauce simmers, make your meatball mixture. Grate your onion and crush your garlic. Heat a little olive oil in a frying pan and add your onions. Saute over a medium heat for a few minutes until softened, then add your garlic and fennel seeds and cook out for another two minutes. Set aside to cool.

Grate your parmesan and chop your parsley. Place your mushrooms in the bowl of your food processor and pulse until they are finely minced. Tip your mushrooms into a large bowl along with your pork mince, breadcrumbs, onion and garlic mixture, parsley, 2/3 of your parmesan, salt and pepper. Combine with your hands until you have a smooth mixture.

Roll into 12 equally sized balls, then heat a little olive oil in a frying pan over a high heat. Add your meatballs and brown on all sides until lovely and caramelised - this will take about 5 mins. They don’t need to be totally cooked through at this point.
Plog your meatballs into your tomato sauce, gently spooning over the sauce to coat. Sprinkle with your mozzarella and remaining 1/3 parmesan, then bake for 15 mins at 200°C. Serve with crusty bread.

name: Spicy Bean & Chorizo Salad
description: Salad for dinner doesn't have to be depressing. This salad is packed with crispy nubbins of chorizo and creamy butter beans.
instructions: Roughly dice the chorizo and halve the cherry tomatoes. Add the chorizo to a cold pan and bring up to a medium-high heat, sizzling until the fat is rendered out, add the fennel seeds and cook for one min.
Remove the chorizo and pour the fat into the bottom of a large salad bowl. Add the dijon, red wine vinegar and shallot - whisk well and then taste and season with salt and pepper.
Roughly tear the parsley and drain the beans. Add the butter beans, parsley, cherry tomatoes and salad leaves to the bowl and toss well to coat.
Plate up and top with crumbled feta and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Spicy Braised Lentils, Peppers & Chorizo
description: These braised green lentils from Ocado are beautifully rich, smoky and saucy, plus they're all cooked in one pot which means minimal washing up.
instructions: Dice the chorizo and fry over a medium heat for 2 minutes in a large saucepan. Slice the onion, add and reduce the heat slightly. Cook for about 5 mins until soft.
Slice the peppers and add them to the pan. Mince up the leaves from the rosemary and slice the garlic. Add both along with the chilli flakes and paprika. Cook for another 2 mins.
Add the lentils, cook for a minute and then pour in the stock.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for about 25 mins until the lentils are tender, most of the stock has been absorbed and the texture is thick and saucy.
Ladle it into bowls and enjoy. Great with a chunk of crusty bread.

name: Spicy Breakfast Burrito
description: The perfect start to your day, all packed up in a tight burrito. Filled with crispy chorizo, spicy salsa, cheese, avocado and soft fluffy eggs.
instructions: Whisk the eggs in a large bowl with some salt and pepper.
Add the chorizo into a hot pan and cook for 8 mins. Remove and set aside, leaving behind the stained chorizo oil.
Turn the heat down to the lowest setting and pour in your eggs. Using a spatula cook for 3 - 5 mins on a very low heat stirring constantly until the eggs are just set.
Finely chop the tomatoes, red onion and coriander. Mix this all in a bowl with some hot sauce and the juice and zest of a lime.
Grate the cheese and scoop the meat out of the avocado, slice thinly.

Grab your tortilla and add in ¼ of the eggs. Add a few tablespoons of salsa, chorizo then cheese and finally avocado. Roll tightly in a burrito fashion and then toast on a dry saucepan seam side down.
Wrap in foil to keep warm and enjoy.

name: Spicy Butter Bean & Kale Stew with Quick Flatbreads
description: Smoky bean stew finished with tangy feta and yoghurt. The homemade two-ingredient flatbreads almost steal the show.
keywords: Spicy Butter Bean & Kale Stew with Quick Flatbreads
instructions: Finely chop the parsley stalks and pick the leaves. Add a generous glug of olive oil into a large saucepan. Grate the garlic straight into the pan, add in the smoked paprika and parsley stalks. Place on a medium heat, cook stirring for 1 min. Then, add the chopped tomatoes, the butterbeans, and your stock. Let it simmer for 20-25 mins.

Meanwhile, make the flatbreads. Add the self-raising flour and yoghurt into a bowl with 1 tsp of salt. Using your hands, mix together until a dough forms – it will be very sticky so don't worry! Liberally flour a clean surface and portion the dough into 6 balls. Flatten and roll out the balls until 1cm thick, you don't have to be super neat here.

Place a frying pan over high heat, cook the flatbreads in the hot dry pan on both sides until fluffy and golden brown spots appear, 2-4 mins. Transfer to a plate, lightly brush with some olive oil and season with salt. Continue doing this until no more dough is left, stack the flatbreads on top of each other.
When the stew is done simmering, add in the kale and stir until wilted, 3-5 mins.

Serve the spicy butter bean and kale stew into bowls, top with the remaining yoghurt, and a drizzle of olive oil. Crumble over some feta and finish with a scattering of parsley leaves and a good squeeze of lemon. Serve with a flatbread per person.

name: Spicy Butternut Squash Soup Recipe
description: This spicy butternut squash soup is a great recipe for batch cooking as it re-heats super well and can be frozen in individual portions. If vegan, check the curry paste doesn’t contain fish sauce. The beansprouts, if using, add a pleasing fresh crunch.  If you’re going to use the beansprouts then they need to be fried briefly in a little toasted sesame oil before eating.
instructions: Peel the butternut squash then chop into small chunks, around 2cm.
Finely slice all of the spring onions (both green and white parts). Set a quarter aside in a bowl for topping the soup later.

Heat the coconut oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the spring onions and crushed ginger and cook off for a few mins until fragrant. Add the curry paste and cook it out for 3 mins then add the butternut squash, along with the vegetable stock and coconut milk. Bring up to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer away for 25-30 mins until the squash is completely tender and mashable with the back of your spoon.
Blitz the soup in the pan using a stick blender until completely smooth, season with salt, pepper and lime juice to taste.
Roughly chop the salted peanuts. If it needs it, re-warm the soup, then divide between bowls.
Top with the peanuts, remaining spring onions, Thai basil or coriander, and if using, a pile of bean sprouts to serve.

name: Spicy Butternut and Ricotta Cannelloni
description: The days may be getting longer and lighter, but I still like to finish the day with something warm and filling. Enter my roasted squash cannelloni, loaded up with not one, but two delicious sauces – one cheesy and creamy, the other rich and tomatoey. Sophie x
keywords: Spicy Butternut and Ricotta Cannelloni recipe
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Halve your butternut squash and scoop out the seeds. Wrap your garlic bulb in foil.
Pop your squash, garlic and half of your chillies on a roasting tray, then drizzle your squash with olive oil and a pinch of salt. Roast for 45 mins.
Finely chop your remaining chilli and garlic cloves.

Heat a saucepan over a low heat with a splash of olive oil. Add your chilli and garlic, then simmer for 2 mins until fragrant. Tip in your tinned tomatoes and simmer gently for 30 mins. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Melt your butter in a sauté pan over a medium heat. Add your flour and cook out for 2 mins. Gradually pour in your milk in small increments, stirring all the while until you have a smooth paste before adding more. Bring the mixture to a simmer for 2 mins to thicken, then turn off the heat.
Add half of your Parmesan into the pan, and tear in your mozzarella. Stir until just melted, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Back to your squash. Once the squash is cool enough to handle, scoop the flesh out of the skins. Squeeze the caramelised pulp from your garlic by pushing down on it with a knife.
Add your squash, chilli (seeds removed) and garlic to your food processor and pulse to a rough paste.
Spoon your squash paste into a bowl. Tear in your basil leaves, then add your ricotta, nearly all of your Parmesan, nutmeg, and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Mix to combine.
Arrange your filling down the width of one of your lasagne sheets, about 4cm from the edge. Roll it up into a cigar shape, then repeat with your remaining lasagne and filling.
Arrange your cannelloni in a row in a baking dish, then top with your tomato sauce. Pour over your béchamel, then sprinkle with your remaining Parmesan and bake for 30 mins.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Spicy Charred Tomato Prawns with Brothy Rice
description: Inspired by bouillon blanc, a Seychellois brothy fish stew - this brothy situation is savoury, sour and completely delicious. Kind of like a tom yum, with a different flavour profile.
keywords: Spicy Charred Tomato Prawns with Brothy Rice
Spicy Charred Tomato Prawns with Brothy Rice recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the spring onion, separating the green and whites. Thinly slice the garlic and finely grate the ginger. If you like heat, mince the scotch bonnet, if not, poke a few holes into the chilli.

Place a saucepan on medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the spring onion whites and thyme stalks, cook stirring occasionally, until softened, 2-3 mins. Stir the tomato purée, ginger and half the garlic in and cook until the purée turns a dark red colour, 2-4 mins.

Stir the scotch bonnet in, squeeze the juice of half of the lime into the saucepan, scraping the bottom of the pot. Let it completely evaporate before pouring in the boiling water. Let the mixture come to the boil. Lower the heat down to a gentle simmer. Before serving, stir the fish sauce in, taste and season with lime juice and more fish sauce, if needed.

Meanwhile, place a frying pan onto high heat. Once hot, add the tomatoes and cook until starting to char, transfer into a bowl. Turn the heat down to medium-high, add a drizzle of olive oil, and add the garlic and prawns, stir until cooked through, 3-5 mins (shell-on prawns will take a little more time than peeled prawns to cook). Return the tomatoes to the pan and remove from the heat. Season with salt.
Share the cooked rice between bowls, pour the broth over and place the tomato and prawn mixture on top. Garnish with the remaining spring onion greens.

name: Spicy Chicken & Chorizo Fajitas
description: It turns out chorizo is the thing fajitas have been missing. The spicy sausage brings the perfect kick to these speedy chicken fajitas.
instructions: Chop the avocado into chunks and add into a bowl with the juice of the lime. Season with salt and pepper and mash everything together.
Chop the chorizo into 2-3cm bite sized chunk and add them to a large frying pan. Place over medium heat and fry until the fat renders out and they become slightly crispy.
Meanwhile, slice the peppers and onion. Thinly slice the chicken. Once the chorizo has gone crispy, stir the peppers and onion in. Cook, stirring, until softened, 4-6 mins.
Once the veggies have softened, add the chicken and fajita seasoning. Season with salt and stir fry until the chicken is cooked through, 4-6 mins. Taste and season with more salt, if needed.

Add a dollop of guac onto the tortilla, then layer the fajita mixture, soured cream and sprinkle with coriander on top. Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly into wraps. To seal, place back into the frying pan over medium heat, and cook, seam side down, until sealed. Wrap in baking paper or foil before serving.

name: Spicy Chicken & Coconut Soup
description: Creamy coconut broth with a kick of Thai green curry paste, tender tenderstem and silky rice noodles. Finished with leftovers from your Spicy Chicken Laab batch. Yum.
keywords: Spicy Chicken & Coconut Noodle Soup recipe
instructions: Heat the neutral oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add the curry paste and fry for 2 mins, until the oil starts to separate. Pour in the coconut milk and chicken stock, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 mins.

Meanwhile, cook the rice noodles according to packet instructions, then drain and set aside. Halve the tenderstem broccoli and add to a pan of salted boiling water. Cook for 4 mins, then drain. Reheat the spicy chicken laab in a frying pan over a medium heat until piping hot. Pick the coriander leaves.
Divide the rice noodles between two bowls. Pour over the broth, then top with the chicken laab and broccoli. Scatter with the coriander and sesame seeds and serve.

name: Spicy Chicken Laab
description: Golden chicken mince in a punchy fish sauce, lime and chilli dressing, finished with toasted rice powder and coriander. Batch cook this and you've got a great base for quick meals throughout the week.
instructions: Add the rice to a dry frying pan and toast gently over a medium heat for 4-5 mins, until golden and fragrant. Tip into a pestle and mortar and grind into a coarse, sandy powder.

Add a third of the neutral oil to a wok over a high heat. Add a third of the chicken mince and cook for 5-6 mins, until the water has disappeared and the chicken is turning golden. Remove from the wok and repeat with the remaining oil and chicken in two more batches.
Finely slice the spring onions and grate the garlic. Add to a large bowl with the chilli flakes, fish sauce, soy sauce, caster sugar and the juice of the limes. Whisk until the sugar has dissolved.

Add all the chicken back into the wok and get it nice and hot. Pour in the sauce, bring to a simmer and stir through the coriander and most of the toasted rice powder. If you're making the rice bowl recipe, save about 3 tbsp of the toasted rice powder for that. Box the chicken up into containers and pop in the fridge.

name: Spicy Chicken Laab Rice Bowl
