description: Transform your Spicy Laab Batch with this vibrant rice bowl. Fluffy jasmine rice, crispy lettuce, cool cucumber and fresh mint, with a hit of sriracha and that crunchy toasted rice powder on top.
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Add to a small saucepan with the water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid, then reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins. Remove from the heat and leave to stand, still covered, for 10 mins, then fluff with a fork.

Meanwhile, halve the lime. Cut half into wedges for serving and squeeze the remaining half over the romaine. Season with a pinch of salt and toss together. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds with a teaspoon and discard. Pick the mint leaves.
Reheat the spicy chicken laab in a frying pan over a medium heat until piping hot.
Add the rice to bowls with the chicken, cucumber and dressed lettuce. Squeeze over the sriracha, scatter with the mint leaves and the remaining toasted rice powder, and serve with the lime wedges.

name: Spicy Chicken Pozole
description: Pozole is a rich, brothy soup. We've made our version using chicken, corn, and shredded cabbage. It's a winner.
instructions: Break the chicken legs into drums and thighs by cutting between the joints. Heat a large casserole pot or saucepan over a medium heat. Thinly slice the onions and garlic.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper and add to the pan with a shot of oil, skin-side down. Cook for 8-9 mins until golden brown and super crispy. The chicken won’t be cooked through yet, so don’t panic.

Remove the chicken from the pan and add ¾ of the onions and all of the garlic. Cook for 5-6 mins until lightly sweated, season with salt and tip in the chipotle paste. Cook for another 3-4 mins, then add the chicken stock. Bring to a bare simmer and return the chicken to the pan. Cook for 18-20 mins until the chicken is cooked through and tender.

Meanwhile, slice the corn from the cobs, cut the tortillas into 1cm strips and finely shred the cabbage. De-seed and dice the tomatoes and thinly slice the radishes. Finely chop the whole bunch of coriander, stalks and all.

Once the chicken is cooked, drop in the corn and cook for a further 4 mins. Add the cabbage to the pot and warm through. At the last minute, stir through ¾ of the coriander and add the juice of two limes. Season with salt and pepper and divide between warm bowls.
Top with the remaining raw onion, feta, radishes, diced tomatoes, jalapeños, remaining limes and sliced tortillas.

name: Spicy Chicken Tahini Noodles
description: Rich, nutty tahini sauce coats silky noodles with wilted spinach and leftovers from your Spicy Chicken Laab on top. Serve it hot or cold, it works both ways.
instructions: Place the baby spinach in a colander and pour over a couple of kettles of boiling water until wilted. Press out the excess liquid and set aside.

Cook the noodles according to packet instructions. Drain and set aside. At this point, decide whether you'd like to serve this hot or cold. If cold, rinse the noodles under cold water to cool them down; if hot, set aside as they are. Pick the mint leaves.
If serving hot, reheat the spicy chicken laab in a frying pan over a medium heat until piping hot. Finely slice the spring onions.

Add the soy sauce, tahini, rice vinegar and sesame oil to a large bowl and mix until combined. Add the noodles, if serving hot, first rinse them briefly in boiling water to heat through again. Add the spinach and toss well, loosening the sauce with a splash of water if needed.
Serve the noodles topped with the chicken laab, spring onions and mint leaves.

name: Spicy Chicken Wings Recipe
description: These chicken wings are everything you want in life. Crispy, sticky, sweet, spicy and salty. Crack open a cold one and get stuck into this pile of spicy chicken wings.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C.

Cut the wings in half at the joint, so you’re left with a drumstick and ‘flat’ part. Remove the wing tip, if they’re on. Pat dry really well with kitchen paper then tip into a bowl. Spoon in the baking powder and cumin seeds and toss really well until evenly coated.
Put two wire racks over two baking trays and lay the wings onto the wire racks, leaving a little space between each one.
Put into the oven for 45-50 mins, flipping halfway through until really golden and crunchy.

Meanwhile, pour the soy sauce, honey and crispy chilli oil into a small saucepan. Use the flat side of a large knife to bash and flatten and smash the garlic on your chopping board, then roughly chop the ginger, no need to peel. Scrape both into the pan.
Set the pan over a medium heat, bring to the boil while stirring, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 mins to thicken slightly. Halve and squeeze in the juice of a lime, then remove from the heat.
Very thinly slice the spring onions and set aside with the coriander leaves.

Once the wings are crisp, tip into a large bowl and pour over the hot sticky soy glaze, tossing really well so everything gets coated. Tip into a serving bowl, along with all the glaze and scatter over the spring onion and coriander.

name: Spicy Chicken With Crispy Sushi Rice
description: Spice up your roast chicken leftovers with a fiery dressing and crispy sushi rice, topped with some fresh greens, this makes for a delicious and easy midweek meal.
instructions: Before you begin, make the No-Fuss Roast Chicken.
This recipe uses up leftover Roast Chicken, so you'll need to have some leftovers to hand to try this recipe.

Tip the sushi rice into a small mixing bowl and rinse with cold water. Repeat the process until the water runs clear. Tip into a non-stick or well seasoned frying pan (25cm) and cover with the water. Add fine sea salt, the sugar and rice vinegar. Cover with a lid and place over a medium heat.

Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 mins. Once 10 mins has passed, remove the lid and allow all of the residual steam to evaporate. Use a chopstick to create little holes throughout the rice and tip in a small amount of sesame oil into each. Cook the rice over a medium-low heat, undisturbed for 10-12 mins more, until the bottom layer is crispy and caramelised.

While the rice cooks, shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces and add to a bowl. Add the mayo, soy and hot sauce as well the juice and zest of half the limes. Mix well until the chicken has broken down a little and the mixture is well incorporated. Add the sesame seeds and have a taste, adjust with lime and sriracha as you like.
Dice the cucumber into 2cm pieces and finely chop the spring onions.
Divide the crispy rice between warm bowls, top with the spicy chicken, diced cucumbers and finely chopped spring onions. Cut the remaining lime in half and serve for squeezing.

name: Spicy Chicken Wraps With Mango Slaw
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Homemade mango slaw is the perfect sweet and citrusy partner for these spicy chicken wraps. High protein, high flavour.
keywords: Spicy Chicken Wraps With Mango Slaw
Spicy Chicken Wraps With Mango Slaw recipe
instructions: Start by making the slaw. Finely slice the red cabbage and transfer to a bowl. Squeeze in the juice of the lime, then massage a little to soften.
Peel the mango, cut off the cheeks and slice the flesh into thin strips. Add to the cabbage bowl. Finely slice the red chilli and add to the bowl, then season and toss well. Set aside.

Peel the onions and cut into wedges. Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat, add a splash of olive oil, then add the onion wedges along with a big pinch of salt. Fry for 10 mins until golden and softened.

Meanwhile, roughly dice the chicken into chunky cubes, then add to the golden onions. Grate the garlic and ginger into the pan, then add the thyme, mixed spice, soy and brown sugar. Season generously with salt and pepper. Stir everything well, then cook for 5-7 mins until the chicken is cooked through.
To serve, heat the flatbreads and top with a big spoonful of yoghurt. Top with the chicken and onions. Add a pile of mango slaw and finish with extra chilli or a pinch of chilli flakes.

name: Spicy Chickpeas With Tomatoes & Feta
description: A painfully easy recipe for one that’s super fresh and filling. A good squeeze of lemon adds a nice zip to the dish. Don’t be afraid to go heavy on the dill.
keywords: Spicy Chickpeas with tomatoes and feta
instructions: Place a saucepan over a medium-high heat and add a tbsp of olive oil. Poke the cherry tomatoes with the tip of a knife, this will encourage them to pop!
Add the cherry tomatoes to the pan and stir for 1 min, they should start to burst. Crush the garlic into the pan.

Throw in the whole tin of chickpeas along with their liquid. Add the stock cube and harissa paste and turn up the heat to high. Use a potato masher or fork to crush the mix a bit- this will help thicken the sauce.
Roughly chop three-quarters of the herbs and stir through the mix along with half of the lemon juice. Taste and season well.
Tip into bowls, drizzle with the yoghurt then top with the feta, parsley, dill, and sesame seeds. Drizzle with olive oil and another squeeze opf lemon juice. Serve it with bread.

name: Spicy Chipotle Burger
description: This smoky, zingy vegan burger will convert even the most avid meat eater. Packed with crispy cumin onions, mango guacamole and a spicy patty, how could it not?
instructions: Thinly slice the red onions and place in a bowl. Add the cornflour and ground cumin and toss to coat.
Fill a saucepan halfway with vegetable oil and set over a medium heat. Shake off any excess cornflour, then add the onions to the cold oil, stirring to separate.
Cook, stirring often, until golden brown and crispy, then drain and season with salt.
Mash the avocado flesh. Finely dice the mango. Finely chop the red onion, green chilli and fresh coriander. Juice the lime.
Place in a bowl, season with salt and pepper, and mix well to combine.
Combine the chipotle paste, garlic powder and smoked paprika with 4 tablespoons of vegetable oil and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Toast the buns then set aside.
Brush the veggie burgers with a little vegetable oil.
Heat the same non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Add theburger patties and cook for 2 mins.
Flip and spoon a third of the chipotle sauce over the burgers. Cook for a further 2 mins.
Flip again, spoon another third of the chipotle sauce over the burgers, and cook for a further 2 mins.
Flip one last time, spooning the remaining chipotle sauce over the burgers, and cook for a final 2 mins.
To assemble, get a good dollop of the mango guacamole on the base of each burger. Top with the burger patties, followed by a good handful of crispy onions and the top bun. Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Spicy Chorizo & Bean Stew with Baked Cod
description: Spicy, rich and proper comforting — this one-pan stew is smoky, creamy and topped with perfectly roasted cod.
keywords: Spicy Chorizo and Bean Stew with Baked Cod
instructions: Cut the chorizo into 1cm cubes. Dice the red onion and thinly slice the garlic.

Add the chorizo to a cold medium saucepan and place over a medium heat. Cook gently for 5–6 mins until the fat has rendered and the chorizo is crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the fat in the pan.

In a small bowl, mix half of the paprika with the olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Rub this all over the cod fillets. Place on a lined tray and roast at 190°C for 8–10 mins until just cooked through and flaky.
Back to the pan: add the onion, garlic and the remaining paprika. Cook for 3–4 mins, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to caramelise.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes and chuck in the kale. Simmer for 10 mins until slightly thickened.
Add the butter beans along with water to loosen. Simmer for 2–3 more mins to warm everything through, then stir in half of the crispy chorizo. Squeeze in a little lemon juice and season to taste.
Divide the stew between bowls and top with the roasted cod. Finish with the remaining chorizo, a dollop of yoghurt and a handful of chopped parsley.

name: Spicy Chorizo & Pepper Stew
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

A banging Spanish butter bean stew topped with a gremolata dressing and a dollop of aioli. Perfect weeknight food.
instructions: Finely chop the red onions and thinly slice ¾ of the garlic cloves. Cut the chorizo into chunky coins and the jarred grilled red peppers into strips about 1-2 cm wide.

Preheat a large saucepan over a medium-high heat and add a good glug of olive oil. Add the chorizo and cook for 3-4 mins, or until rendered and beginning to crisp up a little. Add the onions and cook for 4-5 mins with a pinch of salt before dropping in the sliced garlic.

Cook together for one more minute before tipping in the butter beans, the liquid from their tins, the tinned tomatoes and the jarred peppers. Season with salt and a little pepper. Cook together for 20 mins or so until slightly reduced.
Finely chop the parsley and tip into a bowl with the zest and juice of the lemons. Mix with a little olive oil.
Finely grate the remaining garlic clove into a bowl with the mayonnaise and mix thoroughly.
Divide the stew between warm bowls and top with a few spoons of the gremolata parsley dressing. Finish with a dollop of garlicky mayo and serve. Throw on an extra lemon wedge if you like.

name: Spicy Clam Ramyun
description: Clams and spicy Korean instant noodles are a match made in heaven. The natural brine from the clams add saltiness and umami to an already flavourful dish. Use fresh or frozen clams, it's up to you.
instructions: Get the clams in a colander and rinse them under running cold water to remove any dirt. Fill a mixing bowl with cold water and stir in the salt. Transfer the clams to the salty water and set aside.
For the topping, thinly slice the green chilli and spring onions and mince the white onion. Mix them together in a small bowl and set aside.
Lightly crush the sesame seeds in a pestle and mortar, then set aside.

Peel the garlic cloves then place the knife on top and smash using your palm. Heat the extra virgin olive oil and smashed garlic cloves in a large deep lidded frying pan set over a medium heat. Sauté for 2-3 mins, uncovered, until the edges of the garlic turn golden.
Drain and add the clams to the pan, followed by the sake. Turn the heat to high and gently shake the pan to combine the ingredients. Continue for about 30 seconds to cook off the sake.

Add the chicken stock (or water if you prefer) and cover with the lid (or you can use another pan as a makeshift lid). Bring the liquid to a boil then cook for 1-2 mins until the clams have opened. Transfer the open clams to a plate for now.
To the pan, add the noodles and all their seasoning sachets and mix to combine. Pop the lid back on and cook for a minute less than the noodle packet instructions.
Reduce the heat to low-medium then return the clams to the pan, placing them on top of the noodles, around the outside. Sprinkle over the topping mixture and grate over the lemon zest.
Remove from the heat, finish with the crushed sesame seeds and serve in the pan.

name: Spicy Coconut Mussels
description: This is the best way of pimping those mussels you get in cardboard boxes from the supermarket. Cook them up with a spicy curry paste and coconut milk, and you’ll have an affordable yet bougie meal on your hands.
instructions: Roughly chop two of your chillies (removing the seeds), along with your ginger, garlic and lemongrass.
Add your chillies to a food processor with 1 tbsp vegetable oil, and blend to a smooth paste. Add a splash of water if needed.
Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a good splash of vegetable oil, then tip in your chilli paste. Cook out for 5 mins until your oil is stained red.
Meanwhile, add your garlic, ginger, lemongrass, coriander stalks and cumin to your same food processor, without washing it up. Blitz to a smooth paste, adding a splash of water if needed.
Add your garlic paste to the chilli pan, and cook for another few mins until fragrant. Pour in your coconut milk and simmer for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, cook your mussels according to packet instructions.
Finely slice your remaining chilli and roughly chop your coriander. Cut one half of your lime into wedges.
Add your mussels to your coconut broth along with the fish sauce and juice of your remaining lime. Season to taste with salt.
Serve up in bowls, topped with your sliced chillies, coriander and a lime wedge. Dunk in some crusty bread. Yum.

name: Spicy Couscous & Garlic Butter Prawns
description: The food so nice they named it twice, couscous is paired here with garlic butter prawns for an easy five-minute dinner recipe.
instructions: Put the couscous into a bowl and cover it with boiling water. Pop a plate on top and leave to soak for 3 mins.
Finely slice spring onions and chop most of the parsley. Finely slice the red chilli.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan and crush in the garlic. Add the spring onions and fajita seasoning. Fry for 1 min, until aromatic, then add the sweetcorn and red chilli and fry for a min further. Tip the spring onion mixture into the couscous along with the parsley and the zest and juice of ½ a lime. Fluff the couscous with a fork and season with salt and pepper.
Wipe the frying pan and add the butter, melting it over a medium heat before adding in the prawns. Cook for 2-3 min until bright pink, then take it off the heat.
While the prawns cook, slice the red peppers and add to the couscous and tip into bowls. Top with the prawns and a scattering of parsley. Serve with the remaining lime half.

name: Spicy Crab Mac & Cheese
description: Make this indulgent brown butter and crab macaroni cheese spiked with jalapeńos and hot sauce. It's comfort food on another level.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Boil the macaroni in salted water for 7-8 mins. Drain, holding onto a cup of the cooking water. Thinly slice the jalapeños.

While the pasta cooks, warm the milk until it’s just below a simmer. In a large saucepan, melt the butter over a medium heat. Allow it to melt, foam and start to sizzle. Add ¾ of the jalapeños and cook off for a minute or two before tipping in the flour. Whisk the flour into the butter to make a roux. Cook over a medium heat for 6-7 mins or until it has a caramel brown colour and smells toasty.

Working gradually, whisk the warm milk into the roux, one ladle at a time, ensuring the sauce is smooth between each addition. Keep going until all of the milk has been incorporated and you have a smooth, rich béchamel. Take the saucepan off the heat, grate the cheeses into the béchamel and whisk to combine. Whisk in the sriracha and the brown crab meat. Season with salt to taste.

Fold the pasta through the spicy cheese sauce and tip into a baking dish. Scatter the white crab meat over the top along with the remaining sliced jalapeños. Mix the shichimi togarashi with the breadcrumbs and sesame and sprinkle over the top.
Slide into the oven for 20-25 mins until golden and bubbling. Whip it out, allow it to sit for 10 mins and then serve.

name: Spicy Creamy Cumin Tofu Noodles
description: This noodle dish combines one of my favourite noodles - cumin lamb belt noodles - with the viral creamy mapo tofu, kept meat-free. I love the texture of the crumbled tofu, tossed through a pungent spicy sauce you'd think it was chicken or turkey.
instructions: Crumble the firm tofu into a bowl. Core and chop the green peppers into 2cm chunks and finely mince the garlic. Pick half the coriander leaves and set aside, then thinly slice the rest, stalks and all.
Tip the cumin seeds and Szechuan peppercorns into a blender and blend until ground, then tip into a bowl. Stir the gochujang, balsamic vinegar, soy sauce and water through.

Add the silken tofu to the empty blender, season with salt and blend until smooth. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil, drop in the pappardelle and cook according to packet instructions, then drain, leaving a little cooking water clinging so it stays loose and doesn't stick together.
Place a wok over a high heat with the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the crumbled tofu and fry for 10-15 mins, until lightly golden. Tip onto a tray.
Add the peppers to the wok and cook for 4-6 mins, until starting to soften, then stir the garlic and sliced coriander through until fragrant.

Pour the soy mixture into the peppers and stir the crispy tofu mince through. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to medium and simmer until the sauce absorbs into the tofu and thickens a little, it'll still be a little runny. Taste and season with more salt, vinegar or pepper, if needed.

Toss the pappardelle with ¾ of the creamy tofu sauce and share into bowls or boxes. Top with the remaining creamy tofu sauce and spoon over the spicy cumin tofu. Finish with a scattering of the reserved coriander.

name: Spicy Creamy Garlic Butter Udon
description: A creamy, spicy play on carbonara with chewy udon noodles, jammy boiled eggs and smashed cucumbers to cut through the richness. A super quick midweek meal.
keywords: Spicy Creamy Garlic Butter Udon Recipe
instructions: Cook the eggs in a pot of boiling water for 6 mins then transfer to a bowl of ice cold water to cool (don’t drain the pot of water yet).
Meanwhile, finely slice the spring onions and mince the shallot and garlic.

Whack the cucumber with a rolling pin or cleaver then cut into 1cm slices and add to a mixing bowl. Add the sesame oil, chilli flakes, sesame seeds, apple cider vinegar, sugar, ¼ of the minced garlic and ¼ of the light soy sauce. Mix to combine until the sugar has dissolved.
Cook the udon in the same pot of boiling water for 3 mins then drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, peel and halve the eggs.

Heat the butter in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the garlic and shallots and sauté for 30 seconds. Stir in the gochujang and cook for a minute until the butter turns a reddish hue. Add the single cream and remaining light soy sauce and grate in the Parmesan. Mix to combine and cook for another 2 mins.
Remove the pan from the heat, add the udon noodles and mix gently to coat the noodles in the sauce.
Divide the udon between plate bowls. Top with the eggs, the smashed cucumber and a heap of sliced spring onions.

name: Spicy Croque Madame
description: The tastiest little croque you'll ever eat with a special spicy white sauce and grated gruyère. Stepping up your brunch game.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.
Add a large knob of butter to a frying pan (saving the rest for later). Allow it to melt.
Add the flour and paprika into the pan and stir into a loose paste, this is known as a roux. Add a splash of your milk and stir. Keep adding your milk gradually, stirring out the lumps.
Grate your Gruyère and add half to your pan. Stir until it starts to thicken. Season with salt and pepper and mix together.
Cut eight slices of your sourdough and place them onto a baking tray.

Butter the slices generously with the remaining butter, then add 3 tbsp of the roux sauce onto four of the slices. Add two slices of ham on top of the first layer of roux and top with another slice of bread. Add another 3 tbsp of the roux to the top of each sandwich and spread.
Sprinkle the remaining cheese over the top of each sandwich and then place them under the grill for 8 minutes.
Crack your British Lion eggs into a frying pan, with some olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and cook until each egg has a nice, crispy base.
Get your sandwiches out of the oven and add an egg on top of each one. Then tuck into this delicious dish!

name: Spicy Cumin Roasted Chicken Thighs with Braised Greens
description: A simple weeknight dinner. Crispy slightly spicy chicken thighs go great with brothy braised seasonal greens.
keywords: Spicy cumin roasted chicken thighs with braised greens recipes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Peel all the garlic, pull out 4 cloves and grate them into a bowl. Add in the cumin and chilli flakes with a large glug of oil and mix together.
Rub this onto the chicken thighs and set aside.
Chop up the leeks and pull apart the leaves of the chicory.
Add the kale, leeks, chicory and remaining peeled garlic into a large baking tray a. Rub with salt and pepper then pour in 1 litre of chicken stock.
Pop the chicken thighs on top and generously sprinkle with salt. Pop this in the oven for 20 mins then increase the heat to 200°C for 15 mins to get the skin extra crispy.
Meanwhile, toast your flaked almonds with some oil on a very low heat until golden brown.
Top the chicken thighs with the almond flakes and tuck in.

name: Spicy Egg & Cheese Breakfast Sandos
description: These cheesy breakfast sandwiches with homemade coriander salsa are the best way to start your day. Make a big batch in advance and freeze them until you’re ready to eat. Trust us, knowing you have a stash of these in your freezer will improve your life.
keywords: Make-Ahead Spiced Cheesy Egg Sarnies recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to fan 180°C. Grease and line a 20x20cm baking tray.

Make the chutney: Roughly chop the chillies and ginger. Pick the mint leaves and discard the stems. Add the coriander, stalks and all, into a blender with the rest of the ingredients and a pinch of salt and sugar. Add the oil and blend together until smooth. Then, season to taste with lemon juice, black pepper and more salt and sugar, if needed.
Break up the hash browns into 1cm pieces and cut the cheddar into 1cm cubes. Add them to your prepared baking tray.

Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk together with the salt and crème fraîche, then tip into the tray, over the hashbrown and cheddar pieces. Swirl through ½ the chutney, then slide into the oven to bake for 25-30 mins until the edges have puffed but the centre is still slightly wobbly. Remove from the oven and leave the eggs to cool slightly before transferring to a chopping board until cool enough to handle (10-15 mins). Cut into 12 even portions.
If eating straight away, toast the rolls (skip this step if making ahead). Spread ketchup on one of the sides and chutney on the other. Sandwich the egg in between.
If making ahead, wrap each sandwich in baking paper and freeze for up to 3 months. Before serving, microwave on high for bursts of 30 secs, until heated throughout.

name: Spicy Feta Dip With Crispy Herbs
description: This might be the easiest recipe I’ve written, just lob 5 things in a blender. You can top with fresh herbs, but frying them is a nice, and very pretty, touch.
instructions: Cut the top off the chillies and roughly chop, keeping the seeds in!
Add the feta, yoghurt, chopped chillies to the bowl of a food processor. Finely grate in the garlic and the zest and juice of one lemon. Add a glug of olive oil and whizz until smooth.

Pick the herbs from their stems. Cover the base of a frying pan with olive oil and set over a medium heat. Add a basil leaf, and when it starts to fry and crackle, add a few more, they’ll fizz around a bit and when they stop, they’re done. Lift them out onto a paper towel to drain.
Repeat with the remaining herbs, be careful that the oil doesn’t get too hot. Once your herbs are fried, sprinkle them with fine salt.
Spread your dip out onto a platter and top with a drizzle of olive oil. Scatter with the crispy herbs and Aleppo pepper.
Serve with steamy pitta breads and raw veggies for dipping.

name: Spicy Ginger Chicken Udon
description: A simple, umami rich stir fry laced with chilli, chicken and coriander – the triple C. The key is to have everything prepped before anything touches the pan, then it can be cooked in minutes.
instructions: Get the marinade ingredients in a mixing bowl, season with salt and black pepper and stir to combine. Slice the chicken thighs into 1cm strips then add to the marinade. Mix to thoroughly coat then set aside.
In a separate small bowl, add the ingredients for the sauce, season with salt and black pepper and stir to combine. Set aside.
Mince the garlic and ginger, thinly slice the spring onions on a diagonal, thinly slice the red chilli and roughly chop the coriander. Cut the lime into wedges.
Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil. Add the udon noodles and cook for a minute less than the packet instructions. Drain and rinse with cold water until just warm to the touch. Set aside.

Heat a large dry frying pan or wok over a high heat for 1-2 mins. Add a glug of vegetable oil and the chicken thighs and stir fry for 2-3 mins until the chicken is slightly browned and golden. Add the garlic and ginger and stir fry for a further 1-2 mins until fragrant. Add the spring onion and udon noodles, mix to combine and cook for a further minute.

Push the noodles to one side and add a small glug of vegetable oil to the pan. Crack in the eggs and use a wooden spoon to break the yolks and scramble them with the whites. Let the eggs cook for 30 seconds then mix everything in the pan together, combining the egg with the noodles and chicken.
Pour the sauce into the pan and mix until the sauce is fully combined with the noodles. Add the beansprouts, fresh coriander and red chilli and stir fry for a final 1-2 mins.
Transfer the noodles to bowls immediately. Sprinkle with shichimi powder (or chilli powder if you prefer) and sesame seeds, drizzle with chilli oil and garnish with a wedge of lime.

name: Spicy Gochujang Beef Pasta
description: We’ve combined two of our favourite things: gochujang and pasta. A super simple but delicious dinner that’s on the table in 20 mins.
instructions: Finely dice the shallots and ginger, and crush the garlic. Thinly slice the chilli and spring onions and set aside for garnish.
Fill a large saucepan with salted water and bring it to the boil over a medium-high heat. Once boiling, drop in your pasta and cook following packet instructions until al dente.

Meanwhile, heat a glug of sesame oil in a separate large pan set over a high heat. When the oil starts to sizzle, add the beef mince and use a wooden spoon to spread into a thin layer. Leave the beef to cook for a few mins until nicely browned then flip it over and cook the other side for a couple of mins, using your spoon to break it up. Transfer the beef to a plate and set aside, leaving the juices in the pan.
Return the pan with the juices to the hob and reduce the heat to medium. Add the shallots, garlic and ginger and cook for around 7 mins until softened.

Return the beef to the pan with the softened aromatics then add the tomato purée, gochujang paste, soy sauce, honey and the juice of the lime. Add a couple of ladles of the pasta cooking water then mix to combine and bring to a simmer.

Drain the cooked pasta and add to the sauce, along with another ladle of pasta water if it needs loosening up. Stir to coat and continue to simmer for a minute or two until the pasta is cooked to your liking.
To serve, divide the pasta between bowls and top with the sliced spring onions and chillies, and sesame seeds.

name: Spicy Gochujang Pork Burrito with Kimchi & Rice
description: Take your Spicy Pork Ragú batch to the max with this flavour-packed burrito. With Gochujang mayo and kimchi all wrapped up in a crispy toasted tortilla. A winning midweek lunch or dinner.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Spicy Pork Ragú batch recipe.
Heat the rice following pack instructions.
Warm the Spicy Pork Ragú in a frying pan over a medium heat until bubbling. Stir through the kidney beans and cook for another 2-3 mins until hot.
In a small bowl, mix the mayonnaise with the gochujang and a squeeze of lime juice. Season with salt and black pepper.
Toast the tortillas in a dry frying pan for 30 seconds on each side, until warm and flexible.

To build each burrito, lay a romaine leaf in the centre of each tortilla. Top with the rice, Spicy Pork Ragú, kimchi, and a good drizzle of the Gochujang mayo. Add the second romaine leaf on top.Fold the sides in, then roll up from the bottom. If you like, toast the burrito seam-side down in the hot pan for 1-2 mins to seal and crisp.

name: Spicy Gochujang Tomato Soup
description: Level up your tomato soup by adding gochujang. The umami notes of the gochujang balance out the sweetness of the tomatoes, confusing your taste buds in the best possible way.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Peel and chop the onion, peel and mince the garlic, slice and de-seed the bell peppers, and remove the core from the tomatoes. Grate the cheddar and set it aside.

Place the prepared vegetables (onions, garlic, bell peppers, and tomatoes) in a baking dish. Drizzle generously with olive oil, and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Bake for 45-60 mins, or until the vegetables are soft and slightly caramelised

While the vegetables are roasting, slice the baguette into 1cm thick slices. Spread each slice with a layer of gochujang (using about ⅖ of the gochujang), then arrange on a lined baking sheet and sprinkle with grated cheddar.
When the vegetables are almost done, place the baking sheet with the baguette slices into the oven and bake for about 10 mins, or until the cheese is melted and golden.

Remove the roasted vegetables from the oven and transfer them to a blender. Add the remaining gochujang and a splash of the stock and blend until smooth. Add more stock or water to adjust the soup's thickness to your liking (you may not need all the stock).
Divide the soup across bowls and top each with the cheesy gochujang baguette croutons and a small spoonful of sesame seeds.

name: Spicy Green Aubergine Curry
description: Blending spinach in with your curry paste is a great way to pack in some extra dark leafy greens, plus it gives the curry a really gorgeous deep green colour. The leftovers will keep really well in the fridge or freezer, making it perfect for meal prep.
keywords: Spicy Green Aubergine Curry & Rice recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Set a full kettle of water to boil.

Start by making the curry paste: add the fresh coriander into a sieve and pour the boiling water over to wilt. Repeat the process for the frozen spinach until defrosted, then drain and squeeze as much water out of both greens as you can. Add the greens into a blender with the green chillies, ground spices, water and oil. Blend together until smooth. Set aside.

Trim and chop the aubergine into 2cm chunks. Place onto a lined baking tray, drizzle with some olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss together then slide into the oven to roast for 20-25 mins until soft.
Cook the rice following packet instructions.

Place a frying pan with high sides over medium-high heat. Tip in ½ the coconut milk and cook, stirring, until the coconut splits and the solids golden. Add the curry paste and cook, stirring occasionally, for 7-10 mins until the excess water has evaporated and you have a dark green mixture.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the red onion and transfer to a bowl. Squeeze over the lime juice and season with salt and sugar. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

Stir the curry leaves through the green curry base, until fragrant. Tip the chickpeas in with the remaining coconut milk and water, and season with salt and pepper. Turn the heat down to low-medium and let it gently simmer, stirring occasionally.
Once the aubergines are cooked, stir them through the curry, adding a splash of water if needed to loosen. Taste and season with some of the lime pickling liquid, sugar, salt and black pepper.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls. Spoon in the curry and top with some pickled onions.

name: Spicy Green Chilli & Chicken Noodles
description: Sticky, creamy and a little bit fiery. Chicken mince and green chillis and charred green peppers tossed with udon noodles in a miso-tahini sauce that coats every strand. It's seriously satisfying.
instructions: Thinly slice the green chillies and chop the green peppers into 1cm chunks. Place a large pot of water over a high heat and bring to the boil.

Place a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the chicken mince and cook for 5-7 mins, until browned. Add the peppers and stir-fry for 4-5 mins, until softened and vibrant green. Add the chillies, five spice, oyster sauce and half the sesame seeds and toss everything through. Season with the sugar (or a little more oyster sauce or salt if needed), then remove from the heat and cover to keep warm.
Stir all the sauce ingredients together in a large bowl until smooth. If it's too thick, add a splash more cold water until you get a creamy consistency.

Once the water is boiling, cook the udon according to packet instructions. Before draining, reserve a mug of the cooking water. Drain the udon, then toss into the sauce with a splash of the cooking water until glossy and well coated.
Divide the noodles between bowls and top with the chicken mince. Finish with a drizzle of chilli oil and a sprinkle of the remaining sesame seeds.

name: Spicy Harissa Chickpeas
description: Buckle up, we've got another delicious batch recipe for you. Make these spicy harissa chickpeas and you'll have yourself more delicious meals to eat throughout the week.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic. Place a saucepan over a medium-high heat and add a tbsp of olive oil. Poke the cherry tomatoes with the tip of a knife, this will encourage them to pop!
Add the sliced garlic and cherry tomatoes to the pan and stir for 1 min, they should start to burst. Add the harissa paste and the can of cherry tomatoes. Bubble on a medium heat for 15 - 20 mins.

Throw in the whole jars (or tins) of chickpeas along with their liquid. Add the stock cube and turn up the heat to high. Use a potato masher or fork to crush the mix a bit- this will help thicken the sauce a little. Simmer for 5-10 mins until nicely warmed through.
Add the juice of half the lemon. Season to taste, and enjoy!

name: Spicy Harissa Pasta e Ceci
description: Warming, nourishing, and pretty damn easy to pull together, this take on pasta e ceci is going to tick all of the boxes. We promise.
instructions: Chop up the onions and carrot into a chunky dice and thinly slice the garlic cloves.

Add a shot of oil to a large saucepan and set over a medium heat. Once hot, tip in the onions and carrots and cook with a pinch of salt for 5-6 mins. Add the garlic and harrissa and cook for another 3-4 mins.
Tip in the chickpeas along with the liquid from the jar, the stock and the water. Season well with salt and black pepper. Bring to a boil and drop in the pasta.
Cook for 8 mins before finishing with roughly chopped peppers and finely chopped spring onions.
Add the juice of the orange and divide between warm bowls. Top with chopped dill and crumbled feta.

name: Spicy Harissa Sausage Fusilli
description: A simple spicy sausage pasta recipe that you can make with a batch-cooked sausage ratatouille bake. Dinner doesn't get easier than this.
instructions: Start by making the sausage ratatouille traybake. Heat the oven to 180°C/356°F. Roughly chop all your vegetables and chuck them in a baking tray.

Add the sausages, rosemary, bay leaves, tinned tomatoes and whole garlic clove to the tray. Mix everything together and get it in the oven for 45 mins, then remove and set aside. Optional: if you're batch cooking the sausage ratatouille traybake for the week, portion it out into Tupperware containers now.
Bring a pot of water to the boil, season well with salt, and drop the pasta in for 9-10 mins. Reserve a cup of pasta water.
Use scissors to cut the sausages into 1cm chunks. Stir through the harissa.

Finely chop the parsley and grate the Parmesan. Add the cooked fusilli to the tray and toss to combine with a splash of pasta water. Season with salt and black pepper. Return to the oven for a couple of minutes to warm through.
To serve, spoon into bowls. Finish with the parsley and Parmesan.

name: Spicy Harissa Vegan Sausage Rolls
description: A delicious vegan alternative to your classic sausage roll. Packed with veggie sausages, cumin, caramelised onions, mushrooms, and spicy harissa.
instructions: Thinly slice the onion, mushrooms and garlic.
Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large frying pan or sauté pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 mins or until fragrant.
Add the onion and season with salt and pepper. Turn the heat down to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 mins.
Add the mushrooms, season with another pinch of salt and pepper and toss to combine. Cook undisturbed for 10 mins then toss and cook undisturbed for another 10 mins.
Add the garlic and stir fry for 2 mins then remove the saucepan from the heat and let cool.
Heat your oven to 220°C.
Transfer the mushroom mixture to a food processor.

Break the veggie sausages into pieces and place in the same food processor with the fresh parsley, harissa paste, and 3 teaspoons of maple syrup. Season with salt and pepper and blitz until smooth-ish.
Melt the vegan butter. Add the remaining 2 teaspoons of maple syrup and mix to combine. This is your vegan ‘egg’ wash.
Unroll your puff pastry. Arrange the veggie sausage mix in a sausage shape on the pastry. Tightly roll to form a long sausage roll, seam side down.
Brush the exterior of the roll with the vegan egg wash and sprinkle with the za’atar.
Chop each roll into 8 pieces and arrange spaced apart on a large baking sheets.
Bake for 30 mins, or until they are a deep golden brown and your pastry looks tender and flaky. Serve hot or at room temperature.
For an optional, easy dipping sauce, combine equal parts harissa paste and maple syrup. It works really well!

name: Spicy Honey Miso and Charred Spring Onion Skewers
description: It's BBQ season and I’ve created these skewers that are perfect for a summer cookout. Marinated in a spicy honey miso, they’re as delicious as they sound.
keywords: Spicy honey miso and charred spring onion skewer recipes
instructions: Chop the peppers into 2cm sized chunks and spring onions into 3cm parts lengthways.
Roughly chop your veggie chicken chunks into 2cm-size pieces.

Start assembling your skewers by threading two plant-based pieces followed by a chunk of pepper and spring onion onto your skewer in that order. Continue that pattern until each skewer is filled. Repeat for the remaining skewers.
Grate your ginger and garlic into a bowl. Add miso, soy sauce, honey, chilli flakes, sesame oil and rice wine vinegar, and give it a good mix.
Brush your skewers with the sauce mix and leave to marinate for 10-15 mins.
On medium heat, add the skewers to a griddle pan and lightly brush your skewers with a drizzle of sesame oil. Cook for a few mins on each side until the skewers are golden. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Lamb Hummus Bowl
description: Once you’ve made this, you’ll never be able to look at regular hummus again, because you’ll know that it needs some crispy lamb on top to make it truly epic.
instructions:
Get a large frying pan over a super high heat and drizzle in a splash of oil. Tip in the minced lamb and use the back of a
wooden spoon to break up the meat into small chunks. Fry,
stirring occasionally, for about 8 minutes until all the water has
evaporated and the mince is getting brown and crisp.
Meanwhile, cut and deseed the peppers and cut the cucumber
into rough finger-sized crudités and put on a serving plate. Spoon
both tubs of hummus into one large serving bowl.
Back to the lamb. Add the harissa and season with salt and
black pepper. Give everything a good mix and then leave to cook
for a few minutes more.
Toast the flatbreads while you are waiting.
Tip the lamb on top of the hummus in the bowl, then scatter over
the pomegranate seeds. Tear over the mint and parsley. Serve
with the vegetable crudités and toasted flatbreads.

name: Spicy Lamb Linguine
description: Using leftovers from our Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake, this spicy pasta makes a delicious midweek dinner you can whip up in under 30.
instructions: Make the Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake.
Crumble the meatballs into smaller pieces and roughly chop the roasted chilli.

Thinly slice the garlic cloves and tip into a pan with a shot of olive oil. Set over a medium heat and cook for 2-3 mins before adding the chopped chilli. Now add the lamb meatballs and tip in the chopped tinned tomatoes. Add half a tin of water and bring to a simmer.
Cook for 10-12 mins. Meanwhile, cook the pasta according to the package instructions.
Transfer the cooked pasta to the sauce and toss through, adding a little Parmesan and the juice of the lemon.
Divide between warm bowls and serve with extra Parmesan.

name: Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake
description: Rich and fragrant lamb meatballs spiced with ras el hanout and harissa. There's a lot to love in this Middle Eastern-inspired batch recipe.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Tip the lamb mince into a bowl.

Finely chop a third of the red onions and add to the lamb mince with the pine nuts and raisins. Finely chop half of the parsley along with the red peppers and tip them into the bowl, too. Add the ras el hanout and season well with salt and pepper. Mix vigorously until the mixture starts to get a little sticky.

Grab a large roasting tray and dump in the drained chickpeas. Split the chilli in half and chuck it into the tray, too. Cut the remaining onions into a super chunky dice and get those into the tray with the harissa. Toss everything together with a healthy pinch of salt.

Using wet hands, form the lamb mixture into little meatballs, about the size of golf balls, and lay over the chickpeas. Slide into the oven for 25-30 mins, turning the meatballs halfway. Ensuring they are nice and browned and cooked through.
Once cooked, finish with the rest of the parsley and the zest and juice of the lemon.
Divide between plates and dig in.

name: Spicy Lamb Meatballs & Chickpeas With Tahini Drizzle
description: A dead easy recipe you can make using our batch-cooked spiced lamb meatball traybake.
keywords: Spicy Lamb Meatballs & Chickpeas With Tahini Drizzle
Spicy Lamb Meatballs & Chickpeas With Tahini Drizzle recipe
instructions: Make the Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake.
Reheat the leftovers of your Spicy Lamb Meatball Traybake. Finely slice the red onion and chop up the parsley.
Once the mixture is hot, serve with a drizzle of tahini, fresh parsley and lemon wedges.

name: Spicy Lentil Stew
description: Spicy lentils and charred, roasted cauliflower. An incredible pairing. Topped with a herby, cooling yoghurt sauce. One of the great veggie dishes.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Cut your cauliflower florets in half and place on a baking tray. Drizzle olive oil over the cauliflower and season with all of the turmeric, 1 Tbsp of your paprika, 1 Tbsp of cumin, ½ Tbsp of chilli flakes, a pinch of salt and a good crack of black pepper. Mix the cauliflower to coat in the seasoning and whack in the oven for 20 minutes or until crispy and golden.

Add a large handful of coriander to a food processor, leaving a few sprigs for garnish. Add one clove of garlic and the juice of half a lemon to the blender with 2 tbsp of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Blitz until the coriander is finely chopped.
Add the yoghurt to a bowl and pour in the coriander oil. Mix to combine and season to taste. Place the coriander yoghurt in the fridge until serving.
Time for that spicy stew. Finely dice your onion and carrot. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large saucepan on medium heat and add the onion and carrot. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring often.

Mince the remaining cloves of garlic and add them to the pan with the rest of the chilli flakes, a pinch of salt and a few grinds of pepper. Give it a stir before adding the remaining cumin and paprika. Coat the veg in the spices, add the tomato purée and lentils and give it all a mix. Pour the stock into the pan and leave to simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Once the stew has cooked down, quarter your tomatoes and add them to the pan along with your spinach. Stir the spinach into the stew and leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Serve the spicy lentil stew with a drizzle of coriander yoghurt and your crispy cauliflower. Chop the rest of the fresh coriander and sprinkle it over the stew with a crack of black pepper. Dig in!

name: Spicy Lentil Turkish Eggs
description: The combo of spiced butter, herbs and oozy egg yolks is unmatched. I've taken those elements and mixed them with lentils to make your breakfast even more protein packed. Lovely stuff.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Carefully lower in the eggs and cook for 6-7 mins, then remove, cool and peel.

Add the Greek yoghurt to a bowl, then drain and rinse the lentils before adding them in too. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and grate in the garlic. Season with salt and pepper, then set aside. Finely slice the red chilli, removing the seeds if you don't like it too spicy.

Melt the butter in a small frying pan. Once foamy, add the Aleppo chilli flakes and sliced chilli. Swirl the pan for a couple of seconds, then remove from the heat and set aside. Pick the parsley leaves.
Serve up the yoghurty lentils topped with the halved eggs, chilli butter and parsley.

name: Spicy Mango, 'Nduja & Scotch Bonnet Roast Chicken
description: If you want something to impress a crowd, this recipe is it. Spatchcocked chicken marinated in mango chutney, 'nduja and yoghurt, roasted over a spiced mango sauce until well browned and glossy. Served with a bright lime slaw and warm flatbreads. It's seriously worth the effort.
instructions: Place the chicken breast-side down on a large chopping board. Using sturdy kitchen scissors, cut along either side of the backbone and remove it. Flip the chicken over and press firmly down on the breastbone until you hear it crack flat. Alternatively, ask your butcher to do this for you.

Pat the chicken dry and season all over with a generous pinch of salt. Add all the marinade ingredients to a large bowl and mix together. Add the chicken and turn to coat thoroughly. Leave to marinate for up to 2 hours at room temperature.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the cabbage on a mandolin and tip into a bowl. Thinly slice just the green parts of the spring onions into rounds and add to the bowl, set the white parts aside for another use, like a stir-fry or soup base. Thinly slice the coriander and chillies and add to the bowl with the juice of the lime and the salt. Toss together and set aside.

Heat the oven to 230°C. Add all the sauce ingredients (leaving the scotch bonnet whole) to a 35 x 26cm deep-sided roasting tray and whisk together. Sit the chicken skin-side up on top of the sauce, spreading the legs out so the skin browns evenly. Place on a shelf in the bottom half of the oven, you don't want it too close to the top or the chicken and sauce will burn.

Roast for 20 mins with the legs at the back of the oven, then reduce the heat to 180°C, rotate the tray so the legs are now at the front, and roast for another 30 mins, until the chicken is well browned and cooked through. Transfer to a board to rest for 15 mins.

Discard the cinnamon stick and fish out the Scotch bonnet. Scrape the sauce into a blender, don't worry if it looks curdled, it'll blitz up smooth. Tear half the Scotch bonnet into the blender and blitz until smooth. Taste and add more Scotch bonnet if you want more heat.
Grill the flatbreads in a hot frying pan for a couple of minutes on each side until well browned but still soft.
Once rested, carve the chicken and season with salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Arrange on a platter, pour the sauce around it and serve with the slaw and flatbreads.

name: Spicy Margarita
description: The margarita is an absolute classic. Perfectly balanced and super refreshing. Want to level up? Make it spicy. Toby x
instructions: Cut a small wedge of lime and rub it on the rim of your glass to help the salt and chilli flakes stick. Juice the rest of the lime and set aside.
Cut 4 slices of the jalapeño.
On a small plate, sprinkle the salt and chilli flakes in a circle the same circumference as your glass.
Rub the rim of your glass gently in the chilli salt, fill it with ice and then set it aside.
Add a handful of ice, the tequila, Cointreau, sliced jalapeño and lime juice to your cocktail shaker.
Shake hard for 20 seconds.
Double strain into your glass and garnish with a slice of chilli.

name: Spicy Mayo Fried Prawns on Rice
description: Easy, crispy shallow-fried prawns coated in an addictive tangy spicy mayo, sat on a bed of sushi rice and drenched in a sweet soy sauce. A quick, no-fuss weekday dinner, topped with a herb salad to cut through the richness, this Japanese fusion rice bowl will become a weekly staple before you know it!
instructions: Put the rice into a small saucepan. Add cold water and wash the rice, then drain and repeat twice more, or until the water runs clear.

Add the cold water to the drained rice and let it sit for 15 mins. Put the lid on, set the pan over a very high heat and bring to the boil. Once boiling, lower the heat to its lowest setting and cook for 11 mins. Turn off the heat and let sit for 10 mins with the lid on.

For the spicy mayo, zest the lemon into a large mixing bowl, then add the mayonnaise, sriracha, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp lime juice (save the rest of the lime for the salad) and ½ tbsp light soy sauce. Stir well to combine, then set aside.
Put 6 tbsp light soy sauce, the mirin and 1 tbsp brown sugar into a small saucepan. Heat on high and cook for around 2 mins until the sauce has reduced by one-third. Pour into a bowl and set aside.

For the salad, put 1 tbsp neutral oil, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp brown sugar, the juice of half a lime and the sesame seeds into a bowl. Stir thoroughly to combine until the sugar has dissolved. Slice the coriander into 2cm pieces, slice the red onion as thin as possible and tear the basil leaves. Add to the salad dressing, but don’t mix. Set aside.

Grab a bowl and add the prawns. Grate in the ginger, then add ½ tbsp light soy sauce, a pinch of salt and a few cracks of black pepper. Mix to combine. Add the cornstarch and toss to coat. The batter should be on the drier side. If it isn’t, add more cornstarch.

Add the vegetable oil to a medium frying pan. It should be around 1-2cm deep – add more oil if not. Heat on high for 4 mins, or until the oil is shimmering (trick: grab a chopstick and put it into the oil – if bubbles come out of the tip, the oil is ready). Add the prawns, one by one, and cook for 1-2 mins each side, or until golden. Transfer the prawns straight into the spicy mayo mix, making sure to drain any excess oil first. Toss to coat.
To serve, spoon the rice into a deep bowl and top with the mayo-coated prawns. Drizzle with the sweet soy sauce and finish with a generous handful of the dressed salad.

name: Spicy Miso Beef Udon Noodle Soup
description: A nourishing bowl of noodles should be in everyone's repertoire. This is one of the quickest and easiest one-pot noodle soups out there.
instructions: Thinly slice the steak (skip this step if you’re using pre-sliced steak). Finely mince the garlic. Thinly slice the white onion, shiitake mushroom and radish. Cut the stem off the pak choi and separate the leaves. Finely slice the spring onion and set aside for the garnish.
Add a splash of sesame oil and the minced garlic to a medium pan. Set it over a high heat and sauté for 1 min, or until fragrant.
Add in the beef, onion, mushroom, radish and chilli powder and fry for a further 2 mins.
Pour in the beef stock, gochujang and wakame and then put the lid on and boil for 3 mins.
Add in the udon and pak choi then cook for a further 3 mins.
Add the miso paste and a tbsp of broth to a bowl then stir until combined into a runny paste. Take the soup off the heat then pour in the miso paste and stir to combine.
Divide the soup between large deep bowls and garnish with generous amounts of spring onion.

name: Spicy Miso Carrot Soup
description: This soup is so warm and comforting, with minimal waste as the crispy carrot peels are roasted for extra crunch! We've also added some air fryer crispy rice croutons, but you can skip those if you're in a rush.
instructions: If you're making the crispy rice croutons (optional), cook the rice following packet instructions.
Heat your oven to 200°C / 180°C fan.
Peel and cut the carrots into 1cm slices, reserving the peels. Cut the onion into eighths. Smash the garlic cloves. Thinly slice the ginger. Roughly chop the red chilli.
Place the carrot peels in a small roasting tin. Season with salt and pepper, drizzle with vegetable oil and toss to coat. Roast for 10 mins or until crisp.
Place the remaining veg in a large roasting tin. Season with salt and pepper, drizzle with vegetable oil and toss to coat. Roast for 35 mins, or until the carrots are tender.

Meanwhile, heat the air fryer to 180°C. Mix the warm rice, pepper flakes and sesame seeds together in a bowl. Line a tin with parchment paper. Add the rice and push it down with a wooden spoon to compact into one even layer. Let it cool down fully before cutting into squares. 
Toss the rice squares in a drizzle of oil, then place into the air fryer. Air fry for 7-15 mins, until golden and crispy (if your croutons haven't gotten crispy yet, air fry for another 4 mins).

Slice the ginger into small matchsticks and thinly slice the red chilli.
Heat the vegetable oil in a small saucepan. Add the ginger and chilli and cook for 1 minute, then add the mixed seeds and cook for a further minute. Season with salt and pepper, to taste, then set aside to cool.

Transfer the contents of the roasting tin to a blender. Add the miso and vegetable stock and blitz until smooth. Pour into a saucepan and simmer over medium heat for 5 mins. Taste and adjust the salt level, to your liking.
Divide the soup between bowls. Top with a handful of crispy carrot peels and spring onions and finish with a spoonful or two of the chilli ginger oil, the tuck in and enjoy.

name: Spicy Miso Dense Bean Salad
description: This spicy bean salad’s got crunch, heat and loads of texture thanks to quinoa, edamame and a big hit of gochujang-miso dressing.
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Add the edamame beans and boil for 5 mins, then drain and rinse under cold water. Drain and rinse the cannellini beans.
Slice the romaine lettuce. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds and slice. Finely slice the spring onions.
In a large bowl, whisk together the white miso, gochujang, maple syrup and rice vinegar until smooth.
Add the cannellini beans, edamame, quinoa, lettuce, cucumber and spring onions. Toss everything together and season with salt to taste.

Top with the toasted sesame seeds and torn coriander leaves before serving.If making ahead, box up and chill until needed. The salad will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge. Store the dressing separately to keep the salad fresh.

name: Spicy Mushroom & Lentil Stew with Rice
description: Our Mushroom & Lentil Ragù gets a spicy Sichuan twist with silky tofu, doubanjiang heat & numbing peppercorns. Served over rice, it's fiery comfort.
instructions: Make the Mushroom & Lentil Ragù.
Slice the tofu into 2cm chunks.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the Sichuan peppercorns and toast for 1-2 mins until fragrant.

Stir the doubanjiang in and cook for 1-2 mins until the oil turns red and smells spicy. Add the Mushroom & Lentil Ragù and a splash of water, then bring to a simmer. Gently drop the silken tofu into the stew, stir gently and let everything bubble for 5 mins until warmed through. Taste and season with salt, if needed.
Reheat the rice and share into bowls. Spoon over the spicy mushroom stew.

name: Spicy Mushroom & Tofu Soup
description: Thank yourself later with this all-in-one soup that cooks straight from frozen. Umami-rich, gently fiery and completely slurpable, this one's perfect for when you want something nourishing without the faff.
instructions: Start by slicing the chestnut mushrooms and pak choi. Dice the tofu into small cubes and cut the spring onion into 2cm pieces.
Add the pack choi to a Tupperware along with the tofu, gochujang, spring onions, soy sauce, enoki mushrooms, chestnut mushrooms and mushroom stock. Box up and pop in the freezer until ready to use.
Once ready to cook, transfer the contents of the Tupperware into a saucepan set over a medium heat. Cover with a lid and allow the contents of the pan to melt.
Once melted, leave the soup to simmer for 5 minutes until the broth is piping hot. Then serve up topped with a scattering of sesame seeds and a drizzle of sesame oil.

name: Spicy Mushroom Pozole
description: A vegetarian pozole recipe that makes the most of chipotle paste, tender mushrooms, and corn tortillas. A real hearty affair.
instructions: Cut the mushrooms in half lengthways. Heat a large casserole pot or saucepan over a medium heat. Thinly slice the onions and garlic.
Season the mushrooms with salt and pepper and add to the pan with a shot of oil, cut-side down. Cook for 7-8 mins until golden brown.

Remove the mushrooms from the pan and add ¾ of the onions and all of the garlic. Cook for 5-6 mins until lightly sweated, season with salt and tip in the chipotle paste. Cook for another 3-4 mins, then add the veg stock. Bring to a bare simmer and return the mushrooms to the pan. Cook for 18-20 mins.

Meanwhile, slice the corn from the cobs, cut the tortillas into 1cm strips and finely shred the cabbage. De-seed and dice the tomatoes and thinly slice the radishes. Finely chop the whole bunch of coriander, stalks and all.

Once the soup has had 20 mins, drop in the corn and cook for a further 4 mins. Add the cabbage to the pot and warm through. At the last minute, stir through ¾ of the coriander and add the juice of two limes. Season with salt and pepper and divide between warm bowls.
Top with the remaining raw onion, feta, radishes, diced tomatoes, jalapeños, remaining limes and sliced tortillas.

name: Spicy Mushroom Ragù With Tagliatelle
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

An umami-rich mushroom ragù made using affordable ingredients from Aldi. This one's going to be a hit with the whole family.
keywords: Spicy Mushroom Ragù With Pasta recipe
instructions: Finely chop the walnuts or pulse in a food processor until coarse. Do the same with the mushrooms, working in batches if needed.

Heat the oven to 225°C fan. Spread the mushrooms out in a single layer across two lined baking trays. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15 mins, then scatter over the walnuts and return to the oven for 5–10 mins until everything is golden and toasty.

Peel and finely chop the onion, garlic, celery and carrot. Heat a splash of olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion, celery and carrot, season, and cook for 10–12 mins until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic and cook for 2 more mins until fragrant.

Add the tomato purée and harissa powder to the pan. Cook for 2–3 mins to deepen the flavour. Tip in the tinned tomatoes, then fill the empty tin with water and add that too. Crumble in the stock cube and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the roasted mushrooms and walnuts, along with ¼ of the tomato tin filled with water. Simmer for 15 mins, stirring occasionally, until thick and rich. Season to taste.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the packet instructions until al dente. Reserve a mug of cooking water, then drain.

Finely grate the parmesan. Tip the drained pasta into the sauce with a splash of the cooking water and the parmesan. Take off the heat and stir well to emulsify—the sauce should cling beautifully. Add more water if needed.
Divide between bowls and top with torn basil and extra parmesan, if you like.

name: Spicy Mushroom Skewers With Creamy Noodles
description: Something magical happens when you char mushrooms, and these marinated mushrooms hit all the spots. Served on saucy noodles, it's a quick and satisfying meal.
instructions: First make the mushroom marinade. In a blender, add 80ml soy sauce, 30ml maple syrup, 2 garlic cloves, 1 small chilli, 2 tbsp sesame oil and ginger, and blend until smooth. If you’re using wooden skewers, soak them in water to stop them sticking to the mushrooms later on.

Cut the mushrooms into bite-sized chunks. King oyster mushrooms can be sliced into 3mm ribbons and oyster mushrooms can be torn into pieces. Put the mushrooms and the marinade into a shallow bowl and mix well. Set aside.
Next, make the tahini sauce. In a bowl, add 130g tahini, the juice of one lime, 2 tbsp soy sauce, crispy chilli oil and 4 tbsp/60ml of water. Whisk until smooth. Set aside.

Skewer the mushrooms onto the sticks, finishing with a piece of chilli and spring onion if you like. Discard marinade. Griddle the skewers over high heat on a griddle pan, turning frequently, until charred and cooked through.
Set a pot of salted water to boil. Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions, stirring a few times to prevent sticking. Drain and put back into the pot.
Add the sauce to the noodles and heat through. If the sauce is very thick, add a little water.

To serve, spoon the noodles into a plate and lay the mushroom skewers on top, with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and extra sliced spring onion. Serve with the extra lime on the side to squeeze over the dish.

name: Spicy Peanut Air Fryer Salmon & Greens
description: Crunchy, spicy peanut-crusted salmon with fluffy rice. Quick to make and high in protein and plants, but still feels like a treat. She’s a beauty.
keywords: lunch box: Spicy Peanut Air Fryer Salmon Bowl
Spicy Peanut Air Fryer Salmon Bowl recipe
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions.

For the spice mix, finely chop or crush the peanuts and add to a large mixing bowl. Add the garlic powder, chilli powder, white pepper, sugar and sesame seeds and mix to combine. Transfer ¾ of the spice mix to a large plate, setting aside the rest for garnish.

Take your salmon and pop it on top of the spice mix, flesh side down. Press gently to coat, pressing it up the sides too. Drizzle the salmon with a little olive oil then transfer to the air fryer basket. Cook in the air fryer at 180°C for 8-10 mins or until cooked through (this will depend on the thickness of the salmon).

While the salmon is cooking, make the sauce. Add the peanuts to a high speed blender and blitz until you have a nice smooth sauce, scraping down the sides a few times if necessary. Halve the cherry tomatoes and deseed the chilli (or leave the seeds in if you like it spicy) then throw both into the blender and blitz until smooth. Taste and season with salt and the juice of the limes. Set aside.
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Drop in the green beans for 2 mins until tender, then drain and set aside.
Finely chop most of the coriander, saving some for garnish, and stir it through the cooked rice. Add the green beans to the rice and give it a mix to roughly combine.

Divide the rice and beans between Tupperware containers. Flake the salmon on top with the remaining spice mix. Scatter over the fresh coriander and nestle in a wedge of lime. Keep the sauce separate - either pour over in the morning of stash a little pot in your Tupperware box to add just before eating.Box up and pop in the fridge ready for later. These will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Spicy Peanut Air Fryer Salmon Bowl
description: Crunchy, spicy peanut-crusted salmon with fluffy rice. Quick to make and high in protein and plants, but still feels like a treat. She’s a beauty.
keywords: Spicy Peanut Air Fryer Salmon Bowl
Spicy Peanut Air Fryer Salmon Bowl recipe
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions.

For the spice mix, finely chop or crush the peanuts and add to a large mixing bowl. Add the garlic powder, chilli powder, white pepper, sugar and sesame seeds and mix to combine. Transfer ¾ of the spice mix to a large plate, setting aside the rest for garnish.

Take your salmon and pop it on top of the spice mix, flesh side down. Press gently to coat, pressing it up the sides too. Drizzle the salmon with a little olive oil then transfer to the air fryer basket. Cook in the air fryer at 180°C for 8-10 mins or until cooked through (this will depend on the thickness of the salmon).

While the salmon is cooking, make the sauce. Add the peanuts, cherry tomatoes and deseeded chilli (or leave the seeds in if you like it spicy) into a high speed blender and blitz until smooth, scraping down the sides a few times if necessary. Taste and season with salt and the juice of the limes. Set aside.
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Drop in the green beans for 2 mins until tender, then drain and set aside.
Finely chop most of the coriander, saving some for garnish, and stir it through the cooked rice. Add the green beans to the rice and give it a mix to roughly combine.
To serve, divide the rice and beans between plates. Top with the salmon, the sauce and the remaining spice mix. Scatter over the fresh coriander and serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Spicy Peanut and Squash Soup
description: A glorious soup. Rich with roasted squash, scotch bonnet, ginger and peanut butter, it's going to bring the heat to those chilly winter days.
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Cut your squashes in half and scoop out the seeds. Cut the flesh into large wedges 3cm thick.
Pop onto a baking tray and drizzle your squash with olive oil, salt and pepper. Bake for 30 mins until beginning to soften.
Meanwhile, wrap your bulb of garlic in foil and pop this on the lowest shelf of your oven to roast for 40 mins.
Chop your spring onions and ginger into large chunks. Scoop out the seeds of the scotch bonnet.

After the 30 mins has elapsed, remove your tray from the oven and add your spring onions, your scotch bonnet and ginger. Return to the oven for another 20 mins, by which time your veg should be nice and caramelised.
When your garlic is cool enough to handle, squeeze the flesh out of its skin by pressing a knife on top. Discard the skin.
Tip all your veg into a large saucepan and add your hot vegetable stock, roasted garlic pulp, peanut butter and 4 tbsp of your coconut yoghurt. Whizz to a smooth consistency with a stick blender.
Season your soup to taste - it might need a little salt and pepper.
Garnish with a drizzle of coconut yoghurt, chopped peanuts and coriander. Serve and enjoy!

name: Spicy Pesto Paccheri
description: A simple (and spicy) pesto pasta recipe. You can use our homemade Jalapeño and Cheddar Pesto to add an extra kick to this easy weeknight winner.
instructions: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, add the paccheri and cook according to packet instructions, then drain, reserving a cupful of the pasta water.
Return the pasta to the pan and add the pesto, stir well, adding a splash of pasta water at a time so the sauce coats the pasta. Spoon into bowls and top with grated cheddar and coriander leaves.

name: Spicy Pork & Cabbage Stir-Fry
description: Punchy, spicy pork noodles with crunchy greens, fresh herbs & loads of chilli kick. Perfect for a weeknight blast.
instructions: Grate the garlic and ginger into a small bowl. Add the sriracha, oyster sauce, soy sauces, sugar and black vinegar. Mix well to form your sauce.
Slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens. Roughly chop the cabbage. Thinly slice the cucumber and pick the coriander leaves.
Soak the noodles in freshly boiled water for 90 seconds. Drain and rinse under cold water — they should still have a serious bite.
Set a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add the sesame oil. Add the pork mince and cook for 4–5 mins until browned.
Pour in the sauce, add the spring onion whites and cabbage, and toss everything together over a high heat. Cook for another 3–4 mins until the cabbage softens and the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the noodles to the pan and toss to coat. Splash in a little water if it needs loosening.
Divide between two bowls and top with the cucumber slices, spring onion greens, coriander leaves and sesame seeds.

name: Spicy Pork & Naked Wonton Soup
description: Silky pork meatballs in a deeply savoury chicken broth, served over jasmine rice with pak choi, chilli oil and sesame seeds. All the comfort of a wonton soup, none of the folding.
instructions: Rinse the rice and add it to a small saucepan with the water. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a low heat, cover and cook for 12 mins until tender. Turn off the heat and leave to steam while you get on with everything else.

Meanwhile, finely grate the garlic and ginger, and finely slice the spring onions, keeping half back for the broth step and some greens to serve. In a bowl, mix the pork mince with half the spring onions, the garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil and white pepper until well combined. Then roll into small meatballs.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the mince mixture and cook for 6–8 mins, breaking it up with a spoon, until craggy and caramelised in places.

Pour in the chicken stock, soy sauce, white pepper and chicken powder. Bring to a simmer and cook for 3–4 mins so the broth picks up all the flavour from the pork. Add the pak choi halved and wonton wrappers (if using), and simmer for 2–3 mins until just tender.
Divide the rice between bowls. Spoon over the pork, pak choi and plenty of broth. Finish with the remaining spring onion greens, a drizzle of chilli oil and a scatter of sesame seeds.

name: Spicy Pork & Sesame Noodles
description: This batch cook is a game changer! With everything coming together in just 35 mins, you won’t have to spend your whole Sunday in the kitchen. The best part? It stays fresh in the fridge for up to 5 days, and you can cook the carbs each day to keep it feeling fresh. The beauty of this recipe is how easy it is to switch things up and keep your meals exciting all week long!
instructions: Make the tahini miso sauce: In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together all the ingredients (except the water) until smooth and creamy. Slowly add the water, a little at a time, whisking well after each addition until you’ve got a velvety sauce. Set aside.

Next up, the herb salad. Slice the cucumber in half lengthwise, then thinly cut into half moons. Pick the leaves from the coriander and mint, and finely slice the green tops of the spring onions (reserve the white parts for the pork). Toss everything together in a bowl. For an extra crunch and to help the salad last longer, pop it in some iced water while you finish cooking.

Now for the spicy pork. Add all the ingredients for the pork – excluding the mince and oil, and including your spring onion whites remaining from the salad – in a blender and blitz until smooth and fragrant.

Heat a large frying pan over high heat. Once it’s sizzling hot, add a glug of vegetable oil and ½ the pork mince. Press the mince into the pan and let it brown on one side. After a few mins, use a spatula to break it up. Once fully cooked, remove the pork and repeat with the remaining mince.
Add all the cooked pork back into the pan, then pour in half of the tahini sauce, saving the other half for later on. Stir well and cook for another 2-3 mins, making sure everything is evenly coated.
Cook the noodles according to packet instructions. Once cooked, toss the rest if the tahini sauce with the noodles. Saving a bit for drizzling at the end.
To serve, divide the noodles between plates then top with the pork and fresh herb salad. Finish with an extra drizzle of tahini miso sauce, if you like.

name: Spicy Pork & Thai Basil Fusilli
description: Pad Kra Pao meets pasta, garlicky, fiery pork mince with fragrant Thai basil tossed through fusilli in a salty, umami-packed sauce. On the table in under 30 mins.
keywords: Spicy Pork & Thai Basil Pasta recipe
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Meanwhile, mince the garlic, thinly slice the chillies and pick the basil leaves from the stems.

Heat a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a generous glug of vegetable oil. Add the chillies and garlic and fry for 1-2 mins, until aromatic. Add the pork mince, breaking it up with the back of your spoon, and fry for 7-9 mins until golden and cooked through.

Add the pasta to the boiling water and cook for 2 mins less than packet instructions. Meanwhile, add the oyster sauce, soy sauce and fish sauce to the pork and stir to combine. Cook for another minute.

Transfer the pasta straight into the pork using a slotted spoon, along with one or two ladles of pasta water. Toss to combine, adding more pasta water if needed to coat the pasta. Add most of basil leaves, leaving a handful for garnish later, and toss until wilted.
Divide the pasta between bowls. Cut the lime into wedges and serve alongside for squeezing with the remaining fresh Thai basil scattered over.

name: Spicy Pork Grain Bowl
description: This quinoa rice bowl is the perfect way to use up you Spicy Pork Ragú leftovers. Packed with crunchy cucumber pickles, kimchi and a miso-tahini drizzle all over everything, it’s fresh, balanced and big on umami.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Spicy Pork Ragú batch recipe.
Cook the quinoa according to packet instructions.
Slice the cucumber in half lengthways and scoop out the seeds with a spoon. Thinly slice, then toss with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Reheat the Spicy Pork Ragú in a small frying pan over a medium heat until bubbling and hot.
In a bowl, whisk together the tahini, miso paste, sesame oil and honey with a splash of water until smooth and spoonable. Season with a pinch of salt.

Spoon the cooked quinoa into bowls, then top with the warm ragu, a pile of kimchi, and the quick-pickled cucumber. Drizzle with the miso-tahini sauce, scatter with sesame seeds, and serve with a wedge of lime, if you fancy.

name: Spicy Pork Meatball Sando with Pickled Peanut Slaw
description: We've jazzed up this spicy meatball sandwich with an addictive pickled peanut slaw. It's the sando of your dreams, folks.
keywords: Spicy Pork Meatball Sando with Pickled Peanut Slaw
instructions: In a food processor, blend the garlic cloves and ½ the red chillies with the coriander stems, half of the sugar and all of the soy until you’ve got a rough paste. Tip in the pork mince and blend until the meat starts to form a ball in the machine. Drop in 2-3 ice cubes and blend in.
Form the mixture into golf ball-sized meatballs and set out on a tray. Chill for 5 mins.

While the balls are chilling, make the pickles and the slaw. Finely shred the carrots and radishes and thinly slice the remaining red chilli then tip into a bowl. Add a pinch of salt, the remaining sugar and 2 tbsp of rice vinegar. Toss to coat and set aside.
To make the slaw, finely slice the cabbage and spring onions, toss together in a separate bowl with the peanuts, mint and coriander leaves.
Preheat a large frying pan over a high heat and add a shot of veg oil. Add the meatballs and cook for 4-5 mins a side until caramelised, a little charred and cooked through.

Split the baguette in half lengthways and spread each side with mayo. Combine the pickles with the slaw and toss in the peanuts. Load the baguette up with pork meatballs and top with the slaw. Add the lid and cut the whole thing into four. Serve up with extra slaw on the side.

name: Spicy Pork Ragù
description: Yep, you guessed it, it's another batch recipe. And this one is a tender pork ragù that can be transformed into more delicious recipes to see you through the week. Enjoy.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C.
