Grab a large Dutch oven or saucepan and set over a medium-high heat. Working in batches, brown the pork shoulder with a little sesame oil until lovely and golden brown. We’re looking to build really good flavour here, so take your time.
Cut the red onion into chunky slices, finely slice the garlic and cut the ginger into matchsticks.

Whip the pork out of the pan and drop in the onions. Cook for 6-7 mins or until starting to wilt and sweat. Add the garlic and ginger along with the gochujang and cook for 5-6 mins. Add the pork back to the pan, add roughly chopped spring onions and cover with chicken stock. Add the soy and kimchi and bring to a boil.
Add a lid, leaving a slight gap and slide into the oven for 2.5-3 hours, or until the pork is super soft and the sauce has reduced.
Cool and divide between containers ready for the week ahead. The ragú will last for up to 4 days in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer. Eating some now? Simply serve the ragu with rice.

name: Spicy Pork Ragù Noodles
description: Here's another recipe you can make using your batch-cooked Spicy Pork Ragù. Enjoy.
instructions: Make the Spicy Pork Ragú batch recipe.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions. Rinse briefly under cold water to bring to room temperature.
Cut the cucumber into bite-size pieces and gently warm the ragú up. Combine the noodles, ragu, cucumbers and bean sprouts in a bowl and squeeze over the juice from the limes.
Divide between plates and finish with basil leaves and sesame seeds.

name: Spicy Pork Ragù Rice Bowl
description:
In Partnership with Calvet #ad

This rich pork ragù is the star of our rice bowl - a bold, flavour-packed dish that’s perfect for a date night or a midweek treat. Topped with crunchy veg and punchy kimchi, it’s spicy, vibrant, and seriously satisfying.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C.

Grab a large Dutch oven or saucepan and set over a medium-high heat. Working in batches, brown the pork shoulder with a little sesame oil until lovely and golden brown. We’re looking to build really good flavour here, so take your time.
Cut the red onion into chunky slices, finely slice the garlic and cut the ginger into matchsticks.

Whip the pork out of the pan and drop in the onions. Cook for 6-7 mins or until starting to wilt and sweat. Add the garlic and ginger along with the gochujang and cook for 5-6 mins. Add the pork back to the pan, add roughly chopped spring onions and cover with chicken stock. Add the soy and kimchi and bring to a boil.
Add a lid, leaving a slight gap and slide into the oven for 2.5-3 hours, or until the pork is super soft and the sauce has reduced.
Just before the ragú's ready, heat the rice according to the package instructions and briefly blanch the edamame beans.

Divide the rice between bowls and top with the ragu. Add edamame, kimchi and a little coriander. Add a sprinkling of sesame seeds and get stuck in with a delicious glass of Prestige Bordeaux Red by Calvet. Yum.

name: Spicy Pork Ragù Rice Bowl
description: Make this in just 15 minutes with your batch-cooked Spicy Pork Ragù.
instructions: Make the Spicy Pork Ragù batch recipe.
Pop the ragú into a saucepan and reheat over a medium heat.
Heat the rice according to the package instructions. Briefly blanch the edamame beans.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the ragu. Add edamame, kimchi and a little coriander. Add a sprinkling of sesame and get stuck in.

name: Spicy Pork Rice Bowl with Sesame Broccoli
description: Crispy, caramelised pork coated in a punchy gochujang glaze, with nutty sesame broccoli and fluffy rice.
keywords: Spicy Pork Rice Bowl with Sesame Broccoli
Spicy Pork Rice Bowl with Sesame Broccoli recipe
Spicy Pork Rice Bowl with Sesame Broccoli
instructions: Finely grate the garlic and mix it with the gochujang, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce and sugar in a small bowl. Set aside.
Place a large frying pan over a high heat with the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the pork mince and cook for 5–7 mins, breaking it up with a spoon as you go, until golden and caramelised.
Pour in the sauce and stir through. Cook for another 2–3 mins until thick, glossy and sticky.
Meanwhile, microwave the tenderstem broccoli for 2 mins until just tender. Toss with a pinch of salt, the sesame oil and the sesame seeds. Alternatively, steam or pan-fry if you prefer.
Trim and thinly slice the spring onions.
Spoon the rice into bowls. Top with the pork, sesame broccoli and a scattering of spring onions and extra sesame seeds. Finish with a raw egg yolk, if using.

name: Spicy Porky Rigatoni
description: Big porky flavours, minimal effort. This one’s all about using leftover Spicy Pork Ragù to make the ultimate spicy pasta in minutes.
instructions: Make the Spicy Pork Ragù batch recipe.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. 
Tip in the rigatoni and cook according to pack instructions until al dente.
While the pasta cooks, warm the pork ragù in a separate saucepan over a low heat. Add a splash of water if it’s looking thick.

Once the pasta’s ready, reserve a mugful of the pasta water, then drain. 
Tip the pasta into the ragù pan and toss everything together over a medium heat until glossy and piping hot. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen, if needed.
Grate the Parmesan and stir through most of it into the ragú. Then squeeze in the juice of the lime. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Divide between bowls, then finish with the remaining Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Spicy Potatoes (Batata Harra)
description: This is a take on batata harra – a Lebanese dish which you find as part of a mezze. The red pepper isn’t always included but it’s a nice addition. Jordon x
instructions: Peel and dice the potatoes into roughly one-inch cubes. Parboil in salted boiling water for about 5 mins until just starting to soften. Drain and set aside to steam.
Fill a large deep pan with 3 inches of sunflower oil and set over a high heat. Check to see when it’s hot enough by dropping in a bit of potato, it should sizzle immediately.
Add the potatoes to the pan (if your pan is small, do this in batches so you don’t crowd it). Fry for 5 or 6 mins until lightly golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with salt.
Roughly chop the peppers and mince the garlic and coriander.
Set a large frying pan over a medium heat and add a generous splash of olive oil. Fry the peppers for about 5 mins until softened.
Now add the minced garlic and coriander and fry for another minute.
Add the chilli flakes (you can add more if you like it spicier) and potatoes and mix well, fry for another minute. Season the mix well with salt and add the juice of the lemon.
Plate up and add an extra sprinkle of salt, lemon juice and coriander to taste. This is delicious by itself, as part of a spread, or as a side to a nice piece of grilled fish.

name: Spicy Prawn & Pistachio Spaghetti
description: A bit of a treat but super simple, pistachio pesto tossed through spaghetti with spicy prawns and lemon. Indulgent but easy, just what we like.
instructions: Pop the spaghetti on to cook in plenty of boiling salted water.
Meanwhile, shell the pistachios and add to a blender along with the basil, capers, juice of half the lemon and ⅔ of the olive oil. Whizz until not completely smooth.
Pour into a bowl, grate in the Parmesan and stir to combine. Add as much of the remaining olive oil as needed until you have a nice creamy consistency (you might not need it all).
Roughly chop the prawns and cook in a large frying pan over a high heat with a splash of olive oil for about 2 mins. Turn off the heat, squeeze over the remaining lemon and sprinkle over the chilli.
Once the pasta is al dente, transfer to the pan with the prawns along with a generous splash of the pasta cooking water.
Add the pesto and toss well to combine everything until you have a silky emulsified sauce.
Plate up, finish with another squeeze of lemon and an extra pinch of chilli, if you like.

name: Spicy Prawn Cocktail Salad
description: A high protein take on the 70s classic starter but with a little more heat, thanks to sriracha and cottage cheese. It's serious winner.
instructions: Zest half the lemon and squeeze in ½ the juice (cut the remaining into wedges for serving). Blitz the cottage cheese, sriracha, lemon zest and juice in a blender until smooth and creamy. Transfer to a bowl, season with salt and pepper, and fold through the prawns.
Finely slice the cornichons and finely chop the spring onions. Stir most of them through the prawn mix, saving a few for garnish.
Wash and separate the baby gem leaves. Slice the avocado and quarter the cherry tomatoes.

Mound the lettuce into serving bowls and top with the prawns, avocado and cherry tomatoes. Top with the remaining cornichons and spring onions, then dust with paprika. Serve with extra lemon wedges on the side.

name: Spicy Prawn Cocktail Salad
description: Imagine the 70s classic starter but in high-protein salad form, that’s lighter, fresher and genuinely filling. With no cooking required, it makes for an effortless meal prep lunch too!
instructions: Zest half the lemon and squeeze in ½ the juice (cut the remaining into wedges for serving). Blitz the cottage cheese, sriracha, lemon zest and juice in a blender until smooth and creamy. Transfer to a bowl, season with salt and pepper, and fold through the prawns.
Finely slice the cornichons and finely chop the spring onions. Stir most of them through the prawn mix, saving a few for garnish.
Wash and separate the baby gem leaves. Slice the avocado and quarter the cherry tomatoes.

Mound the lettuce into Tupperware containers and top with the prawns, avocado and cherry tomatoes. Top with the remaining cornichons and spring onions, then dust with paprika. Nestle in a little wedge of lemon. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Spicy Prawn Mayo Sandwich
description: WhatWillyCook shows us how to make a beautiful rendition of a prawn and mayo sandwich using Pret’s new Korean Style Ketchup.
instructions: Combine the prawns with 3/5 of the Pret Korean Style Ketchup and set aside.
Get your BBQ on and thinly slice your spring onions.
Mix the juice of a lemon with the rest of the Pret Korean Style Ketchup, mayonnaise, Worcestershire sauce, and spring onions. Season with salt and pepper.

Pop your prawns on the hot BBQ and cook for 2-3 mins until cooked through and pink. Allow your prawns to cool slightly before mixing them with the tangy sauce. If you don't have a BBQ, you can always pan-fry the prawns.

Cut your avocado in half and remove the stone. Peel off the avocado's skin and slice its flesh thinly. Shred your lettuce and mix it with a tbsp of the prawn sauce before seasoning it with salt and pepper.

Slice open your baguettes and spread on a layer of butter. Grill these baguettes buttered side down on the residual heat of the BBQ to warm them slightly. Remove your baguettes from the BBQ and layer them with your saucy prawn mixture, lettuce, avocado and finish with a scattering of sesame seeds. Chop your sandwich into two and enjoy.

name: Spicy Prawn Pasta Bake
description: A spicy twist on a classic pasta bake with a touch of Korean flair. You only need to partly cook the pasta and prawns, the oven will do the rest!
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Bring a pot of water to boil, add a generous pinch of salt.
Start by prepping the vegetables. Finely chop the broccoli, thinly slice the garlic cloves and finely chop the chives. Set aside.
Add the pasta and broccoli to the boiling water. Cook the pasta and broccoli for half the cooking time stated on the package. Drain once cooked.
Heat the frying pan on medium.

Add olive oil to the pan, along with the sliced garlic. Sauté the garlic for 30 seconds, until soft and slightly coloured. Add the gochujang, fry for a further minute until the oil turns a reddish hue.
Add the double cream and mix to combine.
Add the king prawns followed by the pasta and mascarpone, season with a pinch of salt and sugar, mix thoroughly.
Add the mixture to a high edged oven dish. Tear the mozzarella into strips and thoroughly cover the top. Grate the Parmesan on top, ensuring every bit is covered.
Put the dish into the oven for 20 mins or until golden brown on top. Sprinkle over the chives and serve.

name: Spicy Prawn Rice Bowl
description: Cooked prawns are a brilliant shortcut for quick, no-cook dinners. This vibrant rice bowl channels the flavours of a classic prawn cocktail, but with a spinach mango salad and a spicy sriracha sauce that will have you reaching for seconds.
instructions: Reheat the rice following pack instructions.
Defrost the edamame and spinach in the microwave. Once thawed, squeeze out as much moisture as you can from the spinach and set aside.

Thinly slice the spring onions. Add them to a bowl with the sesame seeds, sesame oil, soy sauce, rice vinegar, the juice of the lemon and the honey. Stir well and taste, you can tweak with more soy sauce or honey if needed.
Peel and chop the mango into 2cm chunks. Toss with the defrosted spinach, edamame and sesame dressing until everything’s well coated. Set aside.

Mix the mayonnaise, sriracha and soy sauce in a bowl, and add the prawns, tossing to coat them all. Squeeze the juice of the lemon, season with black pepper, and taste to check the heat and salt levels.
Divide the rice between bowls or containers. Top with the spicy prawns and spoon over the mango-edamame salad, sprinkle over some extra sesame seeds and get stuck in!

name: Spicy Purple Sprouting & Sausage Pasta
description: A simple but effective sausage and broccoli pasta that's so much more than the sum of its parts. Using purple sprouting broccoli gives it a real pop of colour, too.
keywords: Spicy Purple Sprouting & Sausage Pasta recipe
instructions: Slice the broccoli in half lengthways, then into roughly 2cm pieces. Finely chop the chilli and garlic and set them aside.
Place a deep-sided pan over a medium heat, add a generous drizzle of olive oil and then de-case your sausages and crumble the meat straight into the pan.
After a few minutes, once the sausages have some colour, add the garlic and chilli and fry for another 2 mins, then add the broccoli and a big pinch of salt.
Give it a good stir and pour in the wine to deglaze. Make sure you give the bottom of the pan a good scrape with your spoon.
Meanwhile, put the pasta on to boil in plenty of salted water.

Let the wine bubble away until it’s reduced by three-quarters, then turn off the heat. Once the pasta is al dente, spoon it into the broccoli pan along with half a mug of the pasta cooking water. Set over a medium heat.

Take your time here and stir the pasta as everything bubbles – you want the water to reduce a bit and the whole thing to become saucy and creamy. Squeeze in the lemon, finely chop and add the parsley and half the cheese.
Stir again, plate up and finish with more cheese and black pepper.

name: Spicy Pyjama Tomato Soup with Halloumi Croutons
description: A tomato soup using ingredients you might have in your pantry. Perfect for rainy days when you don't want to leave the house.
keywords: Spicy Pyjama Tomato Soup with Halloumi Croutons Recipe
Spicy Pyjama Tomato Soup with Halloumi Croutons
instructions: Start by making the basil oil. Bring a small pot of water to the boil over a medium heat and add in the fresh basil leaves. Cook for about 15 seconds, then transfer the basil to a bowl of ice water to chill, and wring out the excess water.
Transfer the basil to a high-speed blender with 250ml olive oil and blend on high for about 4 mins, then strain into a bowl through a cheesecloth. Let this happen slowly; do not push it down.
Transfer the basil oil to a glass jar or container and set aside. (It will last for 1-2 weeks in the fridge and can be used for frying eggs, salad dressings, as a soup drizzle, etc.)

For the soup, melt the butter in a large pot set over a medium heat. Peel and thinly slice the onion and garlic, then add to the pot and sauté on medium heat for 10-15 mins, until golden and aromatic.

Stir in the tomato purée and chilli jam, letting them caramelise for a few mins for extra flavour, then add the tinned tomatoes, breaking them apart with a spoon. Slice the red chilli and add to the pot.
Pour in the vegetable stock bit by bit, adjusting for your desired thickness, then simmer the soup gently for 5 more mins to let the flavours meld.
Stir in the cream and remove the sliced red chilli, if you don’t want it too spicy. Blend the soup until velvety smooth. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Cut the halloumi into your desired shape using cookie cutters. Heat some olive oil in a large pan then fry the halloumi pieces for a few mins on each side until golden and crispy.
To serve, ladle the warm tomato soup into bowls. Drizzle with cream and a spoonful of homemade basil oil. Top with halloumi croutons for a delicious finish!

name: Spicy Ragù Pasties
description: The handheld golden pasties are filled with a spicy southern Italian style ragu. Perfect for a picnic!
instructions: Place a large pan over a medium heat and add the pancetta with a splash of olive oil. Fry for about 5 mins until golden.
Meanwhile, dice the onion and celery. Add to the pan with the pancetta and cook for about 5 mins until softened.
Add the chilli flakes, fennel seeds, tomato purée and cook for another 2 mins.
Remove the contents of the pan into a bowl and return to a high heat. Add the pork and a big pinch of salt and cook until browned all over, breaking it up with a spoon as you go.

Pour in the white wine and let it evaporate. Lower the heat, return the onion and pancetta mix to the pan and stir well. Add the chopped tomatoes, bring up to a very gentle simmer, cover and leave to cook for an hour and 30 mins, stirring occasionally.
Once the ragù is ready, remove from the heat and allow to cool. Grab your puff pastry and get yourself either a cookie cutter, bowl, or empty round container with a diameter of about 12cm.
Preheat your oven to 200°C.
On a well-floured surface, unroll the pastry and cut into 8 discs. Add a tablespoon of the ragù to each, followed by a small chunk of mozzarella.
Crack the egg into a small bowl and whisk, then use a pastry brush to brush around the edge of the pastry. Fold the pastry in half to form a semicircle and seal the edges well with your fingers.
Take a fork and carefully press along the sealed edge to form a pattern. Now use a small knife to make a little opening on the top of the pastry to allow steam to escape as it cooks.
Brush the entire surface with a thin layer of the egg wash and transfer to a baking sheet. Cook for 20-25 mins until golden brown. Remove, allow to cool slightly and enjoy.

name: Spicy Roasted Cauliflower with Hummus and Pickles
description: Cauliflower roasted until it turns dark and golden, on a bed of creamy hummus with some zingy pickles for balance. Perfect for sharing with bread.
keywords: Spicy roasted cauliflower with hummus and pickles recipe
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.

Break the cauliflower down into florets and add to a large bowl. Drizzle generously with olive oil, a tsp of salt and the ras el hanout. Mix well then place onto a baking sheet making sure the cauliflower is well spaced out.
Roast in the oven for 30 mins, turning occasionally until golden brown and caramelised on all sides.
While the cauliflower roasts, make the pickles.

Finely slice the radishes and red onions and place into a bowl. In a saucepan warm the vinegar until it just simmers, add the sugar, dissolve and turn off the heat. Pour over the radishes and onions and allow to sit for 20 mins.
To make the hummus, drain the chickpeas and add to a food processor.
Grate in the garlic and squeeze in the lemon juice and add 1 tsp of salt. Run the processor until the chickpeas are smooth, thick and creamy.

Add the tahini and blend again until incorporated. Now, with the processor running, add cold water a tbsp at a time until you have a nice creamy consistency that’s thick enough to hold its own shape but not too claggy or thick.
Taste the hummus and, if it needs it, add salt, lemon juice and tahini to taste, then whizz again.

To assemble, spread the hummus over a large plate or platter. Arrange the cauliflower and pickles over the top, place some pickled chillies around the edge if you like, add some chopped mint and a good drizzle of olive oil.

name: Spicy Salmon Bowl with Sesame Rice & Soy Butter Spinach
description: Every part of this dish is so good. It’s a fresh take on batch cooking – prep everything in advance and keep the marinated uncooked salmon in the fridge so when dinner rolls around, you can just pop it straight in the air fryer and you’re good to go.
keywords: Spicy Salmon Bowl with Sesame Rice & Soy Butter Spinach
Spicy Salmon Bowl with Sesame Rice & Soy Butter Spinach recipe
instructions: Wash the sushi rice until the water runs clear. Add the rinsed rice to a saucepan along with the water. Set the pan over a high heat and let the water come to the boil then cover with a lid, turn the heat down to low and leave to cook for 12 mins. Then turn the heat off and leave it covered, undisturbed for another 10 mins.

For the sauce, grate the garlic into a large bowl then add the remaining sauce ingredients and whisk until incorporated. Dice the salmon fillets into large cubes (about 3 per fillet) and add them to the sauce. Toss well to cover then transfer to a container and leave to marinate in the fridge.

Now let’s make the rice seasoning. In a small bowl, whisk together the salt, sugar and vinegar and set aside. In a blender, blitz the nori into small pieces or cut into small pieces. Once the rice is cooked, stir through the seasoning liquid, nori and sesame seeds.

For the spinach, thinly slice the garlic. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan set over a medium heat then add the sliced garlic and cook for about 3 mins until softened and fragrant. Add the spinach and gently wilt before seasoning with the soy sauce and a squeeze of lemon.
When you want to eat, pop the salmon in the air fryer and pour over the sauce. Cook at 240°C for 3-4 mins. Heat the rice in the microwave until piping hot, if needed. Thinly slice the spring onions.
To serve, spoon the rice into a bowl, top with the salmon, spooning over the sauce. Finish with the buttery spinach, spring onions and some extra nori, if you like.

name: Spicy Salmon Bowl with Sesame Rice & Soy Butter Spinach
description: This meal prep dinner is anything but boring. Marinated salmon and flavour-packed sides, all prepped in advance for an easy, delicious meal straight from the fridge.
keywords: Spicy Salmon Bowl with Sesame Rice & Soy Butter Spinach
Spicy Salmon Bowl with Sesame Rice & Soy Butter Spinach recipe
instructions: Wash the sushi rice until the water runs clear. Add the rinsed rice to a saucepan along with the water. Set the pan over a high heat and let the water come to the boil then cover with a lid, turn the heat down to low and leave to cook for 12 mins. Then turn the heat off and leave it covered, undisturbed for another 10 mins.

For the sauce, grate the garlic into a large bowl then add the remaining sauce ingredients and whisk until incorporated. Dice the salmon fillets into large cubes (about 3 per fillet) and add them to the sauce. Toss well to cover then transfer to a container and leave to marinate in the fridge.

Now let’s make the rice seasoning. In a small bowl, whisk together the salt, sugar and vinegar and set aside. In a blender, blitz the nori into small pieces or cut into small pieces. Once the rice is cooked, stir through the seasoning liquid, nori and sesame seeds.

For the spinach, thinly slice the garlic. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan set over a medium heat then add the sliced garlic and cook for about 3 mins until softened and fragrant. Add the spinach and gently wilt before seasoning with the soy sauce and a squeeze of lemon.
When you want to eat, pop the salmon in the air fryer and pour over the sauce. Cook at 240°C for 3-4 mins. Heat the rice in the microwave until piping hot, if needed. Thinly slice the spring onions.

Divide the rice into your Tupperware containers, top with the salmon. Finish with the buttery spinach, spring onions and some extra nori, if you like. Box up and pop in the fridge until needed. These will keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Spicy Sausage & Cavolo Nero Orecchiette
description: When you fancy something comforting but still healthy, this pasta is the answer. Kitty's  sausage ragù with tender cavolo nero is deeply savoury with a kick of chilli heat. Delish.
keywords: Spicy Sausage Ragù with Cavolo Nero & Parmesan
Spicy Sausage Ragù with Cavolo Nero & Parmesan recipe
instructions: Finely chop the onion and thinly slice the garlic. Strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stalks and roughly chop.

Heat the olive oil in a large, wide frying pan over a medium-high heat. Squeeze the sausage meat out of the skins directly into the pan in rough pieces. Leave it undisturbed for 3–4 mins until a deep golden crust forms underneath, then break it up slightly and cook for another 2–3 mins until crisp and caramelised.

Reduce the heat to medium, add the onion and cook for 5–6 mins until soft. Add the garlic, fennel seeds and chilli flakes (add a little less if you'd like less heat) and cook for a further minute until fragrant. Stir in the tomato pureé and cook for another minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2–3 mins, scraping up any sticky bits from the bottom of the pan, until reduced. Add the chicken stock and bring to a simmer.

Add the cavolo nero, stir to coat, then reduce the heat and cook gently for 15–20 mins until the greens are fully softened and slightly collapsed into the sauce. Add a splash of water if needed to keep it loose.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in a large pan of well-salted boiling water for 7 mins, until just shy of al dente . Reserve a generous mug of pasta cooking water before draining.

Add the drained pasta to the ragù along with a good splash of the reserved cooking water. Toss vigorously over a medium heat for 1–2 mins until glossy and emulsified. Finely grate in the Parmesan and toss again, adding more pasta water as needed to loosen. Squeeze over the lemon juice, taste and adjust the seasoning.
To serve, divide between warm bowls. Finish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and plenty of finely grated Parmesan.

name: Spicy Sausage & Gochujang Noodles with Crispy Spring Onions
description: Quick, spicy noodles tossed in your Sausage Gochujang Ragù batch with some broc and crispy spring onions on top. All done in under 20 mins.
keywords: Gochujang Noodles with Crispy Spring Onions & Tenderstem
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sausage Gochujang Ragú batch recipe.
Slice the spring onions into fine matchsticks. Cut the broccoli in half.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the broccoli and egg noodles and cook for 4–5 mins until the noodles are tender and the broccoli is bright green and tender. Reserve a ladle of cooking water, then drain.

Heat a generous drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over a low-medium heat. Add the spring onions and fry gently for 5–7 mins until golden and crispy. Transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper and set aside.

Return the drained noodles and broccoli to the saucepan. Add the gochujang sausage ragù and set over a low heat. Toss everything together, adding splashes of the reserved noodle water until the sauce is glossy and coats the noodles.
Dish up into bowls and finish with a heap of crispy spring onions on top.

name: Spicy Sausage Arrabbiata Pasta
description: A beautiful spicy midweek meal. This arrabbiata recipe is to die for. It's hot, filling, and the perfect thing to cheer you up after a hard day of work.
instructions: Squeeze out the sausagemeat from the sausages and transfer to a bowl. Finely chop the garlic, then halve the chillies, remove the seeds and finely chop. Finely chop the basil stalks. Crush the tomatoes with your hands.
Heat a dash of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the sausagemeat and mash with a spoon until crumbly. Cook until golden then remove from the pan.

Add the garlic, chilli and basil stalks to the pan, then cook for 1-2 mins. Tip in the tomatoes, bring to a simmer and cook for 5 mins. Return the sausagemeat to the pan, mix well, then cook for 5 mins. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta following pack instructions. Drain, saving some of the cooking water.
Tip the pasta into the ragù with a slosh of cooking water, then mix well. Serve with Parm and the basil leaves.

name: Spicy Sausage Bean Bake
description: All the best ingredients unite in one dish - baked beans, sausage, chorizo, and crunchy ciabatta croutons. What more could you want? Treat yourself MOB.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Break up your chorizo ring into small chunks and remove your sausage meat from its case, then roll into balls (a bit smaller than a ping-pong ball).
Heat a glug of oil in a pan, whack in your chorizo and sausage balls then fry until browned.
Chop your red pepper, onion, and garlic and add to the pan along with your rosemary.
Next, toss in your beans and give it a good stir.
Dissolve your chicken stock in 200ml boiling water and pour into the pan.
Finely chop your parsley and add to the dish (saving some for garnish) along with a good seasoning of salt and pepper. Stir it together and leave to bubble down for a few minutes.
Then tear up some ciabatta croutons and place them randomly on top of your bake.
Drizzle over your olive oil, season with salt and pepper then pop into the oven for 25 minutes to get a crispy finish.
Take your yoghurt and dollop it over the top then scatter with any leftover chopped up parsley and dig in!

name: Spicy Sausage Penne Bake
description: This spicy pasta bake is a crowd pleaser. A fiery, tomato-ey sausage sauce is a perfect match for Napolina Wholewheat Penne.
instructions: Heat a large pan over a medium heat with a splash of Napolina Olive Oil. Squeeze your sausages out of their skins and into the pan, breaking up with the back of your spoon and frying until you have a crisp and golden mixture.
Add your onion to the pan and turn down the heat. Sauté for 10 minutes until they are totally soft. Tip in your garlic, chilli flakes and fennel seeds and cook out for 2 minutes.

Add your white wine to the pan to deglaze, scraping the bottom so you pick up all the caramelised bits. Once it has evaporated, add your chicken stock and chopped tomatoes. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 mins until you have a rich sauce. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat your grill to high. Cook your Napolina Wholewheat Penne for 5 minutes, then save a mugful of pasta water and drain the rest. Add to your pan of sauce, then pour in your pasta water and stir it until it comes together in a silky sauce that clings to your pasta.
Pour your pasta into a baking dish, then tear up your mozzarella and sprinkle on top. Pop your dish under the grill for 10 minutes.
Tear up your basil and sprinkle it on top, then serve.

name: Spicy Sausage Shakshuka
description: Here's a breakfast with a bit of substance, something to get you going in the morning. Sausages are broken up and cooked with spicy harissa and tomatoes, poach a few eggs straight in the sauce and eat with some crusty bread. Beautiful.
instructions: Place a large pan over a high heat and crumble in your sausages. Brown off for a few mins, breaking them up with a spoon as you go.
Slice the onion, add to the pan and reduce the heat to medium. Cook for about 5 mins until the onion has softened.
Drain and slice the peppers and add to the pan along with the cumin and harissa and cook for another 3 or 4 mins.
Add the tomatoes and a tsp of salt, stir and allow to simmer for about 10 mins until thickened.
Reduce the heat to low, make 4 little wells in the sauce and crack 2 eggs in each and season with a pinch of salt.
Cover the pan and cook for another 5 mins or until the eggs are cooked (keep an eye on the yolks to make sure they stay runny).
Remove from the heat, squeeze over the juice of the lemon, sprinkle with fresh parsley and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve hot with crusty bread for dipping.

name: Spicy Sausage Tagine Traybake
description: Any spicy sausage will work in this traybake - Merguez gives a leaner, spicier result and chorizo brings more fat and richness. Either way it will have all the comfort of a Tagine but made in no time.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a large baking tray with baking paper. Cut the red onion into quarters and the pepper into bite-sized chunks. Halve the dried apricots and lightly crush the garlic cloves.

Tip the onion, pepper, cherry tomatoes, olives, apricots and garlic onto the tray. Grate over the ginger, add the harissa and ras el hanout, drizzle over a glug of olive oil and season well with salt. Toss everything together until coated.
Nestle the sausages in among the veg and pour over the water. Roast for 25 mins, until the tomatoes have burst and the sausages are browned and cooked through.
While the tray bake is in the oven, cook the couscous according to packet instructions.
Once the couscous is ready, spoon into bowls and pile the sausages and tray veg on top. Add a generous dollop of yoghurt alongside and serve straight away.

name: Spicy Scampi Rice Bowl
description: Shop bought scampi, zingy veg and coconut rice come together in this fiery rice bowl that’s all about max flavour, zero fuss.
instructions: Cook the scampi following the pack instructions until super golden and crunchy.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the red onion and chuck it into a bowl with a pinch of salt and the juice of half a lime. Scrunch with clean hands for a minute until it turns bright pink. Set aside.

Tip the kale into a mixing bowl. Use the juice of the other half of the lime, add a pinch of salt and massage for a minute until softened. Use a mandolin to finely shave in the brussels sprouts, then toss everything together.
Cut carrots into matchsticks (or grate if easier)
In a small bowl, mix the sriracha, mayo and the juice of half a lime. Give it a taste and adjust the heat if needed.
Heat the coconut rice following the pack instructions and divide between two bowls.
Arrange the scampi, pickled onions, sprout-kale slaw and carrot on top of the rice in little piles. Drizzle over the sriracha mayo and finish with a scattering of coriander.

name: Spicy Seafood Stew
description: This one is a treat for a special occasion. A mediterranean-style spicy seafood stew with flavours from North Africa and Spain, served with a quick aioli.
instructions: Heat a large saucepan over a medium low heat and add in 3 tbsp of olive oil. Finely dice the onion and add it to the pan along with the anchovies, tomato purée and harissa. Cook for 5 mins until the onion has softened.
Mince the garlic and add along with the cumin and olives. Cook for another 2 mins.
Pour in the Cirio Chopped Tomatoes, add a pinch of salt and bring to a simmer for 15 mins.
While the sauce cooks, make the easy aioli. Add the mayonnaise to a small bowl. Grate in the garlic and add the zest and juice of half your lemon. Mix well and set aside.
Pour in the fish stock and return to a simmer. Cut the bass into roughly 2 cm chunks. Add to the stew along with the clams and prawns and simmer for 5 mins until cooked through.
Turn off the heat, stir in the vinegar and sprinkle over the coriander. Seve in a bowl with a dollop of the aioli and a wedge of lemon to squeeze over. Great with some crusty bread!

name: Spicy Shrimp Handrolls
description: Delicious, economical, and indulgent. It's time to experience the joy of making hand rolls from the comfort of your own kitchen.
instructions: Cook the rice following pack instructions. Remove the shells and veins from the prawns. Roughly chop the green onions.
Heat a medium pot of water over a medium heat. Add the shrimp and boil them for 2-3 mins until opaque and fully cooked. Drain and pat dry with kitchen paper.
Roughly chop the shrimp and mix with the mayonnaise, chilli oil and green onions in a bowl.
Cut the nori sheets in half lengthwise and lay them out on a clean flat surface.
Add a tbsp of cooked rice to one half of each nori and press down with a fork. Generously top with the shrimp mixture and roll into a cone shape.
Serve with the remaining shrimp and top with furikake, if you like.

name: Spicy Smacked Cucumber & Peanut Butter On Toast
description: A speedy lunch that uses a lot of store cupboard bits and bobs to pack loads of flavour! It's nice and spicy.
keywords: Spicy Smacked Cucumber & Peanut Butter On Toast
instructions: Get your cucumber and cut it into irregular pieces, around 2cm big. Then, using the back of your knife smoosh them all down a bit.
Add your cucumber to a bowl with grated garlic, caster sugar, black vinegar and soy sauce, then give it a good mix. Finely slice the spring onion and get your bread into the toaster.

When your bread is nice and golden, spread it with a load of peanut butter. The amount is entirely up to you here! Top with the cucumbers, drizzle with crispy chilli oil, and top with the sesame and spring onion.

name: Spicy Smoked Cheddar Tuna Melts
description: We’ve perfected the classic using smoked Cheddar and hot sauce. Make sure you press your toasties down in the pan for ultimate ooziness.
instructions:
Thinly slice the spring onions. Open the tins of tuna and drain off
the water. Put the drained tuna meat and sliced spring onions in
a bowl and add as much mayonnaise and hot sauce as you like.
Season to taste with salt and black pepper and stir together.
Assembly time. Put four slices of sourdough bread onto a
chopping board. Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise over each
slice, then turn them mayo-side-down onto the board. Spoon the
spicy tuna mayo evenly over each piece of bread, then grate the
smoked Cheddar directly over the top of each one.
Top with the remaining bread slices and spread a thin layer of
mayo on the top-facing side of each. (Having mayo on the outside
of the bread is the answer to a super crisp toastie!)
Get two large frying pans, preferably non-stick, over a high heat.
Fry the toasties for 1 minute on each side until golden, squashing
them down with a fish slice or spatula as they cook for ultimate
crispiness. Transfer to plates and serve.

name: Spicy Soy & Sesame Noodles
description: A meat-free version of one of our most popular recipes. Creamy sesame noodles with a spicy soy mince on top and a fresh herby salad, what's not to like?
instructions: Soak the soy mince in boiling water for 5 mins, then drain well. In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the tahini, white miso, the rice vinegar, the soy sauce and the water until smooth and creamy. This is your noodle sauce.

Next up, the herb salad. Finely slice the courgette. Pick the leaves from the coriander and finely slice the green tops of the spring onions, reserving the white parts for the soy mince. Toss everything together in a bowl. Any leftover courgette is great roasted, or thinly sliced into salads.

Now for the spicy mince. Peel the garlic and add it to a blender with the gochujang, the soy sauce, the chilli flakes, the rice vinegar, the caster sugar and the spring onion whites, then blitz smooth.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat. Once it's sizzling hot, add the olive oil and the drained soy mince and cook for a couple of minutes, then pour in the blended sauce. Stir well and cook for another 2-3 mins, making sure everything is evenly coated.
Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions, then drain and toss with the tahini sauce.
To serve, divide the noodles between plates, then top with the spicy mince and the fresh herb salad.

name: Spicy Soy Sausage & Broccoli Rice
description: This Thai-inspired rice dish has got a nice mix of heat, sweet, and acid. A really top dinner.
keywords: Spicy Soy Sausage & Broccoli Rice recipe
instructions: Finely grate the garlic cloves into a bowl, add the fish sauce, sugar, soy and the juice of half of your limes. Mix together and set aside. Cut the other limes in half ready for squeezing later.

Remove the skins of your sausages and chuck into a hot pan with a splash of olive oil. Use a spatula or wooden spoon to smash the sausage meat into small pieces as it cooks. Cook for 9-10 mins or until it’s starting to get super crispy.

Finely slice the broccoli and chuck into the pan with the sausages, toss through the porky, fatty business and cook for 4-5 mins until just tender. Thinly slice your red onions and chillies and chuck them in, too.
Cook for a minute or two, then add the sauce and toss to coat. Cut the chives into 4-5cm batons and stir through the mince along with your mint.
Heat the rice according to the package instructions. Divide the rice between bowls, top with the sausage mixture and serve each with a lime half.

name: Spicy Sriracha Salmon
description: A bold, punchy salmon dish with a fiery sriracha kick, balanced by the umami depth of miso and a touch of honey. Quick, easy, and perfect for an air fryer.
instructions: First, grate your garlic cloves. Then, in a large bowl, whisk together all the sauce ingredients. Cut the salmon into large cubes (about 3 per fillet) and finely slice the spring onions.
Add the salmon cubes to the bowl and toss well to coat. Transfer to a container and leave to marinate in the fridge for at least 10 mins.
Preheat your air fryer to 240°C.
Add the marinated salmon to the air fryer basket and cook for 3-4 mins, until caramelised and cooked through.
Serve with a sprinkle of sesame seeds, sliced spring onions, and lemon wedges.

name: Spicy Teriyaki Tuna Poke
description: Spicy sriracha-teriyaki tuna piled onto sticky rice with cool avocado, a dollop of cream cheese and a zingy lime dressing. Fresh, protein-packed and great for lunch.
ingredients: 4x 145g Can Tinned Tuna in Olive Oil
instructions: Drain the tuna and tip into a bowl with the sriracha, half the sesame oil, the teriyaki sauce and the sesame seeds. Season with salt and black pepper and mix well.
Cook the rice pouches according to the pack instructions. Meanwhile, cut the broccoli into florets and finely slice the spring onions. Peel and slice the avocados.

Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Add the broccoli and cook for 3 mins. Drain and cool under cold running water, then pat dry and toss with the remaining sesame oil and a squeeze of lime juice. Season with salt.
Boil the eggs for 7-8 mins, until just set. Drain, cool under cold water, then peel and halve.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with a scoop of cream cheese, the spicy tuna, avocado, broccoli, spring onions and halved eggs. Scatter with extra sesame seeds, if you like, and serve.

name: Spicy Tofu & Pickled Rice Noodle Salad
description: Cold noodle salads are the perfect healthy midweek meal when it's scorching. This one's packed with crispy fennel tofu, quick-pickled veg and a sweet and sour sesame dressing. Plus it's great for making ahead for a speedy grab and go lunch.
keywords: Crumbled Tofu & Pickled Rice Noodle Salad
Crumbled Tofu & Pickled Rice Noodle Salad recipe
instructions: Set a large saucepan of water to boil. Drain and press the tofu, then finely crumble it using your hands or a food processor.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the crumbled tofu and fennel seeds and stir-fry for 4-5 mins, until the tofu is golden and some bits turn crispy. Add the chilli flakes, season with salt and the sugar, then stir to combine and turn off the heat.

Mix the rice vinegar, sugar, salt and water together in a large bowl. Halve the cucumber lengthways, remove the watery core and cut into strips, then add to the pickling liquid. Drop the bean sprouts into the boiling water and cook for 1 min, then transfer to a bowl of cold water, keeping the water boiling for the noodles. Add the bean sprouts to the pickling liquid along with the coriander. Mix to combine.
Make the dressing. Add the tahini and rice vinegar to a bowl and mix until combined, then add the soy sauce and sugar and mix again. Set aside.
Add the rice noodles to the boiling water and cook for 2-3 mins, until soft. Drain and rinse under cold water.

To serve straight away, add everything to a large bowl, pour over the dressing and toss to combine. To prep for later, add a quarter of the dressing to the bottom of each jar, then layer in a quarter each of the noodles, edamame, pickled vegetables and tofu. Pop the lids on and keep in the fridge. When ready to eat, give everything a good mix and serve cold or at room temperature.

name: Spicy Tomato & Ginger Chicken Noodle Salad
description: Fresh cherry tomato and ginger sauce tossed with soba noodles, shredded chicken, crunchy peanuts and coriander. Layer it into a jar for a ready-to-grab lunch from the fridge.
keywords: Spicy Tomato & Ginger Chicken Noodles Salad
Spicy Tomato & Ginger Chicken Noodles Salad recipe
instructions: Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a drizzle of the vegetable oil. Add the chicken thighs in a single layer, season with salt and cook for 5 mins until golden brown. Flip and cook for a further 3 mins, then pour in the water. Cover with a lid and cook for 20 mins, until the chicken is tender and about two-thirds of the liquid has evaporated. Turn off the heat and leave to cool slightly. Shred the chicken using two forks, then return to the pan and toss through the remaining cooking liquid. Season with salt and set aside.

Quarter the cherry tomatoes, add to a bowl and season with salt, squeezing them gently to release their juices. Finely mince the garlic and ginger and add to the bowl along with the chilli oil, soy sauce, red wine vinegar and honey. Mix to combine.
Cook the soba noodles according to the packet instructions, then rinse under cold water and drain. Roughly chop the peanuts and coriander, and slice the spring onions.

Spoon the tomato sauce into the bottom of each mason jar. Layer in the noodles, then the chicken, coriander, spring onions and peanuts. Pop the lids on and transfer to the fridge. When ready to eat, give everything a good mix and serve cold or at room temperature.

name: Spicy Tomato & Pepper Chickpeas on Toast
description: Creamy, saucy chickpeas cooked in our Spicy Tomato & Pepper Sauce, piled onto crunchy sourdough with melty feta and pesto. Job done.
keywords: Spicy Tomato & Pepper Chickpeas on Toast
Spicy Tomato & Pepper Chickpeas on Toast recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the The Spicy Tomato & Pepper Sauce.

Add the drained chickpeas and Spicy Tomato & Pepper Sauce to a small saucepan set over a medium heat. Let it bubble away gently for 4-5 mins until warmed through. Taste and season with salt and black pepper, if needed.
Toast the sourdough, then pop onto plates. Spoon the chickpeas over the toast, then crumble over the feta. Finish with a generous drizzle of basil pesto and a little olive oil, if you like.

name: Spicy Tomato & Pepper Pasta
description: Punchy, peppery and done in 20. Our Spicy Tomato & Pepper Sauce is the star of this recipe, making for a delicious bowl of pasta with barely any effort.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Spicy Tomato & Pepper Sauce.
Fill a large saucepan with salted water and bring to the boil. Once boiling, drop in the pasta and cook following pack instructions. Just before draining, scoop out 100ml of the pasta water.

Return the cooked pasta to the pan and set over a medium-high heat. Stir through the Spicy Tomato & Pepper Sauce until hot, loosening with a splash of pasta water if needed. Taste and season, if needed.
Spoon into bowls and finish with a generous grating of Parmesan. Dig in.

name: Spicy Tomato & Pepper Sauce
description: Make a big batch of this spicy tomato sauce and thank yourself later. It's perfect for spooning over eggs, stirring through pasta, or whatever you fancy.
instructions: Add the drained roasted peppers and chopped tomatoes to a blender, then blitz until mostly smooth.
Set a saucepan over a medium-low heat and add the olive oil. Gently cook the garlic for about 2 mins until fragrant but not coloured. Add the chilli flakes and cook for 30 seconds more.
Pour in the pepper and tomato mixture, add a big pinch of salt, and bring to a simmer. Let it bubble away for 15–20 mins until thickened to your liking. Taste and season with more salt, if needed.
Transfer the sauce to a clean, heatproof jar and seal tightly. Let it cool completely before storing.
If sealed properly, the sauce will keep at room temperature for up to 1 month. If not sealed, store in the fridge and use within 2 weeks.

name: Spicy Tomato Garlic Butter Pasta
description: The fabulous Gnoch Gnoch has made a very more-ish pasta here. Crispy garlic and oyster sauce are the magical extras to this lovely fusion dish.
instructions: Finely slice your garlic and grate your ginger. Finely slice your spring onions.
Finely chop your parsley. Grate your parmesan.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Fry your garlic for a couple of mins until crispy. Drain on a plate lined with kitchen towel, and set aside until later.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil, then season generously with salt. Add your bucatini and cook until al dente.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Add your butter and ginger, then cook for 2 mins until fragrant.
Get your tomato purée in there and cook for 2 mins until it has darkened slightly. Pour in your soy sauce, oyster sauce and chilli flakes, then give it a good mix.
Once your bucatini is cooked, add it to the pan along with a splash of pasta water. Give the whole mixture a really good mix.
Add your spring onions, parsley and parmesan, then season to taste with salt.
Tong your pasta into bowls, then top with a little more parmesan and your crispy garlic chips. Serve and enjoy!

name: Spicy Tuna & Crispy Rice
description: Use the best quality tuna you can get your hands on for this one. Golden, crackling sushi rice topped with silky soy and sesame-dressed tuna, creamy avocado and a punchy sriracha mayo. Ready in 20 mins.
instructions: Dice the butter and set aside. Thinly slice the spring onions and chop the cucumber into 1-2cm chunks.

Drizzle a little olive oil into a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the cooked sushi rice in one even layer. Scatter the diced butter over the top, cover and cook undisturbed for 7-10 mins, until deeply golden and crispy on the bottom.

Meanwhile, chop the tuna into 1-2cm chunks. Add the tuna, cucumber and spring onions to a bowl, then stir through the soy sauce, sesame oil and sesame seeds. Taste and season with a little salt, or a splash more soy sauce if needed.
Mix together the mayonnaise, sriracha and the juice of the lemon in a small bowl.
Divide the crispy rice between plates. Top with the spicy tuna, sliced avocado and a dollop of spicy mayo.

name: Spicy Tuna Bites
description: A quick and easy snack that will fill you right up. These protein-packed bad boys are a gym bro's dream come true.
instructions: Tip the drained tuna into a bowl and add the sriracha, mayo and yoghurt with the zest of the lemon and half its juice. Finely chop the chives and red onion and add to the bowl along with the chickpeas.
Mix everything together and season with salt. Add more hot sauce if you like it spicy.
Thinly slice the cucumber and lay over the rye bread. Top with a scoop of your tuna mixture and sprinkle with black sesame. Cut the lemon into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Spicy Tuna Caesar High Protein Smash
description: Trust us, tuna in this caesar base really works. Cottage cheese and Greek yoghurt make the base, jalapeños bring the heat, and it all piles beautifully onto toasted sourdough or whacked into a crisp lettuce wrap.
instructions: Drain your tuna, then add to a large bowl along with the cottage cheese and yoghurt.

Finely chop the anchovy fillets and jalapeños and halve the cherry tomatoes. Grate the garlic and finely grate the Parmesan. Add to the bowl along with the Dijon, Worcestershire sauce, juice of the lemon and tear in the basil leaves. If you're using it, finely dice a little red onion and add that in too.
Mix everything together until creamy but still chunky. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper and stir until thick and scoopable.
Toast the sourdough, then pile the mixture generously on top and serve. Any leftovers will keep in the fridge for up to three days.

name: Spicy Tuna Caesar Lettuce Wraps
description: Transform our Spicy Tuna Caesar High Protein Smash into delicious on-the go lunch for a healthier alternative to a sandwich we've rolled in all up in a crisp lettuce wrap.
instructions: Drain your tuna, then add to a large bowl along with the cottage cheese and yoghurt.

Finely chop the anchovy fillets and jalapeños and halve the cherry tomatoes. Grate the garlic and finely grate the Parmesan. Add to the bowl along with the Dijon, Worcestershire sauce, juice of the lemon and tear in the basil leaves. If you're using it, finely dice a little red onion and add that in too.
Mix everything together until creamy but still chunky. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper and stir until thick and scoopable.

Now you can assemble. Lay a large rectangle of parchment paper on your work surface. Arrange the lettuce leaves in two slightly overlapping rows of three, creating one large lettuce sheet. Dollop the smash in the middle and then roll from the short end up and over, like a burrito, then wrap tightly in the parchment, folding in the ends as you go. Slice in half and serve.

name: Spicy Tuna Larb
description: A humble tin of tuna has so much potential. We've used it to make a quick, store-cupboard larb. Lots of spice and acid. Perfect eaten with the leftover rice.
instructions: In a small pan on high heat, add 2 tbsp of rice and toast until medium golden, tossing for 3-4 mins or until it smells like popcorn. Make sure to watch the pan because it can burn quickly. Set aside in a mortar and pestle or blender/spice grinder. Grind or blitz into a fine powder and set aside.

Finely slice your red onion, chilli, coriander stems, and then mince or grate your garlic. Add all of those ingredients to a medium-sized bowl. Add the zest of 2 whole limes along with all the lime juice, fish sauce, honey, pinch of salt and pepper and toss well. Drain the majority of the olive oil from the tin of tuna and gently toss into the bowl, trying not to break up the chunks into mush.
Prepare a platter of iceberg cups, sliced cucumbers, fresh coriander and leftover rice, if you've got any.
Cover the tuna larb in the toasted rice powder and lightly toss. Serve in lettuce cups and tuck in.

name: Spicy Tuna Pickle Sandwiches
description: A simple tuna sandwich jazzed up with pickles, olives, and harissa. It's spicy and briny and delicious.
instructions: Peel and dice the potatoes into 2cm cubes. Bring a pan of very salty water to the boil, add the eggs and potatoes and cook for 6 mins. Drain and rinse under cold water, then peel and slice the eggs into quarters.
Meanwhile, halve the brioche buns and melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium heat. Toast the brioche in the pan for a couple of minutes each side until golden. Roughly chop the parsley.
Spread the buns with harissa, load up with sliced boiled eggs, potatoes, tuna, olives, parsley, and pickles and squeeze over the lemon. Drizzle with olive oil and eat immediately.

name: Spicy Tuna Rice Bowl
description: This spicy tuna rice bowl with sesame, soy and sriracha comes together in no time. It’s perfect for packed lunches.
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions.

Finely slice the spring onions and set aside. Peel and slice the avocado and set aside. Cut the nori into strips, if using and set aside. Finely slice the cucumber and add it to a bowl with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt. Scrunch with your hands until slightly softened.
In a bowl, mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise, sriracha, soy sauce, sesame oil and spring onions. Taste and adjust seasoning with more soy sauce or sriracha if needed.
Divide the rice between containers. Top with a big scoop of spicy tuna, pickled cucumber, avocado and nori, if using. Sprinkle with togarashi and drizzle with more sriracha, if you like.
Pop in the fridge for an easy, flavour-packed meal later. It will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Spicy Tunacado Baked Potato
description: It’s a cult sandwich classic, but we’ve turned it into the perfect midweek dinner by loading the spicy tuna onto a baked and nutritious sweet potato.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Get the potatoes onto a baking tray and rub with olive oil, salt and pepper. Roast for 45 mins to 1 hour until a knife can go through easily and the skin is crisp.

Finely chop the dill and add to a bowl with the pickled jalapeños, drained tuna, mayo, greek yoghurt, capers and a splash of pickle juice. Mix well and season with salt, pepper and hot sauce. Add more if you want it extra spicy!
Dice the avocado. Cut the potatoes open and roughly mash, spooning a bit of the pesto in. Top with the spicy tuna and avocado before garnishing with the sprouts.

name: Spicy Turkey Ragù
description: A lean, mean ragù. This high-protein recipe is sweet, spicy, and going to be your new favourite weeknight dinner. A lovely way to use turkey mince.
instructions: Start by dicing the garlic and ginger.

Heat a large wok or frying pan over a high heat and add a good splash of veg oil. Add the turkey mince and brown off, working in batches if necessary. Once very browned and crispy, remove from the pan and set aside.

Add another splash of oil and tip in the onion, garlic and ginger. Cook for 5 mins until caramelised. Add the turkey back to the pan and add the gochujang, soy and sugar. Cook together for another 4-5 mins.
Add the water and bring to a simmer, let cook away for 20-25 mins. Halfway through, roughly chop the cavolo nero and add to the ragù.
Cook the egg noodles according to the instructions on the pack. Roughly chop the peanuts and finely slice the spring onions.
Toss the noodles through the turkey ragù and divide between warm bowls. Top with a handful of the peanuts, basil, and spring onions.

name: Spicy Vegan 'Nduja Rigatoni
description: "Sugo" is the Italian word for sauce and this spicy pasta recipe includes a sugo made from vegan 'nduja. It's rich and spicy perfection.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and season with salt. Heat your biggest frying pan over a medium high heat.

Thinly slice the onions, garlic and chilli. Meanwhile, halve the cherry tomatoes using a couple of small plates. Add a handful of tomatoes to the bottom plate and place the second, facedown over the tomatoes. Run a bread knife through the middle, halving all the tomatoes at once.
Drop your rigatoni into the pan of boiling water and cook according to the pack instructions.
Add the garlic, onion and chillies to the pan and cook for 2-3 mins over a high heat with a glug of oil. Scoop in the ‘nduja and cook for 1-2 mins until melted.
Add the tomatoes and stir them through, keep the heat high. Season with salt and add a ladle of water from the pasta pot. Bring to a boil and cook for 4-5 mins while the pasta finishes cooking.
Transfer the pasta to the sauce and grate in the vegetarian parmesan. Stir through the half of the basil leaves and vinegar to finish. Garnish with remaining basil.

name: Spicy Watermelon Margarita
description: A sweet and spicy watermelon margarita. This is your drink of the summer. It's the perfect cocktail for a BBQ and pairs great with a tangy watermelon and feta salad.
instructions: Cut up your watermelon and weigh out the correct amount. Set aside two slices as garnish and dust in Tajín.
Juice your limes and slice up the jalapeño.
Rub a bit of lime on your glass rim and then coat in Tajín.
In your cocktail shaker add the desired amount of jalapeño slices (we go for two or three) and agave and muddle them, then your watermelon and do the same until it’s a thick pulp.
Add in your lime juice, tequila and some ice.
Shake for 10 seconds.
Pour into your glass and garnish with the Tajín watermelon slices. Enjoy.

name: Spicy ’Nduja Sprouts
description: You've never had sprouts as good as this. These 'nduja sprouts are a serious upgrade on your bog standard boiled Brussels.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Grab a large bowl and fill with cold water and some ice cubes. Tip the sprouts into the boiling water and cook for 3-4 mins, then use a slotted spoon to move the sprouts into the ice water. Once cool, drain and use kitchen paper to make sure they’re dry, then slice in half.
Peel and finely slice the garlic and finely chop the parsley. Roughly chop the smoked almonds.
Add 1 tbsp olive oil to a frying pan set over a medium heat, then add the ’nduja and fry for 1 min. Add the garlic and sizzle for 1 min until just starting to crisp. Tip into a bowl and wipe the pan.

Add 1 tbsp olive oil to the same pan set over a medium heat. Add the sprouts, cut-side down, and leave to sit for 5 mins until the cut side of the sprouts are charred. Squeeze in the lemon juice, add a big pinch of salt and pepper and toss well. Add most of the parsley, then remove the pan from the heat and return the ’nduja and garlic to the pan.
Tip everything into a serving bowl, top with the remaining parsley and smoked almonds, then serve.

name: Spicy, Herby Fish with Curried Orzo
description: Warming curry-spiced orzo, juicy grilled cod, and heaps of herbs. Fresh, filling, and ready in a flash.
keywords: spicy herby fish with curried orzo
instructions: Add the garam masala to a bowl with half the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Drop in the cod fillets and stir to coat evenly. Set aside.
Thinly slice the garlic, chilli and onion. Pick the basil leaves. Heat the grill to medium.
Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan with high sides over a medium heat. Once hot, add the garlic, chilli and half the onion. Cook for 4–5 mins until softened.

Tip in the orzo and curry powder. Season with salt. Stir for a minute until fragrant, then pour in the stock and water. Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is al dente (check your pack for timings).

Place the cod onto a foil-lined tray and slide under the grill for 5–10 mins, until cooked through and lightly charred. If it’s colouring too quickly, move it down a shelf or turn the grill down slightly.
Stir the coconut milk through, until creamy. Season to taste with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lime juice. Add a splash of water into the orzo to loosen it, if needed.
Spoon the curried orzo into bowls and top with the grilled cod. Finish with a scattering of basil leaves, the remaining onion and chilli.

name: Spinach & Mortadella Lasagne
description: Although regional variations exist across Italy, Bologna is considered the birthplace of lasagne. This is not an authentic Bolognese lasagne! But with the spinach in both the pasta and the filling, plus the layers of mortadella, it is a nod in that direction.
instructions: First, make the pasta. Wash the spinach, then wilt a fifth of the spinach in a dry, non-stick pan. Squeeze all the liquid out of it, leaving you with a small amount of spinach. Put this in a food processor along with the whole eggs and yolk, then blitz to a thin, lightly speckled green purèe.

Tip the flour onto a clean surface in the shape of a mound, then make a crater in the middle of it. Pour the green purèe into the middle, then use a fork to stir and gradually draw flour into the liquid. After a while, use the fork or a bench scraper to turn and chop the flour and eggs into a scraggy mix. Then use your hands to bring the mixture into a ball of dough.

Knead the dough, using the base of your palms to stretch and push the dough, into a smooth, silky but elastic ball. It will take 8-10 mins, but it is therapeutic! Wrap or put in a sealable bag and leave to rest for 90 mins or more (overnight in the fridge is fine).

When ready to roll, cut the dough in half, flatten a little with your palms, then run through a pasta machine, beginning with the widest setting and ending with the pasta around 1mm thick (probably 2-3 settings from the thinnest). Dust with semolina to avoid it sticking and cut to lengths ½-1cm shorter than a 2.5L ovenproof lasagne dish (the pasta sheets will increase in size a little when blanched).

When ready to assemble, par-boil the pasta sheets. Do this in 2-3 batches (to save space and stress), the second two while you are building the lasagne. Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and spread 2-3 tea towels over your work surface. Cook one-third of the pasta sheets for 1 min, until they rise to the top of the water. Pick them out with tongs or a slotted spoon and lay over the tea towels. Repeat as required.

Make the white sauce. Melt the butter in a medium-sized saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 30-60 seconds with a spatula until the combination (a ‘roux’) is slack, light golden in colour and smells only slightly nutty. Add a splash of milk and stir with a spatula until the liquid is completely incorporated. Repeat three or four times, then begin to increase the amount of milk you’re adding and use a whisk instead of a spatula, each time ensuring there are no lumps before adding more milk. Once all the milk is in, add the nutmeg, white pepper, and half the Parmesan, then gently cook over a low heat for 10 mins, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and generously coats the back of a spoon.

Finely slice your garlic. Wilt the remaining spinach in a large pan, turning and stirring occasionally until reduced in volume, dark and glistening. Drain off any liquid (no need to squeeze this time), return to the heat, add the garlic, season generously with salt, the nutmeg and black pepper, then cook gently for 1-2 mins. Remove from the heat.

Heat the oven to 200°C and assemble the lasagne. Spoon a small ladleful of white sauce over the base of your dish. Lay pasta sheets on top, trimming to fit as necessary. Top the pasta with a little white sauce, around ⅙ of the garlic spinach (gaps between mounds is fine), then slices of mortadella. Add another pasta layer and repeat, making sure to save a large ladleful of white sauce for the top. You should have enough to create 6-7 layers of filling, and 7-8 layers of pasta (depending on the dimensions of your dish), so judge the sauce quantities accordingly.
Cover the lasagne with the remaining Parmesan and bake for 35 mins until fully bronzed and bubbling. Leave to rest for 15 mins, then serve.

name: Spinach Arancini With Herby Aioli
description: Turn your leftover risotto into golden crispy arancini. It's not as difficult as you might think.
instructions: Bring a large pan of water to the boil, then add the spinach and cook for a minute, then drain through a sieve and set aside to cool a little. Peel and finely chop the onion. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat, add a large glug of olive oil then add the onion along with a big pinch of salt. Fry until softened but not colouring, it should take about 10 mins.

Press the spinach into the sieve to try and squeeze out as much moisture as you can, then add to a blender along with 100ml of the stock and the basil. Blitz into a purée, season well with salt and pepper. Grate the parmesan into the purée and set aside.

Once the onion had softened, crush or finely grate the garlic into the frying pan. Add the garlic to the pan and sizzle for a minute further, then add the risotto rice. Stir and toast until the rice is coated in the oil and beginning to make a gently popping sound. Then pour in the wine, and bubble down by half, around 2-3 mins. Then add a big splash and stir well.

Continue to add the stock, a big splash at a time, making sure you don’t add any more until each splash has been fully absorbed. Once you’ve used all the stock, check the consistency of the rice, if it's still a little too al dente, add a little more stock and continue to cook, it should have a slightly thicker consistency than a traditional risotto at this point.
Fold in the spinach and parmesan purée along with the 30g butter and the lemon juice. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Make the parsley mayo. Finely grate the garlic into a bowl with the lemon juice, stir well, then add mustard and mayo. Finely chop the parsley and stir through Season well.

Tip the flour into a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Crack the eggs into another bowl and whisk together. Tip the panko breadcrumbs into one last bowl. Set aside a baking sheet. Take a scoop of the risotto and roll in between your hands to create a ball the size of a large lime, around 50g.

Add the ball to the flour and toss until covered, then move into the egg mix, then lift, draining away an excess egg, and add to the bowl of panko breadcrumbs. Toss well, then remove from the panko and return to the egg mix and toss well, then place back into the panko breadcrumbs and toss well. Remove each and set aside on the lined baking tray. Repeat with the rest of the mix.

Tip vegetable oil into a deep saucepan, it should be at least half way up the side of the pan. Place over a high heat and heat to 180°C, then turn the heat to medium to keep it stable at 180°C. Line a tray with kitchen paper.

Lower the arancini balls into the pan using a slotted spoon. Fry for 8-10 mins, until crispy and golden, then use a spider or slotted spoon to remove to transfer to the lined tray to drain. Repeat with the remaining balls.
To serve, place the arancini on a large platter. Serve with the mayo on the side for people to help themselves to in the middle of the table.

name: Spinach Feta Dip With Crispy Pitta Chips
description: Feta and cream cheese are mixed with spinach and beautifully seasoned with oregano and dill. Serve with crunchy, golden pitta chips.
instructions: Blanch the spinach in a pot of boiling water, then drain and set aside. Once cool, squeeze out as much water as possible. Chop into small chunks and set aside.

Add the spinach, feta, cream cheese, garlic, dill, 1 ½ tsp of oregano and the zest and juice of a lemon to a food processor and pulse until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Put the dip in the fridge to chill whilst you make your chips.
Split the pitta in half so you have two thin layers of bread. Cut into whatever shape you fancy, I’ve gone for triangles.
Add a good glug of oil to a pan then add your pitta pieces, season with the garlic powder, onion powder, your remaining oregano, salt and pepper. Fry until crunchy and golden.
Dunk the pita chips into your spinach dip and enjoy.

name: Spinach Pakoras With Tamarind Chutney
description: Crispy battered spinach fritters with a sweet and tangy tamarind chutney.  A perfect recipe for Iftar.
instructions: Soak the tamarind in boiling water for 15 mins, this makes it easy to get rid of any seeds and excess skin.
After 15 mins, use your hands to loosen the tamarind up and pass it through a sieve until you're left with a thick pulp.
Add the tamarind pulp to a saucepan along with 2 cups of water, sugar, dried chillies and salt. Bring to the boil and turn down to simmer for 15 mins or until it reduces by half.
Sieve the chickpea flour and baking powder into a large bowl.

Add all the spices listed above and give it a mix. Add 1 cup of water, till you get a loose batter. Add the spinach leaves and chopped green chillies, mixing everything together really well. Heat up the vegetable oil in a wok or a deep pan to 180°C.
Drop spoonfuls of the spinach mixture into the hot oil and deep fry until golden brown.
Serve straight away with the chutney.

name: Spinach Tortelloni With Courgettes & Spicy Walnut Pesto
description: A simple way to jazz up La Famiglia Rana Spinach & Ricotta Tortelloni. Excellent served with a spicy homemade pesto.
keywords: Spinach Tortelloni With Golden Courgettes & Spicy Walnut Pesto
instructions: Toast the walnuts in a large pan over a medium heat for 2-3 mins until golden. Remove from the heat and allow to cool.

Halve and de-seed the chilli, peel the garlic, and grate the Parmesan. Make the pesto by adding basil, keeping a few leaves for garnish, to a food processor along with the chilli, walnuts, garlic, Parmesan, 3 tbsp of olive oil and the juice of half a lemon. Coarsely blitz until semi smooth then taste and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Get your pan of water on to boil. Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Slice the courgette into ½ cm thick rounds and add to the pan, frying for 2 mins on each side until golden then remove from the oil and drain on kitchen paper.

While the courgette is frying, add the pasta to the boiling water and cook for just 2 mins. Drain and reserve some water, then add to the frying pan with the courgettes and pesto. Mix well until really saucy and coated nicely.
Serve in warm bowls topped with a bit of grated Parmesan, fresh basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Spinach and Garlic Rice
description: This bright green rice is such an easy way to get your veg in. You won't find a better healthy garlic rice recipe about.
instructions: Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear, then drain.
Add the spinach, water, garlic, and butter to a blender. Blend until smooth and vividly green.
Add the rice to a medium-sized saucepan and pour over the blended spinach mixture.
Bring to a boil, then cover with a lid and reduce the heat to as low as possible. Cook for 12 mins.
Turn off the heat and let the rice sit for 10 mins.
Remove the lid and fluff up the rice with a fork. Some spinach may settle on top – just mix it back through the rice.
Cover with the lid again and let sit for a further 5 mins. Season to taste with salt and black pepper before serving.

name: Spinach, Ricotta & Butternut Squash Lasagne
description: A great alternative to the classic - the creamy ricotta and the sweet roasted butternut squash are the perfect filling.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Halve and de-seed your butternut squash. Whack them in oven for 50 minutes or until soft.
Spinach filling time. Finely chop your garlic. Throw them in a pan with some olive oil. Cook for 30 seconds, and then drop in your spinach.
Once wilted (1 minute), add your chopped sage leaves. Then, add half of your ricotta and 30g of your Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper, remove from the heat and set aside.

Take your butternut squash out the oven and remove the skins. Place one butternut squash in a blender. Pulse, adding water, until you have a puree. Cube your other butternut squash into bite-size pieces.
In a large bowl, place your butternut puree, your butternut cubes, the other half of your ricotta, a large tsp of Dijon mustard, some salt and some pepper. Mix it all together.

Assembly time. In an oven proof dish, put a layer of butternut mixture. Then layer on some lasagna sheets. Then a spinach layer, topped with a good grating of Parmesan. Add another layer of lasagna sheets, more butternut squash filling and then more lasagna sheets. Finally, spoon over the remainder of your butternut squash and spinach mixture to make the top layer.
Cover with discs of mozzarella, and grate the rest of your Parmesan over the top.
Add a drizzle of olive oil, a good grinding of black pepper, and put into the oven for 45 minutes, or until golden brown on top.
Remember to check the lasagna 20 minutes into cooking. If the top is browning too quickly, just put on some tin foil, and then remove it 5 minutes from the end. Enjoy!

name: Spoon-Drop Meatballs in Ginger Broth
description: A quick and easy meal to warm you from within. Fiery ginger broth, melted pak choi and bouncy, flavoursome meatballs.
keywords: Spoon-Drop Meatballs in Ginger Broth recipe
instructions: Trim and thinly slice the spring onions. Put the spring onion whites into a bowl with the pork mince, sesame oil, soy sauce, water and salt. Mix thoroughly until combined and the texture has changed to a stickier consistency. Set aside.

Thinly slice the ginger and put it into a saucepan with the chicken stock. Set over a medium heat and, once hot, drop tablespoons of the meat mixture into the hot broth. Continue until no meat remains. Gently poach for 10-15 mins until fully cooked. Skim any foamy bits out of the broth as it cooks.

Meanwhile, separate the pak choi leaves and drop them into the broth for the last 4 mins of cooking time. Stir through the turmeric and spring onion greens, then taste and season the soup with salt or soy sauce and pepper. Finish with a light drizzle of sesame oil.

name: Spring Antipasto Lentil & Quinoa Salad
description: A hearty salad packed with roasted courgette, green olives, artichoke and creamy feta, all tossed in a sharp lemony dill dressing. Dense enough to keep you full for hours, and even better the next day.
keywords: Dilly Antipasto Lentil & Quinoa Salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. If your edamame is frozen, leave it out to thaw.

Rinse the lentils and add to a large saucepan with plenty of cold water. Bring to the boil and cook for 20 mins. Rinse the quinoa and add it to the pan. Cook for a further 10-12 mins, until the quinoa is cooked through. Drain through a fine-mesh sieve, rinse with cold water and leave to dry in the sieve.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the courgettes and spread out on a large baking tray. Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil, grate over the garlic and season with salt. Toss with your hands until everything is evenly coated, then roast for 20 mins, until soft and starting to catch at the edges. Scatter the walnuts onto the tray for the final 6-7 mins, until golden.
While everything cooks, make the dressing. Squeeze the juice of the lemons into a small bowl, add the Dijon mustard and whisk in the extra virgin olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper.
Roughly chop the olives and dill. Quarter the artichoke hearts.
Tip the lentils, quinoa, courgette, edamame, olives, artichokes, walnuts and dill into a large bowl. Pour over the dressing and toss until everything is well coated. Crumble over the feta and serve.

name: Spring Chicken Fatteh
description: Fatteh (“crushed”) comes in all shapes and sizes, depending on where it’s being made and the season. What links them all is the layers of crisp broken up bread.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C.
Start by spatchcocking the chicken. Use a strong pair of kitchen scissors to cut along either side of the spine, from the neck to the tail, and remove (keep it for stock!).
Now flip the chicken over and press down on the breast to flatten. Mix the spices with 2 tbsp of oil and rub all over the chicken along with plenty of salt.
Cut the peppers and tomatoes into roughly two-inch pieces and add to a roasting dish. Season well with salt and a drizzle of olive oil, then place the spatchcocked chicken on top.
Place into the oven and roast for 35 mins, until the juice of the chicken run clear when pierced with a knife.
Meanwhile, mix the yoghurt, tahini, juice of half a lemon and a big pinch of salt in a small bowl. Now add water, 50ml at a time until you have a mix the consistency of double cream. Set aside.

Separate the flatbreads into two layers and cut them into roughly two-inch square pieces, place onto a roasting tray and drizzle with a generous glug of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Mix well and set aside.
