Once the chicken is cooked, remove it from the oven and set it aside to cool until you’re able to handle it.
While the chicken cools, toast the bread in the oven for about 6 or 7 mins until golden brown and crunchy. Remove and toss with the za’atar while still warm.
Shred the chicken into a bowl and mix with 3 tbsp of the roasting juices along with the sumac, juice of a lemon and the pomegranate molasses.
Assemble the dish by spreading a layer of the tahini yoghurt, topping with half of the tomatoes and peppers, half of the crispy bread and a good layer of chicken.
Repeat with a second layer of yoghurt, tomatoes and peppers, bread and chicken, then finish with a final drizzle of yoghurt and the fresh herbs.

name: Spring Chicken Panzanella
description: A great take on a panzanella using leftover roast chicken. This one's got heaps of texture and flavour.
ingredients: Third of a Leftover Roast Chicken
instructions: This recipe uses up leftover Roast Chicken, so you'll need to have some leftovers to hand to try this recipe.

Cut the bread, crusts and all, into chunky cubes. Preheat a large frying pan over a medium heat and add a generous glug of olive oil. Once hot, toss in the cubed bread and toss to coat in the warm oil. Toast over a medium heat, for 4-5 mins or until the bread starts to pick up some colour. At this point, sprinkle in the fennel seeds and use a spoon to press them into the croutons. Keep toasting for 2-3 mins until fragrant. Remove from the heat and leave them in the pan to keep warm.

Shred your chicken into bite-sized pieces, cut the tomatoes & courgette into chunks and toss them all into a large mixing bowl. Thinly slice the red onions and add them to the bowl along with the capers. Season with plenty of salt, black pepper, the sherry vinegar and a glug of olive oil. Set aside for at least 10 mins to macerate.

Bring a small pan of salted water to a boil and boil the peas for 1 minute. Fish them out and add straight to the salad bowl. Cut the asparagus into diamonds, discarding the woody ends, boil for one minute and then add to the bowl.
Tear in the basil leaves, tip in the warm croutons and finish with the shaved parmesan. Toss everything together and divide between plates. Finish with a few twists of black pepper and serve.

name: Spring Chopped Salad
description: Spring has sprung, and there's no better way to celebrate in-season vegetables than with a fresh and flavourful chopped salad.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salty water to a boil the asparagus for 1-2 mins. Drain and run under cold water to stop any further cooking and set aside.
Cook your mixed grains/quinoa according to package instructions and allow it to cool. Add your frozen peas to a microwave-safe bowl and microwave for 2 mins on high. Once cooked, allow them to cool.
Slice your cucumber in half lengthwise and scoop at the seeds. Chop off the tops and bottoms of the radishes.
Add your asparagus, radish, cucumber, and mint (reserving some of the mint for garnish later) to a chopping board and chop them up into rough chunks.
Add your chopped ingredients all to a bowl and throw in your cooked grains and peas.
Make a quick dressing by combining the olive oil, mustard, honey and juice of the lemons. Mix until emulsified and season with salt to taste.
And the dressing to the bowl and toss it vigorously. Garnish with some torn mint and salt. Serve and enjoy.

name: Spring Green Caesar Dressing
description: A beautiful bright green twist on a caesar salad dressing. Add it to salads to combine it with your choice of protein, veg and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Carefully separate the egg yolk (you can freeze the egg whites for meringue), then add the yolk to a bowl and lightly whisk. Add a small squeeze of lemon juice, then very slowly add the oil, a trickle at a time, whisking as you go until it’s emulsified into a thick mayo. Add the Dijon.

Add the parsley, mint, basil and anchovies to a blender with the rest of the lemon juice and a splash of water, then blitz into a paste. Tip the paste into the dressing and stir to combine. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Toss the dressing through a salad or, if meal prepping for the week, transfer to a jar or container and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Spring Green Caesar Salad
description: A beautiful bright green salad with crispy bits of halloumi and pitta. It's all about the texture with this Caesar salad recipe.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Use scissors to snip the pittas into 3cm triangles, then put them on a large baking tray. Add the broccoli and fennel seeds, drizzle with olive oil and season well. Toss and make sure everything is well coated. Slide into the oven for 10-15 mins, or until the broccoli is charred and the pitta chips are crisp.

Meanwhile, make your dressing. Add the yolk to a bowl and lightly whisk. Add a small squeeze of lemon juice, then very slowly add the oil, a trickle at a time, whisking as you go until it’s emulsified into a thick mayo. Add the Dijon.

Add the parsley, mint, basil and anchovies to a blender with the rest of the lemon juice and a splash of water, then blitz into a paste. Tip the paste into the dressing and stir to combine. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Cut the base from the lettuce and pull the leaves apart. Put into a large bowl. Slice the cucumber in half lengthways and use a spoon to scrape out the fleshy middle, then slice into half moons and add to the bowl along with the peas and edamame. Halve, de-stone and peel the avocado, slice into cubes and add to the bowl. Add the herb leaves.
Cut the halloumi into small chunks. Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the halloumi and cook for 5 mins, turning the chunks as they colour. Remove from the heat and add the honey.
Add the pitta chips and roasted broccoli to the large salad bowl, drizzle with the dressing and toss well. Add the honey halloumi and toss briefly, then serve.

name: Spring Onion Soy Udon
description: A super simple, sweet soy-glazed noodle dish! The sauce is cooked using the residual heat of the pan – it concentrates the flavour, giving a sweet and salty profile.
instructions: Slice the chives as finely as possible, cut the spring onions into thirds and slice the shallot in half. Set everything aside.

Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Add the beansprouts and cook for 3 mins. Once cooked, transfer to a bowl with the chives, sesame oil, chilli flakes, sesame seeds and soy sauce. Mix well and set aside.
To the same saucepan, add the udon and cook for around 3 mins until the noodles are separated. Drain and set aside.
For the sauce, combine all the ingredients in a bowl. Mix well until the sugar is dissolved.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat and add the oil. Heat for 1 min, then add the spring onion, shallot and ginger. Cook for 5 mins until the spring onions turn a dark colour. Remove the crispy spring onions to a plate and discard the ginger and shallot.

Turn the heat up to high for 30 seconds, or until smoking. Turn the heat off. Stir the sauce and pour into the pan of oil. This technique will concentrate and caramelise the sauce. Add the udon to the pan and mix well.
Plate the udon, add a handful of the dressed beansprouts and finish with crispy spring onions on top. Enjoy!

name: Spring Onion and Ginger Sauce
description: A fragrant, punchy sauce packed with fresh ginger and spring onion. Perfect as a dip, drizzle, or marinade, this Chinese-inspired condiment adds bold flavour to any dish.
keywords: Spring Onion and Ginger Sauce recipe
instructions: Finely slice the spring onions and mince the fresh ginger. Add the finely sliced spring onions and minced ginger to a heatproof bowl.
Stir in the salt, MSG (if using), and sugar.
Heat the vegetable oil in a small pan over high heat until smoking.
Carefully pour the hot oil over the spring onion mixture, allowing it to sizzle and release its aroma.
Stir well and let sit for at least 5 minutes before serving.

name: Spring Onion and Ginger Sauce
description: A fragrant, punchy sauce packed with fresh ginger and spring onion. Perfect as a dip, drizzle, or marinade, this Chinese-inspired condiment adds bold flavour to any dish.
keywords: Spring Onion and Ginger Sauce recipe
instructions: Finely slice the spring onions and mince the fresh ginger. Add the finely sliced spring onions and minced ginger to a heatproof bowl.
Stir in the salt, MSG (if using), and sugar.
Heat the vegetable oil in a small pan over high heat until smoking.
Carefully pour the hot oil over the spring onion mixture, allowing it to sizzle and release its aroma.
Stir well and let sit for at least 5 minutes before serving.

name: Spring Pea Fattoush
description: A simple spring take on fattoush using peas and green onion with lots of fresh herbs. Toasting the bread instead of deep frying keeps things a bit lighter.
instructions: Preheat your grill.
Finely slice the red onion and add to a small bowl with the vinegar and a tbsp of water to give it a quick pickle.
Finely slice the spring onions and put them into a big bowl of ice water.
Add the peas to a saucepan of well salted boiling water, cook for a minute and then drain. Add the peas to the ice water with the spring onions.
Half the cucumber and use a teaspoon to scrape out the seeds. Finely slice it and add to a large mixing bowl. Drain and add the peas, spring onions and red onions.
Finely chop the parsley and mint and add to the bowl. Set that aside while you toast the bread.
Split the breads into two thin layers and then tear into roughly two-inch pieces and put them on a large roasting tray. Drizzle and toss with olive oil and a big pinch of salt.

Toast under the grill giving them a shake and stir halfway through until nice and golden and crisp. This will only take a couple of minutes so keep an eye on them! Once ready, remove from the grill and sprinkle over the chilli and ½ the sumac.
In a small bowl mix the remaining sumac, honey, lemon juice and a splash of olive oil.

Now, add the bread and dressing to the bowl with the veggies and crumble in most of the feta. Give that a gentle mix and taste for salt and lemon. Plate up, finish with the rest of the feta and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Spring Pesto & Chicken Spaghetti
description: A vibrant spring pasta with homemade pesto, tossed with spaghetti, asparagus and petit pois. All topped with the crispiest chicken mince for extra protein. This is exactly what you want when the sun starts shining again.
instructions: Start by making the pesto. Toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over a medium heat until golden, then remove from the heat and leave to cool slightly.

Add the toasted pine nuts, parmesan, basil, olive oil, juice of the lemon and a splash of cold water to a blender. Blitz until smooth and loose, adding a little more water if needed. Season with salt and black pepper.

Now get on with the chicken. Zest the lemon and grate the garlic. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Add the chicken mince, breaking it up with a spoon, as you fry for about 7-9 mins, until starting to brown.

Stir in the chilli flakes, grated garlic, lemon zest and a good pinch of salt and pepper, then fry for another 2–3 mins until fragrant, then reduce the heat and keep warm. Right before serving, mix through the parmesan and the juice of half the lemon.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and cook the spaghetti according to packet instructions. When the pasta has 3 mins remaining, add the asparagus and petit pois to the same pot.
Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain everything. Return the pasta and vegetables to the pan, add the pesto and a splash of pasta water, and toss until glossy and evenly coated.
Divide between bowls and spoon the chicken mince over the top. Finish with extra parmesan, black pepper and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Spring Potato Salad with Hot Smoked Salmon & Jammy Eggs
description: It doesn't get more spring than asparagus, baby new potatoes and a green herby dressing. Flaky hot smoked salmon, jammy eggs and crisp sugar snap peas to finish.
keywords: Spring Potato Salad with Hot Smoked Salmon & Jammy Eggs
Spring Potato Salad with Hot Smoked Salmon & Jammy Eggs recipe
instructions: Cut any larger new potatoes into half so they're all a similar size. Then set a large saucepan of salted water over a high heat. Add the potatoes and boil for 20-25 mins until just fork tender. Lift them out and set aside, keeping the water on the boil.

Snap the woody ends off the asparagus and cut into three equal pieces. Add to the boiling water along with the sugar snap peas and cook for 1 min, then transfer to a colander and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking. Keep the water boiling.
Carefully lower the eggs into the boiling water and cook for 6-7 mins. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool enough to handle, then peel and set aside.

Add the yoghurt, dill, parsley, lemon zest, lemon juice, garlic, anchovies and extra virgin olive oil to a blender and blitz until almost smooth. If it's too thick, loosen with water a tbsp at a time, you're after a pourable but not watery consistency. Season with salt and black pepper.
Combine the potatoes, asparagus, sugar snap peas and olives in a large bowl. Pour over the dressing and toss to coat.
To serve, divide the salad between four plates. Tear the salmon over each one, halve the eggs and nestle on top, then finish with the dill and a crack of black pepper.

name: Spring Salad with Pistachio Pesto and Whipped Ricotta
description: This is the freshest pasta salad around. It's packed with pistachio and chive pesto, all the spring veg, and lemony whipped ricotta. Stunning all around really.
instructions: Bring a large pan of water to a boil.
Cut the woody end off your asparagus, then cut them into 4cm lengths. Thinly slice your radishes.
Add your asparagus and radishes to a bowl. Season with a drizzle of oil, the juice of ½ a lemon and a good pinch of salt.
Heat a griddle pan over a high heat.
Add your asparagus and radishes to the pan and cook for a few mins until they are lightly charred and tender. Set aside.
Add salt to your boiling water, then add your orecchiette. Cook until al dente – this will take about 10 mins.
Add your ricotta to a mixing bowl along with the zest of a lemon, 25ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Whisk until you have a smooth sauce.
Make your pesto. Add your pistachios, chives, basil, parmesan, the juice of 1 lemon, 70ml olive oil and 50ml water to a small food processor. Whizz to a smooth paste, then season to taste with salt.
Once your pasta is cooked, drain it in a colander. Add it to a bowl along with your charred veg, then tip in your pistachio pesto. Toss until it is totally combined.
Spread your whipped ricotta on the base of your serving dish. Spoon over your pesto mixture, drizzle with olive oil, then serve and enjoy.

name: Spring Tabbouleh with Honey Halloumi & Hummus
description: Herby, fresh bulgur wheat tabbouleh with crisp spring veg, topped with sticky honey and poppy seed halloumi and a big dollop of hummus. Asparagus is only around for a short time in spring, if you can't get it, swap for tenderstem or green beans instead.

instructions: Cook the bulgur wheat according to packet instructions, then set aside to cool slightly.

Meanwhile, cut the woody ends off the asparagus and chop into 3cm pieces. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil, add the edamame and cook for 2 mins, then drop in the asparagus for a final 1 min. Drain and cool under cold running water or in an ice bath.
Squeeze the juice of the lemons into a small bowl, add the olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Whisk together to make the dressing.

Finely slice the spring onions and radishes. Finely chop the mint and parsley. Add the bulgur wheat to a large bowl with the asparagus, edamame, spring onions, mint, parsley and radishes. Pour over the dressing and toss well to combine.

Slice the halloumi. Set a large frying pan over a medium heat (no oil needed) and cook the halloumi for 3 mins on each side until deeply golden and charred. Take the pan off the heat, squeeze in the honey and scatter over the poppy seeds, turning the halloumi to coat.

To serve, spoon the hummus into bowls and pile the tabbouleh alongside. Top with the sticky halloumi and get stuck in. If you're making ahead, transfer the tabbouleh into containers and dollop the hummus on fresh along with the halloumi.

name: Spring Veg Minestrone
description: A spring take on a classic minestrone — it’s fresh, zesty, and full of green veg. Top it with the punchy homemade pesto and that’s dinner made in 30 mins.
instructions: Finely slice the onion. Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion along with a pinch of salt and cook for 2-3 mins. Finely grate the garlic into the pan and add the fennel seeds, toast for 2 mins then pour the stock in and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat down slightly and simmer for 5 mins. Roughly chop the courgette into 2cm chunks and add to the stock and cook for 10 mins.
Blitz the herbs, the zest of the lemon and half of the Parmesan into a rough paste. Add 60ml olive oil and blitz it into a chunky pesto. Season generously.
Trim and cut the green beans into 2-3 cm pieces. Trim 2cm off the bottom of the asparagus and discard. Cut your spears in half. Break the egg noodles into 3cm pieces.

Add the veg and noodles to the pot and cook for 5 mins. Remove from the heat, then squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Spoon the soup into bowls and top with the pesto and a grating of the remaining Parmesan. Serve with crusty bread if you like.

name: Sprout & Chilli Peanut Noodles
description: The legend that is Meera Sodha came to MOB to make her incredible vegan noodles. Using shredded sprouts so none of your brussels go to waste.
instructions: Start by prepping your veg. Finely shred your sprouts and mince up your garlic. Finely slice your spring onions, separating the whites and the greens. Finely chop your peanuts. Keep all these ingredients separate for now.
For the chilli sauce, add the chilli oil to a bowl (you want an equal amount of solid crunchy sediment and liquid oil from the jar) along with the white wine vinegar, sesame oil and soy sauce.
Set aside a handful each of the chopped peanuts, spring onion greens and sesame seeds for garnish. Add the rest to the chilli sauce and mix to combine.
Cook the noodles following packet instruction then rinse with cold water to cool and drain. Set aside.

Heat a glug of sesame oil in a large pan set over a medium heat. Add the garlic and the spring onion whites and fry for 2-3 mins until softened and fragrant. Then, add the sprouts and crank the heat up to high. Hard fry the sprouts for 4-5 mins until tender and starting to char.
Add the noodles and chilli sauce to the pan. Gently mix together then season to taste, adding salt if need be.
To serve, divide the noodles between bowls. Sprinkle over the remaining spring onion greens, sesame seeds and more peanuts. Add more chilli oil if you wish.

name: Sprout & Pancetta Noodles
description: You just can’t beat a stir fry. This one uses staple condiments you’ll already have at home to make the sauce, reminiscent of Japanese yakisoba. Crispy pancetta and charred sprouts complete the mix.
instructions: Mix the ketchup, soy, Worcestershire sauce and honey together in a small bowl with water. Set the sauce aside.
Cut the sprouts in half. Peel and finely slice the carrot into matchsticks (or peel if you can't be bothered). Finely slice the spring onions (both green and white parts).
Pour a small splash of neutral oil into a wok or high sided frying pan. Add the pancetta, fry over a high heat for 4-5 mins until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon into a bowl.

Add the sprouts to the pan. Stir fry for 4-5 mins until they are charred and tender. Add the carrot and three-quarters of the spring onions and chilli. Stir fry for another minute or so, adding a splash more oil if needed then tip in the noodles.
Add the sauce to the pan. Cook for a couple of minutes tossing, until the noodles and veg are coated in the sauce then toss back through the crispy pancetta.
Divide between two bowls, top with the remaining spring onion and chilli oil to serve.

name: Squash & Beans with Crispy Sage
description: An earthy, sweet and umami-bursting butter bean stew, topped with roasted veggies and crispy salty sage leaves. A perfect autumnal vegan dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C. Soak the cashews in boiling water in a small bowl and set aside.
Chop the squash in half and remove the seeds. No need to peel it. Place one half, intact, cut side down on a baking tray. Cut the other half into small pieces and scatter them around the tray.

Peel and roughly chop the red onion into wedges and add to the tray. Slice the top off the garlic bulb and add to the tray, cut side up. Drizzle over a glug of olive oil and season with sea salt then roast for 35-40 mins until the squash is tender and the large intact piece starts to collapse when you touch it. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool.
While the veggies cook, heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan set over a low-medium heat. Add the sage leaves and fry for 30 seconds, then transfer them to a paper towel and sprinkle with sea salt.

Get the pan with the sage-infused oil back over a low-medium heat and add the butter beans. If the beans are organic, add their cooking liquid; if the cooking liquid isn’t already salty, crumble in the stock cube. If the beans aren’t organic, add the water and crumble in the stock cube. Bring the mixture to a low bubble and leave to gently simmer.

To a blender, add the silken tofu, drained soaked cashews, nutritional yeast, juice of the lemon and a pinch of salt. Scoop out the flesh from the large intact piece of squash and squeeze out the flesh from the roasted garlic then add to the blender and blitz until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into the pan with the butter beans, mix to combine and season to taste.
Divide the beans between bowls and top with the roasted squash and red onion, and the crispy sage.

name: Squash & Beetroot Galette
description: Brown butter mascarpone layered with tender seasonal vegetables, this is the perfect showstopper for your veggie Christmas.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C.
Finely chop up the sage and garlic.

Melt 100g of butter in a frying pan and cook for 10 mins on low heat until the butter starts to brown and smell nutty. Tip in the sage and garlic and cook for 2 mins until the sage is crispy and the garlic is lightly browned.
Pour 3 tbsp of your browned butter mixture into a small bowl and allow the rest to chill in a separate bowl.
Cut the 250g butter into cubes.

Tip the flour into a large bowl and mix in the salt. Add in the cubed butter and rub this into the flour with your fingertips until they are the size of a pea. Don’t worry about it being too neat, having irregular chunks means a crispier pastry.

Slowly drizzle in 100ml of ice-cold water and push the flour and butter together to form a rough dough. If it still looks dry, add in more water, 1 tbsp at a time. Shape into a disc and cover with cling film and pop into the fridge for 30 mins.
Peel the butternut squash before thinly slicing it into thin discs along with the beetroot.
Whisk the cooled brown butter with the mascarpone. Add the zest of the lemon. Season with salt and pepper.
Take the pastry out of the fridge and place it onto a floured work surface. Bash it down with a rolling pin and roll it out into a large circle that is 1mm thick.

Spread the brown butter mascarpone in the centre leaving a 5cm gap around the edges. Arrange the squash and beetroot on top of the butter and then drizzle with some olive oil, and season with salt and pepper.
Wrap the pastry edges onto the vegetables and them brush with a whisked egg before placing it all onto a lined baking tray.
Bake in the oven for 45 mins until the pastry is golden. If you have some leakage don’t worry, the butter will help form a crispy bottom.

Meanwhile, make the glaze: mix together the cornflour and 1 tbsp of water to make the slurry. Combine the reserved 3 tbsp of brown butter along with your maple syrup, chilli flakes and 2 tbsp of water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil and add in the slurry mix and cook for 2 mins. Season with salt.
Roughly chop the hazelnuts and toast in a dry saucepan for 4 mins until lightly browned.
Once the galette is cooked, brush with the maple glaze and sprinkle with toasted nuts.
Allow to cool for 15 mins before slicing and enjoy hot or cold.

name: Squash & Chickpea Fattoush With Crispy Pitta Chips
description: A fibre-packed Middle Easten-inspired recipe that'll make a nice change to your weekly food rota.
keywords: Squash & Chickpea Fattoush With Crispy Pitta Chips
Squash & Chickpea Fattoush With Crispy Pitta Chips recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel the squash then slice in half vertically and use a spoon to scoop out the seeds. Slice into 1-2cm half moons and add to a large baking tray. Drain the chickpeas and add to the tray. Add the ground coriander and a generous drizzle of olive oil. Season well and slide into the oven and cook for 30- 40 mins, until caramelised and charred in places.
Cut the pittas into triangles and spread out on a separate baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season well, then slide into the oven for 10 mins, then remove and set aside.

Meanwhile, make the dressing by blitzing three-quarters of the herbs, green chillli, Dijon mustard and honey together. Add the lemon juice along with enough olive oil to make the sauce a drizzle-able consistency. Add a splash of water to loosen, taste and season well, then set aside.
Take the cucumber and slice in half lengthways, then use a spoon to scrape the seeds out from the middle. Lie flat and slice on an angle and set aside.

Remove the chickpeas and squash from the oven and allow to cool for 5-10 mins. Add the remaining herbs to the tray along with the sumac and toss well. Add the pitta chips along with a drizzle of olive oil. Toss then pile into bowls or on a platter. Snuggle the cucumber in. Top with the green dressing, then finish with feta cheese and a crack of black pepper.

name: Squash & Chickpea Pasta
description: This is a great recipe from Jamie Oliver's new cookbook, ONE, that's stuffed with lots of our favourite ingredients. Chilli, rosemary, and a hint of cinnamon.
instructions: Boil the kettle.
Cut the lasagne sheets lengthways into 4 equal strips. Peel and finely slice the garlic. Coarsely grate the squash in long strokes. Finely grate the cheese.
Put a 28cm frying pan on a high heat.

Once hot, put a little drizzle of olive oil into the pan with the garlic, cinnamon and chilli. Strip the rosemary leaves, and when the garlic is lightly golden, add the rosemary, squash and chickpeas.
Scatter the pasta into the pan, then carefully pour in enough boiling kettle waster to just cover the pasta - about 330ml.
Let it bubble away for 4 minutes, or until the pasta has absorbed most of the water and you've got a nice sauce, stirring regularly and loosening with an extra splash of water, if needed.
Turn the heat off, remove the cinnamon and chilli (or you can finely slice or chop the chilli and stir it back through, to taste, for extra heat).
Stir in the cheese, then season to perfection. Finish with an extra grating of cheese and a kiss of extra virgin olive oil, if you like.

name: Squash & Chorizo Orzo with Hazelnut Gremolata
description: This orzo is smoky, creamy and bursting with autumnal flavours like butternut squash and roasted hazelnuts. It’s exactly what we want to eat when the nights get shorter.
keywords: Squash & Chorizo Orzo with Hazelnut Gremolata
Squash & Chorizo Orzo with Hazelnut Gremolata recipe
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C fan.
Halve your squash and scoop out and discard the seeds. Drizzle the squash with olive oil and salt then pop on a baking tray and roast in the oven for 45 mins.
Pop your hazelnuts on a small baking tray, then bake them in the oven for 7 mins.

Once your hazelnuts are cool enough to handle, roughly chop them and add to a medium-sized bowl. Roughly chop your parsley and add to the same bowl. Add the zest of your lemon and 4 tbsp olive oil, and season it to taste with salt.
Peel and finely slice your shallots and garlic.
Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat with a generous glug of olive oil, then add your shallots. Cook them for 10 mins until they’ve softened, then add your garlic and cook them for 2 mins more.
Pour your orzo into the pan then pour in your chicken stock. Bring it up to a boil, then turn down the heat and simmer for 9 mins.
Dice the chorizo. Get a frying pan over a medium heat, and add your chorizo. Cook it for about 5 mins until it has crisped up and the fat has rendered out.
Scoop the flesh out of your squash skin, and add it to a food processor along with the chilli flakes. Whizz it up to form a paste.
Add your squash paste to the orzo. Grate in your parmesan, and add the juice of ½ the lemon. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
To serve, divide your orzo between bowls then spoon over the hazelnut salsa and chorizo.

name: Squash & Fennel Seed Roast Tomato Soup
description: You could make this soup with any winter squash but Delica pumpkin, Onion, Violino or Butternut squash will be the most intensely flavoured. We’ve topped it with Everything Bagel cheese crackers and a glug of olive oil.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Halve the squash, remove the seeds and chop the squash into 3cm thick wedges. Halve the tomatoes through the equator. Flatten the unpeeled garlic cloves with the back of a knife.

Spread the squash over a large baking sheet, drizzle with a glug of olive oil and toss so all the pieces are glossy. Roast for 30 mins, then turn each piece over and cook for another 10-15 mins until each is soft and caramelised at the edges.

Meanwhile, arrange the tomato halves cut side up in a separate roasting tin or other ovenproof dish in which they fit in one snug layer. Use a pestle and mortar to grind the fennel seeds and salt to a coarse powder, stir in the caster sugar, then sprinkle this all over the cut tomatoes.

Squeeze the garlic and thyme sprigs in gaps between the tomatoes, then drizzle with the remaining oil. Roast in the oven for 45-50 mins on the shelf beneath the squash, until the tomatoes are soft and sunken.

Meanwhile, make the cheese cracker. Grate the Cheddar. Set a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Sprinkle in a handful of cheese and cook for 1-2 mins until caramelised. Sprinkle over some Everything Bagel Seasoning then flip the cracker to cook the other side for 2 mins. Transfer to a wire rack to cool and repeat with the remaining cheese.

Once the squash and tomatoes are cooked, combine both in a standing blender or, if you're using a stick blender, a large saucepan. Pick out any woody bits of thyme and squeeze the garlic flesh in, but discard the papery skin. Add the stock and blend until completely smooth and silky.
Before serving, gently heat the soup in a saucepan. Taste and add salt as required. Top up with a little extra water if it’s stiff or purée like.

To serve, ladle the soup into bowls. Add a glug of good olive oil to each bowl and break over the Everything Bagel cheese crackers. If you don't have time to make the crackers, a sprinkling of Everything Bagel seasoning is just as good!

name: Squash & Gorgonzola Quesadilla
description: A seasonal quesadilla for all the blue cheese lovers out there. It's rich, it's tangy, and it's so, so good.
instructions: Peel and dice squash, finely chop the onion and finely slice the garlic, red chilli and sage.

Preheat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a goog lug of olive oil and tip in the squash. Season with salt and cook, tossing regularly, for 12-13 mins, until the squash is starting to soften and pick up lots of colour.

At this point, add the onion and cook for another 5 mins. Now add the garlic, chilli and sage and cook for a final 2-3 mins to take the raw edge off of the garlic. Tip the mixture into a bowl, season with salt and pepper and allow to cool a little.

Grab your wraps and lay them out ready to fill. Top each wrap with a handful of grated mozz, a good spoonful of the squash mixture and dot over a little blue cheese. Add a little chilli jam (not too much!) and fold them over to close.
Toast each quesadilla in a dry pan over a medium heat until the exterior is golden brown and the interior is gooey and melted. Serve with extra chilli jam for dipping.

name: Squash & Sage Beans with Whipped Ricotta
description: These creamy white beans with roasted squash, crispy sage, lemony ricotta and quick-pickled chillies are absolutely packed with fibre. A healthy dinner that’s delicious too.
keywords: Squash & Sage Beans with Whipped Ricotta Recipe
Squash & Sage Beans with Whipped Ricotta
instructions: Preheat your oven to 190°C.
Slice your red chilli and place in a bowl with enough apple cider vinegar to cover. Set aside.
Chop your squash into segments and lay onto a lined baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper and ½ your sage leaves. Place in the oven for 30 mins until soft and caramelised.
Meanwhile, gently fry your remaining sage leaves in olive oil until crispy, making sure not to crowd the pan. Remove from the pan and lay onto a piece of kitchen paper to drain.
Finely chop the shallot and add it to the pan and cook for around 5 mins. Mince the garlic and add to the pan for 30 seconds before adding the beans along with their liquid.
Roughly chop ¼ of the roasted squash and add to the beans, along with some more water if needed, and cook for another 5 mins.
Get the ricotta into a bowl and grate in the zest of the lemon. Add a pinch of salt and pepper and combine using a whisk.
Finish the beans with a squeeze of lemon juice and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Divide the beans between plates and top with the pieces of roasted squash, the whipped ricotta, the pickled chillies, crispy sage leaves and a few roasted hazelnuts.

name: Squash & Sage Spelt Risotto
description: We’ve swapped white risotto rice for spelt in this autumnal squash risotto, giving you four times the amount of fibre and making your gut microbes very happy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C.
Cut the squash into chunky wedges and roast in the oven for 35 mins until soft enough to mash with a fork.
Cook the spelt following packet instructions.
Heat the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over a medium heat and add the sage leaves. Cook for a few mins until they’re crisp, then set aside for garnish and leave the oil in the pan.
Mince the garlic then place in the pan with the sage-infused oil. Fry over a low heat until it turns translucent and smells fragrant.

Remove the cooked squash from the oven and add it to the pan along with the water and spelt. Mix everything together really well until the squash breaks down to form a creamy sauce. Add more water as needed.
Divide the risotto between plates and top with the crispy sage and a sprinkling of Parmesan, if using.

name: Squash Curry Noodles
description: A seriously delicious bowl of butternut squash curry, served with ramen noodles, soy-marinated eggs and pickled ginger.
instructions: Start by making the soy-marinated eggs. Bring a small saucepan of water up to a boil over a medium heat. Add your eggs to the pan and cook them for 7 mins then transfer them to a bowl of icy water to stop them cooking.
Meanwhile, mix the water with the soy sauce and ½ the sugar in a tall, thin circular container (a tall jar would work).
Peel the eggs and put them in your soy sauce mixture. Seal the container and get them in the fridge to marinate for at least two hours, or several days.
Heat your oven to 190°C fan. Peel your squash and dice ½ of it into 2cm chunks. Slice the rest into 3cm thick slices.
Arrange the 3cm thick slices on a baking tray and drizzle them with vegetable oil and salt. Slide into the oven to roast for 30 mins or until tender, flipping the slices over halfway through.
Meanwhile, peel and finely dice your onion and carrot.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a medium-sized saucepan set over a medium heat. Tip in your onion and carrot and cook them for 10 mins, until they’re softened and just starting to take on colour.
Grate your garlic and ginger into the pan. Add your curry powder and turmeric and cook the spices out for 3 mins.
Add your 2cm squash chunks to the pan along with the soy sauce, sugar and ⅖ of the water. Bring the mixture up to a simmer and leave to cook for 20 mins (add a splash more water if it’s drying out).

Transfer the mixture to a blender and whizz it up to a smooth thick sauce. Pour it back into the pan, and loosen it with as much of the remaining water as needed to make it a runny pourable sauce. Keep it warm over a low heat.
Cook your noodles in boiling water according to packet instructions, then drain. Finely slice your spring onions. Remove the marinated eggs from the fridge and slice them in half lengthways.

To serve, divide your noodles between serving bowls and spoon over the curry sauce. Top each bowl with the marinated eggs, some pickled sushi ginger, sliced spring onions and the roasted squash slices.

name: Squash and Halloumi Curry with Caramelised Limes
description:
This creamy curry’s all about contrast - sweet squash, salty halloumi and zingy caramelised lime. A weeknight winner that hits every note.

In partnership with Patak's #ad
instructions: Peel the squash and chop it into 2cm chunks. Heat the vegetable oil in a large sauté pan set over a medium heat. Add the tikka masala paste and cook for 3 mins until darkened, fragrant and the oil has started to separate.
Add the squash, chopped tomatoes, water and a good pinch of salt. Cover with a lid and simmer for 20 mins until the squash is soft.

Meanwhile, finely slice the limes into wheels. Heat another drizzle of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the lime slices for about 4 mins on each side until golden and caramelised. Set aside to cool slightly.
Dice the halloumi into 2cm chunks. Heat a drizzle of vegetable oil in a large frying pan and fry the halloumi for a few mins on each side until golden all over.
Once the squash is soft, stir in the halloumi and simmer for 2 mins. Pour in 150ml of the double cream and season to taste with salt. Finely chop the cooled caramelised limes.
Spoon the curry over cooked rice. Drizzle over the remaining cream, and a dollop of mango chutney. Finish with the chopped caramelised limes, and fresh coriander, if using.

name: Squash and Tofu Red Curry
description: Our vegan version of a Thai takeaway classic. Flavoured with punchy dried chillies and lemongrass, and served up with sticky Tilda Fragrant Jasmine Rice.
instructions: Deseed your red chillies. Then pop them into a heatproof jug. Add 200ml boiling water and leave to soak for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, peel and roughly chop your shallots, lemongrass and garlic.
Add your red chillies with the water to a mini food processor along with the rest of your chopped ingredients and galangal. Add a little oil if needed to blend it into a paste.
Peel your squash, then cut it into large chunks. Chop up your red pepper into 3cm chunks. Cut your tofu into large squares.
Add your cornflour, ½ tsp coriander and a good pinch of salt to a bowl. Add your tofu and toss to coat.

Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a glug of olive oil, then add your tofu to the pan. Fry for a couple of minutes on each side until crisp and golden. Drain on a plate lined with kitchen towel.

Heat a large pan over a medium heat. Add in a big glug of oil and tip in your curry paste and ground coriander and cook for 5 mins until darkened in colour slightly and fragrant. Pour in your coconut milk and 300ml water along with your sugar, soy sauce and a big pinch of salt. Bring up to a simmer.
Cook your Tilda Fragrant Jasmine Rice according to packet instructions.
Add your butternut squash, tofu cubes and red pepper to the curry sauce, then simmer for 15 mins. Your butternut squash should be tender by this time, but leave it to simmer 5 mins more if it’s not.
Spoon your rice into bowls and top with your curry. Garnish with chopped coriander and a wedge of lime, then serve.

name: Squash, Bean & Barley Soup
description: This protein and fibre-packed soup is a hug in a bowl. It’s perfect for those autumn days when you want an easy, comforting and nourishing meal.
instructions: Roughly dice the squash (for small and medium varieties the skin is thin enough to leave on but if you have a really large one you may be better off peeling it). Slice the leeks and finely chop the shallots.
Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the squash then cover with a lid and allow to cook for 5 mins.
Add the leeks and shallots and cook for another 5 mins.

Add the drained beans to the pan along with the pearl barley then cover with the stock. Bring to a simmer then leave to cook for 45 minutes, adding more water as needed, until the pearl barley is cooked.
To finish, stir through the kale until it wilts and season to taste then divide between bowls.

name: Squash, Chestnut, Carrot & Mushroom Festive Centrepiece
description: This festive tart might look impressive, but it’s really easy to put together and is full of flavours and textures. The hasselback squash and the maple harissa drizzle really make it special.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.

You can decide whether or not to peel the squash. Wash it well if you are keeping the skin on. Halve it and scoop out the seeds. Place a chopstick on either side of the squash, on the long edges, then use a sharp knife to cut incisions. The chopsticks will stop the knife from reaching the chopping board, which will keep the squash half intact and create the hasselback effect.

Once you’ve cut both halves, place them onto a baking tray and rub them with olive oil, salt and pepper and garlic powder and smoked paprika if using. Roast for about 45 mins, or until soft enough to be pliable but not too charred on the top, as they will go back into the oven later.

Meanwhile, make the filling, Finely chop the onions and mince the garlic. Add the onions to a frying pan with a good drizzle of olive oil and some salt and cook for 6-8 mins on medium heat until translucent.
Grate the carrots and add them to the onions with the garlic and plenty of salt and pepper. Cook for another 10 mins until the carrots have reduced and started to caramelise.

Roughly chop the mushrooms and add them to a separate pan with no oil, on medium- high heat. Fry them with a little salt and pepper for 6-8 mins until they have released all of their water. Roughly chop the chestnuts, Then add them with a little more olive oil to the mushrooms and continue to cook for another 4-5 mins until golden.
Add the mushrooms and carrots to a bowl along with the cream cheese, miso, soy sauce, toasted pine nuts and harissa. Season well with salt and pepper.
Roll out the pastry a little so that it fits around the tin and patch up any edges with excess hanging over. Poke the base with a fork and bake for 20 mins.

Remove from the oven, spread the cream cheese mixture into the base, then arrange the squash over the top and bake for another 10 mins to warm though before serving. Drizzle over some extra harissa, pine nuts and dill.

name: Squash, Marmite & Chicken Spaghetti
description: Creamy squash, golden chicken mince and of course marmite for that perfect savoury finish. A bowl of comfort that still smashes your protein goals.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel the squash, if you like, and chop into 3cm chunks. Tip onto a roasting tray with a drizzle of Olive Oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat. Add the unpeeled garlic cloves to the tray and roast for 25–30 mins, until soft and caramelised.

Let the squash cool slightly. Squeeze the roasted garlic out of their skins and add to a blender along with the squash, cottage cheese, grated Cheddar, Marmite and the juice of the lemon. Season with salt and pepper and blend until smooth, loosening with a splash of pasta water or boiling water if needed.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta following pack instructions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the chicken mince, season well, and cook for 7–10 mins, stirring, until golden brown and cooked through.

Tip the cooked pasta into the pan with the mince. Pour over the sauce and stir to combine. Reheat gently over a low heat, loosening with a splash of water if needed. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more salt, pepper or lemon juice.
Divide between bowls and finish with a grating of Parmesan and a pinch of chilli flakes.

name: Squashy Parmesan Chickpeas With Brown Butter Fried Eggs
description: This is a squashy chickpea recipe with the most delicious nutty, spicy, brown butter fried eggs and crispy sage – I'm obsessed. The base is really simple and the whole recipe is ready in 30 minutes.
keywords: Squashy Parmesan Chickpeas With Brown Butter Fried Eggs
Squashy Parmesan Chickpeas With Brown Butter Fried Eggs recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Peel and chop the squash into small pieces (approx 2cm), then tip them onto a tray, drizzle with half the olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Pop in the oven for 20-25 mins until soft and slightly charred.

Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic and heat the remaining oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 2 mins, then tip in the chickpeas and their juices before bringing it to a simmer. Bubble away until the veg is done.

Once the veg is out of the oven, put half of the roasted squash mixture into a jug and blitz with a hand blender until smooth. Tip the squash purée and the remainder of the roasted squash back into the chickpea pan and mix well. Keep it simmering on low while you start on the eggs.

For the eggs, pick the sage leaves and set aside. In a separate pan, melt the butter and add the sage leaves. Fry until crisp, then remove from the pan. Crack in the eggs and cook for around 4 mins, basting with the butter and a sprinkle of chilli flakes.

Stir the spinach through the chickpeas until wilted, then taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve the chickpeas in a bowl topped with the buttery fried eggs, crispy sage, some grated parmesan and black pepper.

name: Squid Ragù Bucatini
description: A fresh and salty pasta recipe that's a great introduction to tinned squid. The ragù is rich and isn't too fishy. The jet black aesthetic? Extremely goth.
instructions: Finely dice the fennel and shallot. Thinly slice the garlic cloves and red chilli.
Add the fennel seeds to a small pan and dry toast over a medium heat until fragrant. Tip into a pestle and mortar and coarsely grind.

Grab a large sauté pan and set over a medium heat. Add 4 tbsp of olive oil and tip in the fennel and shallot. Cook in the olive oil with a pinch of salt for 10-12 mins or until soft and translucent. Add the garlic, chilli and fennel seeds and cook for another 3-4 mins.
Tip in the chopped tomatoes and bring to a boil. Cook for 10-12 mins until reduced by half. Add the whole tins of squid and cook over a low heat while you sort the pasta.

Cook the bucatini for 7-8 mins in boiling salted water. Transfer the cooked pasta to the squid sauce and tear in the black olives. Halve the lemon and finely chop the parsley. Add the parsley and lemon juice to the pasta and toss together, adding a little pasta water if necessary.
Divide between bowls and top with crunchy breadcrumbs and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Squidgy French Toast Dippers
description: Golden, custardy French toast made with squishy brioche rolls. Perfect for dunking into yoghurt and piling high with berries.
keywords: french toast with yoghurt and berries
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Slice the brioche rolls in half through the middle, so you’ve got two long pieces from each.

Crack the eggs into a shallow dish. Add the milk, cinnamon and maple syrup or honey. Whisk everything together until well combined. Dunk the brioche into the eggy mixture, turning so they’re fully coated.

Melt a knob of butter in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Let the excess egg drip off the brioche, then lay them into the pan. Fry for 2 mins on each side until golden and crisp. Work in batches if needed.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Slice up the french toast into easy to grab dippers with a spoonful of yoghurt, fresh berries and a little drizzle of honey. 
Parents Plate: Serve up with yoghurt, berries and your favourite toppings.

name: Squished Tomato & Smoked Mackerel Pasta
description: Sweet, squishy tomatoes and smoky mackerel come together in a rich, no-fuss sauce with crunchy oregano breadcrumbs on top. Great hot or cold.
keywords: Squished Tomato & Smoked Mackerel Pasta recipe
squished tomato and smoked mackerel pasta
instructions: Score a cross into the base of each tomato. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and drop in the tomatoes. Boil for 15–30 seconds, until the skins start to peel. Transfer them straight into a bowl of ice water.
Add the pasta to the same boiling water and cook until al dente, following pack instructions. Reserve some pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Meanwhile, peel the skins off the tomatoes. Chuck them into a large bowl and squish them with your hands to make a chunky sauce. Finely chop the Scotch bonnet and add it to the bowl.
Grate the garlic and strip the oregano leaves from their sprigs. Add both to the tomatoes along with a splash of apple cider vinegar, salt and pepper. Mix well and set aside.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the panko and oregano leaves, then cook, stirring, for 3–5 mins until golden and toasted. Set aside.

Toss the drained pasta through the tomato sauce with the olive oil. If it needs loosening, add a splash of the reserved pasta water until it coats the pasta nicely. Taste and season with more vinegar or salt, if needed.
Share the pasta between plates. Flake the smoked mackerel over the top and finish with the oregano breadcrumbs.

name: Sriracha Bloody Mary
description: Make sure to taste your Bloody Mary as you go to wing in as much spice, salt and ice cold vodka as you dare.  Our ultimate trick: sriracha ice cubes.
instructions: Fill a tall glass with chunky ice cubes. Tip in the vodka and tomato juice and stir. Add the Worcestershire sauce, celery salt/tajin, horseradish and give another thorough stir.
Have a taste and decide quite how hungover you are. The more severe, the more spice is required. Adjust with Tabasco, salt and pepper and garnish with a big fat crunchy stick of celery. Drink up.

name: Sriracha Butter Prawns & Cajun Rice
description: We’ve used onion, pepper and optional celery for the base of our Cajun rice; this recipe is a great one to use up any veg odds and ends you have left in the fridge, simply finely chop and soften before adding the rice. Did we mention the sriracha butter prawns.
keywords: Sriracha Butter Prawns & Cajun Rice recipe
instructions: Finely chop the onion, pepper and celery. Scrape into a saucepan along with a pinch of salt and a good drizzle of oil. Cook over a medium to high heat for 6-8 mins, stirring regularly until soft and a little caramelised.

Add the Cajun seasoning and rice, stir so that each grain gets coated then pour in the hot stock. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat to medium, simmer away, stirring regularly for 20 mins until the rice is cooked through, adding a splash more water if needed. Season to taste.
Once the rice is nearly done, drain the sweetcorn. Melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium high heat. Add the raw prawns, cook for 2 mins until they have turned from grey to pink.
Tip in the sweetcorn, add the Sriracha and toss everything to coat so that the prawns get nicely coated.
Divide the rice between two bowls, top with the sriracha butter prawns, sweetcorn and their sauce then scatter over a few parsley leaves and a good squeeze of lemon, to serve.

name: Sriracha Crispy Tofu
description: Coating your tofu in cornflour before you fry it is a great kitchen hack to attain an optimal level of tofu crispiness.
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Meanwhile drain the tofu and cut into cubes. Cut each broccoli stem into three pieces and the lime into four wedges. Thinly slice the spring onions if using.
Spoon the cornflour into a bowl. Season with salt and black pepper. Toss the tofu and the broccoli in the cornflour so that they get an even coating.

Get a large non-stick frying pan over a medium–high heat. Drizzle in a good glug of veg or sesame oil. In two batches fry the tofu and broccoli for 5 mins, turning regularly, until crisp and golden brown.
Put the Sriracha, maple syrup and soy into a small saucepan with 3 tbsp of water over a medium heat. Cook for 3–4 mins untilsticky and bubbling.

Divide the rice between four bowls. Top each one with the crispy tofu and broccoli then pour over the sticky Sriracha sauce. Scatter over the sesame seeds and spring onions, tear over the coriander and serve with the lime wedges.

name: Steak & Eggs with Chimichurri & Chips
description: Crispy chips, juicy steak and a punchy herby chimichurri — this is a proper treat of a dinner, and it all comes together in one pan and an air fryer. Easy.
keywords: steak & eggs with chimichurri & chips recipe
instructions: Bring the steak to room temperature.  Cook the chips in the air fryer or oven following pack instructions.

Pick the parsley leaves from their stalks and finely chop. Peel and finely chop the garlic. On the chopping board, mix the parsley, garlic, oregano and red pepper flakes together. Transfer to a bowl and stir through almost all of the olive oil and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and pepper to taste — that’s your chimichurri done.
Boil the eggs for 7 mins (for jammy centres), then run under cold water until cool enough to peel.

Meanwhile, set a heavy-duty nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Brush the steak with the remaining oil and season well with salt and pepper. Once hot, add the steak and cook for 2 to 2½ mins each side for medium-rare. Remove from the pan and leave to rest, then slice.
Dish out the chips, and the sliced steak. Cut the eggs in half, then drizzle over the chimichurri sauce to serve.

name: Steak & Peppercorn Sauce Recipe
description: This steak and peppercorn sauce recipe uses a hefty amount of black peppercorns and lashings of double cream. When frying your steaks, you want to make sure the pan is super hot as this will ensure you get a caramelised crust with pink juicy meat inside.
instructions: Take your steaks out of the fridge half an hour before you’re going to cook them.
Get a frying pan over a medium heat, scatter in the peppercorns and toast for a minute, then tip into a pestle and mortar or spice blender and roughly grind.
Finely chop the shallot and smash the garlic (still in its skin) with the back of your knife.
Put the frying pan back over a high heat. While it’s heating, drizzle the steaks with 1 tbsp olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper.

Add the steaks to the hot pan along with the bashed garlic. The steak should immediately sizzle when it touches the pan– if not, wait a little longer. Fry the steaks for 2-2 ½ mins on each side for medium rare then transfer to a plate to rest, leaving the garlic in the pan.

Take the pan off the heat and leave it to cool for a couple of minutes, then place back over a medium heat. Add a splash of oil and scrape in the shallot. Fry, stirring occasionally, until golden. Pour in the brandy and use your spoon to scrape any crusty steak bits from the base of the pan.

Once the brandy has reduced by half, pour in the stock. Bubble away for a couple of minutes until reduced by a third then add the double cream and black peppercorns. Cook, stirring well, for 1-2 minutes until the sauce has thickened slightly and the peppercorns are evenly distributed throughout.
Pour the resting juices from the steak into the sauce and season to taste, then serve the steak with the peppercorn sauce and chips, obviously.

name: Steak & Rice with Aromatic Broth
description: Subtle, light and warming, this is the perfect 20-minute beefy meal for you. Inspired by the aromatic broth you get with phở, we’ve poured it over rice and topped with caramelised beef strips.
keywords: steak and rice with aromatic broth
instructions: Thinly slice the onion and place into a bowl of ice-cold water, set aside.
Meanwhile, add the beef into a bowl with the oyster sauce, mix together and set aside.
Bash the ginger, and gently crush the cardamom pods open.

Place a saucepan onto medium-high heat. Once hot, add the star anise and cardamom, toast until fragrant, then add the ginger with a drizzle of oil. Let it simmer for a couple of seconds before pouring the broth/stock in. Let it come to a boil, then turn the heat down to low to keep it hot. Before serving, taste and season with lime juice and fish sauce.
Place a frying pan over high heat. Once hot, add the beef and cook until seared.
Share the cooked rice between bowls. Ladle in the broth, top with the steak strips, onion, coriander and chilli.

name: Steak And Guinness Pie
description: This is a proper pie. Pastry on the sides and bottom, not just the top, and loaded with meltingly tender beef in a rich Guinness gravy. You won’t find a more hearty Guinness pie recipe around or a dish that better defines “comfort food” than this. Yes, please.
instructions: Cut the beef shin into 5cm pieces, or get the butcher to do this for you. Scrape into a bowl.
Halve the onion and cut into a chunky dice, then peel the carrot and cut it into similar-sized pieces and do the same with the celery.
Scatter the beef pieces with the flour and plenty of salt and pepper, then toss to coat really well.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large lidded casserole pan set over a medium-high heat. Lay in some of the beef pieces, leaving a little gap around each so they can fry. Cook for 2 mins on each side until golden and crisp, then remove into a clean bowl. Repeat with the remaining beef pieces, adding a little more oil as you go, if needed.
Add in another drizzle of oil and add the onion, carrot and celery along with a good pinch of salt. Put on the lid and cook for 6-8 mins, stirring regularly until the onions have softened slightly.

Pour the Guinness and beef stock into the pan, spoon in the black treacle and add the bay leaves, along with the beef and any resting juices, back to the pan. Season with salt and pepper and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat to a gentle simmer, put on the lid and cook for 1 hr 30 mins.

Remove the lid and cook for a further 1 hr 30 mins, until the beef is meltingly tender and the sauce is thick. Cool completely to room temperature, then chill for at least 3 hrs. This is essential for a crisp pastry pie!
Divide the pastry into 2 pieces - a piece that uses roughly two-thirds and another that uses the remaining third. Shape into round disks, wrap and and place in the fridge for at least 30 mins.
Heat the oven to 180°C.

Remove the larger piece of pastry from the fridge and turn it out onto a lightly floured work surface. Roll it out into a 40cm circle and use it to line the base and sides of a 23cm loose-bottomed cake tin. This will leave a little overhang which will help you to seal the pie later. Tip all of the chilled beef filling into the pastry case.
Beat the egg in a small bowl, then use a pastry brush to brush the rim with the beaten egg.

Remove the remaining pastry disk from the fridge and roll out on a lightly floured work surface until half a centimetre thick and 5cm bigger than the cake tin. Carefully lift on top of the pie, pressing gently to seal around the edge. Use a small knife to cut away any overhang. Crimp the edge of the pie, then use the small knife to make a 1cm hole in the very centre of the pie, to allow steam to escape. Brush the pie really well with beaten egg.

Put onto a baking tray and into the oven for 40-45 mins until the pastry is a deep golden colour. Remove from the oven and leave to cool for at least 30 minutes (this will help it hold better), then remove the sides and cut into slices.

name: Steak Au Poivre Italiano
description: An Italian take on steak au poivre. This rich and delicious recipe is a great one to whip out for your next dinner party.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.

Start by cutting the potatoes into chips and adding to a large saucepan. Cover with cold water and season generously with salt. Set over a medium heat and allow to blip away for 8-10 mins until tender. Carefully drain, and allow to air dry for 5 mins. Add a tray filled with olive oil into the oven to preheat. Once hot, remove from the oven, add the chips and toss to coat. Season with salt and slide into the oven for 30-35 mins.

Now, roughly chop the peppers and finely dice the shallots. Set a frying pan over a medium-low heat and toast off the black peppercorns. Roughly crush with a pestle and mortar, spice grinder or under a saucepan. Set aside.
Pour the beef stock into a small saucepan and set over a low heat to warm up. Once your chips are ready, pull them out the oven and keep warm on the side.

Season the steaks with salt and more pepper. Preheat a large frying pan over a high heat. Add a shot of olive oil and cook the steaks (working in batches if you need to) for a couple of mins on each side, until cooked to your liking.

Remove from the pan and onto a plate, cover loosely with foil to keep warm. In the residual beef fat, cook off the shallots and peppers with the remaining rosemary for 3-4 mins with a pinch of salt. Add your black pepper and beef stock. Reduce over a high heat until sticky and glossy. Finish with the balsamic vinegar.
Toss the rocket with Parmesan, olive oil and lemon juice.
Carve the steaks and serve with the rosemary chips, your pepper balsamic sauce and rocket salad.

name: Steak Fajitas With Coriander Crema
description:
Fajita Fridays just got an upgrade! Here, strips of sirloin steak, charred peppers and caramelised onions come together with a coriander crema and avo slices.

In Partnership With Aldi. #ad
instructions: Pat the sirloin steaks dry and chuck onto a tray. Mix the coffee and paprika and generously scatter over the steaks. Season with salt and set aside for 5 mins while you prep the veggies.
Cut the peppers into 1cm strips and slice the red onions.

Heat a heavy frying pan over a high heat. Add a shot of olive oil and add the steaks. Cook for 2 mins on each side until charred and caramelised. Pull out of the pan onto a plate and let rest for 5 mins.

With the pan still on high heat, add the veggies and cook with a big pinch of salt for 4-5 mins or until softened and they’ve taken on some colour. Season with the Mexican Barbacoa seasoning and tip onto the plate with the steak.
Add the coriander to a mini chopper with the sour cream and half the feta, whizz until you’ve got a chunky crema. Season with salt to taste. Slice the avocado and lime wedges.
Slice the steaks and mix through the peppers and onions.

Warm the tortilla wraps in a dry pan or microwave and lay out onto a plate. If you want to serve the steak on a sizzling platter. Grab a pan and get it very hot on the stove. Tip the steak and pepper mix into the hot pan (don’t add any oil). Once the steak has started sizzling, add 2 tbsp of water and let it sizzle.
Serve everything family-style on the table for people to build their own fajitas!

name: Steak Salad with Roasted Pepper Chimichurri and Garlic Croutons
description: A salad with substance, delicious and fresh, topped with seared steak, charred spring onions and a punchy dressing.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
Remove the steak from the fridge, season with salt and leave to come up to room temperature (this usually takes about an hour).

Start by mixing the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, white wine vinegar and Parmesan in a bowl. Add the yoghurt, a big pinch of salt and grate in half of the clove of garlic. Finely chop and add ¾ of the chives, mix again and set aside.
Remove the stems from the lettuce, wash and add to a large bowl. Drain the peppers, reserve one for later and chop the rest lengthways into roughly 1 inch wide strips, add to the lettuce.
Add the reserved pepper, coriander, anchovies, chilli and half a lime's worth of lime juice to a blender with a pinch of salt and pulse until coarsely chopped. Set aside.

In a heavy pan over a high heat, cook the spring onions until charred all over and softened, about 5 mins. Add to a small bowl with the remaining lime juice, tbsp of honey and a pinch of salt, mix and set aside.
Return the pan to a high heat and sear the steak for about 1.5 minutes on each side, until medium rare.
Allow the steak to rest and cool. Meanwhile, remove the crusts from the bread and cut into roughly 1 inch cubes.

Add to an oven dish, toss well with a drizzle of olive oil and a big pinch of salt, then bake until golden brown, about 6 mins. Remove from the oven, grate in the remaining half a clove of garlic and mix well.

Toss the lettuce and peppers with the yoghurt dressing. Add the steak and croutons, mix again, then layer up onto a platter. Finish with the charred spring onions, remaining chives and drizzle over the chimichurri.

name: Steak Som Tam(ish) Salad
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This som tam-inspired salad is packed with fresh and fragrant ingredients. Cooking your steak to a ruby red medium rare will ensure the tastiest outcome.
instructions: Take the steaks out of the fridge and let them come to room temperature. Finely dice the shallots and thinly slice one of the chillies. Roughly chop the peanuts. Set everything aside.

Grab a pestle and mortar and add the garlic and sugar to the mortar. Crush to a smooth paste. Roughly chop the remaining chilli and add to the mortar, then lightly crush. Add the soy sauce and the juice of one lime. Stir the dressing and have a taste – it should be salty, sour, spicy and sweet.

For the salad, cut the carrots and apple into matchsticks, thinly shred the cabbage, chop the cooked beans into 4cm lengths and quarter the cherry tomatoes. Combine everything in a large bowl, along with the mint and basil leaves.

Season the steaks with salt and pepper. Heat a frying pan over a high heat and add a shot of olive oil. Cook the steaks for 2 mins on either side until brown and caramelised. We’re shooting for a rare steak here.
Remove the steaks from the pan and add the diced shallots and sliced chilli. Turn off the heat and add a splash of water and half of the dressing. Swirl together and add half of the peanuts.

Toss the remaining dressing with the salad. Divide the salad between serving plates and top with the remaining peanuts. Cut the remaining limes into wedges and serve with the salad. Carve the steaks into thin slices and serve topped with the pan sauce.
Get stuck in.

name: Steak Summer Bowl With Spicy Pico De Gallo
description: Treat yourself to perfectly cooked steak on a bed of brown rice, with a creamy herby dressing, spoonful of pico de gallo and a sprinkling of pumpkin seeds.
instructions: Remove the steak from the fridge and let it come to room temperature. Place a saucepan full of water to the boil. Once boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook until very soft, 5 mins. Drain and run under cold water until cool to the touch. Remove the shell and place the eggs into a blender with the parsley, the zest of 1 lemon and 20ml of olive oil. Blend until smooth, season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Add a spoonful of water to loosen.
Meanwhile, finely dice onion, drain and thinly slice the peppers. Add 2 tbsp of onion into a small bowl, then tip the rest into a large bowl with the peppers and rice and cooked lentils.
Dice the tomatoes, mince the jalapeños, and finely chop the coriander. Add into the onions, season with salt, pepper, lemon juice and 2 tbsp of olive oil.
Place a frying pan on a medium-high heat, season the steak with salt and pepper, and rub oil over it. Cook the steak on each side until seared. Let rest for 5 mins.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to package instructions and tip into the peppers. Slice the steak against the grain.
Share the rice between bowls, top with the steak, a drizzle of creamy herby dressing, a spoonful of pico de gallo and some pumpkin seeds.

name: Steak Tacos With Chilli Pineapple Salsa
description: Steak frites is all well and good but these steak tacos might are the most delicious vessel for bavette we've found. The sweet and spicy salsa brings it home.
keywords: Steak Tacos With Chilli Pineapple Salsa
instructions: Roughly chop 3/4 of the garlic cloves and lob them into a bowl. Finely cut the coriander and add half to the bowl with the garlic. Cover with 4 tbsp of oil and the juice and zest of a lime. Season the steaks with salt and pepper and drop into the marinade. Leave for 30 mins or up to overnight.

While the steaks are marinating, make the pineapple salsa. Cut the pineapple into a fine dice. Now toast the peanuts and sesame seeds in a dry pan. Add the pineapple, peanuts and sesame seeds to a bowl. Add the chilli oil and a good whack of lime juice.

Fish the steaks out of the marinade and preheat a heavy frying pan over a high heat. When smoking hot, add a shot of oil and get the steaks in. Cook for 2-3 mins a side until charred and caramelised. Don’t be afraid of burning some of the marinade. Let the steaks rest for 5 mins.
Whack the avocados into a blender with the sour cream, remaining garlic cloves, coriander, and a squeeze of lime juice. Season and blend until smooth. Finely dice up your shallots.

Heat up your tortillas in a dry pan or over an open flame. Cut the steak into 2cm chunks and toss through any resting juices. Load up the tacos with avocado crema, the steak, fresh cut jalapeños, diced shallots, and the pineapple chilli salsa.
Get stuck in.

name: Steak Tacos with Burnt Tomato Salsa
description: Ugo Monye teaches us how to make the perfect burnt tomato salsa with Bull’s-Eye Kentucky Habanero Hot Sauce.
instructions: Chop your tomato in half and cut the flesh of the red pepper. Peel the garlic cloves and chop 2 limes in half and the other lime in quarters.

Using tongs pop your tomatoes, garlic, red pepper and spring onions onto the flame of the hob charring on all sides until blackened, about 3 -5 mins. You can also use a blowtorch or pop them under a very hot grill.
Thinly slice the red onion and squeeze over the juice of a lime and a pinch of salt. Mix well and allow to quickly pickle on the side.

Pop the garlic and spring onions into a mortar and pestle with a big pinch of flakey sea salt and bash for 5 mins until almost smooth. Add in the red pepper and bash to a paste and then add the tomatoes and continue bashing to form a slightly chunky salsa. Optionally you could blend in a food processor, but the results won’t be as fresh.
Squeeze in the juice of a lime, the Bull’s-Eye Kentucky Habanero Hot Sauce and season with more salt if required.
Combine 1 tsp salt, cumin, chilli powder and oregano in a bowl. Rub this onto the steaks and heat up a cast-iron skillet until smoking hot.
Add a glug of oil and then the steaks. Cook for 3 mins on either side, don’t move the steak whilst it’s on the pan to form a thick crust. Allow the steaks to rest on a chopping board for 5 mins.
Once rested, slice thinly against the grain of the meat. Sprinkle on a pinch of salt and toss with the resting juices.
Wipe the cast iron pan clean with a paper towel and heat to a high heat. Heat up each tortilla until golden and keep warm in a tea towel.
Assemble the tacos with first the beef, then the salsa, crumbled feta, pickled red onion, fresh coriander, and finally a squeeze of lime. Enjoy.

name: Steak With Gremolata & Radicchio Salad
description: Quick, deceptively easy but super impressive - the steak, bitter radicchio salad, hazelnuts and gremolata go together perfectly.
instructions: Preheat your oven to fan 180°C. Pull your steak out of the fridge about an hour before you want to cook it. Season with plenty of flaky salt and rub with a dash of olive oil.
Place the hazelnuts onto a small baking tray and roast for 10-15 mins, until golden and toasted. Then, roughly chop.

Meanwhile, pick the leaves off ⅓ of the parsley and finely chop the rest. Finely grate the garlic, zest 1 lemon. Add the anchovy fillets into a bowl with the garlic and mash until a paste forms. Add the chopped parsley, lemon zest, chilli flakes and 100ml of olive oil. Stir together and season with lemon juice, salt and pepper, set aside.

Add the mustard and honey into another bowl with the juice of 1 lemon. Stir through 40ml of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Trim the radicchio and pick the leaves apart, chop any large leaves in half. Roughly chop the hazelnuts.

Get a frying pan on a high heat. For medium-rare, lay your steaks into the hot pan and cook for 1 min, flip the steak over, add the butter and let it turn brown, baste the steak in the butter and transfer it onto a plate. Let rest for 5 mins.
When the steak is resting, add the radicchio, toasted hazelnuts and parsley leaves to the honey and mustard dressing, toss together until coated.
Slice the steak and serve with a drizzle of gremolata. Finish the salad with a shaving of parmesan.

name: Steak With Roasted Peppers, Chickpeas & Feta
description: Cooking the perfect steak isn't daunting at all. Here's a simple and summery steak recipe.
instructions: A few hours before you want to eat, put the steaks onto a plate and salt them liberally. Transfer to the fridge, uncovered.

Heat the oven to 190°C. Halve the peppers, then cut out and discard the stalks and seeds. Cut each half in half. Remove the onion skins and, leaving the roots intact, half each onion and then cut into wedges.
Toss the peppers and onions in a large baking dish, then drizzle over olive oil and add a good pinch of salt. Give it a mix to coat the peppers, then pop them in the oven and roast for 25 mins.
Remove the steaks from the fridge, pat them dry with kitchen paper and leave to come up to room temperature.
Drain the chickpeas in a colander, rinse under cold water and pat dry with kitchen paper.
Tip the chickpeas and cherry tomatoes on top of the roasted onions and peppers, then sprinkle over the paprika and cumin. Return to the oven for 15 mins.
Pour the chicken stock into the dish and return to the oven for 5 mins.

Meanwhile, set a heavy duty frying pan over a very high heat until it’s screaming hot. Add the steaks to the pan and cook for 2 mins each side. Remove and rest for 15 mins on top of the chickpea mixture.
Transfer the steaks to a chopping board and carve into slices.
Spoon your saucy peppers and chickpeas onto serving plates and crumble over the feta. Place your steak on top, then sprinkle with parsley leaves. Serve.

name: Steak and Ale Pie
description: The greatest pie of all time. Melt-in-the-mouth beef cooked slowly in a rich ale gravy will never cease to warm your cockles.
instructions: Heat your oven to 150°C.
Finely chop your onion and carrots.
Heat a casserole dish over a low heat. Add a little olive oil, then tip in your bacon lardons. Fry for a few mins until the fat has rendered out and they are starting to crisp up.
Add your diced onion and carrot to the pan and cook for 15 mins until softened.
Meanwhile, brown your beef. Start by placing your flour in a large bowl and seasoning generously with salt and pepper. Add your beef and mix so that the flour totally coats all the pieces.

Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a little olive oil. Brown your beef in batches for a minute or two on all sides until there is lots of caramelisation. Remove from the pan, and repeat with your remaining beef.
Pick your thyme leaves off their stalks and add these to the pan along with your tomato purée. Cook out for 5 mins until your puree has darkened.
Add your beef to the veg pan along with your stock and ale. Bring the whole mixture to a simmer, then pop on a lid and place in the oven to cook for 2 and a half hours.
Halve your button mushrooms.
Remove your pan from the oven. Add your button mushrooms, then pop the lid back on. Cook for another hour.
At this point, your beef should be tender and your sauce lovely and thick. Add your Worcestershire sauce, then season to taste with salt and pepper. Allow your pie filling to cool.
Heat your oven to 200°C.
Roll out your pastry to 2mm thickness.
Spoon your beef into a pie dish, then add your pastry on top. Crimp the edges, then brush the surface with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 mins until well risen and golden.
Serve with mash and greens.

name: Steak with Thai Red Tomatoes
description: We like to serve this spicy steak with a massive green salad and loads of bread for mopping up the sauce. It's impressive without being stupidly high effort.
instructions: Set the steak aside for 10-15 mins to come up to room temperature. Heat the oven to 200°C. Tip the tomatoes into the roasting tin, season with salt and pepper. Drizzle with olive oil and slide into the oven for around 15-20 mins.

Meanwhile, cook the steak. Rub the steak in a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place a large nonstick frying pan over a high heat, add the steak and cook for 4-5 mins, flip over and add the butter to the pan. Spoon the butter over the steak while you fry for 3-4 mins further – this will be medium rare, if you’d like it to be more well done, cook for a little longer on each side. Set aside on a plate to rest.

Return the pan to a medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil along with the Thai red curry paste. Peel and finely slice the garlic and add to the pan. Sizzle for 3-4 mins, then add the juice from the tray of tomatoes, cook for a min then add the rest of the tomatoes. Bubble for 2-3 mins and set aside.

Cut the steak away from the T-bone and slice horizontally. Lay the steak slices on a large plate, spoon the tomatoes over the top, drizzle with a little olive oil and scatter with basil leaves. Finish with a crack of black pepper and the lime, cut into wedges on the side.

name: Steak, Watermelon & Peanut Salad
description: A true summer banger. Zingy, fresh, a bit salty, sweet and sour with some chilli heat. This sally is a belter, you’re gonna love it.
instructions:
Get a large frying pan searing hot – this will take a couple of
minutes over a super high heat. Meanwhile, cut the limes in half.
Thinly slice the red chilli and roughly chop the peanuts. Scrape
the chilli and peanuts into a small mixing bowl and set aside.
Season the steaks liberally with black pepper on both sides.
Drizzle some oil into the frying pan and, once sizzling, add the
steaks. Fry for 2 mins on each side.
Dressing time. Crush the unpeeled garlic clove into a large mixing
bowl. Add the fish sauce, soy sauce, light brown sugar and a
splash of neutral oil. Squeeze in the juice from the halves of one
lime. Whisk together with a fork.
Once the steaks are cooked, transfer them to the chopping board
and leave to rest while you assemble the salad.
Separate the baby gem lettuces into leaves straight into the bowl
of salad dressing. Toss together, then tip out onto a large platter.
Scatter over the watermelon chunks.
Thinly slice the steaks, then lay the slices over the salad. Squeeze
