over the juice of the remaining lime halves. Scatter over the
chopped chilli and peanuts to finish. Serve at the table and let
people help themselves.

name: Steamed Chicken Rice Bowl with Peanut & Sesame
description: The easiest, most delicious healthy dinner you can make in 30 minutes. Perfect when you can’t be bothered to cook but want something satisfying.
keywords: Steamed Chicken Rice Bowl with Peanut Sesame Dressing
Steamed Chicken Rice Bowl with Peanut Sesame Dressing recipe
instructions: Wash the brown rice thoroughly in cold water then drain and transfer to the bottom of the steamer. Add cold water at a ratio of 2:1 water to rice.
Thinly slice the chilli, ginger and spring onions.
Pop the top of the steamer on the base. Put the chicken breasts in the top of the steamer then season them generously with sea salt. Scatter over the chilli, ginger and spring onions.
Cover with a lid and set the steamer over a medium heat. Once the water is boiling, reduce the heat to low-medium and steam for 20 mins until the chicken is cooked through.

Meanwhile, make the peanut sesame dressing. Into a bowl, add the tahini, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, toasted sesame seeds, salted peanuts and the juice of the lemon. Stir with a spoon to combine. If it's too thick, add a splash of water to loosen it.
Transfer the cooked chicken to a plate. Cover the steamer with a lid again and leave over a medium heat for another 3 mins to finish cooking the brown rice.
Finely chop the coriander. Slice up the chicken breast.
Once the rice is cooked, season it generously with sea salt and fluff it with a fork.

To serve, divide the warm rice between bowls and top with the sliced chicken breast and the chilli, ginger and spring onions. Drizzle over the peanut sesame dressing and scatter over the sesame seeds, fresh coriander and an extra drizzle of soy sauce.

name: Steamed Cod with Spring Onion & Ginger
description: Steamed fish is a classic in Chinese households. Seasoned with a spring onion and ginger oil, this dish is not only delicious but also nutritious, making it a perfect weeknight staple.
keywords: Steamed Cod with Spring Onion & Ginger
Steamed Cod with Spring Onion & Ginger recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the ginger for the fish. Wash the cod loins, then pat dry and season both sides of the fish with ¼ tsp white pepper. Place on a heatproof plate with the sliced ginger.

To prepare your steaming set up, fill a wok with 3cm water and place a heatproof bowl upside down in the pan. Bring to the boil then turn the heat to low-medium, and place the heatproof plate with the cod on top of the upside-down bowl. Cover with a lid and steam for 7-9 mins until cooked through.
Meanwhile, for the spring onion ginger oil, chop the spring onions into 4cm pieces and slice lengthways, separating the whites and greens. Thinly slice the ginger and roughly chop the coriander.

Heat the vegetable oil in a separate pan set over a low-medium heat. Add the ginger and spring onion whites. Fry for just under a minute, then add the spring onion greens and coriander. Add the soy sauce and sesame oil and fry for just 30 seconds.
Reheat the rice then divide between plates.
Top the rice with the cod, then pour over the spring onion, ginger and coriander oil. Finish with a drizzle of chilli oil.

name: Steamed Fish & Rice With Green Chilli Oil
description: The weeknight dinner you've been needing. A balanced bowl of steamed fish, coconut rice and tangy green chilli oil. Tuck in.
instructions: Start by finely chopping your coriander and set aside for later.

Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear. Add it to a small saucepan along with 200ml of water and a tin of coconut milk. Bring to the boil, then cover with a lid, turn the heat down and simmer for 10 mins. Remove from the heat and let it sit until you’re ready to serve.
Get a pan of water on and pop in the tenderstem and fish. Steam for 5 mins, until the fish is cooked through and tenderstem is al dente.
To the rice, add the juice of ½ a lime and season well with salt. Fluff up with a fork to mix.
Serve up on a plate topped with finely chopped coriander and drizzle with green chilli oil.

name: Steamed Salmon Rice Bowl with Chilli & Ginger
description: A simple steamed supper with tender salmon and fluffy rice. We’re obsessed with this cooking method. It’s healthy, delicious and requires basically zero effort.
keywords: Steamed Salmon Rice Bowl with Chilli & Ginger
Steamed Salmon Rice Bowl with Chilli & Ginger recipe
instructions: Wash the rice thoroughly in cold water then drain and transfer to the bottom of the steamer. Add cold water at a ratio of 2:1 water to rice.
Thinly slice the ginger and scotch bonnet.
Pop the top of the steamer on the base. Put the salmon fillets in the top of the steamer then scatter over the sliced ginger and scotch bonnet.

Cover the steamer with a lid and set it over a medium heat. Once the water is boiling, reduce the heat to low-medium and steam for 13 mins, then remove from the heat and set aside, with the lid on, for another 5 mins to finish cooking. The salmon will steam in the time it takes for the rice to cook.
Meanwhile, finely chop the fresh coriander.
To the cooked rice, add a generous pinch of sea salt and the rice vinegar then fluff with a fork.

To serve, divide the rice between plates and top with the salmon, ginger and scotch bonnet. Drizzle over the soy sauce and sesame oil and finish with a big handful of chopped coriander, toasted sesame seeds and some chilli oil.

name: Steamed Tofu With Chilli Oil
description: Steamed tofu isn’t talked about enough and it’s one of the easiest and speediest meals out there. I used to make this dish at uni quite often when I was in a rush. It only takes 10 minutes to make, and if you have any leftover rice (which I often do) serve it up with that and some of Mama Yu’s Chilli Oil on top. Perfect, easy dinner.
keywords: Steamed Tofu With Chilli Oil recipe
instructions: Grab your tofu and carefully cut along the edge of the packaging. If there’s excess liquid, carefully drain over the sink. Place a plate over the open end of the tofu container, then carefully flip. Cut small holes in all four diagonal corners to let air in, then slowly release the tofu from the packaging.

To prepare your steaming set up, fill a wok with 3cm water and bring to the boil. Turn the heat to low-medium, place the tofu on a heatproof plate and slice into 1 ½ cm pieces, cover with a lid and steam for 6 mins.
Meanwhile, mince the garlic and finely slice the spring onions and chillies. Roughly chop the coriander. Add the minced garlic and spring onion whites to a heatproof bowl.

Pour a glug of vegetable oil into a pot set over medium-high heat. When the oil starts to lightly smoke, add it to the heatproof bowl with the garlic and spring onion. Add the spring onion greens, chillies, coriander, remaining seasonings and sauces, and mix well.
Serve the tofu with some crushed peanuts, crispy shallots and chilli oil (and leftover rice if you have any). Enjoy!

name: Steamed Veg Spelt Bowl with Harissa Tahini Dressing
description: A simple steamed supper that's packed with plant-based goodness and couldn't be easier to make.
keywords: Steamed Veg Spelt Bowl with Harissa Tahini Dressing
Steamed Veg Spelt Bowl with Harissa Tahini Dressing Recipe
instructions: Wash the spelt thoroughly in cold water then drain and transfer to the bottom of the steamer. Add cold water at a ratio of 2:1 water to spelt.
Set the steamer over a medium heat and bring to a boil then cook, uncovered, for 40 mins.
While the spelt is cooking, chop the courgette, red pepper and yellow pepper into 2cm chunks.
For the dressing, combine the tahini, harissa, juice of the lemon, honey and olive oil in a mixing bowl. Slowly mix in enough warm water to achieve a creamy drizzling consistency.

When the 40 mins of spelt cooking time is up, pop the top of the steamer over the base. Add the courgette, peppers and kale to the top of the steamer then cover with a lid and steam for 10 mins until the veggies and spelt are tender.
Meanwhile, finely chop the parsley and dill.

Remove the steamer from the heat. Season the spelt generously with sea salt then transfer to a large mixing bowl along with the veggies and most of the sauce, saving an extra drizzle of sauce for the top.
To serve, divide the spelt and veggies between bowls and top with the remaining sauce, the chopped herbs and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Stewed Saltfish, Plantain & Coconut Dumplings
description: Savoury and sweet. Here’s a stewed saltfish, dumplings and plantain recipe from Chef Kevin Jones inspired by the beautiful islands of St. Kitts and Nevis.
instructions: Place the salt fish in a medium size pot, with enough water just to cover it. Then bring to a boil for 10 mins. Drain and repeat. Allow the saltfish to cool enough to handle, then flake with a fork removing any bones. Set aside.
Dice the onion, green pepper and red pepper. Finely chop the garlic and stab a hole in the scotch bonnet, but leave it whole. Pick the thyme leaves from the stems.
Heat a large saucepan with oil over medium heat. Add onion, thyme, garlic, scotch bonnet and peppers with a pinch of salt. Cook for 7-8 mins or until the onions are translucent.

Add the flaked saltfish, diced tomatoes, tomato purée and seasonings. Cook for 25 mins on low heat with a lid until tomatoes are super soft. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Finely slice the spring onions and sprinkle over top. Set aside and keep warm.

To make the dumplings, tip the flour, coconut, cornmeal, and salt into a bowl and mix thoroughly. Add in 180ml of water while gradually mixing, to form a shaggy dough. Tip onto a clean surface and knead the dough for 10 mins.

Cover the bowl with a cloth and Allow dough to rest for 10 mins. Pull the dough apart forming a golf ball size shape. Roll each piece into a ball, and flatten the middle with your thumb. You want these around 4-5cm thick.
Bring a pan of water to a boil. Place the dumplings into the boiling water and boil for 20 mins and cook until they start to float.

name: Sticky & Spicy Roasted Roots
description: Carrots and parsnips tossed in sweet, sticky, and spicy glaze. Christmas dinner sides don't get much better than this.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.

Slice the rest of the carrots in half lengthways, leaving any smaller ones whole. Slice any large parsnips in half lengthways. Pile into a large roasting tray in a single layer (split between two trays if you need to!) Season, then add in a big splash of water before covering the tray with foil and slide into the oven for 15 mins.

Meanwhile, make the glaze. Mix the balsamic with the honey with 2 tbsp olive oil. Add the cumin seeds and red pepper flakes and season well. Remove the roasting tray from the oven, remove the foil, then toss in the glaze over the veg. Slide back into the oven and cook for 30 mins, tossing regularly, until sticky and golden. If you want them a little more charred, turn on the grill for the last 10 mins.
Spoon onto a platter. Scatter with toasted sesame seeds, parsley, and then finish with a little olive oil and a pinch of red pepper flakes.

name: Sticky Air Fryer Gochujang Aubergine & Sausages
description: We all know that sausage and gochujang pasta is a winning combo, but this time why don't you chuck in the air fryer and see what happens?
instructions: Halve the aubergines lengthwise, then cut into 2cm thick pieces on a diagonal. Add the gochujang, honey, soy sauce and rice wine vinegar to a large bowl and grate in the garlic. Toss in the aubergine.
Halve the cucumber lengthwise and scoop out the seeds before finely slicing. Add to a bowl along with the kimchi and set aside. Finely slice the spring onions.

Add the aubergines to the air fryer and top with the sausages. Heat to 185C and cook for 5 minutes, then turn the sausages and air fry again for 5 mins. Take the sausages out of the machine and slice on a diagonal, then add them back into the basket and cook for a further 5-15 mins or until everything is cooked through and sticky.
If using a pouch of rice, heat according to package instructions. If using pre-cooked rice, heat until piping hot.
Serve up the rice along with the sticky aubergines and sausages. Add the kimchi salad and spring onions before scattering with the sesame seeds.

name: Sticky Aubergine & Miso Mash
description: Miso butterbean mash is the perfect pillowy base for a sweet, spicy, saucy and sticky aubergine topping. It's got all the elements of a perfect meal.
instructions: Mince or chop the garlic. Thinly slice the spring onions and separate the green tops from the whites. Thinly slice the peppers. Chop the aubergine into 1cm cubes. Thinly slice the chilli.

Add 2/3 of the sunflower oil to a large frying pan on medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine cubes for about 4-5 mins on high until starting to brown, season well with salt and pepper. Add the pepper and fry for another 6-8 mins until the aubergine is browned and crispy on all sides and the pepper is nicely charred. Add more oil as you need to make sure the vegetables get brown and caramelised.
Remove the vegetables from the pan and set them aside in a bowl.

Add the remaining oil to the pan and turn it down to medium. Add the fresh chilli and dried chilli (if using) along with your spring onion whites and garlic. Fry for about 3 mins until starting to crisp up. Add the ketchup, soy sauce, maple syrup and stir for 30 seconds to cook and combine the sauce. Add the vegetables and sesame seeds into the pan and fry for another 2 mins until well coated. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
For the miso butter bean mash, drain the beans and add them to a blender with the miso and oat/soy milk. Blend until almost smooth.
Heat the butter in a pot over low heat. Add the butter bean mash to the pot and stir until the mash and butter have combined and the mixture has heated through.
To plate, spread the mash over two plates and top with the sticky aubergine. Finish with the remaining spring onion greens and some chopped roasted peanuts, if you like.

name: Sticky Aubergine Rice Bowl
description: Sticky, sweet and spicy - this aubergine rice bowl’s packed with veg, full of flavour and makes a top-tier lunch box.
keywords: Lunch Box: Sticky Aubergine Rice Bowl recipe
Lunch Box: Sticky Aubergine Rice Bowl
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Slice the aubergines into batons and whack them in a colander.
Salt and leave for 5 mins to extract the water. After 5 mins, pat
dry and get them onto a baking tray. Drizzle with oil and place in the oven for 30 mins.
While your aubergine is roasting, prep your veg. Thinly slice the
spring onions, red cabbage, garlic, ginger and red chillies.
Grab two bowls. Add the spring onions to one and the red
cabbage to the other. Cover the spring onions with the juice of
the lime, a third of the rice vinegar and a sprinkling of salt.
Over the red cabbage pour another third of the rice vinegar,
half the sesame oil and a sprinkle of salt and mix it
through. Cover and place both in the fridge.
Rinse the sushi rice, then add to a saucepan with just enough
water to cover. Leave for 30 mins to soak.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a wok or large frying
pan and add the garlic, ginger and red chillies and fry over a low
heat. Once softened, add the hoisin sauce, soy sauce, sesame seeds, agave, veggie stock cube, chilli oil and the remaining sesame oil and rice vinegar. Give
everything a good mix together, then add the aubergine straight
from the oven.
Add enough water to just cover the aubergine and leave to
simmer until it has reduced into a lovely thick sauce. Stir often.
Drain the rice and add it to a saucepan with 480ml water (if you're adjusting the servings, use a ratio of one part rice to one and a half parts water) and the shichimi. Bring to the boil, then turn to a simmer, cover
with the lid and simmer until cooked, about 15 mins.
Time to build your lunch boxes. Divide the sushi rice between your Tupperware containers. Add a
generous dollop of aubergine sauce, a helping of marinated red
cabbage and some sliced avocado. Garnish with the spring onions,
the crispy chilli bits from the chilli oil and some more sesame seeds. 
Leave to cool, then box up and pop in the fridge ready for lunchtime. These will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Sticky Aubergine Rice Bowl
description: This is a recipe is the Holy Trinity of sticky, sweet and spicy. Give it a go, Mob, you won’t regret it. Plus the variety of veg gives a great kick of fibre.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Slice the aubergines into batons and whack them in a colander.
Salt and leave for 5 mins to extract the water. After 5 mins, pat
dry and get them onto a baking tray. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon of
the vegetable oil and place in the oven for 30 mins.
While your aubergine is roasting, prep your veg. Thinly slice the
spring onions, red cabbage, garlic, ginger and red chillies.
Grab two bowls. Add the spring onions to one and the red
cabbage to the other. Cover the spring onions with the juice of
the lime, 1 tbsp of the rice vinegar and a sprinkling of salt.
Over the red cabbage pour another tablespoon of rice vinegar,
1⁄2 tbsp of the sesame oil and a sprinkle of salt and mix it
through. Cover and place both in the fridge.
Rinse the sushi rice, then add to a saucepan with just enough
water to cover. Leave for 30 mins to soak.
Heat the remaining 1⁄2 tbsp of oil in a wok or large frying
pan and add the garlic, ginger and red chillies and fry over a low
heat. Once softened, add the hoisin sauce, soy sauce, the remaining
1⁄2 tbsp of sesame oil and 1 tbsp of rice vinegar, the chilli oil, sesame seeds, agave and veggie stock cube. Give
everything a good mix together, then add the aubergine straight
from the oven.
Add enough water to just cover the aubergine and leave to
simmer until it has reduced into a lovely thick sauce. Stir often.
Drain the rice and add it to a saucepan with 480ml water
and the shichimi. Bring to the boil, then turn to a simmer, cover
with the lid and simmer until cooked, about 15 mins.
Time to plate up. First, make a bed of your sushi rice. Add a
generous dollop of aubergine sauce, a helping of marinated red
cabbage and some sliced avocado. Garnish with the spring onions,
the crispy chilli bits from the chilli oil and some more sesame seeds
and tuck in.

name: Sticky Aubergine Sesame Rice Bowl
description: This is another lockdown dish I have been loving. It's the Holy Trinity of sticky, sweet and spicy. Give it a go MOB, you won't regret it. Ben x
instructions: Preheat your oven to 170°C/325°F.
Slice your aubergines into batons and whack them in a colander. Salt and leave for 5 mins to extract the water.
After 5 mins, pat dry and get them onto a baking tray. Drizzle with vegetable oil and place in the oven for 30 mins.
While your aubergine is roasting, it's time to prep your veg. Finely slice your spring onions, red cabbage, garlic, ginger and red chillies.

Grab 2 bowls. Add your spring onions to one and your red cabbage to the other. Cover your spring onions with the juice of your lime, 1 tbsp of your rice vinegar and a sprinkling of salt. Over your red cabbage pour 1 tbsp of your rice vinegar, 1 tbsp of your sesame oil and salt and mix it through. Cover and place both in the fridge.
Rinse your sushi rice then add to a pan with just enough water to cover for 30 mins to soak.

Into a wok add your garlic, ginger and red chillies with a bit of oil and fry on a low heat. Once softened, add your hoisin sauce, soy sauce, your remaining sesame oil and rice vinegar, chilli oil, sesame seeds, agave and a veggie stock cube.
Give everything a good mix together then add your aubergine straight from the oven.
Add enough water into the wok to just cover your aubergine and leave to simmer until it has reduced into a lovely thick sauce. Remember to stir every now and then so it doesn't stick to the bottom.
Rice time. Drain your rice and add it into a saucepan with 540ml of water and your shichimi. Bring to a boil then turn down to a simmer and place the lid on until cooked.

Time to plate up. First, make a bed of your sushi rice. Add a generous dollop of your aubergine sauce, a helping of your marinated red cabbage and some sliced avocado. Garnish with your spring onions, shichimi, crispy chilli bits and some more sesame seeds and tuck in. Enjoy!

name: Sticky Aubergine Vegan Ramen Recipe
description: Dive into a bowl of comfort with this Sticky Aubergine Vegan Ramen Recipe, a savoury delight for those craving a plant-based twist on a classic. This vegan ramen combines tender ramen noodles with caramelised aubergine, creating a rich, umami-packed broth that’s perfect for a cosy meal. The sticky aubergine is glazed with a blend of soy sauce, chilli oil, and garlic sauce, infusing each bite with deep, satisfying flavour. Ideal for any time of year, this vegan ramen recipe is not only delicious but also versatile—swap in your favourite vegetables or plant-based proteins to suit your taste. Whether you’re new to Japanese noodle soup or a seasoned fan, this recipe will surely become a staple. Enjoy it as a hearty lunch or a comforting dinner; this ramen will warm your soul and tantalise your taste buds.
instructions: Halve and thinly slice the onion, peel and roughly chop the garlic, then peel the ginger and slice.

Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large saucepan over a high heat. Once smoking hot, scatter in the onion, garlic and ginger, add a pinch of salt and cook for 5 mins, stirring regularly, until lightly charred and softening.
Lower the heat and carefully pour in the vegetable stock (it might spatter a bit). Add the dried shiitake mushrooms and miso and leave to gently simmer for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, cut the cabbage into quarters, then use a speed or potato peeler to very thinly shred the cabbage into a bowl. Add a pinch of salt, the sugar and rice vinegar, then mix well.

Cut the aubergine into 3cm cubes and cut the mushrooms into thick slices. Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with ½ tbsp oil, then fry the aubergine with a pinch of salt for 4-5 mins until charred and crisp. Remove to a plate, then drizzle over ½ tbsp oil. Cook the mushrooms in the same way, then set both the aubergine and mushrooms aside.
Mix the teriyaki sauce with 100ml water and pour into the broth pan. Turn the heat to medium and bubble away for 5-7 mins until thickened and saucy.
Meanwhile, cook the noodle nests in a big pan of salted water following pack instructions, then drain.

Divide the ramen broth between four bowls, then add the noodles. Top each bowl with a pile of the aubergine and mushrooms, then a pile of cabbage. To serve, sprinkle over some sesame seeds and finish with chilli oil.

name: Sticky Aubergine With Roasted Garlic Yoghurt
description: We've coated aubergine in a sticky honey glaze and paired it with a herby, green sauce spiked with chilli and topped it with smoked almonds. Delish.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220ºC. Slice the aubergines in half lengthways, then slice each in half again into 3 long wedges, tip onto a baking tray and sprinkle with salt. Wrap the garlic bulb in foil and snuggle onto the tray. Bake for 30-40 mins.

Meanwhile, make the green sauce by either blitzing or finely chopping the green chilli and herbs, saving a few herbs for the top. Add the juice of the lemon and enough olive oil to make it a drizzle-able consistency. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Whisk the ingredients for the glaze together in a large bowl with 4 tbsp of olive oil, season well. Tip the yoghurt into a separate bowl.

Once the aubergine is charred and soft, remove the garlic from the tray and tip the aubergine into the glaze bowl. Toss well until sticky and coated. Drain the chickpeas and add to the baking tray the aubergine was on, toss with a tbsp of olive oil and return to the oven for 10 mins.
Cut the top from the bulb of garlic and squeeze the flesh from the skin and into the yoghurt, add the juice of half of the lemon and mix well.
Tip the chickpeas into the bowl with the aubergine and toss well.

Spread the garlic yoghurt onto a platter, top with the charred sticky aubergines and chickpeas, spoon over the green chilli sauce and scatter with the extra herbs and smoked almonds. Serve with flatbreads.

name: Sticky BBQ Pork Belly Skewers
description: Sticky, sweet, and just the right level of spicy, Jason Howard’s barbecue pork belly skewers need to be added to your weekly recipe rotation.
instructions: Start by getting the pork belly on to braise. Dice the onions, dice the carrots and smash the garlic clove. Chuck them into a pot with the pork belly, bay leaf, and halved scotch bonnet. Cover with cold water. Bring to the boil and braise for one and a half hours, (or more, depending on size) until tender.

While the pork cooks, make the BBQ sauce. Add all the ingredients to a medium saucepan and set over a medium heat. Bring to the boil and whisk until the sugar has dissolved, the sauce has thickened and everything is combined.

To make the plantain crisps, peel and thinly slice the plantain with a knife or a mandoline. Soak in water and salt (to stop them browning. Leave them for 30-60 mins which will season them slightly). Fry at 180°C in vegetable oil until golden brown. Place on paper towel to drain and excess oil. Keep the frying oil warm.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Once cool, cut the pork belly into 1-inch squares. Carefully fry in the plantain oil at 180°C until golden brown and crispy. Toss with a little of the BBQ sauce and thread onto skewers.
Roast the skewers in the oven until caramelised, turning regularly and brushing with the BBQ sauce. Keep lacquering on the glaze until you have a rich, sticky caramelised crust.
Serve the skewers with extra BBQ sauce, garnish with spring onions and plantain crisps.

name: Sticky Banana Pudding With Miso Oat Caramel
description: A sweet and sticky dessert recipe you're going to love. The miso oat caramel cuts through the sweetness with a gentle hit of salt.
keywords: Sticky Banana Pudding With Miso Oat Caramel
Sticky Banana Pudding With Miso Oat Caramel recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a loaf tin and line with baking paper.

Finely mince the pitted dates and add into a saucepan with 150ml oat milk. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to low and cook until the dates have softened, 3-5 mins. Then, remove from the heat and stir through the baking soda, set aside.
Meanwhile, mash the bananas and add into a bowl with the olive oil, remaining 100ml oat milk, vinegar, vanilla extract, salt, cinnamon and cardamom. Stir together.

Once cooled down a little, stir the date mixture into the bananas. Fold in the flour until completely combined, and pour the batter into the tin. Bake for 30-40 mins, or until a cocktail stick inserted comes out clean.
Meanwhile, add all the caramel ingredients into a pan. Place onto medium heat and cook stirring until thickened, 5-7 mins.
Let the pudding cool down before cutting into, and serve with the caramel.

name: Sticky Beef Mince Brothy Rice
description: Caramelised, glossy beef mince in a fragrant broth, spooned over hot rice and topped with crisp onions, chilli and lime. Slurpy, beefy comfort.
instructions: Thinly slice the onion and chuck it into a bowl of ice-cold water. Leave it to crisp up while you crack on with everything else. Bash the ginger with the side of your knife and gently crush the cardamom pods.

Place a saucepan over a medium-high heat and toast the star anise and cardamom for about a minute until fragrant. Add the ginger and a small drizzle of olive oil. Let it sizzle for 30 seconds, then pour in the beef stock. Bring to the boil, turn the heat down and leave to gently simmer.
Place a frying pan over a high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the beef mince and cook, breaking it up, until well browned and starting to crisp.

Mix the oyster sauce, sugar, sriracha, beef stock, soy sauce and rice vinegar together in a small bowl. Pour the sauce into the pan with the beef and let it bubble and reduce until sticky and caramelised, taste and season with salt and pepper if needed. Then finish by stirring through the butter.
Divide the hot rice between bowls. Just before serving, season the broth with lime juice and fish sauce, to taste. Ladle over the hot broth onto the rice, then top with the beef.
Serve with the sliced onion, coriander and sliced red chilli, and some extra lime wedges on the side if you fancy some more zing. Dig in!

name: Sticky Butternut & Chorizo Traybake
description: We put butternut swquash to use in a traybake loaded with chorizo and chickpeas. You drizzle the dish with guindilla chilli salsa, but jalapeños work, too.
instructions: Heat your oven to 210°C.
Halve your squash, then scoop out the seeds and cut them into large chunks.
Arrange them on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil, paprika and salt. Place in the oven to roast for 25 mins.
Cut your chorizo into discs. Cube your sourdough. Rinse your chickpeas in a colander, then pat them dry.
Tip your chorizo and chickpeas into your roasting tray, then return to the oven for 15 mins.

On to your salsa. Finely chop your guindilla chillies and parsley. Add these both to a bowl and zest in your lemon. Add your lemon juice and 4 tbsp of olive oil. Mix to combine, then season to taste with salt.
Drizzle everything in the tray with honey. Nestle your sourdough bread cubes into the tray, then bake for another 12 mins.
Spoon your salsa over the top, then plate up and serve!

name: Sticky Cardamom Buns
description: These sticky cardamom buns are sweet, fluffy, ridiculously easy to make and delicious with a cup of coffee. What’s not to love?
instructions: Warm the Rude Health Almond Drink in a saucepan until it’s hot but not boiling. Add 2 tsp of the ground cardamom and 50g of butter. Stir to dissolve the butter, then set aside to cool.

Add the flour, 75g of the sugar, the yeast, cinnamon, vanilla extract and ½ tsp of salt into a large mixing bowl or stand mixer. Mix until combined, then pour the milk mix through a sieve into a bowl. Bring together and then either tip your dough out onto a work surface and knead for about 10 mins, or about 5 mins in a stand mixer with a dough hook. Once the dough is smooth and springy, clean out the bowl, oil it lightly, and then return the dough to the bowl.
Cover the bowl with cling film and allow the dough to prove for about an hour somewhere warm, or in the fridge overnight.
Preheat your oven to fan 170°c
To make the filling, mix the remaining 170g of butter with the remaining sugar and 1 tsp ground cardamom until you have a soft paste.

Line 2 baking trays with greaseproof paper. Knock back the dough to remove the air, then use a rolling pin to roll it into a rectangle roughly 40x60cm in size. Now, you’re going to want to spread all of the cardamom butter edge-to-edge across the entire surface. Fold the dough into thirds, like a leaflet, so that you have three equal layers one on top of the other. Next, roll that dough again to compress the layers and make a slightly bigger rectangle.

Slice the rectangle widthways into about 12 even slices. Take a slice and gently twist each end of it until it forms a spiralled sausage, then wrap it around 3 fingers so you have a loop, and finally knot it in on itself. Place each bun on a baking tray as you go. Once they’re all knotted and ready, cook in the oven for about 20 mins until golden brown.

While the buns are baking, make a simple syrup with 5 tbsp of water, 5 tbsp caster sugar and ½ tsp of ground cardamom. Once the buns are out of the oven, brush with the syrup as they cool. Best enjoyed the same day!

name: Sticky Carrots on Puy Lentil Salad
description: A high-protein, high-fibre recipe that'll fill you right up. This is a great dish for all the wannabe flexitarians out there.
keywords: Sticky Carrots on Puy Lentil Salad
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C, you want it to be nice and hot for those carrots. Halve the carrots lengthways and add to a large roasting tin. Toss with 2 tbsp olive oil plus the ras el hanout and fennel seeds season well. Snuggle in the cloves of garlic, keeping them unpeeled! Roast for 30 mins, until the carrots are soft and charred in places. If your carrots are particularly large they may take a little longer. If you want those big carrots to cook a little quicker you can simply cut them in half lengthways again to create long wedges. Feel free to add a tbsp of honey, if you want them stickier.

Meanwhile, heat the lentils according to packet instructions, then tip them into a bowl. Add the zest and juice of the lemon along with 2 tbsp olive oil. Roughly chop most of the herbs, saving a few for the top, and add them to the bowl. Slice two of the spring onions and add to the bowl, too. Season generously, and toss well. Tip your mixture out onto a platter or into a bowl.

Season your yoghurt with salt and pepper, then squeeze the garlic cloves from their skin into the yoghurt and mix well. Top the lentils with the yoghurt, then add the roasted carrots. Finish with the reserved herbs and serve it with some thick wedges of sourdough.

name: Sticky Cauliflower and Peanut Salad
description:
In Partnership with Aldi. #ad.

A super simple salad that will satisfy all your cravings. Crispy cauliflower with bundles of fresh veg? This is perfect for summer.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C.
Tear the florets off your cauliflower and pop them into a roasting tin. Pour a good glug of oil on your florets, season with salt and pepper and roast for 15 mins.
Thinly slice your radishes and red cabbage while peeling your carrots into long thin strips. Pop these into a bowl and set aside.

To make your sauce, roughly chop half of your mint, basil and coriander and thinly slice your spring onions and red chilli. Set aside in a separate bowl. Add water, soy sauce, olive oil, the juice from your limes and the sugar. Give it a good mix.
Crush your peanuts by hand or using a pestle and mortar.
Toss your roasted cauliflower florets with the raw veg, sauce, and the remaining herbs (kept intact). Top with crushed peanuts and tuck in.

name: Sticky Chicken Shawarma
description: This is one of the most addictive meals I have developed recently. When I tested it at home my girlfriend ate 3 portions, one after another, over the space of an hour. If that ain't saying something, then I don't know what will.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add the chicken to a bowl with the shawarma spice, olive oil, yoghurt, honey, salt and pepper. If you can't get shawarma spice, use BBQ seasoning. Mix well, then transfer to a 900g loaf tin, packing it down and flattening the top. Pop into the oven for 30 mins on a medium-high shelf, until charred on top.
While the chicken's cooking, finely slice the cabbage and onion. Add to a bowl and season with salt and the vinegar, smooshing with your hands until it starts to soften, then set aside.
Mix the tahini with the remaining yoghurt, the lemon juice and zest, salt and pepper. Mix well, then loosen with a splash of water if needed.
Cook the grains according to the packet instructions, then finely chop the parsley and mix it through the grains, seasoning with salt and pepper.

Once the chicken is cooked and has rested for at least 10 mins, tip it out of the tin onto a chopping board and finely slice, then spoon over the resting juices. Serve the grains up in bowls, then top with the shawarma, slaw, tahini dressing and pickled onions.

name: Sticky Chicken with Bulgur & Olive Salad
description: Inspired by tabbouleh and Turkish kisir, this herby bulgur is packed with jarred roasted peppers, olives and loads of fresh herbs. Topped with sticky, tangy chicken, it makes for hearty salad that's great for prepping ahead.
keywords: Sticky Chicken with Bulgur & Olive Salad
Sticky Chicken with Bulgur & Olive Salad recipe
instructions: Pour the water and olive oil for the bulgur into a medium saucepan. Add the tomato purée and pomegranate molasses, season with salt and bring to the boil. Once boiling, tip in the bulgur wheat, let it come back to the boil, then cover and turn the heat down to low. Cook for 15 mins, until the bulgur has absorbed all the water. Tip into a large bowl and set aside to cool.

Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 7-10 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through. Add the honey and pomegranate molasses, remove from the heat and glaze the chicken until well coated.

Meanwhile, finely chop the herbs, stalks and all. Chop the olives into halves and finely dice the peppers. Toss everything into the cooled bulgur. Squeeze over the juice of half the lemon and season with salt.

Divide the Bulgur salad between airtight containers and top with the sliced chicken, drizzling over any pan juices. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and nestle one into each container. Box up and pop everything in the fridge. They'll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Sticky Chicken with Bulgur & Olive Salad
description: Inspired by tabbouleh and Turkish kisir, this herby bulgur is packed with jarred roasted peppers, olives and loads of fresh herbs. Topped with sticky, tangy chicken, it makes a super easy, and obviously delicious, lunch or dinner.
keywords: Sticky Chicken with Bulgur & Olive Salad
Sticky Chicken with Bulgur & Olive Salad recipe
instructions: Pour the water and olive oil for the bulgur into a medium saucepan. Add the tomato purée and pomegranate molasses, season with salt and bring to the boil. Once boiling, tip in the bulgur wheat, let it come back to the boil, then cover and turn the heat down to low. Cook for 15 mins, until the bulgur has absorbed all the water. Tip into a large bowl and set aside to cool.

Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 7-10 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through. Add the honey and pomegranate molasses, remove from the heat and glaze the chicken until well coated.

Meanwhile, finely chop the herbs, stalks and all. Chop the olives into halves and finely dice the peppers. Toss everything into the cooled bulgur. Squeeze over the juice of half the lemon and season with salt.

Slice the chicken and share the bulgur salad between plates. Top with the sliced chicken and drizzle over any pan juices. Add a generous dollop of Greek yoghurt and serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

name: Sticky Chilli Chicken Tenders
description: This is the only chicken tenders recipe you will ever need. Brining makes all the difference to ensure maximum juiciness.
instructions: Add all the brine ingredients to a large bowl. Add the chicken fillets, cover and set aside for an hour in the fridge.
Make the batter by whisking together the egg and water, then add the flour slowly, whisking with each addition until you make a smooth batter. Season with salt. Set aside.
To create the seasoned flour, tip the flour into a bowl, add in the dry spices, and toss to combine. Set aside.

To make the sticky chilli sauce, peel and finely grate the ginger and garlic. Melt the butter in a small saucepan over a medium heat, add the grated ginger and garlic, cook for 2 mins then add the chilli powder and cook for a 2 mins further, to toast the spice. Add the gochujang, honey and soy sauce, whisk together to combine, cook for a minute further until the sauce is a sticky consistency then remove from the heat and set aside.
Tip enough vegetable oil into a large sauce pan to come halfway up the sides. Place over a high heat and heat to 150°C, then turn to a medium heat to keep the heat constant.

Remove the chicken from the brine and dry on a paper towel. Working in batches, put a handful of the chicken fillets into the plain flour, then dust off a little. Transfer into the batter, then use your hands to remove from the batter and toss into the seasoned flour. Toss to coat. Use a slotted spoon to lower the chicken into the oil and fry for 2-3 mins, until pale golden. Remove with the slotted spoon and set aside on a wire rack. Repeat with the rest of the chicken.
Turn up the heat under the saucepan to heat the oil to 180°C. Lower the chicken back into the pan, and fry for a few more mins until golden and crispy. Drain on the wire rack.
Reheat the sticky chilli sauce until glossy, then spread the sauce on all of the tenders and enjoy.

name: Sticky Coconut Caramel Tofu
description: This one will convert any sceptics. Crispy tofu chunks tossed in a sticky-sweet coconut caramel with punchy aromatics and chilli heat.
instructions: Cut the tofu into bite-sized cubes, then pat dry with kitchen paper to remove excess moisture. Add the garlic granules to a large bowl with the cornflour. Toss the tofu through until evenly coated, then shake off any excess.
Spray the tofu lightly with oil, then air fry at 180°C for 20 mins, shaking halfway through, until crispy and golden.

Wash the rice in cold water until it runs clear, then drain. Add to a saucepan with enough water to just cover it (roughly 1cm above the rice line). Bring to the boil over a medium-high heat, then cover with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 12 mins, then turn off the heat and leave to steam for another 5 mins. Fluff with a fork.

While the rice cooks, peel and thinly slice the garlic, ginger and shallot. Trim and slice the spring onions into 3cm pieces, separating the white and green parts. Also, slice a few of the spring onion greens and the chillies for garnish and set aside.
Place a large wok or frying pan over a medium heat. Add a drizzle of oil, then fry the garlic, ginger, shallot, most of the chillies and spring onion whites for 2 mins until fragrant.
Push the aromatics to the side to create a gap in the middle of the pan. Add the sugar and cook for 2-3 mins until it melts and turns a dark amber colour – keep an eye on it so it doesn’t burn.
Pour in the coconut water, soy sauce, white wine vinegar and white pepper. Let it bubble for another 2-3 mins until slightly thickened.
Toss in the crispy tofu and gently coat in the sauce until everything’s glossy and sticky.
Serve with the rice, then finish with the reserved spring onion greens, the rest of the chillies and any fresh herbs you fancy. Enjoy!

name: Sticky Coconut Rice Pudding with Mango and Lime
description: Inspired by the iconic Thai sticky rice dessert, I’ve hidden lime-infused mangos underneath the rice. Topped with a crème brûlée-esque burnt sugar for *theatre*
instructions: Combine the rice, coconut milk, vanilla extract, 75g of your light brown sugar and ¼ tsp salt in a heavy-bottomed saucepan. Cook over low heat for 40 mins, stirring regularly to prevent sticking.

Whilst the rice is cooking, macerate your mango. Peel the mango with a peeler and then slice off the two sides of flesh. Chop these into small cubes and place in a bowl with your remaining brown sugar. Zest in the lime and squeeze in the juice. Mix well and allow to sit.
Once your rice pudding has cooked, the rice should be tender and creamy. Loosen with a little water if you like your rice pudding less thick.
Arrange the mango chunks into four ramekins, or even one large baking dish.
Divide the rice pudding evenly between the ramekins (or pour it into your one large one), then place in the fridge to chill until ready to serve.

Sprinkle a thin layer of caster sugar on top of each ramekin. Place the pudding under a hot grill (the hottest it goes) or torch carefully using a blow torch until the sugar melts and forms a solid caramelised top.
Allow to cool slightly so the sugar hardens, then tuck in.

name: Sticky Cumin Lamb & Fresh Herb Salad
description: Sticky cumin lamb with those proper crispy bits, spooned over hot jasmine rice and loaded up with a sharp, herby salad. It’s salty, spicy, a little bit messy and ready in under 30. Perfect midweek stuff.
instructions: Start by prepping your veg for the mince. Finely chop the ginger, mince the garlic and slice the green chillis. Then slice the spring onions and shallots for the salad and set aside for later.

Heat a pan over medium high heat and dry toast the cumin seeds for 30 to 60 seconds, until fragrant. Add the lamb mince and fry for 8-10 mins, breaking it up well, until browned and slightly crispy at the edges.

Stir through the ginger and garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Pour in the Shaoxing wine and let it cook off for a couple of mins, then add the dark soy sauce and oyster sauce. Season lightly with salt and cook until the lamb becomes sticky and glossy. Toss through the sliced green chillies.

In a bowl, combine the coriander, sliced spring onions and shallots with the green chillies and squeeze over the juice of the lime along with a pinch of salt. Toss to combine, and your salad is ready.

Set a small frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Crack in the eggs, and fry for 3-5 mins, until cripsy on the edges and the white is cooked and the yolk is still running. Sprinkle over some salt, and get ready to serve.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the sticky cumin lamb and finish with a generous handful of the herb salad over the top.

name: Sticky Curry & Mango Chicken Traybake
description: Juicy chicken thighs and sweet mango charred and sticky in a tikka and mango chutney glaze, served with pickled red onion, a crisp hispi slaw and herby black bean rice.
keywords: Sticky Curry & Mango Chicken Traybake recipe
instructions: Finely slice the red onion and squeeze over the juice of half the lime. Season with salt, massage with your hands and set aside to quick-pickle. Finely chop most of the coriander, saving some to garnish. Drain and rinse the black beans. Zest the lime and set the zest aside.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread the tikka paste, mango chutney and a drizzle of olive oil across a large baking tray and toss the chicken thighs through to coat. Season with salt and black pepper. Roast for 15-20 mins, until cooked through.

Meanwhile, finely slice the hispi cabbage - you can use a peeler if you like. Add to a bowl with the juice of the remaining lime half and a pinch of salt. Massage with your hands until it starts to soften.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Once cooked, stir through the coriander, lime zest and black beans.
Once the chicken is cooked, peel and slice the mango and add it to the tray, tossing through the marinade. Switch the oven to the grill setting and cook until the mango and chicken start to char.
Serve the chicken and mango over the rice with the hispi slaw, pickled red onion and a spoonful of mango chutney. Scatter over the remaining coriander to finish.

name: Sticky Ginger Cake
description: A gorgeously sticky ginger sponge with coconut caramel and plantain custard. This recipe from Nathan Collymore, head chef of Jam Delish, is a vegan treat.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Add the oat milk to a jug and tip in the apple cider vinegar.

Finely chop dates and add to a pan. Add roughly 120ml of water and simmer for 5 minutes until the dates are moist and have absorbed the majority of the water, remove from heat, and then blitz two-thirds of this to a paste.
In a large mixing bowl, mix the flour, sugar, ginger, bicarb, cinnamon and nutmeg with a pinch of salt.

Tip in the oat milk mixture and beat together, add the date puree and the chopped dates, the vanilla, treacle and vegan butter. Beat together, tip into a lined loaf tin and bake for 45-50 minutes, a skewer inserted should come out clean.
To make the coconut caramel, tip the coconut milk into a pan and add the sugar. Bring to a boil and reduce by one-third. Add a big pinch of salt and keep warm.
To make the custard, blend plantain with milk until smooth, pour into a saucepan, add the remaining ingredients, cook over a low heat till glossy and custard-like consistency. Set aside.
Allow the cake to cool for 10-15 mins before tipping out. Cut into slices and finish with the custard and plenty of the coconut caramel.

name: Sticky Gochujang & Roasted Aubergine Ragù with Rice
description: This speedy dinner packs serious punch. Smoky roasted aubergine folded through your Sausage Gochujang Ragù batch sauce, served with fluffy rice and topped with crispy chilli and ginger.
keywords: Sticky Gochujang & Roasted Aubergine Ragù with Rice
Roasted Aubergine with Gochujang Ragù & Rice
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sausage Gochujang Ragú batch recipe.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Chop your aubergine into large chunks and toss with olive oil, salt and black pepper. Spread out on a tray and roast for 25–30 mins until golden and soft.
Meanwhile, cook the rice following pack instructions. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
Finely slice the chilli and cut the ginger into thin matchsticks.
Warm the Sausage Gochujang Ragù in a saucepan over a low heat. Once the aubergine is ready, stir it through the ragù and keep warm.
In a small frying pan, heat the sesame oil over a low heat. Add the ginger, chilli and sesame seeds and fry for 2–3 mins until golden and crisp. Remove from the heat.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls, spoon over the sausage & aubergine ragù and finish with a generous drizzle of the crispy chilli-ginger oil.

name: Sticky Harissa Chicken Stir-Fry
description: This quick and easy stir fry is absolutely delicious. It only uses 6 ingredients but it’s still jam packed with flavour. It’s perfect for a quick dinner after a busy, busy day.
instructions: Slice the chicken thigh fillets into chunk strips. Season with salt and pepper and toss well to coat. In a small bowl, combine the harissa paste (add less if you want a little less spice)and balsamic vinegar with water.
Place a pot of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, tip the couscous in and cook according to package instructions. Then, drain and set aside.

Heat a splash of vegetable oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add the chicken and cook, tossing occasionally, for 10 mins, or until cooked through. Add the harissa mixture and cook for a further 2 mins, or until the chicken is nicely coated in the sauce.
Share the couscous between plates and top with the chicken. Drizzle the yoghurt over the top and finish with the pomegranate kernels and picked coriander leaves then tuck in and enjoy.

name: Sticky Harissa Onion Linguine With Dukkah Breadcrumbs
description: This vegetarian pasta recipe is sticky, spicy and silky. Oh, and it's jammy, carby and crispy, too. This is an all-timer.
keywords: Sticky Harissa Onion Linguine With Dukkah Breadcrumbs
Sticky Harissa Onion Linguine With Dukkah Breadcrumbs recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180ºC and begin with the dukkah breadcrumbs. Put your hazelnuts onto a baking tray and cook for 10-12 mins, set aside to cool. In the meantime, heat a small pan over a medium-high heat and add the whole spices. Toast for 1 min until fragrant, then tip into a pestle and mortar and set aside to cool. Using the same pan, add 2 tbsp oil and turn to a medium heat. Add the panko breadcrumbs and toast, stirring regularly, until evenly golden. Set aside in a bowl.

Peel and finely slice the red onions. Heat 4 tbsp olive oil in a pot and add the onions with a big pinch of salt. Cook on a low heat for 35-40 mins, stirring regularly until really sticky and jammy. If the onions start to catch too much, pour in a splash of water — a bit of colour is fine but we don't want them burnt! Mince or finely grate the garlic and add to the onions, cooking for a further 5 mins. Add the red wine vinegar and the harissa, stir well to combine.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil.

Meanwhile, finish preparing the dukkah breadcrumbs. Tip your roasted hazelnuts into the pestle and mortar with the toasted spices, then grind until roughly crushed. Tip into the bowl of golden panko breadcrumbs and season with salt.

Finely chop the parsley and grate the Parmesan. Drop the linguine into the boiling salted water and cook according to package instructions, around 10 mins. Use tongs to transfer the linguine to the onions, then add the Parmesan. Use a mug or ladle to add in some pasta water. Give it a good stir to emulsify — add as much pasta water as you need to make the sauce silky — it needs quite a lot! Stir through the parsley before tasting and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.
Plate up and top with the spiced breadcrumbs!

name: Sticky Hoisin Honey Air Fryer Salmon
description: We've made the easiest air fryer salmon recipe with a honey hoisin glaze which has a little bit of ginger and lime in it for extra oomph. Serve it up with a load of crunchy veg and wholegrain rice.
keywords: Sticky Hoisin Honey Air Fryer Salmon
Sticky Hoisin Honey Air Fryer Salmon recipe
instructions: Grate the ginger into a bowl. Add the hoisin, honey, and the juice of half of your limes. Pop the salmon onto a plate, skin-side down and coat with half of the marinade, let it sit for 10 mins.
Halve the pak choi. Finely slice the chilli and the spring onions. Thaw the edamame in boiling water, then drain and repeat.

Toss the stir-fry veg with ½ the olive oil, then season with salt. Add to the air fryer basket then top with the pak choi, drizzling with the remaining olive oil. Place the salmon on top, skin-side down and turn the air fryer to 180°C for 5 mins. Baste with the remaining marinade, letting it fall onto the pak choi and cook again for 3-5 mins, until flaky. This will depend on the thickness of your salmon.
If using pouch rice, heat up in the microwave according to package instructions.
Toss the rice with the edamame, then serve up in a bowl. Add the veg and salmon before topping with spring onions, sesame seeds, and chilli. Cut the remaining lime into wedges and serve alongside.

name: Sticky Honey & Miso Aubergine Rice Bowl
description: Sweet, savoury and umami, this sticky honey and miso aubergine is an easy, flavour-packed meal that’s great for meal prep.
keywords: Sticky Honey & Miso Aubergine Rice Bowl
Sticky Honey & Miso Aubergine Rice Bowl recipe
Sticky Honey & Miso Aubergine Rice Bowls
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan.

Cut the aubergines into wedges and place them on a baking tray. In a bowl, mix the honey, miso, water, sesame oil and lemon juice, then pour over the aubergines, tossing to coat. Roast for 30-35 mins until soft and sticky. Once cooked, remove from the oven and drizzle over the pomegranate molasses.
Meanwhile, cook the rice following pack instructions. Four mins before the end of the cooking time, add the green beans. Slice the red chilli and pick the parsley leaves.

Divide the rice between bowls or meal prep containers. Top with the sticky aubergines, drizzling over any leftover marinade from the tray. Scatter with sesame seeds, red chilli and parsley. Finish with pomegranate seeds, if using. It will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Sticky Honey Gochujang Dressing
description: A sticky-sweet, spicy gochujang sauce with honey, garlic and sesame. Perfect for drizzling over salad, glazing or dunking everything into.
instructions: Peel the garlic and grate into a small bowl.
Add the honey, gochujang, rice vinegar, sesame oil, soy sauce, water and sesame seeds to the bowl with the garlic and whisk until smooth and you’re good to go.CAN

name: Sticky Mango Halloumi
description: This sticky mango halloumi is perfect for meal prep. Combine it with your choice of carb, veg and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Cut the halloumi into strips or cubes. Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high then add the halloumi and fry until nicely golden on both sides. Remove the pan from the heat then stir through the mango chutney and nigella seeds, tossing to coat the halloumi in the glaze.
Enjoy with your choice of carb, veg and topping. If batch cooking for the week, transfer to the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Sticky Mango Paneer Kebabs
description: Charred paneer makes for the ultimate veggie-friendly barbecue snack. Sticky, spicy, and loaded into fluffy naan with curry yoghurt – need I say more? Sophie x
instructions: Soak your wooden skewers in a tray filled with water. Cut your paneer into 3cm cubes and pop them in a large bowl.

For the paneer marinade, roughly chop the ginger and garlic then add to a food processor with the ground cumin, chilli powder and turmeric. Add the tomato purée, vegetable oil, ⅔ of the mango chutney and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Blend until you have a smooth paste. Pour the mixture over the paneer chunks and toss to coat. Leave to marinate for at least 30 mins, or pop in the fridge overnight if you have the time.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the red onion. Heat a little vegetable oil in a frying pan set over a medium heat. Add ½ the onions and cook them for 15 mins until they are totally soft and starting to caramelise. Add your curry powder and cook out for 2 mins until fragrant. Turn off the heat and leave the onions to cool a little.
Add the remaining onion to a bowl and squeeze over the lime juice. Sprinkle in a good pinch of salt, then scrunch up with your onions with your hands to encourage them to pickle. Set aside.
Spoon your caramelised onions into your food processor. Add the yoghurt and remaining mango chutney, then blitz until totally smooth. Set aside.
Heat your grill, BBQ or top broiler to a medium-high heat.

Skewer your paneer pieces onto your wooden skewers. If grilling/broiling, arrange your skewers on a baking tray and slide under the grill to cook for 6 mins on each side, turning until they're evenly cooked and starting to char a little around the edges. If barbecuing, place them on the grills and cook the paneer in the same way.
Heat your naans up in the oven following packet instructions. Roughly chop your coriander and slice your chillies.
To serve, spread a little yoghurt on the base of the naan, then push your paneer off your skewers on top. Finish with the pickled onions, chillies and fresh coriander.

name: Sticky Miso Salmon with Rice
description: We've cooked these miso-marinated salmon fillets under the grill to get them sticky and caramelised on the outside and soft and tender inside. We've served them with fluffy sushi rice and a yuzu broccoli salad for zing. A gorgeous dinner without the fuss.
keywords: Sticky Miso Salmon with Rice recipe
instructions: To make the marinade, add the miso paste, sugar, sake and mirin to a small saucepan and whisk until combined. Set the pan over a high heat for a minute or so until the mixture is almost boiling, then remove from the heat and leave to cool.
Add the salmon fillets to a baking tray or ziplock bag and pour over the miso marinade so the fillets are well covered. Leave to marinate in the fridge for at least 30 mins and ideally overnight.

Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear, then drain. Add the rice to a saucepan along with the water. Pop the lid on and heat on high until boiling, then reduce to the lowest heat and set a timer for 11 mins. When the time is up, turn off the heat and set another timer for 10 mins to finish steaming. Set aside, with the lid still on, until ready to serve.

Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Gently brush any excess marinade off the salmon but don’t wipe it clean off. Transfer the salmon fillets to a baking tray (if they’re not already on one) then slide under the grill for 5-10 mins until cooked through. If its charring too quickly, move the fish down a level.
Pour the excess marinade into a saucepan and set it over a low-medium heat. Let the mixture bubble away for 2-4 mins until reduced by a quarter, then set aside until ready to serve.

For the broccoli, grate the ginger into a salad bowl then add the light soy sauce, yuzu juice and sesame oil and whisk until combined. Bring a pot of water to a boil, add a large pinch of salt and blanch the broccoli for 2 mins then drain. Add to the dressing and toss to coat.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls and top with the salmon and broccoli, spooning over the miso reduction on top of the salmon.

name: Sticky Mushroom Pitta and Hummus Bowl
description: Lots of favourites in this one: sticky, savoury, perfectly cooked mushrooms, herby tahini, hummus and a pitta. It’s simple, but special.
keywords: Sticky Mushroom Pitta and Hummus Bowl
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Mince the garlic cloves.

Pull or chop the mushrooms into bite-sized pieces and add to a large baking tray. Drizzle with plenty of olive oil, there should be enough to cover them well and a little extra at the bottom of the tray. Add the spices and minced garlic and season with salt and pepper. Toss well to make sure everything is covered and bake on the lower shelf for 15 mins, then add the pomegranate molasses, toss well and return to the oven for another 10-15 mins. They should be juicy and starting to crisp up on the edges.

Meanwhile, make the lemony courgette. Use a speed peeler to peel the courgette into ribbons. Use a knife when you can't peel the core any further to slice it thinly. Place it in a small bowl. Thinly slice the chilli and add to the bowl. Squeeze over the juice of half of the lemon, add a sprinkle of salt, toss and set aside to lightly pickle.

Finely chop the herbs in a small food processor or with a knife. Add the tahini, 1 tbsp of olive oil 3 tbsp of cold water, 3 tbsp of lemon juice and blend or whisk to combine. Season to taste with salt and pepper and add more lemon juice or water if needed.
Lightly toast or warm your pittas. To assemble the bowls, add the hummus, mushrooms, courgettes to each bowl. Top with the herby tahini drizzle and tuck in with your fluffy pitas.

name: Sticky Mushroom Udon Stir-Fry
description: Ridiculously satisfying vegan noodles - so rich and moreish. A great weeknight option.
instructions: Slice up your Portobello mushrooms. Matchstick your carrots. Finely chop your onion. Shred 1/3 of a white cabbage. Finely slice 3 spring onions.
Add your sesame oil and vegetable oil to a pan.
Add your carrots, cabbage and onion. Allow to soften for 3 minutes. Throw in your Portobello mushrooms.
Cook for 1 more minute and add your shiitake mushrooms. Mix everything in and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add your spring onions. Cook for another 2 minutes and add the udon noodles. Season with pepper, add your soy sauce and mirin.
Mix everything together, cook for another minute and then your noodles are ready. Remove from the heat and serve whilst hot. Garnish with sliced spring onion and enjoy!

name: Sticky Mushrooms, Creamy Whipped Tofu & Herby Cashew Sprinkle
description: Sticky, sweet and umami mushrooms, creamy tofu and a crunchy herby cashew sprinkle - a great vegan dish to mop up with some flatbreads or naans.
keywords: Creamy Whipped Tofu & Herby Cashew Sprinkle
instructions: Slice the stalk off the chilli and finely slice. Peel the ginger and finely grate half of it. Thinly slice the coriander stalks and pick the coriander and mint leaves. Roughly chop the salted cashews, place them into a bowl with the chilli, coriander, and mint leaves, toss and set aside.

In a blender, crumble the tofu along with 2 tbsp of soy sauce, garam masala, and a piece of whole ginger. Pour in 100ml of water and 50ml of olive oil, then blend together until smooth, it should be as thick as greek yoghurt. Taste and season with salt and pepper to taste. Add a bit more water to the mixture if it needs to loosen.

Tear or slice the mushrooms into large pieces and remove any tough stems. Thinly slice the garlic. Pour 3 tbsp of olive oil into a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the mushrooms, season with salt lightly. Let the mushrooms cook undisturbed until they start to brown, 10-15 mins. Once they brown, stir them to evenly colour the mixture, add another drizzle of oil if they’re looking a little dry.

Once the mushrooms have browned, add the garlic and ginger, cook for 1 min, until fragrant. Add the curry powder, maple syrup, the remaining soy sauce and 30ml of water. Stir to coat and glaze the mushrooms, then remove from the heat.
Spread the whipped tofu over a large platter or plates and then top with sticky mushrooms. Drizzle over the mushroom sauce and garnish with the herby salted cashew mixture.

name: Sticky Nigella Halloumi
description: A sweet and nutty halloumi main that's perfect for your lunch. Pair it with your favourite carb for a dynamite meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Place the nigella seeds, coriander seeds, pepper and urfa chilli flakes in a spice grinder or pestle and mortar and blitz or crush to a fine powder. Stir the spices through the honey and set aside.

Halve each block of halloumi so you're left with 4 thick pieces. Heat a dash of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat, then pan fry for 3-5 minutes on each side until golden and crisp. Transfer to the oven to heat through for 5 minutes. By this point, it should be gooey.
To serve, place a slice of halloumi on each plate and season with a little lemon juice and zest. Drizzle over the spiced honey and serve immediately.

name: Sticky Orange & Ginger Soy Protein Stir Fry
description: We've made this fakeaway dish with textured soy protein, making it a quick and delicious way to pack in the protein with a whopping 24g of protein per serving.
instructions: Add 1 stock cube to 300ml of boiling water in a bowl. Add the soy protein and a splash of soy sauce, and make sure it’s completely submerged. Cover with a plate to steam and set aside for 10 mins.
After 10 mins, drain the protein and squeeze out as much water out as possible.
Meanwhile, make the marinade. Mince the ginger and garlic and put them into a small bowl. Add the sugar, soy sauce, sunflower oil, and then whisk until combined.
Pour the marinade over the soy protein and make sure each piece is completely marinated.

Heat a frying pan over high heat with a drizzle of sunflower oil. Add the soy protein pieces, saving the remaining marinade in the bowl. Fry on a medium high heat until it’s starting to char on the sides. Add the remaining marinade and the juice of one orange to the protein. Give it a final stir and turn off the heat.
Cook your rice or noodles according to the packet instructions. Finely slice the chilli and spring onion if using.
Serve the protein over rice or noodles, finish with sesame seeds, spring onion and chilli, if using. Serve each portion with half an orange to squeeze over the top.

name: Sticky Orange Chicken Traybake
description: This is a simple and incredibly delicious traybake. The freshness of the oranges, creamy peanut butter and tanginess of the fish sauce cooks lovely together.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Finely chop two of the red chillies and roughly chop the onions.

In a large bowl combine the peanut butter, juice and zest two oranges, fish sauce, apple cider vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar, ground cumin and red chillies. Grate in the ginger and garlic. Add in the chicken and onions and mix well.
Slice the remaining orange.
Pour the chicken with the sauce onto a baking tray and push in the slices of orange.
Bake for 35 mins until the chicken has cooked through, basting with the sauce halfway through.
Meanwhile, finely slice the last red chilli as well as your coriander and peanuts.
Finish the chicken with the red chilli, coriander and peanuts. Serve with freshly steamed rice and enjoy.

name: Sticky Peanut Roast Carrots
description: Roast carrots topped with a sticky peanut sauce that's got big satay energy. This is a side you're going to love.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Peel the carrots and chop them into chunky pieces. Smash the 4 garlic cloves.
Pour 4 tbsp of oil into a metal baking tray. Tip in the carrots, smashed garlic cloves and a pinch of salt. Toss everything well.
Roast for 15 mins then flip the carrots and roast for another 15 mins or until charred on the edges.
Meanwhile, combine all the peanut sauce ingredients (except the water) in a small bowl. Add 1 tbsp of water at a time until the sauce is smooth and pourable.
In another small bowl, combine the ingredients for the dark soy glaze.
Finely chop the coriander, including the stems.
Toast the sesame seeds, if needed, by putting them into a small pan and tossing over a medium heat for 3-4 mins or until lightly golden. Remove and set aside in a bowl.
Remove the carrots from the oven and transfer to a shallow bowl, then drizzle all over with the peanut sauce and 2-3 tbsp of the dark soy glaze.
Top with coriander, sesame seeds, crispy shallots and freshly squeezed lime juice.

name: Sticky Peanut and Sichuan Chicken Wings
description: Peanut butter + sichuan peppers = a flavour combo straight from heaven. These wings are sticky & sweet. Ridiculously moreish. Give them a go MOB.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C/374°F.
Lay the chicken wings out on a wire rack with a baking tray underneath to catch any juices. Drizzle and season the wings with a big glug of sesame oil, salt and pepper.
Roast the wings for 30 minutes, until crispy.
Meanwhile, mix the creamy ManiLife peanut butter with the grounded Sichuan peppers, honey, vinegar, soy sauce, grated garlic and ginger and 1 tbsp of sesame oil. Set aside.

Once the chicken is ready glaze the wings with the peanut marinade, making sure each piece is evenly coated and save some for garnish. Return the chicken to the oven for 5-8 minutes until the wings crisp up further.
Thinly slice the spring onions and finely chop and deseed the red chilli. Garnish these over the crispy peanut wings. Drizzle over the leftover peanutty sauce and tuck in!

name: Sticky Pecan Pie
description: I tested this recipe about 50 times, and have finally landed on the ultimate method. It is the perfect pecan pie. Top with a mandatory drizzle of cream. Seema x
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Start by making the pastry. Dice your butter into small chunks and pop it in the freezer to chill for 15 minutes.

Sift your flour into a large mixing bowl, zest in half the orange and add the sugar with a pinch of salt. Tip your very cold butter into the flour and rub it together with your fingers until you have a mixture that resembles coarse yellow breadcrumbs. Don’t worry if there are a few flecks of butter left, a few chunks will just create nice flaky pockets in your pastry.

Carefully separate the egg yolks from the whites (you can freeze the egg whites for meringue). Then create a well in the centre and add in the egg yolks and cold water. Give it all a good mix until it just comes together as a dough. Press it together to form a disk and wrap in cling film to chill in the fridge for half an hour.

Whilst your dough is chilling, start on the filling. Heat the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, then add in the sugar and maple syrup. Bring to a gentle bubble and cook for 5 minutes until slightly thickened and emulsified. Add the cinnamon and vanilla extract, then leave to cool for 10 minutes. Whisk in the eggs until emulsified.

Roll out your pastry on a lightly floured surface to about 2mm. Gently roll it around your rolling pin and slide your pie case underneath - we used a 23 cm tart tin but any regular pie dish would work. Lower your pastry into the case, then fold it into the corners to line it trimming off the excess around the edge. Push in the edges with a bit of extra pastry to create a tight lining.

Gently prick the pastry with a fork - this stops the pastry from rising to create a crispy bottom. Scrunch up a piece of parchment paper, open it up and line the tart tin. Fill it with baking beans, or rice or lentils if you don’t have any.
Bake for 10 minutes, then remove the baking beans and parchment and bake for another 5 minutes until the base is lightly golden. Allow the pastry shell to cool slightly.

Turn the oven down to 140°C. Then roughly chop 200g of your pecans. Give your sugar mixture another good whisk. Add your chopped pecans onto the now slightly cooled pie case. Pour over the sugar mixture and top with whole pecans to decorate.
Bake for 35-40 minutes - it should have a golden top and a slight wobble when you shake it. Leave to cool completely and set.
Remove your pecan pie from its shell and cut it into slices. Drizzle of double cream and enjoy.

name: Sticky Pigs In Blankets
description: These sticky pigs in blankets are going to rock your world. All sausages should be wrapped in bacon and slathered in hot honey.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Lay out the bacon strips flat on a roasting tray. Wrap each one around a chipolata, starting at one end and working your way down to the other. Wrap at a slight angle and make sure you cover as much of the sausage as you can.

Slide into the oven for 15-20 mins until the bacon is starting to crisp. Meanwhile, mix the honey and hot sauce together in a small bowl. Once the pigs are starting to crisp, brush with the honey mixture and return to the oven for 2-3 mins. Repeat a few times until golden and sticky. Serve!

name: Sticky Pomegranate Glazed Chicken & Herby Quinoa
description: Juicy, spiced chicken glazed with sweet-tangy pomegranate molasses. Paired with a fresh, herby quinoa salad.
instructions: Stir the Lebanese 7-spice and 1 tablespoon of olive oil together in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper, then toss the chicken thighs through the marinade. Set aside to marinate.
Cook the quinoa following pack instructions. Once done, set aside to cool slightly.

Finely mince the parsley and coriander (stalks and all). Tip into a bowl with the quinoa and pomegranate seeds. Roughly crush the walnuts and add those in too. Stir through the olive oil, season with salt, and squeeze over the juice of the lemon. Give everything a good mix and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Set a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the chicken thighs and cook for 10–15 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through.
Pour in the pomegranate molasses and honey. Take the pan off the heat and baste the chicken in the sticky glaze for a minute or two until coated and glossy.
Spoon the quinoa salad onto plates. Top with the glazed chicken and any juices from the pan. Serve with any leftover lemon wedges on the side.

name: Sticky Pomegranate Glazed Chicken & Herby Quinoa
description: Juicy, spiced chicken glazed with sweet-tangy pomegranate molasses. Paired with a fresh, herby quinoa salad. Perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Stir the Lebanese 7-spice and 1 tablespoon of olive oil together in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper, then toss the chicken thighs through the marinade. Set aside to marinate.
Cook the quinoa following pack instructions. Once done, set aside to cool slightly.

Finely mince the parsley and coriander (stalks and all). Tip into a bowl with the quinoa and pomegranate seeds. Roughly crush the walnuts and add those in too. Stir through the olive oil, season with salt, and squeeze over the juice of the lemon. Give everything a good mix and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Set a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the chicken thighs and cook for 10–15 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through.
Pour in the pomegranate molasses and honey. Take the pan off the heat and baste the chicken in the sticky glaze for a minute or two until coated and glossy.

Spoon the quinoa salad into Tupperware containers. Top with the glazed chicken and any juices from the pan. Serve with any leftover lemon wedges on the side. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Sticky Pork Noodle Bowls
description: An Asian twist on the classic. Tangy, fragrant meatballs on a bed of soft rice noodles. A real winner at a dinner party.
instructions: Into a bowl, add your pork mince, grated red chilli, fish sauce, 3 finely chopped spring onions, a handful of chopped mint, a handful of chopped coriander, a grated clove of garlic, ½ the cornflour and a tbsp of grated ginger. Season with black pepper.
Mix everything together with your hands. Divide the pork into golf ball sized meatballs. Set them on a plate and put them in the fridge for 10 minutes.

Add some vegetable oil to a pan. Add the meatballs once the oil is hot. Drizzle a tablespoon of soy sauce over the balls. Cook for 3 minutes on each side, turning the balls when they are browning and caramelized.
Add another splash of soy sauce once you’ve turned the balls. Once the balls are brown on all sides, remove them from the pan and set aside.

Remove any excess oil from the pan and make your sauce. Into the pan, add 2 tbsp of soy sauce and 200ml of low-salt chicken stock. With a wooden spoon, de-glaze all the sticky bits off the bottom of the pan. Squeeze in the juice of a lime and grate in a small knob of ginger.
Make your cornflour slurry. In a cup, mix the remaining cornflour with 100ml of water until it has dissolved.
Pour the slurry into the sauce. It should start to thicken. Once is has thickened up, re-introduce your meatballs. Coat the balls in the sauce and remove from the heat.
Serve the meatballs on some hot rice noodles. Scatter over any leftover coriander and mint leaves. Tuck in. Enjoy!

name: Sticky Re-Fried Chicken With Asparagus, Hot Honey & Soy
description: Frying your leftover roast chicken is a great way to breathe new life into it. This hot, sweet, and sticky recipe is a belter.
instructions: Before you begin, make the No-Fuss Roast Chicken.

Finely chop the chillies, ginger and garlic clove and pop into a small saucepan. Add the honey, soy and vinegar. Set over a medium-high heat and bring to a boil. Once boiling, remove from the heat and allow to infuse.

Cut the asparagus into chunky diamonds and shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Set a large frying pan over a high heat and add a glug of oil. Toss in the chicken and cook for 5-6 mins, tossing regularly until the skin is crispy and the meat is reheated. Add the asparagus and cook for 2 mins before tipping in the honey mixture.
Toss the mixture through the asparagus and chicken and keep cooking, reducing the marinade and letting it glaze the contents of the pan.
Heat the rice according to the package instructions. Season with salt.
Divide the rice between warm bowls, top with a pile of sticky chicken and asparagus and finish with torn coriander. Serve.

name: Sticky Sesame Chicken
description: Just whack everything in the tray and let the magic happen. Sticky, fragrant, sesame chicken. You'll be making it over and over again.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Add the thighs to a baking tray. Add dark soy, sesame oil, a crushed garlic clove, a grated knob of ginger and honey. Mix everything together. Place the tray in the oven for 50 minutes.
Baste chicken every 15 minutes in the juices.
Get your rice on (follow pack instructions).
Serve thighs on top of the steaming hot rice. Pour over some of the juices, scatter with sesame seeds and tuck in!

name: Sticky Sesame Chicken Meatballs
description: Homemade chicken meatballs are an excellent protein source. We've thrown them together here with a sticky sesame sauce. It's a healthy fakeaway to remember.
instructions: Crush all the garlic and thinly slice all the spring onions. Combine all the ingredients for the meatballs in a large bowl, then shape into 12 equal-sized balls (just smaller than a golf ball) using wet hands.
Heat the air fryer or oven to 180°C. Cook the meatballs for 16 mins (air fryer) or 20 mins (oven) until cooked through.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens then mince the garlic.
