Add the sauce ingredients into a small saucepan with the garlic and spring onion whites, with a splash of water to loosen. Bring to a simmer on a low heat and cook for 3-5 mins, until bubbling. Stir in the spring onion greens and sesame seeds.
Bring a pot of water to the boil. Chop the broccoli florets, place in the boiling water for 2-5 minutes, until cooked to your liking.
Toss the cooked meatballs in a bowl with the sauce and the sesame seeds and stir to coat really well. Serve over rice with broccoli.

name: Sticky Sesame Popcorn Chicken
description: The sticky chicken you get down at the local Chinese is so easy to do at home. The ginger in this version works wonders.
instructions: Cut chicken into bite-size chunks.
Get two bowls. Fill one with cornflour and crack two eggs into the other. Whisk eggs. Dip a piece of chicken in flour, then egg, then flour. Make sure it is coated. Do this with all your chicken.
Heat a large glug of vegetable oil in a wok (enough for the chicken to shallow fry). Add your chicken bits in batches. Fry until crispy. Remove from the wok and set aside.
Get your rice on – cook according to pack instructions.
Wipe the excess oil out of the wok. Add a tablespoon of sesame oil. Add a large grated knob of ginger and grated garlic cloves. Fry for 30 seconds.
Add sweet chilli sauce, soy sauce, ketchup and rice wine vinegar. Mix everything together.
Add 100ml of cornflour slurry. To make the slurry, add a heaped teaspoon of cornflour to a glass and pour in 100ml of warm water. Mix until the cornflour is dissolved.
Mix everything together. Once it starts thickening, re-add your chicken. Coat it in the sticky sauce.
Serve the chicken on top of the hot rice, with chopped spring onions and sesame seeds scattered on top. Enjoy!

name: Sticky Short Ribs With Herb & Peanut Rice
description: Unctuous and sticky short ribs with a fresh salad and the most addictive peanut dusting. This one's special, folks.
keywords: Sticky Short Ribs With Herb & Peanut Rice
instructions: Prep your short ribs and season them with an outrageous amount of salt. Go big here, they can take it. Get a heavy bottomed pan ripping hot, add a couple of tablespoons of vegetable oil and sear the short ribs all over, until deliciously golden brown. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Slice up the whites of your spring onions, saving the greens for later. Add your garlic, ginger, spring onion whites, miso and mirin to deglaze before adding your short ribs back into the pan. Cover with chicken stock, pop the lid on, and get into the oven at 160°C for 2.5-3 hours or until they fall off the bone.

Roast your peanuts in the same oven for around 20 mins until golden brown and leave to cool. Once cool, crush them in a pestle and mortar or food processor until sandy in texture. Mix through the sugar, salt, MSG and chili flakes and set aside for later.

Pick your coriander leaves and slice your spring onion greens and radishes. I like to give them a bath in iced water here, to crisp them up but it’s totally optional. If iced, dry them off and just mix the sesame oil, soy sauce, sugar and vinegar to make the dressing. You want to dress this just before eating.

Wash your rice two to three times and add to a heavy-bottomed pan with the water. Bring to a simmer, turn the heat down as low as possible and pop the lid on. Cook for 15 mins, turn the heat off and let sit for at least 10 mins. You can leave it longer at this stage if you need to wait for anything. Fluff up your rice before serving.

Get the short ribs out of the oven. Remove from the braising stock, discard the bones and shred with two forks. Strain the stock and reduce by half. Add the shredded beef to the pan with a few ladles of the reduced stock and heat through. You want this a little saucy so you get that wonderful flavour through your rice.
Dress your salad. Add a good portion of rice to a bowl, top with a generous pile of saucy short rib, cover with half the salad and finish with a generous sprinkle of your peanut dust. Enjoy.

name: Sticky Short Ribs With Lemon-y Grains & Salad
description: There's only one thing we're teaming this meltingly tender piece of beef short rib up with, and that's a gorgeous side of lemon grains and herby salad. Oh yes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 140ºC. Slice the onions into wedges (no need to peel) and cut the garlic bulb in half horizontally across the centre.

Heat ½ tbsp of olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a high heat. Season the short ribs with salt and pepper and add to the pan, cook for 3-4 mins, until charred on one side, then turn the ribs until browned on each side. Use tongs to move into a large deep roasting tin.

Add the onions to the pan along with a big pinch of salt and fry until softened, around 5 mins, then tip into the roasting tin with the short ribs. Snuggle in the garlic halves, then pour in the stock. Cover tightly with foil, then slide into the oven for 4 hours.

Meanwhile, rinse the grains until the water runs clear. Add a tbsp of olive oil to a large saucepan over a medium-high heat, then add the fennel seeds and toast for a min. Stir the barley in and toast for a min, then cover with water. Add a big pinch of salt and cook for 45 mins, or until soft with a slight bite.

Drain well and tip into a large bowl. Add the zest and juice of 1 of the lemons. Finely chop the preserved lemon and stir through along with the mustard and 3–4 tbsp of olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper.

To make the salad, pick the herb leaves from the stems, rinse and drain on kitchen paper, then cover and set aside in the fridge until needed — this will keep them crisp. Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat, until they pop and start to turn golden, set aside.

Remove the short ribs from the oven, they should be meltingly tender. Use tongs to move onto a plate and cover with foil. Tip the contents of the roasting tin through a sieve into a large saucepan or deep frying pan, discard the contents of the sieve. Add the pomegranate molasses to the saucepan and place over a high heat, cook for 20-25 mins, until thick and glossy.
Toss the herb leaves with the sumac, pumpkin seeds and the juice of half of the lemon.

Spoon a little of the sauce over each of the short ribs. Spoon the pearl barley salad into bowls, top each with a short rib, adding a little extra sauce over the meat. Add a small handful of the herb salad to the side of the bowl. Finish with the pomegranate seeds and a pinch of the pul biber to serve. Serve with the remaining lemon half, sliced into wedges, on the side.

name: Sticky Soy Chicken & Chilli Crisp Tomatoes
description: If there’s one chicken recipe I think would go down well with everyone (including picky eaters), it’s this one. Sticky soy chicken (basically teriyaki) with chilli crisp tomato salad on top of rice. The juices trickle into the rice… woooow. Perfect dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Pat the chicken dry and season with salt. Place the chicken, skin-side down, into an ovenproof frying pan. Set the heat to medium-high and cook for 8-12 mins until the skin turns golden and the chicken can easily flip over.

Meanwhile, stir the soy sauce, sugar, rice vinegar and water together in a bowl. Once the chicken skin is crispy, turn the thighs skin-side up and pour the sauce into the pan. Transfer to the oven and roast for 20-25 mins, until cooked through.
Cook the rice following packet instructions.
Remove the chicken from the oven and place the pan straight over a medium heat to reduce the sauce. It should glaze the chicken nicely.
Meanwhile, for the salad, trim and thinly slice the spring onions, then chop the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks.
Put the chilli oil into a large bowl and stir through the rice vinegar. Season with salt, then add the tomatoes and spring onion. Toss well.
Share the rice between bowls, then top with the chicken and tomato salad. Drizzle the pan juices over the chicken.

name: Sticky Soy Chicken Noodles & Sesame Sauce
description: Chewy noodles in a creamy sesame sauce topped with glossy soy chicken and chilli oil. This one hits every craving in one bowl.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake batch recipe.
Boil the noodles and edamame in salted water for 5 mins, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Grate the garlic. In a bowl, whisk together the tahini, sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey, garlic and a pinch of salt. Add a splash of water and whisk again until smooth and creamy, like double cream.
Toss the noodles and edamame with the sesame sauce until coated.
Reheat the leftovers from your Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake in a pan, oven or microwave and slice the chicken into strips.
To serve, divide the noodles between bowls, top with chicken, coriander, and a drizzle of chilli oil. Sprinkle over sesame seeds, if using.

name: Sticky Soy Chicken Rice Bowl with Glazed Veg
description: Elevate your leftover Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake with this delish rice bowl. Served with glazed veg and finished with lime and saucy peanut butter, it's an addictive weeknight supper.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake batch recipe.
Cook the rice following pack instructions. Stir through the sesame oil once cooked and set aside.
Slice the aubergine and pepper into bite-sized chunks. Finely slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish later.
Heat olive oil in a large pan and fry the veg with a pinch of salt until charred. Add kecap manis and water, then simmer until glossy and tender.
Mix the peanut butter with lime juice. Loosen with water until the consistency of double cream then season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, reheat your Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake leftovers in a pan, microwave or oven until piping hot. Slice the chicken into strips.
To serve, pile the rice into bowls, top with glazed veg and sliced chicken. Finish with spring onions, coriander, lime wedges and a drizzle of peanut sauce, if using.

name: Sticky Soy Chicken Sandwich with Miso Mayo
description: Still got some of your Caramelised Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake batch left? This mega sandwich takes those sticky chicken leftovers to new heights.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Caramelised Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake batch recipe.
Slice the chicken and reheat in a pan or the microwave until sticky. Finely chop the chives.
Mix the miso paste with mayo, juice of the lime, sesame oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Stir through the chives.
Rinse and slice the romaine, then drain and slice the peppers.
Toast the focaccia slices until golden. Spread both sides with the miso mayo.
Layer on the chicken, romaine, peppers and crispy onions. Close, press gently and slice in half. Now get messy and dig in!

name: Sticky Soy Chicken Stir Fry
description: Tender chicken thighs in a sticky soy and ginger sauce, finished over crispy rice that catches at the bottom of the pot. Comfort food that delivers.
instructions: Cook the sushi or jasmine rice following pack instructions.
Meanwhile, smash the garlic until flattened, then remove the skins. Slice the ginger into thin, round discs and set aside on a plate.
Combine the sauce ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.
Chop the chicken into bite-sized chunks and pat dry with kitchen paper.
Heat the neutral oil in a medium-sized casserole dish or wok. Cook the garlic and ginger for 1-2 mins or until lightly golden.
Push the garlic and ginger to the side, then add the chicken (laying it as flat as possible) and cook for 1 min each side, or until lightly golden.

Now add the sauce and toss well. Add a bit of water, so it’s only one-quarter of the way up the chicken, then bring to a simmer and add a lid. Reduce the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 25 mins, stirring halfway through.
Meanwhile, slice the red pepper, onion, spring onions and chilli into bite-sized pieces. Tear the basil leaves and set everything aside on a large plate.
Remove the lid and bring to the boil, then toss in all the chopped veg. Toss for 2 mins, then add the basil and turn the heat off.

Finish with a drizzle of sesame oil and toasted sesame seeds, then serve over the rice. Alternatively, grab a small pot that will hold all the rice (or individual clay pots) and set it/them over a medium heat. Add 1 tbsp sesame oil to the pot(s) and all the cooked rice, tip the chicken and sauce on top and cover with a lid. Cook for 2-3 mins to crisp-up the base of the rice. Then serve inside the pots

name: Sticky Soy Chicken Tacos with Spring Onion Salsa
description: Sweet, sticky chicken wrapped up in soft tortillas with a zingy spring onion salsa. One of our best batch leftover recipes going.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake batch recipe.
Slice the cucumber in half lengthways and scoop out the seeds and discard. Then finely dice the cucumber.
Finely slice the spring onions and green chilli.
Mix the cucumber, spring onions and chilli with the rice vinegar, sesame oil and a pinch of salt. Set aside to pickle for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, reheat the Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake leftovers in a pan, oven or microwave until hot and glazed. Slice the chicken into strips.

Toast the tortillas in a dry frying pan until soft and warmed through. To build your tacos, spread a little sour cream over each tortilla, then pile on the sticky chicken and spoon over the salsa. Finish with coriander, sesame seeds and sambal, if using.

name: Sticky Soy Chicken with Butterbeans & Charred Courgettes
description: Transform your Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake batch with creamy butter beans and smoky courgettes. A speedy leftover dinner that seriously hits the spot.
keywords: sticky soy chicken with butter beans
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake batch recipe.
Pick the mint leaves and set aside. Slice the courgettes.
Heat the sesame oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and fry the courgettes with a pinch of salt for 5 mins until golden and tender.
Drain and rinse the butterbeans. Grate the garlic and stir through the courgettes for 1 min until fragrant. Tip in the butterbeans and cook for 2-3 mins until warmed through.
Meanwhile, reheat the Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake leftovers in a pan or microwave until hot and sticky. Slice into the chicken into strips.

Squeeze the juice of the lemon into the butterbeans and give it a good stir. Spoon the bean mix into bowls, top with chicken and green beans from the traybake, mint leaves and a nice dollop of sambal, if using.

name: Sticky Soy Maple Ribs with Lime Cashew Slaw
description: Weeknight ribs done right. Using the Russell Hobbs SatisFry Air & Grill cuts your time in half with this simple, sticky recipe. Easy air fryer ribs.
keywords: Sticky Soy Maple Ribs with Lime Cashew Slaw
instructions: Add the ribs to the SatisFry Air & Grill cooking basket and select the slow cook function. Tip in the cola, onion, and half the soy. Add enough water to barely cover the ribs and slow cook for 2 hours or until the meat is tender, but not falling to bits.
Meanwhile make the glaze. Combine the remaining soy, ketchup, gochujang, maple syrup, vinegar and five-spice in a pan. Bring to the boil and reduce by a third.

Once the ribs are cooked, remove from the slow cooker and set up the SatisFry for air fry. Place the grill plate in the cooking pot and then add the ribs and brush on the BBQ sauce. Air fry for 2 mins then brush on more BBQ sauce. Repeat until the ribs are sticky, gnarly and coated. Leave on keep warm while you make the slaw.
To make the slaw, thinly slice the cabbage and fennel. Toss with salt and the juice of two limes. Add smashed cashew nuts and chopped dill.
Serve the ribs with a heaping pile of slaw and extra lime.

name: Sticky Soy Salmon Rice
description: Sticky soy-glazed salmon gently cooked over fragrant rice with sweet peppers and green beans. One-pan, family-friendly and most importantly delicious.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Serving 
Rinse the rice under cold water until it runs clear, then tip into a large lidded frying pan or shallow casserole dish.
Deseed the peppers and slice into thin strips. Trim the green beans and cut them in half. Trim the spring onions, then cut them into 2cm pieces — set a few aside for serving later.

Add the peppers, green beans and most of the spring onions to the pan with the rice. Pour over the hot chicken stock, bring to a simmer, then nestle the salmon fillets into the top. Cover with a lid and cook over a low heat for 15 mins.
In a small bowl, mix together the soy sauce and honey.
Once the time is up, drizzle the soy-honey mix over the rice and gently fold everything together with a spoon, taking care not to break up the salmon too much.

Serve up!
Kids Plate: Dish out the rice as is, with some sliced cucumber on the side.
Parents Plate: Dish out the rice and add the remaining spring onions and add a little extra soy sauce if you fancy, a drizzle of chilli oil and a wedge of lime.

name: Sticky Soy, Ginger & Garlic Chicken Traybake
description: Caramelised, savoury, gingery chicken that practically cooks itself. Chuck it all in the oven and you've got dinner sorted - plus an amazing chicken base for a week of exciting dinners.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C.
In a jug or bowl, mix together the kecap manis, sesame oil, grated garlic, grated ginger, and white pepper. Stir until combined. Add the chicken to a bowl and pour over the marinade. Set aside.
Trim the green beans then toss with olive oil, salt and pepper.

Add the chicken to a 37x29cm roasting tray. Pop in the oven for 10 minutes, then take out the oven and add the green beans, spread out nicely, sitting the chicken on the top  Pour over any remaining marinade and pop back into the oven for 10-15 minutes until the chicken is charred and cooked through.

Leave to cool before storing. The cooked chicken will last in the fridge for up to 5 days in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer. To reheat pop in the microwave and from frozen thaw in the fridge overnight. Eating now?  Serve with rice for a speedy meal.

name: Sticky Sumac Lamb Kofte
description: Lamb kofte spiced with a delicious cumin seasoning and matched up with tahini yog, charred onions and a sticky sumac glaze. Summer, let's have ya.
instructions: Get the BBQ fired up, then finely chop the parsley stalks.

Start by adding the lamb mince to a bowl along with the cumin, parsley stalks and grated garlic. Season with salt and pepper then mix with your hands for 3 mins, this is important for the texture of the kofte. Peel and cut the onions into 8. With damp hands, weigh the lamb mix into 60g balls. then mould the lamb mix into oblongs, then thread onto the skewers. Pop onto a plate, and refrigerate while you prep the rest.

For the glaze, mix the honey with sumac and the juice of ½ a lemon. Cut the remaining lemon halve into wedges for serving. Toss the onions in oil, salt and pepper, then chuck onto the BBQ. Cook for 6-8 mins, until soft and charred. Then put back in the bowl and toss with a couple tbsp of the honey glaze.
To a bowl, add the yoghurt, tahini, juice from the remaining lemon and season with salt and pepper — loosen with cold water if needed. Roughly chop the parsley.

Get your kebabs onto the heated grill, then cook for 6 mins until cooked through and charred. Spoon or brush the glaze over the kofte until nicely coated, then remove onto a plate. Warm the flatbreads.
Spread the tahini yoghurt on the flatbread and top with the kofte, onions, parsley, pomegranate seeds and a bit more sumac, if you like.

name: Sticky Tamarind Chicken with Coconut Slaw
description: If you're after a mid-week dinner that's healthy, high protein and just as delicious, you're in the right place. This Sticky Tamarind Chicken with Coconut Slaw is speedy to prepare and guaranteed to blow your socks off. Enjoy.
keywords: sticky tamarind chicken with coconut slaw
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Combine the tamarind, honey, half the vinegar and fish sauce in a small bowl. Set aside.

Season the chicken breasts with salt and pop a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a glug of oil and lay the chicken breasts into the pan. Sear for 6-7 mins on one side until the chicken has started to pick up some colour. You want to cook the chicken breasts 80% of the way through on this side, before flipping them over.

Once flipped, pour in the tamarind sauce and spoon over the chicken. Keep the pan on the heat and keep basting the chicken with the glaze. As the glaze reduces, it will cling to the chicken. Once the glaze is really coating the chook, sprinkle over the sesame seeds and slide under the grill for 4-5 mins until sticky and gnarly. Pull the chicken out of the pan and rest it for 5 mins.

Heat the rice following pack instructions, then set aside. Coarsely grate the carrots and chuck them into a mixing bowl. Finely chop the spring onions and coriander and get those in with the carrots. Add the coconut and remaining vinegar. Season with salt and toss into a quick carrot and coconut salad.
Divide the rice between warm bowls and add a handful of carrot salad. Cut the chicken into slices and divide between the plates. Spoon over the extra glaze and get stuck in.

name: Sticky Teriyaki Garlic Chicken
description: The garlic and the butter really bring this teriyaki sauce to the next level. Sticky and rich, it's a belter, Mob.
instructions: Drizzle some olive oil into a frying pan and add your chicken thighs. Cook until the skin becomes golden and crispy.
Start cooking your rice (see packet instructions).
Once your chicken thighs are crispy, remove from the pan.

Add butter to a clean pan. Once it has melted, grate your garlic cloves into the pan. Add teriyaki marinade and allow this to simmer for a few minutes. Add Sriracha, honey and allow the sauce to simmer again.
Add your chicken to the pan and coat it in the sauce. Add 6 tbsps of water and leave the sauce to bubble on a low heat for a few minutes.

Serve on a bed of rice and sprinkle some sesame seeds over the top. Pour the remaining sauce over the top of the chicken. Slice up some spring onions to use for a garnish and tuck into this delicious dish.

name: Sticky Toffee Baked Oats
description: A high-protein baked oat brekkie that’s packed with natural sweetness from the dates and bananas. Perfect for a meal prep breakfast – make a big batch on Sunday and you’ve got breakfast for the next few days.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Soak the dates in boiling water for 30 mins, then drain.
Blitz ½ the soaked dates with the oat milk in a blender until smooth.

Mash the banana in a large bowl. Add the oats, protein powder, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, vanilla, cinnamon, cardamom, and a pinch of salt. Pour in the blended date milk and stir well. Transfer to a baking dish and bake for 40-45 mins. If the top browns too quickly, cover with foil and continue baking.
For the toffee sauce, blend the remaining soaked dates with the oat milk, vanilla, maple syrup, sea salt and coconut oil (if using) until smooth. Add a splash of water to loosen if needed.
Add the toffee sauce to a saucepan and heat until bubbling. Then take off the heat.
Let the baked oats cool slightly before slicing. Drizzle with the toffee sauce and serve.
Portion the baked oats into containers for an easy grab-and-go breakfast. Store in the fridge for up to 3 days then eat cold or reheat before eating.

name: Sticky Toffee Hot Cross Bun Pudding
description: If you love sticky toffee pudding, hot cross buns, and bread and butter pudding, then we've got the perfect recipe for you.
keywords: Sticky Toffee Hot Cross Bun Pudding
Sticky Toffee Hot Cross Bun Pudding recipe
instructions: Halve the hot cross buns and spread one side with butter. Nestle into an ovenproof dish around 27cm in diameter.
Heat the oven to 170°C. Pour the milk and cream into a saucepan and heat until it's just about to boil, then remove from the heat.

Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, sugar, vanilla and a pinch of salt in a bowl until combined, then gradually add a small amount of the hot cream, whisking to combine. Continue slowly pouring the cream into the eggs while whisking, ensuring not to go too quickly or the eggs might scramble. Pour over the hot cross buns and let it soak for at least 30 mins (1 hr, if possible).
Transfer the pudding to the oven and cook for around 40 mins until puffed and golden.
To make the toffee sauce, put the butter, golden syrup and sugar into a pot. Melt over a low heat until everything has dissolved, then add the cream and a pinch of salt. Keep warm until serving.
When the pudding is cooked, remove from the oven and let it sit for 5 mins before serving with ice cream and a big drizzle of toffee sauce.

name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: The perfect end to a Sunday roast dinner, complete with a hot toffee sauce and served with a big scoop of melting ice cream.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160C. Butter a 2lb loaf tin, then use baking paper to line. Use an electric whisk to whisk the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, then add the treacle.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well with each edition. Fold in the flour along with a pinch of salt, it should have the consistency of a thick paste.
Add the dates to a pan with 250ml of water and bring the boil, once boiling, remove from the heat, add the vanilla and either use a potato masher or a stick blender to crush or blitz into a paste.

Now whisk in the bicarbonate of soda, it'll froth up a little. Tip into the other ingredients, mix well then spoon into the loaf tin and bake for 40 mins - 45 mins, until firm to the touch. Leave to cool in the tin.
Add the sauce ingredients to a pan and place over a medium heat. Whisk until the butter has melted and the ingredients have combined to make a glossy sauce. Add a pinch of salt.
Let the cake cool to room temp, then slice into chunky portions. Divide between bowls and spoon over the warm toffee sauce. Serve with a big scoop of vanilla ice cream.

name: Stir-Fried Green Beans with Tofu
description: Everything you love about Chinese restaurant green beans: the char, the garlic, the glossy sauce, turned into a proper vegetarian main with crumbled tofu.
keywords: Stir-Fried Green Beans with Tofu recipe
tofu and green bean stir-fry recipe
instructions: Trim the green beans and cut them in half. Peel and very roughly chop the garlic. Remove the tofu from its packaging, wrap in a clean tea towel and crumble into fine pieces.
Get your rice on. Cook the jasmine rice according to packet instructions.

Add 2/3 of the vegetable oil and the garlic to a cold wok or large frying pan. Turn the heat to medium-low and let the garlic slowly cook for 2–3 mins, until soft and lightly golden, it should smell mellow but not catch much colour. Remove the garlic and set aside.

Turn the heat up high. Add the green beans and let them sit and blister before tossing. Season with salt and cook for 3–4 mins until deeply green, slightly wrinkled and charred in spots, but still with some bite. Transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining oil to the pan, then add the crumbled tofu. Let it sit briefly, then stir. Cook for 4–5 mins until lightly golden. Add the soy sauce and sugar and toss to combine, then add the green beans and garlic back in.
Mix the cornflour with the water and stir until dissolved. Pour into the pan and cook, stirring frequently, for 1–2 mins until the sauce has thickened and coats everything glossily.
Serve up with the steamed jasmine rice.

name: Stocking Full Of Coal
description: Something to warm your hands and your chest on cold Christmas nights. Gently heated to be the perfect winter drink, garnished with a quill of cinnamon.
instructions: Heat the water and sugar in a pan until the sugar is dissolved.
Next, you’re going to want to add your spices and reduce the liquid until it has a nice, syrupy consistency.
Fill your chosen glass with ice, then add 1 tbsp of your Christmas syrup.
Add in your Kahlúa and vodka and mix to combine.
Finally, using a spoon, pour in your double cream on top.
Use your cinnamon stick to mix and combine the drink. Enjoy.

name: Store-Cupboard Tuna Pasta
description: This simple tuna pasta recipe is perfect. Absolutely perfect. Don't miss out the breadcrumbs – they add a lovely bit of texture.
instructions: Peel and finely slice your red onion. Peel and finely chop your garlic.

Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a good glug of olive oil, then add your onion to the pan. Cook these for about 15 minutes, until they are totally soft and just starting to caramelise a bit. Add occasional splashes of water if it seems like they are sticking at any point.
Drain your peppers from their brine, and rinse them in a sieve. Finely slice them.
Add your garlic and chilli flakes to the pan, as well as your sliced peppers, and fry them for 2 mins.
Tip your tinned tomatoes into the pan, and turn the heat down to low. Simmer these for about 20 mins.
Drain your olives and your tuna from any liquid, then tip these into the sauce. Simmer for 5 mins.
Cook your spaghetti in salted boiling water until it is al dente, about 7-8 mins.

Add a small glug of olive oil to a frying pan over a medium heat, and tip in your breadcrumbs. Toast these for about 3 mins until they are golden, then tip them into a bowl. Zest in your lemon, and add a pinch of salt, then mix to combine.

Tong your spaghetti directly into the sauce, and add a splash of pasta water. Give it a really good mix so that the sauce gets glossy and coats the spaghetti. Finely chop your parsley and get that into the pan, then season it to taste with salt and lots of pepper.
Tong your spaghetti onto plates and top with your lemony breadcrumbs. Serve it up.

name: Stracciatella Chocolate Overnight Oats
description: Inspired by the classic Italian ice cream, these Creamy overnight oats laced with dark chocolate and topped with thick Greek yoghurt and fresh strawberries make a delish prep-ahead breakfast.
instructions: Add the oats, chia seeds, vanilla and milk into a large bowl. Add the honey and whisk everything together, add a little more if you like it on the sweeter side. Finely chop the dark chocolate into small shards and stir through the oat mixture.
If you're making ahead, you can portion into containers at this point, otherwise just cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 5 hours or overnight.

To serve, hull and quarter the strawberries. Spoon the oat mixture into bowls, top with a dollop of Greek yoghurt and scatter over the strawberries. Finely grate over the remaining dark chocolate and finish with a drizzle of honey.

name: Strapatsada
description: These are eggs like you've never seen them before. Easy to rustle up and equally as delicious, you're gonna be in for a treat.
instructions: Heat the grill to high. Halve your tomatoes and pop them on a tray, then drizzle with oil, a scattering of oregano, and season with salt and pepper. Grill the tomatoes for 10 mins until charred and juicy.
Crack your eggs into a bowl and whisk well. Finely slice the garlic.

Add the butter to a pan over a medium heat, once melted add in the garlic, cooking for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Add the tomato purée and cook for another minute, then reduce the heat to low. Pour in the egg and gently cook whilst stirring so you get soft curds and a dreamy texture. Take it off the heat and fold through the tomatoes before seasoning with salt and pepper.
Toast your bread, top with your eggs, feta, dill, and another crack of black pepper.

name: Strawberries & Cream
description: This is our play on strawberries and cream, with a hint of numbing floral spice from Sichuan peppercorns and some banging homemade meringues. The strawberries get juicier the longer you leave them so feel free to make them well ahead of eating.
instructions: In a small dry frying pan, toast the Sichuan peppercorns over a medium heat until smelling fragrant and amazing. Leave to cool then roughly crush in a pestle and mortar and tip into a bowl. Quarter and cut the tops off the strawberries, add to the bowl with the peppercorns. Sprinkle over ⅔ of the icing sugar and squeeze over the lemon juice. Stir and leave to macerate for at least 1 hour.
Pour the double cream into a large bowl, then sieve in the remaining third of the icing sugar. Whisk together until the cream is just holding its shape.
Serve the strawberries and cream alongside the meringues for the ultimate summer pud.

name: Strawberries & Cream Cocktail
description: A summery clarified cocktail that's perfect for sipping on in the sun. Or at home on the sofa, You do you.
instructions: Cut the tops off your strawberries and masticate them to a pulp.
Pour in your lime, lemon, vodka, Cointreau (and St-Germain if you like it sweet) and mix well.
Leave this to sit for an hour then strain.
Pour your cream into a new container, then pour your cocktail through the cream, this ensures that all the cocktail is clarified. Let this sit for 3-4 hours to clarify.

Gently pour your liquid through a coffee filter, it will run slightly cloudy at first. Let this happen until it is dripping clear, then strain into a new container. This ensures all your drink is nice and clear and silky.
Re-pour your cloudy initial run off back through the top of the filter. Leave to filter, then bottle when finished.
Pour over ice and serve with a thin slice of strawberry on top.

name: Strawberries & Cream Overnight Oats
description: Creamy overnight oats with strawberry jam, tangy Greek yoghurt and toasted flaked almonds. Hardly any effort the night before means breakfast is sorted in the morning.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk all the oat ingredients together until combined. If you're making ahead, you can portion into containers at this point, otherwise just cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or until ready to serve.

When you're ready to eat, hull the strawberries and slice them in half. To serve, spoon a portion of the overnight oats into a bowl. Add a dollop of Greek yoghurt and swirl through some strawberry jam. Scatter over the toasted flaked almonds and top with the strawberries.

name: Strawberry Aperol Spritz
description: We've taken your favourite spritz and given it a makeover with some help from a few fresh strawbs and basil leaves. A delicious summer serve. Drink up.
instructions: First, muddle your strawberries with the sugar and basil in a mixing glass.
Add your Aperol and stir to mix.
Strain your mix into a glass over ice.
Pour in your Prosecco and then top with soda water. Garnish with strawberries and basil, and enjoy!

name: Strawberry Cheesecake Crackers
description: Martyn Odell (aka Lagom Chef) made us this delicious low-waste snack in fifteen minutes flat. A sweet little pick-me-up.
instructions: Start by washing the strawberries in water and removing the stalk and leaves from the strawberry, by twisting or carefully using a knife. Finely chop the stalks and leaves, they’re totally edible!

Slice the strawberries thin and pop them into a mixing bowl, sprinkle over the sugar, gently mix through then set to one side. Tear in some basil leaves and tip in the balsamic vinegar. Mix to combine.
In another bowl, whisk the double cream, icing sugar and vanilla essence until forming stiff peaks, soften the cream cheese in another bowl then gently mix together.
Now you are ready to build your mini cheesecakes, pipe or spoon the cheesecake base onto a cracker leaving a well for the strawberries to sit in. Spoon in the strawberries and some of their juice.
For a fancy garnish, top with extra some fresh basil and a little lick of the strawberry syrup.

name: Strawberry Cheesecake Honey Butter Toast
description: A summery, strawberry-packed alternative to French toast that you'll fall head over heels for.
keywords: Strawberry Cheesecake Honey Butter Toast recipe
instructions: Start by macerating the strawberries. Cut off the tops and then slice. Transfer to a bowl, add the brown sugar and toss together. Leave for 1 hr until the strawberries become juicy.
Heat the oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with baking parchment.
Beat together the soft butter, honey and light brown sugar, then cut the brioche rolls in half and spread both the cut and undersides with the butter mix.

Lay the brioche onto the lined baking tray. Bake in the centre of the oven for 18-20 mins, flipping halfway until deeply caramelised and crisp. Transfer the honey butter brioche to a wire rack and leave to cool for 10 mins.

Meanwhile whisk the double cream in a bowl until it is holding its shape. In a separate bowl, whisk together the soft cheese and vanilla extract to soften the soft cheese, then fold through the double cream.
To serve, lay a piece of brioche on each plate. Top with the cheesecake mixture and the macerated strawberries. Get stuck in.

name: Strawberry Daiquiri
description: We’ve taken one of the world’s most popular cocktails and dialled up the flavour with some help from our pals at Dead Man’s Fingers. The perfect summer serve.
instructions: First, freeze your strawberries.
To make the sugar syrup, pour 50ml of water into a pan, then in with your sugar. Heat gently and mix until everything is dissolved.
In a blender, add your Dead Man's Fingers Rum, lime juice, and 50ml of your sugar syrup along with the frozen strawberries. Blend until smooth.
Pour into your desired glass and garnish with a strawberry. Enjoy!

name: Strawberry Sando
description: A recipe styled after a Japanese konbini sandwich. This simple strawberry sando is a summer delight.
instructions: Whip the cream, maple syrup, vanilla and a pinch of salt in a stand mixer (or use a whisk) until you get medium-stiff peaks. It should easily hold its shape when scooped with a spoon. Add more maple syrup if you prefer it sweeter, then transfer to the fridge.
If making the sando, cut the crusts off the bread. If making the maritozzi buns, slice three-quarters of the way through your brioche buns so they open like a Pac-Man.
Cut the green tops of the strawberries in a ‘V’ shape to reveal strawberry hearts later.

For the sando, spread a generous amount of whipped cream over a piece of bread, then place 3 strawberries, narrow-side down (for the heart shape later), on the diagonal per slice of bread. Add another 2 strawberries in the empty gaps and spread another layer of whipped cream on top. Push the cream into any empty gaps, then add the other slice of bread on top and scrape more cream on the sides like icing a cake.
Lightly make a diagonal cut where the strawberries line is, so you know where to cut later.
Wrap the sandwich tightly in plastic wrap and chill for at least 20 mins.
Carefully remove the sandwich from the plastic wrap and slice to reveal the strawberries inside. Slice again to make four pieces, if you like. Enjoy!

For the maritozzi buns, add a dollop of cream into the back of the bun, then place a strawberry in the centre of the bun. Add 3-4 tbsp cream, then lightly press down on the bun to spread the cream evenly. Use a knife to scrape along the edge to make a flat surface. Add sliced strawberries along the outside and transfer to the fridge.
To finish, roll the bun in toasted nuts, if you like. Use kitchen paper or a brush to clean up the edges.
Chill for at least 20 mins, then cut in half to reveal the strawberry heart.

name: Strawberry and Basil Tonic
description: Cool yourself down with this refreshing, summer number. PS: if you’re not putting basil in your drinks, you’re missing out. It’s a nice switch up from mint.
instructions: Hull and quarter the strawberries. Zest and juice the limes.
Place the strawberries in a jug with 2 tbsp sugar and muddle until combined. If you don’t have a muddler, you can use a whisk or the flat end of a rolling pin.

Thinly slice the fresh basil leaves. Add them to the muddled strawberries and muddle until the basil leaves are broken down. Alternatively, for a smoother drink, you can throw everything into a blender.
Fill the jug with ice cubes, pour in the tonic water and stir to combine.
Combine the remaining 1 tbsp sugar with the lime zest and a good pinch of salt.
Rub lime juice on the rim of your glasses, using the limes from earlier, then dip the glasses into zesty sugar.
Pour the drink into the zesty sugar-rimmed glasses and enjoy!

name: Stuffed Chipotle Tofu Jacket Sweet Potatoes
description: Jacket sweet potatoes loaded with your leftover smoky chipotle tofu mince batch, melted Cheddar and fresh coriander. Big comfort food energy, and it's oven-hands-off for most of it.
keywords: Chipotle Tofu Jacket Sweet Potatoes recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Scrub and dry the sweet potatoes, then rub all over with a little oil. Transfer to a baking tray and roast for 30-40 mins until completely soft when pierced with a knife.
Pick the coriander leaves, thinly slicing the stalks.
Stir the coriander stalks through the chipotle tofu mince and reheat until piping hot, adding a splash of water if needed.
Split each sweet potato in half, spoon over the chipotle tofu mince and grate over the Cheddar. Finish with the coriander leaves and serve.

name: Stuffed Christmas Butternut Squash
description: The best Christmas vegan shout. The creamy coconutty tzatziki makes it.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Halve your butternut squash. Lay them on a tray and sprinkle with a teaspoon of all spice. Season with salt and pepper, add a drizzle of olive oil and roast for 1 hour until soft.
Add your chestnuts to a roasting tray and roast for 30 minutes until tender.
While the squash is roasting, prepare your tzatziki. Pour your coconut yogurt into a bowl. Grate the cucumber, squeeze any excess water out of them and add to the yogurt.
Add a handful of chopped mint, the zest and juice of a lime. Season with salt and pepper and mix together. Cover with cling film and leave to chill in the fridge.
Pour couscous into a bowl and cover with boiling water. Leave it to absorb the water, after which it will be ready to eat.
Finely chop garlic cloves and a red onion. Add it to a large frying pan with a splash of olive oil. Add a heaped teaspoon of all spice and mix everything together. Cook on a low heat for 3-4 minutes.
Remove your squash from the oven. Scoop out the flesh, being careful to keep the skins intact. Break up the flesh with a spoon and set aside.
Remove your chestnuts from the oven. Discard the outer shells and add the chestnut insides to the frying pan with the onions. Add the cranberries to the pan and mix everything together.
Add the couscous, bit by bit. Once it is all mixed in, add the squash. Cook everything for another 4 minutes and remove the pan from the heat.
Re-stuff your squash skins and place them back in the oven for another 20 minutes.
Serve the squash with big dollops of the tzatziki and any leftover mint, cranberries and chestnuts. Enjoy!

name: Stuffed Peppers With Garlic Orzo and Zhoug
description: We've stuffed Romano peppers here are with a mushroom, walnut and lentil mix and baked them with garlic orzo. Served with a punchy, spicy zhoug.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Put the peppers on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Roast for 15 mins. Carefully slice the peppers open lengthwise and scoop out the seeds.

Grab a cast-iron skillet with a lid that’s suitable for the oven.* Weigh out your orzo and heat up the stock, set aside. Mince 5 garlic cloves and then heat the skillet on medium-low with 4 tbsp of olive oil. Fry the garlic for 20 seconds, stirring constantly to stop it from burning. Add the orzo and stir to coat evenly with garlic oil, then add the stock and stir again. Place the peppers snuggly into the orzo, close the lid and bake for 30 mins.

While the orzo is cooking, make the filling. Finely dice the onion and mushrooms, mince three cloves of garlic and set each aside separately. Heat a frying pan over medium heat with a good drizzle of olive oil.

Fry the onion until translucent then add ½ tsp cumin, 1 tsp ras el hanout, ½ tsp paprika and 2 tsp tomato paste. Stir fry the spices for one minute, then add the garlic and mushrooms and a pinch of salt. Cook the mushrooms for 3-4 mins, then add the lentils, raisins and two-thirds of the walnuts. Cook for another 8-10 mins, until cooked through. If it becomes too dry, add a little more olive oil or a splash of water. Then add the Moscatel and turn the heat up high for a minute or so, until the vinegar evaporates. Season well with salt and pepper, turn off the heat and set aside.

To make the zhoug, add the coriander, chopped Jalapeño, ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp cardamom, ½ tsp red pepper flakes and 80ml of olive oil to a food processor and pulse until finely chopped but still chunky. Be careful not to turn it into a paste, there should be plenty of texture. Season generously with salt and pepper.

After 30 mins of baking, the peppers should be soft and the orzo should be perfectly cooked. Carefully fill the peppers with the mushroom mix. Close the lid and bake for 5 more minutes for the flavours to marinate.
When ready to serve, drizzle plenty of zhoug over the top and sprinkle the rest of the walnuts and a good squeeze of lemon.

name: Stuffed Squash with Pine Nut Agrodolce
description: This easy stuffed squash recipe is packed with wintry, caponata-esque flavours.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Rub the squash with a dash of olive oil and season with salt. Roast in the oven for 35-40 mins until just tender. Remove and allow the squash to cool until you can handle them.
Meanwhile, dice the aubergine into 4cm cubes and toss with plenty of salt. Set over a bowl in a sieve for 30 mins.
Dice the red onions, thinly slice the garlic and pick the leaves from the rosemary. Grab a large sauté pan and add 3-4 tbsp of olive oil. Preheat over a high heat.
Chuck in the red onions and two thirds of the rosemary. Cook over a high heat until golden brown, this will take 6-7 mins. Remove from the pan, leaving the olive oil behind.

Squeeze the excess moisture from the aubergine and add to the pan. Cook over a high heat until golden brown and tender. Add the red onions and rosemary back to the pan and chuck in the garlic. Cook for 1-2 mins then add the lentils. Toss together and season with red wine vinegar, between 1-2 tbsp.
Halve the squash lengthways and scoop out some of the flesh to create a big pocket. Toss the extra squash flesh through the aubergine and lentil mixture. Finely chop the parsley and stir through.
Stuff the mixture back into the squash skins and return to the oven for 15-20 mins.

To make the agrodolce, thinly slice the chillies and set a small pan over a medium heat. Add the agave and cook until amber. Add the chillies, raisins and capers. Add the remaining vinegar and rosemary along with the pine nuts. Season with salt and pepper and balance with more agave or vinegar if needed.
Remove the squash from the oven and pop onto a serving platter. Drizzle over the agrodolce and top with a big handful of fresh picked mint leaves. Serve with a wintry salad and crusty bread.

name: Sugar Cookies
description: Sweet, buttery biscuits coated in a crunchy sugar coating. These cookies might look plain but they taste anything but.
instructions: Heat your oven to 160°C Fan. Line two baking trays with baking paper.

Beat the butter and granulated sugar together in a large bowl with an electric whisk for 2-3 mins until light and fluffy. Scrape down the sides of the bowl, crack in the egg, add the vanilla extract and whisk again to combine.
Measure in the flour and baking powder along with a pinch of salt. Whisk until a smooth cookie dough.

For the sugar coating, put the remaining granulated sugar into a shallow bowl. Roll the cookie dough into equal balls weighing about 50g each. Dip each cookie in the sugar, rolling to lightly coat. Once coated in the sugar, place onto the lined baking trays and use the bottom of a glass to flatten into a cookie puck. Repeat until all the cookies are coated in sugar, leaving a decent amount of space between each one on the tray to allow for spreading.
Bake for 10-12 mins until very lightly golden. Leave to cool on the tray for 5 mins then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely. Yum.

name: Sumac & Charred Lemon Chicken Thighs With Tzatziki
description: Juicy roast chicken thighs with a tzatziki sauce. A proper zingy recipe that’s packed full of flavour. Incredible as a midweek meal or as part of a larger spread for a dinner party.
keywords: Sumac & Charred Lemon Chicken Thighs With Tzatziki Recipe
Sumac & Charred Lemon Chicken Thighs With Tzatziki
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Cut the lemon into quarters, then each quarter in half again. Tip into a large roasting tin. Nestle in the chicken thighs skin-side up, drizzle over the oil and season well with salt and pepper. Finally scatter everything with the sumac and put into the oven to roast for 40 mins until the skin of the chicken is super crisp and the lemon wedges charred.

For the tzatziki, coarsely grate the cucumber into a sieve set over a bowl and scatter with flaky sea salt. Leave to drain for 15 mins, then squeeze any of the excess moisture out. Tip into a clean bowl. Spoon in the yoghurt, finely grate in the garlic and zest of the lemon, then squeeze in the juice. Roughly chop ¾ of the mint and ¾ of the dill leaves and scrape into the bowl along with a pinch of salt and lots of cracked black pepper. Drizzle in the oil and gently fold in.

Spoon some of the tzatziki onto the base of a plate and add on the chicken thighs, spooning over any juices from the tray. Scatter over the remaining herbs, squeeze over the jammy lemon wedges and drizzle with a little more oil. Serve with chips or a big green salad.

name: Sumac Chicken
description: Juicy chicken thighs marinated in tangy sumac, garlic, and lemon, then cooked until golden and crisp. This Middle Eastern-inspired side is full of bold, zesty flavour and pairs perfectly with fresh sides like salad or tzatziki for a vibrant, easy lunch or dinner.
instructions: Peel and finely grate the garlic into a bowl. Add the sumac, 7-spice, chicken thighs and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then mix thoroughly. Set aside.
Add a drizzle of olive oil to a frying pan and set over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the chicken thighs and cook for 8-10 mins until cooked through and golden brown on both sides.
Slice the chicken into strips and pair it with your favourite base.

name: Sumac Chicken & Chickpea Pilaf
description: Fragrant rice simmered with chickpeas, cardamom and buttery parsley stems, finished with tender leftover sumac chicken and a cool dollop of yoghurt. A speedy midweeker if ever we saw one.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake.
Wash the rice in cold water until it runs clear. Pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the stems. Lightly crush the cardamom pods.

Melt the butter in a large frying pan with high sides over a medium heat. Stir in the cardamom pods, parsley stems, rice and chickpeas. Pour in the water and bring to the boil. Cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins.
Halfway through cooking, place the sumac chicken and roasted vegetables from the traybake on top of the rice. Replace the lid and continue cooking for the remaining time.
Remove the pan from the heat and leave covered for another 10 mins to finish cooking the rice.
Fluff the rice with a fork, then share between plates. Top with the parsley leaves and a dollop of Greek yoghurt. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

name: Sumac Chicken & Freekeh
description: We've taken inspiration from two great dishes: Palestinian Musakhan and Tabbouleh to create this quick and super flavourful weeknight dish. This recipe isn’t authentic in any way, but the next time you have the chance to try any of the traditional dishes, I would highly recommend.
instructions: For the dressing, combine the tahini, lemon juice and water in a small bowl. Stir together until creamy. Add 1 tbsp more water at a time if you want it looser. Taste and season with salt, then set aside.
Peel and finely grate the garlic into a bowl. Add the sumac, 7-spice, chicken thighs and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then mix thoroughly. Set aside.

Pour the water into a saucepan and bring to the boil. Stir through the freekeh, then put a lid on the saucepan and turn the heat down to low-medium. Simmer for 10-15 mins until the freekeh is cooked and has absorbed all the water.
Meanwhile, mince the parsley, stalks and all. Trim and quarter the cucumber, then chop into 1cm chunks. Zest half the lemon.
Add a drizzle of olive oil to a frying pan and set over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the chicken thighs and cook for 8-15 mins or until cooked through and golden brown on both sides.
Toss the parsley, lemon zest and cucumber into the freekeh with 20ml olive oil, then season with salt and pepper. Slice the chicken into strips. Share between plates and drizzle over the dressing.

name: Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake
description: Juicy, marinated chicken baked over soft aubergines and jammy onions with a tangy hit of sumac. Big flavours, minimal washing up and a perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C.
Finely grate the garlic into a bowl. Add in the 7-spice, sumac and pomegranate molasses with a generous drizzle of oil and season with salt. Toss the chicken through the marinade. Set aside.

Peel and cut the onions into chunky wedges, trim and chop the aubergines into 3cm chunks. Add both into a baking tray with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Season with oregano, salt and pepper. Toss together until evenly coated. Slide in the oven for 30-40 mins, until cooked through and softened.
Halfway through the veggies cooking time, place the chicken on top of the veggies and slide back in the oven for the remainder of the time, until cooked through.

Leave to cool before storing. The cooked chicken traybake will keep in the fridge for 3–4 days and in the freezer for up to 3 months (reheat gently in a low oven or microwave or you can defrost in the fridge overnight).Eating it now? For a quick meal, stir through some cooked orzo into the veggies.

name: Sumac Chicken Fatteh
description: Transform your leftover Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake into a traditional Middle Eastern Fatteh. With chickpeas, creamy tahini yoghurt and pitta crisps - it's full of crunch and packed with protein.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Sumac Chicken & Roasted Veg Traybake.
Shred the chicken from the sumac chicken traybake. Drain the chickpeas, reserving the liquid. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stalks.

Add the chicken, roasted veggies from the traybake, chickpeas and coriander stalks to a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add a splash of the reserved chickpea liquid and reheat until piping hot, adding more liquid if you prefer it saucier. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Meanwhile, finely grate the garlic into a bowl and squeeze over some lemon juice. Season with salt, then stir in the tahini and natural yoghurt. Loosen with a splash of cold water if needed, and taste, adjust with more salt, pepper or a little sugar if it’s too bitter.

Divide the hot chicken mixture between bowls. Spoon over the tahini yoghurt and finish with a sprinkling of sumac, the pitta crisps or croutons, and the coriander leaves. Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: Sumac-Spiced Salmon & Potato Traybake
description: Sumac-dusted salmon roasted over crispy new potatoes and burst cherry tomatoes, finished with fresh dill and a cooling dollop of yoghurt. An delcious weeknight meal all in one tray for minimal washing up.
keywords: Citrus-Spiced Salmon & Potato Tray Bake recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a large baking tray with baking paper. Halve the baby potatoes and tip them onto the tray along with the cherry tomatoes. Crush the garlic cloves with the back of a knife and add those too, then drizzle everything generously with olive oil and season well with salt and black pepper. Roast for 15 mins, until the potatoes are almost tender and beginning to turn golden.

Remove the tray from the oven and push the vegetables to the sides to make space in the centre. Nestle the salmon fillet in the middle, season with salt and scatter the sumac over everything. Return to the oven for a further 12-15 mins, until the salmon is just cooked through.
Remove from the oven and scatter over most of the dill. Spoon onto plates and finish with the remaining dill, a generous dollop of yoghurt and a pinch more sumac and black pepper.

name: Summer Bakewell Tarts
description: These bakewell tarts are a British classic, filled with frangipane and seasonal fruit and topped with almonds and buttercream.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180˚C fan. Grease a 12-hole muffin tray or 12 mini tart tins with butter or oil spray. Cut out 12 rounds of baking parchment to roughly fit the holes/tins.

Roll out the shortcrust pastry to about 3mm thickness and use a cookie cutter to cut out pastry rounds that fit in your prepared cupcake/muffin tray or mini tart tins, allowing extra to cover the sides – approximately 10cm rounds for a standard cupcake tray. Press these carefully into the cavities and refrigerate for around 30 mins.
Line the chilled pastry rounds with the baking parchment rounds and weigh down the paper with baking beans. Slide into the oven and bake for around 10–15 mins, or until starting to brown.

Make an egg wash by whisking together the egg yolk and milk. Remove the pastry rounds from the oven and remove the baking beans and paper. Brush all over with the egg wash and bake for another 2 mins. Remove from the oven and transfer to a wire rack to cool.

Meanwhile, make the frangipane: Whisk the eggs together in a small bowl or mug. In a separate bowl, use an electric whisk to beat the butter and sugar together for approximately 3 mins until thick and creamy. Beat in the ground almonds, then add the eggs a little at a time, beating between additions. Finally beat in the sifted flour.

Spoon 2 tsp of the jam into each pastry case. Spoon or pipe in a layer of frangipane, then top with a few untoasted flaked almonds. Return to the oven to bake for 20–25 mins, or until the frangipane is golden brown. Try to avoid opening the oven before 15 mins have passed, as the delicate structure of the frangipane means they have a tendency to sink. Remove from the oven and place on a wire rack to cool completely.
(Optional:) Melt the apricot jam with a dash of water in a small pan over a low heat and brush over the just-baked tarts to glaze.
(Optional): To serve, top each tart with a dab of almond buttercream, a fresh cherry and some toasted flaked almonds.

name: Summer Berry Pavlova
description: An incredible summer dinner party dessert, with a crisp and slightly chewy meringue, whipped cream and homemade seasonal berry coulis. A real showstopper.
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper. Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolks (you can use the yolks to make your own mayonnaise or dressing) and add the whites to a large bowl

Juice the lemon (you'll need a teaspoon) then add in with the egg whites. Using an electric whisk, whip the egg whites with the lemon juice until soft peaks form. Slowly beat in the sugar – 2 tablespoons at a time – and continue until stiff shiny peaks form.

Beat in the vanilla extract. Use a metal spoon to dollop 4 large spoonfuls of the beaten whites on to your prepared baking tray. Use the back of a spoon to hollow out the middle a little, creating a little dip in the centre. You'll need this to fill with cream and berries later.
Bake until almost completely dry but still slightly chewy in the centre – approximately 3 hours. Remove from the oven and leave to cool.

Meanwhile, make the berry coulis. Place all the ingredients in a medium-sized heavy-bottomed pan and bring to the boil over a gentle heat, stirring continuously. Reduce to a simmer and cook for 15 mins, or until thickened (add a splash more water if it needs it). Allow to cool, then transfer the coulis to a liquidiser or use a hand blender to purée. Finally pass it through a sieve, pushing through as much of the pulp as possible and discarding any seeds. Set aside until ready to serve.

When ready to serve, whip the cream with the sifted icing sugar by hand, until it forms soft swirls. Scoop the cream into the meringue, top with fresh berries (or any other fresh seasonal fruit) and drizzle generously with the coulis. Serve immediately.

name: Summer Chicken & Tarragon Club
description: Got leftovers from your Summer Roast Chicken Dinner batch? Check our ultimate club - thick-cut toast, shredded batch chicken, crispy Jersey Royals and fresh tarragon, all spread with the leftover spinach and butter bean purée.
instructions: Toast the farmhouse bread. Shred the lettuce and pick the tarragon leaves.

Spread the leftover spinach and bean purée generously on the inside of each slice of toast, then layer up the shredded chicken and sliced Jersey Royals. Top with the shredded lettuce and tarragon leaves.
Close the sandwiches and serve up.

name: Summer Chicken Chilli Con Carne
description: A lighter, veg-packed take on chilli con carne, finished with a charred lime corn salsa, creamy avocado and a dollop of soured cream. Bright, fresh and built for warm summer evenings.
keywords: Summer Chicken Chilli Con Carne recipe
instructions: Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over a medium-high heat. Add the mince and cook for 5-7 mins, breaking it up well with a spoon, until browned all over.

Finely dice the onion and fennel (save the fronds for garnish), then add both to the pan with a good pinch of salt. Cook for 5-6 mins, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to turn golden at the edges. Finely chop the garlic and add to the pan, cooking for a further minute, then add the cumin, smoked paprika and chilli flakes and stir for 1 min until fragrant.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 20-30 mins, until reduced by a third.

Dice the courgette and add it to the pan along with the white beans, plus a small splash of water if needed. Stir everything together and cook for a further 8-10 mins, until the courgette is tender. Season generously to taste.

While the chilli cooks, make the salsa. Char the corn directly over a gas flame or in a dry frying pan, turning regularly, for 3-4 mins until lightly blackened in places, then cut the kernels from the cob. You can use tinned sweetcorn instead — just drain well and char briefly in a dry pan for a minute or two to get some colour. Finely dice the red onion and roughly chop the coriander, then mix both with the corn kernels and the juice of the limes. Season well.

Halve, stone and slice the avocados. Divide the chilli between bowls and top with the corn salsa, avocado and a generous spoonful of soured cream. It reheats brilliantly the next day, with the flavour deepening overnight. Scatter over fennel fronds to finish, if you've got them.

name: Summer Crunch Salad
description: A salad all about texture. Crunchy crouton. Crispy smoked bacon. Delicious, soft cherry tomatoes. The Dijon dressing is the one.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.

Cut up your ciabatta into crouton sized pieces. Place in an oven dish and cover in olive oil. Grate the garlic cloves over the bread. Salt generously. Mix together and place in the oven for 45 minutes.
Peel and de-seed your cucumber. Chop the cucumber, lettuce, avocados and tomatoes.
Pan fry your bacon lardons, starting on a low heat and gradually bringing it up to a high heat. Remove when crispy. Save the bacon fat and pour over the croutons.

Dressing time. Chop your anchovies. Then pour 4 tbsp of olive oil, the juice of a lemon, dijon mustard, a sprinkling of salt, a grinding of pepper and the anchovies into a jar. Put on the lid and shake well.
Assemble the salad and enjoy!

name: Summer Gazpacho
description: Gazpacho has to be up there with the all-time great summer recipes. Trust me on the melon, it really, really works! B x
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Roughly dice 1kg of the tomatoes.
Peel and chunk up one of the cucumbers.
Roughly chop one of the peppers and the onion.
Smush the garlic cloves and de-seed and roughly chop the chilli.
Chuck the lot into your biggest mixing bowl with a handful of basil leaves.
Remove the crusts from the sourdough. Cut into croutons and add half to the gazpacho veggies.
Season the veggies generously with salt and pepper and add 60ml of olive oil and the sherry vinegar.
Toss the remaining bread with a glug of oil and a pinch of salt. Bake until golden and crisp, around 10 mins. Remove from the oven and leave to cool.
Leave the veggies to marinate for at least an hour, overnight in the fridge is ideal!
Meanwhile, dice the remaining veggies and melon into equal-sized pieces. I shoot for 2cm dice. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper to make a lovely mixed salad to garnish your soup.
Now, time to blend. Grab the gazpacho mix and blend until super smooth, you might have to do this in batches.
Season to taste and refrigerate until icy cold.
Give the soup a brief whisk to loosen, divide between chilled bowls and top with your salad and crunchy croutons. Finish with a few extra basil leaves, a drizzle of olive oil and get stuck in.

name: Summer Panzanella
description: This recipe uses peak season tomatoes and, along with a few other bits, can become either a panzanella by adding bread or a no-cook sauce for pasta. Jordon x
instructions: Finely slice your onion and add it to a small bowl with your red wine vinegar and a good pinch of salt. Mix well and set aside for at least 10 mins.
Dice then mince the garlic before adding it to a large mixing bowl.
Core and then cut your tomatoes into chunks, add to the bowl along with all of the juices they release.

Drain the onions and add to the bowl with the capers, basil, a large pinch of salt, a good drizzle of olive oil and squeeze of lemon juice. Mix well. Taste for seasoning – it should be bright and zingy, so add more salt/lemon juice as needed.
Now that the base is done, you can choose if you want to add bread and go for a panzanella or cook up some pasta and use it as a simple sauce.
For the panzanella, tear up a few large handfuls of sourdough (bread that’s a few days old works best), add them to the bowl and mix well, letting the bread soak up all of the tomato juice.
For the pasta (I like conchiglie), cook it in boiling salted water until al dente before draining, adding to the bowl with tomatoes, and mixing well. Allow that sit for a few minutes before plating.

name: Summer Roast Chicken Soup
description: The purée from your leftover Summer Roast Chicken Dinner batch becomes a velvety, comforting soup in minutes, just loosened with stock, and topped with leftover toastchicken and finish with cream and spring onions. Ready in under 10 minutes.
instructions: Finely slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish later.
Set a saucepan over a medium heat, and add the batch purée and the chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in the leftover chicken and the double cream and heat through for  2-3 mins.
Pour the soup into bowls, finish with a grind of black pepper and scatter over the spring onions.

name: Summer Roll Salad with Peanut Sauce
description: Punchy cold rice noodles loaded with carrot ribbons, cabbage, herbs and juicy prawns, all drizzled with a creamy peanut sauce and a zingy sweet chilli dressing. Add fresh chilli if you fancy a bit more heat!
keywords: Summer Noodle Salad with Peanut Sauce
Summer Noodle Salad with Peanut Sauce recipe
instructions: Peel the carrots, then continue peeling to make ribbons, or use a julienne peeler for thinner strands. Finely slice or use a peeler to shred the cabbage. Pick the mint leaves, discarding the stems, and roughly chop the coriander, stalks and all. Add all the veg into a large bowl with the prawns — optionally, cover with ice water until ready to use to keep everything super crispy and crunchy, or place in the fridge.
Cook the rice noodles according to packet instructions. Drain and rinse under cold water until cold to the touch.

To make the peanut sauce, stir the peanut butter and five spice together. Squeeze in the lime juice, stir and season to taste with soy sauce. If you need to loosen it, stir in 1 tsp of cold water at a time until you reach your desired consistency.
In another bowl, make the salad dressing — squeeze in the juice of the limes, stir through the sweet chilli sauce and season with soy sauce or salt.
Drain the veg and discard any ice. Toss the noodles and salad dressing together. Divide between plates, drizzle over the peanut sauce and scatter over the peanuts. Serve with lime wedges.

name: Summer Spring Onion Soup
description: Let's be honest – the UK isn't famous for its summers! So when it's raining, or you're just craving something comforting but light, this is the soup for you. It's French onion soup, but speedy and super easy to make.
instructions: Finely chop the white onions, finely slice the spring onions, crush the fennel seeds in a pestle and mortar (or use the back of a knife) and finely grate the garlic.  Grate the Parmesan and Cheddar, and then set it aside.

Melt the butter and olive oil in a large, heavy-based pan. Add the white onion with a good pinch of salt and gently fry over a medium heat for 10 mins until really soft, stirring frequently. Add the spring onions and crushed fennel seeds. Fry for 15-20 mins, stirring frequently until all the onions have collapsed, are really soft and are full of flavour. The more time and love you put into the onions, the better the soup will taste. You'll have to keep an eye at the end to make sure they don’t catch – adjust the heat when necessary.

Add the garlic, stir and cook for 2 mins, then add the flour. Increase the heat slightly and add the wine, stirring so the onions don't catch at the bottom of the pan. Pour in the chicken stock and bring to the boil.

Turn down the heat and simmer for 25 mins. If you want to add the optional pasta, do so 10 mins before the end of cooking time and add more hot water. Season with salt and pepper as needed, plus a squeeze of lemon to balance.

To serve, turn on the grill and toast the bread. Ladle the soup into small heatproof bowls, then place a slice or two of toast on top of the bowl. Top with a mound of grated cheddar, Parmesan and the herb mix, then place under the grill until the cheese is bubbling.
Serve with extra chopped chives and black pepper. Delicious!

name: Summer Steak au Poivre
description: If you want a summer steak recipe, this is it. Seared sirloin (or your favourite cut) with a crust of coarsely cracked black pepper, finished in a peppery cherry tomato sauce , it's got all the summer bistro energy and gets on the table in 30 mins.
instructions: Get the steaks out of the fridge at least 30 mins before cooking. Coarsely crush the peppercorns, then pat the steaks dry with kitchen paper, press the crushed peppercorns firmly into both sides and season generously with sea salt.

Heat a heavy-based frying pan over a high heat until smoking hot. Add the neutral oil and sear the steaks for about 3 mins per side for medium-rare, adjusting for thickness. Add the butter for the final minute and baste continuously as it foams. Remove the steaks to a warm plate to rest.

Lower the heat to medium. Finely chop the shallots and add them directly to the same pan. If using, add the green peppercorns now. Cook for 1-2 mins until softened. Halve the cherry tomatoes and add to the pan, cooking for around 8 mins until they burst and slump, releasing their juices into the peppery pan fat.

If using, pour in the brandy and let it bubble for a minute to cook off the alcohol, or just add a splash of water. Stir in the mustard until the sauce comes together, then squeeze in the lemon juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Slice the rested steaks and arrange on warmed plates. Spoon the peppery tomato sauce generously over the top and serve immediately.

name: Summer Tomato & Egg Cottage Cheese Pot
description: Ripe cherry tomatoes marinated in oregano until juicy, layered with cool cottage cheese, crunchy cucumber and a jammy egg. Perfectly for prep too.
keywords: Summer Tomato & Egg Cottage Cheese Pot
Summer Tomato & Egg Cottage Cheese Pot recipe
instructions: Halve the cherry tomatoes and add them to a bowl with the dried oregano, extra virgin olive oil and a generous pinch of salt and black pepper. Toss to combine and leave to marinate for at least 15 mins. The tomatoes will soften slightly and release their juices, which act as a dressing for the pot, so don't skip this bit, it's what makes them sing. Use the ripest tomatoes you can find, the juicier the better.
Meanwhile, bring a small saucepan of water to the boil. Carefully lower in the egg and cook for 7 mins, then transfer to cold water. Peel and halve. Slice the cucumber into half-moons.

Spoon the marinated tomatoes and all their juices into the base of a jar or pot. Add a layer of cottage cheese, then the cucumber slices. Top with the egg halves and tear over the fresh basil. Finish with a final pinch of salt and black pepper.
Eat straight away or seal and pop in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Summer Veggies With Tonnato
description: Good quality tinned tuna is the key to making a killer tonnato. It's salty, tangy, and the perfect dip for crunchy bits of summer veg.
instructions: To make the tonnato sauce, empty the can of tuna into a blender with the garlic clove, juice of the lemon, egg yolks and mustard. Blend until you have a smooth paste and then drizzle in the oils, with the blender running all the way through. You should have a thick, rich emulsion. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Prepare the vegetables and cut them in half lengthways.
Serve with a pot of tonnato sauce and dill for dunking.

name: Summery Chickpea & Feta Ceviche
description: A ceviche-inspired chickpea salad that's punchy, fresh and tangy. Creamy feta, jalapeño heat and loads of lime, with sweet potato and tortilla chips to spoon it all up. It's perfect for prepping ahead.
instructions: Add a few inches of water to a large saucepan and set over a high heat. Place the sweet potatoes in a steamer basket, set it over the pan and steam for 25-35 mins, until completely tender when pierced with a knife (smaller sweet potatoes will be ready sooner).

Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander, red onion, tomatoes and jalapeños, depending on how spicy you like it, you can add more or less jalapeños. Add to a large bowl and squeeze in the juice of the limes, then add the olive oil and honey. Drain the chickpeas and rinse, reserving their liquid. Tip in the chickpeas along with 2 tbsp of the chickpea liquid, season with salt and mix to combine.
Tear the feta into large chunks and fold gently through the chickpea mixture.
Once the sweet potatoes are tender, transfer to a chopping board, leave to cool slightly, then cut into slices.
To serve, spoon the chickpea and feta ceviche into containers with the sweet potato slices. Box up and store in the fridge until needed. Serve the tortilla chips alongside when ready to eat.

name: Summery Chickpea & Feta Ceviche
description: A ceviche-inspired chickpea salad that's punchy, fresh and tangy. Creamy feta, jalapeño heat and loads of lime, with sweet potato and tortilla chips to spoon it all up. Since we're not cooking the chickpeas, it makes a big difference to go for quality, the ones that come in a glass jar tend to be nicer.
instructions: Add a few inches of water to a large saucepan and set over a high heat. Place the sweet potatoes in a steamer basket, set it over the pan and steam for 25-35 mins, until completely tender when pierced with a knife (smaller sweet potatoes will be ready sooner).

Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander, red onion, tomatoes and jalapeños, depending on how spicy you like it, you can add more or less jalapeños. Add to a large bowl and squeeze in the juice of the limes, then add the olive oil and honey. Drain the chickpeas and rinse, reserving their liquid. Tip in the chickpeas along with 2 tbsp of the chickpea liquid, season with salt and mix to combine.
Tear the feta into large chunks and fold gently through the chickpea mixture.
Once the sweet potatoes are tender, transfer to a chopping board, leave to cool slightly, then cut into slices.
To serve, spoon the chickpea and feta ceviche into bowls with the sweet potato slices and tortilla chips alongside.

name: Sun-Dried Tomato Cottage Cheese Çılbır
description: A quick 15-minute meal, perfect for a work for home lunch or light dinner. High-protein? You bet.
keywords: Sun-Dried Tomato Cottage Cheese Çılbır recipe
instructions: Place a saucepan of water to the boil. Once boiling, gently drop the eggs in and cook for 6 mins, until jammy.

Meanwhile, pick the herb leaves, discarding the stalks. Trim and thinly slice the onion, place into a sieve and wash until cold running water until crispy. Add all three to a bowl, toss with the sumac and a pinch of salt.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl, swirl the pesto through. Top with the boiled egg and garnish with the onion salad. Enjoy with bread.

name: Sun-dried Tomato & Herby Yoghurt Lentil Bowls
description: The herby yoghurt dressing and salted cashews make these lentil bowls feel a bit luxurious. It’s the perfect thing to make when you’ve got your friends over.
keywords: Sun-dried Tomato & Herby Yoghurt Lentil Bowls
instructions:
Pour the boiling water from the kettle into a saucepan over
a medium heat and bring back to the boil. Add the eggs and
set a timer for 61⁄2 minutes (for soft-boiled).
Meanwhile, put the garlic clove and most of the parsley and basil,
stalks and all, into a mini food processor. Blitz until finely chopped.
Add the yogurt and blitz briefly to combine. Season the yogurt
with salt and black pepper to taste.
Get a large frying pan over a high heat. Tip in the sun-dried
tomatoes with their oil and the bag of spinach. Squeeze the
unopened lentil pouches with your hands to break up the lentils,
then open and tip them into the pan. Add a splash of hot water
from the kettle. Season with salt and black pepper, stir and leave
to heat through.
Drain the eggs into a sieve when cooked and run under cold
water until cool enough to handle, then peel and halve. Cut the
lemon into four wedges and roughly chop the cashews.
Spoon the lentils into four bowls. Drizzle over the herby yogurt,
then top each bowl with a halved soft-boiled egg. Tear over the
remaining herbs and scatter over the chopped cashews. Season
with salt and black pepper and serve with the lemon wedges.

name: Sunshine Beans with Crispy Feta Eggs & Radish Salata
description: A no-fuss midweek meal with sumac-pickled radishes, creamy beans and eggs fried straight into bubbling feta. Yes please.
keywords: Sunshine Beans with Crispy Feta Eggs & Radish Salata recipe
Sunshine Beans with Crispy Feta Eggs & Radish Salata
instructions: Strip the oregano from its stem and thinly slice the garlic. Finely chop the dill, and chop the radishes into 1cm chunks.
Stir together the honey, sumac, olive oil and the juice of half the lemons. Toss the radishes through and season with salt.

Add a drizzle of olive oil into a saucepan and place over medium heat.
