Once hot, add the garlic and oregano, cook for a couple of seconds until the smell mellows, then tip in the butter beans (and their liquid). Stir together and warm through, then reduce the heat to low while you crack on with the rest.

Place a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Crumble in the feta to roughly cover the base. Once it starts to sizzle and soften, crack in the eggs. Fry until the whites are set and the yolks still runny (or to your liking). Season with salt and black pepper.

Meanwhile, zest and juice the remaining lemon. Add a pinch of zest and a squeeze of juice at a time to the beans, tasting as you go until it’s as zingy as you like. Season with salt and black pepper, give it a final stir, then spoon into bowls.
Add the dill to the radishes and serve on top of the beans with the Feta fried eggs, finishing with an extra drizzle of olive oil and get stuck in.

name: Super Berry Chia Pudding
description: We’ve created a delicious and nutritious chia pudding pot to make in a big batch and enjoy throughout the week. It’s the perfect way to start your day or as a healthy sweet treat.
instructions: Add all the ingredients for the smoothie into a blender and blend until smooth. Stir the chia through and pour into boxes/jars, cover and place in the fridge until the chia swells up and the mixture thickens.

Crush or roughly chop the nuts. Place into a dry frying pan over medium heat and cook, stirring, until the nuts have toasted, 5-6 mins. Then, remove from the heat and stir the cinnamon and honey through until evenly coated. Season with a touch of salt, add to a plate and let cool fully. Transfer to an airtight container, and leave at room temperature.
Once you’re ready to serve, top the chia pudding with vanilla Greek yoghurt and some cinnamon nuts.

name: Super Easy Crêpes
description: The classic pancakes for Shrove Tuesday. Served simply with lemon and sugar, this is a recipe for pancake purists.
instructions: Tip the flour into a bowl along with a pinch of salt. Crack in the egg, pour in the milk and whisk everything together until a smooth, thin batter. Leave for at least 15 mins or cover with a plate/kitchen foil and leave in the fridge for up to overnight.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a little knob of butter. Swirl it round the pan to completely cover the base. Take a full large ladleful of the batter and pour it into the pan, instantly tipping the pan and moving the batter around so it completely covers the base in a thin, even layer.
Cook for one minute until the batter has set and is free from the pan and lightly golden. Flip the pancake in one movement, or use a spatula, and cook for another minute.
Slide out onto a plate and scatter over a good coating of the sugar and squeeze over the juice of as much lemon as you like. Repeat.

name: Super Easy Rosemary Sourdough Focaccia
description: A beautiful slab of golden focaccia, perfect for sharing with friends. Rosemary & salt is the only topping you need. Recipe by MOB Contributor Thomas Colson.
instructions: The day before you want to bake, place your flour, starter, table salt, and water into a large mixing bowl and combine with a spatula until it forms a loose, shaggy dough. Leave for 30 minutes.
Wet your hands and knead the mixture in the bowl until it becomes smooth and stretchy.
Pour 30ml olive oil into the bowl and rub it over so the dough is coated. Cover your dough on the counter and leave it overnight, for 8 to 12 hours.
The next morning, take your dough out. It should have doubled in size.
When your dough is ready, pour 15ml olive oil into a 39x28cm roasting tray.
Tip your dough into the roasting tray.
Wet your hands, then fold each corner of the dough into the centre so it resembles a square. Then flip the dough over.
Pour 15ml olive oil onto the top of the dough. Leave for another 4 hours in a warm place until it has risen by at least 50%.
Preheat the oven to 220°C / 425°F. Now press your fingers into the dough to make dimples across all of its surface.
Pick all the leaves off your sprig of rosemary then drop them onto the dough, then scatter across the Maldon salt.
Bake for 30 minutes until the dough is crunchy, brown, and crispy. Leave to cool then tuck in!

name: Super Green Brothy Chickpeas
description: Creamy chickpeas in a vibrant green broth. A comforting bowl that’s full of goodness and on the table in 20 minutes.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic cloves. Heat a glug of olive in a large pan set over a low-medium heat and sauté the garlic until fragrant. Remove half of the sautéed garlic and set aside.
Remove the tough stems from the cavolo nero, then roughly chop the leaves and add them to the pan.
Cook over a medium heat for 2 mins, then pour over about ⅓ of the stock. Pop on a lid and gently simmer for about 5 mins until the leaves have wilted slightly.
Transfer everything to a high-speed blender (keep the pan at the ready) and blend on high for a few mins.
Add another splash of olive oil to the pan and pour in the drained chickpeas along with the reserved garlic slices. Cook over a medium heat until warm.
Pour over the green broth from the blender, and stir through as much extra chicken stock as required to reach your desired consistency. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Divide between bowls and garnish with a spoonful of crème fraîche and a sprinkling of pink peppercorns.

name: Super Green Feta Saag with Spiced Ginger Sizzle
description: A comforting, veg-loaded saag with salty feta and a spiced ginger sizzle. It’s a delicious way to put your Super Greens & Garlic Sauce to work midweek.
keywords: Super Green Feta Saag with Spiced Ginger Sizzle recipe
Super Green Feta Saag with Spiced Ginger Sizzle
instructions: Before you begin, make the Super Greens & Garlic Sauce.
Peel and slice the ginger into thin matchsticks. Thinly slice the chilli.

Add the olive oil to a small frying pan along with the ginger and chilli. Set over a medium heat and cook until the oil starts to shimmer. Drop in the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 1 min until fragrant, then take off the heat.

Pour the Super Greens & Garlic Sauce into a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the garam masala and frozen spinach. Cook for 5–6 mins, stirring now and then, until the spinach has fully defrosted and everything’s warmed through.
Break the feta into bite-sized pieces and stir it through the green sauce. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Reheat the rice according to pack instructions, then divide between bowls. Spoon the green feta saag over the top and drizzle with the spiced ginger oil.

name: Super Green Halloumi Salad
description: Honey-glazed halloumi over peas, edamame and broad beans with giant couscous, all piled onto charred lemon yoghurt. Salty, sweet and sharp in every mouthful.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the edamame, broad beans and peas and cook for 3 mins. Drain and rinse under cold water, then remove the broad beans from their shells.

Cook the couscous according to the packet instructions. For wholewheat giant couscous that's 6-8 mins in boiling water. You can use any couscous if you can't get hold of giant wholewheat, and quinoa or any other grain works nicely in this too.
Cut the lemons in half. Put a large frying pan over a medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and lay in the lemons, cut side down. Cook for 4-5 mins, until nicely charred, then remove from the pan.

Cut the halloumi into thick slices and add to the pan with a drizzle of olive oil. Cook for 3 mins on each side, until deeply golden. Take the pan off the heat, squeeze the honey over the halloumi and turn to coat.

In a large bowl, whisk together the honey, vinegar, olive oil and a pinch of salt. Thinly slice the shallot and add it to the bowl. Chop half the parsley and add that too, along with the beans and couscous, then give it all a good stir.

In a separate small bowl, chop the remaining parsley, saving a few leaves for garnishing at the end. Add the Greek yoghurt, squeeze in the juice of one of the charred lemons, grate in the garlic, then add the remaining tsp of honey and a big pinch of salt. Stir together.
Spread the herby yoghurt between plates, top with the bean salad and then the halloumi. Sprinkle over the reserved parsley and serve with the remaining charred lemon halves for squeezing over.

name: Super Green Pasta with Cashew Sesame Sprinkle
description: This is one of my favourite sprinkles and I’m so happy to be sharing it with you. Keep it refrigerated and sealed in a jar for up to a month.
instructions: In a blender, pulse the cashews, sesame, and ¼ tsp garlic powder until you have a crumb the texture of bulgur wheat. Taste and season with salt. Tip into a jar, set aside (it will make plenty more than you need, you can keep it in the fridge, sealed, for up to 1 month).

To the empty blender, add the spinach, basil (keep a few for garnish), miso, 25ml olive oil, 30g tahini and the whole tin of butter beans with the liquid until smooth. Taste and season with salt, if needed.

Cook the pasta according to the package instructions, to slightly al dente. Drain and keep some pasta water. Add the pasta back to the pan with the sauce and stir to combine and heat through. Taste and season with salt and some lemon juice.
Serve the pasta with a generous helping of cashew sprinkle and plenty of pepper and olive oil. Garnish with some basil leaves and a zest of lemon if using.

name: Super Green Risotto
description: This risotto gets its flavour and colour from a good amount of spinach and basil. It might look like The Incredible Hulk but it's got a pretty subtle flavour.
instructions: Bring a large pan of water to the boil, then add the spinach and cook for a minute, then drain through a sieve and set aside to cool a little. Peel and finely chop the onion. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat, add a large glug of olive oil then add the onion along with a big pinch of salt. Fry until softened but not colouring, it should take about 10 mins.

Press the spinach into the sieve to try and squeeze out as much moisture as you can, then add to a blender along with 100ml of the stock and the basil. Blitz into a purée, season well with salt and pepper. Grate the parmesan into the purée and set aside.

Once the onion had softened, crush or finely grate the garlic into the frying pan. Add the garlic to the pan and sizzle for a minute further, then add the risotto rice. Stir and toast until the rice is coated in the oil and beginning to make a gently popping sound. Then pour in the wine, and bubble down by half, around 2-3 mins. Then add a big splash of stock and stir well.

Continue to add the stock, a big splash at a time, making sure you don’t add any more until each splash has been fully absorbed. Once you’ve used all the stock, check the consistency of the rice, if it's still a little too al dente, add a little more stock and continue to cook, it should have a slightly thicker consistency than a traditional risotto at this point.
Fold in the spinach and parmesan purée along with the 30g butter and the lemon juice. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Scoop into bowls and top with a spoon of créme fraîche, extra parmesan, plus a scattering of toasted pumpkin seeds and parsley leaves. Finish with a crack of black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Super Green Soup With Crispy Chickpeas
description: A mega-green, protein-packed soup that’s as vibrant as it tastes. Silken tofu and edamame make it creamy without cream, while the crispy chickpeas on top bring the crunch.
keywords: Super Green Soup With Crispy Chickpeas
Super Green Soup With Crispy Chickpeas recipe
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. Pat the chickpeas dry with kitchen paper and toss them with half of the olive oil, chilli flakes, salt, and pepper. Spread them out on a baking tray and roast for 15 mins, or until golden and crisp.

While the chickpeas roast, slice the onion and slice the garlic. Heat the remaining olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 mins, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Tip in the edamame, spinach, and vegetable stock. Simmer for 5 mins, until everything is tender and the spinach is wilted.

Add the silken tofu and basil to the pot, then blitz everything with a stick blender until smooth and vibrant green. Season generously with salt and pepper to taste. Alternatively, blend in a food processor.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the crispy chickpeas. Finish with an extra pinch of chilli flakes if you like it hot and some basil, if you like.

name: Super Green Soup with Poached Egg
description: A hearty green soup with mega tasty sage croutons. I used beans instead of using potato or bread to thicken this one. How very on-brand, eh? If you too want to feel like the epitome of health, go ahead and make it.
keywords: Super Green Soup with Poached Egg
Super Green Soup with Poached Egg recipe
instructions: Finely slice the red chilli, pick the sage and finely dice the sourdough. Strip the leaves off the kale and finely slice the garlic.

Heat half the oil in a large pot and add the garlic. Cook over a medium heat for 3 mins. Add the fennel seeds and continue to cook for 1 min. Pour in the stock, bring to the boil, pop on a lid and reduce to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 mins. Allow to cool slightly (you could start the croutons) before adding the kale and cooking for 4 mins. Add the beans, then set aside.
Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan set over a medium heat, then add the sage, chilli and diced sourdough. Cook until golden and crisp, then remove from the pan and set aside.

Bring a small pan of water to the boil. Crack an egg into a bowl, then carefully drop the egg into the water, turning the heat down as low as it can go. Cook for 3 mins, then remove from the pan and drain. Repeat with the remaining eggs and set aside.
Blend the soup until smooth, then season with a squeeze of lemon, adjusting to suit your taste. Ladle into bowls. Top with the poached egg, crispy croutons and lemon zest.

name: Super Green Spiced Halloumi & Rice
description: If you love saag paneer, you’re going to love this dish that is inspired by it. Golden halloumi stirred into a spiced creamy spinach and pea mixture.
instructions: Chop the halloumi blocks into 2cm chunks. Trim the chilli and finely chop. Trim, peel, and grate the garlic and ginger.
Place a large frying pan on medium heat with a splash of oil. Once hot, add the halloumi and sear on all sides until golden, 5-8 mins. Set your halloumi aside afterwards.
Add a fifth of your spinach into a blender with the yoghurt and 20ml of water, blend until completely smooth.

Add another splash of oil into the now-empty frying pan on medium heat. Tip the garlic, ginger and chilli into the hot oil, season with salt and cook stirring for 2-3 mins. Add the garam masala and black pepper through, cook for 1 min.

Add the rest of the spinach, a handful at a time, into the spiced mixture and cook until wilted, 4-5 mins. Then, add the frozen peas and cook until hot, 2-3 mins. Remove from the heat then stir in the blended spinach yoghurt. Add the halloumi back in and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Cook the rice according to package instructions. Serve the rice and the super green spiced halloumi with lemon wedges on the side.

name: Super Greens & Garlic Sauce
description: An easy blitz-it-and-go sauce loaded with herbs, all the green veg and a good hit of garlic. One batch made and midweek meals are practically done.
instructions: Defrost the spinach. Thinly slice the onions. Peel the garlic cloves and gently bash them. Strip the cavolo nero leaves from the stalks and roughly chop the leaves. Roughly chop the parsley, stalks and all. Roughly slice the courgette.

Add the olive oil to a large saucepan and set over a medium heat. Add the garlic and let it sizzle gently for a couple of minutes until fragrant, don’t let it go golden. Tip in the sliced onions and cook for 5–6 mins until soft and translucent.
Add the cavolo nero and parsley to the pan and cook, stirring regularly, until just wilted. Take the pan off the heat and leave the greens to cool slightly.
Once cooled, transfer the greens to a blender with the spinach, courgette and vegetable stock. Blitz until smooth.

Pour the sauce back into the empty saucepan and bring to the boil over a medium-high heat. Turn the heat down to medium and simmer until the sauce thickens to your liking. Taste and season to your liking with salt, black pepper and the juice of the lemon.
Pour the sauce into a clean, heat-safe jar and seal tightly. Let it cool completely before storing. If sealed, it’ll keep at room temp for up to a month. If unsealed, chill and use within 2 weeks.

name: Super Greens Pasta
description: A speedy, feel-good pasta powered by our Super Greens & Garlic Sauce. Bright, herby, cheesy and ready in 15.
instructions: Before you begin, make the Super Greens & Garlic Sauce.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Drop in the pasta and cook following pack instructions. Before draining, scoop out 100ml of the pasta water and set it aside.

Tip the cooked pasta back into the empty saucepan. Pour in the Super Greens & Garlic Sauce and place over a high heat. Stir well until heated through. If the sauce feels a bit thick, loosen it with a splash of the reserved pasta water.
Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Divide between bowls and finish with plenty of freshly grated Parmesan.

name: Super Nutty Granola Bars
description: Ditch your shop-bought granola bars for our homemade version. Packed with nuts, seeds and sticky fruit, these are not only ridiculously easy to make but also miles better than anything you’ll find in the shops.
instructions: If you fancy extra depth of flavour, lightly toast the almonds, cashews, pumpkin & sunflower seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for a few mins until golden. Set aside to cool slightly.
Combine all dry ingredients in a bowl.

In a small saucepan, gently warm the date syrup, almond butter & vanilla over a low heat until smooth and glossy. 
Pour the warm mixture over the dry ingredients and stir quickly to coat everything evenly.
Line a tray with baking paper. Tip in the mixture and press it down as firmly as you can, use the back of a spoon or your hands.
Chill in the fridge or freezer for 1–2 hours until set.

Slice into bars. If you’re feeling fancy, drizzle or dip the bars in melted dark chocolate, then chill again until the chocolate sets. Once ready, wrap the bars in baking paper and chill or freeze until needed (these last for a week in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer).

name: Super Nutty Salad
description: This one’s perfect for using up all those odds and ends of nuts and seeds hiding in your cupboard. Crunchy, punchy and packed with plant power, it’s a brilliant make-ahead lunch or light dinner.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C.
Add the nuts and seeds to a baking tray and roast for 12 mins, or until golden and fragrant. Set aside to cool.
Make the dressing. Peel and grate the ginger and garlic into a small bowl. Whisk together with the olive oil, soy sauce, juice of 3 limes, and rice wine vinegar. Season with salt and pepper.

Rinse the quinoa and cook according to pack instructions. With 9 mins left on the timer, add the edamame to the pot. With 2 minutes left, add in the broccoli florets. Drain and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking, then leave to cool completely.
Prep the salad. Peel the carrot and cut into fine matchsticks. Finely chop the coriander.

In a large bowl, toss together the cooled quinoa mix, carrot, chopped coriander, rocket, and roasted nuts and seeds. If eating immediately, drizzle over the dressing and mix well. If meal prepping, store the dressing separately and add just before eating.

name: Super Quick Moussaka
description: A moussaka without the faff of a béchamel sauce. Rich and delicious - one for the Dinner-Party MOB.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Finely slice your aubergines lengthways. Place on a rack, cover in salt, pepper and olive oil. Bake for 15 minutes.
Crumble the whole block of feta into a bowl with the ricotta, the zest of a lemon and an egg. Season with salt, pepper and olive oil. Mix everything together and set aside.
Finely chop the onions and cloves of garlic. Fry in a large sauce pan until soft and add your lamb mince. Allow it to brown.
Add your cinnamon and dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper and add a large handful of chopped parsley. Mix together.
Add a tin of chopped tomatoes. Mix and cook over a medium heat for 8 minutes until the sauce has thickened. Remove from the heat.

Layer time. Spoon half of your lamb mixture into a baking dish. Cover the mixture with half of your slices of cooked aubergine. Cover the aubergine with the other half of the lamb mix and cover this with your remaining aubergines. Cover this with your ricotta mix and place under a hot grill for ten minutes, or until the ricotta mix starts to get little burn marks over on top.
Remove from the oven, slice up and enjoy!

name: Super Seed Sprinkle
description: A nutty, spicy, and extremely addictive sprinkle made from a mix of toasted seeds and quinoa. You can put this on literally everything.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Cook the quinoa in plenty of water for 10 mins, then drain well. Spread over a large baking sheet and drizzle with a little olive oil. Bake for 25-30 mins, stirring every 10 mins, until golden and crispy.

Spread the pumpkin seeds over a large baking sheet. While the quinoa is baking, roast the pumpkin seeds on the shelf below the quinoa for 7 mins, then add the sunflower seeds, linseeds and sesame seeds and roast for another 10 mins, or until golden, tossing once or twice.

Remove the seed mix from the oven (it will probably be done before the quinoa), then add the chia seeds and tamari to the sheet (add the lesser amount of tamari if your preference for saltiness is low). Mix well.
Once the quinoa is done, tip it onto the seed sheet. Use a fork to toss everything together, sprinkle over the nutritional yeast and return to the oven for 2 more mins.
Transfer the quinoa and seed mix to a jar and shake. Store in the cupboard for five weeks or more.

name: Super Simple White Risotto
description: The most simple risotto - the onion, garlic and white wine form the perfect base for this wonderfully easy dish.
instructions: Dissolve your vegetable stock cubes in 1 litre of boiling water. Finely chop the garlic and onions. Add your onions to a pan with a glug of olive oil and 2 tbsp of butter. Cook the onions on a low heat until soft and translucent.

Add your garlic and stir it in. Cook for a further minute and pour in your wine. Bubble the wine off. Add the rind from your Grana Padano, or Parmesan. This will impart its flavour throughout the risotto cooking process. Mix it in and then pour in your rice.
Stir your rice until it starts to toast in the pan. At this point, start adding your vegetable stock bit by bit. Keep beating the rice to release the starch. This will make the dish extra creamy.

Keep adding vegetable stock and beating the rice until it is creamy and cooked through. This should take about 30 minutes. You want your risotto to be a loose, creamy consistency. You should not be able to fit it in a mould.

Once the rice is cooked, add 150g of grated Grana Padano and stir. Add a heaped tablespoon of butter and season generously with salt and pepper. Beat it in, remove the Grana Padano rind and serve up your risotto. Grate more Grana Padano onto each dish, add a drizzle of olive oil  and a nice crack of pepper and tuck in!

name: Supergreen Matcha Smoothie
description: A fresh, punchy green smoothie packed with fruit, protein and matcha goodness. Bang everything in a blender and you’re done. Ridiculously easy.
instructions: Chuck the banana, mango, pineapple, spinach, matcha powder, protein powder, yoghurt, almond milk and honey into a blender. Add a handful of ice, if using, then blitz until smooth and creamy.
Pour into a glass and dust with a little extra matcha powder, if you fancy.

name: Supergreen Matcha Smoothie Bowl
description: A thick, zingy green smoothie bowl packed with protein, matcha and creamy yoghurt. Blitz, top with whatever you like and dive in.
instructions: Chuck the banana, mango, pineapple, spinach, matcha, protein powder, almond milk, skyr, honey and chia seeds into a blender. Blitz until completely smooth and creamy – you want it super thick, so use a tamper or stop and stir between blends if needed.
Scoop the smoothie into a bowl. Top with sliced kiwi, strawberries, a sprinkle of desiccated coconut and some granola, if using.

name: Surendra's Curry
description: Wagamama presents the most delicious, fiery chicken curry with deep-fried sweet potato gratings on top. Get on it MOB.
instructions: Start by soaking the fennel seeds in water for at least 30 minutes. Once soaked, drain the fennel seeds and blend them with the jalapeños to a smooth paste.

Finely dice the onions. Add a splash of vegetable oil to a frying pan and once hot add the chilli powder, turmeric and cumin. Gently cook the spices for 4 minutes. Add the onions to the pan as well as the ginger and garlic paste and cook them until the onions start to become soft.

Dice the chicken and add to the frying pan along with the fennel and jalapeño paste. Sear the chicken and then add the tamarind paste and the coconut milk. Add a large pinch of salt and let the curry simmer for 30 minutes.

Time to move on to the deep fried sweet potato! Peel and grate the sweet potato onto some kitchen cloth to soak up any extra moisture. Fill a medium sized saucepan with the vegetable oil and place it over a medium heat. Deep fry the grated sweet potato in small batches for 3 minutes until crispy, adding salt to the saucepan with each batch. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on a paper towel to soak up the excess oil.
Get the rice on! Cook it according to the instructions on the packet.
When everything is ready, serve the curry on a bed of rice and garnish with the deep fried sweet potato. Then dig into this irresistible fiery curry! Enjoy!

name: Surf 'n' Turf Patty Melt
description: Akwasi (@akwasibmensa) came into the studio to show us how it’s done with his surf and turf shito patty melt. So much flavour, perfect for any night.
instructions: Thinly slice your onions and add to a pan with a good glug of oil and let it cook for 15 to 20 mins until translucent.
Meanwhile, thickly slice your sweet bread in a separate pan and fry until golden then set aside.
Preheat your oven to 180°c.
Heat your pan with the butter until very hot then add your patties. Season with salt and pepper and sear them on both sides.
Add the shito chilli sauce to your onions and let them cook for just a few more mins on low heat until it’s all nice and caramelised.

Now we’re ready to layer it all up. First, grab your toasted bread then add 3 slices of Swiss cheese, a slice of American cheese on top, your cooked patty, some more cheese, then a dollop of shito onions and another slice of toasted bread.
Pop your surf and turf sandwich into the oven for just 5 mins to heat it through, then enjoy!

name: Surf 'n' Turf Summer Salad
description: This whole dish comes in at under a tenner. Chorizo and squid is potentially the ultimate surf 'n' turf combo.
instructions: Peel, pit and mash all three of the avocados.
Thinly slice the spring onions and coriander and add to the avocado mash. Squeeze a lime into the mixture and add salt, pepper and olive oil. Mix well.
Slice your new potatoes in halves and boil for 15 minutes or until cooked all the way through.
Slice the chorizo into chunks and the squid into rings. Cook the chorizo in a pan with some olive oil and then add the squid when the chorizo begins to cook.
Add pepper and lemon juice and continue to cook. Avoid the squid from turning rubbery by not over cooking it.
Once the potatoes are cooked, unevenly mash them with their skins still on.
Serve in a bowl with the guac and the cooked surf ‘n’ turf. Grab a fork and dig in.

name: Swedish Meatballs with Cucumber & Pea Salad
description: Swedish meatballs are a proper treat and are perfect to make ahead. I basically grew up having these weekly, so to me they are like nostalgia on a plate, move over IKEA, these are where it's at.
keywords: Swedish Meatballs with Cucumber & Pea Salad
Swedish Meatballs with Cucumber & Pea Salad recipe
instructions: Add the breadcrumbs and milk to a large bowl and leave to hydrate for 5 mins. Add the egg, season with salt and black pepper, then add the pork and beef mince. Mix thoroughly, this is best done with your hands. Pop the mixture in the fridge while you prep the potatoes.
Peel the potatoes and cut into quarters. Add to a large saucepan of well-salted cold water, bring to the boil and cook for 15-20 mins, until tender. Drain and set aside, keeping the pan.
While the potatoes are boiling, roll the meatball mixture into balls slightly smaller than a ping pong ball, wet hands help here. Return to the fridge while you make the salad.

Defrost the peas. Then add the white wine vinegar, water and sugar to a large bowl and season with salt. Thinly slice the cucumber (use a mandoline if you've got one) directly into the bowl. Add the peas, finely chop the dill and stir everything together. Set aside. The peas may turn a little darker as they sit in the pickle, but they'll still taste great.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and add the vegetable oil. Once hot add the meatballs and fry for 2-3 mins until golden on one side, then flip and fry for another 2-3 mins (you might need to do this in batches). Gently roll the pan to encourage them to brown evenly, this helps keep them nice and round too. They should be cooked through after about 8-10 mins total. Remove from the pan and set aside.

In the same pan, melt the butter for the gravy over a medium heat. Add the flour and let it toast for 2 mins, then gradually pour in the milk, making sure to scrub all the caramelisation off the base of the pan to infuse the gravy. Cook for 3-4 mins, stirring, until thickened. Stir in the dark soy sauce and season with salt and black pepper. Return the meatballs to the pan to warm through.
For the mash, return the pan with the potatoes over a low heat, add the milk and mash until smooth. Add the butter, season generously with salt and stir to combine.

Serve the meatballs and gravy over the mash with the cucumber and pea salad alongside. This recipe might seem like it has a few components (which isn't untrue) but it's all pretty straightforward and is brilliant to make ahead. The meatballs are great to freeze once rolled cooked or raw, and the mash can also be frozen in portions. The pickle can be made a week ahead too.

name: Swedish Spaghetti Meatballs
description: A wholesome, simple, warming dish. Big hearty meatballs with a rich meaty sauce. Go on...
instructions: Add white bread (without crusts) into a bowl and cover with whole milk. Squeeze it together and set aside until the milk is absorbed.
Finely chop onion. Add the all spice and fry until soft. Remove from the heat.
Grab a big mixing bowl. Add your soaked bread, the pork and beef mince, onion, egg yolks, a handful of finely chopped parsley stalks, a grated garlic clove, salt and pepper.
Mix it all together. Divide and roll into 20 balls. Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Heat a large pan. Add a drizzle of olive oil and add your meatballs. Cook for 5 minutes on each side. Remove from the heat when they are brown and caramelised all around.
Get your tagliatelle on the boil.
Set meatballs aside. Drain excess oil from the pan.
Place the pan back on the heat. Add butter. Allow it to melt and add a tbsp of flour. Whisk it in. Add 500ml of beef stock, cider vinegar and a good grind of pepper.
Cook until the sauce has thickened and then reintroduce the meatballs. Throw in a handful of chopped parsley and mix it in.
Serve the meatballs on the tagliatelle with any leftover parsley leaves scattered on the top. Enjoy!

name: Sweet & Sour Aubergine
description: Here's another one to add to your roster of fakeaway meals. The perfect dish to cook up when you're feeding a crowd, the aubergine soaks up all the flavours.
instructions: Roughly chop your aubergines into 3cm wedges. Add the chunks to a colander, then sprinkle with 2 tbsp table salt, toss well, then set aside over a bowl to drain.
Peel your ginger and garlic, and pound them in a pestle and mortar until broken and bruised.

Cut off the tops and remove the stem from the peppers, then slice into 3cm chunks. Slice the spring onions into 3cm lengths. Finely slice the chillies. Peel the onions and slice into wedges. Set all the prepped veg aside.
Pat the aubergine chunks dry with some kitchen paper or a tea towel. Tip the cornflour into a bowl, add the aubergine chunks and toss to coat.

Tip the vegetable oil into a large saucepan until it comes halfway up the side. Heat to 180ºC. Add the aubergine chunks and fry for around 2 mins until crisp, then drain on a plate lined with kitchen paper.
Mix the ingredients for the sauce together until smooth.

Heat a large frying pan or wok over a high heat. Add 2 tbsp vegetable oil to the pan, then tip in the peppers and cook until the skins are blistered, around 4-5 mins. Then use a slotted spoon to remove from the pan. Add the onion wedges to the pan and fry for 2 mins then add the spring onion along with the bashed ginger and garlic and sliced red chilli, fry for 2-3 mins further, then return the peppers and aubergine to the pan along with the sauce. Toss until glossy and thickened. Taste for seasoning and balance of sweet and sour, adding more sugar or vinegar if needed.
Spoon the rice into bowls, and top with the aubergine mix. Top with sesame seeds and enjoy.

name: Sweet & Sour Cauliflower
description: We’ve cracked the secret to the best sweet and sour sauce in this vegan riff on a Cantonese classic. It’s sticky, yum and everything you’d want from a takeaway.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C.

Cut the cauliflowers into medium-sized florets. Roughly chop the stalks and the leaves (the best bit in our opinion) then divide between two baking trays. Season well with salt and black pepper then drizzle with a good glug of neutral oil. Spread out into a single layer so everything cooks evenly. Roast for 25–30 mins until tender and a little charred.

Sauce time. Measure the ketchup, soy, pineapple juice, sugar and rice vinegar into a small saucepan. Place over a low heat and cook until the sugar has dissolved, then bring to the boil. Measure the cornflour into a small bowl, add 1 tbsp of water and mix to a milky smooth paste. Pour the paste into the boiling sauce, stir it in and cook for 3–4 mins until the sauce has nicely thickened. Keep warm.

Cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Once cooked,put the frozen peas into a bowl and pour over boiling water, leave to defrost for 1–2 mins until the peas turn bright green. Drain in a sieve then tip into the rice. Finely grate in the ginger and stir everything together. Keep warm.
Thinly slice the spring onions (green and white parts).
Divide the rice between four bowls and top with the cauliflower. Pour over the sweet and sour sauce and scatter over the spring onions to serve.

name: Sweet & Sour Crispy Roast Chicken Thighs
description: Inspired by the flavours you find in a Thai laab, I've combined a sweet and sour dressing with crispy juicy chicken thighs to create a fresh, vibrant and umami chicken dinner.
keywords: Sweet & Sour Crispy Roast Chicken Thighs
Sweet & Sour Crispy Roast Chicken Thighs recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Season the chicken thighs with salt and black pepper, then place them skin-side down into a cold frying pan. Set the pan over a medium-high heat and cook for 10-15 mins, until the skin is deeply golden brown.

Transfer the thighs skin-side up onto a baking tray and roast in the oven for 15-20 mins, until the skin is crisp and the chicken is cooked through. Meanwhile, cook the rice following packet instructions.

For the salad, pick the mint and coriander leaves, discarding the mint stems and thinly slicing the coriander stems. Thinly slice the shallot. If you want extra crispness, soak the herbs and shallots in a bowl of ice water for a few minutes. Thinly slice the cucumber, sprinkle with a pinch of salt, and let it sit for a few minutes while you prepare the toasted rice dressing.

For the dressing, place a small pan over medium heat and add the raw rice. Dry toast for 4-6 mins, stirring, until golden brown. Transfer to a pestle and mortar and grind into a coarse powder (a little texture is fine). Add the chilli jam, 1/2 the fish sauce and juice of the limes, stirring to combine, and adjust seasoning to taste with more fish sauce, lime juice or jam if needed. Add the shallots and coriander stalks and mix to combine.
Drain the cucumbers then add them to a small bowl along with the fresh herbs and half the dressing. Toss to combine.
To serve, divide the cooked rice between bowls. Top with the herb salad and crispy chicken thighs, then drizzle over the remaining dressing.

name: Sweet & Sour Glazed Aubergines & Sesame Rice
description: Sticky, caramelised aubergines tossed in a sweet pomegranate glaze, served with buttery sesame rice and a zingy cucumber salad.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Trim and chop the aubergines into 2cm chunks. Chuck them onto a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, then toss to coat. Roast for 20–25 mins until softened and golden.
Wash the rice under cold water until it runs clear. Finely grate the garlic. Pick the parsley leaves and finely chop the stalks.

Set a medium saucepan (with a lid) over a medium heat. Add the sesame seeds and butter and cook, stirring now and then, until the seeds are golden and toasty. Stir in the grated garlic and chopped parsley stalks, cooking for another 1–2 mins until fragrant.

Tip in the rice and pour over the water. Season with salt and bring to the boil. Once boiling, pop the lid on and lower the heat. Cook for 12 mins, then remove from the heat and leave to steam with the lid on for another 10 mins.
Thinly slice the cucumber and toss it in a bowl with a pinch of salt. Mix the pomegranate molasses and honey together in a separate bowl.
Once the aubergines are done, pour over half the pomegranate dressing and toss to coat. Return them to the oven for another 10-15 mins until sticky and glossy.

Chuck the pomegranate seeds, cucumber and parsley leaves into the rest of the dressing along with a drizzle of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice. Taste and adjust with a pinch of salt, pepper and a little more honey or molasses if needed.
In a small bowl, stir the tahini with a splash of cold water until it reaches a drizzle-able consistency. Season with salt, pepper and a bit of honey.
Fluff up the rice with a fork and divide between bowls. Top with the glazed aubergines, spoon over the cucumber salad and finish with a drizzle of the tahini sauce.

name: Sweet & Sour Hasselback Aubergine
description: This sweet and sour hasselback aubergine is ideal for meal prep. Combine it with your choice of carb, protein and topping to create your perfect meal prep dish.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan and pop a baking dish in the middle rack of the oven.

To hasselback the aubergines, stick a chopstick a quarter of the way through the aubergine from top to tail, then slice 1cm thick rounds, hitting the chopstick as a guide. Rub salt between each layer and set aside for 10 mins.

Squeeze the aubergines over a sink to release the excess water. Place them into the centre of the hot baking dish. Drizzle olive oil all over, ensuring to coat between each aubergine layer. Add the water to the base of the tray and season the aubergines with a good sprinkling of salt and pepper. Foil the dish very tightly or use a well-fitted lid and roast for 40 mins.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the sweet and sour sauce ingredients and mix well.

When the aubergine cooking time is up, remove the foil and pour the sauce into the aubergine layers. Drizzle a glug of of sesame oil all over the surface of each aubergine. Return to the oven, with no foil, for 20 mins or until the aubergines are caramelised and jammy.

Remove the aubergines from the oven and leave to cool for 5 mins. Sprinkle with the sesame seeds then enjoy with your choice of carb and protein. If meal prepping for the week, allow to cool completely then transfer to a container and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Sweet & Sour Hasselback Aubergine with Rice
description: This faff-free recipe looks super impressive served on a table. If you're not hasselback-ing your aubergines, what are you doing with your life?
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C top and bottom heat, with a tray in the middle rack of the oven. Grab a casserole or baking dish or rimmed baking tray.

Hasselback the aubergines - Stick a chopstick ¼ of the way through the aubergine from top to tail, then slice 1cm thick rounds, hitting the chopstick as a guide. Rub salt between each layer and set aside.
Slice bell peppers, onions and pineapple chunks into thin-sized strips. Slice a whole garlic bulb in half horizontally. Add all the veggies and your whole cherry tomatoes into your dish/tray.

Squeeze the aubergines over a sink, - to release the excess water. Place them into the centre of the veggies, creating an aubergine Yin Yang pattern. Drizzle olive oil all over the veggies, ensuring to rub each aubergine layer in olive oil and coating the garlic halves. Add a ¼ cup of water and season the veggies with a good sprinkling of salt and pepper. Foil the dish very tightly or use a well-fitted lid and roast for 40 mins.

In the meantime, cook your rice. Add your washed rice into a heavy bottom pot, with 2 ¼ cups of water, half of your Sesame oil, and a pinch of salt. Place a lid on and bring to a boil, then immediately reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and keep the lid closed for at least 10 mins before fluffing up. Then keep the lid on until serving.

Add all the cashews onto a baking tray lined with baking paper and toss in the honey and soy sauce. roast in the same oven as the aubergines, for 7- 10 minutes or until caramelised, keep an eye on them as they can burn easily. Remove and mix to coat each cashew in the caramelised soy glaze and set aside to cool.
In a small bowl combine the sweet and sour ingredients and mix well.

After 40 mins, remove the foil and pour half of the sauce into the aubergine layers. Pour the remaining sauce all over the veggies. Drizzle a Tbsp of sesame oil all over the surface of each aubergine. Place everything back in the oven, with no foil, for 20 mins or until caramelised.
Finely slice the spring onions and the coriander, including the stems and set aside for garnishing.

After 20 mins or when the aubergines look caramelised and jammy, allow everything to cool for 5 mins. Then carefully squeeze the hot garlic bulbs back into the sauce. Sprinkle over all the glazed cashews, sliced coriander, spring onions, and sesame seeds, and finish with a drizzle of toasted sesame oil. Serve with hot rice.

name: Sweet & Spicy Ramen Fried 'Chicken' Burger
description: A crispy, golden ramen burger with a spicy rich gochujang sauce. This is totally vegetarian and totally delicious.
keywords: Sweet & Spicy Ramen Fried Quorn Chicken Burger
instructions: Start by peeling your carrots and chopping them into matchsticks. Add to a bowl with the rice vinegar, sesame seeds and a pinch of salt. Give it a mix and set aside.
Mix most of the mayonnaise with the kimchi and set aside.

Heat up your air fryer to 210°C. Using a pestle and mortar, crush the ramen into a breadcrumb-like texture and add to a deep bowl. Paint the Quorn vegetarian fillets with the rest of the mayo, then drop into the crushed noodles, tossing to coat. Drizzle with oil and put in the air fryer for 20-25 mins until golden. Keep checking the fillets as they cook, as airfryers do vary brand to brand. If you don't have an airfryer you can shallow fry in a pan over a medium heat or bake in the oven.

In the meantime, make the glaze by mixing the gochujang and honey and grating in the garlic. Open the ramen flavour sachet and add that too – if you’ve got a little sesame oil to hand, chuck that in too. Don’t worry if not. Loosen with a few tablespoons of water until it’s the same consistency as double cream.
When the fillets are golden, remove from the air fryer and pour over the glaze, coating on both sides.

Spread the buns with some butter and toast in a hot pan until golden. Spread with the kimchi mayo, top with your little gem lettuces, the ramen-crusted fillet, carrot pickles and a touch more sesame. Spread some mayo on the lid and top it all off.

name: Sweet & Sticky Chicken with Broccoli Rice
description: Sweet, sticky chicken over buttery broccoli rice with a spicy-savoury kick. It's a meal prep winner that's ready in under 30 minutes.
instructions: Finely slice the garlic and roughly chop the broccoli. Add the butter to a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Once melted, add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until golden and softened. Add the chopped broccoli and cook for another 2–3 mins.

Wash the rice and stir it through the broccoli mix. Pour in the water and bring to the boil. Pop a lid on, reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 mins to finish steaming.
Meanwhile, mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sriracha and honey in a small bowl.

Slice the chicken thighs into bite-sized chunks — about 5–6 pieces per thigh. Set a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken in a single layer (you may need to work in batches to avoid overcrowding). Season with salt and cook for 6 mins until golden and crispy on one side. Flip and cook for another 2–3 mins until cooked through. Take the chicken out and set aside.

Pour the sauce into the chicken pan over medium high heat. Bring to a boil and cook for 2 minutes, or until the sauce is thick and glossy. Toss in the chicken, coating it in the glaze. If not sticky enough for you, cook for an extra minute or 2.

Thinly slice the spring onions. Spoon the broccoli rice into bowls or containers, top with the sticky chicken and any sauce left in the pan. Finish with spring onions, sesame seeds and a wedge of lemon.

name: Sweet Chilli & Lemongrass Chicken with Spicy Pineapple Salad
description: She’s sweet, spicy and a little bit fruity. This chilli chicken and rice bowl with a zingy pineapple salad really hits the spot.
keywords: Sweet Chilli & Lemongrass Chicken with Spicy Pineapple Salad
Sweet Chilli & Lemongrass Chicken with Spicy Pineapple Salad recipe
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions.

Using scissors, snip the chicken into 3cm bit size chunks. Add to a mixing bowl, season with salt and pepper and set aside. Trim and thinly slice the lemongrass, garlic and bird's eye chilli then set aside.

Place a frying pan onto medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the lemongrass, garlic and chilli and cook for one minute until fragrant. Then, add the chicken and stir fry for 5-7 mins until golden but not yet cooked through. Pour in the water and sweet chilli sauce and bring to the boil, then turn the heat down slightly and simmer for 8-10 mins, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened and glazes the chicken. Taste and season with fish sauce and lime juice.

Meanwhile, for the salad, peel and chop the pineapple into 2cm chunks. Trim the cucumber and chop into the same size as the pineapple. Finely slice the chillies and shallot. Into a large bowl, squeeze in the juice from the limes then stir through the shallots and chillies. Season with fish sauce and sugar to taste. Add the pineapple and cucumber to the bowl and toss to combine.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls. Top with the salad and chicken, spooning any of the chicken sauces on top.

name: Sweet Corn Gazpacho With Coconut Sambol
description: It's sweet corn season. This twist on a Spanish classic is fresh and full of flavour.
instructions: Shuck the corn to remove the kernels. Slice the jalapeño and remove the seeds if you like less heat.

In a large blender, add in the heirloom tomatoes, bell peppers, corn kernels, jalapeño slices, and the juice from one lime. Add in the vinegar and olive oil. If you’re using a nutribullet, you’ll have to halve the recipe and blend it in two goes.
Once it’s all blended, strain the mixture through a fine mesh strainer.
If your gazpacho is too thick, add 2 tbsp of ice water at a time, as needed, to help the blending process.
Pour the gazpacho into a bowl, season with salt and pepper to taste, and add olive oil as needed. Set this in the fridge to chill, until you are ready to serve.
To make the sambol, finely chop the chilli and cherry tomatoes. In a bowl, add in your tomatoes, chilli, and desiccated coconut along with 1 tbsp of lime juice and ½ tsp salt. Mix well.
To serve, pour the gazpacho into a wide and shallow bowl, top with the sambol and drizzle with olive oil.

name: Sweet Dee's Jerk Chicken Wrap
description: Sweet Dee's 24-hour marinated jerk chicken thighs, roasted in the oven, stuffed into a soft tortilla wrap with two sauces, salad and fried plantain.
instructions: Place all of the marinade ingredients in a food processor with a 1 1/2 tbsp of olive oil & blend. Toss with chicken and marinade overnight, or for at least 30 min.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Chuck your marinated chicken onto a tray and roast for 15-16 mins until golden brown, a bit gnarly and cooked through. Allow to rest for 10-12 mins.
Peel and cut plantain into fries. Add enough oil to a saucepan for shallow frying. Fry the plantain over a medium heat on all sides until golden and tender. This will take roughly 4-5 mins.
To make the jerk mayo, mix the mayo with 3 tbsp of jerk sauce and season, set aside.
Roughly chop your chicken thighs and toss with couple of spoons of jerk sauce.
Warm your wraps, stack up with the jerk chicken, salad, avocado, coleslaw and plenty of extra jerk sauce and jerk mayo. Get them wrapped up and get stuck in!

name: Sweet Glazed Sticky Duck with Tilda Fragrant Jasmine Rice
description: This is an outstanding way to cook duck breast. Glazed with a sweet, spiced sauce and served perfectly with Tilda Fragrant Jasmine Rice.
instructions: Preheat your oven 180°C/356°F.
Mix all the marinade ingredients together - cranberry sauce, soy, cinnamon, crushed garlic cloves, salt, pepper and 1 teaspoon of vegetable oil, then set aside.
Score all the skin of duck breast in a criss cross pattern and season with salt and pepper.

Heat a non-stick frying pan with a little drizzle of vegetable oil on a medium heat. Place a duck breast in the pan skin-side down and brown the duck fat until golden and crispy - this will take about 5-8 minutes for each breast. Turn over to lightly brown the flesh side for 1-2 minutes, then remove from the pan and repeat with your remaining duck breasts.

Transfer the duck breasts to a lined baking tray and pour on your marinade, a spoonful on each breast, leaving some of the sauce to serve at the end. Roast the duck for 15 minutes. Half way through the cooking time, spoon the juices that collect in the tray over the duck breasts. When the duck is cooked, cover the baking tray with some aluminium foil and leave to rest for a couple of minutes
While your duck is cooking, in the same pan as you used to brown the duck, heat up the Fragrant Jasmine Tilda Rice in all the yummy duck juices. Stir in the Five Spice.

Slice the duck and plate up your spiced rice, adding the slices of duck onto each bowl of rice. Add a few spoonfuls of the remaining marinade on each portion of duck. Garnish each bowl with thinly sliced spring onions and a sprinkle of black sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato & Bacon Traybake
description: Why have bacon & sweet potato never appeared in the same traybake together? Madness. Paired with charred onions and taleggio, it's a dish straight from heaven.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Start by peeling and chopping your sweet potatoes and butternut squash into cubes. Spread the cubes over 2 baking trays. Chop up your red onion and bacon into quarters and add to the tray followed by your rosemary sprigs (be sure to take them off the stalks). Drizzle a generous glug of olive oil over the trays along with a pinch of salt and a grinding of pepper. Mix everything together with your hands. Place into the oven for 25 minutes.
Once 25 minutes is up, take the trays out of the oven. Transfer everything into one tray and mix together. Place back into the oven for a further 20 minutes.
Taleggio time. Slice it up and place the slices on top of your tray once the 20 minutes is up. Bake for a final 15 minutes.
Chop up your parsley and sprinkle over the top of the traybake. Serve it up and tuck into this warming dish. Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Chilli with Charred Corn
description: Combining the smoky sweetness of charred sweetcorn and sweet potatoes with the richness of black beans, this recipe is perfect for those who love a veggie chilli with a twist. We've added feta for extra tanginess to cut through the smokiness.
keywords: Sweet Potato & Feta Black Bean Chilli Recipe
Sweet Potato & Feta Black Bean Chilli
instructions: Peel the garlic cloves (leave them whole). Pick the tomatoes off their vine, then cut them in half.

Get a frying pan over a medium heat. Toast the cumin seeds until smelling amazing, then tip them into a bowl. Put the pan back over a high heat. Add the garlic and tomato halves. Fry for 3-4 mins, turning regularly until both are charring, then tip the tomatoes and garlic into a blender – keep the pan aside to use later.

Add three-quarters of the cumin seeds to the blender along with the chipotle paste, chilli flakes, coriander stalks and tomato purée. Blitz until a smooth sauce forms – this is the base of your chilli.

Roughly chop 1½ of the red onions, then very finely slice the remaining ½ red onion. Scrape the chopped onion into a large deep frying pan or casserole dish over a medium heat. Pour in 1 tbsp oil, add a big pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6-8 mins until softened.

Meanwhile, put the remaining finely sliced onion into the same bowl as the remaining cumin seeds. Squeeze in the juice of 1 lime, add a good pinch of salt, then scrunch with your hands to soften the onion and quick-pickle. Set aside.

Peel and cut the sweet potato into even small-sized chunks, about 2cm. Stir into the pan with the onions, then pour in your chipotle sauce and black beans along with their liquid. Give everything a good mix, then turn the heat to a simmer and simmer for 20 mins or until the sweet potato is tender but still holding its shape and the sauce has reduced.
Cook the rice following packet instructions.
As the chilli cooks, bring another saucepan of boiling salted water to the boil. Once boiling, drop in the sweetcorn and cook for 3 mins, drain and leave to steam dry.

Get the frying pan you were using earlier back over a super-high heat. Brush or drizzle the sweetcorn with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and season with salt and pepper. Add the corn to the super-hot pan and fry, turning regularly until evenly charred – this will take around 5 mins. Put the corn onto a chopping board to cool slightly.

Once ready to serve, season the chilli to taste, pouring in the lime juice from the pickled onions. Cut the other lime into wedges to serve and pick the coriander leaves. Holding the corn upright, cut downwards with your knife to shave off the charred corn kernels.
Serve the chilli in bowls with rice or tortillas, topped with the charred corn, cumin pickled onions, feta, coriander and a few more chilli flakes if you like.

name: Sweet Potato & Tamarind Tacos
description: Sweet, sticky and sour-sweet potatoes packed into corn tortillas and drizzled with a peanut butter dressing. The ultimate weeknight meal.
instructions: Chop up the sweet potatoes into small pieces and finely chop the chillies. Preheat your oven to 200°C.
In a bowl combine the chillies, soy sauce, light brown sugar and tamarind sauce. Grate in the ginger and garlic. Add in a glug of oil and toss half this mixture with the sweet potatoes.
Spread the sweet potato on a baking tray, drizzle on some olive oil and roast for 30 mins.
Heat up the remaining mixture in a pan with 150ml of water. Heat until bubbling then mix in the peanut butter. Whisk until smooth and add in 100ml of water until its a smooth pourable consistency.
Toast the peanuts in a dry pan and roughly chop them up. Finely chop the mint.
Heat the tortillas in a dry pan and then add in the sweet potato filling. Drizzle over the peanut butter sauce, sprinkle with peanuts, mint and a drizzle of the tamarind sauce.

name: Sweet Potato Rösti & Poached Egg
description: The perfect poached egg. The soft guac. The crispy rösti. A texture match made in heaven.
keywords: Sweet Potato Rösti & Poached Egg recipe
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Grate sweet potatoes with a normal box grater.

Add the grated potato into a bowl. Crack in 3 eggs. Add a handful of chopped parsley, a handful of chopped spring onions and a tsp of crushed chillies. Season with salt, pepper and olive oil. Mix everything together.

Line a baking tray with baking paper. Make 8 fishcake sized röstis, and line them up on the tray. They will be quite loose at this point, so don’t worry. Just squeeze them into shape and put them in the oven. They will firm up and crisp up. Bake for 30 minutes, turning after 20 minutes.

Guac time. Scoop the flesh out of the avocados. Mash it up in a bowl. Add a handful of chopped chives, the lemon juice and season with salt, pepper and olive oil. Mix everything together and set aside.

Egg time. Boil a pan of water. Carefully crack your egg into a glass. With a fork or a whisk, create a little whirlpool in the water. Pour the egg into the water, not in the centre of the whirlpool, but on the edge. Using your fork or whisk in the water, fold the white over the yolk and the egg should form a nice little ball.

Cook for 3 minutes on a medium heat. To check if it’s done, just gently lift the egg with a spoon. If the white is still a bit wobbly, leave it for 10 more seconds. If it’s firm, remove from the heat.
Assemble time. Spoon a good helping of guac on top of the rösti and then put your egg on top. Sprinkle some more chives and crushed chillies over the top, and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato Salad
description: Sweet potato wedge salad with tahini drizzle, pickled cucumber, peanuts and sesame seeds. Serve with salmon or chicken, or add crispy tofu.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the sweet potatoes into long wedges and lay on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and toss well. Season and bake for 30 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Whisk the rice wine vinegar, honey and sesame oil in a bowl together, add a big pinch of salt. Finely grate the garlic and ginger into the bowl. Slice the red chilli and add to the bowl.

Slice the cucumber in half lengthways, use a spoon to scrape out the middle, then finely slice on an angle and add to the bowl. Finely slice or use a mandoline to shave the red cabbage into the bowl. Toss everything together and set aside to pickle.

To make the tahini drizzle, whisk the tahini and lime together, it’ll look split and clumpy to begin with, but don’t sweat- whisk in water, a tbsp at a time, until it’s drizzle-able consistency. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Lay the sweet potatoes on a platter and scatter over the pickled cabbage and cucumber salad. Drizzle with the tahini and scatter with sesame seeds, peanuts, coriander, and spring onions to serve.

name: Sweet Potato Stuffed with Chickpea & Aubergine Curry
description: Sweet potatoes are a weekly essential. We love filling ours with a spicy chickpea and aubergine curry.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Get the sweet potatoes and add to a baking tray, then chuck into the bottom of the oven to warm through. Add the quinoa to a baking tray and drizzle with 2 tbsp olive oil, seasoning with salt and pepper. Mix well and bake for 15-20 mins, giving it a stir every 10-ish minutes - you want it to be dark in colour and really crispy.

In the meantime, chop the garlic and finely chop the coriander stems. Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and add the garlic and coriander stems, sizzling for 2 mins. Add in the curry paste and cook for 1 min, before adding the cherry tomatoes.

Add in a tin of chickpeas with the liquid, and drain the other before adding to the pan along with the aubergine. Let this gently bubble away for 5 mins, then take off the heat and stir through 2 big tbsp of the yoghurt.
Get your sweet potatoes out of the oven, split open and top with the curry, some of the remaining yoghurt, crispy quinoa and the coriander leaves.

name: Sweet Potato Traybake With Satay Sauce
description: This effortless traybake is a full balanced thrown onto a tray, drizzled with a delicious satay style crunchy peanut butter sauce. Finish with a squeeze of lime and you’ve got a delicious, filling weeknight dinner.
keywords: Sweet Potato Traybake With Satay Sauce recipe
Sweet Potato Traybake With Satay Sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.

Wash the sweet potatoes and cut them into wedges. Drain the chickpeas and dry them with a kitchen towel. Add the sweet potatoes and chickpeas to a large baking tray and drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, deseed and slice the peppers thickly.

After the 15 mins are up, remove the tray and add the peppers and broccoli to the tray and add a little more olive oil and seasoning. Roast for another 10-12 mins or until all of the vegetables are cooked through and the chickpeas are getting crispy.
While the vegetables roast, make the satay sauce. Whisk together the peanut butter, rice wine vinegar, soy sauce, coconut milk and chili flakes until smooth. Taste and adjust if needed.
Finely slice the spring onion and roughly chop the peanuts.
When the traybake is ready, drizzle over the sauce, sprinkle over the coriander, spring onions and peanuts and the zest and juice of the lime.

name: Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry
description: The most warming cuzza you will ever eat. The softest chickpeas and sweet potatoes in a rich tomatoey, coconutty sauce. Served with a cooling dollop of yoghurt.
instructions: Peel and dice the sweet potatoes into 2cm chunks. Peel and thinly slice the onion. Peel and finely slice the garlic. Cut the ginger into thin matchsticks. Roughly chop the coriander.

Place a large saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the onion, ginger and garlic. Season with salt and cook, stirring, until the onion has softened. Stir in the garam masala, chilli flakes, ground cumin and ground turmeric. Cook for 1 min until fragrant.

Add the sweet potatoes, chopped tomatoes, drained chickpeas, coconut cream and cherry tomatoes to the pan. Stir well, bring to a boil, then cover with a lid. Reduce the heat to low-medium and simmer for 20-25 mins until the sweet potatoes are tender. Season with salt and black pepper.
Once the sweet potatoes are cooked, stir through the spinach and ½ the chopped coriander. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Ladle the curry into bowls. Top with a dollop of coconut yoghurt and the remaining coriander. Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato, Chickpea & Coconut Curry
description: Riaz Phillips cooked us up a hearty dinner packed with veg and warming spices. An ideal mid-week dinner.
instructions: Dice your onion, garlic, ginger, pepper, tomatoes, carrot and the white part of the spring onions. Peel and chop up your sweet potato into 3cm-sized chunks.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and saute for two minutes, add the garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions, then cook for another two minutes.

Add the curry powder, cumin and a tablespoon of water, and stir for a minute to combine. Stir in the chickpeas, coating them in the seasoning, then add the coconut milk, the all-purpose seasoning and cinnamon, and keep stirring for another minute or so.
Next, stir in the sweet potato, carrot, peppers, tomatoes and thyme. Add the salt, black pepper, maple syrup or sugar, if using, and the desiccated coconut, stir, then add the scotch bonnet.
Turn the heat down to low, cover with the lid and simmer for 15 minutes. Stir, cover again and simmer for a further 10–15 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender.

Meanwhile, cook the okra. Heat the coconut oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and add the chilli flakes. Add the okra and fry until they start to brown slightly. Remove with a spatula and drain on kitchen paper. Add the okra and its spicy oil to the pan of coconut chickpeas or serve separately, if you prefer.
Serve with the green part of the spring onions.

name: Sweet Potato, Coconut & Harissa Soup
description: This soup is similar to one I used to eat in the Seychelles. Gently spiced, warming and super fragrant. Jordon x
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C.
Pop the sweet potatoes on a baking tray. Roast in the hot oven for 45 mins until soft and jammy, then remove and set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, slice the onion, carrot and ginger.
Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and ginger and sweat down for about 10 mins until soft and fragrant.

Once cool enough to handle, peel the sweet potatoes and add them to the pan. Add the water, ¾ of the coconut milk, ½ the harissa and most of the coriander, reserving a handful for garnish. Season with the salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 mins, then use a stick blender to blend until smooth and creamy.
To serve, pour the soup into bowls. Finish with a swirl of the remaining coconut milk and harissa, and a sprinkle of the remaining chopped coriander.

name: Sweet Potato, Ginger & Turmeric Noodle Soup
description: This warming, aromatic soup is absolutely packed with flavour and will see you through the colder months.
instructions: For the spice paste: Roughly chop the fresh ginger, chili and spring onion and add to a blender or small food processor, along with the ground turmeric and the sesame oil. Blitz to a chunky paste.
Peel and cube the sweet potato. Heat a glug of sesame oil in a large pan set over a medium heat. Add the paste and cook for 5 mins until fragrant.

Add the cubed sweet potato and sauté for a couple of minutes to sear the edges. Add the coconut milk, water and soy sauce and bring to a boil, then turn down to a simmer. Cook for about 10 mins until the sweet potato has softened. Stir through the spinach and cook until just wilted.
Meanwhile, cook the udon noodles following instructions.
To serve, divide the noodles into bowls and pour over the soup. Finish with your chosen toppings.

name: Sweet Potato, Minced Beef & Cottage Cheese Bowl
description: Crispy sweet potato, taco-spiced beef, and a cooling dollop of cottage cheese, all drizzled with hot honey. That's your weekly meal prep, sorted.
keywords: Minced Beef & Cottage Cheese Bowl recipe
instructions: Peel and dice the sweet potato into small chunks. Spray with oil and season with salt and pepper.
Cook in the air fryer at 200°C for 16–18 mins until golden and soft. Alternatively, roast in the oven at 180°C for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, set a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the minced beef and cook for 6–7 mins until browned and cooked through. Stir in the taco seasoning and a pinch of salt.
While that’s cooking, halve the cherry tomatoes and shred the iceberg lettuce.

To plate or box up, spoon the roasted sweet potatoes, followed by the cottage cheese and taco beef. Add the lettuce, tomatoes and pickled onions. It will keep in the fridge for 3-4 days. Drizzle over the hot honey and finish with a pinch of chilli flakes if you like it spicy.

name: Sweet Potato, Minced Beef & Cottage Cheese Bowl
description: Crispy sweet potato, taco-spiced beef, and a cooling dollop of cottage cheese, all drizzled with hot honey. That's dinner, sorted.
keywords: Minced Beef & Cottage Cheese Bowl recipe
instructions: Peel and dice the sweet potato into small chunks. Spray with oil and season with salt and pepper.
Cook in the air fryer at 200°C for 16–18 mins until golden and soft. Alternatively, roast in the oven at 180°C for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, set a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the minced beef and cook for 6–7 mins until browned and cooked through. Stir in the taco seasoning and a pinch of salt.
While that’s cooking, halve the cherry tomatoes and shred the iceberg lettuce.
To plate up, spoon the roasted sweet potatoes into bowls, followed by the cottage cheese and taco beef. Add the lettuce, tomatoes and pickled onions.
Drizzle over the hot honey and finish with a pinch of chilli flakes if you like it spicy.

name: Sweet Potatoes With Satay Chickpeas
description: This is my idea of a great jacket potato: saucy satay chickpeas piled over fluffy sweet potatoes, pushed open to get the maximum potato to topping ratio.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Pierce the sweet potatoes all over with a fork, drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper and wrap tightly in silver foil. Bake for 45-55 mins, depending on the size.
Meanwhile, make the chickpea satay topper. Add the peanut butter, the juice of the two limes, soy sauce, chilli flakes, sesame oil, and yoghurt into a large bowl. Whisk to combine.

Dice the cucumber into small cubes, finely slice the spring onion, and drain the chickpeas. Add all of these to the bowl with the dressing and toss well to combine. Taste and adjust the flavour as you like, adding more soy sauce for saltines, lime juice for zest, and yoghurt for creaminess.

To serve, slice open the potatoes lengthwise, open them up fully and push the flesh down with a fork, then season with salt and pepper. Spoon the topping onto the sweet potatoes, top with sesame seeds and coriander leaves.
This is lovely both hot and cold so perfect for meal prep.

name: Sweet Potatoes with Tahini Butter Chickpeas
description: The messy mix of tahini, chilli crunch and crispy chickpeas over soft sweet potatoes is divine, but the tahini butter is the true star of this show.
keywords: Sweet potatoes with tahini butter chickpeas
instructions: Prick the potatoes all over with a fork and rub with a little olive oil, salt and pepper.Here are three options for cooking your sweet potatoes. The time will vary slightly depending on the size of your potato, but check them at the shorter time to make sure they don’t overcook and burn. Oven: 200°C for 40-50 minsAir Fryer: 190°C for 30-35 mins. Turn once or twice.Microwave: 9 mins in total, turning at 3 min intervals. Place the potato on a microwaveable plate with a kitchen towel in it to absorb moisture. If you add more than one at a time, they will take longer, so keep cooking and turning at 3 min intervals until cooked through.

Melt the butter. Add the tahini, soy sauce, maple syrup, lime juice, and 1 tbsp of warm water to a bowl and mix well. It might curdle but keep mixing and add a little more water if you need to thin it down as each tahini brand is slightly different. It will split/ curdle but keep whisking with a fork or a small whisk until it comes together into a smooth sauce, about 2 mins.

Meanwhile, cook the chickpeas. Drain the chickpeas and add them to a large frying pan with a drizzle of olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Fry for about 8 mins on medium heat until they start to brown and pop. Add the kale and stir for another few minutes until the kale has wilted.

When your potatoes have cooked and are very tender, place them on a plate and slice each one down the middle. Feel free to add a little vegan butter into the middle of each one at this point, if you want to. Use a fork to mash the potatoes flat and season them with salt and pepper.
Scatter chickpeas over the potatoes then drizzle plenty of tahini butter over the top. Finish with some crispy chilli oil, if using and some sesame seeds and finely sliced spring onion.

name: Sweet Shortcrust Pastry
description: A handy shortcrust pastry recipe that’s perfect for sweet tarts and pies. You'll need a stand mixer or food processor for this one.
instructions: Ensure your butter is very cold. Grate the cold butter into a bowl and return to the fridge. Chill the mixing bowl and the pastry attachment in the fridge for 30 mins.
Sift the flour, salt and icing sugar into the bowl of the standing mixer. Add the cold butter and combine in quick pulses to just bring it to the breadcrumbs stage.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the egg and extra yolk. Gradually add to the mix, mixing as you do, until it just comes together as a dough.
Wrap the dough in clingfilm and refrigerate for at least 30 mins.

Remove the dough from the fridge and allow it to come to room temperature. Knead it very gently on a lightly floured clean surface to gently soften the dough. Use a floured rolling pin to roll the dough out to your desired thickness.
Use the pastry to line the tart or pie tin of your choice then bake in an oven at 180°C fan until browning and starting to crisp.

name: Sweet Soy Cod with Sriracha Broccoli
description: In Partnership With Aldi. #ad. The sticky soy glaze on this cod is a game-changer. It’s easy to make and served up with spicy broc and a good crunch of peanuts. A perfect high-protein speedy dinner.
keywords: Sweet Soy Cod with Sriracha Broccoli recipe
Sweet Soy Cod with Sriracha Broccoli
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Grate the ginger and add to a small bowl. Add the brown sugar, soy sauce, five-spice and whisk together until the sugar has dissolved.

Lightly season the cod with salt and place onto a foil-lined baking tray brushed with a little olive oil. Spoon over about 1 Tbsp of the sweet soy mix, then slide into the oven. Bake for 13-15 mins, basting the fish with more sauce halfway through. It should turn dark, caramelised and sticky. Once cooked, remove from the oven and let it rest for a couple of minutes.
Meanwhile, bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the broccoli and cook for 2 mins until just tender. Drain and set aside.
In a large bowl, stir the mayonnaise, sriracha, soy sauce, lemon juice, brown sugar until smooth. Add the warm broccoli and toss to coat in the dressing.
Plate the cod alongside the dressed broccoli. Sprinkle with sesame seeds, a drizzle of chilli oil, and crushed peanuts. Serve with rice and dig in.

name: Sweet and Sour Chicken Balls
description: Crispy battered nuggets. A deceptively quick and easy homemade sweet and sour sauce. A properly naughty treat.
instructions: Chop up the chicken into large pieces and toss into a bowl. Add ½ tsp salt, ½ tsp ground white pepper and 1 tbsp self-raising flour, then toss to combine.
Combine the rest of the self-raising flour, ½ tsp ground white pepper, ½ tsp vegetable oil and 250ml of cold water in a large bowl.

In a saucepan, combine the pineapple juice, apple cider vinegar, light brown sugar, ketchup and soy sauce. Mix the cornflour and 1 tbsp of water in a small bowl. Bring the pineapple sauce to a boil, then let it simmer for a couple of minutes. Add your cornflour slurry and give it a good mix - this will thicken the sauce and make it nice and shiny.
Heat up a large pot of vegetable oil, enough to deep fry the chicken, and heat to a medium-high heat.
Using the bamboo skewer, poke a piece of chicken and dip it into the batter, then gently place the piece into the hot oil. Fry for 3-4 mins until golden brown and cooked through.
Repeat filling the pot to fry the chicken in batches.
Serve hot and dipped into the sweet and sour sauce.

name: Sweet and Sour Lentil Meatballs
description: These juicy meatballs are made with Merchant Gourmet’s Puy Lentils and tossed in a classic, sticky sweet and sour sauce. Perfect served with steamed rice.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Blend up the Puy Lentils, 4 cloves of garlic, 3 spring onions, and a chilli with 2 tbsp of soy sauce and the juice of a lime to form a smooth paste. Then add in the breadcrumbs and give it a good mix. Taste the mixture and add a pinch of salt if needed.
Roll the mixture into golf ball-sized balls. Pop these onto a baking tray and bake for 30 mins.
Chop the onions and peppers into large chunks.
Finely chop the remaining garlic and finely slice the spring onions.
Add a glug of oil into a pan and then fry the onions and peppers for 3 mins. Add in the garlic and then cook for 1 minute.
Add in the pineapple juice, apple cider vinegar, ketchup and light brown sugar. Give it a good mix and bring it to a boil.
Make a cornflour slurry by mixing 2 tbsp of cornflour with 2 tbsp of water. Add this into the pan and cook for 3 mins.
Add in your now-cooked meatballs and give it a good mix.
Serve with steamed rice and a sprinkle of sliced spring onions.

name: Sweet and Sour Prawns
description: We’ve cracked the code to making the best Chinese takeaway-style sweet and sour sauce. Perfect served over egg fried rice.
instructions: Wash your Tilda Easy Cook Long Grain Rice, and pop it in a pan. Cover with cold water and cook for 10 minutes until tender. Drain the rice and allow to cool.

Chop up the onions and peppers into large pieces. Roughly chop the garlic, spring onions and red chilli. Whisk the three eggs in a bowl. Combine 1 tsp of cornflour with 2 tbsps of water into a cup to make a slurry.

Add your pineapple juice, apple cider vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and ketchup to a medium sized saucepan set over a medium heat. Bring to a boil, then let it simmer for 2 minutes until your sugar dissolves. Pour in the cornflour slurry and cook until it thickens, about 3 minutes.
In a bowl mix the prawns, white sugar, white pepper powder and a pinch of salt. Then crack in the egg and give it a good mix. Add in 50g of cornflour and mix well and set aside.
Heat a good glug of oil in a wok over a medium-high heat. Fry your prawns for 1 minute or until crisp and starting to curl. Remove from the pan and drain on kitchen paper.

Heat up a large wok and add in a big glug of oil. Add your onion and red pepper and stir fry for a few minutes until softened and starting to char. Tip your prawns and sauce. Give the mixture a really good mix and cook for 3 minutes until it is piping hot. Put into a serving dish.
For the egg fried rice, heat up a large wok until it starts to smoke. Pour in a large glug of oil and add in the garlic. Fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in your eggs and scramble until they are fluffy for 1 minute.
Push the eggs to the side and add in your cooked rice. Push the rice down to separate the grains. Add in the soy sauce, sesame oil and white pepper. Mix well so the rice is well coated.
Finally, add the spring onions and chilli. Stir fry for 1 minute so they are well dispersed in the rice.
Spoon the egg fried rice in a bowl, pour over your sweet and sour prawns and enjoy.

name: Sweet and Spicy Gochujang Fried Chicken
