description: The best type of comfort food. Crispy fried chicken tossed in a killer sauce. It bangs. Xien x
keywords: Sweet and spicy gochujang fried chicken recipes
instructions: Add all the ingredients for the sauces into a bowl. Grate in the ginger and garlic and mix well.
Slice your chicken into long strips and place in a large mixing bowl.
Whisk the two eggs and set aside.

To make 2 bowls of flour mix, add 60g corn flour, 20g plain flour, ½ tsp baking soda to each mixing bowl. Season both bowls of flour with a pinch of salt and pepper and a tsp of garlic powder and onion salt.

Now add the first bowl of flour mix to your chicken thigh strips and mix well. Pour the whisked eggs into the bowl of chicken. Then, one at a time, dredge a single chicken thigh strip into the second bowl of flour mix. Once they’ve all been coated, set aside.
Heat the oil into a deep wok or pot until it reaches 180°C.

Fry the chicken in small batches (making sure to shake off any excess flour before placing in the oil) until they float to the top, this will take a few mins. Then place them on a paper-lined rack lined as this will help absorb any excess oil. You want the chicken to be super crispy so pop them back into the oil for a few mins again for the second round of deep-frying. Set aside your chicken in a deep bowl.
On medium heat, pour the sauce into a separate pot and cook for just a few mins until the sauce thickens a little.
Pour most of the sauce (set aside two tablespoons) onto the chicken and toss well.
Mix the remaining 2 tbsps of sauce with some mayo.
Garnish the chicken with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions and enjoy with your sweet and spicy gochujang mayo.

name: Sweet n Sour Tofu
description: The takeaway classic cooked from the comfort of your own home. Perfectly sweet and sour. The sticky sauce takes your tofu to a whole new level.
instructions: Chop your peppers and onions into 3cm chunks. Chop the tofu into 2-3cm cubes. Add your cornflour to a bowl. Dip each cube in cornflour, make sure to cover the cubes fully.
Fill your wok with an inch of vegetable oil. Add your tofu and fry until golden brown and set aside. Pour the oil out and place back over the heat.
Get the rice on. See pack instructions.
Add the onions and peppers into the wok, and cook on a high heat, until softening and starting to char.

Once softened, chop up your pineapple into chunks and add to the wok. Next, Stir all the sauce ingredients together. Pour into the veggies, and toss the tofu through until thickened. Taste and season with salt, if needed.
Slice up your spring onions for garnish. Serve on a bed of rice and tuck into this delicious dish. Enjoy!

name: Sweet ’n’ Spicy Pineapple Noodles
description: Sweet and spicy pineapple noodles – there's heat from the chillies and a lovely natural sweetness from the pineapple. This a simple weeknight recipe.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Peel and dice the pineapple and coarsely grate the tofu. Zest the limes. Slice the chilli and garlic.
Transfer the tofu to a baking tray and top with the lime zest and soy sauce. Cook in the oven for 20-25 mins, mixing every 5 mins to ensure an even cook.

Add some oil to a hot frying pan and fry the pineapple until golden, then add the stir-fried veg, chilli, garlic and cooked noodles. Cook for 2 mins, then add the curry powder. Cook for 30 seconds. Roughly chop the coriander.
Add the lime juice and some soy sauce, then plate up with the coriander and tofu on top.

name: Sweetcorn Fritters
description: Transform tinned sweetcorn into a delicious breakfast with these herby chickpea flour fritters. They’re packed with plants and high in protein and fibre to give you a good start to your day.
instructions: Add the drained sweetcorn, spring onions, red chilli and fresh coriander and parsley to a blender and blitz until combined but still chunky. Add ⅓ egg and blitz again to combine.

Add the chickpea flour and a pinch of salt and blitz again to a thick batter. Use a spoon to stir through ½ the Daily 30+ (if using). If the batter is too thin, add 1 tbsp of chickpea flour at a time until thickened.

Heat a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add a couple tbsp of the sweetcorn mixture to the pan and cook for 2 mins on each side until golden and cooked through. Repeat for the remaining batter, cooking 2-3 fritters at a time.
While the fritters are cooking, poach your eggs in boiling water to your liking (4 mins for runny yolks). Slice the avocado and halve the cherry tomatoes.
To serve, stack the fritters and top with a tablespoon of Greek yoghurt and a poached egg. Serve with the sliced avocado and cherry tomatoes and an additional sprinkle of Daily 30+ (if using).

name: Sweetcorn Lemongrass and Ginger Fritters
description: The ultimate sweetcorn fritters. The ginger and the lemon grass make for a perfect combo.
instructions: Remove the tough outer layer and end of the lemongrass stick. Chop as finely as you can. Finely slice the coriander stalks and roughly chop the leaves. Finely chop your spring onions.
Using a fork, smash the avocados in a bowl, add 3/4 of the coriander leaves. Season with salt, pepper and lime juice to taste.

Add the coriander stalks and lemongrass to a bowl. Grate in your ginger, add the drained sweetcorn, spring onions, flour, milk, cayenne, 2 beaten eggs and a generous amount of salt and pepper. Beat well to form your sweetcorn batter.
Put the oven on low and get a deep pan of water on the heat to boil.

Pour a drizzle of oil into a non stick frying pan. Dollop four fritters into the pan, using up half of the batter. Fry on a medium heat for 2 minutes on each side. Transfer to a baking tray and repeat with the remaining batter. Keep all the fritters warm in the low heat oven.

Egg time. Carefully crack two of your eggs into two glasses. With a fork or a whisk, create a little whirlpool in the water. Pour the eggs into the water, not into the centre of the whirlpool but on the edge. Using your fork and the water, fold the egg whites over the yolk - the egg should form a nice little ball.

Cook for 3 minutes on a medium heat, you want it to be a rolling boil rather than spluttering. To check if it’s done, just gently lift the egg with a slotted spoon. If the white is still a bit wobbly, leave it for 10 more seconds. If it’s firm, remove from the heat. Repeat with the remaining eggs.
Slice and fry the halloumi in the pan you used for your fritters until golden and crisp.
Assembly time. Place two sweetcorn fritters on each plate. Top with the smashed avo, halloumi and poached egg. Sprinkle over a little cayenne, the coriander and serve with the lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Sweetcorn Risotto with Hazelnuts and Sage
description: The only good thing about the end of summer is sweetcorn season. It’s not around for long so use it while you can! It really shines in this risotto.  Jordon x
instructions: First off let’s prepare the sweetcorn (skip this step if using tinned). If it still has the outer leaves, strip these off and then cook in boiling water for 5 mins until the kernels are soft to a fork tip.
Drain and once cool enough to handle, stand the sweetcorn on its end and use a knife to cut the kernels from the cob. Set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Place a large pan over a medium heat, add the butter and when it foams, add the onion, the sweetcorn, a few chopped sage leaves and a pinch of salt.
Cook gently for 7 or 8 mins until the onion is soft and golden. Add the rice and cook for another 2 mins until it’s well coated in the butter and the edges have gone slightly translucent.
Pour in the wine, stir and let it bubble until almost completely evaporated.
Now add the stock a ladleful at a time, stirring until each ladle is absorbed before adding another. This should take between 15 and 20 mins.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the hazelnuts and lightly toast in a pan. Set aside.
Pick the rest of the sage leaves and fry them in a good slug of olive oil until crispy. Set aside on kitchen paper.

Once all of the stock has been used up, the rice should be cooked through but still have a little ‘bite’ to it - think al dente pasta. At this point, remove from the heat, add the grated cheese, most of the hazelnuts (leave a few to go on top) stir well and cover with a lid. Leave to rest for 5 mins.
Plate up the risotto, top with crispy sage leaves and a drizzle of the olive oil you fried them in.

name: Swiss Meringue Buttercream
description: A classic silky smooth buttercream made using egg whites. Perfect for sandwiching between cakes.
instructions: Carefully separate the egg whites from the yolk (you can use the yolks to make Carbonara, or your own mayonnaise and dressing). Add the sugar and egg whites to a heat proof mixing bowl. Cut the butter into cubes and set aside to soften.

Fill a large saucepan ¼ of the way with water and set it over a medium-high heat until simmering. Place the bowl, with the sugar and eggs, on top of the saucepan (the bottom of the bowl shouldn’t touch the water) and whisk constantly until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is hot and no longer grainy to the touch (rub it between your fingers to check).
Transfer the mixture to a stand mixer, add the vanilla extract and beat on the highest speed, until the bowl is completely cool to the touch and you have stiff peaks.

Switch to the paddle attachment (to avoid air bubbles) and add all the soft, cubed butter all at once. It's very important that the butter is soft and the same temperature as the meringue, otherwise you risk the mixture splitting. Leave the mixer on a medium speed until the mixture comes together (it may look split to start with, but don't worry it will come together), then turn down to low until you have a smooth buttercream.
If the mixture looks split, don't worry; put the whole bowl in the fridge for 10-15 mins then whip again.

name: Tabbouleh on Toast
description: This Levantine salad tastes incredible on thick slices of toasted sourdough, with pomegranate tahini for extra flavour. It makes a perfect healthy lunch.
instructions: For the tabbouleh, finely chop the parsley and red onion and add to a mixing bowl. Cut the tomatoes into quarters and discard some of the water if there is a lot, then finely chop the tomatoes and add them to the bowl along with the lemon juice, olive oil and salt. Tear in the mint leaves, toss well and set aside.

To make the whipped tahini, add the tahini to a bowl and slowly whisk the water through, a little at a time, until you have a smooth, almost yoghurt-like consistency (you may need more or less water depending on the brand of tahini). Stir through the pomegranate molasses, cumin and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Toast the thick slices of sourdough bread.

Layer up a big dollop of tahini, then the salad and an extra drizzle of pomegranate molasses and olive oil. Sprinkle over some sesame seeds, aleppo pepper flakes and a few extra torn mint leaves, if you like.

name: Tagliatelle Bolognese
description: A rich, slow-simmered ragu with red wine and garlic, tossed through tagliatelle and finished with a generous grating of parmesan. Proper Sunday-dinner comfort food.
instructions: Tip the pancetta into your largest saucepan/casserole pot and set over a medium heat. Add 1 tbsp olive oil and cook for 8-10 mins, stirring occasionally, until the fat has rendered and the meat is crisp.
Meanwhile, finely dice the onion, carrot (peel if dirty) and celery into similar-sized pieces.

Add the vegetables to the pan with the pancetta and a splash of oil. Cook, stirring regularly, for 8-10 mins until the vegetables are soft. Crush and add the garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Tip in both the pork and beef mince, season with a good pinch of salt and pepper, then use the back of your spoon to break the mince into smaller pieces.
Turn up the heat to medium-high and cook, stirring and breaking up the meat regularly, for 5-6 mins until the meat has browned.
Pour in the red wine. Bring to the boil and simmer for about 5 mins until the wine has evaporated, then stir in the tomato purée. Cook for 1 min, then pour in the passata and the bay leaves.

Turn the heat down to medium and leave the bolognese to simmer away with the lid off, stirring occasionally, for 1 hr 15 mins. If it starts to catch, give it a good stir and put the lid on for the final 15 mins.
Pour in the milk, stir, then leave the bolognese to simmer away for a further 30 mins until you are left with a rich, thickened ragù. Season to taste.

Once the bolognese is nearly ready, drop the tagliatelle into a large pan of salted water and cook for 1 min less than pack instructions. Drain, saving half a mug of pasta water, then tip the pasta back into the saucepan. Add the bolognese to the pasta, tossing with tongs, and adding any pasta water if it needs it.
Serve the bolognese showered with a mountain of Parmesan and a few basil leaves, if you like.

name: Tahini Miso Beans
description: No time to cook? These creamy miso tahini beans are a store cupboard superstar. Ready in less than 10 mins and packing in plant protein and fibre for your gut microbes, they’re perfect for when you want something nourishing and delicious with minimal effort.
instructions: Finely chop your shallots and garlic. Heat a glug of olive oil in a large pan over a low-medium heat and gently fry the shallots for a few mins until lightly golden.
Add the chopped garlic to the pan and continue to cook for another minute before adding the beans along with their liquid. Cook them down for a few mins until the beans become creamy.
Turn off the heat and stir in your miso paste and tahini. This will thicken the beans so add in more water as needed to reach your desired texture.
Serve with whatever toppings you like: we recommend thinly sliced spring onions, a drizzle of crispy chilli oil and some fresh coriander.

name: Tahini Miso Ramen
description: Tantanmen ramen is a creamy, spicy, perfectly balanced broth made of tahini, miso and soy milk. If you’re looking for ultimate umami, this is it.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil and add the shiitake. Simmer for 5 mins and turn off the heat.
Meanwhile, cook your noodles according to instructions. Drain, drizzle with a little sesame oil to prevent sticking, set aside.
Whisk together 2 tbsp soy sauce, miso, tahini, milk and sesame oil in a small bowl. This is your flavour base for the broth which will be added later.
Grate the garlic and ginger and crumble the tofu into small pieces. Mix together in a small bowl with 2 tbsp of soy sauce and 1-2 tsp of crispy chili oil.

Heat 2 tbsp of vegetable oil in a frying pan. Fry the tofu on medium- high heat until it starts to crisp up, then add a tablespoon of soy sauce. Fry for a minute longer, then remove from the pan and wipe the pan clean to use again for the mushrooms.

Drain the mushrooms, keeping the broth to one side. Slice the mushrooms and fry with a drizzle of vegetable oil and 2 tbsp of soy sauce until cooked through. Add the sesame seeds and fry for another minute.
Finely slice the spring onion and chilli.
Add the mushroom broth back into the saucepan, bring to the boil. Then, remove from the heat and whisk in the miso and milk mixture.
To plate, add noodles to a bowl, then add the broth and top with the mushrooms, crumbled tofu, spring onion, sesame seeds and chilli. Finish with a drizzle of sesame oil and chilli oil.

name: Tahini Noodles with Smacked Cucumbers
description: So fresh, so clean. We love a noodle salad on a hot summery day. This one is paired with marinated smacked cucumbers and tossed in a tasty tahini sauce.
instructions: Trim the ends of the cucumbers. Using the flat blade of your knife or a rolling pin, gently smack the cucumbers until they split then slice into small chunks.
Transfer to a sieve placed over a bowl. Sprinkle with salt and toss well to coat. Leave to sit for 10 minutes to release some of the cucumber water.
Meanwhile, mince the garlic and red chilli.
Transfer to a mixing bowl and add the soy sauce, black vinegar, toasted sesame oil and sugar.
Add the cucumbers, toss well to coat and set aside.
Mince the garlic. Place the tahini in a large mixing bowl with the garlic, soy sauce, black vinegar, toasted sesame oil, sugar, toasted sesame seeds, chilli oil and the water. Whisk until smooth.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Season with salt, add the soba noodles and cook according to the packet instructions.
Drain, rinse with cold water and drain again.
Add the noodles to the tahini sauce, along with the smacked cucumbers, juices included. Toss to combine, ensuring the noodles are saucy and well-coated.
Transfer to a large plate, top with more sesame seeds then tuck in and enjoy.

name: Tahini Salted Caramel
description: Salty sweet > sweet sweet, all day, every day. Adding tahini to your caramel is a game changer. It makes the best ice cream topping.
instructions: Place all the ingredients in a small saucepan with 2 tsp Maldon salt and bring to a simmer over medium-low heat, stirring constantly until the sugar has dissolved.
Cook for 2 to 4 mins, or until golden and syrupy, then transfer to a heatproof bowl to cool. It will thicken as it sits.

name: Tahini Soba Noodle Soup with Miso Aubergine
description: An easy, breezy noodle soup recipe with fudgy miso aubergines. This is a solo vegan weeknight dinner that ticks all the boxes.
keywords: Tahini Soba Noodle Soup with Miso Aubergine
Tahini Soba Noodle Soup with Miso Aubergine recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Dice the aubergine into 2cm pieces. Transfer to a baking tray in a single layer.

Combine the miso, ½ tbsp olive oil, half the soy sauce and a drop of water in a bowl to form a paste. Pour the mixture over the aubergine, then scatter over the sesame seeds. Pop in the oven on the middle shelf for 15 mins, then mix and cook for another 10 mins.
Crumble the tofu onto a lined baking tray. Add the five-spice, the remaining olive oil and a pinch of salt. Slide into the oven on the top shelf and cook for 25 mins alongside the aubergine.
Grab a big soup bowl. Add the tahini, black vinegar, chilli oil and the remaining soy sauce. Mix until smooth. Taste and season with sugar if the tahini is bitter. Boil the kettle.
Cook the noodles following pack instructions, then drain. Finely chop the chives.

Slowly pour boiling water into the soup mix while stirring. If you pour too quickly, the base will split! Add a splash more boiling water if you prefer a thinner sauce. Add the noodles then top with the aubergine. Scatter over the crumbled tofu and chives, then serve with more chilli oil, if you like.

name: Tahini Stuffed Smoky Aubergine
description: This soft aubergine is topped with a garlicky creamy tahini dressing, crunchy chickpeas, and fresh pomegranate seeds. It's healthy and ridiculously good.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Take your garlic and wrap it up in baking paper, then bake for 40 minutes.
Place your aubergines on a baking tray and drizzle with oil, salt, and pepper. Massage in the seasoning and bake for 50 minutes.
Drain the chickpeas and add them to a separate bowl with smoked paprika, salt, a drizzle of olive oil, and cumin. Mix together and place on a baking tray with a pinch of salt. Bake for 30 minutes.
In a separate bowl, spoon in your tahini, a squeeze of lemon juice, a good pinch of salt and pepper and a glug of olive oil. Set aside.

Remove your garlic from the oven and squeeze out the roasted garlic. Finely chop to create a paste and place it in your tahini bowl. Mix this all together with a splash of water and squeeze over the juice of half a lemon until you get a creamy consistency. This is your tahini sauce.
Remove your aubergines from the oven and cut in half.
Once your chickpeas are ready its time to plate up. Place your sliced aubergine on a plate and drizzle with tahini sauce, harissa, crispy chickpeas, pomegranate, and pick over the mint. Tuck in!

name: Tajín Mango, Watermelon & Apple Fruit Skewers Recipe
description: These fruit skewers are coated in Tajín, a Mexican seasoning of lime, chilli and salt which adds a fiery kick to these fruit skewers. If you can’t get hold of it, simply mix the zest of lime with caster sugar, sea salt, crushed chilli flakes, and cayenne pepper or hot paprika. Nothing makes a summer barbecue complete quite like these fresh and delicious fruit kebabs. Refreshment central.
instructions: Cut away both cheeks from the mango, then use a small knife to cut the flesh of each cheek into a large crosshatch, being careful not to cut through the skin completely.
Use the knife to then slide along the peel, underneath the crosshatched flesh to remove the pieces of mango. Cut away any remaining chunks of mango still attached to the stone.
Cut the quarter watermelon into two pieces, then use the knife to cut away the green rind and discard. Cut the watermelon into pieces the same size as the mango.
Cut the apple in half, then cut away the core. Leaving its skin on, also cut into pieces the same size as the mango and watermelon.

Alternating fruit, thread onto the skewers. Sprinkle the tajin evenly over each of the skewers to lightly coat. Taste and add more Tajín, if you like. Eat straight away or chill in the fridge for added freshness.

name: Takeaway Beef Ho Fun
description: This recipe has been passed down from my iconic mum’s Chinese takeaway so you know it’s a goodie. Think tender stir-fried beef, soft rice noodles and an addictive garlicky sauce.
instructions: Thinly slice the beef against the grain. Add to a bowl with the bicarbonate soda then cover with cold water and mix to combine. Set aside for 15 mins to tenderise the meat.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the garlic. Wash the spring onions and choy sum. Chop the ends off the spring onions then chop into three chunks, separating the whites to greens. Chop the ends off the choy sum and then chop into three smaller pieces.
Place the fresh ho fun noodles on a heatproof plate and heat in a microwave or steamer for a few mins until soft. Remove and gently separate with your hands.
In a bowl, mix together all the stir-fry sauce ingredients and set aside.
Rinse the beef to remove the excess bicarbonate soda. Combine the beef marinade ingredients in a separate bowl. Add the beef, massage the marinade into the meat and set aside.

Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a wok set over a medium-high heat. Add the marinated beef and fry for 1-2 mins until mostly cooked then remove and set aside. Add the garlic and the spring onion whites to the same wok and stir fry for 1-2 mins until fragrant.
Add the cooked ho fun noodles and choy sum to the wok then immediately add the prepared sauce, pouring from the edge of the wok. Mix well until evenly coated. Add the beef and mix again.
Add the beansprouts and the spring onion greens and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Serve with crispy chilli oil and enjoy!

name: Tamarind & Tomato Salmon Curry
description: This lively little curry couldn’t be simpler. Blitz up your own curry paste, add your cherry tomatoes for sweetness, then finish with some tamarind. Delish.
instructions: Roughly chop the onion, ginger and chilli (deseed if you like). Cut the coriander stalks away from the leaves, saving the leaves.
Put the onion, ginger, chilli, coriander stalks, garlic, turmeric and 3 tbsp of water into a food processor and blitz to a smoothish curry paste, adding a little more water if it needs it.

Get a large frying pan or saucepan (one that has a lid) over a medium heat. Pour in the rapeseed oil, then scrape in the curry paste. Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5 mins until the raw onion has cooked out and the water has evaporated. Add the cumin and mustard seeds, cook for 1 min more, then tip in the tomatoes.
Simmer the curry for 10 mins, popping a few of the whole cherry tomatoes with the back of your spoon. Start cooking the rice according to the packet instructions.
Next, season the salmon fillets and cut into large chunks. Cut the green beans in half.

Add the tamarind paste to the curry, then season to taste with salt and sugar if needed. Stir through the green beans and place the pieces of salmon on top. Put a lid on the pan and cook for 5–6 mins until the fish is just cooked through – it will flake into large chunks.
Scatter the coriander leaves over the curry and serve in the middle of the table along with the rice for people to help themselves.

name: Tamarind Squash with Crispy Chickpeas
description: The winter salad to end all winter salads. Sticky and sour tamarind squash served with spicy crispy chickpeas and a swoosh of chilli yoghurt is heavenly.
keywords: tamarind squash with crispy chickpeas recipes
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Halve your squash lengthways, then slice your squash into 3cm thick crescents. Scrape out any seeds and pits with a spoon.
Combine your cumin, chilli powder and turmeric in a bowl.
Place your squash on a baking tray and sprinkle on half of your spice mix. Drizzle over a little olive oil and salt, then roast for 45 mins.
Drain your chickpeas, then toss these onto a baking tray with your remaining spice mix, some salt and olive oil. Mix so the chickpeas are totally coated, then bake for 20 mins until crispy.

Finely slice one of your chillies, then set aside to garnish later. Finely chop your remaining chillies and your mint. Tip these into a bowl along with your yoghurt and a good pinch of salt, then mix to combine.

Swoosh your yoghurt onto a plate and top it with your squash and chickpeas. Drizzle tamarind sauce over the surface, then finish with your sliced chillies and a pinch of flaky sea salt. Serve and enjoy.

name: Tamarind and Mango Braised Tofu
description: Spicy and sweet tamarind and mango combined with soft silken tofu. It's a marriage you didn't know you needed.
instructions: Blend up the red chillies to form a smooth paste, empty this into a bowl.
Blend up the garlic, ginger and onion until smooth, don’t worry about washing the blender in between. Pop this into a bowl.
Peel the mango and chop the flesh. Finely dice about 2 tbsps of mango and roughly chop the rest.
Gently take the silken tofu out of its packaging and place it onto a chopping board. Chop your tofu up into large cubes.
Blend the large cubes of mango in a blender until smooth.
Heat a large glug of oil in a frying pan, add in your blended red chillies and cook for 5 mins until the oil is stained red.
Add in the tomato purée and cook for another 5 mins, the purée will darken in colour.
Add in the blended onion mixture and cook for 2 mins. Next, you're going to want to pour in the mango and tamarind purée and cook for an additional 3 mins until slightly thickened.
Pour in 250ml of water and gently add in the silken tofu. Mix gently so as not to break apart the tofu and allow to bubble for 5 mins on low heat.
Finely chop your spring onions.

Meanwhile, get your kettle boiling. Put your tahini in a bowl and pour in 100ml of boiling water whisking constantly to get a thick sauce. You may need to add more water to get the right consistency. Season with salt.
Serve up the tofu in a large bowl, drizzle with the tahini sauce, more tamarind sauce, spring onion and the finely chopped mango. Enjoy with rice.

name: Tandoori Broccoli Wraps
description: Make sure you really char your broccoli. This will allow your spices to toast, bringing out the best flavour.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C/392°F. Line a large roasting tray with tin foil or baking paper.

Cut the broccoli into medium florets and roughly chop the stalks. Mix together half the yoghurt with the curry paste and 1 tbsp neutral oil in a large bowl. Add the broccoli, season well with salt and pepper and mix so that the broccoli gets nicely coated in the curried yoghurt.

Tip the broccoli out onto the roasting tray, making sure to scrape all of the yoghurt marinade onto it then spread out into a single layer. Roast for around 15 minutes until the broccoli is tender with a good bite and nicely charred.

Meanwhile, make the kachumber salad. Finely chop the red onion. Chop the tomatoes and cucumber. Pick the mint leaves, tearing any large ones in half or roughly chop. Mix everything together in a bowl, squeeze in the lemon juice and season with salt, pepper and cayenne, to taste.
Heat the wraps or flatbreads, if you like. Spread with the remaining yoghurt. Top with the tandoori broccoli and kachumber salad.

name: Tandoori Chicken Burger
description: You’ve never had chicken packed with so much flavour. Spicy and smoky from a spell on the Weber BBQ. Loaded into buns with all the fresh bits. A BBQ beauty.
instructions: Add 300g plain of your yoghurt to a bowl and grate in your ginger and garlic. Add your tandoori masala, chilli powder, garam masala and a pinch of salt. Tip in your chicken thigh fillets and mix to combine. Marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Finely chop your mint and coriander. Finely dice your red onion and your tomatoes. Slice your red chilli.

Grate your cucumber into a bowl. Season with salt, then squeeze out over the sink to remove excess liquid. Pop it back in the bowl and add the rest of your yoghurt, chopped mint, the juice of half your lemon and a pinch of salt. Give it a mix.
Add your tomato to a bowl along with your red chilli, red onion and remaining lemon juice. Add your chopped coriander and give it a good mix. Season to taste with salt and pepper
Heat your Weber barbecue to a medium-high heat. Add your chicken thighs and cook for about 7 mins until charred. Flip and cook for about another 7 mins.
Remove your chicken thighs from the barbecue and place on a plate to rest. Meanwhile, toast your burger buns on the barbecue.

Assembly time. Spread some cucumber yoghurt on the base of your burger bun, then add two chicken fillets. Top with your tomato salsa. Spread some mango chutney and more cucumber yoghurt on the top of the burger bun, then place on top. Serve and enjoy.

name: Tandoori Chicken Burgers with Spicy Mayo
description: A spicy twist on a succulent chicken burger. This tandoori chicken burger is the ultimate fakeaway recipe.
instructions: Put the chicken pieces into a large bowl with the curry powder, tandoori paste, juice of the lemon, yoghurt and a pinch of salt and pepper. You can leave it to marinate briefly or use it straight away.
Heat a large lidded frying pan over a medium heat, then add the chicken. Fry for 5 mins on each side, until golden all over.
Meanwhile, combine the sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Set aside.
Slice the red onion into rings and add them to the chicken pan. Cook for 3 mins until charred.
Top the chicken with the cheese slice, then put a lid on the pan and leave for 5 mins, so the cheese melts.
Meanwhile, chop the lettuce and tomatoes.

To assemble, split the burger buns into halves. Spread a light layer of mayo over each bun half, then toast the bun halves, mayo-side down, in a frying pan over a low-medium heat for 2 mins. Spread one burger half with sauce, add some chicken and charred onion, then finish with the shredded lettuce and sliced tomato on top. Top with a bun half and enjoy!

name: Tandoori Chicken with Tamarind Chickpea Salad
description: Charred tandoori chicken, cooling yoghurt, and a zingy tamarind chickpea salad. A bold, fresh and flavourful lunch that's great for your weekly meal prep.
keywords: tandoori chicken with tamarind chickpea salad
instructions: Heat the grill to medium-high.
Finely grate the garlic into a bowl. Add the tandoori spice mix, Greek yoghurt, a pinch of salt and a few cracks of black pepper. Stir to combine into a marinade.
Butterfly the chicken breasts, then pop them between two sheets of baking parchment. Bash with a rolling pin until they’re about 1cm thick. Add the chicken to the marinade and toss to coat well.

Line a baking tray with foil and lay the chicken breasts flat on top, making sure all the marinade is spread over them. Slide under the grill for 10–15 mins until cooked through and starting to char. If they’re catching too fast, lower the tray or turn the grill down.
Meanwhile, dice the cucumber into 2cm chunks and chop the tomatoes into bite-sized pieces. Pick the mint leaves and discard the stems.
Whisk together the tamarind purée, honey and the juice of the lime in a small bowl. Season with salt to taste and tweak with more lime or honey, if needed.
Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and mint with the tamarind dressing until well coated.

Spoon your salad into your Tupperware containers and top with the chicken. Finish with some freshly cracked black pepper and any remaining lime wedges. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Tandoori Chicken with Tamarind Chickpea Salad
description: Charred tandoori chicken, cooling yoghurt, and a zingy tamarind chickpea salad. Bold, fresh and flavourful.
keywords: tandoori chicken with tamarind chickpea salad
instructions: Heat the grill to medium-high.
Finely grate the garlic into a bowl. Add the tandoori spice mix, Greek yoghurt, a pinch of salt and a few cracks of black pepper. Stir to combine into a marinade.
Butterfly the chicken breasts, then pop them between two sheets of baking parchment. Bash with a rolling pin until they’re about 1cm thick. Add the chicken to the marinade and toss to coat well.

Line a baking tray with foil and lay the chicken breasts flat on top, making sure all the marinade is spread over them. Slide under the grill for 10–15 mins until cooked through and starting to char. If they’re catching too fast, lower the tray or turn the grill down.
Meanwhile, dice the cucumber into 2cm chunks and chop the tomatoes into bite-sized pieces. Pick the mint leaves and discard the stems.
Whisk together the tamarind purée, honey and the juice of the lime in a small bowl. Season with salt to taste and tweak with more lime or honey, if needed.
Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and mint with the tamarind dressing until well coated.
Share the salad onto plates and top with the chicken. Finish with some freshly cracked black pepper and any remaining lime wedges.

name: Tandoori Fried Chicken Sandwich
description: James Cochran from 12:51 stuns us with his belter of a sandwich. Expect crispy fried chicken, curry mayo, tangy pickles, and heaps of crunchy Bombay mix.
instructions: Start with making your brine for the chicken. Put tandoori spice, ginger, garlic, 100g salt and 200ml of water in a blender and blend till smooth. Add 300ml water and the spices paste to the pan, bring to a boil and then take it off the heat. Allow it to cool fully in the fridge.
Once the brine is cold, add in the chicken thighs and brine for 2-4 hours.
Combine the buttermilk, 2 tsp curry powder and 1 tsp turmeric in a bowl. Drain the chicken thighs from the brine and add it to the buttermilk. Pop it back into the fridge until you are ready to fry.

On to your pickles. Pick the mint leaves off the stems, reserving the stems and finely slice your red chilli. Bring the mint stems, finely sliced chilli, vinegar, sugar, a pinch of salt and 300ml water to the boil in a small saucepan. Once the sugar has dissolved, after 3 mins, take it off the heat and allow to cool completely.
Once the pickling liquid is cold, very thinly slice your apples and cucumber. Put the apples, cucumber and mint leaves into the cold pickling liquid. Pop this into the fridge for 2 hours.
Add your yoghurt to a bowl and season with salt.
For the curry mayo, add 2 tsp curry powder, 1 tsp turmeric, black mustard seeds, 50ml vegetable oil. Heat for 2 mins on medium heat until bubbling and aromatic.
In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise with 1 tbsp of the curry oil. Season with salt.
Mix together the plain flour and cornflour into a shallow bowl.
Fill up a big pan with vegetable oil and bring it to medium-high heat.

Get your chicken out of the fridge and shake off the excess. Dip it into the flour, pressing firmly so it’s coated completely. Dip the chicken into the hot oil and fry for 4-5 mins until golden brown, crispy, and cooked through. Remove and let it drain on some paper towels.

Now to build the sandwich. Get two slices of bread and layer it up with your fried chicken followed by the seasoned yoghurt and curry mayo, pickled cucumber and apples, a spoon of Bombay mix, some crispy shallots, and mint. Spread yoghurt and curry mayo on the other slice of bread and sandwich the two together. Slice in half and enjoy.

name: Tandoori Whole-Roast Cauliflower with Green Chutney
description: A gorgeous whole-roast cauliflower marinated in an aromatic tandoori rub. The ultimate vegetarian centrepiece.
keywords: Tandoori Whole-Roast Cauliflower with Green Chutney
Tandoori Whole-Roast Cauliflower with Green Chutney recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Melt the butter. Combine all the marinade ingredients in a large bowl, reserving two-thirds of the melted butter to brush the cauliflower while it cooks.
Remove the leaves from the cauliflower, then place the whole head into the marinade bowl. Make sure the cauli is thoroughly coated with the marinade, especially in the crevices.

Place the marinated cauliflower on a baking tray lined with baking parchment. Roast in the oven for 40-50 mins, or until the cauliflower is tender and nicely charred on the outside. Raise the temperature to the highest your oven will go for the last 10 mins of cooking time, and keep brushing with melted butter every 5 mins. Check to see if the cauliflower is done by inserting a knife into its core – it should go through easily.

While the cauliflower is roasting, prepare the green chutney. Put all the ingredients except the yoghurt into a blender and blend until you have a smooth, thick green paste. Add a splash of water if required. Add salt to taste (start with ½ tsp then add more, if you like).
Put the yoghurt into a bowl and fold the blended chutney mix through it. Check the seasoning and set aside.
Drizzle the cauliflower with extra melted butter and serve with the chutney on the side.

name: Tango Ice Blast
description: A homemade version of everyone's favourite cinema slush. Our Tango Ice Blast recipe is even tastier than the real thing.
instructions: Pour each of the Tango flavours into ice cube trays or lolly moulds and freeze overnight.

Take the ice lollies off their sticks. Remove the Tango Apple ice cubes from tray or mould, then put into a processor with a few drops of blue food colouring, a handful of ice, and 1 of the ice lollies. Blitz, pour in a bit more apple tango to loosen it up, mix again, then transfer to the freezer.
Repeat the whole process with the Tango Cherry ice cubes.
Pour the blue tango ice blast into a glass and top with half of the sherbet. Pour over the cherry flavour and sprinkle with the remaining sherbet. Give it a little mix with a straw and get stuck in!

name: Tangy Chicken & Crispy Rice Salad
description: Crispy rice, sticky tamarind chicken and a punchy peanut-lime dressing. This one’s fresh, crunchy and properly zingy. Whip it up in under 40 for a winning mid-week meal.
keywords: Tangy Chicken & Crispy Rice Salad recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.

Line a baking tray with baking paper. Toss the rice with the chilli oil and olive oil, then spread it out on the tray. Slide into the oven and bake for 30–35 mins, tossing halfway, until golden and crispy.
Meanwhile, thinly slice or shave the cabbage. Core and thinly slice the apples. Halve the sugar snaps and the cherry tomatoes.

Make the dressing: Add the cherry tomatoes to a large mixing bowl along with the peanut butter, tamarind purée, lime juice and honey. Stir everything together and gently squash the tomatoes to release their juices. Taste and season with fish sauce to your liking.

Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 10–15 mins, turning occasionally, until golden and cooked through.

Bash the garlic cloves and add them to the chicken along with the tamarind purée, honey, water and fish sauce. Stir and let it bubble for 2–5 mins until thickened into a sticky glaze. Taste and season again if needed.
Once the rice is crispy, toss it into the bowl with the veg and dressing. Mix well to coat.
Slice the chicken and serve on top of the crispy rice salad. Finish with an extra drizzle of chilli oil if you fancy more heat, or olive oil if you're keeping it mild.

name: Tangy Cod & Tomato Brothy Rice with Tadka
description: A flavourful tamarind broth with poached cod, fluffy rice and spiced ghee. Nourishing, light and very comforting.
keywords: Tangy Cod & Tomato Brothy Rice with Tadka
instructions: Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems. Peel and finely grate the garlic.

Heat a saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the ground spices, coriander stems and garlic. Cook for a couple of seconds until fragrant. Then pour the crushed tomatoes in with the tamarind paste, season with salt, a big pinch of sugar and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-8 mins until thickened and darkened.
Pour in the stock, let it come to a boil, turn the heat down, and gently simmer for 5 mins.

Gently place the cod fillets in the broth and let them cook for 3-5 mins or until opaque and cooked through (the thicker the cod fillets, the longer it will take). When the fish is cooked through, taste and season with salt, sugar and more tamarind if necessary.

Meanwhile, reheat the cooked rice and make the tadka. Melt the ghee in a small saucepan set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the mustard and cumin seeds and cook until they start to pop, then drop the curry leaves in (careful, they will splutter) and cook until fragrant and crispy. Remove the pan from the heat.
Share the rice between bowls and ladle in the broth. Top with the poached fish, a drizzle of the tadka and finish with the coriander leaves.

name: Tangy Tamarind Roasted Veg Salad
description: Inspired by the flavours found in Indian chaat, this is a tangy, spicy, hearty salad, perfect for a make ahead nutritious lunch.
instructions: Heat the oven to fan 200°C

Peel (optional) and chop the carrots & sweet potatoes into 2cm chunks. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, season with salt & pepper, then spread out on a baking tray. Roast for 25–30 mins, until softened.
Meanwhile stir the ground cumin, tamarind purée & maple to make the sweet and tangy glaze. Taste & tweak the balance if needed, more tamarind for tang, more maple for sweetness. Set aside.

Trim and thinly slice the onion and green chilli. Pick the coriander leaves, set the coriander stems aside. Place the onion into a sieve and wash under cold running water. Then soak in a bowl full of ice water, this takes away the harsh bite and makes them last longer.
Chuck the coriander stems, yoghurt, green chillies, ground cumin & olive oil into a blender. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt, pepper & lemon juice to taste. Divide between boxes.
Once the veggies are cooked, pour the tamarind glaze over the top, toss together and return to the oven for 5-7 mins until sticky. Leave to cool before boxing up.
Drain the onions and toss with the sliced green chilli, coriander leaves and roasted veg.
Top the dressing with the grains and roasted veg mixture. Refrigerate until needed. Shake before serving.

name: Tangy Tomato & Strawberry Salad
description: This zingy strawberry salad comes together in no time but packs serious flavour. Fresh, satiating and just as good solo as well as topped with chicken or a crispy fried egg for extra protein.
keywords: strawberry salad with fish sauce dressing
instructions: Thinly slice the lemongrass and chillies, then add to a bowl with juice the limes in as well. Add the fish sauce, tasting and adding more if needed.
Halve the strawberries, quartering any larger ones, and chop the tomatoes into 2-3cm chunks. Toss both into the lime dressing.
Thinly slice the sugarsnaps and pick the mint leaves, then toss through the salad with the rice and a drizzle of olive oil.
Divide between containers and store in the fridge until needed.

name: Tangy Tomato & Strawberry Salad
description: This zingy strawberry salad comes together in no time but packs serious flavour. Fresh, satiating and just as good solo as well as topped with chicken or a crispy fried egg for extra protein.
keywords: strawberry salad with fish sauce dressing
instructions: Thinly slice the lemongrass and chillies, then add to a bowl with juice the limes in as well. Add the fish sauce, tasting and adding more if needed.
Halve the strawberries, quartering any larger ones, and chop the tomatoes into 2-3cm chunks. Toss both into the lime dressing.
Thinly slice the sugarsnaps and pick the mint leaves, then toss through the salad with the rice and a drizzle of olive oil.
Divide between plates to serve.

name: Tangy Tomato & Tinned Sardine Curry
description: Inspired by Malaysian sardine curry, this is a punchy, tangy one-pan dinner. Tinned sardines, jammy cherry tomatoes and wilted spinach in a warm, tamarind-spiked curry sauce all ready in under 30 mins.
instructions: Thinly slice the onion, finely grate the ginger and garlic and pick the coriander leaves, thinly slicing the stems. Set aside the leaves for later.

Place a saucepan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the onion and cook for 5-6 mins until softened and starting to brown. Add the garlic, ginger, coriander stems, curry powder and curry leaves (if using) and cook for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Add the soy sauce and stir until it has evaporated.
Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 3-5 mins until starting to soften. Pour in the water, then gently stir through the spinach until wilted.
Stir in the sardines and tamarind paste and cook until piping hot. Taste and season with salt and pepper, add a little more tamarind if you want more tang.
Reheat the rice and divide between bowls. Spoon over the sardine curry and finish with a scatter of coriander leaves.

name: Tantanmen Ramen
description: Here's our vegan take on a Japanese interpretation of Dan Dan Noodles. The spicy, creamy, nutty broth is everything.
instructions: Start by making your tare – this is the flavour bomb that is going to infuse into your broth. In a bowl, combine your tahini, chilli oil, soy sauce and sugar in a bowl. Set aside until later.

Heat a little vegetable oil in a frying pan over a high heat. Get your block of tofu and crumble it with your hands over the pan so it becomes like mince. Fry for 3 mins until it's starting to crisp up, then grate in your garlic and ginger. Stir fry for another minute before adding your dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, mirin and chilli oil. Stir to combine, then set aside.
Cut your pak choi into quarters lengthways, then slice your spring onions.

For the broth, bring the water, soy milk and soy sauce to the boil in a large saucepan. Turn down to a simmer, then whisk in your miso paste. Add your noodles and pak choi, then simmer for 3 mins until tender.

Place a quarter of your tare into the base of a bowl and add your broth. Stir to combine with a spoon, then add your noodles to the broth. Top with your pak choi, tofu, spring onions, and an extra drizzle of chilli oil if you like. Serve and enjoy.

name: Tartiflette
description: One of the most loved winter dish in France, this simple tartiflette recipe is the ultimate comfort food. A classic French recipe.
instructions: Peel and slice the potatoes (3 to 4 mm thick) and pour into a medium pan filled with cold water and 1 tsp of salt. Cover, and cook for 15 mins. Drain and set aside.
Finely slice your onions. Fry the sliced onions with the butter in a large frying pan for 3 to 5 mins under medium heat. Add the white wine and cook until it evaporates. Set aside.
Fry the lardons in the same pan, until golden and crispy, for 5 to 7 mins then remove the fat from the pan.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Put half the potatoes in the bottom of your casserole dish or deep tray. Spread half of the onions, topped with half of the lardons and half of the cream. Top it with the rest of the potatoes then add in the rest of your onions and lardon, and finally the cream.
Slice the Reblochon lengthways, then place on top, crust-side facing up. Pepper to taste.
Cook for 30 mins, until the Reblochon has fully melted and golden on top.
Serve with a dressed salad.

name: Tempeh Burrito Bowl with Black Beans & Salsa
description: A healthy, protein-heavy burrito bowl with crispy tempeh, fresh salsa, black beans and brown rice, all served in a crunchy baked tortilla bowl.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
If making a tortilla bowl, press the wrap into an ovenproof bowl to form a bowl shape. Bake for 10 mins until golden and crisp, then remove and cool. Or, simply serve with tortilla for scooping.
Heat the rice according to pack instructions. Drain and rinse the black beans, then stir them through the rice with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Set aside.

Peel and finely dice the onion. Halve the tomato, scoop out the seeds, then finely dice the flesh. Chop the coriander and combine it all in a bowl with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt and pepper. Slice the roasted peppers.

Crumble the tempeh into mince-sized pieces. Heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the tempeh and fry for 5–6 mins until golden and crisp. Add the paprika, cumin and chilli powder, then stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

To build your bowl, spoon in the rice and beans, top with the spiced tempeh, fresh salsa and sliced roasted peppers. Finish with a dollop of yoghurt, a scattering of coriander and a lime wedge on the side.

name: Tempeh Burrito Bowl with Black Beans & Salsa
description: A healthy, protein-heavy burrito bowl with crispy tempeh, fresh salsa, black beans and brown rice, all served in a crunchy baked tortilla bowl. A meal prep lunch that'll have the whole office seething with envy.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
If making a tortilla bowl, press the wrap into an ovenproof bowl to form a bowl shape. Bake for 10 mins until golden and crisp, then remove and cool. Or, simply serve with tortilla for scooping.
Heat the rice according to pack instructions. Drain and rinse the black beans, then stir them through the rice with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Set aside.

Peel and finely dice the onion. Halve the tomato, scoop out the seeds, then finely dice the flesh. Chop the coriander and combine it all in a bowl with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt and pepper. Slice the roasted peppers.

Crumble the tempeh into mince-sized pieces. Heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the tempeh and fry for 5–6 mins until golden and crisp. Add the paprika, cumin and chilli powder, then stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

To build your bowl, spoon in the rice and beans, top with the spiced tempeh, fresh salsa and sliced roasted peppers. Finish with a dollop of yoghurt, a scattering of coriander and a lime wedge on the side. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Tempeh Noodles
description: Tasty high-protein vegan noodles. What's not to love?
instructions: Crumble the tempeh into small pieces. Roughly chop the mushrooms. Finely slice the spring onions and set aside some of the green tips to serve.

Put the tempeh, spring onions and mushrooms into a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a good splash of sunflower oil and a pinch of salt. Stir-fry for about 10 mins until starting to crisp up.
Meanwhile, make the marinade. Grate the ginger, mince the garlic, and add to a small bowl with the juice of the lime and the remaining ingredients. Whisk well.
In a separate pan, cook the spinach with a pinch of salt over a medium heat until wilted.
Add the marinade to the tempeh. Fry for 5-10 mins until the tempeh and mushrooms are browned on the edges and starting to crisp up.
Cook the noodles following pack instructions, then drain.
For the noodle sauce, first juice the lime into a bowl. Add all the remaining ingredients and whisk well. Toss the cooked noodles through it.
Serve the saucy noodles in bowls topped with the tempeh, reserved spring onion greens, sesame seeds, some extra chilli oil and the wilted spinach.

name: Tempeh Stuffed Aubergines with Thai Basil Salad
description: A brilliant way into tempeh if you've never cooked with it before. Spiced, crispy tempeh packed into soft roasted aubergine, with a bright Thai basil and red onion salad on the side. It's way easier than it looks.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Peel strips of skin from the aubergines so they're zebra-striped, then place in a large ovenproof dish. Rub with a little vegetable oil, season with salt and roast for 30-40 mins, until soft and starting to collapse. Remove from the oven and leave to cool slightly.

Meanwhile, blitz the tempeh in a food processor into a rough crumble and set aside. Peel and roughly chop the garlic. Roughly chop one of the red onions, the pepper, chillies and tomatoes and blitz everything in the food processor with the garlic until finely minced — do this in batches if needed.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the crumbled tempeh and fry for 5-6 mins, until starting to crisp up. Set aside. Add the blitzed vegetables to the pan and cook for 5-6 mins, until softened and most of the liquid has evaporated. Add the tempeh back in along with the soy sauce and the juice of one of the limes. Season with salt and black pepper, then finely chop half the Thai basil and stir through. Turn off the heat.

Cut a slit down the middle of each aubergine, being careful not to cut all the way through. Using a fork or your hands, flatten and open each one up to make space for the filling. Pack a quarter of the filling into each aubergine, don't be shy about it.

Add the tomato purée and water to a jug, season with salt and whisk with a fork until combined. Pour over and around the aubergines in the dish. Return to the oven and bake for 20 mins, until the tops are crisping up and catching at the edges.

Meanwhile, cut the second red onion into strips and toss in a small bowl with the remaining Thai basil and the juice of the second lime. Heat the quinoa according to the packet instructions. Serve the aubergines with the quinoa and the red onion salad.

name: Tequila Sunrise
description: The key to this one is using in season oranges and straining the juice to get rid of the pulp so you get a smooth delicious cocktail!
instructions: Start by rolling and juicing your oranges, then strain them to remove all the pulp so your drink is smooth and delicious.
Load up a highball glass with ice.
Pour in your tequila of choice and orange juice.
Gently pour your grenadine over a spoon to allow the liquids of different densities to slowly mix and create the iconic sunrise colours in the glass.
Garnish with a slice of your orange and enjoy.

name: Teriyaki Aubergine with Whipped Tofu
description: The softest aubergines served with not one, but TWO delicious sauces. Silky whipped tofu for creaminess, glossy teriyaki for a sweet umami hit.
keywords: Teriyaki aubergine with whipped tofu recipe
instructions: Heat your oven to 200°C.
Cut your aubergines into rounds 3cm thick.
Lay them on baking trays lined with parchment paper. Drizzle your aubergine slices with olive oil and a pinch of salt, then pop them in the oven for 30 mins.
Next, make your teriyaki sauce. Add your caster sugar, soy sauce, knob of ginger and the water to a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until your sugar has dissolved.

Mix your cornflour in a bowl with 1 tbsp water to form a paste. Pour this into your sauce and stir immediately. Let the mixture come to a boil. After simmering for 5 mins, it should be drizzle-able and glossy. Add your rice wine vinegar and mix to combine. Set aside.
For the whipped tofu, add your smoked tofu to a blender with your miso paste, water and olive oil. Whizz to a smooth paste, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Add your nori sheet to a spice grinder or food processor and whizz to a powder. Combine this with your chilli powder and sesame seeds in a bowl.
Once the 30 mins for your aubergine is up, flip them over and return them to the oven for another 10 mins.

Chop the woody ends off your spring onions. Heat a griddle pan over a high heat, and place your spring onions into the pan. Cook for a couple of mins on each side until they have deep char lines. Remove from the pan with tongs, then chop into lengths.

Spread your whipped smoked tofu onto your chosen serving platter. Top with your roasted aubergine rounds, then pour over your teriyaki sauce. Add your spring onions and your sesame seed powder on top, then serve and enjoy.

name: Teriyaki Beef & Egg Rice Bowl
description: I feel like most people don't understand how easy it is to make teriyaki sauce, so here's a super quick and simple way of enjoying it.
keywords: Teriyaki Beef & Egg Rice Bowl recipe
Chloe René teriyaki beef rice bowl
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil for the eggs. Meanwhile, pat the beef dry and season with salt and black pepper.

Now for the teriyaki. Peel and lightly crush the garlic clove, then add it to a large frying pan with the soy sauce, sake, mirin and honey. Stir together and place over a medium heat. Bring to the boil, then cook for 3-5 mins, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Pour into a bowl and give the pan a quick clean.
Once the water is boiling, gently lower the eggs in and cook for 6-7 mins, until jammy - go a couple of minutes longer if you like them firmer. Transfer to a bowl of cold water to cool.

Using a peeler, shave the carrots and cucumber into ribbons and add them to a bowl. Season with salt, a splash of soy sauce and the juice of the lime. Toss the toasted sesame seeds and toasted sesame oil through, then set aside.

Place the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the neutral oil, then stir-fry the beef for 2-4 mins, until browned - keep going if you want it more well done. Take off the heat and stir half the teriyaki through.
Reheat the rice according to the packet instructions. Peel the eggs, add them to a bowl with a couple of spoonfuls of the teriyaki and mash with a fork, then toss the rice through.
Share the rice between bowls and top with the salad and beef. Drizzle over any remaining teriyaki and dig in.

name: Teriyaki Beef Tacos
description: These teriyaki tacos are an absolute winner of a fusion dish. They’re super simple to make and taste absolutely delicious.
instructions: Cut the pepper and half of the spring onions into strips. Set the spring onion strips aside for later and chop the remaining spring onions horizontally into coins. Crush the garlic cloves.
Set a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat, then add the spring onion coins, peppers and garlic. Cook for a few minutes, then add the beef mince and fry for around 7 mins until cooked through.
Add the teriyaki sauce, honey and soy sauce to the beef along with water. Stir and simmer for a few minutes over a medium heat until sticky.
Combine the beef mix with half of the grated cheese in a large bowl. Wipe the frying pan clean.

Heat up the tortilla wraps in the microwave to make them more flexible, then reheat the frying pan to a medium heat while dipping each wrap into the mix to cover the outside. Place each wrap, one at a time and saucy-side down, into the pan and add one-eighth of the beef mix plus one-eighth of the remaining grated cheese onto one half of the wrap, then fold over.
Cook for a few minutes, then flip it over to cook the other side. Meanwhile, prepare your toppings by roughly chopping the coriander and slicing the red chilli.
Once cooked, set the cooked tacos aside for a few minutes to cool, then top with the spring onion strips, chilli and coriander.

name: Teriyaki Chicken & Egg Bowl
description: Sticky-sweet teriyaki chicken? Jammy eggs? Easy. This is a bowl of pure comfort with plenty of protein.
instructions: Cook the rice using your preferred method. Boil the eggs for 7 mins, then run under cold water and peel.
Finely grate the garlic and ginger. Trim and finely slice the spring onions, keeping the whites and greens separate.
In a small bowl, mix the soy sauces, brown sugar, grated garlic, ginger, sesame oil, water and cornflour. Mix well until there are no lumps.
Chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces and season with a pinch of salt.
Set a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 6–7 mins, stirring occasionally, until golden and cooked through.
Pour in the sauce and the spring onion whites. Cook for 3-5 minutes until reduced and becomes thick and glossy.
Halve the boiled eggs.
To serve, spoon the rice into bowls. Top with the teriyaki chicken and sauce, the halved eggs and the edamame. Finish with spring onion greens and a scattering of sesame seeds.

name: Teriyaki Chicken & Sticky Wasabi Rice
description: An absolute worldy of a fakeaway. The sticky wasabi rice complements the rich teriyaki perfectly.
keywords: Teriyaki chicken and sticky wasabi rice
instructions: Get your sushi rice on (follow pack instructions).
De-bone your chicken thighs and keep the skins on. Add thighs to a bowl and salt the skins.

Add a splash of oil to a frying pan. Add the chicken, skin side down, and cook for 5 minutes until the skin is nice and brown. Turn the chicken over and cook for another 4 minutes. Keep turning the thighs until they are cooked through. Leave them on a board to rest.

Teriyaki time. Add soy sauce, mirin, 3 tbsp of water and a tsp of ginger to a pan. Mix them all together. Add a level tbsp of sugar. Stir it in. Cook the sauce until it is nice and thick. Remove from the heat.
Once the rice is ready, add a heaped tsp of wasabi paste to it. Mix it in.
Slice up your chicken thighs. Add a big spoonful of the sticky rice to a plate. Top with 2 thighs and pour over your thick teriyaki sauce. Tuck in! Enjoy!

name: Teriyaki Glazed Chicken & Chive Rice Bowl
description: Everyone loves teriyaki chicken, right? This teriyaki-glazed chicken rice bowl is a high-protein wonder. You'll love this fakeaway recipe.
keywords: Teriyaki Glazed Chicken & Chive Rice Bowl
Teriyaki Glazed Chicken & Chive Rice Bowl recipe
instructions: If cooking rice from scratch, wash the rice in a pan with cold water and drain. Repeat twice or until the water runs clear. Add water to the rice in the pan. Let it sit for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, slice the chives as fine as possible and set aside in a bowl. Cut the seaweed in half, stack on top of each other and, using scissors, cut as thin as possible. Set aside.

Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and whisk vigorously. Heat a frying pan over a medium heat, add 1 tsp oil and, using kitchen paper or a brush, smear the oil across the pan. Add half the beaten egg, then tilt the pan to cover the surface with egg. Leave for 1 min or until cooked. Remove the egg sheet to a chopping board and repeat with the remaining egg.
Stack the two egg sheets and roll them up. Slice them as thin as possible, then set the resulting egg ribbons aside.

Bring the pot of soaking rice to the boil over a high heat. Once boiling, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 11 mins. Turn the heat off and leave for a further 10 mins, with the lid on. It’s important not to remove the lid until it’s ready.

Season the chicken on both sides lightly with salt and pepper. Grab the same frying pan that you used for the egg and set it over a high heat for 2 mins. Add 1 tbsp oil and swirl. Add the chicken thighs and cook for 4 mins. Flip over and cook for a further 4 mins. Add the sake, mirin, soy sauce and sugar. Swirl the pan for 1-2 mins until the sugar is dissolved. Flip the chicken to glaze both sides. Remove the chicken and set aside.

Add the cornstarch and cold water to a small bowl. Stir to make a slurry. Turn the heat to its lowest setting and slowly pour the slurry into the pan while stirring. The sauce should thicken – if too thick, add 1 tbsp cold water.
Slice the chicken into 1-2 cm strips.

Divide the rice between deep bowls followed by a generous amount of nori strips and egg ribbons. Add the sliced chicken and pour the sauce on top. Finish with a big handful of chives – the more the better!

name: Teriyaki Salmon
description: The softest, break away salmon on a bed of fluffy rice. The combination of the Sriracha mayo and the sticky teriyaki is out of this world.
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions.

In a small bowl, mix the mayonnaise and sriracha until combined then set aside. Peel and finely grate the garlic and ginger. In a small bowl, stir the cornflour with a splash of water to make a slurry. Thinly slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish.

Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 min until fragrant. Pour in the soy sauce, brown sugar, honey and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for 4-5 mins until the sauce starts to thicken.
Place the salmon fillets into the pan, skin-side down. Cover with a lid and cook for 4-6 mins until fully cooked through. If your fillets are thick, they may take longer.

Divide the rice between bowls and top with the salmon. To the remaining sauce in the pan, add the cornflour slurry and stir. Let it bubble for 1-2 mins until thickened. Add a splash of water if needed to adjust the consistency.
To serve, spoon over the teriyaki sauce and drizzle with the sriracha mayo. Finish with a sprinkle of spring onions.

name: Teriyaki Tofu
description: The sweet pomegranate works so nicely with the teriyaki. The mint freshens it up perfectly. A great mouthful.
instructions: Chop your tofu up into chunks. Cook your rice following pack instructions.
Cover the chunks in cornflour.
Add a splash of olive oil to a hot pan.
Once the oil is hot enough, add the tofu chunks. Turn until each side is golden brown.
Teriyaki time. Add soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, 10 tbsp of water and a tsp of ginger to a bowl. Mix together. Add 1 1/2 tablespoons of agave nectar.
Add your teriyaki sauce to the pan to warm and bubble for a couple of mins until thickened.
Put the pomegranate seeds in a sieve over the pan. Press a teaspoon down onto them, allowing the juices to drip into the pan.
Add the mint and the tofu and mix together.
Place the tofu on a bed of rice. Garnish with pomegranate and tuck in!

name: Thai Basil Chicken (Mob Style)
description: A Thai classic that we've put our own MOB twist on. Definitely worth getting some chicken mince from your butcher for this.
instructions: Finely slice onion, red chilli and garlic. Set them aside.
Add 1 part rice to 2 parts boiling water. Cook until the water has been absorbed.
Put a wok or a large frying pan on the heat. Add a splash of vegetable oil and add the ground chicken. Break it up into lots of little pieces with a spatula .
Once the chicken has turned white, add your chilli, garlic, onion and lemongrass puree. Mix them in.
Once they have softened, add a tbsp and a half of fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar. Mix it all in.
Once the sugar has dissolved, pour in 150ml of water. Simmer it down for 30 seconds. Throw in your basil.
Allow the basil to wilt. Cook the chicken until the water has evaporated.
Remove the wok from the heat and set on a board.
Serve the chicken on top of the steaming hot basmati rice. Enjoy!

name: Thai Basil Chicken High Protein Smash
description: Shredded chicken, jammy eggs and Tenderstem broccoli tossed in a sticky, spicy Thai sauce and smashed together. A meal prep winner.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Drop in the Tenderstem broccoli and blanch for 2 mins, until bright green and just tender. Drain and leave to cool. Then roughly chop, along with the chilli and then add to a large mixing bowl.

Now, for the eggs. You can either boil or fry them, frying lends to a more authentic taste while boiling them adds a creamier consistency.To fry the eggs, simply heat up a few tablespoons of oil in a frying pan and fry the eggs over a medium heat until slightly crispy but still with runny yolks, drain on a paper towel and leave to cool. Then add to the bowl with your broccoli.orTo boil the eggs, use the same pan for your broccoli, top up the water if needed and bring back to the boil. Drop in the eggs and simmer for 8 mins, then cool in iced water. Peel and separate the yolks from the whites, then add to the bowl with your broccoli.
In a small bowl, mix together the sriracha, oyster sauce, sugar, fish sauce and dark soy sauce and grate in the garlic.

Heat a small frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the sriracha, oyster sauce, sugar, fish sauce and dark soy sauce, then grate in the garlic clove. Let the sauce reduce for 1-2 mins until sticky, then pour it over the ingredients in the bowl.
Add the chicken, Thai basil and mayo to your eggs and broccoli, along with the sauce. Using a pizza cutter, smash everything together until evenly cut and combined. Serve on the sourdough.

name: Thai Basil Chicken Stir-Fry
description: An easy chicken stir fry recipe inspired by pad krapow gai. It's spicy, speedy, and a friendly introduction to Thai cooking.
instructions: Make sure your rice is ready before you start.

For the prep: Slice the red pepper, onion, chilli and garlic into thin strips. Chop the green beans into 2cm chunks. Pick the thai basil leaves, discarding the stems. Set everything aside. Slice the chicken breast into 1 inch-thick slices, then cut each slice in half. Add to a small bowl with ¼ tsp salt and 1 tsp fish sauce, mix well and set aside.
For the Thai dressing: Finely slice the chilli and garlic and combine with the remaining dressing ingredients in a small bowl. Set aside.
Combine all the sauce ingredients into a small bowl. Set aside. Fry the eggs to your liking, set aside.

Place a large frying pan over high heat with 2tbsp of neutral oil. Once hot, sear the chicken with a pinch of salt on both sides until golden, you don’t need to cook it through at this stage. Once golden, return it back into its bowl (It will be fully cooked later on – this stage is just for flavour and colour.)

Add another drizzle of oil into the empty pan. Once hot, add the chilli, red pepper and onion, cook, stirring until starting to char, 2-3 mins. Now, add the garlic and toss well to coat in the oil, cook until fragrant. Add the green beans with 2 tbsp water and cook for 1 min.

Pour the chicken and all its juices into the pan with the stir-fry sauce and continuously stir-fry until starting to thicken, then remove from the heat. Roughly tear the Thai basil leaves then mix into the pan until wilted. Season with lots of fresh black pepper.
Share the rice between bowls, top with the stir-fry, fried eggs, lime wedges and drizzle over the dressing.

name: Thai Breakfast Porridge
description: Inspired by Jok, this recipe for Thai breakfast porridge isn't dissimilar from a Chinese congee.
instructions: Peel and slice the carrot into 5cm chunks. Slice three pieces of ginger to thickness of a pound and reserve the rest. Chop the spring onions whites, reserving the green tops. Remove and reserve the stems of the shiitake mushrooms.

Put the washed rice, sliced ginger, spring onion whites, carrot chunks, shiitake and the stems, sesame oil, white pepper and a pinch of salt into a medium-sized saucepan. Add the lesser amount of the stock for a thicker consistency or add the full amount for a looser consistency (you can always add more liquid later if you’re not sure). Bring to the boil, add a lid and cook for 15 mins over a low heat, stirring halfway through to check nothing is sticking to the bottom.
Meanwhile, slice one piece of ginger and finely shred. Finely slice the green spring onion tops. Combine the rice sauce ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.

After 15 mins, remove all the aromatics and veggies into a bowl. Use a whisk to vigorously whisk the stock and rice mix for 2 mins, to break up the rice grains. Add the veg back to the pan, plus the cherry tomatoes, and boil with the lid on for 3-5 mins to make creamy. Add more water to make it soupier, if you like – just make sure to bring it to the boil again. Taste and add a little salt if necessary, but remember the rice sauce is also salty.
Serve with ginger shreds, sliced spring onion tops, the rice sauce, crispy shallots and chilli oil.

name: Thai Chicken Noodles
description: Simple, easy and delicious. Healthier than a takeaway, and so easy to do at home.
instructions: Start by making your noodle sauce. Add your Sriracha to a glass along with soy sauce, sugar and water. Mix together with a fork. Set aside.
Crack your eggs into a separate bowl and whisk. Set aside.
Place your rice noodles into a bowl of cold water, making sure they are completely covered. Set aside to soak for 15 mins until they're soft but still have some bite to them.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Thinly slice up your spring onions, chilli and carrots. Set aside.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a wok set over a high heat. Pour in your beaten eggs and allow the eggs to cook whilst stirring and breaking them up with your spoon.
Once the eggs are cooked through, add in the chicken pieces and cook until the meat is white all over. Add your noodle sauce and grate in your garlic cloves.
Drain and add the noodles to the wok and stir everything together. Add the sliced veggies and the beansprouts. Toss everything together and allow it to cook for 5 mins.
Meanwhile, crush up ½ the peanuts and set aside.
Add the remaining whole peanuts to the wok and give everything a good mix.
Time to serve up! Divide the noodles between plates. Finish with a scattering of crushed peanuts and a a squeeze of lime.

name: Thai Coconut Rice Pudding With Sesame Peanut Crunch
description: We love rice pudding and we love Thai coconut rice. This is the best of both worlds. It's salty and sweet and the crunch on top is so addictive.
keywords: Thai Coconut Rice Pudding With Sesame Peanut Crunch
instructions: Peel and slice a finger of fresh ginger, and slice into four rounds of ginger.

Into a medium sized pot, on medium high heat, add the coconut cream (white part on the top of the can) and cook the ginger slices for 2 mins or until lightly fragrant. Add in all the rice and cook for 1 minute or until fragrant, then add all the remaining coconut milk along with the water, sugar, and salt, then mix well. Bring to a boil, add a lid and reduce the heat to the lowest fire. Cook for 20 mins.

In the meantime, add the peanut, desiccated coconut, sesame seeds into a small pan and toast until the coconut is lightly golden, then remove, into a mortar and pestle, or blender. Add sugar and salt and crush well into a coarse crumble.
In a small cup combine the cornstarch slurry.

After 20 mins, remove the lid, and whisk vigorously for 1 minute to release rice starches. Mix the cornstarch slurry well, then pour into the coconut rice pudding, bring to a boil and cook for 1 minute or until creamy and silky. Serve with nutty sesame crumble sprinkled all over.

name: Thai Dumpling Noodle Soup
description: A simple noodle soup recipe to warm your body and soul. The secret ingredient are frozen dumplings. Grab a bag and get going.
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in a bowl of boiling water according to packet instructions, drain then set aside in the bowl.
Finely slice all the coriander stems, reserve the leaves for garnishing. Slice the garlic.

Into a medium-sized saucepan, on medium high heat, add 1 Tbsp of oil and the chicken, searing the chicken skin, until browned, for around 2 mins. Add the coriander stems and garlic, cook for 2 mins or until the garlic is lightly golden. Add stock, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, fish sauce, Chinese five-spice, white pepper, sugar, and bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat to gently simmer for 20 mins. Flip the chicken half way through

In the meantime, bring a medium-sized saucepan of water to a boil, drop in the dumplings for 3 minutes. Divide your cooked noodles between bowls, then use a slotted spoon to portion dumplings on top of each bowl of noodles. Add the bak choy to the water and cook for 1 minute, then add to bowls. Optionally poach an egg in this water too and place into serving bowls.

After 25 mins, remove the chicken, allow to rest for 5 minutes and optionally shred. Bring the soup to a boil then squeeze half a fresh lime, and ladle onto the noodles. Top with chicken, fresh coriander, chilli flakes, crispy shallots, lime, and chilli oil.

name: Thai Fish Sauce Wings
description: Inspired by Smoking Goat in Shoreditch, these crispy chicken wings are truly a work of art. Dressed in a sticky fish sauce glaze, mint and peanuts. Incredible.
instructions: Whisk the fish sauce, sriracha and sugar together in a bowl and grate in your garlic. Add your chicken wings and toss to coat. Marinade for at least an hour, or overnight if you have time.
Pour your cornflour into a bowl. Remove your chicken wings from their marinade and dunk in the cornflour, then leave to sit in a plate.

Heat a generous amount of vegetable oil in a high sided frying pan. Add your wings a few at a time and fry for about 10 minutes, turning so that they cook evenly. They should be deeply golden and crispy when done.
Meanwhile, pour your marinade into a small saucepan along with a small cupful of water and bring to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes until thick and syrupy.
Finely chop your peanuts and mint, then slice your chilli.
Plate up your wings and drizzle your sauce on top. Sprinkle with chopped peanuts, mint and red chilli, then serve.

name: Thai Garlic Prawns With Nam Jim
description: There's nothing better a plate of spicy, garlicky prawns. The homemade nam jim seafood is unreal.
keywords: Thai Garlic Prawns With Nam Jim
Thai Garlic Prawns With Nam Jim recipe
instructions: Devein whole prawns first by piercing the back of the body with a knife and poking in to release and discard the intestinal tract. Then remove just the body shell, leaving the heads on.
Pat dry the prawns very well on kitchen paper, as they need to be dry to cook in the pan. Set aside in the fridge.

Meanwhile, make the seafood sauce. Into a blender add all the ingredients and pulse until you have a green dressing. Do not over blend this, as you want fine even chunks. Pour into a serving bowl and skim off any foam.
Finely slice the garlic cloves for the prawns, if you have a mandoline this will speed up the process.

Now, cook the prawns. Pour a splash of olive oil into a large frying pan set over a high heat, with a pinch of salt into the oil, then add the prawns and cook for 2 min on each side, allowing the prawns to sear without any interference. Now remove the charred prawns onto a plate (they will get cooked again). Now add all the garlic and a glug of olive oil and tilt the pan, allowing all the garlic to sizzle in the pool of oil for 2 mins or until lightly golden, then return the prawns with a Tbsp of oyster sauce and toss everything together. Turn the heat off and serve into a large plate with all the juices and garlic pieces.
Garnish the prawns with some coriander leaves, cucumbers and the nam jim seafood dipping sauce.

name: Thai Glass Noodle Salad With Prawn & Pork
