description: This glass noodle salad is inspired by 'yum woon sen' – a classic Thai salad that's a staple in Thai cuisine. It's fresh, it's spicy, it's exactly what you want for dinner tonight.
instructions: Soak the noodles in a bowl of hot water until just loosened, then drain. Set aside.
Fill a medium pot halfway with water and bring to the boil.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Using a pestle and mortar, pound the garlic, chillies and whole coriander stems together, or mince by hand. Add the sugar, lime juice, fish sauce and sriracha, then mix well and set aside.
Finely dice the celery, half the cherry tomatoes and finely slice the onions. Transfer it all to a large mixing bowl. Crush the roasted peanuts and add half to the bowl.

Add the noodles to the boiling water for 2 mins, then use tongs to remove back into the same bowl. Cut four large snips in the noodles and set aside. Cook the prawns for 30 seconds in the same water until opaque, then remove to the salad bowl. Now pour out most of the water, leaving just enough to just coat the base of the pot. Add the pork mince with a pinch of salt and 1 tsp fish sauce, then use a spatula to break up the pork. Simmer for 2 mins, or until cooked.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer the pork into the salad along with a spoonful of the pork stock. Tip the hot noodles and all the dressing into the salad bowl, then toss well.
Serve immediately with the remaining peanuts, crispy shallots, sliced cucumber and some lettuce cups.

name: Thai Green Chicken Curry
description: A Thai green curry is hard to beat. This one is spicy, aromatic and coconutty, and quick and easy enough to make for dinner tonight. Perfect served over fluffy jasmine rice.
instructions: Bash the lemongrass and remove the bottom stems and outer husks. Cook the rice following packet instructions, and add the lemongrass stems and husks to the pot as it cooks.
Mince the remaining lemongrass. Slice each shallot into quarters. Cut the aubergines into 1cm coins, then into half moons.
Heat a large dry pan over a high heat. Add the aubergines and char for 2 mins on each side until lightly blackened. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside to continue cooking in their own heat.

Stir the can of coconut milk to distribute the fat. Add ½ the coconut milk to a blender with the Thai Basil leaves and turmeric. Blitz just until smooth and vibrant. Don't over-blend or the vibrant green will turn dull. Set aside to let the flavours infuse.
Slice the boneless chicken thighs into 1 inch strips. Cut the tofu into bite-sized pieces. Drain and rinse the bamboo shoots.
Heat a large pan over a medium-high heat. Add the remaining coconut milk and cook for 2 mins or until the thinner liquid has evaporated and you have a thicker creamy consistency.
Stir in the curry paste and minced lemongrass and cook off for about 5 mins, until the curry paste has darkened slightly and developed an oily sheen. Make sure not to burn it.
Add the chicken. Mix well to coat the meat in the mixture then cook for a couple of minutes until the chicken is lightly golden.

Pour in the chicken stock, blended coconut milk mixture, fish sauce and palm sugar and bring to a simmer. Add the charred aubergine, baby corn, tofu, shallots and bamboo shoots and bring back to a simmer. Tear the lime leaves in your hand to release their aroma and add to the pot. Reduce the heat to low-medium, pop a lid on and cook at a gentle simmer for 15 mins.
Meanwhile, pick the coriander leaves, cut the lime into wedges and thinly slice the red chilli for garnish.
When the cooking time for the curry is up, turn the heat off and leave it to rest for 5 mins. Taste and season with salt, some lime juice and a little more fish sauce if needed.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls and ladle over the curry. Serve with the coriander, lime wedges, fresh chilli and some crispy shallots, if you like.

name: Thai Green Chicken Traybake
description:
This traybake curry method is going to change your life. The green curry paste is quick to throw together,
and goes perfectly with the crispy chicken legs.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Roughly chop the shallots, lemongrass, chillies, garlic, ginger and half the coriander (stalks and all), then add everything to a food processor along with the grated zest of 1 of the limes and the coconut oil. Blitz to a rough purée. Set this curry paste aside.

Place a large roasting tray over a medium heat on the hob. Add the chicken legs to the tray, skin-side down, and cook for 5 mins until they are deeply crispy and the fat has rendered out. Remove from the tray and set aside.

Add the green curry paste to the tray and cook for 3 mins until fragrant. Tip in the coconut milk and chicken stock, then bring to a simmer. Return the chicken legs to the pan, then pop in the oven for 40 mins.

After 40 mins, remove the tray from the oven and stir in the cooked brown rice and veg, then return to the oven for another 5 mins. Meanwhile, cut both limes into wedges, thinly slice the red chilli and roughly chop the rest of the coriander (stalks and all).
Add the brown sugar and fish sauce to the curry and stir to combine, then season to taste with salt. Scatter over the coriander and red chillies, and squeeze over your lime juice. Serve and enjoy.

name: Thai Green Chilli Paneer
description: A punchy, green curry with a creamy sauce and golden seared paneer. This one's perfect when you fancy some frsh but still comforting, plus the flavours only get better the next day.
instructions: First, get your rice on to cook according to the packet instructions.
Add the yoghurt to a large bowl and grate in the ginger and garlic. Add the ground cumin, season with salt and mix until combined. Cut the paneer into pieces, toss to coat and set aside.

Now, make the sauce. Quarter the onion and add to a blender with the remaining yoghurt, garlic, ginger, green chillies, ground coriander and garam masala. Add a splash of water (about 15ml) and blend until smooth.

Heat 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the marinated paneer in a single layer and fry for 2-3 mins until golden brown. Flip and fry for another 2-3 mins on the other side. Paneer can be prone to sticking depending on your pan, so fry it carefully and use a flat spatula to loosen it if needed. Remove the paneer and wipe any burnt bits from the pan.

Add the remaining tbsp of vegetable oil to the pan and pour in the sauce. Cook over a medium heat for 5-6 mins, until the sauce has thickened and mellowed. Pour in the remaining water to loosen to a saucy but not watery consistency, then add the paneer back in. Cook for a further 2 mins until the paneer is heated through.
To serve, spoon the paneer and sauce over the rice. Finish with a few fresh coriander leaves and a squeeze of lemon juice, then serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

name: Thai Green Cod Traybake Curry
description: A vibrant Thai green coconut sauce poured straight over cod, rice and veg - all baked in one tray. Finished with a quick lime-pickled chilli and onion, it's a proper weeknight winner.
keywords: Thai Green Cod Traybake Curry recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Tip the coconut milk into a blender along with the green curry paste, most of the coriander (reserving some leaves to serve), the zest and juice of half the limes and the fish sauce. Blitz until smooth and bright green.
Cut the pak choi into quarters lengthways. Tip the rice into a large roasting tin, nestle in the pak choi and sugar snap peas. Lay the cod fillets on top, then pour over the green sauce.
Transfer to the oven and cook for 20 mins, until bubbling and the cod is cooked through.
Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion and red chilli and tip into a bowl. Squeeze over the juice of the remaining lime, scrunch slightly and leave to pickle.
Spoon the fish, rice and veg into shallow bowls. Scatter over the reserved coriander leaves and serve with the pickled onion and chilli.

name: Thai Green Curry Brothy Rice with Crispy Tofu
description: We’ve served this spicy aromatic Thai green curry soup with fluffy rice and crispy fried soy tofu. It’s fresh and vibrant and packs in extra plant protein from the tofu.
keywords: Thai Green Curry Brothy Rice with Crispy Tofu
Thai Green Curry Brothy Rice with Crispy Tofu recipe
instructions: Cook the rice following packet instructions. Finely slice the red chilli and the spring onion, separating the onion whites and greens.
To a blender, add ½ the spinach, the coriander, coconut milk, soy sauce, stock cube, agave (if using) and vegan fish sauce (if using). Blitz until smooth.

Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large pan set over a low heat. Add the curry paste and spring onion whites and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 mins until fragrant. Add the water, remaining spinach and the blended green sauce to the pan. Leave to gently come to a simmer. Season with lime juice to taste.

Meanwhile, slice the baby corn into bite-sized chunks. Heat a drizzle of vegetable oil in a new large pan set over a high heat. Add the baby corn with a pinch of salt and fry for 2 mins, then add the mangetout and cook for another 3 mins until softened and starting to brown.

Remove the veg from the pan then crumble in the tofu. Add another splash of vegetable oil and cook the tofu over a high heat for 3-4 mins, then add the soy sauce and sesame seeds and cook for another 3 mins until really crisped up.

To serve, divide the rice between bowls, pour over the green sauce and top with the charred veggies and crispy tofu. Finish with the sliced chilli, spring onion greens and a wedge of lime, if you like.

name: Thai Green Turkey Kebab Bowl
description: Herby turkey mince packed with Thai green curry paste, grilled until golden and charred, then piled over silky rice noodles with cool cucumber and a glossy, nutty peanut and lime dressing. Think satay meets kebab, fresh, punchy and absolutely hits the spot.
keywords: Thai green turkey kebab bowl recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Zest and then juice the limes - you'll use the zest for kebabs and juice for the dressing. Finely chop the coriander and spring onions, then peel and grate the garlic
Tip the turkey mince into a large bowl and add the grated garlic, lime zest, Thai green curry paste, chopped coriander and spring onions. Season with salt and black pepper and mix well to combine.

Transfer the mixture to a baking tray (24x32cm) and press down into an even layer. Score into six strips, this makes it easier to portion later. Drizzle with the olive oil and cook in the oven for 15 mins. Remove from the oven and drain off any excess liquid. Crank the grill to high and slide the tray back under for 3-5 mins, until the top is charred and golden.

Meanwhile, in a bowl add the reserved lime juice, peanut butter, soy sauce and honey. Loosen with a splash of water, a little at a time, until the dressing reaches the consistency of double cream. Cut the cucumber into thin matchsticks.
Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions. Pick the mint leaves.
To serve, divide the noodles between bowls and top with the cucumber. Slice up the kebabs and lay them over the top. Drizzle over the dressing and scatter with the mint leaves and sesame seeds.

name: Thai Grilled Chicken Thighs With Roasted Rice Dipping Sauce
description: We've paired up juicy chicken thighs with Thai roasted rice sauce inspired by nam jim jaew. It's fresh, funky, and just what you're craving right now.
keywords: Soy Grilled Chicken Thighs With Roasted Rice Dipping Sauce
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Slot the wire rack into the top shelf. Combine the marinade ingredients in a small bowl. Arrange the chicken thighs on a baking tray, then pour over the marinade. Set aside.

Slice the red peppers into matchsticks, then add to the baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Coat the red pepper sticks well, then scatter all around the chicken thighs. Roast in the oven for 35-40 mins or until charred and golden.

For the coconut rice, wash the rice in a sieve until the water is running clear. Drain well. Tip the washed rice into a medium-sized pot along with the water, sugar, turmeric, salt and coconut milk. Mix well.

Bring the rice to the boil, then immediately add a lid and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 20 mins. Once cooked, fluff the rice with chopsticks or a wooden paddle, then return the lid to the pan for at least 10 mins to increase the fluffy texture. Keep the lid on until serving.

Meanwhile, for the roasted rice sauce, set a small pan over a medium-high heat, add the raw jasmine rice and toast for 3 mins, tossing all the time until lightly golden and the smell of popcorn fills the kitchen. Don’t let it burn – keep your eye on it. Transfer to a small bowl and grind or blend the roasted rice into a powder using a pestle and mortar or blender.
Finely slice the shallot and coriander stems. Combine the toasted rice powder, fish sauce, lime zest and juice (about 5 tbsp), brown sugar, chilli flakes, shallot and coriander stems. Set aside.

Slice the cucumber on the diagonal. Remove the chicken from the oven, fluff the rice and sprinkle the crispy fried onion all over. Serve with the cucumber, coriander leaves and the rice sauce poured over the chicken (reserve some for the side).

name: Thai Omelette Bowl
description: There is no better meal than a fried egg on fresh, fluffy jasmine rice. We've taken that concept and levelled it up by topping it with a tasty Thai omelette.
instructions: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear. Add it to a small saucepan along with 375ml of water. Bring to the boil, then cover with a lid, turn the heat down to low and simmer for 12 mins. Remove from the heat and let it sit, covered until ready to serve.

In the meantime, get all your prep done: peel, halve and thinly slice the shallot. Trim and thinly slice the spring onion and pick the mint leaves. Trim the sugar snap peas and thinly slice. Add all into a bowl of ice water.
Into a large bowl, add the chilli jam, the juice of 1 lime and half the soy sauce. Mix together – this is the dressing. Taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Crack the eggs into a medium bowl. Add the cornflour, half the soy sauce and 1 tbsp of lime juice. Whisk together until frothy, and no cornflour lumps are left.

In a large frying pan and place on high heat. Fill with 2cm worth of oil. Once hot, pour ¼ of the egg mixture into the hot oil, it should puff, cook it undisturbed for 30 secs, then flip the omelette. Cook for another 20 secs and transfer to a wire rack or a plate lined with kitchen paper. Continue doing this until you have 4 omelettes.
Chop the omelettes into 2cm strips, thoroughly drain the shallot mixture and add both to the dressing with the toasted sesame seeds. Toss together until evenly coated.
Share the rice between bowls and top with the Thai omelette mixture.

name: Thai Prawn Mango Som Tam Salad
description: A fiercely delicious salad that's not afraid to hit you with some big flavours. It's sharp, spicy, and incredibly addictively.
keywords: Thai Prawn Mango Som Tum Salad
Thai Prawn Mango Som Tum Salad recipe
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil, then add the prawns, cover with a lid and turn off the heat. Leave for 5 minutes, then strain and set aside.

To make the dressing, roughly chop the garlic cloves and chillies, add to a small bowl with brown sugar, fish sauce and lime juice (this entire process can be done in a pestle and mortar if you have one) then set aside.

Now roughly chop the coriander and finely slice the shallots. Peel the mango and slice it into large, ½ thick cm discs on either side of the seed then slice into thin matchsticks. Peel and cut the carrots into matchsticks or use a peeler to make ribbons. Half the cherry tomatoes and then lightly crush the roasted peanuts. Place everything into a large bowl with the cooked prawns.

Pour the dressing only when you are ready to serve, or the salad will wilt. Toss everything together with a sprinkle of salt and serve immediately. Finish with a pile of crispy shallots and serve with lime wedges.

name: Thai Red Chicken Meatball Curry
description: Got leftovers from our Thai Red Chicken Meatballs with Peanut Sauce? Use them to make this very simple, very delicious curry. She's a winner.
keywords: thai chicken meatballs with peanut sauce
ingredients: 1 Third of the Thai Red Chicken Meatballs with Peanut Sauce Base
instructions: Grab your batch-cooked leftovers from the Thai Red Chicken Meatballs with Peanut Sauce: the meatballs, peanut sauce, green beans and rice.

Heat a large deep pan over a medium heat and add a glug of oil. Add the curry paste and fry it off for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Tip in the coconut milk and add the meatballs. Bring to a simmer then stir through the peanut sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning with fish sauce. Finely chop the spring onions and pick the basil and coriander leaves.
Warm up the rice and green beans until piping hot (you can do this in a pan with a little splash or water or in a microwave).
Heat a shot of oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the meatballs for 10-15 mins until golden all over and cooked through. Set aside.

To serve, divide the rice and beans between plates then top with the meatball curry. Divide your lime into wedges and add to the plates, before scattering over the fresh herbs, sesame seeds and chopped spring onions

name: Thai Red Chicken Meatballs with Peanut Sauce
description: This dinner is perfect for batch cooking so make extra and serve it in different ways throughout the week. It's savoury, spicy and jam-packed with veg. And it's rustled up in just 35 minutes.
keywords: thai chicken meatballs with peanut sauce
instructions: Add a shot of oil to a small frying pan, then add the curry paste and fry for 3 mins. Set aside.

Finely chop the coriander stalks and transfer to a large bowl. Add the chicken mince and half of the fish sauce, then grate in the zest of 1/2 the lime. Add the fried curry paste, eggs, breadcrumbs and seasoning. Mix together really well until it becomes sticky. Form into 12 balls with wet hands, around 60g-70g each.
Heat a shot of oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the meatballs for 10-15 mins until golden all over and cooked through.

For the sauce, get the coconut milk into a saucepan with the peanut butter and the remaining fish sauce. Melt and bring to a simmer, then season with salt and the juice of the remaining lime. Add the sugar, if necessary, to balance the flavour.
Trim and halve the green beans, finely chop the spring onions and pick the coriander leaves.
Cook the rice following pack instructions, then add the green beans 5 mins before the end of cooking time.

If batch cooking for the week, serve up a third of this meal for dinner then store the rest in containers (keep the meatballs, rice/beans, peanut sauce and spring onions separate). Use the leftovers to make our Thai Red Meatball Curry and Thai Red Fried Meatball Fried Rice with Crispy Egg.
Serve the rice and meatballs drizzled with peanut sauce. Top with spring onions and coriander, with a lime wedge on the side.

name: Thai Red Chicken One-Pot Rice
description: Another one-pot wonder to add to your weekly meal plan. Forget boring plain chicken and rice, this Thai red curry-inspired pot rice is full of flavour and free of fuss.
instructions: Dice the chicken into 2-3cm chunks.

Heat a splash of chilli-infused olive oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the diced chicken and the ground cumin. Stir to coat and cook for around 7 mins or until just cooked through then remove from the pan and set aside.
Meanwhile, slice the onion and pepper into chunks and mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat another glug of chilli-infused olive oil in the pan and add the onion, pepper, garlic and ginger. Cook for about 5 mins until fragrant and slightly softened.
Meanwhile, rinse the uncooked rice.

Tip the chicken back into the pan then add the Thai red curry paste, soy sauce, chicken stock, fish sauce and sugar. Stir and bring to the boil. Give it a taste and add extra curry paste if needed. then tip in the rice. Reduce the heat to low then stir, cover and simmer for 10 mins.
Pour in the coconut milk then cover and simmer for another 10 mins or until the rice is cooked and has absorbed almost all of the liquid.⁣⁣⁣ Add an extra splash of water if necessary.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the red chilli, roughly chop the coriander and cut the lime into wedges for garnish.
Divide the rice between bowls and scatter over the chilli and coriander. Serve with prawn crackers.

name: Thai Red Cod & Chickpea Curry
description: A quick and easy recipe for Thai spiced coconut chickpeas, topped with tender grilled cod and on the table in just 30 minutes.
keywords: thai red cod and chickpea curry
instructions: Season the cod generously with salt and pepper and leave in the fridge for 15 mins. Meanwhile, slice ½ of the lime and slice the pak choi. Peel the garlic and ginger.
Heat the grill to high. Drizzle the cod with oil and pop under the grill for 8 mins until cooked through. Set aside.

Meanwhile, blitz the thai red curry paste, garlic, ginger and ½ the coconut milk in a blender. Heat a large pan over a medium heat and pour in the blended mixture along with the drained chickpeas and the rest of the coconut milk. Season with the fish sauce and simmer for 10 mins. Add the edamame and leave to simmer for 1 min, then add the pak choi and stir until it starts to wilt.
Squeeze in the juice of ½ the limes. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, if needed.
Plate up the chickpea curry and top with the cod. Garnish with coriander, a wedge of lime and some sliced spring onions if using.

name: Thai Red Curry Lentils
description: Making a dal or stewy lentil dish is something you should do weekly. It's cheap, quick, low effort and great for stretching over a few meals.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Peel and dice the sweet potato into 2cm pieces, then put on a baking tray and drizzle with half the oil, salt and pepper. Pop into the oven for 20 mins.
Peel and finely chop the onion, then peel and chop the ginger and garlic. Remove the outer layers of the lemongrass, bash with the back of a knife and chop into two pieces.

Heat the remaining oil in a large pot over a medium heat and add the onion, garlic, ginger and lemongrass. Cook for 5-10 mins until soft and slightly golden. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds, then add the curry paste and cook for 2-3 mins until fragrant.

Add the coconut milk and stock. Rinse the lentils, then add them too and stir well. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 mins. Once the dal is cooked, add back in the cooked sweet potato and squeeze in the juice of the limes to taste.
To serve, divide between bowls and enjoy. Optional: if batch-cooking these lentils for the week, portion out into Tupperware containers and keep in the fridge.

name: Thai Red Curry Lentils with Glazed Roasted Carrots
description: Our Thai Red Curry Lentils batch topped with sticky-sweet carrots and a dollop of yoghurt. Parathas on the side is non-negotiable.
instructions: Make the Thai Red Curry Lentils batch recipe.

Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Halve the carrots and quarter any thick ones. Spread onto a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, season well, and roast for 20-25 mins, until tender. Then, drizzle the honey over the carrots, toss to coat, then return to the oven for 5 mins until caramelised and sticky.
Meanwhile, warm the Thai red curry lentils in a saucepan over a medium heat, stirring occasionally until hot. Loosen with a splash of water if needed.
Heat the parathas in a dry pan or according to pack instructions until pliable. Pick the coriander leaves, thinly slice the chilli.
Spoon the lentils into bowls, swirl in some yoghurt, and top with the glazed carrots. Finish with a scattering of coriander and chilli. Serve with hot paratha for scooping.

name: Thai Red Curry Salmon with Lime & Coconut Rice
description: Sticky Thai red curry-glazed salmon with fluffy coconut-lime rice and green beans. Light, punchy and perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Zest both limes onto a small plate and set aside.
In a bowl, mix the Thai red curry paste, honey and the juice of half the limes with the water. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

Wash the rice thoroughly in cold water, then drain really well. Tip into a small saucepan and pour in the coconut milk. Add the lime zest and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover with a lid and cook for 5 mins. Lay the trimmed green beans on top, cover again and cook for another 5 mins. Turn off the heat and let everything steam for a few more minutes with the lid on.
Cut the salmon into chunky, bite-sized pieces and season with salt.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the salmon pieces and fry for 2-3 mins, turning occasionally, until golden all over. Turn the heat to low and pour in the curry dressing. Let it bubble away until thickened and sticky, coating the salmon.

Fluff the coconut and lime rice with a fork and divide between bowls or containers. Taste and season with salt and more lime juice if needed. Add the green beans, top with the sticky salmon bites and scatter over the coriander. Serve with lime wedges on the side from the remaining lime.

name: Thai Red Duck Curry with Pineapple
description: This curry is fragrant, fruity and a little spicy, inspired by a dish from London’s hottest Thai restaurant, Singburi. A perfect date night meal.
instructions: Halve the tomatoes and grapes. Cut the pineapple into bite-sized chunks.
Using a sharp knife, score the skin of the duck breast with diagonal lines then rub it with sea salt flakes.

Place the duck skin side down in a cold non-stick pan set over a medium heat. Cook it for 6 mins then drain the fat that’s been released, flip the breast over and fry the other side for 4 mins. Sear the other edges of the breast for about a minute each until sealed. When it’s done, it will feel soft but spring back slightly when pressed. Transfer the duck to a plate and set aside to rest. If you prefer your duck less pink, continue cooking it for longer in the pan or finish it off in an oven at 180°C for 5 mins.

While the duck cooks, wash your rice three times until the water runs clear. Drain, then transfer to a large saucepan and add water until it reaches just below your first knuckle. Bring to the boil over a medium-high heat, then turn the heat to low and cover with a lid for 12 mins.
For the curry, heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a wok set over a medium heat. Add the curry paste and fry it off for 2 mins; if it’s too dry, add a tbsp or two of water.

Add a ladle of the coconut milk and mix well to combine, then add the remaining coconut milk. Bring to a boil then add fish sauce, lime leaves and palm sugar. If your palm sugar is in large pieces, bash it in a pestle and mortar first.
Turn the heat down to low-medium and add the tomatoes, pineapple and grapes. Bring to a gentle bubble and leave to simmer for 10 mins, then stir through the Thai basil and remove from the heat.
Slice the duck into 1cm thick pieces and set aside.
Divide the rice between bowls, ladle over the curry and top with the duck.

name: Thai Red Lentil Curry with Lime Pickled Onions
description: Homemade pickled onions are the perfect partner for a rich vegetarian lentil base in this easy dinner. Perfect for batch cooking.
keywords: Thai Red Lentil Curry with Lime Pickled Onions
Thai Red Lentil Curry with Lime Pickled Onions
instructions: Make the Thai Red Curry Lentils batch recipe.
Reheat the Thai Red Curry Lentils in a saucepan over a medium heat. Stirring occasionally.

For the lime pickled onions, finely slicing the red onion and adding to a bowl along with the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Give it a bit of a scrunch with your hands. Finely slice the chilli and add that to the quick pickle, too.
Cook the rice according to package instructions.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls then spoon over the lentils. Scatter over the quick pickles and fresh coriander.

name: Thai Red Lentils With Fudgy Eggs & Sesame
description: We'd highly recommend eating your lentils with just-boiled eggs and a sprinkling of sesame seeds.
keywords: Thai Red Lentils With Fudgy Eggs & Sesame
Thai Red Lentils With Fudgy Eggs & Sesame recipe
instructions: Make the Thai Red Curry Lentils batch recipe.
Reheat the Thai Red Curry Lentils in a saucepan over a medium heat. Stirring occasionally.

Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the eggs and reduce the heat so the water is simmering. Cook the eggs for 7 mins, then drain and run under cold water until cool enough to handle. Peel the eggs and cut them in half.
To serve, spoon the lentils into bowls. Top with egg, a drizzle of yoghurt, some torn Thai basil and a sprinkling of sesame seeds.

name: Thai Red Lentils with Sweet Chilli Halloumi
description: Everything's better with a bit of halloumi. Including leftovers from our Thai Red Curry Lentils batch recipe. An easy, filling weeknight dinner.
keywords: Thai Red Lentils with Sweet Chilli Halloumi
Thai Red Lentils with Sweet Chilli Halloumi recipe
instructions: Make the Thai Red Curry Lentils batch recipe.
Reheat the Thai Red Curry Lentils in a saucepan over a medium heat. Stirring occasionally.

While the lentils are warming, prep your sides by finely shredding the cabbage and roughly chopping the coriander. Add to a bowl and squeeze in the lime, seasoning with salt. Give it a bit of a scrunch with your hands and set aside.

Crumble the halloumi into nice chunks whilst heating a dry frying pan over a medium heat. Add the halloumi to the pan and fry until nicely golden on each side. Take off the heat and add the sweet chilli sauce, giving it a good mix. Heat the flatbreads.
Serve the lentils in a bowl with the slaw and top with the sweet chilli halloumi. Load up onto the golden flatbreads and get stuck in.

name: Thai Red Meatball Fried Rice with Crispy Egg
description: Got leftovers from our Thai Red Chicken Meatballs with Peanut Sauce? Use them to make this gorgeous fried rice with runny fried egg. Yes please.
keywords: thai chicken meatballs with peanut sauce
ingredients: 1 Third of the Thai Red Chicken Meatballs with Peanut Sauce Base
instructions: Grab your batch-cooked leftovers from the Thai Red Chicken Meatballs with Peanut Sauce: the meatballs, peanut sauce, green beans and rice.
Cut the meatballs into bite-sized pieces. Heat a glug of oil in a pan over medium heat then add the meatballs, cooking until crisp and piping hot. Pick the herb leaves.
Add the rice to the pan with the meatballs and cook until it's piping hot and starting to catch on the pan. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat another glug of oil in a small pan over a medium high heat and crack in the eggs, basting with the oil until the whites are set and the yolk runny or cooked to your liking.
Toss the herbs through the meatball rice, then plate up. Drizzle with the peanut sauce and scatter with spring onions. Drizzle with sriracha if using.

name: Thai Red Spaghetti
description: Thai red curry paste is the secret ingredient in this quick and simple pasta recipe. Weeknight dinner, sorted.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put a pan of salted water over a high heat to bring the boil. Tip the cherry tomatoes into a roasting tin, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and slide into the oven for 15-20 mins, until soft and charring.

Add spaghetti to the boiling pan. Peel and slice the garlic. In a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add a tbsp of olive oil along with the garlic, sizzle for a minute then add the curry paste and sizzle for a minute longer.
Tip the roasted tomatoes into the pan, then use tongs to transfer the pasta into the pan. Add ½ the lime juice and toss well. Season to taste with sugar, fish sauce and salt.
Twirl into bowls and top with coriander and toasted sesame seeds. Serve with the remaining lime half, sliced into wedges, to squeeze over.

name: Thai Roast Chicken Salad with Lemongrass Dressing
description: Zingy, herby and full of crunch. This salads takes a simple roast chicken to the next level by turning it into this delicious salad, tossed with beansprouts, sugar snap peas and a zesty lemongrass dressing.
keywords: Thai shredded chicken salad with lemongrass dressing
Thai shredded chicken salad with lemongrass dressing recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Take the chicken out of the fridge about 30 mins before roasting – it cooks more evenly that way. If you're super short on time you can always use a Rotisserie chicken instead

Slice the lemon in half. Crush the garlic cloves with the flat side of a knife, leaving the skins on. Stuff the chicken cavity with the lemon halves, garlic and thyme. Drizzle the chicken all over with olive oil. Get stuck in and rub it in properly. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Pop the chicken breast-side up in a roasting tray. Roast for about 50 mins–1 hr, or until the juices run clear when you pierce the thickest part of the thigh.For this recipe used a 1.6kg-2kg chicken, adjust the timings for a smaller or larger bird.

While the chicken is cooking make the dressing. Finely grate the ginger, lemongrass and garlic into a small bowl. Zest one of the limes into the bowl and set aside for later. Then squeeze in the juice of all three limes, add the fish sauce and whisk together. Finely slice the chillies and stir through. Taste and adjust with more lime juice or fish sauce as needed.
Once the chicken has rested carefully shred the meat ready to add to your salad.

Julienne or coarsely grate the carrot. Finely slice the sugar snap peas on an angle. Add both to a large bowl along with the beansprouts, cooled jasmine rice and shredded chicken. Pick the mint, coriander and Thai basil leaves and add to the bowl.

Pour over the dressing and toss everything together until well coated. Pile onto a large platter or divide between bowls, scatter over the roasted peanuts, and the lime zest and serve immediately. If you want it for lunch the next day, hold back the dressing and add it when you're ready to eat.

name: Thai Salmon Laab Salad Bowl
description: A tangy Thai-inspired salmon bowl that's got all the punchy flavours of a laab.
keywords: Thai Salmon Laab Salad Bowl recipe
instructions: Sprinkle the salmon with salt and maple syrup or sugar, then set aside on a plate in the fridge, uncovered.

If you don’t have roasted peanuts, make your own. Start by heating the oven to 160°C. Tip the peanuts onto a baking tray and roast for 15-20 mins, or until lightly golden, then remove and set aside. Don’t roast them too brown, as they will get a tiny bit more brown once out of the oven.

For the optional rice powder, add the rice to a small pan over a medium-high heat and stir the rice constantly until the grains begin to pop, smell like popcorn and are golden brown. Transfer to a pestle and mortar, blender or coffee grinder and pound/blitz into a coarse fine powder with a pinch of salt. It should look like sand. Set aside.

For the dressing, remove the lemongrass husk and finely dice the stalk. Crush the garlic, finely dice the chillies and finely dice the makrut lime leaf, if using. Juice the limes. Add everything to a small bowl along with the remaining dressing ingredients. Mix well, then set aside in a small bowl.

Meanwhile, set a saucepan of water over a medium heat. Once boiling add your eggs. Cook for 5 minutes (you may need a minute more or less depending on your egg size). Remove from the pan and remove the shell. Set aside for later.
Pat the salmon dry with kitchen paper to remove any excess moisture. Add 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt to a medium frying pan set over a high heat, then swirl the oil all over the base of the pan.

Now add the salmon fillets skin-side down and turn the heat to medium. Place a small lid directly on top of the salmon, so it’s gently pressing the fillet. Cook for just 2 mins each side, then transfer to a plate to rest.

Meanwhile, for the salad, finely slice the red onion, spring onion, coriander and halve the cherry tomatoes, then transfer everything to a large mixing bowl. Lightly crush the roasted peanuts and add most of them, too.

Remove the salmon skin, chop it up and add to the salad bowl, if you like (or just discard the skin). Use your hands to gently flake the salmon into juicy, chunky pieces on top of the salad. Add half the dressing and gently toss.

Slice the cucumber and separate the lettuce into leaves. To serve, divide the cucumber and lettuce cups between plates, placing them at the edges. Add the rice, salmon salad and boiled eggs on top. Garnish all over with toasted rice powder, roasted peanuts, crispy shallots and a lime wedge each. To finish, pour the remaining dressing over the salmon.

name: Thai Sausage Breakfast Sandwich
description: This might be the breakfast sandwich to end all breakfast sandwiches. Have a go at this one and you'll be set up for the day to come. Enjoy.
instructions: For the quick pickle, finely slice the shallot into rings (use your thumb to reveal the rings), then place them into a small bowl. Peel and finely slice the garlic, then slice the chilli and strip the leaves of coriander, setting aside for later, then chop up the stalks.
Put a third of the coriander stems into a bowl (reserve the rest for the patty), add all the remaining pickle ingredients and set aside.
Squeeze the sausage meat from the casings into a medium-sized bowl and add all the remaining patty ingredients. Mix well with clean hands or a fork. Divide into two balls and leave in the fridge.

For the Thai omelette, whisk the cornflower with some cold water in a small bowl (at a ratio of 2:1 water to cornflour). Add the eggs and fish sauce and whisk to combine. Bring a medium-sized pan to high heat and add a glug of oil. When the oil is hot add the egg mixture, leaving it for a few seconds to puff up. Then take the pan off heat and drag the egg mixture from the edges to the centre to create large wavy folds whilst tilting the pan to fill any gaps with raw egg. When the egg has mostly set and looks silky, turn the heat off and roughly fold it into 2 pieces roughly the size of the bun. Set the eggs aside on a plate.

Cook the Thai sausage patties in the same pan, add a splash of oil and set the heat to low heat. Flatten the sausage patties into circles around 3 cm-thick (no wider than the bun, though they will shrink slightly). Add the patties to the pan, add a lid and cook for 5 mins, this is the secret to juicy patties. Remove the lid and don’t be alarmed by the lack of colour on the patties, flip the patties, turn the heat to medium and cook for 2-3 mins without a lid or until nicely caramelised.

Remove the sausage patties to a plate to catch any excess juices. Place the pan back on medium heat, and add the buns to the pan, mayo-side down. Press down evenly with your hands and toast until lightly golden brown. Swirl the buns around the pan to soak up all the delicious juices.

To assemble, spread half of the kewpie mayo over the bottom bun, then top with a handful of coriander leaves, one sausage patty, egg, a spoonful of pickles, then the rest of the kewpie mayo on the toasted side of the top bun.
Enjoy sliced in half, with more pickles on the side.

name: Thai Soy Braised Pork Belly
description: This Kai Palo, or Thai pork belly and egg stew, is seriously addictive. Think slow-cooked tender pork belly, aromatic spices, soft-boiled eggs and an umami broth.
keywords: Thai Soy Braised Pork Belly Recipe
instructions: Heat a small dry pan over a medium heat. Add the spices and toast for about 1 min or until fragrant.
Smash the garlic cloves and slice the shallots. Cut the pork belly into large 5cm chunks. Separate the coriander leaves from the stems.
Heat a glug of sesame oil in a large wok or wide-rimmed pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and shallots and cook for 5 mins until lightly golden then remove from the pan and reserve for later.

Return the pan, with the aromatic oil, to a medium-high heat. Working in batches to avoid overcrowding the pan, add the pork belly and sear for a minute or so on each side until golden, just like you would pancetta (a lot of pork fat should render out for delicious flavour). Remove to a bowl and set aside.

Keep the pan with the pork fat on the hob and reduce the heat to low-medium. Add the sugar, using a spatula to gently stir as it melts. Allow it to darken slightly before carefully adding all the hot water (it will splatter!). The sugar will harden but will naturally melt again as the stock simmers. Gently mix to remove it from the base of the pan then add the chicken powder, soy sauce, golden mountain sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, salt and all spices.

Allow the sugar to fully melt and then return the pork belly, garlic and shallots to the pan, along with the coriander stems. Bring to a very gentle simmer, add a lid and cook on the lowest heat for 2 hours.

When the pork has 15 mins left of cooking time, cook the eggs in boiling water for 6 mins. Plunge in cold water then peel (be careful as the yolks will be very soft). Cut the firm tofu into bite-size squares and halve the tofu puffs. Set everything aside into a bowl.
When the pork cooking time is up, add the peeled eggs, tofu and tofu puffs. Turn the heat off for at least 30 mins or as long as overnight.
Before serving, return the pan to the heat and simmer for 5 mins to gently reheat. Serve with cooked rice and steamed greens, if you like.

name: Thai Steak Salad Lettuce Cups
description: A twist on classic laab - seared steak, zesty lime dressing, nutty toasted rice powder and heaps of herbs, in ready to scoop into crisp lettuce cups. Yum.
instructions: Toast the jasmine rice in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 4–5 mins until golden and nutty-smelling. Tip into a pestle and mortar, grind to a coarse powder, and set aside.

Peel and finely slice the shallots. Finely slice the coriander stems. Pick the mint, coriander and Thai basil leaves. Cut the cucumber into thin slices and set aside. Zest half the limes, then squeeze the juice of all of the limes into a bowl.

In a mixing bowl, whisk together the fish sauce, sugar, lime zest, lime juice, coriander stems, chilli powder and a spoonful of the toasted rice powder. Taste and adjust until it’s punchy and balanced.

Season the steak (we used rump but any kind works a treat!). Heat a frying pan with a splash of olive oil until very hot, then sear the steak for 2–3 mins on each side, or until cooked to your liking. Rest for 5 mins, then thinly slice against the grain.
In a large bowl, toss the sliced steak with the dressing, shallots, most of the herbs and another spoonful of toasted rice powder.
Serve with the warm cooked jasmine rice, lettuce leaves, cucumber slices and extra lime wedges if you fancy. Scatter over the remaining herbs and extra toasted rice powder. Wrap, roll and dig in.

name: Thai Stir-Fried Chilli Prawns with Coconut Rice
description: Spicy prawns on fluffy coconut rice. Is there a better combo? If you can't find Nam Prik Pao substitute it with sriracha or sambal.
keywords: Stir Fried Chilli Spinach Prawns on Coconut Rice
Stir Fried Chilli Spinach Prawns on Coconut Rice recipe
instructions: Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear, then drain. Add the rice to a lidded saucepan along with the coconut milk and a pinch of salt, and give it a good stir. Bring the mixture to a boil over a high heat (you might need to give it another stir as the coconut solids melt) then cover with a lid, reduce to the lowest heat and set the timer for 18 mins. When the time is up, turn off the heat and leave the lid on until ready to serve.

Finely mince the garlic and chilli (this dish is spicy so use half the specified amount for less heat). Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok set over a high heat. Add the garlic and chilli and stir fry for 20 seconds until fragrant. Add the prawns and fry for a further 1-2 mins. Add the nam prik pao paste, white sugar, fish sauce, oyster sauce and water. Stir fry for a minute until the sauce ingredients have combined and coated the prawns. Add the Thai basil leaves and a handful of spinach. Stir fry for a couple of minutes until wilted. If the sauce is too dry, add a splash more water.
To serve, divide the rice between plates and top with the prawns and sauce. Finish with a wedge of lime.

name: Thai Sweet Potato Fish Cakes
description: Crispy-coated fish cakes with a fragrant Thai-spiced sweet potato and white fish filling, served on top of minty crushed peas. Worth every minute. They also keep well so you can eat them throughout the week.
keywords: Thai sweet potato fish cakes recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Place the sweet potatoes on a baking tray, drizzle with a little olive oil and season with salt. Roast for 1 hr until completely soft. Remove and leave to cool, you want them fully steamed off before you use them, so don't rush this step.

Once cool, halve the sweet potatoes and scoop the flesh into a large mixing bowl. Finely grate in the ginger and chilli, then add the lemongrass paste, roughly chopped coriander, soy sauce, sugar, juice of the lime and the sliced spring onions. Pat the fish fillets dry with kitchen paper, then finely chop and add to the bowl, mixing well to combine.. Season with salt and black pepper and squish everything together until well combined. Cover with cling film and chill in the fridge for 20 mins to firm up.

Meanwhile, set up a breading station with three shallow bowls: plain flour in the first, beaten eggs in the second and breadcrumbs in the third. Once the mixture is firm, shape it into cakes. Dip each cake in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs. Arrange on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and bake for 35 mins until golden and crisp.

While the fish cakes are in the oven, cook the peas in a pan of boiling water, then drain well. Roughly chop the mint and add to the peas along with the juice of the lemon and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper and mash together until crushed but still a little chunky.
To serve, spoon the crushed peas onto plates and sit the fish cakes on top.

name: Thai Tofu & Roasted Broccoli Rice Bowl
description: Your Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Roasted Broccoli batch goes Thai. Spooned over jasmine rice with quick-pickled cucumber and red onion, a sharp garlicky soy dressing and crunchy toasted rice on top, that last bit is the part you won't want to skip.
keywords: Thai-Inspired Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Broccoli Rice Bowl
Thai-Inspired Crunchy Spiced Tofu & Broccoli Rice Bowl recipe
instructions: Thinly slice the cucumber and cut the red onion into strips. Add to a bowl with the juice of half a lime, the sugar and a pinch of salt. Mix and set aside to lightly pickle.

Place a small frying pan over a medium heat. Add the raw rice and toast, stirring every minute or so, for 3-4 mins until golden brown, you'll know it's ready when it smells like popcorn. Tip into a pestle and mortar and crush until roughly ground. Alternatively, use the base of a heavy pan.
Make the dressing: finely mince the garlic and add to a small bowl with the juice of the remaining lime, the chilli flakes and soy sauce. Mix to combine.

Heat the rice and divide between bowls. Spoon over the tofu and broccoli, then add some of the pickled cucumber and red onion. Drizzle over the dressing and finish with the crushed toasted rice and fresh mint leaves.

name: Thai-Inspired Banana & Cinnamon Roti With Tahini Fudge Sauce
description: Traditionally served with banana and condensed milk, this pud is made from two cooked parathas filled with banana and cinnamon. Finish with a drizzle of tahini condensed milk and a scattering of sesame seeds.
instructions: Put the banana, cinnamon, maple syrup and a pinch of salt into a bowl. Mash together and set aside.
Get the condensed milk into a bowl with the tahini. Mix and then pop in the microwave for 30 seconds. Add a few tbsp water to loosen and stir until smooth. Set aside.

Get the paratha out of the freezer and transfer to a frying pan set over a medium heat. Cook until lightly golden, then add a spoonful of banana mix down the middle. Fold in the corners gently to seal, then flip. Cook for a couple of minutes until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, crush the peanuts.
Serve the paratha up on a plate, drizzle with tahini sauce and then scatter with peanuts and sesame seeds. Add a drizzle more maple syrup, if you like.

name: Thai-Inspired Chicken & Mango Chopped Salad
description: You guessed it - chopped salads are back and better than ever before. This one features tender chicken and juicy mango. We think you might just love it.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Season the chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper, then transfer to a baking tray and cook in the oven for 25 mins. Allow to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm.
Bring a pan of water to the boil, then drop in the green beans and blanch for 2-3 mins.

Put the cooked green beans, mangetout, cooked chicken breasts, mango and most of the coriander onto a chopping board. Chop into even-sized pieces. Add most of the peanuts to the board and chop again. Add all of your chopped ingredients to a large bowl.
For the dressing, squeeze the juice from your lime into a bowl. Finely chop the chilli and add that, too. Grate in the garlic, then add the remaining dressing ingredients.
Pour the dressing into the chopped salad bowl and toss together. Garnish with the reserved coriander and the reserved peanuts. Enjoy.

name: The Almighty Mob Chicken Pie
description: The king of the pies. The tarragon makes it. Mandatory dollop of mustard. You have to give this one a go. Follow this simple recipe and you’ll learn how to make Mob's comforting and delicious chicken pie, filled with tender chunks of chicken and veggies in a creamy sauce, topped with a flaky crust. Cook Mob's chicken and leek pie recipe today you’ll have a new family favourite which literally everyone will want a slice of. It’s a homemade pie recipe that’s impossible to mess up. All you need is a few simple ingredients to make it as well – using shop-bought puff pastry won’t just save you time faffing about in the kitchen but it’ll ensure you get the perfect golden casing for your puffed up pie. Cook smarter, not harder.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Dice up your chicken thighs into chunks. Add some olive oil to a large pan and brown the chicken. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Finely slice your leeks, bacon and onions.
Add bacon to the chicken pan and fry until crispy. Deglaze the pan with a splash of water. Add the leeks and onion.
Fry until soft, adding a splash of water if the vegetables start catching on the pan.
Once soft, add the chicken. Stir it in and add a large handful of chopped tarragon. Stir again and flour.
Mix it in, making sure the flour is all absorbed. Pour in milk, splash by splash. Keep stirring until you have a thick pie filling. Season generously with pepper. Remove the pan from the heat.

Fill a pie dish with the filling. Lay your puff pastry on top. Trim the sides and brush the pastry with egg yolk wash. Add a sprinkle of salt and place in the oven for 30 minutes, or until the pastry is puffed up and golden.
Slice your pie up and serve with a big dollop of Dijon mustard. Enjoy!

name: The Big Mob
description: England has reached the finals of the Euros, and we couldn't be happier. Celebrate by making this banging burger and having a few pints with your mates.
instructions: Peel your chorizo and finely crumble it into a pan. Fry on a low heat for 5 mins until it starts going crispy and the oils have been released. Peel and finely slice the onions.
Remove the chorizo with a slotted spoon and add the onions. Add a pinch of salt and cook on a low heat for 25 mins until your onions have caramelised.
Meanwhile, mince your garlic and slice the cherry tomatoes in half.
Add in the tomatoes, chilli flakes and garlic before cooking it down for a further 10 mins until the tomatoes are softened.
Deglaze the pan with red wine and add dark brown sugar. Cook for 10 mins until thickened to a thick, jammy consistency.
Add the chorizo back in and season with salt, then leave to cool.
Finely dice your gherkin.
Combine the mayo, mustard, ketchup, gherkins and ½ tsp smoked paprika in a bowl. Set that aside for later.
Finely shred your iceberg lettuce.
Season the mince with salt, mixing it loosely with your hands without compressing it too much

Divide your meat into 8 equal-sized pieces. Roll your mince into a rough ball, then place it on a very hot flat top. Flatten the patty with the base of a heavy pan and fry for 2 mins until its deeply caramelised. You want your burgers to be very flat and crisp.

Flip over your patties and add your slice of cheese. Next, you're going to want to pour a splash of water on the flat top before quickly placing a lid over the burger so that the cheese gets steamed. Cook the patty for 2 mins like this until the cheese has melted and the base is caramelised.

Toast your buns. Add chorizo chutney to the base, then layer on your shredded iceberg. Place your two patties on top of the lettuce, then spread your burger sauce on the lid of your bun and place that on top. Serve.

name: The Cheekiest Peri Peri Chicken
description: Cheekier than Nandos, with the tangiest, most delicious Peri Peri sauce you'll ever eat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F
Place chicken in a baking tray. Cover with olive oil. Add two tsp paprika and a tsp of dried oregano. Rub it in. Place chicken in the oven for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, prep the sauce. Cut peppers and red onion into chunks and add to a baking tray. Cut a lemon in half. Add the lemon halves, face side down. Add your chillies to the tray. Drizzle olive oil over everything. Place the tray in the oven for 40 minutes.
After 30 minutes, remove the chicken and baste it in the juices. Place it back in the oven for another 30 minutes.
When the vegetables and lemon are charred and soft, remove from the oven.

Place the onion and peppers into a blender. Add the juice of the roasted lemons. Add cloves of grated garlic, the zest and juice of a fresh lemon, 2 tsp of smoked paprika, two tsp of dried oregano, a tsp and a half of red wine vinegar, a tsp of olive oil and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Blitz until you have a smooth orange sauce.
Pour the sauce into a frying pan and add two bay leaves. Allow the sauce to gently bubble away for a couple of minutes so the bay leaves can infuse.
While the sauce is getting on, take your chicken out of the oven. Baste it in the juices and remove from the tray. Hack it up roughly.
Serve the chicken on a bed of basmati rice and black beans. Pour your sauce over the top. Enjoy mob, this one is a winner.

name: The Chicken Balti Pie
description: The football stadium classic cooked at home. Curry and pastry just works.
instructions: Preheat the oven 180°C/356°F.
Chop thigh meat into strips. Add it to a pan with some oil and brown it off.
Add a finely chopped onion, a sliced knob of ginger and sliced garlic cloves. Add garam masala, curry powder and cinnamon. Mix it all in.
Add mango chutney and mix it in. Add passata, stir it in and reduce the curry down. Once it is thick, plain yogurt.
Season the Balti with salt and pepper and remove from the heat.

Roll out some puff pastry and lay it into a baking tray, Make sure it comes up and hangs over the sides. Lay some baking paper on top of it and pour in a bag of rice to weigh the pastry down. Add the tray to the oven for 12 minutes. Remove the baking paper and bake for another 3 minutes.
Remove the tray from the oven. The pastry should be dry and partially baked. Spoon in your Balti.
Roll out the second layer of puff pastry. Layer it on top of the pie. Squeeze it along the pie edges. Brush the pie with egg yolk, sprinkle on some salt and then bake for 30 minutes until golden.
Cut up the pie and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: The Famous Flygerian Beef Suya
description: Perfect for summer and a top tier Nigerian street food! This meal will have you wishing sweet nothings to a future bae. The Flygerians x
instructions: Place the peanuts in a food processor and process until finely chopped.
Add the paprika, onion powder, ground ginger, ground scotch bonnet pepper, garlic powder and 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil and pulse until combined.
Separately blend the calabash nutmeg with a pinch of black pepper. Sift this into the peanut mixture.
Thinly slice the sirloin steak and place in a large bowl or shallow dish. Drizzle with vegetable oil, sprinkle with 2 tsp salt and toss to coat.
Add peanut mixture and toss again to coat. Refrigerate, covered, for 2 hours.
Drain the beef, discarding marinade, then thread it onto metal or soaked wooden skewers.
Dice the onion and tomato.
Grill the beef, covered and turning occasionally, over medium-high heat for 10-15 mins, or until it reaches your desired doneness. Serve with the diced onions and tomatoes.

name: The Freshest Pork Larb
description: Larb is a Thai classic, and this simple, easy take is sublime. The fresh mint and lime juice at the end lift it perfectly.
instructions: Prep your ingredients. Take your mint and coriander. With a knife, separate the stalks and the leaves. Finely chop the stalks of both but keep them separate. Finely chop your coriander and mint leaves.
Peel your ginger and chop into small matchsticks. Finely slice 1 red chilli and 4 spring onions. Measure out 4 tbsp of fish sauce.
At this point, get 300g of rice on. Rinse the rice and add it to a pan with 2 times the amount of boiling water. Cook without a lid until the water has been absorbed.

In a large wok or frying pan, add a splash of olive oil and then add your pork mince. Fry on a high heat, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. As the pork starts to caramelise, remove it from the wok and set it aside.
In the same wok, add a splash more oil. Add your ginger, red chilli, mint and coriander stalks, spring onions and 2 tsp of lemongrass puree.
Keep mixing your larb base. Once it starts to catch on the pan, pour in your fish sauce and squeeze in the juice of a lime. Mix it together, and then reintroduce the pork mince. Stir.
Add your rice spoon by spoon. Once all the rice and pork is folded together, add your coriander and mint leaves. Mix together. Remove the larb from the heat.
Serve the larb in crispy lettuce leaves and enjoy!

name: The Mob Tricolore
description: Mob's take on the Italian classic. Mozzarella, tomato, avocado and basil. So fresh, so delicious. The key is in the red wine vinegar dressing.
instructions: Chop the tomatoes into chunks, add a big pinch of salt and rub together. This will remove the excess water. Place the colander over a bowl and allow to sit for 15 minutes.
Dressing time. Add the olive oil, red wine vinegar, a tsp of salt, pepper and a tsp of chilli flakes into a jar. Shake until completely combined.
Chop up your mozzarella, and avocados into big chunks and add them into a bowl along with the tomatoes.
Finely chop your basil and scatter over (saving some for garnish). Pour over your dressing and toss all together.
Serve up and garnish with more chilli flakes, salt, pepper and the leftover basil. Tuck in!

name: The Stickiest Ribs
description: This marinade has the most delicious fragrant spiciness to it. In order to get the maximum level of stickiness, you have to baste.
instructions: Grab a bowl. Add soy sauce, honey, cider vinegar, grated garlic cloves, Chinese 5 Spice, cayenne, tomato puree and a good grind of black pepper. Mix it all together.
Place your rack of ribs in a baking tray. Pour ¾ of the marinade over them and rub it in. Cover with tin foil and marinate for 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 160°C/320°F.

Once the ribs have marinated, place the tray, with the tin foil still on, in the hot oven for an hour. After an hour, remove the foil and baste with the juices in the tray. Put the tray back in the oven for half an hour.
After 30 minutes, remove from the oven and pour over the remaining ¼ of marinade. Place the ribs back in the oven.
Keep on basting them every 20 minutes or so, until the ribs have had 3 hours total in the oven.
Remove from the oven, hack them up and tuck in! Enjoy!

name: The Stickiest Soy Drumsticks
description: Sticky chicken drumsticks, with a lovely guacamole dip. A great sharing dish for when the MOB are coming over.
instructions: Pre-heat your oven to 180°C/356°F.
Grab a bowl. Add some baking powder, salt and pepper. Coat your chicken in this mixture.
Put the chicken drumsticks on an oven tray. Place in the oven for 50 minutes, or until golden-brown and crispy.

Whilst waiting, pit and cut your avocados. Finely chop up your bunch of coriander and your spring onions. Whack it all into a bowl and smash. Halve a lime and squeeze all the juices into the bowl. Mix again.
When the chicken is done, grab a large saucepan. Add a knob of grated ginger, chopped garlic cloves and a splash of olive oil. Cook until softened.
Add sweet chilli sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and cook until the sauce is sticky.
Add your cooked drumsticks and toss!
Serve the drumsticks with the guac on the side. Enjoy MOB!

name: The Ultimate Banana Milkshake
description: Yes, you could go down to your favourite fast food chain and get a banana milkshake. But you could make your own and, I promise you, it’ll be so much better.
instructions: Peel the bananas and add to a blender along with the peanut butter, milk, vanilla ice cream, and ice. Blend until smooth.
Tip into a tall glass, top with a mountain of squirty cream. Grate dark chocolate over the top and milkshake your way back to feeling great.

name: The Ultimate Bloody Mary
description: Phoebe Wyburd shows us how to make the best spicy bloody mary in the biz using Sapling Vodka, and let us tell you it is the very best.
instructions: Pour your tomato juice, Sapling vodka, and Worcestershire sauce into a cocktail shaker. Add a pinch of celery salt and a few drops of Tabasco before seasoning liberally with salt and pepper.
Add ice, then pour it from mixer to mixer 6 times – this is called rolling a cocktail.
Pour your bloody mary into glass, then garnish with a celery stick, a pickled chilli and chilli flakes. Serve and enjoy.

name: The Ultimate Carbonara
description: Our take on a classic. Absolutely no cream anywhere near this dish. Pepper, smoked bacon, egg yolk, parmesan, pasta water and (maybe controversially) garlic. Stuff dreams are made of.
instructions: Take a bowl, and grate in your Parmesan and Pecorino (set a pinch aside for sprinkling at the end).

To the cheese, add the egg yolks (don't throw the whites, you can freeze them for meringue) and a very, very generous amount of black pepper. A good carbonara is meant to be peppery – hence the name, CARBONara. Whisk everything together and set aside.
Chop your smoked bacon into little bits, and add to a frying pan set over a medium heat.
As the bacon bits begin to brown, add your spaghetti to a large pan of boiling water. Salt the boiling water – pasta water is meant to be almost as salty as the sea!
Once the bacon is crisp, add your sliced garlic. Allow the garlic to soften – if the garlic or bacon looks like it is catching on a pan, add small spoons of the starchy pasta water.
When the pasta is 1 minute before being ready – so still quite al dente – ladle out some of the pasta water (about 1 ½ ladles for every person you're cooking for) into a bowl. Set this bowl aside.

Drain the pasta, and then pour the pasta into the pan with the bacon and the garlic. Add some of the pasta water (about ½ a ladle per person), and cook everything together over a medium heat. Once the water has evaporated and the pasta is nice and silky, take off the heat.
Allow to cool down for 1 minute, and then add the egg and parmesan mixture, and some more pasta water (about ½ a ladle per person) and mix it all together.
If it looks too thick, add a bit more water. It should be silky smooth! Serve with a sprinkle of parmesan and twist or two more of black pepper! Enjoy!

name: The Ultimate Falafel Burger
description: Crispy, gently spiced falafel patties are the best thing we’ve put in a bun for ages. The tahini mayo is a game changer.
instructions: Pour your dried chickpeas into a large bowl, then cover them generously with water. Pop them in the fridge and leave them to soak overnight.
Finely slice one of your red onions and your radishes.
Add your onions and radishes to a bowl along with the juice of 1 of your lemons and a good pinch of salt. Scrunch up with your hands to lightly pickle, then set aside.

Add your tahini to a bowl along with your vegan mayo and the juice of 1 lemon. Pour in 2 tbsp water, then whisk until you have a smooth sauce - it will look lumpy at first, but then get smooth. Add more water if necessary to get a thick, glossy consistency. Season to taste with salt.
Roughly chop your remaining red onion, cloves of garlic, parsley and coriander - stalks and all.

Dry your chickpeas with a tea towel, then add them to the barrel of a food processor with your red onion, garlic, parsley, coriander, dried cumin, dried coriander, aleppo chilli, chickpea flour, baking powder, and a level tsp of salt. Whizz to combine to a smooth paste - the smoother it is, the easier your falafel will be to shape.
Take a baseball-sized handful of the mixture, and gently shape it into a patty. Repeat 3 more times.
Heat a generous glug of vegetable oil in a frying pan. Add your falafel patties, and fry for 4 mins on each side until deeply golden brown and crispy.
Halve your burger buns and toast them in a dry frying pan.
Slice your cucumber.

Spread your tahini mayo on your burger bases, then add a dollop of chilli jam. Add a falafel burger, your sliced cucumber and pickles on top. Add a little more tahini mayo to the top of the bun, then place this on top.
Serve and enjoy!

name: The Ultimate Fish & Chips
description: Fish and chips. A dish that needs no introduction. This recipe will show you how to nail it at home from scratch.
instructions: First off, if you need to remove the skin from your fish, here’s how ya do it. Grab a sharp, thin knife and pat your fish dry with kitchen towels. Lay the fillet skin side down on your cutting board with the tail towards you.

Now, slide the knife under the flesh and as close to the skin as you can. Grab onto the end of the tail and carefully run your knife away from you, between the flesh and the skin, angled ever so slightly toward the board. Take your time and shimmy off the skin. Cut the fillet into your desired portions, we shoot for 100-110g.

Mix together the salt and sugar and sprinkle each portion with a fine dusting. Lay out on a tray and pop into the fridge for 45-60 mins, until the surface of the fish looks wet and the flesh has firmed up.

Peel the potatoes and cut into chunky-ish chips. Rinse the excess starch from the chips and place in a large pan. Cover with fresh cold water and season generously with salt. Set over a medium heat and gently bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to a bare simmer and cook the chips for 8-9 mins, checking regularly, until they’re cooked through and starting to ruffle around the edges.

Very carefully remove them from the water and lay out on a tray or wire rack to steam dry. If you have time, pop them in the fridge for 20-30 mins to set. This will make them easier to fry without breaking them later.
Once the fish is ready, rinse under icy cold water and pat dry with kitchen paper. Set aside.
To make the batter whisk together the rice flour, plain flour, baking powder and sugar. Combine the vodka and beer in a jug.

Add the oil and beef dripping to a large saucepan and bring to 170°C. Carefully lower your chips, working in batches, and cook for 7-8 mins until golden brown and super crunchy. Keep these warm in a low oven (120°C) while you fry the fish.
To finish the batter, gradually whisk the vodka and beer into the dry mix.

Working in batches, dust the fish in a bit of extra rice flour and dunk straight into the batter. Lift out and let the excess drip off. Gently lay into the hot oil, cook for 3-4 mins a side until golden brown and super crispy. Drain on kitchen paper and season with plenty of fine sea salt. Repeat with the remaining portions.
Pile your fish and chips onto plates and serve with tartar sauce, fresh lemon, ketchup, plenty of mushy peas and of course, malt vinegar.

name: The Ultimate Halloumi, Butternut Squash & Tahini Salad
description: This dish is all about the combo. The halloumi. The roasted Butternut. The creamy tahini dressing. The mint. It just goes on and on...
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Cut the butternut squash into bite-sized cubes and the red onion into chunks then add both to a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast in the hot oven for 30 mins or until caramelised and soft, then remove and set aside.

Dressing time. Grab a bowl. Add the tahini, grate in your garlic, juice in your lemon and pour in the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and mix to combine. Add warm water until you have a thick, creamy consistency. Set aside.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan set over a low-medium heat (watch them carefully, you don’t want them to burn). Set aside.
Steam the kale for about 8 mins or until cooked through then set aside. Pick and roughly chop the mint leaves.
Cut the halloumi into thick slices. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a griddle pan set over a high heat. Add the halloumi and cook for 3 mins on each side until golden and crisp.

Assembly time. To a salad bowl, add the halloumi, butternut squash, onion, kale. Add most of the pine nuts, pomegranate seeds and fresh mint, reserving a handful of each for garnish. Give everything a good mix. Pour in the tahini dressing and toss to combine. Top with the remaining pine nuts, pomegranate seeds, mint leaves.

name: The Ultimate Lasagne
description: We've made the best lasagne recipe. The secret ingredient? Milk. It tenderises the meat, to leave you with the most tender ragù. Use a deep dish and find out how to layer a lasagne.
instructions: Heat the oven to 150°C. Heat a large oven proof pot or casserole over a high heat until smoking hot, then add a glug of olive oil and crumble in the beef mince. Working in batches if necessary, brown the mince until it’s very crispy. The more colour the better, so take your time and make it count!

While the beef is browning, tip the onions, carrots and celery into a food processor and whizz into a finely chopped paste. Grate in your garlic. Tie the herbs together into a little bundle and set aside.

Once the beef is browned off, fish it out of the pan and tip in your veggie mix. Season with salt and cook for 13-15 mins over a medium heat. It should reduce in volume and pick up a little colour. Now add the beef back to the pan and add the wine. Scrape all the flavour off of the bottom of the pan and reduce the wine by half.
Drop in the bundle of herbs and pour in the chicken stock, tinned tomatoes, and milk. Bring to a boil, pop the lid on, and slide into the oven for 2 ½ to 3 hours.

Meanwhile, make the béchamel. Over a medium heat, melt the butter in a small saucepan and tip in the flour. Whisk together and cook for 1-2 mins until it starts to smell biscuity. Now gradually whisk in the milk, making sure you incorporate it fully between each addition. Once all the milk has been added, bring to a boil and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Remove from the heat and whisk in the grated Parmesan. Cover and set aside.
Pull the ragù out of the oven and season to taste with salt and pepper. It should have reduced significantly and be a deep brown colour. Set aside.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and blanch the lasagne sheets for 1 minute before shocking in ice water. Coarsely grate the mozzarella, finely chop the parsley and finely grate the Parmesan.

Increase the heat of the oven to 200°C. Grab a lasagne dish and start to layer up. Start with a thin layer of ragu, then pasta, then bechamel topped with grated mozzarella, parsley and Parmesan, then pasta, then ragù. Repeat until all of the ingredients have been used.

Finish the top layer with bechamel, mozz and parm and slide into the oven for 35-40 mins. It should come out bubbling, with crispy edges and a beautiful, burnished top. Allow to rest for 15 mins (at least!) before slicing and serving.

name: The Ultimate Sourdough Loaf
description: Once you’ve got the hang of this beautiful round sourdough loaf, you’ll never look back. Recipe by MOB Contributor Thomas Colson.
instructions:
A Casserole Pot / Ovenproof Saucepan With Lid
A Razor / A Very Sharp Knife
Mix together the water and flour in a medium mixing bowl and combine until all the flour is absorbed. You should have a loose, shaggy dough. Leave for one hour.
The night before you plan to make your dough, take your starter out the fridge and feed it.
Add the salt and starter to your dough and mix with wet hands until it's combined.
Tip out your dough onto a work surface and knead it for 2 minutes until smooth.

Transfer the dough to a well-oiled medium mixing bowl. Cover with a tea towel and let the dough rise in a warm place until it has doubled in size. This usually takes around 12 hours, but can take as little as four.
Shape your dough. Wet your hands, then gently tip it onto a lightly floured surface and stretch it out gently into a rough rectangle shape, being careful not to knock too many bubbles out.

Wet your hands again, then pick up the dough from the bottom and fold it towards the centre. Then fold it from the left and right side, and finally roll the dough up from the bottom over and onto itself. (see 'Stage 5: The Shape' video).

Wet your hands, then put the dough onto a lightly floured surface and push it gently around in a circular motion until the dough is shaped into a round ball (see 'Stage 5: The Shape' video). Place it, smooth side up, onto a lightly floured piece of baking paper and leave it to rest for a second time for 30 minutes.
While your dough is rising, place your casserole pot in the oven and preheat the oven to 240°C / 464°F.
Using a razor blade or very sharp knife, slash at least once across the diameter of the dough.
Remove the pot from the oven, then carefully lift up the parchment paper with the dough on and drop it gently into the pot.
Place the lid back on and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove the lid and bake for a further 15 minutes.
Remove to a wire rack and cool for 45 minutes to one hour. Enjoy!

name: The Ultimate Vegan French Toast
description: I wanted to crack a brunch classic, and I know you’ll absolutely love it. It's deliciously crisp on the outside, whilst still soft and fluffy on the inside.
instructions: To make the almond butter, roast the almonds for 10-12 mins at 180°C until they start to brown and smell deliciously toasted.

While they are still hot, transfer to a high-speed blender and blitz until smooth. Keep scraping down the sides and blending until you have a smooth almond butter. Add a little salt if you like. (You will need a very strong blender for this).

In a high-speed blender, combine the tofu, brown sugar, chickpea flour, soy milk, vanilla, nutmeg and cinnamon. Blend until completely smooth. Pour the mixture into a shallow, wide bowl or a small baking tray.
Add each slice of bread separately into the mixture and soak each side for 30 seconds, until fully drenched in the liquid.

Heat a frying pan over medium-low heat. Add a 2 tbsp of butter and, when it's almost melted, add a slice of toast. Don’t try to move the toast until at least 2 mins have passed as you will break the crust that is forming. Check after 2 mins if it’s formed slightly charred edges, it could take a few minutes more. It’s better to cook these slowly and on a low heat. When it’s done, flip and cook the other side. Repeat with each slice.
To serve, layer each slice with a squeeze of maple syrup, almond butter and your choice of toppings. I’ve used raspberries, pistachios and a spoon of soya yogurt.

name: Theo's 3 Ingredient Cheesy Gnocchi
description: Three ingredients, one pan, and the milk does all the work. Fry the gnocchi in butter until golden, then let the milk bubble down into a cheesy sauce that coats every piece. It's super comforting and perfect for a beginner.
instructions: Place a medium frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the butter and let it melt, then add the gnocchi.

Fry for 2-3 mins, until starting to colour, then tip in the milk. Let it bubble away for 2-3 mins, until the milk has evaporated and you're left with the cheesy curds coating the gnocchi. Season well with salt and black pepper to serve.

name: Thick and Creamy Chilli Hot Chocolate
description: Inspired by the Mexican chocolate caliente, a popular cacao drink made with spices and chilli. Chilli pairs perfectly with chocolate, but is delicious without.
keywords: Thick and Creamy Chilli Hot Chocolate
instructions: Add about half of the milk to a small saucepan and add the chocolate into it. Set on a low heat and stir often to melt the chocolate, making sure it doesn't come to a boil.

Once the chocolate has melted, add the rest of the milk, chilli powder, nutmeg, vanilla bean pod (if using), sugar, and coffee. Sift in the cocoa powder through a sieve to prevent clumps. Whisk until combined, keeping on a low simmer.

Once all of the ingredients have combined to a smooth mixture, add the cinnamon sticks. If you like lots of heat, you can also add your fresh chilli here to infuse too. Simmer on a low heat, stirring often, for 10 mins to allow the flavours to infuse.
When ready, remove the cinnamon and chilli and set aside. Taste and add more sugar if you like, this will depend on the sweetness of your chocolate.
To serve, pour into your favourite mug and top with coconut whipped cream and a cinnamon stick and chilli for garnish. Finish with a dusting of grated chocolate or cocoa powder.

name: Thom Eagle's Speedy Cabbage Kimchi
description: Fermenting specialist Thom Eagle's cabbage kimchi is a quick recipe inspired by the Korean classic side dish.
instructions: Trim the cabbage of any tough or discoloured outer leaves, then slice across in inch-thick intervals so it falls apart into bite-sized pieces. Place in a bowl.
Sprinkle a tbsp of salt over the cabbage then rub it in with your hands, massaging until it begins to release its juices and feels wet to the touch. Set aside for two hours.
Meanwhile, make the spice paste. Peel the garlic and blitz with the ginger in a food processor or grate finely if you don't have one. Then mix with the chilli, soy, fish sauce and the apple juice.
When the cabbage is ready squeeze it gently and add to the spice paste, leaving behind any salty juices. Mix well to thoroughly coat the cabbage in the paste.

Pack the cabbage into a glass jar or fermenting pot, pushing it right down so it is covered with liquid. You may need to weigh it down – fermenting crocks come with a stone for this purpose, or I often use a lemon. In a small jar a scrunched up piece of baking paper often does the job.
Close the jar and leave to ferment at room temperature for at least three days. Once a day ‘burp’ the container by releasing the lid slightly to allow any built-up gas to escape.
