You will see your kimchi bubble as it begins to ferment and sour – this is good! After three days taste the kimchi to see how it is getting on – you may want to leave it to get a little sourer and funkier.
When you’re happy with the taste, pop the jar in the fridge. It’ll keep there pretty much indefinitely, ready to tuck in to.

name: Three Cheese Paratha With Coriander & Mint Chutney
description: This cheesy paratha is an excellent recipe from Chetna Makan. The bright green chutney is essential for cutting through the richness of the paratha.
keywords: Three Cheese Paratha With Coriander & Mint Chutney
Three Cheese Paratha With Coriander & Mint Chutney recipe
instructions: In a bowl combine the flour, salt and oil. Slowly add the water and bring the dough together. You might not need all the water or need a bit more. Knead for a few seconds. Put a few drops of oil in the palm of your hands and knead the dough for a last time, cover and let it rest for 10 mins.
In another bowl combine all the filling ingredients.

Preheat a skillet to medium heat. Divide the dough into 4 portions, roll each portion to a small circle around 3-4 inches big. Now take a quarter of the cheese filling and place it in the centre of the circle and bring the outside together and seal the cheese. Roll this in some flour and roll to a thinner circle around 8-9 inches big.
Place on the hot pan and cook for a minute before turning over. Cook for another minute then add a tsp of oil on each side and cook for another minute until golden and crispy.

In a blender add all the chutney ingredients (squeezing in the juice of the lime but discarding the skin) except for the yoghurt and blitz to a purée. Now add the yoghurt and blitz again. Serve immediately. You can store this in the fridge for 3-4 days.
Spread some salted butter on top and serve hot.

name: Three Quid Spaghetti
description: A take on the Italian classic, aglio olio. Doesn't really get much better than chilli, parsley and garlic. And it only costs £3. Easy.
instructions: Cook your spaghetti in a large pot of salted boililng water according to package directions.
Peel and finely slice the garlic. Pick the parsley leaves then finely chop both leaves and stems, keeping separate.
Add garlic, chilli flakes and the parsley stalks to a frying pan with 4 tbsp of olive oil.

Once the pasta is al dente, drain, reserving a mugful of starchy pasta water. Add it to the frying pan with the garlic and parsley. Start tossing it all together, gradually adding splashes of pasta water and the chopped parsley leaves.

Once everything is mixed in and the pasta is thick and almost creamy (from the pasta water), remove from heat. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Serve it up with extra chopped parsley leaves on top as a garnish. Enjoy!

name: Tiki Lychee Cooler
description: Combining the flavours of fresh lychee with the enjoyable flavour of mint, this cocktail is a brilliant summer cocktail.
instructions: Combine the sugar, lime and mint in a highball glass and muddle together.
Add plenty of crushed ice along with 50ml of Captain Morgan Tiki Mango & Pineapple and your lychee juice.
Mix well and garnish with extra mint and fresh lychee.

name: Tikka Halloumi & Curried Lentils
description: A vegetarian alternative to chicken tikka that makes the most of halloumi's wonderfully squeaky texture.
instructions: Finely slice your red onion, and add ¼ of it to a bowl. Squeeze over the juice of ½ lime, and a pinch of salt, then scrunch it up in your hands to pickle it a bit. Set it aside.
Mix your curry powder, chilli powder, and ground turmeric together in a bowl.
Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat with a splash of olive oil. Add your remaining red onion, and cook it for about 15 mins, adding splashes of water occasionally to stop them from sticking.
Heat your grill to high.

Grate your garlic into the pan, then add half of your spice mix, and cook them out for about 2 mins. Tip in your tomatoes, lentils and water. Simmer for 10 mins over a medium heat, until the lentils are hot and the sauce is thick.
Add ¼ of your yoghurt to a bowl, and add your remaining spices, as well as a splash of olive oil. Cut your halloumi into slices, then gently coat them in this marinade.
Arrange the halloumi slices on a tray lined with kitchen foil, then grill them for a few minutes on each side until the halloumi is bubbly with charred edges.
Mix your remaining yoghurt with the juice of your remaining lime in a bowl.
Season your lentils to taste with salt, then spoon them into bowls. Top the lentils with your halloumi, a dollop of yoghurt, your pickled red onions and some coriander leaves. Serve it up.

name: Tikka Halloumi Skewers
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Juicy chunks of halloumi marinated in creamy yoghurt and rich tikka masala paste, then cooked in the air fryer until golden and charred. Served with fluffy basmati rice and a herby, crunchy pomegranate salad, this is a proper weeknight winner made with affordable ingredients from Aldi that takes no time at all.
instructions: Cut the halloumi into 2cm chunks. In a bowl, mix ¼ of the yoghurt with the tikka masala paste, a drizzle of olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss in the halloumi to coat, then set aside to marinate.
Slice the courgette into 3cm-thick rounds. Set aside for threading onto skewers later.
Rinse the basmati rice, then cook it in a pan of salted boiling water according to the packet instructions. Drain and fluff with a fork once cooked.
Halve the cucumber lengthways and finely chop. Peel and finely slice the red onion. Slice the red chilli. Pick the mint leaves and roughly chop.
In a bowl, toss together the cucumber, onion, chilli, mint, and pomegranate seeds. Squeeze over the juice of ½ a lime and season with salt and pepper. Cut the remaining lime half into wedges.

Thread the marinated halloumi and courgette onto skewers. Air fry at 200°C for 15 mins until golden and slightly charred, turning halfway. If using mango chutney (optional), stir it through the remaining yoghurt now and season to taste. If not, just season the yoghurt with salt and pepper.
Divide the rice between plates. Top with the herby pomegranate salad and the skewers. Serve with the lime wedges and a dollop of the seasoned yoghurt.

name: Tikka Masala Tofu Skewers
description: A delicious veg-focused recipe that brings bold flavours in no time. Marinate the tofu ahead of time for an extra speedy dinner.
instructions: Soak the skewers in some water (this will help them not catch on fire). Then, marinate the tofu. Add the yoghurt into a bowl and stir through the curry paste. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Cube the tofu into around 2cm pieces and mix it through the yoghurt, making sure each piece is fully covered. Cover the bowl and pop it in the fridge to marinate for at least 30 mins (up to overnight). Save the extra yoghurt for later.

Meanwhile, pick the coriander leaves, discarding the stems. Place the leaves into a bowl of ice water to keep them crisp (optional). Halve or chop the tomatoes into bite sized chunks. Half the cucumber lengthways and scoop the seeds out, then, thinly slice. Heat the grill to high.
Slide the tofu onto the skewers and place onto an oiled baking tray. Slide the tofu under the grill until starting to char, 5-10 mins (keep an eye on them as each grill varies in temperature).

Reheat the rice and share between plates. Add the coriander leaves, tomatoes and cucumber into a bowl. Season with salt and lemon juice and spoon onto the plates. Top with the tofu skewers and finish with a dollop of yoghurt. Serve with any remaining lemon wedges.

name: Tikka Paneer Wraps
description: The ultimate veggie Indian-inspired kebab. Paneer and peppers are fried in tikka masala curry paste and served with a speedy raita, roti and mango chutney.
instructions:
Cut each block of paneer into 12 cubes. Deseed and roughly
chop the peppers. Scrape both into a mixing bowl. Add the oil
and curry paste. Mix to coat the cheese and peppers in the paste.
Get a large frying pan over a high heat. Tip in the paneer and
peppers along with all the oil and paste. Spread out in the pan and
fry for 5 mins, turning everything regularly with a spatula, until
the paneer is crisp on all sides.
Meanwhile, make a quick raita. Dollop the yogurt into a small bowl
and tear in half the mint leaves. Coarsely grate in the cucumber,
then peel and finely grate in the garlic. Season with salt and black
pepper and stir.
Take the paneer off the heat when ready. Warm the chapattis or
rotis in the microwave following the packet instructions and put
two on each plate. Spoon over the tikka paneer and peppers,
then dollop over some raita and mango chutney. Tear over the
remaining mint leaves to finish.

name: Tim Spector's Tofu Butter Curry
description: A delicious and nutritious recipe that's good for your body, soul, and mind. This creamy tofu curry is packed with protein and fibre.
keywords: Tim Spector's Tofu Butter Curry recipe
instructions: Finely slice your onions. Finely chop your garlic and ginger.

Add a good glug of vegetable oil to a sauté pan. Add your onions and cook for 15 mins over a medium heat, until they are fully softened and have just begun to caramelise. Add your garlic, ginger and tomato purée, then cook for 2 mins.
Tip in your chilli powder, garam masala and dried coriander, then add your water and your cream. Bring to a gentle simmer and simmer for 5 mins.
Meanwhile, cut your tofu into large chunks. Remove the outer leaves from the cauliflower and cut it into chunky florets.
Heat a frying pan over a medium heat. Add a big splash of olive oil and add your tofu chunks and cook for 5 mins until each piece is golden on all sides.
Pour your sauce into a blender, then blitz until you have a smooth consistency.

Pour the sauce back into the pan over a medium heat. Tip in the cauliflower florets and add 100ml of water. Cover with a lid and cook for 15 mins until the cauliflower is cooked through. Stir through your tofu. Add your butter, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Finish your curry with a drizzle of kefir and some coriander leaves.

name: Tingly Double Pepper Beef Stir-Fry
description: Beef mince, green beans and onion tossed in a sticky oyster sauce, with a tingly hit of black pepper and Szechuan. Piled over rice with a squeeze of lime, all ready in under 25 mins.
instructions: Thinly slice the onion and trim the green beans, cutting them into 1cm chunks. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems, keeping them separate. Coarsely crush the peppercorns.
Stir all the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl and set aside.
Place a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the oil and brown the mince for 5-7 mins, breaking it up as you go, until cooked through and starting to caramelise.

Add the green beans, onion, coriander stems and crushed spices to the pan. Stir-fry for 3-4 mins until fragrant and the veg is tender but still has a slight crunch. Pour over the sauce, toss everything together and remove from the heat. Toss half the coriander leaves through, then zest the lime in and squeeze over the juice. Taste and adjust with a little more honey or soy sauce if needed.
Reheat the rice according to packet instructions and divide between plates. Top with the stir-fry and scatter over the remaining coriander leaves.

name: Tinned Fish Potluck
description: Looking for a spread with bags of flavour? Loaded with first-class tinned fish and veggies, then finished with sides of crackers and aioli, it's a yes from us.
instructions: Crack open the tin of tuna and drain any excess oil. Tip into a bowl and add the hot sauce, juice of the lime and the sesame seeds. Split the avocado in half. Cut one half into a chunky dice and fold through the tuna. Season the mix to taste with salt and pepper. Thinly slice the other half. Finely cut the chives and fold most through the tuna mix.
Return the spicy tuna mix to the can and top with the sliced avo, extra lime juice, chopped chives and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

Crack open the sardines and leave in the tin. To make the salsa, very finely dice all of the remaining ingredients except the parsley and lemon. Mix in a bowl, season with salt and pepper. Finely chop the parsley and fold through the salsa with the lemon zest and juice.
Top the sardine tin with a healthy spoon of the salsa and a whole pickle.
Pop the butter into the freezer for 30 mins.
Rub the bread with olive oil and preheat a griddle pan over a high heat. Grill the bread on both sides until charred and toasted. Rub with a garlic clove straight away and set aside.

Grab a serrated knife and cut along the surface of the butter, at a 45 degree angle, to create little curls of butter. This might take a couple of tries to get the hang of, but have faith, you’ll crack it.
Open the anchovies and serve with a plate of butter curls, sea salt, and the grilled bread.

To finish the spread, wash and prepare your veggies. If small, I like to cut them lengthways or just leave them whole. Just cut them into pieces that make sense! Serve with crackers, a sprinkling of dill, lemon wedges, aioli and hot sauce. Get stuck in.

name: Tinned Tuna Poke Bowl
description: Spicy tuna, crunchy slaw, sticky rice, and miso dressing. Build your own mouthfuls with nori and go wild.
instructions: Drain the tuna and chuck it into a bowl with the mayo, sriracha and soy sauce. Mix well and set aside.
Peel and shred the carrots. Finely slice the red cabbage. Blanch the edamame in boiling water for 3 mins, then drain.
In a small bowl, whisk together the miso paste, rice vinegar, soy sauce and honey. Add a splash of water to loosen if it’s too thick.
Mix the carrot and cabbage with two-thirds of the miso dressing and toss to coat.
To build your bowls, start with a layer of warm rice. Top with the dressed slaw, spicy tuna and edamame beans.
Drizzle over the remaining dressing, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with lime wedges.
Tear up the nori and use it to scoop up all the good stuff.

name: Tinned Tuna Tostada
description: This simple, but effective, tuna tostada recipe is as affordable as it is delicious. A speedy high-protein pescatarian weeknight dinner.
instructions: To crisp up the tortillas, you can use two different methods: fry or bake them. To bake them, preheat the oven to 200°C, brush each tortilla with oil on both sides, place onto a baking tray and roast in the oven for 10-15 mins, flipping halfway through until golden and crispy. If you’re frying, place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with 1cm oil. Once hot, fry the tortillas for 2-3 mins until golden and crispy. Transfer to a baking tray lined with kitchen paper.

Stir the mayo and hot sauce in a large bowl. Drain the tuna and add that, too. Trim and thinly slice the spring onion and cucumber, add to the bowl and mix well. Season with salt. Thinly slice the avocado.

For the vinaigrette, halve and finely grate the tomatoes into another bowl, discarding the skin. Squeeze in the juice of ½ a lime, then add the remaining vinaigrette ingredients and stir well. Taste and season with salt, adding more lime juice if needed.
Pile the tuna mixture on top of the tostadas. Place a bit of avocado on, and spoon over the tomato dressing. Serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Tiramisu Espresso Martini
description: It’s sweet, it’s punchy, and it’ll wake you the hell up. This tiramisu espresso martini is all you’ve ever wanted.
instructions: Separate your egg whites and yolk (you can use the egg whites for other cocktails), then mix the yolk in a bowl with the sugar until the colour of the yolk turns pale and fluffy.
Add the mascarpone to the bowl and whisk to combine.
Add in the condensed milk and Frangelico then mix until the consistency is thick, but still loose enough to drizzle. Set aside.
Chill a large martini coupe glass with ice and water.
Add all your wet espresso martini elements to a cocktail shaker and shake until a frost forms on the outside of the shaker.
Remove all the ice and water from the coupe and double strain in your martini mix.
Pour over half of your tiramisu mix in circles over the martini. Dust thickly with the cocoa powder and dig in with a sponge finger.

name: Tiramisu Granita
description: This is the perfect dessert for anyone who hates making dessert. It takes soo little effort and skill to whip it up, but the end product is 10/10, heavenly and refreshing. Keep it in the freezer for a quick cooling treat.
instructions: Put the coffee, liqueur, sugar and salt into a bowl and whisk together until the sugar melts. Pour into a large baking dish and transfer to the freezer. Freeze for 3 hrs, making sure to scrape the mixture every 30 mins with a fork, breaking up any large clumps that form. The end texture should be flakes of fluffy ice. Once ready, serve immediately or cover with cling film and keep in the freezer until needed (you’ll have to scrape it again before serving).
Meanwhile, whisk the mascarpone in a bowl until smooth. Add the double cream, amaretto/marsala, and add as much icing sugar as you like. Whisk until soft peaks form.
Spoon the granita into cups or bowls, top with the whipped mascarpone cream and dust with cocoa powder.

name: Tiramisu Mocha
description: We always look forward to a warm drink when the weather is a bit rubbish, and even better when it’s topped up with a bit of Kahlúa.
instructions: In a small bowl mix the cocoa and Horlicks into a paste with a drop of milk, then gradually add more milk until it’s smooth.
Add to a pan with the remaining milk and heat gently, before adding in the Kahlúa and a pinch of salt.
Pour the hot chocolate into a heat-proof glass, top with squirty cream and grate over some dark chocolate.

name: Toasted Coconut Fried Rice
description: Not your average fried rice. Packed with greens and flavour, the base of it is a toasted coconut milk which makes absolutely everything better.
instructions: Pour the coconut milk into a frying pan and place onto medium-high heat. Cook the coconut milk, stirring occasionally until the coconut splits and the solids are golden.

Meanwhile, trim and chop the Tenderstem stems into 1cm chunks, leaving the tops whole. Trim and thinly slice the chilli and spring onions, separating the greens from the whites. Grate the ginger and garlic.

Once the coconut milk has split, stir the spring onion whites, garlic and ginger through until fragrant. Stir fry the Tenderstem stems for 1-2 mins, then add a splash of water, the broccoli tops, and cover with a lid, to steam for 2-4 mins, until tender.
Stir the rice and soy sauce through, making sure to break up any clumps. Stir the spinach and ¾ of the remaining spring onions through until wilted. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Share between bowls, top with the chilli and remaining spring onion.

name: Toasted Rice Sweet and Sour Dressing
description: A bold and aromatic dressing with nutty toasted rice, sweet chilli jam, and tangy lime juice. This sauce adds depth and complexity to grilled meats, salads, and noodle dishes.
keywords: Toasted Rice Sweet and Sour Dressing
Toasted Rice Sweet and Sour Dressing recipe
instructions: Place a small pan over medium heat and add the jasmine rice. Dry toast for 4-6 minutes, stirring, until golden brown.
Transfer the toasted rice to a pestle and mortar and grind into a coarse powder (some texture is fine).
In a bowl, mix the chilli jam, fish sauce, and lime juice. Stir well to combine.
Add the ground toasted rice, finely sliced shallots, and chopped coriander to the dressing.
Mix everything together and let sit for 5 mins before serving.

name: Toby's Breakfast Fried Rice
description: Toby, our magical video editor, treated the studio to his breakfast fried rice and mornings haven't been the same since. This recipe is a scorcher.
instructions: First, chop up your bacon and garlic before cutting your halloumi into cubes that are roughly 2cm in size.

Put a bit of oil in your wok and cook the bacon for 5 mins until it’s crispy. In the same pan, add your sliced garlic and cook for 1 min until it’s all golden. Remove the bacon and garlic onto a paper towel and set aside.
Add another glug of oil and fry the halloumi for 3 mins until golden brown. Allow it to drain on the paper towel with the bacon.

Finally, add your eggs into the pan and scramble for 3 mins until very dry. Add back in the bacon, garlic and halloumi as well as your leftover rice. Give that a stir then add your sesame oil, mirin, soy sauce, and honey, continuing to stir it all together as you go.
When the rice is all coated and mixed well, spoon it onto plates and garnish with some chopped spring onions. Enjoy.

name: Toffee Vodka
description: Never wince at the taste of a vodka shot again
instructions: Open and pour out some of the vodka in the bottle. Save this liquid for another day or drink.
Top up the bottle with some water, depending on how strong you want your drink.
Crush up your Werther's Original in a pestle and mortar.
Pour the crushed Werther’s into your vodka bottle and screw the lid on tight.
Put the bottle into your dishwasher for a 30min to 45 min cycle.
Once it’s finished, cool the bottle in the freezer and enjoy.

name: Tofu & Sweet Potato Curry
description: A lovely, rich curry. One for the vegan MOB. The fresh coriander at the end really lifts the dish.
instructions: Heat a non-stick pan. Add the sliced brown onions and sliced garlic cloves. Fry until soft. Add the tofu cubes and curry paste, stir fry for 1 minute and then add the sweet potato.
Stir well. Dissolve stock cube into 300ml of water and pour the coconut milk and stock over. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 20 minutes
After 20 minutes, remove the lid and let the curry bubble away and reduce until it has thickened. Cover and set aside.

Couscous time. Pour some olive oil into a frying pan and add your cauliflower couscous. Add a large handful of frozen peas. Cook until the peas are hot and then add a large handful of chopped coriander. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from the heat.
Time to serve up. Divide the cauliflower couscous between four plates, top with the curry and garnish with any leftover coriander leaves. Enjoy!

name: Tofu Curry Laksa
description: There are so many types of laksa in Malaysia but this one is my favourite. It's wonderfully aromatic, rich, creamy, spicy and only takes half an hour to make.
instructions: On medium-low heat, fry the paste with a small glug of oil for a few mins until aromatic then pour in the hot water. Let it simmer for a bit then pour in your coconut milk and boil for 10 mins.
Cut all of your tofu puffs in half.

Cook your vermicelli noodles in a heatproof bowl of boiling water. Meanwhile, cook your green beans and beansprouts for a few mins in a pot of boiling water. Use the same pot of cooking water to boil your eggs.
Add palm sugar and fish sauce to your laksa along with pak choi, fried tofu puffs, green beans and beansprouts. Give it a stir.
Add a portion of your vermicelli noodles to a bowl, pour in your hot laksa soup and serve with a boiled egg and fresh coriander per bowl. Enjoy!

name: Tofu Gyros Bowl
description: This high-protein tofu bowl is fresh, zesty, and ridiculously satisfying. Crisp, spiced tofu meets cool Greek yoghurt, herby quinoa, and tangy feta. Perfect for a quick lunch or light dinner.
instructions: Use a vegetable peeler to shave the tofu into ribbons. In a bowl, mix together the olive oil, smoked paprika, oregano, garlic powder, cumin, and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Add the tofu and toss to coat. Leave to marinate for at least 15 mins.
Air-fry the tofu at 190°C for 10 mins, or bake at 200°C for 10-15 mins, until golden and slightly crisp.

Meanwhile, dice the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes, and finely slice the red onion. Cut the lemon into wedges. Add the veg to a bowl and squeeze over ½ the lemon, saving the rest for serving. Cook the quinoa according to the packet instructions, then fluff it up with a fork and season lightly with salt and pepper.

Swoosh the Greek yoghurt into a serving bowl. Pile on the quinoa, crispy tofu, cucumber, tomatoes, and red onion. Crumble over the feta and scatter with mint leaves. Serve with lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.

name: Tofu Gyros Bowl
description: This high-protein tofu bowl is fresh, zesty, and ridiculously satisfying. Crisp, spiced tofu meets cool Greek yoghurt, herby quinoa, and tangy feta. Perfect for a quick lunch or light dinner.
instructions: Use a vegetable peeler to shave the tofu into ribbons. In a bowl, mix together the olive oil, smoked paprika, oregano, garlic powder, cumin, and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Add the tofu and toss to coat. Leave to marinate for at least 15 mins.
Air-fry the tofu at 190°C for 10 mins, or bake at 200°C for 10-15 mins, until golden and slightly crisp.

Meanwhile, dice the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes, and finely slice the red onion. Cut the lemon into wedges. Add the veg to a bowl and squeeze over ½ the lemon, saving the rest for serving. Cook the quinoa according to the packet instructions, then fluff it up with a fork and season lightly with salt and pepper.

Swoosh the Greek yoghurt into a Tupperware container. Pile on the quinoa, crispy tofu, cucumber, tomatoes, and red onion. Crumble over the feta and scatter with mint leaves. Serve with lemon wedges on the side for squeezing. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — it’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Tofu Milanese Ciabatta
description: A vegan twist on an exceedingly delicious Italian sandwich. Crispy tofu. Smoky peppers. Peppery rocket. Pesto spiked mayo. A total delight to eat.
instructions: Cut your ciabattas in half and toast cut side down in a dry frying pan.
Slice each tofu block into 6 thin slices.
Mix your flour, oat milk and 4 tbsp Sacla Vegan Pesto in a bowl until it forms a thick batter. Pour your panko breadcrumbs into a separate bowl.
Dip a tofu slice into your batter, then straight into the breadcrumbs so that it is fully coated. Repeat with your remaining tofu slices.

Heat a good glug of vegetable oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add your tofu slices and fry for 3 minutes on each side until crispy and golden. Remove from the pan and drain on a plate lined with paper towel.
Mix your remaining pesto with your vegan mayo in a bowl.
Slice your tomatoes and drain your jarred red peppers, patting dry with some paper towel if they feel a little wet.
Assembly time. Spread the base of your ciabatta with your pesto mayo, then top with your crispy tofu, red peppers, sliced tomato and rocket. Top with the other side of your bread, then serve.

name: Tofu Noodle Bowl with Grapefruit & Peanuts
description: A minimal cook recipe with a dressing that does all the work. Fresh, creamy, colourful and packed with plant protein, it tastes as good as it makes you feel.
keywords: Tofu Noodle Bowl with Grapefruit & Peanuts
Tofu Noodle Bowl with Grapefruit & Peanuts recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Pat the tofu dry and dice into small 1cm cubes, then tip into a bowl with a drizzle of olive oil and a large pinch of salt. Spread onto a baking tray and roast for 20 mins, giving it a stir halfway.

While the tofu roasts, make the dressing. Squeeze the grapefruit juice into a bowl, grate in the garlic and ginger, then add the tahini, sesame oil, soy sauce and the juice of the lime half. Whisk with a fork until combined. Taste and add the sugar if it needs balancing.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Add the noodles and cook for 3-5 mins, adding the edamame for the final 2 mins. Drain and rinse under cold water.

Peel the carrots, then keep peeling them straight into the dressing bowl to make ribbons. Cut the grapefruit into segments and shred the mint, then add both to the bowl along with the drained noodles and edamame.
Divide between bowls and top with the roasted tofu, chopped peanuts and a generous squeeze of the remaining lime half.

name: Tofu Noodle Traybake
description: Here's a firm vegan favourite that you can get on the table in just 30 mins. Picture a noodle stir-fry... but as a traybake. A sure-fire dinner table win.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Drain the tofu and cut it into medium cubes. Cut the sprouts in half. Spoon 4 tbsp of the cornflour into a shallow bowl and season with salt and pepper. Toss the tofu in the cornflour mix so that it gets evenly coated.

Put the tofu onto one half of a large baking tray, leaving enough space between each cube so that they can crisp up. Spread the sprouts in an even layer onto the other half of the tray. Drizzle the oil evenly across the tofu and sprouts. Roast for 15–20 mins until the sprouts are cooked through and charred and the tofu is crisp.

Meanwhile, toast the peppercorns in a dry frying pan over a medium heat until smelling great. Leave to cool slightly. Thinly slice the red chilli and add to a small bowl. Pour over a splash of maple syrup and 2 tbsp of the rice wine vinegar, stir and leave to quick-pickle.

Crush the peppercorns then tip into a bowl. Add the remaining tablespoon of cornflour and 150ml water and mix until the cornflour is fully combined before adding the remaining 4 tsp of maple syrup, 1 tbsp of vinegar and the soy sauce. Set aside.

Next up, peel and cut the ginger and carrots into rough matchsticks then come back to your roasted tofu and sprouts. Add the noodles to the tin, breaking up any clumps with your spoon, then add the carrot, ginger, sugar snap peas and then finally the sauce. Give everything a good mix together and return to the oven for 5 mins until the noodles and sugar snap peas are heated through and the sauce is reduced.
Divide between four bowls, top with the pickled red chilli and serve.

name: Tofu Poke Bowl
description: A spicy, fresh tofu bowl packed with crunchy veg, juicy mango and a zingy sriracha yoghurt. Perfect for meal prep.
instructions: Dice the tofu into bite-sized chunks. Zest the lime. Add the tofu to a bowl along with the gochujang, soy sauce and lime zest. Toss to coat and set aside to marinate while you prep the rest.
Dice the mango into small pieces. If you'd prefer your quinoa warm, heat it now following pack instructions. Pick the coriander.
In a small bowl, mix the Greek yoghurt with the sriracha and lime juice. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Time to build your bowl. Divide the quinoa between Tupperware containers and top with the marinated tofu, mango, edamame and kimchi. Drizzle over the sriracha yoghurt and finish with a scattering of coriander and sesame seeds. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Tofu Poke Bowl
description: A spicy, fresh tofu bowl packed with crunchy veg, juicy mango and a zingy sriracha yoghurt. No cooking needed. Just chop, mix and dig in.
instructions: Dice the tofu into bite-sized chunks. Zest the lime. Add the tofu to a bowl along with the gochujang, soy sauce and lime zest. Toss to coat and set aside to marinate while you prep the rest.
Dice the mango into small pieces. If you'd prefer your quinoa warm, heat it now following pack instructions. Pick the coriander.
In a small bowl, mix the Greek yoghurt with the sriracha and lime juice. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Time to build your bowl. Divide the quinoa between two bowls and top with the marinated tofu, mango, edamame and kimchi. Drizzle over the sriracha yoghurt and finish with a scattering of coriander and sesame seeds.

name: Tofu Satay Skewers
description: This is our version of a Malaysian street-food snack. We’ve loaded it with bold anti-inflammatory spices, which, when combined with fresh cucumber pickles.
instructions:
First make the pickle. Chop the cucumber in half lengthways
and remove the seedy core, then thinly slice the cucumber and
red onion and add them to a jar or deep bowl. Add the apple cider
vinegar to a saucepan and bring to a simmer over a medium heat.
Add the salt and sugar, mixing well until they dissolve. Pour the
pickling mixture over the sliced cucumber and red onion and let
them sit for 30 mins.
Now for the tofu skewers. Roughly chop the tofu into 3cm (11⁄4in)
cubes and add to a bowl.
Roughly chop the garlic, shallot and the white of your
lemongrass (saving the green part for later) and add to a blender
along with the ground coriander, ground turmeric and chilli
powder. Add a splash of water and blend until smooth. Add this
marinade to the bowl of tofu and mix thoroughly, then set aside.
Meanwhile, make the satay sauce. Start by very finely chopping
the garlic and shallot. Get a saucepan over a medium heat, then add
the vegetable oil and your chopped shallot and garlic. Fry for a few
minutes until the veg is golden.
Add the chilli powder, ground turmeric and coriander to the
pan and mix well. Next, you’re going to want to go in with the
tamarind paste, sugar, salt, peanut butter and the green parts of the
lemongrass you chopped up earlier. Pour in 180ml of water
along with coconut milk and soy sauce. Bring to the boil, making
sure to regularly stir it so the bottom of the pan doesn’t burn. This
will take about 5 mins. Turn the heat down and let it simmer for
30 mins.
Preheat the grill to medium-high.
Thread 3 or 4 marinated tofu cubes onto each of your skewers
(depending on size and personal preference).
Get a griddle pan hot over a medium-high heat. Lightly brush
your tofu skewers with vegetable oil and add a few to the pan at a
time, making sure not to overcrowd them. Cook each batch for a
few minutes on each side until you get nice char lines.
Once they’ve got a nice bit of colour, pop your skewers under the
hot grill for 10 mins to finish them off. Meanwhile, thinly slice
the red chilli, chop the coriander and crush the peanuts in a pestle
and mortar.
Serve the tofu skewers with the satay sauce and pickled
cucumber and red onion. Garnish with the sliced red chilli, chopped
coriander and crushed peanuts.

name: Tofu Spinach Saag Curry
description: This is a vegan riff on saag paneer, an Indian dish using cheese and leafy greens. We’ve used tofu here which absorbs all the flavour from the spices perfectly and finished it off with a tarka. This one also has coconut milk, which is not traditional, but a creamy coconutty addition.
instructions: Cook the rice according to the instructions.
Finely chop the onion, peel and mince the garlic and ginger. Finely chop the chilli.
Bash the cardamom seeds and remove the pods. Crush the coriander and cumin seeds and the cardamom seeds in a pestle and mortar.

Heat vegetable oil in a large pot. Add the coriander and cardamom seeds to the oil and cook on a low heat for about 2 mins until it smells toasted and they are starting to brown. Add the chopped onion and cook for 5-7 mins until translucent, stirring often.
Add the garlic and ginger and half of the chilli. Stir and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant.

Add the spinach in and a good pinch of salt. If it doesn't all fit in the pan, let some cook down before adding more. Stir and cook on low until just wilted, try not to overcook it as you want to keep the brightness of the spinach.

Use an immersion blender, if you have one, or a food processor to blend the spinach into a chunky paste. Take care, as it can get a bit messy using an immersion blender, you may want to cover the pot with a tea towel. Pour the coconut milk, chilli powder, and garam masala into the pot with the spinach and stir to combine.

Cut the tofu down the middle on the thinner side, so you have two rectangular slabs. Then cut the slabs into small cubes. Add the tofu cubes to the coconut spinach and gently stir to heat through. Cook on a low-medium heat for about 10 mins, so that the flavour absorbs into the tofu. Taste and adjust the seasonings, spinach usually needs quite a lot of salt and pepper to bring out the flavour, especially when cooked.

Meanwhile, make the tarka. Finely slice the garlic. Heat your vegetable oil in a small saucepan. Add the garlic, remaining chopped chilli, curry leaves, mustard and cumin seeds to the hot oil. Fry for 2-4 mins, stirring often, until the garlic has just turned brown. Quickly remove the tarka from the hot pan as the ingredients will continue cooking and browning.
Serve the curry with the rice and the tarka on top. Finish with a squeeze of lime.

name: Tofu With Blistered Tomato & Pesto Lentils
description: A tomato and pesto situation teamed with oh-so perfect, golden tofu slices. The perfect 6-ingredient recipe, great for a low lift weeknight dinner.
instructions: Add the whole cherry tomatoes into a saucepan on medium-high heat with 2 tbsp of olive oil. Cook until starting to char, 5-7 mins.

Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice the onion. Add them to the tomatoes and cook until softened, 4-6 mins. Once the onions have softened, stir through the spinach until wilted. Then add the lentils and ¾ of the pesto. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Slice the tofu into 8 slices and pat dry, season with salt and pepper on both sides. Place another large frying pan onto medium-high heat with 5 tbsps of oil. Once hot, add the tofu and fry on both sides until golden, 4-6 mins.
Mix the remaining pesto with 20ml of olive oil.
Share the lentils between your bowls, top with tofu and a drizzle of pesto.

name: Tofu and Mushroom Dumplings
description: Dumplings can be a labour of love but, once you've got a knack for folding, they're fast to make (and eat). These are stuffed with fragrant tofu and mushroom
instructions: Soak your shiitake mushrooms in boiling water for 20 mins. Dice and save the liquid for another time.
Pour your flour and 65ml hot water into a bowl and mix until you have a shaggy dough. Knead until smooth, then cover in a damp tea towel and rest for 20 mins.
Finely slice your leek, dice your mushrooms, slice your spring onions, and grate your garlic and ginger.

Heat a little vegetable oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and add your leeks. Fry for 5 mins until softened, then add your mushrooms and turn up the heat. Fry until caramelised. Chuck in the ginger and garlic and cook out for 1 min, then add the shaoxing rice wine and let it reduce. Turn off the heat.
Crumble your tofu into the pan along with your diced shiitake mushrooms, spring onions, soy sauce, chinkiang vinegar and sesame oil. Give it a good mix and season to taste with salt.
Make a hole in the middle of your dough so it forms a doughnut shape, then twist so that it thins out evenly to about 1 ½ inch thickness. Cut into 12 even pieces.

Cover all but one of your dough pieces in a damp tea towel. Roll out your dough piece until it's an even circle, then place a heaped tsp of filling in the middle. Bring the two sides of dough together and pinch in the centre, then fold in 3 times on either side to seal your dumplings. Repeat with your remaining dough and filling.

Heat a little vegetable oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add your dumplings to the pan flat side down and pan fry for 2 mins until the bases have browned. Add a splash of water to the pan, then quickly place on a lid.
Steam for 8 mins, by which time the dough should be tender.
Serve with crispy chilli oil.

name: Tofu in Aromatic Tomato Sauce
description: This is one of my favourite meals I ate whilst in Vietnam and it couldn't be easier to replicate at home. The tomatoes are intensely savoury with lots of garlic and spring onions, it’s hard to believe something so simple can taste this good. (Switch out the fish sauce for soy sauce to make it plant-based).
keywords: Tofu in Aromatic Tomato Sauce recipe
instructions: Slice the tofu into 2cm pieces, then cut each piece in half diagonally into triangles. Toss with half the oil and a good pinch of salt and black pepper, then air fry at 180°C for 12-15 mins until golden. If using an oven, heat it to 200°C and cook for 15-18 mins.

Meanwhile, rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then add to a medium saucepan with the water and a big pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid and turn the heat down to low. Cook gently for 12 mins, then remove from the heat and leave to steam, still covered, for 10 mins before fluffing with a fork.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Slice the spring onion whites and roughly chop, then finely slice the greens into strips and set aside for garnish. Finely slice the garlic.

Heat the rest of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and spring onion whites and cook for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Add the tomato purée and cook for 1 min, then add the tomatoes and cook for 5 mins. Pour in the vegetable stock, then season with the fish sauce, a good grind of black pepper and the sugar. Simmer for 5-10 mins until the tomatoes have broken down and the sauce is rich and glossy. If your tomatoes are a little underripe, give them a good smoosh with the back of your spoon.

Add the tofu to the sauce and let everything bubble together for a couple of minutes. Taste and adjust with more fish sauce or sugar if needed. Serve the rice topped with the tomatoey tofu, scatter over the spring onion greens and fresh coriander, if using.

name: Tofu, Chickpea & Tempeh Spicy Noodle Soup
description: A cosy, protein-packed noodle bowl loaded with creamy tofu broth, crispy soy-braised tempeh, and spicy chickpeas. Big flavour.
instructions: Crumble the tempeh into a bowl and toss it with one-third of the soy sauce. Set a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry the tempeh for 5–7 mins until golden and crispy around the edges. Set aside.
Tip the silken tofu and water into a blender and blitz until smooth. Pour the mixture into a saucepan set over a medium heat.

Place the miso paste in a small sieve, dip it into the hot tofu broth, and use the back of a spoon to press it through until dissolved. Stir in the gochujang, remaining soy sauce and rice vinegar. Let it simmer gently for 3 mins, stirring to combine.
Meanwhile, bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Add the noodles and cook following pack instructions. Drain and set aside.
Finely slice the pak choi and spring onion. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan for 1–2 mins until fragrant, if using.
Add the chickpeas and pak choi to the broth and simmer for another 2 mins until heated through. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

To serve, divide the noodles between bowls. Ladle over the spicy broth, then top with the crispy tempeh. Finish with sliced spring onion, sesame seeds, chilli flakes (if using) and a drizzle of sesame oil.

name: Tom Kha Gai (Thai Coconut Chicken Soup)
description: A creamy aromatic Thai chicken soup with a comforting fragrant broth. A staple in Thai cooking and especially good for winter. You’ll love it.
instructions: Rinse and drain the rice in a sieve. Add to a medium pot with a tight fitting lid. Add water, to a ratio 1:1.25 rice to water, and a pinch of salt. Pop the lid on, turn the heat to low-medium and cook for 10 mins undisturbed, then reduce the heat to low for another 10 mins undisturbed. Fluff the rice with a fork and leave it to continue steaming with the lid on until needed.
Meanwhile, bash the lemongrass and remove the bottom stems and outer husks. Then slice the outer layer of the galangal.

Add the lemongrass and galangal husks and trimmings to a medium saucepan along with the unsalted chicken stock (or water if you prefer) and set it over a medium heat. Bring to a boil and leave for 5 mins to infuse, then turn off the heat. Quickly remove the husks with a sieve and add them to the cooking rice, making sure to place the lid back on the rice immediately.

Meanwhile, peel and finely chop the remaining lemongrass and cut the shallot into quarters. Smack the galangal with the back of the knife before finely slicing. Bruise the red chillies with the back of your knife. Peel the oyster mushrooms into shreds and slice the firm tofu into bite-size pieces. Slice the boneless chicken thighs into 1 inch strips, ensuring to remove any skin if needed.

Add the chicken thighs and salt to the stock and bring to a gentle simmer over a low-medium heat for 10 mins. Add the chopped and bruised aromatics, sugar, fish sauce, coconut milk and tear in ⅗ of the lime leaves then gently simmer for 3 mins. Then add the tofu, mushrooms, cherry tomatoes and baby corn and gently simmer for another 5 mins, or until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, pick the coriander leaves and roughly chop the stems and remaining lime leaves.

Squeeze in the lime juice and add the chopped coriander stems and lime leaves then season to taste (it may need another tbsp of fish sauce). Remove from the heat and leave to rest for 5 mins with the lid on before serving.
To serve, divide the aromatic rice between bowls, ladle over the soup and top with the coriander leaves.

name: Tom Yum Noodle Soup
description: A quick tom yum-inspired broth made with whatever veggies you've got hanging around. We've gone for mushrooms, greens and cherry tomatoes. This hot and sour noodle soup only takes 20 minutes to make.
instructions: Trim and bash the lemongrass stalk and galangal. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, peel the garlic and crush using the back of your knife.

Place a saucepan on medium heat with neutral oil. Once hot, cook the red Thai curry paste until fragrant, 1-2 mins. Add in the lemongrass, galangal, crushed garlic cloves and Makrut lime leaves. Pour in the stock, stir and let it come to a boil. Once boiling, place a lid on, turn the heat to medium-low and let infuse for 10-15 mins.
Meanwhile, trim and halve the green beans. Discard the stalks from the shiitake and thinly slice. Cook the rice noodles according to package directions.

Once the broth has infused, remove and discard the bits in it. Turn the heat up to medium-high and add the spring onion whites, green beans, cherry tomatoes and shiitake. Cook until the green beans are tender but still have a crunch, 3-4 mins. Remove from the heat and taste and season with lime juice and fish sauce.
Share the noodles between your bowls and pour over the soup base, making sure to share the veggies. Scatter over the spring onion greens and serve with any remaining lime wedges.

name: Tomatey Squash Chickpea & Feta Gnocchi
description: Golden roasted squash, chewy gnocchi, burst tomatoes and creamy feta. It's a winner for all the family.
keywords: butternut squash tomatoes chickpeas and feta gnocchi
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C. Pick the sage leaves, toss them with the olive oil and pop in the oven for 3 to 4 mins until crisp but not coloured. Remove the sage and set aside, leaving the oil in the tray.
Peel, deseed and cut the butternut into 1cm pieces. Drain the chickpeas.
Add the squash, garlic cloves (left in their skins) and gnocchi to the tray with the oil. Place the lemon half cut-side down. Roast for 20 mins, giving the tray a shake halfway through.
After 20 mins, add the cherry tomatoes, chickpeas and nestle in the feta. Roast for another 10 mins, or until the squash is tender and the tomatoes are starting to burst.
Squeeze the garlic from its skins, mash and fold it through the traybake.
Serve up!Kids Plate: Scoop out a kids’ portion, grate over some cheddar cheese.Parents Plate: Dish up the adults and crumble over half of the crispy sage and squeeze over the caramelised lemon.

name: Tomato & Almond Pesto
description: Making your own homemade red pesto is a rewarding way to spend your time.
instructions: Add the sun-dried tomatoes and red chilli to a blender with the smoked almonds. Peel the garlic clove and roughly slice the Parmesan, then add in. Add the harissa paste and lemon juice and season generously with salt and pepper.
Add ⅓ of olive oil and begin to blend, then continue to add olive oil until you get to a thick pesto consistency.

name: Tomato & Basil Pasta
description: I can’t think of a more perfect pasta for a balmy summer evening than this tomato and basil pasta. It’s not often that you can enjoy warm, chewy al dente spaghetti with the bright juiciness of a summer tomato in one forkful. Well, here’s your chance.
keywords: how to make tomato and basil pasta
how to make tomato and basil pasta sauce
instructions: Quarter the tomatoes, finely chop the red onion and tear the basil leaves, reserving a handful for later. Chuck the lot into your largest bowl with the olives and capers. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Add the vinegar and a shedload of good quality olive oil. The oil, vinegar, and tomato juice are going to be the backbone of your sauce, so don’t be shy. Walk away and leave to macerate for 25 mins.
Now cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente. This will take roughly 8-9 mins.
After 25 mins, the tomatoes will have released lots of delicious liquid into the bowl. Keep this, it’s liquid gold.
Crumble most of the feta into your tomato mixture. Add the cooked pasta and a ladle of hot pasta water.

Toss everything together, moving the tomatoes and feta through the pasta until everything is nicely coated. Add a splash of extra pasta water and a glug of olive oil if things need loosening up a little.
Divide between bowls and top with the remaining feta and basil leaves. Get stuck in.

name: Tomato & Chicken Salad With Croissant Croutons
description: If you're not putting croissant croutons in your salad, you're not living. This summery salad is incredible.
keywords: Tomato & Chicken Salad With Croissant Croutons
instructions:
Heat the oven to 160°C. Roughly chop the tomatoes into chunky wedges and
add to a large bowl. Sprinkle with salt and toss and set aside.

Drizzle the chicken with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Heat a large non-stick pan over a high heat. Add the chicken thighs to the pan and cook for 10-15 mins, until cooked through, set aside to cool.

Tear the croissants into large chunks and add to a baking sheet. Season with salt
and pepper then then slide into the oven for 10 mins – until golden and crisp-
you don’t need any oil.

Make the dressing by whisking the ingredients with 3 tbsp olive oil. Season with
salt and pepper.

Drain the tomatoes, then tip back into the bowl. Slice the chicken and add to
the bowl along with most of the basil leaves. Use a peeler to peel most of the
Parmesan into the bowl. Add half the dressing and then tip onto a platter.
Snuggle the croissant croutons into the salad. Drizzle the remaining dressing,
then finish with a pinch of chilli flakes, reserved basil leaves, Parmesan shavings
and a crack of black pepper.

name: Tomato & Chickpea Chaat Salad
description: A punchy no-cook salad packed with tomatoes, chickpeas, crunchy Bombay mix and a fresh coriander chutney. Chaat never looked so fresh.
instructions: Chop the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks. Chuck them onto a plate, season with salt and leave to sit while you prep everything else.
Thinly slice the red onion. Rinse it in a sieve under cold water to mellow out the flavour, then add into a bowl of ice water to crisp up.

For the chutney, pick the mint leaves and discard the stalks. Add the coriander (stalks and all), mint, chillies, ginger, ground cumin, water and ice cubes to a blender. Blitz until smooth, then season with lemon juice, salt, sugar and pepper. Stir through the yoghurt and taste again, it should be punchy and fresh.

Pick the remaining coriander leaves and finely slice the stalks. Mix the tamarind purée with the honey and season with salt. Add a splash of water to loosen if needed – you're after a sweet-sour dressing.
Drain the chickpeas and toss with the coriander stalks, drained onions, and tomatoes (with their juices) into the tamarind dressing.
Dollop the chutney yoghurt onto plates, pile the salad on top, then scatter over the Bombay mix for a big crunch finish.

name: Tomato & Chickpea Salad with Green Kefir Dressing
description: A nice, filling salad with a kefir-packed dressing that's so good you could drink it. This is what summer's all about.
keywords: Tomato & Chickpea Salad on Green Kefir Dressing
instructions: Scoop the avocado into a blender. Add the chives, half the basil leaves, anchovies and lime juice with the olive oil, blend until smooth. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the kefir into the dressing, giving it a quick whizz until mixed. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Set aside in the fridge.

Drain the chickpeas and add to a bowl. Trim and roughly cut the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks, then lightly salt them. Trim, halve and scoop the seeds out of the cucumber, then, chop into 1cm half moons, add to the chickpeas. Roughly chop the salted cashews.
In a small saucepan, add the oil with the cumin seeds and heat up. Once the cumin starts to shimmer, remove from the heat and stir the nuts and pul biber through. Let cool down slightly.
Pour the nutty chilli oil onto the chickpeas and cucumber. Stir through the molasses or glaze, tomatoes until coated.

Pour the yoghurt dressing onto the bottom of a sharing dish or plates and spoon over the tomato and chickpea salad, making sure to drizzle over the chilli oil. Scatter any remaining basil leaves over.
Store the leftovers in the fridge for 2-3 days for a speedy lunch or dinner.

name: Tomato & Feta Gnocchi
description: A really easy delicious dinner with soft pillowy gnocchi, tangy feta and sweet roasted cherry tomatoes. All cooked in one pan for easy cleanup.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Tip the cherry tomatoes and gnocchi into a large baking dish. Snuggle the feta into the middle. Sprinkle with the oregano and the chilli flakes. Season with salt and pepper and drizzle with the olive oil. Wrap the garlic bulb in foil and place on the side of the baking tray. Slide into the oven for 40 mins.
Remove from the oven, unwrap the garlic and snip off the top, then squeeze into the tray.

Add most of the basil and stir well, mixing the melted feta with the juicy tomatoes to make a smooth sauce, add a splash of water if it looks a little thick. Spoon into bowls, top with the remaining basil and a pinch of chilli flakes.

name: Tomato & Garlic Prawns with Beans
description: Juicy prawns, creamy beans and blistered tomatoes make this an incredible quick-fix dinner. Plus, crunchy sourdough to mop up all the good stuff.
instructions: Chuck the tomatoes into a large nonstick frying pan and set it over a medium-high heat. Let them cook for 8 to 10 mins, shaking the pan now and then, until they start to burst and char.

Peel and finely slice the garlic. Push the tomatoes to one side of the pan and add the anchovy oil to the other. Add the anchovy fillets and garlic, and cook for 1 min until the garlic is soft and the anchovies have melted into the oil.

Tip in the butter beans — juice and all — and stir everything together. Let it simmer for 3 mins until you’ve got a thick, saucy mix. Pick most of the basil leaves and stir them through, saving a few baby ones for garnish. Season to taste.
Heat a grill pan over a high heat. Spritz the prawns with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and grill for 2-3 mins on each side until lightly charred and opaque.
Spritz the sourdough with oil and toast in the grill pan until golden on both sides.
Spoon the beans into bowls, top with the prawns and scatter over the reserved basil leaves. Finish with chilli flakes if you fancy, and serve with the toast on the side for scooping.

name: Tomato & Mint Salad With Spicy Paprika Vinaigrette
description: A fresh and spicy salad with a gorgeous lip-tingling paprika vinaigrette. This has summer all over.
keywords: Tomato & Mint Salad With Spicy Paprika Vinaigrette
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C. Firstly, cut the tomatoes up - I like to halve some and slice others depending on the size and type. Put them in a sieve set over a bowl and season with salt, then set aside.

Tear the flatbread into pieces and chuck onto a baking sheet. drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper, then put in the oven for 10-12 mins. Roughly chop the sundried tomatoes and finely slice the red onion.
For the dressing add olive oil, paprika, honey, dijon, the juice of a lemon and chilli flakes to a jar, season generously with salt and pepper then seal with the lid and shake up until emulsified.

Add the tomatoes to a bowl with the sundried tomatoes, red onion, pitta chips and most of the mint leaves, before adding the dressing - give it a good toss and taste for seasoning. Serve up on a big platter and crumble over the feta if using, then scatter over the remaining mint leaves and toasted sesame seeds.

name: Tomato & Olive Baked Rice With Tzatziki
description: A simple baked rice dish with a homemade tzatziki that'll knock your socks off. It's fresh, cooling, and perfect for an instant dinner.
keywords: Tomato & Olive Baked Rice With Tzatziki
Tomato & Olive Baked Rice With Tzatziki recipe
instructions: Make the Greek Tomato Rice Traybake batch recipe.

Halve the cucumber lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Cut into strips and finely dice before adding to a bowl with the yoghurt. Grate in the garlic, then finely chop the mint and add that in too. Zest and juice the lemon into the yoghurt, then season with salt and pepper before giving it a good mix.

Get the rice base into a pot over a medium heat and add the spinach. Cover with a lid and stir occasionally until the spinach has wilted and the rice is piping hot. Serve the rice topped with the tzatziki and more fresh mint, if you like.

name: Tomato & Olive Brothy Rice with Pesto & Feta
description: Pesto and feta add an extra level of indulgence to our simple Greek Rice Tomato Traybake leftovers. Hungry?
keywords: Tomato & Olive Brothy Rice with Pesto & Feta
instructions: Make the Greek Tomato Rice Traybake batch recipe.
Get the leftover rice into a saucepan and add the canned tomatoes and stock. Bring to a gentle simmer, then taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with pesto and a scattering of crumbled feta.

name: Tomato & Peach Caprese Salad
description: This tomato and peach salad is pretty much summer on a plate. You don’t have to do much to make these ingredients taste amazing – just dress them with some polyphenol-rich extra virgin olive oil, season, and you’re done. The leftovers, which have more time to marinate, are arguably even more delicious so it’s a winner for taking to a picnic or making ahead of time for a barbecue with friends. The perfect no-recipe recipe to minimise your time in the kitchen and maximise being outside enjoying the good weather.
instructions: Cut the tomatoes and peaches into chunks (or slice them, depending on your preference) then add to a bowl with the basil leaves, salt, pepper and olive oil. Stir to combine.
Top with the mozzarella and an extra drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.

name: Tomato & Sardine Spaghetti
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad 

This speedy sardine pasta dish is a true lifesaver for busy weeknights. Utilizing simple store-cupboard ingredients, it delivers big flavours with minimal effort.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil.

Meanwhile, peel and slice your garlic cloves as finely as possible, set aside. Add a generous glug of olive oil to a frying pan over a low heat. Add the garlic along with the chilli flakes and sizzle for a minute, careful not to let the garlic burn.

Tip the tin of sardines into the pan and mush them up with a wooden spoon. Let it cook for a couple minutes more. Add some olive brine to the sardine tin, rinse off all the cling-ons and pop that into the sauce as well. Roughly chop the olives and add to the pan.
Whack the spaghetti into the now boiling pan of water and set a timer for 8 mins.
Grab your tin of plum tomatoes and add them to the sauce by squeezing them in your hands then cook for 5 mins further, if it’s a little too thick, you can add a little olive brine to loosen.
Roughly chop up your parsley and add most of it to the sauce, reserving a little for garnishing. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.

Once the timer goes off, use tongs to transfer the al dente spaghetti down into the pan of sauce, add a big splash of pasta water and continue to cook the pasta in the sauce until it’s cooked through and the sauce is coating the pasta, around 2 mins. If it looks a little dry, simply add more of the pasta water.
Plate up time. Twirl it onto serving plates and finish with the reserved parsley, a drizzle of olive oil and a crack of black pepper. BOOM.

name: Tomato Bulgur
description: A beautiful tomatoey bulgur base packed with goodness. Top it with your favourite proteins and dressings.
keywords: Smoky Chicken with Bulgur Bowl recipe
instructions: Pour the water and olive oil into a saucepan. Add the tomato purée and the pomegranate molasses, season with salt and bring the mixture to a boil.
Once boiling, tip the bulgur wheat in, let it come back to the boil, then cover and turn the heat down to low. Cook for 10 mins until the bulgur has absorbed the water.
Once absorbed, use a fork to fluff it up. Taste and season with the juice of a lemon and more salt, if needed.

name: Tomato Bulgur Wheat Salad with Crispy Paprika Chicken Legs
description: Juicy roast chicken legs, crusted in smoky paprika and spices, served over a punchy bulgur wheat salad with jammy cherry tomatoes, pomegranate, and fresh herbs. Tangy pomegranate molasses dressing and a cool herby yoghurt on the side.
keywords: Tomato Bulgur Wheat Salad with Crispy Paprika Chicken Legs
Tomato Bulgur Wheat Salad with Crispy Paprika Chicken Legs recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Drizzle the chicken legs with olive oil and season all over with the oregano, hot paprika, sumac and fine sea salt. Place on a large roasting tray and roast for 25 mins.
Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Tip in the bulgur wheat and cook for 10-12 mins until tender, then drain and leave to steam dry in the sieve for about 10 mins.

Set a frying pan over a medium heat with a large glug of olive oil. Add the tomato paste and chilli flakes and cook for about 5 mins, stirring, until the paste has darkened. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Halve the cherry tomatoes and add them to a large bowl. Season generously with salt and leave to sit — the salt will draw out the juices, which will help dress the bulgur. Finely slice the spring onions and roughly chop the mint and parsley.

In a separate large bowl, combine the cooked tomato paste with the pomegranate molasses, red wine vinegar, a tsp of salt and a glug of olive oil. Add the cooled bulgur wheat and mix until evenly coated. Tip in the tomatoes and their juices, the spring onions, herbs and pomegranate seeds. Toss everything together, taste and adjust the seasoning.

In the final 5 mins of the chicken's cooking time, remove the tray from the oven, press the pitta breads into the chicken juices at the bottom, then sit the chicken back on top. Return to the oven for the remaining 5 mins.
Remove the chicken and pitta from the roasting tray. Pour the chicken juices from the tray into the bulgur salad and mix well.

For the yoghurt sauce, very finely chop the parsley and mint and combine with the yoghurt, honey and red wine vinegar. Season with salt. Serve the bulgur salad with the chicken legs, pitta and yoghurt sauce alongside.

name: Tomato Butter Mafaldine with Gremolata
description: The pasta queen Rosie MacKean shows us a beautiful, simple pasta dish. Grated tomatoes and butter make a ridiculously tasty sauce, topped with punchy gremolata.
instructions: Using the coarse side of a box grater, grate the tomatoes straight into a saucepan, discarding the skin when you get to it. Add in your butter, then place the pan on a medium heat and bring to a simmer.
Cook gently for 10 mins, until the tomato has reduced a bit and intensified in flavour and colour, and the juice has emulsified with the butter. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Make your gremolata. Peel off your lemon zest with a peeler, then finely chop the zest. Peel and finely chop your garlic cloves. Very finely chop your parsley. Combine all the chopped ingredients together in a bowl. If you aren’t confident in chopping, you can use a fine microplane for the garlic and lemon zest.
Bring a large pan of water to the boil and season well with salt - taste it to make sure the seasoning is right. Once bubbling, add your mafaldine and stir well. Cook until al dente.

Keep the tomato butter on a low heat, and add some of the starchy pasta water to loosen the sauce about halfway through the cooking of the pasta. When the pasta is done, use tongs to transfer it straight into the pan of sauce, along with another ladleful of pasta water. Toss well to combine with the sauce and continue to cook, until the sauce comes back to the boil and is coating the pasta well.

Remove from the heat, then grate in your parmesan and mix, adding a bit more pasta water if necessary. Finally add 2 tbsp of gremolata and mix well. Serve immediately sprinkled with more gremolata and more parmesan. Enjoy.

name: Tomato Butter Pasta with Lentils & Whipped Ricotta
description: A rich, buttery pasta dish with nourishing lentils and indulgent creamy ricotta. Sounds luxurious but couldn’t be easier to make.
keywords: Tomato Butter Pasta with Lentils & Whipped Ricotta
instructions: Gently melt the butter in a medium pan over a medium heat. Cut the onion in half and cook cut side down in the butter for 3-4 mins until lightly coloured, then add the sage leaves and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Add the canned chopped tomatoes and chilli flakes and season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil and turn the heat down to a simmer and cook for around 15 mins until the tomato sauce has thickened. Remove the onion and sage from the sauce (they’ve done their work, infusing the sauce with lots of flavour).
Finely grate the Parmesan and blend or beat with the ricotta, olive oil and garlic until smooth, adding just a splash of water to give a more loose texture. Set aside.
Stir the lentils through the tomato sauce and check the seasoning, adding more salt, pepper and chilli flakes to taste.
Cook the pasta to al dente following pack instructions, then drain and stir into the tomato sauce.
Divide the pasta between bowls and top each portion with some of the whipped ricotta. Add a final pinch of chilli flakes and some extra grated Parmesan, if you like.

name: Tomato Cherry Salad
description: This refreshing tomato and cherry salad really hits the spot. Perfect with any type of protein it's the ultimate summery side dish.
instructions: Thinly slice the shallots into rounds, separating the rounds into individual rings. Tip into a bowl and add the vinegar. Set aside for 5 mins to quickly pickle.
Now it’s time to marinate the other veggies. Chop the tomatoes into random chunks and toss into a bowl. Thinly slice your courgette and add to the bowl. Pit the cherries and add to the bowl
Season well with salt and pepper. Tear in the dill and toss through olive oil, stir the shallots through the salad. Leave this to hang out for 30 mins.
Serve the salad with your favourite protein and base.

name: Tomato Chutney Recipe
description: This is our number one chutney to dip dosas into, but it’s also great with so many other things. Make a big batch, as it freezes very well and you'll always have some to hand.
instructions: Finely grate the garlic. Trim and finely dice the onion.
Add a drizzle of oil to a saucepan set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the mustard seeds, chana dal and urid dal, if using. Cook until toasted and the mustard seeds start to pop.

Add the garlic, onion, 1 dried red chilli and all the curry leaves. Cook, stirring, until fragrant. Pour in the canned tomatoes and stir the Kashmiri chilli powder through. Cook for 3-5 mins until thickened. Let the mixture cool completely, then transfer to a blender and blitz well (add a little water if required, plus salt to taste). Transfer to a serving bowl.

For the tempering, add the oil to a small saucepan and place over a medium heat. Once hot, add the mustard seeds. Once they start shimmering, add the urid dal, dried red chilli and curry leaves – be careful: the curry leaves will make the oil splatter. Pour the tempering over the tomato chutney before serving.

name: Tomato Curry
description: This is the easiest, freshest, and quickest tomato curry recipe you'll ever make. My mum can whip it up in under six minutes, and it's always a hit at home – see if you can beat her time! Bursting with rich, tangy flavours from fresh tomatoes, this curry is perfect for busy weeknights when you want something delicious without spending hours in the kitchen. The combination of simple ingredients like onions, garlic, and a blend of spices creates a satisfying dish that can be enjoyed on its own or served with rice or flatbreads. Whether you're a seasoned cook or new to the kitchen, this tomato curry recipe is foolproof and versatile. You can even customize it by adding your favourite veggies or proteins like chicken or tofu. It's the kind of recipe you'll turn to again and again for a comforting, flavorful meal in minutes. Enjoy! Seema x
instructions: Roughly chop the garlic and chop up the tomatoes into large chunks. Finely chop the coriander, including the stems.

Pour two large glugs of oil in a large pan, heat to high heat. Fry the cumin seeds until they start to pop. Add in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until lightly browned. Add in the tomatoes, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, and ½ tsp salt. Stir gently to not break the tomatoes.

Cook for 2 minutes until the tomatoes are just warmed through, you want to keep them whole and not broken down. Stir in the coriander and serve on rice or with rotli/roti/chapati (whichever is your naming preference).

name: Tomato Curry Egg Drop Rice
description: When I am home, tired, hungry and need something quick and nourishing I make this. A take on a classic Hong Kong dish, with a little spice and inspired by Lucas Sin’s egg drop method.
keywords: Tomato Curry Egg Drop Rice recipe
instructions: For perfect fluffy white rice - rinse the rice in a sieve under cold tap water, and shake off as much excess water possible. Tip the rice into a heavy-bottomed pot, with a 1 : 1 ¼ ratio of rice to cold water and a good pinch of salt. Turn the heat to medium low, add a tight fitted lid and boil for 10 mins. Reduce to the lowest heat and cook for another 10 mins. Turn the heat off and leave to steam for 5 mins, before fluffing the rice. Always keep the rice covered, unless serving, or your rice will be dry.

Slice the tomatoes into ¼ wedges (optionally - boil the tomatoes whole, with a 'X' sliced into its bottom, for 30 seconds, then remove to cool and peel the skins before slicing into ¼ , to make a smooth sauce, but this is not necessary). Now mince the garlic, and slice the spring onions into chunks, saving the green parts for garnish.
Combine all the stock ingredients into a jug and mix well. Then in another bowl whisk the egg mixture. Lastly, combine the slurry ingredients in a small cup and set everything aside.

In medium-sized saucepan over a high heat, add a splash of oil and fry the garlic and spring onion for 30 seconds, then add curry powder, tomato purée and tomato wedges with a pinch of salt and toss well. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 2-3 mins or until the tomatoes get jammy.

Pour in the stock mixture and bring to a simmer, cook for 6 mins, then give the cornstarch slurry a quick mix with your finger, before drizzling into the sauce. Gently mix, to make sure not to break the tomatoes too much and cook for 1 minute.

Now drizzle the egg mixture into the pan, creating circular motions and let it simmer for 1 minute then reduce the heat to the lowest fire. Use a spatula to drag three gentle folds of silky ribboned pieces of egg. Add a lid and cook for 1 more minute.
Lastly, drizzle toasted sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds and the spring onions greens to garnish. Use a large serving spoon to gently scoop the tomato curry over some fresh rice to serve

name: Tomato Egg Noodles
description: This homestyle dish is a staple in any Chinese household. I grew up eating it quite often when Mum was in a rush. It's like a warm hug in a bowl, packed with flavour and simplicity. This dish is typically served with rice, but I actually prefer it with noodles!
instructions: Set a pot of water over a medium-high heat and bring to the boil. Add the noodles and cook following pack instructions. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent them from sticking.
Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes into 3cm pieces. Mince the garlic and slice the spring onion, separating the whites and greens.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl and season with salt and white pepper.

Add half of the vegetable oil to a pan or wok set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the eggs. Stir until lightly scrambled, then push the cooked eggs to the side of the pan. Add the rest of the vegetable oil, the tomatoes, garlic and spring onion whites. Fry for a few mins until the tomatoes are softened.
Combine all the sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Add to the pan with the eggs and tomatoes, turn the heat to low-medium and fry for a few mins. Add the spring onion greens and mix well.
Serve the stir-fried tomato and eggs on top of the noodles, with a drizzle of chilli oil on top.

name: Tomato Salad With Jalapeño Caesar Dressing
description: A nice and spicy salad that you can throw together in a couple of minutes. Big on umami, this one.
keywords: Tomato Salad With Jalapeño Caesar Dressing
instructions: Roughly chop/slice the tomatoes, season with salt and put in a sieve over a bowl to catch the juice. For the dressing, peel the garlic, finely chop the pickled jalapeños.
Add the garlic to a pestle and mortar (if you don't have one use a blender or just finely chop everything), smash the garlic then add the anchovies, smooshing them into a paste.

Add the jalapeños and keep smooshing until it comes together, then add the mayo and the lemon zest before juicing in half of the lemon – taste and adjust with the remaining lemon juice if needed. Grate in the Parmesan. Give it a good season with some black pepper and taste again. If you think it needs salt, add it.

Peel the courgette into ribbons and finely slice the fresh jalapeño. Arrange the tomatoes and courgette ribbons on a serving platter. Drizzle with the dressing, scatter with basil, crunchy corn and Parmesan shavings.

name: Tomato Salad with Whipped Peanut Butter & Salsa Macha
description: Fresh tomato salads are a barbecue staple, and this one is extra special. You serve those juicy guys on whipped peanut butter, and top it with a salsa macha- a beautifully spicy, peanutty concoction. Plate lickingly nice.
keywords: tomato salad with peanut butter and salsa macha
instructions: Toast your dried chillies in a dry frying pan for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Pop them in a food processor and whizz them to a powder.
Finely slice your cloves of garlic. Finely chop your peanuts.
Heat a generous glug of olive oil in a small frying pan. Add your garlic and peanuts, then cook very gently for a few mins until your garlic is very lightly golden.
Tip in your powdered chilli and stir carefully to combine. Allow to cool for 10 mins.
Prep your tomatoes. Cut them into rough chunks, then pop them in a sieve set over a bowl. Season generously with salt and pepper, then leave to sit.

Pop your peanut butter into a bowl. Add the water, and the zest and juice of your lime. Whisk to a smooth paste. It will be lumpy at first, but will turn smooth in not too long. Season to taste with salt.
Add your apple cider vinegar and pinch of salt to your salsa macha.
Spread your whipped peanut butter on the plate, then top with your tomatoes. Sprinkle with your salsa macha, then serve.

name: Tomato Sandwich With Miso Butter Bean Hummus & Crispy Chilli Oil
description: Nothing hits the spot like a simple tomato sandwich. Using in-season beef tomatoes ensures the best eating experience.
keywords: Tomato Sandwich With Miso Butter Bean Hummus & Crispy Chilli Oil
Tomato Sandwich With Miso Butter Bean Hummus & Crispy Chilli Oil recipe
instructions: To make the hummus, drain the butter beans, reserving half of the water from the jar. Add the reserved water, butter beans, tahini, lime juice, miso and sesame oil to a high speed blender and blend until smooth. You’ll have hummus leftover, keep it in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Drizzle a frying pan with a little olive oil and heat on medium heat. Toast one side of all your bread slices, until golden. Set aside.
Slice the tomatoes into thick pieces and thinly slice the onion.

Spread the non-toasted side of one slice of bread generously with the hummus, then top with onion and plenty of mint and parsley. Add the tomatoes to the other side and season them with salt and pepper, then a drizzle of tahini and crispy chilli oil. Close the sandwich carefully and enjoy.

name: Tomato Soup
description: Nothing beats a bowl of homemade soup. This recipe for cream of tomato soup is an absolute classic. You’ll never touch the tinned stuff again.
instructions: Peel the onion and carrot and dice into 1cm cubes. Add the butter to a large saucepan over a medium heat, then add the onion and carrots along with a big pinch of salt. Fry gently for 10 mins until softened.

Finely chop the garlic and add it to the pan along with the tomato paste and fry for 2 more min. Add the tomatoes and use your spoon to break them up in the pan, refill one of the cans of tomatoes with water and add to the pan along with the stock cube and the sugar. Bring to the boil, then turn to a simmer and cook for 40 mins.
Use a stick blender to blitz into a smooth purée, taste, and season with the vinegar. Add the cream and gently reheat.
Tip into bowls and top with a pile of grated cheddar cheese and splashing of Worcestershire sauce. Finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Tomato Tart With Whipped Feta & Peppery Watercress Salad
description: Flaky puff pastry topped with spiced tomatoes. Finished with a nutty gremolata and tangy whipped feta – a quick and impressive weeknight dinner.
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into 1cm slices. Place them in a colander or sieve and toss with ½ tsp of salt. Let it sit until ready to use (this will draw out excess moisture from the tomatoes). Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Unroll the puff pastry sheet and lightly score a 2cm border around the edges. Using a fork, prick the pastry inside the border. Once the oven is hot, par-bake the puff for 10-15 mins until lightly golden and puffy. Once par-baked, using a spoon, gently press the pastry down, leaving the border puffy.

Meanwhile, crumble the feta into a small food processor or blender, add the Greek yoghurt and 2 tbsp of olive oil. Blitz until broken down and fluffy. Season with lemon zest and pepper. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.

Peel and thinly slice the onion. Pat the tomato slices dry, and place them into a clean bowl with the onion and ras el hanout, toss together. Add the spiced tomato mixture onto the pastry, making sure to not get any on the border. Drizzle with another 1 tbsp of olive oil and bake for another 10-15 mins, until the pastry is golden brown.

For the gremolata: Tip the toasted almonds onto a chopping board and roughly chop. Finely chop the parsley (stalks and all), then tip the almonds and parsley into a small bowl with the juice of the zested lemon and 70ml of olive oil. Season with salt, mix together and set aside.
