Meanwhile, add the juice of the remaining lemon into a large bowl. Whisk in 40ml of olive oil, season with salt, pepper and sugar (if needed).
Cut the tart into 8 and share between your plates. Dollop the whipped feta onto the tart and drizzle over the nutty gremolata. Toss the watercress into the lemon dressing and serve alongside.

name: Tomato, Caper and Pine Nut Spaghetti
description: Think of this sweet-and-sour pasta dish as puttanesca's vegan little sister. Packed with incredible savoury flavour in a matter of minutes. A total delight.
instructions: Toast your pine nuts in a dry frying pan until golden. Set aside until later.
Slice your garlic and finely chop your parsley, including your stalks. Halve your cherry tomatoes.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Salt generously, then add your spaghetti. Cook until al dente.

Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a glug of olive oil, then tip in your sliced garlic, chilli flakes and parsley stalks. Fry over a gentle heat for a couple of mins until your garlic is fragrant, but not yet changing colour.
Add your cherry tomatoes to the pan and simmer for 3 mins, breaking up with the back of your spoon as you go.
Tip in your raisins, capers and red wine vinegar, then stir to combine.
Ladle some pasta water from the pot into your veg pan and let it bubble up.

Add your spaghetti and toss until evenly coated, adding more pasta water until you have a glossy emulsion which coats your pasta. Sprinkle in your parsley leaves and add your pine nuts back to the pan. Season with salt, then give it one last mix.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Tomato, Shallot & Olive Chicken with Orzo & Feta
description: A banging, high-protein feast that’s pure Mediterranean sunshine - sweet cherry tomatoes, olives and crispy herby chicken.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.

Zest the lemon into a bowl. Add the chilli flakes, oregano, a big pinch of salt, some black pepper and a generous drizzle of olive oil. Rub all over the chicken thighs and set aside to marinate while you prep the rest.

Halve the cherry tomatoes, peel and halve the shallots, then chuck both into a roasting tray with the olives. Season, drizzle with olive oil and toss to coat. 
Nestle the chicken thighs skin-side up on top of the veg. Roast for 35–40 mins until the chicken is golden and cooked through, and the tomatoes are soft and jammy.
Meanwhile, cook the orzo following pack instructions. Drain, season with olive oil, salt and pepper, and set aside.
Thinly slice the red onion. Squeeze over the juice of half the lemon and a pinch of salt. Leave to lightly pickle for 5 mins, then stir through the chopped parsley.
Remove the chicken and shallots from the tray and stir the roasted tomatoes, olives and all those lovely juices through the orzo.
Divide the orzo between bowls, top with the chicken, shallots, pickled onions and crumbled feta. Enjoy!

name: Tomato-Braised Chicken Meatballs & Spaghetti
description: Polpette di pollo al sugo (aka chicken meatballs in tomato sauce) is a deceptively simple dish that the whole family can get behind. You won't find a better spaghetti and meatballs recipe.
instructions: Finely chop the parsley and add to a mixing bowl along with the remaining meatball ingredients. Mix well.
Roll pinches of the mixture into meatballs about 2.5cm in diameter and place them onto a tray.

Place a large saucepan over a medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and fry the meatballs on all sides until golden brown. Remove and set aside. Depending on the size of your pan you might need to do this in two batches.

Add another splash of oil to the pan with the whole peeled garlic cloves. Fry for 1 min until golden, then add the basil and chilli and sizzle for 30 seconds before pouring in the tomatoes and a pinch of salt.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and, after 5 mins, return the meatballs to the pan and let everything cook together for 20 mins.
While the meatballs cook, put the pasta on to boil in plenty of salted water. Time this step so that the pasta will be ready around the same time as the meatballs.
Drain the pasta and use three-quarters of the tomatoes that the meatballs cooked in as a sauce, mixing well and adding extra Parmesan.

Serve the meatballs and pasta with the remaining sauce on the side, as well as a green salad or veggies and a slice of bread for mopping-up. Alternatively, swap the pasta for rice and serve the meatballs and sauce on top.

name: Tomatoey Butter Beans & Cheese
description: A delicious centrepiece for everyone to dive into! If you like beans, this is your guy. We used vegan cheese but feel free to sub it with whatever you want.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Get the tomatoes in an oven-proof dish, drizzle with plenty of olive oil, a good pinch of salt and put them in the preheating oven.

Finely dice the shallots and garlic. In a hot pan, sauté ¾ the shallots in olive oil with a dash of salt for a couple of minutes. Follow with garlic for a minute or so, stirring regularly. Pour in the beans and their juice and add in the stock cube. Mix well, let simmer for 15 mins until thick. If it looks too dry add a splash of water.
Finely chop the herbs. Mix together the remaining shallots with the herbs, lemon juice, salt and enough olive oil to make it a dropping consistency.
Once the tomatoes are slightly bursting and juicy, pour them on top of the beans, along with their juices. Plop the cheese in the middle and drizzle over the herby salsa. Dive in with bread.

name: Tomatoey Gochujang & Sweet Onion Noodles
description: Soft, silky noodles tossed in a our Gochujang Tomato & Sweet Onion Sauce, finished with a punchy herby sesame topping. Fast, spicy and bloomin' delicious.
category: Gochujang Tomato & Sweet Onion Sauce Recipes
keywords: Tomatoey Gochujang & Sweet Onion Noodles recipe
instructions: Before you begin, make the Gochujang & Sweet Onion Sauce.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Once boiling, drop in the noodles and cook following pack instructions.
Meanwhile, make the herb salad. Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the spring onions. Toss both into a bowl with the sesame seeds.

When the noodles are cooked, reserve 100ml of the cooking water, then drain. Tip the noodles back into the pan with the Gochujang Tomato & Sweet Onion Sauce. Set over a low heat and stir to coat, loosening with a splash of the cooking water at a time, if needed.
Stir the rice vinegar through the herb salad.
Divide the noodles between bowls and finish with a generous pile of the herby sesame topping.

name: Tomatoey Harissa Couscous Pots
description: You can make these simple harissa couscous in next to no time. Just add water and you'll have an instant lunch on your hands.
instructions: Finely chop the onion and the sun-dried tomatoes. Drain the chickpeas.
Add a quarter of the harissa and tomato purée along with a drizzle of the sun-dried tomato oil into the bottom of each container with some salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
Layer a quarter of the couscous over the harissa sauce and then a quarter of the rest of the ingredients.
When you are ready to eat, add 240ml of boiling water per pot. Stir and tip out onto a plate, give it a stir and enjoy.

name: Tomatoey Lentil Stew
description: A cosy, tomato-packed lentil stew that’s perfect for little ones and grown-ups alike. Great for batch-cooking and freezer stash dinners.
instructions:
1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids Servings
Finely chop the onion, thinly slice the garlic and finely dice the courgette.
Heat the olive oil in a large lidded saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the onion, garlic and courgette and cook for 5-6 mins until softened.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 1 min until darkened slightly.
Add the red lentils and mix well. Pour in the tinned cherry tomatoes and the water. Season with a pinch of salt.
Cover with a lid and simmer gently for 40-45 mins, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the stew is rich and thick.
Serve up!Kids Plate: Dish up as is.Parents Plate: Top with crumbled feta, a drizzle of harissa and some chopped parsley.

name: Tomatoey Tahini Noodle Salad
description: The perfect speedy dinner with the best of summer produce as the hero. Salting the tomatoes first concentrates their flavour, whilst the juices are added to an addictive sesame sauce for an extra umami flavour. It's one of my favourites and I think it might become yours too.
instructions: Halve the cherry tomatoes and add to a sieve set over a bowl or jug. Season with salt and set aside for 20 mins to let the juices collect.

Meanwhile, cook the noodles according to the pack instructions, then drain, rinse under cold water and leave to cool. Finely grate the garlic and finely chop the parsley, keeping a little back for garnish.

Add the tahini to a large bowl with the harissa, garlic, most of the parsley, the honey, red wine vinegar and the collected tomato juice. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon, then season with salt and pepper and mix well to form a paste. Loosen with the iced water until it's the consistency of double cream. Taste and add more harissa if you fancy an extra kick - not all harissa is made equal.
Add the noodles and tomatoes to the dressing and toss to coat. Divide between plates and finish with the reserved parsley and sesame seeds.

name: Tomatoey Tahini Noodle Salad
description: The perfect speedy dinner with the best of summer produce as the hero. Salting the tomatoes first concentrates their flavour, whilst the juices are added to an addictive sesame sauce for an extra umami flavour. It's one of my favourites and I think it might become yours too.
instructions: Halve the cherry tomatoes and add to a sieve set over a bowl or jug. Season with salt and set aside for 20 mins to let the juices collect.

Meanwhile, cook the noodles according to the pack instructions, then drain, rinse under cold water and leave to cool. Finely grate the garlic and finely chop the parsley, keeping a little back for garnish.

Add the tahini to a large bowl with the harissa, garlic, most of the parsley, the honey, red wine vinegar and the collected tomato juice. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon, then season with salt and pepper and mix well to form a paste. Loosen with the iced water until it's the consistency of double cream. Taste and add more harissa if you fancy an extra kick - not all harissa is made equal.
Add the noodles and tomatoes to the dressing and toss to coat. Divide between plates and finish with the reserved parsley and sesame seeds.

name: Tortilla Fried Chicken Sandwich
description: Chunkz came to the studio to cook his killer crispy chicken sando. Crispy tortilla chip-crusted chicken, corn and feta slaw, chipotle mayo, what's not to love?
instructions: Start by prepping some slaw. Rub your corn with oil, then char it in a hot griddle pan until nice and charred. Cut the corn off the kernels.
Peel your cabbage with a vegetable peeler to get very fine shreds. Finely slice your spring onions. Finely chop the coriander and pickled jalapeños.

Add your corn, cabbage and spring onions to a bowl. Pour the chilli brine and squeeze in your lime juice. Season with salt, then toss with your hands, massaging the dressing into the veg slightly to soften it. Add the coriander and crumble in your feta.
Combine the chipotle paste and mayonnaise in a bowl. This is your chipotle mayo.
On to the chicken. Blitz your tortilla chips to a powder in the food processor.
Prep your chicken. Slice each chicken breast vertically down the middle so that you have two slim fillets.
Lay your chicken pieces flat under a piece of cling film, and bash to even out to a thin piece with a rolling pin.
Place your flour, eggs and tortilla chip crumbs in a bowl each. Season your flour with your smoked paprika, salt and pepper.
Dip your chicken fillets into the flour, egg and tortilla chips respectively until they are totally coated.
Toast your burger buns in a dry frying pan.
Heat a good glug of olive oil in a large frying pan. Add a few chicken pieces at a time and fry for a couple of minutes on each side. Place on a plate lined with paper towel whilst you fry the rest.
Spoon some chipotle mayo onto the base of the bun. Top with your chicken piece and a handful of slaw. Spread some more chipotle mayo on the top of the bun, then pop this on top. Serve and enjoy.

name: Traybake Courgette, Lemon & Mint Salad
description: Quickly roasting courgettes in a hot oven gives them a lovely texture for this easy, fresh salad.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Chop the courgettes into uneven chunks about 5cm thick. Place on a large baking tray and toss with 1 heaped tsp salt and half of the olive oil.
Roast in the oven for 10 mins, shaking halfway, until the courgettes are golden on the edges and have softened but still have bite. Meanwhile, cook the bulgur or couscous following pack instructions.
Combine the sumac, honey, chilli flakes (if using) and zest and juice of half of your lemons with the rest of the olive oil and a pinch of salt in a small bowl to make a dressing. Set aside.

Remove the courgettes from the oven and leave to cool for 5 mins, then toss with the dressing while they’re still warm. Stir through the cooked bulgur or couscous. Leave to sit and soak while you get everything else ready.

Add the Greek yoghurt to a bowl and grate in the garlic. Finely chop and add half of the mint leaves, the zest and juice of the remaining lemon, a big pinch of salt and a few grinds of black pepper. Mix well.
You can either plate this up as one big sharing dish, or on individual plates. Either way, spread the garlic yoghurt across the plate and then pile over the courgettes and bulgur.

Place a small pan over a medium heat, add the butter and pine nuts and let it foam and sizzle. After a minute, add the chilli and mint leaves, cook for another 20 seconds and then pour over the courgettes.

name: Traybake Orange Chicken Noodles
description: Crispy chicken, roasted cabbage, and sticky orange-soy sauce all tangled through noodles. There's nothing like a traybake.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Chop the cabbage into 2–3cm chunks. Chop the spring onion whites into 2cm pieces and thinly slice the greens. Thinly slice the chicken breasts, then toss in a bowl with the cornflour. Season well with salt and pepper.

Pour half the olive oil into a large baking tray and tilt to coat the base and sides. Tip in the chicken, cabbage and spring onion whites, drizzle over the remaining oil and season with salt and pepper, toss together. Slide into the oven for 10–15 mins, until the veggies have softened and the chicken is cooked.
Meanwhile, finely grate the garlic and ginger into a small bowl. Add the orange juice, soy sauce, vinegar, honey and cornflour. Stir to combine, then taste and season if needed.
Once the traybake is cooked, toss through the noodles and sauce. Return to the oven for another 5–10 mins until everything is hot and coated in the thickened sauce.
Toss once more before serving the noodles between plates. Finish with a scattering of spring onion greens.

name: Traybake Tomato & Chicken Curry
description: Crispy skinned chicken baked in a rich, deeply spiced tomato curry sauce. Bold flavour, minimal prep and exactly what you want when you need a comforting dinner with serious punch.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Finely dice the onion. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems. Finely grate the ginger and garlic. Season the chicken all over with salt and pepper.
Place a large ovenproof frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of Olive Oil. Add the chicken skin-side down and cook for 10-15 mins until the skin is golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, add the curry powder, garam masala, grated ginger, grated garlic, tomato purée and chicken stock to a blender and blitz until smooth.
Transfer the chicken to a plate, skin-side up.
Put the pan back over a medium heat. Add the onion, coriander stems and curry leaves with a pinch of salt and cook for 4-5 mins until softened and translucent.

Pour in the blended sauce along with the cherry tomatoes. Bring to the boil, then nestle the chicken back into the pan, skin-side up. Slide into the oven for 20-25 mins until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Reheat the rice following pack instructions if needed. Spoon between bowls, top with the chicken and plenty of sauce, then finish with the coriander leaves.

name: Treacle & Mustard Glazed Air Fryer Roast Beef
description: Roast Beef in an airfryer? Trust us, this recipe makes the most succulent centerpiece that's bound to impress all your family and friends.
keywords: Treacle & Mustard Glazed Air Fryer Roast Beef Recipe
Treacle & Mustard Glazed Air Fryer Roast Beef
instructions: Remove the beef from the fridge 30 mins before you plan to start cooking.
Line the air fryer basket with foil and set the heat to 205°C for 5 mins to heat up. Pour the oil over the beef and spread so it’s even, then season with plenty of salt and pepper.
Put the beef onto the foil, fat-side up, and air fry for 10 mins until the fat is starting to crisp.
Turn the heat down to 170°C and cook for 20 mins.
Combine the treacle and mustard in a small bowl, then paint it all over the joint of beef.
Return the beef to the air fryer for a final 15 mins, or until the internal temperature reaches 55°C on a digital thermometer.
Transfer the beef to a plate, spreading over any glaze left from the foil. Loosely cover with foil and rest for 15 mins before carving into slices.

name: Triple Asparagus Spaghetti
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

This spaghetti is something really special. If you're a fan of asparagus, cheese, and pasta - which, let's face it, most of us are - this one is going to be right up your street.
instructions: Finely slice the bottom ⅓ of the asparagus and add to a bowl with half of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, then set aside.
Cut the rest of the asparagus into 2 cm pieces, separating the tips to the side.
Peel and finely slice the garlic. Heat oil in a pan over a medium heat and add the middle parts of the asparagus and the sliced garlic. Fry for 3 minutes.
Add the fried asparagus and garlic to a blender with the spinach and mascarpone. Blend smooth and season with salt and pepper.

Put a large pot of salted water on to boil and cook spaghetti according to package instructions. Before draining, reserve the pasta water in a jug. Heat the rest of the oil in the frying pan and fry the asparagus tips for 1-2 min over a high heat until charred.
Add the sauce to the drained spaghetti along with the asparagus tips and the rest of the lemon juice. Add a nice slosh of the pasta water and mix well to emulsify.
Top with grated Parmesan, torn basil and the pickled asparagus stems.

name: Triple Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Yeh, chocolate chip cookies are great... but TRIPLE CHOCOLATE CHIP cookies... so much better.
instructions: Melt the butter in a large mixing bowl, allow to cool to room temp.

Mix the flour, baking powder and bicarbonate of soda together with a pinch of salt. Chop the chocolate into chunks, don't chop them up not too small, having larger chunks is key to getting melty cookies.
Combine the melted butter, sugar, vanilla, egg and yolk. Mix well.

Combine the dry and wet ingredients to make the cookie dough, then add the chocolate chips, make sure to mix well so they’re well dispersed. Chill the mix in the fridge for around 30 mins until firm to the touch.

Line 2 baking trays with baking paper. Roll the cookie dough into clementine-sized balls, then flatten slightly into thick pucks. I like to make sure there are good chunks of chocolate on the top of each so you can see the melty chunks! Lie on the baking trays, spacing them 7cm-10cm apart (if you only have one tray, bake them in batches) and put back into the fridge for at least 30 mins (you can leave them for a couple of hours if you have time!) Heat the oven to 170°C.

Bake for 13-15 mins, the middle should look underbaked! Add a pinch of flaky sea salt whilst they’re still hot! If they've spread a lot, use an upside down bowl to gently push the edges of the cookie in, this can help create a more rounded cookie! Set aside for 15 mins to cool then tuck in.

name: Triple Chocolate Chip Muffins
description: What’s not to love about a chocolate chip muffin? We love an assortment of dark, milk and white, but feel free to choose your favourite choc chips. Once baked these muffins will keep for three days in an airtight container, or freeze individually instead.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a muffin tray with 12 paper cases.
Melt the butter, then leave to cool slightly.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt together in a large bowl. Crack the eggs into a separate bowl, add the yoghurt and melted butter, then whisk to combine.

Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and use a spatula to just bring the muffin batter together (it’s fine if not completely smooth), then gently fold through 200g of the chocolate chips – you don’t want to overmix, as this makes your muffins heavy.
Divide the batter evenly between the muffin cases, then sprinkle over the remaining chocolate chips.

Bake on the middle shelf of the oven for 5 mins, then turn the heat down to 160°C and bake for a further 18-20 mins until risen, golden brown and a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. Eat warm or cold – you do you.

name: Triple Chocolate Gloop
description: A decadent chocolate drink that’s ideal for the holiday season. It’s like an adult milkshake.
ingredients: 50ml Ballycastle Chocolate, Hazelnut & Caramel Flavour Country Cream
instructions: Finely chop your dark chocolate, then rim your martini glass with the sauce and dunk it in the chocolate shavings to create a double chocolate rim.
Using the sauce create a swirl pattern, or go artistic and make any pattern you like, on the inside of the glass.
In a blender, add your chocolate ice cream, Ballycastle Blonde Chocolate Cream Liqueur, Ballycastle Chocolate, Hazelnut & Caramel Flavour Country Cream, and whiskey.
Blend until smooth.
Pour into your glass and garnish with some more of the chocolate shavings if you're feeling wild.

name: Triple Honey Mustard Dressing
description: A sweet and tangy dressing made with three different types of mustard. Perfect for pouring over a crunchy green salad.
instructions: Combine the mustards, vinegar and honey in a mixing bowl. Stir to combine before adding the olive oil and seasoning well with salt and pepper.

name: Triple Lemon & Za’atar Rigatoni
description: This pasta dish has got a lovely citrus lift. The combination of za'atar and preserved lemons make it incredibly moreish.
instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Peel and finely slice the garlic and finely chop the preserved lemon half, removing any pips.

Place a large frying pan over a high heat. Slice a lemon in half, then place it cut side-down into the pan, leave for 2 mins, until blackened, then remove the lemon halves and set aside. Drop the rigatoni into the boiling water and cook according to package instructions.

Turn the heat down to medium and add 2 tbsp of olive oil. Add the sliced garlic and fennel seeds and sizzle for 2 mins, then add the preserved lemon. Cook for 30 secs or so, then add the crème fraîche and juice of the second lemon. Stir to combine then remove from the heat until the pasta is ready.

Use a slotted spoon to transfer the pasta into the lemony sauce. Grate the Parmesan straight into the pan, place over a medium heat and toss to combine, until the sauce is coating the pasta. Spoon into bowls and top with black pepper, za’atar and dill. Cut the charred lemon into wedges to serve.

name: Triple Lemon Chickpeas
description: Chickpeas with a zip. If you're into fresh and vibrant veggie-forward dinners then you'll really vibe with this.
instructions: Place a large frying pan over a medium high heat. Slice the lemon in half horizontally and place one half, cut-side down in the pan, cook for 3-4 mins, until charred. Remove and set aside.

Peel and finely slice the garlic. Finely chop the preserved lemon. Give the pan a clean, then return to the heat. Add a splash of olive oil, then add the garlic and fennel seeds. Sizzle for a minute, then add the preserved lemon. Add the chickpeas and their liquid to the pan. Season with salt and turn up the heat to high. Bubble for 5-10 mins, until most of the water has evaporated. Stir in the crème fraîche and finely grate in the Parmesan. Bubble until the sauce is coating the chickpeas, then stir in the spinach.
Add the juice of the charred lemon and the remaining uncharred lemon. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Spoon into bowls, top with za’atar and mint and a drizzle of olive oil to serve.

name: Triple Tomato Salad with Lemongrass & Sesame Saté
description: This salad is lovely and refreshing. Get your toms out and make something delicious.
instructions: Halve the cherry tomatoes and transfer to a bowl along with the rice vinegar and a big pinch of salt. Set aside for at least 1 hr, but preferably overnight. Cut the big tomatoes into wedges, pop into a sieve and sprinkle with salt. Let them hang out until you’re ready to plate up.

Blitz 2 of the spring onions and the garlic together in a food processor. Heat the neutral oil in a frying pan over a low heat. Once shimmering, add the garlic and spring onion mixture, then cook gently for 3 mins.

Meanwhile, blitz the lemongrass in the same food processor. Add the lemongrass to the pan with the garlic and spring onion mixture, then cook for 5 mins. Finely slice the chillies and add to the pan along with the chilli flakes and sesame seeds. Cook for 5 mins, then remove from the heat and add the soy sauce. Set aside until serving.

Finely slice the remaining spring onion. Tear most of the burrata onto a plate, top with all the tomatoes (including the sundried tomatoes), then layer with more burrata. Drizzle with the lemongrass saté and scatter with the spring onion. Serve with bread for scooping.

name: Triple Tomato Spaghetti
description: A beautiful plate of tomato pasta. It's simple, classy, and delicious. You won't find a more satisfying weeknight dinner.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the garlic. Heat a splash of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, add the garlic and sizzle for 2 mins until a little softened, then add the tomato purée and stir well. Cook for a min until the paste takes on a slightly darker colour then add the plum tomatoes, use your spoon or spatula to break them up a little in the pan.
Add half the basil, stalks and all, and season well with salt and pepper. Cover with a lid, turn the heat down to low and bubble gently for 30-40 mins, stirring every 10 mins.

Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Slice the cherry tomatoes in half and finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes. Once the sauce has been cooking for 20 mins, drop the pasta into the boiling water and cook according to package directions.

A minute before the pasta cooking time is up, remove the lid from the sauce and stir in the sun-dried tomatoes, followed by the cherry tomatoes. Taste and season with salt and pepper and a pinch of sugar if you like.
Once the pasta is cooked, use tongs to transfer the pasta into the sauce. Toss well, adding a little of the pasta water to help the sauce to cling to the pasta.
Swirl into bowls and top with plenty of Parmesan and the remaining basil leaves. Finish with a big crack of black pepper.

name: Tropical Green Smoothie
description: This is our favourite green smoothie. We love using fresh spinach because it’s very neutral in taste - you won’t even notice that it’s there!
instructions: Cut the skins off the pineapple, remove the core and cut into large chunks.
Peel the mango and cut around the seed into large chunks.
Peel and roughly chop the ginger.
Deseed and roughly chop the red chilli.
Add all the ingredients to a blender with 150ml cold water and blitz until smooth. If it's too thick for your liking, add some more water and blitz until smooth.
If your fruit and veg aren’t cold, serve over ice. Enjoy!

name: Tropical Sunshine Smoothie
description: Bright, tropical and packed with protein. This golden smoothie brings the sunshine – even when the weather doesn’t.
instructions: Chuck the mango, pineapple, banana, coconut or almond milk, lime juice, turmeric, ginger and protein powder into a blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy. If it’s looking a bit thick, splash in some cold water to loosen.
Pour into a glass and get stuck in.

name: Tropical Sunshine Smoothie Bowl
description: Thick, tropical and golden. A protein-packed smoothie bowl that tastes like a holiday – sunshine vibes guaranteed.
instructions: Chuck the mango, pineapple, banana, milk, yoghurt, juice of the lime, turmeric, ginger and protein powder into a blender.

Start blending on a low speed. Use a tamper to push the mixture down – it’ll be thick, but that’s what we’re after. Only add more liquid if you really need to. Splash in an extra 10ml of milk at a time if it won’t budge.
Scoop into a bowl and top with whatever you fancy – banana slices, coconut flakes, granola, seeds or a drizzle of almond butter.

name: Tuna & Bean Salad
description: All you need is a couple of tins and a few fresh ingredients to bring this bright and zingy salad together. It's high in protein and high in flavour.
instructions: Bring a pan of water to a boil. While you’re waiting for it to boil, finely slice your red onion, chop your tomatoes, and trim your green beans.
Add the green beans and cook for 1 minute. Drain and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking process.
In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, sherry vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Add the tomatoes, capers, and red onion to the dressing and toss to combine.
Pat the butter beans and borlotti beans dry, then add them to the bowl along with the torn basil.
Add the drained tuna, mix everything together, and taste. Adjust seasoning with more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately or chill for later.

name: Tuna & Beans with Crispy Chilli Capers
description: A simple plate of beans and tuna with a spicy crispy caper topping. A hearty healthy supper when you need a bit of comfort but still want to keep things healthyish.
keywords: Tuna & Beans with Crispy Chilli Capers
Tuna & Beans with Crispy Chilli Capers recipe
instructions: Trim and finely dice the shallots, then thinly slice the garlic. Finely chop the chilli, drain the capers.
Place a saucepan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the shallot and garlic and cook, stirring, for 3-4 mins until translucent and fragrant.

Squeeze the lemon juice in and cook it out completely before tipping the canned tomatoes in. Using the back of a spoon or masher, crush the tomatoes. Bring the mixture to the boil, drop half the basil in (stalks and all), then turn the heat down to a gentle simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 mins until thickened.

Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, add a generous glug of olive oil and place over medium heat. Once hot, add the pine nuts, chilli and capers. Cook until the pine nuts have turned golden, then transfer to a bowl, set aside.

Once the sauce has thickened, drain the tuna and beans (reserving the bean liquid) and stir both through the sauce, adding a splash of bean liquid to loosen, if needed. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Discard the cooked basil and stir through the remaining basil leaves.
Share the tuna and beans into a bowl, top with a drizzle of the crispy chilli caper topping.

name: Tuna & Cherry Tomato Pasta
description: A quick, punchy pasta with tuna, juicy cherry toms, plus a chilli kick for grown ups.
instructions: Finely chop the onion, thinly slice the garlic and halve the fresh cherry tomatoes.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the onion, garlic and a pinch of salt. Cook for 5-6 mins until soft and translucent.

Add the halved cherry tomatoes, tinned tomatoes and the water. Let it bubble, then stir in the drained tuna. Bring to a simmer and reduce the heat to low. Let it cook for 15 mins, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thickened and glossy.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta following pack instructions in a large pan of boiling salted water. Once cooked, drain, reserving a mugful of the cooking water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce, adding a splash of the reserved pasta water to loosen if needed. Spoon onto plates.
Serve up! Kids Plate: Dish out the pasta as is.Parents Plate: Top the adult portions with a good pinch of chilli flakes, a scattering of torn basil leaves, grated parmesan and the capers.

name: Tuna & Egg Fried Rice
description: Speedy, salty-savoury tuna fried rice with creamy avocado, crispy nori and plenty of chilli-mayo energy. A super easy lunch or dinner that seriously packs the protein.
instructions: Cut the spring onions into quarters. Place a large frying pan or wok over a medium heat with a drizzle of vegetable oil. Once hot, add the spring onions and cook for about 2 mins until softened and lightly coloured.
Add the frozen edamame and cook for another 2 mins, tossing regularly, until thawed and hot.

Add the rice and toss well to combine, breaking up any clumps. Pour in the soy sauce and toss again to coat everything evenly. Push the rice to one side of the pan, then add the tuna and coriander on top of the rice, but don’t mix it in just yet.

Add a little more oil to the empty side of the pan, crack in the eggs and scramble them, breaking up the yolks. Once the eggs are nearly cooked, fold everything together until evenly mixed, then take the pan off the heat.
Squeeze over half of the lime juice and cut the remaining lime into wedges. Slice the avocado.
Divide the fried rice between bowls. Top with the avocado, crumble over the nori, sprinkle with the sesame seeds and finish with mayonnaise and sriracha. Serve with the lime wedges on the side.

name: Tuna & Green Bean Chopped Salad
description: A fresh and spicy salad recipe you can assemble in 10 minutes, whack in the fridge and take to work. It’s a healthy, high-protein lunch that beats any sad sandwich.
keywords: Tuna & Green Bean Chopped Salad recipe
instructions: Boil your green beans in water until soft, drain, and then allow to cool.
Chop and discard the heads off the pickled guindilla chillies. Add your beans to a chopping board along with your tuna and chillies and roughly chop them up.
Add in your capers and continue to chop.
Add all of your chopped ingredients to a bowl and squeeze in the juice from your lemons. Add in a good glug of olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper.
Divide the salad between Tupperware containers and box up. Pop in the fridge until needed - these will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Tuna & Green Bean Chopped Salad
description: A fresh and spicy chopped salad recipe you can assemble in 10 minutes. It’s a healthy, high in protein, and ridiculously easy to make tuna salad.
keywords: Tuna & Green Bean Chopped Salad recipe
instructions: Boil your green beans in water until soft, drain, and then allow to cool.
Chop and discard the heads off the pickled guindilla chillies. Add your beans to a chopping board along with your tuna and chillies and roughly chop them up.
Add in your capers and continue to chop.
Add all of your chopped ingredients to a bowl and squeeze in the juice from your lemons. Add in a good glug of olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper. Serve and enjoy!

name: Tuna & Green Bean Tonnato Salad
description: Making your own tonnato sauce at home isn't as difficult as you might think. All you need is a half-decent food processor to get the job done.
keywords: Tuna & Green Bean Tonnato Salad recipe
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut any large ones in half. Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil, add the potatoes and cook for 12 mins.

For the tonnato sauce,  separate the yolks from ⅓ of the eggs (you can freeze the whites for meringue). Then add half the tuna, the egg yolks, anchovies, lemon juice and mustard to a food processor. Blitz to a paste, then gradually drizzle in 50ml olive oil to emulsify and thicken it a bit.
Trim and discard the ends of the beans. Add to the potato pan for the last 3 mins of cooking time. Drain the potatoes and beans in a colander and leave to cool a little.

Bring a medium-sized saucepan filled with water to the boil. Lower in the remaining eggs, turn the heat down to a simmer and cook for 7 mins. Plunge the eggs into iced water to stop them from cooking, then peel.
Finely dice the red onion. Slice the celery sticks on a diagonal.

Toss the potatoes, beans, celery and half of the onions with olive oil and salt, then spoon them onto a plate. Top with the tonnato sauce, remaining tuna, capers and red onion. Halve the eggs and pop these on top, too. Serve it up.

name: Tuna & Harissa Spaghetti
description: Garlicky, spicy and deeply tomatoey, this easy store cupboard spaghetti comes together fast and hits hard. Harissa and tuna really are a magic combo.
ingredients: 3x 110g Can Tinned Tuna in Olive Oil
instructions: Finely slice the garlic and roughly chop the parsley.

Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the garlic and fry for a minute or two until softened, then stir in the harissa and cook for another minute. Pour in the tomatoes, breaking them up with the back of your spoon, season well with salt and black pepper and bring to the boil. Reduce to a medium heat and leave to simmer for 10-15 mins, until the sauce has thickened and reduced.
While the sauce reduces, bring a large saucepan of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the spaghetti according to packet instructions. Before draining, reserve a mugful of the pasta water.

Drain the tuna and stir it through the sauce. Add the drained spaghetti and parsley and toss to coat, add a splash of the reserved pasta water to loosen if needed. Grate in three-quarters of the parmesan tossing everything together.
To serve, divide between bowls and grate over the remaining parmesan.

name: Tuna & New Potato Salad with Caper Dressing
description: Chuck this salad on the table, and everyone will be impressed. Tender warm new potatoes, a punchy Dijon and lemon dressing, good tinned tuna and briny capers. It's really simple but seriously punches for a weeknight meal.
ingredients: 2x 125g Can Tinned Tuna in Olive Oil
instructions: Put the potatoes in a large saucepan of cold salted water and bring to the boil. Cook for 10-15 mins, depending on size, until really soft but not collapsing. Drain and leave to steam dry for a minute or two.

While the potatoes cook, make the dressing. Zest the lemon into a jar, then squeeze in the juice. Add the mustard and 3-4 tbsp olive oil, season with salt and black pepper and shake well until creamy.
Pour the dressing over the warm potatoes and toss to combine, don't worry if a few break apart, as the dressing seeping into the potato is a good thing.

Halve and very finely slice the red onion and rinse the capers. Roughly chop the parsley. Spoon the dressed potatoes onto a large platter and top with the drained tuna, capers, red onion and parsley. Taste and adjust with more lemon, oil or salt as needed, and serve warm.

name: Tuna & Sweetcorn Linguine
description: Creamy tuna pasta with pops of sweetcorn, crispy capers & a lemony kick. A family-friendly midweek pasta that’s speedy and satisfying.
instructions: 1 Adult Serving = 2 Kids ServingsBring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.

Meanwhile, heat half of the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Pat the capers and a quarter of the sweetcorn dry. Thinly slice the chilli and garlic. Add the capers and sweetcorn to the pan and fry until crisp, 8–10 mins, adding the chilli and garlic for the final 2 mins until the garlic just starts to turn golden. Transfer to a bowl with a slotted spoon. Finely zest the lemon, squeeze over a quarter of the juice and toss with the roughly chopped parsley — this is your crispy topping for the adults.
Once the water’s boiling, add the linguine and cook following pack instructions. Drain, reserving a mugful of the pasta water.
Grate the cheese and cut the remaining lemon into wedges.

Tip the pasta into the frying pan over a medium heat with the drained tuna, remaining sweetcorn, most of the cheese and the rest of the olive oil. Add splashes of pasta water, tossing, until you’ve got a creamy sauce
Serve up! Kids Plate: Dish up the pasta and top with extra grated cheese.Parents Plate: Serve the pasta with the crispy caper mixture on top. Add lemon wedges on the side.

name: Tuna & Sweetcorn Tonnato Pasta Salad
description: A jazzy little pasta salad packed with crispy sweetcorn, creamy tonnato and a load of crunch. Perfect for lunch boxes.
instructions: Cook the pasta following pack instructions, then drain well, reserving a mugful of the cooking water.

Tip the sweetcorn into a frying pan with the extra-virgin olive oil. Set over a high heat, season with a pinch of salt and fry for a few minutes until golden in spots. Scoop out half the sweetcorn and add it to a blender.
Drain both tins of tuna. Add one of them to the blender with the sweetcorn.
Spoon in the red wine vinegar and mayo, add a pinch of salt and black pepper, then blitz until smooth and creamy. Taste and tweak the seasoning with more salt, pepper or vinegar if needed.
Roughly dice the tomatoes, shred the sugar snap peas and thinly slice the red onion. Tip them all into a large mixing bowl.
Add the drained pasta, creamy dressing and capers to the bowl. Mix everything well, adding a splash of the pasta cooking water to loosen if needed.
Divide between containers. Top each portion with the remaining sweetcorn and tuna. Job done.

name: Tuna & Toasted Rice Chilli Crunch Bowl
description: Spicy, crunchy, creamy, zesty. This one's got it all. A satisfying rice bowl that hits every craving with barely any cooking.
keywords: tuna cucumber toasted rice chilli crunch bowl
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a nonstick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the rice, season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 15 mins until starting to crisp.

Chop the chives. Zest the lemon, then juice it. Add both to a small blender with the cottage cheese, most of the chives and sriracha. Blend until smooth, adding 1–2 tablespoons of water to loosen if needed. Season to taste with salt and pepper, then tip into a large bowl.
Drain the tuna and chuck it into the bowl. Thinly slice the celery and radishes. Finely chop the red onion. Add them all to the bowl along with the chickpeas.
Slice the avocado in half, remove the stone and chop the flesh into chunks. Fold it through the salad.
To serve, divide the tuna salad between bowls and top with the crispy rice, scatter with the remaining chives and drizzle with more sriracha, if you like.

name: Tuna Bean Pasta
description: This is the freshest tuna bean pasta. Perfect for any occasion.
instructions: Finely chop the parsley and slice the garlic into thin discs.

Drizzle the olive oil into a pan on a medium heat. Add the parsley stalks along with the chilli flakes. Give it a good stir and add the garlic. Once the garlic has started to cook, mix in the olives and capers. Pour the cannellini beans including the bean water into the pan and mix.
In a separate saucepan, cook the spaghetti. Add about a cup of the pasta water to the olive-bean mix to thicken up the sauce.

Break the tuna into chunks and add to the sauce with the chopped parsley leaves (saving some for garnish). Add the zest of a whole lemon to the sauce to make it taste extra fresh and to bring out the chilli’s flavour. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Finally, add your cooked spaghetti and fold it into the sauce. Top with more chilli flakes and any leftover parsley. Tuck in!

name: Tuna Caesar with Butternut Squash & Parmesan Crisps
description: Zingy lemon yoghurt, roast squash, and seared tuna come together in this high-protein bowl topped with crispy Parmesan shards. A serious bit of meal prep.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Chop the butternut squash into 5cm pieces, chuck onto a baking tray with half the olive oil, season with salt and black pepper, then roast for 20 mins or until tender and starting to colour.

Peel and finely grate the garlic into a mixing bowl. Mash the anchovies and garlic together using a fork to form a paste. Zest over half the lemon (save the rest for later), then squeeze in the juice. Add the yoghurt, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard and plenty of black pepper. Whisk together, loosening with splashes of cold water until it’s as runny as you like.

Heat a nonstick frying pan over a medium heat. Finely grate the Parmesan directly into the pan in an even layer and cook until bubbling. Remove from the heat, let it cool for a couple of minutes, then gently lift the Parmesan crisp out. Once cool, snap into shards.
Strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and finely shred the leaves. Toss into a bowl with a pinch of salt and the remaining lemon juice. Scrunch it all together with your hands to soften.

Brush the tuna steaks with the remaining oil and season with salt and black pepper. Heat a large nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat, then cook the tuna for 2 mins per side for a pink centre. Transfer to a plate to rest, then sprinkle over the reserved lemon zest.

Toss the roasted squash and lemony dressing through the cavolo nero, then divide between Tupperware containers. Slice the tuna and lay it on top, finishing with the Parmesan crisps. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Tuna Melt Enchiladas
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad
Think tuna melt meets enchiladas. Creamy, cheesy, saucy and baked till bubbling. Proper crowd-pleaser that both kids and grown-ups will demolish.
ingredients: 4x 145g Can Tinned Tuna in Spring Water
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Finely chop 1 red onion and combine in a large bowl with the drained the tuna and sweetcorn. Add 75g of the sour cream and chive dip. Season with salt and loads of black pepper, then fold through half of the mozzarella.
Divide the mixture evenly between the tortillas, then roll them up tightly. Place them seam-side down in a large ovenproof baking dish so they fit fairly snugly.

Add the chopped tomatoes, chop 1 of the red onions, the garlic and most of the coriander to a blender with a drizzle of olive oil. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt and pepper. Pour the sauce all over the tortillas.
Dot over the 100g of the sour cream and chive dip, then scatter over the rest of the cheddar and mozzarella mix. Bake for 30 mins, or until golden and bubbling.
Meanwhile, make the salsa. Finely chop the roasted red peppers, half of the last onion and some coriander.
You could also serve with a spicy herb salad for the parents. This uses any leftover red onion, coriander and some sliced red chillies, tossed in olive oil.

Serve the enchiladas hot from the oven. Add dollops of the remaining sour cream and chive on top, and dress with your salsa. Can serve with your spicy herb salad for the adults, and add an extra dollop of sour cream for the kids.

name: Tuna Niçoise with Air Fryer Boiled Eggs
description: A classic tuna niçoise with a twist. Making boiled eggs in an air fryer is so easy and foolproof, then you can use your perfect eggs to make this banging salad.
instructions: Put the eggs into the basket of an air fryer. Set the temperature to 180°C and cook for 10 mins. Meanwhile, get a bowl of cold water ready. Lift the cooked eggs into the bowl of cold water and leave for 5 mins to cool completely, then peel and chop into halves or quarters.

Drain the can of tuna really well, then tip half into a high-powered blender with a few of the pitted kalamata olives, the mustard, egg yolk, zest and juice of 1 lemon and the olive oil. Whizz until slightly thickened and you have a creamy dressing. Taste and add a little salt, loads of cracked black pepper and another squeeze of lemon. Pour the dressing over the base of a large serving platter.

Drain, then quarter or half the new potatoes and tip into a bowl. Thinly slice the sugar snaps, cut the lettuce into chunky pieces and roughly cut up the tomatoes. Add all to the bowl, then thinly slice the red onion and add to the bowl alongside the parsley leaves, too.
Squeeze in a little lemon juice and toss well, then pile onto the platter. Finish with the chopped eggs, reserved tuna and kalamata olives, plus a little lick of olive oil.

name: Tuna Ragù
description: This simple store-cupboard ragù is an excellent recipe to whip out when you're in a fix. It's packed with lean protein and perfect for meal prepping throughout the week.
instructions: Trim and finely dice the shallots, then thinly slice the garlic.
Place a saucepan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the shallot and garlic and cook, stirring, for 3-4 mins until translucent and fragrant.

Squeeze the lemon juice in and cook it out completely before tipping the canned tomatoes in. Using the back of a spoon or masher, crush the tomatoes. Bring the mixture to the boil, drop half the basil in (stalks and all), then turn the heat down to a gentle simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 mins until thickened.
Once thickened, drain the tuna and stir it through the sauce. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Discard the cooked basil and stir through the remaining basil leaves.

name: Tuna Tataki Salad with Spicy Mayo & Crispy Garlic
description: In Partnership With Aldi. #ad. A speedy, Japanese-inspired tuna salad loaded with crispy garlic chips, a zingy ponzu drizzle and a spicy mayo that’ll have you licking the bowl. This one seriously delivers.
keywords: Tuna Tataki Salad with Spicy Mayo & Crispy Garlic recipe
Tuna Tataki Salad with Spicy Mayo & Crispy Garlic
instructions: Slice the garlic. Heat the vegetable oil in a small frying pan set over a medium heat. Once hot, add the sliced garlic and fry for 1–2 mins until golden. Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and set aside.
Juice the lemon into a bowl and add the remaining ponzu dressing ingredients. Whisk together until combined, then set aside.
In a separate bowl, mix the mayo and sriracha with lime zest and half the lime juice, until smooth. Taste and add extra lime juice if needed. Set aside.
Prep the veg. Thinly slice the onion and cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes and slice the avocado. Pick the coriander leaves from their stems and set aside.

Add the onion, tomato, cucumber, salad leaves, and coriander to a serving bowl and toss to combine. 
Drain the tuna, tear it into chunks, and scatter over the top. Fan out the sliced avocado, then dollop over the spicy mayo. 
Drizzle with the ponzu dressing and finish with the crispy garlic chips and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

name: Tuna, Celery & Miso High Protein Smash
description: Here's a protein-packed recipe that you can 'smoosh' over a bagel, toast, pitta bread or whatever takes your fancy. It's a gamechanger.
instructions: Chop the celery and spring onions into small pieces. Drain your tuna, and juice your lemon.
Combine all of the ingredients in a bowl before ‘smooshing’ over toast – or pitta bread, a bagel, or whatever you fancy. Top with finely chopped spring onions.
Enjoy!

name: Tuna, Egg & Tomato Salad
description: Zingy, herby tuna salad with eggs, crisp fennel and juicy tomatoes. A proper flavour-packed lunch or light dinner that takes no time to throw together.
instructions: Place a small saucepan of water over a high heat and bring to the boil. Gently lower in the eggs, then turn the heat down to medium-high and cook for 9 mins until hard-boiled. Transfer to a bowl of ice water and leave to cool completely.
Meanwhile, finely dice the shallot and add it to a large bowl with the Dijon mustard and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and black pepper and leave to pickle.
Drain the tuna. Chop the tomatoes into bite-sized chunks. Thinly slice the fennel and roughly chop the watercress.
Peel the cooled eggs and coarsely grate them into the bowl with the shallots. Gradually whisk in the olive oil until thick and emulsified. Taste and season with more salt and pepper, if needed.
Toss the tuna, tomatoes, fennel, grains and watercress through the dressing. Divide between plates or box up for later.

name: Tuna, Fennel & Tomato Pasta
description: Tinned tuna is a store-cupboard staple which adds some heft to this tangy tomato pasta.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Cut the sourdough into chunks and toss with olive oil and salt. Slide into the oven for 10-12 mins or until golden brown. Tip into a food processor and pulse until you have crunchy breadcrumbs. Set aside.
Thinly slice the fennel bulbs and tip into a pan. Add a good glug of olive oil and season with salt. Set over a medium heat and cook, stirring regularly, for 10-15 mins or until caramelised.

Meanwhile, finely chop the chilli and garlic and halve the cherry tomatoes. Add the fennel seeds, chilli and garlic to the pan of caramelised fennel and stir through. Crank up the heat and cook for a couple of mins before adding the white wine. Cook for 3-4 mins and reduce by half. Add the tomatoes and swirl into the sauce.

Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and tip in the spaghetti. Cook for 8 mins or until al dente. Transfer the cooked pasta to the sauce and toss together, adding a little pasta water if you need to loosen things up a little. Tip in the tuna and add the zest and juice of the lemon. Tear in the basil and toss.
Divide between warm bowls and top with the crunchy breadcrumbs.

name: Tuna, Lentil & Feta Salad
description: A high-protein salad packed with lentils, butter beans, tuna, and loads of herby zing. Ready in minutes.
instructions: Peel and slice the red onion and add it to a large mixing bowl. Pour in the red wine vinegar, add the dried oregano, capers and olive oil, then season with salt and pepper. Whisk everything together to make a punchy dressing.
Finely chop the mint and stir it through the dressing.
Drain and rinse the lentils and butter beans, then chuck them into the bowl and toss well to coat.
Drain the tuna and crumble the feta.
Serve up the salad into bowls and top with the tuna and feta. Finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Tuna, Lentil & Feta Salad
description: A high-protein meal prep salad packed with lentils, butter beans, tuna, and loads of herby zing. Lunch, sorted.
instructions: Peel and slice the red onion and add it to a large mixing bowl. Pour in the red wine vinegar, add the dried oregano, capers and olive oil, then season with salt and pepper. Whisk everything together to make a punchy dressing.
Finely chop the mint and stir it through the dressing.
Drain and rinse the lentils and butter beans, then chuck them into the bowl and toss well to coat.
Drain the tuna and crumble the feta.

Serve up the salad into Tupperware containers and top with the tuna and feta. Finish with a crack of black pepper. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Tuna, Tomato & Courgette Gnocchi
description: This one’s got serious store cupboard power. Juicy tuna, spicy guindilla chillies, and soft gnocchi in a punchy tomato sauce? Sold.
instructions: Drain the tuna. Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil.
Dice the courgette, slice the garlic and chop the guindilla peppers. Pick the basil leaves and set aside, reserving the stems.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the courgette and cook for 5–6 mins, stirring often, until golden. Scoop out and set aside, leaving the oil behind.
Add the garlic and basil stems to the same pan and cook for 2–3 mins until soft and fragrant.
Pour in the passata and simmer for 15 mins. Remove the basil stems, then stir in the guindilla peppers, drained tuna and half the cooked courgette. Season with salt.
Add the gnocchi to the boiling water and cook for 2 mins or until they float. Transfer straight into the sauce along with a ladle of cooking water.
Stir in the basil leaves and grate in half of the Parmesan. Mix well until glossy and saucy.
Divide between bowls. Top with the remaining courgette, Parmesan and a good crack of black pepper.

name: Turkey Burger
description: This super easy turkey burger really hits the spot. A healthier alternative to a beef burger, made with lean turkey mince.
instructions: Start by making the patties. Coarsely grate the shallot into a bowl then add the mayonnaise and Worcestershire sauce and mix to combine. Add the turkey mince and season with plenty of salt and pepper then give it a good mix until you have a fully incorporated mixture.
Use your hands to divide the mixture into 4 tightly packed, even-sized patties, about 1cm thick. Transfer the patties to a plate.
For the burger sauce, combine the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard and hot sauce in a small bowl. Season to taste with a touch of pickle brine, then set aside.

To cook the patties, heat a large frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, add a drizzle of olive oil then place the patties in. Cook for about 8-10 mins, flipping halfway through, or until cooked through. Be careful not to move the patties around the pan too much, leave them to go golden brown on both sides.
Transfer the patties to a plate then pop a slice of cheese on top of each one, cover with a lid and leave to rest for a couple of minutes until the cheese has melted.
Meanwhile, toast the burger buns in the same frying pan set over a medium heat. Slice the dill pickles to your desired thickness.
To build the burger, spread a dollop of burger sauce onto the cut sides of the buns. Top with a few lettuce leaves, the turkey patty, a few pickles and finally the bun top.

name: Turkish Air Fryer Poached Eggs Recipe
description: Experience a delightful twist on a classic Turkish breakfast with this air fryer poached eggs recipe. Perfectly poached eggs, with their velvety yolks, take on a new level of convenience when made in the air fryer, eliminating the need for an egg poacher or frying pan.
instructions: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl, zest in the lemon and finely grate in the garlic. Season with salt and black pepper and add a squeeze of lemon juice.

Put the butter into a small saucepan set over a medium-high heat. Keep whisking and stirring until the butter turns a light golden brown, then remove from the heat and add the olive oil and aleppo pepper. Season lightly and squeeze in a little lemon juice. Set aside.

Egg poaching time. Put four ovenproof ramekins into the basket of your air fryer. Boil the kettle and half fill the ramekins with boiling water. Crack an egg into each ramekin. Set the temperature to 200°C and cook the eggs for 5 mins until the whites are just set.
Meanwhile, divide the yoghurt between two shallow bowls, swirling it around the base of the bowls.
Carefully use a tea towel to lift out the ramekins from the air fryer, then use a spoon to free the eggs from the ramekins. Pat the eggs a little with kitchen paper and put on top of the yoghurt.
Briefly reheat the flavoured butter, then spoon all over the top.
Scatter with dill fronds and serve with the toasted bread to scoop up and the lemon halves for squeezing over, if you like.

name: Turkish Eggs with Confit Chickpeas & Tomatoes
description: Roasted chickpeas, jammy tomatoes, garlicky yoghurt and runny eggs. Is there any better way to start your day? We’ve adapted this Çılbır, also known as Turkish eggs, to include chickpeas for extra plant power to keep you feeling fuller longer.
keywords: Turkish Eggs with Confit Chickpeas & Tomatoes Recipe
Turkish Eggs with Confit Chickpeas & Tomatoes
instructions: Preheat your oven to 170°C.
Put your tomatoes, chickpeas and garlic in an ovenproof dish with a sprinkle of salt and cover with olive oil. Roast for around 30 mins until the garlic is completely soft and the tomatoes are jammy.
Combine the Greek yoghurt with the roasted garlic (squeezing out the flesh first). Season to taste and then spread over two plates, leaving a well in the middle.
Meanwhile, poach or boil your eggs for 3-4 mins.
Spoon the tomatoes and chickpeas into the middle of the yoghurt before topping with the eggs. Drizzle over a bit of harissa paste and some roughly torn parsley.
Serve with toast and enjoy!

name: Turkish Eggs with Spiced Butter & Herby Yoghurt
description: We've taken the breakfast classic of Turkish eggs and added a few herby, spicy twists that take it to the next level. Perfect for brunch with your mates!
keywords: Turkish Eggs With Spiced Butter & Herby Yoghurt
instructions: For the flatbreads mix the yeast, sugar and warm water in a bowl and set aside for 10 mins until foamy. In another bowl, mix the flour and salt, then add the yoghurt and yeast mix. Using your hands, bring together and knead on a lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, around 5 mins. Transfer to a clean, oiled bowl then cover with a clean towel. Leave in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

Grate the garlic into a blender and chuck in a quarter of the yoghurt. Whizz up with lemon juice and most of the dill, mint and parsley, saving some for garnish. Tip into a bowl and stir through the rest of the yoghurt. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Slice the peppers into 2cm strips.
Melt the butter in a pan with a splash of olive oil, add the red pepper flakes along with the chilli flakes and aleppo pepper. Set aside.

Once the flatbread has proofed, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Divide the dough into 8 pieces and then roll out into small discs around 1cm thick. Heat a griddle or frying pan over a high heat, once really hot add the flatbread and cook the flatbreads for 2-3 mins on each side, or until golden.

Start the poaching process by cracking your egg into a sieve over a bowl and leaving it for 1 min. You should be left with a nice firm white which will prevent your egg from looking ‘wispy’. The key here is to use fridge-cold eggs, and they should be as fresh as possible. Once it's strained, tip it into a small bowl or ramekin. Get a pot of water on to boil, you need it to be about ¾ full. As soon as the water is boiling, use a utensil to stir a small whirlpool in the middle. Swiftly drop the egg into the middle of the whirlpool and turn the heat down to low.

You need the egg to be moving about for a couple of seconds to encourage the whites to spiral upwards and over the yolk. Cook gently for 3-4 mins, until the whites are set but the yolk is nice and runny, then remove from the water with a slotted spoon, draining on kitchen paper.
Spread the yoghurt on a plate, top with the sliced peppers then the poached eggs. Spoon over the warm, spiced butter, garnish with whole herbs, then scoop up with the fresh flatbreads.

name: Turmeric Braised Chicken
description: It's time for another batch, and this one is a turmeric braised chicken base recipe that can be served with rice, flatbread, or broth. It's a corker.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Rub the chicken in ½ tsp turmeric and salt, then brown it in a hot frying pan for 6 mins on each side, until the fat has rendered out and it has browned a bit. Remove the chicken from the pan.
Finely slice the onions, then get these into the same pan over a medium heat. Cook for about 20 mins until softened.
Grate in the garlic and add the remaining turmeric, cumin and paprika. Cook these out for a minute.
Finely chop the preserved lemon and add to the pan, along with the chicken stock, cinnamon stick and chicken. Bring it up to a simmer. Pop in the oven and bake for 30 mins.
Finely chop most of the coriander leaves and add some to the pan, along with the olives. Adjust the seasoning.

name: Turmeric Braised Chicken & Giant Couscous Broth
description: Here's another recipe you can make using your batch-cooked turmeric braised chicken with chickpeas. Enjoy.
instructions: Make the Turmeric Braised Chicken.
Add the couscous to a saucepan and add 1L boiling water. Season with salt, then simmer for 8 mins.
Drain the chickpeas and give them a rinse. Shred the chicken off the bones, then transfer to the pan along with its sauce and the chickpeas. Add the spinach and cook for another 2 mins until wilted.
Season the broth to taste with salt, then spoon into bowls and top with coriander leaves. Serve.

name: Turmeric Braised Chicken With Rice
description: This recipe can be made using a third of your batch-cooked turmeric braised chicken. Plus, it's delicious.
instructions: Make the Turmeric Braised Chicken.
Cook the rice following pack instructions.
Heat up the Turmeric Braised Chicken, then ladle it on top of your rice. Add a dollop of yoghurt and coriander leaves to serve.

name: Turmeric Cauliflower
description: This gorgeous golden turmeric cauliflower is perfect for meal prep. Combine it with your choice of protein, carb and topping to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Cut the cauliflower into rough florets and add to a large roasting tray. Peel the onions and cut into chunky wedges, then add to the tray along with the whole garlic cloves, still in their skins. Add the spices and olive oil, toss well, then season well. Slide into the oven and bake for 30 mins.

If batch cooking for the week, let the cauliflower cool then transfer the to a container and store in the fridge until ready to eat. Serve with a drizzle of chilli oil, a scattering of coriander leaves and some sesame seeds.

name: Turmeric Cauliflower & Halloumi Rice Bowl
description: Ditch your meal deal for this gorgeous, golden cauliflower rice bowl that's got plenty of fresh veggies and even more flavour.
keywords: Lunch Box: Turmeric Cauliflower Rice Bowl recipe
Lunch Box: Turmeric Cauliflower Rice Bowl
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the cauliflower into rough florets and add to a large roasting tray. Cut the halloumi into chunky cubes and add to the tray. Peel the onions and cut into chunky wedges, then add to the tray along with the whole garlic cloves, still in their skins. Add the spices and olive oil, toss well, then season well. Slide into the oven and bake for 30 mins.
Cook the rice following pack instructions and tip into a bowl. Finely chop most of the coriander and add to the rice along with the juice of the lemon.
Remove the tray from the oven, fish out the garlic cloves and carefully squeeze the squishy garlic out of their skins into the rice. Season with plenty of salt and pepper.

Spoon the rice into your Tupperware containers and top with the spiced veggies. Drizzle with chilli oil, scatter with the remaining coriander leaves and finish with sesame seeds. 
Once they've cooled down a bit, box them up and pop in the fridge, until needed - they'll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Turmeric Cauliflower & Halloumi Rice Bowl
description: A gorgeous, golden cauliflower rice bowl that's got plenty of fresh veggies and even more flavour.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the cauliflower into rough florets and add to a large roasting tray. Cut the halloumi into chunky cubes and add to the tray. Peel the onions and cut into chunky wedges, then add to the tray along with the whole garlic cloves, still in their skins. Add the spices and olive oil, toss well, then season well. Slide into the oven and bake for 20-25 mins.
Cook the rice following pack instructions and tip into a bowl. Finely chop most of the coriander and add to the rice along with the juice of the lemon.
Remove the tray from the oven, fish out the garlic cloves and remove their skin, stir into the rice. Season with plenty of salt and pepper.
Spoon the rice into bowls and top with the spiced veggies. Drizzle with chilli oil, scatter with the remaining coriander leaves and finish with sesame seeds.

name: Turmeric Chicken Wraps with Pickled Carrot & Chilli Lime Dipping Sauce
description: Fragrant turmeric and lime leaf chicken mince, tangy quick-pickled carrot, sriracha mayo and fresh coriander, all wrapped up tight. Great for whacking in the fridge for a speedy grab and go lunch.
keywords: Lime Leaf & Turmeric Chicken Wraps with Pickled Carrot & Chilli Lime Dipping Sauce
Lime Leaf & Turmeric Chicken Wraps with Pickled Carrot & Chilli Lime Dipping Sauce recipe
instructions: Peel the carrots and finely slice into matchsticks. Add to a large jar with the vinegar, sugar, salt and the cold water. Shake until the sugar has dissolved, then set aside to pickle for about 30 mins. Drain well and pat dry with paper towels before using.

Cut the chicken thighs in half and add to a food processor. Pulse about 15 times until finely chopped and resembling a coarse mince. Finely dice the onion, mince the garlic, finely chop the lime leaves and finely grate the ginger.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion, season with a pinch of salt and cook for 4-5 mins, stirring often, until tender and lightly golden. Add the chicken and break it up with a wooden spoon, tossing to combine with the onion. Spread into an even layer and season with salt. Cook undisturbed for about 3 mins until golden underneath, then toss and cook for a further 3-4 mins until browned all over.

Add the garlic, lime leaves, ginger and turmeric. Cook for 1 min, stirring, until fragrant. Pour in the water and bring to a simmer. Simmer for about 2 mins until most of the liquid has evaporated. Squeeze in the juice of the lime, sugar and fish sauce, then remove from the heat. Transfer to a mixing bowl and refrigerate until cooled.

Finely slice the coriander stems and set aside for the dipping sauce. Then roughly chop the coriander leaves and toss through the cooled chicken mixture. Taste and season with more fish sauce if needed.

Meanwhile, make the dipping sauce if using. Thinly slice the chilli into rounds and mince the garlic. Combine all the ingredients with the coriander stems in a jar with the water and shake to dissolve the sugar. Store in the fridge until ready to serve.
Combine the mayonnaise and sriracha in a small bowl. Thinly slice the cabbage.

Fill the tortillas with the sriracha mayo, cooled chicken, pickled carrot, cabbage and coriander. Wrap tightly and secure in foil or baking paper. Serve straight away, or store in the fridge for up to three days. To warm through, pan-fry on a medium-low heat until lightly crisp.

name: Turmeric Cod Curry With Crispy Coconut Quinoa
description: Beautiful flaky cod on a bed of rich, coconutty curry. Top it off with crispy quinoa and you've got a hell of a recipe on your hands.
keywords: Turmeric Cod Curry With Crispy Coconut Quinoa
Turmeric Cod Curry With Crispy Coconut Quinoa recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Tip the desiccated coconut and quinoa onto a baking tray, drizzle with oil, salt and pepper and cook for 10 mins until crispy.
Put the ginger, garlic, chilli, shallot, coriander stalks, turmeric, lime juice, and cumin into a blender and blitz until smooth. You may need to add a splash of water to help it along.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a pan, then add the paste you’ve just made. Cook for about 5 mins until thickened. Add the coconut milk, tomatoes, fish sauce and water, then bring to a simmer. Taste and season with salt and pepper if needed.

Add the kale (you may need to do this in batches) and stir until reduced in volume but not entirely wilted. Top with the cod fillets and season them with salt and pepper. Pop the lid back on and cook for 5-10 mins – this will depend on the thickness of the cod fillets. You’re looking for the fish to have no resistance and flake off in big pieces.
Serve the curry topped with the crispy quinoa and reserved coriander leaves. You can eat as is or with a side of rice, potatoes or chapati.

name: Turmeric Roasted Cauliflower With Dukkah & Jammy Onions
description: Dukkah is a spicy, nutty Middle Eastern condiment that adds a really satisfying flavour (and crunch) to this dish. It's even vegan-friendly.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C.
Place the blanched hazelnuts, pistachios, sesame seeds, cumin seeds, coriander seeds and fennel seeds in a small baking tray. Roast for 10 mins, or until nice and fragrant.
Leave to cool then transfer to a food processor, season well with salt and pepper and blitz until finely chopped. Set aside.
Quarter the cauliflower heads.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Place the cauliflower cut-side down and cook for 3 mins, or until nicely browned. Flip and repeat on the other cut side, then transfer to a baking dish.
Combine the turmeric with 4 tbsp olive oil and season well with salt and pepper.
Brush the turmeric oil over the cauliflower and roast for 30 mins, or until cooked through but not mushy.
Meanwhile, finely chop your red onions and garlic.
Wipe out any fallen bits of cauliflower out of your frying pan, then add a splash of olive oil and place over a medium heat.
Add the red onions, along with a good pinch of salt and pepper, and cook for 10 mins, or until softened but not browned.
Add the garlic and Aleppo pepper and cook for 1 min, then add the raisins, pomegranate molasses, sugar and 200ml water.
Season with salt and pepper and cook until slightly reduced and thickened, 3 to 5 mins.
Finely chop the fresh mint.
To assemble, spoon the jammy onions over the cauliflower. Add a good sprinkle of the dukkah and finish with the fresh mint. Tuck in and enjoy!

name: Turmeric Tomato Noodles
description: Udon noodles are such a life-saver when you're pushed for time. We've jazzed them up here with tomatoes, turmeric, and a dash of miso.
instructions: Halve the cherry tomatoes and finely slice the spring onions.
Add 2 tbsp of olive oil to a large frying pan over a medium heat.
Peel the garlic and ginger and finely grate into the pan, cook for a minute, then add the miso and turmeric and whisk together, cook for a minute further. Add the juice of half of the lemon.

Turn up the heat to high and add the noodles, cherry tomatoes, and most of the sliced spring onion to the pan along with 75ml water, toss well for 2-3 mins, until the noodles unravel and are coated with the yellow sauce, add a splash more water if it needs it. Season with salt and pepper.
Twirl into bowls. drizzle with chilli oil. Scatter with toasted sesame seeds, basil leaves and the remaining sliced spring onion. Serve the remaining lemon half, sliced into wedges, on the side.

name: Tuscan Chicken & Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Tagliatelle
description: Golden chicken patties simmered in a creamy sundried tomato sauce, tossed wiht pasta and finished with parmesan. Even the pickiest ones will love this.
instructions: Tip the chicken mince into a large mixing bowl. Add half of the Italian herb mix and season lightly with salt and pepper. Finely chop the drained sun-dried tomatoes and add half to the bowl. Mix everything together well, then form into small patties, roughly golf ball-sized, and flatten slightly.

Heat half of the sunflower oil in a non-stick frying pan set over a medium heat. Fry the patties in batches for 3-4 mins on each side until golden and cooked through. Scoop out onto a plate and set aside.
Get the pasta on to cook, following pack instructions. Once it's cooked, set aside.

Peel and finely chop the onion and halve the cherry tomatoes. Heat the remaining oil in the same frying pan and add the onion, tomatoes and remaining herbs. Cook for 5-6 mins until soft and jammy. Pour in the chicken stock and double cream, then stir through the remaining sun-dried tomatoes. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 5 mins until thickened slightly.
Add the patties back into the sauce and let them warm through for a minute.

Serve up! Kids Plate: Serve the meatballs and pasta separately or tossed together and shower with parmesan.Parents Plate: Toss the pasta through the sauce with the spinach letting it wilt, grate over parmesan and give it a good mix. Dish up and add a scattering of basil leaves.

name: Tuscan Tomato & Bread Soup
description: This is a classic Tuscan dish – it's rich, warming, and unctuous but also super fresh. The perfect way to use up any stale bread you've got hanging around.
instructions: Place a large pan over a medium heat and add 3 tbsp of olive oil. Finely dice the onion and add it to the pan along with the chilli flakes. Cook for about 7 mins until the onions are soft but not browned.
Finely chop 3 cloves of garlic and add to the pan, cook for another 2 mins.
Add the tinned tomatoes and tear in half the basil. Cook for about 15 mins until the tomatoes have thickened up, then pour in the vegetable stock.
Trim the crusts off the bread before tearing into chunks and throwing it in the pan. Cook for another 10 mins until thick and soupy.
To make the gremolata, finely dice the remaining garlic clove and mince the remaining half of the basil. Peel 2 large strips of lemon zest and finely chop. Mix that zest with the basil and garlic.
Plate up, top your soup with the gremolata and a generous drizzle of olive oil.

name: Twice-Roasted Pumpkin & Salted Maple Pecan Drizzle
description: Roasting your pumpkin twice makes it sweet and sticky and incredibly moreish. We've topped it off with a salted maple pecan drizzle that's to die for. A wicked veggie centrepiece.
keywords: Twice-Roasted Pumpkin & Salted Maple Pecan Drizzle
Twice-Roasted Pumpkin & Salted Maple Pecan Drizzle recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Thoroughly wash and dry the pumpkin. Using a sharp knife or skewer, poke holes all over, rub with some oil and place on a foil lined baking tray. Roast for 1-1.5 hours until tender, and a knife can easily go through.
Let the pumpkin cool down so you can handle it, then cut in half and scoop the seeds out and discard. Increase the oven temperature to 220°C.
Tear the pumpkin into large pieces, arrange them flesh-side up and return to the oven for 30-35 mins until lightly charred in areas.

Meanwhile, lightly crush the pecans and place them into a small pan. Turn the heat up to medium and lightly toast, 3-4 mins. Remove from the heat and pour the maple syrup in (careful, it will bubble and splatter). Let cool down a little, before picking out the pecans and transferring them onto a plate.
Add the tahini into a bowl and stir through 1 tbsp of cold water at a time until creamy. Pour in the maple syrup and season with salt and pepper.

Pick the dill and parsley leaves and place into a bowl. Trim and thinly slice the chilli and zest ½ the lemon. Add both into the herbs with 1 tbsp of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice. Toss together until evenly coated.

name: Tzatziki
description: A simple classic tzatziki that goes with just about everything. It's perfect for meal prep; combine it with your choice of protein, carb and veg to create your perfect meal-prep dish.
keywords: Tomato & Olive Baked Rice With Tzatziki
Tomato & Olive Baked Rice With Tzatziki recipe
instructions: Halve the cucumber lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Cut into strips and finely dice before adding to a bowl with the yoghurt. Grate in the garlic, then finely chop the mint and add that in too. Zest and juice the lemon into the yoghurt, then season with salt and pepper before giving it a good mix.

Serve with your choice of carb and protein (it's great with grilled meats, halloumi and rice dishes). If batch cooking for the week, transfer to a container and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Udon Cucumber Salad
