description: This fresh and zingy udon ‘salad’ is not quite a salad, more a cold noodle dish with salad elements. It’s got all the good stuff: crunch, spice, and protein.
instructions: Place the edamame in a heatproof bowl.
Boil a pot of water and simmer the noodles for 3 mins. Drain and pour some of the hot water over the edamame to defrost. Then rinse the noodles under cold water and set aside.
Peel and mince the ginger and garlic and place in a small bowl. Add the soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, brown sugar and whisk to combine. Set aside.

Slice the cucumber into half lengthwise and scoop out the watery seeds with a spoon (you can drain the water out of this and drink it!). Slice the cucumber into diagonal slices around .5cm and place in a large bowl.

Roughly chop the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems. Pick the mint leaves. Cut the chilli in half lengthways, remove the seeds and thinly slice. Roughly chop the peanuts. Finely chop the spring onion.
Add all of the herbs into the bowl with the cucumbers along with the edamame, spring onion, chilli, soy dressing, noodles and toss well.
If using tahini, add a drizzle on top and toss again. Drizzle over the crispy chilli oil and a little more sesame oil and the zest and juice of the lime. Toss well before serving.

name: Udon Noodle Soup With Coconut Tofu
description: This curry udon soup is inspired by Japanese Curry Udon, Malaysian Massaman curry and my love for turning vegetables into sauces.
instructions: Peel and deseed the squash. If you would like some ideas for what to do with the skin and seeds, check out the other squash recipes on site.
Cut the squash into 1cm cubes. Mince the garlic. Wash and grate the ginger, you don't need to peel it.

Heat a large pot over medium heat. Once hot, add oil, onions, ginger and garlic. Sauté for 2 minutes, stirring frequently. Add the butternut squash and season with salt, pepper, and curry powder. Stir to coat well. Then cover and cook for 4 mins, stirring occasionally. Add coconut milk, peanut butter, and vegetable stock. Bring to a low boil over medium heat and then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 mins or until butternut squash is fork tender.

While the soup is simmering, cook the tofu. Drain the tofu and pat it dry. Cut it into 2cm cubes. Heat a drizzle of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the tofu and fry for 3-4 mins until it starts to brown. Add the soy sauce, sesame seeds and coconut, if using. Fry for another minute and remove from the heat.

Use an immersion blender, or transfer soup to a blender, and purée on high until creamy and smooth. If using a blender, return soup back to pot.
Taste and adjust seasonings, adding more curry powder, salt, or sweetener as needed. Continue cooking for a few more minutes over medium heat.
Cook your udon noodles according to package instructions.
To serve, pour the soup into a large bowl, add the noodles and top with the tofu. Scatter some more sesame seeds, coconut coconut and fresh chilli and coriander.

name: Udon Noodles With Hot Oil
description: We’ve taken the technique of pouring sizzling-hot oil over hand-pulled noodles and applied it to udon noodles in this quick and comforting recipe.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Cut the pak choi into quarters lengthways and thinly slice the spring onions.
Finely grate the garlic into a small bowl, add the soy, rice wine vinegar and chilli flakes. Measure 4 tbsp of neutral oil into a small saucepan.
Drop the pak choi into the pan of boiling water. Cook for 1 min. Break the noodles up with your hands then drop into the water with the pak choi. Cook for 1 min more and drain in a sieve.
Divide the noodles and pak choi between four bowls and top each one with spoonfuls of the garlic, chilli and soy mix. Scatter over the spring onions and sesame seeds.
Get the saucepan of oil over a high heat. Once shimmering pour the oil equally into the four bowls to serve. Let people mix the oil into the noodles themselves.

name: Ultimate Bangers and Mash
description: After 3 years of tweaking, this is our definitive bangers and mash recipe. With a lovely, thick red onion gravy. The most warming dish about.
instructions: Firstly, chop up your potatoes (leaving the skins on) and add them to a pan of boiling water. Sprinkle in some salt and leave the potatoes to boil until soft.
Whilst the potatoes boil, it’s sausage time. Pour a large glug of olive oil into a frying pan, then add in your sausages. Fry these on a low heat until they have browned all over.
Gravy time. Slice your red onions and add them to a frying pan along with a glug of olive oil. Once the onions are soft, crush in the stock cube and add your flour. Mix them into the onions.
Pour in your red wine vinegar along with 100ml of boiling water. Stirring continuously until you have a nice smooth gravy, and then chop half of your parsley and add it to the gravy.

Time to boil your peas. Cover your peas in boiling water and bring to the boil for around 3 minutes. Once boiled, drain them and add to the pan the juice of 1 lemon, a tablespoon of olive oil and a sprinkling of pepper. Then, mash the peas roughly, leaving a bit of crunch.

Once your potatoes have boiled and are soft, drain the water from the pan and put them back into it. Add in your butter, milk and a tsp of mustard, along with a sprinkling of salt and pepper. Mash this all together until it is nice and smooth.
Get the mash, peas and sausages onto a plate, pour over your gravy and finish with a big dollop of English mustard on top.

name: Ultimate Breakfast Sandwich
description: Founder of The Fry Up Police, Thomas Shiers, presents his Ultimate Breakfast Sandwich. All your favourite fry-up ingredients in a bap with a secret mayo sauce.
instructions: Start by defrosting your hash browns, mash them up with your hands and cut or form them into 4 patties, set aside.
Squeeze out your sausage meat and cut them into 4 patties. Add a glug of oil into a frying pan and fry your sausage patties on a low and slow heat (good things can’t be rushed).
Move your patties to the edge of the pan and fry your bacon. Flip the bacon once it begins to get brown and crispy on one side.

Make room for your hash browns to fry. Once golden on one side, flip them. Add 2 slices of cheese on top of each sausage patty. Then, place 2 rashers of bacon on top of the sausage and leave to melt together until the cheese is oozing.
Meanwhile, halve and whack your burger buns in and lightly toast so they begin to char. Once your patties are ready, take everything off the pan and set aside.

Fried egg time. Into a new pan, add a generous glug of oil and crack your eggs in once the oil is very hot. Again, cook on a low and slow heat. Drizzle the oil over the top of the egg to baste it. Season with pepper and continue to coat the egg in oil until perfectly cooked. Set your egg aside and construct your sauce.

Take your mayo, ketchup and hot sauce and whisk together in a bowl until fully combined. Smother your buns with a dollop of the sauce. Assemble with your bun, hash brown patty, then your sausage patty with your bacon and finally the egg. Repeat these steps for the rest of the sandwiches. Then, tuck into the best breakfast sarnie you will ever eat. Enjoy!

name: Ultimate Buffalo Wings
description: This simple buffalo wings recipe is tangy and crispy and addictive. These are without a doubt the best buffalo wings you’ll ever eat. Plus, there's no frying required.
instructions: Add the baking powder, salt, and cornflour into a bowl, mix well. Pat the wings dry and toss them into the mixture, until everything is evenly coated. Place the wings onto an oiled wire rack in one even layer and let it dry out for 45 mins-1 hour minimum, or overnight in the fridge until dry. If you don’t have a wire rack, place them onto a parchment lined baking tray in one layer.
Once the wings are dried, preheat the oven to 220°C. Bake the wings, 30-40 mins, until golden and crispy – the skin should have puffed up and bubbled in places.

Meanwhile, add half of the butter into a saucepan. Place onto medium heat and let melt. Cook, stirring constantly until the solids have turned brown, 4-6 mins – it should smell nutty. Remove from the heat and whisk in the hot sauce and remaining butter.
Toss the wings and sauce together before serving.

name: Ultimate Cauliflower Cheese
description: This is Mob’s best ever cauli cheese recipe, with lashings of luscious cheese sauce and roasted cauliflower. No roast dinner table is complete without it.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Cut the cauliflower into large florets, then cut the stem into 2cm pieces. Tip onto a baking tray along with any nice, young leaves from the cauliflower. Drizzle with a little oil, season well with salt and pepper and put into the oven for 25 mins until beginning to char at the edges.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium-high heat. Once foaming, tip in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 4-5 mins until the colour has noticeably darkened and it is smelling toasty. Lower the heat to medium. Measure the milk and cream into a large jug, then pour in a little bit of it and whisk furiously. Keep repeating this process until you have a luscious, smooth sauce.

Coarsely grate the cheddar and gruyère and scatter ¾ of it into the sauce, spoon in the mustard and finely grate in the nutmeg. Stir together over a medium heat until the cheese has melted into the sauce. Season with salt and pepper.

Once the cauliflower has roasted, tip it into a high-sided baking dish where the florets sit relatively snugly in an even layer. Pour the sauce over the top, then scatter with the remaining cheese. At this stage, you could cover and chill for up to 24 hours before finishing.
Turn or heat the oven to 200°C fan. Pop the cauli cheese in the oven (we like to put it on a flat baking sheet to catch any drips) and bake for 20-25 mins or until golden and bubbling.
Finely chop the chives and scatter over for a final allium punch.

name: Ultimate Charred Greens Plate
description: A plate of blistered and charred greens that'll make even the most devout meat-lover swoon. This is some serious business.
instructions: Cut the cabbage into four wedges. Rub with olive oil, season with salt and set aside on a tray. Turn the oven to 180°C fan.
Tip the asparagus, green beans, mangetout and sugar snaps into a large bowl, drizzle with 2-3 tbsp olive oil, season with salt and toss well.

Make the dressing by blitzing the juice of the lemon with the mustard, anchovies (and any oil from the tin) until you get a thick paste. Save a few parsley leaves for the top, then chop the rest of the parsley as finely as you can and tip into a bowl with the blitzed paste. Add enough olive oil to make the dressing a drizzleable consistency, season well with salt and pepper and set aside.
Heat a large frying pan or griddle over a high heat, you want to leave it to get really hot, so you can really char the greens!

Cook the hispi first, lay it on the hot griddle pan with one of the cut-sides down. Cook for 2 mins, until charred, then use tongs to turn and repeat on the other cut side of each wedge. Transfer back to the tray and slide into the oven for 15 mins, until totally softened.
Working in batches, char the other greens in the pan, cooking them for 3-4 mins each. Don’t overcrowd the pan. Lay each batch on a big platter.

Remove the cabbage from the oven and snuggle into the rest of the veg on the platter. Drizzle with the dressing and top with the parmesan. Roughly chop the smoked almonds and scatter on top along with the reserved parsley leaves. Serve with a roast chicken and a big pile of potatoes.

name: Ultimate Cheese Burger
description: The daddy of all burgers. Beef patty, crispy shallots, caramelised onions and an incredible homemade burger sauce. An iconic recipe from Mob Contributor, Thomas Straker.
instructions: Peel and finely slice the onions. Heat a glug of olive oil in a saucepan set over a medium heat. Tip in the onions and cook them slowly for 5 mins until soft. Add a good pinch of salt and then cook for another 5-10 mins until caramelised. Transfer the onions to a plate and set aside.

Finely slice the shallots. Add the cornflour to a bowl and toss the shallots through. Pour your vegetable oil into a large pan and heat it to around 150°C (if you don’t have a thermometer, dip the handle of a wooden spoon and make sure the oil is bubbling steadily around the handle). Add the shallots to the hot oil and fry until golden brown, then remove them with a slotted spoon and transfer to kitchen paper to drain. Season with salt and set aside.
Dice the shallots and mix them with all the other ingredients in a bowl. Set aside in the fridge.
Season the meat with salt and pepper and shape into four equal sized patties.
Set a heavy based frying pan over a medium heat. Cut the buns in half and toast them in the pan on both sides until dark golden. Remove from the pan and set aside.

In the same hot pan, add a glug of vegetable oil. Get the patties in the hot pan set over a medium-high heat (don’t overcrowd it – if it’s a smaller pan, stick to 1 patty so it properly caramelises) and fry it for 2 mins. While the patties cook, press them down firmly to caramelise the edges.
Flip the patty over and whack 2 slices of cheese on top of each. Get the lid on the pan and leave it for another minute or two until the cheese has melted.

Slice your pickles and spread the burger sauce on the bottom of the bun. Add the sliced pickles followed by the caramelised onions, burger patty, more burger sauce and finally the crispy shallots. Add your brioche lid on top and tuck in!

name: Ultimate Chocolate Brownies
description: Meet your new favourite chocolate brownie recipe. They’re fudgy and gooey with crispy tops, and so easy to make.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Line a 25cm square tin with baking parchment. Roughly chop the dark chocolate into 2-3cm pieces. Roughly chop the pistachios.
In a bowl, whisk together the cocoa powder and sifted flours until combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs. Add the chocolate pieces to the same bowl and set aside.
Melt the butter in a small pan over a low heat. Once melted, add the sugar and stir over a low heat until dissolved.
Pour the hot butter into the bowl with the chocolate and eggs and stir until the chocolate has melted. Use an electric whisk to beat the mixture for 3–4 mins.
Add the cocoa and flour mix to the chocolate and butter mix. Use a spoon or spatula to gently fold the ingredients together. Stir in the pistachios.
Transfer the batter to your prepared tin. Bake in the oven for 18 mins, or until you have a crisp top and a middle that wobbles when you gently shake the tray.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool and set in the tin before transferring to a plate. Eat them warm, or keep them in the fridge for later.

name: Ultimate Christmas Dinner
description: The consummate Christmas Dinner. Serves 8. £7.03 a head. Naughty roasties, tender turkey, bacony brussels, pigs in blankets, cranberry sauce & honey glazing.
instructions: Set your oven to full whack.
Take your cumberland sausages and squeeze the sausage meat out of the skin. Next, chop your sage, grate an apple and add some soaked breadcrumbs to a mixing bowl and thoroughly mix together.

Place your turkey into a large baking tray and cover with olive oil and butter, making sure that you cover the entirety of the bird. Next, add a generous amount of salt and pepper and rub into the turkey. Add the ball of stuffing to the cavity of the turkey. At this point, cover the entire tray with tin foil and make a kind of tin foil tent. Now place the turkey in the oven.

As soon as the turkey is in the oven, turn it down to 180°C/356°F and cook for 3½ hours. The most important part of cooking the turkey is basting. Make sure you set yourself a timer every 30 minutes so you don't forget.

First, we need to boil the potatoes. Place your halved potatoes into a saucepan and fill with water to bring to the boil. Once the potatoes are soft on the outside (10 minutes), take them off the boil and drain them. Place them back into the saucepan with the lid on the top and shake them well for a few seconds. This will make them fluffy on the outside – perfect for the golden crunch. Add your goose fat into a baking tray with all 5 cloves of unpeeled garlic and pour the potatoes in. Season with salt pepper and rosemary. Mix thoroughly so the goose fat covers all of the potatoes. Place in the oven for 1 hour, remembering to shake them every 20 minutes to maintain crispiness.

Cut them into strips and halve them. Add 2 tablespoons of honey and wholegrain mustard and mix together. Spread them across 2 baking trays to make sure they all get cooked properly. Place into the oven for 45 minutes.
REMINDER: Make sure you baste that turkey!!!
Take the chipolatas and wrap 12 streaky bacon rashers around the sausages, repeating until this is finished. Spread cranberry sauce over each sausage and place in the oven for 40 minutes.

Half an hour before the turkey is ready, take the foil off and baste for the last time. Once the turkey is cooked take it out of the oven and leave to rest for 30 minutes covering it in foil to retain the heat.

Quarter them and blanch them in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain them. Chop and add your remaining smoked bacon to a wok. Once crispy, chuck in your brussels until they are cooked through. When the dish is ready, chop your tarragon and parsley and add to the wok. Season with salt and pepper.

Take the turkey out of the pan and then place the cooking tray onto a low heat. Take a piece of kitchen roll and run it across the top of the cooking juices – this will remove the top layer of fat that you don’t want in your gravy. Then, crumble a chicken stock cube into the pan. Add your red wine, flour and whisk everything together. Once it is nice and thick, pour the gravy into a jug and its ready to serve!

Peel your onion and stick 5 cloves into it. Pour the milk into a saucepan, add the onion, a bay leaf and a handful of peppercorns. Bring to the boil, then take off the heat and cover with some tinfoil. Allow to rest for 20 minutes before serving. After 20 minutes, remove the onion and bay leaves and sieve the milk, catching the peppercorns. Add the milk back to the pan on a low heat. Add your second knob of butter and 180g of breadcrumbs. Keep whisking the bread sauce until it is a nice, smooth consistency and serve.
Once everything is ready. Carve your turkey making sure to remove the stuffing from the cavities and serve. Enjoy!

name: Ultimate Christmas Gravy
description: Nothing binds a roast dinner together like a few gallons of gravy. This Christmas gravy recipe is completely worth the time and effort.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Chuck the chicken wings onto a tray and coat with a little olive oil. Slide into the oven for 20-25 mins until golden-brown. Whip the tray out and tip in the white wine, then return the tray to the oven for 10 mins.
Roughly chop the veggies into chunks and add to a large saucepan with a shot of oil. Set over a high heat and cook the veggies for 5-10 mins until caramelised.

Tip in the wine and chicken wings and your herbs, scraping all the flavour from the tray as you go, and add the chicken stock. Bring the mixture to a simmer then reduce the heat to low and leave it to gently simmer away for 75 mins, uncovered.

Strain the mixture through a sieve and discard the solids, then return the liquid to the pan and turn the heat up to medium-high. Leave it to bubble away until reduced by one third to thicken. To a small bowl, add the cornflour and an equal amount of water and mix to combine. Tip this slurry into the pan and whisk to thicken into a gravy.
Season with salt and pepper and a splash of sherry vinegar, if needed.

name: Ultimate Cookie Dough
description: This cookie dough recipe has been specially made to be eaten raw, so contains no egg. We’ve used chocolate chips but you can swap for your fave chocolate bar, chopped, for the ultimate cookie dough fix.
instructions: Heat the flour in the microwave for 30 seconds (this makes it sterile) then leave to cool.

Beat the butter and sugars together in a bowl until well combined, then add the milk and vanilla. Sieve in the cooled flour. Mix again until resembling a cookie dough, then stir in the chocolate chips along with a pinch of salt.
The cookie dough is now ready to eat. Our favourite way is to roll it into little balls and add to a bowl of vanilla ice cream.

name: Ultimate Coronation Chicken Sandwiches
description: If Indian food is your cup of tea, you’re in luck. This coronation chicken recipe takes the best aspects of a curry dish and puts them into a sandwich. It’s as good as it sounds.
instructions: Get a small frying pan over a medium heat, tip in the flaked almonds and toast for a few mins, until nicely golden. Scrape into a small bowl and set aside.

Finely chop all the spring onions (both green and white parts), add ⅔ to the same frying pan along with a drizzle of oil and cook over a medium heat for a few minutes until soft, then stir in the curry powder. Cook for 1 minute more then scrape into a large bowl.

If not already broken up, pull apart the chicken into bite-sized pieces, then add to the bowl with the spring onions and curry powder. If using dried apricots, snip with scissors into the bowl, or if using sultanas simply scatter them in.

Add the mango chutney, yoghurt, mayo, chicken and ½ the flaked almonds then give everything a good mix so that the chicken gets covered in the coronation sauce. Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice to taste.
Separate the Little Gem lettuce leaves, squeeze over a little lemon juice and season.

Divide the lettuce between the bases of four slices of the bread, top with the coronation chicken, remaining spring onion and flaked almonds then sandwich together with the remaining bread slices to serve.

name: Ultimate Doughnuts
description: It’s time you made your own doughnuts. These ones are soft and pillowy in the middle and perfectly crisp on the outside. Toss them in sugar or fill them with vanilla custard cream – either way, you’ll love them.
instructions: In the bowl of a stand mix, combine the sugar and warm water. Crumble in the yeast and mix together. Leave to sit for 10 mins, or until starting to bubble slightly. Make sure the butter is at room temperature.

Add the flour and eggs to the yeast mixture and knead until a dough forms. Mix in the salt, then add in the softened butter, a little at a time, making sure it’s incorporated well after each addition. Continue until the dough is smooth and glossy. Cover the bowl and place in the fridge overnight, or prove at room temperature for about 2-3 hours until doubled in size.

Remove the dough from the bowl and place onto a clean work surface. Flour your hands as the dough will be quite wet. Portion the dough out into 60-65g pieces and roll into tight balls (you may need to use a bench scraper if the dough sticks to the surface). Cut 8 squares of baking paper, and place each dough ball onto one. Cover with a tea towel and leave to prove at room temperature for another 30-45 mins.

If you want to fry the doughnuts: Add enough sunflower oil into a saucepan so it’s filled halfway up. Once the dough has proved, set the saucepan over a medium-high heat and heat the oil to 170°C. Drop a couple of doughnuts into the oil then peel back the baking paper and discard. Fry on both sides until golden brown then transfer to a wire rack tray. Continue until all the doughnuts have been fried.
If you want to bake the doughnuts: Heat the oven to fan 180°C. Place the doughnuts onto a large tray, spacing them out, and bake for 20-30 mins, until golden brown and baked through.
Once the doughnuts have cooled, fill them with custard cream or jam, or simply toss in a bit of sugar.

name: Ultimate Fish Pie
description: The secret ingredient in our fish pie? Anchovies. Melt them down into your leeks for a serious umami hit. They go beautifully with the crispy caper topping.
instructions: Prep your veg. Slice your leek and grate your garlic. Chop your parsley and capers and grate your parmesan.

Pour your milk into a medium sized saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer, then pop your salmon and haddock into the pan. Simmer on a very low heat for 5 mins, then remove from the milk with a slotted spoon and pop on a plate until later.

Melt half of your butter in a large pan. Add your leeks and cook over a medium heat for 10 mins until they are super soft. Add your anchovies and grate in your garlic - cook out for 2 minutes, breaking up your anchovies with the back of your spoon.

Add your flour and cook out for 2 minutes before gradually adding your fishy milk, beating to ensure it stays super smooth. Bring your sauce to a simmer for 2 mins until it thickens. Season with salt and pepper and a handful of chopped parsley. Break up your fish into bite sized chunks and add this too, along with your raw prawns.
Heat oven to 190°C/374°F.

Peel and dice your potatoes, then pop them in a pan. Cover them with cold water and add a generous pinch of salt, then bring to a boil. Simmer until tender, about 15 mins. Drain and leave your potatoes to steam dry in your colander for a few minutes, then mash and add the rest of your butter and milk. Season to taste with salt.
Mix your breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, chopped capers and parmesan in a bowl.
Pour your mixture into a pie dish. Top with your mash, then your crispy breadcrumbs. Bake for 25-30 mins in the oven until you have a golden, crispy top. Serve with peas!

name: Ultimate Fry Up by The Fry Up Police
description: The definitive ultimate fry-up, by the legend that is Tom Shiers (of The Fry Up Police). Reckon you can do better?
instructions: Start by cooking your sausages in a frying pan. The key is to cook them low and slow to get the maximum flavour out of them. As the sausages begin to brown, add your bacon to the pan and cook in the same way.

Take a new pan and add a drizzle of olive oil to the pan. Cut your tomatoes in half and cook them middle side down. Add your mushrooms to the pan along with your butter and allow it to melt in to the veg.

Egg Time. Pour a very generous glug of olive oil into a frying pan so it covers the bottom and crack your eggs in. As they begin to cook take a spoon and cover the eggs in the oil. Once cooked set aside and keep warm.
To make your potato rösti, grate your potatoes and wrap them up in a tea towel. Take a bowl and squeeze your tea towel to draw all of the moisture out of your grated potatoes.

Then, place them into a separate bowl and season with salt and pepper and mix together. Take a handful of the potatoes and squeeze together so you get a rectangular shape and add this to a well oiled frying pan (you can use the same one your eggs were in) and repeat until you have 4 evenly sized rösti’s. Cook until golden brown on both sides.
Time for the beans. Whack them into a saucepan and cook until they are nice and hot.
As your meat is cooking, add your slices of black and white pudding, make sure that the pan is nice and hot. The important part of here is to make sure that they get nicely charred on either side.
Once your meat is cooked, take your bread and cook the slices in the fat from the bacon until they are golden brown each side.

Plating up time. Place your eggs on top of your fried bread. Make sure each plate has 2 sausages, 2 rashers of bacon, 2 slices of black and white pudding, 2 eggs, 1 slice of bread, 1 spoonful of beans, 1 spoonful of mushrooms, 1 potato rösti and half a tomato.

To make your bloody mary: add 60ml of your bloody mary mix, next 50ml of vodka, a squeeze of lemon, 50ml of tomato juice and top with some ice and a celery stick. Repeat 4 times and tuck into the best fry up of your life.

name: Ultimate Greek Salad with Crouton Twist
description: A classic greek salad with crunchy croutons - making it more of a main course than a side. Great summer dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F.

First up – the croutons. Slice the ciabatta into cubes and place in a baking tray with a large glug of olive oil. Sprinkle over the chilli flakes with a large pinch of salt and pepper. Crush up the garlic cloves before adding to the tray and mixing the ciabatta cubes well. Place in the oven for 30 minutes.

Now for the salad base. Peel and slice the red onions into semi-circular discs, before adding to a large mixing bowl with the juice of half a lemon and a pinch of salt. Mix the onions well, setting them aside for 20 minutes to marinate.

Peel your cucumber, before slicing in half and scooping out the middle. Then chop each half into semi circles and set aside. Roughly chop up the tomatoes, placing them in a colander over a bowl with a pinch of salt. Give them a good toss, squeezing out the water contents so that you are left with mostly tomato flesh. This helps avoid the salad having a watery consistency.
Onto the dressing. Pour 5 tbsp of olive oil into a jar along with the balsamic vinegar, oregano and a large pinch of salt. Screw the lid on tightly, before giving the jar a good shake!

Assembly time! Into a large salad bowl place your strained tomatoes, chopped cucumber, Kalamata olives and sliced red onion. Crumble two thirds of the feta block in too, before adding the homemade croutons. Roughly chop up the basil, before sprinkling in a handful. Drizzle over the dressing, then toss well.
Time to plate up: serve with a sprinkle more basil, crumbling the rest of the feta over the top. A final glug of oil and another pinch of pepper and you’re ready to tuck in!

name: Ultimate Hot Chocolate
description: This is my take on the French-style hot chocolate. It's super rich and creamy and takes just 4 ingredients and 10 minutes to make.
instructions: Lightly whip 60% of your double cream until you have very soft peaks and set aside in a cool place.
Roughly chop the chocolate.

Place the milk, icing sugar and remaining double cream in a sauce pan and gently warm over a medium heat. Add in the chocolate and reduce to a low heat. Stir for a couple of minutes until the chocolate has all melted and emulsified to create your hot chocolate. It should be a similar consistency to double cream and glossy.
Pour the hot chocolate into mugs and top each with a spoon of the whipped cream.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Ultimate Hot Cross Buns
description: Follow this recipe to the letter and you'll have a perfect batch of hot cross buns on your hands. The ultimate hot cross buns recipe.
instructions: Pour the tea into a large bowl, then stir through the milk and mixed dried fruit. Set aside and let it steep and come down to lukewarm temperature (around 37°C).
Put the sugar, orange zest and lemon zest into another large bowl. Rub together until the sugar goes sandy. Stir through the flour, mixed spice and salt.

Once the tea mixture is lukewarm, discard the tea bag and whisk the yeast and egg into the milky mixture. Stir the wet ingredients and butter into the flour until a dough forms. Tip onto a clean work surface and knead for 10-15 mins until a smooth dough forms. The dough will start off very tacky and sticky, but trust the process – keep kneading and it will transform. Form the dough into a ball and place into a bowl lightly greased with butter. Cover and prove for 1-1½ hrs until doubled in size.

Once proved, tip the dough out onto a clean surface. Portion out into 12 pieces. Roll each piece into a smooth, taught ball and place into a 30cmx22cm baking tin greased with butter. Loosely cover and set aside to prove for 45 mins-1 hr, until puffy. You can test the dough by gently poking it with a wet finger – if it slowly bounces back and leaves an indentation, it’s ready.

Halfway through proving, heat the oven to 180°C. Add the ingredients for the cross into a bowl and gently stir until just combined. Transfer to a sandwich or piping bag and snip a tiny bit of the corner off. Once the buns are proved, pipe the crosses on.
Transfer the buns to the oven and bake for 20-25 mins until golden brown. Once baked, gently heat the apricot jam and brush it over the warm hot cross buns. Leave to cool before serving.

name: Ultimate Hot Cross Buns
description: Follow this recipe to the letter and you'll have a perfect batch of hot cross buns on your hands. The ultimate hot cross buns recipe.

name: Ultimate Hummus
description: Perfect silky smooth hummus. Use the best quality chickpeas and extra virgin olive oil you can as it really makes a difference.
instructions: Pour the water out of the top of the chickpea jar into a jug then tip the remaining chickpeas and their liquid into a blender or food processor. Add the tahini, finely grate in the garlic if using and add the ground cumin and the juice of ½ the lemon, then blitz.

You want to keep blitzing the hummus until it is silky smooth. If still a little coarse, add a little more chickpea liquid and blitz again. Season to taste with salt, pepper and more lemon juice if you like.
Spoon or pour the hummus into a bowl, top with a generous drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkling of za’atar. Serve with everything. Obvs.

name: Ultimate Hummus Bowl
description: Nothing beats a bowl of creamy hummus. Warming the chickpeas and using a lot of tahini are our top tips for getting that silky texture. Serve with flatbreads.
instructions: Flatbread time. Measure the flour, Greek yoghurt, 2 tbsp of za’atar and salt into a large bowl. Pour in 2 tbsp of cold water and mix together to form a dough. If it looks dry, add an extra tablespoon of water. Tip the dough out onto a lightly-floured surface and knead for 2 mins until smooth. Cover with a tea towel and leave to rest.
For the hummus, tip the chickpeas along with their water into a saucepan and gently heat (warmed chickpeas = creamiest hummus).

Ladle the chickpeas, along with a little of their water, into a food processor (if you have a small one you will have to do this in two batches). Cut the lemons in half. Add the cumin, tahini, garlic if using and squeeze in the juice of one lemon. Blitz for 2–3 mins until completely smooth. Season to taste with salt and black pepper, adding a little more lemon if you like and chickpea water if you want a looser texture.
Thinly slice the radishes and scrape into a bowl. Squeeze over the remaining lemon juice and season with salt. Set aside to quick-pickle.
Cut your dough into eight pieces. Using a rolling pin, roll the dough out on a floured surface into oval flatbreads around 5mm thick.

Get a large non-stick frying pan super-hot over a high heat. Cook the flatbreads one at a time, for 2 mins on each side until they have bubbled up and are a little charred in places. Once cooked, pile the flatbreads on top of each other inside a tea towel and sprinkle with a little water – this will keep them squidgy.

Spoon the hummus into a large serving bowl. Drizzle over a good amount of olive oil and swirl the harissa on top. Pile a handful of pickled chillies to one side along with the quick-pickled radishes and sprinkle over the remaining za’atar. Serve with the flatbreads.

name: Ultimate Roast Beef
description: Say goodbye to dry roast beef. This is the ultimate roast beef recipe for a super delicious & juicy centrepiece.
instructions: 1-2 hrs before you start cooking, remove the roasting joint from the fridge and pat it dry with kitchen paper. Generously season all over with salt and leave on the counter uncovered for 1-2 hours to come to room temperature. The salt will season the meat and draw out the excess moisture to allow us to get a better crust. 2 hrs is ideal but 1 hr will do just fine.
When the time is up, heat the oven to 150°C fan. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over a high heat for 3-4 mins.
Pat the beef dry with kitchen paper again then rub with ⅓ of the oil. Season with more salt and pepper.
Add the remaining oil to the hot pan and sear the beef for 30-45 secs on each side until nicely browned.

Remove from the pan onto a wire rack lined oven tray and place in the oven for 45 mins for medium rare. If you have a temperature probe, check the beef after 40 mins and remove from the oven when the internal temperature reaches 38°C.

Remove the beef from the oven and cover loosely with foil to rest for at least 30 mins. You really can’t skip this part; it’s best to view this period as a continuation of the cooking process. If you slice the beef now, it’ll be very uncooked. Over the 30 mins, the internal temperature will gently increase to 55°C and give you an amazing finished product.
To serve, slice the beef against the grain and plate it up. We love to eat it with horseradish cream, gravy and roast potatoes.

name: Ultimate Roast Potatoes
description: The crispiest, most delicious roast potatoes you’ll ever eat. Follow the method to the letter. Roast garlic is key.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F.
Peel your potatoes and quarter them. Add to a pan of boiling water with a large pinch of salt. Parboil for 10 minutes.
While the potatoes are cooking, add goose fat to a roasting tray. Place tray in the oven for 10 minutes so the fat can melt and heat through.
Drain your potatoes and re-add to the pan. Place a lid on top and give them a good shake. Remove the lid. The outside of the potatoes should be nice and fluffy. This is KEY to the crispiness.

Place your fluffy potatoes in the roasting tray. Add 10-12 whole garlic cloves (skin on), a large handful of rosemary, a large handful of thyme, a big pinch of salt and some pepper. Toss everything together. Place the potatoes in the oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
KEY PART OF THE METHOD. Every 25 minutes you need to remove the roasting tray from the oven and gently turn the potatoes in the goose fat. This will ensure a nice even golden outside.
Once the potatoes are gold all over, remove from the oven. Serve with some salt sprinkled on top and enjoy!

name: Ultimate Roast Turkey
description: The perfect roast turkey recipe. Say goodbye to basting, butter and stress. This is the best way to achieve crispy skin and juicy meat. The trick is letting the turkey air dry in the fridge for a couple of days before cooking.
instructions: Remove the turkey from the packaging and pat dry with kitchen paper. Make sure to remove any residue inside the cavity.
Season generously all over with fine salt. Pop a wire rack on top of an oven dish, then place the turkey on the rack.

Put the turkey, uncovered, in the fridge for 24-48 hours to air-dry. This is where the magic happens; the salt is going to pull the moisture from the skin and season the meat to allow for a crispy and juicy bird.
When it’s time to cook, heat the oven to 230°C fan.
Remove the liquid that has collected in the bottom of the oven dish and pat the turkey dry with a paper towel. It’s super important to dry the skin well.
Brush the whole bird with vegetable oil and season with more salt. We want to avoid adding butter here, as butter is full of moisture and will prevent the skin from browning.
Tie the legs together at the ankles with butchers twine and lay the turkey back on the wire rack.
Pop the turkey inside the oven and immediately reduce the oven temperature to 210°C.
If you have a temperature probe the thickest part of the breast should read 66-68°C and the thigh should read 72-74°C.

Remove the turkey from the oven and leave to rest, uncovered, for 35 mins before carving. The turkey needs to rest for this time to cook fully so you can’t skip this step! Serve with all the Christmas dinner sides.

name: Ultimate Spag Bol
description: To be clear, spag bol isn’t about making something ‘traditional’, it’s about having fun. Sure, we’re borrowing some ideas from the Bolognese classic (adding milk) but also ingredients from ragu found in other parts of Italy, like herbs from ragu Toscano, and finishing with a truly British addition, Worcestershire sauce. Rich, meaty, nostalgic you’ll make it again and again.
instructions: Heat your oven to 160°C fan.
Add the pancetta to a large, heavy pan with a drizzle of olive oil. Place it over a low-medium heat and gently cook until the fat is released and the pancetta starts to turn crispy.

Meanwhile finely chop the onion, carrot and celery and peel the garlic. Add to the pan along with the butter, a pinch of salt, the bay leaves and rosemary and fry for 8-10 mins until the veggies are soft and the pancetta is nice and browned. Don’t rush this step.

Transfer the contents of the pan to a bowl and set aside. Return the empty pan to the hob, turn up the heat to high and tip in the beef mince and a big pinch of salt. Use the back of your spoon to break the mince up and fry until brown.

Pour in the red wine and let it bubble away over the high heat until reduced by half. Add the Worcestershire sauce then pour in the stock followed by the plum tomatoes. Return the veggies and pancetta to the pan and pour in the milk. Add the salt (the full amount listed in the ingredients list), bring to a simmer, then place a lid on and transfer to the oven for 2½ hrs.

Once the ragu is ready, you can cook your pasta and serve straightaway, but the sauce is even better made the day before and then reheated. If you are prepping ahead of time, let the ragu cool to room temp and place in the fridge overnight. The next day, use a spoon to scrape off the layer of fat which will have solidified on top.

Either way, when ready to eat, cook your spaghetti in a large pan of boiling salted water for 2 mins less than the packet instructions. Drain in a colander, saving a mug full of the salty, starchy cooking water.

Return the spaghetti to the pan you boiled it in and spoon in the ragu. Place over a low-medium heat and continue cooking, stirring and adding splashes of the reserved water (it should be bubbling but not frying) for another 2 mins or so, until you have a thick glossy sauce that clings to the pasta.
Serve with black pepper, lots of Parmesan, and garlic bread on the side!

name: Ultimate Tiramisu
description: This Italian dessert is surprisingly easy to make and can be made ahead of time. Serve it at your next dinner party and your guests will be scraping their bowls.
instructions: Make the coffee by dissolving the espresso powder into the boiling water. Set aside.

Get the double cream, mascarpone, marsala wine and caster sugar in a mixing bowl. Use an electric whisk to beat until you have a smooth mixture the consistency of thick whipped cream. You can also do this by hand, but it will take longer.
Pour your coffee into a shallow dish, then dip in your sponge fingers, a few at a time, turning each for a few seconds until they are soaked but not soggy.

Place a layer of soaked sponge fingers into a large shallow dish until you’ve used half of the fingers, then spread over half of the creamy mixture. Coarsely grate most of the dark chocolate over the top.
Repeat the layers, using up all the coffee, and finishing with a layer of boozy cream.
Cover the tiramisu with tin foil and chill in the fridge for 2 hours or overnight.
When ready to serve - dust with the cocoa powder and grate over the remainder of the chocolate.

name: Ultimate Tiramisu
description: The one you’ve all been waiting for: our ultimate tiramisu recipe. Creamy but not too sweet, it’s a proper punchy end to a meal thanks to the combo of amaretto and coffee.
instructions: Separate your eggs and put the whites into a mixing bowl or bowl of a stand mixer and the yolks into a small bowl. Add half the sugar to the whites and whisk into soft peaks. Set aside.
Add the remaining half of the sugar to the yolks and whisk until pale. Add the mascarpone and whisk again until smooth.
Carefully fold the egg whites into the mascarpone mix a bit at a time, trying to knock out as little air as possible.
Brew 300ml of coffee, add 50ml of amaretto to that brew, and pour the lot into a small tray.
Line a baking tray with kitchen paper.
Dip the savoiardi biscuits into the coffee mix for about 3 seconds, then place on the tray with the paper (so they don’t sit in the coffee mix and go completely soggy).
Make a single layer of biscuits across the bottom of the tiramisu dish. Now, spread half the cream over the biscuits. Repeat with the second layer of biscuits and remaining cream.
Cover with cling film and leave to sit in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
When ready to serve, dust generously with cocoa powder.

name: Ultimate Toad In The Hole
description: Meaty pork sausages surrounded by Yorkshire pudding batter. Crisp on the outside, custardy and soft on the inside. Lashings of onion gravy to serve. The GOAT. Absolutely yes, please.
keywords: Ultimate Toad In The Hole Recipe
instructions: Start by making the toad in the hole batter. Crack the eggs into a large bowl and pour in the milk, then strip the leaves from half of the thyme into the bowl. Add a pinch of flaky sea salt and whisk together. Tip in most of the flour, keeping about 1 tablespoon for later and whisk again until you have a smooth batter. Pour into a jug, cover and leave for at least an hour, but preferably overnight. (chill if you leave it overnight).

When you’re nearly ready to cook, finely slice the onions and set aside. Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of vegetable oil. Add the sausages and cook for 2 mins on each side, turning so they are deeply golden. Scoop out onto a plate.

Pour another drizzle of vegetable oil into the pan and scrape in the onions along with a big pinch of salt, and strip the remaining thyme leaves in. Pop a lid on (or put a piece of baking paper directly over the onions), turn the heat down to low, and cook for 45-60 mins, stirring regularly until the onions are a deep golden and have started to collapse.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Drizzle a glug of vegetable oil into a large, deep metal baking tin (roughly 25cm x 35cm) and put into the oven to heat for 20 mins.

Scatter in the remaining flour and cook for a minute then spoon in the mustard and pour in the beef stock. Bring to a simmer, turn up the heat and cook for around 15-20 mins or until thickened. Season with salt and black pepper.

Once the oil in the baking tray is hot, arrange the sausages in the tray, then pour in the pre-made batter. Put straight back into the oven and cook for 30-35 mins until puffed and a deep golden brown.
To serve, cut the toad in the hole into quarters and serve with lashings of the onion gravy.

name: Ultimate Tofu Scramble
description: Here's my recipe for the ultimate tofu scramble. It's perfectly creamy, well seasoned, makes a great filling for sandwiches, a toast topping or a tasty side.
instructions: Drain and pat the tofu dry with a teatowel. No need to press it as we want to keep some of the moisture here.

Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat and then crumble the tofu in large chunks into the pan. Season well with salt and pepper and fry. Stirring often for about 8-10 mins until the edges turn golden brown.
Meanwhile, blend all the other ingredients in a blender until smooth.
Turn off the heat and stir through the blender mix. Add a little more milk to the pan if you’d prefer it more runny. Taste and season well with salt and pepper.
Serve in a sandwich with mustard, mayo and cress or as a scramble with toast or on a lovely crumpet (yes most crumpets are vegan!)

name: Ultimate Vegan Bánh Mì
description: It’s not unusual to find street vendors selling vegan Bánh Mì in Vietnam. I’ve recreated a classic version with vegan 'pulled pork' style protein.
instructions: First, make your pickles. Start by slicing the carrot and cucumber into small batons (sticks) with a knife or a julienne peeler. Slice one jalapeño thinly and save the other for garnish.
In a small saucepan, add 240ml water, 240ml white vinegar, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp black peppercorns. Bring to a boil and then turn off the heat.
To make the marinade, mince a thumb-sized piece of ginger and one or two garlic cloves.
Then, whisk together 2 tbsp of olive oil, 3 tbsp tamari, the juice and zest of half a lime, the garlic and ginger, 2 tbsp of lemongrass paste and some black pepper.
Add one 220g pack of Eatplanted Pulled Pork to the marinade and set aside to marinate while you make the rest of the fillings.

To make the paté, add the vegan 'pulled pork' protein to a blender with 85ml of water. Add 1tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp miso, 2 tsp Moscatel or sherry vinegar, 1 stock cube and 2 tsp butter. Blend to a paté, season to taste and adjust the consistency with a little more water if you like.
Mix the mayonnaise with the sriracha in a small bowl.
Slice the remaining chilli, the spring onion and pick some coriander leaves for your garnish.

name: Ultimate Vegan Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Perfect plant-based cookies with dark chocolate chunks. Nobody will guess these are vegan.
keywords: Ultimate Vegan Chocolate Chip Cookies recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to fan 180°C. Line a large baking tray with baking paper. Break the chocolate into 1-2cm chunks.
Whisk the oil, water and sugar together until incorporated and thick.
In another bowl, mix together the sugar, flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, salt and chocolate chunks. Tip this flour mixture into the sugar and water mixture and stir until combined.

Portion out 2 tbsp of cookie dough and roll into a ball then place on the prepared baking tray. Repeat for all the cookies, making sure to space them out. Finish with a sprinkle of flaky sea salt and bake for 10-15 mins, until golden and crisp on the edges.
Let the cookies cool for 5-10 mins before serving.

name: Umami Miso Butter Udon
description: Chewy udon noodles with crispy guanciale in an umami miso butter sauce, topped with soy-cured egg yolk. Sort of a riff on a carbonara.
instructions: For the cured yolks: pour the soy and mirin into a small container, then finely grate the ginger in. Stir, then gently place the egg yolks in. If the soy mixture doesn’t cover the yolks, gently place a kitchen paper towel over, letting the towel absorb some of the marinating liquid. Close the container and place in the fridge for a minimum of 4 hours or up to overnight. The longer you let them marinate, the firmer they will be. If you're in a rush, you can make this dish without the cured yolks.
Place a saucepan full of water to a boil over a medium-high heat. Thinly slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish.
Add the guanciale to a frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Cook for 5-7 mins until golden then turn the heat down to low, add the butter and leave to melt.
Meanwhile, stir the miso with a splash of water until it’s thinned out and a drizzle-able consistency.
Cook the udon in the boiling water following packet instructions. Reserve a cup of udon cooking water, and drain and rinse the udon under cold running water.

Transfer the udon to the pan with the cooked guanciale and turn the heat up to medium-high. Add a splash of the noodle water and the miso mixture and toss to combine until glossy and hot. Remove from the heat and toss the Parmesan through until thickened. If it’s too thick, add another splash of water. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper, if needed.
Drain the cured egg yolks. Share the udon between bowls, spooning over the miso butter sauce. Top with a cured yolk and the sliced spring onion.

name: Umami Pork & Prawn Noodles
description: Inspired by one of my favourite dumplings, siu mai. The same ingredients you’d normally find inside the dumplings, instead stir-fried with noodles. My favourite mushrooms to use are shiitake, they’re a lot more flavourful, but any mushrooms you like will work.
keywords: pork and prawn stir fry noodles
instructions: Stir all the sauce ingredients together in a bowl and set aside. Bring a large pot of water to the boil.
Bash the ginger. Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites from the greens. Thinly slice the mushrooms.

Add the ginger and a drizzle of olive oil to a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once fragrant, 2-3 mins, add the mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned, 6-8 mins. Transfer to a plate.

Return the pan to the heat and, once hot, add the mince, season and fry until browned, 7-9 mins. Meanwhile, cook the noodles according to packet instructions. Drain and rinse under cold running water.

Once the mince has browned, add the prawns, season generously and cook until opaque and cooked through, 3-4 mins. Add the mushrooms back in, then toss through the noodles and sauce until everything is coated. Taste and season with more chilli oil, soy or balsamic if needed.
Divide between plates or boxes and top with the spring onion greens.

name: Urfa Roast Chicken With Peach & Courgette Salad
description: This is the traybake to end all traybakes. The peach and scotch bonnet dressing is next level. Make it, share it, treasure it.
keywords: Urfa Roast Chicken With Peach & Courgette Salad
instructions: Grab the chicken and pat dry. Using scissors, remove the backbone by snipping either side from the legs to the breast. Open the chicken up a little, then using a heavy knife, cut through the back of the breast bone to split the chicken into two halves, see the video for visual cues.

Mix the sugar with double the amount of salt and the urfa and sprinkle all over the chicken with a good glug of oil, pop into the fridge for an hour. When almost ready to cook, pull your chicken out of the fridge to come up to room temperature.

Preheat your oven to 225°C. Leaving the skin on, cut the shallots in half lengthways and chuck into a roasting tin with the drained chickpeas, one whole peach, the whole scotch bonnet, unpeeled garlic cloves and the rosemary. Nestle the chicken on top, skin-side up.

Slide into the oven for 45-50 mins, or until the chicken is cooked through and the juices run clear. Pull out the chicken and let it rest for 15 mins. Add the chickpeas to a large bowl, scooping out the roasted veggies.
Peel the burnt skin from the shallots and separate into petals. Chuck the roasted peach into a bowl with the roasted scotch bonnet. Peel the garlic cloves and get those in there too.

Scoop the pit out of the peach and then, using a fork, mash the scotch bonnet and peach together with a good splash of sherry vinegar. Add any roasting juices from the pan, and a good glug of oil. Season with salt and pepper and have a taste. It should be sweet, tart and spicy. Tip into the bowl with the chickpeas.
Add the roasted shallots, thinly slice the remaining peach and the courgettes and add to the bowl along with the chickpeas. Tear in the basil and have a taste, season if you need to.
Cut the chicken into chunky portions and serve over the chickpea salad, pouring over any resting juices. Get stuck in.

name: Vanilla Bourbon Chicken Wings
description: Sticky, sweet and savoury oven-baked chicken wings with a vanilla bourbon glaze. Get your friends over and whack a tray of these in the oven. They’re seriously addictive.
instructions: Preheat the oven to fan 190°C. Ensure your butter is very cold.

Pat the chicken wings dry, and place them into a bowl with the oil and cornflour. Season generously with salt and toss together. Space them out onto a large baking tray lined with baking paper, and roast for 30-35 mins.

Add the sugar, bourbon, vanilla extract, tomato ketchup, vinegar and cayenne into a saucepan and place over a medium-high heat. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 8-12 mins or until reduced by half. Take it off the heat, and whisk through the cold butter. Taste and season with salt, pepper and an extra dash of vinegar, if needed.
Meanwhile, pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems. Thinly slice the chives then toss all the herbs together with the crispy onions.
Once the wings are baked, transfer to a bowl and toss with the glaze. Toss ½ the herb mixture through.
Plate up and top with the remaining herb mix.

name: Vanilla Ice Cream
description: Making your own ice cream is easier than you think, and it’s so much better than shop-bought. This one is creamy and luxurious with fresh vanilla pods. Perfection.
instructions: Pour the milk into a pan, add the vanilla pod and bring slowly up to scalding point – do not let it reach the boil. Cover the surface with clingfilm to prevent a skin forming, then leave to cool and infuse with the vanilla for approximately 1 hour. Once cool, carefully remove the vanilla pod from the pan and scrape out the seeds into the milk.
Tip a bag of ice cubes into the sink and place a large wide metal bowl on top, to chill the bowl. Alternatively place a metal bowl in the freezer.
In a bowl, beat together the egg yolks and sugar until thick and fluffy – approximately 4 mins. Pour in the vanilla milk and stir until you get a thin custard.

Pour the mixture into a clean heavy-bottomed pan, place over a medium heat and stir continuously with a wooden spoon as you slowly bring it nearly to the boil. When the custard has thickened and the foam bubbles on the surface have disappeared, remove it from the heat, whisk it for a couple of mins with a large balloon whisk (this will help it to cool quicker), then pour into your cold, dry metal bowl.
Leave it to cool for approximately 10 mins, stirring occasionally to prevent a skin forming.

If churning in an ice cream maker: turn on your ice cream maker. Once the mixture has cooled, stir in the cream, churn in the ice cream maker for 30–35 mins, then transfer to an ice cream container and place in the freezer to set completely.

If churning by hand: once the mixture is cool, put it into the fridge for 1-2 hours. Remove, stir in the cream and transfer to an ice cream container. Pop it in the freezer for half an hour, then give it a churn with a spoon returning to the freezer to set completely.

name: Vanilla Panna Cotta With Balsamic Roasted Figs
description: There are few things more pleasing than the gentle wobble of a panna cotta on a plate. Served here with warm, sweet and sour figs. Perfection.
keywords: Vanilla Panna Cotta With Balsamic Roasted Figs Recipe
Vanilla Panna Cotta With Balsamic Roasted Figs
instructions: Fill a bowl with ice cold water and submerge the gelatin leaves in the water to soften.

Pour the double cream, milk, sugar and vanilla bean extract (alternatively, use a vanilla pod: split it in half lengthways and scrape out the seeds) into a saucepan set over a low-medium heat. Heat gently until warm and steaming, stirring regularly, until the sugar has dissolved. Lift the gelatine from the cold water and squeeze out as much cold water as possible. Add the gelatine straight into the pan and stir to dissolve for a minute.
Pour the mixture into a jug and then divide equally between 150ml dariole pudding moulds. Put into the fridge and chill for at least 4 hours but preferably overnight.

When ready to serve, heat the grill to high and line a baking tray with baking paper. Cut the figs into quarters, then lay, cut sides up, on the lined baking tray. Scatter with the sugar and drizzle over the balsamic then slide under the grill for 2-3 mins until golden and bubbling.

Fill a small bowl with warm water. Working one at a time, carefully dip the panna cotta moulds into the bowl of warm water for around 20 seconds, then invert onto a small plate and gently shake until the panna cotta frees itself from the mould. Spoon on the warm figs and any syrup and serve.

name: Vanilla Pouring Custard
description: A beautifully creamy custard that’s perfect for pouring over desserts. No lumps in sight.
instructions: In a heatproof bowl, use a wooden spoon to mix the egg yolks and sugar together until combined.

Heat the cream in a medium saucepan with the salt and vanilla pod until hot but not boiling. You’ll know it’s hot when it starts to steam. Pour the hot cream over the egg yolks, slowly and evenly, whisking continuously as you go. Get someone to help you here if possible – they can pour while you whisk.

Place the bowl over a pan of simmering water. Heat the mixture for about 8 mins, whisking continuously with a large balloon whisk, until it thickens. The custard is ready when the bubbles disappear or when you drag your wooden spoon through the middle and it leaves a mark that takes a moment to disappear.

Remove the vanilla pod, split it lengthways and scrape the seeds back into the custard. If necessary, sieve the custard through a fine mesh to eliminate any lumps, then pour into a jug and serve immediately.

If you’re not planning to serve it right away, you can keep your custard hot by standing it in the jug in a pan of hot water and covering the top (of the custard, not the jug) with clingfilm to prevent a skin forming. If you want to use it cold, you can cover and refrigerate it for up to a day.

name: Vegan Butternut Squash Tagliatelle
description: Roasting and then blending your butternut squash creates a beautiful rich creamy sauce. Topped with crispy sage leaves this plate of food is something else.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/356°F. Cube your sweet potato and slice up your butternut squashes. Add both to a tray. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Roast for 45 minutes.
Finely chop your shallots and garlic. Add to a frying pan with a splash of olive oil and the sage leaves. Cook on a low heat and allow to soften.
Once the squash is soft, remove from the oven. Place half of the squash and sweet potato in a blender with 300ml of water and a stock cube. Blitz until very smooth.
Add the puree to the shallots and stir it in. Add your remaining squash and sweet potato.
Get your pasta on. After 4 minutes, add 5 tbsp of the starchy pasta water to the sauce and mix it in.
Drain the pasta, add it to the sauce and fold it all together. Season well with salt and pepper and tuck in!

name: Vegan Caesar Salad
description: Everyone's favourite salad has had a vegan transformation. We've replicated the funk of anchovies in this plant-based dressing, and it really works.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C/354°F.
Wrap your garlic in tin foil, then place it on a baking tray. Pop it in the oven to roast for 20 mins.

When the 20 mins have elapsed, drain your tin of chickpeas, ensuring you save the liquid from the can. Toss your chickpeas into the tray along with a drizzle of olive oil, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt, then roast for another 10 mins.
Remove your tray from the oven. Tear your ciabatta into the tray, then drizzle with a little more olive oil. Return to the oven for another 15 mins until crispy.
Leave your garlic until cool enough to handle, then place on a chopping board. Press down with your knife to squeeze all the soft, caramelised garlic out.
Measure out 70ml of your aquafaba (chickpea liquid) into a large jug.
Add your roasted garlic, dijon mustard, caper brine, miso paste, soy sauce, the juice of your lemon, 100ml vegetable oil, olive oil and a pinch of salt to the jug.
Pop your stick blender into the jug and blitz until you have a thick and smooth paste - this won’t take very long. Season to taste with salt and lots of black pepper.
Cut the ends off your little gem and separate the leaves.
Put your little gem, chickpeas and croutons into a large serving bowl, along with your capers. Pour in your dressing and toss to coat.
Serve up and enjoy!

name: Vegan Chickpea Stew
description: The creamy tahini dressing drizzled all over the rich, smokey stew is nothing short of sublime. Such a satisfying dish.
instructions: De-seed and slice up your peppers. Chop up your onion.
Add a drizzle of olive oil to a pan. Add peppers and onion. Fry until soft.
Add a handful of chopped coriander, a garlic clove, harissa paste and paprika. Mix well.
Add your butter beans and chickpeas to the pan with their water. Simmer on a low heat for 30 minutes.
Dressing time. Mix the juice of a lemon, tahini, salt and pepper. Add water to loosen the dressing (as much as required).
Add 4 generous handfuls of spinach to the pan and allow to wilt. Season with salt and pepper. Serve in a bowl with a nice drizzle of dressing on top.

name: Vegan Chocolate Chilli
description: A lovely rich chilli. Plant-based. The chocolate brings the depth.
instructions: Finely chop the garlic, onion and peppers. Add to a pan with a splash of olive oil and fry for 5 minutes. Add both cumin and paprika. Mix together. Add a handful of chopped coriander stalks.
Add some water to stop the vegetables catching on the pan. Cook until they have softened.
Add halved chestnut mushrooms. Stir them in and pour in your tomatoes. Mix everything together.. Add cubed tofu. Stir it in.
Add 300ml of water followed by your kidney beans (with the water from the tin).
Get your rice on – follow pack instructions.
Mix the chilli together and let it bubble away on a medium-high heat with no lid for 15 minutes.

After 15 minutes, the chilli should be nice and thick. Add 5 cubes of dark chocolate and allow them to melt. Squeeze in the juice of half a lemon, season with salt and pepper and then add a handful of chopped coriander. Stir it in and remove from the heat.
Serve the chilli on the rice and enjoy!

name: Vegan Chocolate Courgette Cake Recipe
description: The chocolate courgette cake is a delightful vegan treat that cleverly balances rich cocoa with the subtle moisture of courgette. This combination creates a deeply chocolaty cake that remains moist and tender. The courgette, also known as zucchini, not only enhances the cake’s texture but also keeps it moist, making it an excellent choice for a plant-based dessert. The cake can be stored in an airtight container for up to 5 days, preserving its freshness. For longer storage, individual slices can be frozen, making it easy to enjoy a quick cake hit whenever desired. This recipe uses non-dairy milk and plant-based ingredients, perfect for those following a vegan diet. To prepare, you’ll need basic baking equipment like cake pans, parchment paper, and a mixing bowl. For best results, use high-quality cocoa powder and ensure all ingredients, such as self-raising flour and bicarbonate of soda, are well combined to achieve a smooth batter. Enjoy this delicious chocolate courgette cake as a satisfying dessert or a sweet snack!
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Grease a 900g loaf tin with a little oil and line the base with baking parchment.
Whisk the sugar, cocoa powder, flour, bicarb and a big pinch of salt together in a large bowl until there are no lumps of sugar left.
Coarsely grate the courgette using a box grater (no need to peel).

Measure the oil, milk and vinegar into a jug. Whisk with a fork, then pour the wet ingredients into the dry. Add the courgette and chocolate chips and whisk everything together until a rich chocolate cake batter is formed.
Spoon the cake batter into your prepared loaf tin. Bake on the middle shelf in your oven for 50 mins-1 hr until a skewer inserted into the centre of the loaf comes out with a few dry crumbs attached.
Leave the loaf to cool in its tin before cutting into slices to serve.

name: Vegan Coconut Stir Fry
description: Steamy, coconutty rice with delicious charred veggies. Freshened with lime juice. A lovely little dish.
instructions: Chop up all of your vegetables and add them into the wok. Fry them on a high heat until they begin to char. Matchstick your ginger and chop up 1 chilli and add this to your wok, followed by your Kaffir lime leaves. Next, grate your lemongrass into the pan and stir.

Add your rice and stir. Add your soy sauce, grate the zest of your lime into the wok and then squeeze the juice of the lime in. Chop up two thirds of the coriander and Thai basil and add this to the pan and give one final mix.
Garnish with the left over coriander, Thai basil, a squeeze of your remaining lime and your remaining chopped chilli over each dish. Then tuck into this deliciously simple dish.

name: Vegan Creamy Beany Cavolo Nero Pasta
description: A really solid vegan pasta recipe with creamy cannellini beans and a healthy amount of cavolo nero.
keywords: Vegan Creamy Beany Cavolo Nero Pasta
instructions: Trim and halve the fennel, then finely dice. Peel and slice the garlic. Strip the leaves from the cavolo nero stem and roughly chop them. Set everything aside.
Put a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add 4 tbsp olive oil and the pumpkin seeds, then fry for 2-4 mins until toasted. Transfer to a heat-safe bowl and stir the chilli flakes in.

Put the same frying pan over a medium-high heat with another 3 tbsp olive oil. Add the cavolo nero and fennel, then cook for 4-5 mins until wilted and the fennel has softened. Add the garlic, then tip in the veggie stock and the beans (with their liquid). Bring to a boil. Turn the heat down slightly and simmer for 6-8 mins until ¾ of the liquid has evaporated.
Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Once boiling, cook the pasta for 2 mins under al dente.

Once your pasta is ready, use a slotted spoon to transfer the pasta into the greens mixture. Stir in some pasta water to loosen the sauce, if needed. Zest the lemon in, stir and taste. Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Divide the pasta between bowls, dollop the yoghurt on top and finish with the spicy pumpkin seed drizzle

name: Vegan Creamy Tofu Curry
description: We've taken inspo from a curry favourite of ours made with halloumi, but made it vegan. Enter, Creamy Tofu Curry. Don't worry, it's just as delicious.
instructions: Chop the tofu and cauliflower into bite-sized pieces, then finely slice the onion.
Heat a large pan and add the vegetable oil over a medium heat. Add your onions and cook until they start catching on the pan and softening. Once the onions start to brown, add your tofu.

As the tofu starts to brown, grate in peeled garlic cloves and the ginger. Add the turmeric, chilli powder and garam masala. Mix everything together, then add your cauliflower and tomato purée. Mix well.

Pour in your tinned tomatoes and your coconut milk. Stir everything together and smoosh the tomatoes down with the back of your spoon. Simmer on a medium heat until the curry is nice and thick, around 10-15 minutes.
Get your rice on cook, according to package instructions.
Serve the curry on top of your steaming rice. Garnish with freshly chopped coriander.

name: Vegan Don Buri
description: Steve Mangleshot from Wagamama serves up a vegan rice bowl banger in the MOB studio.
instructions:
Prep your veg. Slice your mushrooms and spring onions, then finely chop your garlic and
ginger. Grate your carrot.
Heat your wok over a high heat with a little glug of vegetable oil. Whack in your mushrooms,
garlic and ginger and stir fry for a few minutes until soft and going golden. Add 1 tbsp of
your soy sauce and stir to combine. Set aside and keep warm.
Wipe your wok clean and add a little glug more vegetable oil over a high heat. Crumble your
tofu into the pan and sprinkle over your turmeric with a pinch of salt. Fry for 3 minutes,
breaking up with the back of your spoon to scramble it. Add your remaining soy sauce.
Time to plate up. Divide your rice between four bowls, then top with your mushrooms,
spring onions, grated carrot, tofu and pea shoots. Serve up and enjoy.

name: Vegan Harissa Ragù
description: A thick and rich ragù spiced with a fragrant harissa paste tossed in pasta. This twist on a classic is undoubtedly delicious.
cuisine: Italian, Italian-Inspired, North African, North African-Inspired
instructions: Pulse the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in a food processor until roughly chopped up. This is your soffritto.
Add a big glug of oil to a large pot with a big pinch of salt and add in the soffritto and cook for 15 mins until softened.
Meanwhile, pulse the mushrooms and puy lentils in your food processor until roughly chopped.
Add your rose harissa paste to your sofrito pot and cook for 3 mins.
Then add in the mushrooms and puy lentils and cook for 15 mins until the water has evaporated from the mushrooms.
Add in the chopped tomatoes and let this simmer on a low-medium heat for 30 mins.
Cook your pasta and add this to the sauce with 200ml of pasta water, tossing until it is totally coated.
Serve with parsley.

name: Vegan Mapo Tofu
description: Mapo tofu is the heart and soul of Sichuanese cuisine and is the perfect vehicle for punchy and bold Sichuanese flavours. This vegan version is incredible.
instructions: Gently cut the silken tofu into 2 ½ cm cubes. Get a large saucepan of salted water (the water should be salty like the ocean) over a medium heat. Simmer the tofu on low for 10 minutes then carefully strain.

While the tofu is simmering, get a wok over a high heat and drizzle in the vegetable oil. Once the oil is hot, add the fermented black beans and sugar. Stir continuously until they become fragrant then lower the heat to medium

Add the doubanjiang, stirring continuously so that the doubanjiang doesn’t dry out and stick to the wok (add water to the mixture if it becomes too dry). Add the vegan mince and fry until slightly crisped.

Add 500ml (17fl oz) of water to the wok and then add your strained simmered silken tofu. Be very careful not to break the tofu cubes when incorporating into the other ingredients. At this point add your chilli oil, spring onion, garlic, ginger and 2 tsp of Sichuan peppercorn powder. Mix gently.
Add the cornstarch slurry and gently incorporate. Simmer for a few minutes over a low heat and finish by sprinkling more Sichuan peppercorn powder on top. Serve with rice.

name: Vegan Moussaka
description: This is a classic Greek and Cypriot recipe, made with healthy, plant-based ingredients. It’s a cosy, homely dish that’s perfect for a Sunday lunch. This makes a huge portion but it freezes well, or feel free to halve the recipe.
instructions: You’ll need a large baking dish for this. I used a round, 38cm diameter baking dish but you could use a large rectangular one.
Start by soaking your lentils for at least 20 mins.
Preheat the oven to 180°C Fan.

Wash and peel the potatoes and slice them about 1cm thick. Lay them onto a lined baking tray and brush with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Bake for 20 mins, then flip, brush with a little more olive oil and bake for another 15 mins. They should be cooked through but not too crispy on the edges.

Meanwhile, wash the aubergines and slice 1.5cm thick. Lay them on another baking tray and brush with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Bake below the potatoes for 20 mins, flip and brush with a little more oil, then bake for another 5-8 mins until softened and golden.

To make the lentil filling, finely chop the onions and mince the garlic. Add 3 tbsp of sun dried tomato oil to a large pan or pot. Sweat down the onions on medium heat for about 8-10 mins until translucent. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 -2 mins before adding the chopped tomatoes, then fill each tin with water and add that in too. Drain the lentils well and add these to the pot. Season well with salt and pepper and cook for 20-25 mins until the lentils have softened. Add the soy sauce and balsamic vinegar and cook on high for 3 mins, then turn off the heat.
Finely chop the walnuts, parsley and the sun dried tomatoes and add them to the lentils. Add the nutritional yeast and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Add another tbsp of sun dried tomato oil at the end if you like, for extra richness.

For the béchamel, heat a large saucepan or deep frying pan over low heat and add the olive oil and flour. Use a spatula or a whisk (take care not to use a metal whisk on a non-stick coating) to stir the roux, it will thicken and clump together, but stir as many lumps out as you can. Add the milk very slowly, whisking constantly as you go to get it smooth. Keep adding milk until you have added all of it. 
Add the nutritional yeast, garlic powder, dijon mustard and plenty of salt and pepper. Keep it on a medium-low heat and stir continuously for about 10-15 mins until the sauce has thickened. It should be fairly thick. Taste and adjust seasonings.
Slice the tomatoes 1cm thick.
To assemble, lay the cooked potatoes down first into the baking dish, then spread the lentil mixture, then the tomatoes and finally the aubergines.
Pour the béchamel over the top of the aubergines and spread it evenly. Sprinkle with the breadcrumbs and nutritional yeast, a little salt and pepper and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.
Bake at 200°C for 30-35 mins until the béchamel has a nice golden crust. Allow to cool for at least 10 mins before serving.

name: Vegan Mujadara
description: This recipe is our plant-based version of everyone's favourite dish: mujadara. It’s a hearty, moreish, cosy hug from the inside. Please, please don’t skip the vinegar… it’s essential.
instructions: Finely slice two-thirds of the onions and add to a large frying pan with a glug of olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Cook them over a low-medium heat, stirring often, for 30 mins until deeply caramelised and starting to crisp up. Set aside.

Measure out the water and have it ready. Mince the garlic and add it to a large pot along with a splash of olive oil, the cumin and the tomato purée, if using. Cook for 1 min over a medium heat, stirring constantly to avoid burning, then pour in the water and stock cube.
Rinse the lentils well and add to the pot. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 mins with a lid on slightly ajar.

Add the rice and cook for another 15 mins, again with the lid on ajar, to allow some steam out. Stir the pot every now and then. Add a splash of water if it’s looking a little dry or is sticking to the bottom. Taste and make sure the rice and lentils are very soft – it should be slightly on the wet side.

Add half of the caramelised onions and 1 tbsp vinegar to the pot and stir. Season very well with salt and pepper. Add a splash of water if needed, as the mujadara will thicken up slightly as it cools.

To serve, ladle the lentils into bowls, top with the remaining fried onions and a good drizzle of olive oil and vinegar. If you are brave enough to try it with raw onion (do it), quarter the remaining onion, peel some layers off and use the onion ‘petals’ to scoop up the lentils.

name: Vegan One-Pan Chorizo Gnocchi
description: This creamy and spicy gnocchi is a vegan pasta hit. It's giving all the chorizo vibes without the actual chorizo. And we're here for it.
instructions: Break your plant-based sausages up into small chunks and start to fry in a large pan. Add in the chilli powder and paprika, cook for a few minutes until you have a fragrant red oil.
Chop your peppers into cubes and add them to the pan, stirring them and allowing them to fry in the spicy paprika oil.
Once the plant bases sausages and peppers begin to cook, add your cherry tomatoes whole. Stir and continue to cook on a high heat. Slice your red chili and garlic and add them to the pan.
In a separate bowl, cover your gnocchi with boiling water and allow it to soak for 10 mins.

While the gnocchi is soaking, pour the red wine vinegar into the frying pan and stir it in with the plant-based cream cheese. You should now have a creamy sauce. Add a pinch of salt and pepper to taste. Roughly chop your basil and throw that in there too.
Drain your gnocchi and thoroughly mix it into your sauce. Serve up with a sprinkling of fresh basil. Get stuck in.

name: Vegan Raspberry Buttercream
description: Looking for plant-based buttercream to frost your cakes? Here’s how to make it.
instructions: Use an electric whisk to beat the icing sugar and vegan butter together in a mixing bowl until smooth.
