Stir through the raspberries gradually, adding a few at a time until you have a nice pink colour. Don’t add too many or the buttercream will split.
Keep chilled (it will melt at room temp).

name: Vegan Salted Caramel Sauce
description: Indulgent plant-based salted caramel made with just three ingredients: coconut milk, sugar and salt. Drizzle it over cakes or brownies, spoon some over ice cream or pour it over warm banana bread.
instructions: Set a heavy-bottomed saucepan over a medium high heat. Add the sugar and stir it around the pan for about a minute to heat through. Add the coconut milk and stir to combine.
Bring everything to a boil, then reduce it to a low-medium heat and let it simmer for about 15 mins, stirring occasionally, until the caramel has thickened and sticks to the back of the spatula.
Stir in ¾ of your salt. Don’t try and taste the caramel while it's hot – wait until it's cool.

Remove the pan from the heat and leave the caramel to cool slightly for around 10 mins before tasting and adding more salt if needed. Transfer the caramel to a sealed container and pop it in the fridge for at least two hours to thicken up.

name: Vegan Sausage Gochujang Rigatoni
description: We know you guys love our sausage gochujang rigatoni so we felt it was only right for us to make you a vegan version that packs all the flavour of the original.
instructions: Decase your sausages and fry them in a pan with some oil on a medium-high heat to brown them off. Deglaze with a splash of water when the bottom of the pan starts to caramelise. You want some caramelisation, though, as this will be crucial for the flavour of the dish.
Once the plant-based sausage crumbles are caramelised and golden, remove them from the pan and set them aside.
Mince your shallot and garlic.

Add your vegan butter to the pan then, once it starts to melt, add in your minced shallot and garlic. After that, you’re going to want to go in with the gochujang and vegan single cream. Zest the limes, saving it for later to garnish. Then add the juice from the limes to the pan along with your agave. Finally, add your caramelised plant-based sausage bits back to the pan. Give it a good mix, and leave it to simmer. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Get your pasta in salted boiling water. Once it’s al dente, drain the pasta and reserve the water. That pasta water is the key to bringing your sauce together.
Add a small ladle of starchy water to your pasta and keep mixing until it’s super glossy. If you feel that the pasta needs a bit more water, add another small ladleful.
Add most (but not all) of your chopped coriander to the pasta and give it another mix.
Heat a tablespoon of olive oil in a separate pan before tossing your breadcrumbs in. Take it off the heat and mix with a scattering of your leftover coriander.
Finish the pasta with your coriander breadcrumbs and grate over some lime zest. Tuck in.

name: Vegan Spanakopita
description: This is my recipe for the perfect spanakopita, a spinach and tofu 'feta' pie. As close to the ones we eat at home in Cyprus as possible, it's a real treat.
instructions: To marinate the tofu, pat it dry and crumble it into a bowl, making sure that the pieces are not too small as they will break up further later on. Mix through the garlic powder, nutritional yeast, juice of a lemon and salt.

Preheat your oven at 180C. Then dice the onion and finely slice the leek. Grate or mince the garlic. Crush the fresh herbs (parsley, dill, mint) by rolling them in your hands to release their flavour, then finely chop them. Set aside.
Fry the leek, onion, and garlic with a good drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper until translucent but not brown, for about 10 mins

Meanwhile add the fresh or frozen spinach to another saucepan on medium heat, and cook until it’s cooked down and all the water has evaporated. If using fresh spinach, you may need to add it to the pan bit by bit. This will take about 10 -15 mins to totally dry. Add the cooked leek and onion and a drizzle of olive oil and cook for a few more mins. It’s important that the mix is as dry as possible to avoid a soggy filo.
Turn off the heat and add in the fresh herbs and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Stir the tofu into the spinach mix carefully. Add a splash of apple cider vinegar and plenty of salt and pepper and stir well. Season more than you usually would as both the spinach and tofu need it.

Lay the pastry out with a damp tea towel on top to prevent it drying out. Peel one sheet onto a large piece of baking paper and brunch generously with olive oil, getting onto each edge and corner. Take another sheet and lay it diagonally onto the last one and brush again with oil. Continue laying down 5 sheets in total (you may have one left to patch up any broken bits at the end). Each sheet should be laid down at a different angle so that they make a circle or star shape.

When you have finished layering the sheets, spoon the spinach mix into the centre of them and shape it into a circle with your hands.Lift up the sides of the pastry to cover the top, scrunching the top to create ridges and edges. Brush with more olive oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds or onion seeds if using.

Bake on the lower shelf for 20-30 mins, or until golden brown all over. Leave it to set for 10 mins before serving. Keep it in the fridge for up to 3 days. Delicious served cold or warmed up in the oven.

name: Vegan Sticky Toffee Puddings
description: This gooey dessert is a British classic for a reason. Here it gets a plant-based makeover.
instructions: Start by making the salted caramel sauce (or skip this step if using store-bought). Set a heavy-bottomed saucepan over a medium high heat. Add the sugar and stir it around the pan for about a minute to heat through. Add the coconut milk and stir to combine.

Bring everything to a boil, then reduce it to a low-medium heat and let it simmer for about 15 mins, stirring occasionally, until the caramel has thickened and sticks to the back of the spatula. Stir in ¾ of your salt. Don’t try and taste the caramel while it's hot – wait until it's cool.

Remove the pan from the heat and leave the caramel to cool slightly for around 10 mins before tasting and adding more salt if needed. Transfer the caramel to a sealed container and pop it in the fridge for at least two hours to thicken up.
For the sponges, soak the dates in the boiling water, with the spices. Leave to steep overnight or as long as possible (even an hour is great).
Heat the oven to 180˚C. Grease a cupcake or individual cake tin. (I use a mini bundt pan, well sprayed, but you can use any cupcake-sized baking tin you like.)

Use an electric whisk to beat the olive oil and sugar together until light and fluffy. Mash the ripe banana then add to the mix and beat to combine. In a separate bowl, whisk the flour and bicarb together then add to the mix and beat to combine.
Make sure the dates are cool then blitz them in a blender and add to the mix. Slowly whisk in the plant-based milk; the mix will split but don't worry.
Spoon the mixture into the prepared cupcake moulds, not quite filling them to the top. Bake for 20 mins until set.
To serve, drizzle over the salted caramel sauce.

name: Vegan Yoghurt Dip With A Pesto Swirl
description: Yoghurt spiked with zingy lemon juice and swirled with Sacla' Vegan Pesto might just be the perfect dip.
keywords: Vegan Yoghurt Dip With Pesto Swirl
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Scatter the pine nuts on a tray and roast for 10 mins, until turning brown, then set aside.

Tip the yoghurt into a large bowl, add the juice of the lemon and season well with salt and pepper. Spread the mixture over the base of a large plate. Spoon the Sacla' Vegan Pesto onto the plate and use your spoon to swirl it through the yoghurt. Drizzle with olive oil. Scatter with the toasted pine nuts and herb leaves. Finish with a crack of black pepper and sumac, if using.
Toast the flatbread and scoop through the dip.

name: Veggie Chilli Burrito Bowl
description: The easiest burrito bowl you'll ever make. Using our Veggie Chili Sin Carne leftovers served over rice, topped with cheddar cheese, salsa, and crunchy lettuce. Huge flavors, minimal effort.
instructions: Make the Veggie Chili Sin Carne.

Warm the leftover Veggie Chili Sin Carne in a saucepan set over a low heat, stirring occasionally until piping hot. If it’s thickened in the fridge, add a splash of water to loosen it. Meanwhile, reheat the rice following pack instructions.
Meanwhile, grate the cheddar and thinly slice the lettuce.
Divide the rice between bowls. Top with the veggie chilli, grated cheddar, tomato salsa, soured cream and shredded lettuce. Serve with a wedge of lime.

name: Veggie Chilli Sin Carne
description: This is the ultimate veggie chilli packed full of beans and spices. Make it once and you'll be able to cook more quick and easy meals throughout the week!
instructions: Heat the grill to medium-high. Peel and chop the onion into wedges, then peel the garlic. Chop the tomatoes into wedges and remove the stalks from the jalapeños. Put everything onto a baking tray and slide under the grill for 10 mins, then turn and grill for another 5 mins until charred.
Put your porcini mushrooms into a bowl, then cover with boiling water and leave to stand for 20 mins until the mushrooms are fully hydrated.
Put the onion, garlic, tomato and jalapeños into a blender along with the mushrooms and their soaking water. Blitz until smooth and set aside.

Dice the pepper. Heat a shot of oil in a large lidded pan or casserole dish over a medium heat and fry the pepper for 5 mins, then remove from the pan. Heat a shot more oil over a low-medium heat and add the smoked paprika, cumin, cinnamon and oregano. Cook for 1 min before adding the blitzed mushroom paste and the chipotle paste.

Tip in the coffee and Marmite, then add the tinned chopped tomatoes and drained and rinsed beans. Add the red pepper back in, then cover and simmer on low for 30 mins. If you want the chilli a bit thinner, loosen with water. Finally, melt in the dark chocolate. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

name: Veggie Dumpling Soup
description: Rich mushroom broth with soft veg and pillowy porcini and dill dumplings. Think of matzo ball soup, but veggie.
instructions: Pour in ⅗ of the water over the porcini mushrooms and soak for 30 mins. Once soft, remove the mushrooms from the liquid and squeeze out as much moisture as possible before roughly chopping. Reserve the soaking liquid to use later.

Combine the flour, table salt, mustard powder, porcini mushrooms, most of the dill, suet and a pinch of pepper in a large bowl, then gradually add the rest of the water, mixing with your hands to combine. You are looking for a very soft dough that isn't sticky. If it’s tacky, add a little more flour. Stop mixing once you’ve achieved the perfect texture, otherwise your dumplings will be chewy. Roll into 16 small balls and pop onto a baking tray, then cover with cling film and set aside in the fridge.

Peel and cut the carrots on the bias into 2cm pieces, then cut the celery in the same way. Finely slice the onion and garlic. Melt the butter and a splash of oil in a medium sized pot set over a low-medium heat and fry the onion, garlic, carrot and celery for 10-15 mins. Add the mushroom stock, porcini soaking liquid and bay leaf, then bring to a simmer and cook for 15 mins.

Pick the parsley leaves. Get the dumplings out of the fridge and carefully drop them into the soup so they are just balancing on top of the vegetables, ¼ submerged in the stock - if they sink down too much they will disintegrate. At this point, if you feel like the dumplings will sink, transfer everything to a smaller pot so they can balance nicely. Cover with a lid and cook for a further 10-15 mins – the vegetables will be very soft. Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the parsley and remaining dill.

name: Veggie Egg Fried Rice
description: A belter of a dish. Charred veggies and eggy rice, topped with the crispiest shallots in the land. So easy. So cheap. So delicious.
instructions: Get your rice on (see pack instructions).

Start by dicing all of your vegetables. Heat a frying pan with a glug of vegetable oil and add your chopped carrots, peppers and courgettes and stir. As they begin to cook, add your spring onions, chilli, garlic and ginger.
Once your rice is cooked, add this in and mix. Fry in the pan for a couple of minutes until it starts catching, and then add your soy sauce and vinegar. Fold everything together.

Time to get on with those shallots. Pour around 200ml of vegetable oil into a small frying pan (so that it fills the pan). Slice up your shallots and add to the pan when the vegetable oil is nice and hot. Once the shallots are nice and crispy, set aside.

Egg Time. Crack your eggs into a bowl along with a pinch of salt and whisk. Next, make a well in your frying pan and pour the whisked egg into the middle. Start mixing the egg with your spoon. As it cooks, fold it into the rice. And that’s it! Serve it up with a sprinkling of those crispy shallots and tuck into this bad boy.

name: Veggie Meatball Kebabs With Fennel & Pumpkin Seed Slaw
description: Herby courgette and veggie meatball kebabs on a bed of mustardy and tangy crème fraîche served with fresh and zingy fennel slaw. Delicious.
instructions: If using skewers, soak them in water while you prep everything else.
Chop the courgette into 2cm discs and add into a bowl. Trim, peel, and grate the garlic onto the courgettes. Stir through the oregano, 2 tbsp olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Toss well.

Now, it’s time to make the slaw: shave the fennel as finely as you can into a bowl. Add the lemon zest and juice along with 1 tbsp of olive oil, toss and use your hands to massage the lemon juice into the fennel. Roughly chop the parsley and toss into the slaw. Finally, add the toasted pumpkin seeds along with a big pinch of salt and pepper, set aside.

Heat the oven grill to its highest setting. Take each skewer and thread on the meatballs and courgettes, alternating between the two until you have three meatballs and three pieces of courgette on each skewer. Place them onto an oiled baking tray, slide under the grill for 10 mins, turning halfway, until the meatballs are cooked through and the courgettes are charred.
Whisk the mustard into the crème fraîche, season with salt and pepper and spread over plates or a platter. Top with the kebabs, serve the fennel slaw and flatbreads alongside.

name: Veggie Samosas
description: Mob, it's time to ditch the takeaway. Instead, feast your eyes on these ridiculously delicious and ridiculously easy vegetarian samosas, courtesy of Romy Gill.
instructions: To make the pastry, sift the flour into a large bowl, and then add salt, 3 tsp ghee and ajwain seeds. Rub the oil into the flour with your hands so it’s well combined with the flour and there are no lumps. Gently add water to bring the flour to a dough consistency. Bring the dough together and knead until it forms into a bowl – it should be smooth now. Cover the bowl with a cloth and leave to rest at room temperature for at least an hour.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Next, in a small bowl add all the spices and salt and mix together. Peel and dice the potatoes and sweet potatoes. Then add them to baking tray. Sprinkle the mixed spices, chopped chillies, dried pomegranate seeds and salt over the potatoes and sweet potatoes. Pour over the ghee or oil and mix everything. Place the tray in the oven and cook for 12 mins.
Add the frozen peas to a bowl with hot water. After 5 mins drain the water, and set aside.
Once the potatoes are soft, remove them from the oven and add them to the bowl with the peas. Stir until all of them are well coated.

When you’re ready to start making the samosas, heat a frying pan on a low heat. While the pan is heating, divide the dough into 10 equal-sized balls. Roll each into a circle on a lightly floured work surface to approximately 15cm diameter. Place the dough discs into the frying pan and warm both sides (don't cook them completely). Remove immediately from the pan, and cut them in half to create semi circles.

Brush the edges with water using your fingers, and then fold the semi-circle in half, bringing the straight edges together to make into a cone shape. Fill the cone with the filling. Apply water again to the inside of the cone, pinch and seal the open edge and then push with a fork. Repeat until all the remaining dough balls are made into samosas.

Once all the samosas are made, heat a heavy-based pan, half filled with ghee or vegetable oil. Heat the oil to 180°C. Deep fry in batches for 3-4 mins, until light brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Put them on the plate lined with kitchen paper to drain excess oil. Serve hot with tomato ketchup or Pudina (mint) chutney.

name: Veggie Satay Noodles
description: Charred veggies are key here. Key key key. Paired with the soft noodles and a creamy peanutty sauce its a very special dish.
instructions: Start by slicing all of your veg into strips & finely chop your garlic and ginger.

Drizzle some olive oil into a wok and add all the veggies (not garlic and ginger). Cook on a medium heat and stir. As the vegetables begin to char, add your garlic and ginger and mix well. Set your veggies aside.
Get your noodles on - check pack instructions.
Add your coconut milk to a pan. Next, add the soy sauce and peanut butter. Cook and stir on a medium heat and bring it to a boil. Add the juice of the lime and stir. Allow it to bubble.
Once the sauce is thick enough, add your noodles and mix together. Add your veggies back into the pan and stir everything together and that’s it! Tuck into this tasty and simple dish.

name: Veggie Sausage Traybake with Broccoli Salsa
description: A quick and easy vegetarian-friendly traybake. This one is a Mediterranean-inspired delight.
keywords: Veggie Sausage Traybake with Broccoli Salsa
instructions: Preheat the oven to fan 190°C.

Trim and chop the aubergines and tomatoes into 2cm chunks (leave any small tomatoes whole). Trim the broccoli and chop the stem into 1cm chunks. Discard the tough oregano stems, and thinly slice the garlic.

Add the chopped veg, broccoli stalks, oregano and garlic into an oven-proof dish with 2 tbsp of balsamic vinegar, 5 tbsp of olive oil, salt and pepper. Toss it all together. Place the veggie sausages on top. Roast for 35-40 mins, until the sausages are cooked and the veggies have softened.

Meanwhile, roughly chop the broccoli florets. Add the olives and parsley into a food processor and blitz until finely minced. Transfer into a bowl. Add the broccoli into the processor and blitz until its finely minced. Add your minced broccoli to the minced olives along with 70ml of olive oil and the remaining balsamic vinegar. Season with salt and pepper and mix. Set aside.
Drain the peppers and chop them into 2cm chunks.

Add the couscous into a heatproof bowl with 245ml of boiling water, and season with plenty of freshly cracked black pepper. Cover tightly and set aside to rehydrate for 10-15 mins. Once ready, grate in the Parm, mix, taste and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
Stir the roasted peppers into the veg. Share the couscous between your plates, and top with the sausage traybake and the broccoli green olive salsa.

name: Veggie Sheet-Pan Breakfast Burritos
description: The perfect meal-prep savoury breakfast. Make a big batch on a Sunday and keep them in the freezer until you’re ready for a satisfying high-protein brekkie.
keywords: Veggie Sheet Pan Breakfast Burritos recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Drain and rinse the kidney beans and finely dice the pepper and onion. Transfer to a baking tray and toss with olive oil, cumin, salt and pepper. Thinly slice the mushrooms then add to a separate baking tray and toss with olive oil, salt and pepper.

Slide the kidney bean mix into the middle shelf of the oven, and the mushrooms into the lower shelf of the oven. Leave to roast for 20 mins then swap the trays and roast for another 15 mins. Once cooked, transfer both to a mixing bowl. Finely chop the fresh coriander then add to the bean and veggie mix, seasoning with salt and pepper. Reduce the oven to 160°C.

Fill a bowl with boiling water then add the spinach and leave for 30 seconds to a minute, stirring occasionally, until wilted. Drain the water, squeeze out all of the liquid from the spinach and roughly chop.
Meanwhile, add the cottage cheese to a blender and blitz smooth. Whisk the eggs into a mixing bowl then fold in the smooth cottage cheese. Season well with salt and pepper.

Line a baking tray with parchment paper, then pour in the egg mixture and dot with the wilted spinach. Slide into the oven to bake for 15 mins until golden and puffy, then flip the tray around and cook for another 5 mins. Remove from the oven and leave to cool until easy to handle if serving immediately, or until cooled completely if making in advance.
Grate the Cheddar cheese. Cut the egg into 9 rectangles. Warm the tortillas in a pan.

To assemble, start by placing the egg in the middle of the tortilla, then top with some grated cheese, a big spoonful of beans and a handful of mushrooms. Fold in the edges of the wrap to cover the filling, then roll the longest side up until sealed. Repeat until all the ingredients are used up.
Heat a frying pan over medium heat and add the wraps, seal side down – this will make sure they don’t open up. Repeat until all the burritos are sealed.

Serve immediately. Or, if making in advance, wrap each burrito in tin foil and store in the freezer. To reheat, remove the foil then dampen a piece of kitchen paper and wrap it around the burrito. Pop it in the microwave for 10-15 mins then transfer to the air fryer and cook for 10-15 mins on 180°C until piping hot throughout. These will keep for up to 3 months in the freezer and 3 days in the fridge.

name: Very Boozy Sherry Trifle
description: Layers of booze-soaked sponge, creamy custard and tart mixed berries. An absolute belter of a dessert. It works best with slightly stale sponge cake so bake or buy yours a couple of days in advance.
instructions: In a bowl, stir together the sherry and coulis.

Place ½ of the cake in the bottom of your glass bowl. Ladle a layer of custard on top, sprinkle with fresh berries and drizzle with some of the coulis mix. Repeat to the top, finishing with a layer of fruit.
In a separate mixing bowl, use an electric whisk to whisk the double cream and icing sugar together until thick and soft with stiff peaks forming.
Spoon (or use a piping bag to pipe) the whipped cream in a thick layer on top of the trifle. Top with the toasted flaked almonds.

name: Vibrant Lemon & Cod Rice Soup
description: Vibrant and zingy, this brothy fish soup comes together super quickly. Perfect for a weeknight meal.
instructions: Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites from the greens. Poke a few holes in one of the chillies, then slice the rest. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems.

Place a saucepan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the spring onion whites, coriander stems and the whole chilli. Cook, stirring until fragrant and softened, for 2-3 mins. Quickly add the baharat (Lebanese 7-spice) and turmeric before pouring in the stock. Let it come to the boil, then reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.

Add the cherry tomatoes and fish. Poach for 4-10 mins until fully cooked and opaque throughout (depending on the thickness of the fillet, it may take less or more time). Taste and season the broth with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Before serving, stir the spring onion greens through. Share the rice between bowls, ladle over the broth and top with the tomatoes and fish. Garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Victoria Sponge
description: A classic Victoria sponge recipe with vanilla cream and raspberry jam. Grab your pals and put the kettle on; you just can’t beat a Vicky sponge.
instructions: Heat your oven to 160°C fan. Lightly grease two 20°Cm springform cake tins and line the base with baking paper. Make sure the butter is at room temperature.

Measure your butter into a mixing bowl or stand mixer. Using electric beaters, whisk for a minute or so on its own to make sure it is super soft. Add the caster sugar and continue to whisk for 3-5 mins until super aerated, light and fluffy.
Measure your flour into a small bowl. One at a time, crack an egg into the butter and sugar mixture and add a spoonful of your measured flour at the same time — this stops the batter from splitting.
Whisk together, scrape down the sides of the bowl then repeat until all the eggs are incorporated. Sieve in the remaining flour, add a pinch of salt, the milk and fold together with a spatula.

Divide the batter evenly between the two tins. Smooth the top then bake in the centre of the oven for 20 mins until well risen, the top is golden and the cake has just come away from the sides. If you insert a skewer into the centre it should come out with only a few crumbs attached.
Leave to cool for 5 mins then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

Assembly time. Whisk the double cream with the icing sugar and vanilla extract until it just holds its shape then put one of the sponges top down onto a serving plate and spread raspberry jam all over it. Top with the whipped cream then sandwich together with the remaining sponge and dust with icing sugar to finish. Heavenly.

name: Victoria Sponge Traybake Cake
description: What do you get when a traybake meets a Victoria Sponge? This beautiful Victoria Sponge Traybake Cake. Game, set, and match.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Line a 20cm x 30cm rectangle baking tin or roasting tray. Add the butter and sugar to a large mixing bowl and use an electric whisk to whip until very light and creamy. You can do this manually, but make sure you whisk until it’s super light!
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating with the whisk after each addition until fully combined. If it looks like it’s splitting at all, add a tbsp of the flour. Add the vanilla extract.

Mix the flour and baking powder together with a pinch of salt, then tip into the egg mixture and use a spatula to combine, you want to make sure it’s all combined but try not to beat out too much air. Add the zest of the lemon, then tip into the baking tin. Bake for 20-25 mins, until risen. To check if it's done, try poking it with a skewer – if it comes out clean, the cake is done. Otherwise, very lightly press the top with your finger, it should spring back to shape when you remove it. Set aside to cool for 5 mins, then flip out onto a drying rack, remove the baking paper and allow to cool. It’s best to ice the underside of the cake as it’ll be flat!
While the cake cools, remove the tops from the strawberries and cut into quarters. Add to a bowl with the raspberries. Dust the icing sugar over the top, stir and set aside.
Once the cake is cool, whip the double cream until thick and creamy. If you lift the whisk up, it should leave a little peak but not too firmly, you want it to be lightly whipped.
Stir the raspberry jam into the strawberry and raspberry mixture, they should have a glossy sauce.
Spoon the cream over the cake, using the back of a spoon to swoosh it over. Top with the strawberries and raspberries. Finish with a dusting of icing and then slice into squares to serve.

name: Vietnamese Beef Jerky & Papaya Salad
description: In Vietnam they LOVE beef jerky - and the meaty chew works so well with this crunchy, zingy salad. It's a great summer dinner.
keywords: Vietnamese Beef Jerky & Papaya Salad recipe
Vietnamese Beef Jerky & Papaya Salad beef jerky papaya salad
instructions: Peel the garlic clove and add to a pestle and mortar with however the chilli and gently bash together to break up, but not into a puree. Splash in the fish sauce, spoon in the sugar and squeeze in the lime juice to taste. Mix and taste, adjusting the levels of fish sauce, sugar and lime juice until its to your liking.

Very thinly slice the papaya. You can use a strip peeler, a mandolin with teeth or just thinly slice with a sharp knife then cut into matchsticks. Tip into a bowl. Trim the green beans (keep them raw for that nice crunch) and cut into inch long pieces. Half the cherry tomatoes. Pull, shred or chop the beef jerky or biltong into long pieces.

Pour the marinade over the shredded veg and beef jerky and mix well. Pick in the Thai basil leaves and fold some in too. Divide between two bowls and top with remaining Thai basil and some chopped salted peanuts. Get stuck in!

name: Vietnamese Chicken Rice
description: Golden chicken, turmeric rice and punchy garlic-spring onion oil for grown ups. This weeknight dinner is super easy to make and great for the whole family.
instructions:
1 Adult = 2 Kids Servings
Season the chicken thighs well with salt and pepper. 
Heat a generous drizzle of oil in a large lidded frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry for 3-4 mins on each side until golden. Transfer to a plate.
While the chicken is browning, peel and thinly slice the ginger. Trim the spring onions, cut half into 2cm pieces, and finely chop the rest. Peel and finely chop the garlic.

Turn the heat to medium, then add the jasmine rice, turmeric, chopped spring onion pieces, ginger slices and star anise to the pan. Stir for 2-3 mins until the rice is coated in the oil and starting to toast.

Pour in the chicken stock and bring to the boil. Nestle the browned chicken thighs into the rice, cover with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 12-15 mins until the rice is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed.

Meanwhile make the garlic spring onion oil. Tip half the chopped spring onions into a heatproof bowl with the garlic. Heat the vegetable oil in a small saucepan until hot, then pour it over the garlic and spring onions. Stir and season with salt. Set aside to mellow the flavours.
Once the rice is cooked, remove the chicken thighs. For the kids, shred the chicken keep their portion plain. For the adults, cut the thighs into larger pieces.

Serve up! 
Kids Plate: Dish up the chicken rice as is. 
Parents Plates: Add the larger pieces of chicken over the turmeric rice with spoonfuls of the garlic-spring onion oil and a squeeze of lime. Finish with coriander.

name: Vietnamese Lemongrass Chicken Noodle Salad
description: If you want to feel like you're in Vietnam without having to splurge on a plane ticket, this does the job.
instructions: Remove the lemongrass husk and peel the ginger and garlic, then put all the marinade ingredients into a blender or pestle and mortar and blitz or grind until smooth – it will be quite loose. Pour everything into a large bowl, add the chicken and marinate for at least 20 mins (or up to two days) in the fridge.

Heat the oven to 180°C. Slice the white onion and put into the bottom of a dutch oven or casserole dish. Add the chicken (skin-side up) and marinade on top of the onions, add a lid and cook in the oven for 25 mins.

After 25 mins, remove the lid and turn the heat up to 220°C. Put the dish on the top shelf of the oven and cook for 10-15 mins, to sear the chicken skin. Remove from the oven and set aside to rest for at least 10 mins.
Meanwhile, make the nước chấm dressing. Mince the garlic and ginger, finely chop the chilli, then combine all the ingredients in a small bowl. Mix well to dissolve the sugar and set aside.

For the noodle salad, place the vermicelli noodles into a medium-sized bowl and cover with boiling water. Leave for 4-5 mins. The noodles should be cooked through but still hold their shape, so taste at 4 mins in. Strain as soon as there is no more raw bite and set aside in the same bowl.

Meanwhile, slice the carrot and cucumber into thin matchsticks, or use a peeler to make ribbons, then set aside on a large plate. Finely slice the lettuce, mint and coriander, then set aside on the same plate.
When the chicken has slightly cooled, remove the bones and cut into slices.

Divide the noodles between four serving bowls, then top with the vegetables, herbs and sliced chicken pieces. Drizzle all over with a few tbsp dressing and some spoons of the chicken gravy. Garnish with peanuts, crispy shallots and a lime wedge.

name: Vietnamese-Inspired Poached Chicken Salad
description: A fresh and healthy Vietnamese-inspired salad with tender poached chicken. This is a perfect spring or summer dinner.
instructions: For the poached chicken, start by slicing the ginger in half. Put the chicken breasts into a large pot and cover with cold tap water, so it’s just covering the meat. Add a good pinch of salt, as you would with pasta water, and add the ginger slices. Add a lid and bring to a simmer, then immediately reduce the heat to the lowest fire for just 6 mins. Immediately turn the heat off and leave the chicken for 8 mins. Remove and use a knife to check the centre is not pink, then set aside in a small bowl to cool.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Combine the fish sauce, syrup, vinegar and lime juice in a small bowl. Use a cheese grater or Microplane to grate or mince the garlic and ginger into the dressing. Finely slice the chillies and add to the dressing.

For the salad, ribbon the carrot with a vegetable peeler, then toss into a large bowl. Cut the cabbage into quarters and use a peeler to shred the cabbage, peeling it away from the stem for easy shredding. Transfer to the carrot bowl. Finely slice the onion, mint leaves, coriander with all the stems and chilli, then add to the same bowl. Leave a few leaves behind for garnish.
If you like, bash the roasted nuts in a mortar and pestle, or crush in a bag using a rolling pin. Add half of the nuts to the salad bowl.
When the chicken is cool enough, shred it using your hands, pulling the large pieces of breast into thin shreds. Add one-quarter of the dressing to the shredded chicken and mix well.
Add the remaining dressing to the salad bowl and toss very well, ensuring to coat every bit of veg. Add two-thirds of the chicken to the salad and mix well again.

Divide the salad between serving plates with the remaining chicken on top. Garnish with the remaining nuts, crispy shallots, lime wedges and a few mint and coriander leaves. Make sure you drizzle over all the dressing ingredients that may be left in the mixing bowl.

name: Vignarole Orzo
description: This simple orzo recipe is inspired by vignarole – a spring-summer Roman classic which is like a bright green summer vegetable stew. The artichokes are the key ingredient here.
instructions: Dice the onions and courgettes. Thinly slice the spring onions and roughly chop the lettuce.

Preheat a large frying or sauté pan over a medium heat. Add a good glug of oil and tip in the onions and spring onions with a hefty pinch of salt. Cook for 4-5 mins, until just translucent, before adding the courgettes and half of the peas.

Cook for another 4-5 mins before adding the orzo. Start feeding the stock into the pan, a ladle at a time, stirring constantly, as if making a risotto. Once the pan has dried out, add a ladle more stock and continue like this until the orzo is fully cooked. This should take between 9-10 mins.

Make sure the mixture has a loose texture (add a bit more stock if it tightens up!) before tipping in the lettuce, broad beans, and artichokes. Toss through the orzo. Coarsely blitz the remaining peas in a nutribullet or with a hand blender. Tip into the pan and stir through the pasta.
Finish with the herbs and a good grating of Parm. Add a grating of lemon zest, plus a squeeze of juice right before serving.

name: Vodka Clementine Bitters
description: If you're looking for a quick, refreshing and simple drink look no further. The flaming orange gives the drink an incredible bouquet.
instructions: Using a peeler, peel the orange into a long rind for garnish. Use a knife to then cut a thick slice of the rind off.
Add ice to a balloon gin glass.
Pour in your vodka before adding in two dashes of Angostura bitters and your Fever-Tree Spanish Clementine Tonic Water. Add the orange peel and stir.
Squeeze the rind over the glass and ignite using a lighter to create a wonderful bouquet of aroma.

name: Vodka Gnocchi Bake
description: Flohio joined us to make warming, comforting vodka gnocchi bake, and we are obsessed. A supremely speedy and feel-good dinner.
instructions: Finely chop your onion and garlic. Grate your parmesan.
Heat a sauté pan over a medium heat with a glug of olive oil. Tip in your onion and fry for 15 mins until totally soft.

Add your garlic and chilli flakes, then cook out for a minute. Add all your tomato purée and cook for about 5 mins. It should get nice and dark, and begin sticking to the bottom of your pan. Stir the spice mix until fragrant.
Pour in the vodka and scrape the base of the pan to deglaze it, then add your cream.
Heat your grill to high.
Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil, then tip in your gnocchi. Cook until it rises to the surface, this should take about 2 mins.
Lift your gnocchi into the saucepan with a slotted spoon, then add in 3/4 of your cheese and a splash of gnocchi cooking water to loosen. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.

Tip your mixture into a baking dish, then add your basil and tear over your mozzarella. Sprinkle over your remaining parmesan, then pop your dish under the grill. Grill for about 5 mins until bubbly and golden.
Grind your black pepper over the top. Serve and enjoy.

name: Vodka Rigatoni
description: The perfect vodka pasta recipe doesn't ex... Here's our take on the classic vodka pasta using the ultimate combination of ingredients.
instructions: Finely slice your onion and red chillies. Grate your garlic. Chop off the rind from your block of Parmesan.

Add a splash of olive oil to a pan and add your onions. Cook until translucent, and then add your garlic and chilli. Fry for a minute, and then add your purée. Mix it in, and then cook for 4 mins on a medium heat, allowing the tomato mix to catch on the pan.

At this point, add your vodka, deglazing the sticky bits off the bottom of the pan with your wooden spoon. Once the alcohol has burned off (20 secs) add your cream. Add the rind of your Parmesan. Mix it in and turn down the heat.
Get your pasta on, salting the pasta water generously. After 2 mins, reserve a big mug of pasta water from the pan.
Add a good splash of your pasta water to your vodka sauce. Stir it in. Then add grated Parmesan, salt and pepper. Mix it together and bubble on a low-medium heat until the cheese has melted.
When the pasta is al-dente, remove from the heat and drain. Add the pasta to the vodka sauce. Start tossing it through, add splashes of pasta water to keep the sauce loose.
Serve the pasta into bowls. Top with torn basil and some more Parmesan. Enjoy.

name: Wagamama's Yaki Soba
description: Steve Mangleshot from Wagamama shows us how to make a simple vegan yaki soba that any one you're cooking for is bound to go mad for.
instructions: Chop your vegetables. Slice your pepper, mushrooms, spring onions and red onion, halve your tenderstem broccoli lengthways and finely chop your ginger and garlic. Roughly tear up your kale.
Cook your broccoli for 2 mins in boiling water to part cook, then set aside.
Cook your noodles in boiling water according to packet instructions, then drain and pop to one side.
Time to make your sauce. In a bowl, combine your sugar, soy sauce and sriracha.

Heat a wok over a high heat until it's nice and hot. Add your pepper, mushrooms, red onion, broccoli, kale, garlic and ginger to the wok and stir fry for a few minutes until tender and starting to get beautifully charred. Add your beansprouts and cooked noodles, then stir to combine before adding your sauce. Stir fry for another minute until all your ingredients are combined and it's smelling banging.
Time to plate it up. Top with your spring onion, sesame seeds and coriander, then serve. Enjoy!

name: Walnut & Beetroot Brownies Recipe
description: Welcome to our delicious beetroot brownies recipe, where indulgence meets nutrition! These beetroot brownies are a delightful twist on classic chocolate brownies, incorporating the earthy sweetness of beetroot and the crunchy texture of walnuts. The addition of cacao powder provides a rich chocolate flavour, while the beetroot not only enhances the natural sweetness but also adds a vibrant colour and extra moisture to the brownies. Perfect for those who love a bit of experimentation in their baking, these brownies are a great way to sneak in some vegetables without sacrificing taste. Whether you’re looking for a healthier dessert option or simply want to try a new traybake recipe, these beetroot brownies offer a satisfying treat with a unique twist. Dive into this recipe for a delicious, plant-based dessert that’s as nutritious as it is scrumptious!
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Grease a 20cm brownie tin with a little butter and line the base with baking parchment.
Tip the walnuts onto a roasting tray, then toast in the oven for 6-8 mins until nicely golden and smelling amazing. Set aside to cool. Once cool, roughly chop.
Drain the beetroot, roughly chop then blitz to a thick purée in a blender or food processor. Roughly chop the dark chocolate, then weigh 100g into a small bowl and set aside.

Put the remaining 200g dark chocolate into a heatproof bowl with the butter. Melt together over a pan of barely simmering water or in a microwave, zapping on high in 30 second intervals then stirring until melted.

Measure the sugar into a large bowl. Crack in the eggs then use an electric whisk to beat until the mixture is light and aerated – it should double in size. Add the beetroot purée, melted butter and dark chocolate, flour and cocoa powder along with a big pinch of sea salt. Whisk together until you have a smooth, rich brownie batter.

Scrape half the batter into your lined tin. Scatter over half the chopped dark chocolate and chopped walnuts. Top with the remaining brownie batter, smoothing into all the corners, then poke in the remaining chocolate and walnuts.
Bake in the centre of the oven for 25-30 mins until the edges are set and the centre still has a nice wobble. Once out of the oven, sprinkle with a little extra sea salt if you like.
Leave to cool then cut into 16 squares, to serve.

name: Walnut & Pomegranate Chicken
description: Inspired by Persian khoresh fesenjan, this walnut and pomegranate chicken is creamy, comforting, and the greatest meal you could possibly have any day of the week.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Season the chicken thighs with salt and heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Put the chicken thighs into the pan, skin-side down, and cook for 8-10 mins until the skin is deep golden brown. Transfer to a baking tray.
Peel and thinly slice the onions, then tip them into the empty chicken pan with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 7-10 mins until starting to brown.

Meanwhile, put the walnuts, turmeric, 7-spice, stock and pomegranate molasses into a blender and blitz until smooth. Add this mixture to the onions, bring to the boil, then pour everything over the chicken. Cook in the oven for 20-25 mins.
Meanwhile, finely mince the dill and heat the rice following pack instructions. Toss the two together. Pick the mint leaves.
Serve the chicken with the dill-y rice and a scattering of pomegranate seeds, mint leaves and some extra pomegranate molasses, if you like.

name: Warm Caprese Butter Bean Salad
description: Burst cherry tomatoes with loads of garlic and smooshed down till saucy mixed with butter beans and topped with torn mozzarella and fresh basil. This is our kind of salad.
keywords: Warm Caprese Butter Bean Salad recipe
instructions: Poke all of the cherry tomatoes with a knife and finely slice the garlic. Heat oil in a large pan over a medium heat.

Add garlic to the pan and cook for 2 mins, then add the cherry tomatoes. Simmer for 5 mins, gently squishing them down so they get a bit saucy. Once they’ve simmered, drain and rinse the beans and add them in. Season with salt and pepper then stir through the sherry vinegar.
Plate up and top with burrata, torn basil, and pesto.

name: Warm Chickpea, Feta & Roasted Pepper Salad
description: A warm and herby salad that's perfect for a dinner party side or veg-packed lunch. Heating up your chickpeas makes such a difference.
instructions: Empty the jar of chickpeas into a pan, water and all. Set over a medium heat and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 mins then turn off the heat and set aside.

Cut the tomatoes into even-sized chunks. Cut the peppers into strips and thinly slice the red onion and cucumber. Chuck the lot into a bowl, season generously with salt and pepper and squeeze over the juice of one lemon. Throw in a splash of the pepper liquid, and toss everything together.
Drain the warm chickpeas and add to the salad along with the feta and a dash of oil from the tin. Toss through the rocket and leaves from the basil.
Season, add 50ml of olive oil, and more lemon juice if needed. Divide between warm plates and serve.

name: Warm Greek Beans With Dill & Yoghurt
description: Warm, tomatoey beans topped with dill-infused yoghurt and feta. This is a super delicious and healthy dinner.
keywords: Warm Greek Beans With Dill & Yoghurt
Warm Greek Beans With Dill & Yoghurt recipe
instructions: Dice the onion and slice the garlic. Heat oil in a large pot and fry the onion with a pinch of salt for 4 mins, until slightly softened. Add the garlic and continue cooking for 5 mins. Drain and rinse the beans.

Add the cinnamon, oregano and mint, give it a stir and pour in the tinned tomatoes, capers, olives and beans. Bring to a simmer, and cook for 10 mins until reduced. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Mix the yoghurt with most of the dill, then season with salt and pepper.

Task off the heat and cool slightly – you don't want this to be piping hot. When it's at room temp, squeeze in the lemon juice and mix, then drizzle with the yoghurt dressing and crumble over the feta and the remaining dill.

name: Warming Chorizo & Kale Soup
description: Ana de Costa joins us in the studio to make a glorious caldo verde, a lovely Portuguese soup. Loaded up with tatties, kale and chorizo, this is banging.
instructions: Chop two thirds of your chorizo into cubes and thinly slice the remaining third. Roughly chop your onions and garlic.
Heat a glug of oil in a big pot. Add the cubed chorizo, onions and garlic. Keep stirring until the onions go translucent.
Peel your potatoes and chop them into 2cm cubes.
Add the potatoes and bay leaf to the pan. Stir occasionally so it doesn’t stick to the pot, and let it cook for a few mins.
Add the stock and let it simmer on low heat for 15 mins until the potatoes are fully cooked.
In the meantime, fry the slices of chorizo until they are crispy. Save them for garnish along with the chorizo oil.
Add a couple handfuls of the kale to the pot and blend everything together. If the soup is too thick for your liking, you can add a cup of water.
Add the rest of the kale, along with half of the sliced chorizos. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Serve in your favourite soup bowl and garnish with the crispy chorizo, drizzle of chorizo oil and extra virgin olive oil, alongside some toasted bread slices.

name: Warming Cinnamon & Pear Custard with Rice
description: Our twist on a rice pudding, with sushi rice, spiced pears and a creamy cinnamon custard. A luxurious autumnal dessert with no stodginess in sight.
keywords: Warming Cinnamon & Pear Custard with Rice Recipe
Warming Cinnamon & Pear Custard with Rice
instructions: Heat the oven to fan 200°C.
Peel and halve the pears, remove the cores, and place on a baking tray.

In a small bowl, mix together the honey, water, juice of the lemon, mixed spice and Amaretto liqueur (if using). Pour over the pears and use a spoon or your hands to make sure the pears are well coated.
Break up the butter into small pieces and scatter over the pears. Roast the pears in the oven for 25-30 mins until tender, basting halfway.

Meanwhile, start on the custard. Combine the milk, double cream, honey, vanilla and cinnamon stick in a medium saucepan. Set it over a medium heat and let it come to a gentle simmer then remove from the heat. Pop a lid on and leave for at least 10 mins to infuse the milk (the longer you let it sit, the more flavourful it will be).
When the milk has infused, discard the cinnamon stick. If the milk has cooled down, place it back over a medium-high heat until hot, just before it starts to simmer.

In a large bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, sugar, salt and cornflour until thickened and pale. Add a ladle of the hot milk and whisk until incorporated. Continue, one ladle at a time, until you’ve used ½ the milk.

Sieve the whisked egg mixture back into the saucepan with the remaining milk mixture. Set the pan over a medium heat and cook for 7-10 mins, whisking continuously, until thickened. It should coat the back of a spoon, but still be quite runny.
Reheat your rice and divide between bowls. Ladle over the custard and top with the pear halves. Drizzle over any of the roasting juices.

name: Warming Roast Turkey Bowl with Caesar Dressing
description: Crispy golden turkey, roasted roots, nutty grains & a punchy Caesar dressing – all the cosy flavours of a roast, packed into one epic bowl.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.
Dice the carrots, parsnips and potatoes into 2cm chunks. Strip the kale leaves from their stalks and tear into bite-sized pieces.
Tip the root veg and potatoes onto a baking tray. Season with salt and pepper, drizzle with olive oil and toss everything together. Roast in the oven for 20–25 mins until golden and tender.
Meanwhile, season the kale with a pinch of salt and massage until darkened and wilted. Set aside.
Tear or shred the roasted turkey into chunks

Tip the mayonnaise, anchovy fillets, garlic and juice of the lemon into a blender and blitz until smooth. Finely grate the Parmesan and stir it through the dressing. Taste and season with salt and plenty of black pepper.

Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the turkey and leave it to crisp up for 7–10 mins, turning halfway, until golden on both sides. Take it off the heat and stir the cranberry sauce through to glaze.
Microwave the pouch of rice and quinoa following pack instructions. Toss it through the wilted kale.
Mix the Caesar dressing through the quinoa and kale, then divide between bowls. Top with the crispy cranberry turkey, roasted veg and a scattering of pecans.

name: Warming Squash Soup with Sesame Cheese Cracker
description: In Partnership With Aldi. #ad A silky, spicy squash soup with a crispy, nutty cheddar cracker you smash at the table. Big heat, bold flavour, and a bit of drama too.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C.

Peel the squash and cut it into 3cm chunks. Peel the onion and cut into wedges. Peel the garlic cloves but keep them whole. Halve the chillies lengthways and remove the seeds if you prefer less heat. Trim the spring onions for roasting. Peel and thinly slice the ginger.

Add the squash, onion, garlic and chillies to a roasting tin. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss everything together. Roast for 25–30 mins, turning once, until golden and soft.
Add the sliced ginger and trimmed spring onions to the tin, toss again, and roast for another 10 mins.

Tip all the roasted veg into a large saucepan. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable stock. Stir in the ground turmeric and 1 Tbsp soy sauce. Bring to the boil and simmer gently for 10 mins. Taste and add more soy sauce, if needed.

While the soup simmers, make your sesame cheddar cracker. Grate the cheddar. Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add roughly 50g grated cheddar to the pan in a mound. Let it melt and bubble for 4–5 mins until starting to brown.Sprinkle over some sesame seeds and a pinch of chilli flakes. Keep cooking for another minute or so, until it darkens but doesn’t burn. Carefully lift the cheese from the pan using a spatula and transfer to a tray to crisp up. Repeat with the remaining cheese.
Use a stick blender to blitz the soup until smooth. If it’s too thick, loosen with a splash of hot water or extra stock. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Finely slice the spring onions for garnish. Ladle the soup into bowls, top with the sliced spring onions, and serve with a cheese cracker on top, smash it at the table.

name: Warming Sweet Potato & Chickpea Curry
description: A creamy, fragrant and gently spiced vegan curry that will become a staple in your weekly meal rotation.
instructions: Dice the onion and peel and mince the ginger and garlic. Wash and roughly chop the sweet potato into bite-sized chunks. Pick the coriander leaves, roughly chop them, discard the stems and set aside for garnish.

Heat a generous glug of oil in a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the onion, season with salt and fry until it begins to develop some colour. Add the ginger and garlic, then fry for 1 min. Stir in the spices, tossing frequently until they are toasted – take care not to burn them.
Add the sweet potato, drained chickpeas and chopped tomatoes. Stir until well combined, then bring the mixture to a simmer.
Meanwhile, blend the coconut milk and silken tofu in a blender until smooth.

Pour the coconut milk mixture into the pan, mix until fully combined, then bring it back to a simmer. Allow to simmer for about 15 mins, or until the sweet potatoes are fork-tender. Turn off the heat, then use a fork to smush about one-third of the chickpeas. Season generously to taste, stir in the lemon juice, and let the dish sit for 10 mins.
Top with the chopped coriander, then serve with rice and a dollop of vegan coconut yoghurt.

name: Warming Veg & Bean Soup
description: This is my take on a minestrone. It is THE perfect winter warmer. So hearty and delicious. Hope you love it, Ben x
instructions: Soak your porcini mushrooms in around 100ml boiling water or until they are just covered.
Prep time. Chop your onions, celery, courgette and carrots into chunks and finely chop your herbs and garlic. Zest and juice your lemon.

Add your onions and carrots into a pan to cook first with some olive oil. Once those have softened slightly, add your celery and your courgette. After a couple of mins also add your garlic, chopped rosemary, oregano and chilli flakes
While that is cooking, drain your porcini mushrooms making sure to reserve the water. Chop then add into the pan along with your lemon zest.
Add the reserved mushroom stock to the pan along with your veg bouillon then add in your cannellini beans and water straight from the tin.
Roughly chop your tomatoes and add them in. Give everything a good mix.
Once all your veg has softened, add the remaining boiling water to your pan and simmer for 10 minutes.

Chop your chard and basil and add to the pan after 5 minutes. Let it wilt then finally add in the juice of your lemon and a good grinding of black pepper. Season to taste and serve. I like to eat mine with some toasted crusty bread. Enjoy!

name: Warming White Bean Soup
description: Nothing warms your soul like a good soup. This vegan-friendly bean soup is packed full of protein and comes topped with the crispiest, crunchiest croutons.
instructions: Begin by finely chopping the onions and mincing the garlic.

Set a large pan over a medium heat with a big splash of olive oil. Sweat down the onions with no colour for 10 mins before adding the garlic and a pinch of chilli flakes and cooking for a further 5 mins. Season with salt and pepper.

Add a splash of white wine and let bubble away before draining the beans and adding them to the pan. Pour over the stock, bring to the boil, add a sprig of rosemary then reduce to a simmer and cook for about 20 mins.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Meanwhile, make the gremolata. Finely chop the parsley, discard any thick stalks, and add to a bowl.

Zest the lemon and mince the additional clove of garlic before adding to the bowl and mixing well. Season with salt and pepper. When the soup has cooked for 20 mins, blend with a stick blender until smooth then season with salt and pepper. Set to a low heat to keep warm.
Cut the bread into big croutons and add to a baking tray with a good splash of olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Toss in the oven for 10 mins to crisp up. Serve the soup in deep bowls with the croutons and gremolata on top.

name: Watermelon Rum Punch
description: Watermelon. Rum. Limes. Mint. All in a punch, yes. The most refreshing drink, perfect for any day.
instructions: Take the rind off the watermelon and cut into small chunks.
Blend the watermelon in a food processor. Using a sieve, strain the purée and set it aside.
Chop the limes in half.
In a pitcher, pop the ice in, the juice of the limes, rum, grenadine, watermelon juice, orange juice and a handful of mint leaves.
Give it a stir and enjoy.

name: Watermelon and Feta Salad with Crispy Shallots
description: The ultimate summer salad. We've taken a classic combo and given it a twist with crispy shallots and a sharp, zingy dressing.
instructions: Thinly slice the shallots, place in a small saucepan and cover with 100ml vegetable oil.

Heat the saucepan over medium heat and bring to a slow simmer. Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until the shallots are deeply golden. Don’t be tempted to whack the heat up to speed up the process - getting evenly crisp shallots takes a few minutes.
Strain the oil into a heatproof bowl and let the shallots cool in the sieve. They will crisp up as they cool.
Juice the limes and add them to the strained shallot oil, along with the red wine vinegar and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Leave to cool while you prep the veg.
Peel and cut the watermelon into large chunks. Thinly slice the red onion. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Cut the feta into large chunks. Roughly chop the fresh basil and mint.
Place everything in a large bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Add the dressing and toss to coat.
Plate the salad up on a platter. Top with the crispy shallots then serve and enjoy!

name: Watermelon, Mint, Chilli Ice Pops
description: Fresh and spicy. This flavour combo is perfect for the summertime. Check out the other flavour combos on the website.
instructions: Blend the watermelon (with the seeds for extra nutrients if you like) with the mint, chili and lime, until smooth.
Pour into the molds and freeze for 3-4 hours.
Optional to sprinkle some sumac over them, which is really deliciously zingy.

name: Weeknight Chicken Gyros
description: This one’s all about the contrast between the crispy chicken and the cool, creamy tzatziki. A fakeaway wrap you can make in a flash.
instructions: If you're not using an airfryer, heat the oven to 220°C. Finely grate two-thirds of the garlic cloves. Add to a mixing bowl with the chicken thighs, half of the yoghurt, onion powder, paprika, cumin, oregano, zest and juice of half the lemon, and salt. Season with black pepper and mix well. Set aside to marinate while you prep the rest.

Grate the cucumber and squeeze out any excess liquid using your hands or a clean tea towel. Add to a bowl with the remaining yoghurt, the juice of the other lemon half, the last garlic clove (grated), and a good pinch of salt. Mix together to make your tzatziki and set aside.
Finely slice the red onion and tomato.

Tip the frozen fries into the bottom of your air fryer basket and lay the marinated chicken thighs on top. Cook at 200°C for 10–15 mins until the fries are crisp and the chicken is golden and cooked through.If you're using an oven instead just spread the fries in a single layer on a baking tray and place the marinated chicken thighs on a wire rack above (or on a separate tray). Roast for 25–30 mins, flipping the fries and chicken halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and golden and the fries are crisp.
Toast the flatbreads in a dry pan until warm and slightly charred.

To assemble, spread a generous spoonful of tzatziki over each flatbread. Top with tomato, red onion and slices of the cooked chicken, scatter with the fresh parsley, add the fries, if using, then wrap it all up.

name: Weeping Tiger Noodle Salad
description: Usually for a weeping tiger steak you marinate the steak before cooking - but here we’re going to reverse marinate. Cook the steak until super crisp, but blushing pink in the middle, then put it into a fish and soy sauce, sugar and lime juice marinade.
instructions: If you’re not using rice, head straight to step 2. Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat and add the rice. Cook, tossing, for 2 mins until the grains turn an even golden brown. Tip into a pestle and mortar and grind to a powder, then set aside.
Cook the rice noodles following pack instructions, then drain through a fine sieve and run under cold water to prevent them from cooking further. Drain again and set aside.

Peel the garlic clove and smash it between the chopping board and the flat of a large knife, then add to a shallow bowl. Half and thinly slice the red chilli and scrape half into the shallow bowl and keep half for later. Spoon the fish sauce, soy sauce and sugar into the bowl, then squeeze in the juice of both limes. Mix well and set aside

Drizzle the sirloin steaks with a little oil, then season really well with salt. Get a frying pan over a high heat and leave until screaming hot. Lay the steaks into the pan and cook for 2 mins on each side for medium-rare. Take out of the pan and put straight into the dressing bowl, tossing the steaks to coat in the sauce. Leave to rest while you slice up the veg.
Thinly slice the sugar snap peas at an angle, then thinly slice the radishes. Divide the noodles between two bowls, then scatter over the sliced sugar snap peas and radishes.

Remove the steaks from the dressing and slice at an angle. Spoon some of the dressing over the noodles and veg, then drape the steaks on top. Pour the rest of the dressing over the steaks, then scatter over the herbs, ground rice (if using) and reserved chilli.

name: Welsh Rarebit Burgers
description: This rarebit mix enriched with Guinness takes the cheeseburger to a whole new level. Oozy and delicious.
instructions: Melt 1/3 of your butter in a saucepan and add your flour. Cook out for a couple of minutes until it starts to smell biscuity.

Gradually pour in half of your Guinness, whisking all the while until you have a smooth sauce. Add your Worcestershire sauce, most of the english mustard, leaving a tsp for later and your cheddar, then gently stir together until your cheese has melted and you have a thick mixture. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour your mixture into a container and chill in the fridge until ready to eat.
Peel, halve and finely slice your onions.
Melt your remaining butter in a frying pan. Tip in the onions and fry over a gentle heat for 15 minutes until softened.

Whack up the heat and keep cooking your onions until they are totally caramelised, stirring frequently to pick up any caramelisation from the pan. This will take about 15 minutes longer. Deglaze with your remaining Guinness if the onions needs a little more moisture - this will help the onions steam and soften.
Shred your lettuce, slice your gherkins and toast your burger buns in a dry cast iron pan.
Combine your mayonnaise with your remaining english mustard.
Heat your grill to high.
Get your cast iron pan or large frying pan heating on a high heat with a little vegetable oil.
Get your beef mince and gently shape it into balls - 2 small patties per burger. Season the surface with salt and pepper.
Place a couple of your mince balls in the hot pan and pop a square of baking parchment on top of them. Place another heavy pan on top of the parchment to compress the burgers.
Fry for 2 minutes until the edges are going caramelised and crispy, then flip. Fry for two minutes on the other side. Repeat with your remaining patties.
Place your patties on a baking tray and put 2 tbsp of your rarebit mixture onto each. Grill for 2 minutes until the rarebit mix is bubbly and melted.

Assembly time. Spread a little mustardy mayo on the base and lid of your burger bun. Add some shredded lettuce to the base along with some pickles, then stack on two burger patties. Pop the lid on your burger and serve.

name: What Willy Cook's Chicken Satay Skewers
description: What Willy shows us how to make satay chicken skewers. This peanutty, creamy, spicy sauce is the one. Served up with rice and a fresh little pickle.
instructions: Get your chicken breasts and chop them into chunks. Pop them in a bowl.
Make your marinade. Place your garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, peanuts, cumin, coconut milk, the juice from your lime and peanut butter into a food processor, then whizz until smooth.
Pour your marinade over your chicken and give it a good toss until all coated. Marinade in the fridge for 2 hours.
Meanwhile, soak your wooden skewers in water.
Heat your grill to high.
Remove your chicken from the marinade and place onto your skewers.
Place your chicken under the grill and cook for 20-30 mins until your chicken is all tender and charred around the edges. You’ll need to turn them occasionally to ensure that they cook easily.
Whilst your chicken grills, make your slaw. Get a vegetable peeler and use it to peel large strips of carrot and cucumber. Grate your cabbage. Finely chop your coriander.
Add your vegetable ribbons and cabbage to a bowl and mix with your rice wine vinegar, lime juice, most of your coriander, and black and white sesame seeds.
Heat your remaining coconut milk and sesame oil and give them a good whisk.
Add your peanut butter, soy sauce, fish sauce, chilli flakes, garlic powder and honey to the pan and whisk again until all lovely and smooth.
Serve your skewers on top of rice along with your slaw. Top with crushed peanuts, coriander, chilli flakes and a drizzle of your satay sauce. Eat up.

name: Whipped Feta and Garlicky Tomatoes
description: It’s quick and easy to make and is such a crowd pleaser! Don’t throw away the oil that the tomatoes have been cooking in. It’s incredible! @londonbruncher x
instructions: Put all of the whipped feta ingredients in a food processor with 3 tablespoons of olive oil and blend until smooth and creamy.
Heat your oven to 180°C.
Put all of the slow roasted tomatoes ingredients in an oven dish with 120ml olive oil. Roast for 30-45 mins.
Serve the hot tomatoes on top of the whipped feta with some crusty bread. I love the contrast of the hot juicy tomatoes and cool creamy feta.

name: Whipped Goat’s Cheese and Strawberries on Toast
description:
In Partnership With Aldi. #ad

Beautiful, sweet, and in-season British strawberries tossed through savoury balsamic roasted cherry tomatoes and rested on a bed of creamy whipped goat's cheese. The perfect sweet and savoury snack.
keywords: Whipped Goat’s Cheese and Strawberries on Toast
Whipped Goat’s Cheese and Strawberries on Toast recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Halve the tomatoes and add into a baking tin. Drizzle with balsamic, olive oil, season with salt and pepper, roast for 20-25 mins until softened and bubbling.

Meanwhile, add the goats cheese, Greek yoghurt and heavy cream into a bowl. Whisk together until fluffy. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer the whipped cheese mixture into a piping bag or sandwich bag.
Stir the pesto and olive oil together. Halve the strawberries, quartering any large ones.

Cut the tip of the piping/sandwich bag off and pipe the whipped goat's cheese onto a piece of bread - if you aren’t piping it, spread it on thick, using the back of a spoon. Drizzle over the pesto. Stir the strawberries into the tomatoes and spoon onto the toast. Finish with a crack of fresh black pepper.

name: Whipped Pea, Artichoke & Za’atar with New Potatoes
description: This whipped pea and artichoke combination makes a great base for the warm potato salad. Another protein-packed, balanced meal that’s great for meal prep.
instructions: Defrost the peas. Next, bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the potatoes and boil for around 15 minutes, or until just cooked through. Take care not to overcook; they should be firm but just soft enough to poke your fork through without resistance.

While the potatoes are cooking, add the asparagus spears to the saucepan for 2 minutes, then remove them with tongs and place them in a colander. Rinse under cold running water to stop them cooking, then set aside.
When the potatoes are done, drain them and set them aside in a colander to steam dry.

To make the whipped pea and artichoke purée, blend all the ingredients in a small food processor (which will give you a chunky texture) or a blender (for a smooth texture). Season to taste with plenty of salt and pepper.
Cut the potatoes into bite-sized pieces. Cut the asparagus spears into 3cm pieces. Thinly slice the artichoke pieces.
Combine the potatoes, asparagus, artichokes, rocket and peas in a large bowl. Add the Dijon mustard, lemon juice and olive oil. Toss to combine, and season well to taste.

To assemble, spoon plenty of the whipped pea mixture on to a plate. Top with the potatoes and vegetables, then drizzle with a little more olive oil, and sprinkle over the za’atar and sesame seeds, if using. Tear over the mint leaves and crumble on the vegan feta or tofu, then serve.

name: Whipped Tahini with Tomatoes & Soy Butter Drizzle
description: Velvety whipped tahini with in-season tomatoes and an umami soy butter drizzle.
keywords: Whipped Tahini with Tomatoes & Soy Butter Drizzle
Whipped Tahini with Tomatoes & Soy Butter Drizzle recipe
instructions: Whisk the tahini with the water until creamy, then set aside.
Mince the ginger. Roughly chop the tomatoes and finely slice the spring onion.

Add the vegan butter to a small frying pan set over a medium heat. Once the butter has melted, add the nuts and/or seeds and cook for 5 mins, stirring often, until toasted. Add the ginger and sugar and stir for 1 min, then remove from the heat. Add the chilli flakes, soy sauce and the juice of half the lime. Stir to combine.
Spread the whipped tahini onto plates and top with the chopped tomatoes. Spoon over the soy butter drizzle, squeeze over the juice from the remaining lime half and top with the spring onions.

name: Whiskey Sour
description: This simple cocktail recipe is one that you should be adding to your weekend repertoire. Grab a cocktail shaker and you're set.
instructions: Cut a thin piece of rind off the lemon and set aside for garnish, then juice the lemon.
Add your sugar and water to a pan, simmering until the two are mixed and form a simple syrup.
Separate your egg yolk from the white. Add the white to the cocktail shaker, saving the yolk for a hungover omelette the next day.

Dry shake your white in a shaker to achieve a foamy texture, then add a 25ml measure of the lemon juice, a 25ml measure of the simple syrup (save the leftover syrup for the next round), a double shot of whiskey (50ml or a 25ml single depending how strong you want it) and some ice.
Shake the cocktail shaker for 30 seconds, then pour it out into your glass.
Garnish with a lemon and enjoy.

name: White Asparagus & Bean Soup
description: A simple hearty soup that makes the most of seasonal white asparagus. We’ve used the tough roots and peels to make a white asparagus stock, giving the soup loads of flavour while also reducing waste.
instructions: To prepare the asparagus: peel off the outer layers of skin (sparing the tips) and chop off 1cm from the ends. Slice the peeled and trimmed asparagus into slices.
Heat up the vegetable stock in a medium pot, then pop in the asparagus peels and Parmesan rinds. Reduce the heat to a simmer and simmer away for about 45 mins to let the flavours infuse.
Meanwhile, slice the light green and white parts of the leek (discard the rest) and peel and slice the garlic. If using frozen peas, defrost them in cold water. Chop the kale.
Heat up a glug of olive oil in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the sliced leeks and sauté for about 5 mins until fragrant. Add in the sliced garlic and continue cooking for 2 mins.

Once the leek and garlic are softened, add in the peas, asparagus slices and drained white beans. Stir everything well, add a pinch of salt and black pepper, then let the flavours meld for a few mins.
Strain the broth, discarding the solids, and pour the liquid into the pot with the vegetables. Let it simmer on a low heat for about 15 mins, until the asparagus has softened.
Meanwhile, heat a splash of olive oil in a small pan over a medium heat. Add the almond slices and cook them until lightly toasted (monitor the pan – they burn quicker than you think).
Stir the chopped kale into the soup and cook for 2-3 mins, until just wilted, then remove from the heat.
Divide between bowls and top with a spoonful of toasted almonds. Enjoy!

name: White Chocolate Cheesecake Recipe
description: A creamy no-bake cheesecake loaded with white chocolate is the ultimate dessert for any occasion. This white chocolate cheesecake is simple to prepare, yet it delivers a sophisticated flavour and texture that will impress everyone. The smooth, velvety filling combines rich cream cheese and melted white chocolate, creating a luscious, indulgent treat. With a buttery graham cracker or digestive biscuit crust, it provides the perfect contrast of flavours and textures. You don’t need to worry about baking; just chill the cheesecake in the fridge for a few hours or overnight to let it set. Garnish it with white chocolate shavings, fresh berries, or a drizzle of raspberry sauce for a pop of colour and extra flavour. Whether you’re hosting a dinner party or craving something sweet, this no-bake white chocolate cheesecake is the perfect dessert choice for any occasion.
instructions: Make the cheesecake base. Crush the biscuits by bashing them in a bag with a rolling pin, being careful to keep the pieces of biscuit reasonable large.
Melt the unsalted butter in a pan then stir in the crushed biscuits until coated all over.
Add the buttery biscuit to a serving dish, pressing it into an even layer.
Now make the cheesecake filling. In a mixing bowl, beat the cream cheese and crème fraîche together until soft
In a second mixing bowl, semi-whip the double cream.
Melt the white chocolate buttons over a bain-marie until blood temperature (37°C).
Fold the chocolate into the cream cheese mix, then fold in the semi-whipped cream.
Add the cheesecake filling to the biscuit base and top with white chocolate shavings. Then leave to set in the fridge overnight.

name: White Chocolate Gingerbread Cookies
description: Nothing beats a gently spiced cookie. Loaded up with incredible Dr. Oetker white chocolate chunks, these gooey snacks are going to change your life.
instructions: Add your butter to a saucepan and cook gently for about 3 mins – wait for the butter to brown and for it to start to smell biscuity. Remove it from the heat, then leave to cool for 10 mins.
Add your butter to a large mixing bowl along with your sugar. Whisk until the mixture is light and fluffy.
Crack in your egg and add your vanilla extract, then beat again until combined.
Sieve in your flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, and a pinch of salt, then fold the mixture carefully until it is totally combined.
Roughly chop your white chocolate into large chunks and get this in the mixture.
Pop the mixture in the fridge to chill for 20 mins.
Heat your oven to 170°C.
Line two large baking trays with parchment paper.
Roll your cookie dough mixture into 12 similarly-sized balls, then spread these out evenly across two trays. The mixture will spread as they cook, so make sure there is enough room left between each.
Bake for 12 mins.
Leave your cookies to cool on the tray for 15 mins - they will firm up as they cool. Enjoy!

name: White Chocolate Streusel & Raspberry Muffins Recipe
description: Indulge in the perfect blend of sweet and tangy with this raspberry muffins recipe featuring a rich white chocolate streusel topping. These muffins combine the tartness of fresh raspberries with the creamy sweetness of white chocolate, making each bite a delightful experience. Perfect for breakfast, a snack, or dessert, these muffins are versatile and satisfying. The addition of muffin cups ensures easy baking and serving, while the streusel topping adds a delicious crunch. Whether you’re a fan of classic muffins or looking to try something new, these raspberry muffins are sure to become a favourite. Enjoy them with a dollop of raspberry jam or a drizzle of caramel sauce for an extra touch of sweetness. Perfectly paired with a morning coffee or as a dessert with a scoop of ice cream, these muffins are a must-try for any baking enthusiast.
keywords: White Chocolate Streusel & Raspberry Muffins Recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a muffin tray with 12 paper cases.
Melt the butter for the muffins, then leave to cool slightly. Cut the white chocolate into random chunks.

For the streusel topping, first cut the cold butter into cubes. Stir the flour and brown sugar together in a bowl along with a pinch of salt, then rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs. Set aside.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, caster sugar and salt together in a large bowl. Crack the eggs into a separate bowl, add the yoghurt and melted butter, then whisk to combine.

Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and use a spatula to just bring the muffin batter together (it’s fine if not completely smooth), then gently fold through the raspberries and white chocolate – you don’t want to overmix, as that will make your muffins heavy.
Fill the muffin cases three-quarters of the way full, then sprinkle 1 tbsp streusel topping across the top of each muffin, patting it slightly so that it sticks.

Bake on the middle shelf of the oven for 5 mins, then turn the heat down to 160°C and bake for a further 18-20 mins until risen, golden brown and a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. Eat warm or cold – you do you.

name: White Chocolate and Pretzel Cheesecake
description: This, MOB, is filthily good. The combination of the sweet, creamy white chocolate filling and salty pretzel base is going to blow your minds.
instructions: Line the base of a 20cm round cake tin with baking paper. If you don’t have a cake tin you can use a small roasting tin instead and make a rectangular cheesecake.

Using a mini food processor blitz 150g pretzels in two batches until they resemble fine breadcrumbs. Melt the butter then mix into the crushed pretzels. Tip into your tin and press into an even layer. Put in the fridge for 15 minutes to set up
Break the white chocolate into a microwaveable bowl. Zap in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring in between each one, until melted and glossy. Set aside to briefly cool.
Meanwhile, in a separate bowl whisk the double cream until it just holds its shape and has thickened.

Dump the cream cheese and vanilla extract into the just cooled white chocolate. Whisk to combine then fold through the whipped cream so you have a light and airy cheesecake mix. Spoon the mix on top of the pretzel base. Smooth out the top then put in the fridge for at least 5 hours until set.
To serve, break the remaining pretzels over the top then cut out a sexy slice. Will keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

name: White Chocolate, Matcha & Miso Truffles
