description: These truffles made with miso are perfect for after dinner. Sweet, aromatic and a little savoury. Think salted caramel... trust us, they're delicious.
instructions: Finely chop the white chocolate into shards and place in a heatproof bowl. Add the cream and miso to a small saucepan and bring to a boil. Whisk to incorporate the miso.
Pour into the white chocolate and fold together until completely melted. Pour into a tupperware container and set in the fridge for 2 hours.
Using a teaspoon, scoop out some of the mixture and mold into a ball, or any shape you like.
Roll them in the desiccated coconut, then pop them back in the fridge for 20 minutes to remove any stickiness from the outside of the balls.
Dust with the matcha powder and pop onto a plate in the fridge.
Serve from the fridge, after dinner with a black coffee.

name: Whole Baked Camembert
description: It's the caramelised balsamic grapes that take this baked camembert to the highest level. Dip in your homemade garlicky soldiers and enjoy.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C/356°F.

Line a roasting tray with baking paper. Cut the grapes into small bunches. Put the grapes onto the tray and drizzle with olive oil. Season with a pinch of salt and a grind of pepper. Sprinkle 1 tsp of chilli flakes over the grapes and whack the tray in the oven for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, take the camembert out of the plastic wrapping and its cloth then place it back in the empty box with the lid off. Prick the top of the cheese all over with a sharp knife. Season with a grind of pepper and ½ a tsp of chilli flakes. Once the grapes have cooked for their allotted time, nestle the cheese in the centre of the tray and roast for another 10 minutes.
Ciabatta time. Cut the ciabatta in half lengthways and then in half across the middle. Slice the bread into soldiers around an inch thick and set aside.
Melt the butter in a saucepan or microwave and add to a bowl. Crush the garlic, add to the butter and stir.
Lay your ciabatta soldiers in a single layer on a large baking tray. Pour over the garlicky butter and a pinch of salt and a good grind of pepper. Whack in the oven for 10 minutes.

Take the grapes and camembert out of the oven and drizzle the balsamic vinegar over the grapes. Return the tray to the oven and bake for a final 10 minutes until the cheese is oozy, the grapes are soft and the soldiers are crispy. Serve all together and dig in! Enjoy!

name: Whole Grilled Sea Bass Recipe With Salmoriglio Sauce
description: Grilled sea bass is a delectable choice for any seafood lover, offering a light yet flavourful dish that's perfect for any occasion. This white fish, prized for its tender, flaky texture, absorbs marinades beautifully, making it ideal for grilling on a BBQ or gas grill. To enhance the natural flavours, consider marinating the sea bass in a mixture of fish sauce, white wine, and red pepper flakes before grilling. Pair it with a side of couscous or a fresh slaw for a balanced meal that’s both satisfying and healthy. Whether you're preparing a simple family dinner or an elegant outdoor gathering, grilled sea bass is sure to impress with its delicate flavour and melt-in-your-mouth texture. Salmoriglio is a Southern Italian sauce that is super lemony and made with oregano. It pairs perfectly with this grilled sea bass.
keywords: Whole Grilled Sea Bass Recipe With Salmoriglio Sauce
instructions: Strip the leaves off the oregano, then very finely chop along with the parsley. Scrape into a small bowl. Finely grate in the garlic and lemon zest, then juice in the lemon, add the dried oregano and pour in the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Score the sea bass with three diagonal cuts on both sides, then transfer to a large bowl and spoon half the sauce over and inside the sea bass. Leave to marinate in the fridge for 20 mins.

You can cook this over a well-oiled BBQ; on a large griddle pan over a medium-high heat; or under a hot grill. If cooking under the grill, lay the marinated sea bass onto a flat baking tray – if not, place straight onto the BBQ or griddle pan. Cook for 5-7 mins, then carefully flip the fish and cook for 5-7 mins more depending on the size and thickness of your fish. The sea bass is cooked when the skin is nicely charred, and the flesh is opaque, bright white and flaking away from the bones in large pieces.
Transfer the grilled fish to a platter. Serve with the remaining sauce spooned over. We love to eat this with a big tomato salad and some smashed potatoes.

name: Whole Roast Aubergine With Harissa Chickpea Tabbouleh
description: Roasting whole aubergines seems like it might be a bit of a faff, but it’s actually very quick and easy in the air fryer. For a speedy weeknight meal we've served them with zesty tahini yogurt and stuffed them with a crispy harissa chickpea salad.
keywords: Whole Roast Aubergine With Harissa Chickpea Tabbouleh
Whole Roast Aubergine With Harissa Chickpea Tabbouleh recipe
instructions: Drain the chickpeas, then rinse and pat them dry with kitchen paper. Tip them into a bowl with the harissa and a quarter of the olive oil Season with salt and pepper, then give everything a good mix.
Rub the aubergines with a quarter of the olive oil, then poke them a few times with a fork.
Tip the harissa chickpeas into the air fryer and top with the aubergines. Turn it on to 200°C and cook for 20-25 mins, turning halfway through.

Meanwhile, halve and de-seed the tomatoes, then finely dice. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds, then smash it flat and finely dice. Drain and finely chop the roasted peppers. Wash and finely chop the mint and parsley. Add the tomatoes, cucumber, peppers and herbs to a bowl with some olive oil. Add the juice of the lemon, mix well and season with salt and pepper.
Get the yoghurt into another bowl, add the tahini and grate in the garlic. Squeeze in the juice of the remaining lemon and season with salt and pepper.

Remove the aubergine from the air fryer and gently cut it in half, making sure not to cut all the way through (you’ll fill it like you would a jacket potato later). Let the aubergines drain for a couple of minutes – it helps if you lift them with tongs to let the excess moisture out. Season the insides with salt and pepper.
Add the crispy harissa chickpeas to the tomato bowl and toss well.
Spread the yoghurt over two plates, then top with the aubergine. Fill the aubergines with the chickpea tabbouleh and top with an extra drizzle of tahini and harissa, if you like.

name: Whole Roasted Broccoli with Romesco Sauce
description: Forget about whole roasted cauliflower, roasting your broccoli whole is where it’s at. Serve this with a herby rice salad as a veggie centrepiece.
keywords: Whole Roasted Broccoli with Romesco Sauce
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Trim the broccoli stem down enough so the broccoli can stand up on its own. Place the broccoli into a small roasting tin and drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt, then add 50ml water to the base of the tray. Slide into the oven to roast for 30-40 mins, until charred all over and cooked through.

Meanwhile, make the romesco sauce by blitzing the peppers, lemon juice, toasted almond flakes and smoked paprika together with 3 tbsp of olive oil. Season well with salt and pepper. Add enough water to loosen it to drizzle-able consistency.
Mix the harissa paste with 30ml olive oil to make a bright red oil.

Once the broccoli is cooked through, place upright on a plate. Drizzle with the romesco sauce, followed by the harissa oil. Scatter with toasted almonds and parsley leaves. Finish with a crack of black pepper to serve.

name: Whole Roasted Chipotle Cauliflower With Avocado Crema
description: We've added our own spin to this whole roasted cauli by throwing chipotle paste into the mix. The end result is delicious and goes perfectly with the avo crema.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C.
Mix the chipotle paste with 200ml water, red wine vinegar, 1 tsp sugar and 2 tbsp olive oil. Peel and finely grate 1 of the garlic cloves into the sauce. Season with salt.
Prepare the cauliflower by using a knife to cut away the leaves at the base. Save the leaves – we’ll use them later.

Place the cauliflower into a roasting tray. Pour the chipotle liquid all over the cauliflower, making sure it spreads into all the cracks and seams. Cover the cauliflower with tin foil and slide into the oven, roast for 1 hour until tender when poked with a skewer. Every 20 mins, remove the foil, baste with the liquid in the tray, then cover with the foil and return to the oven.
Add the cauliflower leaves and pumpkin seeds to a separate tray, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt, slide into the oven and cook for 10-15 mins, until the leaves are crisp. Set aside.

While the cauliflower is in the oven, halve and destone the avocados. Spoon the flesh into a blender and add the Greek yoghurt, the zest of one lime and the juice of 2 limes. Add most of the coriander and mint leaves, reserving a few for serving. Peel the remaining garlic clove and add to the blender along with 4 tbsp of olive oil. Season with salt and blend until smooth. Set aside in the fridge.
Make your quick pickled onions. Slice the red onions as thinly as you can, add to a bowl and squeeze in the juice of 2 limes, along with the remaining tsp of sugar and a tsp of salt. Set aside.

When the cauliflower is tender remove the foil and baste again with all the juices. Then turn the oven up to maximum heat. Return the uncovered cauliflower to the oven and roast for 15 mins until charred, basting regularly with the juices — the sauce should be coating the cauliflower.
To serve, spread the avocado crema on the base of the plate and top with the whole roasted cauliflower, cauliflower leaves and pumpkin seeds. Scatter with the pickled onions, and the reserved herbs.

name: Whole Roasted Muhammara Cauliflower
description: This whole roasted cauliflower is a vegan centrepiece banger. We've loaded it up with tahini sauce, muhammara and pomegranate seeds for loads of freshness.
instructions: Heat your oven to 190°C/374°F.
Trim the leaves of your cauliflower and the stem so that you are left with a whole white head that sits flat.

Place your cauliflower in a high sided baking tray and top with a drizzle of olive oil, 1 tsp of your Aleppo pepper and a generous pinch of salt. Rub into the skin with your hands, then pour a splash of water into the base of your baking tray. Place in the oven to roast for 50 mins, adding more water to the base of the tin halfway through - this will steam the cauliflower whilst it roasts to make it super tender.

Whilst your cauliflower roasts, make your muhammara sauce. Place your red peppers, breadcrumbs, walnuts, tomato puree, pomegranate molasses, your remaining aleppo pepper and olive oil into a blender, then whizz up for 30 seconds until you have a totally smooth sauce. Season with salt to taste, then set aside.

Pop your tahini in a bowl and whisk together with your lemon juice and a splash of water until it comes together in a silky, smooth sauce. It will look like it’s split when you first start whisking, but keep going until it comes back together. Loosen with water until it reaches your desired consistency, then season to taste with salt.
Roughly chop your parsley.

Remove your cauliflower from the oven when it’s beautifully caramelised on the outside and tender on the inside - you can test this by carefully sticking a cutlery knife in the side and seeing if it slices through.

Place your cauliflower on your chosen serving dish, then drizzle over your muhammara and tahini sauce. Sprinkle with parsley and pomegranate seeds, then serve up. Pop your extra muhammara and tahini sauce in bowls on the side for people to dunk into.

name: Whole Turkey Breast in Prosciutto
description: Turkey Saltimbocca style, which translates from Italian to ‘jump in the mouth’. For perfectly cooked turkey every time, buy a digital meat thermometer and cook the thickest part of the turkey to 74°C.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170°C fan.
Pat the turkey breast dry with some paper towels and season well with salt and pepper.

In the cavity of the turkey breast, smear ½ the butter and lay the sage leaves. Then smear the remaining butter over the top of the turkey breast. Wrap the breast with prosciutto slices, overlapping them slightly to fully cover the turkey. Secure the prosciutto with kitchen string.

Heat the olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan or skillet set over a medium-high heat. Add the wrapped turkey breast and sear it on all sides until the prosciutto is lightly golden, about 5 mins in total.

Transfer the pan with the turkey breast to the oven and roast for about 1 - 1 ¼ hours, or until the internal temperature reaches 74°C in the thickest part of the meat, and the juices run clear. Baste the turkey breast from time to time as it cooks, spooning over the cooking fats from the pan.
Remove the turkey from the pan, basting the meat once again, then let the turkey rest, covered, for at least 15 mins before slicing.

name: Wholegrain Fusilli & Green Bean Pasta
description: A high-fibre, healthy dinner recipe you can make in just one pot. Minimal washing up, maximum flavour.
keywords: Wholegrain Fusilli & Green Bean Pasta recipe
instructions: Fill a pot with heavily salted water and get it on a good roiling boil.
Trim the green beans and chop them in half. Chunk up your courgette. Add the beans, courgette chunks, and pasta to the pan. Cook for 12 mins. While your pasta is cooking, chop up your basil.

Once the pasta is cooked, drain the mixture and reserve a mug of the pasta water for later. Add your pasta, courgette, and green beans back to the pot with two-thirds of your grated Parmesan and most of your chopped basil. Add in your olive oil, salt, pepper, and a three-quarters of your favourite chilli oil.

Rigorously mix the contents of the pot until the Parmesan has melted. Put the lid on it and let it sit for 5 mins. Serve your plates with more grated Parmesan on top and more fresh basil, chilli oil, and olive oil.

name: Wholegrain Spelt Scones
description: These hearty scones have real depth of flavour, with a sprinkling of ground hazelnuts to bring out the nuttiness of the spelt. Incredible with jam, butter and fresh strawberries.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C fan. Line a baking tray with baking parchment. Grind the hazelnuts in a food processor until a crumbly texture. Melt the butter in a pan over a low heat. Set aside.

If making the dough by hand, whisk together the sifted flour, baking powder, sugar and a pinch of sea salt (skip the salt if you prefer a sweeter dough) in a large mixing bowl. Add the butter and pass the mix through your fingertips lightly, thumbs across fingers, to make breadcrumbs – the aim here is to coat the flour in the butter, not rub it in, so keep your fingers light and fast. This may take 5 mins or so. Alternatively you can use a food processor for this first stage.

Now add the milk and egg, and with well-floured hands bring the mixture together to form a dough. Lightly dust it with flour and shape it into a ball. Wrap the dough in cling film and refrigerate for a minimum of 20 mins. Make an egg wash by whisking together the egg yolk and milk.

Remove the dough from the fridge and gently roll out to 3cm thickness on a lightly floured surface. Cut out rounds using a 6cm cutter and place on your prepared baking tray, leaving a little room for expansion. Brush the tops with a thin layer of egg wash and sprinkle with the ground hazelnuts and some extra brown sugar, if you like.
Bake for 15 mins, or until just lightly browning. Remove from the oven and allow to cool on the tray for 10 mins before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Willy's Pork Roast Bánh Mì
description: Someone’s made a roast, there’s leftover roast pork. What will you do? Make this sandwich of course.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Slice up the cucumber into rounds, coarsely grate the carrot and thinly slice the red onion and chilli. Add to a bowl with the vinegar, 1 tbsp of soy and a pinch of salt to quickly pickle.
Thinly slice the roast pork and chuck the baguettes into the oven for 5 mins.
To make the bánh mì sauce, mix the mayo, sriracha, hoisin and remaining soy in a bowl.
Now slice the baguettes in half lengthways and spread the bottom half with the bánh mì sauce. Top with roast pork and ham and the quick pickles.
Slice the spring onions and add it to your sandwich with some of the herbs. Spread pâté over the top half of the baguette and smash it on top.
YUM.

name: Winter ‘Sorta Caesar’ With Garlic Croutons
description: A creamy version of a caesar but made with tahini and Worcestershire sauce instead of mayo and anchovy. Full of nuts and healthy fats, this is a great alternative to the classic.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the bread into thick pieces, then tear it into chunky croutons and tip them into a bowl with the olive oil, salt and pepper. Grate in half of your garlic.
Roughly chop the nuts. Tip the bread and nuts onto a baking tray and cook for 10-15 mins until golden. Take care not to burn the nuts.
Put the kale into a bowl and squeeze in the juice of half your lemons. Add some salt and massage with your hands until the kale is softened and slightly wilted.

Make the dressing by combining the tahini with the juice of the remaining lemon in a bowl. Grate in the remaining garlic clove and mix until combined – it will seize up, but don’t worry. Add the water and mix until loosened and not lumpy, then mix through the mustard and Worcestershire sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Roughly chop the romaine. Toss the kale and romaine with the toasted nuts and croutons, then mix with the dressing. Top with a grating of Parmesan and get stuck in.

name: Wintery Leek & Potato Eggs
description: This recipe borrows ideas from two of my favourite egg dishes: Tunisian shakshuka and Turkish çılbır. It also makes the most of seasonal winter produce.
instructions: Finely slice the onion and leek and dice the potato into roughly 2cm cubes.
Sweat in 3 tbsp of olive oil over a medium heat until the onion and leek are turning golden and the potato is softening. This will take about 7 or 8 mins.
Slice the cavolo nero, add it to the pan and cook for another few mins until soft.
Now add the spinach in 2 halves, with a pinch of salt each time, and let it wilt down.
Once all of the spinach is cooked, finely chop all of the herbs and add along with the cumin and a big pinch of salt.
Once the herbs have wilted, taste and check for seasoning. After you add the eggs it will be harder to season the mix so do it now.
Make four little dips in the vegetable mix and crack an egg into each one. Cover the pan with a lid and let the heat and steam cook the eggs.
Take the pan off the heat just before the eggs are done, they will keep cooking for another minute or so.
Add a few dollops of Greek yoghurt and spread it around a bit.
Melt the butter in a small pan. Once hot, add the paprika and chilli and swirl the butter around before pouring it over the eggs.
Serve with crusty bread. Enjoy!

name: XO Chicken Caesar Salad
description: XO sauce brings new levels of deliciousness to a creamy caesar dressing. Funky, a bit spicy, really very tasty. You are going to love this one.
instructions: Heat your oven to 180°C.
Place your thighs in a bowl and add your five spice, crispy chilli oil and sesame oil. Grate in one clove of garlic, then season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat a frying pan on a medium-high heat. Add your thighs to the pan skin-side down and cook for 5 mins until the skin is super crispy. Flip over and cook for 4 mins on that side, then remove from the pan and leave to rest and cool.

Tear your ciabatta loaf into small bite-sized pieces. Toss them onto a large baking tray and add your black sesame seeds, a good pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Toss to totally coat, then bake for 10 mins until golden and crispy.
Separate your egg and pop your yolk in a small food processor. Save your white for another occasion.
Add your XO sauce, mustard, parmesan and lemon juice to the food processor, then give it a whizz to combine.
Very gradually pour in 150ml of vegetable oil to the egg mixture. Loosen to a thinner consistency with 2 tbsp water, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
Cut the end off your lettuce and separate the leaves. Put them in a large mixing bowl and add your croutons, chicken and dressing. Toss to combine.
Spoon your salad onto plates and sprinkle with extra parmesan. Serve and enjoy.

name: XO Sauce Omelette with Prawns & Spring Onions
description: XO sauce is a deeply savoury, spicy seafood sauce used widely in Chinese cuisine. As storecupboard ingredients go, this one packs a punch, and a spoonful goes a long way. Few ingredients here, so you’ll be surprised how delicious and quick this recipe is.
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat them well with a fork or whisk until the yolks and whites are fully combined. Season well with a pinch of salt and plenty of black pepper.
Thinly slice and separate the spring onions into green and white parts. Add half the spring onion greens and a pinch of salt to the beaten eggs.

Heat half the butter in a medium or large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Once the butter is foaming, add the prawns and spring onion whites. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring until the prawns are opaque, turning pink and almost cooked through. Stir the XO sauce through and cook for 30 seconds until the prawns are fully cooked through.
Pop the cooked prawn mixture onto a plate and wipe out the pan. Heat the remaining butter in the pan over a medium-high heat and, once the butter is foaming, pour the egg mixture into the pan.

As the omelette begins to set around the edges, use a spatula to gently lift the edges and tilt the pan, all the while slightly shaking the pan to let the uncooked egg flow to the edges. Cook this way for around 1-2 mins.
Once the omelette is mostly set but still slightly runny on top, scatter the prawn mixture on top and carefully fold the other half over.
Slide the omelette onto a plate, season well to taste with salt and plenty of black pepper, then top with the remaining spring onion greens.

name: Xiengni's Midnight Noodles
description: I make this dish minimum 3 times a week, it's my go-to quick dish in any situation. Give it a go! Xien x
instructions: Place the noodles in a heatproof bowl of boiling water for few mins and cover with a lid.
Meanwhile, niche your garlic and slice your spring onions, separating your whites to greens.
Once your noodles are soft, drain using a colander.
Now pour a small glug of veg oil into your wok, and on med heat fry your garlic and white spring onions.
Then add your noodles, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce and the seasoning packet included in your noodle packet. Give it a toss. Then add your green spring onions and give it a final toss.
10 mins bish bash bosh. Enjoy.

name: Xiengni's Vegan Laksa
description: All the flavours of a laksa without any of the meat, this is the ultimate vegan laksa. Every mouthful is a flavour bomb. Rich, warming and spicy, it's a goodie.
instructions: First, soak the dried chillies in boiling water in a heatproof bowl.

Now let's make the spice paste. Roughly chop the ginger, peeled shallots and one lemongrass stalk. Add to a blender along with your garlic and 3 tbsp of vegetable oil. Blend the ingredients till it forms a purée. This is your garlic paste.
Add your garlic paste to a large non-stick wok, pour in 200ml of vegetable oil and let this cook for 30 mins on a medium-low heat.

Meanwhile, roughly chop the fresh chillies and tomato. Blend the drained dried chillies, chopped chillies and tomato with 2 tbsp of vegetable oil in the same blender till it forms a purée. This is your chilli paste.
Now add the chilli paste to your wok and give it a good mix. Let it cook until the oil separates from the paste.

Add in miso paste, turmeric, curry powder and coriander powder before squeezing in the juice of a lime and giving it a good mix. Next you’re going to want to add in the sugar, tamarind paste, coconut milk, stock, and a smashed lemongrass stalk along with a small handful of coriander leaves and 12 curry leaves.
Bring the laska broth to a boil then let it simmer on a low heat for 25 mins.
Meanwhile, chop your tofu into halves then into quarters. Add cornflour, salt, pepper and Chinese five-spice to a large bowl and thoroughly mix the tofu in.
Get a pan on medium-high heat, pour in a glug of oil and fry your tofu until crispy. Set aside.
Thoroughly mix your oyster mushrooms in the same five-spice cornflour mix before chucking them in the pan. Fry on each side for a few mins each until crispy and set aside.
Whack your noodles into a large heatproof bowl with boiling water. This will take 3-4 mins to cook. Drain, rinse with cold water (to stop it from cooking) and set aside.
Get a pot of boiling water on then add your green beans for 3 mins. Add your beansprouts to the same pot and blanch for 15 seconds.
Add the pak choi to your laksa broth and cook for 10 seconds.

Now, add your noodles to a medium-sized bowl, add in a large ladle of laksa broth and the tofu, mushrooms, green beans, beansprouts and pak choi. Garnish each bowl with red chillies, coriander, mint and halved limes and tuck in.

name: Yellow Dal
description: Nothing says comfort like a bowl of creamy, fragrant dal. And nothing says it in a soft, dulcet tone quite like this dal right here. Your ideal yellow dal.
instructions: Peel the ginger and cut into matchsticks.

Rinse the lentils in a bowl of cold water, use your fingers to massage the lentils. Once the water is cloudy, drain and repeat until the water is pretty much clear. Drain the washed lentils in a sieve and tip into a large saucepan. Pour in 2 litres of cold water. Stir in the ginger, turmeric and a generous pinch of salt.

Get your saucepan over a high heat and bring the lentils to the boil. Once boiling reduce the heat to medium, simmer away for 30 mins, stirring occasionally so it doesn’t catch, until the lentils have broken down, most of the water has been absorbed and you are left with a creamy loose dal. Once you are happy with the consistency, season with salt and black pepper then reduce the heat to low to keep the dal warm.

Tarka time. Thinly slice the shallots, garlic and chilli. Get a small frying pan over a high heat. Drizzle in enough neutral oil that it just covers the surface of the pan. Scrape in the shallots and fry for 4–5 mins, stirring regularly, until lightly golden. Add the garlic, chilli, cumin and mustard seeds. Cook for about 1 min more, stirring continuously, until the shallots are just crisp and everything smells unreal. Take off the heat.
Divide the dal between four bowls and spoon over the hot tarka. Tear over some coriander leaves and cut the lime into wedges to serve. We like to eat this with a naan, paratha or roti.

name: Yellow Thai Coconut Broth with Chicken Meatballs & Thai Salad
description: Spicy, soothing and surprisingly quick to make, this Thai yellow curry broth with pan-fried chicken meatballs and a herby spring onion is a winner. Perfect for a midweek meal with friends.
keywords: Yellow Thai Coconut Broth with Chicken Meatballs & Thai Salad
Yellow Thai Coconut Broth with Chicken Meatballs & Thai Salad recipe
instructions: Grate the ginger and garlic. Chop the coriander stalks and leaves, and set aside the leaves for garnish.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a heavy-based pan set over a medium heat. Fry the curry paste for 2 mins then transfer to a large mixing bowl.

Add the chicken mince, coriander stalks, grated ginger and garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, fish sauce and the zest of the lime to the mixing bowl with the fried curry paste(set aside the zested lime for later). Add a pinch of salt and mix until combined and sticky, then form into 16 balls, about 40g each.
Heat a glug of vegetable oil in a large pan set over a medium-high heat. Fry the meatballs in batches for 5-8 mins until golden on all sides, then set aside.

In the same pan, fry the curry paste for 1-2 mins, then pour in the coconut milk and vegetable stock. Bring to a boil, then turn down to a simmer for 10 mins. Squeeze in the juice of the reserved lime and season to taste with salt and fish sauce.
Meanwhile, cook the rice following packet instructions.

Finely slice the spring onions into strips and pick the leaves off the herbs then transfer to a small bowl. To make the dressing, finely slice the red chilli then add to a separate bowl with the other other dressing ingredients and mix until the sugar dissolves. Pour the dressing over the salad.
Before serving, transfer the meatballs to the coconut broth and gently reheat. Serve over rice and top with the salad and extra lime juice.

name: Yellow Thai Coconut Noodle Soup
description: A bright and fragrant coconut noodle soup that'll cure any cold. Let this simmer for a while so the flavour properly builds up.
instructions: Stir almost all of your ground turmeric into the curry paste, leaving a little for later, along with the oil, then set aside. Coat the chicken in the remaining turmeric, then season with salt and plenty of pepper.

Put a large, deep saucepan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add half of the coconut cream and cook until the oil separates and the coconut solids turn golden. Add the curry paste and toast for 2-3 mins.
Pour the chicken stock into the saucepan and bring it to the boil. Turn the heat down to medium and simmer for 20-25 mins to make a broth (skim off any foam that comes up).

Meanwhile, put a frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the chicken until starting to char, then flip and cook through, 6-7 mins on each side. Cook the noodles following pack instructions. Juice the limes.
Strain the broth through a fine mesh sieve, stir through half the remaining coconut cream and season with fish sauce, lime juice and pepper.
Divide the noodles and soup between bowls, top with sliced charred chicken, a drizzle of chilli oil and the remaining coconut cream. Scatter over some coriander to serve.

name: Yoghurt & Chicken Salad with Za’atar Croutons
description: Creamy yoghurt tahini, juicy poached chicken leftovers and crunchy za’atar croutons, all tied together with a zingy lemon dressing. A salad that actually feels like lunch.
keywords: Yoghurt & Chicken Salad with Za’atar Croutons
Yoghurt & Chicken Salad with Za’atar Croutons recipe
instructions: Make the Poached Chicken & Ginger Broth.
Shred the leftover poached chicken and set aside.
Make the Yoghurt Tahini. Grate the garlic. Whisk the skyr, tahini, lemon juice and a pinch of salt in a bowl until smooth, then stir through the garlic. Set aside.
Tear the pitta into bite-sized chunks. Toss with the olive oil, za’atar and a good pinch of salt and pepper.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat and toast the pitta pieces for 5–7 mins, turning often, until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Thinly slice the courgette. Roughly chop the tomatoes. Tear up the dill and parsley. Pit and roughly chop the olives.

Optional 
To make crispy shallots and garlic (if using), thinly slice both and fry in a good glug of oil over a medium heat until deep golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, sumac and a good pinch of salt in a small bowl until emulsified.

Spoon the yoghurt tahini onto plates. Top with the shredded chicken, courgette, tomatoes, olives and herbs. Drizzle over the dressing, then scatter with the za’atar croutons and crispy shallots and garlic, if using. Now get stuck in!

name: Yoghurt Bowl with High-Protein Granola
description: This yoghurt bowl is fresh, fruity and high in protein. Pair it with with our high-protein granola and top it with any fruits or nut butter you like, and you've got yourself a winning breakfast.
instructions: Combine the yoghurt in a bowl alongside your homemade high-protein granola.
Top with your choice of fresh fruit - we used kiwi, blueberries, and strawberries.
Enjoy!

name: Yoghurt Flatbreads With Crispy Chorizo Eggs
description: Easy homemade flatbreads and some hot and spicy eggs. Doesn't get much better than this. Plus, this recipe only has 6 ingredients.
keywords: Yoghurt Flatbreads With Crispy Chorizo Eggs
instructions: Mix 250g of yoghurt and flour with a big pinch of salt in a bowl. Work into a shaggy dough, then tip out onto a work surface and knead until smooth. Turn the bowl over and cover the dough for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, cut the chorizo into a fine-ish dice and finely cut the spring onions.
Split the flatbread dough into 4 and roll each ball out into a rough circle. Preheat a frying pan over a medium heat. Brush each flatbread with a little olive oil.

Carefully lay the first flatbread into the pan and cook for 1-2 mins each side. The flatbread should be nicely golden and puff a little. Add more oil if you want a more golden, crispy bread. Keep the cooked flatbread in a clean kitchen towel while you cook the others.

Once all the flatbreads have been cooked, add the chorizo to the same pan and allow the fat to render out. Once the chorizo is starting to get crispy, crank up the heat, sprinkle in the whites of the spring onions and crack in the eggs.
Season the eggs with salt and pepper and cook over that high heat for 2 mins until lacy and crispy. Once cooked to your liking, scoop them out.
Serve the warm flatbreads topped with the crispy eggs, drizzle with crispy chorizo and scatter over the spring onion greens. Finish with the kimchi or whatever pickled thing you’ve gone for!

name: Yoghurt-Baked Chicken Thighs with Orzo, Oregano & Feta
description: The yoghurt in this marinade gives the chicken just enough pep, but also keeps the chicken thighs extra juicy as they cook. Plus you’ll have a delicious sauce at the end, with which to dress the jumble of orzo, peppers, onions and tomatoes. It couldn’t be any simpler as a midweek recipe – just add herbs and squeeze over plenty of those roasted and gorgeously gunky lemon halves.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Season the chicken with salt and pepper, then set aside.

Combine the yoghurt, oregano and ground spices in a large bowl. Finely grate the garlic into the bowl, plus the zest of half the lemon. Mix well, then tip in the chicken and a splash of olive oil. Mix again, then set aside to marinate for as long or as little as you like.

Slice the onions and peppers and halve the tomatoes (or keep whole if small), then toss with 2 tbsp olive oil and lay in a shallow casserole dish. Place the marinated chicken on top. Slice the part-zested lemon in half, then add that to the dish, too.
Bake in the oven for 35-40 mins until the chicken is beginning to colour and is cooked through, and the vegetables are softened.
Meanwhile, cook the orzo al dente following pack instructions, then drain and toss with a splash of olive oil.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove from the heat and allow to rest for 5 mins. Serve whole or, if you prefer, pull the chicken off the bone and roughly chop, discarding the skin, if you like.
Stir the chicken and vegetables through the orzo, squeezing over the juice from the roasted lemon halves. Crumble the feta on top and sprinkle with roughly chopped oregano to serve.

name: Yoghurt-Marinated Chicken with Courgettes & Crispy Potatoes
description: Spiced yoghurt keeps these chicken thighs juicy under crisp, golden skin, with roast courgettes, crunchy potatoes and a cool minty courgette yoghurt to spoon over.
keywords: Yoghurt-Marinated Chicken with Courgettes & Crispy Potatoes
Yoghurt-Marinated Chicken with Courgettes & Crispy Potatoes recipe
instructions: Grate the garlic and mix with the yoghurt for the marinade, the cumin, ground coriander, chilli flakes, the juice of half a lemon and a generous pinch of salt. Add the chicken thighs and coat thoroughly in the marinade. Leave to marinate for at least 1hr, or overnight in the fridge if time allows. Marinating overnight gives a noticeably deeper flavour and a more tender result, worth doing if you can plan ahead.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the potatoes, toss with the olive oil and a pinch of salt, then spread out in a single layer on a large roasting tray.

Scrape off any big chunks of marinade from the chicken skin so it crisps up in the oven, then add the chicken to a high-sided baking tray with the olive oil. Slide both trays into the oven and roast the chicken for 30-35 mins, until cooked through and the skin is golden and beginning to char at the edges. The potatoes need 20-30 mins, until golden, turning them halfway through, so pull them out once they're ready and keep them somewhere warm. If the yoghurt marinade is catching on the skin before the chicken is cooked through, loosely tent the tray with foil for the middle portion of cooking, then remove it for the final 5-8 mins to crisp back up.

Remove the chicken from the tray and set aside to rest. Slice all but half a courgette into rounds and add to the hot tray, tossing them in all the remaining roasting juices. Slice half a lemon into rounds and tuck those in too. Return to the oven for 8-10 mins, until just tender and catching colour at the edges.
Grate the remaining half courgette and add to the remaining yoghurt with the juice of another lemon half, the extra virgin olive oil and a good pinch of salt and pepper.
Remove the courgettes from the oven, squeeze over the remaining lemon half and scatter with the mint. Serve the chicken on top of or alongside the courgettes, potatoes and raw courgette yoghurt.

name: Yorkshire Puddings
description: Are Yorkshire Puddings the best part of a roast dinner? Whether you love them or hate them, we reckon these ones stand a pretty good chance.
instructions: Heat the oven to 210°C fan.
Add a 1 tsp sunflower oil or goose fat to each of the holes of a 12-hole muffin tin. Then slide into the oven to preheat.

Sieve the flour into a large bowl and season with salt and pepper. Whisk the eggs together in a jug until the whites and yolks are combined, then whisk the eggs into the flour to make a thick paste. Slowly add the milk to create a smooth batter. Tip back into the jug.

Carefully remove the heated muffin tray from the oven. Pour the batter into the tray holes, it should sizzle a little, filling them around half way up. Bake for 25 mins, until risen and golden. Serve with the rest of your roast dinner, or simply lathered with gravy!

name: ZOE Grain Bowl
description: This nourishing grain bowl is absolutely packed with plants, providing dietary fibre and polyphenols which are important for feeding and maintaining your gut microbiome – which in turn, looks after you. Use whichever grains, veggies or seeds you love or have on hand for a personalised and plant-packed bowl.
instructions: Finely slice the red onion and add to a jar or bowl with a sprinkle of salt. Pour over the apple cider vinegar and enough water to cover the onions then place in the fridge for at least 30 mins.

Meanwhile, chop the broccoli into florets, slice the mushrooms and dice the tofu. Pan-fry them, one ingredient at a time, with a drizzle of olive oil over a medium-high heat until crispy. Season with salt.

To make the dressing, mix together the tahini, lime juice and soy sauce and grate in the garlic and ginger. Taste to check the seasoning and add more soy sauce for saltiness or lime juice for acid if needed.
Dice the cucumber and halve the cherry tomatoes.

To build your bowls, start with the grains at the bottom and top with the crispy tofu, broccoli and mushrooms. Add the cucumber, cherry tomatoes and pickled onions then drizzle over the dressing and sprinkle over the hemp seeds.

name: ZOE Granola
description: Meet our ZOE-fied granola, with over 10 different plants to get you towards your 30 per week goal. You’ll also get a boost of fibre from the oat bran, psylium husk, nuts and seeds. Once you make this, you won’t want to go back to store-bought.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan.
In a large bowl, mix together all the dry ingredients (everything except the coconut oil, honey and almond butter) along with a pinch of salt.
In a separate jug or bowl, mix together the coconut oil, honey and almond butter until combined.
Stir the wet ingredients through the dry mixture until everything is coated.
Spread the granola mix out onto a lined tray, pressing it into a single flat layer.
Bake for 25 mins, checking halfway and turning if necessary to ensure it browns evenly.
Rest for 10 mins and do not touch the granola at all if you want large chunks
Once the granola has cooled completely, it should break off into nice chunky pieces. Enjoy immediately or store in an airtight jar for up to a few weeks.

name: ZOE Marinated Olives with Greek Yoghurt
description: Got friends coming over? This plate is a great way to kick things off. Olives are packed with monounsaturated fatty acids including elenolic acid, which has been shown to lower blood sugar levels and promote weight loss. Olives are also a great source of polyphenols, which can help to reduce inflammation and promote better gut health. We’ve marinated our olives using Daily 30+ which adds so much flavour as well as 5g of fibre per scoop from over 30 different plants. The Greek yoghurt is a source of probiotics making this a feast for you and your gut microbes.
keywords: Daily 30+ Marinated Olives with Greek Yoghurt
Daily 30+ Marinated Olives with Greek Yoghurt
instructions: Add the drained olives, Daily30+, olive oil and herbs to a bowl and stir to combine. Set aside – you can do this step a few days in advance to increase the flavour.
Stir a pinch of salt through the greek yoghurt. Spread onto a plate and top with the marinated olives.
Serve with toasted sourdough and enjoy!

name: ZOE Seedy Crackers
description: Looking for healthy snacks? Look no further. These easy oven-baked flaxseed and chia seed crackers are the perfect vehicle for your favourite dip.
instructions: Heat the oven to 100°C.
Mix all the seeds together in a bowl with a pinch of salt. Add the water and give it a good stir then set aside for 15 mins.

Line a baking tray with baking paper. Pour the soaked seed mixture out onto the tray and cover with a second piece of baking paper. Press down and roll the dough out into a thin layer. Carefully peel off the top layer of baking paper.
Bake in the oven for an hour then turn off the oven and leave the crackers in the oven for another 30 mins or until cool.
Once cool, remove from the oven and snap into crackers. You can store them in an airtight container for up to two weeks. They go great with our smashed pea dip!

name: Za'atar Chicken, Olive Rice & Whipped Feta
description: Buttery olive rice, zesty za’atar chicken, salty whipped feta and a fresh crunchy salad. A perfect plate of food and a great one to batch cook.
instructions: Heat the grill to 220°C.

For the rice, finely slice the garlic and chop the herbs. Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear. Pop a medium-sized saucepan over a medium heat and add the butter. Once melted, throw in the garlic and cook for 8 mins until caramelised. Add the olives and a pinch of salt and sugar then cook for a further minute. Tip in the washed rice followed by the chicken stock (or water if you prefer). Bring to the boil then pop the lid on and reduce the heat to as low as possible. Cook for 12 mins, then turn the heat off and let sit for 15 mins. When the rice is ready, mix through most of the chopped herbs, setting aside a handful of each for the salad.

For the chicken, slice the chicken thighs into quarters lengthways and thinly slice the onions. Add both to a large bowl along with the paprika, za’atar, black pepper and olive oil. Season well with salt and mix to combine. Spread evenly on an oven tray then slide under the grill on the top shelf of the oven for 20 mins until cooked through, turning halfway.
For the feta, add the Greek yoghurt to a bowl with the chilli flakes and crumble over the feta. Mix well to incorporate.

For the salad, slice the cucumber in half lengthways, use a spoon to remove the seeds then slice into half moons. Finely slice the red onion and chillies. Add the salad ingredients to a bowl along with the reserved fresh herbs. Season to taste with salt and lemon juice.
To plate, spoon the feta over the bottom of the bowl, top with the rice, the chicken and some salad. Finish with more za’atar, salt, pepper and a lemon wedge, if you like.

name: Zaalouk Beans with a Pistachio Tofu Crumb
description: A rich and creamy butter bean stew inspired by Moroccan zaalouk, with smoky charred tomatoes and aubergines and a nutty tofu crumb. It’s healthy, plant-based and full of flavour.
keywords: Creamy Zaalouk Beans with a Pistachio Tofu Crumb
instructions: Heat your oven to 220°C.

Cut the top off the garlic bulb and add it to a baking tray along with the whole aubergines and tomatoes. Prick the aubergines with a fork then rub everything with olive oil and salt and place in the oven to roast for 35 mins, until the aubergines and tomatoes are collapsing and the skins are a little charred in places.
Meanwhile, soak the cashews in boiling water for 10 mins then drain and set aside.

Chop the red onion very finely. Heat a splash of olive oil in a medium pan set over a medium heat. Add the red onion and a pinch of salt and cook for 6 mins until softened. Add the spices and cook for a further 2 mins until fragrant. Add the tomato purée and the butter beans with most of their jarred liquid. Bring to a simmer and leave to gently cook on a low heat while the aubergines and tomatoes are roasting.

Remove the roasted veggies from the oven and leave for 5-10 mins to cool slightly. Roughly chop the aubergines and tomatoes and add to a bowl. Squeeze in the garlic flesh from the bulb and squish it down with a fork. Season the veggies with salt and pepper then add to the bean mix and stir well to combine. Add a splash of water if it's dry.

For the tofu crumb, add a glug of olive oil to a large frying pan. Crumble in the tofu, chop and add the pistachios, and season with a pinch of salt. Set over a medium heat and cook for 7-8 mins until browned and crispy. Season with more salt to taste.
Blitz the silken tofu, nutritional yeast and drained soaked cashews in a blender and season to taste with salt and lemon juice.
To serve, divide the beans between bowls then top with the cream and nutty tofu crumb. Finish with a few fresh parsley leaves, black pepper and a little drizzle of pomegranate molasses, if you like.

name: Za’atar Aubergine and Bulgur Wheat
description: Juicy aubergine coated in crispy za'atar on a bed of fresh bulgar wheat. This is going to be your new favourite lunch, Mob.
keywords: Za'atar aubergine and bulgur wheat recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Slice the aubergines in half and then score the inside in a cross-section.
Brush the aubergine with olive oil and sprinkle liberally with za'atar and salt. Slice the garlic in half, coat with olive oil then wrap up in foil.
Pop the garlic and aubergine in the oven with the cherry tomatoes and roast for 30 mins.
Bring 800ml of water to a boil then add in the bulgur wheat, pop on a lid and cook for 15 mins. Then turn the heat off and allow it to steam for 10 mins.
Finely chop the red chillies, red onion, parsley and spring onion.

Whisk together five tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil with the juice of a lemon, your roasted garlic, tomato paste, red chillies, spring onions, cumin, three-quarters of the parsley, salt, and pepper.
Toss with the cooked bulgur wheat until it's bright red and evenly coated.
Pour this onto your serving plate and top with the roasted aubergine and cherry tomatoes. Sprinkle with parsley and dollop on the coconut yoghurt. Enjoy!

name: Za’atar Cauliflower With Balsamic Caramelised Onion Hummus
description: Caramelised balsamic red onion hummus with extra jammy onions and za’atar-roasted cauliflower. Roasting the cauliflower like this (by covering and then uncovering it) makes it tender on the inside and perfectly caramelised on the outside. Finished with a zesty pine nut and herb drizzle, it's a delicious dish. Serve with lentils to make a complete meal.
keywords: Za’atar Cauliflower With Balsamic Caramelised Onion Hummus
Za’atar Cauliflower With Balsamic Caramelised Onion Hummus  recipe
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Finely slice the onions and lay them out on a large baking tray in a thin layer. Season with salt and pepper and a good drizzle of olive oil.

Slice the cauliflower in half and season each half with za’atar, plenty of olive oil, salt and pepper, getting into all of the grooves. Place the cauliflower onto the baking tray with the onions. Cover the tray tightly with foil and bake for 30 mins.
Remove the foil, add the balsamic vinegar and stir well. Return to the oven for 15-20 mins until the onions are caramelised and the cauliflower is starting to char.

Meanwhile, make the hummus. Drain the chickpeas, reserving half of the water from the jar. Put the reserved water, chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and olive oil into a blender and blitz until smooth. Keep the hummus in the blender until the onions and cauliflower are ready.
When the onions and cauliflower are cooked, add four heaped spoons of the onions to the hummus and blend again until smooth. Taste and adjust seasonings.

To make the herby drizzle, finely chop the parsley and add to a small bowl. Zest the lemon into the bowl and add half of the juice, the pine nuts, chilli flakes and plenty of olive oil, plus salt and pepper to finish.
To plate up, spread the hummus over a platter and top with the remaining onions and the cauliflower. Drizzle some extra tahini and the herby drizzle on top.

name: Za’atar Smashed Potato Salad
description: A potato salad with a difference. Here, we've thrown in our favourite Middle Eastern herb and served it with smashed spuds and a tomato-y cottage cheese.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Wash and dry the potatoes, then place them onto a baking tray. Drizzle with 2 tbsp of olive oil and rub onto each potato. Season with salt and pepper, space the potatoes out, making sure none of them touch and bake for 25 mins.

Meanwhile, in a small bowl add the za’atar, half the sumac and 80ml of olive oil. Stir together and season with salt. Pick the dill, parsley and mint leaves, keeping the dill and parsley stalks. Peel, halve and thinly slice the red onion.

In a food processor, add the sun dried tomatoes, reserved herb stalks and blitz until finely chopped. Add in the cottage cheese and 30ml of olive oil, whizz until smooth and creamy. Transfer into a bowl with the zest of half a lemon. Taste and season with salt if needed. Cover and refrigerate until needed.
Wash the sliced onion under cold running water then add into a bowl with the remaining sumac and some salt. Toss together and let macerate.

Once the potatoes have cooked for 25 mins, remove them from the oven — at this point they should be cooked. Use the bottom of a flat object to press down on each potato until it’s around 1cm thick. Drizzle over the za’atar oil onto each potato and return to the oven until golden and crispy, 20-30 mins.
Once the potatoes are ready, toss the picked herbs into the sumac onions with 1 tbsp of olive oil and the juice of the lemon.
Spread the whipped cottage cheese onto a platter, arrange the potatoes on top and garnish with the herb and onion salad.

name: Za’atar Smashed Potatoes, Yoghurt & Zhoug
instructions: Bring a pot of well-salted water to the boil. Preheat the oven to 200°C/ 390°F
Wash the potatoes and boil for 20-25 mins or until a fork pierces through them easily. Drain the potatoes and lay them out on a wire rack to cool and release the steam.
Meanwhile, make the za’atar oil by mincing your garlic cloves and then mixing them with 85ml olive oil and your za’atar.
When the potatoes have cooled, lay them out on a large tray lined with baking paper. Use a glass cup to smash each one until it’s burst open and flat, taking care not to push too hard.
Drizzle the za’atar oil over all of the potatoes, making sure it gets into all of the cracks. Roast the potatoes at 200°C for 30-40 mins or until crispy.

To make the zhoug, add the coriander, chilli, cumin, cardamom, and red pepper flakes to a food processor along with the juice of half a lemon and 30ml olive oil. Pulse until you have a chunky paste. Add the mix to a bowl and stir through another 40ml of olive oil and season well with salt and pepper.
To serve, lay a thick layer of yoghurt onto a plate, then top it with the potatoes and generously spoon on the zhoug. Add some lemon zest if you like.

name: Zebra Cake
description: A classic combo of chocolate and vanilla sponge, layered on top of each other to create beautiful swirly stripes. An amazing celebration cake.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180˚C fan assisted/gas mark 6. Grease and line two 20cm cake tins. Make sure your butter is at room temperature.

Use an electric whisk to beat the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy – approximately 4 mins. Add the eggs and beat slowly at first on a low setting, then on medium, until just evenly incorporated, scraping down the bowl after each stage. Remove half the batter to another mixing bowl (we’ll call them batter bowl #1 and #2) and set aside.

In another bowl, sift in ½ the flour and whisk it together with ½ the baking powder and salt. Add ½ of this flour mix to batter bowl #1 and beat on medium speed until incorporated. Add the vanilla and ½ the milk, then the rest of the flour mix. This is your vanilla batter. Set aside.

In the same flour mix bowl, sift in the remaining flour, baking powder and salt with the cocoa powder and whisk together. Add ½ of this flour mix to batter bowl #2, then the remaining milk, then the rest of the flour mix, making sure you scrape down the bowl with each addition and be careful not to over-beat. This is your chocolate batter.

To make the zebra stripes, spoon about 3 tbsp of the vanilla batter into the centre of each of your prepared cake tins. Then add 3 tbsp of the chocolate batter into the centre of that. The vanilla batter will spread out. Continue alternating the batters, adding to the centre each time. Once you are done, don’t be tempted to level the top or merge the layers in any way!

Bake for approximately 25–30 mins, or until a cocktail stick inserted into the centre comes out clean (or just with a few crumbs, and no liquid). Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tins for 10 mins before turning out on to a wire rack to cool completely.

Meanwhile, make the buttercream. Use an electric whisk to beat the butter alone for 4–5 mins on high speed. Sift in the icing sugar and add the vanilla and cream then beat on a low speed to bring it together. Beat on high for another 2–3 mins.

Spread buttercream over one layer and pop the other one on top, sandwiching them together. Spread more buttercream over the top and around the sides. Use any extra buttercream and a piping nozzle to decorate the cake, if you like.

name: Zesty Kale, Bean & Potato Soup with Garlicky Croutons
description: The more carbs, the merrier – this kale, bean and potato soup is exactly what you need for a weeknight comfort meal. Your five-a-day never looked so good.
keywords: White Bean and Potato Soup with Garlicky Croutons
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Peel and finely slice 2/3 of the garlic and slice the spring onions.

Heat half of the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the sliced garlic and spring onions along with a big pinch of salt. Fry for 2 mins, then add the fennel seeds and fry for 30 secs longer. Tip in the veg stock and bring to the boil.
Chop the potatoes into bite-sized chunks, around 3 cm. Add to the pan, cover with a lid and cook for 10 mins.

Tear the bread into chunks and tip onto a roasting tray. Grate the rest of the garlic into a small bowl and add the remaining olive oil. Pour that garlicky oil over the bread chunks and toss well. Season with salt and roast for 10 mins, until crispy and golden. Set aside.

After the potatoes have been cooking for 10 mins, reduce the heat to a low simmer. Check the potatoes are done, turning the heat back up and boiling them a little longer if they’re still a little firm. Drain the cannellini beans and add to the soup, along with the kale. Cook for 2 more mins, until it’s all wilted. Taste and season, adding the juice of half of the lemon.
Spoon the soup into bowls, top with the garlicky croutons, a drizzle of olive oil, and a scattering of dill. Serve with lemon wedges on the side.

name: Zhoug
description: This spicy bright green sauce is an essential component in a variety of dishes. This is our take on Yemenite zhoug.
instructions: Lightly crack the cardamom pods open using the back of your knife. Add the coriander seeds, cumin seeds and crushed cardamom pods into a small frying pan. Place on medium heat and toast until fragrant, 2-3 mins.
Remove the cardamom seeds and discard the pod.

Add the spices into a food processor or blender and blitz until they have broken down slightly (don’t let them become a fine powder). Trim the chillies and add them to the spices with the garlic clove, herbs (stems and all). Blend until broken down, then gradually add the olive oil, until emulsified. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the zhoug into a clean airtight container, stir the lemon juice in and cover with a light layer of olive oil on top. Store in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

name: Zingy & Fresh Creamy Courgette Carbonara
description: This might be an untraditional take on a carbonara but it's seriously good. It's the definition of summer comfort.
keywords: Zingy & Fresh Creamy Courgette Carbonara recipe
instructions: Place a saucepan of salted water on to the boil. Once boiling, cook the pasta until it's 1 min under al dente.
Trim and shave the courgette with a peeler until you get to the middle then thinly slice the centres. Finely slice the garlic.
Crack a whole egg into a bowl, add the separate yolks and whisk. Finely grate the Parmesan into the eggs and mix together with the chilli flakes.
Add the butter into a frying pan, place onto medium heat and let it melt. Stir fry the courgette centres and garlic, season with salt and cook until softened, 5-7 mins.

Using tongs, transfer the pasta straight from the water into the garlic with the courgette. Add the peeled courgettes in with the pasta, garlic and courgette centres. Turn the heat up to medium-high, toss together until the courgette has just started to wilt, then turn the heat down to low. Add a splash of pasta water and the egg mixture. Toss until glossy and thickened. Zest half the lemon in, season with a squeeze of lemon juice and more salt. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen, if needed.
Share the pasta between bowls and top with more Parmesan.

name: Zingy Chicken & Corn Salad
description: Delicious, smokey, perfectly cooked chicken on a crunchy, zingy, fresh salad. A lovely little lunch.
instructions: Preheat oven 180°C/356°F.
Place the chicken breasts and sweetcorn on a baking tray. Add salt, pepper, olive oil, smoked paprika and cumin.
Rub the spices in, making sure everything is coated. Put the chicken and corn into the oven for 30 mins.
De-seed your mixed peppers and chop into cubes.
Peel the skin off the cucumber, chop in half and scoop out the seeds using a teaspoon. Chop into chunks.
Chop the onion in half and cube.
Chop the 2 avocados in half, remove the stones and scoop out the flesh.
Remove the chicken and corn from the oven. Using a knife, check the chicken is cooked through. With another knife, scrape the sweetcorn kernels off the cobs. Slice up the chicken into chunky strips.
Add all the ingredients to a serving bowl including the beans.
Dress with lime juice and olive oil. Toss together. Serve and garnish with coriander leaves. Enjoy!

name: Zingy Coconut Dal & Greens Soup
description: Transform your Coconut Dal batch into a delicious hearty soup. With greens, zingy lemon and a jammy eggs on top, this one is speedy and incredibly comforting.
instructions: Make the Coconut Dal batch recipe.

Pour the Coconut Dal into a saucepan with the veg stock and bring to a gentle simmer. Stir through the spinach and cook for 2–3 mins until wilted. Squeeze in the juice of half the lemon and season with salt and black pepper.
Meanwhile, bring a pan of water to the boil. Gently lower in the eggs and cook for 6 mins. Transfer to a bowl of cold water to stop them cooking further. Peel and set aside.
Just before serving, stir half the yoghurt into the soup. Halve the eggs.

Ladle the soup into bowls and top with a swirl of the remaining yoghurt and the jammy eggs. Finish with pickled onions, coriander leaves and a crack of black pepper. Serve any leftover lemon wedges alongside.

name: Zingy Green Pasta
description: Green kale pasta is a well-loved vegetarian classic. This one comes with some zingy lemon and salty feta for a vibrant twist.
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Meanwhile, peel and finely dice the onion and discard any tough, thick kale stems.

Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the onions and cook for 4-5 mins until softened and translucent. Add the kale to the pan and cook until wilted. Transfer to a blender with half the vegetable stock and all the olive oil. Let it cool down before blending until smooth, then pour it back into the pan.
Once the water reaches a boil, add the pasta and cook for 3 mins until al dente. Transfer the pasta to the sauce, reserving 250ml pasta water.

Set the pasta over a medium-high heat with the remaining vegetable stock. Toss together until hot, thinning it out with pasta water, as needed. Crumble in ½ of the feta and mix to combine. Taste and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Share between bowls and top with lemon zest, walnuts and remaining crumbled feta.

name: Zingy Green Potato Salad
description: Potato salad, with a twist. This dish is a celebration of some of our favourite Thai flavours. It's one of our favourite bbq sides and we're sure it'll be yours too.
instructions: Fill a wide, deep sauté pan halfway with vegetable oil and heat to 150°C.
Thinly slice the shallots and place in a bowl. Add the corn flour and toss well to coat.
Fry the shallots until browned and crispy then drain on some kitchen towel and season with salt.
Quarter the potatoes lengthways. Place them in a saucepan, cover with cold water and season very generously with salt. Simmer for 15 mins, or until cooked through.
Meanwhile, juice the lime, deseed the green chillies and peel the ginger.
Transfer to a blender with the fresh coriander, fresh mint, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, 4 tablespoons of vegetable oil and 4 tablespoons of water and blitz until smooth.
Drain the potatoes and transfer to a bowl. Add the green dressing and toss well to coat.
Thinly slice the red chillies and crush the peanuts.
Plate up the potatoes and top with the sliced chilies, crushed peanuts and crispy fried shallots. Tuck in and enjoy.

name: Zingy Greens & Miso Salmon Traybake
description: This zingy, umami-packed salmon traybake gets its punch from a miso marinade and is baked on a bed of garlicky greens. A weeknight winner and ideal for meal prep.
instructions: Heat the grill to medium.

Zest and juice the lemon, finely grate the ginger and add to a large mixing bowl along with the remaining marinade ingredients. Add the salmon fillets, tossing well to coat. Set aside in the fridge. You can marinate the salmon for up to 24 hours in advance or use it immediately.
Finely grate the garlic into a small bowl, stir the olive oil through.
Add all the frozen veg into a baking tray. Pour the homemade garlic oil all over, season with salt and pepper and place the salmon fillets on top.
Cook the salmon for 10-20 mins, until cooked through (depending on the thickness, it will take shorter or longer). Taste and season the veg with salt, pepper and some extra lemon juice, if needed.

The cooked salmon will keep in the fridge for 3–4 days and in the freezer for up to 3 months (defrost in the fridge overnight and reheat gently in a low oven or flake it cold into dishes to avoid drying out).Eating it now? For a quick meal, serve with some cooked rice.

name: Zingy Lemongrass Pan Con Tomate
description: Pan con tomate is a summer classic, and this version is no exception. Loaded up with lemongrass and vibrant green chillies, this is a dreamy no-cook dinner.
instructions: Bash your lemongrass and peel off the excess woody bits. Roughly chop the rest. Roughly chop your chillies and garlic.
Add your lemongrass, chillies and garlic to a pestle and mortar and bash to a paste.
Zest in your lime and add the juice of half. Add your fish sauce and sugar, then continue bashing until you have a purée situation.
Place a box grater in a bowl. Halve your tomatoes, then grate with the cut side on the coarsest setting - you should just be left with the skins.
Add your lemongrass paste to your tomatoes along with a generous pinch of salt, then mix to combine.
Set a sieve over a bowl and pour your tomato mix into it. Leave to sit for a minute to strain off any excess water.
Heat a skillet pan over a medium-high heat. Drizzle your pan with olive oil, then add your bread. Toast for a few mins on each side until it is deeply crispy.
Spoon your tomato mix over your toast, then top with coriander leaves and crispy shallots. Serve and enjoy!

name: Zingy Miso Salmon Salad with Wasabi Dressing
description: This light, punchy quinoa salad brings heat from wasabi and sweetness from honey, and brings freshness to your Zingy Green Miso Salmon batch leftovers.
keywords: fresh salmon salad with wasabi dressing
instructions: Before you begin, make the Zingy Green Miso Salmon batch recipe.

Whisk the soy, honey, vinegar, wasabi, sesame oil and garlic granules (you can use powder instead if you don't have any) together into a big bowl. Taste and season with salt and more honey, if needed.

Flake the cooked salmon. Pick the coriander leaves and finely slice the stems.Add the quinoa, salmon and coriander to the dressing. Toss everything together until evenly coated. Share between plates and dig in.

name: Zingy, Cold Coriander & Prawn Brothy Noodles
description: Cold noodle soup is a saviour in hot weather. Inspired by Mexican aguachile, this one’s packed with juicy prawns, slippery noodles and a zingy coriander broth with a proper chilli kick.
instructions: Pick ¼ of the coriander leaves and set them aside. Thinly slice the red onion and one jalapeño. Chuck them into a bowl of ice water with the picked coriander leaves and let them chill.

Add the miso, garlic, cucumber, avocado, cold water (you can substitute half of the water with ice cubes if you’ve got a good blender), the rest of the coriander (stalks and all) and the remaining jalapeños to a blender. Blitz until smooth. Season with lime juice, salt and black pepper. Pour into an airtight container and chill in the fridge or freezer until properly cold.
Cook the rice noodles following pack instructions, then rinse under cold water until totally cool.
Drain the coriander and onion. Toss with the prawns, sliced jalapeño, a good squeeze of lime and a drizzle of olive oil.
Divide the noodles between bowls. Pour over the cold broth and top with the zingy prawn salad. Eat straight away while cold.

name: ​​Watermelon & Feta Fattoush with Crispy Flatbread Croutons
description: Juicy watermelon, crunchy radishes and golden flatbread croutons all soaked in a zesty, feta dressing. It’s summer in salad form.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Tear the flatbreads into bite-sized chunks and spread them out on a baking tray lined with baking paper. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and toss to coat. Roast for 7–10 mins until golden and crispy.
Chop the watermelon and tomatoes into 3cm chunks. Tip the tomatoes into a large bowl, season with salt and stir through the pomegranate molasses. Set aside to macerate.
Thinly slice the radishes (a mandolin works well here) and pick the mint leaves, discarding the stems.

To make the dressing, finely crumble the feta into a large bowl. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon, add the za’atar, and slowly whisk in the olive oil until the dressing emulsifies. Pour in any of the tomato juices as well. Taste and season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of sugar, if needed.
Toss the watermelon, tomatoes, radishes, grains, and mint through the dressing until everything’s well coated.
Crumble over the remaining feta, scatter with the crispy flatbread croutons, and serve.

name: ‘Heal Me’ Chicken Soup
description: Fall-apart chicken teamed with wedges of veg and simmered with a bunch of fresh herbs. Plus a few heaping spoons of crème fraîche. Comfort in a bowl.
instructions: Strip the meat from the chicken, keeping the skin on if you can. Cut the celery into chunky diamonds and peel and cut the carrots into little diamond nuggets. Cut the spring onion whites into 3cm chunks and finely slice the green tops.

Pour the chicken stock into a large pot and bring to a simmer. Add the carrots and cook for 10-12 mins until they’re barely approaching tender. Drop in the pasta or noodles along with your spring onion whites and the celery. Let the lot bubble away for 10 mins until everything is beautifully cooked.

Roughly chop the herbs and bung them in with the chicken and plenty of salt and pepper. Add a few tbsp of olive oil for gloss and divide between warm bowls. Top with a healthy dollop of crème fraîche, a pinch of chilli flakes, a squeeze of lemon juice and extra olive oil. Serve with bread and butter if you’re feeling particularly delicate.

name: ‘Nduja Cheese & Tomato Toastie
description: ‘Nduja, Cheddar and sliced baby tomatoes are loaded onto two slices of bread, covered in butter and fried until golden.
instructions: Place a frying pan over a medium heat, add the ‘nduja and a splash of olive oil. Cook for a minute until the 'nduja melts.
Slice the tomatoes into 1cm thick rounds and then fry for a minute either side in the pan with the ‘nduja.
Pop the cooked tomatoes onto 4 slices of bread and pour over the melted 'nduja. Season with a pinch of salt and the oregano.
Grate over the Cheddar and top with the remaining slices of bread.
Place the sandwiches back into the same pan over a medium heat and cook for about 4 mins on each side until the outside is golden brown and the cheese is melted.
Plate up and serve hot. Enjoy!

name: ‘Nduja Lasagne For One
description: Lasagnes tend to be time-consuming projects and recipes typically serve 6-10 people. This one, however, takes very little effort, minimal hands-on time … and feeds just one!
instructions: Combine the tomatoes, butter, vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan set over a medium heat. Simmer gently for 8-10 mins, allowing the sauce to intensify and reduce by around one-third.

While the sauce cooks, bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil. Drop in the lasagne sheets and cook for 2-3 mins. Drain through a colander, cool under a running cold tap, then return the pasta to the pot and fill that with cold water.

Heat the oven to 180°C. Lay a couple of clean tea towels on your kitchen surface. One by one, remove the pasta sheets from the water and arrange them on the tea towels without overlapping (so they don’t stick to each other).

Cut the mozzarella into ½cm slices and break the 'nduja into fingernail-sized pieces. Grab an ovenproof dish (ideally 16cm long, 10cm wide and 4cm deep). Depending on the size of your dish, your lasagne will have five or six layers of pasta – if necessary, trim each sheet to fit.

To assemble, begin with a spoonful of tomato sauce, then a layer of pasta and another spoonful of sauce. Top the next layer with a layer of pasta and a little sauce, plus half the 'nduja and one-third of the mozzarella. Then a layer of just sauce, followed by another layer of 'nduja and mozzarella. Finish with whatever tomato sauce remains, plus the remaining mozzarella and a snowstorm of Parmesan.
Bake in the oven for 25-30 mins until golden and molten. Enjoy with some dressed rocket or other green leaves.

name: ’Nduja & Bean Soup
description: Think of this a bit like a minestrone, but with a whack of added heat from the ’nduja.
instructions: Very finely dice the onion, carrot and celery.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan. Add the diced veg and sprig of rosemary and cook over a medium heat for 15 mins until softened, adding a splash of water if they start to stick.
Add the ’nduja to the pan along with the tomato purée. Cook, stirring, for 2 mins until the ’nduja has released its oil and the mixture has darkened.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and add to the pan: cook for 5 mins, squishing them up with the back of your spoon to break them down.
Add the chicken stock, then top it up with another 500ml of water. Bring it to a simmer, then season to taste with salt.
Drain the cannellini beans, then tip these into the pan along with your pasta. Simmer for 5 mins.

Meanwhile, tear the stalks away from the cavolo nero leaves and discard them. Tear the leaves into rough pieces. Once the 5 mins are up, add the cavolo nero leaves to the pan. Simmer for another 3 mins.
Check that your pasta is tender, then adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper. Spoon into bowls then grate over the Parmesan to serve. Enjoy!

name: “Marry Me” Air Fryer Chicken-Loaded Fries
description: Using reduced-fat versions of pesto, cream cheese and oil makes this seemingly indulgent dish a lot healthier. It’s high in protein and absolutely delicious.
instructions: Use a sharp knife to cut the potatoes into even-sized skinny chips. Transfer them to a microwave-safe container and cook them on a medium-high setting in the microwave for 7 mins until softened.
Meanwhile dice the chicken into bite-sized chunks, crush the garlic cloves, and slice the sundried tomatoes into bite-sized pieces.

Heat the air fryer to 190°C. Transfer the softened chips to the air fryer basket. Spray with the low calorie cooking spray and season with the paprika, mixed herbs and salt and pepper. Shake to coat the fries then cook in the air fryer for around 20 mins until golden.

Spray a large frying pan with the low calorie cooking spray and set it over a medium heat. Add the chicken and pan fry for about 7 mins or until cooked through. Add the garlic and sundried tomatoes and cook for another couple of minutes until fragrant and softened.
Add the ground thyme, ground oregano, ground basil, red pesto, cream cheese and water. Mix to combine and bring to a gentle simmer. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Tip the chips into a bowl and top with the creamy chicken. Scatter over some chopped fresh basil and dig in!

name: “Marry Me” Chicken Gnocchi
description: A quick and easy midweek dinner with pillowy gnocchi and a creamy sundried tomato sauce. Minimal fuss and maximal flavour.
instructions: Finely dice the onion and crush the garlic cloves. Dice the chicken breasts into bite-sized chunks. In a jug, dissolve the stock cube in the boiling water. Set everything aside.

Pour a glug of oil from the sundried tomato jar into a large lidded pan set over a low-medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook for a few minutes, with the lid off, until softened. Add the chicken and cook for about 10 mins or until cooked through.

Slice the sundried tomatoes into bite-sized pieces then add them to the pan with the cooked chicken, along with the pesto, oregano, thyme and a pinch of salt and pepper. Stir to combine then pour in the stock. Stir again and bring the mixture to the boil.
Add the gnocchi then pop the lid on and leave to simmer for 3-5 mins until the gnocchi is cooked. Meanwhile, roughly chop the basil leaves.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir through the single cream and ½ the basil.
To serve, divide between bowls and top with the remaining basil and some grated Parmesan, if you like.

name: “Marry Me” Chicken Orzo
description: Chicken and orzo in a creamy, silky sauce. Make this and you’ll understand the title of the recipe.
instructions: Finely dice the onion and chop the chicken breasts into bite-sized chunks. Slice the sun-dried tomatoes and crush the garlic cloves. Set everything aside.

Add ½ tbsp oil from the sun-dried tomato jar to any deep pan or saucepan, then add the onion and garlic. Cook for a few minutes until softened, then add the chicken and cook for around 10 mins until cooked through.
Add the sundried tomatoes, oregano, thyme, pesto and a pinch of salt and pepper to the pan. Stir to coat, then pour in about 90% of the stock. Stir again and bring to the boil.

Tip in the orzo and reduce the heat to a simmer. Cook for around 7 mins, by which point most of the liquid should have been absorbed (but it should still be quite watery-looking, so add the remaining stock plus some additional water if it’s not). The orzo will continue to soak up the liquid even once it’s off the heat, so don’t worry if it looks a little watery. Stir in the cream, then cook for a further 3 mins or until the orzo is fully cooked and most of the liquid has been absorbed.
Stir through some torn basil, then divide between bowls and top with extra chopped basil and parmesan, if you like.

name: “Marry Me” Spaghetti & Meatballs
description: If you’re looking to impress someone over dinner, look no further. This silky spaghetti with beef meatballs in a delicious creamy sauce will be a definite winner.
instructions: Finely dice the onion, crush the garlic cloves and slice the sundried tomatoes into bite-sized pieces.

Pour a glug of oil from the sundried tomato jar into a large pan over a medium heat. Add the meatballs and fry for about 10 mins or until the meatballs are nicely browned and cooked through. Transfer the meatballs to a plate and set aside.
Meanwhile, set a large saucepan of boiling water over a high heat then add the stock cube and stir to dissolve.
Return the empty meatball pan to the hob and reduce the heat to low-medium. Add another splash of the sundried tomato oil then add the onion and garlic and fry for about 7 mins until softened.
Drop your spaghetti into the boiling water and cook following packet instructions.

Add the sundried tomatoes, oregano, thyme, pesto, salt and pepper to the pan with the onion and garlic. Toss the meatballs back in and stir to coat then pour in the cream and a couple of ladles of pasta water. Stir and bring to a gentle simmer.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the basil.
Drain the cooked spaghetti then add to the pan with the sauce, along with ½ the chopped basil and a splash of the pasta cooking water. Mix well to combine.
To serve, divide the spaghetti between bowls and top with the remaining basil and some grated Parmesan.

name: “Marry Me” Tomato Soup
description: A rich and creamy soup with roasted tomatoes and red peppers, fresh basil and crème fraîche. Indulgent, flavourful and packed with nutrients, this soup is a hug in a bowl.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the vine tomatoes into quarters and the onion and peppers into large chunks. Slice the bulb of garlic horizontally.

Place the chopped vegetables in a deep oven-proof dish, along with the whole cherry tomatoes. Place the bulb of garlic face-up in the centre. Drizzle with a glug of olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 35 mins.

Remove the tray from the oven and transfer all the veggies and their juice to a large saucepan, squeezing out the roasted garlic cloves and discarding the skins. Add the crème fraîche, pesto, torn fresh basil and 500ml vegetable stock and blitz with a hand blender until smooth.
Turn up the heat and warm through the soup until piping hot, stirring occasionally. Divide into bowls and serve with toasted ciabatta.
